title: Localize App Shortcut invocation phrases for the New Chat intent
body:
## Context
The App Intents "New Chat" feature (uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#337, branch `issue/337-app-intents-new-chat`) exposes Siri / Shortcuts / Action-button shortcuts via `HermexShortcuts` in `HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift`. The intents' `title` and `description` strings were added to `Localizable.xcstrings` and are localized in all 17 non-English locales. **The spoken invocation phrases were not** — they have no localized entries anywhere, so Siri voice invocation only works in English.

Surfaced by a Codex review of the uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#337 working tree (P2).

## The phrases (`HermexAppIntents.swift`, `HermexShortcuts`)

There are now **three** App Shortcuts, each with three phrases (nine phrase keys total):

```swift
AppShortcut(
    intent: NewChatIntent(),
    phrases: [
        "New chat in \(.applicationName)",
        "New \(.applicationName) chat",
        "Start a new chat in \(.applicationName)"
    ], ...)
AppShortcut(
    intent: NewChatVoiceIntent(),
    phrases: [
        "New voice chat in \(.applicationName)",
        "New \(.applicationName) voice chat",
        "Start a voice chat in \(.applicationName)"
    ], ...)
AppShortcut(
    intent: NewChatInProfileIntent(),
    phrases: [
        "New \(\.$profile) chat in \(.applicationName)",
        "Start a new \(\.$profile) chat in \(.applicationName)",
        "New chat in \(\.$profile) on \(.applicationName)"
    ], ...)
```

## Why `Localizable.xcstrings` doesn't cover them
App Shortcut phrases are **not** localized through `Localizable.xcstrings`. Apple requires a dedicated string catalog named **`AppShortcuts.xcstrings`** (the `AppShortcuts` table) for phrases to be recognized in non-English locales. That file does not exist in the repo and is not referenced by `HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`.

Impact today:
- Discovery in Spotlight / Shortcuts app / Action Button uses the intent **title** → already localized, works in all locales. ✅
- **Spoken Siri invocation** uses the **phrases** → English-only. ❌

## Scope
1. Create `HermesMobile/Resources/AppShortcuts.xcstrings` (alongside `Localizable.xcstrings`) and add it to the `HermesMobile` target's resources in the project.
2. Add the nine English source phrases as keys. In `AppShortcuts.xcstrings`, interpolations serialize as **named placeholders** — `\(.applicationName)` → `${applicationName}` and `\(\.$profile)` → `${profile}` (not `%@`), e.g.:
   - `New chat in ${applicationName}`
   - `New voice chat in ${applicationName}`
   - `New ${profile} chat in ${applicationName}`

   Keep the placeholders; do **not** hardcode "Hermex".
3. Provide translations for all 17 non-source locales currently in `Localizable.xcstrings`:
   `ar, de, es, fr, he, it, ja, ko, nl, pl, pt-BR, ru, tr, ur, zh-HK, zh-Hans, zh-Hant`
   - Phrases should be **natural spoken commands** a user would say to Siri, not literal word-for-word translations. Multiple natural variants per language are encouraged where grammar differs — the phrase list drives recognition, so more good variants = better recognition.
   - Reuse the i18n translation-batch playbook (sub-agent chunking + glossary + parity check) from uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#291/#292/#293.
   - Keep the `${applicationName}` / `${profile}` placeholders in every translation; their position may move within the sentence per language.
   - RTL note: ar/he/ur phrases are plain recognition text (not layout) — no special handling needed.

## Out of scope
- The intent `title`/`description` strings are already localized — don't touch them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `AppShortcuts.xcstrings` exists, is built into the `HermesMobile` target, and contains all 9 phrase keys (3 per shortcut).
- [ ] All 17 locales have at least one translated variant for each phrase key (no `new`/missing states left for shipped locales).
- [ ] `${applicationName}` / `${profile}` placeholders preserved in every translation.
- [ ] Builds clean: `xcodebuild build -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`.
- [ ] Manual check: set the simulator to a non-English locale (e.g. German), open the Shortcuts app, confirm the New Chat shortcuts' suggested phrases display in that language.

## References
- `HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift` (`HermexShortcuts` / `NewChatIntent` / `NewChatVoiceIntent` / `NewChatInProfileIntent`)
- `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` (locale list + translation style)
- i18n translation-batch playbook (uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#291/#292/#293, `build/i18n/merge_langs.py`)

---

_2026-07-02 triage update: rescoped from 3 phrases / 1 intent to 9 phrases / 3 intents (`NewChatVoiceIntent` and `NewChatInProfileIntent` landed after the issue was written), and corrected the placeholder format for `AppShortcuts.xcstrings` from `%@` to named `${...}` placeholders._

title: Tech-debt backlog: ChatViewModel decomposition · Swift-6 strict concurrency
body:
## Context

These items were explicitly **deferred — not rejected** in the 2026-06-10 improve audit (uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#208) and the master backlog tracker (uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#209). Both trackers were closed in the 2026-06-28 issue-cleanup pass (every other child had shipped); this issue preserves the deferred debt so it stays visible without resurrecting the heavy trackers.

Each is a real, owner-gated decision rather than ready-to-execute work — pick one up only when its trigger fires.

## 1. ChatViewModel decomposition

`ChatViewModel.swift` is a god object (~5,100 LOC as of 2026-07-02, up from ~4,600 when this was written). Real debt, but a wholesale refactor is too risky for a small executor. **Approach:** staged extractions (streaming orchestration, approvals/clarification, attachments/media) along the seams the earlier code-audit issues (uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#46–#48) already mapped — not one big-bang rewrite. Revisit when a change in this file becomes painful enough to justify carving off a slice first.

## 2. Swift-6 strict concurrency migration

Build setting is currently `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = targeted` (not full Swift-6 mode). A full migration is **L-effort / HIGH-risk** and would touch MainActor isolation across most of the app. Deferred to a dedicated decision — don't let piecemeal Antigravity "Swift-6 strict-concurrency" findings drive it ad hoc. Owner decision on whether/when the safety win is worth the churn.

## ~~3. PR CI (build + test on PRs)~~ ✅ Done

**Resolved 2026-07-02:** `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` now builds and runs the full XCTest suite on every PR that touches app code, with a docs-only path filter that skips the macOS runner for markdown/docs/community-file changes (uzairansaruzi/hermex#7, #11). The original cost rationale is also obsolete: the repo is public now, so GitHub-hosted macOS runners are free.

## Notes

- This is a tracking/decision issue, not a `ready-for-agent` slice. If one item earns a "do it" decision, spin it into its own properly-scoped issue (via `hermes-issue-intake`) first.
- Full original rationale (and the list of audit findings that were *rejected* outright) remains readable in the now-closed uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#208 / uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#209.

title: CI: stop exhausting Apple certificate cap on TestFlight signing (use stored signing identity)
body:
### Context
TestFlight CI archives and exports with automatic signing and `-allowProvisioningUpdates`, so a fresh runner can mint a new signing certificate through the App Store Connect API on every run. Apple caps certificates per account; once the cap is exhausted, archiving fails (exit 65, "Choose a certificate to revoke") until certificates are revoked by hand. The owner decided on **manual signing with a stored distribution identity** (Approach 1). Surfaced during the 1.2 release; failing run: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile/actions/runs/27238424564

Today's setup (checked against `master` on 2026-09-30, #896):
- **One upload workflow:** `.github/workflows/release-candidate-testflight.yml`. It runs only in the `external-testflight` environment, the repo's only environment. Its export options are `ci/ReleaseCandidateExportOptions.plist` (`signingStyle` `automatic`). #640 renamed `external-testflight.yml` and `ci/ExternalTestFlightExportOptions.plist` to these, and removed `internal-testflight.yml` and `ci/TestFlightExportOptions.plist`. `pr-ci.yml` builds with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, so it never signs.
- **Four signed targets:** the app `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile`, the share extension `.shareextension`, the Live Activity widget `.liveactivitywidget`, and the notification service `.notifications`.
- **Signing still mints on the runner.** Archive and export both pass `-allowProvisioningUpdates` with the App Store Connect API key. The key was already there when this issue was filed, so the key alone didn't prevent the cap. The archive logs of the latest successful runs (35916971117, 36656627375) show `Signing Identity: "Apple Development: Created via API (…)"` with `iOS Team Provisioning Profile` for all four targets: a fresh runner still creates a certificate through the API.
- **The cap hasn't bitten since this issue was filed.** Five upload runs succeeded: 29219008188, 30888612331, 34004189934, 35916971117, 36656627375. The two failures were a closed release train (30883811600) and an authentication error (35892153089). Whether the certificate count grows per run is unverified.

### Step 0: is the cap still real? (owner)
Before changing any signing, count the certificates in the Apple Developer account (Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles) before and after the next release-candidate run.
- The count doesn't grow: close this issue and link the evidence.
- The count grows: continue with the prerequisites and scope below.

### Prerequisite (owner)
Six secrets must exist in the `external-testflight` GitHub environment before the workflow can succeed:

| Secret | Contents |
|---|---|
| `DIST_CERT_P12_BASE64` | base64 of the Apple Distribution `.p12` |
| `DIST_CERT_P12_PASSWORD` | password used when exporting the `.p12` |
| `PROVISION_PROFILE_APP_BASE64` | base64 App Store profile for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile` |
| `PROVISION_PROFILE_SHAREEXT_BASE64` | base64 App Store profile for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.shareextension` |
| `PROVISION_PROFILE_WIDGET_BASE64` | base64 App Store profile for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.liveactivitywidget` |
| `PROVISION_PROFILE_NOTIFICATIONS_BASE64` | base64 App Store profile for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.notifications` |

The temp-keychain password is generated in-workflow (no secret needed). The agent may open the PR before the secrets exist; final green validation runs once they're in place.

### Provisioning-profile names
The `provisioningProfiles` plist values are keyed by bundle ID and use **profile names** (more stable than UUIDs across renewals):

- `Hermes Mobile App Store` → `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile`
- `Hermes Mobile Share Extension App Store` → `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.shareextension`
- `Hermes Mobile Live Activity App Store` → `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.liveactivitywidget`
- `Hermes Mobile Notification Service App Store` → `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.notifications` (suggested to match the other three; the owner picks the real name)

### Scope (agent)
1. **`ci/ReleaseCandidateExportOptions.plist`:** change `signingStyle` from `automatic` to `manual`; add a `provisioningProfiles` dict mapping the four bundle IDs to the profile names above. Keep all other keys unchanged.
2. **`.github/workflows/release-candidate-testflight.yml`:** add an "Import signing assets" step before Archive that creates a temporary keychain (generated password), imports the `.p12` from `DIST_CERT_P12_BASE64` / `DIST_CERT_P12_PASSWORD`, installs the four profiles from their base64 secrets, and sets the keychain as default and unlocked. Add a matching cleanup step (`if: always()`) that deletes the temp keychain.
3. Remove `-allowProvisioningUpdates` from the Archive step (`:166`) and the "Upload to App Store Connect" step (`:183`). Keep the `-authenticationKey*` flags: the upload still authenticates with the API key. The archive signs with a development identity and team profiles today (see Context), so check that it still signs once the runner can no longer mint them.
4. Extend the "Check required secrets" step to also require the six new secrets.
5. **Docs:** document the secret names, the profile-naming convention, how to export and base64 the cert and profiles, and a rotation/expiry note (distribution certs and profiles expire after about a year) in `TESTFLIGHT.md` § Signing and workflow setup, which describes automatic signing today.

### Acceptance criteria
- The workflow archives and uploads with `signingStyle: manual` and **no** `-allowProvisioningUpdates`.
- All four targets sign with the stored distribution identity and profiles.
- Two consecutive runs succeed back-to-back with no manual cert revocation and no increase in the Apple Developer cert count.
- The temp keychain is created per run and cleaned up; no secrets written to logs or committed.
- Secret/profile handling and rotation documented.

### Validation plan
- Trigger `release-candidate-testflight.yml` twice in a row from `master`; both reach a successful App Store Connect upload with no portal intervention.
- Confirm the uploaded build appears in App Store Connect and is TestFlight-submittable.
- Verify the Apple Developer certificate count does not increase across runs.

### Non-goals
- Auto-submitting Beta App Review / App Store review (stays manual).
- Changing app identity, bundle IDs, or the upload-only nature of the workflow.
- Migrating off GitHub-hosted runners or to fastlane match.

### Out of scope
- Branch TestFlight (`scripts/branch-testflight`). It runs on the maintainer's Mac with the signing identity already in the login keychain; this issue is about CI runners.

title: Shared: Let AdaptiveGlassContainer coordinate sibling glass surfaces
body:
## Context

Follow-up from PR uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#133 / issue uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#126.

Antigravity review noted that `MessageComposerView` currently uses:

```swift
AdaptiveGlassContainer(spacing: 6) {
    VStack(spacing: 6) {
        ...
    }
}
```

Hermes' current `AdaptiveGlassContainer` directly forwards its `@ViewBuilder` content into `GlassEffectContainer` on iOS 26, and forwards the same content unchanged for fallback paths. Because the composer passes one local `VStack`, the underlying iOS 26 `GlassEffectContainer` sees one top-level child instead of independently seeing the composer shell, selector pills, autocomplete, and other sibling glass surfaces.

This is not a correctness bug in PR uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#133. The composer now visually uses shared adaptive glass and the owner confirmed the simulator result looks good. This issue tracks a possible shared API improvement so future glass-heavy surfaces can opt into better sibling coordination without each caller needing local container/fallback layout work.

## Current behavior

- `AdaptiveGlassContainer` is only a thin wrapper around iOS 26 `GlassEffectContainer` when glass is enabled and transparency is allowed.
- Callers still own their layout container (`VStack`, `HStack`, etc.) inside the adaptive container.
- In the composer, that means the actual glass-bearing children are nested below a `VStack` from the glass container's point of view.
- This may reduce iOS 26 Liquid Glass coordination/blending/morphing between nearby sibling glass surfaces.
- The current behavior is visually acceptable and has no known user-facing regression.

## Expected behavior

Design a small shared-container API that lets callers expose true sibling glass surfaces to `GlassEffectContainer` on iOS 26 while preserving equivalent layout for material/opaque fallback paths.

The goal is not to change the look of every screen. The goal is to make the shared glass foundation capable of coordinating multiple nearby glass children when a screen needs that behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a shared adaptive-glass container/layout pattern that can coordinate sibling glass surfaces on iOS 26 without forcing call sites to wrap everything in a local `VStack` inside `AdaptiveGlassContainer`.
- [ ] Preserve existing fallback behavior for:
  - iOS versions without Liquid Glass;
  - glass preference disabled;
  - Reduce Transparency enabled.
- [ ] Migrate the chat composer usage only if it improves or preserves the approved PR uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#133 look and behavior.
- [ ] Keep composer compact height, spacing, secondary chrome visibility, slash autocomplete transition, selector behavior, context ring behavior, attachment strip, voice input, send, and stop behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Avoid broad restyling of Sessions, Settings, transcript rows, tool cards, or unrelated glass surfaces.
- [ ] Keep the shared API small and readable; do not introduce a generic layout system beyond what the current Hermes glass callers need.

## Validation plan

- Run `git diff --check`.
- Run a simulator build with XcodeBuildMCP or raw fallback:
  - `xcodebuild -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=2F5FED41-E76A-4ED8-8F4A-8151FEB7F8FC' -skipMacroValidation COMPILER_INDEX_STORE_ENABLE=NO ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES build`
- If the implementation touches shared `AdaptiveGlassModifier` behavior, run the focused or full XCTest suite based on blast radius.
- Manual simulator validation:
  - Focus/unfocus the composer.
  - Tap the main composer shell and selector pills on iOS 26 and verify Liquid Glass interaction remains visible.
  - Open slash autocomplete and verify the panel position/transition remains unchanged.
  - Open the context window ring popover and verify it remains legible.
  - Verify light/dark mode and Reduce Transparency.

## Non-goals

- Do not change server/API behavior.
- Do not add third-party dependencies.
- Do not implement Remodex drawer behavior, scope picker, custom font picker, custom icons, user bubble color customization, or Chat-pill follow-finger behavior.
- Do not use this issue to broadly restyle composer controls or change the visual design already approved in PR uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#133.
- Do not refactor unrelated SwiftUI layout unless it is required to preserve the exact current composer behavior.

## Priority / timing guidance

This is not urgent and is not required before merging PR uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#133 if the current simulator behavior remains owner-approved.

Implement when one of these becomes true:

1. We notice real Liquid Glass blending/interaction defects in the composer that cannot be fixed by per-surface `isInteractive` flags.
2. Multiple screens start needing grouped glass-sibling coordination and the current `AdaptiveGlassContainer { VStack { ... } }` pattern becomes limiting.
3. We schedule a dedicated shared glass foundation cleanup pass after the current Remodex-inspired chat/composer polish issues land.

Until then, keep this as a tracked enhancement rather than active PR-blocking work.

title: I-057: Add Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets for starting a new session on a configured profile
body:
## Source

Migrated from `ISSUES.md` legacy item `I-057`.

## Metadata

- Type: Feature
- Priority: P4
- Area: Widgets/Session Start
- Previous status: Open
- Tags: owner feedback
- Research date: 2026-05-24

## What to build

Add Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets for starting a new Hermes session on a configured profile.

First slice should prefer a widget/App Intent or deep-link path that opens Hermes Mobile and lets the main app create the session with the configured profile, avoiding credentialed network work inside the widget extension.

## Current mobile/widget state

- The widget target currently exposes the agent run Live Activity widget bundle only.
- **Update 2026-07-02:** the App Intents work (uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#337) has since landed `HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift` with `NewChatIntent`, `NewChatVoiceIntent`, and — most relevantly — **`NewChatInProfileIntent`**, a configurable intent that opens the app on a new chat pinned to a chosen server profile (with a `ProfileEntity` parameter and its own deep-link host `new-chat-profile`). This is most of the plumbing this issue originally asked to build.
- `HermesDeepLink` supports opening an existing session with `hermes-agent://session?id=<session_id>`; there is still no standalone "create a new session" deep link, but the profile-pinned intent path above supersedes the need for one in the first slice.
- `SessionListViewModel.createSession` creates a new session with the app's current defaults.
- `APIClient.createSession` already accepts an optional `profile` parameter.

## Recommended first slice (revised 2026-07-02)

The remaining work is the **widget surface itself**, reusing the existing intent rather than building new plumbing:

- Add a Home Screen widget (and Lock Screen widget/control) to the existing widget extension whose tap invokes the existing `NewChatInProfileIntent` (or `NewChatIntent` for a no-profile variant).
- Make the widget configurable per instance (profile picker via the existing `ProfileEntity` query).
- Let the widget only store/display non-secret profile metadata; the main app performs authenticated session creation with existing Keychain/cookie state, then navigates into the created session (this is what the intent already does).
- Keep background network creation inside the widget extension out of the first slice. That avoids duplicating auth/cookie handling and reduces App Store/privacy risk.

## Security and product constraints

- Do not store passwords, cookies, API keys, or server auth material in the widget extension.
- If an App Group is needed for profile metadata, store only low-risk display data and profile identifiers.
- If the app is not configured or logged in, widget taps should route to onboarding instead of failing silently.
- Profile display names can become stale; the app should validate/create with the server-side profile at tap time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can add at least one Home Screen widget and one Lock Screen widget/control that starts a new session for a selected profile.
- [ ] Tapping the widget opens Hermes Mobile, creates a new session with the configured profile, and navigates to chat.
- [ ] If the profile is missing or invalid, the app shows a clear fallback error or profile picker.
- [ ] If the app is unconfigured/logged out/offline, the app shows the correct existing onboarding/error path.
- [ ] Widgets do not expose secrets in snapshots, shared defaults, or logs.

## Suggested tests and validation

- Unit tests for new deep-link parsing (only if the implementation adds any new deep link).
- View-model tests for "create session with profile from deep link" once the flow is factored.
- Manual simulator/device pass: add widgets, configure profile, tap from Home Screen and Lock Screen, test unconfigured app, test missing profile, test multiple profiles, and verify created session profile on the server/mobile detail surface.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately after scope is confirmed.

---

title: PR CI: skip the macOS runner for docs-only PRs
body:
Docs-only PRs (like #1) were paying for a full 1176-test macOS run. This splits PR CI into three jobs:

- **Detect changed paths** (ubuntu, seconds): classifies the PR's files via the API; fail-closed allowlist — only markdown, docs/, LICENSE, .gitignore, and .github community files count as docs.
- **Build and Test** (macos-26): unchanged, but now conditional on non-docs changes.
- **CI Gate** (ubuntu, always runs): the new required check; passes when Build and Test succeeded or was skipped, fails otherwise. This avoids the classic paths-filter trap where a skipped required check blocks the merge forever.

Branch protection will switch from requiring "Build and Test" to requiring "CI Gate".

Since this PR touches a workflow file (not on the allowlist), it triggers the full suite itself — doubling as the end-to-end verification run for the new repo.

title: macOS app — Phase 1: target scaffolding + desktop-reinterpreted Sessions & Chat
body:
## Problem Statement

Hermex only runs on iPhone. Users who drive their self-hosted `hermes-webui` agent from a Mac have no native option — they either use the iPhone app in a small window (no such option exists) or fall back to the browser UI, losing native streaming chat, Keychain-backed auth, and the app lifecycle/notifications benefits the iPhone app already has. Desktop is also where these users spend most of their working day, making it the highest-friction gap in the current product.

## Solution

Add a second, dedicated native macOS target (`HermesDesktop`) to the existing Xcode project, sharing the platform-agnostic Networking/Models/Auth/Persistence layers already used by `HermesMobile`. Rather than porting iPhone screens as-is, reinterpret the highest-frequency workflow — server connection, session list, and streaming chat — for desktop ergonomics (multi-pane layout, keyboard-driven navigation, resizable windows), while preserving the same server capabilities (SSE streaming, clarifications, approvals, tool calls, transcript rendering).

This PRD covers **Phase 1 only**: target scaffolding, connection/auth, session list, and chat. Broader parity (Tasks, Skills, Memory, Insights, Settings, Onboarding, Share) is intentionally deferred to follow-up issues once this vertical slice validates the shared-layer approach and the desktop interaction model.

## User Stories

1. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to launch a native macOS app, so that I don't have to open a browser tab to reach my agent.
2. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to add/select a server connection using the same account model as iPhone, so that my existing server setup works without reconfiguration.
3. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want my iPhone-configured server credentials NOT to silently sync/share Keychain items across devices in an unexpected way, so that I understand the security boundary (out of scope for this PRD — see Out of Scope).
4. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to authenticate with my server password, so that I can access my agent securely.
5. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want auth failures (wrong password, unreachable server, expired cookie) to show clear, actionable errors, so that I can fix my connection without guessing.
6. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to see a list of my sessions in a persistent sidebar, so that I can switch between conversations without losing context.
7. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want the session list to update live as new sessions are created (e.g. from the CLI or iPhone app), so that the Mac app reflects the true current state.
8. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to search my sessions, so that I can find a past conversation quickly.
9. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to create a new session, so that I can start a fresh conversation with the agent.
10. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to rename a session, so that I can keep my session list organized.
11. As a Hermes user on a Mac, I want to delete/archive a session (matching the destructive-action safeguards already in the iPhone app), so that I can clean up old sessions without accidental data loss.
12. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want a chat transcript view with markdown, code blocks, and math rendering, so that agent output displays correctly.
13. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want streaming responses to render incrementally (not just appear all at once), so that I get the same "live" feeling as the iPhone app.
14. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to see tool call activity (name, status, expandable detail) in the transcript, so that I understand what the agent is doing.
15. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to respond to clarification requests from the agent, so that I can unblock a stuck run.
16. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to approve or deny approval requests from the agent, so that I retain control over sensitive actions.
17. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want a composer to type and send messages, so that I can converse with the agent.
18. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to use hardware Return to send and Shift+Return for a newline in the composer, so that the composer behaves like other native Mac chat/text apps.
19. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to select the model and reasoning effort for my message (matching iPhone's composer controls conceptually), so that I have the same runtime control on desktop.
20. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want to stop an in-progress agent run, so that I can interrupt work that's going in the wrong direction.
21. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want the window to resize/support multiple window sizes gracefully (sidebar + detail split view), so that the app feels native to macOS, not like a stretched phone screen.
22. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want standard macOS menu bar items (New Session, Close Window, Find, Quit, etc.) to work, so that the app respects platform conventions.
23. As a Hermex user on a Mac, I want the app's connection/session data to persist across launches (read-only cache, matching iPhone's offline cache behavior), so that I see my last-known state immediately on launch even before the network round-trip completes.
24. As a maintainer, I want `HermesDesktop` to reuse `APIClient`, `SSEClient`, models, `AuthManager`, `KeychainStore`, and `CacheStore` without modification (only additive changes if a genuine platform gap is found), so that the two targets don't diverge into parallel implementations of the same server contract.
25. As a maintainer, I want the Phase 1 macOS UI code to live under a new `HermesDesktop/Features/{Chat,SessionList,Onboarding}` structure mirroring the existing `HermesMobile/Features/*` convention, so that future contributors can navigate both targets consistently.
26. As a maintainer, I want CI/build tooling to build both targets (or at minimum `HermesDesktop` alone) so a broken macOS build is caught before merge, so that `master` stays release-candidate-buildable per the existing invariant for `HermesMobile`.

## Implementation Decisions

- **New Xcode target:** `HermesDesktop`, macOS (SwiftUI, macOS 15+ to match the minimum reasonable modern SwiftUI feature set used by `HermesMobile`'s iOS 18+ baseline), added to the existing `HermesMobile.xcodeproj` — not a new repo or Swift package.
- **Shared layer, no fork:** `Networking/`, `Models/`, `Auth/`, and `Persistence/` source files are added to the `HermesDesktop` target's membership alongside `HermesMobile` (multi-target file membership within the same project), not duplicated. Any file in these directories that turns out to have a hidden UIKit dependency must be fixed to be platform-agnostic (e.g. via `#if os(iOS)`/`#if os(macOS)` guards) rather than forked.
- **New platform-specific code only for UI:** All new Swift files for Phase 1 live under `HermesDesktop/Features/{Onboarding,SessionList,Chat}/` and `HermesDesktop/App/` (app entry point, window/scene setup). No new networking/model types are introduced unless a genuine desktop-only capability requires one (none identified for Phase 1).
- **Window/scene structure:** A single `WindowGroup` (or `Scene`) with a `NavigationSplitView`: sidebar = session list, detail = chat transcript + composer. This is the "desktop-first reinterpretation" of the iPhone's stack-based navigation.
- **Auth/connection reuse:** Reuse `AuthManager` and `KeychainStore` as-is. Server account model (`ServerAccount`) is shared; Phase 1 does not add cross-device sync of accounts (each platform's Keychain is independent, as today).
- **Streaming:** Reuse `SSEClient` and `ChatStreamCoordinator` logic; only the SwiftUI view layer (`ChatView`, `ChatComposerView`, `ChatTranscriptView` equivalents) is rebuilt for desktop. Investigate whether `ChatViewModel` can be reused directly (it should be, since it's platform-agnostic `@Observable`/`ObservableObject` state, not view code) — reuse it if so; only fork if a concrete platform blocker is found, and document the blocker.
- **Composer key handling:** Return-to-send / Shift+Return-for-newline via `NSEvent`/SwiftUI `onKeyPress` (macOS-only), gated behind `#if os(macOS)` in shared composer logic if the composer view model is shared, or implemented directly in the macOS-only composer view.
- **Menu bar:** Standard `CommandGroup` additions (New Session, Find, etc.) added in the `HermesDesktop` app entry point.
- **Offline cache:** Reuse `CacheStore`, `CachedSession`, `CachedMessage` as-is; no schema changes for Phase 1.
- **Out-of-scope features surfaced but not built:** Tasks, Skills, Memory, Insights, Settings, Onboarding polish beyond basic connect flow, Share extension, Live Activities (iOS-only concept, N/A on macOS), widgets/App Intents. These become their own follow-up issues once Phase 1 ships, per this repo's "one issue → one branch → one PR" workflow.
- **Distribution:** Not addressed in this PRD (no App Store Connect macOS app record, no TestFlight-for-Mac setup). Follow-up work once Phase 1 is functionally validated locally.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests here validate observable behavior (session list renders/updates from a given `SessionsResponse`, chat transcript renders a given sequence of streamed events, composer sends the expected request payload) — not SwiftUI view internals or exact layout pixels.
- Shared-layer regression: since `HermesDesktop` reuses `APIClient`, `SSEClient`, `AuthManager`, `KeychainStore`, `CacheStore` unmodified, existing `HermesMobileTests` covering those types remain the primary regression guard — Phase 1 should not need to duplicate those tests for the new target unless a shared file is genuinely modified.
- New `HermesDesktopTests` target (or shared test target, if the project structure allows) covering: session list view model behavior (load/search/create/rename/delete against a fake `APIClient`), chat view model streaming behavior reused from `HermesMobile` (confirm it passes unmodified against the existing test suite when compiled for macOS), and macOS-specific composer key-handling logic (Return vs Shift+Return dispatch).
- Prior art: existing `HermesMobileTests` for `SessionListViewModel` and `ChatViewModel` are the direct model to follow for structure and fake-`APIClient` patterns.
- Build validation: a build/test run of the `HermesDesktop` scheme (or equivalent) must pass locally before this PRD's implementation is considered complete, matching the existing "don't commit broken builds" invariant.

## Out of Scope

- Full iPhone feature parity (Tasks, Skills, Memory, Insights, Settings, Onboarding polish, Share extension) — deferred to follow-up issues.
- Live Activities / Dynamic Island / widgets / App Intents — iOS-only concepts, not applicable to macOS in their current form; any macOS equivalent (e.g. menu bar status item) is a separate future decision, not part of this PRD.
- Cross-device Keychain/account sync between iPhone and Mac.
- App Store Connect macOS app record, code signing setup beyond local development signing, and TestFlight-for-Mac distribution.
- Any new server-side API surface or upstream `hermes-webui` changes — this PRD only consumes existing endpoints already implemented in `Endpoints.swift`.
- Terminal, file editing, git management, and other P3+ roadmap items per `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` — unaffected by platform; still deferred regardless of platform per existing product decisions.
- Visual/branding polish pass equivalent to the iPhone app's "glass-forward" UI direction — Phase 1 targets functional desktop-reinterpreted UX; a dedicated design pass can follow once the interaction model is validated.

## Further Notes

- This is Phase 1 of a multi-phase macOS initiative (per brainstorm: `Approach C — desktop-first reinterpretation`, chosen over a straight port or aggressive full-parity sprint). Subsequent phases should each get their own PRD/issue as this repo's workflow requires one issue → one branch → one PR; this issue is scoped to be completable as a single agent slice.
- If, during implementation, any file under `Networking/`, `Models/`, `Auth/`, or `Persistence/` is found to have a latent iOS-only dependency, prefer fixing it to be platform-agnostic over forking a macOS-only copy — this keeps the two targets from diverging into parallel server-contract implementations.
- Per `AGENTS.md`, do not invent API endpoints or response shapes — validate against the pinned upstream copy at `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` or a running server before implementing any endpoint call.
- Per `AGENTS.md`, this PRD's implementation should not touch `master` directly, should keep the build green, and needs explicit human approval before pushing/opening a PR.

title: AGENTS.md: add official API docs to endpoint-verification precedence
body:
## What

Rewrites hard rule #1 in AGENTS.md: endpoint/JSON-shape verification is now a three-source precedence — (a) the running server, (b) the official API docs at https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/, (c) the pinned upstream copy at `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` — and explicitly allows refreshing the pinned clone via `git pull`.

## Why

Upstream now publishes hand-written API docs (no version pin; they track the latest release and link to this repo as the reference iOS client). Meanwhile the pinned clone had drifted 6+ weeks stale — it was missing all `/api/git/*` routes the app uses daily, plus `/api/tts` and `/api/model/set`. Docs are best for endpoint intent, the auth contract, SSE event vocabulary, and conventions; routes.py remains ground truth for exact JSON shapes; the running server stays the final arbiter.

Docs-only change; no code touched.
