title: Chat: "Read aloud" via server TTS (POST /api/tts) with on-device synthesizer fallback
body:
## Context

The app already has a **"Listen"** action on assistant messages (`ChatMessageActions.swift:35`) that speaks text with the on-device `AVSpeechSynthesizer` (`ChatViewModel.swift` ~3218, audio-session handling from old-repo #252). On-device voices are instant and work offline, but sound robotic.

The server exposes `POST /api/tts` backed by neural voices (Edge TTS by default — no API key needed). This issue upgrades "Listen" to **prefer server TTS and fall back to the on-device synthesizer** when the server call fails (offline, 4xx/5xx, rate limit).

**Trade-off to understand:** server TTS sends the message text to the server and returns audio — that adds latency (round trip + synthesis) and requires connectivity, in exchange for much better voice quality. The fallback keeps Listen working offline. The server's `engine:"browser"` value is upstream's own signal for "do TTS client-side", which maps exactly to our existing synthesizer path.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/voice/
- **Upstream handler:** `_handle_tts`, `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py:16529` @ `312d3fab` (2026-07-02)
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `POST /api/tts {"text":"Hello from Hermex.","voice":"en-US-AriaNeural"}` → `200`, `Content-Type: audio/mpeg`, 13,392 bytes (MPEG layer III, 24 kHz mono). Response is **fully buffered** (Content-Length set, not chunked) — a single-shot `Data` download is correct; no streaming logic needed.

## API contract (validated)

- Request JSON: `text` (required, ≤5000 chars), `voice` (server default is `zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural` — the client MUST pass an English/locale-appropriate voice, e.g. `en-US-AriaNeural`), optional `rate`/`pitch` (percent/Hz strings), `engine` (`edge` | `elevenlabs` | `openai` | `browser`, default `edge`).
- Response: raw audio bytes (`audio/mpeg` for edge).
- Errors: `400` invalid input · `401` unauthenticated · `429` (~2 s per-client rate limit — debounce repeat taps) · `503` engine API key missing (only for non-edge engines).

## Proposed slice

1. `Endpoints.swift`: add `case tts` → `/api/tts`.
2. New `APIClient` method returning raw `Data` — mirror how `APIClient+Transcribe.swift:12` (`transcribeAudio`) bypasses the JSON `send()` helper for non-JSON payloads. Decode the `{"error": ...}` body only on non-2xx.
3. Playback via `AVAudioPlayer`, reusing the existing Listen audio-session activate/deactivate pattern (`.playback` category — the #252 fix; don't regress to earpiece routing).
4. In the Listen action: try server TTS first; on any failure (network error, 4xx/5xx, timeout) fall back silently to the existing `AVSpeechSynthesizer` path. Text over 5000 chars: skip straight to the on-device path (simplest correct behavior; chunking is a non-goal).
5. Stop semantics unchanged: tapping "Stop Listening" stops whichever engine is playing; starting Listen on another message stops the current one.
6. Tests: endpoint path/body construction, error-shape decode, fallback decision logic (server failure → synthesizer), 5000-char routing. Playback itself is manual-validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Listen on an assistant message plays neural server audio through the speaker.
- [ ] Airplane-mode Listen still works (on-device fallback), with no error alert for the silent fallback.
- [ ] Rapid double-tap does not stack audio or surface a raw 429.
- [ ] "Stop Listening" works for both engines; starting a new Listen stops the old one.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Voice/engine picker UI, elevenlabs/openai engine configuration, rate/pitch controls, >5000-char chunking, background audio.

## Wrap-up note

`docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` row `/api/tts` (currently `roadmap P5 privacy — "mobile can use native TTS"`): owner re-prioritized 2026-07-02; on merge the row leaves the table (implemented is derived from `Endpoints.swift`).

title: Skills: enable/disable skills from the app (POST /api/skills/toggle) + decode disabled/tags
body:
## Context

The Skills screen is read-only today: it lists skills (`GET /api/skills`) and shows content (`GET /api/skills/content`), but a disabled skill looks identical to an enabled one, and there is no way to enable/disable a skill from the phone. Upstream has a dedicated toggle endpoint. This is a small, low-risk slice with real mobile value (toggle a skill before firing off a cron/chat from the phone).

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/skills/
- **Upstream:** `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab` (2026-07-02) — `/api/skills/toggle` handler.
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:**
  - `GET /api/skills` skill objects carry `{category, description, disabled, name}` — `disabled` is live. Docs also list `tags` and `related_skills`; the live response omits them when empty, so decode them as optionals (tolerant decoding, hard rule #3).
  - `POST /api/skills/toggle` with empty body → `400 {"error": "Missing required field(s): name, enabled"}` — route exists; body is `{name, enabled}`.

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Models/Skills.swift:3` — `SkillsResponse` / `SkillSummary` (`SkillSummary` does not decode `disabled`, `tags`, `related_skills`).
- `HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+Skills.swift:4` — read-only client.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Skills/` — list UI.

## Proposed slice

1. `SkillSummary`: add optional `disabled: Bool?`, `tags: [String]?`, `relatedSkills: [String]?`.
2. `Endpoints.swift`: add `case toggleSkill` → `/api/skills/toggle`; `APIClient+Skills.swift`: `toggleSkill(name:enabled:)` POSTing `{name, enabled}`; validate the response shape just-in-time against the pinned handler before coding (record it in the PR).
3. Skills list UI: visually mark disabled skills (dimmed + "Disabled" tag) and add a toggle (swipe action or row control, following existing list patterns). Optimistic UI with revert-on-error, or refetch after toggle — pick whichever matches existing patterns (e.g. session pin/archive).
4. Display `tags` as chips when present; ignore `related_skills` in UI for now (decode only).
5. Tests: tolerant decode (fields present/absent), endpoint path/body, toggle view-model behavior incl. error revert.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disabled skills are visibly distinct in the list.
- [ ] Toggling a skill updates the server (verify by refetching) and the UI reflects the new state.
- [ ] A failed toggle surfaces an error and the UI returns to the true server state.
- [ ] Older/other servers that omit `disabled`/`tags` still decode fine (no crash, no regression).
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Skill authoring (`POST /api/skills/save`/`delete`) — deliberately deferred, larger UX decision.
- `GET /api/skills/usage`.

## Wrap-up note

`docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` row `/api/skills/` (`roadmap P3 write — save/delete`): toggle ships here; the row's note should then read "save/delete remain roadmap".

title: Sessions: archived sessions vanish forever — add an Archived view + unarchive (include_archived)
body:
## Context

The app can archive a session (`POST /api/session/archive`) but never lists archived sessions — once archived, a session is **unreachable from the app** (a "roach motel"). The owner's live server currently reports **8 archived sessions** that are invisible in Hermex. The sessions list endpoint supports opting in to archived sessions; this slice adds an Archived section/view and an Unarchive action.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/sessions/ (`include_archived`, `archived_limit`, `all_profiles`, `sidebar_source` params; `archived_count`/`cli_count` response fields).
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `GET /api/sessions?include_archived=1&archived_limit=3` → response keys include `archived_count` (=8), `archived_cli_count`, `archived_webui_count`, `cli_count`, `other_profile_count`, `sessions`, plus existing fields. Confirmed working.
- **Unarchive contract** (`.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py:14519` @ `312d3fab`): the archive handler sets `s.archived = bool(body.get("archived", True))` — so `POST /api/session/archive {"session_id": ..., "archived": false}` **unarchives**. The app's existing call (no `archived` key) archives, which matches today's behavior.
- Subagent and read-only imported CLI sessions reject archiving with 400 — surface the server message rather than a generic error.

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Networking/Endpoints.swift:8` (`case sessions`), `:16/:122` (`archiveSession` → `/api/session/archive`).
- `HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift:3` — `SessionsResponse` (does not decode `archived_count` etc.).
- `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/` — list UI with existing cron/CLI visibility filters (`SessionListView.swift:499`).

## Proposed slice

1. `SessionsResponse`: add optional `archivedCount: Int?` (decode others only if used).
2. `APIClient` sessions fetch: support `include_archived=1` (+ optional `archived_limit`) as parameters — default off so the main list is unchanged.
3. UI: an "Archived" entry (e.g. at the bottom of the session list or behind a filter menu) showing archived sessions with count; opening an archived session read path unchanged.
4. Unarchive: swipe/context action calling `archiveSession` with `archived: false`; the session returns to the main list.
5. How to distinguish archived rows in the merged response: validate just-in-time whether session objects carry an `archived` flag when `include_archived=1` (check the pinned handler + live server; record in the PR). If they do, filter client-side; if not, use a separate fetch for the archived view.
6. Tests: query construction (param on/off), decode with/without new fields, unarchive body shape, view-model filtering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Archived sessions are reachable from the app and clearly separated from active ones.
- [ ] Unarchive works and the session reappears in the main list without an app restart.
- [ ] Main session list behavior/order is unchanged when the archived view is not open.
- [ ] Archive/unarchive rejections (subagent, read-only CLI) surface the server's message.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- `all_profiles` / `sidebar_source` params, bulk unarchive, auto-archive policies.

title: Chat: gate the reasoning-effort picker per model via supported_efforts (unblocks old I-052)
body:
## Context

The composer shows a **static** effort menu (`none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh`) regardless of model, so users can select efforts the current model does not support. Old-repo issue I-052 (hermes-mobile#4) investigated model-aware reasoning controls and was closed not-planned **specifically because** upstream lacked authoritative capability metadata: *"Do not implement mobile-side filtering from provider/model names until upstream exposes … a richer reasoning-options endpoint."*

That condition is now met: `GET /api/reasoning` returns `supported_efforts` and `supports_reasoning_effort`, and accepts `model`/`provider` query params. This slice adopts the server's vocabulary — no client-side model-name heuristics (still forbidden).

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/models-providers/
- **Upstream:** `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py:11481` @ `312d3fab` — GET handler accepts `model`, `provider`, `base_url` query params and delegates to `get_reasoning_status(...)`. Upstream CHANGELOG (issue #3750 fix) and tests confirm `supported_efforts` drives the WebUI composer chip the same way.
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `GET /api/reasoning` → `{"show_reasoning":true,"reasoning_effort":"medium","supported_efforts":["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh"],"supports_reasoning_effort":true}`.

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+ServerPanels.swift:27` — `reasoning()` → `ReasoningStatusResponse` (does not decode the two new fields, never passes `model`/`provider`).
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:101` — seeds `selectedReasoningEffort` from the response.
- Static effort list in the composer menu + `SlashCommandCatalog.reasoningLevels`.

## Proposed slice

1. `ReasoningStatusResponse`: add optional `supportedEfforts: [String]?`, `supportsReasoningEffort: Bool?`.
2. `reasoning()` client: accept optional `model`/`provider` and pass as query params; call sites pass the session's current model/provider so the answer is model-accurate (mirrors the upstream WebUI chip behavior).
3. Composer: build the effort menu from `supportedEfforts` when present; fall back to the current static list when absent (older servers — tolerant decoding). Hide the effort control entirely when `supportsReasoningEffort == false`.
4. Re-query/refresh gating when the session's model changes (model picker, session update) — upstream fixed a stale-state bug here (their #3750); don't gate off stale session state.
5. If the currently selected effort is not in `supportedEfforts`, snap the UI to the server's `reasoning_effort` value.
6. Tests: decode with/without new fields, query construction, menu-filtering + hide logic, model-change refresh.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A model with limited efforts shows only those efforts in the composer menu.
- [ ] `supports_reasoning_effort == false` hides the effort control (no dead menu).
- [ ] Older servers without the fields behave exactly as today (full static menu).
- [ ] Switching models refreshes the gating without a stale flash of wrong options.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Client-side inference of capabilities from model/provider names (explicitly rejected in I-052).
- Slash-command filtering (`SlashCommandCatalog`) can adopt the same list only if trivial; otherwise out of scope.

## History

Old-repo I-052 (uzairansaruzi/hermes-mobile#4, closed not-planned 2026-06) is superseded by this issue now that upstream exposes the metadata it was waiting for.

title: Settings: expand SettingsResponse decode, drop phantom `version`, and sync the CLI-sessions toggle with the server
body:
## Context

`SettingsResponse` decodes only 4 fields (`botName`, `webuiVersion`, `version`, `theme`) out of the ~75 the server returns. Two concrete problems:

1. **Phantom field:** `version` is not in the docs and (verified live) not in the server response — it always decodes `nil`. Remove it.
2. **Cross-device drift:** the app's "Show CLI sessions" toggle is a purely local `@AppStorage` value, while the server has its own `show_cli_sessions` setting used by the WebUI. The phone and the browser can disagree forever. This slice makes the server the source of truth for that toggle.

**Trade-off (sync direction):** (a) read-only adoption — app displays/uses the server value, toggle writes it back via `POST /api/settings`; one source of truth, works across devices; needs a small write call. (b) keep local-only — no server write, but permanent drift. This issue specs (a): the write is tiny, documented, and scoped to this single key. A general settings-editor UI (bot name, max tokens, …) stays deferred.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/profiles-settings/ (`GET`/`POST /api/settings`).
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `GET /api/settings` returns (among ~75 keys) `bot_name`, `webui_version`, `agent_version`, `theme`, `check_for_updates`, `show_cli_sessions`, `max_tokens`, `max_tokens_effective`, `auth_enabled`, `password_auth_enabled`, `passkeys_enabled`, `passwordless_enabled`. **No `version` key.**
- **Upstream:** `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab` — validate the exact `POST /api/settings` accepted-keys/response shape just-in-time before coding and record it in the PR (hard rule #1).

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift:144` — `SettingsResponse` (4 fields incl. phantom `version`).
- `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:58` + `SessionListView.swift:45` — `@AppStorage(SessionRowDisplaySettings.showCliSessionsKey)` local toggle (key defined at `SessionRowView.swift:368`), feeding `AutomatedSessionVisibility` (`SessionListView.swift:499`).
- Old-repo #256 added the local cron/CLI filtering.

## Proposed slice

1. `SettingsResponse`: remove `version`; add optionals `agentVersion`, `checkForUpdates`, `showCliSessions`, `maxTokens`, `maxTokensEffective`, `authEnabled`, `passwordAuthEnabled`, `passkeysEnabled`, `passwordlessEnabled`. (Decode only what has a consumer or near-term use; all optional.)
2. On settings load, if the server provides `show_cli_sessions`, adopt it into the local AppStorage value (server wins on conflict — it's the cross-device truth).
3. Toggling "Show CLI sessions" writes `POST /api/settings {"show_cli_sessions": <bool>}` (exact body per just-in-time validation) and keeps the local value as an offline cache; on write failure, revert the toggle and surface the error.
4. Per-server isolation: the adopted value must respect the multi-server state isolation rules (`docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`) — a toggle on server A must not leak to server B.
5. Tests: decode (fields present/absent, no `version`), adopt-on-load, write body, revert-on-failure, per-server isolation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SettingsResponse.version` is gone; nothing references it.
- [ ] Changing the toggle on the phone changes what the WebUI shows (same server), and vice versa after a refresh.
- [ ] Servers that omit `show_cli_sessions` leave the local toggle behaving exactly as today.
- [ ] Failed write reverts with a visible error.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- A general settings-mutation UI (bot name, max tokens, theme) — deferred as its own future slice.
- Syncing the cron-sessions toggle (`show_cron_sessions` exists server-side; can follow the identical pattern later — kept out to keep this slice small).

## Wrap-up note

`docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` row `/api/settings` (`roadmap P3 secret`): note should record that the single-key `show_cli_sessions` write shipped; full Settings Write remains roadmap.

title: Memory: surface the project-context document (project_context, shadowed flag, external notes)
body:
## Context

The Memory screen shows the documents from `GET /api/memory`, but the response contains a **fourth document the app never decodes**: the workspace-scoped project context (`project_context`), plus a `project_context_shadowed` flag (true when a local workspace file overrides the global one) and `external_notes_enabled`. Users editing memory from the phone can't see a whole category of what the agent actually reads. This slice is **display-only**.

**Why read-only:** the write endpoint only accepts `section = "memory" | "user" | "soul"` (verified in the pinned handler — `_handle_memory_write`, routes.py @ `312d3fab`). `project_context` has **no write path**, so an edit UI is impossible without upstream changes.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/memory/
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `GET /api/memory` keys include `project_context`, `project_context_mtime`, `project_context_name`, `project_context_path`, `project_context_shadowed`, `project_context_workspace`, `external_notes_enabled` (alongside the already-decoded `memory`/`user`/`soul` triplets).
- **Upstream:** `_handle_memory_write` in `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab` — rejects any section other than `memory|user|soul` (and rejects symlinked targets).

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Models/Memory.swift:11` — `MemoryResponse` (no project-context fields).
- `HermesMobile/Features/Memory/MemoryViewModel.swift` + Memory views.

## Proposed slice

1. `MemoryResponse`: add optionals `projectContext: String?`, `projectContextName: String?`, `projectContextPath: String?`, `projectContextWorkspace: String?`, `projectContextShadowed: Bool?`, `externalNotesEnabled: Bool?` (mtime only if the UI shows it for the other docs).
2. Memory screen: add a read-only "Project Context" section showing the document (rendered like the others), its name/workspace, and a lock/read-only affordance instead of the edit action.
3. When `project_context_shadowed == true`, show a short caption ("A workspace-local file is overriding the global project context") — this is genuinely confusing without it.
4. Show an "External notes enabled" state only if it fits the existing screen naturally; otherwise skip (decode regardless).
5. Empty/absent handling: servers or workspaces without a project context omit/null the field — the section hides entirely.
6. Tests: tolerant decode (present/absent/null), view-model section visibility, shadowed caption logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a project context on the server, the document is readable in the Memory screen.
- [ ] No edit affordance exists for it (and the existing three documents' editing is untouched).
- [ ] Shadowed state shows the explanatory caption.
- [ ] Servers without the fields render the screen exactly as today.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Editing project context (no server write path — see above).
- The 400 symlink-rejection copy for the other documents' writes (candidate for the error-surfacing batch if trivial, otherwise skip).

title: Sessions: export a conversation (GET /api/session/export) to the iOS share sheet
body:
## Context

There is no way to get a conversation out of the app — no copy-all, no file export. Upstream has a documented export endpoint producing a JSON or HTML file. On iOS the natural shape is: session action → download export → present the **share sheet** (AirDrop, Files, Mail, …).

**Note on prior deferral:** `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` lists `/api/session/export` as `roadmap P4 — owner-deferred`. The owner re-approved it on 2026-07-02 during the API-docs gap-analysis triage; this issue supersedes that row's priority.

**Trade-off (format):** JSON is machine-readable (re-import later, pairs with `POST /api/session/import` — deferred); HTML is human-readable/self-contained and the better default for sharing. Simplest good UX: offer both in a small menu ("Export as HTML / Export as JSON"); if that bloats the slice, ship HTML only and leave JSON for later.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/sessions/ (`GET /api/session/export?session_id=…&format=json|html` — response is a **file download, not JSON**).
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `GET /api/session/export` without params → `400` (route present).
- **Upstream:** validate query params, response headers (filename/content-type) just-in-time in `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab` and record in the PR.

## Current app state

- No export endpoint case in `HermesMobile/Networking/Endpoints.swift`; session actions live in the session list / chat toolbar (follow existing action-menu patterns, e.g. rename/archive).
- Raw-`Data` download precedent: `APIClient+Transcribe.swift:12` bypasses the JSON `send()` helper (the TTS issue #15 adds a second precedent).

## Proposed slice

1. `Endpoints.swift`: `case exportSession(sessionID: String, format: ExportFormat)`.
2. `APIClient`: raw-`Data` GET returning the bytes + a suggested filename (from `Content-Disposition` if present, else `"<title-or-id>.<ext>"`).
3. Write to a temp file (`FileManager.temporaryDirectory`), present `ShareLink`/`UIActivityViewController` per existing app patterns; clean up the temp file after dismissal.
4. Add "Export…" to the session's action menu. Foreign/CLI sessions: include if the server exports them (validate just-in-time); otherwise hide the action there.
5. Error handling: 400/404 surface a short alert; large sessions may take a beat — show a progress state on the action.
6. Tests: endpoint/query construction, filename derivation, error mapping. Share-sheet presentation is manual.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exporting a session produces a file that opens correctly (HTML in Safari/Files; JSON is valid).
- [ ] Share sheet offers the file with a sensible filename (not "download.bin").
- [ ] Errors show a friendly alert, not a silent no-op.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- `POST /api/session/import` (deferred — pairs with this later).
- Export of attachments/media beyond what the server file contains.

## Wrap-up note

Update the `feature-gap-index.md` `/api/session/export` row (P4 owner-deferred → shipped; owner re-prioritized 2026-07-02).

title: Workspace: manage the registry from the app (add/remove/rename/reorder)
body:
## Context

The app can **list** workspaces and get path suggestions, but cannot add, remove, rename, or reorder them — for a mobile companion that's an asymmetry: you can point a session at any registered workspace but need a browser to register one. This slice adds registry management to the workspace picker/management surface.

**Stability caveat (understand before building):** these four routes are **not on the official docs site** — the docs deliberately exclude internal endpoints, and undocumented routes carry no stability promise across upstream releases. They are verified working on the owner's live server (final arbiter per CLAUDE.md hard rule #1) and present in the pinned upstream. Mitigation: tolerant decoding, graceful 404 handling (hide the management UI if a route disappears), and the upstream-watch digest will flag route changes.

## Evidence

- **Upstream:** `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab` — `/api/workspaces/add` (14042), `/remove` (14045), `/rename` (14048), `/reorder` (14051).
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02** (empty-body probes; 400 = route exists + required fields):
  - `add` → `{"error": "path is required"}`
  - `remove` → `{"error": "path is required"}`
  - `rename` → `{"error": "path and name are required"}`
  - `reorder` → `{"error": "paths is required and must be a list"}`
- Contract details from the handlers (re-validate just-in-time, record in PR): `add` rejects system-root paths and can auto-create the directory with a `create` flag; workspaces are identified by `path`.

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Networking/Endpoints.swift:44` — `case workspaces` (`/api/workspaces`), `case workspaceSuggestions` (`/api/workspaces/suggest`); read-only.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/` — picker UI.

## Proposed slice

1. `Endpoints.swift` + `APIClient`: four new POST methods (`addWorkspace(path:create:)`, `removeWorkspace(path:)`, `renameWorkspace(path:name:)`, `reorderWorkspaces(paths:)`) with shapes validated just-in-time.
2. Workspace management UI (sheet or edit mode on the existing picker): add (text field with the existing suggestions endpoint for autocomplete), rename, drag-to-reorder, swipe-to-remove.
3. **Remove requires a confirmation dialog** and copy must say it only unregisters the path — it does not delete files (verify that in the handler; if it does more, stop and re-scope). `write`-safety rule 8 from `feature-gap-index.md` applies.
4. Refetch the workspace list after each mutation (no optimistic reorder unless trivial).
5. Errors (invalid path, system-root rejection, duplicates) surface the server's `error` string.
6. Tests: endpoint/body construction for all four, view-model refetch + error paths, confirmation-gating for remove.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add / rename / reorder / remove all work against the live server and the list refreshes.
- [ ] Remove is confirmation-gated with non-destructive copy.
- [ ] A server without these routes (future drift): management affordances fail gracefully with the error surfaced — no crash, list still works.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- File browsing/mutation (`/api/file/*` — separate deferred surface), `/api/upload/extract`, folder download.

## Wrap-up note

`feature-gap-index.md` row `/api/workspaces/` (`roadmap P3 write`): update after shipping (add/remove/rename/reorder implemented; `/suggest` + list were already shipped).

title: Cron: delivery-options picker (replace free-text deliver) + provider field
body:
## Context

Two small cron-editor upgrades bundled into one slice because they touch the same editor:

1. **`deliver` is a free-text field** in the app's cron editor, but the server publishes the valid choices at `GET /api/crons/delivery-options` — a picker eliminates typos in a field where a typo silently misroutes job output.
2. **`provider`** is a documented field on cron create/update/display that the app's models don't carry — a cron can pin a model provider, and the app currently can't see or set it.

**Stability caveat:** `delivery-options` is not on the docs site (internal-endpoint exclusion) but is verified live; if it ever 404s, fall back to the current free-text field. `provider` is fully documented.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/cron/ (`provider` on create/update; job objects).
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `GET /api/crons/delivery-options` → `200` with `{"platforms": [{"value": "local", "label": "Local (save output only)"}, {"value": "origin", "label": "Origin (reply to creator)"}, …]}`.
- **Upstream:** `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py:12428` @ `312d3fab` (delivery-options); cron create/update handlers for `provider` — validate exact shapes just-in-time, record in PR.

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Models/Cron.swift:263` — `CronJobEditorDraft` (free-text `deliver`; no `provider`).
- Cron editor UI + `APIClient` cron methods (create/update bodies currently send `prompt`, `schedule`, `name`, `deliver`, `skills`, `model`, `profile`, `toast_notifications`).

## Proposed slice

1. `Endpoints.swift` + `APIClient`: `case cronDeliveryOptions` → GET, decoded as `[{value, label}]` (tolerant).
2. Cron editor: replace the free-text deliver field with a picker fed by the endpoint; keep the raw string in the draft so an unknown/legacy value still round-trips (show it as an extra "custom" row rather than clobbering it). If the endpoint fails, fall back to free text.
3. Add optional `provider: String?` to the cron job model + editor draft + create/update bodies; display it on the job detail row. Absent/nil = server default (send nothing).
4. Tests: delivery-options decode, picker fallback path, round-trip of an unknown deliver value, create/update body with/without provider.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deliver is chosen from server-provided options; existing jobs with values outside the list still display and save unchanged.
- [ ] Endpoint failure degrades to the current free-text behavior (no dead editor).
- [ ] Provider can be set on create/update, shows on the job, and omitting it preserves today's behavior.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Cron run-history view (`/api/crons/history`, `/recent` — verified live but deferred as its own future slice).

## Wrap-up note

`feature-gap-index.md` row `/api/crons/delivery-options` (`roadmap P2`): shipped here; `/api/crons/history` row stays roadmap.

title: Decode-gap batch: insights cache-efficiency stats + hide profile switcher in single-profile mode
body:
## Context

Two small, unrelated-but-tiny decode gaps batched into one slice (each is too small to justify its own PR ceremony; both are pure additive decoding plus a small UI read):

1. **Insights cache stats.** The server reports prompt-cache efficiency — top-level `total_cache_read_tokens` and `total_cache_hit_percent`, plus per-model `cache_hit_percent` / `cache_read_tokens` — none decoded. Cache hit rate is a genuinely useful cost signal on the Insights screen.
2. **Single-profile mode.** `GET /api/profiles` returns `single_profile_mode`; when `true`, profile switching is unavailable server-side, but the app still renders its profile switcher — which can only no-op or error. Hide it.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/insights-updates/ and https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/profiles-settings/
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:**
  - `GET /api/insights?days=7` top-level keys include `total_cache_hit_percent`, `total_cache_read_tokens`; per-model entries include `cache_hit_percent`, `cache_read_tokens`.
  - `GET /api/profiles` → `{"keys": ["active", "profiles", "single_profile_mode"], …}`.

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Features/Insights/InsightsModels.swift:3` (`InsightsResponse`), `:46` (`InsightsModelBreakdown`).
- `HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift:339` (`ProfilesResponse` — no `single_profile_mode`); profile switcher UI in Settings/session surfaces.

## Proposed slice

1. `InsightsResponse`: add optional `totalCacheReadTokens: Int?`, `totalCacheHitPercent: Double?`; `InsightsModelBreakdown`: add optional `cacheHitPercent: Double?` (+ `cacheReadTokens: Int?` if displayed).
2. Insights screen: show cache hit % where the other totals live, and per-model hit % in the breakdown rows — follow the existing formatting/layout patterns; hide when nil (older servers).
3. `ProfilesResponse`: add optional `singleProfileMode: Bool?`; when `true`, hide the profile switcher affordances (nil/false = today's behavior).
4. Tests: tolerant decode for all new fields (present/absent), switcher visibility logic, insights formatting with nil.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cache stats render on Insights against the live server; absent fields hide cleanly.
- [ ] `single_profile_mode: true` removes the profile switcher; existing multi-profile behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Other `ProfileSummary` field gaps (`visible`, `enabled_skills`, `total_skills` are live on the server but have no UI consumer yet — decode only when something uses them).
- The undocumented `has_env` field question (live server does return it; no action needed).

title: Error-surfacing batch: terminal apperror SSE event · stale-approval 409 · session-move 503 while streaming
body:
## Context

Three small fixes where the server tells us exactly what went wrong and the app drops or genericizes the message. Batched because they share one theme (surface server errors properly) and each is a few lines plus tests.

### 1. `apperror` SSE event is silently swallowed (the important one)

The docs define `apperror` as a **terminal** SSE frame that closes the socket — one of only four socket-closing frames (`stream_end`, `cancel`, `error`, `apperror`). The app's SSE decoder doesn't know it: it falls into the `default` branch → `.ignored` (`HermesMobile/Networking/SSEClient.swift:243`). The stream then dies, reconnect logic eventually recovers, but the **app-level error message the server sent is never shown** — the user just sees a turn end strangely. Map `apperror` to the same handling as `error` (surface payload message, mark terminal).

### 2. Stale approval/clarify responses surface as generic errors

Responding to an approval that already expired returns 409 with `{"stale": true, "error": …}`, and successful responds carry `stale_cleared`/`relayed`. None decoded (`HermesMobile/Models/Approval.swift:143`, `Models/Clarification.swift:168`) — an expired prompt shows a generic failure instead of a friendly "this prompt already expired" state that just dismisses the card.

### 3. `session/move` returns 503 while the session is streaming

Documented behavior. The app (`Endpoints.swift:136` moveSession) shows a generic error; it should say "can't move a session while it's responding — try again when it finishes."

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/chat-streaming/ (SSE vocabulary + terminal frames), https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/approvals-clarify/ (respond shapes, 409), https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/sessions/ (move 503).
- **Upstream:** `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab`; validate the exact `apperror` payload shape and respond-response fields just-in-time, record in PR.
- SSE guide: clients MUST ignore unknown events — that tolerance stays; `apperror` becomes *known*.

## Proposed slice

1. `SSEClient.decode`: add `apperror` case → decode its message payload (same/similar shape as `error`; validate) and emit the existing terminal-error event so ChatViewModel's error path runs unchanged.
2. `ApprovalRespondResponse` / `ClarificationRespondResponse`: add optional `staleCleared`, `relayed`, `stale`; on 409-with-`stale`, show the expired state and clear the pending card instead of a failure alert.
3. Session move: map 503 to the specific user-facing message.
4. Tests: SSE decode of `apperror` (with and without message), terminality (no events processed after), stale-409 mapping, respond-response decode, move-503 mapping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A server-sent `apperror` shows its message in the chat error surface (no more silent drop) and the turn terminates cleanly.
- [ ] Unknown SSE event types are still ignored (no regression on tolerance).
- [ ] Expired approval → friendly expired state, card clears; fresh approvals unchanged.
- [ ] Moving a streaming session explains itself instead of failing generically.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Reconnect-logic changes (`replay_available`/`journal.terminal` decode is deferred — reconnect works today).

title: Settings: read-only Providers status screen (wire up the dead providers() client)
body:
## Context

`APIClient.providers()` and `ProvidersResponse` exist but are **dead code** — declared, never called, and the model is a stub (`providers: [JSONValue]?`). Meanwhile the server returns rich per-provider status: which providers have keys, where the key comes from (env/oauth/config), whether auth is currently erroring, and each provider's model list. A **read-only** status screen answers real questions from the phone: "why is my model failing — did the key expire?", "which providers does this server actually have configured?"

**Scope decision (trade-off):** upstream also supports *managing* keys (set/delete — `secret` safety class). That's deliberately out: entering API keys on a phone into a self-hosted server needs its own UX/safety thinking. Read-only status is high value at near-zero risk and this issue stays a display slice. Key management can be a follow-up if ever wanted.

## Evidence

- **Docs:** https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/models-providers/
- **Live server verified 2026-07-02:** `GET /api/providers` → `{"active_provider": …, "providers": [{"id": "openai-codex", "display_name": "OpenAI Codex", "has_key": true, "configurable": false, "is_plugin_provider": false, "is_oauth": true, "key_source": "oauth", "auth_error": null, "models": [{"id": "gpt-5.5", "label": "GPT 5.5"}, …], "models_total": 5}, …]}`.
- **Upstream:** `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab` — re-validate the full per-provider field set just-in-time (some fields may appear only for certain provider types) and record in the PR.

## Current app state

- `HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+ServerPanels.swift:71` — `providers()` (never called).
- `HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift:139` — `ProvidersResponse` stub (`[JSONValue]?` + `activeProvider`).
- Settings screens under `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/`.

## Proposed slice

1. Replace the stub with a real tolerant model: `ProviderSummary` with optionals `id`, `displayName`, `hasKey`, `configurable`, `isPluginProvider`, `isOauth`, `keySource`, `authError`, `models: [ProviderModel]?` (`id`, `label`), `modelsTotal`.
2. New "Providers" screen reachable from Settings (follow the existing server-panel navigation patterns): one row per provider — name, active indicator (matches `active_provider`), key status (✓ has key / source badge: env · oauth · config), and a prominent error line when `auth_error` is non-null.
3. Tapping a provider expands/pushes its model list (`models` + "N total" when truncated).
4. Loading/error/empty states per existing Settings-panel patterns.
5. Tests: tolerant decode of the live shape (and with fields absent), active-provider matching, auth-error presentation logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Providers screen lists the live server's providers with key status and active indicator.
- [ ] A provider with `auth_error` set shows the error text clearly.
- [ ] No write affordances anywhere on the screen (read-only by design).
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Non-goals

- API-key set/delete (`secret` safety class — needs its own product decision), provider quota/cost history (`/api/provider/…`), model refresh actions.

## Wrap-up note

`feature-gap-index.md` row `/api/providers` (`roadmap P3 secret — set/delete API keys`): after this ships, the note should read "read status shipped; key set/delete remains roadmap".

title: Tracking: API-docs gap-analysis implementation (#15–#26)
body:
## What this is

Master tracking issue for the 12 issues produced by the 2026-07-02 API-docs gap analysis (official docs at get-hermes.ai/api-docs vs. what Hermex implements). Every issue was verified against the live server on 2026-07-02 and is self-contained + `ready-for-agent`. Work them **top to bottom** — the order below is deliberate.

## Ordering rationale

- **Phase 1 first** because the two batches are pure decode/error-mapping with near-zero regression risk — they warm up the tolerant-decoding patterns everything else uses, and #25 fixes a real silent-error bug (`apperror`).
- **Phase 2** are the small high-value features, ordered so the first server *write* surfaces are tiny and well-bounded (#16 toggle → #19 single settings key).
- **Phase 3** pairs the two issues that share new infrastructure: #15 introduces the raw-`Data` (non-JSON) response path; #21 reuses it plus adds the share-sheet flow. Do #15 first — it's the flagship and the pattern-setter.
- **Phase 4** holds the larger/riskier surfaces: bigger list UI (#17), independent new screens (#26, #23), and last the write-heavy workspace registry (#22), which also carries undocumented-route drift risk.

## Checklist (execution order)

### Phase 1 — decode + error-surfacing warm-ups (small, zero-risk)
- [ ] #24 Decode batch: insights cache stats + `single_profile_mode`
- [ ] #25 Error batch: `apperror` SSE · stale-approval 409 · move-503

### Phase 2 — small high-value features
- [ ] #16 Skills: enable/disable toggle + `disabled`/`tags` decode
- [ ] #18 Chat: gate reasoning-effort picker via `supported_efforts`
- [ ] #20 Memory: surface the project-context document (read-only)
- [ ] #19 Settings: decode expansion + `show_cli_sessions` server sync (first `POST /api/settings` write)

### Phase 3 — flagship + shared raw-Data infrastructure (in this order)
- [ ] #15 Chat: "Read aloud" via server TTS with on-device fallback ⚑ flagship, `needs-manual-validation`
- [ ] #21 Sessions: export conversation → share sheet (reuses #15's raw-`Data` pattern)

### Phase 4 — larger surfaces & write-heavy work
- [ ] #17 Sessions: archived view + unarchive
- [ ] #26 Settings: read-only Providers status screen
- [ ] #23 Cron: delivery-options picker + `provider` field
- [ ] #22 Workspace: registry add/remove/rename/reorder (write-heavy; undocumented-route caveat)

## Ground rules for every slice

- One issue → one `issue/<n>-slug` branch → one PR (see `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`).
- Just-in-time shape validation against `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` before coding; record shape + handler + upstream commit in the PR (`docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` rules).
- Tolerant decoding everywhere; full XCTest suite before review; update the relevant feature-gap-index row at wrap-up (each issue's "Wrap-up note" says which).
- The order is a default, not a law — any Phase 2+ issue can be picked out of order if it becomes urgent, **except** #21, which should follow #15.

## Not in scope (triage record)

Dropped: `updates/summary` (undocumented, fires a server LLM call), `commands/exec` (needs product framing). Deferred pending owner opt-in: session import, `replay_available` decode, cron history view, auxiliary model routing, settings-editor UI, profile create/delete, `/api/file/*` mutations + folder zip, skill authoring, command bundles. Full detail lives in the local (untracked) `api-docs-gap-analysis.md` at the repo root.

title: Decode-gap batch: insights cache-efficiency stats + single-profile mode + profile creation
body:
Fixes #24

## Summary

Two small decode gaps batched per the issue, plus an owner-requested addition during the plan gate (create-profile instead of hiding the Settings row):

1. **Insights cache-efficiency stats.** `InsightsResponse` now decodes `total_cache_read_tokens` / `total_cache_hit_percent`, and `InsightsModelBreakdown` decodes `cache_hit_percent` — all optional and lossy (string/int/double tolerated). The Insights screen shows **Cache Hit Rate** and **Cache Read Tokens** cards alongside the existing totals and a "N% cache" caption in model rows; every new surface hides when the server omits the field (older servers, local fallback).
2. **Single-profile mode.** `ProfilesResponse` decodes `single_profile_mode`. When `true`, profile switching is unavailable server-side, so the app hides the switcher affordances: the session-sidebar "Active Profile" disclosure and the composer profile pill. `nil`/`false` keeps today's behavior. The switch response has no such field, so the last known value is carried forward.
3. **Profile creation (owner amendment).** The Settings → Default Profile picker keeps its row and gains a **New Profile** button + form sheet, backed by a new `APIClient.createProfile(name:)` → `POST /api/profile/create` (name-only body this slice). Client-side validation mirrors upstream's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` name rule; server errors surface in the sheet. The affordance hides in single-profile mode, where the server 403s creation.

## API verification (hard rule 1)

- `GET /api/profiles` → `single_profile_mode` verified on the live server 2026-07-02 (issue evidence) and in pinned upstream `routes.py` (`_is_isolated_profile_mode()`).
- `POST /api/profile/create` verified on the **live server** via a safe empty-body probe (`400 {"error": "name is required"}` — no profile created) and in pinned upstream `routes.py:14154` (request fields, `{ok, profile}` success shape, 403 in isolated mode).
- Insights cache fields verified live per the issue evidence (top-level + per-model keys present on `GET /api/insights?days=7`).

## Localization

All 7 new user-facing strings were appended to `Localizable.xcstrings` with translations for the 17 shipped languages (glossary-consistent with existing Profile/Tokens/cache terms), keeping `LocalizationCatalogTests` green. That's most of the diff's line count.

## Validation

title: Monorepo Android Port
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #— (no issue exists for this work; the plan, migration, and Android build phases were requested directly by the maintainer in the working session. Happy to open a tracking issue retroactively if preferred.)

## What changed

This PR takes the repo from "iOS app at the root" to "monorepo with a working Android app at feature parity with the port plan's v1 scope, styled to match the iPhone app."

**1. The plan.** `docs/ANDROID_PORT_PLAN.md`: native Kotlin + Jetpack Compose in this repo as a monorepo, a tech-stack mapping from the locked iOS list, a phased build checklist (updated live — deferred items are unchecked), a shared contract-test strategy pinned to `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA`, risks, and a long-term KMP option.

**2. Monorepo migration.** Everything Apple moved under `ios/` via pure `git mv` (history preserved), including `DEVELOPMENT.md`/`TESTFLIGHT.md`; every path reference updated (CI workflows, `.xcodebuildmcp`, scripts, docs, this PR template's test command); `AGENTS.md` split into a platform-neutral root + `ios/`/`android/` layers; `shared/fixtures/` created for the future cross-platform contract corpus. `pr-ci.yml` keeps its docs-only skip and now also skips the macOS runner for Android-only changes; a new `android-ci.yml` builds and tests the Android app with the same gate-job pattern.

**3. The Android app (`android/`), phases 0–10 of the plan:**
- **Networking + auth:** OkHttp `ApiClient` on the pinned upstream contract with tolerant kotlinx decoding and iOS-parity error mapping; the `hermes_session` cookie persisted host-scoped through an Android-Keystore-backed secret store; the Tailscale plain-HTTP rule (100.64.0.0/10 + loopback only) enforced in the connection layer since Android's Network Security Config can't express CIDR; `AuthManager` mirroring the iOS state machine (health→auth-status probe, passkey-only detection, persist-on-success, 401 demotion, bounded best-effort logout).
- **Onboarding:** welcome → reachability guidance → connect, with the probe, conditional password field, and troubleshooting checklist.
- **Sessions:** list/search/create with a Room raw-JSON offline cache (401 always surfaces past the cache), pinned-first sort, rename/delete/pin/archive via long-press.
- **Chat:** SSE streaming over okhttp-sse with the full iOS event vocabulary (token / reasoning / interim_assistant / tool / tool_complete / title / done / cancel / stream_end / error, unknown types ignored), steer-while-running, stop, and authoritative transcript rebuild from `done`.
- **Composer:** model/workspace/profile selectors riding on `/api/chat/start`, photo attachments via multipart `/api/upload` (byte-compatible with the iOS encoding), slash-command autocomplete from `/api/commands`.
- **Workspace + git (read-only):** file browser, monospace file preview, git status / colored diff / branches.
- **Server panels:** Tasks (cron run/pause/resume), Skills, Memory, Insights.
- **Settings + platform:** default-model picker, theme choice, share-target (text → new chat), run-complete notifications posted only when backgrounded.
- **Polish:** haptics, crossfade navigation, animated banners, empty/error states with retry.

**4. iOS design parity.** A `HermexTheme` design system extracted from the shipping app (`AppTheme.swift`'s `#FFD700` Header Logo Color, pure-black canvas, iOS system grays) and screen layouts matched to the App Store screenshots: HERMEX wordmark home with menu rows and relative-time session list, the white "✎ Chat" pill, gray user bubbles with plain assistant text, collapsible "Thinking" cards, the rounded "Ask anything... /commands" composer whose send circle becomes stop mid-run, and workspace/profile pills.

**Deferred, tracked as unchecked plan boxes:** streaming markdown rendering, approvals/clarifications overlays, voice input, context-window indicator, git mutations, cron create/edit, regenerate/listen, image share-in, ongoing-run notification, Play Console listing (needs the maintainer's Play account + final `applicationId` decision).

## How it was tested

- **Android:** `cd android && ./gradlew build` green locally — **88/88 unit tests** — and re-verified by Android CI on every push. Coverage concentrates on what unit tests can prove: endpoint contract paths/queries/bodies for every API used (sessions, chat, catalog, multipart upload, workspace, git, crons, skills, memory, insights), the SSE parser plus a real `text/event-stream` wire test, the auth/chat/onboarding state machines, cache fallback + 401 pass-through, and tolerant decoding incl. malformed-element drops. The `ComposerConfigTest` caught a real bug pre-merge (Kotlin `buildMap` receiver's `Map.size` shadowing the attachment's `size` field).
- **iOS:** the full XCTest suite ran on this PR's CI against the migrated `ios/` layout — `TEST SUCCEEDED` (one re-run was needed for a simulator-clone launch flake, unrelated to this diff). Phases 5–10 and the restyle touch no iOS code, so later pushes skip the macOS runner by path filter.
- **Manual steps for UI review** (no emulator in the CI environment, so screenshots are pending a device run): `cd android && ./gradlew installDebug`, onboard against a real hermes-webui server, then walk sessions → chat (send/steer/stop, attach a photo, slash commands) → files/git → panels → settings, comparing against the iPhone app side by side.
- All endpoint paths and JSON shapes were read from the pinned upstream source (`.codex-tmp/hermes-webui` at `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA`) and the shipping iOS client — never invented.

title: Error-surfacing batch: terminal apperror SSE · stale-approval 409 · session-move 503 (#25)
body:
Fixes #25

## Plan (E1 — pre-approved for this unattended run)

Smallest slice per the issue:

1. **`SSEClient.decode`**: add `"apperror"` to the existing `"error"` case — decode via the existing `ErrorPayload` (`error`/`message` keys) and emit the existing terminal `.error` event so ChatStreamCoordinator/ChatViewModel error handling runs unchanged. Unknown event types stay `.ignored`.
2. **Respond responses**: add tolerant optional `stale`, `staleCleared` (`stale_cleared`), `relayed` to `ApprovalRespondResponse` / `ClarificationRespondResponse`; add `APIError.indicatesExpiredPendingPrompt` (409 + `{"stale": true}` body). In `ChatPendingActionCoordinator`, on that error dismiss the stale card, surface a friendly "already expired" message, and refresh pending state.
3. **Session move**: in `SessionMutator.move`, map a 503 that carries the server's JSON error payload to a specific `SessionMoveWhileStreamingError`; a proxy/tunnel 503 without a JSON body keeps the generic connectivity message.
4. **Tests**: apperror decode (upstream + docs shapes, missing message, malformed payload), terminality through the stream coordinator, unknown-event tolerance regression, respond-response tolerant decode, approval + clarification stale-409 end-to-end through ChatViewModel, move-503 mapping and proxy-503 passthrough.
5. New user-facing strings externalized and translated in all 17 app languages.

## Upstream shape validation (recorded per issue instructions)

Validated just-in-time against the pinned upstream @ `312d3fab`:

- **`apperror` payload** — `api/streaming.py` `_provider_error_payload`: `{"message", "type", "hint"?, "details"?}`; docs describe `{"error", "type", "session", "terminal_state"?}`. The existing `ErrorPayload {error?, message?}` covers both; both shapes are unit-tested.
- **Clarify respond stale** — `api/routes.py` `_handle_clarify_respond`: 409 `{"ok": false, "error": "Clarification prompt expired or not found. …", "stale": true}`.
- **Approval respond** — benign stale click on an empty queue returns **200** `{"ok": true, "choice": …, "stale_cleared": true}` (decoded, treated as success); gateway relay adds `"relayed"`; the docs' 409-with-`stale` contract is what `indicatesExpiredPendingPrompt` matches. A gateway `gateway_run_unavailable` 409 has no `stale` field and intentionally keeps the generic error.
- **Session move busy** — `api/routes.py` `/api/session/move`: bounded lock acquire → 503 `{"error": "Session is busy (streaming). Please try again in a moment."}`.

## Behavior changed (plain English)

- A server-sent terminal `apperror` frame now shows its message in the chat error surface and ends the turn cleanly, instead of being silently ignored until reconnect gives up.
- Answering an approval/clarification that already expired now dismisses the card and says the prompt expired, instead of a generic failure with a stuck card.
- Moving a session while it is still responding now says exactly that, instead of a generic server error.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` clean.
- Full XCTest suite: `xcodebuild test -scheme HermesMobile` on iPhone 17 simulator (Hermex-W1) — **TEST SUCCEEDED** on the head commit.

## Owner manual checks

- [ ] Start a chat turn that triggers a provider failure (e.g. break the provider key server-side) → the error message appears in chat; turn ends cleanly; no stuck spinner.
- [ ] Trigger an approval, let it expire/resolve elsewhere (respond from the WebUI first), then answer it in the app → card dismisses with the "already expired" message, no generic failure alert.
- [ ] Same for a clarification prompt.
- [ ] While a session is actively streaming, try to move it to another project → specific "still responding, try again when it finishes" message; moving an idle session still works.
- [ ] Normal streaming, fresh approvals/clarifications, and session moves behave exactly as before.

title: Chat: Listen prefers server TTS (POST /api/tts) with on-device fallback
body:
Fixes #15

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Owner manual validation required before merge** (issue is labeled `needs-manual-validation`; express mode used per owner override for the unattended 2026-07-03 batch run).

## Manual validation checklist (owner)

- [ ] **Neural server audio:** Long-press an assistant message → **Listen**. After a short fetch, audio plays through the **speaker** with a neural voice (noticeably better than the robotic on-device voice).
- [ ] **Offline fallback:** Enable Airplane Mode → Listen still speaks via the on-device synthesizer, and **no error alert** appears for the silent fallback.
- [ ] **Rapid double-tap:** Tap Listen twice quickly on the same message. The second tap acts as Stop; audio never stacks and no raw "429/rate limit" error surfaces.
- [ ] **Stop semantics (both engines):** "Stop Listening" stops server audio mid-play; it also stops the on-device voice (test in Airplane Mode). Starting Listen on another message stops the current one.
- [ ] **Long message:** Listen on a >5000-character assistant reply speaks immediately with the on-device voice (server call skipped by design).
- [ ] **No earpiece regression:** Audio comes from the loudspeaker, not the receiver/earpiece (#252 behavior preserved).

## What changed

"Listen" on assistant messages now prefers the server's neural TTS (`POST /api/tts`, edge engine — no API key needed) and falls back **silently** to the existing on-device `AVSpeechSynthesizer` when the server can't serve the request (offline, 4xx/5xx, rate limit, undecodable audio).

- `Endpoints.swift`: new `case tts` → `/api/tts`.
- `APIClient+TTS.swift` (new): `synthesizeSpeech(text:voice:)` returns raw audio `Data` via the existing `sendData` seam (401 → `.unauthorized`; other non-2xx → `.http` carrying the server's `{"error": …}` body). The server fully buffers the response, so a single-shot download is correct — no streaming.
- `ChatViewModel.swift`:
  - `ServerTTSPolicy`: 5000-char server cap routes long text straight to the on-device path (chunking is a non-goal); default voice `en-US-AriaNeural` (the server's own default is `zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`, so the client must always send a voice — verified live 2026-07-02).
  - `ListenAudioPlaying` protocol + `ServerTTSAudioPlayer` (`AVAudioPlayer` wrapper) with an injectable factory so playback is unit-testable.
  - `toggleListening`: tapping the already-listening message — while fetching **or** playing on either engine — toggles off. This also debounces rapid double-taps so a second `/api/tts` call never fires into the server's ~2 s rate limit.
  - `stopListening`: cancels the in-flight fetch (stale responses are dropped by request-ID guard), stops the `AVAudioPlayer`, stops the synthesizer, releases the audio session. The #252 `.playback`/speaker routing and stale-callback guards are preserved and mirrored for the new player.

## Plan (E1, pre-approved for this unattended run)

1. Add `/api/tts` endpoint case. 2. Raw-`Data` APIClient method reusing `sendData`. 3. Server-first Listen with silent on-device fallback, >5000-char bypass, double-tap debounce, unified stop semantics. 4. Unit tests for endpoint/body construction, error mapping, fallback routing, cancellation, and the 5000-char boundary. 5. Register new files in `project.pbxproj`. Playback itself is owner manual validation.

## Decisions made unattended

- **Voice constant, not locale-mapped:** always sends `en-US-AriaNeural` (the issue's example voice, verified live). A locale-aware voice map (13 app languages) risks inventing voice names outside the verified allowlist; a voice picker is an explicit non-goal. Flagged as a possible follow-up.
- **Toggle-off on second tap of the same message** (previously required `isSpeaking`): matches the menu's "Stop Listening" label state and is what debounces double-taps during the async fetch.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` clean.
- Full XCTest suite (`xcodebuild test`, scheme `HermesMobile`) on simulator Hermex-W0 (iPhone 17): **1198 passed, 0 failures** on the head commit.
- No new third-party dependencies; no new user-facing strings (silent fallback), so no localization changes.

title: Chat: gate the reasoning-effort picker per model via supported_efforts (#18)
body:
Fixes #18

## Summary

The composer's reasoning-effort menu was a static list (`none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh`) regardless of model. `GET /api/reasoning` now returns `supported_efforts` + `supports_reasoning_effort` and accepts `model`/`provider` query params, so the app adopts the server's vocabulary — no client-side model-name heuristics (the old I-052 constraint still holds).

- A model with limited efforts shows only those efforts in the menu (server order, unknown ids kept with capitalized titles).
- `supports_reasoning_effort == false` hides the effort control entirely.
- Older servers without the fields keep exactly today's behavior (full static menu, control visible) via tolerant optional decoding.
- Gating refreshes when the model changes (composer picker, `/model` slash command) and on every composer config load (initial load, profile switch). The refresh is token-guarded so an out-of-order response can never apply a stale model's gating (upstream #3750 class of bug), and it runs inside the `isUpdatingComposerConfiguration` window so the menu is disabled until the new model's gating lands.
- If the currently selected effort is not in `supported_efforts`, the UI snaps to the server's coerced `reasoning_effort`.

## Plan (E1, pre-approved for this unattended run)

1. `ReasoningStatusResponse`: optional `supportedEfforts` / `supportsReasoningEffort` + `normalizedSupportedEfforts` (trim/lowercase/dedupe, order preserved).
2. `Endpoint.reasoning(model:provider:)` emits `model`/`provider` query items; `APIClient.reasoning(model:provider:)` with nil defaults (POST save paths unchanged).
3. Loader scopes the reasoning query to the session's resolved model/provider and captures the gating fields into `ChatComposerConfigState`.
4. `ChatViewModel.refreshReasoningEffortGating()` — silent-failure, token-guarded; hooks after `selectComposerModel` and the `/model` slash command; snap-to-server for unsupported selections.
5. `ComposerReasoningMenu` builds options via `ReasoningEffortOption.options(forSupportedEfforts:)`; `showsEffortControl(...)` decides visibility; wiring through `MessageComposerView`/`ChatView`.
6. Tests at every layer (see below).

## Evidence

- Upstream pinned copy: `api/routes.py:11481` (GET accepts `model`/`provider`/`base_url`) and `api/config.py get_reasoning_status` (returns coerced `reasoning_effort`, `supported_efforts`, `supports_reasoning_effort = bool(supported_efforts)`) @ `312d3fab`.
- Live server verified 2026-07-02 (issue body): returns both new fields.

## Out of scope (issue non-goals)

- `SlashCommandCatalog.reasoningLevels` filtering (static `/reasoning` autocomplete list unchanged; the server still validates/coerces).
- Client-side capability inference from model/provider names (explicitly rejected in I-052).
- Passive external model changes (another client editing the session) refresh at the next composer config load rather than instantly; both in-app model-change paths refresh immediately.

## Validation

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 sim (Hermex-W1): **1199 tests, 0 failures** on the head commit (`xcodebuild test -parallel-testing-enabled NO`).
- New/updated tests: response decoding with/without the new fields + normalization; endpoint query contract; loader query scoping + field capture; option filtering / hide logic (`ReasoningEffortGatingTests`); model-change refresh, snap-to-coerced-effort, hide-on-unsupported, and silent-failure behavior in `ChatViewModelSendTests`.

## Owner manual checks

1. Open a chat on a model with a limited effort set (e.g. an OpenAI reasoning model) — the composer Reasoning menu should list only the server's efforts.
2. Switch to a model that doesn't support reasoning effort — the Reasoning control should disappear (no dead menu); switch back and it returns.
3. With an effort selected that the new model doesn't support, switch models — the chip should snap to the server's effort, not keep the stale one.
4. Against an older server (if available): full static menu, identical to today.

title: Sessions: make archived sessions reachable (include_archived) with count entry + unarchive surfacing
body:
## Summary

Archived sessions were a roach motel: the app can archive a session, and a Settings → Archived Sessions screen exists, but its fetch called `GET /api/sessions` **without** `include_archived=1` — and the server's default response excludes archived rows entirely, so the screen was permanently empty and archived sessions were unreachable (the live server reports 8 of them). This PR fixes the root cause and makes archived sessions discoverable.

- **API layer:** `Endpoint.sessions` gains `includeArchived` / `archivedLimit` (query `include_archived=1`, `archived_limit=<n>`); the default request stays parameterless so the main list is byte-identical.
- **Root-cause fix:** `ArchivedSessionsViewModel.load()` now opts in with `include_archived=1` and filters rows client-side on the `archived` flag.
- **Model:** `SessionsResponse` decodes `archived_count` (optional — older servers that omit it still decode).
- **Discoverability:** the session list shows an "Archived Sessions" entry with a count at the bottom when the server reports archived sessions (hidden while searching, offline, or at count 0 / missing field — the list is unchanged for users with nothing archived).
- **Archived screen:** rows now open in `ChatView` (normal read path, unchanged) and get an always-visible unarchive button next to the existing context-menu action; unarchive errors forward to the shared API-error handler (401 → re-login).
- **Error surfacing:** archive/unarchive rejections (subagent, read-only imported CLI sessions) arrive as HTTP 400 + `{"error": ...}` and surface the server's message verbatim; a 200 body carrying an `error` field is surfaced too.

## Plan (E1, pre-approved for this unattended run)

1. Verify the contract against the pinned upstream (`.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` @ `312d3fab`): `include_archived`/`archived_limit` are query params; the merged response rows each carry an `archived` flag (the handler filters on `s.get("archived")`), `archived_count` is present on every response, and `POST /api/session/archive {"archived": false}` unarchives. ✔ (matches the issue's live-server verification of 2026-07-02)
2. Add opt-in `include_archived`/`archived_limit` to `Endpoint.sessions` + `APIClient.sessions` (defaults keep today's request).
3. Decode `archived_count` on `SessionsResponse`; expose it on `SessionListViewModel`.
4. Fix `ArchivedSessionsViewModel.load()` to send `include_archived=1`; keep client-side `archived == true` filtering (validated above).
5. Surface unarchive rejections (thrown HTTP 400 with server message, plus `error` field on 200) and restore the optimistically removed row on failure.
6. UI: bottom-of-list "Archived Sessions" entry with count → existing Archived screen (also still reachable from Settings); tap-to-open archived sessions; visible unarchive affordance.
7. Tests: endpoint contract matrix, query construction on/off, tolerant decode with/without `archived_count`, unarchive body shape, rejection-message surfacing, view-model filtering/count exposure.

## Decisions recorded

- **Archived row detection:** merged `include_archived=1` response + client-side `archived` filter (no separate endpoint); flag verified in the pinned handler, matching the issue's just-in-time validation ask.
- **`archived_limit`** is supported in the API layer but not sent by the archived screen (it wants all archived rows); it is only emitted alongside `include_archived=1`, mirroring upstream semantics.
- A parameterless `APIClient.sessions()` overload is kept so the `InsightsDataClient` protocol witness still matches.
- The new list-entry strings reuse the already-translated "Archived Sessions" catalog key; no new translation keys were introduced.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` clean.
- Full XCTest suite: `xcodebuild test -scheme HermesMobile -destination "id=12128609-569F-45F8-B87B-1C18E1A40068"` → **TEST SUCCEEDED** on the head commit.

## Owner manual checks

1. Session list → scroll to the bottom: an "Archived Sessions" row with a count badge (live server: 8) appears below the sessions. It is hidden while searching and when offline.
2. Tap it → the Archived screen lists the archived sessions (previously empty).
3. Tap an archived session → it opens read-only-as-usual in chat.
4. Tap the unarchive icon (or long-press → Unarchive) → the row disappears; go back → the session is in the main list again without relaunching, and the bottom count drops by one.
5. Settings → Archived Sessions still reaches the same screen.
6. Archive a subagent/read-only imported CLI session (or unarchive one) → the alert shows the server's own message, not a generic error.

title: Onboarding prompt: tailscale serve --bg 8787 silently clobbers port 443
body:
## Suggestion: Add port-443 safety check to onboarding prompt

The onboarding prompt in `OnboardingFlowPolicy.swift` instructs users to run:

```
tailscale serve --bg 8787
```

The problem: when Tailscale Serve is run without an explicit `--https` port, it defaults to port 443. If the user already has a service on port 443 (e.g., Nightscout via Funnel, or any other service), this command **silently replaces** the existing route with no warning.

### Proposed fix

Add a safety check before the `tailscale serve --bg` instruction:

> Before starting, if tailscale is installed and is actively funneling a service that is critical, first run `tailscale serve status` to check if any service is already listening on port 443. If there is, skip the bare `tailscale serve --bg 8787` and use `tailscale serve --bg --https=8787 127.0.0.1:8787` instead — this puts the WebUI on its own dedicated port without disturbing existing services.

Alternatively, the prompt could be changed to always use the explicit `--https=8787` form, which is the safer default.

### Reference

Forks with the fix applied:
https://github.com/Rotor101riot/hermex

title: Chat composer keyboard transition shifts horizontally on iPhone
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Hermex native iPhone app in portrait orientation on the **home page**.
2. Tap the chat button (bottom-right corner) to **create a new session/conversation**.
3. The keyboard appears with a horizontal drift animation instead of rising vertically.
4. For comparison: opening the keyboard in an **already-existing session** produces a normal vertical transition.

The keyboard horizontal drift specifically occurs during the "create new session" entry point from the home page. In an already-open conversation, the keyboard animation behaves normally.

## Expected behavior

The keyboard transition should look like a native chat composer:

- The keyboard stays full viewport width during the transition.
- The keyboard moves vertically from/to the bottom edge.
- The composer/input accessory stays visually attached to the keyboard and moves in sync.
- The chat view should not reveal horizontal clipping, side-shift, or side-panel-like movement while the keyboard appears or disappears.

## Actual behavior

In a local portrait screen recording, focusing the composer makes the keyboard transition look visibly broken/uncomfortable:

- During keyboard appearance/disappearance, the app view and/or composer briefly shifts or clips horizontally.
- The keyboard can appear partially from the side before settling into place.
- The composer does not look synchronized with the keyboard throughout the transition.
- The issue repeats across several focus/dismiss cycles in the same recording.
- Reproducibility: happens every time.
- Scope: only observed in Hermex; other chat apps on the same iPhone show normal keyboard animations.

This appears to be a native iOS client animation/layout issue rather than a server response issue.

## App version / commit

App Store release: Hermex `1.3` from https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hermex/id6767006319

The App Store listing currently shows version `1.3` released on June 18 and identifies the app as the native iPhone Hermex client by Uzair Ansar.

## iOS version and device

Reporter-provided device info: iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 26.5.2.

The available recording is portrait `384x832` at about 30 fps. The App Store listing requires iOS 18.0 or later.

## hermes-webui server version

Current local hermes-webui checkout: `v0.51.852` (`8e26cc03d02a13a785fc7e6f53e868cba1dba6bb`, merge PR #5520 / `release/stage-p1`).

This is likely not relevant to the visual keyboard transition. No server-dependent action is needed to trigger the issue beyond opening a chat and focusing the composer.

## How the phone reaches the server

Reverse proxy.

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Not attached because the original recordings contain private chat content. I can provide a redacted screen recording or redacted frame sheet after reviewing it locally first.

## Notes

The relevant area may be around the chat composer / text input keyboard avoidance behavior, for example `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift`, `ChatComposerTextInputView.swift`, or the surrounding chat layout. I have not debugged the root cause; this is based on visual comparison with a reference recording where the keyboard rises vertically and the composer stays attached smoothly.

title: Fix sideways keyboard slide when starting a new chat
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #53

## What changed

The composer was auto focused while the NavigationStack push animation was still in flight, so iOS composited the keyboard rise with the horizontal slide of the incoming view. That is why the keyboard appeared to drift in from the side on a new chat but rose normally in existing sessions, where nothing auto focuses.

Two changes:

- `PendingNewChatView.requestPendingComposerFocus()` now waits out the push transition (450 ms) before setting focus, instead of a single `Task.yield()`. A `didRequestComposerFocus` flag also makes the two call sites (`.task` and `onAppear`) request focus only once.
- `ChatView`'s initial composer focus policy gets the same settle wait. This covers fast session creation, where the created session swaps `ChatView` in while the push is still animating and its own focus request reintroduced the drift. Refocus after send and after closing a preview keep the old immediate behavior since they never run during a push.

title: Offline cache drops tool call and structured content fields from messages
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. While online, open a session whose transcript contains assistant tool calls (or structured content parts), so it gets written to the offline cache.
2. Go offline (airplane mode) and reopen the same session, so the transcript is served from the cache.
3. Compare it with the live transcript.

## Expected behavior

The cached transcript renders the same as the live one, including tool call rows and structured content.

## Actual behavior

Tool call rows and structured content are silently missing from any transcript restored from the offline cache.

`ChatMessage` carries `toolUseId`, `toolCalls` and `contentParts`, but they are dropped on every cache round trip:

- `CachedMessage.apply()` (Persistence/CachedMessage.swift) copies everything else, including attachments as JSON encoded `Data`, but never persists these three fields.
- The restore path `ChatMessage(cachedMessage:)` in Persistence/CacheStore.swift never passes them back either.

These fields drive real rendering decisions in `ChatViewModel` (tool call visibility, reasoning extraction, stream merge logic), so the cached view quietly diverges from the live one.

## Suggested fix

Add the three fields to `CachedMessage`, encoding the `[JSONValue]` ones as `Data` with the same pattern already used for `attachmentsData`. Populate them in `apply()` and decode them in `ChatMessage(cachedMessage:)`. The new attributes are optional, so SwiftData lightweight migration should handle existing stores. A cache round trip unit test can cover it.

title: Persist tool call and structured content fields in the offline cache

title: Failed profile switch leaves a stale checkmark in the default profile picker
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Settings and the default profile picker with at least two profiles available.
2. Tap a profile while the switch request is going to fail (server down, or the server returns an error for the switch).
3. Look at the list after the error banner appears.

## Expected behavior

The failed profile does not keep a selection checkmark. Only the actually active profile shows as selected.

## Actual behavior

The profile that failed to switch keeps a checkmark alongside the active one until the picker is closed and reopened.

In `Features/Settings/DefaultProfilePickerView.swift`, `save()` optimistically sets `selectedProfileName` before the request, but neither failure path clears it. The server-reported error path returns early and the thrown error path only sets `saveError`. `isSelected()` treats `selectedProfileName` as selected, so both rows show a checkmark.

## Suggested fix

Set `selectedProfileName = nil` on both failure paths in `save()`. The state does not leak across reopens since it is view local, so the bad checkmark only lives while the picker stays open.
