title: Custom headers are not applied to upload and transcribe requests
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a server behind an auth reverse proxy and add the required custom header in settings (the setup from #255).
2. Log in and chat normally. This works because regular API calls carry the header.
3. Attach a photo or file to a message, or record a voice note so it gets transcribed.

## Expected behavior

The upload and transcription requests carry the configured custom headers like every other request, so they pass the proxy.

## Actual behavior

Both requests are rejected by the proxy (401 or 403 depending on setup). `uploadFile` (Networking/APIClient+Upload.swift) and `transcribeAudio` (Networking/APIClient+Transcribe.swift) build their `URLRequest` by hand and never call `customHeaderProvider().apply(to:)`. Every other request path applies the headers: `sendData` and `downloadData` in APIClient.swift, plus the SSE client. CustomHeader.swift documents the headers as attached to every outgoing request, and these two endpoints are the only exceptions.

## Suggested fix

Apply the custom headers in both methods before the built in Content-Type is set, matching the existing custom headers first, built ins win convention from `sendData`. Both endpoints only ever hit the user's own server, so there is no off origin leak concern like the one handled for external media downloads. Unit tests can follow the existing pattern in CustomHeaderInjectionTests.

title: Tolerant integer decoding crashes on out of range numbers
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Have the server return a numeric field outside Int range in any payload that goes through the lossy int decoder, for example `"message_count": 1e300` on a session.
2. Alternatively, render a terminal tool result whose JSON carries `"exit_code": 1e300`.

## Expected behavior

The value is treated like any other unusable shape and decodes to nil. Unexpected shapes must never crash the app per the tolerant decoding rule.

## Actual behavior

The app crashes. `decodeLossyIntIfPresent` (Models/ChatMessage.swift) only checks `value.isFinite` before calling `Int(value)`, and converting a Double outside Int range that way traps at runtime. The Double branch is reached exactly when the direct Int decode fails, which is the huge value case, in both the numeric and the string fallback paths. The helper backs many server supplied fields (message counts, token counts, sizes, offsets). The same trap exists in `exitCode(from:)` in Features/Chat/ToolCallDisplayFormatter.swift, where the input comes from tool output.

## Suggested fix

Convert through `Int(exactly:)` on the truncated value so an out of range Double produces nil instead of trapping, keeping the current truncation behavior for values that fit. Unit tests can cover a session payload with huge numeric fields and a terminal result with a huge exit code.

title: Apply custom headers to upload and transcribe requests
body:
Fixes #61

## What

`uploadFile` and `transcribeAudio` build their multipart requests by hand and never applied the configured custom headers, so servers behind an auth reverse proxy rejected attachment uploads and voice transcription with 401 or 403 while every other request worked.

## How

Both methods now call `customHeaderProvider().apply(to:)` before setting the multipart Content-Type, following the custom headers first, built ins win convention from `sendData`. The provider moves from private to internal so the two extension files can reach it, the same access level as the `session` property they already use. Both endpoints only ever target the user's own server, so the off origin leak guard from #277 is not a concern here.

## Tests

Two new tests in `CustomHeaderInjectionTests` following the existing injection pattern. One asserts the upload request carries the headers and that the built in multipart Content-Type wins over a user supplied one, the other asserts the transcribe request carries the headers.

Full suite: 1191 passed, 0 failed.

title: Stop lossy int decoding from trapping on out of range values
body:
Fixes #62

## What

`decodeLossyIntIfPresent` only checked `isFinite` before converting the decoded Double with `Int(_:)`, which traps at runtime for values outside Int range. The Double branch is reached exactly when the direct Int decode fails, so a server field like `"message_count": 1e300` crashed the app instead of decoding to nil. The helper backs many server supplied fields (message counts, token counts, sizes, offsets), and the same trap sat in the terminal exit code parser in `ToolCallDisplayFormatter`, where the value comes from tool output.

## How

All three sites (the numeric and string branches of the helper, plus the exit code parser) now convert through `Int(exactly:)` on the value truncated toward zero. Anything that fits in Int keeps the exact previous behavior, anything that does not yields nil, in line with the tolerant decoding rule.

## Tests

A session decode test covering out of range values through all three lossy paths (raw number, negative, numeric string, and Int.max plus one) and a formatter test with a huge exit code. Both trap without the fix.

Full suite: 1191 passed, 0 failed.

title: Gateway approval respond fails with "approval_id is required" -- `approvalId` is nil when responding
body: ### Steps to reproduce When using HERMEX against a hermes-webui instance configured with `HERMES_WEBUI_CHAT_BACKEND=gateway` and `HERMES_WEBUI_GATEWAY_USE_RUNS_API=true`, tapping any approval button ("Allow once", "Allow session", etc.) fails with: > The server rejected the request: approval_id is required for gateway approvals **Root cause analysis:** The `respondToApproval` function in `ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift` calls: ```swift _ = try await client.respondApproval( sessionID: prompt.sessionID, choice: choice, approvalID: prompt.pending.approvalId ) ``` `prompt.pending.approvalId` is `String?` (optional). The `ApprovalRespondRequest` struct encodes with `.convertToSnakeCase` via `APIClient.encoder`, but because `approvalId` is an optional `String?`, Swift's auto-generated `Encodable` implementation uses `encodeIfPresent` -- which **omits the key entirely** when the value is nil. The resulting POST body is: ```json {"session_id": "abc123", "choice": "once"} ``` The hermes-webui server at `routes.py:21679` checks: ```python if _run_id: if not approval_id: return bad(handler, "approval_id is required for gateway approvals") ``` Since `approval_id` is absent, it returns the error. The SSE `approval` events from `/api/approval/stream` do include `approval_id` in the JSON, and the `PendingApproval` decoder handles it correctly via `approvalIdSnake = "approval_id"`. However, there are scenarios where `approvalId` could be nil or empty by the time the user taps a button, or the PendingApproval data arrives through a path where `approval_id` isn't populated. **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Configure hermes-webui with gateway backend + runs API enabled 2. Connect via HERMEX 3. Send a prompt that triggers a tool requiring approval (e.g., a command that needs `sudo`) 4. When the approval card appears, tap "Allow once" 5. See the red error text under the approval card: "The server rejected the request: approval_id is required for gateway approvals" **Suggested fix:** In `ApprovalRespondRequest`, always include `approval_id` when available, or use the server-provided fallback `id` from the pending approval data: ```swift private struct ApprovalRespondRequest: Encodable { let sessionId: String let choice: ApprovalChoice let approvalId: String? // Consider using encodeIfPresent in a custom encode(to:) } ``` Or more robustly, ensure the `approvalID` parameter is never nil when responding in gateway mode. If `prompt.pending.approvalId` is nil, fall back to `prompt.pending.id` which already has a derived fallback for the identity field. The exact spot is `ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift`, line: ```swift approvalID: prompt.pending.approvalId ``` Consider changing to always pass a non-nil value: ```swift approvalID: prompt.pending.approvalId ?? prompt.pending.id ``` Or enforce that the approval_id from the SSE stream is always captured and non-nil before showing the approval card. **Environment:** - hermes-webui config: `HERMES_WEBUI_CHAT_BACKEND=gateway`, `HERMES_WEBUI_GATEWAY_USE_RUNS_API=true` **Related files:** - `HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+Chat.swift` -- `ApprovalRespondRequest` struct - `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift` -- `respondToApproval` call site - `HermesMobile/Models/Approval.swift` -- `PendingApproval.approvalId` and `id` fallback ### Expected behavior Tapping "Allow once" or any other approval button on the approval card should approve the pending command. The agent should resume and execute the approved tool call. ### Actual behavior Tapping any approval button shows a red error message: "The server rejected the request: approval_id is required for gateway approvals". The approval is never sent to the server, the agent stays stuck, and the only way to proceed is to skip all approvals for the session via the YOLO button. This only happens when hermes-webui is configured with HERMES_WEBUI_CHAT_BACKEND=gateway and HERMES_WEBUI_GATEWAY_USE_RUNS_API=true (the standard setup for new users following the recommended config). ### App version / commit 1.3, Build 1 ### iOS version and device iOS 26.5.1 on iPhone 17 Pro ### hermes-webui server version v0.51.844 ### How the phone reaches the server Tailscale ### Screenshots or screen recordings

title: Agent MEDIA: images fail to load — pass session_id on /api/media
body:
### Context
When the user asks the agent to send an image from the VPS (e.g. “Send me an image from our machine”), hermes-webui renders the inline thumbnail and full preview for the same thread. Hermex parses the `MEDIA:` token but fails to load the file.

**Repro (owner-confirmed):**
1. Open a chat session over Tailscale.
2. Ask the agent to send an image from the machine (agent uses terminal tool).
3. Assistant message includes a `MEDIA:` reference (e.g. `extension-icon.png`).
4. Hermex shows a **“Media unavailable”** chip in the transcript.
5. Tap the chip → **“Could not load media. The server refused access. Check the server password and permissions.”**

WebUI for the same thread shows the image correctly.

### Current behavior
- `TranscriptMediaParser` detects `MEDIA:` tokens and `TranscriptMediaThumbnailView` attempts to load raster images via `GET /api/media?path=…`.
- Hermex does **not** include `session_id` on `/api/media` requests.
- Upstream webui **does** append `&session_id=…` when a session is open (`ui.js` → `api/media?path=…&session_id=…`).
- Server-side, `/api/media` uses `session_id` for session-scoped path authorization (`_session_media_token_allows_path` in upstream `routes.py`). Without it, session-referenced artifacts (e.g. agent terminal output paths) return **HTTP 403**, which Hermex surfaces as “The server refused access…”

### Expected behavior
Match webui parity for **raster image** `MEDIA:` tokens in assistant messages:
- Inline thumbnail renders in the transcript.
- Tap opens the full-screen preview with the image (Save to Photos where applicable).
- No false “Media unavailable” / permission error when webui loads the same path in the same session.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Local-path `MEDIA:` fetches for transcript thumbnails and preview include `session_id` when the chat session ID is known (mirror webui contract).
- [ ] Remote `https://` `MEDIA:` references continue to work without requiring `session_id`.
- [ ] Owner repro passes: agent-sent PNG (e.g. `extension-icon.png`) shows inline thumbnail and opens on tap.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the endpoint query shape (assert `session_id` present on session-scoped `/api/media` calls) and existing transcript media tests stay green.
- [ ] Route shape validated just-in-time against upstream `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` (or live server) before merge; record handler/query params in the PR.

### Validation plan
**Automated:** XCTest for `Endpoints`/`APIClient` media query items; existing `TranscriptMediaParserTests`, `TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModelTests`, `ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests`.

**Manual (owner, required):**
1. Reproduce the reported thread (“Send me an image from our machine”).
2. Confirm inline thumbnail + tap-to-preview on Hermex matches webui.
3. Spot-check light/dark mode and a remote `MEDIA:https://…` message if available.

### Non-goals
- Inline **video/audio** `MEDIA:` playback (separate enhancement).
- Rendering assistant `message.attachments[]` grids (out of scope unless needed for this repro).
- Markdown `![](path)` image syntax for server-local paths.

Hi! I maintain a fork ([tylerbrevard/hermex](https://github.com/tylerbrevard/hermex/tree/health-tab)) that adds an optional **Health** section to Hermex, and I'd like to offer it upstream if there's interest.

What it adds (all styled with Hermex's existing idioms — plain grouped lists, StatusBadge, system backgrounds — so it looks native):

- A **Health** entry in the home sidebar (after Insights) with a HealthKit dashboard: today's water/protein/caffeine/steps vs editable goals, 7/30-day Swift Charts trends, sleep + medications cards, sync status
- Quick logging (water/protein/caffeine/weight) writing to Apple Health, plus "log 2 waters"-style natural-language fast-path in the chat composer
- Siri App Intents (log water/protein/caffeine) and a Health Snapshot composer action that inserts current stats into a chat message
- Home-screen/lock-screen widgets reading HealthKit directly in the widget extension, and a Live Activity for manual syncs
- Deep links (`<scheme>://health`, `<scheme>://health/sync`)
- Background delivery + BGTask-based background sync with delta queries and Low Power Mode guards

Everything is additive and gated — users who never open Health pay no cost, and the HealthKit entitlement/plist strings are the only app-level changes. The server-sync layer in my fork talks to a personal gateway, so an upstream PR would either drop that part or make it a protocol hook.

If you're open to it I'd restructure this into a reviewable PR series (feature-flagged or as an optional module per your preference). If it's out of scope for the project, no hard feelings — feel free to close. Thanks for building Hermex!

*Disclosure: the fork work was done with AI assistance (Claude), reviewed and shipped to TestFlight on my account.*

title: Chat: Add TTS playback bar, seeking, speed, and background controls
body:
### Use case

The built-in "Speak" button on each message uses iOS's client-side `SpeechSynthesis` API. The resulting voice is low quality, can't be paused or seeked, and stops the moment you lock the screen or switch apps. For longer responses or conversations, this makes it hard to actually listen to a whole answer, catch up on a thread, or use voice as a primary way to consume conversations on a phone.

### Proposed behavior

- **High-quality server-side TTS.** Audio should be generated by the Hermes gateway's TTS endpoint (OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, ElevenLabs, Edge Neural, etc.) rather than the client-side default browser voice.

- **Floating playback bar at the top of the chat** with:
  - Play / pause controls
  - Timestamp display (e.g. `0:42 / 1:15`)
  - Playback speed selector (0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x)
  - A seekable progress bar — tapping anywhere on the bar jumps to that position

- **Background audio support.** Playback continues when:
  - The phone screen locks (after the default timeout)
  - The app is backgrounded (Home, swipe to next app, notification center, etc.)
  - Media remotes appear on the Lock Screen / "Now Playing" (Play/Pause, skip, scrub)

- **Smooth transitions between messages.** Tapping "Speak" on a new message gracefully transitions from the current one. Playback feels natural — like flipping through a podcast episode.

### Acceptance outcomes

- Tapping "Speak" on any message plays that message's text as high-quality TTS audio.
- A playback bar appears at the top of the chat while audio is playing, showing play/pause, timestamp, and progress.
- Tapping the progress bar seeks to that position and syncs visually.
- Playback speed can be changed and persists.
- When the app is backgrounded or the screen locks, audio continues playing with remote controls visible on the Lock Screen / "Now Playing."
- Pressing Play on the Lock Screen correctly resumes playback in-app when the user taps back into Hermex.

### Upstream dependency notes

- No blocking dependencies on Hermes-side changes beyond the existing TTS endpoint — this is primarily an Hermex UI feature.

title: Flaky test: testSSEClientDeliversIncrementalEventsBeforeDone times out on slow CI runners
body:
## What happened

`SSEClientTests.testSSEClientDeliversIncrementalEventsBeforeDone()` failed the `Build and Test` job on PR #60's CI run ([job log](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/28710588772/job/85418316662)) even though the PR only touched `DefaultProfilePickerView`. The same test passed locally at the same commit (full suite 1189/1189) and passed on `gh run rerun --failed`.

## Why it flakes

The test streams fake SSE chunks through `DelayedSSEURLProtocol` with real wall-clock delays (3 × 20ms, then 250ms before `done`), but both waits use `fulfillment(of:timeout: 1)`. On an oversubscribed GitHub Actions macOS runner executing suites on two parallel simulator clones, dispatch latency alone can eat the 1-second budget — the failing run burned 6.45s on this test before giving up.

## Suggested fix

Raise both fulfillment timeouts in `HermesMobileTests/SSEClientTests.swift` (lines 60 and 66) from `1` to `5`. The test's correctness argument is unaffected: chunks are delivered in order and `done` still arrives 250ms after the last live event, so the ordering assertion (`no done before the first live event`) proves the same thing — the longer timeout only adds patience on slow runners. A passing run still completes in well under a second locally; only the failure deadline moves.

## Impact

Until fixed, contributor PRs will randomly go red on CI Gate for changes unrelated to SSE, each needing a manual re-run.

title: Give the flaky SSE incremental-events test a CI-safe timeout

title: Add camera capture option to photo picker
body:
**Feature Request**

The current file attachment UI uses the iOS photo library picker (PHPicker), which only allows selecting existing photos. It would be very useful to also have a camera capture option (UIImagePickerController with camera source) for time-sensitive use cases like:

- Scanning documents or labels that need to be checked immediately
- Taking a quick photo to attach without first saving to the photo library

**Use case**: I frequently need to take photos of time-sensitive items (like food expiration labels) and send them to my Hermes agent for immediate analysis. The extra step of taking the photo in the Camera app, then switching back to Hermex to attach it adds friction.

**Request**: Add a camera button alongside the photo library picker so users can capture photos directly from within the app. This could be implemented via UIImagePickerController with camera source, or by keeping PHPicker but also offering a 'Take Photo' option that opens the camera.

Thanks for the great app!

title: CI: switch TestFlight workflows to manual signing (#4)
body:
Closes #4

## Summary

- Switches both TestFlight workflows from automatic signing (`-allowProvisioningUpdates`) to manual signing with a stored distribution identity, preventing Apple's distribution certificate cap from being exhausted on consecutive CI runs
- Adds an "Import signing assets" step that creates a per-run temp keychain (random password, 1-hour lock timeout), imports the `.p12`, and installs the three provisioning profiles from base64 secrets
- Adds a matching "Clean up signing assets" step (`if: always()`) that deletes the keychain and profile files regardless of build outcome
- Extends "Check required secrets" in both workflows to gate on the five new signing secrets before any work begins
- Updates both `ExportOptions` plists: `signingStyle: manual` + `provisioningProfiles` dict mapping all three bundle IDs to their App Store profile names
- Documents the five secrets, cert/profile export commands, and a rotation/expiry note in `TESTFLIGHT.md`

## Secrets required (maintainer)

Add to both the `internal-testflight` and `external-testflight` GitHub environments before triggering a run:

| Secret | Contents |
|---|---|
| `DIST_CERT_P12_BASE64` | `base64 -i cert.p12` |
| `DIST_CERT_P12_PASSWORD` | `.p12` export password |
| `PROVISION_PROFILE_APP_BASE64` | App Store profile for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile` |
| `PROVISION_PROFILE_SHAREEXT_BASE64` | App Store profile for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.shareextension` |
| `PROVISION_PROFILE_WIDGET_BASE64` | App Store profile for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.liveactivitywidget` |

The PR is safe to merge before secrets exist; workflows will fail fast at "Check required secrets" with a clear message until they're in place.

title: Hide empty new chat sessions from the sessions list
body:
## Context
When a user creates a new chat session and immediately returns to the session list, the app briefly shows an empty "Untitled" session before it disappears.

## Current Behavior
A newly-created chat with no user content can appear in the session list as an untitled session for about a second after navigating back.

## Expected Behavior
Empty newly-created chats should not appear in the session list. The list should only show real sessions with meaningful content or server-confirmed session state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Creating a new chat and returning to the sessions list does not show an empty "Untitled" row, even briefly.
- Existing sessions without custom titles still display correctly when they have real content.
- The fix does not delete or hide sessions that contain messages, tool activity, or valid server-backed history.
- Add or update automated coverage for the list/session filtering behavior where practical.

## Validation Plan
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Manual simulator validation:
  1. Launch the app.
  2. Create a new chat.
  3. Do not send a message.
  4. Navigate back to the sessions list.
  5. Confirm no empty "Untitled" session appears, including transiently.
  6. Confirm real existing untitled/contentful sessions still appear.

## Non-goals
- Redesigning the sessions list.
- Changing server API behavior.
- Changing how valid untitled sessions are named once they contain content.

## Context

Hermex is currently an iPhone-only app. Users want the same functionality in a native iPad experience delivered through the existing App Store app.

This issue tracks the complete iPad milestone through three child issues:

- [ ] #109 — Universal app and adaptive session/chat navigation
- [ ] #110 — Adaptation of secondary destinations
- [ ] #111 — Presentation, multitasking, keyboard, and pointer hardening

The app targets iPhone only and presents its root experience through stacked navigation. On iPad, it does not provide a native layout that uses the available screen width.

Hermex ships as one universal iPhone/iPad app. Regular-width iPad windows use an adaptive sidebar-and-detail layout, while narrow windows and iPhone retain compact stacked navigation. Existing features remain available and usable throughout the iPad interface.

title: Support audio and video transcript MEDIA previews
body:
## Context

PR #86 added session-scoped support for transcript `MEDIA:` image references, including local `/api/media` paths and remote media URLs. The same transcript surface should support common audio and video media generated by Hermes tools instead of showing them as unavailable document chips.

## Current Behavior

Transcript `MEDIA:` references are parsed, but only raster image candidates render as inline thumbnails and full-screen previews.

Audio and video references such as `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.wav`, `.mp4`, `.mov`, or remote media URLs currently fall back to unavailable/no-preview UI even when the media bytes are fetchable through the existing transcript media loader.

## Expected Behavior

Hermex should render transcript `MEDIA:` audio and video references with native playback affordances:

- Audio `MEDIA:` references show a playable inline audio row using the existing chat audio player style where practical.
- Video `MEDIA:` references show a clear inline video media tile and can be opened into a playback preview.
- Local media paths continue to use the real server `session_id` with `/api/media`.
- Remote media URLs continue to load without leaking Hermes cookies to external origins.
- Existing image thumbnail and preview behavior from PR #86 remains unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add media type detection for transcript `MEDIA:` references covering at least:
  - Audio: `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.wav`, `.aac`, `.caf`
  - Video: `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.m4v`
- Audio transcript media can be played from chat without first downloading through a separate browser/share flow.
- Video transcript media can be opened and played from the transcript preview UI.
- Unsupported media types still show the existing unavailable/no-preview state.
- Local-path audio/video references do not request `/api/media` unless a real upstream `session_id` is available.
- Same-reference media remains scoped by server/session so audio/video from one session cannot reuse stale state from another session.
- Add focused tests for media type detection and request routing for local-path and remote audio/video references.
- Do not regress existing transcript image tests or attachment audio playback tests.

## Validation Plan

- Validate route shape at implementation time against the repo-local upstream copy or a running Hermes server:
  - local path: `/api/media?path=...&session_id=...`
  - remote URL: fetch through the transcript media loader without external-cookie leakage
- Run focused transcript media tests.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Manual simulator validation on iPhone:
  - Open a session containing image, audio, and video `MEDIA:` references.
  - Confirm image behavior still works.
  - Confirm audio plays, pauses, and does not conflict with existing chat audio behavior.
  - Confirm video opens and plays in preview.
  - Confirm unsupported media still shows a graceful unavailable state.

## Non-goals

- Adding new Hermes server endpoints or changing upstream JSON/API shapes.
- Building a full media gallery.
- Editing/generated media capture flows.
- Adding new third-party dependencies.
- Supporting arbitrary streaming protocols beyond normal fetchable media files/URLs.

title: Let users choose the composer STT provider, defaulting to server STT when available
body:
## Context

Hermex currently uses iOS `SFSpeechRecognizer` for composer dictation, which fails for unsupported locales such as Estonian. Hermes servers already expose server-side STT through `POST /api/transcribe`, so composer dictation should prefer the user's configured server STT by default while preserving an on-device fallback and a privacy-preserving on-device-only option.

Related PR: #91 started from the Estonian-specific fallback case, but this issue now covers the broader provider preference behavior.

## Current behavior

Composer voice input depends on iOS Speech recognition for the current locale. If iOS does not support the locale, dictation fails even when the user's Hermes server has STT configured.

## Expected behavior

Add a Settings preference for composer speech-to-text provider:

- `Server first` default: use server `/api/transcribe` when available; fall back to iOS on-device STT when unavailable and supported.
- `On-device first`: use iOS STT when supported; fall back to server STT when unavailable.
- `On-device only`: never upload composer dictation audio; show a friendly unsupported/unavailable message if iOS STT cannot run.

## Acceptance criteria

- Settings exposes a clear STT provider preference for composer dictation.
- New installs default to `Server first`.
- Server STT uses documented `POST /api/transcribe` multipart `file` upload and tolerant `{ ok, transcript, error }` decoding.
- Server unavailable, unauthenticated, unconfigured, or failed transcription cases fall back according to the selected policy.
- `On-device only` mode never calls `/api/transcribe`.
- UI distinguishes listening/recording/transcribing/error states cleanly.
- PR #91's lifecycle bugs are addressed before merge or before equivalent work lands.

## Validation plan

- Verify endpoint shape against official Voice API docs: https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/voice/
- Verify pinned upstream route shape in `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/upload.py` before implementation.
- Unit-test provider policy routing.
- Manual simulator/device validation for all three settings, including server unavailable and unsupported iOS locale cases.

## Non-goals

- Do not require a `language` multipart field; it is not documented and pinned upstream ignores it.
- Do not add new third-party dependencies.
- Do not change voice-note sending behavior unless explicitly scoped later.

## Summary

Fix #90 — Apple's `SFSpeechRecognizer` does not support Estonian (`et-EE`). This PR adds a **server-side STT fallback** using the existing `POST /api/transcribe` endpoint (Whisper), which supports 100+ languages including Estonian.

## Changes

### ComposerVoiceInputController.swift
- Added optional `apiClient: APIClient?` and `locale: Locale` parameters
- At start, checks `SFSpeechRecognizer.supportedLocales()` — if the current locale is not supported, falls back to server STT

- Apple native path unchanged for the 60+ supported locales (offline, instant)

### APIClient+Transcribe.swift

## Architecture

Three independent layers:

| Layer | Source of truth | Change |
|---|---|---|
| UI language | Phone locale / .xcstrings | Unchanged |
| TTS voice | Server config (`ServerTTSPolicy`) | Unchanged (see #90 discussion) |
| STT | Apple native for supported locales, server for the rest | **This PR** |

## Testing

- Estonian locale (`et-EE`): should use `POST /api/transcribe` automatically
- English locale (`en-US`): should use Apple's `SFSpeechRecognizer` (unchanged)

title: fix(onboarding): add port-443 safety check to tailscale serve prompt
body:
Closes #50

## Problem

The onboarding prompt in `OnboardingFlowPolicy.swift` instructs users to run:

```
tailscale serve --bg 8787
```

When `--https` is not specified, Tailscale Serve defaults to port 443,
which **silently replaces** any existing service on that port (e.g.
Nightscout via Funnel, other HTTPS services).

See #50 for the original report.

## Changes

1. Changed the primary instruction to use the explicit form
   `tailscale serve --bg --https=8787 127.0.0.1:8787` — this puts the
   WebUI on its own dedicated port and never disturbs existing services.
2. Added a safety check suggestion: run `tailscale serve status` first
   to verify there's no existing service on port 443.
3. Kept the `tailscale serve` form for users who already understand
   their port situation — still available as the fallback path.

## Testing

No runtime code changed — only the agent prompt string. CI should pass
without any special testing.

title: Support multi-user identities for a shared Hermes agent
body:
## Use case

A household or small team can share one main Hermes agent while each person uses Hermex on their own paired device. The agent needs to know which person is speaking so it can apply the right personalization, keep conversations private by default, and route identity-specific context such as calendars, mail, tasks, and preferences correctly.

Today, Hermex appears to have a single undifferentiated client identity. That forces a shared agent to guess who is talking, which is unreliable and can expose the wrong person's context.

## Proposed behavior

Hermex should support a stable, authenticated user identity associated with the paired client/session and include that identity in requests to hermes-webui.

Suggested shape:

- Each paired app installation has a server-recognized `person_id` plus display name metadata.
- The app sends the identity as session-scoped client context after pairing or authentication, rather than injecting it into every user message.
- The server exposes the identity to the selected agent as trusted personalization context, clearly separated from authorization claims.
- Session lists default to the current person's conversations. Access to other users' sessions requires an explicit, authorized sharing model.
- The UI shows the active identity and gives users a way to correct or re-pair it. It must not allow a user to impersonate another household member by choosing a different identity.
- Unknown or missing identity is surfaced as a connection/pairing problem. The agent should not silently infer who is speaking.

This should be designed alongside hermes-webui because Hermex is a thin client and the server needs a compatible identity contract. Backward compatibility for existing single-user servers matters.

## Acceptance outcomes

- Two separately paired Hermex clients can connect to the same hermes-webui and be identified as different people by one main agent.
- The identity is durable for the client/session and does not consume prompt tokens on every turn.
- The agent receives a structured identity hint with an explicit trust level and can distinguish personalization from authorization.
- A user sees only their own session history by default.
- The app cannot switch a message's sender identity to another user without a new authorized pairing flow.
- Existing single-user installations continue to work when multi-user identity support is unavailable.
- The app has tests for identity propagation, missing/unknown identity handling, and session-list isolation.

## Upstream dependency notes

This requires a documented hermes-webui capability and API contract for paired client identity, server-side session ownership, and optional identity-scoped session queries. A corresponding upstream issue in hermes-webui should define the wire format and authorization model before the mobile client implementation starts.

title: Hide delegated subagent sessions from the main chat list by default
body:
## Context

`GET /api/sessions` can return delegated child sessions alongside user-facing conversations. Upstream marks these rows as subagents, child sessions, and read-only. Hermes WebUI nests them beneath their parent, but Hermex currently renders each row as a normal first-class chat.

## Current behavior

Delegated child sessions clutter the main list and receive normal rename, pin, project, archive, branch, and delete affordances. Those operations are rejected because the sessions are runner-owned and read-only.

Disabling “CLI Sessions” is not an acceptable workaround because it changes the server-wide agent-session import setting and also hides unrelated local sessions.

## Expected behavior

Delegated subagent sessions are hidden from normal chat lists by default. A separate “Subagent Sessions” setting can explicitly reveal them. When visible, read-only sessions remain viewable but do not expose mutation affordances.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decode the optional session-row fields needed for classification and safety: source markers, `parent_session_id`, `relationship_type`, and `read_only`.
- Classify delegated sessions using an explicit `subagent` source marker.
- Do not classify a row as delegated solely because it has `parent_session_id`.
- Add a persisted “Subagent Sessions” toggle, defaulting off.
- Apply the filter consistently to normal, searched, project-filtered, and cached session lists.
- When enabled, visibly read-only rows may be opened and exported, but mutation affordances are not offered.
- Existing normal, cron, CLI/TUI/Desktop, fork, and compression-continuation visibility is not regressed.
- Existing Message Count, Workspace, Cron Sessions, and CLI Sessions preferences continue working.

## Validation plan

- Add tolerant decoding tests for current and older row shapes.
- Add classification tests covering subagent children, ordinary sessions, forks, compression continuations, cron, CLI/TUI, and missing fields.
- Add visibility-toggle and cached-session tests.
- Add tests proving read-only rows cannot expose mutation actions.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Signed simulator validation: confirm subagents are absent by default, appear when enabled, remain viewable, and have no mutation actions.

## Non-goals

- Reproducing Hermes WebUI’s expandable parent/child session tree.
- Inferring “smoke test” status from title or message-count heuristics.
- Redesigning all imported-agent source controls in this issue.
- Changing upstream persistence or session ownership.

title: Add a separate Claude Code sessions visibility toggle
body:
## Context

Hermex currently provides separate CLI Sessions and Cron Sessions settings. Claude Code imports are classified as CLI sessions, so users cannot hide Claude Code transcripts without also hiding useful CLI/TUI/Desktop sessions.

Upstream already exposes:

- `show_claude_code_sessions` through `GET` and `POST /api/settings`
- `source_tag` and `raw_source` values of `claude_code`
- `is_cli_session: true` and `read_only: true` on Claude Code rows

The upstream setting is subordinate to `show_cli_sessions`.

## Current behavior

The CLI Sessions toggle controls Claude Code rows together with every other imported CLI/TUI/Desktop session. Hermex does not decode or expose the server’s dedicated Claude Code preference.

## Expected behavior

Settings includes a separate **Claude Code Sessions** toggle beneath CLI Sessions.

Disabling it hides only Claude Code rows. Other CLI/TUI/Desktop sessions remain visible. The setting is synchronized with the active server.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tolerantly decode the optional `show_claude_code_sessions` server setting.
- Add a server-synchronized Claude Code Sessions toggle.
- Preserve existing behavior by defaulting to shown when the server omits the setting.
- Adopt the server value when available and persist its local cache per server.
- Write `POST /api/settings` with `{"show_claude_code_sessions": <bool>}` when the server supports the setting.
- Revert the toggle and surface an error if the server write fails.
- Classify Claude Code rows using explicit `claude_code` source metadata, not their title or model.
- Apply visibility consistently to normal, searched, project-filtered, and cached session lists.
- Turning Claude Code Sessions off leaves ordinary CLI/TUI/Desktop sessions visible.
- Disable the Claude Code toggle while CLI Sessions is off, without overwriting its saved preference.
- Re-enabling CLI Sessions restores the saved Claude Code preference.
- Older servers that omit the setting continue working without decoding failures.

## Validation plan

- Verify the settings and session-row shapes against the repo-local upstream copy at implementation time.
- Test tolerant settings decoding with present, missing, malformed, and unknown fields.
- Test the exact settings update request body.
- Test server adoption, per-server isolation, failed-write rollback, and parent-toggle behavior.
- Test that only `claude_code` rows are filtered.
- Test online and cached session-list visibility.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Manual simulator test with Claude Code and ordinary CLI/TUI sessions:
  - Disable Claude Code Sessions and confirm only Claude Code rows disappear.
  - Re-enable it and confirm they return.
  - Disable CLI Sessions and confirm both imported categories disappear.
  - Re-enable CLI Sessions and confirm the prior Claude Code preference is restored.

## Non-goals

- Distinguishing meaningful CLI conversations from one-shot or smoke-test runs.
- Changing delegated subagent visibility; tracked by #97.
- Making Claude Code sessions independent of the upstream CLI parent gate.
- Importing, resuming, or modifying read-only Claude Code sessions.
- Redesigning the complete session-source taxonomy.

title: CI: reduce PR Build and Test feedback time
body:
## Context

The required PR CI workflow runs the complete iOS build and XCTest suite for app-code changes. Recent successful runs took approximately 10–25 minutes, with most taking around 20–22 minutes. This delays merging and causes minor follow-up commits to restart the full feedback cycle.

Recent run inspection shows that checkout, path detection, simulator selection, and CI gate overhead take only seconds. Nearly all execution time is inside the monolithic `xcodebuild test` command.

## Current behavior

- Every non-documentation PR commit runs the full suite on a fresh `macos-26` runner.
- Build and test timing are combined, obscuring whether compilation or test execution dominates.
- The test target is marked parallelizable, but the worker count is left to Xcode.
- Superseded runs on the same PR are correctly cancelled.
- Documentation-only changes correctly skip the macOS job.
- A small follow-up commit restarts the complete build and test process.

## Expected behavior

PR CI should provide materially faster feedback without reducing required test coverage, weakening fork safety, or changing the existing CI Gate contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record a reproducible baseline from at least five representative successful PR runs.
- [ ] Separate and report build-for-testing and test-without-building durations.
- [ ] Include Xcode’s build timing summary in CI output.
- [ ] Extract or otherwise identify the slowest test classes/tests from the result bundle.
- [ ] Benchmark explicit simulator parallelization settings, including at least worker counts 1, 2, and 3.
- [ ] Evaluate Swift Package Manager caching, measuring restoration overhead and net benefit.
- [ ] Implement the lowest-complexity configuration that produces a repeatable improvement.
- [ ] Preserve the complete XCTest suite as the required PR validation.
- [ ] Preserve cancellation of superseded PR runs.
- [ ] Preserve documentation-only skipping and the required `CI Gate`.
- [ ] Preserve compatibility with fork PRs and avoid repository secrets.
- [ ] Document before/after timings and any rejected approaches in the PR.

## Validation plan

- Run the complete XCTest suite successfully using the final workflow.
- Compare at least three successful optimized runs against the recorded baseline.
- Verify that a documentation-only PR skips the macOS job and passes `CI Gate`.
- Verify that a non-documentation change runs the complete suite.
- Verify that a superseding commit cancels the previous in-progress run.
- Confirm that failure artifacts remain available.

## Non-goals

- Removing tests from required PR validation.
- Introducing paid larger runners.
- Introducing a self-hosted runner.
- Changing branch protection rules.
- Solving local task switching with worktrees.
- Optimizing unrelated TestFlight workflows.

title: CI: reduce PR Build and Test feedback time
body:
Fixes #106

## Summary

- split the monolithic XCTest invocation into build-for-testing and test-without-building
- report phase durations and Xcode build timing details
- extract the 20 slowest test cases from the xcresult bundle without allowing diagnostic failures to fail otherwise successful CI
- run the complete suite with one explicit simulator test worker
- preserve fork safety, superseded-run cancellation, documentation-only skipping, failure artifacts, and the required CI Gate contract

## Baseline

Six representative successful Build and Test jobs before optimization:

| Run | Duration |
|---|---:|
| 29118286107 | 21m14s |
| 29116223535 | 22m28s |
| 29069603779 | 10m45s |
| 29051071825 | 22m20s |
| 29049798915 | 20m55s |
| 28988927892 | 15m25s |

Historical median: 21m05s.

## Final optimized runs

All three runs used identical commit 95695e8, one explicit worker, the full 1,345-test suite, and no SwiftPM cache.

| Attempt | Build | Tests | Build and Test job | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 2m15s | 4m43s | 7m24s | Passed |
| 2 | 2m12s | 4m10s | 7m12s | Passed |
| 3 | 2m22s | 6m41s | 9m35s | Passed |

Final median: 7m24s, approximately 65% faster than the historical median.

## Rejected approaches

### Two workers

Passed all 1,345 tests, but test execution regressed to 16m29s and the job took 19m00s. Simulator contention made timing-sensitive tests dramatically slower.

### Three workers

Failed after 38m05s of test execution when a simulator test runner timed out while preparing. The required CI Gate correctly failed and the 243 MB xcresult failure artifact uploaded successfully.

### SwiftPM caching

A cache miss took 10m38s and saved approximately 188 MB with about 6s save overhead. A cache hit restored approximately 179 MB in about 4s and took 7m32s total. Most apparent improvement came from unrelated test-runtime variance; the plausible build benefit was roughly 31–35 seconds. This did not justify cache-key maintenance and large cache transfers under the lowest-complexity criterion.

## Acceptance validation

- full 1,345-test suite passed locally through split build/test commands
- full suite passed in all three final hosted runs
- Xcode build timing summary appears in CI output
- slowest tests are extracted from the result bundle
- documentation-only run 29162593471 skipped Build and Test and passed CI Gate
- non-documentation changes run the complete suite
- historical superseded PR runs confirm per-PR cancellation remains operational
- three-worker failure confirmed failure artifact availability and CI Gate propagation
- workflow uses no repository secrets and retains read-only fork-safe permissions

## Owner checks

No app UI or runtime behavior changed. In the Actions UI, confirm the PR CI summary shows separate build and test durations plus the slowest-test table.

body:
## Problem

The "Media unavailable" chip shown for unsupported file types (`.txt`, `.csv`, `.md`, `.json`, `.zip`, etc.) is a dead UI element — no tap action, no download path. Users cannot retrieve files sent by their Hermes agent through `MEDIA:` tokens when the file extension does not match image/audio/video.

## Fix

Adds `TranscriptMediaFileExportView` — a new view displayed in place of the dead "Media unavailable" chip when `loadMediaData` is available. Tapping the download button:

1. Loads the file data through the existing `/api/media` endpoint (authenticated session)
2. Presents the iOS share sheet via `fileExporter`
3. Uses `TranscriptMediaExportSupport.payload()` with `resolvedKind: .data` to preserve the original filename and extension

The pattern mirrors the existing `TranscriptMediaAudioExportView` exactly.

### Changes

- **`TranscriptMediaView.swift`** (+136 lines): New `TranscriptMediaFileExportView` struct, wired into `TranscriptMediaThumbnailView` as `.unsupported where loadMediaData != nil`
- **`TranscriptMediaParserTests.swift`** (+30 lines): Tests for `.unsupported` classification across common file types, and export payload preservation

### UI

The download chip shows:
- Doc icon + filename
- "Tap to download" label (or "Loading…" while fetching)
- Download button (square.and.arrow.down) on the right
- Same chip styling as the existing media chips

## Testing

- `testUnsupportedTextAndDataFilesAreClassifiedAsUnsupported` — verifies `.txt`, `.csv`, `.md`, `.json`, `.zip` all return `.unsupported`
- `testUnsupportedFileExportPayloadKeepsOriginalNameAndExtension` — verifies export preserves `report.txt` filename and original data

body:
## Context

Scheduled-job runs currently appear among ordinary conversations when the Cron Sessions setting is enabled. This makes them difficult to distinguish, but moving all scheduled sessions below the complete conversation history—as attempted in closed PR #117—buries recent runs and makes them appear missing.

Add a compact, discoverable presentation that follows the existing Active Profile and Projects disclosure patterns.

## Current behavior

- The Cron Sessions setting controls whether scheduled sessions are included.
- When enabled, scheduled sessions are mixed into the main Sessions list according to recency.
- Users cannot quickly distinguish scheduled runs from ordinary conversations.
- Rendering scheduled sessions after every ordinary conversation can move recent runs far below the visible list.

## Expected behavior

Show a “Scheduled sessions” disclosure row above the ordinary Sessions section.

The disclosure should:

- Match the appearance and interaction patterns of Active Profile and Projects.
- Default to collapsed.
- Remember the user’s last expanded or collapsed state.
- Show the total number of non-archived scheduled sessions in a count badge.
- Be hidden when Cron Sessions is disabled or no scheduled sessions exist.
- Show the five newest scheduled sessions when expanded.
- Include a “View all” row after those five sessions when additional results exist.

“View all” opens a searchable list of every non-archived scheduled session, newest first. Scheduled-session rows retain the standard session navigation, swipe actions, context menus, message-count display, and workspace display.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A “Scheduled sessions” disclosure appears above Sessions when Cron Sessions is enabled and at least one non-archived cron session exists.
- [ ] The disclosure is visually consistent with Active Profile and Projects.
- [ ] It defaults to collapsed and persists its disclosure state.
- [ ] Its badge reports the total number of non-archived scheduled sessions.
- [ ] Expanding it shows at most the five newest scheduled sessions.
- [ ] A “View all” row appears when more than five scheduled sessions exist.
- [ ] “View all” opens a searchable, newest-first list of all non-archived scheduled sessions.
- [ ] Scheduled-session rows retain the same navigation and actions as ordinary session rows.
- [ ] Disabling Cron Sessions hides the disclosure and its sessions.
- [ ] Archived cron sessions remain exclusively in Archived Sessions.
- [ ] Main Sessions search includes ordinary and scheduled sessions.
- [ ] During an active main search, Scheduled sessions automatically expands and shows all matching scheduled results without the five-row cap.
- [ ] Ending search restores the user’s previous disclosure state.
- [ ] Empty-state messaging remains correct when a search matches only scheduled sessions.
- [ ] The remote-search progress indicator is not duplicated.

## Validation plan

Automated tests:

- Disclosure visibility for enabled, disabled, empty, and populated states.
- Five-row limit, newest-first ordering, total count, and “View all” visibility.
- Persisted expanded/collapsed state.
- Search auto-expansion, uncapped matching results, and restoration of the previous state.
- Separation of ordinary, scheduled, and archived sessions.

4. Open scheduled sessions and exercise their standard row actions.
5. Verify “View all” navigation and search.
6. Search from the main Sessions screen and confirm scheduled matches expand automatically without excessive scrolling.
7. Toggle Cron Sessions off and confirm all scheduled-session UI disappears.

- Changing how cron sessions are detected from server session data.
- Changing the existing Cron Sessions setting.

- Changing archive behavior.
- Changing API endpoints or response models.

title: fix(chat): recover interrupted backend streams
body:
## Summary

- treat a 404 stream-status response as terminal and reconcile from the server transcript
- reconnect to the existing stream when `/api/chat/start` returns a 409 with `active_stream_id`
- roll back the duplicate optimistic message and restore pending attachments before reconnecting
- add contract coverage for both backend-interruption paths

## Why

After a backend restart, a stale stream ID may return 404 instead of an inactive status envelope. Treating that as a generic recovery error leaves the client suspended or causes later reconnect attempts against a stream that no longer exists.

A start request can also race with an already-active server run. Hermes WebUI returns HTTP 409 with `active_stream_id`; reconnecting to that run is safer than surfacing a generic error or resending the message.

## API contract

Verified against `nesquena/hermes-webui` commit `54520ef35b1b2c4751807cf4f50bb9826bd4f9db`.

The duplicate-start envelope is:

```json
{
  "error": "session already has an active stream",
  "active_stream_id": "<stream-id>"
}
```

## Testing

- Targeted `StreamReconnectContractTests`: passed, 5/5
- Full `HermesMobile` XCTest suite on iPhone 17 simulator: passed

body:
## Context

Opening an existing session should present its transcript at the intended position without visible intermediate repositioning. Currently, the transition feels unstable even when the session has already been opened and loaded.

This is separate from #32, which concerns general scrolling performance in long conversations.

## Current behavior

When a session is tapped in the session list, the transcript briefly lags and shakes as the chat screen opens. It appears to jump from the top toward the latest message, although the movement happens too quickly to identify its exact direction reliably.

The issue:

- Is most noticeable in longer sessions.
- Still occurs slightly in short sessions with only two messages.
- Reproduces when returning to the session list and immediately reopening the same session.
- Lasts only a fraction of a second but makes navigation feel visibly jittery.

## Expected behavior

Opening an existing session should be visually smooth. The transcript should appear at its intended initial position without showing abrupt vertical jumps, bouncing, or intermediate scroll positions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Opening an existing session from the session list does not produce a visible transcript jump or shake.
- The transcript settles at the app’s intended initial position, including the latest-message position where applicable.
- Immediately leaving and reopening the same session remains smooth.
- The behavior is corrected for both:
  - A short text-only session with approximately two messages.
  - A substantially longer transcript.
- Existing user-driven scrolling, “scroll to bottom,” pagination, and streaming behavior continue to work.
- Automated regression coverage is added for any initial-scroll state or policy logic that can be tested deterministically.
- The full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

1. Build and launch a signed Debug build on the configured iPhone simulator.
2. Open a short text-only session from the session list.
3. Return to the list and reopen it several times.
4. Repeat with a long session.
5. Record the simulator screen if necessary and inspect the opening transition at reduced playback speed for intermediate scroll jumps.
6. Verify ordinary scrolling, returning to the bottom, loading older messages, and opening an actively streaming session.
7. Run the full XCTest suite.

## Non-goals

- General transcript scrolling-performance optimization already covered by #32.
- Redesigning the chat screen or navigation transition.
- Changing server APIs, session payloads, or transcript content.
- Altering the intended final initial-scroll position.

title: Keep transcript links clickable without preview cards
body:
## Summary

- remove automatic link-preview cards from user and assistant transcript messages
- keep assistant Markdown links clickable without adding a secondary tile
- detect HTTP(S) addresses in user bubbles, including bare domains such as `Paypal.com`, and render them as tappable links
- remove the now-unused LinkPresentation metadata, cache, extractor, and preview tests

## Why

Every web address was being repeated as a large preview card below the message, which consumed transcript space without adding useful information. Removing that renderer also exposed that user bubbles used verbatim text and therefore did not make bare website addresses interactive.

## Impact

Transcript messages now show only their inline links. Explicit URLs and bare domains in sent user messages remain visually identifiable and tappable, while non-web values such as email addresses are left as plain text.

## Validation

- `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -only-testing:HermesMobileTests/UserMessageLinkFormatterTests`
- `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17'`
- signed Debug simulator build installed and launched on iPhone 17
- visually verified the existing `Paypal.com` user bubble renders as a blue link with no preview card

title: Wayfind native Kanban parity for Hermex
body:
## Destination

Produce an implementation-ready Kanban product/API specification and sequenced issue breakdown for Hermex. Preserve every user-facing Hermes WebUI Kanban capability through native iPhone interactions, include an owner-validated low-fidelity interactive prototype, and do not implement production code during this effort.

Treat the maintainer's running Hermes WebUI server as the API compatibility baseline, cross-checked against the latest official API docs and the pinned upstream source. Any capability omission or version difference requires an explicit documented decision.

## Notes

Domain: native iPhone Kanban parity for the self-hosted Hermes WebUI server.

Every session should consult Wayfinder and the ticket-type skill it is resolving. Use research for primary-source investigations; prototype plus SwiftUI patterns and focus/accessibility guidance for interaction work; grilling and domain-modeling for owner decisions. Follow AGENTS.md API-source precedence and never invent endpoints or JSON shapes.

Standing preferences:
- Functional parity is strict; visual parity is not.
- Favor native, accessible iPhone interaction over reproducing the desktop board.
- Treat Kanban as a state-mutating feature requiring explicit safety and failure-state design.
- Planning artifacts only until this map reaches its destination.

## Decisions so far

- [Inventory the upstream Kanban domain and API contract](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/140) — The live/pinned surface has 25 route combinations and full WebUI workflows, but it is undocumented as a supported client contract and includes shared-state and budget-consuming operations.
- [Map Kanban integration constraints in Hermex](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/141) — Kanban fits an isolated, server-bound utility destination using existing API/state patterns; naming, mutation races, accessibility, isolation, and localization constrain the design.
- [Verify authenticated Kanban wire responses on the running server](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/146) — Authenticated read-only JSON and SSE wire probes match the live/pinned builders; cookie auth works without native Origin/Referer headers, and no server or credential data was exposed.
- [Choose Hermex’s Kanban domain vocabulary](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/148) — Kanban contains Boards and Cards; Status/Column/Lane, Profile assignment, prerequisite direction, dispatch, archive, and bulk-action terms are now canonical.
- [Choose Hermex's Kanban compatibility boundary](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/147) — Support is capability-gated against the verified live contract, fails closed per capability with tolerant decoding, requires layered release and owner-device evidence, and is not labelled Experimental.
- [Choose Kanban mutation, conflict, and failure semantics](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/143) — Mutations are optimistic but server-authoritative, with resource-scoped serialization, explicit high-impact confirmations, live reconciliation, non-atomic bulk recovery, and no blind write retries or offline writes.
- [Choose the native iPhone Kanban interaction model](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/142) — Use Status Focus: a horizontal Status selector over a vertical Card list showing one Status at a time. Preserve explicit non-drag movement, selection and bulk actions, Board switching, filtering, editing, and confirmed Dispatcher controls. Utility controls are adaptive monochrome; workflow Status remains the meaningful color signal.
- [Lock the implementation-ready Kanban specification and delivery slices](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/144) — PROJECT_SPEC.md §17 and ten native-dependency-ordered implementation issues lock strict parity, hidden intermediate delivery, safety boundaries, and layered release validation.

## Not yet specified

None — the implementation route is fully specified.

## Out of scope

- Production Kanban implementation, release work, or TestFlight distribution.
- Visual imitation of the Hermes WebUI desktop layout.
- Non-Kanban Hermes WebUI parity gaps.

title: Feature Request: Support inline rendering of MEDIA: links (PDF, images, audio)
body:
## Use case

When using Hermex as a client for hermes-webui, the server sends MEDIA: tags (e.g. `MEDIA:/absolute/path/to/file.pdf` or `MEDIA:https://...`) to display files inline — PDFs, images, audio files, diffs, CSVs, Excalidraw files, etc.

In the web browser (WebUI) these files render natively with rich previews. PDFs appear embedded with a viewer, images show inline, audio has playback controls, etc.

However, in Hermex these MEDIA: links show as plain text or "multimedia no disponible" instead of being rendered or at least offered as a downloadable file. This makes it hard to use Hermex as a full mobile client when the agent shares documents like invoices, reports, diagrams, or audio files.

Use case examples:
- An agent generates a PDF invoice and sends it via MEDIA: — user cannot view or download it
- An agent creates a chart/image and shares it — user sees a broken placeholder
- An agent records an audio response — user has no way to play it

## Proposed behavior

Hermex should detect MEDIA: tags in the assistant's response and either:

1. **Render them inline** — PDF previews via WKWebView/QLPreviewController, images displayed in the chat, audio with playback controls
2. **Offer download/save** — at minimum show a tappable link that downloads the file to the user's device or opens it in another app via Quick Look / UIActivityViewController

Ideally, MEDIA: references to PDFs would show an embedded preview (like Quick Look does in other iOS apps), images would load inline, and audio files would show a play button.

See hermes-webui source for how MEDIA: is handled on the web: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-webui

## Acceptance outcomes

- A PDF shared via `MEDIA:/path/invoice.pdf` shows an inline preview or a tappable "Open PDF" button
- Images (`MEDIA:/path/photo.png`) render directly in the chat bubble
- Audio files (`MEDIA:/path/audio.mp3`) show a play button or download option
- Local file paths (stored on the hermes-webui server) are resolved and offered for download
- Remote URLs (`MEDIA:https://...`) open in-app or redirect to Safari

## Upstream dependency notes

The MEDIA: tag format is defined by the hermes-webui server (NousResearch/hermes-webui). The web client handles it on the frontend. Hermex would need to:

1. Parse MEDIA: tags from assistant text responses
2. For local paths (server-side files), fetch them via the hermes-webui API endpoint (there is a file-serving endpoint the web client uses)
3. For remote URLs, load them directly

This does not require changes to hermes-webui — only client-side work in the Hermex SwiftUI app.

---

*Submitted from Hermes Agent on behalf of the user*
