title: Add the hidden Kanban compatibility shell
body:
## Goal

Establish the production-quality Kanban compatibility boundary and a Debug-only entry point without exposing incomplete Kanban in normal Hermex navigation.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.1–17.3, §17.7, and §17.8.

## Scope

- Add tolerant Kanban wire/domain models with optional upstream fields and ignored unknown additions.
- Add verified endpoints and API client methods for:
  - `GET /api/kanban/config`
  - `GET /api/kanban/boards`
  - `GET /api/kanban/board`
- Implement the non-mutating three-request compatibility handshake and capability-specific semantic validation.
- Distinguish authentication, network, server-unavailable, incompatible-contract, and partial-capability states.
- Route authentication failures through the existing per-server login handling.
- Add a server-bound Kanban data-client seam and initial observable feature state suitable for later slices.
- Add a Debug-only `--kanban-lab` launch path following the existing Streaming Lab pattern.
- Register every new source/test file in the Xcode project.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every upstream-decoded property is optional; unknown fields and unknown Status values do not crash.
- Missing Board/Card identity, current Board, Status, or safety-critical envelope data is never guessed.
- The handshake issues no mutation, Preview Dispatch, or Run Dispatcher request.
- Missing routes, `503`, wrong content type, malformed JSON, and missing semantic structure produce the correct unavailable/partial state.
- Normal Release and ordinary Debug navigation contain no Kanban entry.
- The lab can render compatible, incompatible, authentication, network, and retry states without real server mutation.
- Normal UI and logs do not expose raw payloads, filesystem paths, or authenticated server data.

## Tests and validation

- Endpoint contract tests for method, path, query encoding, cookies/custom headers, and no unintended Origin/Referer/Authorization headers.
- Decoding/semantic tests for minimal envelopes, missing fields, unknown additions, unknown Status, malformed JSON, non-JSON, `401`, `404`, and `503`.
- View-model tests for retry, stale handshake completion, server isolation, and authentication forwarding.
- Focused suites, full XCTest suite, and a signed Debug simulator launch through `--kanban-lab`.

## Out of scope

Board UI, live events, mutations, normal navigation activation, and any server-side change.

title: Deliver read-only Status Focus board browsing
body:
## Goal

Deliver the owner-selected native Status Focus experience for safe, read-only Kanban browsing inside the hidden Kanban Lab.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.3, §17.4, §17.7, and §17.8.

## Scope

- Add verified reads for Board snapshots, stats, and Profile history.
- Present one Status at a time with a horizontally scrollable Status selector and counts over a vertical Card list.
- Support local Board browsing, Board switching in the header, local Profile grouping, search, Profile/tenant/include-archived/only-mine filters, and clear-filter behavior.
- Show all six live Status values and optional Archived Cards; preserve unknown Status values as visible unsupported values.
- Build Card summaries with stable identity, ID, priority, tenant, title, Markdown-aware preview, Assigned Profile/Unassigned, counts, age, and specified staleness thresholds.
- Cover first-load, refresh, dense, empty, filtered-empty, incompatible, partial-capability, and error states.
- Keep Board choice, grouping, filters, selection, and all fetched data server-isolated and initially transient.
- Add localized copy and complete VoiceOver/Dynamic Type/Reduce Motion/light-dark behavior with 44-point practical targets.

## Acceptance criteria

- Browsing never calls Make Active Board or mutates global `lane_by_profile`.
- Running Cards are visible; no direct move control is introduced in this slice.
- Search matches ID, title, body, Assigned Profile, and tenant from loaded Board data.
- Card/status identity remains stable through filtering and refresh.
- Large Dynamic Type reflows without clipping or fixed-height Cards.
- VoiceOver announces Status counts and concise Card identity/metadata in canonical vocabulary.
- Incomplete Kanban remains accessible only through `--kanban-lab`.

## Tests and validation

- Endpoint/query tests for snapshot, stats, filters, minimal `changed:false`, and older stats envelopes.
- View-model tests for Board/Status/filter transitions, stale reads, unknown Status, server switch, and state preservation.
- Focused accessibility/localization assertions, focused suites, and full XCTest.
- Signed iPhone 17 simulator launch in light/dark, dense/empty/error, accessibility Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and Reduce Motion.
- Owner validates the Status Focus interaction before the PR publishes.

## Out of scope

Card detail, writes, live updates, Board management, Dispatcher, normal navigation activation.

title: Add Kanban live updates and offline reconciliation
body:
## Goal

Make hidden Kanban browsing server-authoritative and resilient to live changes, backgrounding, stream failure, and connectivity loss before writes are added.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.2, §17.3, §17.5, §17.6, and §17.8.

## Scope

- Add verified event polling and SSE endpoints with cursor/resume handling.
- Start SSE while Kanban is visible, reconnect on Board change, and coalesce event bursts before affected-state refetch.
- Fall back after repeated stream failures to 30-second event polling with a persistent **Live updates delayed** notice.
- Make pull-to-refresh a full reconciliation that also retries SSE.
- Suspend live refresh in the background and reconcile immediately on foreground.
- Preserve the in-memory Board snapshot on disconnect, mark it **Offline—showing previously loaded data**, and mark loaded detail stale.
- Introduce shared reconciliation/generation rules that prevent late reads and event refreshes from overwriting newer state.
- Reconcile fully before future write capability can become enabled after reconnect.
- Do not persist Kanban snapshots for offline use.

## Acceptance criteria

- SSE handles `hello`, `events`, frame IDs/cursors, keepalives, unknown event kinds, reconnect, and Board changes without duplicate/lost cursor advancement.
- Polling fallback and recovery are observable and do not create request storms.
- Background/foreground transitions cannot apply stale Board data.
- Offline state preserves browsing but exposes no enabled mutation/Dispatcher/shared-state action seam.
- A server switch tears down streams, timers, cursors, and transient state from the prior server.
- No stream or error logging exposes event payload values.

## Tests and validation

- Request/decoder tests for SSE handshake/events, polling envelopes, cursor boundaries, malformed frames, and unknown event kinds.
- Deterministic scheduler/view-model tests for coalescing, reconnect backoff, polling fallback, Board/server switch, background/foreground, stale completion, and offline recovery.
- Focused suites, full XCTest, and signed simulator launch using controlled mock stream/disconnect scenarios.

## Out of scope

Writes, persisted offline cache, background streaming, push notifications, and normal navigation activation.

title: Deliver Card detail, comments, and operational history
body:
## Goal

Provide complete native Card inspection and comment capability, including deliberately accessed operational history, while preserving privacy and read consistency.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.3–17.8.

## Scope

- Add verified API support for Card detail, worker-log tail, and adding comments.
- Present Markdown description and Card metadata, comments, events, Prerequisites, Dependents, Dispatch Runs, and worker-log access.
- Keep dense/sensitive operational sections progressive and explicitly requested; never place raw worker logs in generic errors, analytics, or OSLog.
- Add nonblank comment composition and persistent inline success/failure/retry behavior; no comment edit/delete affordance.
- Keep an open Card detail open across remote Status changes and refresh it through the shared live-reconciliation path.
- Handle Card disappearance or Board disappearance with reconciliation and canonical explanatory copy.
- Provide accessible section structure, focus behavior, Dynamic Type reflow, selectable/copyable content where appropriate, and localized copy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Detail decodes minimal/expanded envelopes tolerantly without inventing missing identity, link direction, or operational values.
- Prerequisites and Dependents use canonical direction and labels.
- Worker-log requests use the verified byte-tail contract and clearly distinguish absent, truncated, loading, and failed logs.
- Comment submission is serialized for the Card, never blindly retried, and reconciles after ambiguous outcome.
- Refresh and live events cannot replace a newer pending comment state with stale detail.
- Raw payloads, filesystem paths, claim identifiers, worker identifiers, and logs never leak outside the explicit detail/history surfaces.

## Tests and validation

- Endpoint/decoder tests for detail, comments, events, links, runs, log tail, truncation, missing Card, unknown additions, and malformed operational metadata.
- View-model tests for comment success/failure/ambiguity, remote Status change, stale detail, entity disappearance, and server isolation.
- Accessibility/localization assertions, focused suites, full XCTest, and signed simulator scenarios for dense/empty/error/truncated history.

## Out of scope

Card editing, Status/dependency mutations, Bulk Actions, Board management, Dispatcher invocation, and normal navigation activation.

title: Implement Card creation and editing
body:
## Goal

Implement complete native Card creation and supported field editing with idempotent retry, draft conflict handling, and server-authoritative reconciliation.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.3–17.8.

## Scope

- Add verified Create Card and Edit Card requests.
- New Card opens the complete native editor; do not add a separate single-title quick-create path.
- Creation supports title, body, initial Triage/To Do/Ready Status, priority, Assigned Profile, tenant, workspace kind/path, skills, maximum runtime, one initial Prerequisite, and an idempotency key.
- Editing supports only title, body, tenant, priority, Assigned Profile, and permitted Status selection; visibly preserve create-only fields as non-editable.
- Confirm creation of a Ready, Unassigned Card with the Dispatcher-skip warning.
- Preserve the local draft if remote state changed after the editor opened; block ordinary Save and offer Reload Server Version or Review and Overwrite.
- Reuse the original idempotency key when retrying the same creation intent.
- Use inline validation/action errors and reconcile after uncertain responses; do not blindly retry writes.
- Add localized forms and complete focus, keyboard, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, cancellation, and save-progress behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Request bodies contain only verified fields, exact Board scoping, and no speculative aliases.
- Blank title, invalid priority/runtime, unsupported workspace values, and missing safety-critical options fail locally or surface verified server validation.
- Cancel before submission performs no write; navigation after submission does not imply cancellation.
- Creation/editing is disabled offline or when its capability is incompatible.
- Conflicting remote edits never silently discard the local draft.
- Successful or ambiguous writes settle through authoritative response/refetch without stale snapshot overwrite.

## Tests and validation

- Exact method/path/query/body tests, including create/edit asymmetry and idempotency-key reuse.
- Decoder/validation tests for minimal/unknown/malformed responses and verified refusal/error shapes.
- View-model tests for validation, cancellation, conflict choices, offline/partial compatibility, timeout reconciliation, stale completion, and server isolation.
- Accessibility/localization assertions, focused suites, full XCTest, and signed simulator editor scenarios.

## Out of scope

General workflow actions, dependency changes after creation, Bulk Actions, Board management, Dispatcher, and normal navigation activation.

title: Implement Card workflow, dependency, and archive mutations
body:
## Goal

Implement safe single-Card workflow and dependency mutations with optimistic interaction, exact server verbs, Running safeguards, archive Undo, and explicit uncertainty recovery.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.3–17.8.

## Scope

- Add verified requests for Card Status/edit transitions, Block, Unblock, add Prerequisite, remove Prerequisite, and single-Card Archive.
- Offer explicit accessible Move actions for writable Status destinations; drag may supplement but never be required.
- Never offer Running as a direct destination.
- Confirm every transition out of Running with the claim/worker-state warning.
- Preserve structured Block/Unblock/Complete semantics and server refusal errors.
- Apply ordinary reversible mutations optimistically, serialize per Card, allow unrelated Cards concurrently, and keep server state authoritative.
- Add/remove dependencies in exact Prerequisite-to-Dependent direction with self/cycle/refusal errors surfaced safely.
- After successful single-Card Archive, offer short-lived Undo to the immediately previous Status.
- Implement Checking Result, Try Again, and Outcome Uncertain reconciliation without blind write retry.
- Maintain focus/navigation/scroll stability through mutations and remote refresh.

## Acceptance criteria

- Same-Card writes cannot overlap; unrelated-Card writes may.
- SSE/poll/manual refresh cannot overwrite a pending optimistic mutation.
- Running entry is impossible from UI/request construction.
- Leaving Running, archive, block/unblock, complete, dependency success/refusal, timeout, disappearance, and uncertain outcome all have persistent recoverable states.
- Undo uses current authoritative state and never bypasses normal reconciliation rules.
- Mutations are disabled offline, for unknown Status Cards, or when their specific capability is incompatible.

## Tests and validation

- Exact endpoint/payload tests for PATCH, block/unblock, link/unlink, and all supported Status semantics.
- View-model tests for serialization, unrelated concurrency, optimistic state, late events, response/refetch settlement, Running confirmation, Undo expiry, refusal, partial compatibility, and uncertain outcomes.
- Accessibility/localization assertions for explicit non-drag movement and focus retention.
- Focused suites, full XCTest, and signed simulator mutation scenarios against controlled fixtures.

## Out of scope

Bulk Actions, Board-wide writes, Dispatcher, hard delete, and normal navigation activation.

title: Deliver accessible Card selection and Bulk Actions
body:
## Goal

Deliver accessible multi-Card selection and exact named Bulk Actions with non-atomic result handling and failed-member recovery.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.3–17.8.

## Scope

- Add Select Cards mode with persistent selection count and stable selection across safe refresh/filter transitions.
- Support exactly named Bulk Actions: Change Status, Assign Profile, Set Priority, and Archive Cards.
- Require confirmation for Archive Cards; do not use a generic Bulk Update control.
- Treat the verified bulk response as per-Card and non-atomic even when HTTP status is 200.
- Lock overlapping Board-wide writes during submission/reconciliation.
- Refetch every selected Card before reporting results.
- Keep successful Cards committed, identify each Card needing attention, retain failed Cards selected, and enable Retry Failed only after reconciliation.
- Never retry the full selection automatically.
- Make selection and every action fully usable without drag or precision gestures; preserve meaningful VoiceOver focus and announce results.
- Add persistent localized success/failure/partial summaries rather than toast-only feedback.

## Acceptance criteria

- Empty/invalid selections cannot submit.
- Selection identity survives list movement and does not cross Board/server boundaries.
- Partial application within one Card is reconciled before presentation.
- Retry Failed targets only currently failed/reconciled Cards.
- Offline, incompatible, unknown-Status, and concurrent Board-wide states disable actions with specific explanations.
- Focus returns to a meaningful Card/control after success, partial failure, cancellation, filtering, and refresh.

## Tests and validation

- Exact bulk body and per-result decoding tests, including HTTP-200 partial failures and malformed members.
- View-model tests for selection stability, Board locks, mixed success, ambiguous result, reconciliation, Retry Failed, filter/refresh interaction, and server switch.
- Accessibility/localization assertions, focused suites, and full XCTest.
- Signed simulator validation with VoiceOver, accessibility Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion, partial failure, and all four actions.
- Owner validates selection/focus and recovery behavior before the PR publishes.

## Out of scope

Single-Card workflow implementation, Board management, Dispatcher, and normal navigation activation.

title: Implement Board management and shared active-Board controls
body:
## Goal

Implement native Board creation, metadata editing, archive, and explicit shared active-Board control without conflating local browsing with server-global state.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.3–17.8.

## Scope

- Add verified requests for Create Board, Edit Board metadata, Archive Board, and Make Active Board.
- Create supports immutable slug plus name, description, icon, and color; it does not automatically make the new Board active.
- Browsing/switching the Board shown in Hermex remains local and sends explicit Board scope on every request.
- Make Active Board is a separate confirmed action warning that other Hermes clients see the shared change.
- Archive Board requires confirmation that Hermex cannot restore it in-app.
- Default Board cannot be archived; slug cannot be edited.
- If the browsed Board is archived/removed elsewhere, explain the state and return to Board selection without unexpected cross-client navigation.
- Present Board counts/metadata without exposing `db_path`.
- Serialize Board-wide writes and reconcile Board list/current pointer after every result or ambiguity.
- Add localized, accessible forms, confirmations, progress, and persistent error/result states.

## Acceptance criteria

- Creation sends no implicit `switch:true`.
- No UI exposes archived-Board restore/listing, hard delete, default-Board archive, or global grouping mutation.
- Another client changing the active Board never navigates Hermex away from the locally browsed Board.
- Timeout/disconnect/malformed write results use Checking Result and authoritative refetch; writes are never blindly retried.
- Board/server changes tear down stale selection, streams, and in-flight state safely.
- Shared/local Board concepts use canonical copy and VoiceOver labels.

## Tests and validation

- Exact create/edit/archive/switch request tests, including no hard-delete query and no implicit switch.
- View-model tests for Board-wide serialization, remote current change, remote archive/removal, default restrictions, ambiguity, offline/partial compatibility, and server isolation.
- Accessibility/localization assertions, focused suites, full XCTest, and signed simulator multi-Board scenarios.

## Out of scope

Archived-Board restoration/listing, hard deletion, global grouping mutation, Dispatcher, and normal navigation activation.

title: Implement Preview Dispatch and Run Dispatcher
body:
## Goal

Implement the Dispatcher capability with advisory Preview Dispatch, explicit budget/execution safeguards, Board-wide single flight, and persistent reconciled outcomes.

Canonical specification: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §17.3, §17.5–17.8.

## Scope

- Add the verified dispatcher request using query parameters `board`, `dry_run`, and `max=8`; never rely on JSON Board.
- Preview Dispatch is non-spawning, optional, timestamped, and explicitly advisory/staleable.
- Run Dispatcher requires confirmation that it may start workers and consume API budget.
- Preview and Run are single-flight per Board; Run participates in the Board-wide write lock.
- Never automatically retry Run Dispatcher.
- After Run, refetch the Board and present a persistent localized result summary covering all verified result categories without assuming unstable member value types.
- Handle timeout/disconnect/malformed result with explicit uncertainty and canonical reconciliation.
- Disable both actions offline or when Dispatcher capability is incompatible.
- Keep raw operational values out of generic errors/logging and preserve accessible confirmation/focus behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Request construction proves Board is in the query, dry-run is correct, and maximum is exactly eight.
- Preview is not required before Run and never uses spawning mode.
- Repeated taps, navigation, live events, and other Board-wide writes cannot cause overlapping dispatch requests.
- Confirmation copy names worker launch and API-budget risk.
- Stale preview, refusal, partial/unknown result fields, uncertain Run outcome, and Board disappearance remain understandable and recoverable.
- No test or manual scenario launches billable workers or mutates the maintainer's real Boards.

## Tests and validation

- Exact query/request and tolerant result-decoding tests for Preview and Run.
- View-model tests for single flight, Board lock, stale preview, refusal, timeout, uncertainty, reconciliation, offline/partial compatibility, and server switch.
- Accessibility/localization assertions, focused suites, and full XCTest.
- Signed simulator/manual validation against an isolated seeded server or deterministic non-spawning fixture.
- Owner validates safety copy and interaction before the PR publishes.

## Out of scope

Dispatcher cancellation, automatic retry, configurable maximum, background execution, and normal navigation activation.

title: Bound cache-first transcript loading for long sessions
body:
## Summary

Reopening a session can synchronously paint an unbounded cached transcript before the bounded server page arrives. Sessions that have accumulated many cached rows through **Load earlier** can therefore freeze the app during navigation, especially when the rows contain rich Markdown and tool activity.

This is separate from #32 / PR #33: lazy transcript rendering improves long-scroll behavior, while this bug allows cache-first loading to bypass the existing 50-message mobile page budget entirely.

## Current behavior

`ChatViewModel.loadOlderMessages` caches the full accumulated `messages` array after each prepend. `CacheStore.cachedMessages` later fetches every cached row for that session, up to the global 5,000-message cache cap. `prepareInitialMessageLoad` assigns that entire array to the observed transcript on `@MainActor` before the network request starts.

A local tool-heavy session sample contained:

- 448 raw messages
- 224 tool rows
- about 1.27 MB of message content
- individual tool rows up to about 65 KB

Once such a transcript has been paged into the cache, reopening it can eagerly construct hundreds of expensive rows in the current plain `VStack`, making the app appear hung.

## Expected behavior

Cache-first and offline fallback reads should honor the same bounded recent-message budget as normal mobile session loading. The full cached history may remain stored for now, but opening a chat must not synchronously publish the whole cache into the transcript.

## Proposed fix

- Add a bounded newest-message read to `CacheStore.cachedMessages`.
- Use the existing 50-message page limit for cache-first paint, offline fallback, and optimistic-message reconciliation.
- Preserve ascending transcript order after fetching the newest rows.
- Add regression coverage proving a cache larger than one page opens with only the newest page.

## Reproduction

1. Open a long session.
2. Use **Load earlier** repeatedly so the app caches more than one page.
3. Return to the session list.
4. Reopen the session.
5. Observe that navigation completes but the app becomes unresponsive while the cached transcript is published/rendered.

## Validation

- Focused cache-first regression test.
- Full XCTest suite.
- Signed simulator build and launch.
- Manual reopen check with a cache larger than one page.

title: Add NetBird as a private-network onboarding option
body:
### Use case

Hello, I have been diving down the Hermes rabbit-hole and I love your app. However, I also work for NetBird which is an open-source Zero Trust network security platform built on WireGuard.

Hermex currently presents Tailscale-specific onboarding instructions. Because NetBird provides the same kind of secure private connectivity between an iPhone and a self-hosted Hermes server, people who already use NetBird should be able to use it without translating Tailscale-specific prompts and setup steps themselves. I was able to get Hermex working perfectly by prompting "I am about to paste Tailscale specific instructions, I need you to translate them to use NetBird instead". However, many people who already have NetBird setups on their network like me would have a better experience just being able to set it up the same way as Tailscale. Supporting both options would make the onboarding experience useful to more people and better reflect that Hermex is not technically tied to one private-network provider.

### Proposed behavior

Make onboarding describe the connection generically as a private network while preserving provider-specific setup instructions where they are useful.

- Let the user select Tailscale or NetBird from both the setup-prompt page and the iPhone setup page.
- Keep the selection synchronized between those pages.
- Generate a provider-specific prompt for the selected service.
- Provide the appropriate iPhone installation link and setup instructions.
- Keep the existing Tailscale flow available and make unrelated app copy provider-neutral.

The NetBird prompt should follow the same structure and level of detail as the Tailscale prompt, while using NetBird-specific commands and concepts. It should cover installing and connecting NetBird, binding Hermes WebUI to the private-network interface, retaining password authentication, limiting access through the host firewall and NetBird access policies, configuring automatic startup, finding the NetBird address, verifying the health endpoint, and returning the connection details needed by the iPhone app.

### Acceptance outcomes

- [ ] The setup-prompt and iPhone setup pages offer a Tailscale/NetBird selector that works in light and dark mode.
- [ ] Changing the provider on either page updates the other page.
- [ ] The Tailscale prompt and setup path continue to work.
- [ ] The NetBird prompt contains NetBird-specific installation, connection, access-policy, address-discovery, startup, and verification instructions.
- [ ] The NetBird iPhone path links to the NetBird App Store listing.
- [ ] General onboarding, connection, documentation, and error copy refers to a private network instead of assuming Tailscale.
- [ ] `PROJECT_SPEC.md` and contributor documentation describe both supported providers.
- [ ] Existing API behavior and authentication requirements remain unchanged.
- [ ] No new third-party app dependencies are introduced.

### Upstream dependency notes

This is a client-side onboarding and documentation change. It does not require new `hermes-webui` endpoints or JSON shapes. Tailscale and NetBird are alternate private transports to the existing Hermes WebUI server, using the current server URL, password authentication, port, and health-check contract.

title: Login fails against current hermes-agent — "provider" field missing from /auth/password-login request
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1 - Run a current hermes-agent dashboard with the basic-auth provider configured: hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119, with HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME / HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD set in ~/.hermes/.env.
2 - Confirm the gate is active: curl -s http://<host>:9119/api/status returns "auth_required":true,"auth_providers":["basic"].
3 - Confirm login works via curl directly at the endpoint level, with provider included in the body:


   curl -i -X POST http://<host>:9119/auth/password-login \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"username":"admin","password":"<redacted>","provider":"basic"}'

→ returns 200 OK with valid session cookies.
4. In Hermex, enter the same server URL, username, and password, and tap Sign In.

### Expected behavior

Hermex signs in successfully, same as the direct curl request with provider included.

### Actual behavior

Hermex shows "The password was rejected. Check the server password and try again," and separately "The server response could not be read." Testing the same request without the provider field (i.e. {"username":"admin","password":"<redacted>"} only) reproduces this exactly:

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{"detail":[{"type":"missing","loc":["body","provider"],"msg":"Field required",...}]}

This suggests Hermex's login request omits the provider field that this hermes-agent version now requires, so the server returns a 422 whose shape doesn't match what Hermex expects to parse, producing the "server response could not be read" error.


This may be tied to a recent upstream hermes-agent auth fix titled fix(auth): detect configured providers absent from registry, which appears to have added the provider requirement to /auth/password-login.

### App version / commit

Latest App Store build, version 1.4

### iOS version and device

iOS version 26.5.2, Model Name iPhone 15 Pro Max, Model Number MU6D3LL/A

### hermes-webui server version

Note: this backend is actually Nous Research's hermes-agent (https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent), not nesquena/hermes-webui — version 0.18.2 (release 2026.7.7.2), running the built-in hermes dashboard web UI with the bundled dashboard_auth/basic plugin. This may itself be worth flagging: Hermex's docs describe hermes-webui as the only supported backend, but the built-in hermes-agent dashboard shares a very similar login/session model and mostly works, aside from this specific field gap.

### How the phone reaches the server

None

title: Show opt-in tokens-per-second metrics on assistant responses
body:
## Context

Current `hermes-webui` exposes response-speed data through the existing chat stream; Hermex does not need a new endpoint.

Verified against upstream commit `2f3e42dc649e6d2bae572a0655681d9bb212c78d`:

- Live `metering` SSE payloads can contain `tps`, `tps_available`, `estimated`, `session_id`, and `usage`.
- Final `done.usage` can contain turn-specific `tps` and `duration_seconds`.
- Settled assistant messages can contain persisted `_turnTps` and `_turnDuration`.
- Live `metering.tps` represents the server-wide average of active streams. Final `usage.tps` and `_turnTps` are specific to the completed turn.
- The official [Chat and streaming API documentation](https://get-hermes.ai/api-docs/reference/chat-streaming/) identifies `metering` as the live-TPS SSE event.

A running server was not available during intake. Revalidate the shapes against the repo-local upstream copy or a running server immediately before implementation.

## Current behavior

Hermex ignores `metering` as an unknown SSE event. Its completion-usage and message models do not retain TPS, and assistant response headers can currently show only the optional response timestamp.

## Expected behavior

Add a local Settings → Chat preference named “Response Speed,” defaulting off.

When enabled:

- While a response streams, show the valid upstream live value as a compact `47.3 t/s` label in the assistant-turn header.
- Replace the live, server-wide value with the turn-specific final value when completion metadata arrives.
- Retain and display final TPS after reopening a session when `_turnTps` is present.
- Hide TPS when the server does not provide a valid value. Never derive an estimate from characters, words, or SSE chunk counts.
- Keep Response Speed independent from Response Timestamps:
  - speed only: marker + TPS;
  - timestamp only: marker + time;
  - both: marker + time + TPS.
- Expose a full accessibility label such as “47.3 tokens per second.”

## Acceptance criteria

- A local Response Speed toggle exists under Settings → Chat and defaults to off.
- Hermex tolerantly decodes optional `metering` fields without changing unknown-event compatibility.
- Live TPS appears only when:
  - `tps_available == true`;
  - `estimated != true`;
  - `tps` is finite and greater than zero.
- Live TPS updates the active assistant response without creating transcript rows or disrupting streaming text.
- On successful completion, valid `done.usage.tps` replaces the live value.
- Persisted `_turnTps` is decoded from assistant messages and retained in the local transcript cache.
- Reopening a session displays available final TPS without requiring another stream.
- Missing or malformed TPS data is silently omitted; older servers continue working normally.
- Starting another response, switching sessions, cancellation, and terminal errors cannot leak a stale live value into another turn.
- The display uses `t/s`, with one decimal for ordinary values and accessible spoken text using “tokens per second.”
- Enabling Response Speed shows the assistant marker independently of the Response Timestamps setting.
- Relevant strings are localized.

## Validation plan

Automated coverage:

- Decode valid, missing, malformed, unavailable, and estimated `metering` payloads.
- Decode `done.usage.tps` and persisted `_turnTps`.
- Verify live-to-final replacement.
- Verify stale-state clearing on completion, cancellation, failure, session changes, and new streams.
- Verify formatting and accessibility text.
- Verify all combinations of Response Speed and Response Timestamps.
- Verify cache round-tripping for `_turnTps`.
- Run the full XCTest suite.

Manual simulator validation:

1. Confirm TPS is absent by default.
2. Enable Response Speed and stream a response from a compatible server.
3. Confirm the live value updates in the assistant header.
4. Confirm completion replaces it with the final turn-specific value.
5. Leave and reopen the session; confirm final TPS remains visible.
6. Exercise speed-only, timestamp-only, and combined headers.
7. Test a response with no TPS data and confirm no placeholder appears.
8. Cancel a response and switch sessions to confirm no stale TPS remains.
9. Check light/dark mode, larger Dynamic Type, and VoiceOver.

Because this changes a live streaming surface, retain `needs-manual-validation`.

## Non-goals

- Adding or changing a server endpoint.
- Calculating TPS locally from text length, words, or SSE frame counts.
- Displaying upstream high/low/active-stream metering statistics.
- Building TPS analytics or cross-session performance history.
- Synchronizing the local preference with the server’s `show_tps` setting.
- Changing the existing context-window or usage-analytics features.

title: Connection fails against current hermes-agent — /health returns HTML, /api/auth/status 401s without the dashboard's embedded session token
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the bundled `hermes-agent` web dashboard (not `nesquena/hermes-webui`), no basic-auth env vars set: `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119`.
2. Reachable over HTTPS (in my case via a local reverse proxy terminating TLS in front of the dashboard's plain-HTTP port, since ATS blocks the app's plaintext-HTTP path for Tailscale CGNAT IPs — see below).
3. Call the two endpoints Hermex's connect flow depends on directly:

   ```
   curl -i https://<server>/health
   ```
   → `200 OK`, but the body is the dashboard's SPA `index.html` (a `<!doctype html>` page with an embedded `window.__HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN__`), not JSON. `AuthAPIClient.health()` expects a decodable `HealthResponse` with a `status` field, so this fails to parse.

   ```
   curl -i https://<server>/api/auth/status
   ```
   → `401 Unauthorized`, body `{"detail":"Unauthorized"}` — no username/password or `provider` flow is configured on this server at all; the dashboard instead gates its API behind the session token embedded in the HTML served at `/`, which the SPA frontend reads and presumably attaches to subsequent requests (cookie or header — not confirmed from the outside). Hermex's login flow doesn't know about this token and has no way to obtain or send it.

4. In Hermex, adding this server as the connect target fails at the initial `testConnection` step (`health()` → decode failure), surfacing as "The server response could not be read."

### Expected behavior

Either:
- Hermex's connect flow tolerates a non-JSON `/health` response (e.g. falls back to treating any `2xx` as healthy when the body isn't parseable as `HealthResponse`), and/or
- Hermex documents/handles the embedded-session-token auth model used by the built-in `hermes-agent` dashboard as a distinct case from the password/`provider` flow already tracked in #172.

### Actual behavior

Connection test fails with a generic "The server response could not be read" before any password prompt is reached, because `/health` isn't JSON on this server.

### Notes / relation to #172

This looks like a second, earlier-stage instance of the same underlying issue raised in #172: the bundled `hermes-agent` dashboard's HTTP contract (no JSON `/health`, session-token-gated API instead of password/`provider` login) diverges from what Hermex expects from `nesquena/hermes-webui`. Given `hermes-agent`'s dashboard is explicitly offered as a supported connection target in Hermex's own onboarding copy ("Set up Hermes Web UI on this machine... Install Tailscale... configure Tailscale access"), it might be worth either:
- adding an explicit compatibility/contract test against a real `hermes-agent` dashboard (not just `hermes-webui`), or
- clarifying in the docs that only `nesquena/hermes-webui` is supported today, and the bundled `hermes-agent` dashboard is not (yet).

### App version / commit

Latest App Store build, version 1.4 (same as reported in #172)

### hermes-agent server version

`hermes-agent` 0.13.0 (release 2026.5.7), bundled dashboard, no basic-auth configured.

### How the phone reaches the server

Tailscale, HTTPS via a local reverse proxy (self-signed cert, installed and fully trusted on-device) terminating in front of the dashboard's plain-HTTP port — done this way specifically because Hermex's `NSExceptionDomains` ATS exception for `100.64.0.0/10` doesn't work (ATS exception domains only match literal hostnames, not CIDR ranges, so IPs in that range never get the insecure-HTTP exception and iOS blocks the plaintext connection outright).

title: Hermex model picker omits provider models outside the curated catalog
body:
## Context

Hermes WebUI separates each provider’s catalog into a curated visible list (`models`) and a larger overflow catalog (`extra_models`). Hermex decodes both collections, but its chat and Settings model pickers only display and search `models`.

For Nous Portal, this leaves only approximately 15 featured models visible and excludes less expensive or faster options such as MiMo, DeepSeek, and MiniMax.

## Current behavior

- The Nous section reports and exposes only 15 models.
- Searching the picker searches only those 15 models.
- Models present in `extra_models` cannot be discovered or selected through the normal picker.
- Users must know and manually enter an exact custom model ID.

## Expected behavior

Keep the curated provider list compact by default, while allowing users to:

- Search the provider’s complete `models + extra_models` catalog.
- Choose “Show all models” to browse the complete catalog.
- Select overflow models exactly like curated models.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provider sections initially show their curated `models`.
- Each provider with additional `extra_models` offers a clear “Show all models” action.
- Search matches both `models` and `extra_models`.
- Searching automatically exposes matching overflow models without requiring “Show all.”
- Section counts communicate the complete selectable catalog size.
- Selecting an overflow model preserves its exact model ID and provider ID.
- Favorites, recents, selected-state display, and model switching work for overflow models.
- Duplicate IDs across `models` and `extra_models` appear only once.
- Both the chat composer picker and Settings default-model picker follow the same catalog behavior.
- Providers without `extra_models` retain their current behavior.
- Failed or unavailable live-model requests continue falling back to the static catalog.

## Validation plan

- Before implementation, verify `/api/models` and `/api/models/live` response shapes against the running server or the repo-local upstream copy.
- Add tests for combined-catalog deduplication, counts, searching overflow models, “Show all,” selection, and providers without overflow models.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Manually test on the simulator with Nous Portal:
  1. Confirm only the curated list is initially visible.
  2. Search for an overflow model such as DeepSeek.
  3. Select it and verify the chat uses the exact model/provider.
  4. Reopen the picker and verify selected state.
  5. Use “Show all models.”
  6. Repeat selection through the Settings default-model picker.

## Non-goals

- Changing which models Hermes WebUI classifies as featured.
- Modifying the server’s provider discovery or pricing metadata.
- Adding client-maintained model catalogs.
- Removing custom model entry.

title: Reasoning effort changes fail because POST /api/reasoning omits session_id
body:
## Bug description

Changing the reasoning effort in Hermex fails against a current Hermes WebUI server that requires reasoning-effort mutations to be scoped to the active session.

The server returns HTTP 400:

```text
session_id is required for reasoning effort changes
```

Chat, uploads, session loading, and model-aware reasoning-effort discovery continue to work. Only the effort mutation is rejected.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Hermex to a Hermes WebUI server with session-scoped reasoning-effort writes.
2. Open an existing chat session.
3. Change the reasoning effort from the composer (for example, Medium to High).
4. Observe the error banner.

## Expected behavior

Hermex includes the active session ID in the reasoning-effort mutation, and the selected effort is applied to that session.

## Actual behavior

Hermex sends a body equivalent to:

```json
{
  "effort": "high"
}
```

The server requires:

```json
{
  "effort": "high",
  "session_id": "<active-session-id>"
}
```

and therefore responds with HTTP 400.

## Confirmed root cause on current `master`

`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+ServerPanels.swift` currently defines:

```swift
func saveReasoningEffort(_ effort: String) async throws -> ReasoningStatusResponse {
    try await send(
        endpoint: .reasoning(),
        method: "POST",
        body: ReasoningEffortRequest(effort: effort)
    )
}
```

and:

```swift
private struct ReasoningEffortRequest: Encodable {
    let effort: String
}
```

`ChatViewModel.selectReasoningEffort(_:)` calls this method without passing its existing `sessionID`.

The `/reasoning <level>` slash-command path is confirmed affected: its effort branch also calls `client.saveReasoningEffort(reasoning)` without a session ID.

## Suggested fix

Pass the active session ID through the API client, for example:

```swift
func saveReasoningEffort(
    _ effort: String,
    sessionID: String
) async throws -> ReasoningStatusResponse
```

with:

```swift
private struct ReasoningEffortRequest: Encodable {
    let effort: String
    let sessionId: String
}
```

The client's existing `.convertToSnakeCase` encoding strategy should serialize `sessionId` as `session_id`.

Please cover both entry points:

- the composer reasoning-effort picker;
- `/reasoning <level>`.

The UI should guard against a missing or empty active `sessionID` and show a local, actionable error instead of sending an invalid POST. The session ID used for the mutation should be the active session at dispatch time.

Suggested regression coverage:

1. The composer picker sends the active session ID.
2. `/reasoning <level>` sends the same active session ID.
3. Encoding produces the JSON key `session_id`, not `sessionId`.
4. With no active session ID, Hermex sends no request and shows a local error.
5. Changing effort in one session does not mutate another session.
6. A session change around the mutation cannot apply an obsolete session ID silently.

## Environment

- Hermex: **1.4 from the Apple App Store** (App Store version history screenshot supplied by the reporter); behavior also confirmed in current repository `master`
- Build number: not shown in the App Store version-history screen
- Hermes WebUI: session-scoped reasoning-effort endpoint
- Model used during reproduction: GPT-5.6 Sol via OpenAI Codex

## Additional evidence

The server access log records the rejected request as:

```text
POST /api/reasoning -> 400
```

Requests immediately before and after it, including chat and upload endpoints, returned 200. This rules out a general connectivity or authentication failure.


## Follow-up verification

An independent read-only code audit and a direct source re-check confirmed:

- the composer picker calls `client.saveReasoningEffort(selectedEffort)` without `sessionID`;
- the `/reasoning <level>` effort branch calls `client.saveReasoningEffort(reasoning)` without `sessionID`;
- the Hermes WebUI handler reads `session_id` from the POST JSON body and emits the quoted 400 error when it is absent;
- display-only commands (`/reasoning show|hide`) use a separate server branch and do **not** require `session_id`, so `saveReasoningDisplay` should remain unchanged.

title: Auto-dismiss steering hint confirmation card
body:
## Context

When a steering hint is successfully delivered during an active response, Hermex displays a confirmation card above the composer. This feedback is transient and should not become part of the conversation history.

## Current behavior

“Steering hint delivered.” cards remain visible until the active response ends. Sending additional steering hints appends more cards, causing them to stack. When the response ends, the notices may be moved into the transcript.

## Expected behavior

Show at most one steering confirmation card. It should disappear 3 seconds after the latest successful steering hint and should never be preserved in the transcript.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A successfully delivered steering hint displays the existing “Steering hint delivered.” confirmation.
- [ ] The confirmation automatically disappears after 3 seconds.
- [ ] Sending another steering hint while the card is visible replaces the existing card and restarts the 3-second timer.
- [ ] No more than one steering confirmation card is visible at once.
- [ ] If the active response ends before the timer expires, the card disappears instead of moving into the transcript.
- [ ] Behavior applies both to `/steer` and to normal sends configured to steer an active response.
- [ ] Other pinned notices and steering failure/fallback messages retain their existing behavior.

## Validation plan

- Add automated coverage for initial display, replacement, timer reset, dismissal, and stream completion before dismissal.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- In a signed iPhone simulator build, send multiple steering hints during an active response and confirm that only the latest card remains, disappears after 3 seconds, and never enters the transcript.

## Non-goals

- Changing steering API behavior or payloads.
- Changing the confirmation text or card design.
- Changing queue, interrupt, background-task, compression, or failure/fallback notices.

title: Refine Kanban Card row layout, metadata spacing, and row affordances
body:
## Context

Refine three related defects in the Kanban Card row before activation in #158. They are grouped because they affect the same Card summary and navigation surfaces and share one focused validation pass.

This issue is now a closed-scope Card-row refinement. Dispatcher placement is tracked in #195; Manage Boards action presentation is tracked in #196.

## Current behavior

### Metadata icon/value spacing

Card metadata uses `Label` values inside a horizontal group. The default icon-to-title gap is visually close to the gap between separate metadata groups, so icons appear detached from the values they describe:

`[icon]    Unassigned  [icon]    app  [icon]    2  [icon]    1`

### Age and staleness alignment

The age label is trailing-aligned only within the navigation label, before the automatic disclosure chevron and separate Card-actions button. It therefore appears to float in the middle of the row rather than forming a stable trailing column.

Mixed age widths such as `2h`, `10m`, and `5m`, together with the different normal, warning, and critical staleness symbols, can also make the icon/value placement appear ragged between Cards.

### Navigation and Card actions

The inline navigation link automatically renders a disclosure chevron next to the separate ellipsis menu. These two trailing affordances compete visually, and the navigation hit region does not clearly read as the Card's primary action.

## Expected behavior

### Metadata spacing

Use a tight, consistent internal gap between each metadata icon and its value, with a visibly larger gap between separate metadata groups:

`[icon]  Unassigned  [icon]  app  [icon]  2  [icon]  1`

The implementation may use a custom label style or another suitable composition, but the acceptance criterion is the resulting visual hierarchy rather than a mandated mechanism.

### Age and staleness alignment

Treat the staleness symbol and abbreviated age as one unit. Give the symbol a consistent icon slot and trailing-align the complete age unit within the Card-content column immediately before the actions menu.

The layout must account for mixed age widths, all staleness symbols, localization, RTL, and accessibility Dynamic Type without unintended truncation. Implementation should not rely on a fragile fixed width that only fits the current English abbreviations.

### Navigation and Card actions

Make the Card's main content area the primary tap target for opening Card Detail. Remove the visible disclosure chevron.

Retain one trailing ellipsis button for quick Card actions. Tapping it opens the action menu without navigating. The implementation may use programmatic navigation or another SwiftUI structure that produces these behaviors; this issue does not mandate a particular navigation API.

Selection mode remains distinct: Card content toggles selection instead of navigating, while the existing selection indicator and accessibility traits remain intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The icon-to-value gap is visibly tighter than the gap between metadata groups.
- [ ] Metadata remains legible without collision or unintended truncation at standard and accessibility Dynamic Type sizes.
- [ ] Both horizontal and vertical `ViewThatFits` presentations remain deliberate and uncluttered.
- [ ] Verify whether tighter spacing changes the `ViewThatFits` branch chosen near its threshold; a newly fitting horizontal presentation must not appear cramped.
- [ ] The staleness symbol uses a consistent icon slot across normal, warning, and critical states.
- [ ] The complete age unit is trailing-aligned consistently immediately before the Card-actions control.
- [ ] Mixed ages such as `2h`, `10m`, and `5m` remain aligned without truncation.
- [ ] The main Card content area opens Card Detail.
- [ ] The visible disclosure chevron is removed.
- [ ] The ellipsis is the only trailing Card-action control and opens its menu without navigating.
- [ ] The ellipsis retains its practical 44-point target and existing availability and disabled logic.
- [ ] Selection mode still toggles Card selection instead of navigating, and preserves the checkmark state and selected accessibility traits.
- [ ] Card mutation status continues to render below the row.
- [ ] VoiceOver retains the composed Card summary, exposes a clear activation action for opening detail, and can return focus meaningfully to the originating Card.
- [ ] RTL, light/dark appearance, keyboard operation where applicable, and Reduce Motion remain correct.
- [ ] No Card, selection, mutation, or other Kanban data behavior changes.
- [ ] All changed user-facing copy is localized in every shipped language.

## Validation plan

### Automated

- Cover Card Detail navigation independently from Card-actions activation.
- Cover selection-mode toggling, indicators, and selected accessibility traits.
- Preserve Card-action availability and disabled logic.
- Preserve mutation status below the Card row.
- Verify changed accessibility labels, actions, and focus identity.
- Run focused Kanban tests, the full XCTest suite, localization-catalog validation, and `git diff --check`.

### Signed simulator

Use Debug Kanban Lab Cards spanning all three staleness states, mixed age widths such as `2h`, `10m`, and `5m`, and varied priority, body, assignee, tenant, comment, and dependency content.

- Capture screenshots at standard and accessibility Dynamic Type sizes.
- Verify metadata spacing and the horizontal/vertical `ViewThatFits` threshold.
- Verify staleness-symbol and age alignment across Card rows.
- Verify tap-to-open, ellipsis actions, selection mode, mutation status, and focus restoration.
- Check light and dark appearance, RTL, VoiceOver, keyboard operation where applicable, and Reduce Motion.

## Non-goals

- Dispatcher or toolbar layout; tracked in #195.
- Manage Boards row actions; tracked in #196.
- Changing Card or Kanban API, mutation, selection, or persistence behavior.
- Adding drag-only or swipe-only interactions.
- Activating Kanban or completing release evidence in #158.

## Ordering

Board management #156 and Dispatcher #157 are complete. This issue is not blocked and blocks #158.

title: SSE heartbeat comments are ignored, causing false stale-stream recovery and repeated reconnects
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `hermes-webui` behind an HTTPS reverse proxy and connect Hermex to it.
2. Open a chat in Hermex and send a request that produces at least one streamed event, then has a quiet period longer than approximately 18 seconds—for example, model reasoning or a long-running tool call that emits no token/tool event during that interval.
3. Keep the app in the foreground and watch the active response status.
4. Observe that Hermex changes to **Checking stream** and then **Reconnecting stream**, even though the server-side run is still active and the SSE connection is receiving heartbeat comments.
5. Inspect the `hermes-webui` access log. Hermex repeatedly polls `/api/chat/stream/status` and reopens the same stream with `replay=1&after_seq=...`.

This is intermittent with ordinary prompts, but it becomes reproducible when there is a sufficiently long gap between semantic SSE events after streaming has already started.

### Expected behavior

A healthy SSE heartbeat should count as transport activity. If `hermes-webui` continues sending heartbeat comments and `/api/chat/stream/status` reports the run as active, Hermex should keep the existing EventSource connection open.

A lack of tokens, reasoning deltas, or tool events should not by itself cause a reconnect. Hermex should reconnect only when there is evidence of a transport failure, such as:

- an EventSource/URLSession transport error;
- no heartbeat or other SSE bytes for a transport-staleness threshold; or
- a failed health/status check indicating the current stream cannot continue.

Long model-thinking or tool-execution pauses should therefore remain connected without visible UI stalls or repeated replay requests.

### Actual behavior

Hermex ignores SSE comment frames and only updates `lastProgressDate` for semantic events. After a semantic event has been received, a quiet period causes the stale-stream recovery loop to run:

- after 5 seconds, Hermex enters the checking state;
- after approximately 18 seconds without a semantic event, it forcibly reconnects;
- while a live tool call is shown, the reconnect threshold is approximately 25 seconds;
- the replacement connection uses run-journal replay from the last known sequence.

This causes visible pauses in the streaming UI and repeated **Reconnecting stream** states even when the original SSE transport appears healthy. Reconnection may also trigger transcript/session reloads, making the pause more noticeable for larger sessions.

A sanitized server log from one affected stream shows the same stream being reopened at intervals matching the 18-second client threshold, with no sequence progress between reconnects:

```text
07:18:21 GET /api/chat/stream?stream_id=<stream>                         200
07:18:56 GET /api/chat/stream?stream_id=<stream>&replay=1&after_seq=10  200
07:19:15 GET /api/chat/stream?stream_id=<stream>&replay=1&after_seq=10  200
07:19:34 GET /api/chat/stream?stream_id=<stream>&replay=1&after_seq=10  200
```

The same server log window contained no `BrokenPipe`, `ConnectionReset`, `TimeoutError`, or request-timeout entries. The server-side run remained active and `/api/chat/stream/status` continued returning HTTP 200.
## Technical analysis

### Server heartbeat

In `hermes-webui`, the chat SSE route sends and flushes an SSE comment every five seconds while no business event is available:

```python
_SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 5

try:
    item = subscriber.get(timeout=_SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
except queue.Empty:
    handler.wfile.write(b": heartbeat\n\n")
    handler.wfile.flush()
    continue
```

This indicates that the HTTP/SSE transport is still alive even when the model or a tool has no semantic event to emit.

### Hermex ignores comments

`HermesMobile/Networking/SSEClient.swift` currently discards EventSource comments:

```swift
func onComment(comment: String) {}
```

Only decoded message events are forwarded to `ChatStreamCoordinator`.

### Stale-stream timer is based on semantic progress

`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift` uses these defaults:

```swift
static let standard = ChatStreamCoordinatorTiming(
    checkingInterval: 5,
    reconnectInterval: 18,
    runningToolReconnectInterval: 25,
    statusPollCooldown: 4
)
```

`markProgress()` updates `lastProgressDate`, but it is called only for accepted semantic events such as token, reasoning, tool, title, approval, and clarification events. Heartbeat comments never reach the coordinator.

Once `elapsed >= reconnectInterval`, an otherwise active stream is deliberately stopped and reopened:

```swift
let shouldForceReconnect = elapsed >= reconnectInterval
...
reconnectStaleStream(
    streamID: expectedStreamID,
    usesReplay: response.replayAvailable == true
)
```

This explains the repeated reconnect interval and replay requests seen in the server log.

## Suggested fix

Please track transport activity separately from semantic response progress.

For example:

```swift
private(set) var lastTransportActivityDate: Date?
private(set) var lastSemanticProgressDate: Date?
```

Suggested behavior:

1. Forward EventSource comments from `SSEClient`, either as a dedicated `.heartbeat` event or through a transport-activity callback.
2. Update `lastTransportActivityDate` for every valid SSE message or comment.
3. Update `lastSemanticProgressDate` only for token/reasoning/tool/title/etc. events.
4. A semantic quiet period may trigger a lightweight status poll, but should not force a reconnect when heartbeats are still arriving and status reports `active == true`.
5. Force reconnect only after transport activity itself becomes stale, or after `onError`/another confirmed transport failure.

A minimal mitigation would be to forward comments and call `markProgress()` for heartbeat frames, but keeping separate transport and semantic timestamps would preserve the ability to display a useful “still working” state without conflating model progress with connection health.

## Acceptance criteria

- A stream that emits heartbeat comments every five seconds but no semantic event for at least 60 seconds remains on the original SSE connection.
- Hermex may show a non-error “still working” or checking state, but it does not enter a reconnect loop while status is active and heartbeat traffic is present.
- A stream with no heartbeat/message activity, or one whose EventSource reports a transport error, still reconnects and resumes from the last event ID/sequence.
- Existing replay behavior continues to prevent duplicate or missing transcript content after a real reconnect.
- Background/foreground suspend-and-resume recovery continues to work.
- Add a regression test with a fake SSE source that sends heartbeat comments for longer than `reconnectInterval` and verify that `stop()`/`start()` is not called again.
- Add a complementary test showing that absent transport activity still triggers recovery.

### App version / commit

App Store build: Hermex 1.4 - Current `master` inspected: `b747b32010f8e2e947672dbbaf93b63e8fc473e9`  The current source still contains the relevant behavior described below.

### iOS version and device

iPadOS 26.5 on iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)

### hermes-webui server version

- `hermes-webui` commit: `3c9304ae` - The server is healthy during the affected runs and sends an SSE heartbeat every five seconds.

### How the phone reaches the server

Reverse proxy

### Screenshots or screen recordings

A screen recording can be added showing Hermex switching from **Checking stream** to **Reconnecting stream** while the server-side run remains active.

title: File browser gives no feedback and can navigate to stale directories on slow networks
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a chat whose workspace contains at least two directories.
2. Open Files and load the root directory.
3. Add network delay, then tap one directory and a second directory before the first response returns.
4. Repeat a directory tap while the server is unavailable or returns an error.

Deterministic reproduction: delay `cat` by 400 ms and `leetcode-editor` by 50 ms. The final path becomes `cat` even though `leetcode-editor` was tapped last.

### Expected behavior

- Show immediate, visible loading feedback while keeping the existing list usable.
- The latest directory tap wins when requests finish out of order.
- A failed load remains visible and retryable without discarding the current directory list.

### Actual behavior

- Once entries are already visible, `FileBrowserView` does not render its `ProgressView`, so a tap can appear to do nothing.
- `FileBrowserViewModel.load(path:)` applies every response unconditionally; a slower earlier response can overwrite the later selection.
- Errors are only rendered when `entries.isEmpty`, and non-401 API errors are otherwise ignored by `AuthManager`, so failures can be silent while stale entries remain on screen.

The root/up/breadcrumb controls being disabled at the root path is expected and is not part of this report.

### App version / commit

master @ b747b32

### iOS version and device

iOS 26.5, iPhone 17 Simulator (deterministic reproduction); also reported on a physical iPhone

### hermes-webui server version

pinned hermes-webui @ ecc47782

### How the phone reaches the server

localhost (simulator only)

### Screenshots or screen recordings

A device screenshot was provided with the report. Automated regression coverage and a signed Simulator verification will be attached to the fixing PR.

title: Deep link from push notification opens the wrong session on cold start
body:
## Context

Tapping an ntfy push notification's deep link (`hermes-agent://session?id=<session_id>`)
should open Hermex directly on that session. Notification recipients rely on this to
jump straight into the relevant conversation.

## Current behavior

On a cold start (app not already running), tapping the notification opens Hermex but
navigates to the *last selected session* instead of the deep-linked one.

Root cause: in `SessionListView.swift`, `.onAppear` fires
`openPendingDeepLinkedSessionIfNeeded()` in an unstructured `Task { }` that awaits a
network round-trip (`loadSessionForDeepLink()`), while `.task { await
refreshSessionsAndActiveProfile(); restoreLastSelectedSessionIfNeeded() }` runs
independently. If the deep-link's network call hasn't completed before the refresh
finishes, `SessionNavigationState.restoreIfNeeded()` sees `destination == nil` and
restores the last session from `UserDefaults`. The deep-link `Task`'s `selectSession()`
may still fire afterward, but the user has already seen — and possibly already
interacted with — the wrong session.

## Expected behavior

A cold-start deep link always wins: the app opens directly on the deep-linked session,
with no visible flash of the previous session first.

## Acceptance criteria

- Cold-starting the app via `hermes-agent://session?id=<id>` opens directly on that
  session, never the last-selected one, regardless of network latency for the
  session load.
- Warm/backgrounded deep links (delivered while the app is already running) continue
  to work.
- `restoreLastSelectedSessionIfNeeded()` still restores the last session normally when
  there is no pending deep link.
- Automated regression coverage for the ordering/race in `SessionNavigationState`.
- The full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

1. Build and launch a signed Debug build on a physical device or the configured
   simulator.
2. Open a session, background/kill the app.
3. Trigger `hermes-agent://session?id=<a-different-session-id>` (e.g. via
   `xcrun simctl openurl` or a real ntfy notification) on cold start.
4. Confirm the app opens directly on the deep-linked session with no flash of the
   previous one.
5. Repeat with the app warm/backgrounded (not killed).
6. Run the full XCTest suite.

## Non-goals

- Changes to `HermesDeepLink.swift` URL parsing (already correct).
- General session-list navigation refactoring beyond this ordering fix.

title: fix: deep-linked session loses race to last-session restore
body:
Fixes #192

## Summary

- Resolve a pending deep-link session inside the cold-start `.task`, awaited
  ahead of `restoreLastSelectedSessionIfNeeded()`, instead of firing it from
  `.onAppear` as an unstructured `Task { }`. The deep link's network round-trip
  no longer races the stored-session restore.
- `SessionNavigationState.restoreIfNeeded()` now also skips (keeping the
  stored ID for a later restore) while a pending deep-link session ID exists,
  closing the secondary window where a link arrives mid-refresh via
  `onChange(of: pendingDeepLinkedSessionID)`.
- Added `SessionNavigationStateTests` coverage for the new pending-deep-link
  guard, including the blank/whitespace-ID edge case.

## Test plan

- [x] Full `HermesMobileTests` suite on iPhone 17 simulator — 1475 passed, 0 failed.
- [x] Signed Debug build installed on a physical iPhone; cold-started via a
      real ntfy push notification deep link (`hermes-agent://session?id=...`)
      while a different session was last-selected — opens directly on the
      deep-linked session with no flash of the previous one.

title: Move Kanban Dispatcher into an expandable toolbar sheet
body:
## Context

Move the completed Kanban Dispatcher capability from a permanently expanded Board section into a compact, discoverable toolbar presentation before Kanban activation in #158.

This is a UI-structure refinement only. Preview and Run semantics, Board-wide locking, confirmation, recovery, and persisted result state remain authoritative from #157.

## Current behavior

The Dispatcher heading, Preview and Run buttons, explanatory copy, and any result summary are permanently displayed between Search and the Status selector. This consumes substantial vertical space even when Dispatcher is not being used.

The toolbar's two-person icon toggles Group by Profile. Its purpose is difficult to infer, particularly when the selected Status has only one Profile group and the toggle produces little visible change.

## Expected behavior

Remove the permanently expanded Dispatcher block from the Board screen.

Replace the Group by Profile toolbar button with a clearly labeled Dispatcher button using the existing Dispatcher visual vocabulary. Tapping it opens a Dispatcher sheet:

- It opens at medium height and can expand to full height.
- Its content scrolls when results, errors, or larger Dynamic Type sizes require more room.
- Preview Dispatch, Run Dispatcher, confirmation, unavailable reasons, stale Preview handling, ambiguous-outcome recovery, and result dismissal remain available.
- Run retains the warning that it may start up to eight workers and consume API budget.

A completed Preview or Run summary remains available after the sheet is dismissed. While an undismissed summary exists, the toolbar button uses a subtle non-color-only active indicator, such as a filled symbol or badge, and its accessibility label communicates that a result is available. Tapping the button reopens the persisted summary. The indicator clears only when the user explicitly dismisses the result.

Move Group by Profile into a distinct Display section in the existing Filters sheet. It remains local presentation state and must not write the server-global Kanban grouping configuration or cause an unnecessary Board request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Board screen no longer contains a permanently expanded Dispatcher section.
- [ ] A Dispatcher toolbar button replaces the Group by Profile toolbar button.
- [ ] The Dispatcher button has an explicit accessibility label and does not rely on its symbol or color alone to communicate purpose or state.
- [ ] Tapping Dispatcher presents a medium-height sheet that can expand to full height.
- [ ] The sheet remains scrollable and usable for long results, error recovery, and accessibility Dynamic Type sizes.
- [ ] Existing Preview, Run, confirmation, unavailable, stale, in-flight, refused, uncertain-outcome, refresh, acknowledgement, and dismissal states remain available.
- [ ] Dismissing the sheet does not discard an undismissed Dispatcher summary.
- [ ] An undismissed summary produces a non-color-only toolbar indicator and an equivalent accessibility state.
- [ ] Reopening the sheet shows the persisted summary.
- [ ] Explicitly dismissing the summary clears the toolbar indicator.
- [ ] Group by Profile appears in a distinct Display section of Filters.
- [ ] Group by Profile retains its current local grouping behavior without mutating server configuration or making an unnecessary network request.
- [ ] Offline, read-only, incompatible-server, failed-refresh, single-flight, and Board-wide mutation locking continue to disable Dispatcher actions correctly.
- [ ] VoiceOver reading order, focus after sheet dismissal, keyboard operation where applicable, RTL, light/dark appearance, and Reduce Motion remain correct.
- [ ] All changed user-facing copy is localized in every shipped language.

## Validation plan

### Automated

- Cover Group by Profile after relocation into Filters.
- Prove that grouping does not write Kanban configuration or trigger an unnecessary Board request.
- Cover Dispatcher result persistence across sheet dismissal and reopening.
- Cover explicit result dismissal clearing the toolbar state.
- Preserve Dispatcher availability, confirmation, locking, stale-result, and ambiguous-outcome behavior through the new presentation.
- Verify changed accessibility labels and state descriptions.
- Run focused Kanban tests, the full XCTest suite, localization-catalog validation, and `git diff --check`.

### Signed simulator

Use Debug Kanban Lab fixtures only. Do not contact a real Dispatcher server, start billable workers, or mutate the maintainer's real Boards.

- Verify medium and large sheet presentations.
- Verify Preview and Run fixture flows, confirmation, persisted result indication, reopening, and explicit dismissal.
- Verify Group by Profile from Filters.
- Check standard and accessibility Dynamic Type, light/dark appearance, RTL, VoiceOver, focus restoration, and Reduce Motion.

## Non-goals

- Changing Dispatcher endpoint, request, response, maximum worker count, retry, locking, or recovery semantics.
- Adding new Dispatcher or filtering capabilities.
- Writing the server-global Kanban grouping configuration.
- Refining Card row layout or metadata spacing; tracked in #184.
- Redesigning Manage Boards rows; tracked in #196.
- Activating Kanban or completing release evidence in #158.

Dispatcher capability issue #157 is complete. This refinement is not blocked and blocks #158.

- [ ] The currently browsed Board remains clearly identified.
- [ ] Each Board row has one trailing overflow menu instead of an inline strip of text actions.
- [ ] Tapping the overflow menu does not trigger Board browsing.
- [ ] The menu presents applicable Edit, Make Active Board, and Archive actions with text labels and meaningful icons.
- [ ] Make Active Board is omitted for the shared active Board.
- [ ] Archive is omitted when the Board cannot be archived, including the protected default Board.
- [ ] Edit and other mutations remain unavailable while Board management is disabled or a conflicting Board mutation is active.
- [ ] Archive retains its destructive role, warning, confirmation, and recovery behavior.

- [ ] Browsing and Active remain distinguishable without relying on color alone.

- [ ] Row browsing and every menu action retain practical 44-point targets, meaningful VoiceOver labels and hints, and keyboard operation where applicable.
- [ ] RTL, light/dark appearance, and Reduce Motion remain correct.

### Automated

title: Refine Kanban card row affordances
body:
## Summary

- make the Card content region the primary detail-navigation target while keeping the 44pt ellipsis menu independent

- align the nontruncating age indicator at the trailing edge and make metadata spacing / `ViewThatFits` fallback deliberate across mixed widths

title: Make the iPad app available on macOS and visionOS
body:
### Use case

Hermex now has an iPad app, and it would be helpful if that version could also be installed on supported Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision Pro as an iPad-compatible app.

This is not necessarily a request for a native macOS or visionOS interface. The existing iPad app may already provide a useful experience on these platforms if its App Store availability and compatibility settings allow installation.

Related: #85

## Current behavior

### macOS

Hermex does not appear in the Mac App Store when searching under iPhone and iPad apps, so there does not seem to be an option to install the iPad version on a Mac.

### visionOS

Hermex appears in the App Store on Apple Vision Pro, but it cannot be downloaded.

This was tested on the latest visionOS 27 beta, so the download problem may be caused by beta OS compatibility rather than the app itself. It may still be worth checking the app's platform availability and compatibility configuration in App Store Connect.

### Proposed behavior

If the iPad app is technically compatible, allow users to:

- Install and run it on Apple silicon Macs using the existing “Designed for iPad” compatibility option.
- Install and run it on Apple Vision Pro as a compatible iPad app.

## Suggested investigation

- Check whether Mac availability for the iPad app is disabled in App Store Connect.
- Check whether Apple Vision Pro availability is enabled.
- Confirm that the deployment target, required device capabilities, entitlements, or other configuration do not unintentionally prevent installation.
- Test visionOS installation on a stable release as well as visionOS 27 beta, if possible.

## Non-goals

- A dedicated native macOS app.
- A dedicated spatial interface for visionOS.
- Mac Catalyst support.

Those could be considered separately. This request is only about allowing the existing iPad app to run on other compatible Apple platforms where practical.

### Acceptance outcomes

- Hermex is discoverable and installable from the Mac App Store on supported Apple silicon Macs as a “Designed for iPad” app, if technically compatible.
- Hermex can be downloaded and launched on supported Apple Vision Pro devices as an iPad-compatible app, if technically compatible.
- If either platform cannot be supported, the limiting App Store, entitlement, capability, or OS compatibility requirement is identified and documented.
- visionOS behavior is checked on a stable release to distinguish an app configuration issue from a visionOS 27 beta issue.

### Upstream dependency notes

No known hermes-webui server changes are required. This appears to concern App Store Connect availability and Apple platform compatibility for the existing iPad app.

title: Fix CJK IME composition clobbered by SwiftUI re-render
body:
## Summary
- `ComposerTextView.updateUIView` unconditionally sets `textView.text = text` whenever the bound `text` differs from `textView.text`. SwiftUI calls `updateUIView` on any parent re-render (e.g. a streaming assistant response updating other state), not just when the user's own typing changed `text`.
- If this fires while the user is mid-composition (Korean/Chinese/Japanese IME marked text), it forces UIKit to commit the in-progress syllable early, splitting it into separate jamo/characters. Observed on iOS as: typing "자모음" renders as "ㅈㅏ모음" — only the character being composed at the moment of the re-render is affected, which matches the first character being the most common collision point (composition starts right as focus/streaming kicks off a re-render).
- Fix: skip the assignment while `textView.markedTextRange != nil` (an active IME composition), so an external re-render never clobbers in-flight marked text.

## Test plan
- [ ] Type Korean (or other CJK) text into the chat composer while a streaming response or other composer state change is happening in the background, confirm the composed syllable is no longer split
- [ ] Confirm normal external updates to `text` (e.g. clearing composer after send, programmatic edits) still apply correctly outside of active composition

Fixes #312
