title: Webui /api/tts defaults to Edge TTS when client omits engine, ignoring server tts_engine setting
body:
## Problem

Hermex sends `POST /api/tts` with **no `engine` field** in the request body — only `text` and `voice` — per the design in `APIClient+TTS.swift`:

> _"Only text and voice are sent: the server defaults engine to edge"_

The webui handler then defaults to Edge TTS instead of respecting the server's configured `tts_engine` from settings.json. This means Kokoro TTS doesn't work with Hermex even when properly configured on the server.

## Expected behavior

When the server has `tts_engine: "openai"` (pointing to a local Kokoro instance) in settings.json and the client omits the engine field, the server should use its configured default engine.

## Actual behavior

The webui handler in `api/routes.py` defaults to `engine = "edge"` when the client omits the engine field, ignoring `tts_engine` from settings.json.

## Workaround

Patch `api/routes.py` in hermes-webui to fall back to the server's `tts_engine` when the client doesn't specify an engine.

## Repro

1. Configure server with `tts_engine: "openai"` and `tts.openai.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8880/v1` (Kokoro)
2. Connect via Hermex
3. Enable TTS in Hermex
4. Send a message
5. Observe that `/api/tts` request body has no `engine` field
6. Server uses Edge TTS instead of Kokoro

## Source

Hermex TTS request struct (`APIClient+TTS.swift`):
```swift
struct TTSSynthesisRequest: Encodable {
    let text: String
    let voice: String
}
```

## Affected components
- hermes-webui `/api/tts` endpoint — should fall back to server config when client omits engine

title: Session list stays stale when the app returns to foreground
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Hermex and let the session list load.
2. Leave the list mounted and background the app.
3. Create a new session through hermes-webui or another client backed by the same Hermes session store.
4. Return to Hermex without force-quitting it or navigating away from the list.
5. Observe that the new session is not listed until a manual pull-to-refresh or another event recreates/refreshes the list.

This does not reproduce in the hermes-webui web UI against the same server. The server's `GET /api/sessions` response includes the new session.

## Expected behavior

When Hermex returns to the foreground, it should request the current session list so sessions created or updated by another client become visible.

## Actual behavior

A warm foreground transition can keep showing the locally cached list without issuing `GET /api/sessions`. That makes cross-client visibility appear intermittent: cold launch, pull-to-refresh, and some navigation paths work, while simply returning to the app can remain stale.

The current `SessionListView` refreshes from its initial `.task`, `.onAppear`, and `.refreshable` hooks, but it does not observe `scenePhase`. `ContentView` observes foreground transitions only for shared-import and live-activity work, not session-list refresh.

Observed server-side request logs support this distinction: every session-list request that reached the server returned HTTP 200 quickly, but returning to the already-mounted list did not consistently generate a session-list request.

## App version / commit

App Store 1.4 (build 3). Also confirmed on current `master` at `9bc7ab075b9caeb53c4aae82c4509e77191dd871` by source inspection.

## iOS version and device

iOS 26.5 on iPhone 16 Pro Max.

## hermes-webui server version

A v0.52.28-derived deployment. The failure is app-lifecycle-specific; the web UI and authenticated sessions endpoint show the current data.

## How the phone reaches the server

Tailscale with an HTTPS reverse proxy.

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Not included; the observable difference is whether a foreground transition generates a fresh session-list request.

title: Clear recovered connection warnings and remove Mac-specific timeout guidance

## Context

## Current behavior

## Expected behavior

Recovery-related warnings disappear once the active connection is demonstrably healthy, and troubleshooting text works for any server host.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A transient recovery error remains visible while recovery is unresolved.
- [ ] Subsequent valid stream progress, successful status confirmation, or successful reconnection clears the stale warning without requiring another send.
- [ ] Genuine unrecovered errors remain visible.

title: Keep link long-press from opening the whole-message action menu, and make the menu lift smoothly on long replies
body:
## Context

Long-pressing a link inside an assistant message currently activates both the link interaction and the context menu attached to the entire message bubble.

Both defects in this issue come from the same attachment point: `ChatTranscriptView.swift` puts `.contextMenu` on the whole `MessageBubbleView` (`ChatTranscriptMessageRow`) with no custom preview. For slice 2, UIKit must snapshot the entire bubble as the lifted preview before the menu can appear. On a long assistant reply that snapshot is expensive and far taller than the screen, so the menu is drawn over the undimmed transcript for a frame or more before the system settles, and the long-press feels laggy.

## Current behavior

- Slice 1: the link preview appears while the underlying message menu also opens, showing actions such as Listen, Select Text, Regenerate, Fork, and Copy.
- Slice 2: on a long assistant reply, long-press shows the action menu (Listen, Select Text, Regenerate Response, Fork From Here, Copy) overlapping the transcript text with no dim and no lifted preview for roughly a second, then it pops into its final position. The delay grows with response length. Short replies are fine.

## Expected behavior

- Slice 1: long-pressing a link should show only the system link interaction. Long-pressing non-link content should continue showing message actions.
- Slice 2: long-pressing any assistant or user message lifts a preview clipped to the bubble's on-screen portion, dims the transcript, and presents the menu in one continuous system animation, regardless of response length. Reduce Motion follows the system behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

Slice 1 (links)
- [ ] Tapping links still opens them normally.
- [ ] Long-pressing a plain URL or Markdown link does not open the message-level action menu.
- [ ] Long-pressing non-link content still exposes all appropriate message actions.
- [ ] User and assistant messages without links retain current behavior.
- [ ] Text selection and accessibility actions continue working.

Slice 2 (long replies)
- [ ] Long-pressing a multi-screen assistant reply shows the dimmed background and lifted preview together with the menu; the menu never renders over the undimmed transcript.
- [ ] The lifted preview is clipped to the bubble's visible on-screen portion and never exceeds the screen.
- [ ] Time from haptic to menu on a ~5,000-word reply is indistinguishable from a one-line reply on device.
- [ ] Short replies, user bubbles, and the meta-row copy button look and behave as today.
- [ ] No per-frame re-rendering of Markdown while the menu is open.

## Validation plan

- Add focused tests where practical.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Manually test plain URLs, Markdown links, and mixed text/link messages on a signed simulator.
- Manual, signed Debug build on iPhone 17 simulator and on device: long-press a one-line reply, a reply with code blocks, and a reply longer than three screens; confirm one continuous lift animation with the transcript dimmed. Repeat with Reduce Motion on.
- Screen recording of before and after on the long reply for the PR.

## Implementation notes

- Preferred: wrap the bubble in a `UIContextMenuInteraction` via `UIViewRepresentable`. `previewForHighlightingMenuWithConfiguration` returns a `UITargetedPreview` clipped to the visible rect. The same interaction's `contextMenuInteraction(_:configurationForMenuAtLocation:)` hit-tests the touch location and returns nil when it lands on a link, which is slice 1.
- Cheaper fallback for slice 2 alone: `.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:)` with a compact preview view, accepting that the preview will differ from the bubble.
- Menu contents stay in `ChatMessageActionMenu` (`ChatMessageActions.swift`).

## Non-goals

- Redesigning link previews or changing the available message actions or their order.
- Transcript scroll performance (#32).

title: Chat composer stays active on read-only sessions (Telegram/CLI-origin) — misleading 'session no longer exists' error
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `nesquena/hermes-webui` (current master) against a `hermes-agent` gateway with the Telegram platform connected.
2. Open Hermex, connect to the WebUI server (Tailscale).
3. The Telegram session appears in the session list; its title and history load correctly.
4. Tap into that session, type a message, and send.
5. The send fails with: "That session no longer exists on the server. Reopen another session or create a new one."

### Expected behavior

Read-only sessions (Telegram/CLI/gateway origin) should be surfaced as such in the app:

1. A clear indicator on the session row and/or chat header (e.g. lock icon, "Read-only" badge, or a source label like "Telegram").
2. The composer disabled or hidden for those sessions — or a one-time explanation — instead of allowing a send that always fails.
3. The error message should not claim the session was deleted when it wasn't.

### Actual behavior

Hermex renders non-WebUI sessions as fully interactive: the composer is active, messages send (and fail), and every failure is reported as "That session no longer exists on the server." The session does exist — the server just cannot run chat in it, and the server returns a generic 404 so the client can't tell the difference.

### App version / commit

Latest App Store build. (This is the same behavior described in #172/#176, which were filed against App Store v1.4.)

### iOS version and device

iPhone 17, latest iOS (26.x).

### hermes-webui server version

`nesquena/hermes-webui` master, commit `c275db09` (v0.51.365), paired with NousResearch `hermes-agent` gateway 0.19.0.

### How the phone reaches the server

Tailscale

### App bug vs server bug (per CONTRIBUTING)

Reproduced against the same server in the hermes-webui **web UI**: the web UI handles this correctly — CLI/messaging sessions are flagged read-only (`S.session.read_only`), shown with a "read-only" badge (static/panels.js, static/sessions.js), and commands on them are blocked with a toast (static/commands.js). The API contract is unchanged: `GET /api/session` returns 200 with history, `POST /api/chat/start` returns 404 `{"error": "Session not found"}` for non-WebUI-origin sessions (webui routes.py ~line 6139 documents this as intentional).

**Only breaks in the app** → filing here as an app bug: Hermex does not replicate the read-only handling the web UI already has.

### Notes

The server returns the same 404 for "deleted session" and "exists but read-only," so Hermex needs either a client-side read-only detection (the web UI already exposes `read_only` / `is_cli_session` flags on session objects) or a server-side distinction. Related: #172, #176, #177.

title: Add chat preferences to dismiss the keyboard after send and show completed responses from the top
body:
## Use case

When using Hermex on an iPhone, the on-screen keyboard remains open after a message is successfully sent. This is useful for rapid back-and-forth chat, but it leaves substantially less room for reading a long agent response.

Hermex also follows the bottom of a response while it is streaming. When a long response finishes, the viewport remains at the end, so the user has to scroll back to find the beginning before reading it.

Both behaviors are reasonable defaults, but reading-oriented workflows would benefit from configurable alternatives.

## Proposed behavior

Add local chat preferences, for example under **Settings → Chat**:

1. **Dismiss keyboard after sending**
   - When enabled, dismiss the keyboard and remove composer focus after a message has been submitted successfully.
   - Keep the composer focused if submission fails, so the draft can be corrected and retried.

2. **Position after response completes**
   - **Keep at latest content** (current behavior and default)
   - **Show beginning of completed response**
   - When the second option is selected, scroll the newly completed assistant message to the top of the viewport after streaming finishes.
   - Do not override the reader if they manually scrolled during the response.

These should be app-local presentation preferences and should not change server, session, profile, or transcript state.

## Acceptance outcomes

- [ ] With “Dismiss keyboard after sending” enabled, a successful send hides the keyboard.
- [ ] A failed send does not unnecessarily dismiss the keyboard or discard the draft.
- [ ] With the setting disabled, current focus behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] With “Show beginning of completed response” enabled, the completed assistant message is positioned at the top after a long streamed response finishes.
- [ ] Streaming can continue following the latest content while the response is being generated.
- [ ] A manual user scroll takes ownership and prevents an automatic completion jump.
- [ ] With “Keep at latest content” selected, current scrolling behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Preferences persist locally across launches.
- [ ] Behavior works for standard sends and messages submitted while another response is streaming.
- [ ] VoiceOver focus, Reduce Motion, clarification/approval surfaces, and the scroll-to-bottom control remain usable.

## Upstream dependency notes

No hermes-webui server change should be required. These appear to be native client presentation behaviors.

Implementation context in the current client:

- `sendDraftMessage()` restores composer focus after a successful submission: [ChatView.swift](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/7d38a3b6a8f0c367684be30482d7dbbe47478023/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1422-L1458)
- The transcript follows the bottom during streaming: [ChatTranscriptView.swift](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/7d38a3b6a8f0c367684be30482d7dbbe47478023/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L123-L180)
- `handleActiveStreamChange()` already observes response completion and may be a suitable integration point: [ChatView.swift](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/7d38a3b6a8f0c367684be30482d7dbbe47478023/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1866-L1887)

title: Refresh the sessions list when returning from a contentful new chat
body:
## Context

A new chat initially exists as an empty “Untitled” session. Issue #83 / PR #84 intentionally hid that placeholder so it would not flash in the sessions list when the user returned without sending anything.

A contentful new session must still become visible once messages have been exchanged.

## Current behavior

1. Create a new chat.
2. Send a few messages and receive responses.
3. Navigate back to the main sessions list.
4. The new session is missing.
5. Pull to refresh.
6. The session then appears.

The sessions list is retaining stale in-memory data when returning from the new-chat flow.

## Expected behavior

Returning from a new chat that now contains messages should automatically update the sessions list. The new session should appear without requiring pull-to-refresh.

Returning from a new chat without sending anything must continue to leave the empty “Untitled” placeholder hidden, including during the navigation transition.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After creating a chat and exchanging messages, navigating back shows that session in the main sessions list without manual refresh.
- [ ] The new session appears in the appropriate list position using current server metadata.
- [ ] The behavior works after the first completed exchange and after several exchanges.
- [ ] Creating a new chat and returning without sending anything does not show an empty “Untitled” session, even briefly.
- [ ] Existing contentful sessions with an untitled or placeholder-style title remain visible.
- [ ] Automated regression coverage exercises both branches:
  - a contentful new session becomes visible upon return;
  - an empty new-session placeholder remains suppressed.
- [ ] The full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

- Add focused coverage for synchronizing the session list when leaving the new-chat destination.
- Retain or extend the placeholder-filtering tests introduced by #83/#84.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Manually validate in a signed iPhone simulator:
  1. Create a new chat, exchange messages, and navigate back.
  2. Confirm the session appears immediately without pulling to refresh.
  3. Create another new chat and navigate back without sending anything.
  4. Confirm no empty “Untitled” row appears, including transiently.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning the sessions list.
- Changing server API behavior or session creation semantics.
- Displaying empty new-chat placeholders.
- Adding continuous background polling solely to update the list.

title: Refresh sessions after returning from new chat

title: fix(chat): make stream liveness recovery transport-aware
body:
## Summary
- Track transport activity separately from semantic response progress.
- Treat SSE comment heartbeats as active transport, preventing false stale-stream recovery.
- Detect a silent initial connection after the reconnect timeout, while keeping recovery state hidden during the normal initial wait.
- Add regression coverage for heartbeat-only, missing-transport-activity, and silent-initial-stream paths.

## Root cause
Stale recovery measured only semantic progress: a healthy heartbeat-only stream could reconnect unnecessarily, while a connection with no initial event never became stale. Marking semantic progress at connection start fixes the latter but shows recovery state too early. The coordinator now distinguishes transport liveness from visible response progress.

Fixes #186

## Validation
- `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -parallel-testing-enabled NO` — 1,548 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Normally signed Debug app installed and launched on iPhone 17, iOS 26.5.
- `git diff --check origin/master..HEAD`

## Need to verify
- Live-server heartbeat-only stream and a temporarily silent initial stream on the target deployment.
- A deployment that emits no SSE comments at all — an older server, or a proxy that strips them. Nothing then refreshes transport activity before the first event, so the new silent-initial branch force-reconnects once every `reconnectInterval` (18s, or 25s while a live tool call is running) until the first event arrives. Recovery re-checks `chatStreamStatus` and reconnects with replay, so the user turn is never resent, but the forced reconnect currently has no backoff or cap. Whether the target deployment actually sends comment heartbeats is unverified here: the read-only upstream checkout emits them, but it is neither the compatibility pin nor the live server.

## AI assistance
Prepared with Codex; changes and validation were reviewed before updating this draft.

title: perf(chat): reduce long transcript load cost
body:
> **Draft — not ready for review.** This branch bundles three separable changes and the
> scroll behavior has no device evidence yet. See "Open questions" below.

## Summary
- Render transcript rows lazily (`VStack` → `LazyVStack`) and drop the `.sizeChanges` scroll anchor.
- Load 20 messages per initial and older page instead of 50.
- Reuse one session-scoped cached-message fetch during cache upserts instead of issuing one lookup per message.
- Keep regression assertions aligned with the new page limit and cache window.

## Root cause
Large transcripts paid for eager row construction and one SwiftData lookup per cached message on every upsert.

## Open questions
- **The `.sizeChanges` anchor removal is a partial revert of #137, and the original behavior does not
  justify it.** `ChatScrollPolicy.sizeChangeAnchor` already returned `.bottom` only while
  `shouldFollowLatestMessage` was true and `nil` once the reader scrolled away, so it could not pull a
  reader back to the bottom. Removing it gives up the bottom pin for late Markdown measurement while
  still following the latest message — and `LazyVStack` makes late size changes *more* frequent, since
  rows realize progressively during scrolling. The covering test
  (`testTranscriptSizeChangesStayBottomAnchoredOnlyWhileFollowingLatest`) was deleted with it, so
  nothing guards the #137 jitter regression.
- **The lazy-render work overlaps [#33](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/33)**, which is
  the author's own approach to issue #32. This PR does not claim to supersede it; the maintainer
  should decide the direction before either lands. No `Fixes #32` here on purpose — it would close
  the issue out from under #33.
- **`messagePageLimit` 50 → 20 is a user-visible tradeoff, not a cache optimization.** Reopening a
  session shows 30 fewer messages and needs one more "load older" tap. With `LazyVStack` in place the
  page-limit reduction may no longer be needed at all.

## Validation
- `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -parallel-testing-enabled NO` — 1,543 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Normally signed Debug app installed and launched on iPhone 17, iOS 26.5.
- `git diff --check origin/master..HEAD`
- The `CacheStore` batching is behavior-preserving: `CachedMessage.cacheKey` already embeds
  `serverURLString` and `sessionID`, so the session-scoped fetch resolves the same rows the previous
  per-message lookup did.

## Need to verify
- **No device evidence for the scroll changes yet.** Required manual path on a long persisted
  transcript: open the session, let Markdown finish measuring while a response streams, scroll
  upward, then load older messages — confirm no #137-style opening jitter and no unwanted jump.
- `LazyVStack` + `ScrollViewReader.scrollTo` on rows that have not been realized yet (initial
  scroll-to-bottom and position retention after loading older messages).

## AI assistance
Prepared with Codex; changes and validation were reviewed before updating this draft.

title: Suppress "Checking stream" indicator and status polls while transport heartbeats are fresh
body:
## Context

Follow-up to #186 / PR #216 (merged as `73683cc`). That fix made stale-stream recovery transport-aware: SSE comment heartbeats now count as liveness, so healthy-but-quiet streams are no longer force-reconnected every 18s. One cosmetic leftover remains.

## Current behavior

In `ChatStreamCoordinator.recoverStaleStreamIfNeeded`, once semantic progress is ≥ 5s old (`timing.checkingInterval`), the coordinator sets `recoveryState = .checking` and polls `/api/chat/stream/status` every ~4s (`timing.statusPollCooldown`) — **even when `lastTransportActivityDate` is fresh** because heartbeats are arriving every ~5s (cadence verified against the live deployment on 2026-08-04). A `.heartbeat` event also never demotes `.checking` back to `.idle`; the chip stays until the next semantic event calls `markProgress()`.

So during a long model-thinking pause or slow tool call, the user still sees "Checking stream" for the whole quiet window, and the server gets a status poll every ~4s, despite the connection being provably alive.

## Expected behavior

While transport activity is fresh (e.g. `now - lastTransportActivityDate` below a transport-fresh threshold — something like 10–12s, comfortably above the server's ~5s heartbeat cadence and below `reconnectInterval` 18s):

- keep `recoveryState = .idle` (no "Checking stream" chip), and
- skip or back off the ~4s status polls.

Only enter `.checking` (and start polling) once transport itself has been quiet past that threshold. The existing escalation must be unchanged: a genuinely silent transport still reaches `.checking` and then force-reconnects at 18s/25s.

## Care points

- **Trade-off to weigh:** the status poll path doubles as a safety net that finalizes runs when a `done` event is missed. Backing polls off while heartbeats are fresh narrows that net. Risk looks low — a live connection delivers `done` itself — but the implementer should confirm the finalize-on-inactive paths (see PR #266 history) don't depend on polling during heartbeat-fresh windows.
- Decide whether a fresh `.heartbeat` should also demote an already-set `.checking` back to `.idle` (probably yes, for consistency).
- Don't regress the three regression tests added in PR #216 (`testHeartbeatKeepsSemanticallyQuietStreamOnOriginalConnection`, `testMissingTransportActivityReconnectsStaleActiveStream`, `testSilentInitialConnectionReconnectsWhenStale`) — the first one currently asserts `.checking` + one status request and will need updating to the new expected behavior; that's intentional, not a regression.
- New tests: heartbeat-fresh quiet stream stays `.idle` with zero status polls; transport-quiet stream still escalates to `.checking` → reconnect.

## Out of scope

Reconnect/backoff behavior for no-heartbeat deployments — pre-existing, disclosed in PR #216, and moot on the target server.

title: Voice Conversation Mode — wayfinder map
body:
## Destination

Every design decision for the v1 turn-based voice conversation mode (parent: #36) is resolved, and the final ticket publishes detailed, sliced \`ready-for-agent\` implementation issues under #36. Implementation itself happens outside this map via the normal issue→PR workflow.

## Notes

**Domain constraints (live-verified 2026-08-04):**
- Server voice surface is batch-only: \`POST /api/transcribe\` (multipart → transcript; provider \`local\` whisper, ~2.8 s for a 4 s clip) and \`POST /api/tts\` (JSON → fully-buffered audio; 1.5 s/sentence, ~4.3 s/768 chars; **rate-limited 1 req/2 s per client**; 5000-char cap). No WebSocket/realtime/streaming-audio API; chat replies stream as SSE text tokens only.
- Consequence: incremental (sentence-by-sentence) speech must be on-device \`AVSpeechSynthesizer\`; server TTS only fits whole-reply synthesis.
- App building blocks that exist: live on-device STT partials (\`ComposerVoiceInputController\`), Listen TTS stack with on-device fallback (\`ChatViewModel\`), SSE token tap points (\`appendAssistantToken\`), mic/speech permissions + \`UIBackgroundModes: audio\`. Capture and playback currently mutually exclude via \`ComposerAudioCaptureState\` — a duplex mode replaces that.
- webui precedent: turn-based voice mode (#1333 upstream, \`static/boot.js\`) — listen → auto-send on ~1.8 s silence → wait for full reply → TTS → listen; pref-gated.
- App shell is \`NavigationSplitView\` (session list → chat), no tab bar — #36's "tab" language needs translating into a surface decision.

**Skills sessions should consult:** \`swiftui-patterns\`, \`swiftui-animation\`, \`prototype\` (surface ticket), \`research\`, \`hermes-issue-intake\` (final slicing ticket).

**Standing preferences:** owner wants detailed sliced issues before any code; recommend + explain trade-offs (beginner-friendly); barge-in is IN scope for v1 planning.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: gist + link -->

- [Probe: which server TTS engines and voices are actually usable?](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/235) — edge only (elevenlabs/openai keys unset, 503); hard-coded 15-voice allowlist (en-US Aria/Guy, zh-CN, fr, id only — no coverage for most app locales); ~1.5–4.3 s buffered synth.
- [Research: does .voiceChat AEC keep SFSpeechRecognizer from hearing our own TTS?](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/234) — only if we enable engine voice processing (`setVoiceProcessingEnabled`, not `.voiceChat` alone) AND play TTS through that engine via `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write` — outside-engine audio is only documented as ducked, not cancelled; SFSpeech tasks still need ~1-min restarts.
- [Voice mode surface: where does it live and how is it entered?](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/229) — full-screen overlay (ChatGPT-style) over the current chat; entered via a waveform button in the composer (so it inherits the current session — no session picker); exited via an explicit X button. Prototype on branch `prototype/229-voice-surface`.
- [Unified duplex audio session design](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/232) — new exclusive-lease `VoiceModeAudioController` (existing owners untouched): `.playAndRecord`/`.voiceChat`/`.defaultToSpeaker` + engine `setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)`; activate once/hold until exit; stops Listen + inline players on entry and holds the capture flag; ALL voice-mode playback through the engine (binds #231); audio-I/O-only API; interruption observers with end-session fail-safe (resume UX → [Voice session interruption & resume UX](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/241)).
- [Speaking strategy: incremental on-device default + server quality voice](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/231) — quality voice IN (fleet has ElevenLabs/OpenAI keys): Voice = On-device | server engine (voice picker edge-only, 15-voice list); default seeded from server `tts_engine`/`tts_voice`, local per-server override; NLTokenizer sentence chunking w/ ~20-char runt merge (tunable constants); `SpeechTextNormalizer` extended (fenced code → one-line summary), same text to both paths; new voice-mode rate setting via `AVAudioUnitTimePitch`; single thinking phase, on-device fallback on 503/429/timeout/>5000 chars.

- [Turn-loop behavior: silence window, auto-send, visibility, errors](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/230) — hands-free auto-send after 2.0 s of transcript-stable silence (fixed tunable constant, no v1 setting); never-send-empty + recognizer-restart carryover; live transcript + streaming reply exposed (layout → #240); transient STT errors self-heal, fatal ones exit w/ alert, net-drop keeps partial reply & returns to listening (no auto-resend); mute toggle + ~2 min idle auto-pause, X exits.

- [Voice overlay content: what does the user see while listening, thinking, and speaking?](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/240) — A3 “caption stage”: one thing at a time (big live caption / sequential tool cards + elapsed timer / streaming reply teleprompter), history behind a sheet, orb color = phase; dual barge-in (auto-on-speech primary, tap-orb fallback — mechanics stay with #233); reply text shown, not audio-only.
- [Barge-in design: interrupting the assistant mid-speech](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/233) — recognizer-only detection (no VAD) riding the #232 AEC engine, armed during thinking AND speaking; debounce = min-chars + ~300 ms confirm (tunables); fires → immediate player stop + reuse `cancelActiveStream()`/abort `/api/tts` + interrupting words seed the next turn; partial reply kept verbatim (no marker); tap-to-stop same path w/ empty seed; half-duplex fallback (no speech barge-in) if voice processing unavailable.
- [Voice session interruption & resume UX: calls, backgrounding, Live Activity](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/241) — interruptions pause into #230's Paused state (hybrid resume: manual tap in foreground, auto on `.shouldResume` when backgrounded; resume speech from next unspoken sentence); Pocket Mode: full duplex continues in background (bypass ChatView's suspend path; paused+backgrounded lets iOS suspend, state freezes); route changes continue seamlessly (VoIP convention); stock per-turn Live Activity only, nothing between turns; #232 fail-safe kept for unrecoverable cases.

- [Settings and gating: opt-in, locales, defaults](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/236) — no opt-in gate (composer button hideable via toggle); new "Voice Mode" settings card; per-server values in namespaced UserDefaults; Conversation Language = device locale (no picker); STT ladder on-device → Apple network recognition (skipped under "On-device only") → unavailable alert, server batch STT ruled out; auto-picked on-device voice per locale; Edge locale mismatch = extra on-device fallback trigger; speaking rate global.

- [Write and publish the sliced ready-for-agent implementation issues](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/237) — route published: ten ready-for-agent sub-issues of #36 (#248–#257) with ordering + dependency table (https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/36#issuecomment-5230872341); map complete.

## Not yet specified

(nothing at the moment — every remaining question is a live ticket)

## Out of scope

- Upstream realtime/WebSocket duplex endpoint (true speech-to-speech) — requires hermes-webui server work; revisit as a fresh effort if the destination is ever redrawn.
- Redesigning the existing Listen (read-aloud) feature beyond what voice mode needs.
- Persistent session-long voice Live Activity with interactive End/Mute intents (lock-screen presence between turns) — consciously deferred past v1 while resolving [Voice session interruption & resume UX](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/241); the per-turn activity + system mic indicator suffice for v1.

title: Research: does .voiceChat AEC keep SFSpeechRecognizer from hearing our own TTS?
body:

## Question

title: Probe: which server TTS engines and voices are actually usable?
body:

title: feat(streaming): suppress "Checking stream" chip and status polls while transport heartbeats are fresh
body:
Fixes #227

## Summary

Follow-up to #186 / PR #216. Heartbeats already prevented forced reconnects, but the `.checking` recovery state and the ~4s `/api/chat/stream/status` polls were still driven purely by *semantic* silence (no tokens/tools for 5s). During long model-thinking pauses or slow tool calls the user saw a "Checking stream" chip and the server got a status poll every ~4s, despite SSE comment heartbeats (~5s server cadence, `_SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 5` upstream) proving the connection alive.

- New `ChatStreamCoordinatorTiming.transportFreshInterval` (standard **12s** — comfortably above the ~5s heartbeat cadence, below `reconnectInterval` 18s).
- In `recoverStaleStreamIfNeeded`, once semantically quiet past `checkingInterval`, the coordinator now stays `.idle` and skips status polls while `now − lastTransportActivityDate < transportFreshInterval`. The existing `.checking` → poll → 18s/25s force-reconnect escalation is unchanged once transport itself has been quiet ≥ 12s.
- A `.heartbeat` event demotes an already-shown `.checking` back to `.idle` immediately (never `.reconnecting`, which stays owned by the reconnect flow until real progress lands).

## Safety-net trade-off (issue care point)

Skipping polls while heartbeat-fresh narrows the missed-`done` net only in a double-fault scenario. Verified against the pinned upstream source:

- Normal completion enqueues `done` then `stream_end` — the latter inside a `finally:` when the background title worker runs — and the server drain loop closes the socket on `stream_end`/`error`/`cancel`.
- A worker exception enqueues `apperror`; the client maps `error`/`apperror` to the terminal `.error` path even when the payload is malformed, so the client finalizes without any poll.
- A dropped socket stops heartbeats: either `.transportError` fires (suspend/reconnect path, untouched) or transport goes quiet and polling resumes within ~12s.

The residual gap requires the worker to die *and* its terminal-event enqueue itself to fail while the separate handler thread keeps heartbeating the open socket — previously caught by the ~4s polls via `active=false`, now only by the untouched foreground `refreshTranscriptIfCompleted` net on the next background/foreground cycle.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` clean.
- Focused `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests` + `ChatViewModelSendTests`: 168 passed, 0 failed.
- Full XCTest suite: **1,561 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (iPhone 17 simulator).
- Test changes called out in the issue as intentional: `testHeartbeatKeepsSemanticallyQuietStreamOnOriginalConnection` now expects `.idle` + zero polls; the stale-detection test (renamed to `testStaleDetectionWaitsForTransportQuietThresholdThenPollsStatus`) documents the 5s→idle / 12s→checking timeline; single-clock tests moved from +5.1/+6/+10 to past the 12s threshold. New tests: heartbeat-fresh stays idle with zero polls, heartbeat demotes `.checking`, heartbeat never demotes `.reconnecting`.

## Owner manual checks

1. Start a long response on the live server (something with a long thinking pause or slow tool call): the "Checking stream" chip should no longer appear while the connection is healthy, and the transcript should still stream normally when output resumes.
2. Kill/restart the server (or drop the network) mid-stream: the chip and the reconnect/finalize behavior should appear as before.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Model picker only shows 15 models — ignores extra_models from /api/models response
body:
## Bug

Hermex only shows 15 models in the model picker (7 Anthropic + 7 OpenAI + GLM-5.2). The other 34+ models from the server are invisible.

## Root cause

The hermes-webui `/api/models` endpoint returns a `groups[0]` object with two arrays:

- **`models`** (15 items): the "featured" subset shown by default
- **`extra_models`** (34+ items): everything else, reachable via search/show-all in the web UI

Hermex reads `models` and ignores `extra_models`, so over two-thirds of the configured models are invisible in the picker.

## Reproduction

1. Run a hermes-webui server with OpenRouter configured (34 curated models)
2. Connect Hermex
3. Open the model picker
4. Only 15 models appear — all OpenAI/Anthropic + GLM-5.2

## Expected behavior

Hermex should merge `models` and `extra_models` into a single list in the picker, or provide a search/show-all toggle like the web UI does.

## Workaround

None. Typing a model ID manually is not practical on iPhone — the picker is the only discoverable path to model selection.

## Environment

- Hermex 1.5 from App Store
- hermes-webui server (latest master)
- OpenRouter provider with full curated catalog

## API response shape (for reference)

```json
{
  "groups": [{
    "provider": "OpenRouter",
    "provider_id": "openrouter",
    "models": [
      {"id": "anthropic/claude-fable-5", "label": "..."},
      {"id": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol", "label": "..."},
      {"id": "z-ai/glm-5.2", "label": "..."}

    "extra_models": [

      {"id": "qwen/qwen3.8-max", "label": "..."},
      {"id": "google/gemini-3.6-flash", "label": "..."}
```
