title: Render bare file:// assistant artifacts as downloadable files
body:
## Context

Current upstream Hermes WebUI recognizes bare `file://` references emitted by some gateway/tool surfaces and routes them through `/api/media`. Hermex only recognizes `MEDIA:` references in assistant messages.

Related: #145 covers `MEDIA:` rendering, which is already implemented. This issue addresses the narrower `file://` compatibility gap.

## Current behavior

Given an assistant response such as:

```text
Created file:///Users/hermes/workspace/report.csv
```

Hermex renders the reference as ordinary text or an unusable local URL. It does not create a media preview or download control.

A diagnostic parser test reproduced the failure: no `TranscriptMediaReference` was produced. Existing `MEDIA:/Users/hermes/workspace/report.csv` parsing, loading, and export tests pass.

## Expected behavior

Bare, whitespace-delimited `file://` references in assistant messages should enter the existing transcript-media pipeline:

- File URLs are normalized to server-local paths.
- Images, audio, and video use their existing previews.
- Other files use the existing download chip and iOS file exporter.
- Bytes continue to load through the authenticated, session-scoped `/api/media` endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- Recognize a bare `file://` reference at the start of a line or following whitespace in an assistant message.
- Decode percent-escaped path components and remove the `file://` scheme.
- Preserve surrounding prose and punctuation.
- Do not recognize references inside fenced or inline code.
- Do not change existing `MEDIA:` or HTTP(S) behavior.
- Route normalized paths through the existing session-scoped media loader.
- Generic files preserve their original filename and extension when exported.
- Do not access local iPhone files directly or broaden the server’s media allowlist.
- Add regression tests covering generic files, media files, percent-encoded paths, punctuation, code exclusions, and existing `MEDIA:` behavior.

## Validation plan

- Before implementation, validate the latest upstream `file://` rendering convention and `/api/media` route shape against the repo-local upstream copy or an authenticated running server.
- Run focused parser, media-loading, and export tests.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- Build and launch a signed Debug build on the iPhone 17 simulator.
- Manually replay an assistant message containing an allowed server-side `file://` artifact, save it through the Files exporter, and verify its filename and contents.

## Non-goals

- Building a session artifact browser; tracked separately by #222.
- Adding new preview types or redesigning existing media cards.
- Supporting arbitrary URL schemes.
- Changing upstream media authorization or filesystem allowlists.

title: feat(voice): VoiceModeAudioController — exclusive duplex audio engine owner
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 1 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision tickets #232 (duplex audio session) and #234 (AEC research). Depends on: nothing — this is the foundation slice.

## Context

Voice mode needs full-duplex audio: the mic listens (for speech and barge-in) *while* the app speaks. Today capture and playback mutually exclude via `ComposerAudioCaptureState`, and the app has **zero** `AVAudioSession` observers anywhere. The AEC research (#234) established that mode `.voiceChat` alone does **not** echo-cancel: cancellation comes from the voice-processing I/O unit (`AVAudioEngine.inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)`), and it only cancels audio **rendered through that engine** — outside audio is merely ducked. So all voice-mode playback must flow through this one engine.

## Current behavior

Five audio owners exist (composer dictation, voice-note recorder, Listen, inline attachment player, video preview); none observe interruptions or route changes; capture and playback cannot run concurrently.

## Expected behavior

A new type `VoiceModeAudioController` — a **fifth audio owner with an exclusive lease**, alive only while the voice overlay is up. The four existing owners and `ComposerAudioCaptureState` are **not refactored**.

**Session & engine**
- `AVAudioSession`: category `.playAndRecord`, mode `.voiceChat`, option `.defaultToSpeaker` (`.voiceChat` auto-adds Bluetooth HFP).
- `AVAudioEngine` with `inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)` called while the engine is stopped. If it throws, the controller still starts but publishes `bargeInAvailable = false` (consumed later by the half-duplex fallback — the flag is this slice's only barge-in responsibility).
- Engine graph: input tap for capture out; an `AVAudioPlayerNode` for playback in; an `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` node between player and output (rate stays 1.0 in this slice; the speaking-rate setting wires to it later).
- Routing: speaker by default when nothing is connected; headphones/Bluetooth take over automatically (HFP quality accepted). No route picker.

**Lifecycle**
- Activate once on `start()`, hold engine + session live until `stop()`; deactivate with `.notifyOthersOnDeactivation`. No per-turn `setActive` cycling.
- On `start()`, coexistence steps in order: stop Listen playback **including clearing its `MPRemoteCommandCenter` lock-screen commands** (otherwise lock-screen controls could restart Listen mid-session), pause inline attachment players, then hold `ComposerAudioCaptureState.setCapturing(true)` for the whole session (the playback owners' existing guards then keep them off the session with zero changes to their code). Cleared on `stop()`.

**Observers (first in the app)**
- Registers for `AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification`, `routeChangeNotification`, `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`, and `mediaServicesWereResetNotification`, and republishes them as typed events to its consumer.
- v1 fail-safe policy inside this slice: on engine configuration loss, media-services reset, or a session that won't reactivate, surface an "end session" event so the owner layer can exit gracefully. (Richer pause/resume UX is a later slice.)

**API scope — audio I/O only**
- Mic-tap PCM buffer stream out; playback-buffer scheduling in (schedule / stop-immediately-and-discard-queue); route/interruption/fail-safe events out; `bargeInAvailable`.
- No `SFSpeechRecognizer`, no silence detection, no TTS orchestration — those belong to later slices.

## Acceptance criteria

- `VoiceModeAudioController` exists with the API scope above and compiles into the app without being reachable from UI yet.
- Starting it configures session + engine exactly as specified; stopping it deactivates with `.notifyOthersOnDeactivation` and restores `ComposerAudioCaptureState`.
- Entry stops Listen (and its remote commands) and pauses inline players; exit does not auto-resume them.
- `setVoiceProcessingEnabled` failure is caught and reported via `bargeInAvailable == false`, not a crash.
- All four notification observers registered; each republished as a typed event; fail-safe event fires on media-services reset / config loss.
- Unit tests cover: lifecycle state transitions, coexistence call order, capture-flag hold/release, voice-processing-failure path (via protocol seams / mocks — the real session is not testable in CI).

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green.
- Build for simulator. Real duplex/AEC behavior is device-only and is validated in the end-to-end turn-loop slice; this slice only needs the suite plus a clean build.

## Non-goals

- No UI, no recognizer, no synthesis, no turn loop.
- No refactor of existing audio owners.
- No interruption *resume* UX (later slice — this slice only ends gracefully).

title: feat(voice): continuous speech recognition with restart cadence and STT fallback ladder
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 2 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision tickets #234 (recognizer research), #236 (locale & STT ladder), #230 (restart carryover guardrail). Depends on: the `VoiceModeAudioController` slice (mic-tap buffer stream).

## Context

Voice mode needs continuous live speech partials — they drive the caption, the silence-window auto-send, and barge-in detection. `SFSpeechRecognizer` tasks are stopped by the system after ~1 minute (documented) and the on-device exemption is undocumented, so tasks must be restarted on a cadence regardless. The existing `ComposerVoiceInputController` is a good reference for recognizer wiring but is push-to-talk-shaped; voice mode needs its own service consuming the voice engine's mic tap.

## Current behavior

Composer dictation uses `SFSpeechRecognizer` with `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true` via its own audio path; nothing supports continuous long-running recognition, restart carryover, or a network-recognition rung.

## Expected behavior

A new voice-mode STT service that:

- Consumes PCM buffers from `VoiceModeAudioController`'s mic tap (it never touches `AVAudioSession` itself).
- Recognizes in the **Conversation Language** = `Locale.current` (iOS per-app language override flows in automatically). No language picker.
- Exposes: a live partial-transcript stream, a timestamp of the last transcript change (the turn loop's silence detection is *transcript-stability* based), and start/stop/pause controls.
- **Restart cadence:** proactively restarts the recognition task on a cadence safely under 1 minute, and after audio interruptions/route changes. Accumulated transcript text **carries over seamlessly** — a restart must never send, drop, or reorder words (the turn loop depends on this guardrail).
- **Fallback ladder** (decided in #236): 1) on-device `SFSpeechRecognizer` (`requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true`) → 2) Apple **network-backed** recognition (same API, flag dropped — live partials preserved) → 3) report "voice mode unavailable" to the caller (the overlay shows an alert and exits). **If the app's Dictation Provider setting is "On-device only", rung 2 is skipped** — that preference is an explicit "audio stays on this phone" statement. Server batch STT (`POST /api/transcribe`) is ruled out for voice mode: it has no live partials.
- No extra disclosure UI for the network rung — the standard iOS speech permission prompt already discloses Apple processing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Service produces continuous partials across a >1-minute monologue with no dropped words at restart boundaries (verify by unit-testing the carryover/merge logic with a mocked recognizer).
- Transcript-change timestamps update only when the partial text actually changes.
- Ladder selection honors: locale supported on-device → rung 1; unsupported → rung 2 unless Dictation Provider is "On-device only" → rung 3 signal.
- Restart also fires on the controller's interruption/route-change events.
- Composer dictation is completely untouched (its `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true` and existing ladder stay as-is).
- Unit tests cover carryover, ladder selection (incl. the On-device-only skip), and timestamp semantics.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green; simulator build succeeds.
- Live-mic behavior is validated in the end-to-end turn-loop slice.

## Non-goals

- No silence detection or auto-send (turn loop slice).
- No barge-in debounce logic (barge-in slice) — this service just keeps the stream running.
- No UI.

title: feat(voice): voice mode overlay shell and composer entry point
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 3 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision tickets #229 (surface) and #240 (content, orb identity). Depends on: nothing hard (can run parallel to the audio slices; later slices fill the shell).

## Context

The surface decision (#229): voice mode is a **full-screen overlay** (ChatGPT-style) presented over the current chat, entered from a **waveform button in the chat composer** next to the existing mic — it always inherits the chat you're in, no session picker — and exited via an **explicit X button**. A DEBUG-only SwiftUI prototype of this surface exists on local branch `prototype/229-voice-surface` (commits 48f319e, c273f6e) and is the visual reference if available; if the branch isn't present locally, build from this spec.

## Current behavior

No voice-mode surface exists. The composer has a mic (dictation) and voice-note affordances only.

## Expected behavior

- **Entry:** a waveform button in the chat composer (distinct from the dictation mic), visible by default. (A Settings toggle to hide it ships in the settings slice — but read the visibility from a single flag now so that slice only adds the toggle.)
- **Surface:** a full-screen cover over the chat, with:
  - a central **orb** whose color/animation shifts per **Phase** — Listening / Thinking / Speaking / Muted (see CONTEXT.md Voice Mode glossary). Placeholder phase content areas are fine in this slice; the caption-stage content lands in a later slice.
  - a **bottom control cluster**: Mute toggle and X (end) as siblings. X dismisses the overlay; ending is deliberate, never a swipe.
- **State plumbing:** the overlay renders from an observable voice-session model with a Phase enum; in this slice the model can be driven by a stub/preview engine (the prototype's scripted fake loop is precedent) so phases are demoable before the real turn loop exists.
- Accessibility: orb phase changes carry VoiceOver labels naming the Phase (glossary terms); controls have labels; respect Reduce Motion for orb animation.
- All user-facing strings externalized with `String(localized:)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Waveform button appears in the composer, opens the overlay full-screen over the current chat; X closes it and returns to the chat unchanged.
- Orb visibly distinguishes the four Phases (driven by the stub engine in DEBUG).
- Mute toggle flips the model's state (real mic behavior arrives with the turn loop).
- No regression to dictation or voice-note composer buttons.
- New strings externalized; ar/he/ur RTL layout not broken (spot-check via the standard RTL launch args).

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green.
- Build + launch on the iPhone 17 simulator for owner manual test: enter from composer, cycle stub phases, mute, exit. (This is why the slice is labeled needs-manual-validation.)

## Non-goals

- No real audio, recognition, or turn loop — stub-driven only.
- No caption stage / tool cards / teleprompter / history sheet (dedicated slice).
- No settings card.

title: feat(voice): incremental speech pipeline — normalizer, sentence chunker, on-device synthesis
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 4 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision tickets #231 (speaking strategy) and #236 (voice auto-pick). Depends on: the `VoiceModeAudioController` slice (playback node). Parallel to the STT and overlay-shell slices.

## Context

The default speaking path is **incremental on-device synthesis**: assistant SSE tokens are chunked into sentences and spoken as they arrive, so speech starts before the reply finishes. Per the AEC research (#234), on-device speech must render through the voice-processed engine — `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write(_:toBufferCallback:)` producing PCM buffers scheduled on the controller's player node, never `speak(_:)` and never a separate `AVAudioPlayer`.

## Current behavior

Listen (read-aloud) synthesizes whole messages via its own stack; `SpeechTextNormalizer` strips markdown for it. Nothing supports incremental sentence-by-sentence synthesis.

## Expected behavior

**Normalization — reuse and extend `SpeechTextNormalizer`** (Listen behavior untouched):
- New voice-mode entry point: existing markdown stripping **plus fenced code blocks → a localized one-line summary** ("Code block: 14 lines of Swift" — language from the fence info string; a generic form without one). Inline code is spoken as-is.
- The same normalized text later feeds the server-voice path too, so keep it output-agnostic.

**Sentence chunking:**
- SSE tokens accumulate in a buffer; `NLTokenizer` (`.sentence`) segments it. A sentence flushes only once the tokenizer sees content *after* it (boundary confirmed) — no hand-rolled abbreviation/CJK handling.
- Runt merge: flushable sentences under ~20 chars are held and emitted with the next sentence.
- Also flush on paragraph break (`\n\n`) and unconditionally on stream end.
- Never flush a boundary inside an unclosed code fence.
- All thresholds are **named tunable constants** (the owner expects to retune after latency testing).

**Synthesis:**
- Each chunk = one utterance via `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write` → PCM buffers scheduled on the engine player node. Chunk granularity doubles as the stop unit for barge-in (later slice), so the queue must support "stop now, discard the rest".
- Voice: **auto-pick** the best-quality `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice` for the Conversation Language (prefer enhanced/premium when downloaded). No voice picker. (Write the picker helper so Listen/#104 can reuse it later.)
- The engine's `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` node is the speaking-rate hook; this slice keeps rate 1.0.

## Acceptance criteria

- Feeding a simulated token stream produces sentence-chunked utterances respecting: boundary-confirmation, ~20-char runt merge, paragraph flush, stream-end flush, code-fence guard.
- Fenced code blocks are spoken as localized one-line summaries; inline code as-is; Listen's normalization output is byte-identical to before.
- Chunks render as PCM through the controller's player node; a stop request halts mid-buffer and discards queued chunks.
- Voice auto-pick returns an enhanced/premium voice when available for the locale, else the default.
- Unit tests cover the chunker (including CJK sample text, abbreviations like "e.g.", code fences), normalizer extension, and voice pick ordering. The chunker and normalizer must be pure/testable without audio.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green (this slice is mostly pure logic — test-heavy by design).
- Simulator build; audible end-to-end check happens in the turn-loop slice.

## Non-goals

- No server TTS (dedicated slice).
- No turn-loop wiring, no barge-in, no rate setting UI.

title: feat(voice): turn loop state machine — listen, auto-send, stream, speak
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 5 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision tickets #230 (turn loop) and #233 (state machine). Depends on: the audio-controller, STT, overlay-shell, and speech-pipeline slices. This is the first end-to-end slice: a real spoken conversation.

## Context

The loop is hands-free: listen → auto-send on silence → stream the reply → speak it → listen again. webui precedent (upstream #1333) sends after ~1.8 s of silence; iOS `SFSpeechRecognizer` emits no mid-speech final results, so our trigger is **transcript stability**, not audio energy.

## Current behavior

The overlay shell runs on a stub engine; recognition, chunking, and synthesis exist as unwired services.

## Expected behavior

A voice-session engine (conductor) owning the Phase state machine and replacing the shell's stub:

**Listening → send:**
- Continuous listening, no push-to-talk. The turn auto-sends when the partial transcript **has not changed for 2.0 s** (timer resets on any text change). One named tunable constant; **not** user-configurable.
- Guardrails: never send empty/whitespace; the silence timer only arms once non-empty text exists; recognizer restarts never trigger a send or drop words; no maximum turn length.
- Send goes through the existing chat send pipeline for the current session (the overlay inherited it), so the message and reply land in the normal transcript.

**Thinking:**
- One continuous Thinking phase from send until the first spoken chunk. SSE tokens stream into the speech pipeline's chunker; first chunk ready → Speaking.

**Speaking → Listening:**
- Chunks play through the engine; when playback finishes naturally, return to Listening with a fresh transcript buffer. (The barge-in slice refines this transition with its freshness rule; here, natural end simply clears the buffer.)

**Mute / idle / exit:**
- Mute toggle = Paused: mic fully off, audio session held, half-spoken transcript discarded; tap resumes fresh Listening.
- After **~2 min** of continuous silence while Listening (named constant), auto-pause into the same Paused state. The idle timer never cuts off Thinking or Speaking.
- X exits: stop engine, controller teardown, back to chat.

**Error policy (three classes):**
1. Transient STT hiccups → silently restart listening with short backoff, keeping accumulated transcript.
2. Fatal capture errors (permission revoked, session can't start) → exit voice mode with an explanatory alert.
3. Network drop mid-reply (SSE dies) → keep and speak whatever partial reply arrived via the existing transport-aware stream recovery, show a brief "connection lost" state, return to Listening. **Never auto-resend** — the message may have landed server-side.

**Overlay data:** expose the live partial transcript while Listening and the streaming reply text while Thinking/Speaking (the caption-stage slice consumes these; the shell can show them plainly for now).

## Acceptance criteria

- On device/simulator with mic input: speaking a sentence, then staying silent 2 s, sends it to the current session; the reply streams and is spoken sentence-by-sentence; the loop returns to Listening.
- Pure silence never sends; muting kills the mic and discards the half transcript; idle auto-pause fires after the constant elapses; X always exits cleanly and restores normal chat audio behavior.
- Each error class behaves as specified (unit-test the engine's transitions with mocked services; the net-drop case must keep the partial reply and not resend).
- User message + assistant reply appear in the chat transcript exactly like a typed exchange.
- State machine transitions match the table in #233 (Muted per #230); no transition speaks while Listening or listens while Muted.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green (engine transitions, guardrails, error classes — mocked).
- Build + launch on the iPhone 17 simulator for owner manual test: full spoken exchange, mute/resume, idle pause, X exit, airplane-mode mid-reply. (Simulator mic + AEC quality is limited; final AEC verification is a device concern tracked in the barge-in slice.)

## Non-goals

- No barge-in (recognizer may pause during Speaking until that slice lands — ship this slice half-duplex).
- No server quality voice, no interruption/backgrounding UX, no caption-stage visuals.

title: feat(voice): overlay caption stage — live caption, tool cards, teleprompter, history sheet
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 6 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision ticket #240 (overlay content, "A3 caption stage"). Depends on: the turn-loop slice (real phase + stream data). Prototype reference: branch `prototype/229-voice-surface` commit c273f6e (variant A3), if present locally.

## Context

The overlay hides the chat transcript, and Hermes agent replies often run tools for minutes — silence with a blank orb reads as broken. #240 chose the **A3 "caption stage"**: one thing at a time, current turn only, glanceable. With a server quality voice (later slice), streaming reply text is the *only* progress signal during the silent synthesis wait — so the teleprompter is load-bearing, not decorative.

## Current behavior

The overlay shell shows the orb, plain transcript/reply text, and controls.

## Expected behavior

Replace the shell's placeholder content with the caption stage — one phase view at a time:

- **Listening:** the live partial caption, large type, center stage — the user's confirmation that recognition hears them before auto-send fires.
- **Thinking:** a tool-activity card stack: a "Working…" header with an overall elapsed timer (monospaced digits), one card per tool call rendered **sequentially** — running tool highlighted with a spinner, queued tools dimmed, completed tools collapsed to checkmarks. Maps 1:1 onto the SSE tool events the app already receives. Plain thinking (no tools) shows header + timer alone.
- **Speaking:** the streamed reply as a **bottom-anchored teleprompter** — large type, scrolling as tokens arrive. Reply text is always shown (comprehension aid for robotic on-device TTS; keeps the mode usable muted or in noise).
- **Phase identity:** the orb's color/animation per phase stays the at-a-glance signal (from the shell slice).
- **History:** not inline. A toolbar button opens the voice-session transcript as a sheet (medium/large detents) — reuse the chat message rendering where practical.
- **Barge-in affordances (visual hooks only):** a hint shown during Speaking, and a brief "Heard you — go ahead" confirmation view. In this slice they can be triggered by tap-to-stop only; the barge-in slice wires speech-triggered interrupts to them.

Accessibility: phase views announce transitions; timer and cards are VoiceOver-readable; Reduce Motion honored. All strings externalized.

## Acceptance criteria

- During a real turn with tools, the card stack shows sequential tool progress with the elapsed timer; no-tool turns show header + timer.
- Listening shows the live caption; Speaking shows the scrolling teleprompter synced to arriving tokens.
- History sheet shows the session's messages and dismisses cleanly.
- Exactly one phase view is on stage at any moment; transitions are animated but Reduce-Motion-safe.
- RTL spot-check passes; strings externalized.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green.
- Build + launch on the iPhone 17 simulator for owner manual test against a real Hermes session that runs tools (long tool stretch, teleprompter scroll, history sheet). Labeled needs-manual-validation — streaming UI.

## Non-goals

- No barge-in detection mechanics (next slice) — visual hooks only.
- No paused/interruption visual states beyond what the shell has (interruption slice refines).

title: feat(voice): barge-in and tap-to-stop
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 7 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision ticket #233 (barge-in), grounded in #232/#234. Depends on: the turn-loop and caption-stage slices. Net-new design — upstream webui has no barge-in precedent.

## Context

**Barge-in** (CONTEXT.md glossary): interrupting the assistant while it thinks or speaks by talking over it; the interrupting words begin the next turn. It works because all voice-mode audio renders through the voice-processing-enabled engine (AEC keeps our own TTS out of the mic path), so the recognizer can simply keep running.

## Current behavior

After the turn-loop slice, the mode is effectively half-duplex: recognition stops during Thinking/Speaking; only natural end-of-speech returns to Listening.

## Expected behavior

**Detection — recognizer-only, full duplex:**
- The STT service runs **continuously across Listening, Thinking, and Speaking** — barge-in is the listening loop never stopping. No energy/VAD threshold (raw energy gates hear residual echo and are more false-trigger-prone than recognized speech).
- Armed during **Speaking and Thinking** both (during the later quality-voice silent wait it is the only way out of a stall).
- Only when `bargeInAvailable` (from the audio controller): otherwise run the **Half-Duplex Fallback** — recognizer only during Listening, mic paused during Thinking/Speaking, no speech-triggered barge-in that session; Tap-to-Stop still works. Internal flag only; **no user-facing setting**.

**Debounce:** barge-in fires when a partial transcript of **≥ min-chars of non-whitespace text persists or grows for a ~300 ms confirmation window**. Two named tunable constants (the knob if speaker-route echo phantoms appear in the field). No backchannel-word blocklist.

**Effects of a barge-in, in order:**
1. **Stop audio immediately** — halt the player node mid-buffer, discard all queued chunks. No finish-the-sentence grace.
2. **Cancel in-flight work:** reply still streaming → fire the existing `cancelActiveStream()` path (`GET /api/chat/cancel`, same as the chat Stop button — socket close alone does not stop server generation). (When the quality-voice slice lands, its `/api/tts` wait aborts the TTS request instead — design that seam now.) Speech that outlives the stream → purely local stop.
3. **Seed the next turn:** the interrupting words are already in the transcript; transition to Listening and let the normal 2.0 s silence → auto-send loop take over. The user never repeats themselves.

Partial reply text stays in the chat **verbatim, no interrupted marker** — exactly matching existing Stop-button behavior; zero message-model changes.

**End-of-speech transcript hygiene:** at a **natural** Speaking → Listening transition, keep the transcript buffer **only if it changed within the last confirmation window** (fresh, still-moving speech = an in-progress barge-in — covers "user answers a beat before TTS finishes"); anything staler is discarded as echo junk. One timestamp comparison reusing the confirmation-window constant.

**Tap-to-Stop:** a tap during Thinking/Speaking triggers the same interrupt path with an **empty transcript seed** → fresh Listening. Wire it to the caption-stage hint/confirmation views ("Heard you — go ahead" on speech barge-in).

## Acceptance criteria

- Speaking over the assistant mid-speech stops audio within the confirmation window, cancels the stream via `cancelActiveStream()`, and the interrupting words auto-send after the normal silence window — no repetition needed.
- Barge-in during Thinking cancels the stream the same way.
- Tap during Thinking/Speaking stops identically with an empty seed.
- Natural end-of-speech keeps a fresh (still-changing) buffer, discards a stale one (unit-test the timestamp rule).
- With voice processing unavailable (forced flag), the session runs Half-Duplex: no speech barge-in, tap still works.
- Chat transcript shows the partial reply verbatim, no marker.
- Unit tests: debounce (min-chars + confirm window), effect ordering, hygiene rule, half-duplex arming.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green.
- Build + launch on the iPhone 17 simulator for owner manual test; **AEC quality (does the recognizer hear our own TTS?) must additionally be sanity-checked on a physical device on the speaker route** — the debounce constants are the tuning knob. Labeled needs-manual-validation.

## Non-goals

- No `/api/tts` abort implementation (quality-voice slice — just leave the cancel seam).
- No VAD/energy detection, no barge-in setting.

title: feat(voice): server quality voice via POST /api/tts — fallbacks and server-seeded default
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 8 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision tickets #231 (speaking strategy) and #235 (live engine probe). Depends on: the turn-loop slice (and the barge-in slice's cancel seam).

## Context

Server `POST /api/tts` offers higher-quality voices than on-device synthesis, at the cost of waiting for the **full reply** then one buffered synthesis call (rate limit **1 req/2 s per client**, **5000-char cap**, ~30 s server timeout, fully-buffered audio response). Live probe (#235): `edge` always works (hard-coded 15-voice allowlist, off-list → 400; **server default voice is zh-CN-Xiaoxiao — always send an explicit voice**); `elevenlabs`/`openai` return 503 until the server has keys, and their voices are fixed in server `config.yaml`, not per-request. `voice`/`rate`/`pitch` are honored **only for edge**.

## Current behavior

After earlier slices, every turn speaks via incremental on-device synthesis.

## Expected behavior

**The offering — one "Voice" choice per server:** On-device / Server: ElevenLabs / Server: OpenAI / Server: Edge. (The settings UI ships in the next slice; this slice implements storage, seeding, and the pipeline, testable by setting the stored value directly.)

- Storage: namespaced per-server UserDefaults keys (`"voiceMode.<key>|<serverURL>"`), matching `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`. The Keychain registry blob stays identity/credentials-only.
- **Seed once per server** on first voice-mode use: read `GET /api/settings` speech prefs — `tts_engine` ∈ {elevenlabs, openai, edge} → seed Server voice with that engine (+ `tts_voice` for edge); `browser`/unset → On-device. Thereafter the choice is a **local per-server override, never written back**. Requires adding `ttsEngine`/`ttsVoice` decoding to `SettingsResponse` (currently dropped) — optionals, tolerant decoding.
- **No upfront engine probing** (no discovery endpoint exists).

**Pipeline when a server voice is selected:**
- One continuous **Thinking** phase spans reply streaming + synthesis — no separate "synthesizing" stage; the teleprompter's streaming text is the progress signal. Normalize the full reply with the same voice-mode normalizer, then call `POST /api/tts` with explicit `engine` (and explicit `voice` for edge).
- Decode the returned audio into PCM buffers scheduled on the engine player node (never `AVAudioPlayer` — AEC constraint). Playback stops mid-buffer on barge-in via the existing cancel seam; also abort an in-flight `/api/tts` request on barge-in during the wait.
- Speaking rate still flows through the `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` node, uniform with on-device.

**Fallback to on-device (per turn, setting persists, brief notice in overlay):**
- 503 / request failure / timeout.
- **429** → wait out the remaining ≤2 s rate-limit window (last request time is known), retry once, then fall back.
- Reply over **5000 normalized chars** (no multi-call chunking — matches Listen's `ServerTTSPolicy` precedent).
- **Edge + Conversation Language not covered by the 15-voice allowlist** → on-device for that turn (#236).

## Acceptance criteria

- With a server voice stored, a turn streams silently through Thinking then plays server audio; barge-in during wait aborts the TTS request; during playback stops mid-buffer.
- Each fallback trigger (503, timeout, 429-retry-exhausted, >5000 chars, edge locale mismatch) speaks the turn on-device with a notice, without stalling the conversation, and leaves the setting untouched.
- Seeding: first use against a server whose settings report `tts_engine: edge` + voice lands Edge + that voice; `browser` lands On-device; subsequent server-side changes don't overwrite the local override.
- `SettingsResponse` decodes `tts_engine`/`tts_voice` as optionals; unknown fields never crash.
- Unit tests: seeding matrix, fallback triggers, 429 wait math, per-server key namespacing, request body shape.

## Validation plan

- **Route-shape validation before implementation** (hard rule): verify `POST /api/tts` and `GET /api/settings` request/response shapes against the pinned upstream `_handle_tts`/settings handlers in `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py`, and against the running server where possible; record the validated shapes and upstream commit in the PR.
- Full XCTest suite green; simulator build. Manual check against the live server (edge engine) with owner.

## Non-goals

- No settings UI (next slice).
- No multi-call chunked server synthesis, no engine probing, no writing prefs back to the server.

title: feat(voice): Voice Mode settings page
body:
**Update (2026-10-14):** Settings is now an index of pages (#1252, #1255). This lands as a **Voice** page under Settings → Hermex instead of a card. It takes Dictation Provider from the Composer page, and puts the per-server voice picker under a *This server* header, the way Notifications does. Notes are one line (#1259).

Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 9 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision ticket #236 (settings & gating), with rows from #231. Depends on: the overlay-shell slice (entry button) and the server-voice slice (engine/voice storage).

## Context

#236 decided: **no opt-in gate** — the composer waveform button is visible by default with a toggle to hide it (same pattern as the Files/Git button visibility toggles), and one dedicated **"Voice Mode" settings card** near Interaction rather than rows scattered across Interaction/Active Server.

## Current behavior

Voice mode works but is configured only through stored defaults; no settings surface exists; the entry button cannot be hidden.

## Expected behavior

A new "Voice Mode" card in Settings (placed near Interaction) holding:

1. **Voice picker (per-server):** On-device / Server: ElevenLabs / Server: OpenAI / Server: Edge — writing the per-server namespaced UserDefaults value the pipeline already reads. For ElevenLabs/OpenAI, UI copy states "voice is configured on your server."
2. **Edge voice sub-picker** (visible only when Edge is selected): the hard-coded 15-voice allowlist (zh-CN ×5, en-US Aria/Guy, fr-CA ×4, fr-FR ×3, id-ID ×1), default `en-US-AriaNeural`, matching Listen's default. Below it, one static footnote: voices are language-specific; unmatched languages use the on-device voice. **No dynamic voice disabling.**
3. **Speaking rate:** 0.5× / 1× / 1.5× / 2×, default 1× — **global** (`@AppStorage`, own key, not per-server; deliberately not reusing `ListenPlaybackSpeed`), wired to the engine's `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` node so on-device and server audio shift uniformly, pitch-preserved. No in-overlay rate control.
4. **Show voice mode button** toggle: hides/shows the composer waveform entry button (default on).

Notes:
- No opt-in gate, no silence-window setting (fixed 2.0 s constant — only revisit if TestFlight testers report being cut off), no language picker, no on-device voice picker, no barge-in setting.
- All strings externalized with `String(localized:)`; card follows the existing settings section/card idiom.

## Acceptance criteria

- The card renders with the four items above; Edge sub-picker + footnote appear only for Edge.
- Per-server values isolate correctly across two configured servers; speaking rate applies globally and audibly changes voice-mode speech rate without pitch shift.
- Toggling the button visibility off removes the waveform button from the composer immediately; voice mode remains reachable nowhere else.
- Strings externalized; RTL spot-check passes.
- Unit tests: rate-setting → time-pitch mapping, per-server isolation, allowlist contents/default.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green.
- Build + launch on the iPhone 17 simulator for owner manual test: pick each engine, Edge sub-picker, rate change audibility, hide toggle.

## Non-goals

- No new pipeline behavior (previous slice owns fallbacks/seeding).
- No translations beyond English source strings — the standing translation-batch process covers the 17 locales separately.

title: feat(voice): interruptions, resume, and Pocket Mode
body:
Part of #36 (voice conversation mode). Slice 10 of 10 — design source: wayfinder map #228, decision ticket #241 (interruption & resume UX), layered on #232's fail-safe and #230's Paused state. Depends on: the turn-loop and barge-in slices.

## Context

#241 decided the richer UX on top of the audio controller's v1 fail-safe: interruptions **pause** rather than end; backgrounding continues the conversation (**Pocket Mode**, CONTEXT.md glossary); the existing per-turn Live Activity is reused untouched. The app declares `UIBackgroundModes: audio`; Listen already plays in background, but a background open mic is a first (iOS's mic indicator stays visible — accepted).

## Current behavior

After earlier slices, any audio interruption ends the voice session via the controller's fail-safe; backgrounding follows ChatView's suspend-on-background path, which would kill Pocket Mode.

## Expected behavior

**Interruptions (calls, Siri, another app taking audio) — pause, don't end:**
- On interruption begin: drop into the existing **Paused** state (mic off, session + context alive). Overlay shows the paused state with the reason. If interrupted mid-Listening, the half-spoken transcript is discarded (mute semantics).
- The in-flight turn survives: the SSE stream is network traffic — reply text keeps streaming into transcript/overlay; only speech playback stops.
- **Hybrid resume:** foreground → manual tap only (the mic never auto-reopens while the user is at the screen); backgrounded + iOS `.shouldResume` → auto-resume (fixes the declined-call-in-pocket case).
- On resume with unspoken reply content: resume speaking from the **next unspoken sentence** (the chunker provides the boundary; a never-started reply speaks from the top). Stale readback is self-correcting via barge-in/Tap-to-Stop.
- The controller's fail-safe (end gracefully, transcript preserved, exit with alert) remains for unrecoverable cases: media-services reset, engine configuration loss, session that won't reactivate.

**Backgrounding — Pocket Mode:**
- Backgrounding or locking mid-conversation changes nothing: listening, thinking, speaking, and turn cycling continue under background audio. The ~2-min idle auto-pause bounds a forgotten open mic.
- Implementation consequence: voice mode **bypasses ChatView's suspend-on-background path** (`beginResponseCompletionBackgroundTask` → `suspendStreamForBackground`) — the app isn't suspending while the engine runs, so SSE streams stay connected in background. Normal chat (voice mode closed) keeps today's behavior.
- **Paused while backgrounded** (mute, idle auto-pause, or interruption without `.shouldResume`): deactivate the audio session and let iOS suspend the app. State freezes; reopening the app revives the paused overlay and resume works. If iOS kills the process, the transcript is already in the chat. Accepted: an idle-paused pocketed session can't be woken by voice.

**Route changes:** unplugged headphones / dropped Bluetooth switch to the next route (speaker default) **without pausing** — VoIP convention, no `.oldDeviceUnavailable` pause, no route picker.

**Live Activity:** voice turns reuse the **existing per-stream Live Activity untouched** — starts when the turn's SSE opens (the one call site in `ChatStreamCoordinator.start`), deep-link tap-through returns to the session, reconciler logic unchanged; in Pocket Mode it updates live. **No persistent session-long voice activity** between turns (ruled out of scope on #228).

## Acceptance criteria

- A phone call mid-Speaking pauses the session with a visible reason; reply text keeps streaming in; foreground resume is manual-tap only; a call declined while backgrounded auto-resumes on `.shouldResume`.
- Resume after interruption mid-reply speaks from the next unspoken sentence, not the top.
- Backgrounding mid-conversation continues the full loop (verify: send while backgrounded via voice, hear the reply, next turn cycles); the per-turn Live Activity appears/updates as for a normal stream.
- Pausing while backgrounded releases the audio session (app becomes suspendable); reopening revives the paused overlay.
- Route loss mid-speech continues on speaker without pausing.
- Normal chat backgrounding behavior (voice mode closed) is unchanged.
- Unit tests: interruption → Paused transitions, hybrid-resume decision table, resume-boundary selection, suspend-path bypass gating.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite green.
- Owner manual test — much of this is device-only (real calls, lock screen, mic indicator): simulator pass for state transitions + backgrounded streaming, then a physical-device pass for call interruption, pocket loop, and Live Activity. Labeled needs-manual-validation (live activities + audio interruptions cannot be automated).

## Non-goals

- No persistent session-long Live Activity, no App Intents (out of the map's scope).
- No route picker, no per-route pause behavior.

title: Kanban silently resets locally browsed Board after app relaunch
body:
## Summary

Hermex's locally browsed Kanban Board is transient. After the Kanban feature state is recreated, such as after an app termination/relaunch, Hermex silently returns to the server-global active Board instead of restoring the Board the user last chose on that server.

This can look like stale Kanban data even though snapshot refresh and SSE recovery are healthy: Hermex successfully reloads and reconnects, but it does so for a different Board than the user expects.

## Current behavior and code path

`KanbanFeatureState` explicitly describes its Board choice as transient and not persisted. `selectBoard(_:)` updates only `selectedBoardSlug` in memory. During `load()`, a newly created state has no `previouslySelectedBoard`, so it selects `boardsResponse.current`, the shared server-global active Board.

Relevant code:

- `HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift`
  - the state is documented as transient and non-persisted
  - `load()` chooses `previouslySelectedBoard ?? currentBoard`
  - `selectBoard(_:)` updates only the live state
- `HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift`
  - Board selection is presented as local browsing
  - Manage Boards correctly distinguishes local browsing from changing shared server state

This is separate from foreground live-update recovery in #151 / #165. Runtime observation showed that after reopening the app, Hermex performed fresh successful Board reads and reopened `/api/kanban/events/stream` from the authoritative cursor. The transport was current, but every request had returned to the server-global active Board.

## Reproduction

1. Connect Hermex to a server with at least two Kanban Boards, A and B.
2. Keep A as the shared active Board on the server.
3. In Hermex, use the Board picker to browse B locally.
4. Terminate and relaunch Hermex, or otherwise recreate the server-bound Kanban feature state.
5. Open Kanban again.

### Actual

Hermex silently browses A because it is `boardsResponse.current`.

### Expected

Hermex restores B as the locally browsed Board for that server. If B no longer exists, it safely falls back to the server's current Board and communicates the fallback where appropriate.

## Proposed behavior

Persist the last locally browsed Board per normalized server identity without changing shared server state.

- Restore the saved Board when creating/loading `KanbanFeatureState` for the same server.
- Keep selections isolated between servers.
- Validate the saved slug against the authoritative Board collection before using it.
- If the saved Board was removed or archived, discard it and fall back to `boardsResponse.current` using the existing removed-Board recovery behavior.
- Do not turn local browsing into an implicit “Make Active Board” mutation.
- Preserve the foreground reconciliation and SSE behavior shipped in #165.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting Board B, recreating the Kanban state, and reopening Kanban restores B.
- [ ] App termination/relaunch preserves the locally browsed Board.
- [ ] Server A and server B maintain independent saved Board choices.
- [ ] A saved Board that no longer exists is cleared and falls back safely to the server-current Board.
- [ ] Switching servers cannot briefly request or display the previous server's saved Board.
- [ ] Local Board selection never changes the shared active Board endpoint/state.
- [ ] Foreground reconciliation still fetches a complete authoritative snapshot and reconnects SSE for the restored Board.
- [ ] Tests cover cold-state restoration, per-server isolation, removed-Board fallback, and foreground reconciliation after restoration.

## Related

- #151 / #165: Kanban live updates and foreground/offline reconciliation
- #191: local Board browsing versus shared active-Board controls
- #203: normal Kanban navigation activation

No server or Nesquena WebUI change should be required; this is native Hermex client state behavior.

title: perf(chat): assistant markdown is re-parsed on every SwiftUI body evaluation
body:
### What's happening

Scrolling a long transcript does more work than it needs to, because the app re-parses
assistant messages that have not changed.

Both transcript renderers call `MarkdownMathSegmenter.segments(in:)` inside the SwiftUI
`body`, so it runs on **every body evaluation** rather than once per message. And in the
no-math case — which is almost every message — the renderer then runs
`MarkdownMathFormatter.replacingInlineMath(in:)` over the same string a second time:

```swift
// MarkdownRenderer.swift
let segments = MarkdownMathSegmenter.segments(in: content)
if segments.containsMath {
    ...
} else {
    ChatMarkdownView(
        content: MarkdownMathFormatter.replacingInlineMath(in: content),  // second full pass
        ...
    )
}
```

Each of those two calls walks the content twice internally (build the protection mask,
then scan), so a long answer pays four full passes per evaluation over text that is
identical to last time.

This matters because SwiftUI re-evaluates a body for reasons that have nothing to do with
the message text — a sibling view toggling, a scroll-position change, an `@AppStorage`
write. On a long transcript that cost is paid repeatedly while scrolling.

### Measurement

Compiled the actual segmenter/formatter sources with `-O` and timed
`segments(in:)` + the second `replacingInlineMath` pass on realistic assistant answers:

| answer size | cost per body evaluation |
| --- | --- |
| 666 B | 0.63 ms |
| 2.7 KB | 2.53 ms |
| 8 KB | 7.49 ms |

### Expected behavior

Parsing an assistant message that has not changed should be close to free on repeat
evaluations, and the no-math path should not scan the same string twice.

### Notes

This is independent of the lazy-row work in #32 / #33 / #217 — those reduce how many rows
get *built*, this reduces what a single row *costs each time it is evaluated*. No file
overlap with either.

I have a fix ready with a differential correctness check; happy to open the PR if this
looks worth taking.

### App version / commit

`83127a4` (current master)

title: perf(chat): stop re-parsing unchanged assistant markdown on every body evaluation
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #260

## What changed

**In one sentence:** the app was re-reading and re-parsing assistant messages that hadn't
changed, and now it remembers the result instead.

Here's the situation. Before drawing a message, the renderer has to look through the text
for math (`$$...$$`), because math needs a different view than normal markdown. That search
is not cheap — it walks the whole message twice. The problem is *where* it was being called
from: inside SwiftUI's `body`, which runs again every time anything nearby changes. Not when
the message changes — when *anything* changes. Toggling a card elsewhere on screen,
scrolling, or writing a setting all trigger it.

On top of that, the common case did the work twice. If a message had no display math — which
is nearly all of them — the code threw away what the scan produced and ran a second
whole-string pass to handle inline math:

```swift
let segments = MarkdownMathSegmenter.segments(in: content)
if segments.containsMath {
    ...
} else {
    ChatMarkdownView(
        content: MarkdownMathFormatter.replacingInlineMath(in: content),  // scans it all again
        ...
    )
}
```

Two changes:

1. **Remember the answer.** Settled messages go through `MarkdownMathLayoutCache`, keyed by
   the message text. Same text in, same layout out, without redoing the scan.
2. **Stop the double pass.** The no-math case now reuses the markdown the scan already
   produced, instead of re-deriving it from the original string.

### What it costs now

Timed against the real segmenter/formatter sources compiled with `-O`:

| answer size | before | after (repeat evaluation) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 666 B | 0.63 ms | 0.0010 ms |
| 2.7 KB | 2.53 ms | 0.0035 ms |
| 8 KB | 7.49 ms | 0.0095 ms |

### One correctness subtlety (found in review)

A display-math span with an empty body (`$$ $$`, `\[ \]`) is recognised by the segmenter --
it consumes the delimiters -- but emits no math segment, because the trimmed body is empty.
Reconstructing the plain layout from the surviving markdown therefore dropped that literal
text. The layout now detects content carrying a display delimiter that produced no math and
defers to the original whole-string pass for it. Rare content pays one extra walk; everything
else is unchanged.

### Two decisions worth flagging for review

**Streaming deliberately does not use the cache.** Streaming text changes on nearly every
token, so caching it would add a new entry per token and push out the settled messages the
cache exists to protect. The streaming path calls `uncachedLayout(for:)` — it still gets the
benefit of dropping the duplicate pass (5.08 ms vs 7.49 ms on an 8 KB body) without the churn.

**`NSCache`, not a dictionary.** Entries evict automatically under memory pressure rather
than growing with transcript length, and it is thread-safe, which matters because SwiftUI can
evaluate bodies off the main thread.

### Why this doesn't collide with the other perf work

#32 / #33 / #217 reduce how many rows get **built**. This reduces what a single row **costs
each time it is evaluated**. They stack, and there is no file overlap — this PR touches only
`MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift`, `MarkdownRenderer.swift`, and a new test file.

## How it was tested

**Rendering is unchanged — that's the main thing to verify.** The optimization is only valid
if joining the scan's markdown pieces produces exactly what the old second pass produced. A
seeded differential test (`testPlainLayoutMatchesLegacyPassAcrossGeneratedContent`) generates
thousands of markdown combinations — bold, code fences, tables, quotes, escaped dollar signs,
real inline math, unicode — and asserts the new output is byte-identical to the old for every
one, including the empty display-math spans that caused the bug found in review. The seed is fixed, so any failure reprints the exact input.

Full suite on the branch:

```
xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17'
```

→ **1,579 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (1,572 on master + 7 new).

No UI screenshots: this PR changes no pixels by design. The visual contract is "identical
output, less work," which is what the differential test asserts.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly — n/a, no model changes
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes — n/a, no networking changes

title: Proposal: reworked chat transcript — turn activity grouping, plan surface from todo_state, typography
body:
### Summary

I've been running a fork with a reworked chat transcript for a while, and it's now stable
enough that I'd like to offer it upstream. It's a lot of work — too much for one PR — so
rather than drop a 9,000-line diff on you, I'd like to agree on scope first, and whether you
want any of it at all.

Per CONTRIBUTING ("open an issue first and wait for a maintainer nod"), this is that issue.
Nothing is on the table that you don't ask for.

### Where this came from

Three things bothered me as a daily user:

1. **A turn's activity is hard to scan.** Thinking blocks and tool calls stack up as
   separate cards. On a turn with 70 tool calls you scroll past a wall of chrome to reach the
   answer.
2. **Parallel tool calls don't read as parallel.** They render as a flat list, so you can't
   tell what ran together and what ran in sequence.
3. **The server tells us the agent's plan and the app ignores it.** More on that below —
   it's the smallest and most self-contained piece, so it's the one I'd suggest starting with.

### What it looks like

Same fixture content rendered on current `master` vs the fork, light and dark:

![before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/assets/proposal-screenshots/collage-markdown-before-after.png)

The differences are mostly typographic and structural: quieter status rows (`Thinking` →
`Thought`, tool row gains its target and duration), a softer blockquote treatment, tightened
heading rhythm, and a palette that can run warm or neutral.

### Suggested split

I'd propose these as separate PRs, in this order, and I'm happy to stop after any of them:

**1. Surface the agent's plan from `todo_state`** — ~860 lines, self-contained

The server already emits this and the app decodes neither path. From
`api/todo_state.py` upstream:

- **Live:** a dedicated `todo_state` SSE event mid-stream
- **Cold load:** the session GET attaches `todo_state` derived from the most recent
  `role='tool'` message carrying a `todos` list

So the data is there on every turn and we drop it. Rendering it as a compact "3 of 5" pill
above the composer that expands into the checklist:

![plan states](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/assets/proposal-screenshots/plan-states.png)

Decoding follows the documented contract: always-replace never-merge, reconcile by `ts`,
filter by `session_id`, and an empty list is a valid "cleared" snapshot rather than a no-op.
Tolerant decoding throughout. New files only (`Models/TodoState.swift`,
`Features/Chat/PlanTimelineView.swift`) plus tests — no existing behavior changes.

**2. Group a turn's activity into one container** — the structural change

Thinking and tool blocks for a settled turn collapse under a single row; parallel calls
render indented under a shared connector so you can see what ran together.

![activity fold](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/assets/proposal-screenshots/after-page14.png)

Important detail: this applies to **settled turns only**. A live streaming turn keeps the
existing independent-cards layout — I tried it the other way and it was worse to watch.

**3. Palette and typography** — the widest-touching, most opinionated part

A warm/neutral chat palette with semantic tokens, plus the markdown typography changes. This
is the one most likely to conflict with your own taste, which is why it's last. Entirely
reasonable to want none of it.

### What I'm not proposing

The fork also carries a personal App Store Connect/TestFlight identity and debug gallery
screens. Neither belongs upstream and neither would appear in any PR.

### Questions

1. Is any of this interesting? Happy to hear "no" for the parts that don't fit.
2. If yes, does the split above look right, or would you rather see it sliced differently?
3. #1 (`todo_state`) is genuinely independent and adds a feature from data you already send —
   worth doing on its own even if you pass on the rest?

Existing test suite stays green throughout (currently 1,618 passing on my branch, including
new coverage for each piece).

---

Built with Codex (GPT-5.6).

title: feat(chat): session canvas polish — turn activity grouping, plan surface, palette
body:
## Linked issue

Refs #262 (proposal + rationale). Happy to open a tracking issue to close instead if you'd
rather have one.

## What changed

This is the session canvas work from our DM. Three things, on one branch because they share
a palette layer — I've noted below what could be pulled out if you want it smaller.

### 1. A turn's activity reads as one thing

Thinking blocks and tool calls used to stack as independent cards. On a turn with a lot of
tool calls you scrolled past a wall of chrome to reach the answer. Now a **settled** turn
collapses them under one container with a summary row you can tap:

![activity fold](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/assets/proposal-screenshots/activity-fold.png)

Parallel tool calls render indented under a shared connector, so what ran together is
visually distinct from what ran in sequence.

**One deliberate constraint:** this applies to settled turns only. A live streaming turn
keeps the existing independent-card layout. I tried it the other way first and it was worse
to watch — the container fighting a stream that's still arriving. `liveActivityFold` is
byte-identical to its pre-change version; the container, the auto-expand override, and the
section dividers are all gated on `isHistorical`.

### 2. The agent's plan, which the server was already sending

`hermes-webui` emits `todo_state` in two places — a live SSE event mid-stream, and a
cold-load sidecar attached to the session GET. The app decoded neither, so the plan just
disappeared. It now renders as a compact pill above the composer that expands into the
checklist:

![plan surface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/assets/proposal-screenshots/plan-surface.png)

Decoding follows `api/todo_state.py`: always-replace never-merge, reconcile by `ts`, filter
by `session_id`, and an empty list is a valid *cleared* snapshot rather than a no-op. No new
endpoints, no invented shapes.

### 3. Palette and typography

A `ChatPalette` with semantic tokens, adopted across chat, session list, workspace and
settings. Warm and standard temperatures, light and dark. Same fixture content, before and
after:

![before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/assets/proposal-screenshots/collage-markdown-before-after.png)

Markdown changes: de-slabbed inline code, editorial heading ramp, softer blockquote, quieter
rules. Reasoning renders as real markdown at a damped scale — a thought containing an H1
shouldn't shout louder than the answer beneath it.

Activity indicators use eight orb styles mapped to what the tool is actually doing
(ported from [thinking-orbs](https://github.com/Jakubantalik/thinking-orbs), MIT, attribution
added to `ThirdPartyNotices`):

![orb states](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/assets/proposal-screenshots/orb-states.png)

## Performance notes

Two things I watched for, since this adds animated chrome to the transcript:

- **Animation cost stays flat as tool count grows.** Everything is driven from one shared
  clock rather than a timeline per row — a per-row version measured 78% CPU on a large turn.
- **Folded blocks unmount** rather than laying out hidden rows. A 70-tool turn laying out
  invisible content was real jank.

`ChatTranscriptMessageRow` is `Equatable` so a fold toggling can't invalidate its
neighbours. Closures are excluded from `==` on purpose — they're recreated on every parent
evaluation and would make it always-unequal, silently restoring a transcript-wide re-parse.
There's a comment saying so, since it looks like an oversight otherwise.

## How it was tested

```
xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17'
```

→ **1,622 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.**

Manual: normally-signed Debug build on iPhone 17, walked live streaming turns, settled
turns, parallel tool groups, plan updates arriving mid-stream and on cold load, both
palettes, light and dark, and Dynamic Type up to AX5.

The `#if DEBUG` gallery screens are included — they're how I reviewed each surface in
isolation, reachable via `--surface-gallery --surface-gallery-page N`, and they compile out
of release builds. Happy to strip them if you'd rather not carry them.

## Notes for review

- **This does not include the markdown perf fix in #261.** That's independent and already up
  separately; this branch is deliberately free of it so the two don't conflict.
- **No personal signing config.** My fork carries a separate App Store Connect identity for
  TestFlight; none of it is on this branch.
- **Splitting:** the plan surface (#2) is the most separable — new files only, ~860 lines,
  nothing existing changes. The activity grouping and palette are harder to tease apart
  because the views render through the palette tokens. Say the word and I'll split.
- You closed #221 (turn grouping) back in August — if that was a direction call rather than
  timing, tell me and I'll rework rather than re-litigate.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (`TodoState` uses optionals throughout)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (orb code is vendored, MIT, attributed)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (`todo_state` verified against
      `api/todo_state.py` and a running server)

---

Built with Codex (GPT-5.6).


## Follow-up: reusable plan and goal status rail

The plan pill now participates in a reusable above-composer status rail, and structured `/goal` state uses the same pill-to-card interaction instead of pinning an unbounded server notice over the chat.

- Plan and goal are mutually exclusive when expanded; collapsed status pills share one horizontally scrollable rail.
- Long goals are capped against the live composer dock, scroll independently, show an overflow cue, and keep the composer reachable.
- Active, paused, done, cleared, and unknown goal states have distinct tolerant presentation; active state motion respects Reduce Motion.
- Expanded surfaces share one chrome/padding contract and compact controls retain 44-point tap targets.
- When a backing plan/goal disappears, view-owned expansion state clears instead of leaking into the next snapshot.

### Follow-up verification

- Full `HermesMobileTests` suite on the updated PR branch: **1,653 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Focused goal/plan contract and layout tests: **29 passed, 0 failed**.
- Signed iPhone 17 simulator launch of the long-goal regression gallery: bounded centered card, visible overflow affordance, no sibling clipping, and no composer overlap.
- Independent adversarial integrated-diff and visual closure review: no P0/P1 findings.

title: fix(kanban): decode run IDs from detail events
body:
## Linked issue

No upstream issue — this came out of a client/server contract audit rather than a filed bug report, so there was nothing to link. Happy to open one if you would rather have it tracked separately. The raw audit note is [audichuang/hermex#13](https://github.com/audichuang/hermex/issues/13) (written in Chinese); everything relevant is reproduced in English below.

## What changed

- Decode `run_id` on Kanban detail events using the key the shared decoder actually produces.
- Move the regression test inside the `XCTestCase` so test discovery runs it.

## Root cause

`KanbanDetailEvent.CodingKeys` declared `case runID` with no raw value, so the literal key was `runID`. `APIClient` decodes with `.convertFromSnakeCase`, which maps the server's `run_id` to `runId`. The two never matched, so `runID` always decoded as `nil`. The sibling `CodingKeys` in the same file (`HermesMobile/Models/Kanban.swift:209`) already spells its raw value out, so this was an omission rather than a design choice.

The fix sits on the model every Kanban detail-event consumer decodes through, not on one call site.

## Contract evidence

- Upstream `nesquena/hermes-webui`, read-only local checkout at `ecc47782e3e72a5bf3e848a8f09a2a5a838c71b1` (2026-07-22): `api/kanban_bridge.py:322` writes detail events as `task_events (task_id, run_id, kind, payload, created_at)` — the wire field is `run_id`.
- This repo's compatibility pin `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA` is `f1d399b4` (v0.51.85). The checkout above is newer than the pin and is not itself the pin.
- No live wire capture for this path; see Need to verify.

## How it was tested

- Focused: `APIClientKanbanTests/testKanbanDetailEventDecodesTheRunID` — asserts the decode that the old key could never satisfy.
- Full XCTest, iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.5, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`: 1,573 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

title: fix(auth): handle trusted-header and OIDC sign-in honestly
body:
## Linked issue

No upstream issue — this came out of a client/server contract audit rather than a filed bug report. Happy to open one if you would rather have it tracked separately. The raw audit note is [audichuang/hermex#3](https://github.com/audichuang/hermex/issues/3) (written in Chinese); everything relevant is reproduced in English below. Different root cause from #220 ("Can't login to VPS hosted Hermes"), which is an older server returning HTML.

## What changed

- Distinguish trusted-header, OIDC, passkey-only, and password servers instead of treating every password-disabled server as passkey-only.
- Accept a trusted-header server that has already authenticated the request, without attempting a password login.
- Report OIDC as unsupported in the app instead of implying a browser session will carry over.
- Add the copy to the existing 17-language catalog cohort.

## Root cause

The client inferred `auth_enabled == true && password_auth_enabled == false` ⇒ passkeys. Upstream's `is_auth_enabled()` also covers OIDC and trusted-header deployments, and a trusted-header server may already report the request as logged in — a field the client decoded but never consumed.

That inference was copied in three places (`AuthManager.configure()`, `AuthManager.addServer()`, and `OnboardingViewModel`, which additionally hid the password field). The fix replaces all three with one shared decision over the explicit mode and logged-in fields, so no caller can drift again.

## Contract evidence

- Upstream `nesquena/hermes-webui`, read-only local checkout at `ecc47782e3e72a5bf3e848a8f09a2a5a838c71b1` (2026-07-22):
  - `api/routes.py:12142`, `:12152` — `/api/auth/status` returns `oidc_enabled` as its own field, independent of password auth.
  - `api/routes.py:12160` — the trusted branch keys off `is_trusted_auth_enabled()` or a session whose `auth_type == "trusted"`.
  - `api/auth.py:538` — `is_auth_enabled()` returns true for password auth **or** passkeys **or** OIDC **or** trusted-header, which is why the client's "no password ⇒ passkeys" inference was wrong.
- This repo's compatibility pin `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA` is `f1d399b4` (v0.51.85). The checkout above is newer than the pin and is not itself the pin.
- The OIDC entry point creates a browser cookie; that cookie jar is not shared with the app, which is why this PR reports OIDC as unsupported rather than pretending to sign in.

## How it was tested

- Focused: `CustomHeaderAuthManagerTests` (in `HermesMobileTests/CustomHeaderInjectionTests.swift`) — trusted-header server saved without login, trusted-header without a session explains the proxy, OIDC server reports SSO rather than passkeys, and `addServer` accepts an already-authenticated server.
- Full XCTest, iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.5, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`: 1,576 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `jq empty HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`: clean.
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`: clean.
- Pushed SHA verified against `audichuang/hermex` with `git ls-remote`: `4fc004a50885a65764647a95a95200d00f99c9eb`.

## Need to verify

- **No live sign-in proof.** The deployment I can reach has auth disabled, so neither the OIDC nor the trusted-header path was exercised against a real server. The decision boundary is covered by unit tests over the decoded status; the end-to-end flow is not.
- **No signed-build UI walkthrough** for the onboarding screens for the same reason — with auth disabled, the new states are unreachable in the running app. Both new strings are in the catalog in all 17 languages, but they were not seen rendered on device.
- Contract evidence is source-based rather than captured from the wire.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (`oidcEnabled` / `trustedAuthEnabled` / `loggedIn` are optional; older servers that omit them fall back to the previous behavior)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (fields verified against upstream source above)

Built with Claude Code. The diff, the contract reading, the localized copy, and the test output were reviewed before publishing.

title: fix(sessions): isolate invalid rows from list consumers
body:
## Linked issue

No upstream issue — this came out of a client/server contract audit rather than a filed bug report. Happy to open one if you would rather have it tracked separately. The raw audit note is [audichuang/hermex#10](https://github.com/audichuang/hermex/issues/10) (written in Chinese); everything relevant is reproduced in English below.

## What changed

- Decode session-list rows field by field, so one drifting row no longer fails the whole response.
- Keep rows without a usable session ID available to read-only analytics aggregation.
- Filter unusable IDs at the interactive active/archived list consumers, where navigation and mutation need identity.

## Root cause

`SessionsResponse` and `SessionSummary` used the synthesized `Decodable`, so a single type-drifted field in a single row failed the entire session list — the user sees "all my conversations are gone", and pull-to-refresh never recovers it. This is exactly the case `AGENTS.md` hard rule 3 exists for, and `SessionDetail` / `ProjectSummary` in the same file already decode leniently; only the list was missed.

Where to enforce identity was the real decision. Dropping ID-less rows inside the decoder would fix the list but silently undercount Insights, which only aggregates. So the transport projection stays tolerant and identity is required at the two consumers that navigate and mutate.

## Contract evidence

- Upstream `nesquena/hermes-webui`, read-only local checkout at `ecc47782e3e72a5bf3e848a8f09a2a5a838c71b1` (2026-07-22): the server coerces these very fields on its own side rather than trusting them — `_numeric_count()` (`api/routes.py:8351`) is applied to `message_count` and `actual_message_count` at `:8396`–`:8397`, and `_safe_first()` (`api/routes.py:1062`) normalizes identity fields for externally sourced rows at `:1106`–`:1113`. The server hardening the same fields is upstream acknowledging that these rows are not uniformly typed.
- The list merges three sources (sidecar JSON, `state.db` overlay, and CLI sessions), so heterogeneous rows are structural rather than exceptional.
- This repo's compatibility pin `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA` is `f1d399b4` (v0.51.85). The checkout above is newer than the pin and is not itself the pin.

## How it was tested

- Focused: tolerant decoding of a drifted row, active-list filtering, archived-list filtering, and Insights totals that still include ID-less rows.
- Full XCTest, iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.5, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`: 1,574 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

- **No signed-build UI walkthrough**, for the same reason: with a healthy server the before/after screens are identical, so a manual pass would not have distinguished them.

title: fix(sessions): align duplicate behavior with WebUI
body:
## Linked issue

No upstream issue — this came out of a client/server contract audit rather than a filed bug report. Happy to open one if you would rather have it tracked separately. The raw audit note is [audichuang/hermex#25](https://github.com/audichuang/hermex/issues/25) (written in Chinese); everything relevant is reproduced in English below.

## What changed

- Use `/api/session/duplicate` for a real independent copy instead of overloading the branch endpoint.
- Consume the duplicated session the mutation already returns, instead of firing a second detail fetch.
- Match the WebUI by hiding Duplicate for CLI and messaging sessions, with a view-model guard before any request is sent.
- Update the endpoint list in `PROJECT_SPEC.md` and `CONTRACT_TESTS.md` to match.

## Root cause

Duplicate was wired to `/api/session/branch`. Branch means "fork a lineage child from here": the copy loses `tool_calls` and token accounting and lands in the lineage tree as a child of the original, which is not what the menu item promises. Upstream has a separate endpoint for the copy semantics, and the reference web client uses it.

The visibility rule belongs with it: the duplicate endpoint loads the sidecar session document, so a `state.db`-only external session has nothing to copy and would come back as a server 404. The policy therefore lives in `SessionRowActionPolicy` — one predicate shared by the context menu and the view model — rather than in the menu builder alone, so no future caller can send a request the server will reject.

## Contract evidence

Upstream `nesquena/hermes-webui`, read-only local checkout at `ecc47782e3e72a5bf3e848a8f09a2a5a838c71b1` (2026-07-22):

- `api/routes.py:14366` — `POST /api/session/duplicate` exists and takes `session_id`.
- Inside that handler: `Session.load(sid)` returning nothing is answered as **404 "Session not found"**, and subagent sessions are rejected with 400 — which is what a sidecar-less external session would hit.
- The copy is built with `copy.deepcopy(session.messages)` **and** `copy.deepcopy(session.tool_calls)`, and resets `pinned` / `archived` — so `tool_calls` survive a duplicate but not a branch. This is the behavioral difference the PR is about.
- The response is `{"session": copied_session.compact() | {"messages": …}}`, which is why the client can insert the returned session directly instead of re-fetching it.
- This repo's compatibility pin `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA` is `f1d399b4` (v0.51.85). The checkout above is newer than the pin and is not itself the pin.

## How it was tested

- Focused: `SessionListMutationTests` — endpoint selection, insertion of the returned session, and suppression of the request for external sessions.
- Full XCTest, iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.5, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`: 1,573 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- **Signed Debug build on device.** Normally signed Debug build (no `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`), installed and launched on iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.5, signed in to a live deployment, device language zh-Hant. Long-pressing a normal workspace session shows the context menu with Duplicate ("複製") present between Rename and Move to Project, and the rest of the menu (Pin / Rename / Move / Export / Archive / Delete) unchanged. No duplicate was actually performed — see below.
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`: clean.
- Pushed SHA verified against `audichuang/hermex` with `git ls-remote`: `5e30298084c3772c57cedf2acc8eeeabcbbe5c62`.

## Need to verify

- **No live duplicate was performed.** Tapping Duplicate creates a real, persistent session on the server, so the request/response path is covered by unit tests rather than a live call.
- **The hidden case was not observable live.** The deployment I can reach has no CLI or messaging sessions in the list, so I could only confirm that Duplicate *appears* for a normal session; the suppression side is covered at the `SessionRowActionPolicy` and view-model boundary by tests.
- Webhook, API, tool, and cron sources deliberately keep Duplicate, matching current WebUI behavior. If such a session lacks a sidecar document, the server will still answer 404 and the client surfaces that error rather than pre-empting it.

## Related

Touches `SessionListViewModel.swift` and `SessionListMutationTests.swift`, which #266 also touches. The hunks are disjoint and both currently merge cleanly; merging #266 first leaves this one clean, and I will rebase whichever lands second.

## Checklist

- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (endpoint, request key, and response shape verified against upstream source above)
