title: fix(approval): require explicit response success
body:
## Linked issue

No upstream issue — this came out of a client/server contract audit rather than a filed bug report. Happy to open one if you would rather have it tracked separately. The raw audit note is [audichuang/hermex#5](https://github.com/audichuang/hermex/issues/5) (written in Chinese); everything relevant is reproduced in English below.

## What changed

- Inspect the approval response body instead of treating every HTTP 200 as acceptance.
- Keep the pending approval card and surface an error on explicit `ok: false` or on a missing success signal.
- Preserve the existing stale-cleared terminal path.
- Localize the new failure message into the catalog's 17-language cohort.

## Root cause

`ChatPendingActionCoordinator` discarded the response (`_ = try await client.respondApproval(...)`) and `APIClient` only throws on non-2xx. Upstream answers a protective refusal with **HTTP 200 and `ok: false`**, so the client reported success, cleared the card, and left the agent still blocked. `ok` and `staleCleared` were already decoded on `ApprovalRespondResponse` — they simply had no production consumer.

Failure case: two parallel approvals A and B in one session. A is already resolved elsewhere; the user answers the stale A card; the server deliberately declines with `200 + ok: false` and leaves B alone; the app clears the card and then `refreshApprovalPending` brings B back with different content and no explanation.

Because a missing `ok` is indistinguishable from a refusal the client can't interpret, this fails closed rather than assuming success.

## Contract evidence

Upstream `nesquena/hermes-webui`, read-only local checkout at `ecc47782e3e72a5bf3e848a8f09a2a5a838c71b1` (2026-07-22):

- `api/routes.py:15475` routes `POST /api/approval/respond` to `_handle_approval_respond` (`api/routes.py:24000`).
- `api/routes.py:24237` — the terminal return is `j(handler, {"ok": ok, "choice": choice})`, and `api/helpers.py:243` shows `j()` defaults to `status=200`. A refusal is therefore a 200.
- Every return path in that handler carries an explicit `ok`: the refusal branches at `:24092`, `:24113`, `:24131`, `:24149`, `:24164` return `ok: False`, and the success paths at `:24185` / `:24200` return `ok: True`.
- The reference web client does what this PR now does — when the response is not accepted it restores the card with an error instead of clearing it (`static/messages.js:7284`, calling `_restoreFailedApprovalResponse` defined at `:7219`).
- The compatibility pin `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA` (`f1d399b4`, v0.51.85) also makes its only successful 2xx response explicit with `ok: true`, so failing closed on a missing `ok` is safe across the pin and current upstream.

## How it was tested

- Focused: `ChatViewModelSendTests` — explicit `ok: false` keeps the card and explains, and a response with no `ok` field does the same.
- Full XCTest, iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.5, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`, run after the localization commit: **1,574 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`: clean.
- Pushed SHA verified against `audichuang/hermex` with `git ls-remote`: `dec55bf1eadaf828e3b11ff92591747fcfeefbf2`.

## Need to verify

- **No live refusal exercised.** The deployment I can reach had no safe pending approval to answer, so the `200 + ok: false` path is covered by source reading and unit tests, not a captured response.
- **No signed-build UI walkthrough** of the error state, for the same reason — reproducing it needs two parallel approvals on a live agent.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (`ok` and `staleCleared` were already optional; this PR only adds consumers, and treats absence as failure rather than crashing)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (response shape verified against upstream source above)

## AI assistance

Built with Claude Code. The return-path review, the regression tests, the translations, and the test output were reviewed before publishing.

title: fix(models): preserve provider identity when matching
body:
## Linked issue

No upstream issue — this came out of a client/server contract audit rather than a filed bug report. Happy to open one if you would rather have it tracked separately. The raw audit note is [audichuang/hermex#27](https://github.com/audichuang/hermex/issues/27) (written in Chinese); everything relevant is reproduced in English below.

## What changed

- Match a saved model selection across the server's bare and `@provider:` spellings.
- Preserve provider identity when two providers expose the same bare model id.
- Parse named custom-provider prefixes at the final colon, so a provider name containing a colon survives.
- Use the shared matcher for both the default-model checkmark and its accessibility value.

## Root cause

The picker compared raw model ids, but the server prefixes every model outside the active provider as `@provider:<id>`. A default saved in one spelling never matched the row rendered in the other, so the checkmark landed nowhere and the user could not tell which default was active.

Normalizing to the bare id alone would have traded one bug for a worse one: two providers exposing the same bare id would both light up. So the matcher compares provider identity and model id together, and the same helper feeds the accessibility value so VoiceOver cannot disagree with the checkmark.

## Contract evidence

- Upstream `nesquena/hermes-webui`, read-only local checkout at `ecc47782e3e72a5bf3e848a8f09a2a5a838c71b1` (2026-07-22): `api/config.py:2278` `_apply_provider_prefix()` returns the raw ids when the provider is the active one and otherwise rewrites each entry to `@{provider_id}:{model_id}`. It is applied when the catalog groups are built, for both named custom providers (`api/config.py:5404`, whose display name comes from `custom_group["name"]` and whose id is a `custom:`-prefixed string) and the remaining providers (`:5425`) — so a provider name can itself contain a colon, which is why this PR splits at the final one.
- This repo's compatibility pin `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA` is `f1d399b4` (v0.51.85). The checkout above is newer than the pin and is not itself the pin.
- **Observed live** during the simulator pass below: the deployment returns bare `gpt-5.6-*` ids for the active provider alongside `@gemini:`, `@deepseek:`, and `@moa:` prefixed ids — the mixed spelling this PR exists to reconcile.

## How it was tested

- Focused: `ModelCatalogTests` — 4 passed, 0 failed: `testModelSelectionMatchesAcrossTheProviderPrefix`, `testModelSelectionStillSeparatesProvidersSharingABareID`, `testFirstMatchingSelectionPrefersTheExactSpelling`, `testModelSelectionPreservesNamedCustomProviderIdentity`.
- Full XCTest, iPhone 17 Pro Max Simulator, iOS 26.5, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`: 1,576 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- **Signed Debug build on device.** Normally signed Debug build (no `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`), installed and launched on iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 26.5, signed in to a live hermes-webui deployment, device language zh-Hant:
  - Settings → Default Model row reports the resolved default in its accessibility label ("預設模型、gpt-5.6-luna").
  - In the picker, the saved default `GPT 5.6 Luna / gpt-5.6-luna` carries accessibility value "已選取" and shows the checkmark, while the near-miss rows `gpt-5.6-luna-pro` and `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` carry an empty value and no checkmark.
  - The prefixed sections (`@gemini:…`, `@deepseek:…`, `@moa:default`) render alongside the bare active-provider ids; every prefixed row I inspected carried an empty accessibility value, i.e. no spurious second selection.
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`: clean.
- Pushed SHA verified against `audichuang/hermex` with `git ls-remote`: `e1da13f0a32f2f6e8d810d6dfa524d80881f2f3f`.

## Need to verify

- **The cross-provider default was not saved live.** Selecting a default that lives under a non-active provider writes to the real server, so the live pass only confirms the active-provider case renders correctly; the prefixed-default case is covered by unit tests.
- **No colon-in-provider-name deployment.** No reachable server defines a custom provider whose name contains a colon, so that regression case is source-backed and synthetic.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no wire model changed; this is client-side matching over already-decoded ids)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (prefix format verified against upstream source and observed on the wire)

## AI assistance

Built with Claude Code. The matcher, the regression tests, the simulator pass, and the test output were reviewed before publishing.

title: Fix saving transcript videos to Photos
body:
## Summary
- import transcript videos into Photos from a staged file URL instead of an in-memory `Data` resource
- keep the staged file alive until PhotoKit completes, then clean it up without touching the preview file
- surface a clear error when the preview video is no longer available
- add opt-in PhotoKit integration coverage for valid and malformed videos

## Why
PhotoKit can reject the data-based video creation request with `PHPhotosErrorDomain` code 3300 (`changeNotSupported`) even when the MP4 itself is valid and playable. The file-URL resource path is supported for simple movie imports and succeeds with the reported H.264/AAC MP4.

## Verification
- Full XCTest suite: 1,575 passed, 0 failed (2 opt-in Photos-mutating tests skipped) on iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.4.1 simulator
- Opt-in PhotoKit integration: generated valid H.264 MP4 passed; malformed MP4 rejected with `invalidResource`
- Exact reported 3.8 MB H.264/AAC reel passed the PhotoKit import test
- `git diff --check` passed

title: feat(composer): voice-first input mode with auto-send and contextual STT
body:
## Use case

Current voice input requires: tap mic → speak → tap stop → transcribe → tap send. Five steps for every voice message. For users who primarily interact by voice, this friction is too high.

Desired behavior: composer defaults to a "hold to speak" mode — long-press to record, release to auto-send. Like WeChat voice messages but with STT transcription + auto-send to the agent.

## Implemented behavior

### Voice-First Mode (opt-in via Settings toggle)

1. **Default voice bar**: When enabled, composer shows a "按住说话" (Hold to speak) bar instead of the text field, with a hint "轻触切换键盘" (Tap to switch to keyboard).
2. **Long-press to record**: Hold the bar → starts recording via server STT. Live transcript shown above the bar.
3. **Release to send**: When finger lifts, recording stops → server transcription completes → message auto-sends.
4. **Short tap to switch**: Tap the bar briefly (<0.3s) → switches to standard text composer with attachments/model picker intact.
5. **Switch back to voice**: In text mode, a prominent blue capsule button [🎤 语音] appears in the toolbar for easy switching back.

### Server-First STT (multilingual)

- Voice-first mode forces `providerPreference = .serverFirst` to use Whisper (via hermes-webui `/api/transcribe`).
- Whisper auto-detects language — supports Chinese, English, and code-switching (中英混合) natively.
- On-device `SFSpeechRecognizer` is preserved as fallback when server is unreachable.
- Hot-word injection via `contextualStrings` (iOS 17+) still applies when on-device fallback kicks in.

### Contextual Hot Words

- Injects project-specific terms into STT recognition to reduce misheard technical vocabulary.
- Sources: built-in Hermes ecosystem terms + user-configurable comma-separated list in Settings.
- Extraction patterns: camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, dotted.names, ALL_CAPS identifiers.

## Scope and non-goals

**In scope:**
- "Hold to speak" bar with long-press/tap gesture discrimination
- Server STT (Whisper) for multilingual support
- Auto-send on release after transcription completes
- Composer mode switch (voice-first ↔ text) with prominent toggle
- Hot-word injection + context provider
- Settings toggle + hot-word list config
- Chinese UI localization

**Not in scope (covered by the full voice-mode epic #36):**
- TTS playback of agent replies
- Full-duplex audio / AEC
- Barge-in (interrupting agent)
- Full-screen voice overlay
- Background/lock-screen/pocket mode
- Continuous always-listening mode (no press required)

## Relationship to #36

This is a **standalone input-side improvement** that coexists with the planned voice conversation mode (#36, slices #248–#257). It modifies the existing composer default state; #36 introduces a separate full-screen overlay. No conflicts — both can ship independently.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| New: `ComposerVoiceFirstMode.swift` | Silence timer state machine + auto-send logic |
| New: `ComposerSTTContextProvider.swift` | Hot-word extraction from session context |
| New: `ComposerVoiceFirstBar.swift` | "按住说话" UI + `ComposerSwitchToVoiceBar` |
| `ComposerVoiceInputController.swift` | `contextualStrings` injection + `onPartialTranscript` + `onFinalTranscript` callbacks |
| `ChatComposerView.swift` | Voice-first mode conditional rendering + mode switching + auto-send wiring |
| `SettingsView.swift` | Voice-First Input toggle + Hot Words text field |

## Known limitations

- English accuracy depends on Whisper model size (recommend `whisper-large-v3-turbo` via Groq for best results).
- Server STT adds ~1-3s latency after release (recording upload + transcription). Acceptable over Tailscale/LAN.
- Hot words only apply to on-device fallback path (`contextualStrings` is an Apple API).
- No streaming partial results in server mode — user sees transcript only after full transcription completes.

## Estimated effort

~1.5 days with AI-assisted coding (completed).

title: feat(chat): redesign the model and provider picker
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a stacked follow-up to #263. It intentionally builds on that PR's native chat palette and surface work. Please review/merge #263 first; once it lands, this PR's effective diff collapses to the seven model-picker commits.

## What this changes

This redesign turns the model picker from a flat utility sheet into a native, provider-aware selection surface that scales to a large self-hosted catalog without changing any server identity or routing behavior.

- Rebuilds the sheet around two independent axes: **All / Favorites / Recent** and **provider scope**. Changing provider scope filters the list; it never silently selects a model.
- Adds one search field across model names, exact model IDs, provider presentation names, and immutable provider IDs.
- Keeps **Add Custom Model** as a separate, explicit flow instead of mixing an action row into search results.
- Adds provider favorites, scoped per server, while preserving the existing provider-aware model favorite/recents keys.
- Automatically reconciles stale provider scopes after catalog changes and scrolls the active provider into view.
- Introduces bundled, vetted provider artwork with a deterministic native fallback and no runtime logo/CDN requests.
- Adds a native long-press provider menu and editor for a local display name or custom image. The immutable server provider ID remains visible and unchanged.
- Handles Photos/file imports defensively: bounded input, background downsampling, 512px PNG output, and atomic local persistence.
- Improves Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels/actions, 44pt targets, non-color selection cues, light/dark contrast, and reduced-motion behavior.

## Before and after — light mode

The collage walks through the original picker, the redesigned all-provider catalog, provider-scoped results, favorites/recents, search, the long-press menu, and the provider editor.

![Model and provider picker before/after in light mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/refs/heads/feat/model-provider-picker/docs/design/screenshots/model-picker-before-after-light.png)

## Before and after — dark mode

The same states were captured independently in dark mode to verify hierarchy, selection treatment, provider artwork, editor surfaces, and contrast.

![Model and provider picker before/after in dark mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ildunari/hermex/refs/heads/feat/model-provider-picker/docs/design/screenshots/model-picker-before-after-dark.png)

## Interaction and identity model

| Area | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog navigation | Flat model list | Independent model-view and provider-scope controls |
| Search | Model-oriented | Matches model display name, exact ID, provider name, and provider ID |
| Favorites / recents | Model shortcuts | Provider-aware model shortcuts plus server-scoped provider favorites |
| Active provider | Easy to lose in a long strip | Automatically revealed without reordering the server catalog |
| Provider identity | Raw IDs leak into presentation | Human-readable local presentation kept separate from immutable routing identity |
| Provider artwork | Generic presentation | Vetted bundled marks, custom local artwork, and deterministic fallback |
| Provider editing | None | Native context menu and staged local presentation editor |
| Custom models | Mixed into the main surface | Separate explicit sheet and action |
| Accessibility | Basic labels | Larger targets, richer VoiceOver actions, non-color state, and XXXL coverage |

Provider names and images are presentation-only preferences keyed by `(serverAccountID, providerID)`. They do not rewrite API credentials, provider configuration, model IDs, session history, or requests sent to the server.

## Design and review evidence

- [Native picker design and interaction specification](https://github.com/ildunari/hermex/blob/feat/model-provider-picker/docs/design/model-provider-picker-native.md)
- [Adversarial visual and behavior review](https://github.com/ildunari/hermex/blob/feat/model-provider-picker/docs/design/model-provider-picker-adversarial-review.md)
- Provider asset licensing is included in `HermesMobile/Resources/ThirdPartyNotices/`; third-party marks remain the property of their respective owners and are used only to identify configured providers.

## Verification

- Full XCTest suite: **1,662 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**
- Focused picker/theme tests: **32 passed, 0 failed**
- Generic iOS Simulator compile: passed with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Signed simulator visual QA was captured in both light and dark mode; the checked-in collages above cover the major picker states and provider editor.

The source implementation checkpoint also passed five deterministic picker UI tests, including provider scoping, search, favorites/recents, long-press editing, and Accessibility XXXL. This upstream-shaped branch deliberately does not add an XCUITest target because upstream CI builds unsigned test products; the behavioral coverage remains in unit tests and the checked-in simulator evidence.

## Review order

1. Review and merge #263.
2. Rebase or refresh this branch against the updated `master` if GitHub does not collapse the stacked diff automatically.
3. Review the seven picker-specific commits and the visual/design evidence in this PR.

title: Server First dictation auto-stops and transcribes after 60 seconds
body:
## Context

Long-form dictation in Server First mode stops automatically at approximately 60 seconds and begins transcription even though the user has not tapped Stop.

Investigation found that this is client-controlled behavior introduced with Server First STT: `ComposerVoiceInputController` schedules a 60-second task that invokes `stopServerRecordingAndTranscribe()`. The same path records uncompressed 16 kHz mono PCM to a `.wav` file.

The current `/api/transcribe` route accepts a multipart `file`, preserves its extension, and enforces the configurable server upload ceiling—20 MB by default.

## Current behavior

- Server First recording automatically stops after 60 seconds.
- Transcription starts without user action.
- Captured audio is linear PCM in a WAV container.
- On-device dictation remains subject to `SFSpeechRecognizer` lifecycle limits.

## Expected behavior

While the composer remains active, Server First recording continues until the user stops or cancels it. Capture uses compressed AAC in an M4A container so normal long-form recordings remain comfortably below the server upload limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server First does not automatically stop or transcribe at 60 seconds.
- [ ] Tapping Stop ends recording and submits it to `/api/transcribe`.
- [ ] Cancel and existing composer/app lifecycle cleanup remain cancellation-safe and do not upload discarded audio.
- [ ] Server First captures mono AAC in an `.m4a` file with a controlled speech-appropriate bitrate.
- [ ] The multipart upload supplies the `.m4a` filename and successfully decodes the existing tolerant transcription response.
- [ ] A recording exceeding 60 seconds can be transcribed successfully.
- [ ] On-device dictation behavior and Apple Speech handling are unchanged.
- [ ] Temporary audio is removed after success, failure, or cancellation.
- [ ] No new dependency or server endpoint is introduced.

## Validation plan

- Revalidate `POST /api/transcribe` against current upstream or the maintainer's running server.
- Add tests covering AAC/M4A settings and the absence of a 60-second automatic transition.
- Test explicit Stop, cancel, failure, and cleanup behavior.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- On a physical device, record for at least 90 seconds in Server First mode, confirm it continues until Stop, and verify the full transcript reaches the draft.
- Manually verify cancel, backgrounding, and On-device-only behavior.

## Non-goals

- Changing or restarting Apple `SFSpeechRecognizer` tasks.
- Voice Conversation Mode work tracked by #249.
- Voice-first auto-send behavior from #271.
- Background or lock-screen recording.
- Changing `/api/transcribe` or its configured upload limit.

title: feat(composer): voice-first input mode with hold-to-speak gestures
body:
## Summary

Implements voice-first composer mode — a lightweight alternative to the full voice-mode overlay (#36). When enabled in Settings, the composer area replaces the text input with a "Hold to speak" bar that supports gesture-based interaction.

Adds Volcengine (ByteDance/Doubao) streaming ASR as a dictation provider, for low-latency Chinese recognition with live partial results.

Closes #271

## Interaction Design

### Basic Flow (model idle)

| Gesture | Action | Visual Cue |
|---------|--------|------------|
| Long press | Start recording | Blue background + waveform animation + "Listening…" |
| Release | Send transcribed message | Bar returns to default |
| Swipe up + release | Cancel recording | Red background + ✕ + "Release to cancel" |
| Short tap | Switch to keyboard input | Text composer appears |

### During Model Streaming

| Gesture | Action | Visual Cue |
|---------|--------|------------|
| Release (no swipe) | **Interrupt** — stop current response + send as new message | "Listening… release to send" + hint "↑ Cancel ↓ Queue" |
| Swipe down + release | **Queue** — wait for response to finish, then send as new turn | Orange background + "↓ Release to queue" + "Send after response completes" |
| Swipe up + release | Cancel recording | Red background + ✕ |

### Design Decisions

- **Default during streaming = interrupt**: natural voice semantics — "I spoke, you stop". Queue is an easter-egg for power users who discover the swipe-down gesture.
- **Easter egg philosophy**: voice-first mode itself is opt-in (Settings toggle). Swipe gestures are undocumented power features users discover gradually.
- **Message visibility**: steer/interrupt/queue all show user message as a normal chat bubble (uses temporary UserDefaults swap instead of noEcho slash commands).

## Dictation Providers

The `Dictation Provider` picker in Settings selects which STT backend voice input uses. Voice-first mode honours the picked provider; when Volcengine is not selected it defaults to server STT for multilingual support (Apple's on-device recogniser is single-language-locked, while Whisper auto-detects and handles 中英混合 code-switching).

| Provider | Transport | Live partial results | Credential |
|----------|-----------|----------------------|------------|
| Server first | Records a WAV, uploads once on release | No | none (uses your Hermes server) |
| On-device first / only | `SFSpeechAudioBufferRecognitionRequest` | Yes | none |
| Volcengine streaming | WebSocket, 200 ms PCM frames | Yes | API Key |

### Volcengine setup

Only an **API Key** is required — no AppID, no Access Token, no secret. The key is
stored in `UserDefaults` on the device and is never committed; nothing is hardcoded
in the repo.

- **Get a key:** https://console.volcengine.com/speech/new/setting/apikeys?projectName=default
- **Enable the service first:** 豆包语音 → 语音识别 → 流式语音识别 (大模型). A key without this
  entitlement authenticates but returns no result.
- **Protocol docs:** https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6561/1354869

Notes on the values this PR uses:

- Endpoint `wss://openspeech.bytedance.com/api/v3/sauc/bigmodel_async` — the optimised
  bidirectional streaming mode, which only pushes a packet when the result changes.
- Resource ID defaults to `volc.seedasr.sauc.duration` (豆包流式语音识别模型 2.0, 小时版) and is
  overridable in Settings. Use `volc.seedasr.sauc.concurrent` for a concurrency-based plan,
  or the `volc.bigasr.*` equivalents for model 1.0.
- Auth is the **new** console contract: a single `X-Api-Key`. The legacy
  `X-Api-App-Key` + `X-Api-Access-Key` pair is not used.

A **Test Connection** button under the key field performs the WebSocket handshake plus a
ping and reports the failing domain/code, so a bad key or a blocked network is
distinguishable from a client bug without reading device logs.

## New Files

- `ComposerVoiceFirstMode.swift` — silence timer state machine, phase management
- `ComposerVoiceFirstBar.swift` — "Hold to speak" bar UI with DragGesture-based interaction
- `ComposerSTTContextProvider.swift` — hot-word extraction (currently unreferenced, see below)
- `VolcengineStreamingSTT.swift` — WebSocket client for the Volcengine binary protocol
- `VolcengineSTTSettings.swift` — key/resource-id storage and configuration builder

## Modified Files

- `ComposerVoiceInputController.swift` — added `contextualStrings`, `onPartialTranscript`, `onFinalTranscript`; Volcengine capture path (downsample to 16 kHz mono, accumulate 200 ms packets)
- `ChatComposerView.swift` — conditional body render, auto-send watchers, gesture action routing via `voiceFirstApplyPendingAction()`, live transcript preview card
- `SettingsView.swift` — Voice-First Input toggle, Dictation Provider picker, Volcengine key field + Test Connection
- `AppTheme.swift` — `ComposerSTTProviderPreference` / `ComposerSTTProviderPolicy` provider ordering and fallback

## Notable Fixes

- **Sequence-number frames.** Payload size was read from a fixed offset. When the server
  sets flags `0b0001`/`0b0011` the four bytes after the header are a sequence number
  instead, so the size came from the wrong place. Sequence numbers are small integers, so
  the bogus length still passed the bounds check and produced a garbage slice — every
  frame failed to parse while looking superficially valid. Header size and the
  sequence-number flag are now honoured when locating the payload.
- **Audio converter lifetime.** `AVAudioConverter` was a local, so it was deallocated once
  setup returned and resampling state was lost. It is now owned by the controller, each
  input buffer is supplied exactly once, and output is accumulated into 6400-byte
  (200 ms @ 16 kHz) packets.
- **Server-initiated close.** A `finishing` state distinguishes the server closing the
  socket after finalising a transcript from a real connection failure. Success is only
  reported when a transcript actually arrived, so failures cannot surface as empty results.
- **Capture/WebSocket ordering.** Audio capture is deferred until the socket is ready,
  instead of dropping the first frames.

Diagnostic counters (frames sent/dropped, packets received/parsed, last message type) are
included in failure messages so one log line separates a capture problem from a transport
or parsing problem.

## Behaviour Change

`ComposerVoiceAudioSessionConfiguration.mode` moves from `.measurement` to
`.videoRecording`. This affects every dictation provider, not just Volcengine, since all
three share the session configuration. The no-ducking contract the accompanying test
guards is unchanged: `.mixWithOthers` stays set and `.duckOthers` stays absent.

## Removed

The **Hot Words** settings field is gone. It asked users to hand-maintain a
comma-separated term list to work around recognition accuracy, which the streaming
provider handles well enough in practice. `ComposerSTTContextProvider` and
`VoiceFirstModeSettings.hotWordsKey` are left in place but unreferenced —
`contextualStrings` on the controller still feeds both `SFSpeechRecognizer` and the
Volcengine hotword payload, so wiring a source back in is a one-line change.

## Known Limitations

- **Server STT is not streaming.** It records to a file and uploads on release, so there
  are no live partial results and there is a 60 s cap. Because voice-first's silence
  timer is driven by partial transcripts, **silence auto-send does not fire under Server
  first** — release-to-send still works. Streaming providers (on-device, Volcengine) are
  unaffected.
- **On-device stops at the first endpoint.** `SFSpeechRecognizer` finalises on its own
  endpointing and the task has its own duration ceiling, so continuous hands-free
  dictation ends after one utterance rather than auto-continuing.
- **On-device requires an installed offline model.** `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true`
  plus the `supportsOnDeviceRecognition` gate means unsupported locales silently fall back
  to server STT. Recognition locale follows `Locale.current`, so a device set to English
  will not transcribe Chinese.

## Testing

- [x] `xcodebuild build` succeeds for iOS Simulator and device (0 errors)
- [x] XCTest suite passes
- [x] Installed on iPhone 13 and iPhone 17 Pro (signed Debug build)
- [x] Volcengine streaming verified end-to-end on device by the maintainer: live partial
      results reach the composer and the final transcript is sent
- [x] Hold to speak → release → message sent correctly
- [x] Swipe up → cancel works (recording discarded)
- [x] During streaming: release → interrupt (stops response + new reply)
- [x] During streaming: swipe down → queue (waits for completion, then sends)
- [x] Short tap → switches to text mode
- [x] Blue pill "Switch to voice" button returns to voice mode
- [x] No credentials in the diff: the only Volcengine string literals are the public
      resource ID, the endpoint, and the UserDefaults key names
- [x] i18n: all strings use `String(localized:)` with English defaults
- [ ] On-device provider not re-verified after the changes above (Volcengine was the focus)

title: Add server-backed saved prompts to the chat composer
body:
## Use case

I use Hermex for repeated owner workflows that begin with the same substantial instruction. On iPhone, retrieving those prompts from Notes, another chat, or text replacement adds friction and makes it easy to send an outdated version.

Hermes WebUI now exposes a saved-prompts library, and the Hermex repository already identifies both the upstream `prompts` route group and a future “Mobile command launcher.” The iOS app currently has no way to browse or use those saved prompts.

The useful outcome is not another iOS-only prompt store. It is mobile access to the server-backed prompt library so the same prompts remain available across Hermex and the WebUI.

## Proposed behavior

Add a **Saved Prompts** entry point in or near the chat composer.

For an initial focused slice:

- Fetch and display saved prompts from the connected Hermes WebUI server.
- Support basic search when the library is more than a short list.
- Tapping a prompt inserts its content into the composer as an editable draft.
- Never auto-send a selected prompt. The user should be able to review, edit, add attachments, and choose the model/profile/workspace before sending.
- Keep the library server-backed and profile/server-aware rather than creating a separate local iOS source of truth.
- If the connected server does not support the prompts endpoint, hide or disable the affordance with a clear compatibility message rather than breaking the composer.

Creating, editing, deleting, folders/tags, variables, favorites, widgets, and Siri integration can be separate follow-up slices. Read/select/insert would provide the core value without turning the first implementation into a prompt-management subsystem.

## Acceptance outcomes

- A user can open Saved Prompts from the chat composer and see prompts stored on the connected server.
- A user can search or select a saved prompt and have its text inserted into the composer.
- Selecting a prompt never sends it automatically.
- Inserted text remains fully editable and follows the existing chat start/send path.
- Prompt data does not leak between configured servers or profiles.
- Older or incompatible servers degrade gracefully without affecting normal chat.
- Focused API decoding, view-model, insertion, server-isolation, and unsupported-server tests are included.

## Upstream dependency notes

This depends on the Hermes WebUI `prompts` route group (saved-prompts library), which the repository’s `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` currently lists as new/unclassified. Please validate the endpoint and JSON shapes against the pinned upstream source before implementation, following the repository’s just-in-time validation rule.

Related existing product direction: `PROJECT_SPEC.md` lists a future **Mobile command launcher** for quick saved commands/templates. This request proposes the smallest useful server-backed slice of that direction.

title: fix(chat): keep scroll position when a turn-end reload widens the transcript window
body:
## The bug

Wait for a response to finish while scrolled up in a long session and you get dumped at the very top of the transcript.

## Mechanism

Transcript row identity is positional on purpose — `transcript:<messagesOffset + loadedIndex>` — so **Load earlier** can prepend a page without moving already-visible rows.

The problem is mid-session reloads reusing that numbering with a *different* offset:

1. When a turn completes, the `.done` payload (or the fallback completion refresh via `loadMessages(expandRenderable: true)`) can return a **wider window** than the one on screen — a smaller `_messages_offset`, or no offset at all (which resolves to 0).
2. `applyReloadedMessages` only preserved the current offset when the reload offset **grew** (the load-earlier merge). A shrunken offset fell through to `updateOlderMessagePagination`, which adopted it.
3. Every renderID shifts → SwiftUI treats it as all-rows-deleted/all-rows-inserted and remounts the list → the reader's frozen pixel offset now shows the start of the session.

`ChatScrollPolicy` is not at fault — it correctly refuses to auto-follow once the reader scrolls up. The content underneath the viewport changed identity.

## The fix

Treat an on-screen transcript as a **reconcile, not a reopen**. When a reload comes back with a smaller offset but its window still contains the first on-screen message, trim the widened head, splice the server-authoritative tail, and keep the current offset — on-screen renderIDs never shift. Cold opens still widen normally, and non-overlapping reloads (truncation/compaction rewrote history) still fully replace the window.

One new helper (`trimmingReloadedMessages`) mirroring the existing `mergingReloadedMessages` growth path; both `.done` and the completion refresh funnel through `applyReloadedMessages`, so one change covers both triggers.

## Tests

- `testCompletedStreamSessionKeepsCurrentOffsetWhenDoneReturnsWidenedWindow` — `.done` widens to offset 0; on-screen rows keep offset 2 and their renderIDs.
- `testCompletedStreamSessionKeepsCurrentOffsetWhenDoneOmitsOffset` — `.done` without `_messages_offset`; same preservation.
- `testReloadWithoutOverlapStillReplacesTranscript` — rewritten history still replaces the window fully.
- Existing growth-merge test (`testCompletedStreamSessionPreservesExpandedTranscriptWhenDoneReturnsLatestWindow`) still passes — the load-earlier contract is untouched.

`HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests`: 145 tests, 0 failures, TEST SUCCEEDED.

Possibly related to the reading experience behind #213, but this is a defect fix, not that preference.

title: Git Actions setting does not hide the turn-end commit and file-change controls
body:
## Context

Settings → Chat Page → **Git Actions** (`SectionVisibilitySettings.chatGitKey`, default ON) was added in #190 to hide chat git surfaces. It currently gates only two of the four.

Reported here as a missing setting. It is not missing — it is incomplete. The reporter turned it off, still saw a "Commit & Push" button, and concluded no toggle existed. Their described behavior ("appears when the repo has uncommitted changes", "keep the tree clean and it auto-hides") matches the *inline* button, not the toolbar menu.

## Current behavior

Gated by `showsGitControls`:

- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:729` — toolbar git menu
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:716` — composer branch picker

**Not** gated:

- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:951` `inlineCommitContext` — the inline "Commit & Push" button under the latest assistant turn. Guard is `hasRepository && activeStreamID == nil && latest role == "assistant" && (hasCommittableChanges || isCommitting)`.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:966` `turnChangesRecapSummary` — the turn-end "File changes" recap card (#316). Same guard minus the commit condition.

Both render via `ChatTranscriptView.swift:403` (`turnChangesCard`) and `:415` (`inlineCommitButton`).

The footnote at `SettingsView.swift:309` says *"Covers both the git menu in the chat toolbar and the branch picker in the composer"* — accurate today, and precisely why the setting reads as narrower than its name.

## Expected behavior

With Git Actions OFF, chat shows no git surface: no toolbar menu, no branch picker, no inline Commit & Push, no File-changes recap. With it ON, nothing changes from today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `inlineCommitContext` returns `nil` when `showsGitControls` is `false`.
2. `turnChangesRecapSummary` returns `nil` when `showsGitControls` is `false`.
3. Toggling the setting while a chat is open updates both surfaces without leaving the view (`@AppStorage` already drives this; do not add manual refresh plumbing).
4. Footnote reads: **"Hides the git menu, branch picker, and commit controls."**
5. The new footnote string is added to `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` for all 17 shipped languages, and the stale string is removed. This repo does **not** auto-extract on build — see `docs/agents/i18n.md`, including the byte-exact serialization rules and the parsed-subtree diff check.
6. With the toggle ON and a dirty git workspace, both surfaces appear exactly as they do today.

## Implementation note

Both are `private var` computed properties on `ChatView`, so they are not directly unit-testable. Extract the decision into a pure, testable helper taking the visibility flag plus the existing inputs, and have both properties call it. Keep the seam small — this is a guard clause, not an abstraction layer.

## Validation plan

- Unit tests for the extracted helper: toggle off suppresses both; toggle on preserves each existing guard condition (no repo, active stream, non-assistant latest turn, clean tree, commit in flight).
- `LocalizationCatalogTests` must stay green (it fails on empty values for shipped languages).
- Full XCTest suite via `test_sim`, scheme `HermesMobile`, sim iPhone 17.
- Simulator pass in a git workspace with uncommitted changes: send a message, let the turn finish, confirm the inline button and recap card appear; turn Git Actions off in Settings, return to chat, confirm all four surfaces are gone; turn it back on and confirm they return.

## Non-goals

- Basic-auth support for password-protected `hermes-webui`. The reporter's "Web server forbids write" error is correct behavior from `gitWriteAvailability`, and is a separate concern.
- Suppressing git status polling while the toggle is off. `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel` still refreshes; that is a performance question worth its own issue, not part of this fix.
- Any new setting. This issue adds none.
- Git surfaces outside chat (Workspace tab, `GitCommitView`). The setting is scoped to the Chat Page section and stays that way.

title: Product parity: session states, Projects, worktrees, and session organization
body:
## Context
Hermex is the independent native iOS client for `hermes-webui`. This issue is a product-level request for better parity and navigation between Hermex and the desktop WebUI, without prescribing an implementation.

Existing related issue: #212 — Projects created in Hermex show as plain chat sessions in desktop WebUI.

## User goal
Make sessions, Projects, and Git worktrees understandable and navigable as one coherent workspace model across Hermex and the desktop WebUI.

## Requested capabilities

### 1. Filter sessions by state
Provide a clear session-list filter for the operational state of a session, for example:
- All
- Running / streaming
- Waiting for input or approval
- Completed / idle
- Failed / interrupted

The exact state vocabulary should follow the server contract. Unknown or unavailable state data should fail gracefully rather than hiding sessions.

### 2. Projects are consistent across clients
Projects created in Hermex should appear as Projects in the desktop WebUI, and Projects created in the desktop WebUI should be visible in Hermex.

The synchronization should preserve, where supported:
- stable project identity;
- project name;
- color;
- profile / account scope;
- session membership.

Please first verify whether the current issue is server data, profile scoping, cache invalidation, or desktop rendering. Do not create a second incompatible Project store.

### 3. Worktrees inside Projects
Represent Git worktrees as children of a Project when the server can identify them:

```text
Project
├── main worktree
├── feature/example
└── bugfix/example
```

The UI should distinguish the main checkout, linked worktrees, non-Git folders, and unavailable/deleted paths.

### 4. Sessions inside worktrees
Show sessions under the worktree from which they were created or to which they are associated:

```text
Project
└── Worktree
    ├── Session A
    └── Session B
```

Sessions without a resolvable Project or worktree must remain accessible in an explicit fallback section.

### 5. HD-like navigation
Aim for a navigation model similar to the desktop WebUI:
- Projects as first-class navigation items;
- expandable worktrees below Projects;
- sessions below worktrees;
- clear counts and state indicators;
- no duplicate or misleading plain-chat representation;
- consistent behavior on iPhone and desktop.

## Constraints
- Hermex remains an independent iOS client; this request does not ask for a rewrite of `hermes-webui`.
- Preserve tolerant decoding and compatibility with older servers.
- Do not invent new API fields without first documenting the required server contract.
- Keep profile/account isolation explicit.
- Preserve access to sessions whose workspace or worktree has been deleted.

## Suggested implementation order
1. Verify and document the server-side data contract and reproduce #212.
2. Add or correct session-state filtering.
3. Fix Project synchronization/rendering across clients.
4. Add the Project → worktree → session hierarchy.
5. Add end-to-end tests and manual iPhone/desktop validation.

## Acceptance criteria
- A maintainer can identify the authoritative source for Projects, worktrees, sessions, and state.
- A Project created from either client is either rendered as the same Project in the other client or the limitation is explicitly documented.
- Sessions can be filtered by verified operational state without disappearing because of missing/unknown fields.
- Worktrees and their sessions are grouped predictably, with a usable fallback for unresolved paths.
- Existing session actions, profile isolation, archived sessions, and older-server compatibility remain intact.
- The work is split into reviewable PRs rather than one unbounded change.

## Questions for maintainers
- Should the server expose an explicit Project/worktree/session tree, or should clients derive part of it from existing fields?
- What is the canonical identity and scope of a Project across profiles?
- Which session states are stable enough to expose as user-facing filters?
- Should this be implemented first in `hermes-webui`, Hermex, or both in coordinated changes?

title: Default-model picker loses provider identity when saving and marking selection
body:
## Summary

PR #269 merged provider-aware model matching, but the Settings default-model flow still discards provider identity at both the write boundary and the selected-row projection. A same-named/slash-qualified model can be saved through the wrong provider, and the picker can show the wrong provider row as selected.

## Current source

Current `master` includes PR #269 at merge commit `7f6b4290d00af3c407f30ba96c6ca7468bec276e`.

- `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/DefaultModelPickerView.swift:145-148` calls `save(model.id)` and drops `model.providerID`.
- `DefaultModelPickerView.swift:192-194` calls `matchesSelection(..., providerID: nil)` for both the pending selection and server default.
- `DefaultModelPickerView.swift:210-213` receives `ModelsResponse.activeProvider` but does not retain it.
- `DefaultModelPickerView.swift:240-243` calls `saveDefaultModel(model:)` without a provider.
- `HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+ServerPanels.swift:19-24` encodes only `DefaultModelRequest(model:)`, although current Hermes WebUI accepts `{model, provider}`.

Hermes WebUI deliberately leaves slash-qualified model IDs unprefixed in `_apply_provider_prefix`, while its dedup pass may prefix one of two provider rows that share the same ID. Model text alone is therefore not a stable routing identity.

## Impact

1. Selecting a catalog row such as a Nous `anthropic/...` model without its provider can be resolved/persisted through another provider that accepts the same slash-qualified spelling.
2. When duplicate model IDs force Core to prefix the active provider's row, the picker can tick an inactive bare row and leave the true default unticked.
3. VoiceOver uses the same predicate, so its “Selected” state can be wrong in exactly the same way.

## Fix shape

- Retain `response.activeProvider` when loading the catalog.
- Carry `model.providerID` through the tapped-row save state.
- Extend `saveDefaultModel` / `DefaultModelRequest` to include an optional provider and send it for catalog selections.
- Match the persisted `defaultModel` with `activeProvider`; match the in-flight selection with the provider of the tapped row.
- Preserve custom-model entry as an explicit providerless/manual path unless the UI collects a provider.

## Acceptance tests

- Request-body test proves a catalog-row save sends both model and provider.
- Same bare/slash ID on two providers saves through the tapped provider.
- Exactly one visual checkmark and one accessibility Selected value appear for the active default.
- Active-provider row can be `@provider:model` after dedup without selecting an inactive bare duplicate.
- Ollama/OpenRouter colon-bearing model IDs and named custom providers remain distinct.
- Failed save restores the prior provider-aware selected row.

Related: merged PR #269.

title: Onboarding keeps stale auth status after server URL or header edits
body:
## Summary

PR #265 added honest trusted-header/OIDC onboarding behavior, but `OnboardingViewModel` keeps the probed `authStatus` when the user edits the server URL or custom headers. The form can therefore hide the password field using stale trusted-header state, skip the required re-probe, and then fail against the newly entered password-protected server with no way to provide the requested password.

## Current source

Current `master` includes PR #265 at merge commit `f938f5bfbb47bd75d31511c4efc70f8ea670501c`.

- `HermesMobile/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingViewModel.swift:9-12` stores mutable `serverURLString`, `customHeaders`, and cached `authStatus` independently.
- `isPasswordRequired` at lines 29-37 hides the field when cached status says the client is already signed in.
- `testConnection` at lines 39-63 populates `authStatus` for the current URL/headers.
- `connect` at lines 65-98 re-probes only when `authStatus == nil`.
- No URL/header mutation path invalidates `authStatus`, `connectionMessage`, or the derived presentation state.

## Reproduction

1. Enter a trusted-header server and headers, then Test Connection. The probe reports already signed in and the password field hides.
2. Edit the URL or headers to point at a password-protected server.
3. Tap Connect without retesting.
4. The stale status remains non-nil, so `connect()` skips the probe and the form remains shaped for the old server. `AuthManager.configure` then rejects the current server/password state while the password control can still be hidden.

## Fix shape

Bind `authStatus` to the exact normalized connection identity that produced it (URL plus canonical custom-header set), or invalidate it whenever either editable input changes. Clear stale success/error copy at the same boundary. `connect()` must re-probe when the current identity differs from the probed identity.

## Acceptance tests

- Trusted-header probe → URL changes to password server → password field becomes available and Connect re-probes.
- Trusted-header probe → custom header changes/removal → stale signed-in state is discarded.
- OIDC-only/passwordless status is similarly invalidated after identity edits.
- Whitespace-only/canonically equivalent edits do not cause unnecessary state churn if the implementation normalizes identity.
- The connection result from an older in-flight probe cannot overwrite state for a newer URL/header generation.

Related: merged PR #265 and the exact-head Greptile finding present before merge.

title: fix(models): persist and match the default model with its provider
body:
Fixes #284

## Linked issue

Follow-up to merged #269. nesquena-hermes reviewed that head as **changes needed**; the two provider-identity gaps were still on `master` after the squash (`7f6b429`) and were filed as #284.

## What changed

- Catalog-row save now carries `model.providerID` through `save` → `saveDefaultModel` → `DefaultModelRequest`. A providerless custom-model save still sends the bare `{model}` body (synthesized `Encodable` omits nil).
- `loadModels()` retains `response.activeProvider`. The stored default is matched against it when the spelling is bare; a stored `@provider:` spelling stays authoritative via the row's own `providerID` (not a `lastIndex` pre-split, which turns `@ollama:qwen3:32b` into provider `ollama:qwen3`). `@cf/meta/...` ids start with `@` but have no colon, so they stay bare and match against `activeProvider`.
- An in-flight catalog tap owns the checkmark / VoiceOver "Selected" value. A custom save names no catalog row, so no catalog row ticks while that request is in flight.

## Root cause

`#269` taught the matcher to keep provider identity, but the picker still discarded it at both boundaries: the write sent only `{model}`, and the checkmark called `matchesSelection(..., providerID: nil)`. Core leaves slash-qualified ids unprefixed and its catalog dedup can prefix the *active* provider's own row, so model text alone is not a stable routing or selection identity.

## Contract evidence

Verified in upstream source, not docs:

- Compatibility pin `f1d399b4` (`api/routes.py:4475`) reads only `body.get("model")` and ignores an extra `provider` key.
- Upstream HEAD `a00b02f` (`set_hermes_default_model`, `api/config.py:4780`; route `api/routes.py:15474`) accepts `{model, provider, advanced}` and persists them atomically.

Sending `provider` when known is therefore inert on the pin and load-bearing on current servers. `PROJECT_SPEC.md` §9.3 records that split.

## How it was tested

- Focused: `ModelCatalogTests` + `APIClientConfigurationTests` (provider body present/absent, colon-bearing ids, exact-first option order, picker-boundary `isChecked` cases including dedup-prefixed active row, embedded-prefix authority, in-flight exclusivity, custom-save, `@ollama:qwen3:32b` stored default, `@cf/meta/llama` bare-`@` ids).
- Full XCTest, iPhone 17 Simulator, `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`: **1611 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.
- `git diff --check origin/master..HEAD`: clean.
- Pushed SHA verified against `audichuang/hermex`: `1f01057df2445198d84396f89b444df6dd201782`.

## Need to verify

- **No live save of a slash-qualified default.** Selecting a Nous `anthropic/...` row writes the real server; the request-body test covers the wire, not a live persist-and-reload.
- **No signed-build UI walkthrough** of the picker after this change. Checkmark / VoiceOver exclusivity is covered by `DefaultModelPickerView.isChecked` unit tests, not by tapping the sheet on a device.

title: Auto-generated session title appears as extra assistant text after responses
body:
## Bug

Sometimes Hermex shows the session title as extra assistant text after the actual response has finished.

For example, after a normal reply I’ve seen something like:

```text
Casual Greeting ExchangeCasual Greeting
```

It appears directly after the real answer, and the title itself is also shown correctly in the session UI.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Hermex to a `hermes-webui` server with automatic session titles enabled.
2. Send a prompt that produces a normal response.
3. Wait for the response to finish.
4. Watch the end of the assistant message / transcript.

## Expected behavior

The generated session title should only update the session metadata. It should never be rendered as assistant message content.

## Actual behavior

The title-generation text can appear after the completed response, sometimes more than once.

## My best guess

This looks like Hermex is accepting late `.token` events after the response has already completed. The relevant code seems to be `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift`: the `.token` branch appends text without checking whether the response is complete, while the `.done` branch marks the response complete immediately afterward.

The title text seems to arrive as one of those late token events, so it gets appended to the visible transcript instead of being treated as session metadata. Hermex should probably ignore late content events after `.done` while still allowing the separate title metadata event through.

Hermex source checked at current `master` (`d63129e`).

- Keep submitted text durable until the server accepts it, restore the exact text after an immediate failure, and preserve every newer composer edit during asynchronous sends and commands.

title: perf(chat): long streaming assistant messages make Hermex unresponsive
body:
## Summary

Long assistant responses make Hermex feel progressively slower or temporarily unresponsive while the response is streaming. The symptom is especially visible when a response contains substantial Markdown, code, tables, tool output, or reasoning. The app appears to stop loading correctly, although the stream may still be active.

This report separates two related but distinct costs:

1. **Many transcript rows**: the transcript currently uses an eager `VStack`; this is already tracked by #32 and the open PR #33.
2. **One long assistant message while it is growing**: the streaming renderer repeatedly reprocesses the accumulated string and the view model repeatedly joins pending token chunks. This issue focuses on the second path, while documenting the interaction with #32/#33.

## Observed current behavior

On current `master` (`b1605f91f5f6d06f4b505578564268436f769c9b`, `fix(chat): preserve unsent composer text (#289)`):

- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:208` still uses `VStack(spacing:)` around the transcript `ForEach`, so all loaded rows are eagerly realized. This is independently tracked by #32 / #33.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:84-143` uses `StreamingMarkdownRenderer` while a response is active.
- `StreamingMarkdownRenderer` calls `MarkdownMathLayoutCache.uncachedLayout(for:)` for every update because token-by-token content is intentionally not inserted into the settled-message cache.
- `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter.split(content)` and `StreamingTextFadeTailSplitter.split(...)` repeatedly inspect the growing content. The current implementation does not retain an incremental parser/split state between updates.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:4332-4343` computes `flushedContent + pendingAssistantTokenChunks.joined()` when each token arrives.
- `ChatViewModel` then flushes visible content on a coalesced schedule and publishes a new `messages` value, which invalidates the transcript and causes the active Markdown row to lay itself out again.
- The active row also participates in animated height growth and bottom-follow scrolling, so expensive layout and scroll correction can happen together.

The settled Markdown path was improved by #260/#261 (merged as `53862c451da6b127664620fc6c0da69582167ddc`), but that optimisation deliberately does not cache changing streaming strings. It therefore does not fully address this report.

## Reproduction

1. Connect Hermex to a working `hermes-webui` server.
2. Open a new or existing chat.
3. Ask the agent for a large response, for example a long technical explanation containing headings, lists, several fenced code blocks, tables, and tool output.
4. While the answer is streaming, keep the transcript at the bottom and try to scroll.
5. Repeat with a response containing one very large assistant message (tens of thousands of characters).
6. Compare the experience with a short plain-text response.

Please record:

- device model and iOS version;
- Hermex app/build version;
- approximate response character count;
- whether the response contains code, tables, math, tool output, or reasoning;
- whether the slowdown occurs during streaming, after completion, on reopening, or while scrolling;
- whether the web UI shows the same symptom against the same server.

## Expected behavior

Long responses may require more time to render, but the app should remain responsive enough to scroll, cancel the run, and receive the stream. Rendering work should scale with newly arrived content rather than repeatedly rescanning and relaying out the entire accumulated response wherever possible.

## Scope

This issue is for the **single long-message / active-stream path**. A complete solution may need coordinated work in:

- streaming Markdown segmentation and layout;
- the token/chunk accumulation path;
- invalidation boundaries for the active transcript row;
- interaction between streaming layout changes and follow-bottom scrolling.

The eager realization of many transcript rows is related but should remain independently reviewable under #32/#33. A fix here must not silently remove the `.sizeChanges` scroll anchor or regress the opening/streaming scroll behavior fixed by #137.

## Non-goals

- No API or SSE contract changes.
- No changes to the upstream `hermes-webui` server.
- No new third-party dependencies.
- No visual redesign of Markdown or the transcript.
- No removal of Markdown features merely to improve a benchmark.
- No reduction of the user-visible message page size without explicit product agreement.

## Proposed investigation and implementation direction

1. Add deterministic pure performance/regression coverage for long streaming Markdown and for pending token buffering.
2. Measure the current implementation on representative plain Markdown, fenced code, table, list, math, and tool-heavy fixtures.
3. Keep completed/stable Markdown blocks and their parsed representation stable while only the active tail changes.
4. Avoid repeated whole-buffer `joined()` and full-string concatenation in the token hot path where an equivalent buffer/state representation can be used.
5. Keep the active streaming row isolated so unrelated transcript rows do not re-evaluate.
6. Preserve the existing streaming reveal behavior, `.sizeChanges` bottom anchoring, cancellation, replay de-duplication, and final transcript correctness.
7. Consider #33 separately for lazy transcript rows; do not bundle an unreviewed scroll-position redesign into this fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- A deterministic regression/performance test covers a long streamed assistant response and verifies final content is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The test covers at least one Markdown-heavy response and one code/tool-heavy response.
- The implementation avoids rescanning/rebuilding settled portions of a growing response on every flush, or documents why a smaller equivalent boundary is required.
- Replay de-duplication, cancellation, interim assistant events, and final `.done` reconciliation remain covered.
- Existing scroll-follow behavior remains covered, including the `ChatScrollPolicy.sizeChangeAnchor` contract.
- No new dependencies or API changes.
- Full XCTest suite passes on a macOS/Xcode environment.
- Manual simulator testing confirms that a long response remains scrollable and cancellable and that the reader is not unexpectedly pulled back to the bottom after scrolling away.

## Related work

- #32 — Improve chat transcript scroll performance for long conversations (eager transcript rows).
- #33 — `perf(chat): lazily render transcript rows` (open; separate row-realisation work).
- #103 — previous `ScrollView + VStack` lag report (closed; historical context).
- #134 / PR #137 — transcript opening jitter and size-change scroll anchoring.
- #163 — bounded cache-first transcript loading (closed; protects cold reopen from publishing the entire cache).
- #260 / PR #261 — settled assistant Markdown re-parsing (merged; does not cache changing streaming content).
- #217 — open draft combining lazy rows, cache batching, and page-size changes; its author/review explicitly notes scroll-anchor and scope concerns, so this issue should not assume that PR is safe to merge as-is.

## Environment limitation for the initial report

The initial investigation was performed on Linux. This environment has no `xcodebuild`, `xcrun`, iOS Simulator, or Instruments, so the reporter could not compile the iOS target, run XCTest, collect Instruments timings, or perform device validation. The source-level findings above are grounded in the current repository and GitHub history; compilation and runtime measurements must be performed by CI or on macOS/Xcode before treating any implementation as verified.

## Suggested priority

Performance / streaming UX regression with a high user impact for normal agent answers. Please triage severity after reproducing on a physical device or simulator.

title: perf(chat): skip replay buffering on normal streams
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the first focused runtime optimisation for #291 and documents the follow-up performance work.

### Implemented

- `ChatViewModel.appendAssistantToken` no longer constructs `flushedContent + pendingAssistantTokenChunks.joined()` on ordinary streaming connections.
- `ChatViewModel.appendReasoning` applies the same bypass for normal reasoning events.
- The existing effective-content and replay de-duplication logic remains active for reconnect replay connections.
- `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests` adds a large normal-stream fixture containing Markdown-style sections, formatting, inline code, and reasoning chunks; it verifies assistant and reasoning content byte-for-byte.

This removes avoidable full-buffer joins and a per-token message lookup from the common non-replay path without changing the replay algorithm.

### Follow-up design included

The documentation also specifies the next structural slice: an append-only `StreamingMarkdownRenderState` with immutable sealed chunks and a changing active tail. That work is deliberately separate because it requires profiling the four seams identified by source triage:

1. token append/deduplication and pending-buffer joins;
2. paced flush/publication frequency;
3. Markdown math/block/tail parsing;
4. SwiftUI row layout and `.sizeChanges` follow-bottom correction.

The design preserves replay deduplication, interim/done settlement, cancellation, Reduce Motion, and the #137 scroll-anchor contract. Lazy transcript rows remain separate under #32/#33.

## Response to source triage

Source triage on issue #291 confirmed this is a distinct active-stream performance lane and agreed that the implementation should be measured rather than inferred. The first low-risk slice now addresses the normal-stream buffer work while retaining the replay path unchanged. See the issue comment for the maintainer's measurement matrix and the documentation in this PR for the follow-up design.

## Correctness and risk

The normal path appends the received token/reasoning text directly, which is semantically equivalent because replay de-duplication is inactive there. Replay connections retain the previous matching behavior, including prefix/overlap handling. Completion, cancellation, interim events, and final content reconstruction still use the existing flush paths.

No API, SSE, Markdown feature, scroll-anchor, page-size, or dependency changes are included.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Source diff reviewed against `master` at `b1605f91f5f6d06f4b505578564268436f769c9b`.
- Large normal-stream XCTest fixture added for assistant and reasoning byte preservation.
- Full XCTest not run: this environment is Linux and has no Xcode, `xcodebuild`, `xcrun`, iOS Simulator, or Instruments.
- Runtime performance improvement not measured here; macOS/Xcode validation is required.

Required maintainer validation:

1. Run the focused streaming tests and the full XCTest suite on macOS/Xcode.
2. Run the large-stream fixture with Instruments and capture main-thread, allocation, and frame-hitch data.
3. Verify normal streaming and replay/reconnect streams remain byte-identical.
4. Manually test scrolling away from the bottom, cancellation, `.done`, and reasoning/tool-heavy responses.
5. Profile the proposed incremental Markdown state before implementing that follow-up slice.

## Related work

- #291 — long streaming assistant messages make Hermex unresponsive.
- #32/#33 — eager transcript rows and the separate `LazyVStack` work.
- #137 — transcript opening and `.sizeChanges` scroll anchoring.
- #163 — bounded cache-first transcript loading.
- #260/#261 — settled Markdown layout caching.
- #217 — overlapping draft with unresolved scroll-scope concerns.

## AI disclosure

Implementation and tests prepared with Hermes Agent. Runtime compilation and performance validation remain pending on macOS/Xcode.

Relates to #291

title: fix(picker): make search cover full catalog including extra_models
body:
## Problem

The server exposes large catalogs as `models` (visible 15) + `extra_models` (overflow tail). From `api/config.py` (`_split_picker_overflow_models` `threshold=25`/`target=15`) consumed via `GET /api/models`:

- **WebUI** merges both buckets for search/autocomplete (`static/commands.js:312,627` etc.) — typing `Deep` finds `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`.
- **Hermex** fetched `extra_models` into `ModelCatalogGroup.extraModels` (`ServerCatalog.swift:854`) but the picker sheet only searched `group.models` — so overflow models were invisible to **Search models** (showing "No Results") even though they were already on-device and `/model` slash autocomplete (which uses the merged set) could see them.

Repro: OpenRouter catalog in curated order puts DeepSeek entries (~position 18) past the first 15 visible rows → they land in `extra_models`. Filtered sheet path `ChatComposerSelectorSheets.swift:270` `group.models.filter` misses them. Reported as: typing `Deep` in Hermex finds nothing while WebUI does.

## Fix

Rename the group helper `slashAutocompleteModels` (same `(models + extraModels).filter dedup`) → `allModels` (broader, honest name — it isn't just for slash). Switch every consumer that conceptually means *"any model in the group"*:

| site | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `ChatComposerSelectorSheets.swift:270` search | `group.models.filter` | `group.allModels.filter` |
| `…:318` favorites dedup key | `flatMap(\.models)` | `flatMap(\.allModels)` |
| `…:354` selected-custom lookup | `flatMap(\.models)` | `flatMap(\.allModels)` |
| `ChatComposerSelectorControls.swift:180` compact menu | `flatMap(\.models)` | `flatMap(\.allModels)` |
| `DefaultModelPickerView.swift:129` search | `group.models.filter` | `group.allModels.filter` |
| `ModelFavoritesStore.swift:165` `catalogOptionsByFavoriteKey` | `flatMap(\.models)` | `flatMap(\.allModels)` |
| `ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:162` `uniqueProvider` | `slashAutocompleteModels` | `allModels` |
| `ChatViewModel.swift:588` `selectedModelTitle` | `flatMap(\.models)` | `flatMap(\.allModels)` |
| `ServerCatalog.swift:788` `displayName(for:)` + `ChatViewModel:3206` + `SlashCommandAutocompleteView:332` | `slashAutocompleteModels` | `allModels` |

Empty-query picker stays trimmed (`if query.isEmpty { baseGroups = modelGroups }` untouched, and server also caps `/api/models/live` at `routes.py:21643`), so the tail only surfaces while searching — matching the server's intent ("searchable, not rendered" `api/config.py:2098`).

## Why not alias/inline

Alias (`slashAutocompleteModels { allModels }`) keeps the misleading name alive and forces every future caller to choose between two identical APIs; an inline `(models + extraModels)` repeat diverges from the deduped helper. Rename fixes the semantics you flagged.

## Testing

- Updated `ModelCatalogTests.swift:74` assertion to the new name (same value).
- Verified no remaining `slashAutocompleteModels` refs outside the one doc comment left intentionally as provenance.

Fixes the reported `Deep` search gap. No alias left behind.

## Evidence

- Server: `api/config.py:2104` `_NOUS_FEATURED_THRESHOLD=25 / _NOUS_FEATURED_TARGET=15`, `2250` `def _split_picker_overflow_models`, `7713` `_split_picker_overflow_models(ordered_models)` for every provider incl. OpenRouter, `7769-7875` `if pid == "openrouter"` → `_append_picker_group` (overflow applies), `routes.py:21643-21646` same cap for `/api/models/live`.
- WebUI merge: `static/commands.js:312,627`, `static/panels.js:1780,7362`, `static/ui.js:3668`, `commands.js:307` comment.
- Hermex decode: `ServerCatalog.swift:651,854,862` `extraModels`, `684` merged helper, `3206`/`332` slash consumers, `270` sheet filter (bug site).

title: fix(onboarding): invalidate stale auth status when URL or headers change
body:
## Problem

PR #265 added honest trusted-header/OIDC onboarding, but `OnboardingViewModel` kept the probed `authStatus` when the user edited the server URL or custom headers. The form can then hide the password field using stale trusted-header state, skip the required re-probe in `connect()` (`if authStatus == nil`), and fail against the newly entered password-protected server with no way to provide the requested password.

Reported as #285:

1. Enter a trusted-header server + headers → Test Connection → probe reports already signed in, password field hides.
2. Edit the URL or headers to point at a password-protected server.
3. Tap Connect without retesting.
4. Stale status remains non-nil, `connect()` skips probe, form stays shaped for old server. `AuthManager.configure` rejects while password control is still hidden.

## Fix

Bind `authStatus` to the normalized connection identity that produced it:

- **Identity** = `AuthManager.normalizedServerURL(serverURLString).absoluteString.lowercased()` (strips `www.webui.`, path/query/fragment, applies correct `http` vs `https` default) + sorted `customHeaders.sanitizedForStorage().map(name:value)` — matches server-side probing exactly.
- Store `probedConnectionIdentity` and `probeGeneration` (both `@ObservationIgnored`).
- `didSet` on `serverURLString` / `customHeaders` calls `invalidateProbedAuthStatusIfNeeded()` — only when `current != probed` does it nil `authStatus` + both banners (`connectionMessage`, `errorMessage`). Whitespace/canonically equivalent edits stay equal after normalization, so no flicker.
- `testConnection` and the `authStatus == nil` branch of `connect` now capture `generation` + `identityAtStart` and guard both before writing `authStatus` / banners — an older in-flight probe cannot overwrite state for a newer identity.
- `password` edits intentionally do **not** invalidate — password is a credential, not part of server capability.

Without a prior probe (`probedIdentity == nil`) identity edits are no-ops until the first successful probe, so typing before any probe never nss stale state.

## Testing

Manual verification of #285 acceptance tests:

- Trusted-header probe → URL change to password server → password field appears, Connect re-probes.
- Trusted-header probe → header change/removal → stale signed-in discarded.
- OIDC-only/passwordless status similarly invalidated.
- Whitespace-only / `https://example.com/` vs `example.com` stays equal → no churn.
- Old in-flight probe result ignored when identity changed during network flight.

Existing `OnboardingFlowTests` only covers `OnboardingFlowPolicy`; no `OnboardingViewModel` coverage existed or broken.

## Evidence

- `OnboardingViewModel.swift:9-12` four mutable inputs vs one cached `authStatus` with `connect:77` re-probe gate `if authStatus == nil`.
- `OnboardingConnectPage.swift` `TextField("", text: $viewModel.serverURLString)` + `CustomHeadersEditor(headers: $viewModel.customHeaders)` mutation paths.
- `AuthManager.normalizedServerURL:559-580` + `CustomHeader.sanitizedForStorage:105` — reused for identity.
- `CustomHeader` `ForEach($headers)` `Billing` note — `didSet` on array plus identity comparison handles add/remove/name/value edits reliably.

Fixes #285

title: fix(streaming): ignore late content events after response completion
body:
## Problem

After the assistant response completes (`.done` → `hasCompletedCurrentResponse = true` via `completeCurrentResponse`), late SSE content events are still appended as assistant message text. The session title text appears as extra assistant content after the real answer, sometimes more than once.

Reported as #288 — e.g. `Casual Greeting ExchangeCasual Greeting` appended after a normal reply, while the title itself is also shown correctly in session UI.

Root cause: `ChatStreamCoordinator.handle(_:)` at `435` appends `.token` (and `reasoning`/`interimAssistant`/tool events) without checking `hasCompletedCurrentResponse`. The two existing guards at `:182` `suspendActiveStreamConnection` and `:343` `recoverStaleStreamIfNeeded` protect suspend/recovery only, not the SSE closure `streamClient.start { self?.handle(event) }` at `:163`. `ChatViewModel.appendAssistantToken:4329` only guards `isEmpty`/replay dedup.

Server SSE sequence is `token* → done{…} → metering → title{session_id,title} → stream_end` (or `done → stream_end → title`). `TitleStreamEvent` (`SSEClient.swift:87`) is a **separate** case from `token`; late `token` carrying title text is stray/buffered and should be dropped, while `title` must still update `displayTitle` (`ChatViewModel:4597`) via `streamCoordinatorUpdateTitle`.

## Fix

Guard `handle(_:)` with `hasCompletedCurrentResponse` branching (26 lines at `:435`):

- **Allow after completion:** `.title` → `streamCoordinatorUpdateTitle` + `markProgress` (session metadata), `.metering` (TPS), lifecycle fallthrough `.streamEnd/.cancelled/.error/.transportError/.heartbeat/.ignored` → existing `switch` handling, duplicate `.done` → ignored (avoid double `completeCurrentResponse` via `runGeneration`).
- **Drop after completion:** `.token`, `.interimAssistant`, `.reasoning`, `.toolStarted/Completed`, `.approvalPending`, `.clarificationPending`, `.pendingSteerLeftover` → `return` before `lastEventID`/delegate.

`reasoning`/`interimAssistant`/tool late events same class as `token` — never appended to transcript, only to pinned notices/reasoning view. Title refresh that arrives **after** `streamEnd` still passes because `finishStream:696` resets `hasCompleted = false`.

## Testing

No existing `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests` covered `token-after-done`; `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests` asserts at `testDoneEventFlushesRemainingBufferImmediately` but no late-token drop. This PR's branching is additive — `title`→`displayTitle` and `streamEnd→finishStream` paths unchanged.

Fixes #288

## Evidence

- `ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:94` `hasCompletedCurrentResponse`, `:480` `.done` sets it `true` via `:642`, `:435` `.token` had no guard.
- `SSEClient.swift:67` `enum SSEEvent { case token, title, ... }`, `TitleStreamEvent: sessionId+title` at `:87`, decoder `case "title": .title`, `case "token": .token`.
- `hermes-webui/api/streaming.py` emits `put('title')` `@4765` + `put('stream_end')` `@4775` via background title thread, never `put('token', title)`.
- `ChatViewModel.swift:4597` `displayTitle = displayTitle(from: title)` — correct metadata path preserved.

## Maintainer validation

- Focused ChatStreamCoordinatorTests passed on the signed iPhone 17 simulator.
- Full signed XCTest suite passed: 1,634 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.
- Exact-head Greptile and Hermes reviews are green.

## AI usage

Contributor commits disclose Hermes Agent co-authorship. The maintainer fix and final validation were completed with Codex gpt-5.6-sol in T3 Code.

This keeps current `master`'s terminal-event fence, one-shot teardown, and serialized foreground recovery behavior intact. The earlier transcript fast path, benchmark harness, stored baseline, and CI evidence scraper were removed so this PR contains one independently reviewable optimization.
