title: Native OIDC sign-in with a verified Hermes session bridge
body:
## Objective

Add native OIDC support so Hermex can connect to the role-gated Hermes deployment at `https://hermes.omner.org`, complete Aune MFA, and use the resulting authentication for every REST and SSE request without a WebUI password or a static identity bypass.

## Current live symptom

The protected deployment does not expose a public `:8787` listener. Unauthenticated requests observed during discovery return `302` from `/`, `404` from `/health`, and `401` from protected API endpoints. Hermex therefore currently labels this compatible but protected deployment as missing.

The current WebUI OIDC callback creates an HTTP-only browser cookie. `ASWebAuthenticationSession` does not transfer that cookie to the app's `URLSession` cookie store, so opening the existing browser login URL alone cannot authenticate native REST/SSE traffic.

## Architecture gate — no Swift implementation before resolution

Select and verify one complete session strategy:

1. **Native bearer/token strategy:** a dedicated public PKCE client gives Hermex a role-bearing access token that the same-origin edge or Hermes server validates directly or exchanges for a Hermes session.
2. **Server-hosted OIDC plus one-time native handoff:** Hermes validates OIDC and the required role, returns a short-lived single-use handoff code to an allowlisted app callback, and redeems it at the same origin for the ordinary HTTP-only `hermes_session` cookie.

The selected interface must document endpoint names, request/response shapes, callback allowlisting, recipient/origin binding, TTL and replay behavior, logout/revocation, expiry recovery, and how `hermes-dashboard.access` is enforced. Verify the contract against the live server before implementing app UI or auth state changes. Do not invent endpoints or assume browser/app cookie sharing.

## Requirements

- Use a system authentication session with Authorization Code + PKCE S256; no client secret in the app.
- Preserve Aune MFA and deny identities without `hermes-dashboard.access` before any usable Hermes credential/session is issued.
- Keep long-lived native credentials in per-server Keychain scope; never log secrets or forward credentials cross-origin.
- Make cancellation, expiry, relaunch, and sign-out explicit and preserve other configured servers' state.
- Do not regress password-cookie, no-auth, trusted-header, custom-header, or Tailscale HTTP deployments.
- Discovery must distinguish protected-compatible, incompatible, unreachable, setup-required, and ready servers without exposing operational data publicly.
- REST, uploads, media, SSE, and reconnect must share the same authenticated server state.

## Acceptance signals

- `https://hermes.omner.org` is classified as compatible/auth-required rather than missing.
- `luken` completes Aune MFA and loads sessions/chat in Hermex.
- A valid Aune user without the role receives no usable callback credential or Hermes session.
- Tests cover success, cancel, validation failures, replay/expiry, relaunch, logout, two-server isolation, 401 recovery, redirect credential isolation, and existing auth modes.
- Full XCTest passes; signed Simulator and physical-device OIDC/MFA callback tests pass.

## Delivery shape

Use a small LKML-style local patch series: protocol/test seams first, state/discovery behavior next, session bridge integration next, and UI/lifecycle last. Keep server/edge changes separately owned and reviewed. Do not push or open a PR without explicit approval.

## What changed

Unsent composer drafts now retain staged attachments and effective new-chat model, reasoning, profile, and workspace choices across navigation and app relaunches.

title: Feature request: Bot Mode support for Hermes profiles
body:
## Request

Add Hermes Bot Mode support to Hermex so the mobile app can work with named Hermes bots/profiles the same way Hermes Desktop does.

## Current gap

Hermes Desktop has a Bots tab where profiles appear as named teammates, each with its own persistent Bot Chat, avatar, role/description, memory, skills, routines, and group chats. On mobile through Hermex, that Bot Mode UI is not available, so the user has to either stay in the default chat or rely on text prefixes like `nux:` / `personal:` when a default-profile router is configured.

That is workable, but it is not a good mobile UX:

- no roster of bots/profiles
- no clear way to open a bot's canonical chat
- no @mention autocomplete or disambiguation
- no group chat view
- no bot-specific routines surface
- regular conversations can feel hidden if routing happens behind the scenes

## Desired UX

Hermex should expose a Bot Mode surface similar to Desktop:

1. Show a Bots tab / bot picker listing available Hermes profiles.
2. Let the user open the canonical chat for a specific bot/profile.
3. Support typing or selecting `@bot` to direct a request to a bot.
4. If possible, show bot title/description/avatar and latest activity.
5. Eventually support Bot Mode group chats and routines.

## Suggested phases

### Phase 1: bot roster + direct bot chat

- Fetch available profiles/bots from the connected Hermes WebUI/API server.
- Display name, handle, title/description, avatar if available, and latest session preview if exposed.
- Open/send messages to the selected bot's canonical chat.

### Phase 2: @mentions in the composer

- Add @autocomplete for bots.
- Preserve text exactly, but resolve the target bot/profile explicitly rather than relying on natural-language routing.

### Phase 3: group chats and routines

- Mirror Desktop Bot Mode group rooms once the backend/WebUI exposes them.
- Show bot-scoped routines once available through the API.

## Why this matters

For mobile, Bot Mode matters more than on desktop: the user wants to quickly send the right request to the right specialist without managing hidden profile routing. A native bot picker keeps the mental model simple: choose Personal, Nux, Task Manager, etc., then talk directly to that bot.

title: Git actions (commit/push) fail with unclear error — no path to enable HERMES_WEBUI_WORKSPACE_GIT_DESTRUCTIVE in-app
body:
## Problem

When using Hermex on iPad to interact with a Hermes workspace that uses git, attempting to commit or push fails with:

```
Git Action Failed
Writes disabled on server.
Enable HERMES_WEBUI_WORKSPACE_GIT_DESTRUCTIVE=1 on the server
OK
```

This is confusing because:

1. **No in-app guidance** — the error mentions a server env variable, but Hermex has no UI/settings to help users set it. Users running Hermex on a mobile device have no way to configure server environment variables from the app.

2. **Poor discoverability** — `HERMES_WEBUI_WORKSPACE_GIT_DESTRUCTIVE=1` is buried in server docs. Mobile users shouldn't need to SSH into their server just to enable git in the app.

3. **No toggle in-app** — Hermex lacks a settings toggle to enable/disable destructive git operations, which would let users opt-in without touching server config.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermex on iPad connected to a self-hosted hermes-webui server
2. Connect to a workspace with an active git repo (e.g. scout)
3. Trigger a git action (commit or push)
4. See the error

## Expected Behavior

- Hermex should either:
  - Provide a **settings toggle** ("Enable git commit/push") that guides users to set the env var if needed
  - Or detect the env var is missing and show a **helpful link/instruction** to the specific docs page
  - Or allow git operations if the workspace is already git-initialized (smart default)

## Environment

- App: Hermex (iPad)
- Platform: iOS
- Server: self-hosted hermes-webui
- Workspace: /Users/aya/ai/scout (git repo)

## Impact

Blocks developers from using Hermex as a mobile code companion. The app works great for chat, kanban, and reading — but the one thing that would make it a true mobile dev tool (git operations) is broken with a cryptic error.

title: Correct merged localization and TestFlight agent guidance
body:
## Summary

PR #305 merged as `cecd810a2f4782c79e2ae72c205c3d287ad0b9de` and made `AGENTS.md` plus `docs/agents/` the governing agent contract. The broad consolidation is useful, but four exact factual/authority defects remain on current master.

This issue is documentation-only and should not reopen or revert the broad cleanup.

## 1. Remove the false String Catalog round-trip recipe

`docs/agents/i18n.md` says this is Xcode-exact and byte-identical:

```python
json.dumps(d, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ' : ')) + "\n"
```

Against current `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` (~3.4 MB):

- `sort_keys=True` does not reproduce the bytes;
- `sort_keys=False` does not reproduce the bytes;
- `strings` is not globally sorted;
- the file contains mixed compact grouped entries and expanded Xcode-style entries.

The next paragraph also says grouped append order must not be sorted, contradicting `sort_keys=True`.

### Required correction

Delete the universal serializer claim. Document the safe procedure:

1. parse/validate JSON;
2. make a targeted insertion preserving untouched bytes/order/format;
3. parse before/after and assert a semantic subtree diff changes only intended keys/languages;
4. do not claim a canonical full-file formatter unless one is added and tested byte-for-byte against the current catalog.

## 2. Correct catalog target membership

The guide says `Localizable.xcstrings` is bundled in app, Live Activity widget, and Share Extension.

Current project resource phases show:

- main app `1A2...0060` includes catalog build file `10CA...B001`;
- Live Activity `A045...0060` includes `10CA...B003`;
- Share Extension `B5A...0022` contains only `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`.

### Required correction

Either:

- state accurately that the catalog is app + Live Activity only and document the Share Extension localization policy, or
- deliberately add the catalog to the Share Extension and verify localized share UI in that target.

## 3. Replace the incorrect plural-category family table

The guide calls its family rows the “correct CLDR category set,” but current CLDR differs:

- French: `one`, `many`, `other`;
- Italian: `one`, `many`, `other`;
- Portuguese: `one`, `many`, `other`;
- Hebrew: `one`, `two`, `other`;
- Romanian, another Romance language, has `few`.

The broad `Romance → one/other` and `Hebrew → ...many...` rows are not safe hand-authoring guidance.

### Required correction

Use an explicit per-shipped-locale source of truth from current Apple/CLDR tooling, or instruct agents to derive and verify the category set in Xcode for each locale. Audit existing Hebrew `many` entries separately; do not preserve them merely because this incorrect table lists `many`.

## 4. Reconcile AGENTS and TestFlight commands

`AGENTS.md` says agents must never run `simctl shutdown all`; suggest it and let the maintainer act.

`TESTFLIGHT.md` still tells a fresh Codex validation session to run:

```zsh
xcrun simctl shutdown all
```

### Required correction

Use a targeted shutdown of the exact captured simulator UDID, or make the global shutdown an explicit owner-only manual action outside the agent command block.

Also replace `Workflow path, if implemented:` in TestFlight Step 12. `.github/workflows/external-testflight.yml` already exists and is documented as active in Step 3.

## Acceptance

- All four authorities above agree with the current tree.
- No runtime Swift change is needed unless the maintainer intentionally adds Share Extension catalog membership.
- `git diff --check` and exact Build/Test/CI Gate pass.
- Link this correction from merged PR #305 so future readers do not treat that review thread as unresolved noise.

title: perf(cache): batch cached-message lookups during transcript upsert
body:
## Linked issue

No issue. Salvaged from #217, which bundled this with two changes we are not taking.

## What changed

Caching a transcript issued one SwiftData fetch per message to find the row to update, then a second session-scoped fetch to sweep stale rows — 45 queries to cache a 44-message session.

One session-scoped fetch now serves both. `CachedMessage.cacheKey` already embeds the server and session, so that window holds every row a per-message lookup could have matched. Rows inserted during the pass are absent from the snapshot, which is exactly what the stale sweep wants: their keys are fresh, so the old code filtered them out anyway. Behavior is unchanged; the now-unused `cachedMessage(cacheKey:in:)` helper is removed.

The other two parts of #217 are deliberately excluded:

- **`VStack` → `LazyVStack` + dropping the `.sizeChanges` scroll anchor.** These are not separable — lazy realization churns row heights, the bottom anchor chases them, and #217 resolved that by deleting the anchor and its covering test, silently reverting #137. Left for #32, which needs a benchmark first.
- **`messagePageLimit` 50 → 20.** It also caps the cached read (`ChatViewModel.swift:1315`, `:1489`), and the offline fallback sets `hasOlderMessages = false`, so offline transcripts would lose 60% of their content with no way to load more.

## How it was tested

- Full suite: `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -parallel-testing-enabled NO` — **1,667 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**. Existing `testCacheMessagesWritesLoadedWindowAndRemovesStaleMessages` already covers all three branches (update-existing, insert-new, stale-delete), so no new test was added.
- Signed Debug build installed and launched on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5, against a live `hermes-webui`. Inspected the SwiftData store directly after each step:
  - Open a 44-message session → 44 rows, 44 distinct cache keys, `sortIndex` 0–43 contiguous.
  - Reopen it → still 44/44, `cachedAt` advanced on every row (min == max), confirming the update-in-place branch ran at volume with no duplicate inserts.
  - Open a second 42-message session → 42 rows written, **the first session's 44 rows untouched with their older `cachedAt`** — the hoisted stale sweep stays scoped to its own session.
  - Zero duplicate cache keys store-wide; one server URL.
- Cold relaunch → cached transcript renders correctly (Markdown table intact, bottom-anchored).

Read-only against the live server throughout; no sessions were mutated.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no `Codable` changes)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (no wire changes)

---

Cache batching originally by @audichuang in #217; credited as co-author. Salvage, verification, and device testing by Claude Opus 5 (1M context) via Claude Code.

title: Serialize concurrent foreground stream recovery
Add Shortcut input support for starting a new chat with content
body:
### Use case

HermeX currently exposes App Intents for:

- New Chat
- New Chat with Voice
- New Chat in Profile

These work well for opening a new chat, including one pinned to a selected Hermes profile. However, they do not accept content from iOS Shortcuts.

I would like to build shortcuts such as:

- Share selected text or a URL to a new HermeX chat.
- Send clipboard contents to a chosen Hermes profile.
- Pass text produced by another Shortcut action into HermeX.
- Share a file, image, or other supported content to a new chat.
- Use the iOS Share Sheet to hand content to a particular profile.

At present, a Shortcut can open a new chat, but the user must then manually paste or re-enter the content.

## Related issues

- #6 — widgets for starting a new session on a configured profile
- #2 — localization of the existing New Chat App Shortcuts
- #275 — server-backed saved prompts in the composer
- #299 — Bot Mode/profile-directed chat support

These are related, but none appears to cover passing dynamic Shortcut input into a new chat.

### Proposed behavior

Add an App Intent that starts a new chat with supplied content, optionally pinned to a selected profile.

Suggested parameters:

1. **Content**
   - Required text input.
   - Accepts the output of a previous Shortcut action and the standard `Shortcut Input` variable.
   - Where practical, converts shared URLs and other textual values into text.

2. **Profile**
   - Optional Hermes profile selection.
   - Reuse the existing `ProfileEntity` behavior from `NewChatInProfileIntent`.
   - If omitted, use the current/default profile.

3. **Send automatically**
   - Boolean, defaulting to **off**.
   - When off, prefill the composer and let the user review or edit the content.
   - When on, create the session and submit the message without requiring another tap.
   - If background submission is not appropriate or reliable, this could be deferred to a later slice while retaining composer-prefill support.

Possible Shortcut names:

- **New Chat with Content**
- **New Chat with Content in Profile**

These could be separate intents or one configurable intent with an optional profile parameter.

## Additional content types

A later or expanded version could accept:

- URLs
- files
- images
- PDFs
- other types supported by HermeX attachments

Unsupported input types should produce a clear error rather than being silently discarded. It would also be useful to accept multiple shared items where iOS App Intents permits it.

Text support alone would be a valuable first slice.

## Expected flow

### Review-before-send

1. A Shortcut receives text, a URL, or shared content.
2. The user selects a HermeX profile when configuring the Shortcut.
3. The Shortcut runs the HermeX intent.
4. HermeX opens a new chat pinned to that profile.
5. The supplied content appears in the composer.
6. The user can edit it and tap Send.

### Automatic-send option

1. A Shortcut receives content.
2. The configured HermeX intent creates a new chat in the selected profile.
3. The supplied content is submitted as the first message.
4. HermeX opens the resulting session, or returns an appropriate Shortcut result if background execution is supported.

## Implementation considerations

The existing App Intent and deep-link plumbing appears to be in:

- `HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift`
- `NewChatIntent`
- `NewChatInProfileIntent`
- `AppIntentRouter`
- the `new-chat-profile` deep-link route

The new intent could reuse this flow, but the supplied content should not be placed directly in a URL query parameter. Large prompts, Unicode content, sensitive text, and attachments would make that fragile and could expose content through logs or URL handling.

A safer approach may be to store a short-lived pending intent payload in app-owned state, pass only an opaque identifier through the navigation route, and consume/delete the payload after the composer or send flow receives it.

The exact mechanism should follow the project’s existing cold-launch and draft-storage architecture.


### Acceptance outcomes

- [ ] An iOS Shortcut can pass text into HermeX using a normal text value or `Shortcut Input`.
- [ ] The Shortcut can optionally target a profile using the existing profile entity picker.
- [ ] With no profile selected, the current/default-profile behavior is preserved.
- [ ] The supplied text is preserved exactly, including Unicode, multiline text, Markdown, and URLs.
- [ ] The default behavior opens a new chat with the content prefilled for review.
- [ ] The payload survives both warm and cold app launches.
- [ ] The content is delivered to the intended server and profile when multiple servers or profiles are configured.
- [ ] Missing, deleted, or unavailable profiles produce a clear fallback or error.
- [ ] An empty input is handled clearly and does not create an unwanted empty session.
- [ ] Pending content is not exposed in deep-link URLs, logs, or unrelated session state.
- [ ] A payload cannot be accidentally reused after it has been consumed.
- [ ] Existing New Chat, New Chat with Voice, and New Chat in Profile shortcuts continue to behave as before.
- [ ] Automated tests cover text preservation, profile selection, cold launch, invalid profiles, and one-time payload consumption.
- [ ] Manual validation covers the Shortcuts app, Share Sheet, Action Button where applicable, and multiple configured profiles.

### Upstream dependency notes

_No response_

title: Chat composer splits CJK characters during IME composition
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Korean, Chinese, or Japanese keyboard in the chat composer.
2. Begin composing a character so the input method has active marked text.
3. Trigger a SwiftUI parent update, such as a streaming response update, before the character is committed.

## Expected behavior

Ordinary view updates leave the active composition intact. Deliberate draft clears and replacements still update the composer.

## Actual behavior

The UIKit bridge can assign the bound text back to `UITextView` during composition, prematurely committing the marked text and splitting a character, such as `자` into `ㅈㅏ`.

## Acceptance outcomes

- Parent rerenders do not overwrite matching active marked text.
- A binding containing only committed text does not overwrite the active marked range.
- Deliberate programmatic replacements and clears still apply.
- Focused synchronization tests and the full XCTest suite pass.
- Korean or Chinese input is manually verified while the transcript is streaming.

## Context

title: Preserve uncached optimistic messages during active-stream reload
body:
## Summary

An optimistic user message can disappear when foreground/transport recovery reloads a still-active stream before the server transcript contains that message, if the send path did not receive a `ModelContext`.

This surfaced during review of #314, but it predates that PR and lives in ChatViewModel transcript reconciliation rather than reconnect-task serialization.

## Current source

Current master at `d92d574cc4f03d8b856f6159d0cb86eff5e76a82`:

- Several reachable slash-command paths call `sendMessage(...)` without a `ModelContext`, including queue/steer/interrupt fallbacks and skill sends (`ChatViewModel.swift:2549-2601,2937-2972,4674-4684`).
- `sendMessage` creates a `local-<UUID>` optimistic user message, but cache persistence occurs only when a non-nil context is supplied (`ChatViewModel.swift:2111-2137` and the send helper).
- `loadMessages(modelContext:nil)` adopts `loadedMessages` directly (`:1296-1327`).
- Equal-offset reloads fall through to plain replacement when neither paging-window merge applies (`:1674-1710`).
- Active-stream snapshot reconciliation preserves the snapshot wholesale only when the server transcript is empty; when the snapshot has no streaming assistant ID and the server transcript is nonempty, it returns the server transcript (`:1792-1819`).

A local optimistic slash-command message can therefore be removed by the first nil-context reload. A later reload with `ModelContext` cannot recover it because it was never cached.

## Reproduction shape

1. Existing session has at least one server message.
2. Execute a slash-command path that falls back to `sendMessage` without a `ModelContext`.
3. The optimistic `local-*` user row appears and the stream starts.
4. Suspend transport before the server transcript includes that row.
5. Begin recovery with `reconnectIfNeeded(modelContext:nil)` and return a nonempty stale session transcript.
6. Optionally let a foreground caller join later with a real `ModelContext`.
7. The optimistic user row disappears; the repeated context-aware load cannot restore it.

## Preferred fix

Preserve current-run in-memory optimistic user messages at the reload boundary, independently of cache availability:

- capture local optimistic user rows from `previousMessages` before the await;
- only merge them while the exact active stream/run generation still owns recovery;
- use the existing local-ID/equivalent-user-message normalization to avoid duplicates once the server row appears;
- do not resurrect local rows on unrelated ordinary/session-replacement loads;
- keep attachment identity and timestamp-aware dedup behavior.

Passing `ModelContext` through every slash/queue path is useful defense in depth, but it is easier to miss a caller and should not be the sole loss-prevention boundary.

## Acceptance tests

Production-composed ChatViewModel tests, not coordinator delegate call counts:

1. Nil-context slash send + stale nonempty server reload preserves the local row exactly once.
2. A late nonnil-context join during the first reload still preserves it.
3. When the server transcript contains an equivalent row, the local row dedupes to one user turn.
4. Attachment-bearing optimistic rows retain attachment identity.
5. Stream/run/session replacement does not carry the row into a successor authority.
6. Ordinary non-active reload does not resurrect an obsolete local row.
7. Full XCTest and physical foreground recovery drive remain green.

## Relation to #314

#314 serializes reconnect ownership and is separable from this ChatViewModel data-loss defect. Do not mark this fixed merely because the coordinator repeats a load with a later `ModelContext`; the first nil-context load may already have destroyed the only in-memory copy.

title: Preserve partial streamed responses across process termination
body:
## Context

Priority: P2.

During physical-device testing, terminating Hermex while an assistant response was streaming and reopening the session temporarily hid the beginning of that response. The missing prefix returned as soon as the response completed, so the final server-backed transcript remained correct.

This is separate from PR #296's Observation optimization and issue #315's optimistic-user-message reconciliation.

## Current behavior

Active-stream snapshots are process-local. When the app process is terminated, the snapshot containing the visible partial response and last event ID is lost. A cold reopen loads the server's current session transcript and reconnects to the active stream, but only newly arriving events are visible. The final `done` payload applies the complete session and restores the missing prefix.

## Expected behavior

Reopening a session with an active response should immediately preserve the complete visible prefix received before termination, continue streaming without gaps or duplication, and converge to the server's final transcript.

## Acceptance criteria

- Terminating and relaunching the app during an active response does not temporarily hide content that was visible before termination.
- Recovery remains scoped to the correct server, session, and stream.
- Replayed or restored events do not duplicate assistant text, reasoning, tool activity, or attachments.
- The completed transcript remains authoritative and matches the server.
- Ordinary navigation, background/foreground recovery, transport-error replay, and completion behavior remain unchanged.
- Recovery does not introduce per-token persistent writes or equivalent streaming-path churn.
- Automated coverage models a process boundary with no surviving in-memory snapshot and verifies the visible prefix before `done` as well as the final transcript.

## Validation plan

- Add focused `ChatViewModel`/`ChatStreamCoordinator` tests using scripted SSE and a fresh process-equivalent state.
- Cover server/session/stream isolation and replay overlap without duplicates.
- If the implementation uses active-stream replay, verify the exact supported route and query behavior against the running server or pinned upstream copy before coding.
- Run the full XCTest suite.
- On a physical iPhone: start a long response, wait for visible text, swipe-kill Hermex, relaunch and reopen before completion, confirm the same prefix is immediately present, then confirm the final transcript is complete and unduplicated.

## Non-goals

- Changing server-side execution or transcript ownership.
- Reconstructing arbitrary historical runs.
- Expanding PR #296 or issue #315.

title: Guard oversized Server First recordings before transcription upload
body:
## Summary

PR #321 removed the arbitrary 60-second Server First cutoff and switched capture to 32 kbps mono AAC/M4A. That correctly supports normal long-form dictation. A sufficiently long foreground recording can still exceed the server's upload ceiling, however, and the current failure path deletes the only recording after both server and on-device transcription fail.

This was identified during #321 review and deferred, but no follow-up issue was created.

## Current source

Current master at `a80e707f41e82f8d18f506e69fc86bdddcab5496`:

- Server First records indefinitely until user Stop using 32 kbps AAC (`ComposerVoiceInputController.swift:263-305`).
- Stop reads the entire temporary file into memory with `Data(contentsOf:)` before upload (`:346-366`).
- WebUI rejects multipart bodies above its configured `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (20 MB by default) before transcription (`api/upload.py:415-423`).
- At the configured bitrate the default ceiling is reached after roughly 80–85 minutes, plus container/multipart overhead.
- If the server rejects/fails, Hermex tries on-device recognition only when available and authorized (`ComposerVoiceInputController.swift:406-458`).
- If fallback is unavailable, denied, fails, or returns empty text, the temporary M4A is deleted (`:419-450` and cleanup paths).

A long recording can therefore consume avoidable memory/network work and then be irrecoverably discarded.

## Required behavior

Choose a byte-owned boundary rather than restoring the old arbitrary time cap:

1. Check the on-disk file size before `Data(contentsOf:)` and before network upload.
2. At/near the effective server ceiling, warn and stop safely based on bytes, not elapsed seconds.
3. Do not attempt a known-oversize server upload.
4. If on-device fallback cannot recover the transcript, retain/recover the recording through an explicit user decision instead of silently deleting it.
5. Keep ordinary Stop, Cancel, submit-discard, backgrounding, and successful cleanup semantics unchanged.
6. Do not hard-code a claim that every server uses 20 MB. Prefer an optional server-reported upload ceiling if the Bridge can expose one; otherwise use a documented conservative client boundary and still preserve the file on 413/custom-limit failure.

## Acceptance tests

- Exactly-at-boundary recording follows the intended upload path; one byte over performs zero network upload.
- Oversize recording with available on-device STT bypasses server upload and transcribes once.
- Oversize + unavailable/denied/failing fallback retains a recoverable M4A and shows an actionable choice.
- `Data(contentsOf:)` is never reached for a known-oversize server upload path.
- Cancel/submit/background cleanup still removes intentionally discarded files.
- Normal 90-second recording continues until Stop and transcribes successfully.
- Custom server 413 does not destroy the recording.
- Full XCTest plus physical-device long-form/low-storage validation.

## Relationship

Follow-up to #273 / merged PR #321. Do not reopen the resolved 60-second cutoff bug; this issue owns the separate size-ceiling and failure-retention boundary.

title: Drop stale overflow models after authoritative live refresh
Add an "All profiles" session view to the Active Profile row
body:
## Context

The sidebar's **Active Profile** disclosure lets a user switch which profile is
active, and the session list always shows only that profile's sessions. A user
asked to see every session they own in one list, ordered by recency, without
hopping between profiles to find the one they want.

The server already supports this. `/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/search`, and
`/api/projects` all accept `?all_profiles=1`, which returns the aggregate list
already sorted by recency. Each session row carries a `profile` field that
`SessionSummary` decodes today (`HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift:205`), and
each response echoes back `all_profiles`, `active_profile`, and
`other_profile_count`.

The server refuses `all_profiles` in isolated single-profile mode
(`_all_profiles_enabled` → `_is_isolated_profile_mode()`). That is the same
condition Hermex already uses to hide the entire Active Profile section
(`SessionListComponents.swift:164`, `viewModel.isSingleProfileMode`), so the new
option can never appear where the server would reject it.

**The hard part is not listing — it is acting.** `/api/session` returns **409
`session_profile_mismatch`** for a session outside the active profile, and every
mutation route (`pin`, `archive`, `rename`, `delete`, `move`, `chat/start`, and
the stream endpoints) is gated by `_guard_request_session_visibility` and 404s
the same way. The active profile is a signed `hermes_profile` cookie the app
flips via `POST /api/profile/switch`; Hermex rides `HTTPCookieStorage.shared`,
so the switch is scoped to this client and does not disturb other clients of the
same server.

The agreed rule that resolves this: **acting on a session makes its profile
active, and it stays active.** One rule for opening, archiving, renaming,
deleting, and streaming — no switch-and-switch-back machinery, no hidden state,
and the Active Profile row visibly reflects the change.

## Current behavior

- The Active Profile disclosure lists profiles; selecting one switches the
  server's active profile and reloads the session list.
- The session list only ever shows the active profile's sessions.
- There is no way to see sessions across profiles.
- The Projects disclosure has an unrelated "All" pill that clears the *project*
  filter (`SessionListComponents.swift:296`). This issue does not change it.

## Expected behavior

### Slice 1 — the aggregate list (read path)

- A new **"All profiles"** row sits at the top of the expanded Active Profile
  disclosure, above the profile rows, styled as a peer of `ActiveProfilePickerRow`
  with the same checkmark selection affordance.
- The row shows the server's `other_profile_count` as a subtitle or trailing
  count when it is greater than zero (for example "12 in other profiles"), so the
  option explains itself before it is tapped.
- Selecting it sends `all_profiles=1` on `/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/search`,
  and `/api/projects`. Projects must go aggregate too, or the Projects filter
  would list only the active profile's folders while the session list shows
  everyone's, and the per-project session counts
  (`SessionListComponents.swift:385`) would be wrong.
- Selecting a specific profile row turns "All profiles" off and restores today's
  scoped behavior.
- Rows belonging to a profile other than the active one carry a small profile
  badge. Rows in the active profile do not.
- Existing grouping is unchanged: Pinned / Today / Yesterday / Earlier, recency
  ordered inside each group.
- The selection persists across launches, **keyed per server** — a server
  registry entry, not a global default. Read
  `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` before choosing where it lives.
- The option is hidden whenever the Active Profile section is hidden
  (single-profile mode, or the `#189` visibility toggle).
- **Old-server fallback:** the response echoes `all_profiles`. If we asked for
  `true` and the server echoes `false`, turn the selection off, restore the
  scoped view, and surface a one-line explanation rather than silently showing a
  scoped list under an "All profiles" label.
- **Cache:** `CacheStore.cacheSessions` is keyed by server, and `CachedSession`
  already persists `profile` (`HermesMobile/Persistence/CachedSession.swift:25`).
  Persist rows as returned, and when "All profiles" is off, filter the cached
  list by the last-known active profile name so an offline scoped view never
  leaks another profile's sessions. Persist that name alongside the selection.

### Slice 2 — acting on a session in another profile (write path)

- Opening a session whose `profile` differs from the active one first switches
  the active profile to that session's profile, then loads it. "All profiles"
  stays selected, so the list does not move under the user; the Active Profile
  row updates to the new active profile.
- The same applies to every list action on such a row: pin/unpin,
  archive/restore, rename, delete, duplicate, branch, and starting a new message.
  Switch first, then perform the action.
- A 409 `session_profile_mismatch` returned from `/api/session` is handled as a
  switch-and-retry, not an error. This is the recovery path for a session whose
  cached `profile` is stale, and for entry points that carry only a session ID.
- Concurrent actions must not race the shared profile cookie: serialize the
  switch so two in-flight mutations cannot interleave switches.
- If the switch itself fails, the action fails with a clear message and any
  optimistic UI rolls back. Never show the action as having succeeded.
- After a switch, profile-scoped screen state must reload against the new
  profile — in particular the Projects list, since projects are themselves
  profile-tagged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "All profiles" appears in the expanded Active Profile disclosure, selects
      and deselects, and shows `other_profile_count` when non-zero.
- [ ] With it selected, `/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/search`, and
      `/api/projects` are all requested with `all_profiles=1`; with it
      deselected, none of them are.
- [ ] Sessions from every profile appear in one list, recency ordered, with
      today's Pinned/Today/Yesterday/Earlier grouping intact.
- [ ] Sessions outside the active profile show a profile badge; sessions inside
      it do not.
- [ ] Opening a session from another profile switches the active profile, loads
      the session, and leaves "All profiles" selected.
- [ ] A 409 `session_profile_mismatch` triggers switch-and-retry rather than an
      error state.
- [ ] Pin, archive, rename, delete, duplicate, branch, and sending a message all
      succeed on a session from another profile, via the same switch-first rule.
- [ ] A failed profile switch rolls back optimistic UI and reports the failure.
- [ ] The selection survives relaunch and is scoped to one server: configuring
      two servers and switching between them never carries the selection, the
      active profile name, or cached cross-profile rows across.
- [ ] A server that echoes `all_profiles: false` turns the selection off with an
      explanation.
- [ ] With "All profiles" off and the app on cached data, no session from another
      profile appears.
- [ ] The option is absent in single-profile mode and when the Active Profile
      section is hidden.

## Validation plan

**Route shapes must be verified before implementation.** Confirm against a
running server (the final arbiter) or the pinned copy at
`.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py`:

- `_all_profiles_query_flag` / `_all_profiles_enabled` (~line 483)
- `/api/sessions` profile scoping and the `all_profiles` / `active_profile` /
  `other_profile_count` response fields (~line 2487, ~line 2603)
- `/api/sessions/search` scoping in `_handle_sessions_search` (~line 17915)
- `/api/projects` scoping (~line 14158)
- the 409 `session_profile_mismatch` body (~line 13500)
- `POST /api/profile/switch` and its `Set-Cookie` (~line 16599)

If any of these changed, record the verified handler, shape, and upstream commit
on this issue before writing client code.

**Automated (XCTest, `URLProtocol` mocks + in-memory SwiftData):**

- `Endpoint` emits `all_profiles=1` only when asked, for all three routes.
- `SessionsResponse` decodes `all_profiles`, `active_profile`, and
  `other_profile_count` tolerantly, and still decodes a server that omits them.
- A 409 `session_profile_mismatch` drives switch-then-retry, and the retried
  request carries the expected session ID.
- A failed switch surfaces the error and rolls back optimistic state.
- Serialized switching: two concurrent mutations on sessions in different
  profiles do not interleave their switches.
- Cached-list filtering by profile when the selection is off.
- Per-server isolation of the persisted selection.

**Manual (simulator, against a server with at least two profiles holding
sessions):** select "All profiles" and confirm the aggregate recency ordering
and badges; open a session from a non-active profile and confirm it loads with
the Active Profile row updated; archive and rename a session from a non-active
profile; confirm Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels for the new row and badge,
Reduce Motion on the disclosure animation, and light/dark. Then switch to a
second configured server and confirm nothing carried over.

## Non-goals

- Making Tasks, Kanban, Skills, Memory, or the chat composer aggregate. They
  stay scoped to the active profile, even though Tasks supports the same flag
  server-side.
- Moving a session into a project that belongs to a different profile.
- Changing the Projects disclosure's existing "All" pill.
- Any new choice about which profile a *new* session is created under: it is
  created under whatever profile is active, as today.
- Caching each profile's signed `hermes_profile` cookie to target requests
  individually. Considered and rejected — it builds on undocumented cookie
  internals, is bound to the auth session, and needs re-minting on every login.

title: perf(chat): keep expanded thinking cards responsive during long streams
body:
## Context

Long reasoning streams make an expanded Thinking card jitter and become nearly unscrollable. The severe lag happens primarily while the card is expanded. Collapsed thinking cards and normal response streams do not show the same user-visible failure.

This applies both when a thinking card starts expanded and when the user expands it during an active stream.

`ReasoningBlockView` currently renders the entire accumulated reasoning value as one `Text`. Each reasoning flush replaces that value and makes SwiftUI lay out the growing block again.

A disposable hosted-view probe streamed 80 KB of reasoning-like text in 2 KB increments on the iPhone 17 simulator:

- Expanded thinking card: approximately 584 ms p95 per update.
- Collapsed thinking card: approximately 3 ms p95.
- Disabling text selection did not improve the expanded result.
- Disabling follow-bottom behavior did not improve it.
- Splitting completed text into stable plain-text chunks with a bounded, roughly 1,000-character active tail reduced p95 to approximately 28 ms.

These Debug simulator measurements are directional. Release and physical-device validation remain necessary.

Related work in #291, #292, and #296 reduced stream buffering and redundant observation writes. This reproduction isolates a remaining view-layout problem. #32 concerns transcript-level scrolling across many messages and is separate.

Relevant files:

- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ReasoningBlockView.swift`
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift`
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift`
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift`

## Current behavior

As live reasoning grows, expanding its Thinking card causes increasing layout stalls. The screen begins to jitter, scrolling becomes unreliable, and controls become difficult to use.

Collapsing the card removes the severe lag even though reasoning updates continue arriving.

## Expected behavior

Expanded thinking cards remain responsive throughout a large reasoning stream. The user can scroll, collapse the card, and cancel the response without visible input stalls.

Reasoning text remains complete and ordered. Once streaming settles, the card uses the existing single selectable text presentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Live expanded reasoning no longer lays out the entire accumulated text on every flush.
- Completed reasoning text renders as stable plain-text chunks with stable identity.
- Only a small bounded tail changes during normal prefix appends. Target roughly 1,000 characters, with a hard fallback that also bounds long text without paragraph breaks.
- Chunk boundaries preserve the exact original text and do not split Swift grapheme clusters.
- Existing completed chunks do not reevaluate when only the active tail grows.
- The live renderer is used for cards that start expanded and cards expanded during streaming.
- Collapsed cards do not construct or render the chunk view.
- A non-prefix replacement or new stream resets chunk state instead of retaining content from the previous value.
- Settling reconstructs the exact reasoning text without dropped, duplicated, or reordered characters.
- Settled reasoning returns to the current single selectable `Text`.
- A single selection spanning the whole reasoning block is not required while streaming.
- Typography, spacing, disclosure behavior, colors, reading order, VoiceOver labeling, and Reduce Motion behavior remain unchanged.
- Thinking remains plain text. It does not use the Markdown renderer or its streaming fade.
- Normal assistant-response rendering is unchanged.

The smallest expected implementation is a dedicated live plain-text chunk renderer inside or beside `ReasoningBlockView`. It may reuse or extract the stable chunk bookkeeping from `StreamingMarkdownSupport`, but reasoning should not pass through Markdown parsing.

## Validation plan

Automated tests:

- Feed at least 80 KB in deterministic increments and verify that concatenating the chunks and active tail reproduces the input exactly.
- Verify that prefix appends preserve the identifiers and contents of completed chunks.
- Cover paragraph boundaries, blank lines, long unbroken text, emoji, and multi-scalar grapheme clusters.
- Verify non-prefix replacement and new-stream reset behavior.
- Verify that the settled presentation receives the exact full reasoning value.
- Run the focused chat tests, then the full XCTest suite.
- Keep wall-clock timing assertions out of CI.

Manual validation:

- Run a signed Debug build with an 80 KB deterministic reasoning stream.
- Test a card that starts expanded and one expanded after streaming begins.
- Follow the bottom, scroll away while streaming, collapse and reopen the card, and use the cancel control.
- Let the stream settle, then select and copy the full reasoning text.
- Check a large Dynamic Type size, VoiceOver reading order, and Reduce Motion.
- Record before-and-after measurements with SwiftUI Instruments and Time Profiler in Release on a physical device when available.

## Non-goals

- Changing SSE ingestion, stream pacing, replay deduplication, observation writes, or scroll-anchor behavior.
- Changing the regular assistant-response renderer.
- Solving transcript-level performance across many messages from #32.
- Adding Markdown rendering to thinking cards.
- Changing the server contract or adding a dependency.

title: Kanban header hides the Board picker when the Board name is long
body:
## Context

The Kanban screen's Board picker is a `Menu` in the `.principal` toolbar slot (`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift`, `toolbarContent`, around line 1294). The trailing `ToolbarItemGroup` holds four buttons: Select Cards, New Card, Dispatcher, and Filters. UIKit hides the principal slot entirely when its intrinsic width does not fit between the leading back button and the trailing group. A `Menu` label reports the full text width and never compresses, so a long name removes the picker instead of truncating it. `ChatToolbarTitleLabel` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift`, around line 2616) avoids this with a plain view that is allowed to compress and truncate.

## Current behavior

With a Board whose name is roughly 20 or more characters on an iPhone in portrait, the header shows only the back button and the trailing pill (Select Cards, New Card, Dispatcher, Filters). The Board name, the chevron, and the way to switch or manage Boards are gone. Reproduced on iPhone 17 simulator, dark mode, default text size.

## Expected behavior

- The Board picker is always visible in the header, whatever the Board name length or Dynamic Type size. Long names truncate at the tail.
- The trailing pill holds three items: New Card, Dispatcher, and More. The Dispatcher button keeps its state icon and accessibility label exactly as today.
- More is a `Menu` with two rows: Select Cards and Card Filters. Its icon uses a filled variant while `model.hasActiveFilters` is true.
- While `model.isSelectingCards` is true, the More menu is replaced in place by a visible Cancel button (`xmark`, accessibility label "Cancel") that calls `clearCardSelection()`.
- The enabled and disabled rules for each action are unchanged: Select Cards stays disabled when `bulkActionPhase != nil` or `!canUseBulkActions`; New Card when `!canCreateCards`.
- Accessibility focus behavior is preserved: after the Dispatcher sheet dismisses, focus returns to the Dispatcher button; after entering select mode, focus moves to the selection controls (`selectionControlsAreFocused`, `dispatcherButtonIsFocused`, `KanbanLabView.swift` lines 119 to 122).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Board named with 40 characters shows a truncated name plus chevron in the header on iPhone 17 portrait; tapping it opens the Board menu with Manage.
- [ ] The same holds at the largest accessibility Dynamic Type size.
- [ ] The trailing pill shows New Card, Dispatcher, More. Select Cards and Card Filters open from More and behave as before.
- [ ] More shows the filled icon when a filter is active and the outline icon otherwise.
- [ ] Entering select mode swaps More for Cancel; Cancel exits select mode and More returns.
- [ ] Dispatcher state icons and the persisted result presentation are unchanged (existing `KanbanFeatureStateTests` on `KanbanDispatcherPresentation` still pass).
- [ ] VoiceOver labels exist for More and Cancel; focus restoration after the Dispatcher sheet and on entering select mode still works.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

Simulator, iPhone 17, light and dark:

1. Create or rename a Board to a 40-character name on the server, browse it, confirm the header.
2. Set Dynamic Type to AX5 and repeat.
3. Open More, choose Card Filters, apply one, confirm the filled icon. Clear it, confirm the outline.
4. Open More, choose Select Cards, confirm Cancel appears, tap Cancel.
5. Open the Dispatcher, dismiss it, confirm VoiceOver focus lands on the Dispatcher button.

Before and after screenshots go in the PR. Per the maintainer's design rule, mock the three-button header once and get a pick before editing the real view.

## Non-goals

- Moving the Board picker out of the navigation bar.
- Changing the Board menu contents, Manage Boards, or any Kanban behavior beyond the header.
- Landscape or iPad layouts.

title: fix(chat): make transcript auto-follow an explicit latch
body:
## What changed

Scrolling up a little while a response streamed did not stick: a quarter-second after the finger lifted, the transcript re-pinned itself to the bottom. Expanding a tool card or thinking block near the end also yanked the whole view because the bottom size-change anchor stayed live.

Auto-follow is now an explicit latch driven by scroll gestures instead of a distance test plus cooldown:

- Touching the transcript (pan begin) turns follow off immediately.
- Follow re-arms only when the gesture settles at the true bottom (within 12 pt), evaluated when the drag ends or when momentum comes to rest. A finished drag waits 160 ms for late momentum before its release position is treated as final, so a gentle fling is one interaction.
- Tapping scroll-to-bottom or sending a message re-arms regardless.
- Streaming growth, keyboard presentation, and other non-gesture offset changes never flip the latch on their own.
- The 80/160 pt distance thresholds remain only for the scroll-to-bottom button and the reading-older chrome.
- Reasoning blocks, tool cards, and tool groups suspend the bottom size-change anchor for the disclosure animation (250 ms) so the tapped row stays stationary. The upstream reference disables it for two frames; Hermex animates the height change, so the suspension covers the animation instead.

`ChatScrollPolicy` owns the reducer and constants. `ChatScrollObserver` reports pan begin/end and momentum settle from the UIKit scroll view. `ChatView` feeds events through the reducer and drops the cooldown state.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` on iPhone 17 (iOS 26.5): 1787 passed, 0 failed, 2 pre-existing photo-library skips.
- `ChatScrollPolicyTests` covers touch-down, drag end above and at the bottom, momentum end, layout growth while off and while on (keyboard), non-gesture landing at the bottom, live gesture at the bottom, explicit reset, the strict re-arm threshold, and the disclosure anchor suspension.
- Manual simulator pass is the owner's: scroll up mid-stream and confirm the view stays put; drag back to the bottom and confirm follow resumes; expand a tool card near the end and confirm the row does not move.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally (`xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17'`)
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)

title: feat(chat): answer disclosures, copies, and Git edges with haptics
body:
## Linked issue

Small-interaction haptics polish; no tracking issue.

## What changed

Tapping a tool card, tool group, reasoning block, or compaction card, jumping to the latest message, copying a message, code block, file, session title, deeplink, or onboarding command, and finishing a quick commit, push, pull, or fetch all answered silently. Only send, complete, cancel, and approve gave feedback.

`ChatHaptics` gains four verbs and the existing sites call them, so every new buzz honors the existing Haptic Feedback switch:

title: feat(chat): fade in freshly added transcript rows
body:
## Linked issue

None — a small transcript-feel change with no tracking issue.

## What changed

A message you just sent, and the assistant's first reply, popped into the transcript with no motion at all, so a brand-new row looked exactly like history. Now a user row fades up and an assistant row fades in over 220 ms, and only rows born in the last 3 s get the entrance. Cached history, a reload, paging older messages, and reattaching to a live stream all render in place, and Reduce Motion drops the entrance entirely.

How it works: each transcript row gets an insertion-only `.transition` whose animation is attached to the transition itself (`ChatMotion.freshRowTransition`), so the message append does not need `withAnimation` and no layout is animated: the bottom anchor still snaps and prepend position-preservation is untouched. `ChatTranscriptRowFreshness.isFresh` is a single timestamp comparison per row per body pass (one `Date()` read per pass), not a timer. Removal is always instant, so an optimistic rollback never lingers.

Decision taken: should a future-dated timestamp (server clock ahead of the phone) count as fresh? The reference behavior says yes; I went with a symmetric window (`|now - ts| < 3 s`) so a server clock running ahead by minutes cannot make reconciled history animate. Rows the app creates itself use the phone clock and always pass.

- New `ChatTranscriptRowEntryTests` (4 tests): inside/outside the 3 s window, server clock ahead, nil and non-finite timestamps.

title: feat(chat): pin the clarification card above the composer
body:
## Linked issue

Chat feel polish; no tracking issue.

## What changed

When the agent asks a clarifying question, the card lived inside the transcript. Scroll up to re-read what led to the question and the card, its choices, and its answer field leave the screen; nothing on the way back says input is waiting, and the only Stop is the composer slot.

The request is now pinned above the composer:

- A one-line bar (**Input needed**, the first line of the question, a chevron, and **Stop**) is the permanent footprint. Its measured height is the only thing added to the transcript's bottom inset, and that inset is the same whether the card is open or closed, so the transcript never moves while the card animates.
- The full card (question, choices, answer field, expiry, errors) opens over the transcript from the bar's bottom edge and slides back down behind it: an opaque surface with no crossfade, clipped at the bar so nothing draws over the composer. The transcript stays scrollable underneath.

- A typed answer survives collapse (the draft lives in the pinned container, not the card), collapse releases the keyboard, and the composer below is untouched, so its draft survives too.
- VoiceOver announces each new request once (`Input needed: <question>`); the bar is hidden from VoiceOver while the card covers it.
- Long questions or many choices scroll inside the card past 300 pt, so the answer field stays reachable above the keyboard.
- Submit is still disabled until the field has text; choices still submit on tap; the error footer, the `1 of N pending` count, and the expiry countdown are unchanged.

Approvals keep their modal overlay for now. `ClarificationRequestOverlay.swift` (the old dimmed overlay, no longer referenced) becomes `ClarificationRequestCard.swift`, which holds the pinned container, the bar, and the card.

1. **Stop on the bar even though the composer's send slot also shows Stop during a run.** Kept it: typing a steer flips the composer slot to Send, so the bar's Stop is the one that stays put.

title: Add OrcaRouter as an optional AI provider
body:
Hi maintainers,

We'd like to propose adding [OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai) as an optional AI provider alongside the providers already supported by the project.

OrcaRouter exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and uses standard API-key authentication, so the integration should be able to reuse the project's existing OpenAI/provider abstraction with minimal changes.

## What this would add

- Access to multiple chat, reasoning, image, and video models through one endpoint
- Automatic model routing and provider failover
- Standard API-key authentication
- Prompt caching
- Usage tracking, budgets, and team access controls

The integration would not replace or modify any existing provider. OrcaRouter would simply appear as another provider option that users can configure with their own API key.

## Existing OSS ecosystem

OrcaRouter is already integrated with or available across a growing open-source ecosystem, including RAGFlow, Dify, goose, promptfoo, NocoBase, DB-GPT, CAMEL, and models.dev / OpenCode.

## Partner program disclosure

OrcaRouter operates an optional open-source partner program. Approved OSS projects can receive a 5% revenue share from OrcaRouter usage attributed to their integration.

Participation in the partner program is not required for the provider integration, and we're happy to follow any disclosure or governance requirements maintained by the project.

More information:

https://www.orcarouter.ai/built-with

If this sounds useful, we'd be happy to discuss the integration details and, with the maintainers' approval, open a PR with the implementation.

I'm an engineer on the OrcaRouter team.

title: Add per-task run history: past runs list with full run output on Task Detail
body:
### Use case

Hermes users schedule recurring jobs (morning digests, syncs, nightly sweeps) and the Tasks tab shows the current state — but there is no way to see what a task actually did on its past runs from the phone. The web UI exposes run history; the app surfaces only the most recent output snippets. When a job fails overnight or a digest looks wrong, a phone user has no way to answer "what did this task do yesterday at 3am?"

### Proposed behavior

On the Task Detail screen, add a **Run History** section between metadata and recent output:

- Newest-first list of past runs (date, file size), loaded from the server's per-job run list endpoint, paged 50 at a time with a total count.
- Tapping a run opens a sheet with the full run output (selectable, monospaced) plus any usage metadata the server parsed (model, provider, cost, duration).
- History is an optional enhancement: a failure shows a small inline error with retry and never blocks the recent-output section.

### Acceptance outcomes

- Task Detail shows past runs for the selected job, newest first, with load-more paging.
- Tapping a run shows its full output text on the phone.
- If the run-history endpoints are unavailable (older server), the rest of Task Detail is unaffected.
- All user-facing strings localized; tolerant decoding throughout; no new dependencies.

### Upstream dependency notes

Uses two existing read-only hermes-webui endpoints (verified against upstream source, no server changes needed):
- `GET /api/crons/history?job_id=<id>&offset=&limit=` — paginated run list (filename, modified, size, parsed usage metadata).
- `GET /api/crons/run?job_id=<id>&filename=<name>` — full content of one run.

Note: `GET /api/crons/recent` (the completions feed across all jobs) is related but intentionally out of scope here — it maps to a separate "what ran lately" surface and deserves its own slice.

title: Show a Recent Runs feed on the Tasks tab (what ran lately across all tasks)
body:
### Use case

The Tasks tab lists scheduled jobs, but a phone user opening the app has no quick answer to "what actually ran lately?" across all tasks. The per-task history (see #350) requires drilling into each job. The web UI's completions feed answers "what ran lately" in one place; the Tasks tab should too.

### Proposed behavior

Add a compact **Recent Runs** section at the top of the Tasks list:

- Newest-first rows of recently completed jobs: task name, relative completion time ("2h ago"), and an ok/error badge.
- Tapping a row opens that task's detail screen when the task still exists in the loaded list; otherwise the row is display-only.
- The section hides itself when there is no recent activity, and a feed failure never blocks the task list (small section, optional content).

### Acceptance outcomes

- Opening the Tasks tab shows recently completed runs across all tasks without drilling in.
- Rows are honest about failures (error badge) and time (relative).
- Older servers without the endpoint: task list unaffected, section simply stays empty.
- Tolerant decoding; localized strings; no new dependencies.

### Upstream dependency notes

Uses the existing read-only `GET /api/crons/recent?since=<epoch>` endpoint (verified against upstream source): returns `{completions: [{job_id, name, status, completed_at, toast_notifications, session_id, message_count?}], since}`. The `since` parameter supports future polling; the initial panel just fetches the latest.

title: feat(chat): cap expanded row bodies at a scrollable window
body:
## Linked issue

No linked issue; approved maintainer work on the transcript density pass (follows #354).

## What changed

Expanding a tool row or thinking row with a long body pushed the whole transcript down by the full height of the text, so one big result meant pages of scrolling to get past a single row.

Expanded bodies now open inside a window that stops growing at 240 pt and scrolls on its own behind the row's left hairline. Shorter bodies keep their natural height and cannot scroll. The cap is fixed at every Dynamic Type size.

- `TranscriptLogRowBodyWindow` wraps the expanded body inside `TranscriptLogRowView`, so tool rows and thinking rows share one container. It measures its content with `onGeometryChange`, so the measurement exists only inside expanded bodies; collapsed rows in the lazy transcript gain nothing.
- `TranscriptLogRowBodyWindowLayout` is the pure rule `(contentHeight, cap) → (frameHeight, scrolls)`. The measured height is applied outside the disclosure animation so a tall body opens straight at the cap.
- Live thinking keeps its `UITextView`. Its `sizeThatFits` now reports at most the cap through the same layout rule, turns on the text view's own scrolling only once the content exceeds it, and `TailPinnedTextView` keeps the newest chunk visible on each layout. It stays non-interactive while streaming, so the outer window never scrolls for it and no user offset needs respecting.
- The inner scroller is a separate `UIScrollView`, so the transcript's follow latch and bottom anchor never see it. Expanding and collapsing still run through the existing anchor suspension.

title: fix(chat): keep the reader in place through disclosure toggles
body:
## Linked issue

No linked issue; approved maintainer work on the transcript density pass (follows #355).

## What changed

At the top of a long session, reached with a status-bar tap, tapping "+N previous tool calls", "Show fewer tool calls", a tool row, a thinking row, or a turn fold threw the reader to the bottom of the transcript, and auto-follow re-armed. It was intermittent: it never happened after a real drag on that scroll view.

Frame-by-frame traces on a live session showed three causes, and each gets a small fix:

- **Programmatic scrolls never switched follow off.** Only pan gestures emitted the "user scroll began" event. `ChatScrollObserver` now reports a gesture-free scroll that carries the reader past the streaming threshold in the same viewport (`ChatScrollPolicy.isScrollingAwayFromBottom`), and the latch switches off on it. Streaming growth, keyboard insets, and follow scrolls are excluded by construction.
- **SwiftUI re-applies the bottom anchor on every content-size change after a real status-bar scroll**, until the next drag. The fixed 0.25 s anchor suspension expired while 28 lazy rows were still laying out, and the next size tick moved the reader unopposed. `ChatPrependScrollPositionController` is now `ChatScrollPositionController` with a hold mode: it pins the UIKit offset through the toggle, releases after the content size has been quiet for 0.3 s (2 s cap), and is released early by a gesture or a deliberate scroll (follow, scroll-to-bottom, keyboard). It reverts only an offset change riding on a size change in the same run-loop turn, so a VoiceOver or hardware-keyboard scroll during the hold stands. The turn fold, which toggles in `ChatView`, is routed through the pin as well.
- **Each UIKit-side revert left SwiftUI's own offset model stale**, so lazy rows on screen stopped responding to taps until a real scroll. A hold that had to revert while held at the top ends with a SwiftUI-driven scroll to the transcript's top: nothing moves on screen, SwiftUI's model catches up.

Also, a gesture-free "at bottom" report re-arms follow only when the previous report was already near the bottom, so a relayout artifact from thousands of points up cannot switch follow on.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim`: 1861 passed, 0 failed, 2 pre-existing integration skips.
- `ChatScrollPolicyTests`: gesture-free scroll-away switches follow off; reset survives coasting momentum with the away flag; transient bottom from far above does not re-arm; nearby bottom does; geometry rule cases for jitter, keyboard inset, follow scroll, and anchor-snapped growth.
- `ChatScrollPositionControllerTests`: hold puts back a re-applied anchor, keeps reverting across a multi-frame relayout, clamps when a row below collapses, releases on a deliberate scroll instead of reverting, resyncs only after a revert and only when held at the top, and leaves prepend preservation alone.
- Manual, maintainer, simulator against the live server: fresh session, status bar to top, then fold, "+28 previous tool calls", "Show fewer tool calls", thinking row, tool row: no jump, every row responds on the first tap. Scroll-to-bottom, then expand and collapse a row a screen above the bottom: stays put.
- Pre-PR Codex review: five findings, all addressed before opening (resync scope, hold-aware latch suppression, stale-attachment KVO guards, tests, comment).

title: fix(chat): open the message menu without lifting the bubble
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #208

## What changed

Long-pressing a reply made SwiftUI snapshot the whole bubble as the lifted preview before it could dim the transcript and show the menu. On a multi-screen reply that snapshot was slow and taller than the screen, so the menu appeared over the undimmed text and then jumped once UIKit made room for it. Long-pressing a link also opened the message menu on top of the link interaction.

The menu now comes from a single `UIContextMenuInteraction` on the transcript's scroll view (`ChatMessageContextMenuView.swift`). Each bubble registers a clear, touch-transparent marker view behind itself; a long-press resolves to the bubble under the touch and the menu is anchored at the press point with nothing lifted. The transcript dims and the menu opens in one motion at any reply length, and nothing is re-rendered or snapshotted. Menu items are built from one shared list (`ChatMessageActionItem`) used by both the SwiftUI menu and the UIKit menu, and are also exposed as VoiceOver custom actions.

Why not lift a clipped preview: a copy that fills the viewport leaves UIKit no room for the menu, so it draws the menu first and relocates the copy a frame later (the same pop iMessage shows on long messages). A smaller slice cut the text off and needed a hide-and-restore dance that left a gap on dismissal. The maintainer tried both on the simulator and picked the no-lift behavior; the trade-off is that the pressed message is not visually highlighted, only anchored.

Links: the press cannot be told apart from plain text at the UIKit level, so a long-press on a link opens the message menu (owner decision on the issue's Q1). Taps still open links.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 simulator: 1868 passed, 0 failed, 2 pre-existing skips.
- New `ChatMessageActionMenuTests`: item order per role, disabled states while streaming, listening toggle, callback routing, and the UIKit menu mirroring disabled items.

title: feat(iOS): Add Kanban and Active Task Home Screen / Lock Screen widgets
body:
## Summary

Add native iOS Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets that surface Hermes task work at a glance: a Kanban-board summary and the current active task. This complements, rather than duplicates, #6, which scopes the profile-configured **New Chat** widget/control.

## Motivation

Hermex should make it quick to resume work without opening the full app. A task-focused widget surface would let a user:

- See the state of their Kanban board at a glance.
- Identify overdue or blocked work immediately.
- Resume the active task from the Home Screen or Lock Screen.
- Jump directly to the relevant board or task in Hermex.

## Proposed widgets

### 1. Kanban overview widget

**Suggested families**
- Home Screen: small, medium, and large.
- Lock Screen: rectangular accessory where practical.

**Content**
- Counts by status (for example, To do, In progress, Blocked, and Done today).
- A compact progress/column visual.
- The highest-priority, overdue, blocked, or most recently updated task.

**Behavior**
- Tapping opens the selected Kanban board in Hermex.
- Medium/large variants can list the top 2–4 tasks from **In progress** and **Up next**.

### 2. Active task widget

**Suggested families**
- Home Screen: small and medium.
- Lock Screen: rectangular accessory.

**Content**
- Task title.
- Board/project name.
- Status.
- Priority and due date when present.
- Checklist/progress count and last-updated time when available.

**Behavior**
- Tapping deep-links to the task detail.
- Later iteration: App Intent actions such as mark complete, move to next status, or open a quick update composer.

## Privacy and data handling

- Respect iOS Lock Screen privacy settings.
- Provide a setting to hide task titles/details while locked; use a generic state such as “1 active task” or “Open Hermex to continue.”
- Do not put chat text, credentials, cookies, API keys, or sensitive task metadata in widget snapshots, shared defaults, or logs.
- If an App Group is needed, cache only minimal, non-secret display data plus identifiers; authenticated reads/mutations remain in the main app.
- Show a clear stale/offline state, including the most recent successful refresh time.

## Technical direction

- Use WidgetKit and the existing widget extension.
- Reuse the app’s authenticated task/Kanban layer to assemble a minimal widget timeline payload.
- Deep-link to board/task destinations (exact URL scheme/route should follow existing Hermex deep-link conventions).
- Use timeline refreshes plus explicit widget reloads after in-app task/board changes.
- Keep task mutations out of the first slice unless App Intents can perform them safely with existing authentication and confirmation behavior.

## Relationship to #6

- #6 remains the New Chat / configured-profile widget and control.
- This issue owns read-only Kanban and Active Task widgets.
- A future “Today” widget may combine New Chat, active task, and task counts once both issues’ foundations exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can add a Kanban summary widget to the iOS Home Screen.
- [ ] User can add an Active Task widget to the Home Screen and Lock Screen.
- [ ] Tapping either widget opens the correct board or task in Hermex.
- [ ] Widget data refreshes after task/board updates within WidgetKit’s permitted refresh behavior.
- [ ] The widgets show useful empty, loading, offline, and unauthenticated states.
- [ ] Sensitive task titles/details can be hidden on the Lock Screen.
- [ ] Widgets work in light/dark mode and support Dynamic Type.
- [ ] No secrets or sensitive task data are exposed through snapshots, shared storage, or logs.

## Suggested rollout

1. **Phase 1:** Read-only Home Screen Kanban summary and Active Task widgets with deep links.
2. **Phase 2:** Lock Screen variants, configurable board/profile selection, privacy controls, and offline/stale indicators.
3. **Phase 3:** Carefully scoped App Intent quick actions, if feasible.

title: feat(chat): pill composer with a toolbar row when focused
body:
## Linked issue

No linked issue; approved maintainer work on the composer layout (follows #358).

## What changed

The composer was always a full card with a fixed control row inside it and a second always-on bar under it for workspace, profile, git, and the context meter. Model and reasoning were hard-clamped to ~130 and ~104 pt and truncated, big text sizes ran out of room, and the whole thing took a lot of screen while you were just reading.

Now the composer has two states.

- **Pill** (editor not focused): one capsule with the text, up to three inline attachment thumbnails plus a `+N` chip, the mic, and one trailing circle. The circle is Stop while a response streams and the draft is empty, and Send (which queues mid-run) as soon as there is text.
- **Card** (editor focused, or a composer sheet is up): radius-26 surface with the attachment strip inside above the editor, and a toolbar row under the card, above the keyboard. The row is a horizontal scroller holding add, model, reasoning, workspace, profile, git branch, mic, and the context meter, with an 18 pt fade only on an edge that hides content, plus the pinned Stop/Send circle.

Details:

- `ComposerToolbarScroller` owns the row: horizontal only, no bounce when it fits, taps never dismiss the keyboard, and `ComposerToolbarEdgeFades` is the pure fade rule (4 pt epsilon, RTL-aware).
- One `UITextView` in both states. In the pill it is invisible behind a one-line preview so focus and the draft survive the morph; the card editor runs 72 to 160 pt.
- Every circle and row control is 44 pt. Workspace, profile, and git branch become quiet inline controls to match model and reasoning. Reasoning with one server-supported effort and the profile in single-profile mode render as static labels.
- Surface, editor, row, and the feed inset all animate on `ChatMotion.composerChrome`; Reduce Motion snaps.
- Retired: the always-on secondary bar and the reading-older compact-chrome flag (`ChatScrollPolicy.shouldEnterReadingOlder` and its test go with it).
- The session list's `.refreshable` moves onto the `List`. On the navigation container it was inherited by every `ScrollView` in a pushed chat, which made the attachment strip and the new row pull-to-refresh and drag vertically.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim`: 1874 passed, 0 failed, 2 pre-existing integration skips.
