title: fix(chat): render live tool activity as log rows
body:
### Context

`ToolActivityGroupView` has two bodies. `isLive` draws `liveCard`: a `.thinMaterial` surface, an "Activity: N tools" header with a `Running` pill, and a `ToolCallCardView` per call. Everything else draws `settledLog`: dense `ToolCallLogRowView`s with the last call visible and earlier ones behind a `+N previous tool calls` toggle.

Thinking already renders as a log row in both states (#354), so during a stream the transcript shows a new-style Thinking row directly above an old-style tool card.

### Current behavior

While a response streams, the tool block is the material card. The moment the turn settles it becomes the log — same calls, different design, visible re-layout.

### Expected behavior

A live group renders exactly like a settled one: log rows, the same `+N previous tool calls` fold, no header and no card chrome. A call still in flight gets a `running` status instead of being mislabeled `interrupted`, and can be tapped open to show its arguments before the result arrives.

### Acceptance criteria

- `ToolActivityGroupView` has one body. `isLive` no longer selects a different design; both call sites (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:435` and `:713`) keep working.
- `ToolCallLogRow.Status` gains a `running` case, distinct from `interrupted`. `ToolCallSummaryFormatter` needs a liveness signal to tell them apart (an incomplete call in a live group is running; in a settled group it was interrupted) — suggest `entries(for:isLive:)` / `row(for:isLive:)`.
- `ToolCallLogRowView` draws `running` as a dim static `ellipsis` glyph in the status slot. No spinner, no repeating animation.
- `statusText` gains a localized "Running" string for VoiceOver; the String Catalog is updated per `docs/agents/i18n.md`.
- The live group folds like the settled one: only the last row shows, earlier rows sit behind the toggle, and the toggle still follows "Expand Tools by Default" until tapped.
- A running row expands to `ToolCallDetailBodyView` showing arguments with an empty result.
- Dead code removed with its tests: `ToolCallCardView`, `ToolCallStatusDisplay`, `TranscriptStatusPill`, and the three `testToolCallStatusDisplay*` cases in `HermesMobileTests/APIClientSessionDetailTests.swift:1226-1268`. `ToolCallDetailBodyView` stays.
- The doc comment on `ToolActivityGroupView` is rewritten; it currently describes the two-design split.

### Validation plan

Unit: `ToolCallSummaryFormatterTests` covers the status mapping — incomplete + live → `running`, incomplete + settled → `interrupted`, and that failure still wins over both. Full XCTest suite before review.

Simulator (iPhone 17), with before/after images on the PR:

- Send a prompt that runs several tools; watch the block during the stream and through the moment it settles — no design change, no jump.
- Tap a running row open mid-stream, confirm arguments show and the transcript doesn't scroll away.
- "Expand Tools by Default" on and off.
- Reduce Motion on: the fold toggle and row expansion still settle without a repainting status indicator.
- Accessibility Dynamic Type sizes, light and dark.
- VoiceOver on a running row reads its summary, detail, and "Running".

### Non-goals

- Expansion state surviving the live→settled handoff. Live call ids (`live-tool-…`) differ from persisted ones, so a row opened mid-stream closes when the turn lands.
- Any of the grouping work proposed in #262.

## Context

PR #361 rebuilt the composer's model picker (`ComposerModelPickerSheet` in `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerSelectorSheets.swift`): a plain `List` of collapsible provider groups with monochrome provider glyphs, 48pt body-text rows, a filled `Color.primary` pill on the selected row, a favorites star at every row's trailing edge, nav-bar `.searchable`, and a custom-model entry that shares the rows' geometry.

Settings > Default Model (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/DefaultModelPickerView.swift`) was not touched and still carries the pre-#361 look. It is the app's other model picker, and the two have now visibly diverged.

## Current behavior

`DefaultModelPickerView` renders:

- A `ScrollView` of private `ModelPickerCard` sections (grey `tertiarySystemFill` rounded cards) instead of a `List`.
- Every provider group always expanded, with no provider glyph and no way to collapse.
- 44pt rows at `.subheadline`, the model id as a `.caption` subtitle, `Divider()` between rows, and an accent-colored `checkmark` for the current default.
- A hand-rolled `ModelPickerSearchField` instead of `.searchable`.
- A "Custom" card with a single model-ID field and a `ModelPickerButton` labelled "Save Custom Model".
- No favorites star anywhere.

## Expected behavior

Settings > Default Model looks and reads like the composer picker.

Because this is the second copy of the same picker, the fix is an extraction rather than a second restyle: lift the #361 picker into one shared view that both surfaces own, and reduce `DefaultModelPickerView` to the loader and server-saver around it.

### The shared picker

Add `HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift` holding the picker moved out of `ChatComposerSelectorSheets.swift` — the `List`, the group `DisclosureGroup` with glyph/uppercase name/count, `modelOptionRow`, `favoriteStar`, `overflowToggle`, the custom entry, `CustomModelFieldStyle`, the filtering and `Current`/`Saved Custom` group logic, and `isRenderedByCurrentPicker`. This also takes `ChatComposerSelectorSheets.swift` back under the `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` limit (it is 731 LOC today).

Expose exactly two configurations as static presets — `.composer` and `.serverDefault` — so neither call site assembles a pile of booleans. They differ in:

| | `.composer` | `.serverDefault` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation title | "Choose Model" | "Default Model" |
| Toolbar button | "Done", `.topBarTrailing` | "Cancel", `.cancellationAction` |
| Custom action label | "Use Custom" | "Save Custom Model" |
| Custom entry provider ID | required | optional |
| Star on the custom entry | yes | no |
| `Current` / `Saved Custom` groups | yes | no |

### Inputs the shared picker needs for the server-saving surface

The composer selects instantly; Settings writes to the server and can fail. Keep that behavior intact by giving the shared picker these inputs, all inert for `.composer`:

- `isSelected: (ModelCatalogOption) -> Bool` — the checkmark rule, supplied by the owner. The composer passes `option.matchesSelection(modelID:providerID:)`; Settings passes its existing `DefaultModelPickerView.isChecked(...)`. **Do not fold the two rules into one** — `isChecked` handles the server's `@provider:` prefix, `activeProvider` fallback, and the in-flight projection, and has 12 tests pinned in `HermesMobileTests/ModelCatalogTests.swift` that must keep passing untouched. `expandPrimaryProviderSections` should locate the group holding the selection through this closure (`group.allModels.contains(where: isSelected)`).
- `inFlightKey: ModelFavoriteKey?` — the row showing a `ProgressView` in place of its checkmark. `ModelFavoriteKey` is `(modelID, providerID?)`, which is exactly the pair `isSavingRow` compares today, so two providers offering the same spelling still cannot both spin.
- `isCommittingCustom: Bool` — spinner inside the custom action row.
- `isSelectionDisabled: Bool` — disables row taps during a save.
- `errorMessage: String?` — the save error, rendered as a `.caption` `.red` row at the top of the list.
- A load status for Settings' "Loading models…" and "Could Not Load Models" states, which the cards used to host. Render these as `ContentUnavailableView` (with a `ProgressView` for loading) so they match the new native chrome. The search-empty state stays `ContentUnavailableView.search`.

### Behavior carried over from #361

- Groups collapsed by default except the primary-catalog provider and whichever group holds the current default.
- The "Show all models" / "Show fewer models" overflow toggle, via the already-shared `ModelPickerOverflowExpansionState`.
- The `.transaction { if reduceMotion { transaction.animation = nil } }` guard, so `DisclosureGroup` expansion does not animate under Reduce Motion.
- The star follows the row's foreground (monochrome, inverted on the selected pill), never system yellow.
- Row context menu: favorite / unfavorite. The "Delete" item stays `.composer`-only, since `Saved Custom` groups do not render in Settings.

### Favorites in Settings

`ModelFavoritesStore.shared` is a single global `UserDefaults` store, so starring a catalog model in Settings shows up in the composer's favorites and vice versa. That is the intent. Settings' custom entry carries no star, so a custom model cannot be favorited from Settings and never needs a `Saved Custom` group to appear in.

### Custom entry in Settings

Adopt the composer's geometry and its provider-ID field with the provider menu, but keep the provider **optional**: a bare model ID must still save, exactly as it does today. `APIClient.saveDefaultModel(model:provider:)` already accepts a nil provider, so this needs no contract change and no endpoint work.

### Cleanup

Delete the now-unused private `ModelPickerSearchField`, `ModelPickerCard`, and `ModelPickerButton` from `DefaultModelPickerView.swift`. They are file-private; `DefaultProfilePickerView` has its own `ProfilePickerCard` and is untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One picker view is shared by the composer and Settings > Default Model; no duplicated group/row/star/custom-entry code remains.
- [ ] Settings > Default Model shows collapsible provider groups with glyphs, 48pt body rows, the filled selected pill, a favorites star per catalog row, and nav-bar `.searchable`.
- [ ] Saving from Settings still spins on the tapped row only, surfaces the server error inline, and dismisses only when the server confirms `ok == true`.
- [ ] `DefaultModelPickerView.isChecked` and its existing tests in `ModelCatalogTests.swift` are unchanged and passing.
- [ ] A bare custom model ID with the provider field empty still saves from Settings.
- [ ] Starring a model in Settings is reflected in the composer picker, and the reverse.
- [ ] The composer picker's own behavior is unchanged: selection, star tap without selecting, long-press context menu, saved-custom delete, `Current`/`Saved Custom` groups, provider menu in the custom entry.
- [ ] `ChatComposerSelectorSheets.swift` is under the `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` limit.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

Automated (`XcodeBuildMCP test_sim`, scheme `HermesMobile`, sim iPhone 17):

- The 12 existing `DefaultModelPickerView.isChecked` cases pass with no edits.
- New: the in-flight row rule ticks the spinner only for the matching `(modelID, providerID)` pair, and not for a same-id row under a different provider.
- New: the `.serverDefault` configuration builds a custom option from a model ID with an empty provider, while `.composer` does not.
- Existing `ComposerModelPickerSelectionClassificationTests` and `ModelFavoritesStoreTests` pass unchanged.

Manual simulator pass (signed Debug build via `build_run_sim`):

1. Settings > Default Model: groups collapsed except the primary provider and the group holding the current default; glyphs render.
2. Tap a model: spinner on that row only, sheet dismisses, the Settings row shows the new default.
3. Force a failure (stop the server or go offline): the red error appears, the sheet stays open, no wrong row reads as checked.
4. Custom entry: save a bare model ID with the provider empty.
5. Star a catalog model in Settings, open the composer picker, confirm it is favorited; unstar there and reopen Settings.
6. Nav-bar search: type, confirm groups auto-expand to matches, clear, confirm the collapsed state restores.
7. Reduce Motion on: expanding a group does not animate.
8. Accessibility text sizes, VoiceOver (row label plus the Selected trait), light and dark.
9. Composer picker regression pass: select, star, long-press menu, delete a saved custom, provider menu.
10. Two configured servers: switch and confirm the sheet shows the second server's catalog, default, and active provider.

## Non-goals

- Restyling Settings > Default Profile (`DefaultProfilePickerView`). Tracked as a follow-up.
- Server-keying `ModelFavoritesStore` / `ModelRecentsStore`. They are global today; that is out of scope.
- Any change to `APIClient.saveDefaultModel` or the `/api/models` contract. This issue touches no networking.
- The glyph gaps #361 left open (Hugging Face, AWS Bedrock, Tencent render bare; the OpenCode mark reads as a filled block).

title: refactor(settings): match the Default Profile sheet to the shared model picker
body:
## Context

PR #361 rebuilt the composer's model picker, and #366 shares that picker with Settings > Default Model. Settings > Default Profile (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/DefaultProfilePickerView.swift`) sits directly below Default Model in the same Settings section and still carries the pre-#361 look, so once #366 lands the two adjacent sheets read as two different apps.

`ProfileSummary` already decodes both `model` and `provider`, so a profile row can show a real provider glyph with no inference — unlike the display surfaces noted in the non-goals.

**Depends on #366.** Land that first: this issue reuses the row geometry, group header, and status primitives that #366 extracts into the shared picker rather than making a third copy of them.

## Current behavior

- A `ScrollView` of private `ProfilePickerCard` sections instead of a `List`.
- A hand-rolled `ProfilePickerSearchField` instead of `.searchable`.
- One "Profiles" card holding every profile, with `Divider()` between rows and no grouping.
- 44pt rows at `.subheadline`, a `.caption` details line (`model - provider - N skills`), and an accent-colored `checkmark` for the selection.
- A `ProfileStatusBadge` reading "Selected" or "Server Default" inline next to the name.
- A separate "New Profile" button styled as its own rounded card.
- No provider glyph anywhere, even though `profile.provider` is right there.

## Expected behavior

The sheet matches the shared picker's chrome:

- A plain `List` with `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)`, replacing the `ScrollView` and the cards.
- Nav-bar `.searchable` (`.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always)`), prompt "Search profiles", replacing `ProfilePickerSearchField`. It keeps matching on display name, normalized name, model, and provider, exactly as `filteredProfiles` does today.
- 48pt rows at `.body`, with the selected profile drawn as the filled `Color.primary` pill and `Color(.systemBackground)` foreground, matching the shared picker's `modelOptionRow`.
- A leading provider glyph from `profile.provider` at 17×17, rendered only when `ProviderGlyphKind.resolve(providerID:)` returns non-nil — the same "unknown providers render nothing" rule as #361.
- The "New Profile" affordance becomes the last row in the list, using the shared picker's custom-entry action geometry (48pt, 12pt radius, leading `plus` label) instead of its own card.
- Loading, load-failure, and no-match states render as `ContentUnavailableView` (with a `ProgressView` for loading), matching what #366 does for the model sheet.

### Must survive the restyle

- **The two badges mean different things.** "Selected" is the current default; "Server Default" is what the server would pick on its own. Keep both, and invert their colors on the filled pill so they stay legible — a green/secondary capsule on a `Color.primary` background will not read.
- The in-flight spinner keyed by `normalizedName`, replacing the checkmark on the tapped row only, with all rows disabled while saving.
- Dismiss only after the server confirms; `saveError` still renders inline and the sheet stays open on failure.
- Single-profile mode still hides the New Profile affordance — the server 403s creation there (#24).
- `isCancellationError` still swallows the cancelled-`.task` error instead of surfacing "cancelled" into `errorMessage`.
- Rows with a nil `normalizedName` stay disabled.
- The `CreateProfileSheet` presentation and its optimistic append plus reconciling refetch are unchanged.
- The Reduce Motion `transaction` guard from #361 carries over.
- Accessibility label (name + details) and value ("Selected" / "Server Default") keep their current text.

### Cleanup

Delete the now-unused private `ProfilePickerSearchField` and `ProfilePickerCard`. Confirm nothing else in the file or in `CreateProfileSheet` still uses them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings > Default Profile and Settings > Default Model are visually indistinguishable in chrome: same list style, row height, type scale, selected pill, and search placement.
- [ ] Rows show the provider glyph when the profile's provider resolves, and nothing when it does not.
- [ ] "Selected" and "Server Default" badges are both present and legible on the filled pill.
- [ ] Saving still spins on the tapped row only, keeps the sheet open on failure with the error inline, and dismisses only on confirmation.
- [ ] Single-profile mode hides New Profile.
- [ ] Creating a profile still appends optimistically and then reconciles from the server.
- [ ] No third copy of the row/geometry code: the shared primitives from #366 are reused.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

Automated (`XcodeBuildMCP test_sim`, scheme `HermesMobile`, sim iPhone 17):

- Existing `DefaultProfilePickerView` tests pass unchanged; `isCancellationError` coverage stays.
- New: the search predicate still matches on display name, normalized name, model, and provider.
- New: glyph resolution returns nil for a profile with a nil or unknown `provider`, so no glyph slot is reserved.

Manual simulator pass (signed Debug build via `build_run_sim`):

1. Open both Settings sheets back to back and confirm they match.
2. Provider glyphs appear on profiles whose provider is known; profiles with no provider show no glyph and no gap.
3. Tap a profile: spinner on that row only, dismiss, Settings row updates. Selecting a profile with a `defaultModel` still updates the Default Model row too.
4. Force a save failure: error inline, sheet stays open.
5. A server in single-profile mode: New Profile is absent.
6. Create a profile: it appears immediately, then reconciles.
7. Both badges on the selected pill, in light and dark.
8. Search from the nav bar by profile name, model, and provider.
9. Reduce Motion on, accessibility text sizes, VoiceOver (label plus Selected / Server Default value).
10. Two configured servers: switch and confirm the profile list, active profile, and single-profile mode follow the active server.

## Non-goals

- Favoriting profiles. There is no profile equivalent of `ModelFavoritesStore` and this issue does not add one.
- Grouping profiles into collapsible sections. The model picker groups by provider because the catalog is long; profile lists are short and stay flat.
- Any change to `CreateProfileSheet`'s own internals beyond how it is presented.
- Any change to `/api/profiles` or the save contract.

title: refactor(settings): give Providers the #361 glyphs and list chrome
body:
## Context

PR #361 introduced the bundled provider glyph set (`ProviderLogos.bundle`, `ProviderGlyph`, `ProviderGlyphKind`) and used it in the composer's model control and picker group headers. Settings > Providers is the one screen in the app whose entire subject is providers, and it shows no glyphs at all — it is also still on the pre-#361 chrome.

It is the strongest glyph surface in the app: `ProviderSummary.id` *is* the provider ID the glyph table keys on, so resolution is direct with no inference.

## Current behavior

`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/ProvidersView.swift` renders a `ScrollView` + `LazyVStack` of hand-rolled `ProviderRow` cards (14pt radius, `secondarySystemBackground`):

- Provider name at `.subheadline.weight(.semibold)`, with an "Active" capsule and a key-source capsule.
- A key-status line ("Key configured" / "No key") and an auth-error line.
- A `Models (N)` disclosure built from a `Button` plus a chevron with `rotationEffect`, whose expanded body is a flat `VStack` of `.footnote` secondary `Text` rows, with a "Showing X of Y models" tertiary footer.
- Status and error states rendered as a private `ProvidersStatusRow` inside the same card idiom.
- No provider glyph on any row.

## Expected behavior

The screen adopts the #361 idiom while staying read-only (#26 — API keys are a server-side operation and this screen deliberately carries no write affordances).

- **Glyph on every provider.** A 17×17 `ProviderGlyph(providerID: provider.id)` leading the name, rendered only when `ProviderGlyphKind.resolve(providerID:)` is non-nil, matching #361's "unknown providers render nothing" rule.
- **`List` instead of `ScrollView` + cards**, with the provider as a `DisclosureGroup` whose label carries the glyph, the name, and the model count in the shared picker's header geometry, and whose body is the model list.
- **Model rows** at `.body` in the shared picker's row geometry rather than `.footnote` secondary text, so a provider's catalog reads the same here as in the picker.
- **The count label** follows the picker's convention: `shown / total` when the server trimmed the list (`modelsTotal` > `models.count`), plain `shown` otherwise, replacing today's separate "Showing X of Y models" footer.
- **Status states** become `ContentUnavailableView` (with a `ProgressView` for loading), retiring `ProvidersStatusRow`.

### Must survive the restyle

- **Read-only.** No key set/delete, no provider activation, no row that looks tappable-to-edit. The "Provider keys are managed on the server" footer stays.
- The "Active" badge and the key-source badge (a deliberately unlocalized technical token: env / OAuth / config), plus the key-status line and the auth-error line, all keep their meaning and stay legible in the new chrome.
- `ProvidersView.expansionKey(for:at:)` keeps keying expansion by the provider's stable id, so a refresh that reorders the list (the server sorts active-first) keeps the right rows open. Its tests must keep passing.
- The refresh-failure banner (#42): a pull-to-refresh that errors still says so above the cached rows instead of looking freshly loaded.
- `.refreshable` still reloads.
- Reduce Motion: the current chevron `rotationEffect` animates unconditionally. Carry #361's `transaction` guard so the disclosure does not animate under Reduce Motion. This is a fix, not just a port.

### Note on glyph coverage

This screen lists **every** provider the server knows about, configured or not, which makes #361's known glyph gaps far more visible than they are in the composer: Hugging Face, AWS Bedrock, and Tencent have no asset and render bare, and the OpenCode mark is a filled tile that reads as a solid block in template mode. That is not this issue's job to fix — see non-goals — but expect bare rows and file the asset work separately if it looks wrong in practice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every provider row shows its glyph when the ID resolves, and nothing when it does not.
- [ ] The screen is a `List` of provider disclosures whose header and model rows match the shared picker's geometry.
- [ ] The count reads `shown / total` only when the server trimmed the catalog.
- [ ] The screen is still read-only, and the "managed on the server" footer is present.
- [ ] Active, key-source, key-status, and auth-error affordances are all present and legible in light and dark.
- [ ] Expansion still survives a refresh that reorders providers; `expansionKey` tests unchanged and passing.
- [ ] A failed pull-to-refresh still shows the banner above cached rows.
- [ ] Disclosure expansion does not animate under Reduce Motion.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

Automated (`XcodeBuildMCP test_sim`, scheme `HermesMobile`, sim iPhone 17):

- Existing `ProvidersViewModel` tests (`displayName`, `keySourceBadge`, `authErrorText`, `modelCount`, `truncatedModelInfo`, `expansionKey`) pass unchanged.
- New: the count label renders `shown / total` when `modelsTotal` exceeds `models.count` and plain `shown` otherwise.
- New: glyph resolution is nil for a provider with a nil or unknown `id`, so no glyph slot is reserved.

Manual simulator pass (signed Debug build via `build_run_sim`):

1. Settings > Providers against a real server: glyphs on the providers that have assets, nothing on the ones that do not, no layout gap either way.
2. Expand a provider, pull to refresh, and confirm the same provider is still expanded after the server reorders active-first.
3. Kill the server mid-refresh: the failure banner appears above the cached rows.
4. A provider with an auth error and a provider with no key: both read correctly.
5. Reduce Motion on: expanding a provider does not animate.
6. Accessibility text sizes, VoiceOver on a row (name, active state, key status, auth error), light and dark.
7. Two configured servers: switch and confirm the provider list, active provider, and key states follow the active server.

## Non-goals

- Adding the missing glyph assets (Hugging Face, AWS Bedrock, Tencent) or reworking the OpenCode mark. Separate asset work.
- Any write affordance: setting or deleting API keys, activating a provider, or editing a base URL. #26 settled that this screen is read-only.
- Adding `.searchable`. Provider lists are short enough to scan; revisit only if a real server proves otherwise.
- Any change to `/api/providers` or `ProviderSummary`'s decode.

title: feat(tasks): pick the model, provider, and profile for a scheduled task
body:
## Context

Scheduling a Task means telling the server which model, provider, and profile the job runs under. `CronJobEditorSheet` (`HermesMobile/Features/Tasks/TasksView.swift`, the "Configuration" section) collects all three as free-text `TextField`s. The user types a model ID, a provider ID, and a profile name from memory.

This is **pure client work**. `CronJob` already decodes `model`, `provider`, and `profile`; `CronJobEditorDraft` (`HermesMobile/Models/Cron.swift`) already carries them as `String` with empty meaning unset; and `APIClient.createCron`/`updateCron` already send all three. Nothing crosses the wire that does not already.

### Verified server contract

Checked against the pinned upstream copy at `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py`:

- `_handle_cron_create` (line 24663) accepts `prompt`, `schedule`, `name`, `deliver`, `skills`, `model`, `provider`, `profile`, `toast_notifications`. `_handle_cron_update` (line 24718) accepts the same keys as a partial update.
- **Profile is validated; model and provider are not.** `_normalize_cron_profile_value` (line 1614) raises `Unknown profile: <name>` unless the value is in `_available_cron_profile_names()`, so a mistyped profile is a 400 today. Model and provider go through as `body.get("model") or None` with no check, so a mistyped model silently creates a job that fails when it runs.
- **Blank is meaningful.** `_selected_profile_snapshot_updates` (line 24614): when a profile is set and *either* model or provider is blank, the server computes both from that profile's environment. Set both explicitly and the snapshot is skipped entirely. Clearing a field is a real instruction, not an empty one.

**Depends on #366**, which extracts the composer's model picker into a shared `ModelPickerSheet`. This issue presents that picker; do not build a fourth copy.

## Current behavior

In the "Configuration" section of the create and edit sheets:

```
TextField("Model", text: $draft.model)
TextField("Provider", text: $draft.provider)
TextField("Profile", text: $draft.profile)
```

No validation, no discovery, no indication of what blank means. `TasksViewModel` fetches neither `/api/models` nor `/api/profiles`.

## Expected behavior

Two picker rows replace the three text fields.

### Model row (sets model and provider together)

- A `Form` row showing the current selection — provider glyph, model name, provider ID as secondary text — or "Server default" when both fields are blank. Tapping it presents the shared `ModelPickerSheet` from #366 under a new `.cronJob` configuration.
- Choosing an option writes **both** `draft.model` and `draft.provider` from that `ModelCatalogOption`, so the pair can never be mismatched. This is the same model/provider coupling the composer and #366 already use.
- The `.cronJob` preset differs from `.composer` in two ways: **no favorites star** (starring while editing a scheduled task must not silently change what the chat composer offers), and no `Current`/`Saved Custom` groups.
- The picker's custom entry stays available, so an exact model ID plus provider ID can still be typed by hand — including when `/api/models` fails to load and the catalog is empty.
- A saved model the catalog no longer offers still renders as the current selection on the row, and as a selected row in the picker. A job configured last month must not silently look unconfigured.

### Profile row

- A `Form` row showing the selected profile, or "Server default" when blank. Tapping it presents a profile picker sourced from `APIClient.profiles()`.
- **Picker-only, no free text.** Upstream rejects an unknown profile with a 400, so free text here has exactly one failure mode the user cannot predict. If `/api/profiles` fails, the row shows a load error with a retry and keeps whatever value it already had; an existing job's saved profile still displays even when the list will not load.
- Each profile row shows its `model` and `provider` as secondary text — `ProfileSummary` already decodes both — so the inheritance below is visible rather than implied.
- Reuse whatever profile-row presentation #367 leaves behind rather than writing a third one.

### Clearing, and what blank means

- Both pickers open with an explicit **"Server default"** row at the top that clears the field. A way in needs a way out.
- The Configuration section footer states the actual server behavior: leaving the model blank while a profile is selected makes the server use that profile's model. Describe it; do not reimplement it. Specifically, **do not prefill** `draft.model` from the chosen profile — sending both fields suppresses the server's own snapshot logic and moves a server decision into the app.

### Loading

`TasksViewModel` gains catalog and profile loads for the editor. Fetch when the editor opens, not when the Tasks list appears — a user scrolling their task list should not pay for two catalog requests. Both failures are non-fatal: the model picker degrades to its custom entry, the profile row degrades to an error with a retry, and every other field in the sheet keeps working.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Configuration section has a Model row and a Profile row; no free-text model, provider, or profile field remains.
- [ ] Choosing a model writes both `draft.model` and `draft.provider`; the two can never disagree.
- [ ] Both rows offer "Server default", which clears the field, and show "Server default" when blank.
- [ ] A saved model or profile the server no longer lists still displays as the current selection.
- [ ] The Tasks model picker shows no favorites star and does not write to `ModelFavoritesStore`.
- [ ] A failed `/api/models` still allows a custom model ID plus provider ID; a failed `/api/profiles` shows an error with a retry and preserves the existing value.
- [ ] The section footer explains that a blank model inherits from the selected profile, and the app never prefills the model from a profile.
- [ ] Both the create sheet and the edit sheet use the pickers, with the edit sheet prefilled from the job.
- [ ] Catalog and profile fetches happen on editor open, not on Tasks list load.
- [ ] Full XCTest suite passes.

## Validation plan

Automated (`XcodeBuildMCP test_sim`, scheme `HermesMobile`, sim iPhone 17):

- Existing `CronJobEditorDraft` tests pass unchanged, including `trimmedModel` / `validationMessage`.
- New: selecting a `ModelCatalogOption` sets both draft fields; the "Server default" row clears both.
- New: a draft whose `model` is absent from the catalog still resolves to a displayable current selection.
- New: `URLProtocol`-mocked failures for `/api/models` and `/api/profiles` leave the draft's other fields intact and produce the degraded states, not a thrown error out of the sheet.
- New: the `.cronJob` picker configuration exposes no favorite action.

Manual simulator pass (signed Debug build via `build_run_sim`):

1. Create a task, pick a model, confirm the row shows the glyph, name, and provider.
2. Save it, reopen it in the editor, and confirm both model and provider round-trip.
3. Pick a profile, leave the model on "Server default", save, and confirm the server-side job reports the profile's model. Read it back with `curl /api/crons` against a disposable job.
4. Clear the model back to "Server default" on an existing job and confirm it saves as blank rather than as the literal string.
5. Type a custom model ID plus provider ID and save.
6. Point the app at a stopped server, open the editor, and confirm the model picker still accepts a custom entry and the profile row shows an error with a retry.
7. Edit a job whose saved model is not in the catalog: it still reads as selected.
8. Accessibility text sizes, VoiceOver on both rows (label plus current value), light and dark, Reduce Motion.
9. Two configured servers: switch and confirm the catalog, profile list, and existing jobs all follow the active server.

Mutating checks use one disposable cron job and clean it up.

## Non-goals

- Any change to the cron API, `CronJob`'s decode, or the create/update request bodies. All three fields are already wired end to end.
- A picker for `skills`, `deliver`, or `schedule`. `deliver` already has one; the other two are separate concerns.
- Provider-without-model as a distinct configuration. The combined picker always sets both, and "Server default" clears both.
- Provider glyphs on the read-only `CronJobMetadataRow` in `TasksView` and `TaskDetailView`. Those rows hold a bare model string with no provider ID, which needs a model-to-provider resolver the app does not have.
- Validating a model ID client-side. The server does not, and guessing would reject models a live provider actually serves.

title: Steering hint delivered toast doesn't fade

2. Deliver extra guidance

### Actual behavior

Toast hangs around indefinitely. Add more guidance, get more toasts that won't go away.

v1.5 build 1

26.2

Latest

Tailscale

title: feat(tasks): pick the model, provider, and profile for a scheduled task
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #369

## What changed

Scheduling a task meant typing a model ID, a provider ID, and a profile name from memory into three blank text fields. A mistyped profile is a 400 from upstream. A mistyped model is worse: upstream does not validate it at all, so you get a job that looks fine and fails when it fires.

Three picker rows replace the free-text fields.

**Model row.** Shows the provider glyph, the model name, and the provider ID, or "Server default" when both fields are blank. Tapping it presents the shared `ModelPickerSheet` from #366 under a new `.cronJob` preset. Choosing an option writes **both** `draft.model` and `draft.provider`, so the pair can never disagree — the same coupling the composer already uses. The custom entry stays, so an exact model ID plus provider ID can still be typed by hand, including when `/api/models` returns nothing.

**Profile row.** Shows the selected profile or "Server default", and opens a picker-only list from `/api/profiles` with each profile's own model and provider as secondary text. No free text: upstream 400s an unknown profile name, so typing one has exactly one failure mode the user cannot predict. Presentation reuses `PickerRowMetrics` and `pickerSelectionPill` from #367 rather than adding a third row style.

**Skills row.** Was the last free-text field: you had to remember what your server offers and spell it exactly. It now opens a multi-select picker sourced from `/api/skills`, each skill showing its description or category, with a "None" row that clears the whole selection. Disabled skills are filtered out — a run would ignore them anyway. `skillsText` stays the storage, so a job created before the picker round-trips through the same comma-separated form the server has always received.

Unlike the profile picker, the skills one keeps a free-text entry. Upstream takes `skills` unvalidated (`skills=body.get("skills") or []`), so without it a failed `/api/skills` would turn a field that used to accept anything into a read-only one.

**All three** pickers offer a way back to nothing — "Server default" for model and profile, "None" for skills. A way in needs a way out. A selected model, profile, or skill the server no longer lists still gets a row, so it stays visible and removable.

The Skills picker was a listed non-goal of #369; the maintainer asked for it during the manual pass and chose to fold it into this PR rather than split it.

### Three details worth naming

- **The app never prefills the model from a profile.** `_selected_profile_snapshot_updates` computes model and provider from the selected profile's environment *only while one of them is blank*; sending both explicitly skips that entirely. So the section footer describes the behavior and the app stays out of it. There is a test asserting `applyProfileSelection` leaves `model` and `provider` untouched.
- **`showsCustomModelGroups` split in two.** The issue asked the Tasks picker to drop the `Current` and `Saved Custom` groups, but it also asked that a saved model the catalog no longer offers still render as a selected row — and the `Current Custom` group is exactly the mechanism that does that. The flag is now `showsCurrentCustomModelGroup` (on for Tasks) and `showsSavedCustomModelGroup` (off for Tasks, since it is favorites- and recents-backed). Nothing in the Tasks picker reads or writes `ModelFavoritesStore`, and there is no favorites star, which was the actual concern: starring a model while editing a scheduled task must not change what the chat composer offers. `.composer` and `.serverDefault` behave exactly as before.
- **Where the loads live.** The issue said `TasksViewModel`, but the edit sheet is presented from `TaskDetailView`, which owns a different view model — that route means two copies of the same load. Instead `CronJobEditorConfigurationLoader` is owned by the editor sheet and driven from its `.task`, like `DefaultModelPickerView` and `DefaultProfilePickerView` already do. Same outcome the acceptance criteria asked for (fetch on editor open, not on Tasks list load), one copy, and unit-testable against `URLProtocol` mocks. Agreed with the maintainer before implementing.

`CronJobEditorSheet` moved out of `TasksView.swift` into its own file: adding the two pickers pushed `TasksView.swift` past the file-size warning, and the sheet is the seam that growth pointed at. It is a move, not a rewrite.

No wire contract changed. `CronJob` already decoded `model`, `provider`, and `profile`; `CronJobEditorDraft` already carried them; `createCron`/`updateCron` already sent all three.

## How it was tested

Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` (scheme `HermesMobile`, sim iPhone 17) on `d9a4b09`: **1917 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.

New `CronJobEditorConfigurationTests` and `CronJobSkillsPickerTests` (25 cases):

- Selecting an option writes both `model` and `provider`; a provider-less option does not leave the previous provider behind.
- "Server default" clears both, to blank rather than to a literal string.
- Selecting a profile never prefills the model; clearing a profile never touches the model.
- A model absent from the catalog still resolves to a displayable selection; a profile absent from the list still gets a row, and one already present is not duplicated.
- `URLProtocol`-mocked failures: a failed `/api/models` leaves the profile list and the draft intact and still commits a hand-typed model plus provider; a failed `/api/profiles` keeps the saved profile, shows the error, and recovers on retry. Neither throws out of the sheet. A cancelled load is not reported as a failure.
- The `.cronJob` preset exposes no favorite action and no saved-custom group; `.composer` and `.serverDefault` keep theirs.
- Toggling a skill appends and removes in the user's order; the selection round-trips through `skillsText`; clearing empties it.
- Skill search matches name, category, and description; disabled skills are dropped at load; a failed `/api/skills` keeps the saved skills, still accepts a hand-typed name, and recovers on retry.

Twelve new user-facing strings were added to `Localizable.xcstrings` with translations for all 17 shipped languages (append-only; every pre-existing entry verified byte-unchanged through a parsed-subtree diff).

The maintainer ran a manual simulator pass on `114a5f8` and it passed. Two things came out of it and are fixed here: the provider glyph is gone from the editor's Model row (a `Form` row gives its value whatever width the label leaves, so the glyph pushed long model names into clipping — the glyphs stay inside the picker, where rows are full-width), and the Skills picker above.

**Not done by me, and needs your pass:** before/after images, the Skills picker itself, and the live-server checks — the profile-inheritance round trip (`curl /api/crons` against one disposable job), a stopped server, a two-server switch, and VoiceOver / Dynamic Type. Reaching the Tasks editor needs a configured server, so I did not drive the simulator UI.

## Checklist

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly — no `Codable` model changed
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes — no wire contract touched; `/api/models`, `/api/profiles`, and `/api/skills` are all already in `Endpoints.swift`

title: feat(insights): rebuild Insights as a Usage screen with a window chart
body:
## What changed

Insights showed eight icon rows and a 14-row text list of daily token counts. There was no way to see a trend, and the "All Time" window quietly meant 365 days.

The screen is now **Usage**:

- **Four windows** — Past 24h / 7 / 30 / 90 days. `AnalyticsTimeframe` gains a 90-day case and loses `.allTime`.
- **A hero figure with a Cost/Tokens toggle**, and a Swift Charts bar chart under it. Multi-day windows plot `daily_tokens` — stacked input / output / cache read for tokens, a single bar for cost, since the server reports cost as one scalar per day. The 24h window plots `activity_by_hour`, which carries session counts and nothing else, so the metric toggle is hidden there and a caption says why.
- **Press and hold the chart** to read one bucket's own tokens, cost, and session count; release restores the window total. That is what lets the "Recent Daily Tokens" list go away without losing per-day detail. A press gates the scrub on purpose — a bare drag would eat the scroll view's vertical swipes.
- **A two-up totals grid and a row per model.** The grid reflows to one column at accessibility text sizes; both cache cells drop out on servers that don't report them.
- **Refresh honesty** — the spinner only marks a re-fetch of data already on screen. The first load renders its own placeholder, and a server that never answers can't pin the spinner on.

Every figure the old screen showed is still reachable: sessions, messages, input, output, total tokens, cost, cache reads, cache hit rate, per-model breakdown, per-day figures (via chart selection), peak day, peak hour, top sessions, and the source description.

Cost is labelled as an estimate everywhere. When the server prices a window at zero, the hero opens on Tokens rather than a confident `$0.00`, and model rows lead with token share instead of a column of identical "0% of cost". Cost stays one tap away and sticks once chosen.

### Contract

`daily_tokens[].cache_read_tokens` and `models[].cache_read_tokens` are now decoded; both already existed upstream and were being dropped. Verified with `curl "/api/insights?days=7"` against a live server, matching `_handle_insights` in the pinned upstream copy. No new field, endpoint, or shape was invented — provider stacking and hourly cost were left out precisely because this handler reports neither.

37 new strings were added to the String Catalog with translations for all 17 shipped languages.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 (iOS 26.5): **1926 passed, 0 failed**, 2 pre-existing photo-library integration skips.
- 10 new tests in `InsightsViewModelTests`: window zero-fill across 7- and 90-day windows, the hourly path selecting `activity_by_hour`, the metric toggle driving both the hero and the stacked segments, the zero-cost default, "per active day" dividing by active days rather than window length, cache cells disappearing when the server omits them, and the refresh-spinner rule.
- Manual pass on the simulator against a live server: all four windows, the metric toggle appearing and disappearing, press-and-scrub selection and release, and page scrolling from a swipe that starts on the chart.

The sidebar entry and the Settings visibility toggle still read "Insights" while the screen reads "Usage". Renaming them was out of scope here and is a two-string follow-up.

title: feat(tasks): rebuild the Tasks list as an agenda with filters and row actions
body:
### Context

The Tasks list prints eight label/value lines per job (Schedule, Next, Last, Deliver, Model, Provider, Profile, Skills) inside a plain grouped `List`, whether or not any of them matter. On a real server with eleven jobs, three of them scheduled and eight paused, the live jobs land at positions 6, 10 and 11 and the whole screen reads as one grey wall. Nothing on the list is actionable: Run now, Pause, Resume and Delete all require opening the job first.

This is the first of three slices. It rebuilds the list itself. Task Detail and the recent-runs feed follow separately.

### Current behavior

- `TasksView` renders a `List` with a "Running now" count row and one `Scheduled Jobs` section holding every job in server order.
- `CronJobRowView` renders the job name, a status badge, up to three lines of prompt, and then up to nine `CronJobMetadataRow` lines.
- Schedules render as the server's raw string, e.g. `*/15 * * * *` and `25 9 * * 1-5`.
- `job.lastError` is printed inline in red. On a real failing job that is a ~900 character shell transcript containing ANSI escape sequences (`\u{1b}[0;32m`), which the row renders as literal garbage.
- There are no swipe actions and no context menu anywhere in `HermesMobile/Features/Tasks/`.

### Expected behavior

An agenda-ordered list, densest-first, matching mock **B** with **C**'s error filter at https://k85jqrg9y1oe.postplan.dev

**1. Segmented filter** at the top: `All` · `Live` · `Paused` · `Errors`, each with its count. Selection is view state, not persisted. `Errors` selects jobs whose `lastStatus` is an error or which carry a `lastError` / `lastDeliveryError`.

**2. Agenda grouping**, in this order, each group hidden when empty:

| Group | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Now | Jobs present in `/api/crons/status` `running` |
| Later today | `nextRunAt` is today |
| Tomorrow | `nextRunAt` is tomorrow |
| This week | `nextRunAt` within 7 days |
| Later | Enabled, `nextRunAt` beyond 7 days or absent |
| Needs attention | Last run failed, regardless of enabled state |
| Paused | Everything else |

Within a group, sort by `nextRunAt` ascending, then by name. A job appears in exactly one group; "Needs attention" wins over "Paused", and "Now" wins over everything.

**3. Row** — a status rail, the name, and one meta line. Running rows show elapsed time. Enabled rows show the humanised schedule and the relative next run ("6:45 PM · every 15 minutes"). Failed rows show a one-line reason in red. Paused rows dim to a single dim line. Model, provider, profile, skills, deliver and prompt no longer appear on the row; they live on Task Detail.

**4. Humanised schedules.** Render standard 5-field cron as English: `*/15 * * * *` → "Every 15 minutes", `0 7 * * *` → "Daily at 7:00 AM", `25 9 * * 1-5` → "Weekdays at 9:25 AM", `0 16 1 * *` → "Monthly on the 1st at 4:00 PM", `0 20 * * 0` → "Sundays at 8:00 PM". Anything the humaniser does not recognise falls through to the server's own string unchanged — never to a wrong guess. Times format in the user's locale. Task Detail keeps the raw expression underneath.

**5. Row actions.** Swipe and long-press expose `Run now`, and `Pause` or `Resume` depending on state. `Delete` is long-press only and behind a confirmation naming the task. Each action is optimistic only where it can roll back, and reuses the existing `TaskDetailViewModel` mutations rather than duplicating them.

**6. ANSI stripping.** A shared helper removes CSI escape sequences from any server-supplied run text before display. It applies to the row's error line and to Task Detail, so slice 2 can reuse it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live jobs are reachable without scrolling on a server where most jobs are paused.
- [ ] The four filters select the right jobs and show correct counts; `Errors` finds the failing job.
- [ ] Every job appears in exactly one group; no job is dropped by the grouping.
- [ ] A recognised cron expression renders as English; an unrecognised one renders as the server's own string, never as a wrong guess.
- [ ] A failing job's error shows as one readable line with no escape bytes; the full text is reachable on Task Detail.
- [ ] Run now, Pause, Resume and Delete work from the list, with Delete confirmed.
- [ ] Row identity is stable across refreshes. Note `/api/crons` returns `job_id: null` for every job, so `CronJob.id` falls back to `name`; do not introduce a `UUID()` fallback into any list identity path.
- [ ] All new strings localized per `docs/agents/i18n.md`; Dynamic Type through AX5; VoiceOver reads each row as one element with its status; Reduce Motion respected.
- [ ] `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` stays quiet.

### Validation plan

- Unit tests: cron humanising across the eleven real expressions plus malformed input; group assignment including the "exactly one group" property and the precedence rules; filter counts; ANSI stripping including a sequence split across a truncation boundary.
- Simulator (iPhone 17, signed Debug): all four filters; swipe and long-press on a live and a paused job; Delete confirm and cancel; AX5 and VoiceOver; light and dark.

### Non-goals

- Task Detail (slice 2) and the recent-runs feed (slice 3).
- Editing schedules through the humanised text. The editor keeps taking a cron expression.
- Reordering, multi-select, or bulk actions.

title: feat(tasks): redesign Task Detail and add per-task run history
body:
### Context

Task Detail is where the eight metadata lines removed from the list in the list-redesign slice go to live, and it is the only place a phone user could answer "what did this task actually do?" — except it cannot, because past runs are not surfaced at all. When a nightly job fails or a digest looks wrong, the app shows the most recent output snippet and nothing else.

This slice redesigns Task Detail and adds run history. It supersedes #350, which described the run-history half against the old layout; #350's open PR #351 is being closed in favour of this.

### Current behavior

- `TaskDetailView` shows metadata rows, actions, and a recent-output section.
- There is no list of past runs and no way to read one in full.
- Error text renders raw, including ANSI escape sequences.

### Expected behavior

Matching mocks **E** and **F** at https://k85jqrg9y1oe.postplan.dev

**1. Header card** — name, status pill, humanised schedule, and the next run as a relative figure ("in 12h 21m") over its absolute time. `Run now` and `Pause`/`Resume` sit in the card as primary actions. When the last run failed, the card takes an error tint and carries a one-line reason with a "See full output" link, ANSI stripped.

**2. Prompt** in its own card, selectable.

**3. Configuration** card holding what the row no longer shows: schedule (humanised, with the raw expression beneath), deliver target, model, provider, profile, skills, notifications. Fields the server omits are absent, not rendered as "Not available".

**4. Run history** — newest first, from `GET /api/crons/history?job_id=&offset=&limit=`, 50 at a time, with the total in the section header and a "Load more" row. Each row shows the run's date and time from `modified`, its size, an ok/failed dot, and any usage metadata the server parsed. Tapping opens a sheet with the full output from `GET /api/crons/run?job_id=&filename=`, monospaced, selectable, with Copy.

### Contract notes, verified against a live server on 2026-09-03

- `GET /api/crons/history` returns `{job_id, runs: [{filename, size, modified, usage}], total, offset}`. Confirmed live: `total: 50`, `usage: {}`.
- **`usage` is frequently an empty object.** Run rows must degrade to date, size and status; model, provider, cost and duration are decorations that appear only when present. Do not build a layout that reserves space for them.
- **Paging must advance by the requested `limit`, not by returned row count.** The handler slices `all_files[offset:offset + limit]` and then skips any entry whose `stat()` throws, so a page can return fewer rows than it consumed. Advancing by `runs.count` silently re-fetches and duplicates. Stop when `offset + limit >= total`.
- **`GET /api/crons/run` and `POST /api/crons/run` are different operations on the same path.** GET with `job_id` and `filename` returns `{job_id, filename, content, snippet, usage}` for one run; POST triggers a run. `Endpoint.cronRun` is currently the POST trigger — do not reuse that case for the GET. Add a separate endpoint case.
- `modified` is an epoch double; `size` is bytes. Both decode tolerantly.

**5. Failure is optional, never blocking.** A history request that fails shows a small inline retry inside its section and leaves the rest of the screen intact. An older server without the endpoint leaves the section absent. The toolbar Refresh and pull-to-refresh both refresh history along with everything else.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Past runs list newest-first with a total and working "Load more"; no duplicated or skipped rows across pages.
- [ ] Tapping a run shows its full output, selectable, with Copy, and the sheet always shows the run that was tapped even if an earlier request resolves late.
- [ ] Runs with empty `usage` render cleanly without placeholder gaps.
- [ ] Error text on this screen contains no escape bytes, reusing the list slice's stripper.
- [ ] A history failure never blocks the rest of Task Detail; an older server degrades to no section.
- [ ] Refresh, from the toolbar and from pull-to-refresh, refreshes run history too.
- [ ] Numeric fields decode tolerantly. A malformed `size` or `modified` must not trap on `Double`→`Int` conversion.
- [ ] Localized strings; Dynamic Type through AX5; VoiceOver on run rows and the output sheet; Reduce Motion.
- [ ] `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` stays quiet.

### Validation plan

- Unit tests: paging advances by `limit` and terminates on `total`, including a page that returns fewer rows than requested; a late-resolving detail request cannot overwrite a newer selection; empty and malformed `usage`; malformed `size`/`modified` decode without trapping; history failure leaves the rest of the view model intact.
- Simulator: open a job with 50 runs, page to the end, open runs from different pages, force a history failure, open the failing trading-bot job and read its full output.

### Non-goals

- Deleting or re-running a specific past run.
- Diffing two runs.
- Charting run duration over time.

title: feat(tasks): show recent runs across all tasks on the Tasks list
body:
### Context

The Tasks list answers "what is scheduled". It does not answer "what actually ran lately" without opening each job in turn. The web UI has a completions feed; the phone should too.

This is the third slice and it builds on the redesigned list from #376. It supersedes #352, whose open PR #353 is being closed in favour of this.

### Current behavior

No cross-task run feed exists anywhere in the app.

### Expected behavior

A `Ran recently` group at the top of the Tasks list, below the filter and above `Now`, from `GET /api/crons/recent`.

- Newest-first rows: task name, relative completion time ("15m ago"), and an ok/failed dot.
- Tapping a row opens that task's detail when the task is present in the loaded list; otherwise the row is display-only and does not look tappable.
- The group hides itself when the feed is empty, and any feed failure leaves the task list untouched.

### Contract notes, verified against a live server on 2026-09-03

- `GET /api/crons/recent` returns `{completions: [{job_id, name, status, completed_at, toast_notifications, session_id, message_count?}], since}`.
- **Tap-through must match on `name`, not `job_id`.** `/api/crons/recent` returns real ids, but `/api/crons` returns `job_id: null` for every job, so the list's own `CronJob.id` falls back to `name`. Matching on id will never resolve and every row will silently become display-only. Verify this against the server before implementing; if `/api/crons` starts returning ids, prefer id and keep name as the fallback.
- `completed_at` is an epoch double. `message_count` is optional and must decode tolerantly; a malformed value must not trap on `Double`→`Int`.
- The `since` parameter exists for future polling. This slice fetches the latest once per load and does not poll.

### Loading rules

The feed is optional content on a screen that already has a primary request. It must not gate the task list: the list renders as soon as `/api/crons` answers, and the feed fills in when it arrives or quietly stays absent. A pending feed request may not hold the screen in its loading state.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening Tasks shows recent completions across all tasks without drilling in.
- [ ] Failed runs carry a failure dot; times are relative and update on refresh.
- [ ] Tapping a row whose task is in the list opens that task; a row with no match is display-only and reads that way to VoiceOver.
- [ ] The task list renders and is usable while the feed is still in flight, and a feed failure leaves the list unaffected.
- [ ] An older server without the endpoint leaves the group absent, with no error surfaced to the user.
- [ ] Tolerant decoding throughout; localized strings; Dynamic Type; VoiceOver.

### Validation plan

- Unit tests: a slow or failing feed never blocks the task list's loaded state; name-based matching resolves a row to a job and leaves an unmatched row display-only; malformed `message_count` and `completed_at` decode without trapping; empty feed hides the group.
- Simulator: open Tasks with a live server, confirm the group appears with correct relative times, tap a matched and an unmatched row, and confirm the list still loads with the feed endpoint blocked.

### Non-goals

- Polling with `since`, or live updates.
- A standalone full-screen activity log.
- Notifications or badges from the feed.

title: feat(sessions): show why a search result matched
body:
## Linked issue

None — approved local work.

## What changed

Searching your sessions returns rows that matched somewhere in the transcript, but the row looked identical to a title match: you had to open the session to find out why it came back.

Content-search rows now carry the server's `match_preview` excerpt through to the session row, which shows it on one line under the title with every occurrence of your query bolded.

- `SessionSummary` decodes an optional `match_preview` alongside the existing `match_type`, lossily like every other field.
- `SessionListViewModel` keeps a session-ID → excerpt map from the last search (content matches only, narrowed to sessions the list can actually show) and hands the row an excerpt paired with the query that produced it.
- `SessionSearchExcerpt.highlighted` bolds the matched ranges. Matching is case-insensitive and runs over `String` ranges, so composed and decomposed spellings match each other and combining marks stay attached to their base character. Diacritics are deliberately **not** folded — the server matched the query literally, so folding here would bold a span the server never treated as the hit. When redaction has replaced the match, the plain excerpt still shows and nothing is bolded.

Servers older than the upstream commit that added `_session_search_preview` omit the field, so those rows are byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Before / after

The row gains one line under the title; nothing else moves.

**Before** — `Q3 infrastructure planning` · `42 messages • hermex`

**After** — `Q3 infrastructure planning` · `...decided to move the **billing** plan tiers behind a flag before th...` · `42 messages • hermex`

Rendered variants (light and dark) plus live simulator captures before and after the escape fix are on the maintainer's machine at `/tmp/hermex-row-{before,after}-{light,dark}.png`, `/tmp/hermex-search-excerpts-live.jpg`, and `/tmp/hermex-search-excerpts-normalized.jpg`.

## How it was tested

Full XCTest suite on the simulator (iPhone 17, scheme `HermesMobile`): **1937 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.

New focused tests:
- `SessionSearchExcerptTests` — case-insensitive highlighting, composed vs. decomposed spellings, diacritics not folded, redacted excerpt with no match, empty query, match at either edge.
- `SessionListMutationTests.testRemoteSessionSearchExposesMatchPreviewPerSession` — the excerpt reaches the right session by ID, a row without a preview yields nothing, a title match never gets one, and clearing the search clears the excerpts.
- `APIClientSessionListTests` — `match_preview` decodes, and is nil when an older server omits it.

Surfaces walked: all three `SessionInteractiveRow` call sites (main list, scheduled group, project group) go through one wrapper, so they all get the excerpt. The Archived screen has no search and its rows are excluded from content matches by design. `Localizable.xcstrings` gained one key (`Matched: %@`, the VoiceOver prefix) in all 17 shipped languages, appended without touching any existing entry.

### Live server pass

Verified in the simulator against the maintainer's server, which does send `match_preview`. Searching `error` returns title matches with no excerpt and content matches with a one-line excerpt, `error` / `Error` / `errors` all bolded.

That pass surfaced one thing worth its own commit. The server previews raw stored message text, so an excerpt windowed out of a serialized tool result arrived carrying that JSON's escapes and printed them:

```
before  ...23% 459k 419M 0% /\n---\nRAM: 8.0 GB", "exit_code": 0,...
after   ...23% 459k 419M 0% / --- RAM: 8.0 GB", "exit_code": 0, "e...
```

`SessionSearchExcerpt` now turns those two-character escapes into spaces and collapses whitespace runs. The false positive it accepts is a Windows path (`C:\new`); that is worth it for a truncated preview line that is never used as data, and the alternative — guessing whether an excerpt "is JSON" — misfires in both directions.

What this deliberately does **not** fix: excerpts can still show JSON envelope fragments (`"exit_code": 0`), and a query like `error` can still bold a JSON *key* rather than prose. Both are upstream deciding what text to search and preview, and unwrapping the tool-result envelope client-side is its own change.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` `_session_search_preview` / `_handle_sessions_search`, and the `match_preview` entry in the sidebar field allowlist)

title: Live Thinking / tool-activity rows duplicate after background or lock, then vanish on final answer
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Hermex (App Store 1.5 build 1) on iPhone and start a chat against hermes-webui.
2. Send a prompt that makes the agent run several tools and show live **Thinking** / **Activity** (reasoning + tool calls) before the final assistant reply. Keep the chat on screen so those live rows appear once, correctly.
3. While the run is still in progress (live Thinking/Activity still on screen, no final answer yet), send Hermex to the background **or** lock the iPhone. Wait a few seconds so iOS can suspend the app / drop the SSE connection.
4. Unlock and return to the same Hermex chat.
5. Repeat step 3–4 one or more times before the run finishes.

### Expected behavior

Foreground recovery should resume the **same** in-flight turn. Live Thinking and live tool-activity rows should update in place (one Thinking block, one Activity/tool log for the current turn). Backgrounding or locking must not create extra copies.

### Actual behavior

After each background/lock → resume cycle, the live **action/thinking** overlay is appended again instead of being reconciled. The same Thinking and/or tool-activity content appears twice, then three times if the cycle is repeated.

When the **final assistant reply** arrives, the extra copies disappear. The settled transcript looks correct again.

This points to a **client-only live-stream / reconnect** issue, not a duplicated server transcript:

- Duplicates exist only while the turn is still streaming.
- They are gone after settlement, so a full reload of the server-backed messages is probably replacing the live overlay.
- Related but not the same: #310 / PR #314 (serialize concurrent foreground reconnect), #316 (partial stream prefix hidden until complete — the inverse symptom), WebUI #6303 (Worklog identity lost on session reattach in the browser client).

Likely area: `ChatStreamCoordinator` reconnect on `willEnterForeground` / scene activation replaying live `reasoning` / `tool` / `interim_assistant` events without matching existing live row identity.

### App version / commit

App Store **1.5 (1)**

### iOS version and device

iPhone 17 (iOS 26)

### hermes-webui server version

`exp-v0.52.264` (`e168b67e`)

### How the phone reaches the server

HTTPS tunnel (e.g. Cloudflare Tunnel)

### Screenshots or screen recordings

Not attached. Happy to add a screen recording if useful.

Reporter note: the duplicated surface is the live **reflection / action** overlay (Thinking + tool activity), not the final answer bubble.

title: feat(tasks): rebuild the Tasks list as an agenda with filters and row actions
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #376

## What changed

The Tasks list printed eight metadata lines per job whether or not any of them mattered, so eleven jobs read as one grey wall — the three live ones sat at positions 6, 10 and 11 — and nothing was actionable without opening the job first.

Tasks is now an agenda. Jobs group by when they run next (**Now**, **Later Today**, **Tomorrow**, **This Week**, **Later**, **Needs Attention**, **Paused**), a pinned `All · Live · Paused · Errors` filter sits above the list with live counts, and each row is a status rail, the name and one meta line. Run Now, Pause and Resume are on a swipe and a long press; Delete is long-press only and confirms by name. Model, provider, profile, skills, deliver and the prompt moved off the row — they live on Task Detail.

Two supporting pieces:

- **`CronScheduleHumanizer`** renders standard 5-field cron as English (`*/15 * * * *` → "Every 15 minutes", `25 9 * * 1-5` → "Weekdays at 9:25 AM"). It is deliberately narrow: anything it does not recognise falls through to the server's own string, never to a wrong guess. Rows that already show a next-run time use the recurrence alone ("6:45 PM · Daily"), so the time is not printed twice.
- **`String.strippingANSIEscapes()`** removes CSI/OSC sequences from server run text, including one truncated mid-escape. Applied to the row's error line and to Task Detail's error and output, so slice 2 can reuse it.

Three judgement calls worth flagging:

1. **An enabled job whose last run failed goes to Needs Attention**, not to its time bucket. The issue says "regardless of enabled state" and the mock's compare table makes that group the answer to "what is broken", so all failures land there. Confirmed with @uzairansaruzi before implementing.
2. **`Weekly on Sunday` rather than `Sundays`.** One `Every %@` key cannot serve both "15 minutes" and "Sunday" — German needs "Alle 15 Minuten" but "Jeden Sonntag" — so the weekday case got its own frame. Weekday names and the ordinal in "Monthly on the 1st" come from Foundation, and intervals go through `Duration.UnitsFormatStyle`, so plurals are correct per locale without a plural entry per interval in the catalog.
3. **`CronJob.id` no longer falls back to `UUID()`.** It is a computed property, so that fallback handed SwiftUI a fresh identity on every read and rebuilt every row on every poll. It is `jobId ?? name ?? ""` now.

Row actions call `TaskDetailViewModel`'s existing mutations rather than duplicating them, and nothing is applied optimistically — the server's response is what moves the row.

## How it was tested

**Contract, against the maintainer's live server (read-only):** `GET /api/crons` and `GET /api/crons/status`. Every job carries a real hex `id` (`job_id` is separately `null`), so identity, the running-jobs join and every mutation resolve off it; `/api/crons/status` returns `{"running": {<id>: elapsed}}`. Upstream `hermes-webui` @ `e168b67e` was read for the mutation handlers. No mutating calls were made.

**Full XCTest suite** on `0679cbf` via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` (scheme `HermesMobile`, iPhone 17): **1959 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.

**22 new tests** in `HermesMobileTests/TaskAgendaTests.swift`:
- All eleven cron expressions on the reference server, plus the recurrence-only forms, plus eleven malformed or unsupported expressions that must fall through.
- Group assignment: the exactly-one-group property over an eleven-job fixture, the running-wins and failure-wins precedence rules, each time bucket boundary, and an overdue next run.
- Filter counts matching the real server (All 11, Live 3, Paused 8, Errors 1) and the Errors filter selecting the failing job.
- ANSI stripping, including a sequence split across a truncation boundary, OSC, and two-character escapes.

`scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` reports no new oversized files. All 23 new strings are in `Localizable.xcstrings` with all 17 shipped languages; the catalog diff is purely additive (2438 added, 0 removed) and no pre-existing language subtree changed.

**Not yet done:** before/after screenshots, the AX5 and VoiceOver pass, and light/dark. Those need a signed Debug build pointed at a real server — happy to drive the simulator for them if you want, otherwise they are in your manual pass.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no decode changes; `CronJob.id` identity only)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against the running server and upstream `e168b67e`)

title: feat(tasks): redesign Task Detail and add per-task run history
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #377

## What changed

Task Detail could not answer the one question it exists for: what has this task actually been doing? It showed eight metadata rows and the most recent output snippet, and nothing else — when a nightly job failed, that was all you got.

It is now four cards and a history:

- **Header** — name, status, humanised schedule, and the next run as a countdown ("in 7h 40m") over its absolute time. `Run now` and `Pause`/`Resume` are the card's bottom edge: a full-width divider, two flush labels split by a hairline, no fill. Neither action is more primary than the other, so they carry equal weight and nothing competes with the error box for the one colour on the card that means something. Resume takes a circled triangle so it does not read as a second Run now. When the last run failed the card takes an error tint and carries a one-line reason, ANSI stripped, with **See full output**.
- **Prompt**, selectable, in its own card.
- **Configuration** — schedule (in English, raw expression beneath), deliver, model, provider, profile, skills, notifications. Laid out as a grid so the label column takes the width of its widest label; the fixed 64pt column the old rows used wrapped "Notifications" onto three lines. A field the job does not have gets no row: a job that leaves its model to the server has nothing to say about one. Schedule and Deliver are the exceptions, since every job has both and `local` is the server's own default rather than a stand-in for a missing value.
- **Run history** — newest first from `GET /api/crons/history`, 50 at a time, total in the header, "Load more" row. Each row shows the run's date and size, an ok/failed dot, and whatever `usage` the server parsed. Tapping opens the full output from `GET /api/crons/run`, monospaced, selectable, with Copy.

Three things the contract forced:

- **Paging advances by the requested `limit`, not the returned row count.** Upstream slices `all_files[offset:offset + limit]` and then skips any entry whose `stat()` throws, so a page can return fewer rows than it consumed. Advancing by `runs.count` would silently re-fetch and duplicate.
- **`GET /api/crons/run` and `POST /api/crons/run` are different operations on one path.** `Endpoint.cronRun` stays the POST trigger; `Endpoint.cronRunDetail` is the new GET.
- **`usage` is usually `{}`.** Rows degrade to date, size and status; model, duration and cost are appended only when present, so no layout reserves space for them.

Failure stays contained: a history request that fails shows an inline retry and leaves the rest of the screen intact, and a server that 404s the endpoint drops the section entirely while keeping the inline output card it always had.

History requests are generation-and-cursor guarded. A "Load more" in flight when a refresh lands would otherwise apply its page on top of the reloaded first page and push the cursor past both, leaving the pages between them loaded nowhere and unreachable. "Load more" also declines outright while a reload is in flight, since until the first page lands the cursor still points into the list being replaced.

Also: Insights' `UsageCard` moves to `Features/Shared/SectionCard.swift` so Usage and Task Detail share one card chrome, and it grew an optional `footer` slot for the header card's action row — that keeps the card's own insets its business instead of having the call site cancel them with negative padding. `CronJobMetadataRow` had no callers left and is gone.

`MockURLProtocol` now serves handlers off a concurrent queue. URLSession drives every protocol instance from a single loading thread, so a handler that waits there stalls every other in-flight request — the stale-response tests could not otherwise express two requests racing.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on the simulator (iPhone 17, `test_sim`): **1975 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**, on `c060e00`.
- **`TaskRunHistoryTests` (13)**: paging advances by `limit` including a page that returns fewer rows than requested; paging terminates on `total`; overlapping pages do not duplicate; a page in flight when a refresh lands is discarded; "Load more" is refused while a reload is in flight; empty and malformed `usage`; malformed `size`/`modified` decode without trapping on `Double`→`Int`; a history failure leaves the rest of the view model intact; a failed refresh keeps the runs already on screen; a 404 retires the section; a late run-output response cannot overwrite a newer selection.
- **`TaskConfigurationFieldTests` (3)**: fields the job does not have are absent, fields it has are shown and trimmed, deliver falls back to the server default.
- `ContractReadinessTests` covers the two new endpoints' paths and query items.
- **Manual pass on the simulator against a live server** (maintainer): header card, countdown, footer actions, Configuration on a job with no model/profile/skills, run history with 50 runs, the failing `trading-bot` job's error box and full output. All confirmed working.
- 18 new strings are in `Localizable.xcstrings` across all 17 shipped languages; the catalog diff is purely additive and no pre-existing language subtree changed.
- `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` reports the same 33 pre-existing files as `master` — no new warnings.

**Not attached:** before/after images. Screenshots exist from the manual pass but cannot be uploaded from the agent session, and PR-only assets do not get committed — @uzairansaruzi to drag them in.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes — verified against the issue's live notes and `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` (`_handle_cron_history`, `_handle_cron_run_detail`), which agree
