title: feat(chat): rank slash and skill autocomplete by how well it matched
body:
## What changed

Typing `/` in the composer used to match a command only by a name prefix or a raw
substring of its description, and every hit was shown. A good match could sit
below a weak one, and a large skill catalog dumped everything it touched into the
panel.

Autocomplete now ranks. Each candidate is scored across its name, label,
category, and description — exact, prefix, word boundary, contains, or (names
and labels only) a fuzzy subsequence — keeps its best score, and the panel shows
the best 20. Typing `stop` puts `/stop` above `/interrupt`, which only mentions
"Stop" in its description.

Three smaller things came with it:

- Rows put the name, its hint, and the description on one line, with the
  description truncating so the name is never squeezed. Row fonts and the panel
  height follow Dynamic Type instead of a hard-coded 48 pt.
- The `/skills` list now says why it is empty: "No skills are configured on the
  server." when there is no catalog, "No skills match …" when the query found
  nothing. Both strings already existed in the String Catalog, so all 17
  languages are covered.
- Ranking hops off the main actor once the catalog is big enough (>128
  candidates) for the work to show up as typing lag.

### Plan

1. `SlashCommandRanker` — a pure, lower-is-better scorer. Field bases stagger so
   any name hit beats any label hit, which beats any description hit: name
   `0/2/4/6/100`, label `1/3/5/7/110`, category `20/22/24/26`, description
   `30/32/34/36`. Boundary markers are `-`, `_`, `/`. Ties break by label, then
   name. `rank` returns the best `limit` items (default 20).
2. `SlashCommandCatalog.matching`, `SlashSkillFormatter.matching`, and
   `AgentSlashCommandSuggestion.matching` all route through it.
3. `SlashAutocompleteRanking` holds one pass's inputs so the view can hand it to
   `.task(id:)` and, for a large catalog, to a background task.
4. `SlashCommandAutocompleteView` renders from the ranked results, with
   `@ScaledMetric` row heights and relative fonts.

### Decisions worth knowing

- **An empty query keeps the curated order and the full list.** The built-in
  catalog is ordered deliberately (help, clear, model, workspace, …) and has 24
  entries; alphabetising and truncating it to 20 the moment you type `/` would
  be a regression. The bound exists to tame noisy matches, so it applies only to
  a real query.
- **Sections stayed.** Commands, then skills, then agent commands, each ranked
  and bounded on its own. Merging them into one ranked list would have needed
  group headers and a bigger visual change than this asked for.
- **`/skills` written output is unbounded.** A chat message listing matches
  passes `limit: .max`; only the popover is capped.
- **The "Agent command" placeholder no longer feeds ranking.** Every agent
  command without a server description shares that string, so matching on it
  would have surfaced all of them for a query like `comm`.
- **Agent commands are now excluded against the whole built-in catalog** rather
  than only the currently matched subset. A name you cannot type twice should
  never appear twice.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on the branch head via
  `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'id=E78D6EDB-…'` (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5) — **TEST SUCCEEDED**.
- 14 new tests in `SlashCommandTests`: every score tier for all four fields, no
  fuzzy on descriptions, best-field wins, score → label → name ordering, the
  empty-query passthrough, the top-20 bound, catalog and skill ranking, the
  unbounded written list, and the placeholder-description exclusion.
- `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` — the view grew past 500 LOC, so the ranking
  value types moved into `SlashAutocompleteRanking.swift`; both files are now
  under the limit.

## Owner checks

1. Open a chat and type `/`. The full command list appears in its usual order.
2. Type `/stop`. `/stop` is first, `/interrupt` below it.
3. Type `/code` against a server with skills. Skills whose slug has a `code`
   word (`claude-code`) rank above ones that only mention it in prose.
4. Type `/skills zzzz`. Reads "No skills match "zzzz"." rather than the old
   generic "No matches".
5. Settings → Display → a large Dynamic Type size, then reopen the popover. Rows
   grow with the text and the panel grows with them; descriptions truncate
   instead of pushing the command name off the row.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no `Codable` change here)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (client-side ranking only; no wire change)

title: feat(chat): trigger slash completion at the caret, not the whole draft
body:
Stacked on #383; merge after it.

## What changed

Typing `/` only opened the command panel when the *whole draft* started with it. So `write a note about /model` did nothing, and if the panel was open, picking a row replaced everything you had typed with `/model `.

The composer now knows where its caret is. It looks for the `/` the caret is sitting in — start of the draft or the middle of a sentence — and when you pick a row it swaps just that `/…` for the completion, leaves the rest of the draft alone, and parks the caret right after what it inserted. Undo puts back what you typed.

## Plan

1. `ComposerTextInputView` reports the caret up alongside the text, in one update, so the two can never disagree. A caret the composer places itself carries a revision, so a replayed update cannot yank the caret out from under the user, and a no-op `selectedRange` assignment is skipped because assigning it at all resets predictive text.
2. `ComposerSlashTrigger` finds the trigger at the caret and reports its range. A trigger is a `/` at the start of the draft or after whitespace, running to the caret, never across a line break. It may span a space only when the first word is a command that takes a sub-argument (`/skills`, `/workspace`, `/goal`, …), so ordinary prose like "check the /tmp folder" does not hold the panel open.
3. Accepting a row replaces only that range. A trailing space is dropped when the draft already has one there, and the caret steps over it instead.
4. Programmatic draft changes reach the editor as edits (`UITextView.replace(_:withText:)`) rather than a wholesale `text` assignment, which is what makes the change undoable.
5. A live IME composition is no longer committed half-formed by a parent rerender (#312): a binding that has merely not seen the marked text yet is an echo and is ignored; a deliberate clear or replacement still applies.

Files: `ComposerSlashTrigger.swift` (new), `ComposerTextEditing.swift` (new — selection, minimal edit, marked-text policy, lifted out of the bridge to keep it under the size warning), `ChatComposerTextInputView.swift`, `ChatComposerView.swift`, and `ComposerSlashTriggerTests.swift` (new).

Main risk is the caret: a UIKit text bridge that pushes selection down can fight the user. The revision counter is the guard, and the editor keeps the caret in every case except a completion.

## How it was tested

Full XCTest suite on the iPhone 17 simulator: **2010 tests, 0 failures** (2 pre-existing photo-library skips).

```
xcodebuild -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' test
```

title: feat(chat): show a skill you pick as a chip in the composer
body:
Stacked on #384; merge after it.

## What changed

Picking a skill out of the slash panel used to leave raw `/ask-matt ` sitting in the draft. Mid-sentence it read like typing noise, and backspacing through it chewed the name one letter at a time.

The composer now draws a skill reference as a single chip. Everything that leaves the editor — what is sent, copied, cut, and saved as a draft — is still the exact text you would have typed, so nothing about the message changes. Backspace next to a chip removes the whole reference. Copy and cut put the reference on the pasteboard, and pasting it back brings the chip with it, because chips are read out of the draft rather than stored beside it. Dropping images or files onto the editor on iPad now goes through the same attachment validation and upload as paste, instead of landing in the text as something the draft cannot represent.

**How it works.** A chip is a picture of a substring, never a replacement for it. `ComposerChipTokenizer` finds the `/skill` references in the draft — a `/` at a word boundary, a slug the server knows, whitespace after it — and the editor swaps each one for an image attachment that remembers its source string. Every caret the editor reports and every range the composer asks for crosses a small mapping layer that reads the chips back out of the rendered document, so the slash trigger from #384 and the draft store both keep working in plain draft coordinates.

**Plan.**
1. Verify the reference syntax against the live server before writing anything.
2. Pure, testable tokenizer plus the source↔display offset mapping.
3. Chip rendering that scales off the editor's own font, and the editor mechanisms from t3code's composer: atomic `deleteBackward`, source-serialising copy/cut, typing-attribute restore guarded by `markedTextRange`, and a `UITextDropDelegate` that claims a drop only when the composer can route every item.
4. Wire the skill list into the editor and warm it for a restored draft.
5. Focused tests for the tokenizer and the mapping; full suite green.

## Server contract

Verified against the live server rather than guessed: `GET /api/skills` returns names that are already slugs (`ask-matt`, `babysit-pr`), and upstream's own web UI inserts `/<slug>` for a skill row (`static/commands.js`, the `source:'skill'` branch). There is no `$skill` syntax. Hermex already sends `/<slug> <message>`, so this PR changes only how that string is drawn. No endpoint, model, or request shape changed.

## Notes and trade-offs

- **A reference becomes a chip once it is closed by whitespace.** A half-typed `/ask-ma` stays ordinary editable text, which is also what keeps the autocomplete panel usable. A chip at the very end of the draft survives deleting the space after it, so backspacing the space a completion added does not flicker it back into text.
- **Chips only appear for skills the app has heard of.** The skill list is fetched lazily; when a reopened chat's draft already names a skill, the composer now fetches the list on the spot rather than showing raw text until you open the panel once.
- **Rebuilding the document clears the editor's undo stack.** It happens only when the set of chips actually changes — never on ordinary typing — because an undo recorded against the old document would put back text the chips no longer describe. So `⌘Z` after accepting a *skill* row does nothing, while `⌘Z` after accepting a command row still restores what you typed.
- A slug that collides with a built-in command is never chipped: `/model` is the command, whatever a server calls its skills.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 (iOS 26.5): `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=E78D6EDB-…'` → **TEST SUCCEEDED**.
- New focused tests: `ComposerChipTokenizerTests` (boundary rules, unknown slug, built-in-command collision, multiple references, newline close, trailing preservation, empty catalog) and `ComposerChipDocumentTests` (serialisation of a selection, both offset directions, an offset inside a chip, range round-trip, clamping).
- Signed Debug build installed and launched on the same simulator; no launch or layout regression.
- Live server checked for the reference syntax as described above; no mutating call was made.

**Owner check (needs a connected server, so it is not automatable here):**
1. Open a chat, type `/ask` and pick a skill row → the row's reference becomes one chip with a hammer glyph, the caret sits after it.
2. Type a message and send → the transcript shows `/<slug> <message>`, exactly as before this PR.
3. Type `hello /` mid-sentence, pick a skill → only the trigger is replaced; the rest of the sentence survives.
4. Put the caret after the chip and press backspace once → the whole chip goes, not one letter.
5. Select across the chip, copy, paste into Notes → `/skill-name` in plain text. Paste it back into the composer → the chip returns.
6. Kill and reopen the app with that draft in place → the draft comes back with its chip.
7. VoiceOver over the composer, and one pass at the largest Dynamic Type size; on iPad, drag a photo and a file onto the editor and confirm both land in the attachment strip.

UI evidence: a screenshot needs a session against a real server, so it comes from the owner pass above rather than from CI.

Replaces #385, which GitHub permanently sealed: its base branch was #384's, so merging #384 with `--delete-branch` auto-closed it, and it could not be reopened once its head branch had been force-pushed. Same work, rebased onto `master`, plus two fixes found in owner testing.

Dropping images or files onto the editor on iPad now goes through the same attachment validation and upload as paste.

**How it works.** A chip is a picture of a substring, never a replacement for it. `ComposerChipTokenizer` finds the `/skill` references in the draft — a `/` at a word boundary, a slug the server knows, whitespace after it — and the editor swaps each one for an image attachment that remembers its source string. Every caret the editor reports and every range the composer asks for crosses a small mapping layer that reads the chips back out of the rendered document, so the slash trigger from #384 and the draft store both keep working in plain draft coordinates.

## Fixes since #385

**A restored draft came back as plain text.** The composer asks for the skill list from two `.task` modifiers — the chip warm-up and the autocomplete panel — and the warm-up is keyed on the draft, so hydrating the restored draft cancelled it. The request now lives on a task the view model owns: a cancelled caller cannot take it down, a caller arriving mid-flight awaits that same result, and a failed load clears the handle so the next caller retries.

**The chip vanished when the composer collapsed.** The pill that stands in for the editor drew the draft as plain text. It now lays the same baked chip image inline, so the two composer states cannot drift apart. The renderer memoizes each picture, because the pill draws from `body` and would otherwise re-bake a chip on every parent update during a stream. VoiceOver reads a chip by its label rather than announcing an image.

## Rebase note

#384 was squash-merged while this branch was stacked on it, so this is `git rebase --onto master`. One conflict, in `ChatComposerTextInputView.swift`: this branch renames `text`/`selectedRange` to `sourceText`/`sourceSelection` for chip coordinates, while #384 gained a `generation` parameter for its IME fix. - **Rebuilding the document clears the editor's undo stack.** Only when the set of chips actually changes — never on ordinary typing. So `⌘Z` after accepting a *skill* row does nothing, while `⌘Z` after accepting a command row still restores what you typed.

title: chore(chat): share one load across callers for personality suggestions
body:
`loadPersonalitySuggestions()` has the same shape as the skill loader that caused the chip bug in #386, and the same latent defect.

```swift
guard !hasLoadedPersonalitySuggestions else { return }
guard !isLoadingPersonalitySuggestions else { return }   // returns without awaiting
```

A caller arriving while a load is in flight returns immediately and finds an empty list. If the caller that owns the flag is inside a SwiftUI `.task` whose id changes, that task is cancelled, `client` throws `CancellationError`, the `catch` swallows it into `lastError`, `hasLoaded` stays `false`, and nothing retries. The list stays empty with no visible sign.

Not currently reachable in the same way — nothing warms personalities off a restored draft the way the chip code warms skills — so this is prevention, not a live bug.

**Fix:** the same shape #386 applied to skills. Put the request on a task the view model owns, have concurrent callers await that task, and clear the handle on failure so the next caller retries. `ChatViewModel.loadSkillSlashSuggestions()` on `master` is the reference.

**Test:** the regression test to copy is `ChatViewModelSendTests.testCancellingACallerDoesNotAbortTheSkillLoad`. Verify it fails against the unfixed loader before trusting it.

title: feat(chat): draw a skill reference as a chip in the message bubble
body:
#386 draws a skill reference as a chip in the composer, in both its expanded and collapsed states. Once the message is sent, the transcript bubble still shows raw `/skill-name` text, so the same reference is drawn two different ways either side of the send.

**Scope:** the transcript renderer, not the composer. The composer chip is a `UITextView` attachment; the bubble goes through the markdown pipeline, so this is a separate implementation with its own accessibility and text-selection behaviour. Deliberately split out of #386 to keep that PR to one concern.

**Open questions to settle before building:**

- A sent message is a historical record. If the skill has since been deleted or renamed on the server, does the chip disappear, or should the bubble keep drawing what was true when it was sent? Leaning toward: chip only when the slug still resolves, and plain text otherwise — same rule the composer uses, and it avoids storing anything beside the message.
- Copying a bubble must still yield the exact `/slug` text, the way the composer already guarantees.
- Text selection across a chip inside a markdown-rendered bubble is likely the hard part.

**Reusable pieces on `master` after #386:** `ComposerChipTokenizer` (pure, finds the references), `ComposerChipRenderer` (bakes the picture, memoized), and `ComposerChipTokenizer.spokenText(in:tokens:)` for the VoiceOver reading.

title: feat(session): /clear should clear server-side history, not just the local transcript
body:
## Context

`/clear` is registered as a client-side slash command (`SlashCommandCatalog.swift`, handler `.clientSide(.clear)`) and only calls `ChatViewModel.clearTranscript()`. The server keeps the full history, so the conversation returns on the next session load. The command's description says "Clear the current conversation", so today a shipped command lies.

Upstream `POST /api/session/clear` (pinned copy: `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py`, handler at the `/api/session/clear` branch) truncates the session to empty, sets the truncation watermark so state.db replay cannot resurrect the history, detaches compression lineage, resets the title to Untitled, and answers `{ok: true, session: <compact>}`. Errors answer `{error}` with 400 (subagent view-only) or 404 (not found). The `compact` shape is what the app already decodes as `SessionMutationResponse` for rename and archive.

`docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` lists the endpoint as roadmap P2, write, destructive.

## Current behavior

- `/clear` empties the on-screen transcript only. Reopening the session shows the full history again.
- No confirmation; the command runs immediately.
- Works while viewing cached data, because it never touches the server.
- `/help` describes it as "Clear the local transcript".

## Expected behavior

- Submitting `/clear` shows a destructive alert ("Clear Conversation?", buttons Cancel and destructive "Clear") before anything happens. Confirmation is always shown, including on an empty transcript.
- On confirm, the app calls `POST /api/session/clear` with body `{"session_id": ...}` and, on `ok`, empties the transcript, sets the display title from the returned session (Untitled), and writes the empty message list to the SwiftData cache so a cold open does not show the old chat. No refetch. The session list picks up the new title on its next refresh, as rename does today.
- Guards, in the same order and style as the undo slash command: viewing cached data refuses with "Reconnect to the server to clear the conversation"; CLI sessions refuse (WebUI sessions only); an active stream refuses and asks the user to wait. None of these make a server call.
- A server error (`error` in the body, or a thrown request error) surfaces through the existing slash `unsupported` path and leaves the local transcript intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Endpoint.clearSession` maps to `/api/session/clear`; `APIClient.clearSession(id:)` POSTs `SessionIDRequest` and decodes `SessionMutationResponse` tolerantly.
- [ ] The alert lives in `ChatView` on the slash send path; the view model exposes one async method that performs the server clear and returns a `SlashCommandExecutionResult`. No new result case.
- [ ] Guards: cached view, CLI session, and active stream each return `.unsupported` without a network call.
- [ ] On success: transcript empty, `displayTitle` reset from the response, cache written with an empty list, `.executed(message: nil)`.
- [ ] On failure: transcript unchanged, error message surfaced.
- [ ] `/help` text and the catalog description reflect the server-side clear.
- [ ] `docs/agents/upstream-smoke-checklist.md` gains a `POST /api/session/clear` block on the disposable session, next to the truncate block. `feature-gap-index.md` row moves from roadmap to done.

## Validation plan

- Unit tests (URLProtocol mock, existing `SlashCommandExecutorTests` / `ChatViewModel*Tests` patterns): request path and snake_case body; success adopts title and empties messages; `{error}` and thrown errors leave messages intact; each guard short-circuits with no request recorded.
- Contract: one mutating smoke against a disposable session created for the purpose (create, send one message, clear, `GET /api/session` shows zero messages and title Untitled, delete). Never against a real session.
- Simulator, manual: open a session with history, type `/clear`, cancel and confirm the transcript is unchanged; repeat and confirm, check the transcript empties and the nav title reads Untitled without leaving the screen; kill and relaunch, session still empty; back out to the session list, row title updated after refresh. Repeat once while a response is streaming and once on a CLI session to see the refusal copy.

## Non-goals

- `/goal clear` and the goal-controls "Clear" button (a different feature).
- Session delete, or confirmation changes for other destructive commands.
- Any change to compression or branch behavior beyond what the server does on clear.

title: fix(chat): offer only skills when the slash trigger is mid-sentence
body:
## Problem

Since #384, typing `/` anywhere in the draft opens the autocomplete panel. The panel offers built-in commands and agent commands alongside skills — but a command **cannot work anywhere except the start of the draft**, so picking one mid-sentence silently does nothing.

The gate is in `ChatView.swift`:

```swift
if submittedDraft.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).hasPrefix("/") {
    let result = await SlashCommandExecutor.execute(text: submittedDraft, viewModel: viewModel)
```

`SlashCommandExecutor.parse` trims and checks `hasPrefix("/")` again, so `hello /model gpt-5` never parses as a command. It goes to the server as literal prose.

This is the worst kind of failure: the UI confirms an action, inserts text that looks like a command, and nothing happens.

What actually works, per position:

| Draft | Works? |
| --- | --- |
| `/command-name` | yes |
| `/skill-name hello` | yes |
| `hello /skill-name test` | yes — **confirmed against a live server 2026-09-04**: the agent honors a skill reference that is not at the start of the message |
| `hello /command-name test` | **no** — sent as prose |

## Fix

When the trigger is not at the start of the draft, offer skills only. Exclude built-in commands and agent commands — agent commands are server-side custom commands and go through the same whole-draft gate, so they are equally dead mid-sentence.

This also makes the model coherent with #386: mid-sentence, the only thing that can work is a skill, and the only thing that draws as a chip is a skill.

## Implementation notes

- `ComposerSlashTrigger` already knows `range.location`; it needs to report whether the trigger starts the draft. "Start" should ignore leading whitespace, matching the executor's `trimmingCharacters` gate.
- A trigger at the start of a *line* but not of the draft is still mid-sentence — the executor trims the whole draft, not the line — so it gets skills only.
- Sub-argument commands are dead mid-sentence too (`/workspace ` in the middle of a sentence cannot execute), so the same exclusion covers them. Worth checking this does not fight the `allowsSpaces` rule added in #384.
- Likely files: `ComposerSlashTrigger.swift`, `ChatComposerView.swift` (`showsSlashAutocomplete` / `slashQuery`), `SlashAutocompleteRanking.swift`, `SlashCommandAutocompleteView.swift`.

## Tests

- A trigger at the start of the draft still offers commands, agent commands, and skills.
- Leading whitespace before the trigger still counts as the start.
- A trigger after other text offers skills only.
- A trigger at the start of a second line offers skills only.
- Existing `ComposerSlashTriggerTests` continue to pass.

## Verifying

Needs a manual simulator pass against a live server: mid-sentence `/` shows no command rows; start-of-draft `/` is unchanged; a mid-sentence skill still runs on the agent.

title: feat(tasks): show recent runs across all tasks on the Tasks list
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #378

## What changed

The Tasks list said what was scheduled but not what actually ran; you had to open each task to find out. Now a **Ran Recently** group sits at the top of the list showing every task's last run, newest first, with a green/red dot and a relative time. Tapping a row opens that task's detail. Rows for tasks the list does not have are display-only, with no chevron and no button trait.

How: `TasksViewModel.load()` kicks off `GET /api/crons/recent` on its own task, so the list renders as soon as `/api/crons` answers and the feed fills in when it arrives, or quietly stays absent on any failure (including a 404 from an older server). A reload cancels the previous feed fetch so a late answer cannot overwrite a newer one. Rows match a job by id first, falling back to name.

Contract verified against the live server on 2026-09-04: `/api/crons/recent` returns `{completions: [{job_id, name, status, completed_at, toast_notifications, session_id, message_count}], since}`, unordered, so the client sorts. `/api/crons` returns real ids under `id` (only the `job_id` key is null), which the app already reads, so id matching does resolve; name stays as the fallback the issue asks for.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` on iPhone 17: 2067 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
- New tests in `CronManagementViewModelTests`: feed loads newest-first and matches jobs by id then name, a malformed `message_count` / `completed_at` decodes without trapping, a slow feed does not hold `isLoading`, and a 404 feed leaves the list and error state untouched. `APIEndpointContractTests` covers the new endpoint path.

title: Upstream API parity tracker
body:
## Purpose

Track adoption of every upstream `hermes-webui` endpoint Hermex does not use yet. Upstream at the refreshed pin (2026-08-25) exposes 221 literal route paths; the app references 122. This issue holds the ordered plan and the decisions behind it. Every item was filed as its own sub-issue on 2026-09-06 (#417 to #444); each body names its routes and handler lines at the pin and requires shape validation against the pin or a live server before implementation. Tick the checkbox when the sub-issue closes.

## Decisions (2026-09-04, revised 2026-09-06 at intake)

- **Full parity.** Users should be able to do most things from Hermex. Only browser or desktop-only routes are excluded.
- **One feature per sub-issue**, naming every endpoint it touches. Never one endpoint per issue.
- **Order:** smallest and safest first, dependencies respected, reads before writes.
- **Placement:**
  - Per-session reads live in a new Session details sheet reachable from the chat menu and the session list context menu. Per-session actions live in both menus. Bulk actions live on the session list only.
  - Provider, model, and profile writes extend the existing Settings screens that already show their reads.
  - Things with no home today (MCP, plugins, updates, health, logs) go under one new Server section in Settings.
  - Workspace file management builds on the file tree (#401). Editing builds on the source viewer (#400).
  - Wiki and notes are read-only screens under Memory.
  - Server status and logs are a sibling of the planned per-server connection dashboard, not merged into it.
  - Server-wide session store checks (recovery audit and safe repair) live under Server, not in the per-session sheet: those routes take no session id.

## Sub-issues, in order

- [ ] 1. #417 Gap-index refresh. Docs only: mark git-info, git, and rollback rows as shipped (the app uses sixteen git routes), add rows for every uncurated route below, mark the exclusions n-a.
- [ ] 2. #419 Session details sheet, reads: `/api/session/usage`, `/api/session/lineage/report`, `/api/session/worktree/status`. Adds the Session details row to the chat session menu that 3 creates.
- [ ] 3. #418 Title regenerate: `/api/session/title/regenerate`, in the session list context menu and in a new chat session menu (the chat toolbar has no session menu today; this item creates it). Filed before 2.
- [ ] 4. #420 Rollback in the Git sheet: `/api/rollback/list`, `/api/rollback/diff`, `/api/rollback/restore`. Restore gets the discard-style confirmation.
- [ ] 5a. #422 Provider keys in Settings: `POST /api/providers` (set key), `/api/providers/delete`, `/api/models/refresh`. `/api/providers/self-hosted` is skipped (desktop setup wizard).
- [ ] 5b. #423 Auxiliary model routing in Settings: `/api/model/auxiliary`, `/api/model/set` with `scope: auxiliary`.
- [ ] 5c. #424 Provider cost history on the Usage screen: `/api/provider/cost-history`.
- [ ] 6. #425 Profile delete on the profiles screen: `/api/profile/delete`. Create already shipped; `/api/profile/active` is redundant with the `active` field of `/api/profiles`.
- [ ] 7. #426 Skills: `/api/skills/save`, `/api/skills/delete`, `/api/skills/usage`.
- [ ] 8a. #427 Wiki, read-only, under Memory: `/api/wiki/status`, `/api/wiki/browse`, `/api/wiki/page`.
- [ ] 8b. #428 Notes, read-only, under Memory: `/api/notes/search`, `/api/notes/sources`, `/api/notes/item`.
- [ ] 9a. #429 Server section in Settings with MCP servers and tools: `/api/mcp/servers`, `PATCH /api/mcp/servers/<name>` (enable toggle), `/api/mcp/tools`. Creates the Server card.
- [ ] 9b. #430 Plugins list under Server: `/api/plugins`, read only.
- [ ] 10. #431 Settings write: `/api/settings` for bot name, check for updates, ignore agent updates, update channel, and max tokens. Password and passkey operations are excluded. Today only `show_cli_sessions` is written.
- [ ] 11a. #435 Per-session toolset restriction in the details sheet: `/api/session/toolsets`.
- [ ] 11b. #436 Background compression: `/api/session/compress/start`, `/api/session/compress/status`, replacing the one-shot `/api/session/compress` call behind `/compress`.
- [ ] 11c. #437 Worktree remove in the details sheet, next to the worktree status from 2: `/api/session/worktree/remove`.
- [ ] 11d. #438 Compression recovery in the details sheet: `/api/session/compression-recovery/start`.
- [ ] 12. #432 Bulk session cleanup in the Settings Sessions card (the session list has no toolbar or edit mode): `/api/sessions/cleanup`, `/api/sessions/cleanup_zero_message`.
- [ ] 13. #433 Admin writes: `/api/updates/force` and `/api/updates/clear_lock` next to the existing Update button in the Active Server card; `/api/health/restart` (restarts the active profile's gateway service, not the web server) in the Server card from 9a.
- [ ] 13b. #434 Session store health under Server: `/api/session/recovery/audit`, `/api/session/recovery/repair-safe`. Both are server-wide.
- [ ] 14a. #439 File tree context menu: `/api/file/create`, `/api/file/create-dir`, `/api/file/rename`, `/api/file/move`, `/api/file/delete`, `/api/file/path`. Builds on the file tree from #401.
- [ ] 14b. #440 Workspace transfer: `/api/workspace/upload` into a folder, `/api/folder/download` as a zip. After 14a.
- [ ] 15. #441 Workspace file editing: `/api/file/save`. The source viewer shipped in #400; still after 14a.
- [ ] 16. #442 Escape reads outside the workspace: `/api/escape/authorize`, `/api/escape/list`, `/api/escape/file/read`, `/api/escape/file/raw`. Blocked upstream: authorize is browser-only (Origin + CSRF); ready-for-human.
- [ ] 17. #443 Server status section in Settings, reads only: `/api/system/health`, `/api/health/agent`, `/api/gateway/status`, `/api/dashboard/status`, `/api/dashboard/config`, `/api/project-os/dashboard`. `/api/updates/summary` stays dropped (it fires a server LLM call). **Low priority, may be skipped.**
- [ ] 18. #444 Server logs screen under Server: `/api/logs`. **Low priority, may be skipped.**
- [ ] 19. #421 Live session list: `GET /api/sessions/events`, the server-sent stream that fires on create, rename, archive, and delete, so the list updates without pull-to-refresh. Filed with the first batch; small and felt daily.

## Order and blockers

The sub-issue list on this issue is the tracking order (top to bottom). Blocked-by relationships are set on the issues themselves; in short:

- #418 → #419 → #435, #436, #437, #438
- #429 → #430, #433, #434, #443, #444
- #439 → #440, #441
- #420 waits for the local Git sheet polish draft; #422 and #423 wait for the local model picker polish draft (both are not on GitHub yet)
- #442 waits on an upstream decision
- #417, #421, #424, #425, #426, #427, #428, #431, #432 have no blockers

## Deliberately skipped

- Share links (`/api/share/create`, `/api/share/revoke`, `/api/share/<token>`): owner decision.
- Extensions (`/api/extensions/*`): owner decision.
- Draft sync (`/api/session/draft`): local drafts win; two-way sync is a conflict source for little gain.
- Handoff summary and conversation rounds (`/api/session/handoff-summary`, `/api/session/conversation-rounds`): gateway-session features, and the summary runs the session's model on demand.
- Session import (`/api/session/import`): nobody round-trips exported JSON on a phone.
- Self-hosted provider setup (`/api/providers/self-hosted`): desktop setup wizard.
- Command bundles and mixture-of-agents (`/api/commands/bundles`, `/api/commands/bundles/resolve`, `/api/commands/moa/resolve`): no invocation path in the app.
- Terminal (`/api/terminal/*`) and plugin command exec (`/api/commands/exec`): App Store and safety sensitive; revisit separately.
- The model picker badges polish (default and legacy labels) is optional and independent of this tracker, but should land before 5a touches the same picker.

## Not applicable (browser, desktop, or server-internal)

CSP report, client event log, file reveal, open in VS Code, office-save, admin reload, approval and clarify inject-test, shutdown, upload/extract, onboarding and its OAuth, passkeys, OIDC, `bg-task-complete-ack`, `process-complete-ack`, `anchor-scene` (browser transcript rendering state), and the loopback-only `/api/session/stream`.

## Already owned elsewhere

Cron history (#378), saved prompts (#275), transcription (voice epic #36), session clear (#389), provider quota on the Usage screen (#415).

## Rules for every sub-issue

- Validate the endpoint's request and response shape against `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` or a live server before implementation. Never invent a shape.
- Tolerant `Codable` models. Mutating smokes run against one disposable session only.
- Destructive actions get a confirmation that states the real consequence, and every one-way action ships with its reverse where upstream provides one.
- Update `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` when the sub-issue lands.

title: feat(session): clear server-side history for /clear
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #389

## What changed

`/clear` only emptied the transcript on screen. The server kept the whole conversation, so it came back on the next session load — the command's own description ("Clear the current conversation") was a lie.

Submitting `/clear` now asks first ("Clear Conversation?", Cancel / destructive Clear). On confirm the app POSTs `/api/session/clear`, empties the transcript, adopts the title the server returns (Untitled), and rewrites the offline cache as an empty list so a cold open doesn't repaint the history. No refetch; the session list picks up the new title on its next refresh, exactly like rename.

The guards match `/undo` and all short-circuit before any network call: viewing cached data, CLI sessions, and an active stream each refuse with copy that says why. A server `{error}` or a thrown request leaves the transcript untouched and surfaces through the existing slash `unsupported` path.

Two supporting notes:

- `ChatView.body` is split into `chatContent` plus its confirmation-alert chain, and the approval overlay moved to its own property. One more `.alert` pushed the single chained expression past the compiler's type-checking budget; the split is mechanical, no behavior change.
- `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` drops the `/api/session/clear` roadmap row — `implemented` is derived from `Endpoints.swift`, so the row would otherwise contradict the code. The issue also asked for a block in `docs/agents/upstream-smoke-checklist.md`, but that doc was deleted from the repo in #305 and only exists as an untracked local file, so it's left alone rather than re-added here.

## How it was tested

Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` (scheme `HermesMobile`, iPhone 17) on `5beca9e`: **2074 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.

New focused tests:

- `APIClientSessionMutationTests` — `/api/session/clear` path, snake_case `session_id` body, tolerant decode of `{ok, session}`, and the upstream 400 (view-only subagent) surfacing as a thrown `APIError.http`.
- `ContractReadinessTests` — endpoint contract row for `.clearSession`.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests` — success empties the transcript, adopts the returned title, and empties the SwiftData cache; a `{error}` body and a thrown request both leave messages intact; cached-view, CLI-session, and streaming guards each refuse with no request recorded.

The stale `testClearSlashCommandClearsLocalTranscriptWithoutServerRequest` was removed — it asserted the bug this PR fixes.

Endpoint verified against the pinned upstream handler in `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py` (`/api/session/clear` → truncate-to-empty, watermark sentinel, title reset, `{"ok": true, "session": s.compact()}`). No live-server smoke has been run yet.

### Owner checks

Needs `needs-manual-validation`, on a real server:

1. Open a session with history, type `/clear`, **Cancel** → transcript unchanged, `/clear` still in the composer.
2. Repeat and **Clear** → transcript empties, nav title reads Untitled, no navigation away.
3. Kill and relaunch → session still empty (cache check).
4. Back out to the session list → row title updates after refresh.
5. While a response is streaming, and on a CLI session → refusal copy, nothing cleared.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (reuses `SessionMutationResponse`)

title: fix(sessions): refresh the session list when returning from a chat
body:
## Context

`SessionListNewChatReturn.run` (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1366`) is the only return-refresh the list has, and its first line is `guard case .newChat = oldValue else { return }`. Returning from `.session(...)` exits immediately, so nothing re-reads session metadata.

The other refresh triggers don't cover it either: the cold-load `.task` (`:225`) runs once, `.refreshable` (`:539`) is manual, and `monitorActiveSessionRows` (`:1052`) only polls while rows have live stream IDs. The `.onAppear` that calls `refreshAfterReturningIfNeeded()` (`:254`, `:1048`) is attached to `navigationContainer` (`:113`), which stays mounted across the push, so it does not re-fire on a pop — and on regular width the sidebar never disappears at all.

There is no other path. `ChatViewModel` updates only its own `displayTitle` (`:3004`, `:5060`), never calls `CacheStore.cacheSession` for a rename, and gets no callback or binding from the list (`ChatView` takes `session: SessionSummary` by value, `SessionListView.swift:387`). Nothing reads `CachedSession` via `@Query`, so a cache write would not help.

Found while validating #389: `/clear` resets the title to Untitled, and the row keeps the old title. `/title` and server auto-titling have the same gap.

## Current behavior

- Rename or clear a session from inside its chat, then go back: the row shows the stale title, message count, and timestamp until pull-to-refresh, an active-stream poll, or a cold start.
- Returning from a **new** chat does refresh, correctly.

## Expected behavior

- Navigating away from any destination refreshes the session list, so the row reflects what just happened in the chat.
- Returning from an unused new chat still shows no empty Untitled row, not even transiently.

## Implementation notes

Extend the existing pure seam rather than adding a new one. `SessionListNewChatReturn.run` becomes: when `oldValue != nil && oldValue != newValue`, call `refreshSessions()`; call `suppressEmptyPlaceholders()` first **only** when `oldValue` was `.newChat`, exactly as today. The `.newChat` → `.newChat` route replacement must keep doing nothing. Rename the type to match its widened job.

On regular width this also fires when switching between sessions in the sidebar, which is the intended freshness win.

The empty-Untitled flash (#83/#84) cannot return through this: the placeholder is filtered out of every server response by `shouldAppearInSessionList` inside `load()` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:228`) and at both local insert sites (`:484`, `:1057`). The predicate, not the absence of a refresh, is what suppresses it — and #215 already pairs a refresh with that path today.

Error handling stays as-is (`loadSessions()` → `handleLastError()`), identical to the new-chat return today. A failed refresh on return therefore behaves exactly like a failed pull-to-refresh, including the offline banner. No silent-failure mode; if that turns out to be noisy in practice, it is a follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Returning from an existing session refreshes the list; the row's title, message count, and timestamp match the server.
- [ ] Returning from a new chat still suppresses empty placeholders synchronously, then refreshes.
- [ ] Replacing one `.newChat` route with another still refreshes nothing.
- [ ] On regular width, selecting a different session in the sidebar refreshes the list.
- [ ] No refresh fires when there was no previous destination.

## Validation plan

- Unit: extend `SessionNavigationStateTests` (`:157`–`:207`), which already drives this helper with a recorded event list — add the `.session` → `nil`, `.session` → `.session`, `.utility` → `nil`, and `nil` → `.session` cases.
- Simulator, manual: run `/clear` in a session, back out, row reads Untitled with no pull-to-refresh; same for `/title`. Tap "Chat", back out without sending, and watch closely for an Untitled row appearing at any point, including a slow-motion pass. On iPad, switch between two sessions and confirm rows stay current.

## Non-goals

- Pushing title changes from `ChatViewModel` into the list or the SwiftData cache.
- Observing `CachedSession` with `@Query`.
- Changing the `shouldAppearInSessionList` predicate.
- Any throttling of the refresh.

title: feat(git): review every changed file in one diff surface
body:
## Linked issue

Maintainer-scoped Git review work; no tracking issue.

## What changed

Opening a Git diff gave you one file per sheet as a SwiftUI list: no word-level highlights, no sticky file headers, no way to mark a file as reviewed, and no way to hand a few lines to the agent.

Now the Git changes sheet, the turn recap's "Open diff", and its file rows all open one surface with every changed file:

- **Sticky file headers** that the next file's header pushes off.
- **Collapse and viewed** per file. Tapping the checkbox marks the file viewed and collapses it; un-viewing leaves it collapsed. Collapsing keeps the header where it is drawn, so you are not thrown to another file.
- **Word-level highlights** on paired deleted/added lines, gated so rewrites stay plain (max 4 ranges, ≤ 45 % coverage, lines ≤ 1000 chars, gaps ≤ 1 merged).
- **Striped delete bar** next to the solid add bar, so deletions read without relying on red alone.
- **Per-file horizontal pan** with display-link deceleration; the line-number gutter stays put.
- **Line selection**: tap selects one line, long-press then tap selects a range. **Add to prompt** appends the path, line range, and a fenced diff to the composer draft and closes the sheet.
- **Pull-to-refresh** with a spinner the reload owns.

How: `ReviewDiffCanvasView` is a UIKit canvas sized to the viewport that slides with the scroll offset and draws only the rows intersecting it (four-row overscan) from a flat `ReviewDiffRow` list; `ReviewDiffLayout` is the prefix-sum layout with binary-search hit testing. The canvas is a port of an MIT-licensed native diff view; the notice is kept in the file header. `GitDiffView` is now the multi-file host: it fetches `git/diff` per file, four in flight, starting with the file you tapped, and rebuilds rows off the main thread as each answer lands while the surface keeps the file under the reader anchored. The existing `DiffHunk` parser is unchanged and feeds the row model.

VoiceOver sees the canvas as a container whose elements are created on demand for visible rows (line number, change type, text; headers expose collapse and viewed as actions). Fonts scale with Dynamic Type and rebuild the layout. Colours are system semantic colours, so light and dark resolve at draw time. Draw and layout passes emit `ReviewDiff` signposts.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on the iPhone 17 simulator via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim`: **2103 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** on the final head.
- New focused tests: `ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests` (row ids, notices for loading/failed/binary/too-large/empty, renames, tab expansion, server counts win), `ReviewWordDiffTests` (changed-word ranges, single-character joins, whitespace trim, coverage and count gates, long-line skip, pairing stops at hunk rows), `ReviewDiffLayoutTests` (prefix sums, collapsed heights, hit testing, sticky push-off, visible file), `ReviewDiffSelectionTests` (tap/long-press state machine, Markdown snippet).
- Manual pass by the maintainer on the simulator against the live server: multi-file surface, word highlight, striped delete bar, line selection, and Add to prompt confirmed. Screenshots to follow as a comment.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no model changes)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (reuses the existing `GET /api/git/diff` per file)

title: feat(workspace): browse the workspace as a lazily loaded file tree
body:
## Linked issue

Maintainer-scoped workspace work; no tracking issue.

## What changed

The Files screen showed one folder at a time with Root, Up, and breadcrumbs, and search only filtered that folder. Finding a file three levels down meant three round trips and three screens of context lost.

Now the workspace is one nested tree:

- **Folders first, natural order** (`file2` before `file10`), with a child count once a folder has been listed.
- **Top-level folders open on first visit**, hidden dot-folders stay closed. Every folder is listed from `/api/list` only when it is first opened; nothing recursive, no whole-workspace fetch. Open folders are fetched in parallel.
- **Tap a folder to open or close it.** A failed listing shows a warning mark and tapping retries. Pull to refresh re-lists the root and every open folder and keeps them open.
- **Search over loaded nodes** with t3code's tiered scoring (exact, prefix, boundary, substring, then fuzzy on camelCase-split words). Every token must match; a folder stays visible when any descendant matches, so results keep their path context. Collapsed folders are searched too.
- **Press-down prefetch.** Holding a file row starts its `/api/file` fetch before the tap lands; opening the file hands that fetch to the preview and cancels any other prefetch. Images and known binaries are not prefetched.
- **Expansion state persists per server and workspace** (`fileTree.expanded|<server>|<workspace>` in UserDefaults), so one server's layout never shows up under another.
- Opening a file marks it selected and opens every folder above it, listing any that were not fetched yet.

Rows are 42 pt, indented 18 pt per level, with folder, file, and symlink symbols. The richer per-type icon map is a separate piece of work. Every user-facing string reuses an existing catalog key, so no String Catalog change.

`WorkspaceEntry` gained a memberwise init and `Hashable` (needed for `navigationDestination(item:)`); decoding is unchanged and still tolerant.

title: fix(chat): allow sending attachments without composer text
body:
## Context

The composer disables send when the draft is empty, even with staged attachments. Upstream `hermes-webui` requires a non-empty `message` in `POST /api/chat`, but its web UI allows attachment-only sends by synthesizing the message text (`static/messages.js`, `sendMessage`): `I've uploaded N file(s): <paths>`. - Send is enabled when trimmed text is non-empty OR at least one attachment is staged and not mid-upload.

title: feat(chat): render Markdown workspace images and zoom them in a full-bleed viewer
body:
## Linked issue

No issue; maintainer-approved work.

## What changed

An assistant message written as `![alt](path)` showed nothing at all. The destination went to the Markdown renderer's network image loader, which has no URL to fetch and draws an empty box, so a screenshot the agent had just written was simply invisible. Markdown images now take the same route `MEDIA:` tokens already take: the authenticated media loader, the transcript thumbnail, and the preview surface, with the alt text as the accessibility label.

Containment for media stays with the server. `/api/media` owns the allow-list, and chat images live in the server's own attachment store (`~/.hermes/webui/attachments/`) rather than in any session workspace, so a client-side workspace check only hides images the server is happy to serve. Absolute paths and `file:` URLs pass straight through, `./`, `../`, and `~/` resolve against the workspace, and bare relative paths and `https://` stay with the Markdown renderer, exactly as they do for file links. Nothing new is reachable: `MEDIA:/any/path.png` has always been sent as written.

Opening an image used to land in a scrolling sheet with the picture fit to about a third of the screen, so reading a screenshot meant pinching every time, and pinching did nothing. Images now open full-bleed:

- Pinch, double tap to zoom to the point you tapped, and pan while zoomed, on a small `UIScrollView` surface rather than stacked SwiftUI gestures.
- Flick down to close, but only at fit scale, so the close gesture can never steal a pan from a zoomed image.
- One tap hides the floating chrome so nothing covers the picture. VoiceOver keeps it up, because a hidden Done button is not a way out.
- Reduce Motion drops the close animation.
- Path, file size, Save to Photos, and Export all survive, in a floating bar and caption.

Audio, video, text, and unavailable previews keep the sheets they had. Closing the viewer now restores composer focus when the keyboard was up beforehand, which the transcript media sheet never did.

Structure:

- `TranscriptMediaParser` recognises `![alt](destination "title")`, including angle-bracketed destinations, and skips fenced and inline code.
- `FileReference.absoluteMediaPath` accepts the same syntax as `parse` without its workspace containment, which is right for links and wrong for media.
- `ImageLightboxView` is the shared shell; `ImageLightboxGesturePolicy` holds the thresholds as plain values so they are testable without a scroll view.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` on iPhone 17: **2183 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** (the pre-existing photo-library integration skips).

- Verified against the maintainer's live server rather than assumed: the failing message was `![Image](file:///Users/hermes/.hermes/webui/attachments/<session>/image_…jpg)`, whose session workspace is `/Users/hermes/projects/workspace`. `GET /api/media?session_id=…&path=…` returned `200 image/jpeg`, 292 KB, which is what showed the client-side containment check was wrong.

title: feat(chat): reference workspace files from the composer with @path chips
body:
## Linked issue

Composer follow-up to #386 (skill chips) and #402 (file links and icons); no separate issue.

## What changed

You could not point the agent at a workspace file from the phone: you typed the path from memory or copied it out of the file browser.

Typing `@` in the composer now opens a panel listing the folder you are typing into, folders first, each with its file-type icon. It lists only that one folder through the existing `/api/list` endpoint, scored with the file tree's scorer, capped at 20 rows, and never fetches the workspace recursively. Symlinks that leave the workspace and any `..` path are never offered.

Picking a file inserts `@<workspace-relative path> ` and the composer draws it as a chip with the file's icon. Picking a folder inserts `@folder/` and drills in. Tapping a composer chip opens the file in the source viewer. What is sent, copied, and saved as a draft is always the plain `@path`; chips are pictures of a substring, the same mechanism as skill chips.

**Chips survive leaving the chat.** The accepted paths are not stored; the server is the authority. On opening a chat, the view model scans the restored draft and the sent messages for `@path` candidates, lists each parent folder once, and chips the ones the folder actually contains. The request is owned by the view model like the skill loader, so a cancelled caller cannot kill it and a failure retries on the next open. Those listings also warm the `@` panel.

title: fix(chat): count "Working for" and "Worked for" from the server's turn start
body:
## Context

The transcript tail row shows "Working for Xm Ys" during a run and a fold row "Worked for Xm Ys" once the turn settles. Both derive from `ChatStreamCoordinator.activeRunStartedAt`, which is stamped with the local clock whenever `activeStreamID` changes (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:112`). Adopting an already-running stream on session load (`reconcileSessionLoad`) counts as a change, so the counter restarts on every return to the session.

The comment there claims the server does not report when the run started. It does. The session detail carries `pending_started_at` (decoded as `SessionDetail.pendingStartedAt` in `HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift`, currently only written to the cache and never read), and the settled assistant message carries `_turnDuration` (`ChatMessage.turnDuration`).

Upstream `hermes-webui` starts its live timer from `pending_started_at` (`static/ui.js:14674`, `static/messages.js:1912` for the start response) and labels the finished turn from `_turnDuration` (`static/ui.js:18889`), which is why its timer survives a page refresh.

## Current behavior

1. Open a session with an active stream (cold open, back from the session list, or foreground after backgrounding). "Working for" restarts at 0s.
2. When the turn finishes after such a return, the fold row shows the time since reattach (for example "Worked for 52s") until the transcript reloads, then jumps to the server value (5m 17s). Reproduced on session `29531dadc4dd`, whose final assistant message has `_turnDuration: 317.21`. The fold label (`TranscriptTurnFolding.swift`, `elapsedSeconds`) prefers `_turnDuration`, but the `done` event does not carry it, so the client-measured run ending (`recordRunEndingIfRunning`, built from the reset start date) wins until the next transcript load.
3. The Live Activity elapsed label has the same offset because `startLiveActivity` lets `liveActivityManager.start` default `startedAt` to `Date()`.

## Expected behavior

Both labels and the Live Activity count from the server's turn start and settle on the server's duration, matching the web UI within a second in every entry path.

## Acceptance criteria

- `activeRunStartedAt` is seeded from the server's `pending_started_at` when a stream is adopted on session load or reattach; a same-stream reattach never resets it.
- A fresh send seeds it from `pending_started_at` in the `/api/chat/start` response when present (add the optional field to `ChatStartResponse` in `HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift`), else from the local send time.
- Fallback when the server omits `pending_started_at`: the latest user message's timestamp, then discovery time. Never crash or show a negative value; clamp to zero.
- The run ending recorded at completion (`recordRunEndingIfRunning`) spans from that seeded start, so the client-measured "Worked for" is within one second of `_turnDuration` even before the post-completion transcript refresh lands. The server's `_turnDuration` still wins once present.
- Leaving and re-entering a settled session does not change the "Worked for" value.
- The Live Activity `startedAt` uses the same seeded date.
- The stale comment above `activeRunStartedAt` in `ChatStreamCoordinator.swift` is updated.
- Tests in `HermesMobileTests/ChatStreamCoordinatorTests.swift`: adoption on load with a `pendingStartedAt` yields that start; same-stream reattach keeps it; the recorded ending spans from it; fallback order when the field is nil. One `TranscriptTurnFoldingTests` case for a client outcome seeded from a server start.

## Validation plan

- Route shapes: `curl` `/api/sessions/<id>` on a running session to confirm `pending_started_at` is a float epoch, and POST `/api/chat/start` on one disposable session to confirm whether the response includes `pending_started_at`. Record the verified shapes in the PR.
- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17.
- Manual simulator plan: start a long-running prompt, go to the session list and back, confirm the counter is continuous; background the app for a minute and foreground, confirm again; let the turn finish and compare "Worked for" to the web UI's "Done in" for the same session; check the Live Activity elapsed matches.

## Non-goals

Changing the fold layout or the elapsed formatter. Session-list elapsed indicators. Adopting upstream's compact worklog "Done in" wording.

The composer card uses `cardCornerRadius` (26pt, continuous) in `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift`. The surfaces rendered in the same bottom stack above it each hard-code their own radius, so the stack reads as a set of unrelated shapes:

title: feat(usage): show provider account limits on the Usage screen
body:
## Context

Supersedes #210 and takes `/api/provider/quota` out of #395 item 5. Requested again by cagnulein in https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/395#issuecomment-5549965535.

Upstream exposes `GET /api/provider/quota?provider=<id>[&refresh=1]`. Verified against the live server on 2026-09-05 and against `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/providers.py` (`get_provider_quota`, `_serialize_account_usage_snapshot`, `_sanitize_openrouter_quota`). Two payload families:

Account limits (`openai-codex`, `anthropic`):

```json
{
  "ok": true, "provider": "openai-codex", "display_name": "OpenAI Codex",
  "supported": true, "status": "available", "label": "Account limits", "quota": null,
  "account_limits": {
    "plan": "Plus", "title": "Account limits", "available": true, "unavailable_reason": null,
    "fetched_at": "2026-09-06T02:56:37.848820Z",
    "windows": [
      {"label": "Session", "used_percent": 0.0, "remaining_percent": 100.0, "reset_at": "2026-09-06T07:55:41Z", "detail": "Best of 1 available credentials"},
      {"label": "Weekly",  "used_percent": 98.0, "remaining_percent": 2.0,  "reset_at": "2026-09-07T02:28:47Z", "detail": null}
    ],
    "details": ["1/1 credentials available", "Plans: Plus"],
    "pool": { "...": "ignore" }
  },
  "message": "OpenAI Codex account limits loaded."
}
```

Credits (`openrouter`):

```json
{
  "ok": true, "provider": "openrouter", "display_name": "OpenRouter",
  "supported": true, "status": "available", "label": "OpenRouter credits",
  "quota": {"limit_remaining": 0, "usage": 10.0296785, "limit": 10},
  "message": "OpenRouter quota status loaded."
}
```

`limit` and `limit_remaining` are null when the key has no spending cap. Other statuses seen live: `unsupported` (`supported: false`), `unavailable` (`account_limits: null`, human-readable `message`), `no_key`, and `invalid_key`. Without `provider` the server answers for the active provider. The server caches account-limit probes for 45 s; `refresh=1` bypasses the cache. A cold probe can take several seconds.

## Current behavior

The Usage screen (`HermesMobile/Features/Insights/`) shows only local token and cost analytics from `GET /api/insights`. Subscription limits and credits are invisible; the web UI shows them only when the limited provider is the active one.

## Expected behavior

A "Limits" card group at the top of the Usage screen, above the window picker, one card per provider with an available quota. Reference design: the screenshot below (Codex app). The screenshot is the approved design; no mock round is needed.

Account-limits card:
- Header: provider `display_name` on the left, `plan` as a capsule on the right when present.
- One row per window: `label` verbatim on the left, "N% left" on the right in bold, a full-width progress bar of `remaining_percent`, and a "Resets in Xh Ym" line from `reset_at` (day granularity past 24h, e.g. "Resets in 1d 3h"; "Resets soon" when past).
- Windows with a nil `remaining_percent` show the label and reset only, no bar.
- Footer: "Updated N sec/min ago" from `fetched_at`.

Credits card (OpenRouter):
- Header: `display_name`, no capsule.
- One row labeled "Credits": "$N left" from `limit_remaining` in bold; bar of `limit_remaining / limit` when `limit` is present, otherwise no bar; secondary line "$usage used of $limit", or "$usage used" when there is no limit.
- Footer: "Updated N sec ago" from the client's fetch time (the payload has no timestamp).

Both cards: bar and amount text tint is accent normally, orange at ≤ 25% left, red at ≤ 10% left. Money formats with the user's locale in USD.

Provider selection: the set {active provider, `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, `openrouter`}, filtered to entries `/api/providers` reports with `has_key == true`, deduplicated, fetched concurrently. Render only providers whose response has `status == "available"` and either non-empty `account_limits.windows` or a non-null `quota`. Everything else (unsupported, unavailable, no_key, invalid_key, HTTP 404 on an older server, decode failure) hides silently; the analytics below are unaffected. When no provider qualifies the group is absent.

Loading: quota loads independently of `/api/insights`; a slow probe never delays the chart. Initial load and the window-change reload do not pass `refresh`. The toolbar Refresh button and pull-to-refresh pass `refresh=1`. Stale results from a superseded load are discarded (same generation-token pattern as `ProvidersViewModel`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `Endpoint.providerQuota(provider:refresh:)` builds `/api/provider/quota?provider=<id>` and appends `refresh=1` only when asked. An `APIClient` extension returns a tolerant `ProviderQuotaResponse` (`status`, `displayName`, `accountLimits { plan, windows[label, usedPercent, remainingPercent, resetAt, detail], fetchedAt, available }`, `quota { limitRemaining, usage, limit }`; every field optional; `pool` ignored).
- `InsightsViewModel` gains `limitCards` and the selection rule above; `InsightsDataClient` grows `providers()` and `providerQuota(provider:refresh:)` so tests script both.
- Failure of any quota call never sets the screen's error state or calls `onAPIError`.
- The card group is absent when no provider qualifies.
- Presentation helpers (percent text, money text, tint tier, reset countdown, updated-ago) are pure and unit tested. Localized strings go through the String Catalog per `docs/agents/i18n.md`; "N% left" and the countdown use plural-safe formats.
- Dynamic Type, VoiceOver (a window reads "Weekly, 2 percent left, resets in 23 hours 35 minutes"; credits read "Credits, 0 dollars left of 10"), light and dark, and Reduce Motion (no animated bar fill) all covered. No continuously repainting views; "updated ago" is computed at render, not ticking.
- Switching servers rebuilds the Usage screen (already keyed by server), so quota from one server never shows under another. Nothing is persisted.
- `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` row for `/api/provider/` updated to note quota shipped; cost history remains roadmap.

## Validation plan

- XCTest: `Endpoint` query construction; decode of the live Codex payload, the live OpenRouter payload, an OpenRouter payload with null `limit`, an `unsupported` payload, and an `unavailable` payload with `account_limits: null`; the selection rule with active = `opencode-free` plus Codex and OpenRouter keyed (two cards), active = `openai-codex` (no duplicate), no keyed providers (no cards); a slow or failing quota call leaving analytics untouched; tint tiers at 100, 25, 10, 0; reset formatter across minutes, hours, days, and past dates; money formatting.
- Simulator (owner): open Usage against the live server. Expect an "OpenAI Codex · Plus" card with Session at 100% and Weekly near 2% in red, and an "OpenRouter" card showing $0.00 left of $10 in red. Pull to refresh and confirm the timestamps reset. Check Dynamic Type at the largest accessibility size, dark mode, and VoiceOver on one window. Switch to a server without these providers and confirm the group is absent.

## Non-goals

- `/api/provider/cost-history` (stays under #395 item 5).
- Showing quota in Settings → Providers or on session rows.
- Per-credential pool breakdown (`account_limits.pool`).
- Any polling or background refresh; the screen loads on appear and on explicit refresh only.

## Reference design

_Owner: drag the Codex-app screenshot (IMG_2801) into this section. The card layout it shows is described verbatim under Expected behavior._

title: feat(usage): show provider account limits on the Usage screen
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #415

## What changed

Subscription limits and credits were invisible on the phone: the Usage screen only showed local token and cost analytics. Now a "Limits" group sits above the window picker with one card per provider that reports a quota: an account-limits card (plan capsule, one row per window with "N% left", a remaining bar, and a reset countdown) for OpenAI Codex and Anthropic, and a credits card ("$N left", usage of limit) for OpenRouter. Tint turns orange at 25% left and red at 10%.

How it works: after `/api/insights` starts, a separate task asks `/api/providers` which of {active provider, openai-codex, anthropic, openrouter} have a key, probes `GET /api/provider/quota?provider=<id>` for each concurrently, and keeps only `status == "available"` responses with windows or a quota. Any failure (unsupported, unavailable, no_key, invalid_key, 404 on older servers, decode error) hides silently and never touches the analytics error state. Explicit Refresh and pull-to-refresh pass `refresh=1`; the initial load and window changes use the server's 45 s cache. A redacted placeholder reserves the slot while a cold probe runs so the chart does not jump. Stale results from superseded loads are discarded with the same generation-token pattern as `ProvidersViewModel`. Nothing is persisted, and the screen is already keyed by server.

Shapes verified against the live server and `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/providers.py` (`get_provider_quota`, `_serialize_account_usage_snapshot`, `_sanitize_openrouter_quota`).

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` on iPhone 17: **2299 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** (the pre-existing photo-library skips).

title: docs: refresh the feature-gap index for the parity tracker
body:
Part of #395 (item 1).

## Context

`docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md` classifies every upstream route as implemented (derived from `Endpoints.swift`), `roadmap`, or `n-a`. Against the pinned upstream (`UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA`, `.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/routes.py`) the index has drifted: two rows describe routes the app now calls, thirty routes match nothing, and the "deferred pending explicit owner opt-in" paragraph predates the tracker that gave that opt-in.

## Current behavior

- `/api/git-info` and `/api/git/` are listed as `roadmap` although `Endpoints.swift:62-77` calls sixteen git routes.
- Thirty pinned routes match neither `Endpoints.swift` nor a table row: `/api/auth/oidc/callback`, `/api/auth/oidc/start`, `/api/bg-task-complete-ack`, `/api/chat` (synchronous chat, browser fallback), `/api/commands/bundles`, `/api/commands/bundles/resolve`, `/api/commands/moa/resolve`, `/api/escape/authorize`, `/api/escape/file/raw`, `/api/escape/file/read`, `/api/escape/list`, `/api/extensions/install`, `/api/extensions/registry`, `/api/extensions/sidecar-proxy-consent`, `/api/extensions/status`, `/api/extensions/toggle`, `/api/extensions/uninstall`, `/api/health/restart`, `/api/kanban/` (prefix; implemented), `/api/process-complete-ack`, `/api/prompts`, `/api/session/anchor-scene`, `/api/session/compression-recovery/start`, `/api/session/stream`, `/api/session/title/regenerate`, `/api/sessions/events`, `/api/sessions/gateway/stream`, `/api/share/`, `/api/share/create`, `/api/share/revoke`.
- The "Already triaged" section still says profile create/delete, file mutations, skill authoring, and session import are deferred pending owner opt-in. #395 is that opt-in.

## Expected behavior

The index matches #395's decisions and every pinned route resolves to exactly one status.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Remove the `/api/git-info` and `/api/git/` rows (implemented status is derived, never hand-listed). Keep `/api/rollback/` as `roadmap`, note "→ #395 item 4".
- [ ] Add `n-a` rows: `/api/auth/oidc/`, `/api/bg-task-complete-ack`, `/api/process-complete-ack`, `/api/session/anchor-scene`, `/api/session/stream`, `/api/chat` (exact path; must sit after nothing, since `/api/chat/start` etc. are implemented and prefix matching is first-match, so place it as an exact-path note rather than a prefix), `/api/sessions/gateway/stream`.
- [ ] Add `roadmap` rows with the #395 item in the note: `/api/escape/` (P3, read, item 16), `/api/health/restart` (P5, admin, item 13), `/api/session/compression-recovery/` (P4, write, item 11d), `/api/session/title/regenerate` (P2, write, item 3), `/api/sessions/events` (P2, read, item 19), `/api/prompts` (P2, write, #275).
- [ ] Add `roadmap` rows whose note says "skipped by owner decision (#395)": `/api/share/`, `/api/extensions/`, `/api/commands/bundles`, `/api/commands/moa/resolve`. This keeps them out of the `new` bucket without inventing a fourth status.
- [ ] Update the notes on rows #395 reshapes: `/api/session/duplicate` and `/api/profile/` (create shipped; delete is item 6), `/api/session/handoff-summary` and `/api/session/conversation-rounds` (skipped: gateway features), `/api/session/import` (skipped), `/api/session/recovery/` (server-wide; item 13b), `/api/session/compress/` (item 11b), `/api/session/toolsets` (11a), `/api/session/worktree/` (2 and 11c), `/api/sessions/cleanup` (12), `/api/provider/`, `/api/providers`, `/api/models/refresh`, `/api/model/` (5a to 5c), `/api/settings` (10), `/api/skills/` (7), `/api/wiki/` and `/api/notes/` (8a, 8b), `/api/mcp/` and `/api/plugins` (9a, 9b), `/api/file/` and `/api/folder/` and `/api/workspace/` (14a, 14b, 15), `/api/updates/` (13; `summary` stays dropped), `/api/logs` (18), `/api/system/health`, `/api/health/agent`, `/api/gateway/`, `/api/dashboard/`, `/api/project-os/` (17).
- [ ] Rewrite the "deferred pending explicit owner opt-in" paragraph to: those groups are now planned in #395; do not file them outside that tracker.
- [ ] Prefix order rule holds: specific before general; `/api/file/reveal` and `/api/file/open-vscode` stay above `/api/file/`.
- [ ] No request or response shapes are added. The index stays a classification table.

## Validation plan
