title: feat(sessions): regenerate a session title from the list and a new chat session menu
body:
Part of #395 (item 3). Filed before item 2 because it creates the chat session menu that item 2 extends.

## Context

Upstream can rewrite a session title from its content: `POST /api/session/title/regenerate` (`routes.py:15616` at the pin). Body `{ "session_id": "...", "prefer_latest": false }`. Success returns `{ "session": <compact session>, "title": "...", "status": "...", "raw_preview": "..." }`. Errors: 404 unknown session, 403 read-only imported session, 422 when no better title could be produced (`"Could not generate a better title (...)"`).

The app has two places that act on a session, and only one exists today:

- Session list context menu: `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListComponents.swift:749` (`SessionRowContextMenu`), actions wired through `SessionListRowActions` (`:4-16`) into `SessionListViewModel` and `SessionMutator` (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionMutator.swift`).
- Chat toolbar: `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:800-834` has a title label, an optional goal menu, a Files link, and the Git menu. There is no session menu. Rename is a slash command only (`/title`, `ChatViewModel.swift:3069`).

## Expected behavior

- **Session list:** the context menu gains "Regenerate Title" directly under Rename. While the request runs the row shows the existing per-session in-flight state (`beginSessionMutation` / `endSessionMutation`, `SessionListViewModel.swift:1320`). On success the row title updates from the returned `session`. On 422 the existing "Session Action Failed" alert (`SessionListActionConfirmations.swift:15-30`) shows the server's message. No optimistic title.
- **Chat:** a new trailing toolbar `Menu` (a fourth `ChatToolbarActionSlot`, `ChatView.swift:3067`) with an ellipsis icon, labelled "Session" for VoiceOver, containing "Regenerate Title" as its only item in this issue. It is disabled while a response is streaming for this session and while a regenerate is in flight. On success the title label (`ChatToolbarTitleLabel`, `ChatView.swift:801`) updates and the cached session row is updated so the list agrees when the user goes back. On error, the chat's existing error surface shows the server message.
- `SessionMutator` gains `regenerateTitle(sessionID:) -> SessionSummary` (or the app's compact session type) and is injected into `ChatViewModel` so the chat menu and the list share one code path. `ChatViewModel` keeps calling `renameSession` directly for `/title`; do not refactor rename in this issue.
- Read-only imported sessions (403) hide the item where the app already knows the session is imported; otherwise the error path handles it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Endpoint.regenerateSessionTitle` posts to `/api/session/title/regenerate` with `session_id` and `prefer_latest: false`; the response model is tolerant (`title` and `session` optional, unknown keys ignored).
- [ ] Context menu item present on every session row that allows Rename; hidden where `SessionRowActionPolicy` hides Rename.
- [ ] Chat toolbar menu exists, has the VoiceOver label, is disabled while streaming, and its item updates both the chat title and the cached list row.
- [ ] 422 and 403 surface the server message; no title change on error.
- [ ] Two servers configured: regenerating on server A never touches server B's cache (per `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`).
- [ ] Localized strings added to the String Catalog for "Regenerate Title", the menu label, and nothing else.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: URLProtocol mock for success (title updates from `session`), 422 (error message, title unchanged), and a `SessionMutator` test that the request body matches.
- Simulator, one integrated pass: long-press a session row → Regenerate Title → title changes; open a chat → ⋯ → Regenerate Title → title changes and the list shows the same title on back. Try during a stream: item disabled.

## Non-goals

`prefer_latest: true` (no UI for it). Rename in the chat menu, Session details, or any other item: those come with item 2. Pin, archive, and delete in the chat menu.

title: feat(sessions): Session Details sheet with usage, lineage, and worktree status
body:
Part of #395 (item 2). Depends on the chat session menu from item 3 (#418).

## Context

Three per-session reads have no home in the app:

| Route | Method | Handler | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/session/usage?session_id=` | GET | `routes.py:14057` → `session_ops.session_usage` | `{ input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, estimated_cost, model }` |
| `/api/session/lineage/report?session_id=` | GET | `routes.py:14027` → `agent_sessions.read_session_lineage_report` | `{ found, session_id, lineage_key, tip_session_id, total_segments, materialized_segments, segments: [...], children: [...], manual_review }` plus fields per segment; 404 when `found` is false |
| `/api/session/worktree/status?session_id=` | GET | `routes.py:13417` → `worktrees.worktree_status_for_session` | `{ status: { path, exists, dirty, untracked_count, ahead_behind: { ahead, behind, available, upstream }, locked_by_stream, locked_by_terminal, listed, ... } }`; 400 when the session has no worktree |

The exact keys of `segments[]` and the full worktree `status` must be validated against the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR.

Today the chat shows context usage in the ring (`ContextWindowIndicatorView.swift:20`, fed by `GET /api/session` and SSE `usage` events). The best precedent for a facts sheet is `KanbanCardDetailView.metadataSection` (`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanCardDetailView.swift:146`): an inset-grouped `List` of `LabeledContent` rows with text selection, optional rows omitted.

## Expected behavior

A **Session Details** sheet, reachable from:

- the chat session menu created by item 3 (first item, above Regenerate Title), and
- the session list context menu, directly under "Full Title".

Contents, in order, each section loading independently and showing a one-line inline error on failure instead of failing the sheet:

1. **Session**: title, ID (selectable), model and provider, workspace path, created and updated times if the app already has them from the cached session.
2. **Usage**: input, output, total tokens; estimated cost formatted like the Usage screen; model from the usage payload when it differs from the session's. Fetched from `/api/session/usage`.
3. **Lineage**: only when `total_segments > 1` or `children` is non-empty. A compact list: this session's position (segment N of M), parent or tip, and children as tappable rows that open that session. Hidden entirely when the report says `found` with one segment and no children; a 404 hides it too.
4. **Worktree**: only when the status call succeeds. Path, exists, dirty with untracked count, ahead/behind when `available`, and "In use by a running response" when `locked_by_stream`. A 400 hides the section.

Refreshing: pull to refresh reloads all three. The sheet uses `.medium` and `.large` detents like the Git sheet (`GitWorkspaceView.swift:42`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three new `Endpoint` cases with tolerant models; every field optional; unknown keys ignored; `segments[]` and `children[]` decode with unknown element keys ignored.
- [ ] Sheet opens from both entry points and shows the same content for the same session.
- [ ] Each section fails independently; a 400 on worktree or 404 on lineage hides that section without an error.
- [ ] Loading is cancelled when the sheet is dismissed; no state mutation after dismissal.
- [ ] Rows use `LabeledContent`, support Dynamic Type at accessibility sizes without truncating the ID, and have VoiceOver labels.
- [ ] Two servers: the sheet for server A's session never shows server B's data after a switch (view keyed by active server).

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: decode fixtures for the three responses including a minimal payload with only `session_id`; view model test that a 404 lineage hides the section and a usage failure leaves the other sections intact.
- Simulator: open the sheet from the list and from the chat for a branched session (lineage visible) and for a plain one (lineage hidden); rotate detents; VoiceOver pass on the Usage rows.

## Non-goals

Any write (item 11a to 11d add toolsets, compression, worktree remove into this sheet later). Handoff summary and conversation rounds (skipped in #395). Recovery audit (server-wide; item 13b).

title: feat(git): browse, diff, and restore workspace checkpoints from the Git sheet
body:
Part of #395 (item 4). Land the local Git sheet polish (L25: per-file commit inclusion and toast resizing) first, or accept a merge conflict in `GitWorkspaceView.swift`.

## Context

Upstream keeps workspace checkpoints the agent writes before edits and exposes them per **workspace path**, not per session:

| Route | Method | Handler | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/rollback/list?workspace=` | GET | `routes.py:14680` → `rollback.list_checkpoints` | `{ checkpoints: [ { id, commit, message, date, date_display, files, path } ], workspace, checkpoint_dir }` |
| `/api/rollback/diff?workspace=&checkpoint=` | GET | `routes.py:14694` → `rollback.get_checkpoint_diff` | `{ checkpoint, workspace, diff, files_changed: [ { file, status } ], total_changes }` |
| `/api/rollback/restore` | POST `{ workspace, checkpoint }` | `routes.py:17599` → `rollback.restore_checkpoint` | `{ ok, checkpoint, workspace, files_restored: [...], files_restored_count, errors: [ { file, error } ] }` |

Restore copies checkpoint files back over the workspace. It does not create a checkpoint of the current state first; verify this against `rollback.restore_checkpoint` at the pin and say so in the confirmation copy if it holds.

The app's Git surface: `HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitWorkspaceView.swift` (overview sheet: `summaryHeader` at `:118`, then changed files), `GitActionsMenuButton.swift:23-63` (menu sections Changes, Write, Update), `GitDiffView` for unified diffs, and the destructive-confirmation precedent in `GitCommitView.swift:55-64` ("Discard local changes?" alert whose message states the consequence). The session's workspace path comes from `SessionDetail.workspace` (`HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift:195`).

## Expected behavior

- The Git actions menu gains a fourth section, **Checkpoints**, with one item "Checkpoints…" that pushes a **Checkpoints** list inside the Git sheet. Hidden when the session has no workspace.
- The list shows each checkpoint as a row: message (or the id when empty), `date_display`, and "N files". Empty state: "No checkpoints yet. Hermes saves one before it edits files." Error state matches the Git sheet's.
- Tapping a row opens a detail with the changed files and a **View diff** action that renders `diff` in the existing `GitDiffView`.
- The detail has a destructive **Restore Checkpoint** button. Tapping shows an alert titled "Restore this checkpoint?" with the message "This overwrites N files in <workspace folder name> with the versions saved at <date>. Uncommitted changes to those files are lost. This cannot be undone." Buttons: Cancel, Restore (destructive). The button is disabled while a response is streaming in this session.
- After restore: show the toast the Git sheet already uses with "Restored N files", refresh git status, and if `errors` is non-empty show them in the same "Session Action Failed"-style alert with each file and error, not a bare failure.
- No optimistic UI anywhere in this flow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three `Endpoint` cases keyed by workspace path, encoded as query items for the two GETs and JSON for the POST; tolerant models.
- [ ] Menu item appears only when `SessionDetail.workspace` is non-empty; list, detail, and diff render; diff reuses `GitDiffView`.
- [ ] Confirmation copy contains the real file count, workspace folder name, and date, and says it cannot be undone.
- [ ] Restore is disabled while streaming; partial errors are listed, not swallowed.
- [ ] Haptic on confirm follows `ChatHaptics.destructiveConfirmationAccepted(isEnabled:)`.
- [ ] Reduce Motion: no new animation beyond the existing toast.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: decode fixtures for all three; a view model test that restore with `errors` non-empty surfaces them; a test that the confirmation string interpolates count, folder, and date.
- Simulator, against one disposable session in a scratch workspace on the maintainer's server: create a checkpoint by letting the agent edit a file, open Checkpoints, view diff, restore, see the toast and the git status refresh. Clean up only that session.

## Non-goals

Creating checkpoints from the phone (upstream has no route). Per-file restore. Anything in L25's scope.

title: feat(sessions): live session list via the server's sessions event stream
body:
Part of #395 (item 19, added at intake).

## Context

Upstream publishes a lightweight server-sent event stream when the session list changes: `GET /api/sessions/events` (`routes.py:14394` → `_handle_session_events_stream`, payload built by `session_events._sessions_changed_payload`). Each event is a JSON `data:` line shaped `{ "type": "sessions_changed", "version": <int>, "reason": "<session_rename|session_delete|...>", "profile": <string|null>, "session_id": <string|null> }`. The server writes `: keepalive` comments on a heartbeat interval and coalesces bursts. Whether events carry an `event:` name, the heartbeat interval, and the full `reason` vocabulary must be validated against the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR.

Today the session list refreshes on foreground, on return from a chat (#398), and on pull. A rename or delete done from the WebUI, a cron, or another phone does not show until one of those happens.

Precedent: `HermesMobile/Networking/KanbanEventStreamClient.swift` wraps LDSwiftEventSource with a `Hello`/`Events` decode, reconnect, and an owner that stops it when the view goes away.

## Expected behavior

- While the session list is on screen and the app is in the foreground, the app holds one `/api/sessions/events` stream for the active server. On each `sessions_changed` event it schedules a debounced (about 500 ms) list reload through the existing load path. `version` is used to drop out-of-order or duplicate events.
- The stream is closed when the list disappears, on background, and on server switch. It reopens on foreground and on server switch to the new server only. Nothing from server A's stream ever triggers a reload of server B.
- Reconnect uses the same backoff and quiet-stream handling as `KanbanEventStreamClient`. A failed or unsupported stream (404 on an older server, tunnel closing quiet connections) degrades silently to today's behavior. No banner, no error.
- Pull to refresh and the foreground refresh keep working unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Endpoint.sessionEvents` and a `SessionEventStreamClient` (or a generalization of the Kanban client, if the shapes align without a protocol tower) with an injectable client for tests.
- [ ] Events trigger one reload per burst; `version` monotonicity enforced; a reload already in flight is not duplicated.
- [ ] Lifecycle: opened on appear/foreground, closed on disappear/background/server switch; no callbacks mutate state after the owning view model is gone.
- [ ] Two servers: switching while events are arriving never reloads the wrong server's list.
- [ ] No visible UI change; no continuous animation.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: scripted event fixture (pattern from `ScriptedSSEStreamFixture.swift`) proving debounce, version ordering, and close-on-switch. No sleeps; expectations only.
- Simulator: open the list, rename a session from the WebUI on the same server, see the row update within a second; background and foreground, repeat. Through the Cloudflare tunnel, leave the list idle five minutes and confirm no error surfaces.

## Non-goals

Per-session event streams (`/api/session/<id>/events`), the gateway stream, or using the events for anything but list invalidation.

title: feat(settings): set, replace, and remove provider API keys from the Providers screen
body:
Part of #395 (item 5a). Land the model picker badges polish (L33) first if it is still pending; this issue does not touch the picker, but 5b does.

## Context

Upstream lets a client set, replace, and remove provider API keys and drop a provider's cached model list:

| Route | Handler | Body | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/providers` | `routes.py:15499` → `providers.set_provider_key` | `{ provider, api_key }` (`api_key` null or empty removes) | `{ ok, provider, display_name, action: "updated" \| "removed" }`; `{ ok: false, error }` for OAuth providers, non-configurable providers, keys with newlines, or keys that look too short |
| `POST /api/providers/delete` | `routes.py:15510` → `providers.remove_provider_key` | `{ provider }` | `{ ok, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error }` |
| `POST /api/models/refresh` | `routes.py:15526` → `config.invalidate_provider_models_cache` | `{ provider }` | `{ ok: true, provider }` |

Exact error strings and the remove payload must be validated at the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR.

The app's Providers screen is read-only: `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/ProvidersView.swift` (per-provider `DisclosureGroup` at `:157`, status line "Key configured"/"No key" at `:222`, the note "Provider keys are managed on the server. This screen is read-only." at `:172`). `ProviderSummary` (`HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift:194`) already decodes `hasKey`, `configurable`, `isOauth`, `keySource`, `authError`.

## Expected behavior

- The read-only note is removed. Each provider whose `configurable` is true and `isOauth` is false gets, inside its disclosure: a **Set API Key…** button (labelled **Replace API Key…** when `hasKey`), and when `hasKey` and `keySource` is `config`, a destructive **Remove API Key** button. Providers with `keySource` `env` or `oauth` show a footnote instead: "Managed by the server's environment" or "Signed in with OAuth".
- Set/Replace presents a sheet with one `SecureField`, paste enabled, autocorrect and capitalization off, `textContentType(.password)`, and a Save button disabled until non-empty. Save posts the key and never echoes it back; the field is cleared on dismiss. The key is never stored on the phone, not in Keychain, not in a draft.
- Remove shows an alert: "Remove the <display name> key?" with message "The server forgets this key. Sessions using <display name> stop working until a key is set again." Cancel / Remove (destructive).
- After set or remove: reload `/api/providers` and show the server's `display_name` and `action` in a toast. `{ ok: false, error }` shows the server's error verbatim in an alert.
- A **Refresh models** action in each configurable provider's disclosure posts `/api/models/refresh` and then reloads the provider list so the model count updates.
- The `Active` badge and the auth-error row behave as today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three `Endpoint` cases; tolerant responses; `api_key` is sent in the JSON body only, never in a query string or log line (check `APIClient` request logging masks the body for this endpoint).
- [ ] Controls appear only where `configurable && !isOauth`; Remove only where `keySource == config`.
- [ ] `SecureField` sheet as specified; key cleared from memory on dismiss; no persistence.
- [ ] Remove confirmation copy names the provider and the consequence.
- [ ] Server `error` shown verbatim; list reloads after every successful write.
- [ ] Two servers: a key set on server A never appears on server B's screen (the list is fetched, not cached across servers).
- [ ] Strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: URLProtocol tests for set (body shape, success toast text), set with `{ ok: false, error }`, remove, and refresh; a test that the request body is not included in the client's debug description.
- Simulator, against the maintainer's server only with a provider the maintainer names as disposable: set a bogus key, see the auth-error row after reload, remove it, see "No key". Do not touch any provider in daily use.

## Non-goals

`/api/providers/self-hosted`. Auxiliary model routing (5b). Cost history (5c). Editing base URLs or custom providers.

title: feat(settings): Task Models screen for auxiliary model routing
body:
Part of #395 (item 5b). Touches the shared model picker; land L33 first if it is still pending.

## Context

Hermes routes side tasks (vision, web extraction, compression, approval, MCP reasoning, title generation, and others) to their own models. Upstream exposes:

| Route | Handler | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/model/auxiliary` | `routes.py:13261` → `config.get_auxiliary_models` | `{ tasks: [{ task, provider, model, base_url, timeout, download_timeout, max_concurrency, extra_body, api_key_set, label, description }], main: { provider, model, supports_fast_tier, service_tier } }` |
| `POST /api/model/set` | `routes.py:15477` | `{ scope: "auxiliary", task, provider, model, advanced? }`; `task: "__reset__"` clears every slot; unknown task → 400 listing valid slots. `scope: "main"` sets the default model (the app already does this through `/api/default-model`; do not switch). |

The task catalog lives in `config.AUXILIARY_TASK_CATALOG` (`config.py:4859`); the slot list and the `advanced` keys must be validated at the pin before implementation and recorded in the PR.

App surfaces: Settings → Active Server card (`SettingsView.swift:476`) has Default Model (`DefaultModelPickerView.swift`, using `ModelPickerSheet` with the `.serverDefault` preset) and Default Profile. The picker presets live in `ModelPickerConfiguration.swift`.

## Expected behavior

- A new **Task Models** row in the Active Server card, under Default Model, pushes a screen listing each task from `tasks` with its `label`, `description` as a footnote, and the current value: "Auto" when `provider` is `auto` and `model` is empty, otherwise "<model> · <provider>".
- Tapping a task opens `ModelPickerSheet` with a new `.auxiliaryTask` preset: the same catalog as the default picker plus an **Automatic** row at the top that sends `provider: "auto", model: ""`. Selecting posts `/api/model/set` with `scope: "auxiliary"` and reloads the list. No optimistic value.
- A **Reset All to Automatic** button at the bottom, destructive style, behind an alert: "Reset task models?" / "Every task goes back to automatic routing on the server." Cancel / Reset. Sends `task: "__reset__"`.
- Rows show `api_key_set`, `base_url`, and timeouts as read-only detail text when non-empty; the app does not edit `advanced` in this issue.
- The `main` object is displayed nowhere new; Default Model already covers it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two `Endpoint` cases; tolerant models; unknown tasks from a newer server still render with their `label`.
- [ ] New picker preset adds the Automatic row without changing the composer or default-model presets (snapshot or unit test on preset rows).
- [ ] Set and reset reload from the server before the UI changes; server 400 shows its message.
- [ ] Two servers: the list is fetched per active server, never cached across servers.
- [ ] VoiceOver reads task label, current value, and the footnote; Dynamic Type at accessibility sizes wraps rather than truncates.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: decode fixture with an unknown task; a request-body test for set and reset; a picker preset test.
- Simulator, against the maintainer's server: change the title-generation task to a cheap model and back to Automatic, confirm the WebUI shows the same, then reset. Name the task you changed in the PR.

## Non-goals

`advanced` (timeouts, concurrency, extra body). `scope: "main"`. Service tier.

title: feat(usage): OpenRouter spend history on the Limits card
body:
Part of #395 (item 5c). Narrow by upstream design: only OpenRouter has cost history at the pin.

## Context

`GET /api/provider/cost-history?provider=openrouter&days=7` (`routes.py:13308` → `providers.get_provider_cost_history`, `days` clamped 1…365). Returns one of:

- `{ ok: true, provider: "openrouter", display_name, supported: true, status: "available", window_days, snapshots: [...], limit, label, monthly_budget, message }`
- `status: "unavailable"` with the same keys and the last known `snapshots` (`ok: false`)
- `status: "no_key"` (`ok: false`, `supported: true`)
- `status: "unsupported"` for every other provider (`ok: false`, `supported: false`)
- `status: "missing_provider"` when the query is absent

The per-snapshot keys (date, cost, delta) must be validated at the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR.

The Usage screen already has a Limits section (`HermesMobile/Features/Insights/ProviderLimitsCard.swift`, rendered at `InsightsView.swift:81-86`) that includes OpenRouter credits from `/api/provider/quota` (#415). Chart primitives: `UsageChartCard.swift`, `UsageChartData.swift`.

## Expected behavior

- When the Limits section shows an OpenRouter card, that card gains a **Spend** row: a small bar chart of `snapshots` over the selected window (reuse the Usage window picker's days when it is 7, 30, or 90; otherwise 7), the total for the window, and `monthly_budget` as "of $N budget" when present.
- `status: "unavailable"` renders the last known data with a muted "Last known" caption. `no_key` renders nothing extra (the credits card already explains the missing key). `unsupported` is never requested: the app only calls this for `openrouter`.
- Fetched with the limits, once per screen appearance and on pull to refresh, never on a timer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One `Endpoint` case with `provider` and `days` query items; tolerant model keyed on `status`.
- [ ] Only requested when OpenRouter is in the limits selection; no request for other providers.
- [ ] The chart uses the existing `dataviz`-conformant palette and axis style from `UsageChartCard`; no new colors.
- [ ] Reduce Motion: no animated bar growth.
- [ ] Two servers: the card and its history belong to the active server.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: decode fixtures for `available`, `unavailable`, `no_key`; a view model test that non-OpenRouter selections skip the call.
- Simulator: Usage screen on a server with an OpenRouter key shows the Spend row; switch window; pull to refresh.

## Non-goals

Cost history for any other provider (upstream has none). Budget editing.

title: feat(settings): delete a profile from the profiles screen
body:
Part of #395 (item 6). Create already shipped; `/api/profile/active` is redundant with the `active` field the app reads from `/api/profiles`.

## Context

`POST /api/profile/delete` `{ name }` (`routes.py:16685` → `profiles.delete_profile_api`). Returns `{ ok: true, name }`. Errors: 400 "Cannot delete the default profile.", 400 when the profile does not exist, 403 in isolated profile mode, 409 "Cannot delete active profile '<name>' while an agent is running. Cancel or wait for it to finish." Deleting the active profile switches the server to `default` first. What happens to the profile's sessions must be checked at the pin (`hermes_cli.profiles.delete_profile`) and stated in the confirmation copy.

App surface: `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/DefaultProfilePickerView.swift`, a list of profiles with Selected and Server Default badges (`ProfileStatusBadge` at `:525`), row tap switches (`save(_:)` at `:311`), Create at `:348`. Precedent for a delete confirmation: `SessionListActionConfirmations.swift:31-53`.

## Expected behavior

- Each profile row that is not the server default gets a trailing swipe **Delete** and a context-menu **Delete Profile…**. The default profile's row shows neither.
- Confirmation alert: "Delete profile <name>?" with the message stating exactly what the server does with that profile's sessions and config (filled in from the pin check), ending "This cannot be undone." Cancel / Delete (destructive).
- If the profile is the active one, the alert message adds: "Hermes switches to the default profile first."
- On success: reload `/api/profiles`; if the deleted profile was active, the app reruns the same path it uses after a profile switch (`SessionListViewModel.swift:316-348` and `ChatViewModel.switchProfile`) so the session list, composer defaults, and cached selections move to `default`.
- 409 shows the server message in an alert with no change. 403 hides the delete affordance for the rest of that screen visit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Endpoint.deleteProfile`; tolerant response.
- [ ] Delete hidden on the server-default row; visible on every other row via swipe and context menu.
- [ ] Copy states the consequence for sessions and config, and the switch-to-default case.
- [ ] Active-profile deletion triggers the existing profile-switch reload path; nothing is left pointing at the deleted profile (per-server selections in `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`).
- [ ] 409 and 403 handled as above; no optimistic removal.
- [ ] Destructive-confirm haptic; strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: URLProtocol tests for success, 409, 403; a test that deleting the active profile calls the switch-reload path.
- Simulator, against the maintainer's server: create a throwaway profile, switch to it, delete it, confirm the app lands on `default` with the right session list. Delete only that profile.

## Non-goals

Rename or edit profiles. `/api/profile/active`.

title: feat(skills): edit, create, and delete skills, and show usage counts
body:
Part of #395 (item 7).

## Context

| Route | Handler | Body / query | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/skills/save` | `routes.py:27934` → `_handle_skill_save` | `{ name, content, category? }`; writes `<skills dir>/[category/]<name>/SKILL.md` | `{ ok, name, path }`; 400 invalid name, category, or path; 400 on symlinked skill file |

| `GET /api/skills/usage` | `routes.py:14537` | none | `{ <skill name>: { use_count, view_count, patch_count } , ... }` plus any extra keys upstream adds |

Name and category validation rules must be read at the pin and mirrored client-side so the user sees the error before the request.

App surfaces: `HermesMobile/Features/Skills/SkillsView.swift` (category groups at `:114`, row with toggle at `:181`, `SkillDetailView` at `:276` rendering `content` read-only with `MarkdownRenderer` at `:338`). Editor precedent: `MemoryEditSheet` (`HermesMobile/Features/Memory/MemoryView.swift:195`), a monospaced `TextEditor` with Cancel/Save.

## Expected behavior

- **Usage:** each skill row shows a small trailing count, `use_count`, when the usage call succeeds and the count is non-zero; the detail view shows the three counts as `LabeledContent` rows. Fetched once per screen appearance alongside the list; failure hides the counts silently.
- **Edit:** `SkillDetailView` gains an **Edit** toolbar button that opens a sheet in the `MemoryEditSheet` pattern, seeded with the current `content`, monospaced, with the keyboard-safe layout that sheet already has. Save posts `name`, `content`, and the skill's existing `category`; on success the detail reloads `/api/skills/content` and the list refreshes. The sheet blocks dismissal with unsaved changes behind "Discard changes?".
- **New:** a **New Skill** toolbar button on the list opens the same editor with a name field, an optional category picker limited to the categories already present plus free text, and a Markdown template body. Client-side validation mirrors the server's before Save is enabled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three `Endpoint` cases; tolerant models; the usage map decodes unknown per-skill keys.
- [ ] Usage counts render on rows and detail; failure is silent.
- [ ] Edit, New, and Delete work as specified; server 400 messages surface verbatim; no optimistic content.
- [ ] Editor respects the keyboard, Dynamic Type, and VoiceOver as `MemoryEditSheet` does; no new animation.
- [ ] Two servers: editing a skill on server A never writes server B's cache.
- [ ] Strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: request-body tests for save (with and without category) and delete; a decode test for usage with extra keys; a validation test for names the server rejects.
- Simulator, against the maintainer's server: create a throwaway skill, edit it, see it in the list, delete it. Touch only that skill.

## Non-goals

Editing linked files other than `SKILL.md`. Skill import from the share extension.

title: feat(memory): read-only Wiki browser under Memory

title: feat(memory): read-only Notes search under Memory (Joplin)
body:
Part of #395 (item 8b). Read only; upstream implements search and preview for Joplin sources only at the pin.

## Context

| Route | Handler | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/notes/sources` | `routes.py:28960` → `_handle_notes_sources_list` | `{ enabled, sources: [...], source, inventory_scope, attach_supported, automatic_recall_unchanged, recent_ai_notes: [...] }`; `enabled: false` with empty sources when external notes are off |

| `GET /api/notes/item?source=joplin&id=` | `routes.py:29261` | `{ source, note: {...} }`; same error codes |

Per-source, per-result, and `note` keys must be validated at the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR.

The app already decodes `externalNotesEnabled` from `/api/memory` (`HermesMobile/Models/Memory.swift:26`, exposed as `MemoryViewModel.isExternalNotesEnabled` at `:18`) and uses it nowhere. Memory screen layout: `MemoryView.swift:69-102`.

## Expected behavior

- When `externalNotesEnabled` is true, Memory gains a **Notes** row (NavigationLink). The row is absent otherwise.
- Notes screen: loads `/api/notes/sources`. If `enabled` is false or `sources` is empty, show an empty state "No note sources are connected on the server." A source picker appears only when more than one source is listed; sources other than Joplin are shown disabled with the footnote "Search is not available for this source yet."
- A search field runs `/api/notes/search` debounced (about 300 ms) with the selected source, cancelling the previous request. Results list title and a one-line excerpt when present; tapping opens the note.
- Note screen: renders the note body with `MarkdownRenderer`, with Copy and Select Text; falls back to plain text if the body is not Markdown.
- 502 shows an inline "Joplin did not respond" message with Retry; 404 falls back to the empty state.
- `recent_ai_notes`, when non-empty, appears as a "Recent" section above the search results until the user types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three `Endpoint` cases; tolerant models; unknown source types decode.
- [ ] Row gated on `externalNotesEnabled`; empty, disabled, and error states as specified.
- [ ] Search is debounced and cancels stale requests; no result from an older query replaces a newer one.
- [ ] Note renders with Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and text selection.
- [ ] Two servers: sources, results, and notes follow the active server.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: decode fixtures for enabled and disabled sources, search, item, and 502; a view model test that an older search result arriving late is discarded.
- Simulator: on a server with Joplin connected, search and open a note; on a server without notes, confirm no row.

## Non-goals

Attaching notes to a chat (`attach_supported` is false upstream). Writing notes. Non-Joplin search.

title: feat(settings): Server card with MCP servers, tools, and enable toggles
body:
Part of #395 (item 9a). Creates the Server card in Settings that 9b, 13, 13b, 17, and 18 reuse.

## Context

| Route | Handler | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/mcp/servers` | `routes.py:14665` → `_handle_mcp_servers_list` | `{ servers: [...], toggle_supported: true, reload_required: true }`; per-server keys (name, enabled, transport or command, tool counts, runtime status) at the pin |
| `PATCH /api/mcp/servers/<name>` | `routes.py:17633` → `_handle_mcp_server_toggle` | body `{ enabled: bool }` → `{ ok, name, enabled }`; 400 missing `enabled` or invalid config, 404 unknown name |
| `GET /api/mcp/tools` | `routes.py:14669` → `_handle_mcp_tools_list` | `{ tools: [...], total, source, inventory_scope: "already_known_runtime_only", unavailable_servers: [...] }` |

`reload_required: true` means a toggle takes effect on the next agent start, not immediately. `inventory_scope` says the tool list is what the runtime already knows, not a fresh probe. Per-server and per-tool keys must be validated at the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR. Note the app's `APIClient` has no PATCH helper today; add one alongside the existing verbs rather than tunnelling through POST.

Settings today has no Server grouping: server-scoped rows are split between the Servers card (`SettingsView.swift:727`) and the Active Server card (`:476`, with Default Model, Default Profile, Status, Providers, Connection Headers, Version, and update controls).

## Expected behavior

- A new **Server** `SettingsCard` directly under Active Server, holding one row in this issue: **MCP Servers**, with detail text "N enabled of M" once loaded. The card is the home for later admin rows; build it as a list of `NavigationLink` rows, not a one-off.
- MCP Servers screen: one row per server with name, transport or command summary, a tool count when `tools` reports it, and a `Toggle` bound to `enabled`. The toggle is disabled when `toggle_supported` is false. A footer states: "Changes apply the next time the agent starts." when `reload_required` is true.
- Toggling sends the PATCH, keeps the switch in a pending state until the response, then adopts the server's `enabled`. A 400 or 404 reverts the switch and shows the message. Same optimistic-with-rollback pattern as the skills toggle (`SkillsViewModel.setSkill`).
- Tapping a row pushes a **Tools** list filtered to that server from `/api/mcp/tools` (name and description). Servers in `unavailable_servers` show an "Unavailable" badge and an empty tools list with the reason if one is given.
- Pull to refresh on both screens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Endpoint` cases for list, toggle (PATCH with a path component), and tools; a PATCH path through `APIClient` with a test; tolerant models with every per-server and per-tool key optional.
- [ ] Server card exists as a reusable rows container; MCP row detail text updates after load.
- [ ] Toggle pending/adopt/revert behavior; `toggle_supported` gating; reload footer.
- [ ] Tools list per server; unavailable badge.
- [ ] Two servers: the card's contents follow the active server; no cache crosses servers.
- [ ] VoiceOver reads name, state, and count; Dynamic Type wraps; strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: PATCH request test (method, path, body); toggle revert on 404; decode fixtures for list and tools with unknown keys.
- Simulator, against the maintainer's server: open Server → MCP Servers, view a server's tools, toggle a server the maintainer names as safe off and on again. Leave it as found.

## Non-goals

Adding or deleting MCP servers (upstream has routes; not in this tracker). Plugins (9b). Restart (13).

title: feat(settings): Server Settings form for bot name, update policy, channel, and max tokens
body:
Part of #395 (item 10). Scope fixed at intake: bot name, check for updates, ignore agent updates, update channel, max tokens. Password and passkey operations are out.

## Context

`POST /api/settings` (`routes.py:16703`) merges the body into the server's settings through `config.save_settings`, which "ignores unknown keys". Keys in scope and their validation at the pin:

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bot_name` | string | trimmed; empty becomes "Hermes" |
| `check_for_updates` | bool | when false, `/api/updates/check` returns `{ disabled: true }` unless forced |
| `ignore_agent_updates` | bool | hides agent updates from the check |
| `update_channel` | `"stable"` \| `"experimental"` | enum at `config.py:9954` |
| `max_tokens` | int or null | server validates; `GET /api/settings` also returns `max_tokens_effective` and `max_tokens_fallback` |

The response is the merged settings object. Keys beginning with `_` (`_set_password`, `_clear_password`, `_passwordless`, `_current_password`, `_auth_disabled_acknowledged`) are auth operations and must never be sent by the app.

Today the app writes only `show_cli_sessions` and `show_claude_code_sessions` (`SettingsView.swift:25-30` → `APIClient+ServerPanels.swift:123-139`), with an optimistic-then-revert model in `CliSessionsSyncModel.swift`. `SettingsResponse` (`ServerCatalog.swift:312-359`) already decodes `botName`, `checkForUpdates`, `maxTokens`, `maxTokensEffective`.

## Expected behavior

- The Active Server card gains a **Server Settings** row that pushes a form with:
  - **Bot name** text field, saved on commit; shows the server's returned value after save.
  - **Check for updates** toggle and **Ignore agent updates** toggle.
  - **Update channel** picker, Stable or Experimental, with the footnote "Experimental tracks every batch; Stable tracks promoted releases." Changing it triggers the existing forced update check so the Update row reflects the new channel.
  - **Max tokens** numeric field with a Clear button that sends null; the footnote shows `max_tokens_effective` and, when set, `max_tokens_fallback` as "Effective: N" so the user can see when the server overrides.
- Each control saves independently with the same optimistic-then-revert pattern as `CliSessionsSyncModel`, adopting the server's returned value. A failure reverts and shows the message.
- The two CLI-sessions toggles stay where they are; `CliSessionsSyncModel` may be generalized to carry the new keys, but it must not become a generic settings framework.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One request type per save carrying only the changed key; a test asserts no `_`-prefixed key can be encoded.
- [ ] `SettingsResponse` gains `ignoreAgentUpdates` and `updateChannel` as optionals; decode stays tolerant.
- [ ] Optimistic write, adopt server value, revert with message on failure; per-server state keyed like `CliSessionsSyncModel`.
- [ ] Channel change triggers the forced check and the Update row updates.
- [ ] Two servers: switching mid-edit never writes the wrong server (in-flight saves are dropped on switch, as the CLI toggles do today).
- [ ] Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels on every control; strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: encode tests per key; the `_`-prefix guard; revert on failure; server-switch drop.
- Simulator, against the maintainer's server: change bot name and change it back; toggle check for updates off and on. Do not change the channel on the daily-driver server unless the maintainer says so.

## Non-goals

Password, passkey, passwordless, or any auth setting. Theme (the app has its own). Speech settings. Dashboard plugin flags.

title: feat(settings): clean up empty sessions from the Sessions card
body:
Part of #395 (item 12). Placed in Settings because the session list has no toolbar or edit mode.

## Context

| Route | Handler | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/sessions/cleanup` | `routes.py:15583` → `_handle_sessions_cleanup(zero_only=False)` | deletes every session file whose title is "Untitled" and has zero messages, then removes index entries with no backing file |
| `POST /api/sessions/cleanup_zero_message` | `routes.py:15586` → same with `zero_only=True` | deletes every session with zero messages regardless of title, then the same index sweep |

Both take an empty body and return a count of removed sessions; the exact response keys and whether the index sweep count is reported separately must be validated at the pin or a live server and recorded in the PR. There is no dry run upstream, so the preview count has to come from the app's own session list.

App surfaces: Settings → Sessions card (`SettingsView.swift:394`), which already holds the server-synced CLI-sessions toggles. Delete precedent copy: `SessionListActionConfirmations.swift:31-53`.

## Expected behavior

- The Sessions card gains a **Clean Up Sessions…** row. Tapping presents a sheet with two options, each showing a count computed from the cached session list for the active server:
  - **Remove empty untitled sessions** (title "Untitled", no messages): "N sessions".
  - **Remove all empty sessions** (no messages, any title): "N sessions".
  Counts say "about N" when the cache is older than the last successful list load, and the sheet offers Refresh.
- Choosing one shows an alert: "Remove N empty sessions?" / "This deletes them from the Hermes server. Pinned and archived sessions with no messages are included. This cannot be undone." Cancel / Remove (destructive). Verify the pinned and archived claim at the pin and adjust the copy.
- On success: toast "Removed N sessions" using the server's count, then reload the session list and prune the SwiftData cache for the active server. If the server count differs from the preview, show the server's.
- Both buttons are disabled while a response is streaming in any session on this server, because a brand-new session in the middle of its first turn has zero saved messages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two `Endpoint` cases; tolerant response.
- [ ] Preview counts derived from the active server's cached sessions only; refresh path works.
- [ ] Confirmation names the count and the consequence; no optimistic removal.
- [ ] Post-success reload and cache prune scoped to the active server (see `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`).
- [ ] Disabled while any stream is live on this server.
- [ ] Destructive-confirm haptic; strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: preview count from a fixture list (untitled-empty vs any-empty); request tests; cache prune limited to one server's records.
- Simulator, against the maintainer's server: create two disposable empty sessions, one renamed; run the untitled clean-up, confirm one remains; run the all-empty clean-up, confirm none remain. Touch nothing else.

## Non-goals

Multi-select on the session list. Age-based cleanup (upstream has none).

title: feat(settings): force update, lock recovery, and gateway restart
body:
Part of #395 (item 13). Depends on the Server card from 9a (#429) for the restart row.

## Context

| Route | Handler | Body | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/updates/force` | `routes.py:17307` → `updates.apply_force_update` | `{ target: "webui" \| "agent", channel?: "stable" \| "experimental" }` | discards local changes (`checkout .` + `reset --hard` to the channel ref) and applies; refuses with a message when the reset would rewind to an ancestor |
| `POST /api/updates/clear_lock` | `routes.py:17318` → `updates.apply_clear_lock` | `{ target }` | never deletes the lock; returns a diagnostic and the exact `rm` command for the operator; on a re-call with the lock gone it re-runs the normal apply |
| `POST /api/health/restart` | `routes.py:14958` → `_handle_health_restart` | none | restarts the **active profile's gateway service**, not the web server: `{ ok: true, message: "Gateway service restarted successfully" }` or "...restart initiated (in progress)" or `{ ok: false, error }` |

Exact response keys for force and clear_lock must be validated at the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR.

App surfaces: the Active Server card's update flow (`SettingsView.swift:915` check, `:993` apply with phases idle/applying/recovering/blocked/failed, `:1200` `waitForServerToReturn`). The `blocked` and `failed` phases are where force and clear-lock belong.

## Expected behavior

- **Force update** appears only when the normal apply reports a dirty checkout or a merge conflict (the `blocked` phase, matched on the server's message, validated at the pin). It is a destructive button "Discard server changes and update…" behind an alert: "Discard local changes on the server?" / "Hermes resets the <target> checkout to the <channel> release, throwing away any local edits on the server. This cannot be undone." Cancel / Discard and Update. On success it joins the existing `waitForServerToReturn` flow. A refusal (rewind guard) shows the server's message.
- **Clear lock** appears only when the apply reports a `.git/index.lock`. It is a non-destructive button "Show lock recovery steps" that calls the endpoint and presents the returned diagnostic and command in a selectable, copyable sheet. If the server reports the lock already gone and re-ran the apply, the flow continues as a normal apply.
- **Restart gateway** is a row in the Server card, behind an alert: "Restart the gateway?" / "This restarts the Hermes gateway service for the active profile. Running responses in this profile stop. The Hermex connection is not affected." Cancel / Restart (destructive). Shows the server's `message` in a toast; `ok: false` shows `error`. Disabled while a response is streaming on this server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three `Endpoint` cases; tolerant responses.
- [ ] Force and clear-lock are hidden outside their phases; no path shows them on a clean apply.
- [ ] Copy states target, channel, and consequence; clear-lock never implies the app deleted anything.
- [ ] Restart disabled while streaming; message and error surfaced.
- [ ] Two servers: every action targets the active server only.
- [ ] Destructive-confirm haptic; strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: phase-to-button visibility tests with fixture apply responses for dirty, conflict, and lock; request body tests; restart response handling.
- Simulator: restart the gateway on the maintainer's server only with explicit go-ahead in the PR thread; otherwise validate force and clear-lock against fixtures and describe the manual path.

## Non-goals

`/api/updates/summary` (dropped by owner decision). `/api/shutdown`, `/api/admin/reload` (n-a).

title: feat(settings): Session Store health with safe repair under Server
body:
Part of #395 (item 13b). Both routes are server-wide; they take no session id. Depends on the Server card from 9a (#429).

## Context

| Route | Handler | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/session/recovery/audit` | `routes.py:14036` → `session_recovery.audit_session_recovery` | `{ status, summary: { ok, repairable, unsafe_to_repair }, items: [...] }` |
| `POST /api/session/recovery/repair-safe` | `routes.py:15096` → `session_recovery.repair_safe_session_recovery` | `{ clean, ok, repaired, before, after, backup_repair: { scanned, restored, orphaned_backups, details }, sidecar_repair: {...} }`; HTTP 200 when `clean`, 409 otherwise (the body is still the result) |

The repair is described upstream as "safe, deterministic": it restores shrunken or orphaned sessions from `.bak` files and materializes missing sidecars. It never deletes. Per-item keys must be validated at the pin or a live server before implementation and recorded in the PR.

## Expected behavior

- The Server card gains a **Session Store** row with detail text from the audit: "Healthy" when `repairable` and `unsafe_to_repair` are both zero, otherwise "N repairable · M need attention".
- Session Store screen: the three summary counts as `LabeledContent`, then `items` grouped by their state with the session id, title when present, and the reason. Items that are repairable show what the repair would do in plain words.
- A **Repair Safely** button, enabled only when `repairable > 0`, behind an alert: "Repair N sessions?" / "Hermes restores damaged session files from their backups and rebuilds missing index entries. Nothing is deleted." Cancel / Repair. After the call the screen shows `repaired` in a toast and reloads the audit; a 409 is not an error here, it means some items remain, and the screen says so.
- Items in `unsafe_to_repair` show "Needs manual attention on the server" and no button.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two `Endpoint` cases; the POST treats 409 with a decodable body as a result, not a failure; tolerant models.
- [ ] Row detail text from the audit; screen groups and explains items.
- [ ] Repair button gating, copy, toast, and reload; no optimistic state.
- [ ] Two servers: follows the active server.
- [ ] VoiceOver and Dynamic Type; strings localized.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: decode fixtures for a clean audit and one with items; a client test that 409 with a body returns the result; button gating test.
- Simulator: open Server → Session Store on the maintainer's server (read only). Run Repair only if the audit shows repairable items and the maintainer agrees in the PR thread.

## Non-goals

Per-session repair. Deleting sessions (item 12).

title: feat(sessions): per-session toolset restriction in Session Details
body:
Part of #395 (item 11a). Lives in the Session Details sheet from #419.

## Context

`POST /api/session/toolsets` `{ session_id, toolsets: [names] | null }` (`routes.py:15688`). `null` clears the override so the session follows the active profile's defaults. Validation is shape-only: a non-empty list of non-empty strings, or null. Returns `{ ok: true, enabled_toolsets }`. 400 for subagent (view-only) sessions or a bad shape; 404 unknown session.

The WebUI builds the picker's catalog from `/api/mcp/servers` names (`static/ui.js:5440-5500`); whether built-in toolsets are prepended must be checked at the pin. title: feat(chat): background compression with progress, replacing the one-shot compress
body:
Part of #395 (item 11b). Replaces the one-shot compress behind `/compress` and `/compact`, which can outlive a tunnel's idle timeout.

## Context

| Route | Handler | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/session/compress/start` `{ session_id, focus_topic? }` | `routes.py:16304` → `_handle_session_compress_start` (`:26810`) | starts a background job; returns the job payload `{ ok, status: "running", session_id, focus_topic, started_at, updated_at }`; a repeat call while running returns the same payload; 409 "Session is still streaming; wait for the current turn to finish." or `{ error, type: "agent_runtime_stale", retryable: true }` |
| `GET /api/session/compress/status?session_id=` | `routes.py:13436` → `_manual_compression_status_payload` | `{ ok, status: "idle" \| "running" \| "done" \| "error" \| "cancelled", session_id, focus_topic, started_at, updated_at }` plus result fields when `done` and an error message when `error` (keys at the pin) |

The app today calls the synchronous `/api/session/compress` from `ChatViewModel.compressSessionFromSlashCommand` (`ChatViewModel.swift:3501-3549`) and overwrites the context ring from the response.

## Expected behavior

- `/compress` and `/compact` post to `compress/start` instead. The transcript shows the existing working row with "Compressing…" and the app polls `compress/status` every 2 seconds while `running`, backing off to 5 seconds after 30 seconds, stopping on `done`, `error`, `cancelled`, or when the chat view goes away. Polling resumes on foreground if the session is still open.
- On `done`: reload the session detail through the existing path so the transcript and context ring reflect the compressed state; toast "Context compressed". On `error`: show the message inline like other slash command failures. 409 streaming: the existing "wait for the current turn" message. `agent_runtime_stale`: message plus a Retry action.
- A **Compress Context…** row in the Session Details sheet (#419) triggers the same flow with an optional focus topic field, so the action is reachable without typing a slash command.
- If the app opens a session whose status is already `running` (started from the WebUI), the working row appears and polling begins.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two `Endpoint` cases; tolerant status model keyed on `status`.
- [ ] Slash command and Details row share one code path; polling cadence, stop conditions, and foreground resume as specified; no polling after the view model is gone.
- [ ] `done` reloads the session; ring updates; `error`, 409, and stale handled.
- [ ] Two servers: a poll never targets a server that is no longer active.
- [ ] Reduce Motion respected on the working row (already true; keep it).

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: URLProtocol sequence running → running → done drives one reload; error path; stop-on-teardown; foreground resume. Expectations, no sleeps.
- Simulator, one disposable session with a long transcript through the tunnel: `/compress`, watch the working row, confirm the ring drops and the transcript updates.

## Non-goals

Cancelling a compression (no upstream route). Compression recovery (11d).

title: feat(sessions): remove a session's worktree from Session Details
body:
Part of #395 (item 11c). Lives next to the worktree status in the Session Details sheet from #419.

`POST /api/session/worktree/remove` `{ session_id, force?: bool }` (`routes.py:15863` → `worktrees.remove_worktree_for_session`). Returns `{ ok: true, removed_path, warnings: [...] }`. 400 with a message for: not worktree-backed, locked by an active streaming session, locked by an active terminal session, and dirty or unpushed state unless `force` is true (exact conditions and messages at the pin, `worktrees.py:216-262`). The app already decodes `worktreePath` on sessions (`Session.swift:215`).

## Expected behavior

- In the Worktree section of Session Details, when status reports `exists`, a destructive **Remove Worktree** button. Disabled when `locked_by_stream` or `locked_by_terminal`, with the footnote "In use; stop the running response first."
- Alert: "Remove this worktree?" / "This deletes the folder at <path> on the server. The branch and its commits stay in the repository. Uncommitted changes in the worktree are lost." Cancel / Remove (destructive).
- First attempt sends `force: false`. If the server refuses because the worktree is dirty or unpushed, a second alert quotes the server's message and offers "Remove Anyway" which resends with `force: true`. No other path sets `force`.
- On success: toast "Worktree removed", show `warnings` if any, reload the worktree status so the section reflects the new state, and update the cached session's `worktreePath`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Endpoint.removeSessionWorktree`; tolerant response.
- [ ] Button gating on `exists` and the lock flags; two-step force flow; copy names the path and the consequence.
- [ ] Post-success reload and cache update scoped to the active server.
- [ ] Destructive-confirm haptic; strings localized.

## Validation plan

Creating worktrees (sessions get them at creation via the existing flow). Git operations on the worktree (Git sheet).

title: feat(chat): compression recovery card and focused continuation
body:
Part of #395 (item 11d). Lives in the transcript and the Session Details sheet from #419.

## Context

When compression cannot recover a session's context, upstream stamps the session with a recovery payload (`compression_recovery.build_compression_recovery_payload`): `{ terminal_state, recommended_action: "start_focused_continuation", source_session_id, created_at, title: "Context compression exhausted", summary, action_label: "Start focused continuation", message, details, last_prompt_tokens, ... }`, surfaced on the session object (`routes.py:22704`, key at the pin). `POST /api/session/compression-recovery/start` `{ session_id }` (`routes.py:15363` → `:23726`) creates a new focused continuation session copied from the source and returns it (keys at the pin). 409 "Session does not have a compression recovery action." when the payload is absent; 400 for subagent sessions; 404 unknown.

The app decodes none of this today (`HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift`).

## Expected behavior

- `SessionDetail` decodes the recovery payload tolerantly as an optional struct.
- When present, the chat shows a card at the live edge, in the style of the existing clarification card, titled with the payload's `title`, showing `summary`, and one button with `action_label`. The composer stays usable.
- The same card appears as a section in Session Details.
- Tapping the button shows an alert: "Start a focused continuation?" / "Hermes creates a new session that continues from this one with a compressed context. This session stays as it is." Cancel / Start. On success the app navigates to the returned session and refreshes the list. 409 dismisses the card and reloads the session (the server cleared it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Endpoint.startCompressionRecovery`; tolerant models.
- [ ] Card renders only when the payload is present; copy comes from the payload.
- [ ] Success navigates to the new session; 409 reloads; no optimistic navigation.
- [ ] Reduce Motion: the card appears without animation when set; VoiceOver reads title, summary, and button.
- [ ] Two servers: navigation stays on the active server.

## Validation plan

- `HermesMobileTests`: decode fixture with and without the payload; success navigation; 409 reload.
- Simulator: needs a session in the exhausted state; validate against fixtures and describe the manual path in the PR if none is available.

## Non-goals

Any change to how compression itself runs (11b).

body:

| Route | Body | Returns / errors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/file/create` (`:25410`) | `{ session_id, path, content? }` | `{ ok, path }`; 400 "File already exists" |

| `POST /api/file/rename` (`:25437`) | `{ session_id, path, new_name }` | `{ ok, old_path, new_path }`; 400 invalid name, exists, symlink; 404 |
| `POST /api/file/move` (`:25472`) | `{ session_id, path, dest_dir }` | `{ ok, ... }`; 400 invalid destination, into itself; 404 destination |
| `POST /api/file/delete` (`:25312`) | `{ session_id, path, recursive? }` | `{ ok, path }`; 400 "Set recursive=true to delete directories", symlink; 404 |
| `POST /api/file/path` (`:25640`) | `{ session_id, path }` | `{ ok, path }` absolute on-disk path |

Exact success keys must be validated at the pin or a live server and recorded in the PR.

App: `HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FileBrowserView.swift` (rows at `:78-88`), `FileBrowserViewModel.swift` (`loadDirectory` at `:162`, per-server expansion state at `:278-288`), `FileTree.swift`. The tree has no context menu today. Destructive alert precedent: `SessionListActionConfirmations.swift:31-53`.

## Expected behavior

- Long-press (context menu) on any row: **Rename**, **Move to…**, **Copy Path**, **Delete** (destructive). On folders additionally **New File…** and **New Folder…**. A toolbar **+** on the browser offers New File and New Folder at the root.

- Move to… presents a folder picker built from the same tree data, excluding the item itself and its descendants. Moving into the current folder is a no-op.
- Copy Path calls `/api/file/path` and copies the absolute path with a "Copied" toast.
- Delete alert: files "Delete <name>?" / "This removes the file from the server workspace. This cannot be undone."; folders "Delete folder <name> and everything in it?" with the same second sentence, sending `recursive: true`. Cancel / Delete (destructive).
- After every mutation reload the affected directory (and the destination for moves), keep expansion state, and show the server's message on any 400 or 404. No optimistic tree edits.
- All items disabled while a response is streaming for this session, with a footnote in the menu: "Available when the agent is idle."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Six `Endpoint` cases; tolerant responses.
- [ ] Menu items, toolbar +, alerts, picker, and copy as specified; folder delete always sends `recursive`.
- [ ] Directory reloads are scoped; expansion state survives; errors verbatim.
- [ ] Disabled while streaming.

Errors: 404 "File not found", 400 "Cannot save: path is a directory", 400 "Cannot save to a symlinked entry", 400 "Use /api/file/office-save for Office documents". Save posts and, on success, reloads the viewer so highlighting reflects the saved text; the sheet closes. Errors show the server message and keep the sheet open with the text intact.

title: Escape reads outside the workspace are browser-only upstream
body:
Part of #395 (item 16). Filed `ready-for-human` with `upstream-change`: the authorize step is browser-only at the pin.

## Context

| Route | Handler | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/escape/authorize` `{ session_id, path }` | `routes.py:18065` → `workspace.authorize_escape_target` | returns `{ token, session_id, workspace_root, surface_path, external_root, external_entry_rel, surface_target, expires_at }` (TTL `_ESCAPE_AUTH_TTL_SECONDS`) |
| `GET /api/escape/list?session_id=&token=&path=` | `:18098` | directory listing under the authorized external root |
| `GET /api/escape/file/read?session_id=&token=&path=` | `:18123` | file content |
| `GET /api/escape/file/raw?session_id=&token=&path=` | `:14407` | raw bytes |

**Blocker.** `_handle_escape_authorize` returns 403 "browser origin required" unless the request carries an `Origin` header, then runs `_check_csrf`, which for an authenticated browser-shaped request requires a CSRF token header that matches a cookie the browser receives. Hermex sends neither and has no CSRF cookie flow (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift`). Faking an `Origin` to pass as a browser and reverse-engineering the CSRF pairing would be a spoof of upstream's deliberate guard, not a client feature.

## What the maintainer needs to decide

1. Ask upstream for a non-browser path: either honor the session cookie alone for `escape/authorize` when no `Origin` is present (the same rule `_check_csrf` already applies to "non-browser clients"), or a dedicated token endpoint. File the request in `nesquena/hermes-webui` and link it here.
2. Or close this as `wontfix`: symlinked paths outside the workspace stay unreadable from the phone, which is the safe default.

## If upstream lands a client path, the expected behavior is

- In the file tree (#401), a symlink or entry whose target is outside the workspace shows a "Outside workspace" badge. Tapping it authorizes once per session and target, caches the token until `expires_at`, and browses `external_root` read-only with the same tree and viewer components. Nothing under an escape token is ever written.
- Token expiry re-authorizes transparently on the next request.

## Acceptance criteria (deferred until the decision)

- [ ] Four `Endpoint` cases; token cached per server, session, and target with expiry.
- [ ] Read-only enforced in the UI; no 14a or 15 actions under an escape root.
- [ ] Two servers: tokens never cross servers.

## Non-goals

Any workaround that sends a fabricated `Origin` or CSRF header.

title: docs: correct i18n serializer, catalog membership, plural sets, and TestFlight shutdown guidance
body:
Fixes #308

## What changed

Documentation-only correction of the four authority defects from #308. No Swift, catalog, or project-file changes; nothing reopens the #305 consolidation. (Cross-link for #305 readers: this PR resolves the four factual corrections that review surfaced.)

1. **Removed the false String Catalog serializer claim** (`docs/agents/i18n.md`). The doc claimed a `json.dumps` one-liner reproduces `Localizable.xcstrings` byte-identically. Verified false: both `sort_keys` variants produce ~4.0 MB against the real ~3.8 MB; the file mixes compact grouped lines with expanded entries and its `strings` keys are in grouped-append order, so no `json.dumps` variant can round-trip it. Replaced with the issue's safe procedure: parse/validate, targeted insertion preserving untouched bytes (with the exact working insertion, leading comma included), and a parsed before/after subtree diff asserting only intended keys/languages changed.
2. **Corrected catalog target membership** (`docs/agents/i18n.md`). Verified in `project.pbxproj`: the catalog ships in the app and Live Activity widget only; the Share Extension's Resources phase contains only `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, and its five status strings are hardcoded English literals. The doc now says exactly that and states the Share Extension localization policy.
3. **Replaced the unsafe plural-category family table** (`docs/agents/i18n.md`). "Romance, German, Dutch, Turkish → one, other" and "Hebrew → one, two, many, other" are stale: `es`/`fr`/`it`/`pt-BR` gained `many` in 2021, Hebrew cardinal `many` was removed in CLDR 42 (2022), and Romanian has `few`, so family shortcuts mislead. Replaced with verified per-locale sets for all 18 shipped locales, a derive-and-verify instruction per locale, and a note that the 11 existing Hebrew `many` variations are dead (byte-identical to `other`) and must not be preserved or copied.
4. **Reconciled TESTFLIGHT.md with AGENTS.md.** Step 7's `xcrun simctl shutdown all` now targets the exact captured simulator UDID and retests against `id=<udid>`. Step 12's "Workflow path, if implemented:" now names `.github/workflows/external-testflight.yml`, which exists and is active per Step 3.

## How it was tested

- Every corrected claim was re-verified programmatically before editing: serializer round-trip attempt (both `sort_keys` variants fail), Resources-phase membership in `project.pbxproj`, an 18-locale plural audit against current CLDR cardinal rules (incl. the Hebrew `many` entries), the working catalog-insertion recipe (parse-tested), and workflow existence. `git diff --check` is clean.
- The full `xcodebuild test` suite was not run: the authoring machine has Xcode Command Line Tools only. This diff touches two markdown files and no build inputs. By design, `pr-ci.yml`'s docs-only path skips the macOS Build and Test job for exactly this change; the required "CI Gate" check still runs and passes on a legitimate skip. Happy to run the full suite on request if the maintainer prefers a non-skipped run.

## Checklist

- [ ] The full test suite passes locally — not run; docs-only diff (two markdown files), no Xcode on the authoring machine, and CI's docs-only path skips the suite by design. Maintainer can request a full run.
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly — N/A, no code or models changed.
- [x] No new third-party dependencies.
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes — every documentation claim was verified against the tree and current CLDR data.

Built with an AI coding agent (Prime Agent, GLM).

After merge, I will comment the correction link on #305 per the issue's acceptance note.

title: Bug: In the expanded 1.6 composer, taps on the text never place the caret; double-tap select and the edit menu (Paste/Select/Select All) are dead too
body:
### App & environment
- Hermex 1.6.x from the App Store
- Device: iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26.6.1
- Server: self-hosted hermes-webui (not involved; issue is purely UI-side)
### What happens
Since the 1.6 update, in the **expanded** composer card (keyboard up, editor focused):
1. A single tap anywhere on the text does **not** move the caret to the tapped position. The caret stays where it was.
2. Double-tapping a word does **not** select/highlight it.
3. Long-press does **not** bring up the edit menu (Paste / Select / Select All …).
4. The keyboard's long-press-on-space trackpad mode **still moves the caret** correctly.
Typing, sending, and the slash/@ autocomplete all still work. Collapsed-pill tap-to-focus works.
### What I expected
Tapping to place the caret, double-tap word selection, and the long-press edit menu — all standard UITextView behavior that worked in 1.5.
### Why this looks like a regression in 1.6
The 1.6 composer rewrite introduced `ComposerChipTextView`, which adds its own `UITapGestureRecognizer` (chip-tap detection) in its initializer (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ComposerChipTextView.swift`, `init(frame:textContainer:)`, ~line 58). That recognizer is always installed — even when the draft has no chips. UITextView's tap-to-caret, double-tap-select, and edit-menu interactions are themselves gesture recognizers; an extra competing recognizer (even with `cancelsTouchesInView = false`) is a well-known way to break them (cf. SwiftUI + UIKit gesture conflicts on wrapped text views). In 1.5 the composer editor was a plain `PastingTextView` with no added recognizer, and tap-to-caret worked.
**Liquid Glass is ruled out as the cause:** the composer's `adaptiveGlass` modifier short-circuits to a plain opaque background whenever Reduce Transparency is on (`AdaptiveGlassModifier.swift`, `AdaptiveGlassSurface.resolve`), and the bug persists unchanged with Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Reduce Transparency ON on my device. The interactive glass layer therefore never exists in that configuration, yet taps still fail — pointing squarely at the always-on chip-tap recognizer (the only gesture recognizer the composer adds to its text view; verified by a codebase-wide search).
### Workaround
Long-press spacebar (trackpad mode) still moves the caret, as does typing.

title: feat(auth): connect Hermex directly to Craft servers
body:
## Problem

Hermex currently assumes every configured server is `hermes-webui`: HTTP(S) REST endpoints, password/session-cookie authentication, and SSE chat streams. A user needs Hermex to connect directly to a self-hosted Craft Agents server without a compatibility relay.

Craft uses a distinct WebSocket RPC protocol. Treating its token as a Hermes password or entering a `ws://` URL in the existing Hermes form cannot work and would make failures misleading.

## Verified Craft contract

Verified against the local `craft-agents-oss` checkout on 2026-09-07:

- Headless entry: `packages/server/src/index.ts`
- Transport: `ws://` or `wss://`
- Default bind: `127.0.0.1:9100`
- Authentication handshake:
  ```json
  {
    "id": "<uuid>",
    "type": "handshake",
    "protocolVersion": "1.0",
    "token": "<CRAFT_SERVER_TOKEN>"
  }
  ```
- Success is a `handshake_ack`; invalid credentials return an error/close.
- Craft's smoke coverage is in `packages/server/src/__tests__/smoke.test.ts`.
- Plain `ws://` is acceptable only for localhost development. Remote servers require `wss://`.

Exact session, message, streaming-event, reconnect, and cancellation envelopes must be verified from Craft's typed RPC transport/handlers immediately before each implementation slice. Do not infer them from the Hermes contract.

## Scope

Add Craft as an explicit server kind and build a native Craft transport boundary alongside the existing Hermes API client.

### Slice 1: connection and authentication

- Add an explicit `Hermes` / `Craft` server kind to configured server identity.
- Add a Craft connection form using WebSocket URL plus server token.
- Store the Craft token in Keychain, keyed by canonical server identity.
- Perform the real Craft `1.0` handshake before reporting success.
- Allow `ws://localhost`, `ws://127.0.0.1`, and simulator-to-host development addresses intentionally supported by the app; reject unencrypted non-local remote endpoints.
- Map DNS, TLS, timeout, protocol-version, and credential failures to distinct user-facing errors.
- Never log or persist the token outside Keychain.
- Preserve existing Hermes onboarding and configured servers without migration regressions.

### Follow-on slices in the same integration

- Typed Craft RPC request/response codec with tolerant decoding.
- Session list and session history parity.
- Start, steer, stop, and resume session flows.
- Streaming event handling, reconnect, replay/deduplication, and app foreground recovery.
- Workspace browsing and supported system entry points.
- Explicit capability gating for unsupported Hermes-only and Craft-only features.

## Acceptance criteria for Slice 1

- A local Craft server at `ws://127.0.0.1:9100` can be added from the simulator with a valid token.
- Invalid tokens and incompatible protocol responses do not create or activate a server.
- Non-local `ws://` is rejected before credentials are transmitted.
- Craft credentials, selections, and state do not appear under a Hermes server or another Craft server.
- Removing a Craft server removes its local credential and state using the existing removal semantics.
- Existing Hermes login, server switching, and persistence tests remain green.
- Focused URL-policy, handshake, cancellation, timeout, and Keychain-isolation tests are included.
- A signed Debug build is manually exercised on iPhone 17; both valid and invalid Craft login paths are checked.

## Non-goals

- No Hermex-hosted relay or backend.
- No conversion of Craft into the Hermes REST/SSE contract.
- No enterprise identity provider invented in the mobile client. OIDC/SAML belongs at an explicit, verified server or reverse-proxy contract.
- No third-party WebSocket dependency; use `URLSessionWebSocketTask`.
