title: feat(bots): show tools, reasoning and work progress in chat
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #475

## What changed

Bot chat showed only user and assistant text; tool calls, model-supplied reasoning, plan progress, notices and memory notes were invisible, so an operator on the phone could not tell what the bot was doing.

Bot chat now renders the same log rows Sessions uses (thinking row, dense tool rows with `+N previous tool calls`, expand and long-press copy), plus a Plan row and notices above the composer. Variant A from the maintainer-selected mocks.

- **Settled turns** come from the resume snapshot, which already carries `role: tool` rows (`name`, `context`, `args`) and assistant `reasoning`. `BotTranscriptProjection` anchors them to the message they precede, keeping the `<root>/<row index>` identity.
- **Live turns** reduce gateway events in a bounded `BotTurnActivity`: `tool.start`/`tool.complete` keyed by `tool_id`, `thinking.delta`/`reasoning.delta`/`reasoning.available`, keyed `notification.show`/`clear`, `review.summary` memory notes (64 rows, 32 KB reasoning, 8 notices). `todo.updated` and `todo_state` feed a revision-monotonic `BotPlan`; `status.update` feeds the working label. Activity events during known work update local state without a snapshot read.
- **Replay** rebuilds the current turn when the sequence is continuous, or from the last `message.start` the ring still holds; otherwise the live rows are dropped and the next full snapshot shows the settled ones, so overlap never duplicates a card.
- Display follows the existing global Chat toggles (Thinking and Tool Cards, expand defaults); the Plan row stays visible with cards off. Tool output is text only.
- Deliberately not wired: `message.react` (the snapshot carries no reactions to show back, a one-way door) and `learning.frames` (terminal-sized renders).

title: feat(bots): answer approvals, questions and credential prompts from the phone
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #476

## What changed

A bot that hit an approval, a question or a credential prompt was stuck until someone reached a Mac. Blocking requests are now answered from the phone, in the transcript where the work stopped.

- **Approvals and questions.** The card renders the request, its consequence and the command, and offers exactly the choices the host offered — a smart-denied request legitimately has no session or permanent allow, so neither does the phone. Read from the resume snapshot (`pending_approval`, `pending_clarify`), so an answer given in Desktop clears the card on the next read with no polling.
- **Sudo and secret prompts.** `#491` listed these as Desktop-only. That was a product call, not a wire constraint: `sudo.respond` and `secret.respond` take a `request_id` from any connected client, and the host's own terminal UI answers over the same methods (`ui-tui/src/app/useMainApp.ts:1025`). The phone now answers both — masked field, the host's own wording, the variable name a secret will be saved under — and Skip sends the empty string the host documents as a decline, releasing the bot immediately instead of parking it for 120s/300s.
- **MCP setup.** The only Desktop-renderer kind with a person in the loop and, at ten minutes, the longest wait in the set. Skip sends `{"status": "declined"}`, which the tool reads as a final no and is told never to re-ask.
- **The other five.** `terminal.read`, `window.read`, `preview.read`, `preview.act` and `tour` genuinely cannot be answered here — the answer is data Hermes Desktop's own renderer holds, and nobody types one at the Mac either. Each has a host deadline (30s/45s) after which the bot carries on, so the card reports the wait and keeps Stop rather than sending the user to a desk they are not sitting at.

Answering captures generation, runtime and request id on tap and revalidates at the socket write, so a stale card fails closed. Three outcomes are distinguished: accepted; `resolved: 0` / `status: expired`, an action failure that leaves the card inert with the connection intact; and a lost socket, whose outcome is unknown, warns, and is never resent. `approval.received` only acknowledges delivery and is deliberately never called.

Presentation is Variant A from the maintainer-selected mocks, in the Sessions vocabulary. The Sessions clarification card's surfaces, response field and submit button moved into a shared `PendingRequestSurfaces.swift` that both surfaces now use — a pure move with no visual change to Sessions, and the thing that caught two divergences in the Bot card.

Contract verified against hermes-agent `cd2bd16`: `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py` (`clarify.respond`:1586, `sudo.respond`:1649, `secret.respond`:1654, `mcp.setup.respond`:1640), `server.py` (`_respond`:13834, `_block` deadlines:4547, pending snapshot keys:10881, callbacks:8137/8277), `tools/setup_mcp_tool.py:52` (declined vs unanswered), `tools/terminal_tool.py:530` (empty password is a documented skip).

## How it was tested

- Full suite: `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -parallel-testing-enabled NO` → **TEST SUCCEEDED**, 2436 tests, 0 failures, 2 pre-existing skips.
- New focused tests: `BotPendingRequestParsingTests` (host choice sets, omitted-choice rebuild, batch question ids and locked answers, credential and Desktop-task event mapping, a credential prompt without a request id is dropped), `BotAnsweringTests` (dispatch params per kind, already-resolved, stale-action refusal, dispatch-guard revalidation, lost socket → uncertain and never resent, Desktop answer reconciliation, connection isolation, decline gating), `BotChatPresentationTests` (approval / question / sudo / secret / MCP-setup / Desktop-task cards, secure field, no input where there is no answer).
- Signed Debug build installed and launched on iPhone 17 via `build_run_sim`.
- Not exercised: the live host. No mutations were run against it; the gateway contract above was read from the pinned source.

### Screenshots

All seven cards — approval, already-answered, question, sudo, secret, MCP setup, Desktop task — are in [this comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/504#issuecomment-5638038243). Rendered from the XCTest attachments under scripted gateway fixtures, not mocks.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally (`xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17'`)
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)

## Notes for review

- **Sudo over a tunnel.** The password crosses as a JSON-RPC param on the same wss + basic-auth channel that already carries session content, and the host's terminal UI does the same over the same wire. On a LAN that is unremarkable; through a Cloudflare tunnel it is a Mac admin password leaving the network. Worth a deliberate yes rather than an inherited one. A LAN-only gate is easy to add if preferred.
- **"Always allow"** writes a permanent host rule with no second confirmation, matching the Sessions approval overlay. Desktop does confirm it. Possibly worth a follow-up for both surfaces.

A live tool row arrives with no state change to observe, so nothing signals when the `LazyVStack` has materialized it. title: feat(bots): keep the Bots inbox live and honor Desktop pins and hidden bots
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #474

## What changed

The Bots inbox loaded the roster once and went stale until you refreshed or foregrounded. It also ignored the pins and hidden bots you set in Hermes Desktop.

Now the inbox keeps its socket while on screen. Each `sessions.changed` broadcast coalesces into one roster reload with at most one queued, stale replies are dropped by wire identity, and a dropped socket keeps the roster with a one-line explanation plus Reconnect and pull-to-refresh. Pinned bots sit above the list as large avatar tiles, hidden bots stay out until revealed from a footer button or matched by a search, and the row's long-press menu offers Pin, Unpin, Hide and Unhide. A blue dot marks a bot whose canonical chat moved past what this phone last showed; the mark is device-local and clears on open or return.

Pin and hide writes go through `profiles.configure` with the whole `hermes-bots` object plus `ui_meta_expected_revisions`, so unrelated Desktop fields survive and a Desktop write in between is reported as a conflict with a fresh roster, never as success. Desktop's named sections are not shown: their catalog lives in Desktop's renderer `localStorage` and only an opaque `sectionId` reaches the host, recorded in `docs/agents/bots.md` as an upstream gap.

Contract verified against hermes-agent `ee35a4624fa22237a90426f5e21d8b4f2ce3a49b`: `profiles.list` row shape, `profiles.configure` key-wise merge and CAS in `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py`, `sessions.changed` in `tui_gateway/change_watcher.py`, `gateway.ready.change_events` in `tui_gateway/ws.py`, and Desktop's `hidden-bots.ts` / `user-sections.ts`. Pin and hide were also exercised live against the maintainer's host on the test bot.

title: fix(chat): chat text paints over the nav-bar title while scrolling (iOS 26 soft scroll edge)
body:
# Hermex — chat text paints over the navigation-bar title while scrolling

## Environment
- Hermex (native SwiftUI client), latest master as of 2026-09-15 (560ea07), iPhone PWA-free native UI.
- iOS 26 (Liquid Glass era), dark mode, iPhone 15 Pro-class device.
- Any chat whose transcript overflows and starts scrolling; reproduces every time.

## What happens
When the transcript scrolls, chat text renders *over* the navigation-bar title block
(the `ChatToolbarTitleLabel` two-row title/subtitle in `.principal`) and the trailing
action cluster. The two texts are physically stacked and unreadable until the reader
scrolls somewhere that happens to separate them.

## Why
In `ChatTranscriptView.transcriptScrollView` the `ScrollView` is mounted edge-to-edge
under the system navigation bar and gets `.adaptiveSoftScrollEdges()`, which on iOS 26
applies `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.soft, for: [.top, .bottom])`. A soft top edge keeps the
scrolled layer painting beneath the translucent Liquid-Glass navigation bar. Two things
make the bleed very visible:

1. `ChatToolbarTitleLabel` renders title plus a workspace/profile subtitle in a
   two-row `.principal` slot, so the overlap area is taller than the regular one-line
   title and crosses into the message rows themselves.
2. `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)` lets the user drag content all the way up
   with the keyboard half-open, so the bleed is not just transient.

On iOS < 26 the fallback material path does not show this (opaque bar), which matches
the bug being iOS-26-era.

## Suggested fix
Pick one (the first is the smallest diff and keeps the current design):

A. Give the chat transcript a hard top scroll edge instead of soft, so content stops
   visibly under the bar instead of painting beneath it:

```swift
// ChatTranscriptView.swift, transcriptScrollView
.adaptiveSoftScrollEdges()        // current
// → replace with (on this screen only):
#if compiler(>=6.2)
if #available(iOS 26, *) { ... .scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard, for: .top) ... }
#endif
```
   Concretely: extract the existing `AdaptiveSoftScrollEdgeModifier` design into
   `adaptiveSoftScrollEdges(.bottom)` for this screen (or add an
   `AdaptiveHardTopScrollEdgeModifier` that calls `.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard, for: .top)`
   under iOS 26 and no-ops otherwise). Session list, file browser, and tasks keep soft
   edges; only the chat transcript stops under a hard bar.

B. Alternatively, keep soft edges but never let the two-row subtitle stack — drop
   `headerSubtitle` on narrow widths or hide the subtitle while the reader is not at
   the very bottom. This only reduces the symptom; text still paints under the bar.

## Repro
1. Open a chat with a transcript taller than the screen.
2. Scroll up by any amount.
3. Observe message text rendering across the title/subtitle and toolbar cluster.
4. Repeat with the keyboard half-dismissed (`.interactively`) — stronger bleed.

Expected: content scrolls *under* an opaque (or hard-eged) bar and is never painted on top of the title.

Attached: two screenshots from the user (dark mode, RU locale) — the first while
streaming, the second right after reopening the app, both showing message text over
the title row.

title: fix(chat): stop transcript bleed under the two-row nav title on iOS 26
body:
# fix(chat): stop transcript bleed under the two-row nav title on iOS 26

Fixes a reproducible iOS-26 rendering overlap in the chat screen: when the
transcript scrolls, message text paints beneath the translucent Liquid-Glass
navigation bar and visually collides with the two-row `.principal`
`ChatToolbarTitleLabel` (title + workspace/profile subtitle), plus the trailing
toolbar cluster — text on text, unreadable until the reader happens to scroll
separating rows.

## Root cause

`ChatTranscriptView.transcriptScrollView` applies `.adaptiveSoftScrollEdges()`,
which on iOS 26 maps to `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.soft, for: [.top, .bottom])`.
A soft top edge keeps the scrolled layer painting beneath the bar. The tall
two-row principal title makes even a few pixels of bleed overlap real message
rows; `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)` lets users drag the bleed in
with the keyboard half-open, so it is not transient.

## Change

- Add `AdaptiveHardTopScrollEdgeModifier` in `AdaptiveGlassModifier.swift`:
  same resolution gate as the soft variant (iOS 26 availability +
  `AdaptiveScrollEdgeTreatment.resolve` + Reduce Transparency), but applies
  `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard, for: .top)` — content stops at the bar's bottom
  edge instead of painting beneath it. No-op below iOS 26 where the bar is
  opaque, mirroring the soft fallback path.
- New `View.adaptiveHardTopScrollEdge()` extension next to
  `adaptiveSoftScrollEdges`.
- In `ChatTranscriptView.transcriptScrollView`, keep the existing soft treatment
  only for `.bottom` (`adaptiveSoftScrollEdges(.bottom)`), and add
  `.adaptiveHardTopScrollEdge()` for the top edge.

Session list, file browser, tasks, and Bots views keep their current soft top
edges; only the chat transcript surface changes, and bot chat
(`BotChatView`, which reuses `ChatToolbarTitleLabel`) can adopt the same
modifier in a follow-up if the same bleed is confirmed there.

## Verification

- [x] Diff applies cleanly on master (560ea07).
- [ ] `xcodebuild build -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` — needs a macOS host; please run in CI.
- [ ] Manual on an iOS 26 device: open a transcript taller than the screen, scroll; message text must stop at the nav bar's bottom edge and never overlap the title/subtitle or toolbar cluster.
- [ ] Check Reduce Transparency path (bar falls back to opaque material; modifier is a no-op).
- [ ] Check Reduce Motion and older iOS (< 26) builds — no behavior change.

## Notes for reviewers

- `AdaptiveScrollEdgeTreatment.resolve` is reused unchanged so the hard edge
  honors the same Reduce Transparency fallback the app already standardizes on.
- If the maintainer prefers zero new API surface, an alternative is calling
  `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard, for: .top)` inline in `transcriptScrollView`
  behind the same availability check; the extracted modifier was chosen to
  match the codebase's existing soft/hard treatment pattern and to be reusable
  for `BotChatView`.


Fixes #510

Stacked on #482. Picked from the mock page (option E) on 2026-09-15.

## Problem

The bot editor offers Desktop's 8 shapes and a color, but every drawn face has the same neutral eyes. Bloub (MIT, https://github.com/jeremy-prt/bloub) uses the same 8 shapes plus 16 rest expressions defined as eye width, height, tilt and spacing.

## Scope

- Add a 16-case expression vocabulary (neutral, attentive, surprised, excited, happy, laughing, angry, sad, scared, wary, confused, curious, proud, shy, bored, sleepy) rendered by `BotAvatarMarkView` as eye geometry only. Unknown values render neutral.

Desktop ignores it for rendering.

Out of scope: any animation (separate issue), Desktop parity for rendering expressions.

title: feat(bots): blink idle faces and animate the working bot in chat
body:
Stacked on #482. Picked from the mock page (option G) on 2026-09-15.

## Problem

Drawn bot faces are frozen everywhere. Hermes Desktop blinks its faces every 3.2 s and leans and sways while a bot is thinking or working, on a 15 fps shared clock. Hermex's rule is no continuously repainting animation and every animation respects Reduce Motion.

## Scope

- Idle blink for every drawn face on screen (inbox rows, search rows, editor hero and picker preview): eyes squash vertically for about 180 ms every 3 to 5 s, phase seeded per bot so a list does not blink in unison. Driven by an explicit-entry `TimelineView` schedule so nothing repaints between blinks.
- Working pose only for the open bot in `BotChatView`, only while a turn is live: Desktop's lean-and-sway pose sampled at 15 fps, stopping the moment the turn ends.
- Static under Reduce Motion, static in the shape and expression tile grids, never in the Live Activity or share extension.
- Tests: blink schedule entries, seeded phase differs per bot, Reduce Motion yields a still face, working pose returns to rest when the turn ends.

Grok's bot chat puts the avatar and name in one glass pill beside the back button, and that pill is the way into bot settings. title: feat(voice): CarPlay voice-assistant support (iOS 26.4) — talk to Hermes hands-free in the car
body:
### Use case

I want to talk to my self-hosted Hermes agent hands-free while driving. Today, using Hermes in the car means reaching for the phone and typing or reading in the Chat composer — which is unsafe and impractical at the wheel.

iOS 26.4 added a native CarPlay app category for voice-based AI assistants. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude already ship as CarPlay apps: you tap the app icon on the CarPlay screen ("New voice chat" / "Connect") and get a real, hands-free voice conversation. Hermex currently has no such integration, so there is no way to drive and talk to your own agent.

References:
- ZDNET/Yahoo hands-on "I tested ChatGPT and Perplexity AI as my CarPlay voice assistants": https://autos.yahoo.com/general/articles/tested-chatgpt-perplexity-ai-carplay-020050965.html
- 9to5Mac "iOS 26.4 adds support for a new category of CarPlay apps": https://9to5mac.com/2026/02/18/ios-26-4-adds-support-for-voice-based-ai-apps-to-carplay/
- iClarified (entitlement details, requires iOS 26.4 minimum): https://www.iclarified.com/99965/ios-264-beta-adds-carplay-support-for-voice-ai-apps-like-chatgpt-and-gemini


### Proposed behavior

- Hermex appears as a CarPlay app in the new iOS 26.4 voice-assistant category, shown on the CarPlay dashboard alongside third-party AIs.
- Tapping the Hermex icon starts a hands-free voice session (like ChatGPT's "New voice chat" or Perplexity's "Connect").
- The session talks to the agent on the user's own server: user speaks → Hermex sends to the server's voice/prompt endpoint → STT → agent → TTS → reply is read back through the car audio.
- While the app is listening/processing, a Voice Control template surface shows visual feedback (live captions / thinking state), matching what ChatGPT/Perplexity display on the CarPlay screen.
- Built on top of the existing Voice Mode work (#249–#257), which already handles the speech pipeline, interruption, and pocket mode.


### Acceptance outcomes

- With an iPhone running iOS 26.4 (or later) connected to a CarPlay vehicle, the Hermex icon appears under the CarPlay voice-assistant apps and can be moved up in the CarPlay app list.
- Tapping the icon starts a voice conversation without opening the phone.
- A spoken question to the agent returns a spoken answer through the car audio with no interaction between start and end.
- The CarPlay screen shows visual listening/processing feedback (e.g. live captions) during the exchange.
- Works against a self-hosted hermes-webui / Hermes server; behavior on weak signal or server latency is acceptable (buffered, retried, or clearly announced) rather than failing.

### Upstream dependency notes

- **Server-side voice endpoints:** Hermex relies on the server for transcription (STT), agent processing, and ideally server-side quality TTS (see #255 for `POST /api/tts`). Whether CarPlay voice needs any new server capability vs. reusing the existing `/api/transcribe` + `/api/tts` pipeline depends on what hermes-webui exposes.
- **Link upstream:** `hermes-webui` (nesquena/hermes-webui) — if any additional voice/streaming endpoint is required, this belongs to that repo's issue tracker.
- **Apple side:** requires the iOS 26.4 CarPlay voice-assistant entitlement (app-side, no upstream server dependency).

Thanks for considering this for the roadmap — it would make Hermex complete for on-the-go (car) use.

title: feat(bots): send, stop, approve and retry inside a group room
body:
Part of [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493). **Effort:** L · **Risk:** HIGH. **Depends on:** [#486](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/486) merged (the room viewer), [#526](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/526) merged (pin at 0.21.2).

Contract and owner decisions: the decision comment on [#485](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/485) is the spec. Read it, AGENTS.md, `docs/agents/bots.md` and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` first. Work from a short `issue/<n>-slug` branch based on and targeting `master`. No push, PR, merge, release, new dependency or unapproved live-host mutation is authorized by this ticket.

## Problem

After #486 a user can watch a group room but cannot take part. The operator needs to send a message, stop the room, answer an approval and retry a stalled turn from the phone.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] **Composer.** The room screen gains the Bot Chat composer row (text only, no attachment button, no mic: rooms report `attachments: false` and voice is #487). Placeholder "Message <room name>". Send is `groups.send` with a device-minted `event_id` and a fresh device-minted `thread_id` per send, payload exactly `{text, thread_id}`, text ≤ 64 KiB and non-blank. The result is an acknowledgment that the message is durably appended and work is admitted, not that any bot replied; the sent bubble appears once the result arrives, never before. A lost socket after the write is an unknown outcome: warn, keep the draft, never resend automatically. A resend of the same `event_id` is only ever the user's explicit tap.
- [ ] **Mentions.** Reuse the #484 autocomplete with the room's members as the roster (handle and display name), plus `all` and `everyone`, which the server honors here. Send the text as typed; no annotation is appended because the room policy does the routing.
- [ ] **Stop.** The composer action button becomes Stop while `driver_status.working` or any task is `stopping`, exactly as Bot Chat does. `groups.stop` binds to the whole room: copy says it stops every bot in the room. No confirmation. The button reads "Stopping…" until `driver_status.counts.stopping` is zero and is disabled when nothing is queued or running. The result's `cancelled` count is informational, not proof of completion.
- [ ] **Approvals.** `driver_status.pending_actions` entries of kind `approval` render with the existing pending-request card offering only `once` and `deny`. On tap capture `member_id`, `task_id`, `execution_generation` and `request_id` and revalidate at the socket write; send `groups.approve`. Error 5119 "room approval is no longer pending" leaves the card inert and re-reads state. A lost socket is an unknown outcome and is never resent.
- [ ] **Retry.** A `pending_actions` entry of kind `retry` renders as a Retry row on the same card; `groups.retry {room_id, task_id}`. Error 5118 re-reads state. Any other pending kind shows the existing Desktop-attention state and is never acted on.
- [ ] **Status line.** Under the transcript: "Working…" while `working`, "Waiting for you" while `blocked`, "Stopping…" while stopping, nothing when idle. The server reports counts per status, not which member is working, so the line is generic.
- [ ] `BotClient` allowlists exactly `groups.send`, `groups.stop`, `groups.approve` and `groups.retry` with typed parameter validation, following the `profiles.*` exception pattern. Nothing else enters the allowlist.
- [ ] Rooms whose `authority_gateway_id` is not the connection's are read-only: composer hidden, one-line note. Never call `groups.promote` or `groups.demote`.
- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md` gains the participant section: send acknowledgment semantics, thread policy, Stop binding, approval tuple, unknown-outcome rule.

## Validation

- Focused XCTests at the `BotClient` validation and room reducer seams with scripted fixtures: send result appends exactly one bubble; duplicate `groups.log` events by `seq` are ignored; a stale approval tuple fails closed; Stop transitions through stopping to idle from state fixtures; a lost socket after send leaves the draft and shows the unknown warning; unknown pending kinds render the attention state; a room with foreign authority hides the composer.
- Full suite via `xcodebuild test -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -parallel-testing-enabled NO` → `TEST SUCCEEDED`. Signed `build_run_sim`. `git diff --check`, `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`.
- **Live procedure, owner-authorized on 2026-09-16, run only with Uzair's go at test time:** on the maintainer's host create one room named `hermex-test-<YYYYMMDD>` with members `dev` and `inbox-triage`, send one short prompt, Stop it, answer one approval if one appears, then disband that room and nothing else. Record the real `groups.log` pages from that run as fixtures with the install id replaced by a placeholder. No other room may be created, sent to, stopped or disbanded.
- Manual simulator plan: VoiceOver on the composer, Stop and approval card; Dynamic Type; Reduce Motion; light and dark; keyboard Return sends.

## Boundaries

- No client orchestration: the gateway is the driver. The phone reads state and log while the room screen is open and foregrounded (2 s working or blocked, 10 s idle), nothing in the background.
- Never write to the hidden `Group: <room_id>` member sessions; the server refuses with 4122 and the room log is the canonical transcript.
- Unknown outcomes are never retried automatically. Success is shown only after the server result.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code. Decision recorded with the owner on 2026-09-16.

title: feat(bots): cache group room logs for search and faster opens
body:
Part of [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493). **Effort:** M · **Risk:** MEDIUM. **Depends on:** [#486](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/486) merged.

Owner decision recorded on [#485](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/485) (2026-09-16): the viewer keeps the room log in memory, and room message search waits for this cache. Read AGENTS.md, `docs/agents/bots.md` (Local search) and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` first. Work from a short `issue/<n>-slug` branch based on and targeting `master`. No push, PR, merge or release is authorized by this ticket.

## Problem

Bot search is entirely local: it reads the SwiftData history cache written from Bot Chat snapshots. After #486 a room's name matches in search but its messages do not, and a room's log is re-paged from the server on every open.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] Write each paged `groups.log` result into the history cache under the room id, keyed by configured server and Bot connection UUID like Bot Chats. Only `message.user` and `message.member` events are cached; system and turn events are not searchable. Store the `seq` per row so a search hit opens the room scrolled to that event.
- [ ] The cache is append-only by `seq` and idempotent: a page that overlaps already-cached sequences writes nothing new. A `room_history_expired` error or a disbanded room drops its cached rows.
- [ ] The room screen opens from cache first, then pages from the cached cursor to `latest_seq`. Live reading never depends on the cache.
- [ ] Search matches room messages with the same 16 KB per-message limit and 100-hit cap as bots. A hit row shows the room name and the sending member.
- [ ] Rows follow the server and connection on removal exactly as Bot Chat history does.
- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md` Local search section documents the room rows.

## Validation

Focused XCTests: overlapping pages write nothing new; expired room drops rows; two connections with rooms of identical names stay separate; a hit opens at the right `seq`; a row over 16 KB is omitted. Full suite `TEST SUCCEEDED`, signed `build_run_sim`, `git diff --check`. Manual: search a word from the "Comms" room after opening it once.

title: feat(bots): create, rename and disband group rooms from the phone
body:
Part of [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493). **Effort:** M · **Risk:** HIGH (disband is permanent). **Depends on:** [#527](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/527) merged.

Contract and owner decisions: the decision comment on [#485](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/485) is the spec; the four reference screenshots attached there are the design and replace static mocks. Read AGENTS.md, `docs/agents/bots.md` and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` first. Work from a short `issue/<n>-slug` branch based on and targeting `master`. No push, PR, merge, release or unapproved live-host mutation is authorized by this ticket.

## Problem

After #527 a user can take part in rooms Desktop created but cannot create, rename or disband one from the phone.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] **Create, step one.** From the inbox's Groups section: a "New Group Chat" sheet with a "To:" chip field that filters the current connection's roster as the user types, the remaining bots listed below, and Next top-right. Hidden bots are included when named by the filter. The server caps a room at 2 to 6 members: Next stays disabled under two and the list stops accepting picks at six with a one-line reason.
- [ ] **Create, step two.** Stacked member avatars, a name field prefilled "Group Chat" (≤ 200 characters), a Create button. Create mints a UUID `room_id` on device and calls `groups.create {room_id, name, members}` with each member as `{member_id, profile, handle, display_name?}` where `member_id`, `profile` and `handle` are the Profile name (`default` keeps handle `hermes` only if the roster reports it that way; verify against `profiles.list`), and `display_name` the roster display name when present. No `target` is sent. Success opens the room. A duplicate submit reuses the same `room_id`, which the server treats as idempotent. Error 4123 (worker unavailable) tells the user to restart the Hermes gateway on their Mac; 4110 conflict re-reads the list.
- [ ] **Room profile** from the room pill: stacked avatars, the name as an editable field, a member list whose rows open each bot's profile, and an overflow menu. No "Add member": members are frozen at create and the server has no method to change them. No Routines section.
- [ ] **Rename.** Committing the name field calls `groups.rename {room_id, event_id, name}` with a device-minted `event_id`; the pill and inbox row update only after the result. The `room.renamed` event then arrives through the log and is rendered as a system line.
- [ ] **Disband.** In the overflow menu, red. The confirmation states the real consequence: the room and its history are removed from every device, all bots in it stop, and the room cannot be restored. Disabled with a "Finishing stop…" reason while any task is `stopping`, because the server refuses with 5114 until Stop completes. Calls `groups.disband {room_id}`; on the tombstone result pop to the inbox and drop the room. A lost socket after the write is an unknown outcome: re-read the list rather than retry.
- [ ] `BotClient` allowlists exactly `groups.create`, `groups.rename` and `groups.disband` with typed validation of every field above. Never `groups.promote`, `groups.demote`, `groups.replicate`, `groups.replica_state` or `groups.peer.*`.
- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md` gains create, rename and disband semantics and the permanent-id rule.

## Validation

- Focused XCTests: member count bounds; the create payload shape from a roster fixture including a row missing `display_name`; idempotent re-submit reuses `room_id`; rename waits for the result; disband disabled while stopping; foreign-authority rooms hide rename and disband.
- Full suite `TEST SUCCEEDED`, signed `build_run_sim`, `git diff --check`, `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`.

- Manual simulator plan: VoiceOver on the chip field and the disband confirmation; Dynamic Type; light and dark; keyboard focus order across the two steps.

title: feat(settings): "Buy Uzi a coffee" tip link and a one-time thank-you card
body:
## Context

Hermex is free and open source with no backend to fund it, but there is no way to say thanks. The Settings **App** card already links Privacy Policy and Support through `AppConfig`, so a tip link has a natural home. The maintainer's page is https://buymeacoffee.com/callmeuzi.

**Review risk, decided by the maintainer:** App Store guideline 3.1.1 has been applied to external tip links, and Apple's stated path is an in-app-purchase tip. We are shipping the external link anyway because the app is entirely free and the tip unlocks nothing. Copy must never imply a feature, perk, or unlock. The PR adds an App Review note saying exactly that. If App Review rejects, the fallback is a StoreKit consumable tip sheet in a follow-up issue, not a fight.

## Current behavior

No way to tip. Settings > App shows Version, Build, Privacy Policy, Support.

## Expected behavior

1. **Settings row.** A "Buy Uzi a coffee" row in the App card, after Support, icon `cup.and.saucer`, external-link accessory, opening the Buy Me a Coffee URL from `AppConfig` via `Link` like its neighbours. After the user has tapped it once, the row title becomes "Thanks for the coffee" with the same icon and still opens the same URL, so repeat tips stay one tap away.
2. **One-time card.** A dismissible card at the top of the session list, above the sessions, shown once per device once the device has completed 25 streamed responses across all servers. Copy: title "Enjoying Hermex?", body "It's free and open source. If it's earned a coffee, that would mean a lot.", primary button "Buy Uzi a coffee" (opens the URL), secondary "Not now". Either button hides the card forever. The Settings tap also counts as done and suppresses the card.
3. **Counting.** Count completed responses in the main app's stream coordinator completion path (`ChatStreamCoordinator.completeCurrentResponse`), stored in `UserDefaults` under a `TipJar` key enum alongside the other app-wide settings enums in `HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift`. Device-wide, not per server: this is about the person, and it must not leak into per-server state. Bot chat completions do not need to count.

## Acceptance criteria

- Settings row present, localized, VoiceOver label "Buy Uzi a coffee, opens in browser", opens the URL, flips to the thanked title after a tap and still opens the URL.
- Card appears exactly once, only after the threshold, on every configured server's session list, and never after a tap on either button or on the Settings row. Survives relaunch. Never shows while the shared-import banner is showing.
- Card is static: no animation beyond the list's own insertion, Reduce Motion safe, Dynamic Type safe, light and dark.
- No feature gating anywhere; nothing reads the tipped flag except the two pieces of copy above.
- Tests: threshold and one-shot logic (`TipJarPromptState` or similar) under XCTest, including "tapped in Settings suppresses the card" and "dismiss is permanent".
- Strings added to the String Catalog per `docs/agents/i18n.md`. "Uzi" and "Hermex" stay untranslated.
- No new dependency. No share extension or Live Activity changes.

## Validation plan

Unit tests for the counter and state. Manual on the simulator: fresh install, confirm no card; set the counter to 24 with a debug override or by completing responses, complete one more, confirm the card; tap Not now, relaunch, confirm gone; reset, tap the Settings row, confirm the title flips and the card never appears; switch servers, confirm identical state. Check both appearances and the largest accessibility text size.

## Non-goals

StoreKit tip jar, GitHub Sponsors, README or App Store description links, periodic re-prompts, any nudge in chat, the share extension, or the Live Activity.

title: feat(settings): ask for an App Store rating at a quiet moment, plus Rate and Report rows
body:
## Context

Hermex never asks for a rating, and App Store ratings drive discovery. Apple only allows the system prompt (`AppStore.requestReview`), shows it at most three times per 365 days, and decides itself whether to show it, so the app's job is to ask only at good moments and offer a reliable manual path. App Store ID: 6767006319. Related: #531 shares the completed-response counter and the session-list moment.

## Current behavior

No rating prompt. Settings > App has Version, Build, Privacy Policy, Support.

## Expected behavior

1. **Eligibility.** Device-wide, main-app chat only. Eligible when all hold: at least 10 completed streamed responses, at least 3 days since first launch, no rating request in the last 60 days, and at least 30 completed responses since the last request. Counter and dates live in `UserDefaults` under a key enum next to the other app-wide settings enums in `HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift`, reusing the completed-response counter if #531 landed first.
2. **Moment.** When eligible, call `requestReview` the next time the app enters the foreground with the session list on screen, or when the user pops back to the session list, and no stream is active on the active server. Never during a stream, never on a cold launch, never before the first response. Record the request timestamp whether or not iOS actually showed the prompt.
3. **Rate Hermex row.** In the App card after Support, icon `star`, external-link accessory, opening `https://apps.apple.com/app/id6767006319?action=write-review`. Always visible.
4. **Report a Problem row.** Next to it, icon `ladybug`, opening the repo's bug-report template chooser `https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/new/choose`. This is the honest route for unhappy users instead of a sentiment gate.
5. **Coordination with #531.** The #531 tip card does not show within 7 days of a rating request, and a rating request does not fire in a launch where the tip card is showing.
6. **Debug.** A "Reset rating prompt state" button in the Debug-only Developer card.

## Acceptance criteria

title: feat(chat): show steering hints inline in the transcript
body:
## Context

A user reported that after steering, only the "Steering hint delivered" toast appears and the text is gone from the conversation, so they cannot reference it later.

Since hermes-agent v2026.9.11 (included in our `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` pin), the agent persists each mid-turn steer as its own message. Verified against the live server on 2026-09-17 in a disposable session:

```json
{"role": "user", "display_kind": "steer",
 "content": "[OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE — a direct message from the user, delivered once at this position; not tool output and not a new delivery when replayed from conversation history]\n<steer text>\n[/OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE]"}
```

The same row arrives in the SSE `done` payload's `session.messages` and from `GET /api/session?session_id=…`. The Bot path (`session.resume` history) carries the same agent row. The upstream web UI only shows a transient chip; nothing renders the persisted row. Hermex's `ChatMessage` has no `display_kind` field.

## Current behavior

- Web UI path: `ChatViewModel.steerResponseFromSlashCommand` posts to `/api/chat/steer`, shows a timed notice (`showSteeringConfirmation`), and keeps no record of the text.
- When the turn completes, the persisted steer row is decoded as a plain user message, so it renders as a user bubble containing the raw marker text (or never appears on agents older than 2026-09-09, where the steer was smeared into the tool result).
- Bot chat: `BotTranscriptProjection` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotActivity.swift`) projects the same row as a plain user message.

## Expected behavior

- A delivered steer appears inline at its position in the transcript as a compact, visually distinct "Steer" bubble showing only the user's text, with the marker stripped.
- It appears immediately when the server accepts the steer, and the server-persisted row replaces the local echo when the `done` payload or a reload arrives. No duplicate.
- It survives turn end, session reload, cold launch from the SwiftData cache, and server switch.
- Same rendering in live Bot chat history and cached Bot history.
- The existing "Steering hint delivered" notice and the `pending_steer_leftover` fallback keep working.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ChatMessage` (`HermesMobile/Models/ChatMessage.swift`) decodes optional `display_kind`; unknown values do not crash and fall back to normal rendering. The SwiftData message cache round-trips it.
- A user message with `display_kind == "steer"` renders as a steer bubble (`MessageBubbleView`) with the `[OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE …]` / `[/OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE]` wrapper removed. If `display_kind` is absent but the content is exactly a marker-wrapped block, treat it the same, so older or drifted servers still look right.
- Steer rows are not user-turn boundaries for `TranscriptTurnClassifier`; they do not start a new turn or reset per-turn state.
- After `steerChat` returns `accepted: true`, a local steer row is appended right away and is dropped when the completed transcript from `done` or a reload contains the persisted row.
- Bot chat: `BotTranscriptProjection` carries `display_kind` through, and the same bubble renders in live and cached Bot history.
- Tests: decode of the row above; marker stripping with and without `display_kind`; local echo replaced on `done` via `ScriptedSSEStreamFixture`; Bot projection; turn classification unaffected.
- Dynamic Type, VoiceOver label ("Steering hint"), light and dark appearance.

## Validation plan

- Full XCTest suite.
- Simulator: start a slow tool-using prompt, steer, watch the bubble appear at once, wait for completion, reopen the session, kill and relaunch the app, confirm the bubble persists in both Chat and a Bot chat.

## Non-goals

- Editing or resending a steer from its bubble.
- Changing the toast, the leftover-queued fallback, or the steer transport.
- Rendering the agent's "the user is steering" reasoning differently; that is model output.

title: fix(chat): retry the reconnect probe after a transport drop instead of stranding the stream
body:
## Context

Reported by Brandon by email, with a reproduction, a reference patch, and a validation write-up against 560ea07. He saw the "Could not connect to the server" banner on iPhone while a later backend and tunnel check succeeded. He has no phone logs tying the incident to this path, and neither do we, but the source gap is confirmed on HEAD and matches the symptom for a tunnel hiccup.

## Current behavior

An SSE transport error suspends the stream and launches exactly one status probe:

- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:783` `handleTransportError` sets `isConnectionSuspended`, stops the SSE client, and fires `reconnectIfNeeded()` once.
- `performReconnectIfNeeded` (`:417`) calls `client.chatStreamStatus` once. On any error other than a missing-stream 404 it calls `streamCoordinatorDidReceiveRecoveryError` (`:513`) and returns. The stream stays suspended and the reconnect slot clears.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:2683` the one-second refresh loop `continue`s while the connection is suspended, so periodic recovery never touches it.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:5773` surfaces the URL error text as the composer banner.

Result: after a drop plus one transient probe failure, the banner stays up and nothing retries until scene background/foreground, navigating away and back, or sending a new message. The agent may still be finishing the response on the server the whole time.

Also, `chatStreamStatus` (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+Chat.swift:49`) passes no timeout, so a probe against a black-holed host waits the 60-second session default.

## Expected behavior

A transport drop followed by a transient probe failure self-heals without a lifecycle event. Retries are bounded, stay inside the existing single-flight reconnect task, never resend the chat POST, and surface the error only after the budget is spent. Non-transient failures surface immediately as today.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reconnect probe retries with delays of 1, 2, and 4 seconds, at most three retries after the initial probe, inside the existing `reconnectTask`. A lifecycle `reconnectIfNeeded` call during a backoff joins that task rather than racing a second probe.
- Retry only on transient failures: `URLError` connectivity codes (timed out, cannot connect, connection lost, not connected, cannot find host, DNS failed, data not allowed, resource unavailable) and HTTP 502/503/504. Unauthorized, decoding, other statuses, and the arbitrary 404 surface immediately. Missing-stream 404 keeps its existing finalize path and never retries.
- All existing fences hold at every loop top: task id, stream id, run generation, `activeStreamID`, `isConnectionSuspended`, `Task.isCancelled`. Replacement via `start`, terminal completion, `prepareForNewResponse`, and session reload still cancel the task mid-backoff.
- Recovery only ever issues status and stream GETs. No path resends the original chat POST.
- `chatStreamStatus` sends with an explicit timeout of about 10 seconds so the retry budget is bounded in seconds, not minutes. Verify the endpoint shape is unchanged (`GET /api/chat/stream/<id>/status`) against the pinned upstream copy or a running server.
- `streamCoordinatorDidConfirmRecovery` still clears a recovery banner on the first successful probe.
- The retry delay is injectable so tests do not sleep; the production default is a cancellation-aware `Task.sleep`.

## Validation plan

Focused XCTests in `HermesMobileTests/ChatStreamCoordinatorTests.swift`, using the existing coordinator spies. Keep it to roughly four cases:

1. Transport error, first probe throws a transient `URLError`, second returns active: the stream reattaches with no lifecycle call and no recovery error reported.
2. Four consecutive transient failures: exactly four probes, then one recovery error, stream still suspended and recoverable by a later lifecycle call.
3. Unauthorized, decoding, and arbitrary 404 each surface after exactly one probe.
4. Stream replaced by `start` during a backoff: the loop exits without probing again or touching the delegate.

Run the full suite before review. Manual simulator pass on a signed Debug build: start a long response, kill the local server mid-stream, restart it within a few seconds, and confirm the same reply resumes with no duplicate user message and no lingering banner.

## Non-goals

- Cancelling a pending retry on background or navigation. `suspendActiveStreamConnection` early-returns while suspended today, so the existing single probe already survives those events. Changing that policy needs its own issue with a foreground re-arm test.
- Any change to the stale-stream poll cadence or heartbeat handling.

## Reference

Brandon's patch is the reference shape: retry loop inside `performReconnectIfNeeded`, a `nonisolated static` transient classifier, and an injected sleeper. It targets 560ea07 and no longer applies on HEAD because #534 added a `ratingPromptState` initializer parameter. Reimplement on HEAD rather than applying the diff, and trim its 13 tests to the four above.

## What changed

Mid-turn steering hints now render inline in the transcript as compact, visually distinct "Steer" bubbles instead of leaking the server's out-of-band wrapper text.

- `ChatMessage` gains an optional `displayKind`, decoded tolerantly from `display_kind` under both `convertFromSnakeCase` and plain decoders; unknown values fall back to ordinary rendering.
- Content that is exactly the `[OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE …] … [/OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE]` block is recognized as a steer even without the flag, and the wrapper is stripped for display and dedup.
- Steer rows never open user-turn boundaries, carry no message actions, and show no timestamp or context menu.
- An accepted steer appends a local echo immediately; when the persisted row arrives via `.done` or a reload, the echo is replaced — dedup is kind-aware so an ordinary repeated prompt can't swallow a steer row (or vice versa).
- `displayKind` persists through the SwiftData cache, `BotTranscriptProjection`, and `BotHistoryCache`; cached bot history renders the same bubble.
- Accessibility label is "Steering hint" with the hint text as the value; supports Dynamic Type and light/dark appearance.
- Existing "Steering hint delivered." notice and `pending_steer_leftover` fallback are unchanged.
- Adds the "Steering hint" key to `Localizable.xcstrings` (all shipped languages, `needs_review`); the "Steer" caption reuses the existing catalog key.

## How it was tested

- New `HermesMobileTests/SteerMessageTests.swift`: decoding under both key strategies, unknown/missing `display_kind` fallback, exact marker stripping (including lookalike rejection), turn classification, SwiftData round-trip, Bot projection, kind-aware dedup, and the accept → local echo → `.done` replacement flow through `ScriptedSSEStreamFixture`.
- `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` passes (warning-only, no new violations).
- The full XCTest suite and the signed Debug simulator pass were not run in this environment (no macOS toolchain here); relying on CI. Before/after screenshots to be captured during QA.

title: fix(chat): profile chip still escapes the composer toolbar fade on iOS 27
body:
## Context
Follow-up to #458, which was closed by #459. #459 replaced the profile chip's SwiftUI `Menu` with `ChatUIKitMenuButton` so the chip would stay inside the `ComposerToolbarScroller` mask. That fix was only validated on iOS 26.5, because no iOS 27 runtime was available at the time. The problem still shows on an iOS 27 device. The dev Mac now has Xcode 27.0 and the iOS 27.0 simulator runtime, so it can be reproduced locally.

## Current behavior
In the expanded composer's toolbar row on iOS 27, scroll the row so the profile chip sits at the trailing edge. The chip renders at full opacity past the scroller's bounds and draws under or over the Send/Stop circle, so it is neither masked nor clipped. The model/effort, workspace, git branch, mic and context ring controls all fade correctly. The model/effort chip uses the same `ChatUIKitMenuButton` wrapper and behaves, so the difference is specific to the profile chip.

## Expected behavior
The profile chip fades and clips at both edges of the scroller exactly like its neighbours, and never draws outside the scroller or over the Send/Stop circle.

## Pointers
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerToolbarScroller.swift` holds the `.mask { fadeMask }`.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerSelectorControls.swift` holds `ComposerProfileSelectorMenu`. Compare it with `ComposerModelEffortMenu`, whose label has `.fixedSize(horizontal:)` and `.transaction { animation = nil }`; the profile label goes through `ComposerInlineControlLabel` with neither.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTactileButtonStyle.swift` holds `ChatUIKitMenuButton` and its `UIViewControllerRepresentable` backer.
- `ChatComposerView.toolbarRow`. Check the static single-profile label path (`isStatic`) as well.

## Acceptance criteria
- The bug is reproduced on the iOS 27.0 simulator from current `master` before any change, and the root cause is stated in the PR. If it does not reproduce on `master`, stop and report.
- On iOS 27, the profile chip fades at the leading and trailing edges and is never visible outside the scroller. This holds for both the multi-profile menu chip and the single-profile static label.
- The profile menu still opens from the chip and keeps its selected checkmark, empty state, disabled state and the "Choose profile" accessibility label.
- There is no visual or behavioural change on iOS 26.5.
- Fallback, only if containment proves impossible on iOS 27: the chip becomes a plain button that presents the profile list in a sheet, mirroring the workspace selector. If you reach this point, stop and confirm with the maintainer before building the sheet.

## Validation plan
- Attach before/after screenshots from the iOS 27.0 simulator with the chip at the trailing edge and at the leading edge.
- On iOS 27, also check RTL, an accessibility Dynamic Type size, Reduce Transparency, and light and dark appearance.
- Do one regression pass on the iOS 26.5 simulator.
- Run the full XCTest suite. The existing `ComposerToolbarScrollerTests` and profile menu tests must stay green. A unit test cannot cover the rendering itself, which is why this carries `needs-manual-validation`.

## Non-goals
- Changes to the other toolbar controls, the fade design or width, or the Send/Stop circle layout.
- Any change to profile-switching behaviour.

Part of [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493) (V1, Track A step 4). **Effort:** S/M · **Risk:** LOW. **Depends on:** [#538](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/538) green. **Parallel with:** [#551](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/551) and [#552](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/552) (this slice owns the transcript files, they own the composer); land the Ask Hermex step after the composer lane is merged, since it writes into the composer.

Read AGENTS.md, `docs/agents/bots.md` and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` first. Work from a short `issue/<n>-slug` branch based on and targeting `master`. No push, PR, merge, release, new dependency or unapproved live-host mutation is authorized by this ticket.

## Problem

You cannot copy a bot's reply. `BotArtifactMessageView` builds `MessageBubbleView(message:, textOnly: true)` without a context menu, and assistant turns bypass `MessageBubbleView` entirely, so the long-press menu, text selection and "Ask Hermex" from the regular chat never appear. It reads as broken.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] Long-press on any bot or user message offers Copy, using the existing `chatMessageContextMenu` / `ChatMessageActions` seam. Only actions that are true for Bots appear: no edit, regenerate or branch (history rules were settled in #481).
- [ ] Assistant text supports in-place selection through `ResponseTextSelection`, the same way the regular transcript does (#454).
- [ ] "Ask Hermex" on a selection adds it to the Bot composer (#455 behavior). If that needs the composer quote model, bring only the minimum chip; the quote detail view stays in [#564](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/564).
- [ ] Group room transcripts get the same Copy and selection.
- [ ] No new per-row state that invalidates the transcript while streaming; attach actions the way the regular chat does.

## Validation

- Focused XCTests at the actions seam: which actions a Bot message offers; copied text matches the rendered markdown source; Ask Hermex inserts into the Bot draft and persists through `ChatDraftStore`.
- Full suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` (scheme `HermesMobile`) → all green. Signed `build_run_sim`. `git diff --check`, `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`.
- Manual simulator plan: copy a long reply, select across paragraphs and a code block, Ask Hermex, VoiceOver custom actions, scroll performance while a reply streams.

title: feat(bots): open a bot conversation from a deep link
body:
Part of [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493) (V1, Track A step 6). Carved out of [#488](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/488) on 2026-09-17 so push and Live Activity taps do not wait for the share and Shortcuts pickers. **Effort:** S/M · **Risk:** MED. **Depends on:** nothing unmerged. **Blocks:** [#489](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/489), [#559](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/559). **Parallel with:** the composer lane and Track B slices P1–P4.

Read AGENTS.md, `docs/agents/bots.md` and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` first. Work from a short `issue/<n>-slug` branch based on and targeting `master`. No push, PR, merge, release, new dependency or unapproved live-host mutation is authorized by this ticket. Also read the deep-link handling in `ContentView.handleOpenURL` and the App Intent queue it drains.

## Problem

Nothing outside the app can land you in a specific bot conversation. Live Activity taps route to Sessions, and push notifications will need the same destination.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] A typed Bot destination (from [#488](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/488)): configured-server identity, Bot connection UUID, Profile identity, optional durable conversation identity. Never route by display name.
- [ ] The existing URL scheme (`HERMES_URL_SCHEME`) gains one bot route that encodes that destination. Opening it switches to the owning server if needed, then opens that bot's conversation.
- [ ] Defined outcomes, each tested: warm launch, cold launch (through the existing queued-link drain), logged out (lands after login), connection removed or server deleted (opens the app normally, no error), unknown Profile or conversation (opens that server's Bots inbox), Bot Mode toggle off (opens the session list, no Bot UI leaks).
- [ ] Opening a conversation follows the existing canonical resume rules; a deep link never sends a prompt and never triggers auto-continue on its own.
- [ ] No share-extension or App Intent picker work here; that stays in [#488](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/488).

## Validation

- Focused XCTests at the router seam for every outcome above, including a link for server B while server A is active (isolation: no credentials, cache or drafts cross over).

title: feat(push): hermex-push plugin MVP with sealed previews and a pairing route
body:
Part of [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490) (slice 1) and [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493) (V1, Track B step 1). **Effort:** L · **Risk:** HIGH. **Depends on:** the owner creating the `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push` repository (this ticket does not authorize creating it). **Parallel with:** all of Track A and with [#556](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/556) once the payload shape below is agreed.

The design section of [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490) is the spec. This code lives in the new repo under `plugin/`, not in the app repo. Tracked here so the queue stays in one place.

## Fact checks first (record results here before building)

1. **Does the turn-end hook fire for turns started from webui?** The reference plugin skips platforms that notify natively. Read how webui-originated sessions are tagged on the owner's host and whether `on_session_end` fires for them. [#561](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/561) depends on the answer; if it does not fire, report the size of the plugin change before committing to it.
2. **Can a `kind: platform` plugin mount a dashboard route** (`/api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing`)? If not, fall back to the one-time QR from a `hermes hermex-push pair` CLI, and tell the owner, because one-tap pairing in [#557](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/557) depends on it.
3. Which approval hook exists on 0.21.2: prefer `register_approval_transport`; use observer hooks only if present in `VALID_HOOKS`.

## Scope

- [ ] Platform `hermex`, env `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL`; coexists with Push (Cadu) on one host with exactly one Hermex push per turn.
- [ ] Push kinds for V1: `reply`, `approval`, `clarify`, `turn_error`. Cron `deliver: hermex` is V1.1 ([#566](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/566)).
- [ ] **Every payload carries the session's coarse `source`** (bot / webui / other) from day one, so webui push needs no redesign.
- [ ] Sealed previews exactly as in [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490): AES-256-GCM, key at `<hermes_home>/plugins/hermex-push/preview_key` (0600), AAD `hermex-preview-v1:sha256(install_key)`, HMAC `event_id`, `thread_id` and `collapse_id`. Any failure sends a content-free notification; never plaintext.
- [ ] Server-first pairing: `install_key` generated on first run; pairing route returns `{relay_url, install_key, preview_key}` behind dashboard auth.
- [ ] Coalesced tool-boundary events for Live Activity progress, keyed by session id.
- [ ] pytest fixtures; pin the install identifier form the app will send (`https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push.git/plugin`).

## Validation

pytest green. On the owner's host, with Uzair's go: install next to Cadu, confirm one Hermex notify POST per turn against a local capture endpoint, and that the captured body contains ciphertext only. No secrets in the issue or PR.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code. Scope settled with the owner on 2026-09-17.

title: feat(push): relay MVP on a Cloudflare Worker
body:
Part of [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490) (slice 2) and [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493) (V1, Track B step 2). **Effort:** L · **Risk:** HIGH. **Depends on:** the `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push` repository; the payload shape from [#555](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/555). **Parallel with:** all of Track A, and with [#555](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/555) once the payload is agreed.

The design section of [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490) is the spec. Lives in the new repo under `relay/`. Hosting decided 2026-09-17: **Cloudflare Worker with KV** (the owner already runs Cloudflare; no container to babysit). Open source and self-hostable; Uzair runs the default instance.

## Scope

- [ ] Routes from [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490): register and delete a device, `notify`, register and delete a Live Activity token per session.
- [ ] Devices stored under `sha256(install_key)`; never the key, never plaintext. `event_id` dedupe for ten minutes.
- [ ] The delivery policy (notify or not, interruption level, `apns-collapse-id`, thread id) is one pure function with unit tests, separate from the sender. A session carried by a Live Activity does not also get a banner.
- [ ] Live Activity updates: one-second coalescing, status changes always through, fifteen-minute stale date. Push-to-start is out.
- [ ] APNs token auth (`.p8` in Worker secrets, JWT signed with WebCrypto ES256), topics for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile` and `.branch`, sandbox for Debug and Branch TestFlight.
- [ ] Deploy script, self-hosting README, key-rotation notes.

## Owner actions (not authorized for agents)

Creating the APNs key, the Worker, the KV namespace and the DNS route. The PR ships a click-path checklist.

## Validation

Unit tests green under the Workers test runner. A sandbox push reaches a Debug build on a physical iPhone. A relay-side log of one notification shows ciphertext only.

title: feat(push): enable notifications in one tap from the Hermes connection screen
body:
Part of [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490) (slice 3) and [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493) (V1, Track B step 3). **Effort:** M/L · **Risk:** HIGH. **Depends on:** [#555](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/555) (pairing route and install identifier), [#556](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/556) (device routes). Can start against `URLProtocol` mocks of both as soon as their shapes are recorded. **Parallel with:** Track A; [#558](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/558) (different files: this slice owns `BotConnectionView` and the connection models, P4 owns entitlements, the app delegate and Keychain groups).

Read AGENTS.md, `docs/agents/bots.md` and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` first. Work from a short `issue/<n>-slug` branch based on and targeting `master`. No push, PR, merge, release, new dependency or unapproved live-host mutation is authorized by this ticket.

## Problem

Users need push without a terminal: one action in Hermex that installs the plugin on their Hermes host, points it at the relay and pairs this phone.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] **Enable notifications** in the Hermes connection screen: installs and enables the plugin through the dashboard routes verified in [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490) (`/api/dashboard/agent-plugins/install`, `…/enable`, `PUT /api/env`, `POST /api/gateway/restart`), sets `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL` (default relay prefilled, self-host override), then calls the pairing route and registers the device at the relay. Re-verify each route against the live host before coding.
- [ ] The confirmation states the real consequence: this installs code on your server and restarts its gateway, which interrupts running work. It never runs implicitly. Progress is shown per step; a failure names the step and leaves nothing half-paired.
- [ ] Reverse: **Disable** removes the device at the relay, disables the plugin and wipes both keys. Removing the connection or the server does the same.
- [ ] Install and preview keys live in server-scoped Keychain, never `UserDefaults`.
- [ ] **The Hermes connection row moves out from behind the Bot Mode beta toggle** (owner decision: push also serves webui sessions, and pairing needs this login). Reframe its copy as "Hermes connection" and explain why webui users would add it. The Bots inbox stays gated. `BotModeGate` call sites today: `SettingsView.swift` (toggle row, per-server connection row) and `SessionListView.swift`.
- [ ] Multi-server: pairing belongs to one configured server; a second server pairs separately and never sees the first one's keys.

## Validation

- Focused XCTests with `URLProtocol` mocks of the dashboard and the relay: happy path, each step failing, disable, connection removal, two servers paired independently, gate off still shows the connection row but not the inbox.
- Full suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` (scheme `HermesMobile`) → all green. Signed `build_run_sim`. `git diff --check`, `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`.
- Live, only with Uzair's go: enable and disable once against the owner's host (this restarts the gateway).
- Manual plan: copy review of the confirmation, VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, light and dark.

title: feat(push): decrypt previews in a Notification Service Extension and route taps
body:
Part of [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490) (slice 5) and [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493) (V1, Track B step 5). **Effort:** M/L · **Risk:** HIGH. **Depends on:** [#558](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/558) (access group), [#554](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/554) (bot deep link), [#555](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/555) (sealed format). **Parallel with:** [#560](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/560) and the end of Track A.

No push, PR, merge, release, new dependency or unapproved live-host mutation is authorized by this ticket. This adds a fourth target: make an explicit target-membership decision for every shared file it consumes.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] A Notification Service Extension decrypts `sealed` with the preview key (AES-256-GCM, AAD from [#490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/490)) and rewrites title, subtitle and body. Without a key, or on any failure, it leaves the content-free notification as delivered.
- [ ] The extension links the minimum: crypto, Keychain read, the payload model. No networking, no SwiftData.
- [ ] Tapping a bot notification opens that conversation through [#554](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/554). An approval push only navigates; it never approves.
- [ ] Notifications group per conversation (`thread_id`); a session with a running Live Activity gets no banner (relay policy, verified here).
- [ ] Localized fallback strings; read `docs/agents/i18n.md`.

## Validation

- Focused XCTests: decrypt a fixture sealed by the plugin's own test vector, wrong key and tampered ciphertext fall back cleanly, tap payload → typed destination.

title: test(ci): trim the slowest XCTests so PR CI finishes sooner
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #501

## What changed

PR CI spent about a third of its test step in seven tests. Only the two Bot render tests are slow because of what they do; the other five are fast inside the suite and their CI times were one-off process costs (first shared cookie jar write, first SwiftUI `ImageRenderer`, first ImageIO codec probe) landing on whichever test touched them first.

- **Render tests.** Attaching a 3x capture as PNG cost ~300ms versus ~50ms to draw it. Evidence now attaches as JPEG. The fixtures test took sixteen captures whose text was never read but still ran Vision on each; those now use a no-OCR `capture` helper. The in-flight transcript probe reads only the lower half of the window with the fast recognizer (which also makes "visible at the latest edge" literal) and grows the response in 6 steps of 50 lines instead of 12 of 25. No assertion was dropped.
- **Audio preview.** A CI timing probe showed the extensionless-audio test's cost was ImageIO: a WAV header is a RIFF container, so the image downsampler probes it as a possible WebP and loads a codec plugin on first use (1.1s on CI, 17s on a cold runner). `TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModel` now sniffs known audio containers by magic bytes before trying the image decode, and the preview and export paths share that one byte check instead of each constructing an `AVAudioPlayer` (which also starts the audio subsystem).
- **Clarification failure test.** Probed on CI with per-phase laps: every phase was under 130ms and the test took 0.15s to 0.19s. It has no timeout, retry, or sleep in its path; the 10s and 33s readings on earlier runs were the runner stalling, not the test.

### Before and after

| Test | Baseline CI run 34550593519 | Local before (in suite) | Local after (in suite) | This PR's CI run 35306717479 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `BotConversationTests.testLongInflightResponseRemainsVisibleAtLatestEdge` | 36.2s | 30.8s | 5.1s | 4.6s |
| `BotChatPresentationTests.testBotFixturesAcrossAppearanceKeyboardAndLargerText` | 34.0s | 21.7s | 5.8s | 14.2s * |
| `TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModelTests.testExtensionlessRemoteAudioUsesAudioPreviewInsteadOfVideoFallback` | 16.4s | 0.05s | 0.01s | 0.04s |
| `ClarificationTests.testClarificationResponseFailureKeepsPromptAndPublishesActionError` | 10.1s | 0.02s | 0.003s | 0.15s |
| `CustomHeaderModelTests.testIsApplicableRejectsNonTokenHeaderNames` | 7.7s | 0.001s | 0.001s | 0.07s |
| `StreamingTextFadeTests.testFadeRendererAttachesThroughMarkdownUIAndAppliesStampOpacity` | 5.5s | 0.05s | 0.08s | 6.2s * |
| `AuthManagerStateTests.testRemoveNonActiveServerClearsOnlyItsCookies` | 5.5s | 0.01s | 0.02s | 2.0s * |

\* Runner-dependent. On the previous CI run of this branch (35305190696) the same tests took 9.5s, 0.6s and 0.08s. Every Bot presentation test on the final run took two to three times what it took on that one.

Summed test time for the whole local suite: 205s → 122s. `BotChatPresentationTests` alone went from 139s to 60s because the JPEG attachment helps every capture in it.

**CI `Test without building` duration:** 7m05s on run 35306717479, against 6m23s on baseline run 34550593519. The step is dominated by the runner, not the suite: summed test durations across this branch's four CI runs were 256s, 135s, 135s and 187s against the baseline's 173s, and the same commit's build step ranged from 2m26s to 3m56s. title: test(bots): room mention panel OCR assertion fails on iPhone 17 iOS 27
body:
## Problem

`BotChatPresentationTests/testRoomMentionPanelUsesRoomRoster` fails on **iPhone 17, iOS 27.0** (`6B2EC52F-94E2-4D4D-960C-327911BFA291`), on `master` at ae8c52d and on any branch built from it:

```
XCTAssertNotNil failed - Comms @chief-of-staff chief-of-staff dinbox-triage inbox-triage TIed Everyone @everyone Everyone
HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests.swift:89
```

The assertion is the OCR check for the `@all` row:

```swift
// Vision reads the monospaced "@all" as "@a11" on iOS 27; either spelling is the row.
XCTAssertNotNil(text.range(of: "@a[l1][l1] Everyone", options: .regularExpression), text)
```

On this device Vision reads the monospaced `@all` as **`TIed`**, which the regex does not admit. It is deterministic, not flaky: three separate runs (branch and detached `origin/master`, parallel and `-parallel-testing-enabled NO`) produced the identical string. Every other assertion in the test passes, including the avatar colour bands and the `@everyone` row, so the panel itself renders correctly — this is the OCR reading, not the UI.

[#567](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/567) fixed the same class of problem for iPhone 17e on iOS 27 by widening the pattern; this looks like the same fix needed for a third spelling, or a sign the assertion should not be OCR-based at all.

## Suggested fix

Either widen the pattern again, or stop asserting this row through Vision — the tag list is already asserted directly one line above (`XCTAssertEqual(completions.map(\.tag), names + ["all", "everyone"])`), so the screenshot only needs to prove the row is drawn, not what its glyphs read as.

Found while validating [#551](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/551); baseline confirmed against `origin/master` on the same device.

title: feat(bots): open a bot conversation from a deep link
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #554

## What changed

Nothing outside the app could land you in a specific bot conversation: Live Activity taps route to Sessions, and the push work in #559 needs the same destination. This adds one URL route that names a bot by identity the server owns.

`hermes-agent://bot?server=…&connection=…&profile=…[&conversation=…]` parses into a typed `BotDestination` (configured server URL, Bot connection UUID, Profile name, optional durable conversation) — never a display name, so equal Profile names on two connections can't resolve to each other.

`BotDeepLinkRouter` decides the outcome before anything navigates, from the Bot Mode gate, the server registry, the destination server's Keychain connection and the auth state:

- **Bot Mode off, server deleted, connection removed or replaced** → the link is dropped and the app opens normally, with no error and no Bot UI.
- **Signed out** → held, then resolved again after sign-in.
- **Another server** → that server activates first; the server-keyed tree rebuilds and the held link routes there, so credentials, cache and drafts stay with their own server.
- **Active server** → the session list flips to the Bots inbox, which resolves the destination against its live roster once `open()` settles. A Profile the server no longer has leaves the user on that inbox.

Opening follows the existing canonical resume rules — a link never sends a prompt and never auto-continues on its own. The optional `conversation` is seeded as the expected canonical root, so `BotConversation`'s existing changed-root rejection refuses to open a replacement chat under the link's identity; the inbox then reports that the conversation is no longer available.

No share-extension or App Intent picker work here; that stays in #488.

## How it was tested

- Focused XCTests at the router seam (`HermesMobileTests/BotDeepLinkTests.swift`, 11 tests): URL round-trip including non-ASCII Profile names, links that can't name one bot without guessing, bot/session links never aliasing, and every routing outcome above — including a link for server B while server A is active, and the replaced/stale conversation both ways.
- Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` on **iPhone Air (iOS 27.0)**: **2691 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed** — `BotChatPresentationTests.testBusyComposerShowsSteerAndRequiresExplicitSendAfterIdle`, which fails identically on `ae8c52d` (`master`) on this device and is unrelated to this change. Filed as #569. CI stays on for this PR.
- Signed Debug `build_run_sim` on iPhone Air: builds, installs, launches. `xcrun simctl openurl` with an unroutable bot link (Bot Mode off, unknown server) leaves the app running and on the session list.
- `git diff --check` clean; `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` shows no new oversized file (`BotDeepLink.swift` is 139 LOC).

**Owner checks:** with Bot Mode on and a Bot connection configured, `xcrun simctl openurl <udid> "hermes-agent://bot?server=<your server>&connection=<uuid>&profile=<name>"` warm and cold; the same link while signed out (lands after login) and while a second server is active (switches first); a link naming a Profile that does not exist (stays on the Bots inbox).

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no new wire models in this change)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
