title: feat(bots): suggest skills when typing / in the bot composer
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #551

## What changed

Typing `/` in a 1:1 bot chat did nothing, so people had to remember and type skill names by hand. Now it opens the same panel the Sessions composer uses, filled with that connection's skills.

The panel's rows come from one `commands.catalog` read per conversation, ranked through the existing `SlashCommandRanker` (via `SlashSkillFormatter.matching`). Choosing a row inserts `/name ` and the shared editor draws it as the usual atomic chip.

**Skills only, not commands.** The contract check the issue asked for first showed `prompt.submit` never interprets a leading `/` — slash work lives in `slash.exec` and `command.dispatch`, and Bot Mode exposes no general slash runner. A `/model` row would therefore be text nothing runs, and model/effort/workspace already have native controls from #479. So at Send or Queue a draft opening with a catalog skill is expanded first: `command.dispatch` returns the invocation body the agent reads, and that is what gets submitted. The transcript still shows the typed line, because the host projects the invocation back over the stored message.

Safety, in order of how much it matters:

- The catalog **drops any skill key that also appears in `canon` or `commands`**. Those are registry, quick or plugin commands; `command.dispatch` resolves them *ahead of* skills, and a `quick_commands` entry of type `exec` runs a shell command on the host.
- Only a name the catalog reported as a skill is ever dispatched, and only a `skill` reply is used. Anything else, or a failed dispatch, sends nothing and leaves the draft with an error.
- Expansion happens before any durable marker, so a failure there cannot strand a submission or drop the connection.
- `BotClient` allowlists `commands.catalog` (no parameters) and `command.dispatch` (exactly `name`, `arg`, `session_id`; a bare name with no slash or whitespace) as its third typed exception. `slash.exec` stays unsupported.

A failed catalog read is silent and retried on the next connect: the panel just does not open, and typing and sending never wait on it. The panel is closed for Steer and Redirect, where the host expands nothing. An `@` mention wins over a `/`, so the two panels never stack.

**Group rooms do not get this for free.** `BotRoomComposerView` is a separate composer and is untouched.

## Contract verification

Read-only, against the `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` pin (`3abeca16`, 0.21.2). No live mutation.

| Thing | Where | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commands.catalog` | `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` | No params. Returns `pairs`, `sub`, `canon`, `commands`, `categories`, `skills`, `skill_count`, `warning`. Skills appear in `pairs` (description) and `skills` (`{usage, origin}`); no separate read needed. |
| `complete.slash` | `tui_gateway/methods_complete.py` | `{text}` → `{items: [{text, display, meta, kind}], replace_from}`. A per-keystroke read; the cached catalog replaces it, so it is not used. |
| Profile scoping | both handlers | **Neither is Profile-scoped** (`_rpc`, not `_scoped_rpc`) while `command.dispatch` *is* (`_session_home_scope`). So the list belongs to the connection, not the Profile — recorded on the issue. |
| `/name …` as plain text | `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py` | **Not interpreted.** This is the issue's stop condition; resolved with the owner in favour of the narrow `command.dispatch` path above. |
| Transcript display | `tui_gateway/session_history.py` | `_skill_scaffold_projection` rewrites the user row's `text` to the invocation and tags `display_kind: "skill_invocation"`, so no client work is needed. |

## How it was tested

- New `BotSlashCommandTests` (16) — trigger detection, tolerant catalog decode, command-collision dropping, ranking parity, read-once, stale-reply discard, failed fetch leaving the composer usable, expansion on send, no dispatch for prose or unknown names, refused non-skill reply, no dispatch when steering.
- New `BotClientTests/testSlashAllowlistAdmitsOnlyTheCatalogReadAndABareDispatchName`.
- New `BotChatPresentationTests/testSlashPanelOffersConnectionSkillsAndNeverCommands` — renders the real composer, light and dark, and asserts the chip.
- Final full suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` on **iPhone 17e, iOS 27.0**, with simulator parallelism disabled: **2,719 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**. Includes the merged routing and Copy changes from master.
- `testScrolledSlashSkillsStayInsideTheCard` scrolls a 30-skill fixture and checks rendered text stays within the card's vertical bounds. The panel now constrains and clips its scrolling content before applying Liquid Glass.
- Owner verified suggestions, filtering, chip insertion/editing, keyboard selection, and the corrected card clipping on iPhone Air. Group-room slash suggestions remain out of scope.
- `git diff --check` clean; `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` adds no new oversized production file.

### Scrolled panel clipping

![Scrolled skill rows stay inside the card](./C987D9D6-481B-40DC-9B19-1E9C91568929.jpeg)

### Screenshots

Before: typing `/` in a bot chat did nothing — there is no panel to photograph.

| `/` opens the panel | Filtered to `/tri` | Accepted, as a chip | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![Slash panel open in a bot chat, showing the triage-inbox and write-tests skill rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bad3a8e2-dec1-4ca6-8ea9-6b019f9acbc4) | ![The same panel filtered to the triage-inbox row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31ff40eb-c0fa-48ab-81f9-5cf0e8b05494) | ![The composer with triage-inbox drawn as an atomic chip ahead of the message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9db7e8b8-1f88-4839-91b6-911d829c7c98) | ![The slash panel in dark appearance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fc5e390-8d60-4623-976f-9aedc18acba9) |

## Manual test plan

Against a real Bot connection, in a 1:1 bot chat:

1. Tap the composer and type `/`. The panel opens with your host's skills — no `/model`, `/help` or other commands.
2. Keep typing to filter; type a space and the panel closes, leaving the name as a chip.
3. Pick a skill, add a message, Send. The bot should actually run the skill, and the transcript should show your typed `/name …` line, not the expanded body.
4. VoiceOver over the rows; Dynamic Type at a large size; light and dark.
5. With a hardware keyboard, arrow keys and Return should behave as they do in Sessions.
6. Switch to another configured server and back; the list must not leak between connections.
7. Start work, then switch the composer to Steer — the panel should stay closed.

- [x] The final full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

title: feat(bots): copy bot and room messages
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #553 — see the scope note below; not a full fix.

## What changed

You could not copy a bot's reply. Long-press did nothing, which read as broken.

Bot and group-room transcripts now reuse the long-press seam the Sessions
transcript already has, rather than growing their own:

- `chatMessageContextMenu` takes a plain `[ChatMessageActionItem]`, so any
  transcript can name its own actions without owning a chat view model.
  `ChatMessageActionMenu` keeps working by handing over its `items`.
- `BotMessageActions` supplies **Copy** alone, over the Markdown source the
  transcript rendered, so a code block pastes as a code block. A Bot's history
  belongs to the host, so edit, regenerate and branch have nothing to act on
  (settled in #481).
- VoiceOver gets the same action through the existing `.accessibilityActions`
  path, and the menu attaches to the message content, not the full-width row.

## Scope: two of #553's bullets are not here

In-place text selection and "Ask Hermex" are **not** in this PR. Both were
implemented, and both were pulled back out.

`ResponseTextSelection` hosts its content in a view controller that reports no
height until its row has been laid out. Both bot transcripts use `LazyVStack`,
where a not-yet-realized row then measures short and the scroll lands on blank
space — `testLongInflightResponseRemainsVisibleAtLatestEdge` and
`testRoomSearchHitScrollsToItsSequenceAndDoesNotFollowNewMessages` both catch
it. Making the transcript eager fixes the measurement (the Sessions transcript
it mirrors is already an eager `VStack`) but costs what incident #463 describes:
CI timed out `renderFrames` and snapshot expectations across the Bot
presentation suite, and the local full suite went from 276s to 430–625s.

Ask Hermex depends on the selection UI, so it follows it out. Both want a
lazy-compatible measurement for `ResponseTextSelection` first, which is its own
piece of work — #564 already owns the rest of the quote story.

@uzairansaruzi this is a scope call, so say if you would rather hold this PR
until selection lands rather than take Copy on its own. #553 should stay open
either way.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` on **iPhone 17e / iOS 27**:
  **2684 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.
- New `BotMessageActionsTests`: the menu a Bot message offers, that Copy

  message offers no menu at all.

2. Long-press your own message in the same chat → Copy works there too.
3. Open a group room, long-press a member message → Copy.
4. VoiceOver on a reply: the rotor should offer Copy.

title: chore(dev): sign simulators in from the macOS Keychain
body:
## Linked issue

No issue; maintainer-approved `chore/` work.

## What changed

Each simulator has its own Keychain, so agents driving a fresh or erased simulator kept getting blocked on the login screen (server and Bots).

- `scripts/sim-login <udid>` reads the server and Bot credentials from the macOS Keychain and relaunches the installed Debug build with `HERMEX_DEV_*` environment variables (via `SIMCTL_CHILD_*`). Secrets are never printed or stored in the repo.
- `DevAutoLogin.swift` is compiled into DEBUG builds only. It saves the Bot connection, turns Bot Mode on, then signs in to the server, all through the normal login paths. It does nothing when the variables are absent.
- The sign-in owns its own task. The root view is rebuilt during launch, and a view-owned task got cancelled along with the login requests (found on the iPad run).
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` documents the one-time Keychain setup; `AGENTS.md` points agents at the script.

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 (iOS 27): 2719 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `BotChatPresentationTests.testRoomMentionPanelUsesRoomRoster`, an OCR assertion that reads `@all` as `TIed` on this simulator. It fails alone too and this PR does not touch that code. title: feat(watch): Apple Watch companion app — voice notes to your Hermes agent from the wrist
body:
### Use case

I send a lot of short prompts to my self-hosted Hermes agent from my phone, but the moment I actually need it my hands are full: cooking, walking the dogs, carrying gear, mid-task in the garage. Pulling out the iPhone, unlocking it, opening Hermex and typing is enough friction that I skip the query entirely. A voice note from the wrist is the natural window: wrist up, hold, speak, done, answer arrives as a notification with a spoken (TTS) or glanceable summary.

For a self-hosted agent client this is arguably a higher-value surface than CarPlay: the watch is on your body all day, the phone is not always in hand, and Hermes is exactly the kind of assistant you want at your wrist ("summarise my day", "what's on the calendar", "is the garage door closed", "remind me at 4").

### Proposed behavior

- A minimal watchOS companion app (SwiftUI, watchOS 11+), not a WatchConnectivity mirror of the phone UI. Voice-first by design: record, transcribe, send, receive.
- Core loop:
  1. Raise wrist, tap complication or app icon, hold a record button, speak, release.
  2. Audio is transcribed the same way the phone app already does it (reuse the existing dictation pipeline: server-first via the signed session cookie, on-device/SFSpeechRecognizer fallback per the server-first / on-device-first / on-device-only preference already in Settings).
  3. Transcript goes into a new chat session (or the pinned/active session) on the user's server; reply lands on the watch as a notification, with the full text in the app.
- Recording handling: on-watch recording via `AVAudioRecorder` / `WKAudioRecorder`, (cap the clip, e.g. 60s default, configurable), compressed (AAC/opus) to keep the upload small over the phone relay.
- Transport: either direct from watch (URLSession to the same server URL + password, credentials synced into the watch Keychain via the existing app-group + `HermesKeychainService`) or relayed via the paired phone (WatchConnectivity `transferFile`) when the watch has no connectivity (walking without the phone). Prefer direct-first with phone-relay fallback, since the phone app already holds the session cookie logic.
- Reply path: streamed text replies arrive via the existing SSE stream; on the watch, show text + (optionally later) TTS through the phone. A single "smart summary" notification (first paragraph, or server-asked-for short answer) is enough for v1.
- Complication / Smart Stack widget: tap to open straight into record. No keyboard, no translate, no web view on the watch.

### Acceptance outcomes

- At the wrist with the phone in pocket: raise, tap, hold, speak, release, get a spoken-agent-quality transcript sent to the agent, reply text visible on the watch within normal streaming latency.
- Works when phone is present but not unlocked/watch is standalone (watch-only Wi-Fi or LTE model), degraded gracefully (queued upload, or phone-relay).
- Voice notes appear in the matching Hermes session history on phone and web, so nothing is watch-only or lost.
- Recording flow is safe by accident: hold-to-talk, auto-compress, auto-upload; no accidental sends while wrist is down (auto-cancels on wrist-down without release).
- Credentials on the watch are read-only synced from the phone's existing Keychain plumbing (app group), never re-prompted.

### Upstream dependency notes

- No new server capability needed for STT path: `POST /api/transcribe` (multipart `file` field, `{"ok": true, "transcript": "..."}`) already exists at the Hermex pinned SHA `f1d399b4` (handler `handle_transcribe`, `api/upload.py:271`, routed at `api/routes.py:4336`), same endpoint the iPhone dictation already uses.
- TTS on watch would need `POST /api/tts` (landed on master after the pin, `1c29d6ac`, Edge TTS); for v1, TTS is optional or phone-only playback, so no pin advance is required.
- Token/request sizes: watch network calls should reuse `APIClient` from a shared target (SwiftPM local package or shared target membership), to avoid duplicating the auth/cookie/ATS exception logic. The repo's existing ATS exception for the Tailscale CGNAT range (100.64.0.0/10) already exists in the app target; the watch target needs the same.
- App group + Keychain service are already declared (`HermesKeychainService`, `APP_GROUP_IDENTIFIER` in Config/Shared.xcconfig), so credential sync should work without new entitlements beyond the watch target.

Happy to refine the acceptance criteria further; this sits alongside #524 (CarPlay voice) as part of the same "talk to Hermes hands-free" family but is independent of the voice mode track (#248 to #257), since dictation + streaming reply already covers the watch v1.

title: feat(bots): tag files with @ alongside bot mentions
body:
Fixes #552

## Problem

In the Bot Chat composer, `@` only mentions bots, so pointing a bot at a workspace file meant typing its path from memory. The epic originally excluded `complete.path`; the owner reversed that on 2026-09-17.

## Fix

`@` opens one panel: this connection's bots on top, then this conversation's workspace files. Bots stay the local `BotMentions` roster rows. Files come from the direct connection's `complete.path`, sent as `{word, session_id: live runtime, profile}` so the host completes against the session's current working directory. The contract was verified read-only against the live host before building (host 0.21.3; the shape matches the `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` pin) and is [recorded on the issue](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/552#issuecomment-5737641704).

- The Sessions `@` panel now takes an injected data source: Sessions keeps the existing `directoryList` call, Bots pass `complete.path`. Sessions rendering, ranking, caches and empty states are unchanged.
- A picked file inserts `@path ` and draws the same composer chip Sessions draws; a folder inserts `@path/` and leaves the panel open on its contents. Picked paths are remembered per conversation and cleared when the workspace moves.
- A failed or empty lookup hides the Files group and never blocks typing; stale replies are dropped by the shared generation guard.
- `BotClient` admits `complete.path` as a typed exception (`word`, `session_id`, `profile`; one bare word, no whitespace, both ids non-empty). Cancelling a completion drops the reply without closing the session.
- Group rooms are untouched: members-only mentions, no Files group. `docs/agents/bots.md` documents the panel.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on the branch head, iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.0: 2735 tests passed. Two flakes, neither caused by this change:
  - `BotChatPresentationTests.testRoomMentionPanelUsesRoomRoster` is a Vision OCR flake. It fails 2/2 on `master` with this branch stashed, while the rendered panel is correct in the attached capture; already tracked as #570.
  - `ChatViewModelSendTests.testTransportErrorChecksStatusAndFinishesWhenStreamIsInactive` failed once in the full-suite context and passed 3/3 in isolation on the same head.
- New focused tests: `BotFilePathTests` (word mapping, reply decode, unnameable-row drops, stale discard, workspace reset, section order, rooms, path-vs-mention precedence) and two `BotClientTests` for the allowlist and cancellation behavior.
- `git diff --check` clean; `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` warning-only (BotConversation +44 LOC, already over the limit).
- Owner manual pass on the simulator before publishing: `@` with and without a roster, folder drill-in, file chip, room panel, workspace move.

Evidence: approved panel design (mock A) at https://gzqoz31kkvue.postplan.dev.

title: feat(push): enable notifications from the Hermes connection screen
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #557

## What changed

Push could only be set up from a terminal: install the `hermex-push` plugin on the Hermes host, set its relay address, restart the gateway, then copy the keys by hand.

The Hermes connection screen now does all of it in one confirmed action. `HermexPushProvisioner` drives the host's dashboard routes through the new `BotDashboardClient` — `PUT /api/env` to set `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL` at the root so every Profile inherits it, `POST /api/dashboard/agent-plugins/install` and `…/hermex-push/enable`, `POST /api/gateway/restart`, then `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing` — and stores the install and preview keys in server-scoped Keychain. The confirmation states the real consequence: it installs code on your server and restarts its gateway, interrupting work running there.

- The restart drops the pairing route, so that read retries a 404, a 409 and a refused connection before its step fails. Any failure names its step and wipes the keys, so nothing is left half-paired; the plugin keeps its key pair in `plugin-data`, so a retry gets the same pair back.
- Turning it off removes this phone at the relay, disables the plugin (never removes it) and deletes the keys. Removing the connection, connecting a different account, signing out and removing the server all run the same teardown.
- Keys decode strictly — 64-hex install key, base64 32-byte preview key, https relay (http only to loopback) — because a key the relay would refuse pairs a phone that can never receive a push.
- The Hermes connection row leaves the Bot Mode gate: that login is what pairing needs, and push serves this server's webui sessions too. The Bots inbox stays gated, and the Bot Mode note no longer promises a connection row it does not own.
- Relay device registration goes through a device-token provider that returns nil until the push entitlement lands in #558; the step is skipped, never failed.
- New copy is localized across all 17 shipped languages.

Routes re-verified read-only against the owner's live host (hermes-agent 0.21.3) on 2026-09-19: install takes `{identifier, force, enable, catalog_name, ref}` and has **no** profile parameter, enable and disable are path-only, and only `PUT /api/env` and the gateway restart accept one. No mutation was run against that host.

## How it was tested

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 (`test_sim`, serial): **2,763 passed, 0 failed**, 2 intentional integration skips. An earlier parallel run hit CoreSimulator clone-boot timeouts and two render-expectation flakes; both suites pass serially and neither touches this change.
- 10 focused tests in `HermexPushProvisioningTests` against `URLProtocol` mocks of the dashboard and the relay plus a Keychain double: the full enable sequence with its exact request order and bodies, each step failing (relay address, install, restart, pairing) leaving no keys, the pairing retry while the host restarts, a host that never answers, unusable keys, a rejected relay address, disable, disable keeping the keys when the relay refuses, and two servers pairing independently with removal touching only one.
- Signed Debug build installed and launched on iPhone 17, signed in with `scripts/sim-login`.
- `git diff --check` clean; `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` reports only pre-existing oversized files.

### Screenshots

Before: the server detail screen had no connection row at all unless Bot Mode (beta) was on, and then a bare "Bot connection" link. After:

## Owner checks

1. Settings → Servers → your server: the **Hermes connection** card is there with Bot Mode off; the Sessions/Bots switch is not.
2. Open it: title and section read "Hermes connection", and **Notifications** shows the default relay prefilled.
3. Tap **Turn on notifications…** and read the confirmation, then cancel. It should say it installs code on your host and restarts the gateway. *Confirming this mutates a real server, so only run it with a host you are willing to restart.*
4. VoiceOver over the step rows, Dynamic Type at an accessibility size, light and dark.

Known gap, not fixed here: the rest of this screen's pre-existing copy (the "Setup in Hermes Desktop" section, field labels, error strings) was never added to the string catalog and stays English-only now that the screen is ungated. Worth its own issue.

title: feat(push): add the push entitlement, device registration and a shared Keychain group
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #558

## What changed

Hermex could not receive a push at all: no `aps-environment` entitlement, no APNs registration, and nowhere to keep a server's pairing keys. This slice is the plumbing that [#557](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/557)'s **Enable notifications** action and [#559](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/559)'s Notification Service Extension both build on. It ships no UI; #557 calls `PushRegistrar.enable` / `disable`.

**One source for the APNs environment.** `APS_ENVIRONMENT` (Debug `development`, Release `production`) writes both the `aps-environment` entitlement and the `HermesAPSEnvironment` Info.plist key the app reads, so what we tell the relay and what we signed cannot disagree. It is never derived from the bundle suffix: archives build Release, so **Branch TestFlight reports `production`**, which is what the relay's [APNs environment check](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push/blob/main/relay/README.md) asks for and what [the handoff comment on #558](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/558#issuecomment-5745161096) recorded. An unreadable value yields no environment and registration stops rather than guesses.

**A shared Keychain access group** (`<team>.<bundle>.push`) holding only the per-server install and preview keys. The app's existing default group is listed **first** in `keychain-access-groups`, because the first entry becomes the app's default group — putting the new one first would have moved every credential saved before this change and signed every user out. Nothing else moves to the group. `allPairings()` enumerates it, which is how #559's extension will pick a preview key by `install_hash`.

**`PushRegistrar`** owns registration across servers. It never asks for a token before a pairing exists, so an unpaired user is never prompted; it re-registers on every launch, because the relay revokes a device on its own when Apple reports the token invalid; and it fans a token out to every paired server, since one phone has one token but may be paired with several installs. A rotated token is registered everywhere and the dead one deleted at each relay. Enable stores nothing until the relay accepts; disable removes the device at the relay *before* wiping the keys, so a failure leaves a retryable state rather than a phone that keeps buzzing with no capability left to address it.

**`PushRelayClient`** speaks the two device routes from the relay contract. It deliberately does not go through `Endpoint`/`APIClient`: the relay is a different host with its own tiny, strict contract. The install key is a bearer capability sitting in the URL path, so no URL built there is logged or attached to an error.

Release-sensitive files touched: `Config/Shared.xcconfig`, `HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`, `HermesMobile/Resources/HermesMobile.entitlements`, `HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist`.

## Owner checklist (Apple portal — agents never touch it)

1. **Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles → Identifiers** → `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile`: enable **Push Notifications**, save. Repeat for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.branch`.
2. Let Xcode regenerate the provisioning profiles (Automatic signing picks up the new capability on the next device build).
3. The Notification Service Extension App IDs and the APNs `.p8` are [#559](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/559) and [#556](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/556) respectively; nothing here needs them.

No separate portal step is needed for the Keychain access group — it derives from the team prefix.

## How it was tested

- **Full XCTest suite**, XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim`, scheme `HermesMobile`, **iPhone 17e**: **2771 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped** (the three skips are pre-existing: two Photos-integration tests and one Bot presentation test).
- **19 focused tests** in `PushRegistrationTests`: environment follows the signed entitlement rather than the bundle suffix; registration gated on pairing and on permission; enable stores nothing when the relay rejects; launch refresh re-registers every paired server; a rotated token registers everywhere and deletes the old one at each relay; each server registers under its own install key; a failed re-registration leaves the pairing intact; disable removes at the relay then wipes, and keeps the keys when the relay call fails; the strict registration body and the `installs/{key}/devices` paths.
- **CI parity**: the same suite run the way `pr-ci.yml` does (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) passes. The one test that writes to the real access group skips there with a message naming the cause, because an unsigned build has no entitlements; it runs and passes on a signed build.
- **Built entitlements verified** on the Debug simulator product:
  ```
  aps-environment = development
  keychain-access-groups = [ 6GYD9C9N6R.com.uzairansar.hermesmobile,
                             6GYD9C9N6R.com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.push ]
  ```
- **Signed `build_run_sim` + `scripts/sim-login`** on iPhone 17e: the app launches and signs in, so the new `keychain-access-groups` entitlement does not disturb existing Keychain credentials.
- `git diff --check` clean. `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`: no new file over 500 LOC (largest new production file is 208).

Still open and owned by the ticket's Validation section: a device token reaching the relay from a physical iPhone on LAN and through the tunnel. That needs the portal steps above and a real device.

## Checklist

- [x] The full test suite passes locally
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (the relay's success body is not parsed; only the status is)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes — routes and the strict device body come from `relay/README.md` and `relay/src/contract.ts` in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`

title: feat(push): decrypt previews in a Notification Service Extension and route taps
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #559

## What changed

Every push read "Hermex: New activity", and tapping it only opened the app.

- **New target `HermesNotificationService`.** It finds the pairing whose `sha256(install_key)` matches the payload's `install_hash`, opens `sealed` (AES-256-GCM, AAD `hermex-preview-v1:<hash>`) and rewrites title, subtitle and body. A null `sealed`, no pairing, a wrong key, a tampered blob or running out of time all leave the banner content-free, with only `New activity` localized.
- **Minimal linkage.** The extension compiles `NotificationService.swift` and the shared `HermesMobile/Push/PushPreview.swift` (Foundation, CryptoKit, Security, UserNotifications) and bundles `Localizable.xcstrings`. It reads the push Keychain group with `SecItemCopyMatching`, so KeychainAccess, networking and SwiftData are not linked (`otool -L` checked). Its only entitlement is the push Keychain access group.
- **Tap routing.** The Profile only exists inside the ciphertext, so the extension writes it to `userInfo`. `PushAppDelegate` becomes the notification-center delegate; `PushNotificationRouter` turns a tap into a `BotDestination` (pairing picks the server, that server's Bot connection gives the UUID) and queues the #554 deep link on `AppIntentRouter`, which already handles cold and warm launch, server switching and sign-in. A tap only navigates; nothing is approved from a banner. No conversation is passed, because `session_id` is the run's live session, not the bot's durable root. Webui or unroutable taps just open the app (#561 owns webui).
- **Relay policy, verified not changed:** `thread-id` grouping, `apns-collapse-id`, and "no banner while a Live Activity carries the session" are in `hermex-push` `relay/src/policy.ts` and `apns.ts` (`bannerPush`), read at the repo's current head.

Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md` (new "Push previews and taps"), `docs/agents/i18n.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and the branch xcconfig list the new bundle ID `….notificationservice`.

## How it was tested

- `PushPreviewTests` (6): the plugin's own vector from `plugin/hermex_push_tests/fixtures/sealed_preview.json` decrypts; wrong key, tampered blob, other install's AAD and junk all return nil; rewrite success and content-free fallback; tap → typed destination on the paired server; webui / unopened / wiped pairing / no Bot connection → nil.
- Full suite via XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim`, iPhone 17: 2795 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
- Unsigned CI configuration (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) builds and embeds the new appex; `git diff --check` clean; `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` no new offenders.
- **Not yet done, owner:** physical iPhone, app suspended then terminated, LAN and tunnel. Automatic signing has to register the new `….notificationservice` App ID on first device build.

title: feat(bots): show a working bot as a Live Activity
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #489

## What changed

A bot doing work showed nothing on the Lock Screen or Dynamic Island, and the Live Activity could only ever open Sessions.

Now a running bot turn shows as a Live Activity: the bot's avatar and name, what it is doing, count chips ("Plan 2 of 5", "2 workers", "7 tools"), and how it ended. A tap opens that bot through the #554 bot route. Layout is mock **B** from the selection round (https://aaup73g509vi.postplan.dev), with the bot's avatar in the header as asked.

How:

- `BotConversation.liveActivitySnapshot` projects the conversation into one pure value at its state choke points; the shared `BotLiveActivityFeed` diffs those into calls on the existing `AgentLiveActivityManager`. No second ActivityKit manager.
- The activity is keyed `bot:<connection UUID>:<Profile>` plus the host's turn start, so equal Profile names on two connections never share one, a reconnect inside a turn re-adopts it, and the next turn gets a new one.
- Honest staleness: the bot chat closes its socket with the scene, so a locked phone shows "Not connected" / "Open to reconnect" and reconciles when the chat is active again. Background freshness is #560 and is not claimed here.
- The feed checks `drivenSessionID` before every stale or end call, so it never touches an activity a webui run or another bot took over. Bot activities are excluded from the webui orphan reconciler and removed on cold launch (learning their outcome would mean resuming the chat just to inspect).
- Chips are counts only. Reply text appears only behind the existing response-excerpt setting.
- Avatar: the app renders the photo or drawn face to one PNG in the app group; the widget reads it. **Release-sensitive:** `HermesLiveActivityWidget` gains an entitlements file with the existing app group, and `HermesAppGroupIdentifier` in its Info.plist.
- New `ContentState.chips` and `attributes.bot` are optional, so an activity persisted by the previous build still decodes (tested).
- Four new catalog strings with all 17 languages as `needs_review`. Chips avoid new plural forms except `%lld workers`, which follows the existing `%lld tools` pattern.

No wire contract changed: no new RPC, and the BotClient allowlist is untouched.

title: fix(chat): keep the clarification card on screen while the keyboard is up
body:
## Context
`ClarificationRequestInset` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ClarificationRequestCard.swift`) draws the expanded card as an overlay rising from the collapsed bar. The card takes its ideal height (`fixedSize`), and only the question and choices are capped, at a fixed `bodyHeightCap` of 300. The card never reads the height available above the composer. Found while triaging #462.

## Current behavior
With the keyboard up and the composer at its focused height, a card with four choices extends under the navigation bar and status bar. The header is clipped, so the collapse chevron is unreachable, and that chevron is the control that dismisses the keyboard. The card covers the transcript, so the only way to dismiss the keyboard is to tap the 16pt margins beside the card.

## Expected behavior
The card always fits between the navigation bar and the composer. The header and chevron stay visible, and the question and choices scroll inside the card. Dragging the card's scroll area dismisses the keyboard, as the transcript does.

## Acceptance criteria
- The expanded card never extends above the chat's top safe area, with the keyboard up or down, whether the composer or the card's response field has focus.
- The header, chevron, response field, and submit button stay visible. Only the question and choices scroll.
- Dragging the scroll area dismisses the keyboard.
- If less than one choice row fits, the card collapses to the bar instead of rendering clipped.
- Opening or closing the card still does not move the transcript. The bar stays the only layout footprint.
- The card still fits at the largest Dynamic Type size, and any new animation respects Reduce Motion.
- Before editing components, build two or three static mocks of the keyboard-up state, publish them with `html-communication`, and wait for a pick.

## Validation plan
- Focused unit test for the height calculation if it lands in a testable helper.
- Manual simulator pass on iPhone 17 and one small iPhone. Raise a four-choice card with upstream's loopback `/api/clarify/inject_test` against a localhost server. Check keyboard up and down, composer focus and card-field focus, a long question, and the largest Dynamic Type size. Attach before and after screenshots.

## Non-goals
- The Bots pending-request card.
- Restyling the card or changing the respond contract.
- The tap report in #462, unless this turns out to be its cause.

title: docs(push): describe the relay honestly in README and docs
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #562

## What changed

The README promised "no third-party relay", which stops being true the day the first push build ships. This PR replaces the absolute claim with exactly what is true, using the data inventory settled in #556:

- **README.md**: the "Private" bullet now says push is optional and off until enabled, that notifications go through an open-source relay the user can self-host, and that the relay sees device tokens and ciphertext, never message text, server URLs, or credentials.
- **docs/agents/push.md** (new): a short map of the four components (plugin, relay, app, Notification Service Extension), where each key lives, and the per-server isolation rule. Protocol detail stays in `docs/agents/bots.md`, which this page links to.

Onboarding and Settings were checked and make no "no relay" claims, so nothing changed there. The in-app push copy in `HermexPushSectionView` already describes the relay accurately. The README tagline "No middleman." was left alone: it describes the default path, where push is off. Say the word if you want it softened too.

## Proposed AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md edit (not applied, per the issue)

Current "Open at the core" line:

> There is no Hermex relay, hosted backend, analytics service, or tracking layer: agent work and data stay on the user's hardware.

Proposed replacement in both files:

> There is no Hermex hosted backend, analytics service, or tracking layer: agent work and data stay on the user's hardware. Push notifications are optional and off until enabled. They route through a relay (open source and self-hostable, `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`) that sees device tokens, notification kinds, hashed thread ids and ciphertext, never message text, server URLs or credentials.

Also propose adding `docs/agents/push.md` to the "Docs" bullet list in the same section.

## Draft App Store privacy answers (for the owner to enter)

- **Data type**: Device ID (the APNs device token). Collected only when the user enables push notifications for a server.
- **Purpose**: App functionality (delivering notifications).
- **Linked to the user's identity**: No. The relay stores a hash of the install key, not an account.
- **Used for tracking**: No.
- Everything else moves only between the app and the user's own server, as today. Notification text is encrypted on the user's host and decrypted on the device; the relay cannot read it.

One open question for you: `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` currently declares an empty `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes`. If you answer "yes, Device ID" in App Store Connect, the manifest arguably should match. I left it unchanged since the issue scopes docs only.

## Linked issue

Fixes #553

## What changed

You could copy a whole bot reply (#573) but not select part of it or ask about a passage.

Settled bot replies and room member messages are now selectable in place through `ResponseTextSelection`, the same component Sessions uses. In bot chats, **Ask Hermex** adds the passage to the composer as a quote chip, durable through `ChatDraftStore`, and it becomes a Markdown blockquote only on the way out (after any skill expansion), so a failed send restores the composer exactly. title: Make local simulator tests predictable across worktrees
body:
Local agent test runs can create extra simulator workers, collide across worktrees, and consume model turns polling logs or attempting simulator recovery.

Provide one local XCTest runner that uses the session's assigned simulator, runs tests serially within it, isolates build files by absolute checkout path, and rejects competing runs on the same device. Separate worktree/device pairs must remain concurrent. Save full logs and results, return a concise summary, and stop on infrastructure failure without automatic retries or simulator repair.

Update the local testing instructions. Preserve full-suite validation before review and leave CI behavior unchanged.

title: test(bots): two BotChatPresentationTests time out under full-suite load
body:
## Problem

Two tests in `HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests.swift` fail with expectation timeouts in a full-suite run and pass when the class runs alone. A red full suite costs every agent a diagnosis and a rerun before it can open a PR.

Seen 2026-09-21 on `origin/master` at `e4543ed` (plus a Python-only runner change, [#595](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/595)), iPhone 17e, iOS 27.0, serial tests via `scripts/test-sim`:

- Full suite: 2848 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped.
  - `testActivityRowsRenderAndFollowTheCardsSetting`: `Exceeded timeout of 3 seconds, with unfulfilled expectations: "view recovered"` (line ~853).
  - `testDesktopTaskCardReportsTheWaitInsteadOfSendingTheUserToADesk`: `Exceeded timeout of 5 seconds, with unfulfilled expectations: "Snapshot applied"` (via `awaitSnapshot`, line ~1061).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests` immediately after: 29 passed, 0 failed.

One occurrence so far, so the failure rate is unknown.

## Leads (unverified)

- Both waits depend on a hosted `BotChatView` doing real work (the view's own `.task` recovery, a coalesced snapshot read) inside a 3 to 5 second wall-clock budget. Late in a 2850-test serial run the main actor and simulator are slower than in a 29-test run. AGENTS.md § Verifying: "A test that needs a timeout to pass is wrong."
- `awaitSnapshot` arms `withObservationTracking` on `model.turn` only after the event was sent, and fires only if `turn` changes after arming. If the snapshot lands first, or republishes an equal value, the expectation can never fulfill. The `observeConnection` helper in the other test checks current state before arming; `awaitSnapshot` does not.

## Done when

- The cause is identified from evidence (repeat the full suite or stress the class, rather than guessing).
- Both tests wait on a deterministic signal, not a wall-clock budget, and pass in repeated full-suite runs.
- Raising the timeouts alone is not a fix.

Filed by Claude Fable 5.1 in Claude Code (T3 Code) on Uzair's behalf.

title: chore(ci): skip the iOS suite for changes that touch no app code
body:
## Problem

A change under `scripts/` pays for the whole iOS suite twice: once locally (AGENTS.md § Verifying requires the full XCTest suite before review) and once on CI (`pr-ci.yml` skips `Build and Test` only for its docs-only allowlist). Neither run can catch a defect in such a change, and each one is a chance to hit an unrelated flaky test.

[#595](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/595) changed only `scripts/test-sim`, its Python tests, and `DEVELOPMENT.md`. It cost a 5-minute local suite, two CI runs of 9 and 14 minutes on `macos-26`, one flaky CI failure and rerun ([#596](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/596)), and several extra agent turns, because CI outlasts the agent's 10-minute tool wait. Meanwhile the tests that do cover the change, `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`, run nowhere in CI.

Verified at `859b30d`: nothing in `.github/workflows/`, `ci/`, or `project.pbxproj` references `scripts/`.

## Proposal

1. **CI.** In `pr-ci.yml` § Classify changed files, add `scripts/.*` to the allowlist that sets `run_ios=false`. Keep it fail-closed: a PR that mixes `scripts/` with anything else still runs the full suite.
2. **CI.** Add a cheap `ubuntu-latest` job that runs the runner tests when `scripts/` changed, and have `CI Gate` require it. Check first that the tests pass on Linux (they use `fcntl`, `os.fork`, and process groups, which should be fine, but `xcrun` must stay mocked).
3. **AGENTS.md § Verifying.** Amend the full-suite rule. Proposed wording:

   > **Run the full XCTest suite before asking for review or committing a slice** when the change touches Swift, resources, the Xcode project, or `Config/`. A change limited to `scripts/`, docs, or `.github/` runs its own checks instead (for `scripts/`: `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`).

## Risks to weigh

- If a future build phase or workflow starts calling something in `scripts/`, the skip becomes unsafe. A comment next to the allowlist entry should say so.
- `.github/` is listed in the AGENTS.md wording for the local rule only; CI should keep running the full suite for workflow changes, as it does today.

## Done when

- A scripts-only PR finishes CI without a macOS runner, and its Python tests gate the merge.
- A PR mixing `scripts/` and Swift still runs the full suite.
- AGENTS.md carries the amended rule.

`Config/`, `ci/`, and `.github/workflows/` are release-sensitive, so this needs maintainer sign-off before an agent picks it up.

## Summary

On **Hermex 1.6 (App Store latest)** against **hermes-webui exp-v0.52.264**, a long streaming turn repeatedly re-attaches `/api/chat/stream` **without a resume cursor**. The server answers cursorless attaches with a **full replay of the run journal from `seq 1`** (that is its fresh-viewer contract), while the app processes such a connection as a non-replay "ordinary" restart with **all replay de-duplication disarmed**. Already-rendered text gets appended again → duplicated assistant paragraphs mid-stream; they disappear when the turn settles (the `done` path replaces the live turn with the canonical transcript).

## Evidence

1. **Server emits each paragraph once.** Run journal for the affected turn (`d642526650e643cca81c510db55fda01`, session `29a55098e66f`): concatenating all `token` events (527) yields exactly one occurrence of the duplicated paragraph; it also appears once as an `interim_assistant` frame flagged `already_streamed: true` (all 20 interims flagged). Nothing stored twice. So the duplicate is client-side re-processing, not server duplication.

2. **Warm re-attaches carry no cursor.** `performReconnectIfNeeded` (ChatStreamCoordinator.swift):
   `let replayAfterSeq = response.replayAvailable == true && !hasInMemorySnapshotForActiveStream && lastEventID == nil ? 0 : nil`
   → with a snapshot or a known `lastEventID`, the re-attach URL is plain. Observed: attaches at 21:52:17, 21:52:57, 21:53:28 with no query params; one attach in the same run carried `replay=1&after_seq=2106&after_event_id=…:2106`, so the cursor machinery exists but is not used on warm resumes.

3. **Cursorless attach = full replay from `seq 1`** (measured, webui exp-v0.52.264):
   - `curl -N "/api/chat/stream?stream_id=<live>"` → first frame `id: <stream>:1`, `event: context_status` (whole journal replays).
   - with `after_seq=8400` → first frame `id: <stream>:8401` (gap only).
   Webui contract refs: `docs/rfcs/session-sse-contract-v1.md` §"Cursor and resume semantics" (clients send the last `event_id`; clients dedupe by `event_id`); CHANGELOG #6886 (resume honored via `Last-Event-ID`/`after_event_id`/`after_seq`/`replay=1`).

4. **The app assumes the opposite and can't de-overlap.** `testForegroundReconnectSnapshotWithoutCursorDoesNotReplayFromStart` asserts the cursorless URL on a snapshot resume; `start(…, replayAfterSeq: nil)` clears `lastEventID` and marks `isReplay = false`; the text dedupe (`activeStreamReplayMatchedPrefixLength` etc.) is armed only when `isActiveStreamReplayConnection` — see `ChatViewModel.appendAssistantToken`: "Normal streams cannot contain replayed content". `SSEEvent` carries no event id, so per-event-id dedupe (the documented contract) isn't available.

5. **Frequency.** While foregrounded, the app's recovery timers force re-attaches during quiet windows (long tool calls) — observed in the server access log every ~25–40 s, as low as ~18 s. Each one ingests a full replay.

## Repro

1. hermes-webui exp-v0.52.264; Hermex 1.6; start a long turn.
2. Let a >25 s quiet window pass with the app foregrounded (long tool call).
3. Access log shows cursorless `GET /api/chat/stream?stream_id=…` re-attaches; duplicated paragraphs appear in the live transcript; they vanish at `done`.

## Suggested fix

- Warm re-attaches should pass the resume cursor whenever one exists: `replay=1&after_seq=<runJournalReplayAfterSeq(from: lastEventID)>` — the same helper used by the transport-error path (`testTransportErrorSuspendsAndReconnectsWithReplay`). Only a true fresh attach (no cursor) should go cursorless.
- Complementary hardening: carry `event_id` through `SSEEvent` and dedupe by it (per the webui contract), and/or arm the replay-dedupe path when a "non-replay" connection's first `seq`s are ≤ the last processed seq.
- The two reconnect tests above encode the old assumption and need updating.

## Environment

Hermex 1.6 (App Store), iPhone; hermes-webui exp-v0.52.264; webui restarted 2026-09-20 20:48 local; observed 2026-09-20 evening. Related closed issue: #380 (same symptom class, closed as not reproducible on 1.5).

title: (Design) Add shared Design System foundations and catalog
body:
## Use case

Hermex currently expresses typography, color, spacing, corner radius, shadow, motion, and shared component decisions across individual SwiftUI implementations. That makes the visual system harder to understand and evolve consistently.

The repository also needs one inspectable reference catalog that documents the available foundations, their accessibility behavior, their intended use, and their actual production-adoption status without implying that every existing screen has already migrated.

## Proposed behavior

Add a first-party Hermex Design System foundation consisting of:

- semantic typography roles with Dynamic Type support;
- reusable color, spacing, radius, shadow, icon-size, and motion foundations;
- shared SwiftUI component and pattern foundations;
- an in-repository Expo/React Native catalog that reconstructs and documents the system for browser inspection;
- a generated machine-readable manifest, component-selection guidance, deterministic audits, and focused tests.

The catalog must distinguish native SwiftUI behavior from browser reconstruction and must describe production adoption truthfully.

## Scope boundary

This issue is limited to **adding the Design System foundations and catalog**.

It does **not** migrate normal production screens onto the new foundations. Production adoption, replacement of existing controls, and screen-by-screen migration will be handled through separate, bounded issues and branches. Pre-existing production components and behaviors may be documented, and DEBUG-only fixtures may exercise otherwise-unadopted foundations, but this issue must not create new normal-production dependencies on them.

## Acceptance outcomes

- Foundation APIs live in the existing configuration/shared-component layers and have correct target membership.
- The retained Expo/React Native catalog runs from the repository and documents foundations, components, patterns, accessibility behavior, and adoption status.
- The generated manifest is reproducible and agrees with the catalog source.
- Catalog guidance and audits state that new foundations are available without claiming unimplemented production migration.
- Loading and other animated catalog specimens do not move before the Reduce Motion preference resolves and remain static when Reduce Motion is enabled.
- Typography and shared components retain Dynamic Type, light/dark appearance, Increased Contrast, Reduce Motion, and Reduce Transparency behavior where applicable.
- Focus, overlay positioning, accessibility semantics, localization, and motion-duration contracts covered by the new foundations have focused tests.
- The complete XCTest suite and the catalog/script checks required by repository policy are run and reported truthfully.
- No new third-party dependency is added to the iOS app, and no server/API contract changes.

## Non-goals

- Broad or screen-by-screen production migration.
- Redesigning existing product surfaces.
- Replacing platform-owned controls solely to increase custom-component adoption.
- Changing server, networking, authentication, Push, Live Activity, or multi-server contracts.
- Shipping the separate experimental Vite/React catalog.

## Implementation

PR #974 implements this narrowed foundation-and-catalog scope. Follow-up production adoption should be tracked separately after this foundation is accepted.

title: fix(bots): reconnect the inbox quietly and show loading skeletons
body:
Part of #563 (owner punch list). Stacked on #608; retarget to `master` once that merges.

## Problem

The Bots inbox showed "Connection lost. The bot may still be working." with a manual Reconnect button for any failure outside a short allow-list, including transient server-side RPC errors, and a disconnect during connect could paint that message over a retry that was already scheduled. First loads showed "Connecting…" in the inbox and "Loading current conversation…" in a bot chat instead of the skeletons the rest of the app uses.

## Fix

- `BotInbox.isRetryable` is inverted: every failure retries quietly with the existing growing delays; only sign-in (401/403), unsupported-host (`.unsupported`, `-32601`, 4090, 4130), wrong-identity and bad-address refusals show the message and Reconnect.
- `open()` no longer reports a failure the socket's disconnect callback already handled.
- The saved connection is read in `BotInbox.init`, so a first frame draws the skeleton instead of flashing "Connect to Hermes".
- Inbox: four redacted bot rows (`isLoadingRoster`) until the first roster lands. Bot chat: `ChatTranscriptLoadingSkeletonView` while recovering with nothing on screen; the status line no longer has a connection text.

## Tested

- Full XCTest suite on iPhone 17 / iOS 27 on the stack head: 2905 passed, 3 skipped. New `testTransientServerErrorRetriesQuietlyBehindTheSkeleton`.

title: Approval overlay disappears as soon as it appears while a response is still streaming — approve/deny become unreachable
body:
**Summary:** When an approval request arrives while a chat response is still streaming, the "Approval required" overlay (Allow once / Allow session / Always allow / Deny) disappears almost as soon as it appears. There is then no way to approve or deny from the phone, and the run stays blocked server-side.

**Searched first:** no existing issue matches this (titles, bodies, and comments scanned for approval + hidden/vanish/disappear/streaming phrasings). Closest relatives are listed at the bottom — neither covers this symptom.

### Steps to reproduce

*(as reported; exact device/build/server details not yet captured — happy to add them in a comment)*

1. In a session with approvals enabled (YOLO / session bypass off), send a prompt that makes the agent stream a reply **and** run an approval-gated command in the same turn.
2. While the response is still streaming, the approval request arrives and the overlay appears over the transcript.
3. Within moments the overlay is gone again.
4. No approve/deny control is reachable for the rest of the turn; the session stays waiting on the approval.

### Expected behavior

A pending approval stays actionable until it is answered or expires server-side. Stream-state transitions (a message segment completing, reconnect, transport blip) should not clear an approval the server still holds.

### Actual behavior

The overlay clears on the next stream-state transition and does not come back, because rendering is also gated on a stream being active — so the approve/deny controls become unreachable while the run is still blocked.

### Environment

- **App version / commit:** App Store build **1.6** (latest release: GitHub `v1.6.0`, 2026-09-06; App Store current version 1.6). Code analysis against `master` @ `aa7830b` (`MARKETING_VERSION = 1.7`, the unreleased 1.7 train).
- **iOS version and device:** iOS 27 on iPhone 16 Pro
- **hermes-webui server version:** `exp-v0.52.327` @ `173e673c` (the server the reporter runs; contract read against `GET /api/approval/pending`, `GET /api/approval/stream`, `POST /api/approval/respond`)
- **Connection path:** Tailscale

### Code analysis (source reading against `master` @ `aa7830b` — not a confirmed on-device repro)

1. **Card visibility is coupled to transient stream state.** `ChatPendingActionCoordinator.renderApprovalPromptForCurrentSession()` only assigns `approvalPrompt` when `pendingActionHasActiveStream == true`, and nils the displayed card otherwise (`ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:347-364`; the delegate defines that flag as `activeStreamID != nil`, `ChatViewModel.swift:5703`). The overlay is a pure function of that property — `if let approvalPrompt = viewModel.approvalPrompt` in `ChatView.swift:681`.

2. **Every stream transition force-clears the prompt.** `ChatStreamCoordinator` calls `streamCoordinatorStopAuxiliaryMonitoring(clearPrompt: true)` from five sites: `suspendActiveStreamConnection()` (`:299`), `handleTransportError()` (`:870`), `reconnectStaleStream()` (`:955`), `completeCurrentResponse()` (`:971`, fired on SSE `done`) and `finishStream()` (`:1030`, fired on `stream_end` / `cancelled` / error). `stopApprovalMonitoring(clearPrompt: true)` then nils **both** `approvalPendingBySession[sessionID]` and `approvalPrompt` (`ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:280-295`). So whichever transition fires next after the approval event wipes the card — and because rendering requires an active stream, it cannot return even though `GET /api/approval/pending` would still report the approval as pending.

3. **Empty or unrecognized approval payloads are treated as an authoritative clear.** `applyApprovalUpdate` stores `nil` whenever `pending` is empty (`ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:193-206`), and `ApprovalPendingResponse.streamPayload` returns `pending: nil` for any payload it does not recognize (`Models/Approval.swift:32-44`); SSE `initial` / `approval` events both route through it (`Networking/SSEClient.swift:270-278`). A reconnect snapshot or fallback poll that arrives empty mid-turn hides the card the same way.

### Related, but not duplicates

- **Inverse gap (same coupling):** an approval that exists while *no* stream is active is never shown at all — monitoring only subscribes when `pendingActionHasActiveStream == true` (`ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:267-271`).
- **Sibling bug upstream:** nesquena/hermes-webui#4041 (approval card force-hidden when `S.busy` dipped around stream reattach) — closed there; the client-side clearing described above is app-side regardless.

### Suggested direction

Drive card visibility from the server-held pending approval — clear only on respond/expiry, or on an empty `pending` that is confirmed against `GET /api/approval/pending` — rather than from stream lifecycle; and re-render from `approvalPendingBySession` when a stream (re)starts so a still-pending approval resurfaces.

title: Stabilize PR CI setup and expose failure details
body:
PR CI has variable startup/test times and failures that are difficult to distinguish from compiler errors or assertions.

Implement the maintainer-approved reliability follow-up:
- Pin the previously successful hosted Xcode 26.6 and iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 environment.
- Select an exact simulator UDID, explicitly wait for boot, and try fully serial testing.
- Report failed phases, assertion messages, timings, and diagnostic logs, including failures without a result bundle.
- Preserve the required CI gate and full retained suite; do not add retries or bypasses.

Validate the workflow and reporter locally, then measure the hosted run against the preceding CI baseline. A speed or reliability improvement is not established until hosted validation.

title: ci: stabilize simulator setup and report failure details
body:
PR CI can change toolchains implicitly and leave failures buried in logs. Pin the previously successful environment and summarize the failed phase and assertions while preserving the existing one-worker execution model.

## Linked issue

Fixes #623
Related: #596

## What changed

- Pin Xcode 26.6 and iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5; resolve the exact simulator UDID and fail clearly when unavailable.
- Bound worker preparation and the full suite with a 30-minute test-step timeout, leaving room for diagnostics within the 90-minute job limit.
- Keep phase timing on failures and upload setup/build/test logs alongside any xcresult bundle.
- Report assertion messages and slow tests without allowing diagnostic failures to change the test verdict. Preserve the required CI gate and complete suite.
- Make the activity-card presentation test await fixture recovery directly with automatic view recovery disabled. This removes its load-sensitive three-second startup expectation without weakening rendering assertions.

## How it was tested

- `actionlint .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` passed.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_*.py' -v`: five tests passed.
- Executed exact simulator selection and verified missing-runtime rejection; fixture build/test commands preserve exit 65 through logging.
- Ran the reporter against a real xcresult bundle; counts and slow-test extraction passed.
- Full local suite after the fixture fix: `scripts/test-sim E78D6EDB-57C9-4A73-8B9A-12116F87A974` — 2,904 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped.
- `git diff --check` passed. No production app changes.

### Hosted experiment

The explicit preboot + fully serial trial was rejected: [first run](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35738604297) took 16m52s and hit the known activity-test startup timeout. After fixing that test, [second run](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35743513196) took 21m38s and passed the activity test but hit a different display-frame timeout in room-search presentation. These runs do not establish causation or a reliability improvement; retain the prior one-worker configuration instead of shipping the unproven execution change. Xcode owns its worker clone and boot, so the redundant preboot is removed.

Baseline [run](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35689592798): 4m33s build, 7m51s test step, 12m49s Build and Test job. Latest hosted validation on `8987b54`: [run](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35749112647) passed; Build and Test took 14m30s. Both review bots report 5/5 with no remaining actionable findings. The timeout fix passed actionlint and all five reporter tests locally.

title: fix(bots): show recent chat history before refreshing
body:
## Linked issue

Refs #563 — batch 3; keep the ongoing punch list open.

## What changed

Returning to a recently opened bot or room chat showed a loading skeleton again. Recent transcripts now render synchronously from a bounded memory cache while fresh server state loads in the background. Rich text, tool history, metadata, and room system events survive re-entry; cached values never restore actionable permissions or turn state.

Cache keys include the WebUI server, dashboard connection identity, and profile/room. New ownership prevents late writers from repopulating cleared entries. Connection/profile/room deletion, cache clearing, and fresh roster changes invalidate the appropriate scope. title: feat(sessions): show a "finished, not yet viewed" state on session rows
body:
## Use case

The session list shows what is **running**, but not what **finished while you weren't looking**: the trailing
slot has three states — Approval, Input, Working — and otherwise falls back to a relative timestamp, so a turn
that finished ten minutes ago and hasn't been read looks like a session idle since last week. Push and the Live
Activity cover only a suspended or terminated app (and since #561 a push-paired server drops its local completion
alert), and completions are suppressed while the app is foreground — so a turn that ends with the app open in
your hand gives no cue anywhere.

## Proposed behavior

Add a fourth attention state — finished, not yet viewed — to the same slot: approval → input → working → **New**.
One state at a time, so row height is unchanged (`Features/SessionList/SessionRowView.swift`).

A row is unread when `lastMessageAt` is later than a locally stored per-session last-viewed watermark (the field
is already decoded; upstream has carried it since before the compatibility pin). Use `lastMessageAt`, not
`updatedAt`, which also moves on renames. Count only settled sessions: upstream seeds `last_message_at` from
`pending_started_at` while a prompt awaits its reply, so require not streaming and no pending user message, or
your own unanswered prompt would be marked.

The stream edge can't be the rule. The app does see `isStreaming` go false, but only while the list is on screen
and foreground and only for streaming rows — a run that starts *and* finishes while the phone is locked, or one
started from Desktop, cron, or another client, has no edge at all, and a completion while you are reading that
session must not mark it. Keep the edge as a refresh trigger; let the watermark decide.

Stamp the watermark while the chat is on screen, clear it on open, and seed it the first time a row is seen so a
first launch over existing history doesn't mark everything. Scope per server and Profile. Include **Mark as
read** — a row read on the Desktop would otherwise stay unread — and render the state on cached rows too, since
it is local plus a cached field.

## Acceptance outcomes

- [ ] A session whose `lastMessageAt` is later than its last-viewed instant shows the state; opening it clears
      the mark, durably.
- [ ] A completion while its own chat is on screen is never marked.
- [ ] A completion while the phone is locked, or started from Desktop/cron/another client, is marked on the next
      load.
- [ ] A session whose newest event is your own unanswered prompt is not marked.
- [ ] Never outranks Approval/Input/Working; one state or the relative time, never both.
- [ ] Scoped per server and Profile; removing a server clears its marks; cached rows still show it; "Mark as
      read" clears one without opening.
- [ ] VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, localization and non-color-only hold; no server, session or Profile state
      changes; no new endpoint or dependency.

## Upstream dependency notes

None required: `last_message_at` already ships in the session list payload and is already decoded, and the mark
is device-local by design — the server has no read/unread field and does not need one.

Related, not blocking: #421 (the event stream would update the mark without a refresh), #279 (its state filter
gains a "New" bucket), #561 / #490 (push), #239 (notifications).

title: fix(chat): resume live streams from the last event on reconnect
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #599

## What changed

When a live run's connection dropped, or the app came back to the foreground mid-run, Hermex re-attached to `/api/chat/stream` without a resume cursor, even though it knew the last event it had rendered. Upstream (`api/routes.py` `_handle_sse_stream`) answers a cursorless attach in one of two ways. With the runner adapter enabled, `observe_run(cursor=None)` replays the run from the start, so paragraphs duplicate until `done`. On the default in-process channel it sends only the offline buffer, and events broadcast to a not-yet-reaped old subscriber are lost. The stalled-stream path already sent a cursor; this path didn't.

`performReconnectIfNeeded` now sends `replay=1&after_seq=<last seq>` whenever a cursor exists. A cold process with no snapshot still replays from 0. A snapshot without a cursor, or an unparseable cursor, keeps the ordinary connection as before. Reconnecting with a cursor arms the existing replay de-dupe, the same mode the stalled-stream reconnect already uses.

Skipped the issue's optional hardening (carrying `event_id` through `SSEEvent`): it isn't needed once the cursor is sent.

## How it was tested

- New `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests.testTransportErrorOnLiveRunReconnectsFromLastEventCursor`: a transport error during a live run reconnects with `replay=1&after_seq=4`.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testReopeningActiveStreamRestoresLiveSnapshotBeforeBufferedTailArrives` now expects the snapshot's cursor (`after_seq=4`) and still checks the new tail appends once.
- Focused: `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17e> --only ChatStreamCoordinatorTests --only ChatViewModelSendTests --only StreamReconnectContractTests`: 278 passed.
- Full suite on iPhone 17e (iOS 27.0): 2928 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped. The first full run hit Xcode's "test runner hung before establishing connection" before any test ran, and the retry passed.

body:
## Linked issue

No issue: maintainer-approved follow-up from [#630](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/630).

## What changed

Xcode sometimes fails a local run with `The test runner hung before establishing connection` before any test runs. It happened once in about 90 recorded `test-sim` runs, most recently during #630 on iPhone 17e (iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.0). Diagnostics from that run show the host app launched and started up normally, and xcodebuild reached `AcquiredPID`. But XCTest inside the app logged `notify_get_state check indicated test daemon not ready` and never heard testmanagerd's ready signal, so xcodebuild's 300 s startup timer fired (`AcquiredPID → BootstrappingHang`). The passing run minutes earlier logged the same line and connected about 5 s later. Hermex code wasn't blocking: the main thread stayed responsive. It's not the known "app left attached by build-and-run" trigger either, since `test-sim` already terminates the app. And back-to-back runs on a warm testmanagerd pass routinely, so there's no trigger we can avoid.

title: fix(push): every bot Profile gets notifications, including ones created after pairing
body:
Part of [#566](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/566) / [#493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/493).

## Problem

A bot sends no notifications and its Live Activity never updates when its Profile doesn't have the `hermex-push` plugin. Nothing tells the user. On hermes-agent, plugins are per Profile: each Profile has its own `plugins/` directory and its own `plugins.enabled` list (opt-in), so installing the plugin once on the host only covers the Profiles that had it at the time. This affects every Profile created after pairing, whether it was created in Hermex or on the desktop.

Observed on the owner's host (hermes-agent v0.21.4, `d337b736aa`), read-only, 2026-09-22:

| Profile | `plugins/hermex-push` | `plugins.enabled` |
|---|---|---|
| root, chief-of-staff, dev | installed | includes `hermex-push` |
| inbox-triage, code-man | missing | `[]` |

An inbox-triage turn ("Tell me a 300 word story", 20:18) logged no plugin activity. The phone had registered the activity with the relay, so the relay held back the reply banner while waiting for progress events that never came. The Live Activity stayed stuck on "Thinking" (or "Not connected", see the related handoff bug) and no reply banner arrived.

## Goal

Every bot the user can open in Hermex notifies them, with no terminal work: bots created in Hermex and bots created on the desktop alike.

## What the server already gives us

The desktop backend that the Bot connection already talks to exposes the Profile-scoped `plugins.manage` RPC (`tui_gateway/contracts/tools_mcp_plugins.py`, `methods_tools.py:1521`, `ProfileParams.profile`):

- `action: list`: installed plugins with `status`, `installed_sha`, and so on.
- `action: install`: `identifier`/`repo` (git) or `catalog_name`, with `enable` defaulting to true (`plugins_cmd.dashboard_install_plugin`).
- `action: toggle`: `key`/`name` plus `enable`.

The plugin reads its relay URL from the root `.env` and keeps its key pair under the root home, so a Profile install reuses the existing pairing (verify this during slice 2).

## Proposed slices

1. **Detect.** For a paired server with a Bot connection, `plugins.manage list` per Profile shows which bots won't notify. Surface that where the user already looks: the bot's own screen and Settings → Interaction → Notifications ("2 bots won't notify you").
2. **Fix in one tap.** "Turn on notifications" runs `plugins.manage install` (plus `enable`) for that Profile, or for all missing ones. Copy states the consequence: it installs a plugin on your Hermes host. Add `plugins.manage` to `BotClient`'s allowed methods with a tolerant decode.
3. **New bots in Hermex.** `BotCreator` installs the plugin as part of creation when the server is paired, so a new bot notifies from its first turn.

Non-trivial UI, so slices 1 and 2 go through the static-mock gate first.

## Open questions (resolve just in time, before code)

- Does an install take effect for the Profile's next turn, or does the backend need a restart to load it? If a restart is needed, what can Hermex safely trigger, and what does the copy say?
- Install source: the git URL `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push.git#plugin` for now, and `catalog_name` once the catalog entry from #566 lands. Pin a SHA?
- hermes-webui sessions can also run under a Profile. Do webui Profiles have the same gap, and can a webui-only user fix it from Hermex at all?
- Longer term: ask hermes-agent upstream for host-wide user plugins, or for new Profiles to inherit the root's enabled plugins. That would make slices 1 and 2 a fallback only.

title: fix(live-activity): bot activity says Not connected while the relay handoff is still registering
body:
Found while debugging [#566](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/566).

## Problem

A bot's Live Activity can say "Not connected / Open to reconnect" even though the relay has taken over its updates. If the user leaves the app right after sending, the activity freezes on that state.

## Why

When the app goes to the background, `AgentLiveActivityManager.markStale()` writes the stale state unless `PushRegistrar.isRegistered(owner)` is already true. Registration takes two async steps (ActivityKit issues the push token, then the app PUTs it to the relay), and leaving the app straight after sending often beats them. Nothing keeps the process alive to finish the PUT, and the registration finishing later doesn't undo the stale write. On the owner's phone the relay did hold the activity (it suppressed the reply banner) while the widget still showed "Not connected".

## Fix direction

When a bot activity's relay handoff is in flight at backgrounding, either hold a short `beginBackgroundTask` until the registration settles and then decide stale versus relay-owned, or treat a pending registration as relay-owned. A failed registration must still end up stale. Cover it with a `PushRegistrar` double that completes after `markStale`.

Related: [#566](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/566); the missing per-Profile plugin is https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/634.

title: fix(live-activity): keep a bot activity live while its relay handoff registers
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #635

## What changed

If you left the app right after messaging a bot, its Live Activity could say "Not connected" even though the relay was about to take over. It stayed that way until the relay's next update, which for a turn without tools is "Complete". The owner reproduced this on a phone after [hermex-push#6](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push/pull/6).

Cause: `markStale()` only defers to the relay once `PushActivityRegistrar` has confirmed the activity's token. Getting there takes two async steps (ActivityKit issues the token, then the app PUTs it to the relay), and leaving the app straight after sending usually beats them.

Fix:
- `PushActivityRegistrar.awaitRegistration(_:limit:)` waits for an owner's registration to settle. That includes a token ActivityKit hasn't issued yet and a PUT already in flight. It returns true once the relay confirms, and false when the registration fails, is retired, or runs past the limit.
- When the handoff is still pending, `markStale()` keeps the last state and holds a background task for up to 10 seconds. It writes the stale state only if the registration doesn't succeed. Any newer write (the app returning to the foreground, a new turn, retirement) cancels that deferred write.
- Webui activities, and bot activities on an unpaired device, go stale immediately as before.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 6B2EC52F-… --only HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests` on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0: 100 passed, 0 failed. title: perf(chat): cut profile-switch load time ≥50%
body:
## Summary
Profile switching on Hermex paid **serial** network RTTs after the cookie flip (`/api/models`, `/api/workspaces`, `/api/commands`, `/api/reasoning`), then often another `/api/profiles` (+ possible re-switch). That made profile changes feel slow on real phones/tunnels.

This PR:
- Runs the post-profile composer config fetches as **one concurrent wave**
- Seeds the follow-up config load from the `/api/profile/switch` payload (skip redundant profiles RTT)
- Hands that seed to **empty-chat replacement** `ChatView`s via a one-shot host-keyed cache
- Loads **sessions ∥ projects** after a session-list profile flip, without dropping session `lastError` or leaking project errors into cache fallback
- Keeps the existing profile-cookie ownership fence for empty/populated chat handoff safety

## Measured (XCTest, 80ms/endpoint artificial latency)
| Path | Before | After | Cut |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold composer config load | 400ms (5 serial) | **181ms** | **~55%** |
| Seeded post-switch config load | 400ms follow-up | **83ms** | **~79%** |

Empty-chat UI path now: switch + createSession + 1 wave ≈ **3 RTTs vs ~7**.

- [x] Profile-switch regressions in `ChatViewModelSendTests` — pass
- [x] `SessionListMutationTests` profile switch cases — pass
