title: chore(release): ship one tested TestFlight build and script branch uploads
body:
## Problem

`TESTFLIGHT.md` describes a two-upload release: an internal-only production build (`internal-testflight.yml`, exported with `testFlightInternalTestingOnly`) for device testing, then a second external-capable build (`external-testflight.yml`) for testers and App Review. Apple permanently bars internal-only builds from external testing and the App Store, so the build you test is never the build you ship. The internal workflow has run once (2026-07-02); the last three releases (1.4, 1.5, 1.6) used only the external workflow. So the docs describe a process nobody follows.

The rest of the docs are out of step too: release validation still requires a local full-suite run (#633 made CI the full-suite gate), and every "push to branch testflight" re-derives two `xcodebuild` commands and a build number from `DEVELOPMENT.md`.

## Target flow

| Stage | App | Audience | How it gets there |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feature work | Hermex Branch | Owner only | `scripts/branch-testflight` from the feature branch (internal-only) |
| Release candidate | Hermex | Owner | One external-capable upload from `master`; the internal group auto-distributes it |
| Private testing | Hermex | External "Private testers" group | The **same build**, added by hand after it passes on the owner's phone (Beta App Review) |
| App Store | Hermex | Customers | The **same build**, submitted to App Review, released manually after approval (no phased rollout) |

Hermex Branch stays: it installs beside the daily-driver App Store app. Private testers never get Branch builds (Branch uploads are internal-only). No public beta link for now.

## Slice 1: one release-candidate workflow + release docs

- Delete `.github/workflows/internal-testflight.yml` and `ci/TestFlightExportOptions.plist`.
- Rename `external-testflight.yml` to a "TestFlight release candidate" workflow (file and `name:`). Keep the `master`-only check, `ENFORCE_OPEN_TRAIN`, and the `external-testflight` environment approval. Drop the typed `EXTERNAL_REVIEW` input; the environment approval is the gate.
- Rewrite `TESTFLIGHT.md` around the target flow:
  - Release gates: CI (required on every merge) replaces the local full-suite run. Keep the lint/plist checks and the authenticated smoke.
  - The owner tests the release candidate over an existing install through the auto-distributed internal group.
  - The full manual checklist runs on the **first** candidate of a marketing version. Later candidates of the same version get a focused check of what changed plus an update over the previous install.
  - Promotion: add the tested build to Private testers, then submit the same build for App Review with **Manual release** selected on the App Store version.
- Update `DEVELOPMENT.md` (checklist intro), `AGENTS.md`, and `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` wherever they name the internal workflow or the two-upload flow.

Validation: `actionlint` or a YAML parse of the renamed workflow; `ruby ci/select_testflight_build_number_test.rb`; grep for leftover references to the deleted workflow and plist. No upload in this slice; the next real release is its first run.

## Slice 2: `scripts/branch-testflight`

- One command: archive Release with `Config/BranchTestFlight.xcconfig` and a `YYYYMMDDHHMM` build number, export with `Config/BranchTestFlightExportOptions.plist`, then print marketing version, build number, commit, and branch.

Validation: one real Branch upload from a feature branch, reported by build number.

- [ ] App Store Connect → Hermex → TestFlight: enable automatic distribution on the owner's internal group.
- [ ] Confirm the external Private testers group does **not** auto-distribute.

title: feat(live-activity): hand webui runs off to the push relay
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #566 (the webui Live Activity push item). The issue stays open for presence suppression, cron delivery/new kinds and the plugin catalog.

## What changed

Leave the app during a webui run and its Live Activity says "Not connected" until you come back. Bots stopped doing that once the relay learned to update their activities; webui runs never asked for a push token.

The relay and plugin already handle webui: hermes-webui builds its agent with `session_id=<webui session id>` and `platform="webui"` (`api/streaming.py` at `b09fded7`), the plugin maps that platform to `source: webui`, and `invoke_hook` loads plugins lazily in any process. So this is app-only:

- `AgentRunActivityAttributes` gains an optional `server`, set for webui runs from the coordinator's `client.baseURL`. Older persisted activities decode with nil.
- `AgentRunActivityAttributes.pushTarget` gives one route for both kinds: bots use their destination's server and stored agent session; webui uses its server and session ID. `observePush`, `markStale` (including the #635/#637 handoff wait), `retirePush` and the pairing check all go through it.
- A webui run requests `pushType: .token` only when its server is paired, so webui-only users see no change.
- Cleanup: ending an orphaned webui activity, or finding a finished one at cold launch (`settleActivitiesFromPreviousLaunch`, renamed from `endBotActivitiesFromPreviousLaunch`), retires its relay registration so the relay stops suppressing that session's banners.
- `PushActivityRegistrar.retire` no longer lets a finished activity's cleanup delete a route that a new activity for the same session is still registering.

Known gap: a compression that rotates the webui session ID mid-turn moves the plugin's progress to an ID the relay doesn't know, so that activity goes stale after 15 minutes. Documented in `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 6B2EC52F-… --only PushRegistrationTests --only BotLiveActivityTests --only LiveActivityTests --only ChatStreamCoordinatorTests --only ChatViewModelSendTests` on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0: **381 passed, 0 failed**.
- New tests: the push target for webui, settled bot, unsettled bot and legacy activities; a cleanup running during an in-flight PUT for the same session leaves the new registration alone; the coordinator passes its server.
- `git diff --check` clean. `check-swift-file-sizes` still warns on `AgentLiveActivityManager.swift` (889 → 932 lines, already over).
- Needs a physical phone and a paired server. Owner check: send a webui message that takes a while, lock the phone right away, and confirm the activity keeps updating (tool / Thinking) and ends on Complete, never "Not connected". Then open the app and confirm you see a single Complete activity.

title: feat(live-activity): show tool count and freshness instead of filler on webui activities
body:
A webui run's Live Activity shows a filler panel, "Waiting for the next agent update.", whenever it has no reply text. That's always the case once the relay drives it in the background (#642), and in the app whenever Live Activity excerpts are off. Relay updates never carry text, only status, the running tool, a tool-call count and the start time.

Approved design (variant A): https://8q2pe4v86iy4.postplan.dev

- With no reply text, a webui activity shows the bot chip row instead of the panel: a tool count ("3 tools") and a system-drawn "Updated 12 sec ago". A finished run shows its count and "Open to read the reply". With nothing to say, the row is omitted rather than filled.
- The expanded Dynamic Island shows the bot-style line: current activity · counts.
- "Updated" appears only when the state carries a real timestamp. App-written states always do; the relay adds `updated_at` to each Live Activity content state (hermex-push, deployed with this work). A state without one (an older relay) shows the count alone, never a guessed time.
- The count comes from the relay. While the app drives a reused activity, it carries the relay's last count forward rather than dropping it.
- Reply text, when present, still wins. Bots are unchanged.

title: feat(live-activity): show tool count and freshness instead of filler on webui activities
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #644

## What changed

Once the relay drives a webui run's Live Activity (#642), or whenever Live Activity excerpts are off, the card has no reply text and showed filler: "Waiting for the next agent update." Relay updates carry no text on purpose, only status, the running tool, a tool-call count and the start time.

The owner picked variant A (https://8q2pe4v86iy4.postplan.dev): the bot chip row, filled with what we actually know.

- **Lock Screen:** with no reply text, a webui activity shows `ContentState.detailChips`: the relay's tool count ("3 tools"), then a system-drawn "Updated 12 sec ago", or "Open to read the reply" once complete. With nothing to say, the row is left out rather than filled. Reply text still wins, and bots are unchanged.
- **Expanded Dynamic Island:** a webui run with no text shows "Running command · 3 tools", the same line bots use.
- **Only real update times.** ActivityKit never gives the widget the APNs `timestamp`, and iOS can decode a state again at any time, so a decode-time "Updated" could say "just now" about an old state. [hermex-push#7](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push/pull/7) (merged and deployed, relay version `d4b7d7bf`) adds `updated_at` to every Live Activity content state. The app decodes it, and `updateTimeIsKnown` marks a state without one (an older relay) so it shows the count alone. Re-encoding keeps a guessed time marked as a guess.
- **Counts survive local writes.** Only the relay counts a webui run's tools, so app writes (reconnect reuse, updates, local end, orphan end) keep the count the activity is already showing.
- Catalog: one new key, "Open to read the reply", in all 17 languages (`needs_review`). "Updated %@ ago" already existed.

The mock's footnote said the app would also count tools locally. I dropped that: replayed stream events would double-count, and the relay's count is the one that's right.

- `scripts/test-sim 6B2EC52F-… --only BotLiveActivityTests --only LiveActivityTests --only LocalizationCatalogTests --only PushRegistrationTests --only ChatStreamCoordinatorTests` on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0: **191 passed, 0 failed**. title: feat(bots): set instructions and skip bundled skills when creating a bot
body:
Part of #493.

## Problem

Creating a bot in Hermex only lets you set its name, look, role, model and API-key choice. The host accepts more on `profiles.create`, and Hermes Desktop already uses it:

- **Instructions.** Today every Hermex-made bot starts with the host's generic default `SOUL.md`. You then have to open the editor to write the real instructions.
- **Bundled skills.** Every fresh bot gets the full bundled skill set (about 190 skills), all enabled. A focused bot has no way to start lean.

## What the user gets

On the New Bot sheet:

1. An optional **Instructions** field. When filled in, it becomes the bot's `SOUL.md`. When left empty, the host's default stays.
2. A **Start without bundled skills** toggle (off by default). When on, the bot starts with only the host's essential skills.

Duplicate Bot doesn't get either control. A clone copies the source's instructions and skills, and the host refuses `no_skills` together with `clone_from`.

## Contract

Checked against the pinned hermes-agent source (`HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` `3abeca16`, `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py` `profiles.create`, `hermes_cli/profiles.py` `create_profile`):

- `soul: str`: written to `SOUL.md` after create. Blank or whitespace-only is ignored, and the reply reports `soul_written`.
- `no_skills: bool`: writes the opt-out marker. `seed_profile_skills` then seeds only essentials. The host raises `ValueError` (error 4062) when this is combined with `clone_from` / `clone_all`.

No new RPC is needed. Both are extra params on the existing `profiles.create` call in `BotCreator`.

## Out of scope

These are also on `profiles.create` or in Desktop, but left out on purpose:

- **`clone_from` any bot.** Duplicate Bot already covers cloning.
- **`clone_all` / `clone_channels`.** These copy history and messaging-app bot tokens. Too sharp for a phone create sheet.
- **Toggling skills, toolsets and MCP servers while creating.** The bot editor already does this one tap after create. It could be a follow-up if wanted.

## Acceptance

- New Bot sends `soul` only when Instructions has non-whitespace text, and sends `no_skills: true` only when the toggle is on.
- Duplicate Bot sends neither.
- A Try Again after a partial create doesn't resend the profile step (existing behavior). The fields stay locked once the profile write has started, like the other Setup fields.
- Focused `BotCreator` tests cover the params for new bots and duplicates.

title: fix(live-activity): hide "Updated" when it would repeat the elapsed timer

title: Listen (TTS) ignores server's saved tts_voice setting
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. In hermes-webui Settings → Preferences, set TTS Engine to "Edge TTS (server)" and Voice to a Turkish voice (tr-TR-EmelNeural). Confirm settings.json shows "tts_voice": "tr-TR-EmelNeural".
2. Confirm it works correctly in the web browser client — assistant replies are read aloud in the configured Turkish voice.
3. In Hermex 1.6 (build 1) on iOS, open the same server/session and tap "Listen" on an assistant reply.

### Expected behavior

The reply should be read aloud using the server's configured tts_voice (Turkish, tr-TR-EmelNeural), matching what the web client produces.

### Actual behavior

Instead, the audio comes out in a different (non-Turkish, likely default) voice. Server logs confirm the POST to /api/tts succeeds (HTTP 200) each time, so this isn't a fallback-to-on-device issue — the Hermex client appears to send its own default "voice" value in the request body instead of reading it from /api/settings.

Tried switching Hermex's Dictation preference between Server First / On-Device First — no change in behavior either way.

Part of #566: the presence-suppression slice. Keep the issue open for cron `deliver: hermex`, the new push kinds and the catalog entry.

## What changed

While Hermex was open, iOS showed no relay push at all: `PushAppDelegate` never told iOS how to present one in the foreground, so approvals from other chats were silent too. That also meant the relay's presence lease would have hidden nothing in the app. Its only effect would have been muting replies for up to two minutes after the user left.

Relay pushes that arrive while the app is open now show as banners. `PushPresence` records which conversation is on screen: a webui session ID, or a bot's live agent session. With the new per-server **Quiet the Open Chat** preference on (the default), that conversation's pushes stay hidden except `approval`, `clarify`, `input` and `turn_error`. Pushes for other conversations or servers always show. Local completion alerts keep today's behavior and never show in the foreground.

The preference reuses #601's pattern: it is stored with the pairing and saved through the same serialized relay write, with the same rollback. It is sent as `prefs.presence_suppression`, which the relay has accepted since its first deployed contract (`hermex-push` `relay/src/contract.ts`, present since b57627c). The app never sends `active_session_id` or `active_until`, so the relay never acts on it. Older pairings default to on.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 6B2EC52F-94E2-4D4D-960C-327911BFA291 --only HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests --only HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests` on iPhone 17: **82 passed, 0 failed**.
- New tests cover the foreground rule for each attention kind, other sessions, the same session ID under another server's install, the preference turned off, local alerts, and a wiped pairing. They also check that presence is cleared only by the screen that recorded it. The relay body and tolerant-decode tests include the new field.
- Signed `build_run_sim` on iPhone 17 succeeded. Simulator UI automation timed out, so the Settings screenshot is left to the owner's check.
- Two new catalog strings in all 17 languages, marked `needs_review`.

title: Bot Mode: apply custom headers to dashboard requests and WebSocket (Cloudflare Access)
body:
### Use case

Hermes dashboard exposed through a Cloudflare Tunnel behind Cloudflare Access, used from Hermex in Bot Mode. Access accepts a service token in a single header (`read_service_tokens_from_header` → `Authorization: {"cf-access-client-id": "…", "cf-access-client-secret": "…"}`), which fits the existing Custom Headers setting nicely.

However, custom headers (#255) are only applied to the webui connection (`APIClient`, `SSEClient`, `KanbanEventStreamClient`). Bot Mode (`Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift` / `BotProtocol.swift`) sends `api/status`, `auth/password-login`, `api/auth/ws-ticket` and the `api/ws` upgrade without them, so every Bot Mode request gets a 403 from Access before it reaches Hermes.

Workarounds are not available:
- A VPN (e.g. Tailscale) is not an option when connecting to several Hermes servers on different networks.
- A secret path prefix is rejected by the address validation ("without a path, credentials or query").
- Client certificates (Access mTLS) are not supported.

### Proposed behavior

Apply the configured custom headers — ideally per server — to all Bot Mode HTTP requests and to the WebSocket handshake, the same way `Array<CustomHeader>.apply(to:)` works for the webui client.

### Acceptance outcomes

- With a custom header configured, Bot Mode requests (`api/status`, `auth/password-login`, `api/auth/me`, `api/auth/ws-ticket`, profile/plugin calls) carry the header.
- The `api/ws` WebSocket upgrade request carries the header.
- Bot Mode connects to a Hermes dashboard behind Cloudflare Access with a service token.

### Upstream dependency notes

None — the server side already works. Verified against Hermes Agent 0.21.3 behind Cloudflare Access with the header set: login `200`, `/api/auth/ws-ticket` `200`, `/api/ws` `101`.

title: chore(signing): stop other builds from claiming our bundle IDs before we do
body:
Uploading 1.7 failed because Apple refused to register `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.notificationservice` for our team ("not available"). The owner's account belongs to only one team, so another developer team already held the ID. #656 renamed the extension to `.notifications` to unblock the release.

Likely cause: `Config/Shared.xcconfig` defaults every build to our real bundle IDs. CONTRIBUTING.md asks contributors to set their own `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` in `Config/Local.xcconfig` and override the bundle ID only "if provisioning complains". When someone builds a new target before we have registered its ID, their Xcode can register it for their team first. Existing targets are safe because we registered them long ago; any new target (a widget, a watch app, another extension) has the same exposure.

## Options (owner decision)

1. **Register the ID first.** When a PR adds a target, the maintainer registers its App ID for our team before merging. Cheapest; a checklist line in AGENTS.md "Hit every surface → Targets".
2. **Make contributor overrides required.** CONTRIBUTING.md tells contributors to always set `APP_IDENTIFIER_SUFFIX` or their own bundle prefix in `Local.xcconfig`, not only when provisioning complains.
3. Both.

Recommendation: 3. Option 1 closes the gap for us, and option 2 is one sentence in CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: perf(chat): derive reasoning groups once per transcript change, not 2-3 times per stream tick
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

While a reply streams, Hermex re-derives the reasoning groups for every past assistant turn two or three times per 48 ms drain tick, and again on every composer keystroke. The output is identical each time; only the streaming tail changed.

**perf(chat): store reasoning groups and memoize per-message echo stripping instead of re-deriving them 2-3x per stream tick**

Only the tail of the streaming message changes per tick, and during streaming its reasoning lives in liveReasoningText, not messages. Yet each tick re-runs reasoning-group derivation for every historical assistant message 2-3 times: once in the didSet, then once per ChatView pass. Each derivation splits every reply into paragraphs, runs one NSString replacingOccurrences over that turn's reasoning per paragraph, and word-splits each reasoning block twice. The output is identical to the previous tick's, but it gets fresh String storage every time.

- **Trigger:** A thinking-model session with 12-25 assistant turns carrying 1.5-2 KB reasoning (one or two loaded pages), streaming a 2k-token reply at ~50 tok/s. It also happens while typing in the composer of that chat.
- **Impact (high, per drain tick (~21 Hz), per reasoning flush (~60 Hz while thinking), per keystroke):** Measured replica: 2.8 ms per call at 12 turns and 7.4 ms at 25 turns on M-series; an A-series iPhone is similar or slower. At 2-3 calls per 48 ms tick that is roughly 6-22 ms of main-thread work per tick. In the thinking phase it adds ~3-7 ms per 16 ms reasoning flush. Typing adds 3-7 ms per keystroke. After 'load older' (60-100 turns) it reaches 30+ ms per call, which means dropped frames and a stuttering stream.

**perf(chat): pass each transcript row only its own reasoning groups**

The row equality guard compares O(rows × total reasoning bytes) per ChatView pass, because each pass hands every row a freshly allocated, content-equal array.

- **Trigger:** A long reasoning session after 'load older' (60-100 reasoning turns, 120-200 rows) while streaming (~2 ChatView passes per tick) or typing.
- **Impact (medium, per ChatView pass (streaming ticks, reasoning flushes, keystrokes)):** Under 1 ms per pass for one or two pages. It reaches 7-14 ms per pass on M-series at 60-100 turns, which is enough to drop frames in heavy sessions.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:265`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L265): displayedReasoningGroups is a computed var and rebuilds every group on each read
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:203`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L203): messages didSet → recompute on every drain tick
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:292`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L292): recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages reads displayedReasoningGroups (call #1 per tick)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1360`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1360): messageContent reads it again on every ChatView pass (call #2/#3 per tick, plus once per reasoning flush and per keystroke)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1498`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1498): fileChipReferenceScanToken reads draftMessage in body, so each keystroke re-runs messageContent
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:6105`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L6105): reasoningDisplayGroups: whole-transcript pass over archived groups and every assistant message
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:6366`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L6366): strippedVisibleAssistantEcho: splits into paragraphs, then replacingOccurrences per paragraph; dominant cost (~200 us/candidate)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:6155`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L6155): normalizedReasoningKey runs twice per candidate (6155 and 6159)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:4913`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L4913): liveReasoningText flush every ~16 ms drives ChatView body during the thinking phase
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:255`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L255): non-lazy VStack: every row block is built each pass
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:289`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L289): whole reasoningGroups array passed to every row
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:575`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L575): == compares the full array for every row
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:690`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L690): per-row filter of the full array in body

## Fix sketch

**perf(chat): store reasoning groups and memoize per-message echo stripping instead of re-deriving them 2-3x per stream tick**

(1) Make `displayedReasoningGroups` a `private(set) var` assigned inside recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages, which already runs on messages, messagesOffset and completedReasoningGroups changes. Assign only when `new != displayedReasoningGroups` so the array buffer stays stable. ChatView then reads a stored value, which removes the per-body, per-reasoning-flush and per-keystroke calls. (2) Memoize the expensive per-candidate work in the VM with `@ObservationIgnored var reasoningCandidateCache: [String: (reasoning: String, visible: String?, stripped: String?, key: String)]`, keyed by anchorID or archived group id. Reuse an entry when the input strings are == (unchanged messages share storage, so the check is O(1)). Only the streaming message is recomputed per tick. The static reasoningDisplayGroups can take an optional cache parameter so existing tests keep calling it unchanged. Leave turn folds, terminalReplyRenderIDs and the trim checks alone; they measure negligible.

**perf(chat): pass each transcript row only its own reasoning groups**

Mostly handled by the equality-guarded stored `displayedReasoningGroups` from the item above, which keeps array buffer identity so == short-circuits. For the remaining cases, where groups change at stream end or archive, also store `reasoningGroupsByAnchorID: [String: [ReasoningGroup]]` in the same recompute. Pass `reasoningGroupsByAnchorID[transcriptMessage.anchorID] ?? []` to each block and to the loose blocks at :505. That drops the per-row filter.

## Measurement plan

Before/after: wrap reasoningDisplayGroups in an os_signpost and count calls per second plus total ms during a 2k-token stream on a fixture with 25 reasoning turns. Expected: ~60+ calls/s at ~7 ms each drops to ~21 calls/s at well under 1 ms each. Add an XCTest measure{} that appends 200 word chunks to a VM loaded with 25 reasoning turns, and one test asserting displayedReasoningGroups is not recomputed on a keystroke-only ChatView pass (read twice, same buffer).

Time Profiler on a 150-row reasoning fixture while streaming: self time in `static ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.==` and `Array<ReasoningGroup>.==` before and after (expected: ms-scale to near zero).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `displayedReasoningGroups` is a stored property updated in `recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages()`, assigned only when it changes.
- [ ] Per-candidate echo stripping and reasoning-key normalization are memoized, so a drain tick recomputes only the streaming message.
- [ ] Rows receive only their own groups (`reasoningGroupsByAnchorID`), not the whole array.
- [ ] A focused XCTest proves a keystroke-only ChatView pass does not recompute the groups; existing reasoning grouping tests stay green.
- [ ] Signpost count/time for `reasoningDisplayGroups` during a 2k-token stream over a 25-turn fixture drops from ~60 calls/s at ~7 ms to ~21 calls/s under 1 ms.

## Tradeoffs and risk

One more stored derived property plus a small cache to keep in sync. The existing recompute hook already covers every input, and the cache must be cleared on session switch and reload. Stale-cache risk is low because entries are validated by input equality, not by id alone.

None meaningful. The lookup is simpler than the filter, but it adds a second derived map to keep in sync with the stored groups.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **high**, effort **M**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(chat): store reasoning groups and memoize per-message echo stripping instead of re-deriving them 2-3x per stream tick</summary>

Audited at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. Traced the path: `displayedReasoningGroups` (ChatViewModel.swift:265) is an uncached computed var. It runs from `messages.didSet` → recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages (:203, :292-294), once per 48 ms drain tick (:565, :748, flushAssistantTokens mutates messages at :5170). It runs again in every ChatView pass through messageContent (ChatView.swift:1360). ChatView re-evaluates on messages, on the 16 ms-coalesced streamingScrollTrigger bump, on every 16 ms liveReasoningText flush (:4913; the reasoning flush does not touch messages, yet body still recomputes groups) and on every keystroke, because fileChipReferenceScanToken reads draftMessage in body (ChatView.swift:1498). Nothing is memoized, @ObservationIgnored or off-main. To measure, I ran a -O standalone replica of reasoningTexts/strippedVisibleAssistantEcho/normalizedReasoningKey on an M-series Mac (scratch benchmark). One reasoningDisplayGroups call took 2.8 ms with 12 reasoning turns (1.5 KB each, about one 50-message page), 7.4 ms with 25 turns, and 29-37 ms with 60-100 turns. strippedVisibleAssistantEcho dominates at 175-240 us per candidate (paragraph split plus replacingOccurrences per paragraph); normalizedReasoningKey costs about 45 us and runs twice per candidate. Some sub-claims are micro and REFUTED within this item: the trimming emptiness checks (shouldRenderMessageRow, hasTranscriptMessageRowContent) cost 0.005-0.04 ms per pass, and TranscriptTurnFolds.derive and terminalReplyRenderIDs are dictionary passes of similar scale. The compression-anchor scan (CompressionAnchorResolver.swift:137-190) only matters in compacted sessions and costs about 50 us per scanned message, so it is secondary.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(chat): pass each transcript row only its own reasoning groups</summary>

ChatTranscriptView uses a non-lazy VStack (ChatTranscriptView.swift:255), so every row is constructed each parent pass. Each ChatTranscriptMessageBlock gets the full reasoningGroups array (:289) and `.equatable()` (:321) runs `lhs.reasoningGroups == rhs.reasoningGroups` (:575). Because the array is rebuilt with fresh String storage each pass, Array's same-buffer fast path misses and the texts are compared element by element. Non-ASCII text (em dashes, smart quotes) makes this slower. Measured in the replica: all-row comparison costs 0.17 ms at 12 turns/24 rows, 0.9 ms at 25/50, and 7-14 ms at 60-100 turns/120-200 rows per ChatView pass. This is real waste, but it matters mainly in long, paged-in sessions. The equality-guarded stored property from the item above restores buffer identity while groups are unchanged (the streaming message's reasoning is in liveReasoningText), which makes the compare O(1) with no slicing. The per-row filters at :505 and :690 are trivial.

</details>

title: perf(cache): stop full-table scans and per-row fetches on SwiftData cache writes
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Every cache write runs `performMaintenance`, which loads every cached message and session into memory on the main actor to find expired rows and count the table. `cacheSessions` also issues one fetch per session. On a full 5,000-message cache this lands as a stall on send, on popping back to the list, and on the first server transcript render.

**perf(cache): stop loading every cached row on the main actor in performMaintenance on each cache write**

Every SwiftData cache write runs performMaintenance on the main actor. It fetches every CachedSession, then fetches every CachedMessage twice with no predicate: once to find expired rows in Swift and once only to count against the 5,000-row cap. Each fetch reads every column, including content and the tool-call, content-part and attachment blobs, into the row cache. The code then fires a fault on every object to read expiresAt. Usually nothing has expired and the table is under the cap, so the work is nearly always wasted. cacheSessions also makes one indexed query per session.

- **Trigger:** A heavy user whose cache holds about 3-5k rows (15-25 tool-heavy sessions opened in the last 7 days) and 200 sessions in the list. Each of these triggers the scan: every send before the request leaves, every completed response, every chat open once the network transcript lands, and every session-list load (launch, popping back from a chat, pull-to-refresh), plus rename, pin and new-chat writes.
- **Impact (high, per event (every send, every response completion, every chat open, every list load)):** At the cap, each write reads the whole table twice on the main thread. With tool-output blobs that is likely tens of MB of row data. An estimated 50-200 ms stall on a mid-range iPhone lands on the send tap, on the pop animation back to the list, and on the first server transcript render, along with a transient memory spike. Light users with a few hundred rows pay little, which is why this needs device confirmation.

**perf(cache): batch the per-session SwiftData lookups in cacheSessions**

N+1 SwiftData fetches on the main actor. Each loop iteration builds a #Predicate FetchDescriptor, converts it and runs a SQLite query, and because includePendingChanges defaults to true it also checks the pending inserts from earlier iterations. Then the function fetches the same server-scoped rows again for the stale sweep. All of this runs in the same main-actor turn as applySessions, so it delays the first frame of the refreshed list.

- **Trigger:** A server with ~100-300 visible sessions. Every load(): launch, pull-to-refresh, each pop back from a chat, profile switch, the active-row monitor's reload after a stream ends, and duplicate.
- **Impact (medium, per session-list load (every return from a chat, refresh, and launch)):** Roughly 200 extra fetches on the main thread, an estimated 40-150 ms on device at 200 sessions. It lands exactly as the list re-renders after popping back from a chat, which risks a hitch on the most common navigation. Users with fewer than 50 sessions won't notice.

**perf(cache): stop rewriting the whole window and scanning the full message table on every cacheMessages call**

Each call rewrites every row in a 50-300 row window. That means three JSON encodes per row and new cachedAt/expiresAt values, so every row is dirty for save. The call then runs maintenance, which loads every cached message across all sessions twice to find expired rows and count the total. All of this happens synchronously on the main actor, including in the send path before the network request goes out.

- **Trigger:** About 4-6 calls per chat turn: send, completion, the reload after completion, and older-page loads. The window is 50 rows by default and 100-300 after paging back. The store holds up to 5,000 cached messages after a few weeks of use across sessions.
- **Impact (low, per turn (send + completion + reload), plus each session open and older-page load):** The send path is delayed by a few ms up to tens of ms, and the delay grows with total cache size (up to 5,000 rows scanned twice), not window size. It adds latency to the tap-to-send path and does repeated main-thread I/O. It is unlikely to drop a frame for a typical user, but heavy caches on older phones may notice.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:217`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L217): performMaintenance runs on every write: called from L94 (cacheSessions), L120 (cacheSession), L182 (cacheMessages)
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:225`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L225): deleteExpiredSessions: unfiltered FetchDescriptor<CachedSession>() across all servers, expiry filtered in Swift
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:234`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L234): deleteExpiredMessages: unfiltered fetch of the whole CachedMessage table (all blob columns), expiry filtered in Swift
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:243`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L243): evictOldestMessagesIfNeeded: second full-table fetch just for .count; in-memory sort of all rows only when over 5,000
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:77`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L77): cacheSessions: one fetchLimit=1 lookup per session (N+1), then a server-scoped refetch at L84-89
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CachedSession.swift:6`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CachedSession.swift#L6): CachePolicy.maxMessages = 5_000, ttl = 7 days
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:270`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L270): every session-list load: launch, return from chat, pull-to-refresh
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:1500`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L1500): network transcript load on chat open, same main-actor job that applies the transcript
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:2509`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L2509): send path: runs synchronously before client.startChat, adds to tap-to-send latency
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:2677`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L2677): cacheCurrentMessages, reached from cacheCompletedResponse (L2685) after every finished response
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:74`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L74): upsert loop: one cachedSession(cacheKey:) fetch per session
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:268`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L268): per-row FetchDescriptor with #Predicate on cacheKey, fetchLimit 1
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:84`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L84): server-scoped fetch of all CachedSession rows already happens here for the stale sweep
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:146`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L146): cacheMessages already uses the single-fetch dictionary pattern (#309) to mirror
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:997`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L997): duplicate calls load() then cacheSessions again
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:303`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L303): returnRefreshID task reloads on every return from a chat
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:163`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L163): upsert loop: apply() on every existing row, no change check
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CachedMessage.swift:60`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CachedMessage.swift#L60): apply(): three new JSONEncoder() encodes, and cachedAt/expiresAt are always bumped, so every row is dirty
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:179`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L179): performMaintenance + save run on every call
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:242`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L242): evictOldestMessagesIfNeeded fetches ALL rows again just to count them
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:2683`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L2683): cacheCompletedResponse after each response (ChatView.swift:2711)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:1747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L1747): after loadOlderMessages, and the window grows by 50 per page

## Fix sketch

**perf(cache): stop loading every cached row on the main actor in performMaintenance on each cache write**

In CacheStore: (1) Replace deleteExpiredSessions and deleteExpiredMessages with store-side deletes: `try context.delete(model: CachedMessage.self, where: #Predicate { $0.expiresAt <= now })`, and the same for CachedSession. (2) In evictOldestMessagesIfNeeded, call `let count = try context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<CachedMessage>())`. Only when count > maxMessages, fetch with `sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.cachedAt), SortDescriptor(\.timestamp), SortDescriptor(\.sortIndex)]` and `fetchLimit = overflow`, then delete those rows. (3) Optionally add a static `lastMaintenance: Date?` and skip maintenance if it ran less than ~10 minutes ago. (1) and (2) alone remove almost all of the cost, so treat (3) as optional. (4) In cacheSessions, build `[cacheKey: CachedSession]` from the server-scoped fetch at L84-89, move that fetch above the loop, and use the dictionary for both the upsert and the stale sweep. This mirrors what #309 did in cacheMessages.

**perf(cache): batch the per-session SwiftData lookups in cacheSessions**

In cacheSessions, move the server-scoped fetch (L84-88) above the loop and build `let cachedByKey = existing.reduce(into: [String: CachedSession]()) { $0[$1.cacheKey] = $1 }`. In the loop, replace `try cachedSession(cacheKey:in:)` with `cachedByKey[cacheKey]`. Compute the stale set from the same `existing` array (`existing.filter { !freshKeys.contains($0.cacheKey) }`). Newly inserted rows aren't in the snapshot and their keys are fresh, so the sweep is still correct. This mirrors cacheMessages L141-180. Keep apply() as is so the TTL semantics don't change.

**perf(cache): stop rewriting the whole window and scanning the full message table on every cacheMessages call**

1) In performMaintenance, replace the two full fetches with a predicate fetch `#Predicate { $0.expiresAt <= now }` for expiry and `context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<CachedMessage>())` for eviction. Fetch and sort only when the count is over maxMessages. 2) In the upsert loop, skip apply() when the row's content, reasoning, role and messageId match and toolCallsData?.count equals the new toolCalls count. Bump cachedAt/expiresAt only when the existing cachedAt is more than about an hour old, so LRU ordering stays roughly right. 3) Optional: on send, insert only the optimistic row instead of recaching the whole window, because the completion and reload recache soon after.

## Measurement plan

Add os_signpost intervals around performMaintenance, cacheMessages and cacheSessions. Seed a store with 5,000 CachedMessage rows (about 2-8 KB content, some with toolCallsData) across 20 sessions, plus 200 CachedSession rows. Before: Time Profiler plus the Core Data/SwiftData instrument on device should show two full-table fetches per write and main-thread time in the tens to hundreds of ms for one sendMessage and one SessionListViewModel.load. After: one COUNT query and no row materialization when nothing is expired or over the cap, with the maintenance interval under 2 ms. For a regression check, add an XCTest `measure {}` around CacheStore.cacheMessages(50 messages) on an in-memory container seeded to 5,000 rows.

Add os_signpost intervals around CacheStore.cacheSessions and around the synchronous part of SessionListViewModel.load after the network await. Run a URLProtocol mock returning 200 sessions on a real iPhone and compare the interval before and after in Instruments (Points of Interest plus Time Profiler). With `-com.apple.CoreData.SQLDebug 1`, the SELECT count per load should drop from ~201 to 1. Expect the interval to shrink by the per-fetch overhead times N; the save's UPDATE cost stays.

Add os_signpost around CacheStore.cacheMessages. Seed an in-memory store with 5,000 CachedMessage rows across 100 sessions and a 100-message tool-heavy session. Run Time Profiler on sendMessage, measuring main-thread time from tap to the startChat URLSessionTask resume. Before: expect the full-table fetch plus a 100-row save per call. After: expect a predicate fetch, one count query and only the changed rows saved. Also record the main-thread ms per cacheMessages call.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expiry uses store-side `context.delete(model:where:)`; eviction uses `fetchCount` and only fetches `fetchLimit = overflow` sorted rows when over the cap.
- [ ] `cacheSessions` builds one keyed dictionary from a single server-scoped fetch instead of per-session lookups.
- [ ] Unchanged message rows are not rewritten on every `cacheMessages` call.
- [ ] Existing `CacheStoreTests` (including the cross-server isolation tests) pass; a new test covers eviction at the cap with a count-only path.
- [ ] Time Profiler on device with a 5,000-row cache shows no multi-row fetch on the main thread per write.

## Tradeoffs and risk

A batch delete skips per-object delete processing. That is harmless because CachedSession and CachedMessage have no relationships or delete rules. If maintenance is throttled, the table can briefly go past 5,000 rows or keep already-expired rows. Reads already filter on expiresAt > now (CacheStore.swift:19, L40), so users never see the difference.

None worth noting. It's the same pattern already shipped for messages, and one server-scoped fetch materializes the same rows the loop would have touched anyway. Skipping apply() for unchanged rows would also cut the save, but it changes TTL-refresh behavior, so leave it out of this change.

A field-level equality check can miss a server-side edit hidden inside toolCalls or attachments with the same count. Compare the encoded byte length or a hash if that matters. Bumping cachedAt less often makes eviction order approximate within the throttle window. Predicate fetches need an index on expiresAt to stay cheap; without one it is still a scan, but it no longer loads every object.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE**, impact **high**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(cache): stop loading every cached row on the main actor in performMaintenance on each cache write</summary>

Checked at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. CacheStore.performMaintenance (CacheStore.swift:217-221) runs on every cacheSessions (L94), cacheSession (L120) and cacheMessages (L182) call, and nothing throttles it. Nothing caches or rate-limits it either, and it is not moved off the main actor anywhere: every function is @MainActor and runs on the view's mainContext. deleteExpiredSessions (L225) fetches the whole CachedSession table with no predicate. deleteExpiredMessages (L234) fetches the whole CachedMessage table with no predicate and filters expiresAt in Swift. evictOldestMessagesIfNeeded (L243-244) runs a second unfiltered fetch just to take .count; it sorts in memory only when the table is over the cap. Core Data's default fetch reads every column into the row cache, so both message fetches read content, reasoning, toolCallsData, contentPartsData and attachmentsData for every row. Opening the objects and reading expiresAt/cachedAt then fires faults on each one. The cap is 5,000 rows (CachedSession.swift:6) and the TTL is 7 days (L5). cacheMessages saves the whole loaded transcript. Tool-heavy agent sessions often run 200-400 rows, so opening 15-25 such sessions in a week fills the table. That takes a heavy user and is not rare. The #309 fix batched only the per-session upsert lookups; maintenance was never touched. The calls sit on hot paths: every session-list load (SessionListViewModel.swift:270, i.e. launch, return from chat, pull-to-refresh), every network transcript load on chat open (ChatViewModel.swift:1500, same main-actor job that applies the server transcript), the send path before client.startChat (ChatViewModel.swift:2509), and response completion (L2685 via L2677). Secondary claim: the per-session lookup in cacheSessions (L74-82) really is N+1. It uses one fetchLimit=1 query per session on the unique, indexed cacheKey, then refetches the same server's rows at L84-89. With 200 sessions that is ~200 small SQLite round trips on main per list load. Real, but a smaller cost than the full-table scans. I have not measured the size of the stall, so I left the high impact rating in place but flagged it for Instruments.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(cache): batch the per-session SwiftData lookups in cacheSessions</summary>

Traced at HEAD 952c747. CacheStore.cacheSessions (CacheStore.swift:61-96) loops over every cacheable session and calls the private cachedSession(cacheKey:) helper (L268-276). That helper builds a new FetchDescriptor with a #Predicate on the unique cacheKey and fetchLimit 1, so the loop runs one SwiftData fetch per session. The same function then fetches every CachedSession for the server anyway (L84-89) for the stale sweep. cacheMessages (L141-155) already uses the single-fetch dictionary pattern from #309; the session path never got it. I checked whether the path is hot. SessionListViewModel.load (SessionListViewModel.swift:229) is @MainActor and calls cacheSessions at L270 right after applySessions, all in the same main-actor turn, so the fresh rows can't render until the cache write finishes. load() runs on initial launch, on pull-to-refresh (SessionListView.swift:657), on every return from a chat (the returnRefreshID task at SessionListView.swift:303-306 calls refreshSessionsAndActiveProfile, then loadSessions, then load), after a profile switch, and when the active-row monitor reloads (SessionListView.swift:1187-1208). duplicate (SessionListViewModel.swift:997) runs the path a second time. Data size is realistic: upstream GET /api/sessions returns every visible non-archived session with no page limit (routes.py:14180+), so heavy users send 100-300 rows every time. Nothing caches or debounces this, and it doesn't run off the main actor. One claim needs correcting: every row is dirty on every load because apply() writes cachedAt and expiresAt. That comes from TTL-refresh semantics, not from the lookup, so batching won't remove the 200-row UPDATE on save. It only removes the N fetches (predicate translation plus a SQLite round-trip each). A separate cost is performMaintenance (L216-265), which fetches all CachedMessage rows (up to 5,000) twice per call. That is the auditor's 'finding 1' and is not part of this cluster. Magnitude is uncertain without a device trace (my estimate is ~0.2-0.5 ms per fetch, so roughly 40-150 ms for 200 sessions), but the waste is real and on a per-navigation path.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(cache): stop rewriting the whole window and scanning the full message table on every cacheMessages call</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The waste is real. CacheStore.cacheMessages (CacheStore.swift:125-181) calls CachedMessage.apply (CachedMessage.swift:60-91) on every row in the in-memory window. apply creates a new JSONEncoder for toolCalls, contentParts and attachments, and always sets cachedAt/expiresAt, so every row is dirty and context.save() writes all of them. It runs synchronously on the main actor. On send, it runs between messages.append and `await client.startChat` (ChatViewModel.swift:2509), so the request goes out later. It also runs after loadMessages (1500), loadOlderMessages (1747), completion (ChatView.swift:2711 → ChatViewModel.swift:2683), send rollback (2528/2542/2561) and the reload paths at 4102/4209. Nothing is memoized or debounced, and no @Query observes these rows, so the cost is CPU and I/O, not view invalidation. Two things lower the magnitude. First, the window is 50 rows (messagePageLimit = 50, ChatViewModel.swift:201) and only grows by 50 per older page. Most per-message encodes are small, because tool results come back as plain `content` strings, not encoded JSON. Second, the claim misses the likely bigger cost in the same call: performMaintenance (CacheStore.swift:225-261) fetches every CachedMessage across all sessions and servers. It does this twice, once in deleteExpiredMessages and once in evictOldestMessagesIfNeeded, then filters on expiresAt in memory. That is up to 5,000 rows (CachePolicy.maxMessages) on every cacheMessages call and every cacheSession call. So skipping apply alone saves little. Also, cachedAt is the LRU key for eviction, so skipping the bump entirely would change eviction order. How many ms this adds on the send path cannot be known without a profile, so the verdict is PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED.

</details>

title: perf(launch): restore the last-opened chat without waiting for the projects and profile requests
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

On cold launch the last-opened chat is restored only after the session list, projects, and active-profile requests all finish in series. Over a tunnel that adds two extra round trips (about 200-400 ms) before the user sees their chat.

On a cold launch the remembered chat opens only after three requests finish one after another: GET /api/sessions (plus a main-actor SwiftData upsert of every session row), then GET /api/projects, then GET /api/profiles. Only the first one supplies data that restore uses. ChatView's own cache-first render and its GET /api/session call start only after all three, so a transcript already in SwiftData stays hidden behind about 3 RTTs, the TLS setup and a 200-session JSON decode.

- **Trigger:** Every cold launch with a remembered last session, over a Cloudflare tunnel (~100-200 ms RTT) with ~200 sessions.
- **Impact (high, once per cold launch (and per server switch, since .id(server) re-runs the initial .task)):** Over a tunnel, restore waits roughly 200-400 ms longer than it needs to (the projects and profiles RTTs). With a cache-first restore the whole ~0.5-1 s wait for the network list disappears, because the cached transcript can paint almost at once. Tunnel users see this on every cold launch. LAN users gain only a few tens of ms.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:280`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L280): initial .task awaits SessionListInitialLoad.run, then restores at L292
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1103`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L1103): refreshSessionsAndActiveProfile: loadSessions, then loadActiveProfile, one after the other
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1211`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L1211): loadSessions: viewModel.load, then loadProjects, one after the other
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1503`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L1503): SessionListInitialLoad.run gates restore on the whole refresh
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:255`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L255): load() awaits client.sessions(); the cache is read only in the catch branch (L283)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:269`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L269): CacheStore.cacheSessions runs on the main actor before load returns
- [`HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift:74`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift#L74): one SwiftData fetch per session, plus a full fetch, maintenance and save
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1487`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L1487): restoreLastSelectedSessionIfNeeded needs only viewModel.sessions
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionNavigationState.swift:94`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionNavigationState.swift#L94): restoreIfNeeded looks for lastSelectedSessionID in the sessions array
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListComponents.swift:422`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListComponents.swift#L422): skeleton rows while isLoading && sessions.isEmpty

## Fix sketch

Step 1 (S, no semantic change): in SessionListInitialLoad.run / the initial .task, restore as soon as the deep link has resolved and `viewModel.load` has returned. Then run `loadProjects()` and `loadActiveProfile()` together with `async let`. For example, split refreshSessionsAndActiveProfile into `await viewModel.load(...)`, restore, then `async let p = viewModel.loadProjects(); async let a = viewModel.loadActiveProfile(); _ = await (p, a)`. Keep the `!isViewingCachedData` guard on projects. Step 2 (M, optional, bolder): before the network load, read `CacheStore.cachedSessions(serverURL:in:)` once and call `navigationState.restoreIfNeeded(from: cached, clearsMissingSelection: false, pendingDeepLinkedSessionID:)`, but only when no deep link or webui push is pending. Do not put the cached rows into viewModel.sessions. After the network list arrives, if the restored session is missing, call `navigationState.remove(sessionID:)` to pop it. `clearsMissingSelection` alone only clears the stored ID and does not pop the pushed view.

## Measurement plan

Put an os_signpost interval from the start of the SessionListView initial .task to the first ChatTranscriptView render that has messages. Cold launch 10 times with Network Link Conditioner at 150 ms delay, 200 sessions, a cached 300-message last session. Expected: before is about 3 RTT + TLS + decode (~0.7-1.2 s). After step 1 it should drop by about 2 RTTs (~300 ms). After step 2 the transcript should paint in under 100 ms from the task start. Also check with Instruments' SwiftUI/Hangs that ChatView's network load starts before /api/projects returns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore runs as soon as the deep link resolves and `viewModel.load` returns; projects and active profile load concurrently afterwards with `async let`.
- [ ] Deep-link precedence over stored selection is unchanged (existing `SessionListInitialLoad` tests pass).
- [ ] A focused test with a scripted slow projects/profile response shows restore does not wait on them.
- [ ] Optional follow-up noted in the issue, not required: cache-first restore before the network list.

## Tradeoffs and risk

Step 1: the projects and profile sections can fill in a moment after the chat is pushed, and error banners can show up in a different order. Step 2: the cached session summary can be up to the cache TTL out of date. A session deleted or archived on another device opens briefly and then gets popped, and that pop needs its own handling. It also adds a second restore point that has to respect deep link and push precedence.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **high**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Traced at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The initial `.task` (SessionListView.swift:275-293) awaits `SessionListInitialLoad.run` (L1503-1513). That awaits `refreshSessionsAndActiveProfile` (L1103-1107), which runs `loadSessions` (L1211-1221: `viewModel.load`, then `viewModel.loadProjects`) and then `viewModel.loadActiveProfile` (SessionListViewModel.swift:312). All three run one after another. Only then does `restoreLastSelectedSessionIfNeeded` run (L1487-1495). `restoreIfNeeded` (SessionNavigationState.swift:94-115) only needs `viewModel.sessions`, so the /api/projects and /api/profiles requests hold up navigation for nothing. `load()` (SessionListViewModel.swift:229-310) goes to the network first. `CacheStore.cachedSessions` is read only in the failure branch (L283), so a healthy launch never uses the cached list. ChatViewModel.loadMessages (ChatViewModel.swift:1398+) already paints from cache first, so the transcript is ready as soon as the view is pushed. Nothing on this path is memoized or run in parallel. One correction: the list shows skeleton rows (SessionListComponents.swift:422), not a spinner. Secondary cost: `CacheStore.cacheSessions` (CacheStore.swift:61-96) runs on the main actor between requests. It does one fetch per session, one full fetch, performMaintenance and a save. That is roughly 200 fetches for 200 sessions, which is real but smaller than the network waits. On LAN (<10 ms RTT) the gain is small. Over a Cloudflare tunnel it is 2 or more extra RTTs every cold launch.

</details>

title: perf(kanban): keep the loaded Board when returning from Card detail
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Every pop back from Card detail re-runs an unguarded `.task { await model.load() }`, which blanks the Board, shows a spinner for 0.5-1.2 s, loses scroll position, fires 5 GETs, and reconnects the event stream.

The Board is a pushed destination, and Card detail is pushed on top of it. When the user pops back, the Board appears again and its unguarded `.task` calls `load()`. `load()` is written as a first-time cold start. It tears down all Board state, shows the full-screen 'Loading Kanban' spinner, and runs config, boards, then board one after another before anything is shown again. Stats and assignees come after that, and the SSE stream reconnects from cursor 0. The List is rebuilt from scratch, so the scroll position is lost, and a pending archive undo is dropped.

- **Trigger:** The user opens any Card on a Board (realistically 50-300 Cards) and taps Back, on iPhone or iPad. This happens on every Card visit, which is the most common Kanban round trip. Over a Cloudflare tunnel each GET takes roughly 150-400 ms, so the spinner stays up for about 0.5-1.2 s.
- **Impact (high, Every pop back from Card detail, and also any other push/pop over the Board.):** Every Card visit ends with a visible spinner flash and a 0.5-1.2 s blank Board. The user loses their scroll position in a long Board, and the app makes 5 redundant GETs plus an SSE reconnect. It happens on every back-navigation for anyone who uses Kanban.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:2362`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L2362): The unguarded `.task { await model.load() }` in KanbanView runs again every time the Board reappears after a pop.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:203`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L203): `navigationDestination(item: $presentedCardID)` pushes Card detail onto the same stack, so the Board disappears and then reappears.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:455`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L455): The compact NavigationStack that hosts KanbanView. Card detail is pushed onto this stack.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:884`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L884): `load()` is a cold start. It clears archive undo (L891-892), resets the live cursor (L894), sets `state = .checking` (L900) and nils snapshot/boards/stats (L901-907).
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:914`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L914): Three serial GETs (config, boards, board) run before the Board returns. Stats and assignees follow in loadSupplementaryReads (L2584).
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:168`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L168): `.idle`/`.checking` replaces the Board List with loadingContent, so the scroll position is lost.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2383`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2383): startStream already resumes from `since: liveCursor`, so the onAppear `setVisible(true)` catches up on missed events without a reload.

## Fix sketch

In KanbanView (KanbanLabView.swift:2362), cold-load only when nothing is loaded: `.task { if model.snapshot == nil { await model.load() } }`. This matches the existing `retry()` rule. A load that was cancelled mid-flight or failed leaves snapshot nil, so it still reloads. When a snapshot exists, KanbanStatusFocusView's onAppear already calls `setVisible(true)`, which restarts the live stream from the saved `liveCursor` and catches up on changes made while the Card was open. Nothing else is needed, and pull-to-refresh still reconciles fully.

## Measurement plan

In a Debug build, count URLProtocol requests or add an os_signpost around `KanbanFeatureState.load()`, or use the Instruments Network template. Open a Card on a 100+ Card Board, tap Back, and repeat 5 times. Before: 5 GETs per return (5 load() calls total), with the 'Loading Kanban' spinner shown each time and the scroll reset to the top. After: load() is called once in total, each return makes 0 REST GETs and one SSE reconnect with `since=<cursor>`, no spinner appears, and the scroll position is kept.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Board cold-loads only when `model.snapshot == nil`; returning from Card detail keeps rows and scroll position.
- [ ] Changes made while the Card was open still arrive through the live stream's saved cursor.
- [ ] Archive-from-detail undo survives the return to the Board (today the reload wipes `archiveUndo`).
- [ ] `KanbanFeatureStateTests` cover: no reload on re-appear with a snapshot, reload when the snapshot is nil.

## Tradeoffs and risk

A pop-back no longer re-validates the Kanban configuration or the Board list. The SSE catch-up, the scene-active reconcile (setSceneActive) and pull-to-refresh already cover those changes. As a side effect, the guard also stops the pop from silently clearing a pending archive undo, which is a small non-perf fix in its own right.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **high**, effort **S**. Mechanism is certain from the code; a device trace is still the before/after gate.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

I traced the code at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. KanbanView (KanbanLabView.swift:2348-2365) wraps KanbanStatusFocusView in a `.task { await model.load() }` with no guard. On iPhone, SessionListView.swift:455-459 pushes KanbanView into the compact NavigationStack. KanbanStatusFocusView then pushes KanbanCardDetailView into the same stack via `.navigationDestination(item: $presentedCardID)` (KanbanLabView.swift:203-205). On iPad it goes into the detail NavigationStack (SessionListView.swift:448). Pushing a Card makes the Board disappear, and popping back makes it appear again, so SwiftUI restarts the `.task` and calls `load()` again. The view already depends on this lifecycle: its onDisappear calls setVisible(false) (L246-249), and it restores focus after `presentedCardID` returns to nil (L271-279). Nothing makes `load()` idempotent. KanbanFeatureState.swift:884-910 cancels archive undo, calls `resetLiveUpdates(clearCursor: true)`, sets `state = .checking`, and nils configuration, boards, snapshot, stats and assigneeHistory. The body switch (KanbanLabView.swift:167-169) then replaces the whole Board List with the 'Loading Kanban' spinner, which throws away its scroll position. Before the Board comes back, three GETs run one after another (kanbanConfiguration, kanbanBoards, kanbanBoard at L914-947). Two more serial GETs follow, stats and assignees (loadSupplementaryReads, L2584-2604), and then the live-update SSE stream reconnects from cursor 0. Decoding is off main because APIClient is an actor, so the cost is the visible spinner, the lost scroll and the wasted round trips, not CPU. The existing handling does not cover this. `retry()` has the snapshot guard, but `.task` does not use it. onAppear's `setVisible(true)` would already resume the stream from the saved `liveCursor` (startStream passes `since: liveCursor`, L2383-2390), so the cold reload is pure waste. This is not on the Already fixed list. One correction to the claim: the spinner lasts 3 serial round trips, not 5. Stats and assignees load after the Board is back on screen.

</details>
