title: perf(chat): keep transcript environment closures stable so settled rows skip stream ticks
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

ChatView and ChatTranscriptView inject `\.openURL` and `\.chatDisclosureToggled` as closures rebuilt on every body pass. SwiftUI treats them as changed each time, so every tool group, log row, marker card, and settled reply's nested hosting controller updates on every stream tick and keystroke, despite `.equatable()` rows.

Two environment values are closures rebuilt on every parent body pass: `\.openURL` in ChatView and `\.chatDisclosureToggled` in ChatTranscriptView. SwiftUI cannot prove closures equal, so every view that reads those keys is invalidated each pass. That includes ResponseTextSelection, which reads the whole environment through `\.self`. The `.equatable()` row wrapper does not block environment propagation. So on each ChatView pass, every tool group re-formats all its calls and every settled reply's nested UIHostingController gets a new AnyView root and re-diffs its markdown subtree.

- **Trigger:** Streaming a reply in an open session. The paced drain mutates `messages` about every word-cadence tick (~20 Hz), and ChatView.body re-runs each time. Also every composer keystroke, because `draftMessage` is read in ChatView.body. Realistic load: a default 50-message page with about 10-20 settled replies and 20-40 tool calls. Heavier sessions paged back to 150+ messages scale linearly.
- **Impact (medium, per stream flush tick (~20 Hz while streaming) and per composer keystroke):** Work that scales with the transcript on the main thread at stream-tick and keystroke frequency. It likely contributes to hitches in long agent sessions while streaming and typing. On the default 50-message page it is probably a few ms per pass, and it grows with paged-back history. Needs Instruments to size.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1478`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1478): new OpenURLAction every ChatView body pass
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1498`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1498): fileChipReferenceScanToken reads viewModel.messages and draftMessage in body, so ChatView.body re-runs per stream tick and per keystroke
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:5174`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L5174): messages[index] reassigned on each paced drain tick
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:347`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L347): new chatDisclosureToggled closure (captures proxy) every ChatTranscriptView body pass
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:256`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L256): non-lazy VStack, so every row is realized and affected
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ResponseTextSelection.swift:12`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ResponseTextSelection.swift#L12): @Environment(\.self) depends on every key
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ResponseTextSelection.swift:25`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ResponseTextSelection.swift#L25): reassigns AnyView rootView on the nested UIHostingController each update
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift:164`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift#L164): one ResponseTextSelection per settled assistant reply
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ToolActivityGroupView.swift:25`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ToolActivityGroupView.swift#L25): re-formats every tool call (preview JSON parse x2 + regex compile) when its body re-runs because of the L10 env read
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLogRowView.swift:99`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLogRowView.swift#L99)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkerMessageCardView.swift:12`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkerMessageCardView.swift#L12)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLinkPreviewView.swift:8`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLinkPreviewView.swift#L8): reads \.openURL
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:106`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift#L106): same inline closure env pattern in Bots chat

## Fix sketch

Stabilize the two values at their source, with no API change for readers. (a) Change ChatDisclosureToggledKey's value to a small `final class ChatDisclosureToggleAction { var handler: () -> Void = {}; func callAsFunction() { handler() } }` with a shared no-op default. Keep one instance in ChatTranscriptView `@State`. In the ScrollViewReader body, set `action.handler = { pinReader(proxy: proxy); onDisclosureToggle() }`. This is a plain class write, not observed, so it causes no invalidation. Pass the same instance to `.environment`. The reference is identical every pass, so readers are not invalidated. Do the same in BotChatView.swift:106. Call sites `chatDisclosureToggled()` keep working. (b) In ChatView, keep `@State private var transcriptOpenURL: OpenURLAction?` and build it once in `.onAppear`/init. Alternatively, move the environment write into a tiny child view that owns the OpenURLAction in @State. `handleTranscriptLink` only writes @State and reads `session.workspace`, and ChatView is keyed per session, so a single action stays correct. (c) Optional follow-up only if Instruments still shows re-hosting: in ResponseTextSelection, skip the `host.rootView` reassignment when neither `identity` nor `collectsGlyphs` changed and a small Equatable env signature (colorScheme, dynamicTypeSize, layoutDirection, legibilityWeight) is unchanged. (a) and (b) remove the per-tick churn on their own.

## Measurement plan

Before/after on a device with a 50-message agent session (about 15 settled replies, 30 tool calls), then again after tapping 'older messages' twice (about 150 messages). Add a DEBUG signpost/counter in ResponseTextSelection.updateUIViewController and `Self._printChanges()` in ToolActivityGroupView.body. Stream one ~2k-token reply and type 20 characters. Before: counts ≈ ticks × settled replies, and `_chatDisclosureToggled changed` logs on every tick. After: near zero, only on real row changes. Confirm with the Instruments SwiftUI template (View Body counts, Hitches) and Time Profiler main-thread time in ToolCallSummaryFormatter.entries and UIHostingController.rootView setter during the stream.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `chatDisclosureToggled` is a stable reference (one action object in `@State` whose handler is updated in place); same fix in `BotChatView`.
- [ ] The transcript `OpenURLAction` is created once per ChatView, not per body pass.
- [ ] A DEBUG `_printChanges()` or signpost count in `ToolActivityGroupView` and `ResponseTextSelection.updateUIViewController` shows near-zero updates while streaming and typing (before: ticks x rows).
- [ ] Disclosure toggles still pin the reader and link taps still route correctly.

## Tradeoffs and risk

Very small plumbing change. The action holder is a reference mutated during body. That is safe because nothing observes it, and it always holds the latest proxy and closures by the time a tap runs. Skipping the ResponseTextSelection rootView reassignment (c) risks stale content if some input is missed, so it is left optional.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. (1) ChatView's body runs on every streaming tick and every keystroke. `messageContent` (ChatView.swift:1359) is evaluated inside ChatView.body. Its `.task(id: fileChipReferenceScanToken)` (L1483, token at L1498-1506) reads `viewModel.messages.count` and `draftMessage` (@State, L293). flushAssistantTokens (ChatViewModel.swift:5172-5174) reassigns `messages[index]` on every word-cadence drain tick (L748). Observation tracks the whole `messages` property, so each tick and each keystroke re-runs ChatView.body. (2) Each of those passes builds a new `OpenURLAction(handler: handleTranscriptLink)` (ChatView.swift:1478). ChatTranscriptView gets fresh closure props and has no Equatable, so its body also re-runs and builds a new `chatDisclosureToggled` closure that captures `proxy` (ChatTranscriptView.swift:347-350). SwiftUI cannot compare closures by value, so both keys look changed on every pass. (3) The transcript is a non-lazy `VStack` (ChatTranscriptView.swift:256), so every row is realized. `.equatable()` on ChatTranscriptMessageBlock (L521/570) only skips that row's own body. Descendants that read environment still update. Readers of `chatDisclosureToggled` re-run their bodies: ToolActivityGroupView (L10) re-runs ToolCallSummaryFormatter.entries (L25), which per call parses the preview for resultDisplay and envelopeReportsFailure and compiles an NSRegularExpression in strippingTrailingExitCode (ToolCallSummaryFormatter.swift:335-347, 388-398). Also TranscriptLogRowView (L99) and MarkerMessageCardView (L12). ResponseTextSelection (ResponseTextSelection.swift:12) depends on `\.self`, so any environment change calls updateUIViewController. That reassigns an AnyView `rootView` on a nested UIHostingController (L25-28) for every settled assistant reply (MessageBubbleView.swift:164), and re-runs its content closure under a replaced environment. Nothing caches or throttles this: MarkdownRenderer's parse cache (#260) avoids re-parsing but not the re-host or the tool formatting. #463 and #296 addressed different causes. One correction to the claim: the default page is 50 raw messages (ChatViewModel.swift:201, `messagePageLimit = 50`), so a freshly opened session has about 10-20 settled replies and 20-40 tool calls. The 150-row case only happens after paging back with 'older messages'. That, plus the unmeasured per-row cost, is why impact is medium rather than high. BotChatView.swift:106 has the same inline-closure pattern.

</details>

title: perf(chat): stop keystrokes and the scroll trigger from re-running the transcript and composer
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

ChatView's body reads the draft only to build a `.task(id:)` token, so every keystroke re-runs all transcript derivations. During streaming, a second Int-only `streamingScrollTrigger` bump 16 ms after each drain tick re-runs the same closure (including the composer and its UITextView representable) just to fire one scroll.

**perf(chat): stop re-evaluating the whole chat screen on every composer keystroke**

ChatView.body reads @State draftMessage only to build a `.task(id:)` token. So every keystroke, dictation partial result, or autocomplete insert re-runs ChatView.body. That pass recomputes the reasoning groups, which do heavy string work over every assistant message and reasoning block. It also recomputes turn folds, terminal reply ids, and the file-change recap, then re-runs ChatTranscriptView's body. There every row's `.equatable()` check compares a freshly rebuilt reasoningGroups array. None of this depends on the draft.

- **Trigger:** Typing or dictating in the composer of an open session with about 50-100 loaded messages from a thinking model (reasoning blocks of 2-5 KB, replies of 1-3 KB).
- **Impact (medium, per keystroke / per dictation partial result while the chat screen is open):** The work is proportional to the transcript and runs on the main thread on top of UITextView and keyboard work, once per keystroke and per dictation partial. It can cause input lag or dropped frames in long sessions on reasoning models. Short chats are unaffected. The rows' own bodies are skipped, so there is no markdown re-render cost.

**perf(chat): stop the streaming scroll trigger and per-tick transcript reads from re-running ChatView's content closure and the composer**

The drain tick writes `messages` and invalidates the ChatView content closure. That is required, because the transcript has to update. But the same closure also builds the composer, whose fresh closures defeat diffing, so the composer body and its UITextView representable re-run on every token tick. Then 16 ms later the Int-only `streamingScrollTrigger` bump invalidates the same closure again. That second pass repeats the O(N) derivations (reasoning groups, turn folds, terminal-reply IDs with per-message trims), constructs and compares all N transcript rows (all skipped by `.equatable()`), and re-runs the composer again, just to fire one onChange that scrolls.

- **Trigger:** Any streamed reply. Answer text drains at about 21 ticks/s, which gives about 42 content-closure passes/s. A reasoning-only phase flushes at up to about 30/s (16 ms delay), which gives about 60 passes/s. Cost scales with the loaded transcript, typically 50-150 rows for a tool-heavy session with one or two older pages loaded.
- **Impact (medium, per drain tick (about 21-30/s while streaming), doubled by the scroll trigger):** Per pass the work is O(N) cheap comparisons and string trims plus one composer body and representable update. At 40-60 passes/s this is steady main-thread time taken from markdown layout and the animated follow-scroll during every stream. It adds up to frame drops on long transcripts and older devices, but it is not a stall by itself.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1483`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1483): .task(id: fileChipReferenceScanToken). Its id expression runs during body.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1499`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1499): The only body read of @State draftMessage. It makes ChatView depend on every keystroke.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:2110`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L2110): persistedDraftBinding set writes draftMessage and draftRevision on every keystroke.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1360`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1360): viewModel.displayedReasoningGroups is recomputed on every body pass.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1428`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1428): turnFolds(reasoningGroups:): TranscriptTurnFolds.derive, O(n), trims each message.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1429`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1429): terminalReplyRenderIDs: rebuilds the turn-key map and trims each message.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1465`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1465): turnChangesRecapSummary: latestTurnToolCalls plus TurnFileChangeAggregator. Minor.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:265`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L265): displayedReasoningGroups is a computed property, not memoized.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:6366`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L6366): strippedVisibleAssistantEcho: splits into paragraphs and runs replacingOccurrences per paragraph, for each reasoning block.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:6383`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L6383): normalizedReasoningKey splits into words and rejoins. Called twice per candidate.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:576`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L576): Each row's equatable check compares the freshly rebuilt reasoningGroups array: rows × groups string compares.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:711`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L711): The `chatContent` GeometryReader closure holds `messageContent` (L725) and `messageComposer` (L738) side by side
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1388`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1388): Reads `viewModel.streamingScrollTrigger` only to hand it to an onChange in ChatTranscriptView
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:415`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L415): MessageComposerView gets about 30 fresh closures, so its body and ComposerTextInputView.updateUIView re-run on every pass of the enclosing closure
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:748`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L748): `drainStreamingContentTick` mutates messages every 48 ms (cadence default at L565). This is invalidation #1
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:718`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L718): `streamingScrollTrigger += 1` runs 16 ms after each mutating tick. This is invalidation #2, and it changes no row input
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:188`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L188): The only consumer of `streamingScrollTrigger`
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:236`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerTextInputView.swift#L236): updateUIView re-assigns about 10 closures and calls reportHeight -> sizeThatFits (L601) on every composer pass
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:800`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift#L800): REFUTED part: metering arrives at 1 Hz upstream, so `liveTokensPerSecond` churn is negligible

## Fix sketch

**perf(chat): stop re-evaluating the whole chat screen on every composer keystroke**

Take the draft out of ChatView's body. (1) In ChatView, key the existing `.task(id:)` on a token built only from the transcript and scope (messages.count, transcriptRevision, fileChipScopeRevision). Read `draftMessage` inside the async closure, which is not tracked as a body dependency: `.task(id: transcriptFileChipToken) { await viewModel.loadFileChipReferences(draft: draftMessage) }`. (2) Give MessageComposerView an `onFileReferenceCandidatesChange: (String) async -> Void` prop. Add `.task(id: ComposerChipTokenizer.fileReferenceCandidates(in: draftMessage)) { await onFileReferenceCandidatesChange(draftMessage) }` there. The composer already re-evaluates per keystroke and already tokenizes the draft for `draftMayReferenceSkill`. ChatView passes `{ await viewModel.loadFileChipReferences(draft: $0) }`. Separately, storing `displayedReasoningGroups` in the view model and updating it inside `recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages()` would make any remaining ChatView body passes cheap, including stream flushes. That is the chat-stream-2 finding and is not required for this fix.

**perf(chat): stop the streaming scroll trigger and per-tick transcript reads from re-running ChatView's content closure and the composer**

Step 1 (S, biggest win per line): stop reading `streamingScrollTrigger` in ChatView. Add a tiny leaf, `private struct StreamingFollowTrigger: View { let viewModel: ChatViewModel; let onFire: () -> Void; var body: some View { Color.clear.onChange(of: viewModel.streamingScrollTrigger) { onFire() } } }`, placed as a `.background` inside ChatTranscriptView's ScrollViewReader with `onFire` = the existing follow-and-scroll closure. Pass the view model (or a trigger-reading closure) instead of the Int. The second invalidation per tick then re-evaluates only that leaf. Step 2 (M): move `messageContent` into its own `ChatTranscriptHost: View` that holds `viewModel` and reads messages, `displayedTranscriptMessages`, reasoning groups, live*, turnFolds and terminalReplyRenderIDs in its own body. ChatView passes its @State-derived values and callbacks in. The `.task(id: fileChipReferenceScanToken)` and `.task(id: transcriptSkillReferenceCount)` modifiers also read messages, so move them into the host too. The composer then stops re-rendering per token. Do not add metering rounding or throttling (1 Hz upstream).

## Measurement plan

Before: add `let _ = Self._printChanges()` in ChatView.body, or use the Instruments SwiftUI template (View Body counts). Typing 100 characters in a 100-message reasoning session should show about 100 ChatView body evaluations, plus Time Profiler samples in `reasoningDisplayGroups`, `TranscriptTurnFolds.derive`, and `terminalReplyRenderIDs`. After: 0-3 ChatView body evaluations for the same input, and no samples in those derivations while typing. Also compare the Hitches instrument while typing quickly on a physical device.

In a Debug build, add `let _ = Self._printChanges()` to MessageComposerView and a counter or os_signpost around ChatView.messageContent. Stream a scripted 2k-token reply (ScriptedSSEStreamFixture) into a 100-message transcript. Before: about 40+ composer body evaluations/s and about 2 content passes per drain tick. After step 1: about 1 pass per tick. After step 2: about 0 composer evaluations per token. Confirm with the Instruments SwiftUI template (View Body counts and main-thread time per second during the stream) on a device.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ChatView.body no longer reads `draftMessage`; file-chip candidate scanning moves into the composer.
- [ ] `streamingScrollTrigger` is observed by a leaf view inside the transcript, not by ChatView's content closure.
- [ ] Instruments/`_printChanges()` shows ~0 ChatView body passes per keystroke and one content pass per drain tick (before: two).
- [ ] Scroll-follow while streaming and file-chip rendering behave as before (existing scroll policy and chip tests pass).

## Tradeoffs and risk

Adds one callback prop to MessageComposerView, and the draft-candidate trigger moves into the composer. There are now two tasks, one for transcript changes and one for draft candidates, but `loadFileChipReferences` already serializes loads with its `while let existing` wait. transcriptSkillReferenceCount stays in ChatView, and its scan returns 0 once skills are requested or loaded.

Step 1 is small and self-contained. Step 2 threads many ChatView @State bindings and callbacks through a new host view in a 3.3k-line file. That is mechanical churn with some regression risk around scroll-follow and disclosure pinning, so land step 1 first and measure before deciding on step 2. It overlaps with memoizing turnFolds, terminalReplyRenderIDs and reasoning groups (the chat-stream-2 cluster), which also shrinks the per-pass cost.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **M**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(chat): stop re-evaluating the whole chat screen on every composer keystroke</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. `draftMessage` is @State on ChatView (ChatView.swift:293). The composer writes it on every keystroke through `persistedDraftBinding` (2106-2117). That alone would not re-run ChatView's body, because building the Binding does not read the value. The only read inside body is `fileChipReferenceScanToken` (1498-1506), which runs `ComposerChipTokenizer.fileReferenceCandidates(in: draftMessage)` to build the id for `.task(id:)` at 1483 inside `messageContent`. No other body path reads `draftMessage`. `draftRevision` is only read in functions. The task itself only restarts when the candidate set changes, but the body still re-runs on every keystroke. Nothing on that pass is cached. `viewModel.displayedReasoningGroups` (ChatViewModel.swift:265) is a computed property, not a stored one. It calls `reasoningDisplayGroups` (6105), which for every assistant message trims the full content several times and looks for `<think>` tags (6340-6364). For every reasoning candidate it splits the visible reply into paragraphs and runs `replacingOccurrences` for each one (6366-6381), then `normalizedReasoningKey` twice (6155, 6159), each a split into words and a rejoin. `turnFolds(...)` (ChatView.swift:1677, called at 1428) and `terminalReplyRenderIDs` (1698, used at 1429) each rebuild the turn-key map, and `shouldRenderMessageRow` trims every message. `turnChangesRecapSummary` (1138) runs `latestTurnToolCalls` and the aggregator when idle. It is small but also runs per keystroke. ChatTranscriptView takes closure props, so its body re-runs too. Every row's `.equatable()` check (ChatTranscriptView.swift:321, 570-592) then compares the freshly rebuilt `reasoningGroups` array element by element, with string compares over newly allocated reasoning text: rows × groups × text length. Row bodies are skipped, so there is no markdown re-render. Realistic load: a 50-100 message thinking-model session, about 25-50 assistant messages of 1-3 KB with 10-25 reasoning blocks of 2-5 KB. That is hundreds of KB of Foundation string scanning and thousands of substring allocations per keystroke, plus dictation partials. Not covered by the 'Already fixed' list: #260 and #463 cached markdown and row laziness, not these ChatView-level derivations. The mechanism is certain. The per-keystroke millisecond cost needs a device trace.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(chat): stop the streaming scroll trigger and per-tick transcript reads from re-running ChatView's content closure and the composer</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. Both findings describe the same thing, so they are merged here. Traced from the code: (1) `messageContent` (ChatView.swift:1359) is evaluated inside the `chatContent` GeometryReader/ZStack closure (ChatView.swift:711-742), and `messageComposer` (L738), `composerAccessoryStack`, `clarificationInset` and `approvalOverlay` are built in that same closure. (2) That closure reads `viewModel.messages`, `displayedTranscriptMessages`, `liveReasoningText`, `liveToolCalls` and `streamingScrollTrigger` (L1360-1388). (3) `drainStreamingContentTick` (ChatViewModel.swift:748) mutates `messages` every 48 ms (L565 default). `scheduleStreamingScrollTrigger` (L706) then bumps `streamingScrollTrigger` 16 ms later (L718). That is two separate invalidations per tick. (4) `MessageComposerView` gets about 30 fresh closure literals (ChatView.swift:462+), so SwiftUI can't skip its body. Its `ComposerTextInputView.updateUIView` (ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:236) re-assigns closures and ends with `reportHeight` -> `sizeThatFits` (L601). (5) The scroll-trigger pass changes no row input, so every `.equatable()` row is skipped. The whole pass is overhead: `displayedReasoningGroups` is an uncached computed property (ChatViewModel.swift:265). `turnFolds` (ChatView.swift:1677) and `terminalReplyRenderIDs` (L1698) each rebuild `assistantTurnKeysByAnchorID` and call `shouldRenderMessageRow`, which trims (and copies) every assistant message's content (L1657). Then N rows are constructed and compared, and each comparison checks the freshly allocated `reasoningGroups` array (ChatTranscriptView.swift:576). Nothing on the list of already-fixed issues covers this. #296 skips redundant writes; it does not scope the reads. Parts I refuted: (a) `liveTokensPerSecond` does not arrive at up to 10 Hz. Upstream emits metering at 1 Hz (.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/streaming.py:9507, metering.py get_interval returns 1.0), so rounding or throttling it is a micro-optimization. Drop that part of the fix. (b) The claim that the toolbar, git menu and 'entire 3.3k-line screen' re-run is overstated. The outer modifier chain (`.toolbar`, alerts, onChange of `activeStreamID`) sits outside the GeometryReader content closure, which SwiftUI tracks as its own attribute. I did not verify that those parts re-run on a token tick. The composer, overlays and transcript derivations certainly do. Magnitude depends on transcript size, and the loaded window is bounded by the 50-message pagination plus older pages. I expect medium impact, not high: the per-pass work is O(N) cheap operations plus a sub-millisecond-to-millisecond composer pass, and on-device measurement is needed.

</details>

title: perf(chat): scan the streaming reply once per drain tick, not 8-10 times
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Each drain tick runs about 8-10 full passes over the growing reply on the main actor: a media parse with O(n^2) string concatenation, two renderer passes (one on stale text), and at least four block splits that allocate a String per line. Late in a 20-40 KB reply this is several ms per tick.

Every 48 ms drain tick mutates the streaming message, and on the main actor the streaming row re-runs about 8-10 full-message passes: 1 media parse (per-char hasPrefix plus O(n^2) text concatenation), 2 renderer body passes (each a trim copy, grapheme count, line count and math segmentation, one of them on stale content), and at least 4 block splits (each allocating a String per line plus grapheme distance walks). Stable-chunk sealing at 6k characters bounds only the markdown parse, so this helper work grows with total reply length, and total work over a reply grows quadratically.

- **Trigger:** A long streamed reply (20-40 KB, e.g. a code-heavy answer or report of about 5-10k tokens), during the last half of the stream at 21 ticks/s. Replies under about 6 KB are unaffected in practice.
- **Impact (medium, per drain tick (~21 Hz) while an assistant reply streams):** At about 30 KB and 800 lines, my estimate is several ms of main-thread work per 48 ms tick, led by the quadratic media-parser concat and the repeated splits. That can cost frames at 120 Hz while the fade TimelineView is drawing and the row's height animation runs. It is invisible for typical short replies, so this is a heavy-use problem, not an everyday one.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift:151`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift#L151): TranscriptMediaParser.segments over the full reply on every body pass, not memoized
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMedia.swift:392`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMedia.swift#L392): appendText copies the whole accumulated text segment per line: O(n^2) per parse
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMedia.swift:188`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMedia.swift#L188): three Substring hasPrefix checks per character outside fences (also lines 200 and 218)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:108`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L108): .task(id: content) + Task.yield + displayedContent: body runs twice per tick, first on stale text
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:99`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L99): fallbackReason: full grapheme count + line count per body pass (policy at :831-835)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:121`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L121): uncachedLayout per body pass; Array(content) + mask when the reply contains a dollar sign or backslash (MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift:23-31)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:170`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L170): computed segments re-splits on each read (:176, :185)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:265`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L265): advanceFadeWindow splits oldContent and newContent in full (:265-266)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift:26`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift#L26): String alloc + trimmingCharacters for every line of the whole message
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift:62`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift#L62): text.distance grapheme walk from chunk start at every stable boundary

## Fix sketch

Smallest changes, in payoff order. (1) TranscriptMedia.swift: fix appendText so it mutates the last segment in place (removeLast, append to a local var, re-append) or accumulates a pending text run and flushes it once. Add an early return of [.text(markdown)] when the UTF-8 bytes contain none of the markers ('![', 'MEDIA:', 'file://', or '[' when includesLocalFileLinks). That makes the common case one memchr-speed scan. (2) StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift: stop allocating per line. Trim and test the Substring directly (fence, heading and rule checks work on Substring), and replace text.distance with text.utf8.distance, which is O(1) on native strings. Treat the 6,000 threshold as UTF-8 bytes. Each split becomes one allocation-free linear byte scan. (3) MarkdownRenderer.swift StreamingMarkdownChunkedView: bind let segments = split(content) once in body. In advanceFadeWindow compute only the new split, and keep the previous activeMarkdown in @State (set there and in anchorFadeWindowAtCurrentBlock) instead of re-splitting oldContent. (4) StreamingMarkdownRenderer: in the first body pass skip fallback and layout work when displayedContent is unchanged, or render content directly if the yield indirection has no remaining purpose (it dates from the initial commit; confirm before removing). Incremental resume-from-last-seal splitting is optional once (2) lands.

## Measurement plan

Add os_signpost intervals around MessageBubbleView.assistantMessageRow's media parse, StreamingMarkdownRenderer.body, StreamingMarkdownChunkedView.body and advanceFadeWindow. Stream a scripted 30 KB code-heavy reply (with shell dollar vars) through ScriptedSSEStreamFixture and record the per-tick main-thread ms at 5 KB and 30 KB. Before: expect the per-tick total to grow roughly linearly with length and reach several ms at 30 KB. After: the per-tick total should stay near flat (well under 1 ms). A cheap XCTest measure{} of TranscriptMediaParser.segments and StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter.split on a 30 KB string gives a device-independent before/after ratio.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TranscriptMediaParser.appendText` mutates in place and short-circuits when no media markers exist.
- [ ] `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter.split` works on Substrings/UTF-8 without per-line allocation; the chunked view splits once per body.
- [ ] XCTest `measure` on a 30 KB string for the parser and splitter shows the before/after ratio; existing splitter and media tests pass.
- [ ] Per-tick main-thread time on a scripted 30 KB stream stays roughly flat with length.

## Tradeoffs and risk

(1) and (2) are local and behavior-preserving, and the existing splitter and media tests cover them. (3) adds one @State string. Removing the yield in (4) could change whether the first frame after a content change shows old or new text; confirm there was no intentional coalescing reason. A full incremental splitter would need a reset path for replaced (non-prefix) content, which advanceFadeWindow already detects.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Traced at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The drain runs every 48 ms (ChatViewModel.swift:565, about 21 Hz). Each tick replaces messages[index] (ChatViewModel.swift:5176), so the streaming MessageBubbleView row re-runs its body. None of the whole-message passes below is cached or incremental. The only caches cover sealed chunks (ChatMarkdownView) and settled content (MarkdownMathLayoutCache.layout, which streaming deliberately bypasses). (1) MessageBubbleView.swift:151 runs TranscriptMediaParser.segments over the whole reply on every body pass. Outside code fences it makes three Substring hasPrefix checks per character (TranscriptMedia.swift:188, 200, 218). appendText (TranscriptMedia.swift:391-392) rebuilds the growing text segment with existing + text while the array still holds the old string, so every line copies the whole string so far: O(n^2) per parse. The auditors under-called this pass, and it is likely the most expensive one. (2) StreamingMarkdownRenderer (MarkdownRenderer.swift:95-113) re-runs its body when content changes but renders displayedContent, which is still the old text. Then .task(id: content) plus Task.yield sets displayedContent and the body runs again. So the trim copy, fallbackReason (content.count graphemes plus lineCount, MarkdownRenderer.swift:831-835) and uncachedLayout (:121) all run twice per tick, the first time on stale text. uncachedLayout falls to Array(content) plus a protection mask (MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift:23-31) whenever the reply contains a dollar sign or backslash, which is common in code-heavy replies. (3) StreamingMarkdownChunkedView: segments is a computed var (:170-172) read twice per body (:176, :185), and advanceFadeWindow splits old and new content again (:265-266). That is at least 4 full splits per tick. Each split allocates and trims a String for every line (StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift:26-27) and calls text.distance at every stable boundary (:62). That grapheme walk from the chunk start makes each split roughly (boundaries x chunk size) for prose. The claim that flushAssistantTokens rebuilds content with a full concat copy (ChatViewModel.swift:5176) is true but is one 30 KB memcpy per tick, a micro-cost; I dropped it. For typical 2-6 KB replies all of this totals well under 1 ms, so the cost only shows late in long replies. #291 bounded the markdown re-parse, not these helper scans, so this is not a regression of an already-fixed item.

</details>

title: perf(live-activity): coalesce repeated Thinking updates and bound per-token excerpt work
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Every reasoning SSE event sends an immediate ActivityKit update even though the Lock Screen only shows 'Thinking'; a 30-60 s thinking phase sends 300-600 cross-process updates where the existing 1.5 s throttle would send 20-40. With excerpts on, each token also re-normalizes the whole reply to build a 140-character prefix (same in Bots).

**perf(live-activity): throttle repeated Thinking updates instead of sending one ActivityKit update per reasoning event**

Each reasoning event rebuilds a ContentState that differs only in updatedAt and sends it with immediate: true, which skips the 1.5 s minimumUpdateInterval. Every event therefore becomes a MainActor Task and an Activity.update (a JSON encode, an IPC to the activity daemon, and a Lock Screen/Dynamic Island re-render in the widget process). The visible content ('Thinking') never changes.

- **Trigger:** Any thinking-model turn while a Live Activity is running (the default once Live Activities are authorized; the path is not behind a setting). On the standard webui path that is about 10 events/s, so a 30-60 s thinking phase sends about 300-600 updates where the throttle would send about 20-40. Gateway runs send raw deltas, which is more.
- **Impact (medium, per reasoning event (about 10 Hz typical) for the whole thinking phase of every turn):** No visible in-app jank was shown, but every reasoning turn wastes hundreds of cross-process updates and widget renders, which drains battery during long streams. It also spends the system's Live Activity update budget, which could delay transitions that matter, such as Waiting for approval. The excerpt quadratic is opt-in (default off) and low impact.

**perf(live-activity): stop re-normalizing the whole reply per token once the excerpt prefix is full**

The Lock Screen excerpt is a fixed 140-character prefix, but each token re-normalizes the entire accumulated reply on the main actor. That means one String allocated per word, a join, a trim, and a full grapheme count. Per-token cost grows with reply length, so one reply costs O(n^2) in total. After the prefix fills, the output never changes, yet ActivityKit updates keep going out about every 1.5 s.

- **Trigger:** 'Show response excerpts' is on and the user streams a long reply, e.g. 10k tokens (~40 KB) at ~50 tokens/s. That means about 10k full-text normalizations averaging ~20 KB each on main, plus ~130 redundant Activity updates over the ~3-minute stream.
- **Impact (low, per token, only with the opt-in excerpt setting on):** The work is wasted on a per-token main-actor path, likely about 0.5-1.5 ms per token late in a 40 KB reply (a few percent of main-thread time competing with markdown rendering), plus steady redundant cross-process widget renders. It is only reached with an opt-in setting that defaults to off, and is small for typical 2k-token replies.

**perf(bots): stop normalizing the whole live reply for the Live Activity snapshot on every frame**

Every gateway frame rebuilds liveActivitySnapshot and so re-normalizes the whole live reply. The reply only changes at about 4 Hz, and only the first ~140 normalized characters are kept. Per-frame cost grows with reply length and nearly all of it recomputes an identical value.

- **Trigger:** A Bot chat is open while a bot streams a long reply, e.g. about 12 KB with frames arriving at tens per second.
- **Impact (low, per gateway frame while a Bot chat is open during a running turn):** Probably 0.1-0.5 ms of main-actor string churn per frame late in a long reply. It is measurable but unlikely to drop frames by itself. It is scoped to the Bots screen during an active turn.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:782`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift#L782): every reasoning SSE event calls liveActivityManager.update(.reasoning(text)), with no gate
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:268`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift#L268): `.reasoning` -> updateCurrentState with the default immediate: true; no unchanged-status guard, unlike `.responding` at :289
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:622`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift#L622): the immediate branch cancels the pending throttle and spawns a send Task per event
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:660`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift#L660): await activity.update(...): an XPC call plus a widget re-render per event
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:510`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift#L510): the reducer ignores the text; only updatedAt changes between consecutive reasoning events
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:714`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift#L714): staleDate -> isRegistered -> Keychain pairing read per send for push-paired owners (goes away with throttling)
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:253`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift#L253): opt-in excerpts: rawResponseText grows without bound and is fully re-normalized per token to produce a 140-char prefix
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:346`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift#L346): responseExcerpt normalizes the whole text before trimming to 140 chars
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:609`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift#L609): the transform runs before the `activity != nil` guard at L613, so the work happens even with no activity
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:400`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift#L400): normalizedSingleLine: components(separatedBy: .whitespacesAndNewlines) → filter → joined → trimming over the full reply
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:409`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift#L409): trimmed(): value.count is an O(n) grapheme count over the full normalized reply to keep 140 characters
- [`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:475`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift#L475): settingInterimAssistant → responseExcerpt(text)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:765`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift#L765): gated on showsLiveActivityResponseExcerpts (default false)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:1102`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L1102): defer { syncLiveActivity() } on every observed frame
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:197`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L197): responseExcerpt(reply) over the full live reply, computed even when excerpts are off
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:603`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L603): the only place the live reply changes, once per coalesced session.resume snapshot (~4 Hz)

## Fix sketch

**perf(live-activity): throttle repeated Thinking updates instead of sending one ActivityKit update per reasoning event**

In AgentLiveActivityManager.update, change the reasoning case to `updateCurrentState(immediate: currentState?.status != .thinking) { AgentRunActivityStateReducer.reasoning(text, state: $0) }`. The first transition into Thinking stays immediate. Repeats join the existing 1.5 s coalescing path, which sends the latest currentState. A hard `guard status != .thinking` would be simpler but is worse here: statusState rebuilds with isStale = false, so a reasoning event after markStale would stop clearing the stale flag, and the freshness chip (detailChips, AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:145-150) would freeze. For the opt-in excerpt path, in `.token` stop appending once `rawResponseText.count > 4 * AgentRunActivitySanitizer.maximumExcerptCharacters` (the excerpt is a prefix), which bounds the per-token normalize cost.

**perf(live-activity): stop re-normalizing the whole reply per token once the excerpt prefix is full**

In `case .token` (AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:251), add `guard rawResponseText.utf8.count < 2_048 else { return }` before `rawResponseText += text`. 2 KB of text still normalizes to well over 140 characters. This bounds the normalization cost and stops the no-op updatedAt churn. No sanitizer change is needed. Leave the interimAssistant and clear paths as they are.

**perf(bots): stop normalizing the whole live reply for the Live Activity snapshot on every frame**

At BotConversation.swift:197, pass only a bounded prefix: `AgentRunActivitySanitizer.responseExcerpt(String(reply.prefix(2_048)))`. That is a one-line change, and whitespace collapsing only shrinks text, so the 140-character excerpt stays the same in practice.

## Measurement plan

Before/after in LiveActivityTests: build the manager with a small minimumUpdateInterval, count scheduleUpdate/sendUpdate calls with a test seam, emit 100 `.reasoning` events, and assert one immediate send plus at most one coalesced send per throttle window (before: about 100). On device, put an os_signpost event in sendUpdate and count Points of Interest per thinking turn in Instruments. Expect about 300 to about 20 for a 30 s thinking phase.

Before/after XCTest: start an activity on AgentLiveActivityManager with excerpts on, feed 5,000 tokens of 4 characters each, and assert that rawResponseText stays at or under ~2 KB and that currentStateForTesting() stops changing once the excerpt fills. Wrap the loop in measure {}; expect roughly linear instead of quadratic time. On device, run Time Profiler during a long streamed reply and check that AgentRunActivitySanitizer.normalizedSingleLine drops out of the main-thread samples.

Before/after XCTest: build a BotConversation with a 12 KB live assistant reply and time 1,000 reads of liveActivitySnapshot with measure {}; expect a large drop that no longer scales with reply length. On device, run Time Profiler during a long bot reply and check main-thread samples in normalizedSingleLine.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only the first transition into Thinking is immediate; repeats join the 1.5 s coalescing path, and the stale flag still clears.
- [ ] Excerpt normalization stops growing once the prefix is full (webui and Bot paths).
- [ ] `LiveActivityTests`: 100 reasoning events produce one immediate send plus at most one coalesced send per window.

## Tradeoffs and risk

While already Thinking, the Lock Screen's updatedAt and stale-clear land up to 1.5 s later. Status transitions stay immediate. The excerpt cap assumes the excerpt stays a prefix, which is true for the current reducer.

Once capped, pure token streaming no longer bumps updatedAt or refreshes staleDate (a 300 s window). A single uninterrupted token-only reply longer than 5 minutes could get the dimmed stale treatment, although tool, reasoning and title events still refresh it and markStale still handles suspension. If that matters, allow one refresh every ~60 s instead of returning outright. A 2 KB prefix that is mostly whitespace could give an excerpt shorter than 140 characters, which is negligible.

A reply that opens with more than ~2 KB of whitespace could give a shorter excerpt, which is negligible.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(live-activity): throttle repeated Thinking updates instead of sending one ActivityKit update per reasoning event</summary>

Traced at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:781-782 forwards every `.reasoning` SSE event to liveActivityManager.update, with no gate. AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:268-271 calls updateCurrentState() with the default `immediate: true` (declared at :602-603). That reaches scheduleUpdate (:617-630). The `immediate ||` branch cancels any pending throttled send and starts a Task per event. That Task calls sendUpdate (:652-663), which awaits activity.update. Unlike `.responding` (:289-290) and `.workSummary` (:294-296), nothing dedupes `.reasoning`. AgentRunActivityStateReducer.reasoning (AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:510-517) ignores the text and returns statusState(.thinking, "Thinking") (:604-619) with only updatedAt = now changed. The generation guard drops a send only when a newer one supersedes it before the Task runs, so most events get through. Two claims needed correcting. First, rate: upstream's standard webui path coalesces reasoning to about 10 Hz (.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/streaming.py:10127-10132). Only the gateway path forwards raw deltas (gateway_chat.py:762-766). So '20-100 events/s' holds only for gateway runs; typical is about 10/s, which is about 300 Activity.update calls for a 30 s thinking phase instead of about 20 throttled ones. Second, staleDate(): the Keychain read (:709-717 -> PushRegistrar.isRegistered :377-380 -> PushPairing.swift:116-118) runs per send, but only for confirmed push-paired owners. Throttling the sends removes it as a side effect. The excerpt sub-claim in chat-stream-5 is real but minor. With excerpts on, `.token` (:253-258) appends to rawResponseText and runs settingInterimAssistant -> responseExcerpt -> normalizedSingleLine (AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:346-349, 402-408) over the whole reply on every token. That is quadratic. However, the setting defaults to false (SettingsView.swift:65), so it is opt-in and low impact. It fits in the same small fix. Impact is scored medium, not high. No transcript frame drop was demonstrated: this is an async Task per event plus an IPC to the activity daemon and a widget re-render, a battery and system-budget cost rather than visible jank.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(live-activity): stop re-normalizing the whole reply per token once the excerpt prefix is full</summary>

I traced it at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. When the opt-in setting is on (ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:765), every SSE token reaches AgentLiveActivityManager.update(.token) (AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:251-256). That appends to rawResponseText with no cap, and updateCurrentState runs settingInterimAssistant(rawResponseText) on the main actor for every token. The reducer calls AgentRunActivitySanitizer.responseExcerpt (AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:345), and normalizedSingleLine (L400-405) splits the whole reply into words, filters them, joins them and trims them. trimmed() (L408-416) then counts graphemes over the whole result, only to keep the first 137 characters plus '...'. Nothing caches or short-circuits this. The transform runs before the `activity != nil` guard (L609-613), so it runs even when no activity exists. Once the prefix is full, every token still produces a new state that differs only in updatedAt, and scheduleUpdate (L617-650) sends an ActivityKit update about every 1.5 s that renders the same thing. The claims are accurate, but the impact is overstated as medium. The setting defaults to off (SettingsView.swift:65, @AppStorage default false). The cost is only large for long replies, where a typical 2k-token reply of about 8 KB costs about 0.1-0.3 ms per token. I scored it low. The one real side effect of the no-op updates is that they refresh staleDate (300 s window, L717), which the fix has to account for.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(bots): stop normalizing the whole live reply for the Live Activity snapshot on every frame</summary>

BotConversation.observe (BotConversation.swift:1101-1102) runs `defer { syncLiveActivity() }` on every gateway frame, including the activity-only frames that return early at L1149-1150. syncLiveActivity (L214-216) builds liveActivitySnapshot, which calls AgentRunActivitySanitizer.responseExcerpt(reply) over the entire live assistant reply (L193, L197). That happens every time, even with excerpts off, because the feed only drops the text later (BotLiveActivityFeed.swift:121-129). The reply itself only changes in applySnapshot (L587-604), which the refresh loop coalesces to about 4 Hz (L1198-1211). BotLiveActivityFeed.sync dedupes equal snapshots (L71), so the manager is not hit per frame. The waste is limited to recomputing an unchanged excerpt per frame. That is real, but the per-frame cost for a bot reply of a few KB is probably well under a millisecond, and it only happens while a Bot chat is open during a long reply. Without profiling, the magnitude is uncertain.

</details>

title: perf(sessions): pause the 1 Hz active-row poll while a chat covers the list
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

While any session is streaming, the session list polls the server every second, even when a chat fully covers the list on iPhone. That is 2-3 requests per second of radio and tunnel load for the whole of the app's main use case.

While any visible row is streaming, the list's monitor wakes about once a second. Each tick it sends 1 stream-status GET plus 2 attention-probe GETs per streaming session. The task is keyed only on list data and sits above the NavigationStack, so on iPhone it keeps running while ChatView covers the list. That ChatView is already tracking the same run over its chat SSE and approval/clarify SSE.

- **Trigger:** On iPhone, the user opens a streaming chat and watches a 3-10 minute agent run over a Cloudflare tunnel or cellular. That produces roughly 450-1,600 requests per session. Each additional background-streaming session adds 3 more per tick. The same thing happens after relaunching into a still-running session. On iPad the list is on screen next to the chat, so the loop is visible work there, but it still runs at an aggressive 1 Hz.
- **Impact (medium, periodic (about 1 Hz for the whole length of every agent run while the logged-in stack is alive)):** No frames drop, but it keeps the radio awake and adds about 2-3 requests/s of server and tunnel load for the whole of the app's main use case (watching a run). On high-latency links it also competes with the chat's own requests. The cost is battery and data on cellular, and it scales with the number of concurrently streaming sessions.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:300`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L300): `.task(id: activeSessionMonitorTaskID)` sits on the root container, outside the compact NavigationStack, so pushing a chat does not cancel it
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1053`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L1053): the task ID has no visibility or destination input
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1180`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L1180): fixed 1 s sleep with no backoff, repeated for as long as any visible row streams
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:476`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L476): one GET /api/chat/stream/status per active stream, sent serially every tick
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:599`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L599): then approval-pending and clarify-pending GETs for each streaming session every tick
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:309`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift#L309): the open chat already watches approvals over SSE (list probes duplicate it)

## Fix sketch

1) Add `isListVisible: Bool` to `ActiveSessionMonitorTaskID`, set to `horizontalSizeClass == .regular || navigationState.destination == nil`. In `monitorActiveSessionRows`, extend the existing guard to `guard taskID.hasActiveRows, taskID.isListVisible, !taskID.isViewingCachedData else { return }`. The task restarts when the user pops back, and the existing destination-return refresh reloads the rows immediately. 2) Raise the sleep from 1 s to about 3 s. The chat's own fallback poll uses 1.5-3 s and upstream's sidebar uses 30 s, so 3 s is still far fresher than upstream. Optional follow-up, not in this change: on iPad, skip the attention probes for the session open in the detail pane, since its chat already has the pending-action SSE.

## Measurement plan

In a DEBUG build, count requests in `APIClient.sendPreparedRequest`, or use the Network instrument or server access log. Test on an iPhone simulator with one streaming session open in ChatView for 60 s. Before: about 150-180 requests to /api/chat/stream/status plus approval/clarify pending. After: 0 while the chat is pushed, and about 60 per minute with the list visible at a 3 s cadence (down from about 180).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The monitor runs only while the list is visible (regular width or no pushed destination) and restarts on return.
- [ ] Interval raised to about 3 s.
- [ ] A test drives the task ID and shows no polling while a chat is pushed.

## Tradeoffs and risk

On iPhone, list badges for other sessions (Working, Needs approval, Input) are not refreshed while a chat covers the list. They catch up with the immediate reload on return. With the list visible, badges and the switch from Working to done can land up to about 3 s later instead of about 1 s later.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. Mechanism is certain from the code; a device trace is still the before/after gate.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

All three findings describe the same loop, so they are merged here. I traced it at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The `.task(id: activeSessionMonitorTaskID)` modifier (SessionListView.swift:300) sits on `routedNavigationContainer`, outside the compact NavigationStack (L454-460). Pushing ChatView therefore does not cancel it. `ActiveSessionMonitorTaskID` (L1053-1060, struct L1650) holds only streamIDs, hasActiveRows and isViewingCachedData. It does not track visibility or `navigationState.destination`. The loop at L1174-1194 sleeps a fixed 1 s and then calls `refreshActiveSessionStatesIfNeeded`. That function (SessionListViewModel.swift:463-489) sends one `chatStreamStatus` GET per active stream, one after another. While the stream is still active, `refreshAttentionStates` (L588-600) then sends an `approvalPending` GET and a `clarifyPending` GET together for each streaming session. That is 3 requests per tick per streaming session, and a tick is roughly 1 s plus RTT. There is no backoff and no check on whether the list is on screen. On iPhone this duplicates work ChatView already does. ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:300-311 watches approvals over SSE (`approvalStreamClient`) and polls at 1.5 s only as a fallback, and ChatStreamCoordinator carries the run itself. Pausing the loop is safe: `SessionListDestinationReturn.run` (L346-351) already calls `refreshAfterReturningIfNeeded` when the destination clears, so the list reloads when the user pops back. For comparison, upstream's sidebar streaming poll runs every 30 s and skips while the tab is hidden (`.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/static/sessions.js:5770`, `:5825-5832`). I checked one possible worse case and ruled it out. If a row had `is_streaming` set without `active_stream_id`, the loop would do a full `load()` every tick (L470-472). Upstream derives `is_streaming` from `active_stream_id` (models.py:946), so that case does not happen in practice. Not already fixed: #238 covers the chat's own status polls, not this list loop.

</details>

## Related

- #421 (sessions event stream) would replace polling entirely later.
