title: perf(chat): start chat-open requests immediately and run them in parallel
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Opening a chat waits for the push transition before requesting the transcript, then loads composer config (profiles, models, reasoning, workspaces, commands) and approvals as a serial chain. Over a tunnel the transcript arrives 150-400 ms later than necessary and composer chips settle 0.4-0.8 s late.

**perf(chat): start the transcript request before the push transition finishes**

The session GET (with messages and expandRenderable) is sent only after the UIKit push transition completion fires. The transition (~350-500 ms) and the network round trip plus server work therefore run one after the other instead of overlapping. Only applying the result has to wait for the transition; sending the request and decoding it on the APIClient actor do not affect the main thread.

- **Trigger:** Every existing-session open: tapping a session row, launch restore of the last session, deep links, and notification or Live Activity taps that push a ChatView.
- **Impact (medium, per session open):** On an open with a cache the transcript is already on screen, so the gain is fresher content and earlier stream reattach, about min(transition, RTT) ≈ 150-400 ms. On an uncached open (one of ~200 sessions never opened on this device, or after the cache was evicted), the skeleton stays visible for transition + RTT. Over a Cloudflare tunnel with a 300-600 ms session fetch, that goes from ~0.8-1.1 s to ~0.4-0.6 s, which users notice. There are no dropped frames either way.

**perf(chat): run the independent composer-config and approval requests concurrently on chat open**

On chat open, the transcript fetch, 5-6 composer-config GETs and 2 approval GETs all run strictly one after another. After profiles (plus an optional switch), models, workspaces and commands are independent. Reasoning needs only models. The approval/YOLO refresh needs only the session ID. The serial chain costs about 5-6 RTTs where 2-3 would do, and the approval card sits behind all of them.

- **Trigger:** The user opens any session, or the app restores the last session on launch, over a Cloudflare tunnel (~100-200 ms RTT plus server time). Moving between sessions repeats the chain.
- **Impact (medium, per chat open):** Tunnel users only. Over a tunnel, slash commands, the reasoning-effort chip and supported efforts settle about 0.4-0.8 s later than they could. A pending approval or YOLO badge appears about 1-1.4 s after the transcript refresh instead of in parallel with it. Model, workspace and profile chips are already filled from the session, and on LAN the difference is under 50 ms.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:750`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L750): .task(id: didCompleteInitialAppearance) runs twice: once on appear, then again when the transition completes
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1743`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1743): guard ChatInitialAppearancePolicy.shouldBeginAsyncWork returns early, so no network work happens in the first pass
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1762`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1762): performInitialAsyncWork -> loadMessages, the first point where the session GET is issued
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:2870`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L2870): handleInitialAppearanceCompletion flips the flag
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:86`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L86): coordinator.animate(alongsideTransition:nil) completion reports appearance only after the push animation ends
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:1435`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L1435): client.session(id:includeMessages:messageLimit:expandRenderable:), the request that could be in flight during the transition
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:1608`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L1608): prepareInitialMessageLoad: the synchronous cache paint in the first pass, the natural place to also send the request
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatScrollPolicy.swift:195`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatScrollPolicy.swift#L195): ChatInitialAppearancePolicy: its stated intent covers reconciliation/render work, not network I/O
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:73`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift#L73): profiles; must stay first (decides whether a switch is needed)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:82`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift#L82): conditional switchProfile; must precede models/workspaces (profile-scoped upstream)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:104`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift#L104): models, awaited serially
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:117`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift#L117): reasoning; depends only on resolved model/provider
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:125`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift#L125): workspaces, independent of models/reasoning
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift:136`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift#L136): commands, independent; runs even after a config error
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1767`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1767): loadComposerConfiguration awaited after loadMessages
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1775`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1775): refreshApprovalBypassState (yolo + approvalPending, 2 serial RTTs) waits behind the whole config chain
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:90`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift#L90): sessionYolo then refreshApprovalPending (L378); session-scoped, no dependence on composer config
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:837`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L837): loader call site; the equality guard at L840 reruns the chain if state changed mid-flight

## Fix sketch

**perf(chat): start the transcript request before the push transition finishes**

In ChatViewModel, add `@ObservationIgnored private var prefetchedSessionTask: Task<SessionResponse, Error>?`, using whatever type client.session returns. prepareInitialMessageLoad (already called in the first task pass) starts it with the same arguments as ChatViewModel.swift:1435. In loadMessages, swap the direct `try await client.session(...)` for `try await (prefetchedSessionTask.take() ?? Task { try await client.session(...) }).value`, clearing the stored task before awaiting so a later refresh or reconnect never reuses it. Leave the ChatView gate and all apply logic unchanged, so the result is still only applied after the transition. Cancel the task in the ChatView onDisappear path (for example via cleanupPollingTasks) so a quick back-swipe does not keep it alive.

**perf(chat): run the independent composer-config and approval requests concurrently on chat open**

1) In ChatComposerConfigLoader.loadConfiguration, keep profiles and the conditional switchProfile first. Then start `async let workspaces = try? client.workspaces()` and `async let commands = try? client.commands()`, await models, resolve model/provider, await reasoning, and finally await workspaces and commands. Keep the existing error semantics: a models/reasoning failure sets configurationError, and workspaces follows the same rule as today. This cuts the chain from 5 RTTs (6 with a switch) to 3 (4 with a switch). 2) In ChatView.performInitialAsyncWork, run `viewModel.refreshApprovalBypassState()` concurrently with `loadComposerConfiguration()` via async let. It depends only on the session ID, and the transcript fetch already proves session-scoped routes work before any profile switch. The order between draft-settings restore and config stays unchanged. Do not start config concurrently with loadMessages (the L840 guard would rerun the chain). Do not add a per-server/profile catalog cache: it saves no requests under revalidation, and it needs server+profile keying.

## Measurement plan

Add os_signpost intervals from ChatView first `.task` pass to the `client.session` request start and to the applyReloadedMessages completion. Measure in Instruments on a device, opening an uncached session over the tunnel, or with Network Link Conditioner at 150 ms added latency. Before: the request starts about 350-500 ms after the first pass, and apply ≈ transition + RTT. After: the request starts in the first pass, and apply ≈ max(transition, RTT). Also check that the Animation Hitches instrument shows no new hitches during the push.

Before/after, over the tunnel on a device: log timestamps (os_signpost or NSLog) at the ChatView .task start, at the end of loadMessages, when loadComposerConfiguration returns, and when refreshApprovalBypassState returns. Expect config to drop from about 5×RTT to about 3×RTT after loadMessages (e.g. ~900 ms to ~500 ms at 150 ms RTT + ~30 ms server). Expect the approval refresh to finish in parallel instead of about 2 RTTs after config. Request count per open stays the same; check the waterfall in the Network instrument or server access log to confirm the overlap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The transcript request starts in `prepareInitialMessageLoad` and is awaited by `loadMessages`; a refresh never reuses a stale prefetch.
- [ ] Workspaces and commands load concurrently with models/reasoning; approvals load in parallel with the transcript refresh.
- [ ] Error semantics unchanged (`ChatComposerConfigLoader` tests pass); a new test with a scripted latency client shows concurrency.

## Tradeoffs and risk

One extra stored task and a 'use the prefetch once' rule in the view model. streamCoordinator.prepareForSessionLoad() still runs inside loadMessages, after the request was sent. A stream that starts within that ~0.5 s window could be reflected in the preparation but not in the response, so reattach would fall to the existing reconnect path. That is acceptable, but a test should cover it. A quick back-swipe wastes one request unless it is cancelled. The #134 jitter fix is unaffected because the apply stays gated.

Concurrent requests mean a models failure no longer skips the workspaces/commands fetches, which today are skipped (workspaces) or run anyway (commands). The error aggregation has to stay deliberate. Up to 3 requests are in flight at once on the same host, which HTTP/2 over the tunnel handles fine. No behavior change on LAN beyond negligible latency.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. Mechanism is certain from the code; a device trace is still the before/after gate.

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(chat): start the transcript request before the push transition finishes</summary>

Traced at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. ChatView `.task(id: didCompleteInitialAppearance)` (ChatView.swift:750) calls handleInitialAppearanceTask (L1739). The first pass only hydrates the draft and runs prepareInitialMessageLoad, which paints the SwiftData cache synchronously (ChatViewModel.swift:1608-1619). It then returns at the ChatInitialAppearancePolicy guard (ChatView.swift:1743, ChatScrollPolicy.swift:195). didCompleteInitialAppearance only flips in handleInitialAppearanceCompletion (ChatView.swift:2870), which NavigationAppearanceObserverViewController calls from the transition coordinator's completion block (ChatView.swift:82-98). Only then does performInitialAsyncWork call loadMessages, which awaits `client.session(... includeMessages: true, expandRenderable: true)` (ChatViewModel.swift:1435). So the GET is not sent until the push animation has finished. Transition time and network time add up instead of overlapping.

The gate came from #137 (fix for the #134 jitter, which is on the already-fixed list). Its own doc comments (ChatViewModel.swift:1604-1607, ChatScrollPolicy.swift:192-194) say the goal is to keep *rendering* the richer transcript out of the transition. Nothing in them requires delaying the *request*, so this is a real gap in that fix, not a regression of it. Sending the request early is safe: APIClient is an actor, so the request and the JSON decode run off the main thread; only applyReloadedMessages and reconcileSessionLoad touch UI state. The onAppear reconnectStreamIfNeeded (ChatView.swift:797) does not cover this, because it is a no-op on a cold open with no active stream.

Downgraded from the auditor's framing: most opens already paint the cached transcript at once. Launch restore always does, because the last-selected session was cached. On those opens the saving only makes fresh content and live-stream reattach arrive sooner. It is not a visible jank fix.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(chat): run the independent composer-config and approval requests concurrently on chat open</summary>

I traced ChatView.performInitialAsyncWork (ChatView.swift:1755). It awaits loadMessages, whose network leg is `client.session` at ChatViewModel.swift:1435. Next it awaits loadComposerConfiguration (L1767), then applyRestoredDraftSettingsIfNeeded, then refreshApprovalBypassState (L1775). That last call is itself two serial RTTs: sessionYolo, then approvalPending (ChatPendingActionCoordinator.swift:90 and :378). Inside ChatComposerConfigLoader.loadConfiguration every call is a plain `try await` in a row: profiles (L73), switchProfile when needed (L82), models (L104), reasoning (L117), workspaces (L125), commands (L136). Nothing is cached between chat opens. There are no async lets and no memoization. I checked the upstream handlers. /api/models, /api/workspaces and the switch are profile-scoped, and switch invalidates the models cache (routes.py:13923, 14285, 16842). So profiles and the optional switch must stay first. After that, models, workspaces and commands do not depend on each other. Reasoning needs only the resolved model/provider, which comes from models. Two parts of the claim are overstated. First, the model, workspace and profile chips are already filled from the session at init (ChatViewModel.swift:575-578), and the loader's loading flag is not read by any view. So the settle delay affects the reasoning-effort chip, supported efforts, slash commands and profile options, not all chips. The most user-visible cost is the pending-approval card and the YOLO state: they appear only after the whole chain, about 7 RTTs after the transcript fetch. Second, the per-server cache half of the proposal does not hold up. Models and workspaces are profile-scoped, so the cache would need a server+profile key, which raises multi-server isolation risk. Stale-while-revalidate also still sends every request. Running loadComposerConfiguration concurrently with loadMessages is also weak: loadMessages can overwrite currentProfile/model/workspace (L1734-1737), and the loader's equality guard (L840) would then throw away the finished result and run the whole chain again. On LAN (under 10 ms RTT) the gain is negligible. Over a Cloudflare tunnel it is real.

</details>

---

title: perf(bots): stop per-delta invalidation and full markdown re-render of the live bot reply
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Every `message.delta` frame mutates `liveActivity` even when nothing changed, invalidating BotChatView 30-50 times per second. The live reply also renders through the settled markdown path, re-parsing and re-highlighting the whole document on every snapshot and flooding the layout cache.

**perf(bots): skip the no-op liveActivity mutation so message.delta frames stop invalidating BotChatView**

The @Observable `_modify` accessor calls willSet/didSet unconditionally. Only the plain setter checks equality (verified with a local swiftc scratch program). Each message.delta frame goes into the mutating `liveActivity.apply`, which returns false without changing anything, but BotChatView is still invalidated. The screen body, the ForEach diff over the windowed transcript, the per-row activity filter, the toolbar and the composer body all re-run at the token frame rate. Nothing visible changes, because live reply text only arrives with the 250 ms snapshot.

- **Trigger:** Any Bot Chat reply streaming at a typical 30-60 tok/s. The gateway writes one WebSocket frame per token, with 33 ms send batching only. Cost grows with the windowed transcript (up to 50+ rows) and the settled activity blocks.
- **Impact (medium, per message.delta frame (per token) while a bot reply streams):** About 30-50 wasted full-screen body passes per second on the main actor for the whole reply, against the roughly 4 per second the snapshots need. Each pass is probably sub-millisecond to a few ms. That is steady main-thread and battery waste while streaming, and scrolling in long bot chats on older iPhones gets less headroom. It is not a freeze.

**perf(bots): render the live bot reply with the streaming markdown path**

The live Bot reply skips the streaming renderer that the Sessions transcript uses (from #291). On every snapshot the full reply string is: (1) inserted into the shared MarkdownMathLayoutCache; (2) parsed and laid out by MarkdownUI as one document, where stable-chunk splitting would let unchanged earlier blocks skip their diff; (3) re-highlighted on the main actor when it contains a fenced code block in a highlightable language, after first being reset to plain text, which can flicker.

- **Trigger:** A bot streams a long answer, for example 4k tokens (about 16 KB) containing one or two Swift or Python fenced blocks of about 100-150 lines, over 60-80 s.
- **Impact (medium, per bot snapshot (about 2-3.5 Hz) for the whole duration of a live bot reply):** Per-snapshot main-thread cost grows with reply length: a full MarkdownUI parse and layout of a document up to about 16 KB, plus Highlightr/JSContext on a code block of 100+ lines. At 2-3.5 Hz this causes scroll hitches and visible plain-to-highlighted flicker on long, code-heavy bot replies. A 60 s reply also adds about 150-200 cache entries, which evicts most of the 240-entry layout cache that settled Sessions and Bot rows rely on. Limited to the Bots surface and to snapshot rate, and short chatty replies barely notice, so scored medium, not high.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:550`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L550): default branch: `return liveActivity.apply(type:payload:)` runs _modify, so observers are notified even for message.delta, which apply ignores
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:1149`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L1149): observe() sends every sequenced frame through applyActivity
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:530`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L530): replay loop uses the same path (a one-off burst, not hot)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotActivity.swift:61`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotActivity.swift#L61): BotTurnActivity.handles(_:) exists but is never checked before mutating
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:68`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift#L68): body reads model.liveActivity.hasTurnWork, which registers the dependency
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:118`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift#L118): onChange(of: liveActivity.toolCalls.count) and line 119 reasoning.count are also evaluated in body
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:287`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift#L287): per-row settledActivity filter runs again on every wasted pass (minor)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:340`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift#L340): the composer takes closures, so its body re-runs on every parent pass
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactMessageView.swift:67`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactMessageView.swift#L67): `MarkdownRenderer(content: text)` with isStreaming defaulting to false, even when isLive
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactMessageView.swift:27`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactMessageView.swift#L27): the isLive branch renders the same assistantContent
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:75`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift#L75): the live reply row is mounted with isLive: true
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:603`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L603): each snapshot replaces live-assistant with the full inflight text
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:1197`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L1197): 250 ms coalescing sleep, then an RTT, then another 250 ms (L1210) while dirty: about 2-3.5 snapshots per second
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:54`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L54): the non-streaming path calls MarkdownMathLayoutCache.layout(for:), which stores every intermediate string
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift:332`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift#L332): shared NSCache countLimit is 240
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:526`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L526): resets highlightedCode to nil and yields, then highlights synchronously on main (Highlightr JSContext at L1147), with no result cache

## Fix sketch

**perf(bots): skip the no-op liveActivity mutation so message.delta frames stop invalidating BotChatView**

In applyActivity's default branch (BotConversation.swift:550): `guard BotTurnActivity.handles(type) else { return false }` before `return liveActivity.apply(type: type, payload: payload)`. Better still, move the guard to observe() and the replay loop too, so only consumed types touch liveActivity. Leave reasoning-delta coalescing and the settledActivity grouping out; they are not needed for the win.

**perf(bots): render the live bot reply with the streaming markdown path**

In BotArtifactMessageView.assistantContent, change line 67 to `MarkdownRenderer(content: text, isStreaming: isLive)`. That routes the live reply through StreamingMarkdownRenderer: uncachedLayout, stable chunks that skip their diff, and code blocks with isStreaming=true, which the highlight policy keeps plain until the reply settles. The settled row that replaces the live row keeps today's behavior (cached layout, highlighting, selection).

## Measurement plan

Add a unit test that tracks `model.liveActivity` with withObservationTracking, feeds a scripted message.delta through a fake BotTransport during a running turn, and asserts that onChange does not fire. It fires today. On device, record Instruments SwiftUI 'View Body' counts for BotChatView while a scripted 2k-token reply streams at about 50 tok/s. Expect roughly 30-50 per second before and about 4 per second (snapshot cadence) after.

Before and after: use a scripted fixture that drives BotConversation.applySnapshot at 3 Hz with a growing 16 KB markdown reply containing a 150-line Swift block. In Instruments (Time Profiler plus the SwiftUI template), compare main-thread ms per snapshot in MarkdownUI parse/layout and in Splash/Highlightr, and count hitches. Add a temporary counter on MarkdownMathLayoutCache setObject calls: expect about 200 inserts per 60 s reply before the change and 0 after.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unhandled activity types return early without touching `liveActivity` (live and replay paths).
- [ ] The live bot reply renders with `MarkdownRenderer(content:isStreaming: true)`; the settled row keeps highlighting and selection.
- [ ] `BotConversation` tests show no observable mutation for unhandled deltas.

## Tradeoffs and risk

None. handles() already lists exactly the types apply consumes. Keep them in sync (a test can assert that apply returns false for every type handles rejects).

The live reply picks up the streaming reveal fade on each snapshot chunk. It follows the existing streamed-text animation setting and Reduce Motion. Because snapshots arrive in bursts of about 250 ms, each fade covers a larger chunk. Code blocks stay plain until the reply settles, then highlight once. When the live row is swapped for the settled row, the linger-after-streaming fade handoff does not happen because the view identity changes. That matches how the swap already looks today.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(bots): skip the no-op liveActivity mutation so message.delta frames stop invalidating BotChatView</summary>

I traced the path and tested the macro. BotConversation is @Observable, and liveActivity is a tracked stored property (BotConversation.swift:75). applyActivity's default branch (line 550) calls the mutating `liveActivity.apply(...)`, which goes through the macro's `_modify` accessor. I compiled a scratch program with the local toolchain (scratch benchmark). In it, a no-op mutating call on a tracked struct property fired withObservationTracking's onChange once, so observers get notified even when nothing changed. observe() (line 1149) runs every sequenced frame through applyActivity. For message.delta, apply hits `default: return false` without changing anything, but the notification has already fired. No other state BotChatView reads changes on a message.delta during a running turn: `turn = .running` goes through the equality-checked setter, and `snapshotDirty` and `sequence` are not read by any view. BotChatView.body reads model.liveActivity (lines 68, 118, 119), so each delta invalidates the whole screen body. None of that work produces new pixels, because live assistant text only comes from the 250 ms coalesced snapshot (liveMessages). Upstream tui_gateway/ws.py coalesces tokens for only 33 ms, and send_many still writes one WebSocket frame per token. BotClient.consume calls onEvent once per frame on the main actor, so invalidations run at min(token rate, display refresh): about 30-50 per second for a 50 tok/s reply, against about 4 per second from snapshots. Some claimed costs are smaller than stated. BotArtifactMessageView rows take plain fields (ChatMessage plus a model reference), so SwiftUI probably skips their bodies when the messages array is unchanged. The per-pass cost is the parent body, the ForEach diff over up to 50+ windowed rows, the per-row settledActivity filter (about 50x100 id compares), the composer body (closures, so not skippable), and the toolbar avatar dictionary rebuild over a few entries. Each is minor on its own. The reasoning.count O(n) walks (BotActivity.swift:99, BotChatView.swift:119) only run on reasoning deltas, which really do change state, and cost about 30x a sub-0.1 ms walk per second. I'd call those micro-optimizations, not the finding. The real waste is the no-op invalidation on every message.delta.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(bots): render the live bot reply with the streaming markdown path</summary>

Checked at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. BotChatView.swift:74-75 renders the in-flight reply as `BotArtifactMessageView(isLive: true)`. Its `assistantContent` (BotArtifactMessageView.swift:67) calls `MarkdownRenderer(content: text)`, so `isStreaming` stays false even for the live reply. That sends the live reply down the settled path. `MarkdownMathLayoutCache.layout(for:)` (MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift:341-353) writes a new NSCache entry keyed by the full string on every snapshot, and the cache is shared with a 240-entry limit (L332). The cache's own doc comment (L356-361) says streaming text must use `uncachedLayout` to avoid exactly this eviction. The whole reply goes to one `ChatMarkdownView`, so MarkdownUI re-parses and re-lays out the full document each time, instead of letting the unchanged stable chunks from StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter skip their diff. `ChatCodeBlock` runs `.task(id: highlightRequest)` with isStreaming=false (MarkdownRenderer.swift:476, 515-521). `updateHighlightedCode` sets `highlightedCode = nil` and yields, then highlights synchronously on the main actor through Splash or Highlightr/JSContext (L524-536, L1147). Nothing caches that result, so the growing code block is re-highlighted on each snapshot and can show one plain frame in between. The cadence is real but lower than per token: BotConversation.scheduleRefresh sleeps 250 ms (L1197), awaits a session.resume round trip, applies it, then sleeps 250 ms again while still dirty (L1210). That comes to about 2-3.5 snapshots per second. Each one replaces the `live-assistant` message with the full in-flight text (L602-603). Nothing upstream skips this: the content really does change on every snapshot. Scope: this only affects the Bots surface, and the cadence is snapshot-rate, not token-rate. So I scored it medium rather than high. It is still clearly visible on long, code-heavy bot replies.

</details>

## Related

- #564 (bot chat streaming fade parity).

title: perf(chat): cache per-message media and link scans so Send and done don't rescan every row
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

The action-menu flags (`hasActiveStream`, regenerate/edit/fork) are part of every row's equality, so Send and done invalidate all rows. Each assistant bubble then re-runs an uncached media parse and an NSDataDetector link scan, about 25-75 ms of main-thread work on a full page, right during the send animation.

The action-menu flags are transcript-global but sit in every row's Equatable inputs. When a stream starts on Send and ends on done, every row fails equality. Each MessageBubbleView body then re-runs because its closure inputs are new, which repeats uncached per-message text scans: the media-segment parse and first-URL detection with NSDataDetector. The tool-activity groups probably do not re-run, because their value inputs share storage with the cached lookup.

- **Trigger:** Tapping Send, or a reply finishing, in a session with a full 50-message page (about 25 assistant replies of about 2k characters each). A TTS toggle or a regenerate/edit/fork start also triggers it.
- **Impact (medium, About twice per turn (send and done), plus rare action-flag flips):** Estimated 25-75 ms of main-thread work at two moments per turn, and it lands during the send insert animation. That means a few dropped frames on long pages, not continuous jank. It scales with 'Load older'.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:301`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L301): hasActiveStream plus listening/cached/regenerate/edit/fork flags go to every row unscoped (lines 299-315)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:588`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L588): the flags are part of the Equatable check, so flipping one fails .equatable() (:321) for all rows
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:833`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L833): actionMenu is the real consumer of the global flags
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift:151`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift#L151): TranscriptMediaParser.segments runs on every assistant bubble body, uncached
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift:343`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift#L343): linkPreview calls previewURL; user rows compute it twice (hasLinkPreview at :350)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLinkPreview.swift:48`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLinkPreview.swift#L48): NSDataDetector.matches per non-code line segment; a message with no URL scans every line
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLinkPreview.swift:100`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptLinkPreview.swift#L100): regex range(of:) per line in shouldSkipLine
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMedia.swift:141`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMedia.swift#L141): per-character scan with three Substring hasPrefix checks

## Fix sketch

Smallest fix: memoize the two pure scans by content. Add a main-actor NSCache keyed by message content (plus workspaceRoot for segments) in front of TranscriptLinkPreviewEligibility.previewURL and TranscriptMediaParser.segments. Skip the cache when isStreaming, so partial streaming content never enters it. Also compute previewURL once per userMessageRow body instead of twice. That makes a transcript-wide re-evaluation cheap and also speeds up first open. Optionally, as a follow-up, make hasActiveStream and the regenerate/edit/fork/listening flags one Equatable environment value, read only by ChatMessageMetaRow's menu and the user context-menu leaf. That removes the flags from ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.== so rows stop re-evaluating at all. Do not move tool-call entry computation; it is not on this path.

## Measurement plan

Add os_signpost intervals around MessageBubbleView.assistantMessageRow's segments call and around TranscriptLinkPreviewExtractor.firstWebURL. On a device, open a session with a full 50-message page and record one Send-to-done cycle with the SwiftUI and os_signpost instruments. Before: expect about 2x(rows) firstWebURL/segments intervals, with total main-thread time around 25-75 ms per event. After: about 0 intervals on the send/done events apart from the streaming row, and no hitch in the Hangs/Hitches lane during the insert animation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TranscriptMediaParser.segments` and `previewURL` are memoized by content (NSCache), skipping streaming content.
- [ ] User rows compute `previewURL` once per body.
- [ ] Signposts on a 50-message page show ~0 scans on Send/done beyond the streaming row.

## Tradeoffs and risk

The cache costs a little memory: two small values per message, bounded by NSCache. Content keys can be large strings; hashing a 2k-character string is still far cheaper than NSDataDetector. The environment-flag follow-up touches the user context-menu path, so disabled states must still update live.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Traced at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The core claim holds. ChatTranscriptView.swift:301-315 passes hasActiveStream (activeStreamID != nil), listeningMessageID, isViewingCachedData and isRegenerating/Editing/Forking into every ChatTranscriptMessageBlock unscoped. They are part of its == at :585-590, so when activeStreamID goes nil to non-nil on Send and back on done, `.equatable()` (:321) fails for every row. The per-message cost that follows is not cached. ChatTranscriptMessageRow passes fresh closures and a rebuilt contextMenuActions array to MessageBubbleView, so its body re-runs. For a non-streaming assistant row, assistantMessageRow (MessageBubbleView.swift:151) re-runs TranscriptMediaParser.segments, which walks every character with three Substring hasPrefix checks (TranscriptMedia.swift:141-240). linkPreview (:343, and a second time via hasLinkPreview at :350 for user rows) re-runs TranscriptLinkPreviewExtractor.firstWebURL. For a message with no URL, which is most of them, that runs a regex range(of:) per line (TranscriptLinkPreview.swift:100) plus NSDataDetector.matches on every non-code line segment (:48) with no early exit. Where the claim is weaker: (1) Magnitude is bounded. messagePageLimit is 50 (ChatViewModel.swift:201), so a normal open shows about 20-50 rendered rows, not 150. The cost only grows after 'Load older'. (2) It fires about twice per turn (send and done), plus rarely on TTS toggles and regenerate/edit/fork. It does not fire per token: during a stream the flags are stable and non-streaming rows still skip. (3) The tool-call part is likely wrong. ToolActivityGroupView takes only value inputs (group, isLive). Its groups come from the cached completedToolCallGroupLookup (ChatViewModel.swift:272-274), which shares storage, so SwiftUI's field compare should skip its body. The ToolCallSummaryFormatter JSON decoding and per-call NSRegularExpression (ToolCallSummaryFormatter.swift:339) are therefore not re-run by this trigger; they only cost on first build. (4) MarkdownRenderer's parse is already cached (#260), and it takes value inputs, so it is likely skipped too. Rough estimate: 25 assistant rows of about 2k characters and 30 lines each cost about 1-3 ms per row on an iPhone, so 25-75 ms of main-thread work lands right on the send insert animation and on reply completion. That is a real, possibly visible hitch, but it needs Instruments to confirm, hence PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED.

</details>

title: perf(chat): highlight code off the main actor and cache the result
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Highlightr runs highlight.js in a JSContext on the main actor, once per code block mount, with no result cache. Opening a code-heavy session queues many main-thread jobs (the first also loads the JSContext), and every finished reply re-highlights all its blocks and flashes plain text.

highlight.js runs inside JavaScriptCore on the main actor, followed by Highlightr's fastRender HTML-to-NSAttributedString pass. There is one task per code block, so opening a session queues N back-to-back main-thread jobs, and the first one also pays for JSContext initialization with the full highlight.js bundle evaluated. Nothing is cached by content, so any remount of a block repeats the work and briefly shows plain text. Remounts happen on reopen, on the end-of-stream swap from StreamingMarkdownRenderer to the settled renderer, on row identity changes, and on appearance changes.

- **Trigger:** Opening a coding session whose loaded window holds ~20-30 fenced blocks in python/ts/bash/json of 30-300 lines each. Also the end of every assistant reply that contains code blocks, because the settled swap re-highlights all of them.
- **Impact (medium, Per session open with code blocks; per completed reply containing code blocks; the JSContext init once per launch and appearance):** On a cold launch the first highlighted block pays a one-time JSContext and highlight.js load on main (likely tens of ms or more). After that, each block probably costs a few ms to low tens of ms on main, issued back-to-back during the initial scroll or settle. That plausibly drops frames when a code-heavy session opens. At the end of each code-bearing reply, every block flashes plain then highlighted. The flash is visible, but it is not a stall for short replies. Light sessions without code are unaffected.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:476`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L476): per-block `.task(id: highlightRequest)`; runs on every ChatCodeBlock mount
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:525`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L525): @MainActor: set nil, Task.yield, then synchronous highlight on main (L531)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:1089`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L1089): MarkdownCodeHighlighter.highlightedCode is @MainActor, with no cache
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:1134`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L1134): StableHighlightrStore is @MainActor; the first Highlightr() (L1157) loads highlight.js into a JSContext on main
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:26`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L26): streaming→settled swap remounts ChatMarkdownView, so every code block in the reply re-highlights, with a plain frame first
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:186`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L186): stable chunks mid-stream already highlight (isStreaming:false), so the final swap duplicates that work
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:256`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift#L256): eager VStack: every code block in the loaded window mounts and highlights on open
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/SourceViewer/SourceHighlighter.swift:41`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/SourceViewer/SourceHighlighter.swift#L41): existing precedent: an actor-owned Highlightr pair, off main (a second JSContext pair)

## Fix sketch

1) Turn StableHighlightrStore into an `actor`, like SourceHighlighter, and add `NSCache<NSString, NSAttributedString>` keyed by `"\(scheme)|\(language)|\(code)"`, or by a hash plus length. Keep the Splash path on it too. 2) In ChatCodeBlock, add a synchronous `@MainActor` cache peek. Seed `highlightedCode` from it in `.task` before any reset, and skip `highlightedCode = nil` when the peek hits. Settled-swap remounts and reopens then render highlighted on the first frame. 3) On a miss, `await` the actor, then check `Task.isCancelled` and that the request is unchanged before assigning. Optional follow-up, only if memory shows it matters: let SourceHighlighter and the chat store share one Highlightr pair.

## Measurement plan

Before and after, on a device, in Instruments Time Profiler and the Hitches instrument. (a) Cold-launch a session with 25 highlighted fenced blocks and record main-thread time under JSContext/Highlightr frames and the hitch count during the first 2 s. (b) Stream a reply that ends with 3 code blocks and record main-thread highlighting time at the settle swap, plus whether a plain-text frame appears (screen recording). Add an os_signpost interval around MarkdownCodeHighlighter.highlightedCode. Expected: main-thread highlighting time near zero, and no plain frame on reopen or settle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The chat highlighter is an actor (like `SourceHighlighter`) with an NSCache keyed by scheme, language, and code.
- [ ] A synchronous cache peek seeds settled and reopened blocks, so they render highlighted on the first frame.
- [ ] Cancelled or stale highlight results are never assigned.
- [ ] Time Profiler shows no Highlightr/JSContext frames on the main thread when opening a 25-block session.

## Tradeoffs and risk

The cache holds NSAttributedStrings, which are bounded by NSCache and evicted under memory pressure, so memory cost is small. Moving work off main means a cache miss still shows a plain frame before the highlighted one, as it does today. NSAttributedString crossing the actor boundary isn't Sendable-clean, but under Swift 5 mode with targeted concurrency this is at most a warning. Freezing the result with `copy()` avoids aliasing.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Checked at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The claim holds. MarkdownCodeHighlighter.highlightedCode (MarkdownRenderer.swift:1089-1118) is @MainActor, and so is StableHighlightrStore (L1134). Every settled ChatCodeBlock runs `.task(id: highlightRequest)` (L476), which yields once and then highlights synchronously on main (L525-531). There is no result cache anywhere, only the two Highlightr instances. The first Highlightr() call (L1157) evaluates the highlight.js bundle in a JSContext on main. The transcript's outer stack is an eager VStack (ChatTranscriptView.swift:256), so every code block in the loaded window mounts and highlights when a session opens. Nothing is skipped: streaming blocks return .plain before any work (L930). But stable chunks mid-stream are highlighted (isStreaming:false at L186-190), and after the ~linger delay MarkdownRenderer swaps StreamingMarkdownRenderer for markdownContent (L26-37). That builds fresh ChatCodeBlock instances with nil @State, so every block in a finished reply is highlighted a second time and shows a plain frame first. The codebase already has the off-main pattern: SourceHighlighter is an `actor` owning its own Highlightr pair (Features/Workspace/SourceViewer/SourceHighlighter.swift:41-66). That makes two JSContexts where one would do. Two parts of the claim do not hold. Resetting to nil at L526 adds no pop on first appear, because the state is already nil then. The pop is real only on the streaming-to-settled swap and on color-scheme changes. Rebuilding the Splash theme per call (L1123-1130) is a micro-cost and only matters for `swift` fences. How big this is depends on highlight.js speed on device, which I did not profile, so the verdict is PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED.

</details>

title: perf(share): map shared files instead of holding every attachment in extension memory
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

The share extension loads each shared attachment fully into memory (`Data(contentsOf:)` / `loadDataRepresentation`) before staging it, so a multi-document share can exceed the extension's memory ceiling and fail silently.

The extension's peak footprint is roughly the sum of the accepted attachments' bytes, all dirty malloc memory from unmapped reads, plus any single oversized image/PDF that loadDataRepresentation loads before rejecting it. Share extensions have about a 120 MB jetsam ceiling. On the app side, reserving the import reads every staged file on the main actor while the scene is activating.

- **Trigger:** Sharing several large items in one go, for example 6-10 scanned PDFs of 10-20 MB from Files, or large PNG/JPEG exports. A single ProRAW/DNG (~75 MB) is loaded fully before the extension rejects it. Ten ordinary 24 MP HEIC photos (~30-50 MB total) don't trigger it.
- **Impact (medium, once per share action; rare for large aggregates):** When it triggers, jetsam kills the extension and the share fails silently. That is a severe outcome, but it only happens in heavy multi-document shares, not typical photo or text shares. The app-side hitch is one-time per share: about 25-50 ms at 50 MB, and 100+ ms only near the 150-200 MB worst case.

## Evidence

- [`HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift:32`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift#L32): every accepted attachment's Data is accumulated in ShareInput before anything is written
- [`HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift:158`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift#L158): unmapped Data(contentsOf:) of each file-URL item (after the 20 MB size check at :153)
- [`HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift:133`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift#L133): loadDataRepresentation loads the full image/PDF payload before the 20 MB check at :134
- [`HermesShareExtension/ShareViewController.swift:63`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesShareExtension/ShareViewController.swift#L63): savePendingImport (SHA-256 plus atomic writes) runs on the @MainActor controller; costs CPU only, no extra copy
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:395`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift#L395): each attachment is written from its in-memory Data
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:620`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift#L620): contentID hashes every attachment's full Data (no copy)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:557`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift#L557): main app: loadAttachments reads every staged file fully with an unmapped Data(contentsOf:)
- [`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:208`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/ContentView.swift#L208): main app: reserveNextPendingImport, and so every attachment read, runs synchronously on main during share handoff

## Fix sketch

Smallest change, no model change: (1) ShareInputReader.swift:158: use `Data(contentsOf: url, options: .alwaysMapped)`. File-backed clean pages are not charged to the extension's footprint, and the mapping outlives stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource. (2) Replace loadDataRepresentation at :250 with `loadFileRepresentation(forTypeIdentifier:)`. Inside the completion handler, check the file size against maximumSharedAttachmentBytes before reading, then read it mapped. The mapping survives the provider deleting the temp file. Oversized items are then never materialized. (3) SharedDraftStore.loadAttachments (:557, and loadLegacyAttachments :587): read with `.alwaysMapped`, so reserveNextPendingImport on main only maps files. Page faults move to upload time, where the bytes are needed anyway. hashing (:633) and the write (:395) work on mapped Data unchanged. Keep SharedAttachmentImport as Data. The URL-based refactor isn't needed.

## Measurement plan

On device, use Instruments Allocations plus VM Tracker (phys_footprint) on the HermesShareExtension process. Share 8 x 15 MB PDFs from Files, and separately one ~75 MB ProRAW from Photos. Before: peak footprint should be about 120-140 MB or a jetsam in the device log (JetsamEvent). After: expected peak under 40 MB. For the app side, add an os_signpost around ContentView.importPendingSharedDraftIfAvailable and use the Hangs/Time Profiler instrument on return from the share. Before: tens to 100+ ms on main for a 100+ MB import. After: a few ms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] File reads use `.alwaysMapped`; provider loads use `loadFileRepresentation` with a size check before reading.
- [ ] Existing share staging tests pass; a manual share of several large PDFs succeeds on device.
- [ ] Memory graph during a 150 MB multi-file share stays well under the extension ceiling.

## Tradeoffs and risk

Mapped Data faults pages in lazily, so a file that becomes unreadable between reservation and upload surfaces as a SIGBUS rather than a thrown error. The risk is low because the reservation keeps the files in place until consume, and an unlinked but mapped inode stays valid. loadFileRepresentation doesn't cover providers that only vend in-memory data. Keep loadDataRepresentation as a fallback for those, and they are usually small. The hash and write still run on the extension's main actor. That isn't user-visible, so moving them off main is optional.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The core claim holds. ShareInputReader.input(from:) (HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift:21-38) loads providers one at a time and appends each SharedAttachmentImport, which holds a full Data, to input.attachments. Nothing is written until every provider has loaded. File-URL items are read with an unmapped Data(contentsOf:) at :158. The size check at :153 does happen before that read, so each file is capped at 20 MB. Image and PDF providers go through loadDataRepresentation at :133/:250. That path materializes the whole payload before the 20 MB check at :134, so an oversized ProRAW or large PDF is fully loaded only to be rejected. The activation rule allows 10 files plus 10 images (Info.plist), and the reader caps accepted attachments at 10 (SharedDraftStore.swift:92-93). The worst case is therefore about 200 MB resident against the roughly 120 MB share-extension ceiling. Hashing and writing (SharedDraftStore.swift:620-631, :395) run inside savePendingImport, which the @MainActor controller calls at ShareViewController.swift:63. They don't copy the Data again, so they add CPU time but no extra memory. The extension's view is a hidden label, so the main-thread block there doesn't cause visible jank. I scaled the claim back in three ways. (1) Typical shares are small. Ten 24 MP HEIC photos, the default capture on current iPhones, total roughly 30-50 MB, well under the ceiling. Hitting jetsam needs more than about 100 MB in aggregate, for example 6+ large scanned PDFs or big PNG/JPEG exports, so this is a heavier-use edge case, not a typical one. (2) On the app side, ChatView.uploadInitialAttachmentsIfNeeded (ChatView.swift:2397-2410) passes attachment.data to viewModel.uploadAttachment, so the bytes are needed eventually anyway. The only real waste in the app is doing the read synchronously on main. reserveNextPendingImport -> loadImport -> loadAttachments (SharedDraftStore.swift:174-231, 537-573) runs from ContentView.importPendingSharedDraftIfAvailable (ContentView.swift:193-213), which is reached from .task, onOpenURL and scenePhase .active. It only reads attachment bytes when a share is actually pending. That costs about 25-50 ms for 50 MB with a warm page cache, and approaches 100+ ms only at 150-200 MB. It is a one-time hitch per share handoff. (3) The app has no jetsam risk at these sizes. Magnitude depends on the real extension ceiling and XPC transfer behavior, so it needs on-device measurement. Hence PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED.

</details>

title: perf(kanban): keep the event stream across .inactive and resume from the cursor
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Any `.inactive` phase (Control Center, a notification banner pull, the app switcher) tears down the Kanban stream, and foregrounding runs four serial requests plus a full Board payload and re-render, blocking mutations for about four round trips.

Notification Center, Control Center, system alerts, Face ID prompts, and the app switcher all send .inactive and then .active. Each round trip tears down the Kanban SSE stream. It then runs four GETs in sequence, including the complete board payload with every Card row and its link and comment counts, reassigns snapshot (which invalidates the whole board view), and reconnects the SSE stream, even when no event was written in between. The server's since-cursor would answer the no-change case with a roughly 60-byte envelope.

- **Trigger:** Kanban screen visible while the user pulls down Notification Center or Control Center, gets a system alert, or briefly opens the app switcher
- **Impact (medium, Every .inactive to .active transition while Kanban is visible, several times per session for heavy Kanban users):** Each glance costs 4 serial requests, a full board payload (tens to hundreds of KB for 100-300 Cards), an SSE teardown and reconnect, and a full board re-render. Mutations are gated off while isRefreshing is true, which over a tunnel is roughly 4 RTTs. Limited to users who keep Kanban open.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:254`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L254): onChange(of: scenePhase) sends every phase change to updateSceneActivity
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:323`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L323): isActive = phase == .active, so .inactive suspends
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:1356`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L1356): setSceneActive: false calls suspendLiveUpdates; true runs boards GET, full board GET, stats, assignees, then retryLiveStream
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:1375`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L1375): refreshBoard(usingCursor: false, refreshSupplementary: true) on every return to .active
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2340`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2340): changed == false branch is dead: no caller passes usingCursor: true
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2543`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2543): suspendLiveUpdates stops the SSE client and cancels in-flight loads

## Fix sketch

1) KanbanLabView.updateSceneActivity: suspend only on .background. Ignore .inactive (`guard phase != .inactive else { return }`) so the stream survives transient overlays. 2) In setSceneActive(true): call refreshBoard(usingCursor: true, refreshSupplementary: false) first. Run reconcileBoardCollection and loadSupplementaryReads only when the response had changed != false (have refreshBoard return whether the snapshot changed, or check liveCursor movement). Keep the full usingCursor: false path for pull-to-refresh, offline recovery, filter changes, and mutation reconciliation.

## Measurement plan

Network instrument or URLProtocol request log with Kanban open on a 200-300 Card board over a tunnel. Pull Notification Center down and back up 5 times. Before: 20 GETs (boards, board, stats, assignees x5) plus 5 SSE reconnects. After: 0 requests and no reconnect. After a real background/foreground with no Card changes: 1 cursor GET (about 60 B response) plus 1 SSE reconnect, and no snapshot reassignment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The stream is suspended only on `.background`.
- [ ] Foreground refresh uses the since-cursor first and runs Board-collection and supplementary reads only when the snapshot changed.
- [ ] `KanbanFeatureStateTests` cover inactive-then-active without a full reload.

## Tradeoffs and risk

A Card change that writes no task_event would be missed by the cursor check until the next event or a pull-to-refresh. Board-list changes (a board added or renamed elsewhere) would not show on foreground unless boards is still fetched. Keeping the SSE open during .inactive holds a socket slightly longer, but iOS suspends it at .background anyway.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. Mechanism is certain from the code; a device trace is still the before/after gate.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Traced at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. KanbanLabView.updateSceneActivity (KanbanLabView.swift:322-325) maps any phase other than .active to setSceneActive(false), so .inactive counts as inactive. setSceneActive(false) (KanbanFeatureState.swift:1356-1362) calls suspendLiveUpdates (2543-2553). That stops the SSE stream, bumps liveGeneration, and invalidates activeBoardLoadID. On .active it runs reconcileBoardCollection (GET boards, 2147/2158), then refreshBoard(usingCursor: false, refreshSupplementary: true) (1375-1379). That is a full board GET plus stats and assignees GETs in sequence (2607-2631), then retryLiveStream opens a new SSE connection. Every refreshBoard caller passes usingCursor: false (1007, 1053, 1328, 1376, 1404-1428, 1532, 1621, 2476, 2515), so the changed == false branch at 2340 never runs. Upstream kanban_bridge.py:220-222 returns {changed:false, latest_event_id} when since >= latest_event_id, so the cheap check exists. KanbanBoardRequest already carries `since` (Models/Kanban.swift:232). The reconnected stream already resumes from liveCursor (2388-2389), so events missed during a brief .inactive would be replayed anyway. Nothing here is debounced or cached. isRefreshing = true (2321) also blocks the actions gated at 436/1079 and shows the refreshing state (1092) for four RTTs on every glance. Impact is medium, not high: this only affects users who keep Kanban open, and on LAN the four GETs are cheap. It gets noticeable over a Cloudflare tunnel with a board of hundreds of Cards.

</details>

---
