title: perf(kanban): make live reconciles quiet: no Refreshing row, no per-burst stats requests
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Each live event burst inserts a 'Refreshing Board' row at the top of the list (a visible jump and spinner while reading) and fires stats and assignees GETs that nothing on screen needs. The debounce also cancels in-flight board refreshes.

**perf(kanban): stop inserting the Refreshing Board row on background reconciles**

Every background reconcile flips isRefreshing true, then false 0.3-1 s later. cardList adds a spinner row above all cards and then removes it, so the List does an animated insert and delete, every card moves down about one row and back, and an indeterminate spinner runs for the length of the refresh. The view's structure changes even when no Card moved.

- **Trigger:** Kanban open on a Board where agents are working: each debounced burst of events (claim, comment, status change) or each mutation reconcile. Also pull-to-refresh, where the native .refreshable spinner already covers progress.
- **Impact (medium, Once per debounced live event burst (can be every few seconds on an active Board); once per mutation reconcile):** Visible list jump and a spinner flash on every live burst while the user reads or scrolls a busy Board, plus one extra full-body pass per burst. Idle Boards are unaffected.

**perf(kanban): drop per-burst stats/assignees GETs and stop cancelling in-flight live refreshes**

Each SSE events frame (after a 300 ms debounce) runs a full board GET, which the contract requires. Two more serial round trips follow on every burst: GET stats, whose result nothing renders, and GET assignees. On top of that, a frame that arrives while the board GET is in flight cancels it and starts over, so on a busy Board refreshes can keep getting pushed back and partial downloads are wasted.

- **Trigger:** The Kanban Board is visible while the Dispatcher runs workers. Claim, heartbeat, comment, and complete events each write task_events rows, which gives a few to about 20 bursts per minute. The Board holds 50-300 Cards.
- **Impact (low, per events burst while the Board is visible (at most about 3/s, realistically a few per minute)):** Each burst adds two small JSON round trips (tens to hundreds of ms each over a tunnel), which keeps the radio awake longer, plus occasional wasted and delayed board fetches. The full-board GET that dominates the bytes is inherent to the upstream contract, and upstream's web UI does the same. Kanban is a niche surface, and the Card-detail refetch claimed by the auditor does not happen.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2321`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2321): isRefreshing = true on every refreshBoard, including live, poll, and mutation reconciles
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2326`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2326): cleared only after board + stats + assignees reads (3 serial round trips)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2476`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2476): live SSE burst -> coalesced (300 ms debounce) refreshBoard(refreshSupplementary: true)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2515`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2515): poll path after offline recovery -> refreshBoard
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:1092`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L1092): ProgressView('Refreshing Board') row inserted at List index 0 whenever isRefreshing, then removed
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:1101`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L1101): already handles the snapshot == nil (initial/selectBoard) case separately
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:1239`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L1239): row menus disabled while refreshing via canMutateCard -> canUseServerAuthoritativeActions (:436 in KanbanFeatureState); deliberate gating, not the perf issue
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2607`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2607): loadSupplementaryReads: serial stats GET (2609), then assignees GET (2620)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:341`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L341): `stats` is stored but no view reads it (only tests assert on it)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:592`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L592): profileOptions already merges snapshot.assignees and each Card's assignee, so a per-burst assignee-history refresh adds little
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift:2472`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift#L2472): coalescingTask?.cancel() also cancels a refresh already in flight, not only the pending sleep
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:246`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift#L246): Refutes the detail sub-claim: onDisappear on push calls setVisible(false), which suspends live updates while a Card detail is open

## Fix sketch

**perf(kanban): stop inserting the Refreshing Board row on background reconciles**

In KanbanLabView.cardList, show the progress row only when there is no snapshot yet: change `if model.isRefreshing {` (line 1092) to `if model.isRefreshing, model.snapshot == nil {`. After a Board switch or first load, where snapshot is nil, the loading row still appears. Live, poll, mutation, and pull-to-refresh reconciles no longer insert a row, and pull-to-refresh keeps its native spinner. Leave isRefreshing and the write gating as they are, since that gating is a deliberate policy call. If the maintainer later wants the extra body pass gone as well, split the flag into a user-visible indicator and a write-gate flag, but that is a separate decision.

**perf(kanban): drop per-burst stats/assignees GETs and stop cancelling in-flight live refreshes**

(1) In scheduleCoalescedReconciliation (KanbanFeatureState.swift:2476), call refreshBoard(usingCursor: false) without refreshSupplementary. Keep the supplementary reads on initial load, pull-to-refresh, scene activation (1053), and offline recovery (2515). Optionally remove the stats fetch entirely, since nothing reads `stats`. (2) Split the debounce from the fetch: only cancel the task while it is still in its sleep phase. If a refresh is already running, set an @ObservationIgnored `needsLiveRefresh = true` and have the running task loop once more after it finishes, instead of cancelling and restarting.

## Measurement plan

On a simulator with KanbanLab's scripted live fixture sending an event burst every 2 s, record Core Animation commits or the SwiftUI template for 30 s. Before: one List insert and one delete per burst, a spinner layer, and the card rows' frames moving by about 44 pt. After: no List insert or delete, card frames stay still, and the body count for KanbanStatusFocusView drops by at least the insert/remove passes.

Use the existing recording mock in KanbanFeatureStateTests (recordedCalls includes .stats). Drive 5 scripted events frames, and assert before: 5x board + 5x stats + 5x assignees; after: board calls only (<= 5) and 0 stats/assignees. Add a case where a frame lands while the board fetch is suspended and assert the in-flight call completes and exactly one follow-up board GET runs. On device: count requests in the Instruments Network template over 2 minutes with a running Dispatcher; expect about 3x fewer requests per burst.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The progress row shows only when there is no snapshot.
- [ ] Coalesced live reconciles fetch only the Board; supplementary reads stay on initial load, pull, foreground, and offline recovery.
- [ ] A refresh already in flight is not cancelled by a new burst; a follow-up refresh is queued instead.

## Tradeoffs and risk

While a background refresh runs, users get no in-list sign that data is refreshing. The Live updates delayed and offline banners still cover degraded states, and menus still grey out during a refresh, so there is still some signal. It is a one-line change and needs no change to the policy in docs/agents/kanban.md.

Assignee history from known_assignees (profiles that appear only in past history, not on current Cards) refreshes only on load, explicit refresh, and foreground rather than live. The follow-up-pass logic adds a small state flag to reason about, and it must be reset in suspendLiveUpdates.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. Mechanism is certain from the code; a device trace is still the before/after gate.

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(kanban): stop inserting the Refreshing Board row on background reconciles</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. refreshBoard (KanbanFeatureState.swift:2313) sets isRefreshing = true at :2321 on every call, and the defer at :2326 clears it only after the board GET and, when refreshSupplementary is true, the serial kanbanStats and kanbanAssignees reads (:2607-2631). Background paths reach it with refreshSupplementary: true: live SSE bursts through scheduleCoalescedReconciliation (:2476, a 300 ms trailing debounce), the 30 s poll after an offline recovery (:2515), and every mutation reconcile (:1532, :1621). cardList (KanbanLabView.swift:1090-1099) inserts a 'Refreshing Board' ProgressView row at the top of the List whenever isRefreshing is true, then removes it about three round trips later. Over a tunnel that is roughly 0.3-1 s. Each live burst therefore inserts and removes a list row, shifting every card down about 44 pt and back, and runs a spinner, even though nothing in the list's structure changed. The claimed body-pass cost is overstated. Only the isRefreshing = true write, which lands in its own main-actor turn before the first await, adds a pass. The false write coalesces with the assignees write. Snapshot, stats, and assignees would invalidate the view anyway. So it is about 1 extra pass per burst, not 5. On iOS 26 (Swift 6.2 Observation), writing an unchanged Equatable value does not notify observers. The menu greying is real: .disabled at KanbanLabView.swift:1239 goes through canMutateCard -> canUseCardWorkflow -> canUseServerAuthoritativeActions (:436), which checks !isRefreshing. But that write gating is deliberate safety policy, not waste. The perf and jank part that holds up is the row insert and remove on every background reconcile. How often it happens depends on Board activity: one per debounced event burst while agents are claiming, commenting on, or completing Cards. Idle boards send only keepalive comments, which trigger nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(kanban): drop per-burst stats/assignees GETs and stop cancelling in-flight live refreshes</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. Parts of the claim hold, but the headline magnitude and the detail-refetch part do not. (1) CONFIRMED waste: every coalesced events burst runs refreshBoard(usingCursor:false, refreshSupplementary:true) at KanbanFeatureState.swift:2476, which then runs a stats GET (2609) and an assignees GET (2620) one after the other. `stats` (declared at 341) has no reader in any view. Grep finds only assignments and XCTAssertNotNil in the tests. The per-burst assignee refresh is close to redundant too: profileOptions (592-599) already merges snapshot.assignees and each card's assignee from the fresh board. (2) CONFIRMED cancel: the debounce at 2472 cancels a coalescingTask that may already be inside refreshBoard, which throws away an in-flight board download. Upstream frames can arrive every 0.3 s (kanban_bridge _KANBAN_SSE_POLL_SECONDS), so a busy Dispatcher can keep pushing the refresh back. (3) REFUTED, the detail refetch: KanbanCardDetailView is pushed through .navigationDestination (KanbanLabView.swift:203). The board root's .onDisappear (KanbanLabView.swift:246) then calls setVisible(false), which calls suspendLiveUpdates (KanbanFeatureState.swift:1346-1353, 2543), and handleStreamFrame and scheduleCoalescedReconciliation both gate on isVisible. So no stream bursts, and no snapshot-driven detailRefreshRevision bumps, arrive while a Card detail is open. The remaining bumps come from mutations. The Picker-over-allCards re-render claim fails for the same reason. (4) The full board GET per burst is the design: the upstream board endpoint has no per-card delta ('since' only returns changed:false). Upstream's own web UI does the same full loadKanban plus stats on every events frame, debounced at 250 ms (static/panels.js). Scoping by task_id would need patching the board from detail payloads, and recompute_ready side effects on dependent Cards make that a contract-level redesign, not a perf fix. The 'several MB/min' figure assumes a 300-Card Board with an active 8-worker Dispatcher. That is not typical for Kanban, which is a niche surface. Measured honestly, the waste is two small serial round trips per burst plus possible refresh starvation.

</details>

title: perf(bots): stop rewriting the Bot history file on cursor-only room polls
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Every 2 s room poll rewrites and re-encodes the whole Bot history index (1-8 MB), even when only the cursor moved. A 5-minute run writes 150-1,200 MB to flash and delays each room update by the encode time.

A working room produces many non-message events (tool and status), and each one advances the cursor. `appendRoom` treats a cursor-only change as a real change, so each advancing poll JSON-encodes the whole snapshot array twice (the budget check in prune, then persist) and atomically rewrites the whole file. `readPages` awaits this before returning, so new room messages are published only after the encodes and the write finish.

- **Trigger:** A group room in the working state for several minutes, with members emitting tool or status events. Worst case is a user whose Bot history index is 2-8 MB (several bots or rooms with hundreds of messages each).
- **Impact (medium, Every 2 s poll that advances the cursor while a room is working. Bot chats: a few times per turn (not hot).):** Off the main thread, so no dropped frames. For a room working 5 minutes that is about 150 polls. With a typical 1-2 MB index, that is about 300 full encodes and 150-300 MB of flash writes. Near the 8 MB cap it is about 1.2 GB of writes, and roughly 100-300 ms of encode per poll delays each room update by the same amount. Battery and write volume are real but not dramatic for typical users; the delay is only visible for heavy users.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift:186`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift#L186): The skip-write check needs an unchanged cursor, so a poll that only moves the cursor still rewrites the file
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift:278`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift#L278): prune JSON-encodes the whole array in the while-condition on every write, even under budget; it re-encodes once per removed snapshot when over
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift:299`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift#L299): persist encodes the whole array a second time and atomically rewrites history.json
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift:381`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift#L381): readPages awaits appendRoom before returning, so the cache write delays publishLog
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift:143`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift#L143): poll calls readPages whenever the room's latest seq moved, including non-message events
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotGroupRoom.swift:75`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotGroupRoom.swift#L75): Poll interval is 2 s while working, blocked or stopping
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift:120`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift#L120): replace() prune + persist; only a few times per Bot turn, with an unchanged-snapshot skip at L112-114, so not hot

## Fix sketch

1) In `appendRoom`, when `previous.messages == next.messages`, `earlierBoundary` and `profileName` are unchanged and only the cursor moved, replace the snapshot in memory and return without prune or persist. The next real write persists the newer cursor. If the app is killed first, reopening re-reads from the older persisted cursor, and the existing overlap logic (L163) merges it.
2) In `prune`, encode once. Only loop and re-encode when the count is over 100 or the encoded size is over `maximumBytes`. Pass the final `Data` to `persist` so it does not encode again. That turns 2 full encodes into 1 per write.

## Measurement plan

Add an os_signpost around `appendRoom` and around its encode/write (prune + persist). Seed a fixture cache of about 2 MB and about 8 MB, then play a scripted room of 150 polls where 80% advance only the cursor. Before: about 150 writes and about 300 full encodes, with poll-to-publishLog latency including encode time. After: writes only on polls with new message rows (about 30), one encode each, and cursor-only polls adding no latency. Check write volume on device with the File Activity instrument.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cursor-only changes update memory without persisting; the next real write persists the newer cursor.
- [ ] `prune` encodes once unless over the count or size limit.
- [ ] `BotHistoryCache` tests cover reopen after a kill with an older persisted cursor.

## Tradeoffs and risk

If the process dies before the next message write, the persisted cursor is a few seconds stale. Reopening then re-reads a few extra pages. That is fine for a disposable index. The change does not alter search results.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Checked at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The claim holds for group rooms. It is mostly refuted for Bot chats.

Rooms: when a room is working, blocked or stopping, `BotRoomStatus.interval` is 2 s (BotGroupRoom.swift:75). Each poll that sees `latest > log.cursor` calls `readPages` (BotRoomReader.swift:143), which awaits `cache.appendRoom` (BotRoomReader.swift:381). The early return in `appendRoom` (BotHistoryCache.swift:186-187) needs `previous.cursor == next.cursor`. So any tool or status event that moves the cursor, with no new message row, still runs prune and persist.

The `prune` while-condition (L278) JSON-encodes the whole snapshot array at least once, even under budget. `persist` (L299) encodes it again and atomically rewrites history.json with file protection. That is 2 full encodes and one full-file write per advancing poll.

There is also a user-visible cost the auditor missed. `readPages` awaits the cache write before it returns, so `log.apply`/`publishLog` in `poll()` (L144-146) wait for the encodes and the write. New room messages reach the screen later by that time.

What softens it: the work runs on the actor, off the main thread. The 8 MB ceiling is the pruning cap, not a typical size. Rows are text only, user/assistant or member messages only, 500 at most per snapshot. A typical cache is probably 0.5-2 MB.

Bot chats: `replace()` runs only on full `session.resume` snapshots. Those come from message.start/complete, the prompt, stop, errors and approvals (BotConversation.swift:890, 912, 1082, 1154), coalesced by a 250 ms debounce (L1197). `replace()` also skips the write when rows, root and tip are unchanged within 60 s (L112-114). That is a few writes per turn, not per token, so that half of the claim is not hot.

</details>

title: perf(bots): window the group room transcript like Bot Chat
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

BotRoomView renders every room event eagerly on open. Busy rooms build 150-500 hosted selection controllers and markdown views on the main thread at once.

Every visible room event is built eagerly on open. Each member message is a UIViewControllerRepresentable selection host plus a markdown view. A warm or disk-restored open publishes up to 500 events before the first frame, a cold open builds up to about 200, and each Load earlier adds up to 200 more that are never trimmed. When a new event arrives, every row body probably re-runs, because BotRoomEventView takes a UIImage dictionary.

- **Trigger:** Open a group room that has a recent snapshot or disk cache with 300-500 events, or tap Load earlier a few times in a busy room.
- **Impact (medium, Every room open, every scene re-activation (the revision bump re-runs open()), and each Load earlier.):** On open, 150-500 hosted selection controllers plus markdown views are built on the main thread. That is likely a visible open stall and a memory jump on older iPhones. It is limited to heavy group-room users, a narrower surface than Sessions or Bot Chat.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:31`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift#L31): eager VStack; the #553 comment assumes Load earlier bounds the row count
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:50`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift#L50): ForEach(reader.events) with no window
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:198`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift#L198): each member message builds a ResponseTextSelection hosting controller plus a MarkdownRenderer
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift:63`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift#L63): init restores the recent snapshot, up to 500 events, before the first frame
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift:91`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift#L91): disk restore of up to 500 cached messages when there is no recent log
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift:151`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift#L151): loadEarlier prepends up to 200 more sequence numbers per tap; nothing is ever trimmed
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotGroupRoom.swift:121`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotGroupRoom.swift#L121): windowStart = latest - 200; recentWindow keeps suffix(500)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:372`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift#L372): BotTranscriptWindow (50-row window) that Bot Chat already uses

## Fix sketch

In BotRoomView, window by sequence number instead of by index, because room history is prepended and BotTranscriptWindow's index/openedCount model would shift. Add `@State private var oldestShownSeq: Int?`.
- On `.onChange(of: reader.events.count, initial: true)`, if oldestShownSeq is nil and events is not empty, set it to `events[max(0, events.count - 50)].seq`.
- Render `ForEach(reader.events.filter { $0.seq >= (oldestShownSeq ?? .min) })`, or use a suffix from the first matching index, since events are sorted by seq. New events always show, and prepended history stays hidden until asked for.
- Show Load earlier when older local events exist or reader.hasEarlier is true.
- When tapped: if local events older than oldestShownSeq exist, move oldestShownSeq back 50 indices. Otherwise await reader.loadEarlier() first, then move it back 50. Keep the existing scrollTo(firstShown).
- For the search hit (pendingSequence), set oldestShownSeq to min(oldestShownSeq, sequence) before the scrollTo, so the #553 eager jump still lands.

## Measurement plan

Seed the recent cache with a scripted 500-event BotRoomLog (for example, 125 turns with 3 members). Open the room under Instruments (SwiftUI plus Time Profiler) on a device. Record time to first frame, the main-thread hitch on open, and the count of ResponseSelectionController makeUIViewController calls (add a signpost). Expected before: about 375 hosts and a multi-hundred-ms hitch. Expected after: 50 hosts or fewer. Also check memory right after open.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The room shows the newest ~50 events, windowed by sequence number, with a load-earlier affordance.
- [ ] Prepending history does not shift the window; new events still append.
- [ ] Test covers window stability across prepend and append.

## Tradeoffs and risk

A seq-anchored window adds one @State and a few lines to the Load earlier logic. The search-hit path has to widen the window before scrollTo, or the #553 jump regresses. Load earlier now first reveals rows that are already in memory, so the network pagination happens less often, which is the behavior Bot Chat already has.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

The claim holds up. BotRoomView.swift:31 is an eager VStack, and :50 runs ForEach(reader.events) with no window. For every message.member event, :198-199 builds a ResponseTextSelection (a UIViewControllerRepresentable hosting controller, ResponseTextSelection.swift:6) around a MarkdownRenderer. User messages go through MessageBubbleView instead.

How many rows get built on open depends on where the history comes from:
- Warm open: BotRoomReader init (:63-66) and open() (:74-76) restore the recent snapshot. That snapshot is log.recentWindow() (BotGroupRoom.swift, `events.suffix(500)`), so up to 500 visible events.
- Disk restore: BotRoomReader.swift:91-95 restores up to BotHistoryCache.maximumMessages = 500 rows (BotHistoryCache.swift:76, :178-180).
- Cold open: log.begin(latest:) reads the last 200 sequence numbers (windowStart), and invisible kinds are dropped.
- Load earlier: each tap adds up to 200 more sequence numbers, and nothing ever trims them.

BotChatView bounds the same eager-stack pattern with BotTranscriptWindow (pageSize 50, BotChatView.swift:28, :372-392). BotRoomView does not, even though its #553 comment says "Load earlier ... bounds what this builds". The warm and disk restore paths get around that bound.

Two parts of the original claim are overstated:
- Polls do not re-diff on every tick. poll() returns early when `latest <= log.cursor`, and publishLog() only assigns when `events != visible`. Rows are re-diffed only when new events arrive. Each BotRoomEventView takes `avatars: [String: UIImage]`, which is not trivially comparable, so every row body probably re-runs when a new event arrives. Markdown parsing is cached (#260).
- Impact drops from high to medium. Group rooms are a narrower surface than Sessions or Bot Chat, and reaching 300-500 cached events takes a heavily used room. With 3 members, a user turn is about 4 events, so 500 events is roughly 125 turns. Still, 150-500 hosted selection controllers plus markdown built eagerly before the first frame is the same kind of problem #463 fixed for Sessions and BotTranscriptWindow fixed for Bot Chat.

</details>

title: perf(sessions): compute the filtered session groups once per body
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

The session list body recomputes `scheduledSessionGroups` (filtering and partitioning every session) at five call sites per pass, about 10x the needed work on every search keystroke.

On every SessionListView body evaluation, the full session array is filtered by string-based source classification, optionally search-lowercased, and sorted 11 times, and isCronSession runs over it another 15 times. Ten of the 11 visibleSessions passes are redundant.

- **Trigger:** Typing in the session list search with about 200-500 sessions. Also each list load (launch, pull-to-refresh, return from chat), where sessions and isLoading writes cause 2-3 body passes.
- **Impact (medium, per search keystroke and per list load, plus 1 extra pass per second while an active row is monitored):** Redundant main-thread work, roughly 10x what is needed, on every search keystroke. The estimate is a few ms to about 15 ms per body at 200-500 sessions, which can drop frames while typing on older iPhones. It is invisible for users with fewer than about 50 sessions.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:608`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L608): scheduledSessionGroups read 5x in content: L608, L612, L613, L629, L639
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:867`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L867): computed property with no caching, and each read calls the VM
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:203`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L203): visibleSessions called twice with identical args (L208, L213) plus 3 isCronSession passes (L220-L223)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:166`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L166): visibleSessions: shows() filter over all sessions, a searchableText lowercase+join per session while searching (L1358), then a full sort
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1053`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L1053): activeSessionMonitorTaskID runs another full visibleSessions pass per body (task id at L300) and once per second in the monitor loop (L1176) while rows are active
- [`HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift:686`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift#L686): shows() recomputes 3 string-based classifications per call (L513, L522, L608), each allocating an array and trimmed/lowercased strings

## Fix sketch

1) In SessionListViewModel.scheduledSessionGroups, call visibleSessions once and partition it in one loop: `for s in visible { if s.isCronSession { if s.archived != true { scheduled.append(s) } } else { ordinary.append(s) } }`. Keep the totalScheduledCount pass as is, or fold it into a single sessions loop. 2) In SessionListView.content, bind once at the top of the List builder (`let groups = scheduledSessionGroups`) and use `groups` at the five sites. 3) Optional: in activeSessionMonitorTaskID, filter `viewModel.sessions` by SessionRowView.isActiveStreaming first (usually 0-2 rows) and apply visibility only to those, instead of a full visibleSessions pass. Only move classification flags onto SessionSummary at decode if profiling after steps 1-2 still shows shows() as hot.

## Measurement plan

Before/after: add an XCTest `measure {}` that calls scheduledSessionGroups 5 times plus visibleSessions once, with 300 synthetic SessionSummary rows (some cron/CLI) and a 4-character query. Expect about a 5-10x drop. On device: SwiftUI instrument plus Time Profiler while typing 6 characters into search with 300 seeded sessions via a URLProtocol fixture, comparing SessionListView body duration and visibleSessions call count per keystroke (11 before, 1-2 after).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scheduledSessionGroups` partitions in one pass and is bound once per body.
- [ ] Existing session-list grouping tests pass; search results unchanged.

## Tradeoffs and risk

Steps 1 and 2 change no behavior. Step 3 slightly changes which active rows are monitored when a search or project filter hides them, which is harmless (one extra status poll). Caching flags on SessionSummary would add stored state that every memberwise copy path must preserve, so defer it.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Traced at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. SessionListView.content (L570) reads the computed `scheduledSessionGroups` (L867) five times (L608, L612, L613, L629, L639). Nothing is cached. Each call runs SessionListViewModel.visibleSessions twice with identical arguments (L208 and L213). visibleSessions calls AutomatedSessionVisibility.shows over every session, which means isDelegatedSubagentSession, isCronSession and isClaudeCodeSession, about 11 trim+lowercase string ops per session (Session.swift L513, L522, L608, L686). It also lowercases and joins 6 fields per session while searching (L1358), then sorts. Each call adds three more isCronSession passes (L220-L223). The .task(id: activeSessionMonitorTaskID) at L300 adds one more visibleSessions pass per body (L1053-L1054), and one per second in monitorActiveSessionRows (L1176), but only while an active row exists. Per body that is 11 visibleSessions passes plus 15 isCronSession passes over the full array. /api/sessions is not paginated, so a long-time user realistically has 200-500 rows. The body re-runs on every search keystroke (@State searchText), on remote-search result writes, and on every load (sessions, isLoading). The duplicate visibleSessions call at L208/L213 is plainly redundant. Two sub-claims do not hold. (1) sessionCount(for:) (SessionListComponents.swift L395-L399) short-circuits on `projectId == projectID &&`, so shows() runs only on that project's sessions, not about 2,000 times. It also lives in SessionSidebarUtilityRows, a separate view with its own invalidation, and that view is hidden while searching (L586). (2) ScheduledSessionsView.sessions (L754) is a pushed destination that is rarely open, so two passes there is minor. Magnitude depends on how much Foundation trimmingCharacters/lowercased costs per short string on device. The auditors' estimates range from 2-6 ms to 15-25 ms per body, so this needs profiling. Impact is medium only for users with hundreds of sessions who are typing in search.

</details>

title: perf(networking): share URLSessions across APIClient instances
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

Each APIClient creates its own URLSession, so each chat open starts on a cold connection pool and pays a fresh TLS handshake over tunnels and cellular (about 40-160 ms before the first response).

URLSession connection pools (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, HTTP/2 multiplexing) are scoped to a session instance. Each APIClient owns private sessions and invalidates them in deinit. So each newly opened chat, and its git probe client, starts with an empty pool and must do TCP and TLS before the first byte. That happens even when the session-list client already holds a live connection to the same host.

- **Trigger:** The user taps a session in the list over a Cloudflare tunnel on cellular or remote Wi-Fi, with an edge RTT of about 30-80 ms. The same happens when opening Settings model/profile pickers, Workspace, or Skills sheets.
- **Impact (medium, per chat open (the most frequent navigation), plus per settings/workspace sheet open):** On tunnel and cellular links, roughly 40-160 ms is added before the first response on each chat open. That is invisible for cached transcripts, which paint from SwiftData, but it delays the refresh and uncached opens. It is negligible on LAN.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:42`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift#L42): every init builds a default and an ephemeral URLSession with a per-client CrossOriginHeaderStripper delegate (L42-44)
- [`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:63`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift#L63): deinit invalidates the owned sessions, which tears down each client's pool
- [`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:211`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift#L211): sendPreparedRequest: session.data(for:) has no per-task delegate
- [`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:272`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift#L272): downloadData: session.data(for:) has no per-task delegate
- [`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:326`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift#L326): makeDefaultSession / makeDefaultPublicMediaSession (L334)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:581`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift#L581): new client per chat; loadMessages refresh is its first request
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:406`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L406): @State git availability VM builds another client
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1788`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift#L1788): loadInitialGitAvailability replaces the L406 instance with a third client
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:110`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift#L110): session-list client that holds the warm connection
- [`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotArtifactDownload.swift:42`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotArtifactDownload.swift#L42): existing precedent: redirect guard passed as a per-task delegate via bytes(for:delegate:)

## Fix sketch

In APIClient, replace the per-instance defaults with two process-wide `static let` sessions (default config with `.shared` cookies, and the existing ephemeral media config), created with `delegate: nil`. Keep the per-client `redirectHeaderStripper` and pass it as a per-task delegate at the two call sites: `session.data(for: request, delegate: redirectHeaderStripper)` at APIClient.swift:211 and :272. BotArtifactDownload.swift:42 already relies on this pattern for redirect guarding. Only put the injected sessions in `ownedSessions`. With no owned sessions, deinit invalidates nothing, so the shared pools survive. Tests that inject sessions or call `redirectHeaderStripper` directly are unaffected. Optionally, have loadInitialGitAvailability call `gitAvailabilityViewModel.loadIfNeeded()` instead of building a second VM.

## Measurement plan

Add a temporary URLSessionTaskMetrics log for the first ChatViewModel request (the loadMessages refresh): `transactionMetrics.last?.isReusedConnection` and `secureConnectionEnd - connectStart`. Open 3 chats in a row over the tunnel on a device. Before: isReusedConnection=false and roughly 1-2 edge RTTs of connect/TLS per open. After: true, and connect time is 0. The Instruments Network template should show one connection per host instead of one per chat.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Process-wide shared sessions (default and ephemeral media) with per-task redirect-stripping delegates.
- [ ] Custom headers and cookie scoping per server unchanged (`CustomHeaderInjectionTests`, multi-server isolation tests pass).
- [ ] Network instrument on device shows connection reuse across chat opens.

## Tradeoffs and risk

This touches #277 redirect-stripping wiring. That is security-sensitive, so the existing stripper tests must still pass, and a redirect test should go through a real per-task delegate. Shared sessions outlive server switches. That's acceptable because cookies were already in `.shared` storage and custom headers are applied per request, but it is worth noting in multi-server-state-isolation.md. Keeping a stateful stripper per client avoids a stateless-origin redesign. The magnitude depends on edge RTT and cross-session TLS resumption, so confirm it on a device before prioritizing.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

The structural claim holds (sha 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c). APIClient.init (APIClient.swift:42-44) always builds two new URLSessions with a per-client delegate unless a session is injected. There are 39 `APIClient(baseURL:)` sites in HermesMobile. ChatViewModel.swift:581 makes a fresh client for every opened chat, and ChatView.swift:406 makes another through GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel (GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:92). URLSession pools connections per session, so a chat's first GET /api/session can't reuse the warm connection held by SessionListViewModel's client (SessionListViewModel.swift:110).

The auditors overstate the magnitude, for three reasons:
(1) Over a Cloudflare tunnel, TCP and TLS terminate at the nearest Cloudflare edge, usually 20-80 ms away. The 100-200 ms origin hop is already warm inside the tunnel. So the realistic added cost is about 1-2 edge RTTs (~40-160 ms), not 200-400 ms. On LAN it is a few ms. The maintainer's memory notes that Tailscale is not used.
(2) loadMessages is cache-first (#163/#164), so most chat opens paint from SwiftData first. The handshake only delays the network refresh and uncached opens.
(3) At cold launch, the restored chat's first request races the session list's own first request, so no warm connection exists to reuse yet.

Whether TLS session tickets are reused across URLSession instances is unknown without metrics. That decides 1 RTT versus 2.

Side claims in trace-launch-3:
- The duplicate git VM is real. loadInitialGitAvailability (ChatView.swift:1788-1791) discards the @State instance built at L406 and builds a second one, costing one more client and session pair per chat open. It is cheap, and it disappears once sessions are shared.
- ChatView.init rebuilding ChatViewModel through State(initialValue:) (L398) on each parent re-init is real. Its 1-3 ms cost is unmeasured, and that is a separate view-identity concern, not connection reuse.

The settings pickers, Skills, rating prompt (SessionListView.swift:154) and Live Activity reconcile (AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:885) clients are one-shot and infrequent. They aren't worth fixing on their own, but they benefit for free. LDSwiftEventSource streams need their own long-lived connection anyway (SSEClient.swift:49), so they can stay as they are.

</details>

title: perf(ipad): keep the sidebar's identity when the selection changes
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

On iPad, `.id(navigationState.rootRevision)` sits on the whole NavigationSplitView, so every chat selection rebuilds the sidebar, re-lays out the list, and re-seeks its scroll position.

Changing the view identity on the NavigationSplitView destroys and recreates the whole split view on each root selection: the UISplitViewController host, the sidebar List/UICollectionView, the header, the visible SessionInteractiveRows and their @State. Only the detail column's pushed path needs resetting, and the ChatView/PendingNewChatView detail roots already have their own ids.

- **Trigger:** iPad or a Plus/Max iPhone in landscape (horizontalSizeClass == .regular), tapping a session, New Chat, or a utility destination (Settings, Tasks, Kanban, Bots...) in the sidebar. The sidebar holds about 200 sessions, of which roughly 15-25 rows are visible.
- **Impact (medium, per sidebar selection in regular width):** This happens on the most frequent iPad interaction (switching chats), and the rebuilt sidebar re-lays out and re-seeks its scroll position on top of the new ChatView's own setup. It is limited to regular-width layouts, and the List is lazy, so the extra cost is probably tens of ms, not hundreds. Compact iPhone, the main audience, is unaffected, so this is not high impact.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:453`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L453): .id(navigationState.rootRevision) on the NavigationSplitView re-identifies the sidebar as well as the detail
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:445`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L445): detail NavigationStack: the only part that needs a reset (per #116)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionNavigationState.swift:37`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionNavigationState.swift#L37): select(session) bumps rootRevision; same at 44 (new chat), 50 (utility), 65 (openSessionList)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:664`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift#L664): sidebar List with .scrollPosition(id: $sidebarScrollPosition); the List is recreated on each tap and has to restore its position
- [`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionRowView.swift:544`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionRowView.swift#L544): streaming-dot repeatForever animation restarts whenever the sidebar is rebuilt

## Fix sketch

Move `.id(navigationState.rootRevision)` from the NavigationSplitView (line 453) to the detail `NavigationStack { regularWidthDetail }` (line 445). The detail's pushed path still resets on every root selection, including re-selecting the same utility, which is what #116's testReselectingRootDestinationAdvancesNavigationRevision covers. The sidebar column keeps its identity. rootRevision's other use as a staleness token in openPendingWebuiPush (line 1360) doesn't change.

## Measurement plan

On an iPad simulator or device with about 200 sessions, use the SwiftUI Instruments template while tapping 10 different sessions in the sidebar. Before the fix, expect SessionInteractiveRow/header view creations on every tap and a List re-instantiation. After the fix, expect zero sidebar row creations (only the selection-highlight body updates). Also use Time Profiler/Hitches to compare the tap-to-first-frame interval and hitch time. Manual check: after the fix, the streaming dot no longer restarts and the sidebar scroll offset does not jump when you switch chats.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `.id` moves to the detail NavigationStack; the sidebar keeps identity and scroll position.
- [ ] `testReselectingRootDestinationAdvancesNavigationRevision` and the detail reset behavior still pass.

## Tradeoffs and risk

Re-check #116's manual case: open a nested destination (e.g. Settings > subpage, or a workspace file from a chat), then pick another sidebar root and confirm the nested screen is replaced. Also confirm that a column visibility the user changed (collapsed sidebar) now survives selection. The current full rebuild resets it, and the maintainer may or may not want that.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. SessionListView.swift:453 puts `.id(navigationState.rootRevision)` on the whole NavigationSplitView (sidebar and detail). SessionNavigationState.swift:37/44/50/65 increment rootRevision on every select(session), select(newChat route), select(utility) and openSessionList, so each sidebar tap in regular width gives the split view a new identity. SwiftUI then throws away and rebuilds the sidebar column: the `sessionListSurface` List (a UICollectionView), its header, the floating new-session button and every visible row's @State. For example, the ActiveSessionStreamingIndicator repeatForever animation in SessionRowView.swift:526-556 restarts. The detail column also gets rebuilt, but it needs a new identity anyway: ChatView already has `.id(session.id)` (SessionListView.swift:494) and PendingNewChatView has `.id(route.id)`. The commit that added this, 30dd9cfa (#116), only meant to 'reset nested detail navigation when a sidebar root is selected'. The sidebar rebuild is a side effect. Some parts are safely outside the reset: the list data lives in the view model, sidebarScrollPosition is @State on SessionListView (line 54), and all the `.task`s (lines 143-307, 425) hang off body/routedNavigationContainer above the `.id`, so no network work restarts. The cost is creating the views and the UIKit split/collection controllers again. The List is lazy, so only about 15-25 visible rows are rebuilt, not all 200. Only regular width is affected: iPad (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 1,2) and Plus/Max iPhones in landscape. Compact iPhone uses the NavigationStack branch, which has no `.id`. I found no measurement of the magnitude.

</details>

---

title: perf(workspace): build diff rows once per file as responses land
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

GitDiffView rebuilds rows for every file each time one file's diff arrives, which is quadratic across large change sets and repeats main-thread layout while late files stream in.

Each per-file diff response triggers a full rebuild: every file already loaded gets re-parsed and word-diffed again. Parse and word-diff work therefore grows quadratically with the number of files. Superseded detached builds keep running to completion, and every build that lands does a full main-thread layout pass over all rows. That pass includes String.count per row and a VoiceOver layoutChanged post.

- **Trigger:** Open the Git sheet or a turn diff and tap a file in a change set of roughly 50-500 files (agent refactor, formatter, generated code). Example: 100 files x ~150 lines means ~5k DiffHunk.parse + word-diff passes instead of 100, and ~100 main-thread layout builds over up to ~15k rows while the sheet is scrolling.
- **Impact (medium, Once per diff-sheet open or pull-to-refresh; cost scales with changed-file count squared):** Typical 5-20 file diffs finish in milliseconds and nobody notices. Large change sets waste seconds of multi-core CPU and battery, and the repeated main-thread layout passes can drop frames while late files stream in during scrolling.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift:208`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift#L208): rebuildRows() after every landed file result
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift:250`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift#L250): rebuildRows maps all files; Task.detached at L254 rebuilds rows for every loaded file and is never cancelled when superseded (generation check at L257 only discards the result afterwards)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffRow.swift:106`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffRow.swift#L106): DiffHunk.parse re-run for each loaded file on every rebuild
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffRow.swift:137`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffRow.swift#L137): ReviewWordDiff.annotate (tokenize + LCS per paired line) re-run for each loaded file on every rebuild
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift:190`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift#L190): main-thread rebuildLayout over all rows on each landed build, plus UIAccessibility .layoutChanged post at L202
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffLayout.swift:52`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffLayout.swift#L52): row.columnCount (O(len) String.count, ReviewDiffRow.swift:30) evaluated per row per layout build
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitWorkspaceView.swift:50`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitWorkspaceView.swift#L50): passes all trackedFiles (up to 500), so N can be large; the fetch-all is intentional design, not the defect

## Fix sketch

In GitDiffView, add `@State private var rowsByFileID: [String: [ReviewDiffRow]]`. When a result lands, run ReviewDiffRowBuilder.rows(for: ReviewDiffFileInput) for that one file (in a detached task, or inline in the child task next to fetchDiff so it is already off main) and store it. Then publish `rows = files.flatMap { rowsByFileID[$0.id] ?? placeholderRows(for: $0) }` and bump rowsVersion. Loading and failed placeholder rows are cheap: a header row plus a notice row. That removes the quadratic parse and word-diff and the uncancelled detached builds. To also bound the main-thread layout passes, coalesce publishes so the first (initial) file publishes immediately and later ones publish at most every ~150 ms or every 4 results. Optionally, store columnCount as a `let` on ReviewDiffLine at build time so ReviewDiffLayout stops recounting Characters on each pass.

## Measurement plan

Build a 100-file x 150-line fixture, either through a URLProtocol mock or a unit test that drives ReviewDiffRowBuilder. Before the change: count ReviewDiffRowBuilder per-file invocations or DiffHunk.parse calls per load (expect ~N^2/2, about 5,050), and in Instruments (Time Profiler + os_signpost) record the RebuildLayout interval count and total duration on a device. After the change: exactly N parses, total builder CPU down about 50x at N=100, and RebuildLayout count bounded by the coalescing interval (for example ~10-20 instead of ~100) with no hitches over 16 ms in the Animation Hitches instrument while scrolling during load.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rows are cached per file ID and built once, off the main actor.
- [ ] Diff output unchanged for existing fixtures; a test covers incremental arrival.

## Tradeoffs and risk

The per-file row cache holds the same rows the flat array already holds, so memory barely changes. Coalescing can delay a later file's paint by up to one interval (~150 ms). Rebuilding one file on its own changes nothing in behavior, because ReviewWordDiff pairs never cross a file header and row ids are already per-file.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Traced at 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The load loop in GitDiffView.load() calls rebuildRows() once per landed file (GitDiffView.swift:208). rebuildRows() (L250-258) maps all `files` into inputs, and its Task.detached calls ReviewDiffRowBuilder.rows(for:) over every input. For every file already in `.loaded`, that re-runs DiffHunk.parse (ReviewDiffRow.swift:106), rebuilds each row, and re-runs ReviewWordDiff.annotate (L137), which tokenizes and LCS-diffs every paired -/+ line. So parse and word-diff work grows with N^2/2 across a load. The generation check (L257) only drops stale results after the work finishes. The tasks are never cancelled, so overlapping builds use cooperative-pool CPU. Each surviving result bumps rowsVersion. ReviewDiffSurface.updateUIView then calls setRows, and ReviewDiffCanvasView.rebuildLayout (L190-202) builds a new ReviewDiffLayout on the main thread. That layout is a full pass over every row, and each pass calls row.columnCount, which is an O(len) String.count (ReviewDiffLayout.swift:52, and :78 when wrapping). It also posts UIAccessibility .layoutChanged. The existing mitigations are real: rowsVersion stops SwiftUI from diffing the row array, builds run off main, and fetches are capped at 4 in flight. None of them bound the repeated work. Magnitude, re-scored: for the typical 5-20 changed files the waste is tens of milliseconds of background CPU and nobody would notice. It becomes visible only on large change sets such as agent refactors, formatter runs, or generated files: 100 files x ~150 lines is ~15k rows, ~5k file parses instead of 100, and ~100 main-thread layout passes over a growing row list while the user scrolls. That is why impact is medium, not high. One sub-claim is intentional, not waste: the auditor said a single-file tap fetches every diff. GitWorkspaceView.swift:50 passes all trackedFiles, and the GitDiffView doc comment (L3-6) says this is deliberate: every changed file in one scroll, with the tapped file fetched first. So that part is left out of the fix. ChatView.swift:1058 (turn diff) uses the same path with turn files, which are usually fewer.

</details>

---

title: perf(workspace): draw only the reachable part of very long diff lines
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

The review canvas typesets and draws the full text of a long code line every frame. Minified bundles or source maps (a 400 KB line) freeze the viewer in wrap mode and blow the frame budget when panning without wrap.

**perf(workspace): draw only the reachable columns and visible wrapped lines of long code rows**

A code row is always passed whole to CoreText, and it is redrawn on every scroll or pan frame. Without wrap, a 400 KB minified line is fully typeset each frame, though only the first ~350-400 columns can ever be reached. With wrap, the full-line attributed string is rebuilt and every visual line is sliced and drawn each frame, about 9k draws where roughly 40 are visible. The O(n) String.count in columnCount adds to this on each height lookup.

- **Trigger:** Open a minified .js, a .map file or a single-line .json of up to the server's 400 KB cap in the workspace file preview, then pan horizontally. Worse: turn on Wrap Lines and scroll vertically through the wrapped row. Diffs that touch such files hit the same draw path.
- **Impact (medium, Every scroll or pan frame while a long row is on screen, and once on open):** Wrap mode on a 400 KB line redraws about 9k text lines per frame, which in practice freezes the viewer. Without wrap, one full-line CoreText typeset per pan frame very likely exceeds the 8-16 ms frame budget. These files show up regularly in agent workspaces (dist bundles, source maps, fixtures), though not in every session.

**perf(workspace): measure full-viewport CPU redraw of the review canvas at 120 Hz before tiling or caching lines**

Every scroll frame re-rasterises the full viewport backing store (about 1179x2556 px at 3x) on the main thread: row backgrounds, gutter numbers, and 40-60 re-typeset code lines. A layer-translation or tiled approach would only redraw rows entering the viewport.

- **Trigger:** Fling-scroll a syntax-highlighted source file of about 5k lines, or a large multi-file diff, on a 120 Hz iPhone.
- **Impact (low, Every frame during vertical scroll in the source or diff viewer):** Short-line rows are cheap, and the draw loop already culls to visible rows. The work is steady per-frame CPU and battery cost that could drop frames at 120 Hz on older ProMotion devices, but nothing shows it exceeds budget. It only affects workspace file and diff browsing.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift:276`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift#L276): Non-wrap fast path draws the whole line via NSString.draw even though at most ~2800 pt (~350-400 columns) can be panned into view
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift:281`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift#L281): Wrap path builds an NSMutableAttributedString over the full line on every draw
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift:298`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift#L298): The wrap loop slices and draws every visual line of the row (about 9k for 400 KB at 45 columns) and ignores the dirty rect
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffSurfaceView.swift:234`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffSurfaceView.swift#L234): setNeedsDisplay on every scrollViewDidScroll (line 246), so the cost repeats every scroll frame
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift:362`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift#L362): setNeedsDisplay on every horizontal pan change and deceleration display-link tick
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffRow.swift:33`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffRow.swift#L33): columnCount is line.content.count, O(n), recomputed on each call
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffLayout.swift:78`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffLayout.swift#L78): visualLineCount calls columnCount on every height(forRowAt:), which binary search and the draw loop hit per frame in wrap mode
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/SourceViewer/SourceHighlighter.swift:52`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/SourceViewer/SourceHighlighter.swift#L52): Highlighting already blanks lines over 1,000 characters; drawing has no matching bound
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift:13`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift#L13): draw(_:) fills the rect and redraws every visible row; rows outside the visible range are skipped at line 32, so overscan adds no draw cost

## Fix sketch

**perf(workspace): draw only the reachable columns and visible wrapped lines of long code rows**

(1) Store columnCount once. Add `let columnCount: Int` to ReviewDiffLine, set to content.count in its init (ReviewDiffRowBuilder.reviewLine and SourceFileRows.rows), and have ReviewDiffRow.columnCount return it. (2) Without wrap, draw only the reachable prefix. In drawCodeText, let maxColumns = Int(ceil((style.maxContentWidth + viewportWidth) / style.codeCharacterWidth)). If text.count > maxColumns, draw String(text.prefix(maxColumns)) instead; the existing NSIntersectionRange clamp already trims the runs. Better still, precompute that prefix once at row build time. (3) With wrap, draw only the visible visual lines. Pass the row rect and dirty rect into drawCodeText, and compute first = max(0, Int((rect.minY - origin.y) / wrappedLineHeight)) and last = min(lineCount - 1, Int((rect.maxY - origin.y) / wrappedLineHeight) + 1). Advance the start index with text.index(text.startIndex, offsetBy: first * wrapColumns). Build the attributed string only for the start..<end slice of lines first...last, shifting the runs by the slice's UTF-16 offset, then draw those lines.

**perf(workspace): measure full-viewport CPU redraw of the review canvas at 120 Hz before tiling or caching lines**

Measure first. If the 'Draw' signpost stays under about 4 ms on the oldest supported ProMotion device, do nothing. If it exceeds budget, the smallest change is a small per-row cache: a dictionary from row.id to a prebuilt NSAttributedString (or CTLine), cleared whenever tokensByRowID, wrapsLines, the style, or the trait appearance changes, and bounded to about 200 entries. A scroll frame then only positions and draws cached lines. Tiling the canvas (2-3 viewport-height tiles translated during scroll, each redrawn only when a new band enters) is the larger option.

## Measurement plan

In Instruments, record the os_signpost 'ReviewDiff/Draw' interval (reviewDiffSignposter) and the Animation Hitches track. Open a 400 KB single-line JS fixture. First pan horizontally with wrap off, then scroll through the row with wrap on. Before: expect Draw intervals of tens to hundreds of ms and continuous hitches. After: Draw should be about the same as a normal 80-column file (a few ms), with no hitches.

On a ProMotion device, capture the Instruments os_signpost 'ReviewDiff/Draw' duration distribution and the Animation Hitches track while fling-scrolling a highlighted 5k-line fixture. Act only if p95 Draw exceeds about 4-5 ms or hitches appear; after the fix, compare the p95 Draw interval and the hitch ratio.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `columnCount` is stored per line instead of recounted.
- [ ] Without wrap, only the reachable column prefix is drawn; with wrap, only visible wrapped lines.
- [ ] A 400 KB single-line file pans and scrolls without hitches on device (Hitches instrument).

## Tradeoffs and risk

Slicing by character offset must stay grapheme-safe; use String.Index as the wrap loop already does, and consider a UTF-16 fast path for ASCII-only lines. The prefix cap has to stay in step with maxContentWidth. Row construction gains one stored Int per line.

A line cache costs memory and adds an invalidation surface (tokens, wrap, Dynamic Type, appearance). Tiling is a sizeable rewrite of a ported component. Both are unjustified without a trace showing over-budget draws.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **M**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(workspace): draw only the reachable columns and visible wrapped lines of long code rows</summary>

Audited at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. I traced the path from FilePreviewView.sourceContent (any non-Markdown text file, including minified .js, .map and single-line .json) to SourceFileSurface, then to ReviewDiffSurface with presentation .source. SourceFileRows makes one row per line. Upstream MAX_FILE_BYTES is 400_000 (.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/config.py:1006), so one row can hold about 400k characters. Nothing on the draw path is bounded. SourceHighlighter blanks lines over 1,000 characters, so the long row has no runs. Without wrap, drawCodeText then takes the fast path and calls NSString.draw(at:) on the whole 400k-character string (Drawing.swift:276-277). The clip rect limits rasterisation, but CoreText still typesets the whole line. The pannable width is capped at style.maxContentWidth = 2800 pt (ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift:193-195, 385), so only about 350-400 columns can ever be on screen. With wrap on, the no-runs fast path is skipped because text.count > wrapColumns. Each draw then builds an NSMutableAttributedString over all 400k characters (Drawing.swift:281-284). The loop at Drawing.swift:296-303 then slices and draws every visual line, about 9k at 45 columns. The dirty rect is never consulted, although only about 40 of those lines fit on screen. On top of that, ReviewDiffRow.columnCount (ReviewDiffRow.swift:30-33) recomputes String.count, which is O(n), on every height(forRowAt:) call. That happens in each binary-search probe that lands on the row and in each frame(forRowAt:) during draw. Redraws happen on every scroll frame (updateViewportFrame, SurfaceView.swift:226-236) and every horizontal pan or deceleration display-link tick (setHorizontalOffset, CanvasView.swift:357-363). Nothing is cached: no per-row CTLine or attributed-string cache exists. Minified bundles and source maps are common enough in agent workspaces, so impact is medium. Wrap mode on such a file is close to frozen; the non-wrap cost is large but less certain in magnitude.

</details>

<details><summary>Verifier notes: perf(workspace): measure full-viewport CPU redraw of the review canvas at 120 Hz before tiling or caching lines</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. The waste exists: the canvas is a viewport-sized UIView whose frame follows contentOffset. updateViewportFrame (ReviewDiffSurfaceView.swift:226-236) calls setNeedsDisplay() on every scrollViewDidScroll. So each frame re-fills the whole viewport and re-typesets every visible row on the CPU, even though most rows have only shifted. For rows with syntax runs, drawCodeText builds a new NSMutableAttributedString each time (Drawing.swift:281-290). The claim overstates the row count, though. The draw loop skips rows outside visibleMinY...visibleMaxY (Drawing.swift:32), so the 4-row overscan widens the range query but adds no draw work. That leaves about 40-60 short rows per frame. The magnitude on a real ProMotion device is unknown: CoreText with cached glyphs for about 4k glyphs, plus a full-bitmap fill, may fit in 8.3 ms on recent A-series chips or may not. The design is deliberate (ported from t3code, with a doc comment at ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift:44-47) and already has signposts. Without a trace this is not confirmed.

</details>
