title: perf(model-picker): lazy rows and memoized catalog for large model lists
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

The model picker nests every model inside a VStack in one List row and re-derives the merged catalog per body, so large catalogs (OpenRouter, Nous) hitch on the first search keystroke and on 'Show all'.

Every sheet body pass (each keystroke in search, the Custom Model ID field or the Provider ID field, and each expand, collapse or overflow toggle) recomputes the derived catalog about 10-20 times over the full flattened model list. It also rebuilds the view value for every visible model row, because rows come from helper functions inside the one sheet body. Each expanded group is a single List cell whose non-scrolling LazyVStack builds and lays out all of its rows at once. So searching, which auto-expands every group, or tapping 'Show all models' on an overflow provider puts hundreds of rows into one cell in one pass.

- **Trigger:** Open the model picker from the composer (or from Settings > Default Model, the Task editor, or Bots) against a server with OpenRouter or Nous. Upstream shows 15 models and returns the rest (often 300+) in extra_models. Either type a letter that appears in the provider id ('o', 'r', 'n'), which matches the whole provider catalog, or tap 'Show all models'.
- **Impact (medium, per keystroke / per expand while the picker is open. A user-driven surface opened a few times per session, not a scroll or streaming path.):** Only users with large live catalogs (OpenRouter, Nous, big enterprise catalogs) get a likely visible hitch on the first search keystroke or on 'Show all'. Users of typical 10-30 model providers pay a negligible cost.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:310`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L310): LazyVStack inside a DisclosureGroup inside a single List row, with no ScrollView, so it isn't lazy. Every displayed model row (Button + star + contextMenu + pill) is built in one cell.
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:73`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L73): ForEach(filteredModelGroups) is one List row per group
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:141`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L141): statusPlaceholder evaluates filteredModelGroups a second time per body whenever the catalog is non-empty
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:296`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L296): group.allModels recomputed per group per body; displayedModels also calls allModels when overflow is expanded
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:515`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L515): filteredGroups: up to 3 localizedCaseInsensitiveContains per model over allModels, twice per keystroke
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:536`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L536): customModelGroups reads storedCustomOptions up to 3 times
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:569`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L569): storedCustomOptions builds a Set over the flattened catalog; favorites and recents each rebuild catalogOptionsByFavoriteKey (ModelFavoritesStore.swift:163)
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:626`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L626): selectedCustomOption → selectedModelOption (L705) plus isRenderedByCurrentPicker (L646), each flattening the catalog again
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift:717`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ModelPickerSheet.swift#L717): matches() checks providerID, so a keystroke that is a substring of the provider id matches every model in that provider
- [`HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift:716`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift#L716): allModels is computed (concat + Set dedupe) on every access

## Fix sketch

1) Make allModels a stored `let` computed once in ModelCatalogGroup.init (ServerCatalog.swift). This removes the repeated concat and dedupe. 2) Put a ForEach directly inside the DisclosureGroup content (drop the VStack and LazyVStack wrapper, and render the divider and overflow toggle as sibling rows). A List then turns each model into its own reusable row, and only visible rows get built. Keep .listRowInsets, .listRowSeparator(.hidden) and the pill on each row. 3) At the top of body, compute `let groups = filteredModelGroups` once and pass it to both the ForEach and statusPlaceholder. Inside customModelGroups, read storedCustomOptions once into a local. That's enough; there's no need for @State caching or onChange syncing.

## Measurement plan

Build a synthetic catalog with one 400-model group (15 visible + 385 extra) in ProviderGlyphGalleryView or a debug preview. On a physical iPhone, record with the Instruments SwiftUI template (View Body, Hitches) while you tap 'Show all models' and type 'o' in search. Before: expect one long commit or hitch on expansion and body passes that scale with 400 rows per keystroke. After: hitch-free expansion, and body work limited to the visible rows. Optionally, an XCTest measure{} on ModelPickerSheet.filteredGroups with the 400-model fixture confirms the derived-state work stays sub-millisecond once allModels is stored.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `allModels` is computed once per group; each model is its own List row.
- [ ] The filtered catalog is derived once per query change.
- [ ] Picker selection, favorites, and overflow toggle behave as before.

## Tradeoffs and risk

Turning the group into real List rows changes how the DisclosureGroup indents its children and where the dividers and pill spacing fall, so it needs a light and dark visual check across all 7 call sites. A stored allModels adds a few bytes per group, which is negligible.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **M**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Re-read at 952c7477. Both halves of the claim hold. (1) Each provider group is one List row (ForEach at L73 → modelGroupDisclosure L294). Its content is a VStack with a LazyVStack (L310) that has no enclosing SwiftUI ScrollView, so every displayed model is built and laid out inside that one cell. Each model gets a Button, a star Button, a contextMenu and a pill background. The rows come from a helper function (modelOptionRow) inside the sheet's own body rather than separate view structs, so every sheet body pass rebuilds the view values for every visible row. SwiftUI can't skip this with an Equatable check either: the sheet takes closures (isSelected, onSelect, and so on). (2) Searching auto-expands every group (ComposerModelPickerSectionExpansionState.isExpanded returns true for any group not in collapsedSearchGroupIDs). matches() (L717) also checks providerID, so any keystroke that is a substring of the provider id ('o', 'op', 'r' for openrouter, 'n' or 'o' for nous) matches the entire allModels list of that provider. (3) The derived-state recompute is real: filteredModelGroups runs at L73 and again at L141, each run calls customModelGroups, which evaluates storedCustomOptions up to 3 times, and every one of those flattens allModels through several paths (catalogKeys at L569, plus catalogOptionsByFavoriteKey for favorites and for recents). selectedCustomOption (L626) flattens again via selectedModelOption (L705) and isRenderedByCurrentPicker (L646). allModels (ServerCatalog.swift:716) is a computed concat plus a Set dedupe on every access, and modelGroupDisclosure calls it per group per body (L296, and through displayedModels). Size is the part I couldn't confirm: upstream splits catalogs above 25 into 15 visible plus an extra_models tail (config.py _split_picker_overflow_models, _NOUS_FEATURED_*). So only OpenRouter, Nous, or large live catalogs (hundreds of models) reach the heavy case. Users on openai-codex, anthropic or similar (10-30 models) see negligible cost. The derived-state passes alone are probably a few ms per keystroke at 400 models; the eager build of a few hundred rows in one cell is the likely visible hitch. Without Instruments the size of that hitch is unknown, hence PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED. None of this is covered by the already-fixed list.

</details>

title: perf(workspace): render large Markdown file previews lazily in chunks
body:
Found by the Hermex performance audit of `master` at [`952c747`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/commit/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c) (2026-09-23). Full ranked report: https://vtjzan7f9k8r.postplan.dev

## Problem

FilePreviewView renders a whole Markdown file as one MarkdownRenderer, so large docs parse and lay out in one main-thread pass with a memory peak on open.

A workspace .md file under 80 KB / 2,000 lines is rendered as one MarkdownUI document inside a non-lazy VStack. Every block (headings, lists, tables, code blocks) is parsed, laid out, and kept alive before the first frame, and each code block's syntax highlighting runs on the main actor as soon as it mounts.

- **Trigger:** Open a 30-80 KB Markdown file (CHANGELOG.md, a long README, or AGENTS.md; roughly 1,000-2,000 lines) from the workspace file browser.
- **Impact (medium, Once per open of a large Markdown file):** A one-time hitch on open plus a memory peak, for large but policy-allowed docs. It is not a scrolling or streaming path, and typical 5-20 KB docs are fine, so it only shows up in heavier use.

## Evidence

- [`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewView.swift:228`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewView.swift#L228): markdownContent: ScrollView > VStack > MarkdownRenderer over the whole file
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:31`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L31): settled content goes to MarkdownUI unless fallbackReason fires
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:829`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L829): fallback thresholds 80,000 chars / 2,000 lines; everything below uses full MarkdownUI
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:367`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L367): ChatMarkdownView: one Markdown(content) tree for the whole document
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:476`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift#L476): every code block highlights on the main actor at mount, so N blocks means N synchronous passes on open
- [`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift:16`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift#L16): existing fence-aware 6,000-char chunker, currently used only while streaming

## Fix sketch

In FilePreviewView.markdownContent only: when content.count exceeds StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter.stableChunkTargetCharacterCount, split it once with StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter.split(content). Treat stableChunks plus the trailing activeMarkdown as the chunks, and render them in a LazyVStack(alignment: .leading) via ForEach(chunks, id: \.id) { MarkdownRenderer(content: $0.text) }, with the fileHeader above. Compute the split when the preview loads (for example in the view model next to `preview`), not in body. Leave MarkdownRenderer and the chat path unchanged. A 60 KB file becomes about 10 chunks, and only the first one or two are laid out and highlighted at open.

## Measurement plan

On device, open a 60 KB / ~1,500-line CHANGELOG.md with about 10 fenced code blocks from the workspace browser. Instruments SwiftUI + Hitches: compare the main-thread time from tap to first frame and the longest hitch before and after. Allocations: compare the peak on open. Expect first-frame work to shrink roughly with the chunk count (about 10x).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Files over the stable-chunk threshold are split once and rendered in a LazyVStack of chunks.
- [ ] Small files render exactly as today.
- [ ] Opening a 200 KB Markdown file shows no multi-hundred-ms hang on device.

## Tradeoffs and risk

Chunk boundaries fall on blank lines or closed fences, so reference-style link definitions and loose lists split across a boundary can render differently (rare in real docs). Vertical spacing between chunks needs to match the in-document block margins. Text selection across chunks is already covered by the Select Text context menu, which uses the full content.

## Verification

Adversarially verified by an independent reviewer that re-read the code at `952c747`: **PLAUSIBLE**, impact **medium**, effort **S**. **Confirm the magnitude on device with Instruments before implementing.**

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

Checked at HEAD 952c7477872fa94cbce11bac70f8cf542eda5e1c. FilePreviewView.markdownContent (FilePreviewView.swift:228-236) puts the whole file into a non-lazy ScrollView > VStack > MarkdownRenderer(content:isStreaming:false). For settled content, MarkdownRenderer (MarkdownRenderer.swift:25-37, 51-79) calls MarkdownContentRenderingPolicy.fallbackReason, which switches to plain text only above 80,000 chars or 2,000 lines (MarkdownRenderer.swift:826-840). Anything below that becomes one ChatMarkdownView, meaning one MarkdownUI `Markdown(content)` (L361-367), or a non-lazy VStack of math segments. MarkdownMathLayoutCache (MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift:324) only caches the math segmentation. It does not cache the MarkdownUI parse or layout. The fence-aware 6,000-char chunker (StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter, StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift:13-55) is used only on the streaming path. So a 30-80 KB file is parsed and laid out as one tree before the first frame. On top of that, every fenced code block in the file mounts a ChatCodeBlock whose .task runs MarkdownCodeHighlighter synchronously on the main actor after one Task.yield (MarkdownRenderer.swift:476-478, 524-533). A 60 KB CHANGELOG or AGENTS.md with a dozen code blocks therefore stacks N main-thread highlight passes right after open. Points against a higher rating: this runs once per file open, not in a scroll or streaming path. Once laid out, scrolling a static VStack mostly just moves an offset, so the 'sluggish scrolling' claim is weak. Typical READMEs are 5-20 KB and render acceptably. The workspace preview is a secondary surface. The waste is real at the allowed sizes, but the hitch size (hundreds of ms or more) needs on-device measurement, hence PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED. Not covered by the already-fixed items: #32/#103/#463 made the transcript list lazy, not a single large document, and #291 covered streaming only.

</details>

title: perf(sessions): pause the active-row poll while a chat covers the list
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #677

## What changed

**What's slow for the user:** When any session is streaming, the session list checks the server every second: 1 stream-status GET, plus an approval-pending GET and a clarify-pending GET for each streaming session. On iPhone this keeps going while a chat covers the list, even though that chat already follows the same run over its own chat SSE and approval/clarify SSE. Watching a 3-10 minute run over a tunnel or cellular adds roughly 450-1,600 extra requests. That keeps the radio awake and competes with the chat's own requests.

**How the fix works:** The poll now runs only while the list is on screen. `ActiveSessionMonitorTaskID` (the `.task(id:)` key for the poll) now also tracks whether the list is visible: regular width, no pushed destination, or the Scheduled sessions screen (which shows live rows from the same view model). `shouldPoll` requires active rows, a visible list, and live (not cached) data. When a chat is pushed on iPhone, the task ID changes and the loop exits. When the user pops back, the ID changes again and the poll restarts. The existing return refresh reloads the rows right away, and on compact width it now runs one poll tick right after that reload (new `SessionListReturnRefresh`). Without that tick, an Approval or Input badge from before the push would stay up until the restarted poll's first tick, 3 s later. On iPad the sidebar stays on screen, so selecting a chat there leaves the task ID unchanged and the poll keeps running. The interval also goes from 1 s to 3 s, still much fresher than upstream's 30 s sidebar poll.

**Files:**
- `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift`: the task ID gains `isListVisible`, `isRegularWidth`, `shouldPoll`, `needsTickOnReturn`, and `pollInterval`. It is now internal instead of private so tests can reach it. `SessionListReturnRefresh` runs the return reload and then the one-off tick. The loop's tick moved into a small helper that both paths share.
- `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift`: a doc comment no longer names the old 1 s cadence.
- `HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests.swift`: 5 focused tests.

**Risk:** On iPhone, badges for other sessions (Working, Needs approval, Input) stop updating while a chat or utility screen (other than Scheduled) covers the list, and catch up on return with the immediate reload and one tick (one status GET, plus the approval and clarify probes for each streaming row). With the list visible, badges and the switch from Working to done can arrive up to about 3 s late instead of about 1 s.

**Win: reasoned, not measured.** The tests pin the poll's gating policy; they don't count requests on a device. title: perf(kanban): keep the loaded Board when returning from Card detail
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #672

## What changed

**The problem.** Every time you open a Card and tap Back, the Board reloads from scratch. `KanbanView`'s `.task { await model.load() }` runs again when the Board reappears after a pop, and `load()` is a cold start. It clears the Board and shows the full-screen "Loading Kanban" spinner while three GETs run one after another (config, boards, board). The issue estimates that at about 0.5-1.2 s over a tunnel. Two more GETs follow (stats, assignees). The List is rebuilt, so the scroll position goes back to the top, any pending archive undo is lost, and the live stream reconnects from cursor 0.

**The fix.** `KanbanView` now calls a new `KanbanFeatureState.loadIfNeeded()`. It cold-loads only when no Board snapshot exists, the same rule `retry()` already uses. When a Board is already loaded, coming back from a Card keeps its rows, scroll position, and archive undo. `KanbanStatusFocusView`'s existing `onAppear` → `setVisible(true)` restarts the live stream from the saved `liveCursor`, so changes made while the Card was open still arrive. A first load still cold-loads, and so does a load that failed or was cancelled before a snapshot arrived. Pull-to-refresh, `retry()`, and the scene-active reconcile are unchanged. `load()` itself is unchanged.

**Files.**
- `HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanFeatureState.swift`: adds `loadIfNeeded()` with a doc comment.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift`: `KanbanView`'s `.task` calls `loadIfNeeded()` instead of `load()`.
- `HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests.swift`, `HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests.swift`: 6 focused tests.

**Risk.** Coming back from a Card no longer re-checks the Kanban config or the Board list. The live stream's cursor catch-up, the scene-active reconcile, and pull-to-refresh already cover those changes. There are no visual changes. Server keying is unchanged: the model is still per-`KanbanView` `@State`, and the logged-in subtree is keyed by the active server. There is one call site, in `SessionListView`, and it covers both the iPhone and iPad stacks. The extensions don't use this code.

**Edge: a pop during the first load.** If you tap a Card right after the Board appears, before its stats and assignee reads finish, the pop cancels those reads. On return, `loadIfNeeded()` sees that the reads never settled (neither a value nor a warning was recorded) and finishes them through `refreshBoard(usingCursor: false, refreshSupplementary: true)`, the live-reconcile path. It does not cold-load, so the rows and archive undo are kept here too.

**Edge: a pop during a live refresh.** A live burst moves `liveCursor` before its Board refresh lands (300 ms debounce, then the fetch). A pop inside that window cancels the refresh, and the resumed stream only sends events after the cursor, so those changes would never reach the Board. The old cold load on every Back hid this. On return, `loadIfNeeded()` now also refreshes the Board in place when `liveCursor` is ahead of the snapshot's `latest_event_id` (both come from the same upstream `task_events` id, see `kanban_bridge.py` `_latest_event_id` and the SSE `hello`, which echoes the `since` cursor).

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17e udid> --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests`: **88 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (on `9c617de`).

New tests:
- `testReappearingWithALoadedBoardKeepsItWithoutRequests`: the second appear makes zero requests. The call log is exactly one handshake: configuration, boards, board, stats, assignees.
- `testReappearingWithoutALoadedBoardColdLoadsAgain`: after a cancelled handshake, the next appear loads again.
- `testReappearingAfterACancelledSupplementaryReadFinishesItWithoutColdLoad`: a pop cancels the stats read after the snapshot arrived. On return, the only calls are board, stats, and assignees, with no config/boards handshake.
- `testReappearingWithALoadedBoardKeepsArchiveUndo`: archive undo is still available after the Board reappears.
- `testReturningFromCardResumesStreamFromAdvancedCursorWithoutReload`: after a hide/show cycle, the stream reconnects with `since=13` (the advanced cursor, not 0 and not the snapshot's 11), and no Board request is made.
- `testReturningFromCardRefreshesBoardWhenPopCancelledLiveRefresh`: events move the cursor to 13, then the pop lands inside the coalescing window. On return, one Board refresh brings the snapshot to 13 and the stream resumes with `since=13`.

**Measured or reasoned.** Partly measured. A test pins the request count: returning to a loaded Board that is caught up with the stream makes 0 requests, down from 5, and the stream resumes from the saved cursor. The spinner time (0.5-1.2 s over a tunnel) and the kept scroll position are reasoned from the code and the issue's estimate. Nobody timed them on a device.

## Manual test

On a simulator or device signed in to a server with a Kanban Board that has enough Cards to scroll:

1. Open the Board, scroll down, open a Card, tap Back. Expected: the Board comes back right away with no "Loading Kanban" spinner, at the same scroll position.
2. Archive a Card from its detail view, then tap Back. Expected: the Undo banner is still shown on the Board, and Undo restores the Card.
3. Open a Card. While its detail is open, change a different Card from another client (the web UI). Tap Back. Expected: the change appears on the Board within a moment.
4. Switch to a second server and open Kanban. Expected: a fresh load of that server's Board, with nothing from the first server.

title: perf(chat): start chat-open requests immediately and run them in parallel
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #678

## What changed

**What's slow for the user.** When you open a chat, the app waits for the push animation to finish (about 350-500 ms) before it asks the server for the transcript. After the transcript arrives, it loads composer config and approval state one request at a time: profiles, an optional profile switch, models, reasoning, workspaces, commands, and then two approval GETs. Over a Cloudflare tunnel, an uncached chat shows the skeleton for the transition time plus the round trip. The reasoning chip, supported efforts, and slash commands settle about 0.4-0.8 s late, and a pending approval card or YOLO badge appears about 7 round trips after the transcript.

**How it's fixed.**

1. **The transcript request starts during the push.** `prepareInitialMessageLoad` already runs in the first `.task` pass, while the transition is still animating. It now also sends the transcript request and keeps the task. Only the initial `loadMessages(usesInitialPrefetch: true)` from `ChatView.performInitialAsyncWork` may use that request. The response is still applied only after the transition ends, so the #134/#137 jitter fix is unchanged.
   - The prefetch is used only if the active stream hasn't changed since the request went out. A response fetched before a stream started would look like that stream had ended.
   - Any other load (refresh, reconnect, reload after a mutation) cancels and discards the prefetch. So do the disappear path (`cleanupPollingTasks`) and `deinit`.
   - If the initial load is cancelled, the cancellation is forwarded to the prefetch task.
2. **Composer config loads in parallel.** `ChatComposerConfigLoader` still loads profiles and any profile switch first, because models and workspaces are profile-scoped upstream. After that, models, workspaces, and commands load concurrently, and reasoning still waits for models. Errors keep the old precedence (profiles, then models, reasoning, workspaces). A models or reasoning failure still keeps the workspaces result out of the state, and commands still load after a failure. The chain goes from 5-6 serial round trips to 3-4.
3. **Approvals no longer wait behind config.** `ChatView.performInitialAsyncWork` runs `refreshApprovalBypassState()` with `async let`, alongside `loadComposerConfiguration()` and the draft-settings restore. Config still starts only after `loadMessages`, as the issue says.

**Files.** `ChatViewModel.swift`, `ChatView.swift`, `ChatComposerConfigLoader.swift`, and `ChatScrollPolicy.swift` (a doc comment only). Tests: `ChatComposerConfigLoaderTests.swift`, `ChatViewModelSendTests.swift`.

**Decisions worth a look.**
- **Only the initial load uses the prefetch.** The issue's sketch let any `loadMessages` take it. This is stricter, because send-conflict, goal, undo/retry, and reconnect all reload after a mutation and must never apply a response requested before it. The cost: if a suspended stream reconnects while you come back to the chat, one extra request is sent and then cancelled.
- **Approvals run alongside config, not alongside the transcript.** This follows the issue's fix sketch. The acceptance line "approvals load in parallel with the transcript refresh" reads looser. Moving approvals next to `loadMessages` would be a small follow-up.
- **`SessionResponse` isn't `Sendable`,** so the prefetch wraps the decoded response in a small private `@unchecked Sendable` box. The value is immutable and has one consumer. Making `SessionDetail` `Sendable` would spread well beyond this issue.

**Risk.** A quick back-swipe during the push wastes one cancelled request. Up to 3 config requests are in flight at once on one host, which HTTP/2 over the tunnel handles fine. When models fails, workspaces is now requested and its result thrown away (before, it was never requested). Nothing changes visually: no layout, copy, or UI change. The prefetch lives on the per-server view model, so multi-server isolation is unchanged.

**Measured vs reasoned.** The win is reasoned, not measured. Tests pin the request overlap, but no device, tunnel, or Instruments trace was taken, so the issue's 150-400 ms and 0.4-0.8 s estimates are unverified. The issue's measurement plan (signposts, Network Link Conditioner at 150 ms) is still the before/after check.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 902B936C-554B-4223-83BB-CCC6DB608BCF --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerConfigLoaderTests` (iPhone 18 Pro): **210 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.

New tests:
- `testLoadRequestsWorkspacesAndCommandsWhileModelsIsInFlight`: the scripted `/api/models` answers only after the workspaces and commands requests have arrived, which a serial chain can never do.
- `testPrepareInitialMessageLoadSendsTranscriptRequestThatOnlyTheInitialLoadApplies`: the request starts during preparation while the cached transcript stays on screen. A second first-pass preparation reuses it, and exactly one `/api/session` request is sent.
- `testLoadMessagesWithoutInitialPrefetchDiscardsItAndRefetches`: a refresh never reuses the prefetch, and neither does the later initial load.
- `testInitialLoadRefetchesWhenAStreamStartedAfterThePrefetch`: the stream race the issue names.
- `testCleanupPollingTasksDiscardsTheInitialPrefetch`: leaving the chat drops the in-flight prefetch, and the next initial load asks again.

The config-order assertions in existing tests now allow the new concurrency. The shared request-path recorders are locked (`LockedStrings`), because handlers now run concurrently. `testPrepareInitialMessageLoadPrimesCacheWithoutStartingNetwork` pinned the old "no network in prepare" rule, so it was replaced by the new behavior test.

## Manual test

Tests cover the request ordering. The one thing tests can't show is the feel over a slow link, so this is optional:

1. Connect to a server over the Cloudflare tunnel and open a chat that isn't cached. Expected: the transcript shows up sooner after the push ends, with no jitter during the push animation.
2. Open a chat with a pending approval. Expected: the approval card appears at about the same time as the composer chips, not several beats later.
3. Open a chat and back-swipe right away, then open it again. Expected: the transcript loads normally.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no model changes)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (same endpoints, same requests; only their timing changed)

title: perf(kanban): stop per-burst stats reads and queue live refreshes instead of cancelling them
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #684. Stacked on #695; merge after it.

This PR covers only item 2 of #684. Item 1 (hiding the "Refreshing Board" row when a snapshot exists) is left for a design decision on purpose: it removes a UI indicator that exists today, so it has to pass the mock gate first. `KanbanLabView` is untouched.

## What changed

**What's slow for the user.** While a Kanban Board is on screen and agents are working, each debounced burst of live events runs a full Board GET, which the upstream contract requires. Two more round trips follow it, one after the other: GET stats, which no view shows, and GET assignees, which adds little because `profileOptions` already merges the fresh Board's assignees. Also, a burst that arrives while the Board GET is still downloading cancels that download and starts over. On a busy Board this keeps pushing refreshes back and throws away partial downloads, and over a tunnel it keeps the radio awake longer.

**How the fix works.**
1. A coalesced live reconcile now fetches only the Board. Stats and assignee history still refresh on initial load, pull-to-refresh, scene foreground, offline recovery, Dispatcher runs, mutation reconciles, and `loadIfNeeded`. The stats fetch itself stays. The live refresh still runs those reads in two cases: when they haven't settled yet (for example, a live refresh took over from a `loadIfNeeded` that was finishing them after a pop), and when it took over a refresh that asked for them and hadn't finished reading them (`supplementaryRefreshPending`). The second case covers a pull, mutation, or Dispatcher reconcile that gets superseded by the live events it caused.
2. The debounce is now separate from the fetch. A burst during the debounce sleep still restarts the timer, as before. A burst while the Board GET is in flight sets `needsLiveRefresh` instead of cancelling the GET. When the fetch finishes, the running task waits out the same debounce and runs once more, so any number of bursts during one fetch produce exactly one follow-up GET. `isRefreshing` drops during that debounce, so write actions unlock between passes the way they did before. The flags are `@ObservationIgnored`, and the live ones are cleared in `suspendLiveUpdates`. The task's `defer` clears the fetching flag only while its live generation is still current, so a stale task can't clear a newer generation's flag.

**Files.** `KanbanFeatureState.swift` (the coalescing function, three flags, the suspend reset), `KanbanLiveUpdateTests.swift`, and one sentence in `docs/agents/kanban.md` § Live updates.

**Risk.** Assignee history (profiles that appear only in past history) and the stats and profile-history warnings now update on load, pull, foreground, and mutations, not on every live burst. The follow-up loop adds small flags, and the live ones are reset on suspend.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3 --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests` on 9f396f3: 92 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (iPhone 17e), run twice.

Tests that pin the behavior:
- `testVisibleBoardStartsAtSnapshotCursorAndCoalescesEventBurst` now expects 1 stats call and 1 assignees call after a live burst, both from the load. It used to expect 2 of each.
- `testBurstDuringLiveRefreshQueuesOneFollowUpInsteadOfCancelling` holds the live Board GET, emits two bursts while it's held, then releases it. It checks that the held result is applied, that exactly one follow-up GET runs, that stats and assignees stay at 1 call each, and that `isRefreshing` is false when each debounce starts.
- `testSuspendDuringLiveRefreshDoesNotSwallowTheNextBurst`: when a stale task finishes, it doesn't clear the newer task's in-flight flag.
- `testLiveRefreshThatSupersedesUnsettledReadsFinishesThem`: stats and assignee history still get loaded when a live refresh takes over an unsettled `loadIfNeeded`.
- `testLiveRefreshThatSupersedesAPullFinishesItsStatsAndAssigneeReads`: a burst's live refresh takes over a pull that is still downloading. Stats and assignees are then read once more.

Each new or changed test was checked against the code without its fix. Without the latest commit's production change, the queue test and the pull-supersede test both fail (`KanbanLiveUpdateTests` run 20260923-212845).

**Measured vs reasoned.** The request counts are measured with mock-client tests. A live burst now makes 1 Board GET, 0 stats GETs, and 0 assignees GETs, down from 1 + 1 + 1. Bursts that land during an in-flight GET now produce exactly one debounced follow-up GET instead of cancelling it. The latency and radio-time win on a real tunnel is reasoned from those counts, not measured on a device. `scripts/benchmarks` was not used because it doesn't measure request counts.

## Manual test

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. The change is request scheduling with no visible UI change, and the mock-client tests pin the request counts, ordering, and the refresh flag between passes. If you want a spot check on a live server:
1. Open a busy Kanban Board over the tunnel while agents are working. Expected: cards update as events arrive.
2. Open a Card and pop back. Expected: the Board keeps updating.
3. Open the assignee filter. Expected: it still lists profiles that appear only in history.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename) (none changed)

title: perf(kanban): keep the event stream across .inactive and resume from the cursor
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #683

Stacked on #697; merge after it.

## What changed

**What's slow for the user.** With Kanban open, any `.inactive` phase stopped the Kanban SSE stream. That includes pulling down Control Center or Notification Center, a system alert or Face ID prompt, and a quick look at the app switcher. On return to `.active` the app ran four reads in series: the Board list, the full Board payload (every Card with link and comment counts), stats, and assignee history. It then reassigned the snapshot, which re-renders the whole Board, and reopened the stream. It did all of this even when nothing had changed. Mutations stay locked while `isRefreshing` is true, so over a tunnel each glance locked them for about four round trips.

**How the fix works.**
1. `KanbanLabView` now passes the raw `ScenePhase` to a new `KanbanFeatureState.setScenePhase(_:)`, which replaces `setSceneActive(_:)`. The model ignores `.inactive`, so only `.background` suspends live updates, and the stream and Board stay untouched through a transient overlay.
2. When the app returns to `.active` from `.background`, it fetches the Board with `since` set to the snapshot's `latest_event_id`. This is the cursor path, which no caller used before.
   - If the server answers `changed: false`, the app keeps the snapshot (no reassignment), skips the Board-list, stats, and assignee reads, and resumes SSE from `liveCursor`.
   - If the Board changed, the cursor response already carries the full Board. The app applies it, then reconciles the Board list and reads stats and assignee history as before, then restarts the stream. That is four requests, the same count as before.
3. The cursor is sent only when the snapshot came from the same Board and filters as the current request. Upstream's `latest_event_id` is `MAX(id)` over the whole Board's `task_events` and ignores filters, so after a failed or cancelled filter refresh (snapshot still built from the old filters) the foreground does a full filtered fetch, as it did before.
4. `refreshBoard` now returns an outcome (`failed` / `unchanged` / `changed`) instead of a Bool. Existing callers read `.succeeded`.
5. An unchanged cursor refresh reads stats and assignees only if they are still owed: either one is missing (never read, or a transient failure left only a warning), or a superseded refresh left them pending.
6. Pull-to-refresh, offline recovery, filter changes, live bursts, and mutation reconciliation keep the full `usingCursor: false` path.

**Contract.** Checked against upstream `api/kanban_bridge.py` `_board_payload` (routed at `kanban_bridge.py:1190` for `GET /api/kanban/board`). When `since >= latest_event_id` it returns `{"changed": False, "latest_event_id": latest_event_id, "read_only": False}` (lines 220-222). Otherwise it returns the full payload with `"changed": True`. The code is identical at the pinned `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA` `c67fd2dd` and at the current upstream head `b09fded7`. `KanbanBoardRequest` already sends `since`, and `KanbanBoardSnapshot` already decodes `changed` and `latest_event_id` tolerantly.

**Files.** `KanbanFeatureState.swift` (scene phase handling, refresh outcome, cursor gated on the snapshot's request, skipping unchanged supplementary reads), `KanbanLabView.swift` (forwards the phase), `KanbanLiveUpdateTests.swift`, `docs/agents/kanban.md` (live-update rules).

**Risk.**
- A Card change that writes no `task_event` is missed on foreground until the next event or a pull-to-refresh. This is the tradeoff the issue accepted.
- A Board added or renamed elsewhere while the Board itself didn't change won't show on foreground until a pull-to-refresh or a Board change.
- Holding the SSE socket through `.inactive` costs nothing extra; iOS suspends it at `.background` anyway.
- No visual change.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3 --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests` (iPhone 17e): **96 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.

New and updated tests in `KanbanLiveUpdateTests`:
- `testInactiveOverlayKeepsStreamAndBoardWithoutRequests`: after `.inactive` → `.active` there are no new Board, Board-list, or stats requests, no stream stop or restart, and no snapshot revision bump. A later live event still refreshes the Board, which shows the stream stayed current.
- `testForegroundWithoutNewEventsKeepsBoardAndResumesFromCursor`: `.background` → `.active` with a `changed:false` answer sends exactly one Board GET with `since=11`, makes no Board-list, stats, or assignee reads, leaves the snapshot and revision unchanged and `isRefreshing` false, and restarts the stream with `since=11`.
- `testUnchangedForegroundRetriesStatsThatFailedEarlier`: a stats read that failed during load is retried on a `changed:false` foreground, and its warning clears.
- `testForegroundAfterFailedFilterRefreshReloadsWithoutCursor`: a failed tenant-filter refresh, then `.background` → `.active`, sends the filtered request with no `since`, applies the new Board, and clears the failure.
- `testBackgroundSuspendsAndForegroundReconcilesBeforeRestartingStream` now pins the changed path: `since=11` is sent and the Board list, stats, and assignees are each read once more.
- `testRestoredBoardIsReconciledAndRestreamedAfterForeground` now expects `since=20` instead of no cursor.

**Measured or reasoned.** Reasoned, and pinned by request-count tests with a mock client. No device or network trace was taken.
- Per `.inactive` glance: before, 4 GETs plus 1 SSE reconnect; after, 0 requests and no reconnect.
- Per `.background` → `.active` with no Card changes: before, 4 GETs (including the full Board payload) plus a snapshot reassignment; after, 1 cursor GET (a ~60 B envelope), no reassignment, and 1 SSE reconnect.

## Manual test

On a simulator or device signed in to a server with a Kanban Board:
1. Open Kanban and pick a Board with a few Cards. Pull down Notification Center, then dismiss it. Expected: the Board does not flash a refresh, and moving a Card on the server afterwards still updates it live.
2. Background the app (Home), wait a few seconds, and reopen. Expected: the Board shows the same Cards with no visible reload; a Card change made on the server afterwards still arrives live.
3. Background the app, change a Card on the server (web UI), and reopen. Expected: the change appears after returning.
4. Apply a tenant or Profile filter while the server is unreachable (refresh fails), restore the connection, background and reopen. Expected: the Board shows Cards for the selected filter and the failure banner clears.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)

title: fix(bots): send client.capabilities and a keepalive so approvals and questions work on 0.21.4
body:
## Problem

Against hermes-agent 0.21.4 (the pinned release, `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`), the gateway refuses every server→client request for a session whose attached WebSocket client never sent `client.capabilities {server_requests:true}`: approvals are withdrawn unsent, clarify is answered with an empty string, sudo and secret are skipped (`tui_gateway/server_requests.py:117-153`, `session_transports.py:38-47`; upstream commit `f9d178f78e`, first released in v2026.9.21). `BotClient` never sends it, so on the pinned host a bot's question never shows and a dangerous command is blocked without a card. The 1.7 release candidate is affected; the App Store 1.6 build has no Bot Mode and is not.

Two smaller defects ride along: `BotClient` sends no keepalive while the host sends no JSON heartbeat (an idle socket is torn down every ~45 s), and the legacy answer paths (`clarify.respond`, `sudo.respond`, `secret.respond`, `mcp.setup.respond`) no longer exist at the pin (`-32601`).

## Fix

- [ ] In `BotClient.connect()`, right after the `gateway.ready` check and before any other RPC, send `client.capabilities` with exactly `{"server_requests": true}` on every socket including reconnects; add it to the allowlist; treat `-32601` as "older host" and keep connecting.
- [ ] Send `gateway.ping` every 15 s from the socket owner; keep the 45 s any-inbound deadline.
- [ ] Remove the dead legacy paths (`clarify.respond`, `sudo.respond`, `secret.respond`, `mcp.setup.respond`, the `<kind>.request`/`.expire` parser, `pending_clarify`) and the `mcp.setup` request kind; render `connection.request` as needs-attention; add a Skip answer (`request.answer {value:""}`) for `vault.*` requests.
- [ ] Treat `thinking.delta` as a transient status line and stop appending `reasoning.available` (it carried the final answer text live); pass `session_id` to `commands.catalog`.
- [ ] Do not auto-reply `-32601` to Desktop-only request kinds (a phone reply would pre-empt Desktop).

## Acceptance

- The first outbound frame after `gateway.ready` is `client.capabilities {server_requests:true}`; a `-32601` reply still connects (scripted `BotSocket` test).
- A live clarify on a disposable `inbox-triage` session shows the card and the answer lands (first validation of the request path against 0.21.4; #663 skipped it).
- `docs/agents/bots.md` gains the handshake, drops `mcp.setup`, and names the real pinned release.

Evidence and detail: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §0 and phase 0.1; catalog [gateway events](https://p484x5aloppn.postplan.dev).

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): Hermes as a first-class server type with a shared gateway connection
body:
## Goal

Hermes becomes a first-class server type: `ServerAccount.kind` (`webui` | `hermes`), one shared, typed gateway connection per Hermes server generalized from Bot Mode, custom headers on every request and both WebSocket upgrades, password + ws-ticket auth, a declared minimum release with an "Update Hermes" state, and runtime feature detection by probe. Existing `bot_connection` and `push_pairing` Keychain items migrate to the Hermes server without re-sign-in. Behavior-neutral for webui users.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §1 (facts) and phase 0. Catalog: [REST](https://ety4gte5kr3i.postplan.dev), [RPC](https://ldq8i221lrlj.postplan.dev).

## Depends on

The Bot Mode 0.21.4 fix (filed separately, release-blocking). Nothing else.

## Selected first batch (Uzair, 2026-09-26)

Only the following nonvisual part of 0.2 is selected, as three child issues / ready PRs in one serial dependency chain:

- [ ] #823 — typed existing Bot RPC/REST requests.
- [ ] #824 — shared HTTP authentication and origin-bound request construction; depends on #823.
- [ ] #825 — shared gateway ownership and all saved-connection Bot consumers; depends on #824.

Each child contains the implementation seams, acceptance/tests, inherited preservation requirements, and binding Decision comment. Execute with `hermex-batch 823 824 825` in Claude Code; do not select the whole parent/epic. #699 is already merged. Keep this parent open: server type/storage/pairing migration (0.3), new conversation/replay engine (0.4), minimum-version UI, and remaining foundation acceptance are not completed by this batch.

Editable Hermes headers/persistence and full #657 acceptance are deferred to 0.3. The request boundary is tested with explicitly origin-bound headers; never borrow the active webui header snapshot for the saved Bot address. No new UI/copy, mocks, main-chat migration, live-server writes, companion-repo work, or release operations are selected. Ready PRs may publish under the invoked batch flow; no merge is authorized. Stop after the chain for review and Uzair's physical-iPhone LAN/tunnel validation before storage migration. The post-#701 checkpoint remains separate.

The app compatibility pin is now 0.21.5; the migration report/local upstream reference is older. Revalidate touched contracts against the current `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`, without advancing it in this run.

## Slices

- [x] **0.2 HermesConnection:** typed requests, shared sign-in and shared socket (#823, #824, #825; landed as #826, #827, #829).
- [ ] #897: refuse Hermes releases older than the minimum (0.21.3); a missing method stays off for the connection.
- [ ] #898: custom headers for the Hermes host (delivers #657).
- [ ] #899: a Hermes server kind with its own sign-in (0.3).
- [ ] #900: add a Hermes server from onboarding and Settings (0.3; absorbs #170).
- [ ] #901: reattach a Bot Chat without applying frames early (0.4).
- [ ] #902: keep the shared socket through Control Center and close it on background (0.4).

Order: #898 → #899 → #900, with #897 (any time) before #900; separately #901 → #902. #880, #884 and #886 land first where each child says so.

Moved out (Uzair, 2026-09-28):
- Push pairing on a Hermes server → #706.
- Headers on the Kanban WebSocket → #704.
- Moving saved Bot connections, drafts and pairings off webui servers (`legacyWebuiServerID`, the `bot_connection` fallback read) → #707. In 0.3 a Hermes server copies a saved sign-in instead (only for the exact same address, #900).
- The conversation engine (#903) → #701, built with its first caller in slice 1.1.

The original slice text is in this issue's edit history.

## Acceptance

- Two configured servers, one webui and one Hermes: credentials, headers, cache, drafts and identity stay with their server; switching rebuilds the tree. (Push pairing on a Hermes server is #706.)
- A webui server's saved Bot connection can be reused when adding a Hermes server at the same address, without retyping. (Moving connections and pairings is #707.)
- A host below the minimum release shows "Update Hermes" without sending credentials; a missing method disables its control for the connection lifetime.
- Behind Cloudflare Access with service-token headers, the status check, sign-in, ticket and `/api/ws` all pass. (Kanban WS headers are #704.)

## Tests

URLProtocol mocks and the in-memory gateway transport: handshake order, single login per server, 401 policy, probe classification, header injection on the upgrade request and bearer rejection; `ServerRegistryTests` (kind default, legacy link); `HermesMoveTests` with Keychain doubles (same host, different hosts, two entries to one host, interrupted re-run, no relay call); scripted gateway fixtures for seq-continuous replay, discontinuity on new runtime id / epoch / truncated / `latest_seq < last_seen`, open-request replacement, batch clarify. Manual: physical iPhone on LAN and through the tunnel, background past the idle timeout and reattach; a mid-turn reconnect on a disposable session (only source evidence today).

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): chat and streaming parity on the Hermes gateway
body:
## Goal

Sessions chat runs on the Hermes gateway with today's behavior: send, stream, stop, steer, goal, approvals, questions, sudo/secret, attachments, btw and background, Live Activity update points, and reattach after backgrounding.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §1.2 and phase 1; the live frame order is in the plan's facts (one turn, one clarify round-trip, one post-turn reconnect were captured on a disposable session). Catalog: [gateway events](https://p484x5aloppn.postplan.dev), [RPC](https://ldq8i221lrlj.postplan.dev).

## Depends on

Foundation (phase 0).

## Slices

- [ ] **1.1 Send and reducer.** `ChatStreamCoordinator`, `ChatViewModel`: attach (resume/create), apply changed settings (`config.set` model with `--session`, `session.cwd.set` while idle), then `prompt.submit {runtime id, text, queued:true}` always (`queued:true` avoids the host's busy-input interrupt); reducer `message.start/delta/interim/complete`, `reasoning.delta` (not `thinking.delta`, not `reasoning.available`), `tool.start/complete` by `tool_id`, `session.title` as a suggestion, `session.usage`, `session.info {running}`; turn state machine with `waitingForUser`, `detached`, `reattaching`; turn identity `(stored key, turn_started_at)` replaces `stream_id`; leftover steers are requeued by the host; never `session.close` on leave.
- [ ] **1.2 Requests.** `ChatPendingActionCoordinator`, `ApprovalRequestOverlay`, `ClarificationRequestCard` reuse `BotPendingRequest`: host-computed `choices`; `approval.respond {session_id, choice, request_id}` or `request.answer`; batch clarify via `clarify.lock` per `qid` (a bare `{answer}` is acked `ok` and applied as cancel-all); sudo and secret secure cards; `request.cancel`; yolo = `config.set {key:'yolo', scope:'session'}` plus `approval.respond once` to release the open card; `open_requests` after reconnect.
- [ ] **1.3 Attachments.** `ChatAttachmentCoordinator`: images via `POST /api/chat/image-upload?profile=` and the vision reference line; documents via `file.attach` → `ref_text`; the transcript parser recognises the Hermes reference lines and `@file:` tokens and never shows host paths.
- [ ] **1.4 Goal, btw, background.** `command.dispatch {name:'goal'}` + submit the returned message; `session.control.read/update`; `prompt.btw`/`prompt.background` with `btw.complete`/`background.complete`, `events.since` after a short absence, and the durable `GET /api/sessions/bg_<id>/messages` read (confirm with one disposable run).
- [ ] **1.5 Live Activity update points** from the reducer (attributes change in the system-surfaces phase).

## Acceptance

Streaming, Stop (with `message.complete {status:'interrupted'}` then idle), steer while running, a clarify and an approval answered from the phone, an image and a PDF attached, a goal set, a btw answer shown, background during a turn and reattach with no duplicated text. Stop clears host-queued prompts and denies pending approvals; the copy says so.

## Tests

Port `StreamReconnectContract`, `Clarification*`, `SteerMessage*`, `ChatStreamCoordinator*` to scripted gateway fixtures (frames with `seq`, out-of-order replies, server requests, unprompted `message.start`, lone `error` terminator). Manual on a physical phone through the tunnel.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): sessions and projects on Hermes
body:
## Goal

The session list, transcript paging, offline cache and every session action on Hermes; projects as folder lanes.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §1.5, §2 (Sessions and projects) and phase 2. Catalog: [REST](https://ety4gte5kr3i.postplan.dev) (`/api/sessions*`), [RPC](https://ldq8i221lrlj.postplan.dev) (`session.*`, `projects.*`).

## Depends on

Foundation 0.2 and 0.3; attached-runtime actions need phase 1.

## Decisions

Decided by Uzair, 2026-10-03 (see the decision comment):

1. Unread comes from the host's `unread` field and is shared with Desktop.
2. Clear starts a new chat with the same settings and keeps the old one.
3. Move changes the working folder (`session.workspace.move`).
4. Duplicate uses `session.branch_stored`, with export → import as the fallback.

## Slices

- [x] **2.1 List and cache** → #1046 (list), #1054 (2.1b, offline cache). Hermes `Endpoint` cases; `GET /api/sessions?profile=&order=recent&archived=exclude&limit=100&offset=&exclude_sources=cron,kanban,oneshot,subagent,tool`; dedupe by `id` (pinned rows back-fill on every page); never read `total` (counts hidden rows); identity = `_lineage_root_id ?? id`; `session.active_list` for live state; `sessions.changed` trailing-debounced refresh plus one profile-scoped RPC per listed Profile after each connect; `CacheStore` keyed by (server, lineage root) with per-page upsert and no sweep on partial pages; unread from the host's `unread` field, with `PATCH /api/sessions/{id} {"unread": false}` on open (hidden Bot Chats keep local unread until #709).
- [x] **2.2 Transcript paging** → #1047. `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages?profile=&order=latest&limit=100&include_compacted=true` (offset from the newest; REST rows carry tool output, resume rows do not); row ids on `ChatMessage`/`CachedMessage`; `display_kind` markers; opaque `codex_*` arrays skipped.
- [x] **2.3 Actions** → #1048 (2.3a: rename, pin, archive, delete, export), #1049 (2.3c: edit, regenerate, undo, retry), #1050 (2.3d: compress, clear), #1051 (2.3b: branch, duplicate). rename (`PATCH`, unique titles), delete (`session.close` own idle runtime → `session.delete`; 4023 while another runtime holds it), pin, archive/restore, branch, duplicate (`session.branch_stored`; fall back to export → transform → `POST /api/sessions/import` if the copy loses tool output), compress, undo, retry and edit (`prompt.submit` with `truncate_before_row_id`), clear (starts a new chat with the same Profile, model and folder; the old chat is kept).
- [x] **2.4 Projects** → #1052. `projects.list/tree/create/update/delete`; folder lanes; "Move to project" changes the working folder with `session.workspace.move` and consequence copy (tags dropped; confirm it works on an idle session).
- [x] **2.5 Search** → #1053: `GET /api/sessions/search` with snippets, archived and Bot Chat results labeled, plus `/resume` and `/sessions`.

Split 2026-10-05 into nine sub-issues, one PR each. Order: #1046 → #1047 → #1048 → #1049 → #1050 → #1051 → #1052 → #1053 → #1054. 2.3a–2.3d and 2.5 are also blocked by #1036 and each removes its own slash-command holds. Re-checked at `ca678285`: `session.branch_stored` drops tool output, so Duplicate takes decision 4's fallback (export → import).

## Acceptance

Two Profiles listed and switched with the selected Profile as client state; pages load and dedupe; archived screen labels archived hidden Bot Chats; every action has its reverse where Hermes has one; ids that rotate on compression keep the row's identity; webui-origin rows (12-hex ids) open normally.

## Tests

URLProtocol fixtures from live-shaped rows (`APIClientSessionListTests`, `APIClientSessionMutationTests`), `CacheStoreTests` (per-page upsert, lineage keys), scripted fixtures for `session.create/resume/undo/compress/branch/delete/active_list` and the `prompt.submit` truncation.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): workspace, files and git on Hermes
body:
## Goal

Files, previews, media and the git panel on Hermes with a client-side workspace fence.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §2 (Workspace, files and git), §3 and phase 3. Catalog: [REST](https://ety4gte5kr3i.postplan.dev) (`/api/fs/*`, `/api/files/*`, `/api/git/*`).

## Depends on

Foundation; the session cwd from `session.info` / resume / the REST row (phase 2 adapter).

## Slices

Split 2026-10-08 into six child issues, one PR each, in the 2.0 milestone. Order: #1112 → #1114 → #1115 → #1116; #1113 and #1117 are independent.

- [x] #1112 **3.1 Files:** browse, preview and download the chat's `cwd` (absolute-path composition, `..`/absolute rejection, ENOENT-as-200, symlinked folders not browsable, `read-text` 512 KB, `download` 25 MB cap); caches keyed by server + stored session key + `cwd` with Profile isolation; transcript file links and MEDIA references open from the host; hidden when `terminal_backend != local`; no host paths rendered or logged.
- [x] #1113 **3.1 `@` file search:** the composer panel and file chips on `complete.path`.
- [x] #1114 **3.2 Git read:** status + `review/list` merged by path, root from `/api/fs/git-root`, diffs, branch label; writes hidden.
- [x] #1115 **3.2 Git writes:** stage/unstage/discard (`review/revert` always with `file`)/commit (zero-staged blocked; `rev-parse` for the sha)/commit selected with staging restore/push (detached HEAD blocked); AI message via `review/commit-context` + `llm.oneshot`; running-turn, conflict and cached-data guards; discard and push confirmations.
- [x] #1116 **Branch switch:** native `/api/git/branches` + `/api/git/branch/switch`; a dirty tree refuses with "Commit or discard first".
- [x] #1117 **3.3 Workspace picker:** project folders ∪ recent chat folders ∪ current folder, plus `complete.path`; `session.create {cwd}` for new chats, `session.workspace.move` for existing; registry add/rename/remove/reorder hidden.
- **3.4 Fetch, pull, new branch:** hidden on Hermes in this phase. Their app-side work moves to #710, only if its companion git routes are approved; #703 does not wait on that.

## Decisions (Uzair, 2026-10-08)

1. Fetch, Pull and New branch are hidden; app side belongs to #710 only if the routes are approved.
2. No "Allow Git changes" switch; the guards, confirmations and the existing Git visibility setting cover it.
3. Workspace registry editing is hidden and stash-and-checkout is dropped on Hermes.
4. A dirty branch switch is blocked: "Commit or discard first."
5. The folder picker is project folders, recent chat folders and the current folder; no extra session to discover the Profile default.

Record: [#713 decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6071793652).

## Acceptance

Browse, preview and download within the session workspace; the git panel shows the whole repository (Desktop's scope); every mutation refetches status; no git write runs during a turn; the panel is hidden for non-local terminal backends. #703 closes when its six child issues land.

## Tests

`APIClientGitTests`, `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests` (merge, guards, commit-selected sequence and restore), `FileBrowserViewModelTests` (path composition, fence, ENOENT-as-200, cwd change), `WorkspaceRegistryViewModelTests` (derived list), scripted fixtures for `complete.path`, `llm.oneshot`, `session.workspace.move`.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): Tasks and Kanban on Hermes
body:
## Goal

Tasks on `/api/cron/*` and Kanban on the plugin routes with its ticketed WebSocket. The data is the same host data (webui's `kanban_bridge` writes the same SQLite; cron jobs are the same `jobs.json`), so no import step.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §2 (Tasks, Kanban) and phase 4. Catalog: [REST](https://ety4gte5kr3i.postplan.dev) (`/api/cron/*`), [plugin routes](https://bvlyyj38cmqf.postplan.dev).

## Depends on

Foundation (REST client, ticket minting). No gateway socket.

## Slices

- [ ] **4.1 Tasks.** Split 2026-10-05: #1040 (manage) → #1041 (Run Now) → #1042 (history and output). Hermes `APIClient+Cron` cases with today's view-model shapes: `GET /api/cron/jobs` (bare array, all Profiles, includes paused), `POST …?profile=`, `PUT {updates}`, delete/pause/resume; derived running (`fire_claim`, `latest_execution`) and recent completions (`last_run_at`); Run Now fire-and-reconcile (the trigger is synchronous and can 524 through a tunnel; "Running" only once the server says so); paused-job confirm; run history from `…/runs` (newest 100); run detail and output from the run session's final reply (no `/api/fs/*` reads, decision 7); delivery targets; scheduler-not-ticking warning; Profile locked on edit; Toast Notifications hidden.
- [ ] **4.2 Kanban client.** Split 2026-10-05: #1043 (read-only, Scheduled and Review) → #1044 (changes). `HermesKanbanClient` conforming to `KanbanDataClient`: handshake config → boards → board with statuses from `board.columns` (8, incl. Scheduled and Review), no `changed`, no `read_only`; To Do never offered (decision 2); explicit `workspace_kind`; unassign `''`; block/unblock via `PATCH status` (success = not blocked); dependencies without id echo (`{ok, gated}`; `DELETE /links?parent_id&child_id`); tenant read-only; `age` decoded as a dict; host paths and PIDs never rendered; a 404 on `/config` = plugin absent, not an error.
- [ ] **4.3 Kanban live.** #1045, after #1043, beside #1044; it carries #898's custom headers on the socket. `KanbanWebSocketEventClient` conforming to `KanbanEventStreamingClient` (`start(board:since:)`): fresh ticket per connect as `?ticket=`, no subprotocol, open = hello, 25 s pings, cursor seeded from `latest_event_id` with regression reset, backoff 1/2/5/10/30 s, polling fallback on `board`, custom headers on the upgrade.
- [ ] `CONTEXT.md`: Status gains Scheduled and Review (#1043); Task Run (#1042).

## Decisions

Decided by Uzair, 2026-10-05. Each child's `## Decisions` has the details.

1. Temporary "Tasks" and "Kanban" items in the Hermes inbox's + menu, DEBUG and Hermex Branch only; #709's build gives them a permanent home.
2. To Do is never offered on Hermes: the host promotes a To Do Card with no open prerequisite to Ready within a minute.
3. Run Now on a paused Task asks first; the host resumes it.
4. Scheduled and Review are visible; Cards move out, never in.
5. Tasks cover all Profiles with a Profile label; the Profile is locked when editing.
6. Kanban tenant is create-only.
7. Run history is the newest 100 runs; output is the run session's final reply; no `/api/fs/*` reads.
8. The scheduler warning shows after 3 missed ticks (180 s). Toast Notifications are hidden.
9. `workspace_kind` is sent only when picked.
10. Contract checks run on `scripts/local-hermes`; tunnel checks are merge-walk phone steps; no `needs-manual-validation`.

Source corrections to the plan, at `ca678285`: the Kanban socket sends no hello and no heartbeat (the client pings); the triage → To Do create step is dropped (decision 2); run history has no per-run status.

## Acceptance

Tasks list, create, edit, pause/resume, Run Now with server-confirmed running state, history and output on Hermes; Kanban board, cards, comments, dependencies, dispatch, worker log and live updates through the tunnel on a quiet board.

## Tests

`APIClientCronEndpointTests`, `CronManagementTests` (reconcile machine with a scripted clock: 409, 524, success, paused), `TaskRunHistoryTests`, `KanbanFeatureStateTests` (Hermes handshake and validator), `KanbanLiveUpdateTests` with a fake transport. One disposable-job check that a triggered run survives the client disconnect (else an async companion route).

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): settings, profiles, models, skills, memory, insights and media on Hermes
body:
## Goal

Models, Profiles, reasoning, personalities, providers, quota, updates, skills, memory, insights and media on Hermes.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §2 (Models, profiles, settings…) and phase 5. Catalog: [REST](https://ety4gte5kr3i.postplan.dev), [RPC](https://ldq8i221lrlj.postplan.dev) (`config.*`, `model.options`, `commands.catalog`, `complete.slash`, `project.facts`, `llm.oneshot`).

## Depends on

Foundation 0.2 and 0.3.

## Slices

- [x] **5.1 Settings client and model catalog.** Done: #1015, PR #1034 (2026-10-05). `GET /api/model/options?profile=` / `model.options` adapter (groups, current, providers with `authenticated`, `is_user_defined`, `total_models`); `POST /api/model/set?profile= {scope:'main', provider, model}` with the expensive-model confirm; `GET /api/profiles` + `/active` (`current` seeds the selection); the selected Profile is per-server client state passed on every call (`switchProfile` disappears; never `POST /api/profiles/active`); `profiles.create` (+ custom endpoint); the Profile is a required parameter in the type system.
- [x] **5.2 Composer controls.** Done: #1016, PR #1037 (2026-10-05). Reasoning ladder from `capabilities[model]` with the clamped wire level shown; `config.set` session-scoped (copy says "this chat"); personality list via `complete.slash {text:'/personality '}`, set via `config.set` (Profile default; `personality_switch` marker row hidden or shown as a notice).
- [ ] **5.3 Skills and voice.** Split 2026-10-06: #1069 (list, toggle, SKILL.md) → #1070 (linked files); #1071 (dictation via `POST /api/audio/transcribe`); #1072 (Listen via `POST /api/audio/speak`, on-device fallback kept). Bot voice stays in #766 and #748 under #709 Option B.
- [ ] **5.4 Memory.** Split 2026-10-06: #1073 (MEMORY, USER and SOUL with the `§` canonicalizer, re-read-before-save and the char limits). Corrections from the pin: the mkdir retry uses `POST /api/files/mkdir` (there is no `/api/fs/mkdir`), and project context is hidden on Hermes, with no follow-up: `project.facts` returns file names only and misses `HERMES.md`.
- [ ] **5.5 Insights and updates.** Split 2026-10-06: #1074 (Insights from `/api/analytics/*` and `insights.get`); #1075 (the update machine over `/api/hermes/update*`, `/api/actions/hermes-update/status` and `/api/health`).
- [ ] Provider quota: hidden on Hermes until #710's companion route (decided 2026-10-06). `session.usage.account_lines` needs a live session, so Insights can't show it.

## Acceptance

Every Profile-scoped read switches with the selected Profile; two servers (webui and Hermes) keep separate selections; memory saves round-trip without triggering the agent's drift refusal; the update flow survives a dashboard restart.

## Tests

The `APIClient*` fixture suites from live-shaped JSON, the catalog adapter, the canonicalizer (idempotent, limit refusal), the update state machine with scripted status/404/health sequences.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): Move to Hermes with session reconciliation and fallback import
body:
**What the user gets:** A reviewed, resumable Move to Hermes flow that copies missing chats, preserves drafts and routes old entry points correctly while keeping webui available.
**Why it matters:** Existing users need to switch to direct Hermes without silent loss or misleading success.
**Cost:** Large, six independently testable PRs. Integration and physical-device gates require separate validation grants.

## Current plan · 2026-10-12

**All three foundations are merged.** Scan/import (#1213) landed in [#1221](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1221) at `76a08135`; connection/pairing (#1215) in [#1220](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1220) at `1cdde9e4`; reconciliation/drafts (#1214) in [#1222](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1222) at `b10bb8f9`. Each passed final-head CI and review before merge.

**Owner phone validation passed; final merge waits on the separate CI fix.** Uzair signed off all #1218 tests on Hermex Branch 1.9 (20261013000416), head `e1fa9b45`. #1163's focused CI fix is dispatched with merge-when-green authority. The #1218 thread will integrate it, merge #1225 after final green checks/reviews, verify the epic's remaining gates and close only when satisfied. Disposable phone-test cleanup is authorized. No production release.

**Landed #1214 behavior.** Existing Hermes chats keep their pin and archive settings. On the first move, fill eligible missing titles/folders and transfer safely identified drafts for existing and copied chats; later Copy Missing Chats Again reconciles only newly copied chats.

Persist recorded starting and intended values for metadata operations; re-read before each unsent write. Settle uncertain in-flight writes by observing the intended value, otherwise report uncertainty without resending. Server read/write races remain a documented limitation. Parent-bearing rows with unverified draft identity retain their source draft and are reported; never guess the destination key. Conflicting drafts remain untouched on both sides. A verified title collision gets one short session-ID suffix attempt within the host cap, then any further collision is reported.

Validation stays within existing permissions; no new local-server, Desktop, TestFlight, real-data migration or release grant. #1216 and #1217 are merged; #1218 is implementing under the approval below. [Prior child publication and decisions](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/707#issuecomment-6115174588).

- [x] [#1215](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1215) — commit a Move to Hermes connection and pairing safely. Depends on: none within this split.
- [x] [#1216](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1216) — resume interrupted Move to Hermes work safely. Depends on: [#1213](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1213), [#1214](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1214), [#1215](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1215).
- [x] [#1217](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1217) — route legacy entry points after Move to Hermes. Depends on: [#1215](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1215).
- [x] [#1218](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1218) — guide users through Move to Hermes. Depends on: [#1216](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1216), [#1217](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1217).

Run transfer → reconcile alongside the connection-record work; runner follows those three. Routing follows the connection record. The UI follows both runner and routing. Shared integrations are sequential after their owner child lands.

## Recovery and routing approval · 2026-10-12

Uzair approved both revised plans for Express implementation, tests, PR publication and review; stop before merge.

### Recovery (#1216)

- Select [mock A](https://uu8hz2z0vey0.postplan.dev), with corrected copy: drafts remain on this iPhone under the old server; unchecked chats are distinct from confirmed missing chats. Finish stops retries. Later Copy Missing Chats Again does not recover unfinished metadata/drafts for already-present chats. Real guided UI remains #1218's scope.
- Confirmed presence is not confirmed copying. Present/copy-unconfirmed chats follow existing-chat reconciliation on the first move (eligible missing titles/folders and verified drafts, no pin/archive changes); repeat-copy only reports them.
- Accept and document that replaying an uncertain import may recreate a chat the user deleted during the pause. Replay keeps frozen Profile/ID identity.
- Protected plan plus append-only log, orphan cleanup in pendingMoves, repeat-copy support and skipping/reporting unchecked chats are approved.
- Durable intent precedes dispatch. Final report/finished state must be durable before Keychain completion and journal deletion. Test crashes/save failures at these boundaries. A torn outcome can follow a completed remote write: retain durable intent and settle/replay according to operation type; do not infer no remote action from every torn line. Corruption handling stays conservative.

### Routing (#1217)

- Run-origin webui relay pushes, Live Activity taps and local alerts stay on their original webui server while it remains configured, preserving stream and approval access. After source removal use permitted destination routing. Ordinary links remain destination-first with source fallback only after verified absence.
- Migrated bare links/Shortcuts refuse ambiguity even with unmoved webui configured; no active/first-server tie-break among migrated candidates.
- Saved bare Shortcuts remain resolvable when move records name their Profile; ambiguity is enforced at execution. Keep on webui remains a conflicting claim after source deletion.

- Extra seams in HermesDeepLink.swift, HermesSessionListView.swift and PushAppDelegate.swift are approved. Preserve actual-Profile lookup, unknown-versus-absent distinction, loop prevention and installation pairing trust.

Uzair approved the queued validation work and explicitly said: “my live server may be used for testing if needed.” The existing #1218 thread received the instructions.

1. Run a complete guided move with isolated disposable local webui/Hermes servers, seeded data and dedicated simulator state: move, interruption, Resume, Finish early, repeat-copy, remove test source and open old links. Starting these local test services is now authorized.

It does not authorize migration/export of real chats, edits/deletion of real sessions, host/tunnel restarts, global Profile changes, real pairing/configuration replacement or daily-driver connection removal. These grants supersede earlier statements that local end-to-end, isolated Desktop and Branch TestFlight authorization were pending. The validation gates themselves are not passed by authorization; results must be recorded.

## Pre-phone validation follow-up approved · 2026-10-12

Uzair approved excluding external read-only Claude Code/CLI rows from migration in #1225, testing mixed listings with those rows visible, refreshing Hermex Branch, preparing a usable disposable phone-test setup/checklist, and tracking the two smaller observations separately. The existing #1218 thread received the work; merge remains paused.

Uzair approved the next steps:
