No production release, new TestFlight upload, tester changes or real-data migration is authorized. The prior merge pause is superseded only by the conditional green-check merge authority above.

## Decisions

## Current authorization

**Landed connection behavior.** #1215 includes the approved small PushRegistrar.swift queue/protocol change. Switch to the destination only on Done in #1218, never during commit.

#1213 is merged. Its approved behavior preserves exported images and historical counters, scans without switching Profiles, and exports after Move confirmation through a private source cookie jar with scoped per-Profile switching. #1216 owns uncertain import replay using #1213's pre-dispatch hook and outcomes. [Contract and validation limits](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/707#issuecomment-6115975207).

Uzair also authorized live-server testing and validation if needed. This permits read-only checks and disposable test sessions/data created and cleaned up by the task under the repository rules. It does not authorize migrating or changing real sessions, switching global server Profiles, changing host configuration, restarting the host/tunnels, replacing or deleting real push pairings, or releases. Credentials and real content stay out of output; fixtures must be sanitized. A pairing read that creates keys is not read-only. Broader mutations must be identified before proceeding. [Decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/707#issuecomment-6115456085).

- Guided sheet A, B3 Moved label, explicit mapping M and interruption/removal S. The old entry remains usable with a warning; no read-only chat mode. [Mocks](https://7wnkidmw2l6z.postplan.dev).
- Uncertain changes are report-only. Record in-flight intent before dispatch; after interruption recognize achieved outcomes and report uncertainty without replaying metadata. No exactly-once promise.
- At most four scan requests per server. Failed reads are unknown, not absent. Cross-Profile scanning is best-effort duplicate detection, not concurrency-safe uniqueness enforcement.
- Existing chats route by verified actual location; import/new-chat mapping is separate. Ambiguous bare links/Shortcuts refuse without an active-server preference.
- Pairing verification is after Move confirmation only. Copy only between verified shared installations and never overwrite an existing destination pairing. Cross-host migration retains the destination's pairing; removing the last source installation entry stops that old host's pushes.
- Durable legacy records live on the destination in Keychain with acknowledged persistence. A protected temporary journal holds unfinished operations; failed saves must not publish success.
- Explicit Profile selections, including Keep on webui; no silent unmatched-Profile fallback. Source-only/oversized/unknown chats are reported, never trimmed.
- Keep broad owner backfill excluded. Preserve destination credentials/custom headers and avoid silently replacing existing drafts or adopted-server settings.
- Any still-unsettled behavior (including active-server switch timing or refusal changes conflicting with previous policy) must be resolved in the implementation plan, not inferred from old preparation prose.

## Contract corrections and scope

Preparation checked hermes-agent `ca678285` (0.21.5), webui `c67fd2dd` and app `8ac74b75` by source, not a live server. Reverify at implementation against the compatibility pin.

Use paged per-Profile Hermes sessions, not the all-Profile listing capped at 500 rows per Profile. Import without titles, then reconcile title collisions via PATCH. Unread state is host-owned. Validate folders with workspace.move; report missing paths. Copy confirmed missing chats under the verified import caps and report 400/413 outcomes without silent loss. Same-host metadata may affect shared underlying data: never promise webui is unchanged.

Same-address replacement already exists separately; integrate without regressing it. All entry points and server isolation belong to the acceptance scope.

## Validation gates — live test grant recorded above; other grants pending

Focused unit tests use URLProtocol, Keychain doubles and deterministic interruption fixtures. The children own exact coverage. Main app and tests are expected targets; shared changes require explicit extension-membership review.

Before completion: local disposable Hermes/webui end-to-end move; Desktop with multiple connections must list/open/resume imported chats and @session: links, including imports after its initial backfill; representative tunnel timing; signed simulator validation; physical-phone push/link/Shortcut checks after source removal. A TUI-only pass does not establish Desktop compatibility. Failed Desktop validation returns for a narrow owner decision under #713's release rule.

The live-test permission above covers scoped read-only/disposable validation; other validation environments still need permission. No live migration of real data, release or TestFlight action is authorized. A real move writes user session metadata and needs its own explicit grant.

## Decision history

- [Published split and final four decisions](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/707#issuecomment-6115174588).
- [Approved design and independent-review corrections](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/707#issuecomment-6115082829).

title: feat(hermes): native OAuth sign-in with PKCE
body:
## Goal

Sign in to OIDC-gated Hermes hosts (`nous`, `self-hosted`) from the phone with native PKCE; store bearer and refresh tokens per server; mint ws-tickets with the bearer. Required before webui removal (settled decision).

Facts at the pin: `/auth/native/authorize` accepts only `http://127.0.0.1` or `http://[::1]` redirect URIs (custom schemes, universal links and `localhost` get 400; verified live); the gateway brokers the IdP; the code lasts 120 s single-use; `POST /auth/native/token` returns bearer + refresh; bearer works on every REST route and can mint a ws-ticket; the upgrade itself needs the ticket. Password providers never need a browser (authorize → `POST /auth/password-login` returns the code in JSON → token), so the live host and phase 0 need none of this.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §1.4 and phase 8. Catalog: [REST](https://ety4gte5kr3i.postplan.dev) (`/auth/native/*`, `/api/auth/*`).

## Depends on

Foundation 0.3. Gate: the device spike (8.1) reports go before 8.2–8.4 are scheduled.

## Slices

- [ ] **8.1 Device spike (no product code).** `NWListener` on `127.0.0.1` with an ephemeral port answering `302 <app scheme>://done`; `ASWebAuthenticationSession` with `prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession`; app switch to a password manager mid-login (rebind the same port on foreground, hold a background task); Local Network prompt; Safari HTTPS upgrade on the loopback hop. Report go/no-go with evidence.
- [ ] **8.2 Token store and REST bearer.** `hermes_credential.oauth {provider, userID, accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt}`; REST sends `Authorization: Bearer` from a session with no cookie storage; proactive refresh at 5 min, reactive on 401 `session_expired`, single-flight per server across the app and App Intents; persist a rotated refresh token before using the new access token; 401 on refresh signs out.
- [ ] **8.3 Browser flow.** Detect OIDC hosts (`auth_flows ∋ native_pkce` and a provider with `supports_password:false`); chooser handling; `state` check; 120 s exchange; sign-out deletes tokens (optional best-effort revoke via `POST /auth/logout` with the refresh cookie).
- [ ] **8.4 Header policy.** Reject any custom `Authorization` on OAuth-signed-in servers; point Cloudflare Access users at the two-header service-token form. Document that the browser leg cannot carry custom headers (`additionalHeaderFields` applies to the initial load only and accepts only `X-` names), so header-gated proxies need their own browser login.
- [ ] Later (optional): browserless native flow for password hosts (a 30-day refresh token instead of the stored password).

## Acceptance

An OIDC host signs in through the system browser and loads sessions and chat; cancel, expiry, relaunch, sign-out and two-server isolation behave; password hosts are unaffected.

## Tests

PKCE pair generation, listener callback parsing with `state`, refresh single-flight and rotation persistence, 401 handling, provider detection; URLProtocol mocks. Manual: physical device against an OIDC host.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: design(hermes): Chat vs Bots on a Hermes server
body:
## Decision needed

On Hermes a Bot is a Profile and its canonical chat is one hidden session titled "Bot Chat"; ordinary sessions are per Profile; group rooms are install-wide. Both options below run the same shared connection and the same conversation engine (phase 0), so foundation work does not wait on this choice. The maintainer decides through the mock gate.

Constraints that hold for both: REST session lists never include hidden rows; `session.list {include_hidden:true}` includes them without `last_active`/pin/archive; push taps must land on the exact session (today Bot taps land on the inbox); hidden rows other than Bot Chats (room plumbing, Desktop-hidden) are never shown.

## Option A: one session list, Bots as a lens

A Profile strip of bot avatars above the list; "All" merges every Profile's sessions by recency with a Profile avatar per row; selecting a Profile filters and pins its Bot Chat as the first row; rooms in their own section; one chat view (the Bot Chat adds the face, mentions and the identification note). One identity scheme for drafts, unread, cache, deep links, push and Live Activities (`server`, `accountID`, `profile`, lineage root). Deletes the separate inbox, `BotModeGate` for Hermes servers, the separate Bot deep-link host and `botDestination`. Trade-offs: larger (roughly 2.5–4k lines, 3–5 PRs); moves Bot beta users off a screen they know; looks different from Desktop; two pin concepts (bot pin writes Desktop `ui_meta`, session pin writes REST) kept legible by the strip-vs-rows split; a merged hidden-row list with full flags needs an optional companion route.

## Option B: two surfaces on one shared connection

Today's Bots inbox stays; a Hermes Sessions list sits beside it; both share the connection and `sessions.changed`. Trade-offs: smaller (roughly 1.5–2.5k lines, 2–3 PRs); matches Desktop's separate Bots pane; keeps two unread models, two Live Activity identity schemes and the push/deep-link split forever; "where did my bot's cron run go?".

## Recommendation

Option A. It mirrors the host's own model (Profiles own sessions, one of which is the canonical chat) and removes a parallel routing split that B would carry past webui removal. B can collapse into A later without touching the engine.

## Mock gate

Static mocks via html-communication: the Profile strip with the pinned Bot Chat row; the All view with a Rooms section; B's two tabs; each light/dark with Dynamic Type. Wait for the pick before implementing.

## After the decision

- [ ] List and IA per the choice.
- [ ] Identity unification (drafts, unread, Live Activity key, deep links, push) with migration of the UUID-keyed stores.
- [ ] Under A: delete the inbox path and the gate; under B: re-plumb the inbox onto the shared connection.
- [ ] Bots in the "New Chat in Profile" Shortcut picker follows the choice.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) phase 9 and §7. Related: #299, #493, #332.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: feat(hermes): companion plugin routes for confirmed gaps
body:
## Goal

Extend the `hermex-push` companion plugin with the routes the confirmed gaps need, and only those. Plugins can add authenticated REST routes, their own ticketed WebSocket or SSE, hooks and slash commands; they cannot add RPC methods or `/api/ws` events, cannot declare public routes, and are mounted once at web-server import, so every new route needs the host's API process restarted (no remote API can do it; `POST /api/gateway/restart` restarts only the messaging gateway). Ship routes in at most two batches.

Plan: [migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) §1.6, §3 and phase 10. Catalog: [plugin routes](https://bvlyyj38cmqf.postplan.dev).

## Depends on

Maintainer approval per route (plan §7). Phases 3 and 5 hide the features until the routes answer.

## Slices

- [ ] **10.1** `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/capabilities` (loaded version and route list); the app compares with `GET /api/dashboard/plugins` to tell "installed but not loaded" from "old plugin"; provisioning shows the restart instruction on a 404 `No such API endpoint`.
- [ ] **10.2** `POST …/git/fetch`, `…/git/pull` (`--ff-only`), `…/git/branch` with `{path, remote?, ff_only}` / `{path, name, start?}` on the core's hardened non-interactive git runner, 60 s timeout, `{ok, message}`; app-side Fetch, Pull, New branch appear only when the route answers.
- [ ] **10.3** `GET …/provider-quota?provider=&profile=&refresh=` wrapping `agent.account_usage.fetch_account_usage` in webui's envelope with a 45 s cache; app-side quota panel gated on it.
- [ ] **10.4 (only if option A is chosen)** `GET …/sessions?profile=&order=recent&limit=&offset=` returning REST-shaped rows including hidden Bot Chats.
- [ ] Plugin unit tests in the plugin repo; app-side URLProtocol fixtures and 404-body classification; upgrade = force reinstall + host restart (the subdirectory install cannot `git pull`).

## Not planned

A plugin event socket for parity (the gateway already broadcasts change signals in the foreground; APNs covers the background), memory and cron-output routes (core file routes cover them), a tag store for projects, raw-SQL Kanban tenant edits.

Model and harness: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5 workers).

title: epic(hermes): migrate Hermex from hermes-webui to Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** Hermex 2.0 works fully with only a direct Hermes host: no hermes-webui to install, secure or update. Existing webui servers keep working as legacy.
**Why it matters:** webui is a third-party bridge whose API drifts from Hermes, and every Hermes-only capability is out of reach through it. Bot Mode already proved the direct connection on LAN and through a Cloudflare tunnel.
**Cost:** Large. Twelve phases, tracked in the [2.0 milestone](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/milestone/2). Needs the owner's phone for the system-surface phases; the post-#701 checkpoint has passed.


## Current plan · 2026-10-15

**All 2.0 code has merged.** Every phase is done, and [#1264](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1264) (Move to Hermes for every webui user) merged and closed on 2026-10-15. webui stays supported as legacy; removal is not scheduled. [Owner release rule](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6104134416).

What's left is the release:

1. Upload a production RC from master (`fe7d1349` or later) per `TESTFLIGHT.md`.
2. Run a short pass on that build: install it over the App Store version, sign in, run one chat, then go through the [short-pass checklist](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6181195757) and its [2026-10-15 additions](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6200273889). The full pass on Branch build 20261014120854 doesn't need repeating ([hand-off](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6173687330)).
3. Beta App Review, then release on the App Store.
4. This epic closes when 2.0 ships.

**2.0.1:** [#1241](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1241), [#1274](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1274), [#1280](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1280), [#1333](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1333) (added 2026-10-23: reinstall-level crash on open, fix in [#1334](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1334)). **After 2.0:** contributor PRs per the [2026-10-14 review](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6181739985); [#1111](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1111) waits on a tunnel test.

**Caveat:** browser sign-in has never been tested against a real OIDC provider. The changelog says so.

**Completed foundations:** phases 0–4, 6, 7, 9 and 12 have landed, plus Bot Chat retirement [#1127](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1127). Bot and ordinary Hermes chats share ChatView; rooms keep their own screen, cache and local search. The approved [design and routing](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6088507479) remains in force.



## Problem

Hermex talks to `hermes-webui`, a third-party bridge that users must install, secure and update beside Hermes itself. Its API drifts independently of `hermes-agent`, Hermex pins and tracks it (`UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA`), and every Hermes-only capability is out of reach. Bot Mode already speaks to Hermes directly (`/api/ws` JSON-RPC plus the dashboard REST API) and proves the transport works from a phone, on LAN and through a Cloudflare tunnel. This epic moves the whole app onto Hermes for Hermex 2.0 and keeps webui as legacy.

**Reports.** [Migration plan](https://gink1rr89x8r.postplan.dev) · API catalog pinned to hermes-agent v0.21.4 / `d337b736`: [Gateway RPC](https://ldq8i221lrlj.postplan.dev) · [Gateway events, server requests, sockets](https://p484x5aloppn.postplan.dev) · [Dashboard REST](https://ety4gte5kr3i.postplan.dev) · [Plugin routes](https://bvlyyj38cmqf.postplan.dev). Catalog totals: 704 entries (283 REST, 220 RPC, 12 server requests, 121 events, 53 plugin routes, 15 sockets), 428 live-verified. Parity: of the 130 webui endpoints Hermex uses, 21 exact, 93 reshaped, 10 partial, 4 missing, 2 not needed.

## Settled decisions

1. Hermes becomes the primary backend. **Hermex 2.0 ships only when the Hermes connection is fully implemented and current webui users can switch to Hermes easily and seamlessly without losing functionality.** The app is fully functional with only a direct Hermes host connection. [Release rule amended 2026-10-10](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6104134416). webui stays supported as legacy: bug fixes only, no new features (in force since 2026-09-26), and development targets Hermes. Removal is not scheduled; #712 now makes Hermes the default instead. *(Amended 2026-10-02. Previously webui was removed once every feature was on Hermes or dropped, OAuth had shipped, and Hermes had been the default and webui users had seen a notice for one release each.)*
2. Hermes is a first-class server type (a server is webui or Hermes) with its own credentials, custom headers, cache, drafts and push pairing; saved Hermes connections and push pairings migrate without re-sign-in. *(Amended 2026-09-28: #700 ships the server kind and copies a saved sign-in for the same address; moving saved connections is #707, and push pairing on a Hermes server is #706.)*
3. Transport: gateway JSON-RPC over `/api/ws` plus dashboard REST, generalized from the Bot client. Not the OpenAI-compatible API server (#177 is superseded).
4. Auth: password plus ws-ticket and custom headers first. Native OAuth with PKCE (#708) ships in 2.0 if its device spike (slice 8.1) reports go; otherwise it moves to a 2.x release. *(Amended 2026-10-13: Uzair kept #708 in 2.0; the slice 8.1 spike still runs first.)* *(Amended 2026-10-02. Previously OAuth was required before webui removal, which is no longer scheduled.)*
5. `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` stays the pin; a declared minimum release with an "Update your Hermes" state; runtime feature detection by probe (no `describe` RPC exists).
6. Gaps: use an existing Hermes capability even if shaped differently; else a companion route in the `hermex-push` plugin; else drop by explicit maintainer decision. No upstream change requests.
7. A "Move to Hermes" action per server. Finding: same-host webui sessions already live in Hermes's `state.db` under the same id, so the move reconciles metadata and imports only what is missing.
8. On Hermes a Bot is a Profile and its chats are sessions. #709 takes Option B: separate Bots and Sessions surfaces on one shared connection. *(Amended 2026-10-09: a bot's chat now opens in the regular chat screen, and Bot Chat's own screen retires in #1127. Rooms keep their own screen.)* The v2 bottom bar is approved; the 2026-10-08 amendment keeps its switch visible, adds Bot creation in Hermex and an All Profiles session filter with Profile-name tags, and remembers the last tab (Sessions first).
9. Parity with Hermes Desktop and the CLI, not just webui; Hermes-only capabilities are in scope (amended 2026-10-05, #1036).
10. Project tags are dropped on Hermes; projects are folder lanes (#702 slice 2.4; #212 closed). Confirmed 2026-09-26.
11. Checkpoint after #701: confirm chat streaming and reconnect hold over LAN and the Cloudflare tunnel before committing to later phases. If they don't, reassess the migration. **Passed 2026-10-05.** The migration continues.
12. #703's workspace/Git decisions are approved (2026-10-08): no extra Git opt-in switch, registry editing and stash-and-checkout hidden, dirty branch switching blocked, and the folder list derived without an extra default-folder probe. Fetch/Pull/New branch app work is gated under #710; #703 can finish with its six native children.
13. [#706](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/706) system-surface decisions are approved ([2026-10-10](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/713#issuecomment-6104134416)): onboarding leads with Hermes and keeps Web UI behind a link; the Connect page's Bot Mode beta gate stays until [#712](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/712). The Shortcut picker groups Profiles by configured server, lists each once and starts a new session. On cold launch, an unpaired Hermes Live Activity ends as complete with outcome unknown unless the host still lists the session as running. Shares, New Chat and session links stay on Hermes for Hermes-only users. Unreachable taps use the existing Sessions-list toast; previews-off lookup refuses ambiguous Profiles; subagent pushes open their parent one hop up; another process's approval runtime opens without an invented card. Pairing retains the gateway restart flow, adds missing-route classification and preserves a pairing shared by two entries on one host. Password-less webui move messaging belongs to [#707](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/707). [#1165](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1165) is superseded by [#1179](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1179), and [#488](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/488) by [#1180](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1180) and [#1181](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1181); both old issues are closed.

## Facts that shape the work

- **Resolved release blocker:** #699 landed in PR #775. `BotClient` now sends `client.capabilities {server_requests:true}` and keepalive; preserve that handshake in the shared connection. Physical-phone validation is not implied by the PR being merged.
- Plugin routes mount once at web-server import and `POST /api/gateway/restart` restarts only the messaging gateway, so every companion route needs the host restarted by the user; routes ship in batches (#710) and provisioning copy says so (#706).
- Native PKCE accepts only loopback redirect URIs; password hosts need no browser, OIDC hosts need an in-app loopback listener that gets a device spike first (#708).
- The reconnect contract (20 s orphan grace, 600 s activity threshold, a 512-event replay ring per runtime, runtime-id change as the reap signal) is written up in the plan §1.2 and lands in #700.

## Phase preparation

Before a phase runs, collect its open decisions in one message and split it into batch-ready GitHub sub-issues, one PR each: file-level seams, a `## Decisions` section, blocker links, and contracts checked against `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`. A phase is split only when every planned slice has its own child issue. Slice just in time, one agent per phase. #709, #711 and #712 run as they are; #710 gets one small issue per approved route.

Bot follow-ups: #1127 supersedes #564, #748, #766 and #1038, closed 2026-10-09. #745 (Edit/Regenerate in a bot's chat) and #769 remain outside 2.0 unless the owner selects them. Voice mode #36 and other new features also remain outside it. #1017's sent-attachment work is merged.

title: perf(chat): cache per-message media and link scans for settled rows
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #680

## What changed

**Problem.** Tapping Send and a reply finishing both flip transcript-wide flags (`hasActiveStream`, regenerate/edit/fork, listening) that are part of every row's Equatable inputs, so every `MessageBubbleView` body runs again. Each assistant bubble then repeats two uncached text scans: `TranscriptMediaParser.segments` (a per-character walk) and the link-preview `firstWebURL` (regex plus `NSDataDetector` on every line, even when the message has no URL). User rows ran the link scan twice per body. On a full page that is an estimated 25-75 ms of main-thread work during the send insert animation.

**Fix** (the approach the maintainer picked: a content-keyed `NSCache` plus one `previewURL` read per body; the environment-flag follow-up is skipped):

- `TranscriptMediaSegmentCache.segments(in:workspaceRoot:isStreaming:)` in `TranscriptMedia.swift`: a bounded `NSCache` (countLimit 240) keyed by message text plus workspace root. Streaming text is parsed without touching the cache, so partial content is never stored.

title: perf(chat): derive reasoning groups once per transcript change, not on every stream tick
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #669

## What changed

**Problem.** `ChatViewModel.displayedReasoningGroups` was a computed property, so every read re-derived the reasoning cards for every past assistant turn: splitting each reply into paragraphs, running `replacingOccurrences` once per paragraph, and normalizing each dedupe key twice. It was read in the `messages` didSet (every 48 ms drain tick) and again on every ChatView pass (stream ticks, the ~16 ms reasoning flushes, each composer keystroke), and the answer was the same every time. Each transcript row also got a freshly built copy of the whole array, so the row's `.equatable()` guard compared every row against every reasoning byte.

**Fix (follows the issue's fix sketch):**
1. `displayedReasoningGroups` is now a stored `private(set) var`, derived in `recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages()`, which already runs when `messages`, `messagesOffset`, `completedReasoningGroups`, `streamingAssistantMessageID` or the tool groups change. It is reassigned only when the groups actually differ, so observers stay quiet and the array buffer stays the same across stream ticks and keystrokes.
2. A new `ReasoningCandidateCache` (`@ObservationIgnored` on the view model) memoizes the costly per-candidate work: echo stripping plus the normalized dedupe key, now computed once per candidate instead of twice. Entries are keyed by `message:<anchorID>` or `archived:<group id>` and reused only when their reasoning and visible text equal the current inputs (unchanged messages share string storage, so the check is cheap). Each pass keeps only the entries it used, so the cache never outgrows the loaded transcript and needs no separate clear on a session or server switch; it lives on the per-session view model under the server-keyed subtree. The existing static `reasoningDisplayGroups(messages:messageOffset:archivedGroups:)` keeps its signature with a throwaway cache, so its callers and tests are unchanged.
3. The same recompute stores `reasoningGroupsByAnchorID: [String?: [ReasoningGroup]]` (the nil key holds unanchored cards). `ChatTranscriptView` passes each row `reasoningGroupsByAnchorID[anchorID] ?? []` and the loose blocks read the nil entry, replacing the per-row filters. A row's `==` now looks only at its own, stable cards.

Rendering is unchanged: grouping by anchor keeps the order the old filter produced. Turn folds, terminal reply IDs and the trim checks are untouched, as the issue asks.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer waived the issue's "confirm on device with Instruments" step. The win is reasoned from the audit's replica numbers (2.8–7.4 ms per derivation at 12–25 turns, 2–3 derivations per tick) and pinned by tests below. It was not measured on a device.

## How it was tested

New tests:
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testStreamTicksAndKeystrokesReuseTheStoredReasoningGroups`: loads a two-turn reasoning session; a second read (a keystroke-only pass) returns the same array buffer; after a send, a stream token tick fires no observation on `displayedReasoningGroups` or `reasoningGroupsByAnchorID` and the buffer is unchanged. Fails on the old code.
- `APIClientSessionDetailTests.testReasoningCandidateCacheRederivesOnlyChangedOrUnseenCandidates`: a tick re-derives only the candidate whose inputs changed, and an entry skipped in one pass is dropped.
- `APIClientSessionDetailTests.testMemoizedReasoningDisplayGroupsMatchAFreshDerivationAfterAStreamTick`: after a tick where the streaming reply starts echoing its reasoning, the memoized groups equal a fresh derivation (guards against stale cache entries).

title: perf(bots): stop per-delta redraws and render the live bot reply through the streaming renderer
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #679

## What changed

**Problem.** While a bot reply streams, Bot Chat wastes main-thread work in two ways.

1. Every `message.delta` frame (one per token, 30-50/s) went into the mutating `liveActivity.apply`. It changes nothing for that event type, but a mutating call on an `@Observable` stored property notifies observers anyway, so the whole Bot Chat screen redrew at the token rate. The live text itself only changes with the ~250 ms snapshot.
2. The live reply rendered through the settled Markdown path. On every snapshot the full reply was parsed as one document, a new entry went into the shared 240-entry layout cache (a long reply evicts most of the settled rows' entries), and any fenced code block was reset to plain and then re-highlighted on the main thread, which can flicker.

**Fix.**

1. `BotConversation.applyActivity` returns early (`guard BotTurnActivity.handles(type) else { return false }`) before it touches `liveActivity`. The live `observe()` path and the replay loop both go through `applyActivity`, so one guard covers both.
2. `BotArtifactMessageView` renders the live reply with `MarkdownRenderer(content:isStreaming: isLive)`, the streaming renderer that Sessions already uses. The live reply now bypasses the shared layout cache, and code in the growing part stays plain until the reply settles. Past the renderer's 6,000-character stable-chunk threshold, sealed chunks also skip re-layout, and their code highlights once. The settled row that replaces the live one is unchanged: cached layout, highlighting, selection.
3. Deviation from the issue sketch: the streaming renderer's reveal fade stays off for Bots, through a new `allowsStreamedTextAnimation` environment flag. It defaults to true, and `StreamingMarkdownChunkedView` reads it alongside the existing setting and Reduce Motion. A Bot snapshot delivers 250 ms of text at once, and fading all of it in leaves the latest edge blank. With the fade on, the existing `testLongInflightResponseRemainsVisibleAtLatestEdge` failed 4 of 6 steps. `docs/agents/bots.md` already ruled out reveal animation on coalesced snapshots for this reason, and it now describes the new path. Sessions keeps its fade.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer waived the Instruments pass the issue asked for. The win is reasoned from the code and pinned by tests: `message.delta` no longer notifies observers, and the live reply stays out of the shared layout cache. It was not measured on a device.

Left out on purpose: Bot rooms and delegation reports (the issue doesn't name them), and reasoning-delta coalescing (the issue says to leave it out). #564 (Bot streaming fade parity) stays open, because this PR deliberately does not add the fade.

## Design

Mocks: https://hernk2anzqem.postplan.dev

Pick **B**: the streaming renderer with no reveal fade on Bots. It gets the perf win (no shared layout cache, stable chunks skip re-layout, no re-highlight on every snapshot). The only visible change is that code in the part still streaming stays plain and highlights once it settles. **A** (the Sessions-style fade from the issue sketch) was rejected because a whole snapshot fading in blanks the latest edge, and the visible-output XCTest fails with it. **C** (today's look) keeps the per-snapshot cost.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatStreamCoordinatorTests --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownMathLayoutCacheTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingMarkdownSupportTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingTextFadeTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests` gave **232 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**. The skip is the existing `BotChatPresentationTests.testDelegationCompletionCardKeepsTheFullReportInItsSheet` (no accessibility tree in-process on this toolchain).
- New tests, both of which fail on the old code (with the production change stashed: 0 passed, 2 failed):
  - `BotConversationTests.testMessageDeltaNeverNotifiesLiveActivityObservers`: on both the live and replay paths, an observation probe on `liveActivity` records no change for `message.delta`. The old code recorded 1.
  - `BotConversationTests.testLiveReplyRendersOffTheSharedLayoutCache`: the live reply's text never lands in `MarkdownMathLayoutCache`.
- The existing `testLongInflightResponseRemainsVisibleAtLatestEdge` still passes.
- `ObservationChangeProbe` in `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests.swift` went from `private` to internal so the Bot tests can reuse it.

No after screenshot: the only visible difference (plain code in the part still streaming) appears mid-stream, and producing a live Bot reply means sending a message to a real bot, which was out of scope for this run. A settled Bot chat renders exactly as on master. The branch build launched and signed in cleanly on the iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator.

On a Debug build of `issue/679-live-bot-reply`:

1. Open a Bot chat and ask for a long answer with a Swift or Python code block. Expected: text appears solid with each snapshot (no fade-in), and the latest edge never goes blank. Code in the part still streaming stays plain and highlights once it settles (at the latest when the reply finishes).
2. Once the reply settles, long-press or select its text. Expected: selection and Ask Hermex work as before, and the code is highlighted.
3. Run a Sessions chat stream. Expected: the reveal fade there is unchanged.

title: perf(chat): scan the streaming reply once per update, not 8-10 times
body:
Was stacked on #714 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at dd0c646.

## Linked issue

Fixes #675

## What changed

**Problem.** While an assistant reply streams, every 48 ms drain tick re-ran about 8-10 passes over the whole reply on the main actor: a media parse that checked three markers at every character and recopied the growing text run on every line, four block splits that each allocated and trimmed a String per line and walked graphemes to measure chunk size, and two renderer passes, one of them on stale text. That cost grows with reply length, so late in a 20-40 KB reply it can take several ms per tick.

**Fix** (issue items 1-3, plus the skip-work half of 4; the `Task.yield` indirection stays):
1. `TranscriptMediaParser`: a byte pre-scan for the only markers a media segment can start with (`![`, `MEDIA:`, `file://`, or `[` for Bots). A reply with none of them returns `[.text(markdown)]` immediately. A reply that has one skips the per-character parse on every line that has none. Text runs build up in one pending buffer that grows in place (`SegmentBuilder`) instead of being recopied for each line.
2. `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter`: finds line ends by byte, keeping the old rule that a `\r\n` pair does not end a line. Trims Substrings in place (same scalar set as `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`). Counts the 6,000 seal threshold in UTF-8 bytes, which is O(1) on native strings (`stableChunkTargetUTF8Count`). This is the one intended behavior change: non-ASCII replies seal their stable chunks a little sooner.
3. `StreamingMarkdownChunkedView`: splits once per body. The `onChange` handler reuses that split, and the previous active tail is kept in `@State` (`lastActiveMarkdown`), so old content is no longer re-split.
4. `StreamingMarkdownRenderer`: the displayed text now goes to an equatable child view. On the first pass of each update, before the yield catches `displayedContent` up, the trim, fallback policy and math layout are skipped because the text has not changed.

Adds `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` (built with -O on the host, like `benchmark-math-formatting`; takes an optional source root so it can compare against another checkout).

**Measured vs reasoned.** The per-tick win on a device is reasoned, not measured with Instruments; the maintainer chose to skip the device measurement. What was measured is the host benchmark on the Mac (median ms per call, base branch → this branch):
- media parse, 30 KB code-heavy reply with no media: 3.67 → 0.04
- media parse, same reply with one image: 3.64 → 0.74
- block split, 30 KB: 3.27 → 0.28 (and one split per tick now instead of four)

Behavior was also checked against the old code with host fuzzing: 80,000 random marker-heavy inputs gave identical parser output, and random unicode, CRLF and fence inputs gave identical splitter output once the threshold unit is held equal.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air> --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMediaParserTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitterTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingReasoningTextStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMarkdownImageTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownMathRendererTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingTextFadeTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests` → **179 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.
- New tests: `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitterTests/testStableChunkThresholdCountsUTF8Bytes` (fails on the old code: 0 chunks where 1 is expected), `testIndentedFenceWithTrailingWhitespaceKeepsItsBody`; `TranscriptMediaParserTests/testReplyWithoutMediaMarkersIsOneTextSegment`, `testTextAroundMediaMergesIntoOneRunPerGap`, `testLocalFileLinkWithoutImageMarkerStillParsesForBots`.
- The renderer changes (items 3 and 4) are SwiftUI structure and have no dedicated unit test; counting splits or body passes would need a production seam. They rest on the existing streaming-render and fade-window tests above.
- `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` (host, -O): numbers above.

**Manual test.** Covered by tests; no manual check needed. The rendering path and its outputs are unchanged apart from the byte threshold, which the new splitter test pins, and the fade-window and streaming-render tests pass. title: perf(chat): keep transcript environment actions stable so settled rows skip stream ticks
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #673

Was stacked on #715 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at 617956c.

## What changed

**Problem.** Two transcript environment values were closures rebuilt on every parent body pass. `ChatTranscriptView` (and `BotChatView`) published `\.chatDisclosureToggled` as a fresh closure, and `ChatView` built a new `OpenURLAction(handler: handleTranscriptLink)`. `ChatView.body` re-runs on every paced stream tick (~20 Hz) and every composer keystroke. SwiftUI can't compare closures, so every reader of those keys ran again on each pass, even behind the transcript's `.equatable()` rows. Those readers are tool groups (which re-format every tool call), log rows, marker cards, and link readers.

**Fix.** This covers issue decisions (a) and (b), including `BotChatView`. Fix (c), the `ResponseTextSelection` rootView skip, is left out.
- `\.chatDisclosureToggled` now holds a `ChatDisclosureToggleAction` reference, which has a mutable `handler` and `callAsFunction`. Existing `chatDisclosureToggled()` call sites don't change. The default is a shared no-op.
- A `TranscriptLinkRouter` owns one lazily built `OpenURLAction`. The action forwards to the router's current `handler` through `[weak self]` and falls back to `.systemAction`.
- Two modifiers, `.chatDisclosureToggled(perform:)` and `.transcriptLinks(perform:)`, keep that instance in their **own** `@State`. They refresh `handler` in place and write the same instance to the environment. Nothing observes `handler`, so readers aren't invalidated, and a tap still runs the latest closure (latest scroll proxy, latest `session.workspace`).
- The three owners replace their inline closures with these modifiers.

The instance lives in the modifier's state, not the caller's, and that matters. The handlers are method references that capture the calling view, and so its `@State` storage. If the caller held the instance, you'd get a cycle: instance -> handler -> view -> state -> instance. That cycle would keep `ChatViewModel` / `BotConversation` alive after the screen closed. Review of the first draft caught this.

**What this does and doesn't save.** In a hosted harness, readers of `@Environment(\.self)`, including a `UIViewRepresentable` like `ResponseTextSelection`, were not re-evaluated by the old per-pass closure writes. So this PR doesn't claim `ResponseTextSelection` savings. The confirmed win is for readers of these two keys that sit behind a skipped boundary: `ToolActivityGroupView`, `TranscriptLogRowView`, `MarkerMessageCardView`, and `\.openURL` readers such as `TranscriptLinkPreviewView`. A direct child of a re-running parent that reads `\.openURL` is still re-evaluated, because SwiftUI's getter builds a fresh value on each read.

**Measured vs reasoned.** The win is reasoned and pinned by tests, not measured on a device with Instruments. The maintainer waived that step for this issue.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3` with `--only` for `ChatScrollPolicyTests`, `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests`, `BotChatPresentationTests`, `TranscriptLogRowBodyWindowTests`, `ChatTranscriptRowEntryTests`, `TranscriptLinkPreviewTests`, and `FileReferenceTests`: **98 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**. The skip is the existing `XCTSkipUnless` in `BotChatPresentationTests.testDelegationCompletionCardKeepsTheFullReportInItsSheet`, which fires when no accessibility tree is published in-process.
- New `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests` (3 tests, in `ChatScrollPolicyTests.swift`):
  - **Disclosure and links.** An owner rebuilds its handler on every tick, and a reader sits behind a boundary whose inputs never change, like a settled `.equatable()` row. Each test checks that the owner re-ran 4 times, the reader ran once, and invoking the captured action runs the latest closure. Both fail on the old behavior (reader runs 4 times).
  - **Teardown.** An owner holds a model in `@State` and passes method references that capture itself. After the window is torn down, the model's `deinit` must fire. This fails (times out) when the instance lives in the owner's `@State`.

## Manual test

1. Open a session with tool groups and tap "+N previous tool calls". Expected: the reader stays put and doesn't jump.
2. While a reply streams, expand a tool group or reasoning block. Expected: the reader stays pinned.
3. Tap a workspace file link in a reply. Expected: the source viewer opens at the line.
4. Tap an external link in a reply. Expected: it opens in the browser.

title: perf(live-activity): coalesce repeated Thinking updates and bound excerpt work
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #676

Was stacked on #716 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at 79124c8.

## What changed

**Problem.** While a Live Activity runs, every reasoning SSE event sent an immediate ActivityKit update, even though the Lock Screen only says "Thinking" and nothing but `updatedAt` changed. At about 10 events/s, a 30-60 s thinking phase sent about 300-600 cross-process updates where the existing 1.5 s throttle would send about 20-40. With response excerpts turned on (opt-in), every token also re-normalized the whole accumulated reply to build a 140-character prefix (O(n²) per reply) and kept rewriting a state that no longer changed. The Bot conversation's Live Activity snapshot did the same whole-reply normalization on every gateway frame.

**Fix.**
1. `AgentLiveActivityManager.update(.reasoning)`: only a reasoning event that changes what is shown skips the throttle, meaning entering Thinking or clearing a stale mark. Repeat reasoning events while already Thinking go through the existing 1.5 s coalescing path, which sends the latest state.
2. `AgentLiveActivityManager.update(.token)`: once the excerpt buffer holds `AgentRunActivitySanitizer.maximumExcerptSourceLength` (2,048) UTF-8 bytes, it stops growing, since the excerpt is a prefix. Leading whitespace is skipped before buffering (it never reaches the excerpt), and each appended token is clipped, so a full buffer always yields an excerpt and one huge token cannot blow the bound. A later token still rewrites the state when a reasoning, tool, or stale write replaced "Writing response" (it puts that status back from the bounded buffer, as before). Otherwise it returns early. This bounds the per-token normalize cost and stops the no-op state rewrites. `clearResponseExcerpt` still resets the buffer for the next segment.
3. `BotConversation.liveActivitySnapshot` builds the excerpt from the reply's first 2,048 characters after leading whitespace, instead of the whole live reply.
4. `AgentRunActivitySanitizer.maximumExcerptSourceLength`: one shared, documented constant for both bounds.

What the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island show is unchanged. Only the update frequency and the work per event drop.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The win is reasoned from the code path and pinned by tests. It was not measured on a device with Instruments (the maintainer waived that step).

**Choices worth a look.**
- The reasoning gate is `immediate: !(status == .thinking && !isStale)`, a small refinement of the issue's `status != .thinking`, so a reasoning event after a stale mark still lifts the dimmed treatment at once.
- New test seam `immediateWriteCountForTesting` (counts writes that asked to skip the throttle). ActivityKit is unreachable in unit tests, so tests pin which writes skip the throttle. The throttle itself (at most one pending coalesced send per window) is unchanged.
- Accepted trade-off from the issue: once the buffer is full and "Writing response" is showing, a pure token stream no longer bumps `updatedAt`/`staleDate` (300 s). A reply of more than 5 minutes made only of tokens could get the stale treatment. The issue's 60 s refresh idea is not added (yagni).
- A reply with about 2 KB of whitespace right after its first word could get a shorter excerpt, which the issue accepts.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatStreamCoordinatorTests`: **139 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** on the final code.
- New tests in `LiveActivityTests`:
  - `testRepeatedReasoningJoinsTheThrottleAndStillClearsStale`: 100 reasoning events make 1 immediate write (the old code made 100). After `markStale`, the next reasoning event clears `isStale` immediately and the one after it is coalesced.
  - `testTokensStopRewritingTheExcerptOnceItsPrefixIsFull`: after the prefix fills, 1,000 more tokens leave the `ContentState` byte-identical. A token after `.reasoning`, `.toolCompleted`, or `markStale` still restores `.responding` / "Writing response" / not stale. `clearResponseExcerpt` starts a new segment.
  - `testLeadingWhitespaceDoesNotFillTheExcerptBuffer`: 3,000 bytes of whitespace tokens, then "Hello", reaches `.responding` with excerpt "Hello".
- New test in `BotLiveActivityTests`: `testReplyExcerptSkipsLeadingWhitespaceBeforeTheBoundedHead`: a live reply of 6,000 whitespace characters then "Hello" snapshots as `.responding("Hello")`.
- Old-behavior check: with the token cap and reasoning gate reverted, `--only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests` gave 33 passed, 2 failed (both new tests). With the first version of the cap (return early unconditionally), the status-restore assertions fail.

title: perf(chat): highlight code off the main actor and cache the result
body:
Was stacked on #717 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at 5b4ed32.

## Linked issue

Fixes #681

## What changed

**Problem.** Chat code blocks ran highlight.js on the main actor, and so did the one-time JSContext load. Every block ran it once per mount, with no cache. Opening a code-heavy session queued back-to-back highlight passes on the main thread, and each remount (reopen, scrolling back) highlighted the block again and showed plain text first.

**Fix** (follows the issue's sketch):
1. `MarkdownCodeHighlighter` is now an `actor`, like `SourceHighlighter`. It owns the light and dark Highlightr pair (replacing the `@MainActor` `StableHighlightrStore`) and the Splash path for Swift. Results go into an `NSCache<NSString, NSAttributedString>` keyed by appearance, the length-prefixed fence language, and the code, bounded to 256 entries and a 2M UTF-16-unit cost. Cost counts the key plus the result. Results are frozen with `copy()` before they are stored. Streaming requests, plain fallbacks, and Highlightr failures are never cached, so a failure retries on the next mount as it does today.
2. `cachedHighlight(for:)` is a synchronous, nonisolated peek (NSCache is thread-safe). `ChatCodeBlock` uses it as a body fallback while its `@State` is nil, so a block that was already highlighted draws highlighted on its first frame, and at the start of its `.task`, where a hit seeds the state and skips the reset to nil.
The peek returns early, before building a key, for languages that can never highlight.
3. On a miss the task awaits the actor. The actor skips the pass if the caller was already cancelled. The task assigns the result only if the task was not cancelled and the request still matches the block's current `highlightRequest`.

**Where the cache hits.** Session reopen, scrolling a code block out and back, and code in a sealed stable chunk at the streaming-to-settled swap (replies over about 6 KB). Code in a reply's unsealed streaming tail, which is most code in a typical reply, is highlighted for the first time at the swap, so it still shows one plain frame there. The highlight pass now runs off the main thread. Removing that settle flash for short replies (for example by pre-warming completed fences while the reply lingers) is separate scope.

**Not keyed by server, on purpose.** The cache is content-addressed and highlighting is a pure function of appearance, language and code. A lookup needs the code itself, so a hit can't reveal one server's transcript under another.

Skipped on purpose: sharing Highlightr instances with `SourceHighlighter` (the issue's optional follow-up).

**Reasoned, not measured.** Per the maintainer's override, this wasn't profiled in Instruments on a device. The win follows from the code: Highlightr and JSContext work leaves the main actor, and a remount after the first highlight costs one cache lookup instead of a highlight.js pass. Tests pin both.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownMathRendererTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMarkdownImageTests` (iPhone Air, iOS 27.0): **65 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. New tests:
  - `testMarkdownCodeHighlighterCachesSettledResultsForASynchronousPeek`: the peek misses before the first highlight and returns the identical object afterwards, and a second highlight returns the identical object, so highlight.js did not run again. Fails on the old code, which had no cache.
  - `testMarkdownCodeHighlighterCacheIsKeyedByAppearanceAndSkipsStreaming`: dark and streaming peeks miss after a light highlight.
  - `testMarkdownCodeHighlighterCacheKeySeparatesLanguageFromCode`: a `|` in the fence language can't collide with another block's key.
  - `testMarkdownCodeHighlighterSkipsThePassForACancelledTask`: a cancelled caller gets `.plain(.cancelled)` and nothing is cached.
  - The 5 existing highlighter tests now run `async` against a fresh actor instance.

## Manual test

Optional; the cache and actor behavior are covered by tests. On a simulator:
1. Open a session with several fenced code blocks (Python, JSON, Swift). Expected: they highlight.
2. Scroll a code block well off screen and back, or leave the session and reopen it. Expected: the block is highlighted on its first frame, with no plain-text flash.
3. Toggle dark mode. Expected: code colors switch to the dark theme.
4. Stream a short reply that ends with a code block. Expected: it highlights once the reply settles. One plain frame at the swap is expected (see "Where the cache hits").

title: perf(chat): stop re-running the chat screen on keystrokes and scroll-trigger ticks
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #674

Was stacked on #718 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at aa1649f.

## What changed

**Problem.** Two things re-ran the chat screen's whole content closure more often than needed. Each pass re-ran the transcript derivations, every row's `.equatable()` check, and the composer with its UITextView representable.

1. **Keystrokes.** Every keystroke and dictation partial re-ran ChatView's body. The issue names one cause: `fileChipReferenceScanToken` read `draftMessage` in body. There was a second cause the issue missed. The composer got its draft through `persistedDraftBinding`, a `Binding(get:set:)` over ChatView's `@State`. A hosted test shows SwiftUI re-runs the owner of a get/set binding on every write, even when the owner's body never reads the value: 6 owner passes for 4 keystrokes with a get/set binding, 2 (no change) with a plain `$state` binding. So removing the token read alone would not have stopped the per-keystroke pass.
2. **Streaming scroll trigger.** 16 ms after each drain tick, `streamingScrollTrigger` is bumped only to fire one follow scroll. ChatView read that Int to pass it to the transcript, so the content closure ran a second time on every tick.

**Fix.**

- **Scroll trigger (step 1 of the issue).** `ChatTranscriptView` now takes `streamingScrollTrigger: () -> Int`. A new leaf, `StreamingFollowTrigger` (a `Color.clear` background inside the `ScrollViewReader`), calls it and runs the existing follow-and-scroll closure in `onChange`. A bump now re-runs only that leaf.
- **Keystrokes.**
  - ChatView passes the plain `$draftMessage` binding. `MessageComposerView` gets `onDraftEdit: (String) -> Void`. Every edit the composer makes goes through a new `editDraft(_:)`, which then calls it: typing, slash and `@` completions, dictation. ChatView's `persistDraftEdit` bumps `draftRevision` and writes the draft store, exactly as the old binding setter did. ChatView's own writes (clear on send, restore, hydrate) still skip persistence, as before.
  - Per the issue's sketch, `MessageComposerView` also gets `onFileReferenceCandidatesChange` and a `.task(id: fileReferenceCandidates(in: draftMessage))`. ChatView's scan task now keys only on `[messages.count, transcriptRevision, fileChipScopeRevision]` and reads the draft when it runs. `loadFileChipReferences` already serializes overlapping calls.
- `persistedQuotesBinding` stays a get/set binding: quote edits are rare, not per keystroke.

**Out of scope (follow-up).** Step 2 of the issue: move `messageContent` into its own `ChatTranscriptHost` so the composer stops re-rendering on each token tick. Each drain tick still re-runs the content closure once (before: twice).

**Measured vs reasoned.** Not measured on a device with Instruments; the maintainer waived that. The win is reasoned from the code and pinned by hosted tests. Those tests count body passes for a stand-in owner, not ChatView itself, because ChatView cannot be hosted in tests.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3 --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingFollowTriggerTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatScrollPolicyTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerChipPresentationTests` (iPhone 17e): **273 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**. The skip is an existing one in `BotChatPresentationTests`.

New tests:

- `StreamingFollowTriggerTests.testBumpsFireTheScrollWithoutReRunningTheOwner`: 3 trigger bumps give 3 fires and 1 owner pass.
- `BotChatPresentationTests.testSessionsComposerScansFileReferencesWithoutReRunningItsOwnerPerKeystroke`: types 4 keystrokes into the hosted Sessions composer, now wired like ChatView (plain `$draft`, `onDraftEdit`, a task that reads the draft). It checks that the owner's pass count is unchanged, the file-reference scans are exactly `["", "read @a.md "]`, all 4 edits reach `onDraftEdit`, and reading the draft in the owner's task does not make the owner depend on it. With the old get/set draft binding it fails (6 owner passes vs 2). This pins the composer contract and the binding behavior, not ChatView's body directly.

## Manual test

1. Stream a long reply while scrolled to the bottom. Expected: the transcript still auto-follows.
2. Scroll up mid-stream. Expected: following stops; the scroll-to-bottom button appears.
3. Type `@file.md ` (a real workspace file) in the composer. Expected: the file chip appears.
4. Type a draft, leave the chat, reopen it. Expected: the draft is restored.
5. Accept a slash completion and use dictation, then leave and reopen the chat. Expected: the draft is still saved.
6. Send with the server unreachable so the send fails. Expected: the draft is restored into the composer.

title: perf(bots): stop rewriting the Bot history file on cursor-only room polls
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #685

## What changed

**Problem.** While a group room is working, it polls every 2 s. Each tool or status event moves the room's cursor even when no new message row arrives. `BotHistoryCache.appendRoom` counted a cursor-only move as a real change: on every advancing poll it JSON-encoded the whole Bot history index twice (once for the budget check in `prune`, once in `persist`) and atomically rewrote `history.json`, which can be 1-8 MB. `BotRoomReader.readPages` waits for that write, so new room messages also reached the screen late by the encode and write time.

**Fix (follows the issue's fix sketch).**
1. `appendRoom`: when the messages, `earlierBoundary`, and `profileName` are unchanged and only the cursor moved, the snapshot is replaced in memory and the method returns without prune or persist. The in-memory order is the same as before. The next real write (to this room, another room, or a Bot chat) persists the newer cursor. If the app is killed first, the relaunched cache reads the older saved cursor, the reader re-reads a few pages from it, and the existing overlap merge takes them in without duplicates. A cursor that did not move still returns early, as before. So a long-running room's saved retention timestamp cannot fall 30 days behind and expire on relaunch, a cursor-only move is still saved when the last room write is at least 10 minutes old (`cursorOnlySaveInterval`, from review). On relaunch that clock starts from the newest saved timestamp in the file, so reopening a room does not rewrite on its first cursor-only poll.
2. `prune` now drops snapshots over the 100 count in one call, then encodes once. Under budget, that single encode is returned and `persist` writes it, so a real write costs 1 full encode instead of 2. It re-encodes only when it has to evict a snapshot for the byte budget. `replace()` uses the same path.

Files: `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift`, `HermesMobileTests/BotHistoryCacheTests.swift`.

Notes:
- The cursor-only path skips prune, so other expired snapshots can stay in memory until the next real write, search, or `roomHistory`. `search` and `roomHistory` already prune expired snapshots themselves, so results do not change.
- If an encode fails, `prune` still evicts the oldest snapshot, as before.
- `load()` still encodes separately in `persistPruning`; it runs once per process, so it is left alone.

**Measured vs reasoned.** This was not measured on a device with Instruments; the maintainer waived that step for this issue. The win is reasoned from the code and pinned by the tests below: at most one write per 10 minutes on cursor-only polls instead of one every 2 s, and one encode instead of two on real writes. The encode count itself is not asserted, since that would need test-only instrumentation in production code.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/BotHistoryCacheTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomManagementTests`: 59 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (iPhone 17 Pro Max) on ff9e1e1.
- Changed `testRoomOverlapsAreIdempotentOnDiskAndOnlyMessagesAreSearchable`: its old assertion pinned the behavior this issue removes. A cursor-only page now leaves `history.json` byte-identical while the in-memory cursor advances, and the next real write persists the newer cursor.
- New `testReopenAfterKillRereadsFromTheOlderPersistedCursorWithoutDuplicates`: a cursor-only move is not on disk; a relaunched cache sees the older cursor, and re-reading from it merges to `[1, 3]` with cursor 3.
- New `testCursorOnlyMovesAreSavedPeriodicallySoActiveRoomsKeepTheirRetention`: a cursor-only move 1 s after a write stays unsaved; one 10 minutes later is saved with the newer cursor and `savedAt`; a relaunched cache then leaves the file byte-identical on its first cursor-only poll.
- New `testPruneEvictsOldestSnapshotsToTheCountAndByteBudgets`: the 101st snapshot evicts the oldest, two 4.8 MB snapshots evict the older one, and the file stays within 8 MB.
- Old-code check: with only `BotHistoryCache.swift` reverted, `BotHistoryCacheTests` ran 16 tests with exactly 2 failures, the changed test and the reopen test (checked before the review fix).

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. The change is inside the Bot history cache actor and has no UI. Reopen behavior goes through the existing overlap merge, which the new reopen test exercises.

title: perf(workspace): render large Markdown file previews lazily in chunks
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #693

## What changed

**Problem.** The workspace file preview draws a whole Markdown file as one `MarkdownRenderer` inside a non-lazy `VStack`. For a 30-80 KB doc (CHANGELOG, a long README, AGENTS.md), every block is parsed and laid out, and every fenced code block is syntax-highlighted on the main actor, all before the first frame. The result is a one-time hitch and a memory spike when the file opens.

**Fix.**
- On load, `FilePreviewViewModel` splits a Markdown file over 6,000 UTF-8 bytes (the splitter's seal threshold since #717) once, using the existing fence-aware `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter`, and stores the result as `markdownChunks` next to `preview`. The split never runs in `body`.
- `FilePreviewView.markdownContent` draws those chunks in a `LazyVStack`, one `MarkdownRenderer` per chunk, with the file header on top. Only the chunks near the screen are laid out and highlighted.
- Files at or under the threshold, or with no safe boundary, get `nil` and keep today's exact single-document path.
- MarkdownUI drops a document's outer margins, so each seam restores the gap one document would have drawn: the larger of the previous block's bottom margin and the next block's top margin. The values mirror `MarkdownUI.Theme.chat` (heading or rule 24 top, code block 12 bottom, 16 otherwise; a setext `---` underline counts as a heading, not a rule).
- The splitter now closes a fence only on a line of the same character, at least as long, with no info string. Before, it flipped on any line starting with three backticks or tildes, so a ```` or `~~~` fence holding ``` lines (Markdown about Markdown) could be cut mid-fence. This also fixes the same edge in streaming chat.
- `MarkdownRenderer` and the chat render path are otherwise unchanged. The Markdown-extension check moved into `FilePreviewViewModel.isMarkdownPath` so the view and the view model share one predicate.

**Behavior change above 80 KB.** Each chunk goes through `MarkdownRenderer`'s own size fallback, and each is about 6 KB, so a Markdown file over 80 KB / 2,000 lines, which today shows as plain unformatted text, now shows as formatted Markdown in lazy chunks. This follows the issue's "200 KB file shows no multi-hundred-ms hang" criterion. A single chunk that still exceeds the limit (one giant fence) falls back to plain text as before.

**Known edge (named in the issue).** Each chunk parses on its own, so a loose list, a reference-style link definition, or a `$$` math block that spans a blank-line seam can render differently. Select Text and Copy still use the full file.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer chose to skip the Instruments step the issue asked for. The win follows from the design: a 60 KB file becomes about 10 chunks and only the first one or two lay out at open. Tests pin the behavior; nothing was measured on a device.

## Design

Mocks: https://zxycca22vr1w.postplan.dev

Picked **A: Seamless**. Each seam gets the gap one document would have drawn (24 pt before a heading or rule, 12 pt after a code block, 16 pt otherwise), so a chunked file looks the same as a single document. B (a flat 16 pt gap) leaves headings that start a chunk 8 pt tighter than every other heading. C (a hairline at each seam) puts rules at arbitrary points that are not in the file.

**After** (iPhone Air, a 7 KB / 142-line skill guide from a live workspace, which splits into chunks; top and scrolled past a seam):

![Chunked preview, top](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94304897-3f1b-4866-bfcf-c3fb8ec9e445) ![Chunked preview, scrolled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da7586ac-b6a0-48cb-b4f2-ee8e277ba5cf)

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownPreviewChunkerTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitterTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientWorkspaceFileTests`: 36 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (iPhone Air, iOS 27.0).

New tests:
- `MarkdownPreviewChunkerTests` (4): a small file stays one document; a large file with no safe boundary stays one document; a ~60 KB doc splits into 8 or more chunks that join back to the exact original with no fence split; seam spacing matches single-document block margins, including the setext-vs-rule case.
- `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitterTests.testNestedFenceSealsOnlyAfterItsOwnClosingRun`: a ```` fence and a `~~~` fence each holding a ``` block seal only after their own closing run.
- `APIClientWorkspaceFileTests.testFilePreviewSplitsOnlyLargeMarkdownIntoChunks`: through a mocked `/api/file`, a large `.md` gets chunks that join back losslessly; a small `.md` and a large `.txt` get `nil`.

These fail on master: the chunker and `markdownChunks` do not exist there, and the old splitter seals right after the inner ``` line.

## Manual test

1. Open a small `.md` (under 6 KB) from a session's workspace browser. It looks identical to master.
2. Open a 30-80 KB `.md` with headings and code blocks. It opens without a visible hitch. Scroll through: heading, code-block, and paragraph gaps at the seams are indistinguishable from gaps inside a chunk.
3. Open a Markdown file over 80 KB. It is now formatted, not plain text.
4. Long-press, then Select Text and Copy. Both cover the whole file.

title: perf(cache): stop full-table scans and per-row fetches on cache writes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #670

## What changed

**Problem.** Every SwiftData cache write ran maintenance on the main actor. It loaded the whole `CachedSession` table and the whole `CachedMessage` table twice, including the content, tool-call, content-part and attachment blobs, just to find expired rows and count against the 5,000-row cap. That happened on every write: send, response completion, chat open, every session-list load, and rename, pin and new chat. On top of that, `cacheSessions` ran one fetch per session (N+1), and `cacheMessages` rewrote every row in a 50-300 row window, re-encoding it and bumping its dates, so every row was dirty at save.

**Fix (all in the cache layer; callers unchanged):**
1. **Store-side trim.** A new `saveAndTrim` saves the write first. Then it runs `context.delete(model:where: expiresAt <= now)` for sessions and messages, and eviction starts from `fetchCount`. Only when the table is over the cap does it fetch rows, and then only `fetchLimit = overflow` rows sorted by cachedAt, timestamp, sortIndex (the old in-memory order). A second save runs only if maintenance deleted something. Saving first means the store matches the context, so a row the write just refreshed is not expired in the store either.
2. **Keyed `cacheSessions`.** One server-scoped fetch builds a `[cacheKey: CachedSession]` dictionary, used for both the upsert and the stale sweep (mirrors #309 in `cacheMessages`). Inserted rows join the dictionary, so a duplicated session in the response still produces one row.
3. **Unchanged message rows stay clean.** `CachedMessage.refresh(from:sortIndex:cachedAt:)` compares every field, including the encoded blobs, with the incoming message. Blobs are encoded with one shared sorted-keys encoder so equal values give equal bytes. A matching row is not rewritten; its cachedAt/expiresAt move forward only once `CachePolicy.rowRefreshInterval` (1 hour) has passed, which keeps LRU eviction and TTL roughly right. A changed row, including a changed tool call with the same call count, is rewritten in full as before.

Expiry and eviction stay global across servers, as before; reads and stale-row sweeps stay server-scoped. `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` now names `saveAndTrim`.

Left out on purpose: a maintenance throttle, and the optional on-send optimistic-row change (it touches `ChatViewModel`, which another stack owns).

Trade-offs worth knowing:
- An unchanged row can now expire up to about an hour early (its expiresAt only moves hourly). Reads already filter on `expiresAt > now`.
- Rows stored before this change encode with the old key order, so they are rewritten once, then stay stable. Decoding is unaffected.
- No index on `expiresAt` was added (a schema change). The store-side delete is still a SQLite scan, but it no longer loads any objects into memory.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer chose not to profile on device first. The win is reasoned from the code and pinned by tests; it was not measured with Instruments.

## How it was tested

All on iPhone 17e (`1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3`), `git diff --check` clean.

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/CacheStoreTests`: 23 passed, 0 failed (19 existing + 4 new).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/CacheStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionListMutationTests --only HermesMobileTests/SteerMessageTests --only HermesMobileTests/CacheFallbackPolicyTests`: 325 passed, 0 failed.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatStreamCoordinatorTests`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
- After the doc fix: `--only CacheStoreTests --only SessionListMutationTests --only CacheFallbackPolicyTests`: 104 passed, 0 failed.
- Temporarily swapping `refresh` back to the old full rewrite made `testCacheMessagesSkipsUnchangedRowsUntilTheRefreshInterval` fail; the swap was reverted.

New tests in `CacheStoreTests`:
- `testCacheMessagesSkipsUnchangedRowsUntilTheRefreshInterval`: no rewrite inside the interval, a same-count tool-call edit is still written, and the dates bump after an hour.
- `testCacheMessagesKeepsExpiredRowsTheWriteRefreshes`: guards the save-before-store-delete ordering.
- `testCacheMaintenanceEvictsOnlyTheLeastRecentlyCachedOverflowAcrossServers`: the fetchLimit eviction path.
- `testCacheSessionsKeepsOneRowForADuplicatedSession`: guards the keyed dictionary.

SwiftData exposes no fetch statistics, so "no full-table fetch" rests on reading the code; the tests pin the behavior around it.

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. There is no UI change, and the cache's read and write behavior is pinned by `CacheStoreTests`. Optional smoke: open a few chats, send, go back to the list, then go offline and confirm cached sessions and transcripts still show.

title: perf(model-picker): make each model its own List row and store allModels
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #692

## What changed

**Problem.** In the model picker, an expanded provider group was one List cell. That cell held every model in a `LazyVStack` with no scroll view around it, so the stack was not actually lazy. Typing a search letter that matches a big provider id (`o`, `r`, `n` for OpenRouter or Nous), or tapping "Show all models", built hundreds of rows in one pass. On top of that, every body pass re-derived the catalog many times: `filteredModelGroups` ran twice, `storedCustomOptions` ran up to 3 times, and `ModelCatalogGroup.allModels` redid its concat and de-dupe on every read.

**Fix** (follows the issue's fix sketch):

1. `ModelCatalogGroup.allModels` is now a stored `let`, merged and de-duplicated once in the designated init (`ServerCatalog.swift`).
2. `ModelPickerSheet.modelGroupDisclosure` puts the `ForEach` of models straight into the `DisclosureGroup` content. The header divider, the overflow divider and the "Show all models" toggle are sibling rows. Inside a List each one becomes its own reusable row, so only the rows on screen get built.
   - Each row keeps `.listRowInsets`, `.listRowSeparator(.hidden)` and the pill.
   - The insets reproduce the old stack's spacing: 9pt above the divider, 1pt between rows, 5pt below the group.
   - The List runs with `defaultMinListRowHeight = 0`, so 49pt model rows and hairline divider rows aren't stretched to the system minimum (about 50pt on iOS 26/27). The rows that relied on that minimum (group headers, the error row, the Custom Model header) restore it from the environment value read outside the List.
