title: perf(bots): window the group room transcript like Bot Chat
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #686

## What changed

**Problem.** Opening a group room built every event the reader held. A warm open or a disk restore can hold up to 500 events. Each member reply builds a hosted `ResponseTextSelection` controller plus a `MarkdownRenderer`, all on the main thread before the first frame. Each Load earlier added up to 200 more events, and nothing trimmed them. Bot Chat already limits the same eager stack with `BotTranscriptWindow`. The room didn't, even though its #553 comment said Load earlier kept the build small.

**Fix.** A new `BotRoomTranscriptWindow` (in `BotRoomView.swift`) builds only the newest 50 events. It is keyed to the oldest shown sequence number, not a list position, because room history is added at the top.
- The window covers only the newest page from the first frame on. It stays anchored once the room goes live, so the catch-up after a stale disk-cache restore is not built in full. It anchors again when the room empties (close or background), or when its events no longer cover the anchor (a reconnect restored the trimmed 500-event snapshot, or the room restarted).
- History added at the top stays hidden, so rows on screen don't shift. New events always show at the bottom.
- Load earlier first shows up to 50 hidden events that are already in memory. Only when none are hidden does it call `reader.loadEarlier()`. It still scrolls back to the event you were reading. The button shows when events are hidden or the server has more. It is disabled only when a fetch is needed and not possible.
- Search hit (#553): while `pendingSequence` is in the events, the window widens to include it. Its row exists when `scrollTo` runs, and `reveal` keeps it shown afterwards.
- `docs/agents/bots.md` now describes the room window.

Trade-off, same as Bot Chat: the window grows as new events arrive and never drops rows off the top, so someone scrolled up never loses a row. A long live session can grow past 50.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer skipped the Instruments step, so we took no device trace. The win is reasoned, and a hosted test pins it: a warm room with 300 cached member replies now builds 50 selection controllers instead of 300. With `ForEach(reader.events)` put back, that test fails with `("300") is not equal to ("50")`.

## Design

Mocks: https://mr3hm7am5umt.postplan.dev

Pick: **A**, the room's existing plain "Load earlier" button, per the decision. No new strings and no restyle. The button now also shows when older events are loaded but hidden. B (the shared "Load older messages" capsule from Sessions and Bot Chat, with a spinner) is a restyle and belongs in its own issue. C (a count of hidden events) would show a wrong number once server history is involved, and it adds a plural string.

No after screenshot. A room with more than 50 events can't be reached with a launch and a couple of taps, and no deep link opens a room.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17 Pro Max> --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTranscriptWindowTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`: **69 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (`testDelegationCompletionCardKeepsTheFullReportInItsSheet`, already skipped, unrelated).
- New `BotRoomTranscriptWindowTests` (7):
  - opens on the newest page, before and after seeding
  - a catch-up after a cache restore stays on the newest page
  - a reconnect that restores a trimmed transcript falls back to the newest page
  - history added at the top stays hidden while new events show
  - Load earlier shows hidden pages, then returns false
  - a search hit older than the window is built and stays shown, and a missing hit does not widen it
  - close or restart re-anchors on the newest page
- New `BotChatPresentationTests.testWarmRoomBuildsOnlyTheNewestPageOfReplies`: 300 cached member replies build 50 `ResponseSelectionController`s. It fails on the old `ForEach(reader.events)`.
- The existing #553 search-hit tests still pass. Their target is seq 20 of 80, so it falls outside the window, which covers the widening path.

## Manual test

1. Open a group room with more than 50 events. The newest events show, and the view sits at the bottom.
2. Scroll to the top and tap Load earlier. 50 earlier events appear, and the view stays on the event you were reading.
3. Keep tapping until no hidden events are left. The next tap fetches from the server, as before.
4. Open a room from a message search hit on an old message. It lands on that message.
5. Background the app and come back. The room reloads on the newest page.

title: perf(sessions): restore the last-opened chat before projects and profile load
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #671

## What changed

**Problem.** On a cold launch the remembered chat was restored only after three requests finished one after another: `GET /api/sessions`, then `GET /api/projects`, then `GET /api/profiles`. Restore only needs the session rows. Over a tunnel that adds about two extra round trips before the user sees their chat, and ChatView's cache-first render and its own requests wait behind them.

**Fix (step 1 of the issue only; the cache-first restore in step 2 is out of scope).**
- `SessionListInitialLoad.run` now takes separate closures: `loadSessions`, `restoreSelection`, `loadProjects`, `loadActiveProfile`. It starts the session rows alongside deep-link resolution as before, waits for both, restores the stored selection (and sets `didCompleteInitialLoad`, same as before), and then loads projects and the active profile together.
- New `SessionListInitialLoad.loadProjectsAndActiveProfile` runs the two with `async let`. `refreshSessionsAndActiveProfile` (pull to refresh, retry, return refresh) uses it too, so later refreshes also stop waiting on projects before fetching the profile.
- `loadSessions()` in `SessionListView` is split into `loadSessionRows()` and `loadProjectsIfLive()`. The existing `!isViewingCachedData` guard on projects is kept, and `handleLastError()` still runs after each at the same points. The profile switch path still runs sessions, then projects, as before.
- Deep link precedence is unchanged: restore still runs only after the deep link has resolved.

**Trade-offs.**
- `didCompleteInitialLoad` now flips at restore time, before projects and profile finish. It stays paired with restore, as before; waiting longer would make a user who pops back from the restored chat early skip the return refresh. So the quiet-list poll or a return refresh can start while the first projects/profile loads are still running. That overlap is harmless: `loadActiveProfile` already guards against running twice, and a second `GET /api/projects` is idempotent.
- `loadActiveProfile` never touches `lastError`, so `handleLastError()` after projects still sees only the projects error. Profile errors still go only to `activeProfileErrorMessage`. As the issue notes, error banners can now appear in a different order.

**Win: reasoned, not measured.** The issue asked to confirm the magnitude with Instruments first; the maintainer skipped that. The saving comes from reasoning about the request order (about two round trips per cold launch over a tunnel, a few ms on LAN), and a test pins the new ordering. It has not been measured on a device.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.

With `loadProjectsAndActiveProfile` temporarily made serial, the test fails.

title: perf(kanban): stop inserting the Refreshing Board row on background refreshes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #684

Item 2 of the issue (drop the per-burst stats and assignees reads, and queue live refreshes instead of cancelling them) already landed in #697. This PR does item 1.

## What changed

**Problem.** Every background refresh of a Kanban Board sets `isRefreshing`, and the Card list put a "Refreshing Board" row at the top whenever that flag was true. That covered live event bursts, poll recovery, mutation reconciles, and pull-to-refresh. On a busy Board, each burst pushed every Card down about one row, ran a spinner, then moved the Cards back 0.3 to 1 s later, even when nothing had changed.

**Fix.** A new `KanbanFeatureState.showsBoardLoadingRow` decides when the row shows: while a refresh runs and the Cards on screen don't belong to the current request. That means no snapshot yet (first load, Board switch), or a snapshot fetched under different server-side filters (profile, tenant, archived, only-mine). Live, poll, mutation, and pull refreshes use the same filters as the snapshot on screen, so their Card rows now update in place with no row inserted. Pull-to-refresh keeps only the native pull spinner.

`refreshBoard` now builds its request from the same `filteredBoardRequest` helper the new rule compares against, so the two can't drift apart. The list layout is the same as on master: the row sits above the old Cards during a filter change, and shows alone when there is no snapshot.

`isRefreshing` and the write gating built on it (`canUseServerAuthoritativeActions`, dispatcher and bulk availability, the selection focus hand-back) are unchanged, so menus still grey out during a refresh. The offline and "Live updates delayed" banners are unchanged.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer waived the Instruments measurement. The win follows from the code path: no List row is inserted or removed per burst, so the Cards stay put. Tests pin the behavior; nobody measured it on a device.

## Design

Mocks: https://bbzvw0ylpgxt.postplan.dev (Today, A, B, C).

Pick: **A**, no row while the Board's Cards are on screen. It's the calmest result and the smallest change. Background refreshes should be invisible, degraded states already have their own banners, and pull-to-refresh already has the system spinner. B (a static "Updating" nav subtitle) and C (a thin static bar) would swap the jump for a different flicker on every burst, and they add new UI and copy to maintain.

No after screenshot: both Boards on the maintainer's server are empty right now, and making Cards there would mean writing to the live server.

title: perf(workspace): build diff rows once per file as responses land
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #690

## What changed

**Problem.** When the Git sheet or a turn diff opened a large change set, `GitDiffView` rebuilt the rows for every file each time one file's diff came back. Each rebuild re-ran `DiffHunk.parse` and the word diff for every file already loaded, so the work grew with N²/2: at 100 files that is about 5,050 file builds instead of 100. Builds that a newer one replaced were never cancelled. Every build that landed also caused a full main-thread canvas layout pass and a VoiceOver `.layoutChanged` post, about 100 of them while late files were still arriving.

**Fix.** A new `ReviewDiffLoader` in `GitDiffView.swift` takes over the loading loop:

- Each file's rows are built once, inside the child task that fetched that file (so off the main actor), and stored in a per-load `rowsByFileID` map. Publishing flattens the map in display order, with cheap Loading placeholders for files that have not arrived yet. The old detached whole-list builds, `statesByFileID`, and `rowsBuildGeneration` are gone.
- Publishes are coalesced. The placeholders and the first answer paint immediately. Later answers paint at most once per 150 ms or once per four answers. A trailing flush (a structured child task in the same group, so it is cancelled with the load; any publish makes a waiting flush stale) makes sure a waiting answer paints without needing another answer to arrive. The last answer always paints right away.
- Everything else stays the same: the tapped file is fetched first, at most 4 fetches run at once, the first error is reported once, cancelled fetches are ignored, and a dismissed sheet or a newer load (generation check) stops the loop and publishes nothing more. Output rows are identical to a full `ReviewDiffRowBuilder` build.

The optional "store `columnCount` as a `let` on `ReviewDiffLine`" step from the issue is skipped on purpose: #691 owns that change.

Small shift worth knowing: the Loading placeholder rows (a header and a notice per file) and the "Session ID is missing" rows now build on the main actor instead of in the detached build. They are two cheap rows per file with no parsing.

**Measured vs reasoned.** The win is reasoned from the code and pinned by tests, not measured on a device with Instruments (the maintainer skipped that step for this issue). The new test shows 10 files produce exactly 10 loaded-file builds (the old path did 55) and 5 publishes instead of 11.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffLayoutTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffSelectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewWordDiffTests` (iPhone 17 Pro Max): **31 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. `ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests` alone: 9 passed (6 existing + 3 new).
- New tests in `ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests`:
  - `testLoaderBuildsEachLandedFileOnceAndBatchesPublishes`: 10 files give exactly 10 loaded builds (old code: 55) and 5 publishes (placeholders, first answer, answer 5, answer 9, last answer). The first publish is the Loading placeholders; the last equals a full `ReviewDiffRowBuilder` build in display order.
  - `testLoaderPublishesAPendingAnswerWithoutWaitingForTheNextOne`: the third file is held back, and the trailing flush paints the second answer without waiting for it.
  - `testLoaderRestartsTheFlushIntervalAfterABatchPublish`: a flush scheduled before a batch publish is ignored, and the next answer waits a fresh interval (added after Greptile review; fails on the first commit).

3. Dismiss the sheet mid-load and reopen it. Expected: nothing stale or doubled; the load starts clean.

title: perf(sessions): compute the filtered session groups once per body
body:
Was stacked on #727 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at 36f6f7f.

## Linked issue

Fixes #687

## What changed

**Problem.** Every `SessionListView` body pass read the computed `scheduledSessionGroups` five times, and each read ran `visibleSessions` twice with the same arguments, plus three `isCronSession` passes. The active-row monitor's task ID added one more full `visibleSessions` pass per body and per poll. So each search keystroke filtered, lowercased, and sorted every session about 11 times when once is enough.

**Fix** (the issue's fix sketch, steps 1 to 3):

1. `SessionListViewModel.scheduledSessionGroups` calls `visibleSessions` once and hands the result to a new `ScheduledSessionGroups(partitioning:totalScheduledCount:)`, which splits the rows in one loop and keeps their order. Cron rows go to `scheduled` unless archived; everything else goes to `ordinary`, same rules as before. The global `totalScheduledCount` pass is unchanged.
2. `SessionListView.content` binds `let groups = scheduledSessionGroups` once and uses it at all five sites.
3. The active-row monitor uses a new `viewModel.visibleActiveSessions(...)`: it keeps only streaming rows first (usually zero to two), returns early when there are none, then applies the same visibility rules (automated kinds, project filter, local search and loaded remote matches) to just those rows. Both entry points share a private `visibleSessions(among:...)` core. Visibility is decided per row, so running it on the streaming subset gives exactly the visible streaming rows. The monitor's stream-ID set is sorted and de-duplicated, so the task ID is identical. The view's now-unused `visibleSessions` property is removed.

Behavior is unchanged apart from the waste removed. No caching and no stored flags on `SessionSummary`.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer waived the issue's on-device Instruments check. The gain is worked out from the code (about 11 `visibleSessions` passes per body down to 1, plus one small streaming-rows-only pass) and pinned by tests; it was not profiled on a device.

title: perf(networking): share URLSessions across APIClient instances
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #688

## What changed

**Problem.** Every `APIClient` built its own default and media `URLSession` and invalidated them in `deinit`. Each session has its own connection pool, so every newly opened chat (plus its git probe, and each Settings/Workspace/Skills sheet) started cold. It paid a fresh TCP+TLS handshake even when the session list's client already had a warm connection to the same host. Over a tunnel or cellular link that adds roughly 1-2 edge round trips (about 40-160 ms) before the first response. On LAN the cost is negligible.

**Fix.**
- `APIClient` now defaults to two process-wide sessions: `APIClient.sharedSession` (default config, `.shared` cookie jar) and `APIClient.sharedPublicMediaSession` (ephemeral, cookie-less). Their configs are the same as before, but they have no session delegate.
- The #277 `CrossOriginHeaderStripper` stays per client, bound to the client's baseURL and header provider. It is now passed as the per-task delegate on both request paths (`sendPreparedRequest` and `downloadData`) through `session.data(for:delegate:)`. `BotArtifactDownload` already uses this pattern.
- `ownedSessions` and `deinit` are gone. No client owns a session now, so nothing invalidates the shared pools. Injected sessions stay the caller's to manage, as before.
- Multi-server: the shared sessions hold nothing server-specific. Connections pool per host, cookies were already in the shared jar, and custom headers are applied per request. `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` now records this and says never to invalidate these sessions or give them a delegate.

title: perf(ipad): keep the sidebar's identity when the selection changes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #689

Was stacked on #730 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at f5d433f.

## What changed

**Problem.** On iPad, and on Plus/Max iPhones in landscape, `.id(navigationState.rootRevision)` sat on the whole `NavigationSplitView`. Every sidebar selection (a session, New Chat, or a utility such as Settings, Tasks, Kanban or Bots) bumps `rootRevision`, so SwiftUI threw away and rebuilt the whole split view each time: the sidebar `List`, its header, the visible rows and their `@State` (the streaming dot restarted), and the sidebar's scroll position, which then had to be restored. Only the detail column's pushed path needed resetting (#116).

**Fix.** The regular-width shell is now a small `SessionSplitView` in `SessionListComponents.swift`. It puts `.id(rootRevision)` on the detail `NavigationStack` only. Any root selection, including picking the same utility again, still replaces nested detail screens, as #116 intended. The sidebar keeps its identity, scroll position, row state and search focus. Compact iPhone uses the `NavigationStack` branch and is untouched. `rootRevision`'s other use, as the staleness token in `openPendingWebuiPush`, is unchanged.

**Follow-up fix: pushed detail screens (found in the maintainer's iPad test).** Re-identifying the detail `NavigationStack` rebuilt its root but left screens the old root had pushed (a Settings subpage, a workspace file, a fork) on top: the split view adopts the stack into its detail column's `UINavigationController`, which outlives the stack's identity. A ZStack wrapper, a nested stack, `AnyView`, a `path:`-bound stack and dropping the inner stack were all tried; none popped it. `SessionSplitView` now records the column's navigation controller through a tiny invisible `UIViewControllerRepresentable` in the detail root's background, and on a root selection pops it to the root (no animation), synchronously in the selection's `onChange` so the new root starts on an empty stack. A first version popped on the next main-queue turn; that raced with a new root that pushes on appear (a bot deep link's target) and dropped its push. `testRootSelectionKeepsAScreenTheNewRootPushes` pins that case. The split-view tests now wait on real events (views entering or leaving the window, the new root appearing) instead of a fixed main-queue turn; the focused selection passed 5 runs in a row (39/39). New test `testRootSelectionPopsAScreenPushedInsideTheDetail` pushes a screen with `navigationDestination(isPresented:)`, bumps `rootRevision`, and asserts the column's stack is back to one screen, the sidebar was created once, and the new root can still push. It fails without the fix. `SessionSplitViewIdentityTests` + `SessionNavigationStateTests`: 38 passed, 0 failed (after dropping the flaky hosted portrait test).

**Sidebar visibility.** The old rebuild also reset column visibility as a side effect. The split view now owns a `columnVisibility` binding so that part stays deliberate:
- A sidebar the user opened goes back to `.automatic` after a root selection. In iPad portrait that closes it and gives the chat the full width, as before.
- In landscape, `.automatic` keeps the sidebar beside the detail, as before.
- A sidebar the user collapsed (`.detailOnly`) now stays collapsed. The maintainer approved this change.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer waived the Instruments pass the issue asked for. The win is reasoned from how SwiftUI identity works and pinned by the tests below. It was not profiled on a device.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3 --only HermesMobileTests/SessionSplitViewIdentityTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests`: **37 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (iPhone 17e sim, iOS 27.0).
- New `SessionSplitViewIdentityTests.testRootSelectionRebuildsOnlyTheDetailColumn` hosts `SessionSplitView` in a regular-width window with a UIKit probe in each column and counts how often each column's view is created. After a root selection the detail count goes to 2 and the sidebar count stays at 1. **Red check:** with `.id` moved back onto the whole split view, this test fails.
- The hosted portrait-close test was dropped: UISplitViewController's display-mode change didn't settle reliably on CI's parallel test clones (it failed on a run and its retry while passing locally on iOS 26.5 and 27). The policy test below pins close-vs-keep, and the maintainer confirmed the portrait close by hand on an iPad simulator.
- New `testRootSelectionHidesAnOpenedSidebarButKeepsACollapsedOne` pins the visibility policy: `.all`, `.doubleColumn` and `.automatic` go to `.automatic`, and `.detailOnly` stays `.detailOnly`. The collapsed case is pinned here rather than hosted, because in an iPhone-idiom host `.automatic` also resolves to detail-only.
- The #116 guard `testReselectingRootDestinationAdvancesNavigationRevision` still passes.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

## Manual test

Use an iPad sim (both orientations) or a Pro Max in landscape. This lane had only an iPhone 17e, so these steps have not been run.

1. Open Settings, go into a subpage, then pick a chat in the sidebar. **Expected:** the subpage is replaced by the chat (#116).
2. Open a workspace file from a chat, then pick another chat. **Expected:** the nested screen is gone.
3. Scroll the sidebar partway down and switch chats. **Expected:** the scroll position does not jump, and a streaming dot does not restart.
4. Landscape: collapse the sidebar, then start a New Chat or open something from the detail's own UI. **Expected:** the sidebar stays collapsed.
5. iPad portrait: open the sidebar and tap a chat. **Expected:** the sidebar closes and the chat gets the full width.

title: perf(workspace): draw only the reachable part of very long diff lines
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #691. Was stacked on #729 (merged); rebuilt as one commit on master at 3ff9b8f.

## What changed

**Problem.** The review canvas (the workspace file preview and the diff viewer) handed each code row to CoreText whole, on every scroll and pan frame. Take a minified bundle, a source map, or a single-line JSON up to the server's 400 KB cap:

- Without wrap, each pan frame typeset all ~400k characters, although only a few hundred columns can ever be panned into view (content width is capped at `maxContentWidth` = 2800 pt).
- With Wrap Lines on, each frame rebuilt a full-line attributed string and drew all ~9k visual lines, although about 40 fit on screen.
- On top of that, `ReviewDiffRow.columnCount` recounted `content.count` (O(n)) on every `height(forRowAt:)`, which binary search and the draw loop hit each frame.

**Fix (part 1 of the issue only).**

1. `ReviewDiffLine` counts its characters once in a new explicit init and stores the result as `columnCount`. `ReviewDiffRow.columnCount` returns the stored value, so layout heights and wrap line counts are O(1).
2. `ReviewDiffLayout.drawnCharacterRange(columnCount:reachableColumns:visibleMinY:visibleMaxY:)` returns the characters a draw pass can show:
   - Unwrapped: the first `reachableCodeColumns`, which is `ceil((maxContentWidth + viewportWidth) / codeCharacterWidth)`: the furthest pan plus one viewport of slack. `drawnCodeColumns(for:)` doubles that prefix while it renders narrower than the reach (zero-width characters, proportional fallback glyphs), so nothing on screen goes undrawn. The result is cached per row id (cleared when rows, style, wrap, or viewport width change), so a long row is measured once, not per frame.
   - Wrapped: only the visual lines inside the dirty rect, plus one line on each side for glyph overhang.
3. `ReviewDiffLine.visualLines(in:wrapColumns:)` slices that range by `Character`, so graphemes stay whole. `drawCodeText` now has one path: it draws only those lines and shifts the syntax colour runs (UTF-16 offsets into the whole line) onto each line.

Short lines draw exactly as before. Only rows longer than the reachable prefix or the visible window draw less.

**Left out on purpose.** Part 2 of the issue (redrawing the full viewport on every scroll frame, and whether to tile or cache lines) is measure-first: it needs an Instruments trace on a ProMotion device showing over-budget draws. This PR does not touch it, and #691 stays open for it. The remaining wrap cost is walking `Character`s from the line start to the first visible visual line (O(position), once per frame); an ASCII/UTF-16 fast path is a follow-up only if a trace shows it matters.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer waived the issue's "confirm on device with Instruments first" step. The win comes from reasoning about the code, and the tests pin the bounded draw ranges. It has not been measured on a device.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffLayoutTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffSelectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewWordDiffTests --only HermesMobileTests/SourceFileRowsTests`: **37 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26.5).

New tests (each fails on the old code, which drew the whole line):

- `ReviewDiffLayoutTests.testDrawnCharactersStopAtTheReachableColumnsOrTheVisibleWrappedLines`: a 400k-column row. Unwrapped, drawing is capped at the reachable columns. Wrapped, a window 1,000 lines down draws only lines 999...1021; the row's top draws its first lines, the last line ends at the text, and a row above the window draws nothing.
- `ReviewDiffLayoutTests.testVisualLinesSliceWholeCharacters`: slicing keeps a combining accent and a skin-tone emoji whole, and the stored `columnCount` counts graphemes.
- `ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests.testReachableColumnsCoverTheFurthestPan`: the unwrapped cap covers the furthest pannable x (so it stays in step with `maxContentWidth`) and stays far below the line length.
- `ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests.testDrawnColumnsGrowPastZeroWidthCharactersAndAreMeasuredOncePerRow`: text after 5,000 zero-width spaces is still drawn, and a row is measured once until the rows change (from Greptile's review).

## Manual test

On a branch build, with a workspace that has a minified `.js` or `.map` file (or any single-line file of a few hundred KB):

1. Open the file in the workspace file preview and pan horizontally to the far right edge. Expected: the text renders the same as before all the way to the edge, with syntax colours intact, and panning stays smooth.
2. Turn on Wrap Lines and scroll through the long row, including to its end. Expected: every wrapped line renders with correct colours, no blank bands while scrolling, and the last line ends at the end of the text.
3. Open a normal diff with short lines, with and without Wrap Lines. Expected: identical to before.

title: perf(share): map shared files instead of holding every attachment in memory
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #682

## What changed

**Problem.** The share extension copies every accepted attachment into heap memory before it stages anything. For images and PDFs it loads the whole payload before the 20 MB check, so one oversized ProRAW is read in full and then rejected. Share extensions have a memory ceiling of about 120 MB. A share of several large scanned PDFs can go over it, and then jetsam kills the extension and the share fails silently. In the app, reserving the import reads every staged file on the main actor during share handoff.

**Fix.** This follows the issue's fix sketch. `SharedAttachmentImport` still holds `Data`, and no model changes.

1. `ShareInputReader`: file-URL items are read with `Data(contentsOf:options: .alwaysMapped)` after the existing size check. The size check and the mapped read now live in one helper, `mappedAttachmentData(at:)`.
2. `ShareInputReader`: image and PDF providers now load through `loadFileRepresentation`. Inside the handler, the file size is checked before any bytes are read, and the file is mapped before the provider deletes its temp copy. Oversized items are never loaded into memory. `loadDataRepresentation` stays as the fallback when the provider can't supply a file (or the mapped read fails). An oversized file does not fall back.
3. `SharedDraftStore.loadAttachments` / `loadLegacyAttachments`: staged files are mapped, so `reserveNextPendingImport` on main only maps them. Pages load at upload time, when the bytes are needed anyway. Hashing and writing work on mapped `Data` unchanged. The mapping stays valid after `consume` removes the reserved files (an unlinked inode stays readable), and nothing rewrites a staged file in place.

Both source files already belong to the main app and `HermesShareExtension` targets, so no target membership changed.

Left out on purpose: moving the extension's hashing and writing off the main actor (optional per the issue, not user-visible), and any `ContentView` change (mapping already makes reservation cheap). The SIGBUS risk of a mapped file being truncated before upload is accepted per the issue; staged files are only removed or moved, never rewritten in place.

**Reasoned, not measured.** The maintainer skipped the Instruments pass the issue asked for. The memory win is reasoned from how mapped reads work: mapped file pages are clean, file-backed memory and don't count toward the extension's phys_footprint. Tests pin it (they assert the attachment bytes sit in a file-backed VM region). It was not measured on a device. The size-before-read benefit of `loadFileRepresentation` matters for cross-process providers (Photos, Files over XPC), which unit tests can't reach.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/ShareInputReaderTests --only HermesMobileTests/SharedDraftStoreTests` on iPhone 17 Pro Max: **32 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (12 ShareInputReaderTests + 20 SharedDraftStoreTests). The `HermesShareExtension.appex` is rebuilt in the same run, so the extension target compiles too.
- The same command on the old code with the new tests added: 32 executed, **2 failed** — `ShareInputReaderTests.testFileURLAttachmentIsMappedFromDisk` and `SharedDraftStoreTests.testReservedAttachmentsAreMappedFromStagedFiles`. Both pass now. A small test helper `isFileBacked(_:)` checks this with `vm_region_64` / `VM_REGION_EXTENDED_INFO.external_pager`.
- `ShareInputReaderTests.testImageFileRepresentationIsMappedFromDisk` covers the new file-representation branch for an accepted image. It also passes on the old code (in-process, `loadDataRepresentation` of a file-registered item already maps), so it is coverage, not proof of the fix. Existing data-only provider tests, including the oversized-image test, now go through `loadFileRepresentation` and still pass.

## Manual test

Optional device confirmation; the behavior is covered by tests.

1. On a device or simulator, share 3-4 large PDFs (10-20 MB each) from Files to Hermex. Expected: Hermex opens with every PDF attached, and they upload.
2. Share a single image from Photos. Expected: it attaches as before.
3. Share a file over 20 MB. Expected: the extension shows "Hermex accepts text, URLs, images, PDFs, and files up to 20 MB." as before.

title: epic(bots): adopt the best of OpenMausBot's iOS app
body:
## Goal

Adopt the ideas worth copying from [OpenMausBot's iOS app](https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot/tree/main/ios), a phone companion for desktop agent bots, into Hermex Bots. Every item here is either client-only or uses an RPC, route or event that exists in the pinned hermes-agent (`d337b736`, 0.21.4). Each sub-issue cites the host source by file and line, names the Hermex seams, and includes a plan, acceptance, tests and the "Hit every surface" list, so an implementation agent can start cold.

**Relation to #713.** #713 decision 9 says Hermes-only capabilities get no issues until migration parity. Uzair asked for this epic on 2026-09-24 as an explicit exception. It runs beside #713, and where a feature would otherwise be built twice, it is **blocked by** the #713 issue that owns the foundation (#699, #700, #702, #705, #706). Nothing here is blocked by #709. #709 is a product decision, so the Bot-surface issues ask it as a decision instead (see D1).

## How to work this epic

1. Read every sub-issue (`gh issue view <n> --comments`) before writing code.
2. **Collect every decision before any code, in one pass.** The two tables below cover every `## Decisions` item in the sub-issues.
   - **"Ask" table:** each row needs an explicit answer. Rows whose recommendation reads "Your call" have no default; if the answer is no, or no answer comes, defer that issue.
   - **"Defaults" table:** these are adopted as written unless Uzair overrides them.
   - Record every answer as a comment on its issue: `Decision (Uzair, <date>): …`. The comment is binding for the implementer.
3. **Batch the mock gates.** Issues that change visible UI get static mocks via `html-communication`, and Uzair picks before implementation. Publish them together in one pass. #746, #748 and #761 share **one combined reply-footer mock**: the first of them to land creates the footer row, and the others add to it. Record each pick on its issue as `Design pick: <variant> — <URL>`.
4. **Prerequisites that aren't merged yet.**
   - **Inside this epic:** stack the dependent PR on its prerequisite's branch, say "Stacked on #<PR>; merge after it", and merge bottom-up.
   - **In another repo:** the #740 and #750 hermex-push PRs open first and merge before the app PRs; the app PR links to them.
   - **In #713** (#699, #700, #702, #705, #706): defer the issue until that foundation merges, unless the run explicitly includes it (e.g. #699 as a stack base).
5. **Manual gates.**
   - `needs-manual-validation` normally means Uzair tests before a PR opens. For this epic that is overridden: open the PR with a numbered **Manual test** section, and Uzair tests at review, before merging.
   - **Never done by agents:**
     - device builds and on-device testing;
     - relay deploys and hermex-push plugin installs;
     - host configuration changes;
     - Apple Developer portal or capability registration (the #771 entitlement and the #755 `Info.plist` are code-only);
     - live-host mutations, except where a Decision authorizes one (see D29, D30).
6. One issue → one `issue/<n>-slug` branch → one PR, following the repo's PR rules. Agents never merge.

## Decisions to collect up front

### Ask: needs an explicit answer

| # | Issue | Question | Recommendation | Answer (Uzair, 2026-09-24) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | #741, #742, #747, #748, #749 | Build Bot-surface features on today's Bot screens before #709 decides Chat vs Bots? Answer per issue | Yes for #741, #747 and #749: the status model and the section write path work under either option, and only thin views would move. #742 and #748 lean towards waiting for #709, because Option A replaces the inbox headers and the Bot-only reply action (#748 would then come from #705 5.3) | #741 yes, #742 yes, #747 yes, #748 **no (wait for #709; deferred)**, #749 yes |
| D2 | #742 | Section order on the phone, and where unfiled chats sit | A–Z by name, unfiled chats last; confirm through mocks | A–Z, unfiled last. **Plus: user can reorder sections on the phone** (phone-local order per server + connection, not synced to Desktop) |
| D3 | #743 | Ship host identity as its own slice before #700, or fold it into #700 slice 0.3 | Own slice, first | Own slice, first |
| D4 | #744 | Can a plain-HTTP LAN address be the fallback for an HTTPS tunnel, once `install_id` confirms it's the same host? | Yes | Not asked (#744 deferred) |
| D5 | #745 | Reverse #481's "Copy only" and allow edit/retry, which cuts the shared transcript that Desktop also shows? | Your call (the issue leans yes: Desktop rewinds the same way, and the cut is recoverable on the host) | Not asked (#745 deferred) |
| D6 | #747 | Folded into D1 | — | — |
| D7 | #749 | Folded into D1 | — | — |
| D8 | #750 | Allow answering an approval from a banner (reverses `bots.md` "never answered from a banner")? | Your call (the issue leans yes: Approve once and Deny only, with Approve behind device authentication) | **No answer → #750 deferred** |

title: docs(bots): correct the host claims in bots.md that are stale at the 0.21.4 pin
body:
Part of #737 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

**Related:** partly covered by #711: its bots.md slice owns different facts (handshake, pinned release name, `mcp.setup` removal, `turn_started_at`), and #699 owns the legacy `clarify.respond`/`pending_clarify` lines; neither touches the lines below. The sibling issues for inbox status, Desktop section headers and edit/regenerate each rewrite one of these lines again when they ship.

---

## Problem

`docs/agents/bots.md` and two code comments say the host can't do four things that it can do at `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` (d337b736, 0.21.4). The product choices behind them still hold. The reasons are wrong, and an agent planning Bot work reads "the host has no X" and stops there. Because the sibling feature issues are blocked (#699, #700/#702, #709), their own doc updates may be weeks away, so we should correct the facts now.

This came up during the OpenMausBot iOS audit (the idea of showing inbox status, sections and reactions on the phone).

## Contract

Docs and comments only. No host contract changes. Each fact below was checked at the pin:

1. **Inbox turn state.** `profiles.list` rows still carry no turn state (`ProfileRow`, `tui_gateway/contracts/profiles_vault_complete_foreign_subagents.py:147-163`). But `worker_session` is no longer "the only live signal". `session.active_list` returns live sessions with `status` ∈ `idle|starting|waiting|working|streaming|resuming` and `session_key` (`methods_session.py:962-973`; `server.py:2718-2726` and `:2735-2753`; `contracts/sessions.py:64-70` and `:232-251`). Its scope is the gateway process (`_snapshot_sessions`, `methods_session.py:142-148`), and Desktop polls it per socket (`apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts:521,751`).
2. **Desktop sections.** Desktop writes `sectionName` beside `sectionId` in `ui_meta["hermes-bots"]` on every filing and backfills it for older members (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/types.ts:59-70`, `user-sections.ts:137-199,258-270`; `saveBotMeta` sends the whole meta minus `image`/`pet`, `data.ts:354-367`). Section order and empty sections are still Desktop-local.
3. **Edit, regenerate and branch.** `prompt.submit` rewinds on `confirm_truncate` plus `truncate_before_row_id`, which is the preferred option (`contracts/prompt_voice.py:26-45`; `methods_prompt.py:248-265`). Snapshot messages carry a durable `row_id` (`contracts/common.py:131-142`; `session_history.py:237-239`). `session.branch` exists (`methods_session.py:2035`; `contracts/sessions.py:343-358`).
4. **Reactions.** `message.react` exists (`methods_session.py:1092-1116`; `contracts/billing_delegation_pets.py:467-491`). Reactions persist in `display_metadata.reactions` (`hermes_state.py:1545`; `hermes_state_messages.py:399-428`), and history passes `display_metadata` through to snapshot messages (`session_history.py:250-251`). The agent's reactions arrive live as the `message.reaction` event (`contracts/events.py:550-558`; `tools/react_to_message_tool.py:53`). Storing and reading reactions is not gated: `message.react` and the snapshot work whatever the host config. `display.message_reactions` (default false) gates only the model's side: the reaction note prepended to the next prompt (`methods_prompt.py:134-144`) and the agent's `react_to_message` tool (`tools/react_to_message_tool.py:61-63`).
5. **Internal inconsistency in the same paragraph.** `bots.md:410` says unpinned bots "follow in server order". The code and `bots.md:960-963` sort newest first (`BotInbox.swift:58-66`).

## Plan

- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md:71-76`: Copy alone stays, by the #481 canonical-chat policy. Say the host supports rewind (`prompt.submit` truncation) and `session.branch`, that Bot Chat doesn't offer them yet, and link #745.
- [ ] `bots.md:118-120`: keep `message.react` unwired. Replace "the snapshot carries no reactions" with: the host stores reactions in `display_metadata.reactions` and emits `message.reaction`, reactions are stored and synced whatever the host config (`display.message_reactions` only decides whether the model sees them and can react), and Hermex neither shows nor sends them yet. Leave the `learning.frames` clause as it is.
- [ ] `bots.md:408-416`: change "server order" to newest first. Say Desktop now publishes `sectionName`, so named headers are possible without upstream work, and that Hermex doesn't draw them yet (link #742). Order and empty sections stay Desktop-local.
- [ ] `bots.md:541-544`: list `sectionName` next to `sectionId` among the organization fields a duplicate doesn't copy.
- [ ] `bots.md:576-580`: say Working/needs-attention states aren't shown yet. Keep "the roster row carries no turn state". Replace "the only live signal" with the `session.active_list` fact and its process scope, and link #741.
- [ ] Comments: `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:89-91` (a named section is now available) and `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotMessageActions.swift:6-9` (Copy-only is the #481 policy, not a missing host capability).
- [ ] Cite pinned file:line only where the doc already cites sources that way. Otherwise name the RPC, field or event and leave line numbers out, per "validate volatile details just in time".

## Acceptance

- None of the five lines still says the host lacks something it has at d337b736.
- Every product decision is unchanged: Copy-only menu, reactions not wired, no section headers, no inbox status. Each one is now described as Hermex's choice or pending work, with the owning issue linked.
- No behavior change: the diff touches only `bots.md` and the two doc comments.

## Tests

None. This is docs and comments only. Proofread the diff against the files cited above, and don't run XCTest.

## Landing order

Land this first. The siblings (#741 inbox status, #742 section headers, #745 edit/regenerate, #761 reactions) should rebase onto it and rewrite the corrected line to describe what shipped, instead of fixing the stale text themselves. Whichever lands second takes the one-line conflict. Don't touch the #699 lines (legacy answer paths, `pending_clarify`) or the #711 items.

## Surfaces

- Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md`, plus two Swift doc comments. No other targets.

title: fix(bots): dismiss the keyboard when the Bot Chat transcript is tapped
body:
Part of #737 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

---

## Problem

In a Bot Chat, tapping the transcript leaves the keyboard up. Dragging down is the only way to put it away, so a user who wants to read a long reply has to know that gesture. Sessions chats and group rooms already dismiss on tap, so Bot Chat is the only chat surface that doesn't.

Seen in OpenMausBot's iOS app (`ios/App/ChatView.swift:308`): a simultaneous tap on the transcript clears composer focus, and links, card buttons, and selected text still get the tap.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

What Hermex already has:
- **Sessions:** `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:164` attaches `.simultaneousGesture(TapGesture().onEnded { onDismissKeyboard() })` to the transcript `ScrollView`. It calls `ChatView.dismissKeyboard()` (`ChatView.swift:2858`), which clears the screen-owned `composerIsFocused` (`ChatView.swift:344`) and then sends a global `resignFirstResponder`.
- **Rooms, already done in #627:** `BotRoomView.swift:74-76` uses `.contentShape(Rectangle())` and `.simultaneousGesture(TapGesture().onEnded { dismissKeyboard() })`, with a global resign at `:146`. Covered by `BotChatPresentationTests.testRoomTranscriptDismissesKeyboardWithoutLosingDraft` (`:127`). Rooms need no further change.
- **Bot Chat gap:** `BotChatView.swift:115` has only `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)`. The composer's focus is private state inside the composer (`BotChatComposerView.swift:24`, `@State private var isFocused`), which is passed to `ComposerTextInputView` (`:281-283`).

**Why not copy the room's global resign as-is:** unlike Sessions and rooms, Bot Chat puts text inputs *inside* the transcript. `BotPendingRequestCard` has a question `TextField` (`BotPendingRequestCard.swift:299`) and a sudo/secret `SecureField` (`:382`). A global `resignFirstResponder` fired from a simultaneous tap races the field becoming first responder, so tapping into the card could open and immediately close the keyboard. A global resign would also clear an active `ResponseSelectionInput` selection, which becomes first responder in `ResponseSelectionInput.swift:57-58`. Clearing only the composer's focus, as OpenMaus does and as Sessions does first, avoids both problems.

## Plan

- [ ] Lift composer focus to the screen, matching Sessions: `BotChatView` owns `@State private var composerFocused = false` and passes it to `BotChatComposerView` as `@Binding var isFocused: Bool`. Remove the composer's private `@State`. Its existing uses (`isExpanded`, picker restore, quote focus, settings) keep working through the binding.
- [ ] On the transcript `ScrollView` in `BotChatView`, next to `.scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)` (`:115`) and before the `.overlay(alignment: .bottom)` for the scroll-to-latest button: add `.contentShape(Rectangle())` so empty space and the non-hit-testable empty state register, then `.simultaneousGesture(TapGesture().onEnded { if composerFocused { composerFocused = false } })`. The guard means a tap that doesn't need to dismiss writes no state and doesn't re-evaluate the body.
- [ ] Add a one-line comment above the gesture saying why it is simultaneous (rows keep their taps) and why it targets only the composer (the request card has its own fields).
- [ ] Update the 8 `BotChatComposerView(...)` test call sites in `BotChatPresentationTests.swift` (`:341, :361, :421, :458, :495, :516, :566, :655`) to pass a binding from a small host view, not `.constant`, because the editor writes focus back.
- [ ] No doc change is needed. `docs/agents/bots.md` doesn't describe Bot Chat keyboard behavior.

## Acceptance

- With the composer focused in a Bot Chat, tapping transcript text, empty space, or the empty state ("Send a message to start the conversation.") hides the keyboard. The draft, attachments, and quotes stay, and tapping the composer focuses it again.
- Links in replies open, tool and reasoning rows expand, Load earlier works, and the scroll-to-latest button scrolls, all with one tap. With the keyboard up, that same tap also dismisses it.
- Tapping into a pending question's field or a sudo/secret field focuses that field and keeps the keyboard up. Its buttons (Approve, choices, Send, Skip, Stop) work.
- Long-press text selection in a reply still works, and "Ask Hermex" still focuses the composer.
- Drag-down dismissal is unchanged. Room behavior is unchanged.

## Tests

No UI mocks needed: nothing changes in layout or copy. This matches existing behavior.

- Hosted test in `BotChatPresentationTests`, modeled on `testRoomTranscriptDismissesKeyboardWithoutLosingDraft`: host `BotChatComposerView` with a parent-owned focus binding, focus the `ComposerChipTextView`, and type a draft. Set the binding to false, then assert that the editor resigned, the draft is unchanged, nothing was sent, and the editor can be focused again.
- Hosted test: render `BotChatView(model:)` with a pending question request (see the existing fixtures near `:318` / `:669`), make the card's text field first responder, and clear composer focus. Assert that the card field is still first responder. This guards the reason for targeting only the composer.
- Existing drag assertion: the Bot Chat transcript `UIScrollView` still has `.interactive` `keyboardDismissMode`.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests`
- Manual simulator check: open a Bot Chat, focus the composer, and tap a reply (keyboard hides, draft stays). Tap a link, then a tool row. Trigger a clarify question and tap its field (the keyboard stays). Scroll up and tap Latest. Test once with Reduce Motion on.

## Surfaces

- Entry points: every way into a Bot Chat goes through `BotChatView` (inbox, deep links, push, Live Activity taps at `BotsInboxView.swift:241`), so one change covers them all. Rooms are already done (#627).
- Targets: main app only. The composer's API is test-visible, so the `HermesMobileTests` call sites change.
- Servers: no server state involved. Focus is view-local, so nothing crosses a server switch.
- Reverse states: tapping the composer brings focus back. The draft is never discarded.
- Native quality: VoiceOver is unaffected because the gesture adds no element or trait. A hardware-keyboard tap on the transcript unfocuses the composer, as in Sessions. No strings change and there is no animation.
- Related: #213 (a preference to dismiss the keyboard after send) is a separate Sessions setting. This issue neither needs it nor blocks it. If #709 picks Option A (one chat view), Bot Chat would inherit Sessions' tap-dismiss. This fix is small enough to land now anyway.

title: fix(push): alert when the agent needs an approval or an answer while a Live Activity is running
body:
Part of #737 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

**Related:** related: #566 promised that approvals and questions always alert, and this relay rule breaks that promise; #706 slice 6.2 covers Live Activity identity and routing, not alerts; #699 must land before the Bot half can be checked on a 0.21.4 host

---

## Problem

If a Live Activity is running for a session and the agent stops to ask for an approval or an answer, the user gets no alert. The activity quietly switches to "Waiting for approval" / "Needs clarification", and the agent stays blocked until the user happens to look at the phone. This affects both Bot runs and webui runs on a paired server, whether the app is suspended or terminated. It is the moment the user most needs to know about.

Seen in OpenMausBot's iOS app (`ios/App/LiveActivities.swift:64-84`), which sends an `AlertConfiguration` when a bot starts needing the user.

## Contract

Client-only for Hermex, plus one relay policy change. No new host RPC, event or field.

- **Plugin (no change).** On an approval or a question, the plugin sends two events: `progress{status:"waiting"}`, then a separate `approval` / `clarify` notify event (`hermex-push/plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:285-296` for clarify, `:323-337` for approval). The host fires `pre_approval_request` at `tools/approval.py:914` and `tools/approval_gateway_wait.py:198` (pinned d337b736).
- **Relay (the bug).** `deliveryPolicy` returns `none` for every non-progress event when the session has an activity (`hermex-push/relay/src/policy.ts:9`). `activityPush` sends no `alert` (`relay/src/apns.ts:91-103`). So the `waiting` update is silent and the approval banner is thrown away. The rule is written down in `relay/README.md:67` ("A registered activity suppresses all banners for its session") and in Hermex `docs/agents/bots.md:1203-1205`. Tests that lock it in: `relay/test/policy.test.ts:12-13` and `relay/test/worker.test.ts:110-128`.
- **App.** Nothing in Hermex uses `AlertConfiguration`. The `waiting` states reach the manager from `ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:808-815` (webui) and `BotLiveActivityFeed.swift:119-120` (Bot). They go through `AgentLiveActivityManager.update` (`AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:300-307`), then `sendUpdate` (`:672-682`), which calls `activity.update(ActivityContent(...))` with no alert. `canReceivePush(_:)` (`:747-753`) already tells us whether the relay owns this activity. The "Waiting for approval" and "Needs clarification" strings are already in the catalog (`AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:555-566`).

## Plan

Two PRs. The relay PR lands and is deployed first (epic #737 step 5). The code doesn't need that order, because the local alert is gated on `canReceivePush` and never doubles a relay banner. But the app PR's `bots.md` change and its paired-server acceptance describe relay behavior that only exists after the deploy.

1. **`uzairansaruzi/hermex-push` (land first; the maintainer deploys the relay).**
   - [ ] `policy.ts`: when an activity exists, still send a banner for `approval` and `clarify` (and `input` once #566 adds it). Keep suppressing `reply` and `turn_error`. Subagent muting and previews apply as usual.
   - [ ] Update the tests: `policy.test.ts:12-13` (activity + approval → time-sensitive banner; activity + reply → none) and one worker test (activity registered, `waiting` progress then `approval` → exactly one silent `liveactivity` push and one `alert` push).
   - [ ] Change `README.md:67` to match.
2. **`hermex` (this issue).**
   - [ ] Add a pure `AgentLiveActivityAlertPolicy.alerts(previous:next:canReceivePush:appIsActive:) -> Bool`. It is true only when the status first moves into `.waitingForApproval` / `.waitingForClarification`, the activity is **not** relay-driven, and the app is not active.
   - [ ] Let `sendUpdate` take an optional `AlertConfiguration`. Build it from the attributes' title plus the existing waiting string, with `sound: .default`.
   - [ ] Update `docs/agents/bots.md:1203-1205` (the relay now alerts for approvals and questions during an activity) and add one line to § Bot Live Activity about the local alert.

## Decisions

- **Banner, not a Live Activity alert, on the relay.** Recommended. The banner already carries the sealed preview, which the notification extension opens on the phone ("Approval needed: `rm -rf build`"). A Live Activity push can't run the extension, so the relay could only send generic text. It also can't tell approvals from questions, because `status` is just `waiting`. The banner still arrives if the user swiped the activity away while the app was suspended; the registration outlives that, and today it silently swallows every banner. It is also one line of policy. Only one alert goes out: the `waiting` update stays silent.
- **The app alerts only when the relay can't.** On a paired server the relay banner covers the app in the foreground, in the background, and after termination, so a local alert would be a second buzz. The local alert is for unpaired servers, during the ~30 s of background time after the user locks the phone (`ChatView.swift:2747`). This matches the existing rule that local completion alerts never show in the foreground.
- Out of scope, tracked in #771: the app has no Time Sensitive entitlement (`HermesMobile.entitlements`), so the relay's `time-sensitive` level probably falls back to `active` and won't break through Focus.

## Acceptance

- Paired server, activity running, app suspended or terminated: an approval and a question each produce exactly one banner (with the decrypted preview when previews are on), and the activity shows Waiting. A reply after `done` still produces no banner.
- Unpaired server, app backgrounded within its background window: moving into waiting alerts once, and a repeated waiting event does not alert again. No local alert in the foreground or on a paired server.
- Tapping either alert opens the right session on the right server.

## Tests

- Relay: `npm test` in `relay/` (vitest policy and worker tests above).
- Hermex: `LiveActivityTests` covering the pure alert policy across (previous status, next status, paired, active). `--only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests` and `HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests`. No UI mocks needed; no layout or copy changes.
- Manual (physical phone; APNs and Live Activity alerts don't reproduce on the simulator): paired Bot and paired webui run with an approval while locked; unpaired webui run with an approval right after locking.

## Live checks for the implementer

- On a physical phone, check whether ActivityKit shows an `AlertConfiguration` while the app is in the foreground. If it does, keep the `appIsActive` gate.
- An approval without a host `session_id` is keyed by a derived id (`hooks.py:313-321`), which doesn't match the activity registration, so it already gets a banner. Use one disposable session to confirm which id a webui approval carries.

## Surfaces

- Entry points: webui chat stream and Bot feed both reach the one manager; the alert tap goes through the existing widget URL and push routing.
- Targets: main app only; the widget and notification service are unchanged.
- Servers: gating is per activity's server pairing (`canReceivePush`), so an alert never crosses servers.
- Reverse states: leaving waiting clears nothing; the next waiting transition may alert again.
- Connection modes: the relay path works on LAN and through the tunnel; the local path only needs the live stream.
- Native quality: existing localized strings; sound is `.default`.
- Docs: `bots.md` push and Live Activity sections; relay `README.md`.

title: feat(bots): show Working and Waiting for you on inbox rows and sort them first
body:
Part of #737 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** #699

**Decision needed before implementation:** ship this on today's Bots inbox before #709 is decided (recommended), or hold the presentation slice until #709 picks A or B?

**Related:** partly covered by #702: its slice 2.1 plans `session.active_list` "for live state" on the Hermes session list; this issue builds that status model once, for bot rows, and #702 should reuse it rather than build a second one

---

## Problem

The Bots inbox can't tell a bot that is working, or one that is blocked on an approval or question, from an idle bot. A user who sends a long task and goes back to the inbox has to open each chat to find the one that needs them. `docs/agents/bots.md:577-580` says the roster has no turn state. That is out of date: the host publishes live status per session.

Seen in OpenMausBot's iOS app (`ios/App/ChatListView.swift:771-784`, `BotThreadRow.swift:13-22`, `Sources/CompanionCore/AttentionInbox.swift:36-85`, rank waiting > working > queued > unread).

## Contract

**`session.active_list`**, params `{}` (pinned `d337b736`):
- Handler `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:962-973` returns `{sessions: [item]}`. It covers every non-finalized live runtime in this process, across all Profiles, in insertion order. It is read-only: Desktop re-pulls it on every `sessions.changed` and states it "does not resume, focus, or otherwise mutate a chat" (`apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts:400, 781`).
- Item `server.py:2735-2753`, contract `contracts/sessions.py:232-252`: `{id, session_key, status, last_active, started_at, message_count, model, preview, title, current}`. `session_key` is `agent.session_id` (the live compression tip), falling back to the stored key (`server.py:2759-2760`).
- `status` (`server.py:2718-2725`, enum `contracts/sessions.py:64-70`) is one of:
  - `waiting`: the runtime has an open server→client request. Its kind is internal and not on the item (`server_requests.py:290-294`). Kinds include `approval`, `clarify`, `sudo`, `secret`, `vault.*`, and the Desktop-only `terminal.read`, `window.read`, `preview.read`, `preview.act`, `tour` (`contracts/server_requests.py:58-208`).
  - `starting`: the agent is being built.
  - `working`: a turn is running.
  - `idle`.
  - The enum also has `streaming` and `resuming`, but this function never returns them.
  - A bot with no live runtime (reaped after the orphan grace period) is idle.

**Mapping.** `profiles.list` row `canonical_session` has `id` (the root) and `resolved_id` (the stored compression tip) (`methods_profiles.py:147-178`). A bot's status comes from items where `session_key ∈ {id, resolved_id}`. Match both, because `session_key` falls back to the stored key before the agent exists (`server.py:2759-2760`). Neither catches a tip the live agent rotated after the roster read. That item matches no bot until the next reload re-reads both, which the rotated turn's next `state.db` write triggers. If several items match one bot, the most urgent wins. Items carry no Profile, and Hermes itself does not trust bare ids across Profiles ("Timestamp-based stored ids can exist in several profiles' stores", `server.py:2764-2767`). So an item whose `session_key` matches more than one bot's ids is ambiguous and marks none of them.

**Caveats (verified in source):**
- **Waiting depends on #699.** If every WebSocket client attached to the session never sent `client.capabilities`, the host skips the request, so the status never becomes `waiting` (`server_requests.py:117-153`, `session_transports.py:38-47`). With no client attached, the request stays open and does show as `waiting`.
- **Only this process is covered.** Chat over `/api/ws` runs in-process (`hermes_cli/main.py:2662`), so Hermex and remote Desktop sessions on this host appear. Messaging-gateway (Telegram etc.) and cron turns run in other processes and never appear (`change_watcher.py:118-129`).
- **Lag.** `sessions.changed` follows `state.db` writes, checked every 0.5 s and throttled to at most one per 2 s (`change_watcher.py:200, 209`).
  - The tool-call turn is written before the tool runs (`agent/turn_tool_round.py:116-119`), so an approval opens a moment *after* the last write.
  - `running = False` is set after `message.complete` and post-turn work (`prompt_turn.py:985-1003`).
  - In both cases, a read triggered by the event can see the previous state, and no later write is guaranteed.

**Hermex seams:**
- `BotClient.call` allowlist (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift:142-148`).
- `BotInbox.open/noteChange/reload` (`BotInbox.swift:167-212, 318-370`) and sort order `byActivity` (`:58-67`).
- `BotProfile.init` (`BotConnection.swift:112-127`).
- `BotInboxRow` (`BotsInboxView.swift:519-557`).
- Precedent to reuse: the Sessions list's trailing status slot (`SessionRowView.swift:196-229`) and its `AttentionWorking`/`AttentionInput` tints. The localized strings "Working" and "Waiting for you" already exist in the catalog.

## Plan

- [ ] Slice 1 (model):
  - Allowlist `session.active_list` with exactly `{}` params.
  - Decode `BotProfile.canonicalID` / `canonicalTipID` tolerantly.
  - Add a pure `BotLiveStatus` (`waiting` > `working`, where `working` includes `starting` and `streaming`). An unknown status reads as no status.
  - Read the status inside `reload()` next to `profiles.list`, under the same serial and wire guards.
  - `-32601` hides statuses for the life of the socket.
  - Clear all statuses on disconnect and on a connection change, so a row never claims work it can't vouch for.
- [ ] Slice 1: after each event-driven reload in which any bot is not idle, run one trailing `active_list`-only re-read (~3 s). It is bounded per burst and is not a timer. See Decisions.
- [ ] Slice 1: sort each group (pinned tiles, the timeline, or each #742 section if that lands first) by rank: waiting, then working, then unread, then recency. Rooms rank with idle bots. Keep `ChatRow.id` stable so reordering doesn't rebuild rows.
- [ ] Slice 2 (presentation, after the mock pick): show a still glyph or label in the date slot, plus a marker on pinned tiles. No spinner and no working face pose in the inbox. Put the status in the combined VoiceOver label.
- [ ] Update `bots.md:577-580` (replace the "no turn state" sentence with the source, caveats and refresh rule) and add `active_list` to the verified-contract notes.

## Decisions

1. **Freshness (epic D27, needs your answer).** One trailing read ~3 s after an event burst can't guarantee fresh status. Post-turn work runs before `running = False`, including the goal judge, which is an LLM call (`prompt_turn.py:357`, `:986`, `:840-854`), and no later write is guaranteed. Reads from open or pull-to-refresh also schedule no follow-up.
   - **Option A (recommended):** re-read `session.active_list` every ~5 s, but only while the inbox is visible, connected, and some bot is non-idle. Desktop does the same every 30 s (`use-background-sync.ts:335, 783`). It's polling, so it needs your sign-off. It replaces the trailing read.
   - **Option B:** keep the trailing read, and weaken the promise to "status as of the last read", in both Acceptance and the manual check.
   - **Either way:** add a test where the transition lands after the final read, and assert the chosen behaviour (A re-reads; B keeps the last read and no test depends on a timer firing).
2. **#709. Recommended: don't block on it.** The status model is the same under both options. Option B keeps these rows. Option A moves the same `BotLiveStatus` onto the Profile strip avatars and the pinned Bot Chat row, and #702 reuses it for ordinary sessions. Only slice 2's views would be thrown away, and Bot Mode beta users get the feature in 1.7.
3. **Copy. Recommended: reuse "Working" / "Waiting for you"**, which are already translated and used by the Live Activity. Desktop-only request kinds also report `waiting`. The chat's card already explains those.

## Acceptance

- A bot whose canonical runtime is `working` or `starting` shows Working. A bot whose runtime is `waiting` shows Waiting for you. Idle or absent shows neither.
- Order: waiting, then working, then unread, then recency. Pinned tiles and each #742 section keep their own group; only rows inside a group reorder.
- A change reaches the row after `sessions.changed`, on open and on pull-to-refresh, with no timer.
- Disconnect or a connection switch clears every status. Another server's statuses never show.
- A host without `session.active_list` shows today's inbox unchanged.

## Tests

- `BotInboxTests` with `BotInboxFixtureWire` scripted replies:
  - root/tip mapping; a tip rotated after the roster read matches no bot until the next reload;
  - an item whose key matches two bots marks neither;
  - precedence across multiple matches;
  - unknown status;
  - `-32601`;
  - stale reply dropped after a newer reload;
  - statuses cleared on drop;
  - sort order;
  - exactly one trailing read per burst.
- `BotClientTests`: the allowlist accepts `{}` and refuses any other params.
- No sleeps: inject the trailing delay the way `reloadSpacing` is injected.
- Run `--only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests` (one `--only` per class, `scripts/test-sim:176, 215`).
- **UI mocks required first** (html-communication): the row label vs. glyph vs. still face expression, the tile marker, light/dark, and the largest Dynamic Type size. Wait for a pick before slice 2.
- Manual (sim): two bots, one mid-turn and one idle. Leave the chat, return to the inbox: Working shows and the bot sorts first. It clears after the turn. Reduce Motion stays still.

## Live checks for the implementer

1. After #699, on the disposable `inbox-triage` bot, call `session.active_list` read-only. Confirm that `session_key` equals `canonical_session.resolved_id`.
2. Using only that bot: start a turn that asks a clarify, and check `waiting` shows. Answer it, let the turn finish, and time whether the status clears without the trailing read. Delete only what you created.
3. Confirm that a remote-Desktop turn on the same host appears and a Telegram or cron turn does not.

## Surfaces

- Entry points: inbox rows and pinned tiles only. Push, Live Activity and deep links are unchanged.
- Targets: main app and tests only.
- Servers: status is per `BotInbox` (one server and connection) and cleared on a connection change.
- Reverse states: working and waiting both clear to idle. Disconnect clears.
- Connection modes: statuses depend on the socket. Background calls `close()`, and foreground re-reads through `open()`.
- Native quality: VoiceOver label, Dynamic Type, light/dark, Reduce Motion (nothing animates), and existing localized strings in all 18 languages.
- Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md`.

title: feat(bots): show Hermes Desktop's named sections in the Bots inbox
body:
Part of #737 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

**Decisions needed before implementation:** build this now or wait for #709 (epic D1)? And in what order should named sections appear on the phone, and should unfiled chats sit above or below them? (Recommendation: A–Z by name, unfiled chats last, decided through the mock gate.)

---

## Problem

Hermes Desktop lets users file bots into named sections ("Clients", "Ops"). The Bots inbox ignores them and shows one flat timeline, so a user with a sectioned roster loses that structure on the phone. We skipped sections in #474 because only an opaque `sectionId` reached the phone. That changed in v2026.9.21 (0.21.4, our pin): Desktop now writes the section's name next to its id on each bot, so the phone can show real headers. The comments in `BotConnection.swift:89-91` and `docs/agents/bots.md:413-415` that say otherwise are now wrong.

Seen in OpenMausBot's iOS app (`ios/App/ChatListView.swift:302-317`), where user-named sections are headers under the pinned and unfiled rows.

## Contract

No new RPC. The data is already in the `profiles.list` rows the inbox reads.

- `profiles.list` returns each profile's `ui_meta` exactly as stored in `profile.yaml` (`tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py:241-261`, typed `dict[str, JsonValue]` at `tui_gateway/contracts/profiles_vault_complete_foreign_subagents.py:161-162`). The host has no section-specific fields.
- In `ui_meta["hermes-bots"]`, Desktop stores `sectionId?: string|null` and `sectionName?: string|null` (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/types.ts:59-70`). Filing, renaming, or deleting a section updates each member bot's copy of both fields, one profile at a time (`user-sections.ts:117-131, 209-232, 258-272`). Deleting a section sets `sectionId` to null. Both upstream commits (`1197afc2b9`, `996c18274b`) are ancestors of `d337b736` and first shipped in v2026.9.21.
- The list of sections and their order is saved only on each Desktop machine (`bot-sections-v1`, `user-sections.ts:38, 76-94`). Another Desktop rebuilds sections from the members' fields. When members disagree on a name, a Desktop that already knows the section keeps its own name; a Desktop that doesn't takes the first member's name (`adoptBotSectionsFromMeta`, `user-sections.ts:133-171`). A bot that has `sectionId` but no `sectionName` can't be named, so it counts as unfiled (`groupRowsBySection`, `user-sections.ts:333-376`).
- In Desktop, pinned bots sort first inside their own section (`roster-pane-derivation.ts:210-236`). Hidden bots are left out of sections and shown in a separate flat Hidden group (`roster-pane-derivation.ts:59-62`, `roster-pane-sections.tsx:194-206`). Unfiled bots appear last under an "Unassigned" heading (`user-sections-ui.tsx:146-159`).
- Group rooms can't be sectioned on the phone. A room's section is saved only on the Desktop that filed it and is deliberately kept out of the gateway sync (`user-sections.ts:280-288`, `types.ts:223-230`).
- Filing a bot changes `ui_meta`, not `state.db`, so it does not trigger `sessions.changed`. The phone sees section changes on its next open, pull to refresh, or activity reload, the same way it sees pin and hide changes today.

Hermex code to change:
- `BotProfile.init` (`BotConnection.swift:113-127`) already reads `pinned` and `hidden` from `look`.
- `BotInbox.chats` / `pinned` / `rows(matching:)` (`BotInbox.swift:40-55, 136-141`).
- `BotsInboxView.list`: the pinned grid at `:82`, the timeline at `:111`, and the Show hidden button at `:119`.
- The pin and hide writes (`BotInbox.swift:284-310`) already send the whole `hermes-bots` object back, so they keep the section fields. `testHideRoundTripsDesktopFieldsAndConflictShowsNoSuccess` already covers `sectionId`.

## Plan

- [ ] Mocks first (see Tests), then wait for a pick.
- [ ] `BotProfile`: add `section: (id: String, name: String?)?`. Trim both values and treat an empty value as missing, the same way Desktop's `normalizeBotSections` does.
- [ ] `BotInbox`: add `var sections: [ChatSection]`, where `ChatSection` has `id`, `name` and `chats: [ChatRow]`, to replace the flat `chats` timeline:
  - Name each section by the name most of its members carry. Break ties with the first member in `profiles.list` order.
  - Treat members with no name as unfiled.
  - Order sections by the chosen decision.
  - Within each section, use the inbox's shared row order: newest first (the existing `byActivity`), or #741's attention rank (waiting, working, unread, recency) if #741 lands first. The pinned tiles and every section use the same sort function.
  - Put every room and every unfiled bot in one final unfiled block.
  - Pinned bots stay only in the pinned tiles and are not repeated in their section.
  - When revealed, hidden bots and rooms show dimmed in their own section, as they do in place today.
  - Draw no header for an empty section.
  - With no named sections, show no headers: the inbox looks exactly as it does today.
- [ ] `BotsInboxView`: read `inbox.sections` once per body (see the pattern in #730) and render one `Section` per entry. Show section names with `Text(verbatim:)` on one line, truncated. The unfiled block gets a header only when at least one named section exists.
- [ ] Localize the unfiled header in all 18 catalog languages. Use a new key (for example "Other chats"), not the Kanban "Unassigned" key, because this block also holds group rooms.
- [ ] Update the docs: `BotConnection.swift:89-91`, and `docs/agents/bots.md:408-416`, which is also already wrong about "server order" (the code sorts newest first, as `:960-963` says). Also mention `sectionName` next to `sectionId` at `:543`.
- [ ] Leave out filing or moving bots between sections from the phone (YAGNI). The inbox only reads sections, so there is no one-way door.

## Decisions

1. **Section order.** Only each Desktop saves the order, so the phone must pick its own. Recommend **A–Z by name** (`localizedStandardCompare`, ties by id): it's predictable, and users can control it with prefixes. Trade-off: it won't match a Desktop where the user reordered sections with Move up/down. Rejected alternatives: sorting by the timestamp inside the `sec-<base36 ms>-…` id, which parses an opaque id format; and sorting by latest member activity, which makes headers jump around and breaks the calm feel.
2. **Unfiled chats last or first.** Recommend **last**, to match Desktop. OpenMaus puts them first. The mocks should show both.
3. **Pinned bots.** Recommend they appear in the tiles only. Desktop instead sorts pinned bots first inside their section. Showing them in both places would repeat them.

## Acceptance

- A roster with bots in "Clients" and "Ops" shows those headers, with members in the inbox's row order (newest first, or attention first once #741 lands). Rooms and unfiled bots follow as one block.
- Renaming a section on Desktop shows the new name after a refresh. While members disagree, the majority name is shown.
- Deleting a section on Desktop moves its members to the unfiled block after a refresh. A `sectionId` with no name also counts as unfiled.
- A roster with no sections looks exactly as it does today.
- Pin, unpin, hide and unhide from the phone keep `sectionId` and `sectionName` unchanged.
- VoiceOver announces headers as headers. Long names truncate at the largest Dynamic Type size, in both light and dark mode.

## Tests

**UI mocks required before implementing:** a sectioned inbox with pinned tiles, unfiled last vs first, with hidden bots revealed, and with no sections, each in light and dark mode and at a large Dynamic Type size.

- `BotInboxTests`, using the existing `BotInboxFixtureWire` roster rows (no sleeps):
  - sections are grouped and ordered, with activity order inside each section;
  - majority naming and its tie-break;
  - a missing name or a deleted section counts as unfiled;
  - pinned bots are left out of sections;
  - revealed hidden bots stay in their section;
  - rooms are always unfiled;
  - with no sections, the output matches the current `chats`.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests`.
- Manual check in the simulator: `scripts/sim-login`, then sectioned, pinned and hidden rows, pull to refresh after a Desktop rename, and VoiceOver on headers.

## Live checks for the implementer

- Read only: sign in and call `profiles.list` on the test host. Check whether any `ui_meta["hermes-bots"]` has `sectionName`. If none does, ask the maintainer to file the disposable test bot `inbox-triage` into a section from Desktop 0.21.4 or later, check it, then unfile it. Don't write to `ui_meta` from the phone to set this up.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** only the inbox list. Search, @-mentions, deep links, share and Live Activity stay flat and unchanged.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** sections come only from each connection's roster and nothing is stored on the phone, so no data can leak between servers.
- **Reverse states:** read only. Unfiling happens on Desktop.
- **Native quality:** Dynamic Type, VoiceOver header trait, light and dark mode, 18 languages, right-to-left layout with the header text as given.
- **Docs:** `bots.md` and the `BotConnection` comment, as listed above.
- **Relation to #709:** under Option A the inbox is replaced by a Profile strip. The section logic in `BotInbox` could carry over to the strip, but the headers would not. Whether to build now or wait is epic decision D1: record the answer here before starting. If D1 says wait, this issue moves to "After #709" in the epic.
