title: fix(bots): offer Password AutoFill on the secret field and reset it per request
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #753

Stacked on #775; merge after it.

## What changed

**Problem.** When a bot asks for a secret (usually an API key), the secure field has no content type, so iOS offers no Passwords key. Users with keys in iCloud Keychain or a password manager have to leave Hermex to copy them.

A smaller bug came up along the way. The credential body sits under the card's constant `.id(BotChatView.requestAnchor)`, and its `@State value` isn't tied to any request. A password half-typed into a sudo prompt that times out stays in the field when a `secret` request replaces it, so one tap on Send would save the Mac password to the host's `.env`.

**Fix (client-only).** The host contract doesn't change; it was verified at the pinned hermes-agent `d337b736`: `secret` -> `ValueResult {value}`, and `''` means skip.

1. `BotPendingRequestCard.swift`: `.textContentType(.password)` for both sudo and secret, which brings up the QuickType Passwords key.
2. `BotCredentialRequestBody` is keyed by `credential.requestID` at the `case .credential` site. A new request gets a fresh, empty field, and the old typed value leaves with the old view.
3. The `BotCredentialRequestBody` doc comment now covers AutoFill and the per-request reset.
4. `docs/agents/bots.md` (credential input paragraph): the field uses `.password` AutoFill, is keyed by request id, and iOS offers no "Save Password?" because there is no associated domain.

**Decisions applied**
- From the issue: `.password`, not `.oneTimeCode` or `.newPassword`. No associated-domain entitlement. No new strings; VoiceOver labels unchanged.
- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/753#issuecomment-5824372772): built in the epic #737 run, stacked on #699 (#775). Live checks beyond read-only curl/RPC are not run by the implementer; they are listed under Manual test.

**Surfaces.** Credential cards render only in `BotChatView` (`BotRoomComposerView` renders approvals only). Main app target only. No new copy; Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and dark mode are unchanged. No Xcode project changes. No screenshots, since the layout is unchanged.

## How it was tested

New test `BotChatPresentationTests.testCredentialFieldOffersAutoFillAndResetsForTheNextRequest` hosts `BotPendingRequestCard` through a small `@Observable` harness that swaps the request under one mounted card, as `BotChatView` does. It starts on a sudo prompt, types "hunter2", swaps in a secret request with a different `requestID`, and checks that the secret field is empty and has `textContentType == .password`. It waits on layout through the existing `renderFrames()` expectation, with no sleeps.

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Red check with the fix reverted: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests/testCredentialFieldOffersAutoFillAndResetsForTheNextRequest` gave 1 test, 2 failures (the secret field still held "hunter2"; its `textContentType` was nil). Re-confirmed after the round 1 test reorder (26f1b65).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`: 34 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the existing `XCTSkipUnless` for the in-process accessibility tree, unrelated).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestParsingTests`: 15 passed, 0 failed.

Device: iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator, branch `issue/753-secret-field-autofill`.

### Manual test (Uzair, at review; not run by the implementer per epic #737 N2)

1. Simulator, branch build: on a disposable `inbox-triage` Bot session, trigger a skill secret prompt. Tap the secret field. **Expected:** the QuickType bar shows the Passwords key. Tap **Skip** (sends `{value:""}`) so nothing is written to the host's `.env`, then delete the session.
2. Physical device with iCloud Keychain: submit a secret. **Expected:** no "Save Password?" sheet appears afterward.
3. Optional: type text into a sudo prompt and let it time out (120 s), then trigger a secret request. **Expected:** the new field is empty.

title: fix(networking): let plain HTTP reach .local, single-label and Tailscale ts.net names
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #755

Stacked on #780; merge after it.

## What changed

**Problem.** The Bot connection form sends `.local`, single-label and Tailscale addresses over plain HTTP, and its footer says Tailscale names work. But the main app's ATS policy listed only IP/CIDR exceptions, so `http://host.tailnet.ts.net:<port>` failed with -1022. The webui ATS error also told users that only a Tailscale IP would work.

**Fix.**
- `HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist` (**release-sensitive**: it ships in App Store builds): adds `NSAllowsLocalNetworking = true` and a `ts.net` exception with `NSIncludesSubdomains` + `NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads`. All existing CIDR entries stay, since they are the only thing covering 100.64/10. Still no `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`. The comment above the dict is updated. **Re-check the App Review ATS justification at the next release**: `ts.net` is one more per-domain insecure-HTTP exception.
- Scheme inference is unchanged. A schemeless `host.ts.net` stays HTTPS (Tailscale Serve), and a TLS failure never downgrades to HTTP.
- `APIError.networkMessage`: the ATS case now reuses #751's string, "iOS blocked this insecure HTTP connection. Use HTTPS, a local network address, or a Tailscale name or IP." That string already has all 17 languages in the String Catalog from #751; the old string's catalog entry is removed.
- The Bot-form ATS mapping belongs to #751 and isn't touched here.
- Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md` (the ATS policy line) and `DEVELOPMENT.md` (physical-device HTTP guidance).

### Decisions applied
- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/755#issuecomment-5824373049): add the `ts.net` plain-HTTP ATS exception (D12).
- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/755#issuecomment-5824373049): (N1) stacked on #751, which owns the Bot-form ATS mapping and the ATS string; this PR owns `Info.plist` (code-only; Uzair confirms the App Review side), the webui `APIError` copy and the docs.

### Plan
1. Add `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` and the `ts.net` exception to the main app's ATS dict; keep every CIDR entry.
2. Point the webui ATS error at the shared string from #751; drop the stale catalog entry.
3. Update the ATS lines in `docs/agents/bots.md` and `DEVELOPMENT.md`.
4. Extend the plist policy test so it fails on the old plist.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air> --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionSetupTests`: 12 passed, 0 failed. `testLocalAddressDefaultsHaveNarrowTransportExceptions` now asserts `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` is true, `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` is absent, `ts.net` is present, and `NSIncludesSubdomains` is true for `ts.net`. It failed on the base plist with 3 assertion failures.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/APIClientAuthAndErrorTests`: 17 passed, 0 failed (`testAppTransportSecurityErrorUsesHTTPGuidance` updated for the new copy).
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionAdviceTests`: 1 passed, 0 failed (#751's test of the shared ATS string).
- Full suite not run locally: `Info.plist` lives in `HermesMobile/Resources`, not `Config/` or the Xcode project, and no files were added. CI runs the full suite.

**Local ATS measurement** (iPhone Air simulator, iOS 26; an uncommitted hosted XCTest ran `URLSession` loads against a local `python3 -m http.server 9199`, stopped by its captured PID). Before → after:
- `http://<mac>.local:9199`: -1005 → -1005. Not ATS in either run (the sim loses the connection, likely IPv6 against an IPv4-only server).
- `http://<mac>:9199` (single-label): -1000 → -1000. Not ATS; the Mac can't resolve the name either.
- `http://localhost:9199`: HTTP 404 in both.
- `http://example.com`: -1022 → -1022. Still blocked, as intended.
- `http://login.tailscale.ts.net`: -1022 → -1000. Now gets past ATS.

So on current iOS, ATS already let `.local` and single-label names through; `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` is Apple's recommended declaration of intent and costs nothing. The user-visible fix is `ts.net`.

## Manual test

Labelled `needs-manual-validation`. These checks were skipped by the agent:

1. On a physical iPhone signed into Tailscale, with a Hermes host on the tailnet serving plain HTTP, add a Bot connection with `http://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:<port>`. Expected: it connects (no "iOS blocked this insecure HTTP connection" error). The maintainer doesn't use Tailscale, so this may need a tester who does.
2. On the same device, enter the schemeless `<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net`. Expected: the app uses HTTPS (Tailscale Serve); if TLS fails, it shows the HTTPS error and never falls back to HTTP.
3. In the Bot connection form, enter `http://example.com`. Expected: the ATS message "iOS blocked this insecure HTTP connection. Use HTTPS, a local network address, or a Tailscale name or IP." (#751's mapping; checked here at the URLSession layer only).
4. Add a webui server at a public `http://` address. Expected: the same ATS message as step 3.
5. Before the next App Store release: re-check the App Review ATS justification covers the new `ts.net` per-domain exception.

title: feat(bots): fold a finished Bot turn behind the Sessions "Worked for" row
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #747

Bottom of the stack under #787 and #791.

## What changed

**Problem.** Bot Chat ignored Settings > Chat > Fold Finished Turns. Every finished Bot turn kept all of its reasoning, tool rows and interim replies on screen, so reading back meant scrolling past the work to reach each answer. Separately, when the host had already saved the running turn's prompt plus a mid-turn step, the prompt was drawn twice.

**Fix (client-only; no new host contract).** Bot Chat now reuses the Sessions fold engine unchanged, so a finished turn keeps its first and last reply and folds the rest behind the same "Worked for 42s" row.

- `BotTranscriptProjection.turnFolds(...)` in `BotActivity.swift` is a thin adapter over `TranscriptTurnFolds.derive`. It runs over the ~50-row window only, with `messageOffset: windowStart`, so turn keys stay absolute across Load earlier. Only assistant rows fold. Activity anchored to a user row or after the last message never folds, and neither do live rows, the plan row, request cards, the Working row, delegation cards or rooms. The host sends no turn duration, so the label is the time from the turn's opening row to its last timestamp, or just "Worked" when there are no timestamps.
- **Delegation deliveries open their own turn.** The adapter hands the engine a copy of the window where a `delegation_completion` row reads as a prompt, so the reply to each delivery is its own turn and is timed from the delivery, not across the delegation wait. This matches the #746 time logic, which already treats a delivery as closing a turn. The rendered rows keep their real role.
- **The running turn stays open.** `BotConversation.applySnapshot` sets `activePromptMessageID`: the last prompt or delivery row (steers skipped) dated at or after the turn's `started_at`. The host stamps that row after it starts the turn (`methods_prompt.py:556` before the submit persist; deliveries persist inside the turn). Text can't decide this: a slash skill's saved row shows `/work fix the leak` while the in-flight `user` is the expanded body, and a delivery saves as a card. Only an undated row falls back to the text match. `live-user` is added only when no row is found, so the prompt draws once. The fold treats the latest settled turn as running whenever the bot is streaming and no prompt is only live.
- **BotChatView** reads both display settings through `@AppStorage` and keeps `@State expandedTurnKeys`. It draws `TranscriptTurnFoldRowView` above the host row. Folded activity and bubbles are never built; a gap time separator stays even when the reply after it folds. On toggle it plays the disclosure haptic, stops following and animates with `ChatMotion.disclosure`, which respects Reduce Motion. **Load earlier** opens the turn that would fold away the reply the reader was on, so the scroll target still exists and they keep their place.
- **Perf (folded in from the issue).** `settledActivityByAnchor` is rebuilt in a `didSet` on `settledActivity`, and the view looks up each row's activity by anchor instead of filtering the whole history per message. The body now does no work proportional to `settledActivity.count`. `reasoning.utf8.count` is used in the view's onChange and as an O(1) guard in front of the O(n) trim count.
- `docs/agents/bots.md` activity paragraph updated. The copy, row and VoiceOver strings are the existing Sessions ones, so there are no new strings.
- **Master's test build.** The first commit renames `wire.pendingClarify` to `openClarify` in #774's `testQuestionFieldKeepsTheKeyboardWhenComposerFocusClears`. #775 renamed the field while #774 was open, so the test target stopped compiling once both merged; this file is one #784 also edits.

### Plan

The issue's plan, with one deviation: the fold's running-turn rule is `isStreaming && !hasLivePrompt` rather than `isStreaming && activePromptMessageID != nil`, so a turn with no in-flight prompt (started from Desktop, or a continuation) also stays open instead of folding mid-turn.

### Decisions applied

- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/747#issuecomment-5824371907): build now. Sessions' fold rule; no "You stopped after" label; no mocks.

### Contract

Checked read-only against the pinned hermes-agent `d337b736`: `tui_gateway/session_history.py:205-245` (timestamps only on persisted user/assistant rows, tool rows have none, a reasoning-only row arrives with `text: ""`, a skill turn projects to its invocation with `display_kind: skill_invocation`), `:277-290` (`_start_inflight_turn` sets `started_at`), `session_workdir.py:348-372` (submit-time row stamped after the turn starts), `prompt_turn.py:140` and `session_notifications.py:472` (delegation delivery runs as a turn with `async_delegation_complete`).

## How it was tested

All on iPhone 17e (`1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3`), one `--only` class per run, at `fd4f07b` (BotActivityTests and BotConversationTests at `3cdeaaf`; the later commit only touched the view and a hosted test):

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotActivityTests`: 20 passed, 0 failed. New adapter tests cover the settled fold and label, no timestamps, live vs. saved running turn, a mid-turn mixed snapshot, a running skill or delivery turn staying open, each delivery opening its own turn timed from the delivery, the Load earlier turn lookup, user/nil-anchored activity, cards off, the toggle off, and absolute keys under a window offset.
- `... --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests`: 50 passed, 0 failed. New: `testMidTurnPersistedPromptNamesTheRunningTurnAndDrawsOnce` and `testRunningSkillOrDelegationTurnNamesItsSavedRowByTheTurnClock`.
- `... --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`: 37 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (pre-existing skip). New hosted `testSettledTurnHidesItsInterimReplyBehindTheWorkedForRow` and `testFoldedInterimReplyKeepsItsGapSeparator` (a pause before a folded reply keeps its time separator; confirmed failing without the fix). `testActivityRowsRenderAndFollowTheCardsSetting` now turns folding off for its own run, since its settled turn folds by default.
- Earlier in this branch, before the review fixes (the engine and scroll policy are untouched): `TranscriptTurnFoldingTests` 15 passed, `BotMentionTests` 10 passed, `ChatScrollPolicyTests` 28 passed.

The full suite was not run locally: the Xcode project, `Config/` and shared test infrastructure are untouched. CI runs it. No screenshots: the fold row is the shipped Sessions row, and the hosted test can't tap it (the hosted window exposes no accessibility tree to activate).

### Manual test

Simulator or phone with a Bot connection that has a turn with several tool calls and replies. Live checks against the maintainer's host were skipped (the change is client-only); every step below is still to be run.

1. Open a Bot with a finished multi-tool turn. Expected: the prompt, a "Worked for …" row, the first reply and the final reply. The reasoning, tool rows and interim replies are hidden.
2. Tap the row at the latest edge, then again after scrolling up. Expected: it expands in place without moving the reader or snapping back to the bottom; tapping again collapses. With Reduce Motion on, it snaps.
3. Send a message. Expected: the previous turn stays folded; the running turn never folds while the bot works; the prompt draws once.
4. Run a slash skill (e.g. `/work …`) and leave and reopen the chat mid-turn. Expected: the running turn stays open and the prompt shows once as the invocation.
5. Start a delegation and wait for its delivery. Expected: the reply to each delivery sits in its own turn, and its "Worked for" time counts from the delivery, not from the original prompt.
6. In a Bot with more than 50 messages, scroll to the top and tap Load earlier. Expected: the message that was at the top stays at the top.
7. Settings > Chat: turn Fold Finished Turns off (nothing folds), then turn Thinking and Tool Cards off (a turn whose only hidden work was activity has no row).
8. Check the largest accessibility Dynamic Type size, dark mode, and VoiceOver. Expected: VoiceOver reads the label, "Expanded" or "Collapsed", and the hint.

title: feat(bots): show a read-only status section on the Hermes connection screen
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #752

## What changed

**Problem.** The Hermes connection screen (`BotConnectionView`) is only a sign-in form. When Bots stall or a scheduled Task never reports back, the user can't tell from the phone whether the host is reachable, which release it runs, or whether its messaging gateway is up.

**Fix.** With a saved connection, the screen now opens with a read-only **Status** section. It reads the host's public `GET /api/status` once, sending no cookies or credentials. "Check again" re-runs only that probe.

### Plan

- **`BotHostStatus`** (`BotProtocol.swift`): a tolerant model built from `BotJSON`. Every field is optional: `version`, `gateway_running`, `gateway_state`, `gateway_exit_reason`, `gateway_heartbeat_stale_s`, and `components.platforms.{connected,configured}`.
- **`BotHostStatusProbe`**: one `GET /api/status` on its own ephemeral `URLSession`. It has a 15 s timeout, no cookie storage, sets no cookies and has no credential storage. Results map to typed failures:
  - a `URLError` is **unreachable**, with the system's reason
  - a 401 or 403, or a redirect to another host (such as a Cloudflare Access sign-in page), is **"An access check blocked this request"**
  - any other non-200 is **"The host answered <code>"**
  - a 200 whose body isn't a JSON object is **"This address isn't a Hermes dashboard"**
  - It never uses `BotFailure`'s chat copy.
- **`BotConnectionSetup`**: adds `hostStatus` (`.checking` / `.reachable` / `.unreachable`) and `checkStatus()`.
  - It probes only `saved.address`, and only when a connection is saved.
  - A UUID guard (the same pattern as `attempt`) drops any reply that arrives after `cancel()`, after a newer check, or after the saved address changed. Such a reply never writes state.
  - A sign-in that changes the saved host drops the old host's status and any check in flight, and re-reads the relay after the old connection's cleanup (review round 1).
  - `load()` reads the notification relay for this server from `PushRegistrar`.
  - The probe and the relay reader are injectable for tests.
- **`BotConnectionView`**: adds a top **Status** Form section, shown only with a saved connection. Rows are label/value pairs, and each row is one VoiceOver element that includes its note.
  - Reachability: static "Checking…" text, no spinner.
  - Hermes: the live version, or the stored version marked "at last sign-in".
  - Messaging gateway: the state, plus the exit reason and "Scheduled Tasks won't run until it starts." ("Not responding" when the heartbeat is stale).
  - Platforms: "N of M connected".
  - Notifications: "On · relay host" or "Off".
  - The saved address (selectable) with Copy, and **Check again** (disabled while checking).
  - The footer says the gateway runs scheduled Tasks and messaging platforms, and that Bot chat notifications still arrive while it is stopped.
  - The check loads in `.task` and is cancelled on disappear. There is no polling and no auto-retry.
- **String Catalog**: 22 new keys, each translated into all 17 shipped languages (marked `needs_review`). Existing keys are reused for Status, Notifications, Off, Copy, Copied, Starting, Running and Unknown.
- **`docs/agents/bots.md`**: one sentence on the Status section. The existing "no version warning" line stays.

No new files, so the pbxproj is unchanged. There is no new RPC, so the `BotClient` RPC allowlist is untouched: the probe is a plain public HTTP GET of the existing `BotEndpoint.status`.

### Decisions applied

- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/752#issuecomment-5824372657): "Check again" re-runs only the public `/api/status` probe, with no sign-in (D10).
- Default adopted (same comment): no admin actions, so no gateway restart.

### Design

- Mock: https://edaa2t1bjfl4.postplan.dev §3. **Pick: A**, a top "Status" Form section of label/value rows with static "Checking…" and no spinner.
- Deviations from the mock:
  - The footer names its subject ("The messaging gateway runs scheduled Tasks…") so it reads clearly on its own.
  - A Cloudflare Access redirect or a 401/403 reads "An access check blocked this request", so it isn't mistaken for "not Hermes".
  - While the host is unreachable or still being checked, the gateway, platforms and footer rows are hidden, as in mock A.
- **No screenshot yet.** This screen has no deep link, and the lane couldn't drive the simulator UI without the shared XcodeBuildMCP session defaults. After-screenshots are part of the manual test below.

### Contract

The model was verified against the pinned hermes-agent `d337b736`: `hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:451-523`, with the not-running normalization in `gateway/status.py` `retained_gateway_state`. A read-only, unauthenticated `curl https://<host>/api/status` on 2026-09-24 returned `version` 0.21.5, `gateway_running` true, `gateway_state` running, a null exit reason and a null stale heartbeat, and `components.platforms` `{configured 5, connected 5}`. That matches the model.

## How it was tested

`git diff --check` is clean. Focused tests on iPhone Air `D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A`, each run with `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/<Class>`:

| Class | Result |
|---|---|
| `BotHostStatusTests` (new) | 6 passed, 0 failed |
| `BotConnectionSetupTests` | 15 passed, 0 failed after the rebase onto `25cd2202` (3 new: the check probes only this server's saved host; a late reply after cancel or a newer check is dropped; a sign-in that changes the host drops the old host's status and relay) |
| `BotConnectionVersionTests` | 2 passed, 0 failed |
| `LocalizationCatalogTests` | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| `BotConnectionAdviceTests` (from master) | 1 passed, 0 failed |
| `BotChatPresentationTests/testQuestionFieldKeepsTheKeyboardWhenComposerFocusClears` | 1 passed, 0 failed |

The last row is a one-line compile fix: #774 landed after #775 renamed `BotFixtureWire.pendingClarify` to `openClarify`, so master's test target does not build. It is the same hunk as #784, so whichever merges second takes it as a no-op.

- **Catalog coverage:** `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py` against a signed Debug build covers all 1872 extracted keys.
- **Mutation checks** (each test fails when its guard is removed):
  - The probe's session-configuration test (no cookie storage, no cookie setting, no credential storage, 15 s timeout, no Authorization header, no body) fails if the cookie lines are removed. It replaces a request-header assertion that couldn't catch that.
  - `testRedirectToAnotherHostReadsAsBlocked` fails if the cross-host comparison is removed from `check(_:)`. That is the Cloudflare Access path: a 302 to another host ending on a 200 HTML page.

The full suite wasn't run locally because no Xcode project, `Config/` or shared test infrastructure changed. CI runs it.

### Manual test

On a simulator or device signed in to a server with a saved Hermes connection:

1. Open the connection screen from **Settings → server → Hermes connection**. **Expected:** a **Status** section at the top. It shows "Checking…" briefly, then Reachable, the Hermes version, Messaging gateway **Running**, Platforms "N of M connected", Notifications "On · relay host" or "Off", and the saved address with **Copy**.
2. Open the same screen from the **Notifications** section and from the **Bots inbox** connection sheet. **Expected:** the same Status section on both.
3. Tap **Copy**. **Expected:** the address is on the pasteboard and the button briefly shows "Copied".
4. Turn on airplane mode (or stop the network) and tap **Check again**. **Expected:** the button disables while checking, then the host reads as unreachable with the system reason. The gateway, platforms and footer rows are hidden, and no sign-in is attempted.
5. With a host behind Cloudflare Access (no service token), tap **Check again**. **Expected:** "An access check blocked this request", not "This address isn't a Hermes dashboard".
6. Check Dynamic Type at its largest, light and dark, and VoiceOver. **Expected:** each row reads as one element with its note, and nothing animates continuously.
7. Capture after-screenshots (light, dark, large Dynamic Type) for this PR.

Skipped live checks (not run by the agent):

- The stopped or startup_failed gateway state needs a host mutation. It is covered by fixtures only.
- The Cloudflare Access blocked path was not exercised live (step 5).
- Airplane mode + Check again was not run (step 4).
- The three openers were not driven (steps 1 and 2).

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

title: feat(bots): answer a bot's request to connect an app from the phone
body:
Stacked on #782; merge after it.

## Linked issue

Fixes #770

## What changed

**Problem.** When a bot calls `manage_connections` (to connect Gmail, or to install, enable or sign in to an MCP server), the host holds the tool for up to 300 s while it waits for a connection card. Hermex showed "needs attention", but the user had no way to answer. The bot stayed blocked until the deadline and then carried on with `not_connected`.

**Fix.** Design pick A: stacked rows inside one card in the existing request-card style, with a static deadline and no spinner.

- **Model.** `BotConnectionOperation` (`BotPendingRequest.swift`) reads `connection.request`, `connection.update` and the snapshot's `pending_connection` tolerantly.
  - An unknown `kind`, `action` or `state` keeps its row readable but offers no actions.
  - An operation with no readable row shows as needs-attention with no card.
  - Rows stay in server order and duplicate rows are dropped.
  - A frame replaces the held one only when its `seq` is newer. `settled: true` closes the operation.
  - It is a new `BotPendingRequest.connection` case, ranked after server requests.
- **Conversation (`BotConversation`).**
  - Restores the operation from `pending_connection` on every snapshot. The same revision guard that protects server requests stops an older snapshot from overwriting it.
  - Applies live and replayed frames.
  - Clears the operation when resume omits the field, on the settled frame, and on disconnect or reset. It remembers the last settled `op_id` so a late frame can't bring the operation back.
  - `respondToConnection` captures generation, runtime and `op_id` at tap and revalidates them at dispatch through `answerGuard`. It never retries.
    - A 4004 reply means the operation had already settled: the card goes inert and a refresh follows.
    - A lost reply is marked uncertain and the conversation reconnects.
  - Guide (steer) and Queue send `settled_by: "continue"` before the message.
    - If the host rejects that (for example with 4004), the message still goes.
    - If the Continue reply is lost, the message is held back and the draft is kept.
    - Interrupt already settles the operation on the host, so it sends no Continue.
- **Client.** `connection.respond` is on the `BotClient` allowlist with a strict validator: `{session_id, op_id, result}`, where `result` is either exactly one row (`approved` with an optional non-empty `env`, or `skipped`) or `{settled_by: "continue"}` alone.
- **Card (`BotPendingRequestCard.swift`).**
  - One row per app, showing its name, state, and the host's detail, instructions and discovery error.
  - **Open link** (`openURL`, so the default browser) appears only for connector rows with an https `connect_url` that are pending or initiated.
  - **Connect** appears for MCP enable and install rows that are pending or failed, with one field per `required_env`.
    - Secret fields use `SecureField` with `.password`.
    - A plain field starts at its catalog default and sends it, as Desktop does.
    - Values are trimmed, reset per `op_id` and row, and cleared the moment they are sent.
  - MCP sign-in rows (`authorize`, or an install that returned a `connect_url`) say "Finish on the Mac." and offer only Skip, because the redirect goes to the host's loopback.
  - Failed or expired rows say "Skip it and ask the bot to try again." Try again is deferred per the decision.
  - Each row has Skip, and the card has **Continue without**.
  - The deadline redraws once a minute (`TimelineView(.everyMinute)`) using the system's own duration wording.
  - Buttons stack full width at accessibility sizes, each row action has a VoiceOver label, and the card announces "Input needed: Connect apps".
- **Copy.** 21 new String Catalog keys, each translated into all 17 shipped languages.
- **Docs.** `docs/agents/bots.md` gets a "Connection operations" paragraph (an event plus an RPC, not a server request; the row types the phone can't finish; setup defaults; the contract citation). It replaces the stale "without a card" line.

**Contract.** Every shape was checked against the pinned hermes-agent d337b736 (0.21.4):
- `tui_gateway/contracts/connectors_operation.py`
- `tui_gateway/methods_connectors.py` (`connection.respond`; 4004 is UNKNOWN_OPERATION)
- `tools/connectors/operation.py` and `tools/connectors/contract.py` (seq, settling, which moves are allowed)
- `tools/connectors/mcp.py` (`apply_answer`, `_missing_required`, the install and OAuth flows)
- `tui_gateway/server.py:734-742, 2863-2868` (`pending_connection`)
- Desktop's `connection-request.ts` and `setup-form-dialog.tsx`

### Plan

The issue's plan, as approved by the plan gate. Choices the issue left open:
- An MCP row that carries a `connect_url` is also "Finish on the Mac".
- Open link opens only https URLs.
- The copy says "Opens in your browser" rather than naming Safari.
- Continue-first applies only to Guide and Queue.
- Setup fields also submit on Return.

The conversation-level tests went into the existing `BotAnsweringTests` rather than `BotConversationTests`, because that class already has the answering fixtures. No Xcode project edits were needed.

### Decisions applied

- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/770#issuecomment-5824374673):
  - Tests only; no live validation (D30).
  - Links open in the browser, not an in-app browser.
  - "Try again" on failed rows is deferred.
  - Design pick A.

## Design

Mock: https://d6r8yyjb6ux0.postplan.dev §2. **Pick: A**, stacked rows inside one card in the existing request-card style, with a static deadline and no spinner.

The card only appears during a live `manage_connections` operation, which D30 rules out. These renders come from a temporary hosted test (since removed) using fixture rows in light, dark and AX3. One difference from the current code: `GITHUB_HOST` now shows `github.com` as the field's value rather than as a grey placeholder.

![Connection card, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/433b6608-68d0-4e63-9b80-25a8c98872e3)
![Connection card, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33541419-b654-4e4b-9e17-b3c76abcff2d)
![Connection card, AX3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62d9396b-e6c6-4c6b-8458-00f5631cd7ff)

## How it was tested

All runs were on the final head, device iPhone 17 Pro Max (0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2).

- `git diff --check`: clean
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestParsingTests`: 22 passed, 0 failed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotAnsweringTests`: 53 passed, 0 failed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`: 35 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the existing `testDelegationCompletionCardKeepsTheFullReportInItsSheet`)
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests`: 23 passed, 0 failed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests`: 49 passed, 0 failed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests`: 28 passed, 0 failed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests`: 30 passed, 0 failed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: 7 passed, 0 failed
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 1872 extracted keys covered

The last commit fixed two review findings, and the first three classes were rerun after it. The other classes ran on the commit before; the last commit touches none of their code paths. The full suite was not run locally because there are no Xcode project, Config/ or entitlements changes. CI runs it.

## Manual test

Tests only, per D30. These live checks from the issue were **skipped** and are still open for the maintainer:

1. Whether a Hermex-attached session exposes `manage_connections`. Expected: the tool is in the session's toolset.
2. An MCP install answered from the phone, on a disposable Profile only. Ask the bot to install an MCP server that needs one env value, fill it on the card, and tap Connect. Expected: the row turns Connected and the bot continues. Then remove the Profile's `mcp_servers` entry and `.env` key, or delete the Profile.
3. What `session_platform()` resolves to for a Hermex-created session.

When a live operation is available, also check:

4. Skip one row, then Continue without. Expected: the card clears and the bot continues with `not_connected` for the open rows.
5. A connector row's Open link. Expected: the default browser opens the vendor sign-in, and the row turns Connected after sign-in, with no action on the phone.

title: feat(bots): play the Sessions chat haptics for send, answers, Stop and turn completion
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #756

Stacked on #784; merge after it.

## What changed

**Problem.** Sessions chat plays a haptic when a message is sent, an approval or question is answered, Stop is acknowledged, and a reply finishes. Bot Chat and group rooms play none of these, so sending to a bot or answering one feels dead.

**Fix.** The Bot models now publish one small Equatable value, `BotFeedback { event, id }`, and the views play the matching existing `ChatHaptics` cue. The id goes up with every event, so two identical events in a row both play.

- `BotConversation` sets the value only on success paths that have already passed its stale checks:
  - `sent`: any admitted prompt outcome except `.voiceStopped`.
  - `stopped`: when `session.interrupt` is acknowledged.
  - `approved(choice)`, `answered` or `declined`: only when `deliver` gets `.answered` back from the host.
  - `turnCompleted`: only when a snapshot moves an armed turn from busy to `.idle`. A busy snapshot arms it. Stop, an interrupted snapshot, a snapshot taken while a Stop is in flight (read before the idle branch clears it), a reconnect that lands on a different runtime, and `suspend()` all disarm it. Events and replay never emit it.
- `BotRoomReader` sets `sent`, `stopped` and `approved(choice)` in the accept blocks of `groups.send`, `groups.stop` and `groups.approve`. `groups.retry` sets nothing. Rooms have no turn completion (binding decision).
- `BotChatView` and `BotRoomView` each have one `.onChange(of: feedback)` that calls the new `ChatHaptics.botFeedback(_:isEnabled:)`. That helper maps `sent` to messageSent, `approved` to approvalSubmitted via `ApprovalChoice(rawValue:)`, `answered` to clarificationSubmitted, `declined` to the deny warning, `stopped` to streamCancelled and `turnCompleted` to assistantResponseCompleted. `BotRoomView` gets the `@AppStorage(AppHaptics.isEnabledKey)` toggle.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` manual checklist line now covers Bot Chat and rooms.

**Surfaces.** Every entry point (composer send, keyboard send, the steer/queue/interrupt card, Stop and the Stop inside the pending-request card, the room composer and the room approval card) goes through the model, so one seam covers them. Main app target only. The setting is global and the feedback lives on the per-connection model, so nothing crosses servers. No copy, layout or animation change.

### Decisions applied

- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/756#issuecomment-5824373179): defaults adopted as written. No turn-completion haptic in rooms, and none for a turn that finished while the app was in the background. The second one works because `suspend()` disarms, and `recover()` calls `suspend()`.

### Judgment calls for review

1. The room's explicit "Retry send" of an uncertain send (`send(retry: true)`) also plays `sent` once the host accepts it. The issue's "Retry emits nothing" is read as `groups.retry` only.
2. Completion is armed only by a busy snapshot. A turn so short that no snapshot ever sees it busy plays the send tap but no completion buzz.
3. An automatic socket reconnect to the same runtime while the chat stays on screen keeps the arm, so a turn that really finished across the reconnect plays once. A reconnect to a new runtime, `suspend()` and `recover()` disarm it.

## How it was tested

- New tests:
  - BotConversationTests: `testOnlyAnAdmittedPromptPublishesSent`, `testAcknowledgedStopPublishesStoppedAndItsTurnNeverCompletes`, `testApprovalPublishesItsChoiceOnlyWhenTheHostResolvedIt`, `testABusyTurnSettlingIdleCompletesOnceAndReplayAddsNothing`, `testATurnThatEndedWhileSuspendedOrWasIdleOnOpenPlaysNothing`, `testAReconnectKeepsTheArmOnlyWhenTheRuntimeSurvives`.
  - BotRoomTests: `testAcceptedSendStopAndApprovalPublishFeedbackAndRejectionsDoNot`, `testRetryAndAStaleSendPublishNoFeedback`.
  - ChatHapticsTests: `testBotFeedbackPlaysTheMatchingSessionsHaptic`.
- No Xcode project, Config or shared test infrastructure change, so no full local suite run; CI runs it.

### Manual test

The simulator plays no haptics, so this needs a physical phone.

1. Settings, Haptic Feedback on. Send to an idle bot: one light tap.
2. While the bot works, Steer or Queue: a light tap after the host admits it.
3. Approve an approval: light tap. Deny: a warning buzz. Answer a question: a selection tick.
4. Stop mid-turn: a medium tap, and no success buzz when the turn settles.
5. Let a turn finish on screen: one success buzz. Background the app mid-turn and return after it finishes: no buzz.
6. In a group room: send (light tap), approve (light tap), Stop (medium tap). No buzz when the room's turn ends.
7. Haptic Feedback off: repeat the steps above, and nothing plays.

Skipped live checks: none. The issue is client-only with no host contract, and no live server was touched.

title: fix(push): say notifications are off, not "could not reach host", when iOS permission is denied
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #768

## What changed

**Problem.** If you tapped "Turn on notifications…" while iOS notifications were off for Hermex, setup changed the host first: it set the relay env, installed the plugin and restarted the gateway, which interrupts running work. Only then did it fail, and it said "Could not reach this Hermes host". The registrar and relay errors (`PushRegistrarError`, `PushRelayError`) fell through to that default copy.

**Fix.** Setup now checks iOS permission before it makes any host call. A denial shows a grey "Notifications are off for Hermex" row with Open Settings. Every registrar and relay error now names what actually failed: the relay, iOS, or this build.

### Plan
- `HermexPushProvisioner` takes a `notifications: any ResponseCompletionNotificationScheduling` dependency. `enable()` checks permission after the connection guard and before `signIn()`, in its own `checkingPermission` phase. That phase blocks re-entry but shows no step rows, so the iOS prompt never claims a host step is running. `.authorized`, `.provisional` and `.ephemeral` continue. `.notDetermined` asks iOS once. A denial, whether earlier or at the prompt, makes zero host calls and sets `notificationsOff`. A `PushRegistrarError.permissionDenied` thrown late by the registrar (permission revoked mid-run) also sets `notificationsOff` instead of showing a red failure.
- `showsSteps` on the provisioner decides when the step list is visible: while a host step runs, after a failure, and after a run that changed the host before stopping (permission revoked mid-run), so finished host steps stay checked beside the notice. The list is hidden while iOS prompts. An unknown future authorization status counts as not allowed.
- `notificationsOff` is a single flag, not the issue's `Phase.notificationsOff`. The paired screen needs the same fact (D23), but there the phase is taken up by preference saves and disable. `recheckNotificationPermission()` clears the flag once permission is allowed, and on a paired server it also raises the flag. It never starts setup.
- `HermexPushSectionView` uses design pick A: a grey row with a `bell.slash` symbol, an "Open Settings" link to `UIApplication.openNotificationSettingsURLString`, and no step rows, because nothing ran. The unpaired state has a title and a body. The paired state (D23) has the body only and sits under "Turn off notifications…". `.task(id: scenePhase)` rechecks the permission when the section appears and on every return to the app.
- `signIn()` is wrapped in both `enable()` and `disable()` under a "Sign in to Hermes" title. Only a transport error at sign-in, before anything on the host has changed, says "Could not reach this Hermes host…".
- `message(for:)` now switches exhaustively over `PushRegistrarError` and `PushRelayError`:
  - relay rejections reuse the orphaned "The relay refused this phone (%lld)…" string
  - relay transport, `tokenUnavailable` and `unsupportedBuild` each get their own copy
  - `malformedPairing` and `malformedInstallKey` reuse the `unusablePairing` copy
  - `BotFailure.unsupported` and `.wrongIdentity` say the host lacks the password sign-in that push setup needs
  - the default is now "This step did not finish. Try again."
- 8 new strings in all 17 shipped languages, marked `needs_review`. "Open Settings", "This step did not finish. Try again." and the relay-refused string are reused.
- `docs/agents/bots.md` § Push provisioning: permission is checked before any host call, the notice and its foreground recheck are described, and relay and iOS failures are named as such.

### Decisions applied
- [D23](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/768#issuecomment-5824374530): an already-paired server also shows "Notifications are off" with Open Settings when iOS permission is denied.
- [D24](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/768#issuecomment-5824374530): the batched mock was used instead of skipping mocks.
- [Design pick A](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/768#issuecomment-5824374530) applies to both states.

### Deviations from the issue
- The issue's `Phase.notificationsOff` became a `notificationsOff` flag (reason above). Behaviour is the same: zero host calls, not `isWorking`, and the recheck never starts setup.
- The foreground recheck uses `.task(id: scenePhase)` instead of `.onChange`. One hook covers both appear and foreground, and it is cancelled with the view.
- The paired-state copy (D23) is the mock's draft: "Notifications are off for Hermex, so this server's notifications can't show on this iPhone."

## Design

Mock: https://edaa2t1bjfl4.postplan.dev §5. **Pick: A** (a grey row with `bell.slash`, title, body and an "Open Settings" link, with step rows hidden), used for both states.

There is no after screenshot. To reach the state you need a signed-in Bot connection with Hermex notifications denied. `simctl privacy` can't set notification permission. On a sim where permission has already been granted, getting there by tapping "Set up push" would mutate the live Hermes host. Please capture both states in the manual test below.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests`: **24 passed**, 0 failed, 0 skipped, rerun on the final head after review round 1. The suite covers:
  - denied permission, and notDetermined followed by a refusal: zero HTTP calls and the registrar untouched
  - a first run asks iOS before the first host call, and the phase during the prompt is `checkingPermission`, not a host step
  - allowing notifications in Settings clears the notice with no host calls
  - a paired server raises and clears the notice; an unpaired server doesn't raise it on recheck
  - sign-in to an unreachable host gives "Could not reach"; a host without password sign-in gives the new copy
  - a table-driven `message(for:)` test over every row of the issue's table
  - permission revoked mid-run gives `notificationsOff`, and the finished host steps stay visible
  - an unknown future authorization status is treated like a denial
  - disable against a refusing relay shows the relay copy
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: **7 passed**, 0 failed
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests`: **50 passed**, 0 failed
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py`: the catalog covers all 1859 extracted keys

No project, Config, entitlement or shared test-infra changes, so the full suite is left to CI.

## Manual test

Use the iPhone Air sim on `issue/768-push-notifications-off`, with a signed-in Hermes connection on a server that is not paired yet.
1. In iOS Settings → Notifications → Hermex, turn notifications off. On a fresh sim you can instead tap Don't Allow at the prompt in step 2.
2. In Hermex, go to Settings → Interaction → Notifications, tap **Turn on notifications…**, then **Set up push**. **Expect:**
   - no step list shows while the iOS prompt is up
   - the grey "Notifications are off for Hermex" row appears, with no step rows and no red failure
   - if server logs are available, no host call was made (no env write, install or restart)
3. Tap the row. **Expect:** Hermex's notification page in iOS Settings opens. Allow notifications and return. **Expect:** the row clears without setup running.
4. On a paired server, deny notifications in iOS Settings and return to Hermex. **Expect:** the caption row appears under "Turn off notifications…". Allow again and return. **Expect:** it clears.
5. Capture steps 2 and 4 in light, dark and an accessibility text size, and check VoiceOver reads the row as one element that opens Settings.

Skipped live checks: none needed. The change is client-only and adds no host contract.

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no Codable changes)

title: feat(bots): show Hermes Desktop's named sections in the Bots inbox
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #742

## What changed

Hermes Desktop lets users file bots into named sections. Since 0.21.4, our pin, it writes `sectionName` next to `sectionId` in each bot's `ui_meta["hermes-bots"]`. The Bots inbox ignored both fields and showed one flat timeline.

The inbox now groups bots under the section names Desktop already sends in `profiles.list`, so there is no new RPC. Named sections sort A–Z. The unfiled bots and all group rooms come last under "Other chats". The user can reorder sections on the phone, and that order is saved per server and Bot connection.

## Plan (express, decisions D1/D2 + section reorder + Design pick A)

- **`BotProfile`** reads `sectionId` and `sectionName`, trimmed. An empty value counts as missing. A bot is unfiled when it has an id but no name, or when its id is null because the section was deleted.
- **`BotInbox.sections`** replaces the flat `chats`:
  - Named sections come first, then one final unfiled block with the unfiled bots and every group room.
  - Each block is newest first, using the existing `byActivity`.
  - Pinned bots appear only in the tiles.
  - When hidden bots are revealed, they show dimmed inside their own section.
  - Empty sections are left out.
- **`BotInbox.sectionNames`** names each section by what most of its members carry. On a tie, the first member in `profiles.list` order wins.
- **Order:** sections the user placed come first, in their placed order. The rest follow A–Z (`localizedStandardCompare`, ties by id). Ids that no longer exist are ignored.
- **`BotSectionOrderStore`** saves the placed order in `UserDefaults`, keyed by configured server and Bot connection UUID. It is never sent to Desktop, and Desktop's order is never read. Removing the Bot connection deletes it.
- **`BotsInboxView`** reads `inbox.sections` once per body:
  - Each named section gets a `Section` with a `Text(verbatim:)` header on one line, truncated at the tail, with the `.isHeader` trait.
  - The unfiled block is headed "Other chats" only when a named section exists. With no sections, the list has no headers and looks as it did before.
- **Reorder:** a "Reorder Sections…" item in the + menu appears when there are 2+ named sections the list can head. It opens a native `List` in edit mode with drag handles, "Reset to A–Z" (the way back) and Done.
  - The unfiled block is always last and does not appear in the sheet.
  - A section whose bots are all pinned lives only in the tiles, so the sheet leaves it out (`reorderableSectionNames`). A hidden-only section stays in the sheet, because Show hidden draws it.
  - A drag keeps the placed slot of any section the sheet left out (`placeReorderableSections`).
- **Copy:** "Other chats", "Reorder Sections…", "Reorder Sections" and "Reset to A–Z" are in all 17 non-English catalog languages.
- **Docs:**
  - The `BotProfile` comment is updated.
  - `docs/agents/bots.md` has the roster-organization section, the stale "server order" claim fixed, `sectionName` next to `sectionId` for duplicates, and the rooms-sorting paragraph.
  - `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` has a new per-server row.

**Contract:** checked against pinned hermes-agent `d337b736` (`HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`). `BotMeta.sectionId` and `sectionName` are `null|string` (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/types.ts:59-70`), and Desktop trims `sectionName` (`user-sections.ts:149`). Pin and hide writes already send the whole `hermes-bots` object back, so both section fields survive them.

**Risk:** the section order lives only on the phone, so it won't match a Desktop where the user moved sections. That is the recorded decision.

**Note:** #773 (#738, bots.md host-fact corrections) also edits `docs/agents/bots.md` near the roster-organization and duplicate paragraphs. Whichever PR merges second will have a small doc conflict.

## Decisions applied

All in [the decision comment on #742](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/742#issuecomment-5824371289):
- D1: build now.
- D2: sections sort A–Z by name. Unfiled chats and rooms come last under "Other chats". Pinned bots appear only in the tiles.
- Section reorder: the order is local to the phone and keyed by server and connection. Placed sections come first and the rest follow A–Z. The menu item shows only with 2+ named sections. "Reset to A–Z" is the way back, and the unfiled block always stays last.
- Design pick A.

## Design

Mock: https://edaa2t1bjfl4.postplan.dev §2. Pick **A**:
- Unfiled chats come last.
- "Other chats" is shown only when a named section exists.
- Revealed hidden bots show dimmed in their own section.

The reorder sheet is native list editing, so it had no mock.

## How it was tested

`git diff --check` is clean. Each class ran on its own on iPhone 17 Pro Max (`0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2`) with `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/<Class>`:
- `BotInboxTests`: 25 passed, 0 failed (after the review fixes, on 1733409)
- `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 7 passed, 0 failed
- `BotLifecycleTests`: 19 passed, 0 failed
- `BotRoomTests`: 30 passed, 0 failed
- `BotChatPresentationTests`: 33 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the skip already existed and is unrelated)

New `BotInboxTests` cases:
- A–Z sections with activity order inside each, and unfiled bots last. This also covers trimming, an id with no name, a deleted section, rooms staying unfiled, and pinned bots staying only in the tiles.
- The majority name and its tie-break.
- Revealed hidden bots staying in their section, and a section of only hidden bots drawing nothing.
- Placed order surviving a new inbox, a new section following A–Z, isolation per connection and per server, and Reset.
- The reorder sheet offering only sections the list can head.
- A drag keeping the placed slot of a section the sheet left out.
- The existing flat-list test now asserts one headerless block when there are no sections.
- The hide round-trip test now also carries `sectionName`.

The other four classes above ran on aaff945. The review fixes changed only `BotInbox` and the reorder sheet, and `BotInboxTests` is the class that covers them.

No after screenshot. A signed Debug build of this branch launched on the lane simulator. Reaching Bots would have needed UI automation through shared XcodeBuildMCP session defaults, and the test host is not known to have sectioned bots. The manual steps below cover the visual check.

## Manual test

Needs manual validation (label `needs-manual-validation`). Use a Desktop 0.21.4+ host and the test bot `inbox-triage`.

1. On Desktop, create two sections, for example "Work" and "Alpha". File `inbox-triage` in one and a second bot in the other. **Expected:** after a pull to refresh, the Bots inbox shows the pinned tiles first, then an "Alpha" header, then "Work", then "Other chats" with the unfiled bots and every group room. Rows in each block are newest first.
2. On Desktop, hide a filed bot, then tap **Show hidden** in Hermex. **Expected:** the hidden bot shows dimmed inside its own section, not under "Other chats".
3. Tap + → **Reorder Sections…** (shown only with 2+ named sections that have an unpinned or hidden bot), drag "Work" above "Alpha" and tap Done. **Expected:** the inbox shows Work before Alpha, and the order survives leaving and reopening Bots and relaunching the app.
4. Open Reorder Sections again and tap **Reset to A–Z**. **Expected:** Alpha is back before Work, and Reset is disabled.
5. Rename a section on Desktop and pull to refresh. **Expected:** the new name shows in the same position.
6. Switch to a second configured server with its own Bot connection. **Expected:** it has its own order, and the first server's placement doesn't carry over.
7. Unfile every bot on Desktop. **Expected:** the inbox goes back to one flat list with no headers.
8. VoiceOver reads section headers as headers. At the largest Dynamic Type size, long section names truncate on one line. Check both light and dark mode.

Skipped live checks:
- The read-only `profiles.list` on the test host, looking for a `ui_meta["hermes-bots"].sectionName`, did not run.
- The maintainer step from the issue (file `inbox-triage` into a section from Desktop 0.21.4+, confirm it in Hermex, then unfile it) was not done. Steps 1 and 7 above cover it.

"Reorder Sections…" is inside the existing + menu, which is disabled while the link is not live, so reordering isn't available offline.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

title: fix(push): add the Time Sensitive entitlement so approval banners break through Focus
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #771 (part of #737)

## What changed

**Problem.** The push relay sends approval, clarify, and turn-error banners with `interruption-level: time-sensitive`. iOS only honors that level for apps that carry the `com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive` entitlement, and the Hermex app target doesn't. So a Focus most likely holds back the banner that tells the user their agent is blocked, and Hermex never shows a **Time Sensitive Notifications** switch in iOS Settings.

**Fix.**
- Add `com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive = true` to `HermesMobile/Resources/HermesMobile.entitlements` only. The Notification Service Extension doesn't need it: it does `mutableCopy()` and `PushPreview.rewrite` sets only title, subtitle, body, and userInfo, so `interruptionLevel` passes through. The share extension, widget, and tests are unchanged.
- `docs/agents/push.md` > Components > App: one line saying the app carries the entitlement so non-reply banners can break through a Focus when the user allows it, and that the extension leaves the level alone.
- No Swift changes, no new XCTest (one plist key, per the issue), and no `Config/`, workflow, or project edits.

### Release-sensitive: entitlement change

On the next Automatic-signing device or TestFlight build (the release workflow and `scripts/branch-testflight` both pass `-allowProvisioningUpdates`), Xcode adds the **Time Sensitive Notifications** capability to two App IDs:

- `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile` (production)
- `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.branch` (Branch TestFlight)

The capability needs no Apple approval, unlike Critical Alerts. If signing refuses the entitlement, this PR waits for the maintainer.

### Plan

As written in #771: one key in the app entitlements, a signed simulator Debug build to confirm the key lands in the processed entitlements, one line in `push.md`, and maintainer-owned device and portal checks.

### Decisions applied

None. The issue body stands; there are no decision comments on #771.

Out of scope, per the issue: whether `turn_error` should be time-sensitive at all (relay `policy.ts:18`) is a hermex-push question.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `plutil -lint HermesMobile/Resources/HermesMobile.entitlements`: OK.
- Signed simulator Debug build on iPhone Air (`xcodebuild -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -configuration Debug -destination id=<iPhone Air> build`): succeeded.
- Processed entitlements: `HermesMobile.app-Simulated.xcent` contains `com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive => true` next to `aps-environment = development`, the app group, and both keychain groups. The key is also embedded in the app binary's `__TEXT,__entitlements` section. No other target's `.xcent` has it (NSE, widget, and share extension: 0 matches).
- Full local suite, because entitlements changed: `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air>`: **3057 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped**.

## Manual test

This issue is `needs-manual-validation`, and every check needs a physical device or the Apple Developer portal, so all of them are maintainer-owned and were skipped here.

1. Make a device Debug build or a Branch TestFlight build through Automatic signing. **Expected:** signing succeeds, and the Apple Developer portal shows **Time Sensitive Notifications** on both `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile` and `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.branch`.
2. On the phone, open iOS Settings > Notifications > Hermex. **Expected:** a **Time Sensitive Notifications** switch is there. Record its default state.
3. Pair push on a Hermes server. Turn on a Focus that doesn't allow Hermex but does allow Time Sensitive notifications. Trigger one approval (or clarify) on the disposable test bot. **Expected:** the banner arrives right away with the "Time Sensitive" label.
4. In the same Focus, trigger one plain reply. **Expected:** the reply banner is held by the Focus.
5. Turn off either Hermex's Time Sensitive switch or the Focus's Time Sensitive allowance, then trigger another approval. **Expected:** it is held like any other banner (the user's setting working, not a bug).
6. Check the approval banner from step 3. **Expected:** the preview is decrypted by the NSE (real title and body), and tapping it opens the bot.

The claim that iOS downgrades the level to `active` without the entitlement comes from Apple's documentation and was not observed; steps 3 and 4 confirm the fixed behavior.

title: feat(bots): react to Bot Chat messages with Tapbacks that sync with Desktop
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #761

Stacked on #787; merge after it.

## What changed

**Problem.** Hermes Desktop lets you add a Tapback to any message (❤️ 👍 👎 😂 ‼️ ❓, one per author), and the host saves it. Hermex dropped that data. A reaction set on Desktop never appeared in Bot Chat, and you couldn't add or remove one from the phone.

**Fix.** Bot Chat now shows reactions and can write them, following design B (D15/D26):

- **Projection.** `session.resume` rows now pass the host's `row_id` into a new optional `ChatMessage.rowID`. Only `BotTranscriptProjection` sets it. Reactions are read from `display_metadata.reactions` as `BotReaction`, and the reader is tolerant:
  - entries that aren't objects are dropped
  - entries with an empty emoji or an unknown author are dropped
  - only one entry per author counts
- **Wire.** `message.react` is added to the `BotClient` allowlist with `validateReactCall`. It accepts exactly these params:
  - `session_id`
  - `row_id`, an integer
  - `emoji`, a non-empty string or null

  It refuses `author` and `newest_role`.
- **Model.** `BotConversation.react(to:emoji:)` sends what you meant to do. The host toggles an emoji it already has, so picking your current emoji sends null instead of sending the same emoji again.
  - It is not optimistic: the row changes only when the host's reply arrives with the full list.
  - Only one write per row runs at a time (`reactingRowIDs`).
  - The owner and runtime are checked again at dispatch, so a reply that arrives after you switch Bot or server is dropped.
  - If the host rejects the write, the row stays as it was and the app shows "Could not update the reaction."
  - A lost reply is never resent. The reconnect snapshot, or a full refresh, decides what the row shows.
  - When the agent sends a live `message.reaction` event, the app updates only the agent's entry on that row. The event is written on another host thread and can arrive after a newer `message.react` reply, so it never replaces your reaction.
  - A full snapshot requested before a reaction patch landed keeps the patched row's list (`reactionPatches`, stamped with `reactionRevision`). `session.resume` runs on the host's worker pool and can read history before a `message.react` commits. Without this, a stale list could hide your 👍, and tapping 👍 again would send "👍", which the host would toggle off.
- **UI.** `ChatMessageMetaRow` gains an optional accessory slot. Sessions passes nothing into it and looks the same as before.
  - `BotReplyFooter` (the #746 row) draws `[… → React][chips][time]` on settled replies and `[chips][time]` on prompts.
  - The "…" menu holds a React section: a palette Picker with the six quick reactions.
  - A prompt's long-press menu gets the same inline Tapback row above Copy (`UIMenu` `.displayInline`, `.small`, your emoji checked). Once you have a reaction it also shows Remove Reaction.
  - Your chip is tinted with the accent color, and tapping it removes your reaction. The Bot's chip can't be tapped. It shows the Bot's still face, and VoiceOver reads it as "<emoji>, reacted by <Bot>".
  - Enabled state (connected, and no write in flight for that row) is read only inside the footer's controls. A tap or a reconnect redraws the footers, not every transcript row.
  - The long-press Tapbacks don't read connection state. If you pick one while the chat can't react, the model drops it.
  - Live rows, rooms, delegation cards and the offline cache get no reactions.
- **Strings.** The String Catalog has 7 new keys in all 17 shipped languages.
- **Docs.** In `docs/agents/bots.md`, I replaced the stale line saying `message.react` was deliberately not wired. The doc now describes reactions and the stale-snapshot guard. Reactions only show up on each side (display-only) unless the host turns on `display.message_reactions`, and Hermex never writes that setting.

**Review fixes.** The footer's "…" React menu now closes after one pick, like the prompt's long-press Tapback row ([Decision on #761](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/761#issuecomment-5837335930)): `.menuActionDismissBehavior(.enabled)` on the palette `Picker`, which still marks your current emoji. Checked in the app on iPhone 18 Pro (iOS 27): without it the menu stays open after 👍, with it the menu closes and the 👍 chip shows. No unit test can open a SwiftUI `Menu`, so none pins this.

#748 Listen is deferred, so the "…" menu holds only React.

### Decisions applied
- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/761#issuecomment-5824373698) D15: React lives in the shared reply footer's "…" overflow menu, and chips sit in the footer. Your chip removes your reaction; the Bot's chip is static. Prompts get the inline Tapback row in their long-press menu, plus Remove Reaction.
- D26: the picker offers only Desktop's six quick reactions.
- Live checks beyond read-only calls are not authorized for the implementer (epic #737 N2). They are listed under Manual test below.

### Contract
Checked against the pinned hermes-agent `d337b736` (0.21.4), which contains `message.react` (7d92056c49):
- `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` `message.react`
- `contracts/billing_delegation_pets.py` `MessageReactParams`/`Result`
- `contracts/common.py` `MessageReaction`
- `contracts/events.py` `message.reaction`
- `session_history.py:238` `row_id`
- `hermes_state_messages.py` `set_message_reaction`, which toggles an emoji the author already has
- `tui_gateway/server.py:161-178`: `session.resume` is a long handler that runs on the worker pool

Desktop's six quick reactions come from `store/reactions.ts`.

## Design

Mock: https://yt6luspsvqd9.postplan.dev §2. Pick **B**.

The signed Debug build of this branch runs on iPhone 17e. I haven't captured an after screenshot. Reaching Bot Chat takes UI automation through shared session defaults, and a deep link needs the connection UUID from the keychain. Screenshots come from the manual pass below.

**Risk:** I haven't seen the footer's "…" palette `Picker` inside `Section("React")` render. If it doesn't draw as one inline emoji row with your emoji highlighted, the fallback is a `ControlGroup` with the `.compactMenu` style.

## How it was tested

Every run used `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3` (iPhone 17e) with one `--only` class per run.

Final tree, after the review fixes:
- `git diff --check`: clean
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests`: 65 passed, 9 new. The new cases cover:
  - react, replace and remove, with the exact wire params and nothing painted before the reply
  - a second tap while a write is in flight
  - a rejected write
  - a lost reply that is never resent
  - a reply for a replaced connection, which is dropped
  - the live `message.reaction` patch
  - a late agent event that doesn't replace your newer reaction
  - live and offline rows refusing to react
  - **a stale full snapshot that doesn't erase a reaction reply**, so a second 👍 sends null. This case fails on the old code.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotMessageActionsTests`: 9 passed, 2 new
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`: 37 passed, 1 skipped (it was already skipped before this change)
- `--only HermesMobileTests/ChatMessageActionMenuTests`: 8 passed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests`: 5 passed. This test class isn't touched by this PR. CI's first attempt timed out one render expectation in it, and the rerun was green.

Earlier, before the review fixes, which don't touch these classes:
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotActivityTests`: 23 passed, 3 new
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests`: 20 passed, 1 new
- `--only HermesMobileTests/ChatMessageMetaTests`: 10 passed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: 7 passed
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests`: 33 passed
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py`: covers all 1857 extracted keys
- `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`: no new warnings

### Manual test
Run these on iPhone 17e (branch `issue/761-bot-reactions`) or a device, in a Bot Chat on the test bot. Use a disposable session wherever a step writes.

1. **Read-only `session.resume`** on the test bot (skipped here). Expected: rows carry `row_id`, and a reacted row carries `display_metadata.reactions`.
2. **Disposable-session mutation** (not authorized in this run, N2). Add 👍 on an assistant row, run resume again, react with null, then delete the session. Expected: the list shows 👍 and then empty.
3. On a settled reply, tap "…" and then 👍. Expected: the menu shows one inline row of six emoji with the "React" title only once. A 👍 chip appears only after the host answers.
4. Long-press a prompt. Expected: the Tapback row sits above Copy. Pick ❤️ and a ❤️ chip appears. Long-press again: ❤️ is checked and Remove Reaction is listed.
5. Pick a different emoji on a row that already has yours. Expected: the new chip replaces yours, and there is never more than one chip of yours.
6. Remove your reaction by tapping your chip, and on a prompt by using Remove Reaction. Expected: the chip disappears after the host answers.
7. A known limit (deferred): the host only toggles, so if Desktop set the same emoji since the phone's last snapshot, a tap removes it. The row then shows the host's truth.
8. With Desktop open on the same session, react on the phone and check that Desktop shows it after its resume. React on Desktop and check that the phone shows it after its next snapshot.
9. React to an earlier reply while a turn is running and finishing. Expected: the chip stays after the turn completes, and tapping the same emoji again removes it.
10. VoiceOver. Expected: your chip reads "👍, reacted by you" with the hint "Removes your reaction.", and the Bot's chip reads "‼️, reacted by <Bot>".
11. Try Dynamic Type at AX sizes, light and dark mode, and turn Airplane mode on during step 3. Expected: the footer wraps cleanly, and the "…" menu and chips are disabled while the chat reconnects.

title: feat(bots): move a bot into a Desktop section from the phone
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #749

Stacked on #789; merge after it.

## What changed

**Problem.** After #742 the Bots inbox shows Hermes Desktop's named sections, but the phone can't file a bot into one. Desktop's bot row has "Move to section", "New section…" and "Remove from section".

**Fix.** Filing is one field on the bot's Profile (`ui_meta["hermes-bots"]`), and Hermex already writes that object for Pin and Hide. This PR builds on that write.

- `BotInbox.configure` now takes `[String: BotJSON]` changes, so one write can set several fields. Pin and Hide pass one entry. The notice, conflict handling and re-read work as before: the whole received `hermes-bots` object goes back under `ui_meta_expected_revisions["hermes-bots"]`, set to the row's revision (0 when absent).
- `moveToSection(_:_:)` writes `sectionId` and `sectionName` together. It makes no call if the bot is already in that section under that name.
- `moveToNewSection(_:name:)` trims the name, makes no call for a blank one, and joins an existing section when the name matches it exactly. Otherwise it creates a new section with Desktop's id format, `sec-<epoch ms base36>-<5 base36>` (`BotInbox.newSectionID`).
- `removeFromSection(_:)` writes explicit `null` for both fields. Dropping the keys would not work, because Desktop merges host meta over its local copy and would keep the old section.
- The destinations come from #742's existing `sectionNames`, which is built from every roster profile. So sections whose only members are pinned, or hidden and not revealed, are still offered, in the phone's own section order. A section created here has no stored position, so it falls into the A–Z tail of that order.
- UI: a "Move to Section" submenu in `organizeMenu`, which both the row context menu and the pinned tile menu use. It lists the sections (the bot's current one disabled), then "New Section…", which opens a system alert with a TextField, the same pattern as Rename group. "Remove from Section" appears only while the bot is filed. The whole menu is disabled when `mayEdit` is false. Section names render verbatim. Switching connections clears the alert.
- Six new catalog keys with all 17 non-English locales: Move to Section, New Section…, New Section, Remove from Section, Section name, and Move “%@” into a new section. "Move" and "Cancel" reuse existing keys.
- `docs/agents/bots.md`: removed "The phone never files bots", added a paragraph on section writes (id format, exact-name join, explicit nulls, Desktop adopting the new section), and extended the pin/hide write sentence to cover section writes.
- No `BotClient` allowlist change. It already accepts any `hermes-bots` object under `profiles.configure`.

**Contract check.** Checked against the pinned hermes-agent d337b736:
- `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py` `_configure_ui_meta`: the top-level key-wise merge and the per-key CAS that rejects the whole write with `ui_meta_conflicts`.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/user-sections.ts`: `newSectionId`, `moveBotsToSection` writing `{sectionId, sectionName}` and null on remove, and `adoptBotSectionsFromMeta` appending unknown ids to Desktop's list.

### Decisions applied

- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/749#issuecomment-5824372256): build now (D1, yes). No mock; a native submenu plus a system alert.

### Plan

1. Generalize `BotInbox.configure` to a changes map; keep Pin and Hide on it.
2. Add `moveToSection`, `moveToNewSection` and `removeFromSection` with Desktop's id format and explicit nulls.
3. Add the submenu and the New Section alert to the shared organize menu.
4. Add catalog keys in every shipped language; update `docs/agents/bots.md`.
5. Focused tests in `BotInboxTests`.

### Notes for reviewers

- `sectionNames` is computed inside each row's menu builder. That is O(roster) per row that builds a menu, which is negligible for bot rosters (tens of bots).
- The alert captures the profile when the menu opens. A roster change in between leads to the CAS conflict notice, not an overwrite.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests`: 28 passed, 0 failed (re-run on the final head). Three new tests:
  - `testNewSectionWritesADesktopIDAndTheTrimmedNameUnderTheRowRevision`: id pattern, trimmed name, other Desktop fields unchanged, expected revision, row moves only after apply and re-read, base36 millisecond prefix.
  - `testFilingOffersEverySectionAndJoinsAnExistingOneByIDOrTypedName`: pinned-only and unrevealed hidden-only sections are offered, an existing section's id is reused, an exact name joins, a case-different name does not, and the bot's own section and a blank name make no call.
  - `testRemoveFromSectionWritesExplicitNullsAndAConflictClaimsNoSuccess`: `.null` values are present and encode as JSON null, and a conflict shows the notice and leaves the bot filed.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotProfileEditorTests`: 17 passed, 0 failed.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py --derived-data …`: covers all 1860 extracted keys.

### Manual test

Needs a live Bot connection to a Hermes host with Desktop open on the same profile set.

1. Long-press an unfiled bot row → Move to Section → New Section…, type "Triage", tap Move. Expected: the bot moves under a new "Triage" heading only after the host confirms; Desktop shows the same section after its next roster load.
2. On another bot, Move to Section → pick "Triage". Expected: it joins the same section; "Triage" is disabled in the submenu for a bot already in it.
3. New Section… and type exactly "Triage". Expected: joins the existing section (no duplicate heading on phone or Desktop). Type "triage": a new, separate section.
4. With the alert open, clear the field. Expected: Move is disabled.
5. Remove from Section on a filed bot. Expected: the bot returns to the unfiled list; Desktop also shows it unfiled (not kept in its old section).
6. Repeat 1 and 5 from a pinned tile's menu and on a revealed hidden bot. Expected: same results.
7. Open the New Section alert, then switch servers or Bot connections. Expected: the alert closes and nothing is written.
8. Edit the same bot on Desktop, then move it on the phone without refreshing. Expected: the conflict notice appears and the bot stays where the host has it.

Skipped live checks:
- Read-only `profiles.list` on the test host to confirm bots filed on Desktop carry `sectionId` and `sectionName`. Not run: it needs a ws-ticket RPC session. #742 relies on the same fields.
- The mutating check (file `inbox-triage` into a new section from the phone, confirm Desktop adopts it, then remove it). Not run: live mutation needs maintainer approval and none is recorded. Steps 1 and 5 above cover it.

No screenshots: the change is a native submenu plus a system alert, per the issue's no-mock call, and capturing it needs a live Bot connection.
