title: feat(chat): show diff and patch code blocks with added and removed lines
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #762

## What changed

**Problem.** When an agent sends a ```diff or ```patch fence, Hermex shows it as plain monochrome code. Readers have to scan the +/- column by eye, and nothing shows how big the change is. This affects every MarkdownRenderer host (Sessions, Bot Chat, rooms, and the rest).

**Fix.** A settled diff or patch fence now tints added, removed and hunk rows across the full width, shows `+N −M` next to the language label, and collapses past 80 lines behind a "Show all" row. Streaming tails stay plain until they settle.

### Plan

- New `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownDiffCodeBlock.swift` (main app target only):
  - `MarkdownDiffFormatter.parse` makes one linear pass on the main actor and gives each line a kind: added, removed, context, hunk, fileHeader, or note.
  - An `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` header opens a hunk, and its counts bound it (a missing count means 1). Inside a counted hunk, a removed `--- x` or `-- comment` line counts as a change. Once the counts run out, the next file's `---`/`+++` lines are headers, even without a `diff --git` line.
  - A bare `@@`, a diff with no `@@` at all, or lines left over after the counts run out fall back to prefix rules. Under those rules, `--- `/`+++ ` and git metadata lines are file headers. `\ No newline` counts toward neither side.
- `MarkdownDiffFormatter.document(for:language:isStreaming:)` styles a fence only when all of these hold: it has settled; its language is diff or patch; it is not empty; it is within the highlighter's size limits (it reuses `MarkdownHighlightPolicy.decision`, so a line over 4,000 characters or a block over 2,000 lines stays plain).
- `DiffCodeBlockText`:
  - Rows are tinted across the full width with the `ReviewDiffTheme` colors, which are dynamic for light and dark: green or red at 0.14, and blue at 0.10 for hunks.
  - Text stays primary and the +/- prefix stays visible. Hunk, header and note rows use secondary text.
  - It uses the same 500-character segments and `responseSelectableText` leaves as the plain block, and works with wrapping on and off. In scroll mode each row is at least as wide as the viewport, so the tint reaches the right edge. `DiffCodeBlockScrollBody` owns that viewport width, so the post-layout width write re-renders only the scroll body and never re-parses the diff.
  - VoiceOver reads each row as "added, <text>" or "removed, <text>", using the existing keys.
- `ChatCodeBlock`:
  - `DiffCountsLabel` (+N −M, reused from Git) sits next to the language label.
  - Past 80 lines, a full-width "Show all %lld lines" / "Show first %lld lines" row appears at the bottom of the block, with the hint "Copy includes every line." It does not animate. Copy still copies the full source.
  - The highlight task returns right away for diff and patch, so Highlightr is never called for them and the `highRisk` fallback is no longer logged. diff and patch stay in `highRiskLanguages`.
- `MarkdownPlainCodeFormatter` now exposes `rawLines(in:)` and `segments(in:)` so the diff parser can reuse them. Plain code blocks behave exactly as before.
- 3 new strings in `Localizable.xcstrings` in all 18 languages. The two plural keys copy each locale's plural categories from the existing `%lld lines` entry.
- Updated the `docs/agents/bots.md` streaming note: diff and patch fences are styled once their chunk is sealed or the reply settles.

### Decisions applied

- [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-24)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/762#issuecomment-5824373988): collapse settled diff blocks to the first 80 lines, with "Show all %lld lines" / "Show first 80 lines" (D16).
- [Default adopted](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/762#issuecomment-5824373988): no "open in review sheet".
- [Design pick A on all three questions](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/762#issuecomment-5824373988): `+N −M` next to the language label; full-row tint with the text kept primary and the +/- prefix visible; a full-width "Show all" row at the bottom of the block.

### Review fixes

- Hunk counts are compared, never summed, so an `Int.max` count can't trap.
- Show all calls the transcript's `chatDisclosureToggled()` first, so the reader's position holds while the block resizes.
- Styled diff documents are cached by fence source (`NSCache`, 64 entries), so wrap, Show all and appearance passes don't re-parse. Oversized plain fences are not cached.

### Known limits

- Expanding a long diff inside a sealed stable chunk while the reply is still streaming is undone when the reply settles: the renderer swaps from the streaming layout to the settled one, which rebuilds the block and resets the "Show all" state to collapsed. The issue and decision are about settled blocks, so this PR does not add machinery to carry the flag across that swap.
- After a bare `@@`, a lone `--- x` removal (not followed by `+++`) is shown as a muted header and not counted, as the issue's prefix rules say.
- A context line with no leading space that starts with `index ` or `diff `, outside a counted hunk, is shown muted as a header. The counts are not affected.

## Design

Mock: https://d6r8yyjb6ux0.postplan.dev §1. Pick: **A** on all three questions.

After screenshots (iPhone Air simulator, Debug build of this branch, rendered through the real `MarkdownRenderer` via the debug Streaming Lab with a local diff fixture that is not committed): scroll mode in light and dark, wrap on, and a 136-line diff collapsed behind "Show all 136 lines".

## How it was tested

All from the lane worktree on iPhone Air (`D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A`):

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownDiffFormatterTests`: 15 passed, 0 failed on the final head (14 before review added the overflow test).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownMathRendererTests`: 48 passed, 0 failed (rerun after review fixes: 48 passed).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests`: 5 passed, 0 failed (rerun after the review fix: 5 passed).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite (a new Swift file joins the project), `scripts/test-sim <udid>`: 3072 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped.
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py --derived-data <DerivedData>/Build`: all 1853 extracted keys covered; each new plural value has exactly one `%lld`.

New `MarkdownDiffFormatterTests` (15 tests) covers a single-file diff; `Int.max` hunk counts that must not overflow; the mock's two-file `diff --git` patch (+7 −4, including a removed `--- TODO` inside a counted hunk and a trimmed blank context line); a multi-file `---`/`+++` patch with no `diff --git` line; counted `--- x`/`+++ y` changes, an omitted count, a bare `@@`, and `\ No newline`; a `-- sql` removal, a diff with no `@@`, CRLF input, and an empty block; which fences get styled (streaming, other languages, too many lines, too-long lines); the 80-line cap and VoiceOver labels. `MarkdownMathRendererTests` now also checks that the policy still returns `.plain(.highRiskLanguage)` for diff and patch.

No host contract is involved, so no live server calls were needed.

### Manual test

On a signed Debug build of this branch, against your server:

1. In Sessions, ask the agent for a short ```diff reply touching two files. Expected: once the reply settles, added rows are green, removed rows red, hunk headers blue, file headers muted; the header reads `Diff +N −M` with the right counts.
2. Toggle the wrap button on that block. Expected: with wrap off, the block scrolls sideways and short rows are tinted to the right edge; with wrap on, lines reflow and tints still span the row.
3. Switch between light and dark. Expected: tints stay readable in both; text stays primary.
4. Ask for a ```diff of about 150 lines and watch it stream in Sessions. Expected: plain while streaming, then styled and collapsed to 80 lines with "Show all 150 lines" at the bottom; tapping it shows every line and switches to "Show first 80 lines", with no animation. Copy copies all 150 lines.
5. Repeat step 4 in Bot Chat. Expected: same behavior.
6. Send a reply with more than 6,000 characters of prose followed by a 150-line ```diff. Expected: the diff styles once its chunk seals, before the reply finishes. Known limit: if you tap "Show all" before the reply settles, the block collapses back to 80 lines when it settles.
7. With VoiceOver on a device, swipe through the diff rows. Expected: "added, <text>" / "removed, <text>"; the Show all row reads its label plus "Copy includes every line."
8. At an accessibility Dynamic Type size, check the header. Expected: the `+N −M` counts sit next to the language label without clipping the wrap and copy buttons.

Not done by the agent: steps 1 to 8 against a live server or device (no live-server mutation was authorized; the simulator screenshots above use a local fixture).

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename) (n/a: no Codable changes)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server) (n/a: no wire changes)

title: feat(bots): user-editable quick-reply chips above the Bot Chat composer
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #764 (epic #737)

## What changed

**Problem.** When you drive a bot from a phone, you type the same short follow-ups again and again ("continue", "run the tests"). Bot Chat has no one-tap way to reuse them.

**Fix.** A row of your own quick-reply chips now sits above the Bot Chat composer. Tapping a chip fills the empty draft and never sends. You manage the list in Settings → Interaction → Quick Replies.

### Plan

- `BotQuickReply {id, text}` and `BotQuickReplyStore`: one JSON string under one `@AppStorage` key (`botQuickReplies`). The list is global and empty by default. Decoding is tolerant: an empty or unreadable value becomes `[]`. Entries with a blank or wrong-typed id or text are dropped, and so are repeated ids. Each id is a UUID minted once, so `ForEach` identity stays stable.
- `BotQuickReplyPolicy.showsRow(replies:draft:hasQuotes:hasAttachments:maySend:hasPendingRequest:hasPill:)` is a pure function.
- `BotQuickReplyRow` is a horizontal `ScrollView` of material capsule chips. Each chip is one line and truncates, with a max width that scales with Dynamic Type. VoiceOver reads the reply text with the hint "Fills the draft without sending". The row sits in the status pill's slot (`if let pill … else if showsQuickReplies`), so the pill and the chips never stack. It fades with `ChatMotion.quickState`, which is nil under Reduce Motion. The composer decodes the stored list only when storage changes, not on every keystroke.
- `BotConversation.applyQuickReply` fills the draft only when it is empty. It goes through `editDraft`, so the `mayEditDraft` guard still applies. It never sends. Send, `/skill` expansion and the busy-choice card all still go through the existing `send()` path. Focus doesn't move, so no keyboard comes up.
- Settings → Interaction gets a "Quick Replies" row with a count and a footnote. The row shows only when Bot Mode is on. It opens `BotQuickRepliesEditorView`, a native inset List with:
  - add or edit in a sheet whose Save trims the text and stays off while the text is blank
  - swipe to delete, and an Edit button for delete and reorder
  - an empty state

**Contract:** none. The feature is client-only. The pinned hermes-agent (`d337b736`) has no prompts router in `hermes_cli/web_routers/`, so this adds no host call and doesn't change the BotClient allowlist.

- The row also hides while an attachment import is in progress.

title: feat(bots): show Working and Waiting for you on inbox rows and sort them first
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #741

Rebuilt onto `master` after #773, #775, #782, #786, #789 and #792 landed; the `BotClient.call` allowlist keeps #775's and #786's entries and adds `session.active_list`.

## What changed

**Problem.** The Bots inbox cannot tell a bot that is working, or one blocked on an approval or question, from an idle bot. The host already publishes live status per session through `session.active_list`.

**Fix.** The inbox reads `session.active_list` beside every roster read and shows a still, tinted word in place of the row's date: "Working" or "Waiting for you". Busy bots sort first inside their group. While some bot is busy and the inbox is open and connected, it re-reads the statuses every 5 s, then stops once all are idle.

### Plan (express; decisions D1 and D27 Option A, the sort decision, the copy decision, Design pick A)

- **Contract.** `session.active_list` with exactly `{}` params goes on the `BotClient.call` allowlist. Any other params are refused locally. It is cancellation-safe, and a timeout fails only that read, so a stall never drops the socket. Checked against the pinned hermes-agent `d337b736`:
  - handler `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:962-973`;
  - item `server.py` `_session_live_item` (`{id, session_key, status, last_active, started_at, message_count, model, preview, title, current}`);
  - status `_session_live_status`;
  - enum `contracts/sessions.py` `LiveSessionStatus`;
  - `canonical_session.id` / `resolved_id` in `methods_profiles.py` `_canonical_session_row`.
- **Model.**
  - `BotProfile` now reads `canonicalID` / `canonicalTipID` tolerantly.
  - The new pure `BotLiveStatus` (in `BotConnection.swift`) maps `waiting` to Waiting and `working`/`starting`/`streaming` to Working. Idle, unknown values and a missing key show nothing.
  - `BotLiveStatus.statuses` matches an item to a bot when its `session_key` equals the bot's root or tip. If a key matches two bots, neither is marked. If several items match one bot, the most urgent wins.
- **Reads.** Every `profiles.list` reload starts a status read in its own task. Rooms, `.live` and avatars never wait for it; `open()` only finishes (ending a pull-to-refresh) once it is in.
  - A reply applies only while the wire still owns the inbox, the read was not replaced, and no newer status or roster read has started.
  - `-32601` hides statuses for the life of the socket.
  - Any other failure shows no statuses rather than stale ones, and never drops the socket.
  - A drop, a connection change, or a failed connection read clears all statuses. `close()` keeps them, and `open()` re-reads them.
  - Statuses are written only when they change, so an unchanged re-read does not invalidate the list.
- **Freshness (Option A).** While some bot is busy and the inbox is open and connected, the inbox re-reads `session.active_list` alone every 5 s. The interval is injected as `statusPollInterval`, like `reloadSpacing`. A failed read while a bot was busy keeps the re-reads going until one answers. Polling stops when all bots are idle; `close()`, a drop, or a newer read cancels it, and a cancelled re-read never sends its read. This replaces the trailing ~3 s read.
- **Sort.** One shared `byAttention` order is used inside every group: pinned bot tiles, pinned room tiles, each #742 section, and the unfiled block. The order is waiting, then working, then unread, then newest, with undated rows last and ties broken by id. Rooms rank with idle bots. `ChatRow.id` does not change.
- **UI (Design pick A).**
  - A still, tinted word replaces the row's date: "Working" in AttentionWorking, "Waiting for you" in AttentionApproval.
  - At accessibility sizes the slot moves under the name, as in SessionRowView.
  - Pinned tiles show the same word under the name (up to two centered lines), and the grid is top-aligned so avatars stay level.
  - Nothing animates. The word is part of the combined VoiceOver label.
  - It reuses the existing "Working" / "Waiting for you" catalog strings, which already exist in all 17 non-English languages. There is no new copy.
- **Docs.** In `docs/agents/bots.md`, the "not shown in the inbox yet (#741)" sentence is replaced with the source, the mapping (`resuming` shows nothing), the caveats (the `client.capabilities` handshake, only this host process, a rotated tip) and the refresh rule. The reload paragraph and the rooms-sorting paragraph are updated too.

**Risk.** Polling only runs while a row is busy and the inbox is visible, at one small read-only RPC every 5 s. A host stall on that read fails only the read after the RPC deadline; the roster keeps owning link health.

### Decisions applied

All from [the decision comment on #741](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/741#issuecomment-5824371151):
- D1: build now on today's Bots inbox.
- D27 Option A: re-read every ~5 s only while visible, connected, and some bot is non-idle; interval injected; tests use no sleeps.
- Sort: waiting, then working, then unread, then newest, inside every group.
- Copy: reuse "Working" / "Waiting for you".

### Surfaces

- Entry points: inbox rows and pinned tiles only.
- Targets: main app and tests.
- Servers: statuses live in each server's `BotInbox` and are cleared on a connection change.
- Reverse states: Working and Waiting both clear to nothing.
- Native: VoiceOver, Dynamic Type (AX stacking), light and dark from the asset colors, Reduce Motion (nothing animates).

## Design

Mock: https://edaa2t1bjfl4.postplan.dev §1. Pick: **A** (tinted text label in the trailing date slot; the same word under the name on pinned tiles; no spinner, nothing animates).

No after screenshot: showing Working or Waiting needs a busy bot on the live host, which would be a mutation this run is not authorized for, and an idle inbox looks the same as before at default text sizes. Before/after images come from the manual run below.

## How it was tested

`git diff --check`: clean. All runs on iPhone 17 Pro Max (`0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2`), one `--only` per class, each as `scripts/test-sim 0FDDF62A-2098-432B-ACAF-D0D1B5E191E2 --only HermesMobileTests/<Class>`, on the final code:

- **BotInboxTests: 40 passed, 0 failed.** 28 existing tests plus 12 new ones:
  - root/tip mapping with precedence, unknown status, missing key, and an ambiguous shared key;
  - a rotated tip matches no bot until the next reload;
  - -32601 keeps today's inbox for the socket, and a new socket asks again;
  - a stale status reply is dropped after a newer reload;
  - statuses clear on a drop and on a connection change;
  - waiting, working, unread, newest order in the tiles, a section, and the unfiled block with a room;
  - Option A: a busy bot is re-read until idle with no roster read, then reads stop;
  - re-reads stop when the inbox closes;
  - the inbox goes live with rooms while the status read is still out;
  - a replaced re-read never sends its read (200 event reloads against a zero-interval re-read);
  - a failed connection read clears the statuses a closed inbox kept;
  - a failed re-read while a bot is busy tries again until one answers, without a roster read.
  The last four were run against the code before their fixes and all fail there.
- **BotClientTests: 24 passed, 0 failed.** Includes the new `testActiveListAllowlistAdmitsOnlyTheEmptyRead`; the cancel and timeout tests now also cover `session.active_list` (a cancelled or stalled read keeps the socket).
- **BotChatPresentationTests: 35 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (the skip was already there). The search test now checks the set of calls, since the status read runs beside the room read.
- **BotRoomTests: 30 passed, 0 failed.**
- **BotRoomManagementTests: 12 passed, 0 failed.**
- **BotLifecycleTests: 19 passed, 0 failed.**
- **LocalizationCatalogTests: 7 passed, 0 failed** (on the first commit; no catalog change since).

No full-suite run locally: the Xcode project, `Config/` and shared test infrastructure are untouched, and no files were added. CI runs the full suite.

**Live checks.**
- Live check 1, run read-only on 2026-09-25 against the maintainer host (now hermes-agent 0.21.5 on `127.0.0.1:9119`): `session.active_list {}` returned `{sessions: []}` with no error. The method exists, but there was no live runtime, so `session_key == canonical_session.resolved_id` could not be confirmed.
- Skipped, not authorized (epic #737 N2), and listed below: live check 1's key comparison, which needs a live runtime; live check 2 (a clarify turn on `inbox-triage`, waiting shows, clears without the trailing read); live check 3 (a remote-Desktop turn appears; Telegram and cron turns do not).

## Manual test

Simulator, Uzair at review:

1. Use two bots, one mid-turn and one idle. Leave the busy bot's chat and go back to the inbox. **Expected:** Working replaces the date, and the busy bot sorts first in its group. This also confirms `session_key` matches the canonical tip (skipped live check 1).
2. Let the turn finish without touching anything. **Expected:** Working clears within about 5 s, and the date returns.
3. On `inbox-triage`, start a turn that asks a clarify question. **Expected:** Waiting for you shows and sorts above Working. Answer it and confirm the label clears (skipped live check 2).
4. Pin the busy bot. **Expected:** the tile shows the word under the name, and the avatars stay level.
5. Check the largest accessibility text size: the status sits under the name. Check light and dark mode. With Reduce Motion on, nothing moves. VoiceOver reads the status as part of the row.
6. Switch to a second server. **Expected:** no status from the first server shows.
7. Turn the network off. **Expected:** statuses clear when the socket drops.
8. Start a turn from a remote Hermes Desktop on the same host. **Expected:** it shows Working. A Telegram or cron turn does not (skipped live check 3).

title: fix(voice): fall back across the user's languages when the current locale has no dictation model
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #765 (part of #737)

## What changed

**Problem.** Dictation only tried `Locale.current`, which is the app language plus the device region. Some pairings, such as `en_PK`, have no on-device model. Those users saw "On-device speech recognition is not available for the current locale." even when one of their preferred languages, or `en-US`, would have worked. Separately, the default recognizer factory built `SFSpeechRecognizer(locale: Locale.current)` instead of the locale it had just checked.

**Fix.** This is client-only. `ComposerVoiceInputController` is shared, so the Sessions and Bot composers are fixed together.

- A new pure `ComposerSpeechLocalePolicy` in `ComposerVoiceInputController.swift`:
  - `candidates(current:preferredLanguages:)` returns `Locale.current`, then the first 3 `Locale.preferredLanguages`, then `en-US`. Duplicates are removed before the cap applies, so a preferred language that repeats `Locale.current` does not use up a slot.
  - `firstAvailable(in:supportedLocales:recognizer:)` returns the first candidate that appears in `SFSpeechRecognizer.supportedLocales()` and also supports on-device recognition. The recognizer is built from the matching supported locale, so the recognizer we use is for the locale we checked. Unsupported candidates never create a recognizer.
  - `normalizedIdentifier` matches on language plus region. It ignores the script, the `_`/`-` separator, case, and any `@…` keyword such as `@rg=`. So `zh-Hans-CN` (how `preferredLanguages` reports Chinese) matches `zh-CN` (how `supportedLocales()` lists it). An identifier with no region, such as `en`, falls back to separator-normalized string matching. An exact identifier match wins over a language plus region match, so `hi-IN` never resolves to `hi-IN-translit` (both appear in `supportedLocales()`). Any remaining collision resolves in sorted order.
- `speechRecognizerFactory` is now `(Locale) -> SFSpeechRecognizer?`. `onDeviceSpeechRecognizerForRecording()` uses the policy. The fallback that transcribes the recording on the device after the server fails goes through the same choice.
- Removed the `locale` property and both `voiceInput.locale = .current` call sites (`ChatComposerView`, `BotChatComposerView`).

**Decision applied (from the issue body):** `Locale.current` stays first, so users whose dictation works today keep exactly the same recognizer.

**Notes for review**
- The policy lives in `ComposerVoiceInputController.swift` rather than a new file, because the Xcode project does not use synchronized folders and a new file would mean editing the project.
- The recognizer is still cached for the controller's lifetime, as before.
- A bare preferred language with no region (e.g. `en`) does not match a regional supported locale; `en-US` is the last resort.
- `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` still gives its warning on `ComposerVoiceInputController.swift` (977 lines before, about 1030 after).

Surfaces: Sessions and Bot composers (group rooms have no mic). Main app target only. No new copy, no layout change.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerVoiceDraftComposerTests`: 36 passed, 0 failed. This includes 8 new policy tests: candidate order and the preferred-language cap, which counts distinct languages; dedupe across `_`, `-`, and case; a supported current locale is kept; fallback past an unsupported locale and a locale with no model, where the factory is only asked about supported locales; `@rg=` suffix tolerance; script-tagged Chinese preferred languages (`zh-Hans-CN` picks `zh-CN`, not `en-US`); an exact match preferred over a variant (`hi-IN` versus `hi-IN-translit`); nil when nothing has a model. The existing factory-count test was updated to the new closure shape.
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerVoiceInputServerRecordingTests`: 6 passed, 0 failed.
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/BotDraftTests`: 10 passed, 0 failed (Bot composer caller).
- On macOS, `Locale(identifier:).language` gives `zh`/`CN` for `zh-Hans-CN`, `en`/`US` for `en_US@rg=pkzzzz`, and no region for `en`. The normalization relies on those results.

### Manual test

These checks need a physical phone and were not run in this autonomous lane.

1. On an iPhone, set the app language to English and the region to Pakistan (Settings > General > Language & Region), with English (US) among the preferred languages. Open Hermex, pick a session, and tap the mic in the Sessions composer. **Expected:** dictation starts and English speech is transcribed. There is no "not available for the current locale" error.
2. Do the same in a Bot chat composer. **Expected:** the same result.
3. Set the device language to 简体中文 (zh-Hans) and the region to United States, then dictate in Chinese in either composer. **Expected:** Chinese text, not an English transcript.
4. Put the phone back on a normally supported pairing (e.g. English, United States) and dictate. **Expected:** nothing changes from today.

**Skipped live check:** the issue's device check (log `Locale.current.identifier` when the region differs from the language, and look for an `@rg=` suffix) was not run, because on-device runs were not authorized for this lane. Normalization ignores any `@…` keyword instead, and a test covers `de_DE@rg=atzzzz`.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)

title: test(bots): record real Hermes responses as test fixtures when advancing the pin
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #760

Stacked on #775; merge after it.

## What changed

**Problem:** every Bot test builds the host's payloads by hand, and `BotJSON` returns nil for anything missing. If upstream renames or drops a field, the tests stay green while the feature quietly goes blank.

**Fix:** a script records what a real hermes-agent host sends, sanitizes it with an allow-list, and writes it as JSON fixtures. A new test class runs the real Bot code over those fixtures, so a contract change breaks a test instead of the app.

### Plan

- `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures` is a zsh wrapper, following the `benchmark-streaming-scans` precedent. It compiles `scripts/fixtures/HermesFixtureCapture.swift` with `xcrun swiftc`, so there is no new dependency. It reads the `hermex-bot` Keychain item the same way `sim-login` does and never prints credentials.
- The helper signs in the way `BotClient.connect` does: status, login, `me`, `ws-ticket`, then the socket. It sends `client.capabilities`, then `profiles.list {include_sessions:true}`.
- It then runs `session.create {profile:"inbox-triage", title:"hermex-fixture-capture", hidden:true, follow_profile_config:true, close_on_disconnect:true}` and sends `prompt.submit` with a canned prompt ("Reply with exactly: ok. Do not use tools."). It records inbound frames until the first `session.info` with `running:false` after `message.complete`.
- It checks that `hidden` keeps the session out of the plain `session.list` and that `include_hidden` lists it, and aborts (with cleanup) if either fails. Then it runs `session.resume` on the stored id, `session.close` on every runtime id, and `session.delete` on the stored id (retrying on 4023, treating 4007 as done), and confirms that `session.list {include_hidden:true}` no longer returns the session. On failure it runs the same cleanup, first reopening the socket with a fresh ticket if a timeout or a drop closed it, and prints the ids only if the cleanup itself fails.
- The capture refuses a host whose release differs from the pin.

- Fail-closed: the run aborts if it sees a `tool.*`, `approval.*`, `clarify.*` or `*.request` event, or a server request, during the turn. A leak check then refuses to write if the output contains the host, the username, the password, the ticket, `/Users/`, a raw install id, or any other Profile name as a whole word.

  - Additive only: `profiles.list` rows gained `previous_names` and `role`; `TranscriptMessage` gained nullable `content`, `tool_call_id` and `labels`; `prompt.submit` gained `user_row_id`; `message.complete` gained `persisted_turn`.

Nothing else on the host changed: the other host reads were read-only `/api/status` curls and one ssh `git rev-parse` / `git describe`.

The one failure was `ChatScrollPolicyTests.testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesAndRouteThroughTheLatestHandler` ("5 is greater than 2"), outside this PR's files. `--only HermesMobileTests/ChatScrollPolicyTests` then passed 28 of 28, so it is a timing flake under full-suite load.

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. The app change is one version constant, and the fixture tests exercise it. Live checks that were skipped:

title: test(chat): stop putting deadlines on synchronous renders in response selection tests
body:
## Problem

Two response selection classes are the most common CI flake: 21 failed attempts across 19 PRs since Sept 20, each needing `gh run rerun --failed` on a PR that never touched chat selection. Tests: `ResponseSelectionTests.testRealMarkdownRegistersHeadingsListsCodeAndTableButNotEquations`, `ResponseSelectionTests.testRenderedGlyphOffsetsMatchUTF16IncludingEmojiAndCombiningCharacters`, `ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests.testOffscreenResponsesDeferGlyphRenderingAndRemainSelectableWhenScrolledIntoView`.

## Evidence

All failures ran on hosted `macos-26`, Xcode 26.6, iOS 26.5, 'Clone 1 of iPhone 17', and passed on rerun or the next push. Only the wait failed; every assertion after it passed.

| Test | Fails | Message | Failing / passing duration | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| testRealMarkdown… | 10 (Sept 20–24) | `Exceeded timeout of 5 seconds … "Markdown laid out and drawn"` | 5.2–11.2 s / 0.22–0.26 s | [35501717559](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35501717559/attempts/1) [35676028353](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35676028353/attempts/1) [35687059038](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35687059038/attempts/1) [35907079891](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35907079891/attempts/1) [35909689773](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35909689773/attempts/1) [35935502693](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35935502693/attempts/1) [35950216835](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35950216835/attempts/1) [36028957725](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36028957725/attempts/1) [36034641159](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36034641159/attempts/1) [36053551938](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36053551938/attempts/1) |
| testRenderedGlyphOffsets… | 2 (Sept 24–25) | `Exceeded timeout of 5 seconds … "Unicode text rendered"` | 5.6 s | [36034641159](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36034641159/attempts/1) [36096864401](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36096864401/attempts/1) |
| testOffscreenResponses… | 9 (Sept 20–25) | `Exceeded timeout of 10 seconds … "Visibility and text rendering committed"` | 12.9–45.0 s / 0.93–1.06 s | [35542068694](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35542068694/attempts/1) [35773043831](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35773043831/attempts/1) [35808373730](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35808373730/attempts/1) [35835546042](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35835546042/attempts/1) [35955876864](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35955876864/attempts/1) [35962554574](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35962554574/attempts/1) [35979292096](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35979292096/attempts/1) [36084234243](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36084234243/attempts/1) [36091593385](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36091593385/attempts/1) |

## Likely cause

- `HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests.swift:92-100` (same pattern at `:42-50`, `:127-135`, `:159-167`): the expectation is fulfilled in the same main-queue block that runs `layoutIfNeeded()` and `drawHierarchy(afterScreenUpdates: true)`. Both calls are synchronous. XCTest's 5 s timer runs off the main thread, so the timeout measures how long one render takes, not whether it happened. A render that normally takes 0.2 s stalled for 5–11 s on a loaded runner.
- `ResponseSelectionTests.swift:270-276` with the driver at `:279-294`: `renderFrames()` waits for 3 `CADisplayLink` ticks within 10 s. On the runner the display link stops ticking for seconds. The whole test takes about 1 s when it passes and 13–45 s when it fails. Three frames is only a stand-in: nothing ties them to the visibility change (`MessageBubbleView.swift:170-173`) or the glyph draw (`ResponseTextSelection.swift:169-187`) that the assertions read.
- The underlying stall is probably render-server starvation on the hosted VM. That is unproven, and the fix does not depend on it.

## Plan

One file: `HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests.swift`.

1. Add a private `render(_ window:)` helper. It awaits one main-queue turn (a continuation resumed from `DispatchQueue.main.async`, with no expectation and no timeout), then calls `window.layoutIfNeeded()` and `drawHierarchy(afterScreenUpdates: true)`. Glyphs are collected only when text draws, so each pass has to draw.
2. Replace the four expectation blocks with `await render(window)`.
3. Replace `renderFrames()` with a fixed number of `render` passes, 2 or 3. The first pass reports visibility. The second redraws visible rows with glyph collection on. Delete `ResponseSelectionFrameDriver`.
4. Keep every assertion unchanged. The assertions stay the arbiter.

## Acceptance and tests

- `grep -n "CADisplayLink\|fulfillment(of" HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests.swift` prints nothing.
- 10 consecutive local passes: `for i in {1..10}; do scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests || break; done`
- Mutation check: temporarily pass `collectsGlyphs: true` in `MessageBubbleView` and confirm the offscreen test fails. This shows the new passes did not make it vacuous. Then revert.
- On #649, track that neither class fails in the next 20 PR CI runs.

## Decisions

- **Fix or quarantine:** fix (recommended). The change is small and stays in one file. Quarantining would drop the only coverage of selection geometry and deferral.
- **Fixed pass count or loop until glyphs appear:** fixed count (recommended). A loop is polling. The count needed comes from SwiftUI's update order, not from load, so it stays deterministic.
- **Share a helper with the Bot draft:** no (recommended). This helper must draw on every pass, and the Bot one only lays out. Private helpers also avoid a `project.pbxproj` edit.

## Surfaces

Test-only: `HermesMobileTests`. No production code, extension, widget, or project-file change.

## Blockers

None.

title: test(chat): wait for the steering notice to clear instead of draining the main actor
body:
## Problem

`ChatViewModelSendTests.testSuccessfulSteeringUsesOneTransientConfirmationAndRestartsDismissal` fails in CI about once a day. It has failed on PRs that changed nothing in chat (#595 scripts, #648 live activity, #773 docs, #785 bot host status), and each failure forces a rerun. #649 was opened for this test.

## Evidence

Every failure has the same message, `XCTAssertNil failed: "Steering hint delivered."`, at `ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:9150`. The test passes in 5–8 ms. It fails at 1.5–3.3 s, so the runner was stalled while it ran. All passed on rerun.

| Run | PR | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [35560701035](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35560701035/attempts/1) | #595 | 2.1 s |
| [35692880770](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35692880770/attempts/1) | #617 | 2.3 s |
| [35826851485 a2](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35826851485/attempts/2) | #648 | 1.5 s |
| [36076695988](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36076695988/attempts/1) | #773 | 3.3 s |
| [36090456833](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36090456833/attempts/1) | #785 | 1.9 s |

## Likely cause

- `ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:9147-9150`: after the second `dismissalDelay.resumeNext()`, the dismissal task (`ChatViewModel.swift:4005-4012`) takes this path:
  - resumes on the `ManualAsyncDelay` actor (`:10324`),
  - returns through the nonisolated delay closure,
  - then hops back to the main actor to clear the notice.
- `drainMainActor()` (`:9330-9333`) runs three `Task.yield()`s and one main-actor task. Its own comment says "the leading yields add slack". It drains work already queued on main, not work still running on another executor. When the runner stalls, the hop lands after the drain and the assertion reads the old notice.
- This is a race in the test, not a product bug. The product only has to clear the notice eventually.

## Plan

One file: `HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests.swift`.

1. Before the second `resumeNext()`, register an observation expectation on `viewModel.steeringConfirmationNotice` (`withObservationTracking { … } onChange: { cleared.fulfill() }`). This is the pattern `awaitSnapshot` already uses (`BotChatPresentationTests.swift:1074-1078`).
2. After `resumeNext()`, `await fulfillment(of: [cleared], timeout: 5)`, then keep the `XCTAssertNil`. The wait ends when the state changes. The timeout is only a hang guard.
3. Reword `drainMainActor`'s doc comment: it drains main-actor work that is already enqueued, and does not wait for work resumed from another actor.
4. The other `resumeNext()` callers have no failing-direction race. At `:9142` the notice must stay; at `:9188` it is already nil.

## Acceptance and tests

- 20 consecutive local passes: `for i in {1..20}; do scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests/testSuccessfulSteeringUsesOneTransientConfirmationAndRestartsDismissal || break; done`
- One full class run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests`.
- Mutation check: temporarily skip `dismissSteeringConfirmation()` in the task, and confirm the test fails on the unfulfilled expectation. Then revert.
- On #649, track that the test does not fail in the next 20 PR CI runs.

## Decisions

- **Observation expectation, or make the injected delay main-actor-isolated:** observation (recommended). It is test-only and matches an existing pattern. Changing the closure's isolation touches the production init.
- **The negative check at `:9142-9145`** (a cancelled first timer must not dismiss): a short drain lets it pass vacuously. It cannot flake, it can only miss a regression, and a real check needs a signal from the cancelled task. Recommend leaving it.
- **Where this lives:** if #649 becomes the flake parent, file this as its sub-issue. Otherwise edit #649's body to this plan and let it close with the fix.

## Surfaces

Test-only: `ChatViewModelSendTests.swift`. No production code.

## Blockers

None.

title: test(bots): stop waiting on display-link frame counts in hosted Bot tests
body:
## Problem

Hosted Bot tests fail in CI with `Exceeded timeout of 10 seconds, with unfulfilled expectations: "Layout committed"`. That has happened 18 times since Sept 20. The failures hit a different test almost every time, on PRs that never touched Bots (#648 live activity, #651 memory, #652 insights, #729 workspace diff, #779 push). Each one forces a rerun.

## Evidence

All failures were on hosted `macos-26`, 'Clone 1 of iPhone 17', and passed on rerun or the next push.

| Test (`BotChatPresentationTests.`) | Fails | Failing / passing duration | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| testRoomSearchHitScrollsToItsSequence… | 4 | 18.6–41.6 s / 4.1–4.5 s | [35743513196](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35743513196/attempts/1) [35826851485 a1](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35826851485/attempts/1) [35826851485 a3](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35826851485/attempts/3) [36078751955](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36078751955/attempts/1) |
| testAttachmentPickerOverlayRetainsKeyboardFocus | 3 | 31.5–58.4 s / 1.4–1.6 s | [35666218859](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35666218859/attempts/1) [35970354123](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35970354123/attempts/1) [36100914381](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36100914381/attempts/1) |
| testSessionsComposerRetainsFocusAndAttachments… | 3 | 24.9–67.2 s / 0.40–0.54 s | [35835546042](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35835546042/attempts/1) [35835529021](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35835529021/attempts/1) [36077235386](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36077235386/attempts/1) |
| testRoomManagementShowsMemberChips… | 2 | 26.7–63.5 s | [35676013012](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35676013012/attempts/1) [35687059038](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35687059038/attempts/1) |
| testActivityRowsRenderAndFollowTheCardsSetting | 1 (+2 older "view recovered" waits, removed in #624) | 44.6 s | [35970354123](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35970354123/attempts/1) |
| testSendOnAWorkingBotAsksSteerQueueOrInterrupt… | 1 | 35.7 s / 2.7–3.0 s | [36084057183](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36084057183/attempts/1) |
| testRoomTranscriptDismissesKeyboardWithoutLosingDraft | 1 | 22.8 s | [36078751955 a2](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36078751955/attempts/2) |
| testLocalBotSearchShowsBotNames… | 1 | 69.8 s | [35789702645](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35789702645/attempts/1) |
| testScrolledSlashSkillsStayInsideTheCard | 1 (closed #511 branch) | 31.7 s | [35697171687 a2](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35697171687/attempts/2) |
| testBotFixturesAcrossAppearance… (removed in #619) | 1 | 51.5 s | [35666218859](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/35666218859/attempts/1) |

## Likely cause

- `HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests.swift:1080-1086`: `renderFrames(n)` waits for n `CADisplayLink` ticks from `BotRenderFrameDriver` (`BotConversationTests.swift:993-1015`), with a 10 s deadline. It has 65 call sites, and some ask for 8–40 frames (`:201`). `screenshot(awaiting:)` (`:1092-1101`) calls it up to 8 more times, so one stall anywhere fails the test.
- On the runner the display link stops ticking for seconds. `testSessionsComposer…` takes 9 frames and 0.4 s when it passes, and 25–67 s when it fails.
- The frames are not what the assertions read. The assertions read first-responder state, the view tree, model state, or OCR of a `drawHierarchy` capture.
- `BotConversationTests.swift:964-970` (`renderBotFrames`, 5 sites) uses the same driver. It has not failed yet but has the same exposure.

## Plan

1. In `BotConversationTests.swift`, replace `BotRenderFrameDriver` with an internal `XCTestCase` helper, `settle(_ window: UIWindow, passes: Int = 3) async`. Each pass awaits one main-queue turn (a continuation with no expectation and no timeout), then calls `window.layoutIfNeeded()`. The hosting view applies pending SwiftUI state during layout, so display cadence no longer matters. The file already shares the driver across files, so there is no `project.pbxproj` change.
2. Swap `renderFrames(n)` and `renderBotFrames()` for `settle`, and cut the 8–40 frame counts to the passes each test needs.
3. Keep `screenshot(awaiting:)`'s bounded content retry, but run it on settle passes. The capture, `drawHierarchy(afterScreenUpdates: true)`, forces the commit synchronously and has no deadline.
4. Where content comes from model work, await that work first (`reader.open()`, `model.recover()`, `awaitSnapshot`), then settle.
5. Start with the three most frequent tests (room search, sessions composer, attachment picker), then convert the rest mechanically in the same PR.

## Acceptance and tests

- `grep -rn "CADisplayLink\|BotRenderFrameDriver\|Layout committed" HermesMobileTests` prints nothing.
- 5 consecutive local passes: `for i in {1..5}; do scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests || break; done`. The class's total time should not grow.
- Mutation check: temporarily make the attachment overlay resign focus, and confirm `testAttachmentPickerOverlayRetainsKeyboardFocus` still fails. Then revert.
- On #649, track that there is no "Layout committed" failure in the next 20 PR CI runs.

## Decisions

- **Layout passes, or keep the display link with a longer timeout:** layout passes (recommended). A longer timeout only moves the threshold and makes failures slower; they already take 25–70 s.
- **The `awaitSnapshot` 5 s wait (`:1074-1078`):** it rides a real 250 ms coalescing sleep (`BotConversation.swift:1205`). It failed twice (Sept 20–21) in tests since removed by #619, and it still backs `testSudoCard…` and `BotPendingRequestTests`. Recommend leaving it and noting it. Inject the delay (like `reconnectDelay`, `BotConversation.swift:127`) only if it flakes again, because that changes production init.
- **Fix or quarantine:** fix (recommended). Quarantining the class would drop hosted coverage of the whole Bot composer.
- **A test that turns out to need real frame time** (an animation that isn't disabled): make it wait on model state or disable that animation, not add frames.

## Surfaces

Test-only: `BotChatPresentationTests.swift`, `BotConversationTests.swift`. No production code, target, or project-file change.

## Blockers

None. Independent of the response selection draft.

title: Group room: open and reply inside threads (thread_id)
body:
Part of the group room threading gap found while validating desktop/mobile parity.

## Current behavior

In a group room, replies sent from the iOS app get a fresh, device-minted `thread_id` on every send. A reply composed against an existing thread therefore breaks out of that thread instead of continuing it — the reply lands as the root of a brand new thread rather than as a reply inside the one the user tapped into.

## Desired behavior

1. The group room view shows messages grouped by `thread_id`, with one entry per thread showing the root message, reply count, and last activity.
2. Tapping a thread opens a thread detail view with the root message and its replies in chronological order.
3. Replies composed inside that thread detail view are sent using the existing thread's `thread_id`, not a newly generated one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A thread started on Desktop can be replied to on the phone, and the reply appears in the same thread on Desktop.
- [ ] The XCTest suite passes on the iOS simulator.

## Notes

No push, PR, merge, release, new dependency, or live-host mutation is authorized by this ticket — tracking only.

title: New chat starts on the default profile after switching to another profile
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Hermex to a hermes-webui server that has several profiles (password auth enabled).
2. Switch the active profile to a non-default one (here: `workspace`).
3. Start a new chat and send a message.
4. The session shows profile `default` and the default profile's model.

### Expected behavior

The new session uses the profile selected in step 2.

### Actual behavior

The new chat is created on the `default` profile (wrong model, wrong workspace), not on `workspace`.

Server-side check with curl against the same server (`hermes_profile` = the per-client signed cookie set by `/api/profile/switch`):

| `POST /api/session/new` | Session profile |
|---|---|
| after `switch workspace`, with the `hermes_profile` cookie, no `profile` field | `workspace` (correct) |
| authenticated but without the `hermes_profile` cookie, no `profile` field | `default` (matches what Hermex does) |
| without the cookie, with `{"profile":"workspace"}` in the body | `workspace` (correct) |

So the server behaves as designed: the profile is kept per client through the signed `hermes_profile` cookie, and `/api/session/new` also accepts an explicit `profile` field.

Likely cause: Hermex calls `/api/profile/switch`, but then sends `/api/session/new` without the `hermes_profile` cookie and without a `profile` field, so the server falls back to the process-wide default. Server logs show `session/new` and `profile/switch` calls interleaved (`session/new` right before or after a switch).

Suggested fix: send `"profile": "<selected profile>"` in the body of `/api/session/new` (and ideally on other profile-scoped calls), or keep the `hermes_profile` cookie across requests.

### App version / commit

1.7

### iOS version and device

iOS 27.0 on iPhone 17 Pro

### hermes-webui server version

Upstream tag `exp-v0.52.318` (commit `adbb3258`, 2026-09-17), running behind Hermes Agent 0.21.3.

### How the phone reaches the server

Tailscale (HTTPS via Tailscale Serve, tailnet only).

title: feat(bots): show a Copy button in the Bot reply footer
body:
## Problem

In Bot Chat, a settled Bot reply has no visible Copy button. Its footer (`BotReplyFooter`, from #746 and #761) shows the "…" React menu, the reaction chips and the time, but passes `onCopy: nil` to `ChatMessageMetaRow`. Replies have no long-press menu, so Copy is only reachable through VoiceOver. In Sessions, the same meta row shows `ChatCopyButton`.

Found in review of [#791](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/791) (#761, design B). Uzair chose to do it as a follow-up, not a new commit on that PR (2026-09-25, epic #737 merge walk).

## Plan

- `BotReplyFooter` passes an `onCopy` for settled Bot replies that have text, using the same copy path as `BotMessageActions` (pasteboard plus the haptic setting). Prompts keep Copy in their long-press menu, and live rows and rooms stay as they are.
- The footer then reads `[…][Copy][chips][time]` on replies, matching the Sessions meta row's order.

## Acceptance

- A settled Bot reply shows a Copy button in its footer. A tap copies the reply's text.
- Prompts, live replies and group rooms are unchanged.
- A reply with no text shows no Copy button.
- VoiceOver still offers Copy, with no duplicate action.

## Tests

A focused `BotChatPresentationTests` (or `BotMessageActions`) test asserts which rows get `onCopy` and what text they copy, using the injectable `copy` closure.

## Hit every surface

The main app only (Bot Chat). Not rooms, the share extension or the Live Activity. Nothing crosses the wire and there are no new strings, since Copy reuses the existing label.

title: Attachment camera: app stops responding after entering and leaving the camera
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a chat and tap the plus button in the composer.
2. In the attachment panel, tap **Camera**.
3. Leave the camera again (back to the panel), then repeat entering and leaving the camera a few times.

### Expected behavior

The panel returns to its menu each time and the app stays responsive.

### Actual behavior

After entering and leaving the camera, the app stops responding to touches. Nothing on screen reacts; the only way out is to force-quit from the app switcher.

The device crash report (`bug_type 309`) from that force-quit shows:

- `0x8BADF00D`, `Failed to terminate gracefully after 5.0s`, `WatchdogEvent: process-exit`, `WatchdogVisibility: Foreground`.
- The main thread was idle in the run loop (`__CFRunLoopRun` → autorelease pool pop), not blocked on a lock or on the camera session queue.
- Application CPU time was 0.378 s (1%) over the watchdog window.

So the app is not spinning or deadlocked on the main thread; it looks like input stops reaching the UI after the camera round trip. I have not pinned the exact cause yet. Candidates I looked at in `CameraPickerView.swift` / `CustomAttachmentPicker.swift`: the `start()`/`stop()` calls from `onAppear`, `onDisappear` and `scenePhase` interleaving on `sessionQueue` during quick in/out, and the sibling `UIHostingController` overlay host that the picker installs next to the root view. The overlay host is removed on dismiss, so it is probably not a leftover hit-test layer, but I could not rule it out from code alone.

Reproduces identically in the App Store build and in a source build of current `master` (the camera and picker files are unchanged between them).

### App version / commit

App Store 1.7 (released 2026-09-24). Also reproduced on a source build based on `master` at the 1.8 merge.

### iOS version and device

iPhone Air (iPhone18,4), iOS 27.2 beta (24B5089g).

### hermes-webui server version

exp-v0.52.328

### How the phone reaches the server

Tailscale

### Screenshots or screen recordings

I can attach the `.ips` crash report or a screen recording if that helps.

title: fix(chat): detach the camera preview off the main thread
body:
Fixes #809

**Problem.** After leaving the attachment camera, the app stopped responding for about 9 seconds; touches were queued and delivered all at once afterwards, and the camera privacy indicator stayed on for the same period. A HangTracer report from an iPhone Air (iOS 27.2 beta) showed a 9009 ms main-thread hang with every sample in `HermexAttachmentCameraPreview.dismantleUIView` → `-[AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer setSession:]` → `-[AVCaptureSession _buildAndRunGraph:]`, waiting for the session to rebuild its graph. The session itself had already stopped on its queue within ~100 ms.

**Fix.** Setting the preview layer's `session` to `nil` now runs on the camera controller's existing `sessionQueue`, so the main thread never waits for the graph rebuild. No other camera behaviour changes.

**Testing.**
- New `HermexAttachmentPickerPolicyTests.testCameraPreviewDetachesOffTheMainThread`: fails without the fix (detach observed on main), passes with it.
- `scripts/test-sim --only` for `ChatComposerSendGateTests`, `HermexAttachmentPickerPolicyTests` and `BotChatPresentationTests`.
- On device: repeated camera in/out, photos in/out and panel open/close stay responsive; HangTracer records no hang and the indicator turns off promptly.
- Pre-existing on `master` locally, unrelated to this change: `BotChatPresentationTests.testScrolledSlashSkillsStayInsideTheCard` (0.2 pt over the bound) and `testRoomMessageSearchShowsRoomAndSenderAfterOpeningTheRoom` (failed 3/3 on a clean `master` run on the same simulator).

Maintainer validation: Uzair confirmed the camera works on his physical iPhone in Hermex Branch 1.8 (20260926140456). The combined build passed 53 focused tests. Updated from current master to include the already-landed Bot fixture fix that blocked the old CI run.

AI disclosure: investigated and implemented with Claude Opus 5.5 via Hermes Agent, reviewed and device-tested by me.

title: fix(live-activity): say a stale Bot activity is waiting on you, not "Not connected"
body:
## Problem

When a Bot turn stops for a question or an approval and the phone is locked, the Lock Screen Live Activity says **"Not connected"** with an **"Open to reconnect"** chip. The Dynamic Island shows the real state ("Needs clarification" / "Waiting for approval"). The user sees a connection problem on the Lock Screen when the bot is actually waiting on them.

Seen on a phone during the epic #737 merge walk (2026-09-25), testing #779 on Hermex Branch.

## Cause

Both views read the same state: `status` is `.waitingForClarification` (or `.waitingForApproval`) and `isStale` is true, because the app marks a Bot activity stale once its socket closes after the phone locks (`AgentLiveActivityManager`, `AgentRunActivityStateReducer.stale`).

- The Lock Screen checks stale first. `AgentRunLockScreenView.activityText` returns "Not connected" for any stale Bot activity, and `botChips` appends "Open to reconnect" (`HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift:120-135`). The expanded island's `countsLine` does the same (line 65).
- The compact island ignores `isStale` and shows `status.compactTitle`.

## Plan

A waiting-on-you status stays true after the socket closes, because the host keeps waiting until the user answers. So when a Bot activity is stale **and** its status is `.waitingForApproval` or `.waitingForClarification`:

- lead with the status text ("Needs clarification" / "Waiting for approval"), not "Not connected";
- show an "Open to answer" chip instead of "Open to reconnect";
- keep the stale dimming, and the "Not connected" treatment for every other stale state (running, stopping).

Apply the same rule to the expanded island's `countsLine`. Widget only; no change to the manager's stale rule.

## Acceptance

- A stale Bot activity that's waiting on the user says what it's waiting for on the Lock Screen and in the expanded island, with "Open to answer".
- A stale Bot activity that's running still says "Not connected" / "Open to reconnect".
- Webui (non-Bot) activities are unchanged.

## Tests

A focused test on the presentation rule: status × stale → lead text and chip, for Bot and webui activities. Move the rule into a small pure helper in the shared `AgentRunActivityAttributes` code if the widget views can't be tested directly.

## Hit every surface

The Live Activity widget target (Lock Screen and expanded island). One new string ("Open to answer") in all shipped languages. The Reduce Motion, light/dark and VoiceOver reading of the chip row stay as they are.

title: ci: run the full suite on every push to master
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: maintainer-approved chore from the epic #737 merge-walk review.

## What changed

PRs don't have to be up to date to merge, so two PRs that are each green can still break master together. In the #737 merge walk, #774 used a test helper that #775 had just renamed. Master's tests didn't compile for 76 minutes, and seven more PRs merged on top before anyone noticed, because CI only ran on pull requests.

`pr-ci.yml` now also runs on pushes to `master`:
- **Trigger:** `push: branches: [master]` alongside `pull_request`.
- **Changed paths:** a push always runs the full suite. The PR file lookup needs a PR number, which a push doesn't have.
- **Concurrency:** PR runs still cancel older runs of the same PR. A master run always finishes; pushes that land meanwhile wait, and only the newest waiting one runs, so a burst of merges ends with one result for the latest master.

## How it was tested

- `actionlint .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml`: no findings.
- This PR's own CI exercises the unchanged `pull_request` path.

## Manual test

After merge: open Actions and confirm a **PR CI** run for the merge commit on `master`, with *Detect changed paths* logging "Push to master — running the full suite." and *Build and Test* running.

## Checklist

- [x] No app code changed; no new dependencies; no API shapes touched

title: test(bots): stop waiting on display-link frame counts in hosted Bot tests
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #801
Closes #596

## What changed

Hosted Bot tests waited on `CADisplayLink` ticks (`renderFrames(n)` and `renderBotFrames()` through `BotRenderFrameDriver`), each with a 10 s deadline. The hosted `macos-26` runner's display link stalls for seconds, so PRs that never touched Bots failed with `"Layout committed"` timeouts (18 times since Sept 20). The assertions never read the frames.

Test-only, per the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/801#issuecomment-5839957556):
- `BotRenderFrameDriver` is replaced by `XCTestCase.settle(_ window:passes: = 3)` in `BotConversationTests.swift`. Each pass awaits one main-queue turn (no expectation, no timeout) and then calls `window.layoutIfNeeded()`, where the hosting view applies pending SwiftUI state.
- All 65 `renderFrames(n)` and 5 `renderBotFrames()` sites now call `settle(window)`, and frame counts of 4 to 40 drop to 3 passes. `screenshot(awaiting:)` keeps its bounded retry, now on settle passes.
- Room message search (was 40 frames) waits for the hit through `screenshot(awaiting:)`, which covers `BotSearchView`'s 200 ms debounce.
- Model-row test: the pill-to-card morph is the composer's own `.animation(_:value:)`, which the root `disablesAnimations` does not stop. The fixture turns on Reduce Motion so the morph snaps, and the test waits for the toolbar row with `screenshot(awaiting:)`, because the row can be empty on a cold first capture.
- Local bot search: `BotSearchView` focuses its field from `.task`, so the test awaits `UITextField.textDidBeginEditingNotification` before checking first responder. Three passes were not enough on iOS 26.5 CI.
- `testActivityRowsRenderAndFollowTheCardsSetting`, the last #596 flake, lost its `renderFrames(12)`. `docs/agents/bots.md` no longer mentions display-link frames.
- Deliberate, per the decision: the `awaitSnapshot` 5 s wait and its 250 ms coalescing sleep stay.
- Left for #799: `ResponseSelectionTests.swift`'s own display-link driver (2 remaining grep hits).

## How it was tested

- Acceptance grep `grep -rn "CADisplayLink\|BotRenderFrameDriver\|Layout committed" HermesMobileTests`: 8 hits on master. Only #799's 2 hits remain.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air> --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests`: master 110 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (a toolchain skip that already exists). The final head passed 5 runs in a row with the same result. Per-test times match master within noise: summed over BotChatPresentationTests, the quietest run was 44.5 s against master's 42.5 s.
- Model-row test run cold on its own, 3 times: attempt 0 captures an empty toolbar and attempt 1 lands "Model Alpha • High", every time.
- Search focus mutation: removing the view's `.task { searchFocused = true }` fails the test (unfulfilled begin-editing notification, then `XCTAssertNotNil failed`). With it restored, `--only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests` gave 41 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped.
- Mutation: forcing the attachment overlay to resign focus makes `testAttachmentPickerOverlayRetainsKeyboardFocus` fail on settle passes (`Opening/Closing attachment choices must retain keyboard focus.`). The mutation was reverted.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (none touched)

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator

1. On this PR's CI run (hosted `macos-26`, iPhone 17, iOS 26.5), open the test log. Expected: `BotChatPresentationTests` and `BotConversationTests` pass with no `Layout committed` or `Exceeded timeout`, including `testBotComposerUsesSessionsModelAndEffortRow` and `testSendOnAWorkingBotAsksSteerQueueOrInterruptBeforeWriting`. Local runs used iOS 27.0 only.
2. Optionally, on an iOS 26.5 iPhone 17 simulator, run `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests` 3 times. Expected: 110 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped each time.
3. On #649, watch the next 20 PR CI runs. Expected: no `"Layout committed"` failure.

title: test(chat): wait for the steering notice to clear instead of draining the main actor
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #800 (sub-issue of #649).

## What changed

`testSuccessfulSteeringUsesOneTransientConfirmationAndRestartsDismissal` fails in CI about once a day with `XCTAssertNil failed: "Steering hint delivered."`. The restarted dismissal timer resumes on the `ManualAsyncDelay` actor, then hops back to main to clear the notice. `drainMainActor()` only drains work already queued on main, so on a stalled runner the assertion reads the old notice. The race is in the test; the product is fine.

- Before the second `resumeNext()`, the test registers a `withObservationTracking` expectation on `steeringConfirmationNotice` (the `awaitSnapshot` pattern in `BotPendingRequestTests.swift`), then awaits it and keeps the `XCTAssertNil`. The 5 s timeout is only a hang guard.
- `drainMainActor`'s doc comment now says it does not wait for work that will hop back to main from another actor.
- Per the [Decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/800#issuecomment-5839957336): the cancelled-timer negative check and the other `resumeNext()` sites are unchanged; the delay closure's isolation is not touched (Rejected).

## How it was tested

Simulator iPhone 18 Pro, `scripts/test-sim <udid>`:
- `git diff --check origin/master..HEAD`: clean.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests`: 206 passed, 0 failed.
- 20 consecutive runs of `--only …/testSuccessfulSteeringUsesOneTransientConfirmationAndRestartsDismissal`: 20/20 pass, including one stalled run at 5.41 s (CI failures were 1.5–3.3 s).
- Red: a 200 ms sleep injected after `dismissalDelay.wait()` in the test's delay closure reproduces the CI failure on the old body (`:9150 XCTAssertNil failed: "Steering hint delivered."`); the new body passes with the same stall. Not committed.
- Mutation: with `dismissSteeringConfirmation()` removed from the timer, the new test fails on `Exceeded timeout of 5 seconds … "Steering notice cleared"`. Reverted; production code is unchanged.
- Tracking the next 20 PR CI runs happens on #649 after merge.

## Checklist

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (none touched)

## Manual test

Covered by tests; no manual check needed (test-only change, per the Decision comment).

title: chore(test): stop local test runs and branch builds from piling up on disk
body:
## Problem

Local test and build tooling leaves output behind that nothing ever cleans up. A storage audit on 2026-09-25 found:

- **208 leftover parallel-testing clones** in `~/Library/Developer/XCTestDevices` ("Clone N of iPhone 17"): about 1 TB apparent and about 50 GB real, created Aug 29 to Sep 20. The shared scheme marks the test target `parallelizable = "YES"`. Xcode only deletes clones when a run exits cleanly, so every killed or timed-out run left its clones behind. `scripts/test-sim` stopped creating them in #591 (`-parallel-testing-enabled NO`), but XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` and the Xcode GUI still follow the scheme.
- **`scripts/test-sim` never prunes `runs/`**: 80 result bundles (~0.95 GB) in 4 days under `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/hermex-tests-<key>/runs/`.
- **`scripts/branch-testflight` keeps every work dir**: 6 archives in 3 days (~150 MB each) under `build/branch-testflight/<build_number>/`.

## Proposed fix

1. **Scheme:** set `parallelizable = "NO"` on the test target in `HermesMobile.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/HermesMobile.xcscheme`. CI isn't affected, because `pr-ci.yml` passes `-parallel-testing-enabled YES` with a worker count, and that flag overrides the scheme's per-target setting. Local runs from Xcode and XcodeBuildMCP become serial, which matches `test-sim`.
2. **`scripts/test-sim`:** after each run, keep only the newest 10 directories in `runs/`.
3. **`scripts/branch-testflight`:** after a successful upload, keep only the newest 2 work dirs in `build/branch-testflight/`, so recent dSYMs stay available. A failed run keeps its dir for debugging.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Running the test plan from Xcode or XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim` creates no `Clone N of …` devices in `~/Library/Developer/XCTestDevices`.
- [ ] PR CI still runs tests in parallel with `TEST_WORKER_COUNT` workers.
- [ ] `test-sim` leaves at most 10 run dirs, covered by a focused test in `scripts/tests`.
- [ ] A successful `branch-testflight` leaves at most 2 work dirs; a failed one leaves its own dir in place.

Filed from a storage audit run with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).

title: chore(scripts): let test-sim repeat tests in one build and reboot after a runner hang
body:
## Problem

The first `/hermex-batch` run (four small test-only issues) took 2h46m, and most of it was `scripts/test-sim`, not the agents:

- **Repeated runs rebuild and relaunch every time.** #800's acceptance asks for 20 passes in a row. That was 20 separate `test-sim` calls, 91 minutes in all, because each call is a full `xcodebuild test` with a new launch.
- **Runner hangs cost about 6 minutes each.** The iPhone 18 Pro lane hit "The test runner hung before establishing connection" 13 times in 25 runs. Each hang waits out `xcodebuild`'s own 300 s timeout before `test-sim` retries, and every launch is another chance to hang. That came to 81 minutes.
- **A stuck `simctl terminate` holds a run for 120 s** before it stops, because it reuses the boot timeout.

## Plan

One file: `scripts/test-sim`, plus `scripts/tests/test_sim_runner.py`.

1. **`--repeat N`** runs the selected tests up to N times in one build and one launch: `-test-iterations N -run-tests-until-failure`. It stops at the first failure and reports it like any other failure.
2. **After a runner hang, reboot the assigned simulator before the one retry.** Shut down only this UDID, then boot it and wait for boot status. It stays under the existing four-device check and the device lock.
3. **`simctl terminate` gets a 25 s timeout** instead of the boot timeout.

## Acceptance and tests

- New unit tests cover these three cases:
  - `--repeat` adds the iteration flags, and omitting it adds none;
  - a hang reboots the simulator before the retry;
  - `terminate` uses the short timeout.
- Existing tests pass: `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`.
- A real run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HapticButtonTests --repeat 3` shows one build and 3 iterations.

## Decisions

- **Same process or a relaunch per iteration:** same process (recommended). It's fastest, and relaunching would bring back the handshake hangs this change avoids.
- **Stop at the first failure or run all N:** stop at the first failure (recommended). A stress run only needs to know whether anything failed.

## Surfaces

Local tooling only. No app code, CI, or project file changes.

Model and harness: Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code in T3 Code.

title: fix(chat): keep the composer above the keyboard after returning from Files
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #810

## What changed

Returning from Files could restore the keyboard before SwiftUI updated its safe area, leaving the composer behind it. The editor now defers focus until the navigation transition finishes.

Explicit dismissal and removal cancel pending restoration. Navigation-driven resignation preserves the composer's focus intent, so back-button and swipe returns restore the keyboard only when it was previously active. A cancelled swipe does not open the keyboard on Files.

## How it was tested

- The contributor reproduced the original safe-area bug on an iPhone Air running iOS 27.2 beta and verified the initial fix on device.
- Final correction: 53 focused tests passed on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 using `scripts/test-sim`, selecting `ComposerFocusTransitionTests`, `ComposerChipPresentationTests`, `ComposerChipGestureTests`, `ComposerChipDocumentTests`, `ChatComposerSendGateTests`, `HermexAttachmentPickerPolicyTests`, and `BotMentionTests`.
- The bound-dismissal regression fails against the original PR, and the focused navigation round-trip regression fails before the follow-up correction.
- Signed simulator app: back-button return, swipe return, cancelled partial swipe followed by successful return, and returning with the keyboard initially dismissed. Uzair confirmed the corrected behavior works.
- Hosted tests use lifecycle expectations and clean up editing, windows, and root controllers.

## Checklist

title: test(chat): stop putting deadlines on synchronous renders in response selection tests
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #799 (sub-issue of #649).

## What changed

The response selection tests are the most common CI flake. The failures are timeouts in the test's own waits, and every assertion after the wait passed. Four tests fulfilled an expectation in the same main-queue block that ran `layoutIfNeeded()` and `drawHierarchy(afterScreenUpdates: true)`. Both calls are synchronous, so the 5 s timeout measured how long one render took on a loaded runner. The visibility tests waited for 3 `CADisplayLink` ticks within 10 s. Those ticks stall on the runner, and nothing ties them to the visibility change or glyph draw the assertions read.

Only `HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests.swift` changes:
- A file-private `render(_:)` helper waits one main-queue turn (a continuation, no expectation, no timeout), then lays out and draws the window. Every pass draws, because selection leaves collect glyphs only when text draws.
- The four expectation blocks are now `await render(window)`.
- `renderFrames()` is now a private `renderVisibleRows(_:)` with 2 render passes. The first pass reports which rows are visible, and the second draws them with glyph collection on. `ResponseSelectionFrameDriver` is deleted.
- Every assertion is unchanged, including the #463 Preserve checks: offscreen rendering is still deferred, text is still selectable after scrolling, and the transcript height is unchanged.
- Per the [Decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/799#issuecomment-5839957142): the tests are fixed, not quarantined. They use a fixed pass count instead of a loop, and the helper stays private. It is not shared with #815's Bot `settle(_:passes:)`, so the names don't clash.

## How it was tested

Simulator iPhone 17e, `scripts/test-sim <udid>`:
- `git diff --check origin/master HEAD`: clean. `grep -n "CADisplayLink\|fulfillment(of"` on the file prints nothing.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- The same selection with `--repeat 10` (one build): 70/70 test-case passes, 0 failures. This replaces the issue's 10-run loop.
- Red: on master (b96ef438), a 6 s `Thread.sleep` in the render block makes `testRenderedGlyphOffsetsMatchUTF16…` fail with `Exceeded timeout of 5 seconds, with unfulfilled expectations: "Unicode text rendered"`, the exact CI message. With the same stall in the new `render(_:)`, the test passes 1/1.
- Mutation (#463): with `collectsGlyphs: true` in `MessageBubbleView`, `testOffscreenResponsesDeferGlyphRendering…` fails with `("264") is not less than ("132") - Scrolling must not rasterize selection text throughout the transcript`. The change was reverted.
- Tracking the next 20 PR CI runs on #649 happens after merge.

## Manual test

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. This is a test-only change, with no production, extension, widget, or project-file edits.

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>`, with the selection and results recorded above
- [x] No `Codable`, dependency, or API contract changes

title: fix(chat): create new chats in the selected profile

body:
## Problem and outcome

Part of #700 slice 0.2 in epic #713. Bot RPC requests currently enter the network boundary as method strings and dictionaries, with important validation scattered through `BotClient`. Preserve those rules; merely replacing method strings with enum raw values is insufficient.
- [HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift:490](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/cf50deb0f8167750c96bb96e3263e74bde6ee8f9/HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift#L490) contains artifact download, Profile deletion and image upload call sites. - Add the smallest `HermesCall` and `HermesREST` boundary under `Networking/Hermes/` (names can follow the code's seam). Represent currently used operation payloads with typed fields/associated values, preserve optional contract fields and tolerant response decoding, and wire the existing production callers through it. Include supported room operations; do not broaden room administration or the RPC allowlist.
- Preserve wire formats, Profile/runtime targeting, response/error mapping, `validateDispatch` immediately before actual send, and cancellation/timeout classification. Move request construction, not authentication/session/socket ownership; the next two children own those.
- No unused facade, raw unrestricted escape hatch, generated catalog of every upstream method, or speculative methods for later migration phases. A temporary compatibility adapter is acceptable only if production calls still pass through the typed validation and its removal is owned by the following child.

- [ ] Existing Bot screens use the typed boundary; current allowed payloads retain exact wire shapes, including omitted fields where required.
- [ ] Wrong/unscoped payloads and currently forbidden methods cannot bypass admission. Preserve scoped model writes, room restrictions, dispatch-time stale-target checks, and queued prompt behavior.

- [ ] PR names the exact selected test classes/results and verifies source contract drift only for touched operations.
