#699 (already closed; preserve its handshake and keepalive). Next child depends on this PR's request boundary.

## Preservation from implementation history

Preserve (#775): Every socket sends capabilities immediately after ready, then keepalive; preserve the 45-second inbound deadline and nonfatal capability rejection. Never directly reply to server-request frames and withdraw Desktop requests. https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/775

title: refactor(hermes): share the gateway across Bot consumers
body:
## Problem and outcome

Part of #700 slice 0.2 in epic #713. Each Bot screen currently creates a socket and replaces one pair of transport callbacks; screen teardown closes the wire. Make the connection server-owned with independent consumer subscriptions, so concurrent Bot features share a gateway safely.

## Plan and evidence

Evidence is pinned to Hermex `cf50deb0`; recheck against the execution base and preceding children.

- [HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:133](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/cf50deb0f8167750c96bb96e3263e74bde6ee8f9/HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift#L133) exposes one `onEvent`/`onDisconnect` pair. [HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:195](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/cf50deb0f8167750c96bb96e3263e74bde6ee8f9/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift#L195) creates a client and installs those callbacks; its `resetConnection` closes the wire. [HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift:532](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/cf50deb0f8167750c96bb96e3263e74bde6ee8f9/HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift#L532) cancels every pending request and closes the socket.
- [HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:95](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/cf50deb0f8167750c96bb96e3263e74bde6ee8f9/HermesMobile/ContentView.swift#L95) keys the logged-in subtree by server; put the shared owner in the appropriate existing server lifetime and reuse child 2's auth context. Keep the current saved-connection model until 0.3. Endpoint/username changes can preserve UUID: invalidate changed configuration rather than reusing a connection by UUID alone.
- Audit every client construction/callback/close site: `BotInbox`, `BotConversation`, `BotCreator`, `BotProfileEditor`, `BotRoomReader`, `BotRoomCreator`, `BotConnectionSetup` in `BotConnectionView`, `HermexPushProvisioner`, and `Config/DevAutoLogin`. Setup probes for an unsaved replacement must remain isolated from the active connection; on successful save use the committed connection's owner. Keep intentional isolated test/probe paths documented rather than silently sharing uncommitted credentials.
- Give consumers independent subscriptions/request ownership (an owned handle/adapter is fine). Local `close`/cancellation releases that consumer's work; another screen's stream/socket stays alive. A genuine socket fault or server/credential replacement invalidates the connection generation and notifies all relevant consumers once.
- Route session events and server requests to the correct runtime/consumer; fan out connection/Profile events only where appropriate. If two views observe the same conversation, avoid duplicate request responses and duplicate state application. Keep RPC reply matching and dispatch-time ownership checks.
- One ready/capabilities/keepalive handshake per shared socket; fresh ticket per socket; one coordinated socket reconnect even when several consumers notice a failure. Preserve existing conversation resume/replay behavior and app-background behavior under the shared owner. Do not implement the new generalized 0.4 engine, alter snapshot/replay rules, or close a host session when leaving a screen.
- Owner teardown cancels pending work/subscriptions/uploads/downloads without publishing stale state. Per-consumer disposal cannot run a global disconnect or replay an uncertain mutation. Optional read cancellations/timeouts remain local; actual wire failure is connection-wide.

## Acceptance and tests

- [ ] Simultaneous consumers open one socket/sign-in; removing inbox/editor/room/chat consumers cannot cancel another consumer's active work.
- [ ] Interleaved replies, events, and server requests reach correct targets; broadcasts are delivered appropriately; canceled subscriptions receive no late callbacks or duplicated pending actions.
- [ ] Concurrent reconnect triggers create one replacement socket/ticket/handshake; consumers retain existing reconnect behavior. Server switch, Bot replacement, logout, and app background follow explicit shared ownership with no stale mutations.

title: refactor(hermes): type existing Bot RPC and REST requests
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #823 (part of #700 slice 0.2, epic #713).

## What changed

**Problem.** Bot RPC requests reached the network boundary as method strings and dictionaries (`BotTransport.call(_ method: String, _ params: [String: BotJSON])`). The rules that decided what could be sent were split between the `BotClient` validators and `BotRoomRPC.validate`. REST routes lived in `BotEndpoint`, and each call site built its own `URLRequest`.

**Fix.**
- New `Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift` (main app target only). It has one case for each of the 45 JSON-RPC operations the app sends, and no case for any other upstream method. Each case carries only the values callers change. Values the contract fixes (the Bot Chat title, `queued`, the avatar asset, the room page size, `scope: session`) are written once. `params()` is the only way to the wire, and it runs admission first. Admission covers every value rule the old allowlist enforced that the types can't express: non-empty session, bare skill name, room id format, the `--session` model value, effort level, and member uniqueness.
- New `HermesREST.swift` (main app target only) replaces `BotEndpoint`. It builds the method, path, query and JSON body for status/login/identity/ticket, Profile delete, image upload, artifact download and the push provisioning routes, and it builds the gateway `ws`/`wss` URL.
- `BotTransport.call` now takes a `HermesCall`, and every production caller uses it. `BotDashboardClient`, attachment upload and artifact download now build their requests through `HermesREST`.
- `BotClient` still owns auth, session and socket ownership. It still runs `validateDispatch` right before the socket write, and it keeps the room/setting error mapping and which calls are cancellation-safe or time out locally.
- Unchanged: wire shapes, Profile/runtime targeting, host error mapping, handshake and keepalive (#775). No compatibility adapter was left, so #824 has nothing to remove. `docs/agents/bots.md` describes the typed boundary.

**Contract.** The pin was not advanced (`HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` 0.21.5 / `ca678285`). I checked every method and param Hermex sends against `gateway-contract.openrpc.json` at that commit, and all of them exist there. One difference predates this PR and I left it alone: `connection.respond` there wants `owner` instead of `session_id`. Details are in the comment below.

## How it was tested

- New `HermesRequestTests` checks the exact wire shape of every `HermesCall` case and every `HermesREST` request, including method, URL, body, headers, cache policy and gateway URL. The expected values were copied from the call sites before the refactor. The `BotClientTests` allowlist tests were converted: rejected values are still asserted to never reach the socket, and wrong shapes now fail to compile. Test transports run `call.params()`, so caller tests also go through admission.
- Red evidence: none possible. The new tests use types that don't exist before this change. Behaviour is pinned by the caller tests' `(method, params)` assertions, which I didn't change. They passed on master CI and pass on this branch.
- `git diff --check`: clean. `scripts/test-sim <17e>`:
  - `--only HermesRequestTests --only BotClientTests`: 31 passed.
  - Full suite (the Xcode project changed), split into 3 batches: 2,689 passed, 3 skipped (existing), 1 failed. Batch A (42 classes: all Bot*, Hermes* and Hermex* classes, including `HermesAgentFixtureTests`) passed all 640 tests. The one failure is `ComposerFocusTransitionTests.testBoundBlurDuringAPopCancelsDeferredFocus`, which also fails on `origin/master` cf50deb0, both locally and in [CI](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36277248149).
- A signed Debug build was built, installed and launched on the simulator. The UI was not driven.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator, physical iPhone

1. iPhone simulator, Bots: the roster, live status, rooms and avatars load as before.
2. Open a bot's chat: history loads, the model/effort chips fill in, `/` lists skills, `@` lists files.
3. Edit a bot: its details and model list load. Save only on a test bot; the change is saved.
4. Open a group room: the log and state load. Settings > Bot connection > Check again shows host status.
5. iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) simulator: repeat steps 1–2 in split view, moving between the inbox and a chat. Each chat keeps its own history and chips.

Physical iPhone on LAN, then again on the Cloudflare tunnel, against a maintainer-owned test bot (pending for Uzair, not claimed): send a message and get a reply; steer during a turn, and queue a second message; answer an approval and a clarify; send a message in a test room and see it in the log. title: refactor(hermes): share Bot authentication and HTTP requests
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #824 (part of #700 slice 0.2, epic #713). Stacked on #826; merge after it. #826 left no compatibility adapter, so there was nothing to remove.

## What changed

**Problem.** `BotClient` and `BotDashboardClient` each made their own cookie session and signed in on their own, so every Bot screen, every reconnect and push provisioning ran status → login → identity → ticket from scratch.

**Fix.**
- New `Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift` (main app only). `HermesConnection` owns one ephemeral cookie jar, a single-flight sign-in, and the only path for Bot HTTP requests and the gateway upgrade. `HermesConnections` hands every consumer of the active server's saved connection the same one. `HermesHeaders` is the header policy.
- Sign-in reads public `/api/status` and checks install identity before the password goes out, then verifies the returned identity (Preserve #777). An omitted install id never clears the stored one. Cancelling one waiting consumer never cancels the shared sign-in.
- A signed-in 401 signs in again once, shared by every concurrent 401, then resends: the auth gate refuses `/api/*` before any handler runs. A Bot screen's delete, upload or download checks it still owns the request before each send, the resend included. A 401 from login itself signs out and stops. Transport failures and 5xx fail only their request and are never resent (Preserve #508/#791/#520).
- Provisioning keeps 120/180 s deadlines, for its steps and a sign-in it starts, on a second session sharing the jar; everything else stays 15/30 s.
- The registry holds one entry weakly, keyed by configured server + connection UUID. Another server or UUID, or a new address, username or password under the same UUID, retires the old connection: its sign-in stops and late replies throw `.stale`. Switching, signing out of or removing the server, and saving other Bot credentials or removing them, retire it at once (`AuthManager.state`, `BotConnectionStore`); a rename or install id backfill keeps it. No hostname pooling.
- Inbox, chat, creator, profile editor, rooms and provisioning share it; the connection form and dev auto-login probe unsaved credentials on an isolated one.
- The gateway upgrade is a `URLRequest` with `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: hermes-gateway-v1, hermes-gateway-ticket.<t>`; the socket factory receives it.
- `HermesHeaders` refuses transport-owned names, the names Hermes reads itself at the pin (`Origin`, `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, `X-Hermes-Session-Token`) and `Bearer`, accepts the Cloudflare Access JSON form, lets built-ins win, sends only to the connection's origin and strips on cross-origin redirects. Production passes none: no editor, storage, webui header snapshot or Keychain change.
- Artifact downloads still refuse redirects and cap at 25 MB. `docs/agents/bots.md` and `multi-server-state-isolation.md` updated. Pin not advanced; verified handlers are in the comment below.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check` clean. `scripts/test-sim` on iPhone 17e (iOS 27):

After the review fixes, `HermesConnectionTests`, `HermexPushProvisioningTests`, `BotClientTests`, `BotConnectionSetupTests`, `BotConnectionVersionTests`: 82 passed.
  - Callers `BotInboxTests`, `BotConversationTests`, `BotLifecycleTests`, `BotProfileEditorTests`, `BotRoomTests`, `BotRoomManagementTests`: 195 passed.
  - After the 2026-09-28 review fixes: `HermesConnectionTests`, `AuthManagerStateTests`, `BotClientTests`, `BotAttachmentSendingTests`, `HermexPushProvisioningTests`, `HermesRequestTests`, `BotConnectionVersionTests`: 114 passed; the other Bot classes: 246 passed, 1 skipped.
  - Full suite (project file changed), 3 batches: 3,242 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed: `ComposerFocusTransitionTests.testBoundBlurDuringAPopCancelsDeferredFocus`, which also fails on master cf50deb0 ([CI](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36277248149)).
- Red: `BotClientTests.testReconnectsReuseTheSignInAndRecoverAnExpiredSessionOnce` on the old code fails `("2") is not equal to ("1") - A reconnect reuses the stored sign-in`, then `rejected(401)`. `testOnlyProvisioningAndItsSignInGoOutOnTheLongDeadlineSession` fails `[true, false] != [false, true]` for the provisioning login on the previous head, and for install, enable and restart with `deadline: .provisioning` dropped. The other new tests can't compile against the old API. Review fixes, red on 916ed762: the closed-screen test resent `/api/profiles/old-bot` and `/api/chat/image-upload` (`("2") is not equal to ("1")`); the header test admitted `Origin`; the retirement test read `false` for server switch, sign-out, removal and credential changes.
- Signed Debug build on the simulator: Bots loaded roster, rooms and avatars over the new upgrade against the 0.21.5 host (read-only).

## Manual test

1. iPhone simulator, Bots: roster, rooms and avatars load. Open a chat, go back, reopen it: it connects with no error.
2. Settings > server > Hermes connection > Check again: shows host status.
3. Bots inbox > Bot connection (gear): change the address to the same host's other route (LAN ↔ tunnel), Connect, dismiss. The inbox reconnects on the new address with no "no longer current" message. Change it back.

title: refactor(hermes): share the gateway across Bot consumers
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #825 (part of #700 slice 0.2, epic #713). Stacked on #827; merge after it. Applies the [2026-09-26 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/825#issuecomment-5850724402): no UI, copy, wire or pin change.

## What changed

**Problem.** Every Bot screen made its own socket with one `onEvent`/`onDisconnect` pair. The inbox, a chat, a room and the editor each minted a ticket and ran a handshake, and one screen's close ended its whole wire.

**Fix.**
- New `Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift` (main app only) owns the one gateway socket of a `HermesConnection`, so it has #824's server and credential lifetime; `HermesConnection.retire()` retires it.
- `BotClient` is now a per-screen handle with the same `BotTransport` API, so consumers are unchanged. `connect()` joins the open socket or waits on the one opening it: one ticket, one ready → capabilities → keepalive handshake (Preserve #775). The last screen to leave closes it, so backgrounding still does.
- A reply settles only its caller. Events and server requests go to every attached screen, and each keeps its admission check (chat by runtime, inbox by `sessions.changed`). The gateway never answers a server request.
- `close()`, or cancelling a call with an unknown outcome, ends only that screen's calls, uploads, downloads and callbacks. A required call past its deadline ends only its screen, which hears `.transport` once. A lost socket (read or send failure, 45 s of silence) tells each attached screen once, and later signals from it are dropped by generation. Retirement reports `.stale` and refuses reconnects.
- Setup and dev auto-login still probe on an isolated connection; push provisioning stays HTTP-only. `docs/agents/bots.md` and `multi-server-state-isolation.md` updated. Host behavior this relies on is in the comment below.

## How it was tested

The other `HermesGatewayTests` can't compile against the old API.
- Signed Debug build (read-only): the Bots inbox loaded roster, rooms and avatars; opening a room and going back left the inbox live.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator, physical iPhone

1. iPhone simulator: inbox → chat → bot profile editor → back → back, then reopen the chat. No reconnect message at any step; the chat shows its history once, nothing duplicated or missing.

title: fix(bots): send connection.respond with the 0.21.5 owner field
body:
## Problem and outcome

The Bot connection card (approve a connector row, or Continue without it) sends `connection.respond` with a top-level `session_id`. hermes-agent 0.21.5, our pinned `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`, replaced that field with `owner: {type: "session", session_id}` and rejects extra fields. So the card's answer probably fails on 0.21.5 hosts. After the fix, answering a connection card works on the pinned host again.

## Evidence

- Upstream contract (`apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`, `ConnectionRespondParams`):
  - 0.21.4 (`d337b736`): properties `session_id, op_id, result, profile`; required `session_id, op_id, result`; `additionalProperties: false`.
  - 0.21.5 pin (`ca678285`): properties `owner, op_id, result, profile`; required `owner, op_id, result`; `additionalProperties: false`. `SessionOwner` is `{type: "session", session_id}`, both required.
  - The change came in upstream `70f5dc5f` ("connect an app without a chat session", #115191).
- The app still sends `session_id`: `HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift:436` on master (`validateConnectionCall` requires exactly `session_id, op_id, result`). The pin moved to 0.21.5 in #798 without this method changing.
- After #826 merges, the payload is built in `HermesCall.connectionRespond(sessionID:opID:answer:)` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift`). Callers: `BotConversation.swift` Continue and row-answer paths.

Found during #823 (see [#826 implementation notes](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/826#issuecomment-5851415843)). It predates that PR, which kept the wire format unchanged on purpose.

## Plan

1. Read-only first: confirm the live host's reported version (`/api/status`). No writes and no connection-card answers on the live host.
2. Build `connection.respond` params as `owner: {type: "session", session_id}` plus `op_id` and `result`, keeping the restricted `result` shapes exactly as they are.
3. Update the admission rule and its tests to the new shape.

## Acceptance and tests

- [ ] The encoded `connection.respond` payload matches the pinned schema: `owner`, `op_id`, `result`, and nothing else. A focused encoding test fails on today's code.
- [ ] Continue and row approve/skip still carry exactly the shapes they do today inside `result`.
- [ ] `BotClientTests` and the connection-card tests in `BotConversationTests` pass.
- [ ] Manual (Uzair, maintainer-owned test bot): answer a connection card on the pinned host.

## Decisions

- **Hosts older than 0.21.5?** ➡️ Follow the pin and send `owner` only. The pin is the compatibility contract and it already says 0.21.5. Instead: fall back to `session_id` when the host rejects the params. That's safe because an invalid-params rejection happens before execution, but it adds a second code path.
- **When?** ➡️ After #826 merges, so it doesn't conflict with the typed request boundary.

Blocked by #823. Surfaces: Bot chat on iPhone and iPad; no extension, widget or App Intent path.

title: fix(chat): keep a blurred composer blurred when UIKit restores focus mid-pop
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #831

## What changed

`ComposerFocusTransitionTests.testBoundBlurDuringAPopCancelsDeferredFocus` failed in about half of CI runs, and the cause is in the product, not the test. During a back navigation, #820 defers the composer's focus until the pop finishes, and a bound blur cancels that pending focus. But UIKit's own `-[UITextView _restoreFirstResponder]` can call `becomeFirstResponder` again *after* the blur, still inside the same pop. With nothing pending, that re-arms the deferred focus. The pop then finishes, the composer takes focus, and `isFocused` flips back to `true`. Whether UIKit's restore lands before or after the blur is timing, hence the flake. Temporary logging captured the late restore's stack on a failing run.

Fix: `ComposerChipTextView.wantsDeferredFocus` lets the owner say whether it still wants focus at the moment the deferred focus lands. The composer's representable answers with its bound `isFocused`, so a blur wins no matter which order the calls arrive in. Bot chat uses the same representable, so it gets the fix too. The plain editor defaults to `true`, which keeps the #820 behavior. The test now performs UIKit's late restore explicitly, so it covers the losing order every run instead of by chance.

## How it was tested

title: While dictating: keep the screen awake and lock the orientation
body:
## Use case

I dictate long messages with the composer microphone. While dictation is active I want the phone to behave the way Telegram does when it records:

- the screen never sleeps, so I can dictate without touching the phone;
- the orientation is locked, so I can move or turn the phone while speaking, without the layout flipping and without the capture being cut.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a chat, tap the composer mic, start dictating.
2. Keep talking without touching the screen → the display turns off on the auto-lock timer, the dictation ends and the text recognized so far is lost.
3. Or, while dictating, turn the phone to landscape → the dictation ends as well (the side button locking the screen does the same).

## Expected

While dictation is active: screen held awake and orientation locked, Telegram-style; rotating the device touches neither the capture nor the layout, nothing is lost.

## Actual

The capture stops as soon as the display sleeps, the screen is locked, or the device is rotated; the partial transcript is discarded.

## Environment

- Hermex 1.7 (App Store)
- iOS 27 on iPhone 17 Pro Max
- Composer mic dictation
- hermes-webui v0.52.106

title: bug(push): the default relay hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev returns Cloudflare 1027 for every request
body:
# bug(push): the default relay `hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev` returns Cloudflare 1027 for every request

**Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

Part of the push epic (#490). The relay slice is #556 (closed); the plugin slice is #555.

---

## Problem

**What the user saw.** Turning on notifications in the iOS app ends in a single failure message: **"Could not reach this Hermes host. Check the connection, then try again."** Everything before that point completes successfully:

- ✅ Installing / registering the plugin on the host
- ✅ Dashboard pairing — the app signs in and stores the returned keys
- ✅ The host connects the `hermex` platform (`✓ hermex connected`)
- ❌ The notifications step, which reports the host as unreachable

The host is in fact fine. **The default relay is disabled by Cloudflare** and answers every request with HTTP 429 / `error code: 1027`.

Error 1027 is a Cloudflare *account-level* response (Worker blocked / invocation quota exceeded), not a rate limit. It is persistent, not transient. The failure is indistinguishable from a host problem in the app because of the catch-all copy tracked in #768 (`PushRelayError.transport` / `PushRelayError.http(n)` both fall through to "Could not reach this Hermes host").

**How this was diagnosed.** The user reported the failure and the setup path was worked backwards from the iOS error: the host, the plugin, the dashboard pairing route and the platform adapter were checked first and all passed, which isolated the remaining link — the relay — and a direct `curl` of it returned the 1027 above. Reporting this because the error text actively points the user at the network between phone and host, which was never the problem.

## What I found

Reproduced from a working host (hermes-agent v0.21.5, plugin `hermex-push` enabled and paired). All checks on 2026-09-27, ~20:26 UTC:

**1. Liveness route**

```
$ curl -i https://hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev/health
HTTP/2 429
server: cloudflare
cf-ray: a41d3ecfac99efcb-ATL

error code: 1027
```

Three consecutive attempts, identical response — so not rate limiting or a transient edge.

**2. The route the plugin actually posts to** (`notify_url()`, `hermex_push/relay.py`)

```
$ curl -i -X POST \
  https://hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev/installs/<64-hex>/notify \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
HTTP/2 429

error code: 1027
```

Both the liveness route and the notify route fail the same way. Cloudflare's own site answers 200 from the same machine, so this is specific to the Worker.

**3. Everything on the host side works.** For completeness, these all pass:

- `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing` → `200` with `{relay_url, install_key, preview_key, platform, payload_version}`; the app therefore gets its keys and reports the *install* as successful.
- Keys are generated correctly under `<hermes root>/plugin-data/hermex-push/{install_key,preview_key}` (install_key 64 hex, preview_key 32 bytes, mode 0600).
- `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL` is set and `https`.
- The `hermex` platform adapter connects: `gateway.run: ✓ hermex connected`.

So the failure is isolated to the relay. **Plugin install succeeds; the host is unreachable — because the relay rejects every request.**

## Why this is user-visible as a host error

Matching the table in #768: a relay `HTTPError` (429) or a transport failure both currently render as "Could not reach this Hermes host…", which sends the user off to debug a network that is working. This is a concrete case of that mis-mapping — worth noting that fixing #768 would have pointed straight at the relay here.

## Suggested fix / what I'd like to know

1. **Is the default Worker blocked deliberately or over quota?** If it is over the free-tier request limit it should recover on the next daily reset; if the account was actioned, the default instance may need to move. Either way a `502`/`503`-style relay-unavailable response (or a documented status banner) would be far clearer than a Cloudflare 1027.
2. **Is the intended setup now self-hosting?** The root README describes `relay/` as self-hostable with Uzair running the default instance, so if the default is no longer maintained, the docs may want to lead with self-hosting and say so explicitly.
3. **If self-hosting is expected:** what is the supported path for a user whose Apple developer account is **free**? The relay needs `APNS_PRIVATE_KEY` (`.p8`, ES256/P-256) + `APNS_KEY_ID` + `APNS_TEAM_ID`, and `.p8` auth keys are only issued to paid Apple Developer Program accounts — so a free account cannot sign APNs requests at all. Additionally the relay pins `bundle_id` to `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile[.branch]` (`relay/src/contract.ts`), and a device token is only valid for the app+team that registered it, so a user-hosted Worker signing with their own key could not deliver to tokens minted for the shipped app. I would like to confirm that understanding rather than assume it — it changes whether self-hosting is a config step or a rebuild-the-app project.

## Reproduction

1. Host with hermes-agent 0.21.5 + `hermex-push` enabled, `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL=https://hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev`.
2. In the iOS app, start push setup. Plugin install/registration and dashboard pairing both succeed and the app stores the keys.
3. Continue to the notifications step → **"Could not reach this Hermes host. Check the connection, then try again."**
4. Only then, `curl` the relay's `/health` (or the plugin's notify URL) → `429` / `error code: 1027`.

Note the ordering: the app reports the failure at a step that never touches the phone↔host network path, and the host side is verifiably healthy at that moment.

## Environment

- hermes-agent **v0.21.5+2350.g32b4acf** (2026.9.24)
- Platform plugin `hermex-push` 0.1.0 (`uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, source: user), enabled in `plugins.enabled`
- Host: Arch Linux, dashboard on `hermes dashboard` with the `basic` password provider (pairing route works)
- Relay: the default `https://hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev`
- First observed 2026-09-27 ~16:07 UTC; re-confirmed ~20:26 UTC (no change)

Happy to run any further diagnostics on the host side, or to test a redeployed default instance.

title: chore(deps): build every checkout and CI run against the same Swift package versions
body:
## Linked issue

None: maintainer-approved chore from the CI/test feedback plan.

## What changed

`Package.resolved` had been gitignored since the first commit, so every checkout and every CI run resolved the newest version each package's requirement allowed. They had already drifted apart: the main checkout built swift-cmark 0.8.0 and swift-eventsource 3.3.0, while CI and newer worktrees built 0.9.0 and 3.3.1. CI could test different package code than the build on a phone, and a future package cache would have nothing stable to key on.

- The app's `Package.resolved` is now committed, pinned to exactly the versions CI resolves today, so CI's behavior doesn't change. All other `Package.resolved` files stay ignored.
- Both `xcodebuild` steps in PR CI pass `-disableAutomaticPackageResolution`, which Apple recommends for CI. A pin that no longer matches the project now fails the build instead of silently re-resolving.
- Dependabot gets a weekly `swift` entry, grouped into one PR. It has supported Xcode-managed packages since March 2026.
- CONTRIBUTING.md says where the versions come from.

Release-candidate archives also pick up the pin automatically, which makes them reproducible too.

## How it was tested

- Pin matches CI: a fresh `xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` (Xcode 27.0) wrote format version 3 with the same eight versions the latest master CI run printed under "Resolved source packages": SwiftMath 1.7.3, swift-cmark 0.9.0, Highlightr 2.3.0, Splash 0.16.0, swift-eventsource 3.3.1, swift-markdown-ui 2.4.1, NetworkImage 6.0.1, KeychainAccess 4.2.2.

title: test(kanban): count polls exactly instead of racing a 20 ms timer
body:
## Linked issue

Refs #649 (CI flakes that force reruns). No dedicated issue: maintainer-approved chore from the CI/test feedback plan.

## What changed

`KanbanLiveUpdateTests.testRepeatedFailuresFallBackToPollingWithoutRequestStorm` failed on [#829's CI](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36299451614) with `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("2") is not equal to ("1")`, even though that PR touched no Kanban code. title: chore(scripts): stop compiling a second copy of the app to launch it after tests
body:
## Linked issue

None: maintainer-approved chore from the CI/test feedback plan. Related to #817 (local build output piling up on disk).

## What changed

`scripts/test-sim` and XcodeBuildMCP built the same signed Debug app into two different folders: `~/Library/…/hermex-tests-<hash>/Build` and XcodeBuildMCP's own workspace folder. So the final app launch after a test run compiled a second copy. On this Mac, the main checkout alone held five full builds (~7.5 GB).

Both now build into the checkout's gitignored `.build/DerivedData`:
- `test-sim` passes it as `-derivedDataPath`.
- `.xcodebuildmcp/config.yaml` sets `derivedDataPath`. XcodeBuildMCP resolves the relative path against the checkout, so each worktree gets its own folder.
- A new runner test reads the config and fails if `test-sim` ever stops matching it.
- Removing a worktree now removes its build. Logs stay under `~/Library/…/hermex-tests-<hash>/runs/`.

I used `.build/DerivedData` rather than `DerivedData/`, because `DerivedData/` is where CI-style unsigned (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) builds go, and mixing those with the signed build is how the App Intents registration broke before.

The folders these tools used before are left in place; clearing them is a job for `/disk-sweep`.

## How it was tested

Measured on the main checkout with iPhone 17 (Xcode 27.0):

| Launch after a test run | Build time |
| --- | --- |
| Before: separate XcodeBuildMCP folder, last built 5 days earlier | 51 s |
| Before: same, right after a one-line edit (the edit compiles twice) | ≥ 28 s more than needed |
| **After:** shared folder, XcodeBuildMCP 2.7.0 `simulator build-and-run` right after `test-sim` | **12 s** (27 C files in swift-cmark plus relinks; no Swift recompiles) |
| After: launching twice in a row | 6 s, nothing compiled |

The 12 s is not zero, because the test action builds swift-cmark with coverage flags and the plain build doesn't. The next `test-sim` run after a launch pays about the same back (9–11 s build). Swapping in both directions still beats compiling a second full copy.

- The first `test-sim` run into the new folder is a one-time cold build per checkout: 107 s here.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 19 OK. The new test fails when `test-sim` points back at the old path.
- A real `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests` passed four times against the new folder, and `build-and-run` reported `derivedDataPath: …/hermex/.build/DerivedData`, then installed and launched the app.

title: fix: preserve waiting status in stale Bot Live Activities
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #813

## What changed

Add a small pure presentation helper in the existing shared AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift that takes the presented content state and Bot identity flag and supplies the stale Bot lead and action chip: only waitingForApproval and waitingForClarification use status.title and localized “Open to answer”, while other stale Bot statuses retain “Not connected” and “Open to reconnect”. Wire that helper into the Lock Screen activityText and botChips and the expanded island countsLine, preserving each surface's existing fresh/error/webui fallback semantics and existing count ordering; show the answer action in the expanded waiting line as required by acceptance. Keep the helper in the actual widget execution path, with no injected callbacks or test-only abstraction, and leave state reduction, socket lifecycle, serialization, deep links, compact island text, and stale dimming unchanged.

A Bot waiting for approval or clarification can lose its socket when the phone locks, leaving its Live Activity stale while the host still waits for the user. The Lock Screen currently gives staleness precedence over that actionable status and displays “Not connected” plus “Open to reconnect”; the expanded island repeats the misleading lead. The compact island already displays the waiting status. Issue #813 requests a widget presentation correction, retaining stale styling and existing treatment of other stale states and webui activities.

## How it was tested

Matrix over AgentRunActivityStatus.allCases × stale/fresh × Bot/webui: exactly the two stale Bot pending-input statuses select status.title and the answer action; all other stale Bot statuses select disconnected/reconnect; fresh and webui states receive no Bot override.
Both pending-input statuses retain their lead even with empty or unrelated currentActivity, an errorSummary, nil chips, or existing count chips. Confirm counts are retained and the action appears once; reconnecting removes the stale action.
Regression checks cover generic .waiting, running/tool statuses, and final/error statuses without expanding the exception. Assert presentation does not mutate isStale, timestamps, status, excerpt, or encoded state.
Existing Bot lifecycle tests continue to cover disconnect/reconnect behavior, and LiveActivityTests cover shared state/reducer regressions. Existing LocalizationCatalogTests enforce all shipped translations; no editorial-copy snapshot suite is needed.

title: feat(settings): point the tip card and Settings row at memberships
body:
## Problem

The session-list tip card (`TipJarCard`) and the Settings "Buy Uzi a coffee" row only ask for a one-time coffee and link to the main Buy Me a Coffee page. The card shows once ever: tapping it or "Not now" hides it for good.

Since the card shipped (~2026-09-25), coffees jumped (11 of 34 all-time in 4 days), but no one-time donor has given twice and only 1 of 34 became a member. Memberships were restructured on 2026-09-28 (Supporter $5 / Insider $10 / Patron $25, with yearly plans), and nothing in the app points people to them.

## Change

1. **Copy**: lead with membership ("Become a supporter") and keep coffee as a secondary link. Final copy comes from a picked mock.
2. **Link**: the primary action opens `https://buymeacoffee.com/callmeuzi/membership`. Coffee stays on `AppConfig.tipURL`.
3. **Re-show**: once per major app version, for users who dismissed the card but never opened a link. Users who opened a link never see it again. Replace the `tipJar.dismissed` bool with the major version the card was dismissed on; an existing `dismissed == true` counts as dismissed on the current major version, so nobody sees it twice on upgrade.
4. **Settings row**: same destination split (membership as primary, coffee still reachable).

## Constraints

- **No perks listed in the app.** Don't mention TestFlight, Discord or votes; the BMC page sells them. This keeps the paid TestFlight perk out of App Review's view (Guideline 2.2) and avoids 3.1.1 questions.
- The app never unlocks, badges or changes anything based on BMC status.
- Keep the existing gating (25 completed responses, share-import and rating-prompt spacing) and Reduce Motion behavior.

## Before implementation

Build 2–3 static mocks of the card (and the Settings row) and get one picked before editing `TipJarCard`.

## Tests

`TipJarPromptState` eligibility: dismissed on an older major version → eligible; dismissed on the current major version → not eligible; link opened → never eligible; migration of the old bool.

title: test(bots): cut Bot presentation test time by checking outcomes instead of reading the screen
body:
## Linked issue

None: maintainer-approved chore from the CI/test feedback plan. **The maintainer asked to review this one before it merges, because it gives up some visual coverage.**

## What changed

`BotChatPresentationTests` costs a median of ~108 s per CI run (range 65–170 s), about half of all test-case time in the suite. Almost all of it is Vision OCR: ~36 full-screen text reads per run at ~2 s each on CI. Many of those reads re-checked a decision that's already asserted directly, or read text where a stronger UIKit or model signal exists.

This PR changes only `HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests.swift`; no product code changed. OCR call sites drop from 31 to 15, and each run makes at least 18 fewer reads.

- **Two consolidations, no coverage lost:**
  - the question-card test folds into the question-field test (identical fixture)
  - the folded-reply gap-separator test folds into the "Worked for" fold test (one fixture, one read)
  - A third fold, the zero-result "No bots found" check, was reverted after review. It only checked the state where a message matched, so `testMessageQueryDoesNotShowNoBotsFoundInAllScope` stays as it was.
- **Stronger signals than OCR:**
  - **Room search target, warm and cold:** each settled paragraph mounts a real `ResponseSelectionLeafView` whose frame is the paragraph's. The tests assert that "Message 20" is inside the transcript's visible bounds, and that newer messages are built but not visible. OCR could only say "text found somewhere".
  - **Send on a working bot:** waits for the choice card's UIKit host view (its identifier is set on the view, not via the accessibility tree) to appear and then disappear. It asserts the offered choices via `busyChoices(...).filter(model.maySubmit)` and keeps the no-write checks.
  - **Room member view:** the "Message 3" leaf is visible, and the composer's label is "Message Comms".
  - **Slash panel:** the panel's scroll view appears after `/` and goes away once the argument starts. The listed skills come from `SlashSkillFormatter.matching`.
- **Model-covered reads replaced by the model value the view renders:**
  - room profile status lines → `reader.finishingStop`, `reader.foreignAuthority`
  - approval "already answered" → `requestResolution`
  - sudo card → a `.credential(.sudo)` request with its handling copy
  - bot search rows → `inbox.rows(matching:)`
  - recovered draft → no error messages
  - mention panel → the `Everyone` completion; its avatar colour bands are still checked from pixels
- **Unchanged on purpose:**
  - the two composer-pill tests, which would otherwise lose their view wiring
  - the room-management chip read, since nothing else checks that chips render
  - the OCR recognizer settings
  - the three callback waits that #844 changes

## Visual coverage given up

These are consciously given up, each with the direct assertion that still covers the decision:

- **Room transcript:** the rendered room title and sender caption. The sender is still asserted in `BotRoomTests`.
- **Send-choice card:** the rendered row titles. The row set and filtering are covered by the model check and `testBusyChoicesDropSteerWhenTheDraftHasAttachments`.
- **Room profile:** the rendered "Finishing stop…" and "Managed by another Hermes" lines.
- **Approval card:** the rendered "already answered" line.
- **Sudo card:** the rendered title, handling line, Skip button, and the absence of a Desktop hand-off. Identity rendering is still covered by the approval card read.
- **Bot search:** the rendered bot rows.
- **Recovered draft:** the composer pill as pixels.
- **Slash panel:** the row names as pixels. A view change that adds command rows while the model stays clean would no longer fail.

## How it was tested

All runs were on iPhone 17e with `scripts/test-sim`.

- **Baseline:** `--only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests` gave 41 passed, 1 skipped. The skip is the delegation accessibility-tree check, which is skipped on CI too.
- **After the change**, with `--repeat 3`: 38 passed, 1 skipped on every iteration. The count dropped by 3 at the time; restoring the zero-result test brings it to 39. The restored test and the room message search test pass together.
- **Local class time** (summed test durations): 48.0 s before; 28.8 s after one run, 16–25 s on repeats.
- **CI class time** (summed case durations from the job log): **62.3 s** in this PR's run. That's one sample. The same day's 6 unchanged runs took 83–135 s (median about 97 s), and the Sep 26–27 median was 108 s.
- **Mutation checks.** Each product change was made temporarily and then reverted:
  - Removing `proxy.scrollTo(sequence…)` fails both room-search tests.
  - Submitting directly on a working bot fails the send test (no card, a write happened, draft cleared). Never presenting the card also fails it.
  - Changing the room placeholder, or not rendering member rows, fails the room member test.
  - Also failing as expected:
    - flipping `finishingStop`
    - answered instead of already-resolved
    - renaming "Everyone"
    - a slash panel that never opens or never closes
  - **Known gap, unchanged:** removing the `pendingSequence == nil` follow guard is not caught, by these tests or by the original OCR versions. The fixture never reaches that in-between state.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation per `AGENTS.md` § Verifying: selection and results above
- [x] No server-facing model changes
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No API contract changes

title: test(chat): warm the keyboard before focus tests start their clocks
body:
## Linked issue

None: maintainer-approved chore from the CI/test feedback plan. It **corrects #840**, whose diagnosis was wrong, and replaces #844, closed unmerged.

## What changed

#840 blamed `ComposerFocusTransitionTests.testBoundBlurDuringAPopCancelsDeferredFocus`'s CI failures on runner stalls and raised its ceilings from 3 s to 30 s. The next failure waited the full 30 s ([36386999966](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/36386999966)). #844 applied the same reasoning to a Bot presentation test.

The simulator's unified log in 4 of 5 failure bundles shows what actually happens:
- A freshly cloned CI simulator boots without the keyboard daemon (`kbd`) running.
- The first test in the process to focus a text view launches it: `activating connection … com.apple.TextInput`, then `kbd` is spawned.
- When the push moves focus off the composer, UIKit blocks the app's main thread in `-[UIKeyboardTaskQueue _lockWhenReadyForMainThread]` until `kbd` answers. That took 5–30+ s on hosted runners.
- In the 30 s run, SpringBoard and the render server both timed the app out, and the main thread logged nothing from 28.3 s until `kbd` logged "Preparing keyboard for activity" at 58.1 s. The push can't animate, so no ceiling is safe.
- It never reproduces locally, because a simulator that stays booted already has `kbd` running.

The fix:
- `XCTestCase.warmUpSoftwareKeyboard()` sits next to the shared `settle` helper in `BotConversationTests.swift`. It focuses and unfocuses a throwaway `UITextView` once per process. On a fresh simulator, that's where the `kbd` wait happens.
- The only two classes that focus text views, `ComposerFocusTransitionTests` and `BotChatPresentationTests`, call it from `class setUp()`, where no clock runs. Whichever runs first pays the wait; the other gets a no-op.
- #840's ceiling comment now describes the actual cause. The three Bot presentation callback waits from #844 get the same 30 s safety net, commented as a safety net and not a fix.

## How it was tested

- **Cold keyboard on iPhone 17e.** I shut the simulator down first so `kbd` started cold. This Mac starts it in about 1 s, so the CI stall itself can't be reproduced locally, but the wait moves where expected:

  | `ComposerFocusTransitionTests` after a cold boot | First test (push/pop) |
  | --- | --- |
  | Without warm-up | 3.29 s |
  | With warm-up | 2.22 s (the class setup absorbs the difference) |

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17e> --only …/BotChatPresentationTests --only …/ComposerFocusTransitionTests --repeat 2`: 48 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the accessibility-tree test that CI also skips).
- **Pre-existing and unrelated to this change:** on the main checkout's iPhone 17 simulator, `testTranscriptComposerEditsDraftAtAccessibilitySizeWithoutSending` fails with and without this change. The editor loses focus after typing at an accessibility text size. It passes on iPhone 17e and on CI, so it looks like that device's state. I'll report it separately rather than fix it here.
- CI is the real proof. `testBoundBlur…` should stop failing, and its duration in the log should sit near the 1–2 s the later tests in the class take. I'll keep watching ordinary PR runs.

title: feat(push): offer a hermex-push plugin update from Settings
body:
## Problem

Hermex users never get hermex-push plugin updates. The app installs the plugin only when the pairing route answers 404 (`HermexPushProvisioner.enable`). After that, a paired host is never touched again. So plugin fixes reach a host only if someone runs `hermes plugins update hermex-push` in a terminal and then restarts `hermes dashboard`. Recent examples are uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#12, which cuts relay traffic, and #14, which gives markdown-free banners.

When an old plugin returns keys this build cannot use, the only hint is the failure text "This Hermes host returned pairing keys Hermex cannot use. Update the hermex-push plugin." (`HermexPushPairing.swift`). It has no action.

## Contract from the plugin

uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#15 adds `plugin_version`, a semver string such as `"0.2.0"`, to `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing`:
- It is the version of the code the dashboard process has loaded, not what is on disk.
- A missing field means older than 0.2.0.
- The on-disk version is `plugin.yaml`'s, reported per plugin as `version` by `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/hub`.
- Every merged plugin change bumps the version.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] Decode `plugin_version` tolerantly, as an optional string, in `HermexPushPlugin.pairing`, and keep it with the pairing state. A missing or unparseable value counts as older than any known version.
- [ ] Add an app constant for the newest plugin version this build knows, bumped in app releases. Compare versions numerically, not as strings.
- [ ] Settings → Notifications: when push is paired and the loaded version is older, show an "Update available" row. No launch popup. Decide in the mocks whether a one-time dismissible banner on the connection screen is also worth it.
- [ ] Tapping the row asks for confirmation, then:
  1. Re-installs with the call provisioning already uses: `installPlugin` → `POST /api/dashboard/agent-plugins/install {identifier, enable: true, force: true}`. It re-clones from `main`. The keys live in `plugin-data`, so the pairing survives.
  2. Calls `restartGateway` (`POST /api/gateway/restart`).
  3. Reads the pairing route again.
- [ ] If the new version answers, the row reads up to date. If the hub's on-disk version is new but the loaded version is still old, show "Restart Hermes to finish" with a plain instruction. The dashboard process that runs Bot turns loads plugin code only at start, and no API restarts it. Expect this to be the usual outcome today.
- [ ] The row stays in the restart-needed state until the new version answers. Check when the Notifications section appears (one pairing GET), not on every launch.
- [ ] The existing "Update the hermex-push plugin." failure offers the same action.
- [ ] UI goes through mocks first.

## Where

- `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift`: `enable`, `hostState`, `pairAfterRestart`, `message(for:)`.
- `HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotDashboardClient.swift`: `installPlugin`, `restartGateway`, `pairing`. Endpoints are in `BotProtocol.swift`.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushPairing.swift`: `HermexPushPlugin.pairing`, `installIdentifier`, failure text.
- `HermesMobile/Push/PushPairing.swift`: the stored pairing.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushSectionView.swift`: the Notifications section.
- Prior art for an update row with confirm, phases and wait-for-return: `serverUpdateNote` and `applyServerUpdate` in `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift` (hermes-webui updates).

## Notes

- Prefer the force install over `POST /api/dashboard/agent-plugins/hermex-push/update`. The update route re-clones subdirectory installs only on hermes-agent 0.21.5 and later; older versions refuse with "not a git checkout".
- Check whether `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/hub` caches its rows; `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/rescan` may be needed after an install.
- #710 slice 10.1 plans a `/capabilities` route that can later report the same loaded version. This issue doesn't need it.
- Out of scope: asking upstream hermes-agent to reload a plugin in place after an update, or to add a dashboard restart endpoint. Either would make this one tap end to end.

## Validation

- Unit tests with URLProtocol fixtures:
  - pairing with and without `plugin_version`
  - the update path succeeding
  - on-disk new but loaded old, which shows the restart instruction
  - an install failure
- Manual, on a real host running a 0.1.0 plugin: the row appears; after updating, it shows the restart step; after restarting `hermes dashboard`, it clears.

title: epic(app): send-path fixes, clearer alerts, edit diffs, and polish
body:
## Goal

Fix a set of bugs and add focused improvements found in a review of Hermex's iPhone and iPad experience. The bugs include a mid-run Send that can stop the agent, queued messages that are silently lost, and an alert that doesn't say which chat finished. The features include diffs for file edits and in-app links. Every item is either client-only or uses a route that exists at the pinned hermes-webui `c67fd2dd`. Each sub-issue cites the code by file and line, names its seams, and includes a plan, acceptance, tests, and surfaces, so an implementation agent can start cold.

**Relation to #713.** #713 freezes webui to bug fixes. The webui-specific items here are bug fixes (#856, #857, #875). Everything else is client-side and carries into the Hermes migration: #701 keeps `ChatViewModel`, `ChatStreamCoordinator`, and the transcript views and only swaps the transport.

## How to work this epic

1. Run it with `/hermex-batch epic 855`. Every decision is already answered below (Uzair, 2026-09-28). Each sub-issue's `## Decisions` section repeats its answers; any remaining implementation choice there carries a recommendation.
2. **Mock gates:** #864 (edit diffs), #865 (undo toast), and #871 (folded messages) need static mocks and a pick before implementation. #858 adopts the Bot composer's send-mode menu, and #868 changes the existing "Hermes is working" pill in place, so neither needs mocks.
3. **Stacks:** #856 → #857 → #858 → #872 (the send and queue path; #872 joined because it rewrites the same Send button), #862 → #863 (notifications), #868 → #869 (the run-status pill). Everything else is independent.
4. **Manual testing happens at review, on one build.** This overrides the staged mode of `needs-manual-validation` for this epic: PRs open with a numbered **Manual test** section and Uzair tests before merging. Every PR with manual steps marks `Device: physical iPhone`, so the merge walk builds one integration branch and one Branch TestFlight build for all of them.
5. **Never done by agents:** live-server mutations, relay deploys, Apple Developer portal changes, and TestFlight uploads. The merge walk runs the Branch TestFlight upload only when Uzair says "push to branch testflight".
6. One issue → one `issue/<n>-slug` branch → one PR. Agents never merge.

## Work, in order

| # | Issue | Priority | Stacks on | Mock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #856 | P1 | — | |
| 2 | #857 | P1 | #856 | |
| 3 | #858 | P2 | #857 | |
| 4 | #859 | P1 | — | |
| 5 | #860 | P1 | — | |
| 6 | #861 | P1 | — | |
| 7 | #862 | P1 | — | |
| 8 | #863 | P2 | #862 | |
| 9 | #864 | P1 | — | ✓ |
| 10 | #865 | P2 | — | ✓ |
| 11 | #866 | P2 | — | |
| 12 | #867 | P2 | — | |
| 13 | #868 | P2 | — | |
| 14 | #869 | P2 | #868 | |
| 15 | #870 | P2 | — | |
| 16 | #871 | P3 | — | ✓ |
| 17 | #872 | P3 | #858 | |
| 18 | #873 | P3 | — | |
| 19 | #874 | P3 | — | |
| 20 | #875 | P3 | — | |
| 21 | #876 | P3 | — | |

## Decisions (Uzair, 2026-09-28)

### Ask: answered

| # | Issue | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | #856 | What happens when the server refuses a steer? | Never stop the run. Copy the upstream web UI: server-queued → queue it and say "Queued, sends when this run finishes"; the run already ended → send it as a normal message; anything else → keep the text in the composer and show "Couldn't steer" with Retry. |
| D2 | #856 | Staged attachments when steering? | They ride along on the steer as an attached-files note, like the web UI. |
| D3 | #857 | Queued messages when you leave a chat mid-run? | Move them back into that chat's draft. Nothing sends by itself, and the stale "Queued" notice is cleared. |
| D4 | #858 | How do you pick the send mode per message? | Tap sends with the Settings default; long-press Send opens Queue / Steer / Stop & send; the icon shows what a tap will do. Adopt the Bot composer's menu. |
| D5 | #859 | Replace the pulsing dot on session rows, or remove it? | Remove it. The coloured Working / Approval / Input label already says the same thing. |
| D6 | #862 | What do local alerts cover? | Name the chat, open it on the right server, group per chat, and also alert on failed runs. Approvals stay with the Live Activity. |
| D7 | #863 | What does the one-time offer turn on? | Push when the server can pair, otherwise local alerts. Asked once per install, sharing one "already offered" flag with #769. |
| D8 | #865 | What gets an Undo toast? | Archive only for now; the toast is reusable. |
| D9 | #866 | A setting to use the default browser instead? | No. The sheet has its own "Open in browser" button. |
| D10 | #868 | New pill design? | No. Reuse the existing "Hermes is working" pill: a static dot plus elapsed time instead of the spinner. |
| D11 | #869 | What shows while offline? | A calm "Waiting for network" state instead of retries that end in an error. |
| D12 | #872 | Which composer polish? | The Send/Stop icon morph, a haptic on autocomplete picks, and a shorter composer in landscape. |
| D13 | #873 | Which transcript polish? | iPad reading width, an edge fade on wide tables (not code blocks, which already wrap), a one-shot entrance for live tool rows, and a "Forked from" row. |
| D14 | #874 | Push checks in Settings? | A test-notification button only. |
| D15 | #876 | Which session-list fixes? | Multi-word search, "2m ago" labels that stay current, and ⌘1–9 / ⌃Tab chat shortcuts on iPad. |
| D16 | all | When does manual testing happen? | At review, all together, in one Branch TestFlight build (see How to work, step 4). |

### Batch run answers (Uzair, 2026-09-28)

Asked in the `/hermex-batch epic 855` run; every recommendation accepted. Each issue's `Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-28)` comment carries its full answer.

| # | Issue | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| D17 | #872 | Stack on #858? | Yes. Both rewrite the Send button; the Send/Stop morph returns to the default mode's glyph. |
| D18 | #862 | Alert on runs that end failed without an error event (stale stream, dropped connection)? | Yes, matching the Live Activity's "Response failed". |
| D19 | #870 | The acceptance trace needs a streamed reply (a live-server write). | Agents record only the Session Open trace in the simulator; Uzair captures Stream Batch Apply at review. |
| D20 | #871 | Text selection while folded (device gate). | Keep selection on; if a simulator selection Copy gives only the visible lines, turn it off while folded. |
| D21 | #873 | Tool rows fading in again on stream replay? | No: check in the simulator and turn the entrance off during replay if they do. |
| D22 | #876 | iPadOS may swallow ⌃Tab. | Ship ⌃Tab and the ⌘⇧[ / ⌘⇧] fallback; the manual test checks both on iPad with a hardware keyboard. |
| D23 | #868 | Pill spacer at large text sizes (needs a live run to check). | Always measure with `onGeometryChange`; check it in a `#Preview` at AX5. |
| R1 | #863, #769 | #769 plans a per-connection "offered" key. | Pointer posted on #769: it reuses #863's per-install flag. |

**Design picks:** #864 A · trailing counts column ([mock](https://945zu9w8e0ol.postplan.dev)); #865 A · glass capsule above the Chat button ([mock](https://qne3lf9w61ov.postplan.dev)); #871 A · "Show more" bottom-leading ([mock](https://g9eo56she1jl.postplan.dev)).

**Defaults adopted:** listed per issue in each decision comment. The #865 toast uses "Close", not "Dismiss", whose es and ru translations mean "fire someone".

**After the run:** all PRs go into one integration branch and one Branch TestFlight build for testing (Uzair, 2026-09-28).

## Not doing

Decided against on 2026-09-28, so future reviews don't re-propose them:

- **Tool-group summaries that count calls and failures.** Not wanted; tool-row design stays with #262.
- **Tinting the context ring as it fills.**
- **File-type icons on tool rows.** The colour icons would lose the red failure tint.
- **Zooming the image viewer out of the tapped thumbnail.** It fights the existing swipe-to-dismiss.
- **Continuously animated status icons or shimmering text.** This conflicts with the no-endless-animation rule.
- **Drag-to-reorder pins and a cross-device queue.** The server has no fields for them. Read state is different: webui has none, but Hermes keeps unread state on the server, shared with Desktop, and #702 owns it on Hermes.

title: fix(chat): a refused steer must not stop the run
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Steer is the default "Send While Responding" choice (`HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:694-696`, `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:267`). When the server refuses a steer, Hermex stops the user's run.

- `steerResponseFromSlashCommand` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:2884-2913`) posts `/api/chat/steer`. On anything but `accepted == true`, or on a thrown error, it puts the message at the back of the queue and calls `cancelActiveStream()` (`:2910-2911`).
- The cancel route answers `ok: true` for any visible stream (pinned `api/routes.py:13281-13294`). The coordinator then finishes the stream as cancelled (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:278-288`), and `finishStream` drains the queue (`:1040` → `ChatViewModel.swift:5412-5439`), which sends the message as a new turn. The user asked to steer and got Stop-and-send.
- The notice "Steer was unavailable, so the message was queued and the current response was stopped." (`ChatViewModel.swift:2912`) shows even when the cancel failed.
- `cancelActiveStream()` clears `lastError` (`ChatViewModel.swift:4331`). A steer network error stored at `:2907` is wiped before `ChatView` reads it, so it never reaches `onAPIError`.
- Staged attachments: an accepted steer ignores them and leaves them in the composer, with no hint that they were not sent. A refused steer pulls them into the queued message (`:2910`).

The server says the opposite: "The frontend must surface that failure without cancelling the active run" (pinned `api/streaming.py:10633-10635`). A server that runs webui's gateway chat backend refuses every steer with `gateway_steer_queued` (`api/streaming.py:10668-10683`), so on those servers every mid-run send with the default setting stops the run.

## Contract

`POST /api/chat/steer {session_id, text}` → `200 {accepted, fallback, stream_id}` (pinned `api/streaming.py:10615-10728`, route `api/routes.py:15199-15201`). Hermex already decodes all three fields in `ChatSteerResponse` (`HermesMobile/Models/ServerCatalog.swift:67-72`) through `APIClient.steerChat` (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+Chat.swift:98-104`). No new fields or routes.

`fallback` when `accepted` is false:

| `fallback` | Meaning | Pinned line |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway_steer_queued` | The run belongs to the gateway backend, so steer can't reach it | `streaming.py:10682` |
| `no_cached_agent` | No live agent for this session | `:10693` |
| `agent_lacks_steer` | Agent too old to steer | `:10698` |
| `session_not_found` | Session is gone | `:10707` |
| `not_running` | The session has no active run | `:10711` |
| `stream_dead` | The run already ended | `:10717` |
| `steer_error` | `agent.steer()` raised | `:10724` |
| `null` | `agent.steer()` returned false | `:10727` |

Plus client-side failures: network errors, and HTTP 400 for an empty `text` or `session_id`.

What the upstream web UI does (pinned `static/commands.js`, `_trySteer` at `1546-1661`). It never interrupts:
- `gateway_steer_queued`: queues the message with its files, clears the draft, toasts "Steer queued for next turn" (`1622-1639`).
- `stream_dead`: restores the draft and offers Send as a normal message (`1394`, `1448-1450`).
- Anything else, including a network error (`1596`): restores the draft, keeps files staged, toasts the reason and shows a Retry row (`1641-1660`).
- Staged files are uploaded and added to the steer text as this note (`1542`):

```
[Attached files for this steer: <paths>]
Use the file tools/read_file to inspect these documents if needed.
```

Hermex uploads files when they are staged (`PendingAttachment.path`), so the note needs no new request. Normal sends add `[Attached files: …]` through `PendingAttachment.chatMessageText` (`HermesMobile/Models/UploadResponse.swift:155-173`); reuse its path-or-name reference list.

**Carries into #701:** the gateway's `session.steer` answers `{status: "queued"}` when accepted and `{status: "rejected"}` otherwise, or errors 4002/4010 (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:2174-2203`, pinned hermes-agent `ca678285`, 0.21.5). Decision 1 models the outcome once, so #701 only changes the mapping. The "never stop the run" rule stays.

## Plan

- [ ] **Outcome.** Add a small `ChatSteerOutcome` (`delivered`, `serverQueued`, `runEnded`, `refused(reason)`) mapped next to `steerChat` (`APIClient+Chat.swift:98-104`): `accepted == true` → delivered; `gateway_steer_queued` → serverQueued; `not_running` or `stream_dead` → runEnded; everything else, including `fallback == nil`, HTTP and network errors → refused.
- [ ] **Rewrite `steerResponseFromSlashCommand`** (`ChatViewModel.swift:2884-2913`). It never calls `cancelActiveStream()`.
  - delivered: keep the echo and "Steering hint delivered." (`:2900-2904`). Remove the staged attachments that rode along and delete their durable draft copies, as `sendMessage` does (`:2447-2452`).
  - serverQueued: `enqueueQueuedSlashMessage(text, attachments: consumePendingAttachments())`. The queued send later carries real attachments, not the note. Return the notice "Queued, sends when this run finishes".
  - runEnded: queue the message at the front with its attachments, then ask the coordinator to confirm the run is over. Add one narrow coordinator method that reuses the inactive branch of `recoverStaleStream` (`ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:881-942`) and `finalizeInactiveStream` (`:1010`). `finishStream` then drains the queue (`:1040`) and the message goes out as a normal send. No notice.
  - refused: keep `lastError` for transport errors, record a "couldn't steer" state (reason, retry available), and return a result that does not consume the draft.
- [ ] **Attachment note.** If attachments are staged, append the web UI note above to the steer text. `appendLocalSteerEcho` (`ChatViewModel.swift:2919-2927`) must echo the exact text sent, so the echo still merges with the persisted steer row (`SteerMessageTests.testSteerEchoOnlyMatchesPersistedSteerRows`).
- [ ] **Keep the draft on refusal in both send paths** of `ChatView.sendDraftMessage` (`ChatView.swift:1880-1961`): the typed `/steer …` path (`:1905-1917`), which today consumes the draft even for `.unsupported`, and the mid-run path (`:1926-1940`). Add one `SlashCommandExecutionResult` case (for example `.notDelivered(reason:)`, `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/SlashCommandExecutor.swift:10-16`) that both paths treat as "show the reason, keep the draft". A typed `/steer x` stays as `/steer x`.
- [ ] **Couldn't steer + Retry.** Give `ComposerStatusView` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:4-52`) an optional trailing action and add a case to `composerStatus` (`:1025-1045`). Retry calls `sendDraftMessage` with Steer forced: add an optional behavior parameter there, which #858 reuses. Clear the state on the next send, on a draft edit, or when the run ends.
- [ ] **Strings.** Delete the "Steer was unavailable…" string and its catalog entry. Add "Couldn't steer" and "Queued, sends when this run finishes" to `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` for all 17 shipped locales (`docs/agents/i18n.md`). "Retry" is already translated.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** A refused steer never stops the run. Copy the web UI. Server-queued (`gateway_steer_queued`): queue it client-side, show "Queued, sends when this run finishes", no stop. Run already ended (`not_running`, `stream_dead`): send it as a normal new message. Anything else: keep the text and attachments in the composer and show "Couldn't steer" with Retry. The user can then pick Queue or Stop & send through `/queue`, `/interrupt`, or #858's menu.

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Staged attachments ride along on a steer as an attached-files note, like the web UI.

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Replace the misleading "…the current response was stopped" notice and keep the steer error instead of wiping it.

1. **Where the outcome is modeled.** Recommend the `ChatSteerOutcome` enum at the `APIClient` boundary. The view model switches on four cases, and #701 swaps only the mapping. Alternative: switch on raw `fallback` strings in the view model. That is one type fewer, but the gateway migration then has to edit view-model logic.
2. **How "run ended" sends.** Recommend queue-at-front plus a coordinator status check, then the normal drain. It reuses the existing finalize path and can't race a server that still holds the session. Alternative: finish the stream locally and send at once. That is faster, but `/api/chat/start` can fail if the server has not released the session yet.
3. **Reason copy.** Recommend the single line "Couldn't steer", plus the system error text (`error.localizedDescription`) only for transport errors. The server codes are internal, and eight per-code lines times 17 locales is not worth it. Alternative: per-code lines like the web UI (`static/i18n.js:308-315`).
4. **Note format.** Recommend the web UI note verbatim and unlocalized. It is agent-facing like `[Attached files: …]`, and a steer then looks the same from either client. The steer row shows the note as plain text. Alternative: Hermex's own `[Attached files: …]` suffix. The transcript already turns that suffix into chips (`HermesMobile/Models/MessageAttachment.swift:92-138`), which looks nicer, but it drops the tool hint and differs from what the web UI stores.

## Acceptance

- A refused steer never calls `/api/chat/cancel`. The run keeps streaming, and the Live Activity does not end as cancelled.
- `gateway_steer_queued`: the message and its attachments leave the composer, the pinned notice reads "Queued, sends when this run finishes", and the message is sent as a new turn after the run ends.
- `not_running` or `stream_dead`: the message is sent as a normal new message once the client confirms the run ended. No stop notice.
- Every other refusal, including network errors: text, quotes and attachments stay in the composer. The composer status shows "Couldn't steer" with Retry, and Retry steers again with what is in the composer. A typed `/steer x` stays as `/steer x`.
- A transport error still reaches `onAPIError`, so an expired login still signs the user out.
- An accepted steer with staged attachments sends the note, clears the attachment strip, deletes their durable draft copies, and shows one steer row after the run ends (no duplicate).
- The string "…the current response was stopped" is gone from the app.

## Tests

Existing classes: `ChatViewModelSendTests` (steer tests start at `HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:9102`), `SteerMessageTests`, `APIClientAgentControlTests` (`steerChat` at `:194-211`). Each new test below fails on today's code, which calls `/api/chat/cancel`, consumes the draft, or has no outcome type.

- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testRefusedSteerKeepsRunDraftAndAttachments`: steer returns `{"accepted":false,"fallback":"no_cached_agent"}`. Assert no `/api/chat/cancel` request (the mock's default branch fails the test), `activeStreamID` unchanged, attachments still staged, result is the not-delivered case.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testSteerNetworkErrorKeepsRunAndLastError`: steer throws `URLError(.notConnectedToInternet)`. Assert no cancel and `lastError` set.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testGatewaySteerQueuedQueuesWithoutStopping`: fallback `gateway_steer_queued`. Assert no cancel, the notice, then `streamEnd` → one `/api/chat/start` carrying the text and the attachment payload.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testStreamDeadSteerSendsAsNewMessage`: fallback `stream_dead`, then `/api/chat/stream/status` reports inactive. Assert no cancel and one `/api/chat/start` with the text.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testAcceptedSteerCarriesAttachmentNote`: the steer body ends with the note, the strip is empty afterwards, the durable copy is deleted, and the echo content equals the sent text.
- `APIClientAgentControlTests.testSteerOutcomeMapsEveryFallback`: table test from each fallback, `null`, and a thrown error to `ChatSteerOutcome`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/SteerMessageTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientAgentControlTests`

## Mocks

Not required: no new screen. Retry is a button on the existing composer status line, and the rest is behavior.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build)

Use the tunnel server first, then repeat step 1 on LAN.

1. Start a run that uses several tools. Mid-run, attach a small file, type "also read the attached file", tap Send (default Steer). Expected: "Steering hint delivered."; the composer and attachment strip empty; after the run, the steer row shows the text and the attached-files note once.
2. Start another long run. Turn on Airplane Mode, type "hint", tap Send. Expected: no "Response cancelled", no "…was stopped" notice; "hint" stays in the composer; the status line shows "Couldn't steer" with the network reason and Retry.
3. Turn Airplane Mode off and wait for the stream to reattach (foreground the app if needed). Expected: the run is still going. Tap Retry. Expected: "Steering hint delivered." and the composer empties.
4. During step 2, check the Lock Screen Live Activity. Expected: it stays on the running state and never shows cancelled.
5. Type `/steer x` while offline mid-run and tap Send. Expected: "Couldn't steer"; the composer still reads `/steer x`.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the composer Send button (default Steer), a typed `/steer`, and the hardware-keyboard send (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ComposerChipTextView.swift:545-552`) all reach `steerResponseFromSlashCommand`. App Intents only open new chats, and the share extension, deep links, session-list menus and Live Activity taps don't send mid-run, so they don't apply.
- **Targets:** main app and `HermesMobileTests` only.
- **Servers:** no new state. The queue lives in the chat's view model and the draft is keyed by server and session.
- **Contracts:** no new fields. The only change at the boundary is mapping the existing response to an outcome.
- **Reverse states:** a refused steer can be retried, or sent as Queue or Stop & send. A server-queued message can still be stopped with Stop or replaced with `/interrupt`.
- **Connection modes:** a refusal caused by a network error is the common tunnel case. The run keeps going and reattaches through the normal reconnect path, unchanged here.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver label on Retry, Dynamic Type in the status line, new strings for all 17 locales (RTL is text only). No animation.
- **Docs:** none. No doc in `docs/agents/` describes Sessions steer.

## Outside reach

None. Reproducing `gateway_steer_queued` on a real server needs webui configured with its gateway chat backend. The tests cover it, so no server change is needed.
