title: fix(chat): keep queued messages when leaving a chat mid-run
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** #856

## Problem

Messages queued behind a running response are lost when the user leaves the chat. The "Queued" notice then comes back anyway, so the screen says a message is waiting when it is gone.

- The queue is a private in-memory array on the view model (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:543`, element type at `:6108-6111`). The only feedback is a pinned notice, "Queued for next turn (#N)." (`:2881`), which `ChatView` pins because a run is active (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:2045-2050`).
- The view model is `@State` on `ChatView` (`ChatView.swift:402-409`). `ChatView` is pushed with `.id(session.id)` and is not cached (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:506-515`). Leaving the chat throws the view model, and its queue, away.
- `onDisappear` only flushes drafts and suspends the stream (`ChatView.swift:793-801` → `ChatViewModel.swift:4486-4488` → `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:290-300`). Suspending saves a stream snapshot that includes `pinnedLocalNotices` but not the queue (`ChatViewModel.swift:4525-4552`). The next view model restores those notices (`:4588`).
- Result: after leaving and reopening a chat mid-run, the queued text is gone, the "Queued for next turn" notice is back, and nothing is sent when the run ends.
- Queued attachments are lost too. Queuing takes them out of the composer (`consumePendingAttachments`, `ChatViewModel.swift:2880`), so `syncDraftAttachments` drops their draft records (`ChatView.swift:2264-2278`). Their durable copies become orphans that the next launch-time sweep deletes once they are 24 hours old (`HermesMobile/Persistence/ChatDraftStore.swift:815-831`).

Drafts already persist per server and session, with text, quotes and attachments (`ChatDraftKey` at `ChatDraftStore.swift:138-158`, `ChatDraft` at `:72-83`). On reopen, `hydrateDraftIfNeeded` restores the text (`ChatView.swift:2138-2170`) and `restoreDraftAttachments` re-uploads attachments from their durable copies (`:2186-2243`). The fix only has to put the queue into that draft.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

**Carries into #701:** the queue and drafts stay client-side after the transport swap. #701 submits queued messages with `prompt.submit {queued: true}`, but the Hermex-side queue that this issue parks is unchanged.

## Plan

- [ ] **Hand the queue over.** Add a view-model method that returns the queued messages (text and attachments, in queue order), empties the queue, and removes their receipt (Decision 2). A message already being drained (`isDrainingQueuedSlashMessage`, `ChatViewModel.swift:5412-5439`) is out of the queue and in flight, so leave it alone.
- [ ] **Merge rule.** Add a pure merge helper next to `ChatDraftSendReconciliation` (`ChatDraftStore.swift:108-136`) that combines the existing draft with the queued messages (Decision 1). Add a `ChatDraftStore` method that writes the merged text and the union of attachment records for one key in one step. `ChatDraftStore` is `@MainActor` with synchronous setters (`:533-600`), so the write lands even if the view is going away.
- [ ] **Park on leave.** In `ChatView`'s `onDisappear` (`ChatView.swift:793-801`), before `flushDraftsBestEffort()` and `suspendStreamForNavigation()`: take the queue; if it is not empty, write the merged draft to the store for `draftKey` (`:2103-2110`). Also set `draftMessage` to the merged text and put the queued attachments back in the composer (`ChatAttachmentCoordinator.restorePendingAttachments`, `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatAttachmentCoordinator.swift:309-312`). That covers a chat that is only covered by another screen (Files, a fork): it shows the draft on return, and its next keystroke can't overwrite the stored merge with stale composer text.
- [ ] **Receipts can't outlive the queue.** Keep queue receipts out of the stream snapshot, so a new view model never restores one (Decision 2).
- [ ] Nothing else changes on reopen. Hydration and attachment restore already handle the parked draft.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** When a chat is left with queued messages, move them into that chat's draft so the user reviews and sends them on return. Nothing sends on its own. The stale "Queued" notice is cleared.

1. **How the queue and an existing draft merge.** Recommend: queued texts in queue order, then any existing draft text last, joined by a blank line. Existing quotes stay quotes. A queued text keeps the quote formatting it already has, because quotes are folded into the text at send time (`ChatView.swift:1883-1886`). Queued attachments go after the draft's own attachments, with duplicates removed by id. Why: the order matches when things were typed, nothing is lost, and the composer holds everything. Alternative: restore only the first queued message. That is simpler but silently drops the rest.
2. **Queue receipts.** Recommend deriving the receipt from the queue instead of pinning one string per queued message. Show one line while the queue is not empty, using #856's "Queued, sends when this run finishes". It disappears when the queue drains or is parked, and never enters the snapshot. Trade-off: receipts no longer drop into the transcript when the run ends (`flushPinnedLocalNoticesToTranscript`, `ChatViewModel.swift:5389-5395`), because the sent message bubble is the real receipt. The per-message "Queued for next turn (#N)." line goes away. Alternative: tag pinned notices with a kind and filter queue receipts on park and on snapshot save. That keeps today's per-message lines but changes the snapshot model (`ActiveChatStreamSnapshot`, `ChatViewModel.swift:6039-6054`). Either way, the interrupt fallback line "…the interrupt message was queued for the next turn." (`:2943-2945`) must not survive a park.
3. **When to park.** Recommend every `onDisappear`: back, iPad sidebar switch, server switch, and pushing Files or a fork. It is the same trigger that already suspends the stream, and a suspended stream can't drain the queue anyway. Trade-off: after only opening Files mid-run, the queue comes back as a draft instead of sending by itself. Alternative: park only when the chat is really dismissed. SwiftUI has no clean "popped versus covered" signal, so that needs extra machinery.
4. **Backgrounding.** Recommend leaving it out of scope. The queue stays in memory while the app is in the background, so a kill there still loses it, as today. Parking on background would stop queued messages from sending when the run ends while the app is briefly backgrounded.

## Acceptance

- Leaving a chat mid-run with queued messages puts their text and attachments into that chat's draft. Reopening shows them in the composer, and the attachments restore from their durable copies.
- Nothing is sent when the run finishes after the chat was left.
- After returning, no "Queued" notice shows unless something is really queued again.
- An existing draft is kept and merged by Decision 1.
- A parked draft stays with its own server and session. Switching servers and back shows it only under the right one.
- Coming back from Files or a fork push shows the parked text in the composer, and typing does not lose it.

## Tests

Existing classes: `ChatViewModelSendTests` (queue tests at `HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:9207` and `:9288`; leave-and-return snapshot pattern at `:2575` and `:6162`) and `ChatDraftStoreTests`. Each new test fails on today's code: there is no hand-over API, the queue drains on stream end, and the snapshot restores the receipt.

- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testLeavingChatHandsOverQueuedMessagesInOrder`: start a stream, queue two messages (one with an attachment), take the queue. Assert both come back in order with the attachment, the queue is empty, and no receipt is shown. Then emit `streamEnd` and assert no `/api/chat/start` request.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.testReturningToChatDoesNotRestoreQueueReceipt`: queue a message, hand the queue over, suspend for navigation. A new view model restoring the snapshot shows no queue receipt.
- `ChatDraftStoreTests.testQueuedMessagesMergeIntoEmptyDraft`: two texts become one blank-line-joined draft, and the attachment records are stored.
- `ChatDraftStoreTests.testQueuedMessagesMergeBeforeExistingDraftText`: existing text goes last, existing quotes are kept, and attachments are unioned without duplicates.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatDraftStoreTests`

## Mocks

Not required: no new UI. The parked messages appear in the existing composer.

## Manual test

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. The merge and hand-over are model logic with focused tests. The `onDisappear` wiring is exercised in the implementer's required simulator pass:

1. Start a long run and queue two messages (`/queue a`, then `/queue b` with a photo attached). Go back to the session list and reopen the chat. Expected: the composer reads "a", a blank line, "b"; the photo is in the strip; no "Queued" notice; nothing sends when the run ends.
2. Type "c" in the composer, queue "d", open Files from the toolbar, come back. Expected: the composer reads "d", a blank line, "c".

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** every way to leave a chat goes through `ChatView.onDisappear`: back, iPad sidebar selection, server switch (the logged-in tree is keyed by server), Files push, fork push (`ChatView.swift:863-865`), and Archived Sessions (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/ArchivedSessionsView.swift:28`). A new chat that has become a session uses the same `ChatView` (`SessionListView.swift:1810-1824`). Queues can be filled from Send (Queue default), `/queue`, `/interrupt`'s fallback, and #856's server-queued path; all park the same way.
- **Targets:** main app and `HermesMobileTests` only.
- **Servers:** the draft key includes the server, and the parked draft is written only to the leaving chat's own key.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** a parked draft is sent, edited or cleared by the user like any draft. Deleting the session discards it with the other drafts.
- **Connection modes:** not applicable. Parking is local.
- **Native quality:** no new UI. If Decision 2 is taken, the receipt reuses #856's string, so there is no new copy here.
- **Docs:** none.

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(chat): choose Queue, Steer or Stop & send per message
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** #857

## Problem

What Send does while a response is running is a single global setting. To do something else for one message, the user has to change Settings or type a slash command. The Send button doesn't say which of the three it will do.

- Settings › "Send While Responding" is the only control (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:218-226`). `ChatView` always sends with the stored value (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1926-1931`). The default is Steer (`HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:694-696`).
- The Send button has no menu and no long-press (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:825-850`). It always draws `arrow.up` (`:847-849`) and VoiceOver always reads "Send" (`:835`), even when a tap will steer or stop the run.
- A per-message choice means typing `/queue`, `/steer` or `/interrupt` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/SlashCommandCatalog.swift:117-137`).
- The comment above the button says Send "queues mid-run" (`ChatComposerView.swift:823-824`). That is wrong: it does whatever the setting says.

Bots already solved this. On a busy bot, Send opens a small card with Steer, Queue and Interrupt (`BotSendChoiceView`, `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatComposerView.swift:644-726`, opened at `:218-231` and `:473-484`). Titles and symbols come from `BotPromptMode` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPromptMode.swift:7-33`). The card is built from shared chat pieces: `HermexKeyboardRetainingOverlay` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/CustomAttachmentPicker.swift:391`) and `HermexAttachmentMenuRow` (`:1000`). The Sessions composer already hosts that overlay for its media picker (`ChatComposerView.swift:498`).

`StreamingSendBehavior` (`AppTheme.swift:663-697`) has Settings descriptions ("Steer active response", "Stop and send", "Send after response"). It also has a `title` property whose literals are not localized and are used nowhere, and it has no symbols.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

**Carries into #701:** the menu only picks a `StreamingSendBehavior` for one message. #701 changes what each behavior calls on the gateway, not the menu.

## Plan

- [ ] **Behavior metadata** (`AppTheme.swift:663-697`). Give `StreamingSendBehavior` localized titles and a `systemImage`, reusing Bots' symbols (`BotPromptMode.swift:19-26`): Steer `arrow.turn.up.right`, Queue `text.append`, Stop and send `stop.circle`. Replace the unused `title` literals.
- [ ] **Share the card.** Move `BotSendChoiceView` (`BotChatComposerView.swift:644-726`) to `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/` as one send-choice card that works over a tiny protocol (title plus symbol) adopted by `BotPromptMode` and `StreamingSendBehavior` (Decision 1). Bots keep their call site and rules unchanged.
- [ ] **Send button** (`ChatComposerView.swift:821-850`). While a run is active and Send is showing (the draft has text or quotes):
  - draw the default behavior's symbol, and give VoiceOver the default's Settings description as the label;
  - a long-press opens the card with the existing keyboard-retaining overlay; a tap sends with the default;
  - add `.accessibilityAction(named:)` for each choice, because VoiceOver users can't long-press.
  When idle, or when the button is Stop, nothing changes. Close the card if the run ends while it is open, as Bots do (`BotChatComposerView.swift:229-231`). Fix the comment at `:823-824`.
- [ ] **Composer inputs.** Add `streamingSendBehavior` (the default, for the symbol and label) and `onSendWithBehavior: (StreamingSendBehavior) -> Void` to `MessageComposerView` (`ChatComposerView.swift:84-199`), wired from `messageComposer` (`ChatView.swift:419-581`).
- [ ] **ChatView.** Use the optional behavior parameter that #856 adds to `sendDraftMessage` (`ChatView.swift:1880-1961`). An override wins over the stored value. `streamingSendBehaviorCommandName` (`:2092-2101`) takes the resolved behavior, so the receipt matches what was chosen.
- [ ] **Attachments.** Sessions always offer all three choices. Do not use `BotPromptMode.busyChoices(hasAttachments:)` (`BotPromptMode.swift:28-33`), which hides Steer when files are staged: on Sessions, #856 sends staged files with a steer as a note.
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/agents/bots.md:512-517` describes the Bot busy chooser as "a Sessions-style native menu" whose selected action is "labeled beside a separate Stop button". The code opens the card and submits on pick. Rewrite that paragraph to describe the shared card.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** A tap sends with the Settings default. A long-press on Send while a run is active opens Queue, Steer and Stop & send. The Send icon and its VoiceOver label show what a tap will do.

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Adopt the menu from the Bots implementation. Reuse the `BotPromptMode` and `StreamingSendBehavior` titles, symbols and logic rather than designing new UI. No mocks.

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Keep #856's attachment rule. Attachments ride on a steer as a note, so Sessions keep Steer in the card when files are staged. This differs from Bots, which drop Steer then; Bots keep their rule.

1. **How to share the card.** Recommend one generic card over a two-property protocol that both enums adopt. Alternative: map `StreamingSendBehavior` onto `BotPromptMode`. That avoids a type, but shows the wrong label, because Bots' "Interrupt" means redirect.
2. **How to detect the long-press.** Recommend the composer mic's timer-based tap-versus-hold gesture (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerVoiceControls.swift:20-26, 93-140`). The repo already relies on it to stop a hold from also firing the tap, and it pairs with VoiceOver named actions the same way (`:48-57`). Alternative: SwiftUI `Menu(primaryAction:)`. That is native and the least code, but it shows a system menu instead of the Bots card.
3. **Labels and order.** Recommend Bots' order (Steer, Queue, Stop and send) and existing catalog strings: "Steer", "Queue" and "Stop and send" are already translated in all 17 locales. The button's VoiceOver label while running reuses "Steer active response", "Send after response" or "Stop and send". Alternative: a new "Stop & Send" string, which needs 17 new translations.
4. **Stop and send glyph.** `stop.circle` on the button looks close to the Stop button's `stop.fill`. Stop only shows when the draft is empty, and one is an outline and the other solid, so recommend accepting it. Alternative: keep `arrow.up` when the default is Stop and send. That is clearer next to Stop, but the icon then hides what a tap does.
5. **Discoverability.** A long-press is invisible. Recommend one footnote under the Settings picker: "Long-press Send to choose for one message." (one new string). Alternative: no footnote.

## Acceptance

- During a run, with text in the composer, the Send icon and VoiceOver label match the Settings default, and a tap does exactly that.
- A long-press opens the card with Steer, Queue and Stop and send. Picking one sends only this message that way. The Settings default does not change.
- A long-press never also sends through the tap.
- With files staged, Steer is still in the card.
- When idle, the button looks and behaves as today, and a long-press adds nothing.
- The card closes if the run ends while it is open.
- VoiceOver offers named actions for all three choices.
- Command-Return still sends with the default (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:646-650`).
- Bots behave as before.

## Tests

Existing classes: `ChatComposerSendGateTests` (`HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerSendGateTests.swift:9`) and `BotChatPresentationTests` (`HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests.swift:9`; Bots' choices are pinned at `:506-528`). The new tests fail today because the running glyph, labels and Sessions choice list don't exist.

- `ChatComposerSendGateTests.testRunningSendShowsDefaultBehaviorGlyphAndLabel`: for each behavior, a running composer with text gets that behavior's symbol and VoiceOver label; idle stays `arrow.up` and "Send".
- `ChatComposerSendGateTests.testSessionChoicesKeepSteerWithAttachments`: the Sessions choice list is Steer, Queue, Stop and send, whether or not attachments are staged.
- `BotChatPresentationTests.testBusyChoicesDropSteerWhenTheDraftHasAttachments` stays green unchanged.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerSendGateTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`

## Mocks

Not required: the maintainer chose to reuse the Bots send-choice card and its symbols, so there is no new visual design.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build). The logic has focused tests; these steps check how it looks and feels on a real phone:

1. Start a long run and type "x". Expected: the button shows the Steer arrow. Long-press it. Expected: the card opens above the button, the keyboard stays up, and nothing is sent.
2. Pick Queue. Expected: "x" is queued, not steered, and Settings still says Steer.
3. Tap Send quickly. Expected: it steers with no card.
4. Turn on VoiceOver and focus Send. Expected: the label reads "Steer active response", and the actions rotor lists Steer, Queue and Stop and send.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the composer Send button (tap, long-press, VoiceOver actions). Command-Return and typed slash commands are unchanged. The Bots composer shares the moved card with no behavior change. App Intents, the share extension, deep links and Live Activity taps don't send mid-run.
- **Targets:** main app only. The card moves within the main app. `HermesMobileTests` gets the new tests.
- **Servers:** none. The default is an app-wide `@AppStorage` value, and the per-message pick is not stored.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** a pick affects one message only. The card closes with the scrim tap or escape, as it does on Bots.
- **Connection modes:** not applicable.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver label and named actions; Dynamic Type in the reused card rows; Reduce Motion is already respected by the card (`BotChatComposerView.swift:699-720`); in RTL the card anchors to the trailing edge; light and dark mode; localization reuses existing strings, plus the footnote if Decision 5 is taken.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md:512-517`, as in the Plan.

## Outside reach

None.

title: fix(sessions): remove the streaming dot from session rows
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

A session row that is streaming shows a green dot that pulses forever, and it also shows a coloured status label on the right. The dot adds nothing and costs something.

- `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionRowView.swift:23-25` draws `ActiveSessionStreamingIndicator` whenever `isActiveStreaming(session) && !isViewingCachedData`.
- The indicator (`SessionRowView.swift:526-558`) is a green circle scaled by `.easeInOut(duration: 0.4).repeatForever(autoreverses: true)` (`:554`). It turns off under Reduce Motion, but otherwise it never stops. It is the app's only `repeatForever`.
- In every case where the dot shows, the trailing slot already shows a label. `effectiveAttentionState` (`:76-93`) returns the polled state, or falls back to `SessionRowAttentionState.resolve`, which returns `.working` for a streaming row (`:423-437`). The slot draws that label in place of the time (`:197-207`).
- The dot can contradict the label: it says "busy" while the label says Approval or Input.
- The pulse repaints while the row is on screen. On iPad the sidebar stays visible next to a live transcript, so it runs for the whole response.
- When the dot appears or disappears the row's text shifts sideways by the dot plus the 10 pt stack spacing (`:22`).

The blue unread dot uses the same leading slot, but only when there is no attention state (`:26-31`). It is not affected.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

- [ ] `SessionRowView.swift:22-32`: delete the `isActiveStreaming` branch. Keep the unread branch (`if isUnread && effectiveAttentionState == nil`).
- [ ] `SessionRowView.swift:526-558`: delete `ActiveSessionStreamingIndicator`.
- [ ] `SessionRowView.swift:372-374`: rename `streamingIndicatorTopPadding` to `unreadDotTopPadding`, since only the unread dot uses it now.
- [ ] `SessionRowView.swift:327-329`: rewrite the comment so it no longer mentions "the pulsing dot". For example: "Streaming has no badge: the trailing Working label already says it."
- [ ] Leave `SessionRowView.isActiveStreaming` alone. `SessionListViewModel`, `RatingPromptState` and `SessionRowAttentionState.resolve` still use it.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Remove the streaming dot entirely. Do not replace it with a static dot or another marker. The trailing Working, Approval or Input label is the single signal. Keep the unread dot.

1. **VoiceOver needs no change.** The dot is `accessibilityHidden` (`:535`). `accessibilityStateLabels` (`:94-129`) reads the attention state, so a streaming row still reads "Working". Recommend: leave it as it is.
2. **Unread rows still shift sideways.** They do so when the unread dot appears, which is existing behaviour and outside this issue. Recommend: leave it. The alternative is to reserve a fixed leading gutter on every row, which costs width on every row to fix a rare shift.

## Acceptance

- A streaming row shows no dot on the left and the coloured Working label on the right. The same holds for Approval and Input rows.
- A streaming row's title starts at the same x position as an idle row. Nothing shifts when a response starts or finishes.
- A finished row with a newer reply still shows the blue unread dot.
- Cached (offline) rows show neither a dot nor a label, as today.
- `grep -rn repeatForever HermesMobile` returns nothing.

## Tests

- No new test. This removes a view, and a test that checks a deleted private view is absent would be a deletion regression test, which the maintainer does not want.
- Existing tests must stay green, because they pin the behaviour that remains. `SessionRowAttentionStateTests` covers Working, Approval and Input precedence, the VoiceOver labels, and cached rows showing no state. `SessionIdentityTests` covers `isActiveStreaming` and the accessibility labels.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SessionRowAttentionStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionIdentityTests`

## Mocks

Not required: this removes a redundant marker and adds no new look. The maintainer already decided the outcome.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build)

1. Open a chat and send a prompt that runs for a while, then go back to the list. Expected: the row shows "Working" on the right, no dot on the left, and the title is aligned with the rows around it.
2. Trigger an approval, for example a command that needs approval. Expected: the row shows "Approval" and no dot.
3. Let the response finish while you stay on the list. Expected: the row switches to its time without shifting sideways. If the reply is newer than you last saw, the blue unread dot appears.
4. On iPad, or iPhone landscape with a sidebar, keep a streaming chat open in the detail pane. Expected: the sidebar row shows Working and nothing pulses.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** `SessionRowView` renders every session row. That covers the main list and iPad sidebar (`SessionListComponents.swift:624` through `SessionInteractiveRow`), the Scheduled disclosure and Scheduled screen (same component), and Archived Sessions (`Features/Settings/ArchivedSessionsView.swift:100`). All of them get the change from one edit.
- **Targets:** main app only. The Live Activity widget has its own views and is untouched.
- **Servers:** not applicable.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** not applicable.
- **Native quality:** this removes the app's only continuously repainting animation, which helps both Reduce Motion users and the GPU. VoiceOver output is unchanged. Check Dynamic Type at accessibility sizes, where the unread dot keeps its top padding. Check light and dark mode. No new strings.
- **Docs:** only the in-file comment at `SessionRowView.swift:327-329`.

## Outside reach

None.

title: fix(sessions): refresh the session list when the app returns to the foreground
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

If you leave Hermex and come back, the session list shows whatever it had when you left. Sessions created, renamed, finished or deleted in the meantime (from the web UI, a cron job, or another device) stay stale until you pull to refresh or open and close a chat.

Nothing reloads the list on foreground:

- `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:131-142`: the `scenePhase` handler records `.background`, and on the next `.active` only asks for the rating prompt.
- `HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:52-58`: on `.active` it only imports pending shares and reconciles Live Activities.
- `SessionListView.swift:318-322`: `.onAppear` calls `refreshAfterReturningIfNeeded()`, but `onAppear` does not fire on foreground.
- `SessionListView.swift:275-300`: the initial `.task` runs once per view lifetime.
- The only partial cover is the active-row poll (`SessionListView.swift:1189-1204`). iOS suspends its 3 s sleep in the background. On resume, one tick reloads the list if a visible streaming row's stream has ended (`SessionListViewModel.swift:523-551`). A list with no streaming rows never refreshes.

The Bots inbox already reopens on every activation (`Features/Bots/BotsInboxView.swift:539-542`). Issue #421 described the list as refreshing on foreground. It never did, and this issue makes that true.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract. The fix reuses the existing reads (`GET /api/sessions`, projects and profiles through `refreshSessionsAndActiveProfile`, `SessionListView.swift:1115-1122`). Under Hermes, #702 slice 2.1 moves list freshness to `sessions.changed` plus a refresh after each connect. Keep this trigger independent of transport, by calling the view's existing refresh path, so that slice inherits it.

## Plan

- [ ] `SessionListView.swift:131-142`: in the existing `.background` → `.active` branch (the one that uses `wasBackgrounded`), also call a new `refreshAfterForegroundIfNeeded()`. Keep the rating-prompt lines as they are.
- [ ] Add `refreshAfterForegroundIfNeeded()` next to `refreshAfterReturningIfNeeded()` (`:1184-1187`). It asks a small pure gate whether to refresh, then calls `refreshAfterReturningIfNeeded()`. That sets `returnRefreshID`, so the existing `.task(id: returnRefreshID)` (`:310-317`) runs `SessionListReturnRefresh.run` (`:1565-1583`). That path reloads rows, projects and the active profile, then runs one poll tick where the poll was paused. A new foreground changes the task id, which cancels any return refresh still in flight, so repeated foregrounds never stack.
- [ ] Add the gate as a pure helper beside `SessionListReturnRefresh`, for example `SessionListForegroundRefresh.shouldRefresh(didCompleteInitialLoad:isLoading:)`. It returns true only when the initial load has finished and no load is already running (`viewModel.isLoading`, set in `SessionListViewModel.swift:286-298`). It deliberately does not skip cached mode (Decision 3).
- [ ] Update the doc comment on `SessionListReturnRefresh` (`SessionListView.swift:1565-1568`). It currently says the helper runs only the refresh that `SessionListDestinationReturn` requests; it now runs on foreground too.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Reload the list when the app comes back to the foreground. Reuse the existing return-refresh path. Never stack a second load on top of one already in flight.

1. **No time throttle (recommended).** Three checks already stop wasted reloads: the `.background` → `.active` requirement ignores Control Center, Notification Center and app-switcher peeks, which only pass through `.inactive`; a reload is skipped while one is in flight; and the task id cancels a superseded refresh. The Bots inbox takes the same approach. The alternative is to skip when the last successful load finished less than about 30 s ago. That needs a `lastLoadedAt` on the view model. Add it only if large lists over a tunnel prove slow.
2. **Refresh even when a chat covers the list on iPhone (recommended).** It is simpler: one GET, and the rows are fresh when you go back. On iPad the sidebar is visible anyway. The alternative is to skip on compact width while a destination is pushed, because popping back already refreshes (`SessionListDestinationReturn`, `:1589-1612`).
3. **Reload in cached mode too (recommended).** A failed load quietly falls back to the cache with no alert (`SessionListViewModel.swift:323-354`), so a foreground reload while offline is harmless. Once the server is reachable again, it is how the list goes back to live without a pull. The alternative is to skip while cached, which leaves the user on stale cached rows until they pull to refresh.

## Acceptance

- Background Hermex, change sessions on the server (rename one, start one, delete one), then foreground. The list shows the changes within about a second, without a pull.
- Pulling down Control Center or Notification Center and dismissing it does not reload the list.
- Foregrounding while the list shows cached data tries a reload. While still offline, the cached rows and banner stay, with no new error. Once the server is reachable, the list goes live without a pull.
- Rapid background and foreground cycles run at most one list reload at a time.
- Foregrounding into a Live Activity, push or deep-link tap still opens the target chat. The reload does not change navigation.
- With two servers, a foreground reload fetches only the active server and caches rows under it.

## Tests

- `SessionNavigationStateTests` (the home of `SessionListReturnRefresh` and `SessionListDestinationReturn` tests, `HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests.swift:211-433`). Add gate tests that fail today because the helper does not exist:
  - refreshes after the initial load when live and idle;
  - skips before the initial load completes;
  - refreshes while viewing cached data;
  - skips while a load is in flight.
- The reload path itself is already covered by `testReturnToCompactListTicksOnceAfterReloadingRows` and `testReturnSkipsTheTickWhenThePollNeverPaused` in the same class.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests`

## Mocks

Not required: no visible UI change.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build)

1. On LAN, open the session list. On the Mac's web UI, rename a session and start a new chat with one message. Switch to another app for about 10 s, then return. Expected: the new title and the new chat appear without pulling.
2. Repeat through the Cloudflare tunnel, leaving Hermex in the background for more than 5 minutes (past the tunnel's idle timeout). Expected: same result, and no error banner.
3. Swipe down Control Center and dismiss it. Expected: no visible reload.
4. Add a second server and switch to it. Change something on the first server, then background and foreground. Expected: only the second server's sessions show, unchanged by the first server's edit.
5. Turn on airplane mode and pull to refresh, so the list shows cached rows and the offline banner. Background and foreground. Expected: the cached rows and banner stay, and no new error appears. Turn airplane mode off, then background and foreground again. Expected: the list goes live without a pull.
6. On iPad with a chat open in the detail pane, background and foreground. Expected: the sidebar updates and the open chat is unaffected.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** foreground is the trigger. It covers the iPhone list, the iPad sidebar, and the Scheduled screen, which reads the same view model. Share-extension handoff, Live Activity taps, push taps and deep links also foreground the app. Their routing runs as before, and the reload does not touch `navigationState`.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** `SessionListView` is rebuilt per server (`ContentView.swift:95`, `.id(server)`), and `load` caches under that server (`SessionListViewModel.swift:314-316`). A foreground reload can only hit the active server. Check this with two servers (manual step 4).
- **Contracts:** existing endpoints only. For Hermes, see the Contract section (#702 slice 2.1).
- **Reverse states:** not applicable.
- **Connection modes:** LAN and the Cloudflare tunnel after an idle period. The tunnel closes idle connections, so a failed foreground reload should fall back quietly, as `load` already does (`SessionListViewModel.swift:323-354`).
- **Native quality:** no new UI, no animation and no new strings.
- **Docs:** none. #421 is closed, so leave its body alone.

## Outside reach

None.

title: fix(privacy): declare required-reason APIs in the app and share extension
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Apple requires every bundle that calls a "required reason" API to declare it, with an approved reason, in that bundle's `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. Hermex calls three such APIs that are not declared. App Store Connect can flag missing entries on upload (ITMS-91053), and review can reject them.

**Main app.** `HermesMobile/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` declares only UserDefaults `CA92.1`. It is missing:

- **File timestamp, `C617.1`.**
  - `HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:481` and `:504` read `.contentModificationDateKey` on items in the app-group share inbox.
  - `HermesMobile/Persistence/ChatDraftAttachmentStore.swift:104` and `:111` read `.creationDateKey` on draft attachments in Application Support (directory set at `:71`).
- **UserDefaults for an app-group suite, `1C8F.1`.** `HermesMobile/AppIntents/ProfileEntity.swift:153` opens `UserDefaults(suiteName: HermesShareDraft.appGroupIdentifier)`. `CA92.1` covers only defaults private to the app.

**Share extension.** `HermesShareExtension/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` declares nothing (`NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes` is an empty array). The extension compiles `SharedDraftStore.swift`, per its Sources phase in `HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:2738-2746`: `SharedDraftStore.swift`, `ShareViewController.swift` and `ShareInputReader.swift`. `ShareViewController.swift:63` calls `HermesShareDraft.savePendingImport`, which calls `cleanTemporaryItems` (`SharedDraftStore.swift:165`), which reads `.contentModificationDateKey` (`:504`). So the extension needs File timestamp `C617.1`. None of its three files touch `UserDefaults`, so it needs no UserDefaults entry.

**Re-grep of every target.** Patterns: `creationDate`, `modificationDate`, `contentModificationDate`, `DateKey`, `attributesOfItem`, `fileModificationDate`, `stat(`, `systemUptime`, `mach_absolute_time`, `volumeAvailableCapacity`, `statfs`, `UserDefaults(suiteName`, `activeInputModes`. No other hits need an entry:

- `.fileSizeKey` (for example `HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift:181`) is not on Apple's required-reason list.
- `PHAsset.creationDate` (`Features/Chat/CustomAttachmentPicker.swift:101`, `:926`) is Photos metadata, not a file timestamp API.
- `Features/Shared/AdaptiveGlassDebugFixture.swift:16` is a `#if DEBUG` private suite, which `CA92.1` already covers.
- The `stat()` in `Models/CronRunHistory.swift:7` is a comment about the server.
- Nothing reads system boot time, disk space or the active keyboard.
- The Live Activity widget (`AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift`, `HermesDeepLink.swift`, `AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift`) and the notification service (`NotificationService.swift`, `PushPreview.swift`) call no required-reason API. They need no manifest.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

- [ ] `HermesMobile/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`:
  - Add `1C8F.1` to the existing `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults` reasons array, next to `CA92.1`.
  - Add a new `NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes` entry: `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp` with reason `C617.1`.
  - Leave `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes` (the push device ID, #665), `NSPrivacyTracking` and `NSPrivacyTrackingDomains` unchanged.
- [ ] `HermesShareExtension/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`: add one `NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes` entry, `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp` with reason `C617.1`. Change nothing else.
- [ ] Do not add manifests to `HermesLiveActivityWidget` or `HermesNotificationService`.
- [ ] Match the existing tab-indented plist formatting, so the diff shows only the new entries.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Add the missing declarations and nothing more.
- Main app: File timestamp `C617.1` and UserDefaults `1C8F.1`.
- Share extension: File timestamp `C617.1`. Add a UserDefaults entry only if the extension uses a defaults suite. Verified above: it does not.
- Validate with `plutil -lint`, plus an archive privacy report if one is feasible. No manual check.

1. **Why `C617.1`.** It covers "timestamps, size, or other metadata of files inside the app container, app group container, or the app's CloudKit container". That matches both the share inbox and the Application Support draft files. No other file-timestamp reason fits.
2. **Why `1C8F.1`.** It is the reason for defaults shared with members of the same App Group. Today only the main app reads that suite, since the widget does not compile `ProfileEntity.swift`. The suite is still an app-group suite, and the doc comment at `ProfileEntity.swift:141-143` expects out-of-process readers. Recommend `1C8F.1`. The alternative, stretching `CA92.1` to cover it, misstates what the suite is.

## Acceptance

- Both manifests pass `plutil -lint`.
- The main app manifest lists UserDefaults with `CA92.1` and `1C8F.1`, and FileTimestamp with `C617.1`. The share extension manifest lists FileTimestamp with `C617.1`.
- A Release build bundles both manifests: one in `HermesMobile.app` and one in `HermesShareExtension.appex`.
- If an archive is made, Xcode's privacy report shows these reasons for both bundles and no unexplained entries.

## Tests

- No XCTest change. This is a plist-only change with no runtime behaviour.
- Lint:
  `plutil -lint HermesMobile/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy HermesShareExtension/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`
  This is the same check `TESTFLIGHT.md:75` runs before a release.
- Read back:
  `plutil -extract NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes json -o - HermesMobile/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`
  and the same for the extension. Paste both outputs in the PR.
- Compile-only Release build (`TESTFLIGHT.md:76`):
  `xcodebuild -project HermesMobile.xcodeproj -scheme HermesMobile -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build`
  Then `find <DerivedData>/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos -name PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` should list the app's copy and the extension's copy.
- Optional: if a signed archive exists (the next Branch TestFlight archive), run Organizer › Generate Privacy Report and attach the PDF to the PR.

## Mocks

Not required: no UI.

## Manual test

Covered by the lint and build checks above; no manual check needed. The change has no runtime behaviour, and the next TestFlight upload is the real gate.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** not applicable.
- **Targets:** main app and share extension get manifest entries. The Live Activity widget and notification service were checked and need none. `HermesMobileTests` does not ship. Target membership was confirmed from the Sources phases in `project.pbxproj`: main app `:2211`, share extension `:2738`, notification service `:2748`, widget `:2757`.
- **Servers:** not applicable.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** not applicable.
- **Native quality:** not applicable. No strings, and no change to the App Store privacy label, because nothing new is collected.
- **Docs:** none required. `TESTFLIGHT.md:75` already lints both manifests. Anyone who later adds a file-timestamp or app-group-defaults call to a file the extension compiles must update both manifests.

## Outside reach

The locked third-party packages (LDSwiftEventSource, swift-markdown-ui, Splash, Highlightr, KeychainAccess, SwiftMath) own their own privacy manifests. Xcode's privacy report aggregates them, but this issue cannot change them.

title: feat(notifications): local alerts name the chat, open it, and cover failed runs
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

On a server without push, Hermex can post a local alert when a run ends while the app is in the background. Today that alert says little and goes nowhere:

- **It doesn't say which chat.** Every alert reads "Hermes response complete" / "The assistant finished responding." (`HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:519-521`). With two chats running, the user can't tell which one finished.
- **Tapping it opens the app wherever it was.** The alert carries only `session_id` (`AppTheme.swift:525-528`). The tap handler routes only when push pairings exist (`HermesMobile/Push/PushAppDelegate.swift:61`), and both routes need a relay payload: `webuiDestination` requires `source == "webui"` and an `install_hash` (`HermesMobile/Push/PushNotificationRouter.swift:14-16`), and `botDestination` requires `source == "bot"` (`:47`). The local payload has neither (`HermesMobile/Push/PushPreview.swift:29-36`), so nothing routes.
- **Alerts pile up.** Each alert gets a new identifier (session ID + a fresh UUID) and no `threadIdentifier` (`AppTheme.swift:586-598`), so Notification Center neither groups nor replaces them.
- **A failed run is silent.** Only normal completion alerts. The chat site always passes `completedNormally: true` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:2734-2740`), and the policy rejects anything else (`AppTheme.swift:502-516`). A run that ends with an error (`finishStream(ending: .failed)`, `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:829-833`) records a `.failed` outcome (`ChatViewModel.swift:5879-5890`) but posts no alert. The cold-launch reconciler also notifies only `.complete` (`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:1036-1040`).

What already works and stays as it is:

- Local alerts are skipped for push-paired servers (`AppTheme.swift:634`), because the relay covers them.
- Approvals and questions already alert through the Live Activity (`AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:57-66`, `:683-695`).
- `WebuiPushDestination(server:sessionID:)`, its `.url`, and `ContentView.handleOpenURL` → `routeWebuiPush` already open a session on the right server. They switch servers or wait for sign-in first when needed (`PushNotificationRouter.swift:65-108`, `HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:99-107`, `:151-161`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

- [ ] **Request model** (`Config/AppTheme.swift:494-529`). Replace `completedNormally: Bool` with an outcome (`.completed` / `.failed`). `ResponseCompletionNotificationRequest` gains `outcome`, `title` (chat title) and `server`. The policy allows `.completed` and `.failed`. User-stopped runs never reach it (see Decisions 3).
- [ ] **Content and identity** (`AppTheme.swift:581-605`):
  - Title: the chat title, passed through `AgentRunActivitySanitizer.sessionTitle(_:)` (`LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:341-344`). That trims the title and falls back to "Hermes session", the same way the Live Activity does.
  - Body: the existing "Response complete" / "Response failed" strings (Decisions 1).
  - `threadIdentifier` and a stable request identifier, both built from the server and the session (Decisions 2). A new alert for the same chat then replaces the previous one.
  - `userInfo`: `session_id`, `server_hash` (lowercase hex SHA-256 of `server.absoluteString`) and `source: "local"`.
- [ ] **Tap routing** (`Push/PushAppDelegate.swift:57-71`). Before the `if let pairings` guard, try a local alert. Find the configured server whose `sha256(id)` matches `server_hash` in `ServerRegistry.shared.servers`, build `WebuiPushDestination(server:sessionID:)` and call `AppIntentRouter.shared.requestDeepLink(destination.url)`. A missing server, hash or session means the tap just opens the app. Put the parser next to the request type so the payload's writer and reader stay together.
- [ ] **Failed runs in chat** (`ChatViewModel.swift:5874-5890`, `ChatView.swift:2665-2741`):
  - In `streamCoordinatorDidFinishStream`, when the recorded ending is `.failed`, bump a trigger. It fires once per run, because `finishStream` is guarded by `isTransportFinished`.
  - Alert on it just like completion does: same scene-active gate, same `server:` skip for paired servers.
  - Keep the background task open until the alert is scheduled. Today `handleActiveStreamChange` ends the task when the stream goes inactive unless a completion trigger is pending (`ChatView.swift:2669-2674`). A failure would end it before the async schedule runs. The simplest fix is one "run ended" counter (bumped on completion and on failure) that the tracker (`AppTheme.swift:535-556`) and the background-task check both read. The completion haptic keeps its own trigger.
- [ ] **Cold launch** (`AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:32-36`, `:452-481`, `:964-1041`). Add `sessionTitle` (from `state.sessionTitle`) to `OrphanedLiveActivity`. Notify for `.complete` and `.failed`, never `.cancelled`, and pass the outcome and title to `notify`. The notification keeps using the `server` the reconciler checked (`:998-1004`).
- [ ] **Settings copy** (`Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:198-202`). Keep the toggle title. Change the footnote to "Alerts when a reply finishes or fails, for servers without push notifications." Add it to `Localizable.xcstrings` in all 17 shipped languages. Remove the two catalog keys that are no longer used ("Hermes response complete", "The assistant finished responding.") with a targeted edit (`docs/agents/i18n.md` § Editing the catalog).
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md:71`: say that local alerts now cover failed runs and carry a server hash, so a tap can only open its own server. Add one sentence to `docs/agents/push.md` noting that unpaired servers get local alerts that route the same way.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- The alert title is the chat title and the body is the outcome.
- Tapping the alert opens that chat on the right server.
- Alerts are grouped per chat with `threadIdentifier`.
- Failed runs alert too, not just normal completion.
- Approvals stay with the Live Activity.

Implementation choices, with recommendations:

1. **Copy.** Recommend reusing "Response complete" and "Response failed" as the body. Both strings already exist in all 17 languages, because the Live Activity uses them (`ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:824-833`), so the alert body needs no new translations and matches the Lock Screen. Alternative: new wording such as "Finished" / "Stopped with an error", which would mean 2 new strings × 17 languages.
2. **Replace or stack alerts for the same chat.** Recommend replacing: use the stable identifier `run-alert-<first 16 hex of server_hash>-<sessionID>`. Only the latest outcome matters, and "failed, then completed after a retry" should show one alert, not two. Adding a request with a delivered request's identifier replaces that alert and alerts again. Alternative: keep a UUID per alert and rely on `threadIdentifier` grouping alone. That keeps history, but it's noise.
3. **User-stopped runs.** Recommend no alert for `.cancelled` from any source: Stop in the app (`ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:278-288`) or a `cancelled` event because someone stopped the run elsewhere (`:826-827`). The person who stopped it already knows. Alternative: alert "Response cancelled". The string exists, but it's noise.
4. **Server in `userInfo`: a hash, not the URL.** Recommend `server_hash`. iOS stores delivered alerts, and CLAUDE.md treats server URLs as credential-like. Matching a hash against the configured servers also drops taps for a server that was removed. Alternative: the raw `server.absoluteString`, which is simpler (no lookup) but writes the URL into the system's notification store.

## Acceptance

- With Response Complete Alerts on and an unpaired server, background the app during a run. When the run ends, the alert title is the chat title and the body is "Response complete" or "Response failed".
- Tapping the alert opens that chat. If another server is active, Hermex switches to the alert's server first, or waits for sign-in on it, then opens the chat.
- A second alert for the same chat replaces the first. Alerts from different chats group separately.
- A run stopped by the user produces no alert.
- A push-paired server still gets no local alert, and approvals still alert only through the Live Activity.
- A cold launch after a run that ended within the last 5 minutes alerts for complete and failed runs, never for cancelled ones.
- An alert whose server was removed opens the app without navigating.

## Tests

- `ResponseCompletionNotificationPolicyTests` (`HermesMobileTests/AppThemeTests.swift:194`): `.failed` in the background now schedules. Replace `testBlocksCancelledOrFailedCompletion` with a failed-allowed case, and add a case showing a cancelled outcome is not representable.
- `ResponseCompletionNotificationServiceTests` (`AppThemeTests.swift:249`): replace `testRequestCarriesOnlySessionIDPayload` with a test for the new `userInfo` (`session_id`, `server_hash`, `source: "local"`), the stable identifier and `threadIdentifier` (same chat on two servers → different identifiers), and the title fallback to "Hermes session".
- `PushPreviewTests` (`HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests.swift`): a local alert's `userInfo` resolves to `WebuiPushDestination(server:sessionID:)` for a configured server, with no pairings at all. An unknown hash or an empty session resolves to nil. A relay payload is not mistaken for a local one.
- `ResponseCompletionNotificationTrackerTests` (`AppThemeTests.swift:301`): a failure bump keeps the background task open until its context is consumed.
- `LiveActivityTests.testReconcilerNotifiesOnlyCompletedTerminalStateOnColdLaunch` (`HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests.swift:1131`): now expects `errored` to notify with a failed outcome, and add an `interrupted-by-user` orphan that is ended but not notified.
- `PushRegistrationTests.testLocalCompletionSuppressionFollowsServerPairingAndDisable` (`HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests.swift:13`): update the call site, and add a failed-outcome case that is also suppressed for a paired server.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseCompletionNotificationPolicyTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseCompletionNotificationServiceTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseCompletionNotificationTrackerTests --only HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests --only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests`

## Mocks

Not required: system notification chrome, with the existing localized body strings and the chat's own title. The only visible copy change is one Settings footnote.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

Setup: two configured servers, A and B, neither push-paired. Settings → Notifications → Response Complete Alerts on. After backgrounding, the app keeps a stream alive for only about 30 seconds (`ChatView.swift:2644-2647`, `:2744-2757`), so use prompts that finish within about 20 seconds.

1. On A, open a chat titled, say, "Deploy notes". Send a short prompt and lock the phone right away. Expected: one alert titled "Deploy notes" with the body "Response complete".
2. Send another prompt in the same chat and background the app. Expected: the new alert replaces the first; Notification Center shows one alert for that chat.
3. Switch to server B and background the app. Tap A's alert. Expected: Hermex switches to A and opens "Deploy notes".
4. Make a run fail: send a prompt with a model whose provider has no working key, then background the app. Expected: an alert with the chat title and the body "Response failed". Tapping it opens the chat.
5. Start a run, background the app, and stop the run from the web UI on the Mac within the window. Expected: no alert.
6. Pair server A for push and repeat step 1. Expected: no local alert; only the relay's banner.
7. Remove server B while it has a delivered alert, then tap that alert. Expected: the app opens without navigating.
8. Run step 1 with the phone in Arabic or Hebrew. Expected: the body is localized; the title is the chat title as written.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the chat completion path (`ChatView`) and cold-launch reconciliation (`ContentView.swift:40-49`), both covered. Bot chats alert through the relay and are unchanged. The tap enters through `PushAppDelegate` → `AppIntentRouter` → `ContentView.handleOpenURL`, the path deep links, App Intents and relay taps already use.
- **Targets:** main app only. `AppTheme.swift`, `PushAppDelegate.swift` and `PushNotificationRouter.swift` are app-only. `AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift` is shared with the widget, but this issue only reads its sanitizer. `HermesNotificationService` doesn't run for local notifications. The share extension is not involved.
- **Servers:** the identifier, thread and hash include the server, so the same session ID on two servers never collides. A tap only resolves against configured servers. The paired-server skip is unchanged.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** the Settings toggle turns alerts off. Stopping a run never alerts. A removed server's alert opens nothing.
- **Native quality:** the title comes from the chat. The body reuses localized strings, and one new footnote string needs all 17 languages. No animation.
- **Docs:** `multi-server-state-isolation.md:71` and `push.md`.

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(notifications): offer notifications once after the first run
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** #862

## Problem

A new user who starts a long run from the phone and switches apps never hears that it finished. Hermex doesn't tell them notifications exist:

- Local alerts are off by default (`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:6`, `Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:268`).
- Hermex asks for iOS notification permission in only two places, both inside Settings: the Response Complete Alerts toggle (`Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:196-205`, request at `:1377`) and push setup (`Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift:245-252`, request at `:247`). The provisioner is only created by `HermexPushSectionView` (`Features/Bots/HermexPushSectionView.swift:18-19`), a collapsed disclosure group in Settings (`:9`, `:23`).
- #769 offers relay push once after the first Hermes (Bot) connection, keyed per connection UUID (`push-offer-seen.<connection UUID>`). It is blocked by #700 and #706. It doesn't cover local alerts, users with no Bot connection, or the moment a run is actually in progress.

The best moment to ask is right after the first run starts from the phone. The user has just given the agent work and will want to know when it's done.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract. The push path only opens the existing Settings flow; it adds no host or relay call of its own.

## Plan

- [ ] **Policy and flag.** New file `HermesMobile/Config/NotificationOffer.swift`:
  - `NotificationOffer.hasOfferedKey = "notificationOffer.hasOffered"` (standard `UserDefaults`, per install; a bool is not credential-like).
  - A pure `NotificationOffer.decide(hasOffered:localAlertsEnabled:authorization:isPaired:canPair:) -> Offer?`, where `Offer` is `.localAlerts` or `.push`.
  - No offer when: already offered; local alerts already on; iOS permission `.denied`; or the active server is already push-paired.
  - `.push` when the build can push (`PushRegistrar.shared != nil`, `Push/PushRegistrar.swift:59-62`), the server has a saved Bot connection (`BotConnectionStore().load(server:)`, `Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:94-96`) and it isn't paired (`PushRegistrar.pairing(for:)`, `:175`). `.localAlerts` otherwise.
- [ ] **Shared enable for local alerts.** Move the body of `SettingsView.enableResponseCompletionNotifications()` (`SettingsView.swift:1361-1385`) into `ResponseCompletionNotificationService` (`Config/AppTheme.swift:608-646`) as one function. It returns whether alerts are now on, plus the status message Settings shows. Settings and the offer both call it, so the permission prompt, the `hasRequestedPermissionKey` flag (`AppTheme.swift:197`) and the toggle stay in step.
- [ ] **Hook.** In `ChatView`, where a send reports `didStart == true`: `sendStandardMessage` (`ChatView.swift:2009-2013`) and `sendVoiceNote` (`:1972-1975`). Run the policy there. If it returns an offer, set `hasOfferedKey = true` **before** showing it, so a crash or kill can't show it twice, then present it. `didStart` is true only after the server returned a stream ID (`ChatViewModel.swift:2584-2615`), so a failed send never uses up the offer. Queued, steered and slash-command sends don't count.
- [ ] **The offer.** One standard `.alert` on `ChatView`, attached off the main body chain like `.onChange(of: viewModel.latestRunOutcome)` (`ChatView.swift:1480-1484`), because the body is at the type checker's limit.
  - `.localAlerts`: **Notify Me** calls the shared enable, so iOS asks for permission if it never has and the toggle turns on. The run in flight is covered, because `ChatView` reads the preference when the run ends (`ChatView.swift:2734-2740`). **Not now** changes nothing.
  - `.push`: **Open Settings** opens Settings → Notifications with the push section expanded, where the existing confirmation, step list and failure rows run unchanged (Decisions 2). **Not now** changes nothing.
- [ ] **Open Settings at Notifications.** Add `SettingsScrollAnchor.notifications` (`SettingsView.swift:8-10`), put `.id(SettingsScrollAnchor.notifications)` on the push section (`:196`), and give `HermexPushSectionView` an `init` parameter that starts it expanded (`HermexPushSectionView.swift:9`, `:15-20`). `ChatView` is built in four places (`SessionListView.swift:509`, `:1812`, `ChatView.swift:864`, `Features/Settings/ArchivedSessionsView.swift:28`). So instead of a closure, `SessionListView` sets a small environment action that calls `selectDestination(.settings(.notifications))` (pattern at `SessionListView.swift:831`, `:1474-1477`), and every `ChatView` inherits it.
- [ ] **Strings.** Add these to `Localizable.xcstrings` in all 17 shipped languages: the alert title, the two messages and "Notify Me". "Not now" and "Open Settings" already exist.
- [ ] **Docs.** Add the new key to the Global list in `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` (next to `:71`). In `docs/agents/push.md:3-6`, note the one-time offer. Post a comment on #769 naming `NotificationOffer.hasOfferedKey` as the shared flag (Decisions 3).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- After the first successful run started from the phone, ask once: "Want a notification when it's done?"
- Offer push if the active server can pair (existing provisioning); otherwise turn on local alerts.
- Once per install.
- One "already offered" flag shared with #769, so nobody is asked twice.

Implementation choices, with recommendations:

1. **Offer UI: a standard alert, no mock.** Recommend a system `.alert` with two buttons. The system draws it, so only the copy is new. Alternative: a custom card or sheet. That's new layout, which by CLAUDE.md needs mocks and a pick first. It isn't worth it for a question asked once.
2. **Push path: open Settings, don't provision from the chat.** Recommend **Open Settings** → Settings → Notifications, expanded. Setup can install a plugin on the host and restart its gateway (`HermexPushSectionView.swift:61-67`), and its progress and failure rows only exist in that section. Running it behind a chat alert would hide both, and restarting the gateway right after the user started work is the worst timing. The user leaves the chat, but the run keeps going on the server and the chat is one tap back. Alternative: move the "push off" controls into a shared `HermexPushEnableControls` (as #769 plans) and show them in a sheet over the chat. That's more code and new UI needing mocks. Leave it to #769.
3. **Flag key and owner.** Recommend `NotificationOffer.hasOfferedKey = "notificationOffer.hasOffered"`, owned by `Config/NotificationOffer.swift`. #769 should check and set this same key rather than its own per-connection `push-offer-seen.<connection UUID>` key. The first offer either surface shows then silences the other. Alternative: keep #769's per-connection key and also check this one. But "once per install" means a single key is enough.
4. **Copy.** Recommend:
   - Title: "Want a notification when it's done?"
   - Local message: "Hermex can alert you when a reply finishes or fails while the app is in the background. You can change this in Settings → Notifications." Buttons: **Notify Me** / **Not now**.
   - Push message: "Push notifications reach this iPhone even when Hermex is closed. Setup can change your Hermes host, so it runs step by step in Settings." Buttons: **Open Settings** / **Not now**.
5. **When the permission prompt is refused.** Recommend doing nothing more. The toggle stays off and the flag stays set. iOS won't prompt again, and Settings already explains a denied permission (`SettingsView.swift:1379-1382`).

## Acceptance

- On a fresh install, the first message that starts a run shows the offer once. Later runs, other chats, relaunches and other servers never show it again.
- On a server without a Bot connection, **Notify Me** shows the iOS permission prompt (if never asked). Allowing turns on Response Complete Alerts, and the run already in flight alerts if it ends while the app is in the background.
- On a server with a Bot connection that isn't paired, **Open Settings** lands on Settings → Notifications with the push section open. Nothing reaches the host until the user confirms there.
- **Not now** changes no setting and no permission.
- No offer when local alerts are already on, the server is already paired, or iOS permission is denied.
- A send that fails, or a queued or steered message, never shows or uses up the offer.

## Tests

- `NotificationOfferTests` (new, `HermesMobileTests/`): the `decide` matrix (already offered; local alerts on; denied; paired; Bot connection and pushable build → `.push`; everything else → `.localAlerts`).
- `ResponseCompletionNotificationServiceTests` (`HermesMobileTests/AppThemeTests.swift:249`): the shared enable with `SpyResponseCompletionNotificationScheduler`. Not determined → requests once and sets the requested flag. Denied → stays off with the denied message. Authorized → on with no prompt.
- `HermexPushProvisioningTests` (`HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests.swift`): no change expected; run it to confirm the section still behaves when it starts expanded.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/NotificationOfferTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseCompletionNotificationServiceTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests`

## Mocks

Not required: a standard system alert with two buttons. Only the copy is new, and it's written out in Decisions 4. The push path opens the existing Settings section unchanged.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. Delete Hermex, install the Branch build, sign in to a server with no Bot connection, and send a message. Expected: right after the run starts, the alert "Want a notification when it's done?" with **Notify Me** / **Not now**.
2. Tap **Notify Me**, allow notifications, then lock the phone within about 20 seconds of a short run ending. Expected: the run-ended alert from #862, and Settings → Notifications shows Response Complete Alerts on.
3. Send more messages, open other chats, relaunch the app. Expected: the offer never returns.
4. Delete and reinstall. Sign in to a server that has a Bot connection and no pairing, and send a message. Expected: the push version of the alert. Tap **Open Settings**. Expected: Settings opens at Notifications with the push section expanded and "Turn on notifications…" visible. Nothing has changed on the host.
5. Reinstall once more, send a message and tap **Not now**. Expected: Settings unchanged, no iOS prompt, and no offer on later sends.
6. With VoiceOver on, repeat step 1. Expected: the title, message and both buttons are read in order. At the largest Dynamic Type size, the alert text wraps without truncation.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** text and voice sends from the chat composer. The share extension and App Intents create chats but hand off to the chat screen, so their first send also passes through this hook. Bot chats are out of scope; #769 covers the Bot connection moment. Settings stays the lasting control.
- **Targets:** main app only. Share extension, `HermesLiveActivityWidget` and `HermesNotificationService` are untouched.
- **Servers:** the flag is per install on purpose. Pairing and Bot connection are read for the active server only, so the push offer never names another server's state.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** **Not now**. The Settings toggle turns alerts back off, and "Turn off notifications…" undoes push.
- **Native quality:** system alert (VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, RTL for free). 4 new strings × 17 languages. No animation.
- **Docs:** `multi-server-state-isolation.md`, `push.md`, and a pointer comment on #769.

## Outside reach

None.
