title: perf: signposts on hot paths and a debug hitch meter
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

We can't measure the paths users feel most. When opening a chat or streaming a long reply stutters, nothing tells us which step took the time:

- The only `OSSignposter` in the app is the review diff canvas (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift:39-42`, used at `ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift:15-16`).
- There's no hitch meter, `XCTOSSignpostMetric`, `measure(`, MetricKit, open-latency or scroll benchmark. `CADisplayLink` appears only for the diff's horizontal deceleration (`ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift:112`, `:441`).
- Host CPU benchmarks exist for two pure scans (`scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans`, `scripts/benchmark-math-formatting`, sources in `scripts/benchmarks/`). They can't see SwiftUI, SwiftData or the main thread.
- The research audit already recommended native signposts on these paths before any bigger rendering work (`docs/research/t3code-mobile-adoption-audit.md:370-374`).

Debug launch switches exist but aren't written down anywhere: `--streaming-lab` (`HermesMobile/HermesMobileApp.swift:57-65`) and `--rating-prompt-eligible` (`HermesMobile/Config/RatingPromptState.swift:38-42`). Only the `HERMEX_DEV_*` sign-in variables are documented (`DEVELOPMENT.md:188-204`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

- [ ] **One signposter.** New `HermesMobile/Config/PerformanceSignposts.swift` (all builds; signposts cost almost nothing unless Instruments is recording): `let performanceSignposter = OSSignposter(subsystem: Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier ?? "HermesMobile", category: "Performance")`. The subsystem expression matches the app's existing `Logger`s and the review-diff signposter. Leave `reviewDiffSignposter` as it is.
- [ ] **Intervals.** Exactly these six names (`StaticString`). Metadata is integers only, marked `privacy: .public`:

  | Interval | Begin | End | Metadata |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `Session Open` | Session row tap: `open:` in `SessionListView.sessionRowActions` (`Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1079-1081`) | First transcript frame in `ChatView`: the first time `viewModel.messages` is non-empty, ended on the next main-queue turn so the interval includes that frame's layout; or the initial load finishing with an empty transcript (`Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1760-1770`) | `messages=%d` |
  | `Transcript Apply` | Start of `renderCachedMessagesBeforeReload` and `applyReloadedMessages` (`Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:1706`, `:1914`) | Their return | `messages=%d` |
  | `Markdown Parse` | `ChatMarkdownView.body` (`Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:405-411`): build `MarkdownContent(content)` inside the interval, then pass it to `Markdown(_: MarkdownContent)` (both are public MarkdownUI initializers) | After `MarkdownContent` is built | `chars=%d` |
  | `Stream Batch Apply` | `flushPendingStreamingContent` (`ChatViewModel.swift:806-819`) | Its return | `mutated=%d` (0/1) |
  | `Cache Read` | `CacheStore.cachedSessions` / `cachedMessages` (`Persistence/CacheStore.swift:6`, `:24`) | Their return | `rows=%d` |
  | `Cache Write` | `CacheStore.cacheSessions` / `cacheSession` / `cacheMessages` (`CacheStore.swift:61`, `:109`, `:134`) | Their return | `rows=%d` |

  `Session Open` spans two views. Keep its `OSSignpostIntervalState` in a small `@MainActor` holder keyed by session ID. The ID is used only for matching and is never emitted. A new tap first ends any open interval, so none dangle.
- [ ] **Privacy.** No prompt text, message text, titles, paths, URLs, session IDs or model names in any name or metadata. Integers only. Explain this in a comment on `performanceSignposter`.
- [ ] **Keep the benchmarks building.** Don't add signposts to files that `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` or `scripts/benchmark-math-formatting` compile on their own (`TranscriptMedia.swift`, `StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift`, `FileReference.swift`, `MarkdownMathFormatter*.swift`, `MarkdownMathSegmenter.swift`). None of the sites above are in that list. Run both scripts once to prove it.
- [ ] **Hitch meter (DEBUG only).** New `HermesMobile/Config/HitchMeter.swift`, entirely inside `#if DEBUG`:
  - A pure `HitchAccumulator` that takes `(timestamp, targetTimestamp)` pairs. It counts a hitch when a frame arrives more than half a frame late (`actual > expected × 1.5`), adds up the late time, and reports hitch ms per second, hitch count and measured Hz over a rolling 1-second window.
  - A `CADisplayLink` in `.common` run-loop mode, so it keeps measuring while a scroll view is tracking, feeds it.
  - A small overlay label in the top-leading safe area, for example `12.4 ms/s · 3 hitches · 60 Hz`, updated at most twice a second so the meter doesn't repaint every frame. It uses `Text(verbatim:)`, `.allowsHitTesting(false)` and `.accessibilityHidden(true)`.
  - Enabled only by the launch argument `--hitch-meter`: attached in the DEBUG branch at `HermesMobileApp.swift:66-70`, stopped and invalidated when the overlay disappears.
- [ ] **DEVELOPMENT.md.** Add a section "Launch arguments and profiling" after § Signing a simulator in (`DEVELOPMENT.md:188`):
  - A table: `--streaming-lab`, `--rating-prompt-eligible`, `--hitch-meter` (all DEBUG only; what each does; `xcrun simctl launch <udid> com.uzairansar.hermesmobile <arg>`), plus the `HERMEX_DEV_*` variables with a pointer to `scripts/sim-login`.
  - "Recording signposts": Product → Profile (Release), choose the Animation Hitches or Time Profiler template, add the `os_signpost` instrument, and filter by the app's subsystem and category `Performance`. The six interval names. The command-line form with `xcrun xctrace record --template 'Animation Hitches' --device <udid> --attach Hermex --output <path>` (check the flags against `xcrun xctrace help record` when writing it).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- Signpost intervals on session open (tap → first transcript frame), transcript apply, markdown parse, stream batch apply, and SwiftData cache read/write, with no prompt text, titles or URLs in names or metadata.
- A DEBUG-only on-screen hitch meter, based on a display link and enabled by a launch argument. Users never see any of it.

Implementation choices, with recommendations:

- **Docs.** Recommend documenting how to record the intervals in Instruments, plus a small launch-argument table in `DEVELOPMENT.md` covering `--hitch-meter` and the existing undocumented flags.
1. **Naming scheme.** Recommend subsystem = the bundle identifier (`Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier ?? "HermesMobile"`, like the app's loggers) and a single category `Performance` for all six intervals, with the names in the table. One filter shows everything. The Branch TestFlight app records under `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.branch` on its own. Alternative: `OSLog.Category.pointsOfInterest`. That shows up in every Instruments template without adding a track, but `Markdown Parse` fires many times per streamed reply and would crowd a lane meant for rare events.
2. **Signposts in Release.** Recommend compiling them into every build. Instruments profiles Release builds, and an idle `OSSignposter` is almost free. Alternative: DEBUG only, which would measure a build users never run.
3. **Frame rate.** Recommend not adding `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` (the app doesn't set it today). The meter reports the Hz it actually measures (`targetTimestamp − timestamp`), so a 60 Hz reading on a ProMotion phone is honest, not wrong. Changing the app's frame-rate policy is a separate decision.
4. **Tests.** Recommend testing only `HitchAccumulator`, the one piece of logic. Signposts have no behaviour to test, and an `XCTOSSignpostMetric` performance test would add a slow, noisy gate to CI. Alternative: add `measure(metrics: [XCTOSSignpostMetric(...)])` for `Session Open`. Revisit once there's a baseline worth defending.

## Acceptance

- An Instruments trace of opening a cached session and streaming one reply shows all six intervals under the app's subsystem, category `Performance`. The PR includes a screenshot of that trace as evidence.
- No signpost name or metadata contains user text, titles, paths, URLs or IDs.
- `Session Open` begins on the row tap and ends when the transcript first shows, and a second tap before the first finishes leaves no open interval.
- A DEBUG build launched with `--hitch-meter` shows the overlay; without the argument it doesn't exist. Release builds contain no hitch-meter code.
- The overlay doesn't take touches, isn't read by VoiceOver, and updates at most twice a second.
- `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` and `scripts/benchmark-math-formatting` still build and run.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` documents all three launch arguments, the `HERMEX_DEV_*` variables, and how to record the signposts.

## Tests

- `HitchMeterTests` (new, `HermesMobileTests/`, inside `#if DEBUG`), feeding synthetic timestamps to `HitchAccumulator`:
  - steady 16.67 ms frames give 0 hitches and about 60 Hz;
  - one 50 ms gap in a 60 Hz stream counts one hitch of about 33 ms;
  - samples older than one second fall out of the window;
  - an 8.33 ms target (120 Hz) uses its own threshold.

  It fails today because the type doesn't exist.
- The benchmark scripts, run as a build check: `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` and `scripts/benchmark-math-formatting`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HitchMeterTests`

## Mocks

Not required: the overlay is a DEBUG-only developer readout hidden behind a launch argument, and users never see it.

## Manual test

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. The only logic, the hitch math, is unit-tested. The signposts are proven by the Instruments screenshot the Acceptance asks for in the PR, which the implementer records on the simulator from a Release profile build. Optional for the maintainer: `xcrun simctl launch <udid> com.uzairansar.hermesmobile --hitch-meter`, scroll a long chat, and watch the readout.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** session open is measured from the session-list row tap. Deep links, App Intents and notification taps open sessions without it, and that's fine for a profiling aid. Every other interval sits in shared code that all entry points go through.
- **Targets:** main app only. The widget, share extension and `HermesNotificationService` are untouched. `HermesMobileTests` gains one DEBUG-only test class.
- **Servers:** no per-server state. Metadata never names a server.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** the meter is off unless launched with the argument.
- **Native quality:** no user-facing strings. Overlay text uses `Text(verbatim:)` so the catalog check (`ci/check_string_catalog.py`, `docs/agents/i18n.md:32-48`) ignores it. No animation; the readout is throttled.
- **Docs:** `DEVELOPMENT.md` (the new section).

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(chat): fold long user messages
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

A long user message fills the screen. When a prompt is a pasted log, a spec or a long quote, the user has to scroll past a wall of their own text to reach the reply.

- **Always full height.** The user bubble always draws its whole text, with no line limit (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MessageBubbleView.swift:301-323`). It draws `userBubbleText`, which is the full `message.content` minus the optional attachment-path marker (`:510-517`).
- **Quotes make it worse.** A quoted passage is sent as ordinary `>` Markdown text (`ComposerQuote.swift:39-52`), so long quotes make long bubbles.
- **Bots too.** Bot Chat and Bot rooms draw user messages with the same view in `textOnly` mode (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactMessageView.swift:38-44`, `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:265-273`).

There's already a similar pattern. Diff fences fold behind "Show all N lines" (`MarkdownRenderer.swift:575-600`), and they call `chatDisclosureToggled()` before toggling. That call pins the reader's scroll offset while the height changes (`ChatScrollPolicy.swift:178-191`). The Sessions transcript installs it at `ChatTranscriptView.swift:352-355`, and Bot Chat at `BotChatView.swift:146`.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

- [ ] **Pure rule** (new `UserBubbleFoldPolicy`, next to `MessageBubbleView.swift`):
  - `mayFold(text:)` is a cheap pre-filter: more than 8 hard lines, or more than about 300 characters. Short messages, which are nearly all of them, stop here and are never measured.
  - `lineCount(text:width:font:)` counts wrapped lines with TextKit (`NSLayoutManager`, or `boundingRect` divided by `font.lineHeight`) at the given width and body font.
  - `folds(lineCount:)` is true when the count is over 8. `visibleLines` is 6.
- [ ] **Measure once per width** (`MessageBubbleView.swift:85-110`, `:301-323`):
  - Only candidates from `mayFold` read their width, with one `onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self)` on the row's width. The action fires only when the width changes.
  - The text width is the row width minus `userBubbleLeadingGutter` (`:484-486`) minus the bubble's 28 pt of padding (`:308`).
  - Keep the count in `@State`, keyed by width and Dynamic Type size. Use `UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body)` for the current size.
  - Nothing is measured while scrolling.
- [ ] **Folded bubble** (`:301-323`). When folding:
  - Apply `.lineLimit(6)` to the bubble's `Text`. `ComposerChipTextLine.text` returns a single `Text`, chips included (`ComposerChipRendering.swift:316-345`), so chips just take their place in the text.
  - Lay a one-line `LinearGradient` over the bottom of the text, from clear to `userBubbleBackground` (`:488-490`). It's a solid colour, so no alpha mask or offscreen pass is needed.
  - Put a "Show more" button under the text inside the bubble. Once expanded, it reads "Show less".
  - Toggle with `chatDisclosureToggled()` then a plain state flip, with no animation, like the diff Show all (`MarkdownRenderer.swift:576-579`).
  - `@State private var isExpanded = false` lives in `MessageBubbleView`.
- [ ] **Full text stays reachable:**
  - The bubble's accessibility label stays the full text (`:318-322`).
  - The context-menu Copy still reads `message.content`.
  - Fix the comment at `:295-300`: it mentions a "Select Text" action that the bubble's menu doesn't have.
- [ ] **Strings.** Add "Show more" and "Show less" to `Localizable.xcstrings` for all 17 translated languages (`docs/agents/i18n.md`). The catalog has only a title-case "Show Less" (used by `TasksView.swift:200`). Add sentence-case keys to match the transcript's "Show all N lines".

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- User messages longer than about 8 lines show the first 6, with a fade and "Show more" / "Show less".
- Copy and text selection still use the full text.

1. **How lines are counted.** Recommend: the character pre-filter, then one TextKit count at the bubble's real width, redone only when the width or text size changes. It's exact for wrapped paragraphs, CJK and emoji, and costs nothing during scrolling. Alternative: estimate lines from the character count alone, with no measuring. That's cheaper, but it's wrong for CJK (about twice the width per character) and for wide iPad bubbles. Rejected: measuring the full text with a hidden duplicate `Text`. That doubles text layout for every long bubble in the eager transcript.
2. **Does the fold state survive leaving the chat?** Recommend: no. It's `@State` in the view. It survives scrolling, because the transcript keeps row identity. It resets when the chat is reopened or reloaded. Alternative: remember it per message. That needs storage keyed by server and session, for little gain.
3. **Skill chips and quotes.** Recommend: nothing special. Chips are inline images in the same `Text`, so `lineLimit` handles them. Quotes are plain `>` text, so they fold like any other text. The link preview card and the attachments sit outside the bubble and stay visible.
4. **Bot Chat and rooms.** Recommend: yes, for free. They use the same `userBubble` in `textOnly` mode. Bot Chat pins with its own `chatDisclosureToggled`. Rooms don't install one, so the default no-op applies.
5. **Text selection while folded.** Recommend: keep `.textSelection(.enabled)` (`:307`), and confirm on a device that its Copy gives the full string. If it gives only the visible lines, turn selection off while folded; the context-menu Copy still copies everything. Alternative: always turn selection off while folded. That's simpler, but it breaks a gesture people already use.
6. **Steer bubbles** (`MessageBubbleView.swift:116-150`). Recommend: leave them as they are. They're short hints, not prompts.

## Acceptance

- A user message of 9 or more wrapped lines shows 6 lines, a fade over the last line and "Show more". 8 lines or fewer shows in full with no button.
- "Show more" shows the full message and "Show less" folds it again. The reader's scroll position doesn't jump.
- Context-menu Copy copies the full message while folded.
- VoiceOver reads the whole message. "Show more" / "Show less" is its own button.
- Rotating, or changing Dynamic Type, re-measures: a message that now fits unfolds, and one that no longer fits folds.
- The same happens in Bot Chat and Bot rooms.
- Scrolling a long transcript does no extra text measuring (Instruments: no TextKit layout during scroll).

## Tests

- New `UserBubbleFoldPolicyTests` (each fails today because there is no rule):
  - 8 short lines don't fold; 9 do.
  - A 50-character message is never measured.
  - One 1,200-character paragraph at 300 pt with the 17 pt body font counts more than 8 lines.
  - The same text at 700 pt counts fewer lines than at 300 pt.
  - CJK text wraps to more lines than Latin text of the same character count.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/UserBubbleFoldPolicyTests`

## Mocks

Required first. Publish them with the `html-communication` skill, then stop for a pick. Show:
- Folded and expanded bubbles, including a bubble with a skill chip and one with a `>` quote.
- Light and dark, default size and AX3 Dynamic Type, and one RTL (Arabic) bubble.
- Two options for where "Show more" sits (bottom-leading inside the bubble, or bottom-trailing).

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. In a Sessions chat, send a 30-line message (paste a log). The bubble shows 6 lines, a fade and "Show more".
2. Tap "Show more": the full text shows and the screen doesn't jump. Tap "Show less": it folds again.
3. Long-press the bubble → Copy, then paste into Notes. All 30 lines are there.
4. Long-press the text itself. Whatever it copies is the full message (Decisions 5).
5. Send a 3-line message: no button.
6. Rotate to landscape. A borderline message re-evaluates (it may unfold). Rotate back.
7. Set Dynamic Type to AX3, then reopen the chat. It folds by visual lines, and the button is readable.
8. Turn on VoiceOver: the bubble reads the full message, and "Show more" is a separate button.
9. Repeat step 1 in Bot Chat.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:**
  - Sessions transcript user rows
  - Bot Chat and Bot rooms (the shared `textOnly` bubble)
  - Bot cached history uses plain `Text` rows and is unchanged.
  - No deep link, intent or extension draws user bubbles.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** view state only. Nothing is stored, so nothing can cross servers.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** Show more ↔ Show less.
- **Native quality:**
  - VoiceOver: full-text label, separate toggle.
  - Dynamic Type: re-measure on change.
  - Reduce Motion: no animation is added (instant toggle).
  - Light and dark: the fade uses the bubble colour in both schemes.
  - RTL: the vertical fade doesn't depend on direction, and the button follows the layout direction.
  - Localization: two new strings in all 17 translations.
- **Docs:** none.

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(chat): smoother Send and Stop, a tap on autocomplete, and a shorter composer in landscape
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Three small rough edges in the composer. Each is its own slice and can land in the same PR as separate commits.

**(a) Send and Stop snap.** The Sessions composer's (`MessageComposerView`) trailing circle swaps between the up arrow and the stop square with a plain `if/else`, so the icon jumps (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:838-851`). It flips often: when a run starts or ends, and when the user starts or clears a draft mid-run (`ChatComposerSendGate.showsStopButton`, `:1170-1176`). The app already morphs symbols elsewhere with `.contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .symbolEffect(.replace))` (`ChatMessageMeta.swift:143-146`, `MarkdownRenderer.swift:487-490`).

**(b) Picking an autocomplete row gives no feedback.**
- Picking a slash command, skill, sub-argument or file runs `applyCompletion` / `applyFileCompletion` with no haptic (`ChatComposerView.swift:326-356`, call sites `:417`, `:433-447`).
- The rows are `.plain` buttons (`SlashCommandAutocompleteView.swift:195`, `:209`, `:224`, `:238`, `:402`; `FilePathAutocompleteView.swift:118`), so there's no press feedback either.
- Other pickers already play `ChatHaptics.configurationSelected`, a selection tick (`ChatHaptics.swift:87-89`, used at `ChatView.swift:511`). Stop keeps its medium impact (`ChatHaptics.swift:50-52`).
- The Bot composers pick rows the same way, with no haptic (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatComposerView.swift:254-287`, `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomComposerView.swift:24-28`).

**(c) In iPhone landscape the composer eats the screen.**
- The editor grows with the text up to 160 pt (`ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:602-607`). When expanded, it's never under 72 pt (`:46`, `:73-75`).
- iPhone landscape is on (`HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist:137-142`). There the screen is about 390 pt tall, and the keyboard takes about half of it. A few lines of draft leave almost no transcript visible.
- Nothing in the app reads `verticalSizeClass`.
- All three composers share this editor (`ChatComposerView.swift:735`, `BotChatComposerView.swift:304`, `BotRoomComposerView.swift:32`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

**(a) Morph**
- [ ] `ChatComposerView.swift:838-851`: merge the Stop and Send branches into one `Image(systemName: showsStopButton ? "stop.fill" : "arrow.up")` with `.contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .symbolEffect(.replace))`. The view already reads `reduceMotion` (`:85`). The progress branch stays as it is. The button's action, label and colours don't change (`:825-836`).
- [ ] `BotRoomComposerView.swift:64`: this is already one `Image`. Add the same `.contentTransition` and an `accessibilityReduceMotion` environment read.

**(b) Haptic**
- [ ] `ChatHaptics.swift`: add `autocompleteAccepted(isEnabled:performer:)`. It emits `.selection`.
- [ ] `ChatComposerView.swift`:
  - Add `@AppStorage(AppHaptics.isEnabledKey) private var isHapticsEnabled = true`. `AppHaptics.isEnabledKey` is at `HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:190`.
  - Add a `pickCompletion(_:)` that calls `applyCompletion` and then the haptic. Use it for the five `onSelect…` closures (`:433-447`). Play it after `applyFileCompletion` for `onSelect` (`:417`) too.
  - Don't play it for `onDismiss` (`:448-450`), which also calls `applyCompletion("")`. That's why the haptic can't go inside `applyCompletion` itself.
- [ ] `BotChatComposerView.swift:259-287` (bot, file and skill picks) and `BotRoomComposerView.swift:24-28` (mention picks): add the same `@AppStorage` read and call the haptic after the draft edit.

**(c) Landscape cap**
- [ ] New pure `ComposerTextInputHeight.expanded(measured:verticalSizeClass:)`. Regular height gives `max(72, measured)`, which is today's rule. Compact height gives `72`.
- [ ] `ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:73-75`: read `@Environment(\.verticalSizeClass)` and use the rule for the expanded frame. The text view already scrolls past its frame (`:216`), and UIKit keeps the caret visible. The collapsed pill (22 pt) and the coordinator's 160 pt cap (`:607`) don't change.
- [ ] Update the comment at `:73-74` to mention the landscape cap.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- (a) The Send/Stop icon morphs. With Reduce Motion it changes instantly.
- (b) A selection haptic plays when an autocomplete item is picked, and it respects the existing haptics setting. Stop's medium impact stays.
- (c) In compact height (iPhone landscape) the composer is capped lower, so it doesn't fill the screen with the keyboard up.

1. **Morph in the Bot Chat composer.** Recommend: not in this issue. Bot Chat's Stop and Send are two separate buttons, with different actions, disabled rules and a ⌘↩ shortcut (`BotChatComposerView.swift:326`, `:442-471`). In the expanded card they even sit side by side (`:365-369`). Merging them is a real refactor, not a few lines. Alternative: merge them into one button now. That makes this issue bigger and risks the shortcut. Bot rooms do get the morph, because their button is already a single `Image` (Plan (a)).
2. **Haptic for a folder pick.** Recommend: yes, play it for folders as well as files. The user tapped a row either way. A folder pick keeps the panel open (`ChatComposerView.swift:336-342`), and the tick confirms the tap landed. Alternative: files only. That leaves a tap with no feedback.
3. **Landscape cap value.** Recommend: 72 pt, which is about 3 lines at the default text size. It's the editor's existing expanded minimum, so in landscape the editor stops growing and scrolls inside. Alternative: a 44 pt (2-line) cap. That needs a lower minimum too, and the comment at `:73-74` gives a reason for keeping 72 pt as a tap target.
4. **Bot composers and the cap.** Recommend: yes, for free. The rule lives in the shared `ComposerTextInputView`. iPad keeps regular height in every orientation, so it never changes.

## Acceptance

- (a) In a Sessions chat, starting a run morphs the arrow into the stop square. Typing mid-run morphs it back to the arrow, and clearing the draft morphs it to stop again. With Reduce Motion on, every change is instant. VoiceOver still reads "Send" or "Stop response". Bot rooms morph the same way.
- (b) Picking any slash command, skill, sub-argument or file row (Sessions), or any bot, file or skill row (Bot Chat), or any mention row (Bot rooms) plays one selection tick. It plays nothing when Settings → Haptics is off. Dismissing the panel plays nothing.
- (c) In iPhone landscape with the keyboard up, a 10-line draft keeps the editor at about 3 lines and scrolls inside it. In portrait it still grows to the old 160 pt cap. On iPad nothing changes.

## Tests

- `ChatHapticsTests`:
  - A new case: `autocompleteAccepted` plays `.selection`.
  - Add it to `testHapticsRespectEnabledSetting`, so a disabled setting plays nothing.
  - Both fail today because the function doesn't exist.
- New `ComposerTextInputHeightTests`:
  - In regular height, measured values 22, 120 and 160 give 72, 120 and 160.
  - In compact height, all three give 72.
  - A nil size class counts as regular.
  - These fail today because there is no rule.
- (a) is a view-only change. It's covered by the manual check.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatHapticsTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerTextInputHeightTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerSendGateTests`

## Mocks

Not required: these are small changes to existing controls, and each look is already decided.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. Send a message in a Sessions chat. The arrow morphs into stop. Type a letter mid-run: it morphs to the arrow. Delete it: it morphs back to stop.
2. Turn on Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Reduce Motion and repeat step 1. The icon changes instantly.
3. Type `/` and tap a command: one light tick. Type `@`, tap a folder, then a file: one tick each. Turn Hermex's haptics setting off and repeat: no ticks.
4. In Bot Chat, pick a skill after `/` and a bot after `@`: one tick each. In a Bot room, pick a mention: one tick. The room's Send/Stop morphs when a bot starts.
5. Rotate to landscape, focus the composer and paste 10 lines. The editor stays about 3 lines tall, scrolls inside, and the caret stays visible. The transcript above is still readable.
6. Rotate back to portrait: the editor grows to its usual height.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:**
  - The Sessions composer, the Bot Chat composer and the Bot room composer.
  - The hardware keyboard has no autocomplete accept key today, so there's nothing to add there.
  - The Sessions composer is `MessageComposerView` (`ChatComposerView.swift:84`). Only `ChatView` builds it (`ChatView.swift:420`), and a pending new chat opens `ChatView` (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1812`), so new chats get all three changes too. The share extension has no composer.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** none.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** the morph plays in both directions.
- **Native quality:**
  - Reduce Motion is honoured by the morph.
  - Haptics follow the app setting.
  - VoiceOver labels don't change.
  - Dynamic Type: the 72 pt landscape cap is fixed in points, like today's 160 pt cap. The editor scrolls at large text sizes.
  - Light, dark and RTL: no change.
  - Localization: no new strings.
- **Docs:** none.

## Outside reach

None.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-webui c67fd2dd.

title: feat(chat): transcript polish — iPad reading width, table edge fade, tool-row entrance, "Forked from" row
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Four small transcript gaps. Each is its own slice and gets its own commit. They can ship in one PR or be split.

**(a) Lines run too long on wide screens.**
- The transcript column is the viewport minus 32 pt (40 pt at accessibility sizes) (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:388-394`, used at `:127-128`, `:348-350`).
- The app runs on iPad (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2"`). There the chat sits in a balanced `NavigationSplitView` detail column (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:454-460`, `SessionListComponents.swift:16-25`). With the sidebar hidden, that column is the whole screen, and iPhone landscape is about 900 pt wide. Lines of 150+ characters are hard to read.
- The composer has no max width (`ChatView.swift:725-749`).
- Only a few cards cap themselves (`ClarificationRequestCard.swift:158` at 560 pt, `ApprovalRequestOverlay.swift:22` at 520 pt).
- Bot Chat and Bot rooms have the same full-width layout (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:68-142`, `:205`; `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:30`, `:110`).

**(b) Wide tables don't show that they scroll.**
- A markdown table scrolls sideways inside a plain `ScrollView(.horizontal)` with no hint (`MarkdownRenderer.swift:1411-1428`). A cut-off column looks like the whole table.
- Code blocks already have a wrap toggle (`:484-494`).
- The only edge fade in the app belongs to the composer toolbar. It's built on a pure, RTL-aware rule, `ComposerToolbarEdgeFades`, which is tested (`ChatComposerToolbarScroller.swift:3-34`, `ComposerToolbarScrollerTests`). The toolbar draws it as an alpha mask (`:78`, `:82-102`).

**(c) New tool rows pop in.**
- During a live run, the newest tool row is swapped with `ToolCallLogRowView(entry: lastEntry).id(lastEntry.id)`, with no transition (`ToolActivityGroupView.swift:42-43`).
- Message rows already get a one-shot entrance, `ChatMotion.freshRowTransition`: 0.22 s, insertion only, off under Reduce Motion (`ChatMotion.swift:48-59`, applied at `ChatTranscriptView.swift:327`, `:376-382`).

**(d) A forked chat doesn't say where it came from.**
- "Fork From Here" (`ChatMessageActions.swift:160`, `ChatViewModel.swift:4063-4106`) and `/branch` / `/fork` (`ChatViewModel.swift:3540-3562`) create a child chat and push it (`ChatView.swift:863-865`). The child looks like any other chat.
- `parentSessionId` and `relationshipType` are decoded (`HermesMobile/Models/Session.swift:220-221`, `:351-352`) and cached (`HermesMobile/Persistence/CachedSession.swift:43-44`), but no feature reads them.

## Contract

(a) to (c) are client-only.

(d) is read-only, with no new endpoint. At the webui pin (`c67fd2dd`):
- `/api/session/branch` creates the child with `parent_session_id=<source>` and `session_source="fork"` (`api/routes.py:15084-15085`).
- The list and detail JSON (`compact()`) emit `parent_session_id` only when it's set (`api/models.py:1751-1753`), and always emit `session_source` (`:1771`).
- Fork rows carry **no** `parent_title`. `parent_title` and `relationship_type: "child_session"` exist only on agent (state.db) rows (`api/agent_sessions.py:377-382`, `api/models.py:7223-7226`). Those include subagent, cron and CLI `/new` children, not just forks (`.codex-tmp/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/cli_session_mixin.py:579`, `tools/delegate_tool.py:245`, `tools/cronjob_tools.py:533`).
- The webui itself treats `session_source == "fork"` as the plain-fork signal (`api/models.py:4998`, `:5027`).

## Plan

**(a) Reading width**
- [ ] Add `ChatReadingWidth` (e.g. in `ChatTranscriptView.swift` or `HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift`) with `maximum = 768` and a pure `contentWidth(viewportWidth:horizontalPadding:)` that returns `min(max(0, viewport − 2 × padding), 768)`.
- [ ] `ChatTranscriptView.swift:392-394`: use the rule. At `:350`, change the outer `.frame(width: viewportWidth, alignment: .leading)` to `.center`, so the column is centred. The `ScrollView` stays full width, so the scroll bar stays at the screen edge and swipes in the margins still scroll.
- [ ] `ChatView.swift:740-748`: cap `composerAccessoryStack` and `messageComposer` with `.frame(maxWidth:)`. Size it so their edges line up with the transcript column (column plus the composer's own side insets). The `ZStack(alignment: .bottom)` centres them. `BottomComposerMaterialFade` stays full width.
- [ ] `BotChatView.swift:68-142` and `:205`, and `BotRoomView.swift:30` and `:110`: apply the same cap and centring to the transcript stack and the composer.
- [ ] Check, with nothing expected to change:
  - User bubbles stay trailing-aligned inside the column (`MessageBubbleView.swift:85-110`).
  - Every "jump to latest" button is a bottom-centre overlay, so it stays centred on the column (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:170-178`, `BotChatView.swift:168-171`, `BotRoomView.swift:94-96`).

**(b) Table edge fade**
- [ ] Move `ComposerToolbarEdgeFades` to a shared `HorizontalOverflowEdgeFades` (new file in `Features/Chat/`) with no change to the rule.
- [ ] Add a `horizontalOverflowFades(_ style:)` modifier. It owns the `@State` fades, the `onScrollGeometryChange` hookup (`ChatComposerToolbarScroller.swift:68-77`) and the Reduce-Motion-aware animation (`:79`). It has two styles:
  - `.mask` keeps today's toolbar look, which fades over glass.
  - `.overlay(Color)` puts an 18 pt `LinearGradient` from clear to the colour on each edge that hides content. It shows only while that edge hides something. There's no mask, so no offscreen pass while scrolling.
- [ ] `ChatComposerToolbarScroller.swift:55-80`: use `.mask`, so it looks the same as today.
- [ ] `MarkdownRenderer.swift:1419-1427`: apply `.overlay` to the table's scroll view. Read the colour from a new environment value (default `Color(.systemBackground)`, the transcript background, `ChatTranscriptView.swift:181`):
  - Memory (`List`, `HermesMobile/Features/Memory/MemoryView.swift:69`) and Kanban card detail (`.insetGrouped`, `KanbanCardDetailView.swift:112-130`) set `Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground)`.
  - Bot room bubbles use a translucent fill (`BotRoomView.swift:289`), so they set `nil`, which means no fade.
- [ ] Code blocks don't change.

**(c) Tool-row entrance**
- [ ] Add a pure `ToolActivityEntrance.animatesNewestRow(isLive:reduceMotion:)` (true only when live and motion is allowed).
- [ ] `ToolActivityGroupView.swift:42-43`: add `.transition(isLive ? ChatMotion.freshRowTransition(isUserRow: false, reduceMotion: reduceMotion) : .identity)` to the newest row.
  - The animation is attached to the transition, so it plays without `withAnimation`. Removal stays instant.
  - Row identity is the stable `presentationID` (`HermesMobile/Models/ToolCall.swift:5-6`, `ToolCallSummaryFormatter.swift:40`). A `tool.start` → `tool.complete` update of the same call doesn't replay it.
- [ ] This covers the Sessions live groups (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:445-451`, `:740-746`) and Bot Chat live groups (`BotActivityViews.swift:19`, `isLive` from `BotChatView.swift:108-111`).

**(d) "Forked from" row**
- [ ] Add a pure `ForkOrigin.resolve(session:parent:) -> ForkOrigin?` (for example in `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/`). It returns nil unless `session.sessionSource == "fork"` and `parentSessionId` is not empty (Decisions 5).
  - The title comes from the parent's `SessionRowView.displayTitle(for:)` (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionRowView.swift:44-50`), so it matches the list.
  - With no parent, the row reads "Forked from another chat".
- [ ] `HermesMobile/Persistence/CacheStore.swift`: add a `@MainActor` lookup `cachedSession(id:serverURL:in:)` built on `cachedSession(cacheKey:in:)` (`:260-269`). It includes archived and expired rows, since it's only for a label. It never crosses servers. The session list writes this cache on every load (`SessionListViewModel.swift:316`, `:1058`), so it is the "loaded list".
- [ ] `ChatView`: resolve once when the chat appears (and when `session` changes). Pass the origin and an `onOpenForkParent` callback into `ChatTranscriptView`.
  - On tap: push the cached parent `SessionSummary` with a `.navigationDestination(item:)`, like `forkedSession` (`ChatView.swift:863-865`).
  - If the parent isn't cached, fetch it with `client.session(id:includeMessages:false,messageLimit:nil)`, the call `forkFromMessage` already makes (`ChatViewModel.swift:4095-4106`), then push it.
  - If the fetch fails, show "The original chat is no longer on this server." through the existing message-action error path.
- [ ] `ChatTranscriptView.swift:261-262`: draw the row first in the stack, above the "Load older messages" button. Copy `TranscriptTurnFoldRowView`'s style (`TranscriptTurnFolding.swift:233-271`): secondary subheadline, 44 pt minimum height, hairline. Use an `arrow.triangle.branch` icon and a trailing `chevron.forward`. Make it a button with the label "Forked from <title>" and the hint "Opens the original chat."
- [ ] Strings: add "Forked from %@", "Forked from another chat", "Opens the original chat." and the error to `Localizable.xcstrings` for all 17 translated languages (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- (a) Cap the transcript and composer to a readable width (about 768 pt) and centre them on wide layouts.
- (b) Fade the edge of wide tables only, not code blocks, by pulling the existing overflow-fade rule into a shared modifier.
- (c) Tool rows that arrive live get the same one-shot entrance as messages. It never plays for history or reloads, and it's off under Reduce Motion.
- (d) A "Forked from <parent title>" row sits at the top of forked chats, and tapping it opens the parent.

1. **(a) Which screens.** Recommend: Sessions chat, Bot Chat and Bot rooms, all through `ChatReadingWidth`. Each is two modifiers, and one rule keeps the three chat screens consistent. Alternative: Sessions only. That's smaller, but Bot Chat would still show full-width lines on iPad.
2. **(a) 768 pt and iPhone landscape.** Recommend: the cap applies wherever the column would be wider, including iPhone landscape (about 900 pt). Alternative: iPad only (by size class). That leaves 900 pt lines on iPhone landscape, which is the same readability problem.
3. **(b) Overlay vs mask.** Recommend: a background-colour overlay, drawn only while the table overflows. A mask forces an offscreen pass for every visible table while scrolling. The catch is that the host must tell the overlay its background colour (Plan (b)). Alternative: reuse the toolbar's mask everywhere. It's always correct on any background, but it costs frame time in the scrolling path.
4. **(c) Which rows animate.** Recommend: only the newest row of a live group, when a new call replaces it. SwiftUI normally runs a transition only on the view being inserted, not on its children (confirm this while implementing). So when a whole live group appears at once (the first call, or a reattach replay), it draws as today with no fade, and settled groups never animate. Alternative: also fade the whole live group in when it first appears. That's more motion for little gain, and it would replay on every reattach.
5. **(d) Which chats count as forks.** Recommend: only `session_source == "fork"` with a `parent_session_id`. That's exactly what Fork From Here and `/branch` create, and the webui uses the same signal. Alternative: also agent rows with `relationship_type == "child_session"`. Rejected for now: that includes subagent, cron and CLI `/new` children, which would be mislabelled "Forked from". With this scope the title is resolved on the device from the loaded list, because fork rows never carry `parent_title` (see Problem). If agent child rows are ever wanted too, decode `parent_title` as an optional on `SessionSummary` (`Session.swift:220-221`, `:309`, `:351-352`) and prefer it over the cache.
6. **(d) Fallback copy.** Recommend: "Forked from another chat" when the parent isn't cached. The row stays tappable. A failed fetch (deleted or on another profile) shows "The original chat is no longer on this server." Alternative: hide the row when the parent is unknown. Rejected: the chat really is a fork, and the tap usually still works.

## Acceptance

- (a) On an iPad with the sidebar hidden, and in iPhone landscape, the transcript and composer are at most about 768 pt wide, centred, with the edges lined up. User bubbles stay on the trailing side of the column. The jump-to-latest button stays centred. iPhone portrait looks exactly as it does today. The same holds in Bot Chat and Bot rooms.
- (b) A table wider than the column shows a soft fade on its trailing edge. After scrolling, the leading edge fades too, and at the end only the leading edge fades. A table that fits shows no fade. RTL mirrors this. Code blocks are unchanged. The composer toolbar looks the same as today.
- (c) During a live run, each new tool row fades in over about 0.2 s. Reopening the chat, pulling to reload or reattaching doesn't animate. With Reduce Motion on, nothing animates. Bot Chat live rows behave the same.
- (d) A chat made with Fork From Here or `/branch` shows "Forked from <parent title>" as its first row. Tapping it opens the parent, and Back returns to the fork. A normal chat shows no row. An uncached parent reads "Forked from another chat" and still opens. A deleted parent shows the error.

## Tests

- New `ChatReadingWidthTests`:
  - A 393 pt viewport with 16 pt padding gives 361.
  - 1,366 pt gives 768.
  - A 0 pt viewport gives 0.
  - 20 pt accessibility padding is honoured.
  - These fail today because there is no rule.
- `ComposerToolbarScrollerTests`: rename it with the moved rule (for example `HorizontalOverflowEdgeFadesTests`). The six existing cases carry over unchanged. (b) adds no other pure logic.
- `ChatTranscriptRowEntryTests`: add `animatesNewestRow` cases. Live with motion gives true, settled gives false, and live with Reduce Motion gives false. These fail today because there is no type.
- New `ForkOriginTests`:
  - A non-fork gives nil.
  - A fork with a cached parent gives the parent's display title, and an empty title gives "Untitled Session".
  - A fork with no cached parent gives the fallback.
  - A `child_session` row that isn't a fork gives nil.
- `CacheStoreTests`:
  - `cachedSession(id:serverURL:in:)` finds an archived parent.
  - It returns nil for the same id cached under another server (multi-server isolation).
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatReadingWidthTests --only HermesMobileTests/HorizontalOverflowEdgeFadesTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatTranscriptRowEntryTests --only HermesMobileTests/ForkOriginTests --only HermesMobileTests/CacheStoreTests`

## Mocks

Not required. (a) to (c) change layout and motion in ways that are already decided. (d) copies the existing turn-fold row style (`TranscriptTurnFolding.swift:233-271`), with one icon and one line of copy.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build). Step 1 also needs an iPad, or the iPad simulator if no iPad is at hand.

1. (a) On iPad, open a long chat and hide the sidebar. The text column and composer are centred and about 768 pt wide. Show the sidebar: the column fills the narrower detail pane. Rotate the iPhone to landscape: it's centred and capped. Portrait is unchanged. Open Bot Chat and a Bot room: the same.
2. (b) Ask the agent for an 8-column markdown table. The trailing edge fades. Scroll right: both edges fade. At the end, only the leading edge fades. Try it in dark mode, in a Memory entry with a wide table, and with the RTL chat toggle.
3. (c) Ask for a task that runs 5+ tools. Each new tool row fades in. Leave the chat and reopen it: no fades. Turn on Reduce Motion and run again: no fades. Repeat in Bot Chat.
4. (d) Long-press a message → Fork From Here. The new chat's first row reads "Forked from <original title>". Tap it: the original opens. Back returns to the fork. Type `/branch test` in another chat: the same row appears.
5. (d) Delete the original chat, reopen the fork and tap the row. The error shows, and the app stays on the fork.
6. VoiceOver on the forked row reads "Forked from …, button" and the hint "Opens the original chat."

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:**
  - (a) Sessions chat (also from Archived Sessions, `ArchivedSessionsView.swift:28`), Bot Chat and Bot rooms.
  - (b) Every `MarkdownRenderer` host: Sessions, Bot Chat, rooms, delegated results, Memory, Skills, Kanban and file preview.
  - (c) Sessions and Bot Chat live groups.
  - (d) Any route that opens a fork's `ChatView`: the session list, the navigation push right after Fork From Here or `/branch`, and Archived Sessions.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** (d) looks up the parent only in the active server's cache, and fetches through the active server's client. (a) to (c) keep no state.
- **Contracts:** (d) reads `session_source` and `parent_session_id`, which are already decoded tolerantly. No new fields.
- **Reverse states:** (d) Back returns from the parent to the fork. (b) the fades clear as each edge is reached.
- **Native quality:**
  - VoiceOver: the (d) row label and hint.
  - Dynamic Type: (a) keeps the accessibility padding, and (d) has a 44 pt minimum height.
  - Reduce Motion: (c) is off, and (b)'s fade change is instant.
  - Light and dark: (b) reads its colour from the host.
  - RTL: (a) centres, (b) is mirrored by the shared rule, and (d) uses `chevron.forward`.
  - Localization: four new strings in all 17 translations.
- **Docs:** add "Fork" (a chat created from another by `/api/session/branch`, `session_source: fork`) to `CONTEXT.md`. It isn't defined there today.

## Outside reach

Agent-side child sessions (CLI `/branch`, subagents, cron) can't be told apart from other child sessions using the fields the pinned webui sends. They get no "Forked from" row (Decisions 5).

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-webui c67fd2dd.

title: feat(push): send a test notification from Settings
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Once push is on, users have no way to check that it works. If no banner ever arrives, they can't tell whether the relay is down, Apple refused the push, or this iPhone can't open the preview:

- The push section offers toggles, the relay host and "Turn off notifications…", but no test and no health check (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushSectionView.swift:75-141`).
- `PushRelayClient` speaks only the devices and activities routes (`HermesMobile/Push/PushRelayClient.swift:42-107`).
- When the default relay was switched off by Cloudflare (#834), every request came back `HTTP 429` with the body `error code: 1027`. Hermex showed "Could not reach this Hermes host", which sent the user to debug a host that was fine.

**The phone can already send a test itself.** Relay `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push` at `2f1388c`:

- `POST /installs/<install key>/notify` is the plugin's own route. Its only credential is the 64-hex install key in the path (`relay/src/index.ts:33`, `:39-42`). There's no signature, shared secret or per-caller rate limit.
- `relay/src/policy.ts` is delivery etiquette only: which kinds banner, muted replies and subagents, presence (`policy.ts:13-25`).
- The limits are the 16 KiB body cap (`index.ts:19`), a strict schema (`contract.ts:22-33`), 32 devices per install (`coordinator.ts:119`), and at most 4096 event receipts per install, each kept for 10 minutes. Past that cap the relay answers `429 event_limit` (`coordinator.ts:171-173`).
- The phone holds the same install key and the preview key in its pairing (`HermesMobile/Push/PushPairing.swift:10-17`), so it can post a valid `reply` event with a sealed preview. It uses the same capability it already uses for `/devices`. No new relay route is needed.

What a notify returns (`coordinator.ts:164-205`, `index.ts:5-7`, `:58-66`):

- `200 {"result":"accepted"}` once Apple accepted every banner. This also covers devices whose own settings skipped the banner.
- `503 apns_rejected` or `delivery_retry` when Apple refused or failed.
- `429 event_limit` at the receipt cap.
- `400 invalid_request`.
- Cloudflare's own `429 error code: 1027` page (not JSON) when the Worker is blocked (#834).

## Contract

`POST {relayURL}/installs/{installKey}/notify`, `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must contain exactly these fields: the schema is `.strict()`, so an unknown field gets a 400 (`contract.ts:24-33`).

```json
{ "v": 1, "event_id": "<32 hex, new per tap>", "thread_id": "<32 hex, fixed test constant>",
  "session_id": "hermex-test", "source": "other", "is_subagent": false,
  "sent_at": <unix seconds>, "kind": "reply", "collapse_id": "<32 hex, fixed test constant>",
  "sealed": "<base64 nonce(12)||ciphertext||tag(16) of {\"title\":…,\"body\":…}>" }
```

- The relay turns this into an alert with `mutable-content`, `thread-id`, `apns-collapse-id`, and `install_hash`, `session_id`, `source`, `kind` and `sealed` in the payload (`relay/src/apns.ts:76-89`).
- `sealed` is dropped for devices with previews off (`apns.ts:84`), so those phones see the plain "New activity".
- `HermesNotificationService` opens the preview with AAD `hermex-preview-v1:<sha256 install key>` (`HermesMobile/Push/PushPreview.swift:52-65`, `:110-131`).
- `source: "other"` means a tap only opens the app. `webuiDestination` and `botDestination` both ignore it (`Push/PushNotificationRouter.swift:14`, `:47`).
- In the foreground the banner still shows, because its install matches a pairing (`PushNotificationRouter.swift:142-157`).

## Plan

- [ ] **Relay call** (`Push/PushRelayClient.swift`). Add `sendTestNotification(pairing:) async -> PushRelayTestOutcome`:
  - Outcome: `.delivered`, `.unreachable`, or `.rejected(statusCode: Int, result: String?)`.
  - Build the URL with the same guard as `devicesURL` (`:104-107`). Send the exact body above. Read the response body's `result` tolerantly: `nil` if it isn't JSON.
  - One request, no retry.
  - Never log the URL or the key: follow the logging in `send(_:describedAs:)` (`:89-102`).
- [ ] **Sealing.** Add `seal(_ preview:, keys: PushPreviewKeys) -> String?` next to the client, mirroring `PushPreview.open` (`PushPreview.swift:56-65`): AES-256-GCM, random 12-byte nonce, the same AAD, standard base64 with padding. Keep it in the app target. `PushPreview.swift` is shared with the extension, which never seals.
- [ ] **Provisioner** (`Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift`):
  - Inject `testSender: (PushPairing) async -> PushRelayTestOutcome`, defaulting to `PushRelayClient()` (`:59-75`).
  - Add `sendTestNotification()` with a `.sendingTest` phase (`:31`), counted in `isWorking` (`:77-82`), so one tap is one request.
  - Publish the result: `.delivered` → a `testResult` success line; `.unreachable` and `.rejected` → `.failed(Failure(...))`, shown by the existing red `failureRow` (`HermexPushSectionView.swift:140`, `:199-206`).
  - Clear the result on the next action or when the section disappears (`leaveSettings`, `:131-133`).
- [ ] **Button** (`HermexPushSectionView.swift`, in the paired branch after the preference block, `:77-95`). A "Send Test Notification" button with a 44 pt minimum height, like its neighbours.
  - While the request runs, the label reads "Sending…" (no spinner, matching "Saving…" at `:96-98`).
  - The footnote under it is in Decisions 2. The success line goes below it.
  - Disabled while `isWorking`, when Reply Notifications are off (`effectivePreferences.replies == false`; the relay would skip the banner and still say accepted, `policy.ts:18-20`), or when iOS notifications are off for Hermex (`provisioner.notificationsOff`, `:105-107`).
- [ ] **Strings.** Add the button label, "Sending…", the footnote, the replies-off hint, the success line, the four failure messages, and the sealed title and body to `Localizable.xcstrings` in all 17 shipped languages.
- [ ] **Docs.** In `docs/agents/push.md` § Components → App, add that Settings can send one test `reply` through the paired relay. In `docs/agents/bots.md` § Push provisioning (`:1386`), document the test body and that the phone calls `/notify` only from this button.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- A "Send test notification" button in the push settings that goes relay → APNs → notification service end to end and reports pass or fail with a clear reason (relay unreachable, rejected, or delivered).
- The copy says the test rings every phone paired to that server.
- It does not test the host plugin → relay leg, and the UI says so.
- Mind the relay's free-plan quota: no retry loop, one tap = one request.

Implementation choices, with recommendations:

1. **Calling `/notify` from the phone.** Recommend it. The route's only auth is the install key in the path (`relay/src/index.ts:33`, `:39-42`), which the phone already holds and already uses for `/devices`, and `policy.ts` has no caller checks. Each tap costs one Worker request, one Durable Object request, one KV read per paired device and a few Durable Object storage writes, and makes no KV writes. That's tiny against the free plan. Alternative: a new relay `/test` route. That's more relay surface, a relay deploy, and it wouldn't exercise the real notify path.
2. **Copy.** Recommend:
   - Button: "Send Test Notification". Busy: "Sending…".
   - Footnote: "Sends one test through the relay to every iPhone paired with this Hermes host. It checks the relay, Apple and this iPhone, not your host's connection to the relay."
   - Replies off: "Turn on Reply Notifications to send a test."
   - Delivered: "Sent. Apple accepted the test; it should arrive in a few seconds."
   - Unreachable: "Couldn't reach the relay. Check this iPhone's internet connection, then try again."
   - Rejected by Apple (`apns_rejected`): "Apple refused the test notification. Turn notifications off and on again for this server."
   - Relay busy (`delivery_retry`, `temporarily_unavailable`, `event_limit`): "The relay couldn't deliver the test right now (HTTP <code>). Try again in a few minutes."
   - Refused, no relay answer (not JSON, e.g. #834's `429`): "The relay's hosting refused the request (HTTP <code>). The relay may be over its daily limit or switched off."
   - Sealed preview: title "Hermex test notification", body "Push through this server's relay reached this iPhone."
3. **Grouping and repeat taps.** Recommend a new random `event_id` for every tap, so the relay never treats a second test as a duplicate, and fixed test constants for `thread_id` and `collapse_id`. A second test then replaces the first banner instead of stacking. Alternative: random ids for all three, which lets test banners pile up in Notification Center.
4. **Proving this iPhone showed it.** Recommend relying on the relay's answer plus what the user sees. Watching `willPresent` for the test's `session_id` would only work with the app in the foreground and adds a timeout. Alternative: a 15-second wait for the banner in the foreground. That's more code for a check the user makes with their own eyes.

## Acceptance

- On a paired server, the push section shows "Send Test Notification" with the footnote above.
- One tap sends exactly one request (checked in tests). The button is disabled while it runs.
- With a working relay, a banner titled "Hermex test notification" arrives on this iPhone within seconds, and on other iPhones paired with the same host. Settings shows the success line.
- With previews off, the banner reads "New activity", and the test still reports success.
- Transport failure, an Apple rejection, a busy relay, and a non-JSON refusal (#834) each show their own message, never "Could not reach this Hermes host".
- Tapping the test banner only opens the app.
- The button is disabled when Reply Notifications are off or iOS notifications are off for Hermex.
- The install key never appears in a log line, error or UI string.

## Tests

- `PushRegistrationTests` (`HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests.swift`, "Relay wire shape" at `:461`), with `MockURLProtocol` like `testRelayRegistrationSendsTheStrictBodyToTheInstallsPath` (`:463-494`):
  - POSTs to `/installs/<key>/notify` with exactly the ten keys above, `kind: "reply"`, `source: "other"`, a 32-hex `event_id` that changes per call, and fixed `thread_id` / `collapse_id`;
  - `200 {"result":"accepted"}` → `.delivered`;
  - `503 {"result":"apns_rejected"}` → `.rejected(503, "apns_rejected")`;
  - `429` with the body `error code: 1027` → `.rejected(429, nil)`;
  - transport error → `.unreachable`;
  - a malformed install key → no request.
- `PushPreviewTests` (`HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests.swift`): a sealed test preview opens with `PushPreview.open` using the same keys, and `PushPreview.rewrite` shows its title and body. It fails with another install's keys.
- `HermexPushProvisioningTests` (`HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests.swift`), with an injected `testSender`:
  - one call per `sendTestNotification()`, including when called twice while the first is running;
  - each outcome maps to the success line or its failure message;
  - Reply Notifications off makes the test unavailable.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests --only HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests`

## Mocks

Not required: one button, one footnote and one result line inside the existing push section, using its existing button, caption and failure-row styles.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. Settings → Interaction → Notifications on a push-paired server. Expected: "Send Test Notification" with the footnote about every paired iPhone and the host → relay leg.
2. Tap it. Expected: the button reads "Sending…" and can't be tapped again. While #834 is unresolved, the result is the "relay's hosting refused the request (HTTP 429)" message. Once the relay is back: the success line, and within seconds a banner titled "Hermex test notification". Any second iPhone paired with the same host shows it too.
3. Tap the banner. Expected: Hermex opens and doesn't navigate.
4. Turn Show Previews off and send again. Expected: the banner reads "New activity", and it replaces the previous test banner instead of stacking.
5. Turn Reply Notifications off. Expected: the button is disabled with "Turn on Reply Notifications to send a test."
6. Turn on Airplane Mode and tap. Expected: "Couldn't reach the relay…".
7. Switch to a second, unpaired server. Expected: no test button there.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** Settings → Interaction → Notifications only. The test is a Settings diagnostic, not a chat action.
- **Targets:**
  - Main app: button, client and sealing.
  - `HermesNotificationService`: unchanged; it opens the test preview through the existing `rewrite` path.
  - Widget and share extension: untouched.
- **Servers:** the section and its provisioner are per server (`Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:196-214`, `.id(server)`), and the test uses only that server's pairing. Two configured servers that reach one host share an install (`docs/agents/push.md:52-55`), so the test rings for both. The footnote says "every iPhone paired with this Hermes host", which covers that.
- **Contracts:** the relay's `/notify` schema, verified in source at `2f1388c`. The body is strict, so the test pins its exact keys.
- **Reverse states:** a result line clears on the next action or on leaving Settings. The banner replaces itself (fixed `collapse_id`).
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver reads the button, footnote and result, and the failure row keeps `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`. Dynamic Type wraps. No spinner. About 11 new strings × 17 languages.
- **Docs:** `push.md`, `bots.md` § Push provisioning.

## Outside reach

At runtime, each tap makes one POST to the server's configured relay (by default Uzair's Cloudflare Worker, `https://hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev`), which pushes to every iPhone paired with that host. Development and CI must use `MockURLProtocol` only. The only live relay call is the maintainer's manual test on the Branch build.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-webui c67fd2dd; relay source `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push` at `2f1388c`.

title: fix(sessions): a new chat started under a project filter joins that project
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Filter the session list to a project, tap Chat, send a message and go back. Your new chat is missing from the list, because it was created with no project and the filter hides it. You have to clear the filter to find it, then move it into the project by hand.

- `openNewChat()` builds `PendingNewChatRoute()` with no project (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1455-1457`). The route type has no project field at all (`:1667-1695`).
- `PendingNewChatView.createSessionIfNeeded` calls `viewModel.createSession(modelContext:profile:)` (`SessionListView.swift:1926-1931`). That calls `client.createSession(workspace:model:modelProvider:profile:)` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:1321-1339`), whose body `NewSessionRequest` has no project field (`Networking/APIClient+Sessions.swift:62-73`, `:208-213`).
- The list keeps only rows whose `projectId` equals `selectedProjectID` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:227-230`). The new session has none, so it is hidden.

The upstream web UI puts a new chat in the active project filter by default, so the same server behaves differently in the two clients.

## Contract

`POST /api/session/new` accepts an optional `project_id`:

- The pinned handler passes `project_id=body.get("project_id") or None` to `new_session` (`api/routes.py:14208-14216`).
- `new_session` stores it on the session as given, without checking that the project exists (`api/models.py:4633`, stored at `:4680`).
- `compact()` echoes `project_id` in the response (`api/models.py:1724`). The client already reads it back: `SessionSummary(from: SessionDetail)` copies `projectId` at `Models/Session.swift:394`.
- The web UI sends the active filter unless the caller overrides it (`static/sessions.js:1411-1415`, excluding its "unassigned only" filter, which Hermex does not have).
- The client encodes request keys with `.convertToSnakeCase` (`Networking/APIClient.swift:51`), so a `projectId` property goes out as `project_id`. A nil optional is omitted from the body.

This is a webui-only bug fix, which the freeze in #713 allows. On Hermes, project tags are dropped and projects become folder lanes (#702 slice 2.4), so that migration replaces this path.

## Plan

- [ ] `SessionListView.swift:1667-1695`: add `let projectID: String?` to `PendingNewChatRoute`, defaulting to nil in `init`.
- [ ] `SessionListView.swift:1455-1457`: `openNewChat()` builds `PendingNewChatRoute(projectID: selectedProjectID)`. Three entry points already go through it: the Chat button (`:479`, `:837-871`), the iPad empty-detail "New Chat" button (`:497`), and ⌘N (`openNewChatFromKeyboard`, `:1151-1154`).
- [ ] `SessionListView.swift:515-526`: pass `route.projectID` into `PendingNewChatView`. Store it next to `profileName` (`:1773`, `:1785-1805`), and pass it in `createSessionIfNeeded` (`:1931`). Retry (`:1955-1960`) reuses the same value.
- [ ] `SessionListViewModel.swift:1321-1339`: add `projectID: String? = nil` to `createSession`, trimmed with `Self.nonEmpty`, and forward it.
- [ ] `APIClient+Sessions.swift:62-73` and `:208-213`: add `projectID: String?` to `createSession` and `projectId: String?` to `NewSessionRequest`. Update the two `ChatViewModel` callers (`Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:1233-1238`, `:3606-3611`) to pass nil, or give the parameter a nil default.
- [ ] Leave these creators unchanged, so they do not inherit the filter:
  - App Intents and deep links (`openRequestedNewChatIfNeeded`, `SessionListView.swift:1444-1453`);
  - share imports (`:1370-1375`);
  - `/new` (`ChatViewModel.swift:3590-3622`);
  - profile-switch new sessions (`ChatViewModel.swift:1229-1245`).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** A new chat started while a project filter is active joins that project. It is a webui-only bug fix.

1. **Which entry points inherit.** Recommend only in-app New Chat: the Chat button, the iPad empty-state button and ⌘N, which all go through `openNewChat()`. On iPad, ⌘N inherits even when the sidebar is collapsed, as the web UI does. App Intents, deep links, share imports, `/new` and profile-switch sessions do not inherit, because the user cannot see the filter from those places. The alternative is that every creator inherits, so a Siri or Share-sheet chat would silently land in whatever project the list was last filtered to.
2. **When the filter is read.** Recommend taking a snapshot at tap time: the route carries the project the user saw when they tapped. The alternative is to read the filter when the server call runs. On iPad the user can change the filter while the new-chat composer is open, which would be surprising.
3. **Deleted project.** The server does not validate the id. If the project is deleted between tap and create, the chat keeps a dangling id and still appears under All. Recommend accepting this, since it is rare and the server owns the rule.

## Acceptance

- With a project filter active, a chat started from the Chat button, the iPad "New Chat" button or ⌘N is created with that project. After the first message it stays visible in the filtered list.
- With no filter, the request body has no `project_id` key, the same as today.
- New chats from App Intents, deep links, the share extension, `/new` and profile switches are created without a project.
- The web UI shows the new chat inside the project.

## Tests

- `SessionListMutationTests`, following `testCreateSessionAfterProfileSwitchPinsProfileWithoutCookieOrWorkspaceLookup` (`HermesMobileTests/SessionListMutationTests.swift:415-462`):
  - `testCreateSessionSendsProjectIDWhenGiven`: the body `project_id == "p1"`, and the created summary's `projectId == "p1"`. This fails today because `createSession` has no project parameter.
  - `testCreateSessionOmitsProjectIDByDefault`: the body has no `project_id` key.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SessionListMutationTests`

## Mocks

Not required: no visible UI change.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build)

1. Open Projects in the list, pick a project, tap Chat, send "hello", and go back. Expected: the new chat is in the filtered list.
2. Clear the filter. Expected: the chat is also under All. The web UI shows it in the same project.
3. With the filter still set, start a chat from the "New Chat" App Shortcut or Siri. Expected: after sending, it does not appear under the project filter, only under All.
4. Share a text snippet from Safari into Hermex while a filter is active, and send it. Expected: that chat has no project.
5. Switch to a second server. Expected: no filter is active there, and a new chat has no project.
6. Optional, on iPad with a hardware keyboard: filter to a project and press ⌘N. Expected: the chat joins the project.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** Chat button, iPad empty-state button and ⌘N inherit. App Intents, deep links, the share extension, `/new` and profile switches do not (Decision 1).
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** `selectedProjectID` is `@State` on `SessionListView` (`:53`), which is rebuilt per server (`ContentView.swift:95`), so one server's filter can never reach another server's request.
- **Contracts:** `POST /api/session/new` with `project_id` (see Contract). Endpoint, body and decode all change together.
- **Reverse states:** the user can still move a chat out with the existing "Move to project" menu.
- **Native quality:** no UI, strings or animation.
- **Docs:** none.

## Outside reach

None.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-webui c67fd2dd.

title: feat(sessions): multi-word search, live "2m ago" labels, and iPad chat shortcuts
body:
Part of #855 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

Three independent slices. Each can land as its own commit, and they touch different code.

## Problem

**(a) Search needs words in exact order.**
- Local search joins a session's title, workspace, model, provider, profile and source label into one lowercased string (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:1423-1434`). It then checks that the whole query appears in it (`:231-234`).
- So "deploy wrangler" finds nothing unless those words sit next to each other in that order. "wrangler deploy" and "deploy myrepo" (title plus workspace) both fail.
- Ordering stays as it is: local matches first, then remote content matches, each sorted pinned-first and then by recency (`:235`, `:254`, `:1409-1417`).

**(b) "2m ago" labels go stale.**
- `relativeDate` computes against `Date()` only when the row renders (`Features/SessionList/SessionRowView.swift:376-384`).
- Nothing in SessionList runs a timer, so a row that said "1 min. ago" still says it ten minutes later until something else re-renders the row.

**(c) iPad keyboard users cannot move between chats.**
- The app commands are ⌘N (New Chat), ⌘F (Search Sessions) and `SidebarCommands` (`HermesMobile/HermesMobileApp.swift:21-40`, `:78-81`).
- The only other shortcuts are ⌘Return to send (`Features/Chat/ComposerChipTextView.swift:545-553`, `Features/Bots/BotChatComposerView.swift:470`) and Escape to close Bot search (`Features/Bots/BotSearchView.swift:146`).
- There is no way to jump to a chat or step to the next one without the pointer or touch.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract. Remote content search keeps sending the raw query, unchanged (`SessionListView.swift:304-306`).

## Plan

**(a) Multi-word local search**
- [ ] `SessionListViewModel.swift:219-234`: split the normalized query into terms once per call, on whitespace, dropping empties. Do this outside the per-row closure. A row matches when every term is contained in its searchable text.
- [ ] Keep `searchableText(for:)` (`:1423-1434`) as it is. Terms contain no spaces and fields are joined with a space, so a term found in the joined string is always inside one field. Do not add project names.
- [ ] Leave the remote-match merge (`:237-254`) and `activeRemoteSearchQuery` handling unchanged.

**(b) Live relative time**
- [ ] `SessionRowView.swift:376-384`: replace the `relativeDate` property with `static func relativeDateLabel(for: SessionSummary, now: Date) -> String?`.
- [ ] `SessionRowView.swift:200-207`: in `trailingStatusSlot`, wrap only the time text in `TimelineView(.everyMinute) { context in relativeDateText(Self.relativeDateLabel(for: session, now: context.date) ?? "") }`. This follows `Features/Bots/BotPendingRequestCard.swift:494-500`. Change `showsTrailingStatus` (`:209-211`) to check whether a timestamp exists, not whether the string does.
- [ ] `accessibilitySummary` (`:386-409`) keeps using `Date()` at render time (Decision 6).

**(c) Chat shortcuts**
- [ ] `HermesMobileApp.swift:4-8`: add two members to `HermexSceneActions`: `openChat(atPosition: Int)` (1-based) and `openAdjacentChat(offset: Int)`.
- [ ] `HermesMobileApp.swift:21-40`: add these commands (placement in Decision 4):
  - "Next Chat" on ⌃Tab (`.keyboardShortcut(.tab, modifiers: .control)`);
  - "Previous Chat" on ⌃⇧Tab;
  - "Go to Chat 1" through "Go to Chat 9" on ⌘1–⌘9, using one format key, "Go to Chat %lld".
  Disable the commands only when `actions == nil`.
- [ ] `SessionListView.swift:1143-1149`: implement the new closures. Work out the ordered chats when the key is pressed, not in `body`, because `content` already notes that grouping filters and sorts every session (`:583-585`). Open the chat with `startOpeningSession(_:)` (`:1479-1482`), the same path as a row tap (`:1079-1081`).
- [ ] Add a small pure helper next to `SessionNavigationState` (`Features/SessionList/SessionNavigationState.swift`). It returns:
  - the nth chat, or nil when out of range;
  - the next or previous chat relative to `selectedSessionID`, wrapping at the ends. With no selection, or a selection not in the list, next goes to the first chat and previous to the last.
- [ ] Add "Next Chat", "Previous Chat" and "Go to Chat %lld" to `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` with all 17 shipped locales (`docs/agents/i18n.md`). The number in "Go to Chat %lld" is a position, not a count, so it needs no plural variants. Keep the `%lld` placeholder in every translation.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- (a) Search matches several words in any order: split the query into words, and every word must match some field. Remote content search is unchanged.
- (b) "2m ago" labels stay current while the list is on screen.
- (c) With a hardware keyboard, ⌘1–9 jumps to the nth chat in the visible list, and ⌃Tab / ⌃⇧Tab moves to the next or previous chat.

- **Implementation notes (recommended).** (a) Don't add project names to the searched fields, since project tags go away on Hermes. (b) Wrap only the time label in a per-row `TimelineView(.everyMinute)`, so the whole list never re-renders. (c) Give the commands titles so they appear in the ⌘-hold menu.

1. **Which rows count for (c).** Recommend the ordinary chat rows (`scheduledSessionGroups.ordinary`) in on-screen order, after search and the project filter, skipping the Scheduled group. Then ⌘1 is the same chat whether Scheduled is expanded or collapsed. The alternative is every visible row in on-screen order, including expanded Scheduled rows.
2. **Ends.** Recommend that ⌃Tab wraps from the last chat to the first, like browser tabs. The alternative is to stop at the ends.
3. **If ⌃Tab is swallowed.** A focused composer (`UITextView`) or Full Keyboard Access might take ⌃Tab. If so, recommend switching the pair to ⌘⇧] / ⌘⇧[, Safari's tab convention, which nothing in Hermex uses. Ship one pair, not both. Nothing in the app uses ⌘1–9, ⌃Tab or ⌘⇧[ ] today. The only existing shortcuts are the ones listed in the Problem, plus ⌃⌘S from `SidebarCommands`.
4. **Menu placement.** Recommend the View menu, right after the sidebar item (`CommandGroup(after: .sidebar)`), so the items sit with Toggle Sidebar in the ⌘-hold overlay and the iPadOS menu bar. The alternative is a new top-level "Go" menu.
5. **Disabled state.** Recommend that an out-of-range ⌘digit does nothing and is not greyed out. Greying it out would mean filtering and sorting every session on each body pass to count rows. The alternative is exactly that: disable items past the count and pay for it.
6. **VoiceOver time.** The row's VoiceOver label (`:386-409`) is built at render time, so its "N min ago" can lag until the row next re-renders, for example on the next poll, reload or foreground. Recommend accepting that. The alternative is to wrap the whole row in the `TimelineView`, which re-renders each visible row once a minute.
7. **Matching style for (a).** Recommend keeping the lowercase `contains`. Switching to `localizedStandardContains`, which ignores diacritics, would be a separate change.

## Acceptance

- (a) "deploy wrangler" finds a session titled "Wrangler deploy fix". It also finds "Deploy" whose workspace is `/src/wrangler`. It does not find a session with only "Deploy". The project filter and ordering are unchanged, and remote content matches still follow the local ones.
- (b) On an idle list, a row that shows "1 min. ago" moves to "2 min. ago" within the next minute, without scrolling or reloading. The same applies in Archived Sessions and the Scheduled screen.
- (c) With a hardware keyboard:
  - ⌘1 opens the first chat, ⌘3 the third, and ⌘9 with fewer than 9 chats does nothing.
  - ⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab step through chats and wrap.
  - Both work with the composer focused.
  - Holding ⌘ shows the new titles.
  - All of this respects the active search and project filter.

## Tests

- (a) `SessionListMutationTests`, next to `testVisibleSessionsFiltersSubagentsAcrossSearchAndProjects` (`HermesMobileTests/SessionListMutationTests.swift:3261`): add `testLocalSearchMatchesEveryWordInAnyOrderAcrossFields`. It covers the three cases in Acceptance plus pinned-first order. It fails today.
- (b) `SessionIdentityTests` (existing `SessionRowView` static-helper tests): add `testRelativeDateLabelUsesSuppliedNow`. The same session gives different labels at `now` and `now + 2h`, and nil when it has no timestamp. It fails today because no `now` seam exists.
- (c) `SessionNavigationStateTests`: add `testChatShortcutPositionPicksNthChatOrNothing` and `testNextAndPreviousChatWrapAndStartFromTheEndsWithoutSelection`. Both fail today.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SessionListMutationTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionIdentityTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests`

## Mocks

Not required:
- (a) has no UI.
- (b) keeps the existing look.
- (c) adds only system menu titles.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build). Step 3 needs a hardware keyboard: use an iPad with a keyboard if you have one, otherwise the iPad simulator with I/O › Keyboard › Connect Hardware Keyboard.

1. Search "wrangler deploy" (reversed word order) for a session titled "deploy wrangler …". Expected: it is found.
2. Send a message in a chat, go back to the list and leave it idle for 3 minutes. Expected: the row's time counts up once a minute.
3. With the keyboard:
   - Hold ⌘. Expected: the menu lists Next Chat, Previous Chat and Go to Chat 1–9.
   - Press ⌘2. Expected: the second chat opens.
   - Press ⌃Tab twice, then ⌃⇧Tab. Expected: selection moves down two and up one.
   - Focus the composer and press ⌃Tab. Expected: it still moves; if not, apply Decision 3.
   - Filter to a project and press ⌘1. Expected: the first chat of that project opens.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:**
  - (a) also applies on the Scheduled screen, which uses the same `visibleSessions` (`SessionListComponents.swift:841`).
