  - (b) applies to every `SessionRowView`: the list, the iPad sidebar, Scheduled, and Archived (`Features/Settings/ArchivedSessionsView.swift:100`). Bot rows share `SessionRelativeDateFormatter` but are out of scope.
  - (c) works on iPad and on iPhone with a keyboard. The scene value is set at `SessionListView.swift:377`.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** all three read the server-keyed view model and navigation state, so nothing crosses servers.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** ⌃Tab has ⌃⇧Tab.
- **Native quality:**
  - `TimelineView(.everyMinute)` ticks once a minute and only for rows on screen. That is not a continuous animation, and it pauses in the background.
  - Dynamic Type is unchanged.
  - VoiceOver: see Decision 6.
  - Localization: three new keys in all 17 locales.
- **Docs:** none.

## Outside reach

Whether iPadOS or Full Keyboard Access reserves ⌃Tab can only be checked on a device or simulator with a hardware keyboard. Decision 3 covers the fallback.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-webui c67fd2dd.

title: epic(hermes): clearer Bot errors, reliable push, and polish
body:
## Goal

Fix the places where Hermex hides what's going on and add a few focused improvements, found in a review of the direct-Hermes experience and the push path.

- **Hidden or wrong errors.** A failed Bot turn shows only a sad face. Cloudflare Access and proxy setups get wrong sign-in advice.
- **Lost or silent notifications.** Approval banners are dropped when the phone is briefly offline, and runs shown in a Live Activity finish silently.
- **Dead ends.** PDFs and media show "No Preview".
- **Missing basics.** There's no app lock, and no way to answer a password-vault or 2FA prompt from the phone.

Every item is client-only, a change to the relay or host plugin in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, or uses a method or route that exists at the tested Hermes pin `ca678285` (0.21.5). Each sub-issue cites the code by file and line, and includes a plan, acceptance, tests, and surfaces, so an implementation agent can start cold.

**Relation to #713.** #713 freezes webui to bug fixes and defers Hermes-only features until parity (decision 9). Everything here is a bug fix, client-side, push work, or tooling. The one exception is #891 (password-vault and 2FA prompts), which Uzair approved as an explicit exception on 2026-09-28. Several networking items change code that #700 is about to rework. They land first, and #700 keeps their behavior (see each issue's notes).

## How to work this epic

1. **Run it after #855's PRs have merged** (`/hermex-batch epic 877`). #880, #884, #886, #889 and #894 touch files that #855 also changes. Every decision is already answered below (Uzair, 2026-09-28). Each sub-issue's `## Decisions` section repeats its answers; any remaining implementation choice there carries a recommendation.
2. **Mock gates:** #878 (failure row), #883 ("Always allow" scope line), #885 (app lock), #891 (password and 2FA field) and #895 (group chat empty state) need static mocks and a pick before implementation.
3. **Stacks:** #880 → #884 (the same sign-in advice code), #881 → #888 (the same relay send path). Everything else is independent.
4. **Two repos.** #881, #882, #888 and #893 land in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, and #887 spans both repos.
   - The `hermex-push` PR opens and merges first.
   - Uzair deploys the relay or reinstalls the plugin; agents never deploy.
   - The app PR links to the `hermex-push` PR.
   - The relay runs on Cloudflare Workers Paid, so these changes are about cost and reliability, not free-plan limits.
5. **Manual testing happens at review, on one build.** PRs open with a numbered **Manual test** section, and Uzair tests before merging. Every PR with manual steps marks `Device: physical iPhone`, so the merge walk builds one integration branch and one Branch TestFlight build for all of them.
6. **Never done by agents:** live-server mutations, relay deploys, plugin installs on the host, Apple Developer portal changes, and TestFlight uploads.
7. One issue → one `issue/<n>-slug` branch → one PR per repo. Agents never merge.

## Work, in order

| # | Issue | Priority | Repo | Stacks on | Mock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #878 | P1 | app | — | ✓ |
| 2 | #879 | P1 | app | — | |
| 3 | #880 | P1 | app | — | |
| 4 | #881 | P1 | hermex-push | — | |
| 5 | #882 | P2 | hermex-push | — | |
| 6 | #883 | P2 | app | — | ✓ |
| 7 | #884 | P2 | app | #880 | |
| 8 | #885 | P2 | app | — | ✓ |
| 9 | #886 | P2 | app | — | |
| 10 | #887 | P2 | both | — | |
| 11 | #888 | P2 | hermex-push | #881 | |
| 12 | #889 | P2 | app | — | |
| 13 | #890 | P2 | app (tooling) | — | |
| 14 | #891 | P2 | app | — | ✓ |
| 15 | #892 | P3 | app | — | |
| 16 | #893 | P3 | hermex-push | — | |
| 17 | #894 | P3 | app | — | |
| 18 | #895 | P3 | app | — | ✓ |
| 19 | #896 | P3 | app | — | |

## Decisions (Uzair, 2026-09-28)

### Ask: answered

| # | Issue | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | #878 | Where does a failed turn's reason show? | A row under the failed turn, with Retry when retrying helps, the reset time for rate limits, a billing link when present, and "reply shown but not saved". It clears on the next send. |
| D2 | #879 | Which files open in Quick Look? | Whatever the preview can't show, from all three entry points, up to about 25 MB. |
| D3 | #881 | How long are banners held? | Approvals and questions up to 5 minutes (under the approval timeout), replies about an hour; routine Live Activity updates still drop. (Open: questions wait 1 hour on the host by default, so #881 recommends holding them for their own timeout.) |
| D4 | #882 | Relay traffic and monitoring? | The plugin sends routine progress only while a phone has a Live Activity for that session. No usage-check automation: Uzair's Cloudflare billing alert covers spend. |
| D5 | #883 | Explain "Always allow"? | One plain line on the approval card, in Sessions and Bot Chat, naming what each choice covers. |
| D6 | #884 | After a rejected password? | The button opens the sign-in form instead of resending the old password. |
| D7 | #885 | How does the app lock behave? | One toggle, off by default. It locks on a cold launch and after more than a minute in the background, and the app switcher shows a blank cover. No "require after" picker. |
| D8 | #886 | Pasted dashboard links? | Strip what browsers add, map `ws`/`wss` to `http`/`https`, and show "Will connect to …". Path prefixes are out of scope. |
| D9 | #887 | Banner titles? | "<bot> · Approval needed" (and the other kinds) in the phone's language. The bot's name stays inside the seal. |
| D10 | #888 | Silent finish under a Live Activity? | The Live Activity update alerts once when a run finishes or fails. No separate banner, so the #490/#740 rule stands. |
| D11 | #890 | Local test server? | Yes, with a scripted model, loopback only and manual approvals. A second slice records tool and approval fixtures from it. |
| D12 | #891 | Password-vault and 2FA prompts? | Answered on the phone (an exception to #713 decision 9). No extra Face ID step; values are never saved or logged. |
| D13 | #892 | Withdrawn requests? | A short note on a timeout or a stopped run; silent when the request was answered elsewhere. |
| D14 | #894 | Composer polish? | ↑ recalls your last message, and staged documents show a real preview. |
| D15 | #895 | Group chat empty state? | Members' faces and "Say something to the group". Static, with no animation. |
| D16 | all | When does manual testing happen? | At review, all together, in one Branch TestFlight build. |

### Batch run answers (Uzair, 2026-09-29)

Run `epic-877` also includes #851. Each issue's decision comment is binding.

| # | Issue | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | push issues | Push to `hermex-push`? | Yes: branches and ready PRs for #881, #882, #887, #888, #893. That repo has no review bots, so each PR gets one Codex review (`gpt-6-astra`, high). Never a deploy. |
| R2 | push issues | When are push changes tested? | After merge: merge the hermex-push PRs, Uzair deploys the relay and updates the plugin, then the app stack walk and all phone checks on one Branch TestFlight build. |
| R3 | #890 | Local Hermes on the Mac? | Yes: clone at the pin, install with uv under `~/Library/Caches`, serve on 127.0.0.1:9199, approve only `python3 -c "print(1)"`. |
| B1 | #878 | Failure row after backgrounding? | Kept until the next send or a new turn. |
| B2 | #880 | Redirect check? | Compares the host, like the status probe. |
| B3 | #884 | Connect with an unchanged password? | Any successful save reconnects. |
| B4 | #881 | Question banner hold? | 3600 s (the host's question timeout), not 300 s. Settles D3's open point. |
| B5 | #882, #887, #851 | Plugin versions? | #882 → 0.2.1, #887 → 0.3.0 (merges after #882); #851's newest-known constant is 0.3.0. |
| B6 | #883 | Plugin rules without a tool name? | Name from the rule key, else the command, else "every action like this one"; never the raw key. |
| B7 | #892 | Cancel while the phone is locked? | Shown after reconnect, matched in the replay. |
| B8 | #890 | One PR or two? | One PR, two commits. |
| B9 | #851 | Restart Hermes from the phone? | Not in #851; tracked in #934. |

Design picks: #878 C, #883 A, #891 A (https://h8y1ulmv5xvh.postplan.dev); #885 A, #895 A (https://dduu03ggmql5.postplan.dev); #851 C with no connection-screen banner (https://ozrsjnnq33ac.postplan.dev).

## Not doing

Decided against on 2026-09-28, so future reviews don't re-propose them:

- **Offering "Attach as file" for very long pastes.** It changes how the agent receives your text.
- **Continuously animated faces, typing dots, custom tab bars and self-playing onboarding.** This conflicts with the no-endless-animation rule.
- **Widgets or a Watch app that hold every server's credentials.** It breaks per-server isolation.
- **On-device AI titles generated for each row while scrolling.**
- **Closing the Hermes session when you leave a chat.** It closes it for every device.
- **Putting the WebSocket ticket in the URL.** It leaks into proxy logs.
- **An injection-risk badge on tool output.** Hermes never blocks or redacts; it only labels.
- **A context-usage breakdown by category, and moving the Hermes networking code into a separate package.**
- **Automated relay usage checks.** Cloudflare's billing alert covers this.

title: fix(bots): show why a Bot turn failed
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

When a Bot turn fails, Bot Chat shows a sad face in the title and nothing else. The user can't tell a rate limit from a bad API key, a billing wall, or a host crash, so they don't know whether to wait, retry, or fix something on the Mac.

- `BotConversation.swift:819-822` reduces the whole failure to one flag: `turnFailed = inflight["error"] != .null`. That flag only drives the Sad title face (`:318-325`) and the Live Activity's failed state (`:252`).
- A live `message.complete` only triggers a snapshot read (`:1418-1433`). Its `error`, `warning`, `billing` and `failure_reason` are never read.
- No Swift file under `HermesMobile/` reads `error_surface`, `failure_reason`, `billing` or `recoverable`.
- `BotChatView.swift:100-133` draws the failed turn's prompt and any partial reply, then goes straight to the plan and request card. Nothing under the turn says it failed or why.
- A host warning that a reply was not saved to history is also dropped.

#737 lists this under "Noticed, not filed". #701 slice 1.1 (Sessions on Hermes) will need the same decoding, so this issue builds it in a place 1.1 can reuse.

## Contract

Read-only use of fields the host already sends, plus one existing RPC shape for Retry. All pinned at hermes-agent `ca678285`.

**Retained failure, from `session.resume` (`inflight`).** A failed turn is kept until the next turn starts or the session closes (`tui_gateway/session_history.py:347-368`, called from `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py:842-853`). The resume snapshot carries it as `inflight: {user, assistant, error, status: "error", recoverable, error_surface?}` (`tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py:29-43`, built at `tui_gateway/session_auto_continue.py:377-383`). This is the only source that survives a disconnect, backgrounding, or a push tap that opens the chat later.

**`error_surface`** (`tui_gateway/contracts/events.py:145-155`, built by `agent/error_surface.py:88-99, 140-185`):
- `layer`: `provider`, `endpoint`, `streaming`, `auth`, `billing`, `gateway`, `disk`, plus `runtime` for an agent that could not start (`tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py:166`).
- `code`: the failure reason, for example `rate_limit`, `auth`, `context_overflow`, `model_not_found`, `timeout`, `stream_drop`, `free_tier_rate_limited`.
- `retryable`: false when retrying unchanged repeats the failure (`agent/error_surface.py:50-58, 171-175`).
- Optional: `provider`, `model`, `resets_at` (epoch seconds when a rate limit lifts, `:177-181`), and `message` (the host's own sentence, sent for `free_tier_*` codes, `:161-167`). Unknown extra keys are allowed (`extra: allow`).

**Live-only fields, from `message.complete`** (`tui_gateway/contracts/events.py:183-201`, built at `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py:806-865`):
- `billing: {provider, provider_label, model, billing_url?, message, unverified?}` (`events.py:158-167`) and `failure_reason`. Both are sent only together, when the provider reports a billing wall (`prompt_turn.py:833-836`).
- `warning`: at the pin, only "History changed during this turn — the response above is visible but was not saved to session history." (`prompt_turn.py:264-301`). It can arrive on a successful turn.
- `text`: for a failure with no reply, the host's plain-English account (`tui_gateway/user_messages.py:73-86`). It names slash commands (`/retry`, `/model`, `/compress`) that Bot Chat doesn't have, and it is never persisted. Hermex doesn't use it.

`billing`, `failure_reason` and `warning` are not retained in `inflight`, so after a reconnect only the replay ring (`session.events.since`) still has them.

**Retry.** Use the same call #745 specifies: `prompt.submit {session_id, text, truncate_before_row_id, confirm_truncate: true, confirm_empty_truncate: true}` with no `queued` (`tui_gateway/contracts/prompt_voice.py:26-45`). The host cuts the failed prompt's row and starts the turn again in one call under the history lock (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:241-374`). Errors: 4009 busy (`:650`), 4018 target gone, 4028/4029 missing confirmation. The failed prompt's row exists: the host writes the user row at submit time (`tui_gateway/session_workdir.py:348-374`). Because the failed turn is the last one, the cut removes nothing else.

**#700 must preserve:** delivery of `message.complete` payloads and replayed events to `BotConversation.observe`/`reconcileReplay` unchanged, the resume snapshot's `inflight` object, and the new `HermesCall` case below with its admission check.

## Plan

- [ ] **Decode.** Add `HermesTurnOutcome` (a pure value type in `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/`, beside `HermesCall`, so #701 slice 1.1 reuses it). It has two tolerant initializers:
  - `init?(inflight:)` for the retained failure: `error`, `error_surface` (layer, code, retryable, resets_at, message, provider), `recoverable`.
  - `init?(complete:)` for `message.complete`: the same fields plus `billing`, `failure_reason`, `warning`.
  - Every field is optional. An unknown layer or code falls back to the generic title.
- [ ] **State.** In `BotConversation`, replace `turnFailed: Bool` (`:165-166`) with `turnFailure: HermesTurnOutcome?`.
  - Derive it from every applied snapshot. It is non-nil only in the interrupted-with-error branch (`:819-822`). `titleFace` (`:318-325`) and the Live Activity phase (`:252`) read `turnFailure != nil`, so they behave exactly as today.
  - Add `turnNotice: HermesTurnOutcome?` for the live-only fields. `observe` (`:1369-1436`) sets it from a `message.complete` payload. `reconcileReplay` (`:652-688`) also takes the last `message.complete` of the current turn from `missed`, so a phone that was backgrounded when the turn ended still gets the billing link and warning while the ring holds them.
  - Clear both on `message.start` and when the host accepts the next prompt (right after `emit(.sent)` in `submit`, `:970`). A refused send keeps them. Clear them on disconnect or generation change like other turn state.
  - Never write either into `BotHistoryCache` or the recent transcript.
- [ ] **Row.** Add `BotTurnOutcomeRow` and draw it in `BotChatView.swift` right after the live reply (`:113-115`), before the plan and request card. The row shows, in order:
  - a title for the failure (Decision 1);
  - the host's raw `error` as secondary detail, 4 lines at most, selectable;
  - "Limit resets at 14:05" when `resets_at` is in the future;
  - the billing `message` and an "Open billing page" button when `billing_url` is an `https` URL. It opens in Safari, as #770 decided for connector links;
  - the `warning` text when present, including on a successful turn;
  - Retry (Decision 2).
- [ ] **Retry.** Add `HermesCall.promptRewind(sessionID:text:beforeRowID:)` (`HermesCall.swift:44` area, params beside `:252-253`, admission in `admit()` at `:320-381`). Name it for #745, which reuses it for edit and retry-from-here.
  - `BotConversation.retryFailedTurn()` is guarded like `maySend` (`:306-309`).
  - Target: the settled prompt row that `activePromptMessageID` names, and its `rowID`.
  - Text: the snapshot's raw `inflight.user`, which keeps the mention note. For a `/skill` row, resend the displayed invocation, per #745's rule.
  - After dispatch, run `refreshAfterPrompt()`. Map 4009 and 4018 to the #745 messages. Never resend automatically.
  - Hide Retry when there is no row id.
- [ ] Add every new string to `Localizable.xcstrings` for all shipped languages (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).
- [ ] Update `docs/agents/bots.md` (the title-face paragraph near `:584-588` and the turn-state notes): what the row shows, where each field comes from, and that live-only fields are lost once the replay ring drops them.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Show the host's failure reason in the chat as a row under the failed turn: Retry when the host says retrying can help, the reset time for rate limits, a billing link when present, and the "reply shown but not saved" warning. The row clears on the next send. Mocks first.

1. **Title copy.** Recommend Hermex's own localized titles, keyed by `layer` plus a few codes where the fix differs: `rate_limit`/`upstream_rate_limit`, `context_overflow`/`payload_too_large`, `model_not_found`, `content_policy_blocked`, `timeout`, `overloaded`/`server_error`. Add a generic "The turn failed" for anything unknown. The titles mirror the host's wording without slash commands (`tui_gateway/user_messages.py:17-49`), and `error_surface.message` wins when the host sends one. Alternative: show only the raw `error` under a generic title. That is simpler, but raw provider text is often a JSON blob, which defeats the point.
2. **When Retry shows.** Recommend showing it when `error_surface.retryable` is true, or when the surface is missing and `recoverable` is true, which is how every host-retained failure is marked (`session_history.py:358`). Alternative: hide Retry whenever the surface is missing, which gives an older host no Retry at all.
3. **Retry mechanism.** Recommend the truncating `prompt.submit` above: one atomic call, and the same seam #745 needs. Alternative: `command.dispatch("retry")` followed by `prompt.submit`. That takes two writes, refuses attached media (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:750-774`), and widens `command.dispatch` beyond skills (`BotConversation.swift:1046-1076` deliberately runs nothing else; `HermesCall.swift:339-343` admits one bare name).
4. **Reset time.** Recommend a static "Limit resets at 14:05" formatted in the user's locale, hidden once the moment has passed on the next redraw. Alternative: a live countdown. It repaints every second, which the performance rules rule out.
5. **Warning text.** Recommend showing the host's `warning` verbatim. It is a free-form field, so a fixed Hermex sentence could lie if the host adds another warning. Alternative: a localized sentence keyed on the field being present.
6. **Scope.** Recommend Bot Chat only. Session-level `error` events outside a turn (`events.py:86-92`) and room `turn.failed` lines (`BotGroupRoom.swift:109`) stay as they are. Alternative: fold them in now, which is a larger change with different sources.

## Acceptance

- A turn that fails with a rate limit shows the row under the turn: a title, the provider detail, "Limit resets at HH:MM" when the host sent `resets_at`, and Retry.
- A failure the host marks `retryable: false` (bad key, billing, unknown model) shows no Retry.
- A billing wall shows the host's billing message and an "Open billing page" button that opens Safari.
- A turn that ends with the "was not saved" warning shows it, even when the turn succeeded.
- Reopening the chat, returning from the background, or tapping a "Turn failed" push rebuilds the title, detail and Retry from the resume snapshot.
- Retry starts the turn again without duplicating the prompt in the transcript, and Desktop shows the same transcript after it reloads.
- Sending a new message hides the row as soon as the host accepts it. A refused send keeps it.
- A user Stop shows no row.
- The Sad face and the Live Activity's failed state behave exactly as before.

## Tests

In `BotConversationTests` with `BotFixtureWire`. Each fails today because nothing decodes these fields:
- `testAFailedTurnReadsTheHostsReasonFromTheResumeSnapshot`: `inflight` with `error` and `error_surface {layer: provider, code: rate_limit, retryable: true, resets_at}` produces a `turnFailure` with those values. It survives `suspend()` then `recover()`.
- `testRetryIsOfferedOnlyWhenTheHostSaysItCanHelp`: `retryable: false` means no Retry; a missing surface with `recoverable: true` means Retry.
- `testBillingAndTheSaveWarningComeFromMessageComplete`: a live `message.complete` with `billing` and `warning` sets `turnNotice`, and a replayed one does too after a reconnect.
- `testTheOutcomeRowClearsWhenTheNextSendIsAccepted`: it stays after a rejected send.
- `testRetryResubmitsTheFailedPromptInPlace`: exact `prompt.submit` params (row id, raw text, both confirmations, no `queued`), then a refresh. 4009 shows the wait message and nothing else.
- `testAStopShowsNoOutcomeRow`.

Also:
- `HermesRequestTests.testEveryCallSendsItsExactWireShape`: add `promptRewind`.
- `BotLiveActivityTests.testAHostErrorEndsAsFailedAndAStopAsCancelled` must keep passing unchanged.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesRequestTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests`

## Mocks

Required first. States:
- rate limit with a reset time and Retry;
- bad API key (no Retry);
- billing wall with the link;
- context overflow;
- unknown failure with only raw error text;
- a partial reply followed by a failure;
- the "not saved" warning under a successful reply.

Show each in light and dark, and one at the largest accessibility text size.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

Use the test bot on a disposable Profile, never a daily-driver bot.

1. Give the test Profile a model whose provider key is invalid, then send "hi" in Bot Chat. Expected: the Sad face and a row titled for rejected credentials, with the provider detail and no Retry.
2. Background the app for a minute, then reopen the chat through the tunnel. Expected: the same row, rebuilt from the host.
3. Put the working model back and send "hi". Expected: the row disappears as soon as the host accepts the message, and the reply arrives.
4. For a retryable failure, stop a local model endpoint the Profile uses (for example Ollama), or use a provider that is rate-limiting, then send a message. Expected: the row offers Retry, plus a reset time if the provider named one. Bring the endpoint back and tap Retry. Expected: the turn runs again, and the prompt appears once, both here and in Desktop after it reloads.
5. VoiceOver: the row reads the title, then the detail, then its buttons.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** Bot Chat opened from the inbox, a deep link, a "Turn failed" push (`hermex-push` `2f1388c`, `plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:284-287`), or the Live Activity all land on the same conversation. The row rebuilds from the snapshot, so every entry shows it. Rooms and Sessions are out of scope (Decision 6).
- **Targets:** main app only. The Live Activity keeps showing just "failed", with no new text on the Lock Screen. No change to the share extension or notification service.
- **Servers:** the outcome lives on the per-server, per-connection, per-Profile `BotConversation` and is never cached, so it cannot appear under another server.
- **Contracts:** tolerant decode of existing fields and one new `HermesCall` case, shared with #745.
- **Reverse states:** the row clears on the next accepted send, on the host clearing the failure, and on Stop. Retry has a way out: the new turn can be stopped like any other.
- **Connection modes:** the retained failure comes from `session.resume`, so LAN, tunnel and reconnect after backgrounding all rebuild it. The live-only billing and warning come back only while the replay ring holds them.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver order and button labels, Dynamic Type (the row wraps; nothing truncates except the 4-line detail), light and dark, no animation, all shipped languages in the String Catalog.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(files): open files Hermex can't preview in Quick Look
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

PDFs, Office documents, audio and video open to a dead end. The workspace file preview marks them unsupported and shows "No Preview" with only an Export button.

- The list is hard-coded: `pdf`, `doc`/`docx`, `xls`/`xlsx`, `ppt`/`pptx`, `mp3`, `m4a`, `wav`, `mp4`, `mov`, `svg`, `zip` and more (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewViewModel.swift:143-148`). `load()` sets `.unavailable` for them (`:84-85`). The view draws "No Preview" (`FilePreviewView.swift:191-208`) and keeps Export in the toolbar (`:90-98`).
- The same view opens from three places:
  1. The workspace Files browser (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FileBrowserView.swift:32-39`).
  2. File links in chat, and file chips in the composer (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:560-562`, `:648-672`).
  3. Chat attachments, through a separate view with its own copy of the same list (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatAttachmentPreviewView.swift:76-81`, used at `:405-406`). This sheet has no Export at all.
- Bots already solve this. `BotArtifactPreview` wraps `QLPreviewController`, owns its temporary file and deletes it on dismissal (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactPreview.swift:8-57`, `:92-112`). Its download is capped at 25 MB, even without a length header (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotArtifactDownload.swift:4-15`, `:29-54`).
- The webui download has no cap. `rawFileData` reads the whole body into memory (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+Workspace.swift:55-57` → `APIClient.swift:119-131`).

## Contract

Client-only on webui: no new route.

- Bytes still come from `GET /api/file/raw` (`git -C .codex-tmp/hermes-webui show c67fd2dd:api/routes.py`, `:13315-13316`). `_serve_file_bytes` (`:17925`) sends `Content-Length` (`:17959`), so the app can refuse a large file before it reads the body.
- On Hermes, #703 slice 3.1 moves file previews to `GET /api/fs/download` (`.codex-tmp/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:733-743`). That route has no size limit on the server, which is why #703 already plans a 25 MB client cap. Build the Quick Look path on a `download: () async throws -> Data` closure, like `BotArtifactPreviewModel.load(name:download:)` (`BotArtifactPreview.swift:14`), so #703 only swaps the data source.
- #700 must preserve: the Bot artifact cap and the `Content-Length` check in `BotArtifactDownload` (`:4-15`, `:37`) when it folds artifact download into `HermesREST`.

## Plan

- [ ] **Shared Quick Look pieces.** Move the temp-file owner and the viewer out of `BotArtifactPreview.swift` into a new `HermesMobile/Features/Shared/QuickLookFilePreview.swift`, with neutral names:
  - A temp file that deletes its directory when released (today `BotArtifactTemporaryFile`, `:53-57`), and a `write(data:name:)` helper that runs off the main actor (`:22-34`).
  - `QuickLookFileView`, today's private `BotNativeFilePreview` (`:92-112`).
  - `BotArtifactPreview` keeps its sheet and its generation guard, and uses the shared pieces. Update `BotArtifactTests.swift:110` if a type is renamed.
  - Add the new file to the main app target in `project.pbxproj` only (membership is explicit there, see `:510`, `:1097`).
- [ ] **One policy, not two lists.** Replace the two identical sets (`FilePreviewViewModel.swift:143-148`, `ChatAttachmentPreviewView.swift:76-81`) with one shared policy that says, per extension: Quick Look, or no preview. Archives, executables, object code and databases stay "no preview" (Decision 1).
- [ ] **Capped download.** Add a bounded read to `APIClient`, beside `sendDataReturningResponse` (`APIClient.swift:139-162`). It has to live in `APIClient.swift`, because `customHeaderProvider` is private there (`:17`).
  - Use `session.bytes(for:delegate: redirectHeaderStripper)`. Map 401 and non-2xx exactly as `mappedHTTPResponse` does (`:207-230`).
  - Throw "too large" when `expectedContentLength` is over the cap. Otherwise buffer with `BotArtifactBuffer` (`BotArtifactDownload.swift:4-15`), which also stops a chunked body at 25 MB.
  - Expose it as `rawFilePreviewData(sessionID:path:)` in `APIClient+Workspace.swift`.
- [ ] **Workspace preview.** In `FilePreviewViewModel.load()` (`:72-100`), send Quick Look types down the new path:
  - Add a `FilePreviewContent` case that holds the temp file (`:263-268`). Update every switch on it: `FilePreviewView.swift:180-193`, `ChatAttachmentPreviewView.swift:145-154`, `:243-257`, `:314-338`.
  - Keep the downloaded bytes in `exportData`, so Export doesn't download the file again (`:119-121`).
  - Skip the request when the size is already known and over the cap. Pass `entry.size` through `FilePreviewView.init` (`:27-44`); `WorkspaceEntry.size` is at `HermesMobile/Models/Workspace.swift:97`.
  - When the file is too large, show the existing No Preview layout with the existing string "This file is too large to preview on this device (25 MB maximum)." (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifact.swift:17`). Export stays.
- [ ] `FilePreviewView.previewContent` (`:179-194`): draw `QuickLookFileView` for the new case, full-bleed under the existing title and toolbar.
- [ ] **Attachment sheet.** Same change in `ChatAttachmentPreviewViewModel.load` (`ChatAttachmentPreviewView.swift:389-409`).
  - The audio check stays first, so `m4a`/`mp3`/`wav` keep the inline player (`:400-404`).
  - Use `item.size` (`:9`) for the known-size shortcut.
- [ ] After writing the temp file, check `QLPreviewController.canPreview(_:)`. If Quick Look declines, fall back to No Preview (Decision 2).
- [ ] Cleanup. The preview content owns the temp file, so a refresh, a dismissal or a server switch deletes it. The logged-in tree is rebuilt per server (`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:95`). Dismissing mid-download cancels the view's `.task`, which cancels the byte loop.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Files the preview can't show open in Quick Look from all three entry points (Files browser, chat file links, chat attachments). Files over about 25 MB don't preview and keep Export. Reuse the existing Quick Look wrapper.

1. **Zip and other archives stay unsupported.** Recommend: yes. Apple's list of what `QLPreviewController` shows (iWork, Office, RTF, PDF, images, `public.text`, CSV, USDZ) has no archives, so an archive would only show a file icon. Also keep `7z`, `a`, `bin`, `bz2`, `class`, `db`, `dmg`, `dylib`, `exe`, `gz`, `jar`, `o`, `pkg`, `pyc`, `rar`, `sqlite`, `tar`, `tgz` and `xz` on No Preview with Export. Alternative: send them to Quick Look too. That means a download that ends at an icon.
2. **Formats that may not render.** Recommend: send `svg`, `flac`, `avi` and `aiff` to Quick Look, and let `canPreview` decide after the download. On-device support for these wasn't verified. Alternative: a smaller fixed allow-list, which needs guessing now and editing later.
3. **Quick Look types that fall into the text path today.** `key`, `numbers`, `pages`, `rtf` and `usdz` aren't on the list, so they go to `/api/file` as text (`FilePreviewViewModel.swift:86-99`). Recommend: add them to the Quick Look set; it's five entries in the same policy. Alternative: leave them for a follow-up.
4. **The cap.** Recommend: reuse `BotArtifactBuffer.maximumBytes` (25 MB) and its buffer type as they are. Alternative: rename the buffer to a neutral name, which edits `Networking/Bots/` files #700 is about to rework.
5. **Export in the attachment sheet.** It has none today. Recommend: don't add one here. Over the cap it shows the too-large message, and under the cap the user can use Quick Look's own sharing. Alternative: add the Export button from `FilePreviewView` for parity.
6. **`MEDIA:` references to documents.** These render an export chip (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMediaView.swift:150-158`), not a preview dead end. Recommend: out of scope. Alternative: route them to Quick Look too.

## Acceptance

- A PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, MP4 or MP3 up to 25 MB opens in Quick Look from the Files browser, from a chat file link and from a chat attachment.
- A ZIP still shows No Preview with Export.
- A file over 25 MB shows "This file is too large to preview on this device (25 MB maximum)." Export still works in the file preview. A workspace entry with a known size over the cap makes no preview request.
- Export after a Quick Look preview reuses the downloaded bytes (one `/api/file/raw` request in total).
- Dismissing the preview, or switching servers, deletes the temporary file.
- Bot artifact previews behave as before.

## Tests

- `APIClientWorkspaceFileTests`, next to `testFilePreviewExportPayloadFetchesRawDataForUnsupportedPreview` (`:575`). Keep that test: zip stays unsupported. Add:
  - `testFilePreviewOpensPDFInQuickLook`: `Docs/report.pdf` makes one `/api/file/raw` request, the preview is the Quick Look case with a `report.pdf` file on disk, and `exportPayload()` makes no second request. Fails today: pdf is `.unavailable` with no request.
  - `testFilePreviewRefusesAFileOverTheCap`: a response with `Content-Length` over 25 MB gives the too-large state and writes no file.
  - `testFilePreviewSkipsTheRequestWhenTheKnownSizeIsOverTheCap`: no request at all.
  - `testQuickLookFileIsDeletedWhenThePreviewIsReleased`.
- New `ChatAttachmentPreviewViewModelTests`:
  - A `pdf` attachment gives the Quick Look case (fails today).
  - An `m4a` still gives `.audio`.
  - A `zip` still gives `.unavailable`.
- `BotArtifactTests`: the existing `testPreviewCleanupAndLateDownloadCannotRecreateDismissedPreview` (`:109`) must still pass after the move.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientWorkspaceFileTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatAttachmentPreviewViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests`

## Mocks

Not required. Quick Look is the system viewer and fills the existing content area. Title, toolbar and Export don't change, and the too-large state reuses the No Preview layout with an existing string.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build). Put a small PDF, a DOCX, an XLSX, an MP4, an MP3, a ZIP and a 40 MB MP4 in a session's workspace.

1. Files → open each file. PDF, DOCX, XLSX, MP4 and MP3 render or play in Quick Look. The ZIP shows No Preview with Export.
2. Open the 40 MB MP4. You see the 25 MB message, and Export saves the file.
3. Ask the agent to "link report.pdf". Tap the link: the sheet opens Quick Look. Tap Done.
4. Attach the PDF in the composer and send it. Tap the attachment in the sent message: Quick Look.
5. Over the Cloudflare tunnel, open the 20 MB file and tap Done before it loads. Reopen it: it loads normally.
6. Switch to another server and back. Nothing from the first server shows.
7. Open a Bot artifact PDF: unchanged.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the Files browser (including search results, which open the same destination), chat file links, composer file chips, and chat attachments. Bot artifacts already use Quick Look. `MEDIA:` document references are out of scope (Decision 6).
- **Targets:** main app only; new shared file in the main target. Tests in `HermesMobileTests`. Share extension, Live Activity widget and notification service are untouched.
- **Servers:** temp files belong to one presentation, and nothing is cached across servers. The server switch rebuilds the tree, which releases the file.
- **Contracts:** webui `GET /api/file/raw` unchanged. The cap anticipates #703's Hermes route (see Contract).
- **Reverse states:** Done or back deletes the file. Too large → Export.
- **Connection modes:** the cap limits tunnel and cellular downloads. Dismissal cancels the download.
- **Native quality:** Quick Look brings its own VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, dark mode and zoom. No new strings if the existing 25 MB string is reused. No animation.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md:424-441` describes the Bot Quick Look path; update it only if the move changes what it says.

## Outside reach

None.

title: fix(bots): sign-in errors that name the real problem
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Three sign-in failures show a message that sends the user to the wrong fix.

**1. An access proxy's sign-in page reads as "not a dashboard".** Behind Cloudflare Access, `GET /api/status` is redirected to the proxy's login page on another host. `HermesConnection` sends every request with `CrossOriginHeaderStripper` as the task delegate (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:38`, `:55`, `:197`). That delegate only strips custom headers (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:367-408`), so the redirect is followed. The HTML page then fails to decode and becomes `.notDashboard` (`HermesConnection.swift:94`); a 401 from the proxy becomes `.notDashboard` too (`:93`). The user reads "hermes.example isn't a Hermes dashboard. Use the dashboard address, not the Hermes Web UI." (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:98-99`) for an address that is correct. The status screen already knows better: its probe calls a cross-host redirect or a 401/403 `.blocked` (`BotProtocol.swift:215`), but that probe runs only from `checkStatus()` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:280`), never during sign-in.

**2. A host that only offers browser sign-in reads as "no Bot chat".** When `/api/status` lists no `basic` provider (an OIDC host using `nous` or `self-hosted`), sign-in throws `.unsupported` (`HermesConnection.swift:99-100`), whose copy is "This Hermes connection does not support Bot chat here." (`BotProtocol.swift:47`). The host supports Bot chat; Hermex just can't do browser sign-in yet (#708).

**3. A refused gateway upgrade reads as "couldn't reach".** After a good HTTP sign-in, the `/api/ws` upgrade can still be refused. The failure arrives as a raw `URLError` from the first `task.receive()` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:227-233`, `:414`). The form shows "Couldn't reach hermes.example. Check the address and network." (`BotProtocol.swift:89`), the inbox counts it as a route failure and retries (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:391-395`), and a chat reads any non-`BotFailure` error as `.transport` and retries quietly (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:1496-1498`). The comment at `BotProtocol.swift:52-54` says "Hermes never answers 403 or 520-530 itself": true for its REST routes, wrong for this upgrade.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract. Host behavior this relies on, at the pin:

- `/api/status` is public (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/public_paths.py:15`) and reports `auth_required`, `auth_providers` (provider names) and `auth_flows` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:357-379`, read at `:496`, merged into the reply at `:518`). The only password provider shipped is `basic` (`plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py:117-119`); `nous` and `self-hosted` are OIDC (`plugins/dashboard_auth/nous/__init__.py:43`, `plugins/dashboard_auth/self_hosted/__init__.py:79`). `basic` registers alongside any other provider once `dashboard.basic_auth` has a username and password (`basic/__init__.py:1-8`, `:256-263`). Hermex always logs in as provider `basic` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:37-40`).
- The webui answers an unknown `/api/*` path with 401 and a JSON body `{"error":"Authentication required"}` when its auth is on (`git -C .codex-tmp/hermes-webui show c67fd2dd:api/auth.py`, lines 1096-1102).
- `/api/ws` checks the ticket, Host and peer before accepting, and closes before accept on failure (`hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:139-151`, `:583-585`). Closing before accept reaches the client as an HTTP 403 handshake failure with no close code (`tests/hermes_cli/test_display_ws_ticket.py:30-34`). The ticket travels in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (`hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py:206-217`; a missing one is `no_credential`, `:265-270`) and lives 30 s (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/ws_tickets.py:21`). So a proxy that drops that header, or one without WebSocket support, is refused after a good sign-in.

## Plan

- [ ] `BotProtocol.swift:39-64`: add three `BotFailure` cases with hostless copy (table below), so the room screen, which shows `localizedDescription` (`BotRoomReader.swift:425-429`), gets the same words: `blocked`, `browserSignIn`, `upgradeRefused(Int)`. Rewrite the comment at `:52-54`: Hermes's REST routes never answer 403, but the gateway upgrade does (see `.upgradeRefused`). `BotConnectionAdvice` (`:70-106`) needs no new branch: `case let failure?` already returns the description.
- [ ] `HermesConnection.send` (`HermesConnection.swift:195-201`): when the final `response.url` is not the request's origin (`HermesHeaders.isSameOrigin`, `:291-300`), throw `.blocked` before looking at the status. This covers the status, login, identity and ticket steps and every REST call.
- [ ] Status read in `beginSignIn` (`HermesConnection.swift:89-94`): a 401 whose body decodes as a JSON object stays `.notDashboard` (the webui shape); any other 401 is `.blocked`. 404 and a non-JSON 200 stay `.notDashboard`. This needs the 401 body, so read the status step with a small helper beside `decoded` (`:185-189`) that keeps the response.
- [ ] Status gate (`HermesConnection.swift:99-100`): `auth_required == true` with no `basic` in `auth_providers` throws `.browserSignIn`. `auth_required` false or missing stays `.unsupported` (Decision 4). Leave a one-line comment that #708 replaces this branch with the browser flow.
- [ ] `NativeBotSocket.receive` (`HermesGateway.swift:412-417`): when the receive fails and `task.response` is an `HTTPURLResponse` with a status other than 101, throw the mapped failure instead: 408, 429 and 5xx become `.rejected(status)` (today's retry and proxy/tunnel copy), anything else becomes `.upgradeRefused(status)`. Put the mapping in one pure function so tests reach it without a socket. Keep the socket boundary (`BotSocket`, `:406-410`) unchanged.
- [ ] Retry classification: add `.blocked`, `.browserSignIn` and `.upgradeRefused` to the permanent list in `BotInbox.isRetryable` (`BotInbox.swift:379-387`). `BotConversation.disconnected` already treats any other `BotFailure` as permanent (`BotConversation.swift:1496-1501`); keep it that way. `BotInbox.isRouteFailure` (`:391-395`) is unchanged, so a 5xx upgrade still counts toward the route advice.
- [ ] Push setup: in `HermexPushProvisioner.message(for:)` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift:327-366`), add `.browserSignIn` to the password-sign-in row at `:359`, and return `.blocked`'s own description instead of falling to "This step did not finish" (`:363-364`). Push setup never opens the socket, so `.upgradeRefused` can't reach it.
- [ ] Add the three strings to `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` in all 17 shipped languages as `needs_review`, following `docs/agents/i18n.md`.
- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md:147-149`: extend the sentence to name the three new cases: an access proxy's sign-in, a host with browser sign-in only, and a refused gateway upgrade.

Proposed copy (hostless, so one string serves the form, inbox, chat and room; match the file's straight apostrophes):

| Failure | Message |
|---|---|
| `.blocked` | Something in front of Hermes, such as Cloudflare Access, wants its own sign-in first. Hermex can't do that yet. Use an address that skips it, such as the dashboard's local network address. |
| `.browserSignIn` | This Hermes host only offers sign-in with a browser, which Hermex doesn't support yet. To connect now, add a dashboard username and password on the host. |
| `.upgradeRefused` | Hermes accepted the sign-in, but the live connection was refused. If a proxy or tunnel sits in front of Hermes, turn on WebSocket support and let the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header through. |

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** These three cases (an access proxy's login redirect, a host that only offers browser sign-in, and a refused `/api/ws` upgrade) get accurate, actionable copy instead of today's misleading messages. The browser sign-in case says it isn't supported yet and does not implement OIDC (that is #708).

1. **How to spot the redirect.** Recommend following it and comparing the final URL's origin, as the status probe already does (`BotProtocol.swift:215`) with a tested fixture (`HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:536-557`). Alternative: a Hermes-only delegate that refuses cross-origin redirects. Nothing would then reach the other host at all (today a 307/308 on the login POST would carry the body there), but a refused redirect needs new fixture work, and the status GET, which is sent first, already stops an access proxy.
2. **401 on `/api/status`.** Recommend reading a 401 with a JSON-object body as the webui (`.notDashboard`) and any other 401 as `.blocked`. Cloudflare Access can answer 401 instead of redirecting, and Hermes never 401s this public route. Alternative: keep every 401 on `.notDashboard` and reword it to mention both causes, which is longer and leaves the user to guess.
3. **Refused upgrade is permanent.** Recommend showing the copy with Reconnect and stopping the quiet retry for non-5xx statuses: a proxy that drops the header doesn't heal on its own, and each retry mints a ticket. 408, 429 and 5xx keep retrying as today. Alternative: keep retrying and change only the copy.
4. **`auth_required: false` stays `.unsupported`.** A phone reaches such a host only through a tunnel that rewrites the Host header, because a loopback-bound host without `dashboard.public_url` answers any other Host with 400 (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:480-491`, `:1122`). Keeps `testMissingPasswordGateFailsBeforeCredentialsOrSocket` (`HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests.swift:773-787`) as is. Alternative: its own sentence, for a rare case.
5. **Copy.** Recommend the table above as the review artifact (text inside existing error rows, no layout change), as #751 did. Approve or edit it on this issue.
6. **Provider check by name.** Recommend checking for `basic` in `auth_providers` (what the gate does today). It matches exactly what Hermex can log in with. Alternative: read `supports_password` from `/api/auth/providers` (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py:183-192`), one more request for no gain until #708.

## Acceptance

- Behind an access proxy that redirects to another host, the form, inbox, chat and room show the `.blocked` copy. No login request is sent, and the inbox doesn't retry on its own.
- A 401 on `/api/status` with a non-JSON body shows the `.blocked` copy; the webui address (JSON 401 or 404) still shows "isn't a Hermes dashboard".
- A host whose `auth_providers` lacks `basic` shows the browser sign-in copy, and no login request is sent.
- A gateway upgrade refused with 403 (or any other non-5xx status except 408/429) shows the refused copy with Reconnect in the form, inbox and chat, and neither retries on its own. A 502 at the upgrade still retries quietly as today.
- Push setup's sign-in step shows the `.blocked` and browser sign-in copy, not "This step did not finish".
- Every existing row in `BotConnectionAdviceTests` keeps its text.

## Tests

- `BotClientTests` (`HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests.swift`), using `BotHTTPFixture` (`:1023-1036`). Give the fixture a `redirect` like `BotStatusHTTPFixture.redirect` (`BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:545-557`) and a raw-body option:
  - `/api/status` redirected to `https://team.cloudflareaccess.com/…` throws `.blocked`, and the only path requested is `/api/status`.
  - A 401 with an HTML body throws `.blocked`; the existing JSON 401/404 test (`:836-851`) still expects `.notDashboard`.
  - `auth_required: true, auth_providers: ["nous"]` throws `.browserSignIn`, and no `/auth/password-login` request is made.
  - The upgrade mapping function: 101 maps to nothing, 403 and 404 to `.upgradeRefused`, 429 and 502 to `.rejected`.
  - A `BotScriptedSocket` whose first receive throws `.upgradeRefused(403)` makes `connect()` throw it.
- `BotConnectionAdviceTests` (`BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:397-430`): one row each for `.blocked`, `.browserSignIn`, `.upgradeRefused(403)`.
- `BotInboxTests`: beside `testAWebUIAddressShowsTheAdviceInsteadOfRetryingForever` (`HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests.swift:614`), each new case shows its message, leaves the skeleton, and builds one wire (`spare == 1`).
- `BotConversationTests`: beside `testReconnectStopsWithAdviceWhenTheAddressIsNotADashboard` (`HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests.swift:270`), `.upgradeRefused(403)` on reconnect sets the message and schedules no retry.
- `HermexPushProvisioningTests`: a sign-in failing with `.blocked` or `.browserSignIn` shows that copy.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionAdviceTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`

## Mocks

Not required: three new sentences inside existing error rows, no layout change. The copy table is the review artifact.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build). The maintainer's host is reachable only through the Cloudflare tunnel.

1. Settings → the server → Hermes connection → Connect with the tunnel address. Expected: it connects as before.
2. Enter the webui address and Connect. Expected: "… isn't a Hermes dashboard. Use the dashboard address, not the Hermes Web UI." (unchanged).
3. Open the Bots inbox and a chat, background the app past the tunnel's idle timeout, return. Expected: both reconnect quietly; no new message appears.
4. Only if a hostname behind Cloudflare Access is available: enter it and Connect. Expected: the `.blocked` copy.

The browser sign-in and refused-upgrade cases need host or proxy changes, so `BotClientTests` covers them.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the one connection form (Bots inbox gear `BotsInboxView.swift:171-173`, sheet `:511-512`; Settings `SettingsView.swift:2242-2247`; push `HermexPushSectionView.swift:126-127`), the inbox message row (`BotsInboxView.swift:68-70`), the chat pill, the room pill (`BotRoomReader.swift:425-429`), and push setup's sign-in step (`HermexPushProvisioner.swift:314-321`).
- **Targets:** main app only. `BotProtocol.swift`, `HermesConnection.swift` and `HermesGateway.swift` are in the `HermesMobile` target alone.
- **Servers:** the copy is hostless and nothing is stored, so nothing crosses servers.
- **Contracts:** status read and socket failure mapping only; no request changes.
- **Reverse states:** every new failure keeps the Reconnect button (#884 swaps it for a rejected password only).
- **Connection modes:** the redirect and 401 rows are the Cloudflare Access case; the refused upgrade is the reverse-proxy and tunnel case; LAN is unchanged.
- **Native quality:** three strings in all 17 languages; the error `Text` rows already wrap for Dynamic Type.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md:147-149`.
- **Related issues:**
  - #700 must keep these classifications when it moves sign-in and reconnect into the server-type work: `.blocked` in the shared send path, `.browserSignIn` at the status gate, the upgrade mapping at the socket. Its 0.3 Add Server probe should reuse `BotConnectionAdvice` rather than write new 400/401/429 copy. When #700 adds editable headers (#657), point the `.blocked` copy at the service-token headers. Until then there is no editor to name (`HermesConnection.swift:255-262`: production passes `.none`).
  - #708 slice 8.3 replaces the `.browserSignIn` branch with the real browser flow. It detects OIDC through `auth_flows` and `/api/auth/providers`; this issue uses only `auth_providers` names and implements no OIDC.
  - #744 should treat `.blocked` and a non-JSON 401 on a route's probe as "route unusable", like its Host-header 400, so a tunnel behind Access falls back to the LAN route.
  - #751 (merged via #780) owns the advice table. Keep every row, its ATS string, and the rule that `URLError` is never wrapped for retry purposes (only the upgrade's HTTP status is mapped here).
  - #752 (merged via #785) owns the status probe. Don't change `BotHostStatusProbe` or "Check again"; this issue brings sign-in in line with the probe's `.blocked` rule.

## Outside reach

None.
