title: fix(push): hold approval and reply banners instead of dropping them
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P1 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

If the phone is offline for a moment when a push goes out (a lift, a tunnel, a weak signal), the push is lost for good. An approval the user never sees leaves the agent blocked until the approval times out. A reply the user never sees means they don't know the run finished.

The relay tells APNs not to keep anything. Its one shared `send()` hardcodes `'apns-expiration': '0'` (`hermex-push/relay/src/apns.ts:47`, hermex-push `2f1388c`). With `0`, APNs tries to deliver once and doesn't store the push. With a future date, APNs stores it and delivers it when the phone comes back. It keeps only the most recent notification per app, so a phone coming back gets the latest banner, not a backlog. That one header covers every banner kind: reply, approval, clarify and turn_error (`bannerPush`, `apns.ts:76-89`). It also covers every Live Activity push, including `end` (`activityPush`, `apns.ts:91-104`).

Nothing chose `0` on purpose. It arrived with the first relay commit (`b57627c`), and no test checks the header (`relay/test/apns.test.ts:47-54` checks topic, priority and push type only). The only retry is at the HTTP level: after a 5xx the plugin retries once, 2 s later (`plugin/hermex_push/relay.py:113-137`). That does nothing for a phone that is offline.

Approvals time out after 300 s by default (`.codex-tmp/hermes-agent/tools/approval_context.py:239-257`, pin `ca678285`).

## Contract

No host, app or plugin change. The code lands in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, in `relay/` only.

- APNs `apns-expiration`: a UNIX time in seconds. `0` means "try once, don't store". A nonzero value means "store and keep trying until that time". APNs stores at most one notification per bundle ID. ([Sending notification requests to APNs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/sending-notification-requests-to-apns))
- The relay's HTTP contract with the plugin and the app doesn't change.

Deploy order: the hermex-push PR merges, then the maintainer deploys the relay. Agents never deploy. There is no Hermex PR. This issue closes once the relay is deployed.

## Plan

All in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, in one PR (suggested title `fix(relay): let APNs hold banners while a phone is offline`).

- [ ] `relay/src/policy.ts:3-6, 13-25`: add `hold` (seconds APNs may store the push) to the `banner` variant of `Delivery`. Set it from the table in Decisions: approval and clarify 300, reply and turn_error 3600. Delivery etiquette stays in this one pure file.
- [ ] `relay/src/apns.ts:5`: add `expiration: number` to `Push` (UNIX seconds, `0` = don't store).
- [ ] `apns.ts:76-89` `bannerPush`: take `now` (seconds) and set `expiration: now + policy.hold`. Pass `Math.floor(now / 1000)` from `coordinator.ts:188-189`.
- [ ] `apns.ts:91-104` `activityPush`: set `expiration` to `now + 900` for `event: 'end'` (`done` / `failed`) and to `0` for every `update`.
- [ ] `apns.ts:47`: send `String(push.expiration)` in place of the literal `'0'`.
- [ ] `relay/README.md:65, 67`: one sentence each giving the hold for banners and for activity pushes.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Approvals and questions are held for up to 5 minutes (under the approval timeout), and replies for about an hour. Routine Live Activity updates keep `0`.

1. **Exact values.** Recommended:

   | Push | Hold |
   | --- | --- |
   | `approval` | 300 s |
   | `clarify` | 300 s |
   | `reply` | 3600 s |
   | `turn_error` | 3600 s |
   | Activity `update`, routine or status change | 0 |
   | Activity `end` (`done`, `failed`) | 900 s |

2. **`turn_error`: 3600 s.** A failed run is still true an hour later, just like a reply. Alternative: 300 s, if a late failure banner feels stale.
3. **`end`: 900 s, not 0.** With `0`, a phone that was offline at the end of a run never learns the run ended. Its activity shows "running" until the 15-minute stale date greys it. 900 s matches that stale date and the relay's end marker (`coordinator.ts:263-267`). A stored `end` targets the old activity's own token, so it can't touch a newer activity. Apple doesn't say whether Live Activity pushes share the one-per-app storage slot with banners. Either way the latest push wins, which is fine. Alternative: keep `0` and accept a stale activity after a network drop.
4. **Clock: the relay's `now`, not the plugin's `sent_at`.** Host clock skew could put a `sent_at`-based expiry in the past. Relay time is at most a couple of seconds later than the host event. Alternative: `sent_at + hold`. That is closer to the host's own timeout, but it trusts the host clock.
5. **Questions wait longer than 5 minutes on the host.** The clarify timeout defaults to 3600 s (`tools/clarify_gateway.py:259-266`, `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:204-211`). A question banner missed for more than 5 minutes is dropped while the agent is still waiting. Recommend keeping 300 s as decided. Alternative: hold `clarify` for 3600 s like replies.
6. **Docs: the relay README only.** `docs/agents/push.md` is the map and has no delivery details. Alternative: add one line to push.md, which would mean a Hermex docs PR.

## Acceptance

- A banner carries `apns-expiration` = send time + its hold: 300 s for approval and clarify, 3600 s for reply and turn_error.
- A Live Activity `update` carries `0`. An `end` carries send time + 900 s.
- Nothing else in the payloads, priorities, collapse ids or delivery policy changes.
- On a phone that was offline for less than the hold, the latest banner arrives once it's back online.

## Tests

- `relay/test/apns.test.ts`: a new table test builds a banner for each kind at a fixed `now` and checks `push.expiration`. Extend the existing header test (`:47-54`) so `'apns-expiration'` is `'0'` for a routine update and `String(now + 900)` for a `done` push. Both fail today, because the header is always `'0'`.
- `relay/test/policy.test.ts:7, 15`: the exact `banner` objects gain `hold` (300 or 3600).
- Run: `cd relay && npm run check` (typecheck plus vitest; relay CI runs the same plus `deploy:dry-run`).

## Mocks

Not required: this is a relay header change with no UI.

## Manual test

Device: a physical iPhone with any current Hermex build, paired to a server. No app build is needed. The maintainer deploys the relay before this check.

1. With the app in the background and no Live Activity, turn on Airplane Mode. From the Mac, start a turn in a disposable session that asks for an approval. After a minute, turn Airplane Mode off. Expected: the approval banner arrives within seconds.
2. Repeat with a turn that just replies. Stay offline for about 10 minutes, then reconnect. Expected: the reply banner arrives.
3. Repeat step 1 but stay offline for 6 minutes or more. Expected: no approval banner. A "turn failed" banner can appear if the approval timed out.
4. Clean up the disposable session.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** every relay banner kind, for bot, webui and other sources. Live Activity pushes for bot and webui runs.
- **Targets:** none in Hermex. The NSE sees the same payloads, just later.
- **Servers:** holds are per push, and each push is already per install. No change to isolation.
- **Contracts:** APNs request headers only. The relay's HTTP contract is unchanged.
- **Reverse states:** a held approval that the user answered elsewhere can still arrive late. A tap on it only navigates, as today.
- **Connection modes:** helps phones that drop off cellular or Wi-Fi. LAN versus tunnel doesn't matter, because this is the relay-to-APNs leg.
- **Native quality:** no UI.
- **Docs:** `hermex-push/relay/README.md`.

## Outside reach

The maintainer deploys the relay (`npm run deploy` from `relay/`).

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-agent ca678285 and hermes-webui c67fd2dd; hermex-push 2f1388c.

title: perf(push): send progress only when a phone is watching
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

The plugin posts Live Activity progress for every eligible session, whether or not any phone shows a Live Activity for it. Most of that traffic goes nowhere, and each request costs a Worker request and a Durable Object call.

- `HermexPush._emit_progress` sends every snapshot that passes `should_notify` (`hermex-push/plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:191-205`, hermex-push `2f1388c`). Routine updates are throttled to one per session every 5 s (`plugin/hermex_push/progress.py:15`, from hermex-push#11). A session that stays busy can still send about 17,000 requests a day.
- CLI and other non-chat platforms are eligible too (`plugin/hermex_push/sources.py:38-44`). No phone ever has an activity for those sessions.
- Every non-health request reaches the install's Durable Object (`relay/src/index.ts:63`). For progress, the relay already knows the answer: `notifyProgress` finds no activity for the session and sends nothing (`relay/src/coordinator.ts:209-234`). It then answers `200 {"result":"accepted"}`, the same as when it did deliver. So the plugin can't tell the difference.

This is cost hygiene on Workers Paid, not an outage fix.

## Contract

Code lands in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, in `relay/` and `plugin/`, in one PR. There is no host change and no app change.

- **Relay (new result value).** `POST /installs/{key}/notify` with `kind: progress` answers `200 {"result":"no_activity"}` when no registered device has a live activity for `session_id`. Otherwise it answers `200 {"result":"accepted"}` as today. Other kinds and other status codes don't change.
- **How the phone registers.** The app creates the activity and forwards each ActivityKit push token with `PUT /installs/{key}/devices/{token}/activities/{session_id}` (`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:819-837` → `HermesMobile/Push/PushRegistrar.swift:382-389, 495-498`). It re-sends them on launch (`PushRegistrar.swift:299`). Only the relay sees these calls, so the relay's reply to progress is the only way the plugin can learn about them without polling.
- **Compatibility.** An old plugin ignores the response body. A new plugin talking to an old relay always sees `accepted`, so it keeps today's cadence. Neither order breaks anything. Deploy the relay first anyway, so the saving shows up as soon as the plugin updates.

Order: the hermex-push PR merges, then the maintainer deploys the relay, then updates the plugin on the host. Agents never deploy. A small Hermex docs PR links the hermex-push PR.

## Plan

**`uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`** (suggested title `perf(plugin): slow progress for sessions no phone is watching`):

- [ ] `relay/src/coordinator.ts:224-233`: after the end-marker cleanup, return `ok('no_activity')` when `active` is empty and `ok('accepted')` otherwise.
- [ ] `relay/README.md:61`: add `no_activity` to the 200 results, with one sentence on what it means.
- [ ] `plugin/hermex_push/relay.py:26, 53-62, 113-137`: the post function returns `(status, result)`. `_urllib_post` reads the small JSON body and takes `result`, or `""` when it can't parse it. `enqueue(url, event, on_result=None)` calls `on_result(result)` on the drain thread after a 2xx. It is never called after a failure.
- [ ] `plugin/hermex_push/progress.py`: add `quiet_until` to `SessionProgress`.
  - `unwatched(session_id, now)` sets `quiet_until = now + QUIET_SECONDS` (60), but only once `now - started_at >= GRACE_SECONDS` (30).
  - `watched(session_id)` clears `quiet_until`.
  - In `_update`, a routine update (no status change) while `now < quiet_until` is held as pending. A status change still goes out at once.
  - `due` and `flush_delay` wait for the later of `last_emit + HOLD_SECONDS` and `quiet_until`. When the quiet window ends, the held update goes out and serves as the next probe.
- [ ] `plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:191-205`: `_emit_progress` passes an `on_result` for that session. Under `self._lock`, `no_activity` calls `unwatched` and any other 2xx result calls `watched`. Then it calls `_arm_flush()`.
- [ ] `plugin/hermex_push_tests/conftest.py`: `CapturingSender.enqueue` accepts `on_result`.
- [ ] `plugin/README.md:81-92`: update the progress cadence line. Bump `PLUGIN_VERSION` in all four files (README § Development).

**`hermex`** (docs only; land after the relay deploy):

- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md:888-903` (Freshness): one sentence. A session no phone watches gets routine progress about once a minute, so an activity started mid-turn catches up within a minute or at the next status change.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** The plugin sends routine progress only while a phone has a Live Activity for that session. No usage-check automation; Uzair's Cloudflare billing alert covers spend.

1. **Signal: the relay's progress response.** It costs nothing extra, because the request is already made. Alternatives: a route the plugin polls (more requests, which defeats the point), or the phone telling the host (a new host route that is hard to reach across processes). Both rejected.
2. **A 30 s grace period, then one probe a minute.** The phone registers its activity token around the time the plugin sends a turn's first `running` event, so the first reply often says `no_activity` even for a watched turn. The grace period ignores that answer for the first 30 s of the turn. After that, an unwatched session sends at most one routine update a minute, down from 12. That is roughly 12 times less traffic for a session busy all day. An activity started mid-turn gets relay updates within 60 s, or at the next status change if that comes sooner. Alternative: back off from 5 s up to 60 s. It has no grace constant, but it is harder to reason about.
3. **Status changes always go out** (`running`, `waiting`, `done`, `failed`, at most a few per turn). They double as probes, and `done`/`failed` end the activity. Alternative: quiet them too. That saves almost nothing, and a watched activity could miss its end.
4. **No special case for CLI or `other` sessions.** The signal quiets them on its own. Alternative: skip progress for `source: other` outright. That saves the one-a-minute probe, but it hard-codes the assumption that no phone ever watches those sessions.
5. **Quiet state lives per turn.** `turn_ended` already forgets the session (`progress.py:96-101`), so every new turn starts at the normal cadence and probes again. There is no state to persist or expire.

## Acceptance

- A session with no Live Activity on any device: after its first 30 s, at most one routine progress event a minute reaches the relay. Status changes still go out at once.
- A session with a Live Activity: cadence unchanged, at most one routine update every 5 s.
- An activity registered mid-turn starts getting relay updates within 60 s, or at the next status change if sooner.
- Approvals, questions, replies and turn errors are untouched.
- Against an old relay, the plugin behaves as today.

## Tests

- `plugin/hermex_push_tests/test_progress.py`:
  - An unwatched answer inside the grace period is ignored.
  - After the grace period, routine updates are held until the quiet window ends, and the latest is flushed then.
  - A status change skips the window.
  - `watched` restores the 5 s cadence.
- `test_relay.py`: `deliver` hands the parsed `result` to `on_result` after a 2xx, `""` for a non-JSON body, and makes no call after a 4xx, a 5xx or a network error.
- `test_hooks.py`: a sender that answers `no_activity` quiets a long turn to one routine event a minute after 30 s. The next `waiting` still goes out at once.
- `relay/test/worker.test.ts:306-317` (progress without an activity) now expects `no_activity`. A new test covers an activity that exists (`accepted`) and a new turn after an end marker (`no_activity`). These fail today, because the relay always answers `accepted`.
- Run: `cd relay && npm run check`, and from the repo root `.venv/bin/python -m pytest plugin -q` (plugin README § Development). CI doesn't run plugin tests, so run them locally.

## Mocks

Not required: no UI.

## Manual test

Device: a physical iPhone with any current Hermex build, paired to a server. The maintainer deploys the relay and updates the plugin on the host (`hermes plugins update hermex-push`, then restart the Hermes processes) before this check.

1. In Hermex, start a long bot turn with several tool calls and lock the phone right away. Expected: the Live Activity keeps updating its tool count every few seconds, as before.
2. Start a long turn from the Mac (Desktop or CLI) with no activity on the phone. After a minute, open that chat in Hermex so it shows a Live Activity, then lock the phone. Expected: the activity picks up relay updates within about a minute.
3. During step 1, trigger an approval. Expected: the approval banner and the "Waiting" state both arrive at once.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** every relay-driven Live Activity: bot and webui runs on paired servers, including activities started on reattach.
- **Targets:** none in Hermex. The widget sees the same content state, just fewer routine updates for unwatched sessions.
- **Servers:** quiet state is per plugin process and per session. Each relay install is one server's pairing. No cross-server state.
- **Contracts:** one new `result` value on an existing 200. The request shape is unchanged.
- **Reverse states:** `watched` undoes `unwatched`, and every new turn starts un-quieted.
- **Connection modes:** unaffected. The host-to-relay leg only.
- **Native quality:** no UI.
- **Docs:** `hermex-push/relay/README.md`, `hermex-push/plugin/README.md`, and one sentence in `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Outside reach

The maintainer deploys the relay and updates the plugin on the host, then restarts the Hermes processes that run agents.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-agent ca678285 and hermes-webui c67fd2dd; hermex-push 2f1388c.

title: feat(chat): say what Allow session and Always allow cover
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

An approval card offers **Allow session** and **Always allow**, but it never says what they will allow. The user has to guess whether "Always allow" covers this one command, every command like it, or everything the bot does. That is exactly the moment a wrong guess costs the most.

- **Sessions** (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ApprovalRequestOverlay.swift:70-86`) shows the host's raw pattern keys as monospaced chips under a "Pattern keys" caption. A key such as `plugin_rule:browser:3f9a1c2b7d4e` means nothing to a user. All four buttons always show (`:102-112`).
- **Bot Chat** (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequestCard.swift:110-189`) shows the description and the command, then the host's offered choices, with no scope at all. `BotApprovalRequest` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequest.swift:84-131`) drops `pattern_key`, `pattern_keys` and `tool_name`. It reads `smart_denied`, `allow_session` and `allow_permanent` only to rebuild choices for an older host (`:117-123`).

## Contract

Client-only: no new calls. It reads fields both servers already send.

**What the keys are (hermes-agent `ca678285`):**
- **Shell commands.** `detect_dangerous_command` returns `(True, description, description)`, so the pattern key *is* the danger description, for example `recursive delete` or `system shutdown/reboot` (`tools/approval_detection.py:1515-1540`, used at `tools/approval.py:1084` and `:1197`).
- **Other kinds of key:**
  - `tirith:<rule_id>`: security-scanner findings (`tools/approval.py:1199-1206`).
  - `plugin_rule:<rule_key>`: plugin tool rules, where `rule_key` defaults to `<tool>:<sha12>` of the reason (`:1106-1113`).
  - `execute_code`: every Python script (`:1248`).
  - `ssh_config_write` (`tools/file_tools_write_guards.py:370-371`).
  - `cua:<action>:<foreground|background>`: computer use (`tools/computer_use/tool.py:396-398`).
- **Keys that can never be allowed.** Deleting the root filesystem, a system directory or the home directory never reaches an approval card (`tools/approval_detection.py:88-95`).

**What each choice does on Hermes (Bot Chat):**
- **Allow session** adds every key to an in-memory set for this chat's session key (`tools/approval.py:249-252`, `:380-389`). The TUI gateway never clears it, so it lasts until Hermes restarts (`clear_session` at `:285-291` has no caller under `tui_gateway/`).
- **Always allow** also adds each non-Tirith key to the Profile's own permanent set and writes it to that Profile's `command_allowlist` in `config.yaml` (`:328-347`, `:366-369`, `:380-389`, `:448-472`). It takes effect at once.
- **Tirith findings.** "Always" is downgraded to session for them (`:380-389`), and a prompt with only Tirith findings hides Always (`:1216-1223`).
- **Payload.** The approval payload carries `pattern_key`, `pattern_keys`, `description`, `allow_session`, `allow_permanent`, `smart_denied` and `choices` (`tools/approval.py:858-868`, `tui_gateway/server.py:711-724`). The snapshot's `pending_approval` has the same keys plus `tool_name` (`tui_gateway/contracts/common.py:195-208`, `contracts/server_requests.py:72-86`).

**What each choice does on webui (Sessions, `c67fd2dd`):** `api/routes.py:23686-23695` collects `pattern_keys` (or `pattern_key`). **session** approves them for the webui session, and **always** approves them permanently and saves the allowlist. Unlike Hermes, webui makes Tirith keys permanent too. Sessions already decodes both key fields (`HermesMobile/Models/Approval.swift:56-75`, `:99-119`).

**#700:** nothing in `Networking/Hermes/*` changes. #700 must keep delivering `pending_approval` and `approval` request params to `BotApprovalRequest` unchanged.

## Plan

- [ ] **Formatter.** Add `ApprovalScope` (a pure type in `HermesMobile/Models/Approval.swift`, main app target only). It builds one line from:
  - the keys;
  - the description;
  - which of Allow session and Always allow are offered;
  - the session noun ("this chat" or "this session");
  - where Always persists ("for this Profile" on Hermes, "on this server" on webui);
  - whether Always downgrades Tirith keys.

  It returns nil when neither choice is offered, as in room approvals, which offer only once and deny.
- [ ] **Labels per key.**
  - A shell key is quoted as the host wrote it: “recursive delete”.
  - `plugin_rule:…` becomes "every <tool> call for this reason", taking the tool from `tool_name` or the default key shape.
  - `execute_code` becomes "every Python script".
  - `ssh_config_write` becomes "writes to SSH config".
  - `cua:<action>:<mode>` becomes "computer use: <action> (<mode>)".
  - `tirith:<rule>` becomes "this security finding".
  - Anything else becomes "actions like this one".
  - Several keys are joined with the list formatter.
- [ ] **Bot Chat.**
  - `BotApprovalRequest.init` (`BotPendingRequest.swift:103-125`) also reads `pattern_keys`, falling back to `[pattern_key]`, and `tool_name`, all optional.
  - `BotApprovalRequestBody` (`BotPendingRequestCard.swift:117-154`) shows the line under the command, in caption and secondary style, above the buttons.
  - Room approvals (`BotRoomComposerView.swift:103-109`) get nothing, because the formatter returns nil for once and deny.
- [ ] **Sessions.** `ApprovalRequestOverlay` (`:70-86`) replaces the "Pattern keys" chips with the same line. It passes webui's scope, and both choices, since the overlay always shows all four buttons.
- [ ] Add new strings to `Localizable.xcstrings` for all shipped languages. Host-written key text stays as sent, inside quotes.
- [ ] Update `docs/agents/bots.md` in the `BotApprovalRequest` paragraph (`:366-371`): which fields are read, and what the line says.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** One plain line on the approval card, in both Sessions and Bot Chat, naming what "Allow session" and "Always allow" cover (for example "Always allows every recursive delete for this Profile"). Mocks first.

1. **Wording shape.** Recommend one sentence with two clauses, for example: "Allow session covers every “recursive delete” in this chat; Always allow covers it for this Profile from now on." Each clause is dropped when its button isn't offered. Alternative: a caption under each of the two buttons. That is clearer per button, but it is two lines and it changes the button grid.
2. **Sessions chips.** Recommend replacing the raw "Pattern keys" chips with the line. The chips are the same information in unreadable form. Alternative: keep the chips below the line for power users.
3. **webui feature freeze.** Recommend treating the Sessions change as a fix to confusing copy. It reads fields webui already sends and adds no webui capability, so it fits #713's bug-fix-only rule for webui. Alternative: Bot Chat only, leaving Sessions as it is until #701 moves Sessions onto Hermes.
4. **Tirith on Hermes.** Recommend that a mixed prompt's Always clause names only the keys Always really persists, with "the security finding stays allowed for this chat only" appended. Alternative: leave Tirith keys out of the line. That is shorter, but it overstates what Always does.
5. **Session lifetime.** Recommend "in this chat" with no "until Hermes restarts". The host detail is true at the pin but may change, and the user's mental model is the chat. Alternative: say it outright. That is more precise, but a restart is not something the user controls or sees.

## Acceptance

- A Bot Chat approval for `rm -rf ./build` whose host offers all four choices shows one line naming “recursive delete” for this chat (Allow session) and for this Profile (Always allow).
- A smart-denied approval (only Allow once and Deny) shows no line.
- A Tirith-only prompt (no Always offered) names only the session scope.
- A plugin-rule approval names the tool, never the `plugin_rule:…:<hash>` key.
- The Sessions overlay shows the same kind of line where the "Pattern keys" chips were, scoped to "this session" and "this server".
- Room approval cards are unchanged.

## Tests

- `BotPendingRequestTests`:
  - `testApprovalReadsPatternKeysAndToolName`: `pattern_keys` wins over `pattern_key`, and both are optional. This fails today because the fields aren't read.
  - Formatter cases, each asserting the exact line:
    - one shell key with both choices;
    - session only;
    - once and deny only (nil);
    - `plugin_rule`, `execute_code`, `cua`, `ssh_config_write`;
    - a mixed Tirith and shell prompt with the Hermes downgrade;
    - the same keys with webui scope (no downgrade);
    - an unknown key shape.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests`

## Mocks

Required first:
- Bot Chat card: a shell command with all four choices, a plugin rule, a Python script, a mixed Tirith prompt, and a smart-denied prompt (no line).
- Sessions overlay: before (chips) and after (line).
- Light and dark, and the largest accessibility text size for the Bot card.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. In Bot Chat on the test bot, ask: "Run `rm -rf ./hermex-approval-test` in the terminal." Expected: the approval card shows one line naming “recursive delete” for this chat and for this Profile. (A `/tmp/…` path is classified as “delete in root path” instead, which is also fine as long as the line names it.)
2. Tap Deny. Expected: nothing is written to the Profile's allowlist.
3. In a Sessions chat on the webui server, ask for the same command. Expected: the overlay shows the line where the "Pattern keys" chips were, and Deny works as before.
4. With VoiceOver on, the line reads after the command and before the buttons.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the Bot Chat request card and the Sessions approval overlay. The room card reuses the Bot card and correctly shows nothing. The approval push banner has no actions (#750 is deferred), so it isn't touched. No deep link, intent or share path answers approvals.
- **Targets:** main app only. The formatter lives in the app target, and `Approval.swift` has no extension membership to add.
- **Servers:** the line is built from the request on screen. The scope wording follows the server type of the card's own server, never the active server.
- **Contracts:** tolerant reads of existing optional fields. No wire change.
- **Reverse states:** the copy is informational. There is no in-app way to remove an Always rule; the user edits `command_allowlist` in the Profile's `config.yaml` (Desktop shows the same path). The line doesn't promise an undo.
- **Native quality:** Dynamic Type (the line wraps), VoiceOver order, light and dark, all shipped languages. Host key text stays untranslated inside quotes.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Outside reach

None.

title: fix(bots): open the sign-in form after a rejected password
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** #880

## Problem

When the host rejects the saved password (a 401 from `POST /auth/password-login`), the only button on screen is Reconnect, and Reconnect sends the same password again:

- Inbox: the message row offers `Button("Reconnect") { revision = UUID() }` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotsInboxView.swift:68-70`), which reruns `inbox.open()` (`:534`) with the stored record.
- Chat: once the error pill is dismissed, the pill becomes `.reconnect` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatComposerView.swift:122`, `:574`), and its button (`:619`) reruns `recover()` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:264-266`, `:434`).
- Room: the same `.reconnect` pill when the reader stops (`BotChatComposerView.swift:586`; `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:105`).

A 401 is never retried automatically (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:379-387`; `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:1497-1500`), so every tap is one more failed login. The host allows 10 password logins per 60 s per client IP, and successful ones count too (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py:338-356`, checked first at `:382-384`). A few taps on a bad password can therefore lock this network out of signing in for a minute, which also affects Desktop and the browser when they share the phone's public IP through the tunnel. Returning to the app does the same: the inbox and chat reopen on every foreground (`BotsInboxView.swift:539-541`, `BotChatView.swift:267-268`).

The fix, the sign-in form, is two taps away and not linked from the error: the inbox gear (`BotsInboxView.swift:171-173`, sheet `:511-512`) or Settings → server → Hermes connection (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:2242-2247`). Push setup already gets this right: it says "This Hermes host rejected the saved sign-in. Update the Hermes connection, then try again." (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift:353-354`) next to a permanent link to the form (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushSectionView.swift:124-137`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract. A rejected password is `BotFailure.rejected(401)` from the login step (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:101`, thrown by `send` at `:199`). After #880, a 401 on the public `/api/status` becomes `.notDashboard` or `.blocked`, and a signed-in request's 401 is retried once with a fresh sign-in (`HermesConnection.swift:144-153`). So a `.rejected(401)` that reaches a screen always means the host refused the saved username or password.

## Plan

- [ ] **Flag.** Add `private(set) var needsSignIn = false` to `BotInbox`, `BotConversation` and `BotRoomReader`, set only for `BotFailure.rejected(401)`:
  - `BotInbox`: set in `drop` (`BotInbox.swift:801-805`) and in the no-client branch of `open()` (`:337-341`). Clear it when a connect starts (`:305`) and when the saved record changes (`:293-297`).
  - `BotConversation`: set in `disconnected` (`BotConversation.swift:1496-1502`); clear in `recoverConnection` (`:557-558`).
  - `BotRoomReader`: set in `fail` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift:425-429`); clear in `open` (`:86`).
- [ ] **Inbox row** (`BotsInboxView.swift:68-70`): when `inbox.needsSignIn`, the button reads "Update sign-in" and sets `showingSetup = true`. Otherwise it stays Reconnect.
- [ ] **Pill.** Add `case updateSignIn` to `BotComposerPill` (`BotChatComposerView.swift:558-594`). `resolve` and `room` take `needsSignIn` and return `.updateSignIn` where they return `.reconnect` today (`:574`, `:586`). `BotComposerPillView` (`:598-641`) gains `onUpdateSignIn` and draws `Label("Update sign-in", systemImage: "key")` in the Reconnect slot. The error pill still comes first, as today.
- [ ] **Chat and room return to the inbox.** `BotChatView` (`BotChatView.swift:38-46`) and `BotRoomView` (`BotRoomView.swift:21`, `:105`) get an `onUpdateSignIn` callback. The inbox builds both (`BotsInboxView.swift:279-292`, `:517-525`) and passes `{ selection.profile = nil; showingSetup = true }` (or `selection.room = nil`). Returning first is required, not cosmetic; see Decision 1.
- [ ] **Form.** `BotConnectionView` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:13`) takes an optional flag that focuses the password field on appear. Keep the stored values in the fields (Decision 3).
- [ ] **No automatic resend** (Decision 2): while `needsSignIn` is set, `BotInbox.open()` skips connecting unless the saved record now differs from the rejected one (compare the loaded record at `BotInbox.swift:288` with `connection`). The chat's foreground recovery (`BotChatView.swift:264-268`) skips `recover()` while its flag is set.
- [ ] **Copy.** Change the 401 text (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:51`) to "Hermes didn't accept the username or password." The button now carries the action, and the same text also shows in the form after a mistyped password. Update the row in `BotConnectionAdviceTests` (`HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:423`). Add "Update sign-in" and the new sentence to `Localizable.xcstrings` in all 17 shipped languages as `needs_review`.
- [ ] **Docs:** add one sentence to `docs/agents/bots.md` after `:147-149`: a rejected password offers "Update sign-in", which opens the form, and the app never resends it on its own.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** When the saved password is rejected, the button opens the sign-in form ("Update sign-in") instead of Reconnect.

1. **Chat and room hand off to the inbox's sheet.** Recommend closing the chat or room and opening the inbox's sheet. A chat's `BotConversation` holds a `BotClient` bound at creation to the connection the host rejected (`BotConversation.swift:193`). Saving a new password retires that connection (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:100-104` → `HermesConnection.swift:247-252`), and a password change keeps the UUID, so the chat's identity (`BotsInboxView.swift:289`) doesn't change and the chat would only reconnect to `.stale`. A room is worse: it builds a new client from its old record on each open (`BotRoomReader.swift:85`), which would retire the fresh connection and sign in with the old password again (`HermesConnection.swift:233-240`). The inbox reloads the record when the sheet closes (`BotsInboxView.swift:511`, `BotInbox.swift:288`). Alternative: present the form from the chat and rebuild the chat on save. That keeps scroll position but needs a credential revision in the chat's identity, and there must never be credentials in keys (`HermesConnection.swift:227`).
2. **Never resend a rejected password on its own.** Recommend that foregrounding, pull to refresh and closing the sheet without saving don't sign in again while the flag is set and the record is unchanged. Alternative: leave them; each foreground then spends one of the host's 10 logins a minute.
3. **Form contents.** Recommend keeping the stored address, username and password, and focusing the password field. On iOS, typing into a refocused secure field replaces its contents, so the user can type a new password or tap Connect to retry after fixing the host. Alternative: clear the password, which forces retyping even when the host was the problem.
4. **Scope.** Recommend only the inbox, chat and room. The creator and editor sheets show their errors inline and are opened from a live inbox. Push setup already links the form.
5. **Mocks.** Recommend none: the decided label replaces an existing button's label and action, with no layout change.

## Acceptance

- With a rejected saved password, the inbox shows "Hermes didn't accept the username or password." and an "Update sign-in" button. Tapping it opens the Hermes connection sheet with the password field focused, and sends no request.
- After a successful Connect in that sheet, the inbox reconnects with no further tap.
- In a chat or room, once the error pill is dismissed, the pill reads "Update sign-in". Tapping it returns to the inbox and opens the sheet.
- Foregrounding the app, pulling to refresh or closing the sheet without saving sends no login while the password is still the rejected one.
- Every other failure still shows Reconnect and behaves as before.

## Tests

- `BotInboxTests` (`HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests.swift`): extend `testRefusedConnectionShowsTheMessageAndDoesNotRetryOnItsOwn` (`:691-704`) to assert `needsSignIn`. Add: a second `open()` with the unchanged record builds no wire (`spare == 1`), while a record saved with a new password connects and clears the flag. A `.notDashboard` failure leaves the flag false.
- `BotConversationTests`: `.rejected(401)` on reconnect sets `needsSignIn` and schedules no retry; `.rejected(502)` leaves it false.
- `BotRoomTests`: a room whose connect fails with `.rejected(401)` sets `needsSignIn`.
- `BotChatPresentationTests` (`HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests.swift:33-39` has the room pill cases): `resolve` and `room` return `.updateSignIn` instead of `.reconnect` when `needsSignIn`, and an error text still wins.
- `BotConnectionAdviceTests`: the 401 row's new text.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionAdviceTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`

## Mocks

Not required: the decided label replaces the label and action of an existing button and pill; nothing is laid out anew.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

A rejected saved password needs the host's dashboard password to change, which is a host mutation. Run steps 1-4 only if Uzair chooses to rotate the test host's password; otherwise the tests above cover the flow.

1. With Bots connected over the tunnel, change the dashboard password on the host (Uzair only). Pull to refresh the Bots inbox. Expected: "Hermes didn't accept the username or password." with "Update sign-in".
2. Background and foreground the app twice. Expected: the same message, and the host's log shows no new login attempts.
3. Open a bot chat from the cached roster, dismiss the error pill, tap "Update sign-in". Expected: back on the inbox with the sheet open and the password field focused.
4. Type the new password, Connect. Expected: the sheet closes and the inbox loads the roster.
5. Regression, no host change: open a chat, turn on Airplane Mode, then turn it off. Expected: the chat shows reconnecting, and no "Update sign-in" appears.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the inbox row, the chat pill and the room pill change. The form itself (gear, Settings, push) is unchanged. Deep links that open a chat route through the inbox (`BotsInboxView.swift:183-190`), so they reach the same path.
- **Targets:** main app only (`BotsInboxView`, `BotChatComposerView`, `BotConversation`, `BotRoomReader`, `BotProtocol` are `HermesMobile`-only).
- **Servers:** the flag lives on per-server screen models and resets when the saved record changes; the sheet edits the active server's record only.
- **Reverse states:** a rejected password → Update sign-in → Connect → connected. Closing the sheet without saving leaves the message and button in place.
- **Connection modes:** a 401 is independent of LAN or tunnel. Not resending also protects the shared per-IP login budget behind the tunnel.
- **Native quality:** the pill label is a `Label` with a symbol; VoiceOver reads "Update sign-in, button". Two new strings in all 17 languages. No new motion: the pill keeps its existing transition, which already honors Reduce Motion (`BotChatComposerView.swift:75`).
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`.
- **Related issues:**
  - #880 changes the same `BotFailure` copy and makes `.rejected(401)` mean only a rejected password; land it first.
  - #700 slice 0.3 plans "one silent re-login on 401 then `.loggedOut` only on bad credentials". When that lands, `needsSignIn` should come from that signed-out state rather than from the error value, with the same button.
  - #708: on an OAuth-signed-in server, "Update sign-in" should start the browser sign-in instead of the password form.
  - #744 adds a second address to the same form. The button opens the form unchanged.
  - #751's advice table owns the 401 row; this changes only its text. #752's status section and "Check again" never sign in, so they stay as they are.

## Outside reach

None. The optional device check rotates the host's dashboard password and needs Uzair's go-ahead.

title: feat(security): lock Hermex with Face ID or the passcode
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Anyone holding an unlocked iPhone can open Hermex and read every chat, bot conversation and workspace file, and act on the user's servers. The app switcher also keeps a snapshot of the last screen, so a glance at the switcher shows a chat.

Hermex has no app lock. No target, plist, project file or config mentions `LocalAuthentication`, `LAContext` or `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` (checked across `HermesMobile/`, the three extensions, `HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` and `Config/`). The main Info.plist carries the other usage strings but not Face ID's (`HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist:112-125`).

Everything that opens the app goes through one scene. `HermesMobileApp` has a single `WindowGroup` (`HermesMobile/HermesMobileApp.swift:55-82`), and multiple scenes are off (`Info.plist:126-129`). All three App Intents set `openAppWhenRun = true` (`HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift:38`, `:58`, `:77`) and route through `ContentView`, as do URLs, the share extension's handoff and notification taps (`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:23-35`, `:99-149`). So a lock at the scene covers every way in.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

- [ ] **Policy and state.** New `HermesMobile/Auth/AppLock.swift` (main target; add it to `project.pbxproj`): a `@MainActor @Observable` `AppLock` with `isEnabled` (UserDefaults, default off), `isLocked` (needs authentication) and `isCovered` (the scene isn't active). Inputs: the scene became inactive, entered the background, or became active. Rules:
  - Cold launch with the lock on → locked.
  - Entering the background records the time on `ContinuousClock` (Decision 2). Becoming active more than 60 s later → locked. Becoming active sooner → not locked.
  - Inactive or background → covered. Active → uncovered.
  - Authentication goes through a small `AppLockAuthenticator` protocol: the real one makes a fresh `LAContext` per attempt and evaluates `.deviceOwnerAuthentication` (Face ID or Touch ID, falling back to the passcode). Tests use a fake.
- [ ] **Cover window** (Decision 1). The lock and the blank cover live in their own `UIWindow` on the app's window scene, at a level above alerts, with a `UIHostingController` root. It shows whenever `isLocked || isCovered` and hides otherwise. When it appears, end editing in the app window, so the keyboard and its suggestions don't stay on top, and make the lock window key. To get the window up before the first frame on cold launch and before the app-switcher snapshot, create it from a scene delegate: return a `UISceneConfiguration` with a `delegateClass` from `application(_:configurationForConnecting:options:)` in the app's one delegate, `PushAppDelegate` (`HermesMobile/Push/PushAppDelegate.swift:7`, adopted at `HermesMobileApp.swift:46`). Drive `AppLock` from `sceneWillResignActive`, `sceneDidEnterBackground` and `sceneDidBecomeActive`.
- [ ] **Lock view** (mocks first). Static, with no animation: app icon, "Hermex is locked", and an Unlock button. It prompts once by itself when it appears while active. After a cancel or failure it waits for the button (no prompt loop; the Face ID sheet itself makes the scene inactive, so that inactive/active pair must not count as returning from the background). While the scene is inactive, the same window shows the blank cover (icon only).
- [ ] **Behind the lock.** Content stays mounted, so streams, Live Activities and reconnects keep running (the lock is a cover). URLs, intents, notification taps and share handoffs route as today and land behind the cover.
  - Hold the "New Chat with Voice" dictation start until unlock: `autoStartVoiceInputIfNeeded` checks only `scenePhase` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:1214-1220`), and the phase stays active under the cover (Decision 7).
  - Turn off the ⌘N and ⌘F commands while locked (`HermexCommands`, `HermesMobileApp.swift:21-41`; the actions come from `SessionListView.swift:377`).
- [ ] **Settings** (mocks first). One toggle, off by default, placed where the mock pick says (the App card at `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:582-663` or a new Privacy card). The label follows `LAContext.biometryType` (Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode only). The footer says notifications, Live Activities and the share sheet still show their content. Turning it on or off asks for authentication first; a failure leaves it as it was (Decision 4). With no device passcode the toggle is disabled and the footer says why.
- [ ] **No passcode later** (Decision 5): if the passcode is removed while the lock is on, the lock view says the lock can't work without a passcode and lets the user in. It never opens silently.
- [ ] **Info.plist:** add `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` to `HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist` ("Hermex uses Face ID to unlock the app when the lock is on."). Without it, Face ID requests can fail.
- [ ] **Strings:** add the lock view, toggle and footer copy to `Localizable.xcstrings` in all 17 shipped languages as `needs_review` (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).
- [ ] **Docs:** the rules (what locks, what the cover hides, what it can't cover) go in `AppLock`'s doc comment. No agents doc owns app-level settings.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- One toggle in Settings, off by default. No "require after" picker.
- It locks on cold launch and when returning after more than 1 minute in the background.
- The app switcher shows a blank cover instead of chats.
- Deep links, notification taps, App Intents and share handoffs land behind the lock.
- Streaming keeps running while locked (the lock is a cover).
- Settings copy says notifications, Live Activities and the share sheet aren't covered.
- Mocks first: the lock screen and the setting.

1. **Separate window, not a SwiftUI overlay.** Recommend a window above alerts, created by a scene delegate. An `.overlay` on `ContentView` sits under every sheet, full-screen cover, alert, menu and the keyboard, so an open sheet (for example the Hermes connection form) would show over the lock and in the switcher snapshot. `.fullScreenCover` can't present over an open sheet. Alternative: the overlay plus `onChange(of: scenePhase)`. Less code, but it fails the snapshot and sheet cases.
2. **Clock.** Recommend `ContinuousClock`, which keeps counting while the phone sleeps and ignores changes to the wall clock. Alternative: `Date`, which moves if the user changes the time.
3. **Cover on inactive, not only background.** Recommend covering on `sceneWillResignActive`: iOS takes the switcher snapshot as the scene leaves, and the switcher itself makes the scene inactive first. Side effect: Control Center, Notification Center and system alerts (for example the notification permission prompt) also show the blank cover behind them. Alternative: cover only in the background, which risks the snapshot showing a chat.
4. **Authenticate to turn it on and off.** Recommend both. Turning it on proves the user can unlock and triggers the Face ID permission prompt in context. Turning it off stops someone holding the phone from simply switching it off. Alternative: only when turning on.
5. **No passcode.** Recommend a disabled toggle with a reason while no passcode is set, and, if the passcode is removed later, a visible "can't lock without a passcode" note that lets the user in. Failing closed would lock the user out with no way back, since iOS can't authenticate without a passcode.
6. **Face ID usage string in English only.** Recommend matching the other usage strings, which are English-only (`Info.plist:112-125`; there is no InfoPlist catalog). Alternative: add an `InfoPlist.xcstrings` for all usage strings, a separate change.
7. **Voice intent waits for unlock.** Recommend holding dictation until unlock, so the microphone never starts behind a lock screen. Alternative: start at once, as today.
8. **Push presence while locked.** Recommend reporting no chat on screen while locked, so "Quiet the Open Chat" (`HermesMobile/Push/PushNotificationRouter.swift:142-158`) doesn't hide banners for a chat the user can't see. Alternative: leave presence as is.
9. **Storage.** Recommend `UserDefaults` for `isEnabled`: an app-wide preference, not a credential, and the same for every server.

## Acceptance

- With the lock off (the default), nothing changes: no cover, no prompt, no Face ID permission request.
- With it on, a cold launch shows the lock before any chat content. Returning after more than 60 s in the background shows the lock; returning sooner doesn't.
- The app switcher shows the blank cover, including when a sheet was open.
- A sheet, alert or keyboard that was open stays under the lock and is back after unlocking.
- A reply streaming at lock time keeps streaming; after unlock the transcript and Live Activity are current.
- A notification tap, deep link, App Intent or share handoff that arrives while locked opens its destination behind the lock. The voice intent starts dictation only after unlock.
- Cancelling Face ID leaves the lock up with an Unlock button, and doesn't prompt again by itself.
- VoiceOver on the lock reads only the lock view.
- The Settings footer states that notifications, Live Activities and the share sheet aren't covered.

## Tests

- New `AppLockTests` (add to `HermesMobileTests` in `project.pbxproj`), with a fake authenticator and an injected clock:
  - Cold launch with the lock on is locked; off is not.
  - Background, then active after 59 s is unlocked and after 61 s locked.
  - Inactive then active (Control Center, the Face ID sheet) never locks.
  - Covered exactly while not active.
  - A successful authentication unlocks; cancel and failure stay locked; the automatic prompt runs once per lock.
  - Enabling fails without a passcode, and enabling or disabling requires a successful authentication.
  - A passcode removed while enabled gives the visible "can't lock" state, not a silent open.
- `LocalizationCatalogTests`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/AppLockTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`
- The window level, snapshot and VoiceOver behavior need a real device (Manual test).

## Mocks

Required first, published with `html-communication`, then wait for a pick:
- The lock screen: prompting, after a cancel (Unlock button), and the no-passcode note.
- The blank app-switcher cover.
- The Settings toggle with its footer (off, on, and disabled without a passcode), and where it sits in Settings.

Each in light and dark and at a large Dynamic Type size.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. Settings → turn on the lock. Expected: a Face ID prompt; the toggle turns on only after success.
2. Swipe up to the app switcher. Expected: the blank cover, not a chat.
3. Go home for 30 s, return. Expected: no lock. Go home for 90 s, return. Expected: the lock, and Face ID unlocks it.
4. Open Settings → the server → Hermes connection (a sheet), go home for 90 s, return. Expected: the lock covers the sheet; after unlock the sheet is still there.
5. Start a long reply in a chat, go home for 90 s, return. Expected: the lock; after unlock the reply has kept streaming and the Live Activity was updating meanwhile.
6. While locked, tap a Hermex notification. Expected: after unlock, that chat is open.
7. Force-quit, then run "New Chat with Voice" from the Action button or Shortcuts. Expected: the lock first; dictation starts only after unlock.
8. Share a photo to Hermex from Photos while Hermex is locked. Expected: after unlock, the shared import is waiting.
9. On the lock, cancel Face ID. Expected: the Unlock button, and no new prompt until tapped.
10. Turn on VoiceOver, lock. Expected: only the lock view is read.
11. Turn the lock off. Expected: authentication first.
12. With a hardware keyboard (iPad or Mac), press ⌘N while locked. Expected: nothing happens.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** cold launch, foreground, URLs, notification taps, App Intents (Action button, Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight), share handoff, Live Activity taps and keyboard commands all land behind the one scene's lock.
- **Targets:** main app only. The share extension, the Live Activity widget and `HermesNotificationService` run in their own processes and aren't covered; the Settings footer says so. `HermesMobileTests` gains `AppLockTests`.
- **Servers:** app-wide, not per server. Switching servers neither locks nor unlocks.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** turn on ↔ turn off (both authenticated); locked ↔ unlocked; a cancelled prompt → the Unlock button.
- **Connection modes:** unaffected. Streams and reconnects run behind the cover.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver sees only the lock (modal window). Dynamic Type on the lock and in Settings. No animation on the cover or lock: it must be on screen before the snapshot, and nothing repaints. Light and dark. New strings in all 17 languages. The label follows Face ID or Touch ID. iPad Split View and Slide Over: check that sharing the screen doesn't flash the cover while Hermex stays active.
- **Docs:** `AppLock`'s doc comment holds the rules.
- **Related issues:** none of #700, #744, #751 or #752 touches the scene, Settings' App card or app launch. #708 will present a browser sign-in sheet from the app window. When both have landed, check that the lock never sits over that sheet while the app is active and unlocked.

## Outside reach

None.

title: fix(bots): accept a pasted dashboard link
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

The easiest way to get the Hermes address is to copy it from the browser, but the connection form refuses what the browser shows. `BotConnection.address(_:)` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:38-63`) rejects any path, query, fragment or credentials, and any scheme other than `http`/`https` (`:47-52`). The user gets "Enter a Hermes HTTP or HTTPS address without a path, credentials or query." (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:60`). Opening the dashboard's root sends the browser to `/sessions` (`.codex-tmp/hermes-agent/web/src/App.tsx:128-130`), so the link a user copies from the address bar is almost never accepted. The same goes for `/login?next=…`, a `wss://…/api/ws` URL from a config file, or `/api/status` from a curl command.

The form also hides a guess. With no scheme, a public host becomes `https://` and a private or local one becomes `http://` (`BotConnection.swift:41-46`, `:57`, `:65-86`), but nothing shows which one Hermex will use until sign-in fails. The field's footer says only "Domains, Tailscale names and IP addresses work. You can include http:// or https://." (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:30-32`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract. The paths come from the dashboard at the pin:

- The dashboard root redirects to `/sessions` (`web/src/App.tsx:128-130`); `/chat` is its chat tab (`:140-145`); other pages are single top-level routes (`:158-221`).
- The login page is `/login?next=…` (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py:176-180`). A host with one OAuth provider sends browsers to `/auth/login?provider=…&next=…` (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py:101-106`, route at `routes.py:197`).
- The gateway socket is `/api/ws` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:583`); Hermex builds its `ws`/`wss` URL from the address (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:82-90`).
- A dashboard served under a path works through `X-Forwarded-Prefix` (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/prefix.py:61-81`). Out of scope here.

## Plan

- [ ] **Parser** (`BotConnection.swift:38-63`), before the existing checks:
  - Map an explicit `ws://` to `http://` and `wss://` to `https://`.
  - Trim trailing slashes from the path. Clear it when it is empty or its first segment (case-insensitive) is `login`, `auth`, `api`, `chat` or `sessions` (Decision 1), whatever follows.
  - Any other path throws the path error, naming the path (Decision 2).
  - Drop the query and fragment (Decision 3). Credentials are still refused.
  - Host checks, the numeric-host guard (`:53-56`), the scheme guess (`:57`) and lowercasing (`:58-59`) stay as they are, so ATS behavior doesn't change.
- [ ] **Errors** (Decision 4): add `enum BotAddressError: LocalizedError { case path(String), invalid }`, thrown only by `address(_:)`. `BotFailure.invalidAddress` stays for request building (`HermesREST.swift:49`, `:51`, `:86`) and the inbox's permanent list (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:381`). In `BotConnectionSetup.connect` (`BotConnectionView.swift:344-346`), show `error.localizedDescription` when no URL was parsed.
- [ ] **Preview:** `BotConnectionSetup` (`BotConnectionView.swift:203-262`) gets a computed `addressPreview: URL?` from the observed `address` text. The address section's footer (`:30-32`) shows "Will connect to <URL>" as its first line while the text parses, above the existing hint. Parse errors still appear only on Connect (Decision 5).
- [ ] **Copy.** Three strings in `Localizable.xcstrings`, all 17 shipped languages, `needs_review` (`docs/agents/i18n.md`):
  - "Will connect to %@"
  - Path: "Remove “%@” from the address. Hermex needs the dashboard's main address, like https://example.com:9119, and can't use a dashboard served under a path yet."
  - Invalid (replaces `BotProtocol.swift:60` for the form): "Enter the dashboard's HTTP or HTTPS address, like https://example.com:9119, without a username or password."
  - Check the preview in the RTL pseudolanguage (`docs/agents/i18n.md` § RTL). If the URL flips, wrap it in Unicode isolates.
- [ ] Dev auto-login parses through the same function (`HermesMobile/Config/DevAutoLogin.swift:62`), so `HERMEX_DEV_*` addresses follow the same rules. Nothing to change there.
- [ ] **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md:135-140` gains two sentences: which pasted parts are removed and which are refused, and that the form shows the address it will use before saving. Keep "TLS failures never trigger an HTTP downgrade".

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Strip what browsers add (`/login`, `/api/...`, `/chat`, a trailing slash) and map `ws`/`wss` to `http`/`https`, then show "Will connect to <URL>" before saving. Path-prefix support is not in scope. No cleartext warning (#754 was declined).

1. **Also strip `/sessions` and `/auth/…`.** Recommend yes. `/sessions` is where the dashboard's root lands, so it is what the address bar shows most of the time, and `/auth/login?…` is where a gated dashboard sends the browser. Both are "what browsers add". Alternative: only the decided list, which still refuses the most common paste.
2. **Any other path is refused, naming it.** Recommend refusing, since the only real non-page paths are reverse-proxy prefixes, which Hermex can't use yet. Alternative A: strip every path. One rule, and the preview shows the result, but a prefixed dashboard would silently point at the proxy's root and fail later as "isn't a Hermes dashboard". Alternative B: also strip every dashboard page (about 20 routes, `web/src/App.tsx:158-221`). More pastes work, but it's a list to keep in step with upstream.
3. **Query and fragment are always dropped.** Recommend dropping them: browser links carry them (`/login?next=%2F`), and they never belong in the saved address. Alternative: drop them only together with a stripped path and keep refusing `https://host/?x`.
4. **Parser errors get their own type.** Recommend `BotAddressError`, so typing mistakes stay apart from connection failures and `BotInbox.isRetryable` doesn't grow. Alternative: a `BotFailure.addressPath(String)` case.
5. **Preview placement.** Recommend the first footer line, shown only while the text parses, with errors on Connect as today. Alternative: live error text while typing, which nags mid-word.

## Acceptance

- Each of these shows "Will connect to …" with the root shown, and connecting uses that root:
  - `https://hermes.example.com/sessions`
  - `https://hermes.example.com/login?next=%2F`
  - `https://hermes.example.com/api/status`
  - `wss://hermes.example.com/api/ws` → `https://hermes.example.com`
  - `http://192.168.1.5:9119/chat/` → `http://192.168.1.5:9119`
- A scheme-less address shows the guess: `hermes.example.com` → `https://hermes.example.com`, `192.168.1.5:9119` → `http://192.168.1.5:9119`.
- `https://hermes.example.com/hermes` shows no preview. Connect shows the path copy naming `/hermes`, and no request is sent.
- `https://user:pass@hermes.example.com` is still refused, with the invalid copy.
- A saved address never has a path, query or fragment, so the status section's Copy (#752) copies the root.

## Tests

- `BotConnectionVersionTests.testAddressDefaultsHonorLocalNetworksAndExplicitSchemes` (`HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:79-109`):
  - Add the pasted-link cases above to the accepted table.
  - Move `host?key=x` and `host#fragment` to it (`:105-106`).
  - `host/path` stays refused, now as `BotAddressError.path("/path")`. `user:pass@host`, `ftp://host` and the port cases stay refused.
- `BotConnectionSetupTests.testAddressFailureIsVisibleBeforeAClientExists` (`:111-119`): expects the path copy naming `/not-supported`. Add a test that `addressPreview` is nil for invalid text and the root URL for a pasted link.
- `BotDraftTests.testAddressValidationAndOptionalRosterMetadata` (`HermesMobileTests/BotDraftTests.swift:157-161`): credentials and `/path` still throw; `https://host?ticket=x` and `https://host#x` now parse to `https://host`.
- `LocalizationCatalogTests`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionSetupTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotDraftTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`

## Mocks

Not required: one footer line under an existing field, plus two error texts in the existing error row. No layout change.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. In Safari, open the dashboard through the tunnel and copy the address bar (it ends in `/sessions`).
2. Hermex → Settings → the server → Hermes connection. Paste it into the address field. Expected: "Will connect to https://<tunnel host>" under the field.
3. Connect. Expected: it signs in and saves; reopening the form shows the address without `/sessions`.
4. Type `https://<tunnel host>/hermes`. Expected: no preview. Connect shows "Remove “/hermes” from the address…".
5. Type `192.168.1.5:9119`. Expected: "Will connect to http://192.168.1.5:9119" (don't connect).
6. Turn on a large Dynamic Type size. Expected: the preview wraps.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the one connection form, opened from the Bots inbox gear (`BotsInboxView.swift:171-173`), Settings (`SettingsView.swift:2242-2247`) and push setup (`HermexPushSectionView.swift:126-127`). Dev auto-login shares the parser.
- **Targets:** main app only (`BotConnection.swift` and `BotConnectionView.swift` are `HermesMobile`-only).
- **Servers:** parsing is pure and writes nothing. The saved record stays keyed by the configured server, and the UUID rules at `BotConnectionView.swift:307-319` are unchanged, so a pasted link for the same root keeps drafts, cache and push pairing.
- **Contracts:** none; the saved root is what every request is built from, as today.
- **Reverse states:** n/a (field input). A refused path can be edited and retried.
- **Connection modes:** the preview makes the LAN `http://` and tunnel `https://` guess visible. No downgrade on TLS failure.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver reads the footer line. It wraps at large Dynamic Type. Three strings in all 17 languages. RTL checked through the pseudolanguage.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md:135-140`.
- **Related issues:**
  - #744 parses its "Other address" with the same `address(_:)`, so it inherits the stripping. Its field should show its own "Will connect to" line, and its form mocks should include it.
  - #700 slice 0.3 adds a Hermes Add Server and onboarding field. It should parse through this function (or its successor), so a pasted link behaves the same there. The move to `hermes_credential` must keep saved addresses root-only.
  - #751 owns the ATS copy and the rule that address errors show before any transport exists (`docs/agents/bots.md:139-140`); both are kept.
  - #752's status section shows and copies the saved address, now always the root.
  - #708: a pasted `/auth/login?provider=nous` link strips to the root, and #880's browser sign-in copy then explains that such a host isn't supported yet.

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(push): banners name the bot, in the phone's language
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Relay banners don't say which bot is asking, and part of their text is always English.

- The plugin seals fixed English titles: "Turn failed" (`hermex-push/plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:285-287`), "Question" (`:303-304`) and "Approval needed" (`:346-348`), hermex-push `2f1388c`. With several bots, "Approval needed" doesn't say which bot is blocked. On a phone set to German it is still English.
- Reply banners use the Profile slug (`self._profile or "Hermes"`, `hooks.py:291`), not the name the user gave the bot. A bot titled "Inbox Triage" shows as `inbox-triage`.
- The Notification Service Extension copies title, subtitle and body verbatim (`HermesMobile/Push/PushPreview.swift:125-127`). Only the fallback body "New activity" is localized (`:122`).

The pieces for a fix already exist:

- The NSE bundles the shared `Localizable.xcstrings` (`HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:549`).
- `kind` travels in cleartext next to the seal (`PushPreview.swift:33`).
- The host exposes a bot's names in `profile.yaml`: `bot_title` (from `ui_meta["hermes-bots"].title`) and `display_name` (`.codex-tmp/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/profiles.py:811-836`, pin `ca678285`).
- The app names bots in this order: title, then `display_name`, then the slug, with `default` shown as "Hermes" (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:111-113, 154`).

## Contract

No relay or host change. The relay never sees the name.

- **Sealed preview (plugin → phone).** The sealed JSON `{"title","subtitle","body","profile","request_id"}` (`plugin/hermex_push/payload.py:10`) gains an optional `"bot_name"`: a plain string, clipped to 80 characters, never empty when present. It stays inside the AES-GCM seal, so the relay's view is unchanged. Older phones ignore the extra field, because `PushPreview` decodes optionals.
- **Host read (plugin only).** `hermes_cli.profiles.get_profile_dir(name)` (`profiles.py:306-319`) and `read_profile_meta(profile_dir)` (`:811-836`) return `bot_title` and `display_name`. The read is cached by file signature (`:607-621`), so reading it on every banner is cheap. These are hermes-agent internals, like the plugin's existing `hermes_cli.config` import (`hooks.py:62-66`). A host without them falls back to the slug.
- Nothing here touches `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/*`, so #700 is unaffected.

Order: the hermex-push PR (plugin) merges first. The Hermex PR links it and can merge any time after, because an app with no `bot_name` falls back to the sealed title. The maintainer updates the plugin on the host.

## Plan

**`uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`** (suggested title `feat(plugin): seal the bot's name with each banner`):

- [ ] `plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py`: add an injectable `bot_name: Callable[[], str]` to `HermexPush.__init__` (`:103-124`, like `relay_url`). The default reads `read_profile_meta(get_profile_dir(self._profile or "default"))` and returns `bot_title`, then `display_name`, then the slug, and "Hermes" for the default Profile. Any exception falls back to the slug or "Hermes".
- [ ] `plugin/hermex_push/payload.py:114-124`: `preview()` takes `bot_name` and seals it, clipped to `TITLE_CHARS`. Update the docstring at `:10`.
- [ ] `hooks.py:285-291, 303-304, 346-348`: pass `bot_name` to every banner. Also build the sealed English `title` for older app builds: `"<name> · Approval needed"`, `"<name> · Question"`, `"<name> · Turn failed"`, and `"<name>"` for a reply.
- [ ] `plugin/README.md:72-76`: list `bot_name` among the sealed fields. Bump `PLUGIN_VERSION` in all four files.

**`hermex`** (suggested title `feat(push): name the bot in banners, in the phone's language`):

- [ ] `HermesMobile/Push/PushPreview.swift:40-50`: decode `bot_name` as `botName: String?`.
- [ ] `PushPreview.rewrite` (`:116-131`): when `botName` is non-empty, pick the title by `payload.kind`:
  - `approval` → `String(localized: "\(name) · Approval needed")`
  - `clarify` → `"\(name) · Question"`
  - `turn_error` → `"\(name) · Turn failed"`
  - `reply` → the name alone

  With no `botName`, or a kind this build doesn't know, keep the sealed title as today. Subtitle, body and the Profile write-back don't change. The file stays Foundation-only, because it is shared with the NSE.
- [ ] `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`: add `%@ · Approval needed`, `%@ · Question` and `%@ · Turn failed`. Each gets a translator comment ("%@ is the bot's name") and a value in all 17 shipped languages (`needs_review`), following `docs/agents/i18n.md` § Editing the catalog.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md:1484-1492` (the extension builds the title from `kind` and `bot_name`). `docs/agents/push.md:20-22` (the bot name stays inside the seal). `docs/agents/i18n.md:5-7` (the NSE now reads four keys, not one).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Banners read "<bot name> · Approval needed" (and so on) in the phone's language. The bot's name stays inside the seal, so the relay never sees it.

Implementation notes (recommended): the plugin seals the name using the app's chain (title, then display_name, then slug); the NSE builds the localized label from the plaintext `kind` and falls back to the sealed title for older plugins.

1. **One format key per kind** (`%@ · Approval needed`), not a label plus a separator joined in code. Each language then controls word order and the separator, which matters for Arabic, Hebrew and Urdu. Alternative: separate label keys plus one `%1$@ · %2$@` key. That is fewer phrases, but word order is fixed in code.
2. **Wording: keep today's English** ("Approval needed", "Question", "Turn failed"), as decided. That needs 3 new keys × 17 languages. Alternative: reuse "Approval required", which is already translated and matches the in-app card (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequestCard.swift:120`). It saves one set of translations but changes the banner's wording.
3. **Reply title: the bot's name alone.** The subtitle already shows the user's message and the body the reply. Alternative: "<name> · Reply", which adds noise to the most common banner.
4. **Name source: the host's `read_profile_meta`.** It is the same source `profiles.list` uses, so the banner matches the roster, and a rename shows up on the next banner. Alternative: the plugin parses `profile.yaml` itself with PyYAML. That also works on hosts without `bot_title`, but it copies host parsing that can drift.
5. **Older app builds get the name too.** The sealed `title` carries the English "<name> · <label>", so builds before this change show the bot's name, in English. Alternative: keep the old titles for older builds. That changes nothing for them.
6. **Test data: seal the new preview inside the Hermex test** with CryptoKit and the existing test keys. The plugin's fixed vector (`plugin/hermex_push_tests/fixtures/sealed_preview.json`) still covers decryption. Alternative: add a second plugin fixture with `bot_name`. That gives a cross-repo vector, but it means fixture churn in two repos.

## Acceptance

- A bot whose Desktop title is "Inbox Triage", on a phone in English:
  - approval banner title "Inbox Triage · Approval needed"
  - question "Inbox Triage · Question"
  - failed turn "Inbox Triage · Turn failed"
  - reply "Inbox Triage"
- The same phone in any shipped language shows the label translated and the name unchanged.
- A bot with no Desktop title uses its `display_name`, then its Profile slug. The default Profile with neither shows "Hermes".
- A push from an older plugin (no `bot_name`) looks exactly as it does today.
- The relay-facing payload still carries no name. Only ciphertext changes.

## Tests

- Plugin:
  - `hermex_push_tests/test_hooks.py`: a new test covers the name chain (title → display_name → slug, and default → "Hermes") with an injected `bot_name`. It checks the sealed `bot_name` and English `title` for all four kinds.
  - Update `test_default_profile_titles_as_hermes` (`:151-156`).
  - Extend `test_no_event_of_any_kind_carries_plaintext` (`:135-149`) so the name never appears outside the seal.
  - `test_payload.py`: `bot_name` is clipped to 80 characters.
- App:
  - `HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests`: a new `testRewriteNamesTheBotWithTheKindsLabel` covers approval, clarify, turn_error and reply in `en`, the scheme's test language. It fails today, because `bot_name` isn't decoded and the sealed title is copied.
  - A new `testRewriteKeepsTheSealedTitleWithoutABotName` covers no `bot_name` and an unknown `kind`.
  - `HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: a new `testPushBannerLabelsAreLocalizedInEveryShippedLanguage`, following the Kanban tests (`:111-135`). It fails today, because the keys are missing.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`. For the plugin, run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest plugin -q` from the hermex-push root. CI checks catalog coverage with `ci/check_string_catalog.py`.

## Mocks

Not required: these are system banners with no layout, and the copy is decided above.

## Manual test

Device: a physical iPhone, bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build. Before this check, the maintainer updates the plugin on the host (`hermes plugins update hermex-push`, then restart the Hermes processes).

1. With the app in the background, trigger an approval from a bot that has a Desktop title. Expected: "<title> · Approval needed", with the command as the body.
2. Trigger a question and then a normal reply from the same bot. Expected: "<title> · Question", then a banner titled "<title>".
3. In iOS Settings › Hermex › Language, pick German and trigger another approval. Expected: the label is in German and the bot's title is unchanged.
4. Trigger a reply from a webui chat on the default Profile, with no title set. Expected: the banner is titled "Hermes".

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** every relay banner (bot, webui and other sources) passes through the NSE. Foreground presentation (`PushAppDelegate`) shows the same rewritten content. Tap routing still uses the sealed `profile`, which is unchanged.
- **Targets:** `PushPreview.swift` is compiled by the app and `HermesNotificationService`. The catalog is already in the NSE, the app and the widget. The share extension and the widget don't read this.
- **Servers:** the name is sealed per install and opened only with that install's key (`PushPreviewKeys.matching`). One server's bot name can't show on another's banner.
- **Contracts:** one optional sealed field. The app decodes it tolerantly.
- **Reverse states:** none.
- **Connection modes:** none.
- **Native quality:** 3 new keys in all 17 shipped languages. Right-to-left order is handled by the translations. VoiceOver reads the banner title as usual.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`, `docs/agents/push.md`, `docs/agents/i18n.md` and `hermex-push/plugin/README.md`.

## Outside reach

The maintainer updates the plugin on the host and restarts the Hermes processes that run agents.
