title: feat(push): alert once when a Live Activity run finishes or fails
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** #881

## Problem

On a push-paired server, a run shown in a Live Activity finishes or fails in silence. The activity quietly flips to its final state, with no sound, no Dynamic Island pop and no banner. A user who locked the phone after sending doesn't find out until they look.

Why nothing alerts today (hermex-push `2f1388c`):

- The relay drops reply and turn_error banners while the session has an activity (`hermex-push/relay/src/policy.ts:15`).
- After `done` or `failed`, the relay keeps an `ended` marker for 15 minutes (`relay/src/coordinator.ts:263-267`). It keeps that marker even when the phone deletes the activity (`:153`).
- The plugin sends `done` before the reply (`plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:279-291`), so the reply banner is always dropped.
- The activity push itself carries no `alert` and no `dismissal-date` (`relay/src/apns.ts:95-102`). The run's end is silent, and the finished activity stays on the Lock Screen for up to four hours by default. The app's own local end removes it after 300 s (complete) or 30 s (failed) (`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:782-790`).
- The app's local completion alert returns early for paired servers (`HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:635`), because the relay was meant to cover them.

The rule "a session carried by a Live Activity never also gets a banner" is on record in #490, #740 ("a reply after `done` still produces no banner"), `relay/README.md:67` and `docs/agents/bots.md:1515-1519`. This issue keeps that rule. It changes only the silent finish.

Unpaired servers are covered by local alerts in #862.

## Contract

Code lands in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, in `relay/` only. There is no plugin, host or app code change.

- **Alerting update, then end** (ActivityKit push, topic `<bundle_id>.push-type.liveactivity`, priority 10). On `done` / `failed`, for a device whose rules allow it (Decisions 1):
  1. `aps.event: "update"`, with the same final `content-state` as today, plus `aps.alert`:
     `{"title": "Hermex", "body": {"loc-key": "Response complete"}, "sound": "default"}`
     (`"Response failed"` for `failed`).
  2. `aps.event: "end"`, as today, plus `aps["dismissal-date"]` = now + 300 (done) or now + 30 (failed).

  A device that shouldn't alert gets only step 2.
- The ActivityKit docs show `alert.title` and `alert.body` as objects with `loc-key` / `loc-args`, and `dismissal-date` as a UNIX time on `end` ([Starting and updating Live Activities with ActivityKit push notifications](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/activitykit/starting-and-updating-live-activities-with-activitykit-push-notifications)). On iPhone, an alerting update lights the screen and shows the expanded Live Activity, or a banner on devices without a Dynamic Island. The title and body text show on Apple Watch (`AlertConfiguration` docs). Apple doesn't document alerts on `end`, so the alert rides on the update.
- **Loc keys.** "Response complete" and "Response failed" already exist in `Localizable.xcstrings` in all 17 shipped languages. That catalog is bundled in the app (`project.pbxproj:2177`) and the widget (`:2204`). The app uses these strings in code (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:822, 832`, `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotLiveActivityFeed.swift:135-137`).
- Nothing here touches `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/*`, so #700 is unaffected.

Order: after #881 (same `apns.ts` send path), the hermex-push PR merges and the maintainer deploys the relay. Agents never deploy. The Hermex PR (docs plus one guard test) links the hermex-push PR and lands after the deploy, because its docs describe deployed behavior.

## Plan

**`uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`** (suggested title `feat(relay): alert once when a Live Activity run ends`):

- [ ] `relay/src/policy.ts`: add a pure `endAlert(event: ProgressEvent, device: Device, now: number): 'complete' | 'failed' | null`, following Decisions 1. Leave `deliveryPolicy` and its line 15 as is.
- [ ] `relay/src/apns.ts:91-104`: `activityPush` adds `'dismissal-date'` to `end` pushes (now + 300 for `done`, now + 30 for `failed`). Add a builder for the alerting `update`: final content state, `alert` as in Contract, priority 10, and the same `expiration` as `end` from #881.
- [ ] `relay/src/coordinator.ts:237-273` `progress()`:
  - On `done` / `failed`, when `endAlert` returns a value and `activity.alerted !== event.event_id`, send the alerting update first and wait for it.
  - On `'sent'`, set `activity.alerted = event.event_id` before sending the `end`.
  - A plugin retry after a failed `end` then sends only the `end`. Today `latest.event` is set only after the send succeeds (`:260-262`), so without `alerted` a retry would alert twice.
  - `invalid-token` from either push removes the activity, as today.
- [ ] `relay/README.md:67`: status transitions, plus the one end alert and its rules, plus `dismissal-date`. Keep "suppresses reply and turn-error banners".

**`hermex`** (suggested title `docs(push): a Live Activity run alerts once when it ends`):

- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md:1515-1519`: the relay still sends no reply or error banner while an activity carries the session. Instead, the activity's final update alerts once ("Response complete" / "Response failed"), following the Replies and subagent preferences. The activity then leaves the Lock Screen after 5 minutes (done) or 30 s (failed).
- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md:904-909` (Attention): one clause noting that finish and failure alert through the relay on paired servers.
- [ ] `HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: add `testRelayLiveActivityAlertKeysAreLocalizedInEveryShippedLanguage` for "Response complete" and "Response failed", with a comment that the relay sends them as `loc-key`s. Also add that note as the `comment` on both catalog entries (targeted edit, `docs/agents/i18n.md` § Editing the catalog). A rename or cleanup can't then silently turn the alert into English.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** This reverses the silent finish, not the no-banner rule. When a run shown in a Live Activity finishes or fails, the Live Activity update alerts once: a sound and generic localized text ("Response complete" / "Response failed", sent as `loc-key`). There is no separate banner, so the #490/#740 rule stands. The alert respects the per-server Replies preference and muted subagents. Add a `dismissal-date` that matches the app: 300 s for done, 30 s for failed.

1. **Which rules gate each alert.** `done` follows the reply banner's rules: Replies on, not a muted subagent, and not presence-suppressed for that session (`policy.ts:17-20`). `failed` follows the turn_error rules: only the subagent mute. A failure is worth a buzz even with Replies off, just as the turn-error banner is today. Alternative: gate both on Replies, so Replies off means a fully silent finish.
2. **Alert text.** Title "Hermex" (plain, like the generic banner title, `apns.ts:79`). Body `loc-key` "Response complete" / "Response failed". The iPhone shows the activity itself, and only Apple Watch shows the text. Alternative: title `loc-key` "Response complete" and body `loc-key` "Open to read the reply" (already translated). That is richer on Watch but adds a second key to guard.
3. **Two pushes, sent in order.** Update-then-end is the documented form. Awaiting the update before sending the end keeps them in order on the relay's side. APNs doesn't promise ordering across pushes, so check it on a phone. Alternative: one `end` with an `alert`, which Apple doesn't document.
4. **A stopped run is reported as `done`.** The plugin ends an interrupted turn with `done` (`hooks.py:279-282`). So a run stopped from another device while the phone is locked would alert "Response complete". A Stop in Hermex itself retires the relay registration before the host finishes interrupting (`AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:761`, from `ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:285`), so it usually doesn't alert. Recommend accepting this and naming it in the docs. Alternative: add a `cancelled` progress status across the plugin, the relay schema (`relay/src/contract.ts:36`) and the app's content-state decoder (`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:100-101`), with the relay deployed first. That is honest, but it is a three-part change.
5. **App in the foreground.** The relay's `done` can reach APNs before the app's own local end retires the registration. If iOS plays Live Activity alerts while Hermex is in the foreground, the user watching the chat hears one chime. Recommend: check on a device (Manual test 5). If it chimes, file a follow-up. Don't reuse the relay's presence lease, which `docs/agents/bots.md:1520-1528` rejects on purpose.

## Acceptance

- Paired server, phone locked, and a run in a Live Activity finishes. Exactly one alert: a sound, and the Dynamic Island expands (or a banner on phones without one). No reply banner. The activity leaves the Lock Screen about 5 minutes later.
- The same for a failed run: one "Response failed" alert, and the activity leaves after about 30 s.
- With Replies off for that server, a finished run ends silently. A failed run still alerts.
- A subagent's activity never alerts while "mute subagents" is on.
- A retried `done` (a plugin retry after a relay 503) doesn't alert twice.
- Approvals and questions behave as in #740. Unpaired servers are unchanged (#862).

## Tests

- `relay/test/policy.test.ts`: a table for `endAlert` covering done/failed × Replies on/off × subagent muted/unmuted × presence lease.
- `relay/test/apns.test.ts:41-45`:
  - The `end` payload now includes `'dismissal-date'` (+300 for done, +30 for failed).
  - The alerting update carries `alert.body['loc-key']`, `sound: 'default'` and priority 10.
- `relay/test/worker.test.ts`:
  - `sends status changes immediately…` (`:110-128`): `done` now sends an alerting update and then an `end`, and the reply stays suppressed.
  - A new test: after a failed `end` (`mockResolvedValueOnce('retry')`), a retried `done` sends only the `end`.
  - A new test: Replies off means `done` gets one silent `end`, and `failed` still sends the alert.

  All three fail today, because there is no alert or dismissal date.
- Hermex: the `LocalizationCatalogTests` guard above. It passes today and protects the cross-repo `loc-key` contract.
- Run: `cd relay && npm run check`, then `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`.

## Mocks

Not required: iOS draws the alert from the existing activity views and existing strings. There is no layout or copy change.

## Manual test

Device: a physical iPhone. Live Activity pushes don't reach the Simulator. No app code change is needed, so any current build works. The maintainer deploys the relay before this check.

1. On a paired server, start a bot turn in Hermex and lock the phone. When it finishes, expect one alert (sound, activity expanded) and no reply banner. The activity leaves the Lock Screen after about 5 minutes.
2. Make a turn fail (for example, stop the model provider on a disposable Profile). Expect one "Response failed" alert, and the activity leaves after about 30 s.
3. Turn Replies off for the server in Hermex and repeat step 1. Expect no alert, and the activity ends. Repeat step 2. Expect the alert.
4. Repeat step 1 with a webui chat on the same paired server. Expect the same single alert.
5. Keep Hermex open on the chat until the run finishes. Note whether the phone chimes (see Decisions 5).
6. With an Apple Watch paired, check that the alert reads "Hermex / Response complete" in the phone's language.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** bot and webui runs on paired servers, both relay-driven. A tap on the alert uses the activity's existing widget URL.
- **Targets:** no app code. iOS resolves the `loc-key` from the app's bundle, where the catalog already lives. The widget draws the final state as today. The NSE doesn't run for Live Activity pushes.
- **Servers:** the rules use that pairing's device preferences. Each install is one server.
- **Contracts:** new APNs payload keys only (`alert`, `dismissal-date`). The plugin-to-relay contract is unchanged.
- **Reverse states:** Replies off and subagent mute silence the done alert. Turning them back on restores it.
- **Connection modes:** the relay-to-APNs leg only, so it works the same on LAN and through the tunnel. The hold for an offline phone comes from #881.
- **Native quality:** the alert animation is the system's own. Existing strings in all 17 languages.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md` and `hermex-push/relay/README.md`.

## Outside reach

The maintainer deploys the relay. #881 must be deployed first or in the same deploy.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-agent ca678285 and hermes-webui c67fd2dd; hermex-push 2f1388c.

title: chore(bots): log the Hermes connection's lifecycle
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

When a Bot connection misbehaves on a phone (the tunnel drops it, the upgrade is refused, a call never answers), the device log says nothing about it. There is no `Logger`, `os_log`, `NSLog` or `print` in `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/` (4 files), `HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/` (5 files) or `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/`. The silent points:

- A reply whose id matches no open call is dropped without a trace (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:318`).
- `end(_:)` hands the error to the screens and records nothing (`HermesGateway.swift:352-368`).
- The WebSocket close code is never read. There is no `URLSessionWebSocketDelegate`, and our own close always sends `.normalClosure` (`:416`). `URLSessionWebSocketTask` exposes `closeCode` after a close without a delegate.
- A refused upgrade's HTTP status sits on `task.response` and is never read (`:227-233`, `:414`).
- The 45-second silence timer cancels the socket silently (`:302-306`), and so does a call past its deadline (`:141-146`, `:179-191`).
- Sign-in steps fail without a record of which step or status (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:86-113`, ticket at `:157-161`).

Other areas already log with privacy annotations: `SSEEventDecoder` (`HermesMobile/Networking/SSEClient.swift:224-227`), `ChatStreamCoordinator` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:6-9`), and the push relay (`HermesMobile/Push/PushRelayClient.swift:32`, `:94`, `:99`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract. What the host sends on `/api/ws`, at the pin:

- A refusal before accept arrives as an HTTP status with no close code (`hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:139-151`, `:583-585`).
- After accept, a stalled send closes with 1011 (`tui_gateway/ws.py:222-228`), and teardown closes normally (`:400-401`).
- No close reason is sent on this route. A proxy can put any bytes there, so the reason is never logged.

## Plan

- [ ] **One logger** (Decision 1): `Logger(subsystem: Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier ?? "HermesMobile", category: "HermesConnection")`, shared by `HermesConnection.swift` and `HermesGateway.swift` (same target).
- [ ] **Anonymous tags.** Give each `HermesConnection` a process-local serial (`c1`, `c2`, …) and use the gateway's `generation` (`HermesGateway.swift:45`) as the socket number (`s3`). Lines from two servers or two sockets can be told apart without naming either.
- [ ] **Reason describer.** A small pure function returns only:
  - `URLError <code>`
  - `HTTP <status>`
  - the `BotFailure` case (`rejected(403)`, `transport`, …)
  - `DecodingError`, `cancelled`, or the error's type name.

  Never `String(describing:)` or `localizedDescription` on a `URLError`: its user info carries the failing URL, which contains the host.
- [ ] **Sign-in** (`HermesConnection.beginSignIn`, `:86-113`, and `gatewayUpgrade`, `:157-161`): `.notice` on success with the reported release; `.error` on failure naming the step (`status`, `login`, `identity`, `ticket`) and the reason. `retire()` (`:176-182`): `.notice` "connection retired".
- [ ] **Socket open** (`handshake`, `HermesGateway.swift:218-249`): `.notice` once the keepalive starts. If opening fails, `.error` with the reason, which includes the upgrade's HTTP status.
- [ ] **Native socket** (`NativeBotSocket.receive`, `:412-417`): when a receive fails, add to the log the close code (`task.closeCode.rawValue`, when not `.invalid`) and the HTTP status, when `task.response` holds one other than 101. Never `closeReason`.
- [ ] **Silence** (`:302-306`): `.error` "no frame for 45 s; closing".
- [ ] **End** (`end(_:)`, `:352-368`):
  - nil error → `.notice` "socket closed, last screen left"
  - `.stale` → `.notice` "socket closed, connection retired"
  - anything else → `.error` "socket dropped: <reason>", with the number of calls failed and screens told.
- [ ] **Unmatched reply** (`consume`, `:318`): `.notice` "reply for call <id> matched no open call". Skip the keepalive's string ids (`heartbeat-N`, sent at `:278`), or a healthy idle socket logs every 15 s.
- [ ] **Unanswered call** (`expire`, `:179-191`, and the local timeout at `:144`): `.error` "<method> got no reply in <n> s". Store the method name in `Pending` (`:59-65`); `HermesCall.method` is a fixed string.
- [ ] **Privacy:** interpolate only numbers, step names, method names, case names and the describer's output, each with `privacy: .public`. Never interpolate a host, address, URL, session or runtime id, Profile name, title, message text, ticket, replay epoch or install id. A comment above the logger says so.
- [ ] **Docs:**
  - `docs/agents/bots.md`, after the `HermesConnection`/`HermesGateway` paragraphs (`:22-77`): one short paragraph on what is logged, the category, and the privacy rule.
  - `DEVELOPMENT.md`: a line on watching it in Console.app. If #870's "Launch arguments and profiling" section has landed, put it there.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Log when the Hermes connection opens, drops (with the reason), is refused (with the HTTP status), and when a reply or request goes unmatched. Never log session ids, hosts, titles or message text.

1. **Subsystem and category.** Recommend the bundle identifier, like most loggers here and #870's signposter, with the category `HermesConnection`. The Branch TestFlight app then logs under `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.branch` and never mixes with a side-by-side production install. Alternative: the fixed `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile` the push files use (`PushRelayClient.swift:32`, `HermesMobile/Push/PushRegistrar.swift:64`). One filter works for both builds, but their lines mix.
2. **Levels.** Recommend `.notice` for normal lifecycle (sign-in succeeded, socket open, quiet close, retired, unmatched reply) and `.error` for failures (sign-in refused, upgrade refused, a drop with an error, silence, an unanswered call). Both are stored, so `log show` and Console keep them; `.info` and `.debug` are dropped by default. An unmatched reply stays at `.notice` because it is usually a late reply to a screen that already closed (`leave`, `HermesGateway.swift:103-111`). Alternative: `.debug` for it, which then disappears from `log show`. No `.fault`.
3. **"Unmatched request" means our call that got no reply.** Recommend logging a call that passes its deadline. A server request that no open screen claims is normal (the host keeps it in `open_requests`, and the chat reads it on resume), so logging it would be noise. Alternative: log every server request delivered while no screen claims it.
4. **No per-frame logging.** Recommend no lines for events, deltas or keepalive pongs: they are high volume and near message content.
5. **Tests.** Recommend testing only the describer, the one piece that can leak a host. Alternative: inject a log sink and assert every call, which is more machinery than value.
6. **`Logger`, not `NSLog`.** Recommend `Logger`: `NSLog` has no privacy redaction. Note that on the simulator here, `simctl … log show` doesn't show the app's `Logger` lines, so check this on a device.

## Acceptance

- With Console filtered to the category, opening the Bots inbox logs a sign-in and a socket open. Going home logs a quiet close. Losing the network logs a drop with a `URLError` code or the silence line. A refused upgrade logs its HTTP status.
- A call that passes its deadline logs its method name; a stray reply logs its call id.
- A healthy idle inbox logs nothing on the 15 s keepalive.
- No line in the category contains the host, address, session or runtime ids, Profile names, titles, message text, tickets or the install id.

## Tests

- New `HermesConnectionLogTests` in `HermesMobileTests` (add it to `project.pbxproj`):
  - A `URLError(.networkConnectionLost)` whose user info has `NSURLErrorFailingURLErrorKey` = `https://secret-host.example/api/ws` describes as `URLError -1005` and doesn't contain `secret-host`.
  - `BotFailure.rejected(403)` describes as `rejected(403)`; a `DecodingError` as `DecodingError`.
  - After #880 lands, `.upgradeRefused(403)` describes with its status.
- These fail today: the describer doesn't exist.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionLogTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests` (`BotClientTests` guards the touched gateway paths).

## Mocks

Not required: no UI.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build), cabled to the Mac.

1. Open Console.app, select the iPhone, start streaming, and filter `subsystem:com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.branch category:HermesConnection`.
2. Open the Bots inbox. Expected: a sign-in line with the release, then "socket s1 open".
3. Go home. Expected: "socket s1 closed, last screen left".
4. Return. Expected: "socket s2 open" and no new sign-in line (the sign-in is reused).
5. Open a chat, turn on Airplane Mode for a minute, then turn it off. Expected: a drop line with a `URLError` code or the silence line, then a new socket open.
6. Leave the inbox open for a minute. Expected: no line every 15 s.
7. Search the stream for the tunnel's hostname and a bot's name. Expected: no hits.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** every Bot screen and push provisioning share `HermesConnection`, so all their sign-ins and sockets are logged. Push setup's REST steps aren't (only its sign-in).
- **Targets:** main app only; the extensions never open this connection.
- **Servers:** lines never name a server; `cN` and `sN` tell connections and sockets apart after a server switch.
- **Contracts:** none; reads only what the client already has.
- **Reverse states:** n/a.
- **Connection modes:** the drop, silence and close-code lines are the evidence for tunnel idle drops and LAN hiccups.
- **Native quality:** n/a (no UI, no strings).
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md`.
- **Related issues:**
  - #700's later slices (0.3 server kinds, 0.4 reconnect and replay) should log through this logger and follow the same privacy rule: sequence numbers and counts, never session keys or runtime ids.
  - #744's route choice should log which route won as `primary` or `alternate`, never its host.
  - #880 maps the refused upgrade at the same `NativeBotSocket.receive` line. Whichever lands second logs the mapped failure.
  - #708's token refresh must never log a token.
  - #751 and #752 need nothing; the public status probe stays unlogged.
  - #870 uses the same subsystem convention for its signposter.

## Outside reach

None.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-agent ca678285 and hermes-webui c67fd2dd.

title: chore(test): a local Hermes test server with a scripted model
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

The only Hermes host we can test against is the maintainer's real server on another Mac. So two things are hard:
- **Tool and approval turns in the simulator.** We can't run one without a real model call on a real bot, and without a real approval reaching a real terminal. CLAUDE.md rule 2 keeps agents from mutating that server.
- **Fixtures for those turns.** `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures` runs one canned "Reply with exactly: ok. Do not use tools." turn (`scripts/fixtures/HermesFixtureCapture.swift:14-16`), so the fixtures have no tool or approval frames. The known event set is text, thinking and title only (`HermesMobileTests/HermesAgentFixtureTests.swift:9-15`). The capture is also tied to the real host in three places:
  - the `hermex-bot` Keychain item (`scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures:29-34`),
  - the `inbox-triage` Profile (`HermesFixtureCapture.swift:14`),
  - a release check against the pin (`:181-182`).

A pinned Hermes running on this Mac, driven by a tiny scripted model, fixes both. It's deterministic, it makes no model calls, and it can't touch real sessions.

## Contract

Hermes host, at the pin (`HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`: `ca678285`, 0.21.5). Each fact was checked in `.codex-tmp/hermes-agent`:

- **Custom model endpoint.**
  - `model.provider: custom` with `model.base_url` points the main model at any OpenAI-compatible server (`website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md:1510`, `website/docs/user-guide/configuring-models.md:131-137`).
  - No API key is needed: `_custom_runtime` substitutes `"no-key-required"` (`hermes_cli/runtime_provider_custom.py:455-458`).
  - `model.streaming: false` turns off streaming for the session (`agent/agent_init.py:1201-1204`). So the stub can answer plain JSON on `POST /v1/chat/completions`, with `tool_calls` when it wants a tool.
  - Set `model.context_length: 256000`. Otherwise Hermes probes, falls back to 256K (`agent/model_metadata.py:298-312`), and refuses anything under 64K (`:317`, `agent/agent_init.py:2019`).
  - Background calls (titles, compression) hit the stub too. `auxiliary.title_generation.enabled: false` turns titles off (`agent/title_generator.py:455-456`).
- **The tool.** The terminal tool is `terminal`, with a `command` string argument (`tools/terminal_tool.py:1377-1385`).
  - `python3 -c "print(1)"` needs approval: `detect_dangerous_command` flags interpreter `-c` through `_execution_flag_findings` (`tools/approval_detection.py:961-977`, `:1536`). The old regex entries at `:461-465` are only aliases for stored approvals.
  - The default approval mode is `smart`, which asks an auxiliary model (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1633`, `:1656`). Set `approvals.mode: manual`.
  - The terminal backend defaults to `local` with `cwd: "."` (`:278`, `:284`). **An approved command really runs on this Mac**, so the script only ever asks for `python3 -c "print(1)"`, never `rm`.
- **Sign-in.** Basic auth comes from `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` and `_PASSWORD` (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1018-1023`; `plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py:6-8`).
- **Hermex refuses an ungated host.** It needs `/api/status` to report `auth_required: true` with a `basic` provider (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:99-100`). A plain loopback bind has the gate off (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:470-477`). The workaround:
  - Keep the loopback bind, and set `HERMES_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_URL` (`config_defaults.py:1035-1041`) to a non-loopback URL such as `http://hermex-local.invalid`. That turns the gate on (`web_server.py:480-491`, applied at `:1122`), and `/api/status` reports it (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:357-371`, `:518`).
  - A `127.0.0.1` Host header is still accepted on a loopback bind (`web_server.py:572-573`), for the WebSocket too (`hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py:165-189`).
  - Cookies are non-`Secure` over plain HTTP (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/cookies.py:10`).
  - Hermex's ATS allows HTTP to `127.0.0.0/8` (`HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist:53-54`, `:70-73`).
- **Stable identity across runs.** `install_id` is minted in `$HERMES_HOME/install_id` when `HERMES_HOME` is outside `~/.hermes` (`hermes_cli/install_identity.py:16-17`, `:60-83`; `hermes_constants.py:217-233`). Hermex pins it on the first connect and rejects a different one (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:30-36`). A new temporary home would break the saved connection on every run, unless the script writes a fixed id first.
- **Approvals on the wire (slice 2).** The host sends an `approval` server request, and the client answers with `approval.respond {session_id, request_id, choice}` (`apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json:64`, `:37423`). Hermex already builds that answer (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift:260-261`). Tool frames are `tool.start` / `tool.complete` (`:38476`; consumed at `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotActivity.swift:62-90`).
- **Python.** hermes-agent needs Python `>=3.11,<3.14` (`pyproject.toml:15`); this Mac's default `python3` is 3.10. The web server's dependencies are core (`pyproject.toml:128-134`).
- **Never stop the server with `hermes dashboard --stop` or `hermes update`.** Both SIGTERM every `hermes dashboard|serve` process they find in the process table (`hermes_cli/subcommands/dashboard.py:38-44`). That is exactly the kill-by-pattern CLAUDE.md rule 1 forbids.
- **#700.** #700 must preserve nothing here: this is a dev tool. But #700 slice 0.3 rewrites `DevAutoLogin` and `scripts/sim-login`, so this issue leaves both alone.

## Plan

**Slice 1: the server script and docs**
- [ ] New `scripts/local-hermes` (Python, standard library only, like `scripts/test-sim`):
  - **Setup, once per pin.** Read the commit from `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` line 1. Clone `https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent` at that commit into `~/Library/Caches/hermex-local-hermes/<sha>/src`. Create `…/<sha>/.venv` with `uv venv --python 3.13` and install with `uv pip install -e src`. Never install into `.codex-tmp/hermes-agent`, which is a read-only reference. Later runs reuse the cache.
  - **Home.** Make a temp `HERMES_HOME` with `tempfile.mkdtemp`, containing a `workspace/` folder. Write `config.yaml`:
    ```yaml
    model: {provider: custom, base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:<stub-port>/v1", default: hermex-stub,
            streaming: false, context_length: 256000}
    approvals: {mode: manual}
    auxiliary: {title_generation: {enabled: false}}
    terminal: {backend: local, cwd: "."}
    ```
    Also write a fixed 32-hex `install_id`, so a saved Hermex connection survives restarts.
  - **Stub model.** A `ThreadingHTTPServer` on `127.0.0.1:0`, running in-process. It answers `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a pure function of the request body:
    - No `tools` in the request (a background call) → a short plain reply.
    - The last message is from the user → "Let me run a quick check." plus one `terminal` tool call, `python3 -c "print(1)"`, with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`.
    - The last message is a tool result → "The command returned: <first line of the result>." with `finish_reason: "stop"`. This also covers a denied approval.
    - `"stream": true` → 400 with a clear message, so a config mistake is loud.
    - `GET /v1/models` → one model, `hermex-stub`.
  - **Server.** `subprocess.Popen([<venv>/bin/hermes, "serve", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", <port>], start_new_session=True, cwd=<home>/workspace, env=…)`. The env has `HERMES_HOME`, the two basic-auth variables and `HERMES_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_URL`. Record the PID; with `start_new_session` it is also the process-group id.
  - **Readiness.** Poll `GET /api/status` until it answers. Fail loudly unless `auth_required` is true and `auth_providers` contains `basic`, which is the gate Hermex checks.
  - **Output.** Print the address, the username and the password.
  - **Stop.** On Ctrl-C or exit, `os.killpg(<recorded pid>, SIGTERM)`, wait up to 10 s, then `SIGKILL` the same group. Delete the temp home the script created, unless `--keep-home` is set. Never look up a process by name.
  - **Flags:** `--port` (default `9199`, Decision 2) and `--keep-home`.
- [ ] Stub tests: `scripts/tests/test_local_hermes.py`, loading the script the same way `scripts/tests/test_sim_runner.py:19-24` loads `test-sim`.
- [ ] `DEVELOPMENT.md`: add "### Local Hermes test server" after "### Signing a simulator in" (`:188-203`). Cover:
  - what the script runs, and that it runs a real harmless command on this Mac when approved;
  - that it's simulator-only (loopback);
  - how to point the app at it: in the simulator, Settings → the server's **Hermes connection** (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:2237-2245`) → address `http://127.0.0.1:9199` with the printed credentials (Decision 3);
  - that a webui login is still needed, because Bot connections are saved per webui server (`BotConnection.swift:95-105`; the logged-in root is keyed by the webui server, `HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:77-95`);
  - that `scripts/sim-login` won't replace an existing connection (`HermesMobile/Config/DevAutoLogin.swift:57-60`).

**Slice 2: fixtures from the local server**
- [ ] `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures --local`:
  - Skip the Keychain read (`:29-34`). Export `HERMEX_CAPTURE_ADDRESS`, `_USERNAME` and `_PASSWORD` with the local values the capture tool already reads from its environment.
  - Refuse to run unless `http://127.0.0.1:9199/api/status` answers.
- [ ] `scripts/fixtures/HermesFixtureCapture.swift`, in local mode:
  - Use the `default` Profile instead of `inbox-triage` (`:14`).
  - After `client.capabilities {server_requests: true}` (the existing call), submit one prompt. Wait for the `approval` server request and answer `approval.respond {session_id, request_id, choice: "once"}`. Record every frame until `message.complete`, then close and delete the session as today.
  - Write only a new `HermesMobileTests/Fixtures/HermesAgent/turn-tool-approval-frames.json`, carrying its own `hermes_agent_sha` and `version`. Leave the real-host fixtures untouched (Decision 4).
  - The pin check (`:181-182`) passes on its own, because the local server runs the pinned commit. The leak check must also treat the temp home path as a secret.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` § Working with the server: one sentence saying the tool/approval fixture comes from `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures --local` against `scripts/local-hermes`.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- Slice 1: a script runs the pinned Hermes on this Mac with a scripted stub model: some text, then a harmless command that needs approval, then more text. Loopback only, manual approvals, temp home. Plus a `DEVELOPMENT.md` section on using it with the simulator.
- Slice 2: `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures` can target this local server, to record tool and approval turns.

1. **Non-streaming stub.** Recommend: plain JSON with `model.streaming: false`. That's the smallest stub that gives text → tool → approval → text. Alternative: a streaming SSE stub, which also exercises `message.delta` but is about three times the code.
2. **Fixed port and credentials.** Recommend: port `9199` and fixed dev credentials (for example `hermex` / `hermex-local`), plus the fixed `install_id`. Then the Hermes connection saved in the simulator keeps working across runs. It's safe because only loopback peers can connect. Alternative: random values per run. Safer in theory, but you re-enter the connection every time.
3. **Pointing the simulator at it.** Recommend: document the manual switch in the Hermes connection form for now. Alternative: a `--local-hermes` flag in `scripts/sim-login` plus a replace flag in `DevAutoLogin`. Wait for #700 slice 0.3, which rewrites both and makes a Hermes server a first-class server that could be added on its own.
4. **Where local captures go.** Recommend: a new fixture file only. The status, Profile list and plain turn stay recorded from a real host, which is the point of those fixtures. Alternative: a second full fixture set in its own folder. More files and a second pin check, for little gain.
5. **Setup location.** Recommend: a per-pin cache under `~/Library/Caches`, cloned from GitHub. It lives outside the worktree, survives worktree cleanup, and is shared by every worktree. Alternative: `--source <path>` to reuse an existing checkout; add it only if the clone becomes a problem.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/local-hermes` starts in under a minute after the first setup. `/api/status` on `127.0.0.1:9199` reports `auth_required: true` with `basic`.
- In the simulator, a Bot Chat with "Hermes" on that connection shows "Let me run a quick check.", then an approval card for `python3 -c "print(1)"`.
  - Approve → the command runs, and the reply is "The command returned: 1."
  - Deny → the reply reports the denial.
- Ctrl-C stops the server and every child in its process group, and deletes the temp home. No other Hermes process on the Mac is touched.
- Restarting the script keeps the saved simulator connection working, with no "different host" error.
- `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures --local` writes `turn-tool-approval-frames.json` and nothing else.

## Tests

- Slice 1: `scripts/tests/test_local_hermes.py`.
  - The stub's decision function: no tools gives plain text; a last user message gives the `terminal` tool call with exactly `python3 -c "print(1)"`; a last tool message gives the closing text with the result's first line; `stream: true` gives an error.
  - The generated `config.yaml` has `approvals.mode: manual`, `model.streaming: false`, and a loopback `base_url`.
  - Stop signals only the recorded process group: patch `os.killpg` and assert its argument.
  - All fail today: there is no script.
  - Plus one real run of the script, as CLAUDE.md asks for a changed script.
- Slice 2: `HermesAgentFixtureTests` gets `testToolApprovalTurnDecodesAndSettles`:
  - The `approval` request parses as `BotServerRequest` with a `.approval` pending request whose command contains `python3 -c` and whose choices aren't empty (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequest.swift:50-73`, `:84-110`).
  - Every event type is in a known set extended with the tool events.
  - Replaying the frames settles one turn with one completed tool.
  - `fixture()` skips when a file can't be read (`HermesAgentFixtureTests.swift:20-26`). So read `manifest` first to prove the tree is present, then `XCTFail` if the new file is missing. It must fail today, not skip.
- Run: `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v` and `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesAgentFixtureTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests`

## Mocks

Not required: no UI.

## Manual test

Device: the simulator on this Mac. The server listens on loopback only, so a phone can't reach it.

1. Run `scripts/local-hermes`. The first run clones and installs; later runs start in seconds. The address and credentials print.
2. In the simulator (signed in to your webui server), open Settings → your server → Hermes connection. Enter `http://127.0.0.1:9199` and the printed credentials, then save.
3. Bots → Hermes → send "hi". You see "Let me run a quick check.", then an approval card for `python3 -c "print(1)"`. Approve: "The command returned: 1."
4. Send again and Deny: the reply reports the denial.
5. Ctrl-C the script and run it again. The connection reconnects without re-entering anything.
6. Slice 2: with the script running, run `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures --local`. Only `turn-tool-approval-frames.json` changes in `git status`.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** developer tooling only. It exercises Bot Chat approvals, which Sessions doesn't use on Hermes yet.
- **Targets:** none change in slice 1. Slice 2 adds one fixture file and one test in `HermesMobileTests`.
- **Servers:** the simulator's Bot connection is saved per webui server. Pointing it at the local server replaces the saved one, as Decision 3 documents.
- **Contracts:** verified above at the pin. The local server always runs the pinned commit, so it moves when the pin moves.
- **Reverse states:** start → Ctrl-C stops it and removes the temp home. Approve and Deny are both scripted.
- **Connection modes:** loopback only, by design. LAN and tunnel stay covered by the real server.
- **Native quality:** none; no app UI.
- **Docs:** `DEVELOPMENT.md` (slice 1) and one line in `AGENTS.md` (slice 2). `docs/agents/bots.md` doesn't change.

## Outside reach

None. The first run needs network access, to clone hermes-agent and install its dependencies.

title: feat(bots): answer password-vault and 2FA prompts on the phone
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P2 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

When a bot needs to unlock its password vault, save a login, or enter a sign-in code, Bot Chat says "Answer this in Hermes Desktop on the Mac" and offers only Skip. A user away from the Mac can't finish the sign-in. They can only skip it or let it time out, so the bot's browser work stops.

- `BotDesktopTaskRequest.Kind` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequest.swift:290-332`) lumps `vault.unlock_prompt`, `vault.save_login` and `vault.code` in with the renderer-only tasks. It marks them `needsSomeoneAtTheMac` (`:321`) with the detail "Answer this in Hermes Desktop on the Mac. Skip it here and the bot carries on without it." (`:323-327`).
- `BotServerRequest.init` (`:68-69`) drops their params: `display_name`, `origin`, `site`, `hint`.
- `BotConversation.declineDesktopTask` (`BotConversation.swift:1227-1236`) can only send the empty value, and `BotDesktopTaskRequestBody` (`BotPendingRequestCard.swift:433-477`) offers only Skip and Stop.
- `docs/agents/bots.md:394-399` records this as "the phone cannot answer them".

## Contract

**The prompts (hermes-agent `ca678285`, `tui_gateway/contracts/server_requests.py`):**

| Method | Params | Host timeout |
|---|---|---|
| `vault.unlock_prompt` | `{session_id, backend, display_name}` (`:125-131`) | 120 s |
| `vault.save_login` | `{session_id, origin, site}` (`:134-140`) | 180 s |
| `vault.code` | `{session_id, site?, hint?}` (`:143-149`) | 180 s |

The timeouts are set in `tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py:219-233`.

**The answer.**
- All three answer with `ValueResult {value: str}`, and `""` means declined (`:22-26`).
- Hermex already answers `sudo` and `secret` the same way, through the acknowledged proxy `request.answer {id, result: {value}}`. The host resolves it for any client and replies `ok` or `expired` (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:1162-1175`, `tui_gateway/server_requests.py:201-236`).
- Hermex's wire path already exists: `HermesCall.requestAnswer(id:result:)` with `.value` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift:52`, `:139-143`, `:262-263`, admitted at `:375`).

**What the host does with each answer:**
- **Unlock.** The master password goes to the manager's CLI (`1Password` or `Bitwarden`, `agent/vault_backends/onepassword.py:32`, `bitwarden.py:34`). Only a session token stays in host memory, per Profile, until the chat that unlocked it ends or it sits idle for 30 minutes (`agent/vault_backends/unlock.py:1-22`, `:76-143`, `tools/browser_vault_tool.py:260-286`).
- **Save login.** `value` must be a JSON-encoded string `{"identifier": …, "password": …}`, and both must be non-empty (`tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py:222-230`, `tools/browser_vault_tool.py:312`). `_ask` re-encodes a non-string value (`tui_gateway/server.py:1319-1325`), but the contract says string, so send a string. The login is stored in **Hermes's own encrypted vault on the host**, bound to that origin, and then filled into the page (`agent/vault_store.py:1-16`, `tools/browser_vault_tool.py:291-328`). Desktop calls this vault Settings → Passwords & Logins. See Decision 1.
- **Code.** The host strips spaces and dashes (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:379`) and types the code into the page. The model never sees it.

**#700 must preserve:**
- `request.answer` admission and its `.value` shape;
- the `client.capabilities {server_requests: true}` handshake, without which the host declines these prompts for a session only the phone is attached to (`docs/agents/bots.md:94-100`, `tui_gateway/server_requests.py:117-122`);
- the rule that request params and answer values are never cached or logged (`docs/agents/bots.md:335`).

## Plan

- [ ] **Model** (`BotPendingRequest.swift`):
  - Move the three `vault.*` kinds out of `BotDesktopTaskRequest.Kind` (`:292-321`) into `BotCredentialRequest.Kind` (`:229-246`) as `vaultUnlock`, `vaultSaveLogin` and `vaultCode`.
  - Carry their params as optional strings (`displayName`, `origin`, `site`, `hint`), read in `BotServerRequest.init` (`:63-67`).
  - Give each kind a `title`, `detail`, `handling` and `skipConsequence`, like `sudo` and `secret` (`:232-278`).
  - Add `static func saveLoginValue(identifier:password:) -> String`. It JSON-encodes with `JSONEncoder` or `JSONSerialization`, never string interpolation.
- [ ] **Delete the Desktop-only decline**, since nothing else uses it:
  - `needsSomeoneAtTheMac` (`:316-321`) and its detail branch;
  - `BotConversation.mayDecline` (`:371-376`) and its use in `prepareAnswer` (`:1161-1163`);
  - `declineDesktopTask` (`:1227-1236`);
  - the Skip branch in `BotDesktopTaskRequestBody` (`BotPendingRequestCard.swift:462-470`) and its `canDecline`/`onDecline` inputs (`:33-35`, `:63-64`);
  - the callers at `BotChatView.swift:129` and `:331-334`, `BotRoomComposerView.swift:108`, and `BotChatComposerView.swift:132`;
  - `BotFeedback.Event.declined`, which loses its only producer, with its `ChatHaptics.swift:22` and `:73` cases and the `ChatHapticsTests` entry.
- [ ] **Answer.** `answerCredential` (`BotConversation.swift:1206-1218`) already sends `.value` and maps `expired`. `skipCredential` (`:1220-1225`) is the Skip for all three. Save login calls `answerCredential` with `saveLoginValue(…)` only when both fields are non-empty.
- [ ] **Card** (`BotCredentialRequestBody`, `BotPendingRequestCard.swift:362-431`, still keyed by request id at `:58-60`):
  - **Unlock:** one `SecureField`, `.textContentType(.password)`.
  - **Save login:** a plain `TextField` for the email or username (`.username`, no autocapitalization or autocorrection), then a `SecureField` for the password (`.password`). Password AutoFill can then fill the site's login from the user's Passwords app. Save is disabled until both are filled.
  - **Code:** one `SecureField`, `.textContentType(.oneTimeCode)`.
  - Every field is cleared the moment it is sent, as `submit()` does today (`:423-430`).
- [ ] **Copy** (recommended; mocks settle it). Each kind names what the value is for, where it goes, and "Hermex never saves it":
  - **Unlock.** Title: "Unlock {display_name}". Handling: "Goes straight to {display_name} on this bot's Mac to unlock it for this chat. Hermex never saves it."
  - **Save login.** Title: "Save your {site} login?". Detail: "The bot reached a sign-in page at {origin} and has no login for it." Handling: see Decision 1.
  - **Code.** Title: "Verification code for {site}". Handling: "Typed into the page on this bot's Mac. The model never sees it, and Hermex never saves it."
- [ ] Add every new string to `Localizable.xcstrings` for all shipped languages.
- [ ] Rewrite `docs/agents/bots.md:384-399`. The vault prompts are answered from the phone, and only the renderer tasks (`tour`, `terminal.read`, `window.read`, `preview.read`, `preview.act`) stay Desktop-only.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** This is an explicit exception to #713 decision 9 ("Hermes-only capabilities … get no issues"). A secure field on the phone for all three prompts. No extra Face ID step before sending (the app lock, #885, covers device access). Never cache or log the values. The save-login copy says plainly where the login is saved. Mocks first.

1. **Save-login wording.** At the pin, `vault.save_login` writes to Hermes's own encrypted vault on the host, not to 1Password or Bitwarden (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:312-320`, `agent/vault_store.py:1-16`). Desktop describes it as "encrypted on this machine" and points to Settings → Passwords & Logins. Recommend handling copy that stays true: "Saved in Hermes's password vault on this bot's Mac, then filled into the page. The model never sees the password, and Hermex never saves it." Alternative: shorter copy that names only "Hermes's password vault". Don't call it "your password manager": it is not 1Password or Bitwarden.
2. **Where the vault kinds live.** Recommend folding them into `BotCredentialRequest`. They share the `{value}` answer, the masked field, Skip-as-empty and the "never stored" rule, and the Desktop-only decline path disappears. Alternative: a separate `BotVaultRequest` case. That keeps sudo and secret untouched but duplicates the answer, guard and card plumbing.
3. **Code field style.** The decision says a secure field, so the code is masked, and the host already strips spaces and dashes. Recommend verifying on a device that the Messages or Mail code suggestion appears over the masked field. If it doesn't, bring that back as a question rather than silently switching to a plain field.
4. **No countdown.** Recommend no deadline on these cards, the same as sudo (120 s) today. When one expires, `request.cancel` removes it, and #892 adds the note. Alternative: a once-a-minute "N min left" line like the connection card (`BotPendingRequestCard.swift:494-499`). It is informative, but it is extra copy on a short-lived prompt.

## Acceptance

- An unlock prompt shows "Unlock 1Password" (or Bitwarden) with a masked field. The typed password reaches the host as `request.answer {id, result: {value}}`, and the bot continues with the vault unlocked.
- A save-login prompt shows the site, a username field and a masked password field. Save sends one JSON string with both, and the bot fills the page. Save stays disabled until both are filled.
- A code prompt shows the site and a masked field that offers the one-time code suggestion. The code is sent as typed.
- Skip on any of the three sends `value: ""`, and the bot carries on without it.
- An answer to an expired prompt reports "already answered or has expired" and resends nothing.
- No value appears in drafts, the history cache, the recent transcript, logs, or a replacement card: a new request id starts with empty fields.
- `terminal.read`, `window.read`, `preview.*` and `tour` cards are unchanged apart from losing the unused Skip branch.

## Tests

In `BotPendingRequestTests` (each fails today because the vault kinds are unanswerable Desktop tasks):
- `testVaultPromptsAreAnswerableCredentialsWithTheirParams`: replaces the vault rows in `testDesktopTaskKindsMapFromTheirServerRequests` (`:146-165`).
- `testAVaultUnlockSendsTheMasterPasswordAsItsValue`.
- `testASaveLoginSendsIdentifierAndPasswordAsOneJSONString`: decode the sent string back to `{identifier, password}`. An empty identifier or password is never sent.
- `testAVaultCodeIsSentAsTyped`.
- `testSkippingAVaultPromptSendsAnEmptyValue`: replaces `testAVaultPromptIsSkippedFromThePhone` (`:627-644`).
- `testAnExpiredVaultPromptReportsAlreadyResolved`.
- `testADesktopTaskThatCannotBeDeclinedNeverDispatches` (`:648-660`) becomes "a Desktop task is never answered", with no decline API left to call.

Also:
- `BotChatPresentationTests`: one hosted test that the save-login card has a plain identifier field, a secure password field and a disabled Save until both are filled. Drop the `canDecline`/`onDecline` arguments from the card built at `:1412`.
- `ChatHapticsTests`: drop `.declined`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatHapticsTests`

## Mocks

Required first:
- the unlock card, the save-login card (two fields) and the code card;
- each while answering, and after the host said it had expired;
- light and dark, and the largest accessibility text size.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

These steps need the test bot's host to have the browser tool. The unlock step also needs the 1Password or Bitwarden CLI enabled. Skip any step the host can't produce.

1. In Bot Chat, ask the test bot: "Open https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/login and save a login for it." Expected: a "Save your … login?" card with a username and a masked password field. Enter `tomsmith` / `SuperSecretPassword!` and tap Save. Expected: the bot fills the page and reports success. Nothing is added to the iPhone's Passwords app.
2. Repeat, but tap Skip. Expected: the bot says you chose not to save a login.
3. If a vault CLI is enabled: ask the bot to sign in to a site whose login lives in that manager. Expected: an "Unlock 1Password" (or Bitwarden) card. Enter the master password. Expected: the bot continues.
4. If you have a site that sends a code by text: let the bot reach its code page. Expected: a code card, and the keyboard offers the code from Messages over the masked field. Tap it and send. Expected: the bot continues.
5. Leave one card unanswered for 3 minutes. Expected: it disappears (see #892 for the note), and nothing is sent.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the Bot Chat request card only.
  - The inbox shows the bot as waiting, and the Live Activity shows "waiting for answer"; neither answers.
  - The push plugin sends no banner for vault prompts (`hermex-push` `2f1388c`, `plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:1-11`: only reply, turn error, approval and clarify), so this issue adds none.
  - Group rooms keep showing Desktop attention for them (`BotRoomComposerView.swift:110-117`).
  - No deep link, intent or share path.
- **Targets:** main app only. Nothing in the share extension, widget or notification service reads these types.
- **Servers:** answers are bound to the captured generation, runtime and request id and revalidated at the socket write (`BotConversation.swift:1312-1321`), so one server's prompt can't be answered on another.
- **Contracts:** the existing `request.answer`. The save-login value is a JSON string.
- **Reverse states:** Skip on every card. A saved login is removed on the Mac (Desktop → Settings → Passwords & Logins, or `hermes vault`); the copy points there rather than promising an undo on the phone.
- **Native quality:** the secure fields with the right content types, VoiceOver labels for every field and button, Dynamic Type, light and dark, all shipped languages.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(bots): say when a request was withdrawn
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

When the host withdraws an approval, question or password prompt, its card just vanishes from Bot Chat. A user who comes back to the phone can't tell whether someone answered it at the Mac, it timed out, or the work stopped. For an approval that matters: a timeout means the command did **not** run, and the bot's next message may only make sense once you know that.

`BotConversation.applyRequestCancel` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:1438-1451`) removes the matching envelope and clears the card. It reads `id` and `method` but never `reason`.

## Contract

Client-only: no new calls. `request.cancel {id, method, reason}` is already received (`tui_gateway/contracts/server_requests.py:212-230`, hermes-agent `ca678285`). The contract names five reasons and allows free text from approval callers (`:226`):

| Reason | When the host sends it |
|---|---|
| `timeout` | A blocking request's deadline passed (`tui_gateway/server_requests.py:167-176`), or an approval's own timeout (`tools/approval_gateway_wait.py:182-192`). Approvals default to 300 s (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1657`). The unanswered approval fails closed: nothing ran. |
| `interrupted` | The session was stopped, from this phone or from anywhere else (`tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py:637` → `tui_gateway/server.py:1399-1403`), or the wait itself died (`server_requests.py:158-166`). |
| `shutdown` | The host process is exiting (`server.py:1403`, `sid=None`). |
| `session_closed` | An approval woken with no choice: the session was torn down or the turn ended (`approval_gateway_wait.py:182-192`). |
| `resolved` | An approval answered on another surface (`approval_gateway_wait.py:182-192`). |

**Answered elsewhere is already silent for other requests.** A clarify, sudo, secret or vault prompt answered from another client settles through `resolve_response` with no `request.cancel` at all (`server_requests.py:201-236`). The next snapshot's `open_requests` drops it. So `resolved` is the only answered-elsewhere signal, and only approvals send it.

**#700:** no change to `Networking/Hermes/*`. #700 must keep delivering sequenced `request.cancel` events with their `payload` to `BotConversation.observe`.

## Plan

- [ ] **Model.** Add `BotRequestWithdrawal` (in `BotPendingRequest.swift`), holding the withdrawn request's family and a reason.
  - Family: approval, question, or other.
  - Reason: `timeout`, `stopped` (`interrupted` or `session_closed`), `shutdown`, or `other` (any other non-empty text).
  - It has a localized `message` (Decision 2).
- [ ] **State.** In `applyRequestCancel`, before removing the envelope, set `BotConversation.withdrawnRequest` only when all of these hold:
  - the cancelled envelope's `pending` is the request on screen (`pendingRequest?.requestID`), so a request queued behind it or never seen stays silent;
  - the reason isn't `resolved`;
  - it isn't a renderer task (`tour`, `terminal.read`, `window.read`, `preview.read`, `preview.act`). Their cards already say the bot carries on without them (`BotPendingRequest.swift:323-327`);
  - for `interrupted`, this phone has no Stop in flight (`uncertainStop || stopAcknowledged`). The user who tapped Stop already knows.
- [ ] **Clear** `withdrawnRequest`:
  - when the host accepts the next prompt (after `emit(.sent)`, `:970`);
  - when a new request arrives (the server-request branch of `observe`, `:1372-1382`, and a snapshot that installs a pending approval);
  - on disconnect or generation change.

  Never write it into the history cache or the recent transcript.
- [ ] **View.** In `BotChatView.swift:119-133`, when there is no `pendingRequest`, draw the note in the card's slot, where the work stopped.
  - Style: one centered caption line in secondary color with a small symbol (`clock` for a timeout, `stop.circle` otherwise). This matches the room system line style (`BotRoomView.swift:300-301`).
  - No transition. VoiceOver announces it once when it appears.
- [ ] Add the strings to `Localizable.xcstrings` for all shipped languages.
- [ ] Update `docs/agents/bots.md:337-339` (the `request.cancel` paragraph): which reasons show a note, and that `resolved` and this phone's own Stop don't.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** A short note when a card is withdrawn because it timed out or the run stopped; stay silent when it was answered elsewhere.

1. **Where the note shows.** Recommend the card's own slot in the transcript, kept until the next accepted send or the next request. It explains the bot's next words, and it is still there when the user comes back to the phone. Alternative: the composer's error pill, which auto-dismisses after 5 seconds (`BotChatComposerView.swift:87-92`). Anyone not looking at that moment would miss it.
2. **Copy.** Recommend full sentences per family, never glued fragments, so every language can translate them whole:

   | Reason | Approval | Question | Other (sudo, secret, password manager) |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `timeout` | "Approval timed out, so it didn't run." | "Question timed out. The bot carried on without an answer." | "Request timed out. The bot carried on without it." |
   | `interrupted`, `session_closed` | "Approval withdrawn because the work stopped." | "Question withdrawn because the work stopped." | "Request withdrawn because the work stopped." |
   | `shutdown` | "Approval withdrawn because Hermes shut down." | "Question withdrawn because Hermes shut down." | "Request withdrawn because Hermes shut down." |
   | other text | "Approval withdrawn." | "Question withdrawn." | "Request withdrawn." |
   | `resolved` | none | none | none |

   Alternative: one line for every reason ("This request was withdrawn."). That is simpler, but it hides the one fact that matters for an approval: nothing ran.
3. **Unknown reasons.** Recommend the generic "… withdrawn." line: the card vanished, and saying so is better than silence. Alternative: stay silent. That is quieter, but it is the confusion this issue fixes.
4. **This phone's own Stop.** Recommend no note. Alternative: always note `interrupted`. It is accurate, but it tells the user what they just did.

## Acceptance

- An approval left unanswered until the host's timeout disappears and leaves "Approval timed out, so it didn't run." where the card was.
- An approval answered in Desktop disappears with no note.
- Stopping the bot from Desktop while a question is open leaves "Question withdrawn because the work stopped." Stopping it from this phone leaves no note.
- A withdrawn request that wasn't on screen, and a renderer task (`preview.read` and the like) timing out, leave no note.
- The note goes away when the next message is accepted or a new request arrives. It never appears under another server or bot.

## Tests

In `BotPendingRequestTests`, using the existing `request.cancel` fixture (`testModernCancelMatchesEnvelopeIDAndMethodAndRejectsCapturedAnswer`, `:843-857`). Each fails today because `reason` is ignored:
- `testATimedOutApprovalLeavesANote`.
- `testAnApprovalResolvedElsewhereLeavesNoNote`.
- `testAStopFromThisPhoneWithdrawsWithoutANote` and `testAStopFromElsewhereLeavesANote`.
- `testACancelForARequestNotOnScreenLeavesNoNote`.
- `testRendererTasksTimeOutSilently`.
- `testUnknownReasonShowsTheGenericNote`.
- `testTheNoteClearsOnTheNextAcceptedSendAndOnANewRequest`.
- One table test of `BotRequestWithdrawal.message` for every family and reason.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests`

## Mocks

Not required: one caption line in the existing system-line style. The PR shows before and after screenshots of a timed-out approval, in light and dark.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. In Bot Chat on the test bot, ask: "Run `rm -rf /tmp/hermex-withdraw-test` in the terminal." Don't answer the approval. Wait 5 minutes (the default `approvals.timeout`). Expected: the card goes and "Approval timed out, so it didn't run." takes its place. The bot's next message says the command was blocked.
2. Send any message. Expected: the note disappears.
3. Ask for the same command again and answer it in Desktop. Expected: the card goes with no note.
4. Ask the bot to ask you a question (clarify), then press Stop in Desktop. Expected: "Question withdrawn because the work stopped."
5. Repeat step 4 but press Stop on the phone. Expected: no note.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** Bot Chat only.
  - The inbox and the Live Activity already follow the snapshot back to working or idle.
  - An approval or question push banner that is already delivered stays in Notification Center after the withdrawal. The plugin has no withdrawal hook (`hermex-push` `2f1388c`, `plugin/hermex_push/hooks.py:333-358`), so it is out of scope.
  - Group rooms get their pending actions from `groups.state`, not `request.cancel`, so they are unaffected.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** the note lives on the per-server, per-connection, per-Profile conversation and is cleared on disconnect. It is never cached.
- **Contracts:** reads `reason` from an event already received. Unknown values fall back to the generic line.
- **Reverse states:** the note is informational and clears itself. Nothing to undo.
- **Connection modes:** a `request.cancel` lost in a sequence gap already drops the card without a note (`BotConversation.swift:1393-1403`). Silence on uncertainty is correct.
- **Native quality:** a VoiceOver announcement, Dynamic Type wrapping, light and dark, no animation, all shipped languages.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Outside reach

None.

Research: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), pinned hermes-agent ca678285 and hermes-webui c67fd2dd.

title: perf(push): skip relay storage writes for unchanged registrations
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Every launch of Hermex rewrites the phone's relay registration for every paired server, even when nothing changed. Each rewrite is a paid KV put plus a KV delete.

- `PushAppDelegate` calls `refreshOnLaunch` on every process launch (`HermesMobile/Push/PushAppDelegate.swift:14`, `HermesMobile/Push/PushRegistrar.swift:235-239`).
- The token callback then re-registers every pairing (`PushRegistrar.swift:243-262`) with an unconditional `registerDevice` (`:281`). The only check (`:293-298`) guards the local Keychain save, not the relay call.
- On the relay, each registration writes a new immutable KV revision, points the registry at it, then deletes the previous revision (`hermex-push/relay/src/coordinator.ts:117-128`, hermex-push `2f1388c`). It never checks whether the record is identical.

The launch refresh has a purpose: the relay revokes a device on its own when APNs reports the token invalid (`coordinator.ts:195`), and re-registering recovers from that. That must keep working. This is cost hygiene on Workers Paid.

## Contract

Code lands in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, in `relay/` only. There is no app, plugin or host change.

`POST /installs/{key}/devices` keeps its request and response. An unchanged registration still answers `200 {"result":"ok"}`, which is all the app checks (`HermesMobile/Push/PushRelayClient.swift:98`). Only the storage behind it changes.

Order: the hermex-push PR merges, then the maintainer deploys the relay. Agents never deploy. There is no Hermex PR. This issue closes once the relay is deployed.

## Plan

In `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push` (suggested title `perf(relay): skip KV writes for unchanged device registrations`):

- [ ] `relay/src/coordinator.ts:117-128` (`register`):
  - Compute `digest = sha256(<canonical JSON of command.device>)`, using the existing `sha256` (`relay/src/contract.ts:54-57`). The input is the parsed device after the lease cap in `relay/src/index.ts:46`.
  - If `registry[token]` exists and the Durable Object row `digest:<token>` equals `digest`, return `ok()` with no KV or storage write.
  - Otherwise do what the code does today, but write the digest in the same `storage.put({ devices: registry, ['digest:' + token]: digest })` as the pointer. That keeps the pointer and digest atomic.
- [ ] `coordinator.ts:76-84` (`removeDevice`): delete `digest:<token>` along with the device's activity rows, so after a DELETE or an APNs invalid-token revocation the next registration writes again.
- [ ] Canonical JSON: sort keys before hashing, so the digest doesn't depend on zod's output key order.
- [ ] `relay/README.md:23, 42`: one sentence each. The coordinator keeps a digest beside each device pointer. Registering an identical record again writes nothing.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** The relay skips KV writes when a registration is unchanged (cost hygiene on Workers Paid). The app's launch refresh stays, because it recovers from revocation.

1. **Where the digest lives: a separate `digest:<token>` row in the Durable Object.** It is written in one call with the registry pointer and deleted with the device. The existing `event:`, `activity:` and `due:` rows and the legacy index pass (`coordinator.ts:335-358`) don't touch it. Alternative: encode the digest into the KV revision name (`…:<digest>.<uuid>`). That needs no new row, but the pointer string then carries meaning and has to be parsed.
2. **What goes into the digest: the whole parsed device.** That is `device_token`, `bundle_id`, `environment` and every `prefs` field. So a new token, an environment change (sandbox or production) or any preference change writes as today. Alternative: hash only `prefs` and `environment`. The token is already the registry key, but hashing everything costs nothing and misses nothing.
3. **Unchanged answers the same `200 ok`.** The app reads only the status. Alternative: a new `unchanged` result. Nothing reads it, and tests can check storage directly.
4. **No KV read to confirm the record still exists.** The KV record is written before the pointer and removed after it. A pointer without a record only happens after a manual KV edit. Alternative: a KV `get` on the unchanged path, which heals that case. It is cheaper than a write, but it is still a paid read on every launch.
5. **Registrations from before this change have no digest,** so each writes once on its next registration and is skipped after that. No migration is needed.
6. **Out of scope: activity re-registration at launch.** `activities.refresh(republish: true)` (`PushRegistrar.swift:299`) re-PUTs each live activity. That writes Durable Object rows (`coordinator.ts:132-147`), not KV. It is small, and a separate concern.

## Acceptance

- Registering the same device with the same body again makes no KV put and no KV delete. The registry keeps pointing at the same revision.
- Changing any preference, the environment or the device token writes one new revision and deletes the old one, as today.
- After `DELETE /devices/{token}`, or after APNs reports the token invalid, the next registration writes again and the device receives banners.
- Notifications and activity updates reach a device whose last registration was skipped.

## Tests

- `relay/test/worker.test.ts`:
  - A new test registers the same device twice. With `vi.spyOn(bindings.hermex_relay, 'put')` and `'delete'`, it checks one put and no delete, and that the KV key name is unchanged. Then it notifies and checks that the banner is sent. This fails today, because the second registration writes a new revision and deletes the first.
  - A new test covers a preference change (new revision), an environment change (new revision), and a DELETE or invalid-token revocation followed by an identical registration (writes again).
  - The existing `registers under only the install hash, updates preferences, and revokes immediately` (`:29-44`) still passes unchanged.
- Run: `cd relay && npm run check`.

## Mocks

Not required: no UI.

## Manual test

Covered by tests; no manual check is needed. The change is storage bookkeeping behind an unchanged HTTP contract, and the worker tests use the real Workers runtime with local KV and Durable Objects. After the deploy, the maintainer can optionally watch the KV write count in the Cloudflare dashboard while relaunching Hermex a few times.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the launch refresh, the token rotation path (`PushRegistrar.swift:256`), Enable (`:117-137`) and preference saves (`:181-231`). All still reach the relay. Only unchanged records skip the write.
- **Targets:** none in Hermex.
- **Servers:** digests live in each install's own Durable Object. Two servers are two installs.
- **Contracts:** the request and response are unchanged.
- **Reverse states:** revocation and DELETE clear the digest, so the recovery path still writes.
- **Connection modes:** unaffected.
- **Native quality:** no UI.
- **Docs:** `hermex-push/relay/README.md`.

## Outside reach

The maintainer deploys the relay.
