title: feat(chat): recall your last message with ↑ and preview staged documents
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Two small composer gaps. Each is its own slice and can land in the same PR as separate commits. #872 (epic #855) also edits the composer and runs first. This issue doesn't repeat its Send/Stop morph, autocomplete haptics or landscape cap. Rebase on it before starting.

**(a) No way to bring back what you just sent.** On a hardware keyboard, the only composer shortcut is ⌘↩ to send:
- It's `ComposerChipTextView.keyCommands` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ComposerChipTextView.swift:545-553`), gated in `canPerformAction` (`:555-558`).
- Bot Chat's Send button has the same shortcut (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatComposerView.swift:470`).
- Nothing handles the arrow keys anywhere in the app.

To fix a typo in the last message, or send it again, the user has to retype it or copy it out of the bubble.

**(b) Staged documents are anonymous.** An image gets a thumbnail, but a staged PDF or document gets a colored icon, its extension, its name and its size (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerAttachmentStripView.swift:135-141`, `:167-210`). The collapsed pill shows a plain `doc` symbol (`:72-90`). Two staged PDFs look the same.
- Every staged attachment already has a local copy on disk. `ChatDraftAttachmentStore` writes `<uuid>-<original name>` under Application Support (`HermesMobile/Persistence/ChatDraftAttachmentStore.swift:66-84`), and `PendingAttachment.draftFileName` names it (`HermesMobile/Models/UploadResponse.swift:21-24`).
- Sessions sets `draftFileName` when staging (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatAttachmentCoordinator.swift:67-74`, `:191-200`), and Bot Chat does too (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotAttachmentDraft.swift:38-39`, `:70-71`).
- The store only resolves a name to a URL privately (`ChatDraftAttachmentStore.swift:138-147`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

**(a) Recall with ↑**
- [ ] New pure rule `ComposerRecall.lastSentText(in: [ChatMessage]) -> String?`. It scans from the newest message and returns the first user message you wrote, as text:
  - Skip any row that isn't `role == "user"`.
  - Skip Bot system deliveries: `displayKind` set, and not a steer (`HermesMobile/Models/ChatMessage.swift:19-23`, `:129-132`).
  - Unwrap steers with `strippedSteerText` (`:145-160`).
  - Strip the `[Attached files: …]` marker with `MessageAttachment.contentWithoutAttachedFilesMarker` (`HermesMobile/Models/MessageAttachment.swift:123-136`).
  - Skip a message that is empty after that (an attachment-only send).
- [ ] `ComposerChipTextView`:
  - Add `var recallLastSentText: (() -> String?)?`.
  - In `keyCommands` (`:545-553`), add a `UIKeyCommand` for `UIKeyCommand.inputUpArrow` with no modifiers. Set `wantsPriorityOverSystemBehavior = true`, because arrow keys go to text editing first otherwise. Title it "Recall Last Message".
  - In `canPerformAction` (`:555`), allow it only when the editor is empty, there are no quotes, and the closure returns text. Otherwise ↑ keeps moving the caret.
  - The action calls `insertText(_:)`. That goes through the normal edit path: the coordinator's `textViewDidChange` updates the draft binding and draws chips (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:519`), the caret ends up at the end, and ⌘Z undoes the recall.
- [ ] `ComposerTextInputView` / `ComposerTextView` (`ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:5-45`, `:173-260`): pass the closure through, in both `makeUIView` and `updateUIView`, next to `onKeyboardSend` (`:224-225`, `:256-257`). It defaults to nil.
- [ ] Sessions:
  - `ChatViewModel` gets `var lastSentText: String? { ComposerRecall.lastSentText(in: messages) }` (`messages` at `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:203`).
  - `ChatView` passes `{ viewModel.lastSentText }` into `MessageComposerView` (built at `ChatView.swift:420`), and the composer passes it on at `ChatComposerView.swift:735-760`.
  - It's a closure, so the scan runs only when ↑ is pressed, not on every render while a stream updates `messages`.
- [ ] Bot Chat: `BotChatComposerView` (`:304-321`) passes `{ ComposerRecall.lastSentText(in: model.messages) }` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:64`). Bot user rows already hide the client's mention note (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotActivity.swift:198-203`).
- [ ] Bot rooms (`BotRoomComposerView.swift:32-40`) pass nothing (Decision 1).

**(b) Document thumbnails**
- [ ] `ChatDraftAttachmentStoring` (`ChatDraftAttachmentStore.swift:8-18`): add `func fileURL(named:) async throws -> URL`, backed by the existing private resolver (`:138-147`), so it keeps rejecting `..` and path separators. Update the test doubles that conform to it.
- [ ] New `ComposerDocumentThumbnails` in `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/`. It's a `@MainActor` cache keyed by `PendingAttachment.id`. The id is stable across a draft restore (`ChatAttachmentCoordinator.swift:100-106`).
  - `thumbnail(for:size:scale:) async -> UIImage?` resolves the draft copy through the store, then runs `QLThumbnailGenerator.shared.generateBestRepresentation(for:)` with `representationTypes: .thumbnail`. `.thumbnail` gives the first page, or a text excerpt for text files. `.icon` would give back today's generic icon.
  - It skips images (they have `thumbnailData`) and attachments without a `draftFileName`.
  - It caches failures as nil, so a document Quick Look can't draw isn't retried on every render.
  - It cancels the request on task cancellation (`QLThumbnailGenerator.shared.cancel(_:)`).
  - Keep a small count limit, for example 32. Inject the store and the generator so tests can use doubles.
  - Create it on the main app's side, not per view.
- [ ] `ComposerAttachmentThumbnailView.filePreview` (`ChatComposerAttachmentStripView.swift:167-210`):
  - Load with `.task(id: attachment.id)`.
  - When an image arrives, draw it in the badge's existing 58×68 pt slot (`:169-182`), `scaledToFill`, clipped to the same 10 pt corner, with the existing 0.25-opacity separator stroke so a white page reads in dark mode. Name and size stay.
  - Until then, and when it fails, draw today's badge.
  - Swap without animation.
- [ ] `ComposerAttachmentPillPreview.tile` (`:71-90`): use the same cached image for documents in the 30 pt tile.
- [ ] VoiceOver labels don't change (`:107`, `:209`).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** (a) With a hardware keyboard, ↑ in an empty composer recalls your last sent message in that chat. (b) Staged PDFs and documents show a real preview instead of an icon.

1. **Where ↑ works.** Recommend: in Sessions and Bot Chat, which share the editor and whose transcripts are `[ChatMessage]`. Not in Bot rooms: a room transcript mixes many authors and isn't `ChatMessage` rows, so "your last message" needs its own rule. Alternative: include rooms with a room-specific rule.
2. **Where the recalled text comes from.** Recommend: the chat's own transcript (Plan (a)). It survives leaving and reopening the chat and an app restart, and it is per chat and per server by construction. Alternative: remember the last draft at send time in memory. That's simpler, but it's lost when the chat closes.
3. **How chips come back.** Recommend: rely on the existing text-to-chip drawing, with no new code.
   - The composer draws skill, `@file` and Bot mention chips from the draft's own text (`ComposerChipTextView.swift:80-103`), and Sessions already confirms `@path` references found in the transcript's user messages (`ChatViewModel.swift:3373-3408`). So a recalled `/skill` or `@file` redraws as a chip wherever it did in the bubble.
   - Quotes come back as their `> ` Markdown text, not as quote chips (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ComposerQuote.swift:42-50`).
   - Attachments aren't re-staged.
   - Alternative: parse `> ` blocks back into quote chips. That's fragile, because a quote the user typed looks exactly the same.
4. **↓ and walking further back.** Recommend: no. It's one step: ↑ only fills an empty composer, and after that ↑ and ↓ move the caret as usual. ⌘Z undoes the recall. Alternative: shell-style history with ↑/↓. That needs a history index and "was it edited?" state, and it fights caret movement in multi-line drafts.
5. **Thumbnail placement.** Recommend: the badge's slot and the 30 pt pill tile, as in the Plan, so the tile's size and text don't change. Alternative: a full 96 pt card like staged images (`:161-163`). That's a layout change that would need mocks first.
6. **Failures.** Recommend: keep the icon badge silently. A thumbnail is decoration, and the file still sends. Alternative: a "no preview" mark, which is noise.

## Acceptance

- (a) With a hardware keyboard, in a Sessions chat with an empty composer, ↑ fills the composer with your last sent message and puts the caret at the end. Skill and file chips draw as they did in the bubble, and ⌘Z clears it.
  - With text in the composer, ↑ moves the caret.
  - In a chat you haven't sent in, ↑ does nothing.
  - An attachment-only last send is skipped for the text message before it. A steer is recalled without its wrapper.
  - Bot Chat behaves the same. Bot rooms don't react.
  - The shortcut shows in the iPad ⌘ overlay.
- (b) A staged PDF shows its first page in the strip and in the collapsed pill. A staged `.md`, `.txt` or `.docx` shows a rendered excerpt. A `.zip` keeps its icon badge.
  - Removing and re-adding doesn't flicker.
  - Leaving and reopening the chat (draft restore) shows the thumbnail again.
  - Bot Chat staging behaves the same.

## Tests

- New `ComposerRecallTests`:
  - The newest user message wins over later assistant and tool rows.
  - The attachment marker is stripped, and an attachment-only message is skipped.
  - A steer is unwrapped.
  - A `role: "user"` row with a non-steer `displayKind` is skipped.
  - No user message returns nil.
  - `ComposerChipTextView`:
    - `keyCommands` contains an unmodified up-arrow command with `wantsPriorityOverSystemBehavior`.
    - `canPerformAction` for it is true only when the text is empty and the closure returns text.
    - Performing it sets the text and puts the selection at the end.
  - All fail today: the rule and the command don't exist.
- `ChatDraftAttachmentStoreTests`: `fileURL(named:)` returns the saved file's URL and throws for `../x`. Fails today: the method is private.
- New `ComposerDocumentThumbnailsTests`, with an injected generator and a temp-directory `ChatDraftAttachmentStore(directoryURL:)`:
  - Two requests for one id generate once.
  - Images and attachments without `draftFileName` never call the generator.
  - A failure is cached as nil and not retried.
  - Cancelling the task doesn't store a result.
- Existing: `ComposerVoiceDraftComposerTests.testComposerSendKeyboardCommandIsDiscoverableCommandReturn` still passes (⌘↩ unchanged).
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerRecallTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatDraftAttachmentStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerDocumentThumbnailsTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerVoiceDraftComposerTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerChipDocumentTests`

## Mocks

Not required. (a) has no visible UI. (b) puts the thumbnail in the badge's existing slot and pill tile, with no new layout (Decision 5 names the alternative that would need mocks).

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build), with a Bluetooth keyboard. Or an iPad with a hardware keyboard.

1. In a Sessions chat, send "check @README.md with /some-skill" (use a real file and skill). Press ↑ in the empty composer: the message comes back with both chips, and the caret is at the end.
2. Type a letter and press ↑: the caret moves, and nothing is recalled. Clear the composer, press ↑, then ⌘Z: the composer is empty again.
3. Open a chat you haven't sent in and press ↑: nothing happens.
4. In Bot Chat, send "@hermes hello". Press ↑: it comes back with the mention chip. In a Bot room, ↑ does nothing.
5. On iPad, hold ⌘: "Recall Last Message" is listed.
6. Attach a PDF: within a moment the tile shows page 1, and the collapsed pill shows it too. Attach a `.md` and a `.docx`: excerpts. Attach a `.zip`: icon badge.
7. Leave the chat and come back: the staged PDF still shows its page. Repeat with dark mode and the largest accessibility text size.
8. Share a PDF into a chat from Files through the share extension: its tile shows page 1.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:**
  - (a) Hardware keyboard in the Sessions composer and the Bot Chat composer. Bot rooms are excluded (Decision 1). New chats use the same composer (`ChatView`).
  - (b) Every path that stages a document, and all of them end in these two strips: picker, paste, drop, share-extension handoff, draft restore, and Bot Chat staging.
- **Targets:** main app only. The share extension stages through the app group and the app stages the file, so it needs no change. Widget and notification service are untouched.
- **Servers:** recall reads only the open chat's transcript. Thumbnails come from app-owned draft copies and are keyed by attachment UUID, so nothing crosses servers.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** ⌘Z undoes a recall. Removing an attachment drops its tile, and the cache entry is harmless.
- **Connection modes:** none. Recall and thumbnails are local, and work offline and on cached data.
- **Native quality:**
  - Accessibility labels don't change.
  - The thumbnail swaps in without animation, which satisfies Reduce Motion.
  - The accessibility text layout keeps its wider tile (`:197-202`).
  - Dark mode keeps the border.
  - One new string, "Recall Last Message", goes into `Localizable.xcstrings` for every shipped language (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).
- **Performance:** the recall scan runs only on the key press. Thumbnails are generated off the main thread at tile size, once per id.
- **Docs:** none.

## Outside reach

None.

title: feat(bots): show who's in a new group chat
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

A new group chat opens on a blank screen that says "No messages yet." (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:59-61`). The user just picked two to six bots, and the first thing they see doesn't show who they picked or invite them to start. The member faces only appear as three overlapping 30 pt avatars in the title pill (`:123-131`, `BotRoomAvatars` at `:320-336`, capped at `prefix(3)`).

Everything needed is already loaded:
- `reader.room.members` has each member's id, Profile, handle and display name (`BotGroupRoom.swift:26-37`).
- `BotRoomMemberAvatar` draws a still face from the connection's roster (`BotRoomView.swift:338-351`).

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

For the copy: at the pin (hermes-agent `ca678285`), a room message with no `@mention` goes to every member ("no mention meaning everyone", `gateway/hosted_room_discussion.py:302-318`, `:638-645`). So "Say something to the group" is accurate.

**#700:** no networking change.

## Plan

- [ ] **Condition.** Add a static `BotRoomEvent.hasConversation(in:)` in `BotGroupRoom.swift`. It is true once any `message.user` or `message.member` event is loaded.
  - The welcome shows when `reader.link == .live`, `!reader.hasEarlier` and `!BotRoomEvent.hasConversation(in: reader.events)`.
  - This replaces today's `reader.events.isEmpty` gate (`BotRoomView.swift:59`). A room renamed before its first message still counts as new, and an older room whose loaded window happens to hold only system rows doesn't (see Decision 1).
- [ ] **View.** Add `BotRoomWelcomeView(room:roster:avatars:showsPrompt:)` in `BotRoomView.swift` and draw it in place of the `Text("No messages yet.")`.
  - Every member (a room has two to six, frozen at creation, `docs/agents/bots.md:1337-1339`) gets a `BotRoomMemberAvatar` (still, 44 pt) with `member.name` underneath, one line, middle-truncated.
  - Members sit in a centered wrapping row.
  - Below them, "Say something to the group" in secondary style.
  - No animation and no transition. `BotRoomMemberAvatar` already draws with `motion: .still` (`:346`, `:348`).
- [ ] **Foreign authority.** Pass `showsPrompt: reader.showsComposer` (`BotRoomReader.swift:195`). A room managed by another Hermes hides the composer, so it shows the members without the prompt.
- [ ] **Accessibility.** Combine into one element: "Group members: Ada, Linus and Grace. Say something to the group." Use the list formatter for the names. At accessibility text sizes, stack members vertically.
- [ ] Add strings to `Localizable.xcstrings` for all shipped languages. Remove the "No messages yet." key; `BotRoomView.swift:60` is its only use.
- [ ] Update the room transcript paragraph in `docs/agents/bots.md` (`:1285-1291`).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Before the first message, show the members' faces and names with "Say something to the group" instead of "No messages yet." Static (no animation). Mocks first.

1. **What "before the first message" means.** Recommend "no user or member message loaded, and no earlier history to load". Alternative: keep today's `events.isEmpty` gate. It is simpler, but a rename before anyone speaks would hide the welcome.
2. **A mention hint.** Recommend no hint. The decided line is enough, and the composer's `@` panel already lists members (`docs/agents/bots.md:1304-1305`). Alternative: a second caption, "Mention @name to ask just one bot." It is accurate at the pin, but it is extra copy on a screen meant to be calm.
3. **Tapping a face.** Recommend no tap action. The room profile (the title pill) already links each member to its bot profile (`BotRoomProfileView.swift:37-45`). Alternative: link each face to that bot's profile. It is handy, but it adds a second way in to maintain.

## Acceptance

- Creating a group chat with three bots opens on their three faces and names and "Say something to the group", with no "No messages yet.".
- The welcome disappears when the first message (the user's or a bot's) arrives, and doesn't come back on reopen.
- A six-member room shows all six. Long names truncate without overlapping.
- A room managed by another Hermes shows the members without the prompt line.
- Nothing on the welcome animates, with or without Reduce Motion.

## Tests

- `BotRoomTests`: `testARoomIsNewUntilItsFirstUserOrMemberMessage`. It checks system-only events such as `room.renamed`, the first `message.user`, and the `hasEarlier` case. This fails today because the helper doesn't exist.
- `BotChatPresentationTests`: `testANewRoomShowsItsMembersUntilTheFirstMessage` (hosted, like `testRoomShowsMemberMessagesAndTextOnlyComposer`, `:168-187`). A live room with an empty log shows every member name and "Say something to the group", and not "No messages yet.". After a `message.member` event, the welcome is gone.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`

## Mocks

Required first:
- a new room with two members, with six members, and with long display names;
- a foreign-authority room (no prompt line);
- light and dark, and the largest accessibility text size (stacked).

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the run's single Branch TestFlight build).

1. Bots inbox → + → New Group Chat. Pick three bots, name it, and create it. Expected: the room opens on the three faces and names and "Say something to the group".
2. Send "hello everyone". Expected: the welcome is replaced by your message, and each bot replies.
3. Leave and reopen the room. Expected: the transcript shows, not the welcome.
4. With VoiceOver on, open a new room. Expected: one element reads the member names, then the prompt.
5. Disband the test room from its profile when done.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the room screen, opened from the inbox, from New Group Chat, or from a room search result. The inbox row and room profile are unchanged. No deep link, intent, share or Live Activity entry exists for rooms (`docs/agents/bots.md:938`, `:1332-1333`).
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** reads only the open room's members and that connection's roster, so no cross-server data.
- **Contracts:** none.
- **Reverse states:** the welcome leaves on the first message and never needs a way back.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver (one combined element), Dynamic Type (stacks at accessibility sizes), light and dark, Reduce Motion (nothing moves anyway), all shipped languages.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Outside reach

None.

title: docs: correct stale release notes about push signing and CI
body:
Part of #877 · **Priority:** P3 · **Blocked by:** nothing

## Problem

Two release notes describe a setup that no longer exists. An agent who trusts them will look for files and checks that aren't there.

**1. The push environment comment** (`HermesMobile/Push/PushEnvironment.swift:3-13`) makes two wrong claims:
- It says `APS_ENVIRONMENT` lives in `Config/Shared.xcconfig`. It doesn't: `Shared.xcconfig` never mentions it. It is a project-level build setting in `HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`: `development` for Debug (`:2800`) and `production` for Release (`:2868`). Those are the `PBXProject` configurations (`:3219-3223`). The two files the comment names do use it: `HermesMobile/Resources/HermesMobile.entitlements:5-6` and `HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist:36-37`.
- It says a mismatched provisioning profile "is a signing-time check (see the PR checklist)". `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` has no such item, and git history shows it never had one. The comment arrived in #582 (`a2d27584`) without a template change.

What is actually true:
- Both upload paths archive **Release**: `.github/workflows/release-candidate-testflight.yml:162` and `scripts/branch-testflight:46`.
- Both export with `method` `app-store-connect` and `destination` `upload` (`ci/ReleaseCandidateExportOptions.plist`, `Config/BranchTestFlightExportOptions.plist`). The app goes straight to App Store Connect, so no IPA exists locally to inspect, and nothing checks the signed entitlement.
- The practical risk is low, because Release sets `production` on both sides.

**2. Issue #4 describes workflows that were deleted.** It asks to change `external-testflight.yml`, `internal-testflight.yml`, `ci/ExternalTestFlightExportOptions.plist` and `ci/TestFlightExportOptions.plist`, all removed in #640 (`a08b9da1`). It also lists three signed targets and three provisioning profiles. Today:
- **One upload workflow**: `release-candidate-testflight.yml`. It runs only in the `external-testflight` environment (`:33`), which is the repo's only environment now (`gh api repos/uzairansaruzi/hermex/environments`). Its export options are `ci/ReleaseCandidateExportOptions.plist` (`:40`). `pr-ci.yml` builds with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` (`:154`, `:178`), so it never signs.
- **Four signed targets.** The notification service joined the app, share extension and widget: bundle IDs `$(APP_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER)`, `.shareextension`, `.liveactivitywidget` and `.notifications` (`project.pbxproj:2940`, `:3044`, `:3100`, `:3129`).
- **Signing still mints on the runner.** The workflow signs automatically with `-allowProvisioningUpdates` and an App Store Connect API key (`:103-114`, `:166-169`, `:183-186`). The key was already there when #4 was filed (`git show bcdffe3c:.github/workflows/external-testflight.yml`, `:167-170`), so the key alone didn't prevent the cap then. The latest successful run's archive log shows `Signing Identity: "Apple Development: Created via API (…)"` (run 35916971117), so a fresh runner still creates a certificate through the API.
- **The cap hasn't bitten since #4 was filed.** Four upload runs succeeded (29219008188, 30888612331, 34004189934, 35916971117). The two failures were a closed release train (30883811600) and an authentication error (35892153089). Whether the certificate count grows per run is unverified.

`TESTFLIGHT.md:46-47` has the same stale fact: it lists three targets for automatic signing.

## Contract

Client-only: no host contract.

## Plan

- [ ] `HermesMobile/Push/PushEnvironment.swift:3-13`: rewrite the doc comment to say only what's true. Suggested wording (keep every fact, adjust the phrasing):
  ```swift
  /// … but from `APS_ENVIRONMENT`, the one build setting that writes both the
  /// `aps-environment` entitlement (`HermesMobile.entitlements`) and the
  /// `HermesAPSEnvironment` key read below (`Info.plist`). It is a project-level
  /// build setting in `HermesMobile.xcodeproj`: `development` for Debug,
  /// `production` for Release, so at build time the two always agree. Only
  /// export re-signing could make them differ, and nothing checks the uploaded
  /// app: both upload paths export straight to App Store Connect. Both archive
  /// Release (`release-candidate-testflight.yml`, `scripts/branch-testflight`).
  ```
  The first lines (`:3-8`) are accurate and stay. Change no code.
- [ ] Refresh #4's body with `gh issue edit 4 --body-file <file>`. Keep the owner's decision (manual signing with a stored distribution identity) and the non-goals. Change:
  - **Context:** name `release-candidate-testflight.yml` and `ci/ReleaseCandidateExportOptions.plist`. Add the run history and the "Created via API" evidence above.
  - **A new first step:** before changing any signing, check Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles in the Apple Developer account before and after the next release-candidate run. If the count doesn't grow, close #4 and link the evidence. If it grows, continue.
  - **Secrets:** only in the `external-testflight` environment. Add a fourth profile secret for `com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.notifications`, so six secrets in total. Suggest the profile name `Hermes Mobile Notification Service App Store`, to match the other three; the owner picks the real name.
  - **Scope steps 1-4:** one plist and one workflow, not two. Four entries in `provisioningProfiles`. Remove `-allowProvisioningUpdates` at `:166` and `:183`.
  - **Out of scope:** Branch TestFlight (`scripts/branch-testflight`). It runs on the maintainer's Mac with the signing identity already in the login keychain, and #4 is about CI runners.
- [ ] Post one short comment on #4: the body was refreshed on this date, and the 2026-07-02 checklist comment is replaced by the body's secret list. Don't edit the old comment.
- [ ] `TESTFLIGHT.md:46-47`: list all four targets (Decision 1).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** Correct the `PushEnvironment.swift` comment to say what's actually true, and refresh #4's body to the current workflows and targets. This is one comment change in code plus an issue-body edit, which the implementer makes with `gh issue edit`.

1. **Fix `TESTFLIGHT.md:46-47` in the same PR.** Recommend: yes. It's the same stale fact (three signed targets instead of four) and a one-line edit. Alternative: leave it, and the doc keeps contradicting the refreshed #4.
2. **Add a PR checklist item for the push environment.** Recommend: no. Release already sets `production`, and a checklist line nobody can verify from a PR diff is the same kind of promise this issue removes. Alternative: add "Push entitlement environment matches the build configuration" to the template.
3. **#4's old checklist comment.** Recommend: add a new comment rather than editing the 2026-07-02 one, so the history stays readable. Alternative: edit it in place with `gh api`.

## Acceptance

- `PushEnvironment.swift` names no file or check that doesn't exist. It says where `APS_ENVIRONMENT` is set and that nothing inspects the uploaded app.
- #4's body names only files, workflows, environments and targets that exist on `master`. It lists four profiles and starts with the "is the cap still real?" check.
- `TESTFLIGHT.md` lists four signed targets.

## Tests

- No new tests: no executable code changes.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests`. It confirms the file still builds and the environment tests still pass (`HermesMobileTests/PushRegistrationTests.swift:235-244`).

## Mocks

Not required: no UI.

## Manual test

Covered by the focused test run. A comment, a doc line and an issue body have no runtime behavior to check on a device.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points, servers, contracts, connection modes, reverse states, native quality:** none; no behavior changes.
- **Targets:** none change. The refreshed #4 now covers all four signed targets, including `HermesNotificationService`.
- **Docs:** `TESTFLIGHT.md` (Decision 1). `docs/agents/push.md` doesn't mention the environment setting, so it doesn't change.

## Outside reach

Everything #4 itself will need, later and outside this issue: counting certificates in the Apple Developer account, and creating secrets and profiles. This issue only edits text.

title: feat(hermes): refuse Hermes releases older than the minimum
body:
Part of #700 (slices 0.2 and 0.3) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #880 · **Unblocks:** #900

## Problem and outcome

Hermex signs in to any Hermes host, whatever release it runs. A host older than 0.21.3 publishes no gateway contract, so approvals, questions and replay behave in ways Hermex was never built for, and the user sees generic failures. The only version UI, the untested-version note, was removed in #626. Separately, when a host answers `-32601` (method not found), only the one chat that asked remembers it (`BotChatControls`), so every other chat on the same connection asks again.

After this, Hermex reads the host's release from the public `/api/status` before any password goes out and refuses a host older than the declared minimum with "update Hermes" advice. For the life of the connection it also remembers which gateway methods the host doesn't have, so a control that can't work stays off everywhere.

## Contract

Evidence is pinned to Hermex `699074e7` and hermes-agent `ca678285` (0.21.5, `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`). Recheck against the execution base.

- `/api/status` is public and reports `version` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:499`). Hermex already reads it before the auth gate (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:96`).
- `__version__` is a plain `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` string (`hermes_cli/__init__.py:6`). Canary builds carry a suffix (tag `v0.21.4+canary.20260928T071354Z`), so compare the numeric part only.
- Contract diff (`apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`) for every method `HermesCall` sends, across 0.21.3 (`v2026.9.14`), 0.21.4 (`v2026.9.21`) and the pin:
  - `client.capabilities` is absent at 0.21.3. It is already tolerated: a `-32601` reply connects as before (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:240-246`).
  - `connection.request` and `connection.respond` are both absent at 0.21.3, so that card never appears there. Nothing to disable. #830 owns their 0.21.5 shape.
  - `prompt.submit` only gained an optional `title_preview` in 0.21.4.
  - Every other method is present and unchanged.
  - 0.21.2 (`v2026.9.11`) publishes no gateway contract at all.
- `-32601` means the method is absent. A deliberately invalid-parameter probe answering `4000` means present; an ordinary `4000` is not a missing-method signal (#700 decision comment, 2026-09-26; plan §1.3).

## Plan

- [ ] **Constants.** New `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCompatibility.swift` (main app target only): `minimumVersion = "0.21.3"`, `testedVersion = "0.21.5"`, and a pure `isSupported(_ version: String?) -> Bool` that compares numeric components. A missing or unparseable version counts as supported (Decision 2). Move `BotConnection.testedHermesVersion` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:19-21`) here and update its callers.
- [ ] **Pin test.** `BotConnectionVersionTests.testPinFileMatchesRuntimeConstant` (`HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:14-22`) checks `testedVersion` against line 2 of `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`, and that `minimumVersion <= testedVersion`. `HermesAgentFixtureTests` (`:35`, `:60`) reads the moved constant.
- [ ] **Sign-in gate.** In `HermesConnection.beginSignIn` (`HermesConnection.swift:86-113`), right after the status decode and `version` read (`:90-96`), throw `BotFailure.outdated(version)` when `isSupported` is false. The install check, login, identity and ticket requests (`:97-105`, `:157-161`) never run.
- [ ] **Failure case.** Add `BotFailure.outdated(String)` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:39-64`) with the copy in the table below.
  - It is permanent: add it to the permanent list in `BotInbox.isRetryable` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:379`). `BotConversation.disconnected` already treats unknown `BotFailure`s as permanent (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:1496-1500`).
  - Push setup's `HermexPushProvisioner.message(for:)` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift:327`) returns its description instead of the generic "This step did not finish".
- [ ] **Missing methods, per connection.**
  - `HermesConnection` keeps `private(set) var unavailableMethods: Set<String>`.
  - `HermesGateway.consume` (`HermesGateway.swift:318-332`) records the method of any reply whose error code is `-32601`. Store the method name on `Pending` (`:59-65`), the field #889 also adds.
  - The handshake's own `client.capabilities` call is exempt (#775).
  - The set lives as long as the connection: a retired or new connection starts empty.
- [ ] **Chat controls.** `BotChatControls` reads the connection's set instead of keeping its own (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatControls.swift:40`, `:63-65`, `:126`, `:142`, `:227`, `:244-245`), so a second chat never re-sends a call the host already refused. Keep its `403` and `.unsupported` handling as it is.
- [ ] **Copy.** One string in `HermesMobile/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`, all 17 shipped languages, `needs_review` (`docs/agents/i18n.md`). Interpolate both versions; don't hard-code the minimum.
- [ ] **Docs.**
  - `docs/agents/bots.md:107-116` (version pin) gains the minimum, the gate and the probe rule from Decision 4.
  - Fix `README.md:110`, which still describes the "Untested Hermes version" note that #626 removed.

| Failure | Message |
|---|---|
| `.outdated(v)` | This Hermes host runs %1$@. Hermex needs Hermes %2$@ or later. Update Hermes on the host, then try again. |

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- The minimum release is 0.21.3.
- A method the host doesn't have turns its control off for the connection's lifetime.
- The deliberate invalid-parameter probe waits for its first consumer.

1. **Where the gate runs.** Recommend at sign-in only, after the public status read and before the password. Every Bot screen and push setup signs in through `HermesConnection`, so one check covers every entry point. The form's Status section keeps showing the live version as it does today (#752 owns it). Alternative: also badge the status row, which changes #752's probe.
2. **Missing or unreadable version.** Recommend proceeding. The pin always reports it (`status.py:499`), so a missing value means a proxy or a fork, and blocking would lock those users out on a guess. Alternative: refuse.
3. **Copy placement.** Recommend the existing error rows (form, inbox, chat pill, room pill, push setup), as #880 does. No new screen or "Update Hermes" button, since Hermex can't update the host. Alternative: a dedicated state view, which needs mocks.
4. **No probe yet.** The invalid-parameter probe (`{"__hermex_probe": true}`: `4000` present, `-32601` absent) is not built here, because nothing needs to know about a method before calling it. Record the rule in `docs/agents/bots.md` so the first consumer (#701 onward) uses it.
5. **Connection card.** No work: 0.21.3 never sends `connection.request`.
6. **#713 decision 5 is met as copy, not a screen.** #713 asks for an "Update your Hermes" state. Here it is the `.outdated` message in the existing error rows (Decision 3), with no separate view.
7. **Keep 0.21.4 working when #830 lands.** `connection.respond` takes `session_id` at 0.21.4 and `owner` at 0.21.5, and unknown keys are refused with 4000 (`tui_gateway/contracts/registry.py:95-107`). #830 must send the shape the host's release expects.
8. **The maintainer's host is safe.** Its public `/api/status` reported 0.21.5 on 2026-09-28, so the 0.21.3 gate won't lock it out. Approvals do arrive at 0.21.3: the capability gate first shipped in 0.21.4.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A host reporting 0.21.2 fails sign-in with the `.outdated` copy in the form, inbox, chat and push setup. The only request sent is `GET /api/status`.
- [ ] 0.21.3, 0.21.5, `0.21.4+canary.20260928T071354Z`, a missing version and an unparseable one all proceed to login.
- [ ] A `-32601` reply to `session.cwd.set` in one chat leaves the workspace control off in a second chat on the same connection, which doesn't send the call. A new connection (another server, or new credentials) starts with the control on.
- [ ] No warning for a release between the minimum and the tested one, or newer than the tested one (#626).

## Tests

These fail on today's code unless noted.

- `HermesConnectionTests`, using `HermesHostFixture` (`HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests.swift:339`):
  - a 0.21.2 status stops before `/auth/password-login`
  - the version table above
  - the missing-method set is shared with a second consumer and empty on a new connection
- `BotConnectionVersionTests`: pin and constant consistency including `minimumVersion <= testedVersion` (existing test, extended); the `isSupported` table.
- `BotConnectionAdviceTests` (`BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:397`): one row for `.outdated`.
- `BotChatControlsTests`: the connection-wide set.
- `BotInboxTests`: `.outdated` shows its message and builds one wire.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionAdviceTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatControlsTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesAgentFixtureTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`

## Mocks

Not required: one sentence inside existing error rows. The copy table is the review artifact.

## Manual test

Device: simulator. Refusing a real host would need an old release, so the tests cover that case.

1. Open the Bots inbox signed in over the tunnel. Expected: it connects as before; the host runs 0.21.5.
2. Open a chat and its chat controls. Expected: the model, workspace and control rows behave as before.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the connection form (inbox gear, Settings → server → Hermes connection, push section), the inbox, chats, rooms and push setup. All of them sign in through `HermesConnection`.
- **Targets:** main app only. `HermesCompatibility.swift` joins `HermesMobile` alone; `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` is still read only by tests. The share extension, Live Activity widget and notification service are unchanged.
- **Servers:** the missing-method set lives on one server's connection, and nothing is stored.
- **Deep links, App Intents:** unchanged; bot links reach the same sign-in.
- **Native quality:** one new string in 17 languages; error rows already wrap for Dynamic Type.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/bots.md`, `README.md`.

## Preservation

- #880: keep `.blocked` in the shared send path and `.browserSignIn` at the status gate. The version check sits in the same status step, after the redirect and body checks and before the install and provider checks.
- #626: no warning for any release at or above the minimum.
- #775: a `-32601` on `client.capabilities` stays nonfatal and is not recorded.
- #889: if it has landed, log the refusal as step `status` with the reported version (public) and nothing else.

## Blockers

#880 (the same status step and `BotFailure` copy), set as a GitHub dependency.

## Outside reach

None. A read-only `curl` of `/api/status` is fine.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code.

title: feat(hermes): send custom headers to the Hermes host
body:
Part of #700 (the #657 slice) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #880 · **Unblocks:** #899, #900 · Delivers #657; its PR closes both.

## Problem and outcome

A Hermes dashboard behind Cloudflare Access, or any proxy that wants its own header, can't be used from Hermex. Every Bot request reaches Access without a service token and bounces (#657). The plumbing already exists: `HermesConnection` applies an admitted `HermesHeaders` set to every request for its own origin, including the gateway upgrade, and a redirect guard keeps them off other hosts (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:47-55`, `:156-161`, `:203-213`, `:255-300`). But production passes `.none`, and there is nowhere to enter headers (`:47`, `:262`).

After this, the Hermes connection form has a Connection Headers row, and the headers are saved with the connection in the Keychain. They ride on every request to that host and nowhere else: the public status check, sign-in, identity, ticket, REST and plugin calls, uploads, downloads and the `/api/ws` upgrade.

## Contract

Evidence is pinned to Hermex `699074e7` and hermes-agent `ca678285` (0.21.5).

- **`Authorization`.** Hermes reads only the `Bearer` scheme from it. A present but invalid Bearer value gets a 401 even with a valid cookie, and any other value, such as Cloudflare's single-header JSON token, is ignored (plan §1.4; #657 comment of 2026-09-24). The #657 reporter verified this at 0.21.3 behind Access: login 200, ticket 200, `/api/ws` 101.
- **Which requests need them.** Access headers must go on every request to the origin: the public `/api/status`, sign-in, the ticket and the upgrade (#700 comment of 2026-09-28).
- **Cloudflare's token forms.** The standard service token is two headers, `CF-Access-Client-Id` and `CF-Access-Client-Secret`. Access treats a request carrying only one of them as unauthenticated.
- **A refused upgrade.** `/api/ws` refuses before accepting, as an HTTP 403 (`hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:139-151`). #880 maps that to `.upgradeRefused`.
- **The ticket.** It travels in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, set on a `URLRequest` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:79-89`) and opened with `webSocketTask(with:)` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:227`). Slice 0.2 passed on a physical iPhone over the Cloudflare tunnel (#700 comment of 2026-09-28). That answers #700's device check: iOS honors the header, so no `?ticket=` fallback is needed.

## Plan

- [ ] **Record.** `BotConnection` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:4-17`) gains `var headers: [CustomHeader]?`, decoded tolerantly so old records read as nil. It stays in the same Keychain item (`BotConnectionStore`, `:94-109`), so it carries into the server-kind child (#899) unchanged and becomes per-address in #744.
- [ ] **Production wiring.**
  - `HermesConnections.connection(for:server:)` (`HermesConnection.swift:233-240`) builds `HermesConnection(connection:headers:)` from the saved headers.
  - `HermesConnection.adopt` (`:165-171`) also requires equal headers. Saving new headers therefore retires the live connection through `BotConnectionStore.save` (`BotConnection.swift:100-104`), so no cookie, sign-in or socket keeps the old set.
  - Headers never appear in a registry key.
- [ ] **Unsaved and public probes.**
  - `BotConnectionSetup.connect` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:298-349`) signs its candidate in with the form's headers.
  - `BotHostStatusProbe.check` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:196-225`) sends the saved headers to the same origin. Today it sends `.status` bare, which Access refuses.
  - **First give the probe the redirect guard.** It uses its own `URLSession` with no redirect handling (`BotProtocol.swift:208-212`), so a redirect to another host would carry the headers, including an Access secret. Route it through `CrossOriginHeaderStripper` (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:358-410`), as sign-in does, before adding any header.
  - `DevAutoLogin` stays header-less.
- [ ] **Form.** Add a "Connection Headers" row to `BotConnectionView` (`BotConnectionView.swift:23-33`; placement chosen by the mock pick). It opens the existing `CustomHeadersEditor` (`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/CustomHeadersEditor.swift:6`), as Settings (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:562-571`), onboarding (`HermesMobile/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingConnectPage.swift:79`) and Add Server (`SettingsView.swift:2418`) already do.
  - Saving runs the list through `HermesHeaders.init` (`HermesConnection.swift:275-286`).
  - A rejection shows with its reason in the connection form, under the Connection Headers row: a reserved name (`:267-271`, or any `Sec-WebSocket-*`), a `Bearer` authorization, or a malformed header. `CustomHeadersEditor` itself stays unchanged.
- [ ] **Half pair.** When exactly one of `CF-Access-Client-Id` and `CF-Access-Client-Secret` is filled, the connection form shows a warning under the Connection Headers row, and Connect stays enabled (Decision 3).
- [ ] **Copy.**
  - #880's `.blocked` text gains a pointer to Connection Headers now that the editor exists (#880, Related issues).
  - New strings go in `Localizable.xcstrings`, all 17 languages, `needs_review`.
- [ ] **Docs.**
  - `docs/agents/bots.md:22-36` covers where the headers live and where they go.
  - `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md:129-151` says the headers belong to the Hermes connection's record, never the webui's `custom_headers::<server>`.
  - Remove the "no editor or storage yet" sentence in the `HermesHeaders` comment (`HermesConnection.swift:255-262`).

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- **Added (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** the status probe gets the redirect guard before it carries headers.
- Headers are their own child, landing before the server kind.
- They're stored inside the Hermes connection's Keychain record and edited with the existing Connection Headers editor.
- The Kanban WebSocket part moves to #704.
- The editor warns when a Cloudflare Access pair is half filled.
- The end-to-end check behind Access stays a pending manual check for Uzair.

1. **One editor.** Recommend reusing `CustomHeadersEditor` unchanged, so Hermex has a single header editor. Alternative: dedicated Access "Client ID / Secret" fields, which are friendlier for Access but add a second model. #900's Cloudflare connection mode can prefill the two header names instead.
2. **Header changes keep the UUID.** Recommend treating new headers as a proxy change, not a new account: drafts, cache and push pairing stay, and only the live connection is retired. Alternative: a new connection, which discards data over a proxy tweak.
3. **Half pair: warn, don't drop.** Recommend a warning in the connection form, under the Connection Headers row ("Cloudflare Access needs both CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret."), then sending what the user saved. Silently dropping one would be a hidden rule, and refusing to save would block users halfway through setup. Alternative: send neither.
4. **The status probe carries headers.** Recommend yes. Behind Access, an unauthenticated probe otherwise always reads `.blocked`. It still sends no cookies or credentials (`BotProtocol.swift:193-206`).
5. **Webui headers stay separate.** Never copy the webui server's `custom_headers::<server>` or fall back to them, and never read `CustomHeaderStore.shared` (`HermesMobile/Networking/CustomHeader.swift:137-153`). The webui and Hermes origins differ (#824).

## Acceptance

- [ ] With headers saved, requests captured through URLProtocol carry them on all of these:
  - `/api/status`, for both sign-in and the status probe
  - `/auth/password-login`, `/api/auth/me` and `/api/auth/ws-ticket`
  - one REST call (Profile delete)
  - image upload and artifact download
  - push pairing and plugin install
  - the `/api/ws` upgrade request
- [ ] A redirect to another host carries none of them (`CrossOriginHeaderStripper`, `HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift:358-410`), including a redirect of the status probe. `PushRelayClient` requests carry none (`HermesMobile/Push/PushRelayClient.swift:31-36`).
- [ ] Saving changed headers retires the live connection once, and the next request signs in with the new set. Saving unchanged headers keeps it.
- [ ] `Authorization: Bearer …` and any reserved name can't be saved, and the editor says why.
- [ ] Records saved before this change load and connect as today.

## Tests

- `HermesConnectionTests` and `CustomHeaderInjectionTests`:
  - The production factory passes saved headers (fails today).
  - `adopt` compares headers (fails today).
  - Each request listed above carries them; redirects and the relay don't.
- `BotConnectionSetupTests` (`HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:32`): the candidate uses the form's headers (fails today); the rejection copy.
- `BotHostStatusTests` (`BotConnectionVersionTests.swift:434`): the probe carries headers (fails today), and a probe redirected to another host carries none (fails today).
- `BotConnectionVersionTests` or `BotDraftTests`: a record without `headers` decodes; a record with them round-trips.
- `LocalizationCatalogTests`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/CustomHeaderInjectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionSetupTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotHostStatusTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotAttachmentSendingTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`

## Mocks

Required: the form gains a row and a warning. Build static mocks of the Hermes connection form with the Connection Headers row in two or three placements (inside the sign-in section, an "Advanced" disclosure like onboarding's, or its own section). Also show the editor with the half-pair warning and a Bearer rejection, in light and dark and at a large Dynamic Type size. Publish them and wait for a pick before implementing.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight).

1. Open the Bots inbox over the tunnel with no headers. Expected: unchanged.
2. Add a harmless header (`X-Hermex-Test: 1`) and connect. Expected: it connects, and chat works.
3. Enter `Authorization: Bearer x`. Expected: refused, with the reason.
4. Uzair only, optional: a hostname behind Cloudflare Access with a service token, tried once with the two-header form and once with the single-header JSON form. Expected: status, sign-in, inbox, chat and push setup all work. Without the headers, the `.blocked` copy appears.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the single connection form, opened from the inbox gear (`BotsInboxView.swift:171-173`), from Settings (`SettingsView.swift:2236-2249`) and from the push section (`HermexPushSectionView.swift:126-130`). Every Bot screen and push provisioning inherit the headers through `HermesConnections`.
- **Targets:** main app only. The extensions never open this connection.
- **Servers:** headers live in one server's Hermes connection record, and switching servers retires the connection.
- **Reverse states:** headers can be removed, and removing them retires the connection.
- **Connection modes:** Access is the tunnel case; LAN is unchanged. #744 later stores headers per address, and its alternate address starts with none.
- **Native quality:** the editor already handles Dynamic Type and VoiceOver. The new strings ship in 17 languages.
- **Kanban:** Hermes has no Kanban client yet. #704 must send these headers on `/api/plugins/kanban/events` through `HermesConnection`.

## Preservation

- #880: `.blocked` detection and the upgrade mapping stay as they are; only the `.blocked` copy gains the headers pointer.
- #824: headers never come from the webui snapshot, and never reach `PushRelayClient` or another host through a redirect.
- #751: every advice-table row keeps its text.
- #889: never log header names or values.

## Blockers

#880 (the `.blocked` copy and the shared send path), set as a GitHub dependency.

## Outside reach

The Access check needs a Cloudflare Access application with a service token on Uzair's account. Agents don't touch the tunnel or the Access configuration.
