title: feat(hermes): a Hermes server kind with its own sign-in
body:
Part of #700 (slice 0.3) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #884, #898 · **Unblocks:** #900

## Problem and outcome

Every server in Hermex is a webui server:
- The server registry has no kind (`HermesMobile/Models/ServerAccount.swift:16-32`).
- Sign-in probes the webui's `/health` and `/api/auth/status` (`HermesMobile/Auth/AuthManager.swift:132-139`).
- The logged-in tree is always the webui session list (`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:77-95`).

A Hermes host can be reached only as a side connection stored under a webui server (`bot_connection::<webui URL>`, `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:94-109`), and only while the webui sign-in holds. When the webui rejects its cookie, the user lands on onboarding even though the Hermes connection still works (`AuthManager.swift:450-467`).

After this, a configured server is either **webui** or **Hermes**. A Hermes server has its own sign-in record, signs in through `HermesConnection`, and opens on the Bots inbox. It falls back to its own sign-in form only when the host rejects the saved username or password. Webui servers don't change, including their side Hermes connection, their Bots row and their push pairing.

## Contract

Client-only storage and routing. Evidence is pinned to Hermex `699074e7` and hermes-agent `ca678285`.

- **Hermes sign-in is unchanged.**
  - Sign-in reads the public status, then logs in, then checks identity (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:86-113`).
  - A signed-in request that gets a 401 signs in once more and is resent (`:144-153`).
- **Login budget.** The host allows 10 password logins per 60 s per client IP, successful ones included (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py:338-339`, `:384`).
- **No password-less hosts.** A Hermes host bound anywhere but loopback always requires sign-in (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:470-495`).

## Plan

- [ ] **Kind.** `ServerAccount` (`ServerAccount.swift:16-83`) gains `kind: ServerKind` (`webui` | `hermes`) and `serverVersion: String?`.
  - A missing or unknown `kind` decodes as `webui`, in the tolerant init (`:62-83`). One bad entry must never drop the whole list (`:142`).
  - A Hermes server's `id` and `urlString` are its address normalized by `BotConnection.address(_:)` (root only after #886). Never use `AuthManager.normalizedServerURL` (`AuthManager.swift:578-634`), whose rules differ.
- [ ] **Sign-in record.** A Hermes server's credentials are a `BotConnection`, saved under that server's own URL (`bot_connection::<Hermes URL>`) through the existing `BotConnectionStore` (Decision 1). Every Bot store already keys by server URL plus connection UUID, so the inbox, chats, drafts, caches, section order and bot links work unchanged when `server` is the Hermes URL.
- [ ] **AuthManager.**
  - Add `addHermesServer(_:)` beside `addServer` (`AuthManager.swift:215-279`). It saves the record, then registers and activates the server.
  - `addHermesServer` refuses an address that's already in the registry, with the same guard `addServer` uses (`AuthManager.swift:230`; the registry dedupes by URL, `ServerAccount.swift:170-190`). A webui server and a Hermes server can never share a URL.
  - `restoreSavedServer` (`:556-576`) restores a Hermes server as `.loggedIn` when its record exists, without probing the webui.
  - `signOut`, `removeServer` and `clearLocalArtifacts` (`:301-342`, `:415-423`) touch only that server's record and Bot data. Signing out of a Hermes server deletes its record and shows its sign-in form with the address filled in.
  - `PushRegistrar.forget` has nothing to delete, because a Hermes server has no pairing until #706.
- [ ] **Rejected password on a Hermes server.** When the login step answers 401 for the active Hermes server (`HermesConnection.swift:101`, including the one silent re-login a signed-in 401 triggers, `:144-153`), `AuthManager` moves to `.loggedOut(server)`.
  - No Bot screen exists in that state, so nothing can resend the rejected password. Saving a changed record from the sign-in form signs in again.
  - Transport errors, 5xx, `.blocked`, `.outdated` and 429 keep `.loggedIn`, with the inbox's error row.
  - Don't store a sign-in flag on `HermesConnection`. `HermesConnections` holds the connection weakly (`HermesConnection.swift:231`) and `BotInbox` releases its client on a failure (`BotInbox.swift:798`), so such a flag would be lost and the next open would resend the password.
  - A webui server's side connection keeps #884's per-screen flag exactly as #884 built it.
- [ ] **Root.** `ContentView.content` (`ContentView.swift:70-95`) branches on the active server's kind:
  - A logged-in Hermes server opens a Hermes home: `BotsInboxView(server:)` as the root, with a toolbar entry to Settings (from the mock pick).
  - A logged-out Hermes server shows the Hermes sign-in form (`BotConnectionView(server:)`), with the saved address and username filled in and the password field focused (#884, Decision 3).
  - Keep `.id(server)` so a switch rebuilds the tree. `AuthManager.state.didSet` already retires the old connection (`AuthManager.swift:59`).
- [ ] **Connection form on a Hermes server.** The address field is read-only and "Remove Hermes connection…" is hidden (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:24`, `:77`, `:298-349`). The address is the server's identity, and removing a Hermes server goes through Settings → Servers. Username, password and headers stay editable.
- [ ] **Settings on a Hermes server.**
  - Keep: Servers (switch, add, remove), the Hermes connection row, app-wide settings and the Preview card.
  - Hide the webui-only rows: Archived Sessions (`SettingsView.swift:123-130`), the webui update check (`:1018`, `:1209`), the webui Connection Headers row (`:562-571`) and Notifications (#706).
- [ ] **Beta gate.** Adding a Hermes server requires `BotModeGate` on (`HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:330-343`). With the gate off, an existing Hermes server still opens (Decision 4).
- [ ] **System entry points while a Hermes server is active** (Decision 5):
  - New-chat intents and links (`ContentView.swift:108-126`), session links (`:135-138`) and share imports (`:140-144`, `:193-212`) first switch to the first webui server in the registry, through `authManager.switchActiveServer(to:)`, the way webui push taps already do (`:150-160`).
  - With no webui server configured, new-chat and session links show a short message ("Add a webui server to start a chat") instead of doing nothing. A queued share shows the same message with a Discard action, so it never pops into a chat later without warning.
  - Bot links route as today (`:130-133`; `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotDeepLink.swift:102-116`), and they must resolve a Hermes server by its URL. `BotDeepLinkRouter` ignores every link while the Bot Mode gate is off (`BotDeepLink.swift:110`); a link for an existing Hermes server must still open (Decision 4).
  - App Intents: `ProfileEntityProvider` reads `.serverURL` and calls the webui's `/api/profiles` (`HermesMobile/AppIntents/ProfileEntity.swift:115`). Leave Hermes servers out of its Profile list until #706 brings Hermes Profiles to Shortcuts.
  - `reconcileOrphanedLiveActivities` (`ContentView.swift:61-67`) skips Hermes servers.
- [ ] **`HermesConnections`.** Its shape doesn't change: it keeps one entry, the active server's (`HermesConnection.swift:228-253`).
- [ ] **Dev sign-in.** `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes` exports a flag. With it, `DevAutoLogin` (`HermesMobile/Config/DevAutoLogin.swift:10-72`) adds and activates a Hermes server from the `HERMEX_DEV_BOT_*` values; it already turns on `BotModeGate` (`:58`, `:72`). Without the flag, nothing changes. Document it in `DEVELOPMENT.md` § Signing a simulator in. #890's local server can then be targeted by address.
- [ ] **Docs.**
  - `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` gets a kind column and the Hermes server rows (`:129-151`).
  - `docs/agents/bots.md:3-36` covers a Hermes server's record.
  - `CONTEXT.md` gets the server kinds: "webui server" and "Hermes server".
  - Propose, but don't make, the `AGENTS.md` glossary change for "server".

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- A Hermes server opens on today's Bots inbox plus Settings, and can be added only while Bot Mode (beta) is on.
- Existing Bot connections are copied, not moved; the move is #707's. So there's no `legacyWebuiServerID` link and no fallback read of `bot_connection::<webui URL>`.
- Push on a Hermes server waits for #706.
- **Revised (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** #884's per-screen flag stays as #884 built it. On a Hermes server, a rejected password takes the app to that server's sign-in form, where no Bot screen can resend it.
- **Added (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** refuse a duplicate address; lock the address and hide Remove on a Hermes server's connection form; keep Hermes servers out of the Shortcuts Profile list until #706; open bot links for an existing Hermes server even with Bot Mode off; show a message, and a Discard for a queued share, when no webui server exists.
- **Amends #713 decision 2 and #700:** moving saved connections is #707, and push pairing on a Hermes server is #706.

1. **Record key.** Recommend reusing `bot_connection::<server>` for a Hermes server's own sign-in. It is the same `BotConnection` JSON keyed by the Hermes server's URL, so every Bot store, deep link and cleanup path works without a second key or a copy step. #700's `hermes_credential::` name existed for the fallback-read move, which is now #707's job. Alternative: a new `hermes_credential::` key, which every Bot store would have to learn as a second lookup.
2. **The password stays required.** #700's "password optional" is for OAuth. #708 adds it when it has a caller.
3. **A reused sign-in gets a new UUID.** When #900 copies a webui server's side connection into a new Hermes server, the copy gets a fresh UUID and the same `installID`. Two servers never share a connection UUID, so no store keyed by UUID alone (`BotAvatarStore`, `BotUnreadStore`, `BotRoomOrganizeStore`; see `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:242-250`) can cross servers. Alternative: keep the UUID. A later move (#707) might like that, but today it would share state between two live servers.
4. **Gate off.** Recommend that turning Bot Mode off hides "Hermes" in Add Server but never locks a user out of a Hermes server they already have. Alternative: hide Hermes servers from the switcher while the gate is off.
5. **Webui-only entry points.** Recommend switching to a webui server, as webui push taps already do. Alternative: ignore them silently while a Hermes server is active.
6. **Downgrade risk accepted.** An older build that re-saves the registry would drop `kind` and read a Hermes server as webui (`ServerAccount.swift:339-347`). App Store builds can't be downgraded, and the Branch app keeps its own Keychain service (`KEYCHAIN_SERVICE = $(APP_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER)`, suffix `.branch`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A registry blob without `kind`, or with an unknown one, loads every server as webui.
- [ ] **Two servers, one webui and one Hermes.**
  - Switching rebuilds the tree.
  - The Hermes server opens on the Bots inbox; the webui server opens on its session list, with its own Bots row and side connection unchanged.
  - Credentials, drafts, caches, section order and bot links stay with their server.
- [ ] **Rejected password on a Hermes server.** When the host rejects it (a login 401, including after the one silent re-login), the app shows the Hermes sign-in form with the password focused. Foregrounding, pull to refresh and bot links send no login until a changed record is saved. A 5xx, a transport error, `.blocked` or a 429 keeps the inbox, with its error row.
- [ ] A webui 401 never signs out a Hermes server, and a Hermes 401 never signs out the webui server.
- [ ] With a Hermes server active, "New Chat" from the Action button switches to the first webui server and opens a new chat. With no webui server configured, the message appears, and a queued share can be discarded.
- [ ] Adding a Hermes server at an address already in the registry is refused, with a message.
- [ ] On a Hermes server's connection form, the address can't be edited and there's no "Remove Hermes connection…".
- [ ] The Shortcuts Profile picker lists only webui servers' Profiles.
- [ ] With Bot Mode off, a bot link for an existing Hermes server opens it.
- [ ] Removing a Hermes server deletes only its record and Bot data; the relay is never called.
- [ ] `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes` lands on a signed-in Hermes server. Without the flag, it behaves as before.

## Tests

These fail on today's code unless noted.

- `ServerRegistryTests`: default and unknown kind; Hermes id normalization; round-trip.
- `AuthManagerStateTests`:
  - Hermes restore reaches `.loggedIn`, and rejected credentials reach `.loggedOut`.
  - A 5xx or transport error keeps the state.
  - Webui and Hermes 401s stay isolated.
  - Removing the Hermes server; switching retires the connection.
- `AuthManagerStateTests`: a login 401 on the active Hermes server moves to `.loggedOut` and sends no further login until a changed record is saved; 429, 5xx and transport errors keep `.loggedIn`; a duplicate address is refused.
- `BotInboxTests`, `BotConversationTests`, `BotRoomTests`: #884's tests pass unchanged.
- `BotConnectionVersionTests` (connection form): the address is read-only and Remove is hidden for a Hermes server.
- `AppIntentNewChatInProfileTests`: Hermes servers are left out of the Profile list.
- `BotDeepLinkTests`: a bot link for a Hermes server resolves and switches to it, including with the Bot Mode gate off.
- `BotModeGateTests`: the add path is gated; an existing Hermes server opens with the gate off.
- `scripts/sim-login`: a real run with and without `--hermes`, plus `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` if it gains tests.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ServerRegistryTests --only HermesMobileTests/AuthManagerStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotDeepLinkTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotModeGateTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests --only HermesMobileTests/AppIntentNewChatInProfileTests`

## Mocks

Required, for three screens:
- the Hermes home: the inbox as the root, with the Settings entry and the server's identity
- the trimmed Settings
- the signed-out sign-in form

Show each in light and dark, on iPhone and iPad, and at a large Dynamic Type size. Wait for a pick. The add-server UI is #900's.

## Manual test

Device: the simulator first, then a physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight) over the tunnel.

1. Run `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`. Expected: the Hermes home with the Bots inbox, and chats open.
2. Switch to the webui server in Settings → Servers. Expected: the session list, with its Bots row and Hermes connection unchanged.
3. Switch back to the Hermes server, background the app past the tunnel's idle timeout, and return. Expected: the inbox reconnects quietly.
4. Use the Action button's "New Chat" while the Hermes server is active. Expected: Hermex switches to the webui server and opens a new chat.
5. On iPad, check the Hermes home layout and switching.

Testing a rejected password needs a host change. That is Uzair's call and optional.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the root, Settings → Servers, bot links, new-chat App Intents, session links, share imports, webui push taps and Live Activity reconciliation (all listed in the plan).
- **Targets:** main app only. `ServerAccount.swift` is a member of `HermesMobile` alone. The share extension, Live Activity widget and notification service don't read the registry.
- **Servers:** the whole point. Walk the two-server acceptance above.
- **Reverse states:** a Hermes server can be removed and signed out of. A rejected password leads through the form back to signed in.
- **Connection modes:** unchanged; sign-in is `HermesConnection`'s.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver labels on the new toolbar entry. The new strings ship in 17 languages.

## Preservation

- #884: its per-screen flag and "Update sign-in" button stay as built; never resend a rejected password; OAuth changes the button later (#708).
- #880: `.blocked`, `.browserSignIn` and the upgrade mapping stay as they are.
- #886: Hermes server URLs are root-only, through the same parser.
- #777: the install identity is checked before the password, and an omitted id never clears a stored one.
- #574: DEBUG sign-in survives root rebuilds, including on iPad.
- #824 and #825: server switch, sign-out, removal and credential changes retire the shared connection at once.

## Blockers

- #884: the rejected-password rule this keeps (it edits the same files).
- #898: both edit `HermesConnections`, `adopt` and the `BotConnection` record.

Both are set as GitHub dependencies.

## Outside reach

None. The optional rejected-password check changes the host's dashboard password, which only Uzair does.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code.

title: feat(hermes): add a Hermes server from onboarding and Settings
body:
Part of #700 (slice 0.3) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #897, #898, #899, #880, #886 · Absorbs #170.

## Problem and outcome

Onboarding and Add Server only understand the webui:
- They probe `/health`, then `/api/auth/status` (`HermesMobile/Auth/AuthManager.swift:132-139`).
- They ask only for a password (`HermesMobile/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingConnectPage.swift:40-86`; `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsView.swift:2391-2428`).
- A Hermes dashboard address fails with webui errors.
- Their connection help assumes Tailscale (`OnboardingConnectPage.swift:33`, `OnboardingTailscalePage.swift:13-19`, `OnboardingWelcomePage.swift:77`, `:84`). Real setups also use the local network and Cloudflare tunnels, and #170 asks for NetBird.

After this, the user types an address and Hermex checks what answers there:
- **A Hermes dashboard** gets username and password fields. If a webui server's saved Hermes connection uses exactly the same address, the user can reuse that sign-in instead of typing it.
- **A webui** gets today's flow.
- **A choice of Same Wi-Fi, Private network or Cloudflare Tunnel** changes only the placeholder, the help text and which fields show.

## Contract

Evidence is pinned to Hermex `699074e7` and hermes-agent `ca678285`.

- **Hermes status.** `/api/status` is public on Hermes and reports `version` and `install_id` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:499-524`), plus `auth_required` and `auth_providers` (`:357-379`).
- **Webui answers.** An unknown `/api/*` path gets a JSON 401 when the webui's auth is on (#880, Contract), or a 404. Its `/health` answers `{"status": "ok"}`, which is today's probe.
- **Wrong Host header.** A request under an unexpected hostname gets `400 Invalid Host header…` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:577-593`). `BotConnectionAdvice` already maps it to "set `dashboard.public_url`" (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:93-95`).
- **Rate limit.** Too many logins get a 429 (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py:338-339`, `:384`), which already has an advice row (`BotProtocol.swift:96-97`).
- **Always signed in.** No Hermes host bound off loopback runs without sign-in (`web_server.py:470-495`), so every Hermes server needs a username and password.

## Plan

- [ ] **Kind detection** (Decision 1). Parse the typed address with `BotConnection.address(_:)` (#886) and send `GET /api/status` there, with the form's headers (#898).
  - A JSON object carrying `auth_required` means Hermes. It then goes through `HermesConnection`'s own sign-in, which runs #897's version gate and #880's classifications.
  - Anything else falls through to today's webui path, which uses `AuthManager.normalizedServerURL`.
  - `.blocked` and a 400 show their advice directly, without falling through.
- [ ] **Hermes branch.**
  - Username and password fields, plus Connection Headers (#898).
  - One sign-in through `HermesConnection`, then `AuthManager.addHermesServer` (#899).
  - Errors go through `BotConnectionAdvice`. Write no new 400, 401 or 429 copy (#880).
  - A 401 is never retried on its own (#884).
- [ ] **Reusing a saved sign-in.**
  - When a configured webui server's side connection has **exactly the same normalized address** (`BotConnection.address(_:)`, #886), offer "Use the sign-in saved on <server name>".
  - Never match by `install_id`. It comes from the public `/api/status`, so any host can report another host's id and would then be offered a saved password (and it would cross servers, against `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md:140-141`). After sign-in, the saved `installID` is still checked as today (#777).
  - Accepting fills in the username, password and headers.
  - The new server's record gets a fresh UUID (#899, Decision 3).
  - One real sign-in still verifies it. The webui server's side connection is untouched.
- [ ] **Connection mode.** Three choices: Same Wi-Fi · Private network (Tailscale, NetBird…) · Cloudflare Tunnel.
  - The choice changes only the placeholder (`http://192.168.1.5:9119`, `http://my-mac.tailnet-name.ts.net:9119`, `https://hermes.example.com`), the help text, and which fields show.
  - Cloudflare Tunnel shows Connection Headers with an Access hint and the two `CF-Access-Client-*` names prefilled.
  - It is not saved, and no network behavior depends on it (Decision 2). The scheme is still inferred by the parser, and #886's "Will connect to" line shows the result.
- [ ] **Provider-neutral copy** (#170). The Connect page's help (`OnboardingConnectPage.swift:33`) follows the chosen mode. The Tailscale page (`OnboardingTailscalePage.swift:13-19`) and the welcome copy (`OnboardingWelcomePage.swift:77`, `:84`) say "private network" and name Tailscale and NetBird. The webui setup prompt (`OnboardingAgentPromptPage` / `OnboardingFlowPolicy.swift:8-37`) is unchanged (Decision 3).
- [ ] **Beta gate** (#899). When the preview is off and a Hermes dashboard is detected, the form says so and offers "Turn on Bot Mode (beta) and continue" (Decision 4).
- [ ] **One view model for both entry points.** Onboarding (`OnboardingViewModel.swift:6`, pages at `OnboardingView.swift:44-62`) and Add Server (`AddServerView`, `SettingsView.swift:2363-2510`) share the detection and branch logic.
- [ ] **Strings.** `Localizable.xcstrings`, all 17 languages, `needs_review`. Check the RTL pseudolanguage for the placeholders and the URL preview (`docs/agents/i18n.md` § RTL).
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/agents/bots.md` (connection form); `README.md:69-79` (setup options) gains Same Wi-Fi and names NetBird.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):**
- Hermes appears in Add Server only while Bot Mode (beta) is on.
- A webui server's saved sign-in can be reused, so nobody retypes a password.
- A Same Wi-Fi / Private network / Cloudflare choice changes only the placeholder, the help and which fields show.
- #170 is absorbed and closed.

1. **Probe order: Hermes status first.** `/api/status` is public and cheap, and a webui answers it with a JSON 401 or a 404, which falls through to today's path. Alternative: probe the webui first, which costs a Hermes user a failed webui round-trip on every add.
2. **The mode is help only.** Recommend it isn't saved and doesn't pick the scheme. The parser's rules and preview (#886) stay the single source of truth. Alternative: let the mode force `http` or `https`, a second rule that would contradict the preview.
3. **The webui setup prompt stays unchanged.** Webui gets bug fixes only (#713, decision 1), and the prompt is a tested Tailscale recipe. A NetBird-specific setup prompt, as #170 proposes, is not built; the provider-neutral copy and the NetBird mention are what this issue delivers for #170. Alternative: write and maintain a second recipe for a frozen backend.
4. **Preview gate: offer it inline.** Recommend a one-tap "Turn on Bot Mode (beta) and continue" wherever a Hermes dashboard is detected, so a first-run user with only a dashboard isn't stuck. It is still a deliberate opt-in. Alternative: tell them to turn it on in Settings, which onboarding can't reach before any server exists.
5. **The username field shows only for Hermes.**
6. **Reuse matches the address only (revised by Uzair, 2026-09-28).** Matching the public `install_id` would let a hostile host claim a saved password. The trade-off: a host reached at a new address (for example LAN versus tunnel) gets no offer, and the user types the password once.
7. **Supersedes #706 slice 6.5's kind detection and username field.** #706 keeps only what's left of 6.5 (the basic-auth setup prompt).

## Acceptance

- [ ] The tunnel's Hermes dashboard address, typed into Add Server, shows username and password. Connect signs in once and lands on the Hermes home (#899).
- [ ] A webui address behaves exactly as today, in both onboarding and Add Server.
- [ ] A saved side connection with exactly the same address is offered. Accepting it connects without typing. The new record has a new UUID, and the webui server's side connection is unchanged.
- [ ] A host at a different address is never offered a saved sign-in, even when it reports the same `install_id`.
- [ ] Each failure shows its existing copy: a Host-header 400 (`dashboard.public_url`), 429, `.blocked`, `.browserSignIn` and `.outdated`. There is no second login after a 401.
- [ ] Switching the mode changes only the placeholder, the help and the fields shown. Nothing is saved.
- [ ] With the preview off, a detected Hermes dashboard shows the opt-in. Accepting it turns on `BotModeGate` and continues.

## Tests

These fail on today's code.

- `OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests` and `OnboardingFlowTests`, with URLProtocol fixtures:
  - A Hermes status goes to the Hermes branch.
  - A webui JSON 401 or 404 on `/api/status` falls through to `/health`.
  - A 400, a 429, `.blocked` and `.outdated` each show their copy.
  - The gate-off opt-in.
- `AuthManagerStateTests`: adding a Hermes server from onboarding and from Add Server.
- A reuse test: the saved side connection is offered only for the exact same normalized address; a different address reporting the same `install_id` is not offered.
- `LocalizationCatalogTests`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests --only HermesMobileTests/OnboardingFlowTests --only HermesMobileTests/AuthManagerStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionSetupTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`

## Mocks

Required:
- the address step with the three modes
- the Hermes sign-in fields
- the reuse-saved-sign-in offer
- the gate-off opt-in
- an error row

Show each in onboarding's dark style and in the Settings sheet, on iPhone and iPad, in light and dark, at a large Dynamic Type size, and with RTL. Wait for a pick.

## Manual test

Device: the simulator for onboarding (a fresh install), then a physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight) for Add Server over the tunnel. The maintainer's dashboard listens on loopback only, so the Same Wi-Fi mode can be checked only for its copy on that host.

1. Run a fresh simulator install without `sim-login`, and type the webui address. Expected: today's flow.
2. In Settings → Add Server, type the tunnel's dashboard address. Expected: username and password appear, and the reuse offer names the webui server.
3. Accept the offer and connect. Expected: the Hermes home. Switching back to the webui server shows its Hermes connection unchanged.
4. Turn Bot Mode off and repeat step 2. Expected: the opt-in.
5. Switch among the three modes. Expected: only the placeholder and help change.
6. Try a large Dynamic Type size and the RTL pseudolanguage.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** onboarding (first run, and after the last server is removed) and Settings → Add Server. The connection form for a webui server's side connection is unchanged.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Servers:** a new Hermes server never changes an existing one. The reused sign-in is a copy.
- **Reverse states:** a Hermes server added here can be removed (#899).
- **Connection modes:** this issue is where they're named. There's no downgrade on a TLS failure (#751).
- **Native quality:** the segmented choice and new fields get VoiceOver labels. The new strings ship in 17 languages, and the RTL preview is checked.

## Preservation

- #880: reuse `BotConnectionAdvice`; no new 400, 401 or 429 copy.
- #886: parse through `address(_:)`, save root-only addresses, and show the "Will connect to" line.
- #751: keep the ATS copy, and show address errors before any transport exists.
- #777: check the install identity before the password.
- #897: the version gate. #898: headers on the probe and the sign-in. #884: never resend.

## Blockers

#897, #898, #899, #880 and #886, set as GitHub dependencies.

## Outside reach

None.

title: fix(bots): reattach a Bot Chat without applying frames early
body:
Part of #700 (slice 0.4) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** nothing · **Unblocks:** #902

## Problem and outcome

When a Bot Chat reconnects, it re-reads the conversation in four steps: find the Bot Chat, resume, replay missed events, then resume again for the snapshot (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:573-610`). Three things go wrong on that path.

1. **Live frames are applied in the middle of recovery.**
   - `observe` accepts any frame for the current runtime while the chat is `.recovering` (`:1370`).
   - The runtime is updated at `:601`, before the replay reply arrives. So a live frame that lands between the resume and that reply advances `sequence`.
   - The common case is a gap: after a drop, the first live frame skips ahead. The discontinuity branch (`:1394-1403`) clears `liveActivity` and jumps `sequence` to that frame, the replay then skips every missed event at or below it (`:663`), and with no later `message.start` the activity stays cleared (`:677-678`).
   - Less often, a frame beyond the replay's `latest` lands first, and `reconcileReplay` moves `sequence` backwards (`:669`).
   - **What the user sees:** after a mid-turn reattach (unlocking, pulling down Control Center, a network blip), the running turn's tool rows and reasoning vanish until the turn settles, and the Live Activity's tool count drops with them. Rows can't duplicate: they're keyed by `tool_id` (`BotActivity.swift:70-78`), and text comes only from the snapshot.
2. **A reconnect downloads the transcript two or three times.** The first resume only checks identity, but `resume()` defaults to full history (`:594`, `:637-639`), and the snapshot resume downloads it again (`:608`). After a gap, `fullSnapshotNeeded` stays set, so `:625` triggers a third full read (`:1469`). Over a tunnel on cellular, that multiplies the reconnect payload. Partial refreshes already pass `omit_messages`, and that reply still carries `session_id` and `session_key` (`tui_gateway/server.py:2903-2904`).
3. **Temporary resume refusals are treated as permanent.**
   - While a replaced runtime is being swapped, the host answers `4007 "session no longer live; retry resume"`. While a client-gone interrupt settles, it answers `4009 "session disconnect interrupt settling"` (`tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py:690-698`).
   - `disconnected` retries only transport errors, 408, 429 and 5xx (`BotConversation.swift:1496-1501`), so these show advice and stop.

After this, a reattach holds live frames until the replay is reconciled, then applies only the frames after it. It identifies the session with `omit_messages: true`, downloads the transcript once, and retries 4007 and 4009 for up to 60 seconds.

## Contract

Evidence is pinned to Hermex `699074e7` and hermes-agent `ca678285` (0.21.5).

- **`session.resume`** takes `profile`, `lazy`, `defer_history`, `omit_messages`, `eager_build` and `cols` (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:547-556`), plus `close_on_disconnect` (`:576`).
  - Reusing a live session, it replies with `running`, `turn_started_at`, `session_id` (the runtime), `session_key`, `status` and `messages_omitted`.
  - `inflight`, `queued`, `pending_approval`, `open_requests` and `pending_connection` appear only when non-empty (`tui_gateway/server.py:2876-2915`).
- **`session.events.since`** returns `events`, `latest_seq`, `truncated`, `count`, `epoch` and `open_requests` (`methods_session.py:2324-2338`). `replay_epoch` rides on `gateway.ready` (`tui_gateway/ws.py:297-302`).
- **The replay ring** holds 512 events and 4 MiB per session, and 64 sessions and 64 MiB per process (`tui_gateway/event_replay.py:28-34`). Evicting a ring resets its `seq` to 1 (`:74-78`), so a backwards `seq` on a live socket is a real case.
- **4007 has two meanings with the same code.** "Session no longer live; retry resume" (`session_lifecycle.py:696`) is temporary. "Session not found" (`methods_session.py:703`) is not. **4009** is at `session_lifecycle.py:698`.
- **Timings.** A disconnected session is reaped after a 20 s grace; a running turn survives while its activity is fresher than 600 s (`server.py:127-137`). These are unchanged since 0.21.4 (`d337b736`): the pin's reaper diff only adds exit-time turn stopping and skips pinned rows.

## Plan

- [ ] **Hold frames.**
  - While `.recovering`, `observe` buffers frames for this runtime instead of applying them, up to 512. Past that, rebuild from the snapshot (Decision 2).
  - After `reconcileReplay` and the snapshot, apply buffered frames with `seq > sequence`, in order, and drop the rest.
  - A gap schedules the existing coalesced refresh (`:1452-1482`).
  - Server requests (envelopes with string ids) keep today's replace-by-id path (`:1374-1376`) and revision guards (`:657`, `:799-803`).
- [ ] **One full resume.** The identity resume sends `omit_messages: true` (`resume(full: false)`); the snapshot resume stays full. Check the omitted-messages reply against the pin: `session_key` and `session_id` must still be present for the identity check at `:595`.
- [ ] **Retry window.**
  - Treat 4007 and 4009 from `session.resume` as retryable for up to 60 s from the first refusal, on the existing backoff (`:1509-1527`). After that, show today's advice.
  - Other methods' 4007 and 4009 are unchanged.
  - `HermesGateway.consume` drops the host's message for plain rejections (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:327-328`). Carry the code alone; no string matching (Decision 1).
- [ ] **Test fixture.** Drive `BotConversation` over the shared gateway with `BotScriptedSocket` (`HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests.swift:1039-1113`), which can interleave replies with `seq` frames. `BotFixtureWire` (`HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests.swift:1505-1673`) can't. Keep the helper inside `HermesMobileTests`. If it becomes shared test infrastructure, the repository's local full-suite rule applies.
- [ ] **Logging.** If #889 has landed, log each reattach through its logger with counts only: frames held, applied and dropped, and retries. Never log session keys or runtime ids. If it hasn't, skip logging; #889 is not a blocker.
- [ ] **Docs.** The reconnect section of `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** this is the first reconnect child (#902 is the second; the engine moved to #701). It stops applying frames early, attaches with `omit_messages`, and retries 4007 and 4009 for 60 s.

1. **Retry 4007 without matching strings.** Recommend retrying any 4007 or 4009 from `session.resume` within the 60 s window. The two 4007 meanings differ only in message text, and matching it breaks the day upstream rewords it. A real "not found" costs at most 60 s before today's advice, and `session.list` found the chat moments earlier. Alternative: match "retry resume".
2. **Buffer bound.** Recommend the ring size, 512 frames. Past it, rebuild from the snapshot, as a truncated replay does today.
3. **Keep the Bot Chat's text model.** Text still comes only from the snapshot and `inflight`. This issue doesn't add a delta reducer; that is #701's.
4. **Don't key by runtime id** (#700 comment of 2026-09-28). The chat keeps its root and tip identity (`:95`, `:103`, `:155`). A resume that returns a new runtime resets replay (`:597-601`), as it does today.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Mid-turn, a live frame that skips ahead is delivered before the replay reply. The missed tool rows and reasoning are applied from the replay, nothing vanishes, and the live frame is applied once after it. (Fails today: the test must send that gap frame before the replay reply.)
- [ ] A `seq` frame delivered between the identity resume and the replay reply is applied once, after the replay. `sequence` never moves backwards, and the chat doesn't rebuild when nothing was missed. (Fails today.)
- [ ] A frame at or below the replay's `latest_seq` is dropped. A gap after the held frames schedules one refresh.
- [ ] The identity resume carries `omit_messages: true`, and each reconnect downloads full history once. (Fails today.)
- [ ] A `session.resume` answering 4007 and then succeeding reconnects without advice; 4009 behaves the same. A 4007 that persists past 60 s shows today's advice. (Fails today.)
- [ ] The existing replay rules still pass: epoch change, `truncated`, `latest_seq < last_seen`, a backwards live `seq` and the ring rebuild (`BotConversationTests.swift:799`, `:917`, `:1132`).
- [ ] No prompt, answer, stop or setting is ever resent (`BotConversation.swift:1507-1508`).

## Tests

- `BotConversationTests`: new cases on the socket-level fixture, plus the existing ones unchanged.
- `BotPendingRequestTests`: open requests after a reattach with held frames.
- `BotLiveActivityTests`: disconnect and reattach.
- `HermesAgentFixtureTests` and `HermesGatewayTests`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesAgentFixtureTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesGatewayTests`

## Mocks

Not required: no visible change.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight) over the tunnel. The mid-turn steps need a real turn, either on Uzair's own test bot or on #890's local server once it lands.

1. Start a long reply in a Bot Chat, lock the phone for about 30 s, then unlock. Expected: the text resumes with no duplicated tool rows and no flash of an empty chat.
2. Mid-turn, turn Airplane Mode on, then off. Expected: the chat shows reconnecting, then catches up.
3. Mid-turn, background the app past the tunnel's idle timeout, then return. Expected: it reattaches with no "Connection lost" advice.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** Bot Chat on iPhone and iPad, opened from the inbox, from a bot link or from a push tap.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Live Activity:** it is updated through `syncLiveActivity`, and a reattach marks it current again.
- **Rooms:** unaffected, since they don't replay (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomReader.swift:131-153`).
- **Share extension, notification service, App Intents:** unchanged.
- **Connection modes:** the tunnel's idle cutoff and cellular hand-offs are the target cases.

## Preservation

- #508: recovery restores unconfirmed drafts and attachments and never resends a prompt, answer, stop or setting.
- #506: session-change refreshes stay coalesced.
- #775: every socket sends ready, then capabilities, then the keepalive.
- #791: a lost reaction reply stays uncertain.
- #777: host identity is checked.
- #880: `.upgradeRefused` stays permanent. #884: `needsSignIn` stops reconnects.
- #889: log counts, never ids.

## Blockers

None. (#889 is optional: log through it if it has landed.)

## Outside reach

The mid-turn manual steps run a real turn on a bot Uzair owns. Agents don't write to the live host.

title: perf(hermes): keep the shared socket through Control Center and close it on background
body:
Part of #700 (slice 0.4) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #901 · **Unblocks:** nothing

## Problem and outcome

Since #829, every Bot screen on a connection shares one gateway socket. That socket closes for the wrong reason: each screen leaves on any non-active scene phase.

| Screen | Where it leaves |
|---|---|
| Bot Chat | `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatView.swift:267-270` |
| Bots inbox | `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotsInboxView.swift:539-542` |
| Room | `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:142-146` |
| Room profile | `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomProfileView.swift:79-83` |
| Creator | `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotCreateView.swift:113` |
| Room creator | `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomCreateView.swift:40` |
| Profile editor | `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotProfileEditorView.swift:54-56` |

Pulling down Control Center or a notification banner makes the scene `.inactive`. Today that tears the socket down, and every screen reconnects. During a running turn that reconnect also sets off #901's bug (the turn's tool rows vanish). Meanwhile, nothing at the gateway guarantees a clean close when the app really goes to the background.

After this, the socket stays open through `.inactive`, closes once when the app goes to the background, and reopens on `.active`.

## Contract

Evidence is pinned to Hermex `699074e7` and hermes-agent `ca678285`.

- **Reaping.** A chat with no attached socket is reaped 20 s after the drop if it's idle. A running turn continues while its activity is fresher than 600 s (`tui_gateway/server.py:127-137`; `session_lifecycle.py:723-834`).
- **Why close on background.** Noticing a half-open socket can lag by the tunnel's idle cutoff (about 100 s), so the app should close cleanly on background (plan §1.2).
- **Every new socket** gets a fresh ticket, then ready, capabilities and the keepalive (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:218-249`).

## Plan

- [ ] **Background.** One owner closes the gateway silently when the scene enters `.background`, for example `HermesConnections` observing the scene phase from `ContentView`.
- [ ] **Screens.** The screens in the table react to `.background` instead of any non-active phase, so `.inactive` keeps the socket. They reconnect on `.active`, as today.
- [ ] **Logging.** If #889 has landed, log each background close. Never log ids.
- [ ] **Docs.** The `HermesGateway` header comment (`HermesGateway.swift:3-24`) and the gateway section of `docs/agents/bots.md`.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** stay open through `.inactive` and close only on background.

**Revised (Uzair, 2026-09-28):** the "reopen the socket past about 8 attached chats" recycle, its attached-chat registry and visible-turn reporting are cut. No problem has been measured: the host's replay caps are per process, the costs of an attached chat come from any single attachment, and the socket likely already reopens on each inbox → chat hop (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotsInboxView.swift:543`). Revisit only if #889's logs show a real cost.

1. **`.inactive` keeps the socket.** Frames keep arriving for the few seconds a banner or Control Center is up, which is cheaper than a full reconnect.
2. **The background close is silent.** No pill and no advice; screens reconnect on `.active`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `.inactive` (Control Center, a notification banner) causes no close and no reconnect.
- [ ] `.background` causes one silent close, and `.active` one reopen with a new ticket and one handshake.
- [ ] Today's behavior holds: the last screen leaving closes the socket, and retiring the connection still ends everything with `.stale`.
- [ ] Rooms still stop on background, dismissal or socket loss (#533).

## Tests

These fail on today's code unless noted.

- `HermesGatewayTests`, on `BotScriptedSocket`: one background close; no close on `.inactive`.
- `BotConversationTests` and `BotInboxTests`: `.inactive` keeps the connection; `.background` then `.active` reconnects once.
- `BotRoomTests` and `BotRoomManagementTests`: rooms still stop on background, dismissal or socket loss (passes today; must keep passing).
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesGatewayTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomManagementTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotProfileEditorTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotLifecycleTests`

## Mocks

Not required: no visible change.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight) over the tunnel.

1. Open a chat, pull down Control Center, then dismiss it. Expected: no reconnect flash.
2. Mid-turn, pull down Control Center and dismiss it. Expected: the turn's tool rows stay.
3. Go home, wait 2 minutes, and return. Expected: a quiet reconnect.
4. On iPad in split view with the inbox and a chat, background and foreground the app. Expected: one reconnect.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** every Bot screen on iPhone and iPad.
- **Targets:** main app only.
- **Live Activity:** a background close marks the activity stale, as today (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotLiveActivityFeed.swift:100-111`).
- **Push:** unaffected; the relay doesn't depend on the socket.
- **Share extension, notification service, App Intents, deep links:** unchanged.
- **Connection modes:** a clean background close matters most behind the tunnel.

## Preservation

- #825: one socket, one handshake per socket, and each screen's close ends only its own calls.
- #533: rooms stop on background, dismissal or socket loss.
- #574: DEBUG sign-in survives root rebuilds.
- #775: the handshake runs on every new socket.
- #901: frames are still held during a reattach.

## Blockers

#901 (the same recovery and gateway code), set as a GitHub dependency.

## Outside reach

None.

title: refactor(hermes): one conversation engine for Bot Chat and Hermes sessions
body:
Part of #701 (slice 1.1) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #902 · Moved from #700 on 2026-09-28: build it in the same run as #701 slice 1.1, its first production caller, so the engine never sits unused.

## Problem and outcome

#701 moves the main chat onto the Hermes gateway and needs what a Bot Chat already does: attach to a session, replay what was missed, rebuild on a gap, restore open requests, and never resend. That logic lives inside `BotConversation`, a 1,554-line class that also owns things only Bots need:
- the lookup of each bot's one chat by title (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:573-593`)
- mentions, reactions, slash commands, file search, delegated work and chat controls

Its keys also assume one conversation per Profile:
- draft (`:305`), recent transcript (`:216-218`) and attachments (`:203-204`)
- `BotRecentTranscripts`, keyed `.bot(server, connectionID, profile)` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift:332-334`)

After this, a `HermesConversation` engine owns attach, replay and request restore for a `ConversationTarget`:
- `.canonicalChat(profile)`: today's Bot Chat, with the title lookup and the rejection of a changed root.
- `.session(profile, key)`: a stored session, with no title lookup.
- `.new(profile)`: created with `session.create`, and accepting the reduced resume reply for a session that hasn't started yet. That reply carries only `session_id` and `stored_session_id` (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:629-652`), and today it fails the identity checks (`BotConversation.swift:595`, `:730`).

`BotConversation` keeps its Bot features on top of the engine and behaves exactly as it does after #901 and #902.

## Contract

Evidence is pinned to Hermex `699074e7` and hermes-agent `ca678285`.

- **Two ids per session.** The stored key identifies a session. The runtime id keys session-scoped calls and `seq`, changes after a reap, and is never persisted (plan §1.1).
- **The Profile is required.** It goes on every call.
- **Reply shapes.** Live reuse (`tui_gateway/server.py:2876-2915`); cold (`methods_session.py:767-783`); the reduced shape for a new session (`:629-652`).
- **Creating a Bot Chat** stays in `BotCreator.ensureChat`, which adopts an existing chat before creating one and handles 4022 (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotCreator.swift:280-297`).

## Plan

- [ ] **Extract the parts that aren't Bot-specific** into the engine:
  - the generation and owner guard (`BotConversation.swift:641-650`)
  - the recovery skeleton (`:549-635`)
  - replay reconciliation (`:652-690`)
  - snapshot application
  - the safety rules for submit, stop and answer
  - backoff (`:1509-1527`)
  - #901's frame holding and #902's registry hooks

title: feat(notifications): local alerts name the chat, open it, and cover failed runs
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #862

## What changed

On a server without push, the local run alert always read "Hermes response complete", never named the chat, opened nothing when tapped, stacked a new copy every time, and never fired for a failed run.

Decisions applied: #862 Decisions 1-4 and its [decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/862#issuecomment-5879913000); [#855](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/855) D6 and D18.
- `ResponseCompletionOutcome` (`.completed` / `.failed`) replaces `completedNormally`. A stopped run has no case, so it can't alert.
- The alert title is the chat title (through `AgentRunActivitySanitizer.sessionTitle`, fallback "Hermes session"). The body is "Response complete" or "Response failed", the Live Activity's own strings. The identifier and `threadIdentifier` are `run-alert-<16 hex of server_hash>-<sessionID>`, so a newer alert for a chat replaces the older one. `userInfo` carries `session_id`, `server_hash` (SHA-256 of the server URL) and `source: "local"`. It has no `install_hash`, so #653 still holds.
- Tap: `PushAppDelegate` first matches a local alert against the configured servers, then reuses `WebuiPushDestination`, which switches server or waits for sign-in. If the alert's server was removed, the tap only opens the app.
- Chat: `runEndTrigger` bumps once per run that ends completed or failed: on `done`, and on any new ending `finishStream` records (`.error`, a `stream_end` without `done`, `finalizeInactiveStream`, `handleTransportError`). When a reconnect's session load clears the stream, the failure is recorded against the run start captured before the load. The background task stays open until the alert is scheduled. If a newer run in the same chat ends while an older alert is still waiting, the older one is dropped.
- Cold launch: orphans carry their chat title and server. `.complete` and `.failed` alert, `.cancelled` does not. An orphan from another server never alerts from the active server. Neither does one from a build before 1.7.0, which recorded no server.
- New Settings footnote in 17 languages (`needs_review`), and 3 unused keys removed. Updated `multi-server-state-isolation.md` and `push.md`.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air>`, run 1: Policy, Service and Tracker tests, `PushPreviewTests`, `LiveActivityTests`, `PushRegistrationTests`: 117 passed. Run 2, the callers: `ChatViewModelSendTests`, `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests`, `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 288 passed. After the review fixes: `LiveActivityTests`, `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests`, `ChatViewModelSendTests` and the three `ResponseCompletionNotification*` classes: 335 passed. After round 2, the `ResponseCompletionNotification*` classes, `PushRegistrationTests` and `LiveActivityTests`: 105 passed.
- Red on unchanged code: cold launch notified `["s-done"]`, not `["s-done", "s-failed"]`; a dropped connection left `runEndTrigger` at 0, not 1; a bare `stream_end` left it at 3, not 4; the reconciler notified `s-other` and legacy `s-legacy`.
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all extracted keys covered.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (n/a, no server models)

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone
Setup: two unpaired servers, A and B. Turn on Settings → Notifications → Response Complete Alerts. Use prompts that finish within about 20 s.
1. On A, in a chat titled "Deploy notes", send a prompt and lock the phone. Expected: one alert titled "Deploy notes" with the body "Response complete".
2. Send again in the same chat and background the app, then do the same in a second chat. Expected: the newer "Deploy notes" alert replaces the first. The second chat's alert groups separately.

title: fix(chat): a refused steer must not stop the run
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #856

## What changed

When the server refused a steer, Hermex queued the message and called `/api/chat/cancel`. Steer is the default Send While Responding choice, so a mid-run Send could stop the user's run, and on servers using webui's gateway backend every mid-run send did. The "…the current response was stopped" notice showed even when the cancel failed, and the cancel wiped the steer's network error.

Following [#855](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/855) D1/D2 and the [#856 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/856#issuecomment-5879911931), no steer outcome stops the run any more:
- `APIClient.steerChat` returns a non-throwing `ChatSteerOutcome`: `accepted` → delivered, `gateway_steer_queued` → serverQueued, `not_running`/`stream_dead` → runEnded, anything else (null, unknown code, HTTP or network error) → refused. #701 only swaps this mapping.
- Delivered: exact-text echo (#542) plus one "Steering hint delivered." (#326). Staged files ride along as the web UI's attached-files note, then leave the strip and their draft copies are deleted.
- Server-queued: queued with the files that rode along, notice "Queued, sends when this run finishes". Run ended: queued at the front, then the existing `refreshTranscriptIfCompleted` checks `/api/chat/stream/status`. It finishes the run once the saved reply is in the transcript, and the drain sends the message as a normal turn. Otherwise the live SSE ends the run itself, and the message stays queued with the notice until then. Files staged while a steer is in flight stay in the composer.
- Refused: the draft, quotes and files stay. The composer status shows "Couldn't steer" (plus the system reason for transport errors) with Retry, which steers again through `sendDraftMessage(behavior: .steer)`. Typed `/steer x` stays as typed. `lastError` is kept, so an expired login still signs out. A refusal that lands after the run ended goes out as a normal turn instead, or shows as a send error for a network failure.
- Strings: removed "Steer was unavailable…"; added "Couldn't steer" and "Queued, sends when this run finishes" in all 17 locales.

## How it was tested

- Red on unchanged code: 5 new `ChatViewModelSendTests` failed, 15 assertions (each hit `/api/chat/cancel`; lastError was the cancel's -1000, not the steer's -1009). The 4 review-fix tests each failed on the head before their fix: "Couldn't steer" on an idle composer, a later file swept into the queued send, and a run failed early.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid>` on iPhone 17e: ChatViewModelSendTests + ChatStreamCoordinatorTests + SteerMessageTests + APIClientAgentControlTests + BotChatPresentationTests + LocalizationCatalogTests + LiveActivityTests + StreamReconnectContractTests → 406 passed, 1 skipped (no in-process accessibility tree). After the review fix: ChatViewModelSendTests + SteerMessageTests → 231 passed. After the review round: ChatViewModelSendTests + ChatStreamCoordinatorTests + SteerMessageTests → 308 passed. `--repeat 10` on the new steer tests: 60/60, 20/20 and 40/40.
- New: 10 `ChatViewModelSendTests` (refused, network error, gateway-queued, stream_dead, not_running while still active, stream_dead before the reply is saved, a file staged mid-steer, accepted with a file, refused or offline after the run ended), `APIClientAgentControlTests.testSteerOutcomeMapsEveryFallback`, `SteerMessageTests.testSteerEchoWithAttachmentNoteMatchesPersistedSteerRow`.
- `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: covers all 1959 keys. Fallback codes and the note checked against pinned upstream c67fd2dd (`api/streaming.py`, `static/commands.js`).

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))

Settings > Send While Responding = Steer (the default). Tunnel server first, then repeat step 1 on LAN.
1. Start a run that uses several tools. Mid-run, attach a small file, type "also read the attached file", tap Send. Expected: "Steering hint delivered."; composer and attachment strip empty; after the run, one steer row shows the text and the attached-files note.
2. Start another long run. Turn on Airplane Mode, type "hint", tap Send. Expected: no "Response cancelled" or "…was stopped"; "hint" stays; a red status line reads "Couldn't steer" with the offline reason on a second line and a Retry button.
3. During step 2, lock the phone. Expected: the Lock Screen Live Activity stays on running, never cancelled.
4. Airplane Mode off; foreground until the stream reattaches. Expected: the run is still going. Tap Retry. Expected: "Steering hint delivered."; composer empties.
5. Offline mid-run, type `/steer x`, tap Send. Expected: "Couldn't steer"; the composer still reads `/steer x`.
6. Repeat step 2's status line with Larger Text at the largest accessibility size, in dark mode, and with the app language set to Arabic, then Hebrew, then Urdu. Expected: the text wraps, nothing is clipped, and Retry stays tappable at the trailing edge.
7. Start a short run ("say hi"). Tap Send on "follow up" as the last words stream in (retry a few times to land after the run ends). Expected: "follow up" goes out as one new turn; no "Couldn't steer"; the Live Activity ends as complete, not "Response failed".
8. iPad simulator, regular width, over the tunnel: start a long run, turn off the Mac's Wi-Fi, type "hint", tap Send. Expected: the step 2 status line with Retry, laid out cleanly in light and dark.

title: fix(bots): answer connection cards in the shape the host's release takes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #830

## What changed

Answering a connection card (approve a connector row, Skip, or Continue) failed on 0.21.5 hosts. 0.21.5 renamed `connection.respond`'s `session_id` to `owner: {type: "session", session_id}`, and it refuses unknown keys with `4000`. 0.21.4 does the same in reverse, so switching every host to `owner` would break 0.21.4 hosts instead.

Now `HermesGateway.send` passes the `/api/status` version from the last sign-in to `HermesCall.params`. Before 0.21.5 it sends `session_id`; otherwise it sends `owner`. Only the numeric part of the version counts, so `0.21.4+canary…` is treated as 0.21.4. A missing or unreadable version gets `owner`, the pinned shape. The `result` shapes and admission rules are unchanged. `docs/agents/bots.md` records both shapes.

Contract, checked against the upstream `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`: at 0.21.4 (`d337b736`), `ConnectionRespondParams` requires `session_id, op_id, result`. At 0.21.5 (`ca678285`, the pin) it requires `owner, op_id, result`. Both set `additionalProperties: false`. The maintainer's host reports 0.21.5 on its public `/api/status` (read-only `curl`).

Known limit: if a host is upgraded while Hermex stays signed in, Hermex keeps the old version until its next sign-in.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17 Pro Max> --only HermesMobileTests/BotClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesRequestTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests`: 45 passed.
- `--only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests`: 70 passed.
- New `BotClientTests.testConnectionRespondNamesTheSessionTheWayTheHostsReleaseTakesIt` sends a real socket frame for 0.21.4, a 0.21.4 canary, 0.21.5, 0.22.0, a missing version and `dev`. On master the 0.21.5 case fails.
- Manual: not run. The card comes only from upstream's `manage_connections` tool, whose `check_fn` requires the Nous connectors gateway to be enabled and entitled (`tools/connectors/gateway/config.py`). The maintainer's host doesn't have it, so no prompt shows the card. Merged on the contract check and the socket-level test.

title: feat(chat): reconnect when the network returns and say "Waiting for network"
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #869. Stacked on #904; merge after it.

## What changed

Offline for more than a few seconds mid-run, a suspended stream used up its 4 status probes (about 7 s), showed a network error in the composer, and never retried when the network returned. Meanwhile the pill still said "Hermes is working".

- **Monitor**: new `Networking/NetworkPathMonitor.swift` (main app target only), one `@MainActor @Observable` wrapper around `NWPathMonitor` started in `HermesMobileApp.init`. It publishes `isSatisfied` and `changeCount`. Only `.unsatisfied` counts as offline, and unknown counts as online. Repeated identical paths are dropped on the monitor's queue, so they never reach the main actor. The counter moves only when reachability flips or the interfaces change while online.
- **Gate**: `ChatStreamCoordinator` takes `isNetworkAvailable` (defaults to the monitor). While offline, the suspended reconnect, a transient probe failure, and the stale-stream loop send no probe. They park in the new `ActiveStreamRecoveryState.waitingForNetwork`, stay suspended, report no error, and don't spend the budget.
- **Trigger**: `ChatView.onChange(of: changeCount)` → `networkPathDidChange(modelContext:)`. A suspended stream retries through the existing single-flight `reconnectIfNeeded`, so a flapping path joins one attempt. A live stream that was waiting drops back to idle, and the stale loop decides. Errors go through `onAPIError`, the same as the foreground trigger.
- **UI**: `ChatActiveRunStatusKind.waitingForNetwork`, "Waiting for network" (VoiceOver: "Hermes is waiting for the network to return"). The transcript chip shows the same label with a static dot even with Reduce Motion off. Both strings ship in all 17 locales.
- Per the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/869#issuecomment-5879914848): Bots (D3, left for #701), Kanban, the session list, and the extensions are unchanged. Interface changes on a live stream don't force a reconnect (D1).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatStreamCoordinatorTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatActiveRunStatusPolicyTests --only HermesMobileTests/NetworkPathMonitorTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: 101 passed, 0 failed.
- New tests: `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests` `testReconnectWaitsForNetworkWithoutSpendingProbeBudget`, `testTransientFailureWaitsForNetworkWhenThePathDrops`, `testNetworkReturnReconnectsSuspendedStreamOnce`, `testStaleRecoverySkipsProbesWhileOffline`; `ChatActiveRunStatusPolicyTests.testWaitingForNetworkMapsToItsOwnKind`; 5 in `NetworkPathMonitorTests`. The existing tests use an always-online fake.
- Red: against an API skeleton with no behavior, 9 of 10 new tests failed. Examples: `testReconnectWaitsForNetworkWithoutSpendingProbeBudget` gave `("4") is not equal to ("0")` (offline, it spent all 4 probes), and `testNetworkReturnReconnectsSuspendedStreamOnce` gave `("idle") is not equal to ("waitingForNetwork")`.
- Full suite (the pbxproj changed), in 4 chunks: 3,269 passed and 6 failed. The failures were in `BotChatPresentationTests` x3, `StreamingTextFadeTests` x2, and one `StreamReconnectContractTests` timeout on a heavily loaded machine. All passed on focused reruns (39 passed, 1 skipped; 262 passed). `git diff --check` was clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (n/a, no server models)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (n/a, client-only)

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone; iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))

1. iPhone, tunnel server: start a run that works for several minutes and scroll up a little. Turn on Airplane Mode for about 2 minutes, past the tunnel's idle timeout. Expected: the pill reads "Waiting for network" with a static dot, the composer shows no red error, and the Live Activity is marked stale.
2. Turn Airplane Mode off and stay in the app. Expected: within a few seconds the stream reattaches with no backgrounding, the text continues with no duplicates, the pill returns to "Hermes is working · …", and the Live Activity updates again.
3. Tunnel server, mid-run: turn Wi-Fi off so the phone moves to cellular. Expected: the run continues or reattaches on its own.
4. LAN server: start a run, then turn Wi-Fi off. Expected: the existing error shows after about 7 s, not "Waiting for network". Turn Wi-Fi back on. Expected: the stream reattaches without foregrounding.
5. Scroll to the bottom and repeat step 1 briefly. Expected: the transcript chip reads "Waiting for network" with a static dot and no spinner, with Reduce Motion off.
6. Mid-run, open a fork or the file browser over the chat, then toggle Airplane Mode on and off. Go back to the chat. Expected: it shows the current stream with no duplicate text. The hidden parent chat may reattach while covered, as it already does on foreground.
7. Mid-run, start Listen and lock the phone for over 30 s so the background task expires, then toggle Wi-Fi. Expected: audio keeps playing. When the app opens, the stream is current with no duplicates. A reattach while in the background is acceptable.
8. iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) simulator, regular width, tunnel server: start a long run, scroll up, then turn off the Mac's Wi-Fi (and Ethernet) for about 20 s. Expected: the pill in the split-view detail column reads "Waiting for network" with a static dot and fits. At the bottom, the chip reads the same. Turn Wi-Fi back on. Expected: the stream reattaches.

title: feat(notifications): offer notifications once after the first run
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #863

Stacked on #905; merge after it.

## What changed

A new user who starts a long run from the phone and then switches apps never finds out it finished. Hermex only mentions notifications inside Settings, and local alerts are off by default.

Decisions applied: #863 Decisions 1-5 and its [decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/863#issuecomment-5879913192); #855 D7. #769 already has its [pointer comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/769#issuecomment-5879918190) naming the shared flag.
- New `Config/NotificationOffer.swift`. A pure `decide` returns nil once the offer was made, with local alerts on, with iOS permission denied, or when the active server is already paired. It returns `.push` when this build can push and the server has a saved Hermes connection, and `.localAlerts` otherwise. The pairing and connection Keychain reads are lazy, so denied and paired installs skip them. `claim(server:)` sets the per-install `notificationOffer.hasOffered` (shared with #769) before it returns an offer, and leaves it unset if the chat closed meanwhile.
- `ResponseCompletionNotificationService.enable` replaces Settings' private enable. The toggle and the offer's **Notify Me** both call it, so the one-time prompt, the asked-once flag and the preference stay in step.
- ChatView claims the offer in a task beside the send, so it never delays the send haptic. It does this only after `sendStandardMessage` or `sendVoiceNote` started a run, not in `sendDraftMessage`, which steers also reach. The offer is one system alert: **Notify Me** / Not now, or **Open Settings** / Not now.
- `SessionListView` installs an `openNotificationSettings` environment action (a stable reference), so every chat it hosts can open Settings → Notifications: from the list, a new chat, a fork, or Archived Sessions. On compact width it first pops to the list, then opens Settings once the list is back on screen, so a fork or archived chat can't stay on top. `SettingsScrollAnchor.notifications` sits on a wrapper around the push section. `HermexPushSectionView` gains only `startsExpanded`.
- Four new strings in 17 languages. Docs: `multi-server-state-isolation.md` and `push.md`.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air>` with `NotificationOfferTests`, `ResponseCompletionNotificationServiceTests`, `HermexPushProvisioningTests` and `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 54 passed. Full suite, since the pbxproj changed: 3282 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.
- After the review fixes (lazy Keychain reads, the offer off the send path, the compact pop before Settings): `NotificationOfferTests` + `ResponseCompletionNotificationServiceTests`, 22 passed; `SessionNavigationStateTests` + `NotificationOfferTests`, 50 passed. The compact pop is view navigation with no unit seam, so steps 4-6 below check it.
- `ci/check_string_catalog.py` covers all 1960 keys, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Red run against stubs of the new API (it doesn't exist on the base, so there was nothing to compile against without them): 8 of 22 failed. For example, `testOffersPushWhenTheServerCanPair` got `nil`, not `.push`, and `testEnableAsksOnceWhenPermissionWasNeverRequested` got `isEnabled: false`.
- No screenshots: the alert only appears after a message that starts a run, which is a write to the live server that a lane can't make. The physical-iPhone steps below cover it.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (n/a, no server models)

Tap Open Settings. Expected: the chat pops back to the list, then Settings opens, scrolled to Notifications, with the push section expanded and "Turn on notifications…" visible. Nothing changed on the host.

title: feat(chat): show file edits as diffs in tool rows
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #864

## What changed

When the agent edits a file, the tool row doesn't show what changed. An opened `patch` row shows `old_string`/`new_string` as two blobs, the real `diff` in the result shows as uncoloured text (or raw JSON when the webui cuts it at 4,000 characters), and the collapsed row gives no sense of size.

Built per the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/864#issuecomment-5879913574), **Design** pick A (https://945zu9w8e0ol.postplan.dev):
- New pure `ToolCallDiff` resolver for `.write` rows. Sources in order: the result's `diff`, a result that is a unified diff, args `patch`/`diff`, `old_string`/`new_string` (behind a hidden synthetic `@@` header), then `content` (additions only). Args stand in only when the result is missing, cut off, or a success envelope. Failed edits (`is_error`, or a result reporting failure) and no-ops keep today's row. That includes a stored result whose one-line envelope is followed by hermes-agent's subdirectory hints.
- A cut-off source shows no counts, and neither does a `replace_all` args fallback, since one pair would understate the edit. A cut-off source also gets the caption "Partial diff. The server sent only the first part of this edit." Parsed documents live in their own 128-entry `NSCache`; diffs past the chat highlighter's size guards resolve to nothing.
- Collapsed row: `TranscriptLogRowView` gets an optional trailing accessory (default `EmptyView`, so Thinking and Plan rows are unchanged). "+N −M" sits before the chevron, on its own line at accessibility sizes, only once the call succeeded. `DiffCountsLabel.deletions` is optional.
- Opened row: the diff in an inset surface, then remaining Arguments, then Result (unless it was the source or cut off). Honours wrap code lines; caps at 80 lines with Show all / Show first 80 (calls `chatDisclosureToggled()` first). Long-press copy is unchanged.
- Bots: resumed edit rows use the snapshot's original result (`content`, hermes-agent `ca678285` `tui_gateway/session_history.py:239-242`), so they match the live row.
- The caption is in all 17 translations (`needs_review`).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro> --only HermesMobileTests/ToolCallDiffTests --only …/ToolCallSummaryFormatterTests --only …/BotActivityTests --only …/MarkdownDiffFormatterTests --only …/APIClientSessionDetailTests`: 116 passed on the final head.
- Full suite (project.pbxproj changed), all 229 classes in four batches, on c96f2e07 (the last round touched only `ToolCallDiff.swift` and its tests): 3,276 passed, 3 skipped. Three Bot timing tests timed out in batch 1 at load average 39; their classes (`BotArtifactTests`, `BotConversationTests`, `BotChatPresentationTests`) then passed 118/118.
- Red: against a stub resolver, all 13 new tests failed and existing ones passed. The four review-round tests (hint suffix, `is_error`, `replace_all`) each failed on the head before their fix.
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py`: covers all 1959 keys. `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`: no new warnings.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no new models; every result shape parses tolerantly)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (checked against webui `c296673e` and hermes-agent `ca678285`)

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPhone simulator
1. Sessions chat: ask the agent to change one line in a small file. The live `patch` row shows "+1 −1" before the chevron. Tap it: one red and one green line, then Arguments (path, replace_all). No Status line: the webui sends no duration.
2. Pull to reload. The same counts and diff show.
3. Ask for an edit over 4,000 characters. The row shows a diff built from the args, or the Partial diff caption with no counts. Never raw JSON.
4. Ask for a new file with `write_file`. The row shows "+N" only and green lines.
5. Ask for an edit that can't match. No counts, and the error shows in Result. Reload: still no counts, error still visible.

11. Dark mode: tints and the Partial diff caption read clearly. AX3: counts sit on their own line under the file name. VoiceOver: "Updated, App.swift, 3 added, 1 removed, Completed"; diff lines read "added, …" or "removed, …".

title: fix(chat): keep queued messages when leaving a chat mid-run
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #857 · Stacked on #906; merge after it.

## What changed

Messages queued behind a running response lived only in the chat's in-memory queue, so leaving the chat lost them and their files. The pinned "Queued for next turn (#N)." line still came back from the stream snapshot, so the chat said something was queued when nothing was.

Following the [#857 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/857#issuecomment-5879912201) and [#855](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/855) D3:
- **Park on leave (D3):** `ChatView.onDisappear` takes the queue (`takeQueuedMessages()`) before the draft flush and stream suspend, and writes it into the chat's own server+session draft in one synchronous store step. The composer gets the merged text and the queued files too, so a chat covered by Files or a fork shows them on return. The run's end sends nothing.
- **Merge (D1):** `ChatDraftQueueParking.merged` puts queued texts first in queue order, then the draft's own text, joined by a blank line. Quotes stay quotes, and queued files go after the draft's own with duplicate ids removed.
- **Derived receipt (D2):** one line, #856's "Queued, sends when this run finishes", shows while the queue is not empty and never enters the snapshot. The queue, steer and interrupt paths no longer pin a per-message receipt, and the "Queued for next turn (#%lld)." key is removed. Failure and fallback notices still pin (Preserve #326). Handing the queue over unpins the interrupt fallback line. An interrupt whose cancel was in flight during a park reports nothing.
- A chat still on screen when its session is deleted (iPad sidebar) doesn't re-create the draft the delete discarded.
- Adjacent: a drained queued send no longer swaps files staged during its send out of the composer.

Known edges, not fixed: a queued message that fails mid-drain after its chat is gone is lost (out of scope per the decision). The same goes for a steer in flight at leave time that the server answers as server-queued. A send in flight at park time can reappear in the draft next to the parked text (duplicated, not lost). Removing the active server mid-run on iPad parks its queue under the removed server's key; it shows again if that server is re-added.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatDraftStoreTests`: 256 passed, 0 failed. `LocalizationCatalogTests` + `SteerMessageTests`: 24 passed.
- New: `ChatViewModelSendTests` testLeavingChatHandsOverQueuedMessagesInOrder, testReturningToChatDoesNotRestoreQueueReceipt, testInterruptParkedWhileCancelIsInFlightReportsNoQueue, testQueueParkedDuringADrainedSendKeepsItsFilesInTheComposer; `ChatDraftStoreTests` testQueuedMessagesMergeIntoEmptyDraft, testQueuedMessagesMergeBeforeExistingDraftText, testParkingAfterSessionDeleteLeavesNoDraft. The hand-over test also parks the real hand-over into a draft store, so it covers the view model and the store together. Four #856 steer tests and two queue tests now expect `.executed(message: nil)` plus the derived receipt.
- Red: all 7 failed on unfixed code for the intended reason. The reopened chat restored "Queued for next turn (#1)."; the run's end sent the queued message (2 `/api/chat/start` calls, expected 1); the drained send swapped the parked file out of the composer; the refused cancel returned the fallback line after the park; a park after delete re-created the draft.
- No simulator pass: reaching the state needs a running response, which is a live-server write this run doesn't allow.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))

Settings > Send While Responding = Queue; a chat with a long run in progress.
1. Queue "a", then "b" with a photo. Expected: one line above the composer, "Queued, sends when this run finishes".
2. Tap back, reopen the chat. Expected: the composer reads "a", a blank line, "b"; the photo is in the strip; no Queued line; nothing sends when the run ends.
3. Start a run, type "c", queue "d" with a photo, open Files, come back. Expected: "d", a blank line, "c", and the photo; keep typing and nothing is lost.
4. Mid-run with a queued message, open an image full screen and close it. Expected: nothing lost. Either the queue parked into the composer (as in step 3) or the Queued line stays and it sends at run end; note which.
5. Queue a message on server A, switch to server B and back. Expected: the draft shows only in A's chat, and B's chats are unchanged.
6. iPad, regular width: queue a message, pick another chat in the sidebar, come back. Expected: the draft holds it, under the original chat only.
7. iPad: mid-run with a queued message, delete the open chat from the sidebar. Expected: the detail column clears with no error, and no other chat shows the queued text.
