title: feat(chat): transcript polish — reading width, table edge fade, tool-row entrance, "Forked from" row
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #873

## What changed

Four transcript gaps: lines run ~900 pt wide on iPad and iPhone landscape, wide tables don't show they scroll, new tool rows pop in, and a forked chat doesn't say where it came from. Built per the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/873#issuecomment-5879915918), one commit per slice. No mocks: the issue decided layout and motion, and (d) copies the turn-fold row.

- **(a) Reading width.** `ChatReadingWidth` caps the transcript column at 768 pt and centres it; the ScrollView stays full width. The Sessions composer and status stack cap at 768 + 2×16 so their edges line up. Bot Chat and Bot rooms use the same rule. iPhone portrait is unchanged (the cap only binds above 800 pt).
- **(b) Table edge fade.** `ComposerToolbarEdgeFades` moves unchanged to `HorizontalOverflowEdgeFades` with a `horizontalOverflowFades(.mask | .overlay(Color))` modifier. The toolbar keeps `.mask` (Preserve #360). Tables use `.overlay`: an 18 pt gradient into the host colour, only on an edge that hides content, no offscreen pass. The colour is the env value `markdownTableEdgeFadeColor` (default `systemBackground`; Memory and Kanban card detail set `secondarySystemGroupedBackground`; Bot room bubbles and translucent local cards set nil). Code blocks are unchanged.
- **(c) Tool-row entrance.** The newest row of a live `ToolActivityGroupView` gets `ChatMotion.freshRowTransition`. `ToolActivityEntrance.animatesNewestRow` turns it off for settled groups, under Reduce Motion, and while a reattached stream replays (`ChatViewModel.isActiveStreamReplayConnection`), per the decision.
- **(d) "Forked from" row.** `ForkOrigin.resolve` returns a value only for `session_source == "fork"` with a `parent_session_id` (upstream `/api/session/branch` stamps both). The title comes from the new `CacheStore.cachedSession(id:serverURL:in:)`, which never crosses servers; archived parents are never cached, so they read "Forked from another chat". A tap pushes the parent, fetching it first when uncached; a 404 or 409 `session_profile_mismatch` shows "The original chat is no longer on this server." Four strings in 17 languages; "Fork" added to `CONTEXT.md`.

## How it was tested

- Full suite on 3499566 (project.pbxproj changed): 3281 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped. New or changed classes: `ChatReadingWidthTests` 5, `HorizontalOverflowEdgeFadesTests` 6 (moved), `ChatTranscriptRowEntryTests` 8 (4 new), `ForkOriginTests` 7, `CacheStoreTests`, `ComposerToolbarScrollerTests` 7, and `ChatViewModelSendTests.testLoadForkParent…`.
- The review fix (an expired-row lookup test and an archived-parent test instead of a hand-built archived row) on the final head: `--only CacheStoreTests --only ForkOriginTests`, 33 passed.
- Review round 1 (the row now also shows on an empty fork; view only): built, and `--only ForkOriginTests --only ChatReadingWidthTests --only ChatTranscriptRowEntryTests` gave 20 passed.
- Red: the new tests don't compile against master (`cannot find 'ChatReadingWidth' / 'ToolActivityEntrance' / 'ForkOrigin' in scope`). The 409 assertion failed before its fix: `"Server returned HTTP 409: …" is not equal to "The original chat is no longer on this server."`

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no new fields; `session_source` and `parent_session_id` were already optional)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (webui pin `c67fd2dd`: `api/routes.py` branch handler, `api/models.py` `compact()`)

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))
1. (a) iPhone portrait: Sessions chat, composer, Bot Chat and a Bot room look exactly as on master. Rotate to landscape: on a Pro Max-size phone the transcript and composer are centred and capped at about 768 pt with edges lined up; on smaller phones the column already fits under the cap and looks as on master (iPhone Air: about 745 pt). Jump-to-latest stays centred; same in Bot Chat and a Bot room. Repeat at an accessibility text size (20 pt padding).
2. (a) iPad simulator: open a long chat, hide the sidebar. Column and composer are centred at about 768 pt, edges aligned; user bubbles stay trailing. Show the sidebar: the column fills the narrower pane. Repeat in Bot Chat and a Bot room.
3. (b) Ask for an 8-column table. The trailing edge fades; scroll right: both fade; at the end only the leading edge fades. A narrow table shows no fade. The composer toolbar fade looks as on master.
4. (b) Settings → Right-to-Left Chat Layout on: the table fade is solid at the screen edge, never a band 18 pt in. With the device language set to Arabic, check the composer toolbar fade the same way.
5. (b) Dark mode, wide table in the Skill linked-file sheet, Bot delegated-work sheet, a Kanban card detail and a Memory row: no visible band against the background.
6. (c) Ask for a task with 5+ tools. Each new row fades in over about 0.2 s; the first call's group appears without a fade. Background mid-run and return, and cold-reopen a running chat with no partial reply on screen: replayed rows don't fade. Reduce Motion on: no fades. Repeat in Bot Chat.
7. (d) Fork From Here on a message: the fork's first row reads "Forked from <title>" with a branch icon and a chevron. Tap: the original opens; Back returns to the fork. `/branch test` in another chat shows the same row. A normal chat shows no row.
8. (d) From step 7, in the parent pushed on top of the original, type a draft, go Back twice: the original's transcript is current and its draft is intact.
9. (d) Archive a fork's parent, reopen the fork: the row reads "Forked from another chat" and still opens it. Delete the parent, tap: the error shows and the app stays on the fork. A fork with no messages (`POST /api/session/branch` with `keep_count: 0` on a disposable chat) shows the row above the empty state, and it opens the parent.
10. (d) VoiceOver on the row reads "Forked from …, button" with the hint "Opens the original chat."

title: feat(chat): choose Queue, Steer or Stop & send per message
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #858 · Stacked on #913; merge after it.

## What changed

During a run, what Send does was one global setting. Picking something else for one message meant a Settings trip or a slash command, and Send always drew `arrow.up` and read "Send", even when a tap would steer or stop the run.

Per the [#858 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/858#issuecomment-5879912390) and [#855](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/855) D4:
- **Send button:** `ChatComposerSendButton` models the trailing circle. Mid-run with text it shows the Settings default's symbol and VoiceOver label ("Steer active response", "Send after response", "Stop and send") through one computed `systemName`, which #872 animates. Idle it is the plain arrow; with an empty draft it stays Stop (Preserve #360).
- **Long-press (Decision 2):** a timer-driven `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)` beside the Button, as the mic does, keeping `.chatTactile` and `.disabled`. A 0.5 s hold opens the card in the existing keyboard-retaining overlay with Steer, Queue, Stop and send (Decision 3), and the hold's release never sends. VoiceOver gets a named action per choice. The card closes when the run ends or Send turns into Stop or is disabled. Sessions keep Steer with files staged, since #856 sends them with the steer as a note.
- **Shared card (Decision 1):** `BotSendChoiceView` moves to `ChatComposerPresentation.swift` as `SendChoiceCard` over a two-property `SendChoice` protocol that `BotPromptMode` and `StreamingSendBehavior` adopt. Bots keep their call site and still hide Steer with attachments (Preserve #616).
- `StreamingSendBehavior` gets localized titles and Bots' symbols (`stop.circle` for Stop and send, Decision 4). ChatView sends picks through #856's `sendDraftMessage(behavior:)`, so the receipt matches; Command-Return still uses the default.
- Settings footnote "Long-press Send to choose for one message." in all 17 languages (Decision 5). `docs/agents/bots.md` describes the shared card instead of the old native menu.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerSendGateTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: 56 passed, 1 skipped (the existing no-accessibility-tree skip). After the review fixes, the first two classes: 51 passed, 1 skipped.
- New in `ChatComposerSendGateTests`: testRunningSendShowsDefaultBehaviorGlyphAndLabel, testRunningSendOffersEveryChoiceAndIdleOrStopOffersNone, and for the hold's release-swallow model (`ChatComposerSendHold`) testHoldReleaseIsDroppedAndQuickTapActs and testClosingTheCardAfterLiftingOffSendKeepsTheNextActivation. `BotChatPresentationTests.testBusyChoicesDropSteerWhenTheDraftHasAttachments` is unchanged and green.
- Red: the two button tests failed against a stub of today's button (15 assertion failures), e.g. `("arrow.up") is not equal to ("arrow.turn.up.right")`. The lift-off test failed against the pre-fix hold rule: "an activation after the card closed".
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 1959 extracted keys are in the catalog. No project file change.
- The press gesture itself was not run: reaching mid-run is a live-server write this run doesn't allow. The Manual test covers it.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))

Settings > Send While Responding = Steer; a chat with a long run in progress.
1. Settings > Interaction. Expected: "Long-press Send to choose for one message." under the picker.
2. Type "x" in the collapsed pill, then in the expanded composer. Expected: Send shows the Steer arrow, and a quick tap steers once with no card. Idle, a quick tap sends once.
3. Type "x" and hold Send for half a second, with the keyboard up and again with it down. Expected: the card opens above Send without covering it, the keyboard stays as it was, and lifting sends nothing.
4. Pick Queue. Expected: "x" is queued, not steered, and Settings still says Steer.
5. Hold Send until the card opens and keep it open until the run ends. Expected: the card closes and nothing is sent.
6. VoiceOver on, text typed mid-run, focus Send. Expected: it reads "Steer active response", and the actions rotor lists Steer, Queue, Stop and send.
7. VoiceOver off: hold Send until the card opens, slide off the button, lift, and pick Queue. Turn VoiceOver on, type "y" mid-run and double-tap Send. Expected: "y" steers.
8. Bot Chat, on a working bot, with a photo staged: tap Send. Expected: the same card without Steer; with no photo, Steer is listed.
9. iPad, regular width with the sidebar: hold Send mid-run. Expected: the card anchors at the trailing edge by Send. Command-Return on a hardware keyboard steers with no card.

title: feat(chat): open web links in an in-app Safari sheet
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #866. Applies the [2026-09-28 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/866#issuecomment-5879914240): every Markdown screen gets the sheet, Universal Links always use it, it's a `.sheet`, and the handler lives in `TranscriptLinksModifier`. Preserves #718, #402 and #507.

## What changed

Tapping a web link in a chat left Hermex for Safari (or whichever app claims the link), and going to the background can suspend a streaming reply. Most other Markdown screens had no link handler at all.

- `InAppBrowserPolicy.opensInApp`: true only for `http`/`https` (any case) with a host. `mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`, `file:` and app schemes still go to the system.
- `SafariView` wraps `SFSafariViewController` with its defaults. Its delegate clears the sheet item when the controller's own Done/Close button closes it.
- `TranscriptLinkRouter`: the screen's handler returns `OpenURLAction.Result?`, where `nil` means "not mine". The pure `decision(for:hostResult:)` picks the screen's result, then the in-app browser for web links, then the system. It stays one stable router in the modifier's `@State` (#718), and the modifier owns the `.sheet(item:)`, so a screen already in a sheet presents from its own level.
- Sessions: `handleTranscriptLink` returns `nil` for anything that isn't a file; workspace file links still open the source viewer (#402).
- Bot Chat: one `.transcriptLinks()` on the transcript, so a page opened from a streaming reply stays open when the reply settles into its own row. Each row checks artifact links first (#507) and hands the rest to it. The connection card's "Open link" now calls `UIApplication.shared.open`, so it still leaves for the browser.
- `.transcriptLinks()` on Bot rooms, delegated-work results, Memory, Skill detail and linked file, Kanban card detail and file preview.
- The link preview's VoiceOver hint reads "Opens the web page" in all 17 translations.
- Still leave the app on purpose: the tip jar, Rate Hermex, report links and the Bot connection "Open link".

## How it was tested

All on iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0 (`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only …`). `git diff --check` is clean.

## Linked issue

Fixes #872 · Stacked on #916; merge after it.

## What changed

Three rough edges in the composer: Send and Stop snapped between glyphs, autocomplete picks gave no feedback, and in iPhone landscape the editor grew to 160 pt and hid the transcript. One commit per slice, per the [#872 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/872#issuecomment-5879915664) and [#855](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/855) D12/D17:
- **Morph:** the Sessions circle is still #858's single `Image(systemName: sendButton.systemName)`, now with `.contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .symbolEffect(.replace))`. Stop morphs to and from the Send While Responding default's glyph (the plain arrow when idle). The Bot room button gets the same. Actions, colours, the progress branch and VoiceOver labels are unchanged. Bot Chat's two separate buttons are out of scope (Decision 1).
- **Haptic:** `ChatHaptics.autocompleteAccepted` plays `.selection` behind the app's haptics setting. Sessions play it for every `/` row (a new `pickCompletion`) and for file and folder picks (Decision 2); Bot Chat for bot, file and skill picks; Bot rooms for mention picks. Dismissing the `/` panel still calls `applyCompletion("")` and plays nothing. No extra press feedback on rows.
- **Landscape cap:** a pure `ComposerTextInputHeight.expanded(measured:verticalSizeClass:)` gives `max(72, measured)` in regular or nil height (today's rule) and 72 pt in compact height (Decision 3). All three composers share it (Decision 4); iPad is always regular. The 72 pt minimum stays (Preserve #360).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatHapticsTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerTextInputHeightTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerSendGateTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerChipPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerFocusTransitionTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`: 71 passed, 1 skipped (the existing no-accessibility-tree skip). `git diff --check` clean.
- New: `ChatHapticsTests.testAutocompleteAcceptedPlaysOneSelectionTick`, the disabled-setting case, and `ComposerTextInputHeightTests` (regular, compact, nil), which lives in `ComposerChipTests.swift` so the project file is untouched.
- Red: the haptic tests failed to build ("Type 'ChatHaptics' has no member 'autocompleteAccepted'"). The height rule extracted with today's behaviour failed only the compact case: `("120.0") is not equal to ("72.0")`, `("160.0") is not equal to ("72.0")`.
- The morph and the haptics were not run: the morph needs a live run (a server write this run doesn't allow) and the simulator plays no haptics. The Manual test covers them.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPhone simulator, iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))

1. iPhone, Sessions chat: send a message. Expected: arrow, then spinner, then Stop, with no morph at send. Mid-run, type a letter: Stop morphs to the default's glyph (e.g. the Queue glyph if Queue is the default). Delete it: back to Stop. When the run ends: Stop morphs to the arrow. VoiceOver still reads "Send" or "Stop response".
2. Turn on Reduce Motion and repeat step 1. Expected: every glyph change is instant.
3. Bot room: send to a bot. Expected: Send morphs to Stop when a bot starts, and back when it finishes; instant with Reduce Motion.

5. Bot Chat: pick a bot after `@`, a file, and a skill after `/`. Bot room: pick a mention. Expected: one tick each.
6. Settings > Haptics off, repeat steps 4 and 5. Expected: no ticks.
7. iPhone landscape: focus the Sessions composer and paste 10 lines. Expected: the editor stays about 3 lines (72 pt) tall and scrolls inside. Also check the issue's goal, that the caret, the Send row and the transcript clear the keyboard. On the iPhone 17e simulator they don't (see Screenshots). Repeat in Bot Chat and a Bot room.
8. In portrait, with a long draft and the caret at the end, rotate to landscape. Expected: the editor shrinks to 72 pt and the caret is visible (or becomes visible on the next keystroke).
9. Rotate back to portrait. Expected: the editor grows 72 to 160 pt, then scrolls.

title: feat(sessions): undo archive from a toast
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #865

## What changed

Archiving a session from the list takes one tap, and there was no way to undo it from there. The list's archive also ignored the response, so a 200 with `ok: false` or an `error` counted as success.

- `SessionMutator`: `archive` and the new `unarchive` share `setArchived`, which throws on a non-empty `error` (shown as written) or `ok: false`. A refused archive shows the existing "Session Action Failed" alert and no toast. New key "The server could not archive this session." in all 17 locales.
- `SessionListViewModel.unarchive` has the same shape as `archive`. The per-session mutation guard means a double tap sends one `archived: false` request, and the reload that follows puts the row back in its old place.
- New reusable `Features/Shared/ActionToast.swift`. `ActionToastState` holds one toast; `show` replaces it; it leaves after 4 s (the sleeper is injected). Under VoiceOver it never auto-dismisses, adds a "Close" control, and takes focus. `ActionToastView` is a glass capsule. At accessibility sizes it becomes a card with Undo below the message. With Reduce Motion it only fades.
- `SessionListView` shows "Archived · Undo" 10 pt above the Chat button, as wide as the column, in the iPhone list and the iPad sidebar. `SessionListArchiveToastRoute` picks the screen when the reply lands. The toast shows where the row was swiped (the list or Scheduled) if the user is still there, otherwise on the other session screen, otherwise nowhere. An older archive's reply never replaces a newer one's toast. Undo unarchives, reports failures through `handleLastError`, and plays the archive haptic. It does not reopen a chat. The toast state lives in the server-keyed view and is dismissed on disappear.

Decision: [#865 comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/865#issuecomment-5879913910). `GitActionToastOverlay` is untouched (Decision 7).
**Design:** pick A, a glass capsule above the Chat button: https://qne3lf9w61ov.postplan.dev

- Red: on master, `testArchiveOkFalseResponseIsNotTreatedAsSuccess` failed on all three assertions: `{"ok": false}` counted as success, no error was set, and the list reloaded. `ActionToastStateTests`, the two unarchive tests and the route tests can't compile on master.
- No screenshots. The toast only appears after a real archive, which is a live-server write this run doesn't make.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone
Device: iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))

1. iPhone: swipe a session and tap Archive. Expected: the row leaves, and "Archived · Undo" appears 10 pt above the Chat button, as wide as the list. The Chat button doesn't move.
2. Tap Undo. Expected: the session is back in its old place and the toast leaves. Archive it again and wait. Expected: the toast leaves after about 4 s, and the session is under Archived Sessions.
3. Archive from the long-press menu, then archive two sessions quickly. Expected: the same toast, then one toast for the second archive. The first session is in Archived.
4. Open Scheduled (View all) and archive a row. Expected: the toast slides in at the bottom of that screen, clear of the search field and the home indicator. Go back and archive a list row. Expected: that toast also animates in. Check both for a toast that just pops in.
5. Over the tunnel, archive on Scheduled and tap Back right away. Expected: the toast shows on the list. Reopening Scheduled shows no old toast. Archive two list rows quickly. Expected: Undo restores the second one.

title: perf: signposts on hot paths and a debug hitch meter
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #870

## What changed

We had no way to see which step of a session open or a streamed reply takes the time. There was one `OSSignposter` in the app (the review diff), no hitch meter, and the debug launch switches weren't written down anywhere.

- `PerformanceSignposts.swift` (every build) adds one signposter: subsystem is the bundle ID, category is `Performance`. It has six intervals, and their metadata is integers only, marked `.public`: `Session Open`, `Transcript Apply`, `Markdown Parse`, `Stream Batch Apply`, `Cache Read`, `Cache Write`. `Session Open` begins in `startOpeningSession`, so taps and keyboard opens both count ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/870#issuecomment-5879915065)). It ends in `ChatView` one main-queue turn after the transcript first has messages, or when the initial load comes back empty. An open that fails before a chat shows ends with no metadata. A small `@MainActor` holder matches the end to its begin by session ID and never emits the ID. A new open ends any unfinished one first.
- `HitchMeter.swift` is entirely inside `#if DEBUG`. A `CADisplayLink` in `.common` mode feeds a pure `HitchAccumulator`, which counts a frame as a hitch when it is more than 1.5× late. An overlay shows ms/s, the hitch count and Hz. It updates at most every 0.5 s, takes no touches, and VoiceOver skips it. It pauses while the app is in the background, and it is attached only when the app is launched with `--hitch-meter`.
- `ChatMarkdownView` now builds `MarkdownContent` itself, so the parse can be timed. `Markdown(_: String)` does exactly the same thing internally.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` gets a "Launch arguments and profiling" section. It lists the three launch flags and the `HERMEX_DEV_*` variables, and shows how to record the signposts in Xcode and with `xctrace`.
- I didn't touch any file that the benchmark scripts compile.

## How it was tested

- Red: `HitchMeterTests` against unchanged code fails to compile with `cannot find 'HitchAccumulator' in scope`.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro> --only HermesMobileTests/HitchMeterTests`: 4/4 passed. After the review fixes, `--only HitchMeterTests --only CacheStoreTests --only SessionListMutationTests`: 108 passed.
- Full suite, because `project.pbxproj` changed: 3269 total, 3266 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped.
- `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` and `scripts/benchmark-math-formatting` both build and run. `ci/check_string_catalog.py` passes. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Session Open trace: I ran `xctrace record` on the simulator with a signed Debug build and opened a cached session (read-only). The export shows all six intervals under the app's subsystem, category `Performance`, with `Session Open` at `messages=19`. The export is in the evidence comment below.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)

1. iPhone, Instruments (Time Profiler plus `os_signpost`, filtered to category `Performance`): open a chat and send one message that streams a reply. Expected: `Stream Batch Apply` intervals with `mutated=1` during the reply, plus `Markdown Parse` rows with `chars=`.

Local session search needed the words in exact order, "2m ago" row labels only updated when something else re-rendered the row, and iPad keyboard users had no way to jump between chats.

title: feat(chat): fold long user messages
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #871

## What changed

A long user message (a pasted log, a spec, a long `>` quote) always drew at full height, so the reader scrolled past a wall of their own text to reach the reply. Sessions, Bot Chat and Bot rooms share this `MessageBubbleView` bubble.

- New `UserBubbleFoldPolicy`: a cheap `mayFold` pre-filter (hard lines plus one line per 18 UTF-8 bytes, scaled by body size, sized for capitals in the narrowest 228 pt column), then a TextKit 1 `lineCount` capped at 9 lines. Over 8 lines folds to 6.
- `MessageBubbleView`: only candidates read their row width (`onGeometryChange`) and re-measure on a new width, text or Dynamic Type size, so scrolling never measures. A stale measurement never folds.
- Folded: `.lineLimit(6)`, a one-line gradient into the solid bubble colour, and "Show more ⌄" / "Show less ⌃" at the bottom-leading edge. The toggle calls `chatDisclosureToggled()` and flips state with no animation, like the diff block's Show all.
- Unchanged: VoiceOver reads the full text and the toggle is its own button; context-menu Copy reads `message.content`; `.textSelection(.enabled)` stays (in the simulator a long-press opens the message menu, whose Copy gave the full text).
- "Show more" / "Show less" in all 17 languages (needs_review). Two new files in project.pbxproj.

title: perf(chat): put limits on the transcript image caches
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #867 (part of #855). Applies the [decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/867#issuecomment-5879914476): one shared 48 MB / 150-image cache, no clear on sign-out, fallback aspect-fit to 512 px; Preserve #545 and #86.

## What changed

The two transcript thumbnail caches (`AttachmentImageCache`, `TranscriptMediaImageCache`) were unbounded dictionaries: process-wide, never shrinking, deaf to memory warnings, and able to keep a full-size image when downsampling failed (`?? data`). The attachment cache also re-ran `previewData` on its actor.

- New `actor TranscriptImageCache` replaces both: an `NSCache<NSString, UIImage>` with `totalCostLimit` 48 MB, `countLimit` 150, and cost = decoded bytes. In-flight de-duplication is unchanged.
- Loads run in `Task.detached`, off the actor. `thumbnail(from:)` decodes with `UIImage(data:)`, then `preparingForDisplay()` (already ≤ 512 px) or `preparingThumbnail(of:)` aspect-fit to 512 px. A small image `preparingForDisplay()` can't pre-decode shows undecoded (`preparingForDisplay() ?? image`, the maintainer's [#867 alt3](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/867) pick); any other failure returns nil, so the row shows its existing fallback glyph, and isn't cached. `testSmallImagesInUnusualFormatsStillShow` pins 16-bit gray PNG and CMYK JPEG; the simulator pre-decodes both, so there is no red run (the refusal is device-only).
- One memory-warning observer, registered in `init`, calls `removeAllObjects()`; loads in flight finish normally. The second `previewData` pass is gone.
- `AttachmentImageCacheKey` / `TranscriptMediaImageCacheKey` stay and gain `cacheKey` (`attachment|<len>|<namespace>|<path>`, `media|<len>|<namespace>|<id>`): the kind prefix keeps the two apart, the byte-length prefix fixes the namespace boundary. `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` names the new cache and key.
- Surfaces: webui chats and archived sessions, main app target only. Bot Chat, Bot rooms and cached history are not affected, although the decision comment expected them to be: they render `MessageBubbleView` with `textOnly: true` and no image loaders.

body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #874 (part of #855). Applies the [decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/874#issuecomment-5879916135) (#855 D14).

## What changed

Once push was on, users had no way to check that it worked, and when the relay was switched off (#834) Hermex said "Could not reach this Hermes host", which sent people to debug a host that was fine.

- **Button:** Settings → Notifications on a push-paired server has "Send Test Notification" and a footnote saying it rings every iPhone paired with the host and doesn't test the host → relay leg. It reads "Sending…" while running (no spinner) and is disabled while any step runs, when Reply Notifications are off, or when iOS notifications are off.
- **Relay call:** `PushRelayClient.sendTestNotification(pairing:)` posts one `reply` to the existing `POST /installs/<key>/notify` with exactly the strict schema's ten keys: a new `event_id` per tap, fixed `thread_id`/`collapse_id` (a new banner replaces the last), `source: other` (a tap only opens the app). One request, no retry. The URL and key are never logged.
- **Sealing:** `PushPreview.seal` (app target only) seals "Hermex test notification" with the pairing's keys and the AAD `open` uses (now `PushPreviewKeys.previewAAD`); the notification service opens it unchanged.
- **Results:** any 200 (including `deduplicated`) is delivered. `apns_rejected`, busy codes, a non-JSON refusal (#834), any other answer and no answer each get their own message under one title, "Test notification failed", in the existing red row. None blames the Hermes host. The next action or leaving Settings clears the result.

title: chore(ci): build with the same Xcode locally, on CI, and for release
body:
## Problem

CI and local development build with different Xcode versions, so some failures only appear on CI, late.

- `pr-ci.yml` pins Xcode 26.6 and tests on the iOS 26.5 simulator ("Match the last validated hosted toolchain").
- The maintainer's Mac, and every agent working on it, builds with Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), mostly on iOS 27 simulators. `release-candidate-testflight.yml` uses the `macos-26` runner's default Xcode.

## What it cost in the epic-855 merge walk (2026-09-29)

- After #908 and #905 both landed, Xcode 26.6 could no longer type-check ChatView's main modifier chain ("unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time"). Xcode 27 builds it fine locally, so it showed up only in #905's CI after a rebase. The fix split the chain (in #905).
- #917's link-reader regression reproduced on the iOS 26.5 runtime (the one CI tests on), not on local iOS 27 runs. It kept `master` red for about 3 hours (fixed in #929).

## Options

- **A. Move CI (and the release workflow) to Xcode 27**, if the hosted `macos-26` image offers it, and keep testing on an iOS 26.x simulator runtime too, since the app supports iOS 18 and later.
- **B. Keep Xcode 26.6 on CI** and make the local pre-merge check use it. This Mac has no admin rights, so installing a second Xcode may need IT.

Recommendation: **A**, after checking which Xcode versions the hosted image provides. Building locally, on CI and for release with one compiler removes a whole class of "green locally, red on CI" failures. The iOS 26.x runtime keeps the OS coverage that caught #917.

## Acceptance

- One Xcode version is written down for local work, CI and release builds, and the pins agree.
- CI still runs the suite on an iOS 26.x simulator.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` names the version and how to pick it locally.

title: feat(push): restart Hermes from the phone after a plugin update
body:
## Problem

After a hermex-push plugin update, the new code only runs once the Hermes dashboard restarts. #851 ends in a "Restart Hermes to finish" state that asks the user to restart `hermes dashboard` on the host by hand. Hermex users run Hermes on remote machines, so a manual restart is a real dead end.

## What exists at the pin (hermes-agent `ca678285`, 0.21.5)

- Plugin API routes mount once, at dashboard import (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:1001`), and the plugin's hooks for Bot turns run in that same process.
- `POST /api/gateway/restart` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/actions.py:139`) restarts only the messaging gateway, not the dashboard.
- `POST /api/hermes/update` (`actions.py:219`) updates Hermes itself. It isn't a restart: manually started dashboards are stopped and not restarted because Hermes doesn't know their launch arguments (`hermes_cli/dashboard_procs.py:574-595`). The phone would lose the host.
- No route restarts or reloads the dashboard.

## Proposal

- A hermex-push plugin route, for example `POST /api/plugins/hermex-push/restart`, that restarts its own dashboard process. Re-executing with the process's own argv sidesteps the "unknown launch arguments" problem.
- #851's "Restart Hermes to finish" state gets a "Restart Hermes" button that calls it, waits for the host to return, then re-reads pairing.
- Ship it in the next plugin version. Hosts on older plugins still need one manual restart, because the route only exists once loaded. So the sooner it ships, the fewer manual restarts users ever do.
- File an upstream hermes-agent request for a supported dashboard restart or in-place plugin reload. If it lands, prefer it over the plugin route.

## Questions to settle before building

- Does a re-exec behave under each launcher: Hermes Desktop, launchd, systemd, a terminal? Verify on each before shipping. A bad restart leaves the phone unable to reach the host.
- What confirmation copy is needed? Restarting interrupts running Bot turns.
- Should it live here or in #710 (companion plugin routes)?

## Out of scope

- Changing #851's update flow beyond adding the button.
- Using `/api/hermes/update` as a restart.

Follows up #851 (decision 2026-09-29). Filed by Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code) for the maintainer.

## What changed

Three Bot sign-in failures sent the user to the wrong fix. Cloudflare Access redirecting `/api/status` to its login page, or answering with its own 401 page, read as "isn't a Hermes dashboard". A host with only browser (OIDC) sign-in read as "does not support Bot chat". A refused `/api/ws` upgrade after a good sign-in read as "Couldn't reach…", and the inbox and chat kept retrying it.

- `BotFailure` gains `.blocked`, `.browserSignIn` and `.upgradeRefused(Int)` with the issue's approved hostless copy, so the form, inbox, chat, room and push setup show the same words.
- `HermesConnection`: every request goes through `exchange`, which throws `.blocked` when the final reply came from another host. Only the host is compared, like the status probe ([Decision 2026-09-29](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/880#issuecomment-5902966584)). On `/api/status`, a JSON-object 401 (the webui) stays `.notDashboard` and any other 401 is `.blocked`.
- Status gate: `auth_required` with no `basic` provider throws `.browserSignIn` before the password goes out. #708 replaces this branch. `auth_required: false` stays `.unsupported` (Decision 4).
- `NativeBotSocket.receive` maps a refused handshake through `BotFailure(upgradeStatus:)`. A 101 maps to nothing, so a `URLError` on an open socket is never wrapped. A 408, 429 or 5xx becomes `.rejected`, which still retries quietly. Any other status becomes `.upgradeRefused`.
- `BotInbox.isRetryable` treats the three new cases as permanent. Push setup shows the `.blocked` and `.browserSignIn` copy. The three strings are added in all 17 languages (`needs_review`), and `docs/agents/bots.md` names the new cases.

## How it was tested

- Red: stubbed cases, behavior unchanged, run `20260929-224742-tr1boki7`: 175 passed, 8 failed. Example: `testAnAccessProxyRedirectIsBlockedBeforeThePasswordGoesOut`: `.notDashboard` is not equal to `.blocked`, and the other seven new assertions failed the same way.
- Green: `scripts/test-sim <17e> --only` BotClientTests, BotConnectionAdviceTests, BotInboxTests, BotConversationTests, HermexPushProvisioningTests, LocalizationCatalogTests, HermesConnectionTests, HermesGatewayTests, HermesAgentFixtureTests, BotHostStatusTests, BotConnectionSetupTests: **238 passed** at 90785e80. After review fixes, BotClientTests, HermexPushProvisioningTests, HermesGatewayTests, BotInboxTests, BotConversationTests, BotConnectionAdviceTests and LocalizationCatalogTests: **201 passed**. `git diff --check` is clean.
- `testANativeSocketNamesARefusedUpgradeButNotALaterDrop` drives the real socket over loopback: a 403 upgrade throws `.upgradeRefused(403)`, and a 101 upgrade followed by a drop keeps its own error. It fails with the mapping removed.
- `HermesConnectionTests.testACrossOriginRedirectDropsTheHeadersBeforeTheRelay` now expects `.blocked`. It still asserts that headers are stripped on the hop and that no login is sent.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator
1. iPhone, Bots gear → Hermes connection: Connect with the tunnel address. It signs in as before. Then try the webui address: it still says "… isn't a Hermes dashboard". Cancel.
2. iPhone: open the Bots inbox and a chat, background the app past the tunnel's idle timeout, then return. Both reconnect quietly, with no refused-connection or Cloudflare Access message.
3. iPhone, Settings → Hermes connection and push setup's sign-in: Connect with the tunnel address. Both sign in without the Cloudflare Access copy.
4. iPhone, only if a Cloudflare Access hostname or a proxy that refuses `/api/ws` is available: the Access host shows "Something in front of Hermes…". The proxy shows "Hermes accepted the sign-in, but the live connection was refused…" with Reconnect, and it does not retry.

title: fix(bots): show why a Bot turn failed
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #878

## What changed

A failed Bot turn showed only the Sad title face, so the user couldn't tell a rate limit from a bad key, a billing wall or a host crash, and didn't know whether to wait, retry or fix something on the Mac.

- `HermesTurnOutcome` (Networking/Hermes, reusable by #701) tolerantly decodes what the host already sends: the retained failure in `session.resume` `inflight` (`error`, `error_surface`, `recoverable`) and the live-only `message.complete` fields (`billing.billing_url`, https only; `failure_reason`; `warning`).
- `BotConversation.turnFailure` replaces `turnFailed` and is derived from every snapshot; the Sad face and the Live Activity failed/cancelled state read `turnFailure != nil`, unchanged. `turnNotice` holds the billing link and warning; both survive suspend and reconnect, clear on `message.start`, the next accepted send or a new turn, and are never cached.
- `BotTurnOutcomeRow` sits under the live reply, before the plan and request card: a Hermex title (host sentence, then a custom endpoint, then code, then layer, else "The turn failed"), the raw error (monospace, 4 lines, selectable), "Limit resets at 14:05" while ahead, Retry or "Open billing page" (Safari), and a "Reply shown but not saved" block with the host's warning verbatim.
- Retry is `HermesCall.promptRewind`: one `prompt.submit` cutting at the failed prompt's saved row with the raw `inflight.user` (a `/skill` turn keeps its attachments and mention note), both confirmations and no `queued`. 4009 says to wait and changes nothing; 4018 says the message can't be changed, hides Retry for that row and rereads (an agent that never started always gets 4018). Retry never resends on its own and never touches the draft.

**Design:** pick C (inline notice), #878 section of https://h8y1ulmv5xvh.postplan.dev. Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-29) on #878 applied: no long billing text, Retry tappable before a reset, row kept across disconnect.

title: chore(bots): log the Hermes connection's lifecycle
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #889 (part of #877). Stacked on #935; merge after it.

## What changed

When a Bot connection went wrong on a phone (a tunnel drop, a refused upgrade, a call that never got a reply), nothing showed up in the device log. Now one `Logger` (subsystem is the bundle ID, category `HermesConnection`) is shared by `HermesConnection` and `HermesGateway`. It follows the issue's plan and the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/889#issuecomment-5902968073).

- Each line names its connection (`c1`, `c2`, …) and its socket (`s0`, `s1`, …, from the gateway's `generation`). No line names the server.
- `HermesConnectionLog.reason(_:)` returns only `URLError <code>`, the `BotFailure` case (such as `rejected(403)` or #880's `upgradeRefused(403)`), `DecodingError`, `cancelled`, or `<NSError domain> <code>`. It never reads an error's description or user info.
- Sign-in logs its success with the release. A failure logs the step (`status`, `login`, `identity`, `ticket`) and the reason, once. A failed re-sign-in after the ticket's 401 logs only its own step.
- Socket lines: open; failed to open (a refused upgrade shows its status through #880's mapping); 45 s of silence; closed because the last screen left or the connection was retired; dropped, with the counts of calls failed and screens told. A close code sent by the other end is logged, but the close reason never is.
- A reply whose integer id matches no open call is logged. The keepalive's string-id pongs are not. A call past its deadline is logged by method name, which `Pending` now keeps.
- Docs: a paragraph in `docs/agents/bots.md`, and "Watching the Bot connection log" in `DEVELOPMENT.md`.

## How it was tested

- Red: I replaced the describer with a stub, `String(describing: error)`. `HermesConnectionLogTests` then had 4 of 5 fail. One example: the `URLError` came out as `Error Domain=NSURLErrorDomain Code=-1005 … https://secret-host.example/api/ws`, where `URLError -1005` was expected.
- Green: `scripts/test-sim <17e> --only` HermesConnectionLogTests, BotClientTests, HermesGatewayTests, HermesConnectionTests: **64 passed** at the review fix. The full suite ran after the Xcode project change: **3427 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped** at 137e3574. `git diff --check` is clean. The touched files build with no warnings.
- Per Decision 5, only the describer has tests. The log lines themselves are checked on a device, below.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (client-only; no contract change)

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone
1. Cable the iPhone and open Console.app. Stream the iPhone filtered by `subsystem:com.uzairansar.hermesmobile.branch category:HermesConnection`, then open the Bots inbox. Expect "c1: signed in, release …", then "c1 socket s0 open".
2. Go home, then return. Expect "c1 socket s0 closed, last screen left", then "c1 socket s1 open". There should be no new sign-in line, and no "closed by the other end" line.
3. Open a chat. Turn on Airplane Mode for a minute, then turn it off. Expect a "dropped: …" line (probably `NSPOSIXErrorDomain 57` or a `URLError` code) or "no frame for 45 s; closing", then a new "socket sN open".
4. Leave the inbox open for a minute, then search the stream for the tunnel's hostname and a bot's name. Expect no line every 15 s and no hits for either search.
5. [Only if the host restarts during the session, e.g. a planned update] Over the tunnel, expect "closed by the other end with code N", then a drop line. This was only measured on macOS against loopback.

title: feat(security): lock Hermex with Face ID or the passcode
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #885 (part of #877)

## What changed

Hermex had no app lock: anyone holding an unlocked iPhone could read every chat, and the app switcher showed the last one.

Per the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/885#issuecomment-5902967409): new `AppLock` (off by default, `UserDefaults`, app-wide) locks on cold launch and when Hermex becomes active more than 60 s after going to the background (`ContinuousClock`). While on, the scene is covered (icon only) whenever it isn't active, except under the lock's own Face ID sheet. It prompts once per lock; after a cancel only Unlock retries. Turning it on or off needs authentication; it can't go on without a passcode, and if the passcode is removed later the lock says so and Continue turns it off.
- `AppLockSceneDelegate` (installed from `PushAppDelegate`, which still sets the notification delegate in `didFinishLaunching`, #583) shows a UIWindow above alerts in the same scene callback, so sheets, alerts and the keyboard stay under it. It follows Theme, is VoiceOver-modal, shows the current app icon (alone whenever the scene isn't active), and resigns any text input behind it (including one focused after it appears) and gives the keyboard back after unlock.
- Settings: a Privacy card above App with "Require Face ID/Touch ID/Passcode" and the decided footer; disabled with "Set a passcode…" when there's none.
- While locked: every `HermexCommands` shortcut is off (#119/#921 unchanged when unlocked), "New Chat with Voice" waits for unlock, and `PushPresence` reports no chat on screen (#653).
- `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`, and 13 new strings in all 17 languages (`needs_review`).

1. Settings → Privacy → turn on Require Face ID and cancel the prompt, then turn it on and approve. Change the icon in Settings → App Icon and swipe up to the app switcher. Expected: the switch stays off after the cancel; the switcher shows the new icon, no chat.

title: feat(push): offer a hermex-push plugin update from Settings
body:
Part of #851

**Problem.** Hermex installs hermex-push only when the pairing route answers 404, and never touches a paired host again, so plugin fixes never reach it. The "Update the hermex-push plugin." pairing failure offers no action either.

**Fix (design C, callout card; no connection-screen banner).**
- `HermexPushPlugin.loadedVersion` decodes the pairing route's `plugin_version` tolerantly; missing or unparseable counts as older than every known version. `installedVersion(hub:)` reads the on-disk `version` from `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/hub` (new `HermesREST.pluginsHub`). `HermexPushPluginVersion` compares numerically (0.10.0 > 0.9.0, 0.3 == 0.3.0). `newestVersion` is 0.3.0.
- `checkPlugin()` runs when the Notifications section appears on a paired server: one pairing GET, plus the hub only when the loaded version is behind (newest on disk means "restart needed", otherwise "update available"). Kept in memory, never in `PushPairing`.
- `updatePlugin()`, only after a confirmation: setup's force install, `POST /api/gateway/restart`, then the pairing route again (restart retry schedule). It ends at "Plugin up to date" or, usually, "Restart Hermes to finish", which names `hermes dashboard` and offers "Check again" (one read). Keys stay in `plugin-data`, so the phone stays paired; the install clears the hub's 5 s cache, so no rescan.
- Failures whose text says "Update the hermex-push plugin." (setup's pairing step, the test notification's `.unusablePairing`) offer "Update plugin…"; that update never pairs by itself. The update's own failures show in the card: "Try again" (confirmed) after the reinstall or restart, "Check again" (one read) after the version read. Turning notifications off drops the card, since its install would enable the plugin again.
- The collapsed row keeps "Push on · Current server" and adds one line. No spinner, no animation. 21 strings in all 17 languages (`needs_review`); `docs/agents/bots.md`, `docs/agents/push.md`, and a `TESTFLIGHT.md` release gate (`newestVersion` equals hermex-push `main`'s `plugin.yaml`).

**Decisions applied.** [Decision (Uzair, 2026-09-29)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/851#issuecomment-5902993440) with every Preserve line (#581, #788, #827, #924, #910). Contract checked against hermex-push `plugin/dashboard/plugin_api.py` (hermex-push#16) and hermes-agent ca678285 (`_merged_plugins_hub`; `_plugin_action` clears the hub cache).

**Merge gate.** Merge only once 0.3.0 is on hermex-push `main` (0.2.0 today). Until then every paired host shows the update, and an update lands back on it.

**Design.** https://ozrsjnnq33ac.postplan.dev, pick C.

**Tests.** `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests`: 38/38 on the final head (10 new, 1 updated row). On 7825c4fa: HermesRequestTests 2, LocalizationCatalogTests 7, HermesConnectionTests 12, all passing (the follow-up commit changes neither requests nor strings). `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: covers all 2009 keys. `git diff --check` clean.
Red: against a skeleton of the new API, 27 passed and 8 failed (no card, no pairing GET, remedy `.none`, nil versions). Review fixes: `testTurningNotificationsOffDropsThePluginUpdate` (card still `.available`) and `testAnUpdateThatStopsAfterThePairingFailureLeavesTheSetupStepsHidden` (`showsSteps` true) failed on 7825c4fa; `testAnUpdateWhoseCheckFailsOffersTheReadAgainRatherThanAnotherRestart` failed on ecac87c5 (card `.failed(retryUpdate)`).

**Manual test**
Device: physical iPhone, iPhone simulator, iPad simulator
Physical iPhone (Uzair only, over the Cloudflare tunnel, after 0.3.0 is on hermex-push `main`):
1. [Push paired on a host with an older plugin] Settings → Interaction → Notifications: the row adds "Plugin update available"; expanded, the card names the loaded version and 0.3.0.
2. Tap the card, then Update plugin: it steps through 1–3 of 3 and ends at "Restart Hermes to finish" (or "Plugin up to date") with no sign-in error; Send Test Notification still arrives.
3. Before restarting, set Hermex's language to Arabic: the restart card's `hermes dashboard` renders as code. Set it back.
4. Restart `hermes dashboard` on the host, then tap Check again: the card reads "Plugin up to date"; reopening Settings shows no card.
iPhone simulator:
1. [Push paired, older plugin] Larger Text at AX2: the collapsed row's second line and the card wrap without truncating, and tapping anywhere on the card opens the confirmation. Tap Cancel.
iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5)):
1. [Push paired, older plugin] Expand Notifications and tap the card: the "Update the hermex-push plugin?" confirmation anchors to the section, and tapping outside or Cancel dismisses it with nothing sent to the host.

title: fix(bots): open the sign-in form after a rejected password
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #884 (part of #877). Stacked on #938; merge after it.

## What changed

When the host refused the saved Bot password (a 401 from the login step), the only button in the inbox, chat and room was Reconnect, which sent the same password again. So did foregrounding and pull to refresh, and each try spends one of the host's 10 password logins a minute per client IP.

This follows the issue's plan and the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/884#issuecomment-5902967239):
- `BotInbox`, `BotConversation` and `BotRoomReader` get `needsSignIn`, set only for `BotFailure.rejected(401)`. Every other failure keeps Reconnect and its retry rules.
- The inbox row, the chat pill and the room pill show "Update sign-in" (key symbol) in Reconnect's slot. The error pill still comes first (#614, #627). A chat or room closes and the inbox opens the Hermes connection sheet (Decision 1), which keeps the stored values and focuses the password field (Decision 3).
- Nothing resends a refused password (Decision 2). The inbox skips the unchanged record, and a chat or room handing off marks the inbox first (`noteRejectedSignIn`). The chat skips foreground recovery. A room reopen restores its saved history and stops without building a client. Any save from the form clears the flag, even for an unchanged record (D3).
- The 401 copy is now "Hermes didn't accept the username or password." Two strings in all 17 languages as needs_review. There is a paragraph in `docs/agents/bots.md`.
- The room profile also offers Update sign-in in Reconnect's place while the password is refused.

## How it was tested

## Linked issue

Fixes #891 (part of #877)

## What changed

When a bot needed its password manager unlocked, a login saved, or a sign-in code, Bot Chat said "Answer this in Hermes Desktop on the Mac" and offered only Skip, so away from the Mac the bot's sign-in stalled.

- **Model:** `vault.unlock_prompt`, `vault.save_login` and `vault.code` move from `BotDesktopTaskRequest.Kind` into `BotCredentialRequest.Kind`, which now reads `display_name`, `origin`, `site` and `hint` (new fields default to nil, so existing inits compile). Each kind has its own title, detail, handling line and Skip hint from the approved mock. `BotCredentialRequest.saveLoginValue(identifier:password:)` JSON-encodes `{identifier, password}` with `JSONEncoder` and returns nil unless both are filled.
- **Card (design A):** unlock gets a masked "Master password" (`.password`); save login gets "Email or username" (`.username`, Return moves to the password field) above a masked password with the round send arrow, and the origin shown once in monospace; code gets a masked field (`.oneTimeCode`). Symbols `lock.fill`, `person.badge.key.fill`, `123.rectangle.fill`. Fields empty the moment a value is sent and stay keyed by request id.
- **Answer:** the existing `answerCredential` / `skipCredential` → `request.answer {id, result:{value}}`. Skip sends `""`; `expired` maps to already-resolved; generation, runtime and request id are captured on tap and rechecked at the socket write (Preserve #504, #775).

title: feat(files): open files Hermex can't preview in Quick Look
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #879 (part of #877)

## What changed

PDFs, Office and iWork documents, audio and video opened to a "No Preview" dead end in the Files preview, chat file links, composer file chips and chat attachments. They now open in Quick Look, capped at 25 MB.

- **Shared pieces.** New `Features/Shared/QuickLookFilePreview.swift` (main target only): one `BinaryFilePreview` policy (`.quickLook` / `.unavailable`) replaces the two copied extension lists; `QuickLookTemporaryFile` owns its own temp directory and deletes it on release; `FilePreviewContent.loadQuickLook(name:knownSize:download:)` takes a download closure so #703 only swaps the data source; `QuickLookFileView` is the old private `BotNativeFilePreview`. Bot artifacts use the same pieces with no behavior change.
- **Capped download.** `APIClient.sendBoundedData` streams `GET /api/file/raw` through `session.bytes(for:delegate:)` with `sendData`'s custom headers, redirect guard and `mappedHTTPResponse` error mapping. A 2xx `Content-Length` over 25 MB (webui's `_serve_file_bytes` sends one, pinned `c67fd2dd`) is refused before the body is read; `BotArtifactBuffer` stops a body with no length (Decision 4).
- **Files preview and attachment sheet.** Quick Look types take the capped path. A known size over the cap (`entry.size`, `item.size`) sends no request and shows the existing 25 MB string in the No Preview layout; Export stays and reuses the downloaded bytes. Audio attachments keep the inline player (#88). `canPreview` gets the final say (Decision 2). Archives, executables and databases stay No Preview with no request (Decision 1); key/numbers/pages/rtf/usdz join Quick Look (Decision 3). No Export in the attachment sheet (Decision 5); `MEDIA:` untouched (Decision 6).
- **Preserved.** Press-down prefetch never fetches Quick Look or No Preview types as text (#401). The preview content owns the temp file, so refresh, dismissal or a server switch deletes it (#507). Per the [decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/879#issuecomment-5902966368).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro> --only …APIClientWorkspaceFileTests --only …ChatAttachmentPreviewViewModelTests --only …BotArtifactTests --only …FileBrowserViewModelTests --only …APIClientChatEndpointTests`: 67 passed, 0 failed (32 / 4 / 9 / 12 / 10).
- Full suite (the Xcode project changed): 3422 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped.
- New: PDF opens in Quick Look with one `/api/file/raw` request and Export reuses it; `Content-Length` over the cap gives too-large with no file; a known size over the cap sends no request; releasing the preview deletes the file; the bounded read stops a body with no length and maps 401/403 like `sendData`; attachment PDF → Quick Look, m4a → audio, zip → No Preview with no request. The prefetch test now asserts pdf/rtf/zip are never fetched as text.
- Red on master `b0d1503e`: `testFilePreviewOpensPDFInQuickLook` (no request, "Preview is not available for this file type.") and the prefetch test (`notes.rtf` prefetched as text) fail. The rest need the new API and don't compile against master.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator; iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5)); physical iPhone. Put a small PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, MP4, MP3, a ZIP and a 40 MB MP4 in a session's workspace.

1. iPhone, Files: open the PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, MP4 and MP3. Expected: each renders or plays in Quick Look under the title, with Export in the toolbar. Tap the PDF to go full screen and tap again: back and Export return; going back to the list leaves no Quick Look toolbar. The ZIP shows No Preview with Export.
2. iPhone, Files: open the 40 MB MP4. Expected: "This file is too large to preview on this device (25 MB maximum)." and Export saves the full file.
3. iPhone, chat: tap a file link to report.pdf, then a composer @file chip for the MP4 and start it playing, then tap Done. Expected: both sheets open Quick Look; Done closes the sheet and playback stops.
4. iPhone, chat: send the PDF and an m4a as attachments and tap each. Expected: the PDF opens in Quick Look with a share button visible (Decision 5 relies on it); the m4a keeps the inline player.

title: chore(test): a local Hermes test server with a scripted model
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #890

## What changed

The only Hermes host we can test against is the maintainer's real server. So tool and approval turns can't run in the simulator, and the Hermes fixtures have no tool or approval frames.

**Commit 1, the local server.** New `scripts/local-hermes` (Python, standard library only):
- The first run clones the pinned hermes-agent into `~/Library/Caches/hermex-local-hermes/<sha>` and installs it with `uv`, under a lock. Later runs reuse the cache once its install is stamped complete.
- Each run uses a temporary Hermes home with a fixed install id. It serves on `127.0.0.1:9199` behind basic auth (`hermex` / `hermex-local`), with manual approvals.
- An in-process stub model scripts every turn: "Let me run a quick check.", then one `terminal` call for `python3 -c "print(1)"`, then "The command returned: <first line>."
- Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP stops only the process group the script spawned, then deletes the temp home. Loopback calls skip any HTTP proxy. Stub tests are in `scripts/tests/test_local_hermes.py`, and `DEVELOPMENT.md` has a new "Local Hermes test server" section.

**Commit 2, the recorded fixture.**
- `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures --local` records one approved tool turn from that server into `turn-tool-approval-frames.json`, with its own pin stamp. It writes nothing else.
- Only `--local` relaxes the no-tools rule, and only for exactly one `approval` request. The allow-list gains command, description, choices, name and request_id. The leak check now also refuses each Profile's home path.
- Real-host capture is unchanged: it produced byte-identical output to master's.
- `HermesAgentFixtureTests.testToolApprovalTurnDecodesAndSettles` checks four things: the approval decodes to a `.approval` card, every event type is known, the events settle one completed `terminal` call, and the turn ends with `running: false`.

Decisions applied: Decisions 1–5 in the issue and the [2026-09-29 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/890#issuecomment-5902968256), including every Preserve (#798) line. Two defaults were taken: `security.tirith_enabled: false` keeps each run offline, and `uv --system-certs` handles TLS-inspecting networks. DevAutoLogin and `scripts/sim-login` are untouched (#700).

## How it was tested

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v`: 35 OK (17 new). Red before the change: `FileNotFoundError: …/scripts/local-hermes`; the 6 added in review each failed on the code before its fix.
- `scripts/test-sim <17e> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesAgentFixtureTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConnectionVersionTests`: 8 passed. Red before the change: `Missing turn-tool-approval-frames.json` (it fails, not skips).
- Real starts and stops, each with the PID captured at spawn. Ready in 11.2 s cold and about 3.5 s warm; `/api/status` reported `auth_required: true` with `basic`. A rerun right after Ctrl-C also started. SIGINT exited 0, the process group was gone and the temp home was deleted.
- A real `--local` capture wrote only the new file. `--local --from-raw` with the server stopped reproduced the same shasum. A planted home path was refused. The local raw capture in real-host mode was refused on `tool.start`.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator

1. Run `scripts/local-hermes`. It prints `http://127.0.0.1:9199` and `hermex` / `hermex-local`. In the simulator, signed in to your webui server, open Settings → your server → Hermes connection, enter those values, and save.
2. Open Bots → Hermes and send "hi". "Let me run a quick check." appears before the approval card for `python3 -c "print(1)"`. The host sends that line as `message.interim`, which Bot Chat only picks up from a snapshot read, so if it never shows, that is a follow-up. Approve: the reply is "The command returned: 1."
3. Send again and Deny: the reply reports the denial ("The command returned: BLOCKED: …" or similar).
4. Ctrl-C the script and run it again. The saved connection reconnects with no "different host" error; the previous run's sessions are gone. Afterwards, re-enter your real Hermes connection.

Fixes #887. Needs uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#19 (plugin 0.3.0) on the host to show anything new; it can merge before that, because a push without `bot_name` looks exactly as it does today.

## What changed

Relay banners said "Approval needed", "Question" or "Turn failed" in English, without naming the bot, and titled a reply with the Profile slug. With several bots you couldn't tell which one was asking, and a phone in German still read English.

title: feat(bots): say when a request was withdrawn
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #892

## What changed

When the host withdraws the approval, question or password prompt on screen (`request.cancel`), its card just vanished: `applyRequestCancel` never read `reason`, so nobody could tell whether it timed out (for an approval, nothing ran), the work stopped, or it was answered elsewhere.

Client-only, no new calls, no change to `Networking/Hermes`:
- **Model.** `BotRequestWithdrawal` maps family (approval / question / other) and reason (`timeout`; `interrupted` or `session_closed` as stopped; `shutdown`; any other text) to one whole-sentence localized line (issue Decision 2) and a symbol (`clock` / `stop.circle`). `resolved`, a missing reason, and renderer tasks (`tour`, `terminal.read`, `window.read`, `preview.*`, excluded by method name so #891's vault kinds stay "other") are silent.
- **State.** `BotConversation.withdrawnRequest` is set only when the cancelled envelope (id + method, #530) is the card on screen and nothing takes the slot. It stays silent for this phone's own stop: a Stop in flight or acknowledged, an Interrupt (Stop & send, `session.redirect`) in flight or answered `redirected` (a `queued` one stopped nothing), or an accepted voice stop.
- **Away** ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/892#issuecomment-5902968564)). The on-screen envelope (no params) is remembered on `suspend()` and on a dropped socket, and matched in `reconcileReplay` only when it is the replay's last `request.cancel`. Request frames are unsequenced, so a later cancel is the only trace of a card that came after. A truncated or reset replay stays silent.
- **Clearing.** The next accepted prompt, a new request, a snapshot that puts a card on screen, disconnect or reset. Never cached.
- **View.** `BotRequestWithdrawalNote` in the card's slot: one centered secondary caption with a symbol (the room system-line style), no transition, announced once to VoiceOver. 12 keys in all 17 languages. `docs/agents/bots.md` documents the rules.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only BotAnsweringTests --only BotPendingRequestParsingTests --only BotConversationTests --only LocalizationCatalogTests --only BotAttachmentSendingTests --only BotLiveActivityTests` → 206 passed, 0 failed.
- 11 new tests in `BotPendingRequestTests.swift`: a table of all 12 sentences plus silent cases; timeout, resolved elsewhere, Stop here vs elsewhere, Interrupt (redirected vs queued) and voice stop, not on screen, renderer tasks, unknown reason, clearing on send / new request / snapshot, and the away path (suspend, dropped socket, truncated replay, a later cancel in the replay).
- Red: against a stub (`init?` returning nil), 9 failed, e.g. `testATimedOutApprovalLeavesANote`: `("nil") is not equal to ("Optional("Approval timed out, so it didn't run.")")`. title: feat(chat): recall your last message with ↑ and preview staged documents
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #894 (part of #877). Applies the [decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/894#issuecomment-5902968881): Bot Chat scans `messages + liveMessages`, one shared thumbnail cache, ⌘↩ unchanged (#119), draft copies read-only (#298).

## What changed

On a hardware keyboard there was no way to bring back what you just sent, and a staged PDF or document showed only a generic icon, so two PDFs looked the same.

- **↑ recall:** `ComposerRecall.lastSentText(in:)` returns the newest message the user typed. It skips other roles, Bot system deliveries, compaction marker rows and attachment-only sends (Sessions' "I've uploaded N file(s)" text, Bot Chat's image note and `@file:` refs to its UUID-named uploads). It unwraps steers and strips attachment text. `ComposerChipTextView` adds an unmodified ↑ command, "Recall Last Message", with priority over caret movement. It is listed only where there is a recall source, and it is enabled only in an empty, editable composer with no quotes. It draws chips as the bubble does, puts the caret at the end, and registers its own undo, so ⌘Z empties the composer. Sessions and Bot Chat pass a closure, so the transcript is scanned only on the key press. Bot rooms pass none.
- **Document previews:** `ChatDraftAttachmentStoring.fileURL(named:)` exposes the name-checked resolver. The `@MainActor` `ComposerDocumentThumbnails.shared` makes a Quick Look `.thumbnail` from the draft copy, keyed by attachment id. It caches failures, stores nothing when cancelled, and keeps 32 entries. The strip's 58×68 badge (with hairline) and the pill's 30 pt tile show the preview without animation. Until one arrives, or when Quick Look can't draw one, today's icon stays.
- One new string in all 17 languages. Main app only; the extensions are untouched.

## Linked issue

Fixes #886

## What changed

The Hermes connection form refused any path, query or fragment, so the link a user copies from the browser (the dashboard root lands on `/sessions`) was never accepted. It also never showed whether a schemeless address would use http or https.

Built as written with defaults 1-5 ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/886#issuecomment-5902967571)):
- `BotConnection.address(_:)` maps `ws`/`wss` to `http`/`https`, drops the query and fragment, trims trailing slashes, and clears a path whose first segment (any case) is `login`, `auth`, `api`, `chat` or `sessions`. Any other path throws `BotAddressError.path`, naming it; credentials, other schemes and bad hosts or ports throw `.invalid`. Host checks, the numeric-host guard, the scheme guess (#626) and lowercasing are unchanged, so every address master accepted still yields the same URL.
- `BotAddressError` is thrown only by the parser; `BotFailure.invalidAddress` stays for request building and the inbox. `connect()` shows the parser's copy before any client exists (#780).
- The address footer's first line reads "Will connect to <root>" while the text parses. A trailing LRM keeps a URL ending in `]` in one left-to-right run, and the path in the error copy sits in a first-strong isolate so `/hermes` keeps its slash in front in Arabic, Hebrew and Urdu.
