title: fix(chat): explain the "restart Hermes WebUI" 409 and offer a fix prompt
body:
> After someone updates Hermes on their server, every send fails with a raw "Server returned HTTP 409: …" banner until hermes-webui is restarted. This makes that banner say plainly what happened, and in chat adds a **Copy fix prompt** action the user can paste to their agent over Telegram or Discord, so they can recover without SSH until upstream adds a restart route.

## Context

Many users report this after every Hermes Agent update. hermes-webui deliberately refuses local Agent actions once the Agent checkout changes under the running process (`api/agent_runtime.py::ensure_agent_runtime_current`) and only recovers after a manual WebUI restart. Upstream docs: `docs/troubleshooting.md` § "Hermes Agent was updated while Hermes WebUI was running".

Response shape (upstream `8ac497df`, `agent_runtime_stale_payload`), HTTP 409:

```json
{
  "error": "Hermes Agent was updated while Hermes WebUI was running. …",
  "type": "agent_runtime_stale",
  "retryable": true,
  "restart_scheduled": false,
  "agent_update_state": "unverified"
}
```

`agent_update_state` is one of `active`, `incomplete`, `stale`, `unknown`, `unverified` and may be absent. The same payload is returned by chat start, voice/regenerate turns, compression, commit-message generation, and handoff summaries.

A client cannot restart WebUI today. The only lever is `/api/updates/apply`, which restarts only after an actual update and moves the Agent to `origin/main` (reproduced 2026-09-30), so it is not a recovery path. The restart route is proposed upstream in nesquena/hermes-webui#7934.

Messaging gateways (Telegram, Discord, …) are unaffected: they run in the Hermes gateway, which `hermes update` restarts itself. Users already recover by asking their agent there to restart the WebUI, but a vague ask makes the agent deep-dive instead of just restarting. A precise prompt fixes that.

## Current behavior

`APIError.errorDescription` falls through to `"Server returned HTTP 409: <message>"`. `ErrorPayload` does not decode `type`. Current upstream's message is 229 characters and gets clipped by `displayedServerMessageLimit` (200).

## Expected behavior

### Plain copy on every surface

- Any `.http(409, body)` whose body has `"type": "agent_runtime_stale"` shows app-owned copy instead of the server text:
  - Default: "Hermes was updated on your server. Restart Hermes WebUI there, then try again."
  - `agent_update_state == "active"`: "Hermes is still updating on your server. Wait for it to finish, restart Hermes WebUI, then try again."
  - `agent_update_state == "incomplete"`: "A Hermes update on your server didn't finish. Check it, restart Hermes WebUI, then try again."
- This lives in `APIError` (decode `type` and `agent_update_state` tolerantly in `ErrorPayload`, check before the status switch), so every surface that shows `errorDescription` picks it up with no per-call-site changes.

### Copy fix prompt (chat composer error banner only)

- When the chat send error (`ChatViewModel.sendErrorMessage`, rendered through the composer's `errorMessage`) came from this 409, the banner offers a secondary **Copy fix prompt** action. The view model exposes the error kind; the composer stays dumb.
- Hidden when `agent_update_state == "active"` (the right move is to wait).
- Copies this text to `UIPasteboard` and confirms with a light, non-animated acknowledgement (VoiceOver announcement included):

  > My Hermes WebUI is refusing chats with "Hermes Agent was updated while Hermes WebUI was running." Please do only this:
  > 1. Check that no Hermes update is still running and the last one finished without errors. If it didn't, stop and tell me.
  > 2. Restart the Hermes WebUI server the same way it was started (systemd, launchd, ctl.sh, Docker, or whatever runs it). Don't update, reinstall, or reconfigure anything.
  > 3. Confirm it's back: its `/health` endpoint should return 200.
  >
  > If it doesn't come back up, show me the last lines of its error log and suggest a fix, but don't change config, environment variables, or Hermes source until I say so.

- The banner copy and the prompt go through the String Catalog per `docs/agents/i18n.md`.

### Unchanged

- The composer keeps the unsent text (already true via `ChatDraftStore.resolveSubmission`; don't regress it).

## Design gate

The banner action is a UI change: build static mocks of the error banner with the action (light/dark, largest Dynamic Type), publish them with `html-communication`, and wait for the maintainer's pick before editing the composer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A 409 with `type: agent_runtime_stale` and no or unknown `agent_update_state` maps to the default copy.
- [ ] `active` and `incomplete` map to their copy.
- [ ] A 409 without that `type` (for example the `stale: true` expired-prompt 409 or `session_profile_mismatch`) behaves exactly as today, with no Copy fix prompt action.
- [ ] Unknown extra fields in the payload never break decoding.
- [ ] In chat, the stale 409 shows **Copy fix prompt** (hidden for `active`); tapping it puts the exact prompt on the pasteboard.
- [ ] A failed send with this error leaves the draft in the composer.
- [ ] The action has a VoiceOver label, works at the largest Dynamic Type size, and uses no repeating animation.

## Validation plan

- Focused XCTest on `APIError` mapping (the cases above), plus a `ChatViewModel` send test using a `URLProtocol` mock returning the stale 409 that asserts the copy, the exposed error kind (and its absence for other 409s), and that the optimistic message rolls back.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` those classes.
- One signed Debug build and a short manual simulator plan for the banner and the Copy action. Reproducing the 409 against a real server means updating the Agent, which is out of bounds, so the manual check uses a mocked response or a debug hook.

## Non-goals

- A Restart button. It needs the upstream route (nesquena/hermes-webui#7934); it gets its own issue once that route's shape is merged, with feature detection via `restart_available`.
- Copy fix prompt outside the chat composer (Git commit-message generation, compression errors get the plain copy only).
- Detecting the stale state before the user sends (no read endpoint reports it).
- Any use of `/api/updates/apply` or `/api/updates/force` as a restart lever.

title: bug(chat): a long approval description pushes Allow / Deny off-screen on iPhone
body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. On the Hermes side, queue a pending approval whose `description` is long (~1,000–1,500 characters). Any `pre_tool_call` plugin returning `{"action": "approve", "message": <long text>}` does it, or a `pre_approval_request` hook that rewrites the queued entry's description (e.g. to add a plain-English summary plus a code excerpt).
2. Open that chat in Hermex on an iPhone, portrait.
3. The "Approval required" sheet appears.

### Expected behavior
The Allow / Deny actions stay reachable however long the description is. For example, the description area scrolls or is collapsed behind "Show more", and the action buttons stay pinned to the bottom of the sheet.

### Actual behavior
The sheet grows to fit the description, command block and pattern keys, and the action buttons end up below the bottom of the screen. The sheet doesn't scroll, so there's no way to approve or deny from the phone. The request just waits until it times out or is answered from another client.

The description is free-form text from plugins and hooks, so the client can't count on it being short. (I've shortened ours on the agent side as a workaround.)

### App version / commit
Hermex 1.7.0

### iOS version and device
iOS 27 on a 6.3" iPhone (1206×2622 screenshot)

### hermes-webui server version
hermes-webui 0.52.379 + Hermes Agent v2026.9.24 (v0.21.5); the app's Hermes connection points at the Hermes dashboard

### How the phone reaches the server
Tailscale

### Screenshots or screen recordings
Redacted screenshot in the first comment (the description text is blurred; it fills the sheet down to the home indicator and no buttons are visible).

title: feat(push): show the bot's avatar in its notifications
body:
## Problem

A push notification from a bot shows the Hermex app icon. Since #887 the title names the bot, but with several bots the icon is the same for all of them, so you can't tell at a glance who is asking.

## Idea

Every notification that comes from a bot (approval, question, reply, turn failed) shows that bot's avatar in place of the Hermex icon, the way Messages shows a contact's photo. Notifications that don't come from a bot keep the Hermex icon.

## Notes for the plan

- iOS draws a sender image in place of the app icon only for **Communication Notifications**: the notification service extension donates an `INSendMessageIntent` whose sender `INPerson` carries the image, then updates the content from it. The main app needs the `com.apple.developer.usernotifications.communication` entitlement, registered on both App IDs (production and Hermex Branch).
- The sealed preview already carries `profile` and, from plugin 0.3.0, `bot_name`, so the extension knows which bot sent it. It does not have the image.
- Avatars exist today only in memory in the app (`BotAvatarStore`, Desktop assets read through `profiles.get_asset`), and a bot with no asset gets a drawn face (`BotAvatarMarkView`). The extension can't fetch or draw either. One option: the app writes a small PNG for each bot into the app group whenever the roster loads, keyed by server and Profile so equal names on two servers never share an image (`docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`). The extension reads it, and falls back to today's icon when there's none.
- Keep the extension's imports small (Preserve #583: Foundation, CryptoKit, Security, UserNotifications today); adding `Intents` is the one new framework this needs.
- Worth checking: how Focus and notification summaries treat communication notifications, and that Settings → Notifications' "Replies" and subagent mutes still apply.

Suggested by Uzair during the epic #877 merge walk, after #887's bot names shipped.

title: fix(push): update the plugin without a terminal prompt on current Hermes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #851

## What changed

Settings' "Update plugin" (#941) got HTTP 400 on the maintainer's host. Current Hermes asks at a terminal before it replaces an enabled plugin that declares Python packages; hermex-push declares `cryptography`. A dashboard reinstall has no terminal, so Hermes refuses it ("Reinstall declined: dependency install skipped (non-interactive)"). Hermes's own Update route re-clones subfolder installs through the same install, so it fails the same way. The Hermes commit Hermex is pinned to (`ca678285`) predates that prompt.

`updatePlugin()` now turns hermex-push off first (`POST /api/dashboard/agent-plugins/hermex-push/disable`), then runs the same forced install with `enable: true`. A disabled plugin skips the terminal prompt, and enabling it goes through Hermes's normal dependency admission, which needs no prompt. Turning a plugin off only edits config, so the running gateway keeps it. If turning it off or the install fails, the app turns the plugin back on, so the next restart doesn't drop push. If Hermes confirmed the turn-off and turning it back on fails, the card says Hermes still has the plugin off and notifications stop at its next restart (one new string, 17 languages, `needs_review`); Try again runs the whole update. First-time setup is unchanged: it installs a plugin that isn't enabled yet, so the prompt never applies. `docs/agents/bots.md` explains why the plugin goes off first.

Contract: hermes-agent `7239625ae1` on the maintainer's host (`hermes_cli/plugins_transaction.py` `publish_plugin(require_consent=True)`, `plugins_cmd_install.py` `_consent_python_deps`, `plugins_cmd.py` `dashboard_set_agent_plugin_enabled`). The same sequence was run against that host on 2026-09-30, moving 0.1.0 to 0.3.0: disable returned 200, install returned 200 with `enabled: true` and `gateway_reloaded: true`, and the gateway restart returned 200.

title: fix(push): a slow plugin check can overwrite a finished update's result
body:
## Problem

`HermexPushProvisioner.checkPlugin()` is the passive read that runs each time Settings → Notifications appears on a paired server. It checks `!isUpdatingPlugin` before its read and again after the read returns. If the user starts **Update plugin** while that read is still in flight, and the read only returns *after* the whole update has finished, the second check passes again (no update is running any more). The stale pre-update answer, usually "Plugin update available", then replaces the update's result ("Plugin up to date" or "Restart Hermes to finish").

It's rare, because the passive read has to outlast a reinstall plus a gateway restart, which needs a slow host or tunnel. When it happens, though, the card offers an update the host has already taken.

## Suggested fix

Keep a generation counter on the provisioner. `updatePlugin()` and `checkPluginAgain()` bump it, `checkPlugin()` captures it before its read, and a read whose generation has changed is dropped. Add a test with a `URLProtocol` fixture that holds the passive read's response until an update completes.

Found during the epic #877 run (#941, #958).

title: chore(test): test-sim stops before testing on a simulator that never had Hermex installed
body:
## Problem

Before each attempt, `scripts/test-sim` runs `xcrun simctl terminate <udid> com.uzairansar.hermesmobile` with a 25 s limit (`TERMINATE_TIMEOUT`). On iOS 27, `simctl terminate` hangs, rather than failing fast, when the app has never been installed on that simulator. `run()` stops the process group and re-raises `TimeoutExpired`; `terminate_app` doesn't catch it, so `main()` prints "STOP: command timed out" and exits **124** before any test runs. The docstring says the exit status is ignored, and it is, but a timeout isn't an exit status.

So the first `test-sim` run on a fresh or newly assigned simulator always fails. The workaround today is to install the app once (for example with `run-sim.sh`) and run it again. That happened to lanes in the epic #877 batch run.

## Suggested fix

The 25 s limit is deliberate: a terminate that outlasts it usually means the simulator itself is stuck, and the script should keep stopping there. So skip the terminate when the app isn't installed. `xcrun simctl get_app_container <udid> <bundle id>` fails quickly in that case; check that it doesn't hang on iOS 27 too. Cover it in `scripts/tests` alongside the existing test-sim tests.

title: fix(bots): reattach a Bot Chat without applying frames early
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #901

## What changed

When a Bot Chat reattached mid-turn, a live frame that landed before the replay reply was applied at once. A frame that skipped ahead cleared the live rows and moved `sequence` past the missed events, so the running turn's tool rows and reasoning vanished; a frame past the replay's `latest_seq` moved `sequence` backwards. A reconnect also downloaded the transcript two or three times, and the host's temporary resume refusals (4007, 4009) showed advice and stopped.

Following the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/901#issuecomment-5922434333), `BotConversation` now:
- **Holds frames** while recovering, up to 512 (the host's replay ring). After the replay and the full snapshot, a held frame at or below the replay's cursor is dropped and each later one takes the live path, so a gap still schedules the coalesced full read. Past 512 it rebuilds from a full read (Decision 2). Host requests (string ids) are never held; a held `request.cancel` or `connection.*` frame bumps the request revision as a live one does, so a withdrawn card keeps its note.
- **Downloads the transcript once.** The identity resume sends `omit_messages: true` (the pin, `ca678285`, still returns `session_id` and `session_key`), and the recovery snapshot covers any full read asked for before it.
- **Retries 4007 and 4009** from `session.resume` on the existing backoff for 60 s from the first refusal in a row, by code only (Decision 1), then shows today's advice. Other calls' codes are unchanged.
- **Logs** each reattach (retries; frames held, applied, dropped) and each retried refusal code through #889's logger, never ids. Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md`.
- Preserved: #508 (nothing resent), #506, #775, #791, #880, #884.

## How it was tested

New `BotConversationTests` cases run over a real `BotClient` and `HermesGateway` with `BotScriptedSocket` (`BotSocketHost`, kept in that file): a gap frame before the replay reply, a frame ahead of an unchanged replay, a gap after held frames, one transcript read, the 512 overflow, 4007/4009 then success, 4007 past 60 s, and a lookup 4007 that is not retried. `BotAnsweringTests`: a held cancel withdraws the reattached card with its note, whether the snapshot was read before or after the cancel.

- Red on unchanged code: 6 new tests failed, e.g. after the gap-frame reattach `toolCalls` was `[]` not `["a", "b"]` and `sequence` 5 not 6; the identity resume read the transcript (`[true, true]` vs `[false, true]`). The cancel-after-snapshot ordering failed without the review fix (`withdrawnRequest` nil). Details in a comment below.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` BotConversationTests, BotAnsweringTests, BotPendingRequestParsingTests, ApprovalScopeTests, BotLiveActivityTests, HermesAgentFixtureTests, HermesGatewayTests: 235 passed. The other Bot classes (attachments, deep links, slash commands, mentions, file paths, artifacts) passed on the first commit.
- The 9 new tests with `--repeat 10`: 90 passed.

body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #934. Plugin side: uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#22. **Merge the plugin PR first**, after Uzair's launcher checks, because merging it to `main` is the release.

## What changed

After a hermex-push update, Settings ends on "Restart Hermes to finish" and asks the user to restart `hermes dashboard` on the host. On a remote host that is a dead end. hermex-push 0.4.0 adds `POST /api/plugins/hermex-push/restart` (202, then the dashboard re-execs itself on the same PID), and this PR adds the button that calls it.

title: feat(hermes): send custom headers to the Hermes host
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #898
Fixes #657

Stacked on #961; merge after it.

## What changed

A Hermes dashboard behind Cloudflare Access, or any proxy that wants its own header, couldn't be reached: every Bot request went out without one, and there was nowhere to enter it (`HermesConnection` had the plumbing, but production passed `.none`).

- `BotConnection.headers: [CustomHeader]?` lives in the same Keychain record. It's nil when empty, so old records decode and re-encode unchanged.
- `HermesConnection` takes its headers from the record (`HermesHeaders(saved:)`), so the shared connection and the form's unsaved candidate both send them: status, sign-in, identity, ticket, REST and plugin calls, uploads, downloads and the `/api/ws` upgrade. `adopt()` compares headers, so saving changed ones retires the live connection once and keeps the UUID (Decision 2).
- The status probe gets `CrossOriginHeaderStripper` first, then the saved headers. `HermesHeaders.applied(to:origin:)` and `redirectGuard(for:)` are shared by both paths.
- Form ([Design pick C](https://37cb011rg61x.postplan.dev)): Connection Headers is its own section between the sign-in fields and Connect, pushing the unchanged `CustomHeadersEditor`. Its footer shows a refused header in red with the reason (Bearer, reserved, malformed) and keeps Connect off; a half Access pair warns in orange and Connect stays on (Decision 3). The form loads the saved record once per presentation, so coming back from the editor keeps unsaved edits.
- The `.blocked` copy now points at Connection Headers (Preserve #880). Six strings in 17 languages, `needs_review`. Docs: `bots.md`, `multi-server-state-isolation.md`.
- Preserved: #824 (never from the webui store, never to `PushRelayClient`, dropped on a cross-host redirect), #889 (never logged), #751 (other advice rows unchanged).

title: bug(chat): message text scrolls under the navigation bar and overlaps the chat title
body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Open any chat with a long assistant reply (headings, bullet lists, code spans).
2. Scroll so the message text passes under the top navigation bar (back button, chat title + "workspace" subtitle, folder button).
3. Look at the top of the screen, also behind the status bar.

### Expected behavior
The navigation bar (and status bar area) has a background or scroll-edge effect, so content scrolling underneath is hidden or blurred and the chat title stays readable.

### Actual behavior
Content under the navigation bar is drawn at full opacity, right through it. The chat title and the message text underneath overlap and neither can be read. For example, a bold heading in the reply sits on top of the bold chat title and the two merge into one unreadable line. The same happens with text behind the status bar (clock and signal icons). Only the back and folder buttons have their own circular backgrounds, so they stay legible; the title and subtitle don't.

It happens both on the plain chat view and behind the "Approval required" sheet (#956).

### App version / commit
Hermex 1.7.0

### iOS version and device
iOS 27 on a 6.3" iPhone

### hermes-webui server version
hermes-webui 0.52.379 + Hermes Agent v2026.9.24 (v0.21.5)

### How the phone reaches the server
Tailscale

### Screenshots or screen recordings
No screenshot attached because the overlapping text is private conversation content. The steps above reproduce it with any long reply.

title: perf(hermes): keep the shared socket through Control Center and close it on background
body:
Stacked on #962; merge after it.

## Linked issue

Fixes #902

## What changed

Since #829 every Bot screen shares one gateway socket, but each screen left it on any non-active scene phase. Pulling down Control Center or a banner (`.inactive`) tore the socket down and every screen reconnected, which mid-turn also set off the #901 reattach. Nothing guaranteed a clean close on a real background.

Following the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/902#issuecomment-5922434534):
- **Screens** (chat, inbox, room, room profile, creator, room creator, profile editor) leave on `.background` only; `.inactive` keeps the socket and its frames. On `.active` a screen reopens only if it is not connected, read from model state: `BotConversation.isActive` (now `private(set)`), `link == .idle` for the inbox and rooms, and the new `BotProfileEditor.holdsConnection`. The creators reconnect on their next Create, as before.
- **One owner:** `ContentView` calls `HermesConnections.shared.closeForBackground()` on `.background`. The gateway closes the socket once and silently, logging `cN socket sM closed, app in background` (serials only, per #889). `.active` gives one fresh socket, a new ticket and one handshake.
- **Docs:** the `HermesGateway` header and `end()` comments, and the gateway section and log list in `docs/agents/bots.md`.
- Preserved: #825, #533 (rooms stop on background, dismissal or socket loss), #775, #901 (frames held during reattach). The Live Activity still goes stale on background.

## How it was tested

New: `HermesGatewayTests/testTheBackgroundClosesTheSocketOnceAndSilently` (one silent close, in-flight call fails `.transport`, no `onDisconnect`, the return makes one socket with a second ticket and one `client.capabilities`), plus hosted scene-phase tests for `BotChatView`, `BotsInboxView` and `BotProfileEditorView` (`.inactive` keeps the connection, `.background` then `.active` reconnects once).

- Red on unchanged scene handling: Control Center made the chat suspend and recover (`3` not `1`); the inbox closed and opened a second wire after `.inactive` (`1` not `0`); the editor reloaded twice (`2` not `1`). The gateway test cannot compile against the old API.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` HermesGatewayTests, BotConversationTests, BotInboxTests, BotRoomTests, BotRoomManagementTests, BotProfileEditorTests, BotLifecycleTests, BotChatPresentationTests, HermesConnectionTests, HermesConnectionLogTests, BotClientTests, BotPendingRequestTests: 336 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing).
- The three hosted tests with `--repeat 30`: 90 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>`; selection and results above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (none changed)

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator

1. (iPhone, over the tunnel) Start a long reply in a Bot Chat. Mid-turn, pull down Control Center, dismiss it, then let a notification banner come and go. Expected: no reconnect flash, and the tool rows stay.
2. (iPhone) Go home for about 2 minutes, then return. Expected: the Live Activity went stale while away, and the chat reconnects quietly.
3. (iPhone) Open a bot's profile editor from its chat, go home and return; again while the editor is still loading. Expected: it reloads with no failure, and Console shows `closed, app in background`, not `last screen left`.
4. (iPhone) Open the new-bot creator sheet, go home and return. Expected: the sheet stays up with its models listed; no Create needed.
5. (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5), regular width) Show the inbox and a chat side by side, background the app, then return. Expected: one reconnect; the log shows one new socket and one ticket.

title: fix(live-activity): open a tapped activity's session on the server it belongs to
body:
## Context

A Live Activity records the server its run belongs to (`AgentRunActivityAttributes.server`), but the tap link for a webui session drops it. `AgentRunTapTarget.url(for:)` in `HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift` builds `HermesDeepLink.sessionURL(sessionID:)`, which is `hermes-agent://session?id=<id>` with no server. `ContentView.handleOpenURL` then hands the bare ID to `pendingDeepLinkedSessionID`, which opens it on whatever server is active.

Bot activities are unaffected: their `destinationURL` already carries `server`, and `routeBot` switches servers. Push notification taps are unaffected too: `WebuiPushDestination` (`HermesMobile/Push/PushNotificationRouter.swift`) builds `hermes-agent://webui-push?server=…&id=…` and `route(state:servers:)` switches to the owning server, waits for sign-in, or ignores an unknown server.

## Current behavior

With two configured servers, A active and a run's Live Activity from B on the Lock Screen, tapping the activity opens session `<id>` against A. Depending on A, that shows an error, an empty chat, or a different session that happens to share the ID.

## Expected behavior

Tapping a webui Live Activity opens its session on the server that owns it, switching servers if needed, the same way a push notification tap does.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A webui Live Activity whose attributes carry a `server` taps through to a link that names that server, and the app routes it through the same path as `WebuiPushDestination` (switch server, wait for sign-in, or ignore a server that's no longer configured).
- [ ] An activity with no recorded server (persisted by a build before 1.7.0) keeps today's bare `session?id=` link and behavior.
- [ ] The link builder the widget uses lives in code the widget target compiles (`HermesDeepLink.swift` is shared with the widget; `PushNotificationRouter.swift` is main-app only). Make an explicit target-membership decision and don't duplicate the URL format: one builder, one parser.
- [ ] Bot activity links are unchanged.
- [ ] Tests: the widget's tap URL for a webui activity with and without a server; a round trip through the parser `handleOpenURL` uses.

## Validation plan

- Focused XCTest: `LiveActivityTests` plus whatever covers `WebuiPushDestination` parsing and routing.
- Simulator, two configured servers: start a run on B, switch to A, lock, and tap the activity. Expected: the app switches to B and opens the session. Repeat from A's login screen. Then remove B and tap again. Expected: nothing opens on A.

## Non-goals

- Dismissing a finished activity on tap (#970, which builds on this one).
- Changing the push notification tap route.

title: feat(live-activity): remove a finished Live Activity when it's tapped
body:
## Context

A user report: "Make live notifications disappear when we tap on them, they stay there like forever."

Tapping a Live Activity (Lock Screen, or the expanded or compact Dynamic Island) only opens its `widgetURL` (`AgentRunTapTarget.url(for:)` in `HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift`). Nothing ends the activity. A finished activity stays until its dismissal date: the app's local end uses 300 s for complete and 30 s for failed or cancelled (`AgentLiveActivityManager.dismissalPolicy(for:)`), and since #888 / uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#18 the relay's `end` push carries the same dates. Before #888, a relay-ended activity could stay for up to 4 h.

## Current behavior

A user taps a finished activity, the app opens the session, and the activity is still there when they lock the phone again.

## Expected behavior

Tapping a **finished** activity (`isFinal`: complete, failed or cancelled) opens it as today and removes that activity at once. Tapping an unfinished one (running, waiting, waiting for approval or clarification, stale) opens it and leaves it up.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The widget's tap link carries the tapped activity's `context.activityID` as a query item (for example `activity=<id>`) on both the webui session link and the bot link (`bot.destinationURL`). Existing parsers ignore unknown query items; confirm `HermesDeepLink.sessionID(from:)`, `HermesDeepLink.botDestination(from:)` and `WebuiPushDestination(url:)` still parse.
- [ ] On open, `ContentView.handleOpenURL` (or one helper it calls first) looks up `Activity<AgentRunActivityAttributes>.activities` by that exact ID. If the activity is final, or its `activityState` is `.ended`, it ends it with `dismissalPolicy: .immediate` and retires its push registration the way the other end paths do (`retirePush`). Routing then continues unchanged.
- [ ] An unfinished activity is never ended or changed by a tap.
- [ ] A link without the activity ID (an activity rendered by an older build) or with an ID that no longer exists only opens; nothing else is ended. There's no fallback match by session ID.
- [ ] If the tapped activity is the one `AgentLiveActivityManager` still tracks, the manager's in-memory state stays consistent (reset, as `endOrphanedActivity` does for its current stream), so the next run in that session starts clean.
- [ ] Applies to webui and bot activities alike, and to activities the relay ended by push.
- [ ] Tests: the dismiss decision as a pure policy (final, ended, running, waiting, stale, missing ID, unknown ID); the widget URL carries the ID for webui and bot activities; the parsers above still accept links carrying the extra item.

## Validation plan

- Focused XCTest: `LiveActivityTests`, `BotLiveActivityTests`, `BotDeepLinkTests`.
- Simulator (`build_run_sim`), Live Activities enabled:
  1. Finish a webui run with the app backgrounded, then tap the finished activity on the Lock Screen. Expected: the session opens; after locking again, the activity is gone.
  2. Tap a running activity. Expected: the session opens and the activity keeps updating.
  3. Tap an activity waiting for approval. Expected: it stays.
  4. Repeat 1 for a bot turn.
  5. Repeat 1 from the Dynamic Island on a device with one.
- Physical iPhone on a push-paired server: let the relay end a run while locked, then tap. Expected: it's removed immediately rather than after 5 min.
- Confirm `end(_:dismissalPolicy: .immediate)` removes an already-ended activity that is still showing its final state; if ActivityKit refuses, record what it does instead in the PR.

## Non-goals

- Dismissing when the session is opened another way: the session list, foregrounding the app, or a notification banner tap.
- Changing the 300 s / 30 s dismissal dates, or anything in the relay.
- The cross-server tap route (#969). Land #969 first: both change `AgentRunTapTarget.url(for:)`, and the `activity` item rides on whichever link #969 produces.

title: feat(hermes): a Hermes server kind with its own sign-in
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #899

Stacked on #964; merge after it.

## What changed

Every configured server was a webui server. A Hermes host was only a side connection under one, usable only while that webui sign-in held.

- **Kind.** `ServerAccount` gains `kind` (`webui` | `hermes`; missing or unknown → webui) and `serverVersion`. One unreadable registry entry no longer drops the whole list. A Hermes server's id is its address as `BotConnection.address(_:)` parses it.
- **Sign-in record.** The same `BotConnection` under `bot_connection::<its URL>`, so every Bot store works unchanged (Decision 1).
- **AuthManager.** `addHermesServer` needs Bot Mode and refuses a configured address (so does webui onboarding). Restore, switch and removal enter a Hermes server `.loggedIn` only while its record exists, with no webui headers. Sign Out keeps the server and deletes its record and Bot data; removal skips the relay, the webui logout and same-host cookies. A webui 401 never signs it out.
- **Refused password.** `HermesConnection` reports a login-step 401, including the silent re-login, through `HermesConnections.onSignInRejected`; only the active Hermes server goes `.loggedOut`. #884's per-screen flag is unchanged.
- **Root** ([home C, Settings B, sign-in A](https://37cb011rg61x.postplan.dev)). Signed in: `HermesServerHome`, the inbox as root of one stack, full width on iPad (D5), the server's avatar in place of the gear (tap: Settings, hold: switcher). Signed out: `HermesServerSignIn`, the form as root, address locked, password focused, no Remove or Done, the avatar as the way out (D3); errors sit under the password (D4).
- **Settings** on a Hermes server skips every webui load and hides those rows, plus Main Page, Sessions, Archived, Notifications and Offline Data (D2). Its Active Server card shows the connection and version. In Settings → Servers its button is Remove Server, and saving its sign-in there signs it back in.
- **Entry points.** New-chat links and intents, session links and shares switch to the first webui server; with none, an alert explains and a queued share can be discarded or kept. Bot links for a Hermes server open with Bot Mode off. Shortcuts Profiles come only from a webui server. Live Activity reconciliation skips Hermes servers.
- **Dev.** `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`; `HERMEX_BOT_*` can point it at `scripts/local-hermes`. Docs: bots.md, multi-server-state-isolation.md, CONTEXT.md, DEVELOPMENT.md. Five strings in 17 languages.

Decisions applied: [Uzair, 2026-09-30](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/899#issuecomment-5922433976) (D2–D5) and the issue's Decisions 1–6.

## How it was tested

- Red: `ServerRegistryTests/testOneUnreadableEntryLeavesTheRestOfTheListLoaded` on unchanged code: `("[]") is not equal to ("["https://a.test"]")`. The other new tests call API the old code lacks, so they can't compile there.
- `scripts/test-sim`, one `--only` per class: ServerRegistry, AuthManagerState, HermesConnection, BotInbox, BotConversation, BotRoom, BotDeepLink, BotModeGate, BotConnectionVersion, BotConnectionSetup, BotConnectionAdvice, AppIntentNewChatInProfile, AppIntentNewChat, LocalizationCatalog, CustomHeaderInjection, HermesGateway, HermexPushProvisioning: 398 passed, 0 failed. After the review fixes: LocalizationCatalog, AuthManagerState, BotConnectionVersion: 51 passed.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 35 OK. `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 2113 keys. `git diff --check` clean.
- Signed Debug build against `scripts/local-hermes`: `sim-login --hermes` lands on the Hermes home, without the flag on the webui list; sign out, wrong and right password, switcher, new-chat link to the webui server, a bot chat pushing.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator, physical iPhone

iPhone simulator, after `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`:
1. [Hermes server only: remove the webui server in Settings → Servers] Share a photo to Hermex, then open it. Expected: "Add a WebUI server to start a chat." with Discard and Cancel. Cancel, leave and return: offered again. Discard: gone.
2. Settings → Account → Sign Out, then avatar → Settings → Servers → the Hermes server. Expected: its button reads Remove Server; Hermes connection there with the right password returns to the inbox.

iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5)), after `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`:
1. Expected: the inbox fills the width in one column; a chat pushes over it, and Back returns.
2. Tap the avatar: Settings pushes in the same stack. Hold it: the Servers menu; pick the webui server. Expected: its usual session list and Bots row.
3. Switch back, Settings → Account → Sign Out. Expected: the sign-in form fills the screen, password focused, no Done; a wrong password's error shows under the password field, above the keyboard; the right one returns to the inbox.

Physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight):
1. Install over the previous build. Expected: every existing server opens on its session list, with its Bots row and Hermes connection unchanged. A Hermes server on a phone waits for #900's add UI (dev sign-in is Debug-only).

title: feat(hermes): add a Hermes server from onboarding and Settings
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #900

Stacked on #971; merge after it.

## What changed

Onboarding and Add Server only understood the webui. A Hermes dashboard address failed with webui errors, and the connection help assumed Tailscale. Both entry points now share one connect form (`OnboardingViewModel`, `entry: .onboarding | .addServer`):

- **Kind detection (Decision 1).** The first Connect, Add or Test Connection reads the public `/api/status` at `BotConnection.address(_:)`'s URL, with the form's headers, through a new `HermesConnection.status()`. A JSON object carrying `auth_required` is Hermes. Hermes' own Host-header 400 (`"Invalid Host header…"`) and `.blocked` show their advice and stop. Anything else, including any other 400, goes to today's webui path unchanged.
- **Hermes branch.** Username and password appear. The next Connect signs in once on its own `HermesConnection`, so #897's version gate, #777's install check and #880's copy apply, with no retry (#884). It then calls `AuthManager.addHermesServer` (#899). An address already configured is refused before the password goes out.
- **Reuse (Decision 6).** `AuthManager.savedHermesSignIns(at:)` offers a webui server's side connection only at exactly the same parsed URL, never by `install_id`. Accepting it fills username, password and headers. The new record gets a fresh UUID and still expects the source's `install_id`. The copies stay until the address parses to another URL (even one differing only in scheme) or a webui answers there. Then they all leave, including any header row that still carries a copied value.
- **Gate (Decision 4).** With Bot Mode off, a found dashboard offers "Turn on Bot Mode (beta) and continue".
- **Connection mode (Decision 2).** Same Wi-Fi, Private network (the default) or Cloudflare Tunnel. It isn't saved. It changes only the placeholder, the help and two empty `CF-Access-Client-*` rows, and it leaves any error showing.
- **D6 and D7.** Header rows without a value are never sent or saved. "Will connect to" shows the Hermes parser's URL until a webui answers, then `AuthManager.normalizedServerURL`'s.
- **Copy (#170).** The welcome and network pages now say "private network" and name Tailscale and NetBird. The webui setup prompt is unchanged (Decision 3). 26 new strings ship in 17 languages (needs_review), and 7 replaced keys are removed. Docs: bots.md, multi-server-state-isolation.md, CONTEXT.md and README.

Decisions applied: [Uzair, 2026-09-30](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/900#issuecomment-5922434153) (D6, D7) and the issue's Decisions 1–7.

## Design

[Mocks](https://typw3cvuz88l.postplan.dev). Picks: mode control B (three choice rows), reuse offer A (an inline row above the fields), status next to the address, and a full-width URL row in Add Server.

## How it was tested

- Red: the new tests on #899 with an inert API scaffold: 10 failed, for example `testAHermesStatusRevealsTheDashboardSignInAndNeverReachesTheWebui`: `("nil") is not equal to ("Optional(HermesMobile.ServerKind.hermes)")`. The review fixes on the pre-fix form: 3 failed. A plain-text 400 never reached `/health`. A scheme-only edit kept the copied password (`("saved") is not equal to ("")`) and the Access secret. A mode switch cleared the advice.
- `scripts/test-sim`: OnboardingViewModelIdentity, OnboardingFlow, AuthManagerState, BotConnectionSetup, LocalizationCatalog, HermesConnection and BotModeGate: 113 passed. After the first review fixes: OnboardingViewModelIdentity, AuthManagerState, OnboardingFlow, HermesConnection and BotConnectionSetup: 103 passed. After the bot review: OnboardingViewModelIdentity, AuthManagerState and OnboardingFlow: 70 passed. `ci/check_string_catalog.py` covers all 2132 keys. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Signed Debug build on iPhone 17e: Add Server on the live tunnel made one read-only `GET /api/status` and showed the reuse offer and the fields. No sign-in.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator, physical iPhone

iPhone simulator, fresh install with no `sim-login` (Bot Mode is off):
1. On the welcome page, expect "private network, such as Tailscale or NetBird". On Connect, tap each mode. Expect only the placeholder and help to change. Cloudflare Tunnel also opens Advanced with empty `CF-Access-Client-Id` and `CF-Access-Client-Secret` rows.
2. Type the webui address and Connect. Expect today's password step, then the session list.
3. Reinstall, type a Hermes dashboard address (the tunnel or `scripts/local-hermes`) and Connect. Expect the "Turn on Bot Mode (beta) and continue" card. Tap it. Expect Username and Password to appear, with the cursor in Username.
4. At AX5 text size, then in the RTL pseudolanguage, repeat step 3. Expect the three mode rows and the card to wrap without clipping, and "Will connect to" and the placeholders to read left to right.

iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5)), after `sim-login` (a webui server with a saved Hermes connection):
1. Hold the avatar, then Add Server…. Expect a sheet with the Network card (Private network checked) and a full-width URL row.
2. Type the Hermes dashboard address and tap Add. Expect "Will connect to", "Use the sign-in saved on <webui server>", Username and Password. Accept, set a name and color, then Add. Expect the sheet to close on the Hermes home, showing that name and color.
3. [two Hermes dashboards, such as the tunnel and `scripts/local-hermes`] From the Hermes home, hold the avatar and add the other dashboard with a name and color. Expect the same result.
4. Turn Bot Mode off and repeat step 2 up to Add. Expect the opt-in card to fit the sheet.

title: feat(design-system): add shared foundations and catalog
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #607

Issue #607 was narrowed on October 4, 2026 to the reusable Design System foundations and retained catalog. Normal production adoption and screen-by-screen migration belong to separate bounded issues, so this PR completes the foundation scope without claiming migration is finished.

## What changed

- Adds first-party typography, color, spacing, radius, shadow, icon-size, and motion foundations with Dynamic Type and platform accessibility behavior.
- Adds reusable SwiftUI component and pattern foundations without migrating normal production screens onto them.
- Adds the retained in-repository Expo/React Native catalog, generated machine-readable manifest, component-selection guidance, icon references, and deterministic validation tooling.
- Addresses the maintainer's requested correction areas: localization and accessibility copy, composer-focus coverage, reliable overlay validation, Segmented Control sizing, declared motion durations, truthful catalog/guidance, the native-control audit policy, and retirement of the stale duplicate session-row implementation.
- Fixes the catalog Loading and Shimmer Reduce Motion startup race: motion remains static while the preference is unresolved or enabled and begins only after an explicit no-preference result.
- Fixes catalog-owned React diagnostics by passing Icon primitive keys directly and using platform-appropriate SVG accessibility props for Icon and circular Loading.

## Production boundary

This is a foundations-and-catalog change, not a production migration.

- No normal production screen imports the new Issue #607 foundation APIs, components, or tokens. Pre-existing production components documented by the catalog remain explicitly marked production-adopted; this PR does not migrate them.
- Search and Selection Sheet are foundation-available in the component set and catalog; this PR does not migrate normal production callers to either foundation.
- `TopNav` and `ListItem` provide reusable foundation behavior without claiming all production toolbars or picker rows have adopted them.
- `AppTheme.swift`, `TranscriptLogRowView.swift`, `TranscriptLogRowBodyWindowTests.swift`, and `CustomAttachmentPicker.swift` are byte-identical to current `origin/master`.
- The app target contains the new foundation files and a `#if DEBUG` `--hermex-overlay-lab` launch hook for inspection.
- The adoption audit includes a fail-closed disconnection boundary for the three production files that briefly gained Issue #607 dependencies. Legitimate future adoption remains allowed, but must update that boundary explicitly in the same bounded change.
- No server/API, networking, authentication, Push, Live Activity, or multi-server contract changes.

## Catalog and dependency boundary

- The shipped catalog is the retained Expo/React Native catalog under `design-system-catalog/native-preview`; the separate experimental Vite/React catalog is not included.
- Catalog examples are browser reconstructions grounded in native SwiftUI foundation and component source contracts; adoption claims are limited to verified normal-runtime callers and are stated explicitly per entry.
- The iOS app adds no third-party dependency. The catalog retains its existing npm toolchain and known dependency advisories, which this PR does not claim to resolve.
- Fresh browser verification on October 5, 2026 reports one dependency-origin React diagnostic for `collapsable={false}` from the pinned `react-native-web` ScrollView plus existing `shadow*`, `pointerEvents`, and web `useNativeDriver` development warnings. Candidate-owned key-spread and SVG accessibility-prop errors are resolved.
- `Design System Contract` is a required PR-CI dependency. Catalog-only changes skip the macOS XCTest job but still run the Node/TypeScript, manifest, design-system-guide, repository-location, and adoption-audit contracts.

## Verification

Verified on the final local candidate before publication:

- `scripts/test-sim AD2688B6-5D45-468C-86B3-FBCF31E605B8` — **4,276 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.
- The four maintainer-named overlay tests — **4 passed, 0 failed** on the established simulator whose SwiftUI accessibility tree is available.
- The same four tests on fresh iOS 27 and iOS 26.5 simulators — **2 passed, 0 failed, 2 capability-gated skips** on each. The geometry and hit-testing contracts remain active; only accessibility Escape dispatch is skipped when an independent normal SwiftUI accessibility probe proves that the simulator published no in-process accessibility tree.
- `node --test design-system-catalog/test/hermes-catalog.test.mjs` — **411 passed, 0 failed**.

Unprotected orphan copies are reclaimed first. No cleanup UI is added.

Serialized admission, persisted recency and ownership leases protect open composers, restores, uploads, queued sends and shared copies. title: docs(contributing): promise a first answer and say how PRs get closed
body:
**What the user gets:** An outside contributor knows before writing code what will be accepted, how soon they will hear back, and why a PR or issue was closed.
**Why it matters:** 8 outside PRs are open and 6 have no word from the maintainer; the oldest have waited since mid-August. The policy below has to exist before those can be answered by citing it.
**Cost:** Small. Docs only, nothing to test by hand.

## Context

Decided with Uzair on 2026-10-02 after comparing Hermex with how `pingdotgg/t3code` handles outside contributions. Hermex keeps its narrow door (small fixes welcome, anything bigger needs approval first) and adds the three things that door was missing: a response promise, a stated way PRs get closed, and a visible approval signal.

Two sentences are taken from t3code's `CONTRIBUTING.md` in spirit: opening a PR creates no obligation to review or merge it, and every policy closure names the rule, the evidence, and how to get reconsidered.

## Current behavior

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` § "What PRs we welcome" says to "open an issue first and wait for a maintainer nod", but nothing says what a nod looks like, how long an answer takes, or when a PR is closed.
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` asks for a linked issue and nothing about approval.

## Expected behavior

### `CONTRIBUTING.md`

1. **§ "What PRs we welcome (and what we don't)"**: add, in plain words, that Hermex has one maintainer and limited review time, and that opening a PR does not create an obligation to review or merge it. Keep the existing welcome list and the one-logical-change rule.

2. **New section "What to expect"**, placed after "What PRs we welcome":
   - **First answer within 7 days.** Every outside issue, and every outside PR once it is marked ready for review, gets a public first answer within 7 days. An answer is a review, a question, a label with a short reply, or a closure. It is not a promise to merge.
   - **Who writes it.** Triage replies may be drafted by the maintainer's coding agent. Each one says so, naming the model and harness, and the maintainer approves it before it is posted.
   - **How things get closed.** A closure names the rule in this file that applies, the evidence for it, and what would get it reconsidered. Closed work can be reopened.
   - **The 30-day rule.** A draft PR with no activity from its author for 30 days is closed with a "reopen when ready" note. An issue where the maintainer asked a public question and the reporter has not answered for 30 days is closed the same way. The clock starts at the question, not at a label.

3. **§ "PR workflow", step 1 ("Start from an issue")**: say what approval is.
   - Small fixes (a bug fix, test coverage, a docs correction) need a linked issue and nothing more.
   - For anything larger, comment on the issue asking to take it. The maintainer assigns the issue to you on GitHub; that assignment is the go-ahead.
   - Say why: issues that are not assigned to a contributor may be built by the maintainer's agents at any time, including overnight, so an unassigned issue is not reserved.

### `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

- In the "Linked issue" comment, add one line: for anything larger than a small fix, the issue must be assigned to you (link to the `CONTRIBUTING.md` section). No new heading and no new checklist item.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` states the no-obligation sentence, the 7-day first answer, who drafts replies, how closures are written, the 30-day rule with its clock, and approval by assignment.
- [ ] The PR template's "Linked issue" comment mentions assignment and links the section.
- [ ] Every relative link and anchor added resolves.
- [ ] No other file changes.

## Validation plan

Docs only: no XCTest run. `git diff --check`, and follow each new link once in the rendered Markdown.

## Non-goals

- No workflow, bot, or scheduled job. The weekly inbox session and the triage skills live outside this repo.
- No size or trust labels on PRs, and no stale bot.
- No change to what kinds of PRs are welcome.
- Agent-side rules (agents skip assigned issues) belong to #993, not this one.

title: docs(agents): plan each release with a milestone and a plain header on every issue
body:
**What the user gets:** Uzair can open any issue and see in three lines what it is for, and can see "what's next" as one short list on GitHub: the open release milestone.
**Why it matters:** The work queue is a 51-item ranking in a local cache, written by an agent and not reflected on GitHub. Issue bodies are specs for the implementing agent, so the owner cannot judge importance or order. 15 open issues carry no triage role.
**Cost:** Medium. Docs plus label and milestone changes on GitHub; nothing to test by hand.

## Context

Decided with Uzair on 2026-10-02. `pingdotgg/t3code` was the comparison, but it tracks no plan in public (no milestones, assignees, or roadmap), so everything here is ordinary open-source practice fitted to how Hermex already works: the owner picks, agents implement, `master` is the release candidate.

Planning stays private in purpose: the milestone is for the maintainer and agents. It is not a public roadmap or a promise.

## Current behavior

- `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md:32`: "Pick implementation work from issues labeled `ready-for-agent`". Nothing says which of the 31 such issues comes first or belongs to the next release.
- `AGENTS.md:59` repeats the same rule.
- No milestone exists. Releases happen when the owner judges `master` ready.
- Issue bodies open with the spec. 7 open issues carry an ad-hoc `**Priority:** Pn` line that no doc defines.
- `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` lists the triage roles but does not say an issue must have one, and its component table omits `area:kanban`, which exists.
- Labels `audit` (25 uses) and `improve` (101 uses) both mean "found by an audit". `good first issue`, `help wanted`, `question`, and `invalid` have never been used. `duplicate` has never been used, though 44 issues were closed as not planned.

## Expected behavior

### `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`

1. **New section "Issue body"**: every issue opens with a plain header written for the owner, above the spec:

   ```
   **What the user gets:** one sentence.
   **Why it matters:** who asked, or what breaks without it.
   **Cost:** Small, Medium, or Large, and whether it needs the owner's hands on a phone.
   ```

   - Issues created by the maintainer or an agent carry it at the top of the body.
   - On an outside reporter's issue, do not edit their words: the header goes in the maintainer's first triage comment.
   - Do not write a `Priority: Pn` line. Order comes from the milestone.

2. **New section "Release milestones"**:
   - One open milestone per release, named for the marketing version (`1.9`). A serious bug found after shipping gets a patch milestone (`1.9.1`).
   - Everything in the milestone is intended for that release. The release ships when the milestone has no open issues, no open `release-blocker` issue exists, and the RC checklist in `TESTFLIGHT.md` passes.
   - To ship sooner, the owner moves what is left to the next milestone. Agents never move an issue into or out of a milestone without the owner saying so.
   - An issue with no milestone is backlog. Backlog is unranked.

3. **§ "Branch and PR Workflow"**: replace "Pick implementation work from issues labeled `ready-for-agent`" with: work comes from the open release milestone, or from an issue the owner names. The triage label says how the issue runs (express or staged); the milestone says when. Skip any issue assigned to someone other than the maintainer: that contributor has been given the go-ahead (`CONTRIBUTING.md`).

4. **New section "Choosing the next release"**: the owner picks. An agent's job is a shortlist of about 10 candidates, each shown by its plain header with the evidence for it; the agent does not rank the whole backlog.

5. **New section "Bulk findings"**: when an agent produces many findings at once (an audit, a review sweep), it gives the owner one list of plain one-liners, and only the accepted ones become issues. Children of an epic the owner already approved are exempt.

### `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`

- State the rule: every open issue carries exactly one triage role.
- Agents apply labels without asking. Closing an issue and posting a public comment still need the owner's approval.
- `needs-info` means a question was asked publicly and the reporter has not answered. An issue waiting on the owner is `ready-for-human`.
- `duplicate`: close as a duplicate with a link to the original, instead of "not planned".
- `improve` is the one label for audit findings.
- Add the missing `area:kanban` row to the component table.

### `AGENTS.md`

- Line 59: "Implement only the issue the maintainer selected or one labeled `ready-for-agent`" becomes "...or one in the open release milestone labeled `ready-for-agent`". `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink and follows.

### `TESTFLIGHT.md`

- § "Release gates": add that the release's milestone has no open issues. (The `P0/P1` wording in the same list is changed by #994; leave it here.)

### GitHub, through `gh` (not part of the PR)

Run these after the PR merges and list each in a comment on this issue:

- Create milestone `1.9`. Leave it empty; the backlog walk fills it.
- Add `improve` to every issue and PR labeled `audit`, then delete `audit`.
- Delete `good first issue`, `help wanted`, `question`, `invalid` after confirming each still has zero uses.
- Move [#209](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/209) from `needs-info` to `ready-for-human`.
- Keep the five `wayfinder:*` labels.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `issue-tracker.md` defines the plain header, release milestones, where work comes from, the shortlist, and the bulk-findings gate.
- [ ] `triage-labels.md` states the one-role rule, who may apply labels, the `needs-info` meaning, `duplicate`, the single audit label, and lists `area:kanban`.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md:59` and `TESTFLIGHT.md` § "Release gates" match.
- [ ] Milestone `1.9` exists; `audit` and the four unused defaults are gone; no issue lost a label it needed; #209 is `ready-for-human`.
- [ ] This issue's own body follows the header it defines.

## Validation plan

Docs only: no XCTest run. `git diff --check`. For the label work, record the before and after counts from `gh label list` and a search for each deleted label in the issue comment.

## Non-goals

- No GitHub Project board, no priority labels, no public roadmap.
- No rewriting of existing issue bodies: the backlog walk adds headers issue by issue with the owner.
- No change to the triage skills; they live outside this repo and are edited separately.
- No change to `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md`, whose `P0/P1` scale ranks upstream parity gaps, not issues.

title: feat(bots): show a Copy button in the Bot reply footer
body:
## Linked issue
Fixes #804

## What changed
Settled Bot replies had no visible Copy button. Text-bearing replies now show the existing Copy control between React and reaction chips, even without timestamps or reactions. Copy preserves original Markdown and the haptics preference, with no duplicate content VoiceOver action. Sessions, prompts, live replies, delegation cards, and rooms keep their behavior.

Applies the [binding decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/804#issuecomment-5944558386).

## Design
[Approved trivial control reuse](https://yi8t3kbh9xf4.postplan.dev#issue-804): footer order More, Copy, chips, time; footer stays outside selectable text.

## How it was tested
- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/BotMessageActionsTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatMessageMetaTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotRoomTests`: 105 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Hosted view red: missing-Copy assertion failed against the old view (1 failed); green asserts one Copy control and no duplicate custom action.
- Initial red: tests could not compile against unchanged production code because `BotMessageActions.footerCopy` did not exist; 0 tests executed. Fixture initializer errors were corrected before isolating this failure.
- `git diff --check` passed; `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` passed with existing warnings, none in changed files.
- `~/.agents/skills/hermex-flow/scripts/run-sim.sh D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A`: signed Debug build, install, and launch passed. Rebase onto latest `origin/master` made no changes. After the review test fix, all four classes were rerun.

## Checklist
- [x] Local validation passes; selection and results above
- [x] No changed Codable models
- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] No new endpoints or wire shapes

## Manual test
Owner merge-walk checks; no live-host writes are needed.
Device: iPhone simulator (iPhone Air)
1. Open an existing settled Markdown Bot reply. Verify More, Copy, chips when present, time; select text and confirm the footer stays outside selection.
2. Tap Copy and paste into the unsent composer: original Markdown is preserved. Disable Message Timestamps and check a reply without reactions: Copy remains visible. Clear the unsent paste and restore the preference.
3. With VoiceOver, confirm one footer Copy control and no duplicate Copy action on reply text; at large Dynamic Type, confirm the footer remains usable.
Device: iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))
1. At regular width, repeat footer order and text selection checks on an existing settled Markdown reply.
2. Copy/paste into the unsent composer with timestamps disabled and no reactions; confirm original Markdown and visible Copy, then clear the paste and restore the preference.
3. At large Dynamic Type and with VoiceOver, confirm usable layout and a single Copy control.
Device: physical iPhone
1. In the combined Branch TestFlight build, copy a settled reply with haptics enabled, then disabled; feedback follows the preference. Restore the preference.

Model: gpt-6-astra, medium effort. Harness: Codex CLI.

title: feat(bots): save or share an attachment from the Bot preview
body:
**What the user gets:** Save to Files and a share sheet on the attachment preview in a Bot Chat, so a file the agent produced can leave the app without a detour.
**Why it matters:** A user reported having to open a bot's own conversation to get at a file they could already see. The preview they were sent to has no way to keep it.
**Cost:** Small. One screen, one toolbar, reusing the existing export document. Needs the owner's hands on a phone to confirm the Files and share flows.

## Context

Reported in chat: "files sent in group chats cannot be downloaded directly. PDFs, images, and videos can be viewed, but to download them, I have to open the bot's profile and access the conversation session."

Triage checked that premise against the code and it does not hold. Group rooms do not render attachments at all: `BotRoomEventView` sends member text through `MarkdownRenderer` on `payload["text"]` alone (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotRoomView.swift:305`, `:329`), so there is no thumbnail, no tap target and no viewer. The room composer is text-only, matching `attachments=False` in the room capability catalog (`.codex-tmp/hermes-agent/tui_gateway/methods_groups.py:162`). At the pinned upstream SHA a room `message.user` payload is validated with `_exact_fields` against `{text, thread_id}` (`.codex-tmp/hermes-agent/gateway/hosted_room_discussion.py:60,200,369`), so an `attachments` key is a protocol error, not an ignored field. Room attachments are an upstream project and are out of scope here.

The real defect is one surface over. A Bot attachment is viewable and not exportable: `BotArtifactPreview` renders Quick Look with a single-item toolbar (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactPreview.swift:64`). `QuickLookFileView` is a child inside Hermex's own `NavigationStack`, so Quick Look's share chrome is not reachable either. There is no Save to Files, no share sheet, no other way out.

## Current behavior

`BotArtifactPreview` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactPreview.swift:38-68`) is presented from two places:

- assistant artifacts in a Bot Chat (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotArtifactMessageView.swift:76-80`)
- a staged attachment in the composer strip (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotChatComposerView.swift:191`)

`BotArtifactPreviewModel` (`:7-36`) downloads the bytes once, writes them through `QuickLookTemporaryFile.write` (`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/QuickLookFilePreview.swift:53-66`) and keeps only the temporary file handle. `cleanup()` drops it, and `QuickLookTemporaryFile.deinit` deletes the directory it created (`:48-50`). The bytes are discarded, so nothing downstream can reuse them.

`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/` contains no `.fileExporter` and no `ShareLink`. Export exists only in Sessions chat (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/TranscriptMediaView.swift:343,467,722`) and Workspace (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewView.swift:109`).

## Expected behavior

- [ ] The preview's toolbar carries **Save** (Files) and **Share** alongside Done. Both act on the bytes already fetched for Quick Look. No second request, no new cap, no change to `BotArtifactBuffer.maximumBytes` or the download transport.
- [ ] Save uses the established Workspace pattern verbatim: `ExportedFileDocument` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FileExportSupport.swift:6`) behind `.fileExporter`, resolving `UTType(filenameExtension:) ?? .data` and the last path component of `reference.displayName`, matching `FilePreviewViewModel.exportPayload()` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewViewModel.swift:120,173`). Sanitize the filename the way `QuickLookTemporaryFile.write` already does, falling back to `File` for an empty or dot name.
- [ ] Share is a `ShareLink` over the preview's temporary file URL, the pattern already used for session export (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListComponents.swift:1163`). A downloaded temporary file stays on disk until the sheet dismisses, so the URL is valid for the whole presentation.
- [ ] Both controls are absent while loading and on the error state, where there are no bytes. They never appear on a failed or oversized download.
- [ ] A failed export raises an alert naming the real cause, mirroring `FilePreviewView`'s "Export Failed" (`:123-138`). Never silent, never a success the user cannot confirm.
- [ ] Dismissing mid-export leaves no orphan directory: `cleanup()` and the exporter must not race. A late completion is dropped by the existing `generation` guard.
- [ ] Accessibility labels name the file, as `FilePreviewView` does. Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion, light and dark. New strings go to the String Catalog per `docs/agents/i18n.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `BotArtifactPreview` presents three toolbar items once loaded, one while loading, and no export control on the error state.
- [ ] Opening a preview and exporting it issues exactly one download.
- [ ] Export filename and content type come from the reference's filename; a name with no extension exports as `.data`.
- [ ] Export failure presents an alert and leaves the preview usable.
- [ ] Dismissal during export deletes the temporary directory and writes nothing.

## Validation plan

- Focused XCTest on `BotArtifactPreviewModel`, extending `HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests.swift:110`: export payload derived from filename; one download across open and export; no payload after a failed or oversized download; `cleanup()` drops a late completion. Model and policy assertions only.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests`.
- Signed Debug `build_run_sim`, then manual on the phone: Save to Files and Share from a Bot Chat artifact and from a staged composer attachment; PDF, image, audio and a `.docx`; VoiceOver on the toolbar; Dynamic Type at AX5; Reduce Motion; light and dark; confirm a saved file opens from Files.
- `git diff --check`, `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes`.

## Non-goals

- Group rooms. No attachment rendering, no room download route. Needs an upstream change to the room payload contract first; file separately if it is still wanted.
- Save to Photos. Sessions chat has it (`TranscriptMediaView.swift:722`); not requested here.
- Composer upload, the `+` picker, or attachment sending.
- Refactoring the Sessions and Workspace export code into a shared component. Reuse `ExportedFileDocument` as it stands; extract only if it falls out for free.
- Changing the download cap, the 25 MB limit, or `fs/download`.

Model and harness: generated during intake.

title: feat(bots): show Desktop group chats read-only in the Bots inbox
body:
**What the user gets:** Group chats made in Hermes Desktop appear in the Bots inbox as read-only rooms showing their recent messages, instead of not appearing at all.
**Why it matters:** Uzair found during the 2026-10-02 merge walk that Desktop group chats and Hermex rooms never show up in each other's lists, so a room started on the Mac seems to vanish on the phone.
**Cost:** Small to Medium. Needs a phone check against a host with Desktop group chats.

## Why they don't cross over

Desktop and Hermex use two separate room systems on the same host:

- **Desktop Group Chats** are run by the Desktop client. It decides who speaks next and runs each member turn in a hidden session it owns. The full log lives in Desktop's plugin storage. Desktop never calls `groups.*`.
- **Hermex rooms** use the gateway's server-owned `groups.*` rooms (`HermesCall.swift`, `BotGroupRoom.swift`). No first-party upstream client uses them, so Desktop never lists them.

Desktop does write a bounded mirror "so mobile can show the same messages" ([group-chat.ts](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5c975b9ed8fc2a5d50263c321391fd4559e0b3e2/apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-chat.ts#L274-L279)). It goes into the default profile's `ui_meta["hermes-bots-groups"]`, on the same `profiles.list` row where we already read `ui_meta["hermes-bots"]`.

The upstream request to unify the two systems is [NousResearch/hermes-agent#131723](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/131723). This issue is the phone-side part, which works whether or not upstream acts.

## Scope

- Decode `hermes-bots-groups` tolerantly. The v3 shape is `{version, updatedAt, rooms, deleted?}`, where `rooms` is keyed `id:<roomId>` or `name:<name>` → `{name, roomId, log, members, revision, omitted?, image?, holdDetection?}`. A log entry is `{id, from:{kind, name, source?}, text (≤1200 chars), at (ms), thread?}`. `deleted` maps a room key to its tombstone revision. An unknown `version` hides the section; it never crashes.
- Show these rooms as Desktop group chats in the inbox, read-only: the last 16 messages, a note that earlier messages exist when `omitted` is set, and a plain "Continue in Desktop" line in place of the composer.
- Never write `hermes-bots-groups`. Desktop owns it, and a write from the phone would reach no bot.
- Rooms are scoped to the configured server and connection, like the rest of Bots.
- Refresh with the existing roster reads (open, pull to refresh, `sessions.changed`).

## Out of scope

- Continuing a Desktop room from the phone. That needs upstream #131723.
- Showing Hermex's `groups.*` rooms in Desktop. That is upstream's side.

## Verify before building

Check the live mirror's shape on the test host with a read-only `profiles.list`; the format has already changed from v1 to v3. Run the mock pass first: this adds visible UI.

title: fix(chat): keep the /goal notice from hiding the live conversation
body:
## Linked issue
Fixes #772

## What changed
The server's goal-set notice ("⊙ Goal set (N-turn budget): <whole goal>", then two more lines; upstream `api/goals.py:622-626`) stays pinned above the composer for the whole run. The pinned notice stack had no line limit, but the transcript reserved a fixed 60 pt per notice, so a long goal covered the newest tool calls, thinking and replies until the run ended.

- `PinnedLocalNoticeStack` caps each notice at two lines. VoiceOver still reads every notice in full, Goal → Status still shows the full goal, and `flushPinnedLocalNoticesToTranscript` still moves notices whole into the transcript.
- `ChatView` measures the notice stack with `onGeometryChange` (the run-status pill already works this way) and uses that height for the transcript inset and scroll-to-bottom offset instead of `count * 60`. The inset now also fits several notices and large Dynamic Type.
- Preserve (#326): the steering confirmation is still the transient card in the same stack. It never enters the transcript, and like every pinned notice it now stops at two lines.

Applies the [binding decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/772#issuecomment-5961799244) (A).

## Design
[Pick A, compact pinned card](https://i59lu7f6h93w.postplan.dev#issue-772)

## How it was tested
- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-3BDD-4474-924E-501BC7DBC2D3 --only HermesMobileTests/PinnedLocalNoticeStackTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatActiveRunStatusPolicyTests`: 11 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- New `PinnedLocalNoticeStackTests.testALongGoalNoticeStopsAtTwoLinesOnAPhone` hosts the stack at 361 pt with the upstream goal-set format. It checks that the notice is shorter than three footnote lines plus padding and taller than a one-line notice. Red against unchanged production code: `201.67 is not less than 70.54` (about 11 lines). With the fix it measures 57.67 pt.
- `git diff --check` clean. No test covers the measured inset; the manual steps below check it.

## Checklist
- [x] Local validation passes; selection and results above
- [x] No changed Codable models
- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] No new endpoints or wire shapes

## Manual test
Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11-inch (M5))
Physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight build), in a disposable chat:
1. Send a long `/goal` (two or more sentences). The goal card above the composer stops at two lines and ends in an ellipsis.
2. While it runs, stay at the bottom of the chat. The newest tool calls, thinking and replies stay visible just above the card and run-status pill. The transcript does not jump when the card first appears.
3. Goal menu → Status shows the full goal. When the run ends (or after Stop), the full goal-set notice appears as a transcript row.
4. At an accessibility text size (Settings → Accessibility → Larger Text), repeat step 2. With the card and the run-status pill both showing, the last message is not hidden behind them. Then clear the goal and delete the chat.
iPad simulator, regular width, in a disposable chat:
1. Send the same long `/goal`. The card stops at two lines, and the newest transcript content sits just above the card and run-status pill, not behind them. Then clear the goal and delete the chat.

Model: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context). Harness: Claude Code (hermex-batch lane).

title: feat(bots): save or share an attachment from the Bot preview
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1001

## What changed

The Bot attachment preview let you view a file but not keep it: its only toolbar item was Done, and Quick Look's own share controls are unreachable inside Hermex's NavigationStack.

- `BotArtifactPreviewModel` keeps the downloaded bytes beside its temporary file. A new `export` (data, filename, content type) is nil while loading, on error, and after `cleanup()`. Content type is `UTType(filenameExtension:) ?? .data`, as in Workspace. No second download; cap and transport unchanged; the `generation` guard still drops late completions.
- Once loaded, Save (`square.and.arrow.down`, "Save <file> to Files") opens `.fileExporter` with `ExportedFileDocument`, and Share is a `ShareLink` over the temp file (`square.and.arrow.up`, "Share <file>"), beside Done. Loading and error show only Done. An exporter failure raises the existing "Export Failed" alert and keeps the preview open.
- `QuickLookTemporaryFile.write`: the `File` fallback for empty or dot names never fired, because `URL(fileURLWithPath:)` resolved `..` against the working directory. It now splits on `/`. Workspace and Sessions previews change only for those degenerate names.
- Two String Catalog keys with all 17 languages (`needs_review`).

Applies the [binding decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1001#issuecomment-5961799482). Both entry points get it: Bot Chat artifacts and staged composer attachments.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A --only HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests`: 11 passed, 0 failed.
- `--only ChatAttachmentPreviewViewModelTests --only APIClientWorkspaceFileTests --only LocalizationCatalogTests` (other `QuickLookTemporaryFile` callers and the catalog guard): 45 passed, 0 failed.
- Red: against unchanged code the tests could not compile (no `export` on the model). Then, before the sanitizer fix, `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("nil") is not equal to ("Optional("File")")` for a `..` name.
- `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 2156 keys covered. `git diff --check` clean; `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` no new warnings; signed Debug build launched on iPhone Air.

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator
Physical iPhone (Branch TestFlight build):
1. In a Bot Chat, open an agent-produced PDF or .docx. Tap Save, pick a folder, then open the saved file from Files: same content.
2. Tap Save again and cancel; tap Share and back out. The preview still shows the file and does not reload.

4. While a preview loads only Done shows, with no empty toolbar capsule; an oversized or failed file shows no Save or Share.
