title: feat(bots): slash commands in Bot Chat
body:
**What the user gets:** In Bot Chat, typing `/` lists the host's commands as well as skills, and running one shows the host's answer, as in a Hermes chat.
**Why it matters:** Hermes Desktop runs these commands in bot chats. Bot Chat's panel offers only skills today.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator only.

Epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1036

## Context

- Bot Chat's panel is skills-only by design: `BotSlashCatalog.skills(from:)` drops any key in `canon` or `commands` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotSlashCommands.swift:52`). `BotSlashAutocompleteView.swift` says commands are absent because `slash.exec` isn't exposed.
- The catalog is read in `BotConversation.loadSlashCatalog` (`BotConversation.swift:477`). Skills expand through `command.dispatch` in `skillText` (`:1027-1048`).
- #1036 adds the shared engine: the catalog rows, `complete.slash` argument suggestions, `slash.exec` with its directive handling, and the `HermesCall` cases. Its Contract section applies here unchanged.

## Decisions (Uzair, 2026-10-05)

1. Same engine and rules as #1036. The full host list, user quick commands and plugins included; unknown names go out as text.
2. **App-owned in Bot Chat:**
   - `/stop` → interrupt;
   - `/model`, `/reasoning` and `/fast` → Bot Chat's own controls (`BotChatControls.swift`);
   - `/yolo` → `config.set yolo` for the session.
3. **Refused permanently:** `/new` `/reset` `/resume` `/sessions` `/branch` `/fork` `/title`. Bot Chat is one canonical chat per bot (`docs/agents/bots.md`; upstream `apps/desktop/src/AGENTS.md` § Bot Mode). The notice says so, and nothing is sent.
4. **Held, with a notice:**
   - `/compress` `/compact` `/undo` `/retry` `/clear` until #702 slice 2.3.
   - `/btw` and `/bg` until Bot Chat renders `btw.complete` and `background.complete`. Through `slash.exec` only their acknowledgement would arrive.
5. Group rooms stay out (`BotRoomComposerView` is a separate composer).

## Expected behavior

- [ ] The panel lists every catalog command, not only skills. Choosing a skill still inserts its slug chip.
- [ ] Argument suggestions and send resolution follow #1036, with Bot Chat's app-owned, refused and held sets.
- [ ] Results show in Bot Chat's own notice style. A `send` directive goes through Bot Chat's Send/Queue path.
- [ ] The re-read of the catalog before a skill dispatch stays.
- [ ] Update `docs/agents/bots.md` § Slash suggestions for Bot Chat.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In Bot Chat, `/` lists host commands and skills; `/context` shows the host's text.
- [ ] `/model <id>` and `/reasoning high` change Bot Chat's controls, as the menus do.
- [ ] `/new` and `/title x` are refused with the one-chat notice and send nothing.
- [ ] `/btw hi` shows the held notice and sends nothing.
- [ ] A skill still expands and sends as today.

## Tests

- `BotChatPresentationTests.testSlashPanelOffersConnectionSkillsAndNeverCommands` flips to cover commands.
- `BotSlashCommandTests`: catalog rows with commands.
- Send routing on the scripted gateway: app-owned, refused, held, host command, skill.
- Run `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotSlashCommandTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatControlsTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotConversationTests`.

## Manual (simulator, `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`)

1. Open a bot's Bot Chat and type `/`. Expected: commands and skills.
2. Run `/context`. Expected: the host's summary as a notice.
3. Run `/new`. Expected: the one-chat notice.

## Non-goals

- Group rooms.
- `/btw` and `/bg` answers in Bot Chat.
- The #702 commands.

title: feat(hermes): keep attachment thumbnails and preview sent files in a Hermes session
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1030

## What changed

When you reopened a Hermes session, a photo you had sent showed a plain file icon, a sent PDF wouldn't open, and nothing you sent could be saved. The cause: each attachment chip dropped the host path of its file, and the chat had no way to download from the host.

- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.displayed` keeps the host path on each chip. The path stays out of the bubble text, chip names, VoiceOver labels and composer recall.
- New `attachmentData(path:)` downloads through the session's Bot transport (`HermesREST.downloadArtifact` with the session's Profile and stored key), the same way Bot Chat does. It throws `.stale` while the session is detached or once a reattach starts.
- Thumbnails go through `TranscriptImageCache`, keyed by connection, Profile and stored key.
- Tapping a Hermes chip that has a path opens `BotArtifactPreview` (Quick Look plus Save to Files and Share) for every kind of file. A chip without a path still opens its local copy. Webui chips, previews and the lightbox are unchanged.
- `BotArtifactPreview` takes an optional `title`, so the preview and the saved file use the chip's name (`Q3 report.pdf`, not `<uuid>-Q3 report.pdf`).

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro> --only HermesChatAttachmentTests --only ChatAttachmentPreviewViewModelTests --only ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests --only BotAttachmentSendingTests --only TranscriptMediaParserTests`: 88 passed. `--only BotArtifactTests --only HermesChatTurnTests`: 34 passed.

New and changed tests in `HermesChatAttachmentTests`: rebuilt chips keep their paths while the text has none; a thumbnail download sends `path`, `profile=default` and `session_id=tip`; a download that is still running when the chat reattaches is dropped; the cache namespace differs across connections and Profiles.

Owner checks (simulator on `scripts/local-hermes`):
1. Send a photo and a PDF, leave the chat and reopen it. The photo shows its thumbnail and no host paths appear.
2. Tap the PDF, then the photo. Both open in Quick Look with Save to Files and Share.
3. With the host off, reopen the chat. Chips show file icons with no spinner. Tapping one shows "Could Not Load File" with Try Again.

title: feat(hermes): manage Tasks on a Hermes server
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes server, Tasks works: see every scheduled Task across all Profiles, and create, edit, pause, resume and delete them, with a warning when the host's scheduler has stopped. **Why it matters:** #704 (phase 4) of Hermex 2.0 (#713). Today a Hermes server's home is only the Bots inbox, so Tasks can't be reached at all. **Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator only. Part of #704 (slice 4.1a) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #1041 (Run Now) ## Problem and outcome Tasks is webui-only: - Every Tasks view model calls the concrete `APIClient` (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+Cron.swift`, webui `/api/crons/*`), with no protocol in between: `TasksViewModel.swift:38-42`, `TaskDetailViewModel.swift:54-60`, `CronJobEditorConfigurationLoader.swift:32-36`. - Tasks is only reachable from the webui session list's sidebar (`SessionListComponents.swift:281-284` → `SessionListView.swift:673-674`). A Hermes server routes to `HermesServerHome` (`ContentView.swift:95-100`, `:331`), which is the Bots inbox plus Settings. After this, on a Hermes server, in a DEBUG build or Hermex Branch: - The inbox's + menu offers **Tasks**. It opens today's Tasks screen backed by the host's `/api/cron/*` routes. - The list shows every Profile's Tasks, paused and completed ones included, each with a Profile label. - Create, edit, pause, resume and delete work. The running state and recent completions are derived from the list. - Run Now and run history are hidden on Hermes until #1041 and #1042. webui servers don't change. ## Contract Read from source at `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` (`ca678285`, 0.21.5). `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py` is "router", `hermes_cli/web_server_cron.py` is "wsc". Re-check each against `scripts/local-hermes` before building on it. - **Common.** - Errors are `{detail: string}`, except 424. - `?profile=` is a hint: a job id the named Profile lacks is searched in every Profile (router:70-96, wsc:213-221). Always send the job's own `profile`. - Every job carries `profile`, `profile_name`, `hermes_home` (a host path: never render or log it), `is_default_profile` and `scheduler_heartbeat_age_s` (wsc:126-138, 158-172). - **`GET /api/cron/jobs`** (default `profile=all`) → a **bare array** of jobs across every Profile, paused and completed included (router:105-119, 233-235). Each job carries `latest_execution` from the executions ledger (`cron/jobs.py:1896-1909`). - Fields used: `id`, `name`, `prompt`, `skills[]`, `model`, `provider`, `deliver`, `schedule {kind: once|interval|cron, run_at|minutes|expr, display}`, `schedule_display`, `repeat {times, completed}`, `enabled` (authoritative), `state` (`scheduled|paused|completed|error`), `paused_at`, `next_run_at`, `last_run_at`, `last_status` (`ok|error|delivery_failed|…`), `last_error`, `last_delivery_error`, `fire_claim` (`{at, by}` or null), `latest_execution.status` (`claimed|running|completed|failed|unknown`) and `latest_execution.finished_at`. - `GET /api/cron/jobs/{id}` has **no** `latest_execution` (`jobs.py:1860-1863`). Reload the list instead. - **`POST /api/cron/jobs?profile=

`** with body `{schedule: string, prompt, name, deliver, skills, model, provider}` → the created job (wsc:243-276, `hermes_cli/web_models.py:300-315`). - 400 carries the validation message. - **424** means the job was saved but scheduler registration failed: `detail` is an object. Treat it as saved, show the warning, and reload. - **`PUT /api/cron/jobs/{id}?profile=

`** with body **`{updates: {…}}`** → the updated job (router:165-183, 277-279). - Never send `id` or `profile`; the host can't move a job. - An update can't reactivate a completed job (400, `jobs.py:1912-1925`). - **`DELETE …/{id}?profile=

`** → `{ok: true}`. This also deletes the job's output folder. - **`POST …/{id}/pause`** and **`…/resume`**, no body → the updated job (router:186-191, 282-289). - Resuming a one-shot whose time has passed is an unhandled 500. Show the generic failure. - **`GET /api/cron/delivery-targets?profile=

`** → `{targets: [{id, name, home_target_set, home_env_var}]}`, with `local` first (router:253-274). `deliver` may be comma-separated. - **Editor sources.** - Models: `model.options` for the selected Profile, through the shared `HermesModelCatalog` (#1015). - Profiles: `profiles.list` (`HermesCall.profilesList`). - Skills: **`GET /api/skills?profile=

`** → a bare array of `{name, description, category, enabled, usage, provenance}` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/skills.py:343-370`). List only `enabled` skills. - **Scheduler.** `scheduler_heartbeat_age_s` is the seconds since that Profile's ticker last ran, or null (`cron/jobs.py:1262-1270`). The tick is 60 s (`jobs.py:84`). - **Not on Hermes:** toast notifications. No job field exists. ## Plan - [ ] **Seam.** Add `protocol CronDataClient: Sendable` covering what the Tasks view models call, modeled on `KanbanDataClient` (`APIClient+Kanban.swift:3`). - `APIClient` conforms in `APIClient+Cron.swift` with no behavior change. - The three view-model inits take `any CronDataClient` instead of `APIClient`. - `isMissingEndpoint` (`TaskDetailViewModel.swift:276`) and `isCancellation` (`CronJobEditorConfigurationLoader.swift:98`) recognize the Hermes client's failures too. - [ ] **Hermes client.** Add a REST-only `HermesCronClient` in `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/`, following `BotDashboardClient` (`Networking/Bots/BotDashboardClient.swift:9-91`). - New `HermesREST` cases for the routes above. - Sent through `HermesConnections.shared.connection(for:server:)`, so custom headers, cookies and re-sign-in come from the shared connection. - The host job decodes tolerantly into today's `CronJob` (`HermesMobile/Models/Cron.swift:38`), adding an init where needed. - `hermes_home` is never kept, logged or rendered. - [ ] **Derived state.** - Running: `fire_claim != nil`, or `latest_execution.status ∈ {claimed, running}`. This replaces `cronStatus`. - Recent completions: from `last_run_at` and `last_status` on the list. This replaces `cronRecent`. - [ ] **List.** Every Profile's Tasks, with a Profile label on each row in `CronJobRowView`. Today's filters and agenda (`TaskAgenda.swift`) stay as they are. - [ ] **Editor.** - A new Task defaults to the server's selected Profile (#1015). - The Profile is locked when editing. - Delivery targets come from `delivery-targets` for the Task's Profile. - The Toast Notifications toggle (`CronJobEditorSheet.swift:98`) and the detail's "Notifications" row (`TaskConfigurationFields.swift:75-79`) are hidden on Hermes. - [ ] **Scheduler warning.** When any enabled Task's Profile reports `scheduler_heartbeat_age_s > 180` (3 missed ticks), the Tasks list shows one notice: "Scheduled Tasks aren't running. The host's scheduler hasn't checked in for N minutes." Null shows nothing. - [ ] **Hidden until later slices.** Run Now (#1041), and run history and output (#1042), are hidden on Hermes. - [ ] **Entry (temporary).** The Bots inbox's + menu (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotsInboxView.swift:190-230`) gains **Tasks**, gated by `HermesSessionEntry.isOffered` (`:6-19`), as "New Session" is. It pushes the Tasks screen on the Hermes source. #709's build gives it a permanent home. - [ ] **Docs.** `docs/agents/bots.md` notes the cron REST routes Hermex uses and the heartbeat threshold. ## Decisions **Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-05):** 1. **Way in:** a temporary "Tasks" item in the Hermes inbox's + menu, DEBUG and Hermex Branch only. #709's build gives it a permanent home. 2. **Scope:** all Profiles, with a Profile label on each Task. New Tasks default to the server's selected Profile. The Profile is locked when editing, because the host can't move a job. 3. **Scheduler warning:** shown when the scheduler hasn't ticked for 3 minutes (3 missed ticks). 4. **Toast Notifications:** hidden on Hermes, since the host has no such setting. ## Acceptance - [ ] On a Hermes server in DEBUG or Branch, the + menu offers Tasks. It is absent on webui servers and in Release. - [ ] The list shows every Profile's Tasks, paused and completed included, each with its Profile. - [ ] Create sends `POST …?profile=` with the editor's fields. A 424 shows as saved with the host's warning. - [ ] Edit sends `PUT` with `{updates}` and never includes `profile` or `id`. The Profile can't be changed. - [ ] Pause, resume and delete send the right route with the job's Profile and update the list. A failure leaves the row unchanged and shows the error. - [ ] A job with a `fire_claim`, or with `latest_execution.status` `claimed` or `running`, shows as running. - [ ] Delivery, model, Profile and skills pickers are filled from the host for the Task's Profile. - [ ] The scheduler notice appears above 180 s and is absent at or below it, and for null. - [ ] Toast Notifications, Run Now and run history don't appear on Hermes. - [ ] webui Tasks behave as before. Their existing tests pass unchanged. ## Tests These fail on today's code unless noted. - **Hermes cron client:** `HermesHostFixture` (`HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests.swift:459`) fixtures from the pinned shapes. Cover the bare-array list, paused and completed jobs, a missing `latest_execution`, unknown fields, 424, a 400 detail, the PUT body shape, and that no request carries `profile` inside `updates`. - **Derived state:** running from `fire_claim` and from each `latest_execution.status`; recent completions. - **View models on the seam:** `CronManagementViewModelTests` gains Hermes cases for load, create, edit, pause, resume and delete. The Profile is locked on edit, and the scheduler notice threshold is tested at 180 and 181 s and for null. - **Entry:** `HermesSessionEntry` visibility for Tasks. - **Run:** `scripts/test-sim --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientCronEndpointTests --only HermesMobileTests/CronManagementModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/CronManagementViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/CronJobEditorConfigurationTests --only HermesMobileTests/TaskAgendaTests`, plus the new Hermes classes. ## Validation plan Against `scripts/local-hermes` (pinned commit, this Mac), never the maintainer's host: - `curl` the list, delivery targets and skills. - Create one disposable job, then edit, pause, resume and delete it. Record the shapes in the PR. ## Mocks Not required. The existing screens, rows and pickers are reused. The only new pieces are the row's Profile label and one notice line. If the work needs a new control, stop and ask for a mock. ## Manual test Device: the simulator, signed in with `scripts/sim-login --hermes`. 1. Open + → Tasks. Expected: every Profile's Tasks, each labeled. 2. Create a Task in a non-default Profile, edit its schedule, pause it, resume it, delete it. Expected: each step shows in the list, and the Profile can't be changed while editing. 3. Switch to the webui server. Expected: its Tasks screen is unchanged and shows Toast Notifications. ## Surfaces - **Entry points:** only the temporary menu item. Deep links, App Intents and Settings' Main Page toggles stay webui-only (`SettingsView.swift:409-415`). - **Targets:** main app and tests. No extension reads Tasks. - **Servers:** the client is per server through `HermesConnections`. Walk one Hermes and one webui server. - **Reverse states:** pause ↔ resume. Delete asks first, as today. - **Native quality:** the Profile label has a VoiceOver label, and the notice works at accessibility text sizes. ## Preservation - #898: custom headers reach the host through `HermesConnection`. - #1015: the selected Profile is client state and is never written to the host. ## Outside reach None. title: feat(hermes): Run Now on Hermes Tasks with a server-confirmed running state
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes server, Run Now starts a Task and shows it as running only once the host confirms it, even when the tunnel gives up on the request before the run finishes. **Why it matters:** #704 (phase 4) of Hermex 2.0 (#713). The host's trigger waits for the whole run before replying, so through a Cloudflare tunnel a long run looks like a failure (524 after about 100 s) while it is still running. **Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator, plus one phone step through the tunnel at the merge walk. Part of #704 (slice 4.1b) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1040 · **Unblocks:** #1042 ## Problem and outcome On webui, Run Now is `POST /api/crons/run` and returns at once (`APIClient+Cron.swift:84`, `TaskDetailViewModel.swift:287`). On Hermes, the trigger runs the job before it replies. After #1040, Run Now is hidden on Hermes. After this, on a Hermes server: - Run Now sends the trigger and keeps the request alive without blocking the screen. - The button shows a pending state. "Running" appears only when the host's list says so. - The outcome comes from the host: the trigger's reply, or the list once the run has finished. A 524, a timeout or a dropped connection keeps reconciling and is not reported as a failure. - On a paused Task, Run Now first asks "Run now? This also resumes the Task." The host resumes the Task as it runs it. ## Contract Read from source at `ca678285` (0.21.5). Re-check against `scripts/local-hermes` before building on it. - **`POST /api/cron/jobs/{id}/trigger?profile=

`**, no body (router:194-213, 292-294). - **Synchronous:** `_fire_cron_job_for_profile` → `provider.fire_due` → `run_one_job` (wsc:279-303, `cron/scheduler.py:2705-2776`). It returns the refreshed job (`last_run_at`, `last_status`, `last_error`). - **409** `"Job is already running or was claimed by another scheduler"` when the claim fails. A **completed** job gets the same 409 (`jobs.py:2665`), so Run Now is hidden for `state == completed`. - **409** when a paused job's provider can't force-fire (wsc:292-297). Show the host's message. - **Paused jobs:** the route passes `force=True`, which resumes the job (`enabled=true`) before running it (router:201, `jobs.py:2669, 2703-2704`). It stays resumed. - Active jobs run with `manual=True`, so the next scheduled slot isn't used up (wsc:301-302). - **Client disconnect:** the run executes in a threadpool thread that can't be cancelled, or in a detached worker subprocess under a managed gateway (`scheduler.py:3547-3556`). Either way it should finish and record its result. One disposable-job check confirms this (Validation plan). - **Reconcile read:** `GET /api/cron/jobs?profile=

` (#1040). Running is `fire_claim != nil` or `latest_execution.status ∈ {claimed, running}`. A run that has finished shows `latest_execution.status ∈ {completed, failed, unknown}`, with `last_run_at` newer than the request. ## Plan - [ ] **Run Now machine.** Add a small state machine owned by `TaskDetailViewModel`, with an injected clock: `idle → requested → running → finished(outcome)`. - **requested:** send the trigger detached with a long deadline (at least `HermesConnection`'s `.provisioning`). Leaving the screen doesn't cancel the request. - **Reconcile:** while requested or running, re-read the Task's Profile list every 5 s on the injected clock. - Running appears only when the host shows a claim. - The machine ends when the trigger replies, or when the list shows the run finished after the request. - **Outcomes:** - 200: the refreshed job. - 409 "already running": keep reconciling; it shows as running. - A 524, a timeout or a transport drop: keep reconciling, with no error shown. - A 4xx with a `detail`: show the host's message and return to idle. - Reconciling ends when the screen goes away. The row's running state then comes from the list on the next load. - Stale results from an earlier run never overwrite a newer one (the generation token in `TaskDetailViewModel`). - [ ] **Paused confirm.** On `enabled == false`, Run Now asks "Run now? This also resumes the Task." Cancel sends nothing. - [ ] **Completed.** Run Now is hidden when `state == completed`. - [ ] **Row action.** The list's Run Now (`TasksViewModel.swift:190-244`) goes through the same machine. - [ ] **Show the button.** Lift #1040's Hermes hiding of Run Now. ## Decisions **Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-05):** 1. **Run Now on a paused Task** asks first ("This also resumes the Task"), then runs. The host leaves the Task resumed. 2. **"Running" only once the host says so.** A tunnel 524 or timeout is not a failure. 3. **No companion route** unless the disposable-job check shows the run dying with the request. ## Acceptance - [ ] Run Now sends exactly one trigger with the Task's Profile. - [ ] "Running" appears only after the list shows a claim or a running execution. - [ ] A 524, a timeout or a dropped connection ends in the host's outcome, not an error. - [ ] 409 "already running" shows the Task as running. - [ ] A paused Task asks first. Confirm runs it and the Task ends resumed; Cancel sends nothing. - [ ] Run Now is hidden on completed Tasks. - [ ] Leaving the screen stops reconciling and the trigger isn't resent. - [ ] webui Run Now behaves as before. ## Tests `CronManagementTests` gains the reconcile machine on a scripted clock, with no sleeps. These fail on today's code. - 200 directly. - 524 then the list shows running then finished. - Timeout with the run finishing later. - 409 already running. - A paused confirm and cancel. - A 4xx `detail`. - Teardown mid-reconcile. - A stale reply after a newer run. **Run:** `scripts/test-sim --only HermesMobileTests/CronManagementModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/CronManagementViewModelTests`, plus the new class. ## Validation plan On `scripts/local-hermes`, with one disposable job: 1. Trigger it and drop the request after about 5 s (`curl --max-time 5`). 2. Confirm the run finishes and `last_run_at` and `latest_execution` update. 3. Delete the job. Record the evidence in the PR. If the run dies with the request, stop and report: the fallback is a companion route (#710). ## Mocks Not required. The pending state reuses the existing button's progress state, and the confirm reuses a standard alert. ## Manual test 1. **Simulator, `scripts/sim-login --hermes`:** Run Now on a short Task. Expected: pending, then running, then the result. 2. **Simulator:** Run Now on a paused Task. Expected: the confirm. Afterwards the Task is active. 3. **Device: physical iPhone, Cloudflare tunnel.** Run Now on a Task that takes longer than 2 minutes. Expected: no error at about 100 s, it shows running, and it finishes with the host's result. ## Surfaces - **Entry points:** the detail button and the list row action. - **Targets:** main app and tests. - **Connection modes:** the tunnel case is the reason for this slice. - **Reverse states:** the paused confirm can be cancelled. ## Preservation - #1040's derived running state is the single source for "Running". ## Outside reach A companion async trigger route (#710), only if the validation fails. Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: feat(hermes): Task run history and output on Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes server, a Task's detail shows its recent runs. Opening one shows what the agent produced. **Why it matters:** #704 (phase 4) of Hermex 2.0 (#713). After #1040, run history and output are hidden on Hermes. **Cost:** Small to medium. One PR. Simulator only. Part of #704 (slice 4.1c) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1041 (only to avoid conflicts in `TaskDetailViewModel`) · **Unblocks:** none ## Problem and outcome On webui, history and output come from the run's `.md` files: - `cronHistory` → `/api/crons/history`. - `cronRunDetail` → `/api/crons/run`. - `cronOutput` → `/api/crons/output` (`APIClient+Cron.swift:112-126`). - These feed `TaskRunHistorySection`, `TaskRunOutputSheet` and the detail's latest output (`TaskDetailViewModel.swift:82, 195, 262-276`). On Hermes, each run is a session. After this, on a Hermes server: - The detail lists the newest 100 runs, with no "Load more". - Each run shows when it started, how long it took, its preview, and its tokens and cost where present. - The newest finished run shows the Task's `last_status` and `last_error`. Older runs show no ok or failed, because the host keeps status per Task, not per run. A run still in progress shows as running. - Opening a run shows its session's final assistant reply. - The detail's latest output is the newest run's final reply. - Nothing is read from the host's disk. ## Contract Read from source at `ca678285` (0.21.5). Re-check against `scripts/local-hermes` before building on it. - **`GET /api/cron/jobs/{id}/runs?profile=

&limit=100`** → `{runs: [...], limit}`. `limit` is clamped to 1–100, and there is no offset (router:126-159, 243-245). - Rows are `state.db` sessions with `source='cron'` and an id starting `cron_{job_id}_`, newest first (`hermes_state_portability.py:212-226`). - Fields used: `id` (`cron_{job}_{YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS}`; can be a compression-tip id, `scheduler.py:2072-2088`), `started_at` and `ended_at` (epoch floats), `end_reason`, `message_count`, the token and cost fields, `title`, `preview`, `is_active` and `profile`. - The rows also carry `system_prompt` (the query is `s.*`). **Don't decode it.** - **Run output:** `HermesREST.sessionMessages(key: , profile:)` (#1013, `HermesREST.swift:98-107`) → `{session_id, profile, messages: [{role, content, tool_calls}]}`, the latest 500 rows oldest first, or 404. The output is the last `assistant` message's `content`. ## Plan - [ ] **Client.** `HermesCronClient` gains the runs read and the run-output read, behind the `CronDataClient` seam from #1040. - Runs map to the history row model, adding optional fields where today's `CronRunHistoryItem` (`HermesMobile/Models/CronRunHistory.swift:42`) lacks them. - The run id is the row's identity. - [ ] **History.** `TaskRunHistorySection` on Hermes: - one page of 100 runs, with "Load more" hidden; - the newest finished row carries the Task's `last_status` and `last_error`; - `is_active` rows show as running. - [ ] **Output.** - `TaskRunOutputSheet` shows the run's final reply as Markdown, as today. A run with no assistant reply shows "No output for this run." - The detail's latest output reads only the newest run. - [ ] **Show it.** Lift #1040's Hermes hiding of history and output. - [ ] **Docs.** `CONTEXT.md` adds **Task Run**: one execution of a Task. On Hermes it is a session `cron__`; on webui it is an output file. ## Decisions **Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-05):** 1. **History:** the newest 100 runs, with no deeper paging. 2. **Output** is the run session's final reply. Nothing is read from the host's disk (`/api/fs/*`): those routes take absolute host paths, and nothing links a run to its file. 3. **Status:** only the newest run shows ok or failed. ## Acceptance - [ ] A Hermes Task's detail lists up to 100 runs, newest first, with no "Load more". - [ ] The newest finished run shows the Task's last status and error. Older runs show none. Active runs show running. - [ ] Opening a run shows its final assistant reply. A run with no reply says so, and a 404 shows the run as unavailable. - [ ] No request goes to `/api/fs/*`, and `system_prompt` is never decoded. - [ ] webui history, paging and output behave as before. ## Tests `TaskRunHistoryTests` gains Hermes cases. These fail on today's code. - The runs shape, with `system_prompt` present and ignored. - An empty list. - An active run. - The newest-row status. - The final-reply extraction, including no assistant message and a 404. - A stale history reply after a reload (the generation scheme). **Run:** `scripts/test-sim --only HermesMobileTests/TaskRunHistoryTests --only HermesMobileTests/CronManagementViewModelTests`. ## Validation plan On `scripts/local-hermes`: `curl` `…/runs` for a job that has run, and that run's `sessions/{id}/messages`. Record the shapes in the PR. ## Mocks Not required. The history section and output sheet are reused. ## Manual test Device: the simulator, signed in with `scripts/sim-login --hermes`. 1. Open a Task that has run several times. Expected: the runs listed newest first, and the newest shows its status. 2. Open a run. Expected: the agent's final reply. ## Surfaces - **Entry points:** the Task detail only. - **Targets:** main app and tests. - **Servers:** the history is per Task, and the Task's Profile goes on every read. ## Preservation - #1013: `sessionMessages` keeps its id validation. ## Outside reach None. Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: feat(hermes): Kanban boards and Cards on Hermes, read-only
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes server, Kanban opens: boards, every Column including the host's Scheduled and Review, Card details, comments, dependencies and the worker log. In this slice it is read-only.
**Why it matters:** #704 (phase 4) of Hermex 2.0 (#713). Today a Hermes server's home is only the Bots inbox, so Kanban can't be reached at all.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator only.

Part of #704 (slice 4.2a) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #1044 (Kanban changes), #1045 (live updates)

## Problem and outcome

Kanban is webui-only:
- `KanbanView` builds `KanbanFeatureState` with `APIClient(baseURL:)` and the SSE stream client (`HermesMobile/Features/Kanban/KanbanLabView.swift:2347-2357`, `KanbanFeatureState.swift:432-454`).
- It is reached only from the webui sidebar (`SessionListComponents.swift:287-289` → `SessionListView.swift:675-676`).
- The handshake and validator assume webui shapes (`KanbanFeatureState.swift:928-1029`, `HermesMobile/Models/Kanban.swift:1096-1150`):
  - `config.columns` must be present;
  - `snapshot.changed == true`;
  - `read_only` must be present, or writes are disabled.
- Error handling only understands `APIError`: `classify` (`:2794`), `markOfflineIfNeeded` (`:2687`) and `KanbanEndpointCompatibility.isMissingCapability` (`:41-52`).
- Statuses are hard-coded to seven in five places, none with Scheduled or Review:
  - `liveStatuses` (`KanbanFeatureState.swift:343`, `:626-634`);
  - `KanbanStatus.isSupported` (`Kanban.swift:1057`);
  - `KanbanCardEditorState.createStatuses` (`:36`);
  - `ordinaryDestinations` and `canMutateCard` (`:687-702`);
  - `KanbanStatusPresentation` (`KanbanLabView.swift:2314-2344`), which shows unknown statuses as "Unsupported: x".
- **Bug on both backends:** Card `age` is a dict on the host (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:4259-4269`), and webui forwards the same dict as `age_seconds` (`hermes-webui/api/kanban_bridge.py:126-132`). Hermex decodes it as a lossy double (`Kanban.swift:632`), so the staleness badges (`:645-657`) never show.

After this, on a Hermes server in a DEBUG build or Hermex Branch:
- The inbox's + menu offers **Kanban**. It opens today's Kanban screen backed by the host's Kanban plugin.
- Boards, the board's Columns from the host, Card details, comments, dependencies, stats, assignees and the worker log load.
- Every write control is disabled, and live updates are off. Pull to refresh and returning to the foreground reload the board.
- A host without the Kanban plugin shows today's "Kanban isn't available" state, not an error.

webui servers keep their seven Columns.

## Contract

Read from source at `ca678285` (0.21.5). `P` = `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`. Everything is under `/api/plugins/kanban`. Re-check against `scripts/local-hermes` before building on it.

- **Mount and absence.**
  - The plugin is bundled and mounts unless it is disabled (`hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py:782-795, 871`).
  - Absent means **404 on `GET /config`**: `{"detail": "No such API endpoint: …"}` when not mounted, or `{"detail": "Plugin not found"}` when disabled at runtime (`web_server.py:597-636`).
  - Errors are `{detail: string}`; 422 carries `{detail: [...]}`.
  - Most routes take `?board=<slug>`. An unknown board is 404 (P:65-73).
- **`GET /config`** → `{default_tenant, lane_by_profile, include_archived_by_default, render_markdown}`, with **no columns and no `read_only`** (P:1123-1131).
- **`GET /boards?include_archived=`** → `{boards: [meta], current}` (P:1385-1401).
  - Meta fields used: `slug, name, description, icon, color, archived, is_current, counts, total, default_workspace_kind, project_name`.
  - **Never kept or rendered:** `db_path` and `default_workdir`.
- **`GET /board?board=&tenant=&include_archived=`** → `{columns: [{name, tasks}], tenants, assignees, latest_event_id, now}` (P:279-354).
  - Columns are the fixed `triage, todo, scheduled, ready, running, blocked, review, done`, plus `archived` only when included (P:169, 307-308).
  - **No `changed`, no `read_only`.**
  - Card fields used are today's, plus `age` as a dict: `{created_age_seconds, started_age_seconds, time_to_complete_seconds}` (P:174-183).
- **`GET /tasks/{id}`** → `{task, comments, events, attachments, links {parents, children}, link_tasks [{id, title, status}], child_results, runs}` (P:359-387). `link_tasks` is new since 0.21.4.
- **`GET /tasks/{id}/log?tail=`** → `{task_id, path, exists, size_bytes, content, truncated}`. A missing log is `exists: false`, not a 404 (P:1229-1240).
- **`GET /stats`**, **`GET /assignees`** → `[{name, on_disk, counts}]` (P:1214-1226).
- **Host paths and PIDs, never rendered or logged:**
  - paths: `workspace_path`, `attachments[].stored_path`, the log `path`, `db_path`, `default_workdir`;
  - process data: `worker_pid`, `claim_lock`, `run.worker_pid`.
- **Auth:** the shared `HermesConnection` (cookie session). The routes take no `profile`; boards are host-wide.

## Plan

- [ ] **Hermes client.** Add a REST-only `HermesKanbanClient: KanbanDataClient` in `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/`, following `BotDashboardClient`.
  - New `HermesREST` cases for the reads above.
  - It implements config, boards, board, stats, assignees, card detail and the worker log.
  - The writes keep the protocol's default `KanbanUnsupportedClientMethod` (`APIClient+Kanban.swift:28-111`) until #1044.
  - `kanbanEvents` throws unsupported, because the host has no events route.
- [ ] **Adapters.**
  - The config's columns come from the board's `columns`.
  - Every envelope reports `readOnly: true` in this slice, so writes stay disabled. #1044 flips it.
  - `changed` is absent, so the Hermes path treats every board reload as changed.
- [ ] **Handshake and validator.** `KanbanCompatibilityValidator` gains a Hermes path:
  - non-empty `columns` and `boards.current`;
  - no `changed` requirement;
  - unknown statuses still flag.

  A 404 on `/config` maps to today's missing-capability state.
- [ ] **Errors.** `classify`, `markOfflineIfNeeded` and `isMissingCapability` recognize `BotFailure`:
  - `.transport` is offline;
  - `.rejected(404)` on config is a missing capability;
  - a stale or signed-out connection uses today's copy.

  Hermes sign-out stays with `HermesConnection.onLoginRejected`, not `forwardAuthentication`.
- [ ] **Statuses.** Add `scheduled` and `review` to `KanbanStatus`, `KanbanStatusPresentation` ("Scheduled", "Review", with SF Symbols in today's style) and the live set.
  - The Columns shown follow the board's own list, so webui keeps seven.
  - Moves into or out of Scheduled and Review come in #1044.
- [ ] **Age.** Decode `age` and `age_seconds` as the dict on both backends, keeping a plain number as a fallback. Staleness reads `started_age_seconds` for running Cards and `created_age_seconds` otherwise. This fixes the webui badges too.
- [ ] **Live updates off on Hermes.** The feature state starts no stream and polls no events for a Hermes source. Foreground and pull to refresh reload the board. #1045 adds the socket.
- [ ] **Entry (temporary).** The inbox's + menu (`BotsInboxView.swift:190-230`) gains **Kanban**, gated by `HermesSessionEntry.isOffered`. It pushes `KanbanView` with the Hermes clients. #709's build gives it a permanent home.
- [ ] **Board preference.** The selected board stays keyed per server (`KanbanFeatureState.swift:319-335`).
- [ ] **Docs.**
  - `CONTEXT.md` Status adds **Scheduled** and **Review**, with one line each on what the host uses them for.
  - `docs/agents/kanban.md` gains a "Hermes" section: routes, absent-plugin detection, and the host fields Hermex never renders.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-05):**
1. **Way in:** a temporary "Kanban" item in the Hermes inbox's + menu, DEBUG and Hermex Branch only. #709's build gives it a permanent home.
2. **Scheduled and Review** are shown as Columns. Cards can move out of them but not into them (#1044).
3. **Read-only first.** This slice ships reads with writes disabled. #1044 adds the writes and #1045 the live socket.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a Hermes server in DEBUG or Branch, the + menu offers Kanban. It is absent on webui servers and in Release.
- [ ] Boards list, and the board shows the host's eight Columns in the host's order, with Scheduled and Review labeled (not "Unsupported").
- [ ] Card detail, comments, dependencies, worker log, stats and assignees load.
- [ ] Every write control is disabled.
- [ ] A host without the plugin (404 on `/config`) shows the unavailable state.
- [ ] Offline shows today's offline state, not a generic error.
- [ ] Running, Ready and Blocked Cards show staleness from the age dict, on Hermes and on webui.
- [ ] No host path or PID appears in any view or log.
- [ ] webui Kanban shows its seven Columns, and its tests pass unchanged except the age fixtures.

## Tests

These fail on today's code unless noted.
- **Hermes Kanban client:** `HermesHostFixture` fixtures from the pinned shapes. Cover config, boards (with `db_path` ignored), a board with eight Columns and the age dict, Card detail with `link_tasks`, a log with `exists: false`, a 404 config in both body shapes, and unknown fields.
- **`KanbanFeatureStateTests`:** the Hermes handshake and validator (no `changed`, eight Columns), the absent plugin, `BotFailure` classification, and live updates not started.
- **Age:** dict and number decoding, and staleness per status.
- **Statuses:** the presentation of Scheduled and Review, and that webui's Columns are unchanged.
- **Run:** `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientKanbanTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanCardDetailStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests`, plus the new Hermes class.

## Validation plan

On `scripts/local-hermes`: `curl` config, boards, board, one Card's detail and its log. Then disable the plugin to see the 404 body, and re-enable it. Record the shapes in the PR.

## Mocks

Not required. The Scheduled and Review Columns reuse the existing Column style with new labels and symbols. If a new control is needed, stop and ask.

## Manual test

Device: the simulator, signed in with `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`.
1. Open + → Kanban. Expected: the active board with eight Columns, including Scheduled and Review.
2. Open a Card. Expected: detail, comments, dependencies and the log, with no host paths.
3. Switch to the webui server's Kanban. Expected: seven Columns, unchanged, now with staleness badges on old Cards.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** only the temporary menu item. There are no Kanban deep links, intents or extensions.
- **Targets:** main app and tests.
- **Servers:** the board preference stays per server. Walk one Hermes and one webui server.
- **Native quality:** the new Column labels and symbols have VoiceOver labels.

## Preservation

- #898: headers go through `HermesConnection`.
- `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`: Kanban board preference.

## Outside reach

None.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: feat(hermes): change Kanban Cards and boards on Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes server, Kanban can be changed from the phone. Create and edit Cards, move them, block and unblock them, assign them, link dependencies, comment, dispatch, and manage boards.
**Why it matters:** #704 (phase 4) of Hermex 2.0 (#713). #1043 ships Kanban on Hermes read-only.
**Cost:** Medium to large. One PR. Simulator only.

Part of #704 (slice 4.2b) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1043 · **Unblocks:** none · Can run beside #1045

## Problem and outcome

After #1043, `HermesKanbanClient` throws `KanbanUnsupportedClientMethod` for every write and reports the board read-only. The host's write contract differs from webui's in ways that would mislead the user if they were mapped naively:
- **To Do doesn't stick:**
  - A Card in To Do whose prerequisites are all done is promoted to Ready on the next dispatcher tick and dispatched (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:2128-2159`, `kanban_db_dispatch.py:2158`).
  - A Card with no prerequisites is always promoted.
- **Block, unblock and dependency replies are shaped differently:**
  - Block and unblock are status changes.
  - Dependencies don't echo ids.
  - Comments don't return the comment.
- **Tenant can't be edited,** and an empty assignee on create is a 400.

After this, on a Hermes server:
- Every Kanban write works.
- To Do is never offered as a place to create or move a Card. Cards go to Triage or Ready, and the host itself puts a Card in To Do while it has an open prerequisite.
- Scheduled and Review can be moved out of but not into.
- Tenant is set on create and read-only after.

webui servers don't change.

## Contract

Read from source at `ca678285` (0.21.5). `P` = `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, `DB` = `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`, and all routes are under `/api/plugins/kanban`. Re-check against `scripts/local-hermes` before building on it.

- **`POST /tasks?board=`** → `{task, warning?}` (P:392-433). The warning means a ready, assigned Card with no dispatcher running.
  - Body: `title` (required, non-empty), `body`, `assignee`, `tenant`, `priority`, `workspace_kind`, `parents[]`, `triage`, `idempotency_key`, `max_runtime_seconds` and `skills`.
  - The starting status is `triage` if `triage`; otherwise `todo` if any parent isn't done; otherwise `ready` (`kanban_db_graph.py:45-51`).
  - **`assignee: ""` is a 400.** Send null for none.
  - **`workspace_kind`** is `scratch|worktree|dir` (DB:112). If omitted on a project board, the Card inherits the project and `scratch` becomes `worktree` (DB:1288-1305). An explicit `scratch` opts out of the project.
- **`PATCH /tasks/{id}`** → `{task}` (P:668-690).
  - `title`, `body`, `priority` and `assignee` (`""` unassigns; a running or claimed Card is 409).
  - There is **no tenant field** (P:509-527).
  - The patch isn't one transaction: an assignee change commits before a later 409.
- **`PATCH {status}` transitions** (P:570-579, 614-631):

  | Status sent | What the host does |
  |---|---|
  | `done` | Forced completion |
  | `review` | Request review |
  | `blocked` | Block, with `block_reason` |
  | `scheduled` | Schedule |
  | `archived` | Archive |
  | `ready` from `blocked` or `scheduled` | Unblock |
  | anything, from `review` | Reopen |
  | `running` or an unknown value | 400 |
  | a refused move | 409, naming the blocking parents |

  - **Block** is valid only from `running` or `ready` (409 otherwise, DB:3279-3281). A repeat untyped block can land the Card in `triage` with a 200 (DB:3322-3327).
  - **Unblock** is `PATCH {status: 'ready'}`. The result can be `ready`, `todo` or `review` (DB:3644-3685). Success means a 200 and `task.status != 'blocked'`.
- **`POST /tasks/{id}/comments`** with `{body}` → `{ok: true}`, with no comment returned (P:776-783).
- **`POST /links`** with `{parent_id, child_id}` → `{ok, gated}`, with **no id echo** (P:791-795). `gated` means a Ready child went back to To Do. A self-link, an unknown id, a running child or a cycle is 400.
- **`DELETE /links?parent_id=&child_id=`** → `{ok}`. It is 200 even when nothing was removed (P:798-801).
- **`POST /tasks/bulk`** with `{ids, status?, assignee?, priority?, archive}` → `{results: [{id, ok, error?}]}`. Partial failures are 200 (P:832-851).
- **`POST /dispatch?board=&dry_run=&max=8`** → `DispatchResult`. Its keys match today's `KanbanDispatchResult` (`kanban_db_dispatch.py:91-130`).
- **Boards:**
  - `POST /boards` with `{slug, name?, description?, icon?, color?, switch}` → `{board, current}`;
  - `PATCH /boards/{slug}`;
  - `DELETE /boards/{slug}?delete=false` (archive) → `{result, current}`;
  - `POST /boards/{slug}/switch` (P:1414-1514).
  - Never send `default_workdir` or `project_id`.

## Plan

- [ ] **Writes on the client.** `HermesKanbanClient` implements every write in `KanbanDataClient`:
  - create, edit, status, block and unblock, comment, add and remove dependency, bulk, dispatch, and board create, edit, archive and switch;
  - every envelope reports `readOnly: false`;
  - dependency envelopes are filled from the request, because the host echoes no ids;
  - `KanbanDependencyMutationValidator` (`HermesMobile/Models/Kanban.swift:748`) accepts that filled echo;
  - with no `changed` from the host, every successful write refetches the board or the Card.
- [ ] **No To Do on Hermes.**
  - `createStatuses` on Hermes is Triage and Ready. Ready with an open prerequisite lands in To Do by the host's own rule, and the UI shows the Card where the host put it.
  - `ordinaryDestinations`, the bulk menu and restore-from-archived never offer To Do on Hermes. Restore goes to Ready.
- [ ] **Scheduled and Review.** Neither is offered as a destination. A Card in either one offers today's destinations. Moving it to Ready from Scheduled unblocks it, and moving it anywhere from Review reopens it.
- [ ] **Block and unblock.**
  - Block is offered only for Ready and Running Cards on Hermes.
  - The Card is placed where the reply says, which can be Triage.
  - Unblock succeeds when the reply's status isn't `blocked`.
- [ ] **Assign.** Unassign sends `""` on PATCH, and create sends null when there is no assignee.
- [ ] **Tenant.** The editor's tenant field (`KanbanCardEditorView.swift:108-117`) is editable on create and read-only on edit on Hermes. Edit requests never carry `tenant`.
- [ ] **Workspace kind.** The editor sends `workspace_kind` only when the user picks one. It defaults to the board's `default_workspace_kind`.
- [ ] **Messages.** A 400 or 409 `detail` shows the host's message in today's error placement. A create `warning` shows as a notice.
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/agents/kanban.md` § Hermes gets the To Do rule, the block and unblock semantics, and tenant being create-only.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-05):**
1. **To Do on Hermes:** never offered when creating or moving. Cards go to Triage or Ready, and the host puts a Card in To Do while it has an open prerequisite.
2. **Scheduled and Review:** a Card can be moved out of them, never into them.
3. **Tenant:** set on create, read-only after.
4. **Workspace kind:** sent only when the user picks one, so a project board keeps its default.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Create offers Triage and Ready on Hermes. Triage sends `triage: true`. Ready with an open prerequisite shows the Card in To Do.
- [ ] No Hermes menu, bulk action or restore offers To Do. Scheduled and Review are never destinations.
- [ ] Edit never sends `tenant`. Unassign sends `""`. Create with no assignee sends null.
- [ ] Block is offered only on Ready and Running Cards. A block that lands in Triage shows the Card in Triage without an error. Unblock succeeds on any non-blocked reply.
- [ ] Add and remove dependency succeed without an id echo, and `gated` reflects the child's new Column after the refetch.
- [ ] Comments appear after posting.
- [ ] Bulk shows per-Card failures. Dispatch shows today's summary.
- [ ] Board create, edit, archive and switch work and keep the per-server board preference.
- [ ] Every 400 or 409 shows the host's message, and the Card returns to where the host has it.
- [ ] webui Kanban writes behave as before.

## Tests

These fail on today's code unless noted.
- **Hermes Kanban client writes:** fixtures for each route above. They cover `""` vs null for the assignee, no `tenant` on PATCH, `workspace_kind` only when picked, the dependency echo fill, the 409 detail, and bulk partial failure.
- **`KanbanCardEditorStateTests`:** Hermes create statuses, a read-only tenant on edit, and the workspace-kind default.
- **`KanbanFeatureStateTests`:**
  - destinations with no To Do, Scheduled or Review;
  - block availability and a block landing in Triage;
  - unblock to To Do or Review;
  - a refetch after each write;
  - rollback of an optimistic move on a 409.
- **Run:** `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanCardEditorStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanCardDetailStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientKanbanTests`, plus the Hermes Kanban client class.

## Validation plan

On `scripts/local-hermes`, on one disposable board:
- create in Triage and in Ready (with and without an open parent);
- move, block twice, unblock, link and unlink, comment, bulk-move and dispatch with `dry_run`;
- archive the board.

Record the replies in the PR. Never on the maintainer's host.

## Mocks

Not required. Today's editor, menus and sheets are reused, with fewer options on Hermes. If a new control is needed, stop and ask.

## Manual test

Device: the simulator, signed in with `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`, on a disposable board.
1. Create a Card in Triage, then move it to Ready. Expected: no To Do option anywhere.
2. Add a prerequisite to a Ready Card. Expected: it moves to To Do on its own.
3. Block and unblock a Ready Card. Expected: Blocked, then back.
4. Edit a Card. Expected: tenant shown but not editable.
5. Switch to webui. Expected: To Do is offered there as before.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the board, the Card detail, the editor and the bulk menu.
- **Targets:** main app and tests.
- **Reverse states:** block ↔ unblock, archive ↔ restore, link ↔ unlink, assign ↔ unassign, and an optimistic move rolls back on refusal.
- **Servers:** writes go only to the active server's connection.

## Preservation

- #1043's read paths and its Hermes validator.
- `docs/agents/kanban.md`'s optimistic-update rules.

## Outside reach

Card delete, attachments, runs, reclaim and reassign, specify and decompose. These are not in today's app.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: feat(hermes): live Kanban updates on Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes server, the Kanban board updates live as agents move Cards, including through a Cloudflare tunnel on a quiet board.
**Why it matters:** #704 (phase 4) of Hermex 2.0 (#713). #1043's Hermes board only refreshes on pull or foreground. The host's live channel is a ticketed WebSocket that sends nothing while the board is quiet, so a tunnel drops it unless the phone keeps it alive.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator, plus one phone step through the tunnel at the merge walk.

Part of #704 (slice 4.3) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1043 · **Unblocks:** none · Can run beside #1044

## Problem and outcome

`KanbanEventStreamingClient` is URL-based, `start(url:onFrame:onFailure:)` (`HermesMobile/Networking/KanbanEventStreamClient.swift:57-65`):
- `KanbanFeatureState.startStream()` builds webui's SSE URL itself (`KanbanFeatureState.swift:2467`).
- The SSE client sends webui's `CustomHeaderStore` headers (`:68-145`).
- Backoff is 1/2/4 s, with polling of webui's `/events` after three failures (`:2525-2642`).

The Hermes host has no events route and a different socket.

After this, on a Hermes server:
- The board opens a Kanban socket with a fresh ticket and the connection's saved custom headers.
- It refreshes when events arrive and stays alive through the tunnel with client pings.
- It reconnects with backoff and falls back to polling the board.

webui keeps its SSE stream.

## Contract

Read from source at `ca678285` (0.21.5). `P` = `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`. Re-check against `scripts/local-hermes` before building on it.

- **Socket:** `wss://<host>/api/plugins/kanban/events?board=<slug>&since=<int>&ticket=<t>` (P:1730-1739).
  - **No subprotocol.** The server accepts without echoing one, so offering one fails in strict clients.
  - The board is fixed for the life of the connection. An invalid slug silently uses the active board. A non-integer `since` becomes 0.
- **Ticket:** `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` → `{ticket, ttl_seconds: 30}`. It is single-use and not bound to a path (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py:458-467`, `ws_tickets.py:21-60`). Mint one per connect, as `HermesConnection.gatewayUpgrade` does (`HermesConnection.swift:209-223`).
- **Auth failure:** the server closes before accepting, which arrives as **HTTP 403 on the upgrade**, not a 1008 frame (P:1732-1734). A server error closes with 1000.
- **Frames:** `{events: [{id, task_id, run_id, kind, payload, created_at}], cursor}`, sent only when new events exist. The server polls every 0.3 s, with at most 200 events per frame (P:1666, 1696-1707). Client messages are read and ignored (P:1745-1749).
- **No hello and no heartbeat.**
  - uvicorn's protocol pings (20 s) are **off on loopback binds** (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:1166, 1182-1202`), which is how a tunneled dashboard runs.
  - The phone must send WebSocket ping frames itself, or Cloudflare closes the idle socket at about 100 s.
- **Cursor:**
  - Seed it from the board's `latest_event_id`.
  - The server sends `id > since` only, so a recreated database with a lower `MAX(id)` stays silent (P:1696-1699).
  - The client resets when a board reload's `latest_event_id` is lower than its cursor.
- **No REST events route.** The polling fallback reloads `/board` and compares `latest_event_id`.

## Plan

- [ ] **Protocol.** `KanbanEventStreamingClient.start` takes a board and cursor instead of a URL: `start(board:since:onFrame:onFailure:)`.
  - The webui SSE client builds its own URL from these.
  - `KanbanStreamSpy` (`HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests.swift:730-757`) and the DEBUG Lab stream (`KanbanLabView.swift:2995`) follow.
- [ ] **Hermes socket.** Add `KanbanWebSocketEventClient` beside the Hermes networking.
  - Each connect mints a ticket and builds the upgrade through `HermesConnection`, so the saved custom headers go on it, same-origin only, as on `/api/ws`. This is the piece #898 left here.
  - The upgrade uses `?ticket=` and no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`.
  - The socket goes through the connection's `URLSession` or an injected socket factory for tests (the `BotSocket` pattern, `HermesGateway.swift:34, 463`).
  - The open state comes from a successful upgrade. No hello frame is expected; the feature state treats open as live.
  - Frames decode into `KanbanStreamFrame.events`, and unknown keys are ignored.
- [ ] **Keepalive.**
  - Send a ping frame every 25 s.
  - If no pong or frame arrives within 25 s of a ping, treat the socket as dead and reconnect.
  - Close cleanly when the app goes to the background, and reconnect on foreground with the current cursor.
- [ ] **Reconnect and fallback.**
  - Backoff on Hermes is 1, 2, 5, 10, then 30 s, held at 30 s.
  - A 403 on the upgrade mints a new ticket once before backing off.
  - After three failures, `liveUpdatesDelayed` shows as today, and polling reloads the board every 30 s, comparing `latest_event_id`. A successful reconnect stops polling.
- [ ] **Cursor regression.** When a board reload reports `latest_event_id` lower than the cursor, set the cursor to the reload's value and reconnect.
- [ ] **Turn it on.** Lift #1043's "no stream on Hermes".
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/agents/kanban.md` § Hermes covers the socket, the keepalive and the regression rule. `docs/agents/bots.md` notes that custom headers go on both Hermes sockets.

## Decisions

**Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-05):**
1. **The phone keeps the socket alive** with ping frames every 25 s, because the host sends nothing on a quiet board and no protocol pings when it is bound to loopback.
2. **Custom headers go on the upgrade** through `HermesConnection` (carried from #898).
3. **Testing:** the socket is checked against `scripts/local-hermes`. The quiet-board tunnel check is a phone step at the merge walk, with no `needs-manual-validation` label.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Opening a Hermes board connects one socket with a fresh ticket in the query and no subprotocol. The saved custom headers are on the upgrade, and are dropped for a different origin.
- [ ] An event frame advances the cursor and triggers one coalesced board reload.
- [ ] A quiet board stays connected through the tunnel for more than 5 minutes.
- [ ] A dead socket (no pong) reconnects with the current cursor. Backoff follows 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 s.
- [ ] Three failures show "live updates delayed" and start board polling. A reconnect stops polling.
- [ ] A cursor regression resets and reconnects.
- [ ] Leaving the board, backgrounding or switching servers closes the socket. Nothing is mutated after its owner is gone.
- [ ] webui live updates behave as before.

## Tests

These fail on today's code unless noted.
- **`KanbanLiveUpdateTests`** on a fake socket and a scripted clock, with no sleeps:
  - ticket per connect;
  - the URL and no subprotocol;
  - headers on the upgrade;
  - frames advance the cursor;
  - ping timeout and reconnect;
  - the backoff sequence;
  - 403 then a fresh ticket;
  - the polling fallback and recovery;
  - cursor regression;
  - teardown with no late mutation.
- The existing webui cases pass through the new `start(board:since:)`.
- **Run:** `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanEventStreamClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests`.

## Validation plan

On `scripts/local-hermes`:
1. Connect with `websocat` (or the app) using a fresh ticket.
2. Move a Card on a disposable board and confirm a frame arrives.
3. Confirm a reused ticket gets 403.

Record the evidence in the PR.

## Mocks

Not required. The existing "live updates delayed" state is reused.

## Manual test

1. **Simulator, `scripts/sim-login <udid> --hermes`:** open a board, then move a Card from another client (the host's dashboard). Expected: the phone updates within a second or two.
2. **Device: physical iPhone, Cloudflare tunnel:** open a quiet board and leave it for 5 minutes, then move a Card from the dashboard. Expected: the phone updates without a pull to refresh.
3. **Device: physical iPhone:** background the app for a minute and return. Expected: the board catches up.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the board screen only.
- **Targets:** main app and tests.
- **Servers:** one socket per open board per server. Switching servers closes it.
- **Connection modes:** loopback, LAN and tunnel differ in whether the host pings. The client ping covers all three.

## Preservation

- #898: headers are same-origin only and stripped on cross-origin redirects.
- #775 and #825: this socket is separate from `/api/ws` and never shares its ticket.

## Outside reach

None.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: feat(hermes): list and open sessions on a Hermes server
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes server, a Sessions list shows the selected Profile's sessions, newest first, with live status and unread dots shared with Desktop. Tapping a row reopens that session in the main chat. **Why it matters:** Today a Hermes server can only start new sessions (Debug and Branch builds only), and nothing reopens an old one. Every other #702 slice, #709's Sessions tab and #703's session folder build on this list. **Cost:** Large. One PR. Simulator against `scripts/local-hermes` plus a read-only look at the live host; no phone needed. Part of #702 (slice 2.1) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #1047 (2.2), #1048 (2.3a), #1052 (2.4), #1053 (2.5) ## Problem and outcome A signed-in Hermes server never reaches `SessionListView`: - `ContentView.swift:98-100` routes it to `HermesServerHome` (`:331-358`), whose root is `BotsInboxView`. - The only way into a Hermes session is the inbox's "New Session" (`BotsInboxView.swift:220-224`, `openNewSession` `:348-363`). It is gated by `HermesSessionEntry.isOffered` (`:3-19`: Hermes home plus a DEBUG build or a `.branch` bundle id) and pushes `ConversationTarget.new(profile:)`. - `ConversationTarget.session(profile, key)` (`Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:7-52`) exists. Nothing constructs it except `.new` promoting itself (`:435`). - `SessionListViewModel` (`Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift`, 1,637 lines) talks only to webui through `APIClient(baseURL:)`. It loads once with no paging (`load`, `:282-363`), and unread is a device-local "seen" mark (`:566-639`, `SessionNavigationState.swift:190-208`). After this, on a Hermes server: - The inbox's + menu also offers **Sessions**, under the same `HermesSessionEntry` gate. It pushes `SessionListView` backed by Hermes. #709 replaces this entry with the bottom bar. - The list shows the selected Profile's sessions (`HermesProfilePreference`, `Features/Chat/HermesChatSettings.swift:7-9`, from #1015) and can switch Profile. - Pages load 100 rows at a time and dedupe. Rows show title (or the host's `preview`), recency, pinned, and the host's `unread`. Rows with a live runtime show their status. - A row tap opens `ChatView(hermesSession:)` with `.session(profile, key: row.id)`. Opening marks the session read on the host, so Desktop agrees. - The list refreshes on `sessions.changed`. webui servers don't change. ## Contract Evidence is pinned to Hermex `490120d1` and hermes-agent `ca678285` (0.21.5). `wr/` = `hermes_cli/web_routers/`, `tg/` = `tui_gateway/`. None of these changed since 0.21.4. **List.** `GET /api/sessions?profile=

&order=recent&archived=exclude&limit=100&offset=&min_messages=1&exclude_sources=cron,kanban,oneshot,subagent,tool` (`wr/sessions.py:173-265`). - `limit` is capped at 100. The defaults are `order=created`, `min_messages=0` (empty sessions are listed) and no source filter. Always send all of these. - Response: `{sessions, total, limit, offset, storage}`. **Never read `total`:** it counts hidden rows the list never returns and leaves out the pinned back-fill (`hermes_state_sessions.py:1473-1484`). A page with fewer than 100 non-back-filled rows ends paging. - **Pinned back-fill:** every page appends every pinned row the page missed, ignoring the archive filter (`hermes_state_sessions.py:1345-1370`). So a page can exceed `limit`, the same pinned rows repeat on every page, and an archived pinned row arrives under `archived=exclude`. Dedupe by `id` and drop rows with `archived == true`. - Row fields used: `id`, `title`, `preview` (first user message, 60 characters, `hermes_state_sessions.py:78-85`), `last_active`, `started_at`, `pinned` and `archived` (booleans), `unread` (`:1374-1375`), `model`, `cwd`, `message_count`, `profile`, `parent_session_id`, and `_lineage_root_id` (on legacy compression chains only, `:1028-1065`). There is no project field. - Errors: 400 (bad param or invalid Profile name), 404 (unknown Profile), 503 (store busy or `storage: {profile: "corrupt"}`). - A GET can auto-archive idle rows when the Profile's `sessions.auto_archive` is on (off by default, `wr/sessions.py:192-194`). **Unread.** `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` body `{unread: false, profile}` sets `last_read_at` to now. `{unread: true}` sets it to 0 (`wr/sessions.py:751-790`, `hermes_state_sessions.py:869-976`). Flags apply across the compression lineage. A session with no `last_read_at` counts as read, so `unread` stays false until some client marks it. **Live state.** `session.active_list` (already `HermesCall.sessionActiveList`) lists runtimes in this gateway process: `{id (runtime), session_key, status, last_active, …}`, where `status` is `idle|starting|waiting|working|streaming|resuming` (`tg/server.py:2781-2801`). Map onto rows by `session_key == row.id`. Messaging-gateway and cron turns never appear. Ignore the REST row's `is_active`: it is a 300 s heuristic. **Refresh.** `sessions.changed` carries `{}`. It is broadcast to every client when any watched `state.db` moves, at most once per 2 s, and fires on every streamed write (`tg/change_watcher.py:118-129,197-239`). A Profile's store is watched only after some RPC names that Profile (`_profile_home`, `tg/server.py:522-543`), so after each connect the list sends one Profile-scoped read (the live-state read below is enough if it carries `profile`; otherwise a cheap Profile-scoped call). A Profile the host no longer has answers 4064. **Identity.** A row's identity is `_lineage_root_id ?? id`. Open and mutate the row's `id`: on a legacy chain that is the tip. By default, compression is in place and never rotates the id (`config_defaults.py:658-663`). ## Plan - [ ] **Endpoint and REST.** Add a `HermesREST` session-list request (`Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift`, beside `sessionMessages`) that takes the Profile as a non-optional parameter and builds the recipe above. Add a `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` helper limited to `{unread}` here; 2.3a extends it. - [ ] **Row adapter.** A tolerant `Codable` for the REST row (every field optional except `id`) that maps to `SessionSummary` (`Models/Session.swift`). Keep `profile`, the lineage root and the host's `unread` and `preview`. Rows that fail to decode are skipped, not fatal. - [ ] **List backend.** Give `SessionListViewModel` a backend switch, like `ChatViewModel.backend` (`ChatViewModel.swift:204`): webui keeps `APIClient`, and Hermes uses the server's shared `HermesConnection`. - On Hermes: page with dedupe and the archived drop; Pinned / Today / Yesterday / Earlier sections as today (`:158-186`); and "Load more" or near-end paging that stops on a short page. - Use the existing `SessionRowView` and sections. Untitled rows show `preview`. - Actions that later slices own (rename, pin, archive, delete, duplicate, move, export, Copy Deeplink) are hidden on Hermes rows, through `SessionRowActionPolicy` (`SessionListComponents.swift:880-960`). "Mark as Read/Unread" stays and writes the host's `unread`. - [ ] **Unread.** On Hermes, `isUnread` reads the row's `unread`. Opening a row sends `PATCH {unread:false}` and clears the dot optimistically, rolling back if the PATCH fails. Leaving a chat whose turn finished while it was open sends it again. The webui seen-mark store is untouched. - [ ] **Live state.** Read `session.active_list` after each load and on `sessions.changed`, and map status onto rows (streaming and waiting indicators as on webui). Follow the inbox's rule for a missed turn end: re-read `session.active_list` alone every 5 s while some row is busy (`docs/agents/bots.md` § live status). - [ ] **Refresh.** Subscribe to `sessions.changed` while the list is on screen. Use a trailing debounce of about 1 s, with at most one reload in flight and one queued, applied only if it is the newest. Unsubscribe when the screen leaves. - [ ] **Open a row.** Route `SessionNavigationDestination.session` on a Hermes server to `ChatView(hermesSession:)` with `HermesSessionChat(target: .session(profile: row.profile, key: row.id))`. The draft key follows `.hermesSession` (`Persistence/ChatDraftStore.swift:168-185`). "New chat" from the list opens `.new(profile:)` in the listed Profile. - [ ] **Profile switch.** A Profile menu on the Hermes list reads `profiles.list`, writes `HermesProfilePreference` and reloads. It is the same preference the composer chip uses (#1015), so the two agree. - [ ] **Entry.** Add "Sessions" to the inbox's + menu under `HermesSessionEntry.isOffered`, pushing the Hermes list. Update `HermesSessionEntry`'s comment to say #709 replaces both entries. - [ ] **Docs.** Add a "Sessions list on Hermes" section to `docs/agents/bots.md` covering the recipe, the dedupe rule and unread. Add a row to `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` if any new per-server state appears. ## Decisions Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-05): 1. **Unread comes from the host** (`unread` plus `PATCH {unread:false}` on open) and is shared with Desktop. 2. **Reuse `SessionListView`** with a Hermes backend. A temporary Debug/Branch "Sessions" entry in the inbox opens it until #709 builds the bottom bar. 3. **One Profile at a time:** the selected Profile, switchable from the list. "All Profiles" waits for #709's filter button (#332). Recommended here: 4. `min_messages=1`, so empty drafts don't list (the webui list hides them too, `Session.swift:585-602`). 5. Re-mark read when leaving a chat whose turn finished while it was open. Without this, the reply you just watched shows as unread. ## Acceptance - [ ] On a Hermes server in a Debug or Branch build, the inbox + menu offers Sessions. The list shows the selected Profile's sessions, newest first, with pinned rows in Pinned. - [ ] More than 100 sessions page in without duplicates. Pinned rows never repeat, and archived rows never appear. - [ ] Untitled rows show the first user message. - [ ] Tapping a row opens it with its transcript, and the composer sends into it. - [ ] A session read on Desktop shows no dot, and one opened on the phone clears its dot on Desktop. Mark as Unread works both ways. - [ ] A session streaming from Desktop shows as busy and settles when it ends. - [ ] Sending from Desktop moves the row to the top within a few seconds, without pull-to-refresh. - [ ] Switching Profile reloads the list and matches the composer chip. - [ ] A webui server's list is unchanged. ## Tests These fail today. - **`APIClientSessionListTests`, Hermes cases (URLProtocol):** the exact query, including `min_messages` and `exclude_sources`; tolerant decode with unknown and missing fields; a skipped bad row. - **New `HermesSessionListTests`:** - paging stops on a short page - pinned back-fill dedupe across pages - archived pinned rows dropped - `total` ignored - lineage-root identity - `preview` for untitled rows - unread read, the PATCH on open, and rollback - `session.active_list` mapping - `sessions.changed` debounce and newest-wins - Profile switch - 4064 for a removed Profile - **`SessionNavigationStateTests`:** a Hermes row routes to `.session(profile,key)`. - **`BotInboxTests`:** the Sessions entry follows `HermesSessionEntry`. - **Fixtures:** shaped from the pinned handler and checked once against a read-only `curl` of the live host's `GET /api/sessions`. Sanitize titles and previews. - **Run:** `scripts/test-sim --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientSessionListTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionRowAttentionStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConversationTests` ## Mocks Not required. The list, rows and sections are reused, and the entry is one menu item. If the Hermes list needs a new control beyond the Profile menu, stop and ask for a mock. ## Manual test Device: the simulator, signed in with `scripts/sim-login --hermes`, against `scripts/local-hermes` with two Profiles. 1. Open Sessions from the inbox + menu. Expected: the selected Profile's sessions, pinned first. 2. Open an older session and send. Expected: the reply streams into it, and it moves to the top. 3. On the host's web dashboard, open another session, then return to the phone list. Expected: its dot is gone. 4. Switch Profile from the list. Expected: the list and the composer chip both change. ## Surfaces - **Entry points:** the inbox + menu (temporary). Deep links, push and Live Activity taps into Hermes sessions are #706. Search is 2.5. - **Targets:** main app and tests. - **Servers:** the list follows the active server's connection and per-server Profile. Walk two Hermes servers and a webui server. - **Reverse states:** Mark as Read and Mark as Unread; Profile switch and back. - **Native quality:** row VoiceOver labels as today; Dynamic Type; no new animation. ## Preservation - #825: one shared gateway connection per server. - #903: draft keys follow the conversation target. - #1015: the selected Profile is client state and never written to the host. Never call `POST /api/profiles/active`. - Bot Chat's own unread (`BotUnreadStore`) is unchanged; hidden Bot Chats never appear in this list. ## Blockers None. The foundation (#700) and the Hermes chat (#701) are merged. ## Outside reach Reading the live host's list with `curl` is fine. The phone pass and any session it creates are Uzair's. Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: feat(hermes): page a Hermes session's transcript with tool output
body:
**What the user gets:** Reopening a long Hermes session shows the latest 100 messages with full tool output, and "load earlier" pages back through the rest, compacted turns included. **Why it matters:** Today a Hermes session's transcript comes from one `session.resume` snapshot: no paging, no tool output and no compaction marker. Undo, retry, edit and branch (2.3) also need each row's durable id. **Cost:** Medium to large. One PR. Simulator against `scripts/local-hermes`; no phone needed. Part of #702 (slice 2.2) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1046 (2.1) · **Unblocks:** #1054 (2.1b), #1051 (2.3b), #1049 (2.3c), #1050 (2.3d) ## Problem and outcome How a Hermes session's history loads today: - `ChatViewModel.loadMessages` hands Hermes chats to `loadHermesSession` (`ChatViewModel.swift:1577-1580, 2683`), which runs `HermesConversation.attach` (`Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:366-404`). - The transcript is the full snapshot's `messages`, projected by `BotTranscriptProjection.project` (`Features/Bots/BotActivity.swift:155-219`) in `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.rebuild(from:running:)` (`Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:576-606`), then applied by `hermesReplaceTranscript` (`ChatViewModel.swift:6886-6905`). That sets `hasOlderMessages = false`, and `loadOlderMessages` returns early for Hermes (`:1919-1920`). - Snapshot rows carry no tool output except `write_file`/`patch`/`skill_manage`, and tool rows have no `row_id` (`tg/session_history.py:233-246`). - Message ids are `/`. They are stable per snapshot, but not across a REST page. - A snapshot with `messages_omitted` is refused (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:578`), and there is no compaction marker. After this: - A Hermes session's settled history comes from REST `/messages` pages, newest first, 100 rows at a time, with tool output and the compaction marker. - Each row keeps the host's row id as `ChatMessage.rowID` and in its message id. - The live turn still streams over the socket as today. - Bot Chat doesn't change. ## Contract Evidence is pinned to Hermex `490120d1` and hermes-agent `ca678285`. Unchanged since 0.21.4. **Messages.** `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages?profile=

&order=latest&limit=100&offset=&include_compacted=true` (`wr/sessions.py:606-643`). - `{id}` resolves by prefix, then to the compression tip (`hermes_state_messages.py:1122-1161`). Only that segment is read; legacy ancestors are not walked. - `offset` counts display rows from the newest. With `include_compacted=true`, rows are deduped display rows, including in-place-compacted rows (`active=0, compacted=1`) and excluding model-only rows (`hermes_state_messages.py:1018-1040, 1069-1078`). Each page is returned in chronological order. - Send both `limit` and `order`: a `limit` without `order` returns oldest-first, and no `limit` returns the latest 500 (`:621-623, 642`). - Response: `{session_id, profile, messages, pagination: {limit, offset, order, returned}}`. There is no `total` and no `has_more`, so `returned < limit` means the start was reached. - Errors: 400 for a bad `order`, 404 for an unknown session or Profile. **Rows.** These are `messages` columns (`hermes_state_common.py:402-429`): - `id` (the row id, the target for `truncate_before_row_id`), `role`, `content` (string or list), `tool_call_id`, `tool_calls` (parsed), `tool_name`, `timestamp`, `finish_reason`. - `reasoning` / `reasoning_content`, `display_kind`, `display_metadata`, `active`, `compacted`, `_compressed_summary` (when true). - `role: "tool"` rows carry the full output in `content`. - `codex_reasoning_items` and `codex_message_items` are raw JSON text. Skip them; when they are present, the host's `display_commentary`, `display_reasoning` and `display_content` already project them. The display projection (`wr/sessions.py:574-603`) adds: - `tool_call_labels`; - `display_kind: "failed_turn"` on untyped failure rows; - `display_content` for compaction summaries, or `display_kind: "hidden"`. **`display_kind`** is an open string. Known values: - `hidden` (never render); - `failed_turn`, `steer`, `async_delegation_complete`, `process_complete`; - `model_switch`, `auto_continue`, `internal_notification` (seen in host tests). `skill_invocation` arrives only over RPC. An unknown kind renders its row's content by role. **Live tail.** `message.complete` carries `persisted_turn {row_ids, complete, user_row_id?, final_assistant_row_id?}` (new since 0.21.4), and `PromptSubmitResult` gains `user_row_id`. ## Plan - [ ] **REST.** Extend `HermesREST.sessionMessages` (`Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:98-107`; today it returns the latest 500 for `/background` results) with `order`, `limit`, `offset` and `include_compacted`. The `/background` caller keeps its current behavior. - [ ] **Row projection.** Add a REST row projection beside `BotTranscriptProjection`. It is new code; Bot Chat keeps its snapshot projection. - Message id `"/row-"`, and `rowID = id`. - Tool rows pair with their assistant row's `tool_calls` by `tool_call_id` into `ToolCallGroup`s with the full output as the result.
