title: fix(chat): repeated session_rotated 409 after WebUI compression
body:
## Bug

A WebUI-backed chat opened on a sealed/compressed parent cannot send again: `/api/chat/start` returns HTTP 409 with `code: "session_rotated"` and `continuation_session_id`. Hermex currently surfaces the conflict without opening the existing continuation, so retrying the parent repeats the rejection.

## Reproduction / expected behavior

1. Open a WebUI session in Hermex and let compression rotate it to a continuation.
2. Submit text, quotes or attachments from the old parent (also reachable through idle `/queue` and `/steer` fallbacks).
3. Observe HTTP 409 rather than a usable continuation.

Expected: validate and open the already-existing continuation on the same server and source Profile, retain rejected input plus concurrent edits/files, and require explicit resend. Do not create a new continuation or automatically replay the rejected message.

## Scope and duplicate check

Current upstream `master` bf3fcc04e9a5997ce4d4a402adffb9e09e4bbb6d contains no `session_rotated` / `continuation_session_id` handling in app/test sources. Searches of issues/PRs found no equivalent fix. #955 / PR #1005 handles `agent_runtime_stale`, not rotation. PR #1099 implements direct-Hermes gateway compression, not WebUI chat-start rejection. #438 concerns exhausted-context recovery that creates a new focused continuation; its closure explicitly defers WebUI parity during the migration. This report is a narrow retained WebUI-path compatibility/data-preservation bug, not a request to revive that feature roadmap; maintainer scope acceptance remains your decision.

## Prepared fix and evidence

A reviewed fix is available in https://github.com/rheo-bot/hermex/pull/1 at `1ddb1c11e5a02cc5db303ee28eda6893bd59154d`.

Actual Xcode 27 fork CI: https://github.com/rheo-bot/hermex/actions/runs/37820107661 — Build and Test, Tooling Tests, and CI Gate all SUCCESS. XCTest console case totals: 4013 passed, 5 skipped, zero failed. Python tooling: 9 CI tests and 43 script tests pass. Portable source-extracted regressions additionally cover draft preservation, handoff hydration races and slash-command consumption; these are not device/UI acceptance.

Signed Debug manual iPhone acceptance has not been performed. No live-server/session mutations or device installation were made for this publication.

AI disclosure: implemented with gpt-6.1-sol via Hermes Agent, with independent Codex CLI supplied-source reviews.

title: fix(chat): recover compressed WebUI sessions without losing drafts
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1109.

## What changed

Recover a WebUI chat rejected after compression by opening its **existing, validated continuation on the same server and source Profile**, carrying the unsent composer rather than automatically replaying the message.

- Recognize only HTTP 409 with the exact `session_rotated` code and a valid `continuation_session_id`; leave unrelated conflicts unchanged.
- Retain rejected text, quotes and attachments alongside concurrent edits. Refuse an occupied destination draft; snapshot the latest composer immediately before atomic handoff, including edits during awaited draft hydration.
- Roll back rejected optimistic messages even after cancellation/navigation, retain their files, retire the sealed parent's send path, and do not mistake an accepted stale POST for a rejected send.
- Preserve rejected `/queue` and `/steer` fallback input before slash-result consumption and navigation.
- Add parser, draft-store and mocked send/navigation regressions, plus development/manual acceptance notes. This is one logical recovery fix: lifecycle cleanup and draft retention must land together to avoid partial recovery/data loss; most of the delta is regression coverage. No dependencies or server changes.

### Upstream duplicate / compatibility check

Fetched and inspected upstream `master` at `bf3fcc04e9a5997ce4d4a402adffb9e09e4bbb6d`, plus issue/PR searches for rotation, continuation, compression and 409. No equivalent handler exists in app/test sources. PR #1005 handles the distinct `agent_runtime_stale` 409; PR #1099 handles direct-Hermes gateway compression, not this WebUI chat-start response. Closed #438 creates focused continuations after exhausted compression, unlike navigating an already-created continuation here.

We acknowledge #438's migration-related closure: this proposal fixes a retained WebUI compatibility/data-preservation path, not the deferred recovery-card feature. Maintainer scope acceptance remains your decision.

This PR preserves the exact tested fork head `1ddb1c11e5a02cc5db303ee28eda6893bd59154d`. Upstream advanced by nine commits after that fork test base; `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD upstream/master` returned exit 0 (no merge conflicts). **Fork CI proves the published head, not a fresh build of the new upstream merge tree.** Upstream PR CI is the integration gate.

## How it was tested

### Actual Apple-platform CI — passed

[Final fork CI run 37820107661](https://github.com/rheo-bot/hermex/actions/runs/37820107661), on the exact published head above:

- **Build and Test: SUCCESS** — Xcode 27 build-for-testing and full retained XCTest suite, iPhone 17 simulator. Downloaded console log contains **4,013 passed, 5 skipped, zero failed** test cases and `TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED`.
- **Tooling Tests: SUCCESS**.
- **CI Gate: SUCCESS**.

Earlier CI found one compile-only test visibility error and then two fixture failures (`XCTUnwrap` of a missing staged attachment). Both were corrected: remove a redundant inaccessible helper assertion while retaining the exact unsupported-result guard; give the isolated continuation fixture the real temporary attachment backing store. No production visibility changes, test disablement or weakened retention/no-replay assertions. The final run above is green.

### Local and portable evidence

Fresh publication-time rerun, on the unchanged published head:

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_*.py' -q`: **9 passed**.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -q`: **43 passed**.
- `git diff --check upstream/master...HEAD`: **passed**.

Previously executed on that final head, recorded with the fork proposal:

- Swift 6.2.1 Linux frontend `-parse -swift-version 5 -enable-bare-slash-regex`: **579 Swift sources parsed**; syntax-only, not Apple SDK typechecking.
- Actual `APIError.swift` with a Linux localization shim: **16 checks passed**; two unmodified parser XCTest methods extracted and executed: **2 passed**.
- Source-extracted production draft policy with persistence/key doubles: **9 checks passed**.
- Actual UI slash-result → reconciliation → draft-store bodies with SwiftUI-state/persistence/session-model doubles: **21 checks passed**; pre-fix handler failed **10** checks in the same harness.
- Source-extracted handoff smoke: **8 checks passed**, including concurrent edits during destination hydration.
- Actual draft/file-store portable red/green proof: original fixture refuses staging; corrected fixture writes real bytes, persists/reloads destination text and attachment identity, and retains bytes after handoff.
- Independent supplied-source reviews, including the final test-fixture delta: no actionable findings after corrections.

Portable/extracted checks establish scoped policy behavior, **not integrated iOS navigation or physical-device acceptance**. See also the [fork proposal](https://github.com/rheo-bot/hermex/pull/1) for the development and CI-fix history.

### Not performed / remaining acceptance

The local host is Linux, so `python3 scripts/test-sim <assigned-udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests` cannot run (`xcrun` absent). Apple-platform compilation/XCTest was instead exercised by the linked CI. **Signed Debug manual acceptance, physical iPhone testing and screenshots have not been performed.** No live-server/session mutations, device installation, merge or auto-merge are part of this publication.

Manual acceptance on a normally signed build:

1. Open a WebUI parent that compression has rotated; send text/quotes/files. Expect its existing continuation to open with unsent input and no automatic second chat-start POST.
2. Edit the composer while the response or destination hydration is pending. Both rejected and newer input must survive.
3. Repeat with idle `/queue` and `/steer` fallbacks.
4. Leave during rejection: no late navigation, phantom optimistic message or lost files. Return via Back: the sealed parent cannot submit again or duplicate the transferred draft.
5. Verify invalid continuation metadata, wrong source Profile, occupied destination and two-server isolation.

File links and MEDIA references in replies open the same way. **Why it matters:** Today the Files button is hidden on Hermes, and a tapped file link or MEDIA reference in a Hermes reply still calls webui routes and fails. This is #703 slice 3.1. **Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator against `scripts/local-hermes`; no phone needed. Part of #703 (slice 3.1) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #1114 ## Problem and outcome The Workspace feature reads webui, session-scoped routes through a concrete `APIClient`: - `FileBrowserViewModel` (`Features/Workspace/FileBrowserViewModel.swift:10, 123, 177, 229`) → `directoryList`/`file`. - `FilePreviewViewModel` (`FilePreviewViewModel.swift:77, 90, 103, 141`) → `rawFileData`/`rawFilePreviewData`/`file`. - `TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModel` (`Features/Chat/TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModel.swift:9`) → `mediaData`. - `APIClient+Workspace.swift:44-72`. In `ChatView`, Files is gated off on Hermes (`ChatView.swift:1027`), but `handleTranscriptLink` (`:772`), `onOpenFileReference` (`:659`) and `presentTranscriptMediaPreview` (`:717`) are not, so on Hermes they open `FilePreviewView`/`TranscriptMediaPreviewView` against webui routes the host doesn't have. After this, on a Hermes chat whose `terminal_backend` is `local`: - Files appears (same `showsFilesButton` setting) and lists the chat's `cwd`, folders first, as the host sorts them. - Text and code preview from `read-text`; images, PDFs, audio and video preview from `download`; Save to Files and Share work. - File links in replies and MEDIA references open the preview from the host. - A missing folder shows the existing "folder missing" state, not an error toast. - webui behavior is unchanged. ## Contract (pin `ca678285`) - `GET /api/fs/list?path=` → `{entries:[{name, path, isDirectory}]}` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:617-637`). - Not recursive. Hides `.git .hg .svn .cache .next .turbo .venv __pycache__ build dist node_modules target venv` (`:54-57`) and credential files. - `isDirectory` is `is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)`: **a symlinked folder lists as a file**. - `path` is built from the **resolved** folder, so it may not start with the `cwd` the client sent (a symlink in the `cwd`). Never use it for the fence or for child paths. - Read errors are **200** `{entries: [], error: "ENOENT" | "ENOTDIR" | "EACCES" | }`. - `GET /api/fs/read-text?path=` → `{text, binary, truncated, byteSize, language, mimeType, path}`; first 512 KiB (`:640-656`). 404 missing, 413 over 64 MiB. - `GET /api/fs/download?path=&profile=

&session_id=` → the bytes (`:733-743`). With `session_id` the host checks the session exists and resolves a relative `path` against **its stored cwd** (`:705-716`). Already modelled as `HermesREST.downloadArtifact` (`Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:101, 273`). - `HermesREST.fsList` and `.fsReadText` already exist (`HermesREST.swift:165-168`). ## Plan - [ ] **Workspace context.** `(server, profile, stored key, cwd, terminalBackend)` for the chat, read from `session.info` (`tui_gateway/server.py:2177`: `{cwd, branch, terminal_backend, …}`) by `HermesChatTurnCoordinator` (`Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:132, 871`); `cwd` changes when `session.info` re-arrives (Move to Project, Desktop, #1117). #1113, #1114 and #1117 reuse it. - [ ] **Seam.** A `WorkspaceFileClient` protocol (list folder, read text, download bytes) with `APIClient` as the webui conformance and a `HermesWorkspaceFileClient` over `HermesConnection`, following `CronDataClient`/`HermesCronClient`. The three view models take the protocol. Paths across the seam stay **workspace-relative**; only the Hermes client composes host paths. - [ ] **Composition and fence.** The fence is a client rule, not a security boundary: any signed-in client can already read any host path, and the agent has a shell. Host path = `cwd + "/" + rel`. Reject a `rel` that is absolute, contains a `..` component, or is empty past the root. Child paths come from the parent's `rel` plus `entry.name`, never `entry.path`. Downloads send the relative path with `profile` and `session_id` so the host resolves it. - [ ] **ENOENT-as-200.** `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` on the root → "folder missing"; on a subfolder → that row's failure. `EACCES` → the row's permission failure. - [ ] **Caches.** On Hermes the tree, prefetches and `FileTreeExpansionStore` (`FileBrowserViewModel.swift:269-290`, today keyed by `(server, workspace)`) key by **server + Profile + stored session key + `cwd`**. A `cwd` change from `session.info` drops the tree, expansion and prefetches and reloads. - [ ] **Gate.** Files shows only when the workspace context has `terminalBackend == "local"` and a `cwd`. Unknown (no `session.info` yet) or any other backend hides it; cached/offline view keeps the existing `.disabled`. - [ ] **Entry points.** Transcript file links, composer file chips' open action, and MEDIA references route through the Hermes client on a Hermes chat. Image previews keep the 25 MB client cap on `download`. - [ ] **Privacy.** Rows, breadcrumbs and errors show relative paths. No host path reaches `os.Logger`/`NSLog` or an error string. - [ ] **Docs.** A Workspace section in `docs/agents/bots.md`: the fence, ENOENT-as-200, the hidden folders. ## Decisions Decided: - Client-side fence; `terminal_backend != local` hides Files (#703 body, plan §2). - Cache scope is server + stored session key + `cwd`, with Profile isolation (#703 body; Uzair, 2026-10-08). - The file browser stays read-only: #439, #440 and #441 were closed not planned, so no write action is added. Approved with the split (Uzair, 2026-10-08): 1. **Relative paths across the seam,** absolute paths only inside `HermesWorkspaceFileClient`. Keeps the view models backend-agnostic and makes the fence one function. 2. **Downloads use `session_id` + relative path,** so the host, not the phone, anchors them to the stored cwd. 3. **Symlinked folders are not browsable.** The host lists them as files; opening one shows the preview's existing "can't preview" state. 4. **The host's hidden folders stay hidden** (`build`, `dist`, `node_modules`, …), as in Desktop. No workaround. ## Acceptance - [ ] On a local-backend Hermes chat, Files lists the `cwd`; folders expand; text, image and PDF previews open; Save and Share work. - [ ] A file link and a MEDIA reference in a Hermes reply open the preview from the host. - [ ] Moving the chat's folder (Move to Project) reloads Files at the new `cwd`, with no rows from the old one. - [ ] A folder read that fails with `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` shows "folder missing" (unit-tested). On a local backend the host re-homes a deleted `cwd` to its nearest existing parent (`_heal_dead_cwd`, `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py:94` at `ca678285`), so Files lists that parent after the next `session.info`. - [ ] A non-local backend, or no `session.info` yet, hides Files. - [ ] Two servers, two Profiles, or two chats in the same folder never share a tree or expansion state. - [ ] webui Files, previews and transcript media are unchanged. ## Tests - `FileBrowserViewModelTests`: path composition, `..`/absolute rejection, children from `name` not `path` (resolved-root fixture), ENOENT root vs subfolder, `cwd` change drops caches, key isolation by server, Profile and stored session key (two chats on one `cwd` stay separate). - New `HermesWorkspaceFileClientTests` with URLProtocol fixtures: list, read-text (truncated, binary), download query (`path`, `profile`, `session_id`). - `TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModelTests`: a Hermes chat downloads through the Hermes client. - Existing `APIClientWorkspaceFileTests`, `FileTreeTests`, `FileReferenceTests` unchanged and passing. ## Validation `scripts/test-sim --only HermesMobileTests/FileBrowserViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesWorkspaceFileClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientWorkspaceFileTests`. Read-only `curl` of the three routes against `scripts/local-hermes` recorded in the PR. Manual (simulator, `scripts/local-hermes`): open Files, preview a Swift file and a PNG, tap a file link in a reply, Move to Project and reopen Files. ## Non-goals Writing files (edit, create, rename, delete, upload, zip). The composer `@` panel (#1113). Git (#1114). Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #703 intake.

title: feat(hermes): `@` file search and file chips in Hermes chats
body:
**What the user gets:** Typing `@` in a Hermes chat suggests files and folders from the chat's working folder, and `@path` chips confirm like they do on webui.
**Why it matters:** The composer's `@` panel and chip check call webui's directory listing (`ChatComposerView.swift:543-548`, `ChatViewModel.swift:4334-4445`), which a Hermes host doesn't have, so the panel is empty and chips never confirm. Bot Chat already does this through `complete.path`.
**Cost:** Small. One PR. Simulator; no phone needed.

Part of #703 (slice 3.1, `FilePathSearch`) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** none

## Problem and outcome

`ComposerFilePathSearch` (`Features/Chat/FilePathSearch.swift`) has two engines: webui listing (`search(_:sessionID:apiClient:)`) and the Bot one (`search(_:load:)`, `:105-125`) that `BotConversation` feeds from `complete.path` (`Features/Bots/BotConversation.swift:487-520`, `BotFilePathSearch`). A Hermes chat uses the webui engine. After this, a Hermes chat uses the Bot engine against its live runtime, and chip confirmation asks the same source.

## Contract (pin `ca678285`)

`complete.path {word, session_id, profile}` → `{items:[{text, display, meta}]}`, completing against the live session's `cwd`, `meta: "dir"` for folders (`tui_gateway/methods_complete.py`). Already `HermesCall.completePath` (`HermesCall.swift:135, 444, 542`).

## Plan

- [ ] On a Hermes chat, `ChatComposerView` drives the panel with `search(_:load:)` and a loader on `HermesChatTurnCoordinator` that sends `completePath` on the current runtime, mapping rows with `BotFilePathSearch`.
- [ ] `loadFileChipReferences` confirms a candidate when `complete.path` for its parent lists it.
- [ ] The cache resets on a `cwd` change (`session.info`), as `resetFileChipReferences` already does for webui.
- [ ] Same `terminal_backend == local` gate as #1112; otherwise no `@` panel.

## Decisions

Approved with the split (Uzair, 2026-10-08):
1. **Reuse the Bot engine** rather than #1112's listing. `complete.path` ranks and caps on the host and needs no path composition. This also keeps #1113 independent of #1112.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `@Sou` in a Hermes chat lists matching entries from the `cwd`; picking a folder continues into it.
- [ ] An `@path` that exists becomes a chip; one that doesn't stays text.
- [ ] After Move to Project, old-folder rows and chips are gone.
- [ ] webui and Bot Chat `@` behavior is unchanged.

## Tests

`FilePathSearchTests` (Hermes loader, stale reply after reset), `BotFilePathTests` unchanged, a scripted-gateway case in `HermesChatTurnTests` for `complete.path` on the current runtime.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/FilePathSearchTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotFilePathTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests`. Manual: type `@` in a Hermes chat on `scripts/local-hermes`.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #703 intake.

title: feat(hermes): read-only Git panel in Hermes chats
body:
**What the user gets:** In a Hermes chat inside a git repository, the Git menu shows the branch and ahead/behind, the Changes sheet lists changed files with diffs, and the turn's file-change card appears as on webui. Writes stay hidden until #1115.
**Why it matters:** Git controls are hidden on Hermes today (`ChatView.swift:1039`). Reading the repository is the base every Git action builds on. This is the read half of #703 slice 3.2.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator against `scripts/local-hermes`; no phone needed.

Part of #703 (slice 3.2) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1112 (workspace context and gate) · **Unblocks:** #1115

## Problem and outcome

Git view models call webui's session-scoped routes through a concrete `APIClient`:
- `GitWorkspaceViewModel`, `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel`, `GitCommitViewModel` (`Features/Workspace/GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:10, 69, 498`), `GitDiffView` (`GitDiffView.swift:195`).
- `APIClient+Git.swift:6-95`; models in `Models/GitWorkspace.swift`.

After this, a Hermes chat with a local backend whose `cwd` is in a repository shows the Git menu, the Changes sheet with per-file diffs, and the turn-changes card. Every write entry (commit, stage, discard, push, branch switch, fetch, pull) is hidden on Hermes.

## Contract (pin `ca678285`)

All take `path=<repo root>` (porcelain paths are root-relative, so `cwd` would misaddress files in a subfolder):
- `GET /api/fs/git-root?path=<cwd>` → `{root: <abs> | null}` (`web_routers/files.py:746-754`).
- `GET /api/git/status?path=` → `null` on a non-repo, else `{branch, defaultBranch, detached, ahead, behind, staged, unstaged, untracked, conflicted, changed, added, removed, files:[{path, staged, unstaged, untracked, conflicted}]}`; **`files` is capped at 200** while `changed` is the full count (`hermes_cli/web_git.py:198-235`).
- `GET /api/git/review/list?path=&scope=uncommitted` → `{files:[{path, added, removed, status, staged}], base}`, uncapped, sorted (`:247-280`).
- `GET /api/git/review/diff?path=&file=&scope=uncommitted&staged=` → `{diff}`; an untracked file returns a synthesized all-add diff (`:288-299`).
- `GET /api/git/file-diff?path=&file=` → `{diff}` vs HEAD (`:302-311`).
- `GET /api/git/branches?path=` → `{branches:[{name, checkedOut, isDefault, isRemote, worktreePath}]}` (`:651-673`) for the current-branch label.
- Errors: a failed git call is 400 `{detail: <git stderr>}` (`web_routers/git.py:35-41`).

## Plan

- [ ] **Seam.** A `GitDataClient` protocol over the read calls, webui `APIClient` and `HermesGitClient` conformances; view models take it.
- [ ] **Root.** Resolve the root once per `cwd` from `fs/git-root`; null → no repository (menu hidden). A `cwd` change re-resolves.
- [ ] **Merge.** Rows from `review/list` (counts, status letter, staged) joined by `path` with `status.files` flags (unstaged, untracked, conflicted). A row past the 200 cap has no flags: mark the status truncated (`changed > files.count`).
- [ ] **Map** into the existing `GitInfo`/`GitStatus`/`GitFile`/`GitBranches` models so the views don't change.
- [ ] **Hide writes** on Hermes via the existing `GitWriteAvailability`/presentation types.
- [ ] **Refresh** at turn end, as the webui path does.
- [ ] **Privacy.** Map 400 `detail` to the existing friendly copy; never show or log stderr or the root path.

## Decisions

Decided:
- The panel shows the whole repository (Desktop's scope), not only the `cwd` subtree (#703 acceptance).
- `terminal_backend != local` hides Git (#703 body).

- Fetch, Pull and New branch stay hidden on Hermes in this phase; their app side belongs to #710 only if its companion routes are approved (Uzair, 2026-10-08).

Approved with the split (Uzair, 2026-10-08):
1. **Ship read before write** so the merge and root logic is reviewed on its own.
2. **Keep the existing models** and adapt at the client, so `GitWorkspaceView`, `GitDiffView` and the ReviewDiff canvas are untouched.

## Acceptance

- [ ] In a repo, the Git menu shows branch, ahead/behind and dirty state matching `git status` on the host.
- [ ] Changes lists modified, staged, untracked and conflicted files; each opens its diff; an untracked file shows an all-add diff.
- [ ] With the `cwd` in a repo subfolder, rows and diffs address the right files.
- [ ] A non-repo `cwd` hides the menu. More than 200 changes shows the list and the truncation state.
- [ ] No write control appears on Hermes. webui Git is unchanged.

## Tests

`APIClientGitTests` gains `HermesGitClient` URLProtocol fixtures (root, status, review list, diffs, 400 mapping). `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`: merge by path, the 200 cap, subfolder `cwd` uses the root, non-repo, `cwd` change re-resolves. `ChatGitControlsVisibilityPolicyTests`: Hermes gate.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatGitControlsVisibilityPolicyTests --only HermesMobileTests/TurnFileChangeAggregatorTests`. Read-only `curl` of the five routes on `scripts/local-hermes` recorded in the PR. Manual: a Hermes chat in a dirty repo on `scripts/local-hermes`.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #703 intake.

title: feat(hermes): stage, discard, commit and push from a Hermes chat
body:
**What the user gets:** On Hermes, the Git sheet can stage, unstage, discard, commit (with an AI-suggested message), commit only selected files, and push, with the same guards as webui.
**Why it matters:** Hermes runs every Git write with no host-side guard: no running-turn lock, `commit` stages everything when nothing is staged, discard without a file wipes the tree, and push silently does nothing on a detached HEAD. The guards have to live in the app. This is the write half of #703 slice 3.2.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. Simulator against `scripts/local-hermes` with a throwaway repo; no phone needed.

Part of #703 (slice 3.2) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1114 · **Unblocks:** #1116

## Problem and outcome

Writes live in `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel.quickCommit`/`performRemoteAction` and `GitCommitViewModel` stage/unstage/discard/suggest/commit/commitSelected (`GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:212-310, 577-690`). After this, those work on Hermes through `HermesGitClient`, and every mutation re-fetches status.

## Contract (pin `ca678285`, `hermes_cli/web_git.py`)

- `POST /api/git/review/stage|unstage {path, file?}` → `{ok}`; one file per call; **no `file` = whole tree** (`:314-321`).
- `POST /api/git/review/revert {path, file?}` → `{ok}`: `checkout HEAD -- f` then `clean -fd -- f`; **no `file` = whole tree + `git clean -fd .`** (`:324-329`).
- `POST /api/git/review/commit {path, message, push}` → `{ok}`; **runs `git add -A` when nothing is staged** (`:340-347`). Then `GET /api/git/review/rev-parse?path=` → `{sha}`.
- `POST /api/git/review/push {path}` → `{ok}`; pushes upstream or `-u origin <branch>`; **silent no-op on detached HEAD** (`:350-361`).
- `GET /api/git/review/commit-context?path=` → `{diff, recent}`; the diff is staged-or-HEAD, truncated, with untracked names appended (`:364-383`).
- `llm.oneshot {template: "commit_message", variables: {diff, recent_commits, avoid?}, session_id?, profile?}` → `{text}`; errors 4030/4031/4032/5030 (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:1163-1192`, `agent/oneshot.py:43-68`). New `HermesCall` case.
- 400 `{detail: <stderr>}` on failure.

## Plan

- [ ] **Writes** on `GitDataClient`; `HermesGitClient` always sends `file` for stage, unstage and revert (one call per path); it never sends a file-less revert.
- [ ] **Guards** (client-side, Hermes):
  - No write while the chat's turn is running (existing `GitWriteAvailability.isStreaming`) or on cached data.
  - Refuse a commit with zero staged files (the host would `add -A`). Quick commit stages its paths first, so it qualifies.
  - Refuse conflicted rows for stage, discard and commit.
  - Refuse push on detached HEAD with copy that says so.
  - Refuse quick commit when the status is truncated (existing `tooManyChanges`).
- [ ] **Commit selected:** remember the staged set → unstage all (file-less unstage is safe) → stage selected → commit → restage the remembered set minus committed paths. On a failure mid-sequence, restore the staged set and report.
- [ ] **AI message:** `commit-context` → `llm.oneshot` with `recent` as `recent_commits`; "selected" concatenates per-file `file-diff`s; Regenerate sends the last suggestion as `avoid`.
- [ ] **Consequence copy** for discard (untracked files are deleted) and push (names the branch and remote state).
- [ ] **Refetch** status after every mutation, success or failure.

## Decisions

Decided:
- Commit-selected is a non-atomic sequence with staging restore; `shell.exec` is rejected (plan §2).
- AI message via `commit-context` + `llm.oneshot`, Desktop's flow (#703 body).

- **No "Allow Git changes" switch** (Uzair, 2026-10-08). The running-turn, conflict and cached-data guards, the discard and push confirmations, and the existing Git visibility setting cover it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Stage, unstage and discard one file and a selection; status refreshes each time.
- [ ] Discarding an untracked file asks first, then deletes only that file.
- [ ] Commit with staged files commits only those and shows the sha; with none staged the button is disabled.
- [ ] Commit selected leaves the other previously staged files staged.
- [ ] Suggest fills a Conventional Commits message; Regenerate gives a different one.
- [ ] Push works with and without an upstream; detached HEAD refuses with copy.
- [ ] During a running turn every write is disabled.
- [ ] webui Git writes are unchanged.

## Tests

`GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`: each guard, commit-selected order and restore including a mid-sequence failure, refetch after failure. `APIClientGitTests`: request bodies always carry `file`; `llm.oneshot` admission and reply mapping in `HermesRequestTests`.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesRequestTests`. Mutating checks only against a throwaway repo on `scripts/local-hermes`; never the maintainer's host. Manual: the acceptance list on that repo.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #703 intake.

title: feat(hermes): switch branches from a Hermes chat
body:
**What the user gets:** The composer's branch picker on a Hermes chat lists local and remote branches and switches to one. With uncommitted changes it says "Commit or discard first".
**Why it matters:** Hermes has native branch list and switch routes (`/api/git/branches`, `/api/git/branch/switch`), but #703's slice list never placed them; webui's stash-and-checkout has no Hermes equivalent.
**Cost:** Small. One PR. Simulator; no phone needed.

Part of #703 (slices 3.2/3.4) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1115 (write guards) · **Unblocks:** none

## Problem and outcome

The picker is `GitBranchPickerView` in the composer, hidden on Hermes with the other session controls (`ChatComposerView.swift:977-981`, `ChatView.swift:671`); switching is `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel.checkout` (`GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:181-210`). After this, on Hermes the picker shows and switches; Create Branch and the stash path are hidden.

## Contract (pin `ca678285`)

- `GET /api/git/branches?path=<root>` → local heads first, then remote-tracking refs without a local head (`web_git.py:651-673`).
- `POST /api/git/branch/switch {path, branch}` → `{branch}`; runs `git switch <sanitized>` (`:676-681`). `git switch` on `<remote>/<name>` fails, so send the short name and let git create the tracking branch.

## Plan

- [ ] `HermesGitClient.branches` and `.switchBranch`; strip the `<remote>/` prefix for remote rows.
- [ ] Show the picker on Hermes when #1114's repository check passes; hide Create Branch and the stash confirmation.
- [ ] Refuse when the status has any changed file: "Commit or discard first." Same running-turn and cached-data gate as #1115.
- [ ] Refetch status and branches after a switch.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-08):
- Stash-and-checkout is dropped on Hermes.
- **A dirty tree blocks the switch** with "Commit or discard first", rather than letting `git switch` carry changes across.
- Fetch, Pull and New branch stay hidden; their app side belongs to #710 only if its companion routes are approved.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Clean repo: switching to a local branch and to a remote-only branch works; the branch label updates.
- [ ] Dirty repo: the picker refuses with "Commit or discard first."
- [ ] No Create Branch, Fetch or Pull on Hermes. webui branch picker unchanged.

## Tests

`GitWorkspaceViewModelTests` (remote prefix strip, dirty refusal, refetch); `APIClientGitTests` fixtures for both routes.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests`. Manual on a throwaway repo on `scripts/local-hermes`.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #703 intake.

title: feat(hermes): choose a working folder from the Hermes composer
body:
**What the user gets:** A Hermes chat's composer shows its working folder and lets the user pick another from recent folders, project folders, or a typed path. A new chat starts there; an existing chat moves there.
**Why it matters:** The workspace selector is hidden on Hermes (`ChatComposerView.swift:977`), so the only way to change folders is Move to Project from the list. This is #703 slice 3.3.
**Cost:** Small to medium. One PR. Simulator; no phone needed.

Part of #703 (slice 3.3) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** none

## Problem and outcome

`ChatViewModel.refreshWorkspaceRoots`/`loadWorkspaceSuggestions`/`selectWorkspacePath` (`ChatViewModel.swift:1192-1330`) read webui's workspace registry. Most Hermes pieces exist:
- `HermesCall.sessionNew(profile:cwd:model:)` (`HermesCall.swift:49`) via `ConversationTarget.new(profile:cwd:)` (`Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:18, 450`).
- `HermesCall.sessionWorkspaceMove` (`:70`), used by Move to Project (`SessionListViewModel.swift:2558`).
- `HermesFolderCompletion` over `completeFolder` (`Networking/Hermes/HermesProjects.swift:41-80`).

After this, on Hermes the selector lists a derived set and completes typed paths; a pick on a new chat sets the `cwd` it is created with, and on an existing idle chat calls `session.workspace.move`. Registry management (add, rename, remove, reorder) is hidden.

## Contract (pin `ca678285`)

- `projects.tree {profile}` → nodes with `path` (already `HermesProjectTree`).
- `GET /api/sessions?profile=` rows carry `cwd` (`HermesSessionPage.swift:49`).
- `complete.path {word, profile}` outside a session → host folders (`HermesFolderCompletion`).
- `session.workspace.move {session_key, cwd, profile}` → `{cwd, branch, git_repo_root}`; 4007/4016/4017/5007; moves a live runtime too and emits `session.info` (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:965-1001`).

## Plan

- [ ] Derived list: user project folders from `projects.tree` ∪ distinct `cwd`s from the first page of the Profile's session list ∪ the current `cwd`, deduped, current first.
- [ ] Typed paths complete through `HermesFolderCompletion`.
- [ ] New chat: the pick becomes `.new(profile:, cwd:)`; no pick omits `cwd` (host default).
- [ ] Existing chat: `session.workspace.move` with copy that files aren't moved; refused while a turn runs (existing copy). Success updates the header subtitle; #1112/#1113/#1114 caches follow the `session.info` it emits.
- [ ] Hide `WorkspaceManagerView` entry points on Hermes.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-08):
- Registry writes (add, rename, remove, reorder) are hidden on Hermes.

title: fix(bots): save and share a zero-byte MEDIA file
body:
**Problem:** Saving or sharing a MEDIA file that is zero bytes fails with "Could not load file." It happens in Bot Chat and, once #1112 lands, in Hermes chats.

`BotClient.artifactData` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift:77`) calls `BotArtifactDownload.data` without `allowsEmpty`, so an empty 200 body becomes `BotArtifactFailure.unavailable`. #1112's workspace Files path already passes `allowsEmpty: true` for the same download (`HermesWorkspaceFileClient.swift:85`).

**Fix:** allow an empty body when exporting (save or share). Inline image and preview loads can keep refusing it. Add one test for an empty 200 on the export path.

**Origin:** the third independent review of #1112 (run t3-epic-703-20261009T010352Z-m8odf859) found this. #1112 shipped at its review cap, and Uzair chose to track this here (2026-10-08).

title: feat(hermes): choose a working folder from the Hermes composer
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1117 (Part of #703, slice 3.3)

## What changed

On Hermes the composer's workspace selector was hidden, so Move to Project was the only way to change a chat's folder. Now a Hermes chat's composer shows a folder chip. Its picker lists the current folder, the Profile's project folders (`projects.tree`) and recent folders (distinct `cwd`s on the Profile's first Sessions page), deduped with the current folder first. A typed `/` or `~/` path completes through `complete.path`.

- A pick calls `session.workspace.move`, the same call as Move to Project. A stored chat first asks "Move to …?" / "Files aren't moved." (existing copy). The move is refused mid-turn, and idle is checked again at the socket write. A 4017 shows the existing "can't find the folder" copy.
- **Untouched new chat:** this uses `session.workspace.move` with no confirmation, not the plan's `.new(profile:, cwd:)`. The Hermes session already exists on the host before the first send: `session.create` runs when the chat opens (`HermesConversation.identify`). The host supports re-homing a draft (`methods_session.py:965-1001` at pin `ca678285`); verified on `scripts/local-hermes`, where the first prompt's row carried the picked `cwd`. Once any prompt has reached the socket, the confirmation is required.
- **Header subtitle** now shows the `cwd` folder name, as webui chats do (plan: "Success updates the header subtitle"). The Profile stays on its own chip.

title: perf(chat): show streaming text as it arrives, without the fade
body:
**What the user gets:** Streaming replies appear as the agent writes them: whole words, at most 50 ms after they arrive, with no fade, no catch-up bursts, and a transcript that stops wobbling while it grows.
**Why it matters:** Uzair finds streaming clunky. Text trails the agent by 0.8–2 s or more, the reveal ripple changes speed, the view scrolls onto blank space that fills in later, and the end of a reply lands in one dump. Three stacked smoothing layers cause it. For comparison, t3code dropped per-token reveal and never animates text per glyph.
**Cost:** Medium. Two PRs plus an experiment build that is never merged. Needs the owner's iPhone to judge the feel, take `--hitch-meter` readings, and try the Branch TestFlight build.

Hermes sessions and webui share this path. Bot Chat picks it up when it moves onto `ChatView`, which is tracked separately.

## Problem

Each text delta passes through three smoothing layers before it is readable:

1. **Word drain** (`ChatViewModel.swift:923`, `StreamingWordDrain.swift`). One word comes out every 48 ms. When a burst arrives, the per-tick quota scales up, but the 1 s "max lag" only sets that rate; nothing enforces it as a deadline. A 100-word burst takes about 2.1 s to drain.
2. **Glyph fade** (`StreamingTextFade.swift`, `StreamingTextFadeRenderer.swift`, and the fade window in `MarkdownRenderer.swift:167-415`).
   - Each glyph is scheduled 12 ms after the previous one, about 14 words/s. That is slower than the drain, so the queue keeps compressing and the ripple speed wobbles.
   - Reveal times can run up to 0.45 s ahead, and each glyph then fades from 0 to 1 over 0.35 s.
   - A `TimelineView(.animation)` ticks at display rate for the whole stream plus about 0.9 s after it. Every frame walks each fading glyph twice and takes a lock per glyph.
3. **Row and scroll animation** (`MessageBubbleView.swift:228`, `ChatView.swift:3507-3515`, `ChatMotion.streamingFollow`). A 0.15 s ease-out keyed on the text restarts on every tick, so the row never settles. Because it is scoped to the whole row, it probably also fades in new paragraphs (not confirmed).

Hermes sessions reach this through `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:751`, which calls `ChatViewModel.appendAssistantToken`. hermes-agent already batches deltas on the server every 33 ms (`tui_gateway/ws.py:76`, pin `ca678285`), so arrival is already steady.

## Reference

t3code (`c9fa1367`):
- Token mode was removed in pingdotgg/t3code#2829 over "half-word repaints".
- Its server releases text only at paragraph or block boundaries, at most every 400 ms.
- Web fades each new block once (600 ms, respects reduced motion).
- iOS has no text fade, and its follow-scroll snaps.

hermes-webui's own UI does not fade by default.

## Plan

### Children (run with `/hermex-batch epic 1121`)

- [ ] #1125 Slice 1: remove the glyph fade, its frame clock, the Settings toggle and the Streaming Lab, and snap the streaming row and follow-scroll. The word drain stays for now.
- [ ] #1126 Slice 2: replace the word drain with one word-boundary reveal gate in `ChatViewModel`. Blocked by #1125.

### Owner steps after the merge walk

#### Experiment: reveal mode (branch only, never merged)

- [ ] On top of #1126, add a temporary Settings "Reveal mode" picker with three options:
  - **Live words:** the #1126 behavior.
  - **Blocks:** cut at the last block boundary (a blank line, a closed fence, a list-item start, or a heading once its first content line arrives). If about 1 s passes with no boundary, release up to the last whole word.
  - **Blocks + fade:** Blocks, plus a one-time 300 ms opacity fade on each new block. Off under Reduce Motion.
- [ ] Upload with `scripts/branch-testflight`. The owner picks before the 2.0 release candidate. If Blocks wins, a slice 3 makes it the only rule, with the fade if chosen. If no decision is made, Live words ships.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-09):
1. No per-glyph or per-word animation. No streamed-text fade of any kind, unless the experiment picks Blocks + fade.
2. No display pacing. The screen never trails received text by more than one tick, and bursts land as they arrive.
3. No per-frame app work while streaming. Only brief, event-driven transitions are allowed.
4. The streaming row and the follow-scroll snap.
5. The Settings toggle and the Streaming Lab are deleted.
6. The gate lives in `ChatViewModel` and covers Hermes sessions and webui. Bot Chat gets it by moving onto `ChatView` (separate issue).
7. Ships in 2.0.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Streamed words appear within one tick (≤50 ms) of arriving. No partial word shows, except a fragment held for one tick.
- [ ] While streaming there is no fade, no row-height animation, and no animated follow-scroll. Text already on screen never animates again.
- [ ] When a turn ends, the full reply shows immediately. Cancel, error, interim and snapshot paths keep their current results.
- [ ] Behavior is identical with Reduce Motion on and off.
- [ ] Settings has no "Streamed Text Animation" toggle, and Debug has no Streaming Lab.
- [ ] On the owner's iPhone, the `--hitch-meter` readout during a long Hermes reply is lower after the change than before. Record both numbers in the PR.

## Tests and validation

Each child issue lists its own focused tests and checks. #1121 itself adds one owner check:

- [ ] **Hitch readings.** On the owner's iPhone, run a Release build with the Branch app's bundle ID (`Config/BranchTestFlight.xcconfig`), installed with `devicectl` and launched with `--hitch-meter`. Build it once from `master` before #1125 merges and once after #1126 merges. Use the same long prompt in a throwaway Hermes session, over LAN and over the Cloudflare tunnel. Record both readings here.
- [ ] **Fallback.** If that install doesn't work, push to Branch TestFlight and judge by feel.

title: fix(hermes): reattach when the host reclaims an idle session
body:
**What the user gets:** A Hermes chat left idle long enough for the host to reclaim its runtime reconnects quietly. The next message sends on the first try instead of failing and needing to be resent.
**Why it matters:** The host reaps idle or orphaned runtimes, then announces it with `session.reclaimed`. Hermex ignores that event and only notices on the next write, when the send fails with 4001 and has to be resent. Desktop reattaches as soon as the event arrives. This is a remote-readiness gap on every Hermes chat.
**Cost:** Small. One PR. Simulator only; no phone needed.

## Problem and outcome

- The host tears down a live runtime on `idle_timeout`, `lru_evict` and `ws_orphan_reap`, then broadcasts `session.reclaimed {session_id, stored_session_id, reason}` to every client (`tests/tui_gateway/test_session_reclaim_notify.py:33-45`, pin `ca678285`).
- It stays silent when the client itself closes the runtime (`tui_close`, `ws_disconnect`, `branched`), and when a newer resume supersedes the runtime (`superseded_by_resume`, `tui_gateway/server.py:2659`). Reattaching on the event therefore cannot start a loop.
- Hermex never handles the event: `grep session.reclaimed HermesMobile` finds nothing.
- Today a reaped runtime is discovered only when a write fails. A send gets 4001, then `reattach()` runs and the prompt surfaces as not sent (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:326-329`). Other writes recover the same way (`:657-666`).
- After this change, a chat whose runtime is reclaimed reattaches to its stored key right away, using the existing `reattach()` (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1070`). The next send goes out normally.

Desktop reference: on this event it drops the runtime's cached state and resumes from the stored row (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/lifecycle.ts:91-105`).

## Plan

- [ ] Each chat already admits only its own frames from the shared gateway (`HermesGateway.swift:18-20`). Have the chat also admit `session.reclaimed` when `session_id` is its current runtime, or when `stored_session_id` is its stored key.
- [ ] On admission, call the existing `reattach()`. It only reads, and it never resends a prompt (#508).
- [ ] If a turn is live when the event arrives, treat it as a lost stream and use the existing recovery path, which shows the recovery or waiting line.
- [ ] Ignore the event for any other runtime.
- [ ] Bot Chat still runs on `BotConversation` until it moves onto `ChatView`. Put the handling in the shared engine (`Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift`) if both chats admit frames through it; otherwise put it only in the `ChatView` path.

## Decisions

Recommended (needs owner sign-off):
1. Reattach as soon as the event arrives, as Desktop does. A reattach only reads, so this has no user-visible cost.
2. Never resend anything on reclaim. A prompt that was not sent stays in the composer, as today.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A scripted `session.reclaimed` for the open chat's runtime triggers exactly one reattach, and the next send goes out with no not-sent state.
- [ ] The same event for another runtime or stored key changes nothing.
- [ ] The event arriving during a live turn ends in the existing recovery state, not a stuck spinner.

## Tests

`HermesChatTurnTests` with the scripted gateway: matching runtime → reattach; stored-key match → reattach; other session → ignored; mid-turn → recovery. No sleeps.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConversationTests`

Mocks: none. Blockers: none. Outside reach: none; the contract was read from the pinned upstream. Surfaces: iPhone and iPad chat.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code), from a grilling session with the owner.

title: feat(hermes): `@` file search and file chips in Hermes chats
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1113 · Part of #703 · Stacked on #1119

## What changed

**Problem:** in a Hermes chat, the composer's `@` panel and `@path` chip check call webui's directory listing, which a Hermes host doesn't have. The panel stays empty and chips never confirm.

**Fix:** on a local-backend Hermes chat, `@` now asks `complete.path` on the chat's attached runtime (the Bot Chat engine, mapped by `BotFilePathSearch`). Picking a folder continues into it, and chips are confirmed through the same call. A `cwd` or backend change from `session.info` (Move to Project) drops the chips and in-flight lookups, and an open panel reloads its query in the new folder.

- A `complete.path` that gets no reply fails only that lookup, and the chat stays connected. This timeout is request-local and applies to Hermes chats only (`HermesCall.completePath(timesOutLocally:)`). Bot Chat keeps its existing policy, and webui `@` is unchanged, including a workspace switch with the panel open.
- Chip confirmation asks for the candidate's own path, not its parent folder, because the host caps a listing at 30 rows.

title: perf(chat): remove the streamed-text fade and the streaming row animation
body:
**What the user gets:** Streaming replies stop fading in glyph by glyph, and the streaming message stops wobbling as it grows. Text shows solid as soon as the chat receives it.
**Why it matters:** The glyph fade, its full-rate frame clock and the 0.15 s row animation are two of the three layers that make streaming feel laggy and uneven (#1121). This slice is the biggest improvement you'll notice, and it is almost all deletion.
**Cost:** Small to medium. One PR, mostly deletions. Needs the owner's phone for a feel check.

Part of #1121 (slice 1) · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #1126

## Problem and outcome

- **Glyph fade** (`StreamingTextFade.swift`, `StreamingTextFadeRenderer.swift`, and the fade window in `MarkdownRenderer.swift:167-415`). Each glyph waits 12 ms behind the previous one and can be scheduled up to 0.45 s ahead. It then fades in over 0.35 s. A `TimelineView(.animation)` (`MarkdownRenderer.swift:254`) redraws at display rate for the whole stream plus about 0.9 s. Each frame walks every fading glyph twice and takes a lock per glyph (`StreamingTextFadeRenderer.swift:16-53`).
- **Row and scroll motion.** The streaming row animates every text change over 0.15 s (`MessageBubbleView.swift:228-231`), and the follow-scroll uses the same curve (`ChatView.swift:3507-3515`, `ChatMotion.swift:25-30`). Updates arrive every 48 ms, so each animation is cut off by the next and the row never settles.

After this slice, streamed text draws solid, the streaming row snaps to its new height, and following the stream scrolls without animation. The word drain (`StreamingWordDrain`) stays until slice 2.

## Plan

- [ ] Delete `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/StreamingTextFade.swift` and `StreamingTextFadeRenderer.swift`.
- [ ] In `MarkdownRenderer.swift`:
  - Delete `lingersAfterStreaming` and its `onChange`/`task` (`:19-49`).
  - Delete `AllowsStreamedTextAnimationKey` and its environment value (`:167-185`).
  - Delete the fade window state and callbacks, the `TimelineView`, and `StreamingFadeBlockView` from `StreamingMarkdownChunkedView` (`:193-415`).
  - Keep the stable-chunk split (`StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter`). The active tail renders as one `ChatMarkdownView(isStreaming: true)`.
- [ ] Remove the `.environment(\.allowsStreamedTextAnimation, false)` uses (`BotArtifactMessageView.swift:117`, `ResponseSelectionTests.swift:385`).
- [ ] Delete `StreamedTextAnimationSettings` (`Config/AppTheme.swift:206-221`).
- [ ] Delete the Settings → Chat "Streamed Text Animation" toggle and its footnote (`SettingsView.swift:97, 339-347`), along with their `Localizable.xcstrings` entries. Leave the orphaned `chatTranscript.streamedTextAnimationEnabled` default untouched.
- [ ] Delete the Streaming Lab:
  - `Features/Settings/StreamingLabView.swift` and `StreamingLabReplay.swift`
  - the Debug Settings row (`SettingsView.swift:722-727`)
  - `--streaming-lab` (`HermesMobileApp.swift:93-100`)
  - the `DEVELOPMENT.md:259` row
- [ ] Remove the streaming `.animation(…, value: messageText)` at `MessageBubbleView.swift:225-231`.
- [ ] Make the follow-scroll while streaming unanimated (`ChatView.swift:3507-3515`) and delete `ChatMotion.streamingFollow`. Keep `ChatMotion.scrollToLatest` for scrolling when no stream is active.
- [ ] Delete `StreamingTextFadeTests.swift`, `StreamingLabReplayTests.swift`, and the `streamingFollow` assertions (`TranscriptDisplayModelTests.swift:808-818`, `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests.swift:311-324`).
- [ ] Update the reveal-fade sentence in `docs/agents/bots.md:510-516`.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-09; see #1121):
1. Streamed text never fades: no per-glyph or per-word animation, and no `TimelineView` while streaming.
2. The streaming row and the follow-scroll snap. Reduce Motion behaves the same as before.
3. Delete the Settings toggle and the Streaming Lab. Reduce Motion is the only motion opt-out the app needs.

## Acceptance

- [ ] While streaming, text draws solid with no fade, the streaming row doesn't animate its height, and follow-scroll isn't animated. Text already on screen never animates again.
- [ ] When the stream ends, the reply settles into the static renderer immediately, with no linger.
- [ ] Settings has no "Streamed Text Animation", and Debug has no Streaming Lab.
- [ ] Bot Chat still renders its live reply. It never used the fade.

## Tests

This slice is deletion only. The renderer, transcript and selection tests that remain must stay green, with no new sleeps.

## Validation

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptDisplayModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests`.
- Then build once in the simulator with `build_run_sim`.

Device: physical iPhone. Manual test: stream a long Hermes reply over LAN and over the Cloudflare tunnel. Check that it has no fade, the row doesn't wobble, and following the stream works.

Mocks: none, since this only removes UI. Blockers: none. Outside reach: none. Surfaces: iPhone and iPad chat, Bot Chat's live reply, Settings.

title: perf(chat): reveal streamed text through one word-boundary gate
body:
**What the user gets:** Streamed words appear within 50 ms of reaching the phone, instead of trailing the agent by up to 2 s. Bursts land as they arrive, and the end of a reply no longer shows up in one dump.
**Why it matters:** The word drain releases one word every 48 ms. Its 1 s "max lag" only sets the drain rate and is never enforced as a ceiling, so a 100-word burst takes about 2.1 s to show (#1121). hermes-agent already batches deltas on the server every 33 ms (`tui_gateway/ws.py:76`, pin `ca678285`), so arrival is steady without any client pacing.
**Cost:** Small to medium. One PR. Needs the owner's phone for a feel check.

Part of #1121 (slice 2) · **Blocked by:** #1125 (both change `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests` and the streaming path) · **Unblocks:** #1121's reveal-mode experiment

## Problem and outcome

The drain path today:
- Tokens are buffered in `pendingAssistantTokenChunks`. The first flush comes after 16 ms; after that, `drainStreamingContentTick` (`ChatViewModel.swift:918-943`) releases a quota every 48 ms from `StreamingWordDrain.drainQuota` (`StreamingWordDrain.swift:63-78`), cut by `flushAssistantTokens(maxWordUnits:)` (`ChatViewModel.swift:6571-6590`).
- The tunables are `streamingWordRevealCadenceNanoseconds` and `streamingMaxRevealLagNanoseconds` (`ChatViewModel.swift:578-584, 679-680, 742-743`).
- Turn-end paths call `flushPendingStreamingContent()` (`:963`), which skips the pacing.

Hermes sessions reach this path through `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:751` → `appendAssistantToken` (`ChatViewModel.swift:6540`), the same route webui tokens take.

After this slice, one small, pure gate decides what is visible on each tick:
- It shows everything buffered up to the last whitespace.
- A trailing fragment that was already held back on the previous tick is released, so CJK text, long URLs and code never stall.
- Ticks run at most every 50 ms.
- Every turn-end path flushes everything.

## Plan

- [ ] Add a pure gate type, e.g. `StreamingRevealGate`, in `Features/Chat/`. Given the buffered text and the fragment held at the previous tick, it returns the text to show and the new held fragment.
- [ ] Replace `drainStreamingContentTick` and `flushAssistantTokens(maxWordUnits:)` with one tick that uses the gate, and reschedule only while text is held.
- [ ] Delete `StreamingWordDrain.swift`.
- [ ] Remove `streamingWordRevealCadenceNanoseconds` and `streamingMaxRevealLagNanoseconds`. Keep one injectable tick interval (default 50 ms) for tests.
- [ ] Keep `flushPendingStreamingContent()` and every caller of it as they are, so done, cancel, error, interim and snapshot still flush everything.
- [ ] Leave reasoning flushing as it is.
- [ ] Re-check the scroll-trigger coalescing (`scheduleStreamingScrollTrigger`, `:880-895`) so it fires at most once per tick.
- [ ] Live Activity excerpts read deltas before the gate (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:749`). Confirm the webui path does the same, and leave it unchanged.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-09; see #1121):
1. No display pacing. The screen never trails received text by more than one tick.
2. Cut at the last whitespace. A fragment held for one tick is released anyway.
3. The tick is 50 ms rather than 33 ms: it still looks continuous and costs about a third fewer updates.
4. The gate lives in `ChatViewModel` and covers Hermes sessions and webui. Bot Chat picks it up when it moves onto `ChatView`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Received words show within one tick, and no partial word shows except a fragment held for one tick.
- [ ] A burst of 100 words shows on the next tick, not over about 2 s.
- [ ] CJK text and a long URL with no spaces still stream, at most one tick behind.
- [ ] Done, cancel, error, interim and snapshot paths show the full text immediately and keep their current results.
- [ ] Reduce Motion behaves the same as before.

## Tests

- **New gate tests:** whitespace cut, held-fragment release, CJK, a burst, an empty buffer.
- **`ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests`:** rewrite around the gate using the injectable tick and scripted fixtures, with no sleeps.
- **Cleanup:** delete `StreamingWordDrainTests.swift`.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests --only HermesMobileTests/<GateTests> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests`

Device: physical iPhone. Manual test: stream a long Hermes reply over LAN and over the Cloudflare tunnel. Words should keep up with the agent, and the end of the reply shouldn't arrive in one dump.

Mocks: none. Blockers: #1125. Outside reach: none. Surfaces: iPhone and iPad chat. Live Activity is unaffected.

title: feat(bots): open a bot's chat in the regular chat and retire Bot Chat's screen
body:
**What the user gets:** A bot's chat opens in the same chat screen as every Hermes session. It gains edit history, slash commands, host voice, paged history, the offline cache and live streaming, and keeps its avatar pill and `@`bot mentions. Every Hermes chat also gains Bot Chat's plan, outcome and delegated-work views.
**Why it matters:** Bot Chat has its own screen (`BotChatView`, `BotConversation`, `BotChatComposerView`, `BotArtifactMessageView`; about 6.1k lines in Features/Bots). It predates Hermes sessions living in `ChatView` (Bot Chat #495 shipped on 2026-09-10; #1020 on 2026-10-05).
- **The two screens are drifting apart.** Since Oct 5, about 20 commits added features to the regular chat and one went to Bot Chat.
- **Work is being planned twice.** Issues plan the same feature for both screens (#748/#1082, #766/#1087, #745/#1098, #1038/#1055).
- **#706 would wire everything twice.** It would connect push, Live Activities and deep links to two chat screens.

Decided on 2026-10-09: retire Bot Chat's screen, so that new features get built once.
**Cost:** Large. About eight child PRs, plus a pass on the owner's phone (entry points, Live Activity tap, push tap).

Part of #713 · **Runs after:** #703 · **Before:** #706, which then wires one chat screen · Streaming comes from #1121 (#1125, #1126)

## Goal

A bot's one canonical chat is a hidden Hermes session titled exactly "Bot Chat" (`docs/agents/bots.md:1550`).
- **Engine support exists.** The shared engine already targets it as `.canonicalChat(profile:)` (`Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:7-53`).
- **The regular chat can already show it.** An archived Bot Chat opens in `ChatView` today (`ArchivedSessionsView.swift:160`).

Open it as `ChatView(hermesSession: .canonicalChat(profile))` from every entry point, and delete Bot Chat's own screen. The server already sends plans (`todo.updated`, `todo_state`), delegation (`subagent.*`) and turn outcomes (`message.complete` outcome fields) for every session (`tui_gateway/tool_progress.py:319-325, 443-447`, `prompt_turn.py:822-840`, pin `ca678285`). That means every Hermes chat can show them, not only bot chats.

## Decisions (Uzair, 2026-10-09)

**1. Every Hermes chat gains** (webui chats don't: legacy per #713):
- **Plan row** ("N of M · current step") from `todo.updated` and `todo_state`. Today the regular chat ignores both (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:806`). Port from `Bots/BotActivityViews.swift:27`.
- **Turn outcome row**: error detail, reset time, Retry, billing link and the "not saved" warning (`Bots/BotTurnOutcomeRow.swift`). The regular chat shows error text only (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:892`).
- **Delegated work**:
  - a toolbar button with a count, and a sheet for following and interrupting delegated work (`subagent.list/tail/interrupt`, `Bots/BotDelegatedWork.swift`)
  - the "delegation done" card (`Bots/BotDelegatedWorkView.swift:186-286`). Today it probably shows as plain text.
- **Desktop-task card with Stop**, replacing the "Waiting for you" pill (`Bots/BotPendingRequestCard.swift:58, 500`).
- **App-connection card** for `connection.request/update/respond` (`BotConversation.swift:829-858, 1001-1009`). Regular sessions refuse it today (`HermesChatRequests.swift:94-98`).
- **"Update sign-in"** after a refused password (#884, #942). Never resend.
- **Fast toggle** (`config.set fast`; `Bots/BotChatControlViews.swift:37`).
- **Loop and heartbeat pause/resume** (`session.control`), merged into the existing goal menu.
- **Reply files through the host's download** (`wire.artifactData`), with Quick Look, Save and Share. This probably also fixes reply media in Hermes sessions, which today goes through webui's media API keyed by a webui session ID (`ChatAttachmentCoordinator.swift:422-447`).
- **Offline cache for the bot's chat too**, including showing the last transcript before the refresh (#628). Bot Chat rows are excluded today (`CacheStore+Hermes.swift:70`).

**2. Only in a bot's chat:**
- the avatar pill with its working, waiting and failed face. The face stays still after a short beat (#776) and respects Reduce Motion.
- a fresh Profile read after an edit
- "chat replaced → back to the inbox" with a toast (#554)
- `@`bot mentions. The server only delivers them in this chat (`tools/bot_mode_dm.py:122-131`).

**3. Rules for a bot's chat:**
- **Refused:** `/new` `/reset` `/resume` `/sessions` `/branch` `/fork` `/title`, Fork from here, rename and archive. The Profile chip can't start a new chat (#1038).
- **`/clear`:** refused with a hint to use `/compress`.
- **`/compress`:** allowed. The engine must follow the session's new stored key after compaction (`HermesConversation.swift:237`).
- **Edit, Regenerate, `/undo` and `/retry`:** hidden, per #481. #745 decides whether to reverse that.
- **Allowed:** `/btw`, `/background`, `/goal` and `/yolo`.

**4. Where the two chats differ, the regular chat's behavior wins:**
- Stop asks only when something would be lost.
- Dictation uses the host's speech-to-text.
- Search and read marks come from server search and the host's `unread` flag. The local Bot search index is dropped.
- Request cards sit above the composer.
- The workspace picker is #1117's `session.workspace.move`.
- `@` file search is #1113's, which already reuses `BotFilePathSearch`.

**5. Removed everywhere:**
- **Reactions:** Bot Chat menu, chips, live agent patch, and the #791 stale-snapshot rule. The host keeps them off by default and Desktop hides them, so on the phone they did nothing visible.
- **Gap time separators:** Bot Chat and rooms. Delete `TranscriptTimeline`/`TranscriptTimeSeparator` (`ChatMessageMeta.swift:295-345`). Per-message times stay.
- **Vault prompts:** Bot Chat stops answering `vault.*` (#943 is reversed). Desktop may answer them.
- **Quick-reply chips:** including their Settings editor (`SettingsView.swift:256`) and `botQuickReplies`.
- **Bot Chat's 250 ms `session.resume` snapshot loop and its 50-row local window:** the regular chat's delta streaming and paged history replace them.

**6. Rooms stay on their own screen** (`BotRoomView`). A room is a polled log with whole replies, threads, several speakers, and no plans, attachments or streaming (`gateway/hosted_rooms.py`, `hosted_room_member_activity.py:1-30`). From the files being retired:
- move `BotComposerPill`/`BotComposerPillView` (`BotChatComposerView.swift:574-667`) and `BotChatTitlePillFallback` (`BotChatView.swift:479-488`)
- cut `BotMessageActions` down to Copy
- replace `BotReplyFooter` with `ChatMessageMetaRow`

The room composer stays text-only (#485).

**7. Guards:**
- **Find the bot's chat by exact title.** A Profile's hidden sessions also include room sessions (`Group: <room_id>`, and Desktop's `Group: … · …`), so match the title "Bot Chat" exactly (as today).
- **Never open a room session in `ChatView`.** Sending into one fails with 4122 (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:206-238`), or desyncs a Desktop room. Filter them out of search and archived lists.

## Entry points

Each of these opens `ChatView` on the bot's canonical chat, with the "chat replaced" and "update sign-in" callbacks:
- **Inbox:** the row and the pinned tile (`BotsInboxView.swift:403, 224, 472`)
- **Bot search:** a result (`BotSearchView.swift:66, 361`)
- **Deep link:** `bot?…` (`BotDeepLink.swift:24` → `BotsInboxView.swift:343`)
- **Push tap:** `PushAppDelegate.swift:90`
- **Live Activity tap:** `BotLiveActivityFeed.swift:38`
- **Sessions search:** a hit (`HermesSessionListView.swift:323`)
- **Archived sessions:** a Bot Chat row (`ArchivedSessionsView.swift:160`)

## Must not regress

- **#884 and #942:** a refused password never auto-resends.
- **#628:** show the last transcript while reconnecting.
- **#776:** the face stops moving after a short beat.
- **#617:** a prompt is drawn once even when history already lists it.
- **#716:** no update per token. Use #1126's gate.
- **#553 and #463:** keep the eager list bounded.
- **#878 and #937:** Retry resends the host's raw `inflight.user`.
- **#508:** never resend.
- **#948:** withdrawal notes.

Bot Chat also counted `auto_continue`, `queued` and `pending_connection` as busy. Check that the regular chat does the same.

## Slices

Child issues get written after #703 merges, per #713's phase rule, then run with `/hermex-batch epic <this>`. The expected shape is about eight children:
1. **Every Hermes chat gains the decision 1 features**, in about four PRs:
   - plan and outcome rows
   - delegated work and the "delegation done" card
   - the request cards, "Update sign-in", fast mode and session controls
   - reply files and the bot chat's offline cache

   These need mocks for the new rows and the toolbar button.
2. **The bot's chat in `ChatView`**, in two or three PRs:
   - the pill, the rules, mentions and the "chat replaced" callback
   - rerouting the entry points
   - the compaction key fix
3. **Delete Bot Chat's screen**, in one or two PRs:
   - reactions, time separators, vault prompts and quick replies
   - moving the shared room pieces
   - migrating the tests: `BotConversationTests` (89 tests), the Bot Chat half of `BotChatPresentationTests`, `BotLiveActivityTests`, `BotMessageActionsTests`, `BotAttachmentSendingTests`, `BotArtifactTests`, `BotPendingRequestTests`, `BotMentionTests`, `BotSlashCommandTests`, `BotFilePathTests` and `BotActivityTests`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every entry point listed above opens the bot's chat in `ChatView` with its pill. Nothing opens `BotChatView`.
- [ ] A Hermes session shows the plan, outcome, delegated-work, desktop-task and connection UI, driven by the server events above.
- [ ] Commands and actions refused in the bot's chat are absent, or refused with copy.
- [ ] No reactions, gap time separators, vault prompts or quick replies anywhere.
- [ ] Rooms work as before, without time separators.
- [ ] Switching between two servers keeps each bot chat's drafts, cache and identity with its own server.

## Surfaces

iPhone, iPad, deep links, push (notification tap), Live Activity tap, and Settings (the quick-reply editor is removed). The share extension and App Intents are unaffected.

Mocks: required for the new rows and the toolbar button (slice 1). Outside reach: none beyond read-only contract checks against the pin. Blockers: none in code. #706 runs after this phase.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code), from a grilling session with the owner.

title: perf(chat): remove the streamed-text fade and the streaming row animation
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1125 (part of #1121, slice 1)

## What changed

Streaming replies faded in glyph by glyph behind a display-rate `TimelineView`, and the streaming row and follow-scroll re-animated on every 48 ms update, so text felt laggy and the row never settled.

Now streamed text draws solid and settles into the static renderer the moment the stream ends:
- Deleted the glyph fade (`StreamingTextFade`, `StreamingTextFadeRenderer`), its frame clock, fade-window state and post-stream linger. The kept stable-chunk split renders the active tail as one `ChatMarkdownView(isStreaming: true)`.
- Removed the streaming row's `.animation(value: messageText)`; follow-scroll snaps while a stream is active. `ChatMotion.streamingFollow` is gone; `scrollToLatest` still animates outside streams and, like every remaining curve, is nil under Reduce Motion (#549).
- Removed Settings → Chat "Streamed Text Animation" (toggle, footnote, divider, strings) and the Debug Streaming Lab (views, row, `--streaming-lab`, docs row), plus their tests and pbxproj entries.

Decisions applied: [decision comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1125#issuecomment-6075784332) (build as written; stale doc refs, pbxproj entries and trailing divider removed). The orphaned `chatTranscript.streamedTextAnimationEnabled` default is left untouched per plan.

## How it was tested

title: fix(hermes): keep an unmatched turn-recap path from opening a root file's diff
body:
**Problem:** A Hermes chat's turn-changes recap can show and open the wrong file's diff when the chat's folder is a symlink with a different name (for example `~/current` → `~/projects/app/Sources`).

`HermesGitClient.rowPath(_:folder:root:)` (#1114) can't match a cwd-relative tool path like `App.swift` to the repository root through a renamed symlink, so it returns the path as written. If the root's own `App.swift` is also dirty, the recap row then shows and opens that root file's diff. The `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` spelling is already handled.

**Fix:** a path that can't be anchored inside the root stays unmatched: no row and no diff. If the tool result has a resolved path, use that instead. Add one test for a renamed-symlink folder with a dirty same-named file at the root.

**Origin:** the third independent review of #1114 (run t3-epic-703-20261009T010352Z-m8odf859). #1114 shipped at its review cap, and Uzair chose to track this here (2026-10-09).

Filed by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: feat(hermes): read-only Git panel in Hermes chats
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1114 · Stacked on #1123

## What changed

Git was hidden in Hermes chats, so there was no way to see the branch, the changed files, or a turn's file changes. Now a Hermes chat on a local backend whose folder is in a repository gets the Git menu (branch, ahead/behind, Changes), the Changes sheet with per-file diffs, and the turn-changes card.

- A `GitDataClient` seam carries the reads. `WebUIGitClient` wraps webui's routes unchanged. `HermesGitClient` resolves the root once per folder (`fs/git-root`) and reads `git/status`, `git/review/list` and `git/review/diff` at the root, so a subfolder cwd addresses the right files. Turn tool paths are mapped to root-relative rows (`.`/`..`, `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp`).
- Writes are hidden on Hermes: Stage, Commit, Push, Fetch, Pull, the composer branch picker and the inline commit button. A git refusal shows the existing "Repository status unavailable", never stderr.
- Decisions ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1114#issuecomment-6072292234), [ship](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1114#issuecomment-6076420468)): Preserve #1005, the webui 409 restart prompt is untouched; writes hidden until #1115.
- **Deviation from the issue** ([lead note](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1114#issuecomment-6075443118)): Hermes status is never marked truncated past 200, because `review/list` is uncapped while `repo_status` caps `files[:200]` (`hermes_cli/web_git.py` at ca678285, `repo_status` ~231 vs `review_list` ~247-280). Rows past the cap take untracked from `?` and conflicted from `U`; a staged row's unknown unstaged state reads the whole change via `file_diff_vs_head` (302-311), and before the first commit via `fs/read-text`.
- Known follow-up: #1129 (a renamed-folder symlink cwd can misattribute the turn-changes recap).

Review fixes: 2 red (subfolder tool paths; capped staged row read staged-only), then 5 red (dot segments, symlinked folder, unborn-repo diff, branch summary ×2).
- Read-only curl of every route above against `scripts/local-hermes` 0.21.5 (ca678285) with throwaway dirty, unborn and subfolder repos matched the contract.

## Screenshots

- [x] No new third-party dependencies

title: perf(chat): reveal streamed text through one word-boundary gate
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1126. Part of #1121. Stacks on #1128 (#1125); merge that first.

## What changed

Streamed assistant text drained word by word every 48 ms with a 1 s max-lag catch-up, so a fast burst (LAN) trickled behind the agent and a slow tunnel ended in a dump.

Per the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1126#issuecomment-6075784596), `StreamingWordDrain` is replaced by a pure `StreamingRevealGate`: each 50 ms tick shows everything buffered up to the last whitespace and holds the trailing fragment for one tick only, then releases it even without whitespace, so CJK, long URLs and code never stall.

- One injectable tick (`streamingRevealTick`, default 50 ms) replaces the cadence and max-lag tunables; it reschedules only while a fragment is held.
- `flushPendingStreamingContent()` and its turn-end callers are unchanged; reasoning still flushes whole on each tick.
- Live Activity excerpts still read deltas before the gate (Hermes `message.delta` and webui `.token`).
- A cancelled tick no longer clears the task slot a newer tick owns.
