title: feat(hermes): open a Hermes session from a server-qualified link
body:
**What the user gets:** A link names a server, a Profile and a stored session, and Hermex opens exactly that Hermes session on that server, switching servers or waiting for sign-in first. A session it can't find, or can't tell apart, is never guessed.
**Why it matters:** The route every later #706 surface uses (push, Live Activity, Shortcuts, shares). Today a Hermes server has no session link: `hermes-agent://session?id=` switches to a webui server or shows "Add a WebUI server to start a chat." #706 slice 6.3.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. **needs-manual-validation**, Device: physical iPhone (two servers, cold and warm link).

Part of #706 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #1177, #1179, #1180, #1181

## Contract (pin `ca678285`, 0.21.5)

- `GET /api/sessions/{id}?profile=` (`HermesREST.sessionRow`, `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py:510-523`): authenticated (401 `{"detail":"Unauthorized"}` without sign-in). Body is the stored row (`id`, `source`, `parent_session_id`, `title`, `hidden`, `archived`, `ended_at`, `end_reason`, …) plus `profile` (the requested Profile, not the row's) and `is_default_profile`. 404 `{"detail":"Session not found"}` for a key this Profile doesn't have, including one only another Profile has; 404 for an unknown Profile; 400 for an invalid Profile name.
- It resolves an exact id, else **one unambiguous prefix** (`hermes_state_sessions.py:820-829`). It does **not** follow a compressed session to its tip and returns no `_lineage_root_id`.
- `session.resume` (non-lazy) follows a legacy compression chain to its tip (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:706-721`); `ConversationTarget.session` already relies on it (`HermesConversation.swift:415-417`).
- `profiles.list {include_sessions:false}` returns every Profile with `name` and `is_default`.
- No route maps a stored key to its Profile (verified: none in `web_routers/` or OpenRPC).

## Plan

- [ ] **Link.** `hermes-agent://session?server=<url>&profile=<name>&id=<stored key>` (`HermesDeepLink.swift:109-146`): a builder and a typed `HermesSessionDestination(server, profile: String?, key)`, all parts as query items. `profile` optional. Parsing normalizes the server (`AuthManager.normalizedServerURL`).
  - Legacy forms keep today's behavior: `session?id=` without `server` (webui, `ContentView.swift:168-171`), `webui-push?server=&id=` (`PushNotificationRouter.swift:65-101`), and `session?server=<webui server>&id=` maps to `WebuiPushDestination`.
- [ ] **Routing** (`ContentView.handleOpenURL` `:125-178`, a `routeHermesSession` beside `routeBot` `:195-212`): server not configured → ignore; another server active or signed out → hold it and switch or wait, as a Bot link does; a held link resolves again on `authManager.state` changes (`:41-46`). `HermesServerHome` (`:334-389`) takes a `pendingSessionDestination` binding, turns to Sessions and closes Settings, as `pendingBotDestination` does for Bots.
- [ ] **Resolver** (new, `Features/Hermes/HermesSessionLookup.swift`, main app only), authenticated, on the server's saved connection:
  - Profile given: one `sessionRow(key, profile)`. `""` means the Profile `profiles.list` marks `is_default`.
  - Profile missing: `profiles.list`, then `sessionRow` for every Profile in parallel. Exactly one hit opens; none is "gone"; two or more is "ambiguous" and opens nothing.
  - A reply whose `id` differs from the requested key (a prefix match) counts as no hit.
  - Lineage root: while the row's `parent_session_id` names a row whose `end_reason` is `compression`, step up (at most 8 hops); the chat opens by the requested key and identifies under that root, so its draft and cache match the list row's.
  - The found row opens the way its list row would (`HermesSessionListView.swift:675-700`): a Bot Chat row (`hermesBot`) becomes a `BotDestination` on the Bots tab; anything else pushes `ChatView(hermesSession:)` from `hermesChat(...)`, with `parentKey` and `botChatRoot`.
  - Room sessions (`isRoomSession`) never open.
- [ ] **Refusal** (mock 1 A): "gone" and "ambiguous" show an `ActionToast` on the Sessions list; a transport failure or 503 shows nothing and the link is dropped; a 401 follows the existing sign-in path (#942).
- [ ] `docs/agents/bots.md` (deep links), `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` (the link names its server; resolution never reads another server's credentials).

## Decisions
- **Refusal UI (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** mock 1 A, the existing `ActionToast` on the Sessions list.
- **Missing Profile (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** probe every Profile and refuse ambiguity, rather than trusting a cached Profile hint first.
- **No prefix matches:** a link's key must come back as the row's `id`.
- **Bot Chats keep the Bot route** (#1146): one chat never gets two screens.
- **Moved webui servers (#707):** every legacy form (`webui-push`, `session?server=<webui>&id=`, a local alert) parses into `WebuiPushDestination` and nothing else, so #707 slice 7.4 can send a moved entry's links to its Hermes server in that one place. Same-host sessions keep their id on Hermes, so the key carries over.
- **A link never answers anything.** Approvals and questions appear only as the attach's `open_requests` report them.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each link form above opens its destination on the named server from cold and warm launch; a link for another server switches first; signed out, it waits and opens after sign-in.
- [ ] Missing Profile: one match opens; zero shows the "gone" toast; the same key under two Profiles shows the "ambiguous" toast and opens nothing.
- [ ] A link to a Bot Chat opens the bot's chat on the Bots tab; a room session never opens.
- [ ] Two servers: a link never reads, signs in to or opens anything on a server it doesn't name.
- [ ] Legacy `session?id=` and `webui-push` links behave exactly as before.

## Tests
`HermesSessionLinkTests` (new): parse and build round trip, legacy forms, routing outcomes. `HermesSessionLookupTests` (new): with the URLProtocol / in-memory transport, Profile given, `""`, missing with 0/1/2 hits, prefix echo refused, compression-root walk, Bot Chat and room rows. `BotDeepLinkTests` unchanged and passing.

## Validation
Focused: the three classes. Simulator: links via `xcrun simctl openurl` on two servers, cold and warm. Owner, physical iPhone: a link from Notes to a session on the non-active server.

## Targets
Main app and `HermesMobileTests`. `HermesDeepLink.swift` is shared with `HermesLiveActivityWidget`: only Foundation additions there. The resolver is main-app only. The share extension and notification service are unchanged.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #706 intake.

title: feat(push): land push taps on the exact Hermes session
body:
**What the user gets:** Tapping a Hermes notification opens the session it is about, including a session started from Hermes Desktop or the TUI, with previews on or off, and its approval card when the host still has the approval open. A subagent's notification opens its parent.
**Why it matters:** Today every non-webui tap opens the Profile's Bot Chat, or nothing with previews off (`PushNotificationRouter.swift:26-61`). #706 slice 6.1 routing; the #706 comment's cases 1-3 (an outside reporter).
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. **needs-manual-validation**, Device: physical iPhone (real pushes, previews on/off, cold/warm).

Part of #706 · **Blocked by:** #1176 · **Unblocks:** #1179, #707

## Contract (pin `ca678285`; plugin `hermex-push` origin/main `0259e57`)

- Cleartext payload fields outside `aps` (relay README): `install_hash`, `session_id`, `source` (`bot`|`webui`|`other`), `kind`, `is_subagent`, `sealed`. The Profile exists only inside `sealed` (`plugin/hermex_push/payload.py`), as `""` for the default Profile. `PushPreview.rewrite` writes it back as `hermex_profile` only when the preview opened.
- `session_id` is `agent.session_id`, the stored key, in every hook, including `pre_approval_request` for `/api/ws`, TUI and Desktop sessions (`tools/approval_context.py:67-68`, bound in `model_tools.py:804-817`). When no session is bound, the plugin sends an opaque `keyed_id` instead (`hooks.py` `_approval_session`), which no lookup finds.
- `source` is `bot` for platforms `ios`, `desktop` and `tui` (`plugin/hermex_push/sources.py`), so it no longer distinguishes a Bot Chat from an ordinary session.
- A subagent push carries the child's stored key and `is_subagent: true`; the child row's `parent_session_id` names the parent (`tools/delegate_tool.py:232, 291-296`).
- An approval card comes from `open_requests` / `pending_approval`, which `session.resume` returns only when it reuses a runtime live in the dashboard's own process (`methods_session.py:932-934`, `server.py:2909-2915`). A session whose runtime lives in another process (Desktop's private loopback backend, a standalone `hermes` TUI) resumes cold, with no open requests.
- Compression is in place by default (`config_defaults.py:658-663`): the stored key does not rotate. Legacy `compression.in_place: false` rotates it; `session.resume` follows the tip.

## Plan

- [ ] **Router** (`Push/PushNotificationRouter.swift`): `source == "webui"` keeps `webuiDestination` (`:10-24`). Any other source, with a matching pairing whose server is Hermes-typed (active server first, then by URL), becomes a `HermesSessionDestination(server, profile: hermex_profile, key: session_id)` and queues #1176's link (`PushAppDelegate.swift:68-95`). `is_subagent` asks the resolver to open the row's `parent_session_id` (one hop). The existing `botDestination` (`:38-61`) stays only for a webui server's Bot connection (legacy Bot Mode).
- [ ] **Resolver** (#1176's): no new lookup; a subagent's parent step is the one addition.
- [ ] **Presence** (`ChatViewModel.swift:564-567`, `PushPresence`): a Hermes chat reports its current `engine.storedKey`, updated when `adoptStoredKey` moves it, so foreground suppression matches the payload.
- [ ] **Local run alerts** (`Config/AppTheme.swift:600-635`): a Hermes chat's alert carries its Profile and stored key, and its tap opens #1176's link instead of a webui route.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/push.md` (Hermes taps, the shared-host caveat now names Hermes servers) and `docs/agents/bots.md` § Push previews and taps (the old "the destination carries no conversation" rule goes).

## Decisions
- **A push is a hint, never authority.** A tap only navigates through the authenticated lookup; it never answers an approval or question. Notification actions stay #750.
- **Previews off:** no Profile, so the lookup probes every Profile and refuses ambiguity (#1176) (Uzair, 2026-10-10).
- **Stale or expired:** a session that is gone shows #1176's toast; an approval the host has already settled or expired simply has no card.
- **Another process's runtime:** the tap opens the transcript with no card. Hermex never claims a card it cannot answer (Uzair, 2026-10-10).
- **Subagents:** one hop to the parent (Uzair, 2026-10-10).
- **Bot Chats keep the Bot route** through #1176's row mapping.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An approval in an ordinary session (not a Bot Chat) started from Hermex, Desktop or the TUI against this dashboard opens that session with its current approval card (#706 comment, case 1).
- [ ] A session compressed since the push opens at its current tip, under the identity its list row uses (case 2).
- [ ] With previews off, a key under two Profiles refuses; a deleted session refuses; the push never answers (case 3).
- [ ] A Bot Chat push still opens the bot's chat; a webui push and a webui server's Bot push are unchanged.
- [ ] A subagent push opens its parent.
- [ ] Foreground: a reply about the open session is suppressed when "Quiet the Open Chat" is on; approvals still show.
- [ ] Two servers on one host (LAN and tunnel) open on the active one; nothing routes to a server the pairing doesn't name.

## Tests
`PushPreviewTests` / `PushRegistrationTests` routing matrix: source (`bot`, `webui`, `other`) × server kind × Profile present / `""` / missing × `is_subagent`. `PushPresence` with a moved stored key. A local-alert tap on a Hermes server.

## Validation
Focused: those classes plus #1176's lookup tests. Owner, physical iPhone, Branch TestFlight, LAN and tunnel: a reply, an approval and a question push in an ordinary session, previews on then off, app suspended then terminated; one approval started from Desktop or the TUI; one subagent push. Needs one disposable session on the test bot per AGENTS.md rule 2; the owner grants it at validation time.

## Targets
Main app and tests. `PushPreview.swift` (shared with `HermesNotificationService`) is unchanged: the extension stays network-free and only writes `hermex_profile` back (target-membership decision for #706's notification-service slice: no change). Share extension: no change.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #706 intake.

title: fix(push): finish pairing a fresh Hermes host and keep a shared host paired
body:
**What the user gets:** Turning on notifications for a host that has never loaded the plugin ends with a clear "Restart Hermes on the host, then Check again" instead of a failed "Pair this iPhone" step. Removing one of two entries that reach the same host keeps the other one's notifications.
**Why it matters:** Plugin routes mount only when the dashboard starts, and `POST /api/gateway/restart` restarts only the messaging gateway, so a fresh install can't finish today. `PushRegistrar.forget` deletes the relay device that both entries share. #706 slice 6.1 provisioning; #706 acceptance "two entries … without unregistering each other".
**Cost:** Small to Medium. One PR. **needs-manual-validation**, Device: physical iPhone (two entries on one host). The fresh-host check runs against `scripts/local-hermes`, never the live host.

Part of #706 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #707

## Contract (pin `ca678285`)

- Plugin routers mount once at import (`web_server.py:1001` → `web_server_dashboard.py:871`).
- `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing` 404 bodies:
  - `{"detail":"Plugin not found"}`: the plugin is not enabled, or not installed and not listed in `plugins.enabled` (`web_server.py:630-635`).
  - `{"detail":"No such API endpoint: /api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing"}`: enabled but not mounted, i.e. installed after the dashboard started, or listed in `plugins.enabled` but missing on disk (`web_server_dashboard.py:222-223`).
  - Under `hermes serve` the catch-all is `{"error":"Headless backend (hermes serve): …"}` (`:87-129`).
- `POST /api/gateway/restart` spawns `hermes gateway restart`: the messaging gateway only, not the dashboard or its in-process `/api/ws` (`web_routers/actions.py:139-144`).
- `HermesREST.pluginsHub` lists agent plugins with their on-disk version.
- Relay device records are keyed by install and device token (relay README), so two entries for one host share one registration.

## Plan

- [ ] **Classify the pairing 404** (`Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift:294-340`, `HermexPushPlugin` decode):
  - "Plugin not found" → today's full sequence.
  - "No such API endpoint…" or the headless body → read `pluginsHub`: hermex-push on disk → a new `restartNeeded` outcome with no install; not on disk → the full sequence.
  - After the sequence, a pairing read that still answers "No such API endpoint" stops retrying and ends in `restartNeeded`, not a failed step.
  - Any other 404 is reported as it is.
- [ ] **Copy:** reuse the plugin card's existing "Restart the dashboard on the host" with `hermes dashboard` and Check again (bots.md § Push provisioning), so no new layout. Check again re-reads the pairing route only.
- [ ] **Shared install** (`Push/PushRegistrar.swift:144-172`): `forget` and `disable` skip the relay device delete, and keep remote registration, when another stored pairing has the same install key and relay URL; the Keychain item still goes.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md` § Push provisioning (gateway restart vs dashboard restart; the 404 table) and `docs/agents/push.md` (the shared-host caveat covers removal; one host's preferences are one relay registration).

## Decisions
- **Keep the gateway restart step** as it runs today (Uzair, 2026-10-10). It is harmless for push and the webui path relies on the sequence; only the 404 handling changes.
- **Shared install (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** forget and disable skip the relay delete while another pairing shares the install.
- **The phone never restarts a dashboard that hasn't loaded the plugin.** No dashboard-restart route exists without it, and no companion route is added.
- **Shared-host preferences are shared:** both entries write the same relay registration, so the last saved choice applies to both. Documented, not split (Uzair, 2026-10-10).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Fresh host (plugin never loaded): enable ends in "Restart the dashboard on the host"; after a restart, Check again pairs.
- [ ] Plugin on disk but not mounted: no reinstall runs; the restart instruction shows at once.
- [ ] Already paired host: no change; webui servers: no change.
- [ ] Two entries on one host: removing or disabling one keeps pushes arriving for the other; removing the last one deletes the relay device.

## Tests
`HermexPushProvisioningTests`: each 404 body, `pluginsHub` on disk or not, retry stop. `PushRegistrationTests`: forget and disable with a second pairing sharing the install (no relay delete), and with none (delete).

## Validation
Focused: the two classes. Simulator against `scripts/local-hermes` with the plugin installed while the dashboard runs (the owner grants running local Hermes on this Mac at validation time). Owner, physical iPhone: one host as a LAN entry and a tunnel entry, remove one, then a test notification still arrives on the other.

## Targets
Main app and tests only. Notification service and share extension unchanged.

title: feat(hermes): Live Activities for Hermes sessions that tap through and stay fresh
body:
**What the user gets:** A Hermes session's Live Activity opens that session on a tap, keeps updating while the app is suspended or terminated on a paired server, and ends cleanly after a relaunch.
**Why it matters:** A session's activity has no tap target and registers the relay under a key no plugin event uses (`hermes:<profile>:<key>`, `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:913-917`; `AgentRunTapTarget` `HermesDeepLink.swift:150-173`), so it goes stale once the app is suspended. #706 slice 6.2; absorbs #1165.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. **needs-manual-validation**, Device: physical iPhone (suspended and terminated, LAN and tunnel).

Part of #706 · **Blocked by:** #1176, #1177 · **Unblocks:** #1180

## Contract (pin `ca678285`; relay README at hermex-push `0259e57`)

- The relay keys activity tokens by session id: `PUT` / `DELETE /installs/{key}/devices/{token}/activities/{session_id}`. Progress events carry the plugin's `session_id`, the stored key. A registration expires after 8 h; each push sets a 15-minute stale date.
- `session.active_list` (`methods_session.py:1004-1014`, rows `server.py:2781-2802`): every live runtime in the dashboard process across all Profiles; rows carry `id` (runtime id), `session_key` (stored key) and `status` (`waiting`, `starting`, `working`, `idle`; also `streaming`, `resuming`); no Profile field.
- Legacy compression moves the stored key mid-turn; `session.info.stored_session_id` reports it (`adoptStoredKey`, `HermesConversation.swift:200-210`).

## Plan

- [ ] **Attributes** (`LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:170-191`): optional top-level `destinationURL` and `pushSessionID`, decoded with `decodeIfPresent` so older activities load. Bot activities keep `AgentRunActivityBot` unchanged.
- [ ] **Identity** (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:897-918, 1408-1440`): a session's activity is `sessionID: hermes:<profile>:<root>` with its `server`, stream `<turn_started_at>`, `destinationURL` #1176's link, and `pushSessionID` the current stored key. `root` is the chat's identity, so a reconnect inside a turn reuses the activity across a key move.
- [ ] **Push target** (`AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:60-69, 655-670, 855-897`): `pushTarget` reads `pushSessionID` for a Hermes session (not `sessionID`), and a session's activity asks for a token only when its server is paired.
- [ ] **Tip change:** when `adoptStoredKey` moves the key, the driven activity registers its token under the new key and retires the old one, for a session and for a bot (`AgentRunActivityBot.pushSessionID`) alike.
- [ ] **Tap** (`AgentRunTapTarget.url`): `destinationURL` when present; the `hermes:` no-destination guard goes. An archived Bot Chat opened by key gets #1176's link, which reopens it by key (#1165).
- [ ] **Cold launch** (`settleActivitiesFromPreviousLaunch` `:507-527`): a paired session activity is adopted like a bot's (the relay drives it). An unpaired one, on the signed-in active Hermes server, is checked once with `session.active_list` (never `session.resume`): its stored key listed and not `idle` → left running; else ended as complete ("Response complete"), since the outcome is unknown. Activities of other servers wait for their stale date.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md` (Live Activity identity and tap), `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` (activity identity row).

## Decisions
- **Two identity schemes stay** (#709 option B): the bot's `bot:<connection>:<profile>` and the session's above.
- **Unpaired cold launch (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** end as complete, outcome unknown, unless `session.active_list` still lists it as running (#713 open decision).
- **#1165 absorbed (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** an archived Bot Chat's activity opens it by key.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Paired server: an ordinary session's activity updates while the app is suspended and while it is terminated, ends at the run's end, and its tap opens the session.
- [ ] A legacy-compression key move mid-turn keeps the same activity updating.
- [ ] Unpaired server: after a relaunch, a finished run's activity ends; a still-running one stays.
- [ ] A bot's activity and a webui activity behave as before; an archived Bot Chat's activity reopens it (#1165).
- [ ] An activity persisted by the previous build still decodes and renders.

## Tests
`LiveActivityTests` (generalized push target, token re-register on a key move, `active_list` reconciliation with listed / idle / absent keys, old-attributes decode), `HermesChatLiveActivityTests` (identity and destination), `BotLiveActivityTests` (bot re-register on a key move).

## Validation
Focused: those classes. Owner, physical iPhone, Branch TestFlight, LAN and tunnel past the idle cutoff: start a run, lock, suspend; start a run, terminate; tap the activity; one paired and one unpaired server.

## Targets
Main app, `HermesLiveActivityWidget` (`AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift` and `HermesDeepLink.swift` are shared: optional decode, precomputed URL, no new widget work), tests. Notification service and share extension unchanged.

title: feat(hermes): New Chat Shortcuts on Hermes servers
body:
**What the user gets:** New Chat, New Chat with Voice and New Chat in Profile open a new Hermes session on a Hermes server, and the Profile picker lists each server's Profiles under that server's name.
**Why it matters:** On a Hermes server all three switch to a webui server or show "Add a WebUI server to start a chat." (`ContentView.swift:139-159, 219-230`), and the picker shows only webui Profiles (`ProfileEntity.swift:100-108`). #706 slice 6.4.
**Cost:** Medium. One PR. **needs-manual-validation**, Device: physical iPhone (Siri, Action button, Shortcuts).

Part of #706 · **Blocked by:** #1176 (routing into `HermesServerHome`), #1179 (file overlap) · **Unblocks:** #1181

## Contract (pin `ca678285`)

- Public `GET /api/status` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:456-552`, listed in `public_paths.py:15`) reports `profiles`, a list of Profile **names**, even on a gated host. Display names are not public.
- `session.create {profile, cwd?, model?}` returns `stored_session_id`; an unknown Profile is error 4064 (`server.py:512-530`). `ConversationTarget.new` already sends it on the first attach.
- Custom headers ride on the `/api/status` read, as every request to the server origin does (the intent process reads them from the Keychain as `ProfileEntityProvider` does today).

## Plan

- [ ] **Entity ids** (`AppIntents/ProfileEntity.swift`): Hermes entities are `<server URL>|<profile>`; webui entities keep their bare name, so saved Shortcuts keep resolving as they do now.
- [ ] **Picker:** `suggestedEntities` returns sections per configured server (mock 3 A). A Hermes section reads `/api/status` `profiles` with that server's headers, titled by the display name the Bots roster last cached in the app group, else the slug. Failure falls back to that cache, per server.
- [ ] **New Chat in Profile:** a Hermes entity opens `ChatView(hermesSession: .new(profile:))` on its server through #1176's routing (switch or wait for sign-in). A bare id keeps today's webui route.
- [ ] **New Chat and New Chat with Voice:** on an active Hermes server, open `.new(profile:)` on the Profile the Sessions list's New Session uses, with voice auto-start for the voice variant (`ChatView.autoStartsVoiceInput`). On an active webui server, unchanged. `reachWebuiServer` then serves only shares (#1181).
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md` (Shortcuts on Hermes).

## Decisions
- **Picker layout (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** mock 3 A, one section per configured server.
- **Bots in the picker** (#713 open decision): a Profile is a bot, so it is listed once; New Chat in Profile starts a new session in it, never its Bot Chat (Uzair, 2026-10-10).
- **Moved webui servers (#707):** a bare-id Shortcut resolves through one function (`ProfileEntityProvider.profileServer`), so #707 can point a moved entry's saved Shortcuts at its Hermes server without the user re-creating them.
- **New Chat and New Chat with Voice (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** open a Hermes session on an active Hermes server; never switch to a webui server.
- **No sign-in from the intent process:** names come from the public status; the app shows the chat.

## Acceptance
- [ ] On a Hermes server, each of the three intents opens a new Hermes session on the right Profile and server; voice starts dictation.
- [ ] Two servers with the same Profile name appear as two choices; each opens on its own server.
- [ ] A Shortcut saved before this build still opens its webui Profile.
- [ ] Offline or signed out, the picker shows the cached names and the intent waits for sign-in.

## Tests
`AppIntentNewChatInProfileTests` (id round trip, legacy bare id, per-server sections, cache fallback), `AppIntentNewChatTests` (Hermes vs webui active), entity provider with URLProtocol mocks for `/api/status`.

## Validation
Focused: those classes. Owner, physical iPhone: Siri "New chat in Hermex", Action button, a New Chat in Profile Shortcut for each of two servers.

## Targets
Main app (App Intents run in the app process) and tests. Widget, notification service and share extension unchanged.

title: feat(hermes): share text and files into a new Hermes session
body:

title: feat(onboarding): a setup prompt for a Hermes dashboard
body:
**What the user gets:** Onboarding's step 1 leads with a prompt that sets up the Hermes dashboard for the phone: password sign-in, sign-ins that survive a restart, the right public address, and an HTTPS route.
**Why it matters:** Step 1 only knows how to set up Hermes Web UI over Tailscale (`OnboardingFlowPolicy.swift:8-37`, `OnboardingAgentPromptPage.swift`). A Hermes host off loopback refuses to run without sign-in, and a per-process secret signs the phone out on every restart. #706 slice 6.5 (kind detection and the username field landed in #900).
**Cost:** Small. One PR. Simulator only.

Part of #706 · **Blocked by:** none · **Related:** #712 (this child takes onboarding's share of the Hermes-first default)

## Contract (pin `ca678285`)

- Basic auth (`plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py:191-253`): `dashboard.basic_auth.username` plus `password_hash` (from `plugins.dashboard_auth.basic.hash_password`) or `password` in `config.yaml`, or the `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_*` env vars. Without `dashboard.basic_auth.secret` (or `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET`) the signing key is per process, so every restart signs the phone out.
- A non-loopback bind or a non-loopback `dashboard.public_url` requires the gate (`web_server.py:470-495`). `dashboard.public_url` (or `HERMES_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_URL`) must match the address the phone uses, else `400 Invalid Host header` (`web_server.py:577-593`).
- `hermes dashboard --host --port`, default port 9119.

## Plan

- [ ] `OnboardingFlowPolicy.hermesSetupPrompt`: inventory first (the running dashboard, its host and port, `config.yaml`, any tunnel), reuse working state, set basic auth with a hashed password and a random persistent secret, set `dashboard.public_url` to the phone's address, expose it over HTTPS (Cloudflare Tunnel or a private network) or same Wi-Fi, never run without the gate, verify with `curl` against `/api/status`, reply with the address and username. Today's webui prompt stays word for word.
- [ ] `OnboardingAgentPromptPage` (mock 2 C): titled "Set up Hermes", shows the Hermes prompt, and a "Using Hermes Web UI instead?" link swaps in today's webui prompt (and a link back). The copy reminder follows the prompt shown; the page count is unchanged.
- [ ] Strings in `Localizable.xcstrings`, all languages, `needs_review` (`docs/agents/i18n.md`); the prompt text itself stays English, as today.
- [ ] Docs: `README.md` setup options and `DEVELOPMENT.md` (a Hermes host needs basic auth and a persistent secret).

## Decisions
- **Hermes first (Uzair, 2026-10-10):** mock 2 C. Hermex encourages the Hermes connection because webui will be sunset; Web UI stays one tap away as legacy.
- **"Password-less webui setups cannot move" copy moves to #707**, where moving is offered (Uzair, 2026-10-10).
- **Bot Mode (beta) gate:** the Connect page's "Turn on Bot Mode (beta) and continue" offer (#900) stays until #712 removes it (Uzair, 2026-10-10).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Step 1 opens on the Hermes prompt; the link swaps to the webui prompt and back; Copy copies the one shown; the copy reminder still gates Continue.
- [ ] The Hermes prompt names `dashboard.basic_auth.secret` and `dashboard.public_url` and never suggests `--insecure`.
- [ ] Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, RTL pseudolanguage and light/dark pass on the page.

## Tests
`OnboardingFlowTests`: the Hermes prompt's required lines (basic auth, secret, public_url, no `--insecure`), Hermes shown first, the copy reminder per prompt, page count unchanged.

## Validation
Focused: `OnboardingFlowTests`. Simulator: both sides at the largest Dynamic Type size, VoiceOver, light and dark.

Main app and tests only.

title: feat(onboarding): a setup prompt for a Hermes dashboard
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1182 (part of #706)

Stacked on #1184.

## What changed

Onboarding step 1 only offered the Hermes Web UI setup prompt, so people running a Hermes dashboard had no guided way to make it reachable and signed in from the phone.

Step 1 now opens on **Set up Hermes**. Its prompt has the agent take stock first, then set up basic auth with a hashed password, a persistent `dashboard.basic_auth.secret`, `dashboard.public_url`, and HTTPS through a Cloudflare Tunnel or a private network. It verifies with `curl --fail <exact-phone-address>/api/status` (never `--insecure`). "Using Hermes Web UI instead?" swaps in today's Web UI prompt, byte-identical; "Back to the Hermes setup" returns. Copies are tracked per prompt, so the copy reminder follows the prompt shown. The bottom bar's fade no longer catches taps, and step 1 pads past the fade, so both switch links stay readable and tappable. Five new strings in all 17 languages (`needs_review`); README and DEVELOPMENT.md cover Hermes host setup. Contract checked against the pinned hermes-agent (`HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`); no live host touched.

Decision: [Uzair, 2026-10-10](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1182#issuecomment-6104457176), build as written.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Link back from Web UI reads "Back to the Hermes setup" (alt: "Using Hermes instead?").
- Copies tracked per prompt; copying one doesn't satisfy the other's reminder (alt: one shared copied flag).
- Hermes reminder: "…so Hermes sign-in and HTTPS are configured correctly."; Web UI message unchanged (alt: one generic message).
- Same Wi-Fi only as a confirmed manual fallback that explains the unencrypted password (alt: an equal option).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/OnboardingFlowTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: 21 passed, 0 failed (12 + 9). On the final head: OnboardingFlowTests 12 passed, 0 failed.
- Red: against a stub API, 3 of 12 failed as intended (`Missing Hermes setup instruction…`; `("webUI") is not equal to ("hermes")`; copy reminder ignored the shown prompt). The first review fix's red run failed on the forced `curl --fail https://<`.
- Greptile repair: Continue Anyway bypasses the reminder only for the prompt shown. `testSkippingOnePromptsReminderStillRemindsForTheOther` red (one skip covered both), green; OnboardingFlowTests 13 passed, 0 failed on the top head.
- The fade fixes are visual and have no unit test: checked on the iPhone 18 Pro simulator, where the link swaps both ways and both links clear the fade at default and the largest text size. Screenshots are in a comment below.
- `git diff --check` clean; Web UI prompt byte-diffed identical to `master`.

## Design

Mock: https://yo2g0j141ar8.postplan.dev/v/1, pick **2C** (Hermes prompt first, Web UI one tap away).

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator
1. Open onboarding to step 1: it opens on "Set up Hermes" with "Using Hermes Web UI instead?" under the card.
2. Tap the link: "Set up Hermes Web UI" shows today's prompt; tap "Back to the Hermes setup" to return.
3. Tap Continue without copying: the alert mentions Hermes sign-in and HTTPS. Copy, swap to Web UI, tap Continue: the alert returns with the Tailscale message.

title: fix(push): finish pairing a fresh Hermes host and keep a shared host paired
body:
Fixes #1178

Stacked on #1195.

## What changed

**Problem.** On a fresh Hermes host, the pairing route answers 404 until the dashboard process restarts and mounts the newly installed plugin, so setup fails at "Pair this iPhone" with no way forward. Separately, when one host was saved as two entries (LAN + tunnel), removing or turning off one entry deleted the shared relay device and disabled the host plugin, so the other entry stopped getting pushes.

**Fix.**
- The app reads the body of a pairing 404 (hermes-agent ca678285). `Plugin not found` runs the full setup. An unmounted route (`No such API endpoint` or the headless catch-all) checks the plugins hub: if hermex-push is already on disk, setup stops at a new `setupNeedsRestart` card (the existing "Restart `hermes dashboard` … Check again" copy) and installs nothing; otherwise it runs the full setup. Any other 404 is reported as it is.
- Check again re-reads the pairing route and pairs, setting the relay first on a 409. It never installs anything or restarts the host.
- `PushRegistrar` skips the relay-device DELETE while another stored pairing on the same install key and relay still holds that exact device token (forget, disable, enable rollback, stale preference-write and launch-refresh cleanup). The Keychain item still goes; the last owner deletes as before. If the Keychain can't list the other entries, forget and refresh cleanup skip the DELETE and keep the APNs registration, and disable fails without changing anything.
- Turn off skips the host plugin disable while another entry shares the pairing, rechecking right before the request (after any sign-in). An unreadable Keychain stops Turn off before sign-in. A shared-host confirmation variant says so (17 translations, `needs_review`).
- A plugins-hub reply with no readable plugins list fails the Pair step instead of reinstalling.
- Every registrar device write runs on one queue (enable, forget, disable, refreshes, preference saves); removal waits for in-flight writes, then checks ownership against the tokens entries actually store. A server with no stored pairing and no enable in flight skips the queue.
- Integration repair (5bbf31e4): `PushActivityRegistrar`'s three replacement/retirement guards compare the relay route identity (relay URL, install key, device token, push session ID) instead of the configured server, so removing one shared entry no longer deletes the other entry's Live Activity route. Two new tests failed first.
- Settings → Interaction now shows the Notifications section on a Hermes server too; a stale "waits for #706" gate had hidden it, so push could not be turned on there (6b7eaf92).
- Removing or signing out of a Hermes server now forgets its push pairing too. Removal skipped it behind a stale #706 condition and sign-out never called it, so the host kept pushing to this iPhone. A relay device that another entry still holds is kept (cc2d3b4b).
- Docs: `bots.md` § Push provisioning (404 table, gateway vs dashboard restart, route ownership) and the shared-host caveat in `push.md`.

**Decisions made overnight** ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1178#issuecomment-6104456616))
- Check again uses a separate `setupNeedsRestart` case and installs nothing (alt: reuse `.restartNeeded` with a flag, or re-run the full enable).
- An on-disk but unmounted plugin does not write `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL`, so a self-hosted relay is never overwritten (alt: always write the default relay).
- A failed or list-less plugins-hub read fails the Pair step with the existing unexplained-404 copy; nothing is installed (alt: treat as not on disk, or a restart card / hub-specific message).
- Shared-host Turn off gets its own confirmation copy (alt: keep the original, which overstates what happens).
- A server whose own enable is queued takes the queued removal path, so removing it mid-enable can't leave an orphan pairing (alt: fast path on "no stored pairing" alone).
- The review limit was reached with a serious finding left (ownership changing during sign-in); it was fixed once more at 6148d96d without another review. The queue repair at f0d1ae57 was independently reviewed with no findings.

**Known limitation.** Removing an entry while its own enable still waits for notification permission or the device token is not covered; this predates this PR.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air> --only PushRegistrationTests --only HermexPushProvisioningTests --only HermesConnectionTests --only LocalizationCatalogTests`: 137 passed at 6148d96d and at f0d1ae57. `ci/check_string_catalog.py` covers every key.
- In-flight pairing (03957ad7): an entry mid-pairing counts as sharing the host, so the other's Turn off keeps the plugin on; `testAnEntryStillPairingSharesTheHostWithTheOneTurningOff` failed first. Push 129/129; top cedbbdb3 268/268.
- Red: the fresh-host, shared-forget, shared-disable, rollback, stale-cleanup, queue (`testRemovingASharedEntryWaitsForTheOtherEntrysRefresh`/`…Enable`, `testRemovingAnUnpairedEntryDoesNotWaitForAnotherServersRefresh`), Greptile-repair and integration-repair tests each failed before their fix. `testDisableChangesNothingWhenTheKeychainCantListTheOtherEntries` has no red run (the old seam couldn't throw).

title: fix(hermes): adopt a chain's tip draft when a root or middle link opens first
body:
Found in review of #1176 ([#1185](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1185)); deferred at the review limit.

## Problem

A legacy compression chain `root -> middle -> tip` can have an unsent draft saved under `tip` by the old Sessions-list behavior. #1185 keys a chain's draft by its lineage root and moves a draft saved under the *opened segment's* key. If the first opening after that change is a link naming `root` or `middle`, the tip draft is never adopted:

- `segmentDraftKey` comes only from the requested `engine.target` key (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift` ~266-268). For `root` it is nil, so adoption returns at once; for `middle` the guard reads only root and middle (`ChatViewModel.swift` ~2986-2988).
- `ChatView` hydrates the empty root key (~2896-2900); the tip draft stays inaccessible.
- If the user then writes a root draft, opening the tip later also skips adoption (root already has one), leaving two records for one conversation.
- `session.resume` updates `engine.storedKey` to the resolved tip but leaves `engine.target` unchanged (`HermesConversation.swift` ~370-374, 418-420), so no later adoption runs.
- `HermesChatTurnTests.testEverySegmentOfACompressionChainSharesOneDraft` opens tip first, which masks this.

## Suggested fix

When opening a non-tip segment, use a confirmed server/Profile-scoped chain tip (offline cache or the attach/resume result) to adopt its old draft before concluding the lineage draft is empty. Never overwrite an existing root draft. Add fresh-store tests that seed only `tip` and open `root` first and `middle` first, asserting the restored content and removal of the migrated tip record.

Severity: small (only drafts saved before #1185 on legacy chains, first opened via a root/middle link).

title: fix(push): keep APNs registered while a queued enable waits behind the last removal
body:
Found by Greptile on #1184 (https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1184#discussion_r4240140554) after that PR's bot-repair budget was spent.

**Problem.** `PushRegistrar.enable` captures the device token and then waits in the registration queue. If that wait is behind removing or turning off the *last* pairing, the removal's `unregisterIfUnpaired()` stops APNs and clears `currentToken`. The queued enable then saves its captured token without registering with APNs again. The new server looks paired, but the iPhone has stopped receiving remote notifications until the next launch refresh re-registers it.

**Reachable when:** you remove or turn off your only paired server while setting up push on another one.

**Suggested fix.** In `unregisterIfUnpaired()`, skip unregistering and keep `currentToken` while `enablesInFlight` is non-empty. Deterministic test: A is the last pairing; hold A's relay DELETE; start enable for B (it captures the token and queues); release; assert `unregisterCount == 0` and that B stores the token.

body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1179 · Fixes #1165 (absorbed) · Part of #706 · Stacked on #1188

## What changed

A Hermes session's Live Activity had no tap destination, pushed under the key it started with, and lost track after a legacy-compression key move or a relaunch. Now its attributes carry a `destinationURL` (the #1176 session link for the chat's root key and Profile), so a tap opens the session, and an archived Bot Chat row's activity reopens it by key (#1165). Pushes follow the stored key: `movePushSession` retires the old route and registers the moved key for sessions and bots alike, and every start or re-adoption reapplies the engine's current key. The moved key persists per server + activity identity in the main app's defaults, so a relaunch keeps updating. At cold launch a paired activity is adopted; an unpaired one on the signed-in Hermes server is checked once against `session.active_list`: listed and not idle stays running, otherwise it ends as complete. `docs/agents/bots.md` updated.

Decisions applied: [issue comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1179#issuecomment-6104456748).

**Decisions made overnight**
- An older `hermes:` activity without `destinationURL` still builds no route; the tap opens the app as it is (alt: drop the guard and send it down the webui route).
- Cold-launch check: a failed read keeps the activity, any status but `idle` counts as running, match on push key or identity root/key (alt: a failed read ends it).
- The tap link names the chat's root key, not the turn-start tip (alt: the tip).
- Moved keys live in main-app `UserDefaults.standard`, keyed by server + identity (alt: app-group defaults, or keying by `Activity.id`).

title: fix(hermes): remove saved push keys when a turn ends without an ActivityKit activity
body:
Found during independent review of #1190 (#1179); deferred at the review limit. Severity: small.

**Problem.** With Live Activities disabled in iOS, or when `Activity.request` fails, every Hermes session/bot turn still records its push key in `LiveActivityPushKeys` and nothing removes it when the turn ends.

**Evidence** (`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift` at 023bb4a1):
- Each turn records its key at 346-348 (`rememberPushKey()`), before the authorization guard at 359-361; the `Activity.request` catch at ~880-882 also leaves the record behind.
- On completion, `endActivity`'s nil-activity branch (985-989) only calls `resetIfStillCurrent`, which clears the in-memory identity (~1116-1124) without removing the saved key.
- Each turn has a new stream ID, so completed turns leave distinct entries. `prune` runs only in `settleActivitiesFromPreviousLaunch` (~621-624), so nothing bounds the growth during a long-lived process.
- `LiveActivityPushKeys.record` reads and rewrites the whole dictionary (~1416-1445), so an install with Live Activities off accumulates durable session records and progressively more main-actor work. This contradicts the record's intended cleanup-at-end lifecycle.

**Suggested fix.** Capture the ending push identity with the ending turn and remove its record when no ActivityKit activity was acquired, with lifecycle protection so a newer turn's record can't be removed. Also release records for failed or superseded creation that no surviving activity needs. Add a focused no-activity completion test on an isolated defaults suite: old entries disappear, a newer driven turn's entry survives.

title: AgentLiveActivityManager reads Activity.activities synchronously on the main actor
body:
Found while repairing a CI failure on #1192 (#1180). Pre-existing: `master` has the same read. Severity: small to medium (a UI hitch if it reproduces on device).

**Problem.** `AgentLiveActivityManager` is `@MainActor` and reads `Activity<AgentRunActivityAttributes>.activities` synchronously on the main actor at every stream start (`requestOrUpdateActivity`, `HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift` ~809 on #1192's head, ~617 on `master`) and on the end path. That ActivityKit read can block.

**Evidence** (simulator, instrumented local runs of `ChatViewModelSendTests`):
- The gap between "LA request begin" and "LA activities read" was about 2.55 s in 6 of 60 iterations (about 10% of stream starts); `startChat` itself returned in under 1 ms.
- That stall starved a 2 s expectation in `ChatViewModelSendTests.testQueueParkedDuringADrainedSendKeepsItsFilesInTheComposer` and failed CI run 38118628210 ("Drained send started" timeout). #1192 fixed the test side by defaulting the test's view model to `SpyChatLiveActivityManager`; production code is unchanged.
- Not yet measured on a physical device.

**Suggested fix.** Keep `Activity.activities` off the main actor: read it in a detached/nonisolated task and hop back with the result, or cache the activities the manager itself requested and refresh the cache from `Activity.activityUpdates` instead of re-reading at each stream start and end. Add a focused test that a stream start doesn't wait on the ActivityKit read (e.g. an injected activities source that blocks), and confirm on device with an Instruments hang trace.

title: fix(auth): 3-tier server URL recovery cascade + Keychain diagnostics
body:
## Problem

When the iOS Keychain purges the primary `server_url` entry (iOS storage pressure, backup/restore, iCloud Keychain sync reset), `AuthManager.restoreSavedServer()` falls straight to `.unconfigured` — presenting the full onboarding screen to a returning user. The user loses their configured server even though the multi-server `ServerRegistry` still holds the entry.

## Root Cause

`restoreSavedServer()` had a single recovery path: read `server_url` from the Keychain or give up. The `ServerRegistry` (also Keychain-backed, but a separate entry) was never consulted as a fallback, and there was no diagnostic logging to distinguish "key genuinely absent" from "Keychain API error."

## Fix

### 1. Three-tier recovery cascade in `AuthManager.restoreSavedServer()` (`AuthManager.swift`)

| Tier | Source | Outcome |
|------|--------|---------|
| 1 | `keychain.load(.serverURL)` | Primary path — fast, unchanged. |
| 2 | `serverRegistry.activeServer` | Fallback when tier 1 returns nil: recovers from the multi-server registry and **re-persists** the URL to the primary Keychain key so subsequent launches skip the fallback. |
| 3 | `KeychainStore.loadWithDiagnostics(.serverURL)` | When both sources are empty: distinguishes `.missing` (first launch / full sign-out) from `.error(Error)` (Keychain locked, ACL mismatch) and logs the exact reason. |

### 2. Diagnostic Keychain loading (`KeychainStore.swift`)

- Added `KeychainStore.LoadResult` enum (`.value(String)`, `.missing`, `.error(Error)`).
- Added `loadWithDiagnostics(_:)` method that returns full error detail instead of swallowing it.

### 3. Structured logging (`AuthManager.swift`)

- `os.Logger` instance with subsystem/category for `AuthManager`.
- `.notice` for successful restores and clean first-launch.
- `.warning` for registry fallback recovery and session expiry transitions.
- `.error` for Keychain read failures.
- `.debug` for ignored 401s on active Hermes servers.

## Test Coverage

**`RestoreServerFallbackTests.swift`** — 9 test cases:

| # | Test | Verifies |
|---|------|----------|
| 1 | `testRestoresServerFromKeychainWhenPresent` | Happy path: primary Keychain read works |
| 2 | `testFallsBackToRegistryWhenKeychainServerURLMissing` | **Core fix**: registry fallback prevents `.unconfigured` |
| 3 | `testRegistryFallbackRepersistsURLToKeychain` | Re-persistence to primary key after recovery |
| 4 | `testRegistryFallbackRespectsServerKind` | Server kind honoured through fallback |
| 5 | `testEntersUnconfiguredWhenBothKeychainAndRegistryEmpty` | Correct `.unconfigured` on genuine first launch |
| 6 | `testLoadWithDiagnosticsReturnsValueWhenPresent` | `LoadResult.value` path (macOS/iOS only) |
| 7 | `testLoadWithDiagnosticsReturnsMissingWhenAbsent` | `LoadResult.missing` path (macOS/iOS only) |
| 8 | `testMalformedKeychainURLFallsBackToRegistry` | Malformed URL treated as missing |
| 9 | `testSignOutClearsRegistryPreventingFalseRecovery` | Sign-out clears both sources, no false recovery |

Tests 6–7 are gated behind `#if canImport(Security)` (Keychain API required).

title: feat(hermes): share text and files into a new Hermes session
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1181
Stacked on #1192.

## What changed

On a Hermes server, a share switched to a webui server or asked the user to add one. Now it opens a new Hermes session on New Session's Profile with the shared text and files in the composer. Decision: [#1181 comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1181#issuecomment-6104457013).

`ContentView` hands its reserved share to the Hermes home. Once the Sessions list has read the host live, `SharedImportReservation.transfer` moves the whole share into that Profile's new-session draft. `ChatDraftStore.appendShare` makes durable file copies, commits text and files in one change and flushes to disk. Only then is the reservation consumed and `.new(profile:)` pushed. The share's item id is stored on the draft, so a retry or replay adds it once. A composer's attachment sync keeps records it never saw. The extension is unchanged, and so is the webui flow.

**Decisions made overnight**
- `reachWebuiServer` keeps its other callers but loses its "Add a WebUI server" alert. Those links now open nothing. *Alt:* keep an OK-only alert for them.
- On Hermes, each share opens as it arrives (`SharedImportGate`). Webui keeps its Open Next banner. *Alt:* add a Hermes Open Next banner (needs a mock).
- A later share appends to the draft's unsent text after a blank line, and its files go after the staged ones. *Alt:* replace the text as webui does, or use a single newline.
- A share with a file Hermes can't take now (type, unreadable, 8 files/50 MB counting what's already staged) fails as a whole and stays queued, with a `BotAttachmentFailure` toast. *Alt:* admit only the files it can take, or drop the rejected files.
- Composer sync merges records it never saw (`setAttachments(_:replacing:for:)`). *Alt:* close the covering chat and wait for its flush.
- Shipped at the review limit with three serious findings filed as follow-ups. *Alt:* hold for another review.

## Known issues (shipped at review limit)
- #1196: a share with a file Hermes can't take blocks every later share on a Hermes-only setup, with no way to discard it in the app.
- #1197: sharing the same content again, after editing the draft it went into, is skipped.
- #1198: typing in an open new-session composer while a share moves in overwrites the shared text. A guard now notices, takes the share back and leaves it queued instead of losing it; composer ownership is still open.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim` (iPhone 17e) on the rebased head, with `--only` for SharedDraftStoreTests, ChatDraftStoreTests, HermesSessionListTests, ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests, AppIntentNewChatTests, AppIntentNewChatInProfileTests and ChatViewModelSendTests: **413 passed, 0 failed**. - Review repair (b349359a): 4 new SharedDraftStoreTests (rollback saved before requeue, text typed over during the write, commit-time 8-file recheck, 25 MB per-file limit). Red on 56a1088b: 4/34 failed. Green: SharedDraftStoreTests **34/34**; ChatDraftStoreTests, HermesSessionListTests, ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests **95/95**.
- Integration repair (014e89f2): on Hermes, queued shares open one after another (webui still waits for Open Next); `testQueuedSharesOpenOneAfterAnotherOnlyOnAHermesHome` red (`XCTUnwrap`), SharedDraftStoreTests **35/35**.

## Manual test

1. On a Hermes-only setup, share a photo and a PDF to Hermex, then send. You get one session, and each file uploads once.
2. Share again and back out right away. Reopen New Session: the content is still staged.

5. Share two items in a row on a Hermes server: both land in the new-session draft, once each.

title: fix(hermes): give declined shares a recovery or discard path so they cannot block the inbox forever
body:
Found by the independent review of #1195 (#1181), which shipped at the review limit.

**Where:** `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:681` (at 56a1088b) · severity: serious

## Evidence
Failing input: on a Hermes-only configuration, share nine small valid PDFs into an empty draft, then share ordinary text. The unchanged extension/inbox accepts up to ten files (SharedDraftStore.swift:93 and ShareInputReader.swift:32). moveIntoDraft admits at most eight and throws on the ninth (HermesSessionListView.swift:699-711), so transfer declines the entire item. ContentView.releasePendingSharedImport releases it back to pending without changing its original createdAt (ContentView.swift:232-238; SharedDraftStore.swift:265-279). reserveNextPendingImport always chooses the oldest pending item (SharedDraftStore.swift:190,512-524), so each share URL, foreground or relaunch reserves those same nine PDFs and fails again; the later text never reaches a composer. One permanently unsupported file has the same effect. The Hermes home has no Open Next or inbox management UI, and this diff removes the only share Discard action. The bytes survive, but there is no in-app way to unblock sharing or remove the offending file on a Hermes-only setup.

## Suggested fix
Keep declined bytes recoverable while providing an explicit discard/edit or skip-and-review path that allows later shares to route. Do not automatically discard rejected files. Cover a permanently inadmissible oldest item followed by valid text and verify the user can recover or deliberately remove the first item and open the second.

title: fix(hermes): identify a transfer occurrence rather than permanently deduplicating its content hash
body:
Found by the independent review of #1195 (#1181), which shipped at the review limit.

**Where:** `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:697` (at 56a1088b) · severity: serious

## Evidence
Failing input: share text A plus notes.pdf, let the transfer consume the reservation, then remove notes.pdf and replace A with B without sending. Share the same original A and notes.pdf again. The inbox creates a fresh item after consumption, but itemID is SHA256 of text, filenames, types and bytes, excluding createdAt (SharedDraftStore.swift:371-379,626-637), so the new share has the old itemID. The retained nonempty draft still contains that ID: setContent and attachment removal do not clear sharedImportIDs. moveIntoDraft therefore skips all file preparation, and appendShare takes its existing-ID branch, merely flushes and returns (ChatDraftStore.swift:742,765-769). transfer consumes the fresh reservation, and the replacement composer restores B with no PDF. No copy or insertion was made for the newly requested share. The added reservation test helper assigns random UUID itemIDs, hiding this production identity reuse.

## Suggested fix
Persist an occurrence identity stable across retries of one queued item but distinct when identical content is enqueued again after consumption; the payload createdAt together with itemID can distinguish these without changing the extension format. Add a real-inbox test with two identical saves separated by consumption and a user edit/removal, asserting that the second share stages its text and file.

title: fix(hermes): protect shared text from the outgoing composer before acknowledging the transfer
body:
Found by the independent review of #1195 (#1181), which shipped at the review limit.

**Where:** `HermesMobile/Persistence/ChatDraftStore.swift:783` (at 56a1088b) · severity: serious

## Evidence
Failing interleaving: a new-session composer for this server/connection/Profile contains A; share text B into it, suspend appendShare persistence after the merge, and type another character in the still-visible old composer. openPendingShare leaves covers.chat unchanged until transfer returns (HermesSessionListView.swift:570-575). ChatView.persistDraftEdit writes the old local composer text A! through setContent (ChatView.swift:2872-2878; ChatDraftStore.swift:681-685), replacing the merged A plus B while retaining the share marker. When the flush resumes, appendShare checks only that marker and attachment IDs; for a text-only share the ID subset is empty, so the check succeeds even though B is gone. transfer consumes B, the replacement chat restores A!, and the scheduled persistence overwrites the earlier disk snapshot. A share containing files also loses its text while its files pass the check. This violates the binding staged-share preservation decision. The fix report acknowledges the text overwrite window, but the post-flush ownership check does not cover it.

## Suggested fix
Coordinate the outgoing composer ownership or reconcile its text edits with the newly appended share before consumption. A changed text snapshot must not count as successful ownership solely because the marker survived. Add a deterministic suspended-persistence test that applies the old composer text edit, resumes the transfer and verifies both the edit and shared text remain recoverable before acknowledgement.

title: fix(hermes): approval cards stop arriving after the approval SSE stream drops (dropped connection never reported to the consumer)
body:
## Summary

In a Hermes (hermes-webui) chat, approval cards stop arriving after the first turn in which the long-lived `/api/approval/stream` connection silently drops. Clarify prompts keep working; approvals never show again until the app is fully closed and reopened. The app is in the foreground and unlocked the whole time — this is not a backgrounding issue.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect to a hermes-webui server over a VPN such as Tailscale (any path where the socket can be reset works; a server restart also does it).
2. Send a turn. `GET /api/approval/stream?session_id=…` opens (visible in the server log).
3. Break that socket without changing the device's network path: toggle Tailscale off and on, or restart the server.
4. Send a turn that needs approval (e.g. a `write_file` to `AGENTS.md`, which the write guard gates).

**Expected:** an approval card.
**Actual:** no card. The server log shows turn 2 opening `chat/stream` and `clarify/stream` only — no `approval/stream` and no `/api/approval/pending` polling. Closing and reopening the app restores approvals (`ChatView.onDisappear` clears the monitor state).

## Root cause

`SSEClient` configures LDSwiftEventSource with

```swift
config.connectionErrorHandler = { _ in .shutdown }
```

so consumers own reconnection. But in `LDSwiftEventSource.dispatchError`, `handler.onError` is **only called when the action is not `.shutdown`**:

```swift
func dispatchError(error: Error) -> ConnectionErrorAction {
    let action: ConnectionErrorAction = config.connectionErrorHandler(error)
    if action != .shutdown {
        config.handler.onError(error: error)
    }
    return action
}
```

`SSEEventHandler.onError` is what emits `.transportError`. With `.shutdown`, a dropped socket produces `onClosed()` (a no-op in `SSEEventHandler`) and nothing else. `ChatPendingActionCoordinator` still has `approvalMonitoringSessionID` set, so `startApprovalMonitoring` on every later turn returns early (the stream is "already attached"), and `startApprovalFallbackPolling` — wired to `.transportError` — never runs. The coordinator's fallback design is correct; the signal that triggers it was unreachable.

The same path serves the chat and clarify streams, so an abruptly dropped chat stream also never reached `handleTransportError` directly (the stale-stream loop and network-path handling covered it later).

## Environment

- Hermex 1.9 (master `d9444f3`), iPad mini (A17 Pro), iPadOS 26
- hermes-webui on a Mac reached through Tailscale (`tailscale serve`)

I have a fix with tests and an on-device verification; PR to follow.

title: fix(networking): report a dropped SSE connection to the stream's consumer
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1205

## What changed

`SSEClient` tells LDSwiftEventSource to `.shutdown` on any connection error so the consumers (chat stream resume, approval/clarify fallback polling) own reconnection. The library, however, skips `handler.onError` whenever the handler answers `.shutdown` (`LDSwiftEventSource.dispatchError`). Since `onError` is the only producer of `.transportError`, a dropped socket was silent: the approval coordinator kept believing its long-lived `/api/approval/stream` was attached, declined to reopen it on later turns, and never engaged `startApprovalFallbackPolling`. Approval cards stopped arriving until the app was closed and reopened.

The fix calls `handler.onError(error:)` from the connection-error handler before returning `.shutdown`, which is exactly what the library would have done for any other action. Intentional `stop()` is unaffected: the library already excludes `NSURLErrorCancelled` and guards on `readyState == .shutdown`, so no error is reported for a stop or after a restart. A clean server close (no error) still takes the library's own reconnect path as before.

Consumers of `.transportError` are unchanged and were designed for this signal: `ChatPendingActionCoordinator` falls back to polling for approvals and clarifications; `ChatStreamCoordinator.handleTransportError` saves a snapshot and enters the single-flight reconnect.

Possible follow-up (not in this PR): after a drop, approval monitoring stays on the poller for the life of the chat rather than retrying SSE.

## How it was tested

- New `SSEClientTests.testSSEClientReportsTransportErrorWhenAnOpenStreamDrops`, driving the real `SSEClient` through the existing `DelayedSSEURLProtocol` fixture. The fixture gained `keepOpen` (leave the response open after its chunks) and `failActiveConnection(with:)` (complete the task with an error, which is how URLSession reports a reset socket). The test waits for the stream to be open (heartbeat), drops it with `URLError(.networkConnectionLost)`, and waits for `.transportError`. No sleeps; each step is gated on the previous expectation.
  - Without the fix (`master`'s `SSEClient.swift`): `0 passed, 1 failed — unfulfilled expectations: "dropped connection reported as transportError"`.
  - With the fix, `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SSEClientTests`: 5 consecutive runs, `34 passed, 0 failed` each.
- Intentional `stop()` cannot trigger the new path: the library skips `dispatchError` for `NSURLErrorCancelled` and returns early once `readyState == .shutdown` (`LDSwiftEventSource.swift`, `didCompleteWithError`). The full suite below, which stops streams constantly, agrees.
- The next link in the chain is already covered and unchanged: `ChatViewModelSendTests.testApprovalFallbackFindsLateApprovalAfterEmptyIdleProbe` feeds the approval stream a `.transportError` and asserts fallback polling finds the late approval.
- Full suite via `xcodebuild test` on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.0): **4034 passed, 0 failed**.
- On device (iPad mini, signed Debug build of this fix, hermes-webui over Tailscale): turn 1 opened `approval/stream`; toggling Tailscale off/on killed the socket; the server log then shows `GET /api/approval/pending` polling from the device every ~1.5 s, and the next turn's approval card (a write-guarded `write_file` to `AGENTS.md`) appeared. Before the fix the same sequence produced no polling and no card. A plain Wi-Fi toggle does *not* reproduce the drop under Tailscale (the socket is bound to the `utun` interface and survives), which is part of why the issue looks intermittent.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies

title: Server-initiated turns (background-job notifications, cron) never appear while the app is idle — Hermex does not subscribe to /api/session/stream
body:
## Summary

A turn that the **server** starts in a session — a `terminal(background=true, notify=true)` process finishing and injecting its notification, a cron job, another client — never appears in Hermex while the app is idle on that session. The reply exists in the session journal; the app shows it only after the user sends their next message (which fetches the session) or leaves and re-enters the chat.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a Hermes WebUI session opened in Hermex, ask the agent to run something in the background with completion notification, e.g. "run `sleep 60; echo done` in the background and tell me when it finishes" (Hermes uses `terminal(background=true, notify=true)`).
2. Leave the app open and idle on that chat.
3. When the process ends, hermes-webui injects the completion notice and runs an agent turn on its own.

**Expected:** the new assistant turn streams into the open chat, as it does in the browser WebUI.
**Actual:** nothing. Send any message and the missed turn appears above it.

Server log for one instance (session `4fa5…`): the background run finished at 18:40Z and the server-initiated turn ran 18:40:27–18:41:08 (run `4533e491…`, 120 tokens, 2 tool calls). The phone made **no requests at all** between 18:38:50 and 18:47:13; at 18:47:13 the user's next `POST /api/chat/start` fetched the session and the turn showed up.

## Why

hermes-webui has a persistent per-session SSE channel built for exactly this: `GET /api/session/stream?session_id=…&known_count=N` (added in WebUI v0.51.340, `_handle_session_sse_stream` in `api/routes.py`). It emits

- `server_turn_started` `{session_id, stream_id, source}` — a turn began that this client did not start; the browser attaches to `stream_id` and watches it live;
- `session-updated` `{session_id, message_count}` — on (re)subscribe, when the server's persisted message count is ahead of the client's `known_count` (a turn started *and finished* while the client was disconnected); the browser reloads the session;
- `bg_task_complete`, plus an `initial` frame and 30 s keepalive comments; on subscribe the server also hands over the active `stream_id` if a turn is already mid-flight.

The browser WebUI subscribes at session mount (`static/messages.js`, `session/stream`). Hermex opens `chat/stream` for its own turns and `approval/stream` / `clarify/stream` for prompts, and knows `/api/session/status` (`Endpoints.swift`), but never opens `/api/session/stream`. While idle it has no way to learn that the session changed.

## Proposed fix

A session-channel coordinator next to the approval/clarify ones, using the existing `SSEClient`:

1. Subscribe to `/api/session/stream` (with `known_count`) while a chat is on screen and no turn of its own is streaming; close on leave.
2. `server_turn_started` → attach to the given `stream_id` through the existing stream-resume path.
3. `session-updated` with `message_count` above the local count → reload the session.
4. `.transportError` → fall back to polling `/api/session/status` until the SSE reconnects (same pattern as approval fallback polling; depends on #1205 so a dropped socket is actually reported).
5. A Settings toggle (on by default) so the behaviour can be disabled.

I have this working locally and will open a PR once it is verified on device.

## Environment

Hermex 1.9 (master `d9444f3`), iPad mini (A17 Pro), iPadOS 26; hermes-webui `fd0141fa` (exp-v0.52.458) over Tailscale.

title: fix(hermes): add a share again when the same content is shared after it was consumed
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1197

## What changed

Sharing the same text and files into a Hermes session a second time could silently do nothing. The share inbox names each item by a hash of its content, so the second share got the first one's id. If the draft still remembered that id (the user had edited it but not sent), the new share was skipped and then consumed.

A Hermes draft now remembers each share by its **occurrence**: the content id plus the `createdAt` time the extension already writes (`SharedImportReservation.occurrenceID`). That stays the same across retries, releases and relaunch replays of one queued item, so those still add nothing. It changes when the same content is shared again after it was consumed, so that share gets added. The extension's file format is unchanged. This code hasn't shipped yet (#1195), so drafts on disk need no migration.

## How it was tested

- New `SharedDraftStoreTests.testTheSameContentSharedAgainAfterConsumptionIsAddedAgain` uses a real inbox: share text and a PDF, consume it, edit the text and remove the file, share the same thing again. It checks the second share adds its text and file. With the old `itemID` key it fails as the issue reports: the text and the PDF are both missing.
- The relaunch-replay test now also checks that the occurrence id is unchanged on replay.

title: feat(chat): keep an idle chat in step with turns it did not start
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1208

Stacked on #1206 (the branch includes that commit): the fallback poller depends on `SSEClient` reporting a dropped socket as `.transportError`.

## What changed

A turn the server starts on its own — a `terminal(background=true, notify=true)` process finishing, a cron job, another client — never appeared while Hermex sat idle on the session; it showed up only after the next send. Hermex opened `chat/stream` for its own turns and never subscribed to the webui's persistent per-session channel, `GET /api/session/stream?session_id&known_count` (hermes-webui ≥ v0.51.340), which emits `server_turn_started` and `session-updated` for exactly this case.

- **`ChatSessionChannelCoordinator`** (new) mirrors `ChatPendingActionCoordinator`: one `SSEClient` on the channel while the chat is on screen and idle. The view model opens it after each successful `loadMessages`, closes it when a turn of its own starts (`streamCoordinatorStartAuxiliaryMonitoring`, where `chat/stream` carries everything), reopens it when the turn ends (`streamCoordinatorDidFinishStream`), and closes it on leave (`cleanupPollingTasks`).
- **Reaction = reload.** `server_turn_started`, and a `session-updated` whose `message_count` is above the transcript, ask the view model to reload. `loadMessages` already reads the session's `active_stream_id` and `reconcileSessionLoad` attaches to it exactly as a chat that opens mid-turn does — so the server-started turn streams live, and a turn that started *and* finished during a gap is pulled in. One reload at a time; a burst coalesces.
- **Fallback.** A channel that was open and then drops (`.transportError`) polls `/api/session/status` (which now decodes `message_count`) and reloads on a new `active_stream_id` or a higher count, until the chat streams a turn of its own or leaves. A channel that never opened (older server without the endpoint, or a proxy rejecting the path) is left alone — no polling against servers that don't have it.
- **Setting.** Settings → Interaction → **Live Session Updates**, on by default; off restores today's behaviour. Forwarded to the open chat like the Live Activity toggle.
- `SSEEvent` gains `serverTurnStarted` / `sessionUpdated` (explicit `CodingKeys` — the decoder is not snake-case); the chat, approval and clarify handlers ignore them.

## How it was tested

- `ChatSessionChannelCoordinatorTests` (17 tests, scripted SSE client + `MockURLProtocol`): opens with `known_count`, not while streaming, idempotent start, stop, preference off/on; `server_turn_started` reloads; `session-updated` reloads only when ahead; other-session and post-stop events ignored; bursts coalesce; dropped channel polls and reloads on a new stream / higher count; polling ends when a turn of its own starts; a channel that never opened does not poll; wire-name decoding incl. empty body; `SessionStatusResponse.message_count` incl. older servers. 3 consecutive runs, 17/17 each.
- `ChatViewModelSendTests.makeViewModel` injects a spy for the new stream client (it was hitting the strict mock's unexpected-path check).
- Full suite via `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests`: **4170 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped**.
- On device (iPad mini, Debug build, hermes-webui over Tailscale): asked the agent to run `sleep 45; echo done` in the background with completion notify. Server log shows the device open `GET /api/session/stream?session_id=…&known_count=1498`; when the job finished and the server started its own turn, the device fetched the session and attached to that turn's `chat/stream` (`463c7a0c…`) with no user input — the reply streamed into the idle chat. Before the fix the same sequence produced no requests until the next send (log excerpt in #1208).

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above

title: fix(hermes): let a share Hermes can't take be discarded so it stops blocking later shares
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1196
Was stacked on #1209, now merged; rebased onto master.

## What changed

On a Hermes server, a share Hermes can't take (nine files, an unsupported type, a file over the limit) failed with a toast and went back to the queue. The queue always offers the oldest share next, so it failed again on every later share, foreground and relaunch, and nothing behind it could open. Nothing in the app could remove it.

Now that failure shows an alert, "Couldn’t Add Shared Files", with the reason and one button, **Discard Share**. Decision: option D from the [owner-approved mock](https://6751loh7c2jq.postplan.dev/v/2), with the owner's copy. While the alert is up, the share stays claimed, so no other share opens. Discard lets it go through the existing consume path. That deletes only that share, and the next queued share opens. If the list goes away before the user taps Discard (a server switch, a Shortcut's chat), the share is released and comes back next time. There is no Keep and no partial import.

`transfer(into:route:decline:)` loses `decline`: a failure now just rethrows and the caller decides. #1209's `transfer(…decline:)` call is updated here too.

**Copy gaps (accepted for now)**
- The 8-file / 50 MB check also counts files already waiting in the New Session draft. If the draft has 7 files and the user shares 2, the alert says to share fewer files, but the real fix is to send or remove the waiting ones. Behavior is unchanged.
- Approved copy covers the limit and unsupported-file reasons. Unreadable files and save failures use the v2 mock strings ("One of the files couldn’t be read." / "Hermex couldn’t save the files on this iPhone."). A save failure on a text-only share (rare) still says "files".

## How it was tested

- New `SharedDraftStoreTests`, using a real inbox with an unsupported file shared first and text after it:
  - `testDiscardingAShareHermesCantTakeOpensTheNextOne`: nothing else opens while the failed share is held; Discard deletes it, the text share opens in the draft, and the inbox ends empty.
  - `testAFailedShareTheUserDidNotDiscardStaysQueued`: released instead, it comes back with its file.
- Existing `transfer` tests drop `decline`. The #1198 quit-replay test now models the quit with an expired reservation instead of a release.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air> --only SharedDraftStoreTests --only HermesSessionListTests --only ChatDraftStoreTests --only LocalizationCatalogTests`: **124 passed, 0 failed**. `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all keys covered. 7 new keys, 17 languages, `needs_review`.
- Owner test, run on the iPhone Air sim against a Hermes server through the real share extension: unsupported file, Discard opens the next share, nine PDFs, Cancel keeps it, relaunch brings it back. All pass; screenshots are in [this comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1211#issuecomment-6113703780). iOS adds a Cancel button next to Discard Share; Cancel keeps the share queued.
