- **Record.** Each Hermes entry now has `ServerAccount.movedWebuiServers`. A record holds the source webui server's id, the Profile mapping chosen at Review (a Hermes Profile or Keep on webui), when the move finished, and the last-known remaining/unchecked/oversized counts. A missing count means unknown, never zero. Decoding is tolerant: an unreadable record or mapping, including one naming both choices, is dropped on its own, so that Profile counts as unmapped instead of guessed.
- **Commit.** `AuthManager.commitMove` (new `AuthManager+MoveToHermes.swift`) writes the destination and its record in one save through `ServerRegistry.commit`, which waits for the Keychain to confirm. If the save fails, nothing is published in memory and a new destination's sign-in is put back.
  - An existing Hermes server is adopted. Its sign-in, name, colour, headers and pairing stay as they are.
  - A new one takes the source's name, initials and colour. Webui custom headers are never copied.
  - One record per webui server across all servers. The commit refuses the same address (that's the existing replacement flow, #1027) and an address a webui server holds, comparing hosts case-insensitively.
  - The commit never switches the active server; #1218 switches when the user taps Done.
- **Older copies can't wipe records.** `ServerRegistry.update` keeps the stored records, so an identity edit made from a stale copy of an entry can't drop them.
- **Removal.** The record lives inside the destination's entry. It survives removing the source and signing out of the destination, and goes when the destination is removed. The removal paths needed no code change.
- **Pairing.** `MovePushPairing.carry` is #1216's first step after the user confirms Move.
  - It reads the destination host's pairing only when the source is paired and the destination isn't.
  - It copies the source's pairing (token and preferences) only when the host reports the same install.
  - The copy runs in `PushRegistrar`'s existing queue, with no relay call, and checks again that the destination is still configured.
  - A cross-host move copies nothing.
- **Docs.** New row in `multi-server-state-isolation.md`.

No new endpoint or data shape: the pairing read is the existing `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing`.

## How it was tested

Simulator: iPhone 17e (`1D3BFD51…`), branch `issue/1215-move-commit`.

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/MoveToHermesCommitTests`: 13 passed. Covers a failed save with nothing published and the sign-in put back, a new destination versus an adopted one, tolerant decoding, one record per source and repeat commits, an identity edit from an old copy, removing the source, signing out and removing the destination, acknowledged record updates, same-install copy with zero relay calls, cross-host copying nothing, an existing pairing preserved without a read, an unreadable host, and a destination removed before the copy ran.
- Related suites `ServerRegistryTests`, `AuthManagerStateTests`, `PushRegistrationTests`, `HermexPushProvisioningTests` and the new file: 223 passed.
- Full suite locally, because `project.pbxproj` changed: 4168 passed, 1 failed, 2 skipped. The failure is `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests.testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesWhileTheKeyboardIsUp` (keyboard never appears), which fails the same way on `master` on this device: filed as #1219.

title: feat(hermes): scan and import chats for Move to Hermes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1213 · Parent #707 (slice 1/6). No UI yet: the runner (#1216) and the guided sheet (#1218) call this.

## What changed

Move to Hermes needs to know which webui chats Hermes already has and copy only the missing ones, without duplicating, trimming or misplacing any. This adds that engine.

- **Scan** (`MoveToHermesScan`): one `GET /api/sessions?all_profiles=1&include_archived=1` on the webui, which never switches Profiles. Then it pages every Hermes Profile with the per-Profile `/api/sessions` (`archived=include`, no source filter) until the host's `total`, because every page re-sends its pinned rows. Any id no listing showed gets an exact `GET /api/sessions/{id}` in every Profile. The host falls back to a prefix match, so a row under another id counts as absent. 404 means absent; errors, timeouts and cancellation mean unknown; two matches mean ambiguous. At most four requests per server.
- **Copy** (`WebuiSessionTransfer`): for each source Profile, switch Profiles in a private cookie jar that has the source server's own cookies and headers, so the app's shared jar never sees the switched cookie. Then export, convert, recheck by exact id, record through `willDispatch`, and import once. The conversion keeps content as exported (images included), uses webui's own counter mapping (`state_sync.py`) and `created_at`, and sends no title, folder, pin or parent.
- **Limits and errors:** batches stay under 500 sessions, 50,000 messages and 25 MB. A chat over 10,000 messages or 5 MB is reported, never trimmed. A 400 drops the chats it names and a 413 halves the batch; both wrote nothing. Anything else is `.uncertain`, for the runner to replay, since the host skips ids it already has.
- **Transport** (approved): `sessionScanPage`, and `HermesSessionRefusal.entries`, so a 400 keeps every named session, not just the first.

title: feat(hermes): reconcile moved chats and transfer their drafts
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1214 · Parent #707 (slice 2/6). No UI yet: the runner (#1216) calls this.

## What changed

The import from #1213 leaves out titles, pins and folders, and unsent drafts stay on the webui. This adds `MoveToHermesReconcile`, which fills those without overwriting anything set in Hermes:

- **Plan** reads each chat's Hermes row once. Every operation records that value as `from`, plus the value it writes (`to`), so the journal keeps the starting values.
- **Apply** reads the row again before every write. Still at `from` → `willDispatch`, then the write. Already at `to` → applied. Anything else → left alone and reported changed.
- **Settle** handles a write whose reply was lost, or one the journal still shows in flight: applied when Hermes holds `to`, otherwise reported uncertain and never resent. A field back at `from` still counts as uncertain.
- **What gets filled:**
  - Titles and folders only where Hermes has none. Folders go through `session.workspace.move`; 4017 is reported as a missing folder.
  - Pins only on chats this Move copied. Chats Hermes already had keep their pin and archive state, and the import already carries archive.
  - Hidden rows get nothing, including rows hidden after planning.
- **Title collision:** one retry as `Title (6789ab)`, shortened to fit the host's 100-character cap. A second collision is reported.
- **Drafts:** `ChatDraftStore.transferDraft` copies the draft, confirms it's saved, then removes the source. A destination holding a different draft is a conflict, and both stay untouched. A failed save rolls back and keeps both.
- **Draft key:** a draft moves only when the row has no parent, so the Sessions list keys it by that id. A row with a parent could be a compression continuation or a branch, so its draft stays on the webui and is reported. Draft moves read the row again first, so a session deleted, hidden or continued since planning keeps its draft too.
- **Scope:** the first move reconciles copied chats and chats Hermes already had. Copy Missing Chats Again reconciles only the chats it copied.

Known limits, documented in the code: a pin or unpin made between the read and the write still loses to the write, and a flag flipped and flipped back looks unchanged. The host keeps no per-field version.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17e> --only MoveToHermesReconcileTests`: 18 passed. Covers starting values, edits made after planning, the landed-write-then-user-edit resume case, collision retry and cap, 4017, lost replies, draft identity, conflict, and both save failures.
- `ChatDraftStoreTests`, `SharedDraftStoreTests`, `MoveToHermesTransferTests`: 105 passed.
- Full suite (project file changed): 4,203 run, 1 failure: `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests.testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesWhileTheKeyboardIsUp`. It fails the same way on master on this simulator and is already tracked as #1219.
- Live, on the 0.21.5 host's `dev` Profile with two disposable imported sessions: rows return flags as `0`/`1` with null `cwd` and `parent_session_id`, a duplicate title returns 400 "already in use", and the pin landed. Both sessions were deleted and confirmed 404. No real session was touched.

title: feat(hermes): route legacy entry points after Move to Hermes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1217 · Part of #707 (slice 5/6).

## What changed

After a webui server moves to Hermes, its old links, pushes, alerts and Shortcuts must find the moved chat or Profile without guessing a server. Before this, they ignored the move record, and most stopped working once the webui entry was removed.

The webui server's move record lives on its Hermes destination (#1220). `MovedWebuiRoute` (in `ContentView.swift`) routes by it:

- **Webui links** (`webui-push`, `session?server=<webui>`) open on the destination with no Profile, so the lookup finds where the session actually is, not where Review mapped it. Only a clean "no Profile has it" falls back to the webui server, if it's still configured. A failed read never counts as absence, and the fallback link (`onSource=1`) can't redirect again.
- **Run-origin entry points** (webui pushes, local run alerts, Live Activity taps) stay on the webui server while it's configured, so a run still executing there keeps its live stream and approval card. Once that server is removed, they go to the destination.
- **Pushes after a same-host webui server is removed** open on the one paired Hermes server holding a record. Two such servers open nothing. A cross-host move's old install is paired with nothing once removed. Local alerts match the record's server hash.
- **Bare `session?id=` links and webui "New Chat in Profile" Shortcuts** open only where every candidate agrees, unmoved webui servers included. The active server never breaks the tie. Shortcuts follow Review's mapping; a "Keep on webui" on a removed server still counts as a claim. Saved Shortcuts keep resolving while a record names their Profile.
- With no move records, every route is unchanged. A refusal opens nothing, as today. No new UI or copy.

Small seams: `HermesSessionDestination.movedFrom` (`HermesDeepLink.swift`, also compiled by the widget; default nil), the Hermes list's "not found" fallback, and one line in `PushAppDelegate`. No project file or target membership changes. `docs/agents/push.md` gains a "Moved webui servers" section.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` on iPhone 17e (`1D3BFD51…`), branch `issue/1217-legacy-routing`:
- `MovedWebuiLinkTests` (new), `HermesSessionLinkTests`, `HermesSessionLookupTests`, `PushPreviewTests`, `AppIntentNewChatInProfileTests`, `MoveToHermesCommitTests`, `BotDeepLinkTests`: 129 passed.
- `LiveActivityTests`, on iPhone Air (`D5388D52…`) because another session took the 17e: 55 passed.

New tests cover: the actual Profile differs from the mapping, a failed read isn't absence, fallback without a loop, source kept/removed, destination signed out or removed, run-origin links staying on their source, bare-link and Shortcut ambiguity (including an active holder), same-install and cross-host pushes, and local alerts.

No live-server calls: the change adds no endpoint or shape and reuses the existing lookup. Moved routes need a real move record, which only #1218's UI creates. Physical-phone push/link/Shortcut checks after a real removal still need their own grant (#707).

title: feat(hermes): resume interrupted Move to Hermes work safely
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1216 · Parent #707 (slice 4/6). There's no UI yet: the guided sheet (#1218) owns the runner.

## What changed

A Move to Hermes can be stopped partway: the sheet closes, the app quits, the network drops, or a save fails. Resuming it must not re-send a change whose result is unknown, and must not claim more than it can confirm. This adds that runner.

- **Journal** (`MoveToHermesJournal`): one folder per move, named by a hash of both server ids (no address), using the drafts' file protection.
  - `plan.json` freezes Review (Profile mapping, Hermes Profiles, scan) before the commit.
  - `log.jsonl` is append-only. Each import, plan and metadata write is flushed to disk before it is sent, and a failed append sends nothing.
  - A torn last line is cut off. If it was an outcome, the complete intent before it stays in flight: an import is sent again, a metadata write is only checked by reading.
  - A damaged line (doesn't decode, breaks the numbering, or names a chat or Profile outside the plan) stops all work until a fresh scan. An unreadable or newer-format journal is kept and never acted on.
- **Runner** (`MoveToHermesRunner`): writes the journal, then runs `commitMove`. Cancelling or failing before the commit leaves nothing. Each pass then runs:
  - the pairing carry (only after the commit), the copy, reconcile and drafts;
  - imports re-sent to the same frozen Profile under the same id; metadata writes never re-sent, only settled.
  - A pass with work left pauses for Resume. `finishEarly` (mock A) ends it and sends nothing.
  - The final report is on disk before the move record is marked complete, and stays until Done.
- **Being in Hermes vs. copied:** only an import reply naming a chat counts as a copy.
  - A chat found after a send with no reply is reported as "present, copy unconfirmed".
  - On the first move it's treated like a chat Hermes already had: empty title and folder filled, draft moved, never pinned. Copy Missing Chats Again only reports it.
  - Documented limit: replaying an unconfirmed import recreates a chat the user deleted in Hermes during the pause.
- **Removal:** `AuthManager.removeServer` marks the destination as being removed before its first await, and deletes its journals after its entry is gone. `MoveToHermesPending.all` deletes journals no record owns.
  - The runner treats a destination as gone from the start of its removal. `MoveToHermesReconcile.moveDrafts` gained a `canTransfer` check just before each transfer, because removal discards the destination's drafts before its entry goes.
- **Docs:** a new row in `multi-server-state-isolation.md`.

`MoveToHermesRunner.swift` is 677 lines, over the size warning. The report and progress fold could move out later.

## How it was tested

Simulator iPhone 17e (`1D3BFD51…`), branch `issue/1216-move-resume`.

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only MoveToHermesRunnerTests`: 17 passed. Covers each stop point, a write that landed before its outcome was saved (then edited in Hermes), torn complete-intent vs unfinished-intent lines, a damaged line, a newer-format journal, a missing journal, orphans, a failed `finished` append and a failed Keychain save, Finish early, a draft conflict, Copy Missing Chats Again with the record's mapping, and destination removal.
- Review round 1 added tests for a lost copy outcome, a missing log, a suffixed title retry, and a draft read while the destination is being removed. `MoveToHermesRunnerTests`: 21 passed; with Reconcile, Commit and `AuthManagerStateTests`: 100 passed.
- Mutation checks: each of the four checks below makes its test fail when removed: the unconfirmed-send flag, the attempt id, torn-tail truncation, and `canTransfer`.
- Related: Runner, Commit, Reconcile, Transfer, `AuthManagerStateTests`, `ServerRegistryTests`, `ChatDraftStoreTests`: 196 passed.
- Full suite (the project file changed): 4,219 passed, 1 failed, 2 skipped. The failure is `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests.testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesWhileTheKeyboardIsUp`, the known iPhone 17e failure, #1219.
- No live calls: there's no new endpoint or shape, and the pairing read can create host keys. The Desktop multi-connection gate, the end-to-end local webui/Hermes check and the phone check stay open and need their own permission.

title: fix(voice): stop the fallback test depending on the simulator's speech service
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1163

## What changed

`testServerFirstFallsBackOnDeviceAfterTheHostRefuses` failed on CI (on master and on #1225) with `STT is disabled` and 0 authorizations. It still made three live Speech framework calls: `SFSpeechRecognizer.supportedLocales()`, `SFSpeechRecognizer(locale:)`, and `supportsOnDeviceRecognition`. On a fresh CI simulator one of them came back empty, so the controller found no on-device recognizer and skipped the fallback.

The fix adds a small test seam with production defaults unchanged:

- `ComposerSpeechRecognizing`, a two-member protocol (`supportsOnDeviceRecognition`, `recognitionTask(with:resultHandler:)`) that `SFSpeechRecognizer` conforms to. The factory and the cached recognizer use it.
- A `supportedLocales` init parameter that defaults to `SFSpeechRecognizer.supportedLocales()`.
- The test injects the current locale and a stub recognizer that reports an on-device model. Recognition never starts, because the test denies authorization first.

The test isn't skipped, and its timeouts aren't changed.

Head `61326f8` incorporates upstream `master` at `bbaeef1` (2.2 preparation, HTML workspace/report preview #1714 and the date-test correction #1715). Both the initial merge conflicts and the subsequent test conflict are resolved without rewriting history. The fork's default branch follows upstream. A targeted Mac walkthrough found missing chat constraints and over-wide task rows after the merge. The Catalyst follow-up restores bottom-docked chat/error layouts, readable pushed session/Kanban pages and the connection-sheet size, and centers the task agenda in an 800-point column. The daily 2.2 app was replaced and opened successfully; the owner must sign in again because the new team's Keychain group differs. The old app/config are backed up and old containers remain intact. This local provisioning does not resolve the official maintainer-team Mac App ID prerequisite.

title: fix(i18n): count chats, not folders, in the missing-folder report line
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1226

## What changed

The move report's missing-folder line counted affected chats but called them folders, and its detail was always plural. With one chat it read "1 folder not on this host / Those chats open without a folder." When several chats shared one missing folder, it overcounted folders. `foldersMissing` holds one folder change per chat (`MoveToHermesReconcile.plan` emits at most one `.folder` op per chat), so the number is chats.

title: fix(hermes): open Files collapsed and save files before the first message
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1138

## What changed

When a new Hermes chat starts in the home folder, Files opened every top-level folder at once. The host lists folders one at a time, and macOS-protected folders (Desktop, Documents, …) each block for 6–11 s, so every folder hit the 15 s timeout and the host stayed busy for about 30 s. Separately, Save to Files and Quick Look failed in a chat that hadn't sent its first message yet, because the download named a session the host hadn't stored.

- **Folders open collapsed on Hermes.** `WorkspaceFileClient.opensTopLevelFolders` is false for Hermes, so Files lists only the chat's folder and lists each subfolder when it's tapped. webui keeps opening its top-level folders.
- **Downloads by host path.** A workspace file's download sends `cwd + "/" + path` with the Profile and no `session_id`, the same way list and read-text already send it. The host only resolves `session_id` to find a folder, and it 404s that until the session is stored. MEDIA paths keep the `session_id` because the host resolves them against the session. Download queries now keep a literal `+` (`%2B`), as list and read-text already do.
- **Line count.** A file ending in a newline no longer counts an extra line. CRLF is handled too, and an empty file has 0 lines.
- `docs/agents/bots.md` describes the new behavior.

The four Git nits from the issue moved to #1232.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17 Pro Max> --only` FileBrowserViewModelTests, HermesWorkspaceFileClientTests, FileTreeTests, BotArtifactTests, HermesChatAttachmentTests, APIClientGitTests, HermesConnectionTests, BotClientTests, HermesRequestTests and TranscriptMediaPreviewViewModelTests: PASS.

New and updated tests cover: a Hermes tree opening collapsed and listing a folder on tap, file downloads without `session_id` while MEDIA downloads keep it, `+` encoding, and line counts.

**Owner check:** on a Hermes host, start a new chat in the home folder, open Files (it should open at once, with folders closed), tap a folder, then Save to Files on a file before sending any message.

title: fix(hermes): reattach when the host reclaims an idle session
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1122

## What changed

When the host reaps an idle chat's runtime, it broadcasts `session.reclaimed`. Hermex ignored it, so the chat only noticed when the next send failed with 4001 and had to be sent again.

The host sends this event without a top-level `session_id`, with the ids in its payload: `{type: "session.reclaimed", session_id: "", payload: {session_id, stored_session_id, reason}}` (`tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py` `_announce_session_reclaimed` → `server.py` `_event_frame`, pin `ca678285`). The per-runtime filter dropped it.

`HermesConversation`, the engine behind every Hermes chat (Bot Chat included), now admits the event when its payload names this chat's runtime or stored key. It hands it to the owner as lost frames, so the chat runs its existing gap recovery: one reattach that only reads, then a rebuild from the snapshot. A live turn ends the way any lost stream does. Nothing is resent. The host never announces a close the client asked for, or a resume that supersedes a runtime, so this can't loop.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConversationTests`: 77 passed, 0 failed.

New `HermesChatTurnTests` cases:
- a matching runtime gets one read-only reattach, and the next send goes out on the new runtime
- a match on the stored key alone reattaches
- another session's reclaim changes nothing
- a reclaim mid-turn settles the turn with no spinner left

Owner check: none needed. Reaping an idle runtime takes the host's idle timeout, and the scripted gateway covers the paths.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)

title: feat(hermes): companion capabilities route that gates plugin features
body:
**What the user gets:** Nothing new on screen by itself. Hermex learns which companion routes a host has actually loaded, so Fetch, Pull and New branch (#1236) and provider limits (#1237) show only where they work. A plugin that is installed but not yet loaded gets "Restart Hermes to finish" instead of "refused (HTTP 404)".
**Why it matters:** Uzair approved route 10.1 for 2.0 ([approval](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/710#issuecomment-6153869162)). A dashboard mounts plugin routes only at startup, and a POST route can't be probed without running it, so the app needs one read with no side effects that lists what is loaded.
**Cost:** Small. Two PRs: one in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, one here. Simulator and fixtures; no phone needed.

Part of #710 (slice 10.1) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** none · **Unblocks:** #1236, #1237

## Problem and outcome

- The app reads the loaded plugin version only from `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/pairing` (`BotDashboardClient.swift:82-86`). That route answers 409 when `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL` is unset and creates the pairing keys on first read (hermex-push `plugin/dashboard/plugin_api.py` docstring). A host that uses the plugin only for git must not need push set up.
- `loadedPluginVersion()` goes through `send()` (`BotDashboardClient.swift:84, 102-107`), so its 404 skips `HermexPushPlugin.missingRoute` (`HermexPushPairing.swift:51-61`). Settings → Notifications' passive check, "Check again" and the post-restart reads then end in `.checkFailed` with "This Hermes host refused the step (HTTP 404)…" (`HermexPushProvisioner.swift:543-552, 753`), not the restart card.

After this: the plugin answers `GET …/capabilities`; the app has one read and a route gate that #1236 and #1237 use; a not-mounted plugin on the version read shows "Restart Hermes to finish".

## Contract

- **New plugin route:** `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/capabilities` → `{"plugin_version": "0.5.0", "routes": ["GET /capabilities", "GET /pairing", "POST /restart", …]}`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. No side effects, never 409. `routes` is built from the plugin's own `router.routes` (method plus path relative to the mount), so it cannot drift from what is mounted.
- **Missing-route bodies** (pin `ca678285`): an unmatched `/api/*` GET answers 404 `{"detail":"No such API endpoint: /…"}` (`hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py:219-223`); the plugin off answers `{"detail":"Plugin not found"}`; headless answers `{"error":"Headless backend …"}` (`docs/agents/bots.md:2465-2470`).
- A mounted 0.4.0 plugin also answers "No such API endpoint" for `/capabilities`, through the same catch-all. A 404 alone can't tell "old plugin" from "not loaded"; the hub's on-disk version already does (`HermexPushPairing.swift:41-49`, `pluginStanding` at `HermexPushProvisioner.swift:572-579`).

## Plan

hermex-push PR:
- [ ] `plugin/dashboard/plugin_api.py`: `GET /capabilities`.
- [ ] Bump to 0.5.0 in the four places `test_plugin.py` checks (`plugin/README.md:161-163`).
- [ ] `hermex_push_tests/test_plugin.py`: the route returns the version and a list holding itself, `GET /pairing` and `POST /restart`. Reading it creates no keys in plugin-data.
- [ ] `plugin/README.md`: document the route.

hermex PR:
- [ ] `HermesREST.swift` (cases `:110-114`, URLs `:341-343`): a `.pluginCapabilities` case beside `.pushPairing`.
- [ ] `HermexPushPairing.swift`: a tolerant `HermexCompanionRoutes` (`plugin_version`, `routes` as a set; unknown fields ignored) with `supports(_:)`. Bump `newestVersion` to 0.5.0 (`:20`).
- [ ] `BotDashboardClient`: `companionRoutes()`. A 200 decodes; any 404 is an empty set (gate closed); other failures throw.
- [ ] `loadedPluginVersion()` classifies a 404 the way `pairing()` does (`BotDashboardClient.swift:72-80`), so `.notMounted` with the plugin on disk lands on `.setupNeedsRestart` (`HermexPushProvisioner.swift:613-633`).
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md` § Push provisioning (the capabilities route; the version read's 404 handling); one line in `docs/agents/push.md`.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-13): route 10.1 ships in 2.0; routes ship in at most two plugin batches.

Recommended (taken unless Uzair says otherwise at approval):
- **Gate on the route list, not the version number.** POST routes can't be probed safely, and a version number says nothing about a route added on a branch.
- **Keep the existing hub comparison** for "installed but not loaded" vs "old plugin" (`pluginStanding`). Bare `GET /api/dashboard/plugins` lists only plugins activated for the dashboard frontend and is a public path (`web_routers/dashboard_ui.py:131-146`, `dashboard_auth/public_paths.py:23`), so it adds nothing over the hub.
- **A closed gate is silent where the feature lives.** Git and Usage just don't show the feature; the restart nudge lives only in Settings → Notifications, which already owns plugin standing.
- **No cache.** Each consumer reads `companionRoutes()` when its screen loads, through that server's own `HermesConnection`. One small GET per screen, and nothing can leak across servers.
- **Plugin batch 1 is 0.5.0** with this route and #1236's git routes. #1237 rides 0.5.0 if it merges in the same walk, else it is batch 2 (0.6.0).
- **Grant:** this issue's lane may push a branch and open one ready PR in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`. Merging it, installing it on any host and restarting any host stay with Uzair. Land the hermex-push PR first; the app PR is safe in either order, since a missing route only closes the gate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Plugin: `GET …/capabilities` returns the version and the route list; the version check in `test_plugin.py` passes at 0.5.0.
- [ ] App: a 200 marks every listed route supported; a 404 with any body closes the gate; unknown fields are ignored.
- [ ] Settings → Notifications: a host whose hub lists 0.5.0 on disk while the version read 404s "No such API endpoint" shows "Restart Hermes to finish", not the HTTP 404 failure.
- [ ] A host with 0.4.0 loaded is offered the update.

## Tests

- `HermexPushProvisioningTests` with `PushHTTPFixture` (`HermexPushProvisioningTests.swift:1607, 1680-1700`): capabilities decode; 404 → empty; the not-mounted version read → restart card. Update the existing update/restart tests for 0.5.0.
- Plugin: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest plugin -q` in hermex-push (`plugin/README.md:152-159`).

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests`, plus the plugin suite above. A live check waits for Uzair to release and install 0.5.0 (owner step on #710).

## Mocks, outside reach, surfaces

- **Mocks:** none. No new UI or copy; this reuses the existing restart card.
- **Outside reach:** the hermex-push PR (granted above). No live-host writes.
- **Surfaces:** main app only (Settings → Notifications, plus the gate for chat Git and Usage). Not the share extension, Live Activity widget, notification service, deep links or App Intents.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #710 intake.

title: feat(hermes): Fetch, Pull and New branch in Hermes chats through the companion plugin
body:
**What the user gets:** In a Hermes chat inside a git repository, the Git menu gains Fetch and Pull (fast-forward only), and the branch picker gains "New branch…", the same controls as on webui. They appear only when the host's Hermex plugin has these routes loaded.
**Why it matters:** Uzair approved route 10.2 for 2.0 ([approval](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/710#issuecomment-6153869162)). Hermes has no fetch, pull or branch-create route (`hermes_cli/web_routers/git.py` ends at `branch/switch`, `:207`), so a Hermes chat can push but never pull.
**Cost:** Medium. Two PRs: one in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, one here. Simulator and fixtures; no phone needed.

Part of #710 (slice 10.2) and #703 (slice 3.4) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1235 (route gate) · **Unblocks:** none

## Problem and outcome

- On Hermes, `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel.supportsSync` is `session.sessionId != nil` (`GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:125-127`). It hides Fetch and Pull (`GitWriteAvailability.hidesSync` `:527-536`; the menu's Update section, `GitActionsMenuButton.swift:76-88`) and turns off New branch (`allowsCreate`, `ChatComposerView.swift:1203-1221`).
- `remoteCall` sends fetch and pull only through webui's `apiClient` (`GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:283-294`). `HermesGitClient.checkout` refuses `newBranch` (`HermesGitClient.swift:383-385`).

After this: when #1235's gate lists the three routes, a Hermes chat shows webui's Fetch, Pull and New branch, backed by the plugin. Stash-and-switch stays dropped (#1116).

## Contract (to build; host pin `ca678285`)

Plugin routes under `/api/plugins/hermex-push/`, behind dashboard auth:
- `POST /git/fetch {path, remote?}` → `git fetch --prune --no-recurse-submodules [remote]`.
- `POST /git/pull {path, remote?}` → `git pull --ff-only --no-recurse-submodules [remote]`.
- `POST /git/branch {path, name, start?}` → `git switch -c <name> [start]`. Create and switch, matching the existing "Create the branch from the current HEAD and switch to it." copy (`GitBranchPickerView.swift:139-152`).
- Success: 200 `{ok: true, message}`. Failure: 400 `{detail}`, as the core git routes answer (`_git_op`, `web_routers/git.py:35-41`). That way `HermesGitClient`'s refusal mapping (`HermesGitClient.swift:491-502`) applies unchanged and git's stderr never reaches the UI.
- **Reuse the host's hardening in-process:**
  - The path goes through `hermes_cli.web_server_files._fs_path` (`:24`), as core's `_git_path` does (`web_routers/git.py:44-45`).
  - Git runs through `hermes_cli.web_git._git(cwd, args, timeout=60)` (`web_git.py:43`), which applies `harden_git_argv` and `noninteractive_git_env` (`_subprocess_compat.py:53, 321`).
  - `name` goes through `_sanitize_branch` (`web_git.py:531`), as `branch_switch` does (`:676-681`). `remote` and `start` are refused when they start with `-`.
  - Each route runs off the event loop (`asyncio.to_thread`).
- Each route appears in `/capabilities` automatically (#1235 builds the list from the router).
- Reference arguments: webui's `git_fetch`/`git_pull` (`.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/workspace_git.py:1684, 1702`).

## Plan

hermex-push PR:
- [ ] The three routes in `plugin/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, or in a sibling module its router includes.
- [ ] Tests in `hermex_push_tests/`, against a temp repo with a local bare remote:
  - fetch updates the remote ref;
  - pull fast-forwards;
  - pull on diverged history answers 400 and makes no merge commit;
  - branch creates and switches;
  - an option-like `remote`, `start` or `name` is refused.

  Host-helper cases skip where hermes-agent isn't importable, like `test_restart_needs_the_dashboard_sign_in`.
- [ ] `plugin/README.md`: document the routes.

hermex PR:
- [ ] `HermesREST.swift`: three cases beside `.pushPairing` (`:110-114`, `:341-343`).
- [ ] `HermesGitClient`: `fetch()`, `pull()`, `createBranch(name:)`, each through `beginWrite()` and `writableRoot()` (`:452, 461`) and `write(…, deadline: .provisioning)` as push does (`:315-320`). `checkout` with `newBranch` calls `createBranch` instead of refusing; validate the name with `HermesREST.isBranchName` first.
- [ ] `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel`: read `companionRoutes()` (#1235) when the panel loads. On Hermes, `supportsSync` is true when all three routes are listed. Route fetch and pull through `git` in `remoteCall`. Stash-and-switch stays off on Hermes even when `supportsSync` is true.
- [ ] Refetch status after each action, and branches after New branch, as push does.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md:1482, 1531` ("Fetch and Pull are webui-only…") describes the plugin routes and their gate.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-13): route 10.2 ships in 2.0; stash-and-checkout stays dropped (#1116).

Recommended (taken unless Uzair says otherwise at approval):
- **Always fast-forward only; no `ff_only` flag.** The plan sketched `{path, remote?, ff_only}`. A non-ff pull would need a merge commit that nobody can edit from a phone, so the flag would only ever be `true`.
- **New branch on a dirty tree is allowed.** `git switch -c` from HEAD carries uncommitted changes onto the new branch, which is the usual reason to make one. #1116's "Commit or discard first" stays for switching to an existing branch.
- **One gate for all three.** They ship in one plugin release, so per-route flags add states nobody sees.
- **Fetch also takes the write guard**, like push. It changes refs, and one rule is simpler than a carve-out.
- **Same copy as webui:** Pull's confirmation "Pull Remote Changes?" / "Pull uses fast-forward only and will not create a merge commit." (`ChatView.swift:1630-1640`) and the existing toasts. No new strings.
- **Plugin batch 1 (0.5.0)** with #1235; no extra version bump when both merge in the same walk.
- **Grant:** this issue's lane may push a branch and open one ready PR in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`. Merging it, installing it on any host and restarting any host stay with Uzair. Land the hermex-push PR first; the app PR is safe in either order.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Gate open: Fetch, Pull and New branch show on a Hermes chat. Pull asks first; each action refetches status; New branch switches the branch label.
- [ ] Gate closed (no plugin, old plugin, not loaded): the controls stay hidden, exactly as today.
- [ ] A diverged pull, an auth failure or a timeout shows the existing "Git Action Failed" alert with the generic refusal copy, never git's stderr or a host path.
- [ ] No git write runs during a turn (the existing `beginWrite()` guard). webui's Fetch, Pull and New branch are unchanged.

## Tests

- `APIClientGitTests` with `HermesGitHost` (`APIClientGitTests.swift:990-1056`): the three requests' paths and bodies, 200 and 400 replies.
- `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`: `supportsSync` follows the gate; fetch and pull route through `git`; New branch on a dirty tree; stash stays off.
- Plugin: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest plugin -q` in hermex-push.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`, plus the plugin suite. Simulator pass: open a Hermes chat with the gate stubbed open and closed, and check that the menu and picker match the acceptance criteria. A live check waits for Uzair to release and install 0.5.0 (owner step on #710), on a throwaway repo.

## Mocks, outside reach, surfaces

- **Mocks:** none. The controls, copy and layout are webui's existing ones.
- **Outside reach:** the hermex-push PR (granted above). No live-host writes.
- **Surfaces:** iPhone and iPad chat (Git menu, composer branch picker). Not the share extension, Live Activity widget, notification service, deep links or App Intents. Multi-server: the gate and the requests go through the chat's own server connection.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #710 intake.

title: feat(hermes): provider limits in Hermes Usage through the companion plugin
body:
**What the user gets:** Usage on a Hermes server shows the provider limits card webui already shows (Codex and Claude plan windows, an OpenRouter key's quota) for the selected Profile. It appears only when the host's Hermex plugin has the route loaded.
**Why it matters:** Uzair approved route 10.3 for 2.0 ([approval](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/710#issuecomment-6153869162)). Hermes has no structured quota route, and `session.usage.account_lines` is text that needs a live session (#705), so Usage on Hermes hides Limits today (`HermesInsightsClient.swift:34-44`).
**Cost:** Medium. Two PRs: one in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`, one here. Simulator and fixtures; no phone needed.

Part of #710 (slice 10.3) and #705 (provider quota) in epic #713 · **Blocked by:** #1235 (route gate) · **Unblocks:** none

## Problem and outcome

`HermesInsightsClient.providers()` returns no providers, and `providerQuota` throws `.unsupported` (`HermesInsightsClient.swift:34-44`), so `InsightsViewModel.loadLimits` never shows a card (`InsightsViewModel.swift:246`, `showsLimits` `:371`). After this, when #1235's gate lists `GET /provider-quota`, the same `ProviderLimitsSection` fills on Hermes from a plugin route that speaks webui's envelope. The view model and card code don't change.

## Contract (to build; host pin `ca678285`)

- `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/provider-quota?provider=&profile=&refresh=`, behind dashboard auth. An omitted `provider` means the Profile's configured `model.provider`.
- **Body:** webui's `/api/provider/quota` envelope, so `ProviderQuotaResponse` (`APIClient+ProviderQuota.swift:15-70`) decodes it unchanged.
  - Envelope keys: `ok, provider, display_name, supported, status (available|unavailable|no_key|invalid_key|unsupported), quota, message`, plus `label` and `account_limits` when present (`.codex-tmp/hermes-webui/api/providers.py:2090-2122, 2133-2246`).
  - `account_limits` is serialized as `_serialize_account_usage_snapshot` does (`:1557-1598`): `provider, source, title, plan, windows[{label, used_percent, remaining_percent, reset_at, detail}], details, available, unavailable_reason, fetched_at`.
- **Source:** `agent.account_usage.fetch_account_usage(provider, base_url=None, api_key=None)` (`agent/account_usage.py:675-689`), which fails open to `None`.
  - Built-in fetchers: `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, `openrouter` (`:648-651`). Any other provider goes to its provider plugin's hook, bounded at 10 s (`:658`).
  - The calls are synchronous httpx with timeouts up to 15 s, so the route runs them in a thread.
- **Profile scope:** run inside `config_scoped_to_thread(profile, fn)` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/_common.py:50-57`), so config and secrets come from that Profile, as the gateway's `_account_usage_lines` does (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:1283-1294`).
  - The fetchers resolve their own credential when `api_key` is None; OpenRouter's does it through `resolve_runtime_provider` (`account_usage.py:611-614`).
  - Verify that Codex and Anthropic do the same inside the scope, and record the result in the PR.
- **Status:**
  - A snapshot with `available` → `available`.
  - A snapshot with `unavailable_reason`, or `None` for a provider with a fetcher or hook → `unavailable`, with a short `message`.
  - No fetcher or hook → `unsupported`.
  - `no_key` and `invalid_key` only where the fetcher can tell them apart.
- **Cache:** 45 s keyed by `(profile, provider)`, at most 64 entries. `refresh=1` skips the read. A `None` never replaces a good entry (webui `providers.py:1983-2030`).

## Plan

hermex-push PR:
- [ ] The route in `plugin/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, or in a sibling module its router includes.
- [ ] Tests with `fetch_account_usage` and the scope helper monkeypatched:
  - the envelope for each status;
  - a cache hit, and `refresh` bypassing it;
  - a `None` keeping a cached good entry;
  - the Profile passed to the scope;
  - an omitted provider resolving to the configured one.

  Host-helper cases skip where hermes-agent isn't importable, like `test_restart_needs_the_dashboard_sign_in`.
- [ ] `plugin/README.md`: document the route.

hermex PR:
- [ ] `HermesREST.swift`: a `.companionProviderQuota(provider:profile:refresh:)` case beside `.pushPairing` (`:110-114`, `:341-343`).
- [ ] `HermesInsightsClient.providers()`:
  - Gate open: read `model.options` for the Profile (`.profileModelOptions`, as `HermesCronClient.swift:91-95` does). Map it to `ProvidersResponse`: `activeProvider` is the payload's `provider`, and every authenticated provider has `hasKey: true` (`HermesModelCatalog.swift:13-36`).
  - Gate closed: no providers, as today.
- [ ] `HermesInsightsClient.providerQuota(provider:refresh:)`: the plugin route with the client's `profile`, deadline `.provisioning` (a Codex read can retry after a 401).
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md:1608` ("The host has no … provider limits (#710)"); the doc comment at `HermesInsightsClient.swift:8-9`.

## Decisions

Decided (Uzair, 2026-10-13): route 10.3 ships in 2.0, through the companion route, in webui's envelope.

Recommended (taken unless Uzair says otherwise at approval):
- **Use webui's provider selection unchanged:** the active provider first, then any authenticated one of `openai-codex`, `anthropic` and `openrouter` (`providerQuotaSelection`, `InsightsModels.swift:472-477`). The card code stays shared.
- **No OpenRouter credits object.** The agent's OpenRouter snapshot gives a window only for a key with a spending limit, which shows as "API key quota". A key with no limit gets no card on Hermes, while webui shows its credit balance. Rebuilding webui's separate credits call in the plugin duplicates provider code for a minor case. Leave `quota` null.
- **Plugin release:** rides 0.5.0 if it merges in the same walk as #1235 and #1236; otherwise it is batch 2 (0.6.0, which bumps `newestVersion` too).
- **Grant:** this issue's lane may push a branch and open one ready PR in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push`. Merging it, installing it on any host and restarting any host stay with Uzair. The app PR is safe in either order.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Gate open with a Codex or Anthropic Profile: Usage shows that provider's card with its windows and reset times, as on webui. Pull-to-refresh sends `refresh=1`.
- [ ] With another Profile selected, Usage shows that Profile's provider and limits.
- [ ] Gate closed, or every probe unavailable: no Limits group and no error, as today.
- [ ] webui servers are unchanged.

## Tests

- `HermesInsightsClientTests`: replace `testLimitsAndTheSessionsFallbackAskTheHostNothing` (`:171`) with two tests.
  - Gate open: the providers come from `model.options`, and the quota request carries the provider, the Profile and `refresh`.
  - Gate closed: no quota or `model.options` requests.
- A fixture in webui's envelope, reusing `APIClientProviderQuotaTests`' live-captured `available` payloads, decodes into a card.
- Plugin: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest plugin -q` in hermex-push.

## Validation

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesInsightsClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/ProviderLimitCardTests --only HermesMobileTests/InsightsViewModelTests`, plus the plugin suite. A live check waits for Uzair to release and install the plugin (owner step on #710).

## Mocks, outside reach, surfaces

- **Mocks:** none. This is the existing `ProviderLimitsSection` card and copy.
- **Outside reach:** the hermex-push PR (granted above). No live-host writes.
- **Surfaces:** main app Usage screen (iPhone and iPad). Not the share extension, Live Activity widget, notification service, deep links or App Intents. Multi-server: each request goes through that server's connection and names the screen's Profile; nothing is cached on the phone.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during #710 intake.

title: feat(hermes): companion capabilities route that gates plugin features
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1235. Plugin side: uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#25, which merges first.

## What changed

Hermex couldn't tell which hermex-push routes a host has loaded, so Git (#1236) and provider limits (#1237) had nothing safe to gate on. Separately, if a paired host had the plugin on disk but its dashboard hadn't loaded it, Settings → Notifications showed "refused the step (HTTP 404)" instead of the restart card.

- `HermesREST.pluginCapabilities` → `GET /api/plugins/hermex-push/capabilities` (plugin 0.5.0).
- `HermexCompanionRoutes` decodes `{plugin_version, routes}` tolerantly. `supports("POST /…")` is the gate, and `.closed` supports nothing.
- `BotDashboardClient.companionRoutes()`: a 200 decodes, any 404 is `.closed`, and other statuses throw. There's no cache: each screen reads through its own server's connection.
- `loadedPluginVersion()` now classifies 404s the same way `pairing()` does (one shared `readPluginRoute`). `pluginStanding` treats "not mounted" as nothing loaded, so if the newest version is on disk the card says "Restart Hermes to finish", and an older version on disk is still offered the update.
- `newestVersion` is now 0.5.0, which is why the plugin PR has to merge first.
- Docs: `bots.md` § Push provisioning and one line in `push.md`.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17 Pro Max> --only HermesMobileTests/HermexPushProvisioningTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesRequestTests`: **68 passed** on the rebased head.

title: chore(hermes): make Hermes the default and label webui servers legacy
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #712

## What changed

Adding a Hermes server stopped at a "Turn on Bot Mode (beta)" opt-in, and Move to Hermes only showed up with Bot Mode on. Nothing marked a webui server as legacy.

- A found Hermes dashboard goes straight to its username and password fields, in onboarding and in Settings → Add Server. `AuthManager.addHermesServer`, `replaceWebuiServer` and `commitMove` no longer check `BotModeGate`.
- Settings → Servers shows a gray **Legacy** pill on every webui server that hasn't moved (VoiceOver: "legacy webui server"). Moved servers keep their orange Moved pill.

title: fix(hermes): open a share while a chat covers the Sessions list
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1212

## What changed

Sharing a file from Files while a Hermes new-session chat was open did nothing until the user went back to Sessions. Sharing sends Hermex to the background, which closes the Sessions list's host connection. When the app comes back, a list with a chat on top doesn't reconnect, and a share opens only once the list has read the host. So the share waited.

title: fix(hermes): a share over a share-opened chat leaves the new chat half-loaded
body:
**What the user gets:** every chat a share opens finishes loading, however many shares arrive in a row.
**Why it matters:** after #1212 (PR #1240) a share opens straight into the composer. But a second share, made over the chat the first share opened, opens a chat that never finishes loading. Backing out and opening New Session again recovers it.
**Cost:** unknown until diagnosis; somewhere in how two back-to-back chats share the Hermes host connection.

## Repro (iPhone Air simulator, iOS 27, PR #1240 head 273f9a09, live Hermes host over Cloudflare)
1. On a Hermes server, open New Session.
2. In Files, share a file to Hermex. Hermex returns and the file is in the composer; the chat loads normally.
3. Without leaving that chat, share another file from Files.
4. **Observed:** the new chat holds every shared file, but stays half-loaded for over a minute:
   - the header subtitle falls back to the Profile ("Default") instead of the workspace;
   - the workspace chip and Files button are blank;
   - the model control says "Reasoning" instead of the saved effort ("Low").

   Nothing is sent. Back → New Session loads normally, with the draft intact.

Reproduced 3 of 3 for a share over a share-opened chat. A share over a chat opened by hand loaded normally 3 of 3, and so did a manual New Session after a share-opened chat.

## Evidence
- Log (`HermesConnection`): `c1 socket s21: reply for call 93 matched no open call` and `Hermes session reattached after 0 retries: frames held 1, applied 0, dropped 1`. One `NSURLErrorDomain -1001` timeout about 30 s after a stuck chat opened. The host answered normally throughout.
- Screenshots of the working steps: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1240#issuecomment-6158712965

## Scope
Not a verified root cause. The trigger is #1240's close-and-reopen as the app returns to the foreground: the share-opened chat closes and a new chat with the same draft opens while the shared socket reconnects after `closeForBackground`. Check what the closing share-opened chat does on that socket (reattach, call cancellation) versus a chat opened by hand. Keep #1197 occurrence identity, #1198 text preservation and #1212's prompt opening intact.

title: feat(hermes): Fetch, Pull and New branch in Hermes chats through the companion plugin
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1236. Plugin side: uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#26, which merges first.

## What changed

A Hermes chat's Git menu could push but never fetch or pull, and its branch picker had no "New branch…". The host's own git routes stop at `branch/switch`, so hermex-push 0.6.0 adds the three routes. The app shows the controls only while the plugin lists those routes.

- `HermesREST`: `gitFetch`, `gitPull` and `gitCreateBranch` → `POST /api/plugins/hermex-push/git/{fetch,pull,branch}` with `{path}` (and `name`). A name the host's sanitizer would rewrite is refused before the request goes out (`isBranchName`).
- `GitDataClient` gains `supportsSync()`, `fetch()` and `pull()`. webui syncs as before through its session routes. `HermesGitClient.supportsSync()` reads the #1235 gate on the chat's own connection and needs all three routes listed. Each write takes `beginWrite()` and the lock, like push, and then reads the status again. git's `message` and its 400 `detail` never reach the screen.
- A `checkout` with `newBranch` now creates the branch from HEAD instead of refusing. That works on a dirty tree too, carrying the changes along. Switching to an existing branch still refuses uncommitted changes, and there is still no stash.
- `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel` reads `supportsSync` alongside each load, and all three remote actions go through `git`. It no longer holds the session or webui client, so its designated init is `init(git:)` (most of the test diff is that rename).
- The push confirmation now picks Hermes vs. webui wording by `git.isHermes` instead of `supportsSync`.
- `HermexPushPlugin.newestVersion` → 0.6.0, so hosts on 0.5.0 are offered the update.
- Docs: `bots.md` § Workspace on a Hermes host and one line in `push.md`.

title: fix(hermes): Listen reaches the host while a chat reconnects
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1072 (the last slice; #1082 was the first).

## What changed

On Uzair's iPhone, Listen in a Hermes chat kept using the iOS voice against the real host. There were two causes:

- **Host (fixed there, not in this PR):** the host's edge-tts 7.2.7 got a 403 from Microsoft's speech service, so every `/api/audio/speak` call returned 400 and Hermex fell back to on-device speech, as designed. edge-tts 7.3.1 (released 2026-10-13) fixes it. After the upgrade and a dashboard restart, `POST /api/audio/speak?profile=default` returns 200 with `audio/mpeg` from `edge`.
- **App (this PR):** `BotClient.speech` threw `.stale` without sending whenever the chat's consumer wasn't attached to the gateway socket, for example while the chat reconnects. Speak is plain HTTP and doesn't need the socket. The guard is gone. `HermesConnection.authorized` still refuses a retired connection, and the attempt check still stops the send if the screen closes or reconnects during sign-in. `ChatViewModel` already drops a late result by request ID (#15).

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check` is clean.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro> --only` ListenSynthesisTests, HermesSpeakTests, APIClientTTSTests on the rebased head: 11 passed.
- New: `testAHermesReplyPlaysInTheHostsVoiceWhileTheChatReconnects` drops the chat's socket, then taps Listen; one speak request goes out and the host's audio plays. On the old guard it fails: 0 requests, spoken on device.
- Host contract re-checked through the tunnel with curl (default Profile): 200, `{ok, data_url, mime_type: "audio/mpeg", provider: "edge"}`.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (2.0 RC pass)
1. Open a Hermes chat on the default Profile and tap Listen on a short reply. Expected: the host's Edge voice, not the iOS voice.
2. Background the app for a few seconds, return, and tap Listen at once. Expected: the host's voice.

title: feat(hermes): keep a browser sign-in's tokens and send its bearer
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #708: slice 8.2, with 8.4 folded in, per the [go comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/708#issuecomment-6160580151). Slice 8.3 (the browser sheet itself) is a stacked PR and closes the issue.

## What changed

A host that only offers browser (OIDC) sign-in issues an access token and a refresh token that rotates on every use. Hermex had nowhere to keep them and no way to send them. This PR builds that half. Nothing can obtain the tokens until 8.3, so password hosts behave exactly as before.

- `BotConnection.oauth` (provider, user id, refresh token) lives in the existing Keychain record, so sign-out, removal and Move handle it with the record.
- On sign-in, a browser connection posts the refresh token to `/auth/native/refresh`. It saves the rotated token **before** using the new access token, then checks `/api/auth/me` (same provider and user). The access token stays in memory and goes out as `Authorization: Bearer` on every signed-in request. The socket upgrades still present a ticket.
- A signed-in 401 drops the bearer, refreshes once and resends, the same path a password sign-in already uses. A 401 from the refresh itself is the new `.signInExpired`, which signs the active server out to its form with "Your Hermes sign-in expired. Sign in again."
- A new connection reads the refresh token from the Keychain, not from a possibly stale copy of the record. A rotated token is written only while the record is still that connection holding the sent token, so a removed server or a newer sign-in is never overwritten.
- 8.4: the header policy refuses any custom `Authorization` on a browser connection. Cloudflare Access users get pointed at the two-header form. `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` covers this, plus the fact that the browser leg can't carry Connection Headers.
- Cut per the go comment: no proactive 5-minute refresh, and no App Intents single-flight.

New copy (catalog entries added with all 17 translations, `needs_review`):
- "Your Hermes sign-in expired. Sign in again."
- "This server signs in through the browser, so Hermex sends its own Authorization header. Remove this header to connect. For Cloudflare Access, use the CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers instead."

Contract: read at the pin `ca678285` (`dashboard_auth/routes.py` `auth_native_refresh`, `_bearer_payload`, `middleware.py` bearer path), and the token, bearer and ticket legs were exercised on a phone in the 8.1 spike.

title: feat(hermes): sign in to a browser-only Hermes host
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #708 (slice 8.3). Stacked on #1247 (8.2, the token store), which merges first.

## What changed

On a Hermes host whose only sign-in is a browser (OIDC) provider, Hermex says "Hermex doesn't support this yet" and stops. Now the connect form and the server's own sign-in form offer **Sign In with Browser** instead of a username and password.

- `HermesBrowserSignIn` reuses the 8.1 spike's loopback listener on `127.0.0.1`, trimmed. It opens the host's `/auth/native/authorize` (S256 PKCE, `state`, fully percent-encoded) in an ephemeral `ASWebAuthenticationSession`. It keeps only a callback whose `state` matches, and every callback bounces `302 hermexsignin://done` to close the sheet. The code goes straight to `/auth/native/token`, and the new `HermesConnection.signIn(browserCode:verifier:)` turns the result into 8.2's `BotConnection.oauth` and signs in with the bearer, so the version, install and identity checks all still apply.
- Detection: `auth_flows ∋ native_pkce` and no `basic` provider. No `provider` is sent: at the pin, `_select_native_provider` picks the sole interactive provider itself and renders its own chooser when there are several. That matches the go comment's "pass it when there's exactly one" without an extra `/api/auth/providers` read.
- Entry points: onboarding Connect, Settings → Add Server, and a Hermes server's sign-in form (shown after sign-out or `.signInExpired`). That form now reads the server's status even when signed out. Signing the same account in again keeps the connection's UUID, so drafts, cache and push pairing survive. Closing the sheet shows nothing.
- Not covered: a webui server's Bots connection and Move to Hermes's destination stay password-only. Move saves its destination's record long after the check, apart from the connection that would rotate its token. A browser host there gets the existing `.browserSignIn` refusal.
- **Testing toggle:** Settings → Testing → "Browser sign-in on password hosts", in Debug and Hermex Branch builds only (gated on the `.branch` bundle-ID suffix). It sends a host that also offers `basic` through the browser, with its `/login` page shown inside the sheet.
- Cut per the go comment: no foreground rebind, no background task, no revoke call. Sign-out deletes the record and its token.

New copy (all 17 translations, `needs_review`):
- Button: **Sign In with Browser**
- Server form, in place of the fields: "This server signs in through your browser."
- Connect form banner: "Hermes dashboard found. It signs in through your browser."
- Error: "The browser sign-in didn't finish. Try again."

## How it was tested

- Full local suite on this head (the Xcode project changed): 4292 passed, 2 skipped. After the 8.2 review fixes and this rebase, the focused run (`HermesBrowserSignInTests`, `OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests`, `BotConnectionSetupTests`, `HermesConnectionTests`) passed: 65 tests.
- New tests: the PKCE challenge against an independently computed value; the authorize URL's encoding; detection, including the toggle; a real loopback hop where a stray `state` is ignored, both callbacks bounce, and the exchanged verifier matches the challenge and leads to a bearer identity check; sheet cancel and a refused code; onboarding adding a browser host's server; the server form signing the same account in again with its UUID kept.
- No simulator screenshots: the owner asked to rely on tests because simulator taps are unreliable on this Mac.

**Test coverage limit (owner decision):** no real OIDC provider was tested. No such host is available, so the owner chose to skip that check. Browser sign-in was tested only on a password host's browser path, through the debug toggle: the host's `/login` page inside the sheet, then the same loopback, code exchange and token flow an OIDC host uses. The IdP's own pages, and its redirect back through the host's `/auth/callback`, have never run against a real provider. The 8.1 spike covered only the HTTPS `302` to loopback that such a redirect ends in.

**2.0 release notes line:** Sign in to Hermes hosts that use browser sign-in (OIDC). Tested so far only through a password host's browser sign-in, not against a real OIDC provider.

**Owner check (physical iPhone, Hermex Branch, live password host):**
1. Settings → Testing → turn on "Browser sign-in on password hosts".
2. Settings → Servers → sign out of the Hermes server. The form shows "This server signs in through your browser." and **Sign In with Browser**.
3. Tap it. The sheet shows the host's `/login`. Sign in (AutoFill is fine). The sheet closes on its own and Sessions and chats load.
4. Force-quit and relaunch. You should still be signed in (one refresh, no prompt).
5. Sign out, tap Sign In with Browser, then Cancel in the sheet. No error appears, and tapping again works.
6. Turn the toggle off, sign out. The username and password form is back, and a password sign-in still works.

body:
## Problem

Hermex 2.0 adds Sign In with Browser for Hermes hosts that use browser sign-in (OIDC), through [#1247](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1247) and [#1248](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1248). Two other ways of connecting to a Hermes host still accept only a password, so they can't reach a browser-sign-in host:

- **Move to Hermes**, when a webui server's destination host signs in through a browser.
- **A webui server's Bots connection**, when its Hermes host signs in through a browser.

## Done when

Both paths offer Sign In with Browser when the host only accepts it, and reuse the token store and sheet from #1247 and #1248. Password hosts behave the same as before.

Split out of [#708](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/708) so it doesn't hold up 2.0. Browser sign-in has so far been tested only through a password host's browser path, not against a real OIDC provider.

title: Redesign Settings as an index of focused pages
body:
**What the user gets:** a short Settings screen that opens on an index of a few pages, with everything about one server on that server's own page.
**Why it matters:** Settings is one scroll of ~17 cards and 40+ rows that mixes app-wide and per-server choices, and the server you are on sits near the bottom. Voice Mode (#256) would make it longer still.
**Cost:** Large overall, split into the slices below. Needs the owner's pick of a mock before any slice starts; visual review on a phone at the end.

## Decisions (grilled 2026-10-14)

- **Shape:** the top screen is an index of rows that each open a focused page (inspired by the t3code iOS app's Settings). No toggles on the top screen.
- **Built on** `List` with `.insetGrouped`, `NavigationLink`, and standard section headers and footers. This replaces the custom `SettingsCard` / `SettingsToggleRow` / `SettingsDivider` scroll.
- **Rule:** top-screen pages hold settings that apply on this iPhone to every server. Anything specific to one server lives on that server's page. Notifications (and later Voice) are the exceptions, and label their per-server part *This server*.
- **webui servers** get the same layout. webui-only rows appear on that server's page.
- **The top screen never waits on the network.** Row values only where they are known locally: server rows (host, Hermes or webui, a checkmark on the active one), Appearance (theme), Notifications (*Push on* or *Push off*).
- **No search** in Settings.

## Map

**Top screen**
- **Servers**: one row per server, which opens its page · Add Server
- **Hermex**
  - **Appearance**: Theme, App Icon, Tint New Chat & Send
  - **Composer**: Send While Responding, Dismiss Keyboard After Sending, Dictation Provider, Files Button, Git Actions
  - **Chat**: Thinking & Tool cards, Fold Finished Turns, Position After Response, Message Timestamps, Response Speed, Wrap Code Block Lines, Right-to-Left Chat Layout, Hide Attachment Paths
  - **Notifications**: *This server* (hermex-push) · *On this iPhone* (Response Complete Alerts, Live Activity Excerpts). A page instead of today's fold-out.
  - **General**: Haptic Feedback and Pulse While Streaming, App Lock
- **About**: About Hermex (version, build, Privacy Policy, Support, Report a Problem, Become a supporter, Buy Uzi a coffee, Rate Hermex) · Developer (Debug and Branch builds only)

**Server page.** Today's Active Server card and `ServerDetailView` become one page.
- **Identity**: avatar, display name, initials, header color. The single editor; the top-level Identity card goes away.
- **Connection**: URL, status, version and update, Hermes connection or Connection Headers
- **Sessions**: Archived Sessions · webui only: Main Page entries, session row visibility, Bot Mode (beta)
- **Defaults** (webui only): Default Model, Default Profile, Providers
- **Data**: Offline Cache (webui only), Move to Hermes
- **Switch to This Server** (on servers that aren't active) · **Sign Out** or **Remove Server**

**Links in:** "Manage Servers" opens the top screen. The chat's one-time notification offer (#863) opens the Notifications page directly. `SettingsScrollAnchor` becomes an optional destination with a single case, `notifications`.

## Removals (slice 2)

- The three Thinking & Tool card toggles become one picker, *Hidden / Collapsed / Expanded*. Migration: cards off → Hidden; either expand toggle on → Expanded; otherwise Collapsed.
- Siri & Shortcuts is removed entirely.
- The Developer and Testing cards merge into one Developer page.
- Footnotes are one line at most; those that restate the row are deleted.

Kept on purpose: Tint New Chat & Send, Response Speed, Pulse While Streaming. Bot Mode moves rather than going away.

## Order

1. HTML mocks of three styles (A: colored icon tiles like iOS Settings; B: t3code-style monochrome icons; C: B plus a card at the top for the active server), each showing the top screen, the server page and Chat, in light and dark. **Picked: B** (2026-10-14, https://u8aw252zjnkv.postplan.dev).
2. Done in #1255. Slice 1 (#1253): the new pages with every setting moved over and no behavior change.
3. Done in #1259, which also trimmed the push setup copy. Slice 2 (#1254): the removals.
4. Voice (#256) adds a **Voice** page in the Hermex section when it lands. It takes Dictation Provider from Composer and puts its per-server voice picker under *This server*. Until then, Dictation Provider stays on Composer.

title: Move Settings into an index and focused pages
body:
**What the user gets:** Settings opens on a short index, and each group of settings has its own page. Every existing setting still works and keeps its value.
**Why it matters:** Slice 1 of #1252. It is the structural move, kept free of behavior changes so it reviews and reverts cleanly.
**Cost:** Large. Owner visual review on a phone.

**Style: B** (monochrome glyphs, rounded grouped cards, t3code-like), picked by the owner 2026-10-14 from https://u8aw252zjnkv.postplan.dev.

## Scope

Build the top screen and pages exactly as #1252's **Map** says, in the style the owner picked, on `List` (`.insetGrouped`). Move every current control as-is: same storage keys, same copy (footnotes may be shortened only in slice 2), same confirmations and alerts.

- Split `SettingsView.swift` (2,821 lines) into one file per page under `Features/Settings/`. Delete the custom card, row and divider components once nothing uses them.
- Merge the Active Server card into the server page. Server-scoped loads (default model and profile, webui version and update, status) run on the server page, never on the top screen.
- Identity is edited only on the server page. Keep today's sync into the registry entry (`updateServerIdentity`).
- Notifications becomes a page. `HermexPushSectionView` loses its `DisclosureGroup`. The `.notifications` destination pushes it with push shown expanded (#863).
- "Manage Servers" opens the top screen; drop the `.servers` anchor.
- Developer and Testing stay separate in this slice (merged in slice 2).

## Acceptance

- Every row from today's screen is reachable at the path the Map gives, on a Hermes server and on a webui server.
- Switching servers rebuilds the server page; nothing from server A appears under server B.
- The top screen does no network work (no `APIClient` or Hermes call before you open a page).
- Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels, light and dark, Reduce Motion, iPad split view.
- Focused tests: the destination routing, and that the top screen's row values come from local state.

title: perf(chat): long replies render slowly through the per-reply text-selection host
body:
**What the user gets:** chats with long replies open and scroll faster, with text selection unchanged.
**Why it matters:** in a measured chat with 12 long replies, the selection layer costs about 37% of the time from history landing to the first frame.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs a design that keeps selection (#553); simulator benchmarks, then a phone check.

## Evidence

Release build, iPhone 17 simulator, live Hermes host, the "Write a long story #2" chat (12 messages, long replies). Render time is measured from the history landing to the first transcript frame (`Session Open` signpost).

- Baseline: median 1796 ms (1711 to 1856, n=3).
- Probe with `ResponseTextSelection` bypassed (not shippable, removes selection): median 1128 ms (1081 to 1166, n=3). Runs were interleaved.
- A Time Profiler trace puts 722 of 3168 main-thread samples (23%) inside `ResponseTextSelection.sizeThatFits`. The time goes to the inner `UIHostingController` building and updating its own view graph, not to glyph collection or text layout.
- Temporary counters showed 61 `updateUIViewController` calls and 61 size passes for 12 replies during one open. The first size pass of a long reply costs 150 to 200 ms. Later passes cost about 4 ms.

## Likely mechanism

`ResponseTextSelection` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ResponseTextSelection.swift`) reads `@Environment(\.self)` and sets `host.rootView = AnyView(...)` with the whole environment on every update. So every environment change re-runs each reply's inner graph. The transcript is an eager `VStack`, so this applies to every reply, including off-screen ones.

## Directions to measure (not decided)

- Skip `rootView` reassignment when the reply's inputs did not change, without losing environment changes such as Dynamic Type or color scheme.
- Forward only the environment values the hosted content reads.
- Attach the selection host lazily, without breaking the long-press that starts selection.

Uzair ruled out `LazyVStack` in #32. None of these directions depends on it.

Measurement tools: `Session Open` signposts (`HermesMobile/Config/PerformanceSignposts.swift`) read with `log show --signpost` on the simulator, as in `scripts/benchmark-sim-launch`.

Prepared by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code) during a performance pass.

title: perf(hermes): show the cached sessions and transcript while the host connects
body:
## Linked issue

No issue. Uzair asked for a measured performance pass. The follow-up is filed as #1256.

## What changed

On a Hermes server, a cold launch made about 8 tunnel round trips, one after another, before any session row showed. Sign-in alone is 3 of them. Each chat open also waited for the network. The offline cache already held those rows, but it only showed after a failure.

- An empty Sessions list and an empty Hermes chat now show their cached copy at once, marked provisional. The host's first read replaces it. This extends the rule from #1144 (Bot Chat) to every Hermes chat and to the list.
- A provisional copy hides the offline banner, the Cached badges and the reconnect line. Writes stay off, read marks included, and Send waits for the live read. If the connect fails, a cache-eligible error shows the usual offline state. Any other error ends as it does today.
- The list remembers, per server, the last Profile it showed (`hermes.lastListedProfile|<server>`). So the cache paints even when no Profile was picked. The host still settles the Profile, and sign-out or server removal clears the key.
- A chat paints from `prepareInitialMessageLoad`, during the push animation, the way a webui chat does.

## How it was tested

Release build, iPhone 17 simulator, live Hermes host, with the two builds alternated:
- Launch to first session rows: median 2872 → 1257 ms (9 runs each).
- Reopening a chat in the same app session: median 669 → 215 ms (5 runs each).
- The host's live rows land at the same time as before, and the first chat opened after launch shows no measurable difference.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17>` with HermesOfflineCacheTests, HermesChatTurnTests, HermesSessionListTests, HermesTranscriptPagingTests, AuthManagerStateTests, SessionListMutationTests, ChatViewModelSendTests and HermesChatSettingsTests: 532 passed. Each new test fails without its fix.
- Two independent review rounds found four defects, all fixed with tests: a lost streaming reply, Bot Chat stuck after a 401, read marks sent from cached rows, and a Bot Chat losing its copy after a failed history read.

Manual check: relaunch on a Hermes server and look for rows in about a second with no banner. Reopen a chat to see it at once, with Send briefly busy. Relaunch with the network off to see the offline banner and Cached badges.

title: chore(scripts): add sim-doctor to name why a simulator is stuck
body:
## Linked issue

No issue. Maintainer-approved chore from a simulator-wedge investigation.

## What changed

Agents keep losing time to stuck simulators and diagnose each one by hand. Over the last six weeks, transcripts show 5 days where CoreSimulator locked up across several devices, 14 of 585 `test-sim` runs hit the runner hang, and on 2026-10-14 an lldb session left the app a zombie that wedged iPhone Air.

- `scripts/sim-doctor [udid]` runs bounded probes (each stops its whole process group after 20 s) and prints one verdict with the command that clears it: `SERVICE`, `MEMORY`, `DEVICE`, `ZOMBIE_APP`, or `OK`. Heavy swap alone only warns; it becomes the verdict only when a device stops answering.
- `scripts/test-sim` saves swap use per run in `memory.log`, so memory-pressure stalls can be checked against real runs later. On 2026-10-14 this 16 GB Mac had 12 to 13 GB of swap in use, and booting one iOS 27 simulator left 19 of its processes stuck waiting on memory.
- `AGENTS.md` points agents at `sim-doctor` and says to end lldb sessions with `kill`, never detach, and never `simctl terminate` the app while lldb holds it. `DEVELOPMENT.md` § Stuck simulators explains each verdict.

## How it was tested

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 52 tests pass, including the new `test_sim_doctor.py`. Its process-group test fails when `probe()` kills only the leader (checked by mutation).
- A real `scripts/sim-doctor` run with no UDID, with the booted iPhone 17 and iPhone 17e, and with the shut-down iPhone Air returned the expected `MEMORY`/`OK` and `NOT_BOOTED` verdicts in 1 to 5 s each.

No issue. Uzair asked for this fix after test runs kept signing the simulator out.

## What changed

The tests run inside the installed app as their host. A test that reaches the real Keychain, `HTTPCookieStorage.shared` or the standard defaults changes the app's saved servers and sessions. For example, `AuthManagerStateTests` deletes every cookie before and after each test, which drops the webui session. After a `scripts/test-sim` run, the simulator showed "Your session expired" and had to be signed in again with `scripts/sim-login`.

- New `TestHostStateGuard`, the test bundle's principal class (`INFOPLIST_KEY_NSPrincipalClass`). It snapshots the host app's generic-password Keychain items, cookies and standard defaults when the bundle starts, and restores them when the bundle finishes. This covers `scripts/test-sim`, Xcode ⌘U and CI.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` § Local XCTest explains this behavior.

A run that is killed before it finishes can still sign the simulator out. Making each test stop touching real state would be the deeper fix, but 18 test files use the real Keychain store. The guard covers them all, including future tests.

## How it was tested

- **Before:** signed in with `scripts/sim-login`, then ran `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only HermesMobileTests/AuthManagerStateTests`. The app reopened on "Your session expired".
- **After:** the same steps leave the app signed in, with the same 4 Keychain items.
- **Full suite:** `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17>` ran 4303 passed, 1 failed, 2 skipped, and the simulator stayed signed in. The failure, `ComposerVoiceInputServerRecordingTests.testInterruptedRecordingRetainsClipUntilUnlockedAndTranscribesOnce`, also fails on unchanged master on this simulator. It depends on the simulator's microphone permission state and is not related to this change.
