title: test: HermesSlashCommandTests.testOnlyTheNewestCompletionApplies is order-dependent
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing directly; CI stops failing PRs at random on this test.
**Why it matters:** it failed CI on [#1262](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1262) (run 38651238337, attempt 2), a PR that does not touch slash commands, and cost a re-run.
**Cost:** Small, no phone needed.

## Problem

`HermesMobileTests/HermesSlashCommandTests.swift` `testOnlyTheNewestCompletionApplies` starts both calls with `async let`:

```swift
async let older: Void = slash.complete("/approvals x")
async let newer: Void = slash.complete("/approvals ")
```

`HermesSlashCommands.complete(_:)` takes its revision (`completionRevision += 1`) at the start of the call, and the newest revision wins. `async let` children have no guaranteed start order, so sometimes `newer` takes revision 1 and `older` takes revision 2. The "older" reply then wins and `completion?.text` is `/approvals x`. The test assumes the calls start in source order. The production code is fine; only the test is racy.

## Fix

Make the call order deterministic while still letting the replies land in either order. For example, start `older` first and make sure it has taken its revision (it suspends in `completionDelay`'s sleep) before starting `newer`. Keep the assertion that the newer call's reply is the one kept. No sleeps or polling (AGENTS.md § Verifying).

## Done when

- The test passes when run repeatedly, e.g. `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSlashCommandTests/testOnlyTheNewestCompletionApplies` in a loop of 50.
- `HermesSessionListTests.testOnlyTheNewestReadApplies` has been checked for the same `async let` pattern, and fixed the same way if it has it.

title: feat(hermes): make Move to Hermes easy for every webui user
body:
**What the user gets:** every webui user is asked once to move to Hermes, and can do it in a few taps whether or not they've already signed in to Hermes.
**Why it matters:** 2.0 makes Hermes the default, but Move to Hermes is buried in Settings, users who are only on webui retype everything, and hosts that sign in through a browser are refused. The owner is holding 2.0 for this.
**Cost:** Large overall, across four PRs. The sign-in and prompt slices need the owner's hands on a phone.

## Problem

Today the only way in is Settings › Servers › the webui server › Move to Hermes…, and nothing tells a webui user it exists. There are two kinds of users:

- **Users with a Bots connection** on their webui server already skip sign-in: the move reuses that connection's address, password and headers.
- **Users who are only on webui** get a blank, password-only sign-in form inside the move. There's no browser sign-in ([#1249](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1249)), and the Cloudflare headers the app already has for the webui server aren't reused.

## Decisions (grilled with the owner, 2026-10-14)

1. Move to Hermes doesn't have its own sign-in form. Users with a Bots connection go straight to the scan. Everyone else uses the normal Hermes sign-in (password or browser), and is then offered "Bring your chats from <webui server>?". Any Hermes sign-in offers this for webui servers that haven't moved.
2. A one-time sheet the first time 2.0 opens with a webui server that hasn't moved. After that, a dismissible banner on that server's chat list. Settings › Move to Hermes… stays.
3. Any Profile without a same-name match defaults to the host's default Profile, and the user can still change it on Review.
4. The report's Done step offers "Remove <webui server>". With several webui servers, it also offers the next one. Moves happen one at a time.
5. Opened from a move, the Hermes sign-in's headers section offers "Use <webui server>'s headers". It's a tap, never filled in automatically. The address stays blank: the webui can't reliably tell us the Hermes address.
6. The Bots-connection half of #1249 is dropped. #1249 closes when the sign-in slice lands.
7. This ships in 2.0. It's checked with one focused Branch TestFlight pass: both kinds of users, a browser-sign-in destination, resuming after quitting mid-move, and #713's short-pass list.

## Slices

- #1265 token fix
- #1266 sign-in (blocked by #1265)
- #1267 prompt (blocked by #1266)
- #1268 Remove on Done (independent)

The prompt's look and wording come from static mocks the owner picks before the prompt slice and the sign-in slice's UI are built.

title: fix(hermes): keep a browser sign-in's rotated token during Move to Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** moving into a Hermes server you signed in to with a browser doesn't silently break that server's sign-in.
**Why it matters:** the move's connection refreshes the token but never saves the new one, so the host's next refresh fails and the user has to sign in again. Every browser sign-in user goes through this path once #1264's sign-in slice lands.
**Cost:** Small. Covered by unit tests; no phone needed.

Part of #1264.

## Problem

`MoveToHermesDestination.live` builds a plain `HermesConnection(connection: saved)` (`MoveToHermesRunner.swift:290`) and signs in (`:295`). It never sets `initialRefreshToken` or `onRefreshTokenRotated`; only `keepRefreshTokens` sets those (`HermesConnection.swift:538, 582-602`).

So when `refresh` rotates the token (`HermesConnection.swift:266-268`), the new token lives only in that in-memory connection. The Keychain keeps the retired one, and the server's own connection then sends it and gets `.signInExpired`. The runner also skips the wait for a retired connection's refresh that's still in flight (`:584-588`).

## Done when

- The move's connection to a browser-sign-in destination keeps rotated tokens the same way a Hermes server's own connection does. It reuses the existing token store and doesn't add a second one.
- A test fails before the fix: a destination with a saved refresh token, a move whose connection rotates it, then the Keychain holds the new token.
- Password destinations behave as before.

title: feat(hermes): move through the normal Hermes sign-in
body:
**What the user gets:** Move to Hermes no longer has its own sign-in. Users with a Bots connection go straight to the scan. Everyone else signs in through the normal Hermes sign-in, including browser sign-in, and is then offered their chats.
**Why it matters:** users who are only on webui retype everything into a password-only form, and hosts that sign in through a browser are refused.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner on a phone for both kinds of users.

Part of #1264. Blocked by #1265. Its UI (the offer and the headers button) follows the mock the owner picks.

## Flow

- **The webui server has a Bots connection:** keep today's behavior: skip host choice and scan with that connection (`MoveToHermesModel.swift:163-169`).
- **Otherwise:** the destination is either a signed-in Hermes server, or "Sign in to a Hermes host". That second choice opens the normal Hermes sign-in (`AddServerView` / `OnboardingViewModel.addHermesServer`), which already offers browser sign-in, and comes back to the scan once signed in.
- **Signed in to Hermes by any route** (onboarding, Add Server): if a webui server hasn't moved and has no move record, offer "Bring your chats from <webui server>?". One server at a time.
- **Remove the move's own sign-in and its password-only guard:** the `entry == .moveDestination` refusal (`OnboardingViewModel.swift:546-551`) and the browser-only refusal in Checking (`MoveToHermesModel.swift:230`). Today, with the Developer switch "Browser sign-in on password hosts" on, that guard calls a password host browser-only. That false error goes away with the guard.
- **Headers:** opened from a move, the Hermes sign-in's headers section offers "Use <webui server>'s headers". One tap fills in the webui server's `custom_headers`, visibly; never automatically. Update `docs/agents/hermes-server.md:216-217`, which says webui headers are never a source. Leave the address blank.
- **Review:** any Profile with no same-name Hermes Profile defaults to the host's default Profile instead of needing a pick (`MoveToHermesModel.swift:305-309`). The user can still change it.

## Done when

- Users who are only on webui reach a password or browser-sign-in host through the normal sign-in, and the move continues on its own.
- Users with a Bots connection behave as today.
- Model tests cover:
  - which destination path each case takes;
  - the offer after sign-in (shown for a webui server that hasn't moved, not for a moved one);
  - the headers button copying exactly the webui server's headers;
  - the default Profile being preselected.
- Close [#1249](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1249) as covered here. Its Bots-connection half is dropped.

title: feat(hermes): ask webui users once to Move to Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** the first time 2.0 opens, a webui user is asked once whether to move to Hermes. After that, a quiet banner keeps it in reach.
**Why it matters:** Move to Hermes is three levels deep in Settings, and nothing tells a webui user it exists.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner on a phone. The look and wording come from mocks the owner picks first.

Part of #1264. Blocked by #1266, because the sheet sends users into that flow.

## Behavior

- **One-time sheet:** shown for each webui server that hasn't moved and has no move record, the first time the app opens with that server. It explains the move in a sentence or two.
  - "Move to Hermes" goes straight to the scan for a webui server with a Bots connection, and to the Hermes sign-in otherwise.
  - "Not now" closes it, and it doesn't come back for that server.
  - Where the "shown" state lives is decided at implementation. Note that it's keyed per server, so it never shows under another server.
- **Banner:** at the top of that webui server's chat list until the server moves or the user dismisses it with ×. Dismissing is per server and permanent. Settings › Move to Hermes… still works.
- **More than one webui server:** one sheet per server, never stacked. The next shows on a later launch or from the previous move's report.
- **Doesn't show** for a webui server that has moved or has a move in progress; the existing Paused, Finished and Moved banners cover those (`MoveToHermesNotices`).
- No continuously repainting animation, it respects Reduce Motion, and it has VoiceOver labels.

## Done when

- Model tests cover when the sheet and banner show and stay dismissed, for each server, including two webui servers and a server switch.
- One phone pass: update over a 1.x install that has a webui server, then see the sheet once and the banner after.

title: feat(hermes): offer to remove the webui server when a move finishes
body:
**What the user gets:** when a move finishes, the report offers to remove the old webui server, and to move the next one if there is another.
**Why it matters:** today removing the moved server takes a trip into Settings › More…, and each further webui server has to be found by hand.
**Cost:** Small. Covered by unit tests; a quick phone look.

Part of #1264.

  - the next-server offer appears only when a webui server that hasn't moved remains.

title: fix(hermes): keep a browser sign-in's rotated token during Move to Hermes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1265 (Part of #1264)

## What changed

**Problem:** Move to Hermes built its destination connection without the `keepRefreshTokens` path, so when the host rotated a browser sign-in's refresh token during the move, the new token was never saved. The server's own connection, still signed in, then refreshed with the token the host had retired.

**Fix:** The move's destination connection now comes from `HermesConnections.ownConnection`, the same path a server's own connection uses: before each refresh it waits for any in-flight refresh a retired connection on that server left behind (looked up at refresh time, not when the connection was made), saves each rotated token before its access token is used, and on close records any refresh still in flight for the next connection on that server. A browser sign-in's connection also re-reads the saved token before a refresh when it changed since it last looked.

Decision applied: [Preserve #1247, #1224 kept](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1265#issuecomment-6182254158).

**Decisions made overnight**
- `keepRefreshTokens` now re-reads the Keychain before every refresh, so the active server's own connection picks up a token the move rotated (alternative: do only the literal decision and file a follow-up).

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only …`, all pass:
HermesConnectionTests 21, MoveToHermesModelTests 15, MoveToHermesRunnerTests 24, AuthManagerStateTests 48, HermesBrowserSignInTests 6, BotConnectionVersionTests 4, OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests 19.
After the review fix: HermesConnectionTests, MoveToHermesRunnerTests, MoveToHermesModelTests, AuthManagerStateTests, HermesBrowserSignInTests, 116 passed, including the new `testAMovesConnectionWaitsForARefreshRetiredAfterItWasMade` and `testTheServersOwnConnectionWaitsForAMovesRefreshClosedAfterItWasMade`.

Red evidence: `testAMoveSavesTheTokenItRotatesForTheServersOwnConnection` failed on the old code: the Keychain held `refresh-1` where `refresh-2` was expected, and the old connection's refresh never reached the scripted host, showing the rotated token was never saved. Both new tests failed on c07d88b6: each connection sent `[refresh-0, refresh-0]` instead of `[refresh-0, refresh-1]`.

**Manual test:** Covered by tests; no manual check needed. The browser-sign-in destination is checked in #1264's focused Branch TestFlight pass.

title: feat(hermes): offer to remove the webui server when a move finishes
body:
Fixes #1268. Part of #1264. Stacked on #1273 (1269 → 1271 → 1273 → 1270).

## What changed

After a move to Hermes finished, removing the old webui server took a trip into Settings › More…, and each other webui server had to be found by hand.

The report now ends with stacked actions (design 5A, per the [binding decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1268#issuecomment-6182255531)): **Done** switches to Hermes as before. **Move <next> Next** appears only while another configured webui server has no move record. It opens that server's host step and starts no scan until the user picks a host. **Remove <server>…** runs the existing Remove This Server path with its confirmation, so the destination keeps the move record that routes old links. A footnote says the server's chats stay on its host.

**Stack conflict resolutions:** `MoveToHermesModel` host step and entry: kept #1266's `.offer` and `signedIn(at:)`, added `.next` and `useSaved()`, and dropped `useVerified`, which #1266 removed. String Catalog: sorted union.

**Decisions made overnight**
- The report's toolbar Done and in-list "Open <destination>" were dropped, so the stacked Done is the only one (alt: keep both).
- Move Next swaps the sheet's model in place (alt: dismiss, then have each presenter re-present).
- Move Next is `.bordered` gray and Remove is `.bordered` destructive, pinned in a bottom `safeAreaInset` (alt: plain text buttons or an in-list section).
- Move Next opens a new `.next` entry: the host step lists the saved Hermes sign-in first, and the scan starts on tap (alt: reuse `.start` and auto-scan, overruled in review).
- The host step gets one header for that path: "Pick the host that should take %@'s chats. The first is its saved Hermes sign-in." (alt: hide the header).
- Move Next doesn't count toward #1267's one-sheet-per-launch gate and doesn't mark the next server asked (alt: mark it asked).
- The webui test fixture also answers `studio.example` (alt: stop the test at the host step).

## How it was tested

- `MoveToHermesModelTests` + `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 28 passed. Red: with stubs, `testRemovingFromTheReportKeepsTheMoveRecord` and `testTheNextServerIsOfferedOnlyWhileOneHasntMoved` failed. With `.next` behaving like `.start`, `testMoveNextWaitsForAHostBeforeChecking` failed (screen `review`, not `chooseHost`). `testMoveNextAcknowledgesTheReportAndWaitsForAHost` calls the new `moveNext()`, so it has no red run.
- Stack integration: `testMoveNextFromTheQuestionSignsInWithoutClosingIt` and `testRemovingAfterTheOffersMoveKeepsTheDestinationsSignIn`. Full suite on this head: 4331 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped.
- Four new strings, each with 17 translations.

## Design

Mock: https://mpdteu6qforr.postplan.dev/v/1#issue-1268, pick **5A**. There are no screenshots: the report appears only after a real move to a Hermes host, and this run had read-only host access and no local fixture.

## Manual test

1. Settings › webui server A › Move to Hermes… › Move. The report shows Done, red "Remove A…" and the footnote, with no "Move … Next". Tap Remove, Cancel: nothing changes. Remove Server: the app switches to Hermes, A is gone, and an old A link still opens on Hermes.
2. [Needs a second webui server B with a saved Hermes sign-in] Finish A's move. "Move B Next" sits between Done and Remove. Tap it: B's host step lists the saved host first, and Checking starts only after you tap that row.
3. [Needs B] Move Next from the one-time question or the "Signed in to…" offer lands on the next server's sign-in step without closing the sheet; Remove after that move keeps the Hermes sign-in.
4. [Needs B] Settings › B › Move to Hermes… still goes straight to Checking.

2. [Needs B] Repeat iPhone step 2 from the session-list report banner's See Report.

title: feat(hermes): ask webui users once to move, then keep a banner
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1267
Part of #1264

## What changed

**Problem.** Users updating from 1.x with a webui server had no prompt to move to Hermes; the move was only reachable from Settings.

**Fix.** Each webui server is asked once, over its own chat list, about 1 s after the list settles; the question waits until that server's chat list is on screen, and returning to the list restarts the 1 s wait: a "Move <server> to Hermes" half sheet with Move to Hermes / Not Now. One question per launch, only while that server is the signed-in active server, never over another sheet or #1266's offer. Move to Hermes starts the same guided move as Settings. Afterwards a card at the top of that server's chat list (iPad sidebar too) keeps the move in reach until the move or ✕. The state (`nil → asked → dismissed`) lives on the server's registry entry, so it is per server and removed with it; servers with a move record keep their Paused/Finished/Moved banners instead. Applied decisions: [#1267 decisions](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1267#issuecomment-6182255159); [design pick](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1267#issuecomment-6182154015); Preserve #1225 kept.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Flags stored on the server's Keychain registry entry (alt: UserDefaults keyed by id).
- A server counts as asked when the sheet appears (alt: only on a button tap).
- If #1266's offer showed this launch, the question waits for the next launch (alt: show after the offer closes).
- The banner is a neutral card sharing the move banners' shape (alt: orange like the move banners).
- Switching mid-launch to an unasked webui server asks over its own list when no move sheet has shown yet (alt: ask only on a launch that opens on that server).
- Review limit reached with one small finding → follow-up #1274.

title: fix(hermes): wait on the topmost sheet before asking to move
body:
Follow-up from review of #1273 (#1267), left at the review limit as a small finding.

**Problem.** `MoveToHermesQuestionTiming` waits for the presented controller to leave its window before asking "Move <server> to Hermes". It always picks the root's immediate `presentedViewController`, not the topmost one.

**Evidence** (`HermesMobile/Features/MoveToHermes/MoveToHermesView.swift:939`). Failing state: the question is due while the window has root → sheet A → full-screen presentation B. The lookup chooses A. UIKit's `.fullScreen` removes the presenting controller's views after presentation completes ([Apple's fullScreen reference](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uimodalpresentationstyle/fullscreen)), so A's probe has no window even though A stays presented beneath B. The dismissal wait resumes immediately (line 959); `ask` then sleeps one second and repeats against A for as long as B stays open. That is recurring wakeups and probe allocation instead of an event-driven wait. The app has this nesting: `ChatView.swift:1183` presents `fileReferenceSheet`, whose `FilePreviewView.swift:117` presents selectable text with `fullScreenCover`. Source-walked, not reproduced on a device.

**Suggested fix.** Walk each window's `presentedViewController` chain to the topmost covering controller and wait on that one; after it leaves its window, re-evaluate the remaining chain. Add focused coverage for a full-screen controller presented above a sheet, checking that the pending question parks until dismissal instead of repeatedly checking an off-window ancestor.

title: fix(bots): keep a bot's own face after Desktop opens it
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: a maintainer-approved `fix/` change.

## What changed

If you set a bot's face in Hermex and then opened Bots on Desktop, the bot in Hermex went still. It could also turn into a different shape or color. Desktop uploads a 160x160 PNG of its own drawing for any bot without a picture (`pushLocalAvatars`), sometimes drawn from an older look, and Hermex showed that PNG as if it were a photo. On the live host, four bots got these copies in the same second, about 4 s after Desktop started. Two of the copies didn't match the saved look: a green cloud was uploaded as an orange drop, and a squircle as a cloud.

Hermex now uses Desktop's own rule (`isBackfilledFacePng`): unless the look's `imageKind` is `photo`, a 160x160 PNG counts as no picture, so Hermex draws the saved face with its blink and working sway. Only that answer is kept for the look revision, so the copy isn't downloaded again on every open, while an unreadable asset is fetched again next time. Hermex marks its own uploads `imageKind: photo`, so this can't hide one of them. The inbox and the Profile editor's reload use the same rule. `docs/agents/bots.md` describes Desktop's copies.

Desktop's own problems (copies from out-of-date looks, a photo cache that never updates) belong upstream and aren't covered here.

## How it was tested

- New `BotAvatarTests.testDesktopFaceCopyDrawsTheFaceUnlessTheLookSaysPhoto`: a 160x160 PNG for a drawn face is ignored, the same PNG for `imageKind: photo` is shown, a 256x256 upload is shown, a second refresh at the same revision doesn't fetch the copy again, and an unreadable asset is fetched again.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only HermesMobileTests/BotAvatarTests`: 7 passed. `--only HermesMobileTests/BotProfileEditorTests`: 18 passed.
- The live host was checked read-only over ssh. The four affected bots have `imageKind: shape` and a 160x160 PNG asset written after their last look change.

Manual check: open Bots for a bot whose face was set in Hermex and has since been opened on Desktop. It should show its saved shape and color again and blink.

title: bug(composer): keyboard emoji appears as U+FFFC and disappears after send
body:
## Bug description

An emoji selected from the standard iOS emoji keyboard appears normally in Hermex's composer, but after sending it disappears and the message contains only the object replacement character `U+FFFC` (`￼`). No attachment or visible emoji reaches the conversation.

The user selected a flamethrower emoji from the ordinary emoji keyboard as far as they could tell; it may nevertheless be represented by iOS internally as a sticker-style attributed-text object. Hermex accepts it visually but silently loses the object during send serialization.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an ordinary Hermex session chat.
2. Insert the flamethrower emoji from the iOS emoji keyboard into an otherwise empty composer.
3. Confirm it is visible in the composer.
4. Send the message.

## Actual behavior

The emoji disappears after send. The transmitted message contains only `U+FFFC` (`￼`), with no corresponding image or attachment. The receiving conversation therefore shows a blank/object-placeholder character.

## Expected behavior

Hermex should either:

- send the emoji/object successfully as text or an attachment; or
- reject unsupported rich emoji/sticker objects before sending with a clear explanation.

It should not silently send only `U+FFFC`.

## Environment

- Hermex: 1.9 (App Store)
- iOS: 27.2
- Backend path: hermes-webui session
- Device/server identifiers intentionally omitted

## Privacy note

No private transcript, server URL, credentials, or screenshots are needed to reproduce this issue.

title: May I ready a smaller Hermes watch for 2.0?

I read your note on #1092. Thank you for it. You closed that PR on 15 Oct 2026 because the work went beyond #575, the reply path only worked on legacy webui, and #575 stays open for a smaller Hermes-first proposal with an agreed scope. I kept #575 in mind and put together a local build that only does the phone relay: the watch asks the iPhone, and the iPhone uses the Hermes gateway that is already on master. The code is on my machine. I have not opened a pull request.

May I ready this kind of app for Hermex 2.0, within the requirements you set on #575? I would like your feedback on the proposal, and on the system, the design, and the architecture, before I go further.

The shape I followed: the watch does not hold server credentials, prompts go through the iPhone, and the original request is a voice loop rather than Kanban, tasks, skills, memory, projects, or profile switching.

I built this on current master. The branch is local only, `issue/575-hermes-watch`, commits `ee22e24` and `f1a1cf6`. Nothing is pushed.

The watch never opens HTTP and never holds a server URL, token, or credential. It talks to the iPhone over WatchConnectivity. The iPhone uses the existing Hermes gateway. If that session's chat is already open, send and stop go through `HermesChatTurnCoordinator`. Otherwise the phone joins the same `HermesConnection`. That is not a second WebSocket.

Hermes calls I used: `prompt.submit` to send, `file.attach` for files, the HermesREST image upload, and `session.interrupt` to stop, including a phone-started run when `session.active_list` has a runtime id. Transcription is `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. The phone can also read the session list and call `session.new`. Legacy webui still uses its old send path. On-device transcription runs only when Speech is already authorized. There is no permission prompt from the watch relay.

On the wrist, Now has type, speak, photo, listen, and Stop when the phone can cancel. A clarification shows the question and the reply controls. An approval is Open on iPhone only. I do not approve or deny on the watch. Speak has Cancel before send. A finished reply can notify the watch. Read aloud does not send.

title: fix(hermes): let the agent send images and files into Hermes chats
body:
**What the user gets:** Asking the agent for an image or file in a Hermes chat or a bot chat puts it in the transcript instead of a filesystem path.
**Why it matters:** A user reported it, and it reproduces on the latest Branch TestFlight in both a bot chat and a regular session. The agent answers "this is the TUI, so there's no attachment channel — MEDIA: tags print as literal text" and replies with a path, even though Hermex has rendered `MEDIA:` replies since #1143.
**Cost:** Small. One PR. Simulator plus one phone check.

## Cause

The host picks the agent's per-surface system-prompt note from the session's `source`. Hermex never sends one, so `_resolve_session_platform()` falls back to `"tui"`. The `tui` note says `MEDIA:` is not intercepted and tells the agent to state a path (`agent/prompt_builder.py` `PLATFORM_HINTS["tui"]`, pin `ca678285`).

## Contract (pin `ca678285`, same on the live host)

- `session.create` and `session.resume` take `source: str | None` (`tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py` `SessionCreateParams`, `SessionResumeParams`). The host stamps it on the runtime and builds the agent with `platform_override=source` (`methods_session.py` `_new_runtime_ids`, `_resume_eager`). Params are `extra="forbid"`, so the key must exist on every host Hermex accepts (minimum `0.21.3`).
- An unknown platform key has no built-in note (`agent/system_prompt.py` `_default_platform_hint`).
- `platform_hints.<platform>` in a Profile's `config.yaml` adds a note for any platform key: `{append}` or `{replace}`, and a bare string means append (`_resolve_platform_hint`, read in `agent/agent_init.py`). `PUT /api/config?profile=` deep-merges the body over the file on disk (`hermes_cli/web_routers/config_env.py` `update_config`).

## Plan

- [ ] Send `source: "hermex"` on `session.create` (Bot Chat mint and plain sessions) and `session.resume`. The false `tui` note goes away for new chats and for every resumed one.
- [ ] Before a Profile's first session call, make sure that Profile's config has `platform_hints.hermex`, which tells the agent that Hermex renders Markdown and shows `MEDIA:/absolute/path` images, audio, video and files inline. Write it only when the key is absent, so a user's edit or an empty opt-out survives.

## Decisions

- Not `source: "desktop"`. It would bring the Desktop note, but also Desktop's preview tools and `::preview` widgets (which Hermex can't render), launch-folder handling, liveness tracking and `omit_messages` resume behavior, which Hermex's reconnect relies on.
- Not a note added to each message: it would be stored in the transcript and show in titles, other clients, copy and edit.
- Cost of a custom source: the host refreshes MCP tools between turns only for `tui` and `desktop`, so a tool toggled mid-chat applies when the chat is next opened.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On `scripts/local-hermes`, "send me any image from my machine" in a new chat and in a resumed bot chat returns a `MEDIA:` reply that renders inline.
- [ ] A Profile whose config already has `platform_hints.hermex` is left unchanged.
- [ ] webui is unchanged.

## Tests

`HermesCall` params for `session.create` and `session.resume` include `source`; the config write happens only when the key is absent.

title: fix(hermes): let the agent send images and files into Hermes chats
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1278

## What changed

Agents in Hermes chats and bot chats refused to send images. They replied with a host path because the host treated every Hermex session as its terminal UI. That surface's system-prompt note says `MEDIA:` tags print as plain text. Hermex never named a surface, so the host fell back to the terminal one.

- `session.create` and `session.resume` now send `source: "hermex"`. The host then drops the terminal note for new chats and for resumed ones.
- Before the first attach to a Profile, and before a new bot's chat is made, Hermex reads that Profile's config. When `platform_hints.hermex.append` is missing or differs, Hermex writes a short note there. The note tells the agent to send files as `MEDIA:/absolute/path` and says what the chat shows for each kind of file. The host's `PUT /api/config` merges this key into the file and leaves the rest as it is.
- `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` explains the surface note.

**Tradeoffs.** I did not send `source: "desktop"`. That brings Desktop's preview tools, `::preview` widgets and liveness tracking, which Hermex can't serve. I did not add the note to each message either, because it would be saved in the transcript, titles and other clients.

**Blast radius.** Every Hermes session call carries the new key. The host has accepted `source` since 0.21.3 (checked at the first 0.21.4 canary), and it rejects unknown keys, so I checked this first. The config write touches one key in each Profile's `config.yaml`, once. A runtime the host built before this change keeps the old note until the host reaps it. webui is unchanged.

## How it was tested

- **Before the fix, on the live host (read-only).** The two sessions from the report are stored with `source = tui`. The agent's reply quotes the terminal note.
- **After the fix, in the app on the simulator, against `scripts/local-hermes` at the pin (with a stub model that logs the prompts it receives).** I opened a new session and sent "Send me any image from my machine". The system prompt the model received:
  - contains the Hermex note.
  - no longer contains the terminal note.
  - The session row is stored with `source = hermex`.
  - The Profile's `config.yaml` gained `platform_hints.hermex` and kept every other key.

title: fix(hermes): send custom headers to the browser sign-in page
body:
Browser sign-in opens `/auth/native/authorize` in an ephemeral `WebAuthenticationSession` with `additionalHeaderFields: [:]` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesBrowserSignIn.swift`, from #1248). A Hermes host behind a Cloudflare Access policy that admits only a service token (no interactive Access login) detects fine with the server's custom headers, but its authorize page is blocked, so browser sign-in can't finish.

This applies to every browser sign-in entry point (Add Server, re-sign-in, and since #1271 the Move to Hermes sign-in). Raised by Greptile on #1271: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1271#discussion_r4285096858

Open question before implementing: `additionalHeaderFields` covers only the first request, so redirects and page loads inside the sheet may still lack the headers. Verify against a service-token-only Access app before choosing a fix.

title: run Hermes plugin slash commands in Hermex
body:
### Use case

Hi,

Thanks for Hermex! I use it every day with my self-hosted Hermes Agent and hermes-webui. Here’s a feature request.

Hermes plugins can register their own slash commands (ctx.register_command(...)). They give you actions that run directly, without the model, which matters for anything that has to be reliable. For example, I use a /bs command to log health readings. With a small local model (Gemma 4 12B via oMLX), letting the model call a tool to log data was unreliable: it often skipped the tool or claimed it had saved data when it hadn’t. The plugin command fixes that, because it runs a script and shows the actual result.

Today in Hermex:

Plugin commands show up in the slash autocomplete (thanks to #1036).
But sending one, for example /bs help, passes it to the model as ordinary chat text. The plugin never runs, and the model replies that it doesn’t know the command.
The same command works in the hermes-webui web page and over the Hermes iMessage gateway, so Hermex is currently the only place where it doesn’t.

### Proposed behavior

When the user sends a message that starts with / and the command name matches an entry from GET /api/commands with "category": "Plugin":

Don’t start a model run.
Call POST /api/commands/exec with {"command": "<full message text>"}, for example {"command": "/bs 160 before 18:30"}.
Show the user’s message in the chat, then show the returned output as the reply, as plain or monospace text.
If the call fails, show the error in the chat, for example “Plugin command error: …”, and don’t fall back to sending the text to the model.
Everything else stays the same: normal messages, built-in commands Hermex already handles, and text that doesn’t match any plugin command.

### Acceptance outcomes

The plugin runs without the model. With a test plugin registered, sending /hello world shows hello world as the reply, and the server log shows POST /api/commands/exec and no /api/chat/start for that message.

Arguments pass through intact. Everything after the command name reaches the plugin unchanged, including spaces, numbers, decimals and times like 6:30pm.

Autocomplete flows into it. Picking a plugin command from autocomplete, typing arguments and sending runs it.

Errors are visible, not silent. If the plugin raises an error or /api/commands/exec fails, the user sees an error message and the text is not sent to the model.

Nothing else changes. Non-plugin messages, built-in commands and unknown slash text behave as before.

It works with WebUI password auth enabled.

Test plugin to reproduce:

1) Create: ~/.hermes/plugins/hello/plugin.yaml containing name: hello and version: 0.1.0.
2) Create: ~/.hermes/plugins/hello/__init__.py containing:
3) Run hermes plugins enable hello and restart hermes-webui.
4) In the WebUI web page, /hello world replies “hello world”. In Hermex, the same text currently goes to the model.


### Upstream dependency notes

No server changes are needed. hermes-webui already provides everything:
  
 - GET /api/commands, which lists plugin commands with category: "Plugin", plus name, description and args_hint
 - POST /api/commands/exec {"command": "..."}, which returns {"output": "..."}. It tries agent commands first, then plugin commands, and returns 404 if the command is unknown.

The reference behavior is the WebUI web page: static/messages.js (the slash intercept in send()) and api/commands.py (list_commands, execute_plugin_command). Hermex would just mirror that client-side routing.

Plugin output is plain text and may contain characters like < or >. It’s best displayed as plain text, not rendered as Markdown or HTML.

The plugin list is loaded when the server starts. A newly enabled plugin appears after hermes-webui restarts, so refreshing the command list when a chat opens, rather than once per app launch, would pick up changes sooner.

Tested with: hermes-webui latest master as of Oct 15, 2026 (commit dc9b36b), Hermes Agent with a local Gemma 4 12B via oMLX, WebUI accessed over Tailscale, Hermex version [1.9].
Thanks!

title: fix(networking): stop a redirect from carrying a sign-in password to another host
body:
## Linked issue

No public issue: reported privately.

## What changed

When a server answered the password login with a 307 or 308 redirect to another origin, URLSession resent the POST and its body (the password) there. Hermex only noticed and showed "blocked" after the request had already gone out. A misconfigured or compromised proxy, tunnel or redirect rule in front of the host could collect the password that way. The same applied to the webui login and any other request with a body.

The shared redirect guard (`CrossOriginHeaderStripper`) now refuses a cross-origin redirect of anything but GET or HEAD, so the body never leaves the origin. Same-origin redirects, such as a proxy's trailing-slash 307, still go through. A 302 or 303 already turns the request into a bodiless GET, which is still followed with custom headers stripped. On a Hermes server, the refused redirect's 3xx reply ends sign-in as `.blocked`, the same error a redirect to another host already gave.

Checked on Foundation with two local listeners and synthetic data: a 307 or 308 delivers the POST body to the second origin, a 302 sends an empty GET, and refusing the redirect returns the 3xx with the original URL.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only` CrossOriginRedirectHeaderTests, HermesConnectionTests, CustomHeaderInjectionTests, BotClientTests, BotConnectionVersionTests, HermesBrowserSignInTests, HermesGatewayTests: 97 tests, 0 failures.
- New: `testRefusesCrossOriginRedirectOfARequestWithABody`, `testFollowsSameOriginRedirectOfARequestWithABody`, `testALoginRedirectedToAnotherOriginNeverSendsThePassword`. With the production change reverted, the two refusal tests fail.
- `HermesHostFixture`'s `.redirect` now keeps the request method and finishes with the 3xx, so a refused redirect completes as it does on the wire.

title: fix(chat): open the continuation when a compressed webui session rejects a send
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1109.

## What changed

After a webui server compresses a session, it rejects every new send to it with a `409 session_rotated`, and the app showed that as an error every time. Now the app opens the session's continuation on the same server and Profile, and the unsent message (text, quotes, attachments) moves to that composer without being resent automatically.

This continues @rheo-bot's [#1110](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1110). Their commit is unchanged apart from the rebase, and their authorship is kept. On top of it is one fix, `c06e97c4`. In #1110, leaving the chat bumped the send generation. That meant an ordinary webui send whose POST returned after you opened Files (or any pushed view) dropped its stream, and going Back showed your message with no live reply while the server kept working. Navigation no longer invalidates an accepted send. Rotation recovery still won't navigate after you've left, because `ChatView` checks that it's on screen before moving the draft.

A third commit, `2d56916b`, fixes Greptile's P1. If the continuation lookup failed after the 409, the chat kept its "rotated" state with no continuation, so every later Send stopped at the guard and the draft was stuck until you left the chat. The app now keeps the continuation ID, and the next Send retries only the lookup. It never posts the message again. `88e76525` keeps Send off while that retry runs, as the first load already does, so a second Send can't race it and leave part of the draft behind (Greptile's follow-up P1).

Contract: the `session_rotated` 409 and `continuation_session_id` (nullable) are in hermes-webui `api/routes.py`. They were added on 2026-09-20, after `UPSTREAM_TESTED_SHA`, and older servers never send them. Hermes chats return before the new code.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientAuthAndErrorTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatDraftStoreTests`: 312 passed, 0 failed, on #1110's head and again after the fix.
- `c06e97c4` flips one test to assert that an accepted send attaches its stream after navigation, and narrows another to the cancelled-task cases.
- #1110's full-suite fork CI passed (4,013 tests). PR CI on this branch is the full-suite gate.
- Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with GPT-6.1 Sol. Sol verdict: approved. Round 1 found the navigation bug above.

- `testSendAfterFailedContinuationLoadRetriesGETWithoutReplay` covers `2d56916b`. It also checks that Send stays off during the retry, and it fails without either fix. `ChatViewModelSendTests` and `ChatDraftStoreTests` pass: 292 tests.

Simulator, against the live webui (iPhone 17, build `2d56916b`):
- Send, open Files within about 1 s, go Back: passed 3 of 3. Twice the reply was still streaming, and once it had finished. It showed exactly once each time, and the server agreed.
- That pass doesn't prove the race this PR fixes. On the simulator's LAN path the POST returns before the Files tap lands, and #1110's original commit (431ed8e7) passed the same steps. The unit tests are the evidence for it.
- The compressed-session path wasn't run. The live webui is v0.52.113, and `session_rotated` first shipped in v0.52.458.

title: chore(deps): bump swift-eventsource to 3.4.0 and ignore its close after a finished run
body:
## Linked issue

Replaces Dependabot's #1111 (no issue).

## What changed

LDSwiftEventSource 3.4.0 (launchdarkly/swift-eventsource#118) now reports a clean server or tunnel close to the error handler, where it used to reconnect silently. A webui server closes the socket right after a `cancel` or `error` event. On the bare bump, that close reaches the chat as a late transport error after the run has finished. In `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests` it replaces a server error's message with "stream closed by server". In the app, a stop showed no error even on the bare bump (checked in the simulator), so this guard prevents a state bug rather than a visible one on that path.

This branch is Dependabot's bump (`98315189`, unchanged) plus one guard (`3ee08532`): `ChatStreamCoordinator.handleTransportError` ignores transport errors once the run has finished. `start` and session-load reconciliation reset that flag, so live, reconnected and replayed runs still get their errors.

The rest of 3.4.0 is unchanged for us: no backoff, header, URLSession, threading or minimum-OS changes. Only webui streams use this library; Hermes streams over websockets. Other effects of the new close reporting are as designed:
- A chat dropped mid-run now goes through the app's own status check and `replayAfterSeq` resume.
- Approval and clarify streams switch to fallback polling.
- Kanban gets exactly one `onFailure`.
- A btw side question now ends with an error on a mid-answer close, as it already does for an erroring drop. The old silent reconnect couldn't resume it correctly anyway, because `/api/chat/stream` ignores `Last-Event-ID`.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatStreamCoordinatorTests --only HermesMobileTests/SSEClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanEventStreamClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamReconnectContractTests`: 127 passed, 0 failed.
- New tests:
  - A late close after an error and after a cancel. This fails on the bare bump with `["server failed", "stream closed by server"]`.
  - A clean server close reaches the chat as `.transportError`.
- Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with GPT-6.1 Sol. Sol verdict: approved.

Simulator, against the live webui (iPhone 17, build `3ee08532`):
- Stopped a running reply 3 times: no error on screen, the composer returned to Send, and the server showed no stuck stream.
- Backgrounded the app for 60 s mid-reply: it reattached at "Working for 1m 15s" and showed the reply once.
- Held a reply open for 130 s: it finished once, with no error. This went over the LAN path, not necessarily through Cloudflare.
- Not run:
  - A server `error` event: the live webui falls back to a working model when given a bogus one.
  - Kanban: the live webui's board route returns HTTP 500.

title: Trim the XCTest suite to tests that catch real breaks
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing visible. Agents ship slices faster, with fewer false CI failures and reruns.
**Why it matters:** Uzair asked for an audit (2026-10-16). Tests went from 1,413 to 4,345 in three months and are now 78% the size of the app code. Of 117 CI test failures in about 8 weeks, existing tests caught only 2 real regressions; 41% were flakes and 47% were the test harness itself breaking.
**Cost:** Medium. Agent-only, no phone needed.

## Rule

A test earns its place only if it fails when the code breaks in a way that matters to a user.

## Plan

1. Delete the ~850 tests the audit marked (per-file lists in the comments below). Each deletion either names the test that already covers the same thing or says why it can't catch a real break.
2. Cut `BotChatPresentationTests` down to its ~10–14 behavior tests. It has 30 tests but caused 44 of the 117 CI failures and about 20% of measured test time.
3. Fix rather than delete:
   - the 25 MB preview-cap fixtures
   - the real-clock wait in `HermesHistoryRewindTests`
   - the `waitUntil`, sleep and yield polling helpers
   - the tests that assume concurrent tasks start in order
4. Merge copy-pasted setup: inline JSON in `ChatViewModelSendTests`, the fake Hermes hosts in MoveToHermes, and the duplicate fake keychains.
5. Stop it growing back: put the rule above into AGENTS.md and drop "pass N times in a row" acceptance criteria.

## CI impact

The suite gets about 20% smaller, but CI saves only 30–45 seconds of a roughly 12-minute job. Tests grew 2.7× while the test step grew 17%, because about 60% of the test step is simulator and Xcode overhead. The real CI gain is fewer flake reruns, which a September audit found used 22% of CI's macOS time.

## Keep

The two tests that caught real regressions, `ComposerFocusTransitionTests.testBoundBlurDuringAPopCancelsDeferredFocus` and `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests.testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesAndRouteThroughTheLatestHandler`, stay.

Wire contracts, stream reconnect and replay, multi-server isolation, optimistic rollback, persistence and migrations, credential safety, and draft-loss tests also stay.

title: bug(chat): relaunched app lands high in the thread, not at last-read — restore shows wrong context on cold start
body:
FILED FOR LATER — not scheduled. Do not pick up without Chris's word.

**What the user gets:** relaunching the app returns to the thread but scrolled well above where the conversation last left off, so the first thing on screen is old, contextless messages and he must scroll down to find the real tail.

**Why it matters:** Chris's report (16 Oct, voice): "it seems to be way up high inside a different chain of messages and I have to spend time scrolling; I start reading stuff that isn't making sense for where we last left off... it's somehow forgetting where we last left off."

**Cost:** Unknown until re-triaged — do NOT assume Small. The same family (jump/stall/restore) burned many rounds in early Oct and shipped as fixed in 0.12.42 (campaign closed on the cache-wipe + per-width height-set findings). If this is a regression it is NEW evidence, not confirmation of the old mechanism — grep a FRESH device log before reusing any carried-over diagnosis.

**Evidence in hand (do not re-capture):**
- Restore-path reading logs pushed 16 Oct are already on the Studio at `~/.local/share/field-agent/evidence/iPhone/20261016T042212Z/` (four files, launch 2026-10-16T04:19:35Z).
- The 04:19 launch log shows restore LANDED at `target=14662238208 reason=two-passes` with `rows=0->100` and readUpTo == the anchor — i.e. the restore machinery claims it hit the intended anchor on that launch.
- Suspect class: the ANCHOR itself (what was persisted as last-read, or persisted per-thread vs per-chat scope — note the launch log's restore ran with a thread chip armed and an active thread context), or the 0.12.42 height-set machinery interacting with relaunch-with-backlog (a device-only path the gate cannot reproduce — per the 11 Oct lesson).
- First step when triaged: get a NEW reading log from a reproduction on the CURRENT build, and compare `restore phase pending(anchor:)` against what the user actually read last. If the anchor is correct and landing still shows the wrong rows, it is the landing/height machinery; if the anchor is stale, it is the persistence scope.

Related: the mid-conversation RESET lines in the field-agent server log (16 Oct 01:09, 16:23) are a separate server-side phenomenon — only relevant if the repro shows session churn around the bad restore.

title: feat(push): Apple notifications as the primary nudge — relay delivers reply alerts, Telegram DM muted
body:
**What the user gets:** his phone buzzes through Apple's native notification system for my replies, instead of Telegram's pings he has to keep dismissing.

**Why it matters:** Chris's pre-trip wish (17 Oct, voice): 'enable proper Apple notifications so I don't have to keep being triggered by the Telegram notifications.' The Hermex push relay (APNs, end-to-end encrypted, ciphertext-only relay) already exists and is paired; the gap is that reply delivery still rides Telegram, so Telegram pings remain the only nudge.

**Cost:** Medium. Server-side: the gateway's reply-completion path also fires a relay push when the app is paired and Telegram delivery is the transport (replaces the Telegram ping as the nudge; Telegram messages still arrive for history). Client-side: verify the notification-service extension renders the local notification from the relay payload (decrypt + post). User-side: mute the Telegram DM once the relay nudges are confirmed working.

**Design notes:**
- The relay only ever sees ciphertext (standing architecture).
- Dedup: when the app is foreground-active, no push needed (the app already renders the reply live).
- Do not break the existing relay paths (job/cron alerts) — this extends the same pipeline to reply-completion events.
- Sequencing (Chris, 17 Oct): after issue #1292. The Telegram-DM mute is the user's final step, not part of the build.

title: feat(hermes): add the host terminal screen
body:
## Linked issue

None. Needs uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#29 on the host; without it the Terminal button stays hidden.

## What changed

Adds a plain host shell to direct-Hermes chats. Webui chats are unchanged.

- A Terminal button in the chat toolbar (⌘⇧T) opens a full-screen SwiftTerm view in the chat's folder. It only shows when the chat is connected and the companion's capabilities list `GET /terminal/shell/status`, and it's disabled while the chat shows cached data. Settings > Composer gets a Terminal Button toggle next to Git Actions.
- The screen has a native inline nav bar with the folder as subtitle, Done (⌘W), and a menu with Restart Shell, Copy All Output and Paste. It uses the app's code-block colors and SwiftTerm's own keyboard accessory. A status bar only appears while reconnecting or after the shell ends; an ended shell gets a Restart button.
- Pinch zoom sets the terminal font from 9 to 20 pt (default 12) and is remembered. The terminal cells don't follow Dynamic Type; the nav bar and status text do.
- Done only closes the socket. The shell keeps running on the host, and reopening replays its recent output. If the shell is gone when you reopen, the app says "Previous session ended, new shell started". The socket closes when the app goes to the background and reconnects when it comes back. If the app retires the Hermes connection, the screen closes.
- Tapping an http(s) link in the output opens it. Other schemes are ignored.
- 17 new strings in all 17 catalog locales. SwiftTerm 1.18.0 is pinned and its license added to the third-party notices. Both CI workflows (PR checks and the release build) get one new step, `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`. SwiftTerm compiles a Metal shader as part of the app build (`Sources/SwiftTerm/Apple/Metal/Shaders.metal`), and since Xcode 26 the Metal compiler is a separate download that GitHub's runners don't have. The app itself doesn't change. If SwiftTerm isn't added, this step isn't needed either.

## How it was tested

- Focused terminal and catalog tests: 146 passed, none failed or skipped.
- After the review fixes (7c12748, 3bb18e1): focused terminal, catalog and chat-attachment tests, 184 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The new tests failed before the fix. In the simulator, dropping the connection during `sleep` shows Reconnect and Restart; Reconnect returned to the same shell with the command still running, Restart started a new one, and the Terminal button stayed after backgrounding with the network down.
- Two native UI runs on a signed simulator build against a disposable dashboard (driver not part of this PR), both passed: chat → terminal → pwd/ls → Vim open/quit → pinch → leave/return → exit → Restart, and the largest accessibility text size with a 20 pt terminal.
- Full suite: 4,360 passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped. The failure is `testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesWhileTheKeyboardIsUp` timing out on the keyboard notification. It fails the same way on `master` (4,334 passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped) and in isolated runs on both branches. I didn't disable or loosen any test, so this gate isn't green.

Known limits:

- Replay is the raw byte tail. If the column width changed since the output was written, for example after a pinch, zsh's end-of-line `%` markers can show up and an old long command line can lose characters. You can see the markers in the replay screenshot below.
- Coming back from the background reconnects without checking status first, so a shell that died meanwhile is replaced by a new one without the notice.
- Not tested on a physical device, over a tunnel, with a hardware keyboard, or with a real clipboard round trip.

Chat, before and after:

title: Hermes session writes fail on hermes-agent main: missing request_id and expected_revision
body:
**What the user gets:** pin, archive, unread, rename, restore, duplicate and Move to Hermes keep working on Hermes hosts built from `hermes-agent` main.
**Why it matters:** main now refuses session writes that do not carry a write identity (409 `client_upgrade_required`). The next release will ship this check, and every one of those actions will fail.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed beyond a final check.

## The contract (hermes-agent main, verified at 18c525b669b6)

- `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` and `POST /api/sessions/import` need `request_id` and `expected_revision` (`hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py` `_mutate_session_request`). No identity at all gets 409 `client_upgrade_required: ...` (3cdcd412d47a). A partial identity gets 409 `mutation_identity_required`.
- The host compares `expected_revision` to the row's `runtime_revision` and answers 409 `revision_conflict` on a mismatch. `runtime_revision` moves on every durable worker receipt, so the value on a cached list row goes stale as soon as the session has any activity.
- `GET /api/sessions/{id}/mutation-snapshot?profile=` returns `{exists, runtime_revision, runtime_generation}`. Desktop reads it right before each write (`apps/shared/src/session-http-mutations.ts`). The pinned 0.21.5 host has no such route and answers 404 `No such API endpoint`.
- `expected_generation` is optional for sidebar edits and imports. An import whose anchor (`sessions[0].id`) is absent has revision 0.
- RPCs are not fenced. Delete goes through `session.delete`, so it is unaffected. Stable v0.22.2 is not fenced either.

## Plan

1. PATCH: read the snapshot, then send a fresh `request_id` and the snapshot's `runtime_revision`. A 404 with the catch-all body means an older host, so send the PATCH as today. On 409 `revision_conflict`, do not resend: the caller rolls back and reloads, and the user retries. Map `client_upgrade_required` and `mutation_identity_required` to an "update Hermex" message.
2. Import: send a fresh `request_id` and `expected_revision: 0`, since both callers import into an id the host does not have. Move to Hermes treats a 409 as uncertain, not rejected.
3. Follow-up PR: send `confirm_deep_truncate` on a rewind only after the user confirms discarding later turns (Edit and Regenerate), never on Retry. Handle 4033. It is warn-only on main today (`DEEP_TRUNCATE_ENFORCED = False`).

Validate against `scripts/local-hermes` at a main commit as well as the pinned host.

title: fix(hermes): send a write identity on session edits and imports
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1300

## What changed

hermes-agent main refuses REST session writes that carry no write identity. It answers 409 `client_upgrade_required`, so on those hosts pin, archive, unread, rename, restore, duplicate and Move to Hermes all fail.

- A session PATCH reads `GET /api/sessions/{id}/mutation-snapshot` first, then sends a fresh `request_id` and that `runtime_revision`. The revision moves on every turn, so a cached list row can't supply it.
- An import sends a fresh `request_id` and `expected_revision: 0`. Both callers import into an id the host does not have yet.
- A fence 409 becomes `HermesSessionFenceRefusal` and is never resent. Row actions already roll back and reload. Move to Hermes reports a busy or upgrade refusal, and leaves a stale-revision write for its next run.
- Older hosts keep working. When the snapshot route answers a catch-all 404 (`hermes dashboard` or headless `hermes serve`), the PATCH goes out as before. Older hosts ignore the extra import fields.

Out of scope: `confirm_deep_truncate` on rewinds. It gets its own PR, and main still only warns.

Tradeoff: every session edit makes one more round trip for the snapshot read. Desktop does the same.

## How it was tested

- Focused XCTest on iPhone 17 (`scripts/test-sim E65FD38D-… --only` APIClientSessionMutationTests, HermesRequestTests, BotClientTests, MoveToHermesTransferTests, MoveToHermesRunnerTests, MoveToHermesReconcileTests, HermesBranchDuplicateTests, HermesSessionListTests, HermesSessionActionsTests, APIClientSessionListTests, HermesConnectionTests, HermexPushPairingTests): 206 passed. title: fix(chat): confirm a deep rewind when the host asks
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #1300 (the rewind half, after #1301).

## What changed

hermes-agent main can refuse a rewind (Edit, Regenerate, `/retry`) whose cut drops later prompts until the client sends `confirm_deep_truncate` (error 4033). It only warns today, and its next release enforces it. Older hosts, including the 0.21.5 we pin, refuse the key itself with 4000, because their RPC params forbid unknown fields. So the flag can't simply always be sent.

- A rewind goes out without the flag. On a 4033, it goes again with `confirm_deep_truncate: true`, but only when the chat already asked the user to discard later messages ("Discard Later Messages?"). That's any cut with a later prompt.

title: fix(chat): composer crashes while dictating
body:
**What the user gets:** Dictating into the composer no longer crashes the app.
**Why it matters:** A TestFlight tester on Hermex 2.0 (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 27.0.1) crashed while dictating with the keyboard microphone.
**Cost:** Small. The final check needs a physical iPhone, because dictation does not run on the simulator.

## Crash

`EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)` on the main thread. The run loop's undo observer throws:

```
-[NSUndoManager _endUndoGroupRemovingIfEmpty:]
__NSFirePerformWithOrder
__CFRunLoopDoObservers
```

## Cause

`ComposerChipTextView.render` replaces the whole document and then calls `undoManager?.removeAllActions()`. This clear also resets the undo manager's grouping level to 0.

Dictation keeps its own undo group open across insertions. If the composer re-renders inside that group, the clear removes the group. Then dictation closes its group, and the run loop tries to close the event group. That close has no matching begin, and Foundation throws `NSInternalInconsistencyException` ("endUndoGrouping called with no matching begin").

A standalone Foundation program reproduces the same exception from the same frames: begin a group, register an undo, call `removeAllActions`, register again, end the group, and let the run loop turn. The same clear during normal typing, where only the event group is open, does not throw. That is why only dictation crashes.

## Fix

Clear the undo history only when no undo group is open. When a group is open, wait until it closes and clear then.

## Open question

The path that re-renders during dictation is not confirmed. The likely one is the marked-text branch of `applyBoundText`, which treats any out-of-date, non-empty draft as a deliberate replacement. Dictation does not run on the simulator, so check this on a device before changing that branch.

title: fix(chat): keep dictation's undo group open when the composer redraws
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1303

## What changed

A TestFlight tester's app crashed while they dictated into the composer. When the composer rebuilds its document, it clears the undo stack. That clear also drops any undo group that is still open. Dictation keeps one open, so the group's later close had no matching begin, and UIKit aborted the app.

- `ComposerChipTextView` now clears the undo stack at once only when no undo group is open. If a group is open, it waits until the last group closes and clears then.
- A new test opens a group the way dictation does, redraws a chip inside it, and checks two things. The group stays open, and the stale undo is gone after the group closes.

This PR does not change the path that redraws during dictation. That path is not confirmed, and dictation does not run on the simulator (see #1303).

title: feat(chat): support collapsible details, expandable blockquotes, and spoiler text
body:
**What the user gets:** Native interactive disclosure cards for `<details>`, expandable blockquotes with line-height clamping, and tap-to-reveal spoiler masking in chat messages.
**Why it matters:** Hermes agent responses (and bridged Telegram/WebUI turns) increasingly deliver structured tool traces, secondary logs, and sensitive tokens using interactive formatting. In Hermex, these either degrade into raw unparsed HTML/markdown delimiters or dump unbounded vertical text into message bubbles without collapse affordances.
**Cost:** Medium. Client-only (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/`), touching `MarkdownRenderer`, segmented layout caching, and theme blockquote styling. Requires manual simulator testing on `iPhone 17` (`needs-manual-validation`) to ensure scrolling stability with `chatDisclosureToggled`.

---

### Context & Problem Statement

Hermex renders markdown transcripts via `MarkdownUI` (`swift-markdown-ui` 2.4.1) backed by `cmark-gfm`. Because CommonMark does not specify interactive extensions:

1. **HTML Disclosure Blocks (`<details><summary>`)**:
   - `cmark-gfm` treats `<details>` and `<summary>` as raw HTML blocks or inline tags.
   - Long diagnostics or multi-step execution logs cannot be folded, creating excessive vertical scrolling on mobile viewports.

2. **Expandable Blockquotes (`**>**` / Telegram Bot API 7.3+)**:
   - Telegram uses `**>** ` prefixes for expandable quotes. CommonMark parses `**>**` as broken, unclosed strong emphasis, distorting subsequent text.
   - Standard blockquotes in Hermex inherit GitHub theme styling without length clamping or collapse controls.

3. **Inline Spoiler Delimiters (`||text||` / `<tg-spoiler>`)**:
   - Spoilers are rendered literally as pipe characters (`||`) without masking.

### Proposed Architecture & Changes

#### 1. Segmented `<details>` Block Rendering
- **Segmentation**: Extend `MarkdownMathSegmenter` (or implement `MarkdownDisclosureSegmenter`) to detect matched `<details><summary>Title</summary>Body</details>` blocks outside protected code fences.
- **Data Model**:
  ```swift
  enum MarkdownBlockSegment: Equatable {
      case markdown(String)
      case displayMath(String)
      case details(summary: String, content: String)
  }
  ```
- **View Implementation**: Render disclosure sections using a dedicated SwiftUI card with chevron indicators, invoking `@Environment(\.chatDisclosureToggled)` on toggle to pin reader scroll offsets and prevent scroll hitching.

#### 2. Expandable Blockquotes (`**>**` & Long Quotes)
- **Preprocessing**: Normalize leading `**>** ` markers to standard quote syntax with an expandable metadata indicator during tokenizer passes.
- **Theme Configuration**: Add an explicit `.blockquote` handler to `MarkdownUI.Theme.chat` (currently unconfigured) with:
  - An accent-colored vertical indicator line (`Capsule`, width: 3).
  - Configurable line limit (default: 4 lines) for settled quotes.
  - A subtle "Show all (N) lines" / "Collapse" control invoking `chatDisclosureToggled()`, matching the behavior of `MarkdownDiffCodeBlock`.

#### 3. Inline Spoiler Masking (`||...||` & `<tg-spoiler>`)
- **Masking Pass**: In `MarkdownMathFormatter` (or companion inline scanner), parse paired `||` and `<tg-spoiler>` tags outside of fenced and inline code blocks (`MarkdownMathProtection.mask`).
- **Interactive Mask View**: Render obscured text behind a frosted/blurred pill (`.blur(radius: 6)`) with `accessibilityHidden` when concealed.
- **Interaction**: Tap gesture toggles reveal state with a spring animation and light haptic feedback (`ChatHaptics`).

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `<details><summary>` blocks render as collapsed disclosure cards by default; tapping expands nested markdown cleanly.
- [ ] Toggling disclosure states (details or quotes) does not cause scroll jumping or viewport disorientation in the transcript.
- [ ] Telegram-style `**>**` quotes and long standard blockquotes clamp at 4 lines with interactive expand/collapse toggles.
- [ ] `||text||` and `<tg-spoiler>` display as obscured text until tapped by the user.
- [ ] Zero new third-party Swift package dependencies (pure Apple SDK + existing `swift-markdown-ui`).
- [ ] Uncached layout passes on streaming replies remain lightweight with zero unnecessary re-tokenization.

### Upstream Parity & Dependencies

Purely client-side presentation parity. No changes to server-side wire models, endpoints, or SSE event protocols.

title: feat(security): allow manual/pinned companion plugin installation and disable remote updates
body:
## Security/privacy request

I use Hermex with a self-hosted Hermes agent and want the ability to run the iOS client without allowing it to install or update executable code on my Hermes host from a moving GitHub branch.

### Current behavior

From the current code:
- `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushPairing.swift` defines `https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push.git/plugin` as the installation source, without a pinned commit.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift` can install and enable the plugin as part of **user-confirmed** push setup, and the update action reinstalls it from `main`.
- The companion plugin runs within the Hermes environment and registers hooks for model/tool activity. This makes the integrity of the fetched plugin code security-sensitive.

I understand push is optional and setup is already explicitly initiated by the user. My request is specifically for finer control over **remote code installation and updates**.

### Requested behavior

1. Add a clear setting/policy such as **"Never install or update plugins automatically/from the iPhone"**. The app should be able to use an existing, manually installed companion plugin without reinstalling it, and should gracefully disable unsupported companion features.
2. Keep **install**, **update**, **enable/disable**, and **restart** actions explicitly separated, with advance notice of what changes on the host. Do not silently re-enable remote installation via another feature.
3. Allow the plugin source to be pinned to an immutable release/commit (ideally with integrity verification), rather than always fetching from `main`.
4. Document a manual, reproducible installation and update method for operators who audit the source code first.

### Questions

- Is there already a supported way to disable all iPhone-triggered plugin installs/updates while retaining the rest of the Hermex client?
- Can an operator permanently opt out of remote plugin code installation, including when new companion features are added?
- Would you consider pinned plugin versions/SHAs and an optional **manual installation only** mode?

This is a defense-in-depth/supply-chain hardening request, **not an allegation that Hermex or hermex-push contains a backdoor**.

References:
- https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/master/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushPairing.swift
- https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/master/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushProvisioner.swift
- https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push/blob/main/plugin/plugin.yaml

title: feat(privacy): support a fully local/self-hosted push relay with no third-party relay dependency
body:
## Privacy/self-hosting request

I self-host my Hermes agent and would prefer to keep as much of its supporting infrastructure under my own control as possible, including push notifications.

### Current behavior

- Hermex uses `https://hermex-relay.hermex-relay.workers.dev` by default when provisioning push.
- The host can override this through `HERMEX_PUSH_RELAY_URL`, and the relay source is publicly available in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push/relay`.
- The existing self-hosting implementation appears to target Cloudflare Workers/KV/Durable Objects, rather than a straightforward local Docker deployment.
- Notification previews are AES-256-GCM encrypted on the host. However, the relay still processes APNs device tokens and routing/activity metadata, including raw session IDs, timestamps, notification types/sources and some progress/tool metadata.

### Requested behavior

1. Provide a **fully self-hosted relay option on a local server/NAS**, preferably with an officially maintained Docker image and `docker-compose.yml`, with no Cloudflare account or managed relay required.
2. Make choosing **the default hosted relay vs. a custom self-hosted relay vs. push disabled** explicit during setup. Ideally allow entering a custom relay URL in Hermex Settings instead of having to modify host environment variables manually.
3. Document Apple/APNs signing credential prerequisites, persistent storage, HTTPS, networking, authentication, upgrades and backups. A private Tailscale-accessible deployment would be especially useful if feasible; the relay's outbound APNs delivery should not require unnecessarily exposing the Hermes agent itself.
4. Provide a clear inventory of **all plaintext metadata sent to and stored by the relay**, retention periods, and whether fields such as raw session IDs, tool names and usage timestamps can be minimized, hashed or made optional.
5. Ensure opting out prevents any requests to the maintainer-operated relay and doesn't install the push plugin just to use other client features.

### Questions

- Does the project already support running the relay **entirely locally** (Docker/Linux/NAS), rather than deploying one's own Cloudflare Worker?
- Could local hosting and configurable relay selection be supported/documented officially?
- Is it possible to reduce relay-visible metadata or disable these transmissions while still receiving basic push notifications?

I appreciate that push is already optional, the relay is open source, and message previews are encrypted. This request is about **user control, practical local hosting, and metadata minimization**, not a claim that message contents are being leaked.

References:
- https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/master/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/HermexPushPairing.swift
- https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/master/docs/agents/push.md
- https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push/tree/main/relay
- https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-push/blob/main/plugin/hermex_push/payload.py

title: Bot attachments fail on Windows hosts: verifiedPath rejects drive-letter paths
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Hermes Agent 0.22.2 with its dashboard on a Windows host, signed in from Hermex as the server's Hermes backend (password sign-in).
2. Open Bot Chat with any bot and attach a photo (camera or library).
3. The upload succeeds on the host: POST /api/chat/image-upload stores the image and answers {"ok": true, "path": "C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\hermes\\profiles\\<profile>\\images\\dashboard_...png"}.
4. Hermex then shows "This Hermes connection does not support Bot chat here." and the attachment is dropped. Documents through file.attach fail the same way.

### Expected behavior

The attachment is accepted and sent with the Bot Chat message, as on macOS and Linux hosts.

### Actual behavior

BotAttachmentUpload.verifiedPath (HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotAttachmentUpload.swift:96, master b26d7c5) only accepts a path that starts with "/", so a Windows drive-letter path makes it throw .unsupported, which BotProtocol.swift:69 shows as "This Hermes connection does not support Bot chat here." This happens after every successful upload, so the host keeps the file but the app never sends it.

Suggested fix: also accept a Windows absolute path (^[A-Za-z]:[\\/], and UNC \\server\share\ if wanted) alongside POSIX paths, still refusing newlines and NUL. BotArtifactReference.path already accepts such paths for downloads.

### Impact

Minor bug

### App version / commit

0.22.2

### iOS version and device

iPhone, current iOS (Hermex from the App Store)

### hermes-webui server version

Hermes Agent 0.22.2 dashboard (Bot Chat backend) on Windows 11; hermes-webui as the app's server

None
