title: feat(hermes): sign in to a Hermes dashboard that has no password
body:
**What the user gets:** a Hermes dashboard that reports no sign-in (`auth_required: false`) can be added without a username or password, and Hermex warns that anyone who can reach the address can control it.
**Why it matters:** the owner's demo host has no credentials and Hermex can't add it at all. The form asks for a username and password that don't exist, keeps Add disabled, and junk credentials end in "This Hermes connection does not support Bot chat here."
**Cost:** Medium. Sign-in, reconnect, and the WebSocket all change; one manual check against a passwordless host.

## Current behavior

- `AddServerView` detects Hermes from `/api/status` and says "Hermes dashboard found. Sign in with your dashboard username and password." Add stays disabled until both fields are filled.
- `HermesConnection.beginSignIn` throws `.unsupported` when `auth_required` isn't `true` (`HermesConnection.swift:195`).
- Move to Hermes refuses the host with R1 `noSignIn` (`MoveToHermesModel.swift:55`).

## Decision

Show the warning, but don't block sign-in. A passwordless dashboard is the user's call.

## How a passwordless dashboard authenticates

Verified against the pinned `hermes-agent` (`ca67828`, `hermes_cli/web_server.py` `_require_token`, `web_server_chat.py` `_ws_auth_reason`) and read-only against a live 0.21.6 host:

- `GET /api/status` → `"auth_required": false, "auth_providers": [], "auth_flows": []`.
- `GET /` (the dashboard HTML) injects `window.__HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN__="<token>"` and `window.__HERMES_AUTH_REQUIRED__=false`.
- REST: send the token as `X-Hermes-Session-Token: <token>` (preferred; `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is the legacy path and collides with proxy basic auth). Without it, `/api/sessions` → 401; with it → 200.
- `GET /api/auth/me` with the token → `{"user_id":"local","provider":"loopback",...}`.
- WebSocket: `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` is gated-mode only (401 here). The loopback WS path takes `?token=<token>` instead.
- The token is fresh on every server start unless the host sets `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN`, so a 401 after a host restart means: fetch `/` again, take the new token, retry once.

## Context: when this happens

Upstream won't run passwordless on any non-loopback bind, including LAN and tailnet IPs (`should_require_auth`, hardened after the June 2026 attacks, `--insecure` is now ignored). The dashboard reports `auth_required: false` only when it's bound to `127.0.0.1` and has no `dashboard.public_url`. A phone reaches it only through something that forwards to loopback: `tailscale serve`, a Caddy or nginx proxy, or `cloudflared` to `localhost`. That's how the demo host is set up (Caddy → `127.0.0.1:9121`). Over Tailscale serve this is a reasonable private setup. Over a public proxy the whole agent is open to the internet, which is what the warning is for.

## Scope

- **Add Server and onboarding:** when the probe sees `auth_required: false`, hide the username and password fields, enable Add, and show a warning instead of the sign-in footnote. Suggested copy: "This dashboard has no password. Anyone who can reach this address can use your agent. To add one, set `dashboard.public_url` and turn on the dashboard password." Keep the warning visible in that server's Settings too, so it isn't a one-time notice.
- **Connection:** a passwordless `BotConnection` (no username, no password, no OAuth) signs in by reading the token from `/`, then calls `/api/auth/me`. The version gate and `requireSameInstall` still run. Send the token header on REST calls and `?token=` on the WebSocket. Keep the token in memory only and re-read it on a 401.
- **Reverse state:** if the host later turns sign-in on (`auth_required: true`), the connection fails with a clear "this server now needs a password" message that leads to editing the server, not a generic error.
- **Move to Hermes:** drop the R1 refusal and show the same warning on the Review screen.
- **Multi-server:** the token belongs to its server and is never sent to another one.

## Not in scope

- Scraping the token on every request. Read it once per sign-in and again on a 401.
- Any change to hosts that require sign-in.

## Tests

- Sign-in against a scripted passwordless host: reads the token from `/`, sends `X-Hermes-Session-Token`, accepts the `loopback` identity.
- A 401 after a token rotation re-reads `/` and retries once; a second 401 surfaces an error.
- The host flipping to `auth_required: true` surfaces the needs-a-password failure.
- Manual: add a passwordless host (`scripts/local-hermes` behind a loopback proxy, or the owner's demo host), send a message, and watch it stream. Restart the host and confirm the app reconnects.

title: feat(hermes): sign in to a dashboard with no password
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1314

## What changed

A Hermes dashboard bound to `127.0.0.1` without `dashboard.public_url` reports `auth_required: false`. People reach it through `tailscale serve`, Caddy, or cloudflared. Hermex refused it, and every form required a username and password that didn't exist, so Add stayed disabled.

Hermex now signs in to such a dashboard and warns that anyone who can reach the address can use the agent.

- **Sign-in.** A new `HermesSignInMethod` (password, browser, open), read from `/api/status`, replaces the `signsInWithBrowser` flags in every form. For an open dashboard, sign-in reads the session token from the dashboard page and sends it as `X-Hermes-Session-Token`. The gateway and Kanban sockets get it as `?token=`. A 401 signs in again and re-reads the page, so a host restart recovers.
- **Forms.** Add Server, onboarding, and a server's sign-in form hide the credentials and show the warning. The server's Settings page and Move's Review screen keep showing it. Move to Hermes no longer refuses an open host.
- **Reverse state.** If a saved open server later turns sign-in on, the app signs it out to its sign-in form with "This server now requires you to sign in."

The contract was checked against pinned `hermes-agent` `ca67828` (`_require_token`, `_ws_auth_reason`, the token injection in `web_server_dashboard.py`) and read-only against a live 0.21.6 host. title: fix(hermes): View all reopens the session list behind a chat on foreground
body:
## Problem

On a direct Hermes connection, the Scheduled sessions **View all** screen (`ScheduledSessionsView`, from #1297) reopens the session list whenever the app becomes active, even when it shouldn't:

- **Phone:** open View all, open a scheduled chat on top of it, then background and foreground the app. View all calls `openHermes()`, so the list goes live and reloads underneath the chat. The list's own scene-phase handler skips that case.
- **Any device:** View all doesn't check `isHermesConnected`. Pulling down Control Center and dismissing it (`.inactive` → `.active`) triggers a full reload.
- **iPad:** the sidebar list and View all both reopen when the app comes to the foreground, so the host gets read twice. The read serial drops the stale result, so the cost is a wasted request, not wrong state.

## Suggested fix

Move View all's `.task { openHermes() }` and its `scenePhase` handler out of `ScheduledSessionsView`. Put them on the phone's `navigationDestination` in `HermesSessionListView`, next to its `.onDisappear`, and gate them on `covers.chat == nil && !viewModel.isHermesConnected`. iPad would then rely on the sidebar's lifecycle.

Found during an independent review while rebasing #1297 onto #1316.

**What the user gets:** a per-Profile "API Keys & Environment" page on a Hermes server where they can see which keys are set, add a key, replace one, and remove one, all from the phone. **Why it matters:** A user who came over from Vory asked for it by email. Today, adding a provider key on a Hermes server means opening the desktop dashboard or SSH. Hermex only asks for a secret when the agent requests one mid-chat. **Cost:** Medium. The owner picks a mock before work starts, then tests on a phone with a disposable key. ## Today - Hermes servers have no keys screen. `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md:72` lists `model.save_key` / `model.disconnect` as untriaged ("Secrets; deliberate UX first"). - `HermesREST.setEnvironment` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:143`) already sends `PUT /api/env`, but only for the push relay URL, and it sends no Profile. - Webui servers have a read-only Providers screen (`ProvidersView.swift:52`). #422 covered webui key editing and was closed as superseded by #713. This issue is the Hermes version. ## Contract (pinned hermes-agent `ca678285`, `hermes_cli/web_routers/config_env.py`) | Route | Body | Returns | | --- | --- | --- | | `GET /api/env?profile=

` (`:232`) | none | an object keyed by var name. Each row has `is_set`, `redacted_value`, `description`, `url`, `category`, `is_password`, `provider`, `provider_label`, `custom`, `advanced`. Includes known catalog vars plus custom vars from the Profile's `.env` (`category: "custom"`). Process-environment and OAuth credentials are not listed. | | `PUT /api/env` (`:292`) | `{key, value, profile}` | `{ok, key, config_updates}`. A redacted preview sent back as the value gets 400. | | `DELETE /api/env` (`:957`) | `{key, profile}` | `{ok, key, removed, found, ...}`, 404 when the key isn't there. | | `POST /api/env/reveal` (`:975`) | `{key, profile}` | plaintext. Rate-limited and audit-logged. **Out of scope.** | Each Profile has its own `.env`. If `profile` is left out, the host uses the dashboard process's Profile, so always send the selected Profile. Before building, confirm these shapes with `curl` against the live host and record them in the PR. ## Expected behavior - An **API Keys** row on the active Hermes server's page in Settings (`SettingsServerPage.hermesSections`) opens the screen. - A Profile menu at the top starts on the default Profile and lists the others from `profiles.list`. A server with one Profile shows its name with no menu. Switching Profiles reloads the list. - The list shows only keys that are set (`is_set`), grouped by `category` (Providers, Tools, Custom, and so on). Each row shows the name, description, and `redacted_value`. - **+** opens a searchable picker of every key the server knows about (hiding `channel_managed`), plus **Custom key…**, which asks for a name. - Tapping a row opens a sheet to set or replace its value: a `SecureField` with paste allowed and autocorrect off. The value is sent once and never echoed back. It is never written to Keychain, drafts, cache, or logs, and it is cleared when the sheet closes. - Remove is destructive and asks for confirmation. The copy names the key and says what happens: sessions that use it stop authenticating until it is set again. - After every write, reload the list. The server's error message is shown as-is. - A footnote explains what the list leaves out: keys that come from the host's environment or from an OAuth login are still used but aren't shown here. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `HermesREST` cases for GET/PUT/DELETE `/api/env`, each sending `profile`. `setEnvironment` is either reused with an explicit Profile or replaced. - [ ] The value goes only in the JSON body, never in a query string or log line. - [ ] The list is fetched for each server and Profile, never cached. A key set on server A or Profile X never shows under B or Y. - [ ] Strings are localized. The page works with VoiceOver and Dynamic Type. ## Decisions (settled with the owner 2026-10-22) - **Placement:** a row on the Hermes server's Settings page. - **Profile:** a Profile menu inside the screen, starting on the default Profile. - **List:** only keys that are set. Every other known key is reached through the **+** picker. - **Reveal:** never. Only the server's masked preview is shown. - **Validation:** none. Save directly; no `/api/providers/validate`. - **Writes:** `PUT` and `DELETE /api/env` for every key, not `model.save_key`. - **Still to verify in the first slice (a fact, not a decision):** does a running session pick up a changed key without `reload.env`? Test on `scripts/local-hermes`; the result decides the after-save copy. From the source, provider keys seem to take effect on the next turn through the credential pool, but tool keys come from the process environment. - **Before building:** two or three static mocks; the owner picks one. Scale: the pinned host lists 348 keys (98 provider, 199 messaging, 43 tool), which is why the main list shows only keys that are set. ## Non-goals Reveal / copy plaintext. OAuth logins. `model.disconnect`. Webui servers.

title: feat(settings): add, replace and remove a Hermes Profile's API keys
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1318

## What changed

A user who came over from Vory asked for a way to add API keys from the phone. On a Hermes server there was no way to do that: adding a provider key meant opening the desktop dashboard or SSH. Hermex only asked for a secret when the agent requested one mid-chat.

The active Hermes server's page in Settings now has an **API Keys** row. It opens a list of the keys one Profile's `.env` sets, grouped by type, with the masked value the host returns. A Profile menu at the top switches Profiles. **+** opens a searchable picker of every key the host knows, plus Custom Key…. Tapping a key replaces it or, after a confirmation, removes it. It goes through the host's own routes: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/env`. Every request names the Profile. The key value goes once in a request body and is never cached, logged or persisted on the phone. Nothing is cached across servers or Profiles. `HermesREST.setEnvironment` gained an optional `profile`; push provisioning still sends none, so its relay URL still reaches every Profile.

title: fix(chat): accept a Windows host's attachment paths
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1312

## What changed

On a Windows host, a Bot Chat photo or document uploaded fine, then Hermex rejected the `C:\…` path the host returned and dropped the attachment with "This Hermes connection does not support Bot chat here."

- `BotAttachmentUpload.isHostAbsolute` accepts a drive-letter path (`C:\` or `C:/`) as well as `/…`. Newlines and NUL are still refused, and network-share paths aren't accepted. The upload check uses it.

title: fix(hermes): drop Retry when another client's turn fails before it starts
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1158

## What changed

After turn A fails, its Retry targets A's prompt row. If another client's turn B then fails before it starts (a `message.complete` with `status: error` and no `message.start`, as upstream's agent-init refusal sends), the chat ignored the completion. A's Retry stayed, and tapping it cut the transcript at A's prompt, taking B with it.

A completion for a turn this chat never saw start now:
- counts as a turn, so reads begun before it are dropped,
- clears the last outcome right away (`HermesChatActivity.unseenTurnDidComplete`), so A's Retry is gone,
- when it failed, rereads the host's retained failure (the existing `readFailedTurn`), which offers B's Retry only when B's prompt row is provably B's.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim D5388D52-C781-4920-9028-C7182B84CD8A` (iPhone Air) with `--only` for `HermesChatTurnTests`, `HermesChatAttachmentTests`, `HermesAgentFixtureTests`, `HermesChatLiveActivityTests`, `HermesChatRequestTests`, `HermesHistoryRewindTests` and `HermesTranscriptPagingTests`: every class that drives `message.complete`. 188 passed, 0 failed.

New `testAnUnseenFailedTurnReplacesTheEarlierRetry`: A fails → Retry at row 7 → an unseen failing completion arrives → Retry is gone → the reread offers row 9.

No manual test: reproducing needs a second client failing before `message.start` right after a failure in the same chat.

title: feat(chat): explain approval commands in plain words
body:
## Linked issue

None.

## What changed

Approval cards show the flagged command, but a long or unfamiliar shell command can be hard to judge quickly on a phone. This adds an optional, clearly labelled AI explanation to the card without changing the approval decision or delaying its buttons.

- Under the command, a section titled **In plain words (AI summary)** shows a one- or two-sentence explanation. It starts with a small "Summarizing…" placeholder. A failed, blank, cancelled or timed-out result leaves no row and no error.
- Covered surfaces: the approval overlay in direct-Hermes session chats and Bot Chats (`ChatView` → `ApprovalRequestOverlay`), and Bot Room approval cards (`BotRoomComposerView` → `BotPendingRequestCard`). Cards without a direct-Hermes connection, clarification cards and bypass confirmations are unchanged.
- The request is one `llm.oneshot` call per approval over the existing gateway connection, with free `instructions` and `input` (no `template`), `max_tokens: 160`, `temperature: 0.2`, the chat's profile and, for direct chats, its `session_id`. The input is the approval's reason, the command and the working directory when known. The instructions ask for a plain explanation of what the command does, written in the app's display language (named in English, e.g. "Japanese"), tell the model not to recommend Allow or Deny or call the command safe, and to treat the command and description as data, not instructions.
- The client waits at most 20 seconds. Results are kept in memory per server, conversation and approval, so leaving and returning to a still-pending approval doesn't ask again; leaving or answering cancels unfinished work, and a late result can't come back for an answered approval.
- Settings → Chat gets one app-wide **Explain approvals in plain words** switch, **off by default** (`ApprovalSummaries.enabledByDefault`, defined once beside its key), with the footer "Asks the Hermes server's model for a short summary of each approval. Chats on a webui server don't show one." Off, the card is exactly as it is today and no request is made.
- On a webui server, session chats use the legacy approval card, which never gets a summary slot, so they look exactly as on master and make no request. Bot Chats and Bot Rooms run over a direct-Hermes connection, so they get the summary there too.
- New strings are in the String Catalog for all locales (translations marked needs_review).

## How it was tested

Maintainer follow-up (rebased onto master at 153f755b):
- Off by default, as above.
- Council fixes: a remount (a question taking the overlay's place, a room card moving up after the one above is answered, a layout change) no longer cancels a loading summary. Only an accepted answer, a withdrawal, leaving, or the switch turning off ends it. Answering no longer cancels first, so a refused answer keeps the summary. The summary deadline now caps the standard one (`min(standard, 20 s)`), so its gateway test runs in milliseconds. The card tests assert summary state and model calls instead of OCR'd copy, and no longer write PNGs.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17e> --only` ApprovalSummaryTests, BotChatPresentationTests, BotRoomTests, HermesGatewayTests, HermesChatRequestTests, HermesRequestTests, HermesChatTurnTests, LocalizationCatalogTests: 199 passed, 0 failed on 9bb881e7. After the language change: HermesRequestTests, HermesGatewayTests, HermesChatRequestTests, BotRoomTests, ApprovalSummaryTests, 117 passed, 0 failed on f719d2fc; the request test checks that a Japanese app asks for Japanese. The new refused-answer test fails if `respond` retires the summary early, and the new room test covers a card moving up while its summary loads.
- `llm.oneshot` params (`instructions`, `input`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`, `profile`, `session_id`) and the `text` result checked against `LlmOneshotParams`/`LlmOneshotResult` in the pinned `gateway-contract.openrpc.json` at `ca678285`. Bot Room summaries send no `session_id`, so the host answers on that member profile's `title_generation` one-shot model, which can differ from the chat's model (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py`).

Original testing:

- CI on this branch is green (Build and Test, Tooling Tests, CI Gate).
- Locally, CI-style (`xcodebuild`, parallel testing on, one clone): full suite 3,566 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the signed-Keychain access-group test, also skipped in CI). Focused approval and summary suites: 195 passed, 0 failed.
- The tests cover the rendered cards, buttons usable while loading, silent failure, switch off and no connection (card unchanged, zero model calls), cache isolation between conversations with equal approval ids, leave/return, cancellation and the gateway deadline. Two of the card tests first failed in CI because they read the command back from the rendered card with OCR, which dropped a space on the CI runtime; they now check the command `Text` the view emits. With the command's space removed on purpose, both fail.
- Native run in the simulator against a disposable, unmodified local Hermes (0.21.5) with a scripted model: allowed a harmless command while the summary was loading, saw the summary, backgrounded and returned without a second request, and checked the off state.

Known limits: summary quality with a real model, a live multi-member Bot Room, and physical devices weren't tested.

Loading, then the summary:

![Loading, buttons usable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ASKProducts/hermex/pr-media/approval-summary/u1022b-approval-loading.png)
![Summary shown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ASKProducts/hermex/pr-media/approval-summary/u1022b-approval-summary.png)

Switch off, and the setting:

![Card with the switch off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ASKProducts/hermex/pr-media/approval-summary/u1022b-approval-off.png)
![Settings → Chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ASKProducts/hermex/pr-media/approval-summary/u1022b-approval-setting.png)

title: fix(hermes): reopen View all's list on foreground only when it shows
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1317

## What changed

title: Onboarding can't sign in to a saved Hermes server, leaving users stuck
body:
**What the user gets:** Signing in to a server that's already saved signs you back in and opens it, instead of stopping at "This server is already configured" on a screen you can't leave.
**Why it matters:** A v1.9 user is stuck on the sign-in screen after setting up and then dropping a second server. Reinstalling doesn't help, because the server list lives in Keychain. [#1027](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1027)'s reporter hit the same dead end.
**Cost:** Small. Simulator.

## Problem

A legacy webui server that gets a 401 goes to `.loggedOut`, and `ContentView` shows full-screen onboarding on its Connect page (`ContentView.swift:102`). That page has no close button, server switcher or Remove option.

If the user types the address of their saved **Hermes** server there, onboarding detects the dashboard and calls `OnboardingViewModel.addHermesServer`. That function refuses any saved address (`OnboardingViewModel.swift:556`). [#1032](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1032) added a **Replace…** option when the saved server is webui. It deliberately kept this error for a saved Hermes server, which leaves the user with no way out.

The same refusal can also be reached from `.unconfigured` while the server list is still intact (see closed, unmerged [#1194](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1194)).

A saved webui server already has a way back in: `AuthManager.configure` signs it in again and makes it active. A saved Hermes server should work the same way.

## Plan

In `OnboardingViewModel.addHermesServer`, when the saved server at that address is a **Hermes** server and the form was not opened by a move:

1. Sign in on a new connection, exactly as for a new server. A failed sign-in changes nothing and shows the usual `BotConnectionAdvice` message.
2. If the sign-in succeeds, save the record as that server's sign-in and make it the active server, signed in. Do this in one new `AuthManager` method, alongside `addHermesServer` and `replaceWebuiServer`. Keep the saved server's name, initials and color. If a sign-in record already exists, reuse its `id`, so data keyed to that connection stays attached.
3. The Add Server sheet keeps its current error. It already has **Cancel** and a server switcher, so it is not a dead end.

## Decisions

1. **Sign in again rather than add a switcher to onboarding.** Once a saved Hermes server can be signed into again, onboarding can reach every saved server: webui already worked through `configure`. That makes the Connect page a working way out without another control.
2. Moves (`moveSource != nil`) keep today's refusal, matching #1032.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Onboarding Connect, entered from a logged-out webui server: typing a saved Hermes server's address and valid credentials ends signed in to that server, with its saved identity.
- [ ] Wrong credentials leave the saved server and the current state as they were.
- [ ] The Add Server sheet still says "This server is already configured" for a saved Hermes address.
- [ ] Tests cover the success and refused cases (`AuthManagerStateTests` / `OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests`, next to #1032's tests).

Model and harness: Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code in T3 Code. Independent investigation by GPT-6.1 Sol (xhigh) agreed.

title: fix(onboarding): open a saved Hermes server instead of refusing it

## Linked issue

Fixes #1331

Onboarding has no server switcher. When a legacy webui server's session is refused, the app shows onboarding. title: fix(chat): app crashes on launch after opening a chat with a paragraph of thousands of inline elements
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Hermex to a server that has a session whose reply contains one paragraph with thousands of inline elements. A read-only imported Claude Code session that lists a few thousand file paths as inline code is enough (about 3,000 code spans reproduces it; 1,500 does not).
2. Tap that session in the session list.
3. Force-quit and relaunch the app.

### Expected behavior

The session opens and shows its content. Relaunching the app works.

### Actual behavior

The app crashes with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` (SIGSEGV), "Thread stack size exceeded due to excessive recursion". Hermex reopens the last chat on launch, so it crashes again on every start, and the app stays unusable until it is reinstalled.

The crash is on the main thread while SwiftUI resolves a long chain of concatenated `Text` values:

```
0  libsystem_pthread.dylib  ___chkstk_darwin
1  SwiftUICore  Text.resolve<A>(into:in:with:)
2  SwiftUICore  ConcatenatedTextStorage.resolve<A>(into:in:with:)
3  SwiftUICore  Text.Storage.resolve<A>(into:in:with:)
   ... the same three frames repeat ...
```

MarkdownUI joins a paragraph's inline elements (code spans, emphasis, links, soft breaks) with `Text + Text`, so the nesting depth equals the number of elements. The existing fallbacks only cap total characters (80,000) and lines (2,000), not elements per paragraph.

### Impact

Blocks work completely

### App version / commit

Hermex 1.9 (build 1) from the App Store; also reproduced on `master` at 4494746.

### iOS version and device

iOS 26.6.2 on iPhone 15; also reproduced on the iOS 26.3.1 iPhone 17 simulator.

### hermes-webui server version

Not server-dependent. The crash is in the client's text rendering, so the web UI can't reproduce it, and any server that returns such a message triggers it. Reproduced with a local stub that serves one read-only session with a 4,000-code-span reply.

### How the phone reaches the server

Other

### Screenshots or screen recordings

Videos to be attached below: the crash on every launch before the fix, and the same session opening after the fix.

---

I have a fix ready (a per-paragraph inline-element fallback to plain text, plus drawing the plain-text fallback in chunks, since a single `Text` taller than about 16,000 pt does not draw) and will open a PR that links this issue.

Investigated and written up with Claude Sonnet 5.5 in Claude Code.

title: fix(chat): stop a long inline-heavy paragraph from crashing the app on open
body: ## Linked issue Fixes #1333 ## What changed Opening a chat that has one paragraph with a few hundred inline elements (code spans, emphasis, links, soft line breaks) crashes the app with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`, "Thread stack size exceeded due to excessive recursion". Hermex reopens the last chat on launch, so it then crashes on every start until it is reinstalled. Imported read-only Claude Code sessions hit it often, because their replies list many file paths as inline code, but any chat with such a paragraph does. **Root cause.** MarkdownUI 2.4.1 builds a paragraph's `Text` by appending each top-level inline element with `+` (`TextInlineRenderer.defaultRender`). SwiftUI resolves that left-nested chain recursively on the main thread. An iPhone's main thread has a 1 MB stack (1,008 KB in the device crash report), so about 600 elements overflow it. The simulator's 8 MB stack hides the crash until roughly ten times as many. **Fix.** An overlong paragraph renders as one formatted `Text` instead of MarkdownUI's chain. The rest of the message is unchanged. - `MathMarkdownLabel` already sends paragraphs with inline math to `MathInlineText`, which parses them with Foundation's Markdown parser and keeps inline code (monospaced, shaded), emphasis and links. It now does the same for a paragraph over 300 estimated inline elements, about half the measured crash point. - `InlineMathTextRequest.compose` previously added one `Text` per run with `+`, the same pattern in miniature. It now merges consecutive prose runs into one `AttributedString`, joining only at math images, so the paragraph is a single `Text`. - `MarkdownContentRenderingPolicy.hasTooManyInlineElements` is a byte scan that overestimates elements: each delimiter counts once; each line, and each `:` or `@` of a bare URL or email that GFM autolinks, counts twice. `ChatMarkdownView` runs it once per message and folds it into the existing `containsInlineMath` flag, so ordinary messages skip the per-paragraph markdown render. The source change is 33 lines added and 3 removed in two files, plus one test class. The first two commits tried a whole-message plain-text fallback that was later replaced, so a squash merge is cleaner. ## How it was tested - **Crash threshold, without the fix.** I measured it in the simulator with the main-thread stack reduced to 1,008 KB: | Content in one paragraph | Renders | Crashes | |---|---|---| | Inline code spans | 300 | 350 | | Plain lines, no blank line between them | 250 | 350 | Every crash had the same `Text.resolve` / `ConcatenatedTextStorage.resolve` stack as the device report. - **With the fix, same 1 MB stack:** 400 code spans, 3,000 code spans, 400 plain lines, a 400-span list item, 400 bare URLs and 400 bare emails all render. - **Regression test:** `InlineElementStackDepthTests`, appended to `MarkdownMathRendererTests.swift`, so there's no project-file change. It renders a 400-code-span paragraph and a 400-bare-URL paragraph with 1 MB of stack left. Both fixtures crash without the fix: the bare-URL fixture crashed on 2043272 with the #1333 stack, and passes now. - **Existing tests.** Command: `scripts/test-sim --only …`. - `InlineElementStackDepthTests`: 2 passed. - `MarkdownMathRendererTests`: 44 passed. - `TranscriptMarkdownImageTests`: 13 passed. - `ResponseSelectionTests`: 6 passed, 1 failed. `testRowsAroundAResponseStayClearWhenItGrowsAfterFirstLayout` fails the same way on unmodified master on this simulator (iPhone 17, iOS 26.3.1). - **Full suite** (`scripts/test-sim `) on 2043272, before the review changes: 3,551 passed, 1 failed. The failure is the same `ResponseSelectionTests` test as above. - **Manual, iPhone 17 simulator.** I used a local stand-in for hermes-webui serving one read-only Claude Code session whose reply is a 400-span paragraph. The session reopens with inline code pills and bold text intact. The "before" recording on #1333 shows the crash on every launch without the fix. Its "after" recording shows the earlier plain-text version, not this one. After the fix, on this head: the 400-span paragraph keeps its inline code pills and bold text. - **Not tested on a physical iPhone.** The 1 MB-stack runs stand in for one. ## Known limits, unchanged by this PR - **Very tall paragraphs draw blank.** A paragraph of roughly 11,000 characters or more renders blank. A 13,000-character plain paragraph that MarkdownUI draws itself is blank on this branch too, so this looks like a separate SwiftUI limit on one very tall `Text`. It deserves its own issue. - **Hundreds of inline equations.** A paragraph with hundreds of inline math expressions can still overflow, because each equation image still joins with `+`. Surfaces: `MarkdownRenderer` and `StreamingMarkdownRenderer` both render through `ChatMarkdownView`, so cached, reloaded and streaming replies are covered, and so are list items and table cells that use `MathMarkdownLabel`. No networking or `Codable` changes. ## Checklist - [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim ` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above (one unrelated failure, also on master) - [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed) - [x] No new third-party dependencies - [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (none touched) Maintainer follow-up (590beb9): also count scheme-less `www.` autolinks. Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved AI usage: built with Claude Code (Claude Sonnet 5.5, reviewed and revised with Claude Opus 5.5). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(hermes): let session edits through on hosts with a separate gateway
body:
**What the user gets:** Pin, archive, rename and mark read/unread work again on Hermes sessions created in Hermex, when the host runs a separate gateway beside the dashboard.
**Why it matters:** A user reported it after updating to Hermes 0.22.5. On that topology every Hermex 2.0 session refuses these edits, and read marks silently come back after opening a chat. 2.0 is still in App Review, so fixing it before release means App Store users never create affected sessions.
**Cost:** Small. One constant plus a refusal message. Simulator check against a local split host; no phone needed.

## Cause

Since #1279, Hermex creates and resumes sessions with `source: "hermex"` (`HermesCall.swift:22`). When a standalone `hermes dashboard` runs beside a separate `hermes gateway`, `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` is forwarded to the gateway's `session.mutate`. For a session the gateway doesn't have loaded, `authorize_history` only accepts stored sources in `LEGACY_LOCAL_SOURCES` (`cli, tui, gui, desktop, oneshot, tool, acp`) plus `import` (hermes-agent `hermes_state_mutation_binding.py:8-13, :60`; `hermes_state_local_migration.py:15`). `hermex` isn't listed, so the edit answers **404 `{"detail":"not_found"}`**.

- Not new in 0.22.5: v0.22.4 reproduces it, and v0.22.3 has the same code.
- A single combined `hermes serve` is unaffected.
- v1.9.0 sends no source, so its sessions are stored as `tui` and are unaffected. Only 2.0 builds create `hermex` rows.
- We can't change upstream; the fix is Hermex-side.

## Reproduction (local, v0.22.5 `bf0203a7`, dashboard + separate gateway)

Sessions created with `session.create` over `/api/ws`, one prompt each, then edited the way Hermex does (mutation snapshot, then PATCH with `request_id` + `expected_revision`):

| Stored source | pinned / archived / unread / title | Agent's surface note (captured system prompt) |
|---|---|---|
| `hermex` | 404 on all four | Hermex's `platform_hints.hermex` |
| `tui` | 200 | TUI note: "MEDIA:/path tags are NOT intercepted" (the #1278 bug) |
| `cli` | 200 | CLI note: "Markdown does NOT render", no attachments |
| `desktop` | 200 | Desktop note: also promises `::preview` widgets and theme vars Hermex can't render; adds Desktop toolsets |
| `gui` | 200 | **None built in**. With `platform_hints.gui.append` set via `PUT /api/config`, a `gui` session got exactly Hermex's note while `desktop` and `tui` sessions kept theirs |

Also verified:
- `session.resume` with a new `source` does not re-stamp the stored row; edits still 404.
- An imported copy (Duplicate's path) of a `hermex` session edits fine, because import records an owner binding that `authorize_history` checks before the source.
- The legacy `session.archive` RPC can archive a `hermex` row, but it bypasses the write fence and there's no pin or unread equivalent. Don't use it.

## Fix

1. Change `HermesCall.source` to `"gui"`.
   - It's allowed by the gate. It has no built-in prompt note, so Hermex's note (written automatically to `platform_hints.<source>` by `HermesREST.setPlatformNote`) is the only one the agent gets.
   - Official Desktop chats run as agent platform `desktop` (on the canonical protocol, `gui` maps to `desktop`; `gateway/session_policy.py:85`), so they never read `platform_hints.gui`.
   - Also stops `hermex` sessions being refused by worker delegation (`gateway/session_worker_delegation.py:57`) and queued-message controls (`gateway/session_queued_controls.py:30`).
   - Update the doc comment on `HermesCall.source` and the `HermesREST` contract note to say why `gui` (the gate, and the empty default note) and that it applies to the legacy dashboard socket only.
   - Leave the old `platform_hints.hermex` entry in Profile configs alone; it's harmless.
2. When a session edit answers 404 `not_found` or 403 `permission_denied`, say the host refused the change instead of the generic error, or the proxy/Cloudflare advice the 403 shows today (`BotProtocol.swift:78-81`). For sessions made by earlier 2.0 builds, suggest Duplicate, which produces an editable copy. Read/unread marks already roll back silently; keep that.

## Acceptance

- New sessions from Hermex are created and resumed with `source: "gui"`, and the Profile note is written under `platform_hints.gui`.
- On a dashboard + separate gateway host (v0.22.5), pin, archive, unread and rename succeed on a Hermex-created session after it goes cold.
- A refused edit on an old `hermex` session shows the new message, not proxy advice.
- Focused tests: `HermesRequestTests` and `HermesConnectionTests` (they assert the source and config key today), plus one test for the refusal message.

## Out of scope

- Repairing existing `hermex` rows in place. No client-side path changes a stored source.
- Phone-local pin/read state.
- The newer protocol the Desktop app uses (canonical), where `gui` means Desktop. Revisit this source if Hermex moves to it.

## Notes

- Reproduced with a scratch `scripts/local-hermes` at v0.22.5. That release needs Python 3.14 and installs only from `uv.lock`; its `pyproject.toml` pins conflict (pillow). Run `hermes gateway run` and `hermes dashboard --skip-build` on the same `HERMES_HOME` for the split topology.
- Independently confirmed by a GPT-6 Astra source review.

title: fix(hermes): let session edits through on hosts with a separate gateway
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1335

## What changed

On a host where `hermes dashboard` runs beside a separate `hermes gateway`, pin, archive, rename and mark read/unread failed on every session Hermex 2.0 created. The dashboard forwards a session edit to the gateway, and the gateway refuses an edit to a session it hasn't loaded unless its stored source is local (`hermes_state_mutation_binding.py` `authorize_history`, v0.22.5). `hermex` isn't local, so every edit answered 404 `{"detail":"not_found"}`.

- **Sessions now run as `gui`.** The gateway accepts edits for that source, and Hermes has no built-in note for it, so the note Hermex writes to each Profile's config, now under `platform_hints.gui`, is the only one the agent gets.
- **A refused edit says so.** When an edit answers `not_found` or `permission_denied`, it now throws `HermesSessionFenceRefusal.refused`. The message tells the user the server refused the change and suggests Duplicate, which makes an editable copy of an older `hermex` session. Before, the user saw a generic error, or Cloudflare advice for the 403. The new message has all 17 translations, marked `needs_review`.

title: fix(chat): stop currency amounts from pairing into inline math spans
body:
## Summary

Two bare currency amounts on one line pair into an inline-math span, and the prose between them is TeX-rendered: spaces eaten, hyphens turned into minus signs, and any `**bold**` markers inside the span orphaned into literal asterisks.

Real example from an assistant message rendered through this code path:

> Only adjustment: if the Aug 22 $100 was meant to cover through Aug 28 rather than settling past visits, it's 4 visits → $200. But his pattern all summer was pay-in-arrears (every payment lands a few days *after* a Friday mow), so $250 is the honest number.

Currently renders as:

> … it's 4 visits → *200.But his pattern all summer was pay − in − arrears (every payment lands a few days \*after\* a Friday mow), so*250 is the honest number.

**Root cause:** `InlineDelimiter.dollar.isOpen` accepts any non-`$`-adjacent `$` as an opener — including the `$` in `$200` — and the span closes at the next `$` on the line (`$250`). `looksLikeMath` then passes because prose hyphens (`pay-in-arrears` → `y-i`) satisfy the operator rule.

## Fix

Mirror the boundary guards that hermes-webui's renderer already applies — its inline-math regex rejects a `$` opener followed by a digit or whitespace, and a closing `$` preceded by whitespace (the comment there explicitly cites currency false positives like "costs $5 and $10"):

- **opener:** reject `$` followed by a digit or whitespace
- **closer:** reject `$` preceded by whitespace

Digit-led real math (`$2x + 1$`) now stays literal, consistent with the webui; it still renders via `\(…\)` or `$$…$$`. Letter-led math (`$x^2 + y_1$`) is unaffected.

## Tests

- `testCurrencyAmountsOnOneLineNeverPairIntoMath` — the regression cases above (two amounts + hyphenated prose; the bold-orphan case; `=`/`/`-qualified spans)
- `testRejectedClosingDollarDoesNotPairWithALaterSpan` pins the closer guard and the stop below
- `testLetterLedInlineMathStillRendersAfterBoundaryGuards` — pins the positive path

I also verified the algorithm change by porting `replacingInlineMath` + `looksLikeMath` with and without the guards and running the failing inputs through both: the five currency cases are preserved verbatim post-fix, `$x^2 + y_1$` still renders, and the existing preserved cases (`$5`, unmatched `$O=[…]`, escaped \$, code spans) are unchanged.

Note: #1334 also touches `MarkdownMathRendererTests.swift` (different methods, no overlap with `MarkdownMathFormatter.swift`), so this may need a trivial rebase if that lands first.

## Follow-up (maintainer)

Original fix by @CharlesMcquade. Both review bots caught that the closer guard alone let the span search skip a rejected `$` and pair with a later one: `$x^2 $ and $y^2$` rendered as "x² $ and $y²". 1b0182ac ends the candidate at the first live `$` that cannot close, which matches the `[^$]` span in hermes-webui's regex. It also adds `**$5** pay-in-arrears **$10**` to the currency test, because the closer guard alone made the digit-opener guard untested.

Tested with `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownMathRendererTests` (47 passed). I also checked a signed Debug build on the iPhone Air simulator against the webui server: an assistant reply with the currency, loose-math and bold lines keeps $200, $250 and pay-in-arrears as plain text, leaves `$x^2 $` literal, and renders y² as math.

title: feat(app): support the iPhone Duo foldable — cover screen and unfolded layout
body:
### Use case

Hermex is my daily client for steering my Hermes agent, and it now lives on an iPhone Duo (Apple's first foldable, released Oct 2026). The two states are genuinely different surfaces:

- **Cover screen (outer display, compact — a width unlike any iPhone the app has shipped on):** the glanceable surface — push notifications, quick session checks, one-line sends while out. Used one-handed and briefly.
- **Unfolded (inner display, larger and squarer than an iPad):** the work surface — reviewing streaming tool output, long transcripts, kanban, diffs.

Today the app runs on both (it's a normal iOS app) but nothing is designed for either state. Current behavior from the code: layout is size-class-driven — `HermesHomeLayout.usesSplit(isHome:horizontalSizeClass:)` is `isHome && horizontalSizeClass == .regular`, with `SessionSplitView` providing the sidebar/detail shell (doc comment says "iPad, landscape Plus/Max"). So unfolded (regular width) inherits the iPad split shell and the cover screen (compact) inherits the phone stack. That's a solid starting point — the ask is to make both foldable states deliberate and correct rather than incidental.

Concrete overflow already visible at ordinary phone width, which a cover screen would amplify: an assistant inline-math span (rendered from paired `$` currency amounts) overflows the bubble and clips at the right edge without wrapping — fixed by #1337 for the currency case, but wide code blocks and markdown tables still scroll/clip at narrow widths.

### Proposed behavior

Phased, smallest-first:

1. **Cover-screen correctness (compact, extra-narrow):** assistant content never clips at the bubble edge — math renders wrap or scale down, code blocks and tables scroll horizontally *within* their container, tool-call cards and the composer fit the width. Keyboard, dictation, and voice input all behave at cover-screen size.
2. **Unfolded correctness (regular, squarish aspect):** the existing `SessionSplitView` shell works on the inner display; the transcript column keeps a readable line measure instead of stretching full-width; display math centers or scales rather than hugging one edge.
3. **Fold/unfold continuity (polish):** folding or unfolding mid-stream does not remount the transcript or lose scroll position; an in-flight SSE stream survives the display-state change; sidebar selection state carries across.

### Acceptance outcomes

- A session containing wide markdown (code blocks, tables, math) opens on the cover screen with nothing clipped outside the bubble.
- Unfolding mid-stream keeps the stream connected and the transcript at the same scroll position.
- Unfolded, the home screen shows the sidebar/detail split; folding back returns to the stack without state loss.
- No layout thrash or crash when toggling fold state repeatedly during an active tool run.

### Upstream dependency notes

None — purely client-side rendering/layout. Related: #1337 (currency amounts pairing into inline math; its bubble overflow is most visible at narrow widths).

title: fix(bots): follow a Bot Chat the host replaced
body:
**What the user gets:** when Hermes swaps a bot's Bot Chat for a new one, the open chat moves to the new one and says where the old history went, instead of sticking on an error.
**Why it matters:** a user reported their messaging-channel Bot Chats stopped working after an update. Hermes 0.22.3 now renames such chats and creates a fresh one, and Hermex's open chat dead-ends on "The conversation identity changed. Check this bot in Desktop."
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed beyond the usual simulator pass.

## What changed upstream

Since hermes-agent 0.22.3 ([NousResearch/hermes-agent#140973](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/140973), commits `3606e74a21`, `cc856a06fd`), the gateway's first bot delivery moves aside a Bot Chat it can't own: a messaging-channel row (Telegram, Slack…), an API conversation, or a row whose `source` is not one of `LEGACY_LOCAL_SOURCES` (`cli`, `tui`, `gui`, `desktop`, `oneshot`, `tool`, `acp`). The old row keeps its id and history, is unhidden, and is retitled `Bot Chat (<platform or API> <id>)`; a new hidden local `Bot Chat` takes the title. Code at 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`): `gateway/session_bot.py:182-275` (`_target`, `displaceable_bot_chat`, `_displace_bot_chat`).

Since 0.22.1 ([#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742)) a messaging row titled "Bot Chat" also no longer counts as the canonical chat at all (`gateway/session_local_title.py:12-34`). This is deliberate upstream design; Hermex should follow it, not restore the old behavior.

## What Hermex does today

`HermesConversation.identify` (`HermesMobile/Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:409-424`) looks the Bot Chat up by exact title on every attach and throws `BotFailure.wrongIdentity` when the root differs from the one it held. `BotFailure.isRetryable` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:115-118`) treats that as permanent, so the open chat stays on the error until the user leaves and reopens it. A deep link to the old root (`linkedRoot`) hits the same path.

## Scope

- When a `.canonicalChat` lookup finds exactly one `Bot Chat` with a different root, adopt the new root and rebuild the transcript instead of failing (the title is the Bot Chat's identity; the host made the swap).
- Tell the user once, in the chat, that Hermes started a new Bot Chat and the earlier conversation is in Sessions under its new name. No new screen.
- Keep the existing safety for the case the refusal exists for: never send a pending draft or queued prompt into the new chat without the user seeing the swap first.
- Decide the stale deep-link case the same way (open the current Bot Chat, with the same notice).

## Not in scope

- Re-binding a messaging-channel session as a Bot Chat (upstream no longer allows it).
- Migrating or retitling rows on the host.

## Test

One model-level test: an attach whose title lookup returns a new root adopts it and surfaces the notice, and a draft is not sent across the swap. Use the existing scripted gateway fixtures.

title: fix(hermes): explain that a gateway's own listener isn't supported yet
body:
**What the user gets:** pointing Hermex at a Hermes gateway's built-in listener stops at sign-in with a clear "connect Hermex to `hermes dashboard`" message, instead of signing in and then failing every chat with cryptic errors.
**Why it matters:** since hermes-agent 0.22.1 the gateway serves its own copy of the dashboard on a different protocol. Hermex can reach it through a tunnel pointed at it, and then nothing works. Until Hermex supports that protocol (#1341), the failure should be honest and actionable.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed.

## Evidence

A local reproduction against hermes-agent 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`) with isolated homes and a stub model, 2026-10-24:

| Setup | `gateway.ready.session_authority` | Hermex today |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes serve` / `hermes dashboard` alone | absent | works |
| `hermes dashboard` or `serve` beside a running gateway | absent | works |
| `hermes gateway run` listener, password (`dashboard.public_url` set) | `true` | signs in, then `session.resume` → 4001 `invalid_params` (`close_on_disconnect`), `prompt.submit` → 4001 (needs `submission_id`), `session.title`/`delete`/`branch`/`undo`/`compress`/`cwd.set`/`close` → -32601 |
| `hermes gateway run` listener, open | `true` | sign-in fails: the gateway withholds the SPA page token (`gateway/run_api.py` `_bind_state`, `withhold_session_token`), so `HermesREST.pageToken` is nil and the error is `BotFailure.unsupported` |

The gateway listener binds loopback on a random port by default, so this needs a deliberately configured tunnel. It is not the documented remote-dashboard setup, but it is reachable.

## Scope

- `HermesGateway` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:283-286`): when `gateway.ready`'s payload has `session_authority: true`, fail the connect with a dedicated `BotFailure` whose copy says this address is a Hermes gateway's own listener, which Hermex doesn't support yet, and to connect to `hermes dashboard` instead.
- `HermesConnection` open sign-in (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:209-216`): when the page has no token, show the same guidance rather than the generic unsupported copy. Only if it can be told apart from a non-Hermes page without guessing; otherwise leave it.
- Non-retryable, like other permanent connection refusals.

## Not in scope

Supporting the protocol: #1341.

## Test

One test: a scripted `gateway.ready` with `session_authority: true` fails the connect with the new failure and never sends `client.capabilities`.

title: Support the canonical Hermes gateway protocol
body:
**What the user gets:** Hermex keeps working when a Hermes host serves the dashboard from its gateway, the direction upstream is moving every surface toward.
**Why it matters:** hermes-agent 0.22.1 ([NousResearch/hermes-agent#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742)) added a session authority with a different RPC contract on sockets whose `gateway.ready` says `session_authority: true`. Today only the gateway's own listener uses it, and #1340 makes Hermex refuse it clearly. When upstream moves `hermes dashboard` / `hermes serve` onto it (a follow-up in #106742, no date yet), every Hermex chat breaks.
**Cost:** Large. An epic: six child issues, one PR (see Decisions and Slices).

## Decisions

Settled 2026-11-06 by the maintainer. Each child applies the ones it names.

1. **Delivery.** One branch and one PR for the whole epic, one commit per child, in order. The `session_authority` refusal (#1340) stays until the last commit (#1606). The children are the spec for each commit.
2. **Profiles.** One canonical socket per Profile. Session ids repeat across Profiles, and session events don't name their Profile (`gateway/session_server_requests.py:55`).
3. **Stop.** Cancel the known queued admissions, then interrupt the running generation. Never clear the queue just because the interrupt succeeded.
4. **Unknown outcome.** An explicit acknowledge-or-discard action (`prompt.resolve_unknown`), never an automatic retry.
5. **Edit and resend.** Two steps: rewind, then send. Keep the edited text, and say so plainly if the send fails after the rewind. Doing it in one step needs an upstream change.
6. **Host identity.** Check `install_id` after sign-in, before loading data. The Webapp's signed-out status leaves it out, so the check before the password can't run there.
7. **Long gaps.** Restore saved history plus live running, pending and request state. Partial reply text lost from the host's ring buffer isn't rebuilt.
8. **Timing.** The milestone after 2.0.1. #1598 ships first.

## Slices

Upstream Desktop's adapter is the model: `apps/desktop/src/api/canonical-protocol.ts` and `apps/desktop/docs/canonical-gateway-protocol.md` at the pin. Hermex's adapter goes where a `HermesCall` becomes a frame (`HermesGateway.send`).

1. #1601 attach and replay, plus `local-hermes --gateway` and canonical fixtures
2. #1602 send, controls, and request answers
3. #1603 session edits through `session.mutate`
4. #1604 session settings
5. #1605 rooms: seatable Profiles, Retry, Discard
6. #1606 enable Webapp connections, check host identity, docs

## Owner-only steps

- hermex-push's `POST /restart` re-execs the whole gateway when the gateway serves the dashboard, skipping its drain. Confirmed in source 2026-11-06 and filed as uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#33. #1606 hides restart on canonical hosts until that ships.
- Phone validation of the final head (#1606).

## What breaks (reproduced locally against 0.22.5, `bf0203a7`, 2026-10-24; re-run at 0.23.0 in the comments)

Each was sent exactly as Hermex sends it (`HermesCall.swift`, `HermesConversation.swift`), on a legacy socket (works) and an authority socket:

- `session.resume`: 4001 for `close_on_disconnect`. Without it the reply carries `stored_session_id` but no `session_key`, which a Bot Chat attach requires (`HermesConversation.attachedKey`).
- `prompt.submit`: 4001 without `submission_id` / `input_id`. With one, it admits and completes.
- `session.interrupt`: 4001 `stale_generation` without `execution_generation`. Steer and redirect likewise.
- `session.title`, `session.delete`, `session.branch`, `session.undo`, `session.compress`, `session.cwd.set`, `session.close`: -32601. Their equivalents are `session.mutate` / `session.detach`.
- `config.set` model: 4001 `use_session_mutation_model`. `fast` and `yolo` with `scope: "session"`: 4001.
- `session.events.since` without the session's own `replay_epoch` (from the resume snapshot, not `gateway.ready`): `truncated: true, snapshot_required: true`, every time. Snapshots use `pending`/`prompts` rather than `queued`/`inflight`.
- `groups.retry` `{room_id, task_id}`: 4001. It needs `member_id` and `execution_generation`. Indeterminate executions also offer Discard, which Hermex can't answer.
- `groups.capabilities` there adds `seatable_profiles`; the room creator (`BotRoomCreator.swift:35`) should offer only those Profiles.
- Open (no-password) sign-in: the gateway withholds the page token.
- From the source, not reproduced: approvals use `prompt_id` and a different receipt, and sudo/secret answers through `request.answer` can report "expired" while the request still waits.
- hermex-push's `POST /restart` re-execs the whole process after only legacy-session teardown, skipping the gateway's drain. That belongs in uzairansaruzi/hermex-push.

Upstream contract: `x-canonical-methods` in `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`, `gateway/session_controls.py`, `gateway/session_group_controls.py`, `tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py`. On main (unreleased), `36a9d412b3` ([#143105](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/143105)) restores `open_requests` in canonical replay.

title: fix(tasks): show a script-only run's output from its row
body:
**What the user gets:** tapping a run of a script-only Task (a cron job with no agent) shows what it printed, instead of an error.
**Why it matters:** since hermes-agent 0.21.6 these runs appear in a Task's history, but every one fails to open in Hermex, so the history looks broken.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed.

## What the host sends

Since 0.21.6 (`c2182f60c1`, [NousResearch/hermes-agent#122856](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/122856)), `GET /api/cron/jobs/{id}/runs` also lists runs of script-only (`no_agent`) jobs, which never create a session. Each is a synthetic row with `source: "cron_output"`, an id of `cron_output:<job_id>:<stem>` (or `cron_output:<job_id>:exec:<n>` for a metadata-only run whose output file was pruned), a `preview` of up to 180 characters of the output, and `message_count: 0`. Code at 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`): `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py:264-400`, `:593`. Upstream has no route that opens these ids; the row is the whole record.

## What Hermex does today

`HermesCronClient.cronRunDetail` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCronClient.swift:130`) reads the run as a session, `HermesREST.sessionMessages(key:)`. `HermesREST.isSegment` (`HermesREST.swift:451`, `:853`) allows only alphanumerics, `_` and `-`, so a colon id throws `BotFailure.invalidAddress` before any request goes out.

## Scope

- Decode `source` and `preview` on a run row (`HermesCronRuns.Run`, tolerantly).
- A `cron_output` run opens to its preview as the output, with no request, and says it is a preview when the host truncated it. A row with no preview says the run left no output.
- Don't loosen `isSegment`.

## Test

One test: a runs page with a `cron_output:` row opens to its preview and sends no request.

title: chore(hermes): advance the hermes-agent pin to 0.22.5
body:
**What the user gets:** Hermex is tested against the Hermes release people actually run, so drift like the 0.22.x Bot Chat change is caught before users report it.
**Why it matters:** `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` is still 0.21.5 (`ca678285`, 2026-09-24), while the maintainer's host runs 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`) and upstream's latest is 0.22.7. The fixtures and docs still describe 0.21.5.
**Cost:** Medium. No host restart for 0.22.5. It runs against the live host, with one real model call in a disposable session, so a paired phone may get a push.

## Target

0.22.5, the release the host already runs. The pin follows the live host, and 0.22.7 would need the owner to update and restart the host first. Advance again after that.

## Before the procedure

`scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures` runs its turn on the `inbox-triage` Profile (`scripts/fixtures/HermesFixtureCapture.swift`), which no longer exists on the host. Choose another Profile and update the script and its header. Recommendation: a dedicated Profile the owner creates for fixtures, so captures never touch one in daily use.

## Procedure

Run the pin procedure in `CLAUDE.md` § Working with the server: both lines of `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` plus `HermesCompatibility.testedVersion`, `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures` (and `--local` for the tool/approval fixture), the OpenRPC diff for the methods `HermesCall` defines, the `/openapi.json` diff for `HermesREST`, one `clarify` and one approval in a disposable session, `HermesAgentFixtureTests`, `BotConnectionVersionTests`, and `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md`.

A first check found every method `HermesCall` sends still present at 0.22.5 and 0.22.7. It did not reliably compare parameters, so the full diff still has to run.

The host's checkout has local edits to `gateway/platforms/webhook.py` and `hermes_cli/venv_sync.py`. Say so in the PR's validation record.

## Check at the new pin

Low priority, found by source reading on 2026-11-03, not reproduced. Fix them in the pin PR only if trivial; otherwise file them.

- `message.complete` flags: Hermex ignores `response_previewed`, `response_reused` and `response_transformed` (`ChatViewModel.hermesTurnDidComplete` keeps a matching suffix and appends anything else). A rewritten final reply should flash as a duplicate until the receipt's history refresh replaces it, since the stored row holds the rewritten text. Confirm it clears.
- Skipped `clarify` as `null`: `lock_answer` treats `None` as skipped, but `BotQuestionRequest` reads `locked[qid].text`, so a question another client skipped shows as unanswered when reconnecting to a batch that's still open. Hermex's own skip sends `""` and isn't affected.
- Gateway listener: #1341 reproduced against 0.22.5 already. Re-run it if the target moves past that. As of 0.22.7, `session_authority` is still only set in `gateway/run_api.py`.

## Split out

- #1563: a rollback offered as "Update available"
- #1564: a retried Card's age
- #1565: the wrong reason on a refused file read
- #1566: Memory on an SSH Profile

Already fixed: the Bot Chat break that prompted this (#1339, #1346).

title: fix(hermes): balance the Bots and Sessions switch

title: fix(bots): follow a Bot Chat the host replaced
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1339

## What changed

A user's Bot Chats stopped working after a host update. Since hermes-agent 0.22.3, the first bot delivery moves aside a Bot Chat the host can't own (a messaging channel's or an API conversation): it is retitled `Bot Chat (<platform> <id>)` and unhidden, and a new hidden local `Bot Chat` takes the title. Hermex's open chat then dead-ended on "The conversation identity changed. Check this bot in Desktop."

Now the chat follows the new Bot Chat:

- **Follow:** `HermesConversation.identify` adopts the new root instead of throwing `wrongIdentity`, and tells its owner first.
- **Clean rebuild:** the coordinator drops the old chat's history and rebuilds from the new one. The old chat's running turn ends quietly as cancelled, with no alert. Its `/btw` question, background tasks, queued line, run outcome and "Load earlier" go too.
- **Notice:** one notice after the new chat's rows says "Hermes started a new Bot Chat. The earlier conversation is in Sessions under its new name." The same notice covers a chat that opens on a cached copy of the old root, whether or not that copy was shown yet.
- **Send safety:** nothing reaches the new chat before that notice has actually shown.
  - `attachForWrite()` guards send, queue and steer, plus rewind, undo, compress and branch.
  - A write tapped before the notice, or during the attach that finds the swap, fails with "Not sent: Hermes started a new Bot Chat." and keeps the draft.
  - The notice waits for a successful history read, so a failed read keeps the empty-chat error and Retry, and writes stay held.
  - The old root's cached copy is kept until the notice shows, so a chat reopened before then notices the swap again.
- **Deep links:** a stale link (`linkedRoot`) now opens the current Bot Chat with the same notice. The #554 "That conversation is no longer available." pop-back and its plumbing (`linkedRootIsStale`, `onChatReplaced`) are removed.

`docs/agents/bots.md` is updated. The two new strings are in the String Catalog with every shipped language.

**Accepted gaps:**
- `/btw`, `/background`, `/goal`, host slash commands, settings writes and request answers skip the send guard. They can reach the new chat only while its history read is failing, and none of them carries the draft.
- The notice's wording assumes a swap, so it is off when the old chat was archived rather than swapped; the client can't tell the two apart.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim E65FD38D-075D-4F1A-9552-7805FF1F4BE7` with `--only` for `HermesChatTurnTests`, `HermesConversationTests`, `BotDeepLinkTests`, `HermesOfflineCacheTests`, `HermesChatSideTaskTests`, `HermesHistoryRewindTests`, `HermesBranchDuplicateTests`, `HermesSlashCommandTests`, `BotMentionTests` and `HermesChatLiveActivityTests`: 234 passed, 0 failed.
- New and changed tests:
  - `testABotChatTheHostReplacedIsFollowedAndASendAcrossTheSwapIsHeld` covers a reattach that follows the swap. The send is held, the notice comes after the new chat's rows, and the next send goes out.
  - `testANewCanonicalRootDiscardsTheCachedTranscript` covers a cold open on a cached old copy with a failed history read. A send is held, including from a chat reopened through the early reconnect path. The notice then shows and the send goes out.
  - The engine and deep-link tests now assert follow rather than refusal.
- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py` passes: all 2489 keys are covered.
- Signed Debug build (`build_run_sim`) on iPhone 17 against the live Hermes host: a bot's Bot Chat opened from the Bots inbox attaches and shows its transcript, with no notice and no identity error. That's the regression check on the normal path.
- A real swap needs a Telegram or API bot, which the maintainer doesn't run, so there are no before/after screenshots of the notice. The unit tests cover it.

## Checklist

title: fix(hermes): explain that a gateway's own listener isn't supported yet
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1340

## What changed

Since hermes-agent 0.22.1, a Hermes gateway serves its own copy of the dashboard on a protocol Hermex doesn't speak yet (#1341). If Hermex reached that listener through a tunnel, it either signed in and then failed every chat with cryptic errors, or refused with the generic "does not support Bot chat here." Now it says what's wrong and what to do: "This address is a Hermes gateway’s own listener, which Hermex doesn’t support yet. Connect to hermes dashboard instead."

- **Gateway handshake:** when `gateway.ready` carries `session_authority: true`, the connect fails with a new `BotFailure.gatewayListener` before `client.capabilities` or anything else is sent. It is never retried, like other permanent refusals.
- **Sign-in without a password:** the listener's page withholds the session token but still writes `__HERMES_AUTH_REQUIRED__=false`. That bootstrap tells it apart from a page that isn't a dashboard's, which keeps the old `.unsupported` result.
- Push setup and Kanban handle the new case the same way as the other permanent refusals. The copy is in the String Catalog with all 17 shipped languages. `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` covers both checks.

I checked both signals against hermes-agent 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`): only the gateway's listener sets `session_authority` (`gateway/run_api.py` `_bind_state`, `tui_gateway/ws.py`) and `withhold_session_token` (`hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py` `_serve_index`). Plain `hermes dashboard` and `hermes serve`, including the 0.21.5 pin, never do.

**Accepted gap:** Add Server signs in over HTTP only, so a listener with a password is saved, then refused at its first gateway connect. The Sessions list shows the new copy straight away. Opening a socket on every Add Server would change more than the issue scoped.

  - `testAnOpenGatewayListenerIsNamedAtSignIn`: a token-less dashboard page gets the new failure, and a page that isn't a dashboard's still gets `.unsupported`.

title: fix(tasks): show a script-only run's output from its row
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1342

## What changed

Since hermes-agent 0.21.6, a Task's run history also lists runs of script-only Tasks (cron jobs with no agent). Every one of them failed to open in Hermex with "Enter a Hermes HTTP or HTTPS address without a path, credentials or query.", so the history looked broken.

These rows are synthetic: `source: "cron_output"`, an id like `cron_output:<job>:<stem>` that no route opens, and a `preview` of up to 180 characters of the output. Hermex read every run as a session, and the colon in the id failed address validation before any request went out.

Now the row carries its own output. `HermesCronRuns` decodes `source` and `preview`, and only a `cron_output` row keeps its preview as `scriptOutput` (a session row's `preview` is its prompt). `cronRunDetail` takes the run row instead of only its filename, so the Hermes client can answer a script-only run from the row without sending a request. webui still reads by filename. The run sheet adds a short note when the host cut the preview: it ends in "…" and is 179–180 code points long, matching upstream's `_cron_output_run_preview`. A run with no preview shows the existing "No output for this run." `isSegment` is unchanged. The new string is in the catalog in all 17 shipped languages.

Both callers are covered. A failed script-only run's latest-output card on the Task detail now shows its preview (for an `exec:` row, the run's error) instead of nothing.

I checked the contract against hermes-agent 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`, `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py`) and against real rows from that host.

title: Question and suggestion: staying signed in after an iPhone restart
body:
### Use case

Hi Uzair,

First of all, thank you for building Hermex. I really enjoy using it — having a native iPhone app for my self-hosted Hermes setup is genuinely useful, and I appreciate the work you’ve put into the project.

I’ve noticed that after I restart my iPhone, Hermex asks me to enter my password again. My server configuration is still there, but I need to sign in again.

I wanted to ask: **is this expected behavior, perhaps for security reasons?** I couldn’t find documentation mentioning it, though I may have missed something.

If this isn’t intentional, or if there’s room for an improvement, it would be nice to stay signed in across an iPhone restart when it is safe to do so.

### Proposed behavior

Could Hermex securely restore the sign-in after a device restart without asking for the password again, where the server’s authentication flow allows it?

One possible approach might be to use the iOS Keychain to store an appropriate credential or session token, but I’m not sure which approach best fits Hermex’s existing authentication design. Local Keychain storage might be sufficient; I don’t think iCloud Keychain sync would necessarily be needed just for this.

I’d really appreciate your thoughts on whether this is intended and what approach you would consider appropriate. If you’re open to it, I’d be happy to help investigate and work with you on a fix or improvement.

Thanks again for your work on Hermex!

### Acceptance outcomes

- After an iPhone restart, an existing sign-in can be restored without re-entering the password, when supported and secure.
- If the session has genuinely expired or been revoked, the app still asks the user to sign in again.

### Upstream dependency notes

I’m not yet sure whether this behavior comes from Hermex, the server’s authentication/session handling, or the interaction between them.

title: fix(chat): give on-device Listen the same playback controls as server speech
body:
**What the user gets:** Listen shows its playback bar, scrubbing, speed, and Lock Screen / Control Center controls whether the reply is spoken by the server or by the phone's voice.
**Why it matters:** Found while preparing the App Review reply for 2.0 (2) (rejected under 2.5.4 for background audio). When server speech fails, or a reply is over the host's 4,000-character limit, Listen falls back to the on-device voice: the bar flashes and disappears, and audio keeps playing in the background with no way to pause or scrub it. That's also what an App Reviewer is most likely to see.
**Cost:** Small to Medium. Needs the owner's hands on a phone for the background and Lock Screen check.

## Problem

`ChatViewModel.toggleListening` has two playback paths. Server audio goes through `AVAudioPlayer` with the playback bar and `MPRemoteCommandCenter`/`MPNowPlayingInfoCenter`. The on-device fallback (`speakWithOnDeviceSynthesizer`) clears that state and speaks live with `AVSpeechSynthesizer`, so it has no bar, no Now Playing, and no remote commands, while the `.playback` session keeps it audible in the background.

Repro on 2.0 (2), direct Hermes host whose speech fails (here: edge-tts 7.2.7 gets 403 from Microsoft since 2026-10-13; the host is fixed separately): tap Listen → bar flashes → on-device voice plays → go Home → no controls anywhere.

## Fix

Render the on-device speech to audio (`AVSpeechSynthesizer.write`), then play it through the same player as server audio. One playback path: the bar, seek, speed, and remote controls work for both voices, and the live-synthesizer code (utterance tracking, delegate) goes away.

Measured on a Mac: a 10,320-character reply (~9.5 min of audio) renders in ~8 s, first buffer at 0.9 s. A long fallback reply waits on the loading bar before speaking.

## Acceptance

- On-device Listen shows the playback bar with elapsed/duration, seek, and speed.
- After going Home or locking the phone, the Lock Screen / Control Center show the reply with working pause/play and scrubbing.
- Stopping or switching messages during rendering never starts stale audio.
- Server speech behavior is unchanged.

title: fix(chat): keep Listen's controls when the phone's voice reads a reply
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1352

## What changed

When server speech failed, or a reply was over the host's 4,000-character limit, Listen fell back to the phone's own voice. The playback bar flashed and disappeared, and audio kept playing in the background with no way to pause or scrub it, and nothing on the Lock Screen. That's also what App Review most likely saw when it rejected 2.0 (2) under 2.5.4 for background audio.

Now the on-device voice renders the reply to audio first (`AVSpeechSynthesizer.write`), then plays it through the same player as server speech. The playback bar, seek, speed and Now Playing controls work for both voices, and the separate live-speech code (utterance tracking and its delegate) is gone. Trade-off: a long fallback reply waits on the loading bar while it renders, about 3 s for a 4,900-character reply on the simulator.

Also fixed here: changing speed while Listen plays left iOS showing the reply as stopped. iOS takes Now Playing's state from the audio, and a mid-play rate change makes it report Stopped about 60 ms later while speech carries on, so the Lock Screen would show a paused reply whose play button does nothing. Listen now sends Now Playing again about a second after a speed change.

The host-side cause on the maintainer's server (edge-tts 7.2.7 getting 403 from Microsoft since 2026-10-13) is fixed separately on the host. It isn't part of this PR.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/ListenSynthesisTests`: 213 passed. The Listen tests now stub the on-device render, and a new test checks that stopping mid-render plays nothing.
- New `testOnDeviceSpeechRendersAudioTheListenPlayerCanPlay` runs the real synthesizer and decodes the result with the Listen player: passed 3/3 (`--repeat 3`).
- Signed Debug build in the simulator against the live Hermes host, in a disposable session that was deleted afterward:
  - Server speech: the host log shows Edge audio saved, and the bar shows 0:01 / 0:10.
  - On-device fallback (4,900-character reply, no host speech request): the bar shows 0:03 / 4:35. Scrubbing and 1.5× work. iOS's media service logs Hermex as Now Playing, and after going to the Home Screen the audio played to the end in the background.
  - Stop during loading: the bar clears and the media service logs no playback start.
- Speed change during playback, from iOS's media-service log in the simulator. Before the fix, it stayed Stopped at rate 0 while the app kept playing. After the fix, each of three changes was back to Playing at the new rate about 1.1 s later and stayed there. `testChangingSpeedWhilePlayingSendsNowPlayingAgainOnceItSettles` covers the re-send; without the fix it never completes.
- Not checked: the Lock Screen itself. The simulator's Control Center has no media module, so that's a phone check.
