## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Silent socket detection is bounded by the 8-second probe, including a stalled send; record attach time separately, without promising recovery within 10 seconds.
- [ ] Healthy sockets survive path changes; one failed probe yields one shared replacement.
- [ ] Network return wakes visible eligible inbox/list/room recovery without waiting for backoff.
- [ ] Offline recovery holds without network retries; terminal failures remain terminal.
- [ ] Background/close/server replacement cancels probes/retries; no command is resent.

## Manual test plan

1. Start a disposable long turn, switch Wi-Fi to cellular; record probe and reattach timings.
2. Repeat while idle; a healthy socket stays open.
3. Airplane Mode on/off on inbox, Sessions and a room: no offline retry churn, prompt recovery on return. Background/leave while offline and verify no hidden screen reconnects.
4. Use two configured servers to confirm old probes cannot affect the new server.

## Out of scope

Populated-list reconnect headers (#1374), unified connection phase (#1422), address failover ([#744](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/744)), HTTP reachability probes and background socket retention.

## Decisions

title: fix(chat): delay and hold the stream recovery chip so quick recoveries don't flash
body:
**What the user gets:** Quick stream recoveries stop flashing a status chip.
**Why it matters:** Small reusable show-after/hold-for primitive; the home reconnect status builds on it.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 09 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none (10 reuses the primitive) |
| Related GitHub issues | none found |
| Needs mock first | yes (static timing storyboards; preserve the existing chip design) |
| Sources | design-settings-opus #6 (also referenced by navigation-opus #2's 800 ms header delay) |

## Problem

The recovery capsule appears as soon as checking/reattaching starts and can disappear a moment later. Delaying transient checks could remove that flash while holding longer checks briefly. Frequency is unmeasured; capture a baseline before claiming an improvement.

## What T3 does

`packages/client-runtime/src/delayedStatus.ts` and `apps/mobile/src/lib/useDelayedStatus.ts` delay a status 400 ms and hold it 400 ms. `WorkspaceConnectionTitle.tsx` uses an 800 ms header delay. Port the state rule, not the React hook.

## Hermex today

`ChatTranscriptView.swift:549-554` mounts `StreamRecoveryStatusView` whenever raw state is non-idle. Its labels and spinner/static-dot handling are in `ChatTranscriptSupportingViews.swift:969-1016`; the transition uses `ChatMotion.bottomOverlayTransition` (`ChatMotion.swift:32-34`). Webui sets checking around status probes (`ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:730`, `:757`); Hermes maps recovering/disconnected at `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1684-1690`. `ActiveStreamRecoveryState` is at `ChatViewModel.swift:210-217`. There is no equivalent shared delay/hold primitive.

## Proposal

Add a small state machine plus a stable wrapper view. Schedule only the next deadline; use no repeating timer.

```swift
struct DelayedStatusPolicy: Equatable {
    var showAfter: Duration = .milliseconds(400)
    var holdFor: Duration = .milliseconds(400)
}

/// Stores pending/show/hold deadlines. The caller supplies time; the step never sleeps.
struct DelayedStatus<Value: Equatable> {
    private(set) var shown: Value?
    // Also stores showAt / holdUntil; `shown` alone cannot enforce a hold.
    mutating func update(target: Value?, now: ContinuousClock.Instant,
                         policy: DelayedStatusPolicy, immediately: Bool)
        -> ContinuousClock.Instant? // next deadline, or nil
}

/// Remains mounted even while `value` is nil, so it can complete its hold.
struct DelayedStatusView<Value: Equatable, Content: View>: View { … }
```

Rules:

- nil → non-nil: start `showAfter`; clear before the deadline and nothing shows. Changes between pending non-nil states keep that initial deadline.
- Once shown, clearing the target hides only after `holdFor`.
- A different non-nil value while shown swaps immediately and starts its own hold. A new status during a pending hide also replaces the held value immediately.
- `.waitingForNetwork` bypasses the show delay. This means immediately **when the coordinator publishes that state**, not immediately when Airplane Mode is enabled: a socket may still look connected until failure detection.

At `ChatTranscriptView.swift:549`, replace the raw conditional with a permanently mounted `DelayedStatusView`; map `.idle` to nil. The wrapper owns state and drives `update` on target/policy changes, then sleeps only until the returned deadline and steps again. `.task(id:)` cancels the old driver; check cancellation/ownership before every state write after awaiting. Leaving the chat or switching its server/session must discard pending/held status.

Keep `StreamRecoveryStatusView`'s existing layout, copy, accessibility hiding and Reduce Motion transition. Animate from the **shown** value; an animation keyed only on the raw recovery state will miss the delayed transition. Keep this state inside the wrapper so it does not invalidate transcript rows. No new third-party dependency.

## Implementation steps

1. Use `html-communication` for several static timing storyboards (instant / 400 ms / 800 ms delay, with the existing chip). Include short recovery, sustained recovery and offline. Publish, report the URL and stop for a maintainer pick; recommend 400/400 ms.
2. Add `DelayedStatus.swift` under `HermesMobile/Features/Shared/`: the policy, the pure stepper and `DelayedStatusView`. Write doc comments on use. It's shared because 10 uses it on the home headers.
3. Replace the conditional at `ChatTranscriptView.swift:549-554` with `DelayedStatusView`.
4. Check that the accessibility element appears and disappears with the shown value, not the raw state, so VoiceOver doesn't announce flashes either.
5. Add tests, then run one signed simulator pass with a scripted recovery fixture if available. For real network behavior, the maintainer changes only the test phone's connectivity. Do not restart a live dashboard or alter a host/tunnel for this check.

## Surfaces

Sessions/Bot Chat on both server kinds, not rooms; app/tests only. Preserve accessibility hiding/labels, existing Reduce Motion transition and server/session lifetime. No new catalog keys, transport logic or repeating animation. No docs change.

## Tests

`DelayedStatusTests` (new, pure, injected instants, no sleeps; run each through the same mutating step used by the wrapper):

- `testBriefStatusNeverShows`: set, then clear before 400 ms, gives nothing shown.
- `testShownStatusHoldsBeforeHiding`: shown at t = 400 ms and cleared at 450 ms stays shown until 800 ms.
- `testShownStatusSwapsAtOnce`: checking → reconnecting while shown is immediate.
- `testImmediateValueSkipsTheDelay`: waiting for network shows at t = 0.
- Cover a new target arriving during the held hide, so an old scheduled hide cannot erase it. A hosted wrapper case must prove the hold survives target nil and a cancelled/disappeared driver cannot publish late; use an injected deadline sleeper and expectations.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/DelayedStatusTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The maintainer picked a timing storyboard before implementation.
- [ ] A recovery that settles in under 400 ms shows no chip.
- [ ] A longer recovery shows the chip after 400 ms and keeps it at least 400 ms.
- [ ] Checking → Reconnecting changes the label without a hide or show cycle.
- [ ] Once the raw recovery state becomes `.waitingForNetwork`, its chip appears without the show delay.
- [ ] Reduce Motion still uses the opacity transition. No repeating timers are added.

## Manual test plan

1. Use a scripted recovery to verify a sub-400 ms check shows no chip. On a physical test phone, start a disposable Hermes turn and toggle Wi-Fi with cellular available; record observed recovery rather than assuming a one-second network toggle produces a quick check.
2. Keep the test phone's route unavailable long enough for recovery detection. Once the raw recovery state appears, verify the chip's delay/hold; restore connectivity and confirm it clears.
3. Turn on Airplane Mode. Once the coordinator detects disconnection and publishes waiting-for-network, that chip bypasses the display delay.
4. Repeat step 2 with Reduce Motion on.

## Out of scope

Home headers (#1374) and other indicators. Keep the existing spinner/static-dot decision; replacing its visuals is a separate mock decision.

## Decisions

**Timing?** Recommend 400/400 ms for the chip; 10 uses 800 ms for headers. Validate on device rather than treat T3's values as proof.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: fix(home): say "Reconnecting" on populated Sessions and Bots lists instead of going quiet
body:
**What the user gets:** Sessions and Bots lists say Reconnecting/Offline instead of silently clearing every Working label.
**Why it matters:** On a tunnel drop the list currently implies nothing is running when it doesn't know.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 10 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability / UI |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | #1373 (show delay and hold), #1372 (the "reconnect now" hook a tap reuses) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1088](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1088) (overlaps: it redesigns this header as a pinned `TopNav` with an offline `HermexBanner`, so the mock must fit that slot, and whichever lands second adapts) |
| Needs mock first | **yes** |
| Sources | navigation-opus #2, connection-state-sol #3 |

## Problem

A retryable gateway loss keeps populated Sessions/Bots lists on screen but clears live labels and often shows no failure. The list looks idle while freshness is unknown. A quiet reconnect indicator plus explicitly stale labels would explain that state.

## What T3 does

`apps/mobile/src/features/home/workspace-connection-status.ts` derives offline/reconnect/sync text. `WorkspaceConnectionTitle.tsx` delays it 800 ms and opens connection settings on tap. `features/threads/floating-working-status.ts` keeps connection notices independent of retained thread content.

## Hermex today

- Sessions `dropHermes` (`Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:2212-2230`) clears attention states and suppresses retryable errors with rows. `showsOfflineCache` (`:104`) only describes cached data, not this state; `SessionListComponents.swift:746-748` renders errors only for an empty list.
- Bots `drop` (`Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:854-878`) clears `liveStatuses`; route advice requires an empty roster (`:867-869`). `BotsInboxView.swift:151-158` renders only supplied advice/errors.
- Row/roster success is **not status success**: `reloadHermes` starts a separate status read (`SessionListViewModel.swift:1977`), as `BotInbox.reload` does (`BotInbox.swift:607`). Status-read failures also clear labels without dropping the socket (`:2282-2286` and `:647-651`, respectively).
- `SessionsHeader` (`SessionListComponents.swift:212-260`) serves home Sessions (`HermesSessionListView.swift:131-140`) and Bots (`BotsInboxView.swift:238-245`). Standalone `/sessions` has native toolbar chrome (`HermesSessionListView.swift:952-965`).

## Proposal

Expose two separate model facts: retry/reconnect state and live-label freshness. Reuse 08's recovery eligibility rather than invent another retry scheduler.

- Enter reconnecting on a retryable drop with retained rows. Clear it only in the current row/roster read's success branch. `reloadHermes()` catches failures and returns Void, so returning from it is not success. A failed read keeps actionable recovery; a terminal refusal shows existing advice even with populated rows, never an endless reconnect label.
- Derive Offline from the device path, immediately; otherwise show Reconnecting only during eligible recovery. Initial loading is separate. Use 09 with 800 ms show / 400 ms hold; suppress the header when `showsOfflineCache` already explains the state.
- Keep last live labels on retryable loss, styled secondary and announced as "last known". Fresh row data can settle the header before `session.active_list` returns, so freshness must remain stale independently. Only a current successful status reply replaces/clears labels. On transient status-read failure retain stale labels and existing status retry; unsupported `-32601` clears labels and settles instead of looping.
- Terminal disconnect clears labels. Reset recovery/freshness on true close, server/connection replacement and Sessions Profile changes; an internal retry must preserve stale status. Retain wire/read-serial guards and write eligibility.
- Online Reconnecting is a button using 08's guarded `reconnectNow()`. Offline is informational until the path returns. Terminal auth uses existing sign-in recovery. No spinner/countdown; opacity only, none under Reduce Motion.

Place the indicator in the selected header/toolbar slot; this issue does not implement [#1088](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1088)'s proposed redesign.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks first**, using `html-communication`: several distinct static placements (replace logo / line below / proposed TopNav integration), Sessions and Bots, light/dark. Include reconnect/offline, stale labels, terminal advice with retained rows and pushed `/sessions`. Publish URL and stop for a maintainer pick; do not assume TopNav already exists.
2. Add model recovery/freshness facts and success/failure/lifetime rules; preserve stale labels through retry's internal close/open.
3. Build `HomeConnectionStatusView` per the pick using 09; wire both homes and the pushed list. Reuse 08's reconnect hook.
4. Forward freshness into `Features/SessionList/SessionRowView.swift`, ordinary/Scheduled callers, and `BotHeroTile` / `BotInboxRow` (`BotsInboxView.swift:761`, `:806`). Preserve shared webui behavior.
5. Update `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`, run focused tests and a signed integrated pass with before/after evidence.

## Surfaces

Both home sides, compact/split and pushed Sessions; app/tests only. State belongs to active-server models, with Profile resets and stale-reply rejection. Existing chat chip stays independent. Verify Dynamic Type, VoiceOver (one status announcement; "last known" labels), Reduce Motion, light/dark and RTL. Localize selected copy through `docs/agents/i18n.md`. No extension, cache/outbox or transport-contract changes.

## Tests

- `HermesSessionListTests`: drop with rows keeps stale labels and reconnect state; accept rows while holding status reply → header settles but labels stay stale; status success settles freshness. Terminal auth clears labels.
- `BotInboxTests`: same split between roster/status success. Extend the status case for transient failure and unsupported method; a replaced server/Profile's late reply never makes labels current.
- 09's `DelayedStatusTests` owns timing. Use scripted clocks/expectations, no sleeps.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/DelayedStatusTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Maintainer selected a mock before implementation.
- [ ] Retained rows show Reconnecting after 800 ms; brief recovery never flashes. Offline bypasses delay; cache banner suppresses duplicate indicators.
- [ ] Labels remain visibly/accessibly stale until authoritative statuses return, including when roster/pages arrive first.
- [ ] Header settles on row/roster success; terminal failures stay actionable with rows.
- [ ] Online tap bypasses backoff; offline waits without doomed retries.
- [ ] Profile/server replacement rejects old state; no spinner/repeating animation or unchanged-state publication.

## Manual test plan

1. Use disposable work on a test server; alter only phone connectivity. On each home side, observe reconnect/offline and stale labels, then restore the path and verify freshness.
2. Tap online Reconnecting to bypass backoff; offline waits. Check terminal sign-in advice without hiding retained rows.
3. Repeat on iPad split/pushed Sessions, then VoiceOver/Reduce Motion at AX3 and a server switch. Leave live hosts/tunnels untouched.

## Out of scope

Unified per-server connection phase (#1422), diagnosis details (#1395), Bots cache-first roster (#1403), or the larger [#1088](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1088) redesign.

## Decisions

**Placement?** Recommend a quiet line under the logo and the same indicator on pushed `/sessions`; the mock pick decides.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: fix(chat): keep the composer editable while the chat is offline
body:
**What the user gets:** You can type while the chat is offline; only Send waits.
**Why it matters:** Today the composer is disabled offline, so you can't even draft on a train. Prerequisite for the offline outbox.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 1 (#1359) · order 11 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability / UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | #1367 (reuse its disabled reason) |
| Related GitHub issues | none identified; #1407 builds on this |
| Needs mock first | no (existing status line/copy; editing availability only) |
| Sources | composer-opus #1 (slice A only) |

## Problem
When chat falls back to cached data, the composer becomes disabled and the user cannot write the next instruction. Drafts already persist per server and session. Let the user write while holding delivery until reconnect.

## What T3 does
T3 keeps its editor editable when delivery is deferred (`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadComposer.tsx:470-478,599`, `deliveryDeferred` / `canSend`). Sending later through an outbox is separate work (#1407).

## Hermex today
- `ChatView.composerReadOnlyMessage(for:isViewingCachedData:)` returns the reconnect message for `viewModel.showsOfflineCache`, or “Read-only” for a read-only session (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:733-752`, passed at `:539`). `showsOfflineCache` describes a cached-data fallback, not every gateway disconnect.
- `MessageComposerView.isReadOnly` means any non-nil message (`Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:348-350`). It disables the editor (`:968`), focus (`:1596-1598`), file autocomplete (`:376-379`), dictation/voice notes (`:1437-1462`), configuration (`:1433-1435`), branch picker (`:1226`), workspace management (`:826`) and Send (`:1498-1501`).
- `ChatViewModel.sendMessage` already refuses cached-data sends (`Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:2863-2868`). The webui attachment upload path refuses them too (`ChatAttachmentCoordinator.swift:299-304`).
- A provisional cached transcript shown while Hermes connects already keeps editing live and holds Send through `isCachedCopyProvisional` (`ChatView.swift:530-535`). `HermesOfflineCacheTests.swift:330-341` covers that precedent. Preserve it.

## Proposal
Separate editing permission from delivery availability:

- Keep `readOnlyMessage` exclusively for `session.isSessionReadOnly`; all current restrictions remain for those sessions, even offline.
- Add `sendHoldMessage` for `showsOfflineCache`, using the existing reconnect copy/status line. Text, quotes, existing chips, local slash suggestions and ↑ recall remain usable; Send and keyboard/alternate send remain held.
- Hold host-dependent controls: file/host argument searches, voice notes, dictation, configuration/branch/workspace changes and webui attachment imports. Preserve existing Hermes local attachment staging; expanding its UI is out of scope.
- Gate callbacks as well as buttons so an action captured before connectivity changed cannot write. Do not disable Stop merely by disabling Send; preserve its separate current policy where a run still exists.

Draft edits keep using `onDraftEdit` → `ChatDraftStore.setContent(..., for: draftKey)` (`ChatView.swift:687,2780`). Reconnect removes the hold without replacing or sending the draft. No new storage/outbox/connection state.

## Implementation steps
1. Split `ChatView.composerReadOnlyMessage` from a new `composerSendHoldMessage` and pass both to `MessageComposerView`.
2. Add `isSendHeld` to send availability and the host-dependent guards above. Keep `isReadOnly` alone for editor editability/focus. Gate webui picker/paste/drop callbacks without disabling text paste. Block `hostSlashArgumentText`, `fileTrigger`, branch selection and workspace management (`managementServer` at `:826`), including already-open controls.
3. Show the hold in `composerStatus` after a true read-only message (`:1328-1331`). Include it as Send’s disabled reason from 03 without losing the action name.
4. Hold dictation through `isVoiceInputDisabled`, preserving its early return that allows an already-listening user to stop. Offline/on-device dictation is deferred.
5. Update the helper’s existing test call sites (`SessionIdentityTests.swift:116-130`, `SessionListMutationTests.swift:2461,2572`, `HermesOfflineCacheTests.swift:338`). Read `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` before changing draft wiring; no keying change is expected.

## Surfaces
Sessions and Bot Chat use this composer; rooms have their own editing policy and are unchanged. Main app/tests only; share handoff should still populate the main app’s offline draft. Widget/notification service are unaffected. Server/session draft isolation remains intact. Reconnect reverses the hold; no automatic send. LAN, Tailscale and tunnel loss use the same fallback. Preserve Dynamic Type/VoiceOver and existing animation behavior. No durable doc changes needed.

## Tests
- Extend `HermesOfflineCacheTests`: offline cached data allows editing, provides a send-hold reason, and `sendMessage` refuses without a write. Assert availability, not exact copy. Keep provisional-cache coverage.
- `SessionIdentityTests`: a read-only session retains its editing restriction when offline.
- If callback/gate policy is extracted, cover a stale enabled callback after a hold arrives; do not test only the helper string while leaving editor wiring unchecked.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesOfflineCacheTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionIdentityTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionListMutationTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With cached/offline data visible, text/quotes remain editable and persist across chat reopening.
- [ ] Send and every keyboard/alternate send are held with the reconnect reason; host-only controls cannot dispatch.
- [ ] Genuinely read-only sessions remain locked.
- [ ] Reconnect retains the draft and permits one deliberate send; provisional cached behavior remains unchanged.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable chat, disconnect the device network and reopen to show the offline cache. Type/quote, leave and reopen, and verify the draft survives while sends and host controls stay held. Restore the device network and send once. Check webui, a read-only session and server switching; do not stop or reconfigure the maintainer’s tunnel/server.

## Out of scope
Offline delivery/outbox (#1407); new offline attachment controls; on-device dictation changes (#1418).

## Decisions
None. Recommend holding all dictation in this slice.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): name what a tool group did instead of counting hidden calls
body:
**What the user gets:** Collapsed tool groups say what happened ("Ran 4 commands and changed 2 files") and keep failures visible.
**Why it matters:** "+N previous tool calls" hides what a turn did and can hide a failed call.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 12 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none (decoded tool calls) |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#262](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/262) (adjacent; maintainer reserved transcript/denser-row design, so keep this a picked, narrow slice) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | chat-timeline-opus #1, chat-timeline-sol #6 |

## Problem
“+12 previous tool calls” says how much happened but gives no clue what happened. A failed older call also disappears behind that toggle. A concise work summary and static failure marker make the collapsed group useful at a glance.

## What T3 does
`summarizeToolGroup` (`packages/client-runtime/src/work-log/presentation.ts:517-603`) selects two leading action buckets, counts distinct edited files (`:405-420`), and rolls up the rest as other actions. `apps/mobile/src/features/threads/thread-work-log.tsx:1272-1367` carries failure into accessibility text; a visible failure marker is a Hermex proposal.

## Hermex today
- `ToolActivityGroupView` keeps the newest row visible and toggles previous rows with “+N previous tool calls” / “Show fewer tool calls” (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ToolActivityGroupView.swift:38-62,85-112`). The title and VoiceOver label use the same count string.
- `ToolCallSummaryFormatter.Kind` classifies calls (`Features/Chat/ToolCallSummaryFormatter.swift:57-59,113-135`); `ToolCallLogRow.status` exposes failure (`:4-41`). `changedFilesPreview(args:)` extracts unique full paths within a call before making a display string (`:240-268`).
- Sessions and Bot Chat use the same groups, live/settled (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:538,614,832,840`). Settled-turn folding is separate (`TranscriptTurnFolding.swift:24-60`).

## Proposal
Add pure `ToolCallGroupSummary` beside the formatter, derived from the hidden entries already available in the body. Keep structured kind/count values and `failedCount`, then format localized text separately.

- Successful writes count the union of full paths **across** calls. Extract `changedPaths(args:) -> [String]`, reused by `changedFilesPreview`; use a set to aggregate. Pathless writes count as actions, not fictional files.
- Failed, interrupted and running writes do not claim completed file changes: count them among other actions and retain failure information. Other kinds count calls (“read actions” unless distinct file paths are actually known). Unknown kinds are other actions.
- Choose up to two nonzero kinds by priority: write, shell, delegate, search, read, web, then remaining kinds. Roll omitted calls into other actions. The summary describes hidden entries only; the newest row stays separate.
- Use String Catalog plural variants and Foundation list formatting (precedent `BotRoomView.swift:546`), with locale-aware casing only on the initial grapheme. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`; do not capitalize every word or hand-build English conjunctions.
- Collapsed title is the sentence; expanded title stays “Show fewer tool calls”. With failures, show a static triangle and include a localized failure count in VoiceOver. Pick wrapping/truncation through mocks; today’s title is one line.
- Parse no result bodies for this feature. Parent token updates can re-run the body; value inputs do not automatically make it token-independent. Measure before adding a cache and preserve stable row ids.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** use `html-communication` to publish three distinct alternatives (sentence alone; sentence/count; sentence/icons), including failure, light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Report URL and stop for the maintainer’s pick.
2. Extract `changedPaths` without changing `changedFilesPreview` output. Add `ToolCallGroupSummary.swift` in the main app target with structural counts and formatting.
3. Add catalog plural entries and render the picked toggle in `ToolActivityGroupView.previousRowsToggle` using `previousEntries`. Update its old-copy doc comment.
4. Preserve expansion, newest-row identity and Reduce Motion. Run `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` if a production Swift file grows.

## Surfaces
All Sessions/Bot Chat tool groups, live/settled, main app/tests only. Share/widget/notification service do not render transcripts. Pure presentation adds no server state. Expand/collapse remains the reverse path. Cover VoiceOver failure counts, plural/list localization, RTL leading/trailing placement, large Dynamic Type and contrast. No new animation or durable docs.

## Tests
New `ToolCallGroupSummaryTests`: repeated successful writes to one path count one changed file; failed/running/pathless writes cannot invent changed files; the priority rule and other-action accounting preserve all hidden calls. A failed hidden call yields a failure count. Assert structured meaning, not exact sentence copy. Review localized sentences in mocks/manual checks.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ToolCallGroupSummaryTests --only HermesMobileTests/ToolCallSummaryFormatterTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The collapsed toggle names leading work kinds and accounts for remaining hidden actions.
- [ ] Successful edits count distinct paths across calls; unsuccessful work never claims completed file edits.
- [ ] Hidden failures retain a static marker and spoken count.
- [ ] Existing expansion/newest-row behavior and per-call formatting remain functional.
- [ ] New sentences use catalog plurals and localized list formatting.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable Hermes session ask the agent to read several files, edit two and run a command. Expand its settled fold and inspect the summary. Trigger a failed command followed by more calls and inspect the hidden-failure marker. Check VoiceOver, large accessibility text, light/dark and RTL pseudolanguage.

## Out of scope
Turn restructuring, parallel grouping, group-height caps and fold restyling belong to the maintainer’s [#262](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/262) design. No new failure badge on the settled-turn fold.

## Decisions
None. Recommend keeping the failure marker scoped to the tool-group toggle.

title: feat(chat): show the latest thought while thinking, and Thought once settled
body:
**What the user gets:** While the agent thinks, the collapsed row shows its latest thought; settled rows say Thought.
**Why it matters:** Glanceable progress during long thinks; the row is stuck on the first sentence today.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 13 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none (already accumulated reasoning text) |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1029](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1029) (adjacent live-think scrolling); [#262](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/262) (overlapping settled-label idea; maintainer owns transcript design) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | chat-timeline-opus #2 |

## Problem
The collapsed reasoning row shows the first 80 characters throughout a run, so it never tells the reader where the agent has got to. Markdown headings appear with literal asterisks. Settled history still reads “Thinking”, as though it is active.

## What T3 does
A live collapsed work group shows its newest reasoning item’s `liveThoughtLine` (`packages/client-runtime/src/work-log/presentation.ts:633-645`; `apps/mobile/src/features/threads/thread-work-log.tsx:1301-1320`). The helper prefers an initial bold heading within that item, otherwise its first sentence, stripping common markdown. Titles settle from Thinking to Thought (`apps/mobile/src/lib/threadActivity.ts:1849-1854`). Hermex’s backward scan is an adaptation for its accumulated string, not a literal copy of T3’s helper.

## Hermex today
- `ReasoningBlockView` always uses Thinking in both title and VoiceOver (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ReasoningBlockView.swift:28-51`).
- `ReasoningSummaryFormatter.summary(for:)` takes the beginning, collapses newlines and cuts at 80 characters, scanning at most 320 (`Features/Chat/ReasoningSummaryFormatter.swift:6-40`). It does not strip markdown.
- `liveStreamID` distinguishes live/settled rendering (`ReasoningBlockView.swift:11,55-57`). The shared transcript supplies it for live blocks (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:530,821`), not settled ones (`:605,813`).
- `ReasoningSummaryFormatterTests` covers current cut behavior.

## Proposal
Add pure `ReasoningSummaryFormatter.latestThought(in:)`:

- Bound input first with a backward `suffix` of 2,000 characters. Parse only that slice; never regex the full accumulated stream before cutting. This is a fixed character bound, not an absolute byte/time guarantee for arbitrarily complex Unicode graphemes.
- Prefer the last completed bold heading line (`**…**`, optionally followed by text). Otherwise use the first sentence of the last nonempty paragraph in the slice, ending at `. ! ? 。 ！ ？` or paragraph end. Avoid treating a suffix-cut fragment as a whole paragraph when a complete trailing candidate exists.
- Strip common inline markdown: bold/emphasis/backticks, links to their visible text, leading heading/list markers. Preserve underscores inside identifiers. Use simple bounded text rules; do not add a Markdown renderer/parser dependency.
- Reuse existing whitespace/80-character truncation rules **after** stripping. Settled previews use bounded `prefix(scanLimit)` then stripping/cutting; live previews use the bounded tail. Do not silently change existing cut behavior beyond these intentional content changes.
- Live row: Thinking + latest thought. Settled row: Thought + the existing beginning-style summary, with markup stripped. VoiceOver follows the chosen title. Expanded reasoning content is unchanged.

No new state, timer or animation. Keep processing cost bounded per live update; this slice does not optimize the rest of reasoning rendering.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** use `html-communication` to publish 2–3 alternatives showing live heading/plain sentence and settled title, in light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Report URL and stop for a pick. The maintainer may retain Thinking because of the overlap with their transcript design.
2. Add the bounded tail/stripping helpers in `ReasoningSummaryFormatter.swift`; update its comments and tests.
3. Choose title/detail in `ReasoningBlockView` from `liveStreamID`, updating its Thinking-only doc comment.
4. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` and add catalog title/accessibility strings, including Thought if picked. Run `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` when production Swift grows.

## Surfaces
Sessions/Bot Chat live/settled transcripts, app/tests only. Live Activities have separate excerpts; share/widget/notification service are unaffected. This pure presentation adds no server state; reattach/replay naturally updates the latest line. Preserve natural RTL, CJK terminators, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver. No new animation or durable docs.

## Tests
Extend `ReasoningSummaryFormatterTests`: latest heading wins; no-heading fallback uses the last paragraph’s first sentence; common markup strips without corrupting identifiers. A long text with its only heading outside the tail must ignore it. That result assertion checks selection semantics, **not** whether the implementation scanned the whole string; review the bounded-input code separately.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ReasoningSummaryFormatterTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Live collapsed previews progress with recent headings/sentences instead of staying at the beginning.
- [ ] Supported common markup does not leak into live/settled previews.
- [ ] Settled title follows the picked mock and VoiceOver agrees.
- [ ] Input is bounded before parsing; expanded reasoning stays selectable/unchanged.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable Hermes session choose a reasoning model and request a multi-step plan. Watch the collapsed detail advance, then inspect the settled title and reopen from history. Check VoiceOver, CJK prose, long reasoning and a markdown-heavy response.

## Out of scope
Fixing live-think scrolling ([#1029](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1029)); restructuring tool groups or moving thought text above them; full Markdown parsing.

## Decisions
Should the settled title change? Recommend Thought, decided through the mock pick because [#262](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/262) includes that design choice.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): keep answered questions readable in the transcript
body:
**What the user gets:** Answered clarify questions stay readable as Q&A in the transcript.
**Why it matters:** "What did I tell it?" is buried in raw tool output behind a fold.
**Cost:** Small–Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 14 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S–M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes `clarify` tool result, verified at pin below |
| Depends on | none; accommodate 12 if extending its summary enum |
| Related GitHub issues | [#462](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/462) (adjacent pending-card tap bug, not history) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | chat-timeline-opus #3, chat-timeline-sol #3 |

## Problem
After answering a question, the exchange survives as raw JSON in a generic tool row. Settled-turn folding hides it with the other activity. The user needs to see what they told the agent without expanding a whole run.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/QuestionAnswerHistory.tsx:42-80` renders question/answer pairs. Folding preserves those entries (`apps/mobile/src/lib/threadActivity.ts:1217-1219`); preview/accessibility text includes the answer (`thread-work-log.tsx:1009-1017,1162-1178`).

## Hermex today
- `clarify` is `.unknown` in `ToolCallSummaryFormatter.kind` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ToolCallSummaryFormatter.swift:113-148`). The generic result formatter shows JSON (`ToolCallDisplayFormatter.swift:71-83`).
- `ToolCallLogRowView` forces its whole row LTR (`ToolCallLogRowView.swift:43-45`), unsuitable for natural-language Q&A.
- `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock` hides activity and can omit the entire row when folded (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:716-769`). A compact Q&A child alone will not fix this unless `hasVisibleContent` accounts for it.

**Pinned contract:** rechecked using read-only `gh api repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/contents/<path>?ref=ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2` (`HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`, 0.21.5):

- `tools/clarify_tool.py:139-156`: batch `questions` returns this shape (example):
  ```json
  {"responses":[{"id":"q1","question":"Which?","choices_offered":["A","B"],"user_response":"A"}],"timed_out":true,"notice":"Why the wait ended"}
  ```
  Per response, `id` is optional, `choices_offered` can be null, and `user_response` is a string, string array, or `""` for unanswered/skipped. `timed_out` appears only when true; optional `notice` appears only beside it. There is no per-answer `status` or top-level `outcome`.
- Legacy single `question` returns `{question, choices_offered, user_response}` (`:188-236`), with a possible timeout sentinel. Match the exact `TIMEOUT_RESPONSE` at `:13-14`, not arbitrary timeout-like prose. A legacy multi-select answer can wrap that sentinel in a one-element array.
- Errors use `{"error":"…", ...}` (`tools/registry.py:1016-1019`); retain the generic failure row.
- Live `tool.complete` JSON-decodes its result (`tui_gateway/tool_progress.py:286-308`). Hermex carries it through `toolResultPreview` (`Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:466-474`; `Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1653-1663`). History uses the same preview (`Features/Chat/HermesTranscriptHistory.swift:230-237`).

## Proposal
Add pure `ClarifyResult` with exchanges (`question`, text/choices/unanswered answer), optional notice and a timeout flag. Use `ToolCallDisplayFormatter.parsedJSONValue(from:)` after unwrapping the preview. Apply only to normalized tool name `clarify` with a recognized result.

- Accept batch or legacy single form, with at least one nonempty question. Ignore unknown fields and optional metadata; `id`/choices/notice are not required for rendering.
- Map empty strings/arrays and the exact legacy sentinel to unanswered. Missing/unknown answer types are unrecognized, not evidence of a user skip; fall back to the generic result. Reject error envelopes first.
- Recognized rows use a question-bubble icon and a compact question/answer preview; expanded content lists selectable natural-direction pairs and any notice. Unrecognized/incomplete/error results retain the current header, body, status and copy behavior.
- A folded anchor exposes its recognized Q&A compactly, once per tool presentation id/exchange index. Expanded activity uses the full tool row instead. Preserve folding membership and existing first/last reply policy; include Q&A in `hasVisibleContent` for non-host anchors too. Follow the thinking/tool visibility setting in this slice.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** use `html-communication` to publish 2–3 alternatives covering single/batch, multi-select, timeout/notice and folded placement, including RTL, light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Report URL and stop for a pick.
2. Add `Models/ClarifyResult.swift` (main target) and parser tests. Keep result interpretation at the formatter/model boundary.
3. Wire recognized results into `ToolCallSummaryFormatter.row`/`copyText`, using localized Q/A labels. A new `.clarify` kind is optional; if added, update every switch including 12’s group summary.
4. Add `ClarifyHistoryBody` and bypass the row’s **outer** forced-LTR modifier for recognized Q&A, retaining LTR generic code rows.
5. Add the folded projection in `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock`, including `hasVisibleContent` and the setting gate. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` and add plural question-count/accessibility strings.

## Surfaces
Sessions/Bot Chat, live/history, app/tests only. Pending request cards, share, widget and notification service are unchanged. Shared formatting may recognize identical webui JSON without webui-specific work. Transcript identity already scopes server data; deduplicate by tool id, never question text. Reattach/history must converge. Dynamic Type, RTL and VoiceOver read Q/A naturally; retain Reduce Motion. Record the verified contract/pin in the eventual PR.

## Tests
New `ClarifyResultTests`: mixed batch text/blank/choices with optional ids, timeout and notice; legacy timeout including multi-select form; malformed answers and error/unrelated JSON fall back. Assert meaning, not editorial text.

Keep `TranscriptTurnFoldingTests`; cover a non-host activity-only anchor in a hosted/manual rendering pass, checking folded visibility and no duplicate when expanded.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ClarifyResultTests --only HermesMobileTests/ClarificationTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptTurnFoldingTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Recognized results read as Q&A live and after reopening, including multi-select and unanswered results.
- [ ] Timeout/notice remains visible without inventing per-question statuses.
- [ ] Folding retains Q&A even on non-host anchors; expansion shows each exchange once.
- [ ] Unrecognized results stay generic and tolerate unknown fields.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable Hermes session ask two clarify questions (choices/open-ended), answer and reopen. Exercise multi-select and timeout/skip. Fold/expand, including a question after an interim reply; check no duplicates. Check RTL/VoiceOver and hidden-tool setting, then delete only the disposable session.

## Out of scope
Approval history; editing/re-answering past questions; changing the pending card or tool-visibility setting semantics.

## Decisions
None. Recommend following the existing visibility setting for now.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): show the queued prompt as a pending bubble
body:
**What the user gets:** The prompt queued behind a running turn is visible as a pending bubble.
**Why it matters:** The app already knows the queued text but shows only a one-line notice.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 15 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes queued reply / attach `queued.user`; pinned verification below |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#857](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/857) (shipped; adjacent webui queue parking) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | chat-timeline-opus #4, composer-opus #6, composer-sol #8 |

## Problem
After a follow-up queues, the composer says it will send later but does not show its content. The user must remember what they typed before sending another follow-up or stopping the run, which discards the queue. Show the accepted queued text where the conversation continues.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/pending-thread-feed.ts:70-114` appends pending user bubbles. Their metadata says “Pending”; acknowledgement replaces them with ordinary messages. T3’s edit/remove/send-now queue operations require server support beyond this slice.

## Hermex today
- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.queuedPrompt` is a single next-prompt projection (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:147-149`). Accepted `.followUpQueued`/`.redirectQueued` replies merge text with blank lines (`:498-499`). Attach restores it from `queued.user` (`:1207`).
- On normal `message.start`, it clears the queued value and passes its prompt to `beginTurn` (`:1029-1037`), whose synchronous delegate appends a `local-…` user row (`:951-963`; `ChatViewModel.swift:7924-7935`). Cancellation clears the queue (`:1170-1174`). Stop confirmation already accounts for it (`:351`).
- Queued submission does not keep an optimistic transcript message (`ChatViewModel.swift:3166-3175`). Only `queuedMessagesReceipt` appears in the composer (`:539-545`; `ChatView.swift:2230-2240`). That receipt also covers webui’s local queue.
- Transcript footer/bottom anchor live in `ChatTranscriptView.swift:423-435`; follow logic watches `messages.count` (`:266-274`), which does not change when queued text appears/grows.

Pinned read-only `gh api` verification at `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`: `tui_gateway/session_auto_continue.py:136-162,248-291,419-424` implements text-only merging, queued status and `queued.user`; `tui_gateway/server.py:2888-2913` includes the projection in resume. Image-bearing/authored envelopes can queue separately, and `queued.user` exposes only the head. The pinned OpenRPC contract has no dequeue/edit method. This feature renders Hermex’s existing projection, not an authoritative full cross-client queue.

## Proposal
Add a read-only queued user bubble after the current run’s footer, before the bottom anchor, per the picked mock.

- Reuse `MessageBubbleView` user styling, plus `ChatMessageMetaRow(timeText: "Queued", …)` (`Features/Chat/ChatMessageMeta.swift:47-65`). Copy is its only action. Use a dimmed fill with readable contrast; no retry/fork/edit actions or media fetches.
- The bubble is **outside `messages`**, identified by `hermes-queued-prompt` within this chat. Pass `String?` to `ChatTranscriptView`; normalize attachment-reference footers through the existing `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.displayed` helper instead of showing raw transport text. A value input does not itself prevent parent recomputation.
- Render whenever `queuedPrompt != nil`, **including the idle interval** after the old run ends and before the next `message.start`. Gating on `activeStreamID` would create a visible gap.
- The coordinator already clears the queue and appends the real row synchronously on the ordinary start path. Render that row; never append another from the view or deduplicate by text. Pending and real rows have different ids, so do not promise an identity-preserving morph. Verify snapshot/history reconciliation also leaves one real row.
- Add a queue-value/relayout trigger to the existing follow latch: readers at the live edge follow appearance/merged growth; readers in history stay anchored.
- Remove the Hermes composer receipt only when this bubble replaces it. Keep webui’s receipt and all Stop/confirmation behavior.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** use `html-communication` to publish 2–3 alternatives covering pending placement, merged sends and composer receipt removal, in light/dark, RTL and large Dynamic Type. Report URL and stop for a pick.
2. Add the transcript input from `viewModel.hermesTurn?.queuedPrompt` without an active-stream gate. Add the small bubble using existing components, stable presentation identity and copy-only metadata.
3. Wire queue changes into follow/reader pinning and preserve ordinary message rendering/hydration.
4. Change `queuedMessagesReceipt` to cover only `queuedSlashMessages`. Update its comment and `submitHermesPrompt`’s obsolete receipt-only comment (`ChatViewModel.swift:3091-3094`).
5. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`; add localized queued/accessibility labels. Update `docs/agents/bots.md:94-96`, which describes the old receipt.

## Surfaces
Hermes Sessions/Bot Chat including keyboard and long-press Queue. App/tests only; webui queue, share, widget and notification service are unchanged. Coordinator/chat identity isolates server state. Queued→started and queued→discarded reverse presentation; reattach restores the known head. No new animation; ordinary row entrances retain Reduce Motion. Check VoiceOver/contrast and reference-only queued attachments.

## Tests
Extend `HermesChatTurnTests.testQueueHoldsThePromptOnTheHostUntilItsTurnStarts` (`:338-353`): assert the queued projection survives completed/idle events, then clears when exactly one user row appears. Extend the existing remote-Stop test (`:357-370`) rather than duplicating it. Add merged-send/snapshot reattach coverage where absent. Update receipt expectations; retain webui receipt coverage in its owning class and include that class if changed.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Accepted queued text appears once, merges successive text-only sends, and survives the between-turn idle interval.
- [ ] Starting the queued turn leaves exactly one real user row, also after reattach/history hydration.
- [ ] Confirmed Stop removes it; webui receipt remains functional.
- [ ] Queue changes follow only when the reader is already following the end.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable Hermes chat start long work, queue two follow-ups, and inspect one merged bubble with no composer receipt. Let it drain and watch the handoff. Repeat with Stop confirmation and background/reattach. Test while scrolled up and with an attachment queued. Delete only the disposable session.

## Out of scope
Queue editing, withdrawal, send-now, complete multi-client/image-envelope queue modeling, or webui pending bubbles.

## Decisions
None. Recommend replacing the Hermes receipt with the bubble.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): make hardware-keyboard sending truthful and complete
body:
**What the user gets:** Hardware keyboards can send the alternate action, stop with Esc, see truthful titles, and never send mid-IME composition.
**Why it matters:** iPad and Magic Keyboard users; CJK users risk sending half-composed text.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 1 (#1359) · order 16 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none (existing send, steer, queue and stop paths) |
| Depends on | #1367, #1375 (use their current send availability) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#312](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/312) (adjacent: IME composition splitting; command guards do not solve its underlying editing bug) |
| Needs mock first | no (existing system command overlay; reuse current action labels, no Settings or layout change) |
| Sources | composer-opus #2, composer-sol #5 |

## Problem
⌘↩ always appears as “Send Message” even when it steers or queues into an active run. There is no shortcut for the alternate send behavior or Stop. The send selector also lacks a marked-text guard, so an IME command can submit unfinished composition.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/modules/t3-composer-editor/ios/T3ComposerEditorView.swift:93-196` supplies primary/alternate send commands and refuses them during marked-text composition. `apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadComposer.tsx:1089-1101` supplies titles from the actual actions. T3 also offers configurable Return behavior; defer that optional feature here.

## Hermex today
- `ComposerChipTextView.keyCommands` registers ⌘↩ and optional ↑ recall (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ComposerChipTextView.swift:582-601`). `canPerformAction` and the send selector check only `isKeyboardSendEnabled` (`:603-625`).
- The title is static (`ChatComposerTextInputView.swift:675-679`). `MessageComposerView` supplies the enabled flag and callback (`ChatComposerView.swift:970,976`).
- `ChatComposerSendButton.runningBehavior`, `.choices` and `.accessibilityLabel` already describe the real action (`ChatComposerSendGate.swift:38-75`). Staged Hermes files remove Steer. `pickSendBehavior` revalidates choices (`ChatComposerView.swift:1141-1148`).
- `ChatView.cancelStream` owns Stop confirmation (`ChatView.swift:3188-3194`).
- `BotRoomComposerView` also calls `ComposerTextInputView` (`Features/Bots/BotRoomComposerView.swift:36-45`); rooms have a separate room-wide stop and no Steer/Queue choices. Changing the shared input must preserve that distinction.

## Proposal
Build a small value describing commands in `MessageComposerView`, then pass it through `ComposerTextInputView` to `ComposerChipTextView`. Keep UIKit unaware of `StreamingSendBehavior`: pass enabled/title values and primary/alternate/stop callbacks.

- **⌘↩:** existing primary action, named by `sendButton.accessibilityLabel`. Enable only when the actual send gate allows it; never turn this key into Stop on an empty draft.
- **⌘⇧↩:** first enabled choice different from `sendButton.runningBehavior`, excluding `.interrupt`. Send through `pickSendBehavior`, which rechecks availability. Use the choice’s existing localized `settingsDescription`. Idle or only Stop-and-send remaining means no alternate command.
- **Esc:** dismiss an open send-choice, slash or file suggestion panel first; otherwise invoke the existing Stop confirmation path while a run is active, cancellation is not in progress and the session permits it. Keep typed text. Stop availability is independent of whether the primary circle currently says Send or Stop.
- **IME/read-only:** check `isEditable` and `markedTextRange == nil` both in `canPerformAction` and each command selector, not just during command construction. Send callbacks recheck the offline hold from 11. ↑ recall retains its existing empty-editor policy plus the composition guard.
- **Suggestion dismissal:** slash/file triggers are derived from the draft and selection (`ChatComposerView.swift:360-378`), not mutable panels. Suppress the current trigger until text/selection changes so Esc does not immediately reopen it; dismiss without deleting text.
- **Room caller:** retain its primary Send label and enabled callback, with no new alternate/Stop command by default. Do not silently bind Esc to “Stop every bot in this room”.

No new preference or dependency.

## Implementation steps
1. Add a command value near `ComposerKeyboardCommand` and derive it from the actual gated choices in `MessageComposerView`.
2. Thread the value and callbacks through both make/update paths in `ChatComposerTextInputView.swift`; update the room caller with its existing Send behavior and disabled optional commands.
3. Add selectors/key commands in `ComposerChipTextView`, with execution-time editability/composition checks. Avoid stale cached commands when the run/default/hold changes.
4. Wire Esc precedence and trigger suppression in `MessageComposerView`, then the existing `onCancel`. Reuse localized command labels; read `docs/agents/i18n.md` if adding a catalog entry.

## Surfaces
Sessions and Bot Chat share the full policy; Bot room/thread composers preserve their restricted policy. Main app and tests only; share, widget and notification service are unaffected. No server state or new settings. Stop retains confirmation, draft and cancellation behavior. No animation. App navigation shortcuts remain issue #1365.

## Tests
- `ChatComposerSendGateTests`: derive alternate selection from the effective default, not the saved preference. Cover Steer→Queue, Queue→Steer, staged-files→no safe alternate, idle and offline-held sends.
- New `ComposerKeyboardCommandTests`: exercise actual selectors with `setMarkedText`, editability and enabled-state changes; assert no callback during composition or after a gate closes. Verify Esc prefers panel dismissal over Stop. Use `perform`/selectors, not a nonexistent `ComposerChipTests` class.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerSendGateTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerKeyboardCommandTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ⌘-hold titles match the primary and safe alternate actions.
- [ ] ⌘⇧↩ uses the long-press send path and never chooses Stop-and-send.
- [ ] Esc dismisses suggestions first, otherwise stops through confirmation while preserving the draft.
- [ ] Composition, read-only and offline states cannot submit through any shortcut.
- [ ] Room Send and ordinary software/hardware Return behavior remain functional.

## Manual test plan
1. In a disposable chat with hardware keyboard connected, start a run, hold ⌘ and test both send commands with Steer then Queue defaults.
2. Stage a file and verify no destructive alternate is offered. Try Esc with a suggestion open, then with a typed draft and queued prompt; confirm the usual Stop prompt.
3. With Japanese/Pinyin marked text, press the send commands: nothing submits. Repeat after reconnect/offline and read-only changes.
4. Check room Send, normal Return/newlines, and a localized command overlay.

## Out of scope
Return-to-send setting (requires a separate mock-first Settings decision); app-level commands (01, 51); fixing [#312](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/312).

## Decisions
None; recommend keeping Return as newline in this slice.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): turn large pasted text into a removable attachment
body:
**What the user gets:** Pasting a huge log becomes a removable pasted-text.txt attachment.
**Why it matters:** Large pastes bloat the composer, transcript and cache; the host reads the file and Hermes Desktop does the same at 3,000 characters.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 17 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX / performance |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes `file.attach`; verified at pin, with an expansion limitation below |
| Depends on | #1375, #1380 (shared paste/command plumbing) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1089](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1089) (adjacent composer work) |
| Needs mock first | yes (automatic paste conversion, bypass menu and failure behavior) |
| Sources | composer-opus #3, composer-sol #2 |

## Problem
A long pasted log fills the composer and creates expensive TextKit/chip layout work. A removable text attachment keeps the editor manageable while preserving the bytes for the agent. Users still need a direct way to paste inline.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/modules/t3-composer-editor/ios/T3ComposerEditorView.swift:198-244` and `packages/client-runtime/src/textPaste.ts` route large plain-text pastes into named text attachments and offer ⌘⇧V to bypass conversion. Send waits for staging.

## Hermex today
- Plain text reaches `super.paste`; file and image branches take precedence (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ComposerChipTextView.swift:660-691`). With attachments disabled it uses `insertText` (`:661-664`).
- `ChatView.handlePastedFileURLs` calls `viewModel.uploadAttachment` (`ChatView.swift:3464-3479`; `ChatViewModel.swift:1708-1714`). Hermes saves a durable local draft copy; Send/Queue uploads later (`ChatAttachmentCoordinator.swift:91-92,168-207`). Staging already holds Send and enforces eight files, 25 MB each, 50 MB total.
- `uploadsAttachmentsOnSend` identifies Hermes sessions (`ChatView.swift:719`). Rooms use the shared text input with `acceptsAttachments: false` (`Features/Bots/BotRoomComposerView.swift:36-45`).

Pinned-source verification via read-only `gh api .../contents/<path>?ref=ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`:
- `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:900-920`: `file.attach` returns `attached`, `path`, `ref_text` and other metadata. Hermex consumes the acknowledged reference (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:533-539`).
- **Storage is not necessarily in the workspace.** `tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py:82-88,136-187` writes uploaded bytes under the session Profile’s Hermes home `attachments/`, returning an absolute reference if outside cwd.
- `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py:590-605` preprocesses references with `allowed_root=cwd`. `agent/context_references.py:198-245,286-361,462-473` inlines eligible text, warns above a 25% aggregate budget and blocks aggregate injection above 50%. A single oversized text file gets a tools-readable stub instead. Outside-cwd attachments are not guaranteed to expand: only the dedicated `composer-pastes` roots receive the outside-workspace exception. Existing document sends can therefore carry a warning and require an agent tool read, as `docs/agents/bots.md:616-621` describes.
- Desktop’s `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/large-paste.ts:10-26` converts `text.length > 3_000`: **UTF-16 code units**, not Swift `Character`s. Electron writes its files under `composer-pastes` (`apps/desktop/electron/composer-paste.ts:13-24`), a different staging path from Hermex’s.

## Proposal
For Hermes plain-text paste, convert above 3,000 UTF-16 units through the existing attachment path. This reduces editor size; it does not reduce model context usage or guarantee inline host expansion.

- Keep file/image precedence. Require editability, attachment availability and a Hermes conversion flag; webui and rooms stay inline. During IME composition leave ordinary paste to UIKit and disable the custom bypass command; do not silently discard paste.
- Read the pasteboard only during the requested paste/menu action. Check the threshold by walking at most 3,001 UTF-16 units. Encode UTF-8 off the main actor, then stage with `uploadAttachment(data:filename:)`.
- Name files `pasted-text.txt`, `pasted-text-2.txt`, etc. Reserve names against both pending attachments and in-flight pastes **before awaiting**; two rapid pastes must not share a basename. Release reservations on failure/cancellation. Fence work to the captured chat/draft lifetime using existing attachment ownership patterns.
- ⌘⇧V and a touch edit-menu “Paste as Text” action insert the exact clipboard text inline through the normal editable insertion path, preserving selection, draft publication and undo. Scope this command/menu to Hermes composers with conversion enabled.
- Failure uses the existing attachment error and leaves editor/clipboard intact; Paste as Text remains available. Removing a tile is the usual reverse path. Nothing uploads automatically while offline, and Send remains held by 11.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** use `html-communication` to publish 2–3 static alternatives showing conversion, the bypass menu, and staging failure, in light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Report URL and stop for the maintainer’s pick.
2. Add a small pure `ComposerLargePaste` threshold/name policy in `ChatComposerTextInputView.swift`; use bounded UTF-16 counting.
3. Add conversion flag/callback and guarded bypass selector in `ComposerChipTextView`; retain existing file/image routing. Add the touch edit-menu action through `ComposerTextInputView.Coordinator`.
4. Thread inputs through make/update, `MessageComposerView` and `ChatView`. Reserve names and capture the draft before starting asynchronous preparation/staging. Leave text drag/drop and share-extension handling unchanged.
5. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, add the menu string, and document conversion in `docs/agents/bots.md` without claiming guaranteed prompt expansion.

## Surfaces
Hermes Sessions and Bot Chat; main app/tests only. Shared input callers (rooms, webui) retain inline paste. Share, widget and notification service are unaffected. Draft attachments remain server/session scoped. No new dependency/animation. Check VoiceOver, contrast and undo; offline staging is local and still holds Send.

## Tests
New `ComposerLargePasteTests`: threshold routing including non-BMP text (UTF-16 parity), explicit inline bypass/undo, unchanged short and non-Hermes paste, and two rapid pastes reserving distinct names. Test actual routing with an injected pasteboard reader rather than modifying the maintainer’s general clipboard. `ComposerChipTests.swift` contains several classes; there is no class named `ComposerChipTests`.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerLargePasteTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatAttachmentTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Eligible pastes above 3,000 UTF-16 units stage a tile without changing editor text.
- [ ] Rapid pastes retain distinct bytes/names; Send waits for staging.
- [ ] Both bypass actions insert inline with working undo; failure preserves editor and clipboard.
- [ ] The agent can read the uploaded content through existing tools, including outside-cwd references.
- [ ] Webui, rooms, short paste, file/image paste and share text retain their existing routing.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable Hermes session paste a 10 KB log, then a second immediately. Send a request to identify a line in each; verify tool reads where expansion warns. Check both bypass actions and undo, attachment-limit failure, offline staging/reconnect, and leaving/switching chats during staging. Repeat an ordinary paste in webui and a room.

## Out of scope
Changing host expansion rules or writing to Desktop’s staging directory; share/drop conversion; attachment transfer UI (#1419).

## Decisions
None. Recommend Desktop’s 3,000 UTF-16 threshold with an explicit inline bypass.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(workspace): syntax-colour diffs and offer Wrap Lines
body:
**What the user gets:** Diffs get syntax colour and a Wrap Lines toggle.
**Why it matters:** The biggest diff-readability gap; the canvas can already draw both but the sheet never feeds it.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 18 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI / performance |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none (existing loaded diff text) |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#691](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/691) (closed; preserve its visible-column drawing bounds) |
| Needs mock first | yes (colours on diff tints and new toolbar control) |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #4, code-surfaces-sol #1 |

## Problem
Diff text lacks syntax colour and long lines require sideways panning on a phone. The source viewer already highlights visible code and offers wrapping through the same canvas. Connect those capabilities to the diff sheet.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/diffs/nativeReviewDiffHighlighter.ts:34-35` bounds highlighting to viewport/overscan. `apps/mobile/src/features/review/reviewDiffHighlightScheduler.ts:24-48` coalesces small moves. Old/new consecutive side runs are highlighted separately; source and diff share a wrap preference (`apps/mobile/src/features/settings/appearance/useAppearanceCodeSurface.ts`).

## Hermex today
- `ReviewDiffSurface` accepts `wrapsLines`, `tokensByRowID`, `tokensVersion` and a visible-range callback (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffSurface.swift:37-42,86-90`). Its canvas applies token runs to line content regardless of presentation (`ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift:259-300`).
- `GitDiffView` passes none of these and offers only Done (`Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift:59-95`).
- `SourceFileViewModel` shows the pattern: 40-row overscan, a 20-row move threshold, one request at a time and a generation fence (`SourceViewer/SourceFileViewModel.swift:18-35,69-133`). It tracks processed rows separately from nonempty colour runs.
- `SourceHighlighter` is an actor using existing Highlightr; it blanks lines over 1,000 characters (`SourceViewer/SourceHighlighter.swift:41-56`). Resolve language with `SourceHighlightLanguage.resolve(path: path, serverLanguage: nil)` (`:28-35`). Token ranges are UTF-16 (`:4-7`).
- Wrap preference is `SourceFileSurface.wrapsLinesKey` (`SourceViewer/SourceFileSurface.swift:8`), used by `FilePreviewView`’s toggle (`FilePreviewView.swift:24,157-161`).
- Row ids encode file/hunk/line position and can repeat for different text after refresh (`ReviewDiffRow.swift:151-165`). Collapsed rows remain in the flat array with zero height (`ReviewDiffLayout.swift:60-72`); reported viewport indices can span them (`ReviewDiffSurfaceView.swift:238-243`).

## Proposal
Add the existing wrap preference/control to `GitDiffView` and pass it into the surface. Add a sheet-owned `@MainActor @Observable ReviewDiffHighlightModel` exposing token map/version, setRows, visibleRangeChanged, appearance/reset and cancellation methods.

- **Bound work:** use source-viewer overscan/threshold plus a hard cap (e.g. 200 lines per highlighter invocation). Skip collapsed files. A viewport range spanning thousands of collapsed rows must not produce a giant input. Record blank/overlong/plain processed rows and failed grammars independently of token presence to prevent retry loops.
- **Old/new sides:** for eligible rows in one file/hunk/window, build new-side runs (context/additions) and old-side runs (context/deletions), respecting consecutive side line numbers. Map additions/context from new results, deletions from old. Send the prefix-free, tab-expanded `ReviewDiffLine.content` so offsets match drawing. Skip actual no-newline marker rows; nil line numbers alone cannot identify them because synthetic hunks can also lack numbers. Split synthetic runs by hunk/side order.
- **Accuracy:** preserve multi-line grammar only within a contiguous highlighted run. Missing context across viewport/hunk boundaries is an accepted limitation; do not fetch current-file content to colour deletions.
- **Ownership:** map results to captured row ids, never new occupants of array indices shifted by progressive loading. Preserve tokens for unchanged rows when another file publishes. Refresh clears/invalidate old input before scheduling; otherwise old rows can be coloured under a new generation. Appearance changes clear tokens/processed state. Dismissal cancels/invalidate work and completion cannot reschedule.
- **Contrast:** validate theme tokens over addition/deletion/word highlights in both appearances and increased contrast. Fall back to label colour where needed; arbitrary dimming may worsen contrast. No continuously repainting animation.

Keep the existing source model intact; no generalized scheduler abstraction is needed.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** use `html-communication` to publish 2–3 static alternatives for Wrap placement and coloured additions/deletions with word highlights, in light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Report URL and stop for a pick.
2. Add `@AppStorage(SourceFileSurface.wrapsLinesKey)` and the picked control to `GitDiffView`; pass `wrapsLines` through.
3. Add `ReviewDiffHighlightModel.swift` in `Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/` (main target), with pure side-run splitting plus a controllable async highlight closure for deterministic race tests. Default to the existing actor.
4. Feed progressive rows/collapse sets into the model; connect viewport and appearance changes, refresh invalidation and dismissal cancellation. Feed tokens/version to `ReviewDiffSurface`. Keep synchronous layout callbacks to bookkeeping; publish token changes asynchronously.
5. Update `GitDiffView`’s comment and signpost requests with `reviewDiffSignposter`. Run `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` when production Swift grows.

## Surfaces
Both diff presenters (`GitWorkspaceView.swift:43-51`, `Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1419-1429`), app/tests only. Client-only rendering is shared with webui. Tokens remain sheet-local; wrap is a device presentation preference. Extensions/server state are unaffected. Preserve Dynamic Type, text-based VoiceOver, Reduce Motion and stable selection while wrap changes. No durable docs required.

## Tests
New `ReviewDiffHighlightModelTests`: supported old/new rows receive correctly mapped tokens; collapsed files do not request work; plain rows terminate and requests respect the cap. Control completion to prove refresh/dismissal drops stale results and progressive insertion cannot misapply tokens by index. Await tasks/expectations, never sleeps. Follow real-highlighter coverage in `SourceFileViewModelTests`.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffHighlightModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/SourceFileViewModelTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Visible supported diff rows gain side-correct syntax colour; unsupported text stays readable/plain.
- [ ] Wrap matches the source viewer preference and preserves selection.
- [ ] Refresh, appearance change, progressive loading and dismissal cannot apply stale tokens.
- [ ] Collapsed/overlong rows cannot create unbounded or repeated highlight work; scrolling a 5,000-row diff stays responsive.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable workspace review Swift/JSON additions and deletions, including a multi-line string and very long line. Scroll far, toggle wrap, check selection and source-viewer preference, then change appearance and refresh after another edit. Check tinted-row contrast and dismiss/reopen during highlighting.

## Out of scope
Default collapse (#1383), progress persistence (#1384), comments (#1387), and full-file grammar context.

## Decisions
None.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(workspace): start lockfiles and huge diffs collapsed
body:
**What the user gets:** Lockfiles, generated files and huge diffs start collapsed.
**Why it matters:** The real change stops hiding behind package-lock.json.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 19 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX / performance |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none (existing optional status counts and loaded diff rows) |
| Depends on | none; #1384 extends its once-only decisions |
| Related GitHub issues | none identified |
| Needs mock first | no (existing per-file collapse, no new controls/copy) |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #5 |

## Problem
Lockfiles, snapshots and generated output can dominate a review with thousands of lines. Starting them folded lets the user reach source edits immediately. The existing header remains the way to reveal them.

## What T3 does
T3 suppresses files over 400 diff lines or 24,000 characters and offers “Load diff” (`apps/mobile/src/features/review/reviewModel.ts:175-176,278-284`). `reviewState.ts` remembers revealed large-file ids per section. Hermex can use its existing collapse control instead of adding a second reveal mechanism.

## Hermex today
- `GitDiffView` starts `collapsedFileIDs` empty (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift:23`). Header taps toggle it; marking viewed also collapses (`:119-137`).
- `GitFile` has optional additions/deletions/binary (`Models/GitWorkspace.swift:78-93`). Status counts can seed a decision, but may be absent/stale. `ReviewDiffRowBuilder` already computes fallback counts from hunks (`Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffRow.swift:143-149`).
- Binary/too-large results show a short notice, not code (`ReviewDiffRow.swift:130-139`). Hermes caps diff bytes at 512 KiB (`Networking/Hermes/HermesGitClient.swift:46-47`).
- The unrelated private `TurnFileChangeSummary.ignoredComponents` excludes generated and VCS paths from turn attribution (`Models/TurnFileChangeSummary.swift:228-252`). That attribution filter is not a review policy.
- Presenters are the full Changes file list (`GitWorkspaceView.swift:43-51`) and a turn’s subset (`Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1419-1429`). Each may name an `initialFile` the user tapped.

## Proposal
