Add a small pure `ReviewDiffDefaultCollapse` policy in `Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/` and apply it once per file, per sheet lifetime:

- Fold known lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Package.resolved`, `Podfile.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, `composer.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`, `go.sum`), generated suffixes (`.snap`, `.min.js`, `.min.css`, `.map`) and obvious generated directory components (`node_modules`, `dist`, `.next`, `.cache`, `__snapshots__`). Use a small review-local list; leave attribution rules unchanged. Do not fold arbitrary source files merely because a parent directory is named `build`.
- Fold a change over 400 added+deleted lines. When either count is missing, defer the size decision until successful loaded rows provide counts; count additions/deletions, not context rows. Do not interpret a loading header’s zero fallback as a final decision.
- Keep the explicitly tapped `initialFile` and a single-file sheet expanded initially. Keep binary, too-large, failed and loading notices visible; if a default folded a file before its notice arrived, remove only that automatic collapse, not an explicit user choice.
- Track automatic decisions separately from user toggles. A toggle or viewed action immediately settles the choice, even if loading is unfinished. Later results and refresh must not re-collapse a user-expanded file.
- Seed known defaults in `GitDiffView.init`, then resolve deferred decisions at successful publication. The once-only bookkeeping survives refresh; it resets on sheet dismissal until 20 lands.

This changes layout/drawing work, not fetching: all diffs still load with the existing bounded loader. A collapsed file’s rows still exist and layout bookkeeping still visits them; avoid claiming it eliminates all CPU work.

## Implementation steps
1. Add the pure review-local path/count policy and initial seed function, retaining the tapped/single-file exemptions.
2. Seed `collapsedFileIDs` and decision bookkeeping in `GitDiffView`. In `publish`, distinguish pending, loaded and notice states before applying deferred count defaults. Add a small loader result callback only if rows alone cannot represent that distinction.
3. In `toggleFile` and `toggleViewed`, record explicit user choice before any later publish can override it. Preserve ordinary un-view behavior (it stays collapsed).
4. Update `GitDiffView`’s doc comment. Do not refactor `TurnFileChangeSummary` or add a shared generated-path abstraction.

## Surfaces
Both diff presenters, app/tests only; no extension changes. Client presentation is shared with webui at no extra server work. State is sheet-local. Header tap expands again; initial navigation targets stay visible. Preserve existing accessibility collapse announcements and no new animation. No durable docs needed.

## Tests
New `ReviewDiffDefaultCollapseTests`: a lockfile folds, ordinary source does not, and a large change folds. Cover tapped/single-file exemptions and a deferred missing-count result arriving after the user already expanded. A loading/error notice must not settle or override a later legitimate decision.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffDefaultCollapseTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Multi-file reviews start lockfiles/snapshots/large changes folded, except the tapped file.
- [ ] User expansion survives later loading and refresh; single-file reviews open expanded.
- [ ] Missing counts use loaded changed-line counts, with no default applied to a loading placeholder.
- [ ] Binary, failed and too-large notices stay readable.
- [ ] Turn attribution and network loading remain unchanged.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable workspace change a lockfile, snapshot and two source files. Open a source file from Changes and inspect the defaults; explicitly expand the lockfile before all results arrive, then refresh. Open by tapping the lockfile and check it starts expanded. Repeat with a single-file and a too-large diff.

## Out of scope
Skipping fetch for folded files; persistence across dismissal (#1384); a generated-file badge or configurable pattern system.

## Decisions
None. Recommend 400 changed lines as the starting threshold; adjust only with review evidence.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(workspace): remember viewed and collapsed files while a chat is open
body:
**What the user gets:** Viewed and collapsed files are remembered while a chat is open; a re-edited file un-views itself.
**Why it matters:** Review progress is lost every time the sheet closes.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 20 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none (existing Git client/results) |
| Depends on | #1383 (stored/user decisions take precedence) |
| Related GitHub issues | none identified |
| Needs mock first | no (existing controls retain their state) |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #7, code-surfaces-sol #5 |

## Problem
Marking files viewed, returning to chat and reopening Changes loses all review progress. A subsequent agent edit should invalidate the viewed mark for that changed patch while retaining progress on untouched files.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/review/reviewState.ts:23-64,103-173` stores viewed/expanded ids in memory outside the screen, keyed by environment/thread/section. `reviewFileVisibility.ts:13-34` filters ids against visible files. Hermex must account for its two presenters exposing different subsets before borrowing pruning behavior.

## Hermex today
- Both sets are sheet-local `@State` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift:23-24`). Marking viewed collapses; un-viewing leaves it collapsed (`:128-137`).
- `ChatView.turnDiffSheet` supplies a turn’s files (`Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1419-1429`). `GitWorkspaceView` supplies all tracked changes (`Features/Workspace/GitWorkspaceView.swift:43-51`); ChatView presents it at `:1402`.
- The chat’s Git client can be replaced as workspace context changes (`ChatView.swift:2456-2466`). `GitDataClient` has no identity (`Networking/APIClient+Git.swift:8-49`).
- `HermesGitClient.context` carries `HermesWorkspaceContext` (`Networking/Hermes/HermesGitClient.swift:36`; `HermesWorkspaceFileClient.swift:7-14`). `HermesWorkspaceFileClient.scope` demonstrates an in-memory scope including server/profile/stored key/cwd (`:33,43`). Webui’s client is session-scoped (`APIClient+Git.swift:80-89`).
- `GitStatus.truncated` reports a capped list, and `files` is optional (`Models/GitWorkspace.swift:40-51`); a successful HTTP read alone does not establish a complete list.
- `ReviewDiffLoader.FileResult` is nested in **GitDiffView.swift:219-224**, not a separate loader file. Fetch/results/row construction occur in its child task group (`:283-285`), published through a cancellation/generation fence (`:290-305`).

## Proposal
Add an in-memory `@MainActor @Observable ReviewProgressStore`, owned by `ChatView` as `@State`, shared by both presenters. Per scope, hold explicit/default collapse decisions and viewed patch fingerprints. Keep local surface state as the render source and write interactions through to the store.

- **Scope:** add `reviewScope` to `GitDataClient`. Hermes stores a `nonisolated let` computed in init from server, Profile, stored key and cwd (as the file client does). Webui uses session id within the chat-owned, server-scoped store. Read `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` before wiring lifetime. Never log or persist cwd/scope. Closing the chat/server subtree drops the store; workspace changes select a separate scope.
- **Seeding:** read stored decisions without mutating an observable store during view initialization. Commit newly seeded defaults from the owned loading task. Unknown files use 19’s policy; explicit choices win. On an explicit navigation to a tapped `initialFile`, temporarily reveal that file so restored collapse cannot hide the requested content. A known explicitly collapsed single file otherwise retains its stored state; 19’s single-file exemption is a default, not a permanent constraint.
- **Fingerprint:** compute a process-local `Hasher` fingerprint off the main actor from a successfully loaded text patch, path and diff kind. Reconcile only successful results with available text (`binary != true`, `tooLarge != true`, `diff != nil`). Errors/loading/missing text are not empty patches. For content unavailable to fingerprint (binary/too-large), leave collapse memory but do not restore/store a trusted viewed mark.
- **Viewed action:** mark viewed only against a successfully loaded current fingerprint; a click during loading must not certify an old patch. Hide/hold restored viewed marks until the current patch validates. Matching fingerprints keep the mark; changed fingerprints clear it **and expand** in local/store state. An unchanged viewed file can remain manually expanded: viewed does not permanently force collapse.
- **Publication:** propagate result fingerprints with the existing coalesced publication or a fenced result callback, without rehashing all rows on each body pass. Capture scope and load generation; dismissed/stale loads cannot update a store now used by another scope.
- **Pruning:** **never prune against `GitDiffView.files`**: a turn card is only a subset. Prune only from a newly successful `GitWorkspaceView` read in the same scope with `isGit == true`, non-nil `files` and `truncated == false`. Failed, missing, capped/unknown-completeness and non-repository reads are not evidence that files disappeared; do not reuse retained status after a failed refresh. Until a full list is read, chat lifetime bounds retained state.

## Implementation steps
1. Add `reviewScope` to the two production `GitDataClient` conformers (`WebUIGitClient`, `HermesGitClient`). Update any conformers introduced by earlier numbered issues.
2. Add `ReviewProgressStore` in `Features/Workspace/`, with testable seed, toggle, reconcile and authoritative-list pruning transitions. Reuse 19’s decision model.
3. Extend `FileResult`/loader publication in `GitDiffView.swift` with optional successful-patch fingerprints. Keep coalescing and cancellation checks intact; later progressive results must not reset prior decisions.
4. Pass the chat-owned store through `GitWorkspaceView` and both `GitDiffView` entry points. Supply authoritative pruning only from successful full status reads, and preserve the scope captured by each sheet/task.
5. Update the diff view’s comment to describe lifetime and changed-patch invalidation.

## Surfaces
Both presenters share progress for matching workspace scope and patch kind. Main app/tests only; extensions unaffected. Same paths on different server/Profile/cwd scopes remain independent. Un-view/expand remain available. No animation or network/API additions; existing diff reads validate fingerprints. VoiceOver uses existing viewed state.

## Tests
New `ReviewProgressStoreTests`: reopening restores choices; changed patch un-views/expands while identical patch preserves a manual expansion; loading/failure cannot certify or invalidate a patch. Review subset A, then B, then A: A survives. A successful authoritative full list prunes missing ids; failed/capped/unknown lists do not. Scopes are independent. Use controlled loader completion to check stale results cannot write after dismissal/scope change, with no sleeps.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewProgressStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffDefaultCollapseTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dismiss/reopen from either entry point restores review state for matching patches.
- [ ] Changed viewed text patches reappear un-viewed and expanded; failures cannot appear verified.
- [ ] Visiting a turn subset preserves progress outside that subset; a complete successful status prunes absent files.
- [ ] Explicitly tapped files are visible; workspace/server scopes never share progress.
- [ ] Closing the chat discards progress; stale asynchronous results cannot resurrect it.

## Manual test plan
In a disposable workspace review three files and collapse one manually. Reopen through the full Changes list and two different turn cards. Edit one viewed file and reopen: only that mark clears. Tap an explicitly collapsed file from Changes: its content is revealed. Test failed reload, cwd change, server switch and chat close/reopen.

## Out of scope
Disk/process-wide persistence, viewed-count title, and file jumping (#1385). Future branch/last-turn scopes (22, 28) must extend scope identity when implemented.

## Decisions
None. Recommend chat-owned memory for the review → ask → review loop.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(workspace): jump to any changed file from inside the diff
body:
**What the user gets:** Jump to any changed file from inside the diff.
**Why it matters:** Large diffs are hard to navigate one-handed.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 21 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1232](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1232) (adjacent: Git menu nits, different file) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | code-surfaces-sol #6; code-surfaces-opus "Considered and rejected" (navigator pane, iPad only) |

## Problem

The diff sheet shows every changed file in one long scroll. Once it is open, the user can reach a file far down the list only by scrolling past every file before it, or by dismissing to the Changes list and tapping again. With 20+ files on a phone that is tedious.

## What T3 does

`apps/mobile/src/features/review/ReviewSheet.tsx:260–417` has a changed-files navigator. Picking an entry loads its patch if needed, expands it and calls the native `scrollToFile`. Visible-file events keep the navigator's current file in sync (`:536–564`). On wide layouts it becomes a side pane. Reference only.

## Hermex today

- `GitDiffView` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift:7`) is the single diff surface for the Changes sheet (`GitWorkspaceView.swift:43–51`) and the turn-changes card (`ChatView.swift:1419–1430`).
- Its toolbar has only Done (`GitDiffView.swift:59–61`).
- The scroll bridge already exists. `scrollTarget` is `@State` (`GitDiffView.swift:26`) and is seeded once from `initialFile` (`:44`). `ReviewDiffScrollTarget.fileHeader(id)` with a fresh token scrolls again, even to the same place (`ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffSurface.swift:3–23`). The bridge applies a new token once, unanimated (`ReviewDiffSurface.swift:96–99`). `ReviewDiffSurfaceView.scroll(to:animated:)` holds the request until layout can place it (`ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffSurfaceView.swift:125–129`).
- Collapse state is `collapsedFileIDs` (`GitDiffView.swift:23`). A jump to a collapsed file would land on its header with nothing below it.

So the only missing piece is a way to pick a file.

## Proposal

Add a **Files** toolbar button to `GitDiffView`, shown only when `files.count > 1`. It opens a small picker. Choosing a file:

1. removes the file's id from `collapsedFileIDs` if it is there (the user asked to see it; viewed state is unchanged);
2. sets `scrollTarget = ReviewDiffScrollTarget(fileID: file.id, token: UUID())`;
3. dismisses the picker.

The picker lists `files` in sheet order. Each row shows the file name, its parent folder as a subtitle (full relative paths disambiguate duplicate basenames), `DiffCountsLabel` +/− counts, and a checkmark for files in `viewedFileIDs`. Use `.searchable` once the list is long (more than about 8 files). It is built from `files: [GitFile]`, which the view already holds, so the picker needs no new fetch or diff parsing. Expanding a file can still trigger canvas layout.

Presentation is the mock question. Candidates:
- **A.** A `.sheet` with `NavigationStack { List }`, `.presentationDetents([.medium, .large])`, `.searchable`.
- **B.** A toolbar `Menu` of files, with no search. Cheapest, but poor past about 15 files.
- **C.** A "file N of M" jump bar in the bottom inset with previous and next chevrons, plus the list. A scroll-synchronized current-file indicator would also need a callback reporting the visible file; the existing visible-row-range callback reports indices, not a file id.

Recommendation: A. It scales, works the same on iPad, and needs no canvas change.

The jump stays unanimated (the bridge passes `animated: false`), so Reduce Motion needs no special case.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks.** Build static mocks of A, B and C with the `html-communication` skill: light and dark, a 3-file and a 40-file change, and the large Dynamic Type size. Publish them, report the URL and stop until the maintainer picks one.
2. Add `@State private var isShowingFileJump = false` and the toolbar button to `GitDiffView` (`ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarLeading)` or beside Done, per the mock), with `systemImage: "list.bullet"` and accessibility label "Changed files".
3. Add a small `GitDiffFileJumpList` view (same file or `Features/Workspace/GitDiffFileJumpList.swift`). It takes `files`, `viewedFileIDs` and `onSelect: (GitFile) -> Void`.
4. Add `jump(to:)` in `GitDiffView`, following Proposal. If 20 is present, write the reveal through its collapse-decision path while preserving the viewed mark.
5. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, then update the String Catalog: "Changed files", "Jump to File", and the search prompt.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the Changes sheet and the turn-changes card both use `GitDiffView`, so both get it. The Files viewer's source surface is single-file: n/a.
- **Targets:** app only. **Multi-server:** n/a (no state crosses the sheet).
- **Reverse states:** n/a. Jumping is not a mode; Done and the picker's own dismissal cover it.
- **Connection modes:** none; no request.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver labels for the button and rows (row label "name, folder, N added, M removed, viewed"). Dynamic Type in the list. No animation.
- **webui:** the same view serves webui. This is shared, client-only work, so both server kinds get it.

## Tests

Run the existing scroll/canvas coverage; verify the small toolbar action manually. Do not extract a helper just to test a set removal and target assignment.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Files button appears only when the sheet shows more than one file.
- [ ] Picking a file scrolls to its header (clamped near the end of the document), including a file whose diff is still loading.
- [ ] Picking a collapsed file expands it. Picking a viewed file keeps it marked viewed.
- [ ] Picking the same file twice scrolls again.
- [ ] Works from both the Changes sheet and the turn-changes card.
- [ ] VoiceOver reads each row's name, folder and counts.

## Manual test plan

1. In a Hermes chat on a repository with 10+ changed files, open Git → Changes and tap the first file.
2. Tap Files, then the last file. Its header is visible at the expected scroll position.
3. Collapse a file, open Files and pick it. It expands.
4. Mark a file viewed and pick it. It stays viewed.
5. Repeat from a turn-changes card. Check dark mode and the largest Dynamic Type size.

## Out of scope

- An iPad sidebar navigator (T3's wide-layout pane).
- Syncing a "current file" highlight with scroll position. The surface already exposes visible row indices; mapping those to a current file is follow-up work, only if mock C wins.
- Diff colour and wrap (#1382), collapsing generated files (#1383), and remembering viewed state (#1384).

## Decisions

- Which presentation, A, B or C? Recommendation: A (sheet with `.searchable`).


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(hermes): review a branch's committed changes beside uncommitted ones
body:
**What the user gets:** Review a branch's committed changes beside uncommitted ones.
**Why it matters:** Once the agent commits, the phone shows nothing to review.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 22 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes API: `GET /api/git/review/list` and `/api/git/review/diff`, `scope=branch`. Verified at pin `ca678285`; deployment unverified. |
| Depends on | #1384 (extend progress identity by range); 28 later extends this scope |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1232](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1232) (adjacent: Git menu) · [#1114](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1114) (extends its merged Git read path) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #2; code-surfaces-sol #2 |

## Problem

Git → Changes shows only uncommitted work. Once the agent commits, the sheet says “Your working tree is clean.” The committed work disappears from review on the phone even though the host can diff the branch.

## What T3 does

The review sheet's scope menu offers Changes (branch range) and Uncommitted alongside turn sections (`apps/mobile/src/features/review/ReviewSheet.tsx:116–159`, `reviewModel.ts:473–547`). Reference only. The explorer's Hermes Desktop quotation was stale: at the Hermes pin, `apps/desktop/src/store/review.ts:24–26` explicitly uses uncommitted scope only.

## Hermex today

- `HermesREST.gitChanges` and `.gitDiff` hard-code `scope=uncommitted` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:579–586`).
- `HermesGitClient.status()` joins review rows with current working-tree flags (`Networking/Hermes/HermesGitClient.swift:79–90,168–188`); `diff(for:)` selects staged, worktree or whole-file-vs-HEAD (`:97–111`). Neither is suitable unchanged for branch review.
- `GitWorkspaceView` opens all changed files at the selected one (`Features/Workspace/GitWorkspaceView.swift:43–51`) and renders a working-tree empty state (`:78–110`). Writes live in the separate commit sheet/menu.
- `GitDataClient` is shared with webui and already exposes `isHermes` (`Networking/APIClient+Git.swift:8–20`). `GitStatusChip` hides `.unknown` (`GitWorkspaceView.swift:258`), so rows with no reliable change kind need no new badge UI.

**Pinned contract:** read-only GitHub contents verified at `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`; cached Git blob hashes match.

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/git.py:123–132` defines list/diff with `path`, `scope`, optional `base` and, for diff, `file` and `staged`.
- `hermes_cli/web_git.py:137–141,247–267,288–295`: branch scope picks the first available merge-base against origin/HEAD, origin/main, origin/master, main, master. It returns `{files, base}` from `git diff --numstat <base>...HEAD`; diff returns `{diff}` from that range. No base means empty files/null base or empty diff. **Branch scope recomputes its base and ignores supplied `base`.**
- Every branch row has `status: "M", staged: false`, even added/deleted files. Do not infer change kind from this status.
- `/api/git/status` supplies `branch`, `defaultBranch`, `detached` (`web_git.py:228`). Hermex already uses detached to name HEAD (`HermesGitClient.swift:193–196`), but retains neither detached nor defaultBranch as metadata. The default-branch name does not prove which fallback supplied the merge-base.
- The range includes committed changes only. Default branches can have local commits ahead of origin, and detached HEAD can still yield a valid range. Neither condition justifies hiding non-empty results.

## Proposal

Add `GitReviewScope` (`.uncommitted`, `.branch`) and a small read result containing `files`, optional `base`, `branch`, `defaultBranch`, `detached`. Extend `GitDataClient` with `review(scope:)` and `diff(for:scope:)`, preserving existing `status()` and `diff(for:)` for writes and callers. Default protocol implementations support uncommitted via those existing methods; unsupported scopes fail explicitly on webui. Use existing `isHermes` for picker visibility; no duplicate capability flag.

Hermes branch review reads list plus status metadata, maps counts tolerantly, and sets change-kind/status and working-tree flags to nil. Totals come from the review rows, never `git/status.changed`. Branch diffs bypass uncommitted staged/worktree dispatch and retain the 512 KiB display cap.

`GitWorkspaceView` adds “Uncommitted | This Branch”, resetting on each sheet open. Maintain independent result/loading/error state for branch scope. Show branch name and “Compared with branch base”; do not claim a base-branch name the API does not return. Show non-empty results on default/detached branches too, with detached metadata when applicable. Empty/null-base says “No base branch found”; empty/non-null-base says “No committed changes against the branch base.” Fetch failure is retryable, not an empty range.

Open `GitDiffView` with the selected scope and rows. Pass scope into its loader and extend 20's progress key with the range kind (and resolved base when available); authoritative pruning must stay within that range. Uncommitted status must not prune branch progress. Keep selection-to-draft working; no mutation controls in branch review.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for distinct picker/menu variants, header, no-base/empty/error/detached states, light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Publish the URL and stop for a maintainer pick before implementation.
2. Add scope/result models, `HermesREST` query parameters, protocol defaults, and Hermes read implementations. Preserve old uncommitted call behavior.
3. Add branch state/loading to `GitWorkspaceViewModel`. Guard publication against cancellation, a newer request and workspace replacement; this model has no existing retire method.
4. Wire picker, refresh and selected-scope presentation through `GitWorkspaceView` and `GitDiffView`; keep the four-file concurrency limit.
5. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, then localize new copy/plurals. Record verified handlers/shapes and any authorized live check in the PR; do not hard-code another compatibility pin in source comments.

## Surfaces

- Entry: Git → Changes, including a clean working tree. Commit sheet/menu stay uncommitted. Turn cards are 28.
- Targets: app/tests; extensions n/a. Shared view defaults preserve webui.
- Server/Profile/session/folder: per existing repository client; discard stale results after folder/server change. No persistence.
- Reverse: return to Uncommitted. Plain HTTPS reads work across connection modes; failures keep scope-specific error state.
- Native: VoiceOver picker selection, Dynamic Type, light/dark, localized plurals; no new animation or dependency.

## Tests

- `APIClientGitTests`: branch list/diff send root-relative file and repository-root `path`, `scope=branch`, no staged dispatch. Added/deleted fixtures with host status M expose counts without false kinds or working-tree flags.
- `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`: distinguish null-base from empty range and failure; preserve non-empty default/detached results; discard a superseded request. Use scripted continuations/expectations, no sleeps.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean working tree can open Changes → This Branch and review committed files.
- [ ] Rows and diffs use branch range, with honest counts/kinds and scope-specific failures.
- [ ] Default/detached branches with changes remain reviewable; absence of a base is explained.
- [ ] Switching scopes/folders cannot publish late rows under the wrong scope.
- [ ] No mutation controls in branch review; webui has no picker.

## Manual test plan

1. In a disposable test repository/branch, commit two files. Verify branch rows and per-file diffs against the host-selected merge-base, with Uncommitted clean.
2. Check no base, empty range, detached HEAD and a local default branch ahead of origin; valid changes stay visible.
3. Switch scope during a slow request, then change folder. Check no stale rows. On webui, verify the existing sheet.

## Out of scope

Choosing a base, combining committed/uncommitted ranges, turn snapshots (#1392), and PR links (#1391).

## Decisions

Picker placement is decided by mocks. Recommendation: segmented control for two visible choices.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(workspace): comment on selected lines and batch several into one prompt
body:
**What the user gets:** Comment on selected diff or source lines and batch several comments into one prompt.
**Why it matters:** Line-level review feedback to the agent is the core code-review loop.
**Cost:** Small–Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 23 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S–M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none (21 and 22 touch the same sheet; any order works) |
| Related GitHub issues | none found |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #3; composer-sol cross-area note (existing `ReviewDiffSelection` snippet) |

## Problem

A reviewer on a phone wants to say "this line is wrong because…" about several places, then send it once, the way a GitHub review works. Hermex can drop a selected diff range into the composer, but only one range at a time with no note attached, and the sheet closes after each one. The source viewer can't send a selection to the composer at all.

## What T3 does

- Tapping a line, or long-pressing then tapping a range end, opens `ReviewCommentComposerSheet` (`apps/mobile/src/features/review/useReviewCommentSelectionController.ts:69–135`).
- The comment and a fenced diff go into the thread draft as a `<review_comment …>` block (`reviewCommentSelection.ts:333–358`).
- The composer counts them, and the user sends once.

T3's `<review_comment>` tag is its own convention. Hermes has none, so don't copy the tag. Reference only.

## Hermex today

- `ReviewDiffSelection` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffSelection.swift:6–96`) already handles tap and long-press range selection. `snippet(in:)` (`:62–83`) emits `path L1-L9` plus a fenced `diff` block whose fence is longer than any backtick run inside.
- `GitDiffView.selectionBar` shows "N lines selected · Clear · Add to prompt" (`Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift:97–115`). `addToPrompt()` sends the snippet and clears the selection (`:147–152`). Refresh clears the selection too (`:156–161`).
- The host closure `ChatView.addDiffSelectionToDraft` (`Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1434–1440`) appends to `draftMessage`, persists the draft, then **closes both Git sheets** (`activeGitSheet = nil; turnDiffPresentation = nil`). So batching means reopening the sheet and finding your place each time.
- `SourceFileSurface` uses the same selection model, but its bar offers only Clear and Copy (`Features/Workspace/SourceViewer/SourceFileSurface.swift:88–109, 131–138`). `FilePreviewView` has no prompt hook (`Features/Workspace/FilePreviewView.swift:28–34`).

## Proposal

Keep the draft as the only queue. Every comment is appended to the persisted draft as soon as it is added, so there is no new store, nothing to lose on dismissal, and the user can edit everything in the composer before sending.

1. Replace "Add to prompt" with **Comment…** in the selection bar. It opens a small sheet (`.presentationDetents([.height(…), .medium])`) showing the selected range ("`Sources/App.swift` L12–L20"), a `TextField(axis: .vertical)` ("Add a comment (optional)"), and **Add**.
2. **Add** appends Markdown to the draft through the existing closure. The comment comes first, then the snippet:
   ````text
   Sources/App.swift L12-L20: this guard drops the error
   ```diff
   …
   ```
   ````
   An empty comment appends the snippet alone, which is today's behavior.
3. The comment composer dismisses after Add; the underlying diff **stays open**. The selection clears, and the bar becomes a quiet status: "2 comments added · Back to Chat". Back to Chat dismisses the Git sheet. The count is `@State` for this diff's lifetime only; it counts additions made here, not all review blocks in the draft. The draft holds the content.
4. Split the host closure so it no longer dismisses: `onAddToPrompt(String)` only appends and persists, and `onReturnToChat()` dismisses the Git presentation. Do this in `ChatView`.
5. Add the same Comment… action to `SourceFileSurface` when its host passes `onAddToPrompt`. `FilePreviewView` → `FileBrowserView` → `ChatView` thread the closure. The file-reference sheet (`ChatView.swift:847–860`) gets it too. The snippet for a source selection uses a fenced block with the file's language (no `+`/`-` prefixes). Add `ReviewDiffSelection.sourceSnippet(in:path:language:)` beside `snippet(in:)`, reusing the fence-length rule. Capture the snippet when opening Comment…; clear selection and dismiss an open comment composer on refresh/content or workspace replacement so it cannot submit stale line context. For pushed Files previews retain ordinary back navigation with an added-count status; do not refactor navigation just for a one-tap Back to Chat. The transcript file-link sheet can dismiss through `openedFileReference = nil`.

Not in scope: inline comment cards drawn in the canvas, and keeping selections across refresh (YAGNI).

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks.** Use the `html-communication` skill: the selection bar before and after adding, the comment sheet, and the "2 comments added" state, in light and dark and at the large Dynamic Type size, for both the diff and source surfaces. Publish, report the URL, stop for a pick (including the exact copy).
2. `ReviewDiffSelection`: add a default-empty comment argument to `snippet(in:)` and add `sourceSnippet(...)`; keep existing empty-comment output unchanged.
3. `GitDiffView`: comment sheet state, `addedCommentCount`, the new bar states, and `onReturnToChat`.
4. `ChatView.addDiffSelectionToDraft`: stop dismissing. Add a dismiss closure. Thread both into `GitWorkspaceView`, `GitDiffView`, `FileBrowserView`, `FilePreviewView` and `SourceFileSurface`.
5. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, then update the String Catalog: "Comment…", "Add a comment (optional)", "Add", a plural for "%lld comments added", and "Back to Chat".

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the Changes sheet, the turn-changes card, Files → file preview, and the transcript file-link sheet. The share extension and widget: n/a.
- **Targets:** app only.
- **Multi-server:** drafts are already server- and session-keyed (`persistDraftEdit`). Nothing new is stored.
- **Reverse states:** every comment is ordinary draft text; the user deletes it in the composer. Clear still clears a selection.
- **Read-only chats:** new source hooks should be nil for a read-only/cached host. Existing Git callers pass a non-nil closure unconditionally (`ChatView.swift:1405,1428`); they do not already implement that policy. Appending a draft is local and must never send automatically.
- **Native quality:** the sheet field gets focus on open. VoiceOver: "Comment on lines 12 to 20". Dynamic Type. Light and dark. No animation.
- **webui:** shared, client-only. Both server kinds get it.

## Tests

`ReviewDiffSelectionTests`:
- `snippet(in:comment:)` puts the comment on the heading line and keeps the fence safe when the selection contains a fenced block.
- `sourceSnippet` emits unprefixed lines in a language fence.

Two formatting behaviors, two tests. Verify append/persistence order and selection invalidation in the integrated manual pass; no sleeps or polling.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffSelectionTests`. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before catalog edits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting lines and tapping Comment… opens a sheet naming the file and range.
- [ ] Add appends comment plus snippet to the draft and leaves the diff open with "1 comment added".
- [ ] Three comments across two files land in the draft in order. Back to Chat shows them in the composer, unsent.
- [ ] An empty comment appends exactly today's snippet.
- [ ] The source viewer offers the same flow when opened from a chat; Copy still works.
- [ ] Dismissing the sheet with the swipe-down gesture keeps everything already added (it's in the draft).

## Manual test plan

1. In a chat with uncommitted changes, open Changes → a file. Select a range, tap Comment…, type a note and Add.
2. Select a range in another file and Add without a note.
3. Tap Back to Chat: the composer holds both, in order. Send.
4. Open Files → a source file. Select lines, Comment…, Add. The composer gets a language-fenced block.
5. Add two more comments without sending; relaunch: the existing text and all additions remain in order. Refresh or replace the file while Comment… is open: stale context cannot be added.

## Out of scope

- Inline comment cards in the diff canvas.
- Selections that survive a diff refresh.
- Structured review provenance (T3's `<review_comment>` tag).

## Decisions

- Should Comment… replace "Add to prompt", or sit next to it? Recommendation: replace it, because an empty comment is today's behavior and one button keeps the bar uncluttered.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: fix(hermes): let the composer's `@` panel find files in any folder
body:
**What the user gets:** The composer's @ file search finds files in any folder.
**Why it matters:** Confirmed bug: the panel never reaches the host's repo-wide fuzzy search.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 1 (#1359) · order 24 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability (bug fix) |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes RPC `complete.path`. The fuzzy branch was verified at the pin `ca678285` via GitHub; live deployment unverified; integrate only against an explicitly authorized test host. |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1113](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1113) (implements a fix to: `@` file search in Hermes chats, closed) · [#552](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/552) (origin of `BotFilePathSearch`) |
| Needs mock first | no |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus cross-area note 1; code-surfaces-sol #4 ("use an explicit `@file:` query; a plain word follows directory completion") |

**Status: premise confirmed.** At the pin, a word without a leading `@` never reaches the host's repo-wide fuzzy search. Hermex's `@` panel sends exactly that, so `@View` finds only top-level entries whose names start with "View".

## Problem

In a Hermes chat on a `local` backend, typing `@Chat` in the composer should offer `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift`. Today it offers nothing unless a top-level entry's name starts with "Chat". Files deeper than the root are reachable only by typing their full path folder by folder.

## What T3 does

T3's composer runs a server-side workspace search for `@` mentions (debounced, capped), not a one-folder listing. This issue uses Hermes's existing `complete.path` fuzzy branch. Reference only.

## Hermex today

- `ComposerFileTrigger.query` is the trigger text **without** the `@` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ComposerFileTrigger.swift:15–17`).
- `ChatComposerView` runs `searchFilePaths(trigger.query)` (`Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:492`). That goes through `ChatViewModel.searchFilePaths` (`Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:4689–4698`) to `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.completeFilePaths` (`Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:645–651`).
- `completeFilePaths` sends `word: BotFilePathSearch.word(for: query)`, which is the bare query, or `.` when empty (`Features/Bots/BotFilePathSearch.swift:14–16`).
- The same `completeFilePaths` also confirms `@path` chips. `listedFileReferences` sends each full candidate path (`src/App/View.swift`) and checks that the listing contains it (`ChatViewModel.swift:4887–4897`). That use needs the directory-listing behavior and must not change.
- The test `BotFilePathSearchTests.testWordForBareTriggerListsTheRoot` pins `word("") == "."` and `word("src/Ch") == "src/Ch"` (`HermesMobileTests/BotFilePathTests.swift:5–8`).

**Upstream contract:** verified through read-only GitHub contents at pin `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`; cached Git blob hashes match. Source: `tui_gateway/methods_complete.py`.

`complete.path` handler, `:231–274`:
- `is_context = word.startswith("@")`, and `query = word[1:]` when it does.
- A word like `@file:Name` sets `prefix_tag="file"` and `path_part="Name"` (`:253–256`). A bare `@Name` sets `prefix_tag=""` and `path_part="Name"`.
- `bare_word = is_context and path_part and "/" not in path_part` (`:264`).
- **Fuzzy branch** (`:265–266`): `local and bare_word and len(path_part.strip()) >= 2 and prefix_tag != "folder"` calls `_fuzzy_basename_items` (`:103–139`).
  - It walks `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` under the session root (capped at 20,000 files and cached), plus the root's own children and every ancestor folder.
  - It ranks names exact > prefix > word boundary/camelCase > substring > subsequence (`methods_complete_helpers.py:81`).
  - It answers at most 30 items: `@file:rel` for files, `@folder:rel/` for folders, with `meta` set to the parent folder (or `"dir"` for folders).
  - It skips dot-names unless the query starts with `.`.
- **Every other word** calls `_dir_listing_items` (`:186–229`): a case-insensitive prefix match inside the one folder the path names, at most 30 items. A word without `@` answers plain relative paths.
- A bare `@Name` with no prefix tag also gets Profile mention items prepended (`:269–272`). Their text starts with `@`, and `BotFilePathSearch.matches` already drops those (`BotFilePathSearch.swift:33`).
- `@file:` with a query shorter than 2 characters falls to the listing with `prefix_tag="file"`, **which skips folders** (`:214–215`). So use `@file:` only on the fuzzy path.

## Proposal

Give the panel its own word spelling and leave chip confirmation alone.

`panelWord` rules:
- `""` → `"."`.
- Contains `/` → unchanged (folder listing, today's behavior).
- Trimmed length < 2 → unchanged (the root listing keeps folders).
- Otherwise → `"@file:" + query`.

Add `BotFilePathSearch.panelWord(for:)` and rename today's `word(for:)` to `listingWord(for:)`. `completeFilePaths` takes the word kind. The panel path (`searchFilePaths`) passes `.panel`; `listedFileReferences` passes `.listing`. `matches(from:)` already strips `@file:` and `@folder:` and maps `meta: "dir"`, so no decode change is needed. A fuzzy row's `path` is root-relative, which is the same spelling a chip needs.

Why `@file:` and not a bare `@`: the bare form also triggers Profile mentions and the plugin `@prefix:` branch for queries containing `:`. `file` is a built-in prefix (`methods_complete.py:13`), so `@file:` skips both.

webui sessions are unaffected (`ComposerFilePathSearch.search(_:sessionID:apiClient:)` ranks its own listing).

## Implementation steps

1. The pinned contract is verified; no live host was checked. At implementation time, use an explicitly authorized test host and disposable session for an integrated `@file:<name>` check. Do not attach to a real session or add logging just to inspect the reply.
2. `BotFilePathSearch`: add `panelWord`, rename `word` to `listingWord`, and update the doc comments (the type comment's "A path word answers plain relative paths…" paragraph now describes both).
3. `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.completeFilePaths(_:word:)`: take a `BotFilePathWord` (`.panel`, `.listing`). Update both call sites in `ChatViewModel`.
4. Update `ComposerFilePathSearch`'s type comment, which says nothing recurses. That stays true for webui; note that a Hermes host does its own search.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the composer `@` panel in every Hermes chat. `ChatView` is the only place that builds a `HermesChatTurnCoordinator`, and `completeFilePaths` is its only file-search entry. Chip confirmation is deliberately unchanged.
- **Targets:** app and tests. **Multi-server:** n/a (per-session RPC, existing generation guards).
- **Connection modes:** the host caches the file walk per root, and a keystroke costs one RPC, the same as today. `timesOutLocally: true` already bounds it.
- **Backends:** `local` only. The panel is already gated on `workspace.isLocal` (`ChatViewModel.swift:4677–4680`), and the host's fuzzy branch requires local too.
- **Native quality, docs:** no UI change.

## Tests

`BotFilePathSearchTests`:
- Replace `testWordForBareTriggerListsTheRoot` with one table assertion over `panelWord`: `"" → "."`, `"s" → "s"`, `"src/Ch" → "src/Ch"`, `"View" → "@file:View"`.
- `listingWord` keeps the old expectations.
- Keep `testPlainAndDirectiveItemsDecodeToRows`, which covers `@file:`/`@folder:` decoding. Add a scripted coordinator case in `HermesChatTurnTests`: the panel sends `@file:View`, while chip confirmation sends the plain candidate. Helper-only tests miss wrong call-site wiring.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotFilePathSearchTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a Hermes chat on a local backend, `@Chat` offers nested files whose names match, ranked by the host.
- [ ] `@src/` still lists `src`'s entries. `@` alone still lists the root. `@s` still shows folders.
- [ ] Restored drafts still turn known `@path`s into chips (chip confirmation unchanged).
- [ ] webui chats behave exactly as before.

## Manual test plan

1. In a Hermes chat on this repository (local backend), type `@ChatView`: `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift` appears near the top.
2. Type `@HermesMobile/Fe`: the folder listing appears as before.
3. Pick a nested file, send, reopen the chat: the chip still draws.
4. In a Docker or SSH backend chat, the panel stays closed, as today.

## Out of scope

- Files workspace search (25, which reuses `panelWord`).
- Allowing paths with whitespace in the panel (a chip can't name them).

## Decisions

None. This is a bug fix against the pinned contract.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(hermes): search Files across the workspace, not just opened folders
body:
**What the user gets:** Files search finds files in folders you haven't opened.
**Why it matters:** In a lazily loaded tree, unopened folders are unsearchable.
**Cost:** Small–Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 25 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S–M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes RPC `complete.path` (fuzzy basename branch). Verified at pin `ca678285` (GitHub blob hashes match). Live deployment unverified; 24 defines the integration check. |
| Depends on | #1388 (adds `BotFilePathSearch.panelWord` and the verified word spelling) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1138](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1138) (adjacent: why Hermes folders load on tap) · [#222](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/222) (adjacent: session artifacts in Files) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #8, code-surfaces-sol #4 |

## Problem

In a Hermes chat, Files opens folders lazily, restoring any expansion saved for that workspace. The search field filters only what has been listed. Searching for a file the agent mentioned, in a folder the user never opened, shows "No Matches" for a file that exists.

## What T3 does

Typing in Files runs a debounced (200 ms) server search across the whole workspace (`projectEnvironment.searchEntries`, 200-result limit). Hits merge into the tree with their ancestors (`apps/mobile/src/features/files/useFileTreeEntries.ts:105–151, 291–336`). This is filename and path search, not content search. Reference only.

## Hermex today

- `FileTree.visibleNodes(expanded:searchQuery:)` walks only directories already in `children` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FileTree.swift:136–171`). `FileBrowserViewModel.visibleNodes(matching:)` forwards to it (`Features/Workspace/FileBrowserViewModel.swift:41–43`).
- A Hermes client does not auto-expand top-level folders by default; saved workspace expansion can still reopen them: `HermesWorkspaceFileClient.opensTopLevelFolders = false` (`Networking/Hermes/HermesWorkspaceFileClient.swift:34`), per #1138. Unopened subtrees are therefore unsearchable.
- `FileBrowserView` shows "No Matches / Try a different file name or path." when the filter empties (`Features/Workspace/FileBrowserView.swift:72–81`). It has no remote search source; it gets only a `WorkspaceFileClient` (`:9, 16–20`).
- `ChatView` builds `FileBrowserView(files: workspaceFiles, …)` from the toolbar (`Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1123–1131`). It shows only while the Hermes folder is browsable (`ChatView.swift:880–883`, `HermesWorkspaceContext.isLocal`). The chat's `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.completeFilePaths` already runs `complete.path` on the attached runtime (`Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:645–651`).
- At the pin, `complete.path` with `@file:<name>` (2+ characters, no `/`, local backend) runs a ranked, repo-wide basename search capped at 30 rows (see 24 for the line-level contract). Both Files and the composer see paths relative to the session's folder (`HermesWorkspaceFileClient` doc comment, `:21–30`). The result paths can address Files previews. Search is bounded (30 entries from a capped file walk), not an exhaustive index; do not promise every file is discoverable.

## Proposal

Inject optional `FileWorkspaceSearch = @MainActor (String) async throws -> [ComposerFilePathSearch.Match]` into `FileBrowserView`; nil keeps loaded-tree filtering. `ChatViewModel` exposes a loader for the current local Hermes workspace, calling `completeFilePaths(_, word: .panel, browsing: true)` without mutating composer search state. `hermesTurn` is private to that model; ChatView cannot call it directly. Detached runtimes throw `.stale`; webui gets nil.

`FileBrowserViewModel` owns remote matches, in-flight/error state and a generation. Queries shorter than two trimmed characters or containing `/` clear remote state and keep today's tree filtering. Otherwise debounce about 250 ms, cancel on replacement, call the loader and publish only for the captured query/workspace generation. Key the view task by query **and** `files?.scope`; workspace replacement must replace the loader too. Clear immediately on a newer query, disappearance or scope change. Inject the debounce gate in tests.

Show a flat “Workspace” section of file hits (name, parent path) above loaded-tree matches, deduplicated by path. Leave remote folder navigation for later. The host's 30-entry cap includes folders; filtering them may leave fewer file rows. Use static “Searching…” text. Only show No Matches after a successful settled search, not during loading or after failure; failures show “Workspace search unavailable” with Retry while preserving tree filtering.

Tapping a remote row constructs `FileTreeNode(entry:parentPath:)` from a file `WorkspaceEntry` and sets `openedFile` with no prefetch. **Do not call existing `open(_:)`:** it calls `viewModel.select(path:)`, which lists/expands every ancestor (`FileBrowserView.swift:172–183`). The result should open without hidden folder traversal; clear any old `openedFilePrefetch` first.

`BotFilePathSearch.matches` currently drops whitespace paths for composer chips (`Features/Bots/BotFilePathSearch.swift:37–40`). Add `browsing: Bool = false` so Files can retain them. Keep the absolute-path/`..` rejection and default composer behavior.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks.** Use the `html-communication` skill: the search results with a Workspace section above tree matches, the in-flight state, no matches, and a backend without remote search. Light and dark, large Dynamic Type. Publish, report the URL, stop for a pick.
2. `BotFilePathSearch.matches(from:browsing:)`.
3. `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.completeFilePaths(_:word:browsing:)`, building on 24's word kinds.
4. `FileBrowserViewModel`: owned remote state/search, publication guard, and reset/loader replacement in `switchWorkspace(to:)`.
5. `FileBrowserView`: the `search` parameter, the sections, the remote row view (reuse `FileTreeRowView` at depth 0 if it reads well, else a small row), and the empty-state logic.
6. `ChatViewModel`/`ChatView`: expose/pass the loader, nil while cached (Files is already disabled then, `ChatView.swift:1130`).
7. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, then localize “Workspace”, “Searching…” and the inline search failure/retry copy.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** the chat toolbar → Files. The transcript file-link sheet opens a single file: n/a.
- **Targets:** app only.
- **Multi-server:** the closure is the chat's own coordinator (one server, Profile, session and folder). `switchWorkspace` clears results when the scope changes.
- **Connection modes:** one locally timed-out RPC per settled query. Reattach can throw `.stale`; clear results and offer Retry, never show old-scope hits.
- **Backends:** local only. Docker and SSH chats don't show Files today.
- **Native quality:** section header semantics for VoiceOver. Row label "name, in folder". Dynamic Type. Use static “Searching…” text while in flight, respecting the project's no continuously repainting animation rule.
- **webui:** unchanged (fixes only).

## Tests

`FileBrowserViewModelTests`, scripted loader and injected debounce gate:
- A query of 2+ characters publishes the remote matches. A reply for an older query that lands after a newer one is dropped (generation guard).
- A workspace switch with unchanged query replaces the loader and rejects its old reply. Failure is distinct from no matches. No sleeps/polling.

`BotFilePathSearchTests`: `matches(from:browsing: true)` keeps a path with a space; the default still drops it.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/FileBrowserViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotFilePathSearchTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a Hermes local chat, Files → search "GitDiff" finds `HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitDiffView.swift` without opening any folder.
- [ ] Tapping the result opens its preview without listing ancestor folders.
- [ ] One-character and path-shaped queries behave exactly as today.
- [ ] A slow reply never replaces newer results. Moving the folder with the same query clears/reissues the search through the new loader. Failed searches are distinct from no matches.
- [ ] webui Files is unchanged.

## Manual test plan

1. Hermes chat on this repository (local backend) → Files. Don't expand anything.
2. Search "SourceHighlighter": the Workspace section lists it, and tapping opens it.
3. Type quickly "Sou" → "Source" → "SourceF": the results settle on the last query.
4. Search "HermesMobile/Fe": the tree filter only, as today.
5. Turn off the network mid-search: remote results clear, loaded-tree filtering remains, and the inline unavailable state offers Retry without an alert.

## Out of scope

- Content (grep) search.
- Revealing a remote result inside the tree (expanding its ancestors).
- webui servers.

## Decisions

- Should remote **folder** matches show, and what should tapping one do (reveal in tree vs filter to it)? Recommendation: files only for this slice. Revealing a folder means loading every ancestor over the network, which deserves its own small issue if users ask.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(workspace): show a Markdown file's source, and copy any file's path
body:
**What the user gets:** Markdown files get a Source view, and any file can copy its relative path.
**Why it matters:** Small, frequent file-viewer gaps.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 26 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#222](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/222) (adjacent: artifacts in Files) |
| Needs mock first | yes (new Markdown mode and menu layout/copy) |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #9, code-surfaces-sol #7 |

## Problem

A Markdown file in Files (a README, an agent's plan, a skill's `SKILL.md`) renders only as formatted text. There's no way to see its raw text, frontmatter, line numbers or wrap toggle, and its toolbar has no actions menu at all. A transcript link like `PLAN.md:42` opens the rendered document and ignores the line. Separately, no file offers Copy Path, so referring to it in a prompt means retyping the path.

## What T3 does

The file screen's menu offers Preview and Source mode toggles, word wrap, Copy path, and Copy contents (`apps/mobile/src/features/files/ThreadFilesRouteScreen.tsx:242–334, 784–880`). CSV and TSV get a capped table preview (`DelimitedFilePreview.tsx`, 100 rows × 30 columns). Reference only.

## Hermex today

- `FilePreviewView` routes `.text` to `markdownContent` when `isMarkdownFile`, else to `sourceContent` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewView.swift:180–184`).
- The toolbar menu `sourceActionsMenu` (Wrap Lines, Copy, Select Text) is shown only for non-Markdown text (`:75–78, 157–177`). Markdown has only a long-press context menu with Select Text and Copy (`:258–275`).
- `sourceContent` already renders any text on `SourceFileSurface` with `targetLine: initialLine` (`:213–232`). Markdown would get the gutter, colour, wrap and line targeting for free.
- `initialLine` arrives from transcript links (`Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:847–853`). The Markdown path drops it.
- `FilePreviewViewModel.isMarkdownPath` decides the route (`FilePreviewView.swift:278–281`). Large Markdown is pre-chunked by the view model (`markdownChunks`, `:236–247`).
- No Copy Path exists anywhere in the viewer. `entry.path` is workspace-relative on both server kinds; `HermesWorkspaceFileClient` guarantees relative paths in rows, previews and errors (`Networking/Hermes/HermesWorkspaceFileClient.swift:21–30`).

## Proposal

1. **Preview / Source for Markdown.** Add `@State private var markdownMode: MarkdownViewMode = .preview` (`enum MarkdownViewMode { case preview, source }`). Seed it with `.source` when `initialLine != nil`, so a line link lands on its line.
   - `previewContent`: for a Markdown file, `.preview` renders `markdownContent`; `.source` renders `sourceContent(file)`.
   - Show `sourceActionsMenu` for Markdown too. At its top, add `Picker("View", selection: $markdownMode)` with Preview (`doc.richtext`) and Source (`chevron.left.forwardslash.chevron.right`), shown only for Markdown. Wrap Lines appears only in Source.
   - The mode is per view, not persisted (YAGNI).
2. **Copy Path.** Add **Copy Path** to the same menu for every text file. Also add a small toolbar `Menu` (or reuse the export cluster) so images, Quick Look files and unavailable previews get it. It copies a non-empty, workspace-relative `entry.path`, the path the tree or parsed link used. Hide/disable for nil, absolute or escaping paths; never fall back to `file.path` or a host path. Copying gives the existing `ChatHaptics.copied` feedback.
3. Rename the existing "Copy" to **Copy Contents** so the two copies read distinctly.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks.** Use `html-communication`: distinct menu-only vs. visible Preview/Source control variants, plus text/image/unavailable menus, light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Publish the URL and stop for a maintainer pick before implementation.
2. `FilePreviewView`: `MarkdownViewMode`, the seeded state in `init` (`_markdownMode = State(initialValue: initialLine == nil ? .preview : .source)`), the `previewContent` branch, and menu visibility.
3. `sourceActionsMenu(content:)`: the mode picker for Markdown, Copy Path, and the Copy → Copy Contents rename.
4. Copy Path for non-text previews: put it in a menu next to Export, since the current toolbar has separate icon buttons. A single `ellipsis.circle` menu holding Copy Path (and later actions) is enough.
5. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, then update the String Catalog: "View", "Preview", "Source", "Copy Path", "Copy Contents".
6. Update the `FilePreviewView` type comment ("Markdown keeps the chat renderer…") to mention the Source mode.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** Files → file, and transcript file links (`fileReferenceSheet`). Both use `FilePreviewView`.
- **Targets:** app only. **Multi-server:** n/a (view-local state; the path is relative).
- **Reverse states:** the mode toggles both ways from the same menu.
- **Native quality:** the Picker inside a Menu renders as a native inline choice with VoiceOver selection traits. Source mode inherits `SourceFileSurface`'s accessibility. Dynamic Type. Light and dark. No animation.
- **Privacy:** only the relative path is copied, never the chat folder's host path (`HermesWorkspaceContext.cwd` is "never shown").
- **webui:** shared view, client-only. Both server kinds get it.

## Tests

Run existing `SourceFileViewModelTests` and `ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests`, then verify the mode/line-link wiring in the integrated manual pass. Do not introduce a helper and a default-value assertion solely to test a state initializer.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SourceFileViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Markdown file shows the actions menu with View: Preview / Source.
- [ ] Source shows line numbers, syntax colour and Wrap Lines. Preview is unchanged.
- [ ] A transcript link `README.md:12` opens in Source with line 12 placed and highlighted.
- [ ] Copy Path puts the workspace-relative path on the pasteboard for text, image and Quick Look files.
- [ ] Copy Contents retains the existing loaded text/preview behavior; it must not claim a full file when the server preview was truncated.
- [ ] Large Markdown in Preview still renders in chunks (no regression in open time).

## Manual test plan

1. Files → `README.md`. Menu → Source: line numbers show. Toggle Wrap Lines. Back to Preview.
2. Menu → Copy Path, then paste in the composer: `README.md` (relative).
3. Open an image → menu → Copy Path.
4. Have the agent reply with a link to `docs/agents/i18n.md:20` and tap it: Source, line 20.
5. Check dark mode and the largest Dynamic Type size.

## Out of scope

- **CSV / TSV table preview.** A follow-up: a bounded, off-main parse with a real quoted-field parser, capped at about 100 rows × 30 columns, a truncation notice, and the source still available. Needs its own mock. File it separately if wanted.
- HTML or SVG rendered previews.
- Copying the host (absolute) path.

## Decisions

- Should the Markdown mode persist per app (like Wrap Lines) or reset per file? Recommendation: reset per file. Preview is the right default for reading, and a line link already opens Source.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(hermes): show the branch's pull request in the Git menu
body:
**What the user gets:** The Git menu shows and opens the branch's pull request.
**Why it matters:** Completes the agent finished → reviewed → open the PR loop from the phone.
**Cost:** Small–Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 27 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | S–M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes `GET /api/git/review/ship-info?path=`; verified at pin `ca678285`, deployment unverified. Needs authenticated `gh` on the host. |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1232](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1232) (adjacent: menu refresh) · [PR #917](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/917) (merged Safari presenter reused here) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #6; code-surfaces-sol #8 |

## Problem

When the agent opens a PR, the phone has no Git-menu link to it. The user must find a URL in chat. The host can look up the checked-out branch's PR through `gh`, but Hermex never asks.

## What T3 does

Its Git overview offers Open PR with live number/state detail (`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/git/GitOverviewSheet.tsx:126–173,206–224,319–353`). Reference only; its full PR client is out of scope.

## Hermex today

- `GitActionsMenuButton` has Changes, Write and Update sections, no PR row (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitActionsMenuButton.swift:25–90`). Chat wiring is in `Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1442–1480`; `onTap` currently only plays a haptic.
- `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel.load()` reads info, sync support, status and branches (`Features/Workspace/GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:130–176`). Successful branch switch, remote actions and quick commit have separate completion paths (`:225–274,345–359`); `refreshAfterExternalMutation()` covers turn-end/advanced-sheet changes (`:388–399`).
- `HermesREST` has no PR route (`Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:245–293`). `GitDataClient.isHermes` already distinguishes server kind (`Networking/APIClient+Git.swift:20`).
- `SafariView.present` uses `SFSafariViewController`; `InAppBrowserPolicy.opensInApp` accepts only HTTP(S) with a host (`Features/Chat/SafariView.swift:4–21`, `InAppBrowserPolicy.swift:8–10`).

**Pinned contract:** verified through read-only GitHub contents at `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`; cached blob hashes match.

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/git.py:150–152` defines `GET /api/git/review/ship-info?path=`. `path` must be the repository root, as for existing Git reads.
- `hermes_cli/web_git.py:409–416`: missing/unauthed gh yields `{ghReady: false, pr: null}`. Otherwise `gh pr view --json url,state,number` yields `{ghReady: true, pr: {url,state,number}}`, or null PR. State is gh's raw uppercase value, not a Hermes enum; there is no title or draft flag.
- Each gh subprocess has a 30-second timeout (`web_git.py:22,375–395`); ship-info invokes auth status then PR view, so the whole operation is not bounded to one 30-second call. The phone's normal REST request timeout is 15 seconds (`HermesConnection.swift:123`). Keep the normal timeout and silently omit unavailable PR data.
- `POST /api/git/review/pr-list` exists (`git.py:155–157`, `web_git.py:456–484`) but is unnecessary for a number/state link. Do not add it in this slice.

## Proposal

Use only ship-info. Add `GitPullRequest` with required validated number/HTTP(S) URL and optional normalized state (unknown → nil). Parse at the networking boundary using tolerant `BotJSON` access: absent/malformed PR fields mean no actionable link; never crash or show a bogus PR #0.

Add `HermesREST.gitShipInfo(repository:)` and `GitDataClient.pullRequest() async throws -> GitPullRequest?`, defaulting to nil on webui. `HermesGitClient` resolves the existing repository root and reads the route. Transport failures reach the caller; `ghReady == false` is an ordinary nil result.

`GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel` owns one cancellable PR task, independent of status/branch loading. Starting it must not make `load()` or turn-end status wait for gh. Keep a roughly 60-second freshness stamp and coalesce repeated reads. Refresh if stale on initial repository load and menu open; force invalidation after branch checkout, successful push (including Commit & Push) and turn-end refresh, since the agent can create a PR externally. Clear the displayed link immediately when the branch/repository identity changes. Publish only for the captured generation and non-retired model. Retire/disappear cancels ownership; cancellation or a late reply cannot repopulate another folder's menu. No polling timer.

When a valid PR exists, add “Pull Request #N” with optional Open/Merged/Closed state, plus Copy Link. Tap uses the existing Safari presenter after the HTTP(S) policy check. No row/error when absent, unavailable or timed out. Do not add title/draft fields the chosen endpoint cannot supply.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for distinct menu placements, open/merged/unknown state and no-PR variants; light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Publish the URL and stop for a maintainer pick before implementation.
2. Add endpoint, tolerant result mapping and protocol method/default. An authorized read-only deployment check may inspect `/openapi.json` and ship-info; no live host has been checked here.
3. Add the owned PR task, generation/freshness state and invalidation/retirement paths. Wire menu-open refresh through its existing `onTap` callback.
4. Add menu actions and ChatView callbacks. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, then localize number/state/link actions.
5. Record the verified handler/shape and any authorized integration result in the PR.

## Surfaces

- Entry: chat Git menu; no new PR screen. App/tests only; extensions n/a.
- Server/Profile/session/folder isolation follows the repository client. PR state is memory only and additionally invalidated on branch changes.
- Read-only; no reverse mutation. Copy Link uses existing haptics. Tunnel/gh failure must not delay Changes.
- VoiceOver reads number and known state; Dynamic Type and light/dark; no new animation or dependency. webui unchanged.

## Tests

- `APIClientGitTests`: root-scoped ship-info request and valid number/link mapping; missing/invalid fields yield no actionable PR, unknown state keeps a valid link.
- `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`: hold the PR response with a continuation while status finishes; retiring or changing branch prevents the old link from appearing. Force refresh bypasses freshness after a push. No real sleeps.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The current branch's PR opens in Safari; Copy Link copies its URL.
- [ ] No gh, no PR, timeout or malformed response gives no row and no alert.
- [ ] A held PR response does not delay the Changes count.
- [ ] Switching branch/folder/server cannot expose a stale PR link.
- [ ] Menu reopening after freshness expiry rechecks externally changed state; webui unchanged.

## Manual test plan

1. On a test branch with a PR, open the menu, follow the link, close Safari and copy it.
2. Switch to a branch without a PR, then move folder: no previous link remains.
3. Have a separate authorized test action change PR state; reopen the menu after freshness expiry and check the new state.
4. With gh unavailable or a slow host, Changes remains usable and no PR error appears.

## Out of scope

Creating/pushing/merging a PR, title/draft enrichment via pr-list, checks/reviews, and transcript-recovered PRs. Create PR would publish externally and requires a separate maintainer decision and reviewable confirmation flow.

## Decisions

None. Recommend number/state only, using the single existing read route.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: fix(hermes): keep a turn's committed work in its turn-changes card
body:
**What the user gets:** A turn's changes card keeps work the agent committed.
**Why it matters:** The card empties after a commit and mixes in unrelated edits today.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 3 (#1361) · order 28 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability / UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes rev-parse and review list/diff with `scope=lastTurn&base=<sha>`; verified at pin `ca678285`. Live deployment unverified. Exact per-turn history needs new server support. |
| Depends on | #1386 (adds `GitReviewScope` and scoped review reads) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1129](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1129) (open, adjacent wrong-file recap join; preserve its separate scope) |
| Needs mock first | yes (range label and fallback explanation) |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #1; code-surfaces-sol #3 |

## Problem

The latest turn's File changes card joins tool-touched paths with uncommitted Git status. If the agent commits those files, their status rows disappear: the card shows +0 −0 and cannot open them. The host can compare a pre-turn commit with the current tree, though it cannot reconstruct exact turn snapshots.

## What T3 does

T3 opens checkpoint N−1 to N for a turn (`apps/mobile/src/features/review/useReviewSections.ts:97–130`, `ThreadFeed.tsx:1837–1905`). Those snapshots are server-owned. The explorer's claim that Hermes Desktop records HEAD at turn start is stale: at the pin, `apps/desktop/src/store/review.ts:24–26` uses only uncommitted scope and has no `$reviewTurnBase`.

## Hermex today

- `ChatView.turnChangesRecapSummary` covers the latest turn, joining `latestTurnToolCalls` with uncommitted `status` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:1505–1518`). `TurnFileChangeAggregator` gives unmatched paths zero counts/nil `gitFile` (`Models/TurnFileChangeSummary.swift:118–131`). It deliberately excludes shell-tool changes from attribution (`:136–138`).
- `presentTurnDiff` does nothing without diffable rows (`ChatView.swift:1523–1527`). The turn-end stream hook refreshes repository status (`:3612–3628`).
- `HermesREST.gitHead` already reads rev-parse (`Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:601–602`). Prompt dispatch is centralized in `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.submit` after attach/uploads and a `beforePrompt` hook (`Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:450–484`).
- `beginTurn`, `adoptStart` and snapshot replay own turn identity, including starts before the submit reply (`:951–962,1011–1014,1029–1037`). A ChatView send-button hook alone misses queued/external starts and retry/rewind paths.

**Pinned contract:** verified by read-only GitHub contents at `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`; cached blobs match.

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/git.py:145–147` returns rev-parse `{sha}` (nullable), HEAD by default (`web_git.py:332–333`).
- `web_git.py:247–267`: lastTurn list returns `{files,base}` using `git diff --numstat <base>`: commits since base **plus current tracked uncommitted changes**, including changes that predated the turn. Untracked rows carry `status: "?"`; `_review_result` fills bounded insertion counts (`:238–244`). Other rows all carry M, not a reliable added/deleted classification. Missing base gives empty/null.
- LastTurn diff is `git diff <base> -- file` (`:294–295`), empty for genuinely untracked files. Existing `/api/git/file-diff` can synthesize all-add only when the file is still untracked (`:302–311`). It is safer than blindly calling uncommitted review diff, which can all-add a clean tracked file (`:298–299`).
- Neither lastTurn nor rollback provides an immutable end-of-turn snapshot. This slice must not promise exact attribution/history.

## Proposal

Extend 22 with `.since(base: String)` → `scope=lastTurn&base=...`, and expose `HermesGitClient.headSHA()`.

Capture the base at the common coordinator boundary for an idle, direct `.send` only, **awaiting one HEAD read before prompt dispatch** after attach/uploads. Do not launch it fire-and-forget: an agent can commit before that read finishes. This adds one normal REST round trip; errors/null HEAD fall back without retry, while cancellation/stale ownership aborts the send as usual. Recheck generation, workspace and absence of a competing turn after the await; coordinator `isIdle` itself includes `submitsInFlight == 0` and is false inside this submission. The existing 15-second REST timeout bounds a failed request; the latency trade-off requires the maintainer's pick before implementation.

Keep a pending base owned by that submission, then bind it to the corresponding local turn identity when start frames or the accepted reply establish the turn. Start frames can precede the reply. Retain it across a reattach of that same turn; discard on definitive refusal, a different/queued/external/rewound turn, workspace change or teardown. Steer/queue submissions do not overwrite the running turn's base, but a subsequently auto-started queued turn must clear it. Ambiguous association falls back. Do not keep an unkeyed SHA on the availability model.

Expose the latest matching base through `ChatViewModel`. At turn end, `GitWorkspaceAvailabilityViewModel` reads `review(scope: .since(base))` into a separate result keyed by turn and workspace. Drop late reads when either changes; never overwrite the uncommitted toolbar/commit status. The card joins against this result only while its identity matches. A failed scoped read uses the uncommitted fallback and its label.

Include scope/base in `TurnDiffPresentation` so the sheet uses the same range as its counts. Extend 20's progress key by `.since(base)`; current uncommitted status cannot prune this range's progress. LastTurn diff first; if empty for a row originally marked untracked, use existing file-diff for an all-add fallback. Preserve size/binary handling. Keep synthetic M from becoming a false kind badge.

Label the range honestly: “Since turn start” with a visible explanation that it compares the earlier HEAD to today's tree and includes pre-existing uncommitted changes; “Uncommitted changes” without a valid base/result.
