Other sessions/user edits can enter the range. Reopened chats have no base and use the fallback. The Changes sheet remains independent.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks/decision:** use `html-communication` for distinct compact range/explanation treatments and fallback, light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Publish, report the URL and stop for the pick, including approval of the pre-dispatch read latency.
2. Re-read [#1129](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1129); preserve its separate path-matching work. Verify route deployment only on an explicitly authorized test host.
3. Extend scoped requests/client reads from 22, including safe untracked fallback.
4. Implement submission/turn-owned base state in `HermesChatTurnCoordinator`, exposing read-only state via `ChatViewModel`; handle begin/adopt/replay/refusal/teardown.
5. Add keyed end-of-turn result state and publication guards to the availability model. Wire recap source and scope-bearing presentation in `ChatView`.
6. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, localize labels/explanation and update the recap's source comment. Record contract evidence/limits in the PR.

## Surfaces

App/tests only. Applies to latest-turn card and per-file taps on local Hermes workspaces. Direct sends can capture; queued, retry/rewind and external turns safely fall back unless explicitly associated. webui unchanged. Server/Profile/session/folder/turn identity must survive reconnect without carrying across a different turn. Read-only; no rollback. No new dependency/animation. VoiceOver reads range and limitation; Dynamic Type/light/dark apply.

## Tests

- `HermesChatTurnTests`: hold HEAD read with a continuation and prove prompt is not dispatched first; early start-before-reply binds correctly. A queued next turn, refusal or changed workspace cannot reuse the old base. Same-turn reattach preserves it. No sleeps/polling.
- `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`/`TurnFileChangeAggregatorTests`: committed tool-touched file gets scoped counts and an openable row; late previous-turn result is rejected; read failure falls back with the uncommitted scope.
- `APIClientGitTests`: scope/base/root encoding, and an untracked file opens all-add while a file committed since list-read uses its since-base patch.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests --only HermesMobileTests/TurnFileChangeAggregatorTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A direct turn that edits with recognized file tools then commits has counts/openable committed diffs.
- [ ] Untracked files open all-add; already-committed files are not misrepresented as all-add.
- [ ] Scope matches the source used for counts; limitations are visible, and no old base crosses a turn/folder/server boundary.
- [ ] HEAD failure sends normally after that failed read; cancellation does not send. Reopening/external turns use the labeled fallback.

## Manual test plan

1. In a disposable test repo, ask for two edits using file tools and a commit. Review the card and patches.
2. Create an untracked file; open all-add. Check an existing uncommitted edit is explained as included.
3. Queue another turn, reattach during a turn, reopen the chat, and switch folder/server; verify base/fallback ownership.

## Out of scope

Exact snapshots, older-turn history, shell-change attribution, rollback/undo, and changing the global Changes sheet's scope.

## Decisions

Accept one HEAD round trip before direct sends? Recommendation: yes for a reliable base; failure falls back. If latency is unacceptable, defer capture until the server supplies a turn-start SHA rather than knowingly shipping a race.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(sessions): lift sessions waiting for you above the rest of the list
body:
**What the user gets:** Sessions waiting on you appear at the top of the list.
**Why it matters:** "Something needs me" should be the first row, not something to scroll for.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 2 (#1360) · order 29 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes `session.active_list`, already polled; verified at pin `ca678285` |
| Depends on | #1365 (update its ordinary-row walker to include Needs You first) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#279](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/279) (overlaps state filters; ready-for-human) · [#1088](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1088) (overlaps proposed list sections; ready-for-human) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | navigation-opus #3; navigation-sol #1 |

**Status: partial premise false — do not synthesize unloaded rows.** The explorer proposed building waiting rows from active_list beyond the loaded pages. Its items lack Profile and source, and the handler ignores Profile. Keep this issue to loaded rows; recovering unloaded rows needs more server support.

## Problem

A waiting session shows “Input” in its time slot but stays among running and idle rows in recency order. The user has to scan for blocked work. Loaded sessions needing a response should appear together near the top.

## What T3 does

Its inbox prioritizes approval/input/request above working threads, with a separate Working shelf and placement grace (`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/threadListV2.ts:639–747`, `packages/client-runtime/src/state/threadInbox.ts:17–55,110–239`). Adopt the attention group only, not the shelf, grace timer or broader inbox model.

## Hermex today

- Sessions sort pinned first then recency (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:1606–1614`). Search locally matches then keeps that same sort (`:361–367`); it is not relevance-ranked.
- `ScheduledSessionGroups` partitions ordinary/scheduled in one pass (`SessionListViewModel.swift:21–57`). `scheduledSessionGroups` derives it from the current query/project scope (`:386–400`). `HermesSessionListView` calls this from its body and renders scheduled disclosure, then ordinary rows (`Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:132–181`).
- `SessionRowAttentionState.hermesStates` maps waiting to input, starting/working/streaming to working, ignoring idle/resuming/unknown (`Networking/Hermes/HermesSessionPage.swift:336–349`).
- `readHermesStatuses` filters active_list to loaded session keys; it rereads every five seconds while busy, or retrying a failure after busy (`SessionListViewModel.swift:77–79,2268–2289`). A disconnect/failure clears live states (`:2212–2230,2282–2286`), and unchanged maps do not invalidate rows (`:2292–2294`).
- `SessionInteractiveRow` owns existing actions/selection styling and motion (`Features/SessionList/SessionListComponents.swift:849–908`). Bots already rank waiting > working > unread > newest within each group (`Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:133–154`); leave them alone.

**Pinned contract:** read-only GitHub contents at `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`; cached blob hashes match.

`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:1004–1015` returns non-finalized live process sessions in insertion order, reading only `current_session_id`. Runtime rows (`tui_gateway/server.py:2781–2802`) and schema `SessionActiveItem` (`apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`) carry current/id/timestamps/message count/model/preview/session_key/status/title, **no Profile or source**. Waiting does not distinguish approval from question. Stored keys can collide across Profiles (`server.py:2809–2812`): reuse the existing loaded-row attention policy, but do not claim new Profile-qualified accuracy or infer Profile for unknown rows.

## Proposal

Extend `ScheduledSessionGroups` with `needsYou`, passing an optional attention lookup into its pure initializer. After the existing query/project/Profile filtering, partition unarchived non-cron ordinary rows with `.input` into Needs You, preserving their current order; remove them from ordinary. Pinned waiting rows also move up. Keep cron rows in the existing scheduled treatment. Hermes only; omit attention grouping during search or while viewing cached data.

Render Needs You above the scheduled disclosure, after existing header/utility chrome, only when non-empty. Reuse `SessionInteractiveRow` and its actions. Suppress the ordinary-list empty state when either Needs You or scheduled has rows; an all-waiting list must not also say “No sessions”.

Keep grouping derived as today: it must respond to rows, filters and attention changes, not only state-map changes. No new cache, timer or request. Preserve row ids, but do not assume matching `.id` across separate `ForEach` containers guarantees view continuity. Keep selected/open-chat state outside row lifetime and avoid adding movement animation. Existing Reduce Motion policy applies.

Answering a request returns its row to ordinary order on the next successful status read. Lost live status empties the group under today's policy. If 10 changes reconnect behavior, follow that adopted stale-state policy instead of independently clearing or inventing confirmed waiting states.

Update 01's command row source to `needsYou + ordinary` in the same displayed order. Continue skipping scheduled rows, as 01 deliberately does. Compute this at key activation, without another cached ordering.

## Implementation steps

1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for a labeled group vs. waiting rows first without a header; show pinned/scheduled interaction, all-waiting/search/offline states, iPad sidebar, light/dark and large Dynamic Type. Read the comments of [#1088](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1088) and [#279](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/279) to avoid preempting their design decisions. Publish the URL and stop for a pick; those ready-for-human issues do not authorize their broader redesign.
2. Extend the partition initializer and `SessionListViewModel.scheduledSessionGroups` with attention only in the eligible Hermes scope.
3. Render the group in `HermesSessionListView`, reuse rows, update empty-state suppression and the command walker introduced in 01.
4. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`, then localize the header/accessibility copy. Record loaded-row/server limitations in the PR.

## Surfaces

- Entry: Hermes Sessions, iPhone, iPad sidebar and pushed list; keyboard ordering updated. Bots, push, deep links and Live Activities keep their existing destinations.
- App/tests only; extensions n/a. Server/Profile/project filters remain upstream of grouping; no new stored identities or persistence.
- Reverse: waiting → ordinary. Same RPC/backoff across connection modes; unknown/stale attention follows the existing reconnect policy.
- Native: header accessibility trait, existing row labels, Dynamic Type, light/dark and Reduce Motion. No new dependency or animation.

## Tests

In `HermesSessionListTests`, exercise the partition with waiting, working, pinned, archived and cron rows under a project filter: no duplicates, only eligible waiting rows lift, and ordinary order survives. Search/cached/webui inputs do not lift. Test the all-waiting empty-state decision at its policy owner if one is introduced; otherwise verify that rendering manually. No sleeps/polling.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests --only HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A loaded, visible ordinary waiting session appears under Needs You within a successful status read; no unloaded rows are fabricated.
- [ ] Answering restores ordinary order; working-only rows stay put.
- [ ] Search/project/Profile/cached rules remain intact; no contradictory empty state.
- [ ] Keyboard commands use Needs You then ordinary, still skipping scheduled.
- [ ] Disconnect/reconnect follows the adopted live-status policy; webui unchanged.

## Manual test plan

1. In a disposable loaded Hermes session, trigger approval or clarify, return to Sessions and verify grouping; answer and verify return.
2. Check a pinned waiting row, an all-waiting list, cron, search and a project filter. Repeat on iPad with keyboard commands and Reduce Motion.
3. Disconnect/reconnect and switch server/Profile: no invented rows or stale cross-scope group.

## Out of scope

Unloaded waiting rows/counts, Working shelf, unread lifting, new state filters and the broader design in the linked issues.

## Decisions

For unloaded waiting sessions, recommend deferring rows/counts until upstream supplies Profile-qualified identity. Push is optional and Live Activities follow selected work; neither guarantees alerting for these sessions. Group appearance/pinning precedence is decided by mocks.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(sessions): archive a session with a full swipe
body:
**What the user gets:** A full swipe archives a session (Undo already exists).
**Why it matters:** Mail-style one-gesture triage; Delete is never the full-swipe action.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 1 (#1359) · order 30 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none (the existing archive write and its Undo) |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#865](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/865) (adjacent: the archive Undo toast this relies on) |
| Needs mock first | no (native gesture, no new UI) |
| Sources | navigation-opus #6 |

**Corrections to the source:** navigation-opus proposed applying the same change to the Archived screen's Unarchive swipe. `ArchivedSessionsView` has no swipe actions, only a visible Unarchive button and a context menu (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/ArchivedSessionsView.swift:176–220`), so that part is dropped. The Bots inbox is deliberately excluded: its comment says "No full swipe: Delete confirms and Pin is a server write, so nothing should fire from a flick", and its Hide has no Undo (`Features/Bots/BotsInboxView.swift:356–369`).

## Problem

Triage on the session list takes two motions per row: swipe, then tap Archive. Mail and most iOS inboxes let a full swipe commit the primary, reversible action. Hermex already shows "Archived · Undo" after every archive, so a full swipe is safe.

## What T3 does

A full swipe past `max(actionsWidth + 44, rowWidth × 0.58)` commits the row's primary action (settle or archive), with a haptic when it arms and an Undo toast after. A destructive delete is never the full-swipe action when a reversible one exists (`apps/mobile/src/features/home/thread-swipe-actions.tsx:239–415`, `home/thread-undo-notice.ts`). Reference only. SwiftUI's `allowsFullSwipe` gives the native equivalent.

## Hermex today

- `SessionInteractiveRow` (`Features/SessionList/SessionListComponents.swift:849`) is used by both the webui and Hermes lists and the scheduled views (`:759, 1003, 1069`). It sets `.swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: false)` (`:890–892`).
- The trailing buttons are **Archive (first), then Delete** when `SessionRowActionPolicy.offersArchive` is true, and **Delete alone** otherwise (`:917–944`).
  - `offersArchive` is false for read-only rows, Bot Chats, and archived matches a Hermes search lists (`:116–127`).
  - The leading edge (Pin) is also `allowsFullSwipe: false` (`:887–889`).
- Archive shows "Archived · Undo" after the host confirms:
  - Hermes: `HermesSessionListView.archive` (`Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:766–785`).
  - webui: `SessionListView.archive` with `archiveToastRoute` (`Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1311–1333`).
- Delete from a swipe already opens a confirmation (`delete: { covers.deleting = $0 }`, `HermesSessionListView.swift:636`; webui `sessionPendingDeletion`, `SessionListView.swift:1102–1103`).
- This slice changes only the full-swipe gesture on rows that already offer Archive.

## Proposal

Make the trailing edge full-swipeable **only when Archive is its first button**:

```swift
.swipeActions(edge: .trailing,
              allowsFullSwipe: SessionRowActionPolicy.offersArchive(for: session)
                               && canShowSessionMutationActions(for: session)
                               && !viewModel.isMutating(session)) { … }
```

Reuse `offersArchive`; do not add a one-line alias that duplicates the policy.

- SwiftUI commits the first (edge-most) trailing button on a full swipe, which is Archive here. Keep system gesture behavior and existing success haptics; verify Reduce Motion in the integrated pass.
- Archive remains disabled while `viewModel.isMutating(session)`; gate full swipe on the same condition up front. Existing mutation ownership still prevents duplicate requests.
- Leading (Pin) stays `false`: pinning is a server write with no Undo toast.
- Bots inbox and the Archived screen: unchanged (see corrections above).

## Implementation steps

1. Use the expression above on `SessionInteractiveRow`'s trailing `.swipeActions` (`SessionListComponents.swift:890`). Keep the Archive → Delete button order and add a one-line comment that the order is what makes full swipe safe.
2. Check that each host shows the Undo toast after a full swipe:
   - the Hermes list;
   - the webui list;
   - the webui scheduled view, whose `actionToast` is non-nil only when `archiveToastRoute.host == .scheduled` (`SessionListView.swift:698`);
   - the Hermes scheduled view (`HermesSessionListView.swift:436`).

   If a host can archive without showing Undo, use `allowsFullSwipe: false` there.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** session rows on the Hermes and webui lists, the scheduled disclosure and the "View all" scheduled screen. Context menus are unchanged. Hardware keyboard: n/a.
- **Targets:** app only.
- **Multi-server:** n/a (per-row action on the active server).
- **Reverse states:** Undo in the toast, and Unarchive on the Archived screen.
- **Connection modes:** the archive write is unchanged. A failed archive uses the existing mutation failure path and reports through its host.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver users reach Archive through the actions rotor as today; full swipe is touch-only. Reduce Motion is handled by the system. Light and dark unchanged.
- **Cached data:** `canShowSessionMutationActions` is false while viewing cached data, so there are no swipe actions at all.

## Tests

Run existing `SessionListMutationTests`, which covers mutation policy and archive/restore behavior. The new behavior is the gesture reaching the first button; a duplicate policy alias test would not verify it. Prove full swipe, no full-swipe Delete, in-flight gating and Undo on each host in the integrated manual pass.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SessionListMutationTests`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a normal session row, a full trailing swipe archives it and shows "Archived · Undo". Undo restores it in place.
- [ ] On an archived match in Hermes search, a full swipe does nothing beyond revealing Delete. Delete never fires or opens its confirmation from a flick.
- [ ] Leading swipe (Pin) still needs a tap.
- [ ] Bots inbox rows still need a tap.
- [ ] Works on both Hermes and webui lists.

## Manual test plan

1. Hermes Sessions: full-swipe a disposable session left. It archives, and the toast shows. Tap Undo.
2. Search for an archived session, then full-swipe its row: only the Delete button shows.
3. Turn on Reduce Motion and repeat step 1.
4. Repeat step 1 on a webui server and both the scheduled disclosure and View all screens. Check a row mid-mutation cannot fire a second archive. Verify VoiceOver Archive and Undo on iPad too.

## Out of scope

- Full swipe on Bots inbox rows (Hide has no Undo).
- Full swipe for Pin.
- A custom arm threshold or haptic (use the system's).

## Decisions

None.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: bundled into the batch's merge-walk test session.

title: feat(hermes): show the stages reached by a failed connection attempt
body:
**What the user gets:** A failed connection shows which stages passed or failed, with copyable details.
**Why it matters:** Tunnel and proxy users can't tell which hop failed; raised by five explorers.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 31 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes sign-in and gateway requests only; pinned routes verified below; no new probes |
| Depends on | none; 08 adds network-path advice, 10 owns home recovery headers |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1079](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1079) (adjacent remote-reporting plan), [#304](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/304) (closed; discusses user-initiated local export) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | connection-state-sol #4, connection-state-opus #8, design-settings-sol #1, design-settings-opus #4(b,c) |

## Problem
A failed connection shows advice but does not expose which checks succeeded. A user cannot distinguish an unreachable dashboard, rejected credentials, a ticket failure and a refused live connection when reporting a problem. Preserve today's advice and let the user copy the evidence the app actually observed.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/connection/ConnectionDiagnosisDetails.tsx` shows succeeded, failed and unchecked hops, advice, facts and Copy Diagnostics. `packages/client-runtime/src/connection/diagnosis.ts:288–347` derives those facts from typed failures. Its relay health is not available to Hermex; do not invent tunnel-health stages.

## Hermex today
- `BotConnectionAdvice.message(for:address:)` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:132–169`) and `BotFailure.errorDescription` (L73–108) already cover network, auth and upgrade failures.
- `HermesConnection.beginSignIn` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:196–271`) logs a local step: status, page, token, refresh, login or identity. Open dashboards prove their token through `profilesActive` and do not read identity. `upgrade` (L451–470) obtains a ticket or page token; returning a request here **does not prove WebSocket success**.
- `HermesGateway` performs the real socket handshake (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:265–301`) and logs opening failures separately (L249–254).
- Saved setup uses a `BotTransport` and `wire.connect()` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:499–533`). Its browser path uses a local `HermesConnection` (L548–565). Onboarding/Add Server use another local connection (`HermesMobile/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingViewModel.swift:584–595`), preceded by host detection, which can fail before sign-in (L418–473). All currently expose error strings only.
- Pinned source verified read-only with `gh api repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/contents/<path>?ref=ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`: `hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py` (`GET /api/status`, `version`); `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py` (password login, identity, native token/refresh and ws-ticket); `hermes_cli/web_routers/profiles.py` (`GET /api/profiles/active`). No request shape changes are proposed.

## Proposal
Keep one bounded, in-memory `HermesAttemptRecord` per connection. Use ordered stage outcomes and a typed failure category with optional numeric code, formatted using the existing privacy-safe `HermesConnectionLog.reason` pattern (L833–850). Never copy `localizedDescription`, response bodies, addresses, headers, usernames, tokens or install IDs.

Stages: Status, Sign-in, Identity, Live authorization, Live handshake. Unexecuted stages remain Not checked; open sign-in leaves Identity unchecked. Status includes the compatibility/install checks. Sign-in includes page/native token/refresh/password as applicable. Live authorization succeeds after a usable ticket/page token is obtained; Live handshake succeeds only after `HermesGateway` completes its handshake.

Record only work already performed. Onboarding does not open a gateway, so both live stages remain unchecked. A detection failure needs a status-only snapshot from that probe; an invalid address has no attempt record. Browser cancellation is not a failed sign-in, and a token-exchange failure before `beginSignIn` must still be captured as Sign-in failure.

Expose the snapshot through `BotTransport` (a default nil value for doubles), forwarding from `BotClient.http`. Setup and onboarding retain a value before their temporary client goes away. For 32, expose an optional read-only lookup on `HermesConnections` for its current server only; it must never create/sign in a connection. Use attempt IDs plus existing retirement/generation guards: a late probe, sign-in or handshake cannot replace a newer record. A ticket-triggered reauthentication failure remains attributed to sign-in rather than being overwritten as a ticket failure.

Show one reusable `ConnectionAttemptDetails` below existing advice in saved setup, onboarding and Add Server. It contains stage rows and Copy Details. Export app/build/iOS, server kind, reported release, tested release (`HermesCompatibility.testedVersion`, not the commit SHA), timestamp and stages. No persistent log or global cross-server history.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish distinct disclosure, inline-checklist and copy-only mocks across saved setup/onboarding/Add Server, light/dark and AX5. Include copied text. Report the URL and **stop for a maintainer pick**.
2. Add the record and guarded updates in `HermesConnection`, including browser token exchange; wire actual handshake completion/failure from `HermesGateway` without starting any extra connection.
3. Forward snapshots through `BotTransport`/`BotClient`. Capture them in `BotConnectionSetup` and `OnboardingViewModel`, including detection failures. Clear form snapshots when inputs/error ownership change.
4. Add the chosen shared view and pure export formatter. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before editing the String Catalog.
5. Document the local export in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** three setup surfaces; recovery headers remain with 10.
- **Targets:** app/tests; extensions and webui auth n/a.
- **Multi-server:** snapshots follow one form/connection. Clear on retirement, switching or editing the destination; late results never cross servers.
- **Reverse states:** success replaces a failed attempt; error clearance hides Details.
- **Connection modes:** report observed checks, never infer tunnel health from a 52x.
- **Native quality:** localized stage labels, selectable facts, VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, light/dark; no new animation.

## Tests
Use scripted URLProtocol/gateway doubles:
- `HermesConnectionTests`: login 401 records Status passed, Sign-in failed, later checks unchecked; open sign-in does not claim identity success.
- `HermesGatewayTests`: obtaining a ticket followed by refused upgrade leaves authorization passed and handshake failed; retirement/new attempts reject stale completion.
- `OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests`: a failed detection retains only the failed status check for the current form.
- `HermesConnectionLogTests`: export omits fixture URL/credentials even when present in error userInfo.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesGatewayTests --only HermesMobileTests/OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionLogTests`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All three setup surfaces show existing advice plus the picked Details treatment.
- [ ] A usable ticket never claims the socket connected; skipped identity/live stages remain unchecked.
- [ ] Copied text contains only the listed diagnostic fields.
- [ ] Input changes, retirement and server switches cannot expose another attempt's details.

## Manual test plan
Use a disposable test connection: try a wrong password, then an unreachable address, from saved setup and Add Server/onboarding. Inspect stages, copy into Notes, check for host/credential leakage, and repeat with VoiceOver. Compare an open dashboard if available; its identity/live stages must not imply checks that were skipped.

## Out of scope
New probes, tunnel/relay health, persistent logs, remote upload, webui error-copy changes (#1366), network-path headline (#1372), recovery-header redesign (#1374).

## Decisions
Include raw OSLog lines? Recommend no: the bounded observed record is more useful and easier to keep private.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(settings): copy support details and prefill Report a Problem
body:
**What the user gets:** About can copy support details, and Report a Problem opens with versions prefilled.
**Why it matters:** Bug reports arrive without the facts the maintainer needs (see #1351).
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 32 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none added; only cached values, including `ServerAccount.serverVersion` |
| Depends on | none; include 31's attempt record only when already available; 33 adds a sanitized diagnostic summary later |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1079](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1079) (adjacent remote-reporting plan), [#1351](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1351) (example of missing version information), [#304](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/304) (closed; discusses deliberate local export) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | design-settings-opus #2, design-settings-sol #2 |

## Problem
Report a Problem opens GitHub's template chooser. The form asks users to type versions the app already knows, and still labels server version as “hermes-webui server version” although Hermes is the default kind. A previewed local support report and version prefill would reduce missing or incorrect information.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/diagnostics/SettingsDiagnosticsRouteScreen.tsx:29–133` builds a report on entry, distinguishes unavailable/empty states, and confirms Copy after writing to the clipboard. It asks users to read before sharing. `crash-log-model.ts:51–62` formats app version/build.

## Hermex today
- `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift:13–29` shows Version/Build and Report a Problem → `AppConfig.reportProblemURL` (`HermesMobile/Config/AppConfig.swift:7`, `issues/new/choose`). `SettingsView.swift:100` constructs About and has access to `authManager`.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` has text inputs `app-version` (L44), `ios-version` (L51), `server-version` (L58, old label at L60). The `connection-path` dropdown (L65–76) lacks LAN.
- `ServerAccount.kind` and `serverVersion` (`HermesMobile/Models/ServerAccount.swift:46–49`) provide cached kind/release. Webui version is nil here; Settings reads it live elsewhere.
- `HermesCompatibility.testedVersion` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCompatibility.swift:11`) is a tested **release**, not the pinned commit SHA. Its status-version origin is verified at the upstream pin in 31; this feature adds no API call.
- `HermesBrowserSignIn.offersTestingToggle` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesBrowserSignIn.swift:52–57`) checks Debug and the `.branch` bundle suffix. `PushEnvironment` describes APNs environment, not distribution channel. A normal Release bundle cannot distinguish App Store from TestFlight by suffix.

## Proposal
Add a pure `SupportReport`, built on demand from explicit non-secret inputs: app version/build, Debug/Branch/Release channel, iOS version, iPhone/iPad form factor, active server kind and cached release. Include the tested Hermes release **only for Hermes**, labeled accordingly; do not call it the tested webui version or commit. Unknown values say unknown.

Accept 31's existing current-connection snapshot when available and owned by this server. Setup-only records are not automatically available to About. Do not create a connection, sign in, or add global history to populate a report. No URL, host, display name, username, header, session or title enters the report.

About → **Copy Support Details** opens a sheet previewing the exact plain text, with Copy and a read-before-sharing footer. Rebuild for the active server on each open; invalidate/refresh a presented report if its server changes. The report text may remain English for support; UI copy is localized.

Build Report a Problem with `URLComponents`:
`https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml&app-version=…&ios-version=…&server-version=…`.

GitHub documents [custom text-field query prefill](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-an-issue#creating-an-issue-from-a-url-query); its [form schema](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema) identifies `id` as the query key. This verifies these three inputs; it does not establish that other field types cannot be prefilled. Leave connection path for the user because Hermex does not store it.

Opening this URL sends those version values to GitHub and browser history **before submission**. Keep full diagnostics, connection records and stack summaries out of the URL; the full report is copy-only. Retain the chooser fallback when report inputs are unavailable.

Update the template's server-version label to cover Hermes and webui, clarify app/iOS version descriptions, and add “Local network (LAN)” to connection path. Do not add a second localhost option; one exists already. Keep IDs stable.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish distinct About placements (version section versus Support section) and preview sheet mocks, light/dark and AX5. Report the URL and **stop for a pick**.
2. Add `SupportReport`/URL builder in `Features/Settings`, injecting only report fields. Reuse About's version/build readers; add a small Debug/Branch/Release classification using the existing suffix convention.
3. Supply active-server metadata from `SettingsView`; add the chosen sheet and prefilled link in About.
4. Update `bug_report.yml`. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before catalog changes. Do not claim every server kind shows the same Status screen; retain “or the upstream tag/commit you deployed” guidance.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points/targets:** About, main app/tests; extensions do not contribute diagnostics.
- **Multi-server:** only the active server, no cross-server snapshots or new network reads.
- **Reverse states:** sheet dismissal; no retained report history.
- **Connection modes:** user supplies the path; no hostname-based guessing.
- **Native quality:** selectable Dynamic Type text, VoiceOver Copy confirmation, light/dark; no added animation.
- **Docs:** bug template only; optionally mention prefilled versions in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Tests
`SupportReportTests` (new): report with Hermes release/attempt fixture contains allowed fields and omits fixture host/secrets; switching to webui never presents Hermes compatibility as webui compatibility. URL query round-trips spaces, plus signs, Unicode and ampersands and carries all three input IDs, without carrying the full report.

Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SupportReportTests`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Preview equals copied report and contains only listed fields.
- [ ] Report a Problem opens the bug form with three version inputs prefilled; no submission occurs automatically.
- [ ] Template supports both server kinds and LAN, retaining field IDs.
- [ ] Changing servers cannot retain the previous server's release/attempt; no extra request is made.

## Manual test plan
Open About, preview/copy into Notes, and check for host/credential leakage. Open Report a Problem and inspect the three fields without submitting. Repeat on another server and webui: release is unknown unless already cached. Test a Release TestFlight build's channel label; it must not claim App Store based solely on bundle ID.

## Out of scope
Remote upload/consent, screenshots, guessing network paths, new webui version reads, crash history (#1397), App Store/TestFlight receipt classification.

## Decisions
Include a webui release? Recommend only an already cached value; do not add a request to generate support text.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(settings): keep local crash and hang reports with MetricKit
body:
**What the user gets:** Crash and hang reports are kept on the device and can be copied into a bug report.
**Why it matters:** No crash evidence reaches the maintainer today; local-only, no third party.
**Cost:** Medium; needs the owner's hands on a physical iPhone.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 33 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | #1396 (About support placement and optional summary) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1079](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1079) (adjacent remote-reporting proposal; no remote collection here), [#976](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/976) (release crash monitoring), [#304](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/304) (closed; proposes bounded, redacted local export) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | design-settings-opus #3, performance-eng-opus #3 |

## Problem
Users cannot inspect and copy an app-owned crash or hang report from Hermex. Reports such as [#1351](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1351) can arrive without usable evidence. Apple release reporting remains useful, but a local support export would let the user deliberately provide additional evidence; it cannot promise to capture every freeze or crash.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/diagnostics/SettingsDiagnosticsRouteScreen.tsx` reads seven days of Expo startup-crash records, shows selectable details and empty/unavailable states, and copies a formatted report (`crash-log-model.ts`). This is prior art for a local report UI, not proof of MetricKit delivery behavior.

## Hermex today
- No MetricKit subscriber or OSLogStore reader exists in `HermesMobile/` or `HermesMobileTests/` at master `5125b512`.
- `PushAppDelegate` (`HermesMobile/Push/PushAppDelegate.swift:9`, launch at L17) is installed by `HermesMobileApp.swift:81` and is the existing registration point.
- About (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift:13–29`) has version/build and external links.
- Privacy manifests already exist at `HermesMobile/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` and `HermesShareExtension/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. Do not delete them or infer disclosure requirements from this issue.
- Apple distinguishes daily metrics from diagnostics: [MetricKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metrickit?changes=l_8___4&language=objc) documents diagnostic delivery immediately on iOS 15 and later. Delivery is system-controlled and not a guarantee of comprehensive coverage. Apple's [testing sample](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metrickit/track-performance-by-app-state-using-metrickit) says reports require a physical device; Xcode's Simulate MetricKit Payloads command is not a simulator test plan.

## Proposal
Add an app-lifetime `DiagnosticsLog: NSObject, MXMetricManagerSubscriber`, retained by the app delegate and registered once with `MXMetricManager.shared.add(_:)`. Use the existing Objective-C-compatible API supported by iOS 18; no new SDK or iOS 27-only API is needed. The callbacks arrive off-main; convert data there, serialize file operations, and publish view state on the main actor only while its load is current.

Store one **sanitized diagnostic entry** per crash/hang/CPU/disk-write diagnostic in `Application Support/Diagnostics`, main-app container only. A payload can contain multiple diagnostics of different kinds; one payload file is not one crash. Read the typed arrays on `MXDiagnosticPayload` and use each diagnostic's `applicationVersion` and `metaData.applicationBuildVersion`; retain the payload's begin/end time as a window, not an exact event timestamp.

Persist a small app-owned Codable record containing kind, window, app/build, numeric signal/exception or duration when supplied, and bounded stack frames (binary UUID, binary basename, offset, bounded children). Verify stack keys against a device-generated fixture before implementing the projection. Unknown fields are ignored; missing fields remain optional. Do not persist or export arbitrary `jsonRepresentation()`: exception descriptions and signpost metadata may contain user text, paths and other sensitive data; metadata also includes device-model information. Preview alone does not redact it. Omit free-text reasons, signposts, paths and unrelated metadata; preserve frame UUIDs/offsets for off-device symbolication.

Keep at most 10 entries, 14 days and 2 MiB total. Bound an individual entry before writing; deduplicate repeated delivery using its sanitized content. Prune on receive **and read**, so an idle installation cannot expose expired records. Serialize Delete/Delete All with storage so an in-flight older write cannot resurrect a deleted report. Use atomic protected writes; file failures must not crash launch.

About → Diagnostics shows date window, kind and build. Details previews the exact sanitized JSON copied, plus Copy and Delete; the page has Delete All. Empty copy says no reports have been received and that iOS controls availability. It does not claim the app never crashed or that reports require a 24-hour wait. Unreadable retained files show an unavailable entry with Delete.

32 may include a short count/latest-window summary from these sanitized entries; full stacks remain a separate explicit copy action, never URL query data.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish distinct About-row/support-section mocks, list/empty/details states, light/dark and AX5. Report the URL and **stop for a maintainer pick**.
2. Add app-only `DiagnosticsLog` and an injected-directory store, with deterministic time input for retention. Keep disk work off-main and serialize mutations.
3. Register and retain the subscriber in `PushAppDelegate`; update its responsibility comment. Convert callbacks into the sanitized record before storage.
4. Add Diagnostics UI and optional 32 summary. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before adding catalog copy/plurals.
5. Document coverage limits and physical-device fixture capture in `TESTFLIGHT.md`; no upload or release is part of implementation validation.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** About; app/tests only. Extensions are not registered and coverage must say so.
- **Multi-server:** app diagnostics have no server identity, URLs or session data.
- **Reverse states:** Delete/Delete All and retention, including late-write handling.
- **Connection modes:** n/a; collection/export adds no network request.
- **Native quality:** selectable text, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, light/dark, no animation or launch-time parsing.

## Tests
`DiagnosticsLogTests` (new), using sanitized crash/hang fixtures and a temporary directory:
- A mixed payload projection preserves useful signal/build/stack offsets while excluding fixture paths, user text, signposts and device model; missing fields do not discard another valid diagnostic.
- Repeated delivery, age/count/byte retention and Delete All during a pending write behave deterministically with injected time/gates.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/DiagnosticsLogTests`. Simulator tests exercise the store/projection, not real MetricKit delivery. Obtain real fixture shape from Xcode's simulated payload on a signed physical-device Debug build; do not fabricate Apple JSON keys.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Xcode-generated diagnostic payloads on a physical device appear in About with the correct kind/build/window.
- [ ] Preview equals copied sanitized JSON; sensitive fixture content never enters storage/export.
- [ ] Retention and deletion bounds hold without relaunch, including pending writes.
- [ ] No automatic upload, app-group storage, or claim of complete crash coverage.

## Manual test plan
On a signed physical-device Debug build, choose Xcode → Debug → Simulate MetricKit Payloads. Open About → Diagnostics, inspect/copy a report, relaunch to confirm persistence, then Delete All. Use fixture injection for simulator UI checks. Real-world system delivery is supplemental evidence, not a timed acceptance gate.

## Out of scope
Remote telemetry/consent (#1079), third-party crash SDKs, performance metric dashboards, symbolication on-device, extension processes, raw log export.

## Decisions
Report kinds? Recommend all four existing diagnostic arrays; label each explicitly rather than calling every entry a crash. App-launch diagnostics and any future kinds can wait.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the batch's single Branch TestFlight build).

title: fix(live-activity): quiet working states and remove invented progress
body:
**What the user gets:** The Dynamic Island stays quiet while working and only shows words for asks and outcomes; the invented progress rail goes.
**Why it matters:** Flickering clipped words and a bar that moves backwards are lying UI.
**Cost:** Small; needs the owner's hands on a physical iPhone.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 34 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none; land before 35 so its color mocks use this layout |
| Related GitHub issues | none identified in the explorer reports |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | system-surfaces-opus #5 |

## Problem
Compact trailing shows a different abbreviated word for each working phase, duplicating the leading status glyph. The Lock Screen and expanded Island also display a progress fraction invented from status, so a responding → tool → responding sequence moves the rail backward and forward. There is no measured completion percentage behind it.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/widgets/AgentActivity.tsx:148,326–345` shows a static phase glyph while working and words for asks/outcomes. Its comment explicitly favors staying quiet during work. No progress bar claims a fraction of the run is complete.

## Hermex today
- `HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift:37–42` renders `status.compactTitle`. `HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:301–330` maps phases to Start/Think/Tool/Search/Files/Cmd/Reply, asks/outcomes to short words, and waiting to an ellipsis. This property has no other caller.
- `AgentRunIslandCompactMark` (widget L330–344) already renders a tinted status glyph for compact leading and minimal. `AgentRunStatusStyle.symbolName` (L496–526) owns symbols.
- `AgentRunProgressRail` (L369–404) assigns fractions 0.14/0.3/0.52/0.62/0.78/1 to statuses. It appears in the expanded bottom (L69) and Lock Screen activity row (L182).
- `AgentRunElapsedTimerText` (L432–454) uses system `Text(timerInterval:)` with a bounded MM:SS range. It already appears in expanded/Lock Screen views; adding another timer is a choice, not a requirement.
- `AgentRunStaleBotPresentation` (attributes L643–680) preserves pending approval/clarification when stale and labels other stale bot activity disconnected. Do not erase those asks with generic latest-status copy.

## Proposal
Add a small pure compact-presentation policy beside the existing shared stale policy. Use an enum for working, approval, clarification, waiting, complete, failed, cancelled and stale-work, rather than mixing localization with state tests. Resolve words in the view/catalog. Decide finals/asks before the stale-work fallback: a stale approval remains approval; an outcome remains its outcome.

For working states, recommend a **static glyph**, matching the ranked goal. Mocks may offer the existing system timer as an alternative, chosen by the maintainer. Empty trailing content is also permitted by ActivityKit; Apple [documents an empty trailing presentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/activitykit/displaying-live-data-with-live-activities) for limited width. Do not justify a timer using an invented nonempty-content requirement. Keep full-status VoiceOver labels whichever compact treatment is picked.

For asks/outcomes, use short localized words such as Approve/Question/Waiting/Done/Failed/Stopped. Reuse catalog entries when possible. Show Latest only for stale work, consistent with current expanded secondary copy. The compact leading/minimal glyph and tap route keep their existing role.

Remove the fractional rail. Mocks can compare removing it entirely with a static full-width status strip; recommend removal because existing text/glyphs already convey phase. Keep useful elapsed time in the expanded/Lock Screen presentation. Add no app-driven animation; verify Reduce Motion and system-timer rendering without new timers or display-link work.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish distinct compact working treatments (glyph versus elapsed), and rail options (none versus static strip), with the current layout as baseline. Include expanded/Lock Screen, working/ask/final/stale-ask, light/dark, long translation and accessibility examples. Report the URL and **stop for a pick**.
2. Add the exhaustive presentation policy in `AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift`, which is shared by app/widget and available to app tests. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before changing the catalog.
3. Update compact trailing and full accessibility label in the widget. Use the picked working treatment; if timer, reuse `AgentRunElapsedTimerText` rather than scheduling updates.
4. Remove the fractional rail at both callers and its unused theme member. If the static strip was picked, it must not encode a fraction or animate width.
5. Delete unused `compactTitle`. Remove catalog entries only after checking all app/extension readers; common words such as Stopped already exist elsewhere.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** existing `widgetURL` tap routing unchanged.
- **Targets:** widget views, shared attributes/presentation policy, `HermesMobileTests`. Preserve target memberships; no relay or wire-field change.
- **Multi-server/connection modes:** presentation only; no routing or credential changes.
- **Reverse states:** resumed work returns to the picked working presentation; stale asks stay asks; final outcomes stay final.
- **Native quality:** full VoiceOver status, readable localized compact words, Dynamic Type in larger presentations, no added animation; check Reduce Motion.
- **Docs:** no durable architecture change; eventual PR needs before/after images and a short state-transition video.

## Tests
Extend `LiveActivityTests` with one table-driven policy test over all statuses, including stale asks, stale work and final outcomes. Assert enum categories, not exact localized strings or SF Symbol constants. An exhaustive production switch forces a decision when a new status is added.

Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Compact working state uses the picked glyph/timer without clipped phase words.
- [ ] Asks and outcomes have distinct compact presentation and full VoiceOver labels.
- [ ] Staleness never hides pending approval/clarification behind Latest.
- [ ] Neither Lock Screen nor expanded Island claims an invented completion fraction.
- [ ] Existing tap routing and expanded elapsed time remain useful.

## Manual test plan
Use a disposable run on a Dynamic Island iPhone. Observe thinking/tool/responding, then an approval, stale approval after disconnect, reconnect and completion. Long-press and inspect the Lock Screen: no rail moves backward. Check VoiceOver and Reduce Motion. Record the picked treatment and state-transition evidence.

## Out of scope
Adaptive colors/Always-On (#1399), Watch/CarPlay layout (#1400), aggregation (#1416), update frequency (#1371), relay content changes.

## Decisions
Working glyph or elapsed? Recommend the static glyph for calmness. Rail removal or static strip? Recommend removal; the status is already explicit.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the batch's single Branch TestFlight build).

title: fix(live-activity): adapt colors to the host and system material
body:
**What the user gets:** The Live Activity adapts to Always-On, tinted modes, light hosts and iOS 26 glass.
**Why it matters:** Hard-coded dark colours look wrong on the dimmed Lock Screen and iOS 26.
**Cost:** Medium; needs the owner's hands on a physical iPhone.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 35 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | #1398 (these mocks restyle its picked layout) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#607](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/607) (adjacent design foundations), [#5](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/5) (adjacent adaptive glass) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | system-surfaces-opus #3 |

## Problem
The Live Activity supplies a fixed near-black background, white text and saturated phase colors. It has no explicit adaptation for reduced luminance or tinted rendering, and compact views can also appear in a light Mac menu bar. Readability on those hosts needs verification and deliberate styling; hard-coded colors alone do not prove how the system's automatic dimming behaves.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/widgets/AgentActivity.tsx:65–96` uses hierarchical styles in accented/vibrant modes, secondary phase color when luminance is reduced, and light/dark status variants from `colorScheme`. At L244 it calls `activityBackgroundTint(environment.isLiquidGlassAvailable ? "clear" : null)`. That is T3's implementation choice, not a documented native “enable glass” API. `SubscriptionUsage.tsx:43–53` similarly adapts rendering modes.

## Hermex today
In `HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift`:
- L16–17 sets the fixed `AgentRunLiveActivityTheme.background` and action foreground.
- Theme (L456–464) defines white text/strokes/fills, dark background and a green live dot.
- `AgentRunStatusStyle.color` (L466–494) uses fixed RGB values and stale white-alpha.
- Chip fill (L233) and avatar ring (L272) also assume the same dark background.
- No `isLuminanceReduced`, `widgetRenderingMode`, `colorScheme` or `showsWidgetContainerBackground` appears in the **widget target's directory**. The app itself already uses colorScheme extensively.

The deployment target is iOS 18 (`HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`). `activityBackgroundTint` predates iOS 26; the version check here selects a design policy. Apple [documents nil as system default material](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/activitybackgroundtint(_:)); clear is a custom transparent tint, not a guaranteed Liquid Glass switch. Apple [shows compact views on macOS 26's menu bar](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/278/), so “Island means black background everywhere” is unsafe.

## Proposal
Keep one widget-local `AgentRunPalette`, supplied to existing views. Read `isLuminanceReduced`, `widgetRenderingMode` and `colorScheme` in actual View wrappers, not configuration builder closures. Keep symbols in `AgentRunStatusStyle`; replace scattered theme/color reads with palette values.

Apply rules in order:
1. Reduced luminance: mute status/live-dot decoration to a secondary treatment. Text/glyphs still identify status; avoid extra app timers or animation.
2. Accented/vibrant mode: use hierarchical foreground styles and appropriate `widgetAccentable()` grouping. Do not assume Watch/StandBy always produces a particular environment value; honor the values delivered.
3. Normal full color: choose text/status contrast against the **actual background**. An explicitly dark fallback card retains white/white-alpha text even if colorScheme is light. System-material cards and compact host views use colorScheme with darker status variants on light hosts. A blanket `onIsland = true` bypass would break Mac menu-bar contrast.

On iOS 26+, request system default with `.activityBackgroundTint(nil)` and default action foreground; keep inner chip/pill fills subtle. On iOS 18–25, retain today's explicit dark card/action foreground. No new glass effect or glass shader is needed. Verify actual material, bright wallpaper contrast, Increased Contrast and Reduce Transparency on device. Record the OS build and result rather than promising that nil or clear necessarily produces a particular glass appearance.

Palette inputs must distinguish a deliberately dark card from system-material/compact surfaces. In particular, do not choose black “light-host” text for an iOS 18 card whose background remains near-black. Shared compact builders must adapt when mirrored to Mac while retaining normal iPhone Island contrast.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish distinct treatments of 34's picked layout: system-material card on bright/dark wallpaper, reduced luminance, monochrome mode, light compact Mac host and dark iOS 18 fallback. Include asks/failure/stale states. Report the URL and **stop for a pick**; label simulated material fidelity honestly.
2. Add the palette to `AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift`. Pass it through Lock Screen, chip, leading mark, timer pill, status dot and Island views. Leave shared attributes/wire content alone.
3. Put environment reads and background/action modifiers in content View wrappers. Gate only the iOS 26 design choice. Replace raw theme colors, including the live dot and avatar outline; retain status symbols.
4. Verify device rendering and capture before/after evidence: Always-On photo, bright/dark wallpaper and Mac compact rendering if available. Do not make unavailable Mac hardware a reason to claim verification.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points/multi-server/connection modes:** presentation only; existing tap URLs and server scope unchanged.
- **Targets:** widget only; no relay/ContentState changes. 36 reuses this palette in its small layout.
- **Reverse states:** restoring luminance/rendering mode restores the appropriate full-color palette without stale style state.
- **Native quality:** light/dark, VoiceOver labels, Dynamic Type, Increased Contrast, Reduce Transparency/Reduce Motion; no new strings or animation.
- **Docs:** eventual PR records observed hosts/material and captures; no architecture doc needed.

## Tests
No unit tests for RGB constants or screenshots. Build the widget and app as part of the integrated signed Debug pass; exercise the state-to-color rules manually in actual hosts. If a meaningful style-category policy is extracted, test those categories at an existing supported test boundary without adding a widget test target solely for constants.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] iOS 26 card requests system material and remains readable on bright/dark wallpaper; actual appearance/OS build is recorded.
- [ ] iOS 18 fallback retains readable white-on-dark normal appearance, even with a light system color scheme.
- [ ] Reduced luminance and accented/vibrant modes use the chosen muted/hierarchical treatment for all decoration.
- [ ] Mac compact views respect a light host; normal iPhone Island layout/contrast follows 34.
- [ ] Color choices are centralized; no repainting animation, extra timer or wire change is added.

## Manual test plan
Run a disposable turn on an Always-On-capable iPhone (for example iPhone 14 Pro; not every later model supports it). Check bright/dark wallpaper, screen dimming, Increased Contrast and Reduce Transparency. Check StandBy night tint and macOS 26 Live Activities where available. On iOS 18 simulator, verify dark fallback in both system appearances. Record unsupported/unavailable hosts explicitly.

## Out of scope
Layout redesign (#1398), small family (#1400), Home Screen widgets (#1409), per-server colors, custom glass rendering.

## Decisions
Add a status-tinted material wash? Recommend no; let the glyph carry status and choose contrast from the bright-wallpaper mock/device evidence.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the batch's single Branch TestFlight build).

title: feat(live-activity): add a small Watch and CarPlay layout
body:
**What the user gets:** Live Activity gets a small layout for the Apple Watch Smart Stack and CarPlay.
**Why it matters:** Approvals reach the wrist without a Watch app; a cheap step toward #575 and #1277.
**Cost:** Small; needs the owner's hands on a physical iPhone and Apple Watch.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 36 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | #1398 (ask/stale policy), #1399 (palette) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#575](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/575) (adjacent Watch companion; comments suggest Live Activities as a cheaper step), [#1277](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1277) (separate Watch-app proposal awaiting a decision) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | system-surfaces-opus #4 |

## Problem
Hermex supplies no dedicated small-family Live Activity. Apple Watch receives a system fallback; CarPlay uses compact leading/trailing Island views by default. A small layout can show the useful title and full attention state without shrinking the dense Lock Screen layout into a tile.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/widgets/AgentActivity.tsx:288` returns `bannerSmall` alongside `banner`, with logo, attention summary and top run title/status. The explorer inferred the expo-widgets → ActivityFamily.small mapping from naming; generated Swift was not inspected, so do not treat that mapping as verified native API evidence.

## Hermex today
- `HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift:14–18` always builds `AgentRunLockScreenView`; the configuration has no supplemental-family declaration. The repo has no `activityFamily` reader.
- Lock Screen content (L92–218) includes header/mark/title/timer, activity row and chips/transcript. Do not reuse it unchanged for small surfaces.
- Full status titles live in `HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:270–299`; `AgentRunStaleBotPresentation` (L647–680) preserves stale asks. The existing state already has `sessionTitle`; bot activity starts/updates it from the bot's display title (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1482,1539,1551`). `AgentRunActivityBot` itself has no display-name field, and none is needed.
- All relevant targets deploy to iOS 18 (`project.pbxproj`). The installed iPhoneOS SDK `WidgetKit.swiftinterface` declares both `supplementalActivityFamilies` and `EnvironmentValues.activityFamily` at **iOS 18.0**, so no gate is required. CarPlay Live Activities themselves require iOS 26.
- Apple documents the [small-family layout](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/activitykit/creating-custom-views-for-live-activities) and [CarPlay defaults/Mac mirroring](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/278/). No watchOS app target is required for phone Live Activity mirroring.

## Proposal
Add `.supplementalActivityFamilies([.small])` to the `ActivityConfiguration`. Put an `AgentRunActivityContent` View in its content closure, reading `@Environment(\.activityFamily)`. Render a new private `AgentRunSmallView` for small; preserve the picked Lock Screen view for medium and unknown future families. Read the environment in the View, not as a property wrapper inside a builder closure.

The recommended small view has two lines:
- Status glyph plus `presentedState.sessionTitle`, one line/truncated. This already identifies the bot for bot activity.
- Full localized ask/outcome title, or the existing bounded system elapsed timer while working. Stale asks remain asks, final outcomes remain outcomes, and stale work gets latest-status/disconnected wording from the shared policy. Do not substitute 34's compact abbreviations for full small-family text.

Leave out excerpt, rail, chips, photos and pill chrome. Reuse 35's palette, honoring actual luminance/rendering mode/color scheme rather than assuming Watch always uses vibrant/accented mode. Do not add animations or timers.

Retain `widgetURL` on the activity content. Actual Watch/CarPlay tap behavior is system-controlled; verify it instead of promising a Watch tap opens the iPhone. The small card must stand alone without a tap, especially in CarPlay.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish distinct two-line versus status-first small layouts, with working/approval/stale-approval/final states, light/dark, long titles and accessibility sizes. Report the URL and **stop for a pick**.
2. Add the supplemental-family modifier and `AgentRunActivityContent` selector in `AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift`.
3. Add the chosen small view, reusing full status titles, shared stale policy, timer and palette. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before any new String Catalog entry; do not add a display-name wire field.
4. Verify on paired Watch (watchOS 11+) and a supported CarPlay Simulator setup with iOS 26+. Follow Apple's simulator setup rather than assuming an external-display window exercises the actual small family. Attach evidence to the eventual PR.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** existing widget URL remains; record actual Watch tap behavior, treat CarPlay as glanceable display.
- **Targets:** widget only, no app/relay/ContentState/watchOS target change. Full title/stale policy are already shared.
- **Multi-server:** existing activity routing remains scoped; never derive identity from a displayed title.
- **Reverse states:** stale asks, reconnect and final outcome presentations; dismissal policy unchanged.
- **Connection modes:** ActivityKit mirrors app- or relay-driven updates through the phone; no separate Watch networking.
- **Native quality:** combined VoiceOver label with full status/title, no new animation, readable large text and contrast. Strings come from catalog/shared policy.
- **Docs:** add supported surfaces to `docs/agents/push.md` if its surface list needs updating.

## Tests
No tests for layout constants. Reuse 34's `LiveActivityTests` coverage of stale/ask/outcome policy; add a policy test only if small introduces a distinct state decision. Build all existing targets in the integrated signed Debug pass; device/simulator evidence proves family selection. Do not create a new test target solely for this layout.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Watch Smart Stack shows the picked small layout with readable title and full approval state.
- [ ] iOS 26+ CarPlay shows small content, not compact Island abbreviations.
- [ ] Stale asks remain visible; work and final outcomes use the chosen second-line treatment.
- [ ] iPhone medium/Island layouts, tap URLs and relay payloads remain valid.

## Manual test plan
Use a disposable run on an iPhone paired with watchOS 11+. Inspect Smart Stack during work, approval, disconnect/reconnect and completion; record what tapping does. Repeat using supported CarPlay Simulator with iOS 26+. Compare phone Lock Screen/Island before and after. Record unavailable hardware explicitly instead of claiming evidence.

## Out of scope
Watch app/Watch-side approvals (#575/#1277), aggregation (#1416), interactive small-view buttons, new server support.

## Decisions
Which title on small? Recommend existing `sessionTitle`: bot activity already fills it with the bot display title, avoiding another wire field and preserving ordinary session titles.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the batch's single Branch TestFlight build).

title: fix(share): explain which shared items were left out
body:
**What the user gets:** Shares explain which items were left out and why.
**Why it matters:** Oversized or unreadable shared items are dropped silently today.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 37 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1241](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1241) (separate share-navigation bug), [#1196](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1196) (existing whole-import failure recovery), [#1197](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1197) (preserve occurrence identity) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | system-surfaces-sol #3 |

## Problem
Sharing a small PDF and an oversized file can open a composer containing only the PDF, without explaining the omission. Unsupported/unreadable items and files over the ten-attachment limit also disappear. If nothing survives, a generic message shows for only 0.8 seconds before the extension closes.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/sharing/incoming-share-model.ts:230–423` accumulates reasons while retaining usable items and persists warnings with the draft. `IncomingShareProvider.tsx:320–335` distinguishes skipped content from a failed import, offering recovery for the latter.

## Hermex today
- `HermesShareExtension/ShareInputReader.swift:21–38` loads text/URLs, then attempts attachments only until ten succeeded. `ShareInput` (L4–8) carries no omissions.
- Attachment helpers silently return nil for file read failure (L125), unsupported data providers (L129–131), oversized mapped files (L137–138), and absent/oversized data (L144–146). Raw data accepts image/PDF only (L219–224); file-URL providers can supply other files.
- `HermesShareDraft.maximumSharedAttachmentBytes/Count` (`HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:97–98`) are 20 MiB and ten. `normalizedImport` (L338–354) also filters empty/oversized data and truncates count; `loadAttachments` (L565–575) silently omits unreadable staged files.
- `ShareViewController.saveDraftAndOpenHermes` (`HermesShareExtension/ShareViewController.swift:46–71`) gives feedback only when nothing survives, then auto-dismisses. Extension UI uses English literals by convention (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).
- Payload/import types (SharedDraftStore L4–53) hold only accepted content. `contentID` (L631–642) hashes that content; `enqueue` (L376–385) deduplicates pending copies; reservation `occurrenceID` (L63–66) makes later intentional shares distinct.
- Webui routes through `SessionListView.openPendingSharedImportIfNeeded` (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:1450–1468`). Hermes `SharedImportReservation.moveIntoDraft` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:857–891`) remains all-or-nothing, with `HermesShareFailure` for rejection (L897).

## Proposal
Add Foundation-only `SharedSkippedItem` with optional suggested filename and reason (tooLarge, unreadable, unsupported, overLimit). Optional enum synthesis alone does **not** tolerate an unknown raw value: decode explicitly to nil/unknown, or store a raw string. Persist optional skipped records plus `additionalSkippedCount` in `SharedDraftPayload` and hydrate them in `SharedImport`. Cap detail at 20 records; count the rest without loading omitted files.

Return a small loaded/skipped/not-an-attachment result from reader helpers. Try existing file/data fallbacks before recording one failure per provider; a provider with a failed file representation and a working data representation was not skipped. Plain URL/text providers must not generate unsupported-file warnings. Once attachment count is full, inspect advertised types only to count later attachment providers.

Preserve accepted-content hashing, pending dedupe and occurrence identity. Old payloads decode with no warnings. Propagate warnings through normalization/load too: empty/unreadable data is unreadable, oversize is tooLarge, truncation is overLimit. A missing staged file produces an unreadable warning rather than silently disappearing. Do not turn this into partial Hermes transfer: app-side upload admission still succeeds or fails as a whole.

When some content survives, carry the bounded summary into the **visible destination composer**, not a toast on the home covered by navigation/sheets. Reuse `ActionToast` (`HermesMobile/Features/Shared/ActionToast.swift`), which supports VoiceOver persistence and Reduce Motion. Bind presentation to the reservation occurrence so retries do not repeat it. Example: “1 item wasn't added: big.mov is over 20 MB.” A whole-import `HermesShareFailure` takes precedence.

If nothing survives, show a specific reason with a single Done action, persisting until acknowledged. The current 0.8-second dismissal is insufficient for readable/VoiceOver feedback. No retry editor is needed. Keep localization and plural formatting in an **app-only** formatter; the shared store compiles in the English-only extension too.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish toast-versus-inline composer mocks for one/many/over-limit skips, plus the extension's all-skipped Done state, light/dark and AX5. Report the URL and **stop for a pick**.
2. Extend `SharedDraftStore.swift` payload/import, enqueue, normalization and load paths with optional bounded warning metadata. Preserve all existing identity rules and target memberships.
3. Refactor `ShareInputReader` and pass warnings through `ShareViewController.savePendingImport`; add the acknowledged all-skipped state.
4. Carry warnings through `PendingNewChatRoute`/`PendingNewChatView` and Hermes transfer/session destination. Present only after successful acceptance and while that occurrence's composer is visible.
5. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md`; add app-only summary/plurals and retain English extension UI.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** share extension → Hermes/webui composer; the fix is trivially shared for webui.
- **Targets:** shared Foundation model in app/extension, extension reader/controller, app notice, tests. Widget/notification service n/a.
- **Multi-server:** warnings belong to the reservation and destination, never another active server after a switch.
- **Reverse states:** dismiss notice/Done; consuming the import removes staged metadata. Failed transfer retains its recovery path.
- **Connection modes:** local parsing only.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver announcement, Dynamic Type, light/dark, app catalog plurals, verbatim bounded filenames, Reduce Motion.

## Tests
- `ShareInputReaderTests`: mixed small/oversized providers, twelve valid providers, and a failed representation with successful fallback produce accurate omissions without duplicates.
- `SharedDraftStoreTests`: warnings/overflow survive reserve/load; unknown future reason preserves accepted content; differing warnings do not alter content dedupe; unreadable staged files are reported.
- A routing/presentation assertion must show the notice is passed to the destination composer, not merely stored.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ShareInputReaderTests --only HermesMobileTests/SharedDraftStoreTests` plus the destination test class added for the chosen presentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Mixed accepted/skipped content opens the composer with an accurate visible summary.
- [ ] Twelve photos yield ten attachments and two count-limit omissions.
- [ ] All-skipped feedback remains until Done, including with VoiceOver.
- [ ] Old queued shares, pending dedupe and occurrence replay behavior remain valid.
- [ ] Whole Hermes transfer failures retain existing recovery rather than losing content.

## Manual test plan
On disposable test destinations, share a small PDF with a file over 20 MiB, then twelve photos. Inspect composer notice/attachments on Hermes and webui. Share only the oversized file; check the acknowledged extension error with VoiceOver. Repeat while a chat already covers the home so the notice must reach the new visible composer.

## Out of scope
#1241's lifecycle repair, higher limits, partial Hermes transfers, destination picker (#1421), extension-wide localization.

## Decisions
Toast or inline banner? Recommend the existing toast hosted in the destination composer; the mock decides its visibility/readability. Both options need occurrence-scoped metadata through routing.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: bundled into the batch's merge-walk test session.

title: feat(intents): prefill a new chat with content from Shortcuts
body:
**What the user gets:** Shortcuts can open a new chat prefilled with text (never auto-sent).
**Why it matters:** Implements #311 with a prompt-injection-aware handoff.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.
