> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 38 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none added; existing new-chat routing validates the live destination before opening |
| Depends on | none; preserve 37's optional skipped-item metadata if already present |
| Related GitHub issues | [#311](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/311) (implements review-before-send text slice; read body/comments), [#275](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/275) (saved prompts, separate), [#1180](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1180) (existing server-scoped Hermes Profile entities), [#1241](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1241) (adjacent share-navigation lifecycle; preserve ownership guards) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | composer-opus #4, composer-sol #6; #311 source-triage comment |

## Problem
Shortcuts cannot prefill composer content. Add review-before-send text handoff that preserves drafts, concurrent invocations and server ownership.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/prompt-links/threadPromptLink.ts` consumes prefill once and drops stale handoffs. `packages/shared/src/promptLinks.ts` scans hidden characters; `prompt-link-model.ts` supplies provenance; `prompt-link-actions.ts` waits for hydration and asks before replacement. Shortcut text must instead use app-owned storage.

## Hermex today
- `HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift:33–95` defines New Chat, Voice and Profile intents. `AppIntentRouter.pendingDeepLink` (L12–28) is one in-memory URL slot: navigation signaling, not durable content storage.
- `HermesNewChatDestination` (L139–208) already binds a Hermes server/Profile and waits for sign-in/live list state. `ProfileEntity.hermesNewChat` (`HermesMobile/AppIntents/ProfileEntity.swift:45–50`) resolves `<server URL>|<profile>`. Webui entity IDs remain bare names, so they cannot establish a selected entity's original server.
- `SharedDraftStore.swift` (`HermesMobile/Features/Share/`) already provides protected app-group files, atomic enqueue (L370–435), reservations and occurrence IDs (L55–66). Pending identical content deduplicates (L376–385). It does not yet provide per-Shortcut operation identity or immutable destination metadata.
- `normalizedImport` (L338–354), `loadImport` (L547) and `composerDraft` (L133–139) trim or alter text. Reusing those unchanged would violate #311's exact-text requirement.
- Hermes shares transfer into a server/connection/target draft (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:844–890`), using `ChatDraftStore.appendShare` (`HermesMobile/Persistence/ChatDraftStore.swift:739–785`) for idempotent append. The current share route picks the active server/default Profile.
- #311 explicitly recommends durable inbox transport and crash-safe consume. #1180 resolved its older Hermes entity-identity concern, but not the single-slot transport risk.

## Proposal
Add one **New Chat with Content** App Intent: required `String` Content and optional Hermes `ProfileEntity`, `openAppWhenRun = true`. Bind the chosen Hermes entity's server/Profile; otherwise bind the active configured Hermes server and resolve its default when live. Reject bare webui entities for this new action; leave existing intents unchanged.

Extend the existing share inbox with optional source (`shortcut`), operation UUID, immutable server/Profile destination and original text. Store server identity with the protected payload; only an opaque operation ID may enter the navigation URL. Ordinary share records keep their existing normalization and content dedupe. Shortcut records key enqueue/reserve/consume by operation ID, so identical invocations remain distinct and ordered. Preserve original text through every save/load/hydration step; trimmed text is used only to reject blanks.

Publish durably before signaling navigation. Enforce 100 KiB UTF-8 per invocation, at most 10 pending Shortcut records and a 24-hour pending lifetime. Reuse reservation ownership/release/recovery. Deliver one record at a time. Keep later Shortcut records queued while that composer is presented; offer explicit Open Next/Discard using existing inbox concepts, rather than automatically replacing its view. A second invocation cannot overwrite the first. Storage failure throws an intent error. Later removed-server/deleted-Profile failure offers recovery/discard in-app, without fallback or retroactive intent errors.

Extend `SharedImportGate`/`ContentView` routing to validate the payload's bound destination before claim/transfer. Wait through sign-in/server switching using existing routing rules; recheck reservation and destination after every await. Append once under the operation identity only after draft hydration, then consume after durable acceptance. Preserve existing draft text/attachments/settings. Bypass `composerDraft` and `appendShare`'s trimming of earlier draft newlines for this source; ordinary shares retain their normalization.

A draft-scoped dismissible notice says it was added from Shortcuts and should be reviewed. A pure scalar scanner counts bidi embeddings/overrides/isolates, U+200B/U+2060/U+FEFF, and Unicode tag scalars. Do not flag ZWJ/ZWNJ or LRM/RLM. Hidden characters produce a stronger warning. Keep source bytes unchanged by default; a user-selected Remove Hidden Characters action strips only flagged scalars and participates in the editor's Undo. Persist optional notice metadata with the draft; clear it on send/dismiss. Unknown source/reason values must decode safely without authorizing a route.

## Implementation steps
1. Use `html-communication` to publish distinct inline/chip provenance mocks plus hidden-character, pending-next and unavailable-destination states, light/dark, AX5 and RTL. Report the URL and **stop for a pick**.
2. Extend `SharedDraftPayload`/`SharedImport` in `SharedDraftStore.swift` with optional Shortcut metadata, separate operation identity, exact-text handling and bounds. Preserve 37's fields and ordinary share compatibility.
3. Add the intent and App Shortcut registration in `HermexAppIntents.swift`. Persist first, then request opaque navigation; no `pendingPrefill` content singleton.
4. Extend `SharedImportGate`, `ContentView` and Hermes new-chat/share transfer to honor immutable destination and reservation ownership. Keep consume after draft acceptance and the next Shortcut queued until explicit navigation releases the current composer.
5. Add the scanner, app-only notice and draft persistence metadata in `ChatDraftStore` and its persisted payload. Wire Undo through the editor if Remove is chosen. Read `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` and `docs/agents/i18n.md` before these changes.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** Shortcuts/Siri/Action button through the new intent; ordinary links and share sheet retain their existing behavior.
- **Targets:** app/tests; `SharedDraftStore.swift` also compiles in the share extension, so its optional metadata must remain Foundation-only and backward-compatible. Widget/notification service n/a.
- **Multi-server:** immutable destination, no fallback for removed servers/Profiles, no text in URL/logs. Locked/sign-out state waits safely.
- **Reverse states:** discard unavailable handoff, edit/remove text, dismiss notice, undo explicit sanitization.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver notice, Dynamic Type, RTL and catalog localization; no added animation.

## Tests
- `SharedDraftStoreTests`: exact text including leading/trailing whitespace survives publication/reservation/recovery; two identical invocations remain ordered and distinct; stale reservation cannot consume its successor; byte/count/expiry limits use injected time.
- `AppIntentNewChatTests`: chosen server/Profile survives switching/sign-in; removed destination does not fall back; blank/oversized input publishes nothing. Include production routing/acceptance coverage, not just the request struct.
- `ChatDraftStoreTests`: accepted operation survives relaunch and replay without duplicate append or loss of existing draft state.
- `PromptProvenanceTests` (new): flagged scalars are detected/removed while emoji ZWJ, Persian ZWNJ and Hebrew RLM survive.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SharedDraftStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/AppIntentNewChatTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatDraftStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/PromptProvenanceTests`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Warm/cold Shortcut runs prefill exact text for review and send nothing.
- [ ] Identical concurrent invocations survive relaunch/reservation replay as distinct ordered operations.
- [ ] Destination switches/auth waits cannot deliver text to another server; unavailable destinations are recoverable.
- [ ] Existing draft content/settings/attachments survive; one operation appends once.
- [ ] Text never enters URLs/logs; ordinary share dedupe and existing intents still work.
- [ ] Provenance and hidden-character handling match the picked mock; RTL/emoji remain intact.

## Manual test plan
On two disposable test configurations, run clipboard → New Chat with Content warm/cold and twice concurrently with identical text. Choose an inactive-server Profile and wait through sign-in/relaunch. Verify destination, draft preservation, no sends, hidden-character removal/Undo and unavailable-destination recovery; leave daily-driver servers intact.

## Out of scope
Auto-send, files/typed URL inputs, saved prompts, general queue framework and public `?prompt=` links (separately selected follow-up).

## Decisions
Public prompt links now? Recommend deferring them; Shortcuts avoids URL-history exposure. Later links can reuse durable acceptance with separate provenance mocks.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: perf(bots): show the cached roster while the inbox connects
body:
**What the user gets:** The Bots inbox shows its last roster instantly while it connects.
**Why it matters:** Over a tunnel the inbox is grey for 1–2 s on every open.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 1 (#1359) · order 39 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing gateway `profiles.list`, unchanged; verified at pin below |
| Depends on | none; 10 supplies connection status over populated rows |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1180](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1180) (names-only Profile cache for Shortcuts), [#1144](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1144) (Bot Chat transcript cache) |
| Needs mock first | no (same existing rows and connection states; changes paint timing) |
| Sources | connection-state-opus #2 |

## Problem
On cold start/server switching, Bots shows skeletons until sign-in, socket handshake and the roster read finish. A bounded local copy could display the last roster during this wait, while preserving live validation for server writes. It must not turn an old preview into a claim that a bot is currently working.

## What T3 does
`packages/client-runtime/src/state/shell.ts:42,84–106` loads a cached environment shell before opening the socket, moving from cached through synchronizing to live. `apps/mobile/src/connection/environment-cache-store.ts` supplies local storage. The authoritative snapshot still replaces it on connection rather than trusting a cursor to imply a complete cache.

## Hermex today
- Hermes Sessions already calls `showCachedHermesSessions(provisional: true)` in `SessionListViewModel.openHermes`; no change needed there.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:332–380`: `open` clears Profiles when the saved connection ID changes (L337–340), restores seen/room flags/section order (L350–352), then connects (L358–367). `reload` applies `profiles.list` rows after wire/serial guards (L580–590), deduplicating Profile IDs.
- `isLoadingRoster` (L453–455) selects skeletons while empty/connecting. `BotsInboxView.swift:158–166` renders them. A dropped connection keeps rows and clears live status (`BotInbox.drop`, L854–858); stale rows already support ordinary navigation.
- `mayEdit` (L457) gates server edits on live; the New chat menu is disabled when not live (`BotsInboxView.swift:269`). Local Show Hidden/section-order preferences have different gates and must retain them.
- `BotProfile.init?` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotConnection.swift:226–244`) requires `name` and tolerantly reads display/organization/preview fields.
- `BotHistoryCache.Scope` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotHistoryCache.swift:9–19`) keys by SHA-256 server URL plus connection UUID. `BotAvatarStore.swift:4–8` explicitly stores decoded photos **in memory only**; it cannot supply photos after a cold launch.
- Verified via read-only `gh api repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/contents/apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json?ref=ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`: `profiles.list`, `ProfilesListParams.include_sessions`, `ProfilesListResult.profiles`, and `ProfileRow` including `canonical_session`, `ui_meta`, `ui_meta_revisions` and `has_avatar`. No new endpoint/shape is required; the local newer upstream checkout was not used.

## Proposal
Add an injected actor `BotRosterCache`, reusing `BotHistoryCache.Scope`, with load/save/remove-server/remove-scope operations. Store last raw roster rows in `Caches/BotRoster/<serverKey>-<connectionID>.json`, main-app container only, using atomic writes with complete-until-first-unlock protection. Limit to 200 rows and 2 MiB encoded bytes; check read size before decoding. Oversized/corrupt/unavailable data is a cache miss, never a connection failure.

Load off-main during `open`, after resolving the saved connection and before `connect`, only when no current roster remains. Recheck the open generation, server and saved connection after the await; old loads must not overwrite another connection or a live reload. Parse through `BotProfile.init`, applying the same ID dedupe as live. Do not mark previews seen or synthesize live status simply because they were loaded.

Use existing generated faces/placeholders on cold launch. Reuse `avatarStore.images(connectionID:)` only if already present in this process; do not add photo persistence.

Save after a successful guarded `reload`, capturing that request's scope rather than reading a later `self.connection`. Serialize storage writes/removals and invalidate older writers at removal so a delayed save cannot recreate signed-out data. Cache I/O failure must not turn a successful roster read into disconnect. The first live roster replaces cached rows wholesale, preserving stable `BotProfile.id` identity; deleted bots disappear and added bots arrive.

Keep `liveStatuses` empty while showing a cached roster. Server mutations remain disabled until live. Row taps retain existing cached-transcript/reconnect behavior; deep links keep `BotDeepLink.swift:136`'s live gate. Rooms/capabilities are not cached here.

## Implementation steps
1. Read `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`. Add `BotRosterCache` near `BotHistoryCache`, with injected directory, byte bounds and removal/write ownership.
2. Inject it in `BotInbox.init` (L241); load in `open` and save in `reload` with the guards above. Handle an authoritative empty roster as a replacement too.
3. Add server cleanup alongside `BotHistoryCache` in `AuthManager.swift:512,525,543`; add scope cleanup to the connection discard closure (`BotConnectionView.swift:386–393`), which handles removal/replacement. Review `AuthManager.removeBotConnection` (L646–654) so every credential-removal path invalidates pending cache writers.
4. Add the cache/cleanup row to the isolation document. Do not change existing local preference gates or add a new offline UI.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** Hermes Bots home and the existing webui Bot connection share `BotInbox`; this cache fix is trivially shared. iPad uses the same model. Deep links retain live validation.
- **Targets:** app/tests; no extension access.
- **Multi-server:** server digest plus connection UUID; late loads/writes cannot survive ownership changes; removal clears the relevant scope.
- **Reverse states:** live replacement removes obsolete cached bots; sign-out/removal clears cache.
- **Connection modes:** tunnel delay/offline startup show rows without live status; 10 owns header copy.
- **Native quality:** existing row accessibility/Dynamic Type and stable IDs; no new animation or strings.

## Tests
`BotInboxTests`, with an injected temporary cache and controlled transport:
1. Cached rows paint while connect is suspended, with no skeleton/live status or permission to edit.
2. A deferred load for A returning after switch to B cannot paint A; removal during a pending write cannot recreate A's cache.
3. Authoritative live replacement, including empty, removes stale rows; corrupt cache falls back to connection.

Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests`. Use expectations/gates, not sleeps.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Cold startup paints a valid nonempty cached roster before live connect.
- [ ] Server edits/New chat remain disabled; cached rows never claim Working.
- [ ] Live empty/nonempty rosters replace the copy, preserving stable row identity.
- [ ] Two servers/connections never mix rows; sign-out/removal wins over late I/O.
- [ ] Cache failure never blocks normal connection; cold-launch photos are not promised.

## Manual test plan
Use two disposable test configurations. Load Bots, terminate/relaunch through the normal app workflow, and compare delayed connection with airplane mode. Check cached rows, placeholders and disabled server edits. Change the test roster on the disposable host, reconnect, and confirm authoritative replacement. Switch servers and sign out of the test connection; stale rows must not reappear. Do not delete a daily-driver bot for evidence.

## Out of scope
Room/live-status/photo caches, Sessions caching, reconnect-header design (#1374), changing mutation policy, background refresh.

## Decisions
Disable cached row taps? Recommend retaining today's post-disconnect navigation: the chat can show cached history and attempt reconnect independently.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: test: share observation waits and flag sleep-based test ordering in CI
body:
**What the user gets:** Tests stop relying on sleeps and polling; one shared wait helper.
**Why it matters:** Flaky CI runs slow merge walks; the rule exists in AGENTS.md but isn't enforced.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 1 (#1359) · order 40 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | engineering |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | adjacent, not fixed here: [#1170](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1170), [#1018](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1018), [#1207](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1207), [#1219](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1219), [#1263](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1263). The last already has explicit ordering at `HermesSlashCommandTests.swift:335–336`; closing it requires separate verification |
| Needs mock first | no |
| Sources | performance-eng-opus #4; performance-eng-sol “considered and rejected” |

## Problem
`CLAUDE.md` § Verifying requires expectations/scripted fixtures rather than sleeps or polling. The suite has seven sleep/deadline-poll sites plus eight unbounded yield-poll loops used for ordering. Separately, observation-based `waitUntil` has 16 definitions across 15 files, making useful fixes easy to miss.

## What T3 does
`docs/internals/testing.md` describes event-driven waiting; its lint rules flag wall-clock waits and polling in tests. Exceptions carry a reason. Adopt a small source check rather than a Swift lint dependency or a broad flake-cleanup project.

## Hermex today
Verified at master `5125b512`:

| Where under `HermesMobileTests/` | Pattern |
|---|---|
| `KanbanLiveUpdateTests.swift:630` | 20 ms sleep after visibility handoff |
| `KanbanLiveUpdateTests.swift:925–935` | Date deadline loop with 5 ms sleeps |
| `KanbanCardDetailStateTests.swift:217–228` | clock deadline loop with Task.yield |
| `KanbanFeatureStateTests.swift:1549–1560` | same busy-spin wait |
| `KanbanCardEditorStateTests.swift:318–329` | same busy-spin wait |
| `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests.swift:701` | 20 ms sleep to wait out an older toast dismissal |
| `FileBrowserViewModelTests.swift:280` | Thread.sleep in a slow response stub |

These are **seven sites in six files**, not an exhaustive polling inventory. Eight more unbounded `while … == nil { await Task.yield() }` loops exist: `KanbanFeatureStateTests.swift:1721,1760,1843,2024,2116,2140`, `InsightsViewModelTests.swift:556–558`, and `CliSessionsSyncModelTests.swift:215`. Replace them with started-request expectations/continuations signaled where the held operation registers. Together this is 15 sites across eight files; isolated yield calls are not automatically polling. The observation helper has **16 definitions in 15 files**: `HermesSessionListTests.swift` has two (L724/L1061); `HermesChatTurnTests.swift:1351` omits file/line arguments. Examples: `ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:9221`, `StreamReconnectContractTests.swift:459`. They suspend through `withObservationTracking`/`XCTWaiter`, with a five-second failure bound reset after changes; success does not depend on elapsed time. `KanbanLiveUpdateTests.until` (L906–916) is a similar helper with a deliberate ten-second failure bound; keep that bound if sharing its implementation.

Legitimate timer seams/stubs also exist: cancellable hang stubs (`APIClientTests.swift:180`, `ChatStreamCoordinatorTests.swift:585`, `ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:9477`), factory defaults (`HermesConversationTests.swift:374,385`; `ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:9154–9161`), and scripted delays (`SSEClientTests.swift:717`, `ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests.swift:191`). Annotate intentional real delays; they are not permission to use a sleep before asserting.

There is also an unused 50 ms fallback in `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests.swift:261`; all six callers pass manual ticks (L18–176). Remove the optional fallback and require that existing injected tick. This is not an eighth exercised sleep-then-assert behavior, but it would trip the new check.

`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:210–223` runs Linux Tooling Tests, including `python3 -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_*.py'`. New Swift files need explicit Xcode test-target membership.

## Proposal
Add `HermesMobileTests/Support/ObservationWait.swift`: one `@MainActor waitUntil` with call-site file/line defaults and an optional failure bound (default five seconds). Preserve observation semantics; it must not attempt to observe async actor counters. Remove all 16 duplicate definitions; the ten-second `until` can stay a forwarding helper or use the explicit bound.

Replace ordering waits with the nearest real signal:

- All deadline/yield polling helpers: observe actual `@Observable` state; for actor call counts, have the double fulfill an expectation or resume a continuation when the call occurs. Weak deallocation checks also need completion/lifetime signals, not observation of a non-observable weak local.
- Visibility handoff at L630: `KanbanStreamSpy.emit` calls the captured callback synchronously (L963–966), and the production generation guard rejects a hidden stream before scheduling reconciliation (`KanbanFeatureState.swift:2593`). Assert immediately after the callback; waiting for the already-recorded `stopCount` would add no evidence. If the callback path changes, expose a processed-event signal rather than sleeping.
- Toast race: inject the dismiss sleep in `GitActionToastState` (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitActionToastOverlay.swift:19–51`), following `ActionToastStateTests`' manually resumed double. Explicitly release the stale dismissal and await its return before asserting the newer toast survived. If 46 already unified these types, use its existing seam.
- Slow listing: replace Thread.sleep with a gated asynchronous response double. Release it after the newer listing lands, then await the older load. Do not block the URLProtocol callback queue with a semaphore: that can prevent the newer request from running.

Add standard-library Python `ci/check_test_waits.py` scanning `HermesMobileTests/**/*.swift`. Flag direct `Task.sleep`, `Thread.sleep`, `usleep`, `RunLoop.main/current.run(until:)` and the known deadline-loop forms (`while Date() < …`, `while clock.now < …`, including dotted clock expressions), plus `while` bodies that repeatedly await `Task.yield()` instead of suspending on a signal. Exempt only an adjacent `// test-wait: <nonempty reason>` annotation. Annotate real cancellation stubs, default seams and scripted delays individually after checking callers. No arbitrary “under 10 seconds” cutoff, blanket helper exclusion or fragile function-signature parser.

This guards known patterns, not all possible polling. Mask comments/literals and cover multiline loops/file-line diagnostics. Parked continuations need no annotation. Add one Linux Tooling Tests step; no extra macOS job.

## Implementation steps
1. Add the shared helper and test-target membership, then remove the 16 definitions and fix call labels. Preserve the deliberate ten-second Kanban bound.
2. Replace the 15 identified ordering sites and unused reveal-tick fallback as above. Keep each change tied to the behavior its test verifies.
3. Add checker plus `ci/test_check_test_waits.py`, covering each flagged form, real code versus comments, annotations, missing reasons and multiline calls. Run the checker over the complete fixed tree, annotating only justified exceptions.
4. Add `python3 ci/check_test_waits.py` to Tooling Tests. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_*.py'` and the checker itself.
5. Run affected classes, then the full local suite once because shared infrastructure and Xcode target membership changed. An `AGENTS.md` note is optional/separate (`CLAUDE.md` is its symlink).

## Surfaces
- **Targets:** app tests, Xcode membership, `ci/`, workflow; one internal toast sleep-injection seam if needed. No app behavior change.
- **Entry points, multi-server, reverse states, connection modes, native quality:** n/a.
- **Docs:** checker docstring explains local invocation and exception syntax.

## Tests
Checker cases live in `ci/test_check_test_waits.py`. Focused Swift selection:
`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanLiveUpdateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanCardDetailStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanCardEditorStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/FileBrowserViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests --only HermesMobileTests/InsightsViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/CliSessionsSyncModelTests`.
Then `scripts/test-sim <udid>` once. No repeated three-run smoke gate; broaden only for an unresolved failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One shared implementation replaces all 16 observation `waitUntil` definitions.
- [ ] All 15 identified ordering sites use explicit completion/observation, preserving stale-result assertions.
- [ ] Checker passes the fixed tree and fails a newly added unannotated short or long sleep/deadline loop.
- [ ] Every permitted real delay has a specific reason; unused real-time fallback is removed.
- [ ] Linux Tooling Tests runs the checker; Python tests and full local XCTest pass.

## Manual test plan
n/a. Record checker/Python and XCTest results in the eventual PR.

## Out of scope
Resolving unrelated flake issues, closing #1263, XCTSkip quarantine rules, SwiftLint/new dependencies, a complete Swift parser, changes to production timer semantics.

## Decisions
Exclude Support helpers? Recommend no: polling commonly hides there. Adjacent reason comments cover intentional clock simulations.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: perf(chat): count transcript body evaluations during a scripted stream
body:
**What the user gets:** A Debug counter and scripted benchmark show how many transcript bodies re-render per stream tick.
**Why it matters:** Catches the invalidation regressions that make long chats janky before they ship.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 41 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | engineering / performance |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1256](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1256) (adjacent: its "temporary counters" are what this makes permanent), [#32](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/32) (adjacent: eager-stack decision this protects), [#1079](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1079) (boundary: remote diagnostics, not touched) |
| Needs mock first | no |
| Sources | performance-eng-opus #2, performance-eng-sol #4 |

## Problem
Hermex times its hot paths, but nothing counts SwiftUI body re-evaluations. The streaming transcript relies on `.equatable()` rows to skip settled markdown rows on every reveal tick, and nothing checks that. A new non-`Equatable` input, or a value handed to every row, makes every row re-render per tick. Nobody notices until a long chat janks. #1256 needed hand-added counters to find 61 host updates for 12 replies. Separately, the `Stream Batch Apply` signpost misses the normal reveal tick, so a trace undercounts streaming work.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/development/render-counter.ts` / `render-counter-entry.ts` count renders only in development. `apps/mobile/scripts/measure-renders.mts` drives a canned turn and measures a mid-stream window. Its measuring protocol compares the same device/base with interleaved runs.

## Hermex today
- `HermesMobile/Config/PerformanceSignposts.swift:1-19` has eight count-only intervals (documented in `DEVELOPMENT.md:322-346`). There is also `--hitch-meter` (`Config/HitchMeter.swift`, Debug only, flag parsed at `:73`), plus `scripts/benchmark-sim-launch`, `benchmark-streaming-scans` and `benchmark-math-formatting`.
- **Signpost gap (verified):** `ChatViewModel.flushPendingStreamingContent()` (`ChatViewModel.swift:1025-1041`) wraps its work in `Stream Batch Apply`. But the normal scheduled path, `revealStreamingContentTick()` (`:989-1005`, scheduled from `:967-982`), has no interval. The forced flush runs only on completion, cancel, error, interim and snapshot. So `DEVELOPMENT.md`'s row "Applying one batch of streamed tokens" actually measures almost none of a stream.
- The row-skipping contract lives in `ChatTranscriptView.swift:349-356` (comment) and `:687-713` (`ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.==` over value inputs). `hasActiveStream`, `listeningMessageID` and `isViewingCachedData` are compared on every row, so a stream start/end or a Listen toggle re-evaluates every row. That is probably fine, but it is unmeasured.
- A hosted body-count pattern already exists: `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests` (`HermesMobileTests/ChatScrollPolicyTests.swift:263-353`) hosts views in a `UIWindow` and counts passes through `EnvironmentStabilityProbe` (`:356`).
- **Premise correction:** the explorer suggested driving the benchmark from `scripts/local-hermes`. Its stub model answers only non-streaming requests (`scripts/local-hermes:90-97`) and returns one short fixed turn ("Let me run a quick check." plus an approval). It can't produce a long, growing reply. Use the in-process scripted stream seams instead: `SSEStreamingClient` with `ScriptedSSEStreamingClient` (`HermesMobileTests/ScriptedSSEStreamFixture.swift`), and the injectable `streamingRevealTick` (`ChatViewModel.swift:626,722`).

## Proposal
1. Add `Config/RenderProbe.swift`: non-observable, main-actor counters behind `#if DEBUG`, with `hit`, `reset` and snapshot inspection. Count named bodies plus transcript `renderID` in memory only. Probe `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock`, `MessageBubbleView`, `MarkdownRenderer`, `ToolActivityGroupView`, `ReasoningBlockView`; count `ResponseTextSelection` host updates separately. Release calls become an inlined no-op with no counter storage. Logged output, if any, is static names/counts only, never row identities.
2. Wrap `revealStreamingContentTick()` in `Stream Batch Apply` with `mutated` and integer `forced=0`; add `forced=1` to forced flushes. Signposts remain available in Release. Update `DEVELOPMENT.md`.
3. Host real `ChatTranscriptView` with a scripted `ChatViewModel`, about 20 settled replies and a manually driven active reply. Count roughly 30 text-only ticks. **Zero settled-row evaluations is the budget**, with a positive active-row count. Begin only after initial layout/stream-start inputs settle, and keep environment/follow/action inputs fixed. Await token delivery and active-row rendering through expectations and forced hosting layout; manual ticks alone do not prove SwiftUI rendered. No sleeps/polling, timing budget, launch flag or network benchmark script.

## Implementation steps
1. Add `RenderProbe` (Debug counters, plus a `reset()` and `count(_:)` for tests) and the six probe lines.
2. Wrap `revealStreamingContentTick()` in `Stream Batch Apply`. Update `PerformanceSignposts.swift`'s header comment and `DEVELOPMENT.md` § Recording signposts.
3. Add `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests` next to `ChatScrollPolicyTests.swift`, reusing the window-hosting pattern and the controllable token/tick seams from `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests` (its helper types are private; extract only the pieces needed). Assert settled-row counts. Also assert that the active row *is* evaluated, so the test can't pass vacuously.
4. Run it once with `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.==` temporarily returning false, confirm it fails, then restore. Record that run in the PR body.
5. If #1406 has landed, add this test to its table.

## Surfaces
- Entry points: n/a (tooling).
- Targets: main app (Debug-only code), `HermesMobileTests`. Extensions are untouched; the probe file must not join them.
- Multi-server, reverse states, connection modes: n/a.
- Native quality: n/a.
- Docs: `DEVELOPMENT.md` (signpost table and counter inspection).

## Tests
- `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests`: one test for "text-only ticks don't re-evaluate settled rows" with a positive active-row count in the same test. Stream start/end can legitimately invalidate settled rows and are outside this budget.
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `RenderProbe` compiles to a no-op in Release (check with `nm` or a Release build: no `RenderProbe` symbol beyond the inlined stub).
- [ ] An Instruments or `log show --signpost` recording of a streamed reply shows `Stream Batch Apply` intervals for the normal ticks, not just the final flush.
- [ ] The budget test passes on the implementation head and fails when the `.equatable()` skip is broken (shown in the PR).
- [ ] No sleeps or polling in the new test; ticks are driven explicitly.
- [ ] `DEVELOPMENT.md` matches the new interval metadata.

## Manual test plan
1. Debug build on a simulator, start a long reply in one disposable session on an explicitly in-scope Hermes server, and record with `xcrun xctrace … --instrument os_signpost` as in `DEVELOPMENT.md`. Confirm there are many `Stream Batch Apply` intervals with `forced=0` and forced flushes with `forced=1` (completion can invoke more than one).
2. Inspect the Debug counter snapshot after a stream; only named totals may leave the process.

## Out of scope
- Timing budgets in XCTest (Release timings belong in Instruments).
- A gallery or fixture launch mode for screenshots.
- Fixing anything the counter finds: #1417 and #1369 own those.

## Decisions
Scope: the shared Sessions/Bot Chat transcript is covered. Separate Bot room transcripts are not; add a room benchmark only when there is evidence it is needed.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: docs(agents): write down the performance invariants and what guards each
body:
**What the user gets:** Performance invariants are written down next to what guards them.
**Why it matters:** Agents changing the transcript can't find the rules today.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 42 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | engineering |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none (#1405 fills one gap in the table when it lands) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#32](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/32) (adjacent: the eager-stack decision), [#1256](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1256) (adjacent: an invariant with no guard today) |
| Needs mock first | no |
| Sources | performance-eng-opus #7 |

## Problem
"Performance without compromise" is a product pillar (`AGENTS.md` § Performance without compromise). Its concrete rules are scattered across code comments, `docs/agents/bots.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and closed issues. `docs/agents/` has no performance page, so an agent changing the transcript can't find the rules, or the test that will catch it breaking one. Some invariants have no guard at all, and nobody can see that.

## What T3 does
`docs/internals/performance-regressions.md` lists each invariant with the regression command and test files that pin it, and says "Payload budgets belong in these tests so regressions fail locally."

## Hermex today
Verified on master @ 5125b512. Each row is an invariant that exists in code today, with its current guard.

| Invariant | Where it lives | Guard today |
|---|---|---|
| Settled transcript rows skip re-evaluation while a reply streams: live-stream inputs are scoped to the anchor row, and rows compare by value | `ChatTranscriptView.swift:349-356`, `.equatable()` at `:408`, `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.==` at `:687-713` | Partial: `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests` (`HermesMobileTests/ChatScrollPolicyTests.swift:258-353`) pins that environment closures don't invalidate skipped rows. **No test pins the row skip itself**; 41 adds it. |
| The Sessions transcript uses an eager `VStack` (#32); initial/history requests are paged, but loaded pages accumulate | `ChatTranscriptView.swift:338-349`; Hermes page size `HermesREST.transcriptPageSize = 100` (`HermesREST.swift:116`) | The page-size constant is not a cap on rendered rows: `ChatViewModel.loadOlderMessages` (`:2185-2237`) prepends to the existing array. No automated total-row bound exists; do not document one. |
| A Bot room draws only its newest 50 events | `docs/agents/bots.md:377-382` (`BotRoomTranscriptWindow`) | `BotChatPresentationTests.testWarmRoomBuildsOnlyTheNewestPageOfReplies` (`:130`), `BotRoomTests` |
| Streamed text reveals on a tick, not per token; completion flushes immediately | `ChatViewModel.swift:967-1005` (tick), `:1025-1041` (forced flush) | `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests` |
| Only the streaming tail re-parses: settled markdown seals into ~6,000-byte chunks | `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitter.stableChunkTargetUTF8Count` (`StreamingMarkdownSupport.swift:18`) | `StreamingMarkdownSupportTests` (`testStableChunkThresholdCountsUTF8Bytes`, `testLargePrefixStreamReconstructsExactlyAndPreservesStableChunks`); `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` |
| Transcript images: one load per key, decoded off main, capped at 512 px, purged on memory warning, bounded to 48 MB / 150 images, server-namespaced | `TranscriptImageCache.swift:1-14` | `TranscriptImageCacheTests` (single-flight, memory warning, 512 px). The 48 MB / 150 limits themselves are not asserted. |
| The diff canvas draws only visible rows (plus four-row overscan); rows are never views | `Features/Workspace/ReviewDiff/ReviewDiffCanvasView.swift:44-47` | Partial: `ReviewDiffCanvasViewTests.testDrawnColumnsGrowPastZeroWidthCharactersAndAreMeasuredOncePerRow` guards width measurement, not viewport-only drawing; `ReviewDiff` signposter (`:39-42`, intervals at `:195` and `ReviewDiffCanvasView+Drawing.swift:15`) |
| SwiftData newest reads are fetch-limited | `CacheStore.swift:71`, `CacheStore+Hermes.swift:189` | `Cache Read` / `Cache Write` signposts; `CacheStoreTests` covers correctness, not the limit |
| Held live frames during a Hermes attach are bounded by `heldFrameLimit` | `HermesConversation.heldFrameLimit` (`HermesConversation.swift:130-131`) | `HermesConversationTests` (flood test at `:353`). The pin's `tui_gateway/event_replay.py:28` also sets 512 (read-only `gh api` verified at `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`); its byte limits can evict earlier. |
| Signposts carry static names and integer metadata only | `PerformanceSignposts.swift:12-15` | Review only |
| Launch paints cached rows first | `LaunchSignpost` (`PerformanceSignposts.swift:21-42`) | `scripts/benchmark-sim-launch` (interleaved medians) |
| Debug instruments compile out of Release | `HitchMeter.swift` (`#if DEBUG`) | `HitchMeterTests` (logic only) |
| No continuously repainting animation; every animation respects Reduce Motion | `AGENTS.md` § Taste | Review only. `repeatForever` has zero uses in `HermesMobile/` today. |

## Proposal
Add `docs/agents/performance.md`, about one screen long:

1. **Invariants:** the verified rules above, one row each, distinguishing current mechanisms from requirements and known gaps. Link to the symbol, not a copied number (for example "`stableChunkTargetUTF8Count`", not "6,000"), so the page can't drift from the code.
2. **Guards:** each row names its test class or signpost. Write "review only" honestly where nothing automated exists, so gaps stay visible.
3. **How to measure:** Release build for timings, Debug is fine for counts. Use a median of three or more, interleave builds and compare on the same base, as `scripts/benchmark-sim-launch` does. Signposts and their reading commands live in `DEVELOPMENT.md` § Launch arguments and profiling; link there, don't duplicate.
4. **Before you change the transcript:** a three-line checklist. Keep new row inputs `Equatable` and add them to `==`. Pass app-wide values to rows only if a stream tick doesn't change them. Visibility gating is a proposed rule from #1370, not a current guarantee until that change lands.

Add one pointer in `AGENTS.md` § Hit every surface → **Docs**: "performance rules and their guards in `docs/agents/performance.md`." `AGENTS.md` asks that edits to it be proposed, not slipped in, so call that line out in the PR body for sign-off.

## Implementation steps
1. Re-verify every row against the current head. Line numbers drift; prefer symbol names in the doc.
2. Write `docs/agents/performance.md` with the four sections above.
3. Propose the one-line `AGENTS.md` pointer, flagged in the PR.
4. If 41 has merged, fill in the row-skip guard. If 06 has merged, add its visibility-gating invariant.

## Surfaces
- Docs only: `docs/agents/performance.md`, plus one proposed line in `AGENTS.md`.
- Entry points, targets, multi-server, reverse states, connection modes, native quality: n/a.

## Tests
None: docs only. Per `AGENTS.md` § Verifying, a docs-only change runs no XCTest. Do check that every test class the doc names exists (`ls HermesMobileTests | grep <name>`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/agents/performance.md` exists, lists each invariant above, and names a guard or says "review only".
- [ ] Every named test class and signpost exists at the PR head.
- [ ] Numbers are referenced by symbol, not copied, except where a symbol doesn't exist.
- [ ] The `AGENTS.md` pointer is proposed and called out in the PR body.

## Manual test plan
n/a (docs). The maintainer reads the page and checks that the "review only" rows are the gaps they expect.

## Out of scope
- Writing the missing guards: 41 adds the row-skip budget. A `transcriptPageSize` or `repeatForever` lint can be its own follow-up if wanted.
- Converting `scripts/check-swift-file-sizes` into a ratchet.

## Decisions
- Should "no `repeatForever`" become a Linux tooling check (zero hits today, so it's cheap)? Recommendation: yes, as a later S follow-up next to `ci/check_string_catalog.py`, not in this docs PR.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): send a message typed offline once the chat reconnects
body:
**What the user gets:** A message typed offline sends once the chat reconnects.
**Why it matters:** Core remote-ready case; limited to definitely-unsent prompts because the host has no idempotency key.
**Cost:** Large; needs the owner's hands on a physical iPhone.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 43 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability / feature |
| Effort | L (durable text and async ownership are part of correctness) |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes API: `prompt.submit` (verified at the pin, see below). No new server support. |
| Depends on | #1375; reuses the pending-bubble style from #1379 if it has landed |
| Related GitHub issues | [#508](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/508) (adjacent: the submission-uncertainty mark this must cooperate with), [#745](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/745) (adjacent: edit and retry in Bot Chat, separate) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | composer-opus #1 slice B, connection-state-opus #3, connection-state-sol rejected list ("copy automatic durable send retries wholesale") |

## Problem
On a train, in a lift or during a tunnel blip, a Hermes chat can't deliver. After 11 lands the user can type, but Send fails with "Reconnect to the server to send a message." They have to notice, wait for the signal and tap Send again. A waiting-send action could spare that second tap while this chat remains active. iOS does not guarantee reconnection or delivery while the app is suspended. That must never cost a double-executed instruction.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/state/thread-outbox-model.ts` persists an outbox; `threadOutboxDelivery.ts` retries it with backoff. T3's server deduplicates client command IDs (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/CommandReceiptStore.ts`). Hermes cannot safely copy that retry policy.

## Hermex today
- **Pinned contract verified:** read-only `gh api "repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/contents/apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json?ref=ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2"` and base64 decode confirms `PromptSubmitParams.additionalProperties: false`, with no idempotency key. Reuse `HermesCall.promptSubmit`; add no parameter.
- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.submit` (`Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:450-488`) throws `NotSent` only before the conservative dispatch-validation boundary; uploads and replaced Bot Chats have separate flags (`:410-415`). Dispatched/unknown outcomes must never auto-retry.
- `ChatViewModel.submitHermesPrompt` (`:3097-3209`) rolls back an unsent bubble and preserves #508's durable uncertainty mark for a lost answer. Reconnect calls `releaseSubmissionMark` (`:8216-8222`).
- `sendMessage` returns before Hermes submission when cached (`:2863-2876`); 11 changes editor availability, not that guard. The `NotSent` catch alone cannot implement offline Send.
- Drafts are keyed by server/conversation (`Persistence/ChatDraftStore.swift:167-197`), stored in a protected file (`:524-576`) and include `botSubmissionUncertain` (`:72-89`). `ChatView` owns composer hydration and send-result handling (`:2751,2960-2962`).

## Proposal
Keep one waiting plain-text composer Send per active Hermes chat. Exclude files, quotes, slash-command execution, Steer, Queue and Stop & send. Admit an already-disconnected cached intent before the cache guard, or a `.send` failing `NotSent(.transport)` without upload/replaced-chat flags. Preserve every other send path.

Add optional `ChatDraft.waitingSend { text, createdAt }` with tolerant record coding, `isEmpty`, key-migration and cleanup support. Persist before clearing only the captured composer text; preserve edits made during that await. While it waits, the editor remains usable but additional Send is held; Cancel/expiry merges it back. Never concatenate independent instructions automatically.

Drain on foreground reconnect only for the originating active chat, captured server, draft key, stored session/root and owner generation. Claim synchronously before any await and keep one owned task. Recheck ownership after awaits and at socket dispatch; a replaced Bot Chat must not receive it. Submit captured text with **empty attachments**, never newly staged composer files.

Keep a durable recoverable copy through the claim-to-dispatch transition. Before dispatch, transfer it into the existing saved-draft/uncertainty path and flush; clearing the waiting record must not create a crash-loss window. Acknowledgement removes only that send. A lost answer keeps its text and #508 hold, never requeues. Only another qualifying `NotSent` may wait for a distinct reconnect; no retry loop. Other failures merge back without overwriting newer text.

Leaving the chat invalidates/cancels its drain and deadline task even if its view model survives. Reopening/relaunching restores text for deliberate Send, never automatic delivery. Backgrounding pauses delivery; same-chat foreground reattach may resume. Expire after 10 minutes using an injected clock and one cancellable deadline, rechecking on foreground. No suspended-iOS delivery promise.

Show a static pending bubble, “Waiting for connection”, with Cancel; keep it out of cached `messages`. Reuse 15's presentation if present. Return a distinct locally-retained send result to `ChatView`, so composer clearing does not claim server acceptance.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** publish several static pending/cancel/expired treatments through `html-communication`, report the URL and stop for a pick.
2. Extend `ChatDraftStore`. Replace 11's offline Send hold with the approved waiting-send action only for eligible plain-text Hermes drafts; keep true session read-only restrictions. Wire composer admission before `sendMessage`'s cache guard plus the qualifying `NotSent` arm, and update `ChatView` send-result/hydration handling.
3. Add the owned drain/deadline, invalidation hooks and captured-text submission path. Audit every await and dispatch validation.
4. Render the bubble, add localized labels, and update reconnect behavior in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`.

## Surfaces
App and tests: Sessions and Bot Chat share the coordinator; keyboard Send shares composer admission. Intents/deep links/shares prefill and qualify only after deliberate plain-text Send. Other extensions and webui are unchanged. Read `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`: subtree replacement alone cannot cancel retained tasks. Invalidate on server/key/root change, sign-out and chat departure. Cancel, expiry and reopen restore text. Verify LAN/tunnel/foreground recovery, VoiceOver Cancel, Dynamic Type, light/dark and Reduce Motion.

## Tests
New `HermesWaitingSendTests`, using engine fakes, an injected clock and suspended completions:
1. Cached/offline Send is retained, then reconnect dispatches once; duplicate connect callbacks dispatch no second call.
2. Post-dispatch loss never queues/resends and preserves the existing uncertainty recovery.
3. Reopen restores text without dispatch. Cancel/expiry or owner/server/root change during suspended attach preserves newer text and dispatches nothing.

No sleeps/polling. Run `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesWaitingSendTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatDraftStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Only an eligible explicitly offline composer Send or pre-dispatch transport `NotSent` Send waits; read-only sessions, files, quotes and alternate modes stay excluded.
- [ ] One reconnect delivers once; two quick reconnects still deliver once.
- [ ] Cancel, expiry and relaunch return the text to the composer, and nothing is lost.
- [ ] No waiting send crosses servers or chats.
- [ ] The bubble is static (no spinner) and VoiceOver-labelled.

## Manual test plan
1. Signed Debug build, Hermes server over the Cloudflare tunnel. Open one disposable chat and turn on airplane mode.
2. Type and Send: the waiting bubble shows, and the composer is empty.
3. Turn airplane mode off and wait for the reattach: the message sends once, and the reply streams.
4. Repeat, then tap Cancel: the text is back in the composer.
5. Repeat, then kill the app while waiting and relaunch: the text is in the composer, and nothing was sent (check the host transcript).

## Out of scope
- Files, Steer, Queue, Stop & send.
- Multiple independent waiting messages.
- Retrying dispatched-but-unacknowledged prompts. That needs a server-side client message id; file an upstream request if wanted.
- webui servers.

## Decisions
- Expiry: recommend 10 minutes.
- Another device starts a turn before delivery: recommend preserving existing `.send` outcomes. The pin's `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:631-654` calls `_handle_busy_submit`; its exact busy-mode outcome is **not independently verified here**. Verify that handler before promising “Queued”; rejection/unknown outcomes keep current recovery.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the batch's single Branch TestFlight build).

title: fix(insights): keep last-known limit cards when a refresh fails
body:
**What the user gets:** Provider limit cards keep their last-known values when a refresh fails.
**Why it matters:** A tunnel blip shouldn't look like a vanished subscription.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 44 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability / UX |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes API: hermex-push `GET /provider-quota`, capability-gated through `/capabilities` (`HermesInsightsClient.swift:35-55`); webui `GET /api/provider/quota`. Client paths verified in source; the companion route is outside the Hermes-agent pin and its current host status semantics remain unverified. No route or shape change. |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | Adjacent: [#415](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/415) (Limits group), [#1237](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1237) (Hermes quota route) |
| Needs mock first | yes: new inline notice and refresh-failure copy; reuse `ProvidersView` as the visual starting point. |
| Sources | design-settings-sol #4 |

## Problem
On the Usage screen, the user pulls to refresh limits while the tunnel blips, or a provider read times out. The card for that provider silently disappears, as though the subscription were gone, or the old card stays with no hint that the refresh failed. Either way the screen misleads someone who explicitly asked for fresh numbers.

## What T3 does
`src/features/usage/usageLimitsRefresh.ts` serializes refreshes per environment and records the latest outcome. `UsageLimitsPooled.tsx:491-514` keeps the last-known values on screen with "could not refresh limits", inside the Limits section only.

## Hermex today
- `InsightsViewModel.loadLimits` (`Features/Insights/InsightsViewModel.swift:235-301`) silently retains cards if provider selection throws (`:259-265`), but `try?` quota probes (`:279`) turn errors into nil and the final assignment (`:300`) removes those cards.
- `ProviderLimitCard.init?` (`InsightsModels.swift:380-391`) rejects non-available/empty payloads. This is first-load presentation policy, not evidence that `unavailable` means permanent removal. The companion handler's current status semantics remain unverified; do not conflate probe failure and provider disappearance.
- `providerLimitUpdatedText` (`InsightsModels.swift:311`, `ProviderLimitsCard.swift:114`) uses original measurement age. No cards persist; Hermes Insights is keyed by server/Profile entry (`HermesSessionListView.swift:393-396,418-419`).
- `ProvidersView.refreshFailureBanner` (`Features/Settings/ProvidersView.swift:104-131`) supplies a visual precedent. Toolbar/pull refresh passes `refresh: true`, appear does not (`InsightsView.swift:47-56,169-177`).

## Proposal
Tell three outcomes apart per provider, and merge instead of replace.

```swift
private enum LimitProbe { case card(ProviderLimitCard), gone, failed }
```

- A thrown transport/decode failure, `unavailable`, or an unknown/malformed partial payload → `.failed`. A known terminal non-card response (`unsupported`, `no_key`, `invalid_key`) → `.gone`, after checking those semantics in the companion handler. Otherwise → `.card` when usable. Keep tolerant decoding; do not classify every nil `init?` result as authoritative removal. First loads still show no card for any non-renderable response.
- Merge in selection order. `.card` replaces. `.gone` drops. `.failed` keeps the previous card with the same `id`, unchanged (original `updatedAt`), and adds that id to a new `private(set) var staleLimitIDs: Set<String>`.
- A provider that left `selection` (key removed, Profile changed provider) is dropped, as today.
- If `client.providers()` throws while cards are showing, keep all of them and mark them all stale **only after** the same generation/cancellation guard used for successful results. Cancellation and superseded loads must not publish a notice. Empty selection clears cards and stale IDs.
- Clear `staleLimitIDs` entries when a later probe succeeds or returns `.gone`.
- Keep the generation guard (`limitsGeneration`) and the parallel task group as they are.

**Presentation** (`ProviderLimitsSection`, `ProviderLimitsCard.swift:8-33`): when `staleLimitIDs` is non-empty, show one inline notice at the top of the Limits group, in the same style as `ProvidersView`'s banner: "Couldn't refresh limits. Showing the last values loaded." Each card keeps its own "Updated … ago" footer. No error goes to `errorMessage`/`lastError`, so the analytics stay untouched (`testFailingQuotaProbeLeavesAnalyticsAndErrorStateUntouched` must keep passing). First loads with no cards stay silent, exactly as today.

This applies to webui servers too, because the view model is shared. It is a fix, so that's fine.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** publish distinct inline-notice treatments via `html-communication`, report the URL and stop for a pick.
2. Verify companion status meanings read-only on an in-scope host or installed plugin source. In `loadLimits`, replace `try?` with explicit outcomes and merge/stale IDs, guarding all mutations by generation and cancellation. Update its silent-failure comment.
3. Pass stale state to `ProviderLimitsSection`; use a local notice in the approved style without creating a reusable banner abstraction or depending on 46.
4. Add the localized notice after reading `docs/agents/i18n.md`.

## Surfaces
Usage toolbar/pull refresh on Hermes and webui (shared reliability fix), compact/regular width. Main app/tests only. No persisted cross-server/Profile state; retain the existing entry-keyed lifetime. A later successful/gone probe clears stale IDs; empty selection clears everything. Keep analytics error state untouched. Check timeout recovery, VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, light/dark and existing Reduce Motion-aware card animation.

## Tests
In `ProviderLimitCardTests` (where `loadLimits` is tested today, `:200-281`):
1. `testFailedRefreshKeepsTheLastCardAndMarksItStale`: first load returns a card. The refresh throws for that provider, so the card is still present with its original `updatedAt`, and `staleLimitIDs` contains it.
2. `testRefreshThatNoLongerQualifiesRemovesTheCard`: the refresh returns `status: "no_key"`, so the card is gone and nothing is stale.
3. A delayed failed provider-selection request from an older generation cannot mark the newer successful cards stale. Use suspended completions/expectations. Include an `unavailable` response in the retained-card test.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ProviderLimitCardTests --only HermesMobileTests/InsightsViewModelTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A transport or decode failure on refresh never removes a card that was showing.
- [ ] A confirmed terminal status removes the card; unavailable/unknown probe results preserve last-known data.
- [ ] A retained card keeps its original "Updated … ago" time.
- [ ] One notice appears in the Limits group while any card is stale and disappears after a good refresh.
- [ ] First loads with failures stay silent; analytics error state is untouched.

## Manual test plan
1. On a Hermes server with hermex-push provider quota, open Usage and wait for limit cards.
2. Turn on airplane mode, then pull to refresh: the cards stay, the notice appears, and the footers show the old time.
3. Turn airplane mode off and pull again: the notice is gone and the times are fresh.
4. Switch server and back: no stale card or notice carries over.

## Out of scope
- Persisting cards across launches (#1409's snapshot is the persisted form).
- Pace markers, credits pooling, per-provider error detail.
- A selectable or expandable error-detail notice primitive (design-settings-sol #5; see #1410's follow-up note).

## Decisions
Recommend “Couldn't refresh limits. Showing the last values loaded.” Final wording follows the approved mock; first-load failures remain silent.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(widgets): show provider limits on the Home Screen and Lock Screen
body:
**What the user gets:** Provider limits on the Home Screen and Lock Screen.
**Why it matters:** Hermex's first static widget; the snapshot pattern is reusable for #6 and #359.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 45 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes API: hermex-push `GET /provider-quota`, capability-gated (`HermesInsightsClient.swift:35-55`, `HermesREST.companionProviderQuota`); client route verified, companion host contract not independently verified here (see 44). Hermes only; the widget makes no network calls. |
| Depends on | #1408 (the snapshot is written from its merged, stale-aware card state) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#6](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/6) (adjacent: New Chat widget; this sets the snapshot pattern it can reuse), [#359](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/359) (adjacent: Kanban/Task widgets, same pattern) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | system-surfaces-opus #6, system-surfaces-sol #1 |

## Problem
People who drive Claude or Codex through Hermes hit their subscription limits. Today the only way to check what's left before starting work is to open Hermex, go to Usage and wait for the probe. A glanceable widget answers "do I have room for this run?" without opening the app.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/widgets/SubscriptionUsage.tsx` renders Home/Lock Screen limits. `subscriptionUsageSnapshot.ts:75-101,152-166` publishes app-built values with deadlines from the earlier of reset and measurement +15 minutes; expired entries hide percentages. The coordinator skips identical publication; the extension does not make credentialed calls.

## Hermex today
- `HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift:5-10` registers only a Live Activity. Its extension already has the app group (`Resources/HermesLiveActivityWidget.entitlements`, `Config/Shared.xcconfig:11`) and reads shared avatar files (`LiveActivities/AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:238-252`).
- `InsightsViewModel.loadLimits` (`Features/Insights/InsightsViewModel.swift:235-301`) fills `ProviderLimitCard`/`ProviderLimitRow` (`InsightsModels.swift:209-245`). Loading currently belongs to the Usage screen (`InsightsView.swift:47-56`).
- There is no Usage deep link. `HermesSessionListView.swift:393-396,418-419,470` opens it for an explicit Profile.
- `ServerAccount.id` (`Models/ServerAccount.swift:25-31`) contains the server URL; do not copy it into a widget file in clear.

## Proposal
**Start with opportunistic publication from Usage.** Add a limits widget to the existing extension, using the most recently viewed Hermes Usage Profile on the active server. Show the Profile name so its scope is clear. Do not add a foreground polling service or construct a hidden `InsightsViewModel`; opening/refreshing Usage remains the refresh mechanism.

**Snapshot (app writes, widget reads).** Add a small versioned `ProviderLimitsSnapshot: Codable` shared by the app and widget. It contains a SHA-256 `serverKey` (CryptoKit, from `ServerAccount.id`), connection identity, Profile, publication time, and bounded provider/window values. Keep each provider's **original** `updatedAt` and 44's `isStale`. Include only usable percentage windows; credits without a percentage do not become a fake gauge. Omit server URLs, credentials, session IDs and server-name fallbacks that might contain a URL.

Write atomically to `<app group>/Widgets/provider-limits.json` with `completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication` protection. One serialized app-owned publisher captures server/connection/Profile and generation, validating them immediately before committing a write. Switch, sign-out, removal of the snapshot's server, or replacement of its connection invalidates the generation **before** clearing the file. A late quota result cannot recreate an old snapshot. Removing an unrelated inactive server does not clear the active snapshot. Read `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` before wiring these hooks. Bound file size/array counts and treat missing, unsupported-version or corrupt data as empty.

Skip identical writes and call `WidgetCenter.shared.reloadTimelines(ofKind:)` after a changed write or clear. Publication time never makes retained data fresh again. Unknown/missing measurement timestamps fail closed for numerical freshness; do not substitute the refresh time for an old card's age.

**Widget.** Add `ProviderLimitsWidget` (`StaticConfiguration`, kind `ProviderLimits`) to `HermesLiveActivityWidgetBundle`, supporting `.systemSmall`, `.systemMedium` and `.accessoryRectangular`. Small/accessory show the tightest usable window; medium shows at most two providers with two windows each. Use the approved mocks. No network or Keychain access in the extension, and no animations or timers.

Compute each row's validity deadline from the earlier of its reset and its provider's `updatedAt + 1 h`. At/past reset show “Open Hermex to refresh”, not “Reset” or a guessed replenished balance: the widget cannot know the new allowance. 44's failed-refresh state may retain an explicitly stale value only until that deadline. Emit timeline entries at unique future deadlines, with a `.after` refresh policy; correctness comes from precomputed entries rather than assuming WidgetKit refreshes on schedule. Honor accented/vibrant rendering, reduced luminance and container background visibility.

**Tap.** Add a typed Usage URL built with `HermesDeepLink.scheme`, carrying the opaque server key, connection identity and Profile. Route through `ContentView.handleOpenURL` into Hermes home in compact and regular width. Open Usage for that exact Profile only when the active server and connection still match and the Profile exists; otherwise decline to home. Never silently switch servers or show another Profile's numbers.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first.** Publish distinct static small/medium/Lock Screen designs with `html-communication`, covering fresh/stale/empty, light/dark/tinted; report the URL and stop for a pick.
2. Add the snapshot/store and pure timeline policy (shared app/widget membership), with injectable directory and clock for tests. Keep the quota presentation models main-app-only.
3. Wire publication after 44's guarded merge on Hermes Usage. Add generation invalidation/clear hooks to the server/connection lifecycle in `AuthManager`; do not enable this new feature for webui.
4. Add `ProviderLimitsWidget` to the existing bundle. Include its localized strings in the widget's catalog membership; retain the Live Activity.
5. Add the typed URL builder/parser and root routing, including cold launch and rejected destinations.
6. Update the provider-quota entry in `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md` with the opportunistic refresh behavior.

## Surfaces
App: publication and root URL routing; existing widget extension: widget and shared snapshot; tests: store/timeline/routing. No new target/App ID, share or notification-service changes. Active server only, explicitly scoped Profile; invalidate late writes across server/connection changes. Removal/sign-out clears its snapshot. Home, Lock Screen and StandBy use system rendering; support VoiceOver, tinted/vibrant modes and reduced luminance. Localize widget strings in its target. No timers or credentialed extension calls.

## Tests
`ProviderLimitsSnapshotTests` (pure store/timeline/routing policy compiled into the app test target):
1. With an injected date, a row becomes non-numerical at reset/expiry; re-publishing a retained card cannot extend its validity. Include missing dates and corrupt files in this behavior test.
2. Suspend an old publication, switch server/connection, clear, then complete it: the snapshot stays empty. Inject a temporary directory into the publisher; do not assume `AuthManager` already has an app-group directory seam.
3. A matching Usage link opens the recorded Profile; mismatched/removed destinations decline without switching server.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ProviderLimitsSnapshotTests --only HermesMobileTests/ProviderLimitCardTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotDeepLinkTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The widget renders from the snapshot with no network or Keychain access in the extension.
- [ ] The snapshot contains no server URL, credential or session id.
- [ ] Rows past reset/expiry or with no measurement date never show an old percentage; stale publication cannot renew their validity.
- [ ] Server switch, removal of its server, sign-out and connection replacement empty the snapshot; late results cannot restore it. WidgetKit redraw timing is system-owned.
- [ ] Foregrounding makes no extra quota requests; Usage is the documented refresh mechanism.
- [ ] The tap opens Usage for the recorded Profile on the matching active server/connection and never switches servers.

## Manual test plan
1. On Hermes, open Usage and add Home/Lock Screen widgets; verify Profile and percentages.
2. Exercise a short-reset fixture: percentages disappear at the deadline.
3. Switch/sign out during a suspended refresh; old data cannot return. Open Usage on the new server to populate it.
4. Tap fresh and stale links in compact/regular width and after cold launch; mismatches decline to home.
5. Check tinted and Always-On legibility on a device.

## Out of scope
- Per-instance server or Profile configuration (`AppIntentConfiguration`), and multiple servers side by side.
- Background refresh from the extension or push-driven updates.
- Large and extra-large families.
- New Chat ([#6](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/6)) and Kanban ([#359](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/359)) widgets; no shared abstraction is required yet.
- Foreground/background polling, installed-widget detection, webui publication and credits-only widgets.

## Decisions
Expiry: recommend one hour after the original measurement, always capped by reset. This is a product choice, not a freshness guarantee; opportunistic refresh means the widget will often ask to open Hermex.


## Outside reach

None. The widget never makes network calls; it reads an app-written snapshot.

title: refactor(ui): one toast with tone, busy-to-result updates, and swipe to dismiss
body:
**What the user gets:** One toast system with tone, busy-to-result updates and swipe to dismiss.
**Why it matters:** Two inconsistent toast systems and alerts for non-blocking failures.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 46 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI / engineering |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1089](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1089) (overlaps: chat-screen design-system migration), [#1088](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1088) (overlaps: session-list migration), [#607](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/607) (adjacent: shared design-system foundations). Coordinate so this doesn't redo their component work. |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | design-settings-opus #5 (+ design-settings-sol #5 as a follow-up note) |

## Problem
Hermex has two toast systems that look, move and time out differently. Neither can be swiped away. The Git one shows a spinning `ProgressView` while it works, a continuously repainting indicator the app's rules avoid. Some non-blocking failures ("Session Action Failed", "Could Not Update Skill", "Could Not Update Task") still interrupt with a modal alert the user must dismiss before doing anything else.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Toast.tsx` is one toast:
- `tone: default | success | danger`;
- `busy` (an indicator instead of an icon), an optional description line and an action;
- horizontal swipe to dismiss (25% of width or a flick), using `ReduceMotion.System`;
- a VoiceOver announcement.

Inline failures use `Notice.tsx` instead (selectable text, danger tone).

## Hermex today
- `Features/Shared/ActionToast.swift:8-95`: one toast, four-second injected dismissal clock, optional action; VoiceOver keeps it until acted on. `ActionToastView` (`:100-212`) moves focus, supports accessibility-size wrapping and Reduce Motion. Hosts: chat and both session lists. `ActionToastStateTests` covers timing, replacement, VoiceOver and action-once.
- `Features/Workspace/GitActionToastOverlay.swift:1-144`: separate progress/success, six-second un-injected success timer, subtitle/detail layout, top transition, spinning busy `ProgressView` (`:92-100`), no VoiceOver wait. Its only host is `ChatView` (`:376,998`; operations at `:1537-1625`).
- Failure alerts live in `SessionListActionConfirmations.swift:13-29` (both lists), `SkillsView.swift:45` and `TasksView.swift:102`. Tasks' Delete/Run Now alerts (`:88,96`) are confirmations and stay.

## Proposal
Extend `ActionToast` with neutral/success/failure tone, optional subtitle/detail lines and busy state. Busy uses an approved static glyph and never auto-dismisses. Results with detail last six seconds; other ordinary toasts stay four seconds; VoiceOver keeps the existing wait/focus/close behavior. Tone colors the glyph and supplies an accessibility value, not a warning-colored background.

Have `show` return an ID; `update(id:content:)` preserves identity and restarts only the result clock, while `dismiss(id:)` acts only on that current ID. A stale Git completion must not overwrite a newer Undo toast or revive a swiped-away busy toast. Every Git return/cancel/retired path resolves only its captured ID and cannot mutate state after screen departure. Preserve branch subtitles and partial commit/push failure details.

Render the single toast once per host. Chat places Git feedback at the top and other notices at their current location; expose matching transition placement instead of reusing a bottom slide at the top. Delete the separate Git state/overlay.

Add horizontal swipe dismissal at a quarter width or a fast flick, with Reduce Motion fade/no animated snap-back. Direction checks inside SwiftUI `onChanged` alone do not make the recognizer fail vertically; verify actual scroll arbitration and use a direction-gated UIKit recognizer if necessary.

In the same migration replace the three scoped non-blocking failure alerts with failure toasts; Skills/Tasks gain hosts. Keep confirmations as alerts. Wrap failure text to three lines, unrestricted at accessibility sizes.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** publish distinct static toast treatments via `html-communication` (tones, busy glyph, detail, top/bottom, light/dark/accessibility); report the URL and stop for a pick.
2. Extend `ActionToast`/state/view, migrate all Git paths and remove `GitActionToastOverlay.swift`. Update ownership/transition comments.
3. Migrate the three failure-alert sites, add Skills/Tasks hosts, and remove only demonstrably unused catalog keys (`ci/check_string_catalog.py`).
4. Extend focused state/policy tests and verify real gesture/VoiceOver behavior.

## Surfaces
Chat Git controls, both session lists including Archive/Undo, Skills/Tasks and keyboard-triggered equivalents. App/tests only. View-owned state must dismiss on departure/server subtree replacement; stale operations validate their toast IDs. Close/swipe ends presentation without cancelling server work. Check VoiceOver focus/close, accessibility wrapping, light/dark glass and Reduce Motion; reuse/localize existing strings where possible.

## Tests
Add to `ActionToastStateTests`:
