1. `testBusyToastStaysUntilUpdatedThenDismissesOnTheResultClock`: a busy toast schedules no sleeper; `update` to success schedules the injected result clock. Use `ParkedSleeper`/expectations from the existing tests, never elapsed-time sleeps.
2. `testUpdateKeepsTheToastWhileShowReplacesIt`: the state retains its ID across `update` (test this state directly; actual VoiceOver focus remains a manual check). Complete an old operation after replacement/swipe dismissal and assert it cannot replace or revive the toast.

Keep the swipe threshold in a pure `ActionToastDismissPolicy.shouldDismiss(translation:velocity:width:)` with one test, the way `ImageLightboxGesturePolicy` does it.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ActionToastStateTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `GitActionToastOverlay.swift` is gone; Git actions show progress and result in the shared toast.
- [ ] No spinner or rotating indicator in any toast.
- [ ] Horizontal swipe dismisses; vertical scrolling under a toast is unaffected.
- [ ] Under Reduce Motion, nothing slides.
- [ ] The VoiceOver wait-and-focus behavior is unchanged (existing test passes).
- [ ] (Failure migration) The three failure alerts are toasts; confirmations remain alerts.

## Manual test plan
1. In an explicitly disposable Hermes chat and Git test repository, commit and push: one toast goes busy, then success, with detail lines; swipe it away.
2. Archive a session: "Archived · Undo" still works. Swipe right while the list scrolls vertically: the list scrolls and the toast stays.
3. Turn on Reduce Motion and repeat: fades only.
4. With VoiceOver on, push: the toast takes focus and stays until closed.
5. (Failure migration) Force a skill update failure (airplane mode): a failure toast instead of an alert.

## Out of scope
Toast queuing, generic Retry actions and a shared inline-error primitive. 44's Limits notice is independent; coordinate component naming with [#607](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/607) without making it a dependency.

## Decisions
- Should failure toasts carry a Retry action where the operation is idempotent (for example, a skill toggle)? Recommendation: not in this issue. Ship the plain failure toast first, and add Retry per call site when a user asks.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(settings): show the bundled open-source notices under About
body:
**What the user gets:** About lists the bundled open-source notices.
**Why it matters:** Openness pillar; the notices ship but users can't see them.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 4 (#1362) · order 47 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI |
| Effort | S |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | none found |
| Needs mock first | yes: a new About navigation flow; keep it native and compact. |
| Sources | design-settings-opus #8 |

## Problem
Hermex is open at the core and ships third-party code. Their license notices are bundled with the app, but no screen shows them, so users can't see what Hermex is built on or read its bundled license notices.

## What T3 does
About → **Open source licenses** (`apps/mobile/src/features/settings/SettingsOpenSourceLicensesRouteScreen.tsx`) is a searchable list of every bundled package; each pushes its license text.

## Hermex today
- `HermesMobile/Resources/ThirdPartyNotices/` holds 10 files: `NOTICE.txt` (an index), plus Highlightr, KeychainAccess, LDSwiftEventSource, Lucide icons, MarkdownUI, NetworkImage, Splash, SwiftMath (`*-LICENSE.txt`) and `swift-cmark-COPYING.txt` (170 lines; the rest are 13–40 lines).
- It is a **folder reference** in the main app's Resources phase only (`HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:422, 1146, 2465`; the phase `1A2B3C4D5E6F700000000060` belongs to target `HermesMobile`). At runtime it is `Bundle.main` → `ThirdPartyNotices/`.
- No Swift code reads it (`grep -rn ThirdPartyNotices HermesMobile --include=*.swift` is empty).
- `SettingsAboutPage` (`Features/Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift:4-58`) shows Version and Build, then Privacy Policy / Support / Report a Problem, then supporter, tip and Rate links.
- **`NOTICE.txt` has drifted from the lockfile.** `HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved` pins `swift-eventsource` **3.4.0** and `swift-cmark` **0.9.0**, but `NOTICE.txt:6,20` says 3.3.0 and 0.7.1. The other six versions match.

## Proposal
- Add an **Acknowledgements** `NavigationLink` as a new section at the end of `SettingsAboutPage` (`SettingsLabel`-style row, `systemImage: "doc.text"`).
- It pushes `SettingsAcknowledgementsPage`: a `List` of notices read once from `Bundle.main.urls(forResourcesWithExtension: "txt", subdirectory: "ThirdPartyNotices")`, sorted by display name, with `NOTICE.txt` excluded from the list.
- The display name comes from the filename (`MarkdownUI-LICENSE.txt` → "MarkdownUI"). Strip the `-LICENSE` / `-COPYING` suffix before display, then map "LucideIcons" to "Lucide icons". Use names only; parsing versions from a prose notice index is unnecessary.
- Each row pushes a page with the notice in a `ScrollView` → `Text(verbatim:)`, `.textSelection(.enabled)`, monospaced footnote, and the file's name as the title. The detail loads its text on demand; guard cancellation before committing state and show a local read error rather than an empty page. A `.task` is a lifetime hook, not inherently a background executor.
- No search: there are nine entries.
- Fix `NOTICE.txt`'s two stale versions in the same PR.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first.** Publish several static native list/detail treatments with `html-communication`, report the URL and stop for a pick.
2. Add `SettingsAcknowledgementsPage.swift` under `Features/Settings/` (list plus detail, around 60 lines). Name the model `AcknowledgementNotice { name, url }`, built by a static `loadAll(bundle:)` so a test can pass the main bundle.
3. Add the row to `SettingsAboutPage`. Add the strings "Acknowledgements" and the page title to `Localizable.xcstrings`. License text stays `verbatim` (never localized).
4. Update `NOTICE.txt` to `swift-eventsource 3.4.0` and `swift-cmark 0.9.0`.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** Settings → About Hermex only. Not reachable from deep links or intents, and doesn't need to be.
- **Targets:** main app only. The folder is already main-app-only, and the extensions don't need it. Tests: one model test.
- **Multi-server, reverse states, connection modes:** n/a (local, read-only).
- **Native quality:** Dynamic Type (text scales; the monospaced footnote uses a text style, not a fixed size); VoiceOver reads the row names, and long license text is one scrollable selectable element; light/dark via system colors. i18n: the row label and title only.
- **Docs:** none. Optionally note in `CONTRIBUTING.md` that a new dependency needs a notice file. The locked dependency list in `AGENTS.md` already gates new dependencies.

## Tests
One test in a new `SettingsAcknowledgementsTests`: `AcknowledgementNotice.loadAll(bundle: .main)` from the test host returns the expected bundled license set, excluding `NOTICE.txt`, and every URL reads non-empty text. Compare to the expected set of nine filenames: merely iterating whatever enumeration returns would let a missing file pass. This fails if the folder reference falls out of the target or a rename breaks loading, which users would notice as an empty page.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SettingsAcknowledgementsTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Settings → About Hermex shows an Acknowledgements row that pushes a list of nine notices.
- [ ] Each notice opens to its full, selectable text.
- [ ] `NOTICE.txt` versions match `Package.resolved`.
- [ ] No file is read until its page opens (the list reads only file names).

## Manual test plan
1. Open Settings → About Hermex → Acknowledgements: nine entries, sorted.
2. Open swift-cmark: long text scrolls smoothly, and you can select and copy a paragraph.
3. Set accessibility XXL text: the rows wrap, and the text scales.
4. Switch dark mode: legible.

## Out of scope
- Search, and license-type badges.
- Auto-generating notices from `Package.resolved`.

## Decisions
- Should a Linux tooling check keep `NOTICE.txt` in step with `Package.resolved`? Recommendation: not now. Dependencies are locked and rarely change, and a line in the dependency-update PR checklist is enough. Revisit if it drifts again.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): swipe between a message's images in the lightbox
body:
**What the user gets:** Swipe between a message's images in the lightbox.
**Why it matters:** Comparing several screenshots means close-tap-close today.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 48 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none (reuse existing server-bound preview loaders; this issue changes no wire contract) |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#145](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/145) (adjacent: inline MEDIA rendering), [#1133](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1133) (adjacent: MEDIA tile stuck loading; not the same cause), [#1030](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1030) (boundary: Hermes sent-attachment previews stay as they are) |
| Needs mock first | yes: gallery chrome/counter and page accessibility need an approved static design. |
| Sources | chat-timeline-opus #5 |

## Problem
An agent reply often carries several images: before/after screenshots, charts, a set of renders. A user message may carry several photos. The lightbox shows one image, so comparing them means close, tap the next thumbnail, close, tap again.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/messageImageGallery.ts` collects every image in a message (attachments plus markdown embeds) into one gallery. `FilePreview.ios.tsx:39-50` presents it at the tapped index. Natively it is a multi-item `QLPreviewController` (`modules/t3-native-controls/ios/T3NativeFilePresentation.swift:45-127`) with system swipe and a zoom-from-thumbnail transition.

## Hermex today
- `Features/Chat/ImageLightboxView.swift:59-237` displays one image; `ZoomableImageView` (`:275+`) supplies UIKit pinch/pan, double-tap, chrome toggle and fit-scale flick-dismiss. `ImageLightboxGesturePolicy` (`:15-56`) owns thresholds.
- `TranscriptMediaImageLightbox.swift:9-70` and `ChatAttachmentPreviewView.swift:275-320` each own one preview loader. `ChatView.swift:757-795,1173-1180` selects/presents single items. `ChatTranscriptView.swift:103,674,889` and `MessageBubbleView.swift:34` callbacks pass only the tapped reference.
- Hermes sent attachments with a host path open `BotArtifactPreview` (`ChatView.swift:775-784`), **not** the lightbox. Hermes raster reply images use the lightbox; documents keep the sheet (`:760-768`).
- Bot Chat also opens shared `ChatView` (`Features/Bots/BotsInboxView.swift:401`) with media loaders (`ChatView.swift:2036-2040`); the text-only Bot-transcript cache comment is stale for this path.

## Proposal
Keep Hermex's lightbox (its zoom and dismiss gestures beat QuickLook for images) and put a pager around its hosts.

- **Gallery value.** The tap callbacks gain the message's image siblings. Build the gallery at tap time, not on each streaming body pass; preserve order and deduplicate identical reference IDs before `ForEach`:
  - `onPreviewTranscriptMedia: (TranscriptMediaReference, [TranscriptMediaReference]) -> Void`. The row passes the raster references of the same message, in order, from the segments it already parsed, with the same filter `ChatView` applies: `isRasterImageCandidate && !isExtensionlessRemoteMediaCandidate`.
  - Attachments do the same with the message's image attachments.
  - `ChatView` stores `TranscriptImageGallery { items: [TranscriptMediaPreviewItem], startID }` (and the attachment equivalent) instead of a single item. One image is just a gallery of one, so there's a single code path.
- **Pager.** Add `ImageLightboxPager<Item: Identifiable, Page: View>` (new file next to `ImageLightboxView.swift`):
  - `ScrollView(.horizontal) { LazyHStack(spacing: 0) { ForEach(items) { page($0).containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal) } } }`, using `.scrollTargetBehavior(.paging)` and `.scrollPosition(id:)` seeded with `startID`.
  - Reuse each host's loader, retry and error handling, with explicit admission by selected index: only the selected page and optionally its immediate neighbours may start load/decode tasks. `LazyHStack` is not a guarantee about prefetch or retained view count. Cancel loads and release decoded full-size images outside this bounded window; guard late results by page identity and ownership. Keep Save/Export actions tied to the selected image and preserve the existing focus-restoration hooks. Reconcile with 06's visibility gating if it has landed.
  - **Zoom wins over paging:** hosts report `isZoomed` up (from `onZoomChange`), and the pager disables only its horizontal recognizer while the selected image is zoomed. Check nested UIKit pan/pinch arbitration: `.scrollDisabled` alone is not evidence that zoom, image pan and paging coexist. Vertical flick-dismiss stays fit-scale-only through `ImageLightboxGesturePolicy`; make the dismiss and page recognizers fail for the other direction.
- **Counter.** `ImageLightboxView` takes an optional `position: (index: Int, count: Int)?` and shows "2 of 4" in its top bar when `count > 1`. That's also the page's accessibility value.
- **Reduce Motion:** paging is user-driven scrolling, so there's no programmatic animation. The cover presentation is unchanged.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first:** publish distinct static counter/chrome treatments through `html-communication`, including error/accessibility states; report the URL and stop for a pick.
2. Add pure gallery selection/filtering and bounded-load-window policies. Build siblings on tap, not each stream tick.
3. Find every transcript/attachment preview callback via `rg` and thread sibling values through `MessageBubbleView`, `TranscriptMediaView` and composer callers. Preserve row value equality; new changing inputs must be compared.
4. Add the pager and explicit load/decode admission; thread selected-page zoom and position through both hosts. Switch the two image covers to galleries, preserving dismissal focus restoration.
5. Localize the position counter after reading `docs/agents/i18n.md`.

## Surfaces
Shared Sessions/Bot Chat, archived chats and local composer photos. Webui sent photos use the existing shared lightbox; Hermes host-path attachments keep `BotArtifactPreview`. App/tests only. Keep current server-bound loaders/cache namespace and cancel late page work on dismissal. Close/flick works from every page; failure/retry belongs to that page. Verify VoiceOver paging/selected-page-only focus (add an accessibility scroll action if needed), RTL, Dynamic Type and Reduce Motion; use the current dark full-bleed presentation.

## Tests
`ImageGalleryTests`: a message with three images and a PDF, tapping the second image, gives three items in order, starting at index 1, with the PDF excluded. Include duplicate references without duplicate IDs. A second policy assertion verifies that a ten-image gallery admits only the selected ±1 indices, not all ten; verify actual request/decode counts manually.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ImageGalleryTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tapping any image in a multi-image message opens at that image; swiping shows the others in message order.
- [ ] "N of M" shows only when M > 1.
- [ ] While zoomed, horizontal drags pan the image and don't page.
- [ ] Flick-down dismiss works on every page at fit scale.
- [ ] Opening/paging admits only the tapped image and at most its immediate neighbours; full-size decoded images outside that window are released.
- [ ] Save/Export, retry and focus restoration apply to the selected image; a failed neighbour cannot replace it.
- [ ] Single-image behavior is unchanged.

## Manual test plan
1. In one disposable session on an in-scope Hermes server, ask the agent to reply with three images (MEDIA lines or markdown images). Tap the middle one: "2 of 3", then swipe left and right.
2. Pinch to zoom, then drag horizontally: it pans, no page change. Double-tap out and swipe: it pages.
3. Flick down on page 3: dismisses.
4. In one disposable webui session, send two photos and tap one: the attachment gallery pages.
5. VoiceOver: a three-finger swipe changes page and reads "3 of 3".

## Out of scope
- Mixed galleries (attachments plus reply images in one pager).
- The zoom-from-thumbnail transition (`.matchedTransitionSource` / `.navigationTransition(.zoom)`). This is a possible follow-up; it needs a Reduce Motion fallback.
- Routing Hermes sent photos into the lightbox instead of `BotArtifactPreview`.

## Decisions
- Should Hermes sent image attachments open in the paging lightbox (with Save to Files and Share moved into its actions) instead of `BotArtifactPreview`? Recommendation: decide separately after this ships. It changes #1030's chosen behavior, and the agent-reply case is where multi-image galleries mostly happen.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: bundled into the batch's merge-walk test session.

title: feat(chat): fold a scheduled task's host prompt into a "Scheduled task" card
body:
**What the user gets:** A scheduled task's run opens on a compact "Scheduled task" card instead of host boilerplate.
**Why it matters:** Cron runs currently open on ~1,000 characters of host instructions.
**Cost:** Small–Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 49 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UI |
| Effort | S–M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes behavior: the cron prompt the host stores as the run's first user row. Hint text verified at the pin; the stored row shape must be checked live (step 2). |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | none found (closest precedent: [#1140](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1140)'s delegation-completion card, the same "host-authored row is not a user bubble" pattern) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | chat-timeline-opus #6 |

## Problem
A scheduled task's run can bury its task text behind a long host instruction: "[IMPORTANT: You are running as a scheduled cron job. DELIVERY: … SILENT: … FAILURE: … RECURSION: …]". The generic 6-line fold can spend its preview on that boilerplate. Skill expansion is already collapsed on Hermes, but the cron hint remains in the rewritten instruction; the remaining problem is the hint, not uncollapsed skill bodies. Actual stored/displayed history still needs read-only confirmation before implementation.

## What T3 does
`ThreadAutomationMessageRow` (`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadFeed.tsx:1091-1203`, used at `:1555-1577`) replaces an automation-sent user message with a compact bubble: a calendar glyph, "Automation", the task title and a chevron. Expanding shows the full prompt. Its doc comment explains why: "Automation prompts are long, repeated runbooks; a folded bubble keeps them out of the way."

## Hermex today
**Pinned host construction verified** with base64-decoded read-only `gh api repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/contents/<path>?ref=ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`:
- `cron/scheduler_prompt.py:223-243,298-326`: `_CRON_HINT` has nested `[SILENT]` / `[CRON_FAILURE]`; no-skills prompts start with it. Skill blocks (and possibly a missing-skills notice) precede it (`:159-220`). `agent/skill_commands.py:64-77` appends hint + task after the skill-instruction lead-in.
- `cron/scheduler.py:1940,2496` passes the assembled prompt to the agent in a `cron_<job>_<timestamp>` session. This does not verify the live history's `display_content`.

**App:** `SessionSummary.isCronSession` (`Models/Session.swift:657-668`) drives list grouping. Hermes `ChatView` receives a placeholder `SessionSummary` with only a Profile (`ChatView.swift:501-506`), so `session.isCronSession` there cannot gate this card. User bubbles use a six-line fold (`Features/Chat/UserBubbleFoldPolicy.swift:11`). `HermesTranscriptHistory.swift:259,278-325` prefers `display_content` and rewrites expanded skill rows to `/skill <instruction>`, collapsing whitespace. It removes the skill body but **retains the hint in that instruction**. `ChatTranscriptView.swift:901-911` already routes host markers and delegation completions to cards.

## Proposal
Recognize the **remaining displayed hint**, rather than reimplementing skill extraction or claiming to recover raw text the history mapper already discarded.

- Add a pure failable `CronRunPrompt(message:)`, gated by Hermes server kind and a known `cron_` stored target/root. Derive that context from `ConversationTarget.session(profile:key:)` / attached `HermesConversation` identity, not `ChatView.session`'s empty placeholder. Pass the stable Boolean through transcript value inputs/equality; unknown provenance falls back to the bubble. Ordinary messages and webui remain as today.
- Parse `ChatMessage.content`, which is already the app's display projection. Support a hint at the start, or after the leading slash-skill command(s) produced by `HermesTranscriptHistory.skillInvocation`. Do not search arbitrarily inside a user's quoted example or inside raw skill bodies. Scan bracket depth from the exact opener to its matching `]`, accounting for `[SILENT]` / `[CRON_FAILURE]`. Expose optional skill labels, the body after the hint and the unchanged input content. Missing/unbalanced/unknown formats fall back to the existing bubble.
- Add `CronRunPromptCard` to the host-authored-row chain in `ChatTranscriptView.swift:901-911`. Collapsed: static calendar glyph, “Scheduled task”, optional skill label and disclosure. Expanded: the body with line breaks as received, using normal user-text styling. Keep notepad/script/context text; do not guess which part is the task itself.
- Copy returns the unchanged **app-visible input**, including its hint. On the skill path that input is already whitespace-collapsed; byte-for-byte raw host prompt recovery is out of scope. The new card must supply its own Copy affordance because it bypasses the normal bubble/meta actions.
- Use a generic title, not the chat title as a supposedly verified job name. Do not add job lookup or new persisted metadata. If the host already supplies clean `display_content`, keep displaying it; do not dig into hidden raw content just to force a card.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks first.** Publish distinct static collapsed/expanded treatments with `html-communication`, with/without a skill, long body, light/dark and accessibility size; report the URL and stop for a pick.
2. **Verify stored and displayed rows (read-only).** With an explicitly in-scope host, inspect an existing plain cron run and a skill run via the history route already defined by `HermesREST`, then trace `HermesTranscriptHistory`. Record which hint actually reaches `ChatMessage.content`. Do not create/run a scheduled task. If neither path exposes boilerplate, stop and recommend dropping this issue. The pin verifies prompt construction, not the live host's display projection.
3. Expose cron provenance from the coordinator/target, then add the parser/card and context through `ChatView` → transcript → row. Keep `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.==` aligned. Do not rebuild the skill parser.
4. Put the card's labels and expand/collapse/Copy accessibility copy in `Localizable.xcstrings` after reading `docs/agents/i18n.md`.

## Surfaces
Hermes cron chats reached through Tasks, scheduled sessions, search or deep links share the transcript. Main app/tests only; no server state or persistence. Expand/collapse and Copy remain reachable with VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and light/dark. Invoke `ChatDisclosureToggleAction` before disclosure layout changes; respect Reduce Motion. Per-session classification is stateless; webui feature work is out of scope.

## Tests
`CronRunPromptTests`: one fixture-driven behavior test covers both the pinned no-skills hint and the actual Hermes-normalized `/skill <hint> <instruction>` form, proving nested token handling and preservation of input for Copy. Include ordinary/non-cron and unbalanced inputs as fallbacks. Assert a `.session` target with a cron key supplies provenance despite the placeholder `SessionSummary`; an ordinary target does not. A new `HermesTranscriptHistoryTests` behavior test should feed a raw expanded cron skill row through history mapping and parsing so the existing normalization cannot make the new classifier unreachable. Do not assert exact localized copy.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/CronRunPromptTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesTranscriptHistoryTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatMarkerMessageClassifierTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A verified Hermes cron prompt with a recognized displayed hint shows the collapsed card; clean display content and unsupported formats keep the existing presentation.
- [ ] Expanding shows the job's own text; the hint never appears in the expanded body.
- [ ] Copy yields the exact input `ChatMessage.content`, retaining the hint and existing skill normalization.
- [ ] Skill jobs on a Hermes server show the skill name and the job text, with no inline hint.
- [ ] A message without the opener, or with an unbalanced hint, renders exactly as today.

## Manual test plan
Open existing plain and skill Task Runs on an in-scope Hermes host; verify collapsed label, expansion, and Copy preserving app-visible input. Check clean-display and ordinary chats remain unchanged, plus accessibility text size and disclosure scroll stability.

## Out of scope
- An "Open task" link and a job-name lookup.
- Hiding notepad or script-output blocks inside the body.
- Changing how the session list titles cron runs.
- Raw prompt recovery, additional metadata/cache fields, complete raw skill-scaffold parsing and webui feature work.

## Decisions
- Should the card show the run's time ("Ran 9:00 AM")? Recommendation: no. The bubble's existing meta row already shows the timestamp.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: fix(chat): keep the reader's place when the transcript rewraps
body:
**What the user gets:** Your reading place survives rotation, Split View and text-size changes.
**Why it matters:** Rewrapping moves the reader to a different line today (reproduce first).
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 5 (#1363) · order 50 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | reliability / UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1292](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1292) (adjacent only: labelled wontfix and "filed for later"; **do not reopen or pick it up**, see Hermex today), [#1068](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1068) (adjacent: Bot Chat at accessibility sizes) |
| Needs mock first | no (behavior only, no new UI) |
| Sources | chat-timeline-opus #7, chat-timeline-sol #5, performance-eng-opus #5 |

## Problem
A reader halfway up a long reply rotates the phone, resizes Hermex in iPad Split View or Stage Manager, or changes text size. When the effective text width or text size changes, rows may rewrap while the preserved raw offset no longer identifies the same passage. Full-width iPad layouts already wider than the reading cap need not rewrap. **This is inferred from code and has not been reproduced yet.** Step 1 is to reproduce it, and if it doesn't reproduce, close this out.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/thread-feed-live-follow.ts:125-167` captures row identity and an offset fraction, then restores that fraction after measurement. Following keeps the end. `ThreadFeed.tsx:2839-2898,3110-3127` arms reflow for width/text-size changes and cancels on deliberate navigation. This is an approximate row-relative anchor, not a text-selection anchor.

## Hermex today
- `ChatScrollPositionController` (`Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptSupportingViews.swift:393-399`) has `hold` (raw offset) and `prepend` (adds content-height growth). Neither preserves a fraction within a rewrapped row. `pinReader` (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:317-321`) handles disclosure toggles.
- Width and Dynamic Type are read (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:25,193-195`), with no explicit reflow handler. The size-change anchor is bottom only while following (`:209-215`; `ChatScrollPolicy.swift:33-38`); this absence alone does not prove native SwiftUI jumps.
- Rows use stable `renderID` (`:410`). `ChatReadingWidth.maximum = 768` (`:8-14`), so full-width iPad resizes above that cap do not rewrap. Real candidates are iPhone rotation, narrow iPad windows and text that actually scales (broadened by 04).
- [#1292](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1292) is explicitly deferred/wontfix and cites `readUpTo`, restore phases and v0.12.42 absent from this Hermex code. It is not implementation scope or evidence of this defect.

## Proposal
Only after reproduction, add transient row-relative reflow compensation to the existing controller. It approximates the reader's place within a row; a fraction is not an exact text/glyph anchor, especially for mixed markdown, code and images.

- **Capture cheaply and in the right layout epoch.** Keep a plain, non-observed frame store on `ChatScrollPositionController`, keyed by `renderID` and a layout signature (effective capped content width plus text-size inputs). The controller is not `@Observable`, so it does not need `@ObservationIgnored`. Measure rows outside the `.equatable()` boundary using `onGeometryChange` in one documented content coordinate space. Record its origin relative to UIKit scroll content; a content `VStack` origin is not automatically UIKit y=0.
- Retain the **last complete old-layout snapshot and reading offset** before accepting new-signature frames. `onChange(of: width/dynamicTypeSize)` is not guaranteed to run before row geometry callbacks. Merely reading a mutable “latest frames” dictionary there could capture already-reflowed geometry and silently do nothing. The implementation must establish old/new ordering explicitly; use a narrow layout bridge if that cannot be done reliably with the existing observers.
- **Pure math in `ChatScrollPolicy`.** `ReflowAnchor { renderID, fractionWithinRow }` captures the row under a chosen viewport reading line. Normalize UIKit `contentOffset`, `adjustedContentInset.top` and content-origin offset into the same space as frames. Clamp fractions and offsets; reject zero-height/missing frames. Restore the same fraction of the new frame under that same viewport line.
- **Arm only when needed.** React to the effective column width (not a full-width iPad resize above 768 pt) or scaled text size. Following stays bottom-pinned; top stays top. User dragging/tracking/decelerating declines compensation. Freeze the old anchor while new frames arrive instead of repeatedly replacing it.
- **Restore with bounded ownership.** Extend the existing preservation machinery with `.reflow`, applying non-animated correction once the target's new frame is known and layout settles. Reuse `disclosureHoldQuietPeriod` and its maximum deadline, so streaming cannot hold it forever. Ensure correction does not turn the follow latch on or get misclassified as a deliberate scroll. User/VoiceOver/keyboard navigation, explicit follow, missing anchor, detach and a conflicting prepend/disclosure operation cancel reflow; do not silently let “newest arm wins” override an in-flight older-history capture. Keep SwiftUI's offset model/hit testing synchronized, not only the UIKit offset.

This applies to shared Sessions and Bot Chat `ChatTranscriptView`; Bot room transcripts are separate and out of scope. Keep frame updates non-observable and prune rows that leave the loaded transcript. No per-scroll observed dictionary writes.

## Implementation steps
1. **Reproduce first** on a signed Debug iPhone/iPad build: park a distinctive passage under the header; rotate, resize below 768 pt and change Dynamic Type on scaling text. Record before/after evidence. If none reproduces, stop and recommend dropping.
2. Establish coordinate conversion and old/new layout ordering for the reproduced case. Add anchor math to `ChatScrollPolicy` and ownership to `ChatScrollPositionController`; wire epoch-aware geometry in `ChatTranscriptView`.
3. Verify gesture cancellation, prepend/disclosure arbitration, follow behavior and hit testing. Update the controller doc comment.
4. Compare interleaved Release opening/streaming traces and settled-row counts. 41 fixes the normal-tick `Stream Batch Apply` gap; baseline forced-flush intervals alone are insufficient. Repeat the reproduced matrix.

## Surfaces
Shared Sessions/Bot Chat transcripts, Hermes/webui/archived, iPhone/iPad; app and tests only. State is controller-local and discarded on detach. Bot rooms and persisted reading state are excluded. Test concurrent hydration/prepend/disclosure; deliberate VoiceOver/keyboard/follow actions cancel compensation. Dynamic Type is a trigger; vertical math is RTL-independent but merits a manual check. Corrections are non-animated.

## Tests
`ChatScrollPolicyTests`:
1. `testReflowKeepsTheReadingLineAtTheSameShareOfItsRow`: given frames, the anchor is 40% into a row. After that row doubles in height and moves down, the restored offset puts the reading line at 40% of the new frame.
2. `testReflowAnchorIsNilAtTheTopAndWithoutARowUnderTheLine`.

Add one hosted/controller behavior test for the observed failure: old geometry/offset captured before a width change must restore against the new frame, and explicit user movement must cancel. Inject layout/settle completion; use expectations, not elapsed sleeps or polling. Pure arithmetic alone cannot catch capturing the new-layout frame as the old anchor.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatScrollPolicyTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reproduction evidence exists before implementation; otherwise stop.
- [ ] Reproduced reflows retain the same row and approximate passage, including mixed-content replies.
- [ ] Following stays at bottom; top stays top; above-cap width changes do not arm reflow.
- [ ] User navigation cancels without snap-back; prepend/disclosure ownership and hit testing remain correct.
- [ ] Interleaved timings/counts show no material regression.

## Manual test plan
Repeat the recorded iPhone rotation, narrow iPad resize and scaling-text Dynamic Type cases. Include streaming while following and while reading history, immediate scroll after resize, VoiceOver scroll, Load Earlier and disclosure toggles. Confirm no snap-back or dead tap targets.

## Out of scope
- Persisted last-read restore across launches, and anything under #1292.
- Bot room transcripts.
- Changing `ChatReadingWidth.maximum`.

## Decisions
If only one trigger reproduces, recommend fixing that trigger through the shared anchor policy. Add other callbacks only when their behavior is reproduced; do not assume they are free.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: bundled into the batch's merge-walk test session.

title: feat(home): add a ⌘K quick switcher for sessions, bots and destinations
body:
**What the user gets:** ⌘K opens a quick switcher for sessions, bots and destinations.
**Why it matters:** One key reaches anything on iPad.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 51 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | no new API; catalog is local, but existing session-link resolution connects to the host |
| Depends on | #1365 |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1088](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1088) (adjacent: the session list redesign expects the numbered shortcuts to survive) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | navigation-opus #7, navigation-sol #2, composer-opus #9 |

## Problem
Hardware-keyboard users lack a quick way to jump between sessions, bots and utilities. Existing home commands are unwired on Hermes (01 fixes that); this issue adds a searchable navigation palette.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/keyboard/CommandPalette.tsx` and `commandPaletteItems.ts` mix recent threads and destinations, lower the open thread in recents, and mount lazily. `HardwareKeyboardCommandProvider.tsx` supplies the global command. Borrow the behavior, not React code.

## Hermex today
- `HermesMobile/HermesMobileApp.swift:4–12` defines `HermexSceneActions` (New Chat, Search, numbered and adjacent chat). `HermexCommands` (`:25–76`) binds ⌘N, ⌘F, ⌃Tab/⌘⇧[ ] and ⌘1–9, and turns every command off while `AppLock.shared.isLocked` (`:29–32`).
- The only `.focusedSceneValue(\.hermexSceneActions, …)` is in the legacy webui list, `Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift:470`. The Hermes home (`ContentView.swift:525` `HermesServerHome`, `HermesSessionListView`, `BotsInboxView`) publishes nothing. Issue #1365 fixes that, and this issue builds on it.
- Destinations: `SessionListUtilityDestination` (`SessionListView.swift:1802–1818`). On Hermes, `HermesSessionListView.open(_:)` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:457–474`) pushes Tasks/Skills/Memory/Insights for the listed Profile, and Kanban for the whole host. Settings is the home's `isShowingSettings` (`ContentView.swift:548`).
- Rows: the Sessions side's `SessionListViewModel` (`ContentView.swift:714–723`) and its multi-word filter (`SessionListViewModel.swift:358–359`, `searchableText` at `:1622`). Bots: `BotInbox.profiles` (`BotInbox.swift:159`).
- Routing already exists for links: `pendingSessionDestination: HermesSessionDestination` and `pendingBotDestination: BotDestination` (`ContentView.swift:530–531`). The home changes tabs and closes Settings (`:613–623`). A session link performs a live lookup (`HermesSessionListView.swift:667–679`); ordinary loaded-row opening (`:618–631`) can instead open cached content.

## Proposal
A sheet that only navigates: no actions with side effects in v1.

- `QuickSwitcherItem`: session destination, bot destination, utility or Settings. Snapshot loaded active-server rows/profiles on opening; use stable server/Profile/session identities. Respect visibility/readiness. Archived follows its existing availability (`HermesSessionListView.swift:184–185`) and needs an explicit `covers.showingArchived` route.
- Filter with the existing multi-word `contains` rule (lift `searchableText` into a small shared helper if needed, instead of a second matcher). An empty query shows recents (newest first, open chat last) plus destinations.
- Picks use the pending session/bot bindings. Dismiss via the sheet's completion before routing, and recheck active-server identity and app lock there. Session picks inherit the live lookup's offline behavior; this issue does not promise offline opening.
- Entry points: ⌘K in `HermexCommands` (an optional `openQuickSwitcher` action, nil on webui), plus a header menu item. Implement and verify ↑/↓ and Return explicitly on iPadOS; `List` selection alone does not establish this behavior while search owns focus. Keep global ⌘1–9 behavior unchanged.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for distinct searchable-sheet and centered-palette designs plus the phone entry point. Include no results, light/dark and large text. Publish the URL and wait for a pick.
2. Add `openQuickSwitcher` to `HermexSceneActions` and a ⌘K `Button` in `HermexCommands` (File menu, after Search Sessions).
3. Add `QuickSwitcherItem` and a pure `QuickSwitcherModel.items(sessions:bots:destinations:query:openSessionKey:)` in `Features/SessionList/`.
4. Add `QuickSwitcherSheet` with search, stable selected item identity, and keyboard movement/activation. Filtering resets an invalid selection; Return during marked-text composition must not navigate.
5. Present it from `HermesServerHome`, which owns both tabs, the Settings flag and the pending bindings. Wire the scene action that issue #1365 publishes.
6. Route sessions/bots via bindings. Utilities switch to Sessions and consume a pending navigation hook: reuse `open(_:)` for its supported cases and explicitly handle Archived. Close covering UI first. Settings uses `isShowingSettings`.
7. Strings go in the String Catalog. Update `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`'s home section with one sentence on ⌘K.

## Surfaces
- **Targets:** app and tests; extensions n/a. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before catalog edits; use Apple frameworks only.
- **Multi-server:** active server only. A server switch rebuilds the home (`ContentView` keys it by server), which dismisses the sheet. No cross-server catalog.
- **Connection modes:** catalog is local; session activation can fail offline through existing lookup.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver labels per row ("Session, <title>, <Profile>"), Dynamic Type, light/dark. No animation beyond the system sheet.
- **App lock:** command disabled while locked; the sheet must not present over the lock.

## Tests
- `QuickSwitcherModelTests`: an empty query orders recents with the open session last and lists only the destinations visibility allows; a multi-word query matches as the list search does.
- Test destination identity, utility routing from Bots and stale-pick rejection after a server switch (`HermesSessionListTests`). Verify keyboard focus/Return in a hosted test or manual pass.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/QuickSwitcherModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ⌘K opens the switcher on the Hermes home from either tab, and from an open chat at regular width.
- [ ] Typing filters sessions, bots and destinations. Return opens the selected one.
- [ ] Picking a session on the Bots tab turns the home to Sessions and opens it. Picking a bot does the reverse.
- [ ] Only the active server's items appear. Switching servers dismisses the sheet.
- [ ] Disabled while the app lock is up.
- [ ] Reachable without a keyboard from the header.

## Manual test plan
1. iPad simulator with a hardware keyboard on a Hermes server: press ⌘K, type part of a session title, press Return. The session opens.
2. From a chat on the Sessions tab, press ⌘K and pick a bot. The home switches to Bots and opens it.
3. Press ⌘K, pick Tasks. Tasks pushes for the listed Profile.
4. Dismiss, switch servers from the avatar, and reopen: only the new server appears. Cover a switch while dismissal is pending with the routing test; the underlying avatar may be inaccessible under a modal sheet.
5. Lock the app and confirm ⌘K does nothing.

## Out of scope
- Actions with side effects (New Chat in…, archive, model switch).
- Message-content search results inside the palette.
- Cross-server results.
- The legacy webui list.

## Decisions
- **Remote search?** Recommend loaded rows only; ⌘F remains the full search route.
- **Phone entry point?** Recommend a header menu item.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(live-activity): show concurrent runs in one attention-first card
body:
**What the user gets:** One attention-first Live Activity shows all concurrent runs.
**Why it matters:** Starting a second run hides the first run's approval today.
**Cost:** Large; needs the owner's hands on a physical iPhone.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 52 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | L |
| Server dependency | Local aggregate needs none, but loses background freshness. Fresh aggregates need new hermex-push support. Foreground priming would use `session.active_list`, verified read-only at pin `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2` |
| Depends on | #1371 (soft); coordinate with 34/35/36 widget layouts and [#1193](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1193) |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1191](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1191) (adjacent: push cleanup), [#1193](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1193) (overlapping main-actor activity reads), [#566](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/566) (adjacent: relay support) |
| Needs mock first | yes; maintainer must pick the background-freshness trade-off before implementation |
| Sources | system-surfaces-opus #2, system-surfaces-sol #2 and #5 |

## Problem
Starting a run in session B replaces bot A's Live Activity even while A keeps working. The Lock Screen loses A's progress and attention state. Work started outside the phone also gets no card; foreground priming is a separate follow-up.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/widgets/AgentActivity.tsx` renders bounded attention-first rows. `features/agent-awareness/remoteRegistration.ts` primes/reconciles one activity; `infra/relay/src/agentActivity/agentActivityAggregate.ts` builds it using readable titles. Hermex must preserve its privacy boundary.

## Hermex today
- `AgentLiveActivityManager` holds one activity and session/stream identity (`HermesMobile/LiveActivities/AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:181–198`). `requestOrUpdateActivity` reads `Activity.activities` on the main actor and ends every non-reusable activity (`:794–886`).
- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.drivenLiveActivity` checks the manager's `drivenSessionID` (`Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1467–1471`), so a displaced coordinator cannot update/end the replacement.
- Attributes describe one immutable session/bot/tap destination (`AgentRunActivityAttributes.swift:170–193`); dynamic state also describes one run, with explicit decoding/encoding (`:79–139`). Missing state identity falls back to immutable attributes (`:159–165`). Merely adding a property is insufficient with this custom Codable implementation.
- **Relay verified in local sibling `../hermex-push`:** `relay/src/coordinator.ts:91–92` keys registrations by device and session digest; `relay/src/apns.ts:94–114` sends complete `{v,status,tool,tool_calls,started_at,updated_at}` content state, and sends **end** for done/failed. It carries no aggregate rows or plaintext titles. A push can erase rows or end the whole aggregate.
- The app registers tokens through `observePush` and `PushActivityRegistrar` (`AgentLiveActivityManager.swift:1052–1109`, `Push/PushRegistrar.swift:491–548`). Retirement requests relay deletion; it cannot retract already-sent pushes. Cold launch settles leftovers (`ContentView.swift:35–44`), rather than creating cards from active work.

## Proposal
Start with the mock decision. Recommendation: retain per-run relay cards until aggregate relay support exists if background attention is required. A local aggregate is feasible only with explicit acceptance of stale background rows.

For the **local aggregate** choice:
- Key rows by server, Profile/canonical session and turn, keeping mutable push keys separate. Give start/update/stale/end APIs explicit row ownership; `drivenSessionID` alone cannot route updates.
- Put optional, tolerantly decoded/encoded rows in `ContentState`. Cap visible rows at three plus an omitted count and bound encoded bytes below ActivityKit's 4 KB limit. Titles stay on-device, no excerpts. Sort waiting → failed → working → done with a stable tie-break. Row links and card/island taps use server-qualified destinations from **state**, not the original immutable single-session target.
- **Use a fresh local-only activity with no push token when entering aggregate mode.** Retire/end the prior relay-backed activity; do not convert its token in place. This isolates in-flight updates/end pushes. When returning to one row, create a fresh single-run activity with that survivor's immutable attributes and existing registration path. Gate asynchronous transitions by generation and preserve push-retirement ordering.
- Multi-row state has a short stale date and an honest stale presentation. It updates while the app receives events; background approvals/completions cannot reorder/remove rows until foreground recovery. Single-run relay behavior stays intact.
- Finalize only the owned row; retain outcomes for the existing dismissal window, then remove them. End the card when empty. Respect dismissal for that turn. Avoid synchronous main-actor `Activity.activities` reads, coordinated with #1193.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for aggregate and per-run alternatives: Lock Screen/islands, 1/2/4 runs, stale state, light/dark/large text. Publish the URL; wait for a pick and explicit acceptance of aggregate background staleness.
2. Trace manager protocol/callers, cold-launch settlement, push key retirement and avatar cleanup before editing. `BotLiveActivity.writeAvatar` currently deletes every other avatar (`:30–39`); retain referenced files if the picked design uses multiple avatars.
3. Implement row ownership and policy, shared attributes Codable, safe activity-mode transitions and widget layouts. Preserve the prior 34/35/36 behavior. Update app/widget/test target membership; notification service and share extension need no change.
4. Verify lifecycle races and update `docs/agents/bots.md` Live Activity ownership/privacy and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` identity.
5. Record relay aggregation and foreground priming as follow-up requirements in the PR; do not mutate another repository or file issues without authorization.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points/servers:** bot and session coordinators, card/row/island taps, background/foreground and relaunch. Preserve webui's existing single-run behavior and define its interaction with Hermes cards; it must not accidentally erase owned Hermes rows.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver counts/row status, Dynamic Type, light/dark, all widget families, Reduce Motion. Static glyphs; read `docs/agents/i18n.md` for new strings. Apple frameworks only.
- **Reverse states:** finishing one run preserves the others; dismissal, sign-out/server removal and cold-launch cleanup cannot resurrect or misroute rows. A server switch preserves each row's server identity.

## Tests
Extend `LiveActivityTests` and `HermesChatLiveActivityTests`: concurrent row ownership, independent end, stable attention order/tap routing, compaction-key move, and generation-safe local-aggregate/single-run transitions. Exercise old relay payload decoding and late pushes against the retired activity identity. Use injected activity/registrar fakes and expectations, no sleeps.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatLiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests`; add any new policy class to the selection.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Starting B preserves A; ending A affects only A.
- [ ] Waiting rows sort first and every tap opens the correct server/session.
- [ ] Aggregate mode cannot receive a former single-run route's push or end.
- [ ] Background multi-row staleness is visible; foreground restores current rows.
- [ ] Single-run relay updates resume with the correct survivor's identity.
- [ ] Bounded state contains no excerpts; relay gains no plaintext titles.

## Manual test plan
On a paired physical iPhone, start long turns in A and B. While foregrounded, raise an approval in A and verify ordering/taps. Lock the phone: rows become stale; do not expect an approval or completion to update them in local aggregate mode. Foreground, confirm recovery, finish B and check single-run relay recovery for A. Switch servers and exercise both tap targets.

## Out of scope
Push-to-start, relay implementation and foreground priming. Priming's pinned `SessionActiveItem` / `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:1004–1015` lists process-local runtimes without Profile. Loaded-row uniqueness cannot prove host-wide ownership; a follow-up must resolve Profiles and handle deduplication/disappearance/dismissal. It cannot cover all gateway/cron work.

## Decisions
- **Aggregate now or preserve fresh per-run cards?** Recommend per-run cards until relay aggregation can preserve background attention. Pick before implementation; the local aggregate above is the bounded alternative if staleness is accepted.


## Outside reach

Phase 3 needs hermex-push relay changes (another repository) and is out of reach for a batch; implement phases 1–2 only.

Manual checks: Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the batch's single Branch TestFlight build).

title: perf(chat): keep transcript structure quiet while only the reply's text grows
body:
**What the user gets:** Streaming text no longer re-derives the whole transcript each tick.
**Why it matters:** Less main-thread work per reveal; measure with the render counter first.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 53 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none |
| Depends on | #1405 (measure first; this issue may close as "not worth it") |
| Related GitHub issues | [#3](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/3) (adjacent: ChatViewModel decomposition backlog), [#262](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/262) (adjacent: transcript rework; must not fight it) |
| Needs mock first | no |
| Sources | performance-eng-sol #3 |

## Problem
Reveal ticks that flush text replace one message and re-derive history-wide transcript state. The work grows with loaded history; its user-visible cost still needs measurement. Avoiding redundant work may reduce scroll hitching on long streaming sessions.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/state/use-thread-detail.ts` exposes `useQuietThreadStructure`; `packages/client-runtime/src/state/threadDetail.ts` preserves the prior structural projection for text-only replacements using the known changed index. Borrow bounded derivation, not its store architecture.

## Hermex today
- `ChatViewModel.messages` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:224–229`) calls `recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages()` from `didSet` on every assignment.
- The 50 ms reveal (`:722–724,967–982`) calls `flushAssistantTokens`, replacing the active message (`:7066–7081`).
- `recomputeDisplayedTranscriptMessages()` (`:362–383`) runs `reasoningDisplayGroups` over all messages (with `ReasoningCandidateCache`, `:8775`, which skips re-deriving unchanged rows but still walks them), `transcriptActivityAnchorIDs`, `transcriptMessages(from:)` (`:8519–8570`), an O(n) pass that calls `TranscriptTurnClassifier` per row and allocates a new array, and `recomputeCompressionReferenceCard()`.
- `displayedTranscriptMessages` is reassigned every tick with no equality guard, so its observers see a change even when only one row's text did.
- `ChatView.turnFolds(reasoningGroups:)` and `terminalReplyRenderIDs` (`ChatView.swift:2330–2363`) derive from the message arrays during body evaluation, so each tick reruns them too.
- Already good, and to be kept: `onlyRepliesChanged` (`ChatViewModel.swift:6092`) already skips the rewindable-ids pass on text-only ticks, and `displayedReasoningGroups` is reassigned only when it changed (`:369–372`).
- **Text can change structure:** reasoning extraction passes visible reply text into echo removal (`:8451–8480`, cache inputs at `:8781–8803`). Bubble eligibility and compaction also inspect message content (`ChatView.swift:2314–2319`, `ChatViewModel.swift:418–429`). Unchanged ids/counts are insufficient proof that these outputs are unchanged.

## Proposal
Measure, then add one fast path at the source.

1. **Measure with 41:** signpost recomputation over a scripted 500-row stream. If below ~1 ms/tick with no relevant hitch trace, record the numbers and close without a refactor.
2. **Conservative fast path.** The reveal path knows which row it replaced; use that information rather than a whole-array comparison. Eligibility must also prove that content-dependent presentation is unchanged. Initially fall back when the active row has reasoning or an archived reasoning group anchored to it, when its rendered/classifier eligibility changes (including empty → visible), or when compaction depends on it.
   - Patch the matching `TranscriptMessage`, preserving `loadedIndex`, `renderID` and `anchorID`. This still publishes new text; it does not make an array element independently observable.
   - Skip only derivations whose inputs were proved unchanged. Keep the full path for reasoning-echo removal and content-sensitive transitions.
   - Memoize folds/meta only if measurement warrants it. Their invalidation includes display settings (`foldsSettledTurns`, thinking/tool-card visibility), bubble eligibility, offsets, stream identity and run outcome, not just ids/counts. Do not move view settings into the model merely for a cache.
3. Every other mutation (history load or prepend, new rows, tool or reasoning changes, compaction, run start or end, interim and replayed replies) keeps the full recompute.

Use a synchronous private mutation helper with scoped suppression restored by `defer`; no suspension can occur while suppression is active. Preserve the observer's other work. Keep a separate active-reply observable model out of this slice unless measurements require it.

## Implementation steps
1. Run 41's benchmark and record ticks, recompute count and ms per tick at 100 and 500 rows, before any change. Stop here if the cost is negligible.
2. Add `streamingAssistantDisplayIndex` bookkeeping, invalidated by any full recompute.
3. Add the fast path in `flushAssistantTokens` for the existing-row branch only (`ChatViewModel.swift:7066`). The append branch stays on the full path.
4. If folds/meta remain material in the trace, cache them with the complete invalidation inputs above. Otherwise leave them alone.
5. Re-run the benchmark and record before/after numbers in the PR.
6. If #1406 exists, add the invariant "a text-only stream tick does not re-derive transcript structure", with the test that pins it.

## Surfaces
- **Targets:** app/tests, both backends; extensions unchanged.
- **Reverse states:** a cancelled, failed or interim reply must fall back to the full recompute. Test these.
- **Other surfaces:** local derivation only; no visual, network or server-state change.

## Tests
- `TranscriptDisplayModelTests` / `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests`: eligible ticks update the active row, preserve settled rows and skip history-wide work. Compare presented rows/groups with a from-scratch oracle after reasoning echo changes, first visible text, compaction and history prepend; correctness assertions are primary, counters secondary.
- A tool/reasoning chunk triggers the full path. Changing fold/card settings during a stream must immediately update folds/meta if cached.
- `TranscriptTurnFoldingTests`: folds after the reply settles equal folds computed from scratch.
- Use `ScriptedSSEStreamFixture` and expectations; no sleeps.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptDisplayModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptTurnFoldingTests --only HermesMobileTests/StreamingRevealGateTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Before/after benchmark numbers are in the PR (or on the issue, if closed as not worth it).
- [ ] Eligible text-only ticks skip full recomputation; content-sensitive ticks retain correct reasoning, rows and compaction.
- [ ] Every structural event still produces the same transcript as a from-scratch derivation.
- [ ] No visible change in streaming, folding, menus or end-of-turn metadata on webui or Hermes.

## Manual test plan
1. Open a long Hermes session and load two older pages. Send a prompt that produces a long reply with a tool call midway. Streaming looks the same, and the tool card appears at the right place.
2. Repeat on a webui server.
3. Cancel a reply mid-stream. The transcript settles correctly, and Regenerate/Edit menus are right.
4. With `--hitch-meter`, scroll during streaming before and after the change and compare.

## Out of scope
- A ChatViewModel decomposition (#3).
- Transcript redesign (#262).
- Per-row Markdown parsing cost (covered by other issues).

## Decisions
- **Proceed?** Recommend only for ~1 ms/tick at 500 rows or a relevant hitch trace.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: fix(composer): insert dictation at the caret and never overwrite later typing
body:
**What the user gets:** Dictation inserts at the caret and never overwrites typing done meanwhile.
**Why it matters:** Confirmed in code: dictation appends at the end and can overwrite edits.
**Cost:** Medium; needs the owner's hands on a physical iPhone.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 54 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | none. Server recognition keeps using the existing transcribe path (`ComposerVoiceInputController.transcribe`) |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#271](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/271) (adjacent: voice-first mode must reuse the same insertion policy), [#1066](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1066) (not this: third-party keyboard dictation), [#1107](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1107) (not this: iOS keyboard dictation crash) |
| Needs mock first | yes (stale-result copy in the existing voice-status surface) |
| Sources | composer-sol #3 |

## Problem
Mic dictation appends at the end, ignoring the caret/selection. Updates rebuild from the start draft, so later typing can be overwritten by partial or delayed server results. Fix selection replacement and reject stale writes.

## What T3 does
`packages/client-runtime/src/voice-input/controller.ts:69–117` replaces the captured selection and rejects changed owner/text/revision. `apps/mobile/src/features/voice-input/useVoiceInputController.ts` supplies selection and mounted ownership.

## Hermex today
- `ChatComposerView.toggleVoiceInput()` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift:1553–1559`) passes only `draftMessage` and an `editDraft` closure. The caret (`composerSelection`, `:319`, an NSRange in UTF-16 with `revision` and `publishGeneration`, `ComposerTextEditing.swift:9–24`) is not passed.
- `ComposerVoiceInputController.start` stores the base draft (`ComposerVoiceInputController.swift:221`). `ComposerVoiceDraftUpdateSession` (`:1113–1136`) only knows whether updates are still accepted.
- `ComposerVoiceDraftComposer.composedDraft` (`:1097–1111`) trims the whole base draft at both ends and returns `"<base> <transcript>"`.
- Three writers apply it: local partials (`handleRecognition`, `:739–744`), the server result (`:530–533`) and the on-device file fallback (`:605–607`). Each one overwrites the current draft with base + transcript.
- The editor remains editable (`ChatComposerView.swift:348–350,968`), allowing stale-base overwrites. This is source evidence; runtime reproduction remains outstanding.
- Kept as is: start IDs, `captureOwner` arbitration, suspend/resume and teardown (`:207–232`), plus stopping on session change and disappear (`ChatComposerView.swift:742`, `:926`).

## Proposal
Make the update session own a **range**, not a base string.

- Capture owner, validated UTF-16 range and **user-edit revision**. `ComposerSelection.revision` counts deliberate caret placement; `publishGeneration` dates editor publications (`ComposerTextEditing.swift:3–22`). Neither alone distinguishes voice writes from user edits. Include edit-then-undo to identical text.
- Track the dictation-owned range, initially the selection. Each result returns text/caret or nil:
  - If owner, user-edit revision, current text and range remain valid, replace the owned span, update it (including inserted spacing), and return the caret after the dictated text.
  - Otherwise stop accepting updates and leave the draft/selection untouched. A delayed server result never moves to a newly selected caret automatically. Surface a short explanation through existing `errorMessage`/`voiceStatus` (`ChatComposerView.swift:1375–1380`); an Insert/recovery control is a separate design decision.
- Preserve surrounding whitespace and punctuation; trim only the transcript. Add boundary spaces only for ordinary separated words, avoiding extra spaces before punctuation and around Japanese/Chinese text. Use a bounded, tested boundary policy, not a general script-detection subsystem or an assumed server transcript locale.
- The composer passes `composerSelection` and applies the returned caret with `composerSelection.moved(to:)`, as slash completion already does (`ChatComposerView.swift:458–460`).

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks.** Use `html-communication` for distinct static variants of the stale-edit explanation in the existing voice-status line. Publish the URL and wait for a pick before changing copy/UI.
2. Extend `ComposerVoiceDraftUpdateSession` and its pure range replacement policy. Change `toggle`/`scheduleToggle` to receive selection and a live owner/text/user-revision snapshot at commit time, plus an update closure returning text and selection. Reject invalid UTF-16/chip boundaries and active marked-text composition before committing. Wire manual-edit invalidation without counting voice writes as manual edits.
3. Update the three writers (`:531`, `:605`, `:742`) to use the new session.
4. In `ChatComposerView`, pass the selection and apply the returned caret.
5. Strings for the stale-result notice go in the String Catalog.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points/targets:** shared Hermes/webui composer mic and New Chat with Voice (`ChatComposerView.swift:1544`); app/tests, extensions unchanged.
- **Reverse states:** keep the minimal-edit bridge (`ComposerTextEdit`, `ComposerTextEditing.swift:62–103`) and open undo groups intact. Cover the dictation undo fix in [PR #1304](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1304); this issue does not redesign undo grouping.
- **Native quality:** `ComposerMarkedText` allows deliberate replacements, so it alone does not reject a voice write during IME composition. Expose/check actual marked-text ownership. Preserve RTL, emoji and chip boundaries. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` for the status copy; no new dependencies or animations.

## Tests
- `ComposerVoiceDraftComposerTests`:
  - Inserting into the middle with a selection replaces it and puts the caret after it, adding a space on each side only where needed.
  - Partial updates replace only the owned range.
  - An edit after start makes later partials return nil.
  - A late server result after an edit is not written over the edit.
- Cover edit-then-undo, IME marked text, invalidated owner and emoji/chip boundary rejection at the editor layer. Retain `ComposerUndoTests` when changing the bridge.
- `ComposerVoiceInputServerRecordingTests`: a server transcript arriving after the draft changed leaves the user's text intact.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerVoiceDraftComposerTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerVoiceInputServerRecordingTests --only HermesMobileTests/ComposerUndoTests`; include a focused hosted editor test if the bridge changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the caret mid-draft, dictation inserts there and leaves the caret after the inserted text.
- [ ] With text selected, dictation replaces the selection.
- [ ] Typing during dictation is never overwritten by a later partial or server result.
- [ ] An empty draft still gets the bare transcript, with no stray spaces.
- [ ] Existing suspend, resume, lock and session-change behavior is unchanged.

## Manual test plan
1. Type "Fix the bug in the parser and add tests". Put the caret after "parser", tap the mic and say "for nested lists". The result reads "…parser for nested lists and add tests".
2. Select "the bug" and dictate "the crash". It is replaced.
3. With server STT on, dictate, tap stop, then type before the result returns. The draft and caret stay as edited and the picked explanation appears. Use a physical device for real mic recognition; script delayed server results in tests.
4. Repeat 1 with a Japanese keyboard and Japanese speech. No spaces are added.

## Out of scope
- Keeping dictation alive across navigation (composer-opus #7).
- Third-party keyboard dictation (#1066) and the iOS keyboard dictation crash (#1107).
- Voice-first mode (#271).

## Decisions
- **Recover stale transcripts?** Recommend rejection with status explanation. Retained text with explicit Insert needs a separate UI pick.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: Device: physical iPhone (bundled into the batch's single Branch TestFlight build).

title: feat(composer): show which attachment is uploading and which one failed
body:
**What the user gets:** Attachment tiles show which file is uploading and which failed.
**Why it matters:** Long sends over tunnels are opaque and failures don't name the file.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 55 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing image-upload HTTP and `file.attach` RPC, already used; verified read-only at pin `ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2`: `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:330–359` and `gateway-contract.openrpc.json` `FileAttachParams`. No new contract |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1089](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1089) (adjacent: Chat screen design-system migration touches the same strip; coordinate styling) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | composer-sol #7 |

## Problem
Hermes sends upload every file before submitting the prompt. One busy line hides the current file/count; generic transport failures identify no attachment to remove or retry.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/components/ComposerAttachmentStrip.tsx` shows per-file transfer state; `src/lib/composerAttachmentUploadQueue.ts` keys it by environment/attachment. Borrow file identity and phases; keep Hermex upload-on-send.

## Hermex today
- A Hermes session stages local copies only and uploads on Send or Queue (`ChatAttachmentCoordinator.swift:53–56`). A webui session uploads each file as it is staged.
- `ChatAttachmentCoordinator.outgoingAttachments(_:)` (`:246–257`) maps `PendingAttachment` to `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.OutgoingAttachment`, which has **no id** (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:432–437`).
- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.upload(_:runtime:attempt:)` (`:512–553`) uploads serially. Images go through `uploadImage` (an HTTP POST with a base64 data-URL JSON body, `BotAttachmentUpload.swift:58–69`). Documents go through `file.attach`, a gateway RPC carrying base64 (`:90`). The method exposes one flag, `isUploadingAttachments` (`:440`, `:546–547`). The first failure stops the whole send, and nothing is submitted.
- The UI reads that flag through `ChatViewModel.isSendingAttachments` / `isUploadingAttachment` (`ChatViewModel.swift:531–533`). The composer status shows "Uploading attachment..." with Cancel (`ChatComposerView.swift:1340–1341`). On failure the message names no file (`ChatViewModel.uploadFailureMessage`, `:3232–3238`).
- `ComposerAttachmentStripView` (`ChatComposerAttachmentStripView.swift:8–38`) has preview and remove, and no transfer state.

## Proposal
Keep upload-on-send, serial order, and "all files before the prompt". Report **phases, not percentages**.

- Add `id: UUID` (the `PendingAttachment.id`) to `OutgoingAttachment`.
- Publish `AttachmentTransfer?`: ordered ids, current id/phase (reading local data, then uploading), completed ids and failed id. Preserve underlying error classification: `BotAttachmentFailure` does not cover transport failures. Publish phase boundaries only.
- **Composer status:** "Uploading 2 of 4 · report.pdf" with Cancel. On failure: "Couldn't upload report.pdf. Remove it or try again." with the existing kept draft.
- **Tiles:** static phase glyph, completed check, failed exclamation. Failure persists until removal or the next Send.
- **No percentage:** current transports expose no byte progress. This issue adds phase boundaries only.
- Retry is the existing Send: it re-runs the whole set. Files the host already stored are uploaded again, which matches today's behavior (`:516` comment). No partial-upload cache across runtimes.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for distinct badge/overlay designs in strip and collapsed pill, including a fourth-file failure, uploading, cancelled and done states, light/dark and large text. Publish the URL and wait for a pick.
2. Add `id` to `OutgoingAttachment` and pass it in `outgoingAttachments(_:)`.
3. Publish transfer phases in `upload(...)`, with a unique upload owner plus captured attach generation. Guard every write after an await, including completion/failure/defer cleanup: an old task must not repaint or clear a newer upload. Set the failed id for genuine errors; cancellation and `.stale` clear marks and keep today's cancelled outcome. On attachment edits, discard an irrelevant failed mark without losing the active upload's captured file ownership.
4. `ChatViewModel` exposes `attachmentTransfer` (Hermes only; webui returns nil and keeps its current behavior). Make `uploadFailureMessage` take the failed file's name.
5. `ComposerAttachmentStripView` and `ComposerAttachmentPillPreview` take per-id marks (`.waiting/.preparing/.uploading/.done/.failed`) with stable attachment identity. Passing values alone does not guarantee isolated body evaluations; use 41's counters if needed. If a failed/current file is beyond the pill's three visible tiles, its summary still identifies it and opening the strip reveals its mark.
6. Localize count/filename status in the String Catalog.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** Send/Queue, including shared files.
- **Targets:** app and tests. Share-extension staging and other extensions are unchanged. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` before String Catalog changes; Apple frameworks only.
- **Multi-server:** per-chat/attach state clears on owner change.
- **Reverse states:** Cancel stops the upload and clears the marks; removing the failed file clears its badge; a new Send resets everything.
- **Connection modes:** most useful over a tunnel; a reattach mid-upload already throws stale, so show the cancelled state, not failed.
- **Native quality:** accessible phase labels, filenames and Dynamic Type; light/dark badge contrast. Status changes only at phase boundaries. Static glyphs; any optional transition respects Reduce Motion through existing `ChatMotion` helpers.

## Tests
- `HermesChatAttachmentTests` (or `BotAttachmentSendingTests`): with a scripted wire where file 2 of 3 fails, `attachmentTransfer` ends with files 1 completed, 2 failed (by id), 3 never started, and no prompt submitted.
- A cancel mid-upload leaves no failed mark.
- A failed attachment remains identifiable by id/name, including file 4 beyond the collapsed pill. Verify filename copy manually; avoid tests of editorial copy.
- An old upload completing after reattach/new upload cannot change the newer transfer state. Script continuations/expectations, no sleeps.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatAttachmentTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotAttachmentSendingTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] While a Hermes send uploads, the composer says which file of how many is uploading.
- [ ] The tile of the file being uploaded is marked; done tiles show done.
- [ ] A failure names the file and marks its tile until removal or the next send.
- [ ] Cancel shows the cancelled message and no failure mark.
- [ ] No percentage or progress bar appears anywhere.
- [ ] webui sends behave as before.

## Manual test plan
1. On a Hermes server over the tunnel, stage 3 images and 1 PDF, and send. Watch "Uploading 1 of 4 · …" advance, and the tiles mark in order.
2. Refuse file 4 on local Hermes/scripted transport: its filename and badge remain, all draft files stay. A stale attach/cancel instead clears failure marks.
3. Cancel a multi-file send; check cancelled state and VoiceOver phase labels.

## Out of scope
- Byte-level progress.
- Parallel uploads.
- Upload-on-pick for Hermes.
- Retrying only the failed file.

## Decisions
- **Retry just the failed file?** Recommendation: no. Re-running the whole send keeps the "all files on one attach" contract simple, and already-stored files only cost bandwidth.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(chat): show a Hermes session's background processes, with output and Stop
body:
**What the user gets:** See a Hermes session's background processes, their output, and stop one.
**Why it matters:** The phone use of a terminal (is the dev server up?) without shell exposure.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.
