> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 56 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | existing Hermes API: `process.list` and `process.kill`, **verified at the pin `ca678285`** (see below). Not yet in `HermesCall` |
| Depends on | none |
| Related GitHub issues | none found. `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md:68` files `process.*` as "Subagents and processes, untriaged" |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | code-surfaces-opus #10 |

## Problem
Background commands have no phone inspection or Stop surface. Hermes already exposes a session-scoped process list and individual kill; use those instead of adding a terminal.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/terminal/ThreadTerminalRouteScreen.tsx` and `modules/t3-terminal` provide a PTY. Borrow process inspection/output access, not a shell.

## Hermex today
- `HermesCall.swift` has no process methods. Use the delegated-work pattern: `Features/Chat/HermesDelegatedWork.swift:121–215,273–326` owns connection/runtime/generation context, stale-read checks and confirmed writes; `ChatView.swift:1931–1943` renders its toolbar. Tests: `HermesDelegatedWorkTests`.
- `String.strippingANSIEscapes()` exists (`HermesMobile/Models/ANSIEscapes.swift:15`).
- `HermesGateway`'s `isCancellationSafe` and `timesOutLocally` lists (`HermesGateway.swift:452–474`) decide how a read behaves on cancel or timeout.

**Contract verified read-only via `gh api repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/contents/<path>?ref=ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2` (base64 decoded; not the local cache):**
- `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`:
  - `process.list` takes `ProcessListParams {session_id (required), profile?}` and returns `ProcessListResult {processes: [ProcessEntry]}`.
  - `ProcessEntry` requires only `session_id` (**the process id**). Optional display fields: command/cwd/status/uptime, preview/tail and exit metadata. Decode tolerantly; omit rows without usable identity.
  - `process.kill` takes `{session_id, process_id, profile?}`; result has status `killed|already_exited|not_found|error` plus optional output/error/exit metadata.
- Handler: `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:265–281`.
  - Both methods are `live_session=True`, so `session_id` is the **attached runtime id**, resolved by `_sess`, not the stored key.
  - `process.list` returns processes whose `session_key` matches the runtime's, with `output_tail` set to the last 4,000 chars of the buffer (`tui_gateway/server.py:3219–3234`).
  - `process.kill` answers `4012` without `process_id` and `4044` when the process is not this session's. Failures use `5010`.
- `tools/process_registry.py:2308–2317` confirms `session_id: s.id`; `list_sessions` includes running **and recently finished** entries (`:2280–2295`). A refresh does not necessarily remove an exited row. Kill can return an `error` result while the process remains running (`:2124–2135`); never show successful Stop for that result.
- **Never call `process.stop`**: its handler calls registry `kill_all()` without an ownership filter (`methods_tools.py:249`, `tools/process_registry.py:2411–2425`). This is registry-wide across sessions, not a kill of all OS processes.
- No dedicated `process.*` event is declared. Recheck the pin; mutate pinned local Hermes, or disposable sessions on an explicitly authorized host.

## Proposal
`HermesBackgroundProcesses`, an `@MainActor @Observable` sibling of `HermesDelegatedWork`, owned by `HermesChatActivity` and connected at attach with the same `Context`.

- `HermesCall.processList(sessionID:)` and `.processKill(sessionID:processID:)`. Add `processList` to `isCancellationSafe` and `timesOutLocally`. `processKill` is neither (its outcome matters) and is never retried.
- Tolerant `HermesBackgroundProcess`: id from `session_id`, optional display/exit fields, ANSI-free bounded tail (fallback to `output_preview`). Keep a bounded row list and output allocation; unknown statuses are displayable but not stoppable.
- **Refresh:** on attach, when a turn ends, when the sheet opens, and on pull-to-refresh. No timer.
- **Entry:** toolbar while rows exist, with running count. Keep the sheet open when the last process exits; retain output, Refresh and empty/error states.
- **Sheet:** command/status/reported uptime, then an opt-in monospaced tail view reusing source-rendering primitives without a fabricated file path. Confirm Stop, bind confirmation to connection/runtime/generation/process identity and revalidate at dispatch. `killed`/`already_exited` show returned output/exit code; `not_found` or RPC `4044` refreshes; `error`/unknown status keeps the row and shows failure. No optimistic success or retry after a lost reply.
- `-32601` hides the feature using the connection's missing-method cache (`HermesGateway.swift:383–385`), not a new socket-lifetime cache. Reattach resets local context, not connection capability history.

## Implementation steps
1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for distinct toolbar/sheet designs, running/exited rows, tail and Stop confirmation, light/dark and large text. Publish the URL and wait for a pick.
2. Verify the pin, then use one disposable session on pinned `scripts/local-hermes`: start `sleep 600` through the agent, list it, kill that process only and clean up that session. Capture sanitized replies for the PR/tests.
3. Add the `HermesCall` cases and gateway classification. Add a fixture under `HermesMobileTests/Fixtures/HermesAgent/` captured from step 2 (sanitized).
4. Connect/disconnect `HermesBackgroundProcesses` beside delegated work (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1818–1822,1849–1852`); refresh at turn end.
5. Add the view and toolbar item in `ChatView` next to `delegatedWorkToolbarItem`.
6. Docs: move `process.list`/`process.kill` from untriaged to shipped in `hermes-feature-index.md`; add a short "Background processes" paragraph to `docs/agents/bots.md` next to delegated work, including the `process.stop` warning.

## Surfaces
- **Targets:** app, tests; other extensions n/a. No new dependency.
- **Multi-server:** bind context and every result to connection/runtime/attach generation.
- **Reverse states:** confirm Stop; show actual exit metadata when present.
- **Connection modes:** read times out locally and never drops the chat; a cached (offline) chat hides the button (`isViewingCachedData`).
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver command/status/uptime, Dynamic Type, light/dark tail legibility; static UI. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` for catalog changes.
- **webui:** n/a (Hermes only).

## Tests
- `HermesBackgroundProcessesTests` (copy the `HermesDelegatedWorkTests` harness):
  - Listed running and recently exited rows remain inspectable, including a row with missing optional metadata.
  - Kill sends `session_id` = the runtime and `process_id` = the entry's `session_id` (assert those two fields only).
  - `-32601` hides the feature.
  - A reply that arrives after a reattach is dropped.
  - A stale confirmation sends no kill; `error`/unknown results never produce success, and `4044` refreshes safely.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesBackgroundProcessesTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesDelegatedWorkTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesAgentFixtureTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A Hermes chat whose agent started a background command shows a Processes button with the count after the turn ends.
- [ ] The sheet lists command, status and uptime; a row shows the ANSI-free tail.
- [ ] Stop asks first, kills only that process, and shows the result.
- [ ] Hosts without the RPC show nothing and log no error toast.
- [ ] `process.stop` appears nowhere in the code.

## Manual test plan
1. On pinned `scripts/local-hermes`, in a disposable session, start a background command that prints a marker then runs `sleep 600`. After the turn, the Processes button counts one running process.
2. Open it and tap the row. The tail shows the server's log line.
3. Stop it and confirm. The row shows the returned outcome/output; refresh may retain the exited row. Clean up only this disposable session.
4. Open an offline cached copy of the chat. No button.

## Out of scope
- An interactive terminal or stdin write.
- Polling.
- `process.stop`.
- Processes across sessions or Profiles.

## Decisions
- **Placement?** Recommend one shared glass beside workers; decide from the mock.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: feat(share): choose a server and Profile before opening a shared draft
body:
**What the user gets:** Choose the server and Profile before a shared draft opens.
**Why it matters:** Multi-server users must switch servers before sharing today.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 57 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | UX |
| Effort | M |
| Server dependency | no new API; cached `HermesProfileNameCache` names plus existing active-home Profile discovery and new-chat routing |
| Depends on | [#1241](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1241), still OPEN when reviewed; its repeated-share repro must pass first |
| Related GitHub issues | [#1241](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1241) (blocker), [#311](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/311) (adjacent: content plus destination) |
| Needs mock first | yes |
| Sources | system-surfaces-opus #7, system-surfaces-sol #4 |

## Problem
A share opens on the active server. On Hermes it uses the Sessions list's New Session Profile. Someone with multiple servers or Profiles must arrange the destination before sharing; choosing it before draft transfer avoids copying private draft content between servers afterwards.

## What T3 does
`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/NewTaskRouteScreen.tsx` offers destinations; `features/sharing/incoming-share-inbox.ts` reserves content for one destination. `IncomingShareProvider.tsx` opens a draft without sending.

## Hermex today
- `SharedImportQueue` lives in `HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:282–368`. It reserves a share globally, with no destination; the active home's handlers receive it. `claim` removes it from pending while a draft move owns it (`:334–350`). `SharedImportGate` only changes when another queued share may open (`:508–514`); it does not bind the reservation to a server.
- `SharedImportReservation` has stable occurrence identity but no destination (`Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:55–66`).
- The Hermes home selects Sessions (`ContentView.swift:630–650`). `SharedImportReservation.hermesOpening` uses `profile: nil`, resolving the list's New Session Profile, and waits for `isLive` (`Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:830–838`). Draft transfer is atomic/idempotent by occurrence (`:841–858`).
- `HermesNewChatDestination.route` handles configured **Hermes** servers and returns switch/wait/open (`AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift:190–206`). It rejects webui, so it cannot be the webui routing path.
- `ProfileEntityProvider.sections` uses public status discovery plus cached names (`AppIntents/ProfileEntity.swift:112–150`); do not call it wholesale for this picker, as it also reads other servers. Cached Profile identities are server-qualified. webui's existing share opener is `SessionListView.openPendingSharedImportIfNeeded` (`:1450–1465`).

## Proposal
Keep one-destination sharing immediate. For multiple choices, present a main-app sheet **before any home receives or claims the share**.

- Build choices locally: saved Hermes connections with cached Profiles, using live names already held by the active home when available. Include a server-default choice when that host has no known Profile names; an empty cache must not hide the current destination or auto-route to another server. Deduplicate the resolved default/Profile choice. Keep each webui server as one destination using its existing default share route; no new webui Profile picker.
- Preselect the active server's New Session Profile, or its default placeholder until known. Keep a small app-owned pending-share record containing the original reservation plus `ShareDestination` (configured server identity and optional Profile). Keep destination state in `SharedImportQueue`, not in the shared extension payload. No destination URLs in UserDefaults.
- Same-server picks continue there. Other-server picks use `AuthManager.switchActiveServer`; Hermes follows `HermesNewChatDestination.route` semantics, webui its existing signed-in home route. Do not simultaneously send a separate New Chat request that races the share. The rebuilt matching home alone receives/claims it.
- Preserve the chosen destination through `claim`, `abandon` and foreground retries. A different active home cannot take it. Revalidate server/connection and Profile before transfer; a removed destination returns to choice/sign-in, never silently falls back to another Profile/server.
- Cancel releases the reservation without consuming it and suppresses automatic reopening until the next foreground or explicit Open Next. A failed transfer keeps existing recoverable/discard behavior. Nothing sends a prompt.

## Implementation steps
Prerequisite: confirm #1241 is fixed on the implementation base and rerun its repro; otherwise stop without adding routing work.

1. **Mocks:** use `html-communication` for sheet and pre-transfer inline variants, including uncached/offline hosts, cancellation, single destination and accessibility sizes. Publish the URL and wait for a pick.
2. Add app-only `ShareDestination` and pure choice/preselection policy using injected saved-connection availability and cached names. Preserve a default destination when metadata is absent; make zero destinations recoverable.
3. Extend `SharedImportQueue` with held destination/choice state. Gate both Hermes and webui pending-share delivery until selection is complete; maintain a single moving reservation and its destination across rebuilds.
4. Present the picked UI in `ContentView`; route by server kind. Use the chosen Profile in `hermesOpening` and verify it against live names before moving content. Revalidate at claim/dispatch, not just when rendering choices.
5. Update `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`'s home/share contract and `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`. If 37 added omission diagnostics, preserve those during transfer; keep atomic Hermes import behavior.

## Surfaces
- **Targets:** app and tests. Extension staging, widget and notification service unchanged; keep app-only policy outside shared target files.
- **Multi-server/reverse states:** reserve → choose → switch/sign in → claim → transfer → consume, or release/abandon. Destination remains attached until explicitly changed or released; cancellation keeps staged bytes queued. Consult the isolation doc before changes.
- **Native quality:** native accessible sheets, light/dark, Reduce Motion; Apple frameworks only. Read `docs/agents/i18n.md` for strings.

## Tests
`ShareDestinationPolicyTests`: choices/preselection when caches are absent, multiple Profiles exist, or a saved connection is unavailable. `SharedDraftStoreTests` already covers queue/move ownership: extend it for selection gating on both home kinds, chosen Profile/server, cancellation and abandon while switched. A late server-A callback cannot consume a reservation now held for B. Use controlled continuations, no sleeps.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ShareDestinationPolicyTests --only HermesMobileTests/SharedDraftStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One effective destination keeps today's immediate behavior, including an empty Profile cache.
- [ ] Multiple destinations show the picked UI with the active choice preselected.
- [ ] The draft is transferred once, exclusively to the chosen server/Profile; nothing is sent.
- [ ] Cancel/retry, sign-in, removed Profile and a switch during transfer retain recoverable content without cross-server fallback.
- [ ] #1241's repeated-share repro passes.

## Manual test plan
Share to a second Profile, then a second server; inspect composers without sending. Cancel and foreground again. Repeat offline/reconnect, two shares over a share-opened chat, an empty Profile cache and webui Open Next.

## Out of scope
Sharing into existing sessions, destination UI inside the extension, persisting the last pick, new webui Profile discovery, and partial Hermes imports.

## Decisions
- **Include webui destinations?** Recommend one existing default route per server because the shared queue already serves it; add no new webui-specific feature beyond routing this choice.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

Manual checks: bundled into the batch's merge-walk test session.

title: refactor(hermes): give the shared gateway one reconnect owner
body:
**What the user gets:** One reconnect owner per server replaces per-screen retry loops.
**Why it matters:** Consistent Reconnecting/Offline everywhere and one place for network reactions.
**Cost:** Large; simulator-testable.

> T3 adoption plan · batch 6 (#1364) · order 58 of 58. Drafted 2026-10-28 from paired Opus/Sol explorer reports and verified against `master` @ 5125b512; Sources below name those (local) reports.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | engineering / reliability |
| Effort | L |
| Server dependency | none new; preserve existing handshake, attach/replay and command contracts |
| Depends on | #1372; preserve #1374 and #1395 if landed |
| Needs mock first | no; scheduling/ownership refactor with existing UI |
| Sources | connection-state-opus #4 |

## Problem
The shared gateway has one socket-opening attempt, but the inbox, Sessions list and chat independently schedule recovery. A network return or foreground must wake several timers, and one screen can remain on its backoff while another has recovered. Centralizing socket retry can simplify this, provided screen-specific attach failures remain recoverable.

## What T3 does
`packages/client-runtime/src/connection/model.ts` defines per-environment phase/generation; `connection/supervisor.ts` owns retry/reset. Borrow ownership, not its broader supervisor or retry policy.

## Hermex today
- `HermesGateway` shares one opening attempt and handshake among `BotClient`s (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:4–27,93–103`). Concurrent retries already coalesce; this issue is not fixing simultaneous duplicate sockets.
- Its consumer list represents attachment, not durable demand: `end` clears consumers (`:418–440`), `leave` closes when the last leaves (`:106–121`), background closes silently (`:123–133`), and retire permanently rejects joins (`:145–150`). Required RPC deadlines can end just one screen, leaving the shared socket live (`:22–25`).
- Retry owners: `BotInbox.drop` closes its client and starts its 1/2/4/8/16/30-second loop (`Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:854–878`); `SessionListViewModel.dropHermes` does the same (`Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:2212–2229`; delays belong to `HermesSessionListSource` at `:81`); `HermesConversation.scheduleReconnect` retries attach from 1 to 30 seconds (`Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:549–570`).
- Conversation recovery includes session identity, resume, replay and live snapshot, with generation/held-frame guards (`HermesConversation.swift:114–170`). Its 4007/4009 resume-refusal window is 60 seconds (`:132–133,243–280`). `attach` is private (`:363`), so a gateway callback cannot simply call it without an explicit engine interface.
- Rooms/editor reopen on active; creators on their next Create (`HermesGateway.swift:9–10`). `HermesConnections.closeForBackground` closes the current gateway (`HermesConnection.swift:639–643`). The registry holds **one weak current connection**, keyed by active server/connection/configuration, not a dictionary of resident gateways (`:576–620`). A switch/replacement retires the old one.
- Kanban plugin sockets and webui SSE are independent transports.

## Proposal
Centralize **socket-connect scheduling**, keeping session state owned by its screen.

- Observable phase: idle, connecting(attempt), live(generation), waiting(deadline,failure), blocked(failure), retired. Preserve `BotConnectionAdvice` error detail, including URL errors. Transport readiness is separate from screen load/attach readiness; replay must settle before a chat appears live.
- Cancellable demand survives socket loss and recovery-time `BotClient.close()`. Suspend/disappear releases it; last release cancels retry/opening. Background pauses retry independently of callback ordering; retirement cancels permanently. Weak callbacks/explicit leases prevent retaining screens.
- With demand and an active app, one gateway task reconnects using today's 1/2/4/8/16/30-second delays. Preserve reset behavior; feed 08's validated network/probe wakeup and foreground through one generation-safe reset. Do not add jitter, a new stable-connection timer or path-based reachability blocking in this refactor.
- A demanded client joins each live generation once, including late subscriptions, then performs read-only recovery. Expose lifecycle through `BotTransport` for scripted tests; no root-body polling.
- **Keep screen-level recovery for failures on a healthy socket.** A list reload/required-RPC deadline or failed chat resume may need another read without a new socket generation. Preserve bounded/serialized read retry, including the chat's 60-second 4007/4009 window, and isolate permanent session failures from other consumers. Do not turn a session error into server-wide blocked state.
- Preserve command/upload dispatch and unknown outcomes. Recovery never resends prompts/answers/interrupts/settings or repeats a new session's `session.create` after a lost reply.

## Implementation steps
1. Map demand, transport callbacks and screen-read retry against existing tests; put the ownership sketch in the PR.
2. Add phase/demand and one cancellable scheduler to `HermesGateway`, with injected clock/delay. Preserve ticket/handshake ordering, opening coalescing and socket generation rejection. Adapt `BotClient`/`BotTransport` and fakes without requiring concrete-client casts.
3. Migrate Sessions, then inbox, then conversation: remove their **socket-connect** timers and retain explicitly scoped read/attach retry. Expose a generation-safe engine recovery entry point; prevent overlapping initial attach and live-edge recovery.
4. Preserve existing behavior for non-migrated rooms/editor/creators. Register demand only for opt-in consumers; a one-shot client does not gain permanent retry. Ensure both kinds coexist on the socket.
5. Update `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` shared-connection/reconnect contract and `docs/agents/bots.md` per-screen backoff descriptions. Keep 10's UI and 31's diagnostics accurate.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points/targets:** Hermes inbox/list/chats, share routing and foreground; app/tests. Extensions/webui/Kanban unchanged.
- **Multi-server:** read `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`; switch, sign-out, changed credentials/headers and retirement invalidate old demand, timers, callbacks and phase observations.
- **Reverse states:** release → idle, background → pause, Retry → reset, permanent failure → blocked, retire → terminal. Old callbacks cannot revive retired connections.
- **Connection modes:** localhost, Tailscale and tunnel; network move and quiet socket drop retain 08's verified behavior.
- **Native quality:** no UI, dependency or animation change; retry ticks must not redraw message bodies.

## Tests
Extend `HermesGatewayTests` for two consumers sharing one retry; cancellation/last release/background during delay or handshake; retirement/server switch; blocked failure; late subscription to live. Test mixed demanded and one-shot consumers.

`HermesConversationTests`, `BotInboxTests`, `HermesSessionListTests`: successful socket reconnect triggers one recovery per owner; a failed snapshot on a healthy socket still recovers; one session refusal cannot block another screen. Preserve 4007/4009 expiry and prompt/create unknown-outcome behavior. Use scripted sockets, injected delay/clock and expectations, no test sleeps/polling.

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesGatewayTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConversationTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotInboxTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests`; include changed caller suites. Full local suite only if shared test infrastructure, the Xcode project or Config changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Gateway owns one socket-connect retry schedule while demanded and foregrounded.
- [ ] Each screen becomes ready only after its own recovery; healthy-socket read failures still retry.
- [ ] Network/foreground resets cannot overlap opens or duplicate attach/replay.
- [ ] Last consumer, background and retirement cancel owned work; switching servers cannot revive old work.
- [ ] Commands are not resent and session-refusal behavior is preserved.

## Manual test plan
Use pinned local Hermes or a disposable session on an authorized host. With list/chat visible, restore the device network: one replacement socket, independently recovered screens. Repeat foreground, quiet tunnel drop, server switch during retry and #1241's repro. Script sign-in failures; leave live host credentials/tunnels alone.

## Out of scope
New connection UI, Kanban/webui transports, route upgrades, retry-policy tuning, and replaying commands.

## Decisions
- **Migrate other consumers now?** Recommend retaining their current lifecycle and opting them in separately after the three main screens are stable.


## Outside reach

None beyond read-only checks against the live host (standing grant) and read-only GitHub reads of the pinned hermes-agent source. No live-server writes, other repositories, push relay, or Apple portal changes.

title: fix(chat): queue a file-only draft mid-run instead of offering Stop
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1367

## What changed

On a Hermes session, a draft with only staged files showed Stop while a response was running, so the file could not be sent without cancelling the run.

Staged files now count as a draft mid-run: Send shows Queue under every Send While Responding default, offers no hold choices, and a tap or ⌘Return dispatches the behavior the glyph shows (one `onSend(behavior?)` callback replaces `onSend` and `onSendWithBehavior`). The file goes out as a queued `prompt.submit`, with no redirect or cancellation. Removing the files restores Stop. Text plus files keeps Queue / Stop and send from #1023; webui keeps Stop. A dimmed Send with a draft now tells VoiceOver what it is waiting on (sending, compressing, uploading, updating settings) through `ChatComposerSendBlock`, reusing existing localized strings.

Decision applied: [#1367 comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1367#issuecomment-6485586950) (D2, queue under every default).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatComposerSendGateTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatAttachmentTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests`: 52 passed, 0 failed.
- Red on the unchanged base: `testHermesFileOnlyDraftMidRunQueuesInsteadOfStop` failed (Stop shown), and `testAFileOnlyDraftMidRunQueuesUnderAStopAndSendDefault` failed (no Send behavior to dispatch).

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator

1. In a disposable Hermes session, start a long turn, stage a photo with no text, and under each Send While Responding default tap Queue (then repeat with ⌘Return on iPad): the run continues and the queued turn carries the photo. Repeat once from Bot Chat and from a share-extension handoff draft.
2. Remove the photo: Stop returns. Add text plus a photo: Queue and Stop and send are offered, and Stop and send leaves the photo staged.
3. On a webui server, a file-only draft mid-run still shows Stop.
4. With VoiceOver, focus Send while a photo uploads: it keeps its label and reads "Uploading attachment".

title: perf(chat): load transcript media only once it scrolls into view
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1370
Fixes #1155

## What changed

The transcript is an eager stack, so opening a chat started every image thumbnail, MEDIA probe, attachment and MEDIA audio clip, and link preview in its whole history at once.

A shared `loadsOnceVisible(id:admit:)` modifier now admits each media leaf's load the first time it intersects the transcript's scroll viewport, and latches per resource id, so scrolling away never cancels an admitted load. Media inside a settled reply's selection host follows the reply's visibility. Gated leaves: MEDIA image thumbnail and remote probe, attachment image, link preview, and `InlineAudioPlayerView` (attachment and MEDIA audio; a detached source still waits for its load key). Loaders, caches, contracts, and Open/Export are unchanged.

Decision applied: [D3 — both Hermes and webui leaves, closes #1155](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1370#issuecomment-6485587235).

Not claimed: #1133 (image loading symptom) was not reproduced here and is not claimed fixed. Link preview is gated but untested (`LPMetadataProvider` has no loader seam).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMediaVisibilityTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMarkdownImageTests` — 18 passed, 0 failed
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/AttachmentAudioDetectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptLinkPreviewTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatAttachmentTests --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests` — 56 passed, 0 failed
- Red on the base: `testOffscreenMediaWaitsUntilItScrollsIntoView` failed (`"1"` is not equal to `"0"`: `/u/far.png` loaded before it scrolled into view); `testDetachedAudioWaitsForItsLoadKeyAfterScrollingIn` failed (far image had already loaded at mount). `testScrollingAwayKeepsAnAdmittedLoadAndRemountRetries` pins no-cancel-on-scroll-away and retry-on-remount.
- Remote probe: `testOffscreenMediaWaitsUntilItScrollsIntoView` also asserts an extensionless remote MEDIA URL makes zero loads before scrolling and exactly one after (red with the gate reverted: `far-probe` loaded before it scrolled into view). Rerun: `TranscriptMediaVisibilityTests` + `ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests` — 5 passed, 0 failed.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, physical iPhone

iPhone simulator:
1. Open a long media-heavy chat (screenshots, MEDIA images, voice notes, a link preview): media near the bottom loads; older media loads only as you scroll up to it.
2. Scroll up to older media, then away and back: no duplicate loads, no flashing thumbnails.
3. Right after an older voice note scrolls in, play it and use Open/Export: both work.
4. In a webui chat with a link preview further up, scroll to it: the preview fills in once visible.

Physical iPhone (Cloudflare tunnel):
1. Open the same long media-heavy chat over the tunnel and compare request count and Session Open time with the current release: fewer requests at open, faster to usable.
2. Background the app during a Hermes chat, return so it detaches and reattaches: voice notes wait for the attach, then load once visible.

title: fix(chat): keep the composer editable while the chat is offline
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1375. Stacked on #1423.

## What changed

When a chat showed its offline cache, the composer locked completely, so you couldn't even write your next message. Now Sessions and Bot Chat stay editable offline: you can type and add quotes, and the draft survives a reopen through the existing `ChatDraftStore` path. Only delivery waits.

- A new `ChatComposerAccess` keeps "read-only" (true read-only sessions only, still fully locked, offline too) apart from "offline" (`showsOfflineCache`).
- Offline holds Send and keyboard send. The status line shows "Reconnect to send messages.", and VoiceOver reads it as Send's value through a new `ChatComposerSendBlock.offline`.
- Controls that need the host are held too, including callbacks from sheets that were already open: @file and host slash-argument completion, dictation, voice notes, the + menu, model/effort/fast/profile/workspace settings, and branch selection.
- Background @path chip lookups and the `/personality` and skill list loads also wait while offline, then run on reconnect (their task identities now include the offline state).
- Reconnecting lifts the hold and keeps the draft. Nothing sends on its own. The provisional cached copy shown while Hermes connects (#1258) is unchanged.

Decision: [build as written, hold all dictation](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1375#issuecomment-6485587946).

**Decisions made overnight**
- Stop keeps its own policy offline (disabled only while cancelling), as the issue asks. Alternative: keep Stop disabled offline, as before.
- A webui image/file paste offline gets through to `ChatAttachmentCoordinator`, which already refuses it with a reconnect error. Alternative: no-op paste callbacks for webui offline, which would drop the paste silently.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesOfflineCacheTests --only SessionIdentityTests --only SessionListMutationTests --only BotChatPresentationTests --only ChatComposerSendGateTests`: 141 passed, 0 failed.
- After the chip-lookup fix: `--only ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesChatTurnTests --only HermesOfflineCacheTests`: 305 passed, 0 failed.
- After the slash-list fix: `--only ChatViewModelSendTests --only HermesOfflineCacheTests`: 244 passed, 0 failed.
- Red on the base: `HermesOfflineCacheTests` failed with "Reconnect to send messages." (offline kept the composer read-only), and `BotChatPresentationTests.testOfflineComposerKeepsTheDraftEditableAndHoldsSend` found the editor not editable. Red on the first commit: `ChatViewModelSendTests.testAnOfflineDraftReferenceWaitsForTheReconnect` saw an offline `/api/list` for `a`. Red on the chip-lookup commit: `testOfflineSlashListsWaitForTheReconnect` saw offline `/api/personalities` and `/api/skills` requests.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator. Go offline by cutting the simulator's network; send nothing to the live host except step 5's one message to a disposable chat.

1. Open a disposable chat and go offline until the offline cache shows. Type text and add a quote, then leave the chat and reopen it. The draft is still there, and the status line says "Reconnect to send messages."
2. While offline, try Send, ⌘Return, the mic, the + menu, and the branch/workspace/model controls, including a picker you opened before going offline. Nothing sends or changes.
3. While offline, type `@<folder>/<file> `. No chip appears yet. Reconnect, and the chip appears with the draft unsent.
4. While offline, type `/personality `. The host gets no request. Reconnect, and the personality list fills.
5. After reconnecting, send once. Then check a read-only session (still locked offline) and Bot Chat (same behavior as steps 1-2). On iPad, repeat steps 1-2.

title: perf(bots): show the cached roster while the inbox connects
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1403

## What changed

Bots showed a skeleton until the gateway connected and `profiles.list` returned, which takes 1–2 s over a tunnel on every cold launch and server switch. Now `BotInbox.open` paints the last roster for that Bot connection from disk while it connects, and each live read replaces it.

- `BotRosterCache` (actor in `BotHistoryCache.swift`, reusing its `Scope`) stores raw `profiles.list` rows per server digest + connection UUID in Caches, atomic writes, ≤200 rows and 2 MiB; a miss or corrupt or oversized file loads as nil.
- Cached rows go through the live dedupe, use only in-memory avatars, carry no live statuses and keep the link at `.connecting`, so New chat and edits stay disabled. Taps navigate as today ([D6](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1403#issuecomment-6485588896)).
- After the load, `open` re-reads the saved record and stops unless it is the same connection. Only a rotated OAuth refresh token is tolerated, and the fresh record is used from there.
- Sign-out (Hermes and webui), server removal, a replaced or removed Bot connection, and webui Clear Offline Cache delete the file. Sign-out and removal delete it after the connection is retired, so a save from a read in flight can't recreate it.

With cached rows on screen, an unreachable host no longer swaps in the route-advice message (the same gate a dropped live roster already uses). #1374 owns that header. No on-device timing was taken.

**Decisions made overnight**
- `BotRosterCache` lives in `BotHistoryCache.swift`, so the Xcode project is unchanged (alt: its own file with app-target membership).
- webui Clear Offline Cache also clears the roster, matching history; Hermes Clear Offline Cache is unchanged (alt: clear both Bot caches from `SettingsServerPage`).

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/…`: BotInboxTests 56/56, AuthManagerStateTests 47/47, BotConnectionSetupTests 20/20, BotHistoryCacheTests 14/14. Red before each fix: no cached rows painted (`inbox settled` timed out); a replaced connection painted `from-a` and connected A (3 wire calls); sign-out/removal left a `late` roster on all three paths; a mid-load token rotation left the link `.idle`. The two tests that change the saved connection mid-load now make that change in a `willLoad` hook on `BotRosterCache` (a no-op in the app), between `open`'s read and re-read of the record, instead of relying on `Task.yield` ordering.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator

iPhone
1. Signed in to a Hermes server over the tunnel, open Bots and wait for the roster. Terminate and relaunch: Bots shows that roster at once, with no Working/Waiting badges and New chat disabled, then updates once connected.
2. [Needs a second server] Switch to the other server and back: each shows only its own bots.
3. Sign out of the Hermes server and sign in again: no old rows appear before the fresh roster.

iPad
1. Repeat iPhone step 1: the sidebar shows the cached roster, and tapping a cached row opens its chat (cached history, then it reconnects).

title: feat(chat): make hardware-keyboard sending truthful and complete
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1380. Stacked on #1425.

## What changed

With a hardware keyboard, ⌘↩ didn't match the Send circle. It had no truthful title, could fire while Send was blocked, and could send half-composed IME text. There was no way to send the other behavior or close a panel from the keyboard. Sessions and Bot Chat now match the circle:

- **⌘↩** works only while Send is enabled, never as Stop on an empty draft. Its ⌘-hold title is Send's VoiceOver label (Steer active response, Send after response, Stop and send, Send). Offline (#1375) and read-only chats get no send shortcut.
- **⌘⇧↩** sends the first send-choice card option that differs from the current behavior, excluding Stop and send, through `pickSendBehavior`. With files staged under Steer it isn't offered (#1023 preserved).
- **Esc** closes the send-choice card, then an open / or @ panel without touching the text. The panel reopens once the draft or caret moves. Otherwise, during a run, Esc stops through the usual Stop confirmation, and the draft stays.
- No shortcut (↑ recall included) fires while the editor is locked or has IME marked text. Bot rooms keep only their ⌘↩ Send Message. Return stays a newline.

Decision: [build as written; Return stays a newline](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1380#issuecomment-6485588207).

**Decisions made overnight**
- Esc's ⌘-overlay title reuses the existing "Close" key, or "Stop response" when Esc stops the run. Alternative: an untitled command the overlay hides, or a new "Dismiss suggestions" string.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only ComposerKeyboardCommandTests --only BotChatPresentationTests --only ChatComposerSendGateTests --only ComposerChipPresentationTests --only ComposerRecallTests --only ChatViewModelSendTests` on this head: 254 passed, 0 failed.
- Red on the base: `testSendKeysWaitForIMECompositionToFinish` failed (⌘↩ allowed and sent while marked text was set). The ⌘⇧↩ and Esc tests can't compile against the old API.
- Red on the first commit: `testEscapeClosesTheSlashPanelBeforeStoppingTheRun` failed after deleting and retyping `/` (Esc stopped the run because the panel stayed hidden).

## Manual test

Device: iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11, hardware keyboard).

1. In a Sessions chat during a run, hold ⌘ under the Steer default, then the Queue default. The titles match the Send circle's behavior and the alternate. ⌘⇧↩ sends the alternate. Repeat in Bot Chat.
2. Stage a file under the Steer default and hold ⌘. No ⌘⇧↩ entry appears.
3. Type `/` and press Esc: the panel closes and the text stays. Delete and retype `/`: the panel reopens. Esc twice more: it closes, then the usual Stop prompt appears.
4. With Japanese or Pinyin marked text, ⌘↩ and ⌘⇧↩ send nothing. Return still inserts a newline, and a Bot room's ⌘↩ still sends.

title: test: share observation waits and flag sleep-based test ordering in CI
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1404

## What changed

Tests waited on async work in 16 copied observation helpers and about 15 sleeps, deadline loops and `Task.yield` polls. These were slow and racy.

- One shared `@MainActor waitUntil` and a `CallCount` signal for actor doubles, in `HermesMobileTests/TestWaits.swift`, replace all 16 helpers.
- Kanban, Insights and CLI-sync doubles now signal their calls through expectations or `CallCount` instead of being polled. The Git toast, file browser, visibility handoff and dealloc races wait on explicit completion signals. The one production seam is `GitActionToastState`'s injectable `sleep`, which defaults to `Task.sleep` as before.
- `ci/check_test_waits.py` (standard library only) flags `Task.sleep`, `Thread.sleep`, `usleep`, `RunLoop.run`, deadline loops and `Task.yield` polling in tests, unless an adjacent `// test-wait: <reason>` explains the wait. It runs in the Linux Tooling Tests step, so it adds no simulator minutes. 13 real delays are annotated.

Decision applied: [D7](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1404#issuecomment-6485589144). The checker covers test support helpers, and intentional clock simulations carry a reason comment.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Shipped with one full-suite failure, `ComposerVoiceInputServerRecordingTests.testInterruptedRecordingRetainsClipUntilUnlockedAndTranscribesOnce` (idle-timer assertion). It fails the same way on unmodified master on this simulator, while [master CI is green](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/40782257588). The alternative was to stop the lane until it was fixed (adjacent #1170).
- The helper lives at `HermesMobileTests/TestWaits.swift` rather than `Support/ObservationWait.swift`. There is no Support group, and the file also holds `CallCount`. The checker scans all of `HermesMobileTests` either way.

## How it was tested

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_*.py'`: 15 tests OK (6 new checker tests).
- `python3 ci/check_test_waits.py`: 35 findings on unfixed master (red), 0 on this branch.
- Focused `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` for the Kanban (LiveUpdate, CardDetailState, FeatureState, CardEditorState), GitWorkspaceViewModel, FileBrowserViewModel, ChatViewModelStreamingPace, InsightsViewModel and CliSessionsSyncModel test classes: 227 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite (shared test infra and Xcode membership changed): 3581 passed, 1 failed. The failure is the master-reproduced idle-timer test above.
- Red evidence: the checker fails master at every site this issue names, e.g. `KanbanLiveUpdateTests.swift:630: Task.sleep`, `FileBrowserViewModelTests.swift:280: Thread.sleep`, `KanbanFeatureStateTests.swift:1721: Task.yield loop`. The Swift changes refactor existing tests, so they pass before and after this change.

## Manual test

Covered by tests; no manual check needed. App behavior does not change: this PR touches tests, `ci/`, the workflow and a default-preserving sleep seam in the Git toast.

title: fix(hermes): probe the gateway socket when the network changes
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1372

## What changed

**Problem:** after a Wi-Fi/cellular handover a gateway socket can go silent without closing, so the inbox, Sessions list, and rooms sit on a dead connection. Rooms never reconnected on their own.

**Fix:** on a network change, `HermesGateway.probe()` sends one `gateway.ping`. Any frame within 8 s keeps the socket; silence ends it once with `.transport`, and every attached screen shares one replacement ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1372#issuecomment-6485587712)). `HermesConnections.networkPathDidChange()` probes only a live gateway and never opens one. A shared `BotReconnectSchedule` replaces the inbox and list backoff, holds retries while offline, and retries at once when the network returns. Rooms get bounded recovery that reopens through the read path and never resends. Close, background, and leave cancel a waiting reconnect.

`gateway.ping` contract: `tui_gateway/ws.py:353` at hermes-agent `ca678285`.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Left the offline advice copy unchanged (not in acceptance; #1374 owns the reconnect UI). Alt: show "This iPhone is offline." when the path is unsatisfied.
- Room recovery: six backoff attempts (1–30 s), then the timer stops for Reconnect, but a network return always tries again and resets the budget. Triggers: `.transport`, `URLError`, and retryable refusals (408/429/5xx); never `.stale` or room/auth failures. Alt: retry forever like the inbox, or a room-only 408/429/5xx classifier.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <17e> --only` HermesGatewayTests, BotInboxTests, HermesSessionListTests, BotRoomTests, BotRoomManagementTests, NetworkPathMonitorTests, BotClientTests, HermesOfflineCacheTests, HermesBranchDuplicateTests, BotChatPresentationTests: 260 passed, 0 failed.
- After the review fix: BotRoomTests, BotRoomManagementTests, BotInboxTests, HermesSessionListTests, NetworkPathMonitorTests: 145 passed, 0 failed.
- Red: with the behavior stubbed out, the 6 new tests from the first commit failed (no ping sent, silent socket not closed, room/inbox/list never reconnected), except one regression guard. The 2 new room tests from the fix (`testARoomOutOfRetriesReconnectsWhenTheNetworkReturns`, `testARoomKeepsReconnectingPastATransientRefusal`) failed on `af509121` with "Nothing changed while waiting for: reconnected".

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone

1. Over the tunnel, start a long turn in a disposable session, then switch Wi-Fi → cellular. The stream reattaches within about 10 s and the prompt is not resent. An idle handover keeps a healthy connection.
2. Airplane Mode on for a minute with the inbox, Sessions, and a room open, then off. Each reconnects right away without tapping Reconnect.
3. In a room, background the app or leave while it waits to reconnect, then restore the network. The hidden room stays closed.
4. [Two servers] Switch servers while a reconnect is pending. Nothing from the old server appears under the new one.

---

title: fix(sessions): restore iPad keyboard commands on the Hermes home
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1365

## What changed

On a Hermes server, the Sessions and Bots home sides published no keyboard actions, so ⌘N, ⌘F, ⌘1–9, ⌃Tab/⌃⇧Tab and ⌘⇧]/⌘⇧[ were greyed out on iPad. Both sides (and a pushed `/sessions` list) now publish `HermexSceneActions`, routed through the existing New Session/New Bot, search, and row-tap paths. `ChatShortcutNavigation` is now generic over `Identifiable` rows, so the webui list, Hermes sessions, and bot rows share one helper; webui call sites are unchanged.

Decision: [D1 + Preserve (#921)](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1365#issuecomment-6485586550). Numbered and adjacent picks come from `scheduledSessionGroups(...).ordinary` at key press (search and project filter apply, Scheduled skipped), open through the row-tap path, and ⌘digit past the end does nothing. Hermes rows open synchronously, so `covers.selectedSessionID` already names the chat being opened and a second ⌃Tab steps on from it.

**Decisions made overnight**
- A `BotsInboxView` pushed from the webui list publishes no shortcuts, so the webui list's own shortcuts stay as they were. Alternative: publish from every `BotsInboxView`.

**Needs device check:** a pushed `/sessions` list publishes scene actions while the home side under it still publishes its own. SwiftUI documents no precedence for two `focusedSceneValue` publishers. If the parent's actions win, the repair is to stop the home side publishing while its chat has pushed a Sessions list.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/SessionNavigationStateTests`: 38 passed, 0 failed.
- No red run: the new `testNextAndPreviousChatStepThroughBotsAndRooms` passes bot rows to `adjacentChat`, which the old `[SessionSummary]`-only signature cannot compile. The existing webui adjacency and position tests pass unchanged before and after.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim`; selection and results recorded above
- [x] No new `Codable` models, third-party dependencies, endpoints, or JSON shapes

## Manual test

Device: iPad simulator, iPhone simulator

iPad simulator (iPad Pro 11, hardware keyboard, signed in to a Hermes server):
1. On Sessions, hold ⌘: New Chat, Search, Next/Previous Chat and Go to Chat 1–9 are enabled. ⌘1 opens the first ordinary session (Scheduled skipped), ⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab step and wrap, and ⌘9 past the end does nothing.
2. ⌘F focuses the header search. ⌘N opens New Session, and is greyed out while the offline-cache banner shows.
3. Switch to Bots: ⌘1 opens the first pinned bot (or the first row), ⌃Tab steps through bots and rooms, ⌘F opens Bot search, ⌘N opens the New Bot form.
4. From a Bot Chat, type `/sessions`: ⌘1 and ⌃Tab use the pushed Sessions list, not the bots, and ⌘F focuses its search field.

iPhone simulator (hardware keyboard):
1. Open a session and press ⌘F: the chat closes and the header search is focused.
2. In a Bot Chat, type `/sessions`: ⌘F focuses its search field and ⌘1 opens that list's first session.
3. Lock the app: every command is greyed out. On a webui server the list's shortcuts behave as before.

title: fix(hermes): let the composer's `@` panel find files in any folder
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1388

## What changed

In a local-backend Hermes chat, the composer's `@` panel sent the bare query as `complete.path`'s word. The host treats that as "list this one folder", so `@Chat` never found `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift`.

A name of two or more characters with no `/` now goes as `@file:<name>`, which reaches the host's fuzzy search over the whole working folder. The bare trigger (`.`), a path containing `/`, and a single character keep the one-folder listing, so `@s` still shows folders. `@path` chip confirmation keeps sending the plain path. `BotFilePathSearch` splits its word into `panelWord(for:)` and `listingWord(for:)`, and `completeFilePaths(_:as:)` takes the kind. The #1123 request-local, Hermes-only timeout is unchanged, and so are webui `@` search and Bot Chat.

Decision: [build as written, defaults adopted](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1388#issuecomment-6485588507).

**Contract:** `complete.path` in `tui_gateway/methods_complete.py` at the pinned commit. Live read-only check under the standing grant: one disposable hidden session (no prompt sent), closed afterwards and confirmed gone from `session.list include_hidden`. Results: `@file:README` returned 2 nested rows, plain `README` returned 0, `@file:s` returned 6 root files and no folders, `s` returned 14 rows including folders. The live host reports 0.22.2 against the 0.21.5 pin. `complete.path` behaved as the pinned source says, and the pin is not advanced here.

## How it was tested

- Red: against the old production code, the two panel tests in `HermesChatTurnTests` failed as intended (`"Sou"` is not equal to `"@file:Sou"`, for both the first query and the reload after a folder change).

- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)

## Linked issue

Fixes #1394

## What changed

Triage on the session list took two motions per row: swipe, then tap Archive. Hermex already shows "Archived · Undo" after every archive, so a full swipe can commit it safely.

`SessionInteractiveRow`'s trailing `.swipeActions` now sets `allowsFullSwipe` to `offersArchive && canShowSessionMutationActions && !isMutating`. A full swipe commits Archive, the first (edge-most) button. It never fires a lone Delete (archived search matches, read-only rows, Bot Chats) or a second archive while one is in flight. Leading Pin and the Bots inbox stay tap-only. A comment on the trailing builder records that Archive must stay first.

Decision applied: build as written, defaults adopted ([comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1394#issuecomment-6485588714)). title: fix(live-activity): declare frequent updates for push-driven Live Activities
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1371. The device-timing acceptance items are covered by the physical-iPhone Manual test below. The merge walk runs it on the batch Branch TestFlight build before merging, so the issue can close when the PR merges.

## What changed

Hermex receives push-driven Live Activity updates but never opted in to iOS's frequent-updates allowance. iOS budgets priority-10 Live Activity pushes, and the relay sends them on every start, status change, and completion. No stall has been reproduced. This PR only requests the larger allowance. It does not fix a known defect.

- `HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist`: adds `NSSupportsLiveActivitiesFrequentUpdates = true` next to `NSSupportsLiveActivities`. Only the main app gets the key. The widget, notification service, relay, registration, and UI are unchanged.
- `docs/agents/push.md`: notes the relay's priority policy, the app opt-in, and the user's iOS Settings toggle (`frequentPushesEnabled`). It says that neither setting promises delivery timing.

Decision applied: [keep as a bounded opt-in despite no reproduced stall](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1371#issuecomment-6485587493).

Relay policy was checked read-only in `hermex-push` @ `149fc3fb`. Priority 10 on start or status change and priority 5 for same-status progress paced to 1/s are in `policy.ts:49-52`. Up to two priority-10 pushes at completion (alerting update, then silent end) are in `coordinator.ts:274-283` and `apns.ts:112-125`. This is the local source, not the deployed relay.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotLiveActivityTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatLiveActivityTests`: 77 passed, 0 failed.
- The built `HermesMobile.app/Info.plist` contains `NSSupportsLiveActivitiesFrequentUpdates` as Boolean true, and `plutil -lint` passes.
- There is no unit test, because asserting the key would only restate a constant. No simulator can show APNs budget behavior, so the device check is below.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone

1. [Push paired with a test server] Start a disposable session, lock the phone, and watch the Live Activity go running → waiting → running → done. Open the app to answer any approval. Expected: the card follows each status and the completion alert arrives. Note the rough timings.
2. Turn off Settings → Hermex → Live Activities → More Frequent Updates and repeat step 1. Expected: updates and the completion alert still arrive.
3. With the setting off, tap the Live Activity. Expected: it opens that session.
4. Optional: repeat step 1 with Low Power Mode on. Record the iOS version, the Low Power Mode state, and the timings in the issue.

body:
Found in the epic #1359 merge walk while testing #1423 (#1367).

**Problem.** #1367 lets a photo-only draft be queued mid-run, but the composer's **+** button is greyed out while the agent is working, so the only way to stage a photo mid-run is to paste it. Pasting works and the queued turn carries the photo.

**Cause.** `composerPlusMenu` in `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift` uses `.disabled(isConfigurationControlDisabled)`, which includes `isWaitingForStream`. That rule is meant for model, workspace and branch controls, but **+** only opens the media picker (`showMediaPicker = true`).

**Fix.** Give **+** its own rule that stays enabled during a run, matching paste. It should stay disabled where attaching can't work: offline cache (#1375), read-only sessions, and while a host control is held. Check Bot Chat's composer the same way.

Test: start a long turn, tap **+**, pick a photo, tap **Queue**. The queued turn carries the photo.

title: fix(chat): delay and hold the stream recovery chip so quick recoveries don't flash
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1373

## What changed

**Problem:** the stream recovery chip appeared the moment checking/reattaching started and could vanish a moment later, so quick recoveries flashed a status.

**Fix:** new `Features/Shared/DelayedStatus.swift`: a `DelayedStatusPolicy` (400 ms show / 400 ms hold), a pure `DelayedStatus` stepper that takes caller time and returns only the next deadline (no repeating timer), a `@MainActor @Observable` driver that sleeps to each deadline and checks cancellation before every write, and `DelayedStatusView`. `ChatTranscriptView` steps the driver from `.task(id:)` and draws the unchanged `StreamRecoveryStatusView` through it, with the same accessibility hiding and Reduce Motion transition. The chip sits outside the `activeStreamID` gate, so a chip shown just before the reply completes still holds for its 400 ms. #1374 reuses the pair with an 800 ms policy.

**Decisions applied** ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1373#issuecomment-6489644178)): Design B, 400/400 ms; a status change while shown swaps at once and starts its own hold; `.waitingForNetwork` skips the delay once the coordinator publishes it.

**Decisions made overnight**
- State lives in a small driver the transcript holds in `@State`, not in a wrapper view that stays mounted. Alt: the literal mounted wrapper, which adds a spacing gap at the tail of every live stream.
- No hosted test for moving the chip out of the `activeStreamID` gate (review accepted): `ChatTranscriptView` has ~79 inputs and no hosted harness. Alt: build one for a one-line mount move. The hold is unit-tested; the manual step below covers the wiring.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only HermesMobileTests/DelayedStatusTests`: 6 passed, 0 failed (also after rebasing onto `15f89b6e`).
- Red: against a stub that shows at once, 2 passed / 4 failed (no show or hold deadline; the cancelled run never waited). The cancelled-before-start case failed with `XCTAssertNil failed: "waitingForNetwork"` before the entry guard.
- Full suite (project file changed): 3613 passed, 1 failed, `BotChatPresentationTests.testThreadSearchOpensChronologicalDetailAndItsOwnComposer`, unrelated; it passes alone (18/18).

## Design

Design B (local mock, epic #1360). No screenshots: no fixture reaches the recovery chip without cutting the Mac's network, so the physical-iPhone check below covers it.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone
1. Stream a long reply over LAN, then toggle Wi-Fi off for a few seconds and back on. The chip appears only after about 0.4 s and stays at least 0.4 s. Repeat over the Cloudflare tunnel.
2. Toggle Wi-Fi off and straight back on. No chip flashes.
3. Turn on Airplane Mode mid-reply. Once the app sees the network is gone, "Waiting for network" shows with no delay.
4. Let a reply finish while the chip is showing. The chip stays for the rest of its hold, then goes away.

title: fix(home): say "Reconnecting" on populated Sessions and Bots lists instead of going quiet
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1374. Stacked on #1438.

## What changed

**Problem.** When the Hermes socket drops with rows on screen, the Sessions and Bots homes go quiet: the Working/Needs-you labels vanish and nothing says the app is reconnecting or offline.

**Fix.** `SessionListViewModel` and `BotInbox` now keep two facts apart: *reconnecting* (a retryable drop with rows, until a read on the new socket succeeds) and *stale labels* (kept through a lost socket, an offline path or a failed status read, until a current `session.active_list` reply). `SessionsHeader` (both homes, iPhone and iPad split) and the pushed `/sessions` title show a quiet line through #1438's `DelayedStatusDriver` (800 ms show, 400 ms hold): "Reconnecting…" online, a button that runs `reconnectNow()`; "Offline · showing last known status" at once from the device path. Stale labels draw secondary and read "Last known: …" to VoiceOver. A failed read after a reconnect counts as another drop, and the backoff resets only once a page read succeeds. If a reconnect can't reach the host, the live rows stay up under "Reconnecting…" with their last-known labels and keep backing off, instead of swapping to the offline cache; a cold open with no live rows still falls back to the cache. Refusals show over retained Sessions rows. Docs: `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`.

Decisions applied: [Design B decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1374#issuecomment-6489644457).

**Decisions made overnight**
- Added `reconnectNow()` on both models over `BotReconnectSchedule.networkPathDidChange()`, since #1372 shipped no such API. Alt: a dedicated `runNow()` on the schedule.
- Offline comes from the device path at once with eligible rows, and marks labels stale (this replaces the earlier socket-drop-only call, after review). Alt: Offline only after a socket drop.
- Only refusals show over populated Sessions rows. Retryable paging failures stay hidden (this replaces the earlier all-errors call). Alt: a dedicated refusal flag.
- The pushed webui Bots inbox gets stale styling only, no line. Alt: add the line to its toolbar.
- Stale and reconnecting reset on a true close (background, leaving the screen, the Bots/Sessions switch). Alt: keep stale labels across close.
- No VoiceOver announcement. Stale labels read "Last known: …". Alt: post an announcement on each transition.
- A `keepsRows` gate (rows, no cached copy, no refusal or Bots advice) suppresses both lines. Alt: suppress only under the offline-cache banner.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only` on the final head: HermesSessionListTests + HermesSessionSearchTests + HermesOfflineCacheTests + HermesSessionActionsTests + HermesProjectsTests + HermesBranchDuplicateTests **124 passed, 0 failed**. Earlier on this branch: SessionList + BotInbox + DelayedStatus + OfflineCache **133 passed**, plus caller classes **199 passed**. `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all keys covered. After the reconnect repair (ef40426b): HermesOfflineCacheTests + HermesSessionListTests + BotInboxTests **129 passed, 0 failed**.

Red evidence: 3 lost-socket tests failed against inert stubs (labels emptied, `isReconnecting` false). 4 review-fix tests failed with the fixes reverted (the tap after a failed 503 read had nothing to run, offline path not stale on both models, another connection's statuses showing). `testARefusedScheduledLoadMoreClearsOnceARetryLoads` failed on the prior head (the refusal survived the loaded page). `HermesOfflineCacheTests.testAnUnreachableReconnectKeepsTheLiveRowsReconnecting` failed on 6ed507e9 (the failed reconnect swapped the live rows for the cache).

## Design

Design B (local mock, epic #1360): a quiet line under the logo. A (replace the logo) and C (TopNav banner) were rejected.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>`; selection and results above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone, iPad simulator

2. Tap "Reconnecting…". It reconnects at once, the line clears, and the labels regain their colour.
3. Turn on Airplane Mode. "Offline · showing last known status" shows at once. Turn it off and the labels come back.
4. [second server] Switch servers mid-reconnect. Nothing carries over to the other server.

title: feat(sessions): lift sessions waiting for you above the rest of the list
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1393. Stacked on #1439.

## What changed

**Problem.** A session waiting on a clarify or an approval sits wherever the list order puts it, so on a long Sessions list the rows that need the user are easy to miss.

**Fix.** On a Hermes Sessions list, loaded, unarchived, non-cron rows whose label reads Input lift into a "Needs you N" group above the scheduled disclosure. Pinned waiting rows move into the group, and list order is kept inside it. `ScheduledSessionGroups` partitions the rows in its existing single pass, using an optional `needsInput` predicate. `scheduledSessionGroups` passes `attentionState(for:) == .input`, the same lookup the row labels use, and only for a live (not cached) Hermes list that is not being searched. Rows reuse `SessionInteractiveRow` and keep their ids and selection. No new requests, timers, persistence, or animation, and no unloaded rows or counts are made up. The ordinary empty state stays hidden while the group has rows. ⌘1–9 and next/previous now walk Needs you first, then ordinary rows, and still skip Scheduled. webui lists are unchanged. Docs: `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`.

Decisions applied: [Design A decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1393#issuecomment-6489646134).

title: fix(chat): make rendered replies and code follow Dynamic Type
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1368. Stacked on #1441.

## What changed

**Problem.** Agent replies were pinned at 16 pt and code at 13 pt (Highlightr fences at Courier 14). When the user raised the system text size, their own bubbles grew and the reply beside them didn't. This affected every shared Markdown surface.

**Fix.** The new `ChatTypography` resolves 16 pt prose and 13 pt code at Large through body `UIFontMetrics`, capped at 2.2x (about 35 pt prose at AX5). Sizes come from a static per-`DynamicTypeSize` table. `ChatMarkdownView` reads `dynamicTypeSize` and passes the body size into `Theme.chat`, so headings and inline code follow. Plain, highlighted and diff code use the scaled code font. `MarkdownCodeHighlighter` strips absolute fonts before caching and keeps bold and italic as relative emphasis. The cache stays independent of text size, and a size change never re-highlights. Default prose, plain and diff sizes are unchanged. Highlighted fences now use the plain fences' 13 pt SF Mono.

Decisions applied: [Design A decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1368#issuecomment-6489643499).

**Decisions made overnight**
- Tests went into `MarkdownMathRendererTests` beside the highlighter tests. Alt: a new `ChatTypographyTests` file plus a pbxproj entry.
- Inline-math paragraphs (`MathInlineText`) follow the 2.2x cap. Alt: leave them on an uncapped `@ScaledMetric`, about 50 pt at AX5 next to 35 pt prose.
- Tool-call log diffs share `DiffCodeBlockText`, so they scale too. Alt: pin them at 13 pt.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only` MarkdownMathRenderer + StreamingMarkdownSupport + ResponseSelection + MarkdownMathLayoutCache + MarkdownDiffFormatter: **70 passed, 0 failed**. On the final head, MarkdownMathRendererTests: **49 passed, 0 failed**.

Red evidence: on the unchanged master code, `testHighlightedCodeTakesItsSizeFromTheParentFontAndKeepsEmphasis` failed. Emphasis intents were missing, and a Highlightr token measured the same width (211 vs 379.8 expected) at 13 and 26 pt parent fonts. In a second check, `scaled()` was temporarily made flat below AX5 and jumped to the cap at AX5. `testChatTypographyGrowsWithDynamicTypeUpToTheCap` then failed: xxxLarge was 16.0 vs 16.0 for body and 13.0 vs 13.0 for code.

## Design

Design A (local mock, epic #1360): prose and all code follow Dynamic Type, capped at 2.2x. Highlighted fences use the 13 pt monospaced baseline. B (uncapped prose) and C (1.6x cap) were rejected.

## Checklist

title: perf(chat): stop rebuilding settled reply selection hosts when nothing changed
body:
Fixes #1369. Stacked on #1442.

## What changed

Opening a chat with long replies was slow: every settled reply's text-selection host rebuilt its whole hosted SwiftUI graph on every update, even when nothing about the reply had changed.

`ResponseTextSelection` now forwards an audited set of environment values (color scheme, layout direction, Dynamic Type size, display scale, locale, and the chat's own keys) instead of `\.self`. It reassigns the hosted root only when the reply's identity, its declared rendering inputs, or that environment change. Links go through a stable `OpenURLAction` on the controller. Media callbacks go through one main-actor bridge that each body pass refreshes. Height feedback, glyph visibility, identity reset and Ask Hermex are unchanged. This follows the [2026-10-29 decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1369#issuecomment-6489643837): no `LazyVStack`, lazy attachment, renderer rewrite or layout cache.

**Benchmark** (Release, iPhone 17e sim, base f9faef51 vs this branch, 4 alternating rounds): warm open median 189.5 → 177.5 ms, root assignments per warm open 18 → 8, size passes unchanged (18 → 18), cold open unchanged (about 1.1 s, mostly network). What's left is the size passes: SwiftUI re-measures the representable after every parent update, so skipping them would need a layout cache, which the issue rules out.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Benchmark fixture: #1256's fixture isn't on the signed-in server, so the numbers come from a different long, read-only chat (184 messages). Alternative: create a long-reply chat on the live host.
- Values that only come from UIKit traits (Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast) aren't forwarded; the hosted controller inherits them from the window. Alternative: add them to the comparison signature.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only HermesMobileTests/ResponseSelectionTests --only …/ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests --only …/TranscriptMediaVisibilityTests --only …/HermesChatAttachmentTests`: 41 passed, 0 failed (9 + 2 + 3 + 27). Earlier run: `MarkdownMathRendererTests`, `BotChatPresentationTests`, `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests`, `ChatScrollPolicyTests`: 96 passed.
- Two new hosted tests in `ResponseSelectionTests`: `testSettledReplyRebuildsOnlyWhenItsInputsOrEnvironmentChange` (an unrelated update with equal inputs doesn't rebuild; a changed workspace root, appearance, or text size each does), plus a check that links reach the latest handler. After that test grew inputs coverage: `ResponseSelectionTests` + `ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests`, 11 passed, 0 failed.
- Red: on f9faef51 the gating test failed (`"3" is not equal to "2"`: an unrelated update rebuilt the host). Temporary mutations that dropped `colorScheme` from the comparison, or built the rendering with `inputs: nil`, also failed it (the reply kept `/first` instead of `/second`). The media-callback race has no deterministic test; the compiler enforces the main-actor isolation instead.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator

iPhone:
1. Open a long chat with code, a table and inline math. Select from one paragraph across into a code block and use Ask Hermex. The selection and the Ask Hermex draft are correct.
2. With the chat open, switch to dark mode, then change the text size. Settled replies update at once.
3. Scroll to the top and back. Selection still starts on replies that scrolled back in.
4. Open a Bot room and select a member message. Selection works.
5. Switch the app language to an RTL language and reopen the chat. Replies lay out right to left and selection still works.

iPad:
1. Repeat iPhone step 1 in a split view.
2. Toggle dark mode with the chat open. Settled replies update at once.

title: feat(chat): name what a tool group did instead of counting hidden calls
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1376. Stacked on #1445.

## What changed

**Problem.** A collapsed tool group says "+12 previous tool calls": how much happened, not what. A failed older call also disappears behind that toggle.

**Fix.** A new pure `ToolCallGroupSummary` reads only the hidden entries. It names up to two kinds by priority (write, shell, delegate, search, read, web) and rolls the rest into "other actions", e.g. "Changed 2 files and ran 4 commands". A hidden `web_search` counts as a search, not a fetched page. Successful writes count distinct full paths across calls (`changedPaths(args:)`, extracted from the formatter with `changedFilesPreview` output unchanged). Failed, running, interrupted and pathless writes never claim changed files. When a hidden call failed, the toggle shows a static red triangle and VoiceOver adds "N failed". The expanded title stays "Show fewer tool calls". Phrases are 8 new String Catalog plural keys joined with `.list(type: .and)`, capitalizing only the first grapheme. Preserve (#344) holds: row ✕ marks, Expand Tools by Default, and the shared disclosure handler are unchanged.

Integration: a summarized write counts as a changed file only without an explicit failure/no-op signal (error/success:false/no_change, or an anchored hermes-agent write/patch error lead); see #1452 triage.

Decisions applied: [Design A decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1376#issuecomment-6489644739).

**Decisions made overnight**
- No named kind among hidden calls (only skills, memory, unknown tools): keep "+N previous tool calls", still with the triangle and spoken count. Alt: "N other actions" or a new "N tool calls" phrase.
- Reads say "read N files" only when every hidden read succeeded and named a path; otherwise "N read actions". Alt: pathless/failed reads go to other actions.
- Failed non-write calls still count in their kind (a failed command was still run); every failure feeds the triangle. Alt: move all failed calls into other actions.
- The title stays one line at standard sizes and wraps at accessibility sizes, chevron and triangle top-aligned. Alt: always allow two lines.

Translations for the 17 non-English languages are marked `needs_review`.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only HermesMobileTests/ToolCallGroupSummaryTests --only HermesMobileTests/ToolCallSummaryFormatterTests --only HermesMobileTests/LocalizationCatalogTests`: **28 passed, 0 failed**. `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 2503 keys covered. title: feat(chat): show the latest thought while thinking, and Thought once settled

## Linked issue

Fixes #1377. Stacked on #1446.

## What changed

The collapsed reasoning row showed the first 80 characters for the whole run, leaked literal Markdown asterisks, and still said "Thinking" on settled history.

- Strip `*`/`**` runs and backticks, never underscores (alt: also strip `_x_`/`__x__`, which risks `__init__`, `snake_case`).

title: Session search doesn't find archived chats on a webui server
body:
On a hermes-webui server, searching the Sessions list never shows archived chats, so there's no way to find an old chat once it's archived except scrolling the Archived screen.

The server does return them: `/api/sessions/search` includes archived rows with `archived: true` for both title and content matches. The app drops them because it only keeps search hits that are already in the loaded list, and the list leaves archived rows out.

Hermes servers already show archived matches with the Archived badge (#1053), so webui should do the same.

Steps: archive a chat on a webui server, then search for its title or something it said. Only unarchived chats come back.
