title: feat(chat): keep answered questions readable in the transcript
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1378. Stacked on #1447.

## What changed

**Problem.** Once the user answers a `clarify` question, the exchange only survives as raw JSON in a generic tool row, and settled-turn folding hides it with the rest of the activity. To see what they told the agent, the user has to expand the whole run.

**Fix.** The new `ClarifyResult` (`Models/ClarifyResult.swift`) parses the pinned batch `{responses, timed_out?, notice?}` and legacy `{question, choices_offered, user_response}` shapes. It handles text, multi-select and blank answers, and maps the exact `TIMEOUT_RESPONSE` sentinel to "no answer" plus a timeout. Error envelopes, unknown answer types and empty batches return nil, so those rows stay generic. `ToolCallSummaryFormatter` gives a recognized call a question-bubble icon, "Asked N questions" and the first Q·A as its detail, and copies `Question:`/`Answer:` lines. When opened, the row shows selectable pairs and any notice in the transcript's text direction; generic rows keep forced LTR. A folded turn shows compact Q&A lines (they count toward `hasVisibleContent`, so activity-only anchors still render), and an expanded turn shows the full row instead, so each exchange appears once. Both follow the thinking/tool visibility setting. The folded lines come from a pure helper, `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.foldedQuestionLines`, so they are tested directly. VoiceOver and copied text drop the separator after a question that already ends in punctuation, so they no longer read `?.`.

Decision applied: [Design A decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1378#issuecomment-6489645268). Contract checked against pinned hermes-agent `ca678285` `tools/clarify_tool.py` (`TIMEOUT_RESPONSE` :13-14, batch and legacy returns, `tool_error` envelopes).

**Decisions made overnight**
- The collapsed row's detail is the first exchange, "Question · Answer" ("No answer" when blank). Alt: no detail, or every answer joined.
- A timeout with no server notice shows a plain "Timed out waiting for an answer." note. Alt: show only "No answer".
- No new `.clarify` kind: the row recognizes a parsed result before the generic path. Alt: add `.clarify` and update every switch. Follow-up candidate: #1446's `ToolCallGroupSummary` names a clarify call by its raw tool name.

New strings: five (plural "Asked %lld questions"; "Question: %@ Answer: %@" for questions that end in punctuation). All 17 languages are marked `needs_review`.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only` ClarifyResultTests + ToolCallSummaryFormatterTests + TranscriptTurnFoldingTests + ClarificationTests + LocalizationCatalogTests: **49 passed, 0 failed**. After the review fixes (92bb4d55), ClarifyResultTests: **5 passed, 0 failed**. `ci/check_string_catalog.py` covers all 2500 keys.
- Full suite (Xcode project changed): **3610 passed, 1 failed**. The failure, `BotChatPresentationTests.testThreadSearchOpensChronologicalDetailAndItsOwnComposer`, is a hosted-UI settle wait unrelated to clarify or folding; it passed alone, 18/18.
- Red: before the fix, the new Q&A test failed 4 assertions (detail was the raw JSON's first line, and the copy held raw `user_response` JSON). Mutations for the test fix, each reverted: changing the production timeout constant failed the sentinel test, and returning nil for an unrecognized clarify row failed the fallback test's `XCTUnwrap`. For the review fixes: dropping the `hidesActivity` guard from the helper failed the folding test twice (answers shown on expanded and unfolded rows), and the old label failed the copy test (it held `Which environment?. Answer: Staging`).

## Design

Design A (local mock, epic #1360): compact Q/A rows with a question-bubble icon, visible in folded turns.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>`; selection and results above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (`ClarifyResult` parses loosely and ignores unknown fields)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes

Device: iPhone simulator

2. Let the turn settle and fold. The folded turn shows the Q&A lines. Expand it, and the clarify row shows once, with no duplicate lines.
3. Skip a question or let it time out. It shows "No answer" plus the timeout note.

title: feat(chat): show the queued prompt as a pending bubble
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1379. Stacked on #1450.

## What changed

**Problem.** After a follow-up queues behind a running Hermes turn, the composer only says it will send later. The user can't see what they queued before sending another follow-up or stopping the run.

**Fix.** Hermes chats show the host's queued prompt as a dimmed user bubble at the end of the transcript, with "Queued" where the time goes. It lives outside `messages` (id `hermes-queued-prompt`) and comes from `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.queuedPrompt` through the existing `displayed` helper, so attachment references become chips. It stays up through the idle gap between turns and goes away when `message.start` appends the one real row, or when a local or remote Stop clears the slot. An empty chat with a queued prompt now draws the transcript, and its bottom arrow can reach the bubble. Readers at the live edge follow it; readers in history stay put. VoiceOver reads the bubble's own child labels (text with skill names, each attachment name) with "Queued" as its value. `queuedMessagesReceipt` now covers only webui's `queuedSlashMessages`, so the Hermes composer receipt is gone; the webui receipt and #913 draft parking are unchanged. Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md`. One new catalog key (`Queued`) ships in all 17 languages as `needs_review`.

Decision applied: [Design A decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1379#issuecomment-6489645558). Contract: pinned `ca678285` `tui_gateway/session_auto_continue.py` `_queued_prompt_snapshot` sends `queued = {user: text}`. No new RPC, event, or shape.

- Dimmed with an opaque fill (bubble colour mixed 45% toward `systemBackground`), text at full strength, so the long-bubble fold gradient still works. Alt: `.opacity(0.55)` on the fill.
- Copy only in the meta row, no context menu, text stays selectable. Alt: a one-item Copy context menu.
- The bubble sits last, after the working row, outcome and file-changes card. Alt: directly after the live response.

title: feat(chat): turn large pasted text into a removable attachment
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1381. Stacked on #1451.

## What changed

**Problem.** Pasting a long log fills the composer, makes TextKit layout slow, and bloats the transcript and cache.

**Fix.** In Hermes Sessions and Bot Chat, a plain-text paste over 3,000 UTF-16 units becomes a removable `pasted-text.txt` tile. It goes through the existing Hermes staging path: a draft copy with a lease, the eight-file / 25 MB / 50 MB limits, and Send held until staging finishes. The editor and clipboard are left alone. Later pastes take `pasted-text-2.txt` and so on, with each name reserved before any await. "Paste as Text" in the edit menu and ⌘⇧V paste inline (undoable). File and image paste still take precedence, IME composition is never converted, and webui sessions, rooms and the share extension keep inline paste. A staging failure shows the existing attachment error, and a paste over the file limit is rejected by its UTF-8 byte count before it is encoded (same limit error). `ChatAttachmentCoordinator` owns each paste's staging task, and `ChatView.onDisappear` cancels it. A paste cancelled mid-save deletes its uncommitted copy and adds no tile. Docs: `docs/agents/bots.md`.

Decisions applied: [Design A decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1381#issuecomment-6489645895).

**Decisions made overnight**
- iOS may show its "Allow Paste" prompt when Paste as Text or ⌘⇧V reads text copied from another app, because they are custom actions. The pasteboard is read only when the action runs (`hasStrings` gates the menu). Alt: a `UIPasteControl` bypass button, which is new chrome that Design A rejected.
- Paste as Text sits inside the standard edit group, after Cut/Copy/Paste. Alt: its own top-level item or submenu.
- The off-main UTF-8 encode counts as an upload, so Send is held from the moment of the paste. Alt: encode on the main actor, or leave the short gap unheld.
- When the chat disappears, a paste that is still staging is cancelled, including when another view is pushed on top. The editor and clipboard stay intact. Alt: keep it alive across pushes.

Translations: the new "Paste as Text" key is in 17 languages, marked `needs_review`.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-… --only` HermesChatAttachmentTests + ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests + SharedDraftStoreTests + ComposerLargePasteTests on the final head: **88 passed, 0 failed**. Earlier: ComposerLargePaste + HermesChatAttachment + ComposerRecall + ComposerUndo + ChatAttachmentCoordinator + ComposerKeyboardCommand + ComposerChipDocument + LocalizationCatalog **79 passed**. `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 2496 keys covered.

Size-guard repair (da01b231): HermesChatAttachmentTests + ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests + ComposerLargePasteTests **51 passed, 0 failed**. No red run was possible: the limits are fixed static constants, and an oversized paste already ended with the same error, so the only difference is the skipped full-size copy.

Red evidence: with the conversion off, Paste as Text a no-op and in-flight names unreserved, all 3 new tests failed (nothing staged, nothing inserted inline, two pastes both named `pasted-text.txt`). With cancellation a no-op, `testAPasteCancelledMidSaveLeavesNothingBehind` failed: a `pasted-text.txt` tile and its draft copy remained.

## Design

Design A (local mock, epic #1360): the tile plus Paste as Text and ⌘⇧V. B (a one-time "Pasted as a file · Undo" hint) was rejected.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>`; selection and results above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies

title: fix(chat): don't count cut-off or unlisted write errors as changed files
body:
Follow-up from the epic #1360 integration (stack #1453, PR #1446 / issue #1376).

**Problem.** The collapsed tool-group summary (`ToolCallGroupSummary`) can still claim "Changed N files" for writes that changed nothing, in two remaining cases after #1446's integration repairs:

1. **Cut-off previews.** `ToolCallDiff` skips the anchored write-error check when the preview is cut off (`isCutOff`). A long rejection such as "Found N matches for old_string…" can hit the 4,000-character preview limit while the completed call has `.success`, so it counts as a changed file. Greptile: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1446#discussion_r4414764976
2. **Unlisted validation errors.** The anchored error-lead list (pinned hermes-agent ca678285) is closed. Rare `tool_error` texts like "old_string and new_string required", "Unknown mode: x", or a webui-unwrapped MCP "Error: …" still count as changed when the args name a path. (Integration review notes, lane 1.)

**Suggested fix.** (1) Check the anchored error lead before the truncation guard — the start of the message is still present. (2) Consider extending the lead list from `tools/file_tools.py` validation errors, or prefer the webui sending `is_error:true` for unwrapped tool errors upstream.

Evidence: `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ToolCallDiff.swift` (~154–176 at 584a3ea0), `ToolCallGroupSummary.swift` (~48–54). Tests to extend: `ToolCallGroupSummaryTests.testUnsuccessfulAndPathlessWritesNeverClaimChangedFiles`.

title: fix(chat): keep code spans intact in a live reasoning heading
body:
Follow-up from the epic #1360 integration (stack #1453, PR #1447 / issue #1377).

**Problem.** In the live reasoning preview, `ReasoningSummaryFormatter.boldHeading(_:)` treats `**` inside a code span as the heading's closing marker. `**Inspecting `**kwargs` handling**` previews as just "Inspecting", dropping the identifier and the rest of the heading from the collapsed row and its VoiceOver label. Greptile: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1447#discussion_r4414783669

**Suggested fix.** Skip matched backtick code spans (same equal-length-run pairing already used by `stripInlineMarkup`) when searching for the closing `**`. Add the input to `ReasoningSummaryFormatterTests.testLatestThoughtPrefersTheNewestCompletedHeading`.

Not fixed in the stack because the integration repair budget was spent.

title: feat(workspace): color diff syntax and wrap diff lines
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1382

## What changed

The diff sheet (Changes sheet and the turn-changes card) drew every line as plain text and could not wrap, so long lines needed sideways scrolling.

- A new sheet-owned `ReviewDiffHighlightModel` colours the rows in the viewport plus overscan, at most 200 rows a request. It tokenizes the new side (context and additions) and the old side (context and deletions) separately. Collapsed files, unsupported languages and no-newline markers stay plain. Refresh, appearance changes and dismissal drop answers still in flight.
- Syntax colours that fall below WCAG 4.5:1 against the add/delete tint use the label colour instead.
- Wrap Lines sits in an `ellipsis.circle` menu next to Done and shares the Files viewer's preference. Word-diff boxes split across wrapped lines.
- #733 bounds hold: text drawing stays limited to reachable columns and visible lines, and delete stripes on a wrapped row are drawn only inside the dirty rect.

Decision: [issue comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1382#issuecomment-6508754815).

**Design:** mock https://hebuvq6vn3gu.postplan.dev#issue-1382, pick "A ellipsis menu".

title: feat(workspace): remember viewed and collapsed files while a chat is open
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1384

## What changed

Folds and viewed marks in the Changes sheet and the turn-changes diff were sheet-local `@State`, so every reopen started over. Now they last while the chat is open.

- `ChatView` owns an in-memory `ReviewProgressStore`, keyed by `GitDataClient.reviewScope` (webui session, or Hermes server/profile/key/cwd). Closing the chat, switching servers or changing folders leaves old progress unreachable.
- `GitDiffView` keeps one `ReviewDiffProgress` value. It restores stored explicit folds, which win over #1383's defaults, and writes every toggle through to the store.
- A viewed mark shows only once the file's loaded text patch matches the stored fingerprint, a hash computed off the main actor with the rows. If the patch changed, the mark clears and the file unfolds. Loading, failed, binary and too-large loads hide the mark but leave it stored.
- The pull-to-refresh task is cancelled on dismissal, so a late load can't write to the store.
- Pruning runs only after a full, untruncated status read. The Hermes adapter now reports `truncated: nil` when `files` is missing, so a partial read never prunes.
- Preserve #399, per the [decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1384#issuecomment-6508755477): marking a file viewed folds it, un-viewing leaves the fold, and the header stays anchored. A file you tap still opens unfolded.

Deviation: the store is a plain `@MainActor final class` in `@State`, not `@Observable` as the issue suggested. No view observes it, since the surfaces render from local state, and a non-observable store rules out the "don't mutate an observable store during view init" hazard.

Upstream quirk: Hermes `review_list` returns `files: []` when git fails. A present list counts as authoritative, so that failure prunes in-memory progress only.

## How it was tested

- Full suite on 47636db9: `scripts/test-sim <udid>`, 3657 passed, 0 failed (the Xcode project changed).
- Focused on f27b35ca: `--only` `ReviewProgressStoreTests`, `ReviewDiffDefaultCollapseTests`, `ReviewDiffRowBuilderTests`, `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`, `APIClientGitTests`: 127 passed, 0 failed.
- Red: the store tests run against sheet-local behavior failed 6 of 7, e.g. restore expected `["src/App.swift", "notes.md"]` and got `[]`. The review fixes were also red first: a failed refresh left a mark visible (`["A.swift"]` vs `[]`), a Hermes list without `files` pruned (`[]` vs `["A.swift"]`), and a Hermes diff without text could be marked viewed (`true` vs `false`).
- Retry fix on e02cdf43: `testACancelledLoadForgetsNoReviewProgress` checks that a Try Again load cancelled after the sheet closes neither writes nor prunes review progress. `--only` `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`, `ReviewProgressStoreTests`: 79 passed, 0 failed.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator
1. Mark two files viewed and fold a third, then reopen from Changes and from a turn-changes card. The state is restored.
2. Re-edit one viewed file. Only that file is unviewed.
3. Dismiss the sheet mid-refresh, then reopen. Nothing is clobbered.
4. [second signed-in server] Switching servers, or closing the chat, discards progress.

## Linked issue

Fixes #1385

## What changed

In a long diff the only way to reach a later file was scrolling past every file above it. The diff sheet now has a leading list button (VoiceOver: "Changed files", shown when there is more than one file) that opens **Jump to File**: one row per file in diff order with name, folder, +/- counts and a checkmark when viewed, searchable past 8 files. Picking a row closes the list, expands that file if it was collapsed, leaves viewed state alone, and scrolls to its header, again on every pick. The Changes sheet and the turn-changes card both host `GitDiffView`, so both get it; iPad uses the same sheet.

A jump to a file whose rows above are still loading used to land at the top and get lost. `ReviewDiffSurfaceView` now holds a clamped file jump and re-lands it as rows load, until it lands unclamped, the reader drags, VoiceOver reveals another row, or a new jump arrives.

**Design**: https://hebuvq6vn3gu.postplan.dev#issue-1385, pick A

- Tests go through a small static seam, `GitDiffView.jump(to:collapsedFileIDs:)` plus `GitDiffFileJumpList.files(_:matching:)`; the jump cannot reach `viewedFileIDs`, so "viewed stays viewed" holds by construction. Alt: inline the jump and test only search.

**Integration:** conflicts with #1458 and #1460. With #1458, keep this branch's leading `ToolbarItem` and #1458's trailing `ToolbarItemGroup { diffActionsMenu; Done }`. With #1460, the jump call site reads `review.viewedFileIDs` and expands through `ReviewDiffProgress` (the static jump can move there), and the jump should also settle `defaultCollapse` for that file so a later publish doesn't fold it again.

title: feat(hermes): search Files across the workspace, not just opened folders
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1389

## What changed

In a Hermes chat, Files search only filtered folders you had already opened, so a file in an unopened folder couldn't be found. Now, for a local Hermes chat, a query of two or more characters with no `/` waits 250 ms for typing to stop, then runs the host's `complete.path` `@file:` fuzzy search across the whole folder. A **Workspace** section lists the matching files the loaded tree doesn't already show. It sits above the tree's matches, which get an **Open Folders** header. While the search runs the section shows a static "Searching…" row. A failed search shows "Workspace search unavailable" with Try Again, and tree filtering keeps working. Tapping a hit opens its preview straight away. Webui Files is unchanged.

The search can't use the chat's runtime, because opening Files suspends the chat (#902). Each search therefore makes a one-shot `complete.path` call with `cwd` set to the chat's folder and no session. It runs on a short-lived client on the shared gateway socket, which closes after the reply or as soon as the search is cancelled, even mid-connect. Late replies and replies after a folder move are dropped.

Decision applied: [files only, Workspace above Open Folders](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1389#issuecomment-6508756832). Preserve #1233: opening a hit never lists or expands its ancestor folders.

**Design**: https://hebuvq6vn3gu.postplan.dev#issue-1389, pick A (Workspace section first).

**Decisions made overnight**
- No Workspace header when every host hit is already in the tree; the tree's matches show as they do today. Alternative: an empty Workspace header or a "No other files" row.
- VoiceOver reads a root-level hit as its name alone, and other hits as "<name>, in <folder>". Alternative: "File, <name>" or "<name>, in workspace root".
- Files search uses a sessionless `complete.path` with `cwd` on a one-shot client, and the chat stays suspended. Alternative: keep the chat attached under Files, or reattach it for each search.

title: feat(hermes): show the branch's pull request in the Git menu
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1391

## What changed

On a Hermes chat there was no way to see or open the branch's pull request from the phone. The Git menu now has a top section, **Pull Request #N**, with an Open, Merged or Closed subtitle, plus **Copy Link**. The row opens the PR in the in-app Safari sheet. The data comes only from `GET /api/git/review/ship-info?path=<repo root>`. A link is shown only when the PR has a positive number and a web URL. On webui servers nothing is sent and the menu is unchanged.

The view model owns one cancellable read, kept apart from status and branches, so a slow `gh` never holds up the Changes count. Each answer is tied to the branch it was read on: a branch switch hides the old link at once, a folder change or leaving the chat drops late answers, and reads stay fresh for 60 s. Checkout, push and turn end force a new read.

- Decision: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1391#issuecomment-6508757375. A Create PR action was rejected for this slice.
- **Design**: https://hebuvq6vn3gu.postplan.dev#issue-1391, pick A.
- Contract: pinned upstream `ca678285` `hermes_cli/web_routers/git.py:150-152` and `web_git.py:409-416`, plus a read-only call to the live host (0.22.2): `{"ghReady":true,"pr":{"url":"…/pull/975","state":"MERGED","number":975}}`, and `"pr":null` for `/tmp`.
- Integration: expect additive conflicts with #1462 in `APIClient+Git.swift`, `HermesGitClient.swift` and `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests.swift`. Keep both sides.

**Decisions made overnight**
- A failed or timed-out read shows no row and no alert, and it counts toward the 60 s freshness window. (Alt: keep the previous link until a read succeeds.)
- Icons: `arrow.triangle.pull` for the PR row, `link` for Copy Link. (Alt: `doc.on.doc`, or no icons.)
- Most European locales keep the English "Pull request #N". ru, ja, zh, ko, ar, he and ur get translated terms. All are `needs_review`. (Alt: translate the term everywhere.)

Restacked in the integration stack; conflicts resolved per integration notes.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`: 113 passed, 0 failed. This adds 9 tests: ship-info request and mapping, unusable replies, a slow read never holding Changes, a branch switch dropping the link, a late answer after a folder change, a push forcing a re-read, a switch clearing the link before re-reads, leaving the chat cancelling the read, and a switch that finishes off screen reading nothing.
- Red first: against stubs, the first 6 tests failed (nil link, no ship-info request, no read started). The lifecycle fixes then failed first too: the old #42 link still showed after a switch, it landed after the chat left, and a second read started off screen ("2" vs "1").
- Repair 436aa41e: the same two classes plus `LocalizationCatalogTests`, 118 passed, 0 failed. It adds `testAFailedPullRequestReadDropsTheLink`, red under a mutation that kept the last link after a failed read.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly

- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (pinned upstream + live host)

FileTreeNode.init (HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FileTree.swift:20-21) trims whitespace from every entry's name and path. title: chore(scripts): let test-sim builds take turns on 16 GB Macs
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: a maintainer-approved chore from the speed retro of the epic #1361 overnight batch.

## What changed

On a 16 GB Mac, two worktrees running `scripts/test-sim` at once (two booted simulators plus two `xcodebuild` runs) page memory until `sim-doctor` reports MEMORY. In the #1361 batch that forced the run down to one lane for about 9 hours.

On a Mac with 16 GB of RAM or less, `test-sim` now waits on one host build lock (`~/Library/Caches/HermexSimulatorLocks/host-build.lock`, up to an hour) after taking its checkout and device locks, before it boots and builds. The lock is held by the same inherited descriptors as the existing locks, so a crashed runner's child keeps it until it exits. Larger Macs behave exactly as before. The personal `run-sim.sh` helper takes the same lock with macOS `lockf -k`. I checked that `lockf` and Python's `fcntl.flock` exclude each other. `DEVELOPMENT.md` § Local XCTest documents it.

## How it was tested

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 61 tests, OK. The new `test_small_host_runs_one_build_at_a_time_across_devices` fails without the change: with the host lock held, a 16 GB host returns non-zero without building, and a 32 GB host runs.
- Lock interop: Python `fcntl.flock` held → `lockf -t 0` on the same file exits 75 (already locked); after release it exits 0.
- No app code changes, so no simulator run.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with GPT-6.1 Sol. Sol verdict: approved

title: fix(tests): make six timing-sensitive tests wait on events, and find the CI hang after NetworkPathMonitorTests
body:
**What the user gets:** CI that fails only on real regressions, so stacked batches merge without rerun rounds.
**Why it matters:** The epic #1361 merge walk needed 4 CI reruns and lost about 80 minutes to a hung job, all on tests no PR in that stack touched. Every rerun is a full ~30-minute macOS suite.
**Cost:** Small to medium. Tests and test support only; no app code unless a test exposes a real race.

## Problem

Six existing tests fail intermittently under a loaded CI runner, and one CI job hung. Each passed on rerun with unchanged code. They all predate the #1361 batch: none of its PRs edits these tests. Most wait on a fixed deadline or a short RPC timeout instead of on the event they assert.

| Test | Added by | Failing run |
|---|---|---|
| `BotMentionTests.swift:226` `HermesChatMentionTests.testABotChatLoadsItsRostersPictures` | #1164 | [40969277571](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/40969277571) (#1458), [41085072866 attempt 1](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41085072866/attempts/1) (#1459) |
| `BotMentionTests.swift:355` `BotMentionChipTests.testChipRendererCachesImagesWithoutSharingDifferentBotAvatars` | #523 | [41085072866 attempt 1](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41085072866/attempts/1) (#1459) |
| `HermesChatTurnTests.swift:773` `testAnUnansweredCompletionFailsOnlyItself` | #1123 | [41085074766 attempt 1](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41085074766/attempts/1) (#1463) |
| `SessionListMutationTests.swift:2622` `testStaleCanonicalFallbackCannotReplaceNewerDestination` | #320 | [41085074766 attempt 2](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41085074766/attempts/2) (#1463) |
| `HermesSessionListTests.swift:504` `testALostSocketKeepsTheLastKnownStatesUntilTheHostAnswersAgain` | earlier | [40998048384](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/40998048384) (#1464) |
| `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests.swift:66` `testCompletionFlushesTheHeldFragmentImmediately` | earlier | [40991001023](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/40991001023) (#1463) |
| CI hang after `NetworkPathMonitorTests`: no output for about 80 minutes until the job's time limit, 0 failures | — | [41085072214 attempt 1](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41085072214/attempts/1) (#1468) |

## Hermex today

- `HermesChatTurnTests.swift:774` opens the chat with `rpcDeadline: .milliseconds(50)` and expects the unanswered completion to fail on that deadline. On a slow runner, other RPCs in the test can also miss 50 ms, so the wrong call fails with a transport error.
- `BotMentionTests.swift:228` waits for avatars with `waitUntil`, whose default timeout is 5 s (`TestWaits.swift:12`). The CI failures timed out waiting for avatar images.
- `HermesSessionListTests.swift:510–523` waits on three `waitUntil` conditions across a reconnect.
- `ci/check_test_waits.py` (#1429) already bans clock sleeps and polling loops. It does not catch a short production deadline injected into a test.

## Plan

For each test, find what the wait depends on and make it wait for that event, not elapsed time:

1. **Deadline tests** (`HermesChatTurnTests:773`): give only the RPC under test the short deadline, or drive its expiry from a test-controlled clock or fixture. Every other call keeps the normal deadline.
2. **Image and avatar tests** (`BotMentionTests:226`, `:355`): serve the avatar bytes from the scripted fixture synchronously, or await the loader's completion directly, so no network-like latency is involved.
3. **Ordering and reconnect tests** (`SessionListMutationTests:2622`, `HermesSessionListTests:504`, `ChatViewModelStreamingPaceTests:66`): read each with its fixture. Replace any fixed-time wait or timing assumption with an expectation fulfilled by the step it asserts.
4. **Hang:** read run 41085072214 attempt 1. Find the test that ran after `NetworkPathMonitorTests` and never finished, and make sure it cannot block forever: cancel its tasks in `tearDown`, and await expectations with a bound.
5. **Investigation first:** reproduce each fix with `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only <class> --repeat 10` before and after. A test that won't fail locally gets the fix from its CI log evidence; record that in the PR.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each listed test passes `--repeat 10` locally, and no fixed deadline under 1 s remains in a test except the one the test asserts.
- [ ] The hang's cause is identified, and the test can no longer block the job.
- [ ] If a test exposed a real app race, it is fixed in app code with that test as the guard, and named in the PR.
- [ ] No test is deleted to make CI green. A test that guards nothing a user would notice may be removed, with that reason in the PR (detest rules).

## Decisions

None. Recommend one PR per root-cause group (deadlines, avatars, ordering/hang) if the diffs separate cleanly; otherwise one PR.

## Out of scope

CI runner sizing or parallelism; the batch's restack/rerun flow (tracked in the t3-batch skill).

## Outside reach

None. Tests and test support only; no live server, other repos, or portal changes.

## Surfaces

Test target only (`HermesMobileTests`). No app surface unless a real race is found.

title: feat(settings): troubleshoot a problem with your Hermes agent
body:
**What the user gets:** A "Troubleshoot with Hermes" row in About opens a new chat where their own Hermes agent triages the problem and drafts a well-formed issue for their approval.
**Why it matters:** Reports can arrive with good repro steps but no server version or diagnostic evidence (#1351). Every Hermex user already runs an agent on the machine that holds most of that evidence.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable. Needs a mock first.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | feature |
| Effort | S–M (the origin change in the prefill flow is most of it) |
| Server dependency | none added; no new endpoint or companion capability |
| Builds on (merged) | #1396 `SupportReport` (9f974102), #1402 prefill router (c93f28c2), #1395 attempt stages (e617d04a), #1397 Diagnostics (04a2ef6d), #1477 playbook, `via-triage` form and label (5dc5e2ff) |
| Related | #1079 (remote reporting; not needed here) |
| Needs mock first | yes |

> Spec revised 2026-10-31 against `master` @ f35a52cb, after the dependencies merged. Cross-checked independently by GPT-6.1 Sol (xhigh).

## Problem
Report a Problem asks the user to diagnose and describe the bug themselves. They often can't tell an app bug from a server bug, don't know where the logs are, and leave out versions. The triage playbook (`.github/triage/PLAYBOOK.md`) already lets a Hermes agent investigate the server, read Hermex at the user's tag, check for duplicates, and draft a redacted issue that posts only after an explicit yes. Today the user has to find and paste the starter prompt by hand.

## Proposal
Add **Troubleshoot with Hermes** as the first row of Settings → About Hermex → Troubleshooting, above Copy Support Details, Diagnostics and Report a Problem (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift:28`). Keep those three rows; no new page or section. The section has no footer (mock A, picked 2026-10-31): the existing Report a Problem footer goes too.

Tapping it calls `AppIntentRouter.shared.openNewChat(prefilling:server:profile:)` (`HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift:35`) with:

- **text:** the starter prompt below, a blank line, then `SupportReport(server:).text` unchanged, built at tap time from the same active-server snapshot used for the destination.
- **server:** the active server's URL. **profile:** `nil`, which resolves to the Profile New Session uses (the remembered pick if still valid, else the host's current one), with no picker.

```
I'm having a problem with Hermex, the iPhone app I use to reach you. Fetch
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/master/.github/triage/PLAYBOOK.md
and follow it to help me triage it.
```

Call the router directly: don't invoke the Shortcuts intent, put text in a URL, or add another prefill path. The router throws (`empty`, `tooLong`, `tooManyWaiting`, `storage`); show each as an error and never claim a chat opened. The payload is a few hundred bytes against the 100 KiB limit, so never truncate it.

The agent fetches the playbook after Send. The app bundles no playbook, collects no logs, and posts nothing.

## Behavior the prefill path already has (keep it, document it)
- **Hermes only.** `NewChatWithContentIntent.destination` rejects webui, and `HermesNewChatDestination.route` rejects non-Hermes accounts; `openNewChat` itself doesn't check, so the About caller must. On a webui server the row is absent and the other three rows remain.
- **Queued, not instant.** Each tap is a separate durable record in the app-group inbox: 10 waiting at most, expires unopened after 24 h (`HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:183`, `:289`). Earlier texts open first, and a text waits while another imported-text chat is under review (Open Next / Discard). Opening closes Settings and selects Sessions (`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:764`).
- **Appends to an existing draft.** If that Profile's New Session draft already has text, the payload is appended after a blank line, and existing text, attachments and settings survive (`HermesMobile/Persistence/ChatDraftStore.swift:790`).
- **"Unsent" means no agent turn.** Opening a new chat may run normal connection, Profile and `session.new` setup (`HermesMobile/Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:425`); the triage text stays a local draft until Send.

## Change needed: origin, not just Shortcuts
The prefill flow labels everything as Shortcuts. It marks drafts `fromShortcut` (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:1013`), and `ShortcutTextNotice` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptSupportingViews.swift:1302`) shows "Added from Shortcuts. Review before sending.", "Another text from Shortcuts is waiting." and "Shortcut Can't Open" errors. Add a small, durable origin (Shortcuts or Troubleshooting) to the queued record and draft, and pick the copy from it. Keep review-before-send, the hidden-character warning, Open Next / Discard and recovery unchanged. Decode the new field tolerantly: a record written before this change reads as Shortcuts. Use no separate transport.

## What the report carries
`SupportReport.text` (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SupportReport.swift:29`) has the app version, build and channel, iOS version, device class, server kind and cached release, the tested Hermes release, and the current connection's latest attempt when it has one. It holds no server name, address or credential and makes no request. Diagnostics (#1397) stays separate: this row attaches no crash or hang reports. The user can copy one into the chat themselves.

## Availability
Show the row for an active, signed-in Hermes server with a saved connection. Add no reachability probe: hiding it on a failed check would make troubleshooting disappear during the problem. If the server is down, the request waits in the queue like any prefill, and Copy Support Details and Report a Problem remain the fallback.

## Surfaces
- **Entry points:** About only. A link from connection-error screens is a possible follow-up.
- **Multi-server:** the destination is the server captured at tap time; it never falls back to another server.
- **Targets:** main app only; the share extension and widgets are unaffected.
- **Reverse states:** nothing sends until Send; queued texts can be discarded; the chat is an ordinary deletable session.
- **Native quality:** VoiceOver label says it opens a new chat for review; localized row and notice copy (the prompt and report stay English); light/dark; Dynamic Type; no animation.

## Tests
- Activation queues the starter plus report for the captured Hermes server with `profile: nil`, and queues nothing on a webui server.
- A queued text that came from Troubleshooting opens as Troubleshooting, and a record written without the origin field opens as Shortcuts.
- Enqueue failures surface as errors.

Rely on the existing coverage for queue limits, ordering, append and Settings dismissal (`SharedDraftStoreTests`, `AppIntentNewChatTests`, `SessionNavigationStateTests`). Don't assert copy. Run with `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` the touched classes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The row queues the starter plus report for the active Hermes server and the New Session Profile, and never falls back to another server.
- [ ] An empty composer gets the text unsent; an existing draft keeps its text and attachments, and the payload is appended after it.
- [ ] Settings-origin text is never labelled as Shortcuts; real Shortcuts texts are unchanged.
- [ ] It works from iPhone (pushed Settings) and iPad (sheet Settings).
- [ ] Enqueue errors are shown; webui servers don't show the row; Copy Support Details, Diagnostics and Report a Problem still work.
- [ ] Manual: in one disposable session, sending the text fetches the playbook and reaches a complete, redacted issue draft without posting.

## Manual test plan
On a Hermes server: About → Troubleshoot with Hermes, check the notice and composer text, send, and walk a made-up problem to the draft issue, declining to post. Repeat with an existing New Session draft, with a remembered non-default Profile, on a second Hermes server, and with the server unreachable (text waits, then opens). On a webui server, confirm the row is absent. Check iPhone and iPad.

## Out of scope
Webui support, auto-sending, attaching diagnostics, collecting anything beyond `SupportReport`, other entry points.

## Decisions (settled 2026-10-31)
- **Design:** mock A, a plain row with no section footer (https://i7ej4tbejaf2.postplan.dev/v/1).
- **Waiting-text notice:** "Another text is waiting." for every origin, since the waiting text's origin isn't known to the chat showing the current one.
- **Row copy:** "Troubleshoot with Hermes".
- **Notice for Troubleshooting origin:** "Added from Troubleshooting. Review before sending." The hidden-character warning and waiting-text notice follow the same origin.
- **Repeated taps:** keep the existing queue behavior, one record per tap; no deduplication.

title: chore(triage): let a Hermes agent triage Hermex problems and draft the issue
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #1476 (the app row lands there, after #1396 and #1402).

## What changed

Bug reports reach us without versions, logs, or repro steps, and users often can't tell an app bug from a server bug. But every Hermex user already runs an agent on the machine that holds most of the evidence.

This adds a triage playbook that agent follows: `.github/triage/PLAYBOOK.md`. A user sends their Hermes agent a starter prompt (now in `CONTRIBUTING.md`). The agent fetches the playbook from `master`, asks for repro steps, and checks the server with `hermes dump`, `status`, and `logs`. It then reads Hermex at the user's release tag, decides whether the bug belongs to the app, the server, or push, and searches for duplicates and newer releases. Finally it drafts a redacted issue and posts it only after the user says yes. The issue goes through `gh` or a prefilled link to the new `via-triage` issue form.

Because the playbook is fetched from `master`, triage improves without an app release. Adapted from T3 Code's triage playbook.

## How it was tested

- Checked the host commands the playbook names (`hermes --version`, `dump`, `status`, `logs`, and the log layout) read-only against a live Hermes 0.22.2 host. Confirmed that `hermes debug` uploads to a third party, so the playbook forbids it.
- `via-triage.yml` parses, and its six field ids match the playbook.
- Docs and templates only, so no XCTest.
- Still to do: one real triage run, sending a Hermes agent the starter prompt pointed at this branch's raw URL.

- [x] Codable models: n/a

title: fix(live-activity): adapt colors to the host and system material
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1399

Stacked on #1478.

## What changed

The Live Activity painted fixed white-on-dark colors everywhere, so it ignored the iOS 26 system material, a light Mac menu bar, Always-On dimming and tinted/StandBy rendering.

- One widget-local `AgentRunPalette` replaces the fixed theme and status colors. It is built from the environment (color scheme, rendering mode, reduced luminance, contrast) and injected to every Lock Screen and Island region.
- Lock Screen: iOS 26+ requests system material (`activityBackgroundTint(nil)`); iOS 18–25 keeps the explicit dark card.
- Reduced luminance mutes status hues and the live dot to secondary; accented/vibrant rendering uses hierarchical styles with `widgetAccentable` glyphs; full color uses white ink with today's hues on dark hosts and black ink with darker hues on light hosts.
- Status symbols, words, timers, tap URLs, avatar source, #584 stale-Bot copy and #645 freshness chips are unchanged. No ContentState, relay, string or animation change.

Decision applied: [system material, adapt to the host](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1399#issuecomment-6531802819).

- Light-host colors for statuses the mock didn't specify: darker variants of each hue; stale and cancelled share one neutral. Alt: keep separate alphas, tune on device first.
- Dynamic Island follows the host `colorScheme` (supports a light Mac host). Alt: force a dark Island; if the device shows black text in a light-mode iPhone Island, switch the Island regions to the dark card.

title: feat(settings): keep local crash and hang reports with MetricKit
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1397

Stacked on #1479.

## What changed

Crashes and hangs on a user's phone leave nothing behind the user can share, so support starts with guesswork. Hermex now subscribes to MetricKit, stores the delivered crash, hang, CPU and disk-write diagnostics on the device, and lists them under About → Troubleshooting → Diagnostics (mock pick A: newest window first, kind, date window and build). Each report opens its stored JSON with Copy and Delete; Delete All asks first.

The payload is projected into a small tolerant `DiagnosticReport` (symbolication fields kept, exception messages, paths and device model dropped) and saved as one protected, backup-excluded file per report, deduped by content hash. Retention: 10 reports, 14 days, 2 MiB. Nothing leaves the device and no server is involved. Decision: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1397#issuecomment-6531802116. Fixture gate waived there: tests use documented-format sample payloads, since simulators never receive MetricKit data. `TESTFLIGHT.md` documents coverage and how to capture a payload on a device.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Support Details (#1396) is unchanged; alternative: add a diagnostics count and latest window to the report.
- The 14-day limit counts from delivery, so Xcode's simulated payloads with old windows survive; alternative: age by the payload window.
- Footer says "on this device" because the page ships on iPad; alternative: the mock's "on this iPhone".
- Only Delete All confirms; a single delete acts at once; alternative: confirm every delete.
- The list sorts by diagnostic window, newest first, with delivery time as the tie-breaker (fixed after review; one delivery can carry several windows).
- An open Diagnostics page and the About count reload when a new report arrives (fixed after review); duplicate or failed saves post nothing.

**Design**: https://alxw91sh7dqs.postplan.dev#issue-1397, pick A.

## How it was tested

title: feat(intents): prefill a new chat with content from Shortcuts
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1402

## What changed

Shortcuts, Siri and the Action button had no way to start a chat with text already in it. The new **New Chat with Content** App Intent opens a new chat prefilled with the exact text, unsent, on the chosen Hermes server and Profile.

- One app-level entry point, `AppIntentRouter.openNewChat(prefilling:server:profile:)`; the intent is its only caller. It stores the exact text and its bound server/Profile in the app-group share inbox (optional payload fields) and opens the bare share link. Each run is its own record (100 KiB, 10 waiting, 24 h).
- A Shortcut text opens only on its bound server and Profile (a fresh `profiles.list` confirms the Profile), never falls back, and joins that Profile's new-session draft once, untrimmed. A removed server or Profile offers Discard.
- Later Shortcut texts wait while a chat reviews one: the notice offers Open Next / Discard, and closing that chat or rebuilding the Sessions list opens the next.
- Design A: an inline dismissible "Added from Shortcuts" notice above the composer; bidi, zero-width or tag characters turn it into a warning with Remove Hidden Characters and Undo.

Decision applied: [binding decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1402#issuecomment-6531803865); owner shape note: one app-level entry point, the intent its only caller. Overlaps #1401's shared-import payload by design; resolved when the batch is stacked.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Later texts wait while a chat reviews one; the hold ends on Open Next, Discard or chat close; a server switch or sign-out defers the next. Alt: hold until Open Next/Discard only, or reopen at once after a switch.
- Queue copy is count-free "Another text from Shortcuts is waiting." Alt: plural-varied count.
- A failed `profiles.list` read keeps the text queued until the next trigger. Alt: retry at once.
- Unavailable destination offers only Discard (plus Not Now for a removed server). Alt: a "Choose Another…" picker.
- Hidden-character warning is count-free. Alt: plural-varied count.
- Remove Hidden Characters gets an explicit Undo button (the composer drops undo history on programmatic edits). Alt: register with UndoManager.
- No Profile and no active Hermes server: the intent throws and stores nothing. Alt: bind the first Hermes server.
- Tag characters in subdivision flag emoji are flagged like any tag scalar. Alt: exempt sequences after U+1F3F4.
- An edited connection that rebuilds the Sessions list opens the next waiting text at once. Alt: defer it like a server switch.

**Design**: mock https://alxw91sh7dqs.postplan.dev#issue-1402, pick A (inline dismissible notice). Screenshots: not captured (the prefilled chat opens only from a Shortcuts run, which needs a shortcut created on the simulator); the Manual test below covers it.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only SharedDraftStoreTests --only AppIntentNewChatTests --only ChatDraftStoreTests --only HermesSessionListTests --only HermesHomeSplitRoutingTests` on the final head: 157 passed, 0 failed. Earlier round with `SessionNavigationStateTests` and `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 185 passed. `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 2565 keys covered.
- Red: the first slice adds new API, so its 10 tests couldn't compile on master. Fix round 1: 3 new tests failed on the old code (second text reserved during review; a routed webui share blocked the Shortcut; deleted Profile opened a chat). title: feat(hermes): show the stages reached by a failed connection attempt
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1395

## What changed

When a connection attempt failed, the app showed one line of advice and no way to see how far the attempt got, so a user couldn't tell (or report) whether the status check, sign-in, or live socket was the problem.

Each attempt now keeps an in-memory record of five stages (Status, Sign-in, Identity, Live authorization, Live handshake), each Passed, Failed (HTTP n, timed out, couldn't connect, certificate) or Not checked. A collapsed **Details** disclosure under the advice on saved setup, onboarding and Add Server shows the rows and a **Copy Details** export (app, iOS, server kind, reported and tested release, UTC time, stages; no host, credentials or error text). Records carry attempt-number and retirement guards, and drop on a new attempt or any input edit. Documented in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`. Decision: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1395#issuecomment-6531801384

**Decisions made overnight**
- Support-report bridge, added during integration per [#1396's decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1396#issuecomment-6531801743): read-only `HermesConnections.lastAttempt(server:)` feeds About's Support Details "Last connection attempt" lines for the active server only (alt: defer to a follow-up).
- Details shows only the mock's failure categories; anything else reads plain "Failed" (alt: a case name per `BotFailure`).
- An unreachable address on onboarding/Add Server keeps the Hermes status read's record under the webui-path error, hidden only when a webui answered (alt: show Details only for Hermes-path errors, so no Details for an unreachable address).
- Saved setup drops Details on any address/username/password/header edit while the error copy stays as before (alt: keep Details until the next Connect).

title: fix(insights): keep last-known limit cards when a refresh fails
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1408

## What changed

**Problem:** a failed Usage refresh removed the provider limit cards, so a dropped connection looked like the limits had vanished.

**Fix:** `loadLimits` now resolves each quota probe to card, gone, or failed. Terminal statuses (`unsupported`, `no_key`, `invalid_key`) remove the card; a thrown request, `unavailable`, an unknown status, or an unusable payload keeps the previous card unchanged (original `updatedAt`) and marks it stale. A failed providers read marks every showing card stale, after the generation and cancellation guard. While any card is stale, Limits shows one notice at the top: "Couldn't refresh limits. Showing the last values loaded." First loads stay silent, and the analytics error state is untouched.

Decision applied: [build as written, Preserve #416](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1408#issuecomment-6531804172). Server status meanings verified read-only in `hermex-push` `plugin/hermex_push/quota.py` @2da6f660 and webui `api/providers.py` @c67fd2dd.

**Decisions made overnight**
- An `available` response that no longer builds a card keeps the previous card stale (alternative: treat it as gone and drop the card).
- The notice is the icon and the one sentence, with no detail line (alternative: add the underlying error as a second line).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ProviderLimitCardTests --only HermesMobileTests/InsightsViewModelTests`: 39 passed, 0 failed.
- Red before the fix: `testFailedRefreshKeepsTheLastCardAndMarksItStale` (refresh removed both cards) and `testOnlyTheNewestFailedProvidersReadMarksCardsStale` failed; `testRefreshThatNoLongerQualifiesRemovesTheCard` passes before and after to pin terminal removal.
- `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: covers all extracted keys.

**Design:** [mock](https://alxw91sh7dqs.postplan.dev#issue-1408), pick A.

Screenshots: not captured (the stale-limits notice needs a refresh that fails after a good one; cutting the network for a screenshot is off-limits); the Manual test below covers it.

**Manual test**
Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator

2. Turn on airplane mode (or cut the Mac's network) and pull to refresh: the cards stay, the orange notice "Couldn't refresh limits. Showing the last values loaded." sits at the top of Limits, and each footer keeps its old "Updated … ago".

title: feat(hermes): show a session's background processes, with output and Stop
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1420
## What changed

A Hermes session's background commands had no phone surface. The host already exposes session-scoped `process.list` / `process.kill` (verified at the pin `ca678285`), so this adds the read/stop surface without a shell:

- `HermesCall.processList` / `.processKill`: `processList` joins `isCancellationSafe` and `timesOutLocally`; `processKill` is neither and is never retried.
- Tolerant `HermesBackgroundProcess` (identity from `session_id`, ANSI-free 16 KB tail, optional display/exit fields; rows without usable identity omitted).
- `HermesBackgroundProcesses`, a `HermesDelegatedWork` sibling owned by `HermesChatActivity`: refresh on attach, turn end, sheet open and pull - never on a timer - bound to connection/runtime/generation.
- Glass toolbar entry + sheet: command/status/uptime, opt-in monospaced tail, confirmed Stop that re-lists before dispatch. `killed`/`already_exited` show output and exit code; `not_found` and RPC 4044 refresh; `error`/unknown keep the row and report the failure; no optimistic success. `-32601` hides the feature through the connection's missing-method cache; the offline cache's copy shows nothing. `process.stop` is never called (its handler kills registry-wide).
- Tests: `HermesBackgroundProcessesTests` (scripted `BotTransport` double, expectations only). Docs updated.

title: fix(chat): dictate into the caret without overwriting edits
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1418
## What changed

The voice update session now owns a UTF-16 range, not a base string. `ComposerVoiceDraftUpdateSession` captures owner, selection range, `revision`, `publishGeneration`, draft text and IME state; every write (local partials, server transcript, on-device fallback - one `applyDraftUpdate` path) replaces the owned span only when all still hold, and otherwise stops accepting updates and leaves the draft and caret untouched with a one-line explanation in the existing voice status. title: fix(persistence): never clobber an unreadable drafts file
body:
## Linked issue

No linked issue - maintainer-approved bug fix from a session bug scan.
## What changed

A drafts file that exists but cannot be read (a pre-first-unlock launch against the protected file, transient I/O) read as an empty store for the whole process lifetime, and the next debounced write replaced the intact `drafts.json` with that empty state - destroying drafts a later read would have recovered. `ChatDraftFilePersistence` now reports an existing-but-unreadable file (decode failures stay treated as empty, as before); `ChatDraftStore` keeps retrying the read on every access instead of marking itself loaded, and persists nothing while the last read failed, so the intact file survives and the debounced retry picks the write back up once a read succeeds. title: fix(intents): keep the Shortcut prefill's server URL out of the app group
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On a phone with a Hermes server configured, run the **New Chat with
   Content** Shortcut from #1485 (or any Shortcut that uses its intent), bound
   to that server.
2. Before opening Hermex, read the pending item's `payload.json` in the app
   group's share inbox (simulator: the app group container under
   `Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices/<udid>/data/Containers/Shared/AppGroup/`).

### Expected behavior

The app group holds no server URL. `HermesProfileNameCache` already keys its
entries by a digest of the server URL "so the app group holds no server URL"
(`HermesMobile/AppIntents/ProfileEntity.swift:329-333`), and `AGENTS.md` keeps
credential-like values, server URLs included, in the Keychain.

### Actual behavior

`SharedDraftPayload.init` stores the bound server as
`shortcut?.server.absoluteString`
(`HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:35`), and `writeJSON`
writes it in plaintext (`:817-820`) with `completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication`
protection (`:835`). The item can sit there for up to
`shortcutTextLifetime`, 24 hours (`:186`). The app group container is
readable by all three extensions and is included in device backups, so the
URL lands in backups too.

The bound-server check on consume is fine; this is only about what is written
to disk.

A possible fix, following the Profile-name cache: store a digest of the server
URL (or the server registry's ID) in the payload and resolve it against the
registry when the app consumes the item. The "was removed from Hermex" alert
(`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:56`) currently interpolates the URL; it would
need the server's display name, or generic copy once the server is gone.

### Impact

Minor bug

### App version / commit

master at f35a52c (introduced in #1485, c93f28c)

### iOS version and device

Found by code review; not reproduced on a device.

### Server kind and version

Hermes (any; client-side only)

### How the phone reaches the server

Other (independent of connection path)

---

title: feat(chat): send a message typed offline once the chat reconnects
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1407

## What changed

If you typed a message in a Hermes chat while offline, Send was refused, so you had to wait for the connection and tap Send again. Now one plain-text Send waits. It shows as a dimmed bubble with "Waiting for connection · Cancel" and is saved in `ChatDraft.waitingSend`. The next live attach sends it once. It also waits when its `prompt.submit` finds no connection before the write. There is no new RPC: `prompt.submit` is reused, which has no idempotency key at the pin, so the app sends once and never retries. A lost answer keeps the #508 hold and never resends. Cancel, the 10-minute expiry, leaving the chat and a relaunch all put the text back in the composer, ahead of anything typed since. Backgrounding pauses a delivery. The foreground reattach resumes it.

Applied the [binding decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1407#issuecomment-6548736235): Design A, 10-minute expiry, #508 kept, no "Queued" promise. At the pin, a busy submit follows the host's `busy_input_mode`.

**Decisions made overnight**
- The 10-minute notice uses the chat's existing ActionToast for 4 s (alternative: a composer error line)
- The offline status line stays "Reconnect to send messages." (alternative: new copy)
- Leaving during a write lets that write finish. An unsent write returns the text (alternative: cancel the delivery task)
- Only a pre-dispatch transport/URLError NotSent waits (alternative: `.stale` waits too)
- No sent haptic or notification offer for a waiting send (alternative: play the sent haptic)
- A delivery stopped by backgrounding waits again for the foreground (alternative: return the text to the composer)
- A hold that fails shows the existing "Reconnect to the server to send a message." and keeps the text (alternative: new copy for a storage failure)
- While the waiting send is written, every other Hermes submission (Send, Steer, Queue, Stop & send, slash commands, goals) is held in the model on the shared `submitHermesPrompt` path. The composer's Send isn't greyed (alternative: observe the flag in the composer's `isSending`)
- The review limit was reached with serious findings left, so I fixed them once more and shipped without another review (alternative: hold for another independent review)

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` HermesWaitingSendTests, HermesOfflineCacheTests, ChatViewModelSendTests, HermesChatTurnTests, ChatComposerSendGateTests: 337 passed, 0 failed at the head (ChatDraftStoreTests passed earlier at 606107a7, and its code hasn't changed since). `--only HermesWaitingSendTests --repeat 10`: all 10 runs passed. String Catalog check covers all keys. `git diff --check` is clean.
Red evidence: with the admission stubbed off, HermesWaitingSendTests went 0/5 (`"kept"` ≠ `"waiting"`). With the review fixes neutralized, 4 failed (a send from the background, a send after leaving, a send after expiry, text lost when the write failed). Repair: the waiting-send guard moved from `send()` onto the shared Hermes submit path, and its test now sends a Queue after a reconnect onto a running reply. Before the fix, the wire carried `["And this", "Ship it"]`, not `["Ship it"]`. `testALostAnswerKeepsTheTextAndNeverResends` had a test race (the reattach after the loss clears the #508 mark by design). It now holds that reattach with `connectGate`.

**Design**: mock https://psws2x0rnqs4.postplan.dev#issue-1407, pick Design A. Screenshots deferred to integration.

**Integration:** layer 1 of 5, base `master`. #1513 → #1515 → #1517 → #1518 → #1519 (native stack, merge bottom-first). No change in this layer (head unchanged, 91f07028).

**Manual test**
Device: physical iPhone
1. In a disposable chat, turn on airplane mode, type, and tap Send: the dimmed waiting bubble shows and the composer is empty.
2. Turn off airplane mode: the message sends once and the reply streams.
3. Repeat and tap Cancel: the text is back in the composer.
4. Repeat and kill the app while it waits, then relaunch: the text is in the composer and nothing was sent.

title: fix(chat): keep the reader's place when the transcript rewraps
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1414

## What changed

**Problem.** I reproduced this before changing anything. On a rotation, a narrow iPad Split View resize below 768 pt, or a Dynamic Type change, UIKit keeps the raw scroll offset while the transcript rewraps around it. A reader parked 40% into a reply mid-transcript landed 1.2 to 12.7 viewports away. A resize above the 768 pt cap did not move anyone.

**Fix.** The reader's place is now held as a reflow anchor relative to the row under the reading line (`ChatScrollPositionController` / `ChatScrollPolicy`):
- Rows report their frames tagged with the layout they were measured in (capped column width + Dynamic Type size). The first frame of a new layout captures the anchor from the old layout's frames, and the anchor row's new frames restore the same share of that row.
- A new `.reflow` mode reuses the hold machinery: quiet period, 2 s cap, put-back on size change.
- Reflow does not arm when following the latest content, at the top, during a gesture, or when a prepend or hold already owns the position.
- Any deliberate navigation cancels it, including a VoiceOver or keyboard scroll in the same turn as a content-size change. That case was the round-1 review finding, fixed in 5159e152. Follow, scroll-to-bottom and the keyboard also end it through `releaseHold`.
- Plan rows and compression reference cards now report frames too, so reading inside them survives a rewrap (Greptile finding, fixed in 37016d68).

Decision: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1414#issuecomment-6548737145

**Decisions made overnight**
- Reading line = top of the visible content, under the header (alternative: the viewport's center).
- A reading line in the gap between rows anchors to the end of the row above (alternative: decline to compensate).

Stacked on #1511, which sits on #1510. CI's red render-budget test is inherited from #1510 (tracked in #1516).

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` ChatScrollPositionControllerTests, ChatScrollPolicyTests, ChatTranscriptReflowTests, ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests, ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests: **49 passed, 0 failed**. The render budget's settled-row count stays 0 with the new per-row geometry modifier.

Red evidence:
- Hosted repro against base code: rotation drifted +2409 pt (6.2 viewports) one way and -2409 pt (2.9 viewports) back. iPad 694→507 pt drifted 1.2 viewports. Dynamic Type large→xxxLarge drifted 12.7 viewports. The 1024→1194 control passed. Each case is now covered by the hosted `testRewrapKeepsTheReaderAtTheSameShareOfTheirRow`.
- The cancellation fix was red on 4e12e6dc: 344 instead of 100. The deliberate scroll was put back.
- The plan/card fix was red on 5159e152: a reader 40% into a plan row landed at -0.25 instead of 0.4 after a rotation. Green after the fix: 49/49.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator

iPhone:
1. Scroll about 40% into a long reply in the middle of the transcript, then rotate. Expected: the same passage stays at the top.
2. While reading history, change Dynamic Type in Settings and return. Expected: the same passage stays in view.
3. Rotate, then right away scroll with VoiceOver or the keyboard. Expected: the scroll sticks and does not snap back.
4. While following a streaming reply at the bottom, rotate. Expected: it stays at the bottom and keeps following.
5. Expand a plan or a compression card, read inside it, then rotate. Expected: you stay in the same card.

iPad:
1. Read mid-transcript, then narrow Split View below 768 pt. Expected: the same passage stays in view.
2. Right after the resize, tap rows and links. Expected: each tap hits what is under your finger.

title: feat(widgets): show provider limits on the Home Screen and Lock Screen
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1409

## What changed

You had to open Usage in Hermex to see how much of a provider's subscription limits is left. This adds a **Limits** widget (Small, Medium, Lock Screen rectangular; Design B bars) to the existing widget extension, so no new target or App ID. Usage writes an app-group snapshot once its limit cards settle. The snapshot holds a hashed server key, the connection UUID, the Profile and the windows; it has no URL, credentials or session ids. Each row shows its percentage until its reset or an hour after it was measured, whichever is first, then shows "Open Hermex to refresh". Switching servers, signing out, or removing or replacing the connection empties the widget, and a load that finishes late cannot write it back. A tap opens Usage for that Profile only when the signed-in active server and connection still match, and never switches servers. Binding decision: [#1409 comment](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1409#issuecomment-6548736449).

**Decisions made overnight**
- A link that doesn't match opens the app as it is (alt: pop to the Sessions root).
- A link for a signed-out active server is declined, not held until sign-in (alt: hold it like session links).
- Once every window has expired, Small and Lock Screen show the tightest window as expired (alt: the "No limits yet" empty state).
- Medium's "Updated" shows the oldest measurement time among the providers shown (alt: the newest).
- A failed providers read publishes nothing, and a merge publishes exactly what Usage shows (alt: carry old entries forward until their deadlines).
- Colors: orange at 25% or less, red at 10% or less, matching the Usage card; no hue when tinted (alt: orange only).
- Gallery name "Limits", reusing an existing key (alt: "Provider Limits").
- Removing the Bot connection also empties the widget (alt: empty it only when the connection is replaced).

## How it was tested

- Red: `ProviderLimitsSnapshotTests`, 4/4 failing against stubs (expiry, generation guard, invalidation, link check). After review fixes it was 2 failed against the old code (newest-Profile ordering, connection replacement through `BotConnectionStore.save`).
- Focused green after fixes: `ProviderLimitsSnapshotTests`, `InsightsViewModelTests`, `AuthManagerStateTests`, `BotLifecycleTests`, `BotConnectionVersionTests`, `MoveToHermesCommitTests`, `SessionNavigationStateTests`: 141 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite (project file changed): 3757 passed, 1 failed. The failure was `BotChatPresentationTests.testThreadSearchOpensChronologicalDetailAndItsOwnComposer`, which is unrelated and passed 18/18 when run alone.
- `ci/check_string_catalog.py` covers all keys (10 new, all 17 translations). `git diff --check` is clean.

**Design**: mock https://psws2x0rnqs4.postplan.dev#issue-1409, Design B picked. Screenshots will come at integration.

**Integration:** layer 2 of 5, base #1513. #1513 → #1515 → #1517 → #1518 → #1519 (native stack, merge bottom-first). Rebased onto #1513 with no conflicts (String Catalog auto-merged and checked as the union of both layers' keys); no code change.

**Manual test**

`Device: physical iPhone`
1. Open Usage on a Hermes server, then add Small, Medium and Lock Screen Limits widgets. The Profile and percentages match the Usage card.
2. Wait past a reset, or an hour after Usage loaded. That row shows "Open Hermex to refresh".
3. Switch to another server or sign out. The widget shows "No limits yet" and stays empty until Usage opens again.
4. Tap the widget: Usage opens for that Profile. After switching to another server, the tap opens the app without switching back.

`iPad simulator` (regular width)
1. Tap the widget: Usage opens in the detail column for that Profile.
2. Tap the widget again, then pick another sidebar item before Usage opens. That selection stays.

title: perf(chat): settled transcript rows re-render every stream tick when SwiftUI skips .equatable()
body:
**What the user gets:** Settled transcript rows stop re-rendering on every stream tick in builds where SwiftUI skips `.equatable()`.
**Why it matters:** Long chats re-render every row ~30×/s while a reply streams if the row skip silently stops working.

Found by the render-budget test added in #1405 (PR #1510).

## Evidence
- CI run [41256364493](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41256364493) on PR #1510 head `3d87f96790a9238c2af5774f1e65f25afe012ff3` (Xcode 27.0 27A266a, iOS 27.0 24A434, Debug, parallel full suite): `Text-only ticks re-rendered 40 of 40 settled rows (streaming row: 30, host passes: 30); row comparisons: 0, unequal: 0`.
- So in CI SwiftUI never called `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock.==` at all while the host re-ran once per tick: `.equatable()` was bypassed and every settled row re-rendered on every tick.
- Locally (Xcode 27.1, same iOS 27.0 runtime, same Debug flags) `==` runs ~6330×/30 ticks (180 unequal, streaming row only) and settled rows render 0×.
- Ruled out locally: suite-order leaks, keyboard/first-responder leaks, scene-less host window, main-actor-isolated conformance, build flags, runtime. Remaining differences: the Xcode 27.0 toolchain/SDK, or CI's fresh unsigned iPhone 17 parallel clone.
- The same pattern (a View with a main-actor `==` behind `.equatable()`) guards `StreamingMarkdownDisplayedContentView` in `MarkdownRenderer.swift`.

## Suggested fix
Move the row skip off `.equatable()`: give `ChatTranscriptMessageBlock` value inputs plus one stable action reference (instead of ~15 closures), so SwiftUI's default field comparison skips settled rows without a custom `==`. Then the #1405 budget test should pass in CI unchanged. First confirm whether an Xcode 27.0 Release/TestFlight build shows the same behavior (it would affect shipped builds).

title: refactor(ui): one toast with tone, busy-to-result updates, and swipe to dismiss
body:
Fixes #1410

## What changed

Hermex had two toast systems that looked and timed out differently. Neither could be swiped away, and the Git one spun a `ProgressView`. Three non-blocking failures ("Session Action Failed", "Could Not Update Skill", "Could Not Update Task") also used modal alerts.

Now there is one `ActionToast`. It has a tone (neutral/busy/success/failure; the tone tints only the glyph and is the VoiceOver value) and detail lines. `show` returns an ID. `update(id,to:)` keeps that ID and restarts only the result clock, and `dismiss(id)` acts only on the current ID, so a stale Git completion can't overwrite a newer Undo toast or bring back one the user swiped away. Busy toasts never auto-dismiss. Results with detail stay 6 s, others 4 s. A sideways swipe of a quarter width or a flick dismisses (`ActionToastDismissPolicy`). Git uses the shared toast at the top of chat, and `GitActionToastOverlay.swift` is deleted. The three failure alerts are now failure toasts, and Skills and Tasks get toast hosts. Confirmations stay alerts. Three unused catalog keys are removed. Decision: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1410#issuecomment-6548736611

**Design:** mock https://psws2x0rnqs4.postplan.dev#issue-1410. Pick A (tone tints the glyph, static gray busy glyph); placement A (Git toast at the top of chat).

**Sheet errors:** a failed rename or project save keeps its reason inside the open sheet (cleared on dismiss or retry), and a project sheet can't be swiped away mid-save. Red then green: 7 re-pointed tests, and a concurrent row-failure test; then 219 and 186 passed.

**Preserved:** #549 Reduce Motion only fades and snaps back, nothing slides. #919 under VoiceOver the toast doesn't auto-dismiss, keeps focus and Close, and "Archived · Undo" shows in the iPhone list and the iPad sidebar. #1489 the share-composer skipped-items notice still shows once.

**Decisions made overnight**
- Removed the duplicate open-failure alert in `SessionListView`, so one failure shows one toast (alt: keep the alert).
- The pbxproj file removal was validated with focused tests locally and CI's full suite (alt: a local full run).
- Result toasts show a close × as in mock A (alt: close only under VoiceOver).
- A vertical pan that starts on the toast still does nothing, as before (alt: forward the pan to the list).
- On iPad, a failure toast goes to the detail column when Scheduled is open (alt: the sidebar).
- Also fixed the Hermes list's rename/project early-guard errors (alt: webui only).
- The swipe-dismiss guard is on the shared `ProjectFormSheet` (alt: webui call sites only).

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone Air> --only ActionToastStateTests --only ActionToastDismissPolicyTests --only GitWorkspaceViewModelTests --only SharedDraftStoreTests --only SessionNavigationStateTests --only LocalizationCatalogTests`: 183 passed. After a view-only refinement, toast state and policy tests: 7 passed. After the review fix, toast and navigation tests: 47 passed. `ci/check_string_catalog.py` passed.
- Red evidence: not possible on master. The new tests call `show`→ID, `update`, `dismiss(id)`, `Tone`, `ActionToastDismissPolicy` and `noticeShown(destination:)`, none of which exist there, so they don't compile.
- Review: round 1 had two serious findings. Failure-toast routing was fixed. The vertical-pan finding was withdrawn after a hit-test probe showed the toast overlay blocked list pans before this change too.
- **Screenshots: deferred to integration (16 GB host).**

**Integration:** layer 3 of 5, base #1515. #1513 → #1515 → #1517 → #1518 → #1519 (native stack, merge bottom-first). Rebased onto #1515, then one integration commit, e602e972. The only conflict was `ChatView` `onDisappear`, where both dismissals were kept. e602e972 merges Git feedback and the chat notices into one `ActionToastState`. Each `ActionToast` names its edge (default bottom). Git toasts draw at the top, and the share skipped-items notice (#1489) and #1407's 10-minute expiry notice draw at the bottom with neutral tone. New test: `ActionToastStateTests.testAToastShowsOnlyAtItsOwnEdgeAndANoticeAtTheOtherEdgeReplacesIt`. 295 focused tests passed on the stack's top head.
- Decision: chat keeps one toast state for both edges, so one toast shows at a time, and a notice shown during a busy Git action replaces it (alt: two states, so a notice and a Git toast can show together).
- Decision: changing workspace dismisses only the top (Git) toast, and a share or expiry notice stays (alt: dismiss whatever toast is showing).

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator, iPad simulator

iPhone
1. Git > Fetch in chat: a busy toast with a static glyph shows at the top, then the result. Swipe it sideways: it goes away.
2. Archive a session: "Archived · Undo" shows and Undo restores it. A vertical drag that starts on a row scrolls the list, and the toast stays.
3. Turn on Reduce Motion and repeat 2: the toast only fades.
4. A first failure on Scheduled shows there. After Back, a failure shows on the list.
5. On webui, fail a rename or project save: the reason shows in the sheet. Swiping a saving project sheet does nothing.

iPad
1. Archive from the sidebar: "Archived · Undo" shows there. Tapping Undo and Close both work.
