title: feat(chat): swipe between a message's images in the lightbox
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1412

## What changed

When a message had several images, the lightbox showed only the one you tapped. To compare screenshots you had to close it and open the next one. Now a tap opens a pager over that message's images, in message order, starting at the image you tapped. A "2 of 4" counter sits under the title (Design A). It hides along with the chrome and only shows when there is more than one image. Only the selected page and its two neighbours load. Pages outside that window drop their host and image, and they load again when you come back to them. Paging is off while the selected image is zoomed, so drags pan it. Pages keep the screen's safe area. A gallery with one image renders exactly as before. Hermes host-path sent photos still open BotArtifactPreview, and #404's zoom surface, the flick-down dismiss at fit scale, and #1424's visible-admission latch are unchanged.

Binding decision: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1412#issuecomment-6548736767

**Decisions made overnight**
- Hiding the chrome with a tap applies to every page, so it stays hidden when you swipe (alternative: chrome state per page, shown again on each new page).
- In Hermes chats, only pathless (still-sending) image chips join the gallery, and host-path chips keep BotArtifactPreview (alternative: no galleries for Hermes sent attachments).
- VoiceOver pages with the native three-finger scroll plus an adjustable action on the image, and off-screen pages are hidden from accessibility (alternative: a custom accessibilityScrollAction only).
- The pager is a non-lazy HStack: the ±1 window keeps its hosts alive and every other page is a black placeholder (alternative: LazyHStack that releases each page on disappear, so every swipe back reloads).

## How it was tested

- Full suite at fcea095e: `scripts/test-sim 1D3BFD51-…` → 3760 passed, 0 failed.
- Final head 75490f43: `--only ImageGalleryTests --only HermesChatAttachmentTests` → 35 passed, 0 failed.
- Red evidence:
  - Faults injected into the new code (no filter or dedupe, admission always true, paging left on) failed gallery order, the ±1 window, and zoom-stops-paging for the intended reasons.
  - `testZoomingALoadedImageKeepsTheZoomAndStopsPaging` read zoom 1.0 where 2.0 was expected (the zoom reset on redraw). After A, B and back to A, paging was still on.
  - `testAPageLeftWhileLoadingLoadsAgainWhenTheUserComesBack` never refetched.
  - `testThePagerOpensAtTheTappedImage` read offset 0 instead of 780 on the eager stack.
  - The layout probe found pages with zero safe area.
  - All of them pass now.
- `ci/check_string_catalog.py` covers all 2603 keys. The counter reuses the existing `%lld of %lld` key.

**Design**: mock https://psws2x0rnqs4.postplan.dev#issue-1412, pick Design A. Screenshots are deferred to integration.

**Integration:** layer 4 of 5, base #1517. #1513 → #1515 → #1517 → #1518 → #1519 (native stack, merge bottom-first). Rebased onto #1517 with no conflicts (`ChatView`, `ChatTranscriptView` and the project file auto-merged); no code change. The Git toast sits in a top overlay on the chat scaffold, so it can't cover the lightbox's full-screen cover.

## Manual test

Device: iPhone simulator
1. Ask for a reply with three images and tap the middle one. It opens on that image with "2 of 3". Swiping goes both ways in message order and the counter follows.
2. Pinch in on an image and drag sideways. The image pans and the page doesn't change. Double-tap to zoom out, then swipe, and it pages.
3. Swipe to the third image and flick down. The lightbox closes.
4. A reply with a single image shows no counter and works as before.

Device: physical iPhone
1. Tap the middle image of a three-image reply, swipe left and right, and check the counter.
2. Tap once to hide the chrome, then swipe. The chrome stays hidden and the next image is already loaded.
3. Flick down on a later page. It closes back to the transcript.
4. With VoiceOver on, zoom image 1, swipe up on the image to go to image 2, zoom it, and swipe down to go back. Image 1 is still zoomed and three-finger swipes don't page until you zoom out.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above

title: feat(chat): fold a scheduled task's host prompt into a "Scheduled task" card
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1413

## What changed

A scheduled task's run opens on the host-built prompt, which starts with the long `[IMPORTANT: You are running as a scheduled cron job …]` hint (or a skill body or missing-skills notice before it). It rendered as a wall of text in a user bubble.

In a Hermes `cron_` session (or a compressed run whose lineage root is `cron_`), a user row that opens on a closed cron hint now renders as a collapsed **Scheduled task** host card, styled like the delegation completion card: calendar glyph, title, skill chip, one-line preview. Expanded, it shows only the job's own text, plus Copy, which copies the stored row unchanged. A pure, failable `CronRunPrompt` parses the hint by bracket depth; skill names come from the skill markers before it. `/resume` opens a match under its lineage root, so a compressed run's tip gets the card there too. Any other row keeps its bubble. Binding decision: https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1413#issuecomment-6548736962

**Decisions made overnight**
- Missing-skills notice before skills that did load gets the card (skill names from the markers, body kept with its line breaks). Alternative: card only when every skill was skipped.
- `/resume` passes `match.lineageRootID`, so nil still means "ask the cache". Alternative: `match.identity` (`lineageRootID ?? id`), the session list's value.
- Run time stays in the meta row only, without a second Copy. Alternative: drop the meta row under the card, like the delegation card.

**Design**: mock https://psws2x0rnqs4.postplan.dev#issue-1413, picked Design A. Screenshots deferred to integration.

- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesTranscriptPagingTests --only HermesChatAttachmentTests --only ChatMarkerMessageClassifierTests --only LocalizationCatalogTests`: 58 passed, 0 failed. After the lineage-root fix: `HermesTranscriptPagingTests` 18 passed, 0 failed.
- Red: with `CronRunPrompt` stubbed to nil and the gate always false, 2 tests failed (the plain-hint row and the cron gate). With the gate checking the target key only, `testOnlyACronSessionOrLineageIsACronRun` failed on a tip under a `cron_` root.
- After review fixes: `HermesTranscriptPagingTests` + `HermesSlashCommandTests` 40 passed, 0 failed. Red first on the PR head: a missing-skills row's task came out `Rewrite. Keep links.` instead of `Rewrite.\nKeep links.`, and `/resume` opened a `cron_`-rooted match without `isCronRun`.

title: fix(chat): clear the stuck "Connection lost" banner after reconnecting
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: reported directly by the maintainer (a regular Hermes session kept showing "Connection lost. The bot may still be working…" after the connection came back, until the session was reopened).

## What changed

The banner came from the model picker's settings controls, not the chat's connection state. When the socket dropped while `BotChatControls.reload()` was reading `model.options`, the read failed with `BotFailure.transport`. Its catch-all text, which was written for Bot Chat, landed in `controls.errorMessage`, and the composer shows that error as a banner. A reconnect with the same connection and Profile never cleared it, and neither did a later successful read.

The catalog read now ignores transport failures. A lost connection is already the conversation's to report (`conversationDidDisconnect` → `hermesConnectionDidChange`), and every reattach reads the catalog again. Other read failures, and every model, effort, and Fast-mode change, still show their errors.

title: chore(scripts): stop test-sim hangs and leftover simulators from stalling 16 GB lanes
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: a maintainer-approved chore from the speed retro of the epic #1363 overnight batch.

## What changed

The #1363 batch lost hours to `scripts/test-sim` on this 16 GB Mac. Ten runs hung before the test runner connected, and each waited about 6 minutes for `xcodebuild` to give up while holding the shared host lock, so the other lane waited too. A deadlocked test sat out the full 30-minute run timeout. That timeout then left its simulator booted, and every later run on that device kept it up. The two simulators that ended up booted at once broke the other lane's boots twice.

- A test attempt whose log has been silent for 150 s before any suite starts is treated as the known runner hang, and goes straight to the existing reboot-and-retry-once.
- Each test gets a 3-minute allowance (`-test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 180`), so a deadlock fails on its own.
- On a Mac with 16 GB or less, the run always shuts its simulator down unless `--keep-booted` is passed: already-booted devices, timeouts, a runner that hung twice, and a boot that never became ready. Larger Macs behave as before.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` § Local XCTest and the test-sim line in `AGENTS.md` are updated to match. The AGENTS.md clause is a proposal; revert it if you'd rather keep that file unchanged.

## How it was tested

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 64 tests, OK. The three new tests fail on the old script: the silent-handshake retry, the stall detector, and the 16 GB shutdown cases (already booted, hung twice, timed out, never became ready, `--keep-booted`).
- A real run of `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only HermesMobileTests/HapticButtonTests` on this 16 GB Mac passed one test. `xcodebuild` accepted the new flags, and the simulator was shut down afterwards. An earlier attempt timed out in the existing `simctl terminate` step on a freshly booted device; the new rule shut its simulator down too.
- Not reproduced on demand: a real runner hang or a deadlocked test. The unit tests cover the detection and the retry path.

Proved with the script test suite plus two real test-sim runs on the iPhone 17 simulator.

title: test: stop the real on-device speech test from costing up to 4 minutes of PR CI
body:
**What the user gets:** faster PR CI: every macOS run gets back 25 s to almost 4 min, with no change to the app.
**Why it matters:** CI time is the main thing holding up merge walks. This one test is the slowest in the suite by far: in the run below it took 25 s, while the other 3,781 tests took about 112 s combined.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed.

## Problem

`ChatViewModelSendTests.testOnDeviceSpeechRendersAudioTheListenPlayerCanPlay` (`HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests.swift:59`, added for #1352) renders real speech with `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write` through `OnDeviceSpeech.render` and opens the result in `ListenAudioPlayer`. On a fresh hosted simulator, its duration swings widely:

| Run | Test duration |
|---|---:|
| [41274018537](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41274018537) (master) | 25.3 s |
| [41269881966](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41269881966) | 29.7 s |
| [41269878754](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41269878754) | 25.7 s |
| [41259368890](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41259368890) | 76.4 s |
| [41234882308](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41234882308) (master) | 112.0 s |
| [41256693285](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41256693285) (failed run) | 224.0 s |

The cost is most likely the voice's first load on a newly booted simulator, not the short utterance itself. That is inferred and needs a measurement.

## Proposed approach

1. Measure it locally: run the test alone twice on a freshly booted simulator (`scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ChatViewModelSendTests/testOnDeviceSpeechRendersAudioTheListenPlayerCanPlay`). Compare the first and second runs to separate voice warm-up from render time.
2. If a cheaper input (a one-word utterance, or an explicitly chosen installed voice) keeps the test meaningful and gets it under ~2 s on CI, do that.
3. Otherwise, skip it in PR CI with `-skip-testing` on the `Test without building` step, the same way #1085 handled the math benchmark. Keep it in the local suite, and note in its doc comment and in `DEVELOPMENT.md` § PR CI when to run it by hand (any change to `OnDeviceSpeech` or `ListenAudioPlayer`). The spy-based Listen tests stay on CI and still cover the view model's flow.

## Acceptance

- Over two or three PR CI runs, the test costs under ~2 s, or it no longer runs on CI and its doc comment says how to run it.
- No other test changes.

Found while measuring where PR CI time goes.

title: perf(chat): skip the math scan when nothing can open math, and keep shell variables out of math
body:
**What the user gets:** Long replies containing a price, a path, or shell text stream with about 11x less math scanning, and shell variables written as prose no longer turn into equations.
**Why it matters:** We decided against a "disable LaTeX" setting. Fixing the scanner helps everyone, and users who do use math keep it. Today a single `$` or `\` anywhere in a reply sends the whole reply down the slow scan, on every streaming update.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed. Unit tests plus one before/after benchmark.

## Problem

`MarkdownMathSegmenter.segments(in:)` and `MarkdownMathFormatter.replacingInlineMath` only skip their work when the reply has no `$` and no `\` byte. If either byte is present, even as `$5` or `C:\Users`, the reply is converted to `[Character]`, the code mask is built, and the reply is scanned twice. Streaming uses `MarkdownMathLayoutCache.uncachedLayout`, so this runs on the whole displayed reply for every update.

Measured on an M1 Pro, `swiftc -O`, production sources, ~8 KB reply, preprocessing only:

| Input | ms/call |
|---|---|
| Plain prose | 0.6 |
| Same prose plus one `$5` or one `\` | 6.8–7.3 |
| Same, with the prototype prefilter below | 0.59 |

The detector also reads some prose shell text as math (verified against current `MarkdownMathLayoutCache.uncachedLayout`):

| Input | Today |
|---|---|
| `Use $HOME/foo:$PATH.` | `HOME/foo:` becomes an inline equation |
| `Set $FOO_BAR/$BAZ before running.` | `FOO_BAR/` becomes an inline equation |
| `The shell prints $$ and $$.` | `and` becomes a display-math block |

Text inside backticks or code fences is already protected and not affected.

## Slice 1: byte-pair prefilter

Replace the `$`/`\` byte guard in both scanners with one shared, conservative check. It returns true only when the bytes could open math: `\(`, `\[`, `$$`, or a `$` followed by a byte that is not an ASCII digit, space, tab, or newline. The prototype was a single `utf8` walk tracking the previous byte. It must never return false for input the full scan would turn into math. False positives are fine, since they only cost the slow path.

Acceptance:
- Existing `MarkdownMathRendererTests` pass unchanged.
- One test showing a reply whose only `$`/`\` are a price and a path comes back unchanged (`.plain` with identical text).
- The PR body gives before/after numbers for the three inputs above.

## Slice 2: shell-variable false positives

Tighten the inline `$` and display `$$` rules so the three inputs above stay literal. Real math must keep rendering, including `$n$th`, `$x^2$`, `$\alpha$`, `$(4,-2)$`, `$M_S$`, and the #447 sample. Choose the narrowest rule that does this. One idea: reject an inline span whose content ends in `/` or `:`, and a `$$…$$` span whose body has no math signal by the existing `looksLikeMath` test. Record the rule you chose in the PR.

Acceptance:
- One test with the three false-positive inputs, and one with the real-math inputs above.

## Out of scope

- A settings toggle for math rendering (decided against).
- Code-heavy replies with `$HOME` inside fences still take the slow path (~2.6 ms on the same machine), because a real candidate exists. Skipping candidates that sit entirely in code is a possible follow-up, not this issue.

title: fix(chat): keep the reader's place when rotating a Plus/Max iPhone changes the width class
body:
**What the user gets:** Rotating the phone keeps your reading place in a chat, even far up the history.
**Why it matters:** The maintainer rotated an iPhone 15 Pro Max while reading high up a transcript and was dropped at the bottom; rotating back left them there, and the history they'd loaded was gone.
**Cost:** Medium; needs a Plus/Max iPhone (or simulator) to verify.

## Problem

Reported on a physical iPhone 15 Pro Max (iPhone16,2), build `c1c5f244` (master + #1510, #1511, #1514): scrolled up to read, rotated to landscape, and the transcript jumped to the bottom. Rotating back to portrait kept it at the bottom.

## Findings (investigated with GPT-6.1 Sol, read-only)

1. **Compact ↔ regular width rebuilds the chat (verified; certain on Plus/Max).** A Plus/Max iPhone is regular width in landscape. The Hermes home swaps its compact `NavigationStack` branch for the regular-width branch (`ContentView.swift:727`), and `HermesSessionListView.navigationSurface` swaps pushed navigation for `SessionSplitView` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:369`). `ChatView` is built separately in the compact `navigationDestination` (`:388`) and in `regularWidthDetail` (`:432`). The shared `.id(chat.id)` doesn't keep identity across different branches. So rotation creates a new `ChatView`, a new `@State` `ChatViewModel` (`ChatView.swift:415`), and a new transcript with follow on. The transcript opens at `ChatScrollPolicy.initialTranscriptAnchor` (`.bottom`, `ChatTranscriptView.swift:222`). The older pages the reader had loaded are dropped too, since the new model starts from the newest cached page (`ChatViewModel.swift:8435`). The navigation state keeps only *which* chat is open (`ContentView.swift:872`). This dates from the iPad/Plus-Max sidebar (#1316), not #1414. #1414's reflow anchor lives in the transcript's own `@State`, so a rebuilt transcript can't use it. Bots and legacy webui navigation branch the same way.
2. **The exact top has no protection (verified gap; trigger inferred).** At the exact top, and above the first measured row (where "Load older messages" sits), `ChatScrollPolicy.reflowAnchor` returns nil by design ("top stays top", `ChatScrollPolicy.swift:197`; caller `ChatTranscriptSupportingViews.swift:502`), so rotation arms nothing. The code already documents SwiftUI re-applying a default anchor on size changes at the exact top, and disclosure toggles pin against it (`ChatTranscriptView.swift:343`, `pinReader`). Rotation doesn't. This can jump the reader even without a size-class change.
3. **Lower confidence:** `rowFrameChanged` records a new layout even when `armReflow` declines (drag, momentum, prepend or hold active), so frames later in that layout never retry capture (`ChatTranscriptSupportingViews.swift:472`). Rotating right after a scroll or a Load Earlier can lose the anchor.

## Proposal

- For (1), keep the open chat alive across the size-class switch. See Decisions.
- For (2), make "keep the top" explicit during a reflow: pin the reader to `-adjustedContentInset.top` until the size change settles, the way `pinReader` does for disclosures.
- For (3), advance `rowFramesLayout` only after a capture was attempted with reflow allowed.

## Tests

- Controller test (fails today): attach at the top, report narrow-layout frames, report wide-layout frames with follow off, change the content size, simulate SwiftUI moving the offset to the bottom, and assert the reading line stays at the adjusted top.
- Hosted test: the Hermes session list in a window that crosses compact → regular width with a chat open and scrolled up. Assert the same `ChatViewModel` survives and the reading row stays in view.

## Acceptance

- On a Plus/Max iPhone, rotating with a chat scrolled up (mid-history or at the very top) keeps the passage, and rotating back keeps it again. Loaded older history stays loaded.
- Following at the bottom still follows after rotation.

## Manual test

Device: physical iPhone (Plus/Max), iPad simulator (Split View resize across compact/regular)
1. Open a long Hermes chat, Load Earlier once, read near the top, rotate to landscape, then back. You stay on the same passage both times, and the older messages are still there.
2. Repeat at the exact top of the loaded history.
3. While a reply streams at the bottom, rotate. It keeps following.

## Decisions

- **How should (1) be fixed?** Recommendation: keep the chat's model and reading position above the stack/split switch. Hold the open chat's `ChatViewModel` and a saved reading anchor (row ID plus fraction) in the navigation covers, keyed by chat ID, and hand them to whichever `ChatView` the current width builds. The landscape sidebar on Plus/Max stays.
  - Alternative: keep iPhones on the stack in landscape (`HermesHomeLayout.usesSplit` only on iPad). It's a one-line change, but Plus/Max lose the landscape sidebar that #1316 added.
  - Alternative: move to one `NavigationSplitView` that collapses in compact width. It's the platform pattern, but a large navigation refactor.

title: fix(hermes): keep a turn's cards in place after a mid-turn reconnect
body:
**What the user gets:** Thinking and tool cards stay with their own turn after a Hermes chat reconnects mid-turn, instead of piling up at the bottom of the transcript.
**Why it matters:** Found by the owner on a phone. A long tool call can quiet the stream and drop the connection, which then puts the turn's cards under later replies until the chat is reopened. Streaming over a tunnel is a core flow.
**Cost:** Small to Medium; reproducible with scripted fixtures, plus one manual check on a Hermes host.

## What happened
In a Hermes session, a turn ran tools, one tool call hung for about 180 s, the user sent a steer, and the agent then replied. Afterwards, that turn's Thought card and both tool groups rendered **below every row**, under the next turn's reply as well. Killing the app and reopening the chat put them back in place, directly above the steer. Not a regression from #1417; found while testing its build.

## Cause
Two gaps combine.

1. **A rebuild while a turn is running leaves that turn's cards with no anchor.** `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.rebuild(from:running:)` projects the host's saved rows (`historyTranscript()`). `HermesTranscriptProjection.project` attaches pending tool and reasoning rows to the next row that has text, and ends with `flush(anchor: nil)` (`HermesTranscriptHistory.swift`). While a turn runs, its saved rows end in assistant rows with no text plus tool rows, so its cards come out with `anchorMessageID == nil`. `ChatTranscriptView.transcriptLooseBlocks` renders nil-anchored cards after every row. Inferred trigger: the quiet stream dropped (Cloudflare closes quiet streams) and the reattach rebuilt the transcript mid-turn.
2. **Nothing replaces them once the turn ends.** `refreshHistory(after:)` runs only on a `message.complete` whose `persisted_turn.complete` is true. The host sets `complete` only when the turn holds exactly one `user` row (`agent/persisted_turn_receipt.py` on the live host; `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py:801` at `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA`). A steer is a second user row, so a steered turn never re-reads its history and the unanchored cards stay. After the next, unsteered turn the cards had still not moved, so verify whether that turn's refresh applied (`isIdle`, `merged.holds(replyRowID)`).

Verified against the host's rows for the affected session: the turn's tool and reasoning rows sit before the steer row, and a settled projection anchors them to the steer row, which matches the reopened screen.

## Proposal
- In `rebuild` with `running == true`, give the running turn a reply row even before it has text (today `streamingReply` exists only when `inflight.assistant` has text). Anchor the projection's trailing, unanchored groups to that row. Later live deltas and tool frames already attach to `streamingAssistantMessageID`, which `hermesReplaceTranscript` sets from `streamingReply`, so the turn stays in one place.
- At the end of a turn whose transcript was rebuilt mid-turn, re-read the newest rows even without a complete receipt (the same guarded path as `refreshHistory`, keyed on the turn instead of `final_assistant_row_id`), so the cards take their durable ids and anchors.
- Check why the following unsteered turn's refresh didn't apply, and fix it in the same slice if it is the same gate.

## Tests
- Scripted fixture: attach to a running turn whose saved rows end in tool rows. Its cards are anchored to the running reply row, not nil, and live frames after the rebuild join the same row.
- A steered turn that was rebuilt mid-turn re-reads history at its end; afterwards no card has a nil anchor and the transcript matches a fresh projection.

## Surfaces
- Hermes sessions and Bot Chat (both use `HermesChatTurnCoordinator`); webui is unaffected.
- Reverse states: cancel or failure after a mid-turn rebuild still settles the cards with their turn.
- Live host is hermes-agent 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`); the pin is 0.21.5. The receipt rule is the same at both.

## Manual test
1. In a Hermes session, start a turn that runs a slow tool (over 100 s through the tunnel), so the stream reconnects mid-turn. While it runs, send a steer.
2. After it replies, its Thought and tool cards sit above the steer, not at the bottom. Send one more prompt; the cards don't move.

title: perf(chat): stop re-deriving the whole transcript on every streaming tick
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1417

## What changed

While a reply streamed, every ~50 ms reveal tick re-derived the whole transcript (reasoning cards, row list, compaction card), and the chat screen re-ran its turn folds and end-of-turn rows, even though only the reply's text had grown. That cost ~2.7 ms per tick with 500 loaded rows, in the scroll path. Now a text-only tick costs ~0.06 ms.

- `ChatViewModel.replaceStreamingReply(at:with:)` patches just the reply's `TranscriptMessage` row when a flush only adds text to an already-shown assistant row with no reasoning. Anything that can change structure takes the full path as before: a blank reply's first text, in-text `<think>` reasoning, reasoning cards anchored to the reply, and every non-text change (history paging, tools, completion, cancel). The compaction card still re-checks each tick, because its placement reads message text.
- `transcriptStructureRevision` bumps on every full derivation. `ChatView` caches folds and end-of-turn rows in a `TranscriptStructureMemo` keyed on it plus their other inputs (fold setting, activity anchors, stream state, run outcome).
- `docs/agents/performance.md` gains the invariant and a "before you change the transcript" rule.

| Loaded rows | Reply update (before → after) | Folds + end-of-turn rows (before → after) |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | 0.32 → 0.03 ms | 0.28 → 0.001 ms |
| 500 | 1.32 → 0.055 ms | 1.39 → 0.004 ms |

Medians of 30 real reveal ticks on the iPhone 17 simulator, `-O` whole-module build, same harness on both trees ([method](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1417#issuecomment-6560943658)).

title: fix(hermes): keep a turn's cards in place after a mid-turn reconnect
body:
Fixes #1531

## What changed

If a Hermes chat reconnected while a turn was still running, that turn's Thought and tool cards could end up below every later row, including the next turn's reply, until the chat was reopened. A rebuild in the middle of a turn read the host's saved rows. Those rows end in tool rows with no text yet, so their cards had no row to attach to. A steered turn never gets the host's "whole turn saved" receipt, so nothing re-read the rows when the turn ended.

Now:
- A rebuild of a running turn always gives the turn its reply row, empty until text arrives, and the saved rows' trailing cards attach to it. The turn's later tool and text frames already join that row, so the whole turn stays in one place.
- When a turn ends after such a rebuild, the app re-reads the newest rows even without a full receipt. The new rows apply only if they hold this turn's prompt, something after it, and no card left without a row to attach to. Until one re-read applies, every turn end tries again, so an unsteered turn after the steered one also settles it.

Follow-up, not in this PR: tapping Load earlier during a rebuilt turn re-projects the cards unanchored until that turn ends (Sol nit S1).

## How it was tested

- Two new tests in `HermesTranscriptPagingTests` fail without the fix, with the cards unanchored: a rebuild mid-tool anchors the saved cards to the running reply, and later frames join that row; a rebuilt, steered turn re-reads its rows at its end and puts its cards above the steer.
- `scripts/test-sim` with `--only` on `HermesTranscriptPagingTests`, `HermesChatTurnTests`, `SteerMessageTests`, `HermesHistoryRewindTests`, `HermesOfflineCacheTests`, `HermesCompressClearTests` and `HermesChatLiveActivityTests`: 191 passed.
- A signed Debug build on the iPhone 17 simulator against the live Hermes host, in a disposable session I deleted afterwards. I couldn't make the tunnel drop on demand, so I reopened the chat while a 150 s tool ran, which goes through the same mid-turn rebuild. Then I sent a steer, waited for the reply, and sent a follow-up. The cards stayed above the steer the whole time, and a fresh reopen showed the same layout. Screenshots below: reopened mid-tool, steer sent, after the follow-up.

## Checklist

- [x] No new third-party dependencies

title: feat(chat): annotate the screen with Apple Pencil or a finger and send it to the agent
body:
**What the user gets:** Draw on whatever Hermex is showing, then send the marked-up screenshot to the open session. If the agent is mid-reply, the drawing queues as the next message.
**Why it matters:** "This button, not that one" is faster to circle than to describe, especially when giving feedback on UI the agent is building.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner's hands on an iPad with a Pencil and on an iPhone.

## Use case

When I review the agent's work from my phone, describing where something is costs more time than the fix itself. I want to circle the thing, say or type a line, and send.

## Proposed behavior

- A drawing layer over the whole app, in its own window (the same pattern as the App Lock window). It uses PencilKit, so there's no new dependency.
- Ways in: the composer menu, a hardware-keyboard shortcut, and Pencil double-tap or squeeze. iPhone users without a Pencil get finger drawing with a toggle, so normal touches still scroll.
- Tray: pen, eraser, undo, clear, Send, and an Exit control that stays visible in every state, including errors.
- Send captures the app window, composites the drawing on top, and attaches the PNG through the existing attachment path, with an optional typed or dictated line.
- If a turn is running, the annotation goes into the existing queue as the next message. At the pinned commit, `session.steer` takes text only (`SessionCorrectionParams`: `session_id`, `profile`, `text`, no extra properties), so the image can't be added to a running turn. The image goes up the same way as any other image (`image.attach_bytes`, then `prompt.submit`).
- If delivery fails or goes unconfirmed, the drawing and text stay in place and are never resent automatically.

## Acceptance outcomes

- A Pencil stroke follows the tip and stays after lifting.
- The tray never covers the composer's text field.
- A sent annotation shows up in the session as one message with one image.
- Exiting throws the drawing away, and the app works normally after.
- Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels on the tray, Reduce Motion, light and dark.

## Upstream dependency notes

No new endpoints. Uses the existing image attachment path (`image.attach_bytes`) and `prompt.submit`, checked against `gateway-contract.openrpc.json` at the pinned `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` (ca67828). Steering with an image would need an upstream change to hermes-agent and is not part of this issue.

title: chore(ci): free the runner at once when a newer push cancels PR CI
body:
A push to a PR cancels its running CI, but the cancelled run's `Report results` step (`if: always()`) kept the macOS runner for about three minutes, so the new run's jobs waited. On #1534 the superseded run's tests stopped at 20:12:06, its report ran until 20:15:04, and the new run's jobs started only at 20:16:52, five minutes after the push.

`Report results` now runs on `!cancelled()`, like the String Catalog step above it. Failures still report, and so does a hung test run: the test step's own 30-minute timeout ends it as a failure, not a cancel.

How it was tested: this PR's CI is cancelled once while Build and Test runs; on that run, `Report results` is skipped and the job ends at once. The rerun covers the normal path.

title: epic(onboarding): redo onboarding and Add Server around address, detect, sign in
body:
**What the user gets:** One short connect flow (first launch and Add Server) that starts with the address, detects the server, and offers only the sign-in methods that host supports, including Browser on password hosts.
**Why it matters:** Users ask for browser sign-in, and the official Hermes Agent app's Add Instance sheet sets a bar. Today first launch is 5 pages before the address field, and Browser is only used when a host has no password provider.
**Cost:** 2 issues, one PR each; one simulator/phone pass against the live host (it offers `basic` and `native_pkce`).

## Design

Picked **B, one adaptive sheet**: https://cuwlezoue3fj.postplan.dev (B1–B4).

## Issues (implementation order)

1. #1539 — feat(hermes): let users choose browser sign-in on a password host
2. #1540 — feat(onboarding): one address-first Add Server sheet for first launch and Settings *(blocked by #1539)*

## Where Hermex is today (verified on `master` @ 8de33e3b)

- Onboarding is Welcome, Features, setup prompt, Tailscale, Connect (`OnboardingFlowPolicy.pageCount = 5`).
- Onboarding Connect, Add Server (`AddServerView`) and re-sign-in (`BotConnectionView`) are three presentations; the first two share `OnboardingViewModel`.
- The Same Wi-Fi / Private network / Cloudflare Tunnel picker changes only placeholder and help (`OnboardingViewModel.ConnectionMode`).
- Browser sign-in (#708) is chosen only when `auth_flows ∋ native_pkce` and `basic` is absent (`HermesBrowserSignIn.isRequired(by:)`).

## Later (not filed)

- **Spike: sign in through a proxy's login page** (Cloudflare Access interactive). Needs per-server ownership of the proxy cookie for REST and WebSocket traffic and its expiry. Report go/no-go before building. Today's answer stays the service token under Connection Options.

## Decided against

- **QR code / link prefill:** not wanted.
- **Continue with Nous (account-level):** needs a Nous-issued client for Hermex, which we won't request. The official app's client (`hermes-mobile`, `hermesagent://`) must not be reused. A dashboard registered with Nous (`hermes dashboard register`) still signs in through Browser (#1539).
- **Token sign-in:** at the pin, `X-Hermes-Session-Token` doesn't pass the sign-in gate when `auth_required` is on (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:649`), and Hermex already reads the page token on a dashboard without sign-in (#1314).
- **SSH tunnel:** needs swift-nio-ssh (new dependency), weeks of work (host keys, key formats, background suspension), and a tunnel's local port can't be the server's saved identity.
- **Mosh:** a terminal protocol with no port forwarding.
- **Bonjour discovery:** Hermes advertises no service.

## How to work

`/t3-batch epic 1538`, or implement #1539 then #1540 in order. Manual steps in each issue go in one Branch TestFlight or simulator pass.

Researched with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol (xhigh) independently in T3 Code via Claude Code, then merged; upstream claims checked at `HERMES_AGENT_TESTED_SHA` ca678285.

title: feat(hermes): let users choose browser sign-in on a password host
body:
**What the user gets:** On a Hermes host that offers both, a Password | Browser picker, so they can sign in through the dashboard's page with saved passwords, passkeys or another provider.
**Why it matters:** Browser sign-in is a top user request. Hermex already has it (#708) but only uses it when the host has no password provider.
**Cost:** Small–Medium; needs a phone or simulator check against a host with `basic` and `native_pkce` (the live host qualifies).

> Slice 1 of #1538. Verified against `master` @ 8de33e3b and the live host's public `/api/status` (0.22.5: `auth_providers: ["basic"]`, `auth_flows: ["cookie","native_pkce"]`).

## Hermex today

- `HermesSignInMethod.init?(_:)` (`Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:479`) maps a status to one method: `.open` when `auth_required` is false, otherwise `.browser` only if `HermesBrowserSignIn.isRequired(by:)` (`HermesBrowserSignIn.swift:39`): `native_pkce` offered and `basic` absent, or the Developer toggle.
- That single method drives all three forms: onboarding Connect and Add Server through `OnboardingViewModel.signInMethod` (`OnboardingViewModel.swift:115`, set in `foundHermes` at `:411`), and the Hermes server sign-in/edit form through `BotConnectionSetup.signInMethod` (`Features/Bots/BotConnectionView.swift:417`), which prefers the host's status over the saved record.
- Reconnecting a saved browser sign-in already works on any host: `HermesConnection.beginSignIn` takes the `connection.oauth` branch before it looks at providers (`HermesConnection.swift:235`).
- The Developer toggle (`HermesBrowserSignIn.isForcedForTesting`, `forcedKey`, `offersTestingToggle`; UI in `Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift:188–215`) exists only to reach the browser path on a password host.

## Proposal

Separate what the host offers from what the user picks.

- Replace the single derived method with the host's offer: password when `auth_providers ∋ basic`, browser when `auth_flows ∋ native_pkce`, open when `auth_required` is false. Keep decoding tolerant (missing lists offer nothing extra).
- The forms hold the user's pick. Default: Password when offered (today's behavior for password hosts), else Browser.
- Show a `Password | Browser` segmented picker only when both are offered. A browser-only host shows no picker (today's behavior). An open host is unchanged.
- `BotConnectionSetup.signInMethod`: a saved `oauth` record defaults to Browser even on a password host; the picker can switch either way.
- Reverse states: switching a saved server from Browser to Password saves a record with no `oauth`; Password to Browser saves the new `oauth` and an empty password. The saved record never holds both.
- Delete the Developer toggle, its defaults key and its Settings rows; the picker replaces it.
- Custom headers: keep `HermesHeaders(_:signsInWithBrowser:)` validation. When the form's headers can't go with a browser sign-in, show its existing message under the picker (#1280 tracks sending headers to the browser page).
- Button copy stays as today: "Sign In with Browser" for Browser, "Connect" otherwise.

Not in this issue: provider names from `/api/auth/providers` (label stays "Browser"), the new sheet layout (#1538 slice 2).

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** onboarding Connect, Add Server (Settings, avatar switcher, session list, Move to Hermes), Hermes server sign-in after sign-out, Settings → server → connection edit. A webui server's Bots connection keeps its password form.
- **Multi-server:** the pick and `oauth` record are per server in its `BotConnection`; nothing global. The removed Developer default was global.
- **Targets:** app and tests only.
- **Native quality:** picker is a native segmented `Picker` with VoiceOver label "Sign in with"; strings in the String Catalog (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).

## Tests

- Offer decoding: a status with `basic` + `native_pkce` offers both; without `basic` offers browser only; `auth_required: false` is open (`HermesBrowserSignInTests` or a new `HermesSignInOfferTests`).
- `OnboardingViewModel`: picking Browser on a two-method host runs the browser presenter, not `/auth/password-login` (scripted `Presenter`, URLProtocol mocks).
- `BotConnectionSetup`: switching a saved server Browser → Password saves no `oauth`, and the reverse saves no password.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesBrowserSignInTests --only HermesMobileTests/OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests`

## Manual (phone or simulator, live host)

1. Add Server → live host address → picker shows Password | Browser → Browser → dashboard login page in the sheet → signed in, sessions load.
2. Settings → that server → switch to Password, save, relaunch: still signed in with the password.
3. Repeat 1 from onboarding (fresh install).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A host offering both shows the picker in all three forms; a browser-only or open host looks as today.
- [ ] Browser sign-in on a password host connects, survives relaunch, and refreshes.
- [ ] Switching method on a saved server works both ways and leaves no stale credential.
- [ ] The Developer toggle is gone.

title: feat(onboarding): one address-first Add Server sheet for first launch and Settings
body:
**What the user gets:** First launch is a welcome screen and then the same Add Server sheet Settings uses: address first, sign-in after Hermex finds the server, everything optional behind Connection Options.
**Why it matters:** Today someone with a server goes through 5 onboarding pages, and onboarding and Add Server are two different-looking forms for the same job.
**Cost:** Medium; needs a simulator pass of first launch and Add Server.

> Slice 2 of #1538. Picked design: **B, one adaptive sheet** — https://cuwlezoue3fj.postplan.dev (screens B1–B4). Verified against `master` @ 8de33e3b. Builds on #1539 (the sign-in picker).

## Hermex today

- Onboarding is 5 pages: Welcome, Features, setup prompt, Tailscale, Connect (`Features/Onboarding/OnboardingFlowPolicy.swift:4`, pages at `OnboardingView.swift:52–68`).
- Onboarding Connect (`OnboardingConnectPage.swift`) and Add Server (`Features/Settings/AddServerView.swift`, 496 lines) share `OnboardingViewModel` but lay out differently. Add Server opens with Network, Server, Connection Headers and Identity cards (`AddServerView.swift:37–60`).
- The Same Wi-Fi / Private network / Cloudflare Tunnel picker (`OnboardingViewModel.ConnectionMode`, `:28`) changes only placeholder, help and whether two empty Cloudflare Access header rows appear. No request depends on it.
- Entry points: `ContentView.swift:120` (no server), `:133` (webui re-sign-in with `savedServer`), `:791` and `:919` (switchers), `SettingsView.swift:124`, `SessionListView.swift:363`, `MoveToHermesView.swift:36` (with `moveSource`).

## Proposal

**Welcome (B1).** One page: icon, headline, "Add your server" (primary) and "I don't have one yet" (secondary). The secondary opens the existing setup prompt and Tailscale pages. The Features page is removed.

**The sheet (B2–B3).** `AddServerView` becomes the only form, used by Settings, the switchers, Move to Hermes and onboarding (`entry: .onboarding`). `OnboardingConnectPage` is deleted.
- Address field, the "Will connect to" line, and one status line under it (checking, "Hermes 0.22.5", or the error and its existing `ConnectionAttemptDetails`).
- The first tap is **Continue** (probe). Once a Hermes dashboard is found, the sign-in section appears: #1539's picker when the host offers both methods, username and password for Password. The button becomes **Connect** or **Sign In with Browser**.
- A webui server falls through to today's webui path in the same sheet (password field when it asks for one).
- The Replace offer for a saved webui server, saved sign-in rows and Move to Hermes's header offer keep working, in the same sheet.
- Connect pinned at the bottom.

**Connection Options (B4).** A row at the bottom (value "Default" or a count) pushes a page with: Cloudflare Access (Client ID and Secret, the two rows that today appear for the Cloudflare mode), Custom headers (`CustomHeadersEditor`), Name, Initials and color. Name defaults to the host as today.

**Remove** `ConnectionMode`, `ConnectionModePicker` and its sync logic (`syncAccessHeaders`, `withAccessRows`). Network hints stay only in failure advice (`BotConnectionAdvice`), which already names the network problem.

Out of scope: the Hermes server sign-in form after sign-out (`HermesServerSignIn` → `BotConnectionView`) keeps its layout and gets the picker from #1539. Provider names, QR codes and Continue with Nous are out of #1538.

## Surfaces

- **Entry points:** every one listed above, including the webui re-sign-in path at `ContentView.swift:133`, which opens the sheet with the address filled in.
- **Multi-server:** unchanged; adding still never disturbs the active server on failure (#17), and Move to Hermes still adds without switching.
- **Targets:** app and tests only.
- **Native quality:** Dynamic Type at accessibility sizes (sheet scrolls; Connect stays reachable), VoiceOver order Address → status → sign-in → Options → Connect, light and dark, keyboard Return submits. No animation beyond the system's section insert, and none with Reduce Motion. Strings in the String Catalog; remove unused keys (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).
- **Docs:** update onboarding mentions in `DEVELOPMENT.md` / `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` if they describe the old pages.

## Tests

- `OnboardingFlowTests`: the new page count and the setup path.
- `OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests`, `AuthManagerStateTests`: drop `connectionMode` cases; keep that empty Access rows send nothing and that the Access values, once filled, change the connection identity.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/OnboardingFlowTests --only HermesMobileTests/OnboardingViewModelIdentityTests --only HermesMobileTests/AuthManagerStateTests`

## Manual (simulator)

1. Fresh install → Welcome → Add your server → live host → Continue → Password → Connect → home loads.
2. Fresh install → I don't have one yet → setup prompt → Tailscale → back to the sheet.
3. Settings → Add Server → a webui address → password asked → added without switching away on a wrong password.
4. Connection Options → Cloudflare Access values → Connect against a host behind Access (or confirm the headers are sent with a URLProtocol test if none is available).
5. Move to Hermes → Sign In to Hermes opens the same sheet and adds without switching.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First launch is Welcome then the sheet; the setup pages are only behind "I don't have one yet".
- [ ] Onboarding and every Add Server entry point show the same sheet.
- [ ] Headers, Cloudflare Access, name, initials and color live under Connection Options and still save per server.
- [ ] The network picker is gone, and no test or string references it.

title: perf(chat): skip the math scan for prices and paths, and keep shell variables out of math
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1526

## What changed

A single `$` or `\` anywhere in a reply, even in a price like `$5` or a path like `C:\Users`, sent the whole reply through the slow math scan on every streaming update: about 10x the cost of plain prose. Shell variables written in prose also turned into equations (`$HOME/foo:$PATH`, `$$ and $$`).

- **Prefilter (slice 1).** Both scanners now share one byte walk, `MarkdownMathFormatter.mayContainMath`. It returns true only if the text contains `\(`, `\[`, `$$`, or a `$` followed by anything other than an ASCII digit, space, tab, or newline. Every `$` that can open math passes through, so a false positive only costs the slow path.
- **Shell variables (slice 2).** I chose the narrowest rule. An inline `$…$` span whose content ends in `/` or `:` stays literal; that's what catches `$HOME/foo:$PATH` and `$FOO_BAR/$BAZ`. A `$$…$$` span is rejected when its body contains whitespace and fails the existing `looksLikeMath` check, so `$$ and $$` stays literal but `$$42$$` still renders. A rejected pair is skipped whole, so its closing `$$` can't open a later span. `\(…\)` and `\[…\]` are unchanged.

Before and after, ~8 KB reply, `MarkdownMathLayoutCache.uncachedLayout`, `swiftc -O` on this Mac:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Plain prose | 0.52–0.56 ms | 0.57 ms |
| Same + one `$5` | 5.95–6.08 ms | 0.50 ms |
| Same + one `\` | 5.89–6.01 ms | 0.50 ms |

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Use $HOME/foo:$PATH.` | `HOME/foo:` inline math | literal |
| `Set $FOO_BAR/$BAZ before running.` | `FOO_BAR/` inline math | literal |
| `The shell prints $$ and $$.` | `and` display math | literal |

The remaining ~0.5 ms on plain prose comes from `containsDisplayDelimiter`, which was out of scope for this issue.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim E65FD38D… --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownMathRendererTests --only HermesMobileTests/MarkdownMathLayoutCacheTests` (iPhone 17): 55 passed, 0 failed. That includes the existing #447 fixture. The three new tests:
  - The three shell inputs stay literal, and shell prose followed by `$$x^2$$` keeps the equation. This test fails on master. With a rejected pair's closer reused (Greptile's case), it also fails: the prose turns into display math.
  - `$n$th`, `$x^2$`, `$\alpha$`, `$(4,-2)$`, `$M_S$`, and `$$42$$` still render.
  - A reply whose only `$`/`\` are a price and a path stays `.plain` and unchanged. It also asserts `mayContainMath` is false, so removing the filter fails it.
- In the real app: a signed Debug build on iPhone 17 against the live Hermes host, in one disposable session that I deleted afterwards. The agent replied with the four lines. `$HOME/foo:$PATH`, `$$ and $$`, and `$5` stayed literal, and `$x^2$` rendered as x². (The webui server returned `agent_runtime_stale`, so I ran this check on Hermes.)

![Hermes reply: shell variables and price literal, x² rendered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ee4295a-f890-4eff-9dd1-1fed50ff7463)

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (no `Codable` changes)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (no wire changes)

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on xhigh (codex_personal). Sol verdict: approved. Sol also ran a differential check of 91,728 inputs against master's scanner and found no prefilter false negatives.

title: feat(hermes): let users choose browser sign-in on a password host
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1539 (slice 1 of #1538)

## What changed

title: fix(chat): keep MEDIA: tokens inside inline code literal
body:
## Symptom

A `MEDIA:` mention inside inline code becomes a phantom media card. Writing prose that explains the syntax — e.g. "the \`MEDIA:\` line is the fallback" — turns each backticked mention into a download card mid-sentence. A bare \`MEDIA:\` is worst: the reference scanner treats the closing backtick as a legal path byte, so the card's file name is a stray backtick.

## Root cause

`TranscriptMediaParser.appendMediaSegments` computes `inlineCodeRanges` and already applies them to two of its three token branches:

- the `![` markdown-image branch skips cursors inside inline code
- the `file://` branch skips them too (and has a test, `testBareFileURLInsideInlineOrFencedCodeStaysLiteral`)

The `MEDIA:` branch alone had no such check, so inline-code-wrapped tokens were parsed as references. Fenced blocks were already excluded by the line-level fence scan.

## Fix

One condition on the `MEDIA:` branch, matching its siblings:

```swift
if line[cursor...].hasPrefix("MEDIA:"),
   !inlineCodeRanges.contains(where: { $0.contains(cursor) }),
   ...
```

## Testing

- New `testMediaTokenInsideInlineOrFencedCodeStaysLiteral` covers bare and path-bearing mentions inside inline code plus a fenced block, with a bare line-start token on the same line asserting real refs still parse.
- Full suite: 3802 passed, 0 failed on iPhone 17 (scripts/test-sim).
- Also replayed the parser's scan old-vs-new against a real assistant reply containing six backticked mentions: old produced 6 cards (five named "\`", one with a path plus trailing backtick glued on), new produces 0.

title: fix(chat): deliver files wrapped in backticked MEDIA tags
body:
Follows [#1546](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1546). There's no linked issue: Uzair approved this directly.

## What changed

When an agent wrapped a file it meant to send in backticks, as in `` `MEDIA:/tmp/report.pdf` ``, the user got inline code and no file. Models do format paths this way, and both upstream projects treat this form as a real file: `_mask_protected_spans` in hermes-agent's `gateway/platforms/base.py`, and hermes-webui's backtick handling from [#7359](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/7359).

Now a single-backtick code span holding only a `MEDIA:` tag with a path or URL value becomes a media card, and the backticks don't stay behind as text. Everything else stays code: `` `MEDIA:` ``, `` `MEDIA:<path>` ``, a tag inside a longer span, double-backtick spans and fenced blocks.

**Trade-off:** the gateway delivers this form only when the file exists, but the app can't check that. So an example path written as a whole tag in inline code shows a card that fails to open. We chose that over a file that silently never arrives.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMediaParserTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMarkdownImageTests`: 36 passed, 0 failed. PR CI runs the full suite.
- Real app on a live Hermes host, in one disposable session: a reply with `` `MEDIA:/tmp/hermex-verify-media.txt` `` showed a card with the right file name and no stray backticks, and tapping it downloaded the file to the save sheet. `` `MEDIA:` `` and `` `MEDIA:<path>` `` in the same reply stayed inline code. The temp file and the session were then deleted.
- No before screenshot was captured. Before this change, the tag rendered as inline code with no card, as #1546's test asserted.

Not tested on a webui server. The parser is shared, but the download path differs.

title: fix(composer): insert dictation at the caret and never overwrite later typing
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1418

## What changed

Dictation ignored the caret and always appended to the end of the draft. It also rebuilt the draft from a saved copy on every result, so anything you typed meanwhile could be overwritten. Now the words land at the caret or replace the selection, and later typing is never overwritten.

- **One span:** a session owns a range of the draft and replaces only that, and only while the draft is still what it last left. An edit undone back to identical text still counts as an edit. Otherwise dictation stops, leaves the draft and caret alone, and says "Dictation stopped because the draft changed." in a line you can dismiss.
- **New look (option A from the [mocks](https://xkn3a5yfqtop.postplan.dev/v/3), based on Grok Bot and T3):** tapping the mic drops the keyboard and locks the draft, and the bottom row becomes cancel, waveform, timer and finish. Cancel takes back words already written. The keyboard returns afterwards if it was up. Locking is why this stays one PR: it's what keeps typing from racing dictation in normal use.
- **Waveform cost:** the mic is sampled every 80 ms during capture only, and only the waveform view reads it, so the composer doesn't redraw. With Reduce Motion the bars stay flat.
- **Deliberately different from the mock:** no spinner while waiting, because of the no-continuous-animation rule. No Stop button in the row, because the mic is already disabled while the agent runs.

Thanks to @OddlyLabs, whose draft #1495 mapped out this range approach. This is a smaller version written fresh on current `master`, and #1495 stays open for now.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: red stop icon, status line above the composer, keyboard up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23e77240-5245-4ab1-9dab-8fdd8193205c) | ![After: cancel, waveform, timer and finish row, keyboard down](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f52d255-dca4-4980-ad6b-c6947f04fd08) |

## How it was tested

- **Physical iPhone (maintainer), this exact tree:** mid-draft insertion, selection replacement, cancel, server dictation and Japanese, per the #1418 plan.
- **`scripts/test-sim`:** `ComposerChipPresentationTests`, `ComposerVoiceDraftComposerTests`, `ComposerVoiceInputServerRecordingTests`, `ComposerUndoTests`, `ComposerKeyboardCommandTests`, `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 54 passed. The full suite runs in CI.
- **Simulator, signed Debug build:** the row with live waveform and timer appears, and cancel keeps the draft and refocuses the editor. This simulator shows no software keyboard on a plain focus, so the keyboard's return rests on the phone test.

**Surfaces:** composer mic and New Chat with Voice share `toggleVoiceInput`. Main app target only. No server contract change. The way out is cancel. The new string has all 17 shipped languages, marked `needs_review`. VoiceOver labels are set but weren't run with VoiceOver, and Dynamic Type and RTL weren't checked.

title: feat(composer): replace the scrolling toolbar with a fixed row and Model settings
body:
**What the user gets:** A composer where every control is reachable without sideways scrolling, with T3 Code's look and Official Hermes's model settings.
**Why it matters:** The keyboard-up toolbar holds up to eight controls in a horizontal scroller. About three fit at once on an iPhone 17 simulator, and nothing hints at the rest, so even the mic can start off-screen.
**Cost:** Large, and it needs the owner's hands on a phone.

Mocks of the agreed design: https://lspcnh6zw2nr.postplan.dev/v/3

## Delivery

One issue, one branch, one PR, with the slices below as commits. The owner chose this so CI and review run once, not per slice. Validate each slice locally as it lands.

## Agreed layout

- **Bottom row, never scrolls:** `+` · model and effort · mic · Stop/Send. The model label truncates when space is tight. Reserve room for the voice-mode waveform button that #250 commits to, next to the mic.
- **Keyboard down:** a T3-style one-line pill with the same controls in the same order: `+` · draft · provider logo and chevron · mic · Send. The logo is the only model identity in this state; tapping it opens Model settings.
- **Existing chats:** workspace and branch move to the chat header. The subtitle already shows workspace and Profile (`ChatToolbarSubtitleResolver`). Add the branch and the context ring, and make it open Chat settings. No extra line above the composer.
- **New chats:** a row above the composer for workspace, branch, Profile and context, like T3's `draftMode.controls`. It goes away after the first message.
- **Dictation row (#1549):** unchanged.

## Where each control goes

| Control | Destination |
|---|---|
| Files, Camera, Photos | `+`, usable during a run (#1436) |
| Model, effort, Fast, Approvals | Model settings, opened from the model label |
| Workspace, branch, Profile, context details | Chat settings, opened from the header, or the new-chat row |
| Context ring | Header in existing chats, new-chat row otherwise; tapping keeps the details |
| Dictation | Mic |
| Voice note | Still a hold on the mic, plus a labelled row in `+` so it can be found. Hermes sessions keep this gated off |
| Stop, Send, Steer, Queue, Stop and send | Trailing button; hold choices, VoiceOver actions and keyboard shortcuts unchanged |
| Retry, upload cancel, dismiss, Copy fix prompt, configuration notices | Status area above the composer; never inside a sheet |
| `/`, `@`, mentions, quotes, paste, recall | Unchanged editor paths |

## Sheets

**Model settings**, in this order: current model (opens All models), thinking control, Fast switch, Approvals row, Favorites, Recent.

- Changes apply one at a time and show pending or failed beside the setting. No sheet-wide Save.
- Keep the requested-versus-sent effort distinction (`sentReasoningEffort`).
- Fast appears only where the host reports it: `composerFastMode`, gated by `composerMayChangeFastMode`. Hide it otherwise, no "n/a" tile.
- No separate Thinking on/off beside the slider unless the server treats them as separate settings.

**All models:** search across providers and vertical provider sections, with large catalogs collapsed. Not sideways chips. Keep stars, Current Custom, Saved Custom and custom entry. `ModelPickerSheet` is shared with Settings and the Task editor, so check those surfaces.

**Chat settings:** workspace, branch and context, reusing the existing pickers and their capability and write-lock checks. On Hermes, the Profile row says that choosing another starts a new chat, because a session's Profile never changes (`HermesChatSettings`).

## Approvals

Wording follows Official Hermes: **YOLO, Smart, Manual, Off**. The Model settings row shows the state in effect and opens the choices.

Verified against `hermes-agent` at the pinned `ca678285` (0.21.5):

| Choice | Scope | Call |
|---|---|---|
| YOLO | This chat | `config.set` key `yolo`, already in `HermesCall` |
| Smart, Manual, Off | Host config, not this chat | `config.set` / `config.get` key `approvals.mode`; `tui_gateway/methods_config_set.py` persists it with `_write_config_key` and re-emits `session.info` to all sessions |

- Label the three modes **All chats in this Profile**. The desktop app tracks the mode per Profile. Official Hermes's menu doesn't state this scope, but our rule is that copy states the real consequence. Confirm the exact scope against the live host before shipping that label.
- **Off asks for confirmation first**, since every chat it covers then runs without prompts.
- **Descriptions** use the host's desktop copy: Smart "Automatically assess actions and ask when needed", Manual "Ask before actions that require approval", Off "Run without approval prompts". YOLO "This chat runs commands without asking".
- **State:** `session.info` reports `yolo` and `approval_mode`, and `yolo` is also true when the mode is `off` or the host launched with `--yolo`. `HermesChatRequests` only keeps whether the mode is `off` today, so extend it. Row value: Off, then YOLO, then the mode. A YOLO the session can't turn off shows locked (`mayTurnOffApprovalBypass`).
- **webui servers:** YOLO only (`/api/session/yolo`). Hermex has no mode call there. Verify against a running webui before adding one; never invent it.
- Add `approvals.mode` to `HermesCall` and `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md`.

## Thinking control

**Stop here for owner mocks before building the final control.** The owner wants to explore the look, and may relax the no-repaint rule for this one control. Record that decision here.

Whatever the look: only the levels the model supports, a static value when there is one level, unknown future level names preserved, VoiceOver adjustable, a list at the largest text sizes, one commit on release, and Reduce Motion respected.

## Slices, as commits on one branch

1. `+` usable during a run (#1436).
2. Fixed row, pill, header entry, new-chat row and Chat settings. This is the core fix.
3. Scope favorites and recents by server. `ModelFavoritesStore` and the recents store use one global key today, so they cross servers.
4. Model settings and All models.
5. Fast and Approvals rows.
6. Thinking control, after the mock pick.

## Surfaces to walk

- **Servers:** Hermes and webui, and switching between two servers: selection, pending changes, favorites and recents stay with their server.
- **States:** new and existing drafts, dictating and transcribing, streaming, offline or read-only (`holdsHostControls`), uploads, sheet dismissal restoring focus.
- **Native quality:** Dynamic Type including #1068's reachable Send, VoiceOver order, RTL, light and dark, Reduce Motion, hardware keyboard, localization of all new strings.
- **Performance:** no new invalidation of the composer from sheet or meter state.
- **Check at implementation:** whether Bot Chat shares this composer. `BotRoomComposerView` is separate and stays out of scope unless it does.

## Out of scope

Voice-first mode (#271) and the voice-mode overlay (#250), beyond reserving the button's room. Attachment phases (#1419).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No control in the composer requires sideways scrolling, at any supported width and at default text size.
- [ ] Every control in the table above is reachable in its listed place, on both server types where it applies.
- [ ] Choosing a Smart, Manual or Off mode states its scope, and Off confirms first.
- [ ] A rejected or pending change shows beside its setting, and never reads as applied.
- [ ] Favorites and recents do not cross servers.
- [ ] Dictation from #1549 and existing send behaviors are unchanged.

## Manual test plan

Device: physical iPhone.

1. With the keyboard up on a Hermes chat, reach `+`, the model label, the mic and Send without swiping.
2. Tap the header subtitle in an existing chat and change the branch. In a new chat, change the workspace from the row above the composer.
3. Set Fast and YOLO in Model settings, then confirm both from `session.info` or a second client.
4. Switch to Manual, open another chat on the same Profile, and confirm its row reads Manual.
5. Choose Off and confirm the prompt appears before it applies. Then set your usual mode back.
6. Repeat 1 and 2 on a webui server, where Fast and the three modes are absent.

title: feat(bots): add more avatars to pick from
body:
**What the user gets:** 21 more avatars to pick from in Edit Bot and the create sheet, next to our 8 shapes, and "Describe It" to have the host's model draw a new one.
**Why it matters:** bot faces only had 8 shapes. The first attempt, a 3D engine and a full studio ([#1552](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1552)), crashed and went blank on a real iPhone and was closed.
**Cost:** Small. Needs the owner's hands on a phone.

Source: silhouettes and eye positions from [Open Bot Avatar](https://github.com/DominikScholz/open-bot-avatar) (MIT), at `3a5119877844165eebafe57d3100da475f67d0a8`.

## Decisions
- The new avatars are flat shapes in `BotAvatarShape`, drawn by `BotAvatarMarkView` like our classic ones, with no background build.
- Our face view, blink, motion, 16 expressions, swatches and photos stay as they are.
- New avatars have upright eyes at their own positions, kept inside the body. Classic shapes keep their exact look, including their lean.
- Name-seeded faces only ever use the classic shapes, so no existing bot changes.
- The name is stored in the existing `shape` field. Hermes Desktop's source draws a circle for a shape it doesn't know, in the bot's color. Older Hermex builds fall back to a seeded classic shape.
- Upstream's `cloud` is left out: we already have a cloud.

- "Describe It" sends a short flat prompt through `prompt.btw`, whose tools are denied at dispatch. The answer is checked, gets one repair try, and is a draft until Save. It is stored under the Hermex-owned `hermexAvatar` look key, and the bot's `shape` stays for Desktop. The edited bot's model answers; the create sheet uses `default`.

## Out of scope
The 3D engine, studio, depth, eye placement, custom colors, and import and export.

## Acceptance
- A bot with an existing shape looks the same as before.
- Every surface shows a picked avatar at once, with no blank state, on a real iPhone.

title: feat(bots): let users fully customize bot avatars in a 3D Avatar studio
body:
Fixes #1551

## What changed

A drawn bot face only had 8 shapes and 11 colors. Now Edit Bot and the create sheet open a full-screen Avatar studio with 22 ready-made 3D avatars, any body and eye color, a depth control, movable eyes, 17 expressions, JSON import and export, and "Describe it" generation on the user's own host.

It's built on a native Swift port of [Open Bot Avatar](https://github.com/DominikScholz/open-bot-avatar) (MIT, pinned), with no JS and no new dependency. To protect battery, lists draw a cached body bitmap and repaint only the eyes on a blink. Live drawing runs only during a touch in the studio and the chat title's 30 s work beat. Bots nobody customizes keep their flat face, and Hermes Desktop keeps drawing their stored shape.

Three things reviewers should know:
- **"Describe it" uses `prompt.btw`, not a turn.** This changes what the issue first agreed. On a live host, a `prompt.submit` turn ran `terminal` and `write_file` with no approval, kept running after the socket dropped, and auto-continued on `session.resume`. `prompt.btw` denies every tool. It took 198 s on a slow model and can't be stopped, and the screen says so. `llm.oneshot` hit its 60 s host timeout three times out of three.
- **Save can delete a photo.** Changing the body on a bot with a photo warns first, then Save deletes the photo from the server, as agreed in the issue.
- **The app-facing surface is small.** Most of the diff is the engine and its golden fixtures. `BotAvatarEngineFace.swift`, `BotAvatarStudio.swift` and `BotAvatarGeneration.swift` are the places to start.

## How it was tested

**Tests.** `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only` on the avatar, generation, editor, lifecycle, inbox, Live Activity, mention, request and localization classes: 167 passed. The golden tests compare the port against frames recorded from upstream's JS. I didn't run the full suite locally, so PR CI is the full-suite gate even though this changes the project file. CI time should grow only by those focused tests, but I haven't measured it.

**Real app, against `scripts/local-hermes`.** On the iPhone 17 simulator, light and dark: open the studio from Edit Bot, pick an avatar, Done, Save. The host stored `hermexAvatar` and `shape` stayed in place. The inbox shows the 3D faces. "Describe it" ran its full path against the scripted model, including the one repair try and a plain failure. A successful answer was only proven by a direct `prompt.btw` call on a live host, not through the app.

**Review.** An Opus 5.5 review found nine issues, all fixed, including a save that could erase an avatar this build can't read and a cancel that dropped the editor's connection.

**Performance.** Release builds on the iPhone 17 simulator, 13 bots in the inbox, three runs of each:

| | CPU, first 20 s | CPU, 60 s idle | Memory at 20 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| master, classic faces | 0.27 s | 0.72 s | 320-372 MB |
| this branch, classic faces | 0.42 s | 0.80 s | 319-378 MB |
| this branch, 3D faces | 0.82 s | 0.77 s | 382-383 MB |

- Idle cost is the same with 3D faces as with classic ones, which is what the bitmap tier is for.
- Classic faces idle about 0.08 s of CPU per minute above master, roughly 0.13% of one core. The ranges nearly touch (0.71-0.75 against 0.76-0.89). Restoring SwiftUI's primitive paths didn't clearly close the gap, so I haven't explained it. The blink schedule is unchanged.
- Preparing one avatar takes about 50 ms (worst 91 ms) in an optimized build on the Mac, off the main thread and one at a time.
- That no timeline runs on a still face and that scrolling does no main-thread engine work come from code review and cache tests. Scroll hitches weren't measured.

**Not tested:** real battery on a phone, the Live Activity avatar, composer chips in the running app, the photo warning in the running app, and how good a real model's avatars look.

### Manual test plan
1. Long-press a bot, Edit, Customize Avatar. Check that Cancel changes nothing.
2. Pick an avatar, change depth, colors and eyes, Done, Save. Check the inbox, chat title, mention picker and Live Activity.
3. On a bot with a photo, change the body: Done warns, Save removes the photo.
4. Describe it: try a real description, and try Stop Waiting.
5. Open that bot in Hermes Desktop: it shows the simpler shape, and saving there keeps the avatar.
6. Leave the inbox open for a while and watch for heat or battery drain.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)

## What changed

Bot faces only had 8 shapes. This adds 21 avatars from [Open Bot Avatar](https://github.com/DominikScholz/open-bot-avatar) (MIT) to the Edit Bot and create pickers, and a "Describe It" row where the host's model draws a new one.

A short new prompt took 12 s and 40 s on a slow model, against 198 s for upstream's 15 KB prompt. The call can't be stopped, so closing the sheet only ignores the answer, and the sheet says the provider may still bill.
- **A failed model call is shown in the host's words.** `prompt.btw` returns a failed call as ordinary text, such as "OpenCode Go rejected your API key". The app shows that with no repair try, instead of "not a usable avatar".

## Linked issue

Follow-up to #1140 (closed). Takes over #1457 by @sommoMicc, whose commit is kept as-is on this branch, with their authorship.

A third commit, from review, lets the down arrow and the follow path scroll in a chat whose only content is live workers. That case is covered by reading the code, not by a run.

title: fix(intents): keep server URLs out of the app group
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1509

## What changed

Queuing a chat text from the New Chat with Content Shortcut, or from Troubleshoot with Hermes, wrote the server's full URL in plaintext to `payload.json` in the app group. The text only needs to know which server it belongs to, and the app already has that list.

The record now stores a SHA-256 digest of the URL (`serverKey`), the same form the Profile-name cache uses. The app matches the digest against its configured Hermes servers. Text queued before this change, with the old `server` field, still opens on its server; that record stays on disk unchanged until it is opened or expires after 24 hours.

A digest can't name a server that is gone, so the removed-server alert now uses one generic line for both origins, in every shipped language.

The offline cache was the other copy: SwiftData puts it in the app group by default, as `Library/Application Support/default.store`, and its rows name each server's URL. It now opens in the app's own container, which no extension reads, and an install's existing store moves there once at launch. If a store won't open, the app falls back to an in-memory cache, since the cache refills from the server.

**Still true after this PR:** a record queued by an older build keeps its URL until it is opened or expires. The app's own container is still included in device backups, as chat drafts already are.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim` with `--only`: `CacheStoreTests` 33 passed on the final code; `SharedDraftStoreTests`, `AppIntentNewChatTests` and `HermesSessionListTests` 103 passed on the record change. title: Open chat misses the user message and keeps "Working" for turns started on another client
body:
**Setup:** Hermex on iOS connected to a self-hosted Hermes gateway (hermes-agent 0.22.5 with local patches; the
README tests against 0.21.5). Hermes Desktop on macOS is connected to the same gateway.

**Steps:**
1. Open a bot chat in Hermex on the iPhone and leave it open.
2. Send a message in the same chat from Hermes Desktop on the Mac.

**Expected:** The open Hermex chat shows the user message as a bubble, streams the reply, and then clears the
"Working" indicator.

**Actual:** The reply text appears (after about 2.5 s, "Working for 1s" shows; the full reply arrives after about
14 s). The user message bubble is missing. "Working" stays after the turn ends; we saw it more than 1 minute later.
After going back and reopening the chat, everything is correct: the bubble is there, the reply is complete, and the
indicator is gone.

**Notes:** Turns started in Hermex itself render correctly. The gateway's `state.db` has both rows (user 23:24:57,
assistant 23:25:01), so the data is complete server-side. It looks like the live path handles assistant deltas for
foreign turns but not the user message or the completion event.

Possibly related: #1208 (server-initiated turns while the app is idle). Here the app is in the foreground with the chat open.

title: fix(chat): keep RTL replies with code on screen
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1068

## What changed

With right-to-left chat layout on, a reply that mixes prose with a code block or tool row ran off both screen edges, leaving only the middle of each row visible. It has nothing to do with text size. It happens at any size, for anyone with RTL on, which is the default on an RTL-language iPhone.

Forced left-to-right content (code, math, tool rows, images) flipped its alignment guides, so an RTL stack lined siblings up edge to edge and grew past its column: a 358 pt column measured 1,432 pt. I removed the flips and kept only the direction override. Narrow content still sits at the RTL leading edge, on the right, and a new test guards that.

The issue's other symptom, an unreachable Send, did not reproduce. That composer has since been deleted, and today's keeps Send on screen in RTL at the largest text size with a long Hebrew draft focused.

Everything stayed on screen, and Send stayed visible at both sizes with the composer focused. The session is deleted.
- Not run: iOS 18, the deployment target, because no runtime is installed here. Not checked: a physical iPhone, or images and math in a live RTL reply. Bot rooms share the fixed modifier but were not opened.
