title: fix(hermes): stop offering a downgrade as "Update available"
body:
**What the user gets:** Hermex never offers a downgrade as "Update available", and never calls a held build "Up to date" without saying why.
**Why it matters:** a host on a build newer than its release channel is told "A newer Hermes is available", and tapping Update restarts Hermes and moves it back to the older release. Found by the source audit in #1343; not reproduced in the app.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed beyond the usual simulator pass.

## What the host sends

`GET /api/hermes/update/check` at 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`; `hermes_cli/web_routers/actions.py`, `check_hermes_update`, and `hermes_cli/source_check.py`):

- **Rollback:** `update_available: true`, `rollback_to`, `source_version`, and `message` ("This build is newer than … Updating moves it back to that release."). `behind` can be `-1`.
- **Held:** `update_available: false`, `behind: 0`, `held: "downgrade"`, `source_version`, and `message` (the build stays put until a newer release ships).

Check both shapes against the source again at implementation time. A live host only sends them in those states.

## What Hermex does today

`HermesUpdateCheck` (`HermesUpdateClient.swift`) decodes neither `rollback_to` nor `held`. `checkCard` (`HermesUpdateCallout.swift`) then shows:

- **Rollback:** "Update available", "A newer Hermes is available." and an Update action. The host's `message` is decoded but not shown on this path.
- **Held:** "Up to date" and "Hermes … is current."

## Scope

- Decode `rollback_to` and `held` tolerantly.
- Rollback: a card that isn't "Update available", showing the host's `message`. The confirmation says Hermes moves back to the older release.
- Held: show the host's `message` instead of "is current".

## Not in scope

The update run itself and its receipts.

## Test

One test per state, at the layer that picks the card: a rollback isn't offered as an update, and a held build isn't called current.

title: fix(kanban): count a retried Card's age from its current run
body:
**What the user gets:** a retried Card's age and stale warning reflect the run in progress, not the Card's first attempt.
**Why it matters:** a running Card turns warning at 10 minutes and critical at 1 hour, so a Card retried a day after its first start shows critical the moment its new run begins. Found by the source audit in #1343; not reproduced in the app.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed beyond the usual simulator pass.

## What the host sends

At 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`), `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, `_task_dict`:

- `age.started_age_seconds` counts from `tasks.started_at`, the first-ever start (`kanban_db.task_age`; the column is only set through `COALESCE`).
- `current_run_started_at` is the start of the current run, in epoch seconds, or null with no active run (upstream `0ebaf162cc`).

## What Hermex does today

`KanbanCard.ageSeconds` (`HermesMobile/Models/Kanban.swift`) uses `age.startedSeconds` for a running Card. `staleness` and the Card row both read it. `current_run_started_at` isn't decoded.

## Scope

- Decode `current_run_started_at` tolerantly and use it for a running Card's age.
- Keep `age.startedSeconds` as the fallback for older hosts and webui.
- Measure against the server's clock, not the phone's: the field is absolute and the age fields are relative, so `created_at + created_age_seconds` gives the server's time at the read.

Check how `docs/agents/kanban.md` records the Card contract and update it. It cites the old pin.

## Test

One model-level test: a running Card with an old first start and a recent current run isn't stale, and a host without the field keeps today's age.

title: fix(hermes): show the host's reason when it refuses a file read
body:
**What the user gets:** when a Hermes host refuses a file read, Hermex says the host refused it instead of blaming Cloudflare Access.
**Why it matters:** on a host with `HERMES_DASHBOARD_FILES_ROOT` set, opening a file outside that root reads "Something in front of Hermes, such as Cloudflare Access, blocked the request." That sends the user to debug a tunnel that is working. Found by the source audit in #1343; not reproduced in the app.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed beyond the usual simulator pass.

## What the host sends

At 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`), `hermes_cli/web_server_files.py`, `_hosted_fs_read_guard`: 403 with `{"detail": "Path is outside the managed read boundary"}` (upstream `b9d9aeeb58`). An SSH Profile's permission error is also a 403 (`_raise_fs_backend_error` in `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py`).

## What Hermex does today

`HermesCronClient.accepted` maps every 403 to `BotFailure.rejected(403)` before it looks for `detail`. Its comment, and the one on that case in `BotProtocol.swift`, say Hermes doesn't answer 403 on these routes, which is no longer true. `HermesWorkspaceFileClient` and `HermesGitClient` both read through it. Nothing retries, so the wrong copy is the whole bug.

`HermesMemoryClient.accepted` (`APIClient+Memory.swift`) already does this correctly: a 403 with a reason reads as that reason, and a 403 with no reason is the proxy.

## Scope

- Make `HermesCronClient.accepted` read a 403's `detail` first, as Memory does. A 403 with no `detail` keeps the proxy copy.
- Check every caller of `accepted` (Cron, Skills, Insights, Files, Git). Files' path redaction and Git's generic refusal stay as they are.
- Update the two stale comments.

## Test

One test: a 403 with `detail` throws the refusal, and a 403 without one keeps `BotFailure.rejected(403)`.

title: fix(hermes): keep Memory on the host when a Profile's terminal is SSH
body:
**What the user gets:** Memory always reads and edits the Profile's own memory files, even when the dashboard's Profile runs its terminal over SSH.
**Why it matters:** Memory may show empty and editable, and a save may write a `MEMORY.md` on the remote machine instead of the host. Found by the source audit in #1343; not reproduced, because that needs an SSH Profile.
**Cost:** Medium until reproduced. It needs an SSH Profile on a test host, and possibly an upstream question. No phone needed.

## What the code says

At 0.22.5 (`bf0203a7`), `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py`: `/api/fs/read-text` and `/api/fs/write-text` route through `_fs_backend(profile)`. It returns the SSH adapter when that Profile's `terminal.backend` is `ssh`, and with no `profile` it uses the dashboard's current Profile (upstream `e1ab557716`, [NousResearch/hermes-agent#99538](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99538)).

`HermesMemoryClient` (`APIClient+Memory.swift`) takes the host-side folder from the Profile's `profiles.list` row, then reads and writes it through those routes with no `profile`. A 404 reads as an empty, editable file. So the outcome depends on the dashboard's Profile, not the one on screen.

Files and Git aren't affected: they already refuse any non-`local` backend (`HermesWorkspaceContext.isLocal`). Browsing an SSH workspace would be a separate feature.

## Decision needed

Whether this reproduces, and then which route should read Memory. Sending `profile` isn't the fix on its own: it would send an SSH Profile's host-side path over SSH every time.

Recommendation: reproduce it with `scripts/local-hermes` and a throwaway SSH Profile first. If it's real, look for a route that always reads the host, and ask upstream for one if there isn't any. Close this if it doesn't reproduce.

## Test

When a fix exists, one test on whatever decides the route. A live check on an SSH Profile proves the behavior.

title: feat(bots): watch and control a host's screen from the phone
body:
**What the user gets:** Open a bot's Screen in Hermex, watch it work, take over for a login or 2FA prompt, and hand control back, on Linux, Mac and Windows hosts.
**Why it matters:** Bots get stuck at logins, CAPTCHAs and payment steps that only a person can finish, and the official Hermes mobile beta is bringing this to phones. Today a Hermex user has to get to another computer.
**Cost:** Large, in one PR. It needs the owner's hands on a real iPhone in slices 1 and 2 and at the end.

## Handoff

The spec below is approved and has been through council review. The mock pick is made, so the "Before code" step is done. Start at slice 1.

**Where things stand.** No code, branch or plugin repo exists yet. The first comment on this issue has the script that proved the stock contract, and the setup for a Linux test host.

**Owner gates.** Stop and ask only at these. Between them, take the recommended option, keep going, and record each decision in a comment on this issue.

1. Slice 1 done: the owner runs a real iPhone test against a live, busy Codespace screen. This is the go or no-go for the native viewer, and falling back to noVNC needs the owner's dependency approval.
2. Slice 2 done: the owner runs the real iPhone suspension test. If a proxy reads as a clean close, the owner decides what happens next.
3. Slice 4 start: the owner unlocks the Mac test host, approves its driver repair, and approves the plugin install and any restart there.
4. Mac merge gate: the owner runs the phone test on Branch TestFlight.
5. Merge: the owner decides. Production TestFlight and tester invitations stay with the owner.

**Work order.** Do the slices in order, with one commit per slice, following "Every slice runs in this order" below. `sol-loop` follows the owner's account rules. Hold each phone test to a short manual test plan, and batch asks where a gate allows it.

**Plugin and app parallel work.** If delegates work in parallel, one owns the `hermex-screen` repo and another owns this repo, so they cannot collide.

## Summary

Linux hosts already support this through stock Bot Screen. Mac and Windows hosts show their real desktop through a new optional plugin, `hermex-screen`, built on the `cua-driver` that Hermes installs for `computer_use`. The app has one native VNC viewer for all three.

A screen is the place where the bot's `computer_use` acts. That place differs by host, and the app must say which one the user is looking at.

| Host | User controls | Mechanism | Setup | Takeover scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux. Also any host on Hermes 0.22 or newer whose terminal backend is Docker or SSH, which reports `terminal:<backend>` placement | The bot's own virtual desktop | Stock `display.*` and `/api/display/ws` | Desktop packages, or the sandbox image | That bot |
| Mac | The real logged-in desktop | `hermex-screen` using `cua-driver` | Plugin install, dashboard restart on older hosts, Accessibility and Screen Recording | Every bot on the host |
| Windows | The real logged-in desktop | The same plugin | Plugin install, dashboard restart on older hosts, Hermes running in the logged-in session, opt-in setting until testers pass | Every bot on the host |

**Choosing the source.** The app calls `display.status` first. If `supported` is true it uses the stock path. If it is false, it reads the plugin's `/capabilities`:

- A 200 means the routes are live, including a hot-mount on newer hosts.
- `Plugin not found`, matched as the whole message, means offering the install.
- A `detail` starting with `No such API endpoint` or an `error` starting with `Headless backend` means the routes are not mounted. The app offers a dashboard restart only if a second read still says so.
- `Not Found` means a newer host tried to mount the plugin and failed, so a restart will not help and the app points to the dashboard log.

A `-32601` hides the feature. For error `5300`, the app checks `data.code` first. With no code it is a state, such as a stopped screen, and the app shows that state. The app never branches on a version number or an operating system name.

## Scope decisions

| Topic | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Servers and devices | Hermes servers only, not webui. iPhone, iPad and iPhone Duo. |
| Viewer | Native Swift VNC client. No web view and no new third-party dependency. noVNC is the fallback only if slice 1 cannot show a usable picture on a real iPhone. |
| Gating | A per-server "Bot Screen (beta)" toggle, off by default. Turning it off hands back any control and hides the feature. |
| Naming | "Screen" in the UI, with "Take Over" and "Hand Back". A subtitle says "Bot desktop" or "This computer's real desktop". |
| Security | The normal app lock only. No extra Face ID step, no hidden app switcher preview, and no notice on the host. |
| Displays | Main display only on Mac and Windows. Frames are capped at 1920 pixels wide, and tap positions map back to true screen coordinates. |
| Streaming | Only while the view is on screen. No quality setting. The stream stops in the background and control stays. |
| Bot asks for help | It keeps using its normal chat reply. No screen opens by itself, and the app sends no "continue" message after Hand Back. |
| Setup in the app | Linux gets a Start button and an install command to copy, with no phone-driven `sudo`. Mac and Windows get a consent-gated plugin install and written permission steps. |
| Accessibility | VoiceOver reaches every control. The picture is one labelled element, and the app says plainly that VoiceOver cannot read the remote screen. |
| Locked screens | A clear "Screen is locked" state. Mac users can type the password from the phone if testing shows this works. Windows users are told to unlock at the host. |

## Control rules

Upstream treats a clean socket close as a hand-back and a dropped socket as "the human keeps control". Most of the mobile-specific risk sits here.

| Event while holding control | Result | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Switch apps or lock the phone | Control stays. The stream stops. | Must not send a clean close. `HermesGateway` closes with `.normalClosure` on background, so the screen socket needs its own lifecycle. A proxy may also close the origin socket with a clean code when the phone disappears, which would hand back mid-login. Slice 2 must prove this on a real iPhone through public addresses. |
| Connection lost | Control stays. The view retries. | The same reattach as below, with the existing backoff of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then 30 seconds. |
| Return to the app | Control resumes without a prompt. | A new gateway socket means a new viewer ID. If the lease's `viewer_hash` matches the saved viewer ID, call `display.lease.acquire` with the new ID and save it. |
| Close the Screen view | Hands back. | The close button says so while the user holds control. |
| Switch servers | Hands back. | Runs before the logged-in tree rebuilds. |
| Beta toggle off | Hands back, then hides the feature. | The same call as Hand Back. |
| Another person takes over | Last Take Over wins. This viewer drops to watching. | Close code `4000` on stock hosts, and the same code from the plugin. |
| 15 minutes with no phone input | Hands back, connected or not. | "Still there?" appears at 14 minutes if the view is open. The plugin enforces this on Mac and Windows. On Linux the app schedules a local notification and hands back when reopened. |
| App killed on Linux and never reopened | Known gap: the bot stays blocked. | Stock leases never expire and idle stop skips human-held screens. Recovery is a force Hand Back from any client or `hermes computer-use screen stop --force`. A persistent banner and a force action cover the common case. |

The app saves its raw viewer ID in the Keychain, keyed by server and profile, because the server treats it as a capability. It compares `viewer_hash` against the first 12 hex characters of that ID's SHA-256.

Hand Back always releases the saved ID, the one that holds control. It adds `force: true` only when this connection did not mint that ID, such as a server switch before control was retaken. The server releases only if that ID still holds control, so it cannot revoke another person's takeover. It returns success either way, so a hand-back counts as done only when the returned lease says the agent holds. A release with `force: true` and no ID clears any holder, so only the force Hand Back action sends it.

Retaking control on return can race another person's takeover, because stock hosts have no conditional acquire. v1 accepts that small window.

Takeover and return, in order:

1. The phone calls `display.observe` on `/api/ws` and gets a ticket (30 seconds, single use), a `viewer_id` and the lease.
2. The phone opens `/api/display/ws?display_ticket=` and frames start.
3. `display.lease.acquire(viewer_id)` takes control. The user types the login, and bot tools return `human_has_control`.
4. The user switches apps. Sockets drop and the lease stays.
5. On return, a new socket calls `display.observe` and gets a new `viewer_id`, plus the lease with the old `viewer_hash`.
6. The hash matches the saved ID, so the phone calls `display.lease.acquire` with the new ID and reopens the stream with a new ticket.
7. `display.lease.release(new viewer_id)` hands back.

## Stock contract

Read at `ca678285` (the pin, 0.21.5) and `bf0203a7` (0.22.5), then run against stock 0.21.5 in a Codespace over loopback. That run confirmed the handshake, a 1440x900 Tight update, single-use tickets (`4401`), eviction (`4000`), the viewer ID rules, and that a dropped link keeps the lease while a clean close hands back. A live Cloudflare tunnel returned `101 Switching Protocols` for `/api/display/ws` with no Origin header. Streaming over a public address is still unproven. Only solid-fill Tight rectangles appeared on that plain desktop, so slice 1 must test the other Tight types against a busy screen.

| Item | Facts the client must honor |
| --- | --- |
| RPC methods | `display.status`, `.thumbnail`, `.start`, `.stop`, `.observe`, `.lease.acquire`, `.lease.release`. All take the `profile` parameter. The `display.lease` event reaches every attached screen, which must filter on `profile_key`. The app does not use `display.install` in v1. |
| Viewer ID | The server mints it per connection. A reconnect gets a new one. Acquire always refuses an ID this connection did not mint, with `viewer_mismatch`. Release does too, unless `force` is true. |
| Handshake | RFB with security type None. The server's filter expects exactly 12 + 1 + 1 client bytes, then framed messages. It forces the shared flag on. |
| Client messages | Only types 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 150, 248, 251 and 255 are framed. Any other type closes the stream with `1003`. Types 4, 5, 6, 251 and 255 are dropped unless this viewer holds the lease. |
| Stream framing | Chunks of up to 64 KB that do not align with RFB messages, so the client needs a stream parser. |
| Close codes | `4000` control taken, `4001` screen gone, `4401` bad ticket (call observe again), `1003` protocol error. Policy refusal happens before accept, so the client sees an HTTP 403 on the upgrade. A close with `1000` or `1001` from the holder hands back, so `.goingAway` counts too. |
| RPC errors | Every `display.*` failure uses code `5300`. A refusal also carries `data.code` set to `viewer_mismatch`, so the client checks that first. On `display.stop` that code means a human holds the screen and `force` is required. |
| Clipboard | Xvnc never sends the screen's clipboard to viewers. Paste into the screen works for the lease holder, up to 256 KB. |
| Newer fields | `placement` and `image_switch` appear on 0.22. Decode them as optionals. Unknown fields never fail a decode. |

## The `hermex-screen` plugin

A new public repo, separate from `hermex-push`. It is off until installed, and it runs only on hosts where `display.status` reports no stock support. Frames travel directly from host to phone over the existing dashboard address, with no relay. A plugin can add REST routes and its own sockets, but no RPC methods, so everything goes through `/api/plugins/hermex-screen/`.

Proposed routes, which may change during slice 4:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /capabilities` | `{plugin_version, routes}`, in the same shape as `hermex-push`, plus the opt-in state on Windows. |
| `GET /status` | Driver version and contract state, permissions, lock state, display size, and the lease. |
| `GET /doctor` | The self-check testers run first. It reports pass or fail for each requirement, including driver resolution and schema and the private APIs below, and sends no input. |
| `POST /lease/acquire`, `/lease/release` | Take Over and Hand Back across every profile on the host, with an optional force. |
| `WS /stream` | RFB in the same format the viewer already reads. Auth follows the Kanban socket through the dashboard's own gate: a fresh `/api/auth/ws-ticket` ticket, with the connection's custom headers. A page token works only on loopback or `--insecure` dashboards. Like every plugin route, it carries no `profile` query, because Hermes refuses a secondary profile's plugin sockets with HTTP 501. |

| VNC side | `cua-driver` side | Measured on 0.28.2, Mac |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Framebuffer update | `get_desktop_state`, scaled, sent as one Tight JPEG rectangle when the frame changed | 142 ms |
| Button down then up | `click` with a desktop `target` | 299 ms |
| Down, move, up | `drag` with a desktop `target` | 1,100 ms |
| Wheel buttons | `scroll` with a desktop `target` | 326 ms |
| Key event | `press_key` or `hotkey`, to the window the last tap focused. The plugin applies events in order and brings the tapped window forward before any later key, so a password cannot reach a different app. | 13 ms |
| Client cut text | `clipboard_write`, then the paste shortcut | Untested |

Rules:

- **Lease.** Leases are per profile, and `computer_use` reads the current profile's lease file before every action, so a file write reaches separate gateway and worker processes. Take Over calls `tools.bot_desktop.lease.acquire` with `profile_key` set to each path from `list_profiles()`, and a loop applies it within 2 seconds to any profile created during the takeover. A brand-new profile could act inside that window, because a missing lease file means the agent holds control and stock hosts cannot prevent that. v1 accepts it. These are private APIs, so the plugin refuses control if they change. Windows has no cross-process lock there, which is an accepted risk for a short takeover.
- **Auto-release.** A host-side timer hands back after 15 minutes without input and survives a dead phone. The plugin saves its holder ID and deadline to its data directory and reconciles them at dashboard startup, releasing only leases it still holds, so a restart mid-takeover cannot strand the bot. Hermes runs no plugin code on removal, so the app calls the plugin's release route before the delete.
- **Driver.** Uses the driver Hermes itself resolves, running with `--no-overlay` and desktop targets. Window-target taps took about 1,350 ms even with the overlay off, so the plugin avoids them. The resolved version varies: Hermes 0.21.5 installs the latest release, and 0.22 pins 0.21.0. Older drivers use `capture_scope` rather than a target on each action, so the plugin checks the driver's schema and refuses what it cannot map. A version mismatch produces a plain explanation, with no workaround. Some hosts have this mismatch today. The timings above are provisional evidence from 0.28.2.
- **Dependencies.** None beyond what Hermes installs, which also avoids the plugin consent flow for Python dependencies.
- **Isolation.** The stream needs `plugins.isolation: in_process`, the default, because forwarded plugin routes carry no sockets. `/doctor` fails with that one-line fix otherwise.
- **Windows opt-in.** Refuses Windows unless the host sets an opt-in key. The default flips after two testers pass.
- **Install.** `POST /api/dashboard/agent-plugins/install` with `identifier`, `enable`, `force` and `ref`, a full 40-character commit. Hermex does not send `ref` today. The body field exists upstream.
- **Restart.** Older hosts need a dashboard restart for new routes, while newer hosts hot-mount an enabled plugin. When one is needed, the app uses the `hermex-push` restart route when present, and otherwise shows manual steps. "Check again" never installs or restarts anything.
- **Remove.** Hermex can remove what it installed. The consent copy says the routes stay mounted until the next dashboard restart. If someone removes the plugin another way, its leases stay held. `display.status` still reports the lease on every host, so the app still shows a stale takeover, and force Hand Back sends stock `display.lease.release` with `force: true` and no ID for each profile.
- **Updates.** The app pins one commit, so a fix reaches normal users through an app update. Testers and urgent cases can install a newer commit from the command line.

## App design

Type names are proposals.

| Piece | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `Networking/Screen/RFBClient` | Socket, handshake, stream parser, and decoders for Tight, CopyRect and Raw. It takes a `URLRequest` and knows nothing about Hermes, so recorded data can test it. |
| `ScreenSource` | An enum with `.botDesktop` and `.hostDesktop`. Each case supplies the ticket, lease calls and status. Nothing above it branches on host type except the subtitle. |
| `HermesCall`, `HermesREST` | New typed cases for `display.*` and the plugin routes. All models decode tolerantly. |
| `Features/Screen/ScreenSession` | An `@MainActor @Observable` owner of screen state, control state and the auto-release timer, keyed by server and profile. |
| `Features/Screen/ScreenView` | Layout, gestures, key row and banners. It stays dumb. |
| `ScreenFramebufferView` | A UIKit view backed by a `CALayer`, updated outside SwiftUI observation. |

- **Performance.** Decoding runs off the main actor. Frames reach the layer directly and never invalidate SwiftUI. Pointer moves are coalesced. Buffers are bounded. There are no continuous animations, and every animation respects Reduce Motion.
- **Async ownership.** A generation token on `ScreenSession` rejects stale frames, tickets and lease replies. Duplicate lease events are harmless.
- **Quiet streams.** Cloudflare closes idle sockets, so the client sends WebSocket protocol pings every 25 seconds, like the Kanban socket. It never sends the gateway's JSON heartbeat, because the bridge closes on any text frame.
- **Encodings.** Tight needs zlib. The system `libz` is an Apple SDK library and not a new dependency, but linking it changes the Xcode project, so that commit runs the full local test suite.
- **Keyboard.** A hidden text input carries the iOS keyboard, with Paste and password AutoFill, and sends key events. A key row has Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Option/Alt, Cmd and arrows. Hardware keyboards pass through, using `pressesBegan`, which is new to this codebase.
- **Desktop size.** The viewer scales to fit and never resizes the bot's desktop.

## UI

**Touch control: option C, picked by the owner.** Direct touch with pinch to zoom is the default, and one control switches to a trackpad panel. The choice is remembered per server. [Static mocks](https://t2vqc7tetlpd.postplan.dev) show the options, every state, the entries, and appearance and device variants. They are static, and their copy is a draft. The driver mismatch screen's `hermes computer-use install` is an unverified suggestion, so confirm a safe repair before shipping that line.

**Entries.** Bot chat toolbar, Bots home row menu and tile menu, a keyboard shortcut, and a deep link. The menu item sits outside the edit-only group, which `mayEdit` disables. There is no new overflow menu, no App Intent and no Lock Screen control in v1.

**States.** Beta off (no entry). Plugin not installed. Waiting for dashboard restart. Plugin failed to load. Driver mismatch. Permissions missing. Packages missing. Stopped, with Start. Starting. Screen is locked. Watching. You have control. Still there? Reconnecting. Another person took over. Handed back automatically. A bot blocked by a stale takeover. Also light and dark, Dynamic Type on all controls, landscape, iPad, and iPhone Duo folded and unfolded.

## Mac speed test

Run on an unlocked Mac host against `cua-driver` 0.28.2, with no overlay. A throwaway `TextEdit` window held dense colored text and covered about 14% of the display, on top of a real Safari window. All 1920x1080. Phone and cellular speed are still unmeasured.

| Measure | Result (median) | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full-screen capture | 142 ms, 301 KB PNG. With JPEG conversion (25 ms on a plainer screen, 34 KB), about 6 frames per second on the host. | At least 2 frames per second. Passed. |
| Tap to visible change | Right-click menu visible in about 490 ms, and a tap call takes 299 ms. Adding 146 ms for a tunnel gives an estimate of 640 ms. | Under 1 second. Passed on the estimate. |
| Key to visible pixels | 192 ms, before network time. Measured with the overlay on. | Report only |

With the cursor overlay on, desktop taps took about 1,350 ms. Hermes already passes `--no-overlay` on Mac. The driver has also retired the `capture_scope` setting in favor of a target on each action. Headless Macs usually sit locked, and captures then show only the lock screen, so any test has to confirm the session is unlocked first.

**If real use falls short.** A small native capture and input helper is the fallback, which means signing and notarizing a binary. The last resort is shipping Mac as a refreshing screenshot with tap-to-click. Linux does not change either way.

**Still to confirm.** Whether typed keys can unlock a Mac. Paste through `clipboard_write`. Timing on the driver Hermes resolves, with a `computer_use` session running.

## Build plan

One issue, one branch named `issue/<n>-bot-screen`, one commit per slice, and one PR into Hermex. The plugin lands on its own repo's `main` first, and the PR pins that commit.

**Every slice runs in this order.** Implement, run the affected tests with `scripts/test-sim --only`, review with `sol-loop`, trim tests with `detest`, run `/verify`, then commit. Review findings get fixed before the commit, so the PR review starts from reviewed code.

- **Before code.** Publish UI mocks and wait for the owner's pick.
- **Slice 1: watch-only viewer on Linux.** The toggle, `ScreenSource.botDesktop`, `RFBClient`, the framebuffer view, and entries. It starts by exposing a Codespace on a public address with a random password, since it holds repo credentials, and setting `dashboard.public_url` to that address, since the server refuses any other Host. Done when a real iPhone shows a live, busy Codespace screen over HTTPS without a crash. Go or no-go for the native viewer.
- **Slice 2: Take Over and Hand Back.** Lease calls, every rule in the control table, touch controls from the picked mock, keyboard, key row, paste and auto-release. Done when a user on a real iPhone can leave for a 2FA code and return still in control, with `display.status` read during the suspension showing the human still holds the lease. Prove this through the Codespace address and a Cloudflare quick tunnel, because the simulator never truly suspends. If a proxy reads as a clean close, stop and bring the result to the owner, since the bot could resume into a half-typed login.
- **Slice 3: Linux setup.** Start and stop, the install command to copy, memory and sandbox blockers, and the states that come with them. When a sandbox lacks the desktop image, the app shows the server's blocker in place of Start. Switching the image recreates the container, so it stays on the host in v1, like package installs.
- **Slice 4: plugin for Mac, in the `hermex-screen` repo.** Starts with the owner creating the public repo and clearing any driver mismatch on the test host. The first checkpoint runs every mapped operation on the resolved driver, then repeats the timings with a `computer_use` session running. Then routes, RFB server, driver mapping, lease across profiles, host-side timer, self-check and tests. Done when every mapped operation works on the resolved driver with a `computer_use` session running, a tap then typing lands in a window that was not frontmost, a second profile in its own process gets `human_has_control` during a takeover, a profile created mid-takeover gets it within 2 seconds, and a dashboard restart mid-takeover still ends in a hand-back.
- **Slice 5: app support for the plugin.** `ScreenSource.hostDesktop`, pinned install with consent, restart, remove, and lock, permission and mismatch states.
- **Slice 6: Windows, off by default.** Plugin code behind the opt-in, Windows copy in the app, and the tester script. Done before merge when the plugin refuses Windows without the opt-in and `/doctor` says why. Everything else on Windows is verified by testers after the merge.
- **Open the PR.** Rebase on `master`, open a real PR with `Fixes #<n>`, attach images and video, and run the review bots. Merging requires Linux and Mac to pass, using a Codespace and a Mac on Branch TestFlight. Pushing and each Branch TestFlight upload need the owner's word.

## Verification

| Layer | How |
| --- | --- |
| RFB parser and decoders | Unit tests over recorded VNC bytes, split at arbitrary chunk boundaries. These add almost no CI time. |
| Control rules | Model tests for each row of the control table, including stale hash, eviction and timer expiry, with a scripted socket. |
| Linux | A GitHub Codespace (Ubuntu 24.04, 2 cores, 7 GB), stopped between uses. The fallback is a Lima VM. |
| Mac | An unlocked Mac host with a throwaway window, sending no input unless that window is frontmost. |
| Windows and Linux in the wild | Testers, on production TestFlight after the merge and Beta App Review, with a short script. They run `/doctor` first. |
| Server isolation | Switch between two configured servers while holding control. Confirm the hand-back and that no ID or banner crosses over. |
| Real iPhone | Early in slice 1, for the suspension proof in slice 2, and again at the end, since a new renderer has passed simulators and reviews and then crashed on a phone before. |

**Surfaces.**

- **Targets.** Main app and tests only. The share extension, Live Activity widget and notification service do not change.
- **Reverse states.** Take Over and Hand Back, install and remove, Start and stop, toggle on and off.
- **Connection modes.** Localhost, LAN and tunnels, including custom proxy headers on the screen socket.
- **Docs.** A new `docs/agents/screen.md`, `display.*` changed from `n-a` in `hermes-feature-index.md`, vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`, and the plugin gate in `hermes-server.md`.
- **Localization.** All copy goes through the String Catalog.

## Release

- **Merge.** The feature ships dark behind the toggle, so App Store users see nothing until they turn it on.
- **Testers.** They get it through a production release candidate. Branch TestFlight is internal only.
- **App Review.** Every submission's notes describe it plainly as a generic mirror of the user's own host, under guideline 4.2.7, with a demo server ready if Apple asks.
- **Windows.** Stays "not yet supported" until two testers pass. Then the default flips in a new plugin commit and an app update pins it.
- **Leaving beta.** The toggle goes away after one public release with no blocking issues on Linux and Mac.

## Risks

| Risk | Effect | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The driver is slower on the pinned version, busier screens or phones | A laggy Mac and Windows experience, and a bigger PR if a helper is needed | Repeat the timings in slice 4, with the fallback above |
| One PR holds everything | Linux waits for Mac, testers see nothing before the merge, and the review is large | Owner's decision. Clean per-slice commits and pre-commit `sol-loop` reviews reduce it. |
| A proxy turns a dropped phone into a clean close | The bot resumes during a login on a stock Linux host | A slice 2 gate through two public proxies, and the owner's decision if it fails |
| Host screens are usually locked | The feature looks broken on headless Macs | A clear state, and typed unlock if it works |
| Private Hermes APIs in the plugin | An upstream change can break takeover | Fail closed, and `/doctor` reports it |
| Driver version mismatches on real hosts | Some hosts already have one, and testers may too | Detect it and explain it |
| Windows ships unproven code | Testers may find basic failures, including session and lock problems | Off by default, with fixes through pinned plugin commits |
| Shared computers | Someone at the machine can be surprised, since v1 has no host notice | Accepted for v1 |
| App Review classification | A rejection is possible, and TestFlight approval does not prove acceptance | Plain review notes, a demo server, and the toggle |

## Not in v1

- A display picker, quality settings, or a clipboard from host to phone.
- Phone-driven `sudo` installs through `display.install`, or `display.switchSandboxImage`.
- A screen that opens automatically, an "Open Screen" button in chat, or an automatic "continue" after Hand Back.
- App Intents, Lock Screen controls, or a Live Activity for holding control.
- WebRTC, a custom streaming server, or Mac Screen Sharing as the backend.
- The plugin on Linux, a lease expiry proposal upstream, or a listing in the Hermes plugin catalog.
- Reading the remote screen with VoiceOver.

## Council review

Reviewed before approval. Rounds: 4

| Delegate | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Round 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Fable 5.1 (high) | 7/10 | 9/10 | 9/10 | not re-run |
| GPT-6 Astra (high) | 6/10 | 8/10 | 9/10 | not re-run |
| Grok 4.7 (high) | no score | 6/10 | 7/10 | 8/10 |

## Evidence

- [Bot Screen docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/bot-screen) and [Computer Use docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/computer-use)
- [display.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2/hermes_cli/web_routers/display.py), [methods_display.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2/tui_gateway/methods_display.py) and [rfb_filter.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ca6782850432927f33df4775cb6dd45bb51460d2/tools/bot_desktop/rfb_filter.py) at the pin
- [cua-driver](https://github.com/trycua/cua)
- [Apple App Review guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/), 4.2.7
- [Hermes Mobile beta page](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/mobile). The official app's source is not public, so its viewer is unknown.

title: fix(kanban): count a retried Card's age from its current run

## What changed

The host's started age counts from a Card's first start, so a Card retried a day later showed critical the moment its new run began.

title: fix(hermes): keep Memory on the host when a Profile's terminal is SSH
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1566

## What changed

With the dashboard's Profile on an SSH terminal, `/api/fs/*` follows it to the remote machine. Reproduced at 0.22.5: Memory's read and write both answered 404, so Memory looked empty and couldn't save. On a remote that had the same path, it would have read and written the wrong machine's file.

Memory now uses `/api/files/read` and `/api/files/upload`, which stay on the dashboard's machine. The mkdir-and-retry goes away because upload creates the folder. Trade-off: upload isn't atomic where `write-text` was. These are small files and the save already reads back to confirm. Files over 512 KiB or not UTF-8 stay read-only, and the screen gets at most a 512 KiB preview of them.

Skills still reads through `/api/fs/*` and likely has the same problem. That's a separate issue, not this PR.

## How it was tested

- Proof: a signed Debug build against `scripts/local-hermes` at 0.22.5 with `terminal.backend: ssh` pointed at a real SSH host. Memory shows the host's note, and a save landed in the host's file with nothing created on the remote (attached).

title: fix(chat): keep your place when rotating, and stop the Plus/Max rotation lag
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1528

## What changed

Rotating a Plus/Max iPhone while reading up a chat dropped you at the bottom and lost the history you'd loaded. After that was fixed, long chats still lagged on rotation, the screen was cut off for a moment, and the transcript jumped.

The cause of both was the same. A Plus/Max iPhone is regular width in landscape, so rotating swapped the navigation stack for the split view and rebuilt the whole chat inside UIKit's rotation.

- **Plus/Max iPhones stay on the stack in landscape.** The split now also needs regular height, for the Hermes home, Bots and webui. Rotating only reflows. **This costs Plus/Max the landscape sidebar from #1316**, which is the alternative the issue set aside; the maintainer chose it after seeing the profile below.
- **iPad resize and Duo fold still swap, and now keep the chat.** `ChatContinuity` hands the rebuilt `ChatView` the same model, follow latch and reading place. SwiftUI can build an extra `ChatView` that appears and leaves while another stays on screen, so it counts the views on screen instead of naming one owner.
- **The exact top stays the top** through a reflow, whatever the bars' insets become.
- **Small fixes:** the gap during a rotation is no longer black, `covers` is only written when there's a link, and reply leaf ordering no longer copies arrays at every level.

Main-thread work for one rotation of a 68-message chat (Pro Max simulator, Debug, under Time Profiler, so compare the ratio rather than the seconds):

| Rotation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Portrait to landscape | about 4.5s | about 1s |
| Landscape to portrait | about 2.75s | about 0.8s |

**Left out on purpose:**
- The issue's item 3 (retry a yielded reflow). A retry reads frames that are already partly new, or, with a snapshot, could apply a stale anchor long after the reader moved. All of a layout's frames tend to arrive while the gesture still owns the position, so it couldn't serve the case anyway.
- The remaining settle after a rotation: replies still reach their final height over several passes.
- A failed load, then Try Again, then Load Earlier, then an iPad resize still reloads the newest page.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim` on `ChatScrollPositionControllerTests`, `ChatTranscriptReflowTests`, `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests`, `ChatVerticalScrollAxisGuardTests`, `ChatScrollPolicyTests`, `SessionNavigationStateTests`, `HermesHomeSplitRoutingTests`, `BotInboxTests`, `HermesSessionListTests`, `HermesSessionLinkTests`, `ResponseSelectionTests`, `ResponseSelectionVisibilityTests`, `HermesOfflineCacheTests` and `ChatViewModelSendTests`. The last full selection passed 446; after the Greptile fixes, the selection that exercises them passed 451.
- Confirmed failing without the code they guard: keeping the top, the stack in landscape, the handoff through a transcript that never attached, and a returned waiting send reaching the view that stays. The width-crossing hosted test caught the extra `ChatView` while this was being built.
- Physical iPhone 15 Pro Max, by the maintainer, on a build with the stack fix: rotation is smooth and keeps the place. That build predates the review changes (the retry's removal, the handoff fix, and keeping opened turns and returned sends across a rebuild), which only affect iPad and Duo paths and are covered by the tests above, except opened turns, which rely on the shared model.
- Real rotations on the iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator: mid-history and exact top keep their place on the Pro Max before the stack change, and mid-history again with it; the final code stays on its stack in landscape.

title: feat(chat): view and edit a pasted-text attachment before sending
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1456

## What changed

Tapping a `pasted-text.txt` tile opened "No Preview", so you couldn't check or trim a long paste without removing it and pasting again. Now it opens the text, with Edit to change it and Save to keep the change.

Save writes a new local copy, points the tile and draft record at it, saves the draft, then deletes the old copy, so any failure leaves the original intact. The sheet is read-only while a send may be reading the file or its outcome is unknown. Past 256 KB it shows only the start, with a notice, because the file is sent whole. Sent attachments and webui files keep today's preview. Tile thumbnails are now cached per copy, so an edited tile redraws.

Design: option A from the [mocks](https://gxzqqxyxx6d6.postplan.dev). The maintainer picked it, with two changes: Edit opens the keyboard straight away, and swiping down with unsaved changes bounces, with the discard prompt on Cancel.

The 256 KB limit: on a simulator also loaded by another agent's test run, Done stopped responding on a 512 KB sheet and worked at 256 KB. A hosted probe on an idle iOS 26.5 simulator settled 512 KB in under a second, so the cause is unexplained and this limit is the cautious choice. A single 256 KB line settled in 1.5 s, with one 1 s hitch on opening.

Other unsent files still show "No Preview": #1575.

Translations: 9 new keys in 17 languages, marked `needs_review`.

## How it was tested

`scripts/test-sim` with `HermesChatAttachmentTests`, `ComposerDocumentThumbnailsTests`, `SharedDraftStoreTests`, `ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests` and `LocalizationCatalogTests` on the final code: **115 passed, 0 failed**. `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: all 2652 keys covered. The full suite was not run locally or in CI: the maintainer asked to skip CI.

Greptile found that the old copy lost its protection while the draft was being saved, and that typing during a save was lost. Both are fixed on the head. The lease fix has no test of its own: reproducing it needs a concurrent import, a full storage budget and a failed write at once.

Red evidence: with the send guard, the size accounting, the two copy deletions, the per-copy thumbnail key, the character-boundary check and the path check each broken in one run, every test for those behaviors failed. The rollback test (`testAnEditThatCantBeSavedKeepsTheOriginal`) and the lost-answer assertions were added after that run and were not seen failing.

Real app, signed Debug build, with the draft seeded because the simulator must not paste (it syncs the Mac clipboard):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tile opens the text read-only, with Edit (10 KB) | Pass |
| Edit, type, no autocorrect or smart punctuation | Pass |
| Cancel with changes shows Discard Changes; tapping outside keeps editing | Pass |
| Save: new bytes on disk, old copy gone, size updated | Pass |
| Force quit and reopen keeps the edit | Pass |
| Text that isn't UTF-8 shows the unreadable state | Pass |
| 300 KB paste: first 256 KB, notice, no Edit; Done closes it | Pass |
| Edit, type and Save on the final code: new bytes on disk, size updated, one copy left | Pass |
| A real send carries the edited text | **Not run**: Send did not fire on the only simulator assigned to this checkout. Covered by the unit test reading the edited bytes from the outgoing attachment. |
| A real paste becoming a tile | **Not run**: see above. Covered by the #1381 tests. |
| Physical iPhone, Dynamic Type at the largest sizes, VoiceOver, iPad | **Not run**: the maintainer waived the phone check. |

title: feat(bots): watch and control a host's screen from the phone
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1567

## What changed

Bots get stuck at logins, CAPTCHAs and payment steps that only a person can finish, and until now a Hermex user had to get to another computer. Now you can open a bot's Screen, watch it work, take over for a login or 2FA prompt, leave the app for your code, come back still in control, and hand back. It's off until you turn on **Bot Screen (beta)** for that server, so App Store users see nothing.

- **One native viewer.** A Swift RFB client with no web view and no new dependency, for all hosts.
- **Linux** uses stock Bot Screen: the bot's own virtual desktop, with Start, Stop and the setup states.
- **Mac** shows the real logged-in desktop through a new optional plugin, [`hermex-screen`](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex-screen). It's built on the `cua-driver` Hermes already uses. The app asks first, then installs one pinned commit.
- **Windows** uses the same plugin, and it refuses until the host opts in. Testers get a script after this merges.

The rules that matter most: a takeover survives switching apps and a lost connection. The stream never closes cleanly, because a stock host reads that as a hand-back. Control returns only on an explicit Hand Back, a server switch, turning the switch off, or 15 minutes with no input. `docs/agents/screen.md` has the full table and the contract.

Translations: 91 new keys in 17 languages, marked `needs_review`.

## How it was tested

**Real iPhone, by the maintainer.** All three gates passed:
- The native viewer against a live, busy Codespace screen over HTTPS.
- Take Over, typing, locking the phone and returning, through the Codespace's address and a Cloudflare quick tunnel. Those locks ran about 70 s and 50 s by the host's log.
- The Mac on the real host, including the consent install, Take Over, typing, a phone lock, Hand Back, trackpad and zoom.

**Live on the final code, scripted.**
- Linux, stock 0.21.5 over the public address: Take Over, a click, typed text, a suspend, a return with no prompt, Hand Back, Stop and Start.
- Mac, 0.22.5 with driver 0.21.0, through its Cloudflare address:
  - All 8 Profiles held during a takeover. A real `computer_use` in another Profile's process answered `human_has_control`, then worked again after Hand Back.
  - A tap brought a background window forward, and `hello World 42!é€ ok` landed in it.
  - A Profile created mid-takeover was held 1.17 s after its folder appeared.
  - A second viewer's takeover closed the first with 4000.
  - A dashboard restart mid-takeover kept the hold, then the timer handed back on all 8 Profiles.
  - Remove and a pinned reinstall both worked, using the app's requests.
- A phone that vanishes with no close, scripted, held control through a Codespace's address (240 s, twice, plus 180 s), a Cloudflare tunnel (240 s, once) and loopback (180 s).

**Tests.** `scripts/test-sim` with `ScreenSessionTests`, `RFBDecoderTests`, `AuthManagerStateTests`, `BotDeepLinkTests`, `HermesConnectionTests` and `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 170 passed. Greptile's fixes came after that: `ScreenSessionTests` 62 and `AuthManagerStateTests` 49 passed on them, and CI ran the full suite on the head. The decoder tests include a recording of a real busy Xvnc screen, split at arbitrary chunk boundaries. The plugin has 32 unit tests in its own repo. The last full local suite ran on slice 1 and had one failure, `BotChatPresentationTests.testThreadSearchOpensChronologicalDetailAndItsOwnComposer`, which passed alone. Later slices add sources to the project, but the Mac was paging too hard for another full run, so CI is the full-suite gate here.

**Not proven yet**
- The last two commits, Greptile's fixes to how a takeover ends, haven't been on a real phone or a live host. They have tests only.
- A real phone locked past Cloudflare's idle window. The longer case is scripted only.
- Windows beyond the plugin's refusal without its opt-in. That's for testers, by plan.
- Typing a password to unlock a locked Mac. The app offers this on Mac, and a password with symbols may fail, because those go through the clipboard.
- The packages and blocker states ran in model tests only, because the test host has neither.
- iPad, iPhone Duo, landscape, large Dynamic Type and VoiceOver haven't had a manual pass.

Images are from a simulator on the Linux test host. There's no "before": this is a new screen. There's no video in this PR.

![Watching a bot's desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eebe4ba4-693b-4834-a8b9-d48cd7024c3a)
![In control, zoomed to the tapped window, with the inset and key row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53d88255-f6e1-47d8-abca-a75636764f19)

title: test: stop the real on-device speech test from slowing PR CI
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1523

## What changed

The real on-device speech test was the slowest test in most PR CI runs. Over the last 24 runs it took 2.3 s to 377.7 s (median 55 s, mean 96 s), and it passed every time, so it cost time without catching anything.

It now skips itself on CI using the `HERMEX_CI` flag that `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests` already uses, so the workflow doesn't change. It still runs locally. Its doc comment and `DEVELOPMENT.md` § PR CI say to run it by hand after changing `OnDeviceSpeech` or `ListenAudioPlayer`.

The trade-off is that nothing automated renders real speech any more. The spy-based Listen tests stay on CI and cover the view model's flow.

I skipped the issue's cold/warm measurement and cheaper-input option. The same sentence took 2.3 s in one run and 377 s in another, so the text probably isn't the cost, and a different voice would no longer match production.

**This alone may not speed up CI yet.** On this PR's own run the speech test skipped, but `ScreenSessionTests.testABlockedHostStateStillReportsWhoHoldsIt` (from #1578) took 348 s and the test step wasn't faster. Test class order is random. In all three earlier runs that had both tests, whichever ran first was slow (57 to 310 s) and the other took about 2 s or less. title: test: keep the Screen tests off the real notification center so they stop slowing PR CI
body:
**What the user gets:** faster PR CI, if this theory holds: each macOS run could get back up to about 6 minutes, with no change to the app.
**Why it matters:** skipping the real speech test in #1579 didn't speed up CI, because `ScreenSessionTests` now takes the same slowness.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed.

## Problem

On the PR that skipped the speech test, `ScreenSessionTests.testABlockedHostStateStillReportsWhoHoldsIt` took 348 s and the test step wasn't faster. Test class order is random, and in every run with both tests, whichever ran first was slow:

| Run | Ran first | First test | Second test |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| [41856556474](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41856556474) | Screen | 310 s | speech 2.3 s |
| [41864248783](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41864248783) | Screen | 74.5 s | speech 2.0 s |
| [41850080604](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41850080604) | Speech | 57.3 s | Screen 0.05 s |
| [41869463151](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/41869463151) | Screen | 348.6 s | speech skipped |

Before #1578 added the Screen tests, the speech test never finished under 17 s in the 22 runs checked. That suggests a one-time cold start on the CI simulator that both tests hit.

The Screen tests reach the real `UNUserNotificationCenter`: `ScreenSession.open()` cancels the idle notification, and `suspend()` schedules it. They aren't testing notifications, so they shouldn't touch it.

The cause is inferred, not proven. Nothing yet explains why speech rendering and notifications would share a wait.

## Proposed approach

Inject the idle notification through `ScreenHoldStore`, which every call site already has, and turn it off in `ScreenSessionTests`. Production behavior doesn't change.

## Acceptance

- `ScreenSessionTests` no longer reaches the real notification center.
- Over two or three PR CI runs, no test takes more than about 20 s, and the test step drops to around 10 minutes.
- If a third test picks up the wait instead, the cause is elsewhere: record that here and reconsider the speech skip from #1579.

title: feat(settings): manage a server's plugins and browse the marketplace
body:
**What the user gets:** a native Plugins screen to see, toggle, install, update, remove and configure a server's plugins from the phone, and to browse the Hermes marketplace without leaving the app.
**Why it matters:** the official Hermes iOS app has a Plugins screen (a toggle list and a paste-a-repo sheet), so Hermex needs one. Marketplace browsing, per-Profile control and real setup help are how we beat it.
**Cost:** Large. Needs the owner's hands on a phone after slices 1 and 3, and one approved install and removal on the live host before merge.

The layout is chosen: **option A, Store**, in the [mocks](https://vrfuhg6olmf6.postplan.dev/v/1). The "Same in every option" screens there are the starting point for the shared sheets.

## Scope

Hermes servers only. The row lives at Settings → Server → Plugins and is hidden for webui. One issue, one PR. Plugins only: no marketplace skills or connectors. No shortcuts, App Intents or slash commands in this issue.

### Installed

- A Profile picker at the top starts on the server's default Profile. Every action applies to the selected Profile.
- Search, and filters including Updates. Rows are dense and identified by the canonical `key`, because names collide across category folders.
- Toggles apply immediately, except for plugins Hermex or sign-in relies on: the `dashboard_auth/*` plugins, `hermex-push`, `hermex-screen`, the active memory provider and connected messaging platforms. Those get a plain-language confirmation. They are never hidden or blocked. Upstream's own comment says disabling `basic` makes password auth silently fail.
- After any change, show what the server reported: live now, next session, or restart needed. Restart is always a separate confirmed action, and Hermex never restarts on the user's behalf.
- Remove is for user installs only, with a confirmation that names the Profile.
- `hermex-push` and `hermex-screen`: Update and Remove link to their existing settings pages.
- A plugin Nous removed from the marketplace shows that on its row, with the reason.

### Install

- Every install goes through one review sheet: source, tier, pinned commit, Disclosure, required keys and target Profile. Wording gets stronger for community plugins and strongest for a raw repo. Nothing is ever called safe, and nothing installs in one tap.
- No Force toggle. Offer Replace only when the server says the plugin already exists. Enable after install is on by default.
- The repo field also accepts a catalog name, `hermes plugins install <name>`, or a pasted `hermes://plugin/install…` link. All lead to the review sheet.
- Missing keys can be entered straight after install. The detail page renders the plugin's settings form natively, for all six field types.
- If the connection drops mid-install: reload the list, say the result is unconfirmed, and never retry on its own.

### Discover

- Catalog data comes only from the host. There are no stars or featured picks, because only the public feed has them.
- Order is Official, Verified, then Community, with category filters and on-device search. Held in memory per server while the screen is open, with no disk cache.
- Desktop plugins appear only under their own category and in search, labeled "Needs Hermes Desktop".
- A plugin needing a newer Hermes than the host's can't be installed, and the reason is shown. OS limits are label-only.

### Images

- Official shelf with large banners, small thumbnails in lists, and a full banner plus swipeable screenshots on the detail page.
- Load lazily, downsample off the main thread, cancel when scrolled away, and cache. Skip under Low Data Mode. HTTPS from GitHub hosts only, matching upstream's allowlist.
- GIFs show their first frame, and SVGs are skipped.
- **If it looks uneven or unintuitive on the phone, fall back to text only** (mock S6). Banner coverage outside Desktop: Official 18 of 18, Verified 2 of 9, Community 182 of 732.
- No privacy wording in the app or README. READMEs stay out for now, with Open on GitHub as the link.

### Updates

One plugin at a time, no Update All. If the server asks for capability consent or reports scan findings, show them before retrying. A caution result can be overridden after reading the findings. A dangerous result can never be applied.

### Out of scope

Claiming `hermes://`. An app registers a scheme for everyone, the official iOS app already claims it, and iOS doesn't define which app opens when two claim one. That could break the official app's `connections/done` sign-in return for people with both. Revisit if users without the official app ask.

## Contract

Verified at the pin `bf0203a7` (0.22.5). Validate just in time during the build.

| Need | Route | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List, toggle, install, update, remove, settings | RPC `plugins.manage` with `action` and optional `profile` | `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`; `list` read on a live 0.22.5 host, where two Profiles returned different rows and an unknown Profile returned error 4064 |
| Catalog | `GET /api/dashboard/plugins/catalog` | `hermes_cli/web_routers/dashboard_ui.py`; read live: 976 entries, 2.85 MB unpacked, about 1.8 s through a tunnel |
| Secret values | `PUT /api/env` | `hermes_cli/plugins_settings.py`; the same route the API Keys screen uses |
| Restart | `POST /api/gateway/restart` | Already used by Hermex |

- Use RPC for management, not the existing REST routes. REST mutations can't choose a Profile, and they act on the Profile the dashboard runs as.
- Decode tolerantly, and decode the catalog off the main thread.
- Catalog installs send `catalog_name`, so the host resolves the repo and pin and enforces its removal list. Never turn a catalog install into an unpinned repo install.
- RPC install failures arrive as a bare error (5026), so a rich findings screen is possible for updates but not installs at this pin. Upstream's newer `inspect` action can improve this after a pin bump.

## Slices

Each slice is reviewed with `sol-loop` and trimmed with `detest` before commit. Tests stay focused, with no added CI time.

1. **Installed:** client and models, Profile picker, search and filters, toggles, risky-toggle confirmations, real outcomes. Phone test.
2. **Install and remove:** review sheet, repo and paste input, Replace, missing keys, unconfirmed results.
3. **Discover:** catalog, categories, images. Phone test, including a scroll test on a real iPhone.
4. **Updates and settings forms:** consent and scan flows, native forms.

Tests that matter: wrong-Profile and wrong-server dispatch, stale results after a switch, `key` collisions, consent responses, dependency refusals, and unconfirmed installs.

## Validation

- Mutations run on `scripts/local-hermes`. The live host stays read-only until the end.
- Before merge, ask the owner to approve one real install and removal of a small official plugin on the live host.
- Phone builds use `/push-to-iphone`.
- Hit every surface: two servers, Profile switches, LAN and tunnel, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, Reduce Motion, light and dark, and localization.

## Check during the build

None of these change the design.

- **Restarts:** whether the live host really hot-mounts new plugin routes. Source says yes at the pin. If it holds, correct `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` § Plugin routes need a host restart.
- **Git plugin updates:** whether they hit the dependency consent refusal. If so, show the limitation and a fix to run on the host. Don't generalize the `hermex-push` disable-and-reinstall workaround.

title: feat(appearance): add themes, accent, fonts and text size
body:
**What the user gets:** themes with light and dark variants, an accent color, app-wide fonts and text size, and code display settings, with a live preview in Settings > Appearance.
**Why it matters:** Hermex offers only System, Light and Dark. T3 Code mobile and the official Hermes app both go much further, and the goal is to match or beat them.
**Cost:** Large. Three PRs. Needs the owner's hands on a phone early in PR 2.

Mocks: https://f8t9ui8nfos2.postplan.dev/v/1. The layout is chosen: the T3 Code layout, close to mock A. Each section opens with its own sample above its controls. The owner replaced the pinned preview (mock B) after testing it on a phone: it took too much of the page.

## Decisions

- **Color scheme:** System, Light, Dark, as today.
- **Themes:** Default, Paper, Midnight, Grove, Ocean, Ember, Iris, each with light and dark variants. A card sets both modes; an orb sets one. Default looks exactly like today.
- **Accent:** the theme's own, 8 swatches, or a custom color. Status colors and syntax highlighting stay fixed.
- **Contrast:** 4.5:1 floor on all themes except Default, and on any accent pick. A test covers every theme. Default keeps system colors, which miss this floor (system blue on white is 4.02:1).
- **Tint New Chat & Send:** uses the chosen accent if one is set, otherwise the server color.
- **Text size:** the first stop follows the iPhone; later stops are app-wide overrides, including accessibility sizes.
- **Fonts:** San Francisco (default), SF Rounded, DM Sans, Avenir Next, Georgia, Lora, SF Mono, app-wide. Code stays monospaced. System menus and alerts stay San Francisco. Bundle unmodified DM Sans and Lora (both SIL OFL 1.1; Lora has a Reserved Font Name) with notices in `ThirdPartyNotices`.
- **Code:** size follows text until overridden; wrap moves here from Settings > Chat. Covers chat code, tool output, source files and diffs. Leave room for a terminal row later.
- **Scope:** themes, fonts and text size apply across all servers. Server color stays server identity.
- **Out:** math toggle, animated loading indicators, bot animation toggle, and theme support in the Live Activity and share extension. Haptics and app icons stay where they are; the Clear icon stays in #1574.
- **Foundation:** this starts the in-house design foundation, limited to color and typography tokens. #1089 can build on it later. #974's color values and type roles may be used as reference, with credit.

## How it works

Set themes and text size once with window trait overrides, and read colors through static tokens backed by dynamic `UIColor`s.

A throwaway spike on iOS 26.5 changed one custom trait on the window. SwiftUI, nested hosting like reply selection, UIKit and an open sheet all recolored with no view body re-runs. Overriding `preferredContentSizeCategory` the same way resized SwiftUI and auto-adjusting UIKit text. iOS 18, the minimum target, is untested because we have no iOS 18 simulator.

Known exceptions that need explicit work: direct `UIFont.preferredFont` calls, the diff canvas, the math image cache, glass fallbacks, the UIKit composer, the app-lock window and the window background. Fonts can't be swapped by a trait, so about 950 `.font` sites move to typography tokens with a scripted rewrite.

## Delivery

1. Text size and the Code section.
2. Color tokens and themes. Default must look unchanged. Test the themed chat on a phone early. Add one Debug-only gallery screen built from the real chat components, so every theme and font can be checked in one place. No docs, usage guidance or tests of its own.
3. Fonts. Land quickly, because the rewrite conflicts with other open work.

Each PR is built in slices, with `sol-loop` and `detest` before pushing. Each merges with `--admin` to skip CI once the review bots are clean on that commit. PRs 2 and 3 run the full suite locally first; PR 1 runs affected tests.

title: feat(chat): read the transcript while an approval is pending
body:
**What the user gets:** you can set an approval aside, read the chat, and come back to answer it.
**Why it matters:** an approval is often the moment you most need context, but today's overlay dims and blocks the whole transcript until you answer. The idea comes from #1089.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs an owner pick on mocks first and a check on a phone. Build after #1583, so the card starts on the new tokens.

## Today

`ApprovalRequestOverlay` covers the chat for both webui and Hermes sessions (`ChatView.approvalOverlay`), with no way to collapse it. Other requests already solve this: webui questions (`ClarificationRequestCard`) and Hermes questions, sudo, secret, Desktop task and connection prompts (`HermesRequestInset`) pin above the composer, collapse to a one-line bar, and keep a half-typed answer.

## Scope

- Approvals use that same pinned, collapsible slot in Sessions chat, on webui and Hermes servers.
- The transcript stays readable and scrollable while an approval is pending, expanded or collapsed.
- The collapsed bar makes it clear the agent is waiting on you, and tapping it restores the card. VoiceOver can collapse, expand and answer without gestures.
- Keep what works today: only the choices the server offers, the scope line, Skip all, the queue count, optional approval summaries, the error message and haptics.
- Answer state stays with its session and server, and a withdrawn or expired approval leaves the slot.

## Decide in mocks

- Keep direct buttons (one tap, recommended) or move to radio rows with Confirm, as #1089 proposed. The agent is waiting on this answer, so an extra tap has a real cost.
- Whether the composer stays usable while an approval is collapsed, and what sending then does. Check this against the server contract rather than assuming.

## Out of scope

Question paging, Bot Chat's in-transcript card, and new approval choices.

title: feat(settings): let Hermes servers hide home rows
body:
**What the user gets:** on a Hermes server, you can hide the home rows you don't use, so more sessions fit on the first screen.
**Why it matters:** on an iPhone Duo the first session starts about 76% of the way down the Hermes home, below five tool rows, Projects and Scheduled sessions. Webui servers have a Settings switch for each row (#190). Hermes servers don't, even though the Hermes list already reads the same switches. The idea comes from #1088.

- The Main Page toggles (Tasks, Kanban, Skills, Memory, Usage, Active Profile, Projects, Bot Mode) live only on a webui server's Settings page (`WebuiServerSettings`). The Hermes server page (`SettingsServerPage.hermesSections`) has none.

## Scope

- Add a Main Page section to the Hermes server's Settings page with Tasks, Kanban, Skills, Memory, Usage and Projects. Share the toggles with the webui page instead of copying them. Leave out Active Profile and Bot Mode, which the Hermes home doesn't use.

title: fix(scripts): get local-hermes installing and managing plugins at the current pin
body:
## Linked issue

No issue. Found while validating #1582, which relies on this script for its mutations.

## What changed

`scripts/local-hermes` couldn't start at the current pin: a fresh run died with `No module named 'ruamel'`. It also couldn't do what #1582 needs it for once it ran.

- **Install:** the pin's core dependencies are declared only for Python 3.14, and a plain `uv pip install` can't resolve the project's overrides. It now uses Python 3.14 and `uv sync --frozen`.
- **Plugin toggles and installs behind a TLS-inspecting proxy:** the host runs its own `uv`, which didn't trust the system certificates, so these failed with `invalid peer certificate`. The server's environment now sets `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS` and `UV_NATIVE_TLS`.
- **Catalog updates on macOS:** the temp home's path runs through the `/var` symlink. The host compares a resolved plugin folder with an unresolved plugins folder, so a catalog install read as a plain one and its update was refused as pinned. The home is now resolved.

A cache built by the old script at this pin is stamped as installed but broken, so delete `~/Library/Caches/hermex-local-hermes/bf0203a7…` if you ran it.

## How it was tested

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: passes, with the install commands updated and one new test that the home is resolved.
- A real run from an empty cache, under a throwaway `HOME`: installed and started 0.22.5. Against it: a plugin toggle succeeded behind the proxy, a catalog install succeeded, and `update` answered `unchanged`, which is what proves the catalog record is now found.

No app code changes, so no XCTest run.

title: feat(settings): manage a server's plugins and browse the marketplace
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1582

## What changed

There was no way to see or manage a server's plugins from the phone. The official Hermes iOS app has a toggle list and a paste-a-repo sheet, so Hermex needed one. This goes further: per-Profile control, the Hermes marketplace, and real setup help.

Settings → Server → Plugins, on Hermes servers only, using the chosen layout (option A, Store):

- **Installed:** a Profile picker, search and filters, and dense rows identified by canonical key. Toggles apply at once, except plugins Hermex or sign-in relies on, which ask first in plain language. After any change the screen shows what the host reported, and a restart is always a separate confirmed action.
- **Install and remove:** one review sheet for every install, showing source, tier, pinned commit, Disclosure, required keys and target Profile. The wording grows stronger for community plugins and strongest for a raw repo. The field also takes a catalog name, `hermes plugins install <name>`, or a `hermes://plugin/install` link. Missing keys can be entered straight after install. A dropped connection says the result is unconfirmed and never retries.
- **Discover:** the host's catalog as Official, Verified, then Community, with categories and on-device search. Images load lazily from GitHub hosts only, downsample off the main thread, cancel when scrolled away, and skip Low Data Mode.
- **Updates and settings:** one plugin at a time. Capability consent and scan findings show before any retry; a caution result can be overridden after reading it, and a dangerous one can't. Each plugin's page renders its settings as a native form for all six field types.

### Worth a reviewer's attention

- Management uses the `plugins.manage` RPC because only it can name a Profile. `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` § Managing plugins has the contract as verified at the pin.
- **`force` means two things on this RPC.** It replaces the existing copy and also lets a caution scan through on a repo source, and install findings can't be shown at this pin. Replace appears only when the host says the plugin exists, and its confirmation says this plainly.
- A catalog install sends its reviewed commit as `ref`, because without one the host reuses a disabled copy at whatever commit it has.
- **One narrowing of the issue:** `hermex-push` and `hermex-screen` offer no row-level Update. This build pins both, Screen's page has no update action, and Push's update card needs a paired phone. Manage still opens their pages. Screen's removal names the Profile only when opened from here, because the Bots path installs over REST to the dashboard's Profile.

### The issue's open questions

- **Git updates:** no dependency consent refusal at this pin, even when dependencies change, so no limitation text.
- **Older hosts:** a host lacking these methods or the catalog route says so, based on its reply. Tested with mocks, not a real old host.
- **Risky toggles:** per Profile from `/api/memory` and `/api/messaging/platforms`. If those can't be read, the toggle asks first.
- **Restarts: still open.** The live test's plugin mounts no routes, so `hermes-server.md` § Plugin routes need a host restart is unchanged.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <udid>`: the full suite passed locally on `ec355ddb` (3,993 tests), run because the change adds files to the Xcode project. The review fixes in `0af69c6b` passed the plugin tests locally, and CI ran the full suite on that head.
- **Phone:** the maintainer tested slices 1 and 3 on a real iPhone, including the Discover scroll test, and both passed. That caught a search dismissal stutter, fixed here. Slice 4 hasn't been on a phone.
- **Live host, with the maintainer's approval:** one real install and removal of `touchdesigner` on the `hermex-fixtures` Profile through the app. Afterwards every Profile checked matched a snapshot taken before, nothing was left in its config or install record, and the gateway was never restarted.
- **Pinned local host:** real toggles, installs, Replace, a saved key landing in the right Profile's `.env`, removal, all six field types, and a real catalog update using the host's own consent reply.
- **Not exercised against a real host:** a raw repo install, a blocked scan (unit tests only), Replace under a caution scan, a real gateway restart, Low Data Mode, and iPad.

### Hit every surface

- **Entry points:** Settings only, by the issue's scope. No shortcuts, App Intents or slash commands.
- **Targets:** main app and tests. No shared model or extension changes.
- **Servers:** the row shows only for the active Hermes server and is hidden for webui. Nothing is cached past the screen.
- **Reverse states:** install and remove, on and off, set and remove a secret, and undoing a change clears its pending restart.
- **Connection modes:** loopback and the Cloudflare tunnel. LAN doesn't apply to this host.
- **Native quality:** light mode and localization (all strings in 17 languages, marked `needs_review`). Dark mode, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver were asked of the maintainer's phone test but not reported on individually. No continuous animations were added.
- **Docs:** `hermes-server.md` and `hermes-feature-index.md`.

## Checklist

title: fix(sessionlist): close abandoned session-open signpost intervals
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1506

## What changed

Cancelling a session open when the list disappears can leave an unfinished interval in performance traces, making session-opening measurements misleading. The disappearance handler cancelled the opening task without ending its signpost interval. The task then returned at the cancellation guard before reaching the code that could close it.

The view now tracks the session ID whose opening interval it owns and uses a shared cancellation helper to cancel and clear the task, end the interval, and clear that ID. Disappearance, WebUI push navigation, and replacement opens use this helper. A completed open clears the tracked ID so successful navigation retains its existing signpost completion behavior, while failed opens still end their interval directly.

## How it was tested

Ran `./scripts/test-sim` locally on macOS for the hermex SessionListView: change; it fails the same way on the base branch, so the failure predates this change (it fails the same way on upstream/master).
`swift_tests` found no package owning the touched files, so it ran no tests.
`./scripts/test-sim` failed because the required device argument was missing, so it ran no tests.
