title: feat(composer): Turbo mode — fast mode plus annotation, with opt-in debug hot reload
body:
**What the user gets:** one Turbo toggle for fast iteration while the agent builds UI. It turns on the existing Fast chip (#1150) and the annotation overlay proposed in #1535. Only if the user separately opts in, it also hot-reloads the running app with InjectionIII.
**Why it matters:** the slowest part of reviewing UI work from the phone is the loop of agent edit, rebuild, reopen, then describe the change.
**Cost:** small for the toggle, since it only composes existing controls. The hot-reload part is debug-only and sits behind a build flag.

## Use case

When I review UI the agent is building, I want fast replies, to circle what's wrong instead of describing it, and, in a debug build, to see the change land without reinstalling.

## Proposed behavior

- **Turbo toggle:** in the Hermes composer menu, next to the Fast chip.
  - Turning Turbo on sends the same `config.set fast` (`scope=session`) as the Fast chip, and only when the active model allows fast mode. A refusal keeps Turbo off and shows the host's message, as the Fast chip already does.
  - It also enables the annotation entry points from #1535.
- **Hot reload, a separate prompt** after Turbo is on: "Also hot-reload this app while the agent edits it?"
  - It comes with a disclaimer: debug builds only, code is injected into the running process, and it's off by default.
  - It's compiled out of Release, TestFlight and App Store builds. Declining leaves Turbo on without it.
- **Turning Turbo off** restores the previous fast setting and disables the annotation entry points.

## Acceptance outcomes

- Turbo on and off round-trips the fast setting through the existing `config.set` reply handling. Reattaching keeps the state, as #1150 does for Fast.
- The hot-reload prompt never appears in a Release configuration, and is never shown without Turbo.

title: feat(appearance): add an app-wide font setting
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1583 (PR 3 of 3, after #1589 and #1591).

## What changed

Hermex had no font choice: the app was San Francisco everywhere. Settings > Appearance now has a Font row under Text Size: San Francisco (default), SF Rounded, DM Sans, Avenir Next, Georgia, Lora and SF Mono. It applies to every server, changes live, and survives a relaunch. Code stays monospaced.

- **How it works:** a trait can't swap a SwiftUI `Font`, so typography tokens (`AppFont`) read one observable setting. A view that calls a token re-runs only when the font changes, including settled chat rows and a reply's nested hosting. Most of the diff is a scripted move of about 700 `.font` literals to those tokens. `docs/agents/theming.md` has the rules.
- **Text with no font of its own** follows a root font that's set only when a font is chosen. A root font also enlarges list footers, so sections with a footer use `appFooter:` to keep theirs small.
- **UIKit pieces:** navigation titles, the composer and its chips, reasoning text and diff headers follow the setting directly.
- **Bundled fonts:** DM Sans and Lora are bundled unmodified under SIL OFL 1.1, with notices in Acknowledgements.

**Trade-offs**

- These stay San Francisco: empty states (`ContentUnavailableView` sets its own fonts), system menus and alerts, and segmented controls. Empty states can follow later, but that means wrapping about 80 call sites.
- SF Rounded has no italic face, so italics show upright in it.
- `.title3.bold()` renders lighter than `weight: .bold`, so sites that used `.bold()` keep it.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim` full suite on iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 26.5): 4006 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesWhileTheKeyboardIsUp`, times out waiting for the keyboard. It fails the same way on clean master `913b5c79` on the same simulator, and on the iPhone 18 Pro (iOS 27).

- `ci/check_string_catalog.py`: clean.

A new-chat screen has 74 pixels off by 1 level. This diff caught the `.bold()` regression above before review.

title: test: make the Screen idle hand-back test wait on state, not the clock
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing directly; PR CI stops failing at random on an unrelated change.
**Why it matters:** `ScreenSessionTests.testIdleAsksThenHandsBackAndInputPutsItOff` failed PR CI on #1593 (fonts), which doesn't touch Screen session code, and passed on a rerun. A random red check blocks merges and costs a review round.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed.

## What happened

The test timed out after 15.4 s on PR CI ([run](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/42138344724/job/127632138536)), on `Clone 1 of iPhone 17`. Every other test passed. It passed locally in a full run and 30 times in a row with `scripts/test-sim --repeat 30 --only HermesMobileTests/ScreenSessionTests/testIdleAsksThenHandsBackAndInputPutsItOff`.

## Likely cause

The test sets `idlePrompt` to 20 ms and `idleLimit` to 60 ms with a real clock (`options.now = { Date() }`), then waits for "Still there?" before calling `noteActivity()`. If the simulator stalls for about 40 ms between the prompt and the wait seeing it, the session hands back first, and `waitUntil("Still there?")` waits until it times out.

## Fix

Drive the idle timer from a clock the test controls, or give the limit enough room that a CI stall can't skip the prompt. The test should still prove that the prompt appears, that activity dismisses it, and that the session hands back at the limit.

title: fix(hermes): refuse a gateway listener at Add Server and offer a way out
body:
**What the user gets:** pointing Hermex at a Hermes gateway's own listener (now the 0.23.0 Webapp) fails at Add Server with copy that names the right address, instead of saving a server that can never connect.
**Why it matters:** a user reported it today. Hermes 0.23.0 added the Webapp: the gateway serves Desktop in a browser on port 9120, turned on with one switch (`webapp.enabled` or Desktop's Settings → Web Access). Pointing Hermex at it is now easy, and the current failure is a dead end on the home screen.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed.

## What happens today

1. **Add Server saves it.** `OnboardingViewModel` (around `:539`) only does the HTTP sign-in. A listener with a password passes, gets saved, and fails at its first gateway connect with `.gatewayListener` (`HermesGateway.swift:347`). `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` documents this ("saved and refused at its first gateway connect"). The Bots connection form already opens the socket before saving (`BotConnectionView.swift:567`), so Add Server can do the same.
2. **Reconnect is a dead end.** `BotConnectionAdvice.isRetryable` treats `.gatewayListener` as permanent, but the inbox still offers **Reconnect** (`BotsInboxView.swift:179-187`), which reopens the same address. The address is read-only on a saved Hermes server, so the only fix is Settings → remove the server → Add Server.
3. **The copy.** "Connect to hermes dashboard instead" doesn't say that `hermes dashboard` is a command, and it doesn't mention the Webapp or the port. In practice the mistake is likely 9120 (Webapp) vs 9119 (dashboard).

## Scope

- Add Server: after a good HTTP sign-in, open the gateway socket once before saving, so `.gatewayListener` (and `.upgradeRefused`) stop the form instead of saving the server.
- Inbox: for `.gatewayListener`, replace Reconnect with an action that leads to changing the server's address.
- Copy along the lines of: "This address is the Hermes Webapp, served by the gateway. Hermex doesn't support it yet. On the host, run `hermes dashboard` (port 9119 by default) and connect to that address." Final wording is the owner's call.

## Not in scope

Supporting the gateway's protocol: #1341.

## Evidence

- Upstream v0.23.0 (`2bd378ed`): `gateway/webapp_listener.py` (`DEFAULT_PORT = 9120`); `app.state.session_authority` is set only by the gateway's own listener (`gateway/run_api.py:97`), so a standalone `hermes dashboard` still speaks the protocol Hermex supports (`hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:665`).
- An open Webapp still withholds the page token and writes `__HERMES_AUTH_REQUIRED__=false` (`hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py:196-214`), so `HermesREST.withholdsPageToken` keeps catching the open case.

## Test

One test: Add Server against a scripted `gateway.ready` with `session_authority: true` shows the error and saves nothing.

---

title: feat(hermes): attach and replay canonical gateway sessions
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing visible yet. Hermex learns to attach to a session on a gateway that speaks the canonical protocol and replay its events in order. This is the base every other slice of #1341 builds on.
**Why it matters:** first slice of #1341. Upstream moved Desktop and the Webapp to this protocol in 0.23.0, and the dashboard will follow.
**Cost:** Medium. No phone needed.

Part of #1341. Its decisions apply here; read the parent first. Delivery: one branch and one PR for all of #1341, one commit per child (parent § Decisions). The production refusal (`HermesGateway.swift:347`) stays in place; this slice is reached only through tests.

## Reference

Upstream Desktop already speaks this protocol through one adapter. Copy its shape: `apps/desktop/src/api/canonical-protocol.ts` and `apps/desktop/docs/canonical-gateway-protocol.md` at the pin (`2bd378ed`). Put Hermex's equivalent at the one place a `HermesCall` becomes a frame (`HermesGateway.send`, `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:208`). It translates the wire shape and keeps each session's fences. Feature code changes only where the meaning differs.

## Plan

- **Protocol mode.** Record `gateway.ready.payload.session_authority` on the connection (`HermesGateway.swift:342-347`) and expose it next to `replayEpoch` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotProtocol.swift:296`). Throwing `.gatewayListener` moves behind it, unchanged in production.
- **Resume.** On a canonical socket, `session.resume` must not send `close_on_disconnect` (`HermesCall.swift` `.sessionResume`); the host refuses it with 4001 `fields: ["close_on_disconnect"]`. The reply is a `CanonicalSnapshot` (`stored_session_id`, `subscription_id`, `revision`, `execution_generation`, `replay_epoch`, `pending`, `prompts`, `open_requests`; `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json` `components.schemas.CanonicalSnapshot`), with no `session_key`. `HermesConversation.attachedKey` (`HermesMobile/Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:440`) and `HermesChatTurnCoordinator`'s snapshot readers (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1308-1345`) must read it.
- **Replay.** `session.events.since` has to carry the session's own `replay_epoch` from the snapshot, not the socket's (`HermesConversation.swift:376-384`). A missing or wrong epoch answers `snapshot_required` with no events (`gateway/session_events.py:126`); re-resume then.
- **Subscriptions.** Keep each attach's `subscription_id`. Leaving a chat sends `session.detach {session_id, subscription_id}` for that subscription only. Two local consumers of one session must not detach each other (`gateway/session_authority.py:375`, `gateway/session_controls.py:720`).
- **Profile routing.** Pass `profile` on every session call. Upstream routes sibling Profiles by it (`gateway/session_controls.py:307`).
- **Tooling.** `scripts/local-hermes --gateway` runs `hermes gateway run` with `webapp.enabled: true` on a loopback port in its temp home. `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures --local --gateway` records canonical frames into `HermesMobileTests/Fixtures/HermesAgent/canonical-*.json`.

## Decisions

- Profile isolation: one canonical socket per Profile (parent decision 2).
- Long gaps: restore saved history and live state; don't rebuild lost partial text (parent decision 7).

## Acceptance and tests

- `HermesConversationTests`: a canonical Bot Chat resumes with no `session_key`, replays with an epoch different from `gateway.ready`'s, reconnects, and delivers each event once. Fails today at the resume params.
- Two consumers share a subscription; an older attach's late detach leaves the newer one attached.
- Legacy fixtures keep passing unchanged.

## Fixtures

Canonical ready; create; idle and running resume; replay success; epoch mismatch; a replay gap; a repeated subscription; a non-default Profile.

## Not in scope

Sending, controls, session edits, enabling canonical hosts, any user-facing toggle.

## Mocks / blockers / outside reach / surfaces

- **Mocks:** none.
- **Blockers:** none.
- **Outside reach:** `scripts/local-hermes` only, on this Mac. No live-host writes.
- **Surfaces:** conversation attach on iPhone and iPad, including deep links and Live Activity taps that reopen a chat. No extension changes.

title: feat(chat): run and answer canonical gateway turns
body:
**What the user gets:** on a canonical gateway, a chat can send, queue, steer, stop, and answer approvals, clarify, sudo and secret prompts.
**Why it matters:** slice 2 of #1341. A turn that starts but can't be stopped or answered is worse than a refusal, so these go together.
**Cost:** Large. Phone check at the end of #1341.

Part of #1341. Its decisions apply here; read the parent first. Same branch and PR as #1341's other children, one commit. The refusal stays in place.

## Plan

- **Send.** Mint one `submission_id` per deliberate send and keep it for a retry of that same send. The host refuses a send without `submission_id` or `input_id` (`gateway/session_controls.py:819-830`), and the session must be attached first. Today's params: `HermesCall.swift` `.promptSubmit`.
- **Receipts.** Read the canonical admission states. `BotPromptMode.swift:41` knows `streaming` and `queued`, not `started`, `unknown` or `terminal` (`gateway/session_contract.py:53`). Keep `admission_id` apart from `submission_id`.
- **Controls.** `session.interrupt`, `session.steer` and `session.redirect` require `execution_generation` (`CanonicalControlParams`, `CanonicalCorrectionParams`). Use the server's generation from the snapshot and events, never the app's local attach counter. On `stale_generation`, adopt the fences the refusal carries and offer the action again; never resend on its own.
- **Queue.** `pending` holds separate admissions. Track them by `admission_id` instead of the single merged queued string (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:559`, `:825`, `:1310`). A cancelled admission isn't the running turn's completion.
- **Approval and clarify.** They arrive as `approval.request` and `clarify.request` events with `prompt_id` and `execution_generation`, plus `.settled` events, and snapshots restore them in `prompts` (`gateway/session_pending_controls.py:18-60`). Answer with `approval.respond {session_id, execution_generation, prompt_id, choice}` and `clarify.respond {…, answer}`; the host refuses any extra key (`gateway/session_controls.py:931-941`). Replies report `status: resolved | already_resolved` rather than a numeric `resolved` (`HermesConversation.swift:314`). `BotPendingRequest.swift:50` parses today's envelopes.
- **Sudo and secret.** These stay server requests on the canonical socket ("Secret/sudo prompts remain native", `gateway/session_pending_controls.py:4`). Answer them with a JSON-RPC response frame instead of the legacy `request.answer` proxy (`HermesConversation.swift:306`; `gateway/session_server_requests.py:72`, `:125`).
- **Skip all.** Send YOLO for the session without `scope: "session"`, which the canonical handler refuses (`gateway/session_tui_config.py:173`, `:343`).
- `prompt.btw` and `prompt.background` aren't served on a canonical socket (`session.`/`prompt.` methods the gateway doesn't own answer -32601, `tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py`). Hide them there, using the connection's existing missing-method record (`HermesGateway.swift:445`).

## Decisions

- Stop cancels the known queued admissions, then interrupts the running generation (parent decision 3).
- A turn whose outcome is unknown gets an explicit acknowledge-or-discard action (`prompt.resolve_unknown`), never an automatic retry (parent decision 4).

## Acceptance and tests

- `HermesChatTurnTests`: a canonical send clears the draft only after an accepted receipt; two queued admissions stay separate; another admission's cancellation doesn't end the running turn. Fails today.
- `HermesChatRequestTests`: a restored canonical approval answers with its own `prompt_id` and generation. Fails today.
- A lost acknowledgement never resubmits. A stale action sends nothing. A sudo answer doesn't report "expired" while the request still waits.

## Fixtures

Queued, started, terminal and unknown receipts; two queued admissions; a generation change; approval and clarify lifecycles, including batch clarify; sudo and secret; cancellation during another running admission.

## Not in scope

Transcript edits, model settings, rooms, a general retry system.

## Mocks / blockers / outside reach / surfaces

- **Mocks:** required for any changed queue display, the unknown-outcome action, or request-card copy. Build them and stop for a pick first (CLAUDE.md, Visual and design work).
- **Blockers:** #1601.
- **Outside reach:** `scripts/local-hermes --gateway` only.
- **Surfaces:** chat on iPhone and iPad, share-extension handoff into a chat, hardware-keyboard Send, deep-link reattach, Live Activity waiting and completion, notification taps. No secret is persisted.

title: feat(sessions): edit canonical sessions through fenced mutations
body:
**What the user gets:** on a canonical gateway, rename, delete, branch, undo, compress, edit-and-resend and Move to Project keep working.
**Why it matters:** slice 3 of #1341. Each of these answers -32601 or 4001 there today.
**Cost:** Large. Phone check at the end of #1341.

Part of #1341. Its decisions apply here; read the parent first. Same branch and PR, one commit. The refusal stays in place.

## Plan

- **One mutation path.** `session.mutate {session_id, request_id, expected_revision, operation, payload}` (`SessionMutateParams`; operations in `gateway/session_mutations.py:18-22`). Keep the `request_id` for a retry of the same edit. On `revision_conflict` or `stale_generation`, adopt the fresh fences the refusal carries (`gateway/session_controls.py` `mutate`) and keep the user's intent. Today `HermesGateway.swift:442` drops those fields from a failure.
- **Map:**
  - rename (`HermesSlashCommands.swift:282`) → `rename`
  - delete → `delete`
  - branch → `branch` with `through_message_id`, the physical row id of the last kept message (`hermes_state_mutations.py:59`), not today's visible-row count (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1024`)
  - undo and edit → `rewind` with `target_message_id` (`hermes_state_mutations.py:44`)
  - compress → `compress`
  - `session.cwd.set` and `session.workspace.move` → `workspace {cwd}`
  - Call sites: `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:785`, `:857`, `:885`, `:917`, `:1027`.
- **Edit and resend** becomes a rewind, then a fresh send through #1602. A canonical submit refuses the legacy truncate keys (`gateway/session_controls.py:823`).
- **Delete.** Drop the legacy close-every-runtime sequence (`HermesSessionActions.swift:209`). The canonical `delete` has its own fences; detaching is not closing.
- **Bot Chat creation.** Canonical `session.create` already takes `title` and `hidden` (`CanonicalCreateParams`), so skip the follow-up `session.title` (`BotCreator.swift:292`). Avatar generation's draft create and close-and-delete (`BotAvatarGeneration.swift:111`, `:121`) uses the same paths.
- Leave the REST metadata, import and export paths alone unless a canonical fixture shows a defect.

## Decisions

- Edit-and-resend is two steps. Keep the edited text, and say so plainly if the send fails after the rewind (parent decision 5).

## Acceptance and tests

- `HermesSessionActionsTests`: a canonical delete sends `session.mutate delete` with the current revision and never closes unrelated runtimes.
- `HermesChatTurnTests`: branching at a selected row sends that row's physical id; a stale mutation leaves local state unchanged.
- `HermesCompressClearTests`: compress goes through `session.mutate`.
- Bot Chat creation completes without `session.title`.
- Each fails today with -32601 or invalid params.

## Fixtures

Mutation success and refusal; a revision and a generation conflict; branch at a selected row; compaction; a busy delete; a titled create; a rewind followed by a refused send.

## Not in scope

Model and reasoning settings (#1604), an in-place reset for `/clear`, rewriting working REST writes.

## Mocks / blockers / outside reach / surfaces

- **Mocks:** only for the partial-failure state (rewind succeeded, send didn't). Build it and stop for a pick first.
- **Blockers:** #1601 and #1602.
- **Outside reach:** none beyond `scripts/local-hermes --gateway`.
- **Surfaces:** chat actions and slash commands, session-list context menus, Archived, Bot creation, the avatar editor, keyboard shortcuts.

title: feat(chat): adapt canonical session settings
body:

title: fix(rooms): recover canonical room attempts safely
body:
**What the user gets:** on a canonical gateway, room creation offers only Profiles that can join, and a stuck room task offers the action the host can actually do: Retry, or a confirmed Discard.
**Why it matters:** slice 5 of #1341. Retry answers 4001 there, Discard can't be answered at all, and the creator offers every Profile.
**Cost:** Medium. Phone check at the end of #1341.

Part of #1341. Its decisions apply here; read the parent first. Same branch and PR, one commit. The refusal stays in place. The legacy Retry shape stays for legacy hosts.

## Plan

- **Seatable Profiles.** `groups.capabilities` now returns `seatable_profiles` (`gateway/session_group_controls.py:145`). Parse it (`BotGroupRoom.swift:11`), filter the creator's roster with it (`BotRoomCreator.swift:35`, `:72`), and recheck before `groups.create`.
- **Retry.** Send `groups.retry {room_id, member_id, task_id, execution_generation}` (`CanonicalRoomAttemptParams`). Today it sends only room and task (`BotRoomAction.swift:38`; `HermesCall.swift` `.groupsRetry`).
- **Discard.** For an attempt whose outcome is unknown, the host offers Discard rather than Retry (`gateway/session_hosted_controls.py:73`). Send `groups.discard` with the same four fields after the user confirms.
- Keep capability gating, exact pending tuples, read-only handling of unknown actions, and outcome reconciliation (`BotRoomReader.swift:262`, `:364`).

## Decisions

- Include Discard. Leave `groups.continue` (resuming a discussion paused at its cap, keyed by `discussion_event_id`) for its own issue. It isn't in `x-canonical-methods` and isn't the Discard answer.

## Acceptance and tests

- `BotRoomTests`: a canonical deferred task's Retry sends all four fields; an unknown-outcome task offers a confirmed Discard and never Retry.
- `BotRoomManagementTests`: Profiles that can't be seated can't enter a create request.
- Both fail today.

## Fixtures

Seatable roster; deferred Retry; unknown-outcome Discard; a stale tuple's refusal; a lost acknowledgement; a legacy capabilities reply without `seatable_profiles`.

## Not in scope

Peer administration, room attachments, room context, Continue.

## Mocks / blockers / outside reach / surfaces

- **Blockers:** #1601 (protocol mode only).

title: feat(hermes): enable supported Webapp connections
body:
**What the user gets:** Hermex connects to a Hermes Webapp behind a password or browser sign-in and works there like on the dashboard. Open (no-password) Webapps still get a clear refusal.
**Why it matters:** last slice of #1341. It removes the refusal from #1340 once #1601-#1605 are in.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner on a phone.

Part of #1341. Its decisions apply here; read the parent first. Same branch and PR, last commit.

## Plan

- **Enable.** Drop the `session_authority` refusal (`HermesGateway.swift:347`) once #1601-#1605 pass; the protocol mode from #1601 selects the adapter. #1598's Add Server check then refuses only what is still unsupported, namely an open Webapp (`HermesConnection.swift:227`, `HermesREST.withholdsPageToken`).
- **Host identity.** The Webapp's signed-out `/api/status` leaves out `install_id` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:507`, `:630`), so today's check before the password goes out sees nothing (`HermesConnection.swift:210`, `:264`; `BotConnection.swift:39`). Read status again after sign-in, compare it with the saved `install_id`, and refuse a mismatch before loading data. Save it the first time.
- **Tokens.** Password sign-in uses cookies, which keep working. On the Webapp behind sign-in, a bearer token works on its own only if this listener issued it through `/auth/native/token` (`hermes_cli/webapp_sign_in.py:19`). A browser sign-in made elsewhere gets refused once, which needs one deliberate sign-in and never a retry loop (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py:616`).
- **Restart.** The phone's restart action calls hermex-push's process restart (`BotDashboardClient.swift:63`). It skips the gateway's drain when the gateway serves the dashboard (uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#33). Hide it on canonical hosts until that ships.
- **Docs.** Update `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` (connection, detection, the gateway listener), `docs/agents/bots.md`, `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md`, and `CONTEXT.md` if new vocabulary lands.

## Decisions

- Check identity after sign-in, before loading any data (parent decision 6).
- Open Webapps stay unsupported: they hand out credentials only through one-use launch links (`gateway/run_api.py:83`).

## Acceptance and tests

- `BotClientTests` (today's refusal case at `:803`): a canonical handshake now connects.
- `HermesConnectionTests`: a signed-out status without identity, then a signed-in identity mismatch, refuses; password cookies work; a browser token the listener didn't issue asks for sign-in once.
- Add Server saves nothing after a failed live check.
- One integrated signed-Debug pass on the final head covers:
  - both protocols, and two servers
  - a non-default Profile
  - backgrounding and foregrounding
  - attachments and request answers
  - rooms and navigation

## Fixtures

Signed-out and signed-in status pair; password-cookie flow; native token and refresh, accepted and refused; an open Webapp's page; a completed canonical handshake.

## Not in scope

Raising `minimumVersion`, replacing credentials or addresses automatically, server deployment, another pin advance.

## Mocks / blockers / outside reach / surfaces

- **Mocks:** required for any changed connection, refusal or recovery copy. Mock first.
- **Blockers:** #1601-#1605, and #1598.
- **Outside reach:** hermex-push restart verification (other repo). Phone validation by the owner.
- **Surfaces:** every one. iPhone, iPad, share extension, Live Activity and notification taps, deep links, App Intents, multiple servers.

title: fix(scripts): let a backgrounded local-hermes stop on SIGINT
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: a small tooling fix found during #1600.

## What changed

Stopping a backgrounded `scripts/local-hermes` (`scripts/local-hermes &`, as agents run it) with `kill -INT` did nothing. A shell starts a background job with SIGINT ignored, and Python keeps that, so the run kept going, along with its temp `HERMES_HOME`. SIGTERM worked, but nobody expects to need it.

`local-hermes` now handles SIGINT itself, the same way it already handles SIGTERM and SIGHUP. Ctrl-C in a terminal behaves as before.

## How it was tested

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 65 tests, OK.
- A real run: started `scripts/local-hermes &` from a non-interactive shell, waited until it was ready, then sent `kill -INT` to the captured PID. It stopped in 2 s, removed its temp home, and freed port 9199. Before the fix, the same SIGINT left it running.

Fixes #1598

## What changed

Pointing Hermex at a Hermes gateway's own listener, which since 0.23.0 serves the Webapp on port 9120, signed in fine at Add Server and saved a server that could never chat. Its home then showed the error with Reconnect or Retry, which reach the same address. The only way out was Settings → remove the server → Add Server.

title: feat(hermes): speak the canonical session protocol of gateway-served hosts
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1601. Fixes #1602. Fixes #1603. Fixes #1604. Fixes #1605. Fixes #1606. Part of #1341.

This is the epic's one PR, with one commit per child issue (#1341, Decisions §1), plus a capture-script fix and two review fixes. The last commit, #1606, lifts the `session_authority` refusal, so this is the PR that makes a Hermes Webapp behind sign-in connect.

## What changed

Hermes 0.23.0 lets the gateway serve its own Webapp, whose sockets speak a different session protocol. Hermex refused those hosts: signed in, every chat would have broken. #1601-#1605 teach Hermex that protocol, reached only through tests; #1606 turns it on. The first slice attaches to a session on such a socket and replays its events in order.

- **Detection.** `HermesGateway` records `gateway.ready`'s `session_authority` as `speaksCanonicalProtocol`, next to `replayEpoch`. Production still refuses that socket with `.gatewayListener`; only tests set `Options.opensCanonicalSockets`.
- **Adapter.** `HermesCanonicalProtocol.swift` sits at the one place a `HermesCall` becomes a frame, modeled on Desktop's `canonical-protocol.ts`.
  - Resume drops `close_on_disconnect`, which the host refuses with 4001.
  - `session.events.since` carries `profile` and the session's own `replay_epoch` from its snapshot. With any other epoch the host answers `snapshot_required` and sends no events.
- **Subscriptions.** The host keeps one subscription per socket and session, so screens on one session share it.
  - Only the last screen holding a session sends `session.detach`.
  - A screen holds a session from the moment its resume is sent, so an older screen leaving can't end a newer screen's attach that is still in flight.
  - A screen that leaves before its reply arrives still gets the reply's subscription detached.
- **Snapshot readers.** `HermesConversation` reads the canonical snapshot's `stored_session_id` and epoch. The turn coordinator reads the queued prompt from `pending`.
- **Tooling.** `scripts/local-hermes --gateway` runs the pinned gateway with the Webapp on 9121. `scripts/capture-hermes-fixtures --local --gateway` records `canonical-*.json` at `2bd378ed`. AGENTS.md, DEVELOPMENT.md and `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` describe both.

Deferred, with reasons on #1601:
- One canonical socket per Profile (decision 2) moves to #1606, where canonical sockets turn on. It needs a decision on which socket the inbox and rooms use.
- A resume whose requested key resolves to a different session id, overlapping another screen's leave, is a follow-up. It is a rare compression-chain case.

### #1602: run and answer canonical turns

A turn that starts but can't be stopped or answered is worse than a refusal, so these go together.

- **Send.** `prompt.submit` carries `profile` and a `submission_id` minted per send. The admission receipt reads `queued` even on an idle session, so it counts as a start unless a turn runs, a lost turn blocks the queue, or the receipt names the admission already running. A reply naming no admission keeps the draft.
- **Controls.** Steer, redirect and Stop carry the host's `execution_generation`, tracked from snapshots and frames. A `stale_generation` refusal sends nothing more: "The reply moved on before Stop reached it. Tap Stop again." Mock A was picked.
- **Stop** withdraws the known queued admissions (`prompt.cancel`), then interrupts the generation it was tapped for (decision 3).
- **Queue.** One bubble per `pending` admission (mock B). A withdrawn admission's `message.complete` carries no generation and doesn't end the running turn.
- **Lost turn.** A turn lost across a host restart shows "Lost during restart · Discard" (mock A). Discard sends `prompt.resolve_unknown` with that turn's own generation (decision 4).
- **Requests.** Approval and clarify prompts arrive as `*.request` events and snapshot `prompts`, mapped onto today's cards. They're answered by `prompt_id` and generation and retired by `*.settled`. Sudo and secret are answered with a JSON-RPC response frame; the `request.answer` proxy reports "expired" there. Skip all's `yolo` drops `scope`.
- **Differences from the issue, checked live:**
  - `prompt.btw` and `prompt.background` are served on canonical sockets, so nothing is hidden.
  - A batch clarify arrives only when a send sets `clarify_batch`, which Hermex never does.
  - Sudo, secret and lost-turn shapes come from the upstream source; the local stub can't produce them.
- **Tooling.** The `local-hermes` stub asks one `clarify` question when the prompt mentions "clarify". The capture records receipts, a queue, a withdrawn admission, a stale stop, a generation change and a clarify lifecycle.

### #1603: edit canonical sessions through fenced mutations

Rename, delete, branch, undo, compress, edit-and-resend and Move to Project answered -32601 or 4001 on a canonical host.

- **One path.** Each edit is a `session.mutate {request_id, expected_revision, operation, payload}`.
  - Every edit but rename also carries `expected_generation`; verified live: delete and branch refuse without it.
  - The conversation tracks the session's revision next to its generation.
  - A `revision_conflict` or `stale_generation` refusal adopts the host's fresh fences and resends nothing.
  - An edit whose answer was lost goes out again identical when asked again, so the host answers from its receipt. `/undo` reuses it rather than deriving another target.
- **Branch** keeps the rows through the selected row's own id (`through_message_id`); nothing is counted.
- **`/undo`** rewinds the last saved prompt.
- **Edit, Regenerate and Retry** rewind the prompt's row, then send the text as a plain send (decision 5). If the send is refused after the cut, the rows go, the text returns to the composer, and the chat says so: "The later messages were removed, but your edited message wasn't sent. It's in the message box: send it again." Mock A was picked.
- **Delete, Move from the list and the avatar draft cleanup** read fences with an identity resume and send one edit. No runtime is closed.
- **Bot Chat creation** skips `session.title`: a canonical create already titles and hides the chat.
- **Fixture:** `canonical-mutations.json` holds a rename, a revision conflict, a stale-generation rewind, a branch, a rewind, a compaction (`noop`; the stub can't produce a real one), a busy and a settled delete, and a titled create.

### #1604: canonical session settings

`config.set model` answers 4001 `use_session_mutation_model` on a canonical host, and a session-scoped Fast answers 4001. The chips and the confirmation sheet are unchanged.

- **Model.** The pick is the session's fenced `model` edit.
  - A guarded target answers `confirmation_required` with a `confirm` token, and the sheet's Change model resends that exact selection with it.
  - A stale token is answered with a fresh one and asked again, never applied.
  - A pick deferred to the running reply is confirmed later through `session.updated`. The deferred selection is kept apart from the display state `session.info` clears.
- **Fast** goes without `scope`.
- **Reasoning, personality and approval mode** are unchanged.
- **Fixture:** `canonical-settings.json` records a model edit, the acknowledgements, and the `config.set model` and scoped-Fast refusals. The stub model has no price, so the confirmation exchange is built from the upstream shape.

### #1605: canonical group chats

A canonical host fences each room task by member and execution generation, and refuses Retry without them (`invalid_params`, checked live).

- **Retry** sends `member_id` and `execution_generation` as the host named them, only on a canonical socket; the dashboard keeps room and task. A stalled preparation's Retry names every member it couldn't wake (`"chief, coder"`), so that string is sent back unchanged.
- **Discard.** A task whose outcome is unknown after a restart comes as a `discard` action. Its card says "Hermes restarted while this bot was replying, so its reply is lost." and offers Discard, never Retry, confirmed in an action sheet (mock A). It sends `groups.discard` with all four fields.
- **Stale.** A retry or discard the task moved past answers 4001 `stale_generation`: "This chat changed on the server. Reopen it and try again."
- **Who can join.** The creator lists, selects and sends only `groups.capabilities.seatable_profiles`, with a footer when some are left out and an empty state under two (mock A). Create rechecks them. The host refuses an unseatable member before it looks for the room, so a Try Again after a lost reply reads the rooms instead: it opens the room it made, or unlocks the choice. A dashboard names no list and is unchanged.

### #1606: connect to a Webapp behind sign-in

- **Enable.** The `session_authority` refusal is gone. An open Webapp (no sign-in) is still refused: it hands out credentials only through one-use launch links. New copy (mock B): "This Hermes Webapp has no sign-in, and Hermex connects only to one that has. Turn its sign-in on, or connect to hermes dashboard (port 9119 by default) instead."
- **Host identity** (decision 6). The Webapp leaves `install_id` out of a signed-out status. When the public read had none, sign-in reads `/api/status` again signed in and checks the saved install before anything loads; a first sign-in saves it. The public read sends no cookies, so a leftover sign-in can't make the Webapp look like a dashboard.
- **One socket per Profile** (decision 2). On a Webapp each Profile's chats get their own socket, opened with a ticket the Webapp binds to that Profile (`/api/webapp/socket-ticket?socket=gateway&profile=`), so a call that names no Profile (`file.attach`, `prompt.btw`) is answered for it. The inbox, rooms and Settings reads keep the shared socket; a dashboard keeps one socket.
- **A Profile the Webapp doesn't serve.** A gateway that can't serve every Profile (two holding one bot token, a Profile on its own gateway) serves only its default one, and the Webapp refuses the others' sockets with a 403. Found on the owner's phone. Such a chat now says "This Hermes Webapp doesn’t serve the dev Profile, so its chats can’t open here. On the host, hermes gateway status says why. Or connect to hermes dashboard, which serves every Profile." (mock A), with no Try Again.
- **Tokens.** Password cookies work. A browser sign-in's refresh token the Webapp didn't issue is refused as expired and asks for one sign-in.
- **Restart.** hermex-push's "Restart Hermes…" skips a Webapp gateway's drain (uzairansaruzi/hermex-push#33), so it's hidden there, in push Settings and Screen; the fallback text names the gateway (mock A).
- **Docs.** `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` has a canonical-protocol section; `bots.md` and `hermes-feature-index.md` follow. Fixtures: the Webapp's signed-out and signed-in status and a refused native refresh.

## How it was tested

  - A repeated resume reuses its `subscription_id`.
  - A wrong-epoch replay, and one from a cursor ahead of the host's, answer `snapshot_required`.

title: Help users serve every Profile when a Webapp serves only default
body:
**What the user gets:** when a Hermes Webapp can't open a Profile, Hermex says the host's real reason and offers a guided fix that makes every Profile available, without a terminal. **Why it matters:** found on the owner's phone after #1606. A gateway that can't serve every Profile from one process serves only `default`, so every other bot and chat on the Webapp is unusable until someone fixes the host by hand. **Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner on a phone and a host that can be put into the blocked state. Follow-up to #1606, part of #1341. ## What happens today Upstream serves every Profile from one gateway by default (`gateway.multiplex_profiles`), but at each start it falls back to `default` only when its preflight finds a blocker: - two Profiles holding the same bot token - another Profile running its own gateway - a port-binding platform without a `/p//` ingress - a Profile set to `gateway.standalone: true` (`website/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways.md`, "Multiplexing is on by default" and "Blockers and fixes", at the pin.) Hermex then shows the #1606 message ("This Hermes Webapp doesn’t serve the dev Profile… `hermes gateway status` says why…") with no way forward from the phone. On the owner's host the only blocker was `dev` holding the same `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` as `default`. The fix, done by hand on 2026-11-07, was two steps: 1. Remove those two keys from `dev` (`DELETE /api/env?profile=dev`). 2. Run `hermes gateway migrate --multiplex`. After that, all 8 Profiles opened on the Webapp. ## Upstream surface (verified at the pin `2bd378ed`; the plan route also read live on a Webapp) - `GET /api/gateway/migrate/plan` returns the preflight: `blockers` (prose), `notices`, `profiles`, `already_multiplexed`, `eligible`, `command` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/actions.py:169`, `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate.py:177`). - `POST /api/gateway/migrate` runs `hermes gateway migrate --multiplex --yes` detached, re-checking blockers itself (`actions.py:177`). It restarts the gateway: the phone's connection drops and comes back. - `DELETE /api/env?profile=

` removes one key from one Profile and never returns its value (`hermes_cli/web_routers/config_env.py:1080`). Hermex already wraps it (`HermesEnvironmentClient.remove`), but its Environment screen hides bot tokens (`channel_managed`). - The signed-in `/api/status` carries `gateway_mode` and `multiplex_standalone_reason`, the host's plain-English reason. The signed-out Webapp status leaves them out (`hermes_cli/web_routers/status.py:507`). ## Plan 1. **Say the real reason (first slice).** When a Profile isn't served, quote `multiplex_standalone_reason` from the signed-in status instead of "`hermes gateway status` says why". Sign-in already reads that status on a Webapp (`HermesConnection.signIn`). Show the same line on the server's Settings page while the Webapp serves only some Profiles. 2. **Guided fix.** From that message, open a screen that reads the migration plan and lists its blockers. - For a duplicate bot token, ask which Profile keeps the bot, recommending the one that answers today. Remove the duplicate from the other Profile with `DELETE /api/env`, then re-read the plan. - With no blockers left, confirm "Serve every Profile", with copy that states the consequence: the gateway restarts, running work stops, bots reconnect. - Then `POST /api/gateway/migrate`, wait for the host the way the hermex-push restart wait does (`HermesRestartWait`), and verify that the Profile opens. 3. **Fallback for other blockers.** For a blocker the guided fix doesn't handle, offer a recovery chat opened explicitly on the served Profile (Troubleshoot today opens on New Session's Profile, `SettingsAboutPage.troubleshoot`). It names the unserved Profile and the host's reason and asks the agent to explain `hermes gateway migrate --multiplex --dry-run`. Per `.github/triage/PLAYBOOK.md`, the agent proposes commands and never reads `.env` or restarts the gateway itself. ## Decisions for the owner (mock first) - Copy for the reason line, the guided-fix screen and its confirmation (`AGENTS.md`: mocks before real components). - Whether Hermex removes a duplicate bot token natively (recommended: one REST call behind a confirmation, and no value leaves the host), or hands every blocker to the recovery chat. Upstream gives blockers as prose only, so naming the Profile and key means parsing that text. Fall back to the recovery chat when parsing fails, and ask upstream for structured blocker fields. ## Traps - `eligible` is the bar for automatic migration during `hermes update`. It stays false on a host where no Profile runs its own gateway, even when the explicit migrate command works (`gateway_migrate.py:192`). Don't gate on it. - Never write `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` directly. An explicit `true` skips the preflight; use the migrate route. - `POST /api/gateway/migrate` answering `ok` means it started, not finished. Verify after the gateway comes back. - Migrating moves other Profiles' webhook URLs under `/p//`. Say so in the confirmation when the plan's notices mention it. ## Acceptance and tests - A Webapp serving only `default` shows the host's reason for an unserved Profile. - On a host blocked by a duplicate token, the guided fix removes the duplicate from the chosen Profile, migrates after one confirmation, and the Profile opens afterwards. Each server call is checked at the boundary it crosses, using upstream shapes. - A blocker the fix doesn't handle offers the recovery chat on the served Profile. - One phone pass on a real Webapp put into the blocked state, then fixed from the phone. ## Not in scope Editing other Profiles' messaging configuration beyond removing a duplicate token; `profile_routes`; open Webapps; a host terminal.

title: feat(hermes): show why a Webapp serves only one Profile and fix it from the phone
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1611

## What changed

A Hermes Webapp whose gateway can't serve every Profile serves only `default`, and Hermex just said "`hermes gateway status` says why", with no way forward from the phone. On the owner's host every other Profile's chats were unusable until the host was fixed by hand.

Now Hermex says the host's real reason and fixes the common case itself:

- **The reason.** The chat error and the server's Settings page read `multiplex_standalone_reason` from the signed-in `/api/status`. When every blocker is a duplicate bot token, they summarize it ("dev and default use the same Telegram and Discord bots."). The host's own words are one tap away under "What the host says".
- **Serve Every Profile.** "Fix on This Phone" opens a screen that reads `GET /api/gateway/migrate/plan`. For each duplicate bot you pick which Profile keeps it (the one answering today by default), and Hermex removes the token from the other with `DELETE /api/env`; no value ever leaves the host. With nothing left blocking, one confirmation ("Restart the gateway?") starts `POST /api/gateway/migrate`. Hermex then waits for the restarted gateway to report `already_multiplexed` and checks that the Profile's chats open. A chat already showing messages offers the same fix on its composer error.
- **Recovery chat.** A blocker the fix doesn't handle, including a duplicate whose removal didn't clear it (a token in `config.yaml`), offers "Ask the Agent on default". It opens a new chat on `default`, the Profile a standalone gateway serves, with a prompt that names the unserved Profile and the host's words. The prompt asks the agent to walk through `hermes gateway migrate --multiplex --dry-run` and propose commands, without reading `.env` or restarting the gateway. Nothing is sent until the user does.

It never gates on the plan's `eligible` and never writes `gateway.multiplex_profiles` directly: an explicit `true` skips the preflight. Upstream gives blockers as prose only, so recognizing a duplicate means parsing `duplicate_credential_lines`' wording. Anything that doesn't match falls back to the host's words and the recovery chat.

## How it was tested

- **Contract.** Read at the pin `2bd378ed` (`gateway_migrate.py`, `web_routers/actions.py`, `config_env.py`, `web_server_gateway.py`, `status.py`). Checked live on `scripts/local-hermes --gateway`'s Webapp: the plan's blocker text, `DELETE /api/env` answering 200 `{found}` and then 404 `{detail}`, `POST /api/gateway/migrate` answering `{ok, pid, name}`, and the signed-in status carrying the reason.
- **XCTest** on iPhone 17e via `scripts/test-sim`: `ServeEveryProfileTests` (new), `HermesGatewayTests`, `HermesOfflineCacheTests`, `BotChatPresentationTests`, `HermesEnvironmentClientTests`, `AppIntentNewChatTests`, `LocalizationCatalogTests`. All pass. `ci/check_string_catalog.py` covers every key, and all new copy is in the 17 shipped languages.
- **Real-app pass** on iPhone 17e against the pinned gateway's Webapp. It booted on a temp home where `dev` held `default`'s fake Telegram and Discord tokens, so the gateway served only `default`, as on the owner's host. Checked: the Settings row and reason; the `dev` chat error; removal (both tokens gone from `dev`'s `.env`, kept in `default`'s); the confirmation and the host's migration. Then Check Again verified `dev` opens and reloaded the chat, and the Settings row went away. A second boot with a `config.yaml` duplicate showed the recovery chat opening on Default with its prompt unsent. This pass found and fixed two bugs: the Settings row never loading, and the `config.yaml` duplicate dead-ending.
- **Not covered:** in that pass the gateway the migration restarted didn't come back on its own. `local-hermes` gives the Webapp's sign-in only through the environment, which the detached restart doesn't inherit. A real host keeps its password hash in `config.yaml`. The app correctly reported that `dev` still didn't open, and the restart was finished by hand.

Before: "This Hermes Webapp doesn't serve the dev Profile, so its chats can't open here. On the host, hermes gateway status says why. Or connect to hermes dashboard, which serves every Profile." After:

![Settings Profiles row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ba51b8e-f537-4d77-b719-6bd4dd2f4905)
![dev chat error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39977f1c-570c-4cb3-b909-77224c5f92cd)
![Serve Every Profile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6376d343-e84a-4758-ba8d-6e4c95506afb)
![Restart confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b143225-355a-4ded-8cf6-4db5606359df)
![A blocker the fix can't handle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ac2a867-de17-4683-9d6e-6c13fb5895d4)

Follow-up: a duplicate shared by three Profiles takes one removal per pair; the plan re-read shows anything left. Upstream structured blocker fields would replace the prose parsing.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)

title: feat(chat): open links that belong to installed apps (Universal Links) instead of the in-app Safari sheet
body:
## Problem

Since #866, Hermex opens every web link in an in-app Safari sheet (`SFSafariViewController`). iOS never hands links opened that way to the app that owns the domain through Universal Links. So a link like

```
https://mail.google.com/mail/u/?authuser=me%40gmail.com#all/<threadId>
```

opens Gmail on the web in the sheet. Tapping the same link in the ChatGPT iOS app, or in Messages, opens the exact thread in the Gmail app.

This matters a lot for bot-mode assistants. My Hermes bot sends inbox, package and calendar updates with links to the exact email, Google Calendar event or tracking page. Each of those should open in its native app (Gmail, Google Calendar, UPS/FedEx, Amazon) instead of a web view I'm not signed in to. The `googlegmail://` scheme only opens the Gmail app now and no longer deep-links to a thread, so Universal Links are the only route that works.

## Proposal

Before presenting the in-app Safari sheet, try the link as a Universal Link:

```swift
UIApplication.shared.open(url, options: [.universalLinksOnly: true]) { opened in
    if !opened { presentSafariSheet(url) }
}
```

That keeps the in-app sheet for ordinary web pages, but links that belong to an installed app open in that app. A Settings toggle would also do it, e.g. **Open links in: In-app browser / Default browser / Apps when available**.

A smaller alternative: add **Open in Safari** / **Open in App** to the link long-press context menu.

## Environment
- Hermex 2.x on iPhone, connected to a Hermes host in Bot Mode
- Gmail iOS app installed and signed in

title: Preview agent-generated HTML reports in chat
body:
### Use case

I use Hermes to generate self-contained HTML reports with tables, color-coded values, and embedded charts. In Hermex, the file card for a report such as daily-report.html shows “Tap to download”. I'd like to read the report directly in the chat flow on my iPhone, with the original file still available to save or share.

### Proposed behavior

Open .html and .htm file cards in the existing in-app attachment preview for direct Hermes chats. Render the static report with its inline styles and embedded images. Keep JavaScript, external resource loading, and page navigation disabled in the preview.

### Acceptance outcomes

- Tapping an agent-generated HTML file card opens a readable, scrollable preview in Hermex.
- Save to Files and Share export the original HTML.
- Existing download behavior remains available for unsupported file types.

### Upstream dependency notes

This can reuse the current Hermes attachment download. It needs no server API changes or new dependencies. The proposal is scoped to direct Hermes chats.

title: feat(stats): hermex-stats collector for opt-in daily reports
body:
**What the user gets:** Nothing directly. This receives the opt-in daily reports from #1625 and turns them into totals that only the maintainer reads.
**Why it matters:** #1079 needs a first-party, open-source receiver that never keeps an individual report.
**Cost:** Medium. No phone needed. Lives in a new repo.

Parent: #1079. Its Decisions and its report contract are the spec; read them first.

## Outside reach

- Creates the new public repo `uzairansaruzi/hermex-stats` (MIT). The owner approves creating it.
- Creates a D1 database and deploys a Worker on the Cloudflare account that runs the push relay. Name both before running them; the first deploy waits for the owner.

## Plan

Copy `hermex-push/relay`'s layout: `src/`, `test/` (vitest with `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`), `wrangler.jsonc`, `package.json`, and one GitHub Actions job for typecheck and tests.

- `src/report.ts`: parse a v1 report (the table in #1079) into a typed value, or reject it. Allowlist only: unknown keys, unknown enum values, wrong types, numbers out of range, a `day` that is today, later, or more than 8 UTC days back, and bodies over 4 KB are rejected with 400.
- `src/index.ts`: `POST /v1/day` only; anything else is 404. One D1 `batch` (a transaction) per report:
  1. `INSERT INTO seen(id, day)` (`id` is the primary key). A retried report fails this on the key, the whole batch rolls back, and the Worker answers 200 without counting anything.
  2. Upserts that add to `totals(period, start, app, os, device, metric, count)`, primary key everything but `count`:
     - `period='day'`, `start=day`: `active`; `used.<hermes-only|webui-only|both|none>`; `configured.<same>`; `feature.<name>`; `conn.<key>`; `recovery.<key>`; `crashes`; `hangs`. Counts add their value; flags add 1.
     - `period='week'`, `start=<that Monday>`, `metric='active'` only when `firstOfWeek`. Likewise `period='month'`, `start=<the 1st>` when `firstOfMonth`.
- A daily scheduled handler deletes `seen` rows older than 7 days and `totals` rows whose `start` is more than 12 months back.
- `scripts/stats.ts` (`npm run stats -- --days 30`): reads D1 through `wrangler d1 execute --remote --json` and prints daily, weekly and monthly **reported active installations** by app version; the server-kind mix; feature use as a share of active days; the connection pass rate and the top failure keys; recoveries; and crashes and hangs per 100 active days.
- `README.md`: what is stored and for how long, the field table (moved here from #1079, which then links to it), and how to check the account's usage.

## Acceptance

- A valid report adds exactly its totals.
- Posting the same `id` again answers 200 and changes nothing.
- A second report in a week with `firstOfWeek: false` leaves that week's `active` unchanged. The same holds for the month.
- Each rejection class answers 400 and writes nothing.
- The cron deletes only expired rows.
- `npm run stats` prints against a local D1 seeded from the tests' fixture.

## Tests

vitest in the Workers pool with a real local D1: one test per acceptance bullet. No tests for constants or copy.

## Decisions

- **D1, not KV or Analytics Engine.** D1 batches are atomic, which makes retry dedup one statement; KV counters race, and Analytics Engine keeps only 3 months against #1079's 12.
- **Duplicates fail the batch on the `seen` key.** Atomic, with no second round trip and no counted-but-unmarked window.
- **workers.dev URL, like the relay.** A custom domain isn't needed for v1. The URL goes into #1625 as a constant.
- **Cost:** one request and one D1 batch (about 30 row writes) per reporting install per day, well inside the Workers Paid allowance at any plausible volume. Check current D1 pricing at deploy time and note it in the PR.

## Mocks

None.

## Surfaces

None in the app.

title: feat(settings): share an opt-in daily usage and reliability report
body:
**What the user gets:** A one-time question whether to share a small daily usage and reliability summary with the maintainer, a toggle in About → Diagnostics to change the answer, and a page showing exactly what the next report says.
**Why it matters:** This is the phone half of #1079.
**Cost:** Large. Needs the owner's hands on a phone for the consent timing.

Parent: #1079. Its Decisions and its report contract are the spec. Blocked by #1624 for the collector URL and a live endpoint.

## Mocks first

Yes. Build three distinct static mocks covering (1) the consent alert's copy and (2) the sharing section in About → Diagnostics with its "Next Report" page. Publish them and stop for a pick. The copy says what's shared (usage and reliability counts), who receives it (the Hermex maintainer), that chats, files and server details never leave the phone, and that nothing is shared until the user accepts.

## Plan

One PR, one commit per slice.

1. **Report model and store.** New `HermesMobile/Config/UsageReport.swift`:
   - `struct UsageReport: Codable`, matching #1079's table field for field, with typed enums for server kinds, features, connection stages and failures. Nothing outside the contract can be encoded.
   - `UsageReportStore`: today's open day, the pending finished days (at most 8), and the last reported week and month, kept as one JSON file in Application Support like `DiagnosticsStore`. Thread-safe, because MetricKit calls in off the main thread.
   - The sharing answer is in standard `UserDefaults` (`usageReport.sharing`: unset means never asked). It isn't credential-like.
   - Days are UTC; weeks run Monday through Sunday.
2. **Recording.** Each seam calls one `UsageReportStore.shared.note(…)`, which does nothing unless sharing is on.
   - Foreground: on launch and on `.active` (`ContentView.swift:67`), open the day if needed. Record `configured` from the kinds in `authManager.servers`, and `used` from the active server's kind (`authManager.kind(of:)`, as at `ContentView.swift:90`). A server switch records `used` too.
   - `tasks`: `TasksView` appears.
   - `kanban`: `KanbanView` appears (`KanbanLabView.swift:2429`; shown from `SessionListView.swift:700` and `HermesSessionListView.swift:448`, `:479`).
   - `workspace`: `FileBrowserView` or `GitWorkspaceView` appears.
   - `share`: the main app consumes a share import (`ContentView.swift:304`). The extension itself records nothing.
   - `voice`: dictation or a voice note starts (`ComposerVoiceInputController.swift:239`, `ComposerVoiceNoteRecorder.swift:71`).
   - `connections`: a Hermes attempt (#1395) settles, either with every stage passed or at its first failed stage. The record lives in `HermesConnection.swift:592–604`; stages and failures are at `BotProtocol.swift:185–215`. Map `http(401)` and `http(403)` to `auth`, other 4xx to `http4xx`, and 5xx to `http5xx`. An attempt that is superseded or retired (the `attempt == attemptCount, !isRetired` guard) was cancelled and isn't counted. Each attempt counts once.
   - `recoveries`: a webui stream recovery that is confirmed or fails (`ChatStreamCoordinator.swift:507`, `:611`), and a Hermes gateway reconnect through the shared reconnect policy behind `BotInbox.swift:490` and `BotRoomReader.swift:215`. Count one per reconnect cycle, not per retry. Cancellation isn't a failure.
   - `crashes` and `hangs`: `DiagnosticsLog.didReceive` (`DiagnosticsLog.swift:17`) counts reports by kind on the day it receives them.
3. **Upload.** On `.active`, after launch work settles and never blocking UI, send each pending finished day to `POST {collector}/v1/day`, one at a time. Use an ephemeral `URLSession` with no cookies, no cache and none of a server's custom headers. A 2xx or a 400 removes the day; anything else keeps it for the next foreground. The collector URL is a constant from #1624.
4. **Consent alert.** New `HermesMobile/Config/UsageReportOffer.swift`, modeled on `NotificationOffer.swift`: the offer is claimed before it shows, so a crash or kill can't show it twice, and it is asked once per install. It's presented from the root on launch or `.active` when sharing was never asked, no chat stream is running, and no sheet or other offer is up; otherwise it waits for the next calm moment. New installs therefore see it on the connect screen before their first connection. Share turns sharing on; Don't Share stores the decline.
5. **Settings.** In `SettingsDiagnosticsPage.swift` (reached from `SettingsAboutPage.swift:47`), add a "Share Usage & Reliability" toggle with a one-line explanation, and a "Next Report" row. The row opens the open or oldest pending day as its exact JSON, using the same selectable-JSON page as `DiagnosticReportPage` (`SettingsDiagnosticsPage.swift:149`). Turning the toggle off erases the open day, the pending days and the remembered week and month, and cancels any upload in flight.
6. **Disclosures and docs.**
   - `HermesMobile/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`: add ProductInteraction, CrashData, PerformanceData and OtherDiagnosticData, each not linked, not tracking, purpose Analytics.
   - `CLAUDE.md` § Open at the core: name opt-in usage reports as the second exception next to push, and what they never contain.
   - New `docs/agents/usage-reports.md`: how recording, upload and consent fit together. It links to `hermex-stats`'s README for the fields.

## Acceptance

- Off by default: nothing is recorded or sent before the user taps Share.
- The first foreground on a later UTC day turns the open day into a pending report and sends it. A retry after a network failure sends the same `id`.
- `firstOfWeek` is true only on the first reported day of a UTC Monday–Sunday week; the same holds for `firstOfMonth` and the month.
- A day with only background work or push deliveries creates no report.
- Cancelled or superseded connection attempts and cancelled reconnects aren't counted.
- Turning sharing off erases everything unsent, and nothing is sent afterward.
- The alert shows once per install and never over a running stream.

## Tests

Focused, at the layer closest to the behavior:

- `UsageReportStoreTests`: day rollover; the week and month flags across Sunday→Monday UTC and across a month end; turning off erases; the pending cap.
- `UsageReportUploaderTests`, with a `URLProtocol` mock: 2xx and 400 remove the day; 5xx and offline keep it; a retry sends the same `id`; the request carries no cookies or custom headers.
- `UsageReportOfferTests`, like the NotificationOffer tests.
- A settled Hermes attempt counts once, and a superseded one doesn't.
- Encode one sample report and assert the fields the collector needs, not the whole body.

## Decisions

All settled in #1079. Engineering choices: Application Support JSON over SwiftData (a few KB, no queries). Pending days are capped at 8 because the collector rejects anything older. No background upload task; the next foreground is soon enough.

## Surfaces

- iPhone and iPad: form factor is a report field.
- Share extension: records nothing; the main app counts consumed imports.
- Live Activity widget, notification service, deep links, App Intents: not reached.
- Multiple servers: reports carry no server identity, only kinds.
- Localization: new strings go in the String Catalog. VoiceOver labels for the toggle and the Next Report row.

## Outside reach

None in the app beyond calling #1624's endpoint. The first real upload needs #1624 deployed, which the owner approves.

title: fix: small bugs, dead code, and stale docs from a full-project audit
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: a maintainer-requested audit sweep, so this is one PR across several areas by design.

## What changed

I asked for a read of the whole project to find what is broken, inconsistent, inefficient, or no longer needed. That turned up about 250 findings. This PR lands only the ones with a single mechanical fix that was checked against the source; everything that needs a product decision, a device check, or new translations stays on a review list.

**Bugs**
- webui: a `+` in any query value (file paths, search, skill files) reached the server as a space. `Endpoint` now escapes it, as `HermesREST` already does.
- `/Model x` (any capital in a command name) never reached its argument list.
- Tool arguments showed numbers with locale grouping (`port: 8,080`).
- A slow linked-file read in Skill detail could show under another file's title.
- A Tasks list read that landed after a row's pause put the old state back.
- A Hermes sign-out could pull the app back to the old server's sign-in form after a switch.
- Adding a webui server left the previous server's Profiles in the Shortcuts picker.
- Typing a `/workspace` argument could show "The request was cancelled." in the composer; a cancelled Providers refresh showed "Couldn't refresh".
- The delegated-work sheet could stay on "Refreshing" after a cancelled pull.
- A plugin settings page trapped on a repeated settings key.
- A failed Task edit left its error on Task Detail after Cancel.
- Changing the Bot connection kept Screen hidden for the new host.
- A custom header named `accept` could replace the SSE stream's `Accept`.

**Behavior changes worth a look**
- On a Hermes chat the mic is now a plain button. Its hold started nothing there, so a slow tap did nothing.
- A webui server behind a down Cloudflare tunnel (HTTP 520-530) now counts as unreachable: the offline cache is used and the copy says the server can't be reached, as on a Hermes server.

**Performance:** `ChatView.body` read the draft on every pass, so each keystroke re-ran the whole chat screen.

**Native quality:** three animations now respect Reduce Motion; three strings (a Lock Screen line, a VoiceOver value, a Kanban title) use translations the catalog already had.

**No longer needed (about 870 lines, each with zero references in any target or test):** the debug-only Kanban lab (610 lines, no entry point), two old onboarding components, `SessionListViewModel.sections`, and a set of unused helpers, properties, and always-true guards. Five String Catalog keys are now unused; the catalog is untouched.

**Tooling and docs:** `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans` no longer compiled (`BinaryFilePreview` moved beside `FileReference` so the host build finds it). Docs that named tests and views that no longer exist, or said a Hermes server has no push pairing, are corrected. A Profile name can no longer reach the connection log.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim E65FD38D-075D-4F1A-9552-7805FF1F4BE7` (full suite, iPhone 17, iOS 26.5): 4049 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `ServeEveryProfileTests.testADuplicateBotIsRemovedFromTheChosenProfileThenEveryProfileIsServed`, fails the same way on untouched `master` in a full local run and passes alone (`--only HermesMobileTests/ServeEveryProfileTests --repeat 10`).
- New test: `APIEndpointContractTests.testQueryValuesEscapePlus`. `CacheFallbackPolicyTests` now covers 522 and 530 for webui.
- `scripts/benchmark-streaming-scans`: failed to compile on `master`, runs on this branch.

title: perf(sessions): read ordinary and scheduled session pages at the same time
body:
## Linked issue

None. Maintainer-approved performance work, split out of `fix/measured-performance`.

## What changed

Every refresh of a Hermes session list read the ordinary session pages and then the scheduled session pages, one request after another, so the list waited for both round trips back to back. Over a tunnel that wait is most of what a refresh costs.

The two reads are independent, so they now run at the same time: two requests at once, each chain still in page order, however many Profiles are listed.

Two things keep the old behavior intact:

- A Load more that finishes while a refresh is still waiting on the other chain is kept. The refresh extends to that depth before it applies, so it never takes those rows away.
- A refresh that was replaced or cancelled starts no further request.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17 udid>` with `--only` for `HermesSessionListTests`, `HermesSessionSearchTests`, `HermesProjectsTests`, `HermesOfflineCacheTests`, `HermesWaitingSendTests`, `HermesSessionActionsTests`, `HermesBranchDuplicateTests`, `HermesHomeSplitRoutingTests`, `SessionNavigationStateTests`, `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests`: 197 passed.
- Two new tests: both chains start together and stop with their owner, and a scheduled Load more during a refresh keeps its rows.
- `testAFailedListReadDuringScheduledLoadMoreLeavesItUsable` now counts only what the final Load more reads. Whether the cancelled refresh starts its own scheduled read is a race, and the old whole-history assertion flaked under load (10/10 alone, failed in the class run).
- Real app, signed Debug build on the simulator against a live Hermes host: the home list loaded its sessions and its scheduled count, and refreshed correctly after a session was deleted.
- Timed against a live Hermes host through a Cloudflare tunnel, with the app's own two first-page requests for one Profile on a warm `URLSession`, 25 alternating trials:

  | | median | p90 |
  |---|---|---|
  | one after the other (before) | 227.8 ms | 291.1 ms |
  | at the same time (this PR) | 139.9 ms | 165.4 ms |

  That is 88 ms (39%) less waiting per refresh. A list of every Profile reads one pair of pages per Profile, so the saving grows with the number of Profiles.

## Checklist

title: perf(chat): stop redoing math scans, reasoning chunking, and image decoding on every update
body:
## Linked issue

None. Maintainer-approved performance work, split out of `fix/measured-performance`.

## What changed

Four places did the same work over and over while a reply streams or a preview opens. Each is a small, independent fix.

- **Math.** A math opener with no closer made the scan search to the end of the text again for every later opener, so a reply with many unclosed `\[` or `\(` cost quadratic time on every streaming update. A failed search is now remembered for the rest of that pass (per line for `\(`, since inline math cannot cross a line). Delimiter matching also stopped allocating an array per character.
- **Live reasoning.** The live thought's chunked text was rebuilt from scratch whenever its parent re-rendered, then thrown away. It now lives with the mounted text view, so an update only appends.
- **Image previews.** The file preview and the chat attachment preview decoded and downsampled images on the main thread. They now do it off the main thread, and a load that was cancelled or replaced publishes neither a preview nor an error.
- **Cached Hermes sessions.** Reading one Profile's cached sessions fetched every cached row for the server and filtered in memory. The store now filters by the Profile's key prefix.

## How it was tested

`scripts/benchmark-math-formatting`, this branch against `master` at `9fb1917a` (median ms, identical output on every workload):

| Workload | master | this branch | |
|---|---|---|---|
| incremental math 30KB | 832.0 | 381.9 | 2.2x |
| inline math transcript | 1.05 | 0.48 | 2.2x |
| protected code and currency | 0.79 | 0.23 | 3.5x |
| unclosed display openers 512 | 175.7 | 0.97 | 181x |
| unclosed inline openers 512 | 178.1 | 1.02 | 175x |
| plain transcript | 0.35 | 0.24 | 1.4x |
| nested formula | 0.37 | 0.37 | 1.0x |

The 512-opener rows are a worst case added to the benchmark, not a typical reply. The other three changes have no benchmark; they are covered by tests only.

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17 udid>` with `--only` for `APIClientWorkspaceFileTests`, `ChatAttachmentPreviewViewModelTests`, `CacheStoreTests`, `HermesOfflineCacheTests`, `HermesWaitingSendTests`, `HermesChatAttachmentTests`, `HermesWorkspaceFileClientTests`, `MarkdownMathLayoutCacheTests`, `MarkdownMathRendererTests`, `StreamingMarkdownBlockSplitterTests`, `StreamingReasoningTextStateTests`, `ReasoningRenderingTests`, `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests`: 226 passed.
- New tests: unclosed display and inline openers stay literal until the stream closes them, and do not hide math on the next line or under another delimiter; live reasoning shows appends and replacements; a cancelled image load publishes nothing; a Profile whose name starts with another Profile's name keeps its own cached rows.
- Real app, signed Debug build on the simulator against a live Hermes host: a reply with inline `$x^2$`, `\(a+b\)`, display `$$E = mc^2$$`, and unclosed `\[` and `\(` rendered the math and left the unclosed openers as text.
- Not run in the real app: live reasoning and the two image previews.
