title: feat(settings): connect apps to a server's Hermes from the phone
body:
**What the user gets:** a Connected Apps page in Settings to connect apps such as Notion, Gmail or Stripe to their Hermes, see which are connected, and disconnect them, without leaving the phone.
**Why it matters:** the official Hermes iOS app has a Connections screen, and today a Hermex user can only connect an app when the agent asks mid-chat, or from the desktop.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner's hands on a phone twice: the browser spike before any view is built, and the final Connect and Disconnect test.

## Scope

Hermes servers only; nothing on webui. One issue, one PR. Settings is the only entry point: no deep link, App Intent, keyboard shortcut or link from the in-chat connection card.

v1 is the catalog with search and category chips, per-app state, Connect, Reconnect and Disconnect.

### Naming and placement

- The page is called **Connected Apps**. Add it to `CONTEXT.md` with "Connections" and "Connectors" under _Avoid_: "Hermes connection" already means the sign-in, and "Connection Options" is an Add Server page.
- A third row at Settings → Server, under API Keys and Plugins. It always shows on a Hermes server.
- The same Profile picker as API Keys, starting on the server's default Profile. Connected apps belong to a Profile's Nous identity, so every read and action applies to the selected Profile.

### List

- A "Connected" section on top holds connected and waiting apps. The rest is grouped by category below.
- Category chips filter the lower part only. Search matches app name and description on the phone, across both sections, and combines with the chips.
- Each row shows exactly one state:

| State | Row shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| Not connected | Connect |
| Sign-in started, not finished | "Waiting…" with Continue and Cancel |
| Connected | A checkmark; tap opens the detail |
| Failed, expired or revoked | Reconnect |
| Turned off by the account's policy | Greyed out with "Turned off in Nous Portal" |

- Cancel on a waiting row removes the pending account.
- A one-line note says connected apps run through Nous Portal. On a host with no Nous account, the first Connect creates a free guest Nous identity; that is upstream's intended behavior and the host owner can turn it off with `nous.guest: false`. Hermex builds no Nous sign-in.
- Nothing is cached. The page fetches on open and on pull-to-refresh, so an app can never show under another server or Profile.

### Connect

- Connect and Reconnect call `connectors.connect` for the selected Profile and open the returned `connect_url` in a non-ephemeral `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, so the user's existing Safari sign-ins carry over.
- The host hardcodes the browser's return to the desktop scheme (`hermes://connections/done`), and a client cannot supply its own. `ASWebAuthenticationSession` can capture a scheme the app has not registered; the official iOS app claims `hermes://`, so a plain Safari sheet could bounce the user into it. **This is the spike**, see Order of work.
- When the browser closes, by redirect or by the user, call `connectors.operation.wake` and re-read the list once. After that, rely on the host's `connection.update` event. No polling timer.
- If the spike passes, the existing in-chat connection card switches to the same browser in this PR. If it fails, both keep the Safari sheet and the page refreshes on dismissal.

### Detail and Disconnect

- Tapping a connected app pushes a small detail page listing each account with its label and its own Disconnect. v1 cannot add a second account, but a host may already hold two created on the desktop.
- Retired accounts (left behind by a reconnect) are hidden.
- The Disconnect confirmation says only what the contract proves: "Hermes on this server will lose access to <App> for <Profile>". No claim about revoking access at the app itself.

### Logos

- Show the catalog's logos. Load lazily per visible row, with a monogram tile as the placeholder and the failure state, so row height never changes.
- Use the system URL cache. Send no cookies or custom headers to the logo host.
- No privacy wording in the app or README.

### Dead ends

The page explains each of these with a Refresh button:

- The host is too old: the call answers `-32601`.
- Connected apps are turned off or not available for this account: `CONNECTORS_UNAVAILABLE`.
- Nous sign-in is required: `NEEDS_NOUS_AUTH`.

### Out of scope

Renaming accounts, a second account for the same app, per-tool policy (`connectors.policy.*`), per-app tool lists (`connectors.tools`), local MCP server setup (`mcp.*`), and the official app's Device Access (health, calendar, contacts, location).

## Contract

Verified at the pin `2bd378ed` (0.23.0) and read live on a 0.23.1 host. Validate just in time during the build.

| Need | RPC | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Catalog: slug, name, description, category, `logo_url` | `connectors.catalog` | `tui_gateway/methods_connectors_account.py`; read live: 54 apps in 8 categories |
| Per-app state: `enabled`, `connected`, `connection_status` | `connectors.list` with `owner: {type: "account"}` | `tui_gateway/methods_connectors.py`; read live: `available: true` |
| Accounts: `connection_id`, `status`, `label`, `active`, `disabled` | `connectors.accounts` | read live: one pending account |
| Connect and Reconnect | `connectors.connect` with `owner`, `connectors`, `reconnect`, optional `connection_id`; the result's `targets[].connect_url` | OpenRPC `ConnectorsConnectParams` / `ConnectorsConnectResult`; **not run live** |
| Browser came back | `connectors.operation.wake` with `op_id`, `owner` | OpenRPC `ConnectionOperationParams` |
| Disconnect, and Cancel on a waiting row | `connectors.accounts.remove` with `connection_id` | `tui_gateway/methods_connectors_account.py`; **not run live** |
| Live changes | `connection.update` event, broadcast for account operations without `connect_url` | `methods_connectors._connection_update` |

- Every call takes the selected `profile`.
- Errors carry `error.data.reason`; the full set is `ConnectorErrorReason` in the OpenRPC contract.
- Hermex already parses the operation shape for the in-chat card (`BotPendingRequest.swift`, #770, #1141). Reuse it; decode tolerantly.
- The desktop's Connectors page is the reference client: `apps/desktop/src/app/capabilities/connectors/data/`.

## Order of work

1. **Pin advance** to the host's 0.23.1 lands first as its own `chore/` PR, so the connector contract is diffed against the release in use.
2. **Browser spike** on the owner's phone, with the official Hermes app installed: does `ASWebAuthenticationSession` capture the `hermes://connections/done` return and close itself? Record the answer on this issue. It decides the browser for the page and for the chat card.
3. **Mocks**: static mocks of the list, a waiting row, the detail page and the three dead ends. Stop for the owner's pick before any view code.
4. **Build.**
5. **Live test** (approved): one Notion Connect and Disconnect on the owner's host, plus cancelling the stale pending Notion account there.

## Tests

Three behaviors, no more:

- A row's state derived from the catalog, list and accounts answers.
- The three dead ends mapped from their error replies.
- Connect sends the selected Profile, the app and the reconnect flag.

Layout and copy are judged in the mocks and on the phone.

## Docs

- `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md`: the Connectors row becomes covered.
- `CONTEXT.md`: the Connected Apps entry.
- `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`: the `ASWebAuthenticationSession` return, as the spike found it.

title: feat(settings): connect apps like Notion and Slack to Hermes from the phone
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1629

## What changed

The official Hermes app lets you connect apps like Notion, Slack or Stripe to your agent from the phone. In Hermex you could only do that when the agent asked mid-chat, or from the desktop.

Settings → Server now has a **Connected Apps** page for Hermes servers. It lists the apps a Profile's Nous account can reach, with the connected ones on top and the rest by category, and you can Connect, Reconnect and Disconnect from there. Sign-in happens on Nous Portal in a browser sheet that closes itself when you finish.

| The list, on a phone | The list, light | An app's accounts |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| ![The Connected Apps list in a dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cf816c2-3261-4b03-ac59-690d460009eb) | ![The Connected Apps list in light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fee869e2-4b0c-4be3-adc9-56a831abc4f9) | ![Notion's accounts page with Disconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31b5c85b-51de-475a-b513-84892512f92f) |

Things worth knowing when reviewing:

- **It uses the gateway's `connectors.*` methods** with `owner: {type: "account"}`, the same ones the desktop's Connectors page calls. The shapes were read from the pinned OpenRPC contract and run against a live 0.23.1 host. Nothing is cached, and every call names the Profile.
- **The browser is an `ASWebAuthenticationSession`.** The host always asks the portal to return to `hermes://connections/done`, the desktop's scheme, which the official Hermes app has registered and Hermex has not. On a phone with both apps, a Safari sheet ended with iOS asking to open the official app. The auth session catches that scheme without registering it and closes itself.
- **Connect heals a dead link.** The host keeps a cancelled sign-in open for about ten minutes and hands its link back, which the portal answers with 404. When the sign-in it gets names an account the host no longer lists, the app settles it and asks again.
- **Logos are bundled.** The catalog's logo URLs are SVG only, which UIKit can't decode, so the 54 logos ship in the asset catalog by slug and an app added later shows its initial. That is most of this diff's line count. The phone never contacts the logo host.
- **Three dead ends are explained** from the host's refusal code: a host too old for the feature, connected apps turned off or not in the account, and no Nous sign-in.

Left out on purpose: naming accounts, a second account for the same app, per-tool policy, and the in-chat connection card, whose sign-in gets no `hermes://` return to catch.

The 19 new strings are translated into all 17 shipped languages and marked `needs_review`.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17> --only HermesMobileTests/ConnectedAppsModelTests`: 6 passed, 0 failed. They cover the state each row lands in, the three dead ends, what Connect and Reconnect send, the dead-link heal, the one-action-at-a-time lock, and a refused Connect.

- `python3 ci/check_string_catalog.py --derived-data .build/DerivedData`: all 2959 extracted keys covered.

- On the owner's iPhone against a live 0.23.1 host: Connect, closing the browser and Continue, Cancel then Connect again, a finished Notion sign-in with the browser closing itself, Disconnect, and the Profile picker.
- On the simulator against the same host: the page loads with Notion connected and its accounts page opens (the light screenshots above).

Not tested against a real host: Reconnect on a broken account and the three dead-end pages, which are covered only by the scripted tests. VoiceOver and Dynamic Type were not checked.

title: feat(bots): show a card in chat when the bot is using its screen
body:
**What the user gets:** when a bot starts using its computer mid-turn, a small card appears in the chat with Open and Take Over, so they don't have to know to look for the Screen button.
**Why it matters:** the Screen is only reachable from the toolbar and the Bots menus today, so a bot stuck at a login or CAPTCHA is easy to miss. The idea comes from @charleypeng's #1558.
**Cost:** Small, and it needs the owner's hands on a phone.

## Scope

- In a Bot Chat, show a compact card in the transcript while a live turn runs a `computer_use` tool, and after that turn ends.
- Open shows the existing `ScreenView`. Take Over opens it and starts the usual takeover confirmation. Nothing about control, holds or hand-back changes (`docs/agents/screen.md`).
- The card follows the same gate as every other Screen entry: the per-server "Bot Screen (beta)" switch, Hermes servers only, and hidden when `display.status` hides the feature.
- Only live frames raise the card. Replayed history and a rebuild after a gap do not.
- The card clears when the next turn begins.

## Notes for the implementer

- Verify the tool name the host actually sends on `tool.start` against the live host or the pinned contract before matching on it. #1558 also matched every `browser_*` tool; don't, because a browser tool doesn't mean the screen is in use.
- This is new chat UI, so mock it first and wait for a pick.
- #1558's `BotDesktopChatCard` and its `desktopUse` state in `HermesChatTurnCoordinator` are a useful reference for the lifecycle, not code to port: it drives a different viewer.

## Left out, to decide after trying the card on a phone

- A live thumbnail in the card through `display.thumbnail`. It exists in the pinned gateway contract, but only covers stock Linux screens, not `hermex-screen` hosts.
- Opening the Screen automatically when the bot uses it.
- Hiding the picture while the phone is being recorded or mirrored during a takeover (`isSceneCaptured`). That is its own issue if we want it.

title: feat(sessions): open the bot's Screen from a session chat
body:
**What the user gets:** when the agent uses its computer in a regular Hermes session, the same Open and Take Over card appears in that chat, and ⌘⇧S opens the Screen for the session on screen.
**Why it matters:** every Screen entry is on the Bots side today (#1567, #1632). A session whose turn is stuck at a login or CAPTCHA gives no way in without leaving the chat and finding that Profile's bot.
**Cost:** Small, and it needs the owner's hands on a phone.

**Depends on #1632.** Start only after it merges: this reuses its `BotScreenCard`, `BotScreenUse`, `BotScreenOpener`, the `openBotScreen` environment value and `ScreenView`'s `takesOverWhenLive`.

## Scope

- **The card.** A session chat shows the #1632 card with the same lifecycle: raised by a live `computer_use` `tool.start`, kept after that turn, cleared when the next turn starts, never raised by replayed or rebuilt history.
- **⌘⇧S.** The existing Open Screen command opens the Screen of the session chat on screen. It stays disabled when no session chat is open or the gate is off.
- **No toolbar button.** A session's toolbar already carries goal, files, Git and delegated work. See Left out.
- **Which screen.** The session's own Profile, `HermesSessionChat.target.profile`, on `HermesSessionChat.connection` and `HermesSessionChat.server`. Never the Bots home's selected bot.
- **Where it is reachable.** Every place that builds a session `ChatView(hermesSession:)`: both sites in `HermesSessionListView`, `ArchivedSessionsView`, and the pushed branch in `ChatView`. An archived Bot Chat row opened from these lists gets the card too.
- **Same gate.** The per-server "Bot Screen (beta)" switch (`BotScreenSettings.key(for:)`), Hermes servers only, hidden once the host answers -32601 on `display.*` (`ScreenView`'s `onUnavailable`). Turning the switch off closes an open Screen, as `BotsInboxView` does.
- **A Profile the host doesn't serve.** No turn can run there, so the card never appears. ⌘⇧S is not offered while the chat shows its unserved state (`ChatViewModel.errorUnserved`).
- Control, holds, hand-back and the "still held" row on the Bots home (`heldScreenRow`) do not change.

## Notes for the implementer

- This is new UI on the Sessions side, so mock the card in a session transcript first and wait for a pick, even though the card itself comes from #1632.
- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.screenUse` is set only when `policy == .botChat`, and `ChatView.botScreenCard` reads it through `viewModel.hermesBotChat`. Both need to cover `HermesChatPolicy.session`.
- The opener and the `fullScreenCover` live in `BotsInboxView` today (`canOpenScreen`, `openScreen`, `BotScreenTarget`), all private. Recommended: one small modifier beside `BotScreenOpenerModifier` that owns the gate, the target and the cover presenting `ScreenView`, and installs `openBotScreen`. Apply it where each session chat is built. Do not copy the Bots home's logic into four places, and do not move the Bots home onto it in this issue.
- Check that the opener reaches a branch pushed from inside `ChatView`: a value set on the pushing view may not reach a `navigationDestination`.
- The Sessions side cannot see `BotsInboxView`'s private `hostLacksScreen`, so it keeps its own flag from `onUnavailable`. The card may show once on a host without `display.*` before it hides. That is acceptable.
- Multi-server: read the switch with the chat's own `server`, and build `ScreenView` from the chat's `server` and `connection`. The logged-in tree is rebuilt on a server switch, and `ScreenHolds.handBackAll` already hands back the departing server's holds (`docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`). Check with two Hermes servers, one with the switch on and one off.
- ⌘⇧S goes through `HermexSceneActions.openScreen`, which `HermesSessionListView` already publishes its scene actions beside.
- Confirm against the live host that a session's `tool.start` names `computer_use` the same way a Bot Chat's does.
- Update the Entries section of `docs/agents/screen.md`.

## Left out

- A Screen button in the session toolbar. Decide after using the card and the shortcut on a phone.
- A session row menu entry, and a `screen=1` flag on session deep links.
- webui servers. The Screen is Hermes only.
- Everything #1632 left out: a thumbnail in the card, opening automatically, hiding the picture during screen capture.

title: fix(screen): stop retrying forever when the host's desktop can't capture
body:
**What the user gets:** when a Mac or Windows host can't capture its desktop, the Screen says so, with the doctor line and Check Again, instead of showing "Reconnecting" forever.
**Why it matters:** on 2026-11-10 the maintainer's Screen sat on "Reconnecting" with no explanation. The host's driver was failing every capture (uzairansaruzi/hermex-screen#1).
**Cost:** Small. Unit-testable, no phone needed.

## What happens

On the host's desktop (`ScreenSource.hostDesktop`), the plugin closes a stream with `4001` when its capture fails. `ScreenStreamOutcome` maps that to `.retry` (`ScreenSession.swift`, the `4001` case), on the assumption that the next `/status` read will say what's wrong. Here it never did:

- The plugin's `/status` reported `driver.problem: null` and `permissions: null`.
- `ScreenHostFacts` reads `permissions: null` as nothing missing (`json["permissions"]["accessibility"].flag == false` is false), so the pass streams again.
- The loop runs with backoff up to 30 s, showing "Reconnecting" over a blank picture, indefinitely.

## Fix

On the host's desktop, a `4001` close before any frame, after a status read that found nothing wrong, settles to `.driverProblem` on the second pass in a row. That state already shows `hermes computer-use doctor` and Check Again. A frame arriving resets the count, so a stream that drops after it was live still retries as now.

The detail string should say the driver couldn't capture the screen, for example "This computer's driver couldn't capture the screen." It's a new String Catalog entry, so it needs all shipped languages (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).

The bot's desktop (stock) keeps its `4001` meaning, which is that the screen stopped.

## Out of scope

The plugin side (restart a child that keeps failing, and report a failed permission check as a driver problem) is uzairansaruzi/hermex-screen#1. This issue only stops the app from looping when the plugin gives no reason.

## Acceptance

- A `ScreenSessionTests` case: a host-desktop source whose status is clean and whose stream closes `4001` before a frame, twice, ends in `.driverProblem`. Check Again (`open()`) tries again from the start.
- A host-desktop stream that was live, then closes `4001`, still goes to `.reconnecting`.

---
Filed by Claude Code (Opus 5.5).

title: Accepting dictation with the checkmark self-aborts with 'draft changed' though the user never edited
body:
## What happens

Dictating with the composer's own mic button (server-first dictation, host STT) and then accepting the result with the checkmark — without ever touching the keyboard, the field, or the caret — ends the session with the stale-edit explanation from the #1418 guard:

> Dictation was ended because the draft changed

The dictated text is already in the field and nothing is lost, but the guard rejects the session's own finalization and shows a message that implies user editing which never happened. Reproduced on every dictation on my device.

## Steps

1. Open a Hermes chat in Hermex (current App Store build, 2.1-era, Nov 2026; iPhone, exact iOS version on request).
2. Tap the composer's own mic button (not the iOS keyboard mic). Server STT is configured on the host (`stt.language: de`).
3. Dictate one sentence. Do not type, tap in the field, or move the caret.
4. Accept the dictation with the checkmark.

**Expected:** final transcript is applied and the voice session ends cleanly.
**Actual:** the voice status shows "Dictation was ended because the draft changed" as if a user edit had occurred.

## Suspected cause (from reading, not debugging)

The #1418 landed guard applies a voice write only while "owner identity, generation, revision, text and not-marked-text all still hold". Accepting likely causes the composer to commit/finalize the pending (marked) text and/or iOS applies its after-the-fact punctuation and capitalization rewrite. If that system-side commit advances `revision`/`publishGeneration`, the session's own final write sees a changed draft and self-rejects — a false positive of the protection against overwriting user edits.

## Env notes

- Hermex host: Hermes 0.22.x, server-first dictation working (German transcription arrives correctly).
- Happy to provide iOS/Hermex build numbers or a screen recording.

- **Where it goes.** Inside the existing pill (`ChatToolbarActionCluster`), last, after Git, so goal, Files and Git don't move for people who turn the beta on. In the vertical bar (`chatActionRailItems`, iOS 27.1), it is one more item in the same place. No "⋯" overflow menu.

Check that case on the folded iPhone Duo's horizontal header. If the title disappears entirely, file a separate issue for overflow across all header actions; it doesn't belong here.

title: Add a configurable widget to open a specific bot’s chat
body:
## Use case

I’d like to access frequently used bots directly from my iPhone’s Home Screen, without opening Hermex and finding the bot in the inbox each time.

## Proposed behavior

Add a widget that lets me choose a bot when configuring it. The widget shows the bot’s name and, where practical, its avatar. Tapping it opens that bot’s existing chat.

Similar to the ChatGPT Dot widget, each widget would act as a direct shortcut to a chosen bot: show its name/avatar, and tap to open its existing chat in Hermex.

A small widget with one bot would be enough for a first version. Multiple widget instances could each point to a different bot, including bots on different configured servers.

## Acceptance outcomes

- Each widget can be configured for a specific bot.
- Tapping opens the selected bot’s existing chat without starting a new session.
- The destination stays tied to the correct server, even when another server is active.
- Cold launches and signed-out states follow the existing navigation and sign-in flow.
- Removed bots or connections are handled gracefully, without opening another bot.
- The widget stores no credentials and performs no authenticated server calls.

## Related work and implementation context

Related to #6, which covers widgets for starting new sessions with a configured profile. This request focuses on returning to an existing bot chat.

The existing bot deep links and widget extension appear to provide much of the foundation. No new server capability is expected.

Would you prefer this as a separate feature or an extension of #6?

A photo sent from Hermex into a Hermes session shows correctly on the phone, but in Hermes Desktop the same message shows two lines of raw text instead of the picture:

```
[The user attached an image: dashboard_<date>_<id>_camera_<n>.png]
[Examine it with the vision_analyze tool using image_url: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\cache\images\dashboard_<date>_<id>_camera_<n>.png]
```

Expected: the photo appears in the desktop transcript as a picture. The host path should not be shown there either.

The agent does receive the photo and can describe it, so this is about how the message looks in other clients, not about delivery.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Hermex to a Hermes server that is also open in Hermes Desktop.
2. In Hermex, open a Hermes session, take a photo with the camera, add a caption and send it.
3. Hermex shows the photo in the user bubble.
4. Open the same session in Hermes Desktop. The user message shows the caption followed by the two bracketed lines above. No picture.

Seen on every photo sent this way (ten in one session on 2026-11-11).

### Diagnosis

Seen, in Hermex source at tag `v2.1.0` (`458596b3`):

- `HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotAttachmentUpload.swift:110-113`: `imageReference(path:)` builds exactly those two lines and they are sent as part of the prompt text.
- `docs/agents/bots.md:625-631`: images go through `POST /api/chat/image-upload`, and the prompt carries the returned path with the vision-tool instruction. "This deliberately avoids `image.attach_bytes` and its shared next-prompt queue. It does not request native inline vision from the conversation model."
- `HermesMobile/Models/MessageAttachment.swift` turns the pair back into an attachment chip, which is why the phone looks right.

Seen, on the server:

- The stored user message for each phone photo is plain text: the caption, then the two lines. There is no image part.
- A picture attached from Hermes Desktop is stored differently (an `[Image attached at: …]` note plus an image part).
- The Hermes Desktop bundle has no match for the string `The user attached an image`, so it has nothing that would turn the pair into a picture.

Inferred: this is the design decided in #1012 (decision 1), not a regression. That issue says "Native inline vision can be a later issue". This is a request for that follow-up, from the point of view of someone who uses the phone and the desktop on the same sessions: anything that reads the transcript other than Hermex sees the instruction lines and the host path.

Possible directions, for the maintainer to judge: send the image as a real attachment when the server offers a per-prompt way to do it that does not share the next-prompt queue, or raise upstream that Hermes Desktop should draw its own text-mode image reference as a picture.

### Environment

- Hermex 2.1 from the App Store, installed 2026-11-10. Build number, iOS version and iPhone model: not captured.
- Server: Hermes Agent 0.23.1, running inside Hermes Desktop (Microsoft Store build) on Windows 11.
- The phone reaches the server over Tailscale (HTTPS, tailnet only).

### Evidence

No errors in the logs; nothing fails. The evidence is the stored message text shown above (path redacted). A screenshot of the desktop view can be added on request.

### Related issues

- #1012: the decision to use image-upload plus the instruction line.
- #1017: reusing the transcript rule in Bot Chat.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#144581 (open): a different cause that produces the same look in the desktop transcript.

Triaged by Hermes Agent 0.23.1 using claude-fable-5-2

title: feat(chat): show agent HTML reports right in Hermes chats
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1623

## What changed

When an agent sent an HTML report in a Hermes chat, you got a download card and had to open the file somewhere else. Now the report renders right in the chat, in your theme, like the rest of the reply.

- **Inline:** a settled reply's `.html`/`.htm` file shows a small filename strip (download, expand) and then the page itself, flush with the transcript. The page is measured once and locked, up to about three screens; a taller page fades out and expand shows the rest. While the reply streams, and for files over 5 MB, it stays the usual file card.
- **Sheet:** expand opens the existing Hermes document sheet, which now shows the page in a scrolling web view with Save to Files and Share as before.
- **Isolation:** `WKWebView` (the app's first, no new dependency). JavaScript and remote loads are on, but the page loads from a string with an opaque origin into a non-persistent store, so no Hermes cookie, credential or custom header is reachable. The app's scripts run in their own content world and there are no message handlers. Camera, microphone, motion, downloads and new windows are denied, the top frame can't navigate, tapped links go through the transcript's link routing, and in-page anchors scroll (inline, they open the sheet).
- **Theme:** the active theme, accent, font and text size go in as zero-specificity `:where()` defaults plus CSS variables (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--card`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--primary`, `--font-sans`, `--font-mono`), updated live. The page's own styles always win. The web process can't see the bundled DM Sans and Lora, so they fall back to the system sans and Georgia.
- **Performance:** nothing downloads until a report is on screen, and the download waits for the chat's attach. A report is live only while its reply is on screen; off screen it becomes a still image (2x, 48 MB shared limit) and its web view is released.
- **Docs:** `AGENTS.md` (remote loads from agent content), `docs/agents/performance.md` (the live-only-on-screen rule), `docs/agents/theming.md` § HTML reports (variables and a prompt users can give their agent), README.

webui is unchanged: it publishes no report loader, so its replies keep the download card.

## How it was tested

Proved with focused XCTest, a simulator verify run, and the maintainer's iPhone against the live Hermes host.

- `scripts/test-sim E65FD38D-075D-4F1A-9552-7805FF1F4BE7 --only HermesMobileTests/HTMLReportTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotArtifactTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMediaVisibilityTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptMediaParserTests`: pass. `HTMLReportTests` (8) covers: renders on Hermes but not webui or while streaming, the 5 MB limit keeps a card, a load before the chat attaches waits instead of failing, retry after a render failure, a dead web process reloads once then fails, off-screen images past the limit drop the oldest, top-frame navigation and link/anchor routing, and the theme-to-variable mapping.
- `ChatTranscriptEnvironmentStabilityTests.testLinkReadersSkipOwnerPassesWhileTheKeyboardIsUp` fails on this simulator, and also on clean `master` (keyboard never shows), so it is not this change.
- Probes in the simulator: an injected viewport lays a page without one out at device width; anchors arrive as `about:blank%23id` and the fix scrolls to them; web-process memory showed no trend between one- and three-screen pages.
- Simulator verify run (signed Debug, live Hermes host, disposable session on the `hermex-fixtures` test Profile): both reports render on open with no Retry, the short page keeps its own styles, expand opens the sheet with Save and Share. Screenshots below.
- Maintainer's iPhone: rendering, theme, links, anchors, the attach wait and the three-screen cap.
- Full suite runs in PR CI.

title: fix(chat): show Hermex photos as pictures in Hermes Desktop
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1644

## What changed

When you sent a photo from Hermex, Hermes Desktop and other clients didn't show a picture. They showed two bracketed instruction lines and a host path. That's because Hermex wrote the photo into the prompt text as Hermes's text-mode `vision_analyze` pair.

Now, on a canonical gateway (the Webapp listener), the photo goes in `prompt.submit` as `attachments: [{path, mime}]`, and the text holds only what the user typed. The host stores the photo with its own image notes. Desktop draws those notes as a picture, and Hermex reads them as a chip:
- in native mode, `[Image attached at: …]` lines plus `[screenshot]` lines, with the default caption hidden;
- in text mode, the leading `[The user sent an image…` notes.

The rule follows upstream's `split_image_notes`. Session titles and previews drop the notes too. The host's `pending` rows list text only, so a queued photo keeps its chip in memory, by admission, until its turn starts. Dashboard listeners send exactly what they did before (decision 1).

Found while checking the live contract (hermes-agent `3b421578`):
- A canonical `session.resume` snapshot has `inflight: null`, even mid-turn. So `rebuild` and `holdsPrompt` needed no change.
- With an `@file:` ref, the host saves its context footer **before** the native image hints. So the rule lifts the image hints before it cuts the footer.

Departures from the plan:
- `BotAttachmentUpload.typedText` is unchanged, because nothing in the app calls it. In a Hermes chat, ↑ recall reads the displayed rows, which the transcript rule already cleans. A test covers that path.
- Two photo-only prompts can still collide the way two prompts with the same caption already do. A queued one that starts while another photo-only Send waits for its reply can hide its row until the next history read. I kept this as a follow-up, because comparing image paths would show a normal Send twice.
- A photo-only queued prompt after a relaunch shows an empty "Queued" bubble. Stop still discards it.

## How it was tested

Proved with focused XCTest, a simulator run against `scripts/local-hermes --gateway`, and the maintainer's phone with Hermes Desktop on a real Webapp.

- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17>`:
  - `HermesChatAttachmentTests`, `BotAttachmentSendingTests`, `ComposerRecallTests`, `HermesSessionListTests`, `HermesChatTurnTests` and `HermesRequestTests`: 186 passed.
  - `HermesConnectionTests`, `HermesGatewayTests`, `HermesChatSideTaskTests`, `HermesHistoryRewindTests`, `HermesChatSettingsTests` and `BotClientTests`: 176 passed.
  - `HermesChatAttachmentTests` again after test cleanup: 39 passed.
- Simulator, against `scripts/local-hermes --gateway` in native image mode: I sent a photo with "What is this?". The host stored `What is this?\n\n[Image attached at: …/native-inputs/…/dashboard_…_red-square.jpg]\n[screenshot]`, with no `vision_analyze` lines. The reopened chat shows the chip with a downloaded thumbnail and no path (below). The session row title reads "What is this?", even though the host's raw preview is `What is this?  [Image attached at: /…`.
- Maintainer's phone on a Webapp, with Hermes Desktop on the same session: the photo shows as a chip in Hermex and as a picture in Desktop.
- I re-checked the contract on the live local gateway: the upload reply, `attachments` refusals (an extra key, an unlisted mime and a path outside the folder all answer 4001), and the stored forms.

title: feat(bots): open a bot's chat from a Home Screen widget

## Linked issue

Fixes #1643

## What changed

Getting to a bot meant opening Hermex and finding it in the inbox. Now a Home Screen widget opens a bot's existing chat in one tap: a small widget holds one bot, a medium a row of 4, and a large two rows of 4, each bot opening its own chat on its own server.

title: Chat: fenced svg and mermaid blocks render as source text instead of graphics
body:
### What happened

A reply that contains a fenced diagram block renders as a picture in the Hermes
webapp, but in Hermex the same reply shows the raw markup as a
syntax-highlighted code block. This affects both fence languages the webapp
draws:

- ```` ```svg ```` — the webapp renders the SVG inline as a vector image.
- ```` ```mermaid ```` — the webapp renders it as a diagram.

Expected: a fence the webapp draws should either draw in Hermex too, or offer a
tap-to-view affordance. Showing markup with no way to see the graphic is the
least useful outcome, and it is the one Hermex lands on today.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Hermex to a Hermes host.
2. Ask the agent for a reply containing an `svg` fenced block whose body is a
   valid SVG document (a single `<svg>...</svg>` is enough), and a second reply
   containing a `mermaid` fenced block (a two-node flowchart is enough).
3. Open both replies in Hermex, then open the same session in the webapp.

### Diagnosis

Seen, reading tag `v2.1.0` (also verified unchanged on `master`):

- `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift:1256` routes every fenced
  code block through a single entry point:
  `.codeBlock { configuration in MathFenceOrCodeBlock(...) }`.
- `MathFenceOrCodeBlock` (`MarkdownRenderer.swift:225-241`) has exactly two
  branches: a math language that parses as math goes to `DisplayMathView`,
  everything else goes to `ChatCodeBlock`, the syntax-highlighted source block.
- `MathFenceLanguage.languages` (`Features/Chat/DisplayMathView.swift:102`) is
  `["math", "latex", "tex"]` — `svg` and `mermaid` are not among them.
- `grep -ic svg` and `grep -ic mermaid` against
  `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/MarkdownRenderer.swift` both return 0. A
  case-insensitive search of the whole app target for `mermaid`, `SVGKit`,
  `SVGView`, `DiagramView`, `graphviz` and `plantuml` returns no matches.

Inferred: because the fence info string is only inspected for the three math
languages, an `svg` or `mermaid` fence is structurally indistinguishable from a
`python` or `json` fence and can never reach an image renderer.

For contrast, the webapp does have both paths: `apps/desktop`'s rich-fence
registry maps `svg` to a dedicated embed renderer and `mermaid` to a diagram
renderer, which is why the browser shows a graphic for identical text sent by
the same server.

### Environment

- Hermex: 2.1, App Store channel
- iOS: 27.3 (device not recorded)
- Server: Hermes Agent v0.23.1, git install, gateway running
- Phone reaches server over: LAN

### Evidence

No server logs apply — this is a rendering-path gap in the app, not a runtime
failure, and nothing is logged when a fence falls through to `ChatCodeBlock`.
The comparison is visual and deterministic: identical reply text, webapp draws
the graphic, Hermex shows markup.

### Related

- No existing issue covers fenced `svg` or `mermaid` rendering. Searched open and
  closed issues for `svg`, `mermaid`, `fence`, `diagram` and `codeBlock`.
- The closest neighbouring request is the older MEDIA: image-rendering issue
  (#145), which is about media links rather than fence languages.

Triaged by Hermes Agent 0.23.1 using deepseek-v4.1-flash

title: feat(chat): use the native Photos picker without library permission
body:
**What the user gets:** Attach photos in chat through Apple's native Photos picker without granting Hermex full or limited photo-library read access.
**Why it matters:** Steven requested the permission-free selection experience seen in apps such as ChatGPT; Hermex's custom grid currently requests library access before the user can choose an image.
**Cost:** Medium; the owner needs a physical iPhone to validate first-use privacy UI, iCloud-only images, and keyboard/focus behavior.

## Use case

A user wants to attach a few photos to a chat without giving Hermex ongoing access to their photo library. Today, choosing **Photos** requests `.readWrite` access, and denying it leaves the custom browser behind an Open Settings prompt.

Apple's system picker can display the library in a separate system-controlled process and return only the items the user selects. This is the interaction requested here; it does not depend on knowing ChatGPT's internal implementation.

This follows [#600](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/600), which introduced the custom attachment experience. Preserve its ordered multiselection, explicit Add action, camera, and attachment safeguards while replacing the photo-browsing implementation.

## Proposed behavior

- **+ → Photos** opens Apple's native Photos picker without requesting photo-library read permission, including when library access was previously denied or limited.
- Recommended presentation: embed `PhotosPicker` inside the existing attachment panel using `.photosPickerStyle(.inline)`. Keep the attachment menu and the Back/Add controls; let iOS render the photo browser. Native grid styling will differ from today's custom grid.
- Show images only, preserve numbered selection order, and limit selection to the remaining attachment capacity. If capacity is zero, Photos remains unavailable.
- Selecting photos updates the pending selection. Only tapping **Add** imports them into the composer, using the existing draft/staging/upload behavior. Back or dismiss discards the unconfirmed selection.
- Show preparation progress and recoverable import errors for unavailable iCloud assets, unsupported data, or oversized images. Cancel or invalidate asynchronous work when its picker/chat/server owner goes away.
- Apple's first-use privacy explanation is acceptable; it must not be confused with a request for library read access.
- Camera capture and Save to Photos retain their separate camera/add-only permission flows.

## Acceptance outcomes

- [ ] On a fresh install, **+ → Photos → select → Add** works without a photo-library authorization request.
- [ ] The flow also works with existing Photos access set to denied or limited, without asking the user to change Settings.
- [ ] Shared Session Chat and Bot Chat attachment entry points use the native browser and preserve ordered multiselection, remaining-capacity limits, and exactly-once addition.
- [ ] Selecting/deselecting changes only the unconfirmed selection; Back/dismiss adds nothing. Add uses the existing attachment pipeline and upload timing.
- [ ] Imported images retain current orientation, transparency, processing limits, thumbnails, and durable draft behavior.
- [ ] A failed or canceled import leaves the existing draft intact, reports failure when appropriate, and never adds stale or duplicate attachments. Late completion after navigating away or switching chats/servers cannot attach media to the new destination.
- [ ] Opening, returning from, and dismissing Photos preserves composer text and restores keyboard focus appropriately; repeated Photos/Camera/menu transitions remain responsive.
- [ ] No photo-library read authorization or direct library enumeration remains in the selection path. Remove `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` after confirming no other read-access caller needs it; retain `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` for explicit saves.
- [ ] Light/dark appearance, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and Reduce Motion work in the integrated panel.

## Implementation notes

Source investigation at `bec80c635a7eba483c89341f5dd173de73110152`:

- [CustomAttachmentPicker.swift](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/bec80c635a7eba483c89341f5dd173de73110152/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/CustomAttachmentPicker.swift#L84) currently requests read/write permission, fetches `PHAsset` objects, and renders custom thumbnails. Replace that photo-library model and grid with `PhotosPickerItem` selection, using `.continuousAndOrdered` for the embedded picker and the existing Add action.
- Load selected items asynchronously via `loadTransferable`, with bounded/sequential work and cancellation/stale-result guards. Reuse `HermexAttachmentImageProcessor.prepare` and `HermexPickedMedia` to feed the existing callback. Do not fetch `PHAsset` objects to recover filenames; use a safe generated name when needed.
- [ChatComposerView.swift](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/bec80c635a7eba483c89341f5dd173de73110152/HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatComposerView.swift#L760) supplies capacity and hosts the keyboard-retaining overlay. Validate embedded system-picker interaction with this host before considering the UI complete.
- [BotProfileEditorView.swift](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/blob/bec80c635a7eba483c89341f5dd173de73110152/HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotProfileEditorView.swift#L75) already uses the native Photos picker for avatar selection.
- Main app and tests are the affected targets. No new shared model, extension behavior, third-party dependency, or server contract is required.

## Validation

Add focused tests for import success/failure/cancellation and stale completion at the import/attachment boundary. Retain meaningful processing/capacity coverage; do not test Apple's picker internals.

Run affected tests through `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid> --only HermesMobileTests/<TestClass>`. Relevant existing coverage includes `HermexAttachmentPickerPolicyTests`, `ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests`, `HermesChatAttachmentTests`, and `BotAttachmentSendingTests`; select affected callers after implementation. Run the integrated app as a normally signed Debug build.

Owner's manual iPhone pass: fresh/denied/limited access; select, deselect, cancel, reopen, and Add several images; reach capacity; try an iCloud-only image and interrupted import; background/navigate/switch server during preparation; verify keyboard restoration, repeated Camera/Photos transitions, and accessibility. Mutating send checks use only a disposable session on an explicitly in-scope server.

Before/after UI evidence belongs in the eventual PR. This issue records source/documentation feasibility; no implementation or runtime validation has been performed.

## Upstream dependency notes

Client-only. No new Hermes or legacy hermes-webui endpoint, permission, or server upgrade is needed. The embedded picker is available from iOS 17, below Hermex's current iOS 18 minimum.

- [Apple: Selecting Photos and Videos in iOS](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/PhotoKit/selecting-photos-and-videos-in-ios)
- [Apple: Implementing an inline Photos picker](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/photokit/implementing-an-inline-photos-picker)
- [Apple: Embed the Photos Picker in your app](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10107/)
- [Apple: Bringing Photos picker to your SwiftUI app](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/photokit/bringing-photos-picker-to-your-swiftui-app)

Video selection, image editing, camera redesign, and changes to attachment transport are outside this issue.

title: fix(ui): stop screens jumping just after they open
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: requested and checked directly by the maintainer, one fix at a time.

## What changed

Opening a screen, or swiping back to one, often drew a first frame that differed from the settled one: text flashed, the list or transcript moved by a few points, or a button arrived a second later. On the phone that reads as the app twitching on every open.

Each fix makes the first frame match the settled one:

- **iPhone Duo rail.** The system reports no vertical bar while a pushed screen covers a view, so the home redrew without its rail during a swipe back. A bar once seen now stays until the size class changes, for every reader. With the rail, the home has no title to flash and its list no longer takes the pushed screen's bar height.
- **Chat transcript.** A cached transcript now draws each turn's "Worked for" row, where before it arrived with the host's rows and pushed the reply down (`CachedMessage.anchorsWork`, a new nullable column). An empty "active workers" preview no longer adds a gap, and the bottom inset starts from the composer's last measured resting height instead of a guess.
- **Chat header.** A session opened from the list takes that row's title, folder and model, and a bot's chat takes the inbox row's bot, so nothing starts as "Untitled Session", a bare Profile name or "Model". The Files button shows at once, disabled until the host names the folder.
- **Other screens.** Tasks, Skills, a skill's page, Usage and Files show progress instead of an empty state before their first load. Pinned bot tiles reserve their status line. A Kanban card's detail is titled from the board.

## How it was tested

- Proved on an iPhone Duo (signed Debug build of this tree): the maintainer checked each fix as it landed, back button and swipe back, Sessions and Bots.
- The transcript shift was also measured on the iPhone Duo simulator (iOS 27.1) by recording a long session opening and comparing the transcript's position frame by frame: it moved 8 pt when the host's rows landed before the fix, and not at all after.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 17e> --only HermesMobileTests/SkillsViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/InsightsViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/FileBrowserViewModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/CacheStoreTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptTurnFoldingTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatPresentationTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatSettingsTests`: 139 passed, 0 failed.
- One new test: the cache remembers which rows anchor a turn's work, and clears it.
- No unit test for the rail: `toolbarVerticalEdge` can't be set from a test, and the swipe-back jump shows only on the device, not on the iOS 27.1 simulator.
- No before/after images: the evidence is the maintainer's own phone screenshots, which show private session names.

title: feat(chat): view Mermaid code blocks as diagrams
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1649 (slice 2 of 2; slice 1 was #1651).

## What changed

When an agent replied with a `mermaid` code block, you could only read the source. Now a finished `mermaid` block gets the same eye button as `svg` blocks, and it opens the diagram in the report sheet on the same white card.

- The diagram is drawn on tap by Pele 1.13.0 (MIT, the engine Hermes Desktop uses), bundled unmodified as `Resources/pele.global.js` (733,670 bytes) and never fetched from a CDN. It runs off the main thread in a fresh JavaScriptCore context with no network or page access, and links and images are off, as upstream's are. Nothing new runs in a transcript row.
- The diagram is laid out to the sheet's width, so a wide left-to-right flowchart turns vertical on a phone instead of shrinking.
- A diagram Pele can't parse opens the sheet's existing failure state; the code block keeps its source.
- Adds Pele to Settings → Acknowledgements and to the locked dependency list in `AGENTS.md` (approved on #1649), plus a localized "View diagram" VoiceOver label.

title: feat(chat): optionally send with Return on a hardware keyboard
body:
**What the user gets:** an opt-in Settings toggle so Return on a hardware keyboard (iPad Magic Keyboard) sends the message.
**Why it matters:** a user asked: "Is there any way to send your message by hitting return on the iPad Magic Keyboard? Right now it just makes a new line, you have to hit cmd+return to send."
**Cost:** Small; needs a hardware keyboard (iPad simulator is fine).

Revisits the deferred Return-to-send setting from #1380 (decision there: Return stays a newline by default; this keeps that default).

## Behavior

Settings → Composer → **Send with Return** (device-local, off by default).

| Key | Off (today) | On |
|---|---|---|
| Return (hardware) | newline | Send, as a tap on the circle; nothing when Send is unavailable; never Stop |
| ⇧↩ / ⌥↩ | newline | newline |
| ⌘↩ / ⌘⇧↩ | Send / alternate | unchanged |
| Software keyboard Return | newline | newline |

- `UIKeyCommand` fires only for hardware keyboards, so no keyboard detection is needed.
- An unfinished IME composition keeps Return (it confirms the candidate); never submit marked text.
- Return does exactly what ⌘↩ does, including with slash or file suggestions open (⌘↩ already sends there; Esc closes the panel). Picking a suggestion from the keyboard is a separate feature.
- Applies to the shared composer editor: chat, new sessions, Bot Chat, Bot rooms. Edit message, goal, clarification, and Kanban editors keep their buttons.

## Prior art

t3code iOS: Settings → Keyboard → Return key (`apps/mobile/modules/t3-composer-editor/ios/T3ComposerEditorView.swift:94`), defaulting to send.

## Manual test plan

iPad simulator with hardware keyboard: toggle off → Return newline; on → Return sends, ⇧↩/⌥↩ newline, ⌘↩ still sends; empty draft Return does nothing; Japanese IME Return confirms the candidate without sending; Bot room Return sends.

title: feat(sessions): ask for a GitHub star with a card in the session list
body:
**What the user gets:** a small card in the session list that asks them, once, to star Hermex on GitHub, and a "Star on GitHub" row in Settings › About.
**Why it matters:** stars are how other people find an open source project, and today the app never mentions the repo outside of bug reporting.
**Cost:** Small. Needs the owner to pick a design from mocks and to check the card on a phone.

## Behavior

The star card is a second card in the slot the tip card uses at the top of the session list. It is never a modal or sheet.

**When it shows**

- After 15 completed replies (the same counter the tip card and rating prompt use).
- Not in the same launch as the App Store rating prompt, and not within 7 days after a rating request. These are the tip card's existing rules against the rating prompt.
- Not while a shared import is pending, like the tip card.
- To everyone, including existing users already past 15 replies and people who have opened a tip link.

**Against the tip card**

- The tip card's rules and appearance do not change: 25 replies, same dismissal, same copy.
- At most one card per launch.
- When both are eligible in the same launch, the tip card wins. The star card waits for a later launch, after the tip card has been dismissed or one of its links opened.

**Going away**

- The X ("Not now" for VoiceOver) hides the card until the next feature release (major.minor), like the tip card.
- Tapping the button hides it for good. The app cannot verify a star, so opening the link is the signal.

**The button**

- Exactly one button, plus the X. No secondary link.
- It hands `https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex` to iOS, so the GitHub app opens when installed and Safari otherwise. Not an in-app browser: it does not share Safari's sign-in.

**Settings › About**

- Add a "Star on GitHub" row. Opening it also hides the card for good, the way the coffee row does for the tip card.

**Not included**

- No live star count. The app makes no request to GitHub's API.
- No change to the rating prompt's own thresholds.

## Design

Build the star card from the tip card's shell (face, title, X, body, button) so the two read as a pair; extract the shared shell rather than copying it. The tip card must look the same afterwards.

**First step:** static mocks of the star card for the owner to pick from, exploring face colour and expression and the button treatment, in light and dark. Stop for a pick before touching real components.

Starting copy, final wording settled in the mocks:

- Title: **Star Hermex on GitHub**
- Body: **Hermex is free and open source. A star costs nothing and helps more people find it.**
- Button: **Star on GitHub**

Any face animation follows the tip card's rules: no frame updates during pauses, off with Reduce Motion, stopped when the card is off screen or the app is in the background. New strings go through the String Catalog (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).

## Where to look

- `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/TipJarCard.swift`: the card to share a shell with.
- `HermesMobile/Config/TipJarPromptState.swift` and `RatingPromptState.swift`: eligibility, dismissal, and the per-launch guard.
- `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListView.swift`: where eligibility is computed and the card is placed.
- `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift` and `HermesMobile/Config/AppConfig.swift`: the About row and the URL.

## Testing

Policy tests, one per behavior: eligible at 15 replies; the tip card wins when both are eligible; the X hides until the next feature release; opening the link hides for good; held back for 7 days after a rating request.

## After release

Nothing in the app measures this. Compare tip income and the repo's star rate for the two weeks before and after the release, and revisit the 15-reply threshold if tips fall.
