title: feat(app): opt-in weekly usage reports
body:
**What the user gets:** an optional weekly usage report, off until they allow it, that tells the developer which servers, versions and features people actually use.
**Why it matters:** today nothing shows how many users are still on webui, which features go unused, or whether the tip and star cards work, so those decisions are guesses.
**Cost:** Large. Needs the owner to pick the consent card from mocks, deploy a Cloudflare Worker, edit the App Store privacy label, and check the card on a phone.

## What this changes about the promise

`AGENTS.md` and the README say Hermex has no analytics service. This adds one, as a second optional exception beside push. Agreed terms:

- Off until the user allows it. One toggle for the whole device.
- No account, no device identifier field, no IP address stored.
- Never message text, server URLs, credentials, file names, or a custom server version string.
- The collector is open source. Its data is private to the developer; nothing is published for now.
- The exact report is viewable in the app before it is sent.
- The tip card keeps "no ads and no tracking".

The report includes the install day, device model, language and region. Together these can recognise one phone's reports week to week. The owner accepted that and chose not to add a line about it; the in-app preview shows every field.

## What Apple already covers (not built here)

- Crashes and hangs with app version, iOS version and device: Xcode Organizer. All TestFlight users, App Store users who share diagnostics.
- Rough active devices and day 1/7/14/28 retention: App Store Connect, same opt-in, hidden below five devices.
- No crash pipeline and no handled-error reporting in this version. Error text is the likeliest place for a server URL to leak.

## Decisions each field feeds

- Server kind and version: when to stop fixing webui, when to raise the minimum Hermes version.
- Feature used or not: what to prune.
- Card funnel: keep, retime or reword the tip and star cards.
- Completed responses and server counts: how much multi-server polish matters.

## The report

One report per week, sent by the main app only, never from a Debug build. This section is the wire contract for both the app (#1662) and the collector (#1660).

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "week": "2026-W46",
  "channel": "appstore",
  "app_version": "1.9.0",
  "os_version": "26.1",
  "device_model": "iPhone17,2",
  "language": "en",
  "region": "US",
  "install_day": "2026-03-04",
  "days_active": 5,
  "first_report_of_month": true,
  "servers": {
    "hermes": 1,
    "webui": 1,
    "versions": [
      { "kind": "hermes", "version": "0.14.2" },
      { "kind": "webui", "version": "unknown" }
    ]
  },
  "completed_responses": 42,
  "features": {
    "workspace": true, "tasks": false, "skills": false, "memory": false,
    "insights": true, "kanban": false, "bots": true, "share_extension": false,
    "home_widget": false, "live_activity": true, "voice_input": false, "app_intents": false
  },
  "settings": { "push_enabled": true, "app_lock": false },
  "cards": {
    "tip": { "shown": true, "dismissed": false, "link_opened": false },
    "star": { "shown": false, "dismissed": false, "link_opened": false }
  }
}
```

Every key is required. The collector rejects a report with an unknown key, a missing key, or a value outside these limits.

| Key | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `v` | a format version the collector supports |
| `week` | `YYYY-Www`, the ISO week in UTC that the report covers |
| `channel` | `appstore` or `testflight` |
| `app_version`, `os_version` | digits and dots only, 2 or 3 parts |
| `device_model` | the hardware identifier, letters, digits and one comma, at most 20 characters |
| `language` | the app's display language as a BCP 47 tag, at most 16 characters |
| `region` | the device's region setting, two capital letters or three digits |
| `install_day` | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `days_active` | 0 to 7 |
| `servers.hermes`, `servers.webui` | 0 to 99; the app sends 99 for 99 or more |
| `servers.versions` | at most 20 entries, the app sends the first 20 when there are more; `kind` is `hermes` or `webui`; `version` is digits and dots (2 to 4 parts), `other`, or `unknown` |
| `completed_responses` | 0 to 100000 |
| `features.*`, `settings.*`, `cards.*.*`, `first_report_of_month` | true or false |

Definitions:

- **Week.** An ISO week in UTC, whatever the device's calendar or time zone.
- **Active day.** A UTC day in which the app came to the foreground at least once.
- **First report of the month.** True when the app has not yet attempted a report for another week whose Monday falls in the same UTC month.
- **Install day.** The app's existing first-launch date (`RatingPromptSettings.firstLaunchDateKey`), as a UTC day. It resets on reinstall, and for people who installed before that date was first recorded it is the day it was first recorded.
- **Server counts and versions.** Read once, when the report is built. A version is the release the app already knows for that server. `unknown` when it knows none (webui servers store none); `other` when the value is not a plain release number. Building a report never makes a server request.
- **Completed responses.** Responses that finished in the main app during the week. This is a new weekly counter that only runs after consent; the existing all-time counter the tip card and rating prompt read is left as it is.
- **Features** are things the user did during the week. **Settings** are states read when the report is built. #1662 says where each is observed.
- **Cards.** `shown` is true when the card was on screen in at least one launch that week. `dismissed` is the card's own X. `link_opened` is the card's own button; the matching rows in Settings › About do not count.

The collector adds two fields the phone never sends: the arrival day and Cloudflare's country code.

## Consent

- A one-time card in the session-list slot the tip and star cards use, never a sheet.
- It becomes eligible at 5 or more completed responses on the existing all-time counter, so people already past 5 see it too. When it is eligible it wins over the tip and star cards. The existing guards still apply: at most one card per launch, not in the same launch as the rating prompt or within 7 days after one, and not while a shared import is pending.
- Two buttons at equal weight, "Allow" and "No thanks", and no X. "No thanks" is permanent.
- "See what's sent" opens the preview. Opening it neither dismisses the card nor counts as an answer.
- **Preview before consent** is a clearly labelled example. Nothing is tallied before consent, so there is no real report to show yet. Device, language, region, install day and server fields show the phone's real values; the weekly counts show sample values.
- **Preview after consent** shows the report as it would be sent for the week in progress, built by the same code that builds the sent report.
- Both previews list, separately, the two fields the collector adds (arrival day, country).
- The same toggle and preview live in Settings.
- Nothing is tallied or sent while no server is configured.
- Turning it off stops sending and erases the local tallies. A report already sent cannot be recalled or deleted, and the copy says so.

## Format versions

- The app stores the format version the user accepted, and always encodes that version.
- When a build knows a newer version with added fields, it shows a re-prompt in the same slot. "Allow" raises the accepted version. "No thanks" keeps the accepted version, keeps reporting in it, and does not ask again for that version.
- Removing a field also makes a new version number. A version that only removes fields is adopted without a prompt, and the build encodes it from then on.
- The collector keeps a validator for every version still in use, and adds columns to D1 without rewriting old rows.

## Sending

On each foreground, before recording activity for a new week, the app looks at the tallies it holds:

- If they are for the week just ended and no send has been attempted for it, the app records the attempt, checks consent once more, and posts the report.
- Tallies for any older week are discarded unsent.
- A failed request is not retried, including after a relaunch. No background task and no retry queue.

## Collector

- A new public repo (working name `hermex-stats`): one Cloudflare Worker and one D1 database, separate from `hermex-push` so a report can never be joined to a device token.
- A fixed address built into the app, with no setting to change it.
- Stores every row forever. Never stores the IP address; Worker logging is off.
- Accepts unverified reports, with Cloudflare rate limiting and strict shape validation. App Attest is deliberately left out.
- A private dashboard page behind Cloudflare Access. First views: reports received per week and month, and retention by install week; Hermes versus webui and server versions; feature usage, grouped by phones that are Hermes-only, webui-only or mixed; card funnel; app and iOS version spread; completed responses per week and server counts. Counts are labelled "reports received", since nothing proves two reports came from different phones.

## Wording afterwards

- README (`README.md:37`): change "no analytics and no tracking" to "no ads and no tracking", keep the rest of the paragraph (remote resources, push relay), and append: "If you turn on usage reports, the app sends a weekly usage summary to the developer, never message text, server addresses or file names. See exactly what is sent in Settings."
- `AGENTS.md`: usage reports named as a second optional exception beside push; new `docs/agents/usage-reports.md` as the map.
- `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`: consent and tallies are device-wide, not per server.
- `TESTFLIGHT.md` review notes: "no tracking; optional first-party usage reports".
- Privacy manifest and App Store label: add four data types, each not linked, not tracking, purpose Analytics. The existing Device ID entry for push is unchanged.
  - Usage Data → Product Interaction: features used, days active, completed responses, card funnel.
  - Usage Data → Other Usage Data: server counts and versions, settings states.
  - Location → Coarse Location: the country the collector derives from the connection. "Location" will show on the store page.
  - Other Data → Other Data Types: device model, iOS and app version, language, region, install day.

## Owner-only steps

- Create the `hermex-stats` repo, deploy the Worker and D1 database, and put Cloudflare Access in front of the dashboard.
- Edit the App Store privacy label in the same release as the app change. The label changes for every user, including those who never opt in.
- Publish the privacy policy update with the same release (uzairansaruzi/hermexapp-site#31).

## Open checks

- ~~Whether device model, language and country need further App Store label entries.~~ Settled 2026-11-12: four entries, listed under "Wording afterwards".
- Whether Cloudflare Access is free on the account's current plan.

## Research behind this

- T3 Code is opt-out with a persistent hashed install ID and a footer notice; not the model here.
- Syncthing: opt-in prompt, report preview, re-prompt when the report grows. Home Assistant: opt-in tiers. Signal and Home Assistant's iOS app: Apple's data only.

## Children

In order: the collector, the consent card mocks, then the app change.

title: feat(stats): collector Worker and private dashboard for usage reports
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing visible; this is the place opt-in usage reports are sent, and the developer's private page for reading them.
**Why it matters:** the app change in the parent issue cannot be tested end to end until a collector exists.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner to create the repo and deploy to Cloudflare; no phone needed.

Parent: #1659 holds every decision and the wire contract. This issue is the collector only.

## Problem and outcome

There is nowhere to send a usage report. Build a small open source Cloudflare Worker that accepts the weekly report, stores it, and serves a private dashboard.

## Plan

This work is in a **new repo**, working name `uzairansaruzi/hermex-stats`, not in this one. Follow the layout of the relay in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-push` (Cloudflare Worker, Workers Paid).

- `POST /v1/report`: the only route open to the public. Refuse a body over 8 KB before parsing. Validate strictly against the contract in #1659 ("The report"): unknown key, missing key, wrong type or out-of-limit value is rejected and nothing is stored. Reply with no body.
- Keep one validator per supported format version, chosen by `v`. Version 1 is the only one today.
- Store one D1 row per accepted report: every report field, plus the arrival **day** (UTC) and the request's Cloudflare country code (`request.cf.country`). A later format version adds nullable columns; old rows are never rewritten.
- Never read, store or log the IP address. Worker logs, observability and Logpush stay off; say so in the README and in the deploy checklist.
- `GET /`: the dashboard, one server-rendered page of plain tables and simple charts with the views listed in #1659. Cloudflare Access sits in front of it. The Worker also checks the Access token itself on every route except `POST /v1/report`: signature against the team's public keys, issuer, the dashboard application's audience, and expiry. Anything else is refused, including requests that reach the Worker by its `workers.dev` hostname.
- Rate limiting is a Cloudflare rate limiting rule at the edge on `POST /v1/report`, configured in the deploy checklist. Cloudflare applies it; the Worker never sees or keys on the address.
- README: what is stored, what is never stored, retention (forever), and how to deploy a copy.

## Decisions

- **Rows, not totals.** Keep every report so new questions can be asked later.
- **Retention.** Forever.
- **No public data.** The report route accepts posts from anyone; nothing can be read without Access.
- **No App Attest.** Fake reports are an accepted risk in this version.
- **Arrival time.** Day only, not the second.
- **Dashboard design.** No mocks; the owner is its only reader.

## Acceptance and tests

- The example report in #1659 is accepted and stored with arrival day and country.
- A report with an unknown key, a missing key, a wrong type, or a version string shaped like a host name is rejected and nothing is stored.
- A body over the size limit is refused.
- The dashboard refuses a request with no token, a forged token, an expired token, and a token for another audience.
- The stored row has no column that could hold an address, and the code never reads the connecting-IP header.
- Tests run in the Workers test runner the push relay already uses.

## Mocks

Not required.

## Outside reach

- Creating the public repo, the D1 database, the Worker deployment, the Cloudflare Access application, the edge rate limiting rule, and confirming logging is off are the owner's steps. Stop and hand over a deploy checklist; do not deploy.
- Record the final collector URL on the parent issue; the app change needs it.

## Surfaces

None in the app.

title: feat(sessions): mocks for the usage reports consent card and preview
body:
**What the user gets:** the look and wording of the card that asks, once, whether to turn on usage reports, and of the Settings page that shows what is sent.
**Why it matters:** the consent copy is the promise; it gets picked before any real component changes.
**Cost:** Small. Needs the owner to pick from mocks.

Parent: #1659 holds every decision. This issue produces mocks and stops.

## Problem and outcome

The app change needs a consent card, a "See what's sent" preview, and a Settings toggle. Build several distinct static mocks, publish them, report the URL, and stop for a pick. Touch no real component.

## Plan

- The card lives in the session-list slot the tip and star cards use, built from the same shell: `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListCards.swift:33` is the tip card's copy, and `HermesMobile/Config/SessionListCardState.swift:4` (`SessionListCard`) picks which card shows.
- Mock three things, in light and dark:
  1. The consent card: title, one or two lines of body, "Allow" and "No thanks" at equal weight, a "See what's sent" link, and no X.
  2. The preview, in both states from #1659: the labelled example shown before consent, and the real report shown after. Each is a readable list grouped like the contract, with the two collector-added fields (arrival day, country) listed apart.
  3. Settings: the toggle, the preview entry, and the line that says turning it off cannot delete past reports.
- Also mock the re-prompt shown when the report gains a field: it names the added fields and offers "Allow" and "No thanks".

Starting copy, final wording settled in the mocks:

- Title: **Help improve Hermex**
- Body: **Send a weekly usage summary to the developer. Never message text, server addresses or file names.**
- Buttons: **Allow** / **No thanks**
- Link: **See what's sent**

## Decisions

- **A card, not a sheet.** #1657 rules the slot is never a modal or sheet.
- **Equal-weight buttons, no X.** Neither choice is styled as the default, and the card leaves only by an answer.
- **No extra disclosure line** about install date or device model; the preview lists every field.
- **Where the Settings toggle sits** is open: recommend Settings › About, beside the Privacy Policy row (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift:68`).

## Acceptance

Mocks published with the `html-communication` skill, the URL reported, and a pick recorded on this issue.

## Mocks

Required; they are the whole issue.

## Surfaces

iPhone and iPad session list, Settings. Any face animation follows the tip card's rules: no frame updates during pauses, off with Reduce Motion.

title: feat(app): tally, preview and send the weekly usage report
body:
**What the user gets:** a one-time card asking whether to send a weekly usage summary, a preview of exactly what is sent, and a Settings toggle to change their mind.
**Why it matters:** this is the app half of the usage reports epic; without it nothing is collected.
**Cost:** Large. Needs the owner to check the card on a phone and to edit the App Store privacy label in the same release.

Parent: #1659 holds every decision, the wire contract with its definitions, the consent and sending rules, and the wording. Blocked by #1660 and #1661.

## Problem and outcome

The app has no way to count usage or ask for consent. Add local tallies, the consent card, the preview, the Settings toggle, and the weekly send, plus the doc and privacy-manifest edits that must ship with it.

## Plan

- **Tallies.** A small device-wide store in `UserDefaults` holding one week: the week id, the UTC days seen active, completed responses, feature booleans, and each card's shown / dismissed / link-opened. Callers pass it only booleans and counts, never a URL, name or payload. It records nothing unless reports are allowed and at least one server is configured.
- **Completed responses.** Add a consent-gated weekly count beside the existing all-time counter, at the same place that counter is bumped: `recordCompletedResponse()` (`HermesMobile/Config/RatingPromptState.swift:73`), reached from `ChatStreamCoordinator` (webui) and `HermesChatTurnCoordinator` (Hermes). The all-time counter and its readers are untouched.
- **Cards.** `recordLinkOpened()` also calls `dismiss()` (`HermesMobile/Config/SessionListCardState.swift:92`–`:99`), and Settings › About calls it for both cards (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAboutPage.swift:88`, `:106`). So tally at the card view, not inside those methods: `link_opened` from the card's button (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListCards.swift:154`), `dismissed` from the card's X, `shown` when a launch picks the card (`cardShownThisLaunch`, `RatingPromptState.swift:54`).
- **Features and settings.** Observe each as below. Both session list implementations (`SessionListView`, `HermesSessionListView`) and both layouts (compact covers, and the iPad detail column at `HermesSessionListView.swift:520`–`:545`) open these screens, so tally in the destination view's appearance, not at one menu.

  | Key | Counts when |
  | --- | --- |
  | `workspace` | the Workspace browser opens, from the list or from the composer's workspace picker (`ChatComposerSelectorSheets.swift:514`) |
  | `tasks`, `skills`, `memory`, `insights`, `kanban` | that screen appears |
  | `bots` | a Bot's chat or room opens |
  | `voice_input` | a voice recording or dictation starts in the composer |
  | `share_extension` | the main app takes in a staged import whose `source` is nil, meaning a share (`SharedDraftPayload.source`, `HermesMobile/Features/Share/SharedDraftStore.swift:10`); Shortcut and other queued text do not count |
  | `home_widget` | a Home Screen widget's link is routed |
  | `live_activity` | the app starts a Live Activity |
  | `app_intents` | a queued App Intent link is drained (`drainPendingIntentDeepLink`, `HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:303`) |
  | `settings.push_enabled` | read when the report is built: any configured server has a push pairing |
  | `settings.app_lock` | read when the report is built |

  An import or link staged before consent counts only if it is handled after consent. The share extension, widget, Live Activity and notification service targets get no new code.
- **Report.** One `Encodable` value matching the contract in #1659. Server versions pass through one function that returns the release number, `other`, or `unknown`; a webui `ServerAccount` stores no version (`HermesMobile/Models/ServerAccount.swift:48`), so it reports `unknown`. Building a report makes no server request, and no URL enters the type.
- **Preview.** Before consent, a labelled example. After consent, the report for the week in progress, from the same builder the sender uses.
- **Consent card.** A third case in `SessionListCard` (`SessionListCardState.swift:4`), with the eligibility and ordering rules in #1659 "Consent": 5 or more completed responses, ahead of tip and star, existing rating and import guards kept, no X, and "See what's sent" neither dismisses nor answers. The shared card shell treats every link as a permanent dismissal (`SessionListCards.swift:153`), so the preview link needs its own path.
- **Settings.** The toggle and preview where the mocks put them. Turning off stops sending and erases the tallies.
- **Sending.** The rollover rules in #1659 "Sending": record the attempt before posting, check consent again immediately before the request, never retry. Post to the collector URL recorded on #1659 with an ephemeral `URLSession`: no cookies, no custom headers, no server credentials. Never from a Debug build; TestFlight builds set `channel` to `testflight`.
- **Format version.** Store the accepted version and encode that version, per #1659 "Format versions". Only version 1 exists, so this PR builds the stored value and the re-prompt card, not a second format.
- **Docs and manifest, same PR.**
  - `README.md:37`: the edit described in #1659, which keeps the remote-resource and push sentences.
  - `AGENTS.md:13`: usage reports as a second optional exception beside push.
  - New `docs/agents/usage-reports.md`: the contract, consent, collector, what is never sent.
  - `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md`: consent and tallies are device-wide.
  - `TESTFLIGHT.md:395`: "no tracking; optional first-party usage reports".
  - `HermesMobile/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`: add four collected data types, each not linked, not tracking, purpose `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAnalytics`. They match the App Store label entries listed in #1659. The share extension's manifest is unchanged; it sends nothing.
    - `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeProductInteraction`: features used, days active, completed responses, card funnel.
    - `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeOtherUsageData`: server counts and versions, settings states.
    - `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeCoarseLocation`: the country the collector derives from the connection.
    - `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeOtherDataTypes`: device model, iOS and app version, language, region, install day.
  - New strings through the String Catalog (`docs/agents/i18n.md`).

## Decisions

- **One device-wide toggle**, not per server. The report describes the phone.
- **Features are yes or no** for the week, not counts.
- **Exact counts** for completed responses and servers.
- **Install day** is the existing first-launch date as a UTC day.
- **Weeks and days are UTC.**
- **Zero servers:** nothing is tallied or sent.
- **Language** is the app's display language; **region** is the device's region setting.
- **No retry queue.** A lost week is accepted.
- **Tip card copy unchanged.**

## Acceptance and tests

- With reports off, a completed response, an opened feature screen and a card tap tally nothing, and no request is made.
- A report built from two configured servers contains no URL, host name or custom version string (assert on the encoded bytes), and a webui server reports `unknown`.
- The after-consent preview and the sent body are equal for the same tallies.
- A new week on foreground sends exactly one report for the previous week; a second foreground sends none. After a failed send, a new process does not send that week again.
- Tallies two or more weeks old are discarded, not sent.
- Turning reports off between building and posting sends nothing, and erases the tallies.
- The request carries no cookie and no authorization or custom header.
- A Debug build never sends.
- A tip-card button tap sets `link_opened` and not `dismissed`; the Settings › About row sets neither.
- The consent card wins over an eligible tip or star card, never shows with either in one launch, and "No thanks" never shows it again. Opening the preview leaves the card in place. Extend `SessionListCardTests`.

Run with `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/<TestClass>` for the new tests, `SessionListCardTests` and `RatingPromptTests`.

## Mocks

Required and already picked in the mocks issue. Before and after images in the PR.

## Outside reach

- The App Store privacy label edit and the privacy policy page (uzairansaruzi/hermexapp-site#31) are the owner's, and must land with the release that carries this.
- No request to the live Hermes host or the push relay.

## Surfaces

iPhone and iPad main app: session list (webui and Hermes list views), Settings. Share extension, Live Activity widget, notification service: observed only, no code that sends. Two configured servers: the report counts both and names neither.

title: feat(app): tally, preview and send the weekly usage report
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1662

## What changed

Nothing tells us which servers, versions and features people actually use. This adds opt-in weekly usage reports, the app half of #1659. Nothing is counted or sent until the user allows it.

- **Consent card:** asks once, in the session list's card slot, after 5 completed replies. It wins over the tip and star cards and keeps their guards. It has no X; Allow and No thanks are the only ways out. "See what's sent" opens the preview without answering. I read "exactly 5" in the issue as a threshold, so people already past 5 replies are asked too.
- **Preview:** every field, grouped like the wire contract. Before consent it is a labelled example with sample weekly values; after, it is this week so far, from the same builder the sender uses.
- **Settings › About › Usage Reports:** the toggle and the preview. Turning it off erases the tallies and doesn't bring the card back.
- **Tallies and sending:** `UsageReports` keeps one UTC week in `UserDefaults`, recorded only while reports are allowed and a server is configured. Features are tallied where each screen or entry point opens. On a foreground after the week ends, it sends that week once: the attempt is recorded first, consent is checked again just before the request, nothing is retried, and older weeks are dropped. The request goes through an ephemeral session with no cookies, credentials or custom headers, and Debug builds never send. TestFlight builds report `testflight` from StoreKit's app transaction.
- **Allow button:** yellow, the card face's color, as the tip card's button is; No thanks stays gray at the same size. This changes the mock pick of two equal gray buttons, at Uzair's request.
- **Developer settings (Debug only):** "Force usage reports card" forgets the answer and shows the card past its guards until answered, for checking it on a phone.
- **Privacy manifest:** four collected data types (Product Interaction, Other Usage Data, Coarse Location, Other Data Types), each not linked, not tracking, purpose Analytics.
- **Docs:** README, AGENTS, TESTFLIGHT and the multi-server doc, plus a new `docs/agents/usage-reports.md`.

Owner steps outside this PR: the App Store privacy label and the privacy policy page (uzairansaruzi/hermexapp-site#31) ship with the release that carries this.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim` on iPhone 17e: `UsageReportsTests`, `SessionListCardTests` and `RatingPromptTests`, 30 passed. The new tests cover: nothing recorded or sent while reports are off or no server is configured; the encoded report carries no URL, host or custom version string, and a webui server reports `unknown`; the preview equals the sent body; one send per ended week; no retry after a failed send in a new process; tallies two weeks old are dropped; turning off mid-send sends nothing and erases the tallies; no cookie or credential header; a Debug build never sends; card button versus X versus About row tallies; and the card's threshold, precedence and permanent No thanks.
- `ci/check_string_catalog.py` passes. The 56 new strings are translated into all 17 shipped languages, marked for review.
- Live collector: a report encoded by the app's own builder and device code, with the week forced to 2000-W01, was posted to `https://hermex-stats.uzairansar.com/v1/report` and got 204. The stored row was then deleted from D1 (1 row removed, 0 left).
- Signed Debug build on the simulator, after clearing rating and card state: the card shows at 6 replies, both previews and the Settings page render in light and dark, Allow switches the About row to On, and turning it off switches the row to Off, erases the tallies, and the card stays gone after a relaunch.
- Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on high. Sol verdict: approved. It found that the preview hid the closed and link-opened flags when a card was not shown, and that the zero-server path had no test with consent on. Both are fixed.

**Before:** the session list without the card (as on master).

![Session list before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23030382-126d-4474-bced-b38bca9bdda7)

**After:**

![Consent card, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37108e4f-2bb7-4cad-8c9d-3776538e7ab5)
![Consent card, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5bfa7a9c-95e2-4ef9-b4bb-b21dbc4ed8eb)

title: feat(push): open delivery snapshots in the Tasks output reader
body:
## Linked issue

Refs #566. This is the app-side delivery-output slice; it does not close the issue. Cron delivery and the new event kinds belong in hermex-push, and the catalog submission remains a separate follow-up.

## What changed

A scheduled report can be much longer than its notification preview. A `delivery` notification now opens the Tasks output reader for the complete delivery snapshot saved by the companion plugin, using the existing paired-server, Profile and stored-session-key lookup.

The snapshot is a copy of the delivered result in a `hermex-delivery-*` session, not the original agent run or a new item in cron run history. Other notification kinds keep their existing destinations. This route requires plugin 0.8.0 and a relay that forwards the `delivery` kind.

App Store 2.1 can already decrypt an unfamiliar kind, retain its sealed English title and open the same snapshot as a conversation. An older relay explicitly ignores the new kind; the plugin can then send the saved snapshot as `reply`, which follows the Replies preference and the conversation route. The Tasks documentation now describes current `local-*` cron session IDs as well as legacy `cron_*` IDs.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid> --only HermesMobileTests/PushPreviewTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionLinkTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesCronClientTests`: **51 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- The new delivery-tap test checks the paired server, named Profile, snapshot key and Tasks-output destination; a system notification keeps the session destination.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- A normally signed Debug build was installed and launched on a dedicated simulator. This confirmed app launch only, not the delivery-output interaction.
- **Not verified:** the complete APNs-tap-to-output UI flow. No isolated signed-in Hermes UI fixture was configured, and no production host was used. The focused tests cover routing, Profile lookup and the output client. Physical-phone APNs verification remains outstanding.

## Known limitation / owner check

The output sheet is currently held outside `HermesSessionListCovers`. A review raised a possible navigation issue: opening Usage from a widget, a New Session Shortcut or a share while the output sheet is open may navigate underneath that sheet until it is dismissed. This has not been reproduced in the running UI and remains an acceptance check.

On an isolated paired host, open a delivery notification and leave its output sheet visible. Enter through each of those three paths and confirm that the requested destination replaces the sheet. Record the entry point if it does not.

title: epic(hermes): reach webui parity before sunsetting the webui connection
body:
**What the user gets:** everything they rely on with a webui server keeps working when Hermex connects only to a Hermes host.
**Why it matters:** the webui connection is being sunset. A scan of every webui feature against the direct Hermes path (2026-11-12, at host pin `3b421578`, 0.23.1) found about 30 gaps nobody had recorded.
**Cost:** Large in total, split into small children. Four items gate the sunset; the rest ship when ready.

This issue is the record of what was found and what the owner decided. It replaces `docs/agents/hermes-feature-index.md`. Children were filed on 2026-11-12 as sub-issues, each with a file-level plan; each one re-verifies its host contract before editing (AGENTS.md, Working with the server). Run the four that gate the sunset first.

## Adopted: gates the sunset

- [x] #1670 **Default Model in Hermes Settings.** A Profile's default model can only be set from the Bots-side Profile editor (`BotProfileEditorView.swift:125`). Add a Default Model row to the Hermes server page with live refresh, saving through `profiles.configure`, which the Bots editor already uses.
- [x] #1671 **New chat starts in the selected project.** `HermesSessionListView.swift:632` builds `.new(profile:)` with no folder, so New Chat ignores the selected project lane. `.new(profile:cwd:)` already exists.
- [x] #1672 **Settings rows on the Hermes server page.** Message Count, Workspace and Clear Offline Cache exist only on the webui server page (`WebuiServerSettings.swift`). The Hermes list already honors the two switches.
- [x] #1673 **`/workspace` and `/interrupt`.** Neither is a Hermes command, so both are sent to the agent as literal prompt text. Route them to the existing folder move and stop-and-send.

## Adopted: not gating

- [x] #1674 **Session sources.** A source chip on rows (CLI, Telegram and so on) and one toggle to hide CLI and messaging sessions. The phone filters: the host stores CLI and Hermex chats under the same source, so its own filter can't separate them.
- [ ] **Intents and shares while the host is unreachable.** New Chat intents and share-extension imports open nothing until the list has read the host. Open the composer at once and send when the host answers, as webui does. *Not filed yet: it needs a design for holding an unsent Hermes chat first.*
- [ ] **Export as HTML and Markdown.** Hermes offers JSON only. *Not filed. Live check, 2026-11-12, host 0.23.1: the dashboard gateway answers "unknown method" for `session.export`. Only a canonical (Webapp) gateway has it, and there the check could not reach a stored session to prove it. Owner to decide between JSON only and a canonical-only export.*
- [x] #1675 **Copy Deeplink.** Hidden for Hermes sessions (`SessionListComponents.swift:238`), though `HermesDeepLink.sessionURL(for:)` exists.
- [x] #1676 **Any attachment type.** `BotAttachmentUpload.swift:55` refuses video and other files. Live check, 2026-11-12: the host attached a video and an unknown-extension file, so the limit is the app's alone.
- [x] #1677 **Kanban.** Only Mine, Bulk Actions to Review and Scheduled (webui's single-card Move never offered them either), and Complete from outside Review with a result prompt (Bulk Action to Done fails on those Cards today).
- [x] #1678 **Usage, one day.** A one-day total. The host's `days=1` is a rolling 24 hours, so the issue recommends labelling it "24 hours".
- [x] #1679 **Polish.** Skill suggestions in the middle of a sentence; Approval and Input badges on waiting rows (one `approval.pending` call per waiting row, accepted); inline images given by a relative path; a New Chat button on the iPad empty state; a count on the Archived row; each Profile's model in the Profile picker and in Shortcuts.

## Dropped: removed in the sunset PR

These work only on webui and go away with it.

- Voice notes (hold to record and send a clip with its transcript). Dictation stays.
- Reopening the last session on launch.
- The response-speed toggle. The host has no per-turn speed.
- The context popover's Cost and Threshold rows. The host sends neither.

## Dropped: no work

- Subagent Sessions toggle. Subagents show inside their chat.
- Live server Status row in Settings. The connection line covers it.
- Kanban workspace path on create (the host picks it, #1044) and moves to To Do (the dispatcher promotes those itself).
- Busiest weekday and busiest hour in Usage.
- Modified times on Memory sections.
- Skill linked files nested more than one folder deep.

## Accepted: host limits

The host cannot serve these at the pin. No work expected.

- **Chat:** an error flag on tool rows; a personality for one session only; `/reasoning show` and `hide`; steering with staged files; clearing a chat in place (`/clear` opens a new chat); `/model` with an ID the host doesn't list.
- **Tasks:** toast notifications; moving a Task to another Profile; an outcome for each run in history.
- **Usage and Memory:** hourly activity; the project context section.
- **Files and Git:** build, VCS and credential folders hidden by the host; symlinked folders; file sizes in listings; last commit and ahead/behind in the branch picker; unstaging or discarding a rename; staging a conflicted file; Commit Selected with partly staged files; branch names outside the host's allowed characters.
- **Profiles:** creating a Profile with a base URL; a server-wide default Profile.
- **Kanban:** Block from any status; Undo Archive of a Done Card.
- **Live Activity:** a leftover activity from a run without push paired ends as "complete" with no alert, because the host reports no outcome for a finished run.
- **Move to Hermes:** chats over 10,000 messages or 5 MB are refused and stay on the webui server; fork lineage, unread state and cleared-history trimming don't carry over. The Move screen already says so.

## Out of scope

- Files and Git on SSH backends. webui browsed its own host's disk, so this was never a webui feature. The host serves files over SSH at the pin; file it separately if wanted.
- A Providers status screen. API Keys on Hermes already writes keys, which webui could not.

## Decided earlier

Carried over from the retired index.

| Gap | Decision |
| :--- | :--- |
| Git fetch, pull, new branch | Shipped through hermex-push (#1236), gated on its `/capabilities`. |
| Git stash-and-checkout | Dropped. A dirty tree refuses a switch. |
| Workspace registry (add, remove, rename, reorder) | Dropped. A chat's workspace is its session's folder. |
| Session project tags, Move to Project, "No project" | Shipped as host folders (#1052). |
| Kanban tenant edit | Accepted. Set on create, read-only after. |
| Approval mode | Shipped (#1550). |
| Provider quota | Shipped through hermex-push (#1237), with the Limits widget (#1409). |
| Skill tags and related skills | Dropped. The host sends no tags. |
| Reasoning levels per model | Accepted. A fixed ladder; the host clamps. |
| Usage message and activity counts | Accepted. Counted over the newest 500 sessions, shown as "≈". |
| Task run history past 100 runs | Accepted. |
| Password-less and trusted-header servers | Accepted. A Hermes host needs a sign-in provider off loopback. |
| Bot name, update channel, max tokens settings | Dropped. |
| Hidden Bot Chats in a merged recency list | Not applicable. Bots and Sessions are two sides (#709). |
| Live Activity outcome after a mid-turn compression while suspended | Accepted. |
| Claude Code sessions in the list | Not applicable. `session.foreign.*` is never sent. |
| Message reactions | Dropped. |

`cli.exec` and `shell.exec` are a generic host shell and must never be sent. The retired index also listed upstream RPC families Hermex doesn't call; that list is not carried over, and `HermesCall` and `HermesREST` remain the authority for what the app sends.

## Seen in the scan, not put to the owner

Small differences recorded so nobody rediscovers them. None is adopted.

- Attachments: 8 files, 25 MB each and 50 MB in total on Hermes, against 10 files of 20 MB on webui. Images are re-encoded.
- Edit and Regenerate are hidden on prompts with attachments and on compacted rows.
- Listen sends at most 4,000 characters, against 5,000.
- Content search returns at most 100 results.
- Image previews stop at 25 MB and text previews at 512 KiB.
- A remote branch can be checked out only when its short name is unique.
- Run Now is refused on a completed Task.
- Top-level folders don't open on the first Files visit (#1138).
- Kanban hides a Card's workspace path and Claim ID.
- A Profile can only be created from the Bots side.
- Possible bug, not parity: the Hermes Usage chart reads the host's days as UTC (`HermesInsightsClient.swift:113`), while the host groups them by local time.

## Not covered by the scan

- Turns started on another device or by the server while a chat is open.
- The Add Server form, field by field.
- Composer defaults kept per server.

## How the scan was run

Eight read-only passes over the source: chat composer, chat transcript and stream, session list, Settings and Profiles, Workspace and Git, Tasks/Skills/Memory/Usage/Kanban, system surfaces and connection, and a sweep of every `Endpoint` case against `HermesCall` and `HermesREST`. Eleven of the findings were re-checked by hand; the rest carry the file references the passes reported.

title: feat(settings): set a Profile's default model from a Hermes server's Settings
body:
**What the user gets:** a Default Model row in a Hermes server's Settings, so each Profile's starting model can be picked without going through the Bots side.
**Why it matters:** webui users set this in Settings today. On Hermes it exists only in the Bots-side Profile editor, so a Sessions-only user can't find it once webui is gone.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). **Sunset blocker: run it early.** Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
`WebuiServerSettings.swift:99-110` has a Default Model row that saves through `POST /api/default-model`. `hermesSections` (`SettingsServerPage.swift:142-212`) has none. The only Hermes control is the Bots editor's row (`BotProfileEditorView.swift:124-127`), reached from the Bots inbox or a Bot Chat. The Sessions-side composer writes a session-only model.

## Plan
- **Row:** add a "Default Model" link as the first row of the API Keys / Plugins / Connected Apps section (`SettingsServerPage.swift:191-211`). It opens a new page, `HermesDefaultModelView`.
- **Page:** a `ServerProfileRow` at the top (`SettingsRows.swift:14-34`, the pattern `APIKeysView.swift:46-51` uses). Below it, the Profile's current model, which opens `ModelPickerSheet`.
- **Picker setup:** add `static let hermesProfileDefault` next to `.serverDefault` (`ModelPickerConfiguration.swift:55`) with `requiresCustomProviderID: true`; the host needs both a model and a provider.
- **Model:** a new `@MainActor @Observable` class built like `BotProfileEditor` (`BotProfileEditor.swift:115-118` for the injectable `makeWire`, `:142-186` for load). Read the current model with `BotProfileDetails(...).model` (`:21-27`). Save follows `:336-357` and `:373-383`; reply handling follows `:404-411` (`applied.model`, `confirm_required`). Reuse the confirmation alert shape from `BotProfileEditorView.swift:82-89`.
- **Starting Profile:** Archived's rule at `ArchivedSessionsViewModel.swift:291-301` (`profiles.list`, `currentProfile()`, `HermesProfilePreference.resolve` at `HermesChatSettings.swift:53`). Move that function into `HermesProfilePreference` and call it from both screens rather than copying it.
- **Live list:** show the cached list first, then refresh once in the background and replace the list if that read succeeds.

## Contract
- **Current model:** `profiles.describe {name}` (`HermesCall.swift:602`; host `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py:349`).
- **Model list:** `model.options {profile, refresh}`. Add `refresh: Bool = false` to `.profileModelOptions` (`HermesCall.swift:244`, params `:758`) and send `"refresh": true` only when true. Host: `methods_complete.py:319-331`, `inventory.py:227-249`. `.profileModelOptions` already fails only itself on a timeout (`HermesGateway.swift:621`).
- **Save:** `profiles.configure {name, model, provider[, confirm_expensive_model]}` (`HermesCall.swift:1000-1006`; host `methods_profiles.py:386`, `_configure_model` `:658-677`).
- **Live check, 2026-11-12, host 0.23.1:** `model.options` with `refresh: true` answered in about 2 s with the same shape as the cached read (`providers[]` with `slug`, `name`, `models`, `is_current`, `authenticated` and more).

## Acceptance
- Picking a model for Profile "work" makes a new session in "work" start on it, and the Bots editor shows the same value.
- With two servers configured, setting it on one never changes the other's page.
- An expensive model asks for confirmation; Cancel leaves the old model in place.
- The host has no "unset": the way back is to pick the earlier model again.

## Tests
- `HermesRequestTests` (near `:123`): `.profileModelOptions(profile:, refresh: true)` sends `refresh: true`.
- New `HermesDefaultModelTests`, with a fake wire copied from `BotProfileEditorTests.swift:397`: picking a model sends `profiles.configure` with `model` and `provider` for the selected Profile.

## Decisions
- **Which Profile the page starts on:** the Sessions side's pick for that server, since that is where new sessions open.
- **Changing the Profile on this page** does not change the Sessions pick.
- **Favorites in the picker:** not in this issue.
- **A custom model** needs a provider, as in the Bots editor.

## Mocks
Not required. The page is built from existing rows and the shared model picker (owner waived mocks for reused UI, 2026-11-12).

## Blockers
None.

## Outside reach
None. Tests use a fake wire. Do not write a Profile's model on the live host; if a live check is needed, use the `hermex-fixtures` Profile and restore its model.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Settings only. No share extension, Live Activity, App Intents or deep links.
- **New files:** `HermesDefaultModelView.swift` (view and model) and `HermesDefaultModelTests.swift`, both added to `project.pbxproj`.
- **Strings:** "Default Model" exists. New: a footer such as "New sessions in this Profile start on this model."

title: fix(sessions): start a new Hermes chat in the selected project's folder
body:
**What the user gets:** New Session on a Hermes server starts in the project they have selected, as New Chat does on webui.
**Why it matters:** today it ignores the selected project and starts in the Profile's default folder, so the new chat lands outside the lane the user was looking at.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). **Sunset blocker: run it early.** Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
`openNewSession` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:629-633`) builds `.new(profile: profile)` with no folder, though `.new(profile:cwd:)` exists and each lane carries its folder (`ProjectSummary.hermes.folder`, `HermesProjects.swift:29`). webui passes the selected project (`SessionListView.swift:1554-1555`).

## Plan
- Add `SessionListViewModel.hermesNewSessionFolder(lane: String?) -> String?`. It returns `projects.first { $0.projectId == lane }?.hermes?.folder`, and nil while `hermesShowsAllProfiles` is on.
  - The guard matters: `readHermesProjects` is skipped in All Profiles (`SessionListViewModel.swift:1981`), old lanes stay in `projects`, and `selectedProjectID` isn't cleared (`HermesSessionListView.swift:360-365`).
- In `openNewSession`, build `.new(profile:cwd:)` with that folder when `showsProjects` is on.
- Every in-app entry point goes through `openNewSession`: the toolbar button (`:620-623`, both chromes at `:458` and `:600`) and ⌘N (`:639-640`).
- Shortcuts, shares and App Intents do **not** inherit the lane, matching the webui rule at `SessionListView.swift:1551-1553`: `openPendingNewChat` (`:904-906`), `openPendingShare` (`:920-922`), `HermexAppIntents.swift:315`.

## Contract
`session.create {profile, source: "gui", cwd}`, which the app already sends for `/clear` (`HermesCall.swift:143`, `:654-658`; `ChatViewModel.swift:6321-6327`). Host: `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:479` and `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py:236-262`. A folder the host can't find falls back to the Profile default with no error.

## Acceptance
- Select lane "Launch", tap New Session, send: the chat works in that lane's folder and the row lands in the lane.
- Tap "All" and New Session uses the Profile default again.
- All Profiles ignores any lane.
- A second server's lanes never apply.

## Tests
`HermesSessionListTests`, using the `projectTree` pattern at `:492-495`: the folder for `p_1` is `/launch`; after `showAllHermesProfiles()` it is nil. Request encoding is already covered (`HermesRequestTests.swift:58`).

## Decisions
- **An automatic (per-repository) lane passes its folder too**; its sessions already live there.
- **No lane selected:** `cwd` stays nil and the host picks the Profile's default folder, as today.
- **Intents and shares don't inherit the lane.**

## Mocks
Not required. No visible UI change.

## Blockers
None.

## Outside reach
None.

## Surfaces
- iPhone, iPad and the hardware keyboard (⌘N). Not App Intents, the share extension, Live Activity or deep links.
- **New files:** none. **Strings:** none.

title: feat(settings): Message Count, Workspace and Clear Offline Cache on a Hermes server's page
body:
**What the user gets:** the Message Count and Workspace switches and Clear Offline Cache on a Hermes server's Settings page.
**Why it matters:** all three exist only on the webui server page. The Hermes session list already honors the two switches, so once webui is gone nobody could change them, and the only way to clear the cache would be signing out.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). **Sunset blocker: run it early.** Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39`; re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
- The Message Count and Workspace toggles live at `WebuiServerSettings.swift:63-69` (`@AppStorage` at `:11-12`). `HermesSessionListView.swift:43-44` reads the same keys, but `hermesSections` (`SettingsServerPage.swift:142-212`) has no rows for them.
- The Offline Data section is at `WebuiServerSettings.swift:132-147`. The Hermes cache is cleared only by Sign Out or Remove (`SettingsServerPage.swift:122`, `:302`).

## Plan
- **Toggles:** move the two toggles and their `@AppStorage` into a shared `SessionRowDisplayToggles` view in `SettingsRows.swift`. Use it in the webui section and in the Hermes Sessions section (`SettingsServerPage.swift:178-186`).
- **Cache section:** move the Offline Data section, its alert (`WebuiServerSettings.swift:349-358`) and `clearOfflineCache` (`WebuiServerSettingsModel.swift:257-274`) into a shared `OfflineDataSection(server:)` in `SettingsRows.swift`. It holds its own `@State` and `@Environment(\.modelContext)`.
- Attach the alert to the button, not the Section: the comment at `WebuiServerSettings.swift:4-6` warns that Section-level modifiers run once per row.
- **Placement:** add `OfflineDataSection` after the API Keys section, inside the `if let hermesConnection` block at `SettingsServerPage.swift:191`. Delete the webui model's cache properties (`WebuiServerSettingsModel.swift:29-31`).
- No new cache logic: `CacheStore.clearCache` already covers Hermes rows and stops in-flight Hermes chat writes first (`CacheStore.swift:274`, `CacheStore+Hermes.swift:396`).

## Contract
Client-only. It calls `CacheStore.clearCache`, `BotHistoryCache.remove(server:)` (`BotHistoryCache.swift:213`) and `BotRosterCache.remove(server:)` (`:293`).

## Acceptance
- Turning Message Count or Workspace off hides it on Hermes session rows; turning it on restores it. The switches stay app-wide, as today.
- With servers A and B configured, clearing A empties A's offline list and Bot history and leaves B's cache alone. Cleared data refills on the next online load.

## Tests
One: in `CacheStoreTests` (next to `:718`), clearing through the shared helper removes A's roster and history and keeps B's. The toggles need no test.

## Decisions
- **No live Status row** on the Hermes page; the connection line covers it.
- **Clear Offline Cache does not drop push pairing or drafts**; it keeps today's webui behavior.

## Mocks
Not required. Existing rows move as they are (owner waived mocks for reused UI, 2026-11-12).

## Blockers
None. It edits the same Sessions section of `SettingsServerPage.swift` as the session sources issue; whichever lands second rebases.

## Outside reach
None.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Settings only.
- **New files:** none. **Strings:** existing ones move with the code.

title: fix(chat): run /workspace and /interrupt in a Hermes chat instead of sending them as text
body:
**What the user gets:** `/workspace <path>` and `/interrupt <message>` work in a Hermes chat as they do on webui.
**Why it matters:** neither is a Hermes command, so today both are sent to the agent as literal prompt text. A webui user who types them after the sunset gets a confused reply instead of a folder move or a stop-and-send.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). **Sunset blocker: run it early.** Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
`SlashCommandCatalog.swift:223-225` lists the commands Hermex owns in a Hermes chat. `workspace` and `interrupt` are missing and the host has no command by either name (`hermes_cli/commands.py`), so `route` returns `.text` and the line goes to the agent. Neither shows in the `/` panel. The folder chip and holding Send for "Stop and send" already do the same work.

## Plan
- `SlashCommandCatalog.swift:223-225`: add `"workspace"` and `"interrupt"` to `hermesCommands` and update the doc comment at `:216-222`. With `workspace` in the list, `scope.command(named:)` finds it, so the `/workspace ` argument list loads Hermes folders through `ChatComposerView.swift:1360-1361` → `loadWorkspaceSuggestions` (`ChatViewModel.swift:1423-1426`).
- `ChatViewModel.swift:4741`: when `hermesTurn != nil`, call `selectWorkspacePath(path)`, which leads to `selectHermesFolder` (`:1594-1602`).
  - `pendingHermesFolder` set: return `.executed(nil)`; the confirm alert at `ChatView.swift:1530-1546` shows.
  - Moved, or the same folder: `.executed(nil)`.
  - Any other failure: `notDelivered(composerConfigurationErrorMessage)`.
- `ChatViewModel.swift:4354`: when `hermesTurn` is set, return `submitHermesStreamingMessage(args, behavior: .interrupt, to:)` (`:3671-3683`).

## Contract
- **Folder move:** `session.workspace.move {session_key, cwd, profile}` (`HermesCall.swift:685-686`; host `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:1096`). On a canonical host it is `session.mutate` workspace (`HermesCall.swift:345`; host `tui_gateway/contracts/canonical.py:111`). Both already ship behind the folder chip.
- **Interrupt:** `session.redirect {session_id, text}` (`BotPromptMode.swift:38`; host `tui_gateway/methods_session_interrupt.py:174`). With nothing running it is a plain send.

## Acceptance
- In a chat that has run, `/workspace /x` shows the existing "Move to x?" confirm. Cancel keeps the folder; Move moves it.
- A missing folder shows the existing "can't find the folder" message and keeps the draft.
- Mid-run, `/workspace` says to wait, as the folder chip does.
- `/interrupt msg` mid-run stops the turn and sends `msg`. Staged files stay staged, as with Stop and send.
- Both commands appear in the `/` panel.

## Tests
- `HermesSlashCommandTests.testANameRoutesToTheAppTheHoldTheSkillTheHostOrText`: add the two `.appOwned` asserts.
- One test following `HermesChatAttachmentTests.swift:262-279`: during a running turn, `runHermesSlashCommand("/interrupt Stop")` writes `session.redirect`.

## Decisions
- **`/workspace` in a Bot Chat:** allowed, matching the folder chip.
- No new copy: every message is an existing string.

## Mocks
Not required. No new UI.

## Blockers
None.

## Outside reach
None.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad composer, including hardware Return. No share extension, Live Activity, App Intents or deep links.
- **New files:** none. **Strings:** none.

title: feat(sessions): show where a Hermes session came from and hide CLI and messaging sessions
body:
**What the user gets:** Hermes session rows say where a chat came from (CLI, Telegram, Discord and so on), and one switch per server hides CLI and messaging sessions.
**Why it matters:** webui shows the chip and has the switch. On Hermes those sessions are always listed and look the same as chats started in Hermex.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
- Hermes rows set only `sessionSource: source` (`HermesSessionPage.swift:128`), and `sourceDisplayLabel` (`Session.swift:599-631`) needs webui-only fields, so a Hermes row never shows a chip.
- The Hermes server page has only Archived and Cron under Sessions (`SettingsServerPage.swift:178-186`). The list uses `.showAll` plus cron (`HermesSessionListView.swift:665-666`).

## Contract
Client-only. **The phone filters, not the host.**
- `GET /api/sessions` returns every column, `created_source` included (`hermes_state_sessions.py:1085-1087`, `hermes_state_common.py:471-472`).
- `source` is a platform from `gateway/config.py:217-240` or a label: `cron`, `api_server`, `webhook`, `local`, `unknown`.
- CLI, TUI, ACP and Hermex chats are all stored as `source: "local"`, with the real creator in `created_source`: `cli`, `tui`, `acp` or `desktop`. Hermex's own `gui` sessions become `desktop` (`gateway/session_policy.py:86-108`).
- The host's `exclude_sources` matches only the raw `source` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py:182-226`), so it can't hide CLI chats without hiding Hermex's own.
- Platforms: `telegram`, `discord`, `whatsapp`, `whatsapp_cloud`, `slack`, `signal`, `mattermost`, `matrix`, `email`, `sms`, `dingtalk`, `msgraph_webhook`, `feishu`, `wecom`, `wecom_callback`, `weixin`, `bluebubbles`, `qqbot`, `relay`, plus plugin names.

## Plan
- Decode `created_source` in `HermesSessionRow` (`HermesSessionPage.swift:38-116`), tolerantly.
- In `summary` (`:123-133`), set `sessionSource` to `created_source` when `source == "local"`. The offline cache already keeps `sessionSource` (`CacheStore.swift:376`).
- Add a `HermesSessionSource` mapping in `Models/Session.swift`. A chip shows for `cli`, `tui`, `acp`, every platform, `api_server`, `webhook` and unknown client labels. No chip for `desktop`, `gui`, `local`, `unknown`, `fork`, `cron` or empty.
- Point `sourceDisplayLabel` (`Session.swift:599`) at the mapping for Hermes rows. Leave `requiresExternalImport` (`:586`) alone, or Duplicate disappears.
- `AutomatedSessionVisibility.shows` (`:734`): a Hermes row with a chip hides when `showsCli` is off.
- The list sets `automated.showsCli` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:665-666`) from a per-server `@AppStorage`. Reuse `SessionRowDisplaySettings.showCliSessionsKey(for:)` (`SessionRowView.swift:622-643`).
- Add a toggle beside `CronSessionsToggle` (`SettingsServerPage.swift:178-186`, `SettingsRows.swift:325`).

## Acceptance
- CLI and Telegram rows show chips. Chats started in Hermex don't.
- Switch off: those rows leave the list, search, Needs-you and ⌘1-9. Switch on: they return.
- A second server is unaffected.
- A deep link or push to a hidden session still opens it.

## Tests
- `SessionIdentityTests`, after `:78`: `local` + `cli` → "CLI", `telegram` → "Telegram", `local` + `desktop` → nil.
- `HermesSessionListTests`: with the switch off, the grouped list drops the `cli` and `telegram` rows.

## Decisions
- **One switch, on by default**, so nothing disappears for existing users. No Subagent Sessions switch (owner, #1668).
- **`api_server` and `webhook` rows hide with the switch too**, so a chip always means the row can be hidden.
- **A CLI session found only by search shows no chip**: search results carry no `created_source`. Accepted.
- **Chip labels** are the source's name shown as written (brand names), as on webui.

## Mocks
Not required. The chip and the toggle row reuse webui's (owner waived mocks for reused UI, 2026-11-12).

## Blockers
None. It edits the same Sessions section of `SettingsServerPage.swift` as the Settings rows issue; whichever lands second rebases.

## Outside reach
None. Reading `/api/sessions` on the live host to confirm `created_source` is fine.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad session list, Settings, and the offline cache.
- **New files:** none expected. **Strings:** "CLI and Messaging Sessions".

title: feat(sessions): copy a deeplink to a Hermes session
body:
**What the user gets:** Copy Deeplink on a Hermes session's Export menu, as webui sessions have.
**Why it matters:** the item is hidden for Hermes rows even though the app already opens Hermes session links.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39`; re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
`SessionRowActionPolicy.deepLinkURL` (`SessionListComponents.swift:233-246`) returns nil when `session.hermes != nil`. `HermesDeepLink.sessionURL(for:)` (`HermesDeepLink.swift:139`) already builds the link that Live Activities and run-ended alerts use.

## Plan
- `SessionListComponents.swift:233-246`: `deepLinkURL` gains a `server: URL` parameter.
  - A Hermes row that isn't a Bot Chat returns `HermesDeepLink.sessionURL(for: HermesSessionDestination(server:, profile: session.profile, key: sessionId))`.
  - A webui row is unchanged.
  - A Bot Chat row gets no link, because that row opens its bot.
- `SessionListViewModel.swift:165`: make `server` readable from outside (`let server`).
- `SessionRowContextMenu` (`:1346`) takes a `server` value, passed in at `:1082` and used at `:1465`.
- Update the comment at `SessionListComponents.swift:183-185`.
- Every Hermes row carries a Profile (`HermesSessionPage.swift:123-128`).
- There is no in-chat session menu to change.

## Contract
Client-only. Links are parsed by `HermesSessionLookup.swift` `init?(url:)` and opened through `ContentView.swift:156` (`handleOpenURL`).

## Acceptance
- Export → Copy Deeplink on a Hermes row copies a `hermes-agent://session?server=…&profile=…&id=…` link. Opening it opens that session on that server.
- With two servers configured, a link for the other server switches servers first.
- The item is hidden for a Bot Chat, while showing cached data, and while the row is changing.

## Tests
Rewrite `SessionListMutationTests.testAHermesRowOffersItsActionsButNotHTMLOrDeeplink` (`:2819`): a Hermes row's link parses back to `HermesSessionDestination(server:, profile: "default", key:)`, and a Bot Chat row's link is nil.

## Decisions
- **No Copy Link in the Chat settings sheet**; that would be new UI.

## Mocks
Not required. An existing menu item appears on more rows.

## Blockers
None.

## Outside reach
None.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad session list menu, wherever the shared row is used (`SessionListComponents.swift:933`, `:1192`, `:1256`, `:1298`). The link comes back in through deep links.
- **New files:** none. **Strings:** none.

title: feat(chat): attach any file type in a Hermes chat
body:
**What the user gets:** any file type can be attached in a Hermes chat, including video and files with no known type.
**Why it matters:** webui accepts any file. On Hermes the app refuses everything outside a short list with "This attachment type is not supported", though the host accepts them.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
`BotAttachmentUpload.swift:55-58` allows only images, PDF, text, audio, json/yaml/csv, Office files and zip. The limit is the app's alone.

## Contract
- **Send:** `file.attach {session_id, name, data_url}` (`HermesCall.swift:216`, `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:710-716`).
- **What the host enforces** (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:1117-1137`, `tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py:278-353`): a path or a data URL is required (error 4015). Any media type is accepted (`:312-313`). Inline bytes are capped at 256 MiB (`:20`, `:316`). The name is cleaned of control characters and leading or trailing dots (`:228-231`), and a clash gets a `-2` suffix (`:329-342`). There is no type, extension or count check.
- **Images** still go through `/api/chat/image-upload`: `image/*` only, at most 25 MB, and only PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP or WebP by magic bytes (`hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:532`, `:558-563`).
- **Live check, 2026-11-12, host 0.23.1:** `file.attach` answered `attached: true` for `probe.mp4` (`video/mp4`) and for `probe.xyz` (`application/octet-stream`) in a disposable hidden session.

## Plan
- `BotAttachmentUpload.swift:35`: a missing type becomes `.data`.
- `:55-58`: delete the allowlist.
- Delete the `.type` failure at `:6` and `:10`, and its case at `HermesSessionListView.swift:1174-1175`.
- Update the doc comment at `:29-32`.
- Keep every size rule client-side: 25 MB per file and 50 MB in total (the whole file travels base64 in one frame), 8 files, images re-encoded to PNG or JPEG, and the share extension's 20 MB and 10 files (`SharedDraftStore.swift:231-232`).

## Acceptance
- A `.mov`, a `.exe` and a file with no extension each stage and send as an `@file:` reference.
- A file over a size cap still shows the limit message.
- The same files shared in from another app through the share extension reach the Hermes chat.

## Tests
- Rewrite `BotAttachmentSendingTests.testOnlySupportedTypesArePrepared`: `tool.exe` prepares as `application/octet-stream`.
- `SharedDraftStoreTests.swift:820-833` uses `.type` as its failure; switch it to an oversized file and `.limit`.

## Decisions
- **An image the encoder can't read** (an SVG, for example) is sent as a plain file instead of failing as unreadable.
- **Size and count caps do not change.**

## Mocks
Not required. No new UI; two strings are removed.

## Blockers
None.

## Outside reach
None. The live check above is done; tests use the existing fakes.

## Surfaces
- Composer (Files, paste), Bot Chat, the share extension and Shortcuts hand-off (`HermesSessionListView.swift:1111-1150`), and restored drafts.
- **New files:** none. **Strings:** the "attachment type is not supported" strings leave the catalog.

title: feat(kanban): Only Mine, bulk Scheduled and Review, and Complete outside Review on Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** on a Hermes Kanban Board: the Only Mine filter, Bulk Actions to Scheduled and Review, and Complete on a Card that isn't in Review.
**Why it matters:** webui offers all three. On Hermes, Complete is Review-only, so the Bulk Action to Done shows every other Card as failed.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable. Three small parts in one PR.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers and the Kanban plugin routes before editing. `docs/agents/kanban.md` owns the contract; update the lines named below.

## Part A: Only Mine

**Problem.** `KanbanFeatureState.swift:661-663` offers Only Mine on webui only. The host's `/board` has no assignee filter (`kanban.md:92`).

**Plan**
- `HermesKanbanClient.swift:21-22`: add `var mine: String? = nil`.
- `HermesKanbanClient.swift:51`: `let assignee = (request.onlyMine ? mine : request.assignee).flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }`. The filter runs in the app, as the Assigned Profile filter already does.
- `APIClient+Kanban.swift:13-16`: add `var offersOnlyMine: Bool { get }`, defaulting to `true` in the extension at `:41-42`; Hermes returns `mine != nil`.
- `KanbanFeatureState.swift:661-663`: return `client.offersOnlyMine`.
- `KanbanLabView.swift:2444-2451`: `init(server:hermes:mine:)`. `HermesSessionListView.swift:510` and `:541` pass `mine: profile`.

**Acceptance.** Filters shows Only Mine. Turning it on shows only Cards assigned to the Sessions side's listed Profile and disables the Assigned Profile picker. Clear Filters turns it off. No `only_mine` query is ever sent.

**Test.** In `HermesKanbanClientTests`, modelled on `testFiltersTheHostCannotApplyRunOnTheClient` (`:201`): with `mine: "reviewer"` and `onlyMine: true`, `offersOnlyMine` is true, the cards are the reviewer's, and the request carries no `only_mine`.

## Part B: Bulk Action to Scheduled and Review

**Problem.** `Kanban.swift:1203` hides `todo`, `scheduled` and `review` from the Hermes bulk status list. On webui, too, only Bulk Actions offer Scheduled and Review; the single-card Move menu offers Triage, To Do and Ready on both kinds and stays as it is.

**Plan**
- `Kanban.swift:1203`: the Hermes `unofferedStatuses` becomes `["running", "todo"]`; fix the comment at `:1201` and the one at `KanbanFeatureState.swift:747-748`. Its only consumer is `bulkStatusOptions` (`KanbanFeatureState.swift:749-751`).
- No change to the outcome check: `accepts` (`Kanban.swift:1228-1230`) already passes a Card that lands where asked.

**Contract.** `POST /api/plugins/kanban/tasks/bulk?board=` with `{ids, status: "review" | "scheduled"}` (`HermesKanbanClient.swift:159-168`). Host: `BulkTaskBody` (`plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py:554-561`), `_bulk_apply_one` (`:830-838`), `_STATUS_HANDLERS` (`:594-603`).
- `review` calls `request_review(…, force=True)`: only from `running` or `ready`, and only when parents are done (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:3264`, `:3297-3298`, `:3354`).
- `scheduled` calls `schedule_task`: from `todo`, `ready`, `running` or `blocked` (`kanban_db.py:3865-3891`). There is no schedule time and no required field.
- The reply is 200 with per-Card `{ok, error}`; Hermex judges each Card by reading it again (`KanbanFeatureState.swift:1702-1725`).

**Acceptance.** Change Status lists Triage, Scheduled, Ready, Blocked, Review and Done. Ready or Running Cards land in Review; others show as failed with Retry and stay where they were.

**Tests.** Update `HermesKanbanClientTests.swift:288` to the six statuses. New, modelled on `testBulkShowsTheCardsTheHostRefused` (`:408`): bulk `review` on a Ready and a Triage Card sends `{"ids":…,"status":"review"}` and reports one success and one failed id.

## Part C: Complete from outside Review, and bulk Done

**Problem.** `Kanban.swift:1215-1222` offers Complete only from Review on Hermes. The host completes a Ready, Running or Blocked Card when the request carries a result.

**Contract**
- `PATCH /api/plugins/kanban/tasks/{id}?board=` with `{"status":"done","result":"<note>"}`. `UpdateTaskBody` takes `result` and `summary` (`plugin_api.py:533-545`) and calls `complete_task(result=, summary=, force=True)` (`:595-596`).
- Accepted from `running`, `ready`, `blocked` and `review` (`kanban_db.py:2646`, `:2706`). Review needs no note.
- With no note the host answers 400, "completion blocked: <id> has no result or summary evidence" (`kanban_db.py:2595-2604`, `:2777-2808`; mapped at `plugin_api.py:645-646`). If parents aren't done it answers 409 naming them (`:655`, `:658-668`).
- Bulk: `{ids, status:"done", result}`; `BulkTaskBody.result` exists (`:560`).

**Plan**
- `Kanban.swift:1215-1222`: Hermes offers Complete for `ready`, `running`, `blocked` and `review`. Add `completionNeedsResult(from:)`, true on Hermes for anything but Review.
- `Kanban.swift:98-106`: `KanbanCardStatusRequest` gains `var result: String? = nil`. `HermesKanbanClient.swift:124-130` adds `body["result"]` when set. webui never sends it.
- `KanbanFeatureState.swift:206-214`: add `case complete(String?)`. `:796-804`: `completeCard(_:result:confirmingRunningExit:)` writes through a `write:` closure, the way Block does at `:816-834`. Fix the switches at `:910-911` and `:949`, and the retries at `KanbanLabView.swift:1367` and `KanbanCardDetailView.swift:468`.
- **Prompt:** in each view's `request()` (`KanbanLabView.swift:1307-1313`, `KanbanCardDetailView.swift:432-437`), a `.complete` that needs a note opens one text-field alert in place of the "Leave Running?" alert. Copy the "Rename group" pattern at `BotsInboxView.swift:707-718`.
- **Bulk Done:** `Kanban.swift:3-8` adds `case complete(result: String)`, handled at `APIClient+Kanban.swift:372`, `HermesKanbanClient.swift:161` and `KanbanFeatureState.swift:1798-1824`. In the bulk sheet (`KanbanLabView.swift:1990-2000`), when Done is picked and any selected Card isn't in Review, show a "What was done?" field; Change Status stays disabled while it is blank. Retry keeps the note.

**Acceptance.** Complete appears on Ready, Running and Blocked Cards. A non-blank note moves the Card to Done. A host 400 or 409 shows "Update failed" with the host's words and the Card goes back. Review still completes with no prompt. Bulk Done with a note completes non-Review Cards.

**Tests.** In `HermesKanbanClientTests`: update `:293` to `[false,false,true,true,true,false]`; replace `:295-297` so `completeCard(ready, result: "Shipped")` sends `{"status":"done","result":"Shipped"}` and ends `.succeeded`; one bulk `.complete(result:)` case asserting `result` in the body.

## Decisions
- **"Mine" is the Sessions side's listed Profile**, the one New Session opens in (`HermesSessionListView.swift:559-561`); Tasks, Skills and Memory scope to the same value. With no Profile known, Only Mine is not offered. It is captured when Kanban opens.
- **Single-card Move is unchanged.** Scheduled and Review are bulk destinations only, as on webui.
- **No workspace path on create and no move to To Do** (owner, #1668).
- **Send `result`, not `summary`**: it is stored on the Card and `summary` defaults to it.
- **Bulk Review or Scheduled on a Running Card** force-clears its claim with no per-Card warning, as Blocked already does.
- **Copy for the Complete prompt** (recommended; the owner may change it): title "Complete Card?"; placeholder "What was done?"; message "Hermes saves this as the Card's result."; for a Running Card add "Leaving Running may clear the Card's claim and worker state."; buttons Cancel and Complete, with Complete disabled while the note is blank.

## Mocks
Not required. The prompt is a system text-field alert and the bulk field reuses the sheet's existing rows (owner waived mocks for reused UI, 2026-11-12).

## Blockers
None.

## Outside reach
None. Tests use `HermesKanbanClientTests`' fake host. Any live check uses a disposable Board on `scripts/local-hermes`, never the maintainer's Boards.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Kanban (pushed screen and regular-width detail). Nothing else.
- **Docs:** `docs/agents/kanban.md:98`, `:101`, `:115-117`, `:124-126` and `:136-137` become wrong; update them in this PR.
- **New files:** none. **Strings:** the prompt title, placeholder, two messages and "Complete". "Only Mine" exists.

title: feat(usage): a 24-hour window in Usage on Hermes
body:
**What the user gets:** a one-day window in Usage on a Hermes server, next to 7, 30 and 90 days.
**Why it matters:** webui has Today. Hermes starts at 7 days, so there is no way to see what the last day cost.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers before editing.

## Problem
`InsightsFeatures.hermes` (`InsightsViewModel.swift:34`) offers only `.last7Days`, `.last30Days` and `.last90Days`.

## Contract
- The same three reads with `days=1`; no new route. `days` is a whole number from 1 to 365 (`hermes_cli/web_routers/analytics.py:149-153`).
- `days=1` is a **rolling 24 hours**, not midnight to now: `/api/analytics/usage` uses `cutoff = time.time() - days*86400` (`analytics.py:83-86`), with `totals` over that cutoff (`:120-129`). `/api/analytics/models` (`:308-312`) and `insights.get` (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:1121-1123`) use the same cutoff.
- `daily` rows are grouped by the host's local date (`:88-101`), so a 24-hour window spans one or two of them. No reply carries the host's time zone, and there is no hourly data.

## Plan
- `InsightsViewModel.swift:41-98`: add `case last24Hours`, titled "24 hours", with `serverDays` 1 and `isHourly` false. Put it in the rolling branch of `contains` (`:93`).
- `:30`: webui gets the explicit list `[.today, .last7Days, .last30Days, .last90Days]`.
