title: feat(hermes): small parity polish for the session list, chat and Shortcuts
body:
**What the user gets:** six small things webui has that a Hermes server lacks: skill suggestions mid-sentence, Approval and Input badges, inline images from relative paths, a New Chat button on the iPad empty state, a count on Archived, and each Profile's model in the pickers.
**Why it matters:** each is small, but together they are what makes the Hermes side feel less finished than the webui side it replaces.
**Cost:** Medium in total; simulator-testable. One PR, one commit per part.

> Child of #1668 (webui parity before the sunset). Plan drafted 2026-11-12 against `master` @ `08c2d3e39` and the host pin `3b421578` (0.23.1); re-verify line numbers before editing. The parts are independent: if one turns out harder than planned, ship the others and say which was left.

## Part A: skill suggestions mid-sentence

**Problem.** In a Hermes chat the `/` panel opens only at the start of the draft (`ChatComposerView.swift:472-475`); webui also offers skills after other text (`:503-510`).

**Plan**
- `ChatComposerView.swift:472-475`: drop the `startsDraft` guard; keep the host-argument check only at the start of the draft. `ComposerSlashTrigger.isTrigger` already ends a mid-sentence trigger at the first space, and `SlashCommandAutocompleteView.swift:98-104` already ranks skills only.
- `ChatView.swift:658`: on Hermes pass `hasLoadedSkillSuggestions: true`; the catalog is read on connect (`HermesSlashCommands.swift:21`, `:250`), so `:503-508` closes the panel unless a skill matches.
- Move the `slashQuery` gate into a static function in `ComposerSlashTrigger.swift` so it can be tested.
- Feed the Hermes skills into `composerChipCatalog` too, so a sent `/skill` draws as a chip in the bubble (`MessageBubbleView.swift:467`, `ChatView.swift:2560`). Today only the webui load fills it (`ChatViewModel.swift:5076-5080`); composer chips already work on Hermes.

**Contract.** Client-only; the data comes from `commands.catalog`.

**Acceptance.** "use /dem" offers `demo-skill`, and picking it replaces only the `/dem` word with a chip. "/tmp" with no matching skill shows no panel. A `/` at the start of the draft behaves as today.

**Tests.** `ComposerSlashTriggerTests`: with Hermes scope, a mid-sentence word matching a skill opens the panel and one matching nothing stays closed.

## Part B: Approval and Input badges

**Problem.** `hermesStates` maps every `waiting` row to `.input` (`HermesSessionPage.swift:337-348`), so a Hermes row never shows "Approval".

**Plan**
- Add `HermesCall.approvalPending(sessionID:)` → `"approval.pending"` with `{session_id}`, in the switches near `HermesCall.swift:539`, `:711` and `:979`.
- In `readHermesStatuses` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:2345-2368`), after `hermesStates`, call it once per listed `waiting` item, in parallel, under the same `current()` guard. Use the item's **runtime `id`, not `session_key`**.
- Non-empty `approvals` → `.approval`. A failed call keeps `.approval` if that was the last state, otherwise `.input` (the webui rule, `:818-836`). On `-32601`, stop asking for that connection.
- `:391` must also accept `.approval`, or approval rows drop out of Needs-you.

**Contract.** `approval.pending {session_id}` → `{approvals: [PendingApproval]}`; handler `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:1312-1318`, which looks the session up in the process-wide registry (`tui_gateway/session_registry.py:304-320`). **Live check, 2026-11-12, host 0.23.1:** a runtime id answers `{approvals: []}`; a stored id answers 4001 "session not found".

**Acceptance.** A row waiting on a command shows "Approval"; a clarify question shows "Input"; both appear in Needs-you. Once answered, the badge clears.

**Tests.** `HermesSessionListTests` (`live` helper `:985`; extend the wire's `call` at `:1391-1407`): one waiting row with an approval and one without → `.approval` and `.input`. Request encoding in `HermesRequestTests`.

## Part C: inline images from a relative path

**Problem.** `ChatView.swift:2562` takes the workspace root from `session.workspace`, which is nil for a Hermes chat (`:597-598`), so `![chart](out/chart.png)` stays a broken Markdown image.

**Plan**
- Use `isHermesSession ? (viewModel.hermesWorkspace?.cwd ?? hermesRowWorkspace) : session.workspace` (`hermesWorkspace` at `ChatViewModel.swift:1963`, `hermesRowWorkspace` at `ChatView.swift:552`). The row's folder is the fallback so cached transcripts render before the host reports the live folder.
- Put the root on the view model as `transcriptWorkspaceRoot` next to `:1963`, so it can be tested.
- Don't limit it to a local terminal backend: with a session id, `/api/fs/download` serves SSH workspaces and maps Docker paths (`hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:1356-1378`, `:1145-1167`). Anything it can't find shows the existing "unavailable" chip (`TranscriptMediaView.swift:629`).

**Contract.** Client-only; it reuses `/api/fs/download` through `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:743-748`.

**Acceptance.** A reply with `![chart](out/chart.png)` shows an inline thumbnail that opens in the lightbox. A missing file shows the unavailable chip. webui chats behave as before.

**Tests.** One in `HermesChatAttachmentTests`, following `testTheWorkspaceFollowsSessionInfoAndReadsOnTheChatsConnection` (`:765`): after `session.info` sets `cwd`, loading the thumbnail for a relative reference sends the joined absolute path plus `session_id`.

## Part D: New Chat button on the iPad empty state

**Plan.** Replace `HermesSessionListView.swift:547-548` with the webui form (`SessionListView.swift:630-637`): `Button("New Chat", action: openNewSession)` in the `.appProminent` style, disabled while `!canOpenNewSession` (`:626`).

**Acceptance.** On iPad with nothing selected, New Chat opens a new session in the listed Profile. Offline or on cached rows the button is disabled.

**Tests.** None; it reuses `openNewSession`.

## Part E: a count on the Archived row

**Plan**
- Add a `BotTransport` method `archivedSessionCount(profile:)`, throwing `.unsupported` by default (`BotProtocol.swift:353`, `:438`); `BotClient` implements it next to `:174`.
- It calls `.sessionList(…, archived: true)` with `limit=0` (add a limit parameter, `HermesREST.swift:539-553`) and returns the page's `total`.
- After `readHermesProjects` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:1981`), when not in All Profiles, set the existing `archivedCount`. Reloads already follow archive and restore.
- `archivedRow` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:765-791`) copies the webui capsule (`SessionListView.swift:950-957`). Hide the row at 0. Show it without a number while the count is unknown, so the way in never disappears.

**Contract.** `GET /api/sessions?profile=P&archived=only&limit=0&exclude_sources=kanban,oneshot,subagent,tool` → `{sessions: [], total: N}` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py:182-242`; `limit` accepts 0 at `:184`).

**Acceptance.** Archiving a session raises the count; Undo lowers it. Zero hides the row. Another Profile or server shows its own count.

**Tests.** `HermesSessionListTests`: a scripted count of 3 → `archivedCount == 3`; All Profiles → nil. `HermesRequestTests` (`:299`): the URL carries `limit=0`.

## Part F: each Profile's model in the pickers

**Plan**
- **List picker:** `readHermesProfiles` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:2237-2248`) also stores `hermesProfileModels[name] = row["model"]`. `profilePicker` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:717-728`) gives each row a second `Text` with the model, shown as written.
- **Shortcuts:** the App Intents process can't sign in, and `/api/status` lists names only (`ProfileEntity.swift:176-184`), so use the cache:
  - add `var model: String? = nil` to `HermesProfileNameCache.Name` (`:335-338`); optional, so older cache entries still decode.
  - add `model` to `BotProfile` (`BotConnection.swift:200`, init `:232`) and save it at `BotInbox.swift:664`.
  - `ProfileEntity(hermesServer:…)` (`:36-41`) shows the subtitle as the Profile name (when titled) and the model, joined by " · ". `sections` (`:117-152`) passes the cached model through.

**Contract.** `profiles.list {include_sessions}`, already sent (`HermesCall.swift:35`, `:601`); rows carry `model`, `provider` and `display_name` (`tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py:282-297`). **Live check, 2026-11-12:** each row carries `model` and `provider`.

**Acceptance.** The list's Profile menu and the Shortcuts picker show each Profile's model. A model changed on the host appears after the next refresh. Two servers stay separate. A Profile with no model shows no subtitle.

**Tests.** `BotInboxTests.testEachRosterReadLeavesTheProfilesNamesForShortcuts` (`:241`): the cache keeps `model`. `AppIntentNewChatInProfileTests` (`:110-130`): the subtitle includes the model.

## Decisions
- **Sent bubbles draw skill chips on Hermes too** (Part A's last step). The owner confirmed composer chips work; this extends them to sent messages. Recommended, one small change.
- **Badges cost one `approval.pending` call per waiting row** (owner accepted, #1668). On a gateway that lacks the method, fall back to Input.
- **Archived count** includes room sessions the Archived screen hides, so it can run slightly high. Accepted.
- **Shortcuts model subtitle** comes from the Bots roster cache only; the Sessions side's read does not write it.
- **Not in this issue** (owner, #1668): Memory modified times and deeply nested skill files.

## Mocks
Not required. Every part reuses an existing webui element (owner waived mocks for reused UI, 2026-11-12).

## Blockers
None. Part D's button starts in the selected project once the new-chat-in-project issue lands; it needs no code from it.

## Outside reach
None. Before merging Part B, check `approval.pending` against `scripts/local-hermes --gateway` (a canonical gateway).

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad composer, transcript and session list; App Intents and Shortcuts (Part F).
- **New files:** none expected. **Strings:** none new.

title: fix(chat): make the scroll-to-bottom arrow work after a send and mid-fling
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: reported directly by the maintainer.

## What changed

The scroll-to-bottom arrow in a chat stopped working in two cases:

- **After a send.** With "Dismiss keyboard after sending" on, once the reply finished and you scrolled up, tapping the arrow did nothing: no haptic, no scroll. It stayed broken until you opened and closed the composer. On-device probes showed the composer's `GlassEffectContainer` still taking taps over the area the expanded card had covered, after the card collapsed back to the pill. The arrow sits in that area. Turning on Reduce Transparency, which switches the container off, made the arrow work.
- **Mid-fling.** A tap while the transcript was still coasting lost to the scroll view's leftover momentum.

The fix:

- The composer no longer wraps its stack in a glass container. The pill and the card keep their own glass. Without the container, the toolbar row's solid background, which extends up under the card, drew over the card's bottom edge, so the card now draws above the row (`zIndex(1)`).
- The arrow stops any momentum (`stopScrollingAndZooming()`) before running the existing jump.

Most of the `ChatComposerView` diff is re-indentation; `git diff -w` shows the real change.

## How it was tested

- Proved on the iPhone Duo with the maintainer: the failing sequence (new chat, send with auto-dismiss, scroll up, tap the arrow) now jumps to the bottom, a tap mid-fling jumps, and the card's bottom edge no longer clips.
- `scripts/test-sim` on the iPhone 17e, with `ChatScrollPolicyTests`, `ChatVerticalScrollAxisGuardTests`, `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests`, `BotChatPresentationTests` and `ChatComposerSendGateTests`: 81 passed, 0 failed.
- The bug doesn't reproduce on the iPhone 17e or iPhone Duo simulators, so the phone run is the proof. No test was added.

Out of scope: `BotRoomComposerView` uses the same glass container and may have the same bug.

title: fix(sessions): start a new Hermes chat in the selected project's folder
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1671

## What changed

On a Hermes server, New Session ignored the selected project lane and started in the Profile's default folder, so the new chat landed outside the lane the user was looking at.

New Session (toolbar, both chromes) and ⌘N now pass the selected lane's folder as `cwd` to `session.create`, as webui's New Chat does. The folder comes from `SessionListViewModel.hermesNewSessionFolder(lane:)`, which reads this server's own `projects` and returns nil with no lane, with Projects hidden, or in All Profiles (where stale lanes can linger). No new endpoint or field: the app already sends `cwd` for `/clear`, and the host falls back to the Profile default for a folder it can't find.

Decisions applied ([decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1671#issuecomment-6843768315)): automatic per-repository lanes pass their folder too; no lane keeps `cwd` nil; Shortcuts, shares and App Intents don't inherit the lane (matches webui).

title: fix(chat): key unsent new-session drafts by working folder
body:
Found by CodeRabbit on #1681 (https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/pull/1681#discussion_r4559676559) and checked against the code.

**Problem.** `ConversationTarget.draftKey` (`HermesMobile/Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:35`) keys every `.new` target as `.hermesSession(..., key: nil)` and ignores `cwd`. All New Session chats in a Profile share one unsent draft. Before #1681 that didn't matter, because every new chat started in the Profile's default folder; `/clear` chats with a `cwd` already shared it. Now that New Session starts in the selected project's folder, a prompt left unsent in project A shows up in New Session for project B and sends in B's folder.

**Suggested fix.** Add the working folder to the `.new` draft identity (`ChatDraftKey.Context.hermesSession` plus its persisted encoding). Keep the identity of existing nil-folder keys unchanged so saved drafts still load.

Kept out of #1681 because it changes the persisted draft-key format, which is beyond #1671's scope.

title: fix(chat): run /workspace and /interrupt in a Hermes chat instead of sending them as text
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1673

## What changed

In a Hermes chat, `/workspace <path>` and `/interrupt <message>` were sent to the agent as literal text: the host has no command by either name and Hermex didn't own them. Neither showed in the `/` panel.

Both are now Hermex-owned commands in a Hermes chat (`SlashCommandCatalog.hermesCommands`), so they appear in the `/` panel and `/workspace ` completes Hermes folders.
- `/workspace` runs the folder chip's pick (`selectWorkspacePath`): a chat that has run gets the existing "Move to x?" confirm; a refusal (missing folder, mid-run) keeps the draft and shows the existing message.
- `/interrupt` runs Stop and send (`submitHermesStreamingMessage(behavior: .interrupt)`): `session.redirect` mid-run, a plain send when idle; staged files stay staged.

No new endpoints, strings, or UI. Decisions applied: [Uzair, 2026-11-12](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1673#issuecomment-6843769055) — build as written; `/workspace` allowed in a Bot Chat, matching the folder chip.

**Decisions made overnight**
- A stale composer error from an earlier chip action could misreport the command: clear `composerConfigurationErrorMessage` before the pick so only a fresh refusal yields `notDelivered`; same folder is `.executed(nil)` per the issue. (Alternative: leave the old message and compare before/after.)

## How it was tested

- Red on unchanged code: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesSlashCommandTests/testANameRoutesToTheAppTheHoldTheSkillTheHostOrText --only HermesChatAttachmentTests/testInterruptCommandMidRunStopsAndSends --only HermesChatSettingsTests/testWorkspaceCommandPicksTheFolder` → 0 passed, 3 failed (`.text` instead of `.appOwned`; `runHermesSlashCommand` returned nil, i.e. sent as text).

- No live-host writes; the steps below need a disposable session.

## Checklist

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies

3. During a reply, send `/interrupt summarize so far` (on iPad, with hardware Return): the reply stops and the message sends; a staged file stays staged.

title: feat(settings): set a Profile's default model from a Hermes server's Settings
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1670

## What changed

A Hermes server's Settings had no Default Model control; a Profile's starting model could only be set from the Bots-side Profile editor, so a Sessions-only user couldn't find it. This follows [the decision](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/issues/1670#issuecomment-6843767944) as written.

- **Row:** "Default Model" is now the first row of the API Keys / Plugins / Connected Apps section. It opens `HermesDefaultModelView`: a Profile row (starting on the Sessions side's pick for the server, via `HermesProfilePreference.starting`, moved out of Archived and shared) and the Profile's current model from `profiles.describe`.
- **Picker:** the shared `ModelPickerSheet` with a new `.hermesProfileDefault` preset (custom models need a provider; no favorites). The cached `model.options` list shows first, then a `refresh: true` read replaces it.
- **Save:** `profiles.configure {name, model, provider}`, not optimistic. An expensive model shows a confirm alert; Continue resends with `confirm_expensive_model`, Cancel writes nothing. No "unset": the way back is picking the earlier model.
- **Lifecycle:** the page owns its gateway client; leaving mid-reconnect sends no write (dispatch is fenced on the page), backgrounding closes the client and foregrounding reloads, and picks are disabled while the page reloads.

## Linked issue

## What changed

A Hermes chat refused files outside a short type allowlist (a `.exe`, a `.dmg`, a file with no extension), even though the host's `file.attach` accepts any media type.

## Linked issue

Fixes #1674

## What changed

Hermes session rows never showed where a chat came from, and CLI and messaging sessions were always listed, looking just like chats started in Hermex.

- `HermesSessionRow` decodes `created_source` (optional). A `local` row takes it as its `sessionSource`; others keep `source`.
- `sourceDisplayLabel` gives Hermes rows a chip for `cli`, `tui`, `acp`, every messaging platform, `api_server`, `webhook` and other client labels. No chip for Hermex's own chats (`desktop`, `gui`, older `hermex`), `local`, `unknown`, `fork`, `cron` or empty.
- A per-server **CLI and Messaging Sessions** switch in Settings › server › Sessions, on by default, hides every chipped row from the list, search, Needs you and ⌘1-9. Deep links and pushes still open hidden sessions. `requiresExternalImport` is untouched, so Duplicate stays.

- Older Hermex `hermex`-source sessions: no chip (instead of a "Hermex" chip).

title: fix(chat): let the user dismiss a composer error, and clear it on the next edit
body:
**What the user gets:** a chat error above the composer, like a refused `/workspace`, goes away when they edit the draft or tap Dismiss.
**Why it matters:** the maintainer hit this in the #1668 merge walk. After `/workspace /does/not/exist` the red banner never goes away; the only way out is leaving the chat and coming back.
**Cost:** Small. A quick check on the simulator, no phone needed.

## Cause (read at 9b7b9cb, now in master 5f07e0a)

- A refused move sets `composerConfigurationErrorMessage` (`ChatViewModel.swift` ~1640). The `/workspace` handler then copies the same text into `sendErrorMessage` through `notDelivered` (~4801 → 4551), without clearing the original.
- `ChatComposerView` shows `sendErrorMessage`, then falls back to the config error (~1544/1546). A send clears only `sendErrorMessage` (~3376), so the identical config error shows through.
- Typing clears neither: `persistDraftEdit` (`ChatView.swift` ~3426) only clears the steer failure.
- `composerStatus` passes `isDismissible: false`. The only ✕ is hard-wired to the attachment upload error (`onDismissUploadAttachmentError`).
- The config error clears only on the next model, profile, reasoning or folder change, or a new session. The reload that would clear it returns early in Hermes chats (~1221).
- Refused `/model` and failed Hermes chip picks get stuck the same way. The chips fall back to `hermesSettings.controls.errorMessage` (`BotChatControls.swift` ~47).

## Fix

1. **One field, not two.** When the `/workspace` refusal becomes `notDelivered`, move its text into `sendErrorMessage` and nil `composerConfigurationErrorMessage`.
2. **Clear on edit.** Add a guarded `clearComposerErrors()` and call it from `persistDraftEdit` next to `clearSteerFailure()`. It runs on every keystroke, so it writes only when a field is set. It resets `sendErrorMessage`, `composerConfigurationErrorMessage` and the controls' `errorMessage`. Two errors stay, because they describe ongoing state rather than a one-off failure: the unserved-profile "Fix on This Phone" case and the stale-runtime "Copy fix prompt" case.
3. **Dismiss.** Reuse `ComposerStatusView`'s existing ✕ instead of adding a component. Replace `isDismissible` and the upload-only callback with an optional `onDismiss` per status, and label it "Dismiss" for VoiceOver. Turn it on for send, config and upload errors. Visibility already animates through `ChatMotion` with Reduce Motion respected. No timer: an error stays until it's read.

Files: `ChatViewModel.swift`, `ChatComposerView.swift`, `ChatView.swift`, `BotChatControls.swift`.

Test: one focused `ChatViewModel` test. A refused `/workspace` followed by a draft edit leaves no composer error.

## Out of scope

These have the same "no way to dismiss" shape, but the next action already clears each one: Task detail action errors, the Git commit bar, the Bots inbox notice, and room command messages. Kanban's `cardNoticeBanner` ✕ is the pattern to copy if they're picked up later.

Found during the #1668 merge walk.

title: Chat drafts: a persist, attachment admission or deletion can destroy an unreadable drafts file
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Let `ChatDrafts/drafts.json` exist but be unreadable or undecodable (a crash or partial restore can leave such bytes). `ChatDraftFilePersistence.load` logs "Ignoring unreadable persisted chat drafts" and answers `[:]`.
2. Use the app so a persist fires — type in a composer, stage an attachment large enough to trigger retention eviction, or trigger `deleteAttachmentIfUnreferenced`.
3. The store's write path replaces `drafts.json` with the in-memory state, which started empty after the failed read.

### Expected behavior

No write may replace a drafts file the app could not read, from any of the paths that write it. Once the file can be read again, the store should load it and merge the edits it kept in memory.

### Actual behavior

Three write paths call `persistence.write` directly — the debounced `persistNow`, the retention admission's cleanup writes, and `deleteAttachmentIfUnreferenced` — and all replace the unreadable file with the in-memory state, destroying the drafts held there.

### Impact

Major degradation

### App version / commit

master at 34a4df01; the behavior is version-independent. Confirmed in the review on #1504.

### iOS version and device

Code path; any iOS version.

### Server kind and version

Not server-related: `drafts.json` is local to the phone.

title: Model picker and recents show raw model ids for gateway (dashboard) connections
body:
### Summary

With a direct-to-gateway (dashboard) connection, the model settings sheet and the **Recently used** list show the raw model id everywhere — e.g. `zai/glm-5.3-flash:local` — while the Hermes desktop app renders the same model as "GLM 5.3 · Flash".

### Cause

(verified against master `34a4df0`) The gateway's `model.options` payload serves `providers[].models` as **plain strings** — there is no display-name field:

```
providers[].models = ["zai/glm-5.3-flash:local", "qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b:local"]
```

`HermesModelCatalog.swift` therefore builds every option with the id as its own name:

```swift
let option = ModelCatalogOption(id: id, displayName: id, providerID: provider)
```

`ModelFavoritesStore` builds recents the same way (`ModelCatalogOption(id: modelID, displayName: modelID, …)`), which is why the recents rows show the identical raw id as both title and subtitle.

The webui transport already accepts `{id, name|label}` objects via `ModelCatalogParser.parseModelOptions`; only the gateway transport has nothing to fall back on. The Hermes desktop app solves this client-side in `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-status-label.ts` (`displayModelName`).

### Proposal

A display-only Swift helper mirroring that logic, applied when rendering `ModelCatalogOption.displayName` (without changing `id`, favorites keys, or selection):

- strip the vendor prefix (`zai/…` → `glm-…`) and a trailing `:local` (optionally rendered as a grayed "Local" tag)
- split trailing variant tags `-flash`, `-fast`, `-thinking`, `-preview`, `-latest` into the grayed tag ("GLM 5.3" + "Flash"), so distinct ids like `…-flash` vs `…-thinking` never collapse to one label
- vendor casing (GLM, DeepSeek, OpenAI, MiniMax, ERNIE …) and parameter counts (`a22b` → `A22B`)

Picker matching, favorites, and the `id … --provider … --session` selection string must keep using the raw id.

title: feat(chat): give HTML reports --primary-foreground and --muted theme variables
body:
### Use case

Agents increasingly reply with small generated UI (approval cards, pickers, status panels) built on shadcn-style token names. HTML reports (#1623 / #1645) already hand pages `--background --foreground --card --muted-foreground --border --primary --font-sans --font-mono`, which is most of what such a card kit needs. Two common tokens are missing, so a page has to hard-code them and then looks wrong in some themes:

- `--primary-foreground`: text/icon color on a `--primary` button. Without it a page guesses white or black, which fails on light accents (e.g. Paper, Grove).
- `--muted`: the quiet fill behind chips, toggles, and secondary buttons. Without it a page mixes its own from `--card`, which drifts from the app's fills.

Both already exist in `ThemePalette`: `onAccent` and `fill`.

### Proposed behavior

In `HTMLReportTheme` add two variables beside the existing ones, and two rows to the table in `docs/agents/theming.md` § HTML reports:

| Variable | From |
|---|---|
| `--primary-foreground` | onAccent |
| `--muted` | fill |

They stay under `:where()`/`:root` like the rest, so page styles still win, and they are restyled live along with the others.

### Acceptance outcomes

- A report using `background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground)` stays readable in every built-in theme, light and dark, and with a custom accent.
- `--muted` resolves to the same fill the app uses for its own quiet surfaces.
- The existing `HTMLReportTheme` tests cover the two new variables.

### Notes

I checked this with an emulated report host (your `HTMLReportTheme` CSS injected at document start, transparent page, height measured) in Playwright WebKit at 402 px. A four-card kit export (~240 KB, well under the 5 MB inline limit) rendered in light and dark with no overflow or page errors, and followed a live dark-to-light restyle. The only tokens it had to make up were these two. I'm happy to send the PR (two variable lines, a test, a docs row) if you'd like to assign it.

title: Large clipboard paste can leave the new session titled with its UUID
body:
## Reproduction status

The title failure is reproducible from source with a new session whose first message is a generated attachment reference and whose title preview is absent or ignored. The exact ChatGPT iOS clipboard contents and the installed Hermex device build were not available in this investigation, so this report does not claim a live-device reproduction of the clipboard symptom.

## Expected behavior

A new conversation begun with a long pasted prompt receives a meaningful automatic title, while the complete text remains the attachment received by the main model. No manual subject, synthetic user message, or local rename should be required.

## Confirmed title root causes

1. Hermex's large-paste path stages the full clipboard string as `pasted-text.txt` and submits its `@file:` reference, but the previous client did not send the supported titler-only `prompt.submit.title_preview` field.
2. Hermes Agent v0.23.1 accepts and persists that metadata, but its title-eligibility guards reject attachment-only opener text before using a non-empty preview. The confirmed backend issue is [NousResearch/hermes-agent#155525](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/155525), with draft fix [PR #155526](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/155526).

The Hermex draft PR adds explicit provenance for app-generated large-paste attachments and sends a bounded preview only as title metadata to compatible hosts. The full attachment and model-facing `@file:` reference remain unchanged. Manual files and existing user titles are preserved.

## Clipboard classification findings (separate, not confirmed for ChatGPT Copy)

Hermex source checks file `NSItemProvider`s and file URLs before image and text representations. A real file-URL representation therefore wins if a pasteboard item exposes both file and text forms. HTML/RTF-only representations are not treated as files by this route. No live ChatGPT pasteboard UTI list was available, so it is not established that ChatGPT Copy supplies a file URL for ordinary copied text or that this caused the reported symptom.

Large plain-text pastes over 3,000 UTF-16 code units are intentionally converted into an attachment; exactly 3,000 remains inline. Seeing Hermex's generated `pasted-text.txt` is consistent with that intended threshold path, not proof of a false file classification. No clipboard-precedence change is proposed without a reproducible file-URL/text collision.

## Environment and verification

- Hermex public App Store lookup reports version 2.1; release tag `v2.1.0` carries marketing version 2.1. This does not identify the installed device build or prove binary/source identity.
- Current Hermex source is marketing version 2.2; the current source and v2.1.0 share the same paste precedence.
- Added source tests cover 2,999/3,000/3,001 UTF-16 units, short plain text, plain+HTML+RTF, a genuine file-URL item with a text representation, and image routing. Hermex XCTest/build could not run here because the Linux host has no Xcode, Swift, or iOS simulator.
- Hermex draft PR #1702 is awaiting maintainer approval for fork CI; the latest workflow is `action_required` with no jobs.

All reproduction text is synthetic. No private prompts, session identifiers, credentials, or host paths are included.

title: fix(chat): give the session titler the start of a long paste
body:
## Linked issue

Part of #1701. Paste-only first messages also need the upstream host fix, [NousResearch/hermes-agent#155526](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/155526).

## What changed

A long paste (over 3,000 characters) becomes a `pasted-text.txt` attachment, so the session titler only sees an `@file:` reference and names the session poorly, or not at all. Hermes Desktop solves this by sending the start of the paste as `prompt.submit`'s `title_preview`, which the host uses for the title only. Hermex now does the same:

- A paste the composer converts is marked as one, and keeps that mark through edits, drafts and relaunch. A file the user picks, even one named `pasted-text.txt`, never is.
- On send, the first pasted attachment's opening text, bounded to 1,000 UTF-16 units without splitting a character, goes out as `title_preview`. The prompt text and the attachment are unchanged.
- Only hosts reporting 0.21.6 or newer get the field. `PromptSubmitParams` gained it in v0.21.6 (absent in 0.21.3 to 0.21.5), and the schema refuses unknown keys. A host with no readable version gets nothing.

What users notice today, on a 0.23.1 host: a long paste sent with a typed line gets a title drawn from the paste too. A paste sent alone still gets no title until the host fix above ships, because 0.23.1 refuses to title attachment-only openers before it reads the preview.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/test-sim` on iPhone Air, `--only` `HermesChatAttachmentTests`, `HermesRequestTests`, `ChatAttachmentCoordinatorTests`, `ChatDraftStoreTests`, `BotConnectionVersionTests`, `ComposerLargePasteTests`: 121 passed, 0 failed.

- Signed Debug build launched on the simulator and opened a Hermes chat. The real paste was not driven: `simctl pbcopy` leaves the simulator pasteboard empty, and copying inside the simulator would overwrite the Mac clipboard.

Manual check on a phone: on a 0.23.1 host, paste over 3,000 characters into a new chat, type a short line, send, and check the session title reflects the paste.

title: hermex-push: don't push a reply that ends with [SILENT]
body:
**What happens.** With hermex-push 0.7.0, every completed turn sends a `reply` push, including turns where the agent decided there was nothing to say and replied `[SILENT]`.

My setup: a Hermes bot works as a chief of staff. A plugin injects events into its Bot Chat (CI changed, a PR got a comment), and most of them need nothing, so the bot answers `[SILENT]`. Each of those still lands on my phone as a banner whose body is `[SILENT]`. Hermes's cron path already treats `[SILENT]` as "deliver nothing".

**Suggestion.** In `hooks.py` `on_session_end`, skip the `reply` notification when the reply ends with `[SILENT]` (approvals, questions and turn errors unchanged). I'm running this locally and it works:

```python
user_message, reply = captured
if str(reply or "").strip().endswith("[SILENT]"):
    return
self._notify("reply", session_id, ref, subtitle=user_message, body=reply)
```

Environment: hermex-push 0.7.0, hermes-agent 0.23.1, macOS.

title: Add Server crashes when a connection header is named CF-Access-Client-Id or CF-Access-Client-Secret
body:
**What the user gets:** typing or pasting a Cloudflare Access header name into Add Server's Connection Headers no longer crashes the app.
**Why it matters:** a user emailed that they could not configure Cloudflare Access at all; the app hard-crashed the moment either header name was complete (typed, pasted, or a fixed typo).
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed beyond a simulator check.

## Cause

Connection Options (`AddServerView.swift`, `ConnectionOptionsPage`) binds `CustomHeadersEditor` to `OnboardingViewModel.otherHeaders`, a computed projection that hides rows named `CF-Access-Client-Id` / `CF-Access-Client-Secret` (case-insensitive, value not required) because the Cloudflare Access fields above edit those two.

`CustomHeadersEditor` iterates `ForEach($headers)`, whose row bindings address the array by index. When a row's name becomes a Cloudflare name, the next `otherHeaders` read no longer contains it, and the text field's stale binding reads past the end: `Fatal error: Index out of range` in `Binding<MutableCollection>.subscript.getter`. Reproduced in an in-memory harness.

Introduced in #1543, shipped in 2.1.0. Reaches first-run onboarding, webui sign-in again, Add Server from anywhere, and Move to Hermes. The existing webui server and Hermes connection header editors bind plain arrays and are not affected.

Workaround: paste the token's values into the Cloudflare Access Client ID and Client Secret fields instead of adding header rows.

## Fix

Have `CustomHeadersEditor` iterate row snapshots and resolve each field's binding by the row's UUID, so a row that leaves the list reads its last snapshot and ignores late writes. A row given a Cloudflare name moves into the Cloudflare Access fields, as designed.

title: fix(chat): keep a reply visible when a delegation delivery follows it
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1706

## What changed

When a Hermes reply was followed by an async delegation delivery, the long main reply folded under "Worked for …" and only the short text after the delegation card stayed visible.

title: feat(workspace): render HTML files in the file viewer, with a Preview/Source switch
body:
**What the user gets:** an `.html` file opened from a chat link or the Files tree shows the rendered page, with its source one tap away.
**Why it matters:** the owner's 2.2 phone pass asked an agent for an HTML report and got a link; tapping it showed 57 lines of source. Reports only render today when the agent attaches the file.
**Cost:** Small. The owner checks one linked report on a phone.

## Problem

In a Hermes chat, a reply that carries an `.html` file (a `MEDIA:` tag or an image-style embed) renders it in place (#1645). A reply that only **links** to the file (`[Download the report](.hermes/cache/scratch/delegation-report.html)`) is a workspace file link. It opens `FilePreviewView`, which shows source for everything except Markdown, so the report is unreadable. Agents choose a link often: the owner's first natural prompt did.

## What to build

In the workspace file viewer (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewView.swift`):

- An `.html` or `.htm` text file gets the same Preview / Source picker in the file actions menu that a Markdown file has, and opens on **Preview** (owner's decision, 2026-11-15).
- Preview draws the file's text with the page view the report sheet already uses (`HTMLReportSheetPage`, `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HTMLReportWebView.swift`), so it keeps that sandbox and theme: an opaque origin, a non-persistent store, no Hermes cookie, credential or custom header reachable.
- Source is today's view. Wrap Lines, Copy Contents and Select Text keep working as they do for Markdown in each mode.
- The viewer already holds the file's text, so there is no new endpoint, model or dependency, and it applies wherever the viewer opens: chat links, the Files tree, search hits, changed-file cards, on Hermes and webui servers alike.

## Out of scope

- Rendering a linked `.html` file inline in the reply. That changes what a link does in a transcript and needs its own decision.
- Changing how attached reports render (#1645).

## Notes

- Opening on Preview means browsing a project's own `index.html` in Files runs its scripts and loads its remote resources in the sandbox. The owner accepted that. Check whether `AGENTS.md`'s line about agent content loading remote resources needs a word about workspace HTML files.
- Follow the report sheet's limits and failure state for a page that can't draw, rather than inventing new ones.
- Found during the 2.2 release (#1710). It does not block 2.2.

title: feat(chat): open a linked HTML report outside the chat's folder in the report sheet
body:
**What the user gets:** tapping a link to an `.html` report the agent wrote outside the chat's folder opens the rendered report, instead of doing nothing.
**Why it matters:** agents write reports to scratch locations such as `~/.hermes/cache/scratch/`. In a chat on a project folder, a link there resolves outside the folder, so the tap is ignored. GPT models write these links as `sandbox:/abs/path`, and a `sandbox:/mnt/data/…` link never lands inside a folder.
**Cost:** Small.

## What to build

In a Hermes chat, a link whose destination is an absolute `.html`/`.htm` path (`/…`, `~/…`, `file:`, `sandbox:`) that falls outside the chat's folder opens the report sheet (`BotArtifactPreview`), loading through the chat's attach the way a `MEDIA:` report's card does. Links inside the folder keep opening the workspace file viewer with Preview / Source (#1712).

## Out of scope

- Rendering linked reports inline in the reply.
- Bare relative link destinations (`out/report.html`): they look like relative web links.
- Non-HTML files outside the folder.
- webui chats, which have no attach to load through.

Found while testing #1712.

title: Pull to refresh while the session list connects empties it and shows "This action is no longer current"
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to a Hermes server reached over a slow link (an HTTPS tunnel makes the window wide enough).
2. Open the Sessions tab, or bring the app back to it, so the list starts connecting while it shows its cached rows.
3. Pull to refresh before that first connect finishes.

### Expected behavior

The cached rows stay, and the list refreshes once it has connected.

### Actual behavior

The list empties and shows "Could not load sessions — This action is no longer current. Refresh the conversation." for a second or two, until the reconnect brings the rows back.

`openHermes` stores the wire before `connect()` finishes. The pull's `openHermes` takes the existing-wire branch and reads pages on it, and `BotClient` refuses every read on a consumer that has not attached with `.stale`. `reloadHermes` then calls `dropHermes(.stale)`, which drops the cached rows, closes the socket that was still connecting, and shows the error because the list is now empty.

### Impact

Minor bug

### App version / commit

Seen on our fork's TestFlight build of an earlier `master`. Reproduced on `master` at bbaeef1b with a unit test: the refresh empties the list and reports `.stale` (see the linked PR).

### iOS version and device

iPhone, TestFlight build; the unit test ran on an iOS 27.2 simulator

### Server kind and version

Hermes 0.23.1

### How the phone reaches the server

HTTPS tunnel (e.g. Cloudflare Tunnel)

title: fix(sessions): keep the session list when a refresh lands while it connects
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1717

## What changed

Pulling to refresh the Sessions tab while the list was still making its first connection emptied the list and showed "This action is no longer current" until the reconnect brought the rows back.

`openHermes` stores the wire before `connect()` finishes. A second `openHermes` (the pull) took the existing-wire branch and read pages on it, and `BotClient` refuses every read on a consumer that has not attached with `.stale`. `reloadHermes` then called `dropHermes(.stale)`, which dropped the cached rows, closed the socket that was still connecting, and showed the error.

`SessionListViewModel` now keeps `hermesConnectingWire` while `connect()` runs. A refresh, a Profile switch, a change event or Load more on that wire leaves the read to the open that is connecting, which reads right after it connects. title: fix(bots): forget a Profile's cached Bot Chat when the roster no longer lists it
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1152

## What changed

A Profile deleted from another client never reached `BotInbox.forget`, so its cached Bot Chat rows outlived the roster that stopped listing it. `cachedHermesBotChatRoot` and `cachedHermesMessages` kept returning them, and a Profile recreated under the same name could show its predecessor's preview before the attach, especially offline.

`BotInbox.reload` now compares the roster it held before the read with the fresh one. Each Profile that left goes through the existing `CacheStore.removeHermesBotChats(serverURL:connectionID:profile:in:)`, the same remover `forget` uses. That remover:

- deletes the Profile's current and archived Bot Chat scopes;
- revokes pending writers even when no rows were cached yet, so a chat whose first history read is still in flight cannot write the transcript back.

When the purge runs:

- Only after a successful, current `profiles.list`. A failed or superseded read returns before it.
- Before the first `await` in the rest of `reload`, so a reopen or a newer reload that lands during the `uncertainDeletions` cleanup cannot drop the departed Profile from the next comparison.
- Steady-state reloads only diff two in-memory sets. Cache work happens only for a Profile that actually left.
- Present Profiles, other connections and other servers are untouched.

`docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` now lists the roster as a trigger that removes both copies.

Not changed:

- **A deletion made while the app was closed is caught only when the roster cache paints the list first.** That is the usual case, but not when iOS evicted Caches, on a first run, or for rosters too large to cache. Without a previous roster there is nothing to compare. A Profile recreated under the same name still drops the old copy when its new chat attaches on another root, through the existing `removeHermesBotChats(exceptRoot:)`.
- **A partial roster is trusted.** At the pinned host commit, `gateway/session_group_controls.py` `_named_profile_dirs` returns an empty list when listing `profiles/` raises `OSError`, and `profiles.list` still succeeds. A roster read during such an error drops the offline Bot Chat copies of Profiles found only on disk. The host still has them, so the next online read restores them. `profiles.list` carries no deletion marker the app could use instead.
- **Revocation is server-wide**, as with `forget`: other chats open on that server stop refreshing their offline copy until they attach again. This happens only when a Profile actually leaves.
- Unread state, avatar and drafts of the departed Profile are not cleared. `forget` clears them for local deletes, but a roster read alone is not strong enough evidence to discard unsent drafts.

## How it was tested

- `BotLifecycleTests.testARosterOmittingABotDropsItsCachedBotChat`:
  - Caches Bot Chats for `triage` and `keep` on the inbox's connection, plus `triage` on another connection.
  - Brings a roster through a `sessions.changed` event that drops `triage` and `fresh` (`fresh` has no cached rows), with no `inbox.delete`.
  - Checks that `triage`'s cached root is gone, that `keep`'s and the other connection's stay, and that the cache epoch moved.
- With the `BotInbox` change reverted, it fails (`XCTAssertNil failed: "root"`). Restored, it passes.

  | `CacheStoreTests` | 35 passed |

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (none changed)

title: fix(bots): clear a deleted archived Bot Chat from the offline cache

## Linked issue

Fixes #1153

## What changed

Deleting an archived Bot Chat from Archived Sessions removed only the ordinary `hermes|<Profile>|<root>` cache rows. The chat's transcript is cached under `hermes-bot|<connection>|<Profile>|<root>` and `hermes-bot-archive|<connection>|<Profile>|<root>`, so it stayed readable through `cachedHermesBotChatRoot` / `cachedHermesMessages`, and no pending writer was revoked.

title: bug(live-activity): a finished run keeps counting (8h11m shown for a 54s turn) when the terminal push is lost
body:
## What happens

A turn that finished at 23:12 is still shown as running when I open the chat the next morning: **"worked for 8 hours 11 minutes"** on a turn that actually lasted **54 seconds**. The number is wall-clock elapsed since my message (23:11 -> 07:22 when I opened the app), which is also right at the iOS Live Activity limit (~8 h) — the activity was simply never ended.

## Evidence (server side)

- my message: 23:11:38 -> final assistant message 23:12:32, finish_reason = stop (from the Hermes session DB) — real turn duration 54 s
- gateway log at 23:10:51: hermex-push: relay unreachable for a progress event (HTTP 503) (twice, two profiles)
- hermex_push/relay.py (plugin 0.7.0): the only event that ends a Live Activity is the terminal one (progress with status done/failed, plus reply / turn_error). RelaySender.deliver() gives those **one retry** and **persists nothing**. A 503 at the wrong moment therefore loses the end-of-turn event and the activity runs until iOS kills it.

## Workaround I applied locally (hermes-agent side, plugin copy)

- terminal events retried 4x with backoff (2 s / 6 s / 15 s)
- on final failure the event is written to <hermes home>/plugin-data/hermex-push/pending/*.json and replayed every 60 s (bounded to 40 files)
- replaceable progress events stay ephemeral (1 attempt), unchanged

## What I'd ask on the app side

1. **Reconcile on open/reconnect**: when the app opens a session (or reconnects), end/mark-ended any activity whose run already finished server-side, instead of trusting the last push received.
2. **Show the real duration** of a finished run (ended_at - started_at), not now - started_at. A finished turn's timer should freeze at the true value.
3. A client-side watchdog that ends an activity when no progress update arrived for N minutes would have prevented an 8-hour stale timer.

Happy to send the plugin patch upstream (hermex-push) if that repo is preferred.

## Environment

- Hermex iOS (App Store build), iPhone 17 Pro
- Hermes Agent v0.23.1, self-hosted on Linux, hermes-push 0.7.0, relay hermex-relay.*.workers.dev
- several profiles served by one multiplexed gateway (default, secondario, generalistabackup, cronbot, long-running)

title: feat(app): report whether a Hermes server is a Webapp or a dashboard
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing visible; we learn how many Hermes servers connect through a gateway's Webapp versus the dashboard.
**Why it matters:** the weekly usage report (#1659) says whether a server is Hermes or webui, but not which Hermes front door it uses, so we can't tell how much the Webapp path (#1606) is used.
**Cost:** Small in the app, plus a matching collector change. Bumping the report format asks every user who allowed reports again, so it's best shipped together with another new field.

## Today

`UsageReport.Servers.versions` sends each server's `kind` (`hermes` or `webui`) and release. Whether a Hermes server is a Webapp is known only while connected: `HermesConnection.servesWebapp` is set at sign-in and not saved. The report is built from `ServerRegistry` and makes no server request, so it can't read it.

## Change

1. Save the result on `ServerAccount` when a Hermes sign-in resolves `servesWebapp`. Decode it tolerantly; servers saved before this have no value.
2. Add `gateway` to each `servers.versions` entry: `webapp`, `dashboard`, or `unknown` (a webui server, or a Hermes server not signed in since this shipped).
3. Bump `UsageReport.currentVersion` to 2 and list `gateway` in `fieldsAdded(after:)`. A user on version 1 keeps sending version 1 until they accept 2.
4. Land the collector change in `uzairansaruzi/hermex-stats` first: it rejects unknown keys, so it has to accept version 2 before any app build sends it.
5. Update `docs/agents/usage-reports.md`. The field is covered by the existing "Other Usage Data" privacy entry, so the manifest and App Store label don't change.

## Tests

- `UsageReportsTests`: a Webapp server, a dashboard server, and a webui server encode `webapp`, `dashboard`, and `unknown`; a version 1 report has no `gateway` key.
- Sign-in saves the value on the server it belongs to, not the active one when they differ.

🤖 Filed by Claude Code (Opus 5.5)

title: feat(app): report whether each Hermes server is a Webapp or a dashboard
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1724

## What changed

The weekly usage report says whether a server is Hermes or webui, but not whether a Hermes server is reached through a gateway's Webapp or through the dashboard. Now it does.

title: epic(hermes): bring Hermes Desktop's run control and remote admin to Hermex
body:
**What the user gets:** the things Hermes Desktop can do that a phone user misses most: see what is still running and stop it, fix a broken agent while away from the host, and answer the host's sign-in prompts.
**Why it matters:** a scan of Hermes Desktop against Hermex (2026-11-15, at host pin `3b421578`, 0.23.1) found Hermex at parity on most everyday surfaces and behind in three places the host already serves to a phone. One finding is a live defect.
**Cost:** Large in total, split into small children. Ten gate 2.3; the rest ship when ready.

This issue is the record of what was found and what the owner decided (2026-11-16). Children are sub-issues, each with a file-level plan; each one re-verifies its host contract before editing (AGENTS.md, Working with the server). Children that add a new screen, sheet or card are `ready-for-human` and start with static mocks; children that add a control to an existing screen are `ready-for-agent`.

## How it was checked

Six areas of Hermes Desktop (`apps/desktop` in `hermes-agent`) were read against Hermex. On 2026-11-16 every adopted route and method was then checked:

- **Live host, read-only** (0.23.1, dashboard gateway): every REST route the children name is in its `/openapi.json`, and the read calls answered.
- **`scripts/local-hermes` in both modes** (the pinned commit): method presence by an invalid-parameter probe, plus a Task create, trigger, cancel and delete, and a text-file save.

Not exercised, so each child proves its own: a cancel that lands mid-run, Create PR, a pairing approval, `process.kill`, the theme and vault requests end to end, and MCP sign-in.

What the check settled:

- `subagent.steer`, `process.list`, `process.kill`, `rollback.*`, `session.context_breakdown`, `session.control.read`, `mcp.servers.*` and `subagent.roster` answer on both gateway types.
- `prompt.replace_queued`, `prompt.steer_queued`, `prompt.cancel`, `prompt.receipt` and `runtime.describe` answer only on a gateway's Webapp. `session.usage` answers only on a dashboard.
- A Webapp reports invalid parameters as 4001, a dashboard as 4000.
- `catch_up` on a Task is a boolean or null, not a named policy.
- `POST /api/cron/jobs/{id}/cancel` answers `{success, cancelled, execution_id, detail}`, with `cancelled: false` when no run is in flight.

## Adopted: 2.3

- [x] #1727 **Answer the host's theme requests.** Hermex chats run as the host's `gui` surface, so the agent gets Desktop's `set_theme` tool. Hermex never answers `theme.apply` or `theme.pick`, so "make it dark" stalls the turn for 15 s and a picker for up to 5 min. Apply light, dark and accent natively, refuse layout values, answer a picker at once, and tell the agent the phone has no tours or tips.
- [x] #1728 **Route `/rollback` to the rollback calls.** Hermex sends it through `slash.exec`, which a Webapp refuses. No checkpoints screen.
- [ ] #1420 **Background processes: output and Stop.** Amended in its comments: the host declares `agent.terminal.output` and `terminal.close` at this pin.
- [ ] #1729 **Stop a running Task.** Plus the missed-run choice (`catch_up`) and the stop reason the host already puts in a run's title, which Hermex drops. Run Now has no Stop today.
- [x] #1730 **Show a chat as working while its background work runs.** `subagent.roster` gives counts for each stored session in one read, taken on `sessions.changed` and on foreground, not on a timer.
- [ ] #1731 **Create Pull Request.** `POST /api/git/review/create-pr`. Asks first and says it pushes the branch and opens a PR on GitHub. Commit & Push already ships.
- [ ] #1732 **Steer one delegated worker.** `subagent.steer`. Replaces the closed #565. No "pause new spawns": it is global across the host and has no home in one chat.
- [x] #1733 **Working, Unread and Draft filters, and Mark All as Read.** No new API.
- [x] #1734 **"Compacting context" while the host compacts.** Existing `status.update` events. Today auto-compaction looks like a stall.
- [ ] #1735 **Answer the host's sign-in prompts.** Three cards, in chat: a one-time code (`vault.code`, with the field iOS fills from Messages), save a site login (`vault.save_login`, with Password AutoFill), and unlock a password manager with its master password (`vault.unlock_prompt`). A chat waiting on one counts under "Needs you". Nothing typed is stored on the phone. The master password is sent once to unlock the manager for that session. Restores the cards #943 shipped and #1148 removed with Bot Chat's screen.

The 2.3 milestone also holds #1724, filed separately.

## Adopted: ships when ready

**Fix the agent from away**
- [ ] #1736 **MCP server health and Test.** `mcp.servers.status` and `.test`. Never `reload.mcp`: a Webapp refuses it.
- [ ] #1737 **Finish MCP sign-in on the phone.** `mcp.servers.oauth.start` with `client_redirect_uri`, the loopback pattern browser sign-in already uses, from the health page. Blocked by #1736. The mid-chat card's own sign-in stays on the host's loopback at this pin, so retiring "Finish on the Mac" there is an owner decision recorded in the child.
- [ ] #1738 **Approve or revoke people on the messaging bot.** `/api/pairing`, live on `pairing.changed`. The copy says that approving grants access to the agent. Platform setup is out.
- [ ] #1739 **Sign a subscription provider back in.** `/api/providers/oauth`, device-code sign-ins only at this pin. Sign-in and disconnect, not a Providers status screen.

**Chat**
- [ ] #1740 **Read replies aloud as they stream.** `WS /api/audio/speak-stream`. Removes the 4,000-character Listen cap.
- [ ] #1741 **Find in chat.** Searches loaded rows and says so.
- [ ] #1742 **Jump to a prompt.** `GET /api/sessions/{id}/timeline` and `/messages/around`.
- [ ] #1743 **Edit, steer or delete a queued prompt.** Webapp hosts only, hidden elsewhere.
- [ ] #1744 **Goal details.** Why a goal is waiting or blocked, and what counts as done (`session.control.read`).
- [ ] #1745 **What is filling the context window.** `session.context_breakdown`, read when the popover opens.
- [x] #1746 **The host's notices.** `notification.show` as a calm dismissible row.
- [ ] #1747 **List the files and images a chat produced.** Per chat, from loaded rows. Refiles #222.
- [x] #1748 **A View button on HTML code blocks.** SVG and Mermaid already have one.
- [ ] #1749 **Show the image a tool looked at inside its row.**
- [x] #1750 **Remember Thinking and Fast for each model.** Local, kept per server.

**Everything else**
- [ ] #1751 **Connect to a host behind a URL path.** Hermex refuses `host/hermes` today.
- [ ] #1752 **Kanban: a Card's own model and Thinking.**
- [ ] #1753 **Kanban: reclaim a stuck Card and terminate a run.**
- [ ] #1754 **Control Center and Lock Screen controls.** Wraps the existing intents. #6 stays the Home Screen widget issue.
- [ ] #1755 **Edit and save a text file.** `POST /api/fs/write-text`, with a re-read before saving. No create, rename or delete.
- [ ] #1756 **Refresh Tasks, projects and skills when the host says they changed.** `cron.changed`, `projects.changed`, `skills.changed`.
- [ ] #1757 **Tell a new host's user to add a model provider.** `setup.status`.

## Deferred

No child issue. Revisit after 2.3.

- Checkpoints screen (off by default on the host), new chat in a fresh worktree, Task templates, pause new spawns, Kanban orchestration and decompose.
- A gallery of outputs across chats: it means reading many transcripts.
- Live dictation partials, keeping the reading place on reopen, skill lock and hub install, session tidy-up, tips, Profile rename, multi-folder projects, a fallback-model editor.
- Hands-free voice stays on #36. Approve from the notification stays on #750.

## Accepted: host limits

- **A push when the agent needs a sign-in code.** The host tells plugins about approvals, clarify and sudo, not vault prompts. A plugin sees the `enter_code` tool call, but the same call either fills a saved authenticator code or asks the user, and only the vault knows which (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py`). So the code card works when the app is open, or is reopened inside the host's 180 s wait: the host hands an unanswered prompt back to a client that reconnects.
- **Queued-prompt controls on a dashboard.** It keeps one merged slot with no per-row id.

## Not adopted

Ideas raised and turned down for now: a single "What's running" sheet; a "Needs attention" list across approvals, pairings and broken sign-ins; a catch-up card on reopening a long run; an Action Button walkie-talkie; "try it two ways" in parallel worktrees; answering a code from the notification; a "shipped" Lock Screen link; a settings screen generated from the host's schema; a fleet check-in strip across servers; flagging risky tool output.

Desktop features with no phone case: pets, particles and the Star Map graph; the wake word; GPT-Live (needs a WebRTC package); a host shell; billing top-ups; vault administration, credential pools and custom endpoints; the embedded browser and preview annotate; handing a chat off to a messaging app.

## Records corrected

- `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`: a gateway's Webapp has `runtime.describe` and plugin RPC methods. Merged in #1758.
- #1420 and #1668: comments posted 2026-11-16.

title: fix(chat): answer the host's theme requests instead of stalling the turn
body:
**What the user gets:** "make it dark" or "switch the accent to green" works from a Hermex chat, and the agent never stalls waiting for a picker that the phone can't show.
**Why it matters:** today the agent can call `set_theme` in every Hermex chat, but nothing on the phone answers it. The turn hangs 15 s for an apply and up to 5 min for a picker, with nothing on screen to explain the wait.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable once the host sends the request.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
A Hermex session's source is `gui` (`HermesCall.source`, `docs/agents/hermes-server.md:365-381`). For a `gui` session the host folds the client-surface toolsets into the agent, `desktop_ui` included (`gateway/session_policy.py:696-706`, `toolsets.py:67`). `desktop_ui` holds `set_theme`, `show_tip` and `gui_tour` (`toolsets.py:135-141`). `set_theme` sends the attached viewer a `theme.apply` server request and waits 15 s for it, or a `theme.pick` request and waits 300 s (`tui_gateway/theme_bridge.py:10-32`; canonical: `gateway/local_desktop_ui.py:168-186`). Hermex never answers either one.

## Hermex today
- `BotServerRequest` sets `pending` to nil for any method it doesn't know, `theme.apply` and `theme.pick` included, so they get no card and no reply (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequest.swift:33-72`).
- `HermesChatRequests` holds the unanswered request in `open`, so the chat shows "waiting" with no card until the host gives up (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesChatRequests.swift:16-17,112-113,498-509`).
- The phone's look lives in `AppTheme` (`system`, `light`, `dark` under `appTheme`; `HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:30-35`) and `AppAppearanceSettings.accentHexKey` (nil means the theme's own accent; `HermesMobile/Config/AppColor.swift:220-243`). Settings offers eight accent swatches (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAppearancePage.swift:243-252`).
- The platform note says nothing about tours or tips (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:105-110`). `HermesConnection.keepPlatformNote` rewrites a Profile's note whenever its text changes (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:205`).

## Contract
Read from source at the pin (`3b421578`); the theme requests have not been run end to end yet.
- `theme.apply` params: `{session_id, accent?, mode?, layout?}`. `mode` is `light|dark|system`. `accent` is a swatch id (`mono, green, cyan, nous, violet, pink, red, orange`), `theme`, or `#rrggbb` (`tui_gateway/contracts/server_requests.py:324-341`, `tools/set_theme_tool.py:15-25`).
- The answer is `{value}`: a JSON string. Desktop sends `{success: true, applied: {mode?, accent?}}`, where `accent` is the swatch id, `custom:#rrggbb` or null, or `{success: false, error, available}` (`apps/desktop/src/store/appearance-apply.ts:80-117`, `server-requests.ts:91-92,840-848`). The tool hands that JSON to the model as it is.
- `theme.pick` params: `{session_id, picker: accent|layout}`. Answer `{picked}`, `{said: "<text>"}` or `{cancelled: true}`. A non-empty `said` reaches the model as `{said}`; anything else counts as a cancel (`theme_bridge.py:24-32`, `server_requests.py:343-367`).
- Desktop maps `nous` and `theme` both to the theme's own accent (`apps/desktop/src/themes/accents.ts:52-55`).
- **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes` (both modes), in one disposable session, ask for dark mode and then for an accent picker. Capture both request frames, then delete the session.

## Proposal
- **Model:** add a pure `HermesThemeRequest` in a new file, `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesThemeRequest.swift`. It turns `theme.apply` params into the new `AppTheme`, the new accent and the answer JSON, or into a refusal. It turns `theme.pick` params into the `said` text.
- **Answering:** in `HermesChatRequests.receive` (`HermesChatRequests.swift:498`), catch `theme.apply` and `theme.pick` before they join `open`. Apply the change and answer once through the engine's guarded write (`HermesConversation.answer`, `HermesMobile/Features/Hermes/HermesConversation.swift:376`). `theme.apply` reuses `.value`. `theme.pick` needs a new `HermesCall.RequestAnswer.said(String)` that sends `{said}` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift:463-474`). Never answer the same envelope id twice, even when a replay brings it back.
- **Apply:** write `AppTheme.storageKey` and `AppAppearanceSettings.accentHexKey` to `UserDefaults.standard`, then call `AppAppearanceSettings.applyStoredToConnectedScenes()`, as Settings does (`SettingsAppearancePage.swift:86-89`).
- **Platform note:** add one sentence to `HermesREST.platformNote`: "Hermex has no tours, tips, panes or layouts: don't call gui_tour or show_tip; set_theme changes only light, dark and the accent."

## Decisions
- **Mode:** `light`, `dark` and `system` map one to one onto `AppTheme`.
- **Accent:** green → Green `#4CC96B`, cyan → Teal `#30B8C4`, violet → Indigo `#7D7AFF`, pink, red and orange → Hermex's swatch of the same name. `nous` and `theme` clear the pick (nil), as on Desktop. `#rrggbb` is stored as typed. `applied.accent` reports the id the agent sent, or `custom:#RRGGBB` for a hex colour.
- **`mono`:** Hermex has no mono swatch. Refuse it with `{success: false, error: "Hermex has no mono accent.", available: [...]}` and list Hermex's ids.
- **Layout:** any `layout` refuses the whole request, as Desktop's validate-first does: `{success: false, error: "Hermex on iPhone has no layouts.", available: []}`. Nothing is applied, so the agent can retry without it.
- **`theme.pick`:** answer at once with `said`, never `cancelled`, because a cancel reads as the user dismissing the card. The accent text: "Hermex, the iPhone app, has no picker card. Ask the user in the chat which accent they want (green, cyan, violet, pink, red, orange or a hex colour), then call set_theme with it." The layout text: "Hermex, the iPhone app, has no layouts to pick." Both texts are for the agent, so they stay in English and out of the String Catalog, like the platform note.
- **Which chat answers:** only an attached chat on screen receives requests, because leaving drops the socket (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:2149-2156`). If a Desktop window is attached to the same session, whichever window answers first wins. We accept that.
- **Tips and tours** stay as they are: `show_tip` is fire-and-forget, and `tour` keeps its Desktop task card (`BotPendingRequest.swift:303-345`). The platform note steers the agent away from both.

## Acceptance and tests
- "Switch to dark mode" turns the app dark within the turn, and the agent's reply says it's done. "Use a layout called focus" changes nothing, and the agent says Hermex has none.
- "Let me pick an accent" never shows a waiting state: the agent asks in the chat.
- `HermesChatRequestTests`: a `theme.apply {mode: dark}` envelope sends one `request.answer` whose `value` decodes to `success: true` and `applied.mode: dark`, and leaves `open` empty. A `layout` sends `success: false` and changes no stored setting. A `theme.pick` sends `{said}`. The same envelope arriving twice sends one answer. All four fail on today's code.
- Focused unit test for `HermesThemeRequest`: the accent mapping table, including `mono`, `nous` and `#rrggbb`.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatRequestTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests`.

## Mocks
Not required. Nothing new is drawn; the existing appearance changes.

## Outside reach
Step one runs the theme requests end to end on `scripts/local-hermes` in a disposable session. Nothing on the live host.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad, every Hermes chat and Bot Chat (both use `HermesChatRequests`). webui servers: n/a.
- The appearance setting belongs to the phone, for every server. Changing it from one server's chat is what the user asked the agent for. No per-server state is stored.
- The share extension, Live Activity widget, notification service, deep links and App Intents are not affected. They read the same stored appearance at their next launch.
- Docs: add the theme answers to `docs/agents/bots.md` § blocking requests, and the note change to `docs/agents/hermes-server.md:365-387`.

title: fix(chat): route /rollback to the rollback calls so a Webapp host stops refusing it
body:
**What the user gets:** `/rollback` in a Hermes chat lists the host's checkpoints, shows one's diff, and restores files from one, on both gateway types.
**Why it matters:** today a gateway's Webapp refuses `/rollback` outright, so the one way to undo an agent's file changes from the phone is broken. Hermes Desktop routes it around `slash.exec` for this reason.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes` with checkpoints turned on. No phone needed.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
Hermex sends `/rollback` through `slash.exec`. A Webapp's `command_verdict` answers `refused` for any command outside its read and control sets, and `rollback` is in none of them (`gateway/session_commands.py:133-146`). The host serves the same work as three RPCs that Hermex never calls.

## Hermex today
- `/rollback` is a catalog command, so `HermesSlashCommands.route` returns `.host` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesSlashCommands.swift:260-272`) and `run` sends `slashExec` (`:278-282`). Nothing is held (`SlashCommandCatalog.swift:261`).
- `ChatViewModel.runHermesSlashCommand` dispatches routes and shows a notice with `notifyLocally` (`ChatViewModel.swift:4590-4643`, `:4665-4667`).
- Precedents to copy: `/undo` re-reads the newest rows and replaces the transcript (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1053-1079`); `/personality` asks first through a pending value and a confirmation modifier (`ChatViewModel.swift:5019-5035`, `HermesChatSettings.swift:123,287-288`, `ChatView.swift:4886`); busy refusals already map to "Wait for the current reply to finish." for 4009 and Webapp `4001 session_busy` (`ChatViewModel.swift:6523-6549`).
- No `rollback.*` case in `HermesCall`; grep `rollback` in `HermesMobile/Networking` finds only the update client.

## Contract
Checked (2026-11-16): `rollback.list`, `rollback.diff` and `rollback.restore` answer on both gateway types. Read from source at the pin `3b421578`:
- Handlers: `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:1126-1190` (dashboard) and `gateway/session_tui_ops.py:29-32,205-300` (Webapp). All are live-session calls on the runtime id, like `session.undo`.
- `rollback.list {session_id}` → `{enabled, checkpoints: [{hash, timestamp (ISO 8601), message}]}`, newest first. Checkpointing is off by default on the host (`website/docs/user-guide/checkpoints-and-rollback.md:10`), which answers `enabled: false`.
- `rollback.diff {session_id, hash}` → `{stat, diff (at most 4000 chars), rendered?}`. `rendered` is terminal output; ignore it.
- `rollback.restore {session_id, hash, file_path?, all?}` → `{success, restored_to?, restored_files?, skipped_user_edits?, history_removed?, error?}`. A number or a hash is accepted (`tools/checkpoint_refs.py:13-23`). Without `file_path` it keeps the user's hand edits, is refused mid-turn (4009 on a dashboard, 4001 `session_busy` on a Webapp), and may rewind the newest turn (`history_removed`). A failed restore is `success: false` with an `error` sentence, not an RPC error.
- Desktop's routing: `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/slash-desktop-commands.ts:116-139` (parsing) and `:301-345` (calls and transcript reload).
- **Step one proves:** on `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes with `checkpoints.enabled: true`, in one disposable session, have the agent write a file, then list, diff and restore it, once per file and once whole-tree. On the Webapp, confirm a send after a whole-tree restore is accepted (the host rewinds through its own fenced mutation). Record sanitized replies as fixtures.

## Proposal
- `HermesCall`: `.rollbackList(runtime:)`, `.rollbackDiff(runtime:hash:)`, `.rollbackRestore(runtime:hash:filePath:)`. List and diff join `isCancellationSafe` and `timesOutLocally` (`HermesGateway.swift:605-628`); restore joins neither and is never retried.
- `/rollback` becomes one of Hermex's own commands: add it to `hermesCommands` (`SlashCommandCatalog.swift:224-252`) with a new `ServerSideAction.rollback` (`SlashCommand.swift:50-69`) and a `/rollback [diff N | N [file]]` hint.
- `HermesSlashCommands` gains `rollbackList`, `rollbackDiff` and `rollbackRestore`, sent through its existing `write` (`HermesSlashCommands.swift:305-316`).
- `ChatViewModel` parses the argument as Desktop does and answers as a notice: a numbered list (number, short hash, local time, message), a diff as its stat plus a ```` ```diff ```` fence, or the restore's outcome naming the files restored and the hand edits kept.
- Restore asks first through a pending value on the chat and a confirmation modifier beside the personality one. On Restore it sends the checkpoint's hash, never the number.
- When `history_removed > 0`, the coordinator re-reads the newest rows and replaces the transcript as `undo()` does (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1072-1078`).
- Docs: the slash routing order in `docs/agents/bots.md` § Slash suggestions, Hermes chats (`:1957-2010`) gains `/rollback`; `docs/agents/feature-gap-index.md:64` notes it ships for Hermes.

## Decisions
- **No checkpoints screen** (owner, 2026-11-16). Typed command only.
- **Restore confirms first** (owner). Whole tree: "Files the agent changed since this checkpoint go back to how they were. Edits you made yourself are kept. If the newest turn made these changes, it is removed from the chat." One file: "`name` goes back to how it was at this checkpoint. Its current content is overwritten."
- **Whole-tree restore mid-turn** (owner): refused before asking, with "Wait for the current reply to finish."; a host refusal maps the same way.
- **`enabled: false`** (owner): "Checkpoints are off on this Hermes host." with no further hint.
- **The number is resolved before asking.** Recommend reading `rollback.list` when the user runs a restore, showing that checkpoint's time and message in the confirmation, and sending its hash, so a checkpoint taken meanwhile can't shift what gets restored.
- **`--all`** (overwrite hand edits too): recommend leaving it out; it gets the usage notice. The host's default keeps hand edits, which suits a phone.
- **Bot Chat:** recommend allowing list, diff and a one-file restore, and refusing a whole-tree restore with the existing "A bot's chat can't be rewound." (`HermesSlashCommands.swift:87-88`, `HermesChatPolicy.refusal`).

## Acceptance and tests
- `/rollback` on a Webapp lists checkpoints instead of the refusal; `/rollback diff 1` shows a diff fence; `/rollback 1 notes.txt` restores that file after a confirmation; a whole-tree restore that rewinds removes the newest turn from the transcript.
- A host with checkpoints off says so; an unknown number shows the host's `error` sentence.
- Tests (extend `HermesSlashCommandTests`, using its fake wire):
  - `/rollback` sends `rollback.list` with the runtime as `session_id`, never `slash.exec`.
  - Confirming a restore of `1` sends the listed hash and `file_path` when given (assert those fields).
  - A reply with `history_removed: 1` replaces the transcript; `0` leaves it.
  - Cancel sends nothing.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSlashCommandTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesHistoryRewindTests`.

## Mocks
Not required: notices and a system confirmation, as `/personality` uses.

## Outside reach
None beyond `scripts/local-hermes`. Do not run a restore on the live host.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Hermes chats, typed or from the `/` panel and a hardware keyboard. webui chats are unchanged (their catalog has no `/rollback`).
- No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep link or App Intent.
- Multi-server: every call binds to the chat's runtime and attach generation; nothing is stored.
- New copy goes in the String Catalog.

title: feat(tasks): stop a running Task, choose what happens to missed runs, and show why a run stopped
body:
**What the user gets:** a Stop button on a running Task that ends the current run and keeps the schedule, a "Missed runs" choice in the Task editor, and history rows that say a run was stopped and why.
**Why it matters:** a Task burning tokens at 2 a.m. can only be paused or deleted from the phone today, and neither ends the run in flight. A run the host stopped shows no outcome at all.
**Cost:** Small. Simulator-testable; a Stop landing mid-run needs one real run on `scripts/local-hermes`.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
Run Now has no Stop. The host has a cancel route that stops only the live run, a three-way `catch_up` setting, and a stop reason in each stopped run's title. Hermex sends none of these and decodes neither the title nor the cancelled state, so a stopped run reads like nothing happened.

## Hermex today
- Writes are create, edit, pause, resume, delete and trigger (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCronClient.swift:36-89`; routes `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:236-249`). No cancel.
- "Running" is `fire_claim` present or `latest_execution.status` in `claimed`/`running` (`HermesCronClient.swift:282-288`). `CronExecution` decodes `status` only (`HermesMobile/Models/Cron.swift:253-262`); `live_execution` is never read.
- `CronJob` has no `catch_up` key (`Cron.swift:81-105`) and `CronJobEditorDraft` has no field for it (`Cron.swift:430-470`). The editor's Delivery section is where per-server fields sit (`HermesMobile/Features/Tasks/CronJobEditorSheet.swift:96-119`).
- The history row decoder has no `title` (`HermesCronClient.swift:239-242`). A row's outcome is running, completed or failed only (`HermesMobile/Features/Tasks/TaskDetailViewModel.swift:229-247`, `TaskRunHistorySection.swift:201-208`).
- A stopped Task ends with `last_status: "cancelled"` and no `last_error`, so `hasFailedRun` is false (`HermesMobile/Features/Tasks/TaskAgenda.swift:182-187`) and the header shows nothing about it.
- Run Now lives in the header footer (`TaskDetailHeaderCard.swift:132-139`), the detail toolbar (`TaskDetailView.swift:264-270`) and the list row's swipe and context menu (`TasksView.swift:298-304,318-331`). A Hermes Run Now follows the run by reading the list every 5 s (`TaskDetailViewModel.swift:444-552`).

## Contract
- **Checked (2026-11-16):** `POST /api/cron/jobs/{id}/cancel` is in the live host's `/openapi.json`. On `scripts/local-hermes` it answers `{success, cancelled, execution_id, detail, …}`; with no run in flight it is `cancelled: false` with a `detail` sentence. `catch_up` is `true` (one catch-up run), `false` (skip) or `null` (host default); a string is a 422 on create.
- **Read from source:** cancel targets the newest claimed or running attempt whose owner is alive (`cron/cancellation.py:224-242`, `cron/executions.py:704-732`), which the job list carries as `live_execution` beside `latest_execution` (`cron/jobs.py:1993-2002`). It covers a scheduler run hidden behind a refused Run Now's newer row. The reason sent is "cancelled on request (Stop)" (`hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py:708-714`). A cancelled run sets `last_status: "cancelled"` and clears `last_error` (`cron/jobs.py:2404-2407`).
