Create takes `catch_up` only when sent (`hermes_cli/web_models.py:349-350`, `hermes_cli/web_server_cron.py:284-285`); update stores `null` as "default" (`cron/jobs.py:1747-1751`); the host default is `cron.catch_up_missed: true` for recurring Tasks (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1780`). Run titles are `"<STATUS> · <reason or title>"` for cancelled session runs and for script-only runs (`hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py:343-357,587,608-621`); other session rows carry their session title.
- **Desktop:** in flight is `latest_execution.status ∈ {claimed, running}` or `live_execution` present (`apps/desktop/src/app/cron/run-control.ts:6-13`); it settles a Stop by the targeted `execution_id` (`run-control.ts:23-49`).
- **Step one proves:** on `scripts/local-hermes`, start a Task whose prompt runs about a minute, cancel it mid-run, and capture the job list and runs page before and after (sanitized) as fixtures. Confirm the list sends the `live_execution` key, null or not.

## Proposal
- `HermesREST.cronCancel(id:profile:)` → `POST …/cancel`, and `CronDataClient.cancelCronRun(jobID:profile:)`; webui's `APIClient` throws unsupported. Add `CronFeatures.stopsRuns`, true for Hermes.
- `CronJob`: decode `catch_up` (lossy bool), `latest_execution.error`, and whether the payload carries a `live_execution` key and its value. `CronJobList(hermesJobs:)` also counts a non-null `live_execution` as running.
- **Stop:** in the header footer it replaces Run now while the Task runs; in the toolbar menu and the list row's swipe and context menu it replaces Run Now. Confirm first. Accepted: show "Stopping…" and read the list every `runNowReadInterval` until the Task is no longer running, then "Stopped" when `last_status` is `cancelled`, else "Finished before it could stop". `cancelled: false` shows the host's `detail` and reloads. A Run Now already following that run on the screen settles it instead.
- **Header:** when the newest attempt was cancelled and nothing runs, a line "Last run stopped: <reason>" from `latest_execution.error`, not the red failure box.
- **History:** decode `title`; map a leading `CANCELLED`, `FAILED`, `MISSED` or `COMPLETED` label before " · " to a new `RunOutcome.stopped(reason)`, `.failed(reason)`, `.missed(reason)` or `.completed`. Any other title is a session title and is ignored.
- **Editor:** a "Missed runs" picker, Hermes only: Server default, Run once when back, Skip. Create sends `catch_up` only when not default; edit sends it only when it changed, `null` for Server default.
- Docs: a short paragraph in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` beside Tasks; `CONTEXT.md` gets "Stop (Task Run)".

## Decisions
- **Task templates (blueprints):** out, decided.
- **When Stop shows:** whenever the Task shows running on a host whose list carries the `live_execution` key. Recommend this key as the gate for both Stop and the Missed runs picker (same host work, inferred): a host without it shows neither.
- **Confirm Stop:** yes, "Stop this run? The Task keeps its schedule." Stopping cannot be undone.
- **Follow after Stop:** reuse the Run Now read loop and its 3-failure limit; leaving the screen ends the reads.
- **One-shot Tasks:** show the picker for every Task, as Desktop does.

## Acceptance and tests
- A running Task's Stop sends `POST …/cancel` with the Task's Profile; the Task then shows not running and "Last run stopped" with the host's reason. Pause, Resume and the schedule are untouched.
- `HermesCronClientTests`: a job with `live_execution` and a refused `latest_execution` counts as running (fails today); cancel sends the route and Profile; `cancelled: false` surfaces `detail`.
- `TaskRunHistoryTests`: a `CANCELLED · reason` row reads as stopped with that reason; a session title reads as no outcome.
- `CronManagementTests`: a job with `last_status: "cancelled"` shows stopped, not failed; edit sends `catch_up` only when changed, `null` for default.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesCronClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesRunNowTests --only HermesMobileTests/TaskRunHistoryTests --only HermesMobileTests/CronManagementTests`

## Mocks
Not required: a button that swaps with Run Now, one header line, one picker row and two history outcomes, all in existing components.

## Outside reach
None beyond read-only checks on the live host. The mid-run cancel is proved on `scripts/local-hermes` (step one); never cancel a run on the live host.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Tasks list and detail. No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links or App Intents (no Task intents exist).
- Multi-server: a Stop and its follow-up reads belong to the screen's server and Profile; a reply after a server switch is dropped. Nothing is stored.
- Strings: Stop, Stopping…, Stopped, Finished before it could stop, Last run stopped: %@, Missed runs and its three choices, the Stop confirmation. VoiceOver reads the Stop state.

title: feat(sessions): show a chat as working while its subagents or processes still run
body:
**What the user gets:** a session whose turn has ended but whose delegated subagents or background processes are still running keeps its Working label in the session list.
**Why it matters:** today such a chat reads as idle, so "is it actually done?" gets the wrong answer. Hermes Desktop shows these chats as working.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes`.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
A turn can end while work it started keeps going: `delegate_task(background=true)` returns as soon as it spawns children, and a background command outlives its turn. The session list asks the host only which runtimes are mid-turn, so these rows show no state.

## Hermex today
- Row states come from one `session.active_list` read plus `approval.pending` for waiting rows (`SessionListViewModel.readHermesStatuses`, `SessionListViewModel.swift:2375-2411`), mapped by `SessionRowAttentionState.hermesStates` (`HermesSessionPage.swift:351-359`).
- That read starts after each list read (`reloadHermes`, `SessionListViewModel.swift:1997`), so it runs on open, foreground (`HermesSessionListView.swift:388-394`), pull to refresh, a chat closing and `sessions.changed` (`:1790-1794`, debounced at `:2325-2333`).
- While any row is busy it re-reads every `statusPollInterval` (5 s, `:70-72`, `:2409-2410`).
- `subagent.roster` is not in `HermesCall.swift`. Subagents show only inside an open chat (`subagentList`, `HermesCall.swift:295`).
- The row already has a static Working label (`SessionRowView.swift:459-514`); `attentionState(for:)` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:700-703`) feeds it and the Needs you grouping.

## Contract
- **Checked (2026-11-16):** `subagent.roster` answers on both gateway types and returns `{sessions}`.
- **Read from source:** `tui_gateway/methods_subagents.py:121-145`. Params `{profile?}` (`ProfileParams` in `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json:4132`). Each entry is `{session_id, subagents, background}`, only for conversations stored in that Profile's store. No attached session is needed. `session_id` is the stored owner: a child's `owner_agent_session_id`, a process's `parent_session_id` (`:73-90`, `:106-118`). An empty roster is `{sessions: []}`.
- Desktop reads it on connect, on focus and every 10 s (`apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-live-work-roster.ts:72-118`) and keys rows by stored id across compression (`apps/desktop/src/store/live-work-roster.ts:1-15`).
- **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes` (both modes), in one disposable session, start a background command and a background delegation. Capture the roster reply. Confirm the entry shape, and whether `session_id` is the row's tip id or its lineage root. Also confirm that a child's work fires `sessions.changed` (`tui_gateway/change_watcher.py:278-289`). Delete only that session.

## Proposal
- `HermesCall.subagentRoster(profile: String)`, method `subagent.roster`, params `{profile}`. Add it to `isCancellationSafe` and `timesOutLocally` (`HermesGateway.swift:605-628`).
- In `SessionListViewModel`, a separate `hermesBackgroundWork: Set<String>` of listed session ids with any `subagents` or `background` above zero. Keep it apart from `attentionStatesBySessionID` so it never keeps the 5 s re-read alive.
- `startHermesRosterRead(wire)` beside `startHermesStatusRead(wire)` at `:1997`: one read per listed Profile (`hermesListedProfiles`, `:1883-1886`), in parallel. Only the newest read applies (a serial like `hermesStatusSerial`), and only while the same wire is live.
- `attentionState(for:)` returns the active-list state when there is one, else `.working` when the row's `sessionId` or `hermes.lineageRoot` is in the set. Approval and Input still win.
- Clear the set on `teardownHermes`, on a Profile switch (`showHermesProfile`, `:2211`) and while showing cached rows. A failed read clears it, so the rows behave as today. -32601 sets `hermesReadsRoster = false` for that socket, like `hermesReadsStatus` (`:227-228`).
- Docs: one sentence in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` § Reconnect contract, beside the live-state paragraph (`:555-572`).

## Decisions
- **Decided:** reuse the row's existing Working state; no new badge or count.
- **Decided:** read it alongside the existing live-state read, so on `sessions.changed`, on foreground, on open and on pull to refresh. Never on a timer, and never on the 5 s busy re-read. A background process that exits without a session write stays Working until the next of those reads; that is accepted.
- **Decided:** when the host answers -32601, the rows behave as today.
- **Scope:** the session list only. The Bots inbox and Live Activities don't change.
- **Matching:** match on both `sessionId` and `hermes.lineageRoot` until step one shows which id the host sends.

## Acceptance and tests
- A chat whose turn ended while a background delegation runs shows Working; it clears on the first list read after the children finish.
- A row waiting for an approval still shows Approval and stays in Needs you.
- A host without the method shows exactly today's states, with no error.
- Tests in `HermesSessionListTests` (extend `HermesSessionListWire`, `:1427`, with a scripted roster reply):
  - A row idle in `session.active_list` but listed in the roster reads `.working`; a roster id the list doesn't hold marks nothing; Approval beats it. Fails today.
  - The roster is read once per list read: several `statusPollInterval` ticks send no further roster call, and a `sessions.changed` sends one more.
  - -32601 leaves the states as `session.active_list` alone gives, and no later read sends the method.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests`.

## Mocks
Not required: the row reuses its existing Working label.

## Outside reach
None. Step one runs on `scripts/local-hermes` in one disposable session.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad session list (the split sidebar included). VoiceOver reads the existing "Working" label.
- No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep link or App Intent change.
- Multi-server: the set lives on the list's view model, which is rebuilt per server, and every read is checked against the list's own wire, so another server's roster never lands.

title: feat(git): Create Pull Request from the Git menu
body:
> **Partly done on `master`.** The Git menu already has Commit & Push beside Commit (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/GitActionsMenuButton.swift:95-98`), and the commit sheet has "Push after commit" (`GitCommitView.swift:228-246`). On a Hermes host both commit, then push with a separate call (`GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:484-496`). This issue is scoped to **Create Pull Request**; Commit & Push only needs checking (see Decisions).

**What the user gets:** once the agent is done on a branch, one tap in the Git menu opens a pull request on GitHub, after saying it will push the branch.
**Why it matters:** the Git menu shows a branch's PR (#1391) but can't make one, so finishing a run still needs a laptop or a prompt to the agent.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable, but proving it needs a disposable GitHub repository on the host (see Outside reach).

Part of #1726.

## Problem
Hermex reads the branch's PR from `ship-info` and never calls `create-pr`, which the host serves.

## Hermex today
- The PR section shows only when one exists (`GitActionsMenuButton.swift:11-12,34-48`); the Write section has Commit, Commit & Push and Push (`:87-104`). The menu is wired in `ChatView.gitActionsMenu` (`ChatView.swift:1714-1761`); Push already confirms through `GitChatAlert.confirmRemote` (`ChatView.swift:6-17,1942-1954`).
- `HermesGitClient.pullRequest()` reads `ship-info` and keeps only `pr` (`HermesGitClient.swift:528-539`), so "no `gh`" and "no PR" both read as nil. `ghReady` is dropped.
- `GitWorkspaceViewModel.pullRequest` and `refreshPullRequest` cache the read per branch for 60 s and re-read after a push (`GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:552-596`, `:502`).
- Every refused git write reads as `HermesGitRefusal.failed`, so no `detail` (which can name host paths) reaches the screen (`HermesGitClient.swift:22-24,632-648`, `:659-679`).
- `GitDataClient.pullRequest()` defaults to nil, so webui never shows a PR (`APIClient+Git.swift:64-66,98`).

## Contract
Checked (2026-11-16): `POST /api/git/review/create-pr`, `POST /api/git/review/commit` and `GET /api/git/gh-auth` are in the live host's `/openapi.json`; `gh-auth` answers `{authenticated, available}`. Read from source at the pin `3b421578`:
- `POST /api/git/review/create-pr {path}` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/git.py:197-199`, `hermes_cli/web_git.py:557-576`): pushes the current branch to its upstream, or `-u origin <branch>`, **ignoring a push failure**, then runs `gh pr create --fill` (title and body from the commits). Answers `{url}`, or 400 `{detail: "gh pr create failed: <gh stderr tail>"}`.
- `GET /api/git/review/ship-info?path=` → `{ghReady, pr: {url, state, number} | null}` (`web_git.py:479-487`), which Hermex already reads.
- `POST /api/git/review/commit {path, message, push}` (`web_git.py:389-403`): with `push: true` a failed push answers 400 after the commit landed.
- **Not exercised by anyone: Create PR.** Step one proves it on a disposable repository: one success, one refusal with no commits ahead of the base, and one where a PR already exists.

## Proposal
- `HermesREST.gitCreatePullRequest(repository:)` beside `gitShipInfo` (`HermesREST.swift:331-333,707-708`), with a provisioning deadline as push uses.
- `GitDataClient.pullRequest()` becomes a ship-info read that keeps `ghReady` with the PR (for example `GitShipInfo {ghReady, pullRequest}`); webui's default stays "not ready, none". Add `createPullRequest() async throws -> GitPullRequest?` with a webui default that throws unsupported.
- `HermesGitClient.createPullRequest()` takes the write lock and owner check every write takes (`beginWrite`, `writableRoot`), refuses a detached HEAD as `push()` does (`HermesGitClient.swift:397-405`), sends the route, then re-reads ship-info so the menu shows the new PR's number and state. A `url` that `InAppBrowserPolicy.opensInApp` refuses is dropped.
- `GitWorkspaceViewModel` keeps `ghReady` beside `pullRequestRead` and gains `createPullRequest()`, which runs like a remote action (`isRunningGitAction`, `actionErrorMessage`) and forces a PR refresh.
- `GitActionsMenuButton`: a "Create Pull Request" row in the PR section when `ghReady`, no PR is known for the branch, the HEAD is attached and not the default branch. It sets a new `GitChatAlert.confirmCreatePullRequest`; Create runs it with the existing git progress and result toasts (`ChatView.swift:1821-1851`); on success the menu's PR section shows the new PR, which opens as any PR does (`SafariView.present`).

## Decisions
- **Visibility** (owner): only when the host's `gh` is ready and the branch has no PR.
- **Asks first** (owner). Title "Create Pull Request?"; message "This pushes `<branch>` to its remote and opens a pull request on GitHub, titled from its commits."; buttons Create and Cancel.
- **Refusals never echo host paths** (owner). Recommend the generic "GitHub did not open the pull request. Check the branch on the host." for any 400, except "already exists" in `detail`, which re-reads ship-info so the existing PR's link appears. `detail` is matched, never shown.
- **The default branch:** recommend hiding the row there. The host would push it before `gh` refuses. Decode `isDefault` from `api/git/branches`, which the host already sends (`HermesREST.swift:315-318`) and the menu already reads.
- **Commit & Push** (owner: a plain second button beside Commit): already shipped. Recommend keeping commit then push as two calls rather than `push: true`. It reports "committed, push failed" separately, where `push: true` would turn a landed commit into a 400.
- **Draft PRs, reviewers, a custom title:** out. `--fill` only.

## Acceptance and tests
- On a branch with commits and no PR, the menu offers Create Pull Request; confirming opens a PR, and the menu then shows "Pull Request #N".
- Without `gh` (`ghReady: false`), on a branch with a PR, on a detached HEAD and on the default branch, the row is absent. webui chats never show it.
- A refusal shows the generic copy and no host path.
- Tests (`APIClientGitTests`, `GitWorkspaceViewModelTests` with `HermesHostFixture`):
  - Create sends `POST /api/git/review/create-pr` with the repository root as `path`.
  - A 400 whose `detail` names a host path surfaces only the generic message.
  - `ghReady: true, pr: null` offers the row; `ghReady: false` hides it.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientGitTests --only HermesMobileTests/GitWorkspaceViewModelTests`.

## Mocks
Not required: one menu row, a system alert and the existing toasts.

## Outside reach
Proving Create PR opens a real pull request on GitHub. Use a disposable repository the maintainer owns, with `gh` signed in on the host (`scripts/local-hermes` on this Mac is enough), and close the test PR afterwards. Never run it in Hermex's own repository or on the live host's working trees.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad, Hermes chats with a repository, from the Git menu (touch, pointer and hardware keyboard). Not the inline turn-end commit button.
- No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep link or App Intent.
- Multi-server: `ghReady` and the PR are held per chat's Git view model and branch, keyed by `reviewScope` (server, Profile, session, folder); nothing is persisted.
- New copy goes in the String Catalog; the row and alert get VoiceOver labels from their text.

title: feat(chat): steer one delegated worker
body:
**What the user gets:** a Steer action beside Interrupt on each delegated worker, so one worker going the wrong way can be corrected while its parent and siblings carry on.
**Why it matters:** today the only way to correct a worker from the phone is to interrupt it and lose its work. Hermes Desktop has had per-worker Steer for a while. This replaces #565, closed as not planned with "refile after 2.0 ships".
**Cost:** Small. Simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes`; no phone needed.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
The delegated-work sheet lists workers, loads a tail, and interrupts one. There is no way to send a worker a correction. The host takes one on both gateway types.

## Hermex today
- `HermesCall` has `subagentList`, `subagentTail` and `subagentInterrupt` only (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift:295-297`, methods `:584-586`, params `:833-834`, admission `:955-956`).
- `HermesDelegatedWork` owns the sheet's state, bound to `Context {connectionID, runtime, generation}` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesDelegatedWork.swift:121-129`). `interrupt(_:)` re-lists, checks the worker is still current, dispatches once through `validateDispatch`, and never retries (`:272-317`).
- Each worker row ends with Show tail and Interrupt; a sent interrupt reads "Interrupt sent" (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesDelegatedWorkView.swift:243-267`).
- `subagentInterrupt` is in neither `isCancellationSafe` nor `timesOutLocally` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:605-627`).
- `message(for:)` reads 4001 as "no longer owns these workers" (`HermesDelegatedWork.swift:385-388`). On a Webapp, 4001 means invalid parameters instead.
- `docs/agents/bots.md:410-411` says steering stays outside the allowlist.

## Contract
- **Checked (2026-11-16):** `subagent.steer` answers on both gateway types, on the live host (dashboard) and on `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes.
- **Read from source:** params `{session_id, subagent_id, text, profile?}`, result `{status: "queued" | "rejected", subagent_id, text}` (`tui_gateway/contracts/billing_delegation_pets.py:419-433`). Dashboard handler `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:2210-2224`: 4000 without `subagent_id`, 4002 for blank text, and `rejected` when the session doesn't own the worker or the worker stopped taking steering. Webapp handler `gateway/session_ancillary.py:38-63`: the worker must be a child of this session's live agent and still `accepting_steer`.
- **"queued" is not "delivered."** A worker past its last tool batch reports the text as `missed_steer` on its completion entry, and the parent sees "[steer did not land ...]" in the delegate result (`tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py:715-721`).
- Desktop's control: `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/subagent-controls.tsx:21-53`.
- **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes` (both modes), in one disposable session, start a delegated worker running a long tool, steer it, and capture the sanitized `queued` reply plus one `rejected` reply (steer a worker after it finishes).

## Proposal
- `HermesCall.subagentSteer(sessionID:subagentID:text:)`, method `subagent.steer`. Admit only non-empty ids and trimmed non-empty text. Classify it like `subagentInterrupt`: not cancellation-safe, not `timesOutLocally`.
- `HermesDelegatedWork.steer(_ worker:text:) async`: bound to the current `Context`, and `validateDispatch` checks the worker is still in the roster. Sent once, never retried. New state beside the interrupt pair: `steeringWorker` and `steeredWorker`, cleared by `disconnect()` and by `install(_:)` when the worker leaves.
- `HermesDelegatedWorkView.workerRow`: a "Steer…" button before Interrupt. It opens an alert with one text field and Send. `queued` shows "Steer sent" in the row; `rejected` shows "This worker is no longer taking steering."; a lost reply shows the existing "result is unknown" line.
- Update `docs/agents/bots.md:388-411` (Steer is now a worker write, and queued is not delivered) and point #565 at this issue.

## Decisions
- **No "pause new spawns."** Decided by the owner: it is global across the host and has no home in one chat.
- **No re-list before Steer.** Steer is not destructive, and the host checks ownership and `accepting_steer` at dispatch. Recommend keeping Interrupt's re-list for Interrupt only.
- **Copy is honest about delivery.** The alert's message: "The worker reads this after its current tool. If it is already finishing, it may not see it."
- **The text field in an alert, not inline in the row.** It keeps rows compact and needs no new layout. Mocks are not needed.
- **missed_steer is not parsed.** The parent agent already gets the note; Hermex shows no extra state for it.

## Acceptance and tests
- A live worker's row offers Steer. Sending text shows "Steer sent", and in step one's session the worker's result shows it acted on the text.
- A finished worker's steer shows the "no longer taking steering" line and no "sent" state.
- `HermesDelegatedWorkTests` (copy the interrupt harness, `:147` and `:226`):
  - Steer sends `session_id` = the runtime, the worker's `subagent_id` and trimmed `text` (assert those fields only).
  - `rejected` never shows "Steer sent".
  - A worker that left the roster, or an attach that changed before dispatch, sends nothing.
  - A double tap sends one call.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesDelegatedWorkTests`.

## Mocks
Not required: a button and a system alert inside the existing sheet.

## Outside reach
None. Step one mutates only a disposable session on `scripts/local-hermes`, whose test turns run tools. No live-host writes.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad: the delegated-work sheet in a Hermes chat and a Bot Chat (both own `HermesDelegatedWork` through `HermesChatActivity`, `HermesChatActivity.swift:137`). An offline cached chat shows no workers (`ChatView.swift:2277-2279`).
- Share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links, App Intents: not reached. Live Activity worker chips are unchanged.
- Multi-server: nothing is stored; every call is bound to the attach's connection, runtime and generation.
- Strings: "Steer…", "Steer sent", the alert title and message, and the rejection line go in the String Catalog. VoiceOver labels the button "Steer worker".

title: feat(sessions): filter the list by Working, Unread and Draft, and Mark All as Read
body:
**What the user gets:** the session list's Filter menu can show only Working, Unread or Draft chats, and can mark every unread chat in view as read in one tap.
**Why it matters:** on a phone, finding "what finished while I was away" or "what did I leave half-typed" means scrolling the whole list. Hermes Desktop has these filters and Mark All as Read.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
The list can be narrowed by Profile, project lane and search, but not by what a chat needs from the user. Marking read is one row at a time.

## Hermex today
- The home's Filter menu holds only the Profile picker (`HermesSessionListView.swift:727-754`).
- Rows are filtered and grouped in `SessionListViewModel.visibleSessions` and `scheduledSessionGroups` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:337-402`); the screen calls it with the lane and the hidden-row toggles (`HermesSessionListView.swift:685-691`). The lane lives in `HermesSessionListNavigation.selectedProjectID` (`:1332-1335`).
- Order is pinned first, then recency (`SessionListViewModel.swift:356`).
- Live states: `attentionState(for:)` (`:700-703`).
- Unread: `isUnread` (`:708-719`), `canToggleUnread` (`:723-731`), and a single chat is marked through `toggleUnread` → `setHermesUnread` (`:751-752`, `:2159-2172`). That writes `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` with `unread` and shows the mark at once, rolling back if the write fails. The row menu's Mark as Read is at `SessionListComponents.swift:1383-1388`.
- Drafts: `ChatDraftStore` keys a Hermes session's draft as `.hermesSession(connectionID:profile:key:cwd:)` (`ChatDraftStore.swift:182-218`), where `key` is the row's lineage root or stored key (`HermesConversation.swift:31-39`). `ChatDraft.isEmpty` is at `:99-102`. The store is not observable and can't list keys.
- The list already shows transient messages through `actionToast` (`HermesSessionListView.swift:87`, `:241`).

## Contract
No new API. Mark All as Read reuses the existing unread write (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py:933-940`), one per chat; the host has no bulk route (read from source). Desktop's Mark all as read (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/filter-menu.tsx:450-452`) only clears its own local set (`apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts:1571-1575`) and writes nothing to the host. Hermex writes the host's mark, as its single-row Mark as Read does, so the web dashboard and other devices agree.

## Proposal
- `enum HermesSessionStatusFilter { case all, working, unread, draft }` held beside `selectedProjectID` in `HermesSessionListNavigation`, passed into `scheduledSessionGroups` and applied in `visibleSessions` after the lane filter.
  - Working: `attentionState(for:) != nil`.
  - Unread: `isUnread`.
  - Draft: the row's `hermes.lineageRoot` or `sessionId` is in the list's draft-key set for that Profile.
- `ChatDraftStore.hermesSessionDraftKeys(server:connectionID:) async -> Set<DraftRow>` returning Profile and key for each non-empty `.hermesSession` draft with a key. The list reads it when Draft is picked and when a chat closes (`noteHermesReturn`, `SessionListViewModel.swift:1945`).
- A second `Section` in the Filter menu: a checked toggle for each status, then `Mark N Chats as Read`. Fill the filter icon while a status filter is on.
- `SessionListViewModel.markAllHermesRead(rows:) async -> Int` calls the same per-row path as `toggleUnread`, on rows where `isUnread && canToggleUnread`, at most four writes at a time. It awaits the writes and returns how many the host took. The screen shows "Marked N chats as read" in `actionToast` and posts it as a VoiceOver announcement; a failed write shows that row unread again, as today.
- Empty states under a filter: "No working chats", "No unread chats", "No drafts". Load more stays.

## Decisions
- **Decided:** no new sort orders. The host sorts only by date (`sessions.py:197-198`), so a client sort would cover only loaded pages.
- **Decided:** Mark All as Read covers the active server and the list's current scope: the shown Profile (every listed Profile while All Profiles is on) and the selected project lane. Search text and the status filter don't widen or narrow it. It says how many chats it marked.
- **Working** includes Approval and Input rows: a chat waiting on the user is still mid-turn. It picks up subagent and process work once the sibling "working rows" child lands, through `attentionState(for:)`.
- **One status at a time**, not combinable; picking it again goes back to All.
- **Not persisted:** view state, reset on a server switch or Profile change, like the lane.
- **Loaded rows only**, said in the empty state; filters never fetch more pages on their own.
- **No confirmation or Undo** for Mark All: each row's Mark as Unread is the way back, and the menu item names the count before the tap.
- **Hermes servers only.** webui lists get fixes only.

## Acceptance and tests
- Unread shows only unread rows of the current Profile and lane; picking it again shows all rows.
- With 3 unread rows in view, the menu reads "Mark 3 Chats as Read"; after the tap, all three show read, the host got 3 unread writes, and the toast says 3. Rows in another Profile, or on another server, stay unread.
- A chat with typed text and no send shows under Draft; one with an empty composer doesn't.
- Tests:
  - `HermesSessionListTests`: the Unread filter keeps only unread rows under a lane. Mark All writes `unread: false` for only the in-scope unread rows (assert ids and the field) and returns the confirmed count; a refused write leaves that row unread. Both fail today.
  - `ChatDraftStoreTests`: the new key read lists a non-empty Hermes session draft and skips an empty one, a new-session draft and another server's.
- Selection: `--only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests --only HermesMobileTests/ChatDraftStoreTests`.

## Mocks
Not required: one native `Section` in the existing Filter menu, the existing toast and the existing empty state. Owner set this `ready-for-agent`.

## Outside reach
None.

## Surfaces
- iPhone home and pushed list, and the iPad sidebar. Keyboard chat shortcuts (`HermesSessionListView.swift:677-680`) walk the filtered rows, as they walk a lane today.
- No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep link or App Intent change.
- Multi-server: the filter is per-list view state; the draft read filters by the list's server and connection UUID; writes go only through the list's own wire.
- Strings: the filter names, "Mark %lld Chats as Read" and "Marked %lld chats as read" as plurals in the String Catalog (`docs/agents/i18n.md`), and the three empty states.

title: feat(chat): show "Compacting context" while the host compacts
body:
**What the user gets:** while the host summarizes a long chat mid-turn, the run's status reads "Compacting context" instead of a bare "Working for".
**Why it matters:** auto-compaction can pause a turn for a minute or more with no output. Today that looks like a stalled stream, and users stop good runs or reconnect for nothing.
**Cost:** Small. Simulator-testable with a scripted stream; no phone needed.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
The host announces the start and the end of a compaction with `status.update` events. Hermex ignores the start, so the only sign of a compaction is a long silence and then a changed transcript.

## Hermex today
- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator` handles `status.update` only as the end of a `/compress` the host answered `pending` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1464-1466`, flag `compactionPending` at `:273-275`, `pendingCompactionDidFinish()` at `:1171-1178`).
- The transcript's tail row is `ChatWorkingRowView`: three static dots and "Working for 1m 3s", ticking once a second inside a `TimelineView` scoped to the row (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptSupportingViews.swift:1156-1192`). It is placed by `ChatTranscriptView.workingRow` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatTranscriptView.swift:686-693`) from `ChatWorkingRowPolicy.startedAt` (`HermesMobile/Config/AppTheme.swift:607-621`, called at `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:2686-2692`).
- Scrolled away from the bottom, the pill above the composer shows "Hermes is working · 2m 13s" (`ChatActiveRunStatusPresentation`, `AppTheme.swift:534-560`; kinds `:483-510`; view `HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatActiveRunStatusView.swift:8-43`, placed at `ChatView.swift:2166`).

## Contract
- **Checked:** nothing new is called; these are events Hermex already receives on both gateway types.
- **Read from source:**
  - Dashboard: `_status_update` re-tags an auto-compaction "lifecycle" line as `kind: "compacting"` (`tui_gateway/server.py:740-751`). The done edge is `kind: "compacted"` (`agent/conversation_compression.py:81,94-100`). A long compaction re-sends the progress line as a heartbeat (`:77`). An in-process `/compress` sends `kind: "compressing"` and always ends with `kind: "ready"` (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:2092-2093,2112-2115`). The compute host's late end is `compacted` (`tui_gateway/compute_host_bridge.py:410`).
  - Webapp: a local viewer's turn publishes `status.update` with the same re-tag (`gateway/run_turn_progress.py:1092-1095,1116-1119`).
  - Desktop treats `compacting`/`compressing` as the start and `compacted`/`ready` as the end, and also clears on a failed turn, `message.complete`, and `session.info {running: false}`, because a reconnect can miss the end edge (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/status.ts:80-91`, `session-info.ts:189-195`, `message-stream.ts:168`).
- **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes` (both modes), force an auto-compaction in one disposable session (a small context window and a long paste) and record the sanitized `status.update` frames into a scripted fixture.

## Proposal
- `HermesChatTurnCoordinator`: an observable `private(set) var isCompacting = false`. In the `status.update` case, `compacting` or `compressing` sets it; `compacted` or `ready` clears it (and the existing pending-`/compress` branch stays as is). Also clear it in `finish(_:)` (`:1310`), in `applyInfo(_:)` when the host reports not running (`:1506`), and on `conversationDidDisconnect` (`:2292`) and every reattach reset.
- `ChatViewModel` exposes it (`hermesTurn?.isCompacting == true`); `ChatView` passes it to the working row and to `ChatActiveRunStatusPolicy`.
- `ChatWorkingRowView` takes `isCompacting`: its label reads "Compacting context · 1m 3s" and its VoiceOver label "Hermes is compacting context, working for 1 minute 3 seconds". The pill reads the same.
- No new event handling for webui sessions.

## Decisions
- **A static line, no animation.** Decided by the owner. The row keeps its dots and its existing once-a-second elapsed label; nothing new repaints.
- **Same row, new words.** Recommend changing the working row's label rather than adding a second row, so the transcript's tail and the pill never disagree.
- **An idle `/compress` keeps today's feedback.** It has no working row, and its reply already reports the outcome. This child covers compaction during a run.
- **Clear on the turn's end too.** A lost `compacted` edge must never leave the line stuck.

## Acceptance and tests
- During a turn whose host auto-compacts, the tail row reads "Compacting context" from the `compacting` event until `compacted`, then "Working for" again.
- A reconnect that misses `compacted` shows "Working for" once the host reports the run (or its end).
- `HermesChatTurnTests` (scripted SSE, `HermesMobileTests/ScriptedSSEStreamFixture.swift`):
  - `compacting` mid-turn sets `isCompacting`; `compacted` clears it.
  - `session.info {running: false}` clears a compaction whose end never came.
- `TranscriptDisplayModelTests`: the pill's presentation carries the compacting label while compacting.
- `HermesCompressClearTests.testAPendingCompactionIsReadWhenTheHostFinishes` still passes.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests --only HermesMobileTests/TranscriptDisplayModelTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesCompressClearTests`, then `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests` (the tail row gains an input).

## Mocks
Not required: the existing row and pill with new copy.

## Outside reach
None. Step one uses a disposable session on `scripts/local-hermes` only.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad: a Hermes chat and a Bot Chat (same coordinator). Webui sessions: not reached.
- Live Activity: not reached; recommend leaving its status as is.
- Share extension, notification service, deep links, App Intents: not reached.
- Multi-server: nothing is stored; the flag lives on the chat's coordinator and is reset with its attach.
- Performance: the new input reaches only the tail row and the pill, never settled rows (`docs/agents/performance.md` § Before you change the transcript).
- Strings: "Compacting context · %@" and its spoken form go in the String Catalog.

title: feat(chat): answer the host's sign-in prompts: one-time code, saved login and password-manager unlock
body:
**What the user gets:** when the agent signs in to a site for them, the phone shows a card for the one-time code (iOS offers the code from Messages), for saving the site's login (with Password AutoFill), or for unlocking their password manager.
**Why it matters:** the owner wants 2FA to be first class. The text with the code usually arrives on the phone, but Hermex gives these prompts no card, so the agent waits out the host's timeout and the sign-in fails.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner's hands on a phone, because the Messages code suggestion and AutoFill only show on a device.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
The host's browser vault asks the attached viewer for three things: `vault.code`, `vault.save_login` and `vault.unlock_prompt`. Hermex answers none of them. The chat shows "waiting" with no card until the host gives up, and the agent then reports that the user declined.

## Hermex today
- These were answered once. #943 (commit `a44621cc5`, design A from #891) gave Bot Chat a card for each. #1148 removed that screen, and the vault kinds went with it.
- Today `BotCredentialRequest.Kind` knows only `sudo` and `secret`, and its doc says vault prompts are not read (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequest.swift:245-266`). `BotServerRequest` leaves them `pending: nil` (`:47-72`). `HermesChatRequests` documents them as "no card, never answered" (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesChatRequests.swift:14-17`).
- What still works: the open request keeps `isWaiting` true (`HermesChatRequests.swift:113`). `request.cancel` drops the matching envelope (`:512-524`). An attach's `open_requests` replaces the list (`:597-628`). The withdrawal note already files vault methods under `.other` (`BotPendingRequest.swift:610-625`).
- The card body for sudo and secret is `BotCredentialRequestBody`, a `SecureField` with `.password` (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequestCard.swift:381-461`). ChatView answers through `answerCredential` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:2117`), which sends `request.answer {value}` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift:463-474`).
- The list already lifts a waiting chat into "Needs you": the host reports a session with any open viewer request as `waiting` (`gateway/session_active_list.py:15-22`, `tui_gateway/session_registry.py:639-642`), and the list shows `.input` rows there (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:400`).
- No in-app banner exists for another chat. The list stops its status reads while a chat covers it (`SessionListViewModel.swift:1825-1829`).

## Contract
Read from source at the pin (`3b421578`). The vault prompts have not been run end to end.
- Params (`tui_gateway/contracts/server_requests.py:226-250`): `vault.unlock_prompt {backend, display_name}`, `vault.save_login {origin, site}`, `vault.code {site?, hint?}`. Every answer is `{value}`, and `''` means declined (`:26-30`).
- Timeouts: unlock 120 s, save login 180 s, code 180 s (`gateway/session_vault_prompt.py:22-24`; dashboard: `tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py:265-279`).
- Save login sends `value` as one JSON string, `{"identifier": "...", "password": "..."}`. A missing or empty field is a decline: "Do not ask again this turn" (`session_vault_prompt.py:59-66`, `tools/browser_vault_tool.py:362-364`). An empty unlock is `unlock_cancelled` (`:329-331`). An empty code is `code_declined` (`:463-465`). The host strips spaces and dashes from a code.
- Reconnect: both gateways put an unanswered vault prompt in `open_requests` (`gateway/session_server_requests.py:125-133`, `tui_gateway/server_requests.py:113-115,394-399`). Only vault preview operations are left out. The user guide's "not replayed" line refers to those (`website/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault.md:46-49`; `tui_gateway/server_requests.py:19-20`).
- **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes`, in one disposable session, trigger `vault.code` (a test page that asks for a code), answer it, then trigger it again and let it expire. Capture both frames and the `request.cancel`, then delete the session.

## Proposal
- **Model:** bring #943's kinds back into `BotCredentialRequest.Kind` (`vaultUnlock`, `vaultSaveLogin`, `vaultCode`). Read `display_name`, `origin`, `site` and `hint` tolerantly, and keep its `saveLoginValue(identifier:password:)` encoder. Map them in `BotServerRequest.init` (`BotPendingRequest.swift:58-63`).
- **Card:** extend `BotCredentialRequestBody`, starting from #943's design A, with one field layout per kind (see Decisions). Fields empty on send and are keyed by request id.
- **Answering:** reuse `answerCredential`. Skip sends `""`.
- **Banner:** see Decisions for its source. Show it on the active server only, with the chat's title, and open that chat on tap.
- **Docs:** update `docs/agents/bots.md:441-443,545-546` and `HermesChatRequests`'s doc comment.

## Decisions
- **Code field:** a visible `TextField` with `.oneTimeCode` and the number pad. Recommended over a masked field: the code lasts minutes, and the user needs to check the digits. It is sent as typed.
- **Save login:** "Email or username" (`.username`), and Return moves to a masked password (`.password`). Without an associated domain, iOS can't suggest the site's login on its own, but the key button opens the password list. Save needs both fields.
- **Unlock:** a secure field sent once. The host keeps only the manager's session token, for that session (`credential-vault.md:73-79`).
- **Nothing stored:** no Keychain, no draft, no SwiftData, no OSLog line with a value, and nothing posted as a prompt. One correction to "nothing enters the conversation": the host returns the identifier to the agent in the tool result (`browser_vault_tool.py:375`). The card says the password stays private, not the username.
- **Banner source (owner check):** while a chat covers the list, keep the list's existing status read running, at its 5 s busy-only cadence (`SessionListViewModel.swift:72,2375`), only while another listed row is working. Raise a banner when one turns Input or Approval. `session.active_list` doesn't say which prompt is open, so the banner reads "<chat> needs you" for any wait, not only sign-in prompts. The recommendation is to accept that. The alternative is attaching to every working session, which is far heavier.
- **Push:** none. The host doesn't announce vault prompts to plugins, which is an accepted host limit. Reopening the app inside the wait shows the card through `open_requests`.

## Acceptance and tests
- A `vault.code` card appears in the chat; typing the code from the Messages suggestion and tapping Send fills the page, and the turn carries on. Skip sends an empty value, and the agent stops asking.
- A save-login card sends one JSON string, and Save stays off until both fields are filled. An unlock card sends the password once.
- Backgrounding the app and reopening it within 180 s shows the same card. A host `request.cancel` removes it.
- From another chat on the same server, a banner names the waiting chat. Nothing shows for another server.
- Tests (all fail today): in `BotPendingRequestTests`, the three vault methods parse as answerable credentials with their params. In `HermesChatRequestTests`, a code sends `{value}` as typed, a save login sends identifier and password as one JSON string, Skip sends `""`, and a cancel removes the card. A hosted card test checks the code field's `.oneTimeCode` and the Save gate. Port #943's tests rather than writing new ones.

## Mocks
Required. Step one: static mocks of the three cards in a Hermes chat (light and dark, large text), starting from #943's design A, plus the cross-chat banner. Publish them and wait for a pick.

## Outside reach
Proving the prompts end to end (step one) needs `scripts/local-hermes` and a test page that asks for a login and a code. Nothing on the live host. A real password manager unlock is tested only with the owner's consent.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad, Hermes chats and Bot Chats. webui servers: n/a.
- Live Activity: the existing wait (#1014) already covers it through `onOpenChange`; verify only.
- The share extension, notification service, deep links and App Intents are not affected.
- Multi-server: the banner reads only the active server's list, and request state stays per runtime, as today.
- Strings: #943's 21 keys were removed. Re-add only the ones the picked mock uses, with VoiceOver labels for each field.

title: feat(mcp): show each MCP server's health and test it
body:
**What the user gets:** an MCP Servers page for a Hermes server that shows, per Profile, which servers are connected, failing, disabled or need sign-in, with a Test button that probes one server and says what went wrong.
**Why it matters:** "why did my agent lose GitHub?" has no answer on the phone. Hermex lists MCP servers only as on/off toggles in the Profile editor.
**Cost:** Small to Medium. Simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes`; mocks first.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
When an MCP server stops working the agent quietly loses its tools. The host keeps each server's state and can probe one on request, but Hermex never reads either.

## Hermex today
- No `mcp.servers.*` call: the only MCP field Hermex sends is `enabled_mcp_servers` on `profiles.configure` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift:1025`).
- The Bots-side Profile editor lists MCP servers with their transport and an enable toggle (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotProfileEditor.swift:34`, `BotProfileEditorView.swift:133,268-285`). No health, no test.
- Hermes Settings ends with Default Model, API Keys, Plugins and Connected Apps (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsServerPage.swift:194-219`). Plugins is the per-Profile page to copy: a `ServerProfileRow` (`PluginsView.swift:26`) and a model that loads over the gateway (`PluginsModel.swift:169`).
- Gateway call classes: `isCancellationSafe`, `timesOutLocally` and `deadline` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:605-651`); a `-32601` is remembered per connection (`HermesGateway.swift:517`).

## Contract
- **Checked (2026-11-16):** `mcp.servers.list`, `mcp.servers.status` and `mcp.servers.test` answer on a dashboard gateway and on a gateway's Webapp. `status` → `{checked_at, servers}`, each `{connected, disabled, name, needs_auth, plugin, source, status, tools, transport}`.
- **Read from source:** `status` reads cached runtime state and never connects or starts sign-in; without a multiplexer the runtime view exists only for the host's launch Profile (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:1480-1495`). `status` is `connected`, `disabled`, `connecting`, `failed`, `lazy` or `configured`; `needs_auth` means parked on a rejected OAuth credential (`tools/mcp_tool_discovery.py:824-883`). The failure text is not passed through (`methods_tools.py:1490`). `test {name, profile}` connects, lists tools and disconnects → `{ok, tools, prompts, resources, oauth_needed, oauth_tokens_present}` or `{ok: false, error, …}`; an `auth: oauth` server with no token fails as needing sign-in; a cold `npx` server can block a while (`methods_tools.py:1573-1600`).
- **Never send `reload.mcp`:** a gateway's Webapp refuses it (`tui_gateway/ws_legacy_fallback.py:46`).
- **Step one proves:** on `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes, capture `status` and one `test` reply for a working and a broken server (sanitized) as fixtures, and time a cold stdio test.

## Proposal
- `HermesCall.mcpServersStatus(profile:)` and `.mcpServerTest(name:profile:)`. Status is cancellation-safe and times out locally; Test times out locally with a longer deadline (recommend `standard * 4`) and is never retried.
- `HermesMCPHealth`, an `@MainActor @Observable` model built like `PluginsModel`: Profiles, the selected Profile, rows, one Test in flight per row, each result keyed by server, Profile and connection.
- Tolerant row model: name required, every other field optional, an unknown `status` displayed as the host wrote it.
- `MCPServersView` from a new "MCP Servers" row in Hermes Settings, after Plugins. Each row: name, transport, tool count, a state label (Connected, Failing, Disabled, Needs sign-in, Not started, Connecting), and Test. A Test result shows under its row: the tool count, or the host's `error`.
- Read on open, on Profile change and on pull-to-refresh. No timer. `-32601` shows "This server can't report MCP health" and hides the Settings row for the connection.
- Docs: a short "MCP health" paragraph in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`, including the `reload.mcp` warning.

## Decisions
- **Placement:** recommend a Settings page next to Plugins, since health is server administration and the Profile editor owns enabling. Decide from the mocks.
- **A Profile with no runtime view:** its servers read "Not checked" rather than a false Not connected, with Test as the way to know.
- **Sign In:** a needs-sign-in row shows the state only; the Sign In button arrives with the sign-in child.
- **Enable or disable here:** no; the Profile editor already does it.
- **Adding, editing and catalog install:** out, decided.

## Acceptance and tests
- A Profile with one working and one failing server shows each state; Test on the failing one shows the host's reason; Test on the working one shows its tool count.
- Switching Profile, or server, never shows the other's rows or a late Test result.
- New `HermesMCPHealthTests` with a fake wire (copy `PluginsModelTests`): status rows decode with missing fields and an unknown status; Test sends `name` and `profile`; `ok: false` shows `error`; a reply after a Profile switch is dropped; `-32601` hides the page.
- `HermesRequestTests`: the two calls' method names and params.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesMCPHealthTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesRequestTests`

## Mocks
Required. Step one is static mocks through `html-communication`: the Settings row, the page with mixed states and a Test result, a failing Test, the no-runtime Profile, light and dark, and large text. Publish and wait for a pick.

## Outside reach
None. Reads on the live host are fine; a Test there starts the server's process on the host, so ask before testing a server on it.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Settings. No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links or App Intents.
- Multi-server: nothing is stored; every result is bound to its connection and Profile.
- Native quality: state is a label plus a symbol, never color alone; VoiceOver reads name, state and tool count; a Test in flight reads "Testing…" as text, with no repainting animation.
- Strings: MCP Servers, the state labels, Test, Testing, the result lines, the unavailable message.

title: feat(mcp): finish an MCP server's sign-in on the phone
body:
**What the user gets:** Sign In on an MCP server that needs it, completed in a browser sheet on the phone, from the MCP Servers page and from the chat card that today says to finish on the Mac.
**Why it matters:** an MCP server whose token lapsed stays broken until the user is back at the host. Hermex hides the sign-in link on purpose because it assumed the redirect lands on the host's loopback; the host now lets the client own that redirect.
**Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner's hands on a phone for the browser hop.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
An MCP OAuth redirect goes to a listener on the host's own `127.0.0.1`, which a phone browser can't reach. The host now accepts a client loopback address instead and lets the client relay the code back, the pattern Hermex's browser sign-in already runs.

## Hermex today
- `finishesOnTheMac` hides the link for any MCP authorize row (`HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotPendingRequest.swift:437-442`); the card shows "Finish on the Mac." (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesRequestCards.swift:187-196`); tests pin it (`HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests.swift:322-332`).
- Browser sign-in binds `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port, keeps the first `/callback` whose `state` matches its own, and answers `302 hermexsignin://done` to close the sheet (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesBrowserSignIn.swift:21-58,119-214`; `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` § Browser sign-in). It keeps only `code`, matches a `state` it generated, and presents ephemerally (`HermesBrowserSignIn.swift:104-111`).
- Connected Apps presents a third-party sign-in with `.shared` so Safari's sign-ins carry over (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/ConnectedAppsView.swift:128-135`).
- No `mcp.servers.oauth.*` call exists (see the health child for the page this builds on).

## Contract
- **Checked (2026-11-16):** `mcp.servers.oauth.start` and `.oauth.poll` answer on both gateway types. Nobody has run an MCP sign-in end to end.
- **Read from source:** `oauth.start {name, profile, client_redirect_uri}` → `{ok, session_id, auth_url, flow: "pkce"}`; it waits up to 30 s for the URL (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py:1614-1636`, `tui_gateway/mcp_oauth_sessions.py:62-102`). The redirect must be plain `http` on `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1` with a port (`tools/connectors/mcp_oauth.py:208-216`). `oauth.callback {name, session_id, code, state, error, iss}` relays the redirect and the host checks `state` (`methods_tools.py:1654-1660`, `mcp_oauth_sessions.py:161-174`). `oauth.poll` → `pending`, `approved` (with `tools`) or `error` (`mcp_oauth_sessions.py:131-147`); `oauth.cancel {name, session_id}` (`methods_tools.py:1646-1651`). Desktop relays `iss`, which some providers require (`apps/desktop/electron/mcp-oauth-callback-ipc.ts:41-47`).
- **The card's flow stays on the host's loopback at this pin:** the chat card starts its attempt with `client_redirect_uri=None` ("supplies its advertised client redirect in a later part", `tools/connectors/mcp.py:114-118`) and registers it with the same table (`tools/connectors/mcp_oauth.py:315-335`). `oauth.start` refuses a second flow for a server while one is open ("already in progress", `mcp_oauth_sessions.py:73-78`). Skipping the row cancels the card's attempt (`tools/connectors/mcp.py:750-760`, `mcp_oauth.py:99-107`).
- **The running chat:** an RPC sign-in does not reconnect the live MCP connection (`mcp_oauth_sessions.py:84`, `mcp_oauth.py:81-83`). Never send `reload.mcp`.
- **Step one proves:** on `scripts/local-hermes` with a disposable OAuth MCP server, run start, browser, callback, poll to `approved` from the simulator; record the refusal code for "already in progress"; and find when a chat first sees the new tools (new chat, reopened chat).

## Proposal
- `HermesCall.mcpOAuthStart(name:profile:redirect:)`, `.mcpOAuthCallback(…)`, `.mcpOAuthPoll(…)`, `.mcpOAuthCancel(…)`. Start gets a deadline past the host's 30 s; none is retried blindly.
- Generalize `HermesLoopbackListener`: the expected `state` can be set after start (read from `auth_url`), and it records `code`, `state`, `error` and `iss`. Browser sign-in keeps its behavior.
- `HermesMCPSignIn.run(server:profile:connection:presenter:)`: bind, start with `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`, present `auth_url` with `.shared`, relay the callback, poll every second for up to 2 minutes while visible. A sheet closed without a callback sends `oauth.cancel`.
- **MCP Servers page:** Sign In on a row that needs it (`needs_auth`, or a Test with `oauth_needed`); success re-reads status.
- **Chat card:** replace the guidance with "Sign In on This iPhone", which answers Skip for that row, then runs the flow, retrying start once if the host still reports the card's flow open. The row then reads "Signed in. Ask Hermes to try again." Remove `finishesOnTheMac`.
- Docs: `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` gets an "MCP sign-in" paragraph next to Browser sign-in.

## Decisions
- **Path:** the RPC client-loopback path, not the host-callback REST route, which an access proxy in front of the host blocks. Decided.
- **The chat card (needs the owner):** retiring "Finish on the Mac" is only possible by skipping the row first, so the agent hears "skipped" for this request. Recommend Skip-then-sign-in with the copy above. The alternative is to keep the card as is until upstream gives the card a client redirect, and ship only the page's Sign In.
- **Browser session:** `.shared`, as Connected Apps does, so a provider the user is signed in to in Safari needs no password.
- **After sign-in:** say "New chats can use it" only if step one shows that; otherwise say what step one found.

## Acceptance and tests
- From the MCP Servers page, a server needing sign-in signs in on the phone and then reads Connected after refresh.
- Closing the sheet early cancels the host's flow; a refused callback shows the host's `error_message`.
- `HermesBrowserSignInTests`: the listener keeps `code`, `error` and `iss` from a `/callback` whose `state` matches one set after start, and ignores another `state`.
- New `HermesMCPSignInTests` with a scripted wire and presenter: start sends a loopback `client_redirect_uri`; the callback relays `code`, `state` and `iss`; a closed sheet sends `oauth.cancel`; a poll `error` surfaces.
- `BotPendingRequestTests`: the card's sign-in answers Skip for that row before it starts (replaces `:322-332`).
- Selection: `--only HermesMobileTests/HermesBrowserSignInTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesMCPSignInTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests`

## Mocks
Not required: one button on the health page's row and new copy on an existing card. The card copy needs the owner's yes (Decisions).

## Outside reach
Owner on a phone: one real provider sign-in through the sheet. On the live host, signing an MCP server in writes its tokens; ask before doing it there.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad: MCP Servers page, and the connection card in Hermes chats and Bot chats. No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links or App Intents.
- Multi-server: a flow is bound to its connection and Profile; a server switch cancels it and drops any late reply.
- Backgrounding: a listener iOS reclaims shows "can't connect" in the sheet, as browser sign-in documents; signing in again recovers.
- Strings: Sign In, Sign In on This iPhone, Signed in. Ask Hermes to try again., the failure lines.

title: feat(messaging): approve or revoke people on the messaging bot
body:
**What the user gets:** a Messaging Access page for a Hermes server that lists who asked to talk to the agent through Telegram, Discord or another messaging platform, with Approve, and who already has access, with Revoke.
**Why it matters:** someone DMs the bot and waits until the owner is back at the host. Letting a person in, or cutting them off, is a two-tap job that belongs on the phone.
**Cost:** Small. Mocks first; a real approval needs a real pairing request.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
A new person who messages a Hermes bot gets a pairing request that only the host's dashboard, CLI or Hermes Desktop can approve. Hermex has no view of pending or approved people.

## Hermex today
- No pairing call. The word "pairing" in the app means push pairing with hermex-push (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:511`), a different thing; this feature must not reuse that name in code or copy.
- Messaging platforms are read only to warn before a plugin toggle (`HermesREST.swift:182-184,508`; `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesPluginsClient.swift:356`).
- API Keys hides channel-managed credentials on purpose (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesEnvironmentClient.swift:137-144`).
- Hermes Settings rows live at `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsServerPage.swift:194-219`; API Keys is the per-Profile page pattern (`APIKeysView.swift:47`, `APIKeysModel.swift:46-53`).
- Gateway change events are read only for `sessions.changed` (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:1790-1794`, `HermesMobile/Features/Bots/BotInbox.swift:408`).

## Contract
- **Checked (2026-11-16):** `GET /api/pairing`, `POST /api/pairing/approve` and `POST /api/pairing/revoke` are in the live host's `/openapi.json`; `GET /api/pairing` → `{approved, pending}`. No approval has been exercised.
- **Read from source (`hermes_cli/web_routers/ops.py:84-135`, `gateway/pairing.py`):**
  - `GET /api/pairing?profile=` → `pending: [{platform, request_id, user_id, user_name, age_minutes}]`, where an older entry has an empty `request_id` and can only be approved by its code (`pairing.py:557-575`); `approved: [{platform, user_id, user_name, approved_at}]` (`pairing.py:424-430`). Codes are never returned.
  - `POST /api/pairing/approve {platform, request_id, profile}` → `{ok, user}`; 404 when the request expired; 429 only on the code path's lockout. Approving also adds the person to the platform's allowlist when one is configured (`pairing.py:432-441`).
  - `POST /api/pairing/revoke {platform, user_id, profile}` → `{ok}`; 404 when not approved. It removes the allowlist entry too (`pairing.py:443-458`). Bodies: `hermes_cli/web_models.py:385-394`.
  - `pairing.changed` comes on the gateway socket about 2 s after any Profile's ledger changes; it names no Profile (`tui_gateway/change_watcher.py:303-313,378-389`).
- **Desktop:** refreshes on `pairing.changed`, approves by `request_id` only, and skips rows without one (`apps/desktop/src/app/messaging/index.tsx:291-301,507-556`).
- **Step one proves:** on `scripts/local-hermes`, make one pending request with the host's own `PairingStore.generate_code` (`gateway/pairing.py:475`), approve it from the simulator, revoke it, and confirm `pairing.changed` arrives on both gateway types. Capture the replies (sanitized) as fixtures.

## Proposal
- `HermesREST.pairing(profile:)`, `.pairingApprove(platform:requestID:profile:)`, `.pairingRevoke(platform:userID:profile:)`.
- `HermesMessagingAccessClient` and an `@MainActor @Observable` `MessagingAccessModel`: Profiles, the selected Profile, pending and approved rows, one write per row at a time. Tolerant decoding; a row without `platform` or `user_id` is dropped. Platform names come from `.messagingPlatforms(profile:)`, falling back to the id.
- `MessagingAccessView` from a "Messaging Access" row in Hermes Settings, with a `ServerProfileRow`. Sections: Waiting (name, platform, how long ago, Approve) and Has access (name, platform, Revoke).
- Live refresh: while the page is visible, hold a gateway wire and reload on `pairing.changed`; also reload on foreground and pull-to-refresh. No timer.
- Writes are not optimistic: a row shows its pending state until the host answers, then the list reloads. 404 reloads and says the request expired or the person was already removed.
- Docs: a "Messaging access" paragraph in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`; `CONTEXT.md` defines Messaging Access and keeps it apart from push pairing.

## Decisions
- **Approve copy:** decided, it says Approve gives that person access to the agent. Recommend a confirmation: "Approve <name>? They can message your agent on <platform> and it will act for them."
- **Revoke copy:** confirm, "Remove <name>? They can no longer message your agent on <platform>."
- **Platform setup** (tokens, test, Telegram QR): out, decided.
- **Older entries with no `request_id`:** shown without Approve, with "Approve this one on the host." No code entry field.
- **Clear all pending** (`POST /api/pairing/clear-pending`): not offered.
- **Placement:** recommend Settings, after Connected Apps; decide from the mocks.

## Acceptance and tests
- A pending request shows with its platform and age; Approve moves it to Has access after the host answers; Revoke removes an approved person.
- A pairing request made while the page is open appears without a manual refresh.
- New `MessagingAccessModelTests` with a scripted connection: decode with missing names and an empty `request_id`; Approve sends `platform`, `request_id` and `profile`; Revoke sends `platform`, `user_id` and `profile`; a 404 reloads and shows the expired line; `pairing.changed` triggers a reload; a reply after a Profile switch is dropped.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/MessagingAccessModelTests`

## Mocks
Required. Step one is static mocks through `html-communication`: the Settings row, the page with waiting and approved people across two platforms, the empty state, both confirmations, an older entry, light and dark, large text. Publish and wait for a pick.

## Outside reach
A real approval needs a real person messaging a real bot. Prove the contract on `scripts/local-hermes` (step one). Never approve or revoke anyone on the live host without the owner.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Settings. No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links or App Intents.
- Multi-server: nothing is stored; rows and the event wire are bound to the screen's connection and Profile, and leaving or switching servers closes the wire.
- Native quality: VoiceOver reads name, platform and age; Approve and Revoke are labeled actions; no animation.
- Strings: Messaging Access, Waiting, Has access, Approve, Revoke, both confirmations, the expired line, the older-entry line, the empty state.

title: feat(settings): sign a subscription provider back in
body:
**What the user gets:** a Subscriptions page for a Hermes server that lists the account-based providers (Nous Portal, ChatGPT or Codex, xAI Grok, MiniMax and the rest the host offers) with Sign In and Disconnect, where Sign In shows a code and opens the provider's page on the phone.
**Why it matters:** when a subscription's token lapses the agent stops answering, and today the only fix is a terminal or browser on the host. A device-code sign-in is a phone-shaped job: open a link, enter a code.
**Cost:** Small to Medium. Mocks first; one real sign-in needs the owner's account on a phone.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
Hermex can write API keys but cannot sign an account-based provider in or out. The host runs those sign-ins as device-code flows any signed-in client can drive.

## Hermex today
- No `/api/providers/oauth` call anywhere in the app.
- API Keys writes a Profile's `.env` keys only (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/APIKeysView.swift:47`, `APIKeysModel.swift:46-53`); it is the per-Profile page pattern to copy.
- Providers is a read-only webui screen (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/ProvidersView.swift:1-8`), not shown for Hermes.
- Connected Apps opens a Nous Portal sign-in with a `.shared` browser session (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/ConnectedAppsView.swift:128-135`) and has a dead end for a Profile with no Nous sign-in (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnectedAppsClient.swift:83`).
- Hermes Settings rows: `HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsServerPage.swift:194-219`. A REST request gets 15 s per attempt under `.standard` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:29-39`).

## Contract
- **Checked (2026-11-16):** `GET /api/providers/oauth` and its `start`, `submit` and `poll` routes are in the live host's `/openapi.json`; the list → `{providers}`, and the live host's flows are `device_code` and `external`. No sign-in has been exercised.
- **Read from source (`hermes_cli/web_routers/oauth.py`):**
  - List `?profile=` → each `{id, name, flow, cli_command, docs_url, disconnect_hint, disconnect_command, disconnectable, status}`; `status` is `{logged_in, source, source_label, token_preview, expires_at, has_refresh_token, …}` (`oauth.py:718-736,361-371`). Built-in rows: `hermes_cli/web_server_oauth.py:123-146`.
  - `POST /api/providers/oauth/{id}/start?profile=` → `{session_id, flow: "device_code", user_code, verification_url, expires_in, poll_interval}`. An `external` provider is a 400 naming its command; any other flow is "Unsupported flow" (`oauth.py:143-154,841-867`).
  - `submit` is a 400 for every provider at this pin (`oauth.py:896-902`). Not used.
  - `GET …/{id}/poll/{session_id}?profile=&wait=` long-polls up to 25 s → `{status, error_message, expires_at, reason, account_email, model, …}`; status is `pending`, `approved`, `denied`, `expired`, `error` or `cancelled` (`oauth.py:97,910-953`). A Nous sign-in can report the default `model` it switched the Profile to.
  - `DELETE /api/providers/oauth/{id}?profile=` disconnects, refused when `disconnectable` is false (`oauth.py:659-672,774-800`); `DELETE /api/providers/oauth/sessions/{session_id}` cancels a pending sign-in (`oauth.py:975-983`).
- **Step one proves:** on `scripts/local-hermes`, read the list, start one device-code sign-in, long-poll it, and cancel it (no account needed), capturing sanitized replies as fixtures. Also check that cancelling the task presenting the browser closes its sheet, since a device-code page never redirects back.

## Proposal
- `HermesREST` cases for list, start, poll (`wait: 10`, inside the 15 s attempt), disconnect and cancel; a `HermesProviderAccountsClient` that decodes tolerantly (a row needs `id` and `name`; an unknown `flow` is treated as `external`).
- `ProviderAccountsModel` (`@MainActor @Observable`): Profiles, rows, and at most one sign-in in flight, bound to its connection, Profile and `session_id`.
- `ProviderAccountsView` from a "Subscriptions" row in Hermes Settings, with a `ServerProfileRow`. Each row: name, Signed in or Signed out, and Sign In or Disconnect.
- **Sign In:** start, then a sheet with the code large and selectable, a Copy button, and Open Sign-In Page. Copy the code first, then open the `https` `verification_url` in an `ASWebAuthenticationSession` with `.shared`, as Connected Apps does. Long-poll while the sheet shows; `approved` closes it and re-reads the list; `denied`, `expired` or `error` shows the host's words and offers Try Again. Closing early sends the cancel.
- **Disconnect:** only where `disconnectable` and signed in, after a confirmation.
- Docs: a "Subscription sign-in" paragraph in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md`.

## Decisions
- **Scope:** sign-in and disconnect only, decided. This is not the Providers status screen #1668 ruled out: no model catalog, no token details, no source labels.
- **`external` providers:** list them with their state and "Sign in on the host", with the host's `cli_command` as selectable text and a Copy button, plus `docs_url` when given. No Sign In button.
- **A Nous sign-in that changed the default model:** show "Hermes now uses <model> by default" from the poll's `model`.
- **Connected Apps' needs-Nous dead end:** not linked here; a follow-up if the owner wants it.
- **Placement and name:** recommend "Subscriptions" after API Keys; decide from the mocks.

## Acceptance and tests
- A signed-out device-code provider signs in from the phone; the row then reads Signed in. Disconnect signs it out after the confirmation.
- An `external` row offers its host command and never a Sign In.
- Switching Profile or server during a sign-in cancels it and never shows its result elsewhere.
- New `ProviderAccountsModelTests` with a scripted connection: decode with missing fields and an unknown flow; start then poll to `approved` re-reads the list; `expired` shows the host's line; closing the sheet sends the cancel with the `session_id`; Disconnect is absent when `disconnectable` is false.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ProviderAccountsModelTests`

## Mocks
Required. Step one is static mocks through `html-communication`: the Settings row, the list with signed-in, signed-out and external rows, the code sheet waiting and failed, the Disconnect confirmation, light and dark, large text. Publish and wait for a pick.

## Outside reach
A real sign-in needs the owner's provider account on a phone. On the live host a sign-in or disconnect changes which account the agent bills; ask before either.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Settings. No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links or App Intents.
- Multi-server: nothing is stored on the phone; the code and session exist only while the sheet shows.
- Backgrounding: a long-poll cut by suspension polls again on foreground until `expires_at`.
- Native quality: the code is selectable and VoiceOver reads it character by character; no repainting animation while waiting.
- Strings: Subscriptions, Sign In, Disconnect, Signed in, Signed out, Sign in on the host, Open Sign-In Page, Copy Code, the waiting and failure lines, the confirmation.

title: feat(voice): read replies aloud as they stream
body:
**What the user gets:** a "Read replies aloud" switch. With it on, each new reply in a Hermes chat is spoken sentence by sentence as it streams, in the Profile's own voice. Listen on any message has no length cap. **Why it matters:** this is eyes-free use of the agent while walking or cooking. Today speech only starts after the whole clip is made, and replies over 4,000 characters fall back to the on-device voice. **Cost:** Medium. Needs the owner's hands on a phone: audio routes, the Ring/Silent switch, interruptions and a tunnel can't be judged on the simulator. Part of #1726. ## Problem Hermex speaks only on a tap. Listen asks the host for one finished clip of up to 4,000 characters and plays it. The host already offers a streaming speech socket that turns text into audio as it arrives. ## Hermex today - Listen: `ChatViewModel.toggleListening` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift:6642-6696`) asks for server speech under `ServerTTSPolicy.maximumHermesTextLength = 4000` (`:9472-9488`) and otherwise speaks on device. On a Hermes server the speech comes from `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.speech(for:)` (`HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:918`, wired at `ChatViewModel.swift:904-916`), which calls `BotClient.speech` with `POST /api/audio/speak` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Bots/BotClient.swift:152-163`, `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesREST.swift:730-732`). - Playback is one `AVAudioPlayer` built from `Data` (`ChatViewModel.swift:7884`), with the playback bar, speed and Lock Screen controls (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/ChatView.swift:142`, `ChatViewModel.swift:972`). The audio session is `.playback` / `.spokenAudio` (`ChatViewModel.swift:9679-9682`). The app has the `audio` background mode (`HermesMobile/Resources/Info.plist:135-138`). - Reply text arrives as `message.delta` in `HermesChatTurnCoordinator.apply(_:live:)` (`HermesMobile/Features/Chat/HermesChatTurnCoordinator.swift:1363,1386-1393`). Leaving or backgrounding the chat drops its socket (`:2149-2156`). - Socket sign-in: `HermesConnection.upgrade` mints a dashboard ticket (`POST /api/auth/ws-ticket`) or a Webapp one (`POST /api/webapp/socket-ticket?socket=gateway&profile=`), or uses a page token (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesConnection.swift:556-590`, `HermesREST.swift:446-452`). `kanbanEventsUpgrade` already presents a ticket as `?ticket=` (`HermesREST.swift:843-855`). ## Contract Read from source at the pin (`3b421578`). Not exercised. - `WS /api/audio/speak-stream?profile=

`, one socket per stretch of speech. Client → `{"text": "..."}` (incremental), `{"done": true}`, `{"stop": true}` (or a disconnect) to cut it off. Server → `{"type": "start", "sample_rate": N, "channels": 1}`, then binary int16 PCM frames, then `{"type": "end"}`. The server sends `{"type": "fallback"}` only when synthesis produced no audio. Close code 4401 means bad credentials, 4403 a refused origin (`hermes_cli/web_routers/audio.py:604-785`). - Providers with no chunked API (Edge, the default) still stream PCM, one sentence at a time (`audio.py:657-661`). The host cuts sentences, strips Markdown, and flushes after about 2 s of quiet (`:690-740`). - Sign-in: on a dashboard, an unnamed `ws-ticket` opens any socket but the host terminal and relay (`hermes_cli/web_session_sockets.py:37-43,52-60`). On a Webapp, mint `socket-ticket?socket=speak-stream`, which doesn't check the profile (`hermes_cli/web_routers/webapp.py:217-250`). Present the ticket as `?ticket=` (`hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py:377-393`). - **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes, open the socket with each ticket kind and with a page token, send two sentences and `done`, and record the frames. Note `sample_rate` for Edge and for one chunked provider if one is set up. ## Proposal - **Wire:** `HermesREST.speakStreamUpgrade(base:profile:pass:)`, built like `kanbanEventsUpgrade`. Give `.profileTicket` a `socket` argument (default `gateway`). Add `HermesConnection.speakStreamUpgrade(profile:)`, which picks the Webapp or dashboard ticket the way `gatewayUpgrade` does. - **Engine:** a new `HermesSpeechStream` (`@MainActor`, injectable for tests). It owns one `URLSessionWebSocketTask`, an `AVAudioEngine` with an `AVAudioPlayerNode`, and its format from the `start` frame (int16 mono at `sample_rate`). It has `feed(_ text:)`, `finish()`, `stop()` and `onEnd`/`onFallback`. No new dependency. - **Read aloud:** a phone-wide `@AppStorage` switch, "Read replies aloud", in Settings beside Dictation Provider (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsAppPages.swift:42-53`). When it's on, the coordinator feeds `message.delta` text into one `HermesSpeechStream`, but only for live frames (`live == true`), never history or a replay. It calls `finish()` at `tool.start` and `message.complete` (`:1406,1428`) and opens a new stream at the next delta. - **Listen:** on a Hermes server, Listen sends the whole message text and `done` over the same socket, gathers the PCM, wraps it as WAV `Data`, and hands it to the existing player. The bar, speed, seek and Lock Screen controls stay as they are, and `maximumHermesTextLength` goes. webui Listen is unchanged. ## Decisions - **One socket per stretch, not per turn:** finishing at `tool.start` means the socket never sits quiet through a tool run, where a tunnel such as Cloudflare would close it. If a socket closes mid-stretch, the audio already queued plays out and the next delta opens a new socket. Sent text is never resent. - **Fallback:** on `{"type": "fallback"}`, or when the socket fails to open, speak that stretch on device (`OnDeviceSpeech`, `ChatViewModel.swift:9577`).
