- **Bulk reclaim:** not offered.

## Acceptance and tests
- Reclaim on a Running Card stops its worker and the Card shows in Ready after the Board reloads; Terminate Run on the open run does the same.
- Neither shows on webui, on a Card that is not Running, or on a run that has ended.
- `HermesKanbanClientTests`: reclaim and terminate hit their routes with `board` and a `reason`; 409 surfaces the host's `detail` (fails today: no routes).
- `KanbanFeatureStateTests`: a reclaim whose reply was lost settles as succeeded when the Card reads Ready and as failed when it still reads Running.
- `KanbanCardDetailStateTests` or a view-model test: Terminate is offered only for an open run with a numeric id.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesKanbanClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanFeatureStateTests --only HermesMobileTests/KanbanCardDetailStateTests`

## Mocks
Not required: one menu action, one row button and two confirmations in existing components.

## Outside reach
None. Never reclaim or terminate on the live host's Boards; prove it on `scripts/local-hermes` with a disposable Board and no billable model.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Kanban Card detail. No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links or App Intents.
- Multi-server: nothing stored; the write and its reload belong to the Card's server and Board.
- Native quality: VoiceOver labels "Reclaim Card" and "Stop this run"; no animation.
- Strings: Reclaim, Terminate Run, both confirmations, the Review variants.

title: feat(widgets): Control Center and Lock Screen controls for New Chat and voice
body:
**What the user gets:** two controls the user can add to Control Center, the Lock Screen or the Action Button: New Chat, and New Chat with Voice. One press opens Hermex on a new chat, with the mic already listening for the voice control.
**Why it matters:** this is the phone's answer to Desktop's Quick Entry hotkey. Today the same actions need a Shortcut or the Action Button set up by hand.
**Cost:** Small. Needs the owner's hands on a phone: Control Center and Lock Screen controls can't be fully checked in the simulator.

Part of #1726. #6 stays the Home Screen widget issue; this one adds only iOS 18 controls.

## Problem
Hermex already has the intents (New Chat, New Chat with Voice) but no `ControlWidget`, so none of them can be placed in Control Center or on the Lock Screen.

## Hermex today
- `NewChatIntent` and `NewChatVoiceIntent` open the app and queue `HermesDeepLink.newChatURL` or `newChatVoiceURL` through `AppIntentRouter` (`HermesMobile/AppIntents/HermexAppIntents.swift:59-94`). Both URLs are built in `HermesMobile/LiveActivities/HermesDeepLink.swift:32-37,51-56`, and `ContentView` routes them (`HermesMobile/ContentView.swift:171`).
- The intents' file and `AppIntentRouter` are in the main app only. `HermesDeepLink.swift` is already in the widget extension (`HermesMobile.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:3504`).
- The widget extension's bundle holds the agent-run Live Activity, Provider Limits and the Bot widget (`HermesLiveActivityWidget/AgentRunLiveActivityWidget.swift:5-12`). A search finds no `ControlWidget` anywhere.
- The extension already shares the String Catalog (`project.pbxproj`, the `HermesLiveActivityWidget` Resources phase). It also shares an intent file with the app: `HermesMobile/Widgets/BotWidgetIntent.swift` is in both targets (`project.pbxproj:18-19`).
- The deployment target is iOS 18.0 for every target (`project.pbxproj:3596`), so the controls need no availability check.

## Contract
None. This is local only and makes no server call.

## Proposal
- **New file, widget target only:** `HermesLiveActivityWidget/NewChatControls.swift` with two `ControlWidget`s: `NewChatControl` ("New Chat", `square.and.pencil`) and `NewChatVoiceControl` ("New Chat with Voice", `mic`). Each is a `ControlWidgetButton` whose action is `OpenURLIntent` with the matching `HermesDeepLink` URL. Add both to `HermesLiveActivityWidgetBundle`.
- **Step one:** on a phone, prove that `OpenURLIntent` with Hermex's own scheme opens the app and lands on New Chat from Control Center, from the Lock Screen while locked (which asks for Face ID first), and on the Branch build, whose scheme differs.
- **If step one fails:** move the two intents' declarations into `HermesMobile/Widgets/` with both target memberships, following `BotWidgetIntent.swift`, and keep their app-only work out of the widget's build.

## Decisions
- **`OpenURLIntent` first:** it reuses the deep links the intents already queue, with no new intent types and no app code in the widget. The fallback is the shared-intent file.
- **Two controls only.** New Chat in Profile and New Chat with Content need a configuration or text the control can't hold. Profile-pinned controls can come later through #6.
- **#1402's rule still holds:** no control carries text, and none ever sends. New Chat with Voice starts dictation into the composer and waits for the user, as the intent does today.
- **Server:** both open on the active server, as the intents do.
- **Usage reports:** a control press isn't counted. Counting it would add a field to the report's documented contract (`docs/agents/usage-reports.md`), which is a separate decision.

## Acceptance and tests
- After adding the New Chat control to Control Center, one press opens Hermex on an empty New Chat composer on the active server, from a cold or warm launch.
- The voice control opens New Chat with the mic listening. When mic permission was denied, the composer shows its existing error.
- Both controls can be placed on the Lock Screen and on the Action Button, and the device asks for unlock before the app opens.
- The Branch build's controls open the Branch app.
- No new unit test: the controls only hold existing URLs, whose routing `AppIntentNewChatTests` covers (`HermesMobileTests/AppIntentNewChatTests.swift:23-62`). Run that class to confirm nothing moved.

## Mocks
Not required. The controls are system-drawn, from a title and an SF Symbol.

## Outside reach
None. No new target, so no new App ID registration (#659 doesn't apply).

## Surfaces
- **Targets:** the controls are in `HermesLiveActivityWidget` only. The main app gains no file in the `OpenURLIntent` path. In the fallback, the moved intent file gains widget membership and keeps app membership. `HermesShareExtension`, `HermesNotificationService` and `HermesMobileTests` don't change.
- **Entry points:** Control Center, the Lock Screen, the Action Button, and Shortcuts as today.
- **Strings:** "New Chat" and "New Chat with Voice" already exist in the catalog. Each control gets a short description in the control gallery.
- **iPad:** the controls appear in iPad Control Center too. Check them there once.
- Multi-server: no state is stored. The deep link opens on whatever server is active.

title: feat(workspace): edit and save a text file
body:
**What the user gets:** an Edit button on a text file in a Hermes chat's Files, for a quick fix (a config value, a typo) saved straight to the host, without spending a turn.
**Why it matters:** Files is read-only today, so a one-character fix means asking the agent. Hermes Desktop edits and saves text files in place.
**Cost:** Medium; simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes`. Static mocks first.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
A Hermes chat can read every text file in its folder but change none, though the host serves a guarded text write.

## Hermex today
- `WorkspaceFileClient` has reads only (`HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient+Workspace.swift:8-31`).
- `HermesWorkspaceFileClient.file(path:)` reads the first 512 KiB through `fsReadText` with the host path and no session id, and marks it `isPreviewOnly`, `isTruncated` or `isBinary` (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesWorkspaceFileClient.swift:66-83`; `HermesREST.swift:264-266,640-644`). Paths are workspace-relative until `hostPath` composes them (`:117`). A refusal whose `detail` names a path reads as the generic failure (`:139-145`).
- `FilePreviewView` and `FilePreviewViewModel` show the file, with a toolbar menu and Export (`HermesMobile/Features/Workspace/FilePreviewView.swift:94-120,181-215`; `FilePreviewViewModel.swift:72-140`). They open from Files (`FileBrowserView.swift:48-54`, reached from `ChatView.swift:2309-2321`) and from a transcript file link (`ChatView.swift:988-1005`).
- Precedent for a guarded write: Memory re-reads before saving, refuses a changed file with `MemoryConflict`, and treats a file over 512 KiB or not UTF-8 as read-only (`APIClient+Memory.swift:102-118`; `Models/Memory.swift:236`; `docs/agents/bots.md:1388-1396`).
- Git refreshes after a change made outside it with `GitWorkspaceViewModel.refreshAfterExternalMutation()` (`GitWorkspaceViewModel.swift:531-545`); Git writes are refused while the chat's turn runs (`HermesGitRefusal.turnRunning`, `HermesGitClient.swift:673,695`).

## Contract
Checked (2026-11-16): `POST /api/fs/write-text` is in the live host's `/openapi.json`, and a save on `scripts/local-hermes` answered `{ok, path, byteSize}`; a missing parent folder is a 400. Read from source at the pin `3b421578` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py:1082-1142`, body `hermes_cli/web_models.py:184-188`):
- `{path, content, session_id?}`. It resolves the path as `read-text` does, so send it the same way Hermex reads: host path, no `session_id`.
- It writes atomically (temp file, then replace), only over a regular file, caps content at 8 MiB (413), answers 403 when not writable, and **creates a file that doesn't exist**. Stale detection is the client's job.
- A 500 `detail` can carry an `OSError` with a host path; never show it.
- Step one: in one disposable session on `scripts/local-hermes`, save a file, then save again after changing it on disk, and confirm the stale check stops the second save.

## Proposal
- `HermesREST.fsWriteText(path:content:)` and `WorkspaceFileClient.writeText(path:content:expected:)`, with a webui default that throws unsupported and a `canWrite` that is false there.
- `HermesWorkspaceFileClient.writeText`: re-read with `fsReadText`; refuse with a `FileChangedOnHost` error when the file is gone, truncated, binary, or its text differs from `expected`; then write and check the reply's `byteSize` against the content's UTF-8 count. Errors map as reads do, so no host path is shown.
- `FilePreviewViewModel` gains an editing state: `isEditable` (Hermes, text, not truncated, no U+FFFD in the text), the draft, `isDirty`, `save()`.
- `FilePreviewView`: Edit in the toolbar when editable; an editor (plain monospaced text, no highlighting) with Cancel and Save; leaving with unsaved edits asks to discard.
- `ChatView` passes an `onSaved` that runs `gitAvailabilityViewModel.refreshAfterExternalMutation()`, through `FileBrowserView` and the file-link sheet.
- Docs: a short "Saving a file" paragraph in `docs/agents/bots.md` § Workspace on a Hermes host (`:1213`).

## Decisions
- **Edit and save an existing text file only** (owner, 2026-11-16). No create, rename or delete; a file that vanished is a stale file.
- **Re-read before saving and stop if it changed** (owner), so an agent's edit is never overwritten. Recommend the alert "This file changed on the host since you opened it." with Copy My Edits, Reload (drops the edits) and Keep Editing.
- **Refresh Git after a save** (owner).
- **The copy states that Save writes to the host** (owner). Recommend a line under the editor's title, "Save writes this file on the host.", and no extra dialog; mocks can show a confirm variant.
- **While this chat's turn runs:** recommend disabling Save with "Save after the reply finishes.", as Git writes already are; the agent is the likeliest other writer.
- **Not editable:** a truncated file (over 512 KiB), a binary file, or text the host decoded with replacement characters, since saving it would corrupt the file. The preview stays.
- **Unsaved edits** live only while the editor is open; nothing is drafted to disk.

## Acceptance and tests
- Editing `notes.txt` and tapping Save writes it; reopening shows the change; the Git badge counts it.
- If the agent or another device changed the file after it opened, Save writes nothing and the alert shows; the edits stay.
- A file over 512 KiB, a binary file and a webui chat show no Edit.
- Tests (extend `HermesWorkspaceFileClientTests`, and `FileBrowserViewModelTests` or a new `FilePreviewEditTests`):
  - Save sends `POST /api/fs/write-text` with the host path and `content`, and no `session_id`.
  - A re-read whose text differs sends no write and throws `FileChangedOnHost`; so does a 404 re-read.
  - A 500 whose `detail` names a host path surfaces the generic failure.
  - Text containing U+FFFD is not editable.
- Selection: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesWorkspaceFileClientTests --only HermesMobileTests/APIClientWorkspaceFileTests`.

## Mocks
Required. Step one: two or three static mocks with `html-communication` (Edit entry, the editor with its host note, the changed-on-host alert, unsaved-edits discard; light and dark, large text). Publish, report the URL, and wait for the owner's pick.

## Outside reach
None beyond `scripts/local-hermes`. Do not save files on the live host.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad, Hermes chats whose Files is available (a `local` backend), from Files and from a transcript file link. Hidden while viewing cached data. Hardware keyboard: Command-S saves, Escape cancels.
- No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep link or App Intent.
- Multi-server: the draft is held by the open preview, bound to its client's `scope` (server, Profile, session, folder); a workspace change closes it, as Files already does (`FileBrowserView.swift:58-61`).
- VoiceOver labels for Edit, Save and Cancel; Dynamic Type in the editor; new copy in the String Catalog; no animation.

title: feat(app): refresh Tasks, projects and skills when the host says they changed
body:
**What the user gets:** the Tasks list, the session list's project lanes and the Skills list update by themselves when the host changes them, such as a Task created from the terminal, a project made by the agent, or a skill installed from another window.
**Why it matters:** today these lists stay stale until a pull to refresh or a reopen, though the host already announces each change on the socket Hermex holds.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes`.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
Hermex reacts to only one of the host's change events. Tasks, projects and skills changed elsewhere look current on the phone when they aren't.

## Hermex today
- The session list's socket handler admits only `sessions.changed` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:1790-1794`), debounced (`:2325-2333`) into one read in flight plus at most one more (`:2336-2347`). A search finds no other `*.changed` handler in the app.
- Project lanes are read with the list (`reloadHermes`, `:1998-2000`; `readHermesProjects`, `:2851-2868`), or by hand from Move to Project's "Refresh Projects" (`SessionListComponents.swift:1557-1563`).
- Tasks (`TasksView.swift:123-125`) and Skills (`SkillsView.swift:43-45`, `:112-114`) read only on appear and on pull to refresh, over REST, and hold no socket (`HermesCronClient.swift:11-20`, `HermesSkillsClient.swift:10-25`).
- `TasksViewModel.load()` and `SkillsViewModel.load()` set `isLoading` and clear the error first (`TasksViewModel.swift:70-91`, `SkillsViewModel.swift:24-37`). Tasks drops a read older than the one shown (`TasksViewModel.swift:101-109`); Skills has no such guard.
- On iPhone, pushing Tasks or Skills closes the list's socket (`HermesSessionListView.swift:1396-1398`); on iPad the sidebar keeps it. Their entries carry only a client (`:1503-1521`).
- Every event reaches every screen attached to a connection's shared socket (`HermesGateway.swift:544-551`); a screen joins with `BotClient(http:)` (`BotClient.swift:52`) on the server's `HermesConnection` (`HermesConnection.swift:152`). Backgrounding closes them all (`HermesConnection.swift:780`, `ContentView.swift:73`).

## Contract
- **Read from source:** the gateway's change watcher broadcasts `cron.changed`, `projects.changed` and `skills.changed` with an empty payload (`tui_gateway/change_watcher.py:374-389`) to every connected client (`tui_gateway/server.py:632-648`). `cron.changed` follows `cron/jobs.json`, which moves on edits and on scheduler ticks (`change_watcher.py:376`). `projects.changed` follows each served Profile's `projects.db` (`:292-300`). `skills.changed` follows the skill folders (`:364-371`), so installing or removing a skill moves it. None of the three has a server-side floor; `:395` floors only `sessions.changed` and `platforms.changed`. `gateway.ready` says `change_events: true` (`tui_gateway/ws.py:653-659`). Desktop refreshes on these ticks (`apps/desktop/src/store/live-sync.ts:1-15`).
- **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes, with a socket open, confirm each event arrives: create and delete a Task, create and delete a project, and install and remove a skill, each disposable. Delete only what you made.

## Proposal
- **Projects:** in the list's `onEvent`, `projects.changed` starts its own debounced lane read: `readHermesProjects(wire, readSerial: hermesReadSerial)`, one in flight plus at most one more. Only while listening and while one Profile is shown, since a list of every Profile has no lanes (`:1998-2003`).
- **Tasks and Skills:** a small `@MainActor` `HermesChangeFeed` in `Networking/Hermes/`. It owns one `BotClient(http:)` on the screen's server connection, admits a set of event types, and calls `onChange` after the same one-second quiet time with the same one-plus-one coalescing. Its `makeWire` can be injected for tests, like `HermesSessionListSource` (`SessionListViewModel.swift:60-77`). `HermesTasksEntry` and `HermesSkillsEntry` gain the `HermesConnection` their client already uses. The view runs the feed in `.task(id:)` keyed on the scene being active: it starts on appear and on foreground, refreshes once on that foreground (events were missed while closed), and stops on disappear or background.
- **Quiet refresh:** `TasksViewModel.refresh()` and `SkillsViewModel.refresh()` re-read without `isLoading` or clearing rows. A failure keeps the rows and shows nothing. Skills gains the newest-read-wins guard Tasks has.
- Docs: a short "Change events" note in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` § The gateway socket naming the four events Hermex follows.

## Decisions
- **Coalesced:** one second of quiet, one refresh in flight and at most one more, like `sessions.changed`. `cron.changed` also fires on scheduler ticks, so this matters.
- **Only the server that sent it:** each feed and the list's handler act only on events from their own server's connection and current client (`self.wire === wire`). A retired connection's late event changes nothing.
- **Only while on screen:** no feed runs for a list that isn't showing.
- **No gate:** a host that never sends an event behaves as today. Hermex doesn't read `change_events`.
- **Scope:** the Tasks list, not a Task's detail screen. The Skills list, not a chat's `/` skill catalog. `pairing.changed` belongs to another child.
- **webui servers:** unchanged; they have no gateway socket.

## Acceptance and tests
- With Tasks open, a Task created on the host appears within a few seconds with no spinner. A burst of changes causes one or two reads.
- A project the agent creates shows as a lane without a pull to refresh.
- With Skills open, a skill installed on the host appears.
- After a server switch, an event on the old server's socket changes nothing on the new one.
- Tests:
  - `HermesSessionListTests`: a burst of `projects.changed` reads `projects.tree` once and shows the new lane; with All Profiles on, it reads nothing. Fails today.
  - `HermesChangeFeedTests` (new): a burst of admitted events calls `onChange` once, events during that call ask for one more, an event of another type calls nothing, and an event from a replaced client calls nothing.
  - `CronManagementTests`: `refresh()` keeps the rows and `isLoading` false while out, and a failed refresh leaves the rows and no error.
- Selection: `--only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChangeFeedTests --only HermesMobileTests/CronManagementTests --only HermesMobileTests/SkillsViewModelTests`.

## Mocks
Not required: nothing visible changes but the rows' contents.

## Outside reach
None. Step one runs on `scripts/local-hermes` with disposable Tasks, projects and skills.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad: Tasks and Skills reached from a Hermes server's home or sidebar, and the session list's lanes (Move to Project reads the same `projects`).
- No share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep link or App Intent change.
- Multi-server: feeds are built from the active server's connection and end with their screen; the list's view model is rebuilt per server.
- New files: `HermesChangeFeed.swift` and `HermesChangeFeedTests.swift`, added to `project.pbxproj`. No new strings.

title: feat(onboarding): tell a new host's user to add a model provider
body:
**What the user gets:** right after signing in to a host with no working model provider, the session list says so and offers Add API Key, instead of the first chat failing in the transcript.
**Why it matters:** a fresh host is a common first run. Today the user's first message fails with a provider error and nothing points to the fix.
**Cost:** Small; simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes` with an empty Profile.

Part of #1726.

## Problem
Nothing in Hermex asks whether the host can run a model. The first sign the user gets is a failed turn.

## Hermex today
- A search of `HermesMobile/` finds no `setup.status`. `HermesCall` has no case for it (`HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesCall.swift`, beside `sessionActiveList` at `:133`).
- After sign-in the user lands on the Hermes session list. Its top rows are the header, the card slot, the Move to Hermes banner and the offline banner (`HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/HermesSessionListView.swift:162-178`; `OfflineCacheBanner` at `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListComponents.swift:2251-2270`).
- The list holds a gateway socket for its Profile (`hermesProfile`, `HermesMobile/Features/SessionList/SessionListViewModel.swift:179`) and reads it when it opens, on pull-to-refresh and on foreground (`openHermes`, `:1766`). Its `session.active_list` read already hides itself on `-32601` (`:2401-2403`).
- API Keys lives at Settings › server › API Keys (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/SettingsServerPage.swift:202-206`) and takes the server's saved connection (`HermesMobile/Features/Settings/APIKeysView.swift:9-11`).

## Contract
- **Checked on 2026-11-16:** `setup.status` answers on both gateway types. A dashboard returns `{provider_configured, ready, inference_provider, other_providers, free_tier_account, free_tier_route}`. A Webapp returns only `{provider_configured}`. Use only `provider_configured`.
- Read from source: `provider_configured` counts any provider that can run inference, the free tier included (`hermes_cli/free_tier_bootstrap.py:34`). A provider added after boot flips it without a restart (`tui_gateway/methods_config.py:383-414`). The params are `{profile?}` (`tui_gateway/contracts/config_free_tier_control.py:108-128`).
- On a Webapp a `profile` other than the socket's own is refused with `profile_mismatch` (`gateway/session_readiness.py:11-26`).
- On a dashboard the call can block for up to 12 s on a host that has just started (`methods_config.py:60-62`, `hermes_cli/free_tier_bootstrap.py:25`).
- **Step one:** on `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes, call `setup.status {profile}` on a Profile with no keys and on one with a key, and record both replies.

## Proposal
- **Call:** add `HermesCall.setupStatus(profile:)`, which sends `{profile}`. Mark it cancellation-safe and give it a local timeout in `HermesGateway` (`isCancellationSafe`, `timesOutLocally`, `HermesMobile/Networking/Hermes/HermesGateway.swift:605-630`), so a slow host never holds the list.
- **Read:** in `SessionListViewModel`, read once per connect for `hermesProfile`, off the list's critical path, and again on pull-to-refresh and foreground. Keep `providerMissing: Bool`, true only when the reply says `provider_configured == false`. A missing field, an error or `-32601` means false, and `-32601` stops further reads for that socket.
- **Banner:** a `ProviderMissingBanner` row after `OfflineCacheBanner`, in the same style: "No model provider yet. Add an API key so Hermes can answer." Its Add API Key button opens `APIKeysView` for this server in a sheet. Closing the sheet reads `setup.status` again, and the banner leaves once the host says a provider works.

## Decisions
- **Where:** the session list, not onboarding. The list is where every sign-in lands, and it also catches a host whose last key was removed later.
- **Not dismissible:** the banner describes a real blocker and leaves by itself once it's fixed. A dismiss would hide it while every chat still fails.
- **Which Profile:** the list's own, since that's where new sessions start. Switching Profile reads it again.
- **API Keys, not Providers:** the owner's call. Connected subscription sign-in is a separate child of the epic.
- **No first-turn interception:** the chat's error line stays as it is.

## Acceptance and tests
- Signing in to a host whose Profile has no provider shows the banner. Add API Key opens API Keys, and after a key is saved and the sheet closes, the banner is gone.
- A host with a provider, a cached (offline) list, and a host without the method show no banner.
- Tests (all fail today): `HermesRequestTests` checks that `.setupStatus(profile:)` sends `profile`. `HermesSessionListTests`, with a fake wire, checks that `provider_configured: false` sets `providerMissing`, that `true`, a missing field and `-32601` leave it false, and that a reply arriving after a Profile switch is dropped.
- Run: `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesRequestTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesSessionListTests`.

## Mocks
Not required. One row in the existing banner style. Attach light and dark screenshots to the PR.

## Outside reach
None. Step one uses `scripts/local-hermes` with an empty Profile.

## Surfaces
- iPhone and iPad Hermes session list. webui servers: n/a.
- Multi-server: the flag lives on the list's view model, which is rebuilt per active server, and a reply from an old Profile or socket is dropped. Nothing is stored.
- Bots inbox, share extension, Live Activity, notification service, deep links and App Intents are not affected.
- Strings: the banner text and "Add API Key" go in the String Catalog, with a VoiceOver label that reads the whole banner.

title: docs(agents): correct the describe RPC and plugin RPC notes for a gateway's Webapp
body:
## Linked issue

No issue of its own: an approved doc correction, recorded under "Records corrected" in #1726.

## What changed

`docs/agents/hermes-server.md` said two things that are only true on a dashboard: that there is no describe RPC, and that a plugin can add no RPC method or `/api/ws` event. An agent reading it would rule out both on every host.

On a gateway's Webapp, `runtime.describe` returns a `capabilities` list, and a plugin can register `plugin.<plugin_id>.<name>` methods and session events, advertised there as `plugin-rpc-v1`. The doc now says which host type each statement applies to. The advice for hermex-push is unchanged: it registers no RPC method, so a gap it fills is still a REST route.

## How it was tested

Docs only, so no XCTest run. The facts were checked on 2026-11-16 at the pin (`3b421578`, 0.23.1) with `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes:

- Dashboard: `runtime.describe` answers -32601; `gateway.capabilities` returns `{per_session_exclusive_submit}`.
- Webapp (`--gateway`): `runtime.describe` returns `capabilities` including `plugin-rpc-v1`.
- Plugin registration is read from source (`hermes_cli/plugin_rpc.py`, `gateway/session_plugin_rpc.py`); no plugin RPC call was made, since no installed plugin registers one.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation: not applicable, docs only
- [x] No new or changed `Codable` models
- [x] No new third-party dependencies
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source and a running pinned host)

Created with Claude Fable 5.2 in Claude Code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified that dashboards do not provide a describe RPC or plugin RPC methods and WebSocket events, while gateway WebApps expose runtime capabilities and may register plugin RPC methods and session events.
  * Documented that WebApps advertise capabilities through `runtime.describe`, including `plugin-rpc-v1`, which the app does not currently read.
  * Clarified that companion-plugin gaps include REST routes, and that new hermex-push routes require a restart.

title: fix(chat): answer the host's theme requests instead of stalling the turn
body: ## Linked issue Fixes #1727 ## What changed On a gateway's Webapp, a Hermex chat gets the agent's `set_theme` tool, which sends the attached viewer a `theme.apply` or `theme.pick` request. Hermex never answered either, so "make it dark" stalled the turn for 15 s (a picker for up to 5 min) and the agent was told "No Hermes Desktop window answered the theme request." `HermesChatRequests` now answers both before they join `open`, so no card or waiting state appears. The pure `HermesThemeRequest` turns the request into the change and the answer: - `theme.apply` sets light, dark or system and the accent the way Settings > Appearance does (`appTheme`, `appearance.accentHex`, then `applyStoredToConnectedScenes()`), and answers `{success: true, applied}`. Desktop's swatch ids map onto Hermex's swatches; `nous` and `theme` clear the pick; a `#rrggbb` is stored as Settings stores it. Every value is checked first, so `mono`, an unknown value or any `layout` refuses the whole request and changes nothing. - `theme.pick` is answered at once with `{said}` (a new `RequestAnswer.said`), telling the agent to ask in the chat. Never `cancelled`, which reads as the user dismissing the card. - Each envelope id is answered once, including when a replay or a later attach still lists it. - The platform note adds one sentence: Hermex has no tours, tips, panes or layouts, and `set_theme` changes only light, dark and the accent. Where this differs from the issue: - **Only a gateway's Webapp sends these requests.** At the pin, `hermes serve` gives the `desktop_ui` toolset to platform `desktop` only (`tui_gateway/agent_factory.py` `_gui_surface_toolsets`), so a Hermex (`gui`) session on a dashboard can't call `set_theme` at all. The fix answers on both protocols; the docs say where it applies. - `applied.accent` is `null` for `nous`/`theme`, as Desktop reports it, and a hex is stored in uppercase like Settings. ## How it was tested Proved in the app: a signed Debug build on an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator (iOS 27.2) against a local `hermes gateway` at the pinned commit, with a stub model that calls `set_theme`. On `master`, "switch to dark mode" worked for 15 s, the app stayed light, and the tool row showed the "No Hermes Desktop window answered" error. On this branch the app turned dark within a 2 s turn, and "pick accent" and "use the focus layout" were answered in 0 s with the `said` text and the layout refusal. - New tests in `HermesChatRequestTests` and `HermesThemeRequestTests`, written first: on `master` 0 passed, 6 failed (requests sat in `open`, no answer was sent). They cover apply, layout refusal, pick, one answer per envelope, a request restored on reattach, and the accent table. A later accent test fails with `Change.store(in:)`'s accent branch broken. - `scripts/test-sim --only` `HermesChatRequestTests`, `HermesThemeRequestTests`, `BotPendingRequestParsingTests`, `ApprovalScopeTests`: 91 passed, 0 failed. `HermesConnectionTests` (reads the platform note): 37 passed. - Full suite (the project file gained two files): 4153 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `ServeEveryProfileTests.testADuplicateBotIsRemovedFromTheChosenProfileThenEveryProfileIsServed`, doesn't touch this change and passed 3 of 3 on a rerun. - Contract: request params and answers match `tui_gateway/theme_bridge.py` and `contracts/server_requests.py` at `3b421578`, and were captured from `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes. ## Checklist - [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim ` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above - [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename) - [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked) - [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Theme requests can update the app’s light or dark mode and supported accent colors automatically in an active chat. * Unsupported theme options, including layout changes, are reported without changing the current appearance. Accent-selection requests are answered with guidance to choose an accent in chat rather than displaying a picker. * Duplicate and restored theme requests are handled without answering the same request more than once. * **Documentation** * Updated bot guidance to clarify how theme requests and password-vault prompts are handled, and documented the available appearance controls.

title: fix(chat): route /rollback to the rollback calls so a Webapp host stops refusing it
body: ## Linked issue Fixes #1728 ## What changed `/rollback` went through `slash.exec`, which a gateway's Webapp refuses with `unsupported_command` (`rollback` is in none of `command_verdict`'s allowed sets). So on those hosts there was no way to undo the agent's file changes from the phone. `/rollback` is now one of Hermex's own commands and calls `rollback.list`, `rollback.diff` and `rollback.restore` on the chat's runtime, as Hermes Desktop does, on both gateway types. - `/rollback` lists the checkpoints: number, short hash, local time and the host's message. - `/rollback diff N` shows the stat and a `diff` fence. - `/rollback N [file]` asks first, naming the checkpoint's time and message, then restores the whole tree or one file. It uses the owner's copy for the question. - Diff and restore read the list first and send the checkpoint's hash, never the number: every restore adds a "pre-rollback" checkpoint, which shifts the numbers. An unknown number or hash is refused on the phone ("There's no checkpoint N."), because a host answers an unknown hash with an empty diff rather than an error. - A whole-tree restore that rewound the newest turn (`history_removed > 0`) re-reads the newest rows and replaces the transcript, as `/undo` does. Send is held while it's out, with `/undo`'s `isUndoingExchange`. - Refusals: a whole-tree restore while a reply runs, or the host's 4009 / Webapp 4001 `session_busy`, says "Wait for the current reply to finish." Only a gone runtime (4001 `session not found`, `not_found`, `runtime_retired`) reattaches; any other refusal shows the host's reason. `enabled: false` says "Checkpoints are off on this Hermes host." - Restore is sent once and never retried; list and diff are cancellation-safe. The issue's "Recommend" items, implemented as recommended (say if you want them otherwise): - The number is resolved on the phone before asking, so an out-of-range restore number gets the local notice instead of the host's `error` sentence. The host's sentence still shows when a restore it receives comes back `success: false`. - `--all` is left out and gets the usage notice. - In a Bot Chat, list, diff and a one-file restore run; a whole-tree restore is refused with "A bot's chat can't be rewound." Remaining risk: on a Webapp, `rollback.restore` restores the files before it rewinds the turn (`gateway/session_tui_ops.py`). If a turn starts in that gap, the rewind is refused with `session_busy` and the app says to wait although the files were restored. Send is held and a running turn is refused before asking, so the window is narrow; it isn't handled. ## How it was tested Proved in the app: a signed Debug build on an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator (iOS 27.2) against a local `hermes gateway` (Webapp) at the pinned commit with checkpoints on, with a stub model that writes `notes.txt`. On `master`, `/rollback` showed `unsupported_command`. On this branch it listed the checkpoint, `/rollback diff 1` showed `-notes v2` / `+notes v3`, and `/rollback 1` asked, restored `notes.txt` to v2 on disk and removed the rewinding turn from the transcript. `/rollback diff deadbeef` was refused on the phone. - New tests, written first and failing on the code before them (the host-error test was added after the first red run): - `HermesSlashCommandTests`: `/rollback` sends `rollback.list` and never `slash.exec`; a confirmed restore sends the listed hash and `file_path` only for a file; a `success: false` restore shows the host's error; Cancel sends nothing; a diff sends the listed hash and nothing for an unknown checkpoint; only a gone runtime reattaches. - `HermesHistoryRewindTests`: a rewinding restore replaces the transcript on a dashboard and a Webapp chat (`history_removed: 0` leaves it); Send waits while a whole-tree restore is out. - `scripts/test-sim --only` `HermesSlashCommandTests`, `HermesHistoryRewindTests`, `LocalizationCatalogTests`, `SlashCommandTests`, `SlashCommandExecutorTests`, `ComposerSlashTriggerTests`, `HermesAgentFixtureTests`: 132 passed, 0 failed. `ci/check_string_catalog.py` passes. - Contract: the replies were captured from `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes (list, diff, file and whole-tree restore, unknown hash, out-of-range number, busy, checkpoints off) and match `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` and `gateway/session_tui_ops.py` at `3b421578`. Sanitized replies are in `slash-commands.json`. `history_removed` counts rows, not turns (one rewound turn gave 4), so the app only checks `> 0`. - Not exercised: the busy refusal and `enabled: false` have no unit test or app run (their wire replies were captured), and a Bot Chat's one-file restore has no test. ## Checklist - [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim ` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above - [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename) - [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked) - [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added `/rollback` for browsing available checkpoints, viewing their changes, and restoring a checkpoint or selected files. * Restores require confirmation and show which files were restored or skipped, along with whether the newest chat turn was removed. * **Bug Fixes** * Chat history now refreshes after a restore removes the newest turn. * Restore requests are blocked while a reply or another submission is in progress, and whole-chat restores are unavailable in Bot Chats. * **Documentation** * Added guidance on using `/rollback` and its restrictions.

title: feat(chat): show "Compacting context" while the host compacts
body: ## Linked issue Fixes #1734 ## What changed When the host auto-compacts a long chat mid-turn, the run can go quiet for a minute or more. Hermex ignored the host's `status.update {kind: "compacting"}`, so the tail row just kept counting "Working for 1m 3s" and the run looked stalled. `HermesChatTurnCoordinator` now keeps an observable `isCompacting`. While it's set, the tail row reads "Compacting context · 1m 3s" (VoiceOver: "Hermes is compacting context, working for …"), and the scrolled-away pill reads the same. Same row, new words: no second row, no new animation, and the input reaches only the tail row and the pill, never settled rows. - Starts on `compacting` (auto-compaction, re-sent as a heartbeat) and `compressing` (`/compress`). - Ends on `compacted`; on `/compress`'s end, which the host sends as `{kind: "status", text: "ready"}` rather than a `ready` kind; on `message.complete`, `error` and `session.info {running: false}`; when the turn finishes; on every reattach and disconnect; and on the turn's next output (the same 12 event types as Desktop's `COMPACTION_RESUME_EVENT_TYPES`, `moa.*` included). The last one matters: a compaction that makes no progress, or whose summary is refused, sends `compacting` and never `compacted`. - The pending `/compress` handling from #1050 is unchanged. Webui sessions aren't affected. - Two strings in the String Catalog, all shipped languages marked `needs_review`. ## How it was tested Proved in the app: a signed Debug build on an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator (iOS 27.2) against a local `hermes gateway` at the pinned commit, with a low compression threshold and the summary call delayed 45 s. On `master` a compacting turn read "Working for 15s". On this branch it read "Compacting context · 14s", and the line was gone once the turn ended. - New tests, written first: on `master` 0 passed, 6 failed; after the change 6 passed. - `HermesChatTurnTests`: `compacting` mid-turn shows until `compacted`; the turn's end clears a compaction whose end never came; the next output clears one that sent no end; a reattach drops it; `/compress`'s `ready` ends it. - `ChatActiveRunStatusPolicyTests`: the pill carries the compacting line while compacting. - The frames come from a new fixture recorded from `scripts/local-hermes` (`turn-compaction-frames.json`). - `scripts/test-sim --only` `HermesChatTurnTests`, `HermesCompressClearTests`, `ChatActiveRunStatusPolicyTests`: 112 passed, 0 failed (final head). The wider first selection, with every class in `TranscriptDisplayModelTests.swift`, `HermesChatRequestTests` and `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 202 passed. - `ChatTranscriptRenderBudgetTests.testTextOnlyTicksReRenderOnlyTheStreamingRow` fails on this branch and is unstable on `master` here too (passed once on one simulator, failed twice on another, once with the same message). `docs/agents/performance.md` keeps it local-only until #1516, so it gives no clean signal either way. Its host passes `isCompacting: false` as a constant, so nothing this change adds is read per tick. - Contract: the `status.update` kinds match `tui_gateway/server.py` `_status_update`, `agent/conversation_compression.py` and `gateway/run_turn_progress.py` at `3b421578`, and were captured from `scripts/local-hermes` in both modes, including a no-progress and a refused compaction. ## Checklist - [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim ` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above - [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename) - [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked) - [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Chat status now indicates when context is being compacted, with matching text and accessibility labels in the active status and working row. * Added localized compacting-status messages.

title: chore(scripts): make test-sim fail when an --only selection ran no tests
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing directly; a focused local run can no longer report PASS for tests that never ran.
**Why it matters:** `--only` takes a class (or class/method) identifier, but a test file doesn't always share its class's name. `BotPendingRequestTests.swift` holds `BotPendingRequestParsingTests` and `ApprovalScopeTests`. A selection written as the file name runs nothing, the other selections still pass, and the run prints PASS, so the selection recorded in a PR claims coverage it didn't get.
**Cost:** Small. `scripts/` only, no phone needed.

## Steps to reproduce

On `master` (`b1da6b40`), on an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator (iOS 27.2):

```
scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/ApprovalScopeTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests
```

## Expected behavior

The run fails and names `HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests`, which matched no test.

## Actual behavior

```
Tests: 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
PASS
```

The 5 are `ApprovalScopeTests`. xcodebuild skips an `-only-testing` identifier that names nothing, so the 24 tests in `BotPendingRequestParsingTests` never ran. `test-sim` already stops when nothing passed at all ("Cannot confirm a passing test run"), but not when one selection out of several ran nothing.

## Fix

After a passing run, check each `--only` identifier against the tests in the result bundle, and stop with the ones that ran nothing, e.g. `STOP: --only matched no tests: HermesMobileTests/BotPendingRequestTests. Check the spelling, and use the class name, which can differ from its file's.` Cover it in `scripts/tests`.

title: chore(scripts): stop test-sim passing when an --only selection ran no tests
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1762

## What changed

`--only` takes a class or method identifier, but a test file doesn't always share its class's name: `BotPendingRequestTests.swift` holds `BotPendingRequestParsingTests` and `ApprovalScopeTests`. xcodebuild skips an identifier that names nothing, so a selection written as the file name ran none of its tests, the other selections passed, and `test-sim` printed PASS. A PR could then report a selection that never ran.

After a passing run, `test-sim` now reads the tests that ran from the result bundle (`xcresulttool get test-results tests`) and stops with exit 2 when an `--only` identifier ran none:

```

title: fix(tests): stop the HermesConnectionTests and HermesInsightsClientTests request counts flaking on CI
body:
**What the user gets:** nothing visible; `master` and unrelated PRs stop going red on these two tests.
**Why it matters:** between them they failed ten CI runs from 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-17, eight on `master`, and each one costs a manual re-run before a merge or a release candidate.
**Cost:** Small. No phone needed.

## 1. HermesConnectionTests

`HermesConnectionTests.testABrowserSignInRefreshesFromTheKeychainAndSavesTheRotatedTokenBeforeItsBearer` (`HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests.swift:469`) failed in 5 of the last 60 failed PR CI runs (2026-11-03 to 2026-11-17). First seen 2026-11-12.

| Run | Branch | Head | Test time | Message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [43279812569](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/43279812569) | `master` | `6267de24d` | 0.055 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("62") is not equal to ("0")` |
| [43756788966](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/43756788966) | `master` | `7e5757111` | 3.317 s | not captured |
| [43799434336](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/43799434336) | `master` | `255a3c06a` | 3.242 s | not captured |
| [43849290444](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/43849290444) | PR branch `issue-1152-external-profile-deletion` | `7da49ef52` | 0.034 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("8") is not equal to ("0")` |
| [43916448865](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/43916448865) | `master` | `62aee3550` | 0.072 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("62") is not equal to ("0")` |

None of the four `master` commits touched `HermesConnectionTests.swift`. These runs were not re-run; the test passed on later `master` heads, for example run [44104328392](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/44104328392) on `b55d8a223`.

### What fails

The only assertion in the test that compares against `0` is line 508:

```swift
XCTAssertEqual(HermesHostFixture.count("/auth/password-login"), 0)
```

So in the fast failures the fixture's request log held 8 or 62 `/auth/password-login` requests this test never made.

## 2. HermesInsightsClientTests

`HermesInsightsClientTests.testAClosedGateOffersNoProvidersAndAsksForNoLimits` (`HermesMobileTests/HermesInsightsClientTests.swift:215`) failed in 5 of the same 60 runs. First seen 2026-11-06. No other issue tracks it.

| Run | Branch | Head | Test time | Message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [42155153311](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/42155153311) | `master` | `fdae3bdc6` | 0.010 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("3") is not equal to ("1")` |
| [42390313128](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/42390313128) | `master` | `72395bf6f` | 0.015 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("4") is not equal to ("1")` |
| [42756389641](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/42756389641) | `master` | `a1d4e5c94` | 0.016 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("4") is not equal to ("1")` |
| [43268629794](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/43268629794) | PR branch `issue/1649-mermaid` | `257be2887` | 0.015 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("4") is not equal to ("1")` |
| [44104328392](https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/hermex/actions/runs/44104328392) | `master` | `b55d8a223` | 4.641 s | `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("4") is not equal to ("1")` |

### What fails

The only assertion in the test that compares against `1` is line 229:

```swift
XCTAssertEqual(HermesHostFixture.count("/api/plugins/hermex-push/capabilities"), 1)
```

So the fixture's request log held 3 or 4 capabilities requests where the test expects its own one. This is the same shape as the first test: a request count read from the shared log comes back too high. I did not rule out the test's own client asking for capabilities more than once.

## Likely cause for both (not confirmed)

`HermesHostFixture.log` is one process-wide static, cleared only by `reset()` in `tearDown`. Work an earlier test left running (a connection still retrying its password sign-in) keeps writing to that log after the reset, and the next test counts those requests as its own. For the Insights test the stray work would be another connection reading the plugin's capabilities.

The two 3.2 s failures may be a second shape of the same leak or something else; their assertion message is not in the failed-step log, so read the full log of one before assuming.

## Fix

- Find which earlier tests leave requests running past their own end, and make them finish or cancel that work before they return.
- Or scope each count to requests the test's own connection made, so a stray request from another test cannot fail it. One change to how `HermesHostFixture` counts would cover both tests.
- Do not add a sleep or a retry.

Check with `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesConnectionTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesInsightsClientTests --repeat 20`. A class-only run may not reproduce it, since the stray requests would come from another class; if it passes, run the classes that execute just before each test in a failing CI log.

title: feat(sessions): show a chat as working while its subagents or processes still run
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1730

## What changed

A turn can end while work it started keeps going: a background delegation returns as soon as it spawns its children, and a background command outlives its turn. The session list only asked the host which runtimes were mid-turn, so these chats read as idle.

The list now also reads `subagent.roster` and shows such a chat with its existing Working label.

```diff
 reloadHermes
   startHermesStatusRead      session.active_list + approval.pending (unchanged)
+  startHermesRosterRead      subagent.roster, one read per listed Profile
 attentionState(for: row)
   active-list state, if any  (Approval and Input still win)
+  else .working when row.sessionId or row.lineageRoot is in hermesBackgroundWork
```

- `HermesCall.subagentRoster(profile:)`, params `{profile}`, added to `isCancellationSafe` and `timesOutLocally`.
- `SessionListViewModel.hermesBackgroundWork` holds the ids of roster entries with any `subagents` or `background` above zero. It is kept apart from `attentionStatesBySessionID`, so it never keeps the 5 s busy re-read alive. The roster is read beside the existing live-state read (open, foreground, pull to refresh, a chat closing, `sessions.changed`), never on a timer. Only the newest read applies, and only while the same wire is live.
- The set is cleared on teardown, on a Profile switch and while cached rows show. Any failed Profile read clears the whole set, so the rows behave as today. A host answering -32601 sets `hermesReadsRoster = false` for that socket, and the rows show exactly today's states.
- The roster's ids are kept whole rather than cut down to the rows loaded at that moment, so a row that arrives later through Load more, scheduled paging or a host search shows Working without waiting for another list read. Nothing else reads the set, and it never drives the 5 s re-read. (`attentionState(for:)` looks rows up by their own id, so an id no row holds marks nothing.)
- One sentence in `docs/agents/hermes-server.md` § Reconnect contract.

### Tradeoffs for a maintainer call

Two behaviors this PR leaves as they are, both read from the pinned source (`3b421578`), not reproduced on a live host:

1. **A middle segment of a compression chain stays unmarked.** A row is matched on its tip id and its lineage root, as the issue decided. With `compression.in_place` turned off (it is on by default), work started in a middle segment of a chain that has since rotated again is reported under that middle id: a background process takes `HERMES_SESSION_ID` and a subagent its parent's id at start (`tools/process_registry.py:1095`, `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py:438-440`), and `_stored_owner` keeps it (`tui_gateway/methods_subagents.py:113-115`). The host's `GET /api/sessions` rows carry `_lineage_ids` for exactly this (Desktop matches on them, `apps/desktop/src/store/live-work-roster.ts:92`), but `/api/sessions/search` does not, and decoding it means a new wire field through the row model and the offline cache, so it is left for a follow-up.
2. **Working hides the unread dot for longer.** The row shows its unread dot only when it has no attention state, a rule this PR does not touch (`SessionRowView.swift:32`): a row already hid the dot while its turn ran. Because roster work reuses the Working state, a chat with a long-lived background process (a dev server, say) now keeps the dot and VoiceOver's "Unread" hidden after its reply lands, until the process ends and the list is read again. The host's read mark is unchanged, and the row menu's Mark as Read/Unread still works. Showing both would change every Working row or need a second state, which the issue ruled out.

Related, also left alone: Move to Project's confirmation reads "including the reply that's running now" for any row whose attention state is set (`HermesSessionListView.swift`), so a roster-only Working row gets that wording although no reply is running.

## How it was tested

- Contract: on `scripts/local-hermes` at the pinned commit, in both modes (`hermes serve` and `hermes gateway run`), `subagent.roster` with and without `{profile}` answered `{"sessions": []}`, and an unknown method answered -32601. The stub model can't start a background delegation or process, so a non-empty roster was not captured live; the entry shape `{session_id, subagents, background}` is read from `tui_gateway/methods_subagents.py:121-145`.
- New tests in `HermesSessionListTests`, with a scripted roster reply on `HermesSessionListWire`, written first and run against stub implementations: 3 failed (`testBackgroundWorkKeepsAnEndedTurnWorking`, `testTheRosterIsReadOncePerListRead`, `testAHostWithoutTheRosterShowsOnlyTheActiveListStates`). Keeping the roster whole added `testBackgroundWorkMarksARowLoadMoreBringsIn`, which failed before that change (the row read `nil`, expected `.working`). All pass on the final head.
  - An idle row in the roster reads Working and Approval beats it; the roster is read once per list read, never on the 5 s ticks, and once more on `sessions.changed`; -32601 leaves the active-list states and sends no further roster call.
  - `HermesRequestTests` and `BotClientTests` cover the request's params, cancellation safety and local timeout.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro Max> --only` `HermesSessionListTests`, `BotClientTests`, `HermesRequestTests`: 95 passed, 0 failed (final head).
- In the app: a signed Debug build against `scripts/local-hermes` lists sessions with today's states and no error. A Working row from the roster was not seen in the app, for the reason above. No before/after image: the row reuses the existing Working label.

**Merge order:** #1767 (#1733) touches the same files. The two merge cleanly in either order here; if the other lands first I'll rebase this one.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

Implemented with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, reviewed by Claude Opus 5.5 and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol); the tradeoffs above were checked against the pinned source by Claude Fable 5.2.

* **New Features**
  * The session list now marks idle sessions as **Working** when they have active delegated tasks or background processes, including activity associated with a session’s lineage.
  * Approval status continues to take priority over Working status.
  * Activity is refreshed when the session list is read; unsupported or failed status checks do not interrupt the connection.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated reconnect guidance to describe when activity indicators are refreshed and cleared.

title: feat(sessions): filter the list by Working, Unread and Draft, and Mark All as Read
body: ## Linked issue Fixes #1733 ## What changed The session list could be narrowed by Profile, project lane and search, but not by what a chat needs from the user, and marking read was one row at a time. The Filter menu (on the home and on the pushed list) gains a section with Working, Unread and Draft and "Mark N Chats as Read". The menu opens upward, so it reads bottom-up: ```diff Filter menu + Mark 3 Chats as Read + Draft + Unread + Working + ───────── default (Profile picker, unchanged) All Profiles ``` - **Status filter** (`HermesSessionStatusFilter`), held in `HermesSessionListNavigation` beside the lane and applied in `visibleSessions` after it. One status at a time; picking it again goes back to All. Not saved: it resets on any Profile change, whichever way it comes (the menu, a chat's Profile chip, `/sessions` or `/resume`, or the host dropping the Profile). - Working: any live state, Approval and Input included (`attentionState(for:) != nil`). With #1730 it also picks up chats whose subagents or processes still run. - Unread: `isUnread`. - Draft: a non-empty draft is stored under the row's lineage root, in the row's Profile. `ChatDraftStore.hermesSessionDraftKeys(server:connectionID:)` lists them; the list reads it while Draft is picked and again each time a chat closes. - **Only loaded rows are filtered.** A filter never fetches more pages on its own: under a filter, Load more stays a manual tap, and a refresh that changes the row count doesn't fill a project lane either. Going back to All with the Load more row in view loads as its appearing would have. The empty states ("No working chats", "No unread chats", "No drafts") add "Only chats already loaded are filtered." - **Mark All as Read** (`markAllHermesRead`) covers the unread rows of the shown Profile (every listed one under All Profiles) in the selected lane. Search and the status filter don't change it. It goes through the same `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` `unread` write as a row's Mark as Read, at most four at a time, awaits them, and says how many the host took in the existing toast and to VoiceOver. A refused write shows that row unread again, as today. A second tap while writes are out does nothing. The host has no bulk route (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py` at `3b421578`); Desktop's Mark all as read only clears local state, so the web dashboard and other devices wouldn't agree. - The status section is its own view, so reading the unread marks to count the chats in scope invalidates only that section, not the list's body. - Hermes servers only; webui lists don't change. Strings: "Draft", the empty states and their loaded-rows note, and "Mark %lld Chats as Read" / "Marked %lld chats as read" as plurals, all shipped languages marked `needs_review`. ## How it was tested A signed Debug build on an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator (iOS 27.2), English UI, against `scripts/local-hermes` at the pinned commit. | Before (`master`) | After | |---|---| | | | | Working filter, nothing working | Unread filter, nothing unread | After Mark All as Read | |---|---|---| | | | | - In the app: each filter narrows the rows and picking it again goes back to All; a chat with typed text and no send shows under Draft; Mark All marked the unread chat on the host and the toast said so; switching to All Profiles reset the filter. - New tests, written first and run against stub implementations: 4 failed (`testHermesSessionDraftKeysListOnlyThisConnectionsNonEmptyStoredSessionDrafts`, `testTheStatusFiltersKeepOnlyMatchingRowsInTheLane`, `testMarkAllAsReadWritesOnlyTheScopesUnreadRowsAndCountsWhatTheHostTook`, `testMarkAllAsReadSendsAtMostFourWritesAtOnce`). The review fix for repeated taps added `testMarkAllAsReadIgnoresARepeatWhileItsWritesAreOut`, which failed before the fix (5 writes, expected 4). All pass on the final head. - Mark All asserts the ids written and the `unread` field, that rows of another Profile or lane stay untouched, the count the host took, and that a refused write leaves its row unread. - `scripts/test-sim --only` `HermesSessionListTests`, `ChatDraftStoreTests`, `LocalizationCatalogTests`: 104 passed, 0 failed (final head). - The bot-review follow-ups (80fd80e7, 93ba5e17) are view observers on the Load more row, so they have no unit test; the same selection passed after each (104 passed). Not driven in the app: it needs a project lane with more than one page of chats on the stub. - `ci/check_string_catalog.py` on a Debug build: the catalog covers all 3076 extracted keys. - Not measured: list scrolling performance with the new section in the menu; the split into its own view is the only change aimed at it. **Merge order:** this touches the same files as #1766 (#1730) (`SessionListViewModel.swift`, `HermesSessionListTests.swift`). The two merge cleanly in either order here; if the other lands first I'll rebase this one. ## Checklist - [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim ` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above - [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename) - [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked) - [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server) Implemented with Claude Sonnet 5.5 in Claude Code, reviewed by Claude Opus 5.5 and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol), coordinated by Claude Opus 5.5. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Filter sessions by Working, Unread, or Draft status, alongside All. Filters apply to loaded sessions and reset when the selected profile scope changes. * Mark unread sessions as read within the selected profile and visibility scope. A confirmation reports the number successfully marked. * Empty-state messages reflect the selected status, and the filter menu announces the selected profile and status for accessibility. * Draft sessions refresh after a chat closes. Automatic pagination runs only when All is selected; manual loading remains available for other filters.

title: feat(chat): show the host's notices
body: ## Linked issue Fixes #1746 ## What changed The host sends `notification.show` and `notification.clear` on a session's stream for credits, a slow agent start, a dropped model switch, the low-disk question, a plugin's `post_message` and `/login`'s sign-in link. Hermex dropped both, so none of it reached the user. A Hermes chat (and a Bot Chat, which uses the same coordinator) now keeps the host's notices in `HermesHostNotices` and shows the newest one above the composer in `HostNoticeRow`. ```diff HermesChatTurnCoordinator.apply(frame, live:) case "btw.complete", "background.complete", "session.control.update": sideTasks + case "notification.show": hostNotices.show(payload, live:) + case "notification.clear": hostNotices.clear(payload) default: dropped ``` - **Kept by `key`, else `id`, newest last.** A show with a known key replaces that notice in place; `notification.clear` withdraws it. A notice without `text` is ignored. Every field decodes tolerantly. - **`ttl` notices** show only from a live frame, so a replay never brings back an expired one, and hide after `ttl_ms` on one scheduled task. Every other kind stays until cleared or dismissed, and comes back from every replay in order, a rebuilding one's too, so a later `clear` still wins and a first open shows a standing notice. The live frame that reveals a replay gap is still applied, since the rebuild replays only what follows it. - **Lifetime.** A new runtime or a new replay epoch drops the old lifetime's notices and timers, since nothing will clear them. A gap or a cut-short replay within one epoch keeps them. Nothing is cached: leaving the chat drops them. - **One row, not a stack**, as the issue decided: the newest shows, VoiceOver's value says how many wait behind it, and dismissing it reveals the next. A dismissed key stays hidden until the host shows it again with new text. Host text is shown as sent and web links in it are tappable. A notice with `detail` shows two lines and opens `detail` on a tap; one without shows up to six lines, so a warning's hint isn't cut (the issue said two lines; with no `detail` nothing else would reveal the rest). Never a transcript row, the error line or a haptic. The row's insert follows Reduce Motion. - VoiceOver reads the level ("Warning: …", "Notice: …", "Success: …", and the existing "Error: …"). Three new strings, all shipped languages marked `needs_review`. - `docs/agents/bots.md` describes the notices beside the chat's other side state. ### Known limitations - **A new epoch drops notices the host won't resend.** On a canonical host, notices are dropped whenever the session's replay epoch changes. That happens on a host restart, and also when the host ends a session nobody has watched for five minutes (`sessions.orphan_end_grace_s`, default 300 s), which a locked phone triggers. The host does not resend a `/login` link, a plugin message, the low-disk question or an unchanged credits band under the new epoch, so those are gone when the user comes back. Running out of replay buffer does not change the epoch and keeps the notices. The app cannot tell a restart from this cleanup, and keeping notices across a restart would leave ones the host can never clear, so they are dropped in both cases. (Pinned source: `gateway/session_events.py:68-72`, `gateway/session_viewer_close.py:320-321`, `gateway/session_authority.py:438-440`, `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:2299`.) - **`/login`'s link sits behind two dismisses.** `/login` on a local session publishes three sticky notices in a row, each with its own random key: the sign-in link, the code, then "Do not share this code. Waiting for sign-in, up to N minutes." (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py:52-54`, `:188-192`). Hermex shows only the newest notice, so the user sees the waiting line and has to dismiss twice to reach the link, three times once the sign-in result arrives. The count of waiting notices is only exposed to VoiceOver, so nothing on screen says more are behind it. The host never clears these keys. title: feat(chat): remember Thinking and Fast for each model
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1750

## What changed

Thinking and Fast are session-scoped writes that the next model pick doesn't carry, so switching between a fast model and a strong one meant resetting both by hand each time.

Hermex now remembers, per server and per model, the Thinking level and Fast setting last chosen in a Hermes chat or Bot Chat, and sets them again when that model is picked and the host runs the pick at once.

```text
select(effort:) / select(fast:) succeeds
  → record it for the live model           ModelPresetStore, per server

pick model M, host runs it now
  (dashboard: confirm_required false and not deferred;
   canonical: receipt without a status; or once confirmed)
  and the catalog read after it shows M live
  → send M's remembered effort, then Fast, through the same select(…)
    skipping a value equal to the current one, an effort M's ladder lacks,
    Fast on a model that hides it, and Fast once the chat reattached or
    another model took over
```

- `ModelPresetStore` beside `ModelFavoritesStore`: `{effort?, fast?}` per `ModelFavoriteKey` in `UserDefaults` under `hermes.mobile.modelPresets|<server>`, built with the same scoped-key helper. An unreadable blob is empty. Local only: nothing is written to the host's config.
- Removed on sign-out and server removal: `AuthManager.removeBotConnection(for:)` deletes it beside the model lists. A row in `docs/agents/multi-server-state-isolation.md` § Per-server state.
- Recording goes to the model the host last reported (`session.info`), not just the catalog's: if another client switched the session and the catalog hasn't been read since, nothing is recorded for the old model.
- No new UI and no strings: the existing chips take the remembered values.

### A deferred pick applies no preset

The issue expected a pick made while a response runs to take effect "at the end of the response", and the preset to follow it. On the pinned host it doesn't, on either gateway, so this PR applies presets only to picks the host runs at once (or after its confirmation) and leaves deferred picks alone. I recorded the frame order on `scripts/local-hermes` at `3b421578` (0.23.1), one disposable session per run: submit a turn, send the pick while it waits on its approval, approve, wait for `message.complete`, then submit a second turn. `model.options` was read at every step.

**`hermes serve` (dashboard)**, accepted pick:

| t (s) | Frame | Live model (`model.options`) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.79 | `config.set model` reply: `deferred: true` | old |
| 0.92 | `message.complete` (turn 1 ends) | |
| 0.94 | `session.info {model: new, running: false}` | still old, and 2 s later |
| 3.16 | turn 2 submitted, `message.start` | |
| 3.28 | `session.info {model: new, running: true}` | new |

The pick applies when the next turn starts (`tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py:701` → `_apply_pending_model_switch`). At turn 1's end `session.info` already names the pending pick. A pick the host will reject looks the same then (`session.info` names the nonexistent model with `running: false`); the rejection arrives only once turn 2 starts, as `notification.show` (key `model_switch.dropped`) and `session.info` back on the old model.

**`hermes gateway run` (Webapp, canonical)**, accepted pick:

| t (s) | Frame | Live model (`model.options`) |
|---|---|---|
| 3.24 | `session.mutate` reply: `status: deferred` | old |
| 3.41 | `session.info` naming the old model | |
| 3.43 | `message.complete`, then `session.info {running: false}` | |
| 3.45 | `session.info {model: new}`, then `session.updated {operation: model, …}` | new |

The pick commits at the claim boundary about 20 ms after `message.complete`, with no next turn queued (`gateway/session_authority.py` `_claim_next` → `apply_deferred_pick`). A rejected pick arrives at the same point as `session.updated {status: refused, reason: model_resolution_failed}`; no `session.info` names it.

So a client keying on the response's end would see the old model (canonical) or a pending pick that may still be refused (dashboard). Following a deferred pick needs per-gateway tracking up to the next turn's start, and an earlier attempt at it in this branch (reverted in `28540277` and `c09b3878`) grew three new bugs in review, so I left it out. The timings are from the stub model on loopback; the order was the same in both accepted and both rejected runs. Function references are read from source; every row above was measured.

### Known limitation: a model change during a write in flight

Presets and recordings are keyed by the model the chat believes is live when the write lands, and a model change that arrives while a write is in flight can make that belief stale. The cases review found, all in this class (the write case is now closed):

- **The pick's catalog read.** If another client switches the session while this chat's pick reads the catalog, and that client's `session.info` lands first, the pick's success overwrites the reported model (`pickRan`) and the preset can go to the other client's model.
- **A Thinking or Fast write.** Fixed in 65c4001: `select(effort:)` and `select(fast:)` capture the live model before the write and record only if it is still live afterwards.
- **Provider.** The reported-model check compares the model id only, so another client moving the same model id to another provider isn't caught.

Each needs the same model to change within one round trip of a write. The cost is one Thinking or Fast value written to, or remembered for, the wrong model; the chip shows what the host runs, and the user can change it. The catalog-read race needs a report generation, new state I didn't add without a maintainer call; the provider check can't be one comparison, since the canonical gateway's `session.info` carries no `provider` (`gateway/session_local.py:464-473`, while the dashboard's does).

## How it was tested

- `HermesChatSettingsTests` (fake wire) and `ModelFavoritesStoreTests`, written before the code; each review fix started from a test that failed before it. Covered: an effort and Fast pick are remembered; picking a model with a preset sends its effort, then Fast; a canonical pick run at once and a confirmed pick apply the preset; a deferred dashboard pick and a deferred canonical pick apply none; an effort the model doesn't offer isn't sent; no preset without a pick here; a model changed while the preset's effort is sent gets no Fast; a level picked after another client switched isn't remembered for the old model, also when a later `session.info` carries no model; a pick the host ran without reporting a model still applies and remembers; presets stay with their server and an unreadable blob is empty. `AuthManagerStateTests` checks server removal deletes them.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro Max> --only` `HermesChatSettingsTests`, `AuthManagerStateTests`, `ModelFavoritesStoreTests`, `BotChatControlsTests`: 119 passed, 0 failed (final head).
- Not exercised in the app: `scripts/local-hermes`'s catalog lists one model, so a switch between two models with different presets wasn't driven on screen. No before/after image: nothing visible changes beyond the chips.

## Checklist

- [x] Local validation passes using `scripts/test-sim <assigned-simulator-udid>` with the tests required by `AGENTS.md` § Verifying; the selection and results are recorded above
- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

Implemented with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, reviewed by Claude Opus 5.5 and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol); the deferred-pick frames were recorded by Claude Sonnet 5.5, coordinated by Claude Opus 5.5.
