title: feat(chat): apply a model's remembered Thinking and Fast after a deferred pick lands
body:
**What the user gets:** a model picked while a response is running gets its remembered Thinking and Fast once the host actually switches to it.
**Why it matters:** #1750 asked for this case; #1770 ships presets only for picks the host runs at once or after confirmation, so a pick made mid-response still needs Thinking and Fast set by hand.
**Cost:** Medium. Simulator-testable against `scripts/local-hermes`; no phone needed.

Follow-up to #1750 / #1770.

## Why it was left out
#1770's description records the frame order at `3b421578` on both gateways:
- **Dashboard (`hermes serve`):** a deferred pick applies only when the *next* turn starts (`tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py` → `_apply_pending_model_switch`). At the first turn's end `session.info` already names the pending pick, even one the host will later refuse (`notification.show` key `model_switch.dropped`).
- **Webapp (canonical):** the pick commits about 20 ms after `message.complete` at the claim boundary, signalled by `session.updated {operation: model}` (or `status: refused`).

An earlier attempt in #1770 (reverted in `28540277`, `c09b3878`) grew three bugs in review.

## Open question
Is this worth the per-gateway tracking? Keying on canonical's `session.updated {operation: model}` is cheap; the dashboard needs tracking up to the next turn's `session.info` with `running: true`. Applying it on canonical only is an option.

title: Support exact-session navigation from host slash-command replies
body:
## Summary

Could host slash-command replies request opening an existing Hermes session by its **immutable ID**, scoped to the current server and Profile?

Hermex already supports exact-key session links (#1176 / #1185) and host/plugin commands through `slash.exec` (#1036 / #1055). The missing connection is from consuming a host-command reply to exact-key navigation. An alias to `/resume <id>` is not equivalent because local `/resume` selects by mutable title.

A use case is a host/plugin continuation command that creates an independent successor, persists its predecessor metadata, and then asks the phone to open that specific successor. The old chat must remain intact if navigation cannot be confirmed.

## Reproduced with stock production code

Stock source: `255a3c06a8ce7f9be34b99402f737f4c3b1af949` (2.2, build 1). Relevant source was also checked on current default-branch commit `0805880530453661274300b29e22da5ef035b043`; the title selector and supported host-reply variants retain this boundary.

A signed Xcode 27.2 / iOS 27.2 simulator hosted-XCTest run executed the real `ChatViewModel.runHermesSlashCommand`, real reply parser and real `/resume` selection code, with the repository's existing scripted socket and URLProtocol fixtures. Production, project, Config and shared fixture files were unchanged. Seven probe methods/helpers were inserted into the existing slash test class; all existing tests were retained.

Both complete classes ran: `HermesSlashCommandTests` and `HermesSessionLookupTests`. **44 executed: 43 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped.** The sole failure was an ordinary, deliberately retained assertion demanding the immutable child ID—not a compilation error, skip or expected-failure wrapper.

Observed cases (synthetic IDs abbreviated C and U):

1. A catalog-listed command returning ordinary output containing C and its keyed session URL produces a notice, not navigation.
2. A `prefill` response remains a prefill, not automatic navigation.
3. `{type: "alias", target: "resume C"}` selects C when C's title is C: positive control passes.
4. Returning C under a renamed title produces the Sessions-list result.
5. Duplicate case-insensitive titles produce the Sessions-list result.
6. After the alias reaches its consumer, at the subsequent REST search boundary, rename C and give unrelated U the title C. The real stock Swift handler returns an `openedHermesSession` targeting **U**. The assertion demanding C fails.

The synthetic dataset changes when the actual REST search is entered, after alias consumption—not only before the host issues the alias. An issuance-time title check cannot prevent that later selection.

This is a runtime reproduction of the client command/navigation-result handlers with synthetic server replies. It is **not** a manual screen-navigation test, a real-backend rename/search test, or a claim about the exact commit of an installed App Store binary.

## Source boundary

- `HermesSlashReply` supports notice, send, prefill and alias, not an exact-session navigation result.
- `runHermesSlashCommand` consumes those variants without invoking keyed URL/session lookup.
- `resumeHermesSession(named:)` filters search rows using case-insensitive exact **title** equality, then uses the selected row's ID. It does not require that ID to equal the requested successor ID.
- Existing `HermesSessionLookup` already provides the exact-key/Profile checks used by session links.

## Possible directions for maintainer consideration

Either of these could address the client boundary; these are **proposals, not claims about supported protocol shapes**:

- A supported host-reply navigation directive carrying an existing session ID and Profile, reusing the current exact-key lookup and failure handling. This would need coordination with the Hermes host contract.
- An explicit ID-only mode for local `/resume`, callable through an alias, while preserving existing title-resume behavior as a separate mode.

In either case: no title fallback when an ID was requested; no arbitrary external URL opening; no ambiguous/cross-server guessing; preserve the originating chat on failure; do not run the command again merely because navigation failed.

Would you prefer an upstream implementation of one of these approaches, or is there another existing supported route we should use? Happy to provide a minimal test patch if useful; this issue does not presume ownership or approval to implement a larger feature.

Investigation and test preparation were AI-assisted using Hermes Agent; the reported execution results came from actual Xcode/XCTest output.

title: docs(triage): comment on a matching issue instead of filing a duplicate
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: maintainer-approved `chore/` change.

## What changed

Troubleshoot with Hermes could file duplicate issues. The triage playbook ran one search and only *offered* to comment on a match. Step 8 also gave the agent a full recipe for filing a new issue and none for commenting, so agents filed.

Steps 6–8 of `.github/triage/PLAYBOOK.md` now:

- **Step 6:** compare the affected component's version with its releases, run at least three scrubbed searches (plus earlier `via-triage` reports), open the closest matches, follow duplicates to the issue they duplicate, and tell the user what was searched. Then one decision:
  - open match → comment there
  - closed and fixed after the user's version → update (or tell them the fix awaits a release)
  - closed but still broken on a fixed version → new issue linking the old one
  - no match → new issue
- **Step 7:** the outcome menu follows that decision.
- **Step 8:** new comment path (`gh issue comment`) that adds only what the thread lacks. Comments and new issues share one approval gate: the exact text, where it posts, and the `gh` account, then an explicit yes.

The app fetches the playbook from `master`, so this applies to every installed version as soon as it merges.

## How it was tested

Doc-only. Ran the new `gh issue list --label via-triage --search`, `gh issue view --comments` and checked `gh issue comment -R --body-file` flags against this repo.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 3 rounds with gpt-6.2-sol on high. Sol's last finding (one wording fix) is applied; the review budget ended before a final verdict. title: feat(chat): set a model's remembered Thinking and Fast when a deferred pick lands
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1771

## What changed

If you picked a model while a response was running, Hermex didn't set that model's remembered Thinking and Fast once the host switched to it. #1770 skipped this case, so you had to set both by hand.

Now the preset goes out once the host runs the deferred pick. This works on both gateways and doesn't need any per-gateway tracking:

```text
pick answered "deferred"  →  deferredPick = (model, the model it replaces)
while it waits:
  a session.info naming it   →  read model.options
  a read showing it live     →  send its preset (the existing onPickedModelActive path)
  a read showing a third model, a newer pick's answer, another runtime,
  a canonical session.updated {status: refused, target_model}, or
  a dashboard notification.show {key: model_switch.dropped}   →  stop waiting
```

- **Canonical (`hermes gateway run`).** The pick commits at the claim boundary right after `message.complete`, and the host sends `session.info {model: new}`. The read that frame starts shows the new model, so the preset goes out before the next turn.
- **Dashboard (`hermes serve`).** The pick applies only when the next turn starts (`_apply_pending_model_switch`). The `session.info` at the end of turn 1 already names the pending model, but its read still shows the old one, so nothing is sent. The next turn's `session.info {running: true}` reads the new model, and the preset goes out early in that turn. The host doesn't allow it any sooner: `switch_model` resets the reasoning config, so a value sent before the switch would be lost.
- **Settling.** The check runs as each read, read loop and write ends, and is skipped while another one is still running. So a pick that is already live in the read after its own answer also gets its preset.
- **Refusals, drops and asks.** They are followed in order, around a rebuild after lost frames, and on a frame after a gap, beside the host notices; a confirmation ask around a rebuild is held for the reattach. Their shapes come from the pinned source (`gateway/session_deferred_pick.py`, `tui_gateway/session_compression.py`).
- **Renames.** `deferredModel` (canonical only) is now `deferredPick`, used by both gateways. `receiveDeferredConfirmation` is now `receiveDeferredPickUpdate`, since it also handles the refusal.

The issue's open question asked whether to support both gateways or canonical only. I went with both: one rule covers both, and the only per-gateway code is the two lines that clear a refusal or a drop.

**Known limitation**, the same catalog-read race #1770 records. If another client switches the chat while a read is in flight, and that read still shows the deferred pick live, the preset can go to the other client's model. Closing it needs a report generation; I didn't add that new state without a maintainer call.

## How it was tested

- `HermesChatSettingsTests` follow the frame order measured in #1770 for both gateways. Two tests: a deferred pick gets its preset on the dashboard (only once the next turn runs it) and on canonical (once the host commits it); both fail on `master`. Seven more tests each fail with their path removed: a pick already live in the read after its answer; a canonical refusal; a dashboard drop; a drop after a gap in the frames; a confirmation ask after a gap, shown after the rebuild; a third model read through the picker's reload; a newer pick asking to confirm, which keeps its confirmation open.
- `scripts/test-sim <iPhone 18 Pro> --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatSettingsTests --only HermesMobileTests/BotChatControlsTests --only HermesMobileTests/HermesChatTurnTests`: 164 passed, 0 failed.
- Not run in the app: `scripts/local-hermes` needs `uv`, which this Mac doesn't have, and its stub lists only one model.

Proved by red/green XCTest replays of the measured host frame orders. Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.2-sol on high. Sol verdict: approved.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename)
- [x] No new third-party dependencies (the list in `AGENTS.md` is locked)
- [x] No invented API endpoints or JSON shapes (verified against upstream source or a running server)

title: test: stop the CI flakes at their source and cut the tests that kept causing them
body:
## Linked issue

None. This fixes every test that flaked on PR CI over the last few weeks (34 failed runs reviewed).

## What changed

PR CI kept failing on tests that pass on rerun. Each one cost a rerun and a fix-up PR. There were two causes, and a few tests that weren't worth their upkeep.

**Shared state leaking between classes.** `HermesHostFixture` keeps a global request log that only each class's `tearDown` cleared. So the first test of a class could see an earlier class's requests. `ScreenSessionTests` never cleared it at all. This accounts for the most common flakes: `HermesConnectionTests.testABrowserSignIn…` (6 failures: "8 != 0" logins), `ServeEveryProfileTests.testADuplicateBot…` (4: a body-less DELETE from `ScreenSessionTests`) and `HermesInsightsClientTests.testAClosedGate…` (2). The bundle's test observer now resets the fixture before every test, and the 19 `tearDown`s that only did that are gone.

**A cold simulator's keyboard daemon.** On a fresh CI simulator, the first focus change blocks the main thread for 20–55 s, and whichever test is running times out. `warmUpSoftwareKeyboard()` was opt-in per class with a 5 s ceiling, so most classes never warmed up and even the ones that did could still stall. It now runs once from the same observer before the first test, where no test clock is running, and waits up to 60 s.

**Tests cut or shrunk** (the rest of the flakes):
- Deleted `BotChatPresentationTests.testComposerRefocusSupersedesQueuedBlur`. It assumed SwiftUI applies an observed change within three main-queue turns. `ComposerFocusTransitionTests` covers both of its halves.
- Deleted `HermesHomeSplitRoutingTests.testDismissingRegularSettingsReadsTheEditedConnection`, plus its presentation host and the two `HermesServerHome` init parameters only it used. It hosted the whole home to check one `onDismiss:` argument, which `.onAppear` re-runs anyway.
- Shrank the hosted success-send focus test to its one hosted case. It now waits on the editor's end-editing notification; the policy test covers the rest.
- Shrank the bot chip cache test to object identity instead of comparing PNG bytes rendered off-screen.
- Shrank the webui empty-transcript test to the transcriber dropping `ok`.
- Replaced the approval summary card's hosted test with a model test of `ApprovalSummaries.show`. A duplicate request now fails it rather than hanging it.
- The push takeover-during-retirement test now does the takeover inside the spy's DELETE, so its 2 s expectation is gone.
- `ScreenSessionTests.socket(_:)` now waits on observation, as `reach` does. Before, a 5 s timeout was followed by an out-of-range index that crashed the whole test process.
- The 22 waits that gave async work only 1 s to start now get the suite's usual 5 s. `SessionListMutationTests.testStaleCanonicalFallback…` hit one on this PR's first CI run.

Not touched: one-off CI failures that were real breaks on feature branches (fa localization, the reasoning-effort label, Projects lane paging, usage reports).

## How it was tested

title: fix(networking): strip the headers a webui request was sent with on cross-origin redirects
body:
**What the user gets:** custom headers (often secrets, such as a reverse-proxy token) never follow a redirect to another origin, even when the user signs out or switches server while a request is in flight.
**Why it matters:** found in the comment sweep. A request still in flight from the server being left can carry its headers to another host if it is redirected after the switch.
**Cost:** Small to Medium. Unit-testable with a `URLProtocol` mock; no phone needed.

## Problem

`CrossOriginHeaderStripper` in `HermesMobile/Networking/APIClient.swift` builds its strip set at redirect time from `customHeaderProvider()`, which defaults to `CustomHeaderStore.shared.snapshot()`. `AuthManager` replaces that store on sign-out and on a server switch (`headerStore.replace(with:)`), so the names the request was actually sent with can be gone by the time its redirect arrives. Those headers then pass through unstripped. The same happens when the user removes or renames a header while a request is out.

The Hermes path does not have this gap: `HermesConnection` builds its redirect guard from the headers it admitted for that connection.

## Fix

Strip the header names the request was sent with, not the names configured when the redirect arrives. Carry the applied names with the request or its task and have the stripper read those.

## Acceptance

- A webui request sent with header `X` and redirected cross-origin after the store was replaced or `X` was removed reaches the new origin without `X`.
- Same-origin redirects keep their headers, and a cross-origin 307 or 308 with a body still stops, as today.
- `docs/adr/` records the redirect rule; update the decision that describes the live read.

title: refactor: one cancellation check for every screen
body:
**What the user gets:** a read that was cancelled or superseded never shows as an error, on any screen.
**Why it matters:** found in the comment sweep. Nine hand-kept copies of "is this error a cancellation" already disagree with each other.
**Cost:** Small. Unit-testable; no phone needed.

## Problem

Each of these keeps its own `isCancellation` / `isCancellationError`:

- `ArchivedSessionsViewModel`
- `DefaultProfilePickerView`
- `CronJobEditorConfigurationLoader`
- `TranscriptLinkPreviewView`
- `GitDiffView`
- `FileBrowserViewModel`
- the two Kanban states
- `SessionListViewModel`

They differ. Only the cron loader treats `BotFailure.stale` as a cancellation, although `ArchivedSessionsViewModel` throws it. `TranscriptLinkPreviewView` skips the `APIError.network` unwrap. Some also check `Task.isCancelled`.

## Fix

One shared classifier covering `CancellationError`, `URLError.cancelled` (direct or wrapped in `APIError.network`), used by all nine call sites.

`BotFailure.stale` needs a decision per call site rather than a blanket rule: keep each site's current behavior unless the site can throw `stale` and would show it as an error today, and say which sites changed in the PR.

## Acceptance

- The nine local copies are gone.
- A superseded read on a Hermes server (`BotFailure.stale`) shows no error on a screen that can throw it.
- No call site starts hiding an error it showed before, other than the ones the PR names.

title: fix(auth): keep legacy custom headers when their Keychain migration fails
body:
**What the user gets:** someone upgrading from a build that stored custom headers in one global Keychain entry keeps them even if the move to the per-server entry fails.
**Why it matters:** found in the comment sweep. A failed save is followed by deleting the only copy, so the next launch has no headers and a proxy that needs them refuses the app.
**Cost:** Small. Unit-testable with the Keychain double; no phone needed.

## Problem

`AuthManager.hydrateCustomHeaders(for:)` migrates the legacy global `.customHeaders` entry like this:

```swift
try? keychain.save(legacy, forKey: .customHeaders, scope: scope)
try? keychain.delete(.customHeaders)
```

The delete runs whether or not the save succeeded.

## Fix

Delete the legacy entry only after the scoped save succeeds, so a failed migration is retried on the next launch.

## Acceptance

- With a Keychain double whose scoped save throws, the legacy entry is still there afterwards and the headers are still applied for this launch.
- A successful migration still removes the legacy entry.

## What changed

Nine screens each kept their own "is this error a cancellation" check, and the copies didn't agree. On a Hermes server, a cancelled "Load more" in Archived Sessions showed "This action is no longer current. Refresh the conversation." because `BotClient` throws `BotFailure.stale`, not `CancellationError`, when the reading task is cancelled.

All nine now use one `Error.isCancellation` in `APIError.swift`. It matches `CancellationError` and `URLError.cancelled`, either on its own or wrapped in `APIError.network`. Sites whose old copy also checked `Task.isCancelled` (both Kanban states and the link preview) still check it inline.

How each site handles `BotFailure.stale`:

- **Changed: `ArchivedSessionsViewModel.loadMore`.** It now drops a failure when its task was cancelled, the same check `loadHermes` already makes. It still shows `stale` if the task is still running, because that means the client has gone dead. Hiding that case would leave a "Load more" button that does nothing.
- **Unchanged: `CronJobEditorConfigurationLoader`.** It keeps hiding `stale`, as before.
- **Unchanged, but they can throw `stale`:**
  - Archived `loadHermes` already ignores cancelled tasks, and a `stale` while running closes and reports the dead client.
  - Archived delete is a write.
  - Hermes session export runs from a Task nothing cancels.
  - Files, Git diff and Kanban go over REST, where `stale` only means the connection was retired. Hiding it would leave a spinner or an empty screen.
- **Cannot throw `stale`:** profile picker, link preview, and the webui paths in SessionList.

The link preview gains the `APIError.network` unwrap. It never receives an `APIError`, so nothing changes there.

The decision is recorded in `docs/adr/0130-hermes-session-actions.md`.

## How it was tested

- New `HermesSessionActionsTests.testACancelledPageReadShowsNoError`. It fails on the base with the "no longer current" message and passes with this change. The old profile-picker classifier test now targets the shared property (`APIClientConfigurationTests.testCancellationDetection`).
- `scripts/test-sim <udid> --only` runs, all passing:
  - `HermesSessionActionsTests`, `APIClientConfigurationTests` and `SessionListMutationTests`: 112 passed.
  - `CronJobEditorConfigurationTests`, `FileBrowserViewModelTests`, `GitDiffFileJumpTests`, `HermesSessionListTests`, `KanbanCardDetailStateTests`, `KanbanFeatureStateTests`, `TranscriptLinkPreviewTests` and `SessionNavigationStateTests`: 204 passed.
  - After the review fix and the rebase, `HermesSessionActionsTests` and `APIClientConfigurationTests`: 38 passed.
- `ci/check_comments.py`, `ci/check_test_waits.py` and `python3 -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_*.py'` pass.

title: fix(auth): keep legacy custom headers when their Keychain migration fails
body:
## Linked issue

Fixes #1785

## What changed

Upgrading from a build that kept custom headers in one global Keychain entry could lose them: the migration to the per-server entry deleted the global copy even when the per-server save failed, so the next launch had no headers and a proxy that needs them refused the app.

`AuthManager.hydrateCustomHeaders(for:)` now deletes the legacy entry only after the scoped save succeeds. The headers are still applied for this launch either way, and a failed migration retries on the next one. ADR 0148 and the multi-server isolation doc's test list are updated to match.

## How it was tested

- New `CustomHeaderAuthManagerTests.testLaunchKeepsLegacyGlobalHeadersWhenTheirMigrationFails` uses the existing `FailingKeychain` double. title: test(live-activity): stop a leaked title refresh from failing the excerpt test
body:
## Linked issue

No issue: a maintainer-approved flake fix.

## What changed

`testChatViewModelSuppressesLiveActivityResponseExcerptsByDefault` sometimes failed in CI with `"/api/session" is not equal to "/api/chat/start"`. The request came from the test that runs just before it.

**Cause.** `testChatViewModelRunEndTriggerCoversFailedAndCompletedRunsButNotStoppedOnes` emits `done` and then `streamEnd`. That path (`ChatStreamCoordinator.finishStream` → `refreshCompletedResponseTitleIfNeeded`) starts an `/api/session` title refresh, and nothing awaits it. `LiveActivityURLProtocol.handler` is one static shared by every test in the file. So when the URL loading thread reached `startLoading` after the next test had installed its handler, the leaked request went to the excerpt test's strict handler. A slow CI host widens that window; the failing run took about 7 s. The excerpt test's own view model never requests `/api/session`: it emits no `done`, and its `chat/start` succeeds, so neither the title-refresh path nor the error-recovery paths run. Two other tests with strict handlers, `testStreamEndWithoutDone…` and `testFollowupMessage…`, also run right after tests that issue `/api/session`, so they had the same exposure.

**Fix (test-only).** `LiveActivityURLProtocol.makeSession()` gives each test's `URLSession` its own owner header, and `startLoading` serves only requests from the session the current test created. A request left over from an earlier test now fails with `badServerResponse`, which the title refresh already ignores. All 11 call sites use the helper, so the whole file is covered. No app code changed, and no request the app makes is hidden from its own test.

## How it was tested

- **Reproduced first:** a temporary change, not committed, made the protocol hold the `/api/session` load until the next test had installed its handler. On `master` that fails with the exact CI error (`LiveActivityTests.swift:360: XCTAssertEqual failed: ("Optional("/api/session")") is not equal to ("Optional("/api/chat/start")")`). With this fix plus the same temporary change, both tests pass.
- `scripts/test-sim CDCCCF6B-ED3F-4599-B932-FCBD7726D3C2 --only HermesMobileTests/LiveActivityTests --repeat 20`: PASS. All 44 tests ran 20 times (`-run-tests-until-failure`) with 0 failures.
- `python3 ci/check_comments.py`, `python3 ci/check_test_waits.py`, and `python3 -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_*.py'`: all pass.

- [x] New/changed `Codable` models decode tolerantly (optionals for fields the server might add or rename) (n/a, none changed)

title: feat(chat): optional Send with Return on the on-screen keyboard (VoiceOver accessibility)
body:
Hi, thank you for Hermex. I'm a blind user and I use it every day with VoiceOver on iPhone.

**Request:** an optional setting to send the message with the Return key of the iPhone's on-screen (software) keyboard, not only with a hardware keyboard (the "Send with Return" option from #1655 covers hardware keyboards only).

**Why this matters for blind users:**
With VoiceOver, I can't see where the Send button is. After typing, I have to leave the keyboard and swipe through the composer elements one by one to find Send, then come back to the text field to type the next message. On every message this adds several extra gestures, and it's easy to land on the wrong button (mic, attachments, model picker).

The Return key sits right at the bottom of the keyboard I'm already typing on, so VoiceOver users can reach it immediately without moving focus away. Many chat apps offer this option for exactly this reason.

**Suggested behavior:**
- A toggle in Settings > Interaction, for example "Send with Return (on-screen keyboard)", off by default.
- When it's on, the keyboard's Return key is labeled "Send", and VoiceOver reads it as "Send".
- New lines could still be added with Shift+Return on a hardware keyboard, or by turning the toggle off.

This small change would make Hermex much faster and easier for screen reader users. Thank you!
